content: You step onto the lake surface, walk to the center where she once danced, and take out the pendant the old man gave you, your shackles burning red glow.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The shackles didn't point me in the wrong direction. I should've known you're here sooner.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I came to see you, Hamel.
You let go of the pendant, which is wrapped up in red light. It falls onto and cracks open the lake surface.
Icy water sucks you in and engulfs you whole, blocking out the voices calling you from above.

You're besieged by frenzied bubbles, on the verge of losing consciousness. But the prickly icy water wakes you up. You see faint blue glows, but below you is a bottomless abyss of darkness, from which rises a loud din.

speaker: Greedy Woman
content: Did you see something strange again? Don't say anything about it... There's a large crowd of reporters outside. You must present yourself as a great dancer, not some lunatic...

speaker: Greedy Woman
content: Keep quiet, and let me do the talking. All you have to do is dance. You'll become a legend... Just dance, and you can change your fate...

speaker: Greedy Woman
content: Dance for me, my child, my beloved Dancer...

speaker: Dissatisfied Noise
content: She's no legendary dancer, this isn't art for charity... She's nothing more than a lunatic, her audience are lunatics too!

speaker: Dissatisfied Noise
content: She is a demon... a plaything of the rich!

speaker: Arrogant Man
content: You took my money. Now, dance for me, Dancer of the DisCity!

speaker: Haughty Man
content: Don't you defy me. Now, dance for me, dancer of the DisCity!

speaker: Rowdy Cacophony
content: Dance! Why are you not dancing? I've given you the best stage there is. You must dance for us, Dancer!!
Don't go on stage anymore! Leave with me!
You're going mad. You have to stop dancing. It's for your own good... Don't you get it?!

speaker: Twisted Voice
content: He came to the carnival, because you caused him pain. Isn't that so? I comforted him, he's mine now. I'm not giving him to you!

speaker: Twisted Voice
content: Or... Do you want to keep me company? You're different from them all. You're strong, you're beautiful, and you're all alone too... You're more like me! We're the same!

speaker: Twisted Voice
content: <size=44>Love me! Love me the way you've loved him!</size>
Don't go, don't leave me... Come back, Hamel!

Ten meters, twenty meters... You're sinking. You're confined in the depths of the water, and your thoughts are spinning out of control, overwhelming you. But it's all just an illusion! You know you're almost there, for darkness is swimming up fast to greet you...
Who's that... Who's there... disturbing the Dancer...? Who's... trying to take the Dancer...?
Don't you dare take our Dancer!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Get out of my way!

Your shackles drive out the darkness surrounding you. Your field of vision clears up. Countless tentacles reach up from the bottom of the lake, all tangled up. The entire lake is contaminated by Mania and has become a massive abyss of death.
Hamel is down there. Contamination tangles in her long hair and tears at her once-graceful dance dress. Darkness fetters the limbs of the Dancer, as well as her soul.

speaker: Choice
content: Wake up, Hamel!
Contamination has crept onto her face. Mania has been accumulating for 23 years here. Getting close to the lake bottom is enough to make your all sensations burn violently.
Hamel is entombed in this sea of Mania alone, as if she is in a deep sleep from which she can not wake up.

speaker: Choice
content: Wake up! I'm taking you back!
options: Wake up! I'm taking you back!

content: Despite the pain, you walk into the cloud of Mania surrounding Hamel and touch her soul. Clenching your teeth, you use the shackles on her, hoping it can help her resist the encroachment of Mania.
You have successfully used the shackles on her, but she doesn't wake up.
Instead, innumerable hollow, wild eyes light up in the mud amid darkness. The abyss of death shudders.
It's the battered dolls that you saw rotting in the carnival!

speaker: Phantom Shadows under the lake
content: Been woken... Been woken... Have to face this place again...

speaker: Phantom Shadows under the lake
content: <color=#7683a2><size=28><i>So lonely... So much pain... So scared... The explosion hasn't ended... Hamel... Hamel... We need Hamel...</size>

speaker: Phantom Shadows under the lake
content: Don't take her away from us... Don't take her away from us!

speaker: Phantom Shadows under the lake
content: Don't desert us! Don't leave us in this abyss!

speaker: Hecate
content: If the real Hamel didn't get inside the Black Ring until after it had appeared, then who provided the mental contamination needed to initiate the BR-001?

You've seen this before, have seen such a display of craziness. In the abyss of the unclaimed crypt, the inheritance, screaming and howling, consumed countless maniac gangsters to aid its own awakening and revival.
Then it finally comes to you that what a Corpus needs is not a Sinner per se. What it really needs is pure darkness, the vast craziness of people.
It comes from deranged Sinners, bloodthirsty gangsters, or specters that can't let the past go.

speaker: Phantom Shadows under the lake
content: She's our Dancer! Don't you dare take her away!

speaker: Choice
options: It's you who awakened the Corpus, you trapped her!

content: You manage to beat back some of the beat-up enemies. They are weak but numerous. You can't defeat them all at once. You try hard to sever the contamination clinging to Hamel.

speaker: Choice
options: Wake up. Someone is waiting for your return.

content: She doesn't respond.
As you tear away the tentacles on Hamel's arm, more dark substance latches onto you and crushes you so hard that you feel as if all your bones are going to snap.

speaker: Puppets in the Carnival
content: She belongs here, forever and ever! Go to hell!
A split second before you're consumed, Hamel opens her eyes slowly.
...A hush descends. The tentacles of contamination are gone, along with the din. At the lake bottom, where the sun can not reach and time seems to stop, you and Hamel are left alone.

speaker: Hamel
content: Time starts to flow again... I... remember you...
A warm current courses through your body and washes away all your pain. She looks up into your eyes.

speaker: Hamel
content: That black hole in your heart... is it still there?

speaker: Choice
options: It's been filled up. Thank you for bringing my friends back.
Still there. But I can move on now.

speaker: Hamel
content: Really... That's great...

speaker: Choice
options: The carnival's ended. Let me take you out of here.

content: Hamel makes no response. The bottom of the lake starts shaking violently, and low, agitated voices travel through the water and pound on your eardrums.
...It's the specters!

speaker: Hamel
content: They're my audience... They're still here, they need me...

speaker: Hamel
content: I can't leave the stage...

speaker: Choice
options: You don't have to dance for them!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Let's get out of here. People will come and take care of this. They'll deal with your audience.

speaker: Hamel
content: Who... and how...?

speaker: Hamel
content: My audience stays here just for the show.

speaker: Hamel
content: You... will you all be able to soothe all the pain, and comfort everyone here?
You're stunned. How... how many Corruptors are here?

Thirty thousand people went missing on the day the Ring appeared, and every year since then, there have been additional missing people. That's a huge number, even after taking into account the Corruptors consumed by the awakened Corpus.
If they're released from this place, will those by the riverside—your Sinners, Nightingale, and the FAC units, be able to resist them?

In the 23 years BR-001 was suppressed by Hamel, the amount of contamination that has leaked out has been enough to pollute the entire Rust. Even if all the troops are mobilized, can they... resist these tens of thousands of monsters that have been under the influence of the Black Ring?

There is no water pressure in the illusory realm, but the low, continuous moaning makes your chest tight nevertheless. The monsters are still here, threatening to break the peace that came not so long ago.

speaker: Hamel
content: It's okay... I'm happy to dance for them...

speaker: Choice
options: There must be some other way.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You've done enough. You don't need to make sacrifices anymore. We're going back together, like I promised. I can't leave you here alone!

speaker: Hamel
content: Back... I won't be lonely when I'm back?
She raises her hand and rests it on your cheek, her rose-red pupils overflowing with sadness and gentleness. Looking at her, you lose the power of speech.

speaker: Hamel
content: I'm not afraid of loneliness, never have been... Loneliness follows me wherever I go.

speaker: Hamel
content: Here, at least I have an audience, and I can dance freely.
The illusory realm starts trembling. The cries of the Corruptors reach you.

speaker: Hamel
content: Thank you for looking for me... It's all right now... Go back...

speaker: Hamel
content: Go back to your friends.

speaker: Hamel
content: This is the stage I've chosen, it is my home too.
Your word is swallowed up by the waters. Her hand moves from your face to your chest, and gives it a gentle push.

The world is falling away from you. You see a jungle of black hands at the bottom of the lake, see the only spot of light being engulfed by darkness. You try in vain to swim downwards. Inevitably, you are pushed out of the illusory realm. You cry out, but your voice will never reach Hamel.
Hamel is alone at the pitch-black bottom. She rises to her feet slowly, as the stage, a cage made for her, goes up.

speaker: Fear Puppet
content: Don't go... Don't go... Hamel...

speaker: Misery Puppet
content: Dance for us... Lift the curse on us...
She picks up the pendant lodged in the fine sand, looking at it like it's a lost memory. Only after a while does she clutch it in her palm.

speaker: Void Puppet
content: Do you hate us...? Are you scared of us...?

speaker: Void Puppet
content: Because we're monsters, you're leaving us too...?

speaker: Hamel
content: No... You're my audience. It's just that you're ahead of others in reaching the end that nobody can escape...

speaker: Hamel
content: All of us will be lost and lonely eventually...
Water rolls out from the bottom of the lake, sweeping away all the filth, pain, and darkness. The giant Ferris wheel rises and spins. The last illusory realm has come into being.

speaker: Hamel
content: Welcome to the last chapter of our joyous music. It ends with the destruction of this world of ours...

speaker: Hamel
content: Thank you all. When I was lost and lonely, you gave me...

speaker: Hamel
content: A stage whose curtain never comes down.
She raises her arms, the hem of her dress swirling, and starts dancing.

speaker: Phantom Shadows under the lake
content: Those wishes that have been wishful thinking... Those dreams that can never come true...

speaker: Phantom Shadows under the lake
content: Those unresolvable pains... The cruelties... The realities...

speaker: Phantom Shadows under the lake
content: Dance, Hamel, dance... Use your dancing... to make our dreams a reality...

speaker: Phantom Shadows under the lake
content: Thank you, we love you...
Hamel closes her eyes, losing herself in her last dance, impermeable to time and space.
Everyone needs a home. His home is where his friends are, whereas a Dancer's home is forever the stage.
female_content: Everyone needs a home. Her home is where her friends are, whereas a Dancer's home is forever the stage.

content: But the spot where the shackles lie is warm. When she closes her eyes, all she sees is the pained face of the person who has been pushed out of the illusory realm.
He shouts to Hamel, but his voice is pushed back by currents and bubbles. What's he so hung up on? What's he... trying to say?
female_content: She shouts to Hamel, but her voice is pushed back by currents and bubbles. What's she so hung up on? What's she... trying to say?

content: I won't let it end. You still have a lot of time, a big world ahead of you! One day, I'll come back for you. Wait for me!
I'll give you a real stage, where you're going to dance for yourself, not for others. One day, I'll come back for you. Wait for me!

speaker: Hamel
content: What... did he say?
female_content: What... did she say?

speaker: Hamel
content: If we meet again... I want to ask him.
female_content: If we meet again... I want to ask her.

content: In some corner on the banks of the Rust, a black umbrella fishes a black raincoat out of a heap of trash. The lining of the raincoat is covered with stinky skin and flesh.
The owner shakes off the filth on the umbrella, and opens it again.

speaker: Parma
content: So merciless... That spider lady, she really lives up to the name...

speaker: Parma
content: If I had used her then, I would've had a magnificent Black Ring.

speaker: Parma
content: Anyway, the outcome wasn't a shock. After all, it was a feral Corpus that had been suppressed for many years. It was only normal that it lost.

speaker: Parma
content: Yes, it was that defective again.

speaker: Parma
content: It did surprise me that he was the one who destroyed BR-004. But he had earned his right. It was not a battle I could get involved in.
female_content: It did surprise me that she was the one who destroyed BR-004. But she had earned her right. It was not a battle I could get involved in.

speaker: Parma
content: But it's all over now. Now what? Should I do something about him? Kill him, maybe?
female_content: But it's all over now. Now what? Should I do something about her? Kill her, maybe?

content: Bang!
A bullet perforates the black umbrella, enters the man's skull, and penetrates his brainstem.
He falls onto the ground, his mouth open. It doesn't take long for the black flames to burn the body into nothingness.

speaker: Agent from the 9th Agency
content: Is he dead?

speaker: Langley
content: It takes more than two shots to kill a monster like him.

speaker: Langley
content: What? Why look so serious? Is the situation that bad?

speaker: Agent from the 9th Agency
content: Nothing. I was just thinking... that shooting a man from a helicopter might seem a bit over-the-top.
Langley snickers, puts down the handgun, and takes the walkie-talkie from the clerk's hand.

speaker: MBCC Chief
content: What kind of celebratory party leaves out the person being congratulated?

speaker: Langley
content: Sorry... Special agents have a tight schedule. We have to deal with traitors and get rid of the evil forces. Those rats in the gutter have reared their ugly heads again...

speaker: Langley
content: Oh, by the way, you and your MBCC are now officially under the leadership of the 9th Agency, which means, from now on, I'm your boss.

speaker: Langley
content: Enjoy the last bit of your leisure time. Your work ahead won't be easy.
Ignoring the complaints on the other end of the line, Langley hangs up.

speaker: Langley
content: Better get back to the Paradeisos. The geezers are waiting for my report.
A few key words have been marked red on the documents inside the blood-stained document envelope in her hand.
...<color=#fb9259>Syndicate, Deus Corpus, activating. WhiteSands, abnormal activity confirmed.</color>
In an obscure office, a man is sitting by the window alone. A black raven lands on the arm of his chair, glances at the letter in his hand, and suddenly cries out.

speaker: Black Raven
content: Caw... Caw... News from the ruins of the <color=#fb9259>BR-004</color>. A good one, a bad one, and a hard-to-define one.

speaker: Black Raven
content: Which one would you like to hear first, my dear friend? Caw...
The man in the shadows remains silent. The black raven hops and tilts its head, then continues talking.

speaker: Black Raven
content: Alright. I'll start with my favorite, the good one. Blue treasures are coming out of the remains of BR-004 after six months. Not much, but they are there.

speaker: Black Raven
content: You were right, friend. Dark clouds have silver linings. And Syndicate has never lost hope.

speaker: Black Raven
content: <size=30>The bad news is that the filth that came out of nowhere still exists. Strange things are happening in the dead ring,  and a calamity simmers its comeback. Some soldiers stationed there were wounded, so the bigwigs sent in a <color=#fb9259>big gun</color> to investigate in secret.</size>

speaker: Man in the Shadow
content: ...Six months ago, you said the owner of BR-004 was destroyed. That ring has been confirmed silent and unlikely to be active again.

speaker: Black Raven
content: Caw... Caw... I did, and it was true. But it has been awakened by someone else. It's not the only Black Ring in Syndicate, remember? Eight years ago, in the pit, remember?
The lights flicker in the silent room. The items are swept off the table, and an oil lamp shatters into a puddle of flames, startling the raven.

speaker: Black Raven
content: Caw... Calm down, friend. Don't get overwhelmed by the darkness from the past. You have sworn to look for the light. And the last and most important news. Here it is...

speaker: Black Raven
content: The secret investigator is a hidden shepherd with Mania shackles from a secret institution.

speaker: Black Raven
content: It's the one who led the Legion into the trap, controlled the Sinners, and tore the Black Ring—their hero... will come back to Syndicate today.

speaker: Black Raven
content: You have been waiting for this for a long time, right? What do you want me to do? And what will you do?

speaker: Man in the Shadow
content: ...Raye.

speaker: Black Raven
content: What?

speaker: Man in the Shadow
content: Can you quit talking like that when delivering a message? It hurts my ears. You sounded quite normal the last time we met.
The raven crows with laughter and flaps its wings. Its fully stretched body explodes into black ink, splashing on the man's hand and the letter he's holding.
The man picks up the paper and takes a look, <color=#fb9259>BR-004</color>, <color=#fb9259>Legion</color>, <color=#fb9259>Zoya</color>, <color=#fb9259>Earl</color>, <color=#fb9259>FAC</color>...
He throws the letter into the flames on the floor. The fire reflects on the window, and through the reflection, he looks outside.

<size=30>The dawn hasn't fallen yet. The optical camouflage fluctuates, occasionally revealing the Black Ring of DisSea from inside the barrier, but it soon disappears like a mirage. The distant Eastside is still the glory of humanity for its hustle and prosperity.</size>
But that prosperity is far too distant. The vast expanse of land extending silently in front of him is the gray West District factories, his hometown where it has nothing left.

speaker: Man in the Shadow
content: ...I'll find out if he's a friend or foe.
female_content: ...I'll find out if she's a friend or foe.

speaker: Man in the Shadow
content: The fire will come. This time... it won't be extinguished.

7:40 a.m., March 14, N.F.113
BR-004 Post-Disaster Contamination Cleanup Area

In the early morning, the air is slightly cool with some moisture. The disaster and strife are long gone, leaving the buzzing hovering drones. The Hypercube glows a blue light and silently purifies the residual contamination.
Half a year later, you come back to the <color=#fb9259>Keylan Square</color>.

speaker: Nightingale
content: The FAC decontamination force reports an unusual increase of residual contamination in the BR-004 lockdown area was observed two weeks ago.

speaker: Nightingale
content: The contamination level wasn't high, and the M-value in the area was maintained at a low level. But its source has yet to be located.

speaker: Nightingale
content: We need you to investigate...

speaker: Nightingale
content: Are there signs of the Black Ring being revived? Could there be remains of the "Corpus" you broke?
The Black Ring is rooted in the Corpus. It will burst when the Corpus revives and shatter when the "Corpseborne" is destroyed.
BR-004 can't be more dead. Its Corpus is inside you. Nothing can change that.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: There are traces of the ring left at the scene, but it can't be the original Corpus of BR-004. My shackles can't sense any sign of a "Corpus" around, either.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So either there's an unknown contamination mechanism, or the "thing" that caused the mutation has left.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Understood. I'll put together a report of your analysis immediately. Please leave the contaminated lockdown area and return to somewhere safe after the investigation finishes.

speaker: Nightingale
content: You don't have to enter the contamination zone yourself.

speaker: Nightingale
content: ...You are not standing on safe grounds. The mental contamination field is weak but does exist, and FAC has found new Corruptors nearby.

speaker: Nightingale
content: The Sinners aren't with you, are they?

speaker: Choice
options: I think I still have some fight in me.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Yes, your shackles are powerful. However, we know from the tests that the strength and controllability of the shackles are positively correlated with the level of contamination in your area.

speaker: Nightingale
content: In an <color=#fb9259>intense mental contamination field</color>, they can be very powerful, and you have used them to solve many Mania crises and break two Black Rings.

speaker: Nightingale
content: But you are now in a purification zone where the M-value is maintained at a low level. Once you are not in a Mania-contaminated area, the shackles will remain inactive. If you force the Potestas, there will be severe consequences.
She's right. You showed incredible power with the inductive and destructive power of the shackles being pulled out to their extreme—in the Black Ring and highly distorted mental contamination fields.
Outside the Black Ring, you're the "loser" who depends on Sinners. The shackles may have a deep connection with the Black Ring and Mania, and you have more secrets that should be kept unknown.

Fortunately, everything happened in the isolated Mania zone, and you could hide the truth by crowning all the credits to Sinners. Hella has no doubt about it, and Hecate won't say anything. This is what you want.
...Too many people are watching you. It's safer and more convenient to disguise yourself as a weak but necessary loser than a scary "anomaly."

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, are you listening?
The adjutant sighs with a hint of pleading in her tone.

speaker: Nightingale
content: I know you take the Black Ring seriously, and we do need your intuition when it comes to the matter, but please take care of yourself.

speaker: Nightingale
content: The medical department has sent several warnings over the past month. You haven't fully recovered, and there has been an abnormal decline in your physical condition.

speaker: Nightingale
content: The Black Ring is something that exceeds human perception. You keep fighting it and then return to where it used to be. Everyone is worried about the possible side effects it may have on you.

speaker: Choice
options: It's okay, Nightingale. I'll be back soon.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This place is more than a Black Ring, and I'd like to come back every now and then.

speaker: Nightingale
content: ...I see.
There is silence on the other end of the communicator, and you're grateful for her thoughtfulness. Your thought begins to drift to the past.
A ray of blue light falls to the ground.
It's a small Hypercube fragment, light, thin, and fragile like a snowflake.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Did this fall out of a FAC decontamination device?

speaker: Nightingale
content: No, this is a Hypercube piece. It has just precipitated and has not yet formed a cube. Hypercubes come with the Black Ring, and there are various opinions on the reason.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Scientists speculate that when the ring becomes inactive, some areas within will slowly precipitate Hypercubes, just as reduced solubility will lead to supersaturated precipitation.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Hypercubes have been found at BR-004, and FAC is recovering these valuable resources. It's the only comfort people can get after the trauma.
The crystal piece lies quietly in the palm of your hand, and the shattered blue light brings you back to a corner of your chaotic memories.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It reminds me of old friends.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Of course. That's...
You hear an alarm on the other end of the communicator, interrupting the adjutant.

speaker: Nightingale
content: ...There are Corruptors in the blockade area. There aren't too many, but they are close to the anti-Mania base.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This is a clue delivered to our doorstep. Send me the coordinates, and I'll be on my way.
You put away all the sentimentality. Dwelling on the past is not what they would want for you, and those people deserve to be better remembered.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Understood. The Sinners will rendezvous with you immediately, and the FAC decontamination force is out too.

speaker: Nightingale
content: We aren't dealing with a large number of enemies. The only tricky part is the civilians on the scene. Those monsters are extremely hungry for human emotions. They could break through the anti-Mania base and cause more destruction.

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: FAC decontamination force is in position. Chief, could you...

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: Oh... Is it already over? I knew we could count on the Chief! Sorry, we were late.

speaker: Hella
content: Hmph, that worked out just fine. You guys would just hold me back anyways. What do they call it, the division of neighbor? I'll fight the monsters, and you guys clean up after. It's all you're good for anyway.

speaker: Hella
content: Make sure you get the corners too, CLEANUP FORCE.

speaker: Hecate
content: It's "the division of labor," I taught you that last night.

speaker: Hella
content: ...Ahhhh shut up!

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: Pfft... Ahem! Well, Chief ${PlayerName}, please take care of the contamination analysis. I'll go check the civilians.
You walk over to Hecate.

speaker: Hecate
content: FAC has tested the composition, and the contamination wasn't an external invasion. It's exactly the same as the residue of BR-004, which started to proliferate under the influence of some stimulus.

speaker: Hecate
content: The activity level is low, but this is indeed a sign of the ring becoming active.

speaker: Hecate
content: Could the "Corpus"...

speaker: Hella
content: Hey... Don't make scary assumptions. The monsters from half a year ago were really fierce, but those ones just now turned to run as soon as they spotted me like EMP.

speaker: Hella
content: I've grown much stronger, but... I don't think I'm that intimidating yet.
The monsters formed from contaminations will inherit the Mania from the source, which is the obsession of someone deranged.

The Corruptors in the fourth ring were influenced by ground zero, Zoya, and were dominated by a reckless desire to destroy. The Corruptors just now, however, were easily frightened and even tried to run.
What woke them up must be very different from BR-004.

speaker: Hecate
content: What would it be? Something that can penetrate the FAC anti-Mania force field and awaken what's left of the Black Ring... It must be a dangerous and powerful presence, but then how did it hide from the monitoring network?

speaker: Nightingale
content: The 9th Agency has provided the contact key of the agent, but he hasn't responded.
You look over to the anti-Mania base not far away, a ring monitoring network FAC built. It's meant to keep the contamination in and prevent the recurrence of disasters.
Looking down at the remaining filth, you find them turning gray in the Hypercube force field. But they keep trembling like they're struggling to escape or hide.
If the shackles are the power from "the other side"... will it give you hints? You reach out to touch the shackles, but before you manage, a strange sensation sweeps through you...
Without warning, something drums, and the world is submerged by a spurt of shadows. Or maybe you are falling into some gap, and the world around you is spinning.
You see palm prints, a drag mark, a path. It's something huge struggling and crawling through streets, walls, creeping on the roofs toward the northeast...

Your throat becomes parched, and the pungent smell of rust and scorched earth chokes you. Your skin is freezing and burning, and your eardrums are pierced by some terrible sound. You can hear a mournful wail...
<color=#dg1f1f><i>AHHHH... AHHHH...<color=#dg1f1f><i>

speaker: Hecate
content: Chief...?
The epileptic sight is only momentary, the darkness has receded, and everything is back to normal. The people around you look at you in astonishment. They did not see the sight you saw at all.
But the huge scorch marks that crawled across the crumbling city have been burned into your mind.
The call goes through, but it connects to the 9th Agency first, and an unfamiliar voice speaks out.
Hello there, Chief. I am "Rust," the inspector of the 9th Agency in the West District.
Forget it. You shouldn't have asked. It's not the first time you've learned that the 9th Agency is monitoring you.

speaker: Rust
content: Hmm? Aren't you looking for me? I've risked exposure to bring you the long-awaited information.

speaker: Rust
content: But you must have made an important discovery if you are contacting base in such a hurry. How about you do that first?
You recall the "illusion" you just had and look in the direction of the "trail"—northeast of the square, in the direction of the <color=#fb9259>DisSea Black Ring</color>.

speaker: Choice
options: I may have "sensed" something that triggered the mutation.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It passed BR-004 and crawled toward DisSea. Or maybe it's the other way around, heading towards the square from DisSea.

You feel something from the shackles. It's a Corpus, the inheritance from Parma... this you are sure of. But it's impossible to tell if the sight is the past, the present, or just some kind of harbinger of the future.
When the vision fades, and the shackles regain their serenity, it's as if you were hallucinating. The FAC monitoring site never detected a Corpus-level contaminant source.

speaker: Choice
options: Should I follow the trace and investigate?

speaker: Rust
content: Easy, Chief, and don't be so honest. Your time is valuable, and you should hear the info I offer. We may not have your intuition, but our agents have some tricks up their sleeves.

speaker: Rust
content: Recently, an "old friend" has been very active on both sides of the Rust, throwing false leads around for the 9th Agency. However, only one is quite relevant to the direction you pointed out, and it is on the coast of DisSea.
An "old friend" of the 9th Agency, someone connected to the Black Ring... It's him?!

speaker: Rust
content: Yes. I've updated your database with the target location and relevant information. Get ready to go, Chief.

speaker: Rust
content: I have a hunch that the rats have set up a really big show. Please make sure you don't miss it.

speaker: Choice
options: I will go back immediately to get ready.

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: Please wait!

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: Regarding these civilians, Chief ${PlayerName}, can you please keep this under wraps? I mean... don't put it in the report.

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: Trespassing in the ring area to steal resources is a felony, and all those who are suspected will be sent to the detention center. If the people in charge knew about it, it would be the end for them.
An old man in a wheelchair trembles with fear and shivers as he hands over a rag in his hand, as if begging for forgiveness.
You then notice that it's Hypercube shards wrapped in the rag.

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: They are not gangsters, nor WhiteSands smugglers, just some... ordinary people in Syndicate trying to live.

The civilians in front of you are old and frail, women and children, in rags, and the one standing in the front is just a skinny teenage boy. His eyes are filled with bewilderment, fear, and aimless hostility.

The West District chaos did not end following the destruction of the Black Ring and the fall of the gangs. Poverty and despair still shroud Syndicate, and these are the legacy of Mania and humanity. You are facing the victims who got it the worst.

speaker: Choice
options: My duty is to investigate the mutation, not to enforce the law.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What about you?

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: Chief! The FAC's duty has always been to protect the city and its citizens from Mania. I'm going to confirm their mental state and send them home if they're not corrupted.

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: Thank you for your understanding!
He salutes you and clunks off with his bulky armor to attend to the civilians. You ignore Hella's snicker and return to the MBCC to make final preparations.

speaker: Rust
content: Ahead is our destination, <color=#fb9259>the inner bay</color> on the southwest shore of DisSea, the center of the former West District mining belt.

speaker: Rust
content: During the great explosion of DisSea, the inner bay mining area was completely destroyed, and the coast became extremely uninhabitable due to the spreading mental contamination.

speaker: Rust
content: Only civilians who don't want to join the gangs will be forced to settle here. They call this place the <color=#fb9259>Drifter Camp</color>. It was once seen as the slum of the Syndicate.
...They call this a slum?

The car climbs over the slope, and the view opens up. On both sides, shanty towers stretch forward, but at the end lies a colossal structure. Rusted brackets and staggered iron frames make up the most amazing fortress in the Syndicate.
The structure is more than 100 meters high, crowded and skewed, unreasonably unstable but resolutely standing. It's magnificent and full of life, like a steel beast that will leap up the next second.

speaker: Hella
content: WOW! Woah!!! When did Syndicate get something so awesome?!! Why have I never seen this before?

speaker: Rust
content: Oh, of course you haven't. Not long ago, this place was just an ordinary deserted building. The poor drifters paid extortion to the gangs for so many years and couldn't do anything to help themselves.

speaker: Rust
content: Only after the fall of the gangs was the Drifter Camp freed. They've been buttoned down for too long, and once the oppressors are gone, they're growing like weeds.

speaker: Choice
options: You said Parma has been here.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Are they working together on this? Is the Drifter Camp messing with Mania too? Do they have anything to do with BR-004?

speaker: Rust
content: Slow down, Chief. I did see traces of Parma here, but so far, I don't think they are working together.

speaker: Rust
content: On the contrary, because of their disgust for the gangs and the chaos, weapons, and contamination they bring, the Drifter Camp is rather hostile to everything related to Mania.

speaker: Rust
content: They stockpiled Hypercube and built their own anti-Mania equipment to protect the residents. Even when the gangs raged with Mania not long ago, this place was clear from contamination.

speaker: Hecate
content: Resisting Mania contamination without the support of FAC... Not just any ordinary drifters can do that.

speaker: Rust
content: Yes, I've been monitoring the Drifter Camp for some time now, and there are indeed great talents here, as well as information that we have trouble getting our hands on.

speaker: Choice
options: It would be nice if we could work with them.

speaker: Rust
content: Yes, if it were half a year earlier, you would have been able to get help from the Drifter Camp. But now... the situation is tricky.
You can imagine why. You look at the executive officer sitting across from you in a gray and yellow uniform.

speaker: Choice
content: Do you have to come with us?
options: Do you have to come with us?

speaker: Executive Officer
content: That's right. The Drifter Camp is home to a large number of West District outlaws. Since there are now signs of Mania there, and a relapse of BR-004 is involved, we can't complete the reconstruction without looking into this.

speaker: Executive Officer
content: The West District is a complicated area, and you need our authority to ensure personal safety and a smooth investigation.

<size=30>After the outbreak of BR-004, the enforcement of West District Order Management Regulations was suspended, the local security precinct was withdrawn, and the Reconstruction Committee, led by the city council, assumed the district administrative functions.</size>

It's said to be multi-funded, diversified and open, crossing the Rust to the West District in order to cover the economic, medical, educational, and public administration fields, seeking to fix the chaos and help Syndicate get back on track.
...The help, however, now seems like a joke.

speaker: Choice
options: I was hoping it would be a friendly discussion.

speaker: Executive Officer
content: That's unrealistic thinking. Drifter Camp has built illegal constructions and has been arming themselves. They have defied management by stealing Hypercubes. And recently, we have seen them having more friction with the leftover gangsters.

speaker: Executive Officer
content: Those people are selfish, short-sighted, and ungrateful. They are already a serious threat to the new order in the West District and must be strictly monitored.

speaker: Executive Officer
content: The West District can't afford another riot like the Legion had, and it's important to take preventive measures.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm on a very important Mania investigation mission. If we make a big deal out of this and more serious contamination breaks out, can you and your Reconstruction Executive Committee be held accountable?

speaker: Executive Officer
content: That is within your authority and responsibility. We assist but do not interfere.
But he has no intention of leaving either.

speaker: Rust
content: So this is the situation. The sheriffs haven't cleaned up their mess, and the execs are acting too aggressively. Now, the entire Drifter Camp lacks trust in the DisCity authorities.
[Flashback to the 9-1 poacher]
You did get a glimpse of their tactics. Even the FAC couldn't look away, and the locals must be more disgusted. You're kind of getting caught in the crossfire.

speaker: Choice
options: Time is ticking. Need to be flexible.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: West District management is not what I should worry about. The primary goal is to get into Drifter Camp and look for clues about Parma, who is likely to carry a Corpus-level contamination source.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: There must be some connection between the two, and I need to gather as much information as possible.

speaker: Rust
content: You won't be welcome with that uniform, and I can't guarantee what you'll encounter. Chief, are you mentally prepared?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Of course. With you, the undercover agent, and the "insurance measure," how bad could it be?

speaker: Rust
content: ...Hehe, I'd rather not reveal my identity so early. If you encounter any problem, please consider using your personal charm to solve it first.

speaker: T04dRati0s: Ha, if they can make a killer fog outta this sand pit, that'll be a real urban legend. Legend Hunter R.C. [OP]: Ooooh a new urban legend!! Bring it on!! T04dRati0s: Bring on my ass...
content: The worst case scenario...
You roll your eyes and are about to say something when a violent explosion suddenly rocks the ground, stopping the car in its track.

Almost simultaneously, a young man in a cloak suddenly leaps out of the alleyway, hits the front of the car, and rolls to the side. Immediately thereafter, you hear a familiar gruff growl from the rear.

speaker: Executive Officer
content: It's gangsters. Confirm, there is a conflict between Drifter Camp and gangsters. Reporting it immediately and requesting backup.

speaker: Executive Officer
content: Request to enter Drifter Camp to investigate, repeat...
Before you can get out of the car to help, the young man stumbles to his feet and limps away into the misshapen narrow alleys of the slums without looking at you.

speaker: Hecate
content: ...Chief, what should I do?

speaker: Choice
options: Let's deal with the gangsters first.

content: So, is this some kind of trouble or an opportunity that can be seized?

speaker: Rust
content: Buzz... Buzz...

The connection to "Rust" is lost or interfered with. The executive officer is repairing communications to contact headquarters, while the young man has limped off in the direction of the Drifter Camp, with several gangsters chasing after him.
Thinking for a moment, you take a pistol out of the car, load it, and chase after him with the Sinners.

speaker: Hecate
content: The opponents can't be difficult to deal with, but we're unfamiliar with the terrain here, which can be a problem.

speaker: Hella
content: Where's the brat? The gangsters are coming for him. We could get him in the car and send him away first.

speaker: Hella
content: Huh? Wait, stop running! There are gangsters ahead!!! Hey!

speaker: Hecate
content: Chief, are you okay?
Getting a bit out of breath, you slow down the pace and take the opportunity to observe your surroundings.

There are signs of people living in the buildings on either side, but the doors and windows are locked, and some are even taped. Such preparations are obviously too adequate and too skilled for a sudden outbreak of an alley battle.

speaker: Hecate
content: He hasn't gone far. Something is not right, there are fewer gangsters, but we're not the ones doing it.

speaker: Hella
content: Stop right there!

speaker: Hella
content: The gangsters chasing you were all taken out by us, so stop running you little brat! Come down here and thank us!!!

The young man suddenly flips up the hanging ladder and leaps onto the rooftop. He sprints across buildings, tugging on the clotheslines from time to time. It's like he's simply showing off his parkour skills.
While Hella watches in awe, the young man hits an abrupt stop... Hecate's Nightmare has destroyed his path. He seems unable to see the Nightmare and is a little confused.
But you have seen what he's capable of. This is not a runaway with a limp. He could never have fallen into the hands of those violent hoodlums.

speaker: Hecate
content: Why did you pretend to run away when you had the power to deal with them?
The young man turns around, his face hidden in the shadows under his hood, and looks down at you.

speaker: Hecate
content: ...Are you trying to lure us somewhere? Where do you want to take us? Why are you doing this? Who are you?

speaker: Young Man
content: Sinners, you shouldn't be listening to their commands.

speaker: Young Man
content: Don't get in the way.
The young man crushes the tiles beneath his feet, and at the same time, the pipes around you suddenly burst, and a wave of air pushes you against the mud wall. Is it a trap?!

speaker: Hecate
content: Chief?!
Nightmare dumps the young man and rushes over to protect you, and before Hecate can reach you, another explosion comes from not far away. Sounds like the place you came from.

speaker: Hella
content: That direction is... where we got off?

speaker: Hecate
content: Watch out. There's an ambush.
Several Molotov cocktails are thrown down, detonating the oil tanks set up behind you, and the fire quickly blocks your way back.

speaker: Hecate
content: ...Is the Drifter Camp attacking DisCity authorities?

speaker: Young Man
content: We would never dare... Drifter Camp dares not to disobey the executive officers' management.

speaker: Young Man
content: But sadly, the beloved exec was caught and killed in the crossfire of a gang conflict. We were too late to the rescue...
More people emerge from the slum's buildings in all directions, all wearing the same cloak as the young man, with firearms in their hands.

speaker: Rust
content: Worst case scenario... You will be considered enemies. In the event of an attack, communications will be jammed, and then you will be trapped in some mechanism and surrounded by hostile units.

speaker: Rust
content: It's the self-organized forces of the Drifter Camp. They don't use Mania weapons, but their combat capability is excellent.

speaker: Rust
content: Be especially careful when fighting on their turf.

speaker: Hella
content: AHHHHH!!! What the **** was that?!

speaker: Hecate
content: It's a trap! Watch out!
A pipe sweeps head-on to Hella, she reflexively leans back to dodge it, but another one swings out from the other direction and sends her up in the air.
If Nightmare had not grabbed her in time, the regenerating Sinner would have fallen into the suddenly opened crypt below, and no one knows what awaits her there.

speaker: Hecate
content: This road is set up with traps? Is it the defense system of Drifter Camp?
Ten minutes ago.

speaker: Executive Officer
content: Headquarters, Headquarters! Requesting backup... requesting backup...

speaker: Rust
content: It seems that trouble has found us...

speaker: Rust
content: Established as self-defense in response to gang harassment, the Drifter Camp's forces don't pursue violent weapons, relying more on the complex terrain and traps to fight in local streets and alleys.

speaker: Rust
content: They don't have uniforms, but all tend to conceal themselves, preferring to wear cloaks and masks and act cautiously to avoid attracting unwanted attention.

speaker: Rust
content: Like Drifter Camp, these people have been struggling to survive. They are used to being oppressed, keeping a low profile, and holding back. Once such people raise their guns against you...

speaker: Rust
content: It must be a desperate situation for them, and there's no escaping for you.

speaker: Choice
options: Then there are two kinds of situations.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Do they want to kill me or capture me alive? I think the odds of the former are slim.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I have no dealings with them and have no power or intention to mess with the situation in West District. If they've come so far as to take it up to DisCity authorities, there are more suitable targets for assassination.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Instead, taking me hostage will give them some bargaining leverage.

speaker: Rust
content: Haha, haha... Why? Are you trying to pull that trick where you get kidnapped again? Please don't. That scary adjutant will have my head for this.

speaker: Rust
content: Don't try to infiltrate as a hostage. Even if they keep you alive, they will never take you back to their base. It is more likely that they will disguise themselves as gangsters and take you elsewhere to negotiate terms.

speaker: Rust
content: They would never risk leading the trouble back to Drifter Camp.

speaker: Choice
options: Then, will they  hand me over to Parma?

speaker: Rust
content: ...I can't rule that out, but I don't think they would. And...

speaker: Rust
content: I hope you are not asking this question with some wild expectations.

speaker: Choice
options: All right, I won't fall into their hands.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Let them take me for a walk. I'll play my part, and I trust you to come to the rescue—our undercover agent, the "insurance measure."

speaker: Rust
content: Hehe... I shouldn't have called you back.

speaker: Rust
content: Don't worry. I'm already on my way. Langley has instructed me to assist you, so I will.

speaker: Rust
content: But until then, the communication between us will be cut off. Please play it safe, don't make things unmanageable, and get killed before I arrive...

speaker: Rust
content: As long as you can survive, I will send you to Drifter Camp as promised.

speaker: Hella
content: Ouch... This **** is more annoying than MBCC!

speaker: Choice
options: Calm down. These are all ordinary traps.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: There is no contamination, and they're not as powerful as Mania weapons. Just figure out the patterns and don't get hit.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: We won't be beaten by those.
You look at the young man in the front, who's not limping or trembling anymore. He could make a good actor, and they've planned a big game to catch you.
Then the game is on. You should stall for as long as possible and try to figure out the intentions of Drifter Camp.

speaker: Hecate
content: Nightmare!
Nightmare roars and uses its two huge claws to tackle the young man, lifting him into the air. It then leaps down and brings him to you.

speaker: Young Man
content: What?!
The young man is shocked. He tries to break free from the bonds, kicking his legs in the air to escape what is holding him. But there's no aim for his kicks since he can't see the Nightmare at all.
You calm the raging Nightmare and walk up to the young man with a tight grip on your pistol.
His associates also stop attacking, as you expected. From their astonished expressions, it's clear that they can't see the Nightmare either.
...These are ordinary people who have not been corrupted by Mania and have not indulged in violence. In Syndicate, such people are a minority.

speaker: Choice
options: I have no intention of making an enemy of Drifter Camp.

content: He remains quiet without looking up, and the cloak obscures his expression.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: We're not gangsters, and we're not with the Reconstruction Executive Committee. I'm just here to investigate the potential Mania crisis and track down the possible contamination source.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The situation may be worse than imagined, and time is running out. I need to enter Drifter Camp to investigate, and I also need your cooperation and help.

speaker: Young Man
content: ...I know. You're the Chief of the Minos Bureau of Crisis Control.

speaker: Young Man
content: No interest in power and no intention to interfere with the freedom of the West District. You just want to eliminate the Mania contamination and help Syndicans...

speaker: Young Man
content: Hehe... Have you said the same thing to the <color=#fb9259>Legion</color>?
You are taken aback, and the teenager looks up slightly, so you can see the face under the hood.
It's the young man stealing Hypercubes from the ruins of 004!

speaker: Choice
options: Did you enter the Ring area to spy on me?

speaker: Young Man
content: I've heard about you, the <color=#fb9259>friend</color> of the Legion, the <color=#fb9259>friend</color> of Zoya, and the <color=#fb9259>friend</color> of the Syndicate.

speaker: Young Man
content: No... You are the commander of the Sinners, the holder of the shackles, the hero of DisCity who destroyed the Black Ring and put down the rebellion in West District... and the lapdog of authorities.

speaker: Young Man
content: Zoya was supposed to be the leader of Syndicate, strong, bold, wise, and charismatic. She was supposed to be the powerful presence that breaks the shackles and gives us a future.

speaker: Young Man
content: But she believed you, went to that negotiation, and died on the charge of "Mania" in Keylan Square. Then they hunted down the remaining Legionnaires.
No, Zoya is alive. The shackles are not broken. The connection feels weak, and there's no telling where she is, but you're sure she's alive.
The Legion is also still around. The 9th Agency has wiped out the Burns remnants and sent the surviving Legionnaires to WhiteSands for refuge, so they won't be used as scapegoats.
You know that the truth must be kept secret, but you never imagined that BR-004 ended this way in the eyes of Syndicans. How should you explain this?
But the young man in front of you isn't waiting for an answer. He sneers and suddenly shouts...

speaker: Young Man
content: Now!

Bang, bang, bang!!! A dozen flashing bullets hit the ground near you and release the blue light of Hypercubes. The two Sinners freeze in place as a few lasso shots bounce off the ground and silver light flashes wrap around them.

speaker: Hecate
content: Anti-Mania shots... Ah!!!
With only this momentary break, the bullets suddenly burst open, releasing several metal wires and wrapping around the Sinners. Under the electric flashes, both of them show painful expressions.
Immediately after, the other end of the wire is yanked up, throwing them up and into separate cages. Then, cloaked people give them each an injection, robbing them of their strength.
All this took no more than 10 seconds.

speaker: Armed Personnel
content: Stop struggling! Are you addicted to being a lapdog?

speaker: Hecate
content: Let... let... the Chief go...
So this young man in front of you is not a hostage but a bait to make you drop your guard!
You instinctively raise your hand to release the Potestas, but the shackles do not respond. Instead, a sharp pain stabs through your temples.

...Right, this is not the Black Ring, and the mental contamination is not dense enough. The opponents in front of you are <color=#fb9259>ordinary people</color> who have not been corrupted by Mania. Your shackles won't work.

speaker: Young Man
content: I thought you had something special if you were able to defeat Zoya... Guess it was just vile lies.
As the young man gets up and approaches you, you reflexively raise your gun and aim it at him.

speaker: Young Man
content: Shoot me!
The young man doesn't stop. He comes straight up and puts his forehead against your gun.

speaker: Armed Personnel
content: Taran?! What are you doing?!

speaker: Taran
content: Go on, Do it! Just like how you killed those two.

speaker: Taran
content: I will never assume any good in you, and the Syndicate should not assume any good in you. Pull the trigger!
He and you glare at each other, and in his eyes, you see no fear of death but only a cold awareness accompanied by a certain frantic expectation.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Pay for your actions, as you wish!
There's no need to restrain your anger. You swing the gun across his mocking eyes and aim in between. The moment you pull the trigger, you see him smiling...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Don't try to provoke me. Let them go. I came here for a discussion, not a showdown!

speaker: Taran
content: Stop with your big talk. You're not fooling anyone!
Bang! Bang, bang, bang!!!
Gunshots ring out, and you lose control of your body. A great pain comes from your back, shoulders, and waist...
Someone approaches from behind with decisive steps. One shot with each step, the bullets shoot into your body.
You don't get to turn around. Something hangs not far behind your head, and you hear the last shot:
A burst of electricity paralyzes your brain from behind, your sight goes white, and the last thing you hear is Hecate's scream.
Your consciousness is trapped in darkness, prostrating in the mud. Your body feels heavy, like a million chaotic creatures are tangling behind you, dragging you backward.
You failed. This body is so huge, and a burning pain comes from your waist, but you can't feel anything from there on down.
<color=#7683a2>It's... not over yet...</color>
You seem to be moaning, making a sound you are unfamiliar with. The sound is like steel needles scraping across your throat, painful but unstoppable. It's as if you have to keep struggling to live.
<color=#7683a2>...Don't want to die... I... don't want to die...</color>

You struggle to reach your hands forward. Your arms are withered and weak, and your palms are burning with pain, oozing out lava-like filth. It falls on the ground, making a sizzling sound and scorching your nerves.

One step and another... You wail as you reach forward, draging your heavy body across the floor. Something keeps flowing out of the lower half of your senseless body, from which wild monsters gush out. That's your lost life force.
But you don't stop.
Climbing over ditches and hills, crushing everything you pass along the way. You hear a distinct obsession gradually becoming frantic, pulling you forward.
Need to go somewhere and find something, need to...
<color=#7683a2>Live... I need to... live...</color>
...Kill her!!!

Just as your consciousness is about to be torn apart, a strange musical sound splits the darkness, followed by a flash of blue light that cuts through the madness and breaks the foul chaos that traps you...

Your eyes snap open. You are lying on your back, still surrounded by darkness, but the fire and the scorch marks are gone. Only the sensation remains, your back, the back of your head, and the shackles on your hands are all burning with pain.
But the mental chaos has subsided, and you can't help but reach into your pocket—the blue Hypercube fragment is there.
The shackles are responsive, and that... was not a dream, but an omen, a revelation. You've seen the lava-like scorch marks, the very source of the contamination you're chasing.
Whatever induced BR-004's anomaly stopped here.
But where is here?

speaker: Rust
content: You're finally awake.

speaker: Rust
content: Shh, don't talk, and don't move. Check your surroundings first. Is there anyone else around?

You calm down, hold your breath and try to perceive your surroundings... You are trapped in a small rectangular space, and with the help of a shimmering light falling from above, you can tell it is not very high.

You can feel your heart beating, thump, thump... About a minute passes by, and through that gap occasionally comes the sound of airflow, as clearly audible as your heartbeat... This place is quiet, dim, and cold inside and out.

speaker: Rust
content: There doesn't seem to be anyone else around, so you're safe.

speaker: Rust
content: How are you feeling? I heard that the Chief is not in good physical condition lately. The suspended animation lasted 2 hours, and there could be side effects.

Indeed, the places where the "bullets" hit still hurt a little. You thought they would crack your bones, but now it seems... fine. Except for the fake plasma on your clothes, that feels a little nasty.
You recall the scene where he "shot" you in front of everyone.

speaker: Choice
options: I'm surprised no one saw through your little trick.

speaker: Rust
content: Don't underestimate the little toys of an agent. It was quite shocking to see your head explode, plus the reaction of the two Sinners there...

speaker: Rust
content: Don't worry. No one will suspect a thing. That Hecate girl almost blew me away through the cage. It doesn't get any better than that. Though it was a bit of a struggle to save them after that.

speaker: Rust
content: Anyway, the plan went well, Chief, and you have now infiltrated the funeral home at the bottom of the Drifter Camp. Your Sinners are also on their way here.

speaker: Rust
content: As long as they can reunite with you before you are pushed into the crematorium, there won't be a problem, probably.
Back in the car...

speaker: Choice
options: Is there a way to infiltrate the place and investigate?

speaker: Rust
content: The risk is high, but there is indeed a way.

speaker: Rust
content: There is a private funeral home at the bottom of the Drifter Camp. Regardless of your stand, faction, Maniac or not... as long as you die in the territory of the Drifter Camp, you will be taken in and buried.

speaker: Rust
content: Yes, if, unfortunately, there happens to be a conflict, just play it out in front of them. I can meet you halfway.

speaker: Rust
content: As long as I can stop your vital signs on the spot, they won't do anything more to you. Your body already belongs to the funeral home.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Sounds good. I'm already familiar with kidnapping plays. Guess it will be fun to try a new script this time.

speaker: Rust
content: Oh, right, please keep this a secret from your adjutant.
Now, feeling your sore muscles, you regret not spending more time blending in with a disguise.

speaker: Rust
content: Well, the enemies of the Drifter Camp are thinking of the same thing. They've caught several "acting personnel" and tightened up entrance checks recently, so it's not so easy to go undercover.

speaker: Rust
content: Well... the risk has indeed increased. So I'll be keeping a low profile from here, and there will be very little help I can give you.

speaker: Rust
content: Don't try to find me, either. Any "agreement" between you and me will only increase the risk of exposure.

speaker: Rust
content: Haha, sorry, it's not that serious. I have already taken care of everything that should be done, and there will be more suitable people to assist you in the investigation in Drifter Camp. I will step in if it's really necessary.

speaker: Rust
content: Now that you've entered the Drifter Camp, have you sensed anything about the "Corpus"?

speaker: Choice
options: It's been here but has left.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The shackles are very sensitive to their presence, but now it's calm. Parma and his inheritance are no longer in Drifter Camp.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I don't know if this is a good or bad thing.

speaker: Rust
content: It's a good thing. The population density here is very high, and it will be hard to control the situation. We can relax for a while, at least.

speaker: Rust
content: Take this as a starting point and continue the investigation. You can still find out what "the thing" did here and what Parma did.

speaker: Rust
content: Someone will be along shortly to assist you, but be careful. The attack just now was aimed at you, and they seemed to know you well.

speaker: Rust
content: I'm not sure where the info is from, but it will be used against you. Remember, from now on, do not reveal your identity or the fact that you are still alive.

speaker: Rust
content: Drifter Camp may not be your enemy, but they're definitely not your friend.
It reminds you of the conflict you just had, the gun pointed at the young man and his frantic and cold eyes behind it. Although the plan was already in place, you really faltered at that moment.

speaker: Choice
options: You arrived just in time. Thank you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: One second later, he would have died in my hands... Were you trying to stop me?

speaker: Rust
content: Yes. If you shot him, the Drifter Camp and DisCity authorities would be entirely at war, which would be disastrous.

speaker: Choice
options: They should've seen that coming before the assault.

speaker: Rust
content: <size=30>That's not the same, Chief. If you were killed, the incident would have become "the remaining gangsters tried to disrupt the negotiations between the Drifter Camp and DisCity authorities, and the negotiators were all killed in the line of duty, sorrowful tribute."</size>

speaker: Rust
content: But if it's the other way around, "DisCity officials shot and killed Drifter young man," and the news spread, it would no longer be a trivial matter...

speaker: Rust
content: The radicals are only a minority, and most drifters are civilians. But if a particular line is crossed, there is no coming back.

speaker: Choice
options: Do you think I made the wrong choice?

speaker: Rust
content: ...There aren't any right or wrong choices for many things, Chief. Make your choice and keep walking. You can't stop, even if there are sacrifices.

speaker: Rust
content: And the final destination you reach will determine whether the price paid along the way is worth it.
The communication is cut, and you're back in the dark. You can feel the Sinners getting closer on the other end of the shackles, but they will probably take a while.
Before that, you struggle to raise your hand and push the wooden board covering you.
The board wouldn't budge.
Are you too weak after the suspended animation? Or is the wooden box nailed shut?
The corners can be lifted, and you realize that something heavy is pressed into the center of the board.
Is it another wooden box? Many gangsters must have died in that fight just now. It's not too heavy, but you really don't have the strength now, so you decide to lie there and rest.
Instead of making a scene, it's safer to wait for your strength to return or for the Sinners to follow the shackles and find you.
As you ponder, a soft laugh comes from above the wooden box.
Hehe... Giving up so soon?
Someone is out there?!
Oh? Holding your breath again? Aren't you the one talking big, faking your own death just now?
Come one. Make a reasonable offer, and I'll open the lid and resurrect you!
A girl's voice comes from above the board, and you realize she's sitting on it to keep you from getting out. And she's been there since before you woke up!
She must have heard everything you said, and there's no use pretending to be dead. You check for your pistol, but it's not there.

You push again, but nothing happens. Should you try your chance with the Potestas? But without seeing the situation, you could be in trouble if you consume too much of your sanity and there are others outside.
Huh? Where's your offer? Do you want my help or not? You need to work really hard alone to come back from the dead.
Want something to cheer you up?

It's... the sound you heard in the chaos!

Whatever induced BR-004's anomaly stopped here.
But where is here?

content: I wanted to see what your fantastic plan was, but there wasn't enough time. When you were hesitating, someone else had already raised a gun and aimed at the back of your head.

speaker: Rust
content: No. You'd have fallen for their trap if you had shot the kid. The relationship with Drifter Camp would be entirely down the drain, and the Syndicate would face a new riot... Your patience was remarkable...

speaker: Rust
content: It's just you may be used to more surreal battles that are more direct and brutal, but combat with humans is a whole other level of dangerous.

speaker: Rust
content: You have to get used to the cruelty in reality.

speaker: Choice
options: Do you think I made the wrong choice?

It's... the sound you heard in the chaos!
The song ends, and the shrill sound makes you dizzy.
How's that? Are you awake? My suona is unmatched, so you must feel refreshed and delighted.
What you just heard is worth 10,000 DisCoins. So pay up!
Don't try to change the subject! What Sinner? I saved you, and you need to pay up.
Or... are you thinking about using those red spikes on me. You don't want to pay me?!
She knows about the shackles?! Are you exposed?

speaker: Choice
options: I don't want to hurt you.
I don't know what you're talking about.

content: Haha, haha! Liar, you just don't want a war with Drifter Camp.
Haha, haha, so pretentious! Aren't you here to make peace with Drifter Camp? Now, where's your peace offering?
I know what you're thinking, "She's the only one here. No one will know. I can do whatever I want... blast the board off with Potestas and use the shackles on her!"
You can sense through the shackles that the Sinners are getting closer. You stop being led by her little tricks and begin to stall.

speaker: Choice
options: Where did you learn about me?

content: Hmph... I am the all-knowing, the past, the future, everything there is!
You woke up not long ago, destroyed BR-004, wiped out the Corpseborne, and took out the two leaders of the Legion.

speaker: Choice
options: I'm not an enemy of the Legion.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: They are my friends. I tried to save them and failed. But I don't want to fail a second time.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I have come to stop those who seek to harm Syndicans, and I am not your enemy.
Hmph... I know that too.
The Legion doesn't hate you. In their eyes, you're a friend, a good person, and you've done your best.
She says this with some tenderness.
The murmuring gets closer. It's like a hand caressing you through the cold board.
They said it themselves... It's the last message they left to this world... Want to know what they said?
It carries you, steadfast, through the rain of cinders.
Okay, okay, that's enough talking. You won't be getting another word from me without paying the bill.
Just as she's having fun, there's a boom, followed by a whirring sound. Something is blown away, rolling around on the ground.
The board suddenly gets lighter. You easily push it open and sit up, but the dim light dazzles your eyes. At the same time, you hear a familiar voice...

speaker: Hecate
content: Chief!
The Nightmare leaps straight down from a high place with Hecate in its palms, stopping between you and the person knocked aside. You breathe a sigh of relief.

speaker: Hecate
content: She got trapped.

speaker: Hecate
content: Don't worry, she's fine. I'll go back and untie her when we get this sorted out.
Sitting next to the wooden box is a girl in strange attire. She rubs her head and gets up, still clutching a peculiar instrument.

speaker: Strange Girl
content: Woah... Why so aggressive? I was just joking with him, okay?
female_content: Woah... Why so aggressive? I was just joking with her, okay?

speaker: Strange Girl
content: I don't really want to fight you. It's not like I have the power. I just wanted to join the fun, so don't get mad, okay?

speaker: Strange Girl
content: Didn't you say you wanted a talk with the Drifter Camp? I'll help you.

speaker: Choice
options: I don't want to talk to you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The plan has changed. Now I have to hide my identity. And you know too much, Sinner.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You know too much, and you've crossed the line, Sinner.

speaker: Hecate
content: Should we capture her?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Just need to put shackles on her. I can't trust her, and we need to keep her quiet.

speaker: Hecate
content: Got it.

speaker: Strange Girl
content: Haha, can't get a deal and want to get rough? Not going to work!
She blows the instrument in her hand violently, and the piercing waves of sound actually repel the attacking Nightmare for a moment, echoing in the midst of this towering patio.

You and Hecate are a little shaken for a moment. The echoes are slow to subside... No, it's not a constant echo, it's people coming from all directions. You hurriedly take off your Bureau jacket and carry it in your arms.

speaker: Hecate
content: ...The Drifter Camp Force?! Are we exposed?
She leans to the side to avoid a pan that spins down from upstairs.

speaker: Resident
content: So noisy!!! Shattered my cooking pot!

speaker: Resident
content: Dudu, what is it this time?!
The girl called Dudu chuckles.

speaker: Dudu
content: Want to catch me? Do you know where you are? This is my turf.
She suddenly cranes her neck and shouts...

speaker: Dudu
content: Help! Intruders! Intruders are attacking Drifter Camp!!!

speaker: Hecate
content: These are ordinary civilians, and even with combat experience, they can't be difficult to deal with, but...
More people are gathering, and although they can't see the Nightmare, the Sinner's power has clearly aroused suspicion.

speaker: Hecate
content: Chief, we're attracting too much unwanted attention.

speaker: Dudu
content: Hehe, just double the payment for hush money now, and I'll help you cover this up. I'll even throw in a complimentary tune...

speaker: Dudu
content: Coming up next... Good Day!
She laughs and actually picks up the suona again to play a tune.
Let him go...!
female_content: Let her go...!

content: Thump! A shadow falls from the sky and smashes heavily into the ground. It's a person wearing a hood, and on closer inspection...
She maintains a handsome pose on one knee, silent, cold, and stolid, like a monument, attracting everyone's attention. Ten, twenty seconds, everyone holds their breath to keep the silence.

speaker: K.K.
content: Um... ${PlayerName}...

speaker: K.K.
content: Give me a hand...

speaker: K.K.
content: I jumped down too fast, and my feet are numb...
You rush forward to help her up. The Sinner with a superb tolerance for pain is actually grimacing a little.

speaker: K.K.
content: I've been waiting here to meet up with you. Adjutant Nightingale heard of your plans and came to me. I used to live in Drifter Camp before you caught me.

speaker: Hecate
content: No restraints, no trackers, she just put you back in an uncontrolled area... What was Adjutant Nightingale thinking? Wasn't she afraid you would escape?

speaker: K.K.
content: ...Let's deal with the trouble at hand first.
She turns to face the residents holding pots and pans in their hands, who finally come around and start yelling.

speaker: Angry Middle-aged Man
content: Now you're back?! That Whitestone boss of yours... Had drinks at my place for months and never paid a nickel! I want my money back!

speaker: Howling Woman
content: You people agreed to pay for ads this month but vanished last week. Do you know how many punches I got for putting up ads for your?! Pay up!

speaker: Vengeful Man
content: Hey, why are you siding with the intruders? Can't pay us back, so you're selling Drifter Camp out?!

speaker: Gentle Old Man
content: K.K., I know you are a good child. It must have been difficult for you... You can tell me about it...

speaker: Gentle Old Man
content: But do you remember... August 13 last year, my grandson's birthday, I ordered an Eastside smuggled cake from the south, and you still haven't delivered... Can I get a refund?

speaker: K.K.
content: Well... Um...
The girl with pink twin ponytails leaps and gives K.K. a big hug.

speaker: Dudu
content: You should have told me! I thought he was a debt collector. But is this another one you've tricked, um, is this another investor? Great!
female_content: You should have told me! I thought she was a debt collector. But is this another one you've tricked, um, is this another investor? Great!

speaker: Dudu
content: Oh, neighbors, don't worry! For the past six months, Whitestone didn't go bankrupt and run away. K.K. has been looking for a way to save the company, and now she's finally found it!
She turns around and points at you.

speaker: Dudu
content: This is not an intruder. He's a rich guy from the Outlands, and the Sinner next to him is a bodyguard he hired at a heavy price, so don't mess with them again for your safety.
female_content: This is not an intruder. She's a rich gal from the Outlands, and the Sinner next to her is a bodyguard she hired at a heavy price, so don't mess with them again for your safety.

speaker: Dudu
content: He came here to invest in the business opportunities of the redevelopment of West District, and we were discussing investment in Whitestone Industries for the future of Syndicate!
female_content: She came here to invest in the business opportunities of the redevelopment of West District, and we were discussing investment in Whitestone Industries for the future of Syndicate.

speaker: Dudu
content: Right, K.K.? Good job!

speaker: K.K.
content: Yeah, yeah... no matter what those two at Whitestone owe you, K.K. will pay it back!
People begin whispering to each other, but you can see K.K.'s ears reddening a bit under the hood. And some people are looking at you with sympathy in their eyes.

speaker: Dudu
content: Hehe... Sorry, nice neighbors, turns out it was a misunderstanding. K.K.'s friends are my friends. Don't get mad. Just go back to your dinner!

speaker: Dudu
content: Or, how about a little tune for your appetite?
As the girl picks up her beloved... suona? People drop their doubts and scatter, leaving the few of you there.
Dudu is still holding K.K., smiling but not saying anything.

speaker: K.K.
content: ...Okay, okay... Put it on my tab. I owe you a lot more, anyway.
Lying in public seems to have drained all of K.K.'s strength, and with one hand covering her blushing face, she breathlessly answers Hecate's question.

speaker: K.K.
content: I won't run away... I need to get you back to MBCC to complete the commission. Adjutant Nightingale promised a commission fee... and I have to get it.

speaker: K.K.
content: ...I just went back to the store to check. Those two already owe 8 months of rent and utilities, and the door is sealed... So...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Back to the point. Do you know this Sinner?

speaker: K.K.
content: You mean Dudu?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I need to know what's going on and what to do about it.

speaker: K.K.
content: Sigh... You'd better pay the hush money. She's an honest businesswoman, at least. It'll cost a lot, but the Bureau will reimburse you, right?

speaker: K.K.
content: I really don't want a commission to catch my neighbor.

speaker: Dudu
content: Oh? Do you want to pay up now? Okay, let's do the math.
She pulls out an abacus and starts to count.

speaker: Dudu
content: There's faking your death, your Bureau identity, the shackle, helping you explain just now, and... Oh! And 10 great suona tunes...

speaker: Choice
options: Wait, when did I get 10 songs?

speaker: Dudu
content: When you were lying unconscious in that little box, I played a long, long song to wake you up. It's all because of my healing song that you don't have any broken bones or concussions! Count yourself lucky that I'm only charging you for 10 songs.

speaker: Dudu
content: All right! That's 20,000 DisCoins in total!
You hear K.K. draw a cold breath and see her grimace at you. Dudu, on the other hand, looks at you with a smug, condescending expression.

speaker: Dudu
content: No, no deal! Aren't you with the authorities? Why are you so cheap?

speaker: Dudu
content: No, no, this is the best deal you'll get. I'd lose too much otherwise, so take it or leave it!

speaker: Choice - 1
options: 17,500, I'll get an advance on next month's salary.

speaker: Dudu
content: 19,500! My last offer! A friendly price for K.K.! No more bargaining! Countdown to three seconds to close the deal. Three... One!
Poor Syndicate. Prices really are ridiculously low here.
You are about to feel sorry for the low prices of Syndicate when Dudu shows a sly expression.

speaker: Dudu
content: Oh, I almost forgot. The economy has been tough lately, and we have to multiply the inflation factor...
No more, no more. You have my word.

speaker: Choice
options: One more question, and you can charge me extra for this.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You do know a lot. Where did you hear those things? Tell me, and I'll pay you whatever you want.
Dudu's smile stiffens for a moment, and she looks at you with alarm.

speaker: Dudu
content: Huh...? I am all-knowing.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If you were all-knowing, we wouldn't have run into so many accidents. You must have heard about me in advance, but where?

speaker: Dudu
content: Hmph... You can't afford the answer, and I'm not putting a price on it.
You step forward. If it's necessary... even in someone else's territory, you will use force.
But you suddenly feel a chill brush across the back of your neck. This is an extremely deep patio, and there shouldn't be any wind.
A dozen meters away, the walls seem to get darker. From the outline, however, it's a modest one-story bungalow with a long chimney at the back.
A door opens, and a woman leans against the door frame, looking at you.

speaker: Woman in the Shadow
content: Oppression or death... You always assume secrets can be kept by such means.
