content: Then again, if even Julien, the most paranoid person in the camp, is willing to team with you, the others will gradually understand and accept you too. Don't worry.
She knows how to gain the trust from others. Hella probably can't resist her moves either. But you're not in the mood to hear all this. You only want to leave as soon as possible.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: We're only cooperating and getting what we need from each other. You don't need to comfort me.
When you finish, you pick up the bowl of bean soup and down it. Behind the bowl, after a brief silence, she suddenly laughs.

speaker: Lavina
content: Didn't expect you to be a stubborn kid too.
<size=44>?</size>

speaker: Lavina
content: Deep down, you're feeling aggrieved, but you just swallow that feeling and continues to do your job. Has this happened to you often?
Before you retort, her eyes dim.

speaker: Lavina
content: My kid was about your age when she left.
You swallow the words before they escape your mouth. Even if it's just acting, the sadness in her eyes is too infectious. You can't bring yourself to say it.

speaker: Options
options: ...Was it the Executive Committee? Or the sheriffs?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That's why you joined Rustfire...?

speaker: Lavina
content: Don't overthink. It has nothing to do with people on your side. It was many years ago. I've long gotten over it.
She pauses and stands up to get the coffee. She also grabs some sugar cubes for you and sets them on the side.

speaker: Lavina
content: I joined Rustfire to be the mother of more kids. Like you, they all don't know how to take care of themselves. My work is never done.

speaker: Options
options: ...Thank you for taking care of me.

speaker: Lavina
content: ...No. You're neither my child nor our companion.

speaker: Lavina
content: Thank you.

speaker: Lavina
content: They had an urgent assembly today, saying they had to fight against a monster. I heard explosions and gunshots. The depot was in ruins and fire was blazing... Julien told me to prepare for the worst, I thought...
Her hands holding the coffee cup begin trembling.

speaker: Lavina
content: No matter your identity, stance, and purpose... You showed up and protected us.

speaker: Lavina
content: No outsiders have ever stayed for us, and even now, you're still straining yourself to keep working.

speaker: Lavina
content: I didn't lose anyone else, and it's all thanks to you. Regardless of what the others say, I'm... <size=40>truly grateful</size> to you.

speaker: Lavina
content: The second sentence of the post-episode, no background
The first sentence of the post-episode, no background
...It finally tastes like something.

speaker: (Scene change)
content: (Scene change)
When you walk out of the duty room, the logistics officer shoves several more wraps at you and returns to her usual kind and somewhat strict self.
Hella is staring in a certain direction with Hecate, wielding her pipe and cursing.

speaker: Hella
content: It's that jerk that abducted us! He was following us. Who knows what he's up to this time.

speaker: Lavina
content: Oh, Taran? He got scolded by Julien. He's probably holding his temper and has come here to be your bodyguard. That kid's quite skillful in operating mechanisms. He could be useful.

speaker: Hecate
content: I don't trust him. He's hostile toward Chief.

speaker: Lavina
content: He's just stubborn. Don't mind him, and don't waste your energy on him. Once his seniors from the elite squad are back, someone will deal with him.
You look at Taran. He can't hear your shouts from where he stands, so Hella's cursing doesn't do much. But he should be able to see your hands clearly, perhaps you can sign something at him...

speaker: Options
options: Wag your index finger to mock him
Be a reasonable adult and leave him alone

content: You're not sure if he sees your sign. Anyway, he turns to leave once you're done.
You'll teach him a lesson when your work is done.

speaker: Hella & Hecate
content:
Pff.
Hmm?

speaker: Lavina
content: Hahaha. Let's go.
You can't see Taran's reaction clearly, but from the way the pink-haired fighter next to him holds down his shoulders... the kid's likely mad.
You leave contentedly. You have business to tend to. You'll come back to this later.

speaker: Lavina
content: Where do you want to go for your investigation next? Want me to show you those executive officers' messages?
Your body is warming up again. Your stuffed chest is slowly relaxing. The stuck cogs in your brain begin turning gradually. You start thinking again and clues are finally popping up in your head.

speaker: Options
options: No need. It has nothing to do with them.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Both the grievance-loaded executive officers and the shocking, terrifying contamination are all just tricks used by the mastermind behind to aggravate you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: They're not done yet. Once they use up all the executive officers, they'll switch to another type of performance.
As you speak, you hear a clamor mixed with moans and cries for help from a distance. Lavina's communications device sounds.

speaker: Lavina
content: What? Corruptor outbreaks in multiple locations? This...
Before she can react, a gust of moldy-smelling wind sweeps over the garden you're in. A pitch-black flame ignites fear instantly.
The shadow in the flame is still wiggling and is hard to clear. The Rustfire members coming to help are already ashen-faced.

speaker: Armed Personnel
content: What's that thing?! Is it also a trap by the Executive Committee?

speaker: Options
options: Just smoke and mirrors. Stay away from it.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Whatever you hear and see, don't think too much about it. Know how to suppress your emotions? Protect yourselves and those around you!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Make everyone go back inside. Now...
Before you finish, the flame suddenly dwindles. Surprisingly, you see a pitch-black human shape. He stops struggling and makes a shrill roar abruptly. It's a terrifying laugh.
The windows in the whole alley shatter. You hear miserable cries from inside the buildings.
As if petrified, Lavina drops the communications device, shattering it. Hella gets hold of her in time, fearing she may be the next one to break.

speaker: Hella
content: Lavina? Lavina? ****! This is what happens when you don't get used to beating people up. ${PlayerName}, think of something!

Before it lets out another wave of screams, several bolts of blue light flash by. Metal wires are shot from the beams, entangling the wiggling shadow. Next, an enormous mechanical arm spins and smashes down, crushing it into the ground.

speaker: Hecate
content: It's a mechanism. Is Rustfire helping us?
Meanwhile, your communications device sounds.

speaker: Julien
content: Did you get attacked?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But it's not fatal. After all, it's not their goal to spread contamination, but to incite fear. People will be more susceptible to a different kind of Mania trap if their minds are weakened by this.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: They don't need a disguise anymore.
From the crack smashed open on the ground, black flames spill out slowly and flow upward, eventually gathering at the tip of the metal ball and forming a familiar figure.

speaker: Man In Raincoat
content: It's you... It's you... You think you can glimpse it, you think you can escape...

speaker: Man In Raincoat
content: Useless... It's useless... Mere worms, mere ants... will burn to ashes in the end...

It smiles menacingly and raises its hand. That nauseating mark emerges once again, and black flames begin blazing. Its voice grows loud suddenly, piercing the walls and ceilings, shaking the floors of the buildings.

speaker: Man In Raincoat
content: Look at me... Look at me!!

speaker: Man In Raincoat
content: Let us witness... its return!!!
This battle is over. But it's merely the start of a bigger crisis.
In this interconnected Drifter Camp, the echoes travel in every direction, announcing the spread of the chaos.

speaker: Julien
content: Multiple locations in the Drifter Camp saw Corruptor derangement. The commercial district, water station, residential area, and clinic are all highly populated spots.

speaker: Julien
content: There haven't been severe casualties so far, but many people have suffered mental shock. They may trip into Mania if their minds are not stabilized soon.

speaker: Julien
content: Lavina, get it together. We need you.
Ashen-faced, the red-haired woman trembles all over. Her body remains stiff for a while before she finally answers.

speaker: Lavina
content: ...Got it, I'll get to work right away.

speaker: Options
options: Should we evacuate the Drifter Camp?

speaker: Julien
content: ...It'll be very difficult. I'll do what I can.

speaker: Julien
content: And you? Are you going to continue your investigation?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'll find the Corpus and destroy it. Now that we're sure it's their scheme, I can't just let it be.

speaker: Julien
content: ...I see.
He seems to have shifted to another communications device. The voice sounds distant.

speaker: Julien
content: Taran, you're nearby, aren't you? Do you have a map?

speaker: Julien
content: Give it to him.
female_content: Give it to her.

content: Lavina is shocked a bit by his words, and an even stronger protest comes from the other end of the device.

speaker: Julien
content: This is an order. You want to let your temper get the best of you again?

speaker: Lavina
content: Julien, I'll go.
She leaves. Soon, she comes back with a booklet and puts it in your hands carefully.

speaker: Lavina
content: This is an internal map of the Drifter Camp. It includes all the mechanisms, hidden passages, and passcodes. Elite squad clearance.

speaker: Lavina
content: Not many people in the camp have been to school, so Julien has made it as simple as possible. If you can't understand it, I can come with you.
You flip through it. Although the information is packed and diverse, it's organized and clear, each function and mechanism properly categorized.

speaker: Options
options: Don't worry, I can read it. There are others who need you more.

speaker: Julien
content: I'll try to keep in touch and give you the necessary instructions while commanding the others.

speaker: Julien
content: Now, go to elevator E7 and head to level 28 east. I've granted you access, and the key is written in the map. Just use it directly.

speaker: Options
options: Should I search for the black raincoats from there?

speaker: Julien
content: No searching needed. In all the areas detected with abnormal M-values, only that place is desolate, but that's where several <color=#fb9259>men in black raincoats</color> appeared.

speaker: Julien
content: If he decided to go all out, I figure this could be a chance to catch his weakness.

speaker: Julien
content: Level 28 east is highly contaminated to the point it's seriously interfering with the <color=#fb9259>anti-Mania monitoring system</color>. Once you're up there, I can't give you any more precise locations, and this communication device may not work either.

speaker: Julien
content: If you need me, look for the communication terminals on the map. They have some anti-Mania effect and dial straight to my office. But there aren't that many of them, you'll have to rely on yourself most of the time.
You come to elevator E7 under Lavina's guidance. The upcoming battles must be even more dangerous. You won't let her come with you, so the map does offer great help. But you've still got a question.

speaker: Options
options: Are you sure about giving me the map?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I suppose this is top secret to you. I recall that one of the objectives of the Executive Committee's infiltration into the camp is to scout the internal structure, so that they can breach this place.

speaker: Julien
content: You won't cause us any issues.
He says firmly. A moment later, he adds.

speaker: Julien
content: ...When it's all over, be sure to return it.
The smile has returned to Lavina's face. She shoves a few Hypercubes in your hands along with a fancy little box. You smell a weird fragrance.

speaker: Lavina
content: An outland essence oil to help you freshen up. Just now when I fetched the map, a friend wanted me to bring this to you. He wished to help, but was too shy to give it to you himself.
There's a hint of delight in her smile. You look back and find Greta peeking this way from the end of the alley. He hides back as soon as he sees you turn.
You wave in Greta's direction and bid farewell to the two from Rustfire. The elevator is here.

It's an open platform with an iron gate. When the gate opens, a handful of Rustfire members in protective cloaks carrying guns exit hurriedly to leave the elevator to the three of you. The gate shuts and the platform goes up.

speaker: Hella
content: Ugh... This place looks huge, where do we even start...

speaker: Hecate
content: Chief, this is...
Something is stuck on the button of level 28. You peel it off and find that it's a memo. You open it and find only one word written on it.
Shackles

You freeze for a moment and begin sensing subconsciously... Indeed, somewhere above, someone connected to you through the shackles is there. It's K.K. What's happening to her there? Who's this person that left you this message...
You quickly peer down. The people who got out of the elevator haven't gone too far. As if sensing your gaze, one of them suddenly stops and looks back.
The cloak conceals his figure and you can't see his face clearly. He makes a gun with his hand and points it at you, shooting once silently.

speaker: Hecate
content: Ah, it's that person. The undercover man from the 9th Agency.
"Rust" waves at you and turns to leave.

March 15, N.F. 113, 22:51
Secret Passage, Level 28, East District, Drifter Camp
The pipe is broken and spattering water everywhere, but still unable to put out the scattered black embers.
Two figures are stuck in a corner piled with Mania contamination. Che sits with his back against the wall, his right hand reaching out to restrain K.K. and cover her mouth from behind.

speaker: K.K.
content: Mmph...

speaker: Che
content: Close your mouth, hold still.

<size=30>He holds his breath completely and his entire body is straining, tilting his head to glare beyond the corner. K.K. can only follow his gaze out of the corner of her eye. She looks past the metal plate blocking them, past the torn pieces of a black raincoat, and sees the exit of the dark alley.</size>
Over the spattering noise of water, another eerie sound comes from the other end of the dark alley.
Tap. Tap. Tap. The sound of leather shoes. There's only one person, stepping over the puddle and filth, coming this way.

speaker: Che
content: <color=#7683a2>Quiet. Hold your breath...</color>
His voice is almost inaudible, but the hand on her mouth keeps tightening, dragging K.K. deeper into the contamination.

Wriggling, the rotten contamination can't break through the shackles and hurt K.K., but it's crawling onto the boy's skin, corrupting him slowly. Che remains motionless, treating it as a kind of cover of their existence.

speaker: Che
content: <color=#7683a2><size=40>Hold your breath...</color></size>
As the footsteps near, even more rustling noise creeps closer. Eerie sounds of wind crash against the narrow passage. K.K.'s muscles are straining almost to the point of tearing.
...It's those monsters. Those monsters with no faces, only <color=#fb9259>marks of a single red eye</color>!
Che doesn't speak anymore. He triggers the mechanism with a finger of his left hand. The sound of something shattering comes from the far end.
Those howling monsters pause and begin sprinting that way, rushing out of the alley like hyenas smelling prey. The taps of the leather shoes stop, but that person doesn't turn back.
Mania Crystal...? Ha... A small trick.
He keeps going in the original direction and walks inward. The spattering water hits something like a taut tent... An umbrella.
Che grits his teeth and grabs the short ax next to him. He exerts his muscles, but only pulls K.K. further back. She finally makes out the face of her companion...
Anxiety, hatred, and fear she's never seen before... along with a kind of determination that gives her chills.

speaker: K.K.
content: No...
Tap... All of a sudden, the footsteps stop. What comes next is the displeased voice of a man.
...What's the matter?
Hmm... Now? I've finally gotten into the mood to do some overtime work. Why don't you report that tomorrow?
Ha... After running for so many years, she came to you once she showed her face? Why?!
An icy chill sweeps in. The air in the alley suddenly presses down on them. Che's body stiffens instantly.
...I forgot myself. Wait for me, I'll head back now. Thanks for letting me know. If possible, keep her for a bit longer. I'm eager to meet my old friend.
The matters here have been properly arranged. It's a bit of a hassle, but they're a mob after all. I like having dealings with them.
By the time you arrive, <color=#fb9259>it</color> should be ready too...

He closes the umbrella and points the tip to the ground. A hole appears out of nowhere. The man quickly tumbles into the black flames. The hole closes again, leaving no trace, as if it's never appeared.

After a while, only silence remains. Che triggers a mechanism again. The Mania Crystal hidden in another spot shatters and activates a sharp wave of energy. It's his crystal, but this time it doesn't attract any monsters. They've already retreated.
The boy finally lets go of K.K., sliding into the filth like his whole body is giving out.

speaker: K.K.
content: <size=42>Che!</size>
She drags Che away from the contamination immediately. Mania corruption happens very slowly, but he's already injured. He'll feel even worse without ${PlayerName}'s shackles.

speaker: K.K.
content: <size=40>What was that thing just now?! It's hunting you down?! That's neither a Corruptor nor a human?!</color>

speaker: K.K.
content: I saw them, all those new injuries on you. You must have gotten them in the past couple months even if they're not recent. What did you guys do in the past six months? Who did you mess with?

speaker: K.K.
content: <size=40>Where's Bai Yi? Why isn't she with you?!</color>

speaker: K.K.
content: <size=40>Did something happen to her too?!</color>

speaker: Che
content: Jeez, stop yelling mom... My head still hurts...
The boy coughs and tilts his head limply, just like how he used to fake sick to skip work in the past.

speaker: Che
content: It's been half a year... This should be an emotional reunion, why are you getting mad... Is it the utility bills... Or...

speaker: Che
content: Tsk, I forgot to clean up after the last hotpot I had. I hope the place didn't get...

speaker: K.K.
content: You little piece of ****!

speaker: Che
content: Ouch, ouch! Mom I am sorry...
He asked for it, but now he can only hiss weakly. K.K. finally swallows her anger and dresses his wounds swiftly. She bows her head and wraps Che's arm around her shoulders to help him up.

speaker: K.K.
content: Get up, we'll go to ${PlayerName}. The wounds are dressed, but he has to do something with the contamination.
female_content: Get up, we'll go to ${PlayerName}. The wounds are dressed, but she has to do something with the contamination.

speaker: K.K.
content: That man is the mastermind behind this, isn't he? You'll explain it to ${PlayerName}. He's looking into this case too. He's way more reliable than the two of you combined, so don't try to hide anything.
female_content: That man is the mastermind behind this, isn't he? You'll explain it to ${PlayerName}. She's looking into this case too. She's way more reliable than the two of you combined, so don't try to hide anything.

speaker: Che
content: ...Alright. But he's surrounded by people working for that Spider from Paradeisos. I must be careful somehow.
female_content: ...Alright. But she's surrounded by people working for that Spider from Paradeisos. I must be careful somehow.

content: Either because he has lost too much blood or he's calmed down, he seems rather dazed. After he mutters that, he realizes he's let the truth slip.

speaker: Che
content: Ah, no. I mean, I borrowed money from him before. I must hide from him.
female_content: Ah, no. I mean, I borrowed money from her before. I must hide from her.

speaker: K.K.
content: Don't you pull that trick again!

speaker: K.K.
content: I finally seized the chance to come back. I was gonna pay off all the debts and look for you guys. But when I got to Whitestone, there was no one, and the seal was already dusty.

speaker: K.K.
content: <size=40>And when I finally found you, we barely talked before we encountered those monsters. You even tried to abandon me and run away a few times.</size>

speaker: K.K.
content: <size=40>You're already so badly hurt now, and you still refuse to talk? Am I really not worth your trust?</size>
No response. It's hard to tell if he's passed out. With a knot in her chest, K.K. eventually quiets down and walks out of the dark alley with heavy steps.
They're no doubt the closest people to her. She understands these two want to protect her. But that aggrieved feeling is hard to shake, and now she doesn't even understand what exactly she's feeling.
The descending emergency elevator is right before her, and the other end of the shackles seems to be right below. Whatever Che can't tell her... he'll tell that to ${PlayerName}, won't he?
${PlayerName} will protect him and the Drifter Camp.

speaker: Che
content: If that person... hadn't brought you back, I wouldn't have had to risk it...

speaker: K.K.
content: ...What?

speaker: Che
content: What's the point of sending you away...
He lifts his hand to press the elevator's button, staring at the tightening cable below.

speaker: Che
content: Do you still remember what that man in black said on the phone? Once you see ${PlayerName}, tell him everything, word by word. And...
female_content: Do you still remember what that man in black said on the phone? Once you see ${PlayerName}, tell her everything, word by word. And...

content: K.K. gets knocked on the back of her head and her legs go limp. The elevator's gate opens and he tosses her in. The boy presses the button and turns around.
Stunned, she sees six men in raincoats standing behind him.

speaker: Che
content: It may sound a bit lame, but... run, K.K. Find ${PlayerName}. Find Julien. Find whoever you can, pass them the message, then leave. Make everyone leave. Don't look back, and don't ask questions.

speaker: K.K.
content: You... want me to... leave... without you?

speaker: Che
content: I want you to stay alive. Whitestone's future depends on you. Also, running isn't as bad as it sounds.

speaker: Che
content: It's because I ran... I got to see the sun.

The boy grins. The gate closes and with a clack and the scratch of the cable, the elevator starts descending. Che spits out a mouthful of blood and looks at the enemies before him. Their faces are marked with the same familiar runes.

This time it's not the tracking hyenas, but the lurking assassins. The man with the umbrella laid a trap before leaving. He buried his sorcery on the only path, so that when the two stepped on it, they would rouse the monsters, and that would be the end of them.

speaker: Che
content: Sigh... They used to take hostages alive. Do they really want us dead this time? What should I do...
The sound of the elevator's cable rolling behind reassures him. Before him, the monsters wriggle closer, those scarlet single eyes as disgusting as ever.

speaker: Che
content: Alright, I'll pay my own debt this time. Besides...

speaker: Che
content: You guys owe me quite a few things too.
Mania's power begins flowing. The boy draws his ax and dagger, his eyes flashing fiercely. But before he charges, he hears a sudden clack behind him.
The elevator is here again. The gate opens, and a high kick comes flying, sending him to the side.

speaker: Che
content: What the?!

speaker: K.K.
content: Did you think you got me with that cotton punch?! In your ******* dreams!
She's ruined the vibe completely. Three more people walk out of the elevator.

speaker: Hella
content: Yo, blondie's here? How come we see you everywhere we go?

speaker: Hecate
content: Chief's right. The enemies are with K.K. But why do they target you, K.K.?

speaker: K.K.
content: How do I know? I'm not good at these mind games. Isn't the one with the most crooked mind right behind you?

You walk out of the elevator. K.K.'s presence already surprises you, you didn't expect to see the familiar face from <color=#fb9259>Keylan Square</color> as well. Didn't you still owe him something six months ago?
Anyway, let's repay this debt first.
Contamination by the filth disintegrates and vanishes. The black raincoats fall to the ground crestfallenly. The battle is finally over, but Che doesn't wake up.

speaker: Hella
content: How did he get so much contamination all over himself? Did he literally feed himself to Mania? Why did blondie do such a stupid thing? As far as I remember, he's a master of staying out of trouble.

speaker: K.K.
content: Those men in raincoats can hunt down their enemies by recognizing Mania power. To mask our scent, Che buried himself in the contamination.

speaker: K.K.
content: He knew how to fool them. He knew the shackles could protect me. That's why he did such a foolish thing. Yet I know nothing...

speaker: K.K.
content: Idiots... Both of them... Even now...

speaker: Options
options: He wants to keep you safe.
Talk to him when he wakes up.

speaker: K.K.
content: I'm no different. If anything happens to them, I...

speaker: K.K.
content: ...He won't tell me anything. I need to find another way.
She closes her eyes and takes a deep breath. Once she calms down, she turns to face you.

speaker: K.K.
content: Are you gonna use the shackles?

speaker: K.K.
content: I'd like you to contain the contamination. Che is just a lazybones who likes slacking off. All he wants is to bask in the sun freely. If you must lock him up, just take me instead.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I understand. It's all just for containing the contamination.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: He's alright. He's only in this state because you kicked his soul out of him. Relax.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I owe him a lot. I can't repay him everything yet, so I won't take him for now.

speaker: K.K.
content: Really?
It suffices just to be able to sense his location. You have a hunch that you'll need his help again in the future.

speaker: Options
options: Now, can you tell me what happened here?

speaker: K.K.
content: I have no idea either. But... Che wants me to relay a message.

March 16, N.F. 113, 00:44
Secret Passage, Level 28, East District, Drifter Camp
Mulling over the relayed information, you walk up.

speaker: Che
content: Those umbrella salesmen are being bold this time. They showed up personally at the risk of getting targeted by the Spider. ${PlayerName} knows what this means.

Yes. Parma is a cunning, prudent conspirator. He manipulates his puppets to do the dirty deeds for him. He knows how to trigger a disastrous tempest with the slightest move and retreat without ever exposing his identity.

They've only shown themselves twice, during the incidents of <color=#fb9259>BR-001</color> and <color=#fb9259>BR-004</color>. If you're not mistaken, he only risks exposing himself when it's certain he can trigger a Black Ring.
This place is no doubt in danger now.

speaker: Che
content: No matter how well that Corpus is hidden, it was brought in by someone. As long as you can find <color=#fb9259>that man</color>, you can solve the whole crisis. ${PlayerName} must think that, and so do I. I've waited here for a long time for them to show up.

speaker: Che
content: But we're all mistaken. Parma didn't bring that thing.

speaker: Che
content: Just like ${PlayerName}, they chased all the way to Drifter Camp to find the whereabouts of this Corpus. They can't locate it either.
...What does that mean? A <color=#fb9259>Corpus</color> free from Parma's control? A Corpus even Parma fails to find? What exactly is this thing, and why did it choose the Drifter Camp?

speaker: Che
content: What baffles me most is this... Why did it choose the Drifter Camp?

speaker: Che
content: As cowardly as they are, the people here are mostly good folks. It's both costly and risky to try to convert them into useful pawns. Beats me...

Indeed. Corpus are naturally attracted to Mania, just like what happened to the <color=#fb9259>gangsters</color> in the crypt, <color=#fb9259>Zoya</color>, and the <color=#fb9259>Carnival</color> 23 years ago. But Mania wasn't even common in the Drifter Camp to begin with.

Why did Parma leave? Have they given up on this plan? Was it because they were targeted by the 9th Agency? Because of you? No. Corpus must be rare resources. Now that they're already here, they won't give up.
<size=40>Could it be that...</size>
The matters here have been properly arranged. By the time you arrive, it should be ready too.

That's it. Unlike you, Parma doesn't need to find it. As long as he can confirm that the Corpus is here and that it can trigger a Black Ring, that's enough. Parma and his raincoat men can achieve their goal simply by feeding the terror.
Your palms sweat, and you can't help quickening your steps.

speaker: K.K.
content: Che's injury is too bad, he must be treated soon. I have to escort him down. The thing you've told me, I'll find a chance to tell Nightingale about it.

speaker: K.K.
content: Now, are you going on with your investigation? In that case, there's another thing Che wants me to tell you.

speaker: K.K.
content: "If that loony still won't give up, tell him to go to vent E-8."
female_content: "If that loony still won't give up, tell her to go to vent E-8."

speaker: K.K.
content: "That's the last stop of Parma's investigation. He stayed there for a long time."

speaker: [Scene change, large vent]
content: [Scene change, large vent]

speaker: Hella
content: Are you sure it's here?

speaker: Hecate
content: Vent E-8. According to Julien's map, this is it.

speaker: Hella
content: But there's nothing here? No monsters, no contamination. I even prepared myself mentally, but this is so... underwhelming?

speaker: Hella
content: Has that Corpus really been here?
You've seen this place before.
In that dream during your suspended animation. That premonition.
The hidden contamination, the invisible monsters, the silent infiltration. You're certain. The blatant mess staged by Parma above is not its thing. This place is.
You put the Hypercubes in the two Sinners' hands.

speaker: I'm fighting against a terrible, terrible thing.
options: Stay away from me. Protect yourselves.

speaker: Hecate
content: ...Chief, what are you going to do?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It took us a great deal of effort to get here. If we don't take a little risk, we can't see it.

You still remember what you saw in the dream. You remember the handprints on the wall, and where the dragged scorch marks have been. You try your best to weaken the shackles connected to the Sinners, and walk ahead alone.

speaker: Options
options: Touch where the scorch marks have been

content: Sustaining the shackles with your hand, you touch the dusty floor. Flames burn all over you instantly. Everything in your sight twists rapidly. Your sanity is torn, and your vision dims quickly.

speaker: Hecate
content: Chief?!
You can't see anymore. What remains in your sight are the vivid scorch marks, spreading flames, and palmprints. A screeching howl comes piercing...
Very well, you can see clearly now, and you can hear. The scorching body fluid, palmprints, wails, and struggle flow into your perception through the shackles.
You capture the darkest, most cunning one. Frail and in pain, it's devoured by fear. It's imprisoned, scared of making any missteps.

An unknown excitement begins burning. You can't tell whether it's a hunger or a desire for the truth. You step on the scorch marks and walk forward. Enduring both external and internal pain, you reach the edge of the vent following the drag marks.
This is its escape route. It hasn't gone too far. You'll find it!
<color=#dg1f1f><i>Ha... Ha... Ha...<color=#dg1f1f><i>
The screech echoes among the buildings of the Drifter Camp quarter. You don't see the huge monster you expect to find.
And karma has already caught up with you. The murmuring around you is becoming too loud to ignore.
Tens of thousands of people are still hiding from the visible contamination, yet they're traversing the burning filth unknowingly. Captured. Corrupted.

speaker: Nightingale
content: The FAC decontamination force reports an unusual increase of residual contamination in the BR-004 lockdown area was observed two weeks ago.

speaker: Furian
content: A monster... A huge, burning one... It-It was howling... It grabbed me...

Countless voices swarm into your mind along the track. Filled with anxiety, suspicion, fear, and impatience, they make you light-headed. The entire Drifter Camp has turned into an enormous beating heart.
With the thunderous heartbeats comes a twisted voice.
<color=#dg1f1f><i>Hehehe... Haha... Coming back to life... Soon...<color=#dg1f1f><i>
<color=#dg1f1f><i>Give it back to me... Give it all back to me...<color=#dg1f1f><i>

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: <size=44>Show yourself!!!</size>

speaker: Hecate & Hella
content:
Chief!
Oi!
The Sinners drag you away quickly. Your body comes off the track. The shackles fall apart. You're next to that isolated and quiet vent again, safe and sound.
You want to go on with your search, but your body can't take it anymore. You kneel on the floor and begin vomiting.

speaker: Hella
content: What's wrong? You were fine just now, until you suddenly ran off and started yelling and puking. What happened?

You wish you knew. The contamination here is already so severe, but the anti-Mania system still has no reaction at all. Your shackles sense nothing either... How does it conceal itself so perfectly? How long has it been hiding? Days? Years?
Regardless of how weak it may be now, it's undeniably the scariest among all the powerful Corpus you've seen.
The man's voice grows even more repressed on the other end of the communication device.

speaker: Julien
content: You... can't find its true location?

speaker: Julien
content: ...The visible contamination erupting now is only a ploy. The real Mania has already <color=#fb9259>covered</color> the entire camp?
The atmosphere is suffocating.

speaker: Options
options: Send everyone away. Evacuate the Drifter Camp.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Make something up. Blame it on the Executive Committee's deed earlier.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You all must leave.

speaker: Julien
content: ...We've tried that before, but it's impossible to evacuate everyone. They're very reluctant.

speaker: Julien
content: Some people even suspect that Rustfire has turned to the Executive Committee because of our cooperation, and we are coaxing people to leave the Drifter Camp.

speaker: Options
options: How about contacting the FAC? I can help you communicate with them.

speaker: Julien
content: The affairs of the West District are controlled by the Executive Committee, and even if you intend to refute their decisions, it will take time. But we don't have any time left.

speaker: Julien
content: The executive officers' suppression and the gangsters' revenge are waiting for them out there. Even if you straight up tell them a Black Ring is coming, most people lack the courage to step out.

speaker: Options
options: Shouldn't you be the one who gives them the courage?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're the leader here. If even you've lost the will to fight, how can they march on?

speaker: Julien
content: Who cares about a cripple's will? He can't even protect himself.
Silence takes over on the other end of the conversation. When he speaks again, he's already calmed down.

speaker: Julien
content: ...People only rely on the temporary shelter I've reconstructed. They only come to me when they've lost all their courage to fight.

speaker: Julien
content: This is not the Legion. There isn't another Zoya.

speaker: Julien
content: We'll try our best to arrange the evacuation. If you're still determined to chase after it, go back to <color=#fb9259>Romanesque</color>.

speaker: Julien
content: In the process of evacuating house by house, we found some folks who died alone of Mania corruption. We've sent some of the bodies there.

speaker: Julien
content: That Sinner, who walks side by side with death, is taciturn with us. Her only friend Dudu hasn't awakened either. But she may be willing to help you.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Even if people expect or request something from me, they will soon understand that I cannot do anything for them.

speaker: Julien
content: Thank you.
The call ends. Next, an announcement is broadcast throughout the entire camp.

speaker: Julien
content: The Drifter Camp has launched the evacuation procedures. All inhabitants please follow Rustfire members to the shelters.

speaker: Julien
content: Keep calm. Stay rational. Support each other. We've overcome countless hardships before, and we'll do it again this time. I repeat...

speaker: Hecate
content: Chief, are you sure you want to continue? You've been looking unwell for sometime now.
Hecate looks at you worriedly. Come to think of it, touching the <color=#fb9259>scorch marks</color> with the shackles didn't affect them much, but the side effect on you is long-lasting.
You try your best to squeeze out a smile.

speaker: Options
options: I'm fine. I want to try Greta's essence oil.

content: She fumbles for the oil and rubs a drop onto your temple. The strange fragrance reminds you of the sweaty yoga session and that Outlander with a pink headscarf. You quiver all over, and find your mind surprisingly clearer now.
It's not over yet. There are still other things you can do.

You're back to the chilly bottom of the camp. You pass through that narrow passage in the dark, push open the iron gate, walk through the silent hall piled with wooden boxes, and arrive at the graveyard with the monument.
Romanesque, where the dead are remembered. As if separated from the outside world, there are no Corruptors here, no panicking crowd. The living's turmoil can never invade this place.

Oak Casket sits in front of the monument, blended with the pure silence behind and completely unaware of your arrival. The eerie atmosphere almost makes you forget the speech you've rehearsed multiple times, anxiety creeping into your mind.
She doesn't respond, only wearing a faint smile on her face. But Hecate reacts quickly.

speaker: Hecate
content: She's been corrupted by Mania?! Does the Corpus want this Sinner too? Like how it took over Zoya in BR-004?

speaker: Hecate
content: Chief!

You grab onto her and shake her a few times. No response. You vaguely sense Mania gathering. Are there too many bodies of Mania victims here that the <color=#fb9259>Resonance</color> has devoured her?

The moment you connect to her, you fall into an icy cave with your hearing, smelling, and vision completely deprived. After a few seconds of silence, countless woeful cries and wails return to your consciousness slowly.

Burning filth rains down from above, spattering all over the tip of the monument, the chilly soil, and the silent master of the hall. The filth gathers to form grotesque shapes, wailing and approaching Oak Casket!
Too much. It's too much. Suffocated, you feel like your consciousness is being violated by another world.

This is not suppression by the Corpus or the Black Ring, but the heavy pressure from death itself. As if warned by instinct, before the shackles are fully formed, your body lets go of Oak Casket's hand, stepping back.

speaker: (Transition)
content: Purifying sound effect (Transition)
The woman opens her eyes slowly. The chaotic noise is banished instantly. The rain of filth dwindles. You no longer see the burning contamination.
Oak Casket simply sits there as if entirely unaware of the confrontation just now, murmuring something.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Rest in peace... There will be no more suffering. Neither the long nightmares nor that miserable life will ever torment you again. You have received eternal salvation.
After a long while, she finally lifts her gaze from the void to look at you and the Sinners next to you.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: You've brought quite a few friends.

speaker: Options
options: I don't mean to intrude, but what happened was dangerous.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: They're both reliable Sinners who can protect everyone.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Not only them... When I say friends, I don't mean only the living...
As she speaks, she looks behind Hella and gives a mischievous smile. Like getting an electric shock, Hella hops a bit and scurries to grab your hand.

speaker: Hella
content: What the heck are you talking about! S-Stop making up stories! The MBCC is a s-scientific organization, we don't buy your superstitious bullshit!

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Haha, just kidding. You're all too tense. Relax, there's no danger here.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Only some woeful but harmless cries. The deceased have too many grievances. I'm their only listener.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Are they the ones who've recently passed?

speaker: Oak Casket
content: After a person passes away, the Resonance they've left behind also dwindles with time. But since <color=#fb9259>its</color> return has brought about a kind of special resonance, many past voices have reemerged.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: It feels new. While listening, I got sucked into it accidentally.
Dazed as though she's just back from a very long journey, Oak Casket stands up after a long while and looks at you.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Now, I'm back. How can I help you?
Oak Casket listens to you quietly. Though you're talking about the spread of deadly Mania in the Drifter Camp, her expression is as serene as ever.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Don't worry. That Corpus probably won't come here.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Because it detests death, even more than ordinary humans.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Don't worry about me. If the situation becomes too bleak, I won't insist on staying either. I will take your advice and leave to find shelter.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Once this storm passes, I'll have to come back to bid farewell to many people. I must not miss such a grand ceremony.

<size=32>As Oak Casket says that, an eerie smile surfaces on her face, which makes Hella shiver again. You must admit that her job, her ability, where she works, and her... quirky humor, which she'd never revealed to you before, indeed make her quite scary.</size>
You hesitate for a moment and recall how she's helped you before. You decide to confess your request honestly.

speaker: Options
options: I wish to borrow your vision to look for the Corpus.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You just said that its return has roused the long-dead Resonance from years ago. I take it that the people who died then were related to it as well?

speaker: Oak Casket
content: I suppose so.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Then could you please ask them what it really is, what kind of ability it has, why it comes here, and where it'll go?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If we don't find it and stop it, I'm afraid an even bigger disaster will be on its way.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: It's one thing to listen to people's dying wishes, it's another to pry into private memories. Going deeper requires strong persistence. Since I don't have any, I can't fulfill your request.

speaker: Options
options: Then can you take me there?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Just now, when the shackles touched you, I could somehow feel the residual Mania you mentioned. If you allow me to use the shackles again and take me back there, I can look for the answer myself. I promise you I won't take away your freedom.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I've tried my best. But I've run out of means to search for it relying on my own power. I need you.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Tried your best... It's because of it you look so haggard now, am I right?

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Before coming to me, did you touch any dangerous objects with the shackles? How many times? Are you sure you can take it?

speaker: Oak Casket
content: And now, you dare to take a peek at death?
Hecate grips your sleeve instinctively.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But this is the only way I can think of. I can't run away from the enemy, not when it's going to bring about a huge disaster.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You've said that some noble ones redeemed my life with their own. They sacrificed themselves to stop the Black Rings. I can't let them down.
She stares into your eyes. After a long while, she speaks again.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Hmph... A hero who dares to face death head-on. You'll be praised.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Even if I turn you down, you'll find another risky way. Come on then...
She tugs off a glove and reaches out that hand to you.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Due to its return, this spiritual field has been amplified as well. You should be able to hear something through the shackles, through me, now.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: If you've really made up your mind, then... I have something to tell you too.
Air is being squeezed out of your lungs. Your consciousness is gradually detached from your body. The woman in your sight begins to blur, and other figures crowd into your vision.
Shuffling figures and chaotic whispers travel through your consciousness and form a river, pushing you forward from the back.

Everything is blurry at first. Only messy emotions keep pouring in. Confusion, regret, attachment, bitterness. Unintelligible voices lurch inside you, making you turn around and go back up the stream.
Someone grabs your hand. The face is blurry but somehow familiar.
She nods.

speaker: Gray Figure
content: <color=#7683a2>Help me... Please...</color>
The vague phantom quivers and finally sighs softly, disappearing into the colorless stream, amid the suona melody coming from afar.
More turbulence keeps appearing. You find some familiar faces. Another person leaves this world. Sadness and depression gradually entangle your mind. You have no choice but to go on forward.
At last, at the delta in the center of the river, you see the familiar monument and the person waiting under it. Oak Casket stands there silently like she's listening to something.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: This monument was built seven years ago to commemorate those <color=#fb9259>13,004 names</color>. I've been caressing their names, but I'm finally hearing their voices today.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I thought they might be related to the Corpus, but I didn't expect it to be that long ago. What happened then? What other secrets lie in the Drifter Camp's past?

speaker: Oak Casket
content: I wasn't here at the time. I also only heard that story today.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Do you want to hear it too? Then... why don't you come closer?
She reaches out her hand to you again with a mysterious smile on her face.
The soft murmurs spread in your mind again. You hear... many warm voices.

speaker: [White flash]
content: [White flash]

speaker: Chaotic Murmurs
content: <color=#7683a2>No one is born a degenerate. We've only lost our soil... but... Hypercubes are found in contamination too. We're the ones who find them...</color>

speaker: Chaotic Murmurs
content: <color=#7683a2>Come at us. We're not even scared of those Syndican thugs... Let's go, go ahead... Show them what the West District should look like...</color>
You feel surrounded by many people. The cheerful, hopeful smiles push you forward, facing hope, dreams, and a vision for the future. You try to see clearly where they're going...
You see it. Ahead of you, somewhere shrouded by blurry mist, a red ring is slowly spinning.
It's a Black Ring.

speaker: Chaotic Murmurs
content: <color=#7683a2>Let's go. Go back to the Inner Bay. Go back to the mines. We'll reclaim our lives and dignity...</color>
No one hears you. As you hesitate, the figures pass through you. Only one person pauses to look back at you, as if attracted by something. You smell a familiar aroma.

speaker: Hopeful Voice
content: <color=#7683a2>Mom?</color>

speaker: Hopeful Voice
content: <color=#7683a2>Soon, I'll come back soon, wait for me...</color>
You remember. It smells like the delicious wraps by Lavina you tasted recently.

The procession passes straight through your outstretching arms. All the warmth, courage, and hope pour into that luminous ring, as if being sucked into a whirlpool in the sea, only to be torn, shattered, and sunk quietly.
You sense a familiar presence ahead. Mania, unique to that Corpus.

speaker: (Scene change)
content: [Scene Change]

You're back to the monument once again. Beside you is the flowing river of life and death. You don't feel pain, only crippling dejection. All the unredeemable broken emotions turn into tears you can't comprehend, falling down ceaselessly.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Aren't the emotions surrounding death too heavy for you? After all, you're very attached to the living world.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Do you want to continue?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It's indeed here, in the memories of the deceased. Please let me continue. I'm so close to finding the answer.
As you speak, you reach out a hand to her eagerly. Oak Casket is silent for a moment, then lays her hand on your palm gently.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Is that so... Then... you must be careful...

speaker: Oak Casket
content: The deceased who can leave their last words... are not all humans.

speaker: [White flash]
content: [White flash]
Your consciousness is trapped in darkness, prostrating in the mud. Your body feels heavy, like a million chaotic creatures are tangling behind you, dragging you backward.
A burning pain comes from your waist, but you can't feel anything from there on down. You hear yourself whimper.
It's... not over... yet...
Several people are chattering in front of you. You reach out your hand to crush their spirits, to extract their minds. Until death, they haven't become aware of your presence.
Don't want to die... I... don't want to die...

This body keeps going forward, keeps devouring every person it encounters along the way. You notice that this half-body is not trudging on alone. You turn around desperately, wanting to see what's dragging you.

A broken Black Ring floats somewhere even further away. In the center of the Black Ring, a huge dry corpse lies there, nailed into the filthy swamp by red luminous spikes. It's the other half of the body you've lost, long dead.

You wail, but no matter how much you devour, you can't make up for your frailty. Meanwhile, that supposedly dead half-body leaks out contamination like liquid fire, as if everything you devour ends up in its body.

<size=32>The burning pain of Mania contamination strikes you again. Your consciousness is being torn gradually, and somehow you begin to understand. This Mania is not naturally invisible. The contamination has been hidden, in the place where life meets death...</size>

speaker: [White flash]
content: [White flash]

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Cough... Cough!!
Pain banishes you out of the illusory realm, back to the monument. You cough violently, feeling such sharp pain for the first time, as if you've really just experienced death.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: It seems like you've gained a lot. Are you satisfied with your journey to death?
You're in so much pain, but you've genuinely gained something and found the answers to many questions.

speaker: Options (Repeated Choice)
options: How did it conceal its Mania contamination?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: <size=32>Seven years ago, or even earlier, there must have been a Black Ring eruption in the Inner Bay of the West District. That Black Ring plays a huge role in the Drifter Camp's history. I'm afraid those 13,004 people on the Romanesque monument are the ones sacrificed as ground zero.</size>

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: For some reason, that Black Ring was destroyed. The feeble Ring Master found its way to the Drifter Camp, perhaps instinctively tracing food that was similar to itself.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I just have to go and ask Julien, or Lavina, or the FAC. Someone must know about this. It can't stay hidden for long.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Its original body was chopped up and half of it was dead, left in that Black Ring. The other half has kept all its consciousness and is still on the loose.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: <size=32>Perhaps due to the Ring Master's power, the two half-bodies, one dead and one alive, are still somehow deeply connected. The living half is out there spreading Mania and devouring humans' spiritual energy. The resulting contamination is transferred to the dead half.</size>

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That's why no one can find it even after searching every corner of the camp... It's been accumulating power carefully until it can repair its own Black Ring.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Is this all true?

speaker: Oak Casket
content: The deceased don't lie.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I must contact Nightingale and the FAC ASAP and start looking for that broken Black Ring now. It must have already accumulated a lot of power. If we don't stop it, the Black Ring will...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And the Drifter Camp too. We must evacuate everyone. If it can transfer contamination to the Inner Bay, it can transfer it here too. Since you've said... it detests death, that means...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It must want to get rid of its own memories of death!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: We must hurry up. Oak Casket, please take me back!

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Go back? Back to here?
The water level rises and covers your ankles. Through the reflection in the water, you see Hella and Hecate, both looking at you worriedly.
...They seem agitated, which makes you anxious.

speaker: Hella
content: ${PlayerName}, wake up! A Black Ring has erupted, stop dozing! Wake up, please, I'm asking nicely! You...

speaker: Hella
content: ?! How come you're not breathing?

speaker: Hella
content: Oi! Corpse-face, what did you do to ${PlayerName}?! Did you kill him?!
female_content: Oi! Corpse-face, what did you do to ${PlayerName}?! Did you kill her?!

speaker: Hecate
content: Chief... Chief... No...
Panicking, Hecate keeps shaking your body, begging you to respond.

speaker: Options
options: I'm fine. I'll be right back.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: They can't hear you.

<size=32>In the reflection, Oak Casket stands behind them. The surrounding contamination begins to gather and Black Ring monsters emerge one after another. They close in on the two, reaching out their arms to tear at the Sinners who're paralyzed by their mental breakdown.</size>

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Haha... You can't go back. You're already dead.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Why are you shocked? You demanded something from death, and your request has been granted. Weren't you prepared for this?

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Or, do you find death different from what you imagined?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Why?

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Since you said you made up your mind, I have something I wish to tell you too...

speaker: Oak Casket
content: I want you to see, what death really is like...
She's smiling, but it sends a chill down your spine.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: What did you imagine it to be like? Torment on the physical body?
Oak Casket points her gun at the reflection in the lake. In the reflection, she also steps forward and points a gun at your Sinners, but they're completely unaware.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...What are you doing?
Bang! Bang bang!!

You can't release the shackles. Realizing your inability, you immediately turn to plunge into the water to stop that cruel woman. Ripples shatter the reflection, but you're already hearing your companions' cries.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Or, a collapse of the mind? Shattering of dignity?

speaker: Hecate
content: Send him... back... I beg you...
female_content: Send her... back... I beg you...

content: You can't see Hecate's face, but every word she says pricks your nerves. You want to find the way back, but the more you struggle, the more broken and distant their images become.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...If I've offended you, just kill me. Don't hurt them.

speaker: ...And still she is made to suffer that gaze from on high.
content: Are you willing to die for others? Too bad, in your current state, you can't stop anything from happening or do anything for them anymore.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: You can only watch.
She raises her gun again and points it at the void. The ripples are still quivering, so you can't see what's happening in the other world, but it's very clear to you where she's aiming her gun at.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Haha... Do you still want to fight me? You're so used to altering your fate by fighting. This time... are you going to challenge death?
You win! You seize the chance to rush over and restrain her gun-holding hand.
You must stop her. You won't let her hurt them.

speaker: (Transition)
content: Bang!
You hear a gunshot from under the water. You stand still, stunned, as if all strength is drained from you suddenly.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: You're already dead. It's over, your connection to them has been severed eternally. However strong your power is, however stubborn your longing is, you can't change anything now.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Can you understand it now?

The water level keeps rising and slowly covers your head. Countless black hands drag you to the bottom of the river. You don't struggle. You don't feel anything. You simply watch her point her gun at you at last.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: True death is powerlessness.

speaker: [Flash, shattering noise]
content: [Flash, shattering noise]
A crisp shattering noise pierces through the chaos. Your eyes snap open, and your lost senses suddenly return to you. After a dazed moment, you recognize the faces before you.

speaker: Hella
content: Hmm? Are you finally awake? I was gonna give you a punch on the head.

speaker: Hecate
content: Chief, did you find the answer? Mmph!

speaker: Hella
content: Ehh, waa, ahhh! Why are you hugging me? Let go, let go, let go!
You hug the two of them instinctively and keep making sure that they're indeed alive, that they're real, before you let go.

speaker: Hecate
content: Are you okay? Did you have a nightmare?
The two of them stoop before you, unharmed and calm, as if everything you saw just now was nothing more than a bad dream.

And the only person next to you in the dream is now watching you with a smile, the familiar warm smile you're used to. But now, that smile gives you a chill. You prop yourself up to put the two behind you.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Hehe, I fulfilled your request and accepted your shackles. Why should you still be worried?

speaker: Oak Casket
content: You've glimpsed death and been in touch with that world. Are you satisfied with what you've gained?
You hesitate and unleash the shackles warily...
You indeed sense a hint of Mania in the air. Unlike Parma's contamination, it smells faintly like... death. It points vaguely to somewhere above, the high levels of the Drifter Camp.

It's a glimmer of hope. In the past, you would do whatever you could to catch it. But right now, you're out of strength, as if your consciousness is still being crushed by that excruciating powerless feeling.

speaker: Options
options: You created those illusions, didn't you?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm grateful for your help, but why did you show me those horrifying scenes?

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Consider it a small piece of advice.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: You're someone who dares to frequent the realm of death just to achieve your goal, yet you're completely ignorant about death. It helps to have experienced it once yourself, lest you forget.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Death isn't only pain and sacrifice, it's a sheer end and farewell. From then on, you're devoid of power, and you cannot look back. Think it through, how much you're willing to sacrifice in exchange for the resolve to die.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: It must be so hard for you, no? Poor thing... Doomed to walk with death, but so full of yearning.
There's a flicker of sadness in her smile.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: I wish when you finally return to me, pain and regret won't be the only things I'll hear from you.

speaker: (Scene change)
content: Sound of communication connecting

speaker: Julien
content: ...So this is her answer?

speaker: Julien
content: I understand now. The FAC can't possibly control the other half-body of the Corpus. It's buried deep in the <color=#fb9259>dark pit of DisSea</color>. They can't endure that kind of contamination.

speaker: Julien
content: Then, can you locate that monster with this obscure tracking ability?

speaker: Julien
content: ...I see. How long will it take?

speaker: Julien
content: Is that so...

speaker: Julien
content: I haven't given up. I only need to confirm one last thing with you.

speaker: Julien
content: If you can't destroy the demi-Corpus in the Inner Bay, if Rustfire's evacuation operation fails, if you can't find the monster in the Drifter Camp in time... If the Black Ring erupts eventually...

speaker: Julien
content: Can you kill it thoroughly? Just like how you destroyed BR-004.

speaker: Julien
content: ...Okay, good, that's enough. No matter what, please put an end to this.
In the ascending elevator, you get a secret call from K.K.

speaker: K.K.
content: I found a reliable outgoing communication channel and contacted Adjutant Nightingale. The guys from Rustfire won't notice it.

speaker: K.K.
content: Indeed, something strange happened in <color=#fb9259>DisSea</color>. The FAC's troops have set out on their operation, but that area seems very messy now. They said they couldn't guarantee anything.

speaker: K.K.
content: Besides, Adjutant has done some research on the Executive Committee. Julien didn't lie to you. Rustfire's executives and elite squad are all... dead now.

speaker: K.K.
content: She said someone else was behind this, but she worries more about your situation now. She doesn't believe Rustfire is still willing to cooperate with you. She hopes you can leave Drifter Camp as soon as you can and return to MBCC to regroup.
Her concerns make a lot of sense, but...

speaker: Julien
content: No matter what, please put an end to this.
Your last call ended with an ominous feeling. The thought of it makes your stomach lurch.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Leave with your friends, take as many people as you can. Tell Nightingale to focus on her tasks. We can't be too optimistic about the FAC's operation.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'll evaluate the situation and decide.

speaker: K.K.
content: Okay.
There's a brief silence on the other end of the call.

speaker: K.K.
content: ...Did Oak Casket say anything? Can you still stop that Black Ring thing in time?

speaker: K.K.
content: The people here are genuinely nice. And you too. You always come up with something in the end. If you need anything from me, you must tell me.

speaker: Options
options: ...Do your best to evacuate the camp now.

content: How did it escalate to this? From BR-004's accident to Parma, then to that half-dead demi-Corpus, those tens of thousands of people, and the suddenly unearthed Black Ring crisis from eight years ago.

Why did you step into this unfamiliar place? What does this have to do with that unknown Black Ring from eight years ago? Isn't that history all made up? Who are you going to save this time? Do they really exist?
You begin to suspect all of this is a carefully designed trap, but you don't have time to investigate and verify this... because this Black Ring may erupt any second now.
What else can you do to stop the Black Ring from erupting?
(Scene change)
The elevator's gate opens. You see several familiar figures across the corridor. They're hiding behind the anti-Mania shield, shaking constantly.
This is an instinctive response. But for the first time, you feel that even if you win this time, you can't bring any real change.
You win and banish the contamination. No one dies. But it doesn't bring any sense of security at all.

speaker: Ica
content: Waaah!

speaker: Ica
content: Daddy, Mommy... Where are you? Come back please... Waaah!
The child's cries worsen the crowd's anxiety. Many of them are staring at you.
Meanwhile, amid the people's frightened murmurs, you hear a strange voice.

speaker: Strange Voice
content: It's him... It's him... DisCity's lapdog... A spy sent by the Executive Committee... That snake...
female_content: It's her... It's her... DisCity's lapdog... A spy sent by the Executive Committee... That snake...

speaker: Strange Voice
content: Of course this place is dangerous. He brought the contamination. He's... still pretending...
female_content: Of course this place is dangerous. She brought the contamination. She's... still pretending...

content: No response. But the crowd seems influenced by it. Your anger only intensifies their panic.
Rustfire members arrive hastily and want to take over the evacuation work, but even they get dragged into the whirlpool of suspicion.

speaker: Strange Voice
content: Rustfire is no different, colluding with that one. They were the ones who let the armor in. Many people saw it.

speaker: Strange Voice
content: They want to kick us out of the Drifter Camp, want to spare us nothing... I won't accept this!

speaker: Strange Voice
content: The Drifter Camp is our home, isn't it? No other places will accept us. We can't let them have their way!

speaker: Strange Voice
content: ...Kill him!
female_content: ...Kill her!

content: A pair of hands suddenly clutches your neck from behind. You look back to find a familiar face.

speaker: Armed Rustfire Personnel
content: Tally, what are you doing?

speaker: (Transition)
content: Tally's portrait

<size=32>The barbecue stand owner, who once smiled humbly and served you bean curd, is strangling you from behind. His face is filled with terror as if shocked by his own action. Those arms are not restraining you strenuously, but he doesn't dare relax them either.</size>
You stop the Sinners from flipping out and attempt to talk to the man behind you.

speaker: Options
content: Do you believe what they say?
options: Do you believe what they say?

speaker: Tally
content: I... I... don't know...

speaker: Tally
content: You lied to us... You're not an Outland bigwig or a Syndican... You're just an intruder. You have that thing, that Mania power, but you're still pretending...

speaker: Tally
content: You could even take apart that iron monster. If you use your power on us... You...

speaker: Strange Voice
content: Right... The Legion is no more. Zoya is no more. No one can protect us. No one can lead us...

speaker: Tally
content: It was also because of you, that Zoya was... It was you...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If you're going to listen to hearsay, why don't you listen to me? And Julien, Dudu, and K.K. Out of all these people, why do you choose to listen to the most unsettling voice?

speaker: Tally
content: I don't know... but I really don't want to go!

speaker: Tally
content: My skewers are dry and meatless. I know they're not good. Those thugs mucked up my stand many times before.

speaker: Tally
content: But the people here like them. They find them tasty. Even if I don't make as much money here, I don't want to leave...
He seems dazed. If it's not due to Mania, someone must have incited him to make him so on edge, close to having a mental breakdown.

speaker: Options
options: As long as you survive, you'll find another home.

speaker: Strange Voice
content: You won't survive! The homeless can't survive if they get separated! That's what they want!

speaker: Tally
content: Then what do you want me to do?!
You're about to answer him when you look up and see the truss bridge collapse suddenly.

speaker: Options
options: Use your power anyway. You must save him
The shackles are dangerous. Drag him away

content: You forget about the danger of the shackles instantly and raise your hand...
Your power knocks off the steel truss. It smashes down next to your feet, then rolls underground. Tally freezes for a second before he starts crying loudly.
You feel something surge into your mouth and immediately vomit.

speaker: Strange Voice
content: Haha... You're a monster... Winning people over with such deadly power. You're so good at this, so good... You've deceived yet another victim...

speaker: Strange Voice
content: Who's next... When will you act again... You want them all dead anyway...
Something seeps out of the top of your head. You catch that voice. In the crowd, you see an inconspicuous man, that single-eyed curse glinting on his face.
It's too late to alert him, so you drag yourself forward despite still being trapped by those arms, but the strong man won't budge. Suddenly, the force restraining you is gone and someone shoves you.

speaker: Tally
content: Ah...
The man who pushes you away looks dazed. Like a reflex, he stares at you blankly, his eyes full of confusion. The next moment...
The huge truss bridge hits the strong man's head. The joints of his entire body throb and give out, and he tumbles down like a pile of cotton. Within a split second, he vanishes.

speaker: Strange Voice
content: Hehehe... Hahaha... Look, look! This is what they want. We'll all die for nothing!
Something seeps out of the top of your head. You catch that voice. In the crowd, you see an inconspicuous man, that single-eyed curse glinting on his face.

speaker: Single-eyed Puppet
content: Hehehe... Hahaha... Useless... It's useless... Its voice has already spread. You cannot resist it.

speaker: Single-eyed Puppet
content: Thoughts bring fear. Fear brings hatred. And when you infect each other...

speaker: Single-eyed Puppet
content: You desire to follow. Follow the strong ones. Follow the crowd. If you can't do that, you follow the darkness within you... Lowlifes, mere ants... This is your true nature...
Bang bang! Bang!
That strange man falls down with the gunshots, but it isn't you who killed him.

speaker: Lavina
content: It's you guys again...
The shooter is Lavina, a version of her that's entirely strange to you. Her red hair falls loosely and flies up again, as if soaked in blood, blazing. Like a devil returning from hell.

speaker: Hella
content: Lavina? What happened to you...?

speaker: Panicking Crowd
content: Murderer... She killed a man...

speaker: Strange Voice
content: That's right. Rustfire is finally pointing their guns at us... She's been wanting to do that...

speaker: Lavina
content: Who else... I know you're not alone... I know you'll come back...
She shifts her gun to the crowd, passing every terrified face, each pause eliciting a beseeching cry. But Lavina is unbothered. Her once gentle, sad eyes were now filled only with furious malice.

speaker: Strange Voice
content: Hehehe... Hahaha... Look, look! This is what they want. We'll all die for nothing...

speaker: Lavina
content: <size=44>Show yourself!!!</size>
You rush over. She aims the gun at you reflexively, but Hella scurries to her from the other side and pushes her onto the ground. You pry her gun-holding hand open instantly.

speaker: Lavina
content: Let me go! I want to kill it, I want to kill them!
She has shockingly powerful strength, and the unbridled emotions keep stimulating your nerves. The pain reaches your soul through the shackles.
...It's Mania!
(Scene change)

speaker: Lavina
content: My kid was about your age when she left.

speaker: Lavina
content: I didn't lose anyone else, and it's all thanks to you. Regardless of what the others say, I'm... <size=40>truly grateful</size> to you.

speaker: Lavina
content: Let go!

speaker: Hopeful Voice
content: <color=#7683a2>Mom?</color>

speaker: Lavina
content: Ahhh!

Light impales her body and cleaves through her consciousness. As if her soul has been drained from her, Lavina lets go. The gun falls to the ground as she falls into Hella's arms. Meanwhile, Rustfire members have finally contained the situation.
You're gasping for air. Your mind begins to lose focus, one second blur and the next clear. Loaded with intense emotions, broken scenes gradually seep into your mind.

speaker: (Flashback)
content: (Flashback)
Someone is staggering toward a girl. She's frail and seems terrified.

speaker: Dudu
content: Go away, please go away, don't...
Sinner...
Come with me... Your power... Need... your...

speaker: Dudu
content: Back off!!
She picks up the suona and blows out ear-splitting sound waves, piercing through that person before her. The person falls down.
Come back... with me... Rustfire... wants to save you... Rustfire wants to... protect you.

speaker: Dudu
content: Sob... Sorry... Sorry...

speaker: (Flashback)
content: (Flashback)
Next to the broken bridge, K.K. is gripping someone's hand tightly.

speaker: K.K.
content: Don't let go. I still owe you money, remember? I'll pay you back. Hang in there, don't give up. Haven't you been chasing me for the money? Hold on to me... Ahh!!!
Something tumbles down suddenly and hits K.K.'s shoulder. Her hand loosens, and the last thing she hears is a painful cry.

speaker: (Flashback)
content: (Flashback)
The vagabond Outland doctor is stuck in the dark alley, tending to the injured in turn. His face is covered in sad tears, either due to shock or misery.

An amnesiac old woman has just been saved from danger. After bringing her to Rustfire, the man risking his life to save her goes back to rescue more people. He keeps coming back, until finally he doesn't.

Struggle, bitterness, obsession, longing... Emotions are boiling in this place where tens of thousands of people gather. A wicked, filthy monster who only dares to hide in the dark corner sets them ablaze like firewood, then gobbles them down.
Lava-like scorch marks are gradually smeared all over the Drifter Camp. The shackles intensify, waking the fear in the deepest part of your soul that you desperately want to forget.
(Scene change)
...Powerlessness. Just like what she once taught you. You're still alive, but you feel dead. All you can do is watch, unable to accept or stop anything. You're being ripped apart by despair, and...
Ignited by rage.

speaker: Julien
content: The Drifter Camp has launched the evacuation procedures. All inhabitants please follow Rustfire members to the shelters.

speaker: Julien
content: Keep calm. Stay rational. Support each other. We've overcome countless hardships before, and we'll do it again this time. I repeat...

speaker: Hecate
content: Chief?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Go with Rustfire. They'll escort you out. Once you're out, look for an external communications device and contact Nightingale, and tell her about the situation here.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I want to protect those who've escaped. Do your best to hold off the Executive Committee. You can even call the 9th Agency. Anyways, don't let the Executive Committee get involved. Ask the FAC to take over the potential Black Ring zone.

speaker: Hella
content: Hold on, if we are leaving, what about you?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Judging from this Corpseborne's behavior, it's quite cowardly and prudent. It fears death, fears a certain entity that killed it. That's why it must hide, until it takes back its own Black Ring.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Once its Black Ring returns, the shackles will be strong enough to protect me.
You look at the two deeply.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But I can't do this on my own. Please help me.

speaker: Hecate
content: I... can't. My order is to protect you.
Hecate is obviously troubled, struggling with the urge to refuse. You turn to Hella to find her face full of anxiety and hesitation. At last, she asks.

speaker: Hella
content: ...Asking for aid will help you more than just the three of us trying to deal with this alone. Is that what you mean?

speaker: Hella
content: ...I got it.
Gritting her teeth, the girl carries Lavina with one arm and hauls Hecate up with the other.

speaker: Hella
content: Come on, Hecate. The sooner we're done, the sooner we can come back. There's nothing else we can do here besides wasting our time panicking.

speaker: Hella
content: I don't want to see another Black Ring again. I'm sick of watching people die and not being able to help.

speaker: Hecate
content: Let me go, I have to...

speaker: Hella
content: Don't you want to help him? Then just listen to him one more time. You've always trusted him.
female_content: Don't you want to help her? Then just listen to her one more time. You've always trusted her.

speaker: Hella
content: By the way, ${PlayerName}.

speaker: Hella
content: Don't do anything stupid alone! Wait for us, you hear me?
Of course, it's a lie.
In the end, Hella drags Hecate away hurriedly. You watch them disappear in the disorderly structures of the Drifter Camp, then turn back to go up.
(Scene change)

speaker: Julien
content: The Drifter Camp has launched the evacuation procedures. All inhabitants please follow Rustfire members to the shelters.

speaker: Julien
content: Keep calm. Stay rational. Support each other. We've overcome countless hardships before, and we'll do it again this time. I repeat...

You stagger upward. Black crows cover the sky, reeking of death. The shackles' power is surging rapidly. Mania is leaking. The Black Ring is hatching. On the path ahead of you, a crowd of Corruptors is stumbling toward you.
Your power is charging. Suddenly, you hear a familiar voice behind you.

speaker: K.K.
content: Leave them to me. You can't take so many of them. You'll get yourself killed.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I sent them away for their safety. I'm not planning to die.
The shackles that have once touched death now sense that familiar, despicable presence faintly, feeling it becomes stronger. It's right above and will eventually get close to you.
...You won't be defeated by such a detestable creature. You'll find it, trace its path of awakening, and wreck it completely.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I thought you left? Why did you...

speaker: K.K.
content: I took Che somewhere safe. I thought about it, and decided to come back.

speaker: K.K.
content: I'm tired of feeling useless. If those two decide to keep their mouths shut, then I'll look for the answer myself.
Senior Management Office, Drifter Camp
At the broadcasting station, the lanky leader is concentrated on watching various monitors and operating the mechanisms carefully to help fence off Corruptors for those who remain.
He's still repeating the announcement, time after time.

speaker: Julien
content: The Drifter Camp has launched the evacuation procedures. All inhabitants please follow Rustfire members to the shelters.

speaker: Julien
