content: Keep calm. Stay rational. Support each other. We've overcome countless hardships before, and we'll do it again this time. I repeat...

speaker: Julien
content: I repeat. The Drifter Camp has launched...

speaker: Taran
content: Julien?!
The shout from another terminal interrupts him. Unbothered, Julien turns down the volume and finishes his camp-wide announcement before he reconnects Taran's communication.

speaker: Julien
content: Why haven't you left yet?

speaker: Julien
content: Evacuation is mostly done. You'll only increase the risk of unnecessary casualties if you linger. I've ordered the entire crew of Rustfire to leave. Do you want to create more trouble again?

speaker: Taran
content: That's my question too. The entire crew of Rustfire must leave. Then what are you doing here?

speaker: Julien
content: There are things I must see to.

speaker: Taran
content: Then I'll stay. It's my job to protect our leader. As a member of Rustfire, how can I abandon my companion to save my own life?

speaker: Julien
content: You still have over forty thousand companions in the shelters. If you die here, who will protect them?

speaker: Taran
content: Then what about you? Does your life not matter?

speaker: Julien
content: My life will only matter if I die.
He doesn't hesitate to answer.

speaker: Julien
content: Even if it's the wisest decision to give this place up, the fact that I've abandoned my companions will be engraved in everyone's memories.

speaker: Julien
content: <size=32>From then on, Rustfire members will doubt themselves, and the weaker ones will have an excuse to fall into depravity. Within Drifter Camp, within our foundation, everyone will see us as cowardly traitors. If we lose their support, we lose everything.</size>

speaker: Taran
content: But you have a reason. It's all for the sake of Drifter Camp. People will understand.

speaker: Julien
content: They won't. People never listen to reason, that's why conspirators can incite conflict so easily.

speaker: Julien
content: But that can be easily resolved, as long as the one who made that decision stays.

speaker: Julien
content: As long as I die here, this humiliating decision will turn into a grand sacrifice, a public demonstration of Rustfire's belief. This belief will be passed on to you guys, and you will win everyone's recognition.

speaker: Julien
content: You guys will gain unprecedented support and face the real battle.

speaker: Taran
content: What... are you talking about...

speaker: Taran
content: You've said the real battle will only come after this, that we must burn Syndicate down and take back everything that belonged to us. You must lead us. You're our leader!

speaker: Julien
content: ...I'm no leader, and I haven't seen one since.
He produces a bomb. Hypercubes' blue light flickers in the gaps of the intricate structure, sending out dangerous signals.

speaker: Julien
content: The Black Ring is bound to erupt, and I'll stay and find a chance to weaken that thing. After that, those people from Minos will come back to destroy this monster.

speaker: Julien
content: By that time, both the Black Rings here and the Inner Bay one will be resolved. Rustfire must take them over at all costs. Everything we need is there.

speaker: Julien
content: Taran, you have the most battle experience and the most courage. You got the burning passion and what it takes to rally people's hearts. But that is far from enough.

speaker: Julien
content: Because you couldn't control your temper, Rustfire had misjudged ${PlayerName} and delayed our cooperation. Myself included, everyone here died because of your willfulness.

speaker: Julien
content: Remember this, and take responsibility for these lives. Learn to be patient and calm, control your anger, for your dream and everyone behind you.

speaker: Julien
content: There is no one left to lead Rustfire forward except you.

speaker: Taran
content: ...What do you mean? What about the elite squad? Didn't you say Captain and the others are still...

speaker: Julien
content: Raven is still waiting for you in the shelter. Meet her there. She'll tell you everything.

speaker: Julien
content: This is my last order.
Julien cuts off the call and goes back to the broadcasting station.

speaker: Julien
content: The Drifter Camp has launched the evacuation procedures. All inhabitants please follow Rustfire members to the shelters.

speaker: Julien
content: Keep calm. Stay rational. Support each other. We've overcome countless hardships before, and we'll do it again this time. I repeat...

speaker: Julien
content: ...
[Scene Change]

speaker: Julien
content: Those who can't push forward anymore can stay. Both I and Drifter Camp will be here with you till the end.

speaker: Julien
content: But never forget: This is not the end. Whatever is destroyed will be reforged. Whoever is trampled will be honored again. Don't go into death with despair. That's not why you came here in the first place. That's not what the Drifter Camp exists for.

speaker: Julien
content: Remember, we were just not around to see the daybreak, but someone... will light our flame.

Those are his last words. He opens up the secret mechanism and enters the passcode. With a spin of cogs, the hidden slot opens to reveal several anti-Mania bombs inside. He invented these specifically for that thing.
He watches the pale blue light, the long-repressed vengeance awakening in him.

speaker: Julien
content: There are three things I loathe. The first is the vile city-state, the second is the shameless traitors, and the third... is the monster who killed all my companions and destroyed all our hopes.

speaker: Julien
content: What a fine day it is. I can get rid of two of my nemeses at once and lay the path for the others, Rustfire will settle my final revenge.

speaker: Julien
content: I'm eight years late, but I can finally step onto the same battlefield with you guys...

speaker: Julien
content: I'll find it... Even if it means dying together with it...
Clank!

The door is blasted open. The man stands in the doorway. He's not wearing that cloak that conceals his identity. The gray jacket covering his head protects him from the crumbling debris, but he still looks somewhat clumsy.
female_content: The door is blasted open. The woman stands in the doorway. She's not wearing that cloak that conceals her identity. The gray jacket covering her head protects her from the crumbling debris, but she still looks somewhat clumsy.

speaker: Julien
content: ...It's you?

speaker: K.K.
content: Stop standing around. Get inside! They're coming after us!
With the help of the mechanisms, K.K. eventually fights off the bunch of Corruptors and blocks the door. Julien still hasn't recovered from the shock.

speaker: Julien
content: ...Why are you here?

speaker: Julien
content: What about those two Sinners? The Corpus is not here. Why did you waste your time coming here?!
It's the first time you've seen him so impatient. Before offering much explanation, you glimpse the strange bomb in his hand and snatch it, tossing it to the distant corner.
Then you walk over and grab the microphone.
People in various shelters are trembling in fear. Just now, Julien's announcement got cut off and the screen blacked out. Somebody barged into his office.

speaker: Panicking Crowd
content: Why did the announcement stop?

speaker: Panicking Crowd
content: Was there an accident? Did Julien get attacked?! Then what about us...

speaker: Noise In The Crowd
content: He fled... with that spy... He abandoned the Drifter Camp, leaving us to die...

speaker: Panicking Crowd
content: No, he said Rustfire would fight to protect us. He'd been operating the mechanisms to protect us until just now!

speaker: Noise In The Crowd
content: Where are they now?? Contamination has broken out. We're all going to die. Haha, pawns... We're all just disposable pawns!
Bzzzz...
A sharp buzz pierces through the air. The screen is turned on again, but it's not showing Julien's face.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: To those who choose to stay, this is ${PlayerName} from the Minos Bureau of Crisis Control. As requested by your leader Julien, I'm here to protect the Drifter Camp.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: We've already worked together to stop the Executive Committee's violent invasion. Now, we must stop the Mania contamination from escalating.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Before all of you are safely evacuated, we won't go anywhere.

speaker: Taran
content: ...It's him?
female_content: ...It's her?

speaker: Noise In The Crowd
content: The DisCity's authorities sent him to sabotage the Drifter Camp! Liar! It's a plot!
female_content: The DisCity's authorities sent her to sabotage the Drifter Camp! Liar! It's a plot!

speaker: Noise In The Crowd
content: The one who killed Zoya!

speaker: Nervous Inhabitant
content: It's true... He's our enemy...
female_content: It's true... She's our enemy...

speaker: Noise In The Crowd
content: He's in the operation station. We'll go and kill him!
female_content: She's in the operation station. We'll go and kill her!

content: A middle-aged man on the edge of a nervous breakdown gets up slowly and takes out his knife. Just when he wants to step forward, Taran pulls him back and puts him on the ground.

speaker: Taran
content: Stop!

speaker: Taran
content: What's that idiot thinking? Revealing his identity now will get him killed!
female_content: What's that idiot thinking? Revealing her identity now will get her killed!

speaker: Noise In The Crowd
content: It's Rustfire. Rustfire betrayed us too! This is all a scheme. Soon, they'll...

speaker: (Scene change)
content: (Scene change)

Through the glass of the broadcasting station, you peer down at the commotion of the crowd. Though you can't hear them clearly, the angry swings of punches and incessant stones flying this way are clear enough proof of their attitude toward you.
No, it'll be pointless. People have already lost their judgment. Not to mention that under Mania's influence, their minds are extremely weak now.

In times like this, those who can seize the crowd's weakness will win. Parma did that. They caught the despair and fear sharply, exaggerated the situation, and incited panic. You've seen their way. It's a skill beyond your reach.
...Go and look for another weak spot. Human hearts are fragile and often have more than one weakness.
Bang bang bang!

Several bullets hit the glass in front of you, leaving radial cracks with the impact. You can't see clearly what's happening outside anymore. You're uncertain if the shooter did it out of fear or hatred, or if they're in fact one of Parma's spies.
But it doesn't matter who they are. You stop K.K. from rushing over, and look at the camera.
Confess your most sincere emotions to that tiny black hole.

speaker: Options
options: Just now, someone tried to shoot me...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Bravo! You remain vigilant. You refuse to run away. You never give in. You're all regular civilians, yet you have such strong resolve to fight. All of you!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Keep your fighting spirit, because the real enemy will soon emerge. The battle is about to begin.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Hang in there. I'll fight alongside you. Never give up.

speaker: Julien
content: ...You think you can win them over with this cliché? No one's gonna buy it, you...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Hang in there. Zoya is on her way!
This time, even muted by the bulletproof glass, you can still hear the clamor outside.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Why are you surprised? That's Zoya, the Legion's leader, Syndicate's game-breaker, the strongest warrior. How could she die in a place like that, in the hands of some despicable scoundrels?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Listen, I came not just to forge an alliance with Julien. I'm an ally of the Legion. I came to seek vengeance, and to realize the Legion's belief.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The Drifter Camp has suffered the worst disaster. There are people who hate you so much that they can't stand your existence. They'll do anything to banish each one of you and obliterate your home, even if it means using Mania, the most fearsome power.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The same people ambushed the entire Legion using the same trick in Keylan Square six months ago.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Zoya crushed their scheme, but at a heavy cost. Despite that, the Legion's belief has never changed. She wants me to say this to everyone in the Drifter Camp:

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: "Fighting is meaningful, and so is resisting. I'll never give up Syndicate. I'll never be defeated by this!"

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That's right... I came on behalf of Zoya, to fight with you!

speaker: Julien
content: You're lying.
He sees through your lie right away. He lowers his voice so the microphone won't pick it up, but he doesn't hide his doubt.

speaker: Options
options: Don't expose me. Isn't it easier to just believe me?

content: He stares straight at you, ignoring your terrible joke.

speaker: %u
content: Zoya didn't die, but she won't be here. You think it's only a matter of time before this lie gets exposed, but the truth is, I don't need to gain anyone's trust.
The commotion outside grows louder. Shock, suspicion, confusion, and a wary hope... Exactly what you wish for.
Whether they believe or doubt it, desire or hate it, it doesn't matter. As long as they give it their attention, that's enough.
Like cowardice, the desire for a great leader is also a weakness in everyone's heart. You'll give them an ideal leader. Take advantage of this glimmer of hope.

<size=32>Stop imagining unknown fear. Stop worrying about imaginary hostility. If the hatching of a Corpus requires extreme, highly concentrated spiritual energy, then just take away everyone's attention and imagination. You're so sick of it devouring everyone's mind!</size>

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The shackles have touched your half-body. I know you're around.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: A dark, weak, and despicable monster who wants to prey on everyone using all kinds of wicked tricks.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Quit hiding. Now that you've brought this big mess, they're already searching for your other half. All of us will hunt you down and kill you. How much time do you think you have left?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The one who "killed" you eight years ago should be knocking on your door soon too, don't you think?
Crack!
(Transition)
An enormous hand crushes the screen, crushes your face. In a daze, you see the gigantic, inhuman creature perches on top of those screens. It turns its gaze onto you.

speaker: Corpus
content: What are you... prying into...

speaker: Corpus
content: Give me back... my power!!
It lunges up suddenly and vanishes before your eyes again, but that strong power surges toward you.

speaker: Julien
content: Mmph...!
The impact throws Julien onto the wall, off the wheelchair. K.K. catches him in time. She calls out to you.

speaker: K.K.
content: Go! I'll look after him. Just go and fight. You have to win!
You release the shackles. They fill up the space, touching the spilled contamination like a net in an attempt to capture that monster.
Even now, you can't see its true form. But that hysterical, twisted, chaotic presence reeking of death is right before you!
An enormous hand captures you suddenly. The scorch marks burn, spreading through the entire space.

speaker: K.K.
content: Mmph... What... is this... The shackles... don't feel right?

speaker: Corpus
content: Shackles... It's the shackles... but... not her...

speaker: Corpus
content: Just like her... Are you here to devour me too...

speaker: Corpus
content: No... No way... You... don't deserve it...

speaker: Corpus
content: You should die instead!!
The shackles are entangled with it, fighting it. A certain stronger emotion scorches your body and mind.

Is it the pain of losing a friend? Or the rage toward the layers of plot? Your true obsessive nature from your missing memories? An uncontrollable madness and agitation in the depths of your instinct?
You've lost too much of your sanity to recognize this emotion. Julien's figure is blurred now. He seems to be shouting something. You can't tell.
Slowly, a bizarre shape emerges in your vision. Like a red moon, an eye, or a throbbing fetus. It's calling to you, sucking you in...
Chief?!

speaker: (Scene change)
content: (Scene change)
A sharp cry breaks the illusion in your sight. Your mind clears up, though your vision is still blurry and crimson. A familiar figure barges into the office.

You can't speak. Viscous liquid clogs your throat, then leaks out from your nose and eyes, giving off a rusty smell. You can't tell what it is, but Hecate looks like she's witnessing the doom of the world.

speaker: Hecate
content: Nightmare!

Nightmare lunges over, ripping up the Corpseborne instantly. The Sinner almost keels over as if she's been hit hard, but she immediately pushes herself up and runs to you. Your mind becomes clear at once.
The Forbidden Force works and the shackles lash out to pin her on the spot. But it's too late. Discovering the new prey, the Corpseborne roars ecstatically and charges at Hecate.
At that moment, rage and fear incinerate your remaining sanity. Howling, the red shackles shoot forward, piercing its body.

speaker: Corpus
content: Ahhh! How dare you, even you...

speaker: Corpus
content: Even you're trying to... You... How dare you?!
A massive surge of energy explodes within you, but it's not the shackles you know.

The blue light impales your consciousness. You feel pierced by a thousand icicles, the chill penetrating your bones. The red light binding the enemy disintegrates gradually, and the monster it restrains begins struggling.
What an... unexpected accident.

speaker: Corpus
content: I don't exist to help you succeed, not you... not her either!!

speaker: Corpus
content: I won't die here!!

Numerous tentacles claw at you, roaring. Before they reach you and tear you up, a huge metallic structure knocks the creature several steps away. Julien clings to the console with all his strength. He's reached his limit. He only cries out to you.

speaker: Julien
content: Come over. The ground is collapsing!

speaker: Julien
content: Sinners, go and save him! Quick...
female_content: Sinners, go and save her! Quick...

speaker: Corpus
content: Ahhh!
It growls, and a massive flow of energy hits you immediately. You're thrown off the ground, tossed out of the broken window, falling down rapidly.

speaker: Hecate
content: No!! Nightmare, Nightmare?!
The girl's familiar has long been torn apart. Having lost the power she takes for granted, she freezes and just watches you tumble.

<size=32>The Drifter Camp's complex mechanical fortress rises up rapidly. Having lost control of your body, you keep getting hit. Something tries to catch you and protect you. Something soft. Something hard. But then it's all crushed and ripped apart. You continue falling.</size>

You hear the crowd's screams. Your mouth is filled with the taste of blood, cold air and scorching pain clashing in your senses. Time seems to have stilled. Pain puts you to sleep and wakes you up again. Until...
Bang!
[Scene Change]
You fall into complete darkness.
Cold, silence, darkness. It takes you a long time to realize that the face before you belongs to a familiar woman.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Even for a dead person, you look miserable.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: It's still alive. After you provoked it, it got back all its power and wants a fight to the death.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Soon, many lives will be lost again.
You want to lift your hand, but your body won't oblige. You want to speak, but blood clogs your throat. Pain has left you, and soon this body will too. You finally understand why she has come to you.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Almost, seeing that you're back at my side. We've finally found the possibility to defeat it, after so many people sacrificed their lives to protect you. Yet you've arrived here, at last.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Saving the day, then sacrificing yourself. You've glorified yourself with death. Now, the whole Drifter Camp sees you as their hero... Are you happy?

speaker: Options
options: ...Cut it out. I didn't do it on purpose.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I didn't plan to die... I did enough preparation. I was confident I could win, but I didn't expect something like that could happen.
Those blue shackles emerged at the touch of the Corpus. Was that a backfire of your power? Was it a poisonous trap buried in the Corpseborne by Parma? Or...?
No matter what it is, you could neither see through it nor avoid it. Death is ubiquitous indeed. You can't hide from it.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: You seem a little perplexed. Do you regret it?

You never thought the death warning she once gave you would come true like this. You can't go back now. No matter how mad and heartbroken they'll be, how much more danger they'll face, you can't do anything for them anymore.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But somehow, it doesn't hurt as much as I thought it would.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Hmph?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: <size=32>You said you would make the wishes of the dead come true. Now I can understand... Whether my soul will continue to exist after death, whether you will keep your promise, hearing that alone is enough to free me from the powerlessness at the end of life.</size>

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Thank you. You're very kind to the deceased.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So... Please make my wish come true. Destroy it in my stead.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Don't let it crawl back from hell. If I die, it must die with me.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: ...Hmph, is that how you take advantage of others' kindness?

speaker: Options
options: You know me. There are too many things I can't let go of.

content: She smiles.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: The gentle, kind Chief... I wish they could see you now.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: If devils did exist in this world, I suppose they would be as stubborn and shameless as you...
She stoops down and scoops up the blue pendant hanging in front of your chest.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Many people once sacrificed their lives to bring you back. I granted their wish, and I advised you to cherish your life.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: But if you ask me, I'd rather you, who also carries a dying wish, find relief.
"Many people"...?
Before you can ask, she raises a hand to caress your cheek, and her gaze lifts to meet yours. Her voice is eerie, as if touching your bare soul.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: I can grant your dying wish, just so you can be in peace and let go of all your regrets when you leave. I hope you can escape your destined misery... What do you think?

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Captain
Your consciousness is falling apart. This is the final question and answer. You try hard to consolidate your diffusing thoughts, and part your lips instinctively.

speaker: Options
options: I want to live, of course.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I know this answer disappoints you... You're always forced to help a stubborn living person. I know you're not comfortable with it, and you're not willing to do it.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But if I die just like this, won't it be boring for you...? If it so happens, I can only share my pain and regret with you after death. You said you didn't want to hear that.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: ...Which means?

speaker: Options
options: How about we strike a deal?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I want neither to embrace nor escape from death. Perhaps I've never pondered death seriously... because I cherish life. While I'm still alive, I want to dedicate all I have to fighting for what I want and protecting what I love.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If I'm bound to return to you when I die... then please, help me this time while I'm still alive. Not to grant a dying wish, but just so I can...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Bring you more when I die, after I've lived hard.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: ...Do you have any idea what you're talking about? Do you think you can just bribe me like this?
She suddenly cups your face with her hands and looks into your eyes. Those two eyes of different colors, like life and death, are suddenly brimming with smile, looking almost greedy and hysterical.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: I can! I can break the rules for you, and accept the guidance of the living. In exchange, the price you pay is that after you are truly dead, everything will belong to me.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: I want to hear some last words that aren't about pain or regret. I've heard too much already.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Bring me a more interesting death. From this day onwards, this is what you live for. Your death now belongs to me, and so does your life!
This madness makes you shiver. She never wanted a selfless giver. She's a maniac who's obsessed with the realm of death. You have no other choices, and this is in fact what you need.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Hahahaha... Very well... That's a promise of life and death. No one can break it.
You begin to hear the sound of suona as pain strikes you. Proof that you're alive.

The figure before you begins contorting and fading. That distant female voice grows louder and solid beside your ear. Somebody is supporting you. Somebody is confronting the strong enemy. She seems to be in a good mood, filled with joy.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: To me, the living world is total chaos. Since you can see the path ahead, be my eyes, guide me.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Now, tell me. Where is that enemy you want to destroy even at the cost of your life...?
Your hand no longer obeys you, but the shackles stretch forward eagerly...

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Good job, you did well...
Bang! Bang bang!!

speaker: Corpseborne?
content: Ahhh!!

<size=32>Cries pour down from above. A certain being struggles and fails, wrecking the truss bridge of the camp, scraping off numerous walls and broken tiles. The enormous being falls to the bottom of the camp. Amid smoke and debris, it can no longer conceal itself.</size>

speaker: Corpseborne?
content: How dare you... How dare you...!!
Oak Casket lays you flat on the ground and takes a step forward toward that gradually emerging Corpus, holding two guns glimmering with an icy light. Her voice is compassionate and maniacal.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Half of your body and soul have already sunk into the abyss, into eternal slumber. Why must you struggle to live miserably alone? Isn't that torture?

speaker: Corpseborne?
content: Roar!!! Shut up!! I won't die, I must live!!

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Poor child... You need someone to set you free.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: I'll send you home now.

speaker: Corpseborne?
content: Ahhh!!! Can't die, I can't die!
The shackles rip the monster's body into pieces. It turns into ashes and vanishes. Strangely enough, nothing enters your body.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: I thought you'd be more careful after that. Aren't you afraid your body may not take it well?

speaker: Oak Casket
content: At least it's gone now. You should feel blessed you're still alive.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: You don't need to thank me. We made a deal, an excellent deal. I'll be looking forward to it.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: I believe that day... will come soon.
You want to ask her something else when a familiar figure suddenly hops out and grabs your collar, shaking you violently.

speaker: Hella
content: Didn't I ******* tell you not to do anything stupid?! You...

A beating is inevitable, naturally. You skillfully prepare yourself to give her the apology and excuse you've rehearsed, but before you start, the girl stops beating and cursing you. Her voice doesn't sound right.

speaker: Hella
content: Sob... You killed it... The Black Ring didn't erupt, and you didn't die... Nightingale will be here soon, she said she'd be quick...
Hella buries her ashen face in your chest, her body shaking uncontrollably like a child just woken from a nightmare.

speaker: Hella
content: I saw many, many dead bodies on the way... Some of them were Lavina's friends, and...

speaker: Hella
content: I couldn't do anything, couldn't save anyone... I thought the Black Ring was gonna...

speaker: Hella
content: Thank goodness, you killed it... I'm so glad you did...
You hug her wordlessly. She's a kind and innocent girl after all. Witnessing so many deaths is too cruel for her.
You're glad you chose to stay. It was worth betting your life on that fight.

speaker: Options
options: Once you feel better, we'll go find Hecate.

content: She's still in the upper levels. She hasn't moved much. Judging from the shackles' response, she didn't encounter much danger.

speaker: Hella
content: Okay. Come here. I'll give you a piggyback. Look at the mess you got yourself into. With all these injuries, it will take a whole year if you walk by yourself.
You oblige and lean onto her back. Before leaving, you turn back.
Oak Casket has already left, leaving only the silent monument. In the sunlight, half of it is still buried in darkness.

speaker: [Transition] (Staircase background)
content: Beneath the crypt, the ominous pulsations are still continuing. The gangsters are growing uneasy. They've obviously received the signals sent by the sentries, and the grand battle is ready to break out any moment now.

speaker: Hella
content: My original plan was that the two of us would get out quickly, relay the message, and immediately come back for you. But we only took a few steps before Hecate insisted on coming back.

speaker: Hella
content: Earlier, she couldn't wait for another second to see you. Now she is taking her sweet time to come out. I wonder what's taking her so long...

speaker: Hella
content: Tsk, it's all your fault! I forbid you from acting alone next time! You hear me? Come here, let's get your face cleaned up. If she sees your injuries, she's gonna...

speaker: Hella
content: Hecate!
The blue-haired Sinner sits atop the staircase, holding onto the wall and peering down at you. Nightmare has recovered but still seems a little floaty, looking as weak as she is.
Caught off guard, you didn't have time to wipe off the blood on you or get off Hella to make yourself look robust.
But she only looks stunned for a moment, then bows her head and walks down step by step arduously. She comes over to support you.

speaker: Hecate
content: Chief, are you okay?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I heard Dudu's suona. She healed me with her power. The Corpseborne has been banished. It's all over now.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What about you? Are you okay?

speaker: Hecate
content: I'm fine.
Her voice is emotionless, and she doesn't look at you. Something seems off. Is it the effect of that battle just now? Is she mad?

No, that's not it. You know this expression well. It's that stiff expression she had when you first met her, when she only knew to obey orders. But her hands are clutching your sleeve tightly, her knuckles turning white from the grip.
She finally looks up at you, but the windows in her eyes are tightly shut.

speaker: Hecate
content: I'm fine. But things are happening on the Rustfire side.
You want to say more, but a furious roar suddenly comes from above.

speaker: Hecate
content: I think you'll need to make your judgment, Chief.

speaker: (Scene change)
content: Julien's Office

speaker: Taran
content: Julien, hang in there! I'll tend to it right away. Who did this to you? What happened?!

speaker: Taran
content: Doctor! ****! Where's the doctor? Hurry up...
He hears the footsteps and is yelling to the door, but freezes the moment he sees you.
You look past Taran and see the ashen-faced architect next to him. Julien has slumped on the floor, his legs pressed under the fallen rocks, blood welling out toward you.

speaker: Julien
content: ...Ha, you made it back... You did it...
You dash to him, wanting to lift that huge rock but unable to gather enough strength. After Hella and the feeble Nightmare join you, you're finally able to move the rock away.
The man's legs have become a bloody pulp. Painfully, Taran tries to stop the bleeding.

speaker: Julien
content: Haha... Don't worry. My legs have never been useful anyway. Can't take two steps without stumbling. The wheelchair works way better.

speaker: Julien
content: I think it's fallen off somewhere though. I hope it's not ruined. It's quite time-consuming to make a new one... and exhausting.
As he speaks, he suddenly laughs.
That jaded, serious Rustfire leader is actually joking. How can he still laugh now?

speaker: Options
options: How did you get so badly injured?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: With so many mechanisms here, you should have been able to better protect yourself. How come...

You remember. When the building collapsed, something protected you. The machine that knocked off the Corruptors and the mechanism that caught you. You only survived the fall from that height because...

speaker: Options
options: Were you operating the mechanisms to protect me?

speaker: Julien
content: It's nothing. People fall off buildings here all the time. I've... caught quite a few of them. I'm good at this.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That's not the same! You almost died. I didn't ask for that favor.

speaker: Julien
content: I was going to die anyway. It's already a win I'm still alive.

speaker: Options
options: Save your bad jokes. It's not funny at all.

speaker: Julien
content: Why are you mad? You don't like owing me a favor?

speaker: Julien
content: It's okay. You don't owe me anything. It pleased me to do that. Thank you.
The blood loss makes his skin pale and his breathing labored, but the man's eyes bloom with vitality and light. He clutches your lapel and gives a bright smile you've never seen before.

speaker: Julien
content: I've been distressed... The elite squad is dead. The Drifter Camp is in ruins. Before they could even glimpse the future, they kept losing what they had, and they were even pushed to the battlefield when they felt the most lost.

speaker: Julien
content: I thought I could lay the path for them, but what they needed wasn't a path-builder, but a leader. With no one to lead them, their hearts would only be directionless.

speaker: Julien
content: Luckily, you came. You defeated the undefeatable, twice. No one could deny that. No one could look away from you.

speaker: Julien
content: Syndicate has lost Zoya, but it has gained you.

speaker: (Scene change)
content: [Scene Change]
You feel anxious.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I only came to handle Mania. I didn't mean to get involved in your business. I'm going to chase that Corpseborne next.

speaker: Julien
content: Of course. I can tell you more, about that Black Ring from eight years ago, about everything that happened there. I can tell you all that.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: In exchange, what do you ask of me?

speaker: Julien
content: You don't have to give me anything. It's enough just to see you keep living.

speaker: Julien
content: As long as you live, you can motivate everyone... You're a born leader.

speaker: Julien
content: You'll lead us to the battlefield.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're not someone who holds back doubts. What does the Drifter Camp... What does Rustfire want? What do you want?

He doesn't answer anymore, falling unconscious with a smile. You only just realize a crowd has gathered outside that dilapidated door. It's the Rustfire members. The way they look at you has completely changed...

speaker: (Scene change)
content: [Scene Change]
In the contaminated ruins

speaker: Rust
content: It's all over, commander. The rats have already left. Something even more important than the Black Ring... That bigwig is coming up.

speaker: Rust
content: About the Drifter Camp, thank you for not turning to the last resort. Personally, I don't wish to sacrifice the people here. I like them.

speaker: Rust
content: Yes, he's alive. He doesn't look well, and his body is in an abnormal condition. Apparently, there was an accident during his fight with the Corpus. He won, nonetheless.
female_content: Yes, she's alive. She doesn't look well, and her body is in an abnormal condition. Apparently, there was an accident during her fight with the Corpus. She won, nonetheless.

speaker: Rust
content: There are other findings. I'll let him... report to you himself.
female_content: There are other findings. I'll let her... report to you herself.

speaker: (Scene change)
content: [Scene Change]
Wreckage of FAC-Propulsion Type 023
The man lies slumped in the ruined metal. His body contorted into a laughable pose. The broken communications device is making intermittent noise on the side.

speaker: Executive Committee
content: Emergency announcement. Emergency announcement. Black Ring reaction confirmed in the Drifter Camp. All executive officers are to return to the headquarters to regroup and prepare to lock down the Drifter Camp. I repeat...

speaker: Executive Committee
content: I repeat, return to the headquarters and prepare to lock down...

speaker: Donald
content: Lock down on what... They've already moved once they saw a chance, idiots.

speaker: Donald
content: Could've told me earlier that someone capable was coming, I wouldn't have bothered to borrow this big thing and set up this scene. And in the end I didn't get anyone out, wasted my effort and offended both sides.

speaker: Donald
content: What should I say when I go back... I should probably just run away... A... achoo!
The supposedly dead body twitches and suddenly sneezes loudly. Pulling the injured muscles makes the man grimace with pain, but he dares not make any sound.
The patrol are already cleaning up. The man can only swallow the pain and drag his still partly numb body down the wreckage, cursing as he rolls down.

speaker: Donald
content: That ******* kid still can't shoot. Aim at the chest if you want to kill. How did those two bullets end up in my thighs, ouch...
He rolls down a gutter and finally gets up, wiping his face.

speaker: Donald
content: Goodbye, my beautiful Margaret. Take care, until next time.

speaker: Donald
content: And that so-called expert Chief... I misjudged this time. We'll meet again.

speaker: Donald
content: Whoever you are, look after them, and don't do anything stupid.

speaker: Donald
content: Fire is coming... Be careful not to burn your friends.

speaker: (Scene change)
content: [Scene Change]

speaker: Margaret
content: How come you're still not back?...

speaker: (Scene change)
content: (Scene change)
Dark Alley
The moon shifts to above the patio. It's a full moon with a glimmer of red. The light illuminates the graffiti on the wall, catching her eyes.

speaker: Executive Officer?
content: ...Oh? I don't remember seeing this last time.

speaker: Executive Officer?
content: So you do remember to come back... You little punks.
She walks into the room and sees the frail Julien on his sickbed.

speaker: Executive Officer?
content: You said to take this chance and relocate our base to avoid the Executive Committee's attention... You didn't say you were going to sacrifice your own life doing that.
After a brief silence, she lifts her hand to slap the man, but the hand freezes in mid-air.

speaker: Executive Officer?
content: Never mind, it won't hurt now anyway. I'll wait till you wake up.

speaker: Executive Officer?
content: Don't do that again, my friend. Don't pin your hopes on a leader... What you saw in him was not the future, only a phantom of the past.
female_content: Don't do that again, my friend. Don't pin your hopes on a leader... What you saw in her was not the future, only a phantom of the past.

content: She shakes her hand and produces a quill. With a mournful expression, she scribbles some funny words on the man's face, mumbling like she's grumbling.

speaker: Executive Officer?
content: Don't worry. People have settled down in the shelters. They're waiting for you to wake up. Rustfire's epic has yet to begin.

speaker: Executive Officer?
content: The day is already dead. The night is unclear. The only moon is rusty, we can only...
The ink on the man's face begins to float, turning into a black raven at last.

speaker: Black Raven
content: Caw! Ignite it. Light it up.

March 16, N.F. 113, 23:30
Romanesque Hall

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Do you have something to say to me?

speaker: Dudu
content: Shouldn't you have something to say to me?

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Haha, right. Thank you, you came in time. If you were a minute late, ${PlayerName} would probably have been gone.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: I'll be deeply sorry.

speaker: Dudu
content: Hmph... But you look very excited.

speaker: Dudu
content: Do you have new visitors now? There should be many newcomers these days.

speaker: Dudu
content: Just let me know if you need help. I do... miss this place.
She jumps off the platform, brushes off the dust on herself, and leaves.
Oak Casket smiles and looks ahead. A blurry figure emerges.

speaker: Emaciated Woman
content: Miss... You were right... Death has liberated me. My pain can finally end...

speaker: Emaciated Woman
content: Now, can you take me to see Mia...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If there are no souls after death, if only fragments remain, then who are you consoling by granting these dying wishes?
...Is it for the comfort of the living?

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Of course, she's waiting for you too...

speaker: [Scene Change]
content: (Scene change)
Nirvana Headquarters, Eastside
The woman stands by the window and looks toward the west coast, where the huge Black Ring glimmers. At the other end of the long desk, in the shadow, a man in a suit sits quietly.

speaker: Man In Suit
content: I heard that new underling you snatched from the FAC made quite a scene in the West District, then deserted and went MIA. Nirvana has some major investments in the West District. We suffered severe losses this time.

speaker: Man In Suit
content: Are you here to explain this incident to me, Miss Special Agent?

speaker: Langley
content: Haha, I've been busy meeting the underground scumbags. Your new investments in the West District... We'll get to that later.

speaker: Langley
content: However, that new underling of mine did bring me some shocking intel.

speaker: Langley
content: That Black Ring you claimed to have destroyed eight years ago, its owner is still alive and well. That's why I've come to take over that old file.

speaker: Langley
content: Hand over the data you've been keeping. The Inner Bay, the mines, Hypercubes, the workers' protests...

speaker: Man In Suit
content: Hmph... You want to get involved in Hypercubes too... Hyenas from the 9th Agency, have you got permission from Paradeisos?

speaker: Langley
content: This bullet needs no permission from anyone. Hand it over. I need the complete file of <color=#fb9259>BR-002</color>.

speaker: Che
content: ...Did you see anything familiar when you defeated that Corpseborne? Like... fragments, cores, or inheritance inside its body... Whatever you wanna call it. You should know it better than anyone else.

speaker: Che
content: Really? It didn't leave anything behind? Then I'm afraid you haven't won yet...

speaker: Nightingale
content: The FAC has raised the threat level for the DisSea Surveillance Zone, and is also actively dispatching formal troops to support West District. However, there have been a lot of obstacles.

speaker: Nightingale
content: <size=31>Personnel attrition is just one of them. Mania cases have spiked across Eastside these days. The 9th Agency confirmed they were all caused by Parma forces. City Council issued an emergency transfer order for the FAC's main troops to fortify Eastside.</size>

speaker: Nightingale
content: ...Yes. Even though it's part of the enemy's containment plan... they still demand that we prioritize protecting Eastside.

speaker: Hecate
content: Are we going to stay here? Can we trust that man called Julien?

speaker: Hecate
content: Chief, are you going to be Rustfire's leader now?
<size=44>Of course not!</size>

You throw a few crumpled Rustfire <color=#fb9259>propaganda leaflets</color> in front of Julien. They spread like wildfire through the Drifter Camp in just two days, and had also been scattered across all of Syndicate.
In the most conspicuous spot on the leaflet is a photo of you.

speaker: Choice
options: I didn't expect you to do that.

speaker: Julien
content: ...Why did they write it this way? You shouldn't be thrown into the public eye like this.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I don't want to be thrown in front of anyone's eyes. You people are using me.

speaker: Hella
content: Gosh, ${PlayerName} looks furious... What did they write to piss ${PlayerName} off so much?

speaker: Hella
content: The writing's too ugly to understand. Will you read it out for me, Hecate?
Hecate takes a leaflet and starts reading it blankly.

speaker: Hecate
content: "The Executive Officers' brutal mech has been totally destroyed! The mysterious beast is teetering on the brink of defeat! Shocking truth about the Drifter Camp's victory revealed: The hero is a delicate bureaucrat (with two damsels)!?"

speaker: Hecate
content: "Regardless of creed or color, come fight for justice! The hero from the Bureau has joined our side! The architect Julien weeps with joy and faints on the operating table!"

speaker: Hecate
content: "${PlayerName} calls out to all in West District: If the dawn does not come, let the fire burn! Embrace change and make Syndicate great again!"
You make the girls leave before Hella bursts out laughing. Now, only you and Julien remain in the room.

speaker: Julien
content: Rustfire's propaganda style is a bit dramatic, and sometimes... stretches the truth. This is just to catch people's eyes. To win people over, we have to be seen first.

speaker: Julien
content: I don't agree with this wording, especially the part where it describes you as "delicate"... Even if it's meant to give people confidence, it's too biased. I'll change it up for sure.
Julien picks up a leaflet and examines it carefully, pondering for a while.

speaker: Julien
content: How about we change your pic? Add some muscles? Hmm... it'll take too long for you to actually buff up. Maybe we can draw some abs on you, then take another photo in different clothes. That way, you'll look more like Zoya.

speaker: Julien
content: Syndicans value outward <color=#fb9259>strength</color> over mental resolve. They trust those who look tough, so we have to change your image.
Having made up his mind, he looks up at you, brimming with confidence.

speaker: Julien
content: What's your take on this, ${PlayerName}?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm going to take your head off!

9:16 p.m., March 18, N.F. 113
Drifter Camp

speaker: Julien
content: Cup of coffee? Ten sugar cubes. Here, try some.

speaker: Choice
options: Are you allowed to drink stuff like that?

speaker: Julien
content: Ha, it's fine. Lavina's not here. No one will reprimand me.

speaker: Julien
content: She's a lot better now. Good thing you cast your shackles on her in time. The Mania in her is now under control. Maybe she'll even become a Sinner when she wakes up.
Julien's tone is light and cheerful, in stark contrast to his ashen face. His broken legs are hoisted high, and the bloody battle scenes are still vivid in your mind.
All in all, he broke his legs to save you. You sigh and respond to him in a sincere tone.

speaker: Choice
options: You promised to tell me everything.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Tell me about the Corpseborne of this Drifter Camp, what happened 8 years ago, the Black Ring, and... how everything links together.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: My target is the Corpseborne. That's why I stayed to wait for you to wake up—to ask you about it.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If you don't regard me as your foe, but as a <color=#fb9259>friend</color> who fought with you side by side, then please fulfill your promise and tell me everything.

speaker: Julien
content: ...You're right. You've waited long enough.
He turns and takes out an envelope from a bedside shelf and hands it to you.

speaker: Julien
content: I've already prepared everything I need to give you. It's all here.

speaker: Julien
content: To me, and to Rustfire, you're not only a friend, but you're the one who led us out of the darkness.
You take the envelope. It's quite heavy, as if there's a big stack of papers inside. You're touched, but also a bit embarrassed.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: They need someone like Zoya, a warrior who'll go to hell and back for Syndicate, or someone like you, a loyal guardian who'll shoulder pain and burden.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm just an ordinary person. Everything I did... was just for my own purposes.

speaker: Julien
content: But the hope you brought to everyone is real. You were the one who saved the Drifter Camp that day, not Zoya or anyone else.
His smile is warm and sincere, almost blinding. It's hard to imagine this is the same despondent guy you negotiated with a few days ago.

speaker: Choice
options: Really feels like your heart got younger.

speaker: Julien
content: Haha, really? Maybe it's because I remembered to follow my heart again. I'm really happy to have you here.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Can I open it now?

speaker: Julien
content: No.
Your hands pause awkwardly in mid-air.

speaker: Julien
content: I'll send you to a special place where you can take your time to read everything.

speaker: Julien
content: Don't peek before that. You'll get caught.

options: What are you planning this time...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Didn't you say there were no more tests? What's this "special place?" I don't like getting pushed around.

speaker: Julien
content: It's not a test. You'll understand when you get there.

speaker: Julien
content: I know you just want to complete your mission. That "place" is the easiest spot for you to complete it.

speaker: Julien
content: Don't you still have to find the other half of the Corpus you're hunting?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ! How did you know that?

speaker: Julien
content: Everything is explained in the letter. You'll know when you get there. Take this info as a token of thanks from Rustfire.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...All right.

speaker: Julien
content: I'm not going. I have to stay here. I have a surgery in a bit.
He flashes another bright smile, making you anxious again. Just then, there's a knock on the door.
Taran comes inside. Your presence surprises him, but he quickly regains his composure and nods to greet you.

speaker: Taran
content: It's about time. I'll escort you to the car.

speaker: Hella
content: Ooh, so polite all of a sudden? Is it cuz you know who's the real boss now?

speaker: Taran
content: ...Mmm. Please come with me.

speaker: Hella
content: Damn... What's gotten into you?
(Scene change)
In the deepest underground level of the Drifter Camp, you board a railcar that enters a deep, dark tunnel.
The <color=#fb9259>tunnel</color> seems to have no end. The only lights are the ones at the front of the vehicle. Fortunately, the speed isn't too fast, allowing you to observe your surroundings.
It's a place ravaged by violence and time. It's hard for you to tell if the debris all around you are from wars or natural disasters. Time has corroded everything with rust and buried them in dust.

Nevertheless, the ruins are still impressive. The tracks fork and intertwine with each other along a complex but efficient three-dimensional layout... The entire network is a huge infrastructural masterpiece.

speaker: Black Raven
content: Caw...
That black raven flies over your head, lands on the railcar roof and looks down at you. The door sills under its feet are emblazoned with Rustfire graffiti.
Under the graffiti is an older logo.

The logo depicts the letter "<color=#fb9259>N</color>". In contrast to the messy gangster graffiti, it looks as neat as printed font, and appears in almost every corner of the mine, damaged and corroded.
It looks familiar to you. It feels so out of place in Syndicate, and you feel like you've seen it somewhere in Eastside.

speaker: Hella
content: Gosh... What is this place? Have we been whisked away to Eastside?

speaker: Rust
content: You're indeed still in Syndicate.
A Syndican like Hella is even more shocked. Her mouth hasn't closed since she got here.

speaker: Hella
content: I saw a huge <color=#fb9259>robot</color> just now. Even though it's broken now, but that steel claw is still ***ing terrifying.

speaker: Hella
content: If Syndicate really had something like that, the gangs would be nobodies. They'd all kneel and call us "daddy."

speaker: Rust
content: Haha, well, times have changed. The mech you saw was an old model from 28 years ago. That was the golden age of Syndicate.

speaker: Rust
content: The <color=#fb9259>Inner Bay Rail</color> is a special rail track for transporting Hypercubes out of the mines. It's actually a few years older than Keylan Square.

speaker: Rust
content: Too bad it was too close to DisSea. The <color=#fb9259>big explosion</color> destroyed everything.

speaker: Rust
content: Back then, if you stepped above ground, you'd see the industrial center of the world. It was the sole place that produced Hypercubes. Forget about the gangsters—even Eastsiders would call you "daddy."

speaker: Hella
content: No ***ing way! It was that awesome?

speaker: Rust
content: Yeah. Unlike now, it was an honor to work in West District back then. The best and brightest fought to come to Inner Bay.

speaker: Hella
content: Were they really talented?

speaker: Rust
content: Extremely. On average, one of them equals ten Zoyas. You can calculate for yourself how many Hellas that would be.

speaker: Hella
content: Ten Zoyas?!! Wow!!! Then that would be...

speaker: Hella
content: ...Stop messing with me!
A quiet laughter comes from the other end of the phone.

speaker: Rust
content: <size=31>To be honest, I didn't expect them to give you a ride. The conflict between Rustfire and the Executive Committee has worsened, so they desperately need your strength. I thought they'd do everything to convince you to side with the Drifter Camp.</size>

speaker: Rust
content: But it's better this way. Otherwise, you'd be in a very difficult position. The Bureau suits you best.

speaker: Rust
content: Mr. Chief, when you go back after this mission, please get that child to read more. She's from Syndicate, too. She shouldn't be fooled so easily.
female_content: Ms. Chief, when you go back after this mission, please get that child to read more. She's from Syndicate, too. She shouldn't be fooled so easily.

speaker: Hella
content: You little ducker! Come face me if you have the balls! Don't hide behind a phone!

speaker: Hecate
content: Quiet. You'll attract the enemy's attention and put us in danger.
This is common banter between the two, but Hecate's tone is exceptionally cold.

speaker: Hella
content: Nonsense! You can barely hear me over the screeches of this old railcar. Right, ${PlayerName}?

speaker: Hella
content: Why do you look so grumpy? Hecate, you've been acting really weird lately. Did you pop the wrong pills?
She waves her hand in front of Hecate, who ignores her and goes to keep an eye on the other side.

speaker: Hella
content: ...What's the matter with you... Hey ${PlayerName}, do you know what's going on?
You checked—her physical and mental states are normal, and so are your shackles. But Hecate feels like a different person, and she's even been avoiding your questions lately.
The only reason you can think of is the bloody battle with the Corpseborne. This triggers your pain and guilt—though they're battle-seasoned Sinners, they're still little girls.

speaker: Hecate
content: Stay alert. There's contamination ahead.
She cuts off your question once again.

speaker: Rust
content: You've entered BR-000's zone of influence. Though BR-000's core body is strictly controlled by the FAC, its radiation is expansive. The Inner Bay area is the most severely affected.

speaker: Rust
content: I think... buzz... buzz buzz... you will soon.... buzz... BR... 2...

speaker: Rust
content: Jammed... buzz...
Hecate stands up and fixes her gaze on the tunnel ahead. At almost the same time, the railcar stops, and several Rustfire members come out.
One of them goes straight to the front of the railcar and replaces the light. The color changes to the faint blue you're familiar with.

speaker: Rustfire Guard
content: We cleaned this just a few days ago. How did dirty things leak into it again?

speaker: Rustfire Guard
content: Be careful, Chief. You can't get hurt.
The others aim their guns at the dark tunnel ahead.
...Something's coming.

More blue lights were hung after that. After several battles, you finally reach the terminal—an abandoned, barely-refurbished building. It's a small, airtight space with no windows, so you can't see what's going on outside.
When you come up from the underground station, you see mountains of containers and supplies, as well as dozens of eyes staring at you from all directions.

speaker: Blue-Haired Gladiator
content: Ohh... So... that small, scrawny shorty... is our leader?
The one leading the pack sneers. She tries to step forward, but someone else stops her.

speaker: Rustfire Member
content: Don't make trouble! That's a very important person!
The crowd stares at you with anticipation, excitement, hesitation, and fear. Many of them are holding leaflets. You feel a bit suffocated from the atmosphere.

speaker: Black Raven
content: Caw... Caw...
The black raven suddenly lands on your shoulder. It tilts its head, caws, then flies off to a railing.
No one around you is surprised. You realize the raven is showing you the way.

The raven waits on the empty level. Only when you ask the two Sinners to guard the stairs and leave you alone does it continue to fly onwards, leading you to an empty office. Once inside, the raven disappears.

The room is quite messy, with maps, newspapers, and photos sprawled everywhere. It reminds you of Julien's office—only there's no machinery. You wait for a while, but no one comes, so you look around.
On the desk, you see some familiar papers with someone's writing on it. The writing has been crossed out and revised several times.
You're here. Welcome, Chief.
You rip open the envelope Julien gave you and take out the letter inside.
Hope you arrived safely. Now, as promised, I will tell you everything you need to know.

speaker: Julien's Letter
content:
You just came through DisCity's largest underground transport network.
If you had the chance to go above ground, you'd have seen a completely different side of Syndicate.

Grand buildings, meticulous design, stability, wealth, hope— everything was neat and orderly. 
This was West District's Inner Bay, the birthplace of DisCity's Hypercube industry.
People dammed the farthest end of DisSea, carving out some relatively stable waters. 
They then dug deep mines in Inner Bay.

speaker: Julien's Letter
content:
The Hypercube was the treasure they "stole back" with their wisdom from the fearsome DisSea. 

It was the only strategic resource in the era of Nightfall, 

and the bedrock of DisCity's prosperity and status.

speaker: Julien's Letter
content:
<color=#fb9259>People</color> were the foundation of Inner Bay's industry, 
and many talented workers gathered here.
Back then, mech technology wasn't advanced to penetrate Mania fields.
Senior technicians had to manually operate mechs to dig one mine after another.
In N.F. 84, the DisSea Explosion occurred, giving birth to BR-000.
By the time the Broken Frontline was formed, 95% of Inner Bay had been contaminated.
Hypercube production plummeted, hitting DisCity's economic and political status hard.

speaker: Julien's Letter
content:
Inner Bay's workers were the ones who stayed behind in the ravaged mining zone 
to help DisCity pull through its most difficult period. 
They formed militias to fight the emerging gangsters, guarded the remaining mines against 
further contamination, and gave it their all to boost Hypercube reserves.
Sorry for saying so much, but that was the West District we were once so proud of. 
The people back then were the noblest souls of the golden age. We all love Syndicate deeply.
Next, let's talk about BR-002, which is the Black Ring you want to investigate.

speaker: Julien's Letter
content:
In N.F. 104, automated mining tech became common across Eastside. 
On the other hand, due to contamination, outdated equipment and work injury compensation costs, 
Inner Bay was deemed a negative asset by the higher-ups and discarded.

But the workers didn't want to give up. 
They begged the company to keep the mines and outdated equipment, so as to preserve 
West District's economic lifeline.

speaker: Julien's Letter
content:
In the end, the company agreed to the workers' demands on the condition that they give up 
all claim to compensation. The two sides completed the handover of the largest mine W-31 
on November 25. Inner Bay won for Syndicate its own Hypercube mine.

But on November 28, an incident erupted in W-31.
Workers got trapped and contamination spread into the mine, 
which soon developed into a Black Ring—<color=#fb9259>BR-002</color>.

speaker: Julien's Letter
content:
We have very little data on BR-002. BR-000 and 002 were too close in proximity, triggering the mass spread of Mania. BR-000 expanded rapidly, and was barely halted at the FAC's third Broken Frontline.
The radiation from the contaminated zone continued to seep out, eventually covering all of Inner Bay.
The industrial zone became completely isolated from the outside world. Not even the FAC could penetrate this layer of contamination.
After a few years, they confirmed that the M-value inside disappeared, but could not confirm the reason why, hence they left. The survivors of Inner Bay, including their family members, total around 200 people.
Afterwards, the <color=#fb9259>Drifter Camp</color> was formed.

speaker: Julien's Letter
content:
As for those who were trapped in the mine, I could only confirm the names of 13,004 of them. 
<color=#fb9259>The Romanesque monument</color> was built in their honor.

You asked us about our relationship with BR-002—this is it.
I've also told you everything I know about BR-002.

If you want to know more, please go to the next page.
There's very little content on this page.

speaker: Julien's Letter
content:
Since you've made it this far, welcome to Shelter W-31.
Like I said, this is the easiest place for you to complete your mission. 
Once you leave the shelter, you can take a boat across Inner Bay to Mine W-31 in ten minutes. 
This is also the ruins of BR-002.

This was once the Corpseborne's base. You said the half that fled is great at hiding 
because it leaves no traces, since all the contamination gets transferred to the dead half.

speaker: Julien's Letter
content:
Well, lucky you, because the dead half is at the bottom of W-31.
Once you destroy this half, the other half will no longer be able to hide its contamination, naturally exposing itself. Rustfire will show you the way. 
The fighters here are at your command. 
This shelter, which has been a sanctuary for Inner Bay's workers since before the Broken Frontline, has got your back. 
We couldn't let go of our past, so we came back and did what even the FAC couldn't.
We used Inner Bay technology to resurrect the shelter, and stockpiled enough Hypercubes to hold off the contamination.

speaker: Julien's Letter
content:
The battle might be tough, but you can always come back to recharge your supplies.
If I told you this is your reward for helping the Drifter Camp, you wouldn't believe me. 
You're always such a cautious person.

Yes, we each have our own goals, but they're all for the future of Syndicate.
If you're willing to guard our secret from your superiors...
Then please read on.
There's only one line on this page.
Her head lowered, she chokes and shudders, no longer able to string together a full sentence.
You freeze for a second. Just as you're about to flip to the next page, the paper sticks to your hand. To your incredulity, you realize the ink is moving. You hear a woman's voice...
You're reading too slowly, Mr. Chief. Let me read it out loud for you.
female_content: You're reading too slowly, Ms. Chief. Let me read it out loud for you.

content: A women's voice snaps you out of your shock. The ink blots suddenly jump off the paper—some wrap around your hand, and some gather in front of you.
Incredibly, they shapeshift into the form of a human.

speaker: Executive Officer?
content: I came here together with you, Chief.

speaker: Executive Officer?
content: I read the rest already. Let me tell you their real motive.

speaker: Executive Officer?
content: They want to take over a Black Ring and turn it into a mining zone for West District. Their next step is to engage in smuggling, and collude with the Outlands to undermine the economy and security of DisCity!

speaker: Executive Officer?
content: This is a serious crime! All of DisCity's Hypercubes belong to the state. Any Black Ring ruins or leftover mines in West District are under the jurisdiction of the Executive Committee. <color=#fb9259>Nirvana</color> is the only company legally entitled to use them!

speaker: Executive Officer?
content: Chief, you've made a great discovery. Come, let's wipe out these traitors together.

speaker: Executive Officer?
content: Wait? You want to cover for them? You've made new friends since the Legion rebellion?

speaker: Executive Officer?
content: You want to betray us, the 9th Agency, and DisCity again?
The ink wraps around your neck. You can feel the power of a Sinner from it.
In front of you is just a phantom of ink coalescence. The real mastermind is behind you!
You cast your shackles backward, piercing through a larger mass of black ink. A figure dodges your attack. The ink raises her high, and she looks down at you.
Haha. Good reaction.
Relax. I didn't come to fight. I just wanted to make this once-in-a-lifetime encounter with you more dramatic and memorable. Now, let's have a proper introduction.
Hello, Chief. I'm the shelter liaison.
I'm also a Rustfire publicist, Syndicate war correspondent, renowned Drifter Camp author, DisCity ghost writer, and the greatest romantic poet of our time.
I am Raye, but you can call me by my beautiful pen name...

speaker: Raven
content: <color=#fb9259>Raven</color>. I write poems with darkness, and I've come to record this magnificent mission.

<size=31>She returns to the ground. Half of the ink goes into the ink bottle on her right arm, while the other half turns into the black raven that had come with you all this way. The tall woman strikes a graceful pose, and the bird lands gently on her uplifted hand.</size>

speaker: Raven
content: A perfect debut.

speaker: Raven
content: It'd be even better if the audience would show some excitement.
She shuts her eyes to indulge in the moment. You stare at her with pursed lips, counting the seconds in your heart.

speaker: Raven
content: A shy friend, I see. If you're too bashful for words, why not give me a round of applause?
Raven stays in the same pose until you finally clap a few times. She then opens her eyes with a smile.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Hello, Raven. I'm the Chief of the Minos Bureau of Crisis Control, a new friend of Rustfire, an old friend of Syndicate, the heartthrob of DisCity, and... <color=#fb9259>a Mania magnet wherever I go</color>.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: My name is ${PlayerName}. I have no pen name. You can call me "Dear Chief."
Raven laughs, jots down everything in a small notebook, and applauds you dramatically.

speaker: Raven
content: Yes, perfect. Smile and relax, just like that. You look better when you smile.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If I had opened the envelope before I got here, you would've killed me with your "ink," right?

speaker: Raven
content: My, still holding a grudge? I already told you, those were just some dramatic effects for my "debut."

options: Your outfit reminds me of someone...

content: (Scene change)

speaker: Executive Officer
content: Don't resist the orders, don't hinder the execution, or else...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You fit right in with the execs.

speaker: Raven
content: It's part of a journalist's job to do undercover investigations. I've received special training in Eastside.

speaker: Raven
content: Don't worry. Right now, the Executive Committee only regards you as a fool who's ignorant of the rules, not an enemy. They don't dare touch you. After all, you've got the MBCC, FAC, and 9th Agency behind you.

speaker: Choice
options: Looks like you investigated me as well.

speaker: Raven
content: Hehe, I'm a top-notch reporter. Getting the inside scoop, catching eyes, stirring things up and making them go viral—I can do it all.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Are you a member of Rustfire, too?

speaker: Raven
content: Yes, but I have an office job. I don't like violence.

speaker: Raven
content: <size=31>I go undercover to collect intelligence and make my mark on the battleground of public opinion. More importantly, I witness, record, and broadcast those magnificent feats to ignite hope in people's hearts and attract more like-minded companions.</size>

speaker: Raven
content: People often praise my radiant presence by calling me "grandiose."

speaker: Raven
content: If they are the fire upon the rust, then I am the wind that sweeps the land. My words can spark a raging wildfire.
"Regardless of creed or color, come fight for justice! The hero from the Bureau has joined our side! The architect Julien weeps with joy and faints on the operating table!"
You let out a sigh.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I thought journalists would focus on telling the truth.

speaker: Raven
content: Journalists are warriors, too. The truth is just one of the weapons we wield.

options: Then what do you fight for?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You fight injustice and fate like Rustfire? You also want to take back what was lost?

speaker: Raven
content: No, I fight for love.
She suddenly edges close to you and stares into your eyes.

speaker: Raven
content: I love those who struggle in the dark. I love their souls that are torn by despair. I love their eyes that are awash with tears, and how they shine after suffering pain and torment.

speaker: Raven
content: Tragic, dramatic, and brimming with passion, they cling onto the faintest sliver of hope and plunge into the darkness. The fiery sparks of their dreams are but drops in the ocean, to be forever devoured by the darkness.

speaker: Raven
content: Yet this is precisely why that fleeting spark is so dazzling. I must witness and record everything up close, so as to immortalize their lives in my poetry.

speaker: Raven
content: That's right. I'd rather be regarded as the "DisCity Poet" than a renowned journalist. My dream is for my poems to be read across this land for all eternity.
...Immortal poetry? She needs to work on her language skills, then.

speaker: Raven
content: Haha, you have the same look as Julien the first time I told him this. Most of the Rustfire folks had the same reaction. You'll get along just fine.
She suddenly squeezes your chin.

speaker: Raven
content: But I actually looked forward to your arrival, dear Chief. Or should I say... I looked forward to the Shackler of Sinners, the Destroyer of Black Rings, and the Shepherd of DisCity.

speaker: Raven
content: Tell me what you've been up to. I've missed out on so many things lately.

speaker: Raven
content: Tell me about that riveting speech you gave in the Drifter Camp. Tell me what you were thinking when you almost died from that fall.

speaker: Raven
content: How did you convince the Legion? And how did you face "Zoya's" wrath?

speaker: Raven
content: What was on your mind during the chaos of the Carnival?

speaker: Raven
content: Tell me about your Sinners, your shackles, your superiors, and those who have died for you. Tell me about your lost memories and uncertain future.

speaker: Raven
content: What kind of darkness have you witnessed? And why are you still here?

speaker: Raven
content: What are you in pursuit of?
She edges closer to you as if she wanted to devour you alive.

speaker: Raven
content: Tell me. I will use every detail to craft the most authentic representation of you.

speaker: Raven
content: Many believe you can bring about change. They look up to your resolve and yearn for your guidance, and long for you to lead and enlighten them.

speaker: Raven
content: If I use my pen and paper to craft you into a star, to an idol, I'd definitely be able to create a heroic epic! Those in the dark yearn for light and hope the most. They need a hero.

speaker: Raven
content: Will you be this hero? Become the object of my odes, and realize each other's dreams?

speaker: Choice
options: I didn't do it on purpose.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If you're talking about what I said back at the Drifter Camp... I made that up to defeat the Corpseborne. Can I skip this one out?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You guys be the leaders. I have other things to do.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I don't need any odes. Nor do I want to get involved with plans I don't know about.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm here to get rid of the Black Ring, not to be forced into becoming some leader.

speaker: Raven
content: Hahaha! No problem! Remember these words, then. Play your role well.
She pats you on the cheek and leaves you.

speaker: Raven
content: It really is hard for me to fight for you, write poems about you and make sure you don't die at the same time. But I have a better plan to realize my dreams.

speaker: Raven
content: After I become famous in Eastside, I'll return to Syndicate and work with Rustfire to open a school upon the ruins that'll educate the next generation.

speaker: Raven
content: That way, my poems can be passed down generation after generation through my students!

speaker: Raven
content: I've got my eyes on those two little Sinners of yours. Children shouldn't be on the battlefield. Why not send them to be educated at my school?

options: I think it's better if you hired other teachers...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Please spare Syndicate's children.
Raven is already immersed in her own fantasies.

speaker: Raven
content: No worries. You fight your Black Ring, and I'll write my poems. We'll each live our best lives.

speaker: Raven
content: In any case, the ensuing battle will be a much-needed ray of light for this dark era. Grave perils, dark secrets, and even a turning point in history... plus you, an interesting soul.

speaker: Raven
content: This is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity.
She gleefully takes a comb out of nowhere and starts changing up your hairstyle. You feel a bit dizzy from all the combing.

speaker: Raven
content: By the way, since we have some time to chat, I want to tell you that I sold those two kids of yours.

speaker: Raven
content: I'm just joking.
She suddenly aims a camera at you. Snap—the flash blinds your eyes.
The picture prints out quickly. She shakes it and takes a look, apparently satisfied.

speaker: Raven
content: This one's not bad. Your gaze looks sharp, and shows your fighting spirit.

speaker: Raven
content: We leave in half an hour. I'll go prepare the mobilization. Apart from the elite few who will go down into the mine with you, the people waiting above also need some reassuring.

speaker: Raven
content: Don't worry. With my writing skills, I'll be sure to paint a glowing picture of you.

speaker: Choice
options: What are you going to write?

content: You find out for yourself soon enough. It doesn't take long for everyone to get their hands on identical leaflets hot off the press.

speaker: Raven's Leaflet
content:
The darkness of West District rears its head again!
The mysterious force that destroyed the Legion and nourished the gangs appears in the Drifter Camp.
Why is the Executive Committee ignoring it?

Was the Legion really destroyed? Or did they just go into hiding?
Exclusive reveal! The Drifter Camp's mysterious savior is actually Legion Captain Zoya's...
You feel everyone's burning gaze on you.

speaker: Julien
content: Rustfire's propaganda style is a bit dramatic, and sometimes... stretches the truth. This is just to catch people's eyes. To win people over, we have to be seen first.

speaker: Raven
content: Uncover the truth, then use it to mobilize the public. See how excited everyone is?

speaker: Raven
content: By the way, do you want to call Julien? He should be awake from his surgery by now.

speaker: Raven
content: Even though communications are cut off in Inner Bay, I can use my ink raven for long-distance communication. You two leaders can mobilize together.
You rip the leaflet in your hands to shreds, and also confiscate the ones in Hecate and Hella's hands. Raven laughs and waves behind her.

speaker: Raven
content: Everyone, next up is the battle for BR-002! The future of Syndicate is here!

speaker: Raven
content: All right! This is the fateful place where our hopes, glories, and comrades-in-arms are buried. West District might crumble, but even if we are buried, forgotten, and reduced to dust, we will never truly die.

speaker: Raven
content: Go take back our mines, take back West District's Hypercubes, and everything else that rightfully belongs to us, including the future!

speaker: Raven
content: Eight years ago, the fire snuffed out here. 8 years later, this is where the fire shall be rekindled!
Her passionate proclamations echo throughout the mines, stirring up the crowd's fighting spirit...

The mine is an inward-facing, ring-shaped structure that dams the contaminated waters to form a hollow, tiered interior. Each level ranges between a few dozen to a hundred meters high, and cascades onto lower platforms a dozen meters wide.

<size=29>The levels descend into the depths. Beyond the third level is total darkness. Contaminated liquids flow down the walls into the precipitation pools on the platforms. As long as the mine's Mania field is kept relatively low, the precipitation pool can continuously produce Hypercubes.</size>

<size=29>Too bad this grand structure has long stopped operating. The precipitation pool is now dirty and clogged, while the huge elevator to the side is broken. You can only use the safety rope to go down level after level, passing by remnants of the Black Ring that are suspended mid-air.</size>
Finally, you land on a wider platform. In this windless abyss, the only echoes are of Hella's complaints.

speaker: Hella
content: ... Ugh... Finally here... Whose idea was it to use that kind of rope to come down? What if a monster attacked in mid-air?

speaker: Raven
content: Don't worry, there aren't many "monsters" at this depth. People haven't come to Inner Bay for a long time, so there aren't any new Corruptors to be born, while the old Corruptors have all gone to DisSea. It's not that scary here.

speaker: Raven
content: If you're really scared, I'll warn you in advance. There are only two things to watch out for—

speaker: Raven
content: One, <color=#fb9259>machines</color> that can still move.
