content: Our enemy clearly possesses some kind of metal that strongly resonates with Ash Crystals, even channeling the power of the Apostles of Ashes. If that is indeed Aurum Secretum, we need samples for further study.

speaker: Adelaide
content: The Fraser ambassador is currently discussing this matter with DisCity representatives. Some samples have already been submitted to the Ring Research Institute.

speaker: Adelaide
content: With all respect, Chief, Fraser's Aurum Secretum research focuses solely on civilian safety applications, which differs from the modified version the attacker employed. The data we're providing may have limited utility against your enemy.
He hands over a specification document.

Classification: Resonant Synthetic Metal | Extraction Grade: S | Safety Level: High
Code Name: Aurum Secretum
Source: Fraser Rare Earth Minerals
Usage: Aurum Secretum's core mechanism relies on its powerful resonance and amplification properties. When fused with DisCity's precious Hypercube medium, it can be forged into various protective devices capable of resisting Mania-corrupted environments and diverting the paths of calamities.
Except for high-purity Aurum Secretum, standard Aurum Secretum devices exhibit exceptional safety ratings and are extensively deployed across Fraser.

speaker: Adelaide
content: Not everyone can use Aurum Secretum. Its powerful resonance properties require users to share compatible Mania attributes, which means only select Sinners with specific affinities can wield it effectively. This creates a fundamental distinction from Hypercubes, you see.

speaker: Adelaide
content: After years of investigation, Fraser has compiled a list of suspects, including the perpetrator Jelena. This list has already been submitted to the 9th Agency by our ambassador. We hope it proves valuable to your efforts.

speaker: Adelaide
content: From your perspective, all people outside DisCity are collectively referred to as the Outlanders, but the reality is far more nuanced. The Outlands consist of countless scattered communities, each with its own scale, level of development, and distinct ideologies.

speaker: Adelaide
content: Fraser inherited substantial pre-Nightfall assets and trade routes, which naturally positioned us as a hub between settlements. The Farland Alliance was thus formed, a cooperative framework for mutual support and resource sharing in the post-Nightfall era.

speaker: Adelaide
content: However, the Farland Alliance does not—and cannot—extend to all settlements. Even among our members, we cannot compel factions to alter their stances. Many conflicts persist, resistant to quick resolution, and the grievances of years are not so easily set aside.

speaker: Adelaide
content: Nevertheless, Fraser's priorities lie in commerce. Our advocacy for peace and our active promotion of the Great Expo are driven in part by a desire to mend relations between DisCity and the Outlands. I must say, I hold particularly high hopes for this Expo's success.

speaker: Adelaide
content: Beyond this matter, there's crucial intelligence I must deliver to you personally.
He clasps his hands together and leans forward, his gaze at you growing more intent.

speaker: Adelaide
content: Aurum Secretum was initially designed solely to alter environmental Mania fields, with no capability of evoking resonance between Sinners and the Apostles of Ashes. Through secret investigation, I discovered that those who distorted our technology belong to an underground network... a mysterious organization. I hear they go by a different name here...

speaker: Adelaide
content: <color=#fb9259>The DisCity dark web</color>, or as you might call them, the Underground. They are your enemy, are they not?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...! You're saying the Underground is behind all this?

speaker: Adelaide
content: They are indeed stirring animosity among Outlanders towards DisCity, and Jelena can't be the only Aurum Secretum user. The Outlands are vast, sparsely populated, and ravaged by calamities, making both investigations and apprehensions difficult. While Fraser acknowledges the threat, we lack the resources to address it fully. Frankly, some may have already infiltrated through the Great Expo.

speaker: Adelaide
content: —But I'm sure you've already taken all of this into account, hence your vigilance towards me and readiness for conflict. However, what I wish to convey is that this approach alone may not suffice to resolve all issues.

speaker: Adelaide
content: Hatred requires fertile ground to take root and grow. Unless DisCity reconsiders its approach toward the Outlands, I fear you will only end up cultivating more enemies.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...What are you getting at?
[Scene Change]

speaker: Hecate
content: ...It's been too long. They've kept Chief in there for too long.

speaker: Hecate
content: If what you're saying is true, that someone made that accident happen on purpose to make Chief show up... why would they do that?

${PlayerName} may be crucial to anti-Mania operations, yet holds no sway in diplomatic affairs. Among the group gathered just now—a representative from Nirvana, an advisor from Fraser, and a financier known as the stock market guru from Eastside—what could they be discussing?

Recently, Nirvana has been flooding the market with signals: during the Great Expo, they will negotiate Aurum Secretum technology cooperation with Fraser to optimize unmanned mechanical mining systems. To cut risk while severing their reliance on the West District's manual miners.

During the height of the Outlander spy investigations earlier, Nirvana reclaimed a considerable share of external Hypercube trade and transportation from Quinn. Though they've since conceded some control in their deal with Fraser, the benefit is already reaped—their stock prices have skyrocketed to unprecedented levels.

Nirvana and Fraser have also rallied the support of many influential figures. Their machine is in motion, and those who oppose them will be ground to dust. Profit is their only creed, and for it, they will burn the world to ashes. To them, ${PlayerName} is just another pawn, a bargaining chip with moderate value.
But what troubles her even more is...

She bites her lip as memories flood back to her final conversation with that person before his death. Stewart, clutching a half-burned incense stick, had urged his daughter to commit its scent to memory.

speaker: Stewart
content: You're my daughter, and one day you'll inevitably walk down my path. So remember what I've told you, and stay away from this scent.

speaker: Stewart
content: No matter what they promise you, no matter how desperate your situation becomes, you stay away from them. The price is far more than you can bear.
Elvira's jaw locks. That scent sears her memory even now. Of course she would recognize it instantly.

speaker: Elvira
content: That woman just now has the same scent on her. If those people are involved and making deals with Fraser...

Suspicions pile up like storm clouds in Elvira's mind, pulling her deeper into thought until words spill out—unfiltered, unguarded. But she is no longer hidden in that safe cage. Here, every word voiced carries a price.

speaker: Hecate
content: Are you saying that Chief is in danger?

speaker: Elvira
content: This is just my hunch. I...
She wants to say she might be overthinking things, but it's already too late. Hecate instinctively tenses up, causing Nightmare to expand, and then...
[Alarm Blaring]

speaker: Fraser Ambassador
content: Advisor! Mania detected. It's an ambush!
Schorl emerges from your pocket.

speaker: Schorl
content: Conflict identified. Switching to Combat Mode. Threat elimination imminent—

speaker: Max King
content: Now, now, everyone. Just a little false alarm! Let's not allow this to cloud the bright future of our wonderful relations, shall we?

speaker: Max King
content: Tell the reporters outside that both delegations were exchanging anti-Mania technologies. Have maintenance turn back the clock. I want this place spotless in ten hours. Leave the paperwork and politics to me, and rest easy knowing the Speaker of DisCity got your backs! Now, any objections?

speaker: Max King
content: I've already called in people from the Bureau. You lovely young ladies will be going back with them, alright?
He looks at the two girls with an amiable grin on his face, though his voice grows increasingly cold. Elvira instinctively retreats behind Hecate for protection.

speaker: Max King
content: Now you remember to hide? Well, lucky for you, it's not too late yet. There are plenty of paparazzi lenses out there for you to hide from. If that face of yours gets seen again, we won't be just talking about silly gossip.

speaker: Max King
content: That Chief will be in big trouble.
Elvira's face drains of color as King fixes her with a cold stare while voicing the warning. Then, he walks away, striding past you without even a glance, his countenance heavy with shadows.
Surprisingly, the Fraser advisor, who was supposedly ambushed, gazes at the scolded Elvira with a look of admiration.

speaker: Adelaide
content: Our Speaker's being too harsh, isn't he? At this age, few would have the courage to come all the way here. Her concerns were valid, and in fact, the depth of her consideration speaks to remarkable wisdom.

speaker: Adelaide
content: Are you Speaker Stewart's daughter? Your father raised you well.
Elvira frowns, showing no appreciation for the compliment. She remains hidden behind Hecate, and you notice her quietly clenching her fists.
Adelaide seems unfazed. He gestures to his Fraser companions nearby as if to say, "I'll be right there." Then, he turns to you.

speaker: Adelaide
content: I wish for peace between city-states, just as I earnestly hope siblings might always treat one another with mutual respect and love.

speaker: Adelaide
content: DisCity was once the youngest, carefully nurtured by its elders. Now, like Fraser, you've matured into the strongest of human city-states... and with that strength comes an elder sibling's duty to guide those who follow.

speaker: Adelaide
content: DisCity holds this era's one and only survival resource. Do not exploit it for greed, wield it to enslave the weak, nor humiliate those already in anguish. The Hypercube should exist to preserve life. Never let it become a source of sins.

speaker: Adelaide
content: And please, halt this descent. Tend to the Promised Land beneath you with care. Even the faintest Black Ring born here may send catastrophic ripples afar, claiming lives tenfold elsewhere.

speaker: Adelaide
content: Chief, I know you have personally faced the Outland spy who wields Aurum Secretum to summon corruptive rain. This is why I trust you to grasp my meaning, why I believe you're unlike the rest...

speaker: Adelaide
content: Much like lovely little Hella, who always has your name on her lips.
[CG: Waiting for Handshake]
He stands up and extends his hand to you.

speaker: Adelaide
content: Of course, I believe in your ability to inspire change. You once changed Syndicate and brought hope to half the city. Why shouldn't the world be next?

speaker: Adelaide
content: I hope this Great Expo can be the catalyst we need. Let it begin with you and me—mutual understanding, mutual trust—and from there, we address humanity's true challenges together.

speaker: Adelaide
content: You have my sincerest appreciation.

speaker: Adelaide
content: Take your time. We still have plenty before this is over.
You ask Schorl to step aside.

speaker: Schorl
content: Understood. As agreed, I interact only with you alone, Chief. Shutting down now.
Now, only the three of you remain.

speaker: Hecate
content: ...Chief, I'm sorry.

speaker: Elvira
content: I was overthinking and ended up scaring Hecate. I didn't know you had such a strong guard and was being reckless...

speaker: Elvira
content: ...No, you've always been cautious. It's my fault. I keep imagining things that aren't real. I'm sorry...
The two girls bow their heads, voices hushed, looking like children confessing to having broken a vase.

speaker: Option
options: Actually, you two helped me big there.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: To be honest, I was at my wit's end in there. Thank you for saving me.

speaker: Hecate
content: ...Really?
You nod like a bobblehead doll.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Just promise me you'll be more careful next time, okay? Or at least give me a heads-up first.
Only then does she smile.

speaker: Hecate
content: I understand. I trust you, Chief.
But the other girl still looks worried. An FAC troop has arrived at the entrance, ready to escort them back. Before saying goodbye, you think for a moment and quietly call her over.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: About that Adelaide guy, he's really strong, but has one weakness. You absolutely must remember...

speaker: Elvira
content: ...What is it?
You lean in with a serious expression, speaking in a hushed voice. Catching your tension, Elvira nervously grips the hem of her dress and brings her ear closer to hear what you have to say...

speaker: Option
options: That guy has a creepy sister complex.

speaker: Elvira
content: ...Huh?
You deliberately feign a serious expression.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I heard it with my own ears... It's terrifying. All girls should stay away from him, and I need you to do the same, okay? I really need you on the team, and I promise to share intelligence with you and always hear you out.

speaker: Elvira
content: ...Pfft. Okay, got it.
She finally relaxes, her face brightening with a smile more fitting for someone her age.

June ??, N.F. 115
Location: ??
A sandstorm chokes the path, forcing the traveler into a nest of sandworms—the creatures long dead, their burrow now a tomb turned shelter.

speaker: Sibilla
content: ...! Cough, cough—

speaker: Sibilla
content: ...I passed out? How long has it been?

She rolls onto her stomach, pressing her ear to the ground. Breath held, mind sharpened to a blade's edge, she listens. Through the sandstorm, the heavy, rhythmic rumbling in the distance seems to have truly ceased.

speaker: Sibilla
content: ...Lost them... thank goodness...
Huff...

A warm breath tickles her ear. Sibilla shudders—her nerves scream jump, but her exhausted muscles refuse. She chokes on a gasp, still sprawled on the ground. Her traveling companion, pleased with the successful prank, breaks into giggles.

speaker: Sibilla
content: ...Oh, Jasmine. You almost scared me to death. When did you sneak up on me? You're as quiet as a cat.
The woman named Jasmine rises to her tiptoes and spins in a circle. Her tattered cloak flutters, lifting just enough to betray her graceful, nimble figure beneath.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Heh, I do wish I were a cat. Nine lives to spare, free to face whatever comes my way. Here, have some water.

speaker: Jasmine
content: You've been out cold forever. Another hour and you'd have baked into proper human jerky.

speaker: Sibilla
content: Uh, is this really water...? Or...

The first time Sibilla accepted this flask was after they escaped a group of desert bandits. Jasmine killed her way through, then pressed the flask into Sibilla's hands with a smile. Water, she called it. But the stench—rusty and metallic—clings to Sibilla's memory to this day. She didn't dare to ask what kind of water it was back then, only to suffer nightmares for a week straight after drinking it.
But she has no choice but to drink. To continue her journey, she must steel her resolve.

speaker: Sibilla
content: ...Okay, that'll restore strength... restore strength... restore strength... Alright, drink it and I'll hit the road! *Gulp*

speaker: Sibilla
content: Hmm...? The taste is different? It's sweet?

speaker: Jasmine
content: Oh, did you think that was blood? Silly, we haven't seen another soul for ages! Where would I even get extra blood? And honestly, I'd hate to traumatize you all over again.

speaker: Jasmine
content: We still have a long way to go before we get you to the Great Expo. Can't have you losing that spark along the way.

Sibilla has never learned where Jasmine came from. Their paths crossed on a bandit ship, where Sibilla was kidnapped "cargo" and Jasmine seemed to be a hired blade working for the bandits, assigned to guard the cages holding the captives.

To survive, Sibilla tried her best to build rapport with this unpredictable girl, hoping to create a chance to escape. But when that day finally came, Sibilla was shocked to see Jasmine catch up to her. Just like that, Jasmine left her bandit "comrades" behind without a second glance, and Sibilla couldn't fathom why.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Because you share your food and water with me.

The desert bandits had apparently kept Jasmine for quite some time. When the two escaped, the bandits' rage burned hotter than the midday sun. Armed with rattling Gatling guns, they chased them all night without stopping.
Jasmine was treated as a prized fighter. At the very least, she shouldn't have lacked food or water.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Mmm... well, because that DisCity gala you mentioned sounds like fun. I want to go too.
The desert bandits had clearly set their sights on the Great Expo as well. They had been ramping up their attacks on Outland trade caravans traveling during this window of opportunity.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Those desert bandits have become scaredy cats these days. Won't even look at DisCity, and won't let me near it either, saying that I'd stir up trouble... Where's the fun in that?

speaker: Jasmine
content: But you're different from them, Sibilla. I know you'll keep pushing forward without hesitation. If I follow you, I'll find my way. And I'll find what I'm looking for.

speaker: Jasmine
content: So take me to DisCity! I've never been there before. Can't wait to have fun!
Yet her Disian is flawless, showing no trace of the common tongue spoken in Fraser and elsewhere. That's a distinction only those born within the city's walls ever truly master.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Oh, really? Hmm... Maybe I'm just a natural with languages?

speaker: Jasmine
content: Hold on, that's not it. It's my blades that speak Disian. I just picked it up after listening to them for years. Don't believe me? Go ahead, touch them and see for yourself.
It truly is a peculiar pair of blades, one that sends shivers down the spine if stared at too long. Yet Sibilla can't help but reach out her hand...

speaker: Jasmine
content: Just kidding! Don't touch it.

The woman whisks the blades away with a giggle. She often speaks in riddles like this. It is hard to tell if this stems from cultural differences between city-states, the peculiar wiring of her mind, or perhaps...
Sibilla doesn't want to entertain the notion, but Jasmine's power seems to be having a negative effect on her.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Good people like you shouldn't dirty those hands with weapons. You're going there for the celebration, so keep that joy simple and clean. Let me handle the sharp things.

speaker: Sibilla
content: Then what about you, Jasmine? Where do you come from?

speaker: Jasmine
content: Hmm... I don't remember.

speaker: Sibilla
content: I see. Then why do you want to go to DisCity?

speaker: Jasmine
content: I don't remember.
Jasmine's gaze flickers away for a fleeting moment.

speaker: Jasmine
content: I guess the blades want me to go. Yeah, simple as that. And I can protect you along the way. Perfect, right? Alright, that's enough chatter.
She rises to her feet, her expression alert, yet her eyes light up with an eerie spark.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Something's coming. Tuck yourself away nice and tight. And no peeking.

speaker: Shadow Behemoth
content: Hiss... Hisssssss...
With a deafening roar, a colossal sandworm bursts forth from the sand.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Just a worm? And here I was, thinking my moment had finally come.

speaker: Sibilla
content: A sandworm? How did it find us? And why is it so agitated...

speaker: Jasmine
content: Oh! I just remembered. While you were snoozing, I went to fetch water and stumbled on a nest of worm eggs. Since you are not a fan of blood, I thought I'd change things up. Just give these worm babies a squeeze, and they make a pretty tasty drink, you know.

speaker: Sibilla
content: ...That's even worse than blood!
The battle is taking longer than usual. Growing worried, Sibilla leaves the cave to search for Jasmine.

speaker: Sibilla
content: Jasmine?
[Small CG]

The sandworm lies in pieces, its segmented body still writhing on the ground. If not for the precision of each cut, the sight might have resembled the aftermath of wild beasts tearing each other apart. And at the heart of the carnage kneels Jasmine, smiling. Her posture is hauntingly graceful, like a dancer frozen in sculpture.

speaker: Sibilla
content: Jasmine, these wounds...
She slowly sits up, and as her body temperature rises, over a dozen crimson blade wounds gradually sprawl across her skin.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Wounds? Heh, I didn't even realize I had any. Probably slipped my mind. Must've been a long time ago.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Don't worry, these worms couldn't hurt me even if they tried. I'm just... thrilled. I figured they wouldn't be the only ones coming...
But something is wrong with Jasmine. Worried, Sibilla steps closer, only to feel something hard beneath her foot.
Glancing down, she notices a piece of machinery with cloth-wrapped flesh dangling from it. Upon closer inspection, she realizes it's half of a human palm.

speaker: Sibilla
content: A soldier... No, this is... someone from DisCity?

speaker: Jasmine
content: Yes, it's them. I would never forget that scent.

Moonlight cuts through the haze, revealing several motionless, humanoid figures. The leader's neck bears a distinct gash wound, above which sits a cold iron mask. A single glance, and ice floods Sibilla's veins.
[Small CG 1]

Now Sibilla remembers. On her journey to DisCity, she has heard warnings of numerous dangers: mutations, sandworms, the Tide of Ashes, vicious desert bandits, and... a group of black ghosts, said to lurk within the sandstorms.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Look closely, Sibilla. These are WhiteSands' real monsters, so vicious even the desert bandits won't go near them. Keep your distance... never let them catch your scent.

speaker: Jasmine
content: They're not human—they're rabid hounds. Any Outlander who dares step near DisCity? They'll be hunted to the edge of the world, ripped apart, and devoured alive.
Yet contrary to her own words, Jasmine shows no trace of fear. Instead, she releases a soft, unsettling laugh.

speaker: Jasmine
content: So run away now. Far, far away. I'll be busy playing with them, and if I get too carried away... I can't promise you'll stay safe.

speaker: Jasmine
content: You're such a good person. Even I would be sad if you died.
[CG 2]
She staggers forward, clawing off the cloak wrapped around her body. Beneath it, blood-red gashes stripe her skin. The broken shackles at her ankles jingle with each step, delicate as wind chimes.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Let flame ignite the candles bright, not scorch the seedlings in the light.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Let arrows fly to strike the mark, not pierce a grandmother's tender heart.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Let parades roll through fields so wide, yet never steal dreams from inside. Let fireworks gleam in skies above, but never burn the homes of love.
[CG 3]

speaker: Jasmine
content: O traveler, when you join a celebration in a foreign land...

speaker: Jasmine
content: Leave blades of slaughter behind.
As her final word fades, she vanishes, leaving only a swirl of dust in her wake, not even a footprint behind.

The iron mask's gaze sweeps over the carnage—shattered mechanical hands, torn black uniforms strewn among the corpses. When he looks up again, the woman stands merely inches away, twin crimson blades glowing at her sides.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: ...You Outland mongrel.
The moon slips behind the clouds again, surrendering everything to darkness. The vast landscape holds its breath, silent but for the faint tread of bare feet on the sand.
Sibilla's breath stalls in her chest, her body rigid as stone. She scans the darkness, eyes straining for any trace of Jasmine, but the night has swallowed her whole.
In the distance, on the hillside, crimson flashes of blade-light flicker like trapped lightning, dancing against a wall of burnished metal.

speaker: Sibilla
content: They're spreading out fast... too fast! That speed isn't human! How many enemies are there?

speaker: Sibilla
content: Can Jasmine handle it?
The enemies' rigid formation initially hinders their advance, so they quickly scatter, regrouping into a suffocating ring of steel.
However, the bloodthirsty blades whirl forward, cleaving through flesh and metal alike, tearing the encirclement open from the middle.
No! The enemy has recognized Jasmine's speed. They're deliberately opening the encirclement, and the gap leads straight to...

speaker: Jasmine
content: Haha... Hahaha... Hahahaha!!

Amidst Jasmine's maniacal laughter, the violent crash of metal against metal rings out from the distance. Then, the shockwave hits. It ripples through the air, searing into Sibilla's mind with eerie familiarity. Just like before. Just like the calamity that once devastated her homeland.

speaker: Sibilla
content: This is... Mania?
Bang—

The shockwave tears through the air—the blast from some formidable weapon. Sibilla struggles to lift her head, and only then does she see that these enemies wield ominous weapons similar to Jasmine's.

speaker: Sibilla
content: Jasmine!! Watch out!
In the fierce confrontation, Jasmine dodges a barrage of heavy projectiles with several side flips and returns to Sibilla's side.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Oh my! Sibilla, what are you still doing here? You should be running! This isn't your show to play. It's dangerous to stay here. Hehh—!
As she speaks, she casually raises her blades and deflects several <color=#fb9259>glowing</color> bullets aimed at them.

speaker: Sibilla
content: Enough, Jasmine. There are too many of them, and they're coordinating well. You'll get overwhelmed at this rate. I can see you slowing down already.

speaker: Sibilla
content: They're regrouping. Now's our chance to get out! Those weapons... something's not right about them. They—
From a corner hidden from their view, the iron-masked man raises his hand towards the two and clenches his fist.

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...Ugh!
Without warning, several iron pillars wrench free from the ground, and crash into Jasmine's right shoulder.
Sibilla's earrings and the flying iron bullets plunge into the sand, swallowed by the unseen depths. Even her blood turns sluggish, a molten weight dragging through her veins.

speaker: Sibilla
content: ...Magnetism?
Jasmine's twin blades are also pinned to the earth, yet she clings to them, her grip unyielding even as it leaves her exposed.
In the distance, the red blade scar etched across the masked man's neck ignites. Even from afar, Sibilla sees it unfurl: a crimson flower blooming at his throat.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: That weapon doesn't belong to you. Where did you steal it from?

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...Heh, who knows why it picked me? Why don't you ask it yourself? It's being so loud right now... screaming...

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...for me to slit your throat!
She rises to charge back into battle, but a figure pounces on her without warning.

speaker: Sibilla
content: Watch out!
Sibilla throws herself over Jasmine as they tumble aside, narrowly avoiding the barrage that crashes nearby. The shockwave follows, flinging them even farther as debris rains down.

Gunfire cracks through the air again. Another ferocious barrage of bullets seems to be aiming directly at where they have landed, their trajectories indiscernible. Before Sibilla can react, Jasmine drags a sleeve across her bloodied lips, her blades flashing awake once more.

But in the next breath, she whirls around in astonishment. The chaotic gunfire isn't ahead of them at all. It's raking the enemy lines from behind, choking the enemy advance into sudden, eerie silence.
The masked man ceases his attack—not because of his enemy, but at the pulse of a special transmission.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: Hello...

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: Stop? Why?

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: ...I see. Please provide cover for our retreat.
The flower on his neck rapidly withers, followed by a magnetic pulse that twists Sibilla's stomach.

The reinforcements hidden beneath the sand seem to see through the enemy's intentions, hastily pursuing with a downpour of gunfire. Their bullets explode in midair, forming a wall of mist, yet not a single shot finds its mark.
[Transition]
When the wall of mist dissipates and silence falls, the steel ghosts have vanished without a trace.

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...They got away... I haven't even...
Her voice thins to a whisper as she crumples into Sibilla's arms. The crimson gashes across her body rapidly fade, and her skin grows cold...

speaker: Sibilla
content: Jasmine, Jasmine! Wake up! Don't die here!
She's suffering from severe Mania backlash and needs treatment. Let us handle this.

speaker: Sibilla
content: You are...?
From beneath the sand dunes, several cloaked figures shed their camouflage and quickly slide down the sandy slopes toward Sibilla and Jasmine, offering them a bow.
Wasting no time, they quickly administer first aid and protective measures to the unconscious woman before turning to address Sibilla in the common tongue thick with an unfamiliar accent.

speaker: The Joint Caravan
content: We're a trade caravan of the Farland Alliance, here for the Expo. Our camp is nearby, fully stocked with supplies and medicine. It's well-hidden and very safe.

speaker: The Joint Caravan
content: We're not from DisCity, and we mean her no harm. In fact... you've fought bravely against those DisCity mad dogs, and that alone makes you our allies.

speaker: Sibilla
content: ...Please, help her.

The camp crouches near a fresh rift in the WhiteSands, where several merchant ships huddle around, disguised to mimic the ships of desert bandits. Energy usage throughout the camp appears strictly rationed; by now, only a couple tents still pulse with light.
Outside the camp, the sandstorm rages on. It is clear they are taking extreme precautions to remain unseen. Jasmine is carried into a tent that appears to serve as a makeshift infirmary.

People bustle about taking inventory of goods, struggling to communicate in the common tongue, their words tinged with various accents. Sibilla lingers outside the medical tent, carefully studying her surroundings.

speaker: Caravan Member A
content: Her condition is stable now, and she should wake up after some sleep. Don't worry.

speaker: Caravan Member A
content: She may look delicate, but that girl's surprisingly tough and recovers at a shocking speed. Those were the devils of WhiteSands, yet she held her own all by herself. I've never seen a warrior like her before.

speaker: Caravan Member A
content: Oh, right, you got dragged into the fight too. Let me check on you...
She reaches out to Sibilla, only for her to recoil, instinct overriding trust. After a moment of contemplation, Sibilla finally speaks, each word measured.

speaker: Sibilla
content: ...Those weren't desert bandits who attacked us. Were they... soldiers from some proper army?

speaker: Sibilla
content: I've heard that DisCity has set up secure quarters for Outland caravans. Wouldn't you be safer if you relocated there?

speaker: Caravan Member A
content: Well... we asked DisCity officials, but they never gave straight answers. So honestly... I've got no clue where that troop came from. Those brutal bastards just keep attacking any Outlanders who get close to DisCity.
Before Sibilla can ask more questions, another voice cuts in—sharp, agitated.

speaker: Caravan Member B
content: Screw their "secure quarters"! Anyone with half a brain knows those are just pens DisCity set up to watch us. Who the hell would put up with that kind of insult?!

speaker: Caravan Member B
content: That patrol squad's obviously in on it with them! They gun down every Outlander in their sight without even a warning—yeah, I'm talking about those ************s we just fought!!
The man's temper burns quick and bright. After his angry outburst, he catches sight of Sibilla huddling in a defensive curl, his gaze sharpening with sudden suspicion.

speaker: Caravan Member B
content: Hey! What's the deal with that woman in surgery? I caught her accent. That's Disian through and through! You from DisCity? What's your tie to those mad dogs earlier? You two—Gah!
His knee suddenly gives way as though a force from behind has struck him, and his imposing figure, which has been looming over Sibilla, collapses instantly.
The gentle female warrior beside him speaks with a smile.

speaker: Caravan Member A
content: You've been talking a lot, dear. Feeling thirsty? Why don't you get yourself some water?

speaker: Caravan Member B
content: I didn't say anything wrong! These people just appeared out of nowhere. How do we know they're not enemy spies? Campbell said it himself—we can't afford traitors among us, or else—ouch!

speaker: Caravan Member A
content: You weren't actually asleep just now, were you? How did you miss that? That girl was in a total bloodlust, with her Mania completely off the rails. There's no way she's working with them. Now go get some water, seriously.
The tall man rubs the back of his knee and walks away grumbling. The female warrior then turns to Sibilla, her tone now more sincere.

speaker: Caravan Member A
content: I'm sorry about my brother. He's been on night watch these days and is really on edge—gets triggered whenever DisCity is mentioned. By the way, my name is Arienna, and my brother is Adriel.

speaker: Arienna
content: Well, you see, even at the official Great Expo quarters, we can hardly trust DisCity to provide solid protection. That's why we've split up our stuff and stashed some of it here.

speaker: Arienna
content: I'm sure you also know how it is. Everyone brings their most valuable resources all the way to the Great Expo, all to be exchanged for the Hypercubes to bring back home. We can't afford to have them robbed by bandits along the way.

speaker: Arienna
content: Heh, though trading with DisCity isn't much different from being robbed.
Sibilla completely understands. She starts hesitating whether to respond, and Arienna seems to see her right through.

speaker: Arienna
content: What about you? Which caravan are you from? Why are you traveling alone?

speaker: Sibilla
content: Well... I'm just a traveling merchant. I was captured by desert bandits on my way to DisCity and stuck with them for days. Jasmine was there even longer—they used her as a weapon. We managed to escape together.

speaker: Arienna
content: ...Ah, no wonder that girl's in such bad shape... In DisCity, even the bandits don't see us as people.
She falls silent for a while before speaking up again.

speaker: Arienna
content: She's got chains on her ankles. Looks tough on the outside, but she's covered in wounds. Must have been through some brutal stuff...

speaker: Arienna
content: What's more concerning is how the Mania corruption messed with her head. Her mind's all over the place, and it's only getting worse. Good thing you got her out when you did—maybe there's still hope for her.

speaker: Sibilla
content: ...I didn't do anything, really, and I barely know her. She's the one who's been protecting me this whole journey. We're just traveling together, that's all.

speaker: Arienna
content: You really put it all on the line back there to protect her during the fight just now. You're a brave and admirable comrade.

speaker: Sibilla
content: Comrade...?

speaker: Arienna
content: Right. In the shadow of DisCity, all Outlanders are comrades. We understand each other better than anyone.

speaker: Arienna
content: We've got some Hypercubes in our camp. I'll use them to try and ease your friend's condition. Once the Campbell experts from Fraser get back, they can give her more targeted treatment.

speaker: Arienna
content: You should come with us. We have everything here—supplies, shelter, and Fraser's backing to keep us safe. When you return home, you can gather your people and bring them into the Farland Alliance. We really should stand together.
Before Arienna can say more, her brother returns carrying two cups.

speaker: Adriel
content: Look who's talking! You've been yapping nonstop while she barely gets a word out. Can't you see she's uncomfortable? I didn't bring enough water for you. Go grab your own!
As he speaks, Adriel presses one of the cups into Sibilla's hands. It's still warm.

speaker: Adriel
content: Go on, drink up! This is my hometown's special brew. Most guests don't even get to see it!

speaker: Sibilla
content: ...Thank you both.

speaker: Arienna
content: You're welcome. We're just happy to meet a fellow Outlander, especially in a place like this.
[Scene Change to Jasmine]
Night has fully descended. While the caravan members are busy preparing to relocate, Sibilla waits for the right moment when no one is watching and slips into the medical tent.
Jasmine is already awake, still clutching that pair of strange blades in her hands. When she sees Sibilla enter, her face lights up with an innocent, almost pet-like smile.

speaker: Sibilla
content: You're awake. Are you feeling any better?

speaker: ******* hell. I signed up for the pay, not a coffin. I'm not dying in this ****hole...
content: I've been up for ages. Been listening to all the little secrets floating around this place.

speaker: Jasmine
content: So that Great Expo is really hard to get into! Outsiders have to bring their most precious treasures as a tribute just to stand a chance. Isn't that just like those desert bandits demanding their cut?

speaker: Sibilla
content: ...That's right.

Small city-states have no choice but to sell off their already-meager resources, population, technology, or even their very autonomy in return for a mere semblance of protection or aid from DisCity, or perhaps a scant offering of Hypercubes. Such is the true essence of today's Great Expo.

speaker: Jasmine
content: So what's your plan now? You didn't bring anything valuable along. Can you still get into the Great Expo like this? Maybe sell something, or should I go get something for you?
Sibilla gives her a grin.

speaker: Sibilla
content: It's not like I have nothing at all. It takes someone as down on their luck as me to pull out the sympathy card, you know.

speaker: Jasmine
content: The sympathy card? Will anyone actually buy that?

speaker: Sibilla
content: Of course, I'm pretty good at spinning stories.
Jasmine's eyes dart about as she mentally chews over the words, processing their meaning. Once she has fully digested the idea, she gleefully grabs her "teacher's" hands.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Great! Just give me a moment to loosen up these rusty joints. Then we'll hit the road.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Oh, traveling with the people here is another option. They're Outlanders like you and are also heading to the Great Expo. Looks like they've already accepted you as one of their own.
Sibilla falls silent.

speaker: Sibilla
content: Jasmine, I've come to say goodbye.
Jasmine blinks, looking all confused.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Why? You'd die so easily on your own. That's why you need me to protect you, right?

speaker: Sibilla
content: Yes, but now you're the one who needs to be looked after.

speaker: Arienna
content: What's more concerning is how the Mania corruption messed with her head. Her mind's all over the place, and it's only getting worse.

speaker: Arienna
content: We've got some Hypercubes in our camp. I'll use them to try and ease your friend's condition. Once the Campbell experts from Fraser get back, they can give her more targeted treatment.

speaker: Sibilla
content: The caravan people like you a lot, and they can give you proper treatment.

speaker: Sibilla
content: Right now, the most important thing is for you to heal properly. Stop pushing yourself to fight. It's too dangerous.

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...You don't want me to go to the Great Expo, do you?

speaker: Jasmine
content: Are you scared after seeing what I just did? Afraid that I'll do the same thing at the Great Expo? That I'll kill people?

speaker: Jasmine
content: Are you trying to protect the people in DisCity? Or... you have a friend there? What kind of person are they?

Sibilla is beginning to understand Jasmine—the recent fight, her fractured memories, uncontrollable Mania, and the desperate rush to DisCity... She's seen too many like this in the Outlands: souls seething with hatred, arriving with vengeance in their hearts.

speaker: Sibilla
content: Jasmine... it's nothing like that...

speaker: Jasmine
content: Heh... Don't worry, I promise I won't hurt him. You're such a good person, Sibilla, and I'm sure so is your friend. I won't hurt either of you...
female_content: Heh... Don't worry, I promise I won't hurt her. You're such a good person, Sibilla, and I'm sure so is your friend. I won't hurt either of you...

speaker: Jasmine
content: Good people are so rare these days. I hope you all live as long as possible.

speaker: Jasmine
content: So, take me with you, will you? I'll be good. Just don't leave me all alone.
Sibilla lets out a sigh, shaking her head at Jasmine.

speaker: Sibilla
content: Stay here and rest up for now, Jasmine, so when we meet again, I can see a healthier, happier you.

speaker: Sibilla
content: Get well soon, and let's see each other again at the Great Expo. I can already picture you dancing on a grand stage.

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...Dance? Me?

speaker: Sibilla
content: Yeah, it's obvious just watching you. Your steps are so light, and even your fighting looks graceful—every spin, leap, and flip flows perfectly together. It's like watching the lead performer at a grand gala.

speaker: Sibilla
content: You shouldn't bear all these scars. You were born to stand on gala stages, bathed in applause. That's who you really are.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Yeah, I... do feel something, if you say so.
Jasmine raises her hand—as if testing the weight of Sibilla's words—her scarred arms folding gently together.

speaker: Jasmine
content: My body seems to remember those moves my mind forgot... When I swing my blades, even gunfire and explosions sound like familiar music and drum beats.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Who knows? Maybe I really used to not fight at all—just danced wild and free at some celebration instead.

speaker: Sibilla
content: Once they treat your condition, your memories will come back. Then we can meet up at the Great Expo. Maybe by then, you'll even have new friends by your side.

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...Alright then. Let's meet at the Great Expo, and do bring your friend to see my performance.
The two envelop each other in a warm embrace, their smiles oblivious to the world unfolding outside.
Until a violent impact strikes the side of the ship.

speaker: Adriel
content: Enemy! Enemy incoming!! Grab your weapons!! Those bastards from DisCity are back!!
Several hundred meters away...

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: ...As you said, we've tracked down the rabble's camp. There aren't many weapons hidden here. It's a stretch to say they're planning any real trouble.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: But their attitude says it all.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: How convenient. They've picked a blind spot where FAC can't see a thing. They can meet their end in silence right here.
This time, the artillery fire is real, sending violent tremors through the ship.
[Scene Change]
Sibilla has just steadied herself when another wave of dread washes over her.
Her traveling companion, barely settled back into calm, tenses again at the thunder of gunfire. Jasmine sits up, her gaze fixed beyond the tent as if pulled by some unseen force.

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...Heh, sorry, Sibilla. I just promised to behave, but fate's such a cruel jester. Now I have to fight again. Promises on the battlefield always shatter like glass. Forgive me, will you?

speaker: Jasmine
content: But don't worry, those DisCity people are all bad. I know that stench all too well. So really, it's fine to kill them, right?

speaker: Jasmine
content: You just focus on staying alive. That's all you need to do.

She peels away the bandages slowly, the sticky pull of blood and torn flesh registering not as pain, but as some sweet prize. Outside, the caravan warriors roar Jasmine's name, eager for her to join them in battle.
But to Sibilla's ears, it sounds like death's own encouragement—a call to sharpen Sibilla into a blade and hurl her body toward the grave.

This is all wrong. Goodbyes are supposed to lead to joyful reunions—not this. She decided to leave Jasmine behind to keep her safe, far from madness and bloodshed. She can't bear to see her lose herself to violence again. It's just all wrong! With a surge of desperation, Sibilla races after her...

speaker: Sibilla
content: Jasmine! Your body hasn't recovered—
But she fails to catch Jasmine. As she bursts from the tent, her shoe catches on the gunwale. For one breathless moment, her balance wavers, then the world tilts...
It feels as if a hand pushes her from behind. Sibilla loses her balance and plunges headfirst into the swallowing sand. From deep within comes what sounds like the grinding jaws of sandworms.
...Whatever happens now, the battle is no longer her concern.

Sibilla is good at running away. She's always been able to claw her way back from the brink of death, but sometimes, survival is no kinder than an early grave. Now, in the heart of the frenzied sandstorm, she staggers forward, delirious. Her body betrays her, collapsing again and again, yet still she forces herself up, driven by something beyond thought.
Under a sky stained Mania-red, the sand screams on the wind as twilight bleeds into the dunes. Monsters lurk within the storm, occasionally rasping like crows circling rotten meat.
Yet in her dying hallucinations, the only destination she can still remember remains hopelessly far away.

speaker: Sibilla
content: Cough cough... cough... blegh...

speaker: Sibilla
content: DisCity... how much further...
Amidst the raging sandstorm, the traveler catches fleeting glimpses of DisCity's towering skyline, shimmering like a mirage on the distant horizon.

speaker: Sibilla
content: There's still a chance... still hope... I must get into DisCity. I have to find that person...

speaker: Sibilla
content: He will listen... He will help us... I must...
female_content: She will listen... She will help us... I must...

content: Like a dying flame's last gasp of light, she musters her final strength, fingers tightening around the protective charm.

speaker: Villager in the Dream
content: ...Here! We made this bracelet together. It's a protective charm for you! I learned from my big sister. Each bead represents one of us, to keep you safe.

speaker: Villager in the Dream
content: May the sandstorms never hurt you. May you always have food and warm clothes. May you never feel lonely and despair, and may you find good friends and companions wherever you go!

Friends...? Companions...? Jasmine... is she still alive? Clarity has long since slipped from Sibilla's grasp. Now, only instinct drives her forward as the same fractured memories loop endlessly in her mind.

speaker: Villager in the Dream
content: Safe travels! We'll be here waiting for you!

The rumbling of sandworms closes in around her as she collapses to the ground at last. Like driftwood caught in a relentless tide, she sinks, the currents of sand swallowing her inch by inch. Her consciousness wanes, and she can no longer tell if the distant city is real or just a mirage.

Then, a massive shadow engulfs the city—and at last, the traveler surrenders, letting the darkness swallow her in despair. In her final moment of consciousness, a vision flickers: a merchant ship grotesquely opulent.

speaker: Female Voice
content: You got anything?

speaker: Man's Voice
content: Found someone barely alive. Doesn't look like she's from DisCity. Would you like to see for yourself?

A barrage of gunfire sends the sandworms recoiling with furious roars, dropping a few lifeless bodies while keeping their distance without fully retreating. From the merchant ship, several gangways extend downward. Crew members descend to retrieve the worms' prey, hoisting them back aboard.

speaker: Sibilla
content: I'm not a traitor... no...

speaker: Sibilla
content: ...my friend... my friends...

speaker: Sibilla
content: Save them...
Someone tilts up her chin.

speaker: Female Voice
content: That accent... Where are you headed? Who are you trying to save? Can you hear me? Do you understand what I'm saying?

speaker: Sibilla
content: The Campbells... those people...

speaker: Female Voice
content: Oh... so you're also headed to the Great Expo. I can give you a ride since we're going the same way.
She turns to the crew.

speaker: Female Voice
content: Let's move. We're already running late.

With your undercover mission complete, you idly flip through a stack of Aurum Secretum booklets, listening to the technical staff's spiel as casually as if you were window shopping. Your attention drifts, pulling you toward the quieter corners of the exhibition.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The raw materials for Aurum Secretum aren't publicly disclosed? There's not even a map... So mysterious.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Then let's start with an order of 50 units. Besides the resources, I'm also interested in equipment. Even if you don't sell refining equipment, surely you offer storage solutions? What about your after-sales service? Will you have a team permanently stationed in DisCity?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The price isn't a problem. Just send the receipt to this mail address, and someone will handle the reimbursement for me. Right?
You say with a beaming smile, tapping your coat pocket.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: All investigation expenses during the mission will be covered?

speaker: Schorl
content: Paradeisos will cover all operational expenses during the mission. Furthermore, your requested items have already been procured and analyzed by the Ring Research Institute.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But I want the complete analysis results, not just what falls "within my authorization level."

speaker: Schorl
content: I believe there's a misunderstanding. The Ring Research Institute has no secrets to withhold from you on this matter. Aurum Secretum's core technology remains exclusively with Fraser. Even if we were to confiscate all the exhibits here, decryption would still be impossible.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I see... You actually make a pretty good search engine. Now, how about predicting where this technical collaboration between Nirvana and Fraser is headed? I'm really curious—why would they propose this partnership so suddenly, and be so pumped about it?

speaker: Schorl
content: I don't have a deep learning module installed. The randomness of human decision-making also exceeds my computational capabilities.

speaker: Option
options: You don't have it installed, or you just can't tell me?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What a pity, little triangle. With just a bit more polish, you could've been the crown jewel of this entire Expo.

speaker: Schorl
content: Based on my analysis, there is a 75% probability that you are attempting humor. Acknowledged. Ha-ha.

speaker: Schorl
content: For information that falls beyond your clearance level, I would either avoid mentioning it entirely or carefully redirect the conversation to minimize your frustration.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: In that case, let's do some Q&A—

speaker: Schorl
content: Before Nightfall, Fraser had already amassed considerable wealth. In fact, half of DisCity is built with their backing, and that continues to this day.

speaker: Schorl
content: Throughout past conflicts, they've remained neutral—if not occasionally friendly—with us. Take Fraser's involvement in last year's attack: they shared substantial intelligence with us regarding the case.

options: Are we competitors when it comes to Hypercubes?

speaker: Schorl
content: Early on, Fraser used their established wealth to accumulate massive Hypercube reserves. Their strategic neutrality during several Outland conflicts preserved these stockpiles, giving them a competitive edge.

speaker: Schorl
content: According to public records, Fraser currently holds the world's second-largest stockpile of Hypercubes. Their renewed push for partnerships is likely tied to the West District mine reopening—this might significantly impact their position.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Hmm... you're all so enthusiastic about Fraser. Funny, I remember you being much more careful with other Outland forces.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So... it never crossed your mind that something might be off about Fraser and Nirvana working together?
You stop in your tracks, gazing firmly at Schorl as the question that's been on your mind finally spills out. In your thoughts, you recall what Elvira told you in private.

speaker: Elvira
content: When Stewart... when my father was still alive, he once told me about a secret society. It operates in the highest levels of society—discreet, with a wide-ranging infiltration, but loosely organized. No formal rules or common purpose... just powerful people connected in the shadows.

speaker: Elvira
content: Its members might not stand out individually, but each of them holds invisible cards of resources and power. It could be through family ties, shared interests, personal favors, or other means. In short, their influence reaches far, and sometimes just a whisper from them can spark significant changes with ease.

speaker: Elvira
content: Worst of all, there's never a shortage of selfish, gullible parasites just waiting to be corrupted. Father said if someone wants to cheat the system, this secret society is their perfect backdoor.

speaker: Elvira
content: And I believe Fraser is already in contact with them. Just now, I caught a distinct "scent"—a specific incense that only members of this society use.

speaker: Elvira
content: ...Maybe I'm just overthinking this, but if there really is a connection, then Fraser's visit might not be what they claim. Please stay alert, Chief.
Faced with your question, Schorl falls silent for a moment before responding.

speaker: Schorl
content: There are risks, certainly. We monitor all Outland activity with equal vigilance. You've attended the security meeting yourself—you know the efforts being made by the 9th Agency and all the other departments.

speaker: Schorl
content: But since they extended a friendly invitation first, it would be poor diplomacy not to reciprocate. More importantly, they've been quite cooperative in sharing both technology and intelligence during our recent meetings. They've also provided substantial insights regarding the Jelena situation. At a minimum, this alliance gives us leverage against our known enemy.

speaker: Schorl
content: jojo

options: So that Nirvana can have what they want?

speaker: Schorl
content: So that greater conflicts can be avoided. These are turbulent times, and the primary threats to DisCity remain Mania and the Black Rings.
It makes a fair point, enough to earn a measure of your trust.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I understand the need for caution in diplomatic relations.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Adelaide Campbell—If I find him suspicious, conducting a thorough investigation shouldn't be a big deal, right?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If I find evidence against him, can I make an arrest?

speaker: Schorl
content: Of course, as long as you have sufficient evidence. Investigating and uncovering all discrepancies is precisely the purpose of your mission.
You watch the man in the distance as he raises his hand in greeting. You know he has been monitoring your movements, just as you have been tracking his.
You can make a good guess as to why Elvira remains fixated on the Campbell patriarch, despite never having met him in person.

Fraser's attempts to pin the Aurum Secretum leak on "Outland conspirators" fall short in the face of one undeniable truth—Jelena had infiltrated DisCity eight years ago and assumed the role of Elvira Stewart's butler. The technology had already leaked back then.
Silent for a full eight years, the enigmatic Aurum Secretum remained shrouded in obscurity until Fraser's recent extravagant promotion brought it into the spotlight.
Was there a sudden breakthrough in the Aurum Secretum technology itself? Or have recent changes in DisCity presented them with an opportunity to exploit?
While he has indeed divulged a substantial amount of information, you can't rule out the possibility that this information is intentionally provided—whether to win DisCity's trust or to mislead.
Maybe Elvira's emotions have swayed you, or perhaps it's your own intuition at play—
—There's this unsettling aura around him that instinctively repulses you.
But there's no need to share this with the little triangle. You decide to end the conversation by steering it towards a lighter topic.

options: Can I get updates on the negotiation progress with Nirvana?

speaker: Schorl
content: Sorry, you can't.

speaker: Schorl
content: Correction: you can, provided you consent to Nirvana receiving equivalent classified disclosures about you, including location data, private affairs, and such. I suspect that wouldn't be preferable, would it?

speaker: Schorl
content: While we value our trust with you deeply, Paradeisos must also honor its relationships with other key figures.

speaker: Schorl
content: This is how acceptable rules are established.
It gives quite a thorough answer.
People suddenly begin gathering around you, conveniently interrupting your "discussion."

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What's happening? Why are there so many people all of a sudden? Did something happen?

speaker: Schorl
content: Oh, that's because what's about to begin over there is—
[Scene Change]

speaker: Thalia
content: Up next, we're off to the Expo's exclusive live auction, where you'll find so many Outland treasures! And the best part? If something steals your heart, you can take it home that very day or even place custom orders with artists from afar. Isn't that wonderfully convenient?

speaker: Thalia
content: You see, most of these pieces hail from ancient city-states. Beyond their striking exotic beauty, they carry centuries of cultural legacy. And that's what makes them truly priceless treasures for collectors.

speaker: Thalia
content: Just imagine—what better way to showcase your exquisite taste than displaying one of these rare and precious Outland artifacts in your very own home?

speaker: Thalia
content: What's more, our Speaker, Parfait, Nirvana representatives, and a host of other VIPs are all there! With their presence and sway, today's sales are bound to be nothing short of spectacular!

speaker: Thalia
content: So my friends, seize the moment, don't just dream—take action! If something catches your eye, place your order right now. Don't let hesitation turn into regret!
Amidst the exhibition hall teeming with crowds, Thalia maintains a dutiful smile for the camera. However, her expression wavers as the growing throng of people pushes and jostles her from all sides.

speaker: Thalia
content: Hey, hey, hey! Quit pushing! Get in line! Get in line—

speaker: Thalia
content: These offline events are always such a pain at times like this...
Beyond the surging crowd stands a towering set of three-dimensional artworks.

The painting's palette is subdued, yet its arrangement resonates with fervor—a charging bull, a warhorse in terrified wails, contorted human figures writhing in agony... and amidst the desolate ruins, struggling flowers reaching for bloom.
It is the kind of work that pierces one's soul upon first gaze, an impactful expression that leaves viewers profoundly shaken.

speaker: Thalia
content: Ahem, didn't think the Chief of the Minos Bureau of Crisis Control would be here too. Place is packed over there. Let's just skip the crowd and keep moving on our tour!

speaker: Thalia
content: Take a look at this, everyone! Right before us is the most famous masterpiece in this Outland exhibition—Lamentur!

speaker: Thalia
content: Not quite getting it? That's absolutely okay! This is Outland art, after all. It's meant to challenge us. The important thing is knowing you're looking at something truly legendary!

speaker: Thalia
content: Created by an unknown artist, it features sharp brushstrokes and dramatic shapes. The composition may seem chaotic at first glance, but the piece possesses a deeply moving, heart-wrenching power. Reportedly, it depicts the horrors of a devastating war.

She intended to delve into more details and showcase her extensive knowledge, but a quick glance at the comment stream tells Thalia everything—DisCity viewers have no interest in tales from the Outlands.
Ever the professional, she immediately changes course and zeroes in on what really matters.

speaker: Thalia
content: Today, this incredibly special masterpiece isn't just being exhibited at the Great Expo—it's going up for auction for the very first time ever!

speaker: Thalia
content: For all of you watching from home, care to guess the final bid? Who do you think will walk away with this masterpiece? Remember, this isn't just another piece—it's the crown jewel of the entire exhibition!
Yet to her surprise, the audience's focus continues to waver.
No sooner has Thalia finished speaking than the crowd nearby erupts into startled exclamations.

speaker: Thalia
content: Huh? What's going on?
On stage, amidst the paintings, a figure of grace suddenly emerges, capturing the undivided attention of all present.

Framed by abstract paintings, the stage exudes a cold and somber aura. However, at its heart, a dancer stands ablaze with warm colors, utterly incongruous yet commanding the attention of every onlooker in the space.

speaker: Nirvana Representative
content: Well, well, is she also up for auction? Take a look at this, Parfait. The Outlands' creativity grows more brazen by the minute.

speaker: Max King
content: ...Isn't it just part of the show? I surely don't see any "human exhibits" listed on the auction catalog.

speaker: Fraser Ambassador
content: This is a little surprise from Mr. Campbell.

speaker: Fraser Ambassador
content: As long as she catches your interest, she has value. And valuable things naturally find their way to market.
[A figure in the shadows]
Below the stage, you stand among the crowd.

speaker: Schorl
content: Chief, I notice your heightened attention. Do you have any thoughts?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...I don't know.
You find it hard to put the feeling into words. The figure on stage resembles the artworks behind her—eerily surreal, as if stitched together from fragments: some cold, others warm.
She radiates a familiar distortion, yet remains jarringly alien, both repelling and captivating. It's like...

speaker: Parfait
content: It's like seeing a lone flower blooming in the rain... in the middle of a cold cemetery.
[Small CG]

speaker: Fraser Ambassador
content: Next up, we have a special performance for you—an improvised dance piece inspired by Lamentur.
[Big CG] Scene dims

speaker: Fraser Ambassador
content: Presenting the nomadic blade dancer—<color=#fb9259>Jasmine</color>.
She lowers her gaze, her first movements deliberate and slow as if designed to pull every eye toward her. This is someone who knows how to wield attention like a blade.

speaker: Audience
content: Hey, this one's pretty good. Completely different from what you see in DisCity. Is that body paint on her? Hot. She'll definitely fetch a high price.

speaker: Audience
content: Shame about the stage though. Such a downer with all that gloom. Why couldn't they go for something like that fancy painting at Parfait's dinner party—what was the name again...? The Golden City! Right! Now that style would've lit the place up properly.

speaker: Audience
content: Hey look, her lips are moving. You think she's singing? Haha, hope it's not some Outland dialect.
Jasmine's voice is lost to the crowd, yet theirs reach her with eerie clarity—countless murmurs threading through her mind like whispers on an invisible tide.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Is this painting really that gloomy? I actually quite like it.

speaker: Jasmine
content: It's just like what I've dreamed of over and over. And exactly like the celebration I remember. All those forgotten faces, forgotten moments... they're all coming back to me now.

speaker: Jasmine
content: But I must behave... No slicing, no cutting. I promised Sibilla, and her friend might be here too.

speaker: Jasmine
content: That reminds me... someone else made a request...
Slowly, she lifts her blades and performs a crowd-pleasing move intended to elicit applause, all the while scanning the audience until her gaze settles on a long-haired blond man below the stage.
Adelaide Campbell offers her a smile.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Hmph, fox. I remember what you said...

A sharp signal cracks through the air—instantly, she shifts her rhythm. Ropes coil tight around her calves as she's wrenched upside down, then released. Momentum arcs her body backward, and in one fluid motion, the blades in her hands carve straight through the massive painting behind.

speaker: Nirvana Representative
content: Woops... Parfait, looks like your precious collectible is gone.

Amid gasps and cheers, the masterpiece Lamentur is rent into a dozen fragments. Shards of fabric spiral through the air, stealing the audience's gaze. And in that breath of distraction, the woman vanishes. Then, a shout—

speaker: Max King
content: ${PlayerName}!
A streak of pink light slithers through the crowd, serpentine, flaring ever brighter in your vision. Instinctively, you shove aside nearby spectators and plainclothes guards.

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: Chief?!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Stay away from her!
Her gaze lifts, sharp with cold, predatory intent—the kind that would easily shatter an ordinary person's will. At this distance, you finally confirm what you have vaguely sensed all along—
The audience gasps in unison, scattering like startled crows to clear a widening circle around you both.

Schorl shoots out from your pocket, primed to fire, but she swings her blades in a flash of steel at its smooth surface. With a deft twist, she hurls it aside and lunges at you, closing the distance in a heartbeat.

speaker: Schorl
content: Chief, the shackles!
[Release the shackles]
It does buy you a moment's opportunity. The shackles' power already thrums in your palm, but as you raise your hand, she deftly evades. In a breath, she's right before you.
[CG]
She slips into your embrace with fox-like grace. Before you are her eyes brimming with tender affection, yet behind your neck lingers the unmistakable threat of her blades.

The blades delicately circle your neck as the dancer glides around you like a drifting petal caught in a breeze. Her lips hover near yours, curved in a smile that offers no answer. You can't tell whether she means to brush a kiss or sink her teeth into your pulse.

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...Hehe, just for fun. You don't mind, do you?

speaker: Jasmine
content: It's just a dance, nothing more. I hope everyone enjoyed it.
The cool sensation at your nape subsides as she leans in close to your face. A whisper like a gentle breeze brushes past your ear, fading before you can make out the words.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You...?

speaker: Schorl
content: Chief!
A blue glow flickers as Schorl seizes an opening and strikes from behind her. The force is so powerful that it seems to pierce through the woman's body and into yours.
There she collapses into your arms, her eyes half-lidded, the same faint smile lingering on her lips. Around you, flustered guards rush forward to confirm your safety.

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: Chief, please stop charging in like that! Protecting you is our job, not the other way around! Otherwise, our Captain's gonna skin us alive when we report back!

options: I don't think she's the kind of "danger" we expected.

content: As you speak, you gather the twin blades from the ground. They're mere paper props, edges blunt and harmless.
...But what ripped through the canvas? Was it her own hand? Or some kind of ability?

speaker: Adelaide
content: That was all part of the performance design. At the dance's climax, Jasmine selects an audience member for interaction, though we certainly never expected she'd choose the Chief of Minos of all people. My sincerest apologies for startling you, Chief.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: All part of the design... huh? Well, I actually have some questions.

options: Why is there a Sinner in your delegation?

content: His face registers evident shock.

speaker: Adelaide
content: Is that so? I'm sorry, we don't know much about Sinners.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Okay, let me ask another question. The Outland Affairs Bureau already conducted a security check on all registered members of your delegation when you first arrived and didn't identify any Sinners at the time.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So who is she? And how did she manage to evade both inspection and registration?

speaker: Adelaide
content: Jasmine wasn't initially part of our delegation. We came across her in WhiteSands. Though her health was fragile, she was quite determined to accompany us to DisCity. I believe this city holds special significance for her.

speaker: Adelaide
content: Her passion moved me deeply, so I extended the invitation myself. To think such an accident would follow... Do you intend to suspend the Great Expo?
He wears the look of a man poised for drama, eyes alight with anticipation—a sight you can't help but find amusing.

options: There's no need to make such a big deal of it.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: She didn't show any obvious hostility just now. Let's not spoil the fun for everyone.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But I do need to bring her back to MBCC for proper registration. You don't have any objections to that, do you?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: By the way, even before this accident, I had noticed that her physical condition was a bit worrisome. Over at the Bureau, she can get better treatment, though it might take quite some time.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This is all for the safety and well-being of the delegation members.

speaker: Adelaide
content: That would be for the best. I should thank you on Jasmine's behalf.
He hesitates briefly before nodding in agreement. You can't tell whether it's genuine reluctance or just an act, but either way, he quickly has someone go along with him.

speaker: Fraser Ambassador
content: Advisor Campbell, just a reminder, she is an auction item. After that performance just now, many clients have already placed bids.
Adelaide Campbell shows a resigned expression.

speaker: Adelaide
content: Ah, my apologies, Chief—it slipped my mind. Fraser operates on mercantile principles quite distinct from your own. Might I suggest we continue this conversation in a more discreet setting?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: In that case, I'll make an offer, no matter the cost. Ideally, I'd like to keep her long-term.
Schorl, floating beside you, freezes for a moment.

speaker: Nirvana Representative
content: Well, well, Parfait, seems you've finally met someone who can actually play the game. I'm curious, Chief—is MBCC paying you enough to pass up the stock market guru's offer? Or are you planning to "reallocate" city funds to outbid an ordinary citizen?

Like all the others from Nirvana, the man treats you with the same hostility. Your gaze flicks from him to the stock market guru at his side. She's already watching you—and when your eyes meet, she offers a faint, deliberate nod.

speaker: Nirvana Representative
content: I'm just joking. My friend here has already secured the winning bid. We've got an exclusive dinner party coming up and could use such a lovely flower to light up the place.

speaker: Nirvana Representative
content: If you are so fond of her, Chief, perhaps you should try to secure an invitation instead... though I doubt it'd be that easy for you.
Before you can respond, another person speaks up.

speaker: Fraser Ambassador
content: Excuse me, but Miss Parfait isn't currently in the top spot. The leading bid at the moment is...
He displays a shocking figure on his terminal.

speaker: Nirvana Representative
content: How is this price even possible...?! Who is it?!
You notice a woman in red on the upper floor, watching the scene with evident amusement.

speaker: Fraser Ambassador
content: This is, indeed, a highly competitive bid. The lady who placed it mentioned it was for a friend of hers. However, she also made a point of informing me that...

speaker: Fraser Ambassador
content: If Chief ${PlayerName} is interested, she would be pleased to offer it as a gift. She mentioned that it could be seen as... the start of a friendship.
When you look up, the woman in red meets your gaze, acknowledging you with a subtle gesture, then turns and walks away.

speaker: Nirvana Representative
content: Which city-state is she from? This isn't how business works here! Let us speak with her! It's not every day that my friend here finds something that she likes. We can't just let that—
A hand is placed on his shoulder.

speaker: Parfait
content: It's all right, my friend. Let's not allow tensions to rise. The lady put it well—art exists to bridge souls, not to parade fortunes. That would be most inelegant.

speaker: Parfait
content: If our beautiful blade dancer could once again perform freely in the sunlight after her treatment, my greatest wish would be fulfilled.

speaker: Parfait
content: It's been a pleasure to meet you, esteemed Chief. I won't keep you from your duties. Until fate brings us together again.
She gestures to you with such refined elegance that you can't discern whether there's any deeper meaning behind it.
In contrast, the wealthy elites dispersing in her wake all wear visibly disgruntled expressions.

speaker: Nirvana Representative
content: That one... He's a watchdog for the Sinners, if I remember correctly. Are you two close? You seem pretty worked up calling his name just now.
female_content: That one... She's a watchdog for the Sinners, if I remember correctly. Are you two close? You seem pretty worked up calling her name just now.

speaker: Max King
content: Absolutely not! Back in my campaign days, I did try to work with him, but that guy is impossible! Naturally, we went our separate ways. Never expected he'd cause a scene at the Great Expo. Well... seems I'll have to pay him some special attention.
female_content: Absolutely not! Back in my campaign days, I did try to work with her, but that woman is impossible! Naturally, we went our separate ways. Never expected she'd cause a scene at the Great Expo. Well... seems I'll have to pay her some special attention.

speaker: Nirvana Representative
content: Hmph, very well. But let me remind you, Speaker, Nirvana would prefer not to see you associating too closely with that kind of person.

speaker: Max King
content: Rest assured, man.
He bursts into laughter, draping his arm around the suited man's shoulders as they leave.
[White Out]

speaker: Schorl
content: The Bureau personnel have arrived and will promptly provide first aid to this Sinner. A thorough evaluation for Mania will be carried out upon their return.

speaker: Schorl
content: Chief, you seem somewhat reluctant to leave. Is there something else you'd like to do?
You mentally review the sequence of events that just unfolded.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Gather all the intelligence, including information on everyone who participated in the bidding and the entire process of granting entry to the delegation, and bring back everything about that Sinner from Fraser to the Bureau.
And then...

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...Take me with you. You're Sibilla's friend. I trust you.
You watch as the "dancer" is taken away, pausing briefly to reflect.
Let's head back to the Bureau for now.

speaker: Schorl
content: Copy that.
[Scene Change]
In a secluded corner beyond the reach of the hall's commotion, Sibilla flees rapidly through a hidden passage.
The woman in red would return in no time. She must steer clear of her and evade those from Fraser, all the while taking care not to ruffle any feathers among the DisCity people.

The thought of going back among crowds stirs unprecedented anxiety in her. Danger lurks around every corner, and one wrong move could prove fatal. Yet, despite the risks, Sibilla finds herself unable to contain her exhilaration.
The person she worries for, the one she's been pursuing, the very reason for her arduous journey stands within arm's reach. Never has she been this close!

speaker: Sibilla
content: Thank goodness... Jasmine is safe now. She'll get better, thank goodness...

speaker: Sibilla
content: So that's Chief ${PlayerName}. I've finally found you.

speaker: Sibilla
content: I must tell him about the Campbell family. I must—
female_content: I must tell her about the Campbell family. I must—

content: My name is Sibilla. It means "whistle" in our language.
Warnings of coming calamities, prices of distant goods, secrets between neighbors... My voice has carried countless messages because it's precisely my job.
But not every message is for every ear.
I must ensure the information reaches those who truly need it...

speaker: Sibilla
content: I am the whistle of Furor, watching for calamities, protecting the townspeople, and staying vigilant against DisCity spies.

speaker: Sibilla
content: However, around August of last year, I found something unbelievable on the body of a dead DisCity spy.
[Image of Inheritance from Hella's story]

speaker: Sibilla
content: I couldn't grasp it all at once, but the deeper I delved, the more terrified I felt. Even though I couldn't fully comprehend everything in the report, one truth became clear—

speaker: Sibilla
content: This thing is closely connected to the Black Rings and Mania that Hypatia, the researcher at Furor, mentioned. Fraser's stance couldn't be more clear. This is absolutely not something anyone should touch.

speaker: Sibilla
content: From that day on, I could no longer trust anything—the Aurum Secretum, the research lab, the entire shelter project. I needed to warn my people, to raise my voice.

speaker: Sibilla
content: But when it mattered the most, Furor's whistle went quiet...
[Enter Flashback]

speaker: Furor Resident
content: This is absurd! You're just parroting that DisCity spy's lies—he was dying and knew he could pin it on them! The Aurum Secretum? That's impossible... The lab would never harm us! Are you really questioning the Fraser scholars? Questioning Hypatia?

speaker: Furor Resident
content: Wait... have you been turned by DisCity? Are you trying to drive a wedge between our own people?!
[Scene Change]

speaker: Hypatia
content: …I’m sorry… It's classified research—I wish I could tell you more.

speaker: Hypatia
