content: But please, believe me, I’m doing everything I can to find a way. I swear I’ll protect Furor!
[Scene Change]

speaker: Supportive Friend
content: Leave it to me. I've done business runs to DisCity before and worked with a convoy from the West District there. They're solid people. Their leader's reliable and actually knows a Black Ring expert. Could be just the person you need.

speaker: Supportive Friend
content: Anyway, I'll head out now and see what people make of this photo. If there really is something off, I'll come back as soon as I can. Once we have more proof, everyone will believe you.
[Scene Change]

speaker: Synex
content: The friend you sent with that little message? Already dead. Aren’t you gonna say sorry? He died—just because you wanted to spill secrets.

speaker: Synex
content: Now then… where’d our little traitor crawl off to? Where are those sneaky photos hiding?

speaker: Synex
content: WHO, were you planning to send them to in DisCity, huh?
[Scene Change]

speaker: Desert Bandit
content: Look at this one, an Outland bum actually coming to the Great Expo begging for scraps! Where did you even crawl out from? How are you out here all by yourself? You really came all this way without a single penny?

speaker: Desert Bandit
content: Then we sell you to cover the gas money!
[Scene Change]

speaker: Woman in Red
content: Sounds like you've got a history with the Campbells. Spill it all. Depending on what I hear, I might help you... or toss you back to the sandworms. Your call.

speaker: Woman in Red
content: Of course, you could also show me how fast those legs can carry you. Just try not to die too fast.
[Scene Transition Back to Sibilla]

speaker: Sibilla
content: I'm not going to die here!

speaker: Sibilla
content: I ran all the way here, made it alive to DisCity, got into the Great Expo, and I... I saw him! ${PlayerName} is right there! I'm going to him right now!!
female_content: I ran all the way here, made it alive to DisCity, got into the Great Expo, and I... I saw her! ${PlayerName} is right there! I'm going to her right now!!

speaker: Sibilla
content: I'm telling him everything! You won't get your hands on me!!
female_content: I'm telling her everything! You won't get your hands on me!!

content: Sibilla grits her teeth and wrenches free from the handcuffs. Every movement is agony, yet she acts with swift, brutal efficiency—a survival skill the deadly wilderness of WhiteSands taught her.
She dodges the woman in red's guards, pressing herself against the wall as she slips into the shadows of the back door.

But before she can even steady her breath, footsteps rasp behind her. Somehow, several cloaked figures have followed her in. They quickly close in on her, their murderous intent as sharp as a blade pressed against her spine.
Though they move in silence, Sibilla recognizes their deadly motions at once. She had barely escaped their blades once before, deep in the tunnels of Furor.

speaker: Sibilla
content: ...Campbell's assassins!
You're halfway into the vehicle when you freeze. Somehow, you catch a faint sound drifting from behind you, carried on the wind from the direction of the Cristallia.

speaker: Schorl
content: Are you referring to how the MBCC Chief spent a fortune at the Great Expo, all to acquire a Sinner?

speaker: Schorl
content: Correction: it was a bribe received. Further correction: a gift received.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're so funny.

speaker: Schorl
content: Please rest assured, the most important opening day of the Great Expo has been concluded successfully. The FAC and plainclothes personnel are keeping watch on everything else. You can go back and take your rest now.
You smile, and finally get into the vehicle.
—It is probably just your imagination.
[Scene Change]
The woman in red returns, only to find that her guest she brought along, Sibilla, has disappeared.

speaker: Guard
content: Sorry, she managed to escape. We'll track her down as soon as possible.
She bends down and picks up the hemp rope left on the ground—the same one that had bound her "guest." Now it lies frayed and broken, its coarse strands blotched by bloodstains.
She feels a flicker of admiration.

speaker: Woman in Red
content: Just a few minutes of chaos, and she still found a way to slip out. That woman's something else.

speaker: Woman in Red
content: Find her, but no need to bring her back.
The guard nods and leaves, fully understanding the unspoken order.
(Scene Change: Conference Room)

speaker: Schorl
content: The routine examination is finished. Sinner Jasmine is in good health overall, and all her previous injuries have healed completely. The only side effect is her heightened sensitivity to Mania, which sharpens her environmental perception in high-stimulation settings.

speaker: Schorl
content: However, her mental state shows unusual instability. Her cognitive coherence falls well below standard Sinner thresholds. Currently, she's unable to maintain meaningful external communication or fully regulate her own actions.

speaker: Schorl
content: Multiple interrogation sessions have yielded nothing. Her memory is fragmented, her speech incoherent. Even if you went personally, Chief ${PlayerName}, the results would be the same.

speaker: Schorl
content: Such cases are rare in DisCity. We have not yet determined the cause.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Not yet determined the cause...?

speaker: Fraser Ambassador
content: The trigger of her mental disorder is the weapon she has been carrying. That's why Advisor Campbell replaced that pair of blades with props for her stage performance, to prevent further harm.

speaker: Fraser Ambassador
content: The weapon has already been secured and transferred to DisCity for research, with additional enhanced Aurum Secretum restrictions in place.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Yes, it has been sent to the Ring Research Institute.

speaker: Fraser Ambassador
content: They must've said it's been sent to the Ring Research Institute. But according to our intelligence, that weapon actually ended up in FAC's hands.

speaker: Schorl
content: ...You're not doubting that we sealed the intelligence again, are you?
Look at that, now it's playing the victim.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm not so easily tricked into questioning FAC, and I trust that all allied departments will conduct a professional and fair investigation of that suspicious weapon, and will <color=#fb9259>openly and honestly share all reports with me</color> afterward.

speaker: Schorl
content: ...Understood. I will make your expectations clear to them.
You find it somewhat amusing to tease Schorl. When things calm down, you plan to pry for more information.
But for now, these Outlanders strike you as far more suspicious than anyone else.

speaker: Adelaide
content: Jasmine wasn't initially part of our delegation. We came across her in WhiteSands. Though her health was fragile, she was quite determined to accompany us to DisCity. I believe this city holds special significance for her.

speaker: Adelaide
content: Her passion moved me deeply, so I extended the invitation myself. To think such an accident would follow...

Fraser has poured so much effort into every detail—dressing her up, teaching her to dance, placing her center stage at the Great Expo to draw everyone's attention. They couldn't have gone to such lengths just to sell her off at auction.
[Flashback: Duo Dance CG]

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...If they went to all this trouble, the least I can do is play along and see what they're really after.
A faint, almost imperceptible current of electricity whispers past, and the little triangle beside you seems to change its tone.

speaker: Schorl
content: Heh, your positivity is surely refreshing. This reminds me of something... Would you be interested in trying a new technology under development? One that could... provide deeper insight into Sinners.

speaker: Schorl
content: Let's call it... Codename LINK for now.

speaker: Schorl
content: This specialized technology was created for Sinners whose minds are severely corrupted by Mania, becoming chaotic and fragmented after prolonged contact. But ironically, that same corruption makes possible a technology that can resonate with them through Mania.

speaker: Schorl
content: That's right. I'm referring to your <color=#fb9259>shackles</color>.

speaker: Schorl
content: Based on our extended observation and research, we believe your mental resilience now meets the requirements for extensive Mania field exposure. You should be able to connect with the target Sinner's consciousness and achieve deeper synchronization.

speaker: Schorl
content: When that happens, the two of you will share one consciousness, including memories, emotions, personality traits, and even thoughts—if they still exist. You can also guide and manipulate them to extract the intelligence you need.

speaker: Schorl
content: Therefore, the greater a Sinner's psychological collapse, the deeper you can access their consciousness for intelligence extraction.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...You're suggesting that Jasmine meets the requirements for LINK.

speaker: Schorl
content: Oh but of course, this technology isn't fully developed yet, so we strongly advise against current usage. Entering a fragmented mind poses significant risks, and your safety remains our primary concern.

speaker: Option
options: ...You sure seem excited to try it out on me.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Otherwise you wouldn't even have brought it up at a time like this.
Seeing it even has the audacity to beep and boop at you acting all clueless, you let out a sigh.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Everything has risks. Just tell me straight—what's in it for me, what could go wrong, and... how sure you are you can handle it.

speaker: Schorl
content: As long as you remain as rational as you are now, 96.9% of the risks can be mitigated, and you'll have a 100% chance of uncovering the secrets you want about that Sinner—the most authentic, undisguised secrets.

speaker: Schorl
content: We'll ensure your safety is monitored and protected at every stage, and none of the intelligence you gather will be overlooked. After all, for us, this is also valuable data that helps perfect the technology.

speaker: Schorl
content: I admire your bravery. EDGE-02 will be deeply grateful.
As suspected, someone new is pulling the strings now. EDGE-02... you make a mental note of this name.

Jasmine lies still on the bed, her expression serene as if a silent defiance against the restraints coiled around her limbs. At the sound of your footsteps, her eyelids flutter open, and her gaze meets yours.

Not long ago, you were both in the interrogation room engaging in a verbal dance of evasion, wasting time circling around each other. Now, she looks at you with the most friendly, innocent smile, as if that battle of wits had never happened.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Chief, right? You finally came to see me.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Yeah. I just tried to get your blades back for you, but I failed.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: They said those blades might not be completely safe, so for the sake of your health, they need more time to look into the problem.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Ah, I see... I've never left them behind. It feels a bit strange...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Actually, there's another option—if you could get better, that solves all problems. I've had experts put together a few treatments to speed up your recovery. Want to give them a try?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'll go with you, and stay by your side the whole time. You've got nothing to be afraid of.

speaker: Jasmine
content: I see. I trust you. Many people say you're a good person—a very good person, actually.
She takes your hand and gently rubs her cheek against your palm.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Then... help me, please.
(Scene Change: Laboratory)
Jasmine enters a transparent glass chamber and settles inside in silence. Every so often, her gaze meets yours, lips curving into a faint smile.

speaker: Schorl
content: The inhibitor will prevent mental instability during the linking process, and the restraints are to prevent her from harming others in case of mental breakdown.
The transparent mental solution begins to flow in until she is completely submerged.

speaker: Schorl
content: Chief, please try your best to keep the shackles' connection firm and tight while staying vigilant.

speaker: Schorl
content: What you're stepping into is a fractured, chaotic mindscape. The danger level depends on how much this Sinner has endured, and how deep their corruption runs.

speaker: Schorl
content: Well then, I wish you both a safe journey.
You cast your gaze at Jasmine.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Yeah.
(Check if there's a transition effect that can be added here; if not, use a slow fade to black)
The world shatters before your eyes, plunging you into darkness, only to release you moments later, as abruptly as you fell.
Flames suddenly erupt, illuminating everything around you. The raging fires of war, accompanied by the acrid stench of charred flesh and spilled blood.
A silhouette slowly walks toward you.

No, it's not just one person. They don't answer you, but instead raise their hands. The glint of steel in their grip catches your eye: blades and axes—weapons honed for slaughter, more distinct than the faces of these "people" themselves.
Roaring, they charge toward you—
(Scene transitions to battlefield, character portraits crack, bleed, then disappear, with sound effects of flesh chunks hitting the ground)

The chaotic hatred does not overcome you. In an instant, the furious mob charging toward you is obliterated—struck mid-stride by artillery shells. Right before your eyes, right above your head, they are shattered, pierced, engulfed in flames, their bodies melted into grotesque pulp and splattered.
You sit on the ground gasping for breath, your body trembling as the world thrums around you. For a moment, you mistake it for the hammering of your own heart.
But no—it's the ground itself trembling beneath you.
[Small CG: Tank]
One after another, the war chariots grind forward like ironclad beasts, crushing bodies and weapons alike into the churned muck.

Inside each chariot, soldiers with indistinct faces clutch bright red arms, their weapons glinting as they rake the earth. They fire without pause, ruthlessly shredding anything that twitches or whimpers in the sludge.
You collapse between the advancing wheels, catching muffled cries from the mud.

speaker: Vague Voice
content: What did we do wrong...? Did we ever harm you?

speaker: Vague Voice
content: You DisCity people... why are you doing this to us...

The only reply they get is another gunshot. The soldiers kill without hesitation, faces blank as stone, as if they've shed their humanity entirely, becoming little more than the ominous, Mania-emitting weapons they wield.
[Transition] Slow Fade to Black
But the war is far from over.
[Transition, Red In]
Before a roaring bonfire, a soldier drives his bayonet downward, stabbing again and again into a small heap of remains—each thrust mechanical, relentless.
Then, without warning, his blade sinks deep and won't pull free. An instant later, the soldier is yanked forward, swallowed whole by the muck. A stifled gasp, then silence follows.

But then the bayonet resurfaces. It darts across the battlefield now, swift as a viper, piercing soldier after soldier armed with the same deadly steel. Only if you strain your eyes can you glimpse the petite shadow wielding the glowing weapon.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Haha... Hahaha... Hahahaha!!

Blades, guns, ammunition, and even chariots... One by one, she wrenches the red-glowing weapons from their wielders, cutting down their so-called "masters"—or rather "slaves"—as the armaments coalesce in her grip.
When they finally fuse into those twin blades familiar to you, no one else remains alive on the battlefield.
[Transition] Change the red background to a dark, cold-colored palette
Only a ghost lingers now, her skin a lattice of blood-red scars.

speaker: Jasmine
content: It's over, right...? It's all over now, right...? I've killed them all... but why...

speaker: Jasmine
content: The fires won't die out, the gunshots keep coming... Why isn't anyone waking up...

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...Is it still not over? Then... where are the enemies?

speaker: Jasmine
content: The enemies still alive... where are they hiding?

speaker: Jasmine
content: Is it you?!
She finds you in an instant, bursting through the gunsmoke, twin blades a flash of crimson as they carve toward your face.
[Release the shackles]

Your shackles barely block her strike, several thorns piercing through her body only to be instantly dissolved and absorbed. No advantage is gained; instead, the Sinner's madness penetrates your mind, carried on the razor's edge of her scream.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Stop? Why?

speaker: Jasmine
content: If not killing means being killed, then why should I stop?

speaker: Jasmine
content: If not killing means losing people I care about, then why should I stop?

speaker: Jasmine
content: None of you ever stopped! You were the ones who started it!
Her furious roar splits your skull. Your consciousness shudders, disrupted by her rage, but a voice deep within urges you to reject her words—
You open your mouth to speak, but the words that spill forth are no longer yours.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You were the ones who started it. You choked us, left us no way out...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Stop acting innocent! The soldiers you trained have my people's blood on their hands! And you did nothing to stop them!

speaker: Delirious Voice Within
content: When they dropped ████, you supported them. You let it happen. You are guilty—ALL of you!
[Shackles Effect, No Interaction Required]

speaker: Vague Voice
content: Not true...? What is not true...? You are not our enemy?

Your words are cut short as something coils around your ankles. Your gaze snaps downward, and there, you find eyes adrift in a sea of blood—eyes that refuse to close even in death—staring directly at you.

speaker: Vague Voice
content: Die with us... then you won't be an enemy... As long as you live, you are our enemy!

speaker: Vague Voice
content: This is what war is like! This is the war you taught me!!

speaker: Vague Voice & Jasmine
content: You started this war, and you think it can just end that easily?
You turn around to see a sight that fills you with warmth, comfort, and familiarity. They appear to be your companions.
[Small CG: Army]
It's a real army. And every single one of them...
...holds the same deadly blade, each radiating palpable bloodlust.
In the laboratory, alarms blare as everyone scrambles into action, holding their breath with cold sweat streaming down their faces.

speaker: Schorl
content: Resonance levels have exceeded the danger threshold. Increase the inhibitor dosage, weaken the shackles, and if possible, sever the connection again. ${PlayerName}'s condition is on the verge of losing control. Hold him back.
female_content: Resonance levels have exceeded the danger threshold. Increase the inhibitor dosage, weaken the shackles, and if possible, sever the connection again. ${PlayerName}'s condition is on the verge of losing control. Hold her back.

speaker: Schorl
content: If SHP-13 still can't wake up in 15 minutes, proceed with final measures: activate containment protocols to protect ${PlayerName} and execute Jasmine simultaneously to prevent contamination residue.

speaker: Schorl
content: This contamination is beyond anything an S-Class Sinner could wield. What's truly tearing through her mind is...
The cold, rational triangle commands the scene, but beyond its mechanical gaze, more eyes are watching as everything unfolds.

speaker: Schorl?
content: Heh... It's certainly not those petty nobles from Fraser. What will ultimately break this Sinner? I'm afraid they're just as curious about the experiment results as we are...

speaker: Schorl?
content: Stay calm, Chief. I know you can do this. Try to keep a clear head and find the voice you truly believe in... The answer is there.
You are still fighting, struggling against the odds.
But the weapon you're wielding is no longer the shackles.
In your hands, you now grip that pair of crimson blades.

speaker: Vague Voice
content: The battlefield knows no mercy. Anyone could be the one to kill you. If you don't kill them, they'll kill you. If they don't kill you, they can't survive.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Shut up...
The voice from the deadly blades in your hands coils around you.

speaker: Vague Voice
content: Glory, shame, hatred, profit, lies, justice... anything can lead to war, yet everything loses its meaning on the battlefield. The only truth in war is slaughter, and only victory can honor the sacrifices made.

speaker: Vague Voice
content: Begging for peace in hell gets you nothing but trampled. The only way to earn it is to embrace the battlefield.
No... that's not right... You struggle against it, but the weapon in your grip refuses to stop.

It pulls you into a vast, unthinking army, where you no longer have to face yourself. Here, every soldier hears the same voice, marches in lockstep, their spectral figures moving as one. They rally beneath a single banner, and you see it all with terrible clarity.
Even in its distorted form, you recognize it... that's the flag of DisCity.

speaker: Vague Voice
content: Kill... kill... kill... for yourself, for those you love, even for peace. Kill them. Let their skulls become vessels of your triumph, offerings to the heavens—this is the only purpose the enemy serves...

speaker: Vague Voice
content: The enemy... is war's one undeniable truth...

speaker: ?? & ${PlayerName}
content: Shut up!
Slap! Someone covers your ears.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Shh... it's alright now. Don't listen to that voice, it's dangerous.
Your body moves forward, driven by the blades in your hands as they slash toward the woman's throat, but you're too slow. "Jasmine" catches your wrists effortlessly.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Oh, come now. It's obvious you don't really want to hurt anyone. Don't let it take over. Just relax your grip, slowly... I know you are strong enough to fight it. You've totally got this.

speaker: Jasmine
content: There you go... just loosen your grip. Let me help you toss it away.
She takes the blades from your hands and hurls them far away.

speaker: Jasmine
content: All done! Now, let's get you back where you belong.

speaker: Jasmine
content: This place is just dreadful for you, isn't it? But don't worry, you can trust me. Those things cannot control me. After all... I am the master of this world.
She speaks with pride, indifferent to the churning sludge gnawing madly at her bare feet—or perhaps... she simply doesn't care.
"Jasmine" links her arm through yours as you both navigate through a battlefield shrouded in gunsmoke.

No... this isn't her. No matter how similar they look, the girl in front of you is human—her gaze meets yours as an equal. But the Jasmine outside... However she disguises herself, she always looks at you like a beast eyeing a human.
...The person before you is whole, complete. She... is not the Jasmine you know.

Before you can ask anything more, gunfire erupts all around. Bullets rain down at your feet, sending your nerves into overdrive and twisting your gut into knots. Yet, despite the chaos, she gives your hand a reassuring pat.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Don't be afraid. Turn your mind away from the guns and bullets. Just imagine me dancing, and listen again... Don't they sound like drums now? Da-da-da-da-da... A perfect little rhythm for my dance.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Every year we celebrate the harvest season. I'm the best dancer around, the star of the celebration! Everyone comes to my performance, cheering for me. The details? I'll tell you little by little. Just picture it in your head, and you won't be afraid anymore.
And so she speaks to you softly, as if flames were never meant to burn houses and fields—only to light bonfires and candles, to roast sizzling delicacies, to kindle the glow of a heartful feast.

She says bullets and arrows need not take lives. Instead, the targets woven with flowers by young maidens stand tall in the distance, waiting to be struck. Pierce the red bullseye at the heart, and one might just win true love.

She says parade floats loom as massive as tanks in her homeland, bearing scarecrows through the fields. Villagers line the paths in joyous celebration, praying for gentle rains, for heavy sheaves of grain, for health and prosperity.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Look! Fireworks!

You glance up to see a massive artillery shell hurtle toward you. With a mere point of her finger, it explodes midair, blooming into dazzling fireworks that erupt across the sky. Darkness shatters into radiant light, the weight of fear dispelled, terrified screams now joyous cheers.

At this moment, your mind clears, and you see a lightless river stretching beneath your feet. It forms a boundary, a divide. Beyond it lies a vast and silent shore, untouched by the chaos and confusion of this side. That is where you belong.
"Jasmine" watches you, her gaze gradually softening.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Looks like everything's fine now. You should head back. And next time... maybe don't wander in here so carelessly, okay?
...Indeed, you already know enough. This place is far too dangerous for you to stay. It's time to leave and never return. The real fight is waiting for you on the other side.
"Jasmine" takes your hand and leads you forward, guiding you to step into the river. But something makes you hesitate. Your grip tightens instinctively, holding her back as you turn to face her—

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Come with me, to the outside world. Real celebrations are waiting out there.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The war is over now. You don't need to stay here anymore.
She does not resist. Taking her silence as consent, you draw her softly to your side.

But with one mere step forward, the river surges over her feet, and the hand you're holding begins to dissolve. Cracks race along the scars mapping her body, and she crumbles right before you, her smile flaking away like old paint piece by piece. The harder you hold on, the faster she slips through your fingers like grains of sand... until you have no choice but to let go.
She looks at her crumbling hand, then turns to you, still with a smile.

speaker: Jasmine
content: See? Don't even bother.

speaker: Jasmine
content: I can't leave, not for a long time now.

The river surges between you, its swift currents carving an impassable divide. Through the rippling water, she waves goodbye, watching as you leave. Only when the distance swallows you whole does she turn away, stepping back into the world she belongs to, the one on the other side.
[Small CG: Village with Softer Filter]
Across the river, you see the village engulfed in flames. Amidst the hellish inferno, the long-dead stir, twisting, rising one by one. And then, they begin to sing.

speaker: Village Chief
content: We've hit the jackpot, you little wretches! We're set for years. No more worries, not even about war! Every deal's locked in. Now party like there's no tomorrow!

speaker: Phantom
content: Well, well! If we're not wasting gunpowder hunting or picking fights, we can blow it all on the biggest fireworks show ever, right?
The remains of a soldier are pulled upright. He fumbles for his gun, only to have it snatched away.

speaker: Phantom
content: Hey, even if you're a guest from DisCity, no causing trouble! No fighting, no hurting people! Come on, drop the gun. Let's watch Jasmine dance!

speaker: Jasmine
content: Haha, come on! Wherever I am, there's always a celebration!

A gigantic bonfire surges skyward. Around it, fragmented phantoms gather, their faces smeared into oblivion, indistinguishable as friend or foe. Gunfire cracks, drums pound—they dance, spectral and frenzied, a celebration of the already-dead. Hell and revelry shatter, then fuse, twisting into a single, unending moment. This is her eternity.
And "Jasmine" stands atop a high stage at the heart of the battlefield, her blood-stained blades flashing as she dances, each movement a celebration of harvest and peace.
Only upon waking do you grasp the truth: when war broke out, her hometown was in the middle of such a celebration, and then everything was frozen forever on that day.
[Scene Transition] You're awake, Jasmine is not

speaker: Schorl
content: Only 3 minutes and 21 seconds left. Fortunately, you made it back in time. Chief, the experiment was a success with both your body and mind intact. We've collected critical data to optimize the LINK project, which should enhance your future understanding of Sinners.

speaker: Schorl
content: Though you don't look all that pleased.

speaker: Schorl
content: She hasn't woken up yet, but it should be soon.
Jasmine has been moved to a ward bed for health monitoring. She's moaning softly, as if trapped in a nightmare—probably the one you know.

speaker: Jasmine
content: <size=25>Mmm...</size>

speaker: Schorl
content: The experimental data confirms that Sinner Jasmine's mental state is in significantly worse condition compared to DisCity Sinners. This is directly tied to the Outlands' strategic stance toward DisCity. Had they engaged more actively with DisCity in recent years and systematically studied our anti-Mania technology, her condition might not have declined to this degree.

speaker: Schorl
content: Jasmine has lost all conscious will. She's highly sensitive to Mania and extremely susceptible to influence. Fraser likely assumed she could be easily "used" for their purposes, but after a thorough investigation, I believe this is as far as she can go.

You gently take Jasmine's hand. Despite the experiment's original intent, you've uncovered nothing about Fraser, the mission she was given, or the conspiracy behind it—no traces, no leads. Maybe deep in her subconscious, those people truly mean nothing to her. Or perhaps she's simply trapped in that moment.

But for you, it's different. The image of her hand dissolving still lingers in your mind. And the fractured battlefield from your dream haunts you just as vividly. Fraser's conspiracy is no longer the only mystery driving you forward. Now, there are even more questions demanding answers.

options: I may know why Fraser sent her here.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: In her memories, I saw an army, one flying DisCity's flag. Their weapons were unlike anything I'd ever seen... Not like the anti-Mania devices FAC uses now. No, these were something else entirely—brutal, powerful, built purely for killing. Worse yet, they could even drive people into a bloodthirsty frenzy.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So that's how Jasmine got corrupted, right? She took those blades from that DisCity army and brought them back here. Maybe Fraser sent her just to rub that history in our faces... Heh, that's vile.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Judging by her age in the dream, that war wasn't that long ago, but I've rarely heard anyone mention it.
You look at Schorl.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Hardly anyone in DisCity ever talks about that DisCity army. And what's the deal with those "weapons"? Tell me about that war.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Or is this something I'm not supposed to know?

speaker: Schorl
content: Approval complete. EDGE has granted you exclusive access to this information. However, it may not be appropriate for me to be the one to explain. Please wait a moment, Chief.
After a series of electronic beeps, there's a knock at the door. Your adjutant appears in the doorway with a grave expression.

speaker: Nightingale
content: ...Chief.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Nightingale?

speaker: Nightingale
content: I cannot deny your suspicions... It's true that DisCity once had its own army, and went through a long period of territorial expansion. Our history even includes a decade-long period of military dictatorship.

speaker: Nightingale
content:
We leveraged our Hypercube advantage to wage wars, invade the Outlands, exploit satellite towns, plunder resources, and even commit countless atrocities...

As the dominant city-state, DisCity crushed every Outland alliance. The reach of its former military conquests far surpassed even what Nirvana achieves today.

speaker: Nightingale
content:
It truly was an era defined by fanaticism and extremism, marked by foreign wars and domestic oppression.

It's entirely plausible that during the time, someone secretly sanctioned the development of prohibited weapons, later dispersing them to distant lands through war, with one eventually finding its way into Jasmine's hands.

speaker: Nightingale
content: All these mistakes were corrected after the DisSea Explosion.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Confronted with BR-000, EDGE scientists worked tirelessly to negotiate a resolution, eventually convincing the old military regime to shift their focus from warfare to catastrophe response. The DisCorps was then restructured into the city-state's anti-Mania framework—marking the birth of the FAC (Framework Against Catastrophe).

speaker: Nightingale
content: Afterward, we gradually scaled back our expansionist policies, eased tensions among city-states, and dedicated ourselves to reuniting humanity against shared apocalyptic threats.

speaker: Nightingale
content: In N.F. 106, DisCity first proposed a peace initiative at the Great Expo. Despite facing numerous setbacks, we ultimately secured a comprehensive ceasefire agreement with all city-states by N.F. 107.

speaker: Nightingale
content: That chapter of our history is now behind us. Today, DisCity is committed to peace. We urge everyone to let go of past grievances and mistrust, so that together, we may heal these wounds and look toward the future...

speaker: Nightingale
content:
...Even with that said, I know you might not entirely agree, Chief.

Jasmine's situation is undoubtedly deserving of sympathy, and your principles are always unwavering. In the few short years since your awakening, you've seen too much darkness to fully endorse many of the city-state's actions.

speaker: Nightingale
content: In that case, allow me to offer my perspective in defense of my homeland.

speaker: Nightingale
content: The root of all conflict between DisCity and the Outlands has always been Hypercube, and the first and most devastated victim wasn't any distant land... but DisCity itself.

speaker: Nightingale
content: The long-running city-state wars originated with DisCity's anti-colonial movement. The independence war from N.F. 60s to N.F. 80s remains the longest and most devastating conflict ever fought by a single city-state.
You're stunned. Nightingale holds your gaze, and once she's certain you've processed her words, she continues, measured and deliberate.

speaker: Nightingale
content: In N.F. 24, the leading city-states established DisCity along the shores of the DisSea as a semi-colonial production zone for Hypercubes. Its sole purpose was to extract and export Hypercubes to the colonial powers that funded its operations.

speaker: Nightingale
content: The people of DisCity endured the world's most concentrated Apocalypse of Ashes along the DisSea. Yet, the Hypercubes they mined could not be used for their own protection; instead, it was shipped endlessly to the Outlands, sold at rock-bottom prices.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Industrial goods, capital, food, and water were all strictly regulated. Even after years of painstaking savings, colonial powers could easily strip away the people's wealth with minor adjustments to the prices of essential resources.

speaker: Nightingale
content: ...Yes, a stark contrast to what we see today. Back then, DisCity was merely a fledgling mining city, barely surviving on the fringes of a disaster zone. Meanwhile, the colonial powers funding its development had inherited the majority of pre-Nightfall wealth, resources, and heavy weaponry.

speaker: Nightingale
content:
DisCity's earliest upper class all originated from prominent powers in the metropoles, remaining loyal to their "homeland" rather than their place of residence.

Those who challenged this system faced brutal suppression. Yet, despite years of oppression, the people of DisCity refused to submit, and resistance began to take shape.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Then, in the N.F. 60s, when DisCity's Nirvana Port sought autonomous trading rights, the metropoles obliterated it with nuclear weapons.

speaker: Nightingale
content: The radiation contamination devastated what was then the most vital independent shipping route, killing at least 150,000 people—a death toll surpassing any subsequent Black Ring outbreak. This catastrophe became the catalyst for all-out war.

speaker: Nightingale
content: The former military forces mutinied and declared war against the metropolitan coalition. After a prolonged and devastating conflict—one that inflicted heavy casualties and exhausted the city-state's accumulated wealth—they succeeded in expelling the colonizers from DisCity and seizing control of the Hypercubes. They then spent many more years reclaiming their rightful resource cities and satellite towns, ultimately achieving full independence from colonial rule.

speaker: Nightingale
content: During this brutal struggle, the former military—and eventually the entire DisCity—grew increasingly radicalized. In time... they strayed down a dark path.

speaker: Nightingale
content: ...I have to admit, trying to justify it like that feels quite pathetic.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, Paradeisos instructed me to explain these things to you, probably in preparation for more important assignments ahead. I believe you'll soon be granted broader authority and intelligence access to manage more complex missions. Naturally, you'll develop your own perspective on these matters. I cannot—and would not—try to sway your judgment.

speaker: Nightingale
content: But there's one point I think you'll agree on.

speaker: Nightingale
content: If a city-state holds the only Hypercube mine but lacks the strength and resolve to defend itself, its destruction is inevitable, regardless of alliances, enmities, or even notions of justice. This is simply an objective certainty.
Afterward, you walk alone for a long time—so long that you begin to lose track of the people you've met and the conversations you've had along the way.
[Scene Change]
Late at night, Elvira sits alone in the Recreation Area. On the television screen plays a rebroadcast of an interview with Fraser's advisor, Adelaide.

speaker: Adelaide
content: I'm deeply moved to learn that so many have inquired about Jasmine's well-being. Thanks to the tireless work of DisCity's anti-Mania specialists, we're making steady progress in identifying the root cause of her condition.

speaker: Adelaide
content: Jasmine is a civilian from a distant land who was caught in the throes of prolonged conflict and exposed to a forbidden weapon. Her body and mind have been completely shattered. Regrettably, there is no possibility of recovery at this stage.

speaker: Adelaide
content: She is a tragic casualty of war, and a poignant reminder that we must not relive the failures of history... Through sustained joint efforts, DisCity and Fraser have dismantled longstanding divides, forging unprecedented collaboration. Moving forward, we are committed to deepening our partnership in economics, technology, and security intelligence.
Noticing your arrival, Elvira jumps in surprise and hurriedly turns off the television.

speaker: Elvira
content: I... I couldn't sleep.

speaker: Elvira
content: ...Fraser's acting way too eager. That guy "gifted" you a Sinner, then suddenly brought up the FAC and the past war? He's definitely up to something.

speaker: Elvira
content: But I know so little about Outlanders. Even my father rarely mentioned it in front of me. I...

speaker: Elvira
content: ...I don't really understand how actual Outlanders think.
As she speaks, she lowers her head, her mood visibly darkening. She must be thinking of Jelena again.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I understand.
Beyond offering such a simple response of acknowledgment, you find yourself at a loss for words.
[Scene Change] A softly warm-tinted ring Bureau backdrop as Jasmine's special ward
You step into the ward. Jasmine still lies unconscious. She whimpers softly, as if caught in a nightmare.

speaker: Schorl
content: Her condition is gradually deteriorating. The treatment through the shackles' connection is unsustainable in the long term since the corruption has built up over many years. MBCC has already arranged for her transfer to Banyan Medical College, where she can receive more stable care and where further research into the next steps can be better supported.

speaker: Schorl
content: Until then, Chief, please don't force yourself to perform the phase two treatment. It would cause you severe harm.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...I know.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Umm... Uhh... No...! Uhh...
Just a little help shouldn't hurt. You sit down beside her bed.

The shackles emit a faint glow, and the connection between you sends a wave of mild dizziness through your senses. Yet as the moments pass, you watch Jasmine's tense body slowly ease. For now, that is enough.
Time passes by, slow and steady, until night at last recedes and sunlight spills gently into the room. Finally, Jasmine stirs, her eyelids fluttering open.
Her vision is still blurry. She vaguely makes out a hazy figure sitting beside her bed.

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...Chief... is that you?
She squints slightly and looks again, but when her focus returns, the figure has vanished—no one sits beside her.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Heh, hahaha... Running won't help. I can still smell you... Are you really that scared to face me?
Her fingers trace the indentation along the edge of the bed—a mark left by someone who had remained at her side for a long time. The faint warmth still lingers, refusing to fade.
Slowly, Jasmine's laughter fades into silence. She pulls her hand back, the lingering warmth slipping away, her eyes fixed on the ceiling with a dazed expression.

speaker: Jasmine
content: You really are a good person...
June 20, N.F. 115
[Scene: Executive Committee]

speaker: Nirvana Representative
content: We demand a thorough investigation into the drifters disrupting the mining agreement. This is clearly a coordinated attack, specifically premeditated to sabotage Nirvana—no, to sabotage the city-state's crucial project.

speaker: Matilda
content: Do not test our patience. We are open to negotiation, but only under two conditions: full agreement on equity shares and profit distribution, and complete disclosure of the technical plans for Aurum Secretum's production capacity expansion. So far, Nirvana has avoided addressing either point.

speaker: Matilda
content: If you genuinely value the opportunities of the Great Expo, then come back to the table and directly address the core issues instead of using external distractions to pressure us. We expect sincerity. The people of the West District are watching.

speaker: Nirvana Representative
content: Sincerity? The people? Haha, who appointed you as the people's voice? So a handful of stubborn traditionalists get to define "public opinion," while everyone else's voices don't count?

speaker: Nirvana Representative
content: Take a walk through the streets, and ask any Syndican with half a financial brain how much longer they're willing to put up with this charade of yours.
It's just that this time, they're not opposing Nirvana's heavy-handed pressure—

speaker: Protesting Crowd
content: No more delays to the development! West District can't wait! Open the mine! Cooperate for progress! Build our future today!!

speaker: Protesting Crowd
content: The Executive Committee must step aside! No more blocking negotiations for personal gain!!!
A moment's hesitation is all it takes for Matilda to miss her chance to counter. Her opponent immediately pounces on the opening.

speaker: Nirvana Representative
content: Plenty of West District residents already hold Nirvana shares, which is proof we're sharing wealth opportunities. Meanwhile, you're the ones disrupting the labor union's work and standing in the way of real progress.

speaker: Nirvana Representative
content: The Great Expo is already underway, and Hypercube trade is absolutely critical—yet here you are, holding everything back. Let's be honest, aren't you just deliberately damaging our city-states' interests?

speaker: Matilda
content: This is...

Matilda can't definitively claim these protesters are all just vagrants hired by Nirvana to cause trouble. She recognizes that when faced with significant economic opportunities, no one can force people to sacrifice their livelihoods for some "higher cause." After all, everyone has the right to aspire to a better life, especially since the West District has suffered for so long—many truly need the money.
Max King bursts through the door, panting for breath.

speaker: Max King
content: Meeting adjourned! Meeting adjourned!! The protesters are storming the Committee building!! Everyone evacuate now!!

speaker: Nirvana Representative
content: Tch... Of all the times... Weren't they causing trouble in another district? How did they end up here?

speaker: Max King
content: Well, about that... haha, they kind of followed me here. I was trying to bring the sheriffs to smooth things over, but couldn't hold them back, haha.

speaker: Max King
content: Alright, if we don't move now, they'll really kick the door down! I've got cars ready outside. Everyone head back home for now. Let's continue this tomorrow!
The Nirvana representatives hesitate, reluctant to leave but knowing they have no other choice. They are the first to depart, but not before leaving a parting message for Matilda as they pass by her.

speaker: Nirvana Representative
content: Hmph... The investment deal will be finalized before the Expo closes. You'll see.

speaker: Nirvana Representative
content: Everything will be settled at Parfait's dinner party, and you're not even worthy of a seat at that table.
With a scowl, he turns and walks away.

speaker: Max King
content: Get it done soon and don't let it disrupt the Expo. We still need to discuss cooperation with Fraser. Clear?

speaker: Matilda
content: ...Speaker, your attitude sure changed fast. This is nothing like what you said before.

speaker: Max King
content: Well, sorry about that. The higher the seat, the wider the view—your position shapes your perspective. Nah I don't think you'll ever understand this. Now, do me a favor and get back to work, 'kay?
With a darkened expression, he carelessly gathers the scattered documents from the table, shoves them into Matilda's hands, and pushes her away.
As he passes by another West District representative, the latter remains silent for a long moment before finally speaking up.

speaker: Samuel
content: ...For a negotiation this important, shouldn't the Speaker be present in person? Have you been excluded?

speaker: Max King
content: Huh?! Do you know what "Speaker" means? My words and leadership are already echoing through every corridor of power! There's no need for me to personally attend to every single matter.

speaker: Max King
content: You fools... open your eyes! Nirvana is out there seducing everything with money and opportunities—the stock market is the ultimate casino! The tide has already shifted, and they're riding it straight to victory. Meanwhile, what do you have? How many allies can you possibly gain by nitpicking contract clauses all day? Wake up! Do you really believe you can win this fight alone?

speaker: Samuel
content: ...You're right. We've been too naive. I'll change my approach. But I never imagined that after half a year, the Speaker of the City Council would still be standing alone.

speaker: Samuel
content: Where are your OWN allies, Mr. King?

speaker: Max King
content: ...The Speaker of the City Council's allies? It's the entire DisCity, of course! Now, enough of this. Go handle the situation outside before they turn chaos into catastrophe. I'm sure you do not want things to get even worse.
He smiles, and he has no choice but to keep smiling.
On the streets, the protests persist, but now, sharper voices are beginning to emerge from the crowd.

speaker: Protesting Crowd
content: The Executive Committee must step aside! No more blocking negotiations for personal gain!!!

speaker: Protesting Crowd
content: RESIGN! Cavendish OUT of the West District!! Rustfire BACK to the Drifter Camp!!
It's finally over.

Max King trudges down the empty corridor, his steps heavy with exhaustion. Shrugging off his coat, he sinks into the chair beside the ward bed. The report in his hand shows that Nirvana's plans are progressing smoothly, but this is not what he has hoped for.

He hopes that the West District can see through Nirvana's conspiracy, that the citizens won't be swayed by illusory promises of wealth, and that the scarce information he possesses can reach those who need it.

But he can do so little, trapped like a fly in a shadowed web. He never knows which corners hide watching eyes, or which walls steal his whispers to the conspirators' ears. Worst of all, he can't be sure who is safe to trust, or how to keep his "friends" from snaring themselves in the same sticky threads.
On the ward bed, Adrian lies deep in slumber. Thanks to the underground doctor ${PlayerName} introduced, his life is no longer in danger, but he still hasn't regained consciousness.

speaker: Samuel
content: Where are your OWN allies, Mr. King?
Max King sits listening to the steady beep of the heart monitor in silence, his face buried deep in his hands.
[Scene Change]
You're at a discreet, secure meeting point. Having completed your exchange with the disguised agent, you walk toward the door together.

speaker: 9th
content: The Fraser delegation's conduct has been acceptable so far. They've provided numerous Aurum Secretum samples and shared significant intelligence regarding the Farland Alliance... though all of it will take time to verify.

speaker: 9th
content: Adelaide has been getting quite a lot of media exposure. The press is showing tremendous interest in this alleged brother of Quinn's president. Notably, he appears to enjoy the publicity and seldom declines interview opportunities.

speaker: 9th
content: For now, the identification of Outland extremists remains our top priority. Fraser's intel is helpful, but operational delays are inevitable, especially with the massive abnormal sandstorms crippling FAC's mobility outside the city.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Thank you for your hard work. If you have personnel to spare, I'll leave the list of requirements we just discussed in your hands. That intelligence is very helpful to me.

speaker: 9th
content: Understood. We'll contact you immediately when there's any update.

speaker: 9th
content: Let me walk you out. You look like you haven't slept properly in days. Madam would tease you if she saw you like this.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Haha... thanks, but I'll manage. It's no problem.
As you reach the doorway, the agent suddenly stops, the smile on his face turning into something more complex.

speaker: 9th
content: ...Mmm, looks like one of your requests just walked right up to your door.
Following his gaze, you turn toward the entrance, where a woman in red has just parked her car by the road, directly in front of you.

speaker: Woman in Red
content: What happened to you? It's only been a few days and you already look so glum.

speaker: Catherine
content: Hop in. I'll take you for a drive.
Run!
This is the only thought burning in Sibilla's mind. She tears forward, the sting of her wounds lost beneath the rush of adrenaline.
(Scene Change: Back alley of the hall)

speaker: Sibilla
content: <i><color=#7683a2>This is the place. I remember this back alley leads to...</color>
(Scene Change: Syndicate)
Syndicate.

This is the place Sibilla has known only through sketchbooks and the tales of traveling merchants. Vast as a labyrinth, it makes the perfect den of iniquity, where those who wish to vanish slip into the shadows without a trace.
She has no guarantee that she can shake off her pursuer here, but waiting for death is not an option.

speaker: Sibilla
content: Haha, this layout... looks a lot like Furor... I'm good at this.

Dilapidated buildings loom, their alleyways narrow as capillaries. Garbage and filth choke the space between ground and sky, and through it all, people wander—living in the chaos of it. Everything feels familiar to her.
Sibilla glances back, only to see a group of Syndicate thugs have cornered her pursuer in the middle of the street.

speaker: Syndicate Thug
content: Hey, who the **** are you?? Walking around my block like you own it? Where did you even pop out from?

speaker: Syndicate Thug
content: Those clothes... You're not a Syndican. You're a ******* spy from Nirvana, eh?
The armed thugs close in, blocking the assassin from every angle. Their leader snarls a curse, knife glinting in the light. But the answer they get is just one.
Clang—!
With a sharp metallic clang, the thug suddenly finds his hands empty.
Before a scream can escape him, his vision warps, as if his head has torn free from his body, thrown into the sky...
...and lands with a thud on the sewage-streaked ground.

speaker: Sibilla
content: Eeeeek!!!!

When the assassin finally leaves, Sibilla crawls from the blood-splattered garbage heap on all fours, her hiding place now a tomb. But she doesn't even have the luxury of doing something for the decapitated corpse.

speaker: Sibilla
content: That person's an assassin, someone completely mad! There's no way they'll back down!

speaker: Sibilla
content: I can't lead them to where there are people... That would only get innocent people killed!!
She has no choice but to run. Fortunately, running is something she excels at.
She claws her way up crumbling walls and deliberately presses bloody handprints at crossings to lead the assassin astray.
The evasive maneuvers successfully buy her distance from the assassin—but at a cost. Now, she finds herself lost in the vast labyrinth of the slum.

speaker: Sibilla
content: *Pant*...
The sun is gradually setting.

Her fingers have gone numb, her legs distant and foreign beneath her. Pain pulses from her wounds in relentless waves—if this lasts much longer, the assassin won't even need to strike the final blow. Infection or hypothermia will do the work for them.
A ghostly voice suddenly whispers behind her, followed by a searing pain splitting her chest. Sibilla lowers her gaze, only to see a silver blade protrude from her body.
Her vision gradually floods with crimson.
(Black Screen)

speaker: Sibilla
content: Hang in there... Hang in there... Not yet...
Option C - Right Side [Live]

speaker: Sibilla
content: I have to go back... need to give this to someone... I already saw him...
female_content: I have to go back... need to give this to someone... I already saw her...

content: Her strength bleeds away with every step. Fingers clenched around the protective charm—her townspeople's final gift—she staggers around the corner and breaks into a desperate sprint.
But her hope is quickly shattered, plunging her into despair once more.

speaker: Sibilla
content: No...
(Scene Change: Show wall)
Before her stands a solid brick wall. The afterglow of sunset paints the weathered stones with an ominous blood-red hue.
Behind her, she hears the footsteps of death.
That's a dead end.
After tracking through the maze-like slums for most of the day, she has finally cornered the woman in a dead end.
The dark shadow quietly slows her pace at the entrance.
Peering into the alley, she sees the woman at the dead end, standing frozen in place. There appears to be no struggle left in her.
Concealed in the shadows between buildings, she silently approaches her target. When just two meters away, she pounces like a leopard, driving her blade toward the chest of the cloaked woman.
But her blade meets no resistance—none of the jarring halt of flesh or the gritty catch of bone.
Sensing something is wrong, the shadow yanks the cloak away, only to discover nothing beneath. Its owner has long since vanished without a trace.
(Scene Change: Inside Parfait's room)
Sibilla presses her hands firmly against her mouth, terrified that even the slightest sound might alert the assassin lurking outside the window.
[Intensify horror atmosphere]
Sibilla hears a chilling, sinister laugh.

speaker: Fraser Assassin
content: Heh... Heheh... Good, keep running... Scuttle and hide like the filthy little pest you are...

speaker: Fraser Assassin
content: Shut your mouth and I might let you live a little longer...

speaker: Sibilla
content: ...Mmph...

She doesn't dare move—not an inch. Humiliation and rage sear through her, but it's the terror that chokes her, thick as a hand around her throat. Having lost too much blood, her consciousness begins to fray.

The ringing in her ears swallows the world. Every instinct screams at her to rush outside, to hurl herself onto the blade and end it all—No! She claws at the last frayed thread of reason not yet warped by terror. Think. Now.
What options does she have left? Is there anything in this room she can use against that assassin? What could possibly help her survive?!
(Red Flash)
The footsteps draw nearer—closer, louder—until Sibilla sees it. A long, distorted shadow spilling across the window frame, stretching toward her in the cold moonlight.
(Red Flash)

Then, she sees a high heel and a slender leg step through the window frame. Next emerges a suit, its fabric rippling like deep violet in the moonlight, and finally, a cascade of meticulously styled blonde hair...

speaker: Parfait
content: Phew... Finally gone... What gang was that anyway? Prowling around my place...

speaker: Parfait
content: Ugh, there's nothing even worth stealing—OW, MY HAIR MY HAIR! It's stuck—
The woman mutters under her breath about her stuck hair as she raises her head. In the moonlight, she finally spots the intruder inside the room.
After a brief silence, both women simultaneously erupt into ear-splitting screams.
(Red flash + screen shake + sound effect, maximum intensity)

speaker: Parfait & Sibilla
content: AAARRRRRRGGGHHH!!!!

speaker: Parfait
content: Parfait Medici—that's the name of mine that resonates across both banks of the Rust, the name of DisCity's stock market guru. This Parfait is a frequent face in finance magazine interviews, the star of upper-class investment salons, a legend of investment and value, and the most intriguing and mysterious tycoon.
[Television]

speaker: Parfait
content: This stock was once just an unassuming second-tier blue chip, but now, like the unprecedented technological innovations exhibited at the Great Expo, it's rewriting the rules of the capital market right before our eyes.

speaker: Host
content: What a brilliant analogy! But when we look at Eastside Aster Industrial's 46-point surge in just three months, some analysts are calling it pure speculation—hot money chasing momentum. How do you respond to that?

speaker: Parfait
content: Oh dear, when champagne overflows, fools see only the fizz, while the wise taste the decades in every drop.

speaker: Host
content: Look at that! Parfait's words just sent shockwaves through the market. Aster Industrial's stock is up another 2 points! I've said it before, and I'll say it again: Never question the vision of the stock market guru Parfait!

speaker: Parfait
content: Parfait—that's my original name, a con... credit transaction specialist from the West District slums. The closest I ever got to high society was working at an Eastside concert hall, which was perhaps also the closest I'd ever been to wealth.

speaker: Parfait
content: These two identities should be worlds apart, especially in DisCity. And yet, here I stand between them. Not by grinding day and night, not by some miraculous windfall... but simply due to the easiest thing of all—

speaker: Parfait
content: I got a superpower. Just as city-states leverage credit to mint currency, I turn credit into tangible wealth. When people believe the stock market guru can work miracles? The stock market guru indeed conjures real money out of thin air.

speaker: Parfait
content: And I happen to be a natural in gaining trust.

speaker: Parfait
content: Since then, I've been swimming in the investment market like a fish in water. It's a battlefield of information, expectations, and above all, credit. And once I have credit? Information and expectations become my allies.

speaker: Parfait
content: In return, I only need to pay a modest "membership fee" to the organization that grants me power, and occasionally handle some very minor tasks.

speaker: Parfait
content: And there's one more thing to be wary of. The source of this power is everyone's "trust" in the stock market guru. My money flows into the hands of those who believe in me, and if that faith ever starts to waver, everything will vanish like smoke.

speaker: Parfait
content: So, I must be cautious. I have to live up to people's impression of being "wealthy," ensure my financial activities aren't questioned (they've been completely legitimized now, in fact), and also—

speaker: Parfait
content: I can't let anyone discover that I have this superpower, and I can't let anyone find out that beneath the legendary stock market guru "Parfait Medici" is just little broke "Parfait," a nobody.
[Enter Flashback 1]

speaker: Nirvana Representative
content: Mmm... the cover photo does capture essence rather well. As one would expect from the renowned stock market guru. An excellent stylist choice. Is this another gem from your exclusive little black book of contacts? Any chance you could make an introduction?

speaker: Nirvana Representative
content: ...That vacant expression isn't helping anyone. No matter how boring this expo is, we have contracts to sign here. The Fraser representatives are waiting at the negotiation table, and those overseas assets won't manage themselves. Can't you at least pretend to care for their sake?
Investments thrive on prudence, and true wealth demands respect before acquisition. Wouldn't you agree, my friend?

speaker: Parfait
content: I just happened to catch Thalia's stream, absolutely not because I enjoy her budget recommendations. As long as I don't indulge again, no harm done. Everything's perfectly under control.
[Enter Flashback 2] Passing through the VIP hallway

speaker: Nirvana Representative
content: Wait, what?? Who let this outsider jump into the fight?!

speaker: Parfait
content: Patience, my friend. Didn't we agree that everything would be settled at my dinner party?

speaker: Parfait
content: Let's look forward to the feast that awaits us that evening.

speaker: Parfait
content: It's fine. So what if the MBCC Chief is here? That doesn't mean he's hunting Sinners. And even if he is, that doesn't mean I'm his target. Yeah, everything's fine.
female_content: It's fine. So what if the MBCC Chief is here? That doesn't mean she's hunting Sinners. And even if she is, that doesn't mean I'm her target. Yeah, everything's fine.

content: [Flashback 3]

speaker: Fraser Ambassador
content: Next up, we have a special performance for you—an improvised dance piece inspired by Lamentur.

speaker: Fraser Ambassador
content: Presenting the nomadic blade dancer—<color=#fb9259>Jasmine</color>.

speaker: Parfait
content: The MBCC Chief is right beside me, but he's totally lost in the performance. As long as he doesn't notice me, he won't suspect me. Everything's fine...
female_content: The MBCC Chief is right beside me, but she's totally lost in the performance. As long as she doesn't notice me, she won't suspect me. Everything's fine...

content: [Flashback 4]

speaker: Nirvana Representative
content: Which city-state is she from? This isn't how business works here! Let us speak with her! It's not every day that my friend here finds something that she likes. We can't just let that—

speaker: Parfait
content: ...Please stop it, my friend. If you value our friendship, stop drawing his attention already...
female_content: ...Please stop it, my friend. If you value our friendship, stop drawing her attention already...

content: [Flashback 5] Syndicate Slums

speaker: Parfait
content: When I left home that morning, I never imagined the day would turn so... eventful. But it's not over yet. As the night falls, I find my Eastside mansion swarmed with a crowd, all clamoring for wisdom from the "stock market guru." But I desperately need rest.

speaker: Parfait
content: Then, it hits me... Near the Great Expo, there's still one place where I can find peace—my old home, the cradle of my soul. No reporters hounding me, no clients queuing for advice, just the quiet hum of the night. A stolen moment of tranquility.

speaker: Parfait
content: With renewed determination, I carefully disguise myself, move with caution, and avoid any potential threats. Finally, the last step! Open the window, slip inside, and I'll reach my longed-for sanctuary—just one peaceful, quiet night is all I need—
[Big CG]

Their screams pierce the air in unison—then, as if bound by invisible strings, both women clamp their hands over their mouths. The sudden silence leaves only the television's chatter echoing through the room.
[Back to TV]

speaker: Host
content: As we wrap up the program, what advice would you offer to everyday investors?

On the television screen, Parfait plucks a pen from the table, uncaps it with a decisive click, and turns over her interview notes. In swift, sure strokes, she sketches deep blue lines across the blank page, then scatters musical notes above them—the simple notation of a tune.

speaker: Parfait
content: Think of the melody of "La Vie en Rose"—you need the waltz's brisk grace, yes, but never forget the power of a well-timed pause.
Amid thunderous applause, the interview program comes to an end. Parfait waves goodbye to the audience and caps her pen.
...Clack.
That is the sound of the red clown nose falling to the floor from Parfait, who now stands rigid as a fence post in the center of the room, utterly still.

The round red nose rolls across the floor, wobbling to a stop at Sibilla's feet in the doorway. She bends to retrieve it, eyes flicking between the DisFortune Weekly cover on the wall and the woman who has just climbed through the window.

speaker: Sibilla
content: ...Parfait... Medici?

speaker: Parfait
content: You got the wrong person.
She denies it immediately.

speaker: Parfait
content: My full name is Par Florence Isabeau Celestine Montmorency Fait. I have nothing to do with Parfait. Who is Parfait Medici anyway? I don't know her.

speaker: Sibilla
content: You live here? DisCity's stock market guru lives here?

speaker: Parfait
content: No. Tonight is the White-Bearded Elder's Gift-Giving Festival. I dressed like this to secretly deliver presents to Syndicans. The disguise and window-climbing are all part of creating a surprise and maintaining the ceremonial atmosphere. I'm not supposed to reveal my true identity.

speaker: Sibilla
content: So you're a thief?

speaker: Parfait
content: Hell no!!! Everything here is practically bargain-bin! I was just passing through. I wasn't going to take anything!

speaker: Parfait
content: And who are you? You're not a Syndican. This counts as trespassing, which is illegal. Leave now, and I won't report you.
Sibilla doesn't answer. Her gaze locks onto the intruder, unblinking.

speaker: Parfait
content: ...Ma'am, do you understand Disian? Excuse me? Hello? Wait... could you be a lost Outlander?

speaker: Parfait
content: It's okay if you don't understand. Do you know how to get back to your group? I can't take you there myself, but I can point you in the right direction. The Cristallia isn't far from here.

speaker: Parfait
content: Par Isabeau Celestine Fait is pleased to meet you. No need to remember me, and please don't come back.

speaker: Sibilla
content: I understand what you're saying, and I know who you are.
Sibilla steps forward. What was extreme terror moments ago now hardens into a wild, desperate fire—the audacity of a soul betting its last coin on fate.

speaker: Sibilla
content: Do me a favor, or I'll shout and let everyone know you're here, Parfait Medici!

speaker: Parfait
content: Argh, come on...!
How could she forget such a fundamental rule? Once suspicion takes root, building credibility becomes nearly impossible. Now, she has no choice but to change tactics...

speaker: Parfait
content: Wait wait wait, let's talk! Now that you know who I am, why not negotiate? That's right, I am Parfait Medici. I'll give you a masterclass in candlestick charts. What do you say? Results guaranteed, and you'll make serious money!

speaker: Sibilla
content: I don't want money. I need you to do me a favor!

speaker: Parfait
content: What is it? Oh, I see now—you want to stay in DisCity, right? Planning to use the Great Expo visit to sneak away from your delegation, hide here in Syndicate, and have a fresh start as a DisCitizen? I can help but—

speaker: Sibilla
content: I can't get into the Great Expo, and I don't want to become a DisCitizen. I only need you to do one thing for me.
Sibilla steps forward and grabs Parfait by both arms.

speaker: Sibilla
content: Deliver a message for me, Parfait Medici. That's all I want.
Flustered, she shoves a crumpled scrap of fabric into Parfait's hand.

speaker: Sibilla
content: You don't need to know what's inside, and do not peek at it. I'm not asking for anything more. Once you've delivered it, I'll go and never trouble you again, I promise.

speaker: Sibilla
content: But if you reveal my secret, peek inside, or tell anyone about me being here—especially those people from Fraser—I'll expose your secret immediately! I'll start screaming right now! Let everyone know that the stock market guru Parfait is here!

speaker: Sibilla
content: I'm so sorry for doing this to you, but I have no choice. Once you hand it over, I'll disappear immediately—I'd even be ready to die here. Please!
Her bony fingers claw into Parfait's arms with desperate strength. The Outlander's sunken eyes stare back—hollow, fever-bright—as if clinging to their last shred of hope.

speaker: Parfait
content: Whoa, calm down! Nothing has even happened yet.
Parfait firmly grips both of Sibilla's arms, steadying the trembling Outlander. She studies her for a moment, then speaks slowly.

speaker: Parfait
content: Nothing has even happened yet. I won't do anything that scares you. Think about it. You already know my biggest secret, and that terrifies me. Why would I risk making you upset?

speaker: Parfait
content: Don't worry, you can trust me. After all, the most reliable people in this world are the ones whose weaknesses you know, don't you agree?

speaker: Sibilla
content: Is... is that so...

speaker: Sibilla
content: ...I don't know, but... I have no choice but to trust you now. Please...
As Sibilla's breathing steadies, Parfait exhales in relief—there, that's better. They can just talk everything through.

speaker: Parfait
content: Yes, trust me, and let's talk this through properly. Who do you want me to find?

speaker: Sibilla
content: A public official, but... I can't get near him. He seems to be someone quite high up. When something happens, he's immediately surrounded by people.
female_content: A public official, but... I can't get near her. She seems to be someone quite high up. When something happens, she's immediately surrounded by people.

speaker: Parfait
content: Hmm... If he's high-ranking, I actually might have a chance to reach him. You say you can't get close... Have you seen him recently? Where was it?
female_content: Hmm... If she's high-ranking, I actually might have a chance to reach her. You say you can't get close... Have you seen her recently? Where was it?

speaker: Sibilla
content: The Great Expo...

speaker: Parfait
content: A high-ranking official at the Great Expo—that would be among the Chamber of Commerce, the Speaker of the City Council, or the Nirvana representatives. I can definitely reach these people. Just leave it to me.

speaker: Parfait
content: What does he look like? Any specific details you can share?
female_content: What does she look like? Any specific details you can share?

speaker: Sibilla
content: His position... I can't remember. The report had his code name, SHP-13.
female_content: Her position... I can't remember. The report had her code name, SHP-13.

speaker: Parfait
content: Do you know his name?
female_content: Do you know her name?

speaker: Sibilla
content: Name... I think it's ${PlayerName}.
At the sound of the name, Sibilla watches as Parfait contorts into an extremely twisted posture and covers her face with her hands.

speaker: Parfait
content: Argh, oh no...!
Twenty minutes later.

speaker: Parfait
content: My credibility as the stock market guru is everything. I can't afford even a whisper of scandal or any unfitting associations. "Parfait Medici" must remain above suspicion, especially regarding that person—I cannot contact him directly.
female_content: My credibility as the stock market guru is everything. I can't afford even a whisper of scandal or any unfitting associations. "Parfait Medici" must remain above suspicion, especially regarding that person—I cannot contact her directly.

speaker: Parfait
content: So I can only help you with the delivery under conditions where I won't expose myself, won't attract attention, and won't get too involved. I've also got my own deals to handle along the way. This will take some time, so you'll need to be patient.

speaker: Parfait
content: But since I gave you my word, consider it done, and I'll ensure your secret stays locked away as you requested. You're still holding my secret, after all.
Parfait extends her hand with a smile.

speaker: Parfait
content: If these terms suit you, let's shake on it. Now, allow me to reintroduce myself—I'm Parfait, just Parfait without the Medici.

speaker: Sibilla
content: ...I'm Sibilla.
Before Sibilla even realizes it, her hand has already grasped Parfait's. Parfait answers with a radiant smile, then turns away to begin making arrangements.

speaker: Parfait
content: I need to act quickly, but before that, we need to sort out your situation.

speaker: Parfait
content: You're also one of my little secrets now, which means we'll have to hide you away somewhere safer. And when I'm not around, we need to have someone protect you.

Parfait juggles various communication terminals all at once, her keystrokes a rapid-fire symphony that electrifies the cramped space. Sibilla watches, dumbfounded, until at last, Parfait leans back with a heavy exhale—the triumphant sigh of a mission accomplished.

speaker: Sibilla
content: ...That ${PlayerName}... I can tell he's a good person from how he treats Jas... I mean, my friend. But you seem afraid of him. Why?
female_content: ...That ${PlayerName}... I can tell she's a good person from how she treats Jas... I mean, my friend. But you seem afraid of her. Why?

speaker: Sibilla
content: Did he also invest in stocks with you?
female_content: Did she also invest in stocks with you?

speaker: Parfait
content: I can't say anything more about that. You have your secrets, and I have mine. This is the stock market guru's deepest one.

Parfait extends her hand with practiced ease. Sibilla, catching on this time, mirrors the gesture. But before their palms can meet, a thunderous bang shatters the silence, rattling the door in its frame.
Just as Parfait moves to answer it, the flimsy lock gives way with a few shakes, and a swarm of people bursts into her tiny, run-down apartment.

The moment the lock snaps, the intruders freeze as one. At their head stands a red-haired woman who, despite awkwardly fingering her worn brass knuckles, maintains every bit of her intimidating presence.

speaker: Gracelyn
content: Parfait, you big dumb***! They caught you? Are they onto you? Hurry, I've got a car ready. Let's get you out of here and to a safe spot!

speaker: Harry
content: Shh, shh! Quiet, quiet!! It's supposed to be a secret!

speaker: Gracelyn
content: The secret's already blown, for ****'s sake! I told her to cut it out, said she couldn't keep it under wraps—but did she listen? Hell no! She's been faking money! Faking MONEY!! I told her not to—
As they shout and burst through the door, the four of them come face to face, and Sibilla distinctly hears a groan of despair.

speaker: Parfait
content: <size=25>...Oh well...</size>
A few minutes ago.
Parfait and the others take Sibilla with them to another hidden location in the slums.

speaker: Parfait
content: Anyway, I'm just doing a little favor for this new friend of mine. Helping her helps me too.

speaker: Parfait
content: Sibilla got hurt, and she's really shaken. Can you look after her and keep her out of sight for a bit? Aunt Gracelyn, Mr. Harry, I'm counting on you two.

speaker: Parfait
content: Well, I'm off! Save the lectures for next time! See you!
She leaves with a smile plastered across her face—or rather, flees the scene—and then...
[White Out, Scene End] (Change to a dilapidated house background)

BANG! A baseball bat is smashed against the floor. The lead woman slams her boot onto the table, looming over Sibilla, who crumples to her knees. She trembles under the woman's intent stare—a clear act of intimidation.

speaker: Gracelyn
content: Hey, listen up. I'll make this crystal clear: nobody else alive on this planet knows Parfait's secret except us.

speaker: Gracelyn
content: This is Syndicate. Faking cash is barely worth mentioning. Parfait just whipped up some chump change a few years back—peanuts compared to what the Nirvana suits have taken into their pockets.

speaker: Gracelyn
content: Oh, and just so you know, reporting her to that whatever Sinner Bureau won't help you one bit. Their boss is tight with us Syndicans, like thick as thieves.

speaker: Gracelyn
content: Parfait's secret's stayed buried 'cause I've been the one cleaning up her messes. If anything leaks from you... well, let's just say I'm very good at taking out the trash. Got it? Answer me!
How can Sibilla possibly speak? Her breath catches in fear, her body trembling—then, a sudden tap. A hand lands on the red-haired woman's shoulder.

speaker: Harry
content: C'mon, Gracelyn. She's an Outlander—she can barely speak our language. Doubt she even gets what you're saying. Why waste your breath trying to scare her?

speaker: Harry
content: Why don't you grab some water? You've been ranting forever. Your throat's gotta be parched.

speaker: Gracelyn
content: Ugh, why didn't you tell me sooner?? Look at me, all stressed out for nothing! With all that chaos tonight, I totally thought Parfait got into some trouble again and someone was after her.
The red-haired woman visibly relaxes, her entire demeanor softening as she mutters her way into the kitchen. Something about the scene feels strangely familiar to Sibilla.
Meanwhile, the young DisCity man named Harry turns to her, speaking slowly with exaggerated hand gestures. He seems to genuinely believe that Sibilla isn't proficient in Disian.

speaker: Harry
