content: Truth holds an irresistible pull for any chronicler. We pursue it above all else. Life itself included.

speaker: Celine
content: Well now... I trust in your integrity, Chief. After this fair exchange, I have every confidence you'll conduct yourself properly. And as for me...

Her hand quickly slips from yours, and the professor immediately eases back into her seat, looking perfectly poised and beautifully serene once more. She holds your gaze now with a deeply soft, remarkably steady warmth.

speaker: Celine
content: If it's for the sake of truth, a chronicler will stop at nothing.
end
Before you can even begin to formulate an answer, she's already sprung into action, positively luminous with a surge of bright, bustling enthusiasm.

speaker: Celine
content: Oh my, I'll have my hands full now! Field interviews... Should I start with Donald or Matilda? I've heard Mr. Samuel keeps quite the extensive records as well. Chief, could you arrange a few introductions for me today? How many can you line up?

speaker: Linda
content: Professor!! Not again!! The Quinn banquet is tonight. Have you forgotten? Someone might commission a book from you! That's real funding we're talking about! If we can't pull in more support, our research budget is going to hit rock bottom again!

speaker: Celine
content: Not to worry. I can always resolve that with a quick visit to the Fabius estate. It can wait. But you've reminded me of something... Linda, why don't you go and assist Chief?

speaker: Celine
content: ${PlayerName} is unfamiliar with the university, and there's no telling what complications might arise once he's inside those halls. I'd feel far more at ease knowing you were there.
female_content: ${PlayerName} is unfamiliar with the university, and there's no telling what complications might arise once she's inside those halls. I'd feel far more at ease knowing you were there.

content: Linda stands there thunderstruck, mouth hanging open.

speaker: Linda
content: Didn't you just say my fourth draft is due in three days?! And besides, humanities students aren't even allowed inside those buildings!
At her student's heart-wrenching accusation, Celine hides her face in her hands, sorrow pooling in her eyes.

speaker: Celine
content: Alas, the history department's halls grow ever emptier. Of all my students, you're the only one I can truly count on now. But if you're really unwilling...

speaker: Linda
content: W-well... if you really need me to...

speaker: Celine
content: Come now, when would I not need you? Oh! I've also prepared a miner's outfit. It's deliberately weathered, authentic grime and all. Does it suit me? Think it'll help me blend in?

The graceful, cultivated, perpetually unflappable "highborn academic" standing before you now strips away the mask, letting slip a genuine, heartfelt longing for a world her Paradeisos peers would never bother to acknowledge.
She's going to fit in perfectly. They will like her.
You get to your feet and say your goodbyes. After two steps, though, you stop and look back over your shoulder.
Linda has already gone, scratching her head. Only Celine is left, her eyes still on you. Catching your backward glance, she answers it with a smile.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: How much do you know about the <color=#fb9259>Underground</color>, Professor?

speaker: Celine
content: Ah, now... that would be an entirely new consultation. I'd need fresh intelligence in exchange for that one.

speaker: Celine
content: One thing at a time, Chief. First, your opening venture. I'll be here, waiting to hear every detail when you return.

speaker: Celine
content: Every step you take is already pulling at the threads of history, sending ripples outward... I wish you a smooth journey ahead.

You walk out of the Central Library and look up. Sunlight bathes the world in perfect gold, the sky is blue as ever, dappled with clouds. You know your true target is up there, hanging far overhead. It might be out of sight, but never out of mind.

Your gaze returns to earth. Two blocks away, ringed by high walls and green canopies, lies DisCity United University, where the Ring Research Institute resides, where the "symposium" awaits. That is your next stage.
Professor Celine's help was essential, but that alone won't be nearly enough. You need your own kind of preparation.
United University. Ring Research Institute. Science. Genius...

A face comes to mind. You fish out your terminal and punch in an encrypted code. A strange, indescribable ringtone sounds in your ear. The line opens before the second ring. You feel the smile creeping in and let it come.

speaker: Option
options: Hey there, our beloved genius hero. Got time to look over a new script?

content:
<size=40><color=#9C19D9>Pixel</color><color=#F6EF2F>'s</color><color=#1A45DF> Private Channel</color></size>
<color=#F03679><size=50>[Voice of Pix]</size></color>
<size=40><color=#2AFFCC>Makes Its</color><color=#2AFF4C> Grand Comeback!!!</color></size>

Pixel: Helloooooo, my most distinguished guests of the Ring Research Institute symposium. How's your thesis coming along?! Don't you panic, don't you fret! Pixel's Master Ghostwriting Channel is back to haunt your deadlines!

psojfhga:
Oh great. The anonymous paper pusher slithered back into my feed. I've blocked you like five times already, what kind of dark magic algorithm are you running? When's the raid?

Pixel:
Oh shush, you wound me! I poured in all this blood, sweat, and maniacal cackling for you sweethearts, y'know! As for security? Pfft. This lady just gave the whole system a MAJOR, and I mean MAJOR, glow-up!

Pixel:
Servers have been relocated somewhere so undisclosed! DisMyth looks like a Caesar cipher now. Nearly 30 years of United University theses are stored in our databanks!

ioghiahi:
Can you do "System Design of Inspection Robots Based on Large Language Models"? Everyone else ghosted me.

Pixel:
Hehe. Radio silence means they saw "AI" in the title and ran screaming for the hills. Adorable. But graduation projects like this are my comfort food! AI encapsulation, threshold models, and coupling inspection path data? That's my breakfast, lunch, and late-night snack.

Pixel:
Ooh! And speaking of which, sounds like the symposium's sniffing around the same direction this year! But seating's tighter than a miser's wallet, and Quinn's already sprawled across half the chairs. So if you didn't snag an invite, don't you DARE mope about it! Just waltz right over to yours truly and buy the no-filler, all-killer essentials version!

Pixel:
<color=#fb9259>Academic problems? Pixel's got you covered!</color>

hglalwurg:
Can you actually pull off United University stuff? With all these local papers in your system, I'm worried you'll just churn out some patchwork plagiarism.

Pixel:
Oh, my, plagiarism is the caveman approach. United University's plagiarism database? Their advisors' pet peeves? Their citation blacklist? Sweetheart, I know their academic psyche better than they do.

hglalwurg:
Bold words. Can you deliver in a week? I'll need the full package of verifiable experimental data too.

Pixel:
Hmm... Well, cards on the table, but United University material does require a more delicate touch. Prestige demands precision, and quality commands coin! So, you'll need to pay a teeeeny bit extra. Check DMs, payment link's there. Don't leave me on read!

Pixel:
United University... Tsk. Once the shining jewel of Eastside. How many industry titans crawled out of those halls? How many clawed their way in to be so-called "pillars of DisCity"?

Pixel:
I got bored the other day and looked it up. International applicants alone take up over a thousand every year. Honestly, can you blame them? Land a spot there, and your family would frame that acceptance letter in gold leaf.

Pixel:
Of course, what it all boils down to is money, money, and of course, money. The city-state dumps the lion's share of the education and research budget straight into their laps. So the fact that they hoard all the top-tier journal publications? Shocking absolutely no one.

Pixel:
Me? Obviously I didn't make the cut. Here I rot, slaving over your bibliographies, woe is me, cue the tragic violins. Ugh, every time this topic comes up, I just get so sour. So! Allow your bitter host to lead you all on a completely simulated, absolutely-not-bitter tour of this so-very-elite institution!
[Impersonal Chief POV]

Lush greenery blankets the campus. Lawns and gardens are clipped to flawless precision, matching the hushed, reverent dignity of the classical halls they embrace. Stillness reigns. Every corner seems to whisper of scholarship's lofty mien.

The soft sound of falling water guides you toward a graceful fountain standing before the college buildings. Two young people of striking composure converse by its edge. They are of student age, yet their expressions bear a gravity that outstrips their years, their movements effortlessly refined.

speaker: Confident Student
content: The old professor's new lab got approved. He's real grateful to my father, even made a point to set aside a research spot for me. I just need to be on the roster for six months, and the thesis and degree take care of themselves. Leaves me free to focus on things that actually matter.

speaker: Refined Student
content: Must be nice. Wish I had your luck too. A new batch of government-sponsored students just came in from the farlands, and the administration decided I should be the one to play host. Ugh... I've told them I don't need connections like that. What's Fraser got to offer anyway? I want to aim for the city council, but do they listen? Nope. They just keep dumping this stuff on me.

content: I-I see. Truly worthy of the Director's star pupil. Now this is the standard the Ring Research Institute ought to uphold.

speaker: Distinguished Guest
content: Did you rush over here to present on Professor Isomer's behalf?

A shadow passes over Lemma Herzfeld's expression. She draws breath to speak, but a sharp clap rings out. The tall girl next to her has brought her hands together, and every eye in the room snaps toward her.

speaker: Enya
content: That concludes our portion. We'll leave the remainder to Professor Lambert. I'm confident that by now he has a thorough grasp of the material and can field any questions you may have. Please follow him to the conference room next door.
The audience seems unwilling to disperse. However, the staff she summoned continue to file in, growing in number until the majority have no choice but to fall in line and shuffle out.
The old professor approaches them. After an embarrassed word of thanks for saving him from that predicament, he parts his lips to speak, his voice unsteady.

speaker: Lambert
content: ...Did Isomer send you? Does she... does she have anything to say about... my situation?
Lemma's eyes flick to Lambert, then slide away in silence. It's the boy nearby who gently takes the old man by the arm and leads him aside for a quiet word.

speaker: Barrie
content: Shh—Lemma's not really in the best mood lately. Probably best not to bring all this up with her. Just leave it to us. We won't say a word about today to Isomer, alright? Don't you worry, Mr. Lambert. Go home and get some rest.
His words offer a measure of comfort.

speaker: Barrie
content: And maybe... talk it over with your family. Think about retiring a bit early, you know? My grandpa always used to say that once you get up there in years, the mind just can't keep up the way it used to. I imagine that's been happening with you too, Professor? Don't push yourself too hard.

speaker: Lambert
content: I—
Just like that, the old man is abandoned. He is prodded forward, guided out, his gaze empty and unfocused as he vanishes through the exit.
Lemma, meanwhile, makes her way directly to you both, or more accurately, to Summer. She plants herself squarely before her.

speaker: Lemma
content: The great "genius scientist" actually came back to sit through one of Lambert's garbage presentations. You really do have a gift for wasting your own time, Summer.

speaker: Lemma
content: All those years out there, and you never once came back. Was it because you knew you had nothing to show for it? Too embarrassed to show your face?

speaker: Summer
content: Nothing to show for it?!
Summer springs to her feet.

speaker: Summer
content: That just shows how out of the loop you are! I've already completed my greatest masterpiece: <color=#fb9259>The Age of Youth</color> anime trilogy, wrapped and perfect! It's incredible! MBCC still has the master copies. I'll do free screenings for everyone!

speaker: Lemma
content: Just hearing about it makes my blood boil. To think you'd neglect real work to this degree...I'm surprised you haven't packed up and moved into your little fictional world already.

speaker: Summer
content: Wait, that's an option?! Does this mean your Black Ring blah-blah-spatial-dimension-blah-blah-Mania-transition project that's been stalled for ten thousand years finally made a breakthrough? Congratulations, Lemma! Hurry up already, I can't wait to hop over to another world!
The blonde girl's eyelid twitches faintly.

speaker: Summer
content: Ooh, your eye twitched again. Don't tell me...

speaker: Summer
content: Oh, right! Those results at the symposium just now weren't exactly groundbreaking. Surely we didn't get stuck again, did we? What's the holdup this time?
Lemma tilts her head back. They're practically the same height, yet with the impressions she's giving off right now, she's unmistakably gazing down at Summer.

speaker: Lemma
content: We're progressing on our own timeline. A deserter like you hardly has the standing to offer critique.

speaker: Summer
content: Okay, but "deserter" does sound preeeetty cool. Thing is, before I left, I accidentally cleared out the whole task queue. Including the stuff that's not mine. What about you?

speaker: Summer
content: Team leader?
Lemma lets the taunt go unanswered. Then another voice, barely above a whisper, speaks up and draws this ridiculous conversation to a definitive close.

speaker: Sarah
content: Don't get so full of yourself. I remember perfectly well how you slunk away in disgrace five years ago.

speaker: Sarah
content: Have you forgotten what you came crying to me for back then?
Summer wilts before your eyes, every ounce of her earlier spark extinguished.
Lemma takes it in, her stare sharpening with contempt.

speaker: Lemma
content: ...The projects from five years ago are basically elementary school homework compared to what we're doing now. I can't believe you're still stuck back there. Pathetic as ever, I see.

speaker: Lemma
content: You deserve to be left in the dust.
Without so much as a flicker of hesitation, you step up and position yourself as a barrier before the now-drooping Summer.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Does winning a schoolyard shoving match like this actually make you proud? Kicking someone who's already down?
Only then does Lemma spare you a first glance, but her gaze quickly slides away.

speaker: Lemma
content: Did security all take the day off? How did some clueless outsider wander in here?

speaker: Lemma
content: The Ring Research Institute is a serious academic institution. It brings together the brightest minds and the most advanced research. A scientist's time is valuable. Every word spoken here should be a meeting of intellects, not wasted on someone who wouldn't understand it anyway.
Oh, a scientist? You clear your throat. Time to really make your presence heard.

speaker: Option
options: I'm the one bankrolling Summer's anime project.
I'm the MBCC Chief. That makes us colleagues.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Your institute doesn't seem all that picky about clueless outsiders, though. If anything, you threw a high-profile symposium just to welcome them. Even had top-tier talent like yourself come down personally to play host.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If you asked me, I'd even say you guys are actually quite fond of these scientifically-ignorant people. So, how about simply extending that exact same courtesy right here to me?
She glares at you, visibly stung by the remark.
But you didn't come here to pick on a child. While the little prodigy is still fumbling for a comeback, you take the opportunity to cut straight to what matters.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I need to see Isomer. She's your advisor, isn't she?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm here on business. And if we're going to talk business, I'd say speaking with the Director herself would be far more productive.
Something in your words must have hit its mark. Lemma's expression ices over in an instant.

speaker: Lemma
content: Don't try pulling rank on me. Unlike Lambert, I'm an actual research lead. I have full responsibility for my project, my team, and complete autonomy over every decision.

speaker: Lemma
content: I don't take orders from that woman.
Well, well, well. So there's some friction there. Better push it just a little further, then.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Oh? Your project? Impressive. What field, exactly? I have a hard time picturing the Ring Research Institute handing anything critical over to a bunch of kids.
She freezes, her eyes darting to you. Though she holds her mouth shut with every ounce of willpower she can muster, her expression, clearly unversed in hiding things, betrays her.

speaker: Lemma
content: ...If you're so concerned about BR-003, MBCC Chief, then maybe you should be back at your post hunting down the Undergrounders who are threatening to take it. Where exactly do you find the time to indulge some pink-haired brat and her dress-up delusions?
So she does recognize you, and she's aware of what concerns you. A student of Isomer's, perhaps?
In any case, it seems luck's on your side. Had it been Isomer who was here, it's hard to say whether you could pry loose even a single useful word. This girl, however, makes for the perfect wedge.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Well, since you already know who I am, that simplifies things. BR-003 is high on my priority list as well. You handle the research, we handle security. Sounds to me like the Ring Research Institute and MBCC ought to be on the same side.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: On top of that, I do have some insight into how the enemy operates. Wouldn't it make sense to compare notes in the field?

speaker: Option
options: Consider it an "exchange" between the two people in charge.

content: You gaze down at her. This angle offers a clear view of her blonde crown, and you make a point of tilting your chin up a fraction more.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Unless you think this grown-up's being too mean. In which case, we can drop it. I'll take this up with your "real" supervisor instead.

speaker: Lemma
content: ...Fine. Bring it on.

Summer exchanges a glance with the three kids across the way. They're almost synchronized as they make their choice: Summer darts to your side, the others to Lemma's. Two opposing forces now stand here, poised and ready.
Lemma's fingers are already hovering over the keys.

speaker: Lemma
content: I'm not some washed-up hack like Lambert. This time, you won't have any room to cheat.

This "academic exchange" is proving to be quite a marathon. Your chaos-forged combat instincts collide with Summer's unhinged creativity, and the result is what can only be called an unholy mess of a strategy.
And yet, remarkably, the other side rises to meet it. The duel rages on, unrelenting, feeding on its own momentum.

speaker: Research Assistant
content: Ah, um... That was a very meaningful exchange! You're both incredibly impressive—truly evenly matched. But Professor Lambert's presentation next door has already wrapped up, so perhaps we should also...

speaker: Lemma
content: Shut it! I'm not finished!

Lemma stares dead at the screen. There's a faint sheen of sweat on her brow, and her shoulders are coiled with tension. However, she refuses to yield. She strikes the keys at an astonishing pace, the exchange now too quick for the crowd to follow.

speaker: Lemma
content: Accounting for the margin of error, the simulation data he's presented holds up. Mania as a whole is intensifying; the fluctuations are violent, and the interference with existing shielding tech is getting worse by the day.
female_content: Accounting for the margin of error, the simulation data she's presented holds up. Mania as a whole is intensifying; the fluctuations are violent, and the interference with existing shielding tech is getting worse by the day.

speaker: Lemma
content: Tch. Only a few months, and it's already deteriorated this far. Even if we accelerate model iteration by 203%... can we keep up...? No. It's only going to get worse from here. We have to solve this at a more fundamental level...

speaker: Lemma
content: ...We don't have a choice. We need a breakthrough. I...

She lowers her voice, but her gaze remains fixed ahead. The trio behind her is clearly flagging. Still, each time their unwavering little leader delivers an order, they would look at one another, then quickly throw themselves back into the fray.

On the other side, Summer has caught fire. She dives deeper and deeper into the game, her glee escalating with it. She's all but left you in the dust now. As you look towards your opponents, you can't help but feel amazed, followed by a surge of another emotion entirely. The words escape of their own accord—

speaker: Lemma
content: Huh?

The improvisation. The focus. The decisiveness and sheer persistence. The way she learns at lightning speed and applies each lesson instantly. And the absolute, unquestioning trust her team members have in her leadership.

One could dismiss Summer's extraordinary intellect as the work of Mania. This girl, however, is no Sinner. Despite that, she radiates something almost none can deny: unmistakable and undeniable <color=#fb9259>genius</color>.
This child has real talent.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Your technical skills, your analysis, and that brain of yours are all top-tier. With talent like that, why aren't you out supporting the front lines? FAC and the rest of us would kill to have someone like you. You could make a real difference out there!
For a split second, Lemma falters. Out of all things, she hadn't prepared for you to praise her as such.
But she pulls herself together just as quickly, her features settling back into that familiar scowl.

speaker: Lemma
content: Are you serious? This is just a simulated combat environment. Everything's idealized. Real combat is something else entirely. There are way too many variables in this field. If something goes wrong because it wasn't properly tested, people die! A lot of them.

speaker: Lemma
content: This is not enough. Not even close... Just let me run one more set...
A hand firmly presses down on hers, stopping her in her tracks.

speaker: Research Assistant
content: Alright, Chief Scientist. The guests will be returning soon. How about we leave it there for now? You and the Chief can continue this discussion somewhere else. Take your time.

speaker: Research Assistant
content: Hitting a bottleneck is part of the process. Pushing too hard won't get you the results you're after.
Right. You've nearly forgotten that this is someone else's event. Looks like the time has come to pack it in.

You start drafting a request to EDGE in your head. You'd love nothing more than to borrow this kid for a couple of weeks, maybe ten days, even, whatever they'd approve. Imagine if she and Summer joined forces. The Bureau would practically have rockets strapped to it.

Lemma stops. She glances back at the assistant who intervened, her expression one of clear displeasure. You brace yourself for another show of arrogance from this blonde brat, but when she speaks, her voice is ice-cold.

speaker: Lemma
content: ...You're making me sick. I've had my fill of being your entertainment.

speaker: Lemma
content: Every single one of you... Is this what you so-called adults who can't be bothered with real work enjoy? Dressing up and putting on little performances, <color=#fb9259>Isomer</color>?!
A whistle escapes Summer. The three children across, too, are visibly thrown. They look at one another, bewildered, before their gazes converge on the two standing by the podium.
The so-called "assistant" laughs softly, as if she's just stumbled upon some rare amusement. When she speaks, her voice sounds entirely different.

speaker: Research Assistant
content: We already have geniuses like you in charge of academic research. Naturally, I'd need to find other ways to keep myself occupied, wouldn't you agree?

speaker: Research Assistant
content: For instance, all those menial tasks the Chief Scientist can't be bothered with. I'm more than happy to pick those up.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...You're...
The woman loosens her collar and removes her glasses. With a casual sweep of her hand, she brushes the hair from her eyes, then straightens to her full height as she fixes her gaze directly on you.
The mild-mannered researcher who guided you through the exhibition hall has vanished without a trace. Before you now stands someone else entirely.

speaker: Research Assistant
content: Greetings, Chief of the MBCC. I'm Isomer, current Director of the Ring Research Institute.

speaker: Research Assistant
content: It seems I've finally found the "right moment" to introduce myself. It's a pleasure to meet you.

Isomer
Honorary Dean of the College of Science and Engineering, United University
Director of Ring Research Institute
Chief Advisor of BR-003 Observation Hub

With Lemma out of the picture, Summer's game is also over. She reaches for another piece of cake to replenish her drained mental reserves, chewing absently as she scrutinizes the Director—now shed of her disguise—and searches her memory.

speaker: Summer
content: Munch munch... So this is Isomer? Huh. I kind of like her.

speaker: Summer
content: Turns out she's into cosplay and dress-up too.
Lemma shoots Summer a glare. The other three children's gazes dance between Lemma and Isomer, uncertain as to what they should do.
Isomer, on the other hand, looks completely at ease.

speaker: Isomer
content: Thank you all for coming, scientists. To show our appreciation for your guidance today, I've prepared a few gifts on behalf of the symposium organizers.

speaker: Isomer
content: Summer's visit was rather unexpected, so I had to arrange a rush order. If it's not quite to your taste... I do hope you'll forgive me.
She steps gracefully off the stage as she talks. A handful of gift boxes have somehow appeared on a table nearby. She plucks out the most garish one, shakes it, and Summer's eyes light up instantly.

speaker: Summer
content: G*nd*m?!

The genius high school girl throws herself forward. What she sees makes her gasp—it's a limited edition, no less! Beside herself with joy, she cradles the box, smothering it with kisses while bouncing in place. She races out the door, dying to crack it open and lose herself in tinkering.
Isomer sees her off with a smile. Then her eyes shift, and the remaining children go visibly rigid.

speaker: Isomer
content: And as for everyone from the Observation Hub, I recall hearing phrases like "rare collectible," "highly confidential," and "not for public release"... Were you referring to this?

Isomer turns and lifts the black box. In a blur of motion, Enya lunges forward and snatches it away, hugging it to her chest. She then turns around with a composed air, clears her throat, and straightens her expression.

speaker: Enya
content: Ahem! Right. Director Isomer, Lemma, and the Chief here seem to have matters to discuss in private. We shouldn't get in the way. Everyone, with me!
The Director sends the children on their way, simply watching them go. Then, almost casually, she appears at your side.

speaker: Isomer
content: When Summer first came to the Ring Research Institute, she was appointed Chief Scientist immediately. At the time, I was just an ordinary researcher at a Black Ring observation station. Different field, nothing to show for myself either. I doubt a rising genius like her ever even registered my existence back then.

speaker: Isomer
content: But fate has a way of playing tricks. After the Ring Weapon technology was leaked, suspicion spread everywhere. Her identity as a Sinner was dragged back into the spotlight. She came under relentless attack from within the Institute, and in the end, they pinned every charge on her. She was forced to cut ties and fled, branded a deserter.
She lowers her gaze, a touch of sadness in her expression.

speaker: Isomer
content: The years after that must have been brutal. I heard she couldn't even go home. It's truly fortunate that the MBCC found her and cleared her name. The way you two work together is really something to see.

speaker: Isomer
content: That genius girl who once walked alone has finally found companions she can truly trust. I'm so glad she's found a place to belong by your side.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're making it sound way more dramatic than it is. We're just buddies making an anime together. It's not that deep.

speaker: Isomer
content: If only Lemma could learn to trust grown-ups as well. She's an exceptional genius. She climbed to this position through sheer effort and now carries the entire Observation Hub on her shoulders—all without any Sinner powers to enhance her mind.

speaker: Isomer
content: She's the one who took over as Chief Scientist after Summer left. A "mortal genius" capable of going head-to-head with that "legendary monster."
She smiles at Lemma as she speaks. The "compliment," however, lands coldly.

speaker: Lemma
content: So that's what it was. Even if security slipped up, we still have people monitoring the symposium, watching the surveillance feeds. You let them in on purpose.

speaker: Isomer
content: The MBCC are also experts in Mania combat. They have exactly the kind of frontline experience we lack. Various circumstances made cooperation difficult before, but I've finally found the "right moment." Why wouldn't I seize it?

speaker: Lemma
content: Tch. We don't need them.

speaker: Isomer
content: Do you truly think so?
The smile slips from Isomer's face.

speaker: Isomer
content: Then I suppose you'll be troubleshooting the 64PA8 through 64PC7 and the entire 8X38 series obstacles on your own? How many more rounds of closed testing will you need? And the cost projections?

speaker: Isomer
content: I've already covered for you twice on the scheduled EDGE reports. How long of an extension are you asking for this time? Will you be explaining it to them yourself?
Lemma's silence brings the smile back to the Director's face.

speaker: Isomer
content: There we go. Now then, let's set up a simple testing environment. I brought the data with me, conveniently enough.

speaker: Isomer
content: Chief, I'd like to ask you for a favor. Please take a look at this <color=#fb9259>anomaly data reconstruction</color>. The incident occurred within the BR-003 field, and its nature... is somewhat unique.

speaker: Isomer
content: I know you've dealt with Black Rings extensively. You understand them. So, I'd like to hear your perspective. And if you're willing, you're more than welcome to take our systems for a spin and see where they break.

speaker: Lemma
content: Wait! That's internal data, classified material! Not even MBCC has clearance—

speaker: Isomer
content: You said it yourself, didn't you? The shackles generate sporadic, chaotic Mania states that can't be reproduced, which are remarkably close to <color=#fb9259>them</color>. Perfect, then. Use them as a trigger and simulate the enemy's attacks more accurately. You know exactly where you're stuck.
Her tone shifts slightly.

speaker: Isomer
content: And... "Research should never be compromised by politics." "Technology that can't prove itself stable on a real battlefield isn't worthy of trust." Your words, Lemma.

speaker: Lemma
content: ...Tch.
Their exchange carries so much unspoken weight that it's taking your entire focus to keep up. It's not until the Director's eyes land on you that you realize she'd just asked you a question.
No matter how you look at it, this is an opening. You have to take it and play it by ear.
The answer clearly pleases her.

speaker: Isomer
content: Thank you. It's a genuine pleasure working with you, Chief. I'll be counting on you, then.
She turns off the lights. The cube hovering above her palm begins to flicker, then, thread-like tendrils unfurl, sweeping rapidly across the entire room. And with that, the darkness shifts in hue.

It becomes a deranged space, endlessly dividing and folding in on itself, a prison woven from light where recognition falters and comprehension breaks down. But what is truly being disrupted? The space itself, or your consciousness trying to make sense of it? You can't tell.

Whatever the case, there is one thing that's not beyond you—the several nodes hanging suspended in the void. Their signature is unmistakably EDGE's design. Faint blue light wreathes each one, working in concert to hold this churning chaos together.

speaker: Lemma
content: A reconstruction of an incident scene. I scanned and preserved every piece of data from that moment. I've been running simulations against it ever since to verify my findings.

speaker: Lemma
content: You've been digging into BR-003 all this time, haven't you? Well, this is just the tip of the iceberg.
The image breaks into static as she speaks. The disturbance leaves a patch of absolute black that crawls toward the nodes. Then, alarms blare to life.
And at last, stillness returns.

The imaging system, it appears, can pick up your movements and Mania signature, feeding the recorded data back through another simulation pass. You've barely exerted yourself, perhaps because the system has nudged things in your favor. Either way, it's over now.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I still don't fully understand what just happened, but... the sensation felt close to Mania. The shackles seemed to recognize it better than I did. They locked right onto those mutation points.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I was mostly just following my gut. I can't really make sense of what I'm feeling on my own. That said, your scientists might be able to. Want to give it a try?
Your earnest invitation doesn't cheer Lemma up. She looks, if anything, even more crestfallen.
Her plummeting mood, however, merely draws an amused smile from the Director.

speaker: Isomer
content: It seems there were a few hidden cracks in your theory after all. Not the easiest to spot, I'll admit. So. What will you do now?

speaker: Isomer
content: Are you really going to waste more time defending yourself? Is it your theory you're trying to protect... or the pride of a <color=#fb9259>genius</color>? ...Chief Scientist.
The genius girl shoots her a scorching glare.

speaker: Lemma
content: ...I don't need you to spell it out. I'm heading back.

speaker: Lemma
content: The data we just gathered is invaluable. I'll analyze it thoroughly and submit the revised proposal as soon as possible.
The petite blonde girl clicks away in quick little steps. As she passes you by, Isomer's voice, so detestable to her, comes chasing after her from behind.

speaker: Isomer
content: Where's your gratitude?
Her tone is icy and condescending, with undisguised mockery seeping from every syllable. It seizes the girl mid-step, stopping her dead in her tracks.

speaker: Isomer
content: Someone here "assisted with your experiment," "identified flaws in your proposal," and "may provide critical support going forward." What sort of attitude should one show toward such a person? Shall I demonstrate? Or perhaps...

speaker: Isomer
content: You'd rather stay stuck in this bottleneck? Waste a few more months?

Lemma halts at your side and stands there for what feels like an eternity. Then, rigidly, almost painfully, she twists her head back and speaks—one word at a time, each syllable steeped in humiliation.

speaker: Lemma
content: Thank you... for your assistance... Chief ${PlayerName}... of the Minos Bureau of Crisis Control!
BANG! The door slams shut violently, so much so that it still reverberates as the footsteps skitter away down the hall, chaotic and frantic, like a startled deer in flight.

Before a smile can even form on your lips, Isomer cracks first. She leans against the table, arms folded, shoulders shaking. The dignified Director of the Ring Research Institute has let herself loose, laughing softly before your very eyes.

speaker: Isomer
content: Hehehe...

speaker: Option
options: So I'm just your teaching aid now? For wrangling difficult children?

speaker: Isomer
content: Forgive me, that was most unprofessional. Thank you for playing along, Chief. You've given Lemma some genuinely valuable insights to work with.

She dabs at her eyes with a lingering smile, then flicks her hand. A chair glides over, inviting you to sit in it. She takes her own seat across from you, pulls out her terminal, and scrolls through files while playing a few voice messages. It's all the usual: funding, projects, favors sought, and so forth.
Isomer deals with them swiftly, like someone would when sweeping aside trash. She also seems entirely unbothered that you, an outsider, are watching the whole thing.

When the round is done, the smile falls away. The mask reasserts itself, sealing that fleeting moment of openness again. The person sitting across from you right now is, without a doubt, the Director of the Ring Research Institute.

speaker: Isomer
content: The children's games are over. Now then, let's talk, adult to adult.

speaker: Isomer
content: You came to see me to push forward your proposal at the EDGE meeting. You want to remove the obstacles standing in the way of suppressing BR-003, don't you?

Just as you thought, she knows everything. The question is, since when? The moment she first approached you in disguise? Or further back still, far enough that she arranged the symposium, anticipating that you would come, far enough that it traces all the way back to some EDGE meeting where the two of you stood toe to toe?
However deep the roots may go, this mission behind enemy lines has finally brought you to the threshold. The time for battle has arrived.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This visit has made everything clear. The Ring Research Institute is fighting to hold onto BR-003 because it's an essential testing site. You have quite a few projects tied directly to it.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And behind every one of those projects is massive research funding, the very thing that's elevated the Institute to where it stands today. You can't afford to let go.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That's what EDGE-07 really cares about. They preach science and rationality as the Institute's representative, but it's all a tool in reality. Every argument and every assessment serves one purpose: protecting your interests.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You could've kept this charade going, if I'm being honest. Unfortunately...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Your safety system can't actually protect the Black Ring. It's fundamentally unstable; it can't eliminate every risk. That "anomaly" you just showed me is proof, you know that as well as I do. Ten geniuses won't change anything either. That girl hit a wall a long time ago.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The bottom line is, you have no real grounds to oppose my proposal. BR-003 is far more dangerous than what you've been reporting. It has to be suppressed. I'll personally see to it that all of this is presented to EDGE as evidence in the next meeting.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If you don't want it to come to that, then drop the act. Agree to my proposal. That way—

speaker: Isomer
content: Very well. I agree.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: —we'll still have room to negotiate. For example—
[Background + Character Portrait]

speaker: Isomer
content: I agree to your proposal. And I'll do everything in my power to support it.

speaker: Isomer
content: EDGE values science and rationality. So, before the next vote, I'll prepare all the evidence you'll need to support your position. I'll also deal with the person causing you the greatest obstruction.

speaker: Isomer
content: Well?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Backing me offers you zero upside—certainly nothing that compensates for losing the Black Ring. I'm not naive enough to believe you'd make a choice like this without weighing what's at stake.

speaker: Isomer
content: What makes you so sure?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I've already laid out the logic. And besides...
You meet her eyes.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You don't need to sell me. When it actually counts, at the EDGE meeting, I've seen exactly how 07 votes and what stance they take. That person represents the Institute's interests, and by extension, yours. Isn't that right?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: <color=#fb9259>Director</color>?
She offers no direct answer, simply eyeing you as if you were a defiant pupil.

speaker: Isomer
content: So that's your reason for infiltrating the Institute after all. You wanted to dig up the identity behind that number. Bold of you. Crossing that particular line takes nerve.

speaker: Isomer
content: So, who do you suspect? Want me to give you the answer?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: We've come this far. There's no need to keep dancing around each other.
She looks at you, and slowly, she utters a name.

speaker: Isomer
content: Heh... I like that answer. Close, but not quite.

speaker: Isomer
content: Give me a little more time, and I will be EDGE-07. As long as you and I work together to pull down the one sitting in that seat right now.
end

speaker: Isomer
content: <color=#fb9259>Lemma Herzfeld</color>.
[Portrait]

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It's her?!
The shock escapes before you can contain it. Isomer simply watches, savoring your reaction.

speaker: Isomer
content: Our genius Chief Scientist. Proud, domineering, she always has been. Her arguments are forceful and persuasive. She can always be counted on to provide theoretical cover for every faction's private agenda. And on top of that, she holds considerable sway over the BR-003 Observation Hub...

speaker: Isomer
content: I'm only the Hub's nominal head. A front, something EDGE put in place to obscure 07's true identity. I handle the "trivial tasks" on her behalf. Every decision at the Institute revolves around her. I'm nothing more than a glorified babysitter for the genius.

speaker: Isomer
content: That is, of course, when her research is going well. If you want to bring down EDGE-07, you have to strike when she's actually struggling, which is now.

...Struggling? Now that you think of it, that girl indeed seemed anxious. So sensitive, obsessive, and prone to sinking into low spirits—all classic signs of hitting a bottleneck. And the woman before you has taken note of every last one.
[Enter CG]
Isomer has firmly locked onto her prey.

speaker: Isomer
content: During the war, the new BR-005 caused disturbances on an unprecedented scale. BR-003 was forced into operation, and its public exposure severely disrupted the stable research environment she relied on. Even now, it remains under frequent attack from unknown sources.

speaker: Isomer
content: All I need to do is submit the "incident" we just demonstrated. That would give me grounds to grant you special security clearance as a Mania expert. You'd gain access to the BR-003 Observation Hub and be authorized to participate in the safety inspection.

speaker: Isomer
content: And once you're inside, if you want data to prove her theory unreliable, you'll have all the evidence you could ask for. Summer can compile the material and help you build a case to convince EDGE. Doesn't that sound appealing?
Now, the hunter's eyes turn to you.

speaker: Isomer
content: From what I gather, of EDGE's eight seats, only the newly appointed 08 openly supports you. And she's already under heavy scrutiny herself. The two of you being seen working too closely together would only invite unnecessary suspicion. For both your sakes, don't play that card lightly.

speaker: Isomer
content: Beyond her, you have no other allies up there. But I can give you the strongest backing possible. I'll help you defeat EDGE-07 on "rational" grounds. And if it comes to it, I can make sure she disappears from the meeting entirely.

speaker: Isomer
content: That will clear every obstacle between you and the Black Ring. BR-003 will be yours to deal with as you see fit.
Her words trail off. She lets the silence settle, waiting for your answer.
You have to give it to her, she knows how to pitch an offer. Everything she lays out is something you need. The moment you remove 07, a clear path forward and success will be within sight.
...And yet, the moment that number finally maps itself onto a real, tangible person, something inside you shifts, leaving you deeply unsettled.

You look back at the Director, and your mind replays the way she teased the girl earlier, the smile that graced her face. Now it all seems as unreal as the persona she wore before. What remains is nothing but cold, ruthless calculus. It is as though a great fissure has yawned open before you, and an icy dread crawls up your spine.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...If we're going to talk cooperation, then I'll need you to be straight with me first.

speaker: Option
options: Was everything with her just a game to you?

speaker: Isomer
content: Heh. What else would it be?
Jump

speaker: Isomer
content: Hehe... I would've thought that by now, after coming all this way to see for yourself, you'd have worked it out.

speaker: Isomer
content: At this level, science is power. A genius can transcend both birth and class. This is the last stretch of a golden age, an era when even someone of humble origins can still climb to the top. That's exactly how I worked my way here.

speaker: Isomer
content: But then I ran into them. And that was as far as I could go.

speaker: Isomer
content: Unlike those kids, I'm not one of truth's chosen. I can't compete with a real genius or push the research any further. I can't shape the world the way she does.

speaker: Isomer
content: But the moment I stopped fixating on that and looked elsewhere, the view opened right up. Just like now... I've found you, haven't I?
Isomer raises her eyes to you as she speaks. She smiles as she reaches out her hand, her ambition laid utterly bare.

speaker: Isomer
content: The same obstacle stands in our way. Let's remove her together, and we'll both get what we want... And when we do...

speaker: Isomer
content: You get your Black Ring, I get my seat. A perfect win-win. What do you say?

speaker: Isomer
content: Chief ${PlayerName}.

speaker: Celine
content: So... Not only did you meet Isomer in person, but the entire core team at the Observation Hub as well. You confirmed EDGE-07's identity... and even received a covert invitation to collaborate.

speaker: Celine
content: Your little excursion turned out far more eventful than I ever imagined. Something straight out of an adventure novel. If I wrote this into a history book exactly as it happened, I'm afraid I'd be accused of wild exaggeration.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Aren't adventure novels supposed to be more romantic than this? This trip was an eye-opener. I never expected the infighting among scientists to rival anything in politics.

speaker: Celine
content: I'm sorry it wasn't what you hoped for. Academia has never been pure. Science and politics, interests, power... they've always been tangled together. Especially in an era like ours, defined by catastrophe.

speaker: Celine
content: Right now, Aurum Secretum, catastrophe weapons, and new mines are all under intense scrutiny. They're tied directly to economic production and survival, not to mention commercial rivalries and city-state strategy. Who's to say which breakthrough might upend everything and reshape the world?

speaker: Celine
content: Which is why every sector's been pouring in investment, placing their bets. And the scientists who control those technologies rise right along with the tide. Once that happens... well, things get rather complicated.

speaker: Option
options: Is our history professor feeling a little envious?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I've seen pure scholars who are thrown into the circus of fame, eventually losing themselves among all the temptations. What do you make of that, Professor?
Celine smiles.

speaker: Celine
content: I respect them. Reaching that level isn't as wonderful as you'd expect. History is littered with prominent scientists who were kidnapped, or assassinated.

speaker: Celine
content: You might ask your good friend, General Augustus. Back during the Independence War, who ranked higher on the assassination hit list—her, or the EDGE scholar who provided her with technical support.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Sigh... Knowing the general, she'd probably say, "My reputation strikes too much fear. No one would dare. I'll be generous and let the bald scientist in the back take the top spot this time."
Celine lets out a soft chuckle before lowering her gaze.

speaker: Celine
content: At this stage of civilization, a technological breakthrough can no longer be chalked up to the efforts of a few brilliant individuals. It's part of something far larger, a massive system. Often the key piece of it.

speaker: Celine
content: Resources, information, time, talent... it takes the combined strength of entire city-states, of all humanity, really. And you have to navigate something far more complex: human nature. Those pure, idealistic scholars of a bygone era would find it hard to adapt, I think.

speaker: Celine
content: Being able to shut yourself away in an ivory tower and pour everything into your research... that's a luxury in itself.
She heaves a sigh, sadness pooling in her expression.

speaker: Celine
content: But I'd be lying if I said I wasn't a little envious. Just look across the way. The College of Science draws students in droves, year after year. Their halls are always buzzing. Meanwhile, our students keep switching tracks. Now, we've only got Linda left, barely holding on with a threadbare budget... It does get lonely, you know.

speaker: Celine
content: Sigh... If only you could do a little promoting for us, Chief. A few recommendations here and there.
...Well, when she puts it like that, it really is a little heartbreaking.

You picture the Ring Research Institute's sprawling, splendid architecture, the extravagant banquet spreads at their seminars, and the sheer hum of activity over there. Meanwhile, Linda is left with nothing but study rooms borrowed from the library. The College of Humanities has sunk to renting out its own classrooms to outside groups.
She says her seniors, juniors, and even the faculty keep jumping ship. It honestly gets more depressing the longer you think about it.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I've got to give it to Linda for sticking it out through all of this. You know, she told me that she envies the College of Science too.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Said if she had their resources, their leverage, their connections, a little room to operate in the grey, she'd trade like crazy. Swap favors, cut deals, whatever it took to get her hands on unpublished historical records. Write the hell out of some papers.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: She really is your student, sharp as a tack... and that kind of passion isn't something you can fake.

speaker: Celine
content: She said all that? Hehe, thank you, Chief. You have a real gift for lifting someone's spirits.
She looks genuinely happy now. Perhaps, while the moment is right—

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Then how about returning the favor, Professor? I could use a little cheering up myself. Your colleagues over at the College of Science are giving me a splitting headache.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: How deep do the waters run at the Ring Research Institute, really? What are all these factions actually fighting over? Is there anyone I can even trust? And this whole EDGE-07 situation... should I really get involved? How much risk am I taking, throwing in with a careerist like that? I'm completely in the dark here.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: They say history grants wisdom. Well, I could really use some of yours right now.

speaker: Celine
content: I see... I'm honored that you'd come to me with this. Truly, it makes me happy.

speaker: Celine
content: Intelligence, experience, whatever I have that might help, I'm more than glad to share it with you.
For all the tenderness in her voice, she only reaches out with that knowing smile. You recognize the gesture at once. It seems the hour has come for yet another "trade."

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Alright then, let's trade. What are you in the mood for this time?

speaker: Celine
content: Hmm... intriguing. I've read through all the official battle reports, of course. But I could use some personal perspectives to fill in the gaps. Those friends of yours... General Augustus, the Commander-in-Chief, and that Sinner girl who ventured deep into the Outlands. They're all such fascinating subjects.

Jump

content: The expedition... I did notice you left out certain details in the DisSea operation reports. If you'd be willing to let me in on it, I'd love that. Just tell it to me as a story. I also have a few friends who are very keen to hear more about the pioneers' exploits.
end

Any future updates, you can sync at your convenience.

speaker: Celine
content: Though I suspect these materials won't resolve what's really troubling you. They won't answer the questions you're actually facing right now.

speaker: Celine
content: Neither can I.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But...

speaker: Celine
content: So... Why don't we take a break, and you can hear about what I found instead?

speaker: Celine
content: Thanks to the doors you opened, my West District fieldwork turned out to be quite productive. The recordings and photos alone are nearly filling up my storage, and I'm still sorting through everything. Come, join me. Who knows? You might even be able to fill in a few gaps for me while we're at it, Chief.

speaker: Raven
content: You want to talk about Rustfire? Ah, you really know your stuff! Whoever sent you my way, what an eye for talent, what impeccable judgment! I am, without question, the single most devoted witness to that glorious, heart-wrenching chapter of history.

speaker: Raven
content: And not just Rustfire! From the West District to DisCity to the world beyond, from BR-002 to the golden age to the N.F. Chronology! Long, grueling, magnificent, tragic! I couldn't possibly do it all justice in one sitting, but...

speaker: Raven
content: I've composed 108 new epic poems celebrating this radiant era! Not just my own hand, mind you, but collaborative works with the future blossoms of West District! You must include them all in your history book! I hereby grant you full rights!

speaker: Raven
content: Crache! Impeccable timing. Look! I've included that assignment you handed in last time among the 108 poems! You too shall be immortalized alongside the rest of us!

speaker: Hella
content: Ooh, ooh, me too! I know stuff about outside the city, way, way farther than WhiteSands! I just got back, in fact! There's this insanely awesome scientist over in Fraser, like, my age, and she's a total freakin' genius!

speaker: Hella
content: Oh, and I can tell you all about my adventures too! All the... what's that word again? Right! Local customs. And culture. Let's start with Tuco!

speaker: Matilda

speaker: Matilda
content: There are also a few people with rather sensitive statuses. Nirvana has been stirring up trouble nonstop, so it's not safe for them to show themselves. You won't be able to meet them directly, but...

speaker: Matilda
content: If Chief were to accompany you, I believe we could still arrange something. Some of them have been missing their old friend, after all.

speaker: Donald
