You close the forum and set aside the comms device. Well. Now you're even more exhausted.

speaker: Flawed Schorl
content: Your predictions were accurate, Chief. Through more proactive strategic planning, we've shifted from a defensive to an offensive position against the Underground. Morale among the research staff has improved significantly as well.

speaker: Flawed Schorl
content: I'm pleased you were able to reach a consensus with the EDGE majority. It wasn't until you chose to prioritize the protection of the Black Ring that the Ring Research Institute was truly relieved of its pressure. Your extensive experience combating the Underground provides the most reliable support they could ask for.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: With the Sinners there, I'm not too concerned about that front. The strategy we laid out beforehand was more of a small experiment, really. I wanted to test another theory...

Halfway through your response, the black bipyramid starts rotating, its upper and lower halves separating and spinning out of sync. It's a preprogrammed gesture that activates whenever Schorl wants to flatter you or "hype you up."

speaker: Flawed Schorl
content: Oh? Have you formulated another bold and insightful hypothesis? You never cease to surprise. So then, my dear Chief, might I have the privilege of hearing your thought process?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: My "thought process" is this: EDGE should stop wasting time on your emotional support module. You're not cut out for it. Stick to what you're actually good at.
It drops a few inches with a soft whir, seeming demoralized by your words. Only now do you finally feel a hint of perverse satisfaction.
Jump

speaker: Flawed Schorl
content: Oh? You...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No more flattery, Schorl. Be rational and don't waste time. I'll tell you what I'm thinking.
It freezes in midair, then starts rotating in place with a series of mechanical clicks and pops. You're not sure if it's pleased or has simply crashed from being interrupted.
end

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...The experiment was simple. After consulting with Lemma secretly, I deliberately tweaked the testing schedule to add an emergency security calibration session this afternoon, lasting half an hour. Because it was a "last-minute" change, we announced the security vulnerabilities in advance.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: We tampered with the test data before distributing them. The data sent to different individuals were slightly different. These inconsistencies would be hard to detect without close comparison, but were different enough for the recipients to reach different answers for the source of the security vulnerabilities after their calculations.

speaker: Flawed Schorl
content: ...You suspect there's a spy within the research team. You want to test them.

speaker: Flawed Schorl
content: So what was the outcome?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: An attack did occur today, but it didn't target any of the fabricated "vulnerabilities" we announced. The attacker avoided every single trap perfectly. They even purposely chose the most fortified point in the system to launch their assault.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What do you make of that result, Triangle Face?

speaker: Flawed Schorl
content: ...It could be pure coincidence. It could be a communication error among the spies. It's also possible they detected the trap and changed their strategy.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The spy could be operating at a high level. They had all the information at hand, yet still launched the attack as a response to our trap, mocking us. Look, they didn't even bother finding a scapegoat.

speaker: Flawed Schorl
content: That is indeed a possibility, but it factors in the suspect's emotional inclinations. This decision is not the direct result of rational judgment. My calculation module cannot guarantee accuracy when assessing scenarios of this nature.

speaker: Flawed Schorl
content: But Chief, are you hinting at someone specific? Based on your habits, I deduce that you already have a suspect in mind.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Yet instead of investigating her, you praised her for her contributions during the defense against the attack.

speaker: Flawed Schorl
content: You've misunderstood. We received your report and thoroughly investigated all leads. We haven't taken more drastic action because, first of all, the investigation yielded no concrete evidence. Second...

speaker: Flawed Schorl
content: We suspect everyone equally, and we monitor everyone equally. As you noted, keeping pace with the Underground's dimensional technology is critical, and the experimental costs and risks are both extremely high. Every action taken by the Ring Research Institute's personnel has to be strictly scrutinized.
That makes you realize you're under surveillance as well.

speaker: Flawed Schorl
content: The investigation into Isomer is still ongoing. Rest assured, you're not the only one who's filed a report against her.

speaker: Flawed Schorl
content: Lambert and several other professors at the Ring Research Institute have been particularly proactive. They've submitted a substantial amount of documents. We're reviewing them all. Everything will be handled anonymously, of course.
Sounds like another round of infighting within the Institute. Aside from noting how quickly people are willing to turn on a fallen villain, you have little interest in getting involved.
What truly concerns you is the potential connection between Isomer and the Sillage Society.

You pull out your comms device, swipe away the million missed calls from Lemma, and search up the latest enigmatic anime clip Summer sent to you. The genius apparently devised this encryption method specifically for the operation. After decoding and translating it, the message reads:
[TOP SECRET]
Great job, Summer. This is exactly what you need.

speaker: Option
options: Schorly, over here. Got some cool stuff to show you.

content: Schorl drifts over eagerly. You're just about to brief it when your comms device vibrates again. That idol song starts blasting.
Wait... Did Barrie mess with your device? You barely catch who's calling before the line connects on its own.

speaker: Lemma
content: Why did you ignore all my calls?! Didn't we agree to keep each other posted?! Weren't you supposed to personally verify everything?! I was going out of my mind!
Too late to hang up. You can only push the drifting black bipyramid a little further away.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Easy, Lemma. Things are a little complicated on my end. I'm still dealing with the mess here. What about your...

speaker: Lemma
content: Then I'll go first. We haven't finished all the calculations yet. There's still about 14% left to go. And 27 new issues cropped up today. But the results have been promising so far! We've already identified 37 suspicious locations!

speaker: Lemma
content: Assuming the enemy has planted decoys, we're still conducting further analysis to narrow the list down. Once we've cut the number in half, we can start considering...

She enthusiastically recaps everything she already included in her messages. Pure elation radiates from her. She sounds exactly like a teenager eager to share her accomplishments and desperate for some compliments. You quickly offer a few.

options: I heard all about it. Even Summer would be impressed!
I knew you scientists had my back!
Wow, what a genius you are!

speaker: Lemma
content: Tch, I know that already! And I'm not done yet. Listen, there's something else that really annoyed me!

speaker: Lemma
content: Everyone at the Hub has been working their tails off! We're understaffed, and there are so many unexpected problems and a ton of calculations to be done. A few of us literally passed out after overdosing on energy drinks. We even had to pull Summer in to help. And yet... someone still had the nerve to slack off!!

speaker: Lemma
content: Isomer! Director of the Ring Research Institute! The Observation Hub's so-called partner! And she. Never. Showed. Up. Not once! Can you believe that?!
Ah. She's probably busy being investigated right now.

She goes on ranting for a few more minutes, ending up spending more time complaining than bragging about her achievements. She seems completely oblivious to just how calculating the person she's badmouthing really is, or how treacherous the waters around her have become.
You glance at your watch. Almost time for the next phase of the operation.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Lemma, first off, congratulations on your breakthrough. I'm truly happy for you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That said, you need to stay on guard as you progress. I know you hate all this political nonsense, but this is a very important experiment. Many pairs of eyes are on you right now. Don't let your momentum make you careless.
Sensing she's a bit put off, you quickly adjust your tone.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You can always reach out to Professor Celine. She knows how to navigate all this, and she's great at lifting people's spirits. You like her a lot, don't you? Want me to connect you two right now?

speaker: Lemma
content: Ah, wait...!
She stops you, and this time, her tone turns hesitant.

speaker: Lemma
content: ...I wasn't just venting. I mean... We're so close to making it. We need all the help we can get, even if it comes from... Isomer...

speaker: Lemma
content: So I was thinking, you two used to work pretty closely, right? And your personalities are similar too. You're both calculating and shrewd. You two seem to get along... So maybe you could talk some sense into her? Get her to come back and actually contribute?
...Calculating and shrewd?
You hold back the question. You're more curious about something else.

options: I thought you two never got along?

content: She falters for a moment.

speaker: Lemma
content: It's a critical time right now. We need all the brainpower we can get...
You fall silent. You know that's not her only reason. She seems to always expect more from talented researchers.
And the more naive Lemma sounds, the darker and more sinister Isomer's face in your memory becomes.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Precisely because it's a critical time, we need to be more selective about who we choose. You know your experiment can't afford any mistakes.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You need real, dedicated scientists. Isomer... her mind hasn't been on research for long. At this important juncture, don't count on someone you can't fully trust.
The other end of the line goes quiet for a long while.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What's wrong, Lemma? You still there?

speaker: Lemma
content: ...No. There's more to it...
[Brief cut, scene transition]

Having remained silent throughout the entire call, Schorl finally offers a quiet reminder. It's time for you to set out with the team to track down the leads about the Sillage Society. Checking the time, you realize Schorl's right, and Lemma should be preparing for her next experiment as well.
You offer her a few final words.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Focus on your work for now, Lemma. You know the root of all your recent problems is that the project hasn't been moving forward.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Once the experiment succeeds and your theory is validated, all that petty nonsense will be irrelevant in the face of real scientific achievement. I'm buying you time by clearing the obstacles and blocking out the noise. But the definitive blow has to come from you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Show me what a true genius can accomplish when fully focused. Once you've proven yourself, the results will speak far louder than any criticism ever could. And when that day comes, those who doubt you will make their choice accordingly.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'll be there for the experiment the day after tomorrow, at 4 p.m. sharp, bringing the MBCC's "super security team" and a fresh batch of field data. You'd better bring your A game too, 07. I'm counting on you to track down the Underground's nest.

speaker: Lemma
content: Hmph, of course I won't let you down! And don't you let me down, either. Get here early and watch me make it happen.
Finally, you let out a heartfelt chuckle.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Give it everything you've got, genius.
With that, you finally press the button, sending out the documents about Isomer from your device.
If she's clean, then all the better. But if she isn't... it'll be up to you to protect the real scientists.
May 29. While the Observation Hub prepares for its final verification experiment, you clean up another two suspicious hideouts on the ground.
Lemma's instructions are accurate, and your command on the field is equally impeccable. You wrap up the operation well before 3 p.m.
But you don't make it to the experiment, at last.

On May 29, N.F. 116, at 15:00, the BR-003 Observation Hub's core research team is scheduled to conduct the final verification experiment on the Mania dimension eigenvalue. According to EDGE-07's assessment, this experiment will validate her theory and make the dimensional fissure technology a reality.
At 09:00 on May 29, six hours before the final verification experiment, EDGE's Hush unit executes a secret intervention, seizing full control of the Observation Hub.

May 29, N.F. 116
BR-003 High-Altitude Observation Hub

At 10 a.m., led by Chief ${PlayerName}, the MBCC's team launches attacks on two suspected Underground bases. This large-scale operation is executed under considerable tension. At the same time, experiment preparations at the BR-003 High-Altitude Observation Hub come to a sudden halt.

An EDGE unit seizes the observation station without prior warning or explanation. The control room is in lockdown and the scientists' work is suspended. The young researchers are corralled away from their stations, and their tasks are taken over completely.

And the one assuming control of everything is a palm-sized Schorl. ${PlayerName} was accompanied by an identical one during the previous visit, but now, the little device somehow appears completely different.
Right now, the flawless black bipyramid hovers at exactly 1.618 meters above the ground. Rotating slowly as it absorbs data, it seems to be surveying everything below simultaneously.

speaker: Sarah
content: ...What's going on?
Sarah is still dumbfounded. She was in the middle of adjusting an equation when they pulled her away. The normally timid girl uncharacteristically demands to return to her station.

speaker: Barrie
content: We still need to run the final verification on the theory. Can't you wait just a moment? I mean...

speaker: Schorl
content: The verification won't be necessary. Your proposal was thoroughly assessed upon submission. The implementation procedures are clear. The work can be easily transferred.

speaker: Schorl
content: Well done on completing your mission. We'll take over the Observation Hub from here.

speaker: Sarah
content: Stop patronizing us. I know what this means.

speaker: Sarah
content: A change of this magnitude doesn't just happen without prior announcement. Replacing the staff with only six hours' notice is simply ridiculous. We're not...

Before she can finish, a row of Hush humanoid soldiers turns their heads in unison, eerie masks locking onto them, mirroring the terrified young faces. Sarah flinches, instinctively shrinking closer to Barrie. The boy shields her with his own round frame.
But he's scared too, his voice no longer as relaxed as it was when he was doling out potato chips earlier.

speaker: Barrie
content: Does EDGE mean to tell us that... we made a mistake?

speaker: Schorl
content: That is not EDGE's intention. However, a detailed evaluation of the proposal will involve classified information. Following the transfer of authority over the Observation Hub, you are no longer authorized to access such information.

speaker: Schorl
content: Please follow our instructions and exit the control room. Arrangements will be made for all of you.
Only one person steps forward.

speaker: Lemma
content: ...I've received no prior notice. I'm demanding an explanation.
Lemma steps out and stands in front of Schorl. As EDGE-07, she shouldn't fear such a mass-produced device. She tells herself as she clenches her fists.

speaker: Schorl
content: Simply put, EDGE has received credible intelligence that would explain the frequent attacks on the Observation Hub. The real reason isn't merely the technological gap between the enemy and us...

speaker: Schorl
content: ...There's a leaker inside the Hub. And it's very likely a senior technical expert who's crossed critical security boundaries.

speaker: Schorl
content: Security has thus become the top priority. An investigation must be conducted immediately. That's all.
The news is too shocking for Enya. She cries out.

speaker: Enya
content: How is that possible?! Everyone here has devoted themselves to this project. It shouldn't even be possible with all the data security systems we have in place. And even if it were, why would anyone sabotage a project they've poured years of their life into?!

speaker: Enya
content: Let's just say there really is a security risk, that you suspect there's a... spy in the Hub. Do you really need to replace the entire staff because of one or two people? Who's going to maintain all this equipment? What will happen to our research?

speaker: Schorl
content: Your concerns are valid. Rest assured, EDGE won't resort to such foolish measures.

speaker: Schorl
content: We monitor everyone's behavior, but we only take action against specific targets—those under the heaviest suspicion.

speaker: Enya
content: ...What do you mean? You're suspecting... us?

speaker: Lemma
content: Enya!
Lemma stops her colleague. She has heard of situations like this, has even voted to approve similar orders herself, but this...
This is the first time she witnesses and experiences it firsthand. She understands clearly that this conversation cannot go on, at least not in front of everyone.
Keylan-II is hidden in her pocket. Lemma tries to concentrate, activating the brainwave communication discreetly.

speaker: Lemma
content: EDGE-07 requests... an emergency meeting immediately.

speaker: Keylan-II
content: Request received, EDGE-07. Requesting synchronization.

speaker: Schorl
content: As you wish. Requesting synchronization.
[Scene transition. EDGE communication channel]
Once she's connected to the channel, Lemma realizes 03 is the only other numbered channel joining the meeting.

<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07:</color> ...Where are the others?
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-03:</color> You called an emergency meeting. The other representatives must be occupied with their other tasks. I'll relay their opinions.

<color=#fb9259>EDGE-03: </color>Back to your question. You wish to discuss the matter about the Observation Hub? Then, first, compose yourself, and be rational, 07. My time is limited as well. Please set aside your personal emotions so that we can communicate efficiently.
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07: </color>Don't patronize me. I don't need your lecture on the importance of being rational.
She takes a deep breath.

<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07: </color>The Observation Hub is being taken over due to a "leak," but that's just a pretext, isn't it?
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07: </color>I already reported the relevant security concerns long ago. SHP-13 also acknowledged the possibility of an internal leak. We've proven through experimentation that the Underground's threat can be prevented and managed. On the contrary...

<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07: </color>You stormed the Hub without prior notice to its current administrator. EDGE made this decision without letting 07 participate in the discussion. None of this aligns with established protocol. I demand an explanation.
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-03: </color>A reasonable request. Syncing data to EDGE-07's channel. Please approve the transmission.
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07: </color>Transmission approved.
[Electromagnetic sound effect, static screen, 1s]
An influx of data floods her mind. Eight requests to review 07's qualifications in regard to her eligibility for the position within a single year. Lemma's eyes widen.
She suddenly realizes what has transpired behind her back during the year she spent consumed by research, too absorbed to spare any attention for anything else.

<color=#fb9259>EDGE-03: </color>It is true that most research projects you've overseen have seen fast progress. But the "flagship" projects have consistently failed to meet expectations, incurring excessive monetary and time costs, not to mention the vast amounts of research resources consumed.
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-03:</color> Take the current BR-003 dimensional Mania analysis project as an example.
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-03: </color>You've failed seven critical verification procedures. On three occasions, your insistence led to unjustified modifications to the development plan. Last month, you once again rejected the simplified proposal submitted by the technical advisors, further extending the project timeline. This resulted in a series of consequences, the most severe being that...

<color=#fb9259>EDGE-03: </color>The Ring Research Institute's commitment to Nirvana last year, the development of next-generation unmanned mining technology, has seen zero progress. Research on Aurum Secretum has also fallen severely behind schedule.

<color=#fb9259>EDGE-03:</color> EDGE has since initiated a comprehensive review covering all 36 months of your tenure. Your performance in professional decision-making, resource allocation, cost control, and project transparency has been less than satisfactory. More concerning is your overall conduct. Specifically...
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-03: </color><color=#FFBC6F>We're seeing very little cooperation from you, which severely impacts your reliability.</color>
She clenches her fists even harder.

<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07: </color>A review? So what you're saying is I should abandon the hard, crucial problems and waste my time on meaningless, time-consuming garbage projects instead?
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07: </color>Just because you think they're "important" and "the previous staff didn't do a good job," you want to waste a brilliant mind on these projects?  So they can "boost completion rates," "make the review metrics look better," "keep the public happy"... and "keep me from coming under scrutiny"?
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07: </color>And you're questioning my project management and transparency... Does my work violate the Security and Confidentiality Protocol? Or do you want daily reports? Would there even be time left to do actual work? And when I do report, how many of you can even understand it, or bother to listen seriously?

<color=#fb9259>EDGE-03: </color>Be rational, Representative 07. Your talent is beyond question. But overdependence on it creates problems.
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07: </color><size=42>Such as non-cooperation?</size>

<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07:</color> I've given my full technical support to every decision passed at these meetings. Even during the Ash Campaign...
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07: </color>I was strongly against deploying the disaster deterrent due to its risks. But I respected the voting result and expedited adjustments to the Black Ring facilities to execute the plan. And yet I was the one dealing with the resulting damage, exposure risks, and endless side effects.
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07: </color>How much more cooperative do you want me to be? What more can I do?
EDGE-03: Be rational.
It feels humiliating to be reminded of that as a scientist. Lemma's nails dig into her palms.

<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07: </color>Each EDGE representative has their own sacred duty. 07 is responsible for integrating research resources, advancing key technological development, and undertaking core projects vital to society.
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07: </color>BR-003 has been compromised. The Underground's threat persists. We must reverse our strategic disadvantage. Mania dimension technology is clearly the...
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-03:</color><size=42> 07's responsibility is to advance scientific development and accomplish the assigned tasks.</size>
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-03: </color><size=42>You are not responsible for determining which projects deserve more progress and which do not. That duty belongs to other members.</size>

<color=#fb9259>EDGE-03: </color><size=42>Your job is to participate in discussions, accept the decisions, and execute them faithfully. But lately, you've been far too impulsive. You've overstepped your bounds repeatedly.</size>

EDGE-07: Who made these complaints? 06 never speaks up. 08 is still new, and often misses these meetings while away. You don't want her too involved anyway. EDGE-07: That leaves us with Nirvana, the Council... and you, am I right? EDGE-03: You know I'm not allowed to disclose that. EDGE-07: You don't need to tell me. I can work it out myself. In this so-called qualification review process, three of the seven seats have aligned against me. You plan to sway those two abstentions to guarantee the outcome. EDGE-07: But I still have an ongoing collaboration with SHP-13, and it's entering a critical phase. That... EDGE-03: I certainly hope you're not invoking that connection to put pressure on me. EDGE members must be wary of conflicts of interest, particularly where he is concerned. EDGE-07: That wasn't my point. Let me restate my point bearing in mind the rationality and responsibility expected of me as 07.
female_content: EDGE-07: Who made these complaints? 06 never speaks up. 08 is still new, and often misses these meetings while away. You don't want her too involved anyway. EDGE-07: That leaves us with Nirvana, the Council... and you, am I right? EDGE-03: You know I'm not allowed to disclose that. EDGE-07: You don't need to tell me. I can work it out myself. In this so-called qualification review process, three of the seven seats have aligned against me. You plan to sway those two abstentions to guarantee the outcome. EDGE-07: But I still have an ongoing collaboration with SHP-13, and it's entering a critical phase. That... EDGE-03: I certainly hope you're not invoking that connection to put pressure on me. EDGE members must be wary of conflicts of interest, particularly where she is concerned. EDGE-07: That wasn't my point. Let me restate my point bearing in mind the rationality and responsibility expected of me as 07.

content:
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07: </color>SHP-13's proposal was formally approved and authorized for execution at the last EDGE meeting. That means <size=42>you acknowledged the importance of his proposal</size>, and you agreed that <size=42>BR-003's security</size>, as well as <size=42>the tracking of and counterattack on the Underground</size> are the top priorities.
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07: </color>That being the case, we must close the technological gap between the Underground and us in dimensional Mania applications, and locate their hideout before they move again. I've been leading this project for three years. Objectively speaking, I am its core.
female_content:
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07: </color>SHP-13's proposal was formally approved and authorized for execution at the last EDGE meeting. That means <size=42>you acknowledged the importance of her proposal</size>, and you agreed that <size=42>BR-003's security</size>, as well as <size=42>the tracking of and counterattack on the Underground</size> are the top priorities.
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07: </color>That being the case, we must close the technological gap between the Underground and us in dimensional Mania applications, and locate their hideout before they move again. I've been leading this project for three years. Objectively speaking, I am its core.

content:
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07: </color>You're replacing the core personnel at the most critical phase of this project while a major conflict is looming. EDGE's research function will inevitably be disrupted. Can you bear the consequences?
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-03: </color>Regarding that, the members have conducted a thorough professional assessment. A replacement is ready to take over. There will be no issues.
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07: </color><size=60>And who exactly conducted this assessment?</size>

<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07: </color>A vote of no confidence against me can be done by all representatives except myself. That is true. But you're assessing if I have the right qualifications to take on a scientific position at EDGE...
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07: </color>And you're telling me the opinions of scientists don't matter? You're letting three laymen make the final call?
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07: </color><size=60>Did you consult with 01 and 02?!</size>
A silence.

<color=#fb9259>EDGE-03: </color>You're right. The opinions of 01 and 02 are extremely important.
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-03: </color>EDGE-01 is currently engaged in another mission. He's determined that he lacks the bandwidth to properly assess other matters. He has thus responsibly declared his abstention in advance.
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07: </color>What?! You...
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-03: </color>EDGE-02 will exercise his voting right on his behalf. As for EDGE-02...
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-03: </color>On this matter, your mentor has cast her vote in favor. She also provided us with the key technical justification we needed.
The turbulence in her brainwaves disrupts the connection. A splitting headache makes Lemma lose her focus, and she can barely stay connected to the channel.

<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07: </color>She... said that?
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07: </color>What about the evaluation report... and the documents I submitted... What exactly did she say? What did I... fail to do...
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-07: </color>Let me see it. Why...

<color=#fb9259>EDGE-03: </color>Don't worry. She cares little about those documents I shared with you previously. 02 never invests her energy in such administrative matters.
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-03: </color>Those are simply the reasons we've compiled for official purposes, and ones we hope you'll accept. It would be in all parties' best interests that you accept this explanation.
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-03:</color> Your gift of ██ is unparalleled, and you've always taken pride in it... So in the end, emotionally speaking, ██... this is the best way to handle it.
<i>Wait, this isn't right...

<color=#fb9259>EDGE-03: </color>The real reason 02 provided is actually far simpler. However, ██...
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-03: </color>That is information beyond your current clearance level.
<i>...Wait... I still...
<color=#fb9259>EDGE-03: </color>Goodbye, Lemma Herzfeld. Thank you for your contributions during your three years of service.
[System Update] EDGE-07 channel authentication terminated. Permissions revoked. Effective immediately. [Unauthorized Channel]: Wait... Ahh!!

Her permissions are taken, and the connection is severed abruptly. Lemma's consciousness is expelled, her vision violently snapping back to the control room. The emotional impact compounds with the reaction from the neural link, sending a wave of vertigo through her. She staggers, on the verge of collapsing to the floor.

speaker: Summer
content: Pink flash!

Someone quickly darts to Lemma's side, catching her. The sudden movement triggers Hush's built-in reaction, and several soldiers begin moving. But almost simultaneously, electrical currents rush through the alarm chips in their skulls. The Hush soldiers quickly realize...

A drone hovers behind each of their heads. Several meters away, Summer supports Lemma with one arm while her other hand works a projection keyboard, her eyes locked on every artificial soldier. Her expression is darker than ever.

speaker: Summer
content: You brainless pieces of scrap... Nobody move, or I'll blow everything above your necks off.

speaker: Summer
content: Not everyone here works for the Ring Research Institute. I'm an MBCC-registered Sinner. You wanna mess with a genius like me? You gotta ask ${PlayerName} first.

The Hush soldiers stop. Before them stands an S-Class Sinner who once single-handedly crippled the Laboratory of Parma. Moreover, she's a prized talent the Ring Research Institute has been trying to recruit. The units receive a new order that forbids them from escalating the conflict.
And the person issuing that command is drifting closer, in the form of a black bipyramid. It descends slightly before the two girls, rotating leisurely and behaving strangely amiably.

speaker: Schorl
content: Of course, we still wish to continue with our research on Mania's effects on a person's intelligence, and you're an exceptional and valuable subject. EDGE cherishes its good relationship with Chief ${PlayerName}, and we both respect each other's roles and jurisdictions.

speaker: Schorl
content: But I take it that you don't care about any of that right now. You just want to throw a tantrum, don't you?

speaker: Schorl
content: And you're certainly capable of that. When a true genius sets their mind to something big, the consequences often exceed what ordinary brains can fathom and withstand.

speaker: Schorl
content: Planning to surprise ${PlayerName} when he's not watching? <color=#fb9259>Like when you raised hell at the Ring Research Institute five years ago</color>? Back then, your parents' reactions were rather entertaining.
female_content: Planning to surprise ${PlayerName} when she's not watching? <color=#fb9259>Like when you raised hell at the Ring Research Institute five years ago</color>? Back then, your parents' reactions were rather entertaining.

content: Summer is speechless, mouth agape. Her extraordinary mind has just connected the dots. Something isn't right about this black bipyramid.

speaker: Schorl
content: Alright, then let's wait for ${PlayerName} to return. You trust his judgment, don't you? We won't do anything to harm your friend either. Lemma is a valuable asset. Let me speak with her. She needs me.
female_content: Alright, then let's wait for ${PlayerName} to return. You trust her judgment, don't you? We won't do anything to harm your friend either. Lemma is a valuable asset. Let me speak with her. She needs me.

speaker: Schorl
content: I must be tactful about certain things, but once I offer my explanation, I'm sure she'll understand.

Lemma still hasn't recovered from the shock. The black bipyramid observes for a moment, then, slowly and gently, lowers itself and connects to Keylan-II, now stripped of eighty percent of its functions.

speaker: Schorl
content: Poor child. The sudden severance just now has left you disoriented, I see. Now then, think back for a moment. Five years ago, based on your achievements, qualifications, data, and behavioral assessments, you and Summer were both selected as candidates for EDGE-07.

speaker: Schorl
content: Do you know why we chose you in the end?

speaker: Lemma
content: Because Summer... is a Sinner... because she was contaminated by Mania?

speaker: Schorl
content: Indeed. Her cognition was disrupted by Mania, rendering it sometimes unpredictable and chaotic. You, by contrast, have a perfectly logical mind and well-defined methodologies. You excelled at summarizing knowledge and sharing it. Your teamwork skills were also outstanding. Therefore, we determined...

speaker: Schorl
content: Your experience could be effectively summarized, studied, and replicated. And we've been proven right.

speaker: Schorl
content: You were the "genius" who best suited our needs, the perfect choice for EDGE-07.
Lemma's eyes widen. Her brainwaves are still erratic. Her consciousness is drifting, and her senses are blurry.
What happens after that?

The sealed doors of the control room burst open. Someone rushes in, shouting something. The Hush soldiers seem hesitant. Lemma's frightened colleagues cry as they gather around the intruder. Perhaps they're safe now.
But Lemma can hear none of the comforting words, can make out none of the faces.
The only thing she can see clearly is the hovering black bipyramid. It finishes what it needs to say, then rises back to its original position.

speaker: Schorl
content: Look. The next EDGE-07 candidate has arrived. She has worked hard and achieved outstanding results. She deserves recognition. Until EDGE officially retrieves all data, she will assume temporary control of the Observation Hub.

speaker: Schorl
content: Our strategy remains unchanged. No matter who EDGE chooses to be in charge, protecting BR-003, advancing the technology, and tackling the Underground will always be our top priorities.

speaker: Schorl
content: We are about to face an enormous challenge. Before humanity's true enemy arrives, we must make thorough preparations to ensure a seamless transition of operations under all circumstances. Now, initiate the authority transfer procedures.
Is she imagining it? Through Schorl's pristine, flawless surface, Lemma seems to glimpse another face, one that belongs to someone familiar, someone she admires and misses.

speaker: Schorl
content: Come say your goodbyes, Lemma.
Finally, Isomer claims the position of Chief Scientist. With all authority gathered in her hands, her takeover of the Observation Hub is complete.
The once-lively control room is now empty.
The lights are off. In the darkness, the comms device suddenly lights up, the brightness blindingly harsh. It's that encrypted channel again.

<color=#fb9259>[Data Encrypted]</color>: Has the handover been completed? We still have time, but she wants you back on the experiments as soon as possible. The old project is still valuable and should not be delayed.
<color=#fb9259>[Data Encrypted]</color>: A new batch of researchers will arrive shortly. I trust you to make effective use of them.

<color=#A5E3FB>[Reply]</color>: I will. But we're short-handed. I need to keep my current team.
<color=#fb9259>[Data Encrypted]</color>: There will be plenty of new ones for you to choose from.

<color=#A5E3FB>[Reply]</color>: I prefer the ones I'm already used to using.
<color=#A5E3FB>[Reply]</color>: We already succeeded in undermining her. There's no need to worry about her getting carried away over the project's success. The moment we shattered the pride of that "genius," we broke her.
<color=#A5E3FB>[Reply]</color>: I need the best minds to shorten the transition.
<color=#fb9259>[Data Encrypted]:</color><color=#3370FF>...Think carefully about what truly counts as an achievement, Isomer. Don't make the same mistake.</color>
After a long moment of silence, the other side finally continues.

<color=#fb9259>[Data Encrypted]</color>: Remember the timeline. It won't be long. The critical item has yet to be verified. We've entrusted the final phase to you, and we await your feedback... This is crucial.

<color=#fb9259>[Data Encrypted]</color>: Use your rational judgment, Isomer. If you do a good job, she promises to nominate you for the seat.
[Back to Scene]
The messages stop, and all records are automatically destroyed. Isomer clutches the device, her grip tightening. Before she loses control...
Fortunately, another notification tone grabs her attention.

Multiple surveillance cameras line the corridors leading here, and every feed shows the same image: a gray figure forcing their way through layers of guards and checkpoints almost violently, and then...
Bang! A crash against the door. Alarms blare, followed by the beeps of electronic locks being breached. The control room door swings open, and the visitor appears before Isomer.
[Chief's portrait]
Seeing his furious expression, something inside Isomer eases unexpectedly. She smiles.
female_content: Seeing her furious expression, something inside Isomer eases unexpectedly. She smiles.

speaker: Isomer
content: Hello there, Chief. You're late.

You fix her with a piercing glare. The woman remains every bit as cold and composed as she was the first time you met. What infuriates you even more is that she has achieved exactly what she set out to do. Now she wears a smug expression, as though she's about to invite you to share the spoils of her victory.
And you're no longer a collaborator in her scheme. She defeated you. You've lost your true companions, and you're consumed with anger.

You force your way into the control room. Behind you, voices shout, and people try to stop you. Without looking back, you slap the door controls and lock them all outside. Then you face Isomer directly.

speaker: Flawed Schorl
content: Chief, calm down. The current situation is...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: "Security" concerns?! Quit joking!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The Mania frequency spectrum from that chaos cube matches that of the Underground's. If there really is a mole within the Observation Hub, then the prime suspect is Isomer.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You received my report. Yet instead of investigating the real suspect, you replaced the entire core team?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Where is <size=45><color=#fb9259>Lemma</color>?! Is she alone?! Did you lock her up?!</size>
Schorl tries to explain, but the person being questioned speaks first.

speaker: Isomer
content: I knew it. You were the one who submitted that evidence against me. You had Summer keep tabs on me, testing me. I must admit, she did well.

speaker: Isomer
content: Just by staying close to me, she managed to gather that much information. That girl is indeed a genius. Who knows how she pulled it off.

speaker: Isomer
content: And you're good at putting geniuses to work, Chief. I thought I was careful enough around you, yet you still managed to blindside me. What a pain in the neck.
Cold, morose, and arrogant. The sight of her makes you sick.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If those documents had been worth anything, you never would've walked away unscathed!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Do you have Undergrounders inside EDGE pulling strings for you too? Or does humanity's highest council actually favor ruthless opportunists like you?
She sits in silence, studying your fury. For a long moment, she simply watches. Then, slowly, very slowly, she smiles.

speaker: Isomer
content: ...Look at you. Right now, you remind me of Lambert, Laplace, and so many others. Every one of those brilliant minds wore that same frustrated look when I defeated them. It's almost pitiful.

speaker: Isomer
content: This anger will get you nothing. And all this just for some kids? Chief, even at this juncture, you're still looking out for others... It only makes you look more foolish.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Isomer!!
The unrestrained rage is futile yet delicious. It tears open just enough breathing room in this suffocating space. The angrier ${PlayerName} becomes, the stronger Isomer's twisted pleasure grows.
Let's give him a treat.
female_content: Let's give her a treat.

speaker: Isomer
content: I didn't do anything. Those geniuses were discarded by those who <color=#fb9259>used</color> them.
She stares at her accuser, a cruel smile curling at the corner of her mouth.

speaker: Isomer
content: To conquer the unknown for humanity, they were fashioned into perfect tools. They possess neither common sense nor conventional ways of thinking. They see nothing but truth and knowledge. They're so brilliant, and arrogant. And naturally, they fail to see what their patrons truly wanted from them.

speaker: Isomer
content: Nirvana kept BR-003 for the Hypercubes. The council and the city backed her because they wanted stronger catastrophe weapons. All the resources, funding, time, and political capital poured into that project... and look what she did with it in the end.

speaker: Isomer
content: Dimension? What even is that? What about practical applications? The return on investment? Heh. And she still had the nerve to act all superior... Once they're out of the lab, these so-called <color=#fb9259>geniuses</color> are no better than fools. She was finally about to give in... and then you went and gave her another push.

speaker: Isomer
content: Oh, Chief... You're too good at giving pep talks.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Stop twisting the facts! As a scientist, she dedicated herself to her research. As an EDGE representative, she always chose the path that would serve humanity's fight against Mania.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Lemma never once failed to perform her duty. Those corrupt bastards conspired against her. They didn't even bother coming up with some "rational" or "scientific" justification. They simply tore her down with their dirty tricks. This isn't over yet. But that's not why I came here.

speaker: Isomer
content: Heh. Then why are you here? To congratulate me?

speaker: Isomer
content: You never thought I deserved this position. You think cunning, ambitious strategists are inferior to those brilliant, idealistic geniuses.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Stop putting words in my mouth. I never said that, and neither did Lemma!
You step forward and slam both hands on the desk, leaning in to glare at Isomer.

speaker: Option
options: She's always seen you as a genius!

speaker: Lemma
content: I'm extremely selective when it comes to my team. I've read every single paper she's published. From her days in academia, to her work on the Black Ring project, to the years she spent leading her own research team as a professor... That woman was once a remarkable <color=#fb9259>scholar</color>.

speaker: Lemma
content: She's well-rounded, objective, rigorous, and imaginative. She had a particular talent for synthesizing theories, integrating dissimilar ideas, and identifying new avenues for breakthroughs. Her experimental work was impeccable as well. Isomer's accomplishments are truly outstanding. Otherwise, 02 would never have handpicked her.

speaker: Lemma
content: ...I was impressed by those papers. The author was clearly intelligent, passionate, and committed to her work. That's the most valuable type of researcher. If only that old fool Lambert hadn't held her back for so many years...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You were an exception in the Black Ring project. The elite there looked down on your ordinary background. They exploited your talent, but they also feared it. They used every trick to undermine you. You never had a chance to rise.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Finally, in N.F. 104, Nirvana took the Super-Loop Communication system you'd improved to create the Inner Bay mining disaster. Then, a Black Ring erupted unexpectedly, and once again, you became the scapegoat.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: After that, you were placed on leave and underwent treatment, removed from all frontline work. For nine years, you produced nothing. Tell me, Isomer... how much of that was because they pushed you aside? And how much was because you couldn't bear knowing the technology you had created to make the world safer had been used to kill?

speaker: Lemma
content: What was she thinking? If she realized she'd gone down the wrong path, she could have changed course. If people were misusing her research, she should have fought them for it. Didn't she become the Director? Which means she has more power than ever. She could've done so much more, gone so much further.

speaker: Lemma
content: But is that position cursed or something? Does it corrupt everyone who takes it? Her research has stagnated, and all she cares about now is petty politics. She even had the nerve to tell me that it's because "she's not as talented as we are." What a ridiculous excuse!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: To Lemma, talent is never a competition. She's never felt inferior to Summer, nor has she ever looked down on you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: She sees all of you as scholars making contributions to humanity. She believes all talent should be directed where it's most needed.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: She's always hoped you could come back to your role as a researcher, back to that path reserved for a true scientist!
Isomer closes her eyes, but the memories still stir.

speaker: Lemma
content: I don't care how you treat me. That's irrelevant to science, to humanity. But take a good look at yourself. What have you become? You're even more pathetic than that idiot Summer!

speaker: Lemma
content: A genius's mind should be devoted to the pursuit of truth and knowledge. It's a gift to all humanity! And look what you've wasted yours on?!
...It's still so suffocating.

speaker: Isomer
content: Me? A fellow genius? No... The gap between people like us and true geniuses is far greater than you can imagine.

speaker: Isomer
content: ...But none of that matters anymore.
Isomer looks up. Schorl is here. No matter how their form or attitude changes, these devices serve only EDGE—only a "certain representative." She knows this.
But here, now, none of that matters anymore. Isomer speaks.

speaker: Isomer
content: Regarding the replacement of EDGE-07, security risks and cooperation issues were certainly factors. But they accounted for less than thirty percent of the decision.

speaker: Isomer
content: The real reason is the self-reformation of the <color=#fb9259>genius</color> system.
She looks at you. The turbulent emotions from before seem to have faded completely, her voice tepid as still water.

speaker: Isomer
content: Objectively speaking, <color=#fb9259>geniuses</color> are merely superior specimens within humanity. They are efficient decision-making units society requires. The exceptions our civilization relies on to solve all unknowns. But their traits aren't dominant enough. They're rare, and the screening and nurturing of these individuals are extremely difficult.

speaker: Isomer
content: Traditional society glorified science and encouraged generations of people to enter the funnel. The education system then sifted them through layer after layer of selection, directing resources toward those deemed most promising. And after all that? It produced only a handful of "geniuses." The results were inconsistent, resources were misallocated, and the overall efficiency was abysmal.

speaker: Isomer
content: And now, that system has decayed even further. Academia no longer cultivates talent. It's become breeding grounds for corruption. Society no longer values knowledge. Money and fame are what people are after now.

speaker: Isomer
content: Look at the world outside. The disasters keep escalating, city-states grow more competitive with each other, and civilization's demand for "geniuses" only climbs higher. EDGE is desperately looking for a more efficient way to secure that resource. And that's when the <color=#fb9259>most brilliant scientist</color> stepped in...

speaker: Abhorrent Memory
content: Genius worship is nothing more than a romanticized notion born of scarcity. Much like the way financial markets chase high-performance chips. Though I suppose such mystification could be a rational adaptation for a society still in its earlier stages of development...

speaker: Abhorrent Memory
content: But we do need to tackle the scarcity issue. Hmm... We can't optimize every stage of the pipeline just yet, but perhaps we can expand the base pool through other means, and create a more refined environment, where we can improve the efficiency of the screening and cultivation cycle.

speaker: Isomer
content: That genius found a way to manufacture geniuses. She studied Mania's effects on consciousness and leveraged the authority of her position. She was able to screen for high-intelligence individuals who met her criteria on a far larger scale, and through far more rational and stable means.

Heterogeneous Trial 0.1: Initial screening of all newborns based on adaptability and basic traits. Scope: Centered around Banyan Medical College Hospital, covering Eastside, West District, and DisCity's satellite towns. 0.1.4: Sampling groups expanded to include ages 4, 8, and 12. Preliminary assessment: Newborn screening still yields the highest pass rate across all sampling groups. 0.2.1: Current test metrics focus on intelligence, environmental adaptability, physical capacity, and Mania tolerance. Additional metric added: behavioral compliance assessment. 0.3.4: Exceptional candidates approved through final review will be permitted direct entry to Paradeisos. Special files will be created for unselected final review candidates to facilitate long-term monitoring and follow-up. If they pass subsequent tests, they may still be chosen for the cultivation program.
[Insert: Memory of children idolizing their heroes][Small idol CG]

speaker: Isomer
content: The critical window is puberty, when the specimens are highly malleable, passionate, impulsive, and impressionable. More importantly, the new model allows for effective control of the cultivation cycle. The costs of screening, maintenance, and replacement can all be greatly reduced.

speaker: Abhorrent Memory
content: We're currently in a transitional phase, so some degree of socialization needs to be preserved in them. I suggest assigning "families" to the earlier batches. My thanks in advance to all departments for their cooperation.

speaker: Abhorrent Memory
content: That Sinner named Summer has greatly inspired me as well. Heh... Shall we pursue a new experiment in the future?

speaker: Isomer
content: Yes, if this batch fails to meet our expectations, it can simply be replaced. It'll also be a good opportunity to reassess the handover process. There's no need to trouble ourselves over it.

speaker: Abhorrent Memory
content: This is a tremendous scientific breakthrough. Once the process is proven viable, talent will no longer be in shortage. It will become a stable, replaceable, high-quality resource that can be rationally allocated. Humanity should celebrate this achievement.
In the pitch-black room, darkness is strangling every throat, mocking the anger of those who still dare to hope.

speaker: Isomer
content: They were never seen as treasures to begin with, Chief.

You stand speechless, frozen to the core. That girl who takes such pride in her gift. The scholar who swore to live up to the "genius" title. That child who works so hard to catch up to those who came before her... Somewhere beyond your sight, at this very moment, someone has just given her a careless push...
...Shattering her completely. A star shining so brightly, yet made of something so deeply fragile.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Lemma. She doesn't know yet, does she?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: After you've learned about all this... how do you feel about those children now?
<i>How does she feel?
The question catches Isomer off guard.

speaker: Abhorrent Memory
content: So, how do you feel now, Isomer? The word "talent" has always made you feel inferior and inadequate.

speaker: EDGE-02 & Isomer
content:
Are you finally relieved?
...I feel relieved.
At last, she lets out a long-held breath.

speaker: Isomer
content: I'll answer one more question for you, Chief. You and I do share a special connection.

speaker: Isomer
content: The BR-002 eruption in N.F. 104 dealt me a devastating blow. I was demoted and expelled from frontline work. For a long time afterward, I couldn't face my research again. My thoughts were clouded by regret and anxiety.

speaker: Isomer
content: So, nine years later, when the remaining half of the Corpus returned to Drifter Camp, and the Black Ring's shadow loomed once more... it felt like fate. My mind cleared up again. Yet my first thought was no longer how to fight the disaster or save lives. I worked tirelessly designing the defense zone, but it was not out of any noble ideal.

speaker: Isomer
content: The moment the secondary eruption of the West District Black Ring happened... I felt no grief, only relief... joy, even. I thought, now they'd all see how wrong Lambert had been. I could climb higher over his dead body. I...

speaker: Isomer
content: Would become the next <color=#fb9259>Director</color>...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You...
You need to say something. But what? Your mind has gone blank.
She catches the struggle written across your face. She smiles faintly and spares you the trouble.

speaker: Isomer
content: So, you shouldn't feel torn, Chief. You don't need to trust me. Even if I weren't serving the Sillage Society, you and I could never walk the same path again.
Isomer rises to her feet.

speaker: Isomer
content: The report you filed against me wasn't ignored. EDGE reviewed it carefully. They investigated me thoroughly, fairly, and without bias.
The control room door opens. She puts on her coat and walks out.

speaker: Isomer
content: I'm not the spy who sabotaged the Hub. I would never have left behind such obvious traces that could destroy my career.
All the dark, chaotic emotions are sealed away once more, locked into that cold, rigid cube in her hand.

speaker: Isomer
content: But I do have one more piece of information for you. <color=#fb9259>The Sillage Society</color> that you're investigating... might be closer than you think.
She stops before you and offers one last quiet remark.

speaker: Isomer
content: Think about it. Someone who has climbed to the top as I have, who holds that much information, who has the means to help you come after me... Do you really think a person like that can keep their hands clean?
[Celine's portrait flashes on screen]
You snap back to awareness and reach out to stop her.
The moment passes. The people waiting outside flood into the room, and any chance for further conversation vanishes.
At the same time, your comms device vibrates. Another shocking post has just appeared on that academic exposé forum you've been monitoring. A single glance at the headline leaves you stunned.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This is...?!

speaker: Isomer
content: Heh... You'd better hurry back. Don't let outsiders get hold of the evidence first and drag you down with it. Find out who the mole is, the one who let the Underground into the Black Ring. I'll continue helping you best I can.

speaker: Isomer
content: After all, this is my Hub now. And going forward, I'll need it to secure my place in EDGE, to "<color=#fb9259>fight for humanity</color>."

The door of the dark chamber is suddenly smashed open. The sheriff bursts in and shouts with his gun raised.

speaker: Sheriff
content: Hands up! Ugh! Cough, cough! ...What kind of hellhole is this?

The room is barely thirty square meters in size, yet it is crammed with computers stacked three meters high, forming a crooked, makeshift wall. None are powered on. Pitch-black screens stare like hollow eyes at the intruder. The whole mass resembles some grotesque creature, reeking of old plastic and corroded metal.
The sheriff waves away the dust swirling before him and tiptoes toward one of the strange computers. A few quick keystrokes, and a lengthy list instantly pops up on the screen.

Countless commissions for ghostwritten papers, forged experimental data, and leaked exam questions, spanning every academic discipline. Worse still, the client list runs for several pages, each name paired with matching transaction records. A clear, damning ledger of academic fraud involving dozens, if not hundreds, of elite students.

This is precisely the "criminal evidence" he came for. After confirming several untouchable surnames are indeed on the list, the sheriff deletes them with trembling hands. His real mission finally complete, he breathes a sigh of relief.

speaker: Sheriff
content: ...To think that even United University has been tainted by vermin like this. Yeah, these lowlifes never should have been given any opportunities. A stain on academia will sooner or later become a threat to society...

speaker: Sheriff
content: Who's there?! You...!
He whips the gun around. In the shadows, there is nothing but the stack of decrepit, second-hand monitors. No one...?
No, something's wrong! The sheriff shudders. He clearly sees one of those square "monitors" begin to tremble. It's... giggling.

speaker: Pixel
content: Hehe, you caught me... hehehehe...

speaker: Sheriff
content: Tsk... What a freak... Knew it was some crazy kid.

speaker: Sheriff
content: Hands up! You're charged with spreading rumors, defamation, inciting public panic, and undermining the sacred education system of DisCity! You're under arrest! Do not resist!
The computer head laughs even harder.

speaker: Pixel
content: Me? Crazy? Rumors? Defamation? And... undermining the sacred... education system of DisCity? ...Are you sure?
Her screen flickers violently, grotesque "facial" expressions flashing across it quickly. Pixel's body begins writhing as she shrieks with laughter.

speaker: Pixel
content: Who's the crazy one here? The people faking research? The ones profiting from predatory student loans? The scammers exploiting science for money? And what about those who wrap themselves in academic authority while inventing new ways to kill and bury the truth? Aren't they crazier than I am?

speaker: Pixel
content: No one is really that crazy! They're all PERFECTLY NORMAL!!! And a humble ghostwriter like me is just doing my part for DisCity's sacred education system!

Her laughter erupts into a piercing screech. The sheriff's body jerks, and he fires. Several bullets strike Pixel. One shatters the upper-right corner of the monitor screen, and it goes black. Her laugh stops, and her dance freezes. Her entire body becomes as still as a statue.
Then, the statue melts rapidly, forming a shapeless, glue-like puddle on the floor. This isn't a human. It's just a... a 3D-printed monster? A Sinner!

But there's no time to report it. From outside, through the door gap, the poor sheriff hears some rustling noise. Numerous shadows slip into the room. Drawn by the commotion, they've stumbled upon a decent snack.

speaker: Sheriff
content: What the...! What did you do?! You... Don't come any closer... No... AHHH!!!

What follows is like a scene taken out of a clichéd splatter horror film. One after another, the monitors are smashed to pieces, and new screens flicker to life in their place. Finally, Pixel's face fills the entire room. Her fluorescent gaze bathes everything in cold light.

Every computer head in the room erupts in laughter, applauding the madness, celebrating the filth. Betray and be betrayed! This magnificent spectacle deserves nothing less than the highest performance art award!

speaker: Pixel
content: Hahahaha! Let the false brilliance explode! Let the rotten reason collapse! Meet your fall, all of you!!!

speaker: Pixel
content: The sacred halls of academia? The pale blue firmament? It's all so filthy! Every last one of you is rotten to the core!
Late at night, at the Central Library.

A car pulls up quietly at the entrance. A woman steps out and passes the security scan. The door opens. Alone, she climbs the white stone steps, enters the silent corridors, and makes her way deep inside, toward that familiar window.
Celine has just returned from a private banquet in Paradeisos. She's on the phone with someone.

speaker: Celine
content: You're giving me too much credit. My words certainly don't wield that kind of influence. It's all simply the natural course of the times.

speaker: Celine
content: Yes, that's right. And thank you for your support as well. I still have some work to wrap up here. We'll be in touch.
Finally, it's over. Celine retrieves her book, picks up her pen, and prepares to record the day's findings. Just then... she senses something unfamiliar.
In the silence of the night, she is not alone in the library.
She smiles faintly, tidies her things, and settles into her seat.

speaker: Celine
content: "I can sense it through the shackles." ...Come on out, Chief. Come sit with me.

speaker: Celine
content: You came here alone at this hour. It must be something quite important, I imagine.
She says her greeting toward the shadowy corner.
So you come out, stopping roughly seven steps in front of her.

options: Someone suspects you're a spy sent to infiltrate BR-003.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You had two lines of contact. You reached out to Lemma early on, and later, to me. Combined with the exceptionally high clearance you already held, if that really was your plan, you certainly had the means to carry it out.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So I reported it.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But the investigation ruled out that possibility. Someone higher up vouched for you. The evidence that person provided was apparently more convincing. It proved... you weren't working for the Underground.
The sound of flowing water dissolves the icy air. The atmosphere seems to ease up a little.
Yet the visitor's face is still hidden in the shadows.
You toss several books onto the long desk between you. They slide across the polished surface. Three hardcovers and one printed manuscript.

The light is dim, but Celine sees it clearly. A book series titled: <color=#fb9259>Rust and Blood: Tracing the Origins of the Syndicate Riots</color>. The cover image is set against a ruin near the Rust. A mobster grips a Mania weapon, bloodshot eyes staring viciously into the camera. The hatred and madness feel almost visceral, jarring.

Even more jarring is the weighty author byline:
<color=#fb9259>United Humanities Society</color>.
You stop beating around the bush.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: "I have a new book coming out, and it urgently needs proofreading." This is the book you were talking about?

speaker: Celine
content: I did compile it.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This book presents itself as an objective academic analysis, but every line is designed to persuade the reader of something. It deliberately magnifies Rustfire's violence while glossing over their hardships and determination.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It also cites a lot of sources to frame the mining disaster as an "unfortunate accident." It emphasizes Nirvana's apology, portraying the corporation as the innocent victim. And in the end, it points toward the resistance against the current mine development... What kind of conclusion are you trying to draw?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: A chronicler cannot possibly be ignorant of the truth. How could you write something like this?
She remains in her usual spot, leisurely flipping through those books while responding to your questions patiently, just like before.
...She won't even use the name "West District."

speaker: Celine
content: <color=#fb9259>Because people still need it.</color>

speaker: Celine
content: My research may not directly advance society the way Lemma's does, but my field has its own strengths.

speaker: Celine
content: News, commentary, literature, and even these historical writings of mine. They are all crafts in their own right. Our specialty lies in presenting ideas, shaping narratives through writing and multimedia, and ensuring they reach as many people as possible.
Her hand glides over that truth-distorting cover photo, tapping it twice approvingly.

speaker: Celine
content: See, truth isn't simply recorded and unearthed. It can also be subtly reshaped through our work, quietly remolding how people perceive the world. That's an ability modern society needs now more than ever.

speaker: Celine
content: That's precisely why, while the College of Humanities may not enjoy the spotlight the way the College of Science does, we still receive steady funding from a variety of sources. My sponsor likely entrusted this project to me because...

speaker: Celine
content: They found my writing rich in detail, emotionally compelling, and persuasive.
She smiles.

speaker: Celine
content: And I've cultivated quite a respectable reputation too. "Noble," "dignified," "dedicated to scholarship." I've always been careful not to leave traces that might tarnish that image... That makes readers far more inclined to "trust" me.

speaker: Celine
content: After all, my sponsor prefers to keep this deal discreet.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The whistleblower who exposed all this had her account banned. Both the Public Security Bureau and the Underground raided her home. Were you aware of that?

speaker: Celine
content: I am aware now. Thank you for telling me.

speaker: Celine
content: That student has a really unique perspective. I check her site often, and I've always worried about her. Getting that deep into sensitive topics, and being so blunt about them—it's only a matter of time before she catches attention. From a lot of people.

speaker: Celine
content: No need. Not worth it. And don't worry. Pixel's been through this before. She knows who's behind it, and she'll get out of it.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You seem to know your sponsor quite well. You must have worked with them far longer, and far more closely, than you ever did with me. Do tell me more, then.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Out of the four latest Black Ring ruin incidents, the BR-002 mine was hit the hardest, with an ever-growing casualty count. The Underground had no motive to do this. It served none of their core interests. But damage to Rustfire does benefit another group...

options: What's the connection between your sponsor and the Sillage Society?

speaker: Celine
content: I can't disclose that. For now, I still need their "trust."
<color=#fb9259>"Trust"</color>?
The word, spoken aloud, feels laughable. You yourself are laughable too, perhaps.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You once said...

speaker: Celine
content: But for me, the greatest reward was crossing that divide between East and West. Walking down streets I'd only ever seen in photographs. Meeting the people who actually live there. At first, they were wary of a "Paradeisos scholar" like me, and curious, too. But by the end of each conversation... every one of them shook my hand.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You knew the truth wasn't like what you wrote in your book. You went there yourself. You met the people. You saw with your own eyes how much they sacrificed for that mine. You experienced it firsthand.

speaker: Celine
content: Words, in the end, can only hold fragments. The real history has settled into every brick and stone of West District, into the people whose lives are woven into that place. When they opened their hearts to me... that's when I truly saw the marks time had left behind. And the light still shining through them, too...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And what about their trust? Did it mean so little to you that you could simply throw it away?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Did you get me to connect you with West District so you could keep working on this pack of lies you call your "book"?
Some questions answer themselves the moment you ask them. Whatever she says no longer matters.
Yet she still meets your eyes, still smiling, and answers anyway.

speaker: Celine
content: Yes, thank you for setting that up.

speaker: Celine
content: I had to gather rich, authentic details, which I could then filter, refine, and reassemble. That's how I instill "credibility" in my works.
A deathly silence fills the library. Only the high-mounted clocks' pendulums tick in the stillness. Now, in the quiet of the night, you finally hear it...
The clocks are out of sync. Their chimes narrowly miss each other, the discordant sounds making you uneasy.
Celine watches you, the night melting into her deep blue eyes.

speaker: Celine
content: To climb the ladder of the system. To penetrate the deeper, hidden layers.

speaker: Celine
content: My pen bought me entry into their world.
She gently turns the pages in her hands.

speaker: Celine
content: Generations of chroniclers inherited the pages left behind by those before them. They did all they could to record history and the times they lived in, piecing together fragments of truth, then passing it forward. And to obtain this precious fruit, one must always pay a price.

speaker: Celine
content: And so my predecessors staked their wealth, reputation, information, and time... Some even wagered their freedom and lives. I've inherited many invaluable findings, but I've also witnessed a frustrating truth. Even after sacrificing so much, they never received the rewards they deserved.

speaker: Celine
content: Because they couldn't let go of their "conscience," Chief.

speaker: Celine
content: Truth isn't locked away in ivory towers, nor does it rest solely in virtuous hands. It's woven into every corner of society.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You once told me that one must see clearly what one wants in order to move forward. I understand what you want now, but Celine...

options: Isn't there a line you won't cross?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This entire series was written to pressure the mine workers into backing down. You're twisting their persistence into something else. You're not just recording history. You're tainting it.

speaker: Celine
content: An era shapes its chroniclers. To record the truth, you must breathe it.

speaker: Celine
content: So I traded away a few "principles" in exchange for some admission tickets. The same way I borrowed your precious trust to gain entry into West District.

speaker: Celine
content: I've indeed gained a lot. I'll need some time to sort through it all.
She looks at you and smiles. The night, you realize, is cold.
Dazed, you find yourself with nothing left to say.
...One last question.

options: What about Linda? Does she know?

content: Celine's smile deepens.

speaker: Celine
content: She's my chosen successor. Sooner or later, she'll walk the same path.

speaker: Celine
content: Chief, our deal is still valid. Don't forget that.
She sets down the book, rises, and walks toward you.

speaker: Celine
content: The Sillage Society, and the Underground, right? The truth you're looking for may come to light very soon. So... will you wait for me just a little longer?
Celine Fabius stops before you and looks up with a smile. She's waiting, as if she's just posed a question to a "student," or daring an opponent to make the next move.
female_content: Celine Fabius stops before you with a smile, her eyes level with yours. She's waiting, as if she's just posed a question to a "student," or daring an opponent to make the next move.

content: You don't actually need to give her a response. She's most likely unrelated to the leak, and the two of you will probably never walk the same path again.
But... perhaps this moment is exactly why you came to meet her tonight.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Since the moment I decided to face the Black Rings head-on, I've had to rely on the help of the brightest minds. And there was a time when I truly needed all of you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Like many in this city, we believe in logic and reason—the fruits of our civilization. We also believe in those who have reached the pinnacle of rationality, who dedicate themselves to the pursuit of truth and knowledge.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Just as I believe humanity can overcome Mania, I want to... believe in all of you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Give me the true answer, Professor.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I want to understand why someone who would stop at nothing to achieve her goals, someone who claims to have cast aside her own "conscience," would still choose to face me with honesty.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The battle of BR-003 isn't over yet. I am accountable to the people I've made promises to, and I need to eliminate every risk. Until this all comes to an end, until you tell me the truth, I won't be telling you anything more.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But when this is all over...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: When that time comes, I'll be waiting for your answer, and that part of your "conscience" you haven't sold.
Celine stares at you intently. Slowly, her smile melts into something softer.

speaker: Celine
content: ...Thank you, Chief. That's exactly what I needed to hear. Let's talk more when you return.

speaker: Celine
content: Look at me. See right through me. I know you must be able to see it clearly.
