content: Quack, quack quack quack quack? Quack quack, quack quack quack quack. (Heh, playing hard to get? Foul humans, you shall not escape!)
Bureau Confinement Room

When you regain consciousness, you find your hands tied behind your back and yourself locked in the confinement room. There are no guards outside the door, but you can faintly hear the sounds of the duck patrolling in the distance.
The knots aren't secure. You break free from your restraints and take out your communication device, which already has its positioning activated.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Nightingale, can you hear me?

speaker: Nightingale
content: I can hear you clearly! I've already sealed off the area passages within the Bureau based on the message you had EMP bring back, and I can also track your location in real time. Chief, are you alright over there?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Don't worry, I'm fine. Have you figured out why the ducks launched this attack?

speaker: Nightingale
content: We tried negotiating with them, but they keep repeating something like "The world belongs to the ducks" and "All hail the return of the Duck King." Normal communication is impossible.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Moreover, based on the current intelligence we have, the enemy appears to have mastered some kind of technology for stealing Sinners' abilities. We currently can't completely rule out the risk of Mania contamination, so we can't act rashly.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It's right to be cautious. After all, we've never faced anything like this before. Taking more time to investigate and playing it safe is wise.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Before the incident, did the ducks come into contact with anything, or were there any abnormalities?

speaker: Nightingale
content: Surveillance shows that before they encountered EMP, they had been helping organize and repair some instant imaging equipment in the Depot.
You recall the recent battle with the Sovereign Duck. The cards it threw out each time when using its abilities closely resembled photo paper in both size and material.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If that equipment had been contaminated by Mania, then photos taken of Sinners might just produce the effect of copying their special powers.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Although this is still just a hypothesis, if it's true, we can avoid the risks of direct combat. As long as we slowly exhaust the ducks' photo papers, we'll be able to restrict their actions.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Understood. I'll dispatch Sinners to support you based on your movement route. Please make sure to stay safe.

speaker: EMP
content: Chief! The legendary Minos Goddess of War EMP is back to save you! Were you so scared you started crying earlier?

speaker: K.K.
content: Stop bragging already. Just now, I wonder who was hiding in the back.

speaker: EMP
content: I-I-I-I was doing ranged DPS... I rarely get to look cool, so don't call me out!

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, I'm detecting that you've successfully rendezvoused with two Sinners.
The duck squad here has fallen unconscious from your successful ambush. As you listen in on their communications, you rummage through their pockets—but to no avail.

speaker: Nightingale
content: For your safety, I'll plan the shortest route for you to escape the encirclement right now.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No need. The priority is to confiscate those dangerous items that enable the ducks to use Sinners' abilities.

speaker: Nightingale
content: But, Chief...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Just send me the locations of the nearby ducks for now.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Understood. I'll act according to your judgment.
After a fierce fight, the ducks' offense gradually fades. You rush to their retreat and find both used and unused photos left behind.

speaker: K.K.
content: So these are the weapons they use for attacks? They seem disposable. Each photo can only activate an ability once.

speaker: EMP
content: But seeing my signature move perfectly replicated by these ducks is still really weird! It's giving me some serious chills!

speaker: EMP
content: And why do they have so many photos of Sinners?! Look—There's tons of Chief too!

speaker: K.K.
content: Chief's photos aren't that surprising though, after all, they are in short supply in the...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Hm? What did you just say?

speaker: K.K.
content: Ahem... I mean, there are quite a few shortcuts in the Bureau. Wouldn't taking this path here save us some time?

speaker: EMP
content: Heh heh, easy-peasy, not even breaking a sweat.

speaker: K.K.
content: Looks like Chief was right. Once the ducks use up all these photos, they won't be able to use Sinners' special powers anymore.

speaker: EMP
content: Hey hey hey, don't jinx it! You never know if the final boss might pull out some cheat ability or ultimate attack!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Exactly. Don't let your guard down yet—their final line of defense is up ahead. Get ready before we move forward.
Though it took quite some time, by using coordinated tactics, you successfully subdued most of the ducks, and now you finally stand before the last enemy duck.

speaker: Sovereign Duck
content: Quack quack, quack quack quack quack, quack quack quack quack quack! (Finally, you have come! The ultimate battle between ducks and humans was inevitable!)

speaker: Sovereign Duck
content: Quack quack quack quack quack—quack quack quack quack quack quack! (I was reborn and returned here! After enduring countless hardships to reach this place, I declare to the Bureau—the Ducks will decide their own fate from now on!)

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Actually, I've been wanting to ask this for a while... EMP, what novels did you show them?

speaker: EMP
content: Ah, you know those novels with tons of tags and ridiculously long titles that go on forever? So it really is true—the longer the title, the stronger the power?
A quack of absolute fury interrupts your conversation. The duck facing you, seething with rage, pulls out its remaining photos and fans them out menacingly.

speaker: Sovereign Duck
content: Quack quack quack quack! Quack quack quack quack quack quack! (Don't underestimate us Ducks! I'll show you right now that heaven's mandate belongs to Ducks!!!)

speaker: Sovereign Duck
content: Quack quack quack quack, quack quack quack! (My turn, I play my cards!)

speaker: Sovereign Duck
content: Quack... Quack quack quack quack quack quack quack... (No... were all the things in the books really just lies...?)

After the situation was resolved, the Bureau conducted tests on the confiscated instant cameras and photos, confirming the presence of trace amounts of Mania elements in them. The ducks were already mentally unstable after working so much, and this became the final straw that pushed them over the edge.

speaker: Nightingale
content: We've already performed special cleaning on the problematic cameras and photos. However, during the final recovery and inventory, staff reported that far fewer photos were recovered than initially recorded—and the vast majority of the missing ones are yours, Chief...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Go ask K.K. —she might have some idea where the photos ended up.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Most importantly, we need to keep stepping up our Mania detection, and also make sure we're managing the ducks' workload properly. Plus, we can't let up on reviewing the content of the books we purchase.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I really didn't expect this incident would take up so much time. Looks like I'll have to miss those social obligations originally scheduled for this weekend.

Nightingale stands to the side, holding a stack of documents, watching you with something clearly on her mind but hesitating to speak. Her gaze makes you feel a bit guilty—you can't shake the feeling that your dear adjutant has seen right through your attempts to avoid work ever since the duck attack began.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Sor—

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, I'm letting this one slide, but it must never happen again. If you're ever faced with an unreasonable work schedule, do not put yourself in danger just to buy time.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Next time, please let me know first— I'll find a way to help you.
You walk along the beach, your sandals sinking into the fine sand with a soft rustling sound—a completely different experience from walking on WhiteSands.
The salty breeze fills your nostrils as you gaze into the distance at an ocean much like the one around Elysiland.
Of course, there's also... the smell of barbecue.

speaker: Boss
content: Squid, saury, mackerel! Fresh from the sea, hot off the grill!

speaker: Boss
content: One bite and you'll be back for more! Guaranteed fresh, or you get your money back tenfold!

Following the shouts, you spot a large wooden plank from a wrecked fishing boat with "Surf's Bounty" scrawled across it. Tables and stools of different sizes are scattered nearby. The boss and her staff are bustling around the grill, while off to the side stands... a bookkeeper.

speaker: Customer
content: One grilled eel for me, please.

speaker: Boss
content: Alrighty! Want it spicy?

speaker: Customer
content: Sure! The hotter the better.

speaker: Grill Master
content: Copy.
The grill master moves fast. She yanks an eel from a bucket, scrapes the scales off with a few casual flicks of her knife, and slaps it onto a salt-covered cutting board.

After rubbing it in salt for a few minutes, she flashes her blade, creating a clean cut around the gills. In one smooth motion, she peels off the skin and slime, a slick move that draws gasps from the watching diners.

speaker: Customer
content: ...Show-off. Gutting the eel is the tricky part.

speaker: Grill Master
content: We'll see about that.
The grill master doesn't miss a beat. She slits the belly, lifts the organs with her fingertips, and nudges them toward the head.
With three lightning-fast cuts, the innards are effortlessly removed, perfectly intact.

speaker: Customer
content: That's... impossible. I've cooked eel for ten years, never seen anyone do it like that...
It's so reckless. He knows how awful a burst gallbladder tastes, which is why he's spent years carefully scooping the innards out with a spoon.

While the man questions his career, the grill master is already pinning the fillet down. Her blade moves as if it has a mind of its own, sliding along the spine to sever bone from flesh without piercing the meat, deboning the entire thing in one go.
The man rubs his eyes. Surely he's seeing things. This isn't your average freshwater eel. It's a sea eel, far bonier and much more difficult to prepare.
He opens his mouth, but finds he has no words. The spine has been removed, but the fillet is flawless.

The grill master dusts off her hands and moves on to the final step. She slices the fillet, plucking the stray bones as she goes. A brush of sauce, a sizzle on the grill, and the rich aroma of fish fills the air.
The eel's tail is still twitching on the cutting board, while the knife has already been returned to its rack.

speaker: Grill Master
content: Enjoy.

speaker: Everyone
content: I'll have one too!
The crowd erupts, enthralled by her divine knifework and cooking.

speaker: Everyone
content: One for me as well!

speaker: Customer
content: Daddy, is that lady a magician?

speaker: Customer
content: Hahaha, she's no magician, sweetheart.

speaker: Customer
content: She's Daddy's teacher now.
More and more people are drawn in, the tide of bodies pushing you forward.

speaker: Boss
content: Hold it, hold it! One at a time! Our bookkeeper can't keep up with this many orders!

speaker: Bookkeeper
content: It doesn't matter. This volume doesn't even approach my processing limit.

Watching the endless line of customers and her two capable employees, the boss of the seaside barbecue place can't help but smirk to herself. Nothing beats sitting back and watching the money roll in.

speaker: Boss
content: Oops, sorry! We've just sold out of eel. How about something else? All our grilled fish is just as good!
She scratches the back of her head apologetically.

speaker: Boss
content: Who's this troublemaker? Haven't you heard of my...
The boss stomps toward you, grumbling under her breath. But the words die in her throat the moment you look up.

speaker: Bai Yi
content: Haven't you heard of my diligence, hard work, and generous nature? Never mind one eel, I can get you ten if you want!

speaker: Bai Yi
content: Hey, Jane! Come say hi to our Chief!
You turn toward the voice, just in time to see a smoke grenade fly through the air and bounce on the ground.

speaker: Bai Yi
content: Grab the cash and run!
Smoke bursts out, throwing the tourists into confusion. Seizing the opportunity, Bai Yi grabs Jane, the grill master, and makes a run for it.

speaker: Jane
content: Mission aborted. Preparing to evacuate.
Jane zip-ties herself to Bai Yi's back. Once she's secure, Bai Yi strikes a dramatic pose, ready to activate her ability. The bookkeeper stands motionless, silently watching the farce.

speaker: Bai Yi
content: Adios!
When Sinners get up to no good, you have DisCity's most effective disciplinary tool.
Red shackles materialize instantly. Bai Yi activates her ability, but she's a split second too slow. The shackles pin both of them to the ground.
Bai Yi is fast. If she hadn't wasted time showing off, she might have gotten away.

speaker: Bai Yi
content: I mean... ah, do you feel tired? Maybe you could just let me sit down? I promise I won't run this time.
Always looking for a way out.
(Scene change)
When L.L. left, Elysiland vanished with her, leaving the entire space an empty void.
However, after the Eastside government took over the area, the Elysiland Renewal Project was launched.
With the MBCC's help using dark web technology, Elysiland was rebuilt and reopened to the public.
Soon, the place was bustling with more life than ever before.
But at its core, Elysiland still exists on <color=#fb9259>Mania</color>.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, the M-Values in Elysiland are rising. Something is off.

speaker: Nightingale
content: The current theory is that the visitors' heightened emotions are reaching a saturation point, triggering a Mania reaction.
Of course, you already have a contingency plan for this. The Bureau has Sinners monitoring the area in shifts, with any anomalies to be reported immediately.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Jane, Dreya, and...
She hesitates, trailing off.

speaker: Player
content: And who else?

speaker: Nightingale
content: ...Bai Yi.
(Scene change)
The two of them sit meekly at the table. It's almost like they're undergoing an interrogation. All the customers have long since fled the premises.

speaker: Option
options: Have you identified the origin of the Mania?

speaker: Bai Yi
content: But I sent our astronomer! Look, I figured I wouldn't be much help anyway. I can barely tell east from west. Better that I stay here. Besides...
Bai Yi clears her throat.

speaker: Bai Yi
content: Blending in with the tourists is part of the mission! You know, hiding in plain sight, quietly observing from within the crowd. Sometimes you stumble on unexpected leads.

speaker: Player
content: So you've just been selling grilled fish here for days?

speaker: Bai Yi
content: I didn't have a choice, Chief! Che and K.K. were both away on missions, and that debt collector showed up at my door again...
Bai Yi's eyes well up with tears, but you know better than to believe a single word coming out of her mouth.

speaker: Bai Yi
content: He said... he said if I don't pay up this month, he's going to pawn everything from Whitestone!

speaker: Option
options: Might as well sell them. They're only taking up space in the Bureau Depot anyway.

speaker: Bai Yi
content: Not gonna happen! I'm not selling them off for cheap. Every piece is a priceless memory of Whitestone!

speaker: Jane
content: I understand the sentiment.

speaker: Bai Yi
content: That's my temp! I knew you'd get it!
In just a few days, Jane has already been bitten by the Whitestone bug.

speaker: Player
content: How did you end up as a temp for her?

speaker: Jane
content: Last week, I used a Type II Shell on a Corruptor. The shell was too powerful. It went straight through the target and blew up an uninhabited mansion in Eastside.

speaker: Jane
content: According to the regulations, I have to cover 75% of the damage.

speaker: Jane
content: I was at my wits' end when Ms. Bai came to my rescue.

speaker: Jane
content: She gave me this job, and even half the earnings.

speaker: Jane
content: She didn't ask any questions, just said she believed in my abilities... She's more like a friend than a boss.
It seems this is the first time in Jane's life she has ever felt this trusted.

speaker: Bai Yi
content: Hehe, say, Jane, how about you come and work for Whitestone full-time? We desperately need someone as hardworking as you!
You can see the dollar signs in her eyes and quickly cut off the scheming capitalist.

speaker: Option
options: What have you been doing besides selling barbecue?

speaker: Bai Yi
content: Ah, well...

speaker: Jane
content: Performing, finding missing persons, putting up posters, handing out flyers, and fishing. I'd never done most of these things before, but it's fun doing them with a friend.
Bai Yi opens her mouth, but her star employee has already spilled all the beans. She lunges to cover Jane's mouth, terrified of what else she might reveal.

speaker: Bai Yi
content: Ahem... We may not look like it, but we've made some real progress!

speaker: Bai Yi
content: Our astronomer can tell you about it.
Snap.
The ledger snaps shut. A scholar in a white blouse removes her grease-proof apron and comes over to you.

speaker: Dreya
content: I have some preliminary findings regarding this incident.

speaker: Dreya
content: The Mania is affecting this space in an unusual way.
She looks up, gazing toward the horizon. Twilight is silently spreading across the sky, even though the sun was high in the sky when you first arrived.

speaker: Dreya
content: It's disrupting the tidal patterns, making the nights last longer than they should. I can't pinpoint the origin of the Mania yet. We'll need wider observations.

speaker: Dreya
content: However, after the rebuild, 90% of this area is now seawater. Exploring the other zones has become difficult. We'll likely need some kind of watercraft.
The scholar looks troubled. The barbecue boss, meanwhile, lights up.

speaker: Bai Yi
content: A watercraft? Leave it to me!

speaker: Bai Yi
content: Hah...
She takes a deep breath, and a flash of white light cuts the "Surf's Bounty" sign from its post, sending it crashing to the ground.
The weathered sign breaks in half, but the sharp-eyed Jane spots something immediately.

speaker: Jane
content: Look!
A silver surfboard slides out from the broken sign. Bai Yi scoops it up and twirls it with a flourish.

speaker: Bai Yi
content: How about that? Whitestone's prized surfboard! I hid it in here so it wouldn't get lost!

options: I don't even know where to begin.

speaker: Bai Yi
content: It takes you to places, doesn't it?
Just as you're considering requesting a proper boat from the Bureau, Dreya walks right up to Bai Yi and takes the surfboard from her.

speaker: Dreya
content: For now, this is our most practical, and indeed our best, tool.

speaker: Bai Yi
content: Well, if our astronomer says so, there's no time to waste!
Bai Yi waves everyone over. Dreya, however, walks directly to you.

speaker: Dreya
content: Chief, do you know how to surf?

speaker: Dreya
content: The corruption is worse than I expected...
Having reached the shore, Dreya is intently recording the movements of the stars. However...

speaker: Bai Yi
content: Blegh...
Nearby, Bai Yi is doubled over, throwing up non-stop.

speaker: Bai Yi
content: Next time... can we please... find a boat...? BLEGH... The way you speed up... and slow down...

speaker: Jane
content: Here, motion sickness pills.

speaker: Bai Yi
content: ...Thank you.

speaker: Dreya
content: I've observed 31 unknown star clusters. We're not in DisCity, but seeing something like this is still...

speaker: Dreya
content: Exhilarating.

speaker: Option
options: ...We're here to deal with the Mania.

speaker: Dreya
content: My apologies. Even I get distracted when faced with so many new celestial bodies.
She aims her telescope back toward the Mania-affected region, reexamining the space.
As you watch Dreya, an inexplicable sense of unease rises within you. Her expression is as focused as ever, and her words sound normal, yet beneath that calm demeanor, something feels off.
You can't quite put your finger on it. Her actions? Probably not. It's only natural to act differently in a new environment.
Perhaps it's the subtle excitement in her voice, or the occasional pauses in her movements. Or maybe it's just your imagination.
After a long silence, Dreya finally speaks.

speaker: Dreya
content: The western waters.

speaker: Bai Yi
content: Ugh... See? Knew we could count on her... Blegh...
Propped up by Jane, Bai Yi doesn't hold back on the praise, even as she continues to retch.

speaker: Dreya
content: The Mania is concentrated there. Its influence is slowly spreading eastward.

speaker: Dreya
content: The rate of corruption is picking up. We need to act fast.

speaker: Dreya
content: Chief, please give orders.
Someone looks out of place... well, you've long since gotten used to it.
After a few pauses along the way, you finally arrive at your destination. Yet the sight before you...

speaker: Bai Yi
content: It should be... right? That's what our astronomer said.

speaker: Jane
content: Boss, are you sure you didn't read the map wrong?

speaker: Bai Yi
content: No way. Not a chance. I never make the same mistake twice.
Blue. Nothing but blue.
The water here is the clearest you've ever seen, cleaner even than the swimming pools in Eastside's posh mansions.
You can even make out every single pebble and strand of seaweed on the seabed.

speaker: Jane
content: ...Doesn't look like there's any Mania here.

speaker: Dreya
content: No, this isn't right. Something's missing here.
The grill master is the first to spot the problem.

speaker: Jane
content: Fish.
An idea strikes the ever-resourceful boss next to you.

speaker: Bai Yi
content: Hey, that reminds me... There's an old Eastian saying: "Water that's too pure has no fish."

speaker: Bai Yi
content: Maybe this isn't the sea. That's why there are no fish.

speaker: Dreya
content: Then the answer is obvious.
Dreya steps forward and dips her hand into the water. The surface boils at her touch. The currents come alive, and the entire space seems to wake. Bai Yi, taken by surprise, steps back instinctively.

speaker: Bai Yi
content: H-huh? No, wait, I was just kidding!
Before she can finish her words, the water at your feet towers into a colossal wave, its enormous shadow engulfing you all.
(Scene change)
Bai Yi's voice still rings in your ears as you find yourself deep under the sea.
Your vision is consumed by an absolute darkness. At first, you see nothing, only a chilling void.
Slowly, your eyes adjust to the unknown space. Your feet touch the ground. The water doesn't flood your lungs; it feels no different from standing on dry land.
But the "land" here is incredibly heavy. The omnipresent seawater is no longer a gentle medium. You can only feel your way along the seafloor rock, inching forward until you reach a wider clearing.
Heehee...
A giggle cuts through the dense water and pierces your eardrums. The aura of Mania surges and churns with her voice.
It's a blurry silhouette, slender and twisted, almost one with the sea.
Just you? You're not nearly enough...
You strain your eyes, and by the faint, dying glow of plankton, you finally make out the shape of the space.

In a clearing surrounded by jagged reefs, several old school desks and chairs lie about. They clearly don't belong in the ocean. The wood is black and rotten, covered in slimy seaweed and barnacles, their metal parts rusted through.
And slumped in one of the seats, head hung low, is the astronomer who first touched the water.
That feeling of dissonance hits you again.
Even if she were dragged into a Mania's domain, someone with Dreya's power shouldn't have been captured this easily. She wouldn't have acted so rashly, either. What's happening to her...?
Look... another one's here! I always find them. I always do!
It drifts closer to Dreya, as if declaring its victory. The Mania in the space throbs with its words.

speaker: Dreya
content: ...You can't... hurt me...
...Hahahaha! Don't tell me you're scared?
The shadow quivers with excitement, spreading its arms as it slowly approaches the astronomer.
This is an emergency. You have to use the shackles. Even in this virtual space, a Mania incarnate has terrifying destructive power.

speaker: Bai Yi
content: Hiyah! Take this, Mania!
But just as the shackles are about to activate, two figures tear through the darkness like lightning, fierce currents streaming behind them as they land perfectly between the shadow and Dreya.

speaker: Jane
content: Let her go.
The long blade gleams with a cold light as it slashes at the shadow. At the same time, a shock grenade detonates on its other side.
The clash you expected happens, but soon, you realize something is off...
The shadow doesn't shriek in agony or fight back with feral rage as you'd expect from a Mania incarnate.
Instead, it just looks... stunned?

speaker: Dreya
content: See? I told you. You can't hurt me.
The supposed kidnapping victim gets up, gesturing for Bai Yi and Jane to stop. They look at Dreya, confused, then back at the figure they just sent flying...

speaker: Lamia
content: Cough... cough cough...

speaker: Bai Yi & Jane
content: Huh?
(Scene change)

speaker: Bai Yi
content: Whoops... Talk about a misunderstanding. Friendly fire, huh?
Bai Yi scratches her head sheepishly. Next to her, Jane nods so fast that she looks like a nervous woodpecker.
Lamia, their unfortunate target, is laden with an armful of Whitestone Industries' merchandise, from toothpaste, toothbrushes, snacks, to business cards, all part of Bai Yi's apology package.

speaker: Dreya
content: So, you're not the source of Mania here.

speaker: Lamia
content: How could you even think it was me?!

speaker: Player
content: Then how did this place end up like this?
The endless night, the eerie underwater world... None of this is supposed to be here.

speaker: Bai Yi
content: There's no way this is natural, right? If it is, I'm starting the hype on DisMyth right now.

speaker: Jane
content: No. Someone made it this way.
Just as you're all racking your brains, Lamia speaks up hesitantly:

speaker: Lamia
content: Um... actually...

speaker: Lamia
content: I got here earlier than you did. The place wasn't like this at first. It changed... a few days ago? Yeah, that's right! A few days ago!
At these words, even Bai Yi starts paying serious attention.

speaker: Lamia
content: It was just a normal tourist spot at first. The view was great, and night came and went like it should.

speaker: Lamia
content: But after a few days, everything changed... I thought the Bureau was behind it at first, but now, I guess not.

speaker: Option
options: You remember all that pretty clearly.

speaker: Lamia
content: That's because... because...
Lamia mumbles, unable to go on.
Right when she's about to reveal a crucial clue, Lamia gets cold feet.

speaker: Lamia
content: No! I can't say it! It's too embarrassing!

speaker: Bai Yi
content: Don't worry, all my employees at Whitestone Industries are professionally trained. No matter how funny it is, we will keep a straight face.

speaker: Jane
content: That's right.

speaker: Lamia
content: I failed my exam at the Bureau, so they sent me out on this mission early!
Your eyes fall on an exam paper on the desk, covered in red X marks.
You remember that the Bureau held a general knowledge exam last week. It wasn't difficult; half the questions were common sense.
Perhaps you've been too focused on Hella and forgotten that this former Ocean Messenger of the Thaumas Society lacks basic everyday knowledge.

speaker: Lamia
content: Aaah... I said it out loud... I want to die of embarrassment... I just wanted to study here quietly for a retake, and then this happens!

speaker: Lamia
content: I found this thing on the beach, it looked like some kind of astrolabe. I thought it looked cool, so I brought it with me. Then I got trapped here and couldn't get out...
She slumps over the desk in defeat, recounting her story in a mumble.

speaker: Lamia
content: I kept wishing someone could take the exam for me, or at least teach me what I needed to know...

speaker: Lamia
content: But I didn't know it would be you guys! Aaaagh!
The light fades from Lamia's eyes. At this point, she has nothing left to lose.

speaker: Dreya
content: The astrolabe. Where is it?
While the rest of you are busy stifling laughter at Lamia's predicament, Dreya steps forward and takes her hand.

speaker: Lamia
content: W-what?
The sudden gesture makes Lamia jump. The Dreya you know wouldn't do something like this.

speaker: Dreya
content: The astrolabe.

speaker: Lamia
content: ...It's over there.
Lamia points to a desk cluttered with study materials, where a worn astrolabe is illuminated by several glowing patches of moss.

speaker: Dreya
content: Found it...
Dreya beckons gently, and the astrolabe flies into her palm, as if it had come to life.

speaker: Lamia
content: ...Huh?
As Lamia stares in amazement, the underwater illusion that has trapped her for days shatters, and solid ground appears beneath your feet once more.
(Scene change)
By the time the Mania is dealt with, it's already dusk.
Everyone's debating what to get for dinner, where to unwind. Even Bai Yi has changed back into her old clothes now that the threat is gone.
Only Dreya stands apart, staring at the astrolabe in her hands, lost in thought.

speaker: Bai Yi
content: Hey, is that thing really so special?

speaker: Dreya
content: It is. This is the source of the Mania.

speaker: Bai Yi
content: Huh? Wait... what? Am I hearing you right?
Her blunt answer leaves everyone stunned. Didn't the Mania just disappear?

speaker: Dreya
content: And... I remember now. I'm part of it too.
Before anyone can process this, she drops another bombshell.

speaker: Dreya
content: Don't be afraid... The truth is simple.

speaker: Dreya
content: The Mania spilling out of this place came from Dreya. And I... I am a fragment of "her" consciousness from a specific point in time, given form by the Mania.
As "Dreya" says this, her eyes are fixed on the sea and where it meets the sky. You realize at once which point in time she comes from.
All the inconsistencies, all the little things that felt off... they all make sense now. Why she's still so fascinated by the stars, why she's acting unlike the Dreya you know.
She only remembers her original mission. Everything else is a blank.

speaker: Dreya
content: Please... forget me.

speaker: Jane
content: But... we opened a shop together.

speaker: Lamia
content: You didn't take my exam for me, but... you taught me how to answer those questions!

speaker: Bai Yi
content: Right! We went surfing, we did all that cool stuff together! No way we're forgetting that!

speaker: Dreya
content: ...I don't deny any of it, but I'm not the whole of her.
The sea breeze tousles her long hair, but her gaze remains fixed on the horizon.

speaker: Dreya
content: If the Mania continues to expand, these endless waters will spill out of this space... and drown all of DisCity.

speaker: Dreya
content: Now that I remember, it's time for Dreya to fulfill the true purpose she came here for.
With that, the scholar walks forward. You reach out, trying to stop her, but she only shakes her head.
A red light engulfs the sky, and her with it.

speaker: Player
content: Dreya!
The sea breeze. The air. The night. The stars.
The peaceful night sky ripples with an eerie disturbance. The stars lose their brilliance, turning murky and distorted.
The waves are whispering, the stars are watching, they're waiting for someone to understand them... or swallow them.
Since she was a little girl, she has always watched a sky like this one. And the stars have always watched her back.
Even after she lost her consciousness, left with only instinct, the stars have kept watching.

speaker: Dreya
content: You're... here.
Like before, Dreya is once again contaminated by Mania.

speaker: Player
content: You still love the stars so much.

speaker: Dreya
content: Yes... it's engraved into my instincts.

speaker: Dreya
content: But it feels like it's been a long, long time since I've watched them like this.

speaker: Option
options: How about we stay and watch them a little longer?

speaker: Dreya
content: No, I'm not supposed to be here. I've already stayed too long.

speaker: Player
content: You're a part of Dreya. I believe in her... and I believe in you.
The person before you shakes her head.
Black slime drips from the sky, seeping into the ocean. The water churns for a moment before falling still.

speaker: Dreya
content: After all, this is a place built from data... and I'm merely an observer. I can gaze upon everything, but I can't have any of it.

speaker: Dreya
content: For the Dreya from that time to see the stars of decades to come... that's more than I could have ever hoped for.
For a moment, you see the Perishing Star that doomed the world. The source of calamity that Dreya spent a lifetime trying to understand, yet failed to prevent.

speaker: Player
content: Everything here is real. It left behind data because it existed, and that data formed this space.

speaker: Player
content: That's why... that's why it could bring you here. The fading wisp of your consciousness, buried in the depths of a dream, was given form and a place to stay.

speaker: Dreya
content: You're right. To be with people again after so long... Grilling seafood with them, surfing, tutoring...
Dreya keeps turning the astrolabe. With each spin, another piece breaks away, and the space around you shakes violently.

speaker: Dreya
content: This is more than enough. But our time is running short.
Thick sludge drips onto Dreya, but she makes no effort to resist.

speaker: Dreya
content: Until a moment ago, I've been wondering. Why am I here? When I disappear, where will my memories of you go?

speaker: Dreya
content: But seeing you... and seeing the others with you... I think I've found my answer.
Dreya stands up, gazing at the astrolabe in her hand. It melts into sludge, oozing through her fingers.
And in its place, an old, ornate gift box appears in her palm.

speaker: Dreya
content: Do you remember it?
Of course you do. It's the gift you gave Dreya.

speaker: Dreya
content: I think... these past few days we spent together will be like this gift box. Even if covered in filth, it will be kept safe in my dream.

speaker: Player
content: Yes. Just like you.

speaker: Dreya
content: Me? How is that possible... This entire space is...
Dreya stares at you in disbelief, then at the broken, crumbling space around her.
Cracks are rapidly expanding as dust and debris swirl like a storm. The boundaries of the space twist with a low groan, threatening to collapse at any moment.
Dreya comes to your side, urging you to leave before it all comes crashing down.
But you don't move an inch.

options: Trust in humanity, just as you always have.

speaker: Player
content: Humans will always push forward for what we hold dear. It doesn't matter if it's the truth, a lover... or a gift box full of memories.
Your anchor down the collapsing space with your shackles and meet Dreya's gaze.

speaker: Player
content: You are part of Dreya. You are her.

speaker: Player
content: No matter what you've forgotten, I'll help you remember it all again.
The gift box in Dreya's hands begins to glow with a soft blue light, growing brighter and brighter. And from within that light, the voices of your friends ring out, clear as day.

speaker: Bai Yi
content: Hey! Hurry up and deal with that Mania thing already! We can't run the shop without you!

speaker: Jane
content: Agreed. It's a real pain doing the books on our own.

speaker: Lamia
content: You can't die! Or I'm going to flunk my exam for sure!

speaker: Dreya
content: ...Alright.
Those familiar voices cut through the murmurs of the Mania, through all the filth and corruption, reaching her ears.
Slowly, she lowers her head, her gaze falling on the worn box in your hand.

speaker: Dreya
content: Haha...
A heartfelt smile finally blossoms on her pale lips.
So what I had forgotten... was it hope?
Light erupts from her palm, spreading in an unstoppable wave.
The moment the light touches the black sludge, the filth melts away like snow, vanishing as if it had never been there.
She looks up at the brilliant night sky, so different from the distorted, all-devouring sea of stars in her memory.

speaker: Dreya
content: ...No matter the era, humans are always so wonderfully naive.
The image of Dreya before you begins to fade, a sign she is about to disappear.

speaker: Dreya
content: Shall we do it one last time?

speaker: Dreya
content: Let's go surfing.
(Scene change)
Like an enormous soap bubble bursting, everything returns to square one.
The space has been reset. Every citizen who once stepped inside has their memories erased, just as they were at the start.
Even the lingering summer heat seems to have been carried away by the sea breeze.
You return to the fully restored Elysiland, now completely deserted.
For a fleeting moment, you think you see Dreya as she once was.
(Scene change)

speaker: Young Dreya
content: Can I ask you something, sir?
female_content: Can I ask you something, miss?

content: The little girl keeps tugging at your arm.

speaker: Young Dreya
content: What if... what if I forget everything someday?!

speaker: Young Dreya
content: Oh, but I don't want to forget everything... then I'll just remember the stars and you!

speaker: Player
content: When that time comes, I'll help you remember.

speaker: Young Dreya
content: Really? But what if I just can't?

speaker: Player
content: Then I'll just keep trying. That's what friends are for.

speaker: Young Dreya
content: Hehe! You're the best!
The smell of something burning floods your nostrils, pulling you back to reality.
You follow the trail of smoke...
And there, on the beach at night, several familiar figures are bustling about.
Jane is helping at the grill, Bai Yi is hanging up a sign, and Lamia is perched on a rock, reading a book.
The troublemaking Sinners have returned to this beach, but you realize someone's missing.
You search everywhere, but there's no sign of her.
As you sit on a rock, staring blankly at the shore...
A skewer with half a burnt eel appears before you.

speaker: Dreya
content: Grilled eel... would you like to try some?

speaker: Christina
content: Christina, Eastside's most dedicated acting inspector, is back on the case! And today's mystery is...

speaker: Christina
content: Wait! What do we have here? Could this be... an antique cipher machine?

speaker: Christina
content: How absolutely thrilling! This is just the kind of puzzle a classy detective should face!

speaker: Christina
content: (Sniffs) It's... emanating a mysterious energy.

speaker: Christina
content: Well, too bad for you, encryptor! You're up against Christina herself. A little cipher like this is no match for me!
After Christina enters the code, the cipher machine spits out a slip of paper.

speaker: Christina
content: Let's see... there's a website address written here. Let's check it out.

speaker: Christina
content: Huh? It looks like completion records for a game demo... "eatmydust," "GetARealJob," "DarkStick69"...

speaker: Christina
content: Wow, these usernames are... pretty aggressive.
Christina continues scrolling, and the webpage confirms that all the usernames point to a single IP address, exposing a collection of one player's alt accounts.

speaker: Christina
content: So many accounts... "RebornAsGamingGenius," "ReincarnatedForTheWin," "OneLifeRun32," "OneLifeRun56," "OneLifeRun108," "*****Dev"...

speaker: Christina
content: Looks like this player's gaming journey has been... quite the struggle. Let's see where this IP is located.
The search results appear, revealing the device is located inside the Bureau. Its name is displayed with audacious clarity: Nino Sama #2.
With a sigh, Christina navigates to Nino's livestream channel, only to find it offline. A banner announces tomorrow's event:
"Blind playthrough of HollowSong's Ironman Mode, absolutely no spoilers! Come witness Nino Sama complete the game without dying!"

speaker: Christina
content: 340 failure records... Hmm... I don't think I'm misunderstanding what "blind playthrough" means...

speaker: Nino
content: Aaaaah! Christina, what are you looking at?!

speaker: Christina
content: Oh no...! Run!

speaker: Nino
content: Stop right there!!!

speaker: Nino
content: Pant... pant... pant... how are you... so fast...

speaker: Christina
content: Well, I am an acting inspector! I have daily physical training. To catch criminals and bring them to justice, you need exceptional fitness and athletic ability!
Nino rolls her eyes.

speaker: Nino
content: What's there... to be so proud of...

speaker: Christina
content: Don't worry, your secret is safe with me.

speaker: Christina
content: By the way, I glanced at your streaming analytics and noticed a pattern: the more attempts you fail, Nino, the better your viewership and chat engagement get. Constantly failing seems like a pretty clever streaming strategy!

speaker: Nino
content: Just shut up!!!

speaker: Christina
content: The crescent moon hangs in the night sky, a maiden pretends to sleepwalk by... Could the intel be hidden in this little rhyme?

speaker: Christina
content: Sneaking into the Chief's private space, finding little love secrets all over the place. Hehe... no wonder my assistant is so popular, but nothing escapes the great detective Christina!

speaker: Christina
content: When it comes to sleepwalking, the first person that comes to mind has to be...

speaker: Letta
content: Mmm... zZZ... mmmm... snoop... evil snoop... heart invader... mm... found you...

speaker: Letta
content: Must... zZZ... eliminate...

speaker: Christina
content: Whoa! Things have already escalated to elimination?!

speaker: Christina
content: Wait-wait-wait-wait—! I wasn't trying to spy on your secrets on purpose; this was completely an accident!

speaker: Christina
content: I just thought this cipher machine would reveal crucial intel about major unsolved cases! That's the only reason I started decoding it!

speaker: Christina
content: This happens in detective novels all the time! The agency receives a mysterious package that turns out to be a puzzle challenge from some brilliant criminal mastermind!

speaker: Christina
content: Don't worry, I've already destroyed both the original code and the decrypted results. Your secrets are absolutely safe; I give you my word of honor!

speaker: Letta
content: Wha... Christina...? Where am I? Did I sleepwalk again... so tired, going back to bed...

speaker: Letta
content: Sleepwalk... Sleepwalk... Head so fuzzy... Don't remember anything...

speaker: Christina
content: After all that trouble, the information from this cipher machine turns out to be nothing but gossip. Who in the world would collect intelligence like this...

speaker: Christina
content: Could it be... the owner of this machine is actually a tabloid journalist? But who...

speaker: Mess
content: Young adventurer Christina! The legendary sword you requested is complete! Hand over that cipher machine in exchange!

Mess suddenly materializes before Christina. In her left hand, she wields a foam sword studded with light strips that pulse with dazzling rainbow colors. In her right, a speaker blasts her powerful entrance music.

speaker: Christina
content: Mess... Why are you here? I never asked you to forge a sword. Detectives don't even use swords...

speaker: Christina
content: And besides, that thing in your hand...

speaker: Mess
content: Cut the chatter and hand it over!

Whap! The foam sword lands with perfect precision on Christina's head, the impact as crisp as a ping-pong ball. As Christina clutches the stinging spot, Mess's hand darts past her to snatch the cipher machine.
But the sting is fleeting. The young detective shakes it off, tightens her grip on the device, and breaks into a sprint once more.

speaker: Christina
content: Not a chance! This cipher machine absolutely cannot fall into your hands!

speaker: Mess
content: This device doesn't even have the intel you wanted, so what's the harm in giving it to me? Wouldn't it be better to put it to good use?

speaker: Christina
content: No way! If this cipher machine falls into your hands, it would throw the entire Bureau into chaos!

speaker: Mess
content: That's exactly what I want! Chaos! You pull my hair, I slap your face—isn't that super—duper—FUN?

speaker: Christina
content: How can you say that! That's absolutely terrible!

Just as Mess is lost in her excitement, a flash of green darts into the noisy hallway. A girl draws her revolver in one smooth motion—"pew"— and a small, pink flower blooms on Mess's forehead. With elegant nonchalance, she raises the barrel to her lips and blows away imaginary smoke.

speaker: Roulecca
content: In the Bureau, no one touches Roulecca's interests without permission. Understand, darling?

speaker: Mess
content: Roulecca, you jerk! Paintball guns still hurt, you know!

speaker: Roulecca
content: Mess, I regret to inform you that in this game... you have been eliminated.

speaker: Roulecca
content: Pow—pow—pow—pew-pew!
Soon, the hallway becomes a vibrant rainbow of colors.

speaker: Christina
content: Thanks for that, Roulecca.

speaker: Roulecca
content: There we go! That silly Mess has been chased away. Now, be a dear and hand over that cipher machine to Roulecca!

speaker: Christina
content: Does this cipher machine belong to you?

speaker: Roulecca
content: No. But as a reward for that brilliant performance just now, this machine should rightfully go to Roulecca!

speaker: Roulecca
content: Roulecca happens to know this little device records the deepest secrets of anyone who touches it, you know...
Christina recoils as if electrocuted, her hands flying away from the cipher machine she had been clutching so protectively a moment before.

speaker: Christina
content: W-what do you mean?

speaker: Roulecca
content: Roulecca saw with her own eyes how Letta and Nino were fiddling with this thing for a while, and not long after, you managed to decode their secrets...

speaker: Christina
content: Oh no... I promised them I'd keep it confidential.

speaker: Roulecca
content: So Roulecca will place it in the Chief's room, hehe.

speaker: Christina
content: No, absolutely not! I must protect my assistant's privacy!
At the mere mention of "Chief," the fear and worry flee from Christina's eyes, making way for unwavering determination.

speaker: Roulecca
content: Then play a round with Roulecca. Whoever wins gets the cipher machine. Let's see which side Lady Luck favors.
Roulecca deftly twirls the revolver in her hand, the cylinder popping out with a click.

speaker: Christina
content: Nobody can win against you!
Even before Roulecca's performance can reach its finale, Christina is already in motion, clutching the cipher machine tightly as she makes her escape.

speaker: Christina
content: Pant... pant... What in the world is going on today...

Christina's face flushes a deep red as she gasps for air. In the distance, she spots two familiar figures approaching. They move like saviors in a doomsday wasteland. Never before have they seemed so righteous.

speaker: Christina
content: Nino... Letta... help me stop Roulecca! She's trying to steal this cipher machine and use it to invade the Chief's privacy!
No sooner does Christina speak than a crystalline gleam lights Letta's dreamy eyes. They snap shut, and she begins to drift forward, moving with the silent, aimless quality of a specter.

speaker: Letta
content: Mmm mmm... cipher machine... find the cipher machine...

speaker: Nino
content: On second thought, this cipher machine could provide some explosive material for my livestreams!

speaker: Christina
content: You... you guys!
Christina is left utterly speechless. She hasn't even planned an escape route when Mess materializes out of nowhere.

speaker: Mess
content: Roulecca, are you really going to let them butt in like this? And Christina, the cipher machine and an inspector like you are such a perfect package deal, you know!

speaker: Mess
content: But hey, Nino's just doing this for her livestream career, and I support that! As for Letta... well, nothing a sleepwalker does should surprise anyone.

speaker: Mess
content: Come on, I want to see bloodshed!

speaker: Roulecca
content: Don't run, pew pew pew! Roulecca has you in her sights!

speaker: Christina
content: Assistant—! Where are you?! The Bureau's in chaos!
Christina runs desperately until her steps grow unsteady and her vision blurs. Staggering forward in a daze, she collapses into a familiar embrace.
The figure staggers back a few steps with a wince. The impact wasn't just from Christina, but from the sharp-edged cipher machine she was clutching.

speaker: Christina
content: My assistant! You're finally here! Help me!!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Maybe you should help me first...

Your legs buckle, fighting for balance. Cradled in Christina's arms, the so-called weapon is revealed as an old cipher machine, its surface a web of scratches. From it radiates a disorienting aura of Mania.
You probe it with your shackles and instantly recognize the source: Hilda.

speaker: Christina
content: This cipher machine has the power to reveal people's secrets. It ab... absolutely can't fall into their hands!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: They?

speaker: Christina
content: Yeah, it's... Mess and the others... wait... where did they go?
Christina turns. The hallway lies dead silent and utterly deserted. From around the corner, Letta cautiously peeks out, but the moment her eyes meet Christina's, she instantly ducks back into hiding.

speaker: Christina
content: Ugh, those guys...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Let me take the cipher machine. I'll return it to its rightful owner.

speaker: Christina
content: Do you know who owns this cipher machine?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Yes, she's a brilliant cryptographer. I'll introduce you to her when I get the chance. By the way, you did a great job today!
You gently smooth down Christina's wind-tousled bangs, then turn to face the shadowed end of the hallway, your voice cutting clearly through the silence.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: As for the rest of you, no dinner until this hallway is spotless.
The hallway remains empty, the silence broken only by the disgruntled mumbles drifting from around the corner.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Are you ready?
Yes.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: On my cue. Three, two...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: One!
On the clearing beside the old town, the ethereal woman wields the Apostle's power in tandem with your Potestas, steadily raising a high tower.
Foundation, timber, and stone weave and fuse at her command as if enchanted, drawing the peak skyward, floor upon rising floor.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: A day ago, I never would've imagined using Mania to build something like this in my lifetime. Let's finish this in one push.
She turns back to you, offering a smile and a nod.
As you wish.
One Day Ago

speaker: Supervision Center
content: WARNING: Furnace temperature exceeding safe levels.

speaker: Supervision Center
content: WARNING: Furnace temperature exceeding safe levels.

Evening settles in. During the shift change, the temperature in the furnace area adjacent to the cafeteria lounge suddenly soars. The mercury column in the thermometer edges slowly higher, still short of the critical threshold.
Beneath the monitor's stuttering red warning, small clusters of sparks flicker and dance, hopping as they weave and meld. An orange-red feather drifts down to the table and burns with a sharp hiss.
In a corner nearby, something small whimpers softly.
Chirp...?

speaker: Staff A
content: So where you headed this year?

speaker: Staff B
content: Ah, last year was my folks' place, so this year it's the in-laws.

speaker: Staff A
content: That's nice... I can't wait to get home myself...

speaker: Staff B
content: Yeah, tell me about it... Hey, uh, is it just me, or is it getting really hot by the furnace?
The two staff members chat as they step out of the cafeteria, only to notice the abnormal heat radiating from the furnace area.
Waves of heat push through the gap in the door. Something is definitely wrong. The staff members trade a look and nod. One of them carefully wraps a hand around the handle.

speaker: Staff A
content: Alright, you ready? I got you.

speaker: Staff B
content: Yeah, ready...
The staff member counts down in silence for a few seconds, then hauls open the door to the furnace area.
Cheeeeeep!
A scorching gust howls past them, and both workers duck on instinct, throwing their hands up to shield themselves.
Even as they drop low, they glimpse an orange-red ball of light, radiating intense heat, stumbling past their feet at breakneck speed.

speaker: Staff A
content: What is that...?

speaker: Staff B
content: Did that fire just... become something alive?

speaker: Noisy Voices
content: Wait, where'd it go?!

speaker: Noisy Voices
content: Is it somewhere near you?!

speaker: Noisy Voices
content: Behind you! Look behind you!!

speaker: Noisy Voices
content: Careful, don't step on it—whoa!
Coming back from fieldwork, you find yourself constantly rubbing your face against the winter chill, longing for nothing more than to slip back into the Bureau and warm your bones.
But the Bureau greets you with unexpected warmth today, and something else besides... a strange liveliness.

speaker: Yanyan
content: OwO! Over here, over here! It's heading your way. Get the board ready!

speaker: OwO
content: Hehe, you little troublemaker! Just wait till the great OwO gets her hands on—whoa, whoa, whoa!
Whack!

speaker: Yanyan
content: Ah! Chief!! Look out!!!
The voices find you just as you are slipping off your coat and making your way toward the commotion, curious to discover what all the fuss is about.
The shout jerks your gaze forward on instinct, but the moment you raise your head, something warm, soft, and fluffy slams right into your face.
Cheep...
Slowly, you reach up and pinch whatever has latched onto your face, clinging to your hair for dear life, and carefully peel it away. You bring it closer to inspect—
A small bird, vivid orange-red and wreathed in shimmering heat, rests in your palm. Something has clearly agitated it; the tips of its feathers are visibly singed.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Yao?
It looks nothing like what you expect, and its power reads as faint, yet your shackles leave no doubt: this little bird's power source traces back to Yao.

speaker: Yanyan
content: Wait, that's Yao?!

speaker: Yanyan
content: Chief
Yanyan steps out from the clutter and gently scoops the little bird into her hands, staring at it with disbelief. Perhaps sensing that the chase is over, the bird makes no attempt to flee.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The power signature matches hers. I'm thinking... maybe a clone? She might've made it by accident when her power spiked again.

speaker: Yanyan
content: Really? Is she okay, though? We just got some new books in from Eastia, and I read that super powerful people can lose control when they're trying to break past their limits. What if something happened to her?!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Don't worry. The energy feels gentle. If something was really wrong with Yao, it wouldn't be this calm. That's probably why you couldn't tell it was connected to her.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'll go check on her myself. You two...
You retrieve the little creature from Yanyan and take in the chaos that surrounds you: spell-scorched ashes and black smoke, wooden boards from hurried traps, plastic bags strewn about...

speaker: OwO
content: I-it was their idea! They said there was a little spirit running around, so I just... I was just helping!
OwO catches your look and quickly ducks behind the two staff members, pouting with an expression that screams innocence, as if none of this mess could possibly be her fault.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It's fine. You two go take a break. Let the adults handle the rest.
The two staff members nod eagerly. One ushers Yanyan and OwO clear of the mess; the other goes in search of a broom, muttering under their breath about how swamped they are.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Alright, little guy. Let's go figure out where you came from.
The WhiteSands had seen numerous disturbances of late, but Yao put down every last one. WhiteSands has remained relatively peaceful ever since.
Around the New Year, a letter arrived for you, marked with a flame feather and bearing words that she would return to the Bureau in a few days to visit.
Perhaps the effort of suppressing the Apostles had taken too much out of her. Since Yao came back, she has kept mostly to her room, sleeping, and only stirring for meals.

speaker: Fledgling?
content: Chirp! Cheeeep!
As though it senses something, the fledgling in your palm stirs with sudden excitement, its wings beating frantically.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Yeah, yeah. Hang on. We're almost there.
Yao's room feels warmer than any other. Even in the dead of winter, the door handle holds its warmth against your palm.

You push the door open. There she lies, curled up in bed and fast asleep, just as you expect. Soft blankets wrap her from head to toe, letting only her long, lovely hair spill free—flowing like a cascade of tail feathers.

speaker: Fledgling?
content: Chirp, chirp, chirp! Chirp, chirp!

You set the fledgling down beside Yao's pillow. It nuzzles into her hair with obvious delight. You had thought it might revert to a single feather or melt back into raw energy, sinking into Yao once more, but the little bird shows no such intention.

speaker: Yao
content: Chief...?

The bird latches onto a strand of hair and gives a sharp tug, startling the sleeper into consciousness. A bout of muffled grumbling rises from under the blankets before Yao finally surfaces, eyes still half-closed.

speaker: Yao
content: Is something the matter? And this little one... where did it come from?
Yao scoops up the little bird from beside her pillow and gazes into its beady eyes for a long moment. It doesn't take her long to realize that this creature has sprung from her own excess power.

speaker: Yao
content: You came all this way just to bring it back yourself... I take it this little one has been causing mischief?
You chuckle under your breath and drop into a crouch by the bed. One quick poke at the creature in Yao's palm, then you pull out your terminal to check.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Two staff members spotted it hanging around the furnace area. They tried to catch it, and it just bolted. Left sparks everywhere it went.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Nothing too bad, honestly. Scared a few people, a couple dropped plates, some files went flying... Oh, and it set a few cardboard boxes on fire.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But I'm more curious about how it even got there in the first place...
Once she has heard your account, Yao presses her lips into a thin line and gives the little bird a poke. Unrepentant as ever, it simply stares back. She speaks, her voice low.

speaker: Yao
content: ...I've felt safe here at the Bureau. And with you nearby so often lately, my power has been returning faster than I expected. I think... that may be why this little one appeared.

speaker: Yao
content: I should reabsorb it at once. Before it stirs up any more trouble.

A slow stream of golden-red light seeps from Yao's palm, wrapping around the little bird. Yet even after a long moment passes, the fledgling refuses to merge back into her. If anything, it only grows larger.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Did it just get fatter?

speaker: Yao
content: Fluffed up.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Right. Fluffed up.

speaker: Yao
content: Still... that it refuses to return to me is strange.
Yao contemplates this for a moment, then suddenly asks.

speaker: Yao
content: Chief, where did you find it?
You lead Yao to the furnace area. The fledgling clearly approves of this place as it bounces back and forth in her palm, fluttering with visible excitement.
Yao lets her gaze drift over the furnace area, then it finally lands on the little cafeteria just beyond.
It happens to be the midnight shift change. The cafeteria has laid out late-night snacks, and staff clusters together, eating and talking. The talk, as ever, revolves around the coming spring break.

speaker: Yao
content: I think I understand now...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What do you mean?

speaker: Yao
content: It came from me, yes... but what gave it shape was something else entirely.
Yao nods toward the staff members chattering away in the cafeteria, the ghost of a smile pulling at the corners of her mouth.

speaker: Yao
content: In the beginning, the Sun Crow took form because of what people held in their hearts... their faith, their hopes, their wishes.

speaker: Yao
content: This little one's power may have come from the feather I sent you... but the reason it lives...

speaker: Yao
content: ...is because of the longing and wishes they carry as they speak.
Yao runs her fingers gently over the fledgling's feathers. A pleasant shiver ripples from the crown of its head all the way to the end of its tail.

speaker: Yao
content: I don't think a simple recall will be enough to bring it back into my core power... Not as it is now.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So what do we do?
You prod the fledgling's belly softly, then study it once more as you withdraw your hand.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Whatever's in those wishes... it's got some serious fuel behind it. Pretty sure it got bigger since earlier, ahem, I mean, fluffier.
Yao cocks her head, catching the drift of conversation, then answers with a thoughtful air.

speaker: Yao
content: In ancient times, when deities heard the prayers of their people...

speaker: Yao
content: They surely would want to answer them themselves.
While Yao explains why the bird refuses to return, a solution has already formed in your mind. She appears to be arriving at the same conclusion.
Yet neither of you embraces it willingly, because—

speaker: Yugu
content: So, a tale must be woven—a little stage upon which this fledgling's wish may be fulfilled—and only then will it consent to return to Yao. Have I grasped the thread correctly?

speaker: Yugu
content: And should this tale remain untold, our tiny friend here shall continue to swell with the hopes and longings of all who cross its path. Perhaps, in time... a second Sun Crow would rise?

speaker: Yao
content: You see it clearly, Miss Yugu.
You catch the amused expression on Yugu's face while she observes Yao, and quickly jump in.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It doesn't need to be anything fancy. Just a basic setup. Honestly, even an empty room would do the job.
Yugu smiles, drawing a story book from the depths of her wide sleeves, and leafs through its pages with care.

speaker: Yugu
content: A part of me confesses... I should dearly love to witness the birth of a second Sun Crow...
A blank page opens before you. The shackles tremble softly, and Yugu lets her power flow free.

speaker: Yugu
content: ...yet this, too, makes for an enchanting prologue.
Yugu watches, and your forms melt away. Reality dissolves before your eyes as a force seizes you, dragging you down in a dizzying plunge.
Her voice ripples through the void, amused.

speaker: Yugu
content: For you, Chief, and Yao, I shall exercise restraint, a courtesy born of kinship and respect. The ink of this tale shall flow untainted by my influence.

speaker: Yugu
content: That said, a storyteller worth her salt would never suffer her audience to endure a barren narrative...

speaker: Yugu
content: So then. Revel in the story as it unfolds... and do try to enjoy the reflections of your own heart along the way.
The world whirls around you. You feel your body and mind slipping into a heavy darkness. A stretch of time passes, then you touch down softly, and light floods back into the world before your eyes.
(Sound of bustling traffic)

A small town spreads out before you. The streets swim with the warm scent of fresh pastries and drifting steam; red paper couplets still hold the faint tang of ink. It is a bustling, cheerful scene. But beyond the distant mountains, dark clouds gather and threaten.
You scan your surroundings, yet the "little birds" who entered this "story" alongside you are nowhere to be seen.

speaker: Vendor
content: Hey there, friend! Friend! Care for a wishing rope?
A vendor's shout cuts through your thoughts. He extends a colorful rope toward you, his face split with a bright grin.

speaker: Vendor
content: Been watching you look around for a good while now. You're not buying any festival goods, not trading for anything new... so I got to thinking, maybe you're here for one of these, eh?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: A wishing rope...? Is there some kind of deity people worship around here?

speaker: Vendor
content: Oh-ho! Not from these parts, are ya? Well then, you've come to the right fella!
The vendor pushes the pretty rope into your palms, tugs you forward, and gestures toward a spot just ahead, already launching into a lively explanation.

speaker: Vendor
content: We pay our respects to the Sun Crow Goddess! She's got herself a shawl of woven clouds and carries a lantern right from the heavens. Keeps all sorts of calamity away from us! Everyone in these parts, we're all still standing thanks to Her protection!

speaker: Vendor
content: Now, the Goddess herself ain't shown her face in nearly a hundred years. But folks around here, we say when the year's wrapping up, she still slips on down to the mortal world, gathers up what's in folks' hearts, and then...

The vendor's chatter dies mid-sentence, his eyes going wide as he gazes into the distance. You track his stare, and your breath catches. A massive orb flickers with orange light, hurtling toward the earth ahead at terrifying speed.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Wait, is that...?
Boom!!
The lively street goes utterly still. The orb slams into the ground, and nothing remains but thick, rolling clouds of dust.
Before a single soul can respond, a sharp cry pierces through the haze.

speaker: Child
content: It's... It's the Sun Crow Goddess! She really came! The Sun Crow Goddess... she finally came back to see us!
Just off the main street, an open area teems with people gathered in tight rings, lifting their colored rope knots high as they shout out their wishes.
You fight with all your strength to shoulder through the pressing crowd.
Sure enough, standing at the center of the crowd is Yao.
Only now she wears a flowing gauze gown, nearly identical to the Sun Crow Goddess the vendor spoke of, draped in a cloud-patterned ceremonial shawl, a sky lantern held in her hands.

speaker: Fledgling
content: Chirp!
Your sight cuts to black as something warm and fluffy smacks against your face. It's a familiar, feathery weight. In that sudden dark, a hand seizes yours.
You pluck the fluffy ball from your face with practiced ease, then gently let your shackles' power flow free, soothing both the agitated little bird and Yao, whose grip on your hand remains tight.
The crowd sees Yao draw you close, and for one held breath, they go still before bursting into wild cheers.

speaker: Crowd
content: It's the envoy! The Goddess has chosen her envoy!

speaker: Crowd
content: Goddess! Envoy! Please, hear our prayers! Hear our wishes!

speaker: Yao
content: Please... Everyone, please slow down... If you keep pushing forward like this, someone will get hurt...
The crowd presses inward, ring upon ring. The little bird on your shoulder stirs with growing unease beneath the weight of their prayers, shifting anxiously as its round body swells ever larger.
A dull ache throbs through your shackles. Something unseen is gathering strength.
Though you understand this is nothing more than one of Yugu's tales, you find no will to interrupt. They are merely offering their prayers.
Silence, all of you! How dare you act so shamelessly before the Goddess herself!
The Sun Crow Tower isn't even finished, and you lot think you've earned the right to make wishes of Her?!

Just as the tension nears its breaking point, an old man with a silver beard pushes through the crowd on your behalf, granting you a brief reprieve. Once the others draw back, he turns toward you and slowly drops to his knees.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Whoa, no, no, no! Sir, please, you really don't have to do that!
You and Yao rush forward, attempting to lift the elder back to his feet, yet despite your every protest, he remains firmly on his knees and will not rise.

speaker: Old Man
content: We've waited... we've waited almost a hundred years... Sun Crow Goddess... You've finally... You've truly returned to us. In the flesh...!
A low roll of thunder rumbles from afar. One by one, the people who press close just moments before follow the elder's lead, sinking to their knees in reverence.

speaker: Old Man
content: The Goddess Tower is already near halfway built! We'll work faster, we swear it! Just... please, I beg of you... watch over us!

speaker: Crowd
content: Please watch over us!
Past the folded mountain ridges, an endless bank of storm clouds creeps nearer. The dark crimson lightning flickering within grows sharper by the moment, an ominous vision.
You and Yao trade a glance, instantly understanding. The goddess who once shielded these towns from ruin has long since vanished from sight.
The calamity that still rages has likely twisted the wards she left behind. Now the towns teeter on the edge of annihilation...
And so the people raise the Goddess Tower, praying that it might summon her back in time to usher in the New Year in safety.

speaker: Fledgling
content: Cheep! Cheeeeep!!

The little bird on your shoulder latches onto your collar with its beak and tumbles to the ground, then bounces over to the waiting crowd. It snatches a wish ribbon from a young child's grasp and flits back in your direction.

But the ribbon is far too long. Before the bird can hop more than a pace or two, the fabric snarls around its round belly. Bird and ribbon go tumbling end over end, landing in a clumsy heap at Yao's feet.
Yao scoops up the little bird and works the ribbon free, only then catching sight of the shaky, childish script etched upon it. It's a wish, tiny and sincere.
I hope Mom finishes the Goddess Tower quick, so she can come home and eat with us. I hope Dad stays safe, and comes back home safe from the faraway mountains.

speaker: Yao
content: Everyone... please, rise.

Yao lets go of your hand and cradles the little bird in her palms, raising it before her with quiet solemnity. The shackles that bind you together grow still, and in that calm, you understand exactly what she means to do.

speaker: Yao
content: I have heard all of you.

speaker: Yao
content: Since I have returned, and since your hearts have spoken true, I shall watch over this land.

speaker: Yao
content: But... there is no need to raise stones in my name. No need for towers.

speaker: Yao
content: The year is ending. What I long to see... is each of you safe and warm. Home with the ones you love, in good health and good spirits.

speaker: Old Man
content: But the tower is already half standing! If we just leave it be, how could we ever be worthy of Your blessing?
The elder shakes his head, and the surrounding crowd voices their agreement, insisting that the tower must be completed.

speaker: Yao
content: This... this is enough.
Yao slips the wish ribbon free from the elder's wrist. The little bird brushes softly against his skin, leaving a gentle, soothing warmth in its wake.

speaker: Yao
content: Leave your ribbons with me. That is all I ask.

speaker: Old Man
content: But... but surely...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Sir. Please.
You step up and dip into a respectful bow before the elder.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The Goddess has given her word. You can all go home now, really.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If you still want to do something for her... then figure out how to make this new year a happy one. That's what she wants.
Night settles over the land, but the clouds pressing against the far peaks do not melt into shadow. They pulse with a red that grows ever more vivid, ever more threatening.
Together, you and Yao stand at the foot of the unfinished tower, your gazes fixed on the distant horizon, your expressions heavy with unspoken weight.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So... the big crisis in this story looks like some kind of calamity. You got any ideas?

speaker: Yao
content: It spans far and wide... I could address it directly, but the root of it lies much higher. If we wish to truly resolve this...
At these words, the two of you turn in unison, gazing back at the half-finished tower that rises behind you.

speaker: Yao
content: It seems we'll need to see this tower completed, together.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Wait, I have to help build it too?

speaker: Yao
content: Well... this place is a story, after all, woven from Miss Yugu's gift. And since she is a Sinner bound by your shackles...

speaker: Yao
content: Perhaps you might reach through that bond and influence the shape of things.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Yeah... that makes sense...
You follow Yao back inside the tower. There, the little bird lies nestled among a heap of bright wish ribbons, sound asleep.
No longer does it swell round and plump from the prayers and faith it absorbs; instead, it grows slender and elegant, poised as though it might unfurl its wings and leap into the air at any second.
Yao brushes her fingers across the ribbons, touching them as if they were something precious and breakable.

speaker: Yao
content: Tomorrow... let us grant their wishes.
Goddess, please keep my parents healthy! Keep them safe and well on the mountain!
Goddess, I learned how to weave grasshoppers from grass blades now. Can you bring my brother back to see?
Sun Crow Goddess, please make me stronger and more capable! I want to go to the mountain. I want to protect our town!
Goddess...
Sun Crow Goddess...
Yao jerks awake, her heart hammering in her chest.
All around her stretch countless prayer ribbons, some already neatly sorted, others still waiting for her touch. Each one bears lines of tightly packed wishes, identical to those that fill her dream.

speaker: Yao
content: I will... hold your prayers close to my heart.
In your sleep, you seem to catch the sound of Yao's voice, softly murmuring a name. It is a tender sight, one that wears an expression she has never once glimpsed on your face.

speaker: Yao
content: Thank you... for yesterday.
Yao looks up at the tower that is now standing several stories higher, and a trace of exasperation crosses her face.
It is a blessing that both of you can wield your powers. Without them, who knows how long this tower might drag on.
The Bureau will hold a New Year gathering soon. She has to wrap everything up before then and get you back in time to join...
Whoa, no way! The Sun Crow Goddess actually lives here?!
The unexpected voice pulls Yao from her thoughts. Her gaze lifts to the doorway, where a tall, slender boy staggers under an armload of wood, poised with one foot already crossing into the tower.

speaker: Yao
content: Ah... this place is... it has its charms, yes.

speaker: Yao
content: Ahem... But what brings you here?

speaker: Yao
content: I told you before. There's no need for any of you to come build this tower.
At Yao's words, the boy's brow creases in clear unease. He lowers the lumber to the ground and brushes his palms clean.

speaker: Boy
content: Yeah, well... my ma always says, you work hard, you earn your keep. Don't be the kinda person who just takes and takes.

speaker: Boy
content: I know I'm all gangly and awkward. Too tall, balance is shot. I ain't built like my pa is. He can go up the mountain and keep folks safe.

speaker: Boy
content: But just sitting around, letting the goddess protect me and not doing anything for it... that just doesn't sit right. Y'know?
The boy slips his hands into his sleeves and sinks into a crouch by the threshold, averting his face in a flush of embarrassment.

speaker: Boy
content: I still got some muscle in me. I can help with the tower...

speaker: Yao
content: ...Sigh.
A gentle sigh escapes Yao, and she regards the boy with a warm smile.

speaker: Yao
content: I see now.

speaker: Yao
content: But tell me... do the others feel this way too?
The boy freezes for a moment before spinning around to follow Yao's gesture. A cluster of residents peeks from around the door, their heads craning as they listen in on the exchange.

speaker: Villager A
content: He's right, he's right! That's what I've been thinking this whole time!

speaker: Villager B
content: I still got some strength left in me too, y'know!

speaker: Villager C
content: Yeah, it doesn't sit right with me either! Let us help build the tower for the Sun Crow Goddess!

speaker: Boy
content: H-hey—wait, wait, wait! What're you all—?! Quit saying that stuff!!
The boy shoots upright and plows through the cluster of residents in a flustered rush, his cheeks blazing a deep red.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Mmh... what's with all the noise...
Still dragging yourself from sleep, you catch only the noise of a heated commotion nearby. The question slips from your lips before you can stop it.
To your surprise, the voices die at once. That sudden stillness jolts you alert. You force your eyes open and slap lightly at your cheeks to chase away the drowsiness.
What you find then is Yao and a cluster of people mid-argument by the tower entrance, all of them frozen in place as if time itself has stopped, every gaze fixed squarely on you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Uh... morning?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You could've... woken me up sooner.

The heat of embarrassment still lingers in your ears. You grab a wooden plank and pass it to the boy beside you, who fastens it to the hoist rope and hauls it upward to the residents working at the tower's top.

speaker: Yao
content: Forgive me. You seemed so tired... I thought it best to let you rest a little longer.

speaker: Yao
content: The shackles... they weigh on you, too.
A sheepish smile tugs at your lips. Yao has a point: within Yugu's tale, the shackles serve as a tool you can actually wield.
Yet here, their power takes on the cast of divine miracle, only deepening the residents' conviction that you and Yao truly are the envoy and the goddess.
Rumble!!
A low growl of thunder rolls across the distance, and every hand stills. You lift your gaze to the horizon and realize the heavy bank of storm clouds has edged closer, unnoticed until now.

speaker: Boy
