content: Why are you giving us that old man's stuff?! It's bad luck!

speaker: Eve
content: Don't say that. Mr. Benna cares a lot about his granddaughter Shanna.

speaker: Middle-Aged Female
content: Granddaughter? He doesn't have a granddaughter! He's just an old bachelor who makes up different stories every day.

speaker: Middle-Aged Male
content: Exactly! His memory gets worse every year. We've been trying to avoid him for ages. Thank goodness he actually found a job and left! You got scammed, didn't you?

speaker: Eve
content: Aren't you his son and daughter-in-law?

speaker: Middle-Aged Female
content: You must be mistaken. We really don't know this Benna, and there's no Shanna here. Miss, you better leave.

speaker: Middle-Aged Male
content: And take these things with you... Hey, did you also just come out of that factory? Is there contamination on you too?!

speaker: Middle-Aged Male
content: Stay back! If you come over, I'll call the sheriff!

speaker: Eve
content: Bass said he made a lot of friends here.

speaker: Eve
content: He passed away unexpectedly. I wanted to visit on his behalf.

speaker: Orphanage Director
content: Bass... Bass who?

speaker: Eve
content: Don't you remember? A very tall, loud and strong young man.
The orphanage director scratches his head and stops a colleague passing by.

speaker: Orphanage Director
content: Hey, do you remember if we had someone like that?

speaker: Orphanage Staff
content: Let me think... a loud voice? Ah, are you talking about that buffoon?

speaker: Orphanage Staff
content: Bass... so that's his name!

speaker: Orphanage Director
content: Did he have any friends?

speaker: Orphanage Staff
content: Would someone so dumb even know what the word 'friend' means?

speaker: Orphanage Staff
content: Maybe he thinks those who spat at him from upstairs are his friends!

speaker: Milly
content: It seems that no one remembers him... Eh, miss?

speaker: Orphanage Staff
content: Where did she go? She moves pretty fast for someone in a wheelchair.

speaker: Sheriff
content: Kids go missing every day. Where do you expect us to find a kid who's been missing for over ten years?

speaker: Sheriff
content: Get out of here. Don't interfere with our work.

Eve gets pushed out helplessly by the sheriff. The missing person notices that Maresa gave her get scattered all over the ground. Biting her lip, Eve bends over to try to pick them up, but her fingers are always an inch short of the ground.

speaker: Eve
content: Maybe to you, he's just one of thousands of missing children, but he's Maresa's only child...

speaker: Sheriff
content: What are you mumbling about? Pack up your stuff and leave. Don't come back. We can't help you.

speaker: Woman
content: Polly really left nothing behind?

speaker: Eve
content: Yeah, she left nothing. Everything was destroyed in that disaster.

speaker: Woman
content: Isn't there compensation from the factory? How can she just die on us like that! Does that good-for-nothing girl want her little brother to starve?

speaker: Eve
content: Little brother?

speaker: Woman
content: Ah, I mean... Miss Eve, you can see that we're struggling to make ends meet. You are, after all, the daughter of the factory boss. Maybe you can...

speaker: Woman
content: Wh-why are you glaring at me like that...

speaker: Woman
content: Okay, forget the compensation then... No need to be so hostile...

speaker: Eve
content: Bone, I'm throwing you your last birthday party.

speaker: Eve
content: Actually, this birthday party shouldn't exist either, but I promised to take you for a walk. I'm afraid I can't fulfill that promise now.

speaker: Eve
content: I always feel like I owe you something. Let me make it up to you with a birthday party. You won't blame me, will you?
Eve stares intently at the flame in her hand, watching it move slowly down the wooden stick, burning all the way to her fingertips.

speaker: Eve
content: The bear... the fire... it must be a mess outside. But luckily, things didn't get worse.

speaker: Eve
content: I'm sorry, ${PlayerName}. I must've caused you a lot of trouble.

speaker: Eve
content: Apart from my family members, you are truly the nicest person I've ever met.

speaker: Eve
content: You didn't abandon me, nor did you deceive me for ulterior motives.

speaker: Eve
content: The future you offered is so beautiful. I was almost convinced.

speaker: Eve
content: But then I remembered, I've heard about such a beautiful future many, many times...

speaker: Eve
content: I'm sorry I didn't tell you.

speaker: Eve
content: I've already secretly gone to see the world outside the factory.

speaker: Eve
content: Turns out, it's all fake, even faker than the toy families pretending to be real. Turns out...

speaker: Eve
content: ...everyone is a liar.

speaker: Eve
content: Loyal friends, loving family members, the kindness of the world... none of these exist outside.

speaker: Eve
content: Maybe I really could meet new people and start a new life.

speaker: Eve
content: It's strange. As opposed to those small "possibilities" that haven't happened yet, I prefer the old, prefer to stay in place, prefer liars...
Eve withdraws all her Mania power. In the sea of fire in the warehouse, toys fall one by one from the giant bear and disperse to finally reveal the girl beneath the monster.
With her back turned to you, she is struggling to maneuver her wheelchair into the depths of the fire.
You recall what Eureka said about how to resolve the crisis in the simplest way: if the creator is gone, her wish and creations will all disappear.
Amidst the raging fire, your mouth is dry and your voice is hoarse, making it hard to speak.
But you still drag your heavy feet, trying to walk through the chaotic warehouse in fire and get closer to Eve.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Wait... hold on! There must be another way...

speaker: Eve
content: Things are fine the way they are now.

speaker: Eve
content: It's swallowing my obsession of staying here forever. I can't let go of this obsession, but I can let go of myself.

speaker: Eve
content: This is fine. This way, everyone can escape. You have friends, family, hopes, and a future too, right? Go find them, I'm fine. After all, I never really had anything...

speaker: Eve
content: This time, I can truly reunite with my family.
The fire is spreading faster than Mania. In an instant, a wave of heat forms an invisible barrier between you two.
The silhouette in the fire doesn't look back. She stares at the ceiling, lit red by the fire, and cheerily hums a tune.
Rescue seems to have arrived. The shouts of the rescuers and those fleeing drown out Eve's voice. You try but fail to make out what Eve is humming.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: There must be another way to resolve this Mania crisis! Just come out with me first!
As the flames inch closer, spreading to Eve's skirt and hair, she remains motionless.
That figure keeps repeating an answer you've never anticipated...
She doesn't want to leave, not just out of nostalgia, but also because she's seen the outside world.

speaker: Eve
content: It's been a long time since someone cared about me and talked to me this much.

speaker: Eve
content: You should be careful, too. The fire is hot. When it burns you... it hurts.
She parks her wheelchair in the deepest spot of the warehouse and leans back in exhaustion.

speaker: Eve
content: Please tell your friend... that I thank her for liking my toys...

speaker: Eve
content: But I won't be making toys anymore.

speaker: Eve
content: This time, we can truly stay together...

speaker: Eve
content: I'm going home.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No... Eve!!!

The fire completely engulfs the surroundings, and you can no longer see Eve. In the scorching, twisted air, you seem to see familiar toys jump into the sea of fire together: a screaming chicken, a rubber ball, a puppy, a doll, a nesting doll...
All the anomalies created by Eve have already been reversed. Then those who just jumped into the sea of fire were... You want to shout something, but a fiery wave rushes into your mouth and nose.
Amidst the sound of burnt shelves falling over, the stubborn ruin of the Buonanotte Factory finally collapses into the fire. Now, you finally hear the soft humming clearly.
Sleep, Eve...
Tomorrow is another day...
Good night...
Buonanotte.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, the injured are being accounted for and treated one by one.

speaker: Nightingale
content: The fire was quite intense. Right now... we still haven't found the Sinners you mentioned.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You found neither Eve nor Oliver?

speaker: Nightingale
content: No. We can only continue the search after the disaster is under control.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: All right... Have you been up all night and waiting outside the factory?

speaker: Nightingale
content: I firmly believed that Chief would come out safely.
Having inhaled some smoke, you are currently resting on a rock outside the factory. The sky outside has become vividly bright by now.

In front of you, the victims of this accident are being transported away one by one on stretchers. They are digesting the chaotic time difference and information in fear and confusion. Of course, there are also a few who are particularly excited.

speaker: Pepper
content: See! I told you that Pepper is the biggest badass in DisCity!

speaker: Pepper
content: I really made a big hullabaloo this time! I brought so many people out!

speaker: Pepper
content: They were scared to death when they saw that Pepper and Eureka were both Sinners!

speaker: Pepper
content: Chief, Chief! Aside from the factory, I found another fun place! Wanna go next time? Let's go together! Please, please~
The blonde girl is energetically waving her hands from the stretcher.

speaker: Eureka
content: Pepper says she's fine, but it's better to have her checked out.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Thank you. You've protected her well.
Shaking her head with a smile, her gaze follows Pepper as she gets loaded onto the ambulance.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, we can leave the rest to the fire crew and rescue team. The 9th Agency is waiting for your report on this incident. We should go back.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Okay.
You take another look at the factory. The fire shows no signs of diminishing.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Let's go.

You get up and dust yourself off. The solid touch reminds you once again that you're no longer a rag doll. So many things have happened in this one night. You feel a bit dazed as you get in the car and leave with Nightingale and Eureka.

speaker: Scavenger
content: How wonderful it would have been if everyone turned into toys. Victory was in sight. Yet the worst choice was made.

The smoke from the factory blankets the sky above the Rust for a long, long time. It is said to be the most stubborn fire ever faced by DisCity's fire department. In the end, it finally got extinguished by a sudden downpour.

speaker: Oliver
content: Pretty lady, Oliver just escaped from a terrible fire and is now penniless... can you take me in?

Despite all the commotion, neither Eastside nor Syndicate pays any attention. The story of Eve's toy factory is just another stone thrown into the sea. It makes no splash, no sound, and sinks to the bottom of the sea just like countless other stones.

speaker: Sheriff
content: Hey! Come here, there's someone under this slab!

speaker: Sheriff
content: It's a girl... She seems to be alive!

speaker: Bass
content: Benna! You... you broke the machine again!

speaker: Bass
content: Everyone will think Bass did it! They will blame Bass again!

speaker: Bass
content: It's Bass's fault! Bass is no good!

speaker: Benna
content: Child... calm down. It's nothing big, hehe...

speaker: Bass
content: Benna! Fix it together!

speaker: Benna
content: Oh? You want Benna to come fix it? I'll go call him for you.

speaker: Bass
content: You forgot again! You are Benna.

speaker: Benna
content: Oh... haha, right. What a lousy memory I have.

speaker: Benna
content: Okay, let's fix it together... Let me see...

speaker: Eve
content: I'll do it.

speaker: Bass
content: Eve!

speaker: Eve
content: I know, it's not Bass's fault. It's not Benna's fault either.

speaker: Eve
content: Here, look... this part is rusty and enlarged, and all the parts behind it are misplaced. That's why the circuit broke. We just need to replace them.

speaker: Bass
content: Eve is amazing! Applause!

speaker: Bass
content: With Eve, the toy factory will get better and better!

speaker: Eve
content: I am of no help... I'm just a burden to my mom and dad.

speaker: Benna
content: Who would consider their own child a burden... Shanna is talking nonsense again.

speaker: Benna
content: Grandpa never considered Shanna a burden. Grandpa will leave all his treasures to Shanna.

speaker: Bass
content: ...Benna thinks Eve is his granddaughter again! Even dumber than Bass.

speaker: Bass
content: Eve is Eve! She's the smartest person in this toy factory!

speaker: Bass
content: When Eve grows up, she will design a lot of amazing toys, right?

speaker: Eve
content: Me? I don't know...

speaker: Eve
content: I drew some designs, but it looks like mom and dad are very busy, so I won't show them. I don't want to bother them.

speaker: Benna
content: Then give it to Grandpa. I'm happy with anything Shanna does.

speaker: Bass
content: Eve's toys will definitely be awesome! Bass believes that! Bass wants to be the first to play!

speaker: Eve
content: No problem. Bass will be the first one to play with them.

speaker: Bass
content: Then Bass wants a screaming chicken! Cluck, cluck, cluck... Like in that cartoon! Tall and strong! To protect! Eve!

speaker: Eve
content: What about Benna? What kind of toy do you like?

speaker: Benna
content: Um... I don't really know...

speaker: Eve
content: Hmm... Then think of one for Shanna? What does Shanna like?

speaker: Benna
content: A rubber ball! She loves playing with one... I remember it clearly!

speaker: Eve
content: Okay, I'll make them for you guys.

speaker: Bass
content: Let's make a pinky promise.

speaker: Eve
content: It's a promise.

speaker: Eve
content: Whose puppy are you? Why are you here?

speaker: Puppy
content: Whimper whimper...

speaker: Eve
content: You still have a collar... You must have an owner, right? Where's your owner?

speaker: Puppy
content: Whimper...

speaker: Eve
content: I see... they left you here.

speaker: Eve
content: Would you like to come with me?

speaker: Puppy
content: Woof!

speaker: Eve
content: You understand everything! What a smart puppy...

speaker: Eve
content: Look at you, all skin and bones... I'll call you Bone, okay?

speaker: Bone
content: Woof, woof!

speaker: Eve
content: I don't know your real birthday, so can we make today, the day I found you, your birthday?

speaker: Bone
content: Woof, woof, woof!

speaker: Eve
content: Good. Let's have Maresa take you for a bath first, then get Polly to make you some beautiful new clothes.

speaker: Eve
content: From now on, Bone is a clean and healthy puppy, a member of the toy factory... and a member of our family.

speaker: Eve
content: Let Bass find you something delicious, and Benna can take you for a walk, okay?

speaker: Bone
content: Woof...

speaker: Eve
content: Why are you unhappy again?

speaker: Eve
content: Me? I can't take you for a walk...

speaker: Eve
content: As you can see, I need a wheelchair to move.

speaker: Eve
content: You want wheels, too? So that we can go together?

speaker: Bone
content: Woof!

speaker: Eve
content: Silly, I'm just teasing you. What's so good about wheels? I'm the one who envies you...

speaker: Eve
content: I've tried many times, but still can't stand up. I've caused a lot of trouble for my parents...

speaker: Eve
content: Bone...

speaker: Bone
content: Purr?

speaker: Eve
content: I... I want to take you for a walk, too. I want... to try standing up again.

speaker: Bone
content: Woof! Woof, woof! Woof, woof, woof, woof, woof, woof!

speaker: Eve
content: Hahaha, all right, all right. So much drool.

speaker: Eve
content: So close... so close... Ah!!!

speaker: Polly
content: Eve! How did you fall?

speaker: Polly
content: You can call us if you need something.

speaker: Eve
content: I want to stand up. I got very close to doing it just now.

speaker: Polly
content: Why do you want to do that all of a sudden? Did the factory bosses blame you again?

speaker: Eve
content: Emm... No... Mom and Dad are probably quite busy lately. I haven't talked to them for a long time.

speaker: Eve
content: This is something I want to do for myself.

speaker: Eve
content: I always hear you say that it's great outside. Bass says you can make a lot of friends out there, and Benna always mentions his family.

speaker: Eve
content: After hearing so much, I want to see for myself. And...

speaker: Eve
content: I promised Bone I will stand up and take it for a walk.

speaker: Polly
content: Eve...

speaker: Eve
content: Polly, how come you rarely talk about your life outside? Is it as good as they say?

speaker: Eve
content: Your family... Are they as busy as my mom and dad?

speaker: Polly
content: ...Yes, just like they said, it's great outside. My mom and dad... are also great.

speaker: Polly
content: Right. Here, take this as a commemorative gift for the first day of Eve's recovery plan!

speaker: Eve
content: Ah, this doll! Where did you find it? I used to like her a lot.

speaker: Polly
content: There was a piece missing from her face. She wasn't that pretty anymore... just like me.

speaker: Polly
content: You hid her because you didn't want me to be sad when I saw her. I know.

speaker: Polly
content: But look, I fixed her with my sewing skills. As good as new!

speaker: Polly
content: The doll is fixed so there's no need to hide it... Everything will get better.

speaker: Eve
content: Yes... My legs, and Polly's face, will all get better!

speaker: Eve
content: Polly deserves the prettiest, most perfect doll.

speaker: Polly
content: The factory... will get better too, right...?

speaker: Eve
content: Hmm?

speaker: Polly
content: Nothing. It's not important anymore.

speaker: Polly
content: The most important thing right now is to help Eve stand up!

speaker: Maresa
content: Are you all eavesdropping? Have you finished your work? Quit slacking off! Don't you know what the factory is going through right now?

speaker: Benna
content: Oh right... What are we doing here again?

speaker: Bass
content: Dumb Benna! To see Eve! Eve wants to stand up! To stand up!

speaker: Bone
content: Woof!

speaker: Polly
content: Shh... keep it down, don't disturb her.

speaker: Maresa
content: Eve's found something she wants to work hard for... Good for her.

speaker: Maresa
content: You guys didn't tell her about the factory, did you?

speaker: Bass
content: Of course not! Bass is smart! Bass didn't say anything!

speaker: Polly
content: The bosses actually care about Eve a lot, right? They have been taking on such a big burden in silence.

speaker: Benna
content: After all, she's their child...

speaker: Bone
content: Mmmph!

speaker: Polly
content: Oh no, Mr. Benna, you said that word again...

speaker: Benna
content: What word, I don't remember...

speaker: Bass
content: Child! Child! You can't mention child! Can't mention child in front of Maresa!

speaker: Polly
content: ...Bass, stop talking!

speaker: Maresa
content: Child... child...

speaker: Maresa
content: My child, have you seen my child? He was kidnapped! Have you seen him?

speaker: Maresa
content: Child, child...

speaker: Polly
content: Maresa, calm down, it's us... Bass, go get the medicine!

speaker: Bass
content: Run, Bass! Run, Bass!

speaker: Maresa
content: Child, my child, my child...

speaker: Eve
content: What happened? Why are you all gathered here?

speaker: Polly
content: Nothing. Benna mentioned that word again. Bass went to get the medicine.

speaker: Eve
content: But... Bass is back already.

speaker: Polly
content: So soon? Where's Maresa's medicine?

speaker: Bass
content: No medicine! There are bad guys, bad guys! Run, Eve!!!

speaker: Bone
content: Woof... woof! Woof woof woof woof!
In the vast, expansive white fog, the screaming chicken named Bass is standing in place.
He seems to have been waiting for you to return here all along.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Did you come to show me your memories?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: After seeing them, will I have the answer to solve everything?
He doesn't answer, but turns around and runs into the depths of the white fog. You can only follow.
However, at the end of the white fog, you see a scene filled with blood, gun smoke, and contamination.

speaker: Bass
content: Bad guys! There are bad guys! Run, Eve!!!

speaker: Eve
content: Huh? What happened?

speaker: Bass
content: Can't tell Eve! The factory is in huge debt! It's getting worse! Gangsters are coming for money! But we can't tell Eve!

speaker: Eve
content: The factory... I'm also a member of the factory. Why didn't you tell me...

speaker: Bass
content: Ahhhh! Disaster! Eve found out!

speaker: Eve
content: Where are the debt collectors? ...Let go of me, Maresa.

speaker: Maresa
content: You can't go! Child... I can't lose another child...

speaker: Polly
content: That's right! We can fix this! Everything will get better!

speaker: Polly
content: Listen, leave this place! It's safe outside!

speaker: Benna
content: Shanna, be good. Grandpa will buy you a ball to play with...

speaker: Eve
content: Everyone...

speaker: Bass
content: Go, Benna! Beat the bad guys! They've got huge, huge guns! Purple ones! With black smoke!

speaker: Benna
content: There are times when this old man is useful too...

speaker: Bone
content: Woof, woof, woof!

speaker: Benna
content: Good boy, Bone. You come with us, too.

speaker: Polly
content: Eve, leave this to us! You can escape from the back door of the depot!

speaker: Polly
content: Say hello to my mom, dad and little brother for me.

speaker: Eve
content: Polly, wait! Let go of me! Put me down!

speaker: Maresa
content: No! This time, I must keep an eye on my child!

speaker: Eve
content: Wake up, Maresa. I'm not your child!

speaker: Maresa
content: Yes, you are! I'm wide awake... You're all my children!

speaker: Maresa
content: Go, remember to find him for me...

speaker: Eve
content: ...Nooo...
The memories of the toy family members reach their end. The explosion of mania weapons devour everything.
You find yourself back in the white fog, but Bass is nowhere to be seen.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Are these Eve's memories? What should I do?
As you ask, you feel your way through the white fog.
From afar, you see several unfamiliar figures who seem to be gathered together, chatting about something.

speaker: Maresa
content: Eve has been working very hard these years to keep all these things as they are...

speaker: Bass
content: Dummy Eve. Eve is a dummy! Locking herself in the toy factory!

speaker: Polly
content: But it's already happened... Time won't really stop. Bone won't have another birthday.

speaker: Bone
content: Whimper...

speaker: Maresa
content: We're the ones who held her back, right? She must know that we can't bear to lose her.

speaker: Benna
content: Yes... Eve is the smartest child I've ever met...

speaker: Bone
content: Woof!

speaker: Polly
content: Benna! You said that word again!

speaker: Bass
content: Child! Child! Child!

speaker: Maresa
content: No matter what kind of injustice or discomfort she encountered, she would boldly express her feelings and then bravely resist.

speaker: Maresa
content: We've all... moved on.

speaker: Polly
content: Eve will surely move on too!

speaker: Polly
content: There are many things ahead of her that we have never seen or experienced.

speaker: Bass
content: Quick! Make a wish! The power of wishes! ${PlayerName} said so!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Me?

It's as if there is a thick wall between you and them. No one notices you approaching, and no one pays you any attention. They act as if they're simply sitting on the floor of their home, casually chatting amongst themselves.

speaker: Polly
content: Right! Bass is so smart!

speaker: Polly
content: I wish that in my next life, I'll meet Eve again! By then, we will be complete, healthy and well.

speaker: Benna
content: Next life, huh... It feels so far away, yet so near...

speaker: Bass
content: Benna, make a wish too!

speaker: Benna
content: All right. Then I wish that in this life, Eve can leave the factory, and live a long, happy and peaceful life.

speaker: Bass
content: You're not wishing for Shanna? Benna forgot again!

speaker: Benna
content: How could I forget? The one who chatted with me... the one who I watched grow up... is Eve.

speaker: Bass
content: Bass hope Eve can make new friends! Friends smarter than Bass, so Eve won't be troubled! If Eve is happy, Bass is happy!

speaker: Bone
content: Woof, woof! Woof, woof, woof, woof!

speaker: Polly
content: Does Bone want to make a wish too?

speaker: Maresa
content: Bone still remembers its promise with Eve.

speaker: Maresa
content: It wishes that it can go for a walk with Eve... and be Eve's puppy again.

speaker: Polly
content: Go for a walk... That sounds nice. It'd be great if we could all go together.

speaker: Maresa
content: Then let me make the last wish. I hope, all our wishes can come true.

speaker: Maresa
content: Let ${PlayerName} bear witness to these wishes coming true on our behalf. He's the only one around here who can see things through to the end.
female_content: Let ${PlayerName} bear witness to these wishes coming true on our behalf. She's the only one around here who can see things through to the end.

content: Everyone, including Bone, suddenly turns to look at you. Even though their faces are blurry, you can clearly sense their smiles.
Then, an aged group photo ends up in your palm.

speaker: All the Toys
content: Please, take her away from here.
The photo in your hand emits a warmth that doesn't belong to this time and space.

options: Don't worry, I will. You have my words.

content:
Beneath the ocean's surface lies the deep sea, and similarly, beneath the glamor of this city lies its dark side—<color=#fb9259>the DisCity dark web</color>, known as <color=#fb9259>DisMyth</color>.

On DisMyth, users are anonymous, untraceable, and unmonitored by law; it resembles both the chaotic high seas and a lawless swamp teeming with evil.

Malice thrives in the shadows here, concealed from the light and eager to devour the surface.

This place is a jungle, where the rules and justice under the sunlight become laughable, and dark trends often defy the current of era. For instance...
Although BR-002 has ended and the West District's reconstruction proceeds smoothly, many "heroes" face mysterious attacks. Even a certain Chief involved in the investigation has not been spared.

01:23 a.m., February 26, N.F. 114.
As the special task force returns to the MBCC.

speaker: Nightingale
content: All units, head to Chief's last known signal location now! Support team, cover every entrance and exit of District 14. Catch them at all costs!

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief! Can you hear me?! Please respond!
She calls out desperately but hears no response from the other end of the communicator.

speaker: Nightingale
content: What about the ground-tracking bots? Get all of them online now, even the destroyed ones. I need visuals!
Amid the sounds of responses and typing, a burst of static flickers across the screen, then, the last footage captured by a robot is displayed before the entire room.
Under the night sky, a tall woman effortlessly carries the unconscious Chief over her shoulder.

speaker: Nightingale
content: ...An S-Class Sinner?
Noticing the noise made by the robot, she turns her head to look at it.
Against the moonlight, no one can see her face clearly, but none can forget those calm, deep, and dangerous eyes, and the flash of light from the blade, along with the electrical sparks.

It's been confirmed that the kidnapper is a renowned legendary hitman on DisMyth, known for her speed and discreetness in completing her commissions. There are hardly any records of her online or from the authorities, a testament to her skill and carefulness.

In other words, cases that involve her are particularly challenging to tackle.

We're unable to track the shackles because the connection is too weak, or it might have been deliberately interfered with. As a result, the hitman's location, the identity of her client, and the Chief's whereabouts... are all lost in the depths of the dark web.

speaker: Nightingale
content: ...The shackles are still reacting. Chief won't give up, go find him!
female_content: ...The shackles are still reacting. Chief won't give up, go find her!

speaker: Nightingale
content: He must still be fighting.
female_content: She must still be fighting.

content: [Black Screen]

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...The door, it was this way... Ah!
In the darkness, you fall to the ground.
You sigh irritably as you feel the obstacles around your feet. After blinking several times to adjust to the darkness, you finally see…

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Where did these clothes come from?!
Bearing the pain in your knees, you struggle to sit up and untangle the clothes and items wrapped around your feet.
This is the third time, the third time today.
Bedroom, kitchen, and then the living room.
It's absolutely normal to have clothes on the floor or to trip over them, and it's completely normal for the light to suddenly go out.
...But to have all these happen together is really testing one's patience!
The power went out?

You finally free yourself from the clothes that tripped you, and approach the living room window with the phone cradled against your shoulder. Through the heavy curtains that are almost pinned in place, you attempt to look outside.
You can vaguely see the flickering lights.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: There's light in the other apartments, only yours has lost power.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Has someone found us?
You lower your voice, asking the person on the other end of the phone.
The other end of the line falls silent, the dragging sound that you have been hearing also stops abruptly.
Ah.
The person on the line lets out a soft "ah" as if she's realized something.
I forgot to pay the bill.

options: Do you remember where you're working today?

content: Yes. Room 1209, Building 2, Syndicate Oldtown District.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So your memory isn't bad, but you forgot to pay the bill anyway...
As you complain, you open the phone directory on the table and search for the number of the electricity provider.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The phone still works. I'll pay the electricity bill. Do you remember the account number? Every house has one.
Yes.
I remember writing the account number on a piece of paper, just in case I forgot.

options: You forgot the number, didn't you?
Do you remember where the paper is?

content: I saw it within the last seven days. It's in the living room.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You want me to find a piece of paper in this junk... I mean, dark room?
You sigh and start searching for the paper in the dark.

Fortunately, she hasn't realized that if you get the account number, you can find the address of this place. In desperate need to know your location, you're diligently searching every corner of the room.
...Even though looking for that "piece of paper" in this huge junkyard is like looking for a needle in a haystack.
It has to be there. I remember seeing it before going out on a gig this week, I even made a mental note to deal with it later.
I don't make mistakes when it comes to commissions.
Is that something to be proud of? That gig she's talking about is probably the one where she kidnapped you. And there she is, explaining so calmly to you, the victim.
Wait... she said this week...
You run to the drying rack. The clothes she was wearing on the day she kidnapped you are hanging there, you rummage through the pockets and find a lump of soggy paper.
What's wrong?
You grit your teeth and tell her that that piece of paper has turned into a pulp by the washing machine.
Well, there's nothing we can do about it then. But don't worry, having the account number or not doesn't really matter now.

Because I'm out of money. The gig you took on today turned out to be a scam again. Those fraudsters said they were recruiting bodyguards, but they were actually luring people there to harvest their organs.
It's common on the dark web, and you've been carefully screening the jobs to avoid traps, but you still got fooled by one that seemed honest and decent.
It goes to show that you're truly just a rookie in these murky waters.
No worries, I took care of them all. They were no match for me.
I saved a few others who got scammed. I'll talk to them first.

options: I didn't expect you would help them.

content: Well, since I saved them, they should pay up. That will make up for the lost commission fee.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If they have to take this kind of job on the dark web, they probably don't have much money, and they must be terrified now...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Don't make it hard for them. Hide and call the police, come back after you make sure those people are okay.
They survived, they can walk on their own.

options: Consider it a job from me.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'll make sweet red bean soup tonight as your payment.
Okay, I'll take it.
That's quick.
There should be a <color=#fb9259>backup generator</color> at home. Look for it. Be careful until I get back.
See you later.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Hm, see you later, <color=#fb9259>Angell</color>.
You hang up and take a moment to organize the current situation in your head.

First, <color=#fb9259>you've been kidnapped</color>. Someone has hired a powerful hitman on DisMyth. Due to how hidden DisMyth is, the MBCC has been unable to locate you, and it'll be even harder to find the mastermind behind all this.

Lucky for you, this formidable hitman currently can't get in touch with her client either. It's been five days, and all she can do is keep you in this secret safe house, which also gives you some valuable time to stay alive.

Secondly, this <color=#fb9259>Angell</color>, the Top Hitman on DisMyth, an S-Class Sinner, the person who managed to break through the MBCC's defenses... seems to be a bit... unusual, casual, and unpredictable sometimes.

By a stroke of luck, or through hard work, you have gained a bit of her trust over these past few days, helping her with the household chores—something she's <color=#fb9259>not entirely</color> good at. This is an opportunity, there's a lot you can do.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Well, the top priority for me right now is to find the backup generator and reconnect to <color=#fb9259>DisMyth</color>.
You clear your head, stand up and walk... only to get tripped by something on the ground again. This time, it's a pillow with its cotton spilling out.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Survive this, you can do it.
You've cleaned up the living room. What should have been done has been completed, and even the ones that didn't need to be done are finished. At least now, the room is no longer a junkyard.

Even though the house owner will turn the place to its original state once she's back, at least for now, you don't have to worry about tripping over some random stuff and falling face first. You lean back in the chair in front of the computer and let out a long sigh.
Based on the progress of the job, you probably still have an hour or two of free time left. Time to get to business.

Unlike the public and stable surface web, the world of DisMyth is like the deep sea. It's a dangerous place where countless unidentified information sources mingle, exchanging intelligence in the dark, forming transient whirlpools of information.

By using Angell's account, known as the "Top Hitman," you've gained access to valuable intelligence from her account history and the contacts seeking her service. Now, as the investigator closest to DisMyth, you have the best chance to rescue yourself.
You note down some of her usual contacts, and those who have requested her services—especially, those after you. Then you purposefully post some garbled codes on DisMyth.
Soon, someone responds in garbled text processed by the same encryption method, initiating an online conversation with you.

[The following messages are decrypted] User_W21: Got the intel. Chief, are you okay? T_T Haven't been harvested or sold off somewhere, right? Are you still in DisCity? We're worrying sick, please take good care of yourself. QwQ You: Not sure where I am, but everything's fine. Let's cut to the chase. It's easy to get exposed when we're not familiar with the dark web. User_W21: Okay. T_T

It must be the action team formed by the MBCC Intelligence Department and the 9th Agency, you're not sure who is involved, but this isn't the time for detailed reports. As long as the codes match up, that's all that matters. You've been posting ciphertext and secretly calling for help for days.

<color=#fb9259>You</color>: The attacks are still going?

<color=#fb9259>User_W21</color>: Yes, even worse after you were captured.
<color=#fb9259>User_W21</color>: Has <color=#fb9259>Fish</color> revealed who hired her yet?

<color=#fb9259>You</color>: No, they haven't got in touch. Her client seems experienced. They're staying under the radar.
<color=#fb9259>You</color>: But thankfully it's a series of cases, not individual ones, finding what these people have in common should really help.

<color=#fb9259>User_W21</color>: Nine is tracking several gangs. Since order has been restored in West District, it's harder for gangs to survive these days. That's why many of them are turning to DisMyth to make a living.
W21 gives Angell a code name, Fish. Nine naturally refers to the 9th Agency. W21 has been refusing to disclose their identity, but you have a feeling it's Wynn.

<color=#fb9259>You</color>: Alright, I'll keep an eye on Fish's regulars. Can't trace IPs on the dark web, but we can try tracking her gigs in real life.

<color=#fb9259>User_W21</color>: It's dangerous!!! Pleeeeaaase stay put and just wait for rescue! You'll scare us to death!! QwQ

<color=#fb9259>You</color>: I'm kidnapped right now, it's better for me to help out than do nothing. I'll try to find the electricity bill account number to help you guys pinpoint my location.
Encrypting and decrypting these messages are quite taxing. You glance at the time, Angell's commission is probably over, she could be back any moment now.

<color=#fb9259>You</color>: Fish will be back soon. Let's call it a day. I'm counting on you guys to set the trap.

<color=#fb9259>User_W21</color>: Please be careful. T_T
You swiftly clear the chat history, eliminating all the evidence. As you're about to log off, you receive one last message in the chatroom.

<color=#fb9259>User_W21</color>: But why would Fish listen to you? She's the one who kidnapped you.

<color=#fb9259>User_W21</color>: Maybe there's something special about you? The shackles? Or perhaps, your charisma...
You pause for a moment and decide not to reply. After deleting all the history, you close the chatroom and return to the commission page.
You don't want to spend too much time pondering on the question Wynn posed right now. And as you're looking to divert your attention...
Ding-dong... the doorbell rings.
Since you got here, the doorbell has barely rung. Angell has her own keys, so she never needs to use it.
You have a bad feeling. As the doorbell rings again and again, you look through the peephole to see who's outside.

speaker: Stranger
content: ...Angell.
Through the peephole, you see a man wearing a baseball cap at the door, you can't make out his face but his malice is palpable, even the case in his hand seems dangerous.
Alarm sets off in your head. Should you pretend no one's home, or just say you don't recognize him? Either way, you can't open this door, otherwise...

speaker: Stranger
content: Heh, your breathing gives you away.
A sharp, loud crash explodes beside your ear! A huge axe narrowly misses your face as it carves a groove into the thick metal door.
You instantly back away as the man keeps hacking at the door with his axe relentlessly. Meanwhile, a mechanical arm emerges from his case and reaches through the gap on the door, searching around.
But as soon as it touches the doorknob, it's yanked away by a tremendous force!

speaker: Stranger
content: It's you?! You... Aahhh!!
Step away from the door.

The cold voice sends shivers down your spine as you comply and step back immediately. Then, a long blade thrusts through and slices down the metal door, the grating sound of metal being cut through and the thug's screams fill the air.
...You recognize this blade. Angell's back, and she's about to use that blade to take that man's life.
The sounds of intense fighting outside gradually die down. You hold your breath, only able to hear your racing heartbeat.

speaker: Angell
content: It's over.

The thick scent of blood enters your nostrils. With her headphones on, Angell stands quietly outside the door, only two steps away from you. At her feet lies the big guy who you just saw through the peephole.

Her black clothes are soaked with the enemy's blood, darkening them further. Splatters of blood mark her cheeks, and droplets drip from the sharp blade she holds. She briefly glances at the body beneath her feet before sheathing the blade and turning her gaze to you.

speaker: Angell
content: I'll take care of this. Just go back inside.
She enters the house, closing the door behind her. The air seems to have gotten colder in an instant.

speaker: Angell
content: Got held up on the way back. Is there still dinner? Has it gone cold?
Complaining over the phone is easy, but now, the person on the other end of the line is standing right in front of you, holding a blood-stained blade...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Haven't started cooking yet. Just about to make the red bean soup you asked for.

speaker: Angell
content: That's great. I like that soup, it'd be a shame if it's gone cold.
She returns to her room, closing the door behind her. You hear the music coming from her headphones as she passes by you this time.
Days are passing by, living this lie, Not knowing what we're looking for. Gray, these walls are gray and there's no sky. There is no hope, there is no soar. I know somewhere there must be more.
You remember this song.
You're reminded of that night and the nerve-wracking pressure. If her client hadn't lost contact, you would have been killed by that very blade, during the same song.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What will you do with me?

speaker: Angell
content: Nothing. You keep staying here.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Until your client contacts you? When will that be? Do we just keep waiting until they make contact?

speaker: Angell
content: Yes.

speaker: Angell
content: Any other questions?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No, that's all.
You return to the kitchen.
You do have another question, one that someone has asked you, and you've asked her.
User_W21: Why would Fish listen to you? Maybe there's something special about you?
Yes, you've earned her trust, and you take care of the chores and handpick orders for her. Yet, you have no idea why she trusts you.
You dive into your memories to find the day when things began to change...

It was the third day after you were kidnapped, and you were starving. You sneaked into the kitchen in the early morning, only to be caught red-handed by your "roommate" as you were about to pick up a kitchen knife.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...I was just looking for something to eat. I didn't mean to grab this.
She stares at you in silence.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...I haven't eaten for two days. I'm really hungry.
After a silence that feels like a lifetime, she finally speaks.

speaker: Angell
content: I'm hungry too.

speaker: Angell
content: Do you cook?
You've only ever made instant noodles at the Bureau, but you feel it's best to keep that to yourself.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I do. What would you like?

speaker: Angell
content: Red bean soup.

speaker: Angell
content: I like hot red bean soup.

speaker: Angell
content: Thank you.

It was from that moment things began to change. You started with small tasks like cooking and cleaning, slowly making your way into her life while cautiously testing her limits. Eventually, you began picking orders for her, but you never dropped your guard.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Are you sure you want my help? I am your captive, after all.
Angell answers without even looking up.

speaker: Angell
content: I'm not losing anything here. I took the job just to make a living.

speaker: Angell
content: And nothing you do could pose a threat to me.
But when it comes to either waiting out the danger or risking it, you always choose the latter.
The hour hand of the clock ticks past the "12" again, traveling towards the "1."
She didn't answer her phone. There's no response from DisMyth, and no news from the MBCC. You're fighting the urge to contact her again, and choose to wait.

She often can't answer the phone while on a job, but she always messages you afterward to check in with you. This complete loss of contact, however, is certainly unusual, especially since today's commission isn't challenging at all.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: She really doesn't worry about me running away at all.
Sitting in the empty room, countless imaginations start to run wild in your mind.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Did she run into a fake job again? Maybe she got attacked? Or, did she finally get in touch with the client? Then...
Have you been handed over? Is this place still safe?
The ticking of the clock gets louder, echoing, filling the whole room. For a moment, you seem to hear someone knocking on the door, and some unsettling words...

speaker: Mysterious Killer
content: Heh, your breathing gives you away.

You unconsciously hold your breath. You've never experienced something like this before, not in the MBCC. Safe houses are never for people who feel safe. This is a hitman's "home." It's on the edge of society, inside the world of the dark web.

Is someone standing outside the door, spying on you through the peephole? The blackout curtain shields the window completely, but you can't shake the feeling that someone might be lurking behind it, or a sniper rifle might be aiming at you from afar. In a daze, you hear cold, determined footsteps approaching from the corridor outside.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: These footsteps...

You get up, and upon reaching the door, you hold and twist the doorknob you've never touched before. The force from the other side opens the door, and you see the cause of all your troubling thoughts standing at the door, staring at you.

The headphone wire stretches from her ears to her pocket. Over her shoulder hangs a black bag with her blade tucked inside, and she holds a heavy-looking plastic bag in her hand. Her eyes are locked on your hand on the doorknob.

speaker: Angell
content: Where are you going?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I heard you walking down the hallway, so I came to check.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: We just got attacked. I was really worried something went wrong again.
You explain in an exceptionally calm way. She meets your gaze, staring at you for a while before looking away.

speaker: Angell
content: No need to worry now, I'm back.
She turns sideways to enter the door, and walks straight to the dining table to set down the plastic bag.
Inside the bag, there's a large bottle of orange soda and neatly stacked takeout boxes, which completely cover the table when spread out.

speaker: Angell
content: Care for some takeout?
Days are passing by, living this lie, Not knowing what we're looking for. Gray, these walls are gray and there's no sky. There is no hope, there is no soar. I know somewhere there must be more.
The headphones Angell took off are beside her hand, still playing that song.

After opening the lids and pouring the drinks, you take a seat across from her. The table is covered with steaming, appetizing dishes. Now that she's back, a wave of relief washes over you, quickly followed by hunger, so you start eating.
But Angell just looks at you, without even a bowl in front of her, as if all of the food were just for you.

speaker: Angell
content: I didn't call you back earlier, sorry.
That's quite unexpected. You let Angell continue without interrupting her.

speaker: Angell
content: According to your plan for today, I went to that restaurant to help the owner deal with a few thugs asking for protection money.

options: And the owner was really thankful?

speaker: Angell
content: No, she paid me to do a job, simple as that. She was even a bit scared of me at first.

speaker: Angell
content: But I ran into someone there... It was one of the people I saved from the organ harvesting group a few days ago.

speaker: Angell
content: He ran over crying after recognizing me, shaking my hands and calling me a hero. It caused quite a scene in the restaurant, but the owner seemed happy, and she insisted I stay a bit longer. We ended up talking for a long time.
Angell gently twirls the glass in her hand, staring blankly as tiny bubbles rise from the bottom of the orange liquid. They reach the surface and pop, the sound almost imperceptible.

speaker: Angell
content: A lot. That guy used to be a gang errand boy. It took him really long before he decided to finally look for a decent job. But out of habit, he went on the dark web to hunt for jobs and got scammed.

speaker: Angell
content: Remember you asked me to call the police? I made sure he didn't mention me and just said he busted their hideout on his own. Because of that, the sheriff recommended him for a job at the new mine.

speaker: Angell
content: He passed the interview, and he's starting next week. He wants to eat more to bulk up in the meantime.

speaker: Angell
content: As for the restaurant owner, she was very scared of me at first because the dark web's full of dangerous people. She said she would never have posted that job if there was any other option, and she didn't think anyone would accept it with such low pay.

speaker: Angell
content: Later on, she was really grateful and kept apologizing to me. She told me she would recommend the dark web to her friends and family, and asked for my contact for future gigs.

speaker: Angell
content: When she heard I hadn't been eating well lately, she handed me all the food she just cooked and called it a deposit.
The food in your mouth suddenly doesn't taste as good.

Not eating well? True, you might have made too little for the two of you, but you've been cooking for her for several days in a row. Even folks at the MBCC don't get this treatment. Besides, doesn't she like the red bean soup?

speaker: Angell
content: What's wrong?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Nothing.

options: Didn't expect you to be so talkative.

speaker: Angell
content: Talkative? Not really. I've been alone all this time, there's not much to talk about.

speaker: Angell
content: I just thought you should know.

speaker: Angell
content: You were the one who took the job from the restaurant owner, the one who asked me to call the police and save those people. You're the one who deserves their gratitude and gifts, I should pass them on to you.

options: You were the one who actually helped them.

speaker: Angell
content: I only see those "big orders" that come my way. Honestly, I don't care about anything else besides my gigs.

speaker: Angell
content: To me, killing or helping people is the same, they're all just jobs. There's no need to thank me.

speaker: Angell
content: Yeah.

speaker: Angell
content: There were a few seconds of dead air, and then everybody laughed.

speaker: Angell
content: Some say I'm cool, some say I'm funny, and others think I should write novels or become an actress.

You try to keep a straight face but end up laughing anyway. She looks at you with a hint of resignation, probably the exact expression she had in the restaurant. It's quite amusing. You look at her, and remark…
She lowers her head, probably lost in thought. You realize that Angell isn't too hard to read; in fact, she often wears her heart on her sleeve.

speaker: Angell
content: Maybe.

speaker: Angell
content: It's been a long time since anyone worried about me or thanked me. It's not a bad feeling.

speaker: Angell
content: And to be able to help someone, to send them back into the sunlight... feels good.

Her gaze falls on the soda in her hand, and orange light dances on the tablecloth as she gently swirls the glass. It's like she's savoring the moment, or perhaps contemplating, until she finally looks up at you.
You see a faint smile on that usually stern face.

speaker: Angell
content: So, thank you, ${PlayerName}, for letting me feel the warmth I haven't felt in a long time.
You two sit quietly. Only the music from the headphones flows in the air.
Days are passing by, living this lie, Not knowing what we're looking for. Gray, these walls are gray and there's no sky. There is no hope, there is no soar. I know somewhere there must be more.

This is the edge of society, the dark web's domain, a temporary safe house of a hitman that's not really safe. Apart from her name, identity, and the fact that you're on opposing sides, you know nothing about this person.
Don't let your guard down... you think to yourself, looking at the glass of orange soda in her hand, unsure of how to respond.
In the end, you raise your glass.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Here's to everyone feeling warmth under the sun.
Angell smiles and raises her glass to clink against yours, making a crisp sound.
The sound of rustling wakes you up from a chaotic dream.
The noise directs your gaze to the front door—it's wide open. You instantly jolt awake, spring up from the couch and cautiously approach the door.
As you get closer to the front door, the sound of scrubbing grows clearer. The sharp yet familiar smell of cleaner wafts towards you, and it somehow reassures you.
At the door, you see Angell tossing a cloth stained with dark red spots into a black trash bag.
She strides to the end of the hallway, opens the trash chute door, and tosses the bag in with one hand. Moments later, a thud of the heavy object landing echoes up the chute.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Someone was here again?

speaker: Angell
content: Yes. It's all taken care of, you can go back to sleep.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It's fine. It's time to get up anyway.
Angell checks the time, then sheathes her blade and tucks it into the bag by the door before slinging it over her shoulder.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're heading out now? I haven't sorted out the orders yet.

speaker: Angell
content: Yeah, there's something I need to deal with. I'll probably go out for the next few days.

options: Did you take on other gigs?

content: Angell glances at you, knowing full well what you mean by "other gigs," but she shakes her head.

speaker: Angell
content: No, just something personal.

speaker: Angell
content: I only take the gigs you pick.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I see, alright then.
You nod, hesitating about what to ask. In the meantime, she opens the door and heads out.

speaker: Angell
content: I'll be back for dinner.
Angel has been coming home later and later over the past few days, giving you more time to gather information on DisMyth while you wait for her.

DisMyth has been in an uproar for the past two days, with comments ranging from "That MBCC scum is finally dead!" to "That old fox from Minos is playing dead!" Occasionally, bounties are placed on your head; none of them small, some hefty enough to cover this house's electricity for 100 years.

As the chaos on DisMyth begins to subside, and the clock strikes pass three, you finally hear familiar footsteps—she's back. You swiftly erase your browsing history, act as if everything is normal, and greet her as she enters.
Bang!

Your greeting is cut short. Angell tosses her bag on the floor and heavily sinks into the couch. The mood of the apartment, with her return, suddenly becomes solemn, as if this isn't her home but a scene of an assassination mission.

speaker: Angell
content: I'm good, not hungry. Go to sleep, sorry for waking you.
She doesn't even realize you're wide awake waiting for her.
Angell sits in silence, her eyes tightly shut. Her arms crossed in front of her chest, holding the blade. She remains motionless for a few minutes, as if she's fallen asleep.
You glance around, grab a blanket on the couch, and approach her from behind. Before your hand touches her shoulder, her blade suddenly unsheathes.

speaker: Angell
content: ...What are you doing?

A chill runs down your spine. This is the person who "kidnapped" you over a week ago. Unlike that time when she was cleaning the doorway, you can smell the metallic scent even though there's no blood.

Looks like she brought work home. It's probably not about the jobs you picked, but the "personal" stuff she mentioned. She didn't tell you about it when you asked yesterday, which means her lips are sealed.
Now, she does look like someone from another world, cold and distant, driven only by her killing instinct... but you've seen this side of her too.

options: I just want to give you the blanket. Do you want to lie down?

speaker: Angell
content: ...It's okay, I don't want to sleep. I'm just resting for a bit.

options: Should we stay on guard? Is there danger nearby?

content: Or did you think I was about to do something to you? You surely don't think I'm capable of killing you, do you?
Angell slightly tilts her head, looking at you, or perhaps something else. But soon, she slowly puts away the blade, and lets out a sigh. She seems a bit more relaxed, showing a hint of fatigue.

speaker: Angell
content: Sorry, I didn't mean to do that.
Maybe it's just because you're too tired. Relax, you're home now.

Before you can finish, that metallic scent hits you again. Looking down, you notice a deep gash across Angell's arm. The sleeve has been cut open, revealing the crimson flesh that sticks to the tattered leather. The cut is probably so deep that the bone could be seen; it's a ghastly sight.

speaker: Angell
content: Oh, right. Just a scratch, it's okay.
What happened?

speaker: Angell
content: I forgot. I'm used to it, it'll be fine after some sleep. Goodnight.
You're not too slow to pick up the smell of blood, but her calm demeanor makes it seem like she's not the wounded one, making the sight even more painful to look at.
You take a good look at her. She looks pale, and she's speaking much less than usual. Did she lose too much blood?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I did the laundry today, go change into something comfy. Let me tend to your wound afterward.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This is too painful to look at... Do we have a first aid kit here?
Angell nods and gets up with your help. She goes into the locked door, and comes out again after a while.
She's changed into her nightwear. As she walks out, she lifts the sleeve to wrap it around the wound a couple of times, and tucks it in to secure it, turning the sleek silk into a makeshift bandage.
But that's not first aid kit.

It's another mysterious and dangerous world in here. The space is cramped with clutter, and the clothes she just changed out of are scattered on the floor. You quickly pick them up, knowing she could slip on them in her current state as soon as she walks in.

You easily locate the first-aid kit, which is well-stocked but contains many expired items. You sift through and find some antiseptic, cotton balls, and gauze that are still good, and use them to clean her wound.

Under the dim light, she sits on the edge of the bed while you kneel in front of her. The room is filled with the smell of antiseptic. It's so quiet that you can only hear the fizzing sound of the disinfectant as it forms tiny bubbles, prompting you to gasp instinctively.
But Angell has no reaction whatsoever. She said before that her ability makes her senses sharper, but it seems that doesn't include pain.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Do you know any doctors? Or a safe underground clinic?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You should still get it checked. The wound is deep, it might get infected.
Angell looks down at you as you treat the wound, and says slowly.

speaker: Angell
content: Yeah, but he's still in Syndicate. I haven't seen him since the riot. He's not easy to find.

speaker: Angell
content: And I had to get back early. Can't leave you alone at home.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Worried I might run away while you were gone?

speaker: Angell
content: I was worried I'd come back to find you dead.
With the cotton ball in hand, you pause for a moment, then decisively set it aside and switch to gauze.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I can come back to life even if I die, haven't you heard?
She smiles but doesn't respond. The joke is nowhere close to funny, especially since you were carried away by her in plain sight just a few days ago.
You should change the subject.

options: Looks like you also have a place where you can sleep peacefully.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're always on high alert. I thought you wouldn't allow yourself to relax and fall asleep. You know, in case there might be attacks anytime.

speaker: Angell
content: It's fine. I always dream of something good when I'm asleep. Dying in a beautiful dream actually sounds pretty nice.

speaker: Angell
content: At least that's how I feel when I'm alone...

options: It's late, you should really sleep now.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Forget about the orders tomorrow, and don't take any side jobs. Get some sleep, I'll keep watch.

speaker: Angell
content: Wake me up at 7 a.m., or if something's wrong.
Her voice grows slower and softer, you feel a strand of hair slip down, brushing the back of your hand.
You look up to find her nodding off.

You help her lie down on the bed and take a look around. This is a room of around 10 square meters; the window could be bulletproof, but there are no signs of weapons or surveillance, and no valuable intelligence as far as you can tell. The thick blackout curtains shroud the room in deep, peaceful darkness.
The bed is covered with soft bedding, and from the scattered clothes on the floor, you can tell she's fond of cozy home wear... It seems she truly yearns for undisturbed and restful nights.
The Sinner who kidnapped you is asleep and vulnerable. Now would be a good time to put on the shackles. Standing by the bed, you hesitate for a moment before reaching out your hand.

There's no need to rush. You need this place, and more information. You can take control of the situation and meet your goals without breaking her trust. Any sudden moves could jeopardize everything and put you at risk.
Everything will work out as intended... you might as well wait a bit longer.

The living room windows are, as always, covered with blackout curtains. The computer screen flickers with blue and green lights, casting reflections on the fish tank. As the fish swims gracefully, the reflections ripple in circles.
You sit in front of the computer, elbows on the table, fingers steepled in front of your nose as your eyes remain fixed on the flickering screen.

<color=#fb9259>You</color>: Are you sure he's the client? She's never mentioned him before.

<color=#fb9259>User_W555</color>: Yes, yes! It's him! Woohoo, we won!!!

On the dark side of the internet, deep within the shadows of the city, a group of special agents from the 9th Agency, Public Security Bureau and MBCC are cheerfully celebrating their success in advance with anonymous accounts and encrypted messages.

[The following messages are decrypted] User_W555: It got much easier after we figured out the Syndicate gangs are behind the trouble. We just had to track down those who have some money, and guess who have been keeping their eyes on the new mines like hawks? User_Y342: These attacks happened too close to one another. Someone must be pulling the strings behind the scenes. User_9x9: Hehe, want to know how our old friends from the Underground are doing? User_Y342: Just as we expected, a lot of highly modified Sinners are involved. Guess we'll have some big troubles in the future. User_W555: Let's celebrate first! We finally found Chief after all this time, don't be such a downer!

<color=#fb9259>You</color>: Seems like everyone's efficiency has improved a lot after I was kidnapped.
<color=#fb9259>You</color>: Not having to worry about me has really increased your case-solving speed.

<color=#fb9259>User_W555</color>: Don't say that, Chief! Adjutant Nightingale is here, and she's been working hard to get you back ASAP. She is going to talk your ears off when you're back after you said that. っ°Д°;)っ

<color=#fb9259>User_N049</color>: ...

<color=#fb9259>User_N049</color>: This operation wouldn't have been so smooth without the first-hand intel from the dark web. You even found your own location by yourself, you're the one who's been putting in the most work, Chief.
<color=#fb9259>User_N049</color>: But please don't put yourself in such danger in the future.

<color=#fb9259>You</color>: It was nothing. I just paid the electricity bill and surfed the net a little. You guys are here for me anyway, haha.
<color=#fb9259>User_W555</color>: AHHH, Chief, stop that already!っ°Д°;)っ

<color=#fb9259>User_Y342</color>: The rescue team has located you with the power supply records. We're getting ready to arrest the Sinner. Just give us the order, and we'll spring into action.
<color=#fb9259>User_Y342</color>: You've been fighting on your own for so long, Chief. Hang in there, we will rescue you soon.
You pause for a moment.

<color=#fb9259>You</color>: ...No. There's no need to confront this Sinner.
<color=#fb9259>You</color>: We're after the rats hiding behind DisMyth and the trap is set, making a scene here might just scare them off.
<color=#fb9259>You</color>: I'll deal with Angell and try to bring her back to the Bureau peacefully.

<color=#fb9259>User_Y342</color>: ...Chief, she's a DisMyth hitman who has been threatening your life.

<color=#fb9259>You</color>: It would be even more dangerous to confront her. You all know what I've been doing. Trust me, my method is more likely to work.
<color=#fb9259>You</color>: If it would make you worry less, you can stay about a kilometer away and cover me from there.

<color=#fb9259>You</color>: ...I've seen the dark side of the city, and it's more dangerous than I imagined. But fortunately, I met a hitman with a good heart, and I have you guys, who never gave up on rescuing me.
<color=#fb9259>You</color>: Without you all, I might have walked straight into my grave from the start.

<color=#fb9259>You</color>: Thanks to you, I have the courage to take the risk. I believe in you all, and I want to believe in her too.


<color=#fb9259>Others</color>: Chief...
Seeing the mushy talk has worked, you quickly seize the chance to finalize the operation.

<color=#fb9259>You</color>: Alright, let's not waste time here. Once everything is over, we'll have a proper celebration back at the Bureau.

<color=#fb9259>You</color>: We're entering the final phase of the operation. You guys take care of the clients, I'll deal with this Top Hitman.

<color=#fb9259>User_N049</color>: ...Copy that.
<color=#fb9259>User_W555</color>: Copy that!!(｡・ω・｡) 
<color=#fb9259>User_Y342</color>: Copy that!
<color=#fb9259>User_9x9</color>: Copy that.
It's done. Now it's time to think about your plan—how to persuade her and minimize risks. You are lost in thought, and eventually the screen in front of you dims and goes into sleep mode.

The black screen reflects your face and the small room behind you. This apartment has witnessed an oddly peaceful time shared by two people on opposite sides. But soon, it'll end, as everyone must eventually return to where they belong.
Maybe once this is over, the two of you could start anew together, but there's just something...
...that makes you hesitate slightly as you place the final period on this chapter.
Decisions don't always have to be made solemnly. Today, Angell is on the couch, sharpening her blade as usual. The clear, steady sound of her blade scraping against the whetstone fills the room.
You walk away from the computer, sit across her, and ask as casually as possible.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That gig, the one where you need to kidnap me, is about to expire, isn't it? What happens if your client hasn't contacted you by then?
She continues to sharpen her blade without even lifting her head.

speaker: Angell
content: As per the rules of the dark web, a job without any follow-up within three weeks gets canceled, and I can decide what to do with you.
After managing her dark web account for so long, you already knew about this. Angell's response is expected, so you smoothly continue the conversation.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What will you do with me then?
She tilts her head slightly, as if she's pondering.

speaker: Angell
content: ...It's up to you.

speaker: Angell
content: You can go and do whatever you want. After the job ends, I have no reason to keep you here.
That's such a her thing to say, you chuckle and tease her a little.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're so aloof. Won't you miss me? If I'm gone, there'll be no one to cook for you, no more red bean soup.

speaker: Angell
content: It's just going back to how life was before.

speaker: Angell
content: And besides, compared to red bean soup, don't you have more important things to worry about, Chief of the MBCC?
She pauses, then smiles.

speaker: Angell
content: I'll miss your red bean soup.
Rather than a kidnapper and a captive, you two sound more like roommates who genuinely get along well.
Now's the time. You look at her and begin slowly.
She gazes at you.

speaker: Angell
content: Miss what, exactly?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The time I spent with you.

speaker: Angell
content: As a captive?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: More like your roommate. It's been pretty safe here, I get some freedom, and I have good company who also happens to be an excellent bodyguard—even though sometimes you're the one who needs taking care of.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're not that different from my other friends, except you really can't look after yourself. If I don't keep my eyes on you for one second, things go south in the next. So I'm not quite ready to leave you yet. Wait...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I sound like a mom, don't I?

speaker: Angell
content: My mom is a woman.
female_content: My mom doesn't treat me like this.

content: You chuckle, and her lips curve up too.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What I'm saying is, if there's still no news from your client after three days, and you'll set me free...

options: Will you take a job from me?

speaker: Angell
content: What are you getting at?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I want you to come with me, and keep protecting me.
Angell gives no response. You continue.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I can afford your payment. You'll get a salary, and sometimes even bonuses. Well... I don't know how much you usually get for your big jobs, but you're not someone who lives lavishly.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: We've been managing just fine taking on odd jobs these past few days.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: In my place, you won't have to worry about safety, or spend a fortune on safe houses, weapons, and intel to stay alive...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It should be a lot easier for you.

speaker: Angell
content: ...I am a hitman on the dark web.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Yes, a very skilled and experienced one.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Sometimes you just stumble upon a chance that brings you into the sunlight, where you can meet people who need help or have good intentions.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If my offer doesn't sound bad...
She gazes into your eyes, bringing back memories of the night you first saw her. Her eyes were deep and serene, perfectly adapted to the dark.
Now, as the thick curtains shut out the world and artificial light floods the room, those eyes stare at you again, with a hint of light flickering within them.
After a long while, Angell finally shifts her gaze away and replies softly.

speaker: Angell
content: The job isn't over yet. We'll talk about it later.

speaker: Angell
content: ...When the time comes, I'll think about it.
You turn off the stove and ladle the red bean soup into a bowl. As you turn to carry it out, you see Angell, who has appeared at the kitchen door at some point.
She leans against the door frame and quietly watches you. Seems like she has been standing there for a very long time.
You don't remember her ever doing this before.
Your attempt to tease her feels a bit forced, but she looks away and answers you.

speaker: Angell
content: ...Yeah.
She steps aside to let you through, her voice as calm as ever.

After practicing over these days, your culinary skills have significantly improved. The heat control is just right, making the soup thick and fragrant. A spoonful brings out the delicate sweetness of the red beans.
Angell is concentrated on eating, her face obscured by the white steam rising from the bowl.
Through the veil of steam, you can't see her expression clearly, but you can tell she's carefully savoring the red bean soup.
She takes her time with each spoon, slowly savoring it on her tongue before swallowing it. It's almost like she wants to remember the taste of this soup forever.
You both sit in silence, as if trying to etch this moment into your memory using all your senses. One spoonful after another, she finishes the entire bowl of red bean soup.
She places the spoon back in the bowl and finally lifts her head up.

speaker: Angell
content: I'm taking a day off tomorrow. You're going back to the MBCC, right? I'll give you a ride.
Dawn is approaching. The night sky is tinged with clear blue. The glare of city lights hides the stars, and also your gazes.
Sitting behind Angell, the howling wind fills your ears, forcing you to shout to talk with her.

speaker: Angell
content: You seem to have been to a lot of places.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Not really, and it's all just for work. There are many outstanding adventurers in the MBCC, so I always get to hear interesting travel stories.

speaker: Angell
content: I see.

Just as she finishes her sentence, the motorcycle speeds through the shadows cast by towering buildings. The night sky is now overtaken by the rising sun, its dazzling light forcing you to shield your eyes.
We'll have some good weather today, a sudden thought pops into your head.
A moment later, Angell speaks up again from the front.

speaker: Angell
content: You want to bring me into your life, so... what is your life like?
This seems to be the first time she has asked something about you.
You give it some serious thought.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It's... kinda like when I'm with you.
Your helmet is a bit big, and when you lean forward, it touches Angell's back. As you talk, it vibrates noticeably more than the engine's roar, though only you can feel it.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Receive a mission, complete it, eat, sleep... then work overtime again and again...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Many people out there need help, way more than you can imagine. The daily missions can be exhausting, but we receive a lot of thanks, which can be quite embarrassing at times.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Every day you can sleep soundly without fearing someone might take your life. You can have sweet dreams, and might even find a bowl of hot red bean soup by your bed when you wake up.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Well... we have to fight a lot as well, and occasionally we run into ridiculously strong enemies that are on par with dark web hitmen, but nothing I can't handle.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I might not look strong, but I'm also working hard to protect those important to me.

speaker: Angell
content: That's nice. It's a life that suits you.
She goes quiet for a long time, so long that you think the howling wind has swallowed your words.
Then you finally hear a response.

speaker: Angell
content: I'm good. This is fine.

speaker: Angell
content: It's better we stay like this.
Stay like this... Does she mean speeding along on the bike, living together, or...
As you ponder the meaning of her words, the sounds of the engine and hostile growls come from behind.

speaker: Gangster A
content: Found them! It's that Chief! He's out!
female_content: Found them! It's that Chief! She's out!

speaker: Gangster B
content: Hahaha, catch them!

options: Gangsters slipped through the MBCC's net?

content: You're confused. They are after you, but the gangs involved have already been dealt with. Then who are these people? A force hidden behind the scenes? New enemies?
No, they're already within Angell's alert range. Why hasn't she...

speaker: Angell
content: They probably saw the message I sent.
Her voice isn't loud, but it's very clear. Your mind reels.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What do you mean?

speaker: Angell
content: I posted a message on the dark web, saying: "The MBCC Chief is in my hands. The previous gig has expired. If you want him, come with your price."
female_content: I posted a message on the dark web, saying: "The MBCC Chief is in my hands. The previous gig has expired. If you want her, come with your price."

speaker: Angell
content: Just like I expected, within an hour, tons of sky-high offers came in, dead or alive.

options: When did you do that? Why?

speaker: Angell
content: Shocked? Because none of your spies on the dark web noticed this? Heh, of course...

speaker: Angell
content: On the dark web, top-tier orders, intelligence, and users are all hidden with top-level encryption. Even if you logged into my account, what you saw was only the surface of the dark web. You, your Bureau, and those so-called experts, are just newbies.

speaker: Angell
content: The fact that you believe me shows how little you know about this side of the world.
You had thought about using the shackles as the last resort. But this sudden confession sends a wave of panic through you, slowing down your action.
In that brief moment, the bike skids to a sharp halt, and you almost get thrown off. Instinctively, you hold on tight to the driver, missing your chance to use the shackles.

It's difficult to think clearly at this moment. You only see Angell securing your arms around her waist while drawing her blade with her free hand. Her helmet hides her eyes, but you're certain she's looking at the pursuers.
Her actions contradict her words. At that moment, something she said flashes through your mind.

speaker: Angell
content: It's fine. I always dream of something good when I'm asleep, dying in a beautiful dream actually sounds pretty nice.
You blurt out.

speaker: Choice
options: No, you don't care about their offers.

content: She doesn't respond, but even more memories flash through your mind.

speaker: Angell
content: And to be able to help someone, to send them back into the sunlight... feels good.
