She disappears, leaving only a bullet trail gliding slowly toward its target.
Impressive. You've held out for so long. Go easy on me, will you? You really want to win this much?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Now that I know what power this... this creature has, I can't let it fall into your hands.
Maybe to her, this is just a game, but you know how much effort Moore has put in... It's rare to see her so serious and focused.
Why so serious... I still wish you'd treat it as a game. At least you'll have some fun.
She suddenly raises her hand, and the device you're in flies uncontrollably towards her palm.
You won't stand a chance when push comes to shove.
[Bang... Black screen, shutdown]

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: 000?! What are you doing?! Didn't we agree on a fair showdown? This is cheating!
[Release shackles] XN
You struggle desperately, but to no avail.
Haha, the assassination game is over. You've won. I'll give you your reward later.
The next scene might be a bit brutal, so I won't show it to you for your own good.
There's one thing you're right about. I really need its power. Sorry, Chief.

speaker: Hecate
content: Nightmare!!
(A dragon's howl. A girl stands in front of you, outside the "phone screen")

speaker: Hecate
content: Sorry, Chief, we came late. Leave the battle here to me.

speaker: Hecate
content: Leave the battle here to me.
Hecate's figure looks normal, but you see many strange light specks manifesting in the air, and the entire space has become distorted.
An arrow flies out with a strange noise, exploding into unusual fireworks, followed by a robot-like girly voice.
Two more familiar figures stand in front of you.

speaker: EMP
content: Huh? Chief, why are you inside this phone? What happened?

speaker: EMP
content: Uwaah... Chief, please come back! My voice has got so weird, and the VFX are so weird! My awesome arrow, my heroic image, all gone!

speaker: Labyrinth
content: Master, sorry, my body feels strange. It's becoming soft and fragile. This might affect the battle in a bit.

speaker: Labyrinth
content: To ensure your safety, please... quickly... resolve the current issue...
Seeing your companions so close, you feel reassured and even a bit touched.

speaker: Choice
options: How did you guys get here? You really shouldn't have come.

speaker: Rise
content: Yeah, we shouldn't have come. The original plan was to block the contamination leaking from the rift, but they wanted to cross over to find you, even at the cost of their own life. As it so happened, the shackles came through the rift and forced resonance at that very same moment.

speaker: Rise
content: By the time we came back to our senses, we were already here.
You look at the cybersecurity expert, who smiles at you.

speaker: Moore
content: I couldn't participate in the actual combat, so I borrowed Code Duck's device to study the rules of both worlds. I found something interesting.

speaker: Moore
content: 000 seems to have used some special Mania she found on you to bypass the dimensional barriers. Given the fact that the shackles between you and the Sinners are a deeper connection, I went ahead and tested out a little theory of mine. As it happened, you just released your shackles at the very same moment...

speaker: Moore
content: Hence a miraculous coincidence, I guess.
That sounds logical, but...

speaker: Hecate
content: Before we got transported here, Rise grabbed us and tried to pull us out of the rift. As a result, she got dragged along, too.

speaker: Moore
content: Huh? I thought shackles were necessary. So, does that mean I can...

speaker: Rise
content: Stop joking around. Such threats to personal safety weren't covered in the contract.

speaker: Rise
content: Deal with the enemy before us immediately. I need to apply for work injury compensation when we get back.
Strangely, 000 makes no move during your talk. She just stands there, smiling at you from a distance.

speaker: EMP
content: How do we resolve this? Can we awaken the god? Hey... O Mighty Deity... Rise and shine...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It's useless. I don't think our voices can reach its ears. After all, someone is controlling the power.
Everyone looks at the unruly assassin, who is also scrutinizing you.
What a surprise... They all belong entirely to the other side, yet they were able to cross the barrier.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What? You couldn’t foresee this, even with the power of the gods? Feeling scared now?
She giggles.
Not at all. Actually, I've always yearned for such lively scenes and wanted to join in. Come on!
Amidst the flickering light specks, the white Assassin Zone reappears. Various monsters instantly take shape and charge towards you.

speaker: Hecate
content: I've never seen such dire circumstances for a battle. We face too many restrictions here, and Chief is still trapped.

speaker: Choice
options: Try to come up with a counterattack strategy

content: 000 seems to control the entire field. No matter how many monsters you defeat, she can summon more with just a wave of her hand.
Defeating 000 here is almost impossible. Unless...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...I remember... EMP caused a major ruckus before.

speaker: EMP
content: Me? What ruckus? I don't cause ruckus.

speaker: Hecate
content: Yes, I remember Hella mentioned that you once disrupted the entire Syndicate power system with only one arrow, causing great chaos.

speaker: Hecate
content: This city also seems to run on electricity... you can do it.

speaker: EMP
content: Are you kidding? That was a once-in-a-lifetime moment. How can I reenact it here?

speaker: Labyrinth
content: Unless you are OK with speaking in that funny, cute voice for the rest of your life, in which case, Mess would stick it to you without fail.
Labyrinth pokes EMP, who makes a strange yelp.

speaker: EMP
content: No... I don't want to think about it... A powerful and dashing Sinner like me becoming a clown? No way...

speaker: EMP
content: Now it's really you guys forced me to do this!
EMP uses all her strength to shoot an arrow into the sky. A powerful electric current pierces the air, like a thunderstorm descending on the earth.
Instantly, the city plunges into darkness. Yells and exclamations pierce through the glass screen.

speaker: Code Duck
content: Quack?! (What?!)
The duck suddenly wakes up. It gets out of the car and looks really confused.
From a distance, you see it take out its phone, look around, and scratch its head—seemingly at a complete loss as to why it had driven to such a place.
Precisely as you thought.

speaker: Rise
content: ...The duck regained consciousness. The Assassination Field is gone!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The duck... the god is awake now. You lose.
She doesn't respond. She looks toward the horizon, at the dark city regaining lights in the distance, as if listening to something.
You don't know what she sees, but 000 has rarely lost her smile.
Nothing. I just feel a bit regretful.
She looks back at you and smiles again.
This round doesn't count. Someone violated the game rules by overusing Mania and got discovered.
The blackout just now caught the gods' attention. They will soon investigate and find EMP's Mania arrows. Hehe... the consequences should be exciting.

speaker: EMP
content: Uh... what... what'll happen?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: She's just being a sore loser. If there was such a rule, why didn't she mention it at the start? Why didn't she say anything when she used Mania herself?
I was having so much fun, I forgot.
I'm always careful when I do bad things. I know how to cover my tracks. Even if I kill a god, they won't find any clues. As long as everyone dies without any suspicion of foul play, it's fine.
Want me to teach you some tricks next time?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The target has left, which means your plan has failed. Nothing you say can change that.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And I'm not alone in this world anymore. My Sinners are here with me, and you won't have your way from now on.
There's no such thing as "from now on." You've already messed up. If you want to avoid punishment, you have to go back and start over.
Chief, do you know what "restart" means in the game?
In the distance, a loud noise erupts in the direction where "Code Duck" headed. Specks of light slowly gather in 000's palm.
Take a good look. This is a classic game design. When you fail a challenge or make a mistake, it sends you back to a previous save point, giving everyone another chance.
This is its kindest feature. As long as there's still a bit of fight left in you, you can always start over no matter how many times you fail.
She raises her hand, and her body swiftly disintegrates, transforming into a storm that engulfs all of you. The storm disintegrates everything in its path, even freeing you from the phone.

speaker: Hecate
content: Chief!!
You grab Hecate's hand, but then get separated again. In the final moments of getting swallowed up, you faintly hear her voice.
Get ready. We'll meet at our old spot.

speaker: Moore
content: ...Chief... Chief...

speaker: Distant Voice
content: Avocados on sale! Avocados on sale! Half off only for now! Don't miss out on this great deal! Avocados on sale!

speaker: Distant Voice
content: Avocados on sale! Avocados on sale! Half off only for now! Don't miss out on this great deal! Avocados on sale!
Once again you feel that nauseating dizziness, like countless streams of information pouring into your brain all at once.

speaker: Moore
content: Feeling dizzy? Seems like the information from the other dimension is too overwhelming. Let me switch to the filter mode for you...
[The image stabilizes]
The noise disappears, and your senses stabilize again, but this scene... is strangely familiar.

speaker: Moore
content: Chief, are you okay?

speaker: Moore
content: I'm Moore, Rise's colleague and a technician at the Nirvana Cybersecurity Center... Do you remember me?

speaker: Moore
content: Phew... That's good. I was worried you might be affected. To solve DisCity's problems, we have to rely on you to pull a few strings over there, Chief.
You remember these words and everything else. The unexpected journey to another dimension, your altered form... but there are differences...
When you fail a challenge or make a mistake, it sends you back to a previous save point, giving everyone another chance.
You sit up with a jerk, knocking your head against the glass wall. You start to think as you hold your forehead.
Time has been rewound, and your memory is unstable. You can only recall bits and pieces. The differences between the two times you woke up make you aware of the dissonance in your memory.
Last time, 000 was by your side, but this time she's gone. Plus...

speaker: Moore
content: Do you mean the Sinners? Are they not with you?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Wait, you remember the Sinners followed me here too? So you're aware that time has been rewound?
Moore's expression shifted between puzzled and contemplative several times before she nodded thoughtfully.

speaker: Moore
content: That's strange... Although time has been rewound, the Sinners didn't return to DisCity. I thought they were with you.
Her words panicked you a little.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...What's going on? Did something happen to them?
No, if anything happened to them, Moore wouldn’t know. Only one person would.
[Glitch]
A burst of signal interference abruptly cuts off your communication with Moore. The familiar sound of data transmission ensues.
<size=44>WELCOMETOMYTH</size>

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What on earth...
Before you can finish your sentence, your consciousness gets bombarded. The shackles numb your hands, and surreal images flood your mind amidst the pain.
[Transition]
Outside a bustling mall, you see the title "Draco Guests" is displaying on a giant screen. Thunderous applause echoes from beyond your vision.
The next moment you see a familiar figure bolting on that low-resolution screen.

speaker: EMP
content: Ch-Ch-Ch-Chief, help! Something's wrong with this place! Why is everything pixelated? Why did I just become pixelated? Even if it's just Draco behind me...

speaker: Draco
content: Roarrrr!

speaker: EMP
content: Ahhh, sir, I'm sorry, that wasn't me! Sir, have mercy, please...!!
[Transition] (A cleaning robot?)
In a quiet little room, a robot vacuum cleaner is doing its job. Its blue light flashing on and off as it searches for trash...

speaker: Robot Vacuum
content: Smart Home Maid III Labyrinth at your service... No, that's not right. Finding Chief is the top priority.

speaker: Robot Vacuum
content: Chief, where are you? Ch...

speaker: Robot Vacuum
content: Chief is kidnapped. Chief...
A shadow casts over Labyrinth the vacuum from behind. A fuzzy furball tiptoes over, with apparent interest in the cleaning robot.

speaker: Cat
content: Meow—

speaker: Robot Vacuum
content: ...I am sensing something... Beep! Alert! Large feline predator detected, danger, dan...
[Transition]
Hecate opens her eyes. In the distance, a faintly visible starry sky flickers.
The air around her slowly warps, creating an illusory atmosphere. Yet, there’s no sign of Mania, nor is her Nightmare anywhere near.
But she can sense that familiar aura. This is a dream, a dream of someone untouched by Mania.

speaker: Hecate
content: ...Where's Chief? I must find him.
female_content: ...Where's Chief? I must find her.

content: Hecate gets up and starts wandering around, trying to find the way out. Soon, she sees a blurry figure faintly trembling.
It's the owner of the dream, but Hecate can't understand its language. Losing Nightmare makes her uneasy, but soon she has an idea.
...If she turns this place into a nightmare, maybe she can gain power from it and summon back her Nightmare.
So thinking, Hecate doesn't hesitate. She strides towards the shadow and grabs it by the neck. With a firm grip, the shadow collapses to the ground.

speaker: Hecate
content: Sorry, but I'll do anything to get back to Chief. After this, I'll find a way to make you forget this nightmare.
It murmurs softly, but Hecate doesn't understand what it's saying. She thinks it's better not to understand. This way, she can achieve her goal without misgiving.
Hecate waits for a moment and closes her eyes, trying to summon Nightmare again. After a failed attempt, she opens them and finds herself surrounded by more blurry figures.

speaker: Hecate
content: Is this... a collective dream? Oh no!
More figures condense from the illusion, pushing and shoving towards Hecate. They seem drawn to something Hecate created.
Hecate is completely confused. What she created should have been a nightmare that makes people afraid, yet these figures act as if they're enjoying it.
The closer they get to Hecate, the quieter they become. It's as if they've entered a deeper, sweeter dream.

speaker: Hecate
content: ?? No, I need people's nightmares. I need to get back to Chief, I...
But those in the dream don't understand her words. They just rest peacefully, seemingly having a sweet dream.
[Transition]
Information and illusions ebb away like the tide. A bizarre newscast echoes in your ears.

speaker: News
content: The official results of the investigation into the major blackout at 3 a.m. today have been released...

speaker: News
content: A combination of daytime peak electricity usage and high temperatures caused a failure in the power supply equipment. All affected units have now returned to normal. Relevant departments remind citizens to use electricity safely during the hot summer...
Hi, dear Chief. You must have realized what rewinding is and confirmed the safety of your companions by now, right?
In the last adventure, your companions recklessly broke the rules and narrowly escaped being punished by the gods. This time around, to prevent any mishaps, I've adopted safety measures for everyone.
Mania is not allowed in the realm of the gods, who enforce the rules to the letter. Yet there are rifts beyond the rules in this world, where Mania exists alongside surreal fantasies.
Your Sinners are safely hidden there. No matter how they use their Mania, it won't raise any suspicion.
By the way, I even went out of my way to find the most suitable forms for everyone. No need to thank me. After all, I've been watching you all long enough to know a thing or two.
Anyway, have fun in this new world.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Wait!!
[Glitch]
The abnormal signal disappears the moment you snap back to your senses. Now you can hear Moore's voice again.

speaker: Moore
content: Alright, the anomaly has been resolved. Chief, where is the Sinner who kidnapped you?

speaker: Choice
options: She is looking for her next target.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This world is too absurd... but we must act quickly and stop her.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: We must not let her gain more power. Moore, can you locate the next target? Do you know where she is going?
You feel your body vibrating alongside the glass panel.

speaker: Moore
content: The current 5732 game account received an email. Hold on, I'll sync it to you.

I'm Rise. Let me cut to the chase. 
I'm now in the group chat of a weird game development team, and have gathered a lot of info. Currently, three members are missing. I think they were attacked by Sinner 000 and had their powers taken away. Hence the changes in our original world.
It seems that 000 won't attack in public and will specifically choose developers with special permissions. Based on these info, I can now think of one developer who might be her next target. 
Its name is Config Duck, and it is currently discussing a deal at a mall. I've already got its contact information. The development team last contacted it 1 hour and 28 minutes ago.
It seems to have a significant influence on Game 5732, thus I suggest prioritizing its protection to prevent 000 from seizing its permissions. 
I'll keep you guys updated.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Config Duck...
You turn to Moore. Although you don't quite understand, you trust Rise's judgment.

speaker: Moore
content: No problem. With the contact information, I can start the search immediately and transfer you to the target right away. We'll start from there.
You nod, finally feeling completely calm and clear-headed. Next, you need to pursue 000 and round up your scattered companions.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Rise is working so hard even in this world... Is she doing okay?

speaker: Moore
content: Well... don't worry. That kid will be fine no matter where she goes. She's much more reliable than I am.
[Scene Transition: Office]
In a random computer of a certain game company, Rise is secretly learning the rapidly scrolling information, memorizing everything in her mind.

speaker: Rise
content: This should be fine... The information is sent. Next, I've got to stay hidden. I must not expose my identity...

speaker: Rise
content: ...I've had enough of this! How can they be so lame?!
Meanwhile, data transmission for the Chief is in progress...

speaker: Digitalized Corruptor
content: Roarrrr...!
The chaotic data stream writhes, converges, and rushes at you, forming the familiar shape of Corruptors.
[Bang...! The Corruptor quivers and disappears]
With a flash of blue light, they crash into a semi-transparent barrier in front of you. Moore's communications resume immediately.

speaker: Moore
content: Attacks from an unknown source, which seems to have completely locked onto you. The attacks won't stop until your existence is completely erased.
But now you don't even have a physical form. How can you fight?

speaker: Moore
content: I've set up a temporary firewall to protect you, but it's not enough.

speaker: Moore
content: Chief, listen to me. Use your shackles to the greatest extent possible.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But here, the shackles...

speaker: Moore
content: Please trust me, it'll be fine. The firewall will protect you.
[Release the shackles]
You release your shackles, but they soon dissipate, making you dizzy. Just like 000 said, in this world, Mania is banned, and the shackles are useless.
But in that intense moment, you vaguely sense something different from the other end of the shackles.
[A white apparition (EMP) flashes across the screen]
Looking up, you see EMP's giant face showing on the screen.

speaker: Moore
content: Great! There's indeed a reliable Sinner nearby. I'll send you over. She will protect you.
[Flash]

speaker: EMP
content: Chief?! Why are you here... Are you here to save me? Chief, you are really...

speaker: EMP
content: I knew you'd come, Chief!! Waaaah! I've long admired your heroic deeds! The great superhero who single-handedly defeated Draco! Please, oblige me with your intrepid feat!!
...As expected, it's EMP. She rushes towards you, followed by the familiar pixelated little Draco.
Meanwhile, the abnormal data that had been chasing you penetrates the space, merging into the screen and turning into more monsters that lunge at you. Just then...

speaker: Mess
content: Yo, Chief. Rare to see you at your wits' end. Where's that swagger when you defeated Draco and then laughed at me? Need any help?
Another cartoon head pops out on the screen. This familiar voice, this striking purple... It's EMP's gaming playmate back at the Bureau—Mess.

speaker: Choice
options: Mess? How come you're here, too?

speaker: Mess
content: Well, it's still holiday, isn't it? We were in the middle of a game, where I was finally winning! But EMP tried to escape, so I had to get her back.

speaker: Mess
content: But now it seems like... it's more fun over here, hehe. EMP, when did you become such a noob? Aren't you supposed to be a pro?

speaker: EMP
content: ...It's not the same. Playing with a joy stick isn't the same as actually being hunted down!

speaker: Mess
content: Dumb, no matter how real you feel like being chased after, it's still just a game! Look...
She jumps forward to "Draco" and taps it. The dragon pauses, then opens its jaws and swallows Mess whole. EMP lets out a scream.
But before her scream even fades, Mess's purple head shoots out from the other side.

speaker: Mess
content: See? Being eaten won't even give you a scratch. Stop hiding behind Chief. Didn't you always say that one day you'd show everyone what you're capable of?

speaker: Mess
content: Guess what, today is the day! This immersive game is perfect for you to build some guts. Remember how you rubbed it in my face every time you won? Just show a bit of that cockiness and you're good to go.
Though what she said makes perfect sense, you feel kind of weird seeing Mess being so kind and encouraging EMP.

speaker: EMP
content: Sob... She's right. After all, I am the Archer Queen of Syndicate, the Bureau's top gamer, and the indispensable part of the great duo, EMP x Mess. What's there to fear in a little interdimensional game? I'm gonna...

speaker: EMP
content: Aaaaah, I'm not up for this! Chief, run! I'll hold it off, run!

speaker: Mess
content: Hahahahahaha... the top gamer my butt. Finally, I get to have my way!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Yeah, I knew it, she just wants to see EMP making a fool of herself.

speaker: Moore
content: Isn't it great? Let's leave this game to the two who enjoy it most. Chief, we should head to your battlefield.
[You have a new error ticket!]

speaker: Rise
content: Alright, it looks like everything is going well.
Rise swiftly handles the error ticket, drafts an email to Moore, then lets out a cautious sigh of relief.
Meanwhile, in the developers' group...
Rise shakes her avatar in this digital space, ready to execute her task, but the system prompt that pops up prevents her from proceeding.

speaker: Rise
content: ...Insufficient permissions again... Are they extra cautious with interns because there was a mole here?

speaker: Rise
content: But if this continues, I won't be able to gather any information. I have to come up with a plan...
A message from Moore appears in front of her.
If I'll be here for a few more days...

At the same time, Hecate finally escapes the excited dreaming crowd. She walks and listens from a secluded area, searching for those who might be in agony, hoping to extract energy to summon her Nightmare.

speaker: Person in the Dream
content: Ugh...

speaker: Hecate
content: ...Is-is that a nightmare?
If it's a nightmare, it might resonate with my Mania and bring back my Nightmare... I'll give it a try.
She gently places her hand on the figure's head and whispers...

speaker: Hecate
content: Nightmare... come back.
Several wisps of shadows flow out from its consciousness, condensing into thick reams that fall to the ground. They are covered in red crosses, looking grim and eerie.
They look like Hella's homework book, which can indeed be a nightmare for some under certain circumstances.
But such a dream is free from Mania and distortion, and cannot provide energy for battle.

speaker: Hecate
content: ...Sigh.

speaker: Hecate
content: Chief, the nightmares in this world are weak. Please hold on a bit longer. I will try my best to recover my Nightmare and return to you.
The figure, having lost its Nightmare, now appears peaceful and now notices Hecate.

speaker: Person in the Dream
content: <size=26>Softly</size> (You took away my nightmare...)

speaker: Person in the Dream
content: <size=26>Joyfully</size> (You made my dreams sweet again. Thank you!)
It jumps up happily, looking very excited.

speaker: Hecate
content: Your sweet dreams have nothing to do with me. I did nothing!
The phone screen lights up. You’ve reached your destination: a dark, small room with several computer screens, and you’re logged into a phone belonging to someone called Config Duck.
The Config Duck is frantically working on something, muttering strange things you don't understand.

speaker: Config Duck
content:
Quack. Quack. Quack. Quack?! Quack quack quack quack quack... Quack. Quack?!
(This skill description is completely off! How many times do I have to teach them?!)
Buzz...

Rise: Config Duck is responsible for designing combat skills, battle stages, and character parameters in Game 5732.
Rise: If 000 gets its permissions, she might significantly increase her combat intensity. Please be careful.

speaker: Moore
content: Intensity control... Looks like it's another battle we can't afford to lose. We're counting on you, Chief.

speaker: Choice
options: Got it. I'll do my best.

content: From the shadows, data gradually converges into that familiar figure.
Are you ready?
This time, the bullets are swift and tricky. 000 is about to fire again, and you are barely holding out.
At this moment, a fit of laughter suddenly erupts from outside.
The dozing duck wakes up with a start, and the Assassin Zone is lifted.
You attack 000, but she instantly vanishes like a projection.
Well done. The power is yours.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: She disappeared... What's going on?

speaker: Moore
content: ...This isn't her real self, but a projected decoy, so life-like that it could easily be passed off as the real one.

speaker: Moore
content: Is this her new ability? Impressive. The power imbued in it felt very real. Even I couldn't tell right away.
If she is so ready to give up this power... Then she must have another target.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Or does she think I'm not worth fighting? Are we being slighted?

speaker: Moore
content: Heh, I don't think so. Look.
Someone outside pushes the door open, muttering something unintelligible.

speaker: Internet Cafe Boss
content: You've been stuck on this for days. If you can't fix it, just take a break.

speaker: Internet Cafe Boss
content: You've worked yourself to the bone. How can you bring fun to the game in such a sad state? Look at those people actually enjoying their game outside.

speaker: Internet Cafe Boss
content: Playing Pack-Gal on the big screen of the mall... Now that's some proper gaming.

speaker: Moore
content: It's Mess and EMP. They're making quite a scene outside, and they've attracted a big crowd. It's a real ruckus.

speaker: Moore
content: Even after transforming, your companions drew everyone's attention, impacting the world in the process. As long as you hold out long enough, that little duck will wake up and escape 000's assassination. So you've won for sure.

speaker: Moore
content: Now, about the next target. I've found some clues already. Maybe this time we can stay ahead of the game.
In the silent unknown space, Rise's face is grim... while Bagel continues to chatter away cheerfully.

speaker: Rise
content: ...What is this? How did she know...?

speaker: Rise
content: The things she wrote...

speaker: Department Supervisor
content: Huh? Your colleagues are being mean? Are you sure you're not imagining it? Everyone is trying to look after you. Are you under too much pressure lately...?

speaker: Employee A
content: What are you talking about? An intern with no experience and who can't even make basic judgments should just follow orders.

speaker: Employee B
content: So what if you're from a prestigious Eastside university? You still have to serve under me.

speaker: Employee C
content: Young people nowadays are just...

speaker: Moore
content: This makes things much easier... Thank you, Rise.

speaker: Moore
content: So much info can be accessed with just an intern's permissions. These developers need better security measures. No wonder there's a mole.

speaker: Moore
content: Alright, data copy complete. Next...
Cracks of various colors appear around Moore, with monstrous roars echoing from within. As if following a predetermined program, the Corruptors rush toward Moore the moment they take shape.
As she suspected, it's a special type of data. It doesn't belong to 000 or this world at all—its origins are completely unknown. Moore's smile widens.

speaker: Moore
content: I knew you would come.

speaker: Moore
content: Unanalyzable, unblockable... I know you have nothing to do with Mania even under the guise of Corruptor.
She lowers her head, her glasses obscuring her eyes. She lets out a light chuckle.

speaker: Moore
content: That's interesting... Let's put the security system of this world to the test.

Hecate explores one "nightmare" after another, but they are nothing more than fragments of daily life. Things like work, relationships, watching a horror film, or simply being pinned down by a fat cat.
These mild nightmares can't bring power to her Nightmare, but they do provide a sense of peace.

speaker: Hecate
content: Although I can't regain my power, maybe this world is safer for Chief.
There are happy crowds, laughter and joy all around.
But in the horizon, at the distant edge of the dream realm, Hecate sees a foreboding shadow.

speaker: Hecate
content: ...What's that?
As you open your eyes from Writer Duck's device, you see 000 right next to you. This time, she's not waiting for your arrival, but fully focused on browsing some data.
Her lips curl faintly upon seeing you, but her eyes are still on the data in front of her.
You are quick this time. I thought you'd take longer.
Where's your tech expert? How come she's not here?

speaker: Choice
options: I asked her to look into something else.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Besides, who knows if you're using another fake projection to trick me.
Pfft, you're still mad about that?
That god specializes in strengthening Sinners, but I don't need it as I'm already strong enough. You can have it all to yourself.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You think I'd do the same as you for a bit of power?
I just wanted to make you happy.

speaker: Choice
options: No, there is something you want more other than power.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: "The fifth wrote souls and fate"... What you want is here, so you came early.
000 smiles, raises her hand to close the screen in front of her, and stands up.
What about you? Aren't you tempted? You want to get to the bottom of these things, don't you?
Here, you can find the answers to those questions you risked your life in that world to ask me.
She trails off, falling uncharacteristically silent for a moment. Before you can grasp the meaning behind this, she resumes her smile.
...But I guess you won't be tempted by me now. Apart from stopping and eliminating me, you surely have no other choice.

speaker: Choice
options: Yeah. Letting you run amok is not an option.

content: Hehehe... Okay, I understand.
You're Chief, after all.
She snaps her fingers, and with a click, the door lock opens. A white, 30-cm-wide round machine pushes the door open and slowly glides across the floor.

speaker: Labyrinth
content: Smart Home Maid III Labyrinth, vacuum cleaner version, has arrived at the designated location. Next command: support in battle.
It continues forward resolutely, with a few leaves and cat footprints on its body.

speaker: Labyrinth
content: Voiceprint confirmed, MBCC Chief. Pleased to regroup with you, and pleased to see that you have also been fitted into an awkward body, pfft.

speaker: Labyrinth
content: I can teach you how to adapt quickly, and I can also clear obstacles for you. Wherever we are, Labyrinth is the best...
...Meow?
A faint sound wafts into the room, interrupting Labyrinth's confident declaration. You see the white cleaning robot flinching at the sound.

speaker: Labyrinth
content: Smart Home Maid Labyrinth may need a moment... to adjust. Chief, please hold on a bit longer.

speaker: Cat
content: Meow!
A ball of orange fur flies past your screen towards the door. The cleaning robot's alarm goes off immediately, scurrying around the room.
It's rare to have so much excitement around here. Let's play one more round. Chief and cleaning robot maid vs. 000 and cat. Let's start.
000's expression stiffens, and she staggers as if injured. This definitely wasn't caused by you.
She quickly covers it up. This reaction piques your interest. It's the first time you've seen her hide something.
...Forget it, I'm not in the mood anymore. Let's call it quits.
With a wave of her hand, the Assassin Zone dissipates, and 000 vanishes.

speaker: Moore
content: Request received. The target is nearby. Initiating teleportation.

speaker: Labyrinth
content: Chief!

speaker: Cat
content: Meow!

Your companion's shout doesn't catch up with you. The next second, as your consciousness returns, you find yourself in another space. The invisible glass wall that had been suppressing your body disappears.
It's a deeper data space, with bizarre characters floating around. You don't understand their meaning, but you feel an inexplicable aversion.
Amid the data and files, 000 sits at the end with her back to you. She senses your arrival but doesn’t turn around; instead, she slightly covers the wound on her arm. She appears unusually quiet.
Sigh... why are you still following me?
I'm not in a good mood right now. I'll hang out with you some time later.
...Still here? When I'm in a bad mood, I tend to throw a tantrum. It's better that you stay away.

speaker: Choice
options: I'm here to see what's bothering you.
It's rare to see you so vulnerable.

content: She smiles, hooks her pinky around yours, then clasps your palm. She takes your hand and shuffles to your side.
Hehe, what a kind and gentle Chief.
You really think I won't do anything to you?
Oh... if you want to attack me, you'll have to get closer.
As soon as she finishes speaking, she flips you to the ground. Data from the void gathers into bundles, binding your wrists, waist, and ankles.
000 supports herself on your shoulder and looks down at you. Her knee presses against your chest, and before you can speak, she raises her hand to cover your mouth.
You let your guard down too easily around Sinners. Is it because you met too many good people in the past? Or was my acting too superb?

Those cute ducks were just there to confuse you. The games along the way were just for my amusement. Even this little girl persona is something I took from the DisCity dark web. You know what kind of place that is, don't you?
A strange sensation spreads as data turbulence corrodes your body, making you feel nauseous. The force in her hand gradually increases, and you see a familiar madness in her eyes.
I'm not your average person. I'm perfectly comfortable with appreciating your uniqueness while harboring a desire to kill you.
If I can kill the gods and replace them, what is stopping me from doing the same to you?
You struggle a bit and release your shackles, but it doesn't help at all.
She stares at you for a while. Just when you start to feel suffocated, she suddenly lets go.
Okay, I was just kidding.
She releases her hand.
Sinners don't have to be that bad.

speaker: Choice
options: I know what this place is.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This place holds a vast amount of records, detailing everyone's origins, experiences, abilities, preferences, relationships, and even their values and potential future developments. It's more detailed than the Bureau's records.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But you must be thinking, "Not only that. The gods dictate everything."
Haha, yes, the gods dictate everything, including your past, present, and future. Whether it's pain or happiness, they dictate how you experience the world.
Every decision you think you made of your own volition, every path you walked, was actually written by them without exception... but you surely don't believe that.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'd rather believe they installed cameras to spy on our every move and then secretly recorded it all in these documents.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If you claim our original world is a massive game that I shouldn't believe in, then the stories you're telling me could be lies meant to deceive me.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: After all, everyone should choose their own truth by listening to their heart.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Besides, if everything is their creation...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Then why would they create someone like me, who doesn’t believe in them, and someone like you, whom they can’t control? If everyone is their marionette, how do you explain your desire to kill them?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Would they create someone who would want to overturn them?
You have a point.
She looks up at you.
Do you want to see the fate they had in store for me? The "file" they wrote for me?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...I'm not falling for it. If I say yes, you'll try to get me to kill one of them with you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Just tell me. If you believe in fate as determined by the gods, you surely haven't forgotten what they’ve written for you.
A smile shows on her face.
Yes, I remember everything they designed for 000. It's all too simple.
Family: Blank. Education: Blank. Likes, dislikes, fears: Blank. Related characters and events: Blank.
Beliefs? None. Ideals? None. Even the gods don't know what I've experienced since my creation.
If you don't believe me, we can kill this god, take the permissions, and see that version of "me."
Oh... but don't go to where the Sinners are. I wasn't put there.
Go to "Early Settings," look for a file called "[Discarded]CharacterSettings_000.xlsx," and there you'll find everything the gods had for me.
It's something unfinished, something forgotten.
After me, the gods created one Sinner after another, giving them souls and lives, but they never looked at me again.
Well? Is this experience good enough for you?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Do you hate them for abandoning you?
Vengeance? Hahaha, how could I? They never even told me what hate is. How could I seek vengeance?
${PlayerName}, I'm glad you're willing to get to know me, and conversing with me as if I were a human being. But ultimately, I'm something else.
As a Sinner, I wasn't given any beliefs, emotions, or motivations.
So when Mania spread into this space, it took over the empty me effortlessly.
The genius who invented the DisCity dark web could digitalize everything and merge all data into the Mania network, while Mania itself... could cross boundaries and reach rifts in other worlds.
The corrupted data thus reached the abandoned file, filling up all its emptiness, and then created a Sinner that was never meant to exist.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I get it now... You've been overtaken by Mania, which is why you caused all this mayhem. You're driven by the mastermind of the dark web, spurred by Mania, right?
Hahah, now it's your turn to deny my own free will? "Everything might be fake, but we can choose what's real with our hearts." Haha.
She wipes away her tears of laughter.
Since I became conscious, I realized I'm different from other Sinners. They can go to the big world, but I'm trapped in a small grid.
When I finally became a Sinner through Mania, I was immediately deemed a system error by the gods. They constantly tried to hunt me down and erase me, forcing me to hide in the rifts of the dark web.

After learning the underlying logic of the world from the sea of dark web data, learning to edit code to avoid detection, and launching rewinds to save myself, I finally stepped out of the dark web and got to see the world I've longed for as I pleased...

But I couldn't see the beauty anymore. I saw layers upon layers of code behind everything. The world I once yearned for is nothing more than a game created from a higher dimension. The sky has a limit, and there's only one path into the future. The gods have already dictated all possibilities.
...But fortunately, soon after that, I met you.
I don't know why, but from you, I can see the destiny set by the gods and feel the connection from them.

"This person can take me to a bigger world"... Hehe, every time the gods close all the doors on me, I always manage to find a tiny crack. You made this possible for me. The moment I saw you, I made my decision.
So, ${PlayerName}, knowing all this, what do you think I'm up to next?

speaker: Choice
options: ...It isn't our world that you want.

content: If our world is but a game in your eyes, then ruling it means nothing to you...
You brought me to this new world because, for you, only this new world can be considered real.
You want to establish yourself here. And I, along with my world, are just tools for you. You used me to reach here, and my world...
You want to take over my world because there's something valuable in it. What you want is...
At this very moment, the data space suddenly shatters, plunging you into darkness, but it also frees you from her control.

speaker: Raven
content: A field trip to the Otherworld, chaperoned by a great teacher... What a spectacular opportunity!

speaker: Raven
content: You're of age now. It's time to step out of your little shadow, broaden your horizons, and see the bigger world!

speaker: Crache
content: Okay okay, I got it. That Chief seems to be in trouble. If you can't find any ink, then just give way to my little shadows.
The shadows on the wall travel through various surfaces, bringing about large patches of darkness and... cheers. Bystanders excitedly watch on, thinking it's some special light show.
(Scene change)
Looking at the lively scene outside, 000 lets out a sigh.
...Causing such a ruckus again. They're really something, charging around recklessly, and not letting me relax for a moment.
Chief, get ready, I'm going to rewind.
Sometimes you just can't help it, but we still keep going nevertheless.
We're alike. We both understand this very well.
You see crimson light reflecting on the water surface of this world. Two different scenes seem to overlap...

speaker: Moore
content: ...Chief... Chief...
[Slightly trembling lens]

speaker: Distant Voice
content: Avocados on sale! Avocados on sale! Half off only for now! Don't miss out on this great deal! Avocados on sale!

speaker: Distant Voice
content: Avocados on sale! Avocados on sale! Half off only for now! Don't miss out on this great deal! Avocados on sale!

speaker: Moore
content: Feeling dizzy? Seems like the information from the other dimension is too overwhelming. Let me switch to the filter mode for you...
[The image stabilizes]

speaker: Moore
content: Chief, are you okay? I'm Moore. Do you remember me?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: How many "permissions" have she gained?

speaker: Moore
content: Five permissions: visual, audio, functions, strength, narrative... she has gained them all.

speaker: Moore
content: In a real game development, she would already have enough power to dominate everything in the world.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Even if we stop her, she will still use her power to return to this point in time.
In this game, everyone's fate is being manipulated, but for her, it's just a game.
It's been such a hectic day, but looking back... everything is utterly absurd.

speaker: Moore
content: You seem a bit down. Back when we lost contact, what happened between you and her?
You think back for a while, then slowly start to speak.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: She took me to a strange place, and said a lot of strange things... Moore, I want your opinion.
You tell Moore about the conversation with 000, about the so-called settings, discarded file, contamination, and anomalies.

speaker: Moore
content: Wow... "settings database"? What did she see there? I'd really like to see for myself.

speaker: Moore
content: Fate?
She briefly falls silent, then laughs almost inaudibly.

speaker: Moore
content: ...You all like this word.
Before you get to respond, she continues.

speaker: Moore
content: As a programmer, rather than believing in fate, I believe in inevitability.

speaker: Moore
content: Every world has its own rules. Under certain conditions, logic and causal processes determine the direction of development. People are the same; their background, education, relationships, and past experiences collectively shape their thinking and actions.

speaker: Moore
content: Every person and world is a vast and complex system. It self-corrects, self-expands, and continuously progresses based on new information and environmental changes.

speaker: Moore
content: Of these, what can be called underlying logic, or basic premises, or causal laws, or objective external environments... the inevitable results they lead to, in your terms, might be called fate.

speaker: Moore
content: Oops, I droned on and on about these boring things again.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Not at all. It's quite enlightening.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You say fate is inevitability. So is it unchangeable once set? Is everything we do meaningless?

speaker: Moore
content: What I mean by inevitability is that for a programming system, certain inputs lead to relatively certain outputs.

speaker: Moore
content: But if you want a different result, you can change the initial input data. You can also exploit system loopholes like that girl. Some simply destroy everything in the system. That's also a choice.

speaker: Moore
content: See, if you just want to change fate, there are so many paths. Which one would you take, Chief?
Her words momentarily leave you at a loss for an answer.
She smiles breezily.

speaker: Moore
content: Any of them. For me, the most fun is learning about the system.

speaker: Moore
content: Gather as much information as possible, understand its mechanisms. Once I fully grasp its logic... isn't the outcome whatever I choose?

speaker: Moore
content: You are in this quandary because you don't truly understand her, right?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm in this quandary exactly because I don't understand her at all.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What she wants, what she's afraid of, what she plans to do... I have no idea.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: In other words, as long as I take the initiative to understand her and the world, there are still many things I can do.
Moore smiles as you pull yourself together.

speaker: Moore
content: Right on. That's the Chief I've heard about.

speaker: Moore
content: That girl is indeed interesting. She's so clingy, yet there are still many things she hasn't told you. Keep interacting with her to gather info. You'll eventually understand her.

speaker: Moore
content: If it's really too much of a hassle... I can always help you kill her.
[The positive atmosphere instantly drops to freezing point.]

speaker: Moore
content: Of course. According to my analysis, it's entirely feasible.

speaker: Moore
content: The greater her actions and threats, the more the underlying structure is exposed... making it easier to target and strike.

speaker: Moore
content: I'd readily take on the request. It's very challenging, but I'd do it for you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Instead of killing her...

speaker: Choice
options: I'd prefer to completely subdue her.

speaker: Moore
content: Oh, sorry, I misunderstood. It seems Chief can't bear to let that girl die.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...No, it's not that. Her abilities are very special. Whether it's dealing with DisCity's dark web or future enemies, she'd be very useful.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Though I don't believe in predetermined fate, you're right. Everything has its rules, and information is key.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If this world can indeed observe and record our development in some way...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Then I will need her help.

speaker: Moore
content: Hehe, I understand. This task is more complex. We need to neutralize her threats while protecting her from being rejected by the world...

speaker: Moore
content: That's fine, I'll get it done. Since it's your request, I'll ensure her safety until she's by your side.

speaker: Moore
content: But next, I need someone in that world to distract her to buy me more time. Chief, can you help me with that?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're right. No matter how erratic and crazy she is, she must have her own internal logic.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: By the way, since you can track all her information, can you send her a message?

speaker: Moore
content: Of course. But what do you plan to do?

speaker: Choice
options: I want to invite her... to play a game.

content: It's 7:30 a.m., and the pool just opened. No swimmers are here yet, even the lifeguard chair is unoccupied.
The faint echoes of furious quacks create ripples across the water's surface. A restless figure hops back and forth along the deck.

speaker: Mystery Duck
content:
Quack... Quack quack. Quack quack. Quack! Quack quack quack quack?!
(I can't find my phone, so I'll use this one for now. What's up... What? Another failure?!!)

speaker: Mystery Duck
content:
Quack quack quack! Quack! Quack?! Quack quack quack! Quack quack quack!
(I told you to follow the specs, but you never listen! You couldn't even get the requests straight! You know how much trouble you caused everyone? Curse you!)

speaker: Mystery Duck
content:
...Quack... Quack quack. Quack quack quack... Quack quack quack?
(...Forget it... It's done, so deal with it yourself. I have real work to do... What about the mole?)

speaker: Mystery Duck
content:
...Quack? Quack?! Quack?!! Quack????!!!!
(Still? Not? Caught? Yet?!!)

speaker: Mystery Duck
content:
Quack quack quack! Quack quack quack quack quack!!
(Meeting! Are you at work? Meeting, now! Round up all the missing guys for the meeting!)
While jumping around fervently, the duck suddenly slips and falls into the water. Its legs cramp up, and the more it struggles towards the deck, the more the waves push it away.
At this moment, you know she has come to meet you.
...So, here you are.
Ignoring the struggling duck on the other end, 000 dives into the water and retrieves a phone from the bottom of the pool. The phone looks very advanced and is impressively waterproof.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I thought you'd stop playing this game once you got all the permissions. What a shame. I was just getting into it.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm glad you came.
000 tilts her head and looks at you.
You really want to keep playing?
You look at her and remember Moore's instructions.

speaker: Moore
content: From now on, I'll be fully dedicated to the tasks you've given me, and won't be able to support you on the field. My colleagues at the Cybersecurity Center will take over this part of my work. Don't worry, they're all very reliable.

speaker: Moore
content: Plus, I need time... a lot of time. Someone needs to draw her full attention.

speaker: Moore
content: I'll leave these matters to you, Chief. I'm counting on you.

speaker: Choice
options: Of course. You don't seem to be in a hurry. Hang out with me a bit?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: After all, though this duck isn't directly involved in the development, it can hire new developers at any time and reallocate your hard-earned permissions.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Don't worry, it's just me here. No one else.
So saying, you ring the emergency alarm. The drowning duck is sinking, and the alarm is ringing nearby. Someone will probably arrive soon.
000 just watches you doing this. Then, she finally smiles and responds to your anxious anticipation.
Okay. I'll stay with you.
The colorful field spreads open again. Until the rescuers arrive or until the duck dies, it's your game time.
And you shall glimpse the truth about her... and the power she holds.

speaker: Moore
content: But next, I need someone in that world to distract her to buy me more time. Chief, can you help me with that?
You did your best, researching and setting traps in advance. If you can foil her assassination attempt and force her to rewind, you can buy more time for Moore.
But now it seems the odds are slim.
000 grins at you, seemingly seeing through your thoughts. Since reaching the new world, she has grown so much, easily eliminating anyone in her way... and now, she even holds all the "permissions."

She can turn the Sinners into bizarre forms, trap them in dreams, lock them in the web, or chuck them into various rifts. Even if you band together to turn the tide, she can easily launch a rewind and delete all your progress, and you can't do a thing about it.
Sometimes you just can't help it, but we still keep going nevertheless.
Can it really not be helped? Will all these efforts be in vain?
...Maybe there's another possibility?
(Flashback)
The blackout just now caught the gods' attention. They will soon investigate and find EMP's Mania arrows. Hehe... the consequences should be exciting.
(Flashback)
...Sigh, causing such a ruckus again. They're really something, charging around recklessly, and not letting me relax for a moment.
Chief, get ready, I'm going to rewind.
(Flashback)
Each rewind is launched when you successfully stop her. You thought she did this to avoid admitting defeat, but when the assassination of Config Duck failed, she didn't immediately rewind.
Probably... the timing of the rewind isn't directly related to defeat, but rather...
(Flashback)

speaker: I'm telling him everything! You won't get your hands on me!!
content: Mania is not allowed in the realm of the gods, who enforce the rules to the letter.
In the last adventure, your companions recklessly broke the rules and narrowly escaped being punished by the gods. This time around, to prevent any mishaps, I've adopted safety measures for everyone.
(Flashback)

speaker: Choice
options: The purpose of the rewind is to prevent Mania from being exposed.

content: This thought flashes in your mind, and you immediately want to verify it and buy time for the operation. However...
It's too late. If there's no Sinner around to help you...
(Flashback)
Alright. Mania is forbidden in this world. Using the shackle will cause a crisis. Put it away, okay?
(Flashback)

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I should have tried this sooner.
The shackles collide with an invisible wall in front of you, shattering and dispersing. But you don't stop, giving it your all once more.
The narrow space shakes, and you feel a wave of dizziness. Meanwhile, a spot on the glass wall seems to loosen. You feel encouraged by this.
What are you doing...?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You don't want us to use our powers, or have the gods discover signs of Mania. You insist that such actions would incur dire consequences.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So I want to see what consequences could make you act so cautiously. I want to see what could scare the fearless 000.
[Glitch]

Mustering all your strength, you finally break the ever-present wall in front of you. Amidst dizzying noises, blinding light and quaking, you feel like suffocating mud has filled your lungs instead of air.
But you made it out, and your power has returned.
Stop it!
000 raises her hand quickly, causing the entire isolated space to quake. This is her signature move before launching a rewind. You've successfully forced her hand, and she's being cornered.
She's in such a rush that she doesn't escape the truth in time...
[Black Screen]
Just before everything rolls back and whisks you away to the past, you are engulfed in darkness. A certain kind of being chases up, blocking your path with immense pressure.

speaker: Blurry Echo
content: Er▌▌▌detect▌
You can't understand its words, see its form, or even sense its existence. This thing is unlike any enemy you've encountered before. It...

speaker: Blurry Echo
content: ▌▌▌activate▌ clear▌▌
Before you can process it, a powerful force surges toward you. Just as it's about to tear you apart, 000's halo flashes before you.
At the same time...
[Enter Memory] Check Rise's side story

speaker: Moore
content: This is great, Rise. Thank you for providing Bagel's email. She clicked the fake link, and now we have full account access. The operation can continue now.

speaker: Moore
content: Speaking of which, she really trusts you. After going through so much, you've finally made some good friends in your new workplace. Good for you.

speaker: Rise
content: ...We're not from the same world. We're not friends.

speaker: Rise
content: In any case, it's all for the mission. Are you sure this will help Chief?

speaker: Moore
content: Of course. Next, you need to hide well. Isn't that development team desperately looking for the mole? Be careful not to get exposed.

speaker: Moore
content: We still need a bit more time before the real counterattack.
She reviews the operation progress with interest, thinking how much better it would be if Chief could hold out a bit longer.
[Transition] White screen, dizzy sound effects like heartbeat and panting
You barely regain consciousness.
The rewind succeeded.
But you don't remember what happened.
[Transition] 2 seconds, ears ringing, murky chaos, blurry vision
Your consciousness feels shattered and disjointed. You fail at every attempt to piece it back together and make sense of things again. You can't see or hear anything discernible before you.
Someone comes to your side, but only a vague impression remains in your mind.
[Illustration] Injured 000, black gradient
□□ said □□□ stop □□□□ you can't hold out □□□□...
Luckily □□□ I □ just in time □□□□□□□
You can't hear what she's saying, but...
The rewind succeeded, and the operation must continue. You remember that you need to buy more time and challenge this Sinner again, and uncover the truth behind her bit by bit.
[Transition] Eyes opening, first-person view of the sky
You can no longer remember how many times you've been rewound.
This is your modus vivendi to fight against her despite the power disparity. You use your shackles to break the device, release Mania, and force 000 to rewind, buying time for Moore.
But after repeating it several times, you begin to doubt whether it is truly meaningful.
I won again. Do you want to start over?
Through the small phone screen, 000 looks down at you. She flashes her usual grin, seemingly enjoying herself.
You must be exhausted, losing over and over again. I feel sorry for you.
You don't sense any sarcasm in her voice, but rather a bit of genuine pity.
This eases the worries in your heart.

speaker: Choice
options: ...I won't repeat it because I found out that...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Even if I don't try so hard, you are in no hurry to do anything.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: In your theory, you've already gained all the permissions, and have the power to dominate the world. You could easily get rid of me with a flick of your finger. But you haven't done that.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You put aside your target and come here to dilly-dally with me instead... I thought that's not like you.
Her eyes light up. She squats down and leans in closer.
Oh? Then what kind of person am I in your eyes?
...She always takes the bait in unexpected ways.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I haven't read your discarded file, nor do I want to waste time distinguishing your lies from truths.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The 000 I've seen with my own eyes has always been a decisive person, fearless and unscrupulous in achieving her goals.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Whether it's altering fate, usurping the world, or simply playing a game for fun, you won't stop till you're satisfied. As long as there's a chance, you act immediately and grasp onto it with an iron grip.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Now, you can dominate this world and get anything you want with all the permissions of the gods.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Yet you haven't done anything.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Not only that. You've gained so much power, yet you rarely use it recklessly. You only use the permissions when there's a chance that Mania might be exposed.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I think... The permissions work well in Game 5732, but not so much here. So...
You remember Rise's warning about the apparitions creeping into people's dreams, that "cognitive disorder" caused by the dark web.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You need Mania. Mania is infiltrating through the dimensional rifts here, and you're waiting for it to bring changes, to create opportunities for you, or maybe...

speaker: Choice
options: You're the one bringing Mania into this place.

content: ...What a surprise. So according to your analysis, 000 isn't a mad Mania monster, nor some poorly designed program.
"She" actually seems a bit human. How wonderful.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Then don't mess with Mania. Whatever you're planning, it's too dangerous. You'll end up getting yourself burned.
Why? You can see how hard the battles are here. Without the power of Mania, we lowly creations won't be able to cross that line.

speaker: Choice
options: You should know it better than I do.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You've been in DisMyth for so long, so you should know it's the source of all tragedies. This should be something your "gods" designed, right?
But I have the power of the gods who created Mania. The gods initially meant for it to be a source of pain, but I can redesign it to bring joy, if you wish.
...It's hard to tell if she's being optimistic or just perverse.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You've said it yourself, this world rejects Mania. You can't bring in Mania on a large scale here. Delusions can't alter reality.
But I'm already here. We've all come here and done so many outrageous things.
Even the realm of the gods has rifts that can accommodate some delusions and create new possibilities. Chief, is the spell that the gods placed on you so potent that you can't accept any other path?
You want to speak but fall into silence.
Maybe both of you have your points, but at this stage, it's clear that the two of you neither need nor can convince each other. Your starting points are fundamentally opposed.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I don't think you can alter Mania or change fate simply with those "permissions" in your hand, nor will all your wishes be fulfilled. Even if the "gods" can influence our world, I refuse to believe that they control everything.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Call me programmed, brainwashed, or spellbound; I'll gladly accept it. Even if the gods do exist, I don't believe they have total control for a simple reason...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If I accept that they control everything, it would completely negate the will of everyone I've met. I'd rather be forever ignorant and stubborn than deny the possibility of their freedom.
The playful and innocent smile vanishes from 000's face. She looks at you for a long time, then averts her gaze and speaks softly.
You're right.
She doesn't speak again, but leans down and enters the phone screen that you're in, moving to snuggle up next to you. She even changed her outfit for this.
I'm fooling around and enjoying my time.
Aren't you trying to stall for time, to keep me here a bit longer? It's not time yet, so I'll be with you.
Indeed, there's no reason to refuse. Your body can't endure more battles, and you are too tired to speak.
The two of you fall silent, lying flat in the narrow rift of the small phone. Separated by an invisible glass barrier, you gaze at the otherworld's strange sky together.
After a while, a faint light flashes across the sky.
See, this world's boundary is dissolving. Imaginations are seeping into reality, and when they collide, they emit this light. This is the light of Mania.
Isn't it beautiful?
The day I was infected, in that abandoned, pitch-black data space, I saw the same scene.
...Mania, beautiful?

It's the first time you've heard Mania being described this way. Whether it's about DisCity's dark web, or being hunted down, she always describes things in the most eccentric way. Yet in this moment, you can't refute her.
After all, unlike the brutal mutations you usually fight against, the halo gently flowing across the sky right now indeed gives off serene beauty.
Somehow, looking at it makes you think of the ever-changing human hearts.
I often see this scene during the long wait, in others' stories. I watch it give each Sinner strength, allowing them to change their lives.
I've always been envious.
000 reaches out to the sky, towards the flowing light, but can only touch the invisible wall.
I can't escape the gravity of reality to reach your side and grasp this power. I've always hoped it would cross the boundary to my side and give me a chance.
So when Mania appeared before me, I seized upon it straight away.
If everything started over from that moment, I would make the same choice, over and over again.
Yes, Mania is the root of calamity.
But it was also the brightest opportunity I had in the endless night.
As she speaks, the flashing light illuminates the narrow rift. The shackles respond, and you hear familiar voices... It's your Sinners.
Your companions finally overcome the barrier of rewinds to join you in the fight against the lone opponent.
Your opponent chuckles lightly.
Alright, so much for our private time.
She leaves the phone and reverts to her original form. Now she looks like a proper enemy again.
Chief, you'll still try to stop me, won't you?
The strange light in the sky becomes more pronounced, twisting and turning, signaling that Mania is intensifying. It's unclear when it will completely break through the boundary into this world.

Meanwhile, your battle is entirely one-sided. 000 effortlessly neutralizes all your efforts, as if she's just passing the time. Under the wrath of her permissions, the Sinners can't even use their powers.
Hey, I already told you to be cautious when fighting here. You'll get discovered.
Now...
[Glitch] 000's white outfit illustration flashes.
Huh?! What's this...
The force restraining you suddenly lifts, and 000's body flickers. She hasn't been attacked, but she pauses as if her consciousness is interrupted, and her eyes suddenly turn hollow.
At the same time, you hear another familiar soft voice.

speaker: Moore
content: Phew... looks like I made it in time.
…It's you?
A blue data matrix unfolds before you, shielding you from all attacks. Inside the matrix, Moore's projection appears before you.

speaker: Moore
content: Chief, are you alright? I've been too busy handling data to contact you. I was worried you might be pushing yourself too hard and had gotten into trouble.

speaker: Moore
content: But now, it seems the timing is just right.

speaker: Moore
content: Thanks for buying me time. The virus developed against the anomalous Sinner 000 has been successfully implanted in the target. The repair process has started, and the threat she poses will soon be neutralized.

speaker: Moore
content: The plan worked, Chief. I took a gamble, believing she'd slow down to spend more time with you... Hehe, I was right.

speaker: Moore
content: Thus, the virus I planted in your body successfully infected her. This would have been impossible given her level of vigilance.

speaker: Moore
content: Chief, thank you for being my bait.
As she says this, Moore deploys another matrix around you, shielding you from the information turbulence and giving you room to breathe.
What did you do?

speaker: Moore
content: Oh, right, you're still here. Almost forgot.
Moore turns to 000, inspecting her own work contentedly.

speaker: Moore
content: Don't worry. A simple trap like this won't hurt you. The defense system in this world has been putting a lot of pressure on you, hasn't it? I simply built on that.

speaker: Moore
content: From a programming perspective, as an anomaly, you exploited a unique loophole, breaking through the dimensional firewall and delving deep into the system. You've proven your ability to disrupt the system's underlying logic. That's impressive.

speaker: Moore
content: But errors are not uncommon. A so-called "world" remains stable despite its vastness precisely because it has extremely powerful error-correcting capabilities.
As she says this, an endearing smile appears on her face.

speaker: Moore
content: You must have already sustained defensive counterstrikes in places we can't see, right?

speaker: Moore
content: As I realized that no system would ignore a threat like you, a strategy to deal with you dawned on me. I can destroy your underlying logic and completely erase your existence.

speaker: Moore
content: But... our Chief wants you alive. He seems to like you quite a bit.
female_content: But... our Chief wants you alive. She seems to like you quite a bit.

speaker: Moore
content: So I had to take a different approach, go on a slight detour, and bet on this virus. It would be best if I could capture you in one piece.

000 tries to speak, but her body starts flickering. Her voice distorts and gets mixed with other fragmented utterances. She steps forward, but her movements stutter, causing her face to intermittently pixelate and flash unfamiliar faces.

After repeating this a few times, she gets enraged and summons a halo blade, slashing it into her own body. With a high-pitched screech, her distorted afterimages shake violently, causing a shockwave to crash into the firewall in front of you.
A few seconds later, the chaotic malfunction finally subsides. 000 regains her composure, but she's no longer in control of the situation.
...No, this isn't a virus... What did you do?
Her anger doesn't affect Moore at all. Instead, the tech expert is happily recording all of 000's abnormal responses, seemingly impressed by her reaction.
Only when asked does she remember that she is still in front of the enemy.

speaker: Moore
content: Yes, I know you've obtained those "godly" permissions. Any low-dimensional virus I create wouldn't amount to so much as a scratch before being brushed off.

speaker: Moore
content: I just used it to buy some more time.
000 realizes something, but her body can no longer follow her commands. Something is seizing control of herself from within.
Moore watches all this coldly.

speaker: Moore
content: You were born from the rarest loophole in the system. It's a brilliant miracle, but also the source of your misfortune.

speaker: Moore
content: You lived but became an error that no world could tolerate. You were only able to rely on system loopholes to survive as well.

speaker: Moore
content: Your very existence is already a paradox. As a low-dimensional programmer, I can't fix your problem.

speaker: Moore
content: But fortunately, someone can.

speaker: Moore
content: CharacterSettings_000.xlsx, right?
000 looks at her and answers word by word.
...You can't possibly have modification permissions.

speaker: Moore
content: No, I don't. Want to see who does?
[Scene Change] Writer Duck work desk
In the middle of the night, a figure leans on the bed, typing away quickly on a tablet.

speaker: Bagel
content:
Quack quack quack... Quack! Quack quack quack. 
(000... 000... found it! Such an old file...)

speaker: Bagel
content:
Quack quack quack quack... Quack quack quack quack... Quack quack quack.
(Didn't expect boss to like this type. How ancient is this version? It's so hard to modify... Why did they assign me to do it, and in such a hurry, too...)

speaker: Bagel
content:
Quack, quack quack quack... 
(...Hmm, I'll ask Rise for advice...)
(Scene change)
Rise looks at the comms channel in disbelief, finally realizing what her "intelligence" was used for.

speaker: Rise
content: ...It's her?
In another world, in a programmer's tiny apartment, Moore presses Enter to confirm the final command... and the task is complete.

speaker: Moore
content: It's all settled. I've found a solution for you.

speaker: Moore
content: The source of your misfortunes consists of being forgotten by your creator, illegally taken, and spawned where you shouldn't exist. Now, the gods' gaze has finally fallen upon you.

speaker: Moore
content: It will embrace your flaws and mistakes, giving you a complete life. From now on, you won't have to worry about being expelled from the world. No one will hunt you down to erase you.

speaker: Moore
content: Your existence will be acknowledged. Soon, you'll have your own fate, and an ego that will be recognized.

Moore congratulates her, but there's a hint of regret in her eyes. After so many years exploring the web and conducting so many tests, she finally found such a special case, sample, and unexpected gain.
She wishes she could keep 000 a little longer. Maybe she'll try to control her and train her, to see how far she could go.
...What a pity. This girl grew up too fast and became too strong-willed, threatening the safety of Chief. Moore can only make short work of this little bug before 000 causes more damage.
Oh well. Moore seals the last data record and closes the process monitor. Finally, she won't have to pull any more all-nighters. She yawns and shifts her voice to a warmer tone.

speaker: Moore
content: You can stop worrying too, Chief. From now on, she can be a normal Sinner and your companion, just like everyone else.

speaker: Moore
content: In a bit, you can take her back to the Bureau with your shackles.
The prolonged rewind battle has exhausted you greatly. Your mind struggles to take in what they're saying, but even so, you're clear about one thing.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It's not over yet... I can't subdue her as she is now.
In front of you, 000's silhouette keeps dissolving, yet she shows no sign of defeat. More and more data spill out from the cracks in her body.
000 lowers her head, laughing quietly yet fanatically. Her laughter pierces the unbreakable firewall Moore built, faintly unsettling you.
Hahaha... Hahahaha... I've been preparing myself and mustering up the courage to fight against this world.
But I never expected it to end like this...
This is it... Being sent off by my creator. My death feels like my birth.
Yet you...
She looks at Moore.

speaker: Moore
content: Mm-hmm?
You're quite something... Are you not shaken at all after seeing the truth?

speaker: Moore
content: Hmm... I don't feel anything. Every day, all kinds of information are input, but how to process, select and use them is determined by programming.

speaker: Moore
content: Do you need my help?
Hehe, so that's how it is... that's what you're like...
...Save it. Death is no news to me.
000 stands up, wobbling.
I've been too cautious in the past, too eager to preserve that hard-won hope. I've been tiptoeing around like a flinching coward. What a joke I've become.
Around her, the air gradually becomes granular and pixelated, turning into specks of light that gather in her slowly raised right hand. They mix and resonate with her fragmented, dissipating body.
...Then, three dazzling halo blades form, and you hear a shrill alarm from Moore's side of the comms.
Thanks for backing me into a corner, so that I can let loose and have a real good time!
[Transition, special sound effects]
The halos swiftly destroys the first firewall, then the second and the third. Only the fourth firewall manages to block it, but barely.
With a flash of white light, 000 disappears from your sight, leaving behind only constant vibrations that signal the havoc she's wreaking elsewhere.

speaker: Moore
content: Oh dear... even at a time like this, you still want to mess around with the system... I can't be held accountable for what happens next.

speaker: Moore
content: Are you worried about her, Chief?

speaker: Moore
content: It's okay, it's over. After all, these are the rules she trusts the most, which she can't overturn. Let's get ready to go back, shall we?
Saying this, she types on her keyboard several times, and the "game entrance" lights up on the screen.
[Game Icon]

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...I can go back now?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But right now...

speaker: Moore
content: Even if you let things be, a "normal" Sinner will soon come to your side, just as you requested.
The Mania storm outside is still raging, gradually interfering with Moore's comms. The game entrance becomes unstable. You know you should hurry up. But...
[Illustration] 000 with battle damage on her eye(s)
Thinking of 000's final frantic actions, you can't find peace.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I must find her now. Knowing her, she won't give up just like this. It won't end here.
Instead of going into the entrance, you release your shackles with all your might...
[Release the shackles]
[Black Screen]
The moment the shackles break through the firewall, the comms get completely cut off. Moore sits alone in the room, staring at the darkened monitor.

speaker: Moore
content: Hehe... it's too late now.
[Several 3D night scenes are disrupted by glitches]
You regain consciousness. You're not in the phone, and you don't have the protection of the "low-dimensional filter". You feel dizzy and nauseous, but you haven't lost all mobility.
The area is being ravaged by the Mania storm, and its eye is the Sinner going manic in the sky.
Haha, outta my way!
Her body keeps disintegrating, but she doesn't care. She keeps lashing out vengefully, tearing through the sky with her halo blade as she falls.
These aren't gods' permissions; it's her own Sinner power, the power of Mania. The entire city's power supply is affected. Lights flicker, and you can hear the puzzled murmurs of the crowd.
You remember a similar incident not long ago, when she said...
This round doesn't count. Someone violated the game rules by overusing Mania and got discovered.
Next... hehe, the consequences should be exciting.
Now you know what the consequences are.
Square holes burst through her body, and the scattered data quickly dissipate. The attack is so swift, giving her no time to react.

You can't see where the attack came from, but you recall what happened when you first used the shackles to release Mania and forced 000 to launch a rewind: an invisible enemy, an unstoppable attack, and a fierce reaction to Mania...
