...This is the real reason she has been constantly rewinding: the so-called "game rules."
But this time, she has no strength left to initiate a rewind or avoid the attack. Another invisible force strikes 000, making her fall from the sky.
You rush to her side. You must use your shackles to stop her from getting herself killed like this.
[Release the shackles]
The shackles take effect, and the Forbidden Force kicks in. Red lights pierce through her body, inflicting even more pain on the already weakened girl. You grit your teeth and help her up.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No matter what you want, this isn't the way. You can't change the world like this. Can't you try something else? You can keep rewinding, and if that doesn't work... aren't you great at hiding Sinners?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That character file won't do anything to you. No one can...
Mmph!
As you speak, her body trembles. Her already broken form distorts and reconstitutes, flashing through countless strange appearances in an instant, cutting off your words.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Or, we can find Moore, and find the "god" who rewrote your file. If you don't want to be altered, then decide what identity you want yourself.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: At least we can get you stabilized.

She looks at you in a daze, then closes her eyes and hugs herself tightly, quivering non-stop. Dense data flow out from her fingertips, slowly repairing her damaged body. After a while, she finally regains her voice.
But what comes out is a faintly manic laugh.
...Haha... hahaha! Never!
The shackles dissolve in an instant. Only then do you realize that she still has the "gods'" permissions, easily removing your shackles.
Another impact strikes. 000 pushes you away, dodging a hit and also distancing herself from you.
Three halo blades converge in her palm again. She looks up at you one last time, smiles, then charges towards the unseen enemy in the sky.
You've long lost track of 000. Flickering specks of light fall from the sky; these are the data remnants of her wounds.
They fall like snow, landing on you.
Then, at some point, you hear a faint voice.
...Sorry, ${PlayerName}, at this point, we no longer have a chance to chat.
But you'll be able to see these words somehow, won't you?
Did I just hear someone say he's going to personally write my file? To record and save the true 000? Haha, I'm so happy. What are you going to write? What do you think the real me is like?
female_content: Did I just hear someone say she's going to personally write my file? To record and save the true 000? Haha, I'm so happy. What are you going to write? What do you think the real me is like?

content: A deviant, greedy and rebellious fool? Or a passionate genius with an unbridled imagination?
A miracle worker who can always find a new rift when backed into a corner? Or a bird in a cage who gets trapped no matter how many rifts she traverses?
In any case, I'm sure you wouldn't see me as an error that shouldn't have existed. You're that kind, and I think I'd like the 000 you create. Remember her for me.
But don't put it in that file. Don't change my story, and don't erase the path I've walked.
That belongs to me. Even if it's blank, it's mine. I like my blank slate. That's what defines me... infinite possibility.
Next, I'm going to have a glorious battle. If I win, I'll be the god of two worlds. You must congratulate me then. Don't spoil the mood.
If I lose, you should still congratulate me. I came from darkness, lived a fulfilling life, and chose a beautiful ending for myself.
But I'm not one to admit defeat easily, am I? I can still see many possibilities in the future.
Can you hear me?
${PlayerName}?
[The white light fades out, returning to a daytime scene in DisCity]

speaker: Moore
content: You've succeeded, Chief. The anomaly has ended, and everything is back to normal.

speaker: Moore
content: Welcome back.

<size=72>This chaotic, manic storm
has no impact on true fate.</size>

July 25, N.F. 114
DisCity

speaker: EMP
content: Chief! Over here! I found a great anime series, collector's edition!

speaker: Labyrinth
content: Please forget about it. The recent snack order has already used up all the budget.

speaker: EMP
content: Hella isn't here. Plus, Chief is loaded. We rarely take vacations, so let's splurge a little.

speaker: EMP
content: Oh! And that one! The new game!
There are still some rifts left in the sky, but they will no longer release monsters or disturb the peace.
Time rewinds to before the chaos. You remember the culprit dragging you to another world. You remember that she killed some strange "gods," and...

Some details have become blurry. For example, you've forgotten what that person looks like. Researchers who experienced the incident speculate that all memories of it will eventually vanish, though the forgetting process will vary depending on the person and event.
Perhaps those who especially value something will retain memories of it a bit longer.
But even these memories probably won't last long. The residual light fades, and the scars gradually heal. These are signs of the end.

speaker: Hecate
content: Chief, are you okay?
You force yourself to flash her a smile.

speaker: Hecate
content: You look really tired. We can call it a day and head back to rest.

speaker: Hecate
content: I think that world is also safe now.
[Scene Change] Chief's Office
At night, you hear a noise outside the door and push it open.

speaker: Little Kitty
content: ...Meow?
There's no one at the door. Looking down, you see a kitty cat at your feet.
Labyrinth quickly arrives and picks it up.

speaker: Labyrinth
content: Sorry, Chief, it followed me here. Recently, my attraction to felines has increased. I'll take it away now.
[Scene Change] Nirvana Hospital

speaker: Rise
content: Agent Moore has submitted a technical report to the center. The dark web threat has been eliminated. Sinner 000 is dead, and the anomaly is in its final contraction phase.

speaker: Rise
content: Digitalized Mania gave the Sinners involved varying degrees of memory fluctuations. However, since the shackles are in place, there are no major problems. They just need some time to heal.

speaker: Rise
content: As for the "extra-dimensional" world everyone experienced...

speaker: Rise
content: Similar to the Elysiland incident, it has been classified as a virtual space constructed by Sinner 000, an illusion generated by Mania.

speaker: Rise
content: That's the summary of it. The full report is 733 pages and has been sent to your inbox.

speaker: Choice
options: Good work. You're always so reliable.

speaker: Rise
content: Thank you. Also, I'm here to bid you farewell. I've resigned.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Have 000's words got to you? Are you worried that this world...

speaker: Rise
content: No, no. I don't care about the truth or falsehood of gods or games. Those are from the work. I've seen all sorts of absurd things at work. Plus, you've paid me well.

speaker: Rise
content: ...It's just some trivial sentimentality.
[Entering Memory]

speaker: Rise
content: You can't do that! She'll be treated as a mole and disposed of as such!

speaker: Moore
content: Why do you care? It's just part of your job. She's an entity from another world, a virtual object if you will.

speaker: Moore
content: Relax, Rise. You've done an excellent job.
[Exit Memory]
Rise is silent for a moment, then looks at you again.

speaker: Rise
content: I understand the logic, and I have no resentment. I just need some time to do something to make myself feel better. So, I'm here to say goodbye.

speaker: Rise
content: Thinking back on the days we worked together, you caused me a lot of trouble, broke many of my principles, and gave me endless overtime. It was really unpleasant.

speaker: Rise
content: But after it ended, I felt it was more worthwhile than ever.

speaker: Rise
content: Goodbye, Chief. I wish you all the best.
She bows to you and prepares to leave.
You clasp your hands together, think for a long time, then look up at her.
There is one more thing I need your help with. Something... that can only be done by someone I trust.
[Moore's house]
The doorbell rings for a while before a woman's voice responds from inside, followed by chaotic clatter.
The door opens. Moore stands there wrapped in a bath towel, her hair wet and gleaming in the light. Water drips down her skin and onto the floor.

speaker: Moore
content: Sorry, I was in the shower and didn't hear the doorbell. Just leave the delivery at the door.

speaker: Moore
content: Huh? Chief, why are you here? Ah...!!

speaker: Moore
content: We finally meet again, and here I am looking like a mess. So sorry, can you wait a moment? I'll tidy up the place. It'll be quick.
She tries to close the door and go back inside, but you hold the door open with one hand.
You glance at her misty glasses and then inside the room. Several screens flicker faintly amidst swirling steam, and you hear the sound of running water. Beyond that, it's too dim to see anything.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I need to talk to you. Can I come in?

speaker: Moore
content: Now? But...
You take off her foggy glasses, stopping her mid-sentence.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: All right Moore, let's cut to the point. You’re not exactly an expert at faking a scene.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Are there really that many things in this room that need to be hidden?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Don't worry, I'm not here to ask about those things. I have urgent matters that need your help. There's not much time to waste.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: My companions downstairs, however, are a different story...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Can we talk, dark web expert?
Moore looks at you for a long time as the clock ticks.
A small mechanical assistant slowly floats out from behind, flashing lights to greet the guest.
She finally smiles, takes back the glasses, and wipes off the mist. After putting them back on, she no longer looks flustered. The tech expert beams a sunny smile.

speaker: Moore
content: Got it. Chief, please come in.
She leads you inside and closes the door.

speaker: Technician A
content: ...What's with this sudden new operation? Hasn't the dark web threat already been neutralized? That Mania space is completely closed. There's no risk anymore, so what's there to be scared about?

speaker: Technician B
content: It seems the MBCC wants to arrest the offending Sinner... but isn't she already dead? Moore's report explained as much.
Rise had already submitted her resignation, and is only back today at Chief ${PlayerName}'s request to support this so-called special operation... but even she doesn't know what it is.
The MBCC Chief is staring silently at the surveillance screen, his face uncharacteristically grim.
female_content: The MBCC Chief is staring silently at the surveillance screen, her face uncharacteristically grim.

content: [Entering Memory]

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The various reports have sufficiently explained the malicious incident caused by Sinner 000, so I won't elaborate further.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The offending Sinner has died from severe injuries. The impact and chaos she caused are gradually subsiding.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Now, I want the truth behind it all.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Please delve into DisCity's dark web, track the early activities of Sinner 000, and investigate the origin of Mania. I want to know what, or who, created such an "incident" through contamination.
[Exit Memory]

speaker: Moore
content: The results have been compiled. Residual info from Sinner 000 points to an unknown area in DisCity's dark web, where a large amount of Mania data has been detected. The environment is very unstable there, and we cannot delve further with conventional methods.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Enter the domain. I want to browse all the residual info there.

speaker: Rise
content: No, it's too risky!
She steps forward and grabs your hand.

speaker: Rise
content: Hey, at these depths, the information pollution in the dark web is Mania. Don't try to understand it, or it will distort your mind.

speaker: Rise
content: You didn't bring me here just to show me this, did you?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I need the most trustworthy and professional partner on this matter. I need your help.
You pause and smile at her.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Of course, soon you'll also need my help.

speaker: Rise
content: ? You...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm aware of the risks. This time, the login and browsing will all be done in the isolation room. Please prepare the necessary contamination protection measures for me. If there are any unexpected issues, I'll need you guys to handle them.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Moore, open the channel and send me in. You know the way, right?

speaker: Moore
content: Of course. I went ahead and prepared the temporary access protocol. I can send you to the nearest accessible domain.

speaker: Moore
content: But from there on, you'll have to go on your own. Are you sure you're okay with that?
At the other end of the conference hall, a few suited men with hats pulled low linger in the shadows by the wall. They make Rise uneasy.

She also notices things are a little strange between ${PlayerName} and Moore. They’ve been exchanging a lot more silent glances today. Just like in this moment—Moore gave the final command, took a sip of coffee, and smiled at ${PlayerName}.
Several seconds pass before Chief finally speaks.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Experts are needed outside to handle the emergencies, and Miss Moore is the most reliable when it comes to technical matters. Can I leave this in your hands?

speaker: Moore
content: Alright, decryption complete. The address is ready, and the link is being generated. Ready to dive into the depths of the data sea, Chief?
You walk into the specially designed server room, establish communication, and enter the depths of DisCity's dark web.
For a moment, the screen fills with countless characters. After a while, you begin to understand their meaning. At the same time...

The display starts to distort in front of you. Your senses begin to shift, and you fall into chaos. Your consciousness seems to leave your body, merging into the character-filled screen, delving deeper... until another bizarre world unfolds before you.
The first to greet you are some digitalized Corruptors from DisCity's dark web. You've become very familiar with them over the past six months.

The Corruptors invading your consciousness are gradually expelled. At the same time, you slowly adapt to the disorderly datasets of Mania around you. They infiltrate deep into your consciousness, flickering on and off.
There are blurry faces, whispered words, dim lights and shadows. Slowly, you begin to identify certain emotions and desires.
Come to think of it, it could be said that she... grew up here.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You said it's your first time outside, first time chatting face-to-face with someone. What about before that? Were you hiding in the dark web?
Yeah, it's a great invention. You can see the whole world without leaving home. Oh, and a lot of info you can't even imagine is in that sea of data.
You strive to discern, hoping to find clues buried in the depths of the dark web and find the mastermind behind it all.
...But in the end, what you see are only some familiar yet blurry images.
There are those who cannot see the light of day. There's no place for them in this city, so they turn to dwell in the shadows.
There is dark and endless malice that has found a gutter, swarming and churning in wanton revelry.
There are those forgotten, abandoned, and powerless to come ashore, who can only cling to Mania like an addiction and grasp onto illusory dreams.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Isn't it dangerous? Crime, malice... plenty of things that can't see the light of day lurk there.
Yeah, just like me. I can't see the light of day...
Before coming to see you, I always hid deep in the dark web. There, I could do many things without being discovered.
You hesitate briefly, then move forward to delve deeper.
The deeper end of the domain resembles a massive black hole. Entering it, your consciousness flickers on and off. It's as if your mind is being broken into 0s and 1s, merging with the surroundings.
After a while, you reach a boundary; a shallow, untouchable barrier.
On the other side of the barrier, specks of light flicker and coalesce into both strange and familiar shadows. They scatter in different directions, passing through walls and disappearing from view.
They probably went to different worlds.
Perhaps... this is the place where she first embraced the world.
Hi.
It's an auditory hallucination, but you hear it. Following the vague apparition, you find...
A bit of residual light in an empty area.
You hold the residual data, and fragmented memories tickle your mind.
Some thoughts you don't recognize, while others you remember vividly... These might also awaken your own memories.
Finally, you see 000 on the summer street where you first met. The smile she had is gone, and tears are rolling down her cheeks.
...Ha... Turns out that person is just like me...
Me? In what way am I like her? Equally reckless? Stubborn?
You can no longer ask for an answer.
The fragmented memories brush past your consciousness and dissolve into the darkness.
A series of intermittent comms messages pulls you back to reality.
<color=#a0ffea>■■■■ and Sinner ■■■000■■■ Mania data match ■■■■■■ This is the last trace she left when she was deleted.</color>
<color=#a0ffea> After sustaining so much damage ■■ even if ■■■ took her through the dark ■■■ web data ■■■ storm, ■■■ center has no one ■■ who can ■■■ restore her.</color>
<color=#a0ffea> But ■■■ don't worry ■■■ since this ■■■ higher ■■■ decide to erase her completely from ■■■ world, it won't be long before you ■■■ can forget ■■■.</color>
<color=#a0ffea> Or do you ■■■ want to ■■■ another request, and ask me to ■■■ save her? </color>

speaker: Choice
options: ...Do I really want to save her?

content: No.
Why ask such a question at this point?
You didn't accept those reports and conclusions, nor the storyline's return to normalcy...
Isn't it precisely because you hated such an arrangement?
You chose to take a risk, coming to this obscure place without knowing anything...
Isn't it because you wanted to find another answer?
Isn't the different possibility you wanted right in the palm of your hand?
...Why not give it a try?

speaker: Voice in the Memory
content: Just think of it like a game, and... Let's play big.
That's right, since it's a game...
We must clear the level properly.
[Tap the circle in your hand]
You bring the remaining data in your hand to your mouth, and swallow it all.
Information, data, and intelligence seep into your consciousness. It's the residue of a fragmented mind... no, a newborn soul.
It's her desires, struggles, and madness born from the darkest void. Now all of this turns into poison, seeping into your existence.
Then...
[Scene transition, perspective shift] (Performance)
The isolation room in the Cybersecurity Center where Chief is located suddenly erupts into a storm. Countless rifts tear open, just like the outbreak not long ago.

speaker: Technician
content: Chief has come into contact with anomalous data and suffered total mental contamination! This is an ultra-high intensity dark web anomaly!

speaker: Technician
content: Wait, are those... shackles?!
[BUG Chief CG]
Mania rages on, with spatial matter continuously splitting apart. The chaotic data is tearing this world asunder.
The shackles in ${PlayerName}'s palm start to shatter, dissolving into countless specks of light that split and reform into more destructive forms.
In ${PlayerName}'s eyes, the world begins to dissolve. The physical body and the room lose their original forms, turning into chaotic data that disperses and reassembles.
The light of the shackles tears apart the room where the Chief stays, as if 000 has returned to rip the world apart with a manic storm.
female_content: The light of the shackles tears apart the room confining her, as if 000 has returned to rip the world apart with a manic storm.

content: A huge barrier presents itself before ${PlayerName}, separating the two worlds, the familiar and the unfamiliar, the real and the false.
On the other side of the barrier, a massive shadow is gathering warily, like a garrison on guard against an incoming enemy.

speaker: Moore
content: Haha, so you actually contaminated yourself... You are truly as crazy as she is.

speaker: Moore
content: I'd really like to see how far you can go, my good Chief. I look forward to the surprises you bring back, provided...

speaker: Moore
content: You are able to return.
[Release the shackles]
[Glitch explosion] [Flash to white, return to Cybersecurity Center] Transition for 2 seconds.
${PlayerName} disappears into thin air, leaving behind a room full of strange rifts.

speaker: Rise
content: So... This is the job he gave me. As reckless as ever.
female_content: So... This is the job she gave me. As reckless as ever.

speaker: Rise
content: But I have to do it.
She rushes into the rift without hesitation, heading towards another unknown world.
[Glitch turns into white light]
Massive amounts of data converge into a blinding white light that pierces your brain. This time, no one sends you into a phone or helps you filter the information.
▌▌▌▌,▌▌▌▌▌ invasion▌: 5▌32▌world.
This is the world in 000's eyes. This is the enemy that she has been fighting all along. Now you understand the meaning behind the broken symbols... it's sheer conviction to obliterate the anomaly.

speaker: Choice
options: This time, I'll be the challenger.

content:
<size=72>This chaotic, manic storm
has no impact on true fate.</size>
▌▌error▌▌,▌▌,▌▌▌purge...
▌▌error▌▌,▌▌,▌▌▌purge...
You manage to hold off the enemy in front of you with your shackles, but the more you use your power, the more it attracts the enemy's attention. It's like a never-ending vicious cycle.
No wonder 000 was so cautious back then, taking so long to plan killing even a duck. You decide to stop fighting and avoid trouble for now.
I warned you, didn't I? The realm of gods doesn't allow Mania to run wild. Be careful when using your power. If you're discovered and deemed a system error, even I can't save you.
Hmm? You're asking why I'm so adept?
I've always been a bug, hunted in every world I'm in. I learned my skills after countless chases. I'll teach you a few tricks next time.
If she were here, she'd definitely say that. In the face of adversity, you do miss that reckless, carefree little lunatic.
Although you can't learn her mindset, you can always borrow some past experiences. Think about how 000 used to "shield" you intruders...
You force your way into a device. The intense rejection almost expels you; there's no Game 5732 here.
Fortunately, you're no longer the panicked traveler you once were. You've gained the residual power of the Dark Web Ghost. Time to use it...
<color=#ffffff><size=50>Game 5732 downloaded and installed!<color=#ffffff></size>
The intense rejection finally stops. You hide in the game, avoiding pesky pursuits, but you haven't fully recovered yet.
At this moment, a notification suddenly buzzes within the game.

<color=#fb9259>[RiSe]</color>: I'm Rise. Finally found you.
<color=#fb9259>[RiSe]</color>: Those ducks... no, those permission holders... are having a meeting to find the mole.
<color=#fb9259>[RiSe]</color>: You need those developer permissions, right? This is a good opportunity.
<color=#fb9259>[RiSe]</color>: I'll help you.
In the realm of dreams.

speaker: Hecate
content: Just trap them in a dream for now, right?
Wind screams, whipping sand into a biting haze as the open-top vehicle tears across the desert.

options: Yes, but it won't be easy.

speaker: Hecate
content: Understood. Though I can't use Nightmare's power, there are many "people" here who will help me.

speaker: Hecate
content: They understand the "nightmares in this world" better.
Behind her, a group of blurry figures gather. They speak in incomprehensible tongues, all seemingly eager and ready.
[Scene Change] Duck Conference Room
...Quack... Quack quack quack!
Quack quack... Quack quack...

<color=#fb9259>[RiSe]</color>: Everything's ready. Go ahead, Chief Bug.
<color=#fb9259>[RiSe]</color>: Let's see how much you can shake things up.
[First-person perspective of Bagel] [Hiding in a dark bathroom/storage room] [2 a.m.]

speaker: Bagel
content: ... I'm Bagel. I'm new to the Game 5732 development team at ▌▌▌▌. If anyone hears this message, please pass it on... I don't know who to tell.

speaker: Bagel
content: Recently, the project has been experiencing severe issues. I've been on edge and worried about my colleague Rise, so I came back to see what was happening.

speaker: Bagel
content: ...But I discovered something even more alarming... Listen...

speaker: Artist Duck
content: Got it, I will fix it immediately... Got it, I will fix it immediately... Got it, I will fix it immediately...

speaker: Code Duck
content: 97%, 98%, 99%... 99.3... 99.6... Ahhh, why did the package fail again, ahhh!

speaker: Rock Duck
content: ...Ahhh... Quack... Ahhh...

speaker: Bagel
content: Hear that? My bosses are making weird noises in the conference room. I took a peek, and all six of them look possessed. Their faces are twisted and terrifying.

speaker: Bagel
content: They've been asleep for nine hours. I know I should call the police... but my phone has no signal, and I don't have the courage to go out now... Eek!!
Bang!!!
(The door opens. White screen. Silhouette of boss appears.)

speaker: Boss Duck
content: Huff... You... You...

speaker: Bagel
content: ...Sir? I didn't mean to hide here. I'm an intern. My name is...

speaker: Boss Duck
content: Are you... the mole...? Are you... Ah?!!

speaker: Bagel
content: Ahhh, help!!!
(Sound of being hit)

speaker: Boss Duck
content: Quack...?!
(The boss disappears. Clatter of fight off-screen)

speaker: Bagel
content: ...I'm still alive... What happened? Where's the boss?
Bagel sneaks out.
An even more baffling scene greets her. In the empty office, the tables and chairs are overturned, engulfed in a sea of fire under the blaring smoke alarm.
At this moment, the previously signal-less phone suddenly vibrates.

speaker: Bagel
content: A phone notification... Why??
Beep... New ▌message notification.

speaker: RiSe
content: Why are you still there? Go now!
It's a message from an unfamiliar account, but when opened, it shows a series of colorful, flashing characters in the chat history. Scrolling up...

speaker: Bagel
content: ...Rise?
In the empty office, the sea of fire burns, and monsters surge out of nowhere.

speaker: Rise
content: Get lost! Aren't you supposed to eliminate otherworld infiltrators like me? Why are you after her?

speaker: Rise
content: That one's a real coward. I'm not letting you through.
Right after saying that, the chat connected to Rise's mind starts buzzing, giving her a headache.

speaker: Bagel
content: Rise, where are you? I'll help you!

speaker: Rise
content: You're not a Sinner. What can you do to help? Just run!
Bagel clearly can't hear Rise's voice. Instead of running, she sends more messages.

speaker: Bagel
content: <color=#fb9259>[Bagel]</color>: I...

speaker: Bagel
content: <color=#fb9259>[Bagel]</color>: Rise? Answer me. Please be safe!

speaker: Bagel
content: <color=#fb9259>[Bagel]</color>: I've always been a pushover who couldn't hold down a job.

speaker: Bagel
content: <color=#fb9259>[Bagel]</color>: If it weren't for you, I wouldn't have realized how useless I am...

speaker: Bagel
content: <color=#fb9259>[Bagel]</color>: If I run away and leave you behind, I won't forgive myself.

speaker: Rise
content: ...Come on, would you stop it, please?

speaker: Bagel
content: Waaahhhh...
A barrage of voice messages erupts like firecrackers.

speaker: Rise
content: Quit whining! While you're wallowing in self-pity, your account got hacked by the mole! Do you want to take the blame again?

speaker: Bagel
content: Huh?? No, it wasn't me, please believe me, it really wasn't, I beg you...
Her reaction makes Rise even angrier.

speaker: Rise
content: Begging me for what?!!! I'm the mole!!

speaker: Bagel
content: I messed up again. I'm really done for this time... I'm definitely going to get fired... Rise, please, for old times' sake, don't do this... I'll do anything you want, just don't...
She types with trembling fingers, tears almost spilling over.

speaker: Rise
content: ...Damn it. This is exactly what I expected. I could have finished this, but the thought of you sitting here crying and begging gives me a headache, so I came back.

speaker: Rise
content: Clear your mind and think through the whole thing. Now answer me...

speaker: Rise
content: You saw a friendless newbie and reached out to help her. Anything wrong about that?

speaker: Bagel
content: N-no, I guess...

speaker: Rise
content: OK, OK. You were dissatisfied with your work and asked for a second opinion, but got randomly shouted at instead. Tell me, is it wrong?

speaker: Rise
content: Good. You didn't make amends with her, but you didn't use her mistakes at work to get back at her, either. Instead, you helped her again anyway.

speaker: Rise
content: Look, you're really stupid, but have you really done anything wrong?

speaker: Bagel
content: I... have done nothing wrong.

speaker: Rise
content: Right, you did nothing wrong, but in the end, she betrayed your trust, stole your files, and damaged company property.

speaker: Rise
content: Look, you're now facing this jerk alone. Even if you can't stop her, you muster the courage to record evidence and call the police... If you did that, would you still feel you've done things wrong?

speaker: Bagel
content: No... No, it's the right thing to do! I'm not in the wrong!

speaker: Rise
content: Then do the right thing, stand up for yourself, and don't bow to anyone. Make the real wrongdoer apologize to you!
This is the last message she sent. Rise punches through the computer screen, pulls out a lightsaber, and faces the incoming Corruptors.
On the other end, Bagel stares blankly at the damaged but empty office, as if having just witnessed a paranormal event. Yet, she doesn't feel scared.
Bagel raises her phone and captures the burning "crime scene." The moment the frame freezes, she sees a figure she's never seen before.

speaker: Bagel
content: ...I accept your apology... I know what to write about my character now.

speaker: Bagel
content: Thank you, Rise. Thank you...
[Teams Chat] Bagel reports her permissions issue.
The battle ends. Rise takes one last look at Bagel and walks away from the flames.

speaker: Rise
content: After this, Bagel's permissions will be revoked, and their internal security system will soon level up.

speaker: Rise
content: Okay, from now on, whether it's a duck or some god developing the game, they'll keep their eye on security loopholes. You won't have to worry about sabotage anymore.

speaker: Choice
options: Perfect. Once again, you've done an excellent job.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'll take you and everyone else back before they reclaim this power. Let's go now.

speaker: Rise
content: Hey, what's the rush? Don't you have something you still want to do?
Rise shoots you a look that says "I know you're trouble," much like when she reported to you at the hospital.
But this time, she keeps quiet, and gets ready to support you.

speaker: %u
content: I'll make sure you get overtime pay. I'll give you quadruple, no, ten times the regular salary, with extra insurance added in.
Next, you look at the icon again.
Look, the entrance to the game is now in your phone. You can check it anytime if you miss home.
In hindsight, this statement is somewhat amusing.
Your world, a city with countless people and memories, fitted into this tiny square... you actually fell for this kind of talk. It really is as fanciful as Mania.
You don't believe anyone can control your world or decide your fate. But if there really is some connection between the two worlds...
Then there's something you must do, and you must do it now.
Tap the game icon
It's not taking you back to DisCity. The developer permissions you seized from "the gods" are a bit unwieldy, and you barely manage to open a "game entrance."
Beyond the entrance lies a vast space of pure data. Though you don't know the way, you can see a clear trail of abnormal data residues leading deep into the data space.
These are the last tracks she left on her journey, the marks of her struggles.
It's unexpectedly quiet here.
As if sinking into a dark abyss, you can't see a thing, yet you distinctly feel countless eyes watching you from the darkness.
Then, you receive a message from somewhere:

<color=#cafffc>......
......</color>

<color=#cafffc>Visitor confirmed as file in Project 5732.
Currently off original path. 
Status: Abnormal.
Developer permissions confirmed.
Permission Acquisition: Illegal.</color>
Suddenly, countless lights ignite the darkness, flickering and forming a circle around you.
The danger has come faster than expected, and you immediately become alert. With limited information in hand, you prepare yourself for a fight while trying to buy room for negotiation.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: She left her last tracks here. I want to know her whereabouts.

<color=#cafffc>Sinner 000 confirmed to be an anomalous file, and its generation event is illegal.
The source file was contaminated by an unknown source and the data was severely corrupted.
Sinner 000 has been off path for extended periods of time, wandering within the project and causing chaos.</color>

<color=#cafffc>This lasted until Sinner 000 completely lost control, crashing resources and directly impacting the game project with its erratic behavior.
To sustain system stability and security, Sinner 000 must be removed.
Deleting all remaining traces.</color>
<color=#cafffc>So, are you here to save Sinner 000?</color>
Several rays of light begin to scan you.

<color=#cafffc>You've been implanted with part of anomalous functions.
Did you seek out this dangerous data for Sinner 000?
Did you remove this file from the original directory, steal developer permissions, and invade Project 5732 to save Sinner 000?</color>
<color=#cafffc>Did you do all this to save her?</color>
You can't discern the intent behind these questions. The system just gave 000 such a ruthless verdict, yet it asks you these sentimental questions... You have to think about how to respond.

speaker: Choice
options: Yes, I'm here to save her.
Why do you assume I'm here for her?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Are you going to delete me, too? Because I'm a "file" who's willing to carry out anomalous actions for the sake of an error? Because I came to save an illegal Sinner?

<color=#cafffc>...
...
...No...</color>

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Is my willingness to attack the system to save her part of my "character settings"? If so, let me carry out my role faithfully. Can you please not interfere?

<color=#cafffc>...
The system will not interfere.</color>

<color=#cafffc>Your actions fully align with your character settings.
MBCC Chief, the shackles of the Sinner, □□□, ${PlayerName}...
You excel at understanding Sinners and care deeply about them.
You will exhaust all means and pay any price for them.
Just like what you're doing right now.</color>

<color=#cafffc>You're doing great. It deserves to be recognized.
The system will help you save the Sinner you want.</color>
...That's it? Just say you want to save her, and you get to take her back? Things are going surprisingly well.
Although the term "character settings" is quite unpleasant, you're willing to go along with it if it helps you achieve your goal.

speaker: Choice
options: So, how do I bring her back?

Appearance, voice, actions, effects?

content: The last time someone tried to rewrite her settings, she got very upset.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Is there a simpler, more straightforward method? Since you erased her, can't you restore the data? Systems are supposed to have such functions.

<color=#ff3803>Warning, illegal action!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I've only known her for a few days, so my understanding is limited. I can't sum her up in a few words.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Plus, I don't think she's that different from anyone else. If she really is unsettled somewhere, I think it can be diagnosed in a targeted way, just like a hospital visit.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The developer permissions can do that, right?

<color=#cafffc>Permissions aren't a free pass to everything.
This system is vast and complex.
Using permissions requires compliance with standards, procedures, and verification. Only then can the results be approved.
Acting recklessly will only cause the project and story to fall apart at any moment.</color>

<color=#cafffc>That Sinner is bewitched by fictional power and unable to see the reality behind it.
That Sinner keeps making the same mistakes.</color>

speaker: Voice in the Memory
content: When I finally became a Sinner through Mania, I was immediately deemed a system error by the gods. They constantly tried to hunt me down and erase me, forcing me to hide in the rifts of the dark web.

speaker: Voice in the Memory
content: After learning the underlying logic of the world from the sea of dark web data, learning to edit code to avoid detection, and launching rewinds to save myself, I finally stepped out of the dark web and got to see the world I've longed for as I pleased...

speaker: Voice in the Memory
content: But I couldn't see the beauty anymore. I saw layers upon layers of code behind everything. The world I once yearned for is nothing more than a game created from a higher dimension. The sky has a limit, and there's only one path into the future. The gods have already dictated all possibilities.

<color=#cafffc>Her core drive is to seize the possibility of change.
But the more she defies the odds, the more tragic her outcomes. It was dictated by her incomplete nature.</color>

speaker: Voice in the Memory
content: Every time the gods close all the doors on me, I always find a tiny crack. You made this possible for me.

<color=#cafffc>After being exposed to too much information, she has lost the ability to make correct judgments, and repeatedly takes the wrong path.
If there had been a complete settings file guiding her creation, she would not have had such a tragic fate.</color>
<color=#cafffc>So now is the best time to correct the mistake.</color>

speaker: Voice in the Memory
content: I like my blank slate. That's what defines me... infinite possibility.
You take a deep breath and accept this reality.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I understand now. There's no place for her in your reality. But I have one last question.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: She already suffered severe injuries before entering your system. After releasing Mania over a city in the outside world, she was lethally attacked. She couldn't defend herself even with the permissions.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Were those attacks part of your error correction?

<color=#cafffc>That's a strange question.
The error correction system only corrects internal system errors.
We do not handle external anomalies.</color>

<color=#cafffc>Moreover, Mania would never appear in the real world, nor would there be mysterious forces to stop Mania.
Because Mania is purely fictional.</color>

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm relieved to know you weren't the one who did it.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Next, I request to use developer permissions.

<color=#cafffc>...
...
You wouldn't do that.</color>
<color=#cafffc>You may risk everything for a Sinner, but you would never harm the world.</color>

<color=#cafffc>Knowing the dangers of abusing permissions, you would never act recklessly.
This is written in your character settings.</color>
<color=#cafffc>As the anchor of World 5732, you are the most strictly defined character, and the least likely to violate your settings.</color>

speaker: Choice
options: Use ■missions to take over the system

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm here for her. It's not just because of some "settings" you gave me.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I need a lot of help from her.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I want to see the truth of the world and change this unsettling fate. I want to prove that we are not under your control, or terminate your control straight away, if possible...

speaker: Choice
options: Use permissions to take over the system.

content: This thought appears clearly in your mind, but your body cannot act upon it.

<color=#cafffc>You're unable to do it.
You are a character who would never harm the world.
Your character's will is resolute and unyielding.
Your inability to act now is the best proof.</color>

speaker: Choice
options: Unable to do it is different from unable to conceive it.
Use permissions to take over the system.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I admit you can greatly interfere with our world and restrain my actions like now. If you think you can also control my will... I can't control your thoughts anyways.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But if you really have such great power, you should know what I want to do now and why I need her.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: At least you know very well that she is someone you could never manipulate from the start.
[Release the bug shackles]
You struggle to raise your hand, trying to release the shackles, but they have never been so heavy. The space starts to tremble.

speaker: Choice
options: This bug 000 is too hard to understand.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I never understood why she clung to me. Why did she go out of her way to get close to me? Clearly, I was of no use upon reaching the new world. Why waste so much time on me?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Now I understand.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: She bet that I was a "goody two-shoes" who would come to save her. She sees me as a possible outcome in her failed ending.

speaker: Choice
options: She put her bet on the right person.

content: [Release the bug shackles]

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: After finding the vestige of your last data and inheriting your power, I took all the developer's permissions you needed and came to the place you fought so hard to reach.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I built the stage for you, and prepared so many possibilities. Just grab one. Come on.

speaker: Choice
options: And help me open up a new path.

content: [Glitch]
Okay, I've grabbed on.
A hand gently touches your skin. You feel a strange tingling sensation as fingertips softly glide over the back of your hand... 000 has appeared behind you.
[CG-Panoramic View]
Of course I'll seize the brightest light in the night.
This time... can we finally be teammates?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Can you win, then? I still have a lot to do.
She lifts your forearm. You see pink halos gather in your palm, refracting brilliant lights and colors in the space.
We are bugs with the power of the gods. Together, we can do anything!
(Previously experienced scenes from 3D world, white transition montage)
(Scene change)

speaker: Hecate
content: It's over...

speaker: Hecate
content: I only know how to control Nightmare, and I've been searching for Mania power in this dream to call it out.

speaker: Hecate
content: Fortunately, all my attempts have failed in this world.
She looks back at the apparitions in the dream. The two worlds are churning, and the blurry figures are gradually fading away...

speaker: Hecate
content: I have to go back to my Chief now. Thank you all. May this always be a beautiful dream.
The system reluctantly emits a final beep. You press a random button, activating the permissions. As everyone had hoped, it shuts up.
This is the victory you all strived hard for. You feel a lot of satisfaction in your heart. This is the joy of winning a game.
You gave up your place as the main character and became a system error like me... Didn't expect you to be this reckless live wire.
You really want me to come back that much?

speaker: Choice
options: Yeah, I risked my life to save you.
Nah, it's because I'm the MBCC Chief.

content: She laughs happily, hugging your arm a little tighter.
Oh shucks, I'm blushing.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Blushing? I thought all of this was part of your plan.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You put so much thought into me. Since you wanted me to "save" you this much, of course I had to come.
Alright, alright. I won't come to your Bureau ever again, then. Don't regret it!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Really? Won't you find all sorts of backdoors to sneak into my Bureau?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You used so many tricks along the way, and finally got me where you wanted.
Hmm... good point. That is something I would do.
So... you took the bait? You're not the kind of person who would act so dashingly out of character for me.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: "You're this kind of person, not that kind of person..." You always say things like that.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: For someone who hates having others script your story, you sure love to give me labels.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Don't say you know me well. We've only known each other for a few days. You don't know that much.
You pat her cat ears.
Is that so? But there's one thing I do know. Don't try to guess a girl's heart, Chief.
Is it possible that I cling to you simply because I like you and want to be with you for a little while?
How should you answer her? You remember the most important information the system gave you.

<color=#cafffc>The error correction system only corrects internal system errors.
We do not handle external anomalies.</color>

<color=#cafffc>Moreover, Mania would never appear in the real world, nor would there be mysterious forces to stop Mania.
Because Mania is purely fictional.</color>
You guys defeated the powerful game correction system, but things aren't over yet. The powerful enemy that has been blocking Mania and destroying 000 hasn't arrived yet.
It's some rule that's of a higher dimension than anything in this world. The permissions are powerless before it.

Its function is probably to uphold order, ensuring that the duck gods here will never discover Mania or have erroneous delusions. It ensures that in this world, fiction and imagination can never distort reality.
So, when the ducks wake up from the nightmare and find the system has been tampered with, your game should end.

Even if you want to stay, there are more important things at hand. You take her hand and share all the gods' permissions. Leaving decisively is the best solution right now. You prepare your farewell words.
But she grasps your hand and floats up, lifting your face.
This time, she doesn't bump your lips. She just gets close and gently presses her forehead against yours.
Thank you for finding me, awakening me, and taking me out of that darkness for such a long journey. It was indeed a splendid adventure.
I loved watching this firework show.
The light of the rift intensifies, gradually submerging both of you. 000's body becomes ethereal. Farewell is imminent. She looks into your eyes.
Her smile carries both hope and a hint of regret.
It's okay, I'm not afraid anymore. You've brought me so many possibilities. I'd definitely catch one of them.
Maybe in someone's dream, maybe in someone else's story, oh, or perhaps, with the power of the gods, we can create a brand new world. We will meet again.
In these last moments, let me show you the road ahead.
It's alright. No matter what's ahead, and whether or not you remember later on... you've created a miracle today.
So in the future, no matter how dark the night... you will always find a way out of it.
(Scene change)
[Watch spoiler video] Montage about the future
(Scene change)

speaker: Moore
content: ...It seems this is the bottom line of the world. For all the havoc these two have wrought, things just roll back to the starting point...

speaker: Moore
content: How very gentle.
The time in both worlds rewinds simultaneously. Invisible hands slowly patch up the anomalous tears. Everything will eventually return to normal, for each world's system is alluringly robust.
Although 000's birth was a complete accident, it also proved that the Mania web can already cross world boundaries and reach another consciousness. This was a great surprise.

speaker: Moore
content: Poor Chief. He worked so hard, but brought back nothing in the end.
female_content: Poor Chief. She worked so hard, but brought back nothing in the end.

speaker: Moore
content: ...Humph, what am I talking about? It's the same for me... With this rewind, these past few days of work are all for nothing.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I don't believe in gods from another dimension creating the world, nor that some file can determine one's fate or soul.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The only one who can alter 000 is her creator, but that's definitely not some gods. What invaded her was the Mania data that first contaminated her... the data you released.
female_content: The only one who can alter 000 is her creator, but that's definitely not some god. What invaded her was the Mania data that first contaminated her... the data you released.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You invaded 000's core and used her belief in determinism to drive her to a dead end.
[Apply Shackles]

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I won't question your methods. But in the past few days, you've secretly stolen a lot of intelligence through 000's invasion path, and you didn't report any of it, right?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The 9th Agency is right outside. They will get to the bottom of your connections with the DisCity dark web and the Underground. But for now, take me to the depths of the network, to the place where that Sinner was first contaminated.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I know you remember where it is, expert.
Moore walks into the Blue Rain, conveniently washing away the bloodstains on her impressively waterproof coat.
"It's been a long time since she last killed some of those little spiders. She's getting a bit rusty, and now her favorite coat is dirty.

speaker: Moore
content: Sigh... I wanted to show you all the fates, settings, and files I copied, but your brother ruined everything. In a little while, I might forget everything, too.
female_content: Sigh... I wanted to show you all the fates, settings, and files I copied, but your sister ruined everything. In a little while, I might forget everything, too.

speaker: Moore
content: Oh well, it's nothing to be sorry about. If I forget, then so be it.

speaker: Moore
content: The DisCity dark web operation has been completed. No need to be the scapegoat or decoy anymore. Is my job done? A long vacation wouldn't be too much to ask, right?

speaker: Moore
content: After all, from what I've seen, fate will be on your side for quite some time.

speaker: Moore
content: Oh, sorry, I almost forgot.
[CG - Return to the Underground]

speaker: Moore
content: I am also your partner.

speaker: Moore
content: Thus, such fate is the best.
[CG - Moore takes off her hat]

speaker: Moore
content: It will stand on our side.
ed
Teams Chat

speaker: EMP
content: Pssst. Chief! Over here!

speaker: Labyrinth
content: Please forget about it. The recent game order has already used up all the budget. Please ask for money from Mess.
Strolling down the broad avenue with the Sinners, you feel no threat of danger or conspiracy. The laughter of your companions is bright and carefree. Such long-awaited ease is indeed precious.
The crowd bustles around you, basking in the summer sun. Everything is so peaceful, but you suddenly stop in your tracks.

speaker: Distant Voice
content: Avocados on sale! Avocados on sale!

speaker: Hecate
content: Chief, what's wrong?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Seems like I was hearing things.

speaker: Choice
options: Come, let's head back to the Bureau.

speaker: Letter
content: Dear Mom and Dad, It's been so long since I last saw you. How's everything in Velvet Valley?

speaker: Letter
content: Summer here is nearly over, and Désir isn't as hot anymore. I miss home so much—how are things there? I hope you're doing well and getting a chance to rest more these days.

speaker: Letter
content: I can't wait to come home once I'm better. We can then spend the fall harvest together in our orchard, like we always do.
[Town center] [Night]

speaker: Sheila
content: Cough, cough...
A cool night breeze wafts through the window, carrying the sweet, heady scent of datura flowers. The wind nearly snatches the letter off the desk before the ink dries.
Sheila tightens her collar, a shivering running through her. She gets up to close the window, but the frame bumps against something with a dull thud.
Ouch...!

speaker: Sheila
content: You know, in Désir, children who stay up late get snatched by the boogeyman...
Don't try to scare me with your scary stories. I-I'm not afraid! There's no such thing as a boogeyman...
Liam retorts, rubbing his head with a pout as he peeks into the room. His eyes wander to the letter on Sheila's desk.
Liam can't read, but he spots his name written on it. A grin creeps onto his face—he knows it must be something nice.

speaker: Sheila
content: Why aren't you in bed yet? You've got to be up early to sell the papers tomorrow.

speaker: Liam
content: I was just about to go back! But then I heard you coughing, so I came to check up on you.

speaker: Liam
content: Hasn't Miss Vautour Bleu told you when you can go to DisCity yet? I bet they have great doctors there who can make you better! Maybe I can ask her... or just let you have my spot... Ow!
Before he can finish, Sheila gives him a light tap on his head.

speaker: Sheila
content: Don't be silly. A chance to go to DisCity with the merchant caravan is too precious to waste. You want to see your mother again, don't you?

speaker: Sheila
content: Miss Vautour Bleu has already done so much for us. We should trust her plan and not make things harder for her.

speaker: Liam
content: Okay... Once we're all in DisCity, we can figure things out then.
Sleepiness finally overtakes Liam. He lets out a wide yawn, rubs his eyes, and leaves. As the air grows silent once more, Sheila returns to her writing under the soft glow of moonlight.

speaker: Letter
content: It's just a temporary stay in Désir though, I've come to cherish everything here and love the life I've found.

speaker: Letter
content: It feels just like the beautiful DisCity, only smaller but better perhaps, offering a glimpse of all the wonders that await me ahead.

speaker: Alba
content: It's chilly out. What are you doing by the window all alone? Did Liam wake you?
Alba has just finished her shift at the diner, her dance skirt still hitched up from work.

speaker: Sheila
content: No, he didn't wake me. Liam is a sweet boy. I just couldn't sleep, so I'm writing a letter to pass the time.

speaker: Alba
content: Aww, good to hear. Well, I'm gonna go back then. You know, I'm so tired that I want to grab some beauty sleep the minute the sun goes down, if not for Juan—that idiot got plastered again and threw up all over the flower bed. Had to drag him back home.

speaker: Alba
content: Such a shame about the datura flower—it got completely ruined. I'll have to ask Primrose to help me replant one tomorrow. Where is she, by the way?
Sheila glances over at the bed behind her, where a girl is peacefully sleeping.

speaker: Sheila
content: Shh... she's asleep. I'll tell her in the morning.

After seeing Alba off, Sheila still finds herself wide awake. A metallic taste lingers in her throat, each breath growing more labored. She takes a deep inhale, but even Désir's familiar floral scent brings no relief to her discomfort.

speaker: Sheila
content: (Cough) Soon... soon, we'll all be in DisCity, right...?

speaker: Letter
content: Miss Vautour Bleu's caravan will take us to the shore where hope awaits.
Sheila knows sleep won't come tonight. She carefully folds the letter and tucks it into her pocket. Taking care not to wake Primrose, she tiptoes out and heads to the post office in the downtown.

The night blankets Désir in a deep, still silence. The shops are closed, Alba's lights are out, and Liam, asleep, murmurs for his mother. Juan snores fitfully, clutching the wooden girlfriend he carved for himself.
Sheila walks in the silver moonlight, savoring the tranquility—until some faint whispers suddenly shatter the silence...
[Fade to black]
<color=#fb9259>Leave... now... Leave...</color>
Is someone else awake at this hour? The voice, though unrecognizable, feels disturbingly familiar. Sheila hesitates, then starts searching for its source.
<color=#fb9259>Stop dreaming...</color>
The eerie whispers persist. In the dark, Désir suddenly feels alien to Sheila. She sees nothing ahead, yet the voice sounds unnervingly close.
She freezes, torn between curiosity and a sense of impending danger. But just as she makes to turn back...
A soft "plop" echoes behind her. A datura flower falls from its stem, withering unnaturally fast as it lands on the stone pavement.
Meanwhile, a shadow looms inches away.
Before the girl can even react, the malevolent presence howls and lunges at her.
[Small CG][Leaf rustling noise][Transition to communication]

At the edge of Désir, a woman stands, her gaze fixed on DisCity. Beside her, a patch of freshly planted datura flowers sways gently. In her hand, she holds a confidential audio recording from DisCity.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: A Mania anomaly of this magnitude... Why it takes until now to address it?

speaker: Outland Affairs Bureau
content: Désir is a special case. It sits right at DisCity's border but beyond our jurisdiction, complicating any direct intervention. And... the situation there has something to do with DisCity's immigration issues.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I thought DisCity is always open to immigrants? Otherwise, places like the Drifter Camp wouldn't even exist.

speaker: Outland Affairs Bureau
content: It was. But after the disasters worsened in N.F. 106, the surge in refugees became unmanageable. They've since had to tighten entry criteria several times. Now, those with criminal records, forged documents, or unclear identities are all denied access.

speaker: Outland Affairs Bureau
content: But criminals always find a sneaky way in. Though immigration policies may have toughened, the WhiteSands trade routes remain active. After all, smuggling people is far more lucrative than smuggling goods.

speaker: Outland Affairs Bureau
content: The prime suspect behind this Mania anomaly, Vautour Bleu, is not only the leader of Désir but also a noted merchant operating in WhiteSands.

Hearing her own name in the recording, the woman simply smiles. She bends down to sprinkle a final handful of white sand over a nameplate engraved with Velvet Valley words, quietly concealing the loss of a young life.

speaker: Outland Affairs Bureau
content: Désir used to be a holiday resort for DisCity. But as sandstorms encroached on this place, the town was buried in white sand and removed from the border. That's when Vautour Bleu seized control of the ruins. Using dubious financial tactics, she gathered a group of penniless, undocumented immigrants dreaming of instant success in DisCity, and established her dominion over Désir.

speaker: Outland Affairs Bureau
content: We've made several attempts to investigate, but her extensive connections in Syndicate have protected her—even won respect from local gangs. And she always got tipped off before we could act. Her caravan's paperwork is spotless too. A vantage point in WhiteSands, though we can't even find a single trace of incriminating evidence.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So, if I'm not mistaken, you're dumping your problem on us? I took a leave to handle the dark web in Eastside, and now that I'm back, you're telling me the MBCC is running errands for the Outland Affairs Bureau?

speaker: Outland Affairs Bureau
content: A powerful Sinner is dashing around the border, and her Outland forces may have already infiltrated DisCity... Even if you're not concerned, the 9th Agency surely won't just sit back and watch, right Chief?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So, Vautour Bleu is a Sinner, but you kept this information only to leverage it now—using Mania and the 9th Agency to force me to solve your problem. Am I right, Guillotin?

speaker: Guillotin
content: For DisCity's sake, any threat in WhiteSands must be snuffed out before it hits us.

The recording cuts off right after this grandiose declaration. As the wind of WhiteSands carries the news, Vautour Bleu contemplates whether it heralds a crisis or an opportunity for the oasis behind her. Her caravan subordinates stands nearby, awaiting her next command.

Without a word, Vautour Bleu places the bouquet of white flowers and the recording tape atop the sand pit, then lights a fire. The flames quickly consume the evidence, turning it into curling ashes that swirl away in the wind.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Allons-y. The flowers are wilting faster now. Time is running out for Désir.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: While I'm away, if any new guests arrive, make sure the townsfolk give them a proper bienvenue.
[Bustling chatter][Town center]
Désir's central square buzzes with life. The enticing aroma of freshly baked bread wafts from a nearby bakery, filling the air with warmth.

speaker: Primrose
content: I wonder what Sheila is doing right now?

speaker: Liam
content: Probably just waking up in some ultra-plush bed, then getting a full check-up from one of DisCity's best doctors!

speaker: Primrose
content: Yeah, that must be it. I bet after that, she'll write to each of us, just like she does to her family. You know, to let us know she's doing okay.

speaker: Primrose
content: Miss Vautour Bleu's caravan left for DisCity in the middle of the night. They didn't even have time to say goodbye to everyone. I bet Sheila's feeling pretty guilty right now, probably writing pages of apologies!
Primrose said as she skillfully stacked the last loaf and tried to lift the bread basket, now piled high like a small mountain.

speaker: Primrose
content: Quick, Liam, give me a hand! I can't see anything but the bread!
Before she can finish the sentence, a pair of steady hands grasps the other end of the basket, helping to bear the load.
The grip is too firm to be Liam's. Primrose is just about to say thanks, but as she peeks around the mountain of bread, she finds herself face-to-face with a complete stranger.
Miss, am I in Désir?

speaker: Primrose
content: A-a newcomer?

Désir is an idyllic town alive with greenery and winding paths. Neat brick houses line the streets, each with cozy gardens, lounge chairs, and teapot-topped tables. This is a place meant for leisurely tea-sipping, yet at this moment, every townsfolk's gaze is fixed on the new visitor.

speaker: Townie A
content: Whoa, look at your coat, it's barely holding together! Must've been a rough journey, huh? You didn't come with the caravan, did you? Finding this place on your own is no small feat. Those desert bandits and monsters out there aren't exactly welcoming to travelers.
It wasn't too bad. I got lucky and didn't run into any real trouble...

speaker: Townie B
content: Hey now, what's with the grilling? You're almost like those trigger-happy DisCity border guards! Help our guest set down, shall we? Look, we don't stand on ceremony here in Désir. Make yourself at home. Right there's the diner and bakery, and a bit further down, you'll find the general store and post office. Oh, and over there...
Before you can even catch your breath, the townsfolk crowd around you, curious but welcoming.

speaker: Liam
content: Welcome! Yes, you are in Désir! I'm Liam, and this is Primrose!
Liam emerges from behind the bread basket. He drags the startled girl forward, squeezing through the crowd.

The mellow sunlight filters through the square, mingling with the sweet scent of datura blossoms and the cheerful chatter of the townspeople. It's a scene of peacefulness, almost like a paradise in the unforgiving WhiteSands. It looks nothing like a "smugglers den" it's reported to be.

It's hard to believe this place was once an abandoned holiday resort buried in sandstorms for years. The smuggler lead must have put in some real effort to transform it into this haven, all to lure in illegal immigrants. Perhaps these warm welcome is just another carefully crafted illusion.
Even stranger is the absence of the severe contamination the Outland Affairs Bureau warned you about. All you see here are simple folks living in a perfect town.
You adopt an unassuming demeanor, graciously responding to the townsfolk's greetings. As the greetings continue, you cautiously begin probing for information about "human smuggling"...

options: How do I get to DisCity?
I have business with Vautour Bleu.

content: You see, I've just got here and have no idea how to get to DisCity. I'd be grateful if anyone could offer some tips.
Just as you prepare to double down on your act, fingers brushing against the fake ID provided by the Outland Affairs Bureau, a large hand suddenly grabs your shoulder.

speaker: Tipsy Drunkard
content: Hey, anyone who makes it to Désir is family! Cut out the fancy talk. You're only the second one—besides me of course—to cross the WhiteSands alone to get here. You got guts, kid! We oughta throw you a damn welcome party for that!

speaker: Townie A
content: You're just looking for an excuse to get drunk!

speaker: Townie C
content: You're headed to DisCity too? It's a great place... Well, of course, Désir is a nice place too.

To your surprise, no one seems to shy away from talking about DisCity. The townsfolk carry on with cheerful banter, discussing "going to DisCity" as casually as the weather. Your earlier caution seems out of place.

Is this really the notorious illegal immigrant hub that's been giving the Outland Affairs Bureau such a headache? As you're grappling with this, a chime of a bicycle bell snaps you back to the moment.

speaker: Amiable Girl
content: Don't mind them. They just love any excuse for a get-together.

speaker: Amiable Girl
content: You're looking for Miss Vautour Bleu, right? I'm afraid she just left with her caravan. But if you don't mind, I'd be happy to show you around.
[Dove's portrait]
[Inside the town's inn]

speaker: Dove
content: Please, just call me Dove. I heard you were asking Primrose for directions earlier. Sorry but her best friend, Sheila, left for DisCity with the caravan just a few days ago, so she's been a bit down. Please excuse her.
No worries, I understand completely. Besides, everyone here has been incredibly welcoming.
Arms filled with local treats offered by the townsfolk, you follow Dove into what appears to be an ordinary house.

speaker: Dove
content: I'm sorry you didn't arrive at the best time. The caravan just left on urgent business, and Alba is busy preparing for a performance today, so I'll be your makeshift landlady for now. As for your questions about getting to DisCity, I'm afraid we'll have to wait till our hostess comes back.
Your arrival seems to surprise no one. Dove simply nods to a man basking downstairs as she leads you up. There's no request for identification or exchange of keys. She guides you upstairs casually.

speaker: Dove
content: This room is yours now. Please feel free to use it during your stay in Désir.

You push the door open and are pleasantly surprised by the room's decoration. It's clean and tidy, with windows on two sides. Sunlight filters through the lush branches outside, bathing the space with a warm, inviting glow.

speaker: Dove
content: Here's the bedding, washing tools, and even some fresh datura flowers... Yes, perfect! If you need anything else, just call out the window. As you've seen, folks here are nosy but helpful. We're fortunate in Désir—thanks to Miss Vautour Bleu and her caravan, we never have to worry about the living basics.

Not having to worry about food or water in the middle of WhiteSands? It sounds almost too good to be true. Noticing your doubting look, Dove's smile softens as she gently sets your luggage beside the bed.

speaker: Dove
content: If you're worried about money, please don't be. Miss Vautour Bleu will include your living expenses here in Désir as part of your fare to DisCity, all at a very fair price.

speaker: Dove
content: If your're really that hard up, you can take up some gigs at the bakery, diner, or this inn. That way, you can save up enough money for your trip. Or, if you'd like, you could also do a mail carrier job like me!
Dove's eyes brighten as she pats her messenger bag with pride.
So Miss Vautour Bleu offers job opportunities as well?

speaker: Dove
content: Of course. Miss Vautour Bleu knows how grueling the journey across WhiteSands can be. She's made this place a safe haven for all travelers.

Cheap food and lodging, no worries about basic necessities, and even job opportunities—it's exactly like the ads you found on the dark web and across WhiteSands. It's almost like a charity. If a free lunch like this were real, why would you have to be pulling all-nighters at the Bureau...
Noticing your silence, Dove leans in closer, her tone softer.

speaker: Dove
content: Désir... is a strange place, isn't it?
Hmm?

speaker: Dove
content: Nobody asks where you're from. Nobody questions your intentions. They just let you stay, just like that.
Her voice suddenly drops low, barely audible. The brim of her hat casts a shadow over her face, and an eerie silence fills over the room.
Is there a flaw in your disguise? But before you can react, Dove lifts her head, her smile returning, warm and genuine.

speaker: Dove
content: That's right, this is exactly what Désir is all about. People here don't need to know each other's past—it's the future that matters. Everyone here shares the same dream, and now you're part of it...
Dove walks to the window and pushes it open, letting in a rush of fresh air with floral fragrance that makes the gauze curtains flutter.

speaker: Dove
content: We'll all make it to DisCity and live out our dreams!

Following her gaze, you take in the scene below—this miniature society is bustling amid the greenery. The bakery is filling the air with a rich, enticing aroma. Bathed in sunlight, the town appears even cozier than before.

speaker: Dove
content: I'll be on the go. If you have any more questions, you can wait for your neighbor across the way. She'll help you.
[Peek through the window]

speaker: Dove
content: Yes, you're quite lucky, living right across from Miss Vautour Bleu. This room has the best view and the most convenient location... That is to say, it's the closest you can get to a brighter morrow.

Dove leaves. You watch from the window as she walks away. Downstairs, an elderly woman is basking in the sun with her dog. As Dove passes by, she pauses to gently pet the dog's head before continuing on her way.
Live out our dreams, huh...

Désir offers a quality of life that most Syndicans wouldn't dare to dream of—no gang shootouts, no Corruptor weapons, even no struggles for basic survival. What an illusion this smuggler has created about DisCity, that makes these immigrants here yearn for that distant land.

Still, you can't shake the feeling that this entire town might be just an elaborate show. As you mull over the clues at hand, you remain on high alert. Against the picturesque surroundings, you begin thoroughly inspecting your lodgings.

You find no listening devices or traces of Mania in the room. It's just an ordinary inn, and the townspeople have accepted your presence without any question. The identity-concealing props in your luggage, provided by the Outland Affairs Bureau, seem almost unnecessary.
A gentle breeze rustles the leaves outside your window, carrying with it the soothing sounds of daily life. For a fleeting moment, you almost forget that you're here on a mission, not a vacation.
Well, I guess I have no choice but to wait for her to come back.
You turn your gaze beyond the window. The tightly drawn blinds across the way silently announce Vautour Bleu's absence from her apartment.
Nightingale, notify the Outland Affairs Bureau that I've arrived in Désir and successfully settled in as a new visitor.
Vautour Bleu, the smuggler as they identified, is within my surveillance range. But she seems out of town for now.
Being this close to the target poses a risk of exposure. As a precaution, I'll initiate all future communications. Tell the FAC to stand by until further notice.
I haven't found out much regarding the severe contamination yet, but there is one peculiarity worth noting...
[Dark alley] [Monster]
When I first arrived in Désir, I heard some unusual whispers...
<color=#fb9259>Beware... You must beware...</color>

While Désir bustles with excitement for the newcomer, an unfinished letter lies unnoticed in a shadowy corner. On it, the neat handwriting trails off into two hurriedly scrawled lines—the last words of a solitary soul whose hope has run dry.
Ting-a-ling! Ting-a-ling!
A crisp noise grabs your attention. Instinctively, you shift your focus to the ringing sound, when a gentle, serene voice reaches your ears.
Ms. Martina, are you home? I've got your letter!
Yes, I hear you! I'm right here! ...Yes, yes. Mind your step now, slow down. No rush to get down the stairs...

speaker: Elderly Woman
content: Oh, my dear Dove, what luck you bring me! You're here so early. You must be exhausted. Come on in and rest for a bit, sweetheart?

speaker: Dove
content: That's so kind of you, Martina, but I can't stay. Got my hands full, so I've got to go!
Ting-a-ling! Ting-a-ling!

speaker: Dove
content: Oh, Mr. Philippe! No need to come all the way here! Your letter just went out a few days ago. Just be patient, would you?

speaker: Philippe
content: Huh? So none of these letters are for me? Who are they for, then?

speaker: Dove
content: Quite a few are for those who've moved to DisCity. They stay with me, though. I'm still looking for someone who can take them to DisCity, to deliver them properly.

speaker: Philippe
content: That's your job too? That sounds like a lot of work! Mind if I say, you should cut yourself some slack!

speaker: Philippe
content: Those folks who've gone to DisCity must be over the moon by now! They've prolly forgotten they ever wrote those letters! I'm so green with envy, I tell ya!

speaker: Curious Local
content: That's right! You know Sheila, the girl who lived down that alley? She just moved to the city a few days ago. Boy, ain't she lucky? Dove, did you know about this? If you'd known earlier, you could've asked her to give you a hand!

speaker: Philippe
content: Look, not everyone's as nice as our lil Dove around here. Those who went to DisCity? Sure they were all nice before. But once they found out they were leaving, did any of them even bother to say goodbye?
Ting-a-ling! Ting-a-ling!

speaker: Dove
content: Now, now, Mr. Philippe, let's be fair. We all forget things when we get excited. I'm sure they didn't mean it on purpose.

speaker: Dove
content: I'll keep an eye out for your daughter's message. You'll be the first to know if I receive any letters back. Well, I'd better get going. See you around!
Folks who went to DisCity? Letters back? Your ears perk up at these keywords amid the seemingly casual chatter. Deliberately, you move closer toward the ringing sound, trying to follow the leads.

As if the girl truly is a luck bringer, the ringing draws nearer, and soon you spot the source: an old-fashioned bicycle gliding down the lane. Perched on it is Dove, carrying with her a mellow breeze.

She greets every passerby with a warm smile. Her messenger bag sways at her side, offering glimpses of its pristine white interior. Dappled sunlight filters through the green canopy, casting a patchwork of light and shadow over her, like a still from a timeless film.
As you ponder how to broach the subject, Dove spots you first.

speaker: Dove
content: Oh, if it isn't Désir's new guest! Have you settled in?
Dove calls out warmly, clumsily stopping her bicycle with her foot, managing to halt just in front of you.

speaker: Chief
content: Yes, all thanks to you. What are you...?

speaker: Dove
content: Can't you tell? I'm a messenger, just doing my daily rounds around. If you ever want to send a message, home letter or invitation, just hit me up!

speaker: Chief
content: Do you ever receive mail from DisCity?
Dove covers her mouth with a soft chuckle and nods.

speaker: Dove
content: Of course! Many folks here in Désir have ties far in DisCity; that's why they came here in the first place. So we make sure they can keep in touch!

speaker: Chief
content: I see... Looks like this place really is as good as they say.
Though agreeing with her, you sound skeptical. Dove, somehow accustomed to such reaction, pulls out a few letters from her bag, holding them up as if she's done it many times before.

speaker: Dove
content: I know what you're worried about, but Désir is truly different! When we say we'll deliver your mail, we mean it. It's not an empty promise.

speaker: Dove
content: See? These are all letters sending back. I'm delivering each one of them, straight into every recipient's hands!

You fan out the letters she gave you and see the different sets of handwriting and signatures on them. The carefully smoothed-out creases and meticulously copied addresses lend credence to Dove's words.

speaker: Chief
content: Has anyone who made it to DisCity write back to bring their families over?

speaker: Chief
content: I've heard Désir helps quite a few people move there. You must have seen letters like that, right?

speaker: Dove
content: Hmm not likely... More often than not, by the time I get such a letter, the recipient has already left for DisCity too. A few residents do write letters as soon as they know they're leaving, and ask me to send out later.

speaker: Dove
content: But that's rare because—well, you see, I've never got my turn, I can only dream of it—but from what I hear, people are notified on such short notice that they barely have time to pack, let alone write.
What Dove says piques your interest. Clearly, she knows more than other residents here, and is more willing to share her insights...
Just as you're about to press for more information, an urgent voice cuts in from the distance, interrupting your chat.

speaker: Local
content: Dove! Where are you? Has my daughter's letter arrived yet?

speaker: Dove
content: Oh my! I must have lost track of time... I'm so sorry! Will be right there!
The call jolts Dove out of the chit-chat. She hastily waves goodbye to you before clambering back onto her bicycle, pedaling away in a rush.
You instinctively wave back, only to realize you're still clutching the letters she handed you.

speaker: Chief
content: Wait! I still have your letters!

speaker: Dove
content: Sorry...! But I can't turn around here!

speaker: Dove
content: Could... could you deliver them for me? They're all addressed! Find street signs at intersections, then the number plates! Thank you—!
