Dove's voice is swallowed by the breeze, fading into the distance. You watch her pedal away, struggling to keep her balance while trying to fish letters out of her bag. You let out a small sigh.

speaker: Chief
content: Guess she literally has her hands full... Alright, I'll deliver them.

speaker: Chief
content: Might be a perfect chance to get to know the town's layout and its residents.
[Town center]
<color=#fb9259>Leave... Leave...</color>

The eerie whispers still linger near your ears, yet the townsfolk seem unaware of any disturbance. Your investigation so far suggests they are indeed just ordinary immigrants, drawn here by simple dreams. They revere and trust Vautour Bleu, blissfully awaiting the day to move to DisCity.
It's mid-afternoon while the diner is already closing for the day. Liam stretches up on his tiptoes to help hang the Closed sign on the door.

speaker: Liam
content: Time for a clock-out shot! Alba, look over here—snap, snap!
Though exhausted from a day's work, Alba musters the energy to humor Liam, striking a few poses for his toy camera.

speaker: Liam
content: Miss Vautour Bleu says I can get a real camera in DisCity. When we're there, I'll take your picture, Alba! It'll be just as beautiful as the one of my Mom!

speaker: Alba
content: Oh my, then I must sign up for a beauty pageant with that photo!

speaker: Juan
content: Oh crap, that pageant my ass. It's all about the prize money, ain't it?

speaker: Alba
content: Shut it, Juan. It's an honor! You think everyone's like you? Get drunk and yack at Miss Vautour Bleu's door, "Hypercube is my true love! I'mma make tons of Hypercubes in DisCity!" Eww.

speaker: Liam
content: Oh... How many cameras can I buy with one Hypercube?

speaker: Primrose
content: Mmm... I'm not quite sure... but I guess you can buy a whole sack of bread with one Hypercube!

Hypercubes are a strictly regulated resource in DisCity; even Vautour Bleu can't sneak any out to satisfy their curiosity. The group's noisy banter leads nowhere as they while away the last moments before sunset. However, none of them notices the strange voice murmuring in the shadows.
<color=#fb9259>Beware... You must beware...</color>
The whisper creeps close and becomes more distinct. You glance around but see nothing. Primrose, however, seems to notice your unusual behavior.

speaker: Primrose
content: Are you looking for something?

options: Did you hear any strange noise?

speaker: Primrose
content: Noise? Hmm... Maybe it's the sound of the caravan coming back?
No. It sounded more like... someone talking.

speaker: Primrose
content: Usually everyone's heading home around now. Maybe you're overhearing someone grumbling about their day?
Primrose turns back to say something more, but the cloaked figure she was talking to is already gone.
[Dark alley]
<color=#fb9259>Must tell them...</color>
<color=#fb9259>I'm... going to...</color>

Following the whispers, you slip away from the crowds and head deeper into the town. Here, the ever-present datura flowers are surprisingly nowhere to be seen. The walls bear marks of once-lush vines, now only left with withered branches and sparse yellow leaves.
It's as if an invisible barrier is blocking out the sunlight, casting only layer upon layer of oppressive shadows over everything.
The whispers seems to creep close from all sides.
<color=#fb9259>Désir... destroy...</color>
<color=#fb9259>I... destroy...</color>
The voices hover in the air, plucking at your nerves like unseen fingers. Yet, the dark alley stretching ahead remains eerily empty.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Is there anything I can help you with?
The moment the words leave your lips, the whispers cease entirely. A complete silence engulfs the alley, thick and suffocating.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Can you hear me?

You take another cautious step forward. Only silence responds. Save for the soft crunch of moss beneath your boots, you only catch faint sounds of Alba and the others in the distance as the town continues its leisure afternoon.
Was it all in your head? You cast one last glance into the depths of the shadows. Seeing nothing, you make to leave...
Plop. A datura flower withers and drops at your feet all of a sudden.
At the same moment, an icy touch crawls up your shoulder. In the shadows something slowly swells and flows, trying to envelop you within its mass.
As the surrounding vegetation withers rapidly, the air grows heavy, filled again with elusive whispers.
A silhouette gradually takes shape before you. There's no mistaking it, what follows is the familiar feeling of...
Mania!
[avg]
The shackles tear through the oppressive gloom, plunging the alley back into silence. The haunting whispers have vanished; even the wind has stilled.
The report indicated that the M-Value near Désir was approaching disaster range. Yet the contamination you felt just now was mild compared to that... There must be something more.

speaker: Unknown Girl
content: Do you like Désir?
A clear, sweet greeting interrupts the silence. A blonde girl is standing just beyond the shadows.
Betwixt the silent valley and veiled sky, a ray of sunlight falls upon the girl, its golden hue so soft it seems to envelop her in a gossamer veil, lending an ethereal quality to her presence.

speaker: Unknown Girl
content: Do you like Désir?
She repeats, her tone calm yet unsettlingly similar to the whispers you've since heard.
[Dark alley]
The girl stands still in the sunlight, her gaze calm, awaiting an answer from you.
Noticing your hesitation, she responds with a polite smile before turning her glance upward to the veiled sky.

speaker: Unknown Girl
content: I liked it here. Seeing everyone here carrying hope in their hearts, all working together toward a common goal.
Her expression is gentle, her voice soft and her demeanor harmless. Yet her gaze directs toward some distant point beyond you.

You turn to look in the direction of her gaze, but see nothing unusual. The townsfolk in the square are still going about their day. Is she speaking to you? Her tone gives no indication, but there's no one else in the dark alley.

options: Did you see the shadows here just now?

content: The girl doesn't answer. Instead, she smiles softly as she caresses the drooping flower stems. At her touch, another datura blossom withers and falls.

speaker: Unknown Girl
content: We all believe Désir is our gateway to DisCity. Miss Vautour Bleu says we're just a step away from the life of our dreams. You believe that too...

speaker: Unknown Girl
content: Don't you?
The sweet floral scent and warm sunlight seem to dissolve, replaced by a thickening miasma of contamination. Your instincts sharpen—this girl is no ordinary local.

speaker: Unknown Girl
content: Have you ever been to DisCity?
The girl seems oblivious to your growing wariness, her tone unchanged, as if lost in a reverie.
Only from what I've seen in the papers... I guess?
Unfazed by your evasive answer, the girl continues, her tone insistent.

speaker: Unknown Girl
content: What it is like in DisCity... Will the medicine be expensive there? Will the doctors there be impatient with me too...?

speaker: Unknown Girl
content: Will they... shun me for my sickness, like everyone back home...?
Her words grow erratic, and her mood seems unstable. Is she seeking treatment in DisCity? You've heard a similar story from the townsfolk.
Are you alright?
Using the shackles would risk exposing your identity, so you approach her as gently as possible. But the girl suddenly recoils, shaking her head frantically as if terrified.

speaker: Unknown Girl
content: No, stay back... My letter hasn't been sent yet. My parents still haven't heard from me...
Her words and mind spiral into chaos. Yet what she's said rings a bell. A name flashes in your mind... a name that shouldn't be here now in Désir.
The illusion before you freezes. As if struck by shock and fear, the girl begins convulsing violently. Dark tendrils of Mania coil around her, ripping away the facade to reveal her true form.
In a blink, the illusion turns into a monstrous figure twisted by manic obsession. The Corruptor lunges at you with terrifying speed.
You react instinctively, but the narrow alley leaves little room to maneuver, and your physical capabilities are definitely no match for the Corruptor's inhuman speed...
Bang!!
Your attempt to dodge fails. In a split second, you're slammed against the wall by crushing force.

The monster's hands clamp down, muffling your mouth and nose. The miasma of Mania invades your lungs, almost smothering you. As suffocation sets in, your head spins, your heartbeat thunders in your ears, and your vision begins to warp...
You see Désir in ruins, overrun by monsters, with noxious contamination seeping into every inch of the town's soil.
Is this... a hallucination before death?
[Filter][Town center][Portraits of surrounding monsters]

speaker: Liam
content: Primrose, what are you looking for?

speaker: Monster
content: Monsters, so many monsters... surrounding... Désir...

speaker: Primrose
content: Have you seen him? He was here just a moment ago.
female_content: Have you seen her? She was here just a moment ago.

speaker: Monster
content: DisCity... Vautour Bleu's... lie...

Dark clouds loom over the bustling marketplace, where Corruptors run rampant among the townsfolk. These rotting, contamination-ridden monsters brush shoulders with ordinary people, wandering the streets right before your eyes.
[Dark alley]
...Lie? What turned Sheila into that? Numerous questions flood your mind while the prolonged suffocation drains your strength. Your fading consciousness clings to a single, instinctive thought...
No matter what, can't let Mania harm the innocent townsfolk...
Crimson spikes of light begin forming in your palm. But just then, you hear a faint tapping sound drawing near. Tap, tap, tap...
It's footsteps... in high heels.
What are you waiting for?
You instantly retract the shackles in your hand. Before you can proceed, a mysterious figure appears next to you, a warm breath grazing your ear.
Your mind, clouded by suffocation, snaps to sudden clarity. Before you can turn to look, a soft touch encircles your wrist. Then, a gentle yet firm grip pulls you backward...
[Rescue CG][Change background music]
How have the folks of Désir been treating our guest while I was away?
Dove says your place has a lovely view. We should have tea together on the balcony sometime, if you're up for it.
[Balcony flashback]
You are...
The woman effortlessly resolves the impending threat. Before you can utter her name, the wand in her hand and the formidable power have demonstrated her identity.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Here's a little free tip: as a newcomer, it's best not to wander around alone.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Wouldn't you agree... my new neighbor?

Letting out a final shriek, the monster vanishes along with all traces of Mania. The alley, though still cold and dim without sunlight, has regained peace. Only the faint, ghostly scent of datura flowers still lingers in the air around you.
The shackles pulse wildly in your palm. A strong premonition tells you that the Sinner before you deserves every bit of the Outland Affairs Bureau's high-risk rating.
You step back instinctively to keep a safe distance, only to realize she's still holding your wrist. Sensing your retreat, her fingers tighten gently around yours.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: What, are you afraid of me? Did they badmouth me while I was away? Primrose and her friends wouldn't do that. It was Juan, wasn't it?

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: And here I thought you were a brave one, venturing alone into such a desolate place. Lucky for you, I happened to have stumbled upon a lost little lamb.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Don't I deserve at least a merci?

She tilts her head, lips drawing closer to your ear. Her warm breath, tinged with a faint hint of tobacco, brushes against the nape of your neck, sending a shiver down your spine. She notices, of course, but maintains her composure, awaiting your response.
She's not the only one here who can feign calmness after a monster encounter...

Ahem... How strange. I'm not quite sure how I ended up here. Just now, a dark shape appeared out of nowhere, and the next thing I knew, I could barely breathe. Thank you for your help... I should head back now.
You put on a meek, confused look and try to pull your hand free, but she isn't about to let you go that easily.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Is that all? Surely you can do better than that, my friend.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: You see, in my line of work, nothing comes for free.

With her tone honeyed yet firm, she steps forward, guiding you back until your shoulders meet the wall. With deliberate calm, she takes your hand, her fingers lacing through yours, fingertip tracing soft, slow circles that leave a tingling warmth on your palm.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Now, as a token of your gratitude, humor me: What was that red glow in your palm?

So much for hiding the shackles. I'm the MBCC's Chief from DisCity. Surrender now! Part of you has always wanted to pull off a dramatic line like that for once, but with so many mysteries unsolved, it's no time for heroics just yet.

options: Play dumb and change the subject

content: What red glow? What do you mean? All I remember is something scary trying to attack me... It was all a blur after that.
I think I heard that shadowy figure say something. Something about... Vautour Bleu's lie?

You emphasize those last words, widening your eyes in feigned innocence. Looking into her blue eyes, you'd expect some astuteness from a shrewd merchant, but instead, you see only a placid yet penetrating gaze.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: No way. An attack, here in Désir? That would be quite concerning. We certainly wouldn't want to frighten the townsfolk away, would we? Looks like I've got some tidying up to do, to make sure any threat to Désir is... erased.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Now, just to be absolutely clear... You're certain you were attacked by some shadowy figure?

Her deliberate slow tone says it all. She's playing the same game as you are, keeping her cards close while threatening discreetly. It's clear she's dodging the mention of her "lie" and the presence of the Corruptor.
You both keep your friendly, knowing smiles in silence. Any passerby would think you're just having an amiable talk.
As her fingertips brush against your wrist, you feel your pulse quicken. You can control your tone and even expression, but your body betrays you.
Must we stand this close? Frankly, I'd be quite defenseless if you decided to take advantage of the situation, Miss Vautour Bleu.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Oh? How did you know my name? I don't recall introducing myself.
Didn't you just mention that I'm your new neighbor?
I've only just arrived in Désir and haven't had the chance to get to know you. I'd hate to end up being one of those shadowy figures we were just talking about.

Broaching this subject is a gamble. No one in town knows you're here, alone in this alley. If Vautour Bleu wanted to, she could just say you'd successfully snuck into DisCity—just like she did with Sheila.
But you're betting she has reasons to keep her hands clean, just like she's reluctant to acknowledge the monster's existence. You suspect she has her own secrets.

Her gaze sharpens, as if she's seen through your ploy. In the dim alley, two sets of breath and body heat intertwine with mutual hostility. In the looming silence, you're acutely aware of her skin against your wrist, the touch growing hotter with each passing second.
Your gamble pays off. She releases your hand.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Hmm, what an unexpected way to meet my new neighbor. Thank goodness it was all just a misunderstanding.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: I'm glad you're alright. You can relax now. In Désir, we don't ask where people come from—everyone's bound for the same destination. When you're ready to make that trip to DisCity, come see me. Bring your bargaining chips... and your sincerity, of course.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Until then, make the most of your time here in Désir.
She brushes past you out of the dark alley, seamlessly blending into the bustling town center as if nothing happened. Only the lingering scent and warmth in her wake remind you of the silent tension.
Just as you breathe a discreet sigh of relief while watching her walking away, she suddenly pauses, casting a quick glance over her shoulder.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Ah, although you seem to know me already, it wouldn't be proper to not introduce myself as a gracious host.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: I am Vautour Bleu, the owner of Désir. May you have pleasant dreams tonight.
[Guest room]
You return to your room, glancing out the open window toward Vautour Bleu's apartment across the way.

The datura flowers on her balcony seem even more vibrant. Behind the blinds, you hear intermittent sounds of running water. A misty vapor drifts your way, carrying with it the scent of soap mingled with a faint trace of tobacco.
The scent is unmistakable. Just moments ago, this very fragrance was mere inches away from your face.

She noticed your shackles, yet said nothing. She's aware of the monster, but shies away from mentioning it, even concealing its presence. She knows you're investigating the Mania contamination, yet still allows you to stay...

speaker: Dove
content: Miss Vautour Bleu? Ah, everyone here respects her, worships her, even. After all, it's thanks to her that we got to meet each other.

speaker: Outland Affairs Bureau
content: But criminals always find a sneaky way in. Though immigration policies may have toughened, the WhiteSands trade routes remain active. After all, smuggling people is far more lucrative than smuggling goods.

speaker: Primrose
content: Miss Vautour Bleu took me under her wing. Thanks to her, I have work here in Désir and can save up for my journey to DisCity. I'll always be grateful for her kindness!

speaker: Liam
content: This is the only place where I can hear from Mom and wait for her to come and get me. Miss Vautour Bleu has promised to help me! She'll hide me in one of the caravan's cargo boxes when it's time. Those DisCity border guards won't even notice!

speaker: Outland Affairs Bureau
content: That's when Vautour Bleu seized control of the ruins. Using dubious financial tactics, she gathered a group of penniless, undocumented immigrants dreaming of instant success in DisCity, and established her dominion over Désir.

speaker: Alba
content: Who do you think gave me the chance to dance here? Do you have any idea how much it costs to enter a beauty pageant in DisCity? Everything in Désir belongs to Vautour Bleu. Yes, I'm working my tail off for her, but without her, I wouldn't even dare to dream about anything.

speaker: Juan
content: You don't trust Vautour Bleu, you wouldn't stay in Désir. Look, I ain't gonna say yes to everything she does, but I gotta say... she's good people.

speaker: Outland Affairs Bureau
content: For DisCity's sake, any threat in WhiteSands must be snuffed out before it hits us.

You mull over their conflicting words of Vautour Bleu and still can't piece together a coherent picture. Is she an unscrupulous smuggler? A philanthropist? A savior? Or perhaps the real culprit leaving Mania to spread unchecked?

You've run countless missions. You know all too well that words may be wrong but eyes never lie. No matter what others say of Vautour Bleu, there's one thing for certain: she is deliberately hiding the existence of the monsters.

speaker: Communications
content:
█ Contamination is detected in Désir; emotional condensation could be its source. It could possibly threaten the townsfolk. However, there's a significant discrepancy between the Mania level I've observed and the M-value anomalies recorded. I suspect an even larger-scale contamination concealed in this place.

█ Investigation was interrupted by Vautour Bleu. My cover may have been compromised. FAC should prepare for my retreat and, if necessary, emergency civilian rescue.

speaker: Communications
content:
█ In addition, I'll need the Outland Affairs Bureau to verify the following individuals, see if they have recorded activities within DisCity:

█ Sheila, 16 yoa female, Velvet Valley.
Darcy, 23 yoa male, Visserno Town...

speaker: Communications
content: █ One more, Nightingale, there's something I want you to look into...
[Vibrating white flash]
The instant you hit send, a noise outside the window startles you. In a flash, you stash away your communication device and duck behind the gauze curtains.
Through the sheer white curtains, you make out a hazy silhouette behind the blinds of the opposite room.
The figure seems oblivious to your presence. The sounds of running water have long ceased, replaced by the faint rustle of curtains, the chirping of insects, and your own muffled breathing.
You focus all your attention on observing the figure's every movement, but nothing seems to be happening.
The window facing you remains half-open, from which a delicate, misty scent of soap wafts through the air before fading away.
[Town center] [Night]
Night falls early in Désir.

Beneath a blanket of floral fragrance, the town slumbers. In their dreams, the townsfolk piece together fragments of happiness and hope, like an irresistible confection. They chase after the illusion—a treadmill disguised as a wonderful life, where they are drawn to empty promises.
Only whispers of wind brushing against datura leaves can be heard in the hush, especially near the town's borders.
One house remains lit, its stillness decorated by a series of repetitive sounds.
The scribbling of a pen, the folding of letters, the soft tearing of envelope seals, and the dull thuds of objects hitting the floor... punctuated by some occasional snickers, barely audible.
How sweet, how naive... so fragile, so easy to deceive...
Thunk. Something is tossed onto the wooden floor. It contains someone's work, or life, awaiting on the morrow.
[CG of Vautour Bleu watching at night]
Meanwhile, bathed in moonlight, a solitary figure quietly peers down at the town she's crafted by herself.

Moonlight traces her features, casting a soft glow on the desk by the window. Sprawled across its surface is a map of WhiteSands, a red cross drawn casually with lipstick marking the site of a new mine.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: I've checked out that place you told me. Not impressed. You know me, I don't bother myself with just any deal.

Vautour Bleu's gaze drifts through the sheer curtains, the moonbeams laced with floral scent, the half-open window across, finally landing on the slumbering figure in the opposite chamber. At her side, a special communicator vibrates, with its light glowing and fading.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: And I've met that person you mentioned.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: He's... exceeded my expectations—certainly more charming than those stiffs at DisCity's Outland Affairs Bureau. Still, I'm not ready to place my bets on him just yet.
female_content: She's... exceeded my expectations—certainly more charming than those stiffs at DisCity's Outland Affairs Bureau. Still, I'm not ready to place my bets on her just yet.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Désir is different. It's a miracle, even, like an oasis thriving in such a wasteland. Even the most gentle squeeze could take away its brittle life. These delicate seedlings need sturdier soil to take root... Ah, you wouldn't understand, anyway...
Leaning by the window languidly, Vautour Bleu ends the call, her gaze lingering on the mysterious newcomer in the chamber across the way.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Oh, my little neighbor, answers won't come to you if you just peek through the window.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Rouse yourself. Let's see if you have what it takes... to prove your worth to me.
As night shrouds Désir, moonlight cascades over balconies. A delicate fragrance rides the gentle breeze, weaving through the slumbering town and intertwining with the sweet dreams of its inhabitants.
[Town Center] [Dream]
The town square is bathed in particularly bright sunlight. Storefront windows refract a kaleidoscope of shimmering colors that leave passersby a little dazed.

speaker: Liam
content: Time for a clock-out shot! Alba, look over here—snap, snap!

speaker: Alba
content: Oh my, then I must sign up for a beauty pageant with that photo!
The townsfolk's chit-chat drifts in and out of earshot, at times clear and other times blurred. The gentle tinkling of wind chimes punctuates their voices.
Amid this symphony of sounds, a familiar whisper catches your ear once again.

speaker: Sheila
content: Beware... you must beware...
The whisper captivates you, drawing your attention away from everything else. The vibrant town square, Primrose's bakery, Alba's cheerful greetings to customers—all suddenly vanish before your eyes.
All you can see is a dark, endless alley and a vague, pale figure within it.

That "Sheila" moves so fast that you almost have to sprint to keep up. With each step, skeletal branches and thorns crawl out from the walls like an encroaching cage. No matter how fast the girl runs, she's destined to be imprisoned in this frigid, shadowy alley.
You keep chasing after her, until suddenly, the figure halts at the alley's dead end.
As you close in, the slender figure transforms in a breath.
[Vautour Bleu's portrait]
Before you can react, she anticipates your move and grabs your wrist—just as she did once before.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: What? Surprised to see me here?

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: I thought you'd be thrilled to meet me, since you've been watching me through the window all day, haven't you?

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: What were you hoping to uncover, I wonder? The town's hidden mysteries, or perhaps...

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: ...my own little secrets?
She edges closer and takes your hand once again, fingertips tracing on your palm.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: With all that peeking and prying, I'd have thought you've revealed all my secrets by now.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Or perhaps... you just need to get a little closer?
Wisps of ethereal smoke spill from her pipe, weaving an inescapable ward around you. With a firm push, Vautour Bleu pushes you to the ground.
Before you can even struggle, you feel warm breath inching close...
[CG of Vautour Bleu pinning Chief down]

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Now, this should be close enough. Do you see everything now, my curious little neighbor?

Vautour Bleu's body presses against yours. Her right hand traces a teasing path along your face, down your jawline, then slowly drifts to your neck. Her touch is vivid on your skin, so present yet without any warmth.
Sensing your resistance, Vautour Bleu eases her grip slightly to let you catch your breath. But the reprieve is short-lived.
Her left hand effortlessly catches your fidgeting wrists, pinning them against the cold floor. Then, with her body, she confines what little freedom of movement you have left.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Trying to slip away? Am I really that scary?

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Désir isn't a place where you can come and go as you please. After all my hospitality, surely you won't be thinking of running away without a farewell to me, would you?

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Don't you think it's time to return the favor?
Vautour Bleu's warm breath tickles your ear, her voice weaving around, near and far, like puppet strings.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: I know you're curious about me. I can feel your watchful eye on me. So tell me, what do you see? Am I good or evil to you?

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Care to guess what I think of you? A plaything? A threat? Or perhaps... valuable prey?
Suddenly, her hand closes around your throat, tender but increasingly firm. Your senses begin to fade, your vision dimming, each breath slipping away beneath her grip...
The overwhelming pressure drowns you as you feel her open provocation toward your shackles.
As consciousness wanes, you feel her lips brush against your ear as she whispers...

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Come now, don't be shy. Tell me, what's the little secret you're clutching?

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: And what can you offer me?

Repetitive scenarios, the vanished town, endless alleyways, physical touch... This isn't reality, but a crude copy of the memories in your subconscious. The town's Mania contamination is taking a toll on your psyche.
A nightmare it seems? That's an old sport. At least here and now, you don't have to worry about those shackles giving away your true identity.
[In the inn room]

The shackles jolt you awake. Sitting up abruptly, you're greeted by sunlight filtering through the leaves outside, its brightness so blinding as you squeeze your eyes shut. Gradually, your vision clears, and your racing heartbeat slows, as the details of reality come into focus.
It's been ages since contamination last triggered such a vivid nightmare. Did your encounter with Sheila yesterday leave that strong an impression? Something about it just feels off.
Morning birdsong drifts through the window, accompanied by the heady scent of datura blossoms, soothing your frayed nerves. Voices from outside suddenly interrupt your thoughts.

speaker: Familiar Voice
content: You don't need to bring me gifts every day, Alba. Save those for your sister when you'll see her in DisCity.

speaker: Alba
content: Oh, you still remember what I told you about my sister, Miss Vautour Bleu!

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Of course, I do. If I'd had a sibling who gets the chance to study in DisCity, I'd be just as excited as you.

speaker: Alba
content: So... um... when will it be my turn to go to DisCity?

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: I know how hard you've worked here, Alba. You've saved more than enough for your living expenses and the journey to DisCity. But without proper ID from your hometown, it'd be a huge risk for the caravan to sneak you in.

speaker: Alba
content: I get it! Really I do! I'd gladly take the risk. I've got my savings, even more!

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Oh, ma chérie, that's not what I meant. By risk, I mean a rare chance to slip past the checkpoints—an opening we have to wait for. But don't worry, your time will come.

speaker: Alba
content: Right, of course. I'm not in a rush... I get it. Just take some time.

You recognize Vautour Bleu's voice, the same one that haunted your dream. Yet now, though more distant, it also sounds more calm and real, undeniably patient. You rise and push open the window facing hers.
[Vautour Bleu's windowsill]
Vautour Bleu leans casually against the railing, her eyes following Alba as she walks away. Noticing your gaze, she turns to nod at you with a smile.
You seem busy today too, Miss Vautour Bleu. New deals in DisCity for the merchant caravan?
The small talk is a mere greeting, and you don't expect anything from it, but Vautour Bleu gestures toward you with her pipe.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Oh, did I wake you up?

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: You look well rested though. I take it that you slept well? I thought the little adventure in the alley yesterday might have left you a bit shaken.
Hmm? Something happened in an alley yesterday?

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: I wouldn't know. You should probably ask yourself. They say our dreams are echoes of our waking thoughts.
Unfazed by your subtle probing, Vautour Bleu fiddles with the plants on the balcony as she speaks. She seems so relaxed as if she's really just chatting about the weather with a neighbor.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Is this a habit of yours, drifting off into daydreams in broad daylight? What dream kept you dozing for so long?
I dreamed I was on the verge of uncovering the whole truth. A world where your townsfolk were safe from the looming threat of contamination, living the lives they'd always dreamed of.
It's clearly just some story you've made up, but you notice her pipe faintly trembles in her hand.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Well then... I hope your dream comes true.
A cluster of clouds blocks the sun momentarily so you can't see her true expression as she says that.

This is the same woman who lures immigrants with promises of so-called shelter and jobs, who just brushed off Alba's plea with flimsy excuses. Could she really mean what she said, for your dream to come true...?
Dreams alone won't change reality. And dreams promised by others are even less reliable.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Quite the philosopher, aren't you? I must admit I don't always catch the meaning of your words, my little neighbor.
Oh? Well then, once I've uncovered the truth myself, I'll be sure to expound everything in detail. By then, you'd better come up with some new tricks to dodge my questions.
The clouds part, and blinding sunlight floods the balcony and the town below once again. Evading your gaze, Vautour Bleu turns to face the town and draws in a deep breath.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Mmm... can you smell it? Butter and wheat. Primrose's quite the baker. I sometimes find myself craving her bread when I'm out in WhiteSands. You must be starving having just woken up. Don't miss out on some freshly bake bread.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Just head downhill to the town center. Try not to lose your way this time.
...Is this your way of giving me the green light to investigate?
Vautour Bleu says nothing. Instead, she simply raises her pipe and points at your head.
Vautour Bleu seems to be stifling a laugh. As you catch your reflection in the window, you finally notice that your hair is a complete mess from sleep, with an unruly cowlick sticking up.
And to think you've been holding this intense back-and-forth with Vautour Bleu with hair like this...
You could have just told me earlier, and not with that pipe...

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: But isn't that part of the fun of chatting across balconies? I'm not sure if you can hear my every word, but I know you can see my every move.

What is she hinting at now? As Vautour Bleu exhales a long plume of smoke, you find her intentions remain as enigmatic as ever. A small cup of tea is set on her windowsill, beneath which lies a worn, undelivered book of poetry.
N'importe où hors du monde

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: I had someone bring the tea over last night, but you'd already turned in. Such a shame, it's not quite the same when it's cold.

From across the way, Vautour Bleu watches as her lovely neighbor drapes on the cloak brought from DisCity and sets to work collecting evidence of her "misdeeds"—the same neighbor who seems to have forgotten the promise they made in that alley to have tea together.
With a slight shake of her head, Vautour Bleu tips the cup and lets the tea trickle into a flowerpot.

Dappled sunlight filters through dense leaves, casting warmth over the elegant datura flowers, the brick-red accents adorning the flowerbeds, parasols, and awnings, just as usual. It's another leisurely afternoon in this quaint little town.
You find yourself back near the alley where you first sensed Mania.

speaker: Faint Voice
content: ...Oh, dear. Told you you're just overthinking things. Come on in, take a break and have some bread...

speaker: Faint Voice
content: ...Did you not sleep well last night? I've got some herbal tea from my hometown...

The town center hums with life behind you, while a picture of tranquility stretches ahead. It all seems to be posing a gentle, attentive question: Is Vautour Bleu truly an irredeemable villain you think she is? And moreover, are you ready to shatter the peace of this town?
You remind yourself not to be misled by this facade of harmony. This superficial peace won't erase the despair Sheila endured. You must press on and uncover the truth.
Suddenly, you feel a slight tremor from the shackles. It's negligibly subtle, but now sets your every nerve on edge.
You close your eyes, slow your breath, and focus on the most minute details. A faint female voice slips in, its whispers coiling around your eardrums and dancing along your spine.
Another one wracked with guilt, huh? Haha, right up my alley. They're so much fun to play with...
Oh, seems more intriguing than the previous one though... "I'm writing this letter to atone for my deeds," really? Let me see...

speaker: Choice
options: Search for the source of the voice

content: The voice leads the way. You immediately go in that direction, but as you make your way through the area, you find nothing suspicious.
The streets are quiet, uniform buildings lining the road with lush greenery thriving in every corner as you pass by. Everything appears perfectly ordinary.

speaker: Chief
content: ...Just an illusion maybe?
Doubting though, you turn the final corner, almost ready to give up.
But just then, a bicycle catches your eye. Its distinctive bell immediately gives it away—Dove's mail bike.
Your gaze shifts to the house behind it. Amid all these abandoned houses, it's the only one with light glowing from the window. The whispers seem to come from that very spot.
Then again, the greedier, guiltier, and more wicked they are, the easier their wishes are to handle, heh heh...
You tiptoe toward the sole window. In the silence, the taps of your muffled footsteps become a suspenseful countdown, about to reveal the enigmatic figure behind the voice.
One step closer. You hear the tearing of paper, followed by the soft scribbling of a pen on paper.
I am the head nurse at Mr. Wood's ward. I'm sorry to inform you that Mr. Wood, the recipient you formerly addressed, passed away six months ago. Records show that he had no living relatives...

You take a second step. As if roleplaying, the muttering female voice suddenly adopts a serious tone. She reads what appears to be the content of a letter, her voice, calm and steady though, barely masks the mockery beneath.
This should make you more than satisfied, shouldn't it? Oh, how I'd love to see that face of yours right now—must be torn between grief and unspeakable relief...

The third step. The back window is already within arm's reach. You only need to slightly hunch over to make out the silhouette of a young girl in the study, illuminated by candlelight. Spread across her desk are numerous opened letters.
No wonder you look so haunted all the time, old wretch. Now let me help you end this—a death knell tolled for your beloved child, shall we? Haha! How deliciously ironic!
The room's occupant whirls around, her serene silhouette shattered by the flickering candlelight. Your eyes meet, as if everything is frozen all in a sudden.
In the next breath, the moment crumbles—Dove bolts toward the door on the other side, the letters glowing blue rising up in the air, swirling after her like a flock of homing birds.

speaker: Chief
content: That power... She's a Sinner?!
Without a second thought, you pursue her. This is a lead you can't afford to lose. You must catch her.

speaker: Elderly Woman
content: Oh, would you look at that! Dove just brought me yesterday. My little grandson can already write his name! ...Aw, just so adorable!

speaker: Philippe
content: You don't say! Can't wait to bring my family here. My little one's still so young. Maybe I'd raise her like a true DisCity-born, heh!
Désir's town center is bustled with life as ever, with townspeople chattering away. Dove's figure has blended into the crowd, making it even harder to trace.

She has repeatedly given you the slip, using datura-covered corners, hidden passages, and even well-timed passersby as cover. The chase has been relentless though, you've completely lost sight of her.

speaker: Jolly Middle-Aged Woman
content: Hey, newcomer, why running around? Catch a breath will ya?... Don't tell me you're playing some hide-and-seek, haha!

speaker: Chief
content: No, I'm not... Actually, did you just come from the west side? Have you seen which way Dove ran off to?

speaker: Jolly Middle-Aged Woman
content: Ran off? Oh my, she was running, after all! Dove's been a little sickly, so it's rare to see her exert herself like that. Looks like you two are really getting into this, aren't you?
Seeing the woman's cheerful obliviousness to the urgency, you put on a more serious tone and restate your word.

speaker: Chief
content: This isn't a game. I'm trying to catch her because I saw her opening letters she shouldn't have been. She might be tampering with the town's mail, possibly even forging letters.

speaker: Jolly Middle-Aged Woman
content: Huh? That sounds so not true. Dove's a good girl. Maybe she was just fixing some addresses?

speaker: Chief
content: That's possible. But give it a thought—have you noticed how every letter has the same response time and always looks freshly enveloped? They are supposed to be from different places, right?
These discrepancies have been present all along. Even a newcomer like you can spot them, but this woman seems to be purposefully turning a blind eye to them.

speaker: Jolly Middle-Aged Woman
content: Oh, that's nothing to worry about! Dove's already explained it all. Miss Vautour Bleu personally entrusted the caravan to deliver our letters!

speaker: Jolly Middle-Aged Woman
content: They're all capable young lads, moving fast in the desert, always been so reliable. Ain't surprising they keep our letters intact! Hey, you'll get used to it once you've stayed here longer. What's impossible out there is nothing magical in Désir!
No matter how you phrase it, she's just not listening. Seeing no use in pressing further, you give up persuading her and try a different approach.

speaker: Chief
content: ...Is it over there?

speaker: Chief
content: No, it feels more like... here?
Without visual cues, tracking her through Mania-sensing alone is extremely challenging. It's nearly impossible to tell if the traces of Mania belong to Dove.
The longer you stay, the vaguer you could sense her trace amid the crowded townspeople.

speaker: Elderly Woman
content: I may be too old to understand you young folks' play, but I do know one thing: Dove is a good girl! You must have misunderstood her. She was probably just helping others write their letters!

speaker: Philippe
content: Hell yeah! You newcomers are always so quick to worry. Opening letters? I'm sure she was just sorting the mails for us!

speaker: Curious Bystander
content: That's right! You know some people wrote letters before they moved to DisCity. Then of course she's got to open them! How else would she know if it should be handed to the caravan?
As you run, you piece together the townspeople's words. Their reflexive dismissive attitude only makes Dove's deeds more suspicious.
She must be hiding something, and probably so do the townspeople. The key to unraveling this entire mystery is right in front of you—if you can catch Dove.
But how? Your breathing grows heavier and your legs feel like lead. You know you're approaching your limit, and Dove can be down any one of these alleys...
Swish.
Just then, a skirt's hem whips around the corner ahead. There's no mistaking it. It's Dove!
Ignoring the taste of blood rising in your throat, you break into a full sprint, closing the distance with every determined step.

speaker: Dove
content: Huff... huff...
The alley stretches on, giving Dove enough room to flee. But her strength is also fading, her pace slowing with each step.
Finally she collapses to the ground, gasping for air. You took the chance and block her escape route. Through your perseverance, the stubborn chase has finally ended in your favor.

speaker: Dove
content: Oh... oh, it's you! You almost scared me to death. I thought it was a ghost watching me through the back window...

speaker: Dove
content: I'm so sorry. I shouldn't have run like that, made you chase me so far... I've heard some ghost stories around lately, so I might have overreacted...

Surprisingly, Dove speaks up first, her attitude totally not what you expected. Her voice remains soft and gentle, as if your confrontation through the window and the subsequent chase were nothing but a misunderstanding.
As she speaks, she looks up at you with her shiny eyes. She sounds genuinely apologetic, yet obviously avoids mentioning the cause of all this—those letters she opened.

speaker: Chief
content: You did... overreact. But was it really the ghost stories? Or, perhaps it's because I saw what you were doing with those letters?

speaker: Dove
content: Letters? What... I don't know what you're... Oh, you mean those undelivered ones? Yeah I was processing them. That's my work.

speaker: Chief
content: Processing, you mean opening those private letters without permission?

Your voice is steady, making no haste to press further. Instead, you start catching up Dove's every single word. You know that just like in the previous chase, she will eventually lead herself to a dead end.
As you expected, upon hearing the words opening letters, her pupils constrict and face pales.

speaker: Dove
content: ...Is that something you've encountered before? I'll admit, sometimes I do replace envelopes before delivering letters...

speaker: Dove
content: But that's only when one's damaged or tainted with blood. It would be unsightly... Other than that, I swear...

speaker: Chief
content: Oh? So that's why the letters you deliver look so pristine, almost as if they are... forged? Because you replace those envelopes?

speaker: Chief
content: And you did all this because it would be unsightly?
Your words hit the mark. Dove startles and lowers her head, as if trying to cover her face, or escaping your scrutiny.

speaker: Dove
content: I know it sounds foolish, but it's the best I can do to help them—because I'm a mere mail carrier.

speaker: Chief
content: A mere mail carrier? You're far more than that, Dove.

speaker: Chief
content: Didn't you forge letters to "fulfill" the townspeople's wishes? Like that letter from the head nurse, some "tolling the death knell" stuff?

speaker: Chief
content: I don't know how you mimic handwriting, or grasp information not mentioned in the letters... but I assume it has something to do with your special ability?
You keep a watchful eye on her every subtle reaction. Her clenched hands and paling face are betraying her. Still denying though, her voice sounds feeble.

speaker: Dove
content: I... I don't know what you're talking about!

speaker: Chief
content: Alright Dove, cards on the table. I'll go first: I'm an investigator from DisCity and I know enough about Sinners and their power, so don't try and fool me.
You step forward and grasp her wrist. A red light flashes, and the shackles connect you both. You're right. She is a Sinner.
Sensing this unusual connection, Dove jolts her head up and stares at you in shock. She's never expected such an extraordinary investigative technique from you.

speaker: Dove
content: What is this...?! What did you do to me...?!

speaker: Chief
content: Don't be afraid. I'm here to investigate the Mania in Désir and uncover the truth. As long as you cooperate, I won't harm you.

speaker: Chief
content: From what I gather, the letters of the townspeople never actually leave Désir. You open them, using the information to craft those responses. That's why they all look pristine and come back so soon.

speaker: Chief
content: And you use them to deceive the townspeople, playing the role of a kind-hearted mail carrier, all to keep the hoax of Désir's unnatural, deceptive nature. Am I right?
Your pointed, blunt question seem to have touched the truth and stung Dove.

Her shoulders tremble, then suddenly she swings her head up, barely suppressing her anger and hatred. For a moment, you think she may lash out, but in the end, her face just falls into a look of pure hurt.

speaker: Dove
content: No... that's enough! Why do you have to think the worst of me, of this town?

speaker: Dove
content: We're not born in DisCity, and yes, we take stealthy ways to sneak in there... But everyone here is trying their best just to survive!

speaker: Dove
content: Yes, I am a Sinner, and yes, I forged the letters. Maybe you see that as an unforgivable crime...
Dove looks up at you, her eyes glistening with unshed tears. You can't quite tell if they are a sign of her distress, or some deeper pain out of long-standing grief and loss.

speaker: Dove
content: But I really don't know anything about the Mania or any truth of this town! I did all this because...

speaker: Dove
content: Because I... I just want everyone to have a better life! That isn't a lie, at least...

speaker: Chief
content: Your actions tell a different story.
Dove registers your skepticism, her fingers brushing away the tears, seemingly both composing herself and suppressing her emotions.
You stay on high alert in case she lashes out for failing her disguise. To your surprise, she just reaches into her messenger bag and produces several letters.

speaker: Chief
content: ...What was that?!

speaker: Dove
content: They're from those who've gone to DisCity... and the replies I've prepared.
Dove nervously gestures for you to take the letters. She glances around cautiously before continuing.

speaker: Dove
content: Many of them wrote to their families while waiting for their trips. So I made these replies... But some left all in a hurry, without saying goodbye to anyone.

speaker: Dove
content: That's all I have. I hope they could be useful. Otherwise, I can't offer any other help, nor can I prove my innocence...

speaker: Dove
content: Take them if you want. I guess you'll not listen to me anyway.
You look into Dove's slightly petulant and aggrieved expression closely. After a moment's consideration, you decide to trust your shackles and your gut feeling.
You reach out and take the letters from Dove. The one on top is as light and thin as it appears. The sender's name on the envelope catches your eye—Sheila.

You are back in the dark alley where the attack took place. Dim light seeps through narrow gaps, barely illuminating your surroundings. This gloomy corner is worlds away from that bright town, yet it feels the closest to the somber truth right here.
You clutch the letter Dove gave you. Its edges are slightly worn, with Sheila's name printed on the envelope in an elegant script.
Dove said she found it the day after Sheila left. The connection between this lost family letter and that obsessive monster can't be mere coincidence.
Sheila's face and voice are still vivid in your memory, her tone almost echoing in your mind as you imagine her penning these words.

speaker: Letter
content: Dear Mom and Dad, It's been so long since I last saw you. How's everything in Velvet Valley?
An innocuous greeting, followed by typical pleasantries and Sheila's hopeful musings about the future. However, the few last lines look increasingly crooked, scribbled in haste.

speaker: Letter
content: I saw Antoine... and Sallie... No, I HEARD them... They're supposed to be in DisCity... Why are they back?

speaker: Letter
content: I followed their voices... and ended up here... There aren't any datura flowers here... And then I saw them, the monsters...
The once-elegant writing turns jagged, barely legible. Though it still looks like Sheila's handwriting, she must be scribbling these lines using some gravel soil she could grasp.

speaker: Letter
content: The town is full of monsters... No one's ever left for DisCity...

speaker: Letter
content: She lied to us... No one's ever left...

speaker: Letter
content: The flowers... the datura flowers...
It looks like Sheila had been chased by monsters, and hastily jotted down what she knew upon finding a hiding spot.

speaker: Letter
content: We can't see them with the flowers around... they can't hurt us! But I know, they're right next to me...!

Guided by Sheila's words, you walk into the alley. The once-withered vines now show fresh growth. The datura blossoms are blooming vibrantly, too perfect to be natural, as if someone has crafted them.
The guards around them tense up, but Wynn immediately gestures for them to hold still.

speaker: Letter
content: The fragrance has numbed everyone... the monsters... even the Mania...
You continue your work, ripping off one datura stem after another. Each one crumbles into dry leaves before your eyes.
The handwriting in the letter becomes increasingly frenzied, the words barely discernible.

speaker: Letter
content: I want to go home... but I can't... not anymore...

speaker: Letter
content: The flowers are wilting. They're coming...
As the floral scent fades, the growls of the monster grow clearer.
The monsters' been lurking all along, invisible to your eyes just as you are to its.

speaker: Letter
content: My letter hasn't been sent yet. My parents still haven't heard from me...
Another patch of datura wilts. The dark alley is now devoid of white blossoms.
An agonized wail erupts as if from the depths of an abyss, threatening to drag everything into the underworldly void.

speaker: Letter
content: I've promised Primrose... we'll go to DisCity together...

speaker: Letter
content: But I can't now... never...

The letter ends here. Only the taint of Mania lingers beyond those last words. It reminds you of what you sensed with your shackles on Sheila in her Corruptor form—the victim who tried to lead you to the truth, even risking being wiped out by Vautour Bleu.

You finally understand why back then Sheila lunged at you to cover your mouth and nose. You do so and try to block out the fragrance. As the scent fades, your vision clears. This town, once bathed in sunshine and brimming with hope, now reveals its true colors...

Oozing with Mania contamination, horrifying monsters roam aimlessly throughout Désir. They lurk by the flower beds, outside the bakery, down the local inn, haunting everywhere masked by the datura flowers' scent.
Beep. Belatedly, the Bureau's messages arrive:
█ The Outland Affairs Bureau has looked into it: No signs of activity within DisCity for any individuals on your list.
█ As for the other matter you said, we've got the results.

█ Datura flowers are native to the Outlands and have become extremely rare since the disasters began. They contain various toxic compounds that interfere with human neural function. Prolonged exposure can induce a sense of euphoria, even hallucinations.
█ Rumors run in WhiteSands; one says that those who encounter datura blossoms in an oasis will be forever bound to this desert.

While these Outland legends may not always be credible, one has been proven in Désir: No one ever makes it out of here. Their last hopes for DisCity have twisted into obsessive resentment and they are forever trapped in this purgatory as grotesque monsters that shun the light.
Gazing out from the alley, you see datura flowers planted everywhere in this quaint town. They adorn the diner, the post office, Vautour Bleu's balcony, even your own room.
So much effort has been poured into hiding the bitter truth—no one can ever reach DisCity.

You carefully tuck Sheila's letter into your coat and approach these specters laden with unresolved longing. They seem to sense something different in you, their mouths open as if to speak, but only silence follows, heavy with pain.
Their blood-red eyes are void of aggression, yet speak of their suffering; the residue of their resentment compels them to repeat a name over and over again: Vautour Bleu.

These were once residents of Désir, like everyone else you've seen, brimming with hope for the future and working tirelessly to save up for DisCity. Now, they're still the residents of this town, yet existing in a limbo beyond mortal sight.
You've suffered enough. Let me help you end this.
The grotesque forms crumple at your feet, their final breaths whispering the broken dreams for DisCity before they dissolve into dust.
This promising name—Désir—finally reveals itself a deceptive deadfall that preys on the vulnerable human hearts. In this crafted mirage of an oasis, the illusion forevermore renews.
Silence settles over the alley as the scent of Mania fades. The truth has finally come to light, yet you remain rooted where you are.
[Juan]
First, built this town on a wasteland on the border with her merchant caravan, spreading rumors of a gateway to DisCity, luring in those desperate to Désir, those with no means or money.
[Liam] [Primrose]
Next, feeds the newcomers' dreams of DisCity with forged letters and lies; offers them jobs to cover their living expenses here, trapping them here.
[Alba]
And finally, makes up endless excuses to delay their leaves. Living costs mount, they have no choice but to stay.
You push through the tangled mass of withered plants at your feet, struggling to free yourself from their grasp.

Your real goal is to keep them here indefinitely. Perhaps "smuggler" doesn't fit—you've never actually sent anyone to DisCity. No wonder the Outland Affairs Bureau couldn't pin trafficking charges on you.

Their dreams unfulfilled, their resentment grows, festering into monsters in this Mania-infested wasteland of WhiteSands. And so, the tragic cycle continues, fueled by toxic flowers that numb the townsfolk...
Behind you, a pair of high heels crushes the withered vines, the delicate footsteps drawing closer. You know who that is. She's been there, following you, all along.
From the moment I set foot in Désir, you've been encouraging my every step, wanting me to uncover this town, uncover you. But a true villain wouldn't go to such lengths just to expose themselves.
I'd much prefer a fair partnership to being manipulated like a fool.
But partnership never builds without honesty.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: You're sharper than I gave you credit for. I thought you'd need another day to put it all together.
Despite your suspicion and provocation, Vautour Bleu doesn't display any hostility, her composure as unruffled as ever. She holds your wrist gently, then gestures forward.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: If you have more questions, follow that path to the edge of Désir, to see the most picturesque view in this town.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: I'll be waiting for you there, little Chief.
[Town center]
Meanwhile, throughout the town, datura flowers begin to wither, their fragrance gradually dissipating.
Alba sits outside the diner, dazed and motionless, all her energy to dance drained. She forces a smile and mutters the same words over and over again.

speaker: Alba
content: Right, of course. I'm not in a rush... I get it. Just take some time.
As her compulsive muttering continues, black mist gathers behind her, the once-lush plants wilting as soon as they creep closer.

speaker: Juan
content: The hell is that?! Am I still drunk? Holy crap... watch out Alba!
Juan's holler snaps Alba from her stupor. She looks around cluelessly, only to find withered plants surrounding her, oblivious to the contamination she's just caused.
Whispers of despair begin to echo through every shadowy corner of the town.
The despairing monsters, long besieging Désir, are on the verge of breaking free from the town's illusory chains. As the peaceful facade begins to crack, Mania stirs once again.

Désir stands aloof in WhiteSands, a solitary oasis, ringed by endless dunes. This spot behind the inn is the only place with an unobstructed view. From here, one can gaze upon DisCity in the distance—an unknown yet promising land beyond the sands.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Making progress, little Chief. You didn't get lost this time.

Gazing into WhiteSands, Vautour Bleu turns at your footsteps. Her gaze catch yours, and for a moment, it's as if you're both back on the balconies, about to pick up the thread of your usual chat through the windows.
But now, the peaceful disguise has all been torn away, shattered both in dreams and reality.
So this is what you said the most picturesque spot?
All you see is but the deceptively calm expanse of WhiteSands, with DisCity barely visible on the far horizon. But sightseeing is the last thing on your mind right now.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: I'm sure you've seen far more impressive sights in DisCity. To you, such a barren desert is probably nothing remarkable. But to the people of Désir, it's precious.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: This is the only spot in town where you can see DisCity—though not always clearly. When sandstorms sweep across or the weather turns, all you can make out is a hazy outline.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Distance makes it special. Everyone can paint their own picture of DisCity, filling it in with the most magnificent scenery. But I suspect those who actually live here don't really look at it that way.
With a hint of wistfulness, Vautour Bleu drifts back with a gentle question.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: During your stay, have you had a chance to eat at Alba's diner yet?
Not just Alba's diner, I've tried Liam's delivered milk also, and Primrose's bread.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: They're all good kids. It's because of them that people in Désir can still enjoy fleeting moments of happiness.
But is that real happiness? You keep the question to yourself.
I've passed by it, but haven't eaten there yet.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Ah, that's a shame. You really should give it a try. Alba's a good girl, and she's done wonders with that place.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: The red wine they serve is exceptional too. It can hold its own against some of the finest vintages from DisCity.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: It took Alba ages to master how to brew. Poor Juan was roped into being her taster. I hear he nearly swore off drinking altogether by the end. The recipe itself is actually a legacy from when Désir was a holiday resort.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Did you know? This place used to be popular. The wealthy from DisCity would flock to this oasis for their getaways.
The Outland Affairs Bureau briefed me on it.
There's no point in hiding anything now that she's blown your cover.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: I knew who they'd send, but they've prepped you more thoroughly than I anticipated. Enlighten me, what else did they tell you?

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Ah no, let me guess. They probably painted us as a bunch of squatters or some band of lowlifes, wasting our days chasing pipe dreams. Am I close?
Your mind flashes back to Guillotin's briefing. The Outland Affairs Bureau's attitude is indeed just as Vautour Bleu describes.
You seem to know DisCity better than I expected.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: And how much do you know about Désir now?
It's an elaborate trap you perpetuate with lies. You lure in those desperate for a taste of DisCity life, let them chase a dream they'll never catch.
Thinking of Sheila and those despairing specters, you can't keep your tone friendly.
Still, Vautour Bleu remains unperturbed, drifting her gaze toward WhiteSands.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: I don't believe I've told you how I brought them to Désir, have I?

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: I still remember the first time I met Sheila. Our caravan was just passing through Velvet Valley. When her parents heard I could take people to DisCity, they entrusted her to me without a second thought.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: When we departed, her parents saw her off at the door. "You'll get better once you're in DisCity! They'll cure you there!" They kept calling out, and Sheila left with a smile on her face.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: But I could see her condition. Her M-value was already close to the mutation threshold. It was Mania that caused her illness, brought on by the disasters.
Mania?

speaker: Sheila
content: What it is like in DisCity... Will the medicine be expensive there? Will the doctors there be impatient with me too...?

speaker: Sheila
content: Will they... shun me for my sickness, like everyone back home...?
Even DisCity hasn't found a cure for Mania yet.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: But the people beyond DisCity's walls don't know that. To them, it's almost a holy ground. They've pinned all their hopes for the future on this mirage.
You knew it from the start that Sheila's wish would never come true, then why did you...?
"Why did you still take Sheila in?" Your question dies on your lips. It was not Vautour Bleu, but her Mania-fearing hometown and her own family who had sent her away.
Vautour Bleu casts a knowing gaze at you, and continues her story.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: And Primrose, we found her lying in the snow, without even a rough shelter. The poor girl didn't have a sliver of identity proof. Turns out her aunt and uncle had already told everyone she'd died of illness. When she heard we were headed to DisCity, she was almost begging us...
Vautour Bleu bends down, scooping up a handful of sand, then watches it slip through her fingers.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: WhiteSands is vast, but fertile soil for hope is rare. Rarer still are unyielding rocks that can weather the storms. Most of what you see is just this—fine sand, carried here by winds, blowing toward DisCity.

The truths, blowing in the wind, weigh heavy: Sheila's sickness, incurable; Liam's mother, not waiting in DisCity; Alba, never to be a beauty queen... Vautour Bleu has the means to bring them to DisCity, yet she chooses not to strip away the last threads of hope these fragile souls cling to.
Was Sheila really killed by the monsters?
She already knew about the flowers, even seized the chance to write that letter. She could've hidden somewhere safe with datura. So what really killed her? The monsters—or Mania and her own despair?
A weary smile flickers across Vautour Bleu's face. You've edged close to the truth she's guarding, yet neither of you has the heart to say it out.
Sheila wasn't the only one with an M-value nearing the threshold, was she?
The moment these people started their impossible dreams of DisCity, they were already teetering on the edge of mutation.
Vautour Bleu stoops down, her fingers gently brushing away the sand. In the pit lie buried countless withered datura leaves.
[Town center]
Meanwhile, throughout the town, datura flowers begin to wither, their fragrance gradually dissipating.
Freed from the numbing scents, the monsters start appearing, growing restless among the townsfolk.

speaker: Townie B
content: What... what's that sound?

speaker: Townie A
content: I hear it too... It's getting closer.
Eerie noises echo throughout the town. They seem to be coming from just beyond the datura-covered fences.

speaker: Townie B
content: What's happened to these flowers? They've all died.

A townsman approaches the fence, reaching out to pluck off the withered datura flowers. He peeks out curiously through a gap in the planks, and when his gaze reaches something beyond, the color drains from his face.

speaker: Townie B
content: Ahhh! Monsters! There are monsters in the town!!!
Screams and fear spread all the way to the edge of the town. Vautour Bleu turns back, looking at the town she's been striving to sustain, which is now falling apart before her eyes.
She recalls the first time she passed by this place with her caravan: nothing more than a ruin in the sands, yet its soil was so unusually suited for datura flowers.

For the struggling Outlands in WhiteSands, there are never enough Mania-inhibiting Hypercubes to save those with dangerously high M-values. Each stop the caravan made brought new faces, new refugees seeking shelter from Mania's grip.
Vautour Bleu's little neighbor guesses right. Désir's disastrous Mania contamination isn't just because of the monsters—it's because every single resident here is on the brink of mutation.
She's tried, time and again, to save everyone she met. But it never lasted long. The sandstorms and despair would engulf everything each time before she could find the key to sustaining hope.
After all this time searching WhiteSands, she finally found this place and named it Désir, praying it would bring a new beginning.

But her hopes had limits. The datura flowers could only prolong their dreams, not realize them. "Maybe we should just go and rob some Hypercubes," she'd sometimes joke with her crew, but deep down she knew it would only invite greater disaster.
Vautour Bleu takes a long drag from her pipe, feeling the town's decay creeping beneath her feet. She begins counting down in her mind...

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Time's running out, little Chief.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Let's strike a deal.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: I know the town won't hold out for long and the truth will be known. So, before Désir bursts from despair like a balloon... let's pop it ourselves.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: The dreams shall end. Time to wake up.
Dove steps out from her hidden refuge. Before her is a town torn apart by screams, wails, madness, and disorder—a picture of an utter shambles.
The withered datura flowers, like countless lifeless eyes, share Dove's silent gaze at this long-awaited, inevitable collapse.

speaker: Dove
content: So, the day has finally come. Heh, how could a place like this last forever?

speaker: Dove
content: How beautiful it was, their wish and hope. How promising. Now all gone, so ugly, so painful...
As a Sinner, she could have fled this doomed place the moment that terrifying and stubborn Chief was distracted away.
But she stayed. She wanted to witness with her own eyes... the annihilation of that wish far grander than her own.
This is the finale she has forseen, nurtured, and even, in her heart, longed for.

speaker: Dove
content: Ah right, it's time for work! Haven't delivered today's letters yet!

speaker: Dove
content: Job is job, must be done! I can't just stop because someone's wish fell apart—it happens all the time, anyways!
Amid swirling dust and debris, Dove wheels out her bicycle, her messenger bag bulging as always, ready to resume her rounds: Delivering happiness and luck.
Ding-a-ling.
The once-smooth brick roads are now a treacherous landscape of bumps and craters, making Dove's ride an awkward, jolting journey.
Ding-a-ling.
Toppled mailboxes, bent out of shape, lie twisted, their slots resembling twisted, toothy grins.
Ding-a-ling.
The townspeople who once eagerly awaited their letters are gone. The dark, hollow houses have become monsters' lairs, echoing with unsettling growls and clamor of fights.

speaker: Dove
content: Your mail's here! Come on out!

speaker: Dove
content: Anyone home? Hmm, I'll just leave it here! Don't forget to take it!
Dove produces a thick envelope from her messenger bag and gently places it on the toppled mailbox, even taking a moment to straighten it before hopping back on her bike.
But before she can pedal away, a monster emerges from nowhere, shrieking as it kicks the mailbox away. Strong gusts of wind and flying debris shred the letter together with its envelope.

speaker: Dove
content: Oh dear... That's bad. How could you do that to such a precious letter?

speaker: Dove
content: Letters carry dreams and wishes... They're so fragile. If this keeps up, it'll really sadden me to continue delivering them...
Dove turns back, her gaze following the fragments in the wind. Her expression looks both mournful and appreciative. But above all, it seems as if she's confirming some deep-seated belief of her own.
Dove's eyes remain fixed on the shattered letters as they're snatched by the wind. Then, with a serene sigh, she pedals onward, with more letters delivered...

In the danger-ridden town, the mail girl is the only figure moving through the wreckage with smile and unwavering grace. She even nods politely to the roaming monsters, like a lone thread connecting illusion and reality.

speaker: Dove
content: Great! All done!
Dove heaves a deep sigh, hopping off her bicycle. She turns back, and surveys the town with a sense of accomplishment and satisfaction.
What lies before is but a dilapidated town, people gone mad, cozy sight no more, all swallowed by chaos and despair. The dreamlike oasis has been swept away by the tempest.
Yet Dove shows no sign of disappointment. Instead, she smiles, a knowing curve of her lips, as if she has anticipated this all along.

speaker: Dove
content: I knew it... Here, there, or anywhere, there's no escape. So is Désir...

speaker: Dove
content: And here I thought having a righteous partner, a well-intentioned one, would make a difference. Ha...

speaker: Dove
content: Broken. Gone. Ruined... It is what it is, for good or bad. In the end, it's always the same, a mess that no one gives a damn about...
A serene smile remains plastered on Dove's face, eerily contradictory to her pessimistic, hopeless words.
Is it to suppress emotions? Or is it her usual way to resist grievances? No one knows, perhaps not even Dove herself.

Finally, she finds herself at the town's edge, in a quiet corner with a decent view. She sits down, hugging her knees. From here, she can see the townspeople still fleeing, and a lone figure desperately trying to save what's left.

speaker: Dove
content: Ideals, duty, wishes... Who can they truly save? Can you tell me, my Chief from DisCity?
[Dark alley]
As the datura scent fades, more and more townsfolk are snapping out of their numbed state.
Fresh blood mingles with dried stains. Bodies of humans and monsters alike are strewn all over the once-pristine streets.

speaker: Townie A
content: The town... it's overrun with monsters... How did this happen...

speaker: Townie A
content: Where did they come from... What... what do they want...

speaker: Townie B
content: Will they find us here? What do we do? ...Oh god, what are we supposed to do?
Panic strikes the helpless folks as chaos engulfs the town. Stripped of the soothing floral scent, their already fragile minds are crumbling and inching close to hysteria.

speaker: Townie C
content: Vautour Bleu... Miss Vautour Bleu will come to save us, right?

speaker: Townie A
content: That's right, we can still count on Vautour Bleu! She'll get rid of these monsters. She'll protect our town!
At the mention of Vautour Bleu's name, a glimmer of hope spreads through the crowd. They believe she'll protect Désir and everyone, just as she has before.
But one of them recoils, his face suddenly twisting in terror upon hearing Vautour Bleu's name.

speaker: Townie B
content: I don't know... I don't know... Vautour Bleu... Vautour Bleu...

speaker: Townie A
content: What's wrong? Zindy, are you alright?
The one named Zindy shakes his head, muttering broken sentences as if in great shock.

speaker: Zindy
content: I... I can hear the monsters... The monsters are talking... they're saying...

speaker: Zindy
content: Liar... Liar... Vautour Bleu is a liar... She's...

speaker: Townie A
content: What do you mean, liar? Say it clear!
The girl shakes Zindy's shoulders to snap him out of daze, but Zindy just keeps mumbling the same few garbled sentences, his face pale.

speaker: Zindy
content: It says... It's Noffie... Noffie... That monster says it's Noffie!

speaker: Townie A
content: Didn't Noffie leave for DisCity? Miss Vautour Bleu told us she found him work in Eastside...
Huddling together, the townsfolk begin to recall the incoherent ramblings of the monsters outside.

speaker: Zindy
content: Has Vautour Bleu been lying to us all along...

speaker: Townie A
content: No! That's impossible! How dare you spout such nonsense!!!

speaker: Townie A
content: Miss Vautour Bleu would never lie to us! Never!
The monsters are lurking closer like bloodthirsty beasts battering at the door of a cage, the circle they form gradually tightening.

speaker: Monster
content: Destroy... Désir... Destroy everything!!!

speaker: Townie C
content: That voice... Darcy, is that you? Why... why are you here?
Seemingly responding, the monster stiffly twists its neck at an inhuman angle, fixing its hollow gaze on the one who called it name.
A tentacle coils around the person's leg, while another lashes toward an eye, ignoring the desperate screams of its former friend...

speaker: Townie A
content: No! Stay away from me...!!! NO!!!
In a flash, the tentacles are severed. The monster unleashes a bloodcurdling shriek.
Through the splashing blood, a calm figure steps forward, standing before the terrified townsfolk.

speaker: Townie A
content: You're... you're the newcomer...
I'm the MBCC's Chief from DisCity. I'm here to help you.

speaker: Local
content: DisCity... you said DisCity...
At the mere mention of DisCity, a spark of hope ignites as he staggers to his feet.

speaker: Local
content: Has DisCity sent help to us?!
Others emerge cautiously from hiding. They were wary just now seeing you fought off the monsters, but now they begin gathering upon hearing his cries of DisCity.

speaker: Zindy
content: DisCity has sent help! We're saved!

speaker: Local
content: Did Miss Vautour Bleu send you? I knew she'd come through for us! She wasn't lying. She'd never abandon us!
The townsfolk's eyes cling to you as if you're the only thread they can grasp.
...Head to the inn in the town center immediately. There's a safe zone set up there.
You cannot but dodge their questions. Yes, Vautour Bleu did send you, but they can't know that.
It's part of the deal you've made.
[Edge of town]

speaker: Chief
content: Are you hearing yourself? Provoking the townsfolk, draining their emotions, and channeling all this Mania... Once you start, there's no stopping it. If you can't hold the contamination, you'll end up a monster like those.

speaker: Chief
content: You call this a deal? It's a gamble, and a terrible one.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: I'm afraid this is a deal you cannot turn down. Because... it's already started.

speaker: Chief
content: Alright, you'll go through with it anyways, right? You're banking on me to protect them, betting that I'm not like the Outland Affairs Bureau, that I won't abandon them. And you don't care about your own safety, about whether my shackles could hold you back from degradation.

speaker: Chief
content: How on earth did your caravan even get to its scale? Trading yourself for the safety of the whole town, that's the worst deal I've ever heard.
Sensing your mood, Vautour Bleu brushes the dust off your coat with feigned ease and gives your shoulder a reassuring pat.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Well, thank goodness you're here.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Right now, the datura growth can only keep a small area safe—in the town center, around the inn.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: I'll guide as many people there as I can. The monsters will be swarming outside of it.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: And my dear neighbor, I need you to make a dashing entrance just at the perfect time, saving them from despair in the name of DisCity.
You're retreating with us. Don't even think about staging some heroic self-sacrifice. You still need to explain yourself to these people. There's no escaping that.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Explain myself? There's nothing to explain. I did this. I brought them here and deceived them. I'm trapping them in this utopia, feeding them empty promises.
From the town center, the sounds of panic and commotion grow louder, mingled with the clashing cries and the shrieks of monsters.
The hunt for Vautour Bleu has begun.
[Town center]
The small square in front of the inn is the last safe zone Vautour Bleu has created, fortified by the datura flowers. There, she stands in its center, encircled by a seething crowd of townsfolk.
The once familiar faces now regard her with confusion, bewilderment, and burning anger.
