speaker: Vigorous Flower Spirit
content: My my, look how worked up you are—you're sweating! Take a seat, relax, and let me help you freshen up.

speaker: %u
content: I don't need that. I'm looking for—mmph!!

speaker: Taleteller's Narration
content: Countless enchanting figures surge forward to surround the outlander, their melodious laughter more intoxicating than the sweetest floral scent. They grasp onto the outlander's garments, unwilling to release their hold.

speaker: Taleteller's Narration
content: Unfazed by their allure, the outlander firmly pushes away the ethereal beauties around, and with a stern voice and resolute bearing, declares once more:

speaker: %u
content: Don't touch me! I know what you're trying to do, and I want none of it. Let me through—I need to find someone!
I'm looking for the wisteria tree and the one who watches over its flowers!

speaker: Taleteller's Narration
content: Yet, the commotion hushes but for a fleeting moment. The alluring figures share knowing looks, then erupt into a wave of laughter.

speaker: Alluring Flower Spirit
content: Oh, now I see! Another young man bewitched by Yingying's beauty!
female_content: Oh, now I see! Another young lady bewitched by Yingying's beauty!

speaker: Elegant Flower Spirit
content: Alright, your words ring clear. Since you're so fond of Yingying, I suppose we have no other option...

speaker: Taleteller's Narration
content: Releasing their captive, the ethereal beauties pivot away with sinister giggles, veiling their faces. When they turn back, every single one of them bears Yingying's face!

speaker: Vigorous Flower Spirit
content: Well, is this face to your liking, my young lord?
female_content: Well, is this face to your liking, my young lady?

speaker: Alluring Flower Spirit
content: Yingying, a mere child... how could she rival my age-old experience? With this new guise adorning me, tell me, my young lord—between Yingying and I, who radiates greater beauty?
female_content: Yingying, a mere child... how could she rival my age-old experience? With this new guise adorning me, tell me, my young lady—between Yingying and I, who radiates greater beauty?

speaker: Taleteller's Narration
content: The outlander freezes in shock—any attempt to struggle now futile. The enchantresses, all wearing the same beguiling face, drift forth with melodic laughter and scented breeze. Sparing him no chance to protest, they force the outlander out of the building—
female_content: The outlander freezes in shock—any attempt to struggle now futile. The enchantresses, all wearing the same beguiling face, drift forth with melodic laughter and scented breeze. Sparing her no chance to protest, they force the outlander out of the building—

speaker: Taleteller's Narration
content: After multiple failed attempts to enter, the outlander once again stands before the Wisteria Pavilion. Facing its tightly shut gate, he furrows his brow, his heart burning with unbearable anxiety.
female_content: After multiple failed attempts to enter, the outlander once again stands before the Wisteria Pavilion. Facing its tightly shut gate, she furrows her brow, her heart burning with unbearable anxiety.

speaker: Taleteller's Narration
content: Each passing moment wasted here means more souls drawn into this sinister fete. These victims merely fuel the Mania wisteria, nurturing its relentless growth—until it devours all of DisCity.

speaker: Taleteller's Narration
content: How to lure out the wisteria spirit, and how to subdue her? Through torture? Or perhaps... fight charm with charm—might there be a way to tempt that bewitching being?

speaker: Option
options: Stop twisting me into your story!

speaker: %u
content: I am not a puppet of your narrative, and I have no interest in your tales! Show yourself!!!

speaker: Taleteller's Narration
content: Heh, how ironic. The one you seek is right here, yet refuses to meet you—hiding from you.

speaker: Taleteller's Narration
content: The streets now swell with people—citizens of DisCity, all entranced by the festive revelry. These captives of the flower spirit are now being paraded before you, as if to mock your helplessness.

speaker: %u
content: I don't care about your flower spirit or your preaching. None of this interests me in the slightest.

speaker: %u
content: Lift your power, free the hostages! You come face me!

speaker: Taleteller's Narration
content: Heh, all at the Fete yearn for another soul. Yet, how will you ever find her? If she refuses to meet you, what recourse remains in your grasp?

speaker: Taleteller's Narration
content: Fate is unkind, the path ahead treacherous. Let us see how far our wayward outlander can venture.

speaker: Chief
content: Ugh...

Your vision blurs as darkness surges from all sides, accompanied by an overwhelming floral fragrance that seeps into your core and drains your vigor. Your knees buckle, and with your last shred of consciousness, you only manage to adjust your posture to protect your head from the impending fall.
But instead of collapsing helplessly onto the spirit-infested street as expected, you feel an ice-cold hand through your clothes steady your back, deftly halting your fall.
That day... merit... too greedy... futile... thankfully...

You feel yourself being propped up against something. A fragmented voice drifts down from above, the words too indistinct to grasp, and something warm flows into your mouth. You can't tell what it is, but the overpowering darkness that had enveloped you begins to soften.

speaker: Chief
content: ...! Did I... pass out from exhaustion? I knew there was something wrong with this street...

Your consciousness snaps back, and your eyes fly open. Years of experience kick in as you immediately check your limbs for freedom of movement and assess your mental clarity. Only after confirming everything is in order do you cautiously survey your surroundings.
The medicine has barely reached your stomach, and the needles are still in place. My friend, for your own well-being, please remain still and composed for a while longer.

speaker: Chief
content: You're... the one who warned me on the street earlier? Did you save me from those "spirits"?

The young girl emerges silently from the shadows, responding with both a nod and a shake of her head. Her unnervingly serene demeanor remains unchanged as she peers at you through her heavy bangs with clear eyes, delicate acupuncture needles held between her fingers.
Yes. You may call me Wuhuanzi. But... I am but a wandering herbalist from Eastia, traveling across lands to save lives and accumulate merit. I can't slay demons or exorcise evil spirits.

speaker: Chief
content: But you clearly warned me not to linger here... Doesn't that mean you have already noticed something wrong with this place?

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: I merely noticed the ominous shadows surrounding you, signs of vital energy depletion, so I thought to offer a word of caution, hoping to gain some small merit. Had you heeded my warning and turned back then, the situation wouldn't have become so grave.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Yet now, you have glimpsed the forbidden and treaded paths you ought not to have. Your Qi lay scattered... This is why I resorted to such measures—brewing a decoction of eighty-one herbs and applying gold needles to your acupoints—to pull you back from the brink.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Let this serve as a lesson, at least. You must now understand that your constitution cannot withstand the forces at work here. Any further struggle would be futile. You would do well to leave this place of turmoil while you can.

Though her words remain somewhat cryptic, you flex your palm—still pierced with needles—and find your strength has indeed returned. The mysterious decoction she administered radiates warmth in your stomach, its contents unknown yet undeniably potent.

...Could this be the mysterious power of Eastia? You can't help but feel a deep sense of reverence. The young herbalist before you may be peculiar in her demeanor, but she has genuinely helped you—surely not one of those spirits coveting your "Qi."
In that case... you decide to take the risk.

options: I wish I could leave, but there's something I must do first.

speaker: Chief
content: Many others have been drawn into this fete full of strange spirits—both my friends and innocent DisCity people. Their physical bodies, existing beyond this "story," are growing weaker by the moment.

speaker: Chief
content: And that's probably because everyone's vital energy—or Qi—as you mentioned, is being drained—by the spirits, and by the wisteria. If this continues...

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: I see. But this fete harbors unfathomable dangers. In your condition... how do you intend to resolve this? You'll likely collapse again within a few hours.
Her amber eyes fix upon you with an intent gaze, as calm and steady as her voice. Faced with her sobering yet precise question, you take a deep breath.

speaker: Chief
content: You're right, I won't last long. So I was wondering... would you be willing to help restore that "Qi" of mine regularly?

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: You're asking me... just to restore your Qi?

speaker: Chief
content: Yes. You've already saved me once, haven't you? I figure with effective treatments, I can explore more areas and find clues to resolve this fete situation. I don't mind falling down... as long as I can get back up again.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Qi isn't like medicine that you can simply replenish after it's depleted. Repeated treatments won't be very effective, and I can't guarantee they'll be painless or harmless... It's an inefficient and taxing solution.

speaker: Chief
content: An inefficient solution will do. As long as it works... and as long as you're willing to help. I apologize, I know this is a presumptuous request, but there are people I must save, things I must do. I really need your help.
You meet the young Eastian herbalist's scrutinizing gaze with unwavering sincerity. After a moment, Wuhuanzi is the first to avert her gaze.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: ...Is this what they mean by "ignorance is bliss"? ...Very well, I suppose rescuing such a headstrong and audacious soul could be deemed a form of merit.

Muttering to herself, Wuhuanzi bends down to gather her belongings. You watch her movements nervously, only to find that after packing up, all she does is take a single small step to your side, bundle on her back, and plant herself firmly there.

speaker: Chief
content: Does this mean you agree? Are you... coming with me?

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Naturally. A patient lacking self-care awareness requires constant supervision, and I cannot afford to forgo such a chance for merit... Besides, following you should lead to many people in need of treatment—plenty of good deeds to accumulate merit, I dare say.

A burden lifts from your chest now that the concern of "Qi" limitations no longer haunts you. Gathering your strength, you stride forward, and the clear jingling of ornaments trails closely behind like a shadow. A smile unconsciously graces your lips.

speaker: Taleteller's Narration
content: A sea of people floods the grounds before the House of Tales, thronging its entrance. The crowd encircles the small building where Yugu holds court, the ground already strewn with flowers and fruits—a scene of jubilant celebration.

speaker: Taleteller's Narration
content: Outside the gate, a white banner bears bold characters proudly proclaiming—Hazy Fete in a Daze: Volume II.

speaker: Taleteller's Narration
content: It is none other than the story she has prepared just for you.

speaker: Taleteller's Narration
content: After much effort to squeeze through the crowd, the outlander arrives just as the taleteller begins her story.
[Yugu's portrait]

speaker: Yugu
content: They say, a hundred miles south of the town, a female ghost wandered. Her beauty was beyond compare, yet destruction followed in her wake. With her enchanting form, she lured victims into the mountains, draining their life before casting them aside like refuse.

speaker: Yugu
content: Yet neither monks nor priests could subdue her—some lacked the spiritual might to match her power, while others fell victim to her bewitching beauty. For over a decade, none could bring her to heel.

speaker: Yugu
content: Yet, who could have foreseen such a twist? This fearsome ghost, with all her countless sins, one day relinquished her powers, professing an absurd notion of self-reformation—declaring, "I vow to wed none but him."
female_content: Yet, who could have foreseen such a twist? This fearsome ghost, with all her countless sins, one day relinquished her powers, professing an absurd notion of self-reformation—declaring, "I vow to wed none but her."

speaker: Yugu
content: And just who was this mysterious figure who managed to tame such a sinister ghost?

speaker: Spirit Audience
content: —!!

You look around at the audience cheering for her performance—not a single one appears remotely human. Every last one of them is some manner of fiend or spirit, wild-eyed and grotesque in appearance. You can't help but find the situation somewhat amusing.

speaker: %u
content: Creating a fake audience to applaud your own made-up story? Hah, what a narcissistic author we have here.

speaker: %u
content: I wonder if a "taleteller" like yourself can handle having your tales criticized.

You take the teacup from a spirit server and slam it onto the table with a thunderous crash that echoes through the hall. In an instant, every spirit spectator falls dead silent, all eyes fixed upon you.
Even the taleteller on stage pauses her performance, slowly raising her head until her gaze locks with yours.

speaker: Yugu
content: My... do you find my story dissatisfying again, dear guest?
Her words inciting, she's clearly waiting for you to make your move. You step forward to confront her.

speaker: %u
content: The story's quality isn't the issue here. I came in because of the sign outside, but it looks like you're pulling a bit of a bait-and-switch here.

speaker: %u
content: Telling all this ghost story of supernatural nonsense, are you?

speaker: %u
content: Change the story! Tell me what this Fete really is—how you're using it to lure people in and drain their life!

speaker: %u
content: Tell me what these "guests" of yours really are, and what evil scheme you, the taleteller, are plotting here!
The taleteller puts on an act of pure innocence.

speaker: Yugu
content: My dear guest, if the festivities trouble you, direct your inquiries to the rightful host—the mistress of the Wisteria Pavilion, that spirit who breathes life into the blossoms across the streets. Why burden a humble taleteller like myself?

speaker: Yugu
content: I am not even part of this fete—merely a wanderer passing through, an outsider present just to hear a story.

speaker: %u
content: "An outsider?" I'd say this entire fete materialized straight from your "story."
You stride purposefully toward the performance stage at the center. The audience shoots disapproving glances your way, but you pay them no mind.

speaker: %u
content: Let's cut to the chase—this fete, these spectators, even the ancient tree out there, the flower spirit, every single plant and leaf—they're all just illusions you've conjured up.

speaker: %u
content:
In this entire street, you're the only real human here—along with all those 
DisCitizens you've trapped in your scheme.

speaker: %u
content: All this effort to set up the Wisteria Pavilion, staging these absurd scenes to deceive people... and then forcing them to stay against their will.

speaker: %u
content: I heard Eastians pride themselves on their sense of propriety. Aren't you embarrassed to stoop this low?
The taleteller gives you a smile, eyes narrowing.

speaker: Yugu
content: Oh? Are you going to flip the table in a rage and leave in the middle of the show, my dear guest?

speaker: Option
options: Now that would be too dull of a plot.

speaker: %u
content: End this absurd soul-draining fete and release your hostages. Now.

speaker: Yugu
content: Heh... If you follow my script perfectly, step by step, the fete shall end in due time. Why such impatience?

speaker: Option
options: I'm not impatient. I'm just tired of your story.

content: [Release the shackles]
Though your strength is nearly spent, you summon every last ounce of power to unleash the shackles. A crimson light erupts, shattering the stage rails.

speaker: %u
content: Worthless stories. Even all these cheap tricks can't keep your audience. Stop forcing your performance on everyone—you're wasting our time.
In an instant, the guests dissolve like mist, leaving the taleteller alone on the stage.

speaker: Yugu
content: Well, well... I almost forgot what a fascinating being you are. Such remarkable power—how wonderful it would be to weave you into my collection of tales... Yet, before we proceed, let us establish some ground rules.
Her gentle smile never wavers as she raises her hand with delicate grace, and then...
(Multiple portraits appear)
The fiends and spirits from her bizarre tales materialize one by one, their intimidating howls filling the air as they lunge at you!

speaker: Yugu
content: This marks your second interruption of my story. A toll must be paid for such disturbances... Don't you agree, Chief?

After you vanquish the final of Yugu's controlled spirits, the mist dissipates, only to reveal Yugu herself has disappeared without a trace. The hall now stands utterly empty—no storyteller, no audience, nothing remains.

speaker: Yugu
content: Right here.
Yugu's soft whisper tickles your ear, sending chills down your spine, compelling you to hurriedly whirl around.
[Release the shackles]
The crimson light slices through the tea tables like a razor through paper, tearing apart space itself—yet it fails to cut short her increasingly gleeful laughter.
In a daze, Yugu's silhouette appears and vanishes throughout the building, always dancing at the edges of your vision.

speaker: Yugu
content: Ah, such resolve. Are you attempting to dispel this illusion, rouse all from their reveries, and return to your world? What purpose does targeting me serve?

speaker: Yugu
content: If indeed this realm is tangible, the wisteria spirit would be the true culprit, with your dear Yingying as the orchestrator of this nightmare—you should seek her out instead. However, if everything here is but a fabrication, as you assert, a mere narrative woven by a taleteller...

speaker: Yugu
content: The real me should have already been imprisoned in the real world by the real you, restrained so tightly that even wings would not aid in my escape. So why tire yourself rushing here to confront me?

speaker: %u
content: Still taking me for a fool? In the entire Bureau, only OwO and I fell under the illusion—and it happened right when you were telling your story. That's when the wisteria spirit infiltrated DisCity. You're behind all of this.

speaker: %u
content: And you deliberately hid in this fabricated world. If I didn't come in after you, what was I supposed to do? Stand out there and rage at your soulless body, huh?

speaker: Yugu
content: My, how mistaken you are. I witnessed your plight at the fete, lost in pursuit of the flower spirit. Seeing no headway in the rescue, I dared to venture into this realm to offer you my assistance.

speaker: Yugu
content: After all, you appear utterly clueless when it comes to dealing with spirits. Did you truly believe that sheer aggression and brute strength alone could suffice to slay evil and uphold justice?
With her folding fan, she mockingly toys with the luminous thorns of your shackles.

speaker: Yugu
content: Or perhaps you intend to chant divine scriptures to those wicked spirits? To preach ethics, propriety, and moral values until they grasp the enlightenment and transform from sinners to saints?

speaker: Yugu
content: Heh heh, do you not see the futility in such an approach? A narrative so lackluster would never enthrall an audience, let alone tame a malevolent spirit!
...Do you really love him that much? You've never even met, or spent any time together.

speaker: Yugu
content: I have concealed the key to your predicament within my previous tale, hoping to guide you discreetly. If you had only been more patient and listened until the end, all would unveil itself with utmost clarity.
—Tales again. You've grown sick of her endless "tales," wanting only to condemn her, defeat her, and capture her.

However, your shackles defy your commands as the repercussions of your drained life tighten their grip. Wisps of smoke frolic before your eyes, toying with your mind. It dawns on you that Yugu is employing her power to compel you to hear the rest of her narrative.

speaker: Yugu
content: Across the myriad of peculiar tales weaved through time, a common thread binds the most popular narratives of malevolent spirits—their protagonists seldom required profound spiritual prowess to tame those entities.

speaker: Yugu
content: They either possess charm that bewitches at first sight, or wealth so vast it could make spirits bow to their will.

speaker: Yugu
content: And if nothing else, consider the young scholar from my earlier tale—the earnestness in his words so profound that it convinced the ghost of the authenticity of his love, touching her very soul. Given enough time, even the coldest heart can thaw in the warmth of true affection.
female_content: And if nothing else, consider the young maiden from my earlier tale—the earnestness in her words so profound that it convinced the ghost of the authenticity of her love, touching the ghost's very soul. Given enough time, even the coldest heart can thaw in the warmth of true affection.

content: Standing on her stage, her words coil around you like serpents, slithering into your mind. Her voice draws nearer and nearer until you sense her grinning presence mere inches from you.

speaker: Yugu
content: Love blossoms from three yearnings: beauty, power, and genuine affection. Master just one or two, and not only will you persuade the wisteria spirit to amend her ways and spare your people—she might even sacrifice herself for your cause. Who can say? You might even amass an entire legion of spirits and fiends under your sway.

speaker: Yugu
content: My dear guest, have you grasped the meaning of my tale?

speaker: Yugu
content: In these mystical tales, the best way to tame a spirit is to become a charming <color=#fb9259>heart-taker</color>—to make them fall helplessly, desperately in love with you!
In the midst of her playful words, she flings her sleeve—and suddenly, a horde of alluring spectral women surge forth, lunging toward you!

speaker: %u
content: Get out of here!
The crimson light tears through the ghostly veils, only to reveal a book hurtling towards you. You catch it reflexively. Though written in Eastian script, you realize you can understand the title—
Of all things, it's called Chronicles of Romance and Lust.

speaker: Yugu
content: Every secret technique, triumphant tale, and mystical artifact that guarantees victory—it is all inscribed herein. While countless have beseeched me for this tome, my response has always been denial. Yet now, I present it unto you as a gift.

speaker: Yugu
content: I am certain that each word will resonate with you, my dear listener.
You hurl the book away in disgust, refusing to let it sully your hands.

speaker: %u
content: Not everyone in DisCity has a taste for such wicked schemes—especially not when you're causing this kind of trouble.

speaker: %u
content: ..."Tales of the most exquisite beauty," said you? Don't you hear how absurd that sounds?
Seeing your anger, she responds with a soft laugh.

speaker: Yugu
content: Yet this is precisely what captivates the audience, rendering it beautiful and entertaining in its own way. Did you not find delight on your first visit here?

speaker: Yugu
content: If existence is already laden with tribulations, why must narratives burden people further? What harm lies in offering the audience what they yearn for—stories of desire, love, and enchantment? For in truth, I too hold dear their smiles.

speaker: Yugu
content: Or perhaps, you prefer something more... unorthodox?
Her smile grows deeper as she fixes you with an intense, penetrating gaze.

speaker: Yugu
content: Indeed, I have heard of your encounters—the Black Rings, calamities, bitter hatred, painful partings, the grand drama of life and death. Each one eclipses my humble tales of spirits by far.

speaker: Yugu
content: Such tales might not please the common ear, but I find them... fascinating.

speaker: Yugu
content: If you'd be willing to share them with me, I could write something beyond my usual tales of romance and folly... something "truly" remarkable.
The air grows cold as she turns to you, her gaze a disturbing blend of sincerity and hunger that sends a chill down your spine.
Soon, you recognize that creeping sensation as anger, and your composure quickly returns.

speaker: %u
content: If solving your little game requires following your "guidance," fine—I'll play along. But my struggles, my past, my joys and sorrows... they're not for your entertainment. These experiences belong to me alone.

speaker: %u
content: Your pursuit of stories is nothing but watching others suffer from a safe distance, deriving pleasure from their pain. Your so-called "protagonists" are just toys to you. I have no interest in dealing with someone like you, and I don't want to waste my time on you.

speaker: %u
content: Just a friendly reminder—when setting your traps, you might consider being more careful.

speaker: Option
options: Or your toy might just tear your stories apart.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Aconite root, pokeweed, datura flower... Just a moment, my friend. This prescription is rather complex. It's quite potent precisely because of its toxic nature.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Combined with the time-based acupuncture technique, as long as we calculate the right acupoints at the proper hour, we can restore your Qi in no time...

speaker: Chief
content: ...Wait, did you just say the medicine is toxic?! And what's all this about needle techniques, proper hours, and calculating acupoints...?

speaker: Chief
content: (She let herself get led away by some spirit who was obviously suspicious, volunteered for treatment only to make everything worse, and now she's using medicine made from what might as well be poisonous weeds from DisCity's gardens... I really might have asked the wrong person for help...)

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: I've calculated which acupoints we need. Please, have a seat.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: This shouldn't hurt... You can ease yourself further. Should your muscles remain excessively taut, the task of the needles in accessing the acupoints might be impeded, potentially compromising the treatment's effectiveness.

For once, you're actually clear-headed while receiving this mysterious Eastian treatment, though doubt and unease still linger in your mind. Trying to distract yourself, you attempt to relax your muscles while starting a conversation.

speaker: Chief
content: I'd say I'm pretty experienced with handling pain, so this is more like... nervousness, I guess. I mean, I've never had the pleasure of getting the same treatment as a spirit—is this a standard practice?

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Rather than a matter of standard practice... I'd say all afflictions—be they mundane or spiritual—are simply illnesses. For us practitioners of healing, there exist only two kinds: those we can cure, and those beyond our reach.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Even the entities you refer to as "spirits"—their madness, their twisted forms—all stem from illness. Where there is an illness, there lies the potential for remedy. And where healing is achieved, merit is gained.

speaker: Chief
content: So that's why you never shy away from them, even actively seeking them out to treat their illnesses, refusing to give up even when you might be deceived...?
Wuhuanzi nods.

speaker: Chief
content: All this effort for what you call "merit"...? But those conditions you have been treating—they might already be at the terminal stage beyond saving.

As the medicinal concoction bubbles away, you observe Wuhuanzi skillfully inserting needles while you remain seated. Her expression retains its characteristic impassiveness—neither discouraged by failure nor seemingly aware of the subtle probing in your words.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Are you not the same, my friend? You willingly venture into the territory of "spirits" to save companions who may be beyond saving, strangers who might have already been devoured...

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: You stake your own vitality as collateral, treating your Qi as a disposable resource. Yet deep down, you know full well that herbalists are not miracle workers—I cannot wholly rejuvenate a body that has been constantly pushed to the brink of the "terminal stage."

The young herbalist from Eastia deftly pours the medicinal brew into a porcelain bowl and hands it to you. As you grimace at the visibly unpalatable concoction, her voice grows softer, watching you as if pondering something.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: To be honest, I've seen many who spurn treatment, harbor suspicions, question my intentions, or hold fast to the belief that mere healing cannot alter destiny... Yet, never have I crossed paths with someone like you, eagerly allowing me to "reap" merit from them.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: I can't help but wonder—perhaps my decoction isn't bitter enough?

speaker: Chief
content: ...Are you saying there are even more bitter medicines? Don't tell me I didn't need to drink something this bitter...

You wipe away the involuntary tears brought on by the medicine's pure bitterness, unable to hide your growing suspicion. Wuhuanzi, however, merely lowers her gaze, her lips tightening ever so slightly.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Effective medicine often carries a bitter taste, yet increased bitterness doesn't equate to superior efficacy. If stronger bitterness truly meant better effect... I wouldn't mind even if you called me the Yama of Bitter Remedies.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: ...If only it were that simple. Medicine remains just medicine in the end. There will forever be realms beyond its grasp, pains it cannot soothe. Perhaps that's what you meant by the "terminal stage."

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: For now, all I wish... is to help you escape this place before that inevitable state befalls you. And if we can save others along the way... all the better.

There she goes again. You observe this young Eastian girl, whose eerie presence stands out even in this mystical street of spirits, as you silently finish the medicine. She always sees the worst, always speaks of the worst—struggling negatively while enthusiastically giving up.
From her cryptic words and contradictory actions, you can be certain of one thing: this young Sinner before you... must be harboring some hidden truth that drives her to act this way.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Though I suspected as much... aren't you perhaps... putting too much faith in me? I have mentioned before that medicine isn't omnipotent. If you keep depleting your Qi like this, not even divine intervention could save you...

Wuhuanzi's already subdued demeanor has noticeably darkened further in response to the current circumstances—you're certain you're not imagining it. Her words trail off, almost merging into a sigh, prompting you to jump in before she can proceed.

options: This will be the last time.

speaker: Chief
content: I promise. I've gathered all the artifacts Yugu mentioned, so the Wisteria Pavilion should open its gate... I can go in soon and put an end to this fete.

speaker: Chief
content: So...

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Is this last treatment to be both your rejuvenation and parting blessing? You seem quite certain that all answers lie within the Wisteria Pavilion.

speaker: Chief
content: I can't say for sure how much of Yugu's words holds true. But I know without a doubt that the Wisteria Pavilion is the core of this fete. I've been inside before... and the answer to everything lies right there.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: What I want to know is, even if you make it into the Wisteria Pavilion, are you certain you can hold out until you "solve everything"? I could tell from our first meeting that you were already suffering from spiritual and physical exhaustion...

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Despite my efforts to support you on this journey, I could scarcely keep you going—and that hardly made any impact in the broader context. Should you venture into that place... how long can you endure? Will you even be able to fight?

Wuhuanzi's words mirror the chill of her hands—sharp as a surgeon's scalpel, cutting with brutal precision. Though her pessimism can be overwhelming, the concerns she raises are impossible to deny. You find yourself at a loss for words.
As you struggle to stir your thoughts—now as thick and congealed as cold porridge—searching for words that might convince Wuhuanzi, she unexpectedly gives a resigned smile.

speaker: Chief
content: ...Wuhuanzi?

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Save your strength, my friend. There's no need to try convincing me anymore. No matter how much I object, you won't give up anyway, will you?

speaker: Chief
content: You're right... This is the only path left for me to take, after all.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Very well. Your nature has been clear to me from the start—forging ahead despite the insurmountable odds. Interposing at this point would serve as nothing but futile opposition.

Her sudden compliance catches you off guard. As you stare at her in confusion, she produces a handkerchief from her sleeve and carefully unfolds it, revealing a round pill emanating the scent of medicinal herbs.

speaker: Chief
content: This is...?

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: All this time spent rushing around the streets with you, conducting examinations... it hasn't been in vain. I've gained some more understanding of "Qi"—what it drives, what it sustains, and what it changes...

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: And I've learned how it cycles and harmonizes with all else. With this insight, I can prevent your Qi from depleting without resorting to taxing exertions as before. All I need to do now is use medicine to protect your internal organs.

speaker: Chief
content: You mean... if I take this, I won't have to worry about running out of Qi anymore?

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: At least for a short period... yes.

You never expected this young herbalist from Eastia could help you to such an extent. Your eyes widen in amazement as you stare at her. Only after Wuhuanzi gives a solemn nod do you carefully reach out, take the pill, and place it in your mouth.

In an instant, the exhaustion from Qi depletion dissipates, and your mind becomes crystal clear once more. Though you don't understand how it works, the medicine you took without hesitation proves remarkably effective.

speaker: Chief
content: This is incredible... It's not my first time experiencing it firsthand, but Eastian medicine never fails to amaze me... No, this must be because of your exceptional skill, Wuhuanzi. You really are a miracle worker...

Even if it's only temporary, finding a solution to this problem fills you with joy. Like discovering a precious treasure, you shower Wuhuanzi with praise. Even your upcoming mission to the Wisteria Pavilion, which you were unsure about before, now seems more promising.
Yet Wuhuanzi shows not even a trace of joy at your praise. She shakes her head ever so slightly as a deeper melancholy clouds her weary eyes.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Miracle worker... If only there were true miracle cures, if only there were miracle herbalists capable of saving all... but regretfully, this medicine only offers temporary relief, a brief respite from your troubles.

speaker: Chief
content: That's more than enough! I can't expect you to solve everything, can I? I'm the one who chose to save the people trapped here, to deal with this dangerous fete... Even if the medicine wears off, it's my responsibility to figure out what to do.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: "Solve"... Such a vague word, just like "cure." These are things I truly cannot do.

Her words leave you momentarily puzzled, but the young girl from Eastia seems to have no intention of making herself clear. She simply raises her head to gaze at the magnificent building in the distance, its gate tightly shut. Her expression is a paradox—both steeled for battle and resigned to defeat.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Heal one patient, and another appears. Mend old injuries, only for new ones to form... Patients like you, who need treatment again and again despite our best efforts—that is the norm for us herbalists. We are truly powerless, forever fighting a losing battle.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: That's why I tried to warn you—such persistence is futile. Yet, I understand. Even if it means using a cup of water to put out a cartload of burning firewood, like a mantis raising its arms to block a cart, people never learn to turn back until they hit a wall.

Though her Eastian idioms and metaphors elude your understanding, her tightly pressed lips and clenched fists speak volumes—she seems to be fighting something, a battle that exists only within her heart. After a moment of internal struggle, she raises her head again.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: My friend... This is all I can do for you now. Once you enter the Wisteria Pavilion, even if I wish to help you further, I'm afraid my abilities will fall short.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: And it's not just me... Even you might find yourself powerless once inside. Medicine, artifacts, a kind heart, and even the most earnest determination—all might prove futile in the end. But you're still going in, aren't you?
You have no other choice. Though you sense there's more to her words than meets the eye, you can't stop to question her further—not when you're so close to your goal.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: ...I see. Then all I can do is give you my best wishes... May fortune favor you, and may your wishes be fulfilled.

She presses her lips together gently, her gaze fixed on you yet seeming to look through you at something far beyond. Then, shouldering her belongings, she silently accompanies you toward the grand building glowing with lamplight.
