content: But these are my own experiences, words from the depths of my heart... I left my wife too early. Had I known I would die in battle, I should have never accepted her proposal, only to waste her entire life...

speaker: Luminita
content: Come on, it's not like you're the one getting married! This is supposed to be a happy occasion, so stop with all the whining. First rule of being a top-tier real estate agent—the customer's needs come first! Now, listen and repeat after me:

speaker: Luminita
content: Dear friends, we are here today to share in this couple's happiness! Their love is like a meticulously designed luxury apartment, complete with a balcony overlooking the ocean and a sunlit conservatory, every corner filled with warmth and happiness!

speaker: Dullahan
content: Ocean view? Morveth Castle doesn't have an ocean view.

speaker: Luminita
content: DisSea is still a sea, the Rust is still a river—It's about your marketing skills! Don't get hung up on these details. Now, repeat after me: Their love will build a perfect home, and no matter what storms may come, this place will forever be their safe haven!

speaker: Dullahan
content: But life often brings storms we never see coming...

speaker: Luminita
content: Keep a positive mindset, and good things will follow! You've got potential, so why all the downer talk? Tell you what—get a copy of Luminita's Top-tier Real Estate Agent Guidebook, and I promise smooth sailing from here on out!

BANG!! The slightly unhinged figure in a trench coat crashes through the study door, catching you and Graves crouched by the bookshelf, her transformation barely held at bay as your hands grip each other tightly.
[Luminita's Back]

speaker: ${PlayerName} & Graves
content: I must say, your friends are all quite... special.

speaker: Graves
content: I-I don't know her...

speaker: Luminita
content: Don't worry if you don't know me—the best properties will find you! Once you move in, you'll never want to leave, and if you do, you'll never forget it! Prime location, perfect feng shui, it'll fix all your worries and brighten your days! Now, for this charming couple...
[Luminita's Front]

speaker: Luminita
content: How about it? Interested in a property?

speaker: Dullahan
content: Interested in a property?

speaker: Dullahan
content: Your sales speech doesn't seem to be working, Miss Agent.

speaker: Graves
content: Dullahan?
Sales speech?
So that confrontation in the hallway wasn't directed at you at all, but at this... real estate agent here?
The self-proclaimed "speech guru" awkwardly fidgets with her coat and backpack, her eyes darting from you to Graves, before locking onto your hands—which neither of you has thought to release.

speaker: Luminita
content: Well, well, holding hands, are we? Hmm, nice place you've got here... a cozy, intimate little hideaway.

speaker: Luminita
content: I have no idea what you two were... Never mind! Carry on, I didn't see a thing. Not a single thing.
You feel the temperature rising where your skin touches Graves's, her complexion deepening to an even darker shade of red.

speaker: Graves
content: You've got it all wrong! We... we weren't doing anything!

The words have barely left her lips when Graves yanks her hand away and vanishes without a trace. The shadowy figure you've worked so hard to approach, along with the truth you were about to uncover, slip right through your fingers—all because of this uninvited guest.
You glare at the real estate agent before you, but she just grins shamelessly while twirling her keyring, looking you up and down.

speaker: Luminita
content: Don't tell me she's actually shy? Seriously? The legendary ghost bride has fallen for a <color=#fb9259>sleepwalking visitor</color>?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What do you m—Oof!
Before you can finish your sentence, she pulls something from her pocket and shoves it into your mouth—
[White flash] [Flashback]

It's late at the Bureau. After a long day of duties, you return to your bedroom to rest. But one final task remains—examining a mysterious storybook Labyrinth found during her routine cleaning. Nightingale has asked you to inspect it as a precaution.
You flip through the pages casually, nothing suspicious catches your eye. The book recounts an unverifiable tale with little to ground it in reality.

Thorns blanket black stones, a bride roams Morveth Castle—white veil, dark shadow, whispers echo. Spider silk coils around fingers, insect bones float in goblets; guests may drink, promising to stay. Yet no one comes, her dress sweeps the stone stairs, the bride has a wish that cannot be locked away. You, who turn these pages—███, grant her wish, keep her company. When the moon reaches its zenith, go to her—never leave, never forget, never betray.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What's that smell?

The picture book looks utterly ordinary, almost unremarkable, yet a peculiar fragrance wafts from its pages. The scent is faint but persistent, filling the air and creeping into your nose and throat with every breath. It leaves behind a faint, stinging burn that lingers.
By the time you realize something is wrong, it's already too late. Under the influence of the fragrance, drowsiness quickly overtakes you. You sink deep into sleep, until—
You wake up inside a coffin in Morveth Castle.
[End of Flashback]

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Cough, cough...
The book... that strange scent! The events from before you arrived here flood back.

You spit out whatever Luminita stuffed into your mouth, and the memory fragment before your eyes ends. Only then do you see clearly what you've spat out—two white objects about the size of fingernails.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What did you just shove into my mouth?
Before you can press further, she hands you a small advertisement flyer:

GREAT NEWS! GREAT NEWS! FREE PAIR OF EVIL-WARDING DOG TEETH WITH EVERY HOUSE VIEWING!
Protect your home and ensure peace—the lucky charm every generation needs!
For viewings, call Luminita at: <color=#fb9259>0871-1408</color>
[Luminita sticks out her tongue]
[Bureau Lounge]

It's early morning. The Bureau lounge is in complete silence. EMP, overtaken by exhaustion, lies slumped awkwardly in a chair, her breathing slow and steady in deep sleep. Labyrinth has also activated her energy-saving mode, entering temporary hibernation.
Among the Sinners keeping watch over the Chief, only Hecate remains awake. She notices the first signs of movement from the previously unresponsive figure, catching the faint sound of mumbling.
Hecate moves closer with concern, trying to make out Chief's words, but what she hears only leaves her more confused.
No thanks, I'm good, really. I already have my own place... Wait, what? That cheap?
No, no, I was talking about the castle, don't change the subject... Huh? You want to buy my place? It's not for sale! That's government property!
[Corridor]

speaker: Luminita
content: So you're THE Chief? Mamma mia, you MBCC folks sure have special dreams, coming all the way out here to get forced into marrying a beautiful bride! Man, why don't I ever get that lucky... Yes, yes, yes, move that ribbon more to the left!
You try to extract more information from her, but she's either busy directing No. 15 and Dullahan in setting up the venue, or habitually steering the conversation back to real estate.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Should we wait until you're done with this?

speaker: Luminita
content: Don't worry about it! I've got nothing to fret over. I'm standing here in the castle, flesh and blood. You, though... who knows what kind of trick someone pulled to yank your soul out and toss it here... Hey! Those flowers can't be in odd numbers! They must be in pairs!

Soul extraction, astral projection... Luminita is absolutely convinced you're a spirit that drifted here while your body sleeps elsewhere. Could this explain why you lost your memories when you woke up here? But who could possibly do such a thing to you? Though she notices you don't fully trust her theory, she keeps going regardless.

speaker: Luminita
content: But a sleepwalking soul that thinks they're really here, and a bride who exists despite being called a ghost—you two make quite the perfect match! If you actually fall for each other, I'd be happy to chip in for the wedding gift.
She gives your shoulder a hearty pat, then glances furtively around the hall. Seeing that no one is watching, she leans in and lowers her voice:

speaker: Luminita
content: Morveth Castle has the power to manifest longing into physical form—that's how No. 15 and Dullahan came into existence. But that power alone couldn't possibly target you so precisely, could it? Did you know our beautiful bride before all this?

The agent speaks casually about it, but you can't take this situation lightly. Someone deliberately planted that book in the Bureau, lured you into a dream, and pulled you into this wedding while you were vulnerable. You're no stranger to being trapped in illusions, but the power required to orchestrate something like this is far from ordinary.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I didn't know Graves, but I can't rule out the possibility that someone who knows us both arranged this "match."

speaker: Luminita
content: Yep, that's about all I've got, so... congrats on getting married!

speaker: Luminita
content: Hey, hey, hey! No. 15, where did you dig up all this junk? Put it back right now, I'm begging you! Decorations are perfect as they are—we don't need your personal collection! Hey, you there, sir! The flame atop your head has completely burned out the flowers!
Luminita's composure is truly remarkable—she effortlessly handles a Sinner on the verge of becoming a Corruptor, two Mania monsters, and you, a wandering spirit, all without missing a beat.

Thanks to her information, regardless of whether it's true or false, it's time to decide. Dullahan's speech may have felt out of place at the wedding, but he was right—an unintentional trap is a hundred times crueler than any calculated harm.
You look up toward the window—dawn is approaching.

Moonlight spills through the high windows, its final rays dancing across the corridor floor. Dust rises into the air one by one, shimmering like tiny stars as the trailing hem of a dress sweeps through—the bride has arrived.

The contamination on her face is gone, her skin restored to the pale, delicate complexion you first saw—this is the "perfect appearance" she wants, one "worthy of a perfect wedding." She must have exerted tremendous effort to suppress that shadow within her.

speaker: Luminita
content: Let's give the couple some time to themselves! I'm sure they have something important to discuss.

speaker: Luminita
content: Dullahan, No. 15, hurry up and get ready! Follow my lead! Wait until the couple enters before starting the music.
She makes a theatrical show of retreating into the hall, closing the heavy doors behind her, leaving only you and Graves alone in the corridor.
[Corridor Transition]
Without Luminita, silence reclaims the corridor. You stand shoulder to shoulder facing the ceremonial hall doors, neither of you speaking, the air thick with lingering warmth.

Graves hesitates, then gently lifts the hem of her dress, taking one tentative step toward you, then another. She doesn't stop until the moonlight frames both your shadows together beneath the same stained glass window.

You notice her breathing is quicker than usual, her heartbeat betraying her mix of excitement and nervousness. Her veil sways gently with each tiny movement, the delicate fabric brushing against your shoulder. She steals a few glances at you, darting away before they linger too long.
You know she's waiting for the doors to open and the music to begin—this wedding is her lifelong dream, the ultimate proof that she will never be abandoned again.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Graves...

options: I have something I want to tell you.

content: [Confused Graves]

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Do you remember our arrangement? I said I would agree to marry you, and in exchange, you would tell me everything about this place.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I originally just wanted more information to resolve this Mania crisis, but I've realized that the wedding means far more to you than I thought. It's not just your fixation on a ceremony, and it shouldn't have been something I used as a bargaining chip.

She doesn't seem to understand, remaining gentle and attentive, just like when you first met and she served you tea with the innocent formality of a child playing house. She simply tilts her head with a smile.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You want a relationship where you'll never be abandoned again, but I'm not the right person for that.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I haven't told you my story yet, have I? It's complicated to explain, but I don't belong here.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I come from a place that's more brutal and unforgiving, where you can't befriend Mania creatures, where each day brings countless dangers and challenges. I'm familiar with the "birthplace" you created for me, because I did lie in a coffin for a very long time.
Graves hesitates, looking down at her own hand before uncertainly placing it in yours. Under the light, your elongated shadows finally connect.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I can't promise you that I'll never abandon you—that promise means too much to you for me to say it lightly. But there is one thing I might be able to help you with...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I can take on the suffering of the dark shadow for you, and suppress and eliminate the Mania inside you.

Graves furrows her brow slightly, confusion in her eyes, but before she can speak, you've already begun. A red light emanates from between your tightly clasped hands as the temperature rapidly rises, the glow seeping through the gaps between your fingers. You feel her trying to pull away, but you only grip her hand more firmly.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Let's call off the wedding. Dawn is breaking, and I might wake up and return to my own place soon.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I can't marry you. Please find someone who can truly make you happy.
[Dramatic music] [Screen shakes]

The malevolent force seeps out from where your hands meet, slowly but steadily detaching from her body and transferring into you through your joined palms. An overwhelming pressure crashes through you instantly, a suffocating force pressing against your mind, crushing your nerves and thoughts into chaos.
You clench your jaw tightly, feeling the force burning through your nerves. Your limbs begin to tremble, yet you refuse to let go of her hand.

speaker: Graves
content: You...

She watches helplessly as everything unfolds—watching the nightmares that have haunted her every moment slowly fade, while your knuckles turn white and your hand grows colder. Without thinking, she squeezes your hand, as if trying to share some of her warmth with you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm fine, truly. Only my consciousness is here anyway.
Despite your words, your voice has grown noticeably weaker. She tries to speak several times, but in the end, all she can manage is a strained, imperfect smile.

speaker: Graves
content: I know nothing about your Bureau or the outside world, but I do know...
She lifts her other hand and gently brushes her fingers across the space between your eyebrows.

speaker: Graves
content: You don't want to marry me. You never did, right from the beginning.

The shackles continue their absorption as chaotic, tormented thoughts clamor and invade your mind. Dizziness and exhaustion crash over you like waves, leaving your legs weak and unsteady. Just as you begin to falter, a firm, steady hand braces against your shoulder, holding you upright.
Graves leans against you, shoulder to shoulder, using your interlocked hands to steady you.

speaker: Graves
content: Weddings are meant to be joyous occasions, and a worthy bride should never be a burden to you... I'm not good enough. I'm not the perfect partner.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That's not true. You're wonderful, and neither you nor your castle have ever harmed me. When I return, I promise I'll find my way back to you. I'll come in my real body, and we can be friends...

speaker: Graves
content: It's all right. It's all right if you don't like me... Go back now, return to where you truly belong.

speaker: Graves
content: You've already given me what I truly wanted.
She gently rests her head on your shoulder.

speaker: Graves
content: You've already given me... your genuine sincerity.
[Silence]

The shackles have successfully transferred the shadows to you, and the prelude to the wedding march has begun to play. This is your cue, according to Luminita's plan, to make your entrance. But neither of you moves, you lean against the window, letting the notes of the wedding march fade away.

speaker: Graves
content: Before I let you go, would it be too much to ask for one final request?
She keeps her head down, refusing to look up at you.

speaker: Graves
content: Stay with me just a little longer, and recite the vows here together.
[Shoulder Rest CG]

speaker: Graves
content: Just repeat after me. Don't worry, this time there's nothing scary like "we shall never be apart"...

You remain side by side, her breath steady and warm against you. The gentle weight against your shoulder creates a comforting presence. Outside the castle, moonlight gradually yields to the first ray of sun, their warm and cool hues blending as they stream through the stained glass windows, bathing you both in dappled light.

speaker: Graves
content: .　　I swear...　　.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: .　　I swear...　　.

speaker: Graves
content: .　　...in life and in death...　　.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: .　　...in life and in death...　　.

speaker: Graves
content: .　　...in darkness and in light...　　.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: .　　...in darkness and in light...　　.

speaker: Graves
content: ...never to forget Graves.

Her veil falls gently, concealing her face and shrouding her expression. Silence envelops you, broken only by the soft movement of light. The air is filled with an ineffable tranquility and tenderness, tinged with a subtle, bittersweet sadness.

options: I will never forget you, Graves.

content: You repeat the words with solemn sincerity. The wedding march plays, its peaceful melody flowing with deep emotion, yet it seems to mark the end of this fleeting moment of happiness.

speaker: Graves
content: This is enough... It's all I need...
A smile remains on her face, as though suspended in this eternal moment, melting softly into the light.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Thank you, Graves, for sharing this special wedding with me. I promise I'll come back to find you.
[Startled Awake]
When you wake up, dawn is barely breaking over the Bureau. Faint light filters through the window into your room, bringing with it the subtle chill of early morning.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What's wrong, Hecate? You've got dark circles under your eyes.

speaker: Hecate
content: ...I'm glad you're alright. Adjutant Nightingale asked me to give this to you.

Hecate's tone remains calm as ever, but it's clear that she's been worried all night. You choose not to call her out on it, and don't bother to mention the new mass of Mania that's now inside you. Instead, you gently pat her head to reassure her and take the report from her hands.

Sure enough, while you were unconscious, the Bureau discovered the strange scent emanating from the picture book and began investigating Morveth Castle. However, the border satellite town has been abandoned for years and is in a remote location, so pinpointing its exact coordinates will take some time.
You'll find it—not just to resolve the Mania anomaly at the castle, but because you made her a promise... You open the book again, but your hand freezes mid-motion.
Did the story in the picture book... change the moment you opened it?

Thorns blanket black stones, a bride roams Morveth Castle—moonlight, ceremony, music begins. Mottled skin, a magic ring clutched tight, guests have departed, taking with them dreams and night. Yet no one sees what lies within, her dress sweeps the stone stairs, the bride has a secret that cannot be uncovered. You, who turn these pages—███, reaching for light and shadow, ignored the game of reality. The moon never sets, the ring remains—new abandonment, new solitude, new lonely shadow.

This is no hallucination... The symbols on the book twist before your eyes as the text gradually turns crimson, the red spreading and consuming every inch of white space. Then, without warning, flames leap from the page.

Fire consumes the page from its edges, following the paths of the text until the entire page is scorched black. At the center, the smudged text resists, untouched until the flames reach their final moment. As the flames finally recede, a single line of embers lingers, tracing the smudged words...
You, who turn these pages, ${PlayerName}.
It's your name.
(Flashback)

speaker: ${PlayerName} os
content: The coffin reminds me of the Romanesque Hall, the decor echoes the style of Sloane Street, and the ghost story brings to mind the Buonanotte Factory. An unfamiliar, enclosed space thick with Mania, an unstable Sinner with inexplicable fixation... It's practically tailor-made for me.

speaker: Graves
content: When the moon reached its zenith, I made a wish to the night sky, hoping I too would be granted a destined lover.

speaker: Luminita
content: Morveth Castle has the power to manifest longing into physical form—that's how No. 15 and Dullahan came into existence. But that power alone couldn't possibly target you so precisely, could it? Did you know our beautiful bride before all this?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I didn't know Graves, but I can't rule out the possibility that someone who knows us both arranged this "match."
[Exit flashback]

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Hecate, I need Labyrinth to access all of her memories about finding this picture book. Also, check with everyone at the Bureau to see if anyone has smelled a similar fragrance.
You pass the scrap of paper to Hecate, your name etched onto its scorched surface.
Whoever's hiding in the shadows watching this must be feeling quite pleased with themselves right now.

They sent you into this perfectly arranged wedding exploiting Graves's obsession, knowing you'd be lured toward the shadow festering within her... And as you willingly bore the contamination for Graves, they kept on nurturing the darkness growing within her. What a cruel, twisted scheme.
The Mania you consumed in your dream churns restlessly within your body... You have a terrible feeling that the worst is yet to come.
[Castle]

When the final vow was uttered, the figure in the gray coat vanished, yet the sky above Morveth Castle remained without dawn. Graves still sits by the window where you parted, her fingertips gently brushing the sill, feeling the warmth you left behind.

In her palm lies the ring, its pupil gem alternately contracting and dilating. With the ring as its center, Mania silently seeps out—the very power you should have completely eliminated now regenerating in Graves's palm.
Red markings spread across her skin, winding like serpentine veins and consuming her natural pallor.

speaker: Graves?
content: So this is my fate after all... Of course. How could anyone ever accept a monster like me?
[Flash to partially corrupted state] [Add horror sound effect]
[Castle]

speaker: Graves?
content: He's too good to me, always looking out for my feelings and playing along with my silly act. I don't deserve him.
female_content: She's too good to me, always looking out for my feelings and playing along with my silly act. I don't deserve her.

speaker: Graves?
content: I must have scared him with my face. I'm a monster. Friends, family, wedding...
female_content: I must have scared her with my face. I'm a monster. Friends, family, wedding...

speaker: Graves?
content: I was never meant to have any of those things anyway.

The guests in the hall have been waiting for the couple for a long time. No. 15, growing impatient, finally goes and checks on them. She finds only Graves standing there. It doesn't take long for her to figure out what happened. Graves is talking to herself again.

speaker: No. 15
content: It's alright, Graves! You'll find your true love someday!

speaker: Graves?
content: There won't be anyone else, there's only him... and he's already done too much for me.
female_content: There won't be anyone else, there's only her... and she's already done too much for me.

speaker: Graves?
content: I'm too greedy. I want things I have no right to ask for.

speaker: Graves?
content: Monsters belong in abandoned places like this.

speaker: Graves?
content: No. 15, Dullahan, we're all abandoned.

speaker: Graves?
content: He looked cold and indifferent when he left—because you didn't give him enough. Nowhere near enough.
female_content: She looked cold and indifferent when she left—because you didn't give her enough. Nowhere near enough.

content: Graves's breathing grows rapid as her nails dig into her palms. Dark crimson patterns emerge from her wrists, climbing up her arms like burn scars, gradually consuming her entire body.

speaker: No. 15
content: Graves? Are you alright? What are you talking about...

speaker: Graves?
content: I am her. I am the part of her she can never cut away.

speaker: Graves?
content: She couldn't keep her lover, but the promise from the deity of love remains. It's time to begin—a wedding just for you.

speaker: Graves
content: My own wedding...
[Bureau]

The Bureau staff has reviewed all surveillance footage but hasn't found the slightest trace of the picture book. It seemingly materialized out of nowhere, left its taunt for you, then vanished without a trace. Meanwhile, Nightingale has also failed to locate the Morveth Castle so far.

Your knowledge of the castle is limited to the fact that it's in a remote satellite town that fell into abandonment during the time of the great explosion and the Black Ring. Yet, with numerous similar locales scattered across the lands, locating it would be no different than searching for a needle in a haystack.

The notion that Morveth Castle existed solely within a dream has also crossed your mind. However, the burgeoning mass of Mania pulsating within you serves as a stark reminder: Graves remains lost, gripped by fear, ensnared in a new trap.
You try hard to recall details about Morveth Castle from your dream, but only one thing repeatedly surfaces in your mind—a mysterious sequence of numbers:

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Eugene, which do you think is easier: detaining an A-Class Sinner or locating an abandoned landmark?
[Castle]

speaker: Graves
content: That's right, I was born a monster! Born to be abandoned...
The unsettling notes of the discordant Wedding March reverberate sharply, while a storm of Mania relentlessly assaults the surroundings.
The ring floats beside Graves, insatiably draining her power. Endless waves of Mania transform into a spinning black vortex, expanding outward with Graves at its center.

speaker: Graves?
content: Never part? Together forever? A freak like me is cursed to be alone. This waiting, this torment... it never ends! Maybe it's just better to end it all!

At the storm's center, Graves has completely lost her original form—her body twisted into a grotesque shadow. Her dress is torn to shreds, thorn-like protrusions sprouting from her figure, slashing into the ground and walls with ruthless abandon.

The intense suction forces the chandelier to swing violently, emitting a jarring metallic screech. Pews are upturned, delicate floral ornaments are scattered, ancient plaster crumbles away in fragments from the ceiling, and fissures snake across the walls. The entire space succumbs to disorder, disintegrating bit by bit under the unstable force.
In the unbridled chaos and despair, No. 15 and Dullahan, as creations of Mania themselves, are drawn inexorably into the storm.

speaker: No. 15
content: Dullahan, are we going to disappear soon?

speaker: No. 15
content: But I haven't had the chance to teach that jerk a lesson yet. I haven't figured out what I really looked like. I haven't seen Graves find happiness in our place...

No. 15's frame rattles as its components begin to come loose, clanging in a frenzied cacophony. Bit by bit, parts break away, falling to the ground and morphing into irreparable debris. Meanwhile, Dullahan faces an equally dire fate—his armor rapidly rusts, the once vibrant flame atop his head flickering, threatening to die out at any instant.

speaker: Dullahan
content: We should've been gone long ago... We are but hallow vessels of longings, unable to replace true love or truly understand it. To linger here, to exist as we do—it has been an indulgence.

speaker: Dullahan
content: If only I could see their faces one last time... My wife, my child—they were my pride, my joy. If fate hadn't demanded my sacrifice on that battlefield... I would have shielded you, cherished you, until my last breath...
Graves can no longer hear any of their words. The Mania surges within her, showing no signs of subsiding. The twisted dark mist is slowly dragging her former friends toward the abyss.

No. 15's eyelids weigh down heavily, her gaze faltering. As her awareness drifts into the void, she grasps onto Dullahan's corroded sword hilt in a desperate attempt to keep herself from being scattered to the winds.
Dullahan calls out his wife's name from his memories, struggling to keep his last flicker of flame alive, only for it to be snuffed out by Graves's power.
Just as the storm is about to completely devour them—

speaker: Familiar Figure
content: Hey, buddy, now's not the time to give up!

speaker: Familiar Figure
content: Besides, those words only mean something if you tell them to your wife in person!

speaker: Another Familiar Figure
content: Graves is just manipulated by that ring right now. Now that we know the root cause, there must be a way to save her.

speaker: Another Familiar Figure
content: No. 15! Hang in there!

Thorns of crimson light rain down from above, violently slicing open the Mania barrier. The churning dark mist twists and dissolves in the radiance, revealing a breach torn open in the once-inescapable storm.
No. 15 opens her eyes and raises her head in disbelief, looking at you, who vanished and now return, too stunned to speak.
Hello there—though you don't look so great. This isn't the time for pleasantries. Let's find somewhere to take cover.
Long time—though I guess it hasn't been that long. This isn't the time for pleasantries. Let's find somewhere to take cover.
With all your might, the two of you finally manage to pull No. 15 and Dullahan out of the Mania vortex, retreating to a corner barely shielded from the corruption.

speaker: Luminita
content: I thought you wanted a property tour! You tricked me!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If I'd told you this place was falling apart, you probably wouldn't have taken me back here, right? I guess I should thank your property hotline for being accessible 24/7.

With no wedding festivities to crash, Luminita had left the castle shortly after you woke up. But her professional dedication got the better of her, and one phone call was all it took to lure her back. Now she leans against the wall, still shaken and breathing heavily.

speaker: Luminita
content: That thing's power is way too overwhelming—getting close is basically suicide! And I can't believe such a fine property is about to get destroyed too!
While the castle is hardly the priority right now, you don't have the energy to point out her misplaced concerns.

options: We need to distract Graves first.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Graves's attention is completely fixated on that damn ring. Using the shackles now would only agitate her more. We need to find a way to get her attention before there's any chance of talking to her.

speaker: Luminita
content: But how do we do it? She looks completely out of touch with reality. Unless...

Luminita hugs herself in disbelief and steals a glance in your direction before summoning her resolve. With a determined expression, she sheds her coat, preparing to dash forward and unleash a flurry of dance moves.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Even if you were a breakdancing champ, it wouldn't help. I was talking about using the journal from the study.

speaker: Luminita
content: Eleven

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That's not what I mean... Graves doesn't want anyone to learn about her childhood.
The secrets of a little monster... things she wants to keep buried forever...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Luminita, I'm leaving No. 15 and Dullahan in your hands. I'll be right back.

The storm in the ceremony hall is growing more violent by the second, with fierce winds tearing through the entire castle, shredding everything into fractured light and swirling dust. You struggle toward the stairway, each step made on the edge of collapse, the path beneath your feet nearly vanishing in the windswept debris.

Rocks, debris, and unidentifiable objects hurtle chaotically through the storm, howling past your head and crashing everywhere. A sudden piercing sound comes dangerously close to the back of your head. You instinctively dodge to the side—and a split second later, the remains of a chandelier crash down, shattering into countless pieces at your feet.
You have no time to dwell on your close call. A single thought occupies your mind—you must reach the study and find that journal as quickly as possible.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Must move faster...

Gritting your teeth with determination, you clamber over a collapsed stone pillar and barely regain your footing when another violent gust of wind hurls a splintered wooden beam directly at you. You instantly drop into a low slide, your body skimming across the floor for several feet, narrowly avoiding the deadly fragment.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Almost there...
The study door is right ahead. You lunge forward and push it open, plant both feet against the wall to redirect your momentum, and roll smoothly into the room—
As you enter, you reach back to slam the door shut and lock it, temporarily sealing the storm outside.
Seeing the warm glow of light illuminating the walls and desk, you finally let out a breath of relief. Thankfully, this room remains completely intact, untouched by the storm's assault.

That series of death-defying maneuvers has completely drained your strength, but there's little time to recover. After a brief moment to catch your breath, you grasp a bookshelf for support and shakily rise to your feet, beginning your search for the journal that Graves took away.
Finally, in the corner of a toppled bookshelf, you spot the familiar black cover.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Phew... Thank goodness it's still here...
The journal remains open to the last page you were reading:
November 2, N.F. 89, Abandoned infant: unnamed Procurement list: milk powder, diapers, blankets...
After confirming it's the right journal, you swiftly grab it, but just as you're ready to tuck it away into your coat pocket, the entire study lurches violently.
Boom—!!

As a deafening boom rends the air, the storm breaches the sanctuary with ferocious intensity. Frenzied gusts hurl a barrage of debris into the room, causing the floor to convulse violently. Cracks race across the walls, picture frames shatter to the ground, and bookshelves emit shrill. In the next moment—
The weighty bookshelf comes crashing down directly toward you!
[Ceremony Hall]

speaker: Luminita
content: For the love of heaven, please let this old architecture hold together!
Lumi shields the two monsters as they huddle in a corner.

speaker: Luminita
content: Please be okay, my valued client! Don't tell me you left just to skip out on my commission fee! Come on, you wouldn't want to lose both the property and your dear agent—
[Attic]

The study now lies in ruins, reduced to nothing but collapsed rubble. Shattered wooden beams litter the floor, heavy bookshelves lay toppled in chaotic heaps, and fallen candelabras rest among the debris, their flames utterly extinguished.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Cough, cough...

Behind the collapsed bookshelves, the rubble shifts slightly as you struggle to push aside splintered wood and slowly rise from the debris. While your body is covered in scrapes, it's the years-old dust you've accidentally inhaled that truly makes you miserable.
You wave away the floating dust clouds, finally able to see what lies before you. Behind the study walls, hidden away and completely isolated from the outside world, is a small attic...

The cramped, confining space has a ceiling too low to stand upright, with floorboards creaking with each step as if they might give way at any moment. The walls are cobbled together from rough wooden planks, riddled with cracks and wormholes.

A shelf against the wall holds a few modest possessions: an oil lamp, a clay bowl, and a small box containing dried flower petals and ribbons. In the corner lies a small pile of fairy tale books, beside them sits a low stool, clearly cut down to accommodate the height of its user.

Nearby, a single bed, smaller than the standard size, stands strewn with patched-up old dresses, worn cloaks, and a threadbare blanket. In the dim glow of moonlight, several faded crayon drawings on the walls come into view.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Oh right, the journal.

With no time to dwell on this attic, your true purpose springs back to your mind. Amidst the chaos of the collapse, you lost hold of the journal, but luck is on your side—it lies nearby, its yellowed pages spread open to a new page yet to be read.

You pick up the journal, your gaze sweeping across the drawings on the wall... Finally, you understand why Graves didn't want you to see any of this. Childish handwriting accompanies each faded drawing on the wall, and together they tell a complete story about a "little monster."
[Enter Small CG 1 Flashback]
I was abandoned here.

I don't remember the rain that day. All I know is a scene roughly pieced together from what Sister Elsie told me—on a night with no cradle or hugs, a little monster was left all alone on cold stone steps, forgotten in the wind and rain.
Sister Elsie told me that the night was bitterly cold, where the sound of rain falling on the vines outside echoed like weeping.

speaker: Nun
content: But you didn't cry.
That's what she said.

speaker: Nun
content: You didn't make even the slightest whimper. Frighteningly quiet, as if you somehow knew no one would ever come.
Later, I asked her, "Who left me here?"
She just shook her head and said she didn't know.
Then why did they leave me here? I asked again.

speaker: Nun
content: ...Because you are a <color=#fb9259>special</color> child.
What does "special" mean? I don't understand.
Maybe it means I did something wrong, and now I have to do lots and lots of good things to make up for it. Only then would someone come to take me home.
But now I have a new question: What is "home"?
[End of Flashback]

The Mania storm draws closer, with surging dark mist seeping through the cracks, a foreboding sign urging you to leave. You pick up the journal and turn away, but the childish handwriting chronicling the past has already etched itself into your memory, its silent confessions echoing within you.
[Enter Small CG 2 Flashback]
I made my first rag doll. Just as Sister Elsie had named me, I gave her a name too.

speaker: Graves
content: I'll call you "Little Graves."
I made her body from the old hall curtains that had just been replaced, carved her hands and feet from kitchen spoons, and drew big eyes and rosy lips on her face.
That day was also the first time I got brave enough to step outside the castle.

speaker: Child
content: Monster! Monster! Get lost!

speaker: Child
content: We hate you! Stay away from us!

speaker: Child
content: You look disgusting! Freak!
I don't think they like my Little Graves.
But what does "monster" mean? I learn things really slowly. The only word I've learned lately is "friend."
I wanted to be friends with them, but they knocked my doll to the ground. Someone even stepped on her. I heard the wood crack and the fabric rip.
Little Graves was broken.
My hands are too clumsy—that must be why. My doll wasn't pretty enough. Next time, I'll try harder to make her look nicer.
[End of Flashback] [Intense tremor in the hallway]

Returning to the hallway with the journal clutched in hand, you find that the once sinister space has shed its eerie facade. The monsters, who were rehearsing wedding speeches, have vanished along with the disorienting maze that ensnared you.

The shattered hallway no longer blocks your way. A clear, straight path has emerged amidst the collapsed ruins. The remaining stone tiles, toppled pillars, and shattered window frames all seem to align, wordlessly guiding you in one direction—toward the ceremony hall, where Graves now awaits.
[Enter Small CG 3 Flashback]
So that's why Sister Elsie wouldn't let me near the hall—because they held something called a "wedding" there.

speaker: Groom
content: I vow to stand by your side, in life and in death, in darkness and in light, and never to part from you...
So people can be brave... they can stand close to each other without running away... they can hold hands tight and promise for sure—"never to part from you."
Watching them exchange rings, receive blessings, and hug tightly while everyone clapped and cheered... my heart was beating so fast.
The bride's dress was so pretty. Everyone gave her their blessings.
Wedding—I've learned this word now. It sounds happier and like it lasts longer than "friend" or "home."
[End of Flashback]
Luminita crouches behind the last pillar still standing. Beside her, No. 15 and Dullahan lie unconscious.

Talismans, copper coins, peach wood swords, crucifixes, holy water, parchment scrolls... her bag lies completely empty now. As the bride, clad in a dress weaved by resentment, draws near alongside the tempestuous storm, Luminita can only offer prayers to every deity she knows, hoping that someone returns quickly.
[Flashback]
That was my first wedding dress. Even though it was made from rags, I thought it was the prettiest dress in the whole world.
I walked out wearing it. I was sure they'd think I looked pretty, that they'd like me just like everyone likes a bride.
But they just laughed... They threw stones at me. The dress got caught and torn by the stones.
I looked down at my dress, now dirty and torn, and thought about my broken doll.

speaker: Graves?
content: I'm a monster! No one will ever like me!

speaker: Graves
content: Don't say that! Someone will. I will have my own wedding someday!
I started arguing with my other self. After that, we argued a lot.
[End of Flashback]

Graves, consumed completely by her negative persona, now wears an eerie smile on her face. Arms outstretched in a twisted embrace of the darkness, she moves with an unsettling grace. Alone, she glides through the debris, twirling and bowing, head inclined and wrists raised as if in a macabre dance with an unseen companion.

The battered hallway becomes her ballroom, the storm her symphony. Deathly silence envelops the surroundings, with only her dress billowing in the breath of Mania as she performs her solitary, unanswered waltz.
[Flashback]

speaker: Graves
content: Look what I found!

speaker: Graves?
content: A ring?
The ring is so pretty, but my hands... they're red and rough, with long nails like claws.
An ugly monster doesn't deserve happiness. Only if you're pretty enough will someone say, "I vow to never part with you, in life and in death."

speaker: Graves
content: Help me. We can have happiness right away.
This ring is magic. It helped me hide my other self. I also used it to hide this room.
This way I won't be "special" anymore.
I think maybe this time will be different. Maybe... I can finally be a happy bride, just like in the stories.
[End of Flashback]

The turmoil in the hall is growing more violent by the second. The Mania storm, on the brink of reaching its crescendo, threatens to escalate into a catastrophic event. Watching with mounting panic as the hall's entrance gradually becomes buried, Luminita grits her teeth and mutters:

speaker: Luminita
content: Damn it... I'll be done for if I keep waiting—
She takes a deep breath, readying herself to charge recklessly into the whirling vortex, when a tremendous crash sounds from behind her...
You breach through the wall, the red glow from your shackles piercing the swirling dust. In your hand, you clutch tightly to the journal you retrieved from the attic.

speaker: Luminita
content: Where have you been?! This place is about to get demolished!
Despite her grievances, Luminita has not left the two Mania creatures behind, choosing instead to remain with them amidst the chaos. You offer her a comforting pat on the shoulder.

options: I'll come to you for a house purchase later.

content: Without another word, you brush past Luminita with determined steps, your gaze locked on Graves at the center of the vortex. Violent winds tear at your clothes as the storm surges around you, but you push forward and leap into the maelstrom without hesitation.

speaker: Luminita
content: Hey!
Luminita cries out in shock, but your figure has already vanished completely into the depths of the storm.

The ring incites and spreads Graves's darkest powers, while highly concentrated Mania howls and shrieks, resisting your approach. Flowing corruption rages past you, broken debris and sharp fragments grazing your shoulders and limbs. Yet, they fail to stop you.

Within the vortex's depths, Graves's once graceful dance has careened into chaos. Her head droops, body swaying erratically, lips moving slightly as she murmurs indecipherable words—a marionette devoid of its soul, lost to a sinister force.
Trapped in a haze, her mind struggles to grasp the sounds of the outside world. Then abruptly, a pair of hands emerges from the chaos, encircling her waist in a firm grip.
In that moment, her movements freeze. In her daze, a long-forgotten warmth touches her, as though something is pulling her back from the depths of the abyss.
You raise your hand, waving the journal you fought so desperately to recover in front of her unfocused eyes.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm sorry, I accidentally ended up seeing your childhood diary and the room where you grew up.
Graves tilts her head vacantly, her gaze slowly settling on the journal.
Beneath her red skin, her features tighten slightly, confusion and bewilderment intertwined. She glances at the journal, then fixes her gaze on you.

speaker: Graves
content: I thought you already left. What are you doing back here?
She interrogates you in a hushed tone, both her face and tone devoid of any emotion you can detect.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I told you I would find the real Morveth Castle after I woke up and come see you in a more complete form. See? I've kept my word.

speaker: Graves
content: Liar... You were clearly going back to your own place, back to somewhere without freaks. You just left me behind, because I'm a monster...
Her words are whispered as if constructing an impenetrable wall, each syllable a brick to shut you out.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're different. You've convinced yourself that you don't deserve any lasting connection. So you've accepted abandonment as your fate? So you're going to destroy everything now?
Graves offers no rebuttal, only pushing you away forcefully. Despite her resistance, you hold onto her even more firmly.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Actually, I'm a monster too.

speaker: Graves
content: You?

options: Yeah, I'm Devil in the Gray Coat.
I'm the Chief whose very name strikes terror into hearts.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You see, I have dreams no one else can understand, I'm not scared in the slightest when I see you in this way, I can summon light spikes from my hands, and I can even rush into a storm like this to dance with you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Aren't I quite different from what you consider "normal people"?

speaker: Graves
content: But... But...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And look over there at that real estate agent, Luminita. Would you call her normal?
You point quickly, deliberately giving her no time to think.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: She throws herself into every bit of drama, treats exorcisms like she's hawking bootleg DVDs, and not only isn't scared of phantoms—she actually haggles with them. By your standards, would she count as a monster?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If being "special" makes someone a monster, then everyone in this world is a monster.

speaker: Graves
content: So what? People will still fear me and walk away because I'm different from them.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That's only because they refuse to admit they're monsters too. They're just as lonely and restless as you are, so they huddle together to attack a common target. It makes them feel like they're part of the "majority."

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Those children who threw stones at you were monsters too—they were just bigger cowards than you, too scared to confront their own specialness.

While your voice retains its composure, Graves becomes so bewildered by your words that she even forgets to keep dancing, her movements faltering as she clumsily stumbles on her own feet multiple times.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Everyone is special. You're just more visibly special than others, that's all. This isn't your fault, nor should it be the measure of whether you deserve to be loved.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Why must monsters only be with humans? Monsters can be with other monsters, monsters can be with anything. Just look at No. 15 and Dullahan—no matter what they've become, people still visit the castle to express their longings and honor their memory.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Love gained by conforming to everyone's beauty standards isn't necessarily genuine. True love and companionship always surpass all rules and constraints.
Graves presses her lips together and lowers her head in silence, seemingly struggling to process your words.
You hold her tighter, steadying her swaying form to prevent her from losing her balance again.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I may have come on too strong with my points. But I remember you saying, "Graves's story isn't a good one,"—and that's even more unreasonable than what I've said.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It's clearly a good story.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Abandoned but still searching for companions; hurt but still yearning for beauty and goodness. A Graves who tries this hard deserves it all. She shouldn't have to change herself for anyone.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I know that no matter how many dark thoughts that damn ring has forced into her mind, the real "her" is still in there. That brave, strong Graves who never gave up on herself has been there all along. Let's bring her back out, alright?
Her shoulders tremble slightly as her gaze visibly softens. You notice the red hue of her skin beginning to fade, while the crimson patterns across her body lose their ominous depth.

speaker: Graves
content: If that's true... why did you turn me down?

options: I'm not ready for marriage yet...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Who jumps straight to marriage like that? You need to spend time together first and let your feelings grow naturally, don't you think? Don't worry, there's plenty of time ahead for us.

speaker: Graves
content: Isn't marriage just about happily living together? What do you mean by "plenty of time ahead"?
Furrowing her brow, her eyes are clouded with confusion, like a child bewildered by the rules of the adult world.
You shake your head in resignation, letting out a soft sigh before reaching out to take her hand in yours.
[CG] [Battle Music]
You guide her to raise both hands, your fingers intertwining with hers. The shackles gradually draw together as light manifests in your palms, pulsing gently with the pressure of your grip.

Twirling and intertwining, your steps align in flawless harmony. The light spikes of the shackles slice through the lingering veil of darkness, while swirling dust scatters beneath your feet. The fractured floor silently bears witness to the cadence of your advance.

The crimson glow of the shackles courses over your palms, extending with each dance step, weakening the ring's power with every twirl. Cracks materialize as the gem's once vibrant sheen dulls, the malevolent aura slowly receding. But it's not quite enough yet.
To completely destroy this core that has been feeding off Graves, you'll need her own power as well.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Graves, do you know what true vows are really meant to be?

speaker: Graves
content: I vow to...
Having recited the wedding vows countless times in the past, those familiar words instinctively cascade from Graves's lips, only to be interrupted by you this time.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Forget those "in life and in death" clichés. Let me teach you some new stuff.
Meeting Graves's bewildered gaze, you guide her to take a graceful step to the left.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I vow, whether I am monster or human, to embrace myself fully.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: My imperfections are not sins, but medals of my own.
Her movements remain hesitant, her steps carrying a habitual stiffness, as if she's forgotten how to follow another's lead.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I vow, regardless of the world's perception, to never allow their judgments to dictate my path.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I exist, and that alone is enough.
You grasp her waist firmly, guiding her as you turn, feeling the delicate fabric of her dress softly brushing against your ankles. Observing closely, you discern a newfound assurance in her steps.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I vow, regardless of what I am, special or ordinary, to believe in my deserving of happiness.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Rules are nothing but hollow constraints. True love never shuns due to any "imperfection."
Your voice grows more firm. The black markings begin to peel away from her wrist like ashes scattered by the wind, while the cracks in the ring continue to deepen.

options: And finally, also most importantly, the fourth vow...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I vow, no matter how rough or fearful circumstances may become, to never abandon myself.

With your final words echoing in the air, her movements freeze completely for a moment. The crimson markings gradually fade from her fingertips, the presence of Mania still churning violently but no longer tethered to her being.

She gazes at you, with confusion, respect... and perhaps even admiration flickering in her eyes. Perplexed by how you have managed it—why your words have effortlessly shattered her reality—she finds herself captivated, unable to tear her gaze away.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That's it for our first dance. I'm not really sure what follows in the ceremony. Would you lead me through it?
Your voice softens as you lock eyes with her. In this moment, you discern the once impenetrable shell encasing her starting to break, allowing a more genuine emotion to reshape within.

speaker: Graves
content: I vow, no matter how difficult or fearful circumstances may become, to never abandon myself.
She lifts her hand with a deliberate slowness, placing it gently upon your shoulder. Stepping closer, she guides you into a waltz.

The hall remains in ruins, its dome still covered with cracks, but in this moment, her dress billows and your clothing flutters as your dance steps grow lighter. Together, you move toward the sinister ring, allowing it to bear witness to the final ending.

The blue light at its eye struggles like a fading pulse, desperately mustering one last resistance. However, the Mania, devoid of a host to latch onto, finds no refuge. Cracks extend ceaselessly through every facet of the gem's structure, and the ring can no longer maintain its existence.

At long last, it emits a brittle crack and crumbles into fine dust, dissolving in your palm. Fragments hover in the air as the fading shimmer, now without anchor, flickers briefly before transforming into weightless particles to be swept away by the wind, dispersing into the silent night.

Simultaneously, the storm's roar abruptly ceases. The dark mist of Mania recedes rapidly like an ebbing tide, the heavy oppression suddenly lifting, leaving only residual ripples flowing gently through the air.
The world finally returns to silence.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It's finally over.

speaker: Graves
content: The ring... is it really gone?
You nod, speaking in a cheerful tone.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Yes, and now it's your turn—the complete you—to take control of your own destiny and future.

Fallen stone pillars lay silently strewn across the hall, walls adorned with sprawling cracks, shattered glass scattered on the floor. Blood-stained silk sways gently in the breeze before settling back into the profound stillness.
On the horizon, clouds glow with the first faint light of dawn. The night at Morveth Castle is coming to an end.

speaker: No. 15
content: Thank goodness! You're alright, Graves!
No. 15 races toward you both, wrapping Graves in a tight embrace, her eyes brimming with tears.
Nearby, Dullahan clears his throat as if trying to hide his emotions, but the dancing flame betrays his true feelings.

speaker: Dullahan
content: Well, I never would have thought we'd finally witness a wedding miracle.
Luminita saunters over at her own leisurely pace, her agent instincts in full swing as she surveys the surroundings, wincing slightly at the extent of the damage.

speaker: Luminita
content: This place is a total wreck, not a single floorboard spared... Well, at least the crisis is all sorted out. Renovations can always be done later...

You look up at Graves. The contamination hasn't fully receded from her body—crimson patterns still intertwine with her normal skin. Yet she makes no attempt to hide it, nor does she avoid your gaze. She simply stands there in silence, visibly flustered about what to do now that she sees the castle in ruins.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It's all that damn ring's fault. Once we get back to the Bureau, I'll ask you more about it...

speaker: Luminita
content: Hold your horses!
Before you can finish your sentence, Luminita cuts you off.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...What's the matter?

speaker: Luminita
content: I get that you're excited to take your bride home, but hang tight just a moment.
Faced with four puzzled stares converging on her, Luminita responds with a sly wink. She presses her palms together and flashes you an ingratiating smile.

speaker: Luminita
content: Before you dash off, would you be so kind as to do me one tiny little favor, oh esteemed Chief?

Several days later, sunlight streams through the castle's stained glass windows into the hall, casting warm, kaleidoscopic patterns across the interior. The Mania storm that once raged here has faded into history, and the castle now embraces a new chapter—

The debris and rubble have been cleared away, though the chandeliers remain damaged, the floors uneven, and cracks in the walls only partially repaired. Yet these imperfections now add a distinctive charm to the place.
Luminita, dressed in formal business attire with a speaker clipped to her waist, stands surrounded by tourists as she delivers her presentation with boundless enthusiasm:

speaker: Luminita
content: Welcome to Morveth Castle, the premier wedding destination! This place not only carries a century of matrimonial history, but also conceals... mysterious legends of marriages with the departed!
A ripple of gasps spreads through the crowd—exactly the reaction Luminita was hoping for. She nods with satisfaction and continues in a deliberately hushed, mysterious tone.

speaker: Luminita
content: It was in this very hall that brides and grooms pledged their vows of eternal fidelity. Yet, their stories often lacked proper endings... Perhaps some love stories don't end in the realm of the living, but continue beyond the grave.
A young girl curiously raises her hand.

speaker: Girl
content: I read online that if you make a wish here, you can see your deceased lover and reconnect with them. Is that true?

speaker: Luminita
content: Of course!
Luminita puts on her professional smile.

speaker: Luminita
content: True love can break all rules and the boundary between life and death. As long as your bond lingers unresolved, the castle holds the key to closure...
After sharing a few more stories and going over some guidelines, Luminita glances at the watch on her wrist and claps her hands.

speaker: Luminita
content: Alright everyone! It's now free exploration time. Feel free to look around the hall, then meet back here with me in 20 minutes for our next activity!
The tourists disperse throughout the hall, filling the space with a chorus of conversations, laughter, and the clicking of camera shutters.
Two daring young men are teasing each other in front of a deteriorating mural.

speaker: Young Man A
content: Hey, you're always going on about how brave you are. So what do you say, dare to stay the night here?

speaker: Young Man B
content: Why sweat it? You wanna make a bet?

speaker: Luminita
content: Ahem, excuse me.
Luminita steps into the conversation at just the right moment.

speaker: Luminita
content: Just a friendly reminder: Your tickets are for the half-day tour only, so unfortunately, extended stays aren't included. If you're keen on an overnight experience, that's an additional fee—though I could throw in a little discount for you both...
Just as Luminita is busy pitching them discounted packages, a little boy approaches and timidly tugs at the hem of her coat.

speaker: Boy
content: Miss Tour Guide, are there monsters in here?

speaker: Luminita
content: Monsters? Hehe, perhaps. They might even be right behind us as we speak. And by the way, I'm a real estate agent, not a tour guide, little one!

speaker: Boy
content: Ah...
The visibly frightened boy flinches, but Luminita gently pats his head with a reassuring smile.

speaker: Luminita
content: But hey, no need to be spooked! Who says monsters always have to be scary villains? You know what? Some monsters even stumble over their words while rehearsing wedding speeches.
As she speaks, she casts a smiling glance toward a corner of the hall.

In the shadows beyond the visitors' sight, No. 15 cautiously peers out, her gaze fixed on a figure in the crowd who seems both familiar and strange—the boy who once visited the castle to make wishes, now fully grown into a man. He stands quietly at the back of the group, appearing to search for something.
No. 15 hesitates for a moment, but ultimately summons the courage to step forward.

speaker: No. 15
content: ...You're here.
The man whips around, his eyes instantly lighting up.

speaker: Young Man
content: You... you're really still here!

speaker: No. 15
content: Stop coming here to make wishes! Every time you describe me differently—just look what I've become!

speaker: Young Man
content: If I stop making wishes, I'm worried you might vanish without their power keeping you here!

speaker: Young Man
content: I was so young when we first met. I honestly can't remember what you originally looked like...

speaker: No. 15
content: ...I like how I am now. Just remember me as I am today.

They gaze at each other with the most sincere and tender looks. There's still so much left unsaid between them—misunderstandings to resolve, years of longing to express, and countless other things to share.
Meanwhile, Dullahan stands silently in the shadows, his gaze fixed on a mother and son.
They stand at the opposite end of the hall—the energetic little boy bouncing ahead while the young woman holds his hand, her gentle, loving gaze never leaving her child.

speaker: Boy
content: Mom, don't be scared! If any monsters or ghosts really show up, I'll chase them all away! I'm a real man now, and from now on, I'll be the one protecting you!

speaker: Woman
content: Haha, my little hero is so brave.

speaker: Boy
content: Hehe, soon I'll be just as awesome as Dad!

speaker: Boy
content: Dad will be proud of me, right?
Dullahan doesn't approach to disturb them, murmuring softly to himself.

speaker: Dullahan
content: Of course. You have always been my pride, both of you.
Even when separated by life and death, divided between the realms of light and shadow, their stories are never forgotten—they live on eternally in the memories of those who love them.
From another corner of the hall, you and Graves hide in the shadows, silently watching everything unfold.

Graves meticulously adjusts the hem of her dress, yet her curious eyes can't help but dart occasionally toward the bustling scene outside. You notice her unease. Morveth Castle hasn't been this lively in ages, that much is certain.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Don't worry, they're just tourists here for sightseeing. The Bureau has evaluated the M-value and Mania entities in this area and determined they won't be affected.

speaker: Graves
content: Sightseeing?
You nod and begin to explain patiently.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The area around Morveth Castle has been deserted for years, and I doubt anyone will visit this place for a while. Luminita suggested turning it into a paranormal romance-themed tourist spot, but that's really not very practical.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But... if this attraction opens just once, giving closure to some unfulfilled wishes, I suppose there's no harm in letting our agent friend earn some ticket money this one time.
Graves nods, her expression still tinged with a hint of confusion and reluctance.

speaker: Graves
content: Alright... but I still think Sister Elsie would be a little disappointed if people stopped coming here to get married.
You can't help but smile at her grimace.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Relax, everything takes time and happens step by step. At least right now your wedding sanctuary is bustling with life again, isn't it?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: As for what comes after, we can figure that out later—how to revitalize the nearby satellite town, how to manage the lingering creatures in the castle—we can take our time planning it all. After all, there's plenty of time ahead for us.

There's plenty of time ahead—truly a phrase brimming with hope and vitality. It implies endless possibilities and opportunities for change, promising a brighter tomorrow, one always worth looking forward to and chasing after.

speaker: Graves
content: Yeah, there's plenty of time ahead for us.
This time, Graves embraces the idea with remarkable ease. Her smile is unburdened, her expression more radiant and vibrant than you have ever seen before.

speaker: Luminita
content: Time's up, everyone! Please gather around now. We're about to move on to the next part of our tour!

speaker: Luminita
content: As the very first visitors to Morveth Castle, we've prepared something extra special for you—
Amidst Luminita's announcement and the murmuring of guests, you and Graves, both formally dressed for the occasion, walk hand-in-hand into the center of the hall.
Luminita clears her throat and continues with a smile.

speaker: Luminita
content: Today, we gather to witness the first covenant being forged in the newly restored Morveth Castle.

speaker: Luminita
content: However, please note that this is not your typical wedding ceremony, but a covenant founded on freedom, understanding, respect, and coexistence.
The visitors fall silent, all eyes fixed on you both, curious or expectant.

In a corner not far away, No. 15, Dullahan, and the castle's other monsters huddle against the wall. They have promised the Bureau not to disturb the visitors, so they can only crane their necks, watching from afar as the little girl who has kept them company every night takes step after step forward.
The once-lonely "little monster" has finally found someone worthy of her trust and a place where she truly belongs.
You stand firmly in the center of the hall and raise the champagne bottle.
It endures the darkness of night and absorbs the sunlight.
Bang!!
Everyone in the hall turns toward the source of the sound—

In full view of everyone, one of the monsters guiltily tries to hide half of a candelabra base behind its back. However, the pieces and metal fragments still falling from the wall beside it completely betray its "crime."

Most likely, it was watching the ceremony with such nervous excitement that it unconsciously gripped a "handle" too forcefully, accidentally wrenching the wall-mounted decorative candelabra right off.
A mass of glowing eyes in the darkness face the visitors frozen in shock. The two groups stare at each other, unanimously sinking into an eerie silence.
The monsters finally snap out of their daze, frantically scrambling to retreat into the darkness or vanish from sight, but it is clearly too late...

speaker: Young Man A
content: Ghosts! Aaaahhhh—

speaker: Young Man B
content: Spiders! So many of them... and they're huge... Aaaahhhh—

speaker: Girl
content: Aaarrrgh! That statue is moving! It's walking toward us!

speaker: Young Man A
content: Run! Run!! The monsters are coming to eat us! Ahhhhh!!!
The crowd erupts in chaos, unleashing a massive wave of screams and cries so deafening it seems the castle roof might blow off at any moment.
Amid the chaotic stampede, a flustered Luminita darts back and forth, grabbing one visitor and blocking another, her shoes practically striking sparks against the floor.

speaker: Luminita
content: Everyone, please calm down! Don't rush off! Our tour isn't over yet!

speaker: Luminita
content: I swear on my professional reputation that these are just special effects! You have to believe me—
But under these circumstances, such a forced explanation appears utterly unconvincing. Not a single visitor buys it, all of them shaking off her hands as they continue screaming and fleeing in panic.
You're about to direct the nearby guards to handle this chaos when, as if perfectly timed to make matters worse, your terminal starts ringing urgently in your pocket.
The moment you answer, a cacophony of overlapping voices immediately floods from the speaker.

speaker: Hecate
content: Chief, I heard you went to get married. What is that? Is it dangerous?

speaker: EMP
content: Seriously?! You got married without inviting us? That's outrageous!

speaker: Labyrinth
content: Master, Labyrinth anticipates partaking in your marry-making. Powerfrugal Maid III does not require sustenance.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Wait, this is a misunderstanding...
In the midst of your flustered attempt to explain, your eyes instinctively dart toward Graves, who stands beside you.
She stands there with her head lowered, shoulders slightly trembling, lips pressed tightly together.
She's trying hard not to laugh.

Chaos still reigns all around—tourists cowering fearfully in corners, monsters clumsily cleaning up their "evidence," and the barrage of questions still coming through your terminal—but in this moment, she seems to exist in her own dimension of serenity separate from the whole world.

In the distance, sunlight streams through the broken stained glass windows into the hall, falling upon Graves's gently shaking shoulders, as well as the weathered pews, tarnished candelabras, and dust-covered stone tiles, tracing their irregular outlines as if in a dream.
From a crack in the wall, a small, unidentified flower has pushed through unexpectedly, swaying gently in the light.
You see Graves lift her face slightly.

speaker: Graves
content: Perhaps, this really is a good story.
A window, sealed shut for many years, is quietly opened to welcome the first gentle spring breeze after countless lonely seasons.
[ED]
(Scene change)

Somewhere far away, a woman gazes toward Morveth Castle with keen interest. She raises her hand, observing as a wound slowly forms on her ring finger, circling all the way around. Blood seeps out and trickles down along her veins.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
content: ...I would've been fine with it not returned, but why did you have to destroy it? It's not like I lost the ring on purpose.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
content: I'll find you later for compensation.
With a slight pressure from her fingertips, her blood congeals and changes color, transforming into a new ring. The woman chuckles softly before turning and vanishing into the shadows.
(Scene change)
The lights in the Chief's office remain bright, with several investigation reports on Morveth Castle spread across the spacious desk.

What can be confirmed thus far is that Graves has no knowledge of the picture book's or the ring's origins. She simply obtained the ring by chance, which offered the promise of a lover. As for why you were chosen to be her "true love," the latest investigation report hints at a direction:
Within the strangely fragrant ashes of the picture book, you have found a trace of <color=#fb9259>the Underground sorcery</color>.
You gently close the report.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I will find you.
To the MBCC Chief, or whoever gets this:
HURRY! PLEASE! SAVE HER!! Only you can save her. Please, I'm begging you!

speaker: Host
content: Not all men are born equal.

speaker: Host
content: Only the wise amass wealth, only the noble wield power. And only the most distinguished members of our inner circle are worthy of invitation here.

speaker: Host
content: Deep in the high seas, hidden by the white sands, lies the ultimate resort, a haven of absolute safety, purity, and freedom.

speaker: Host
content: Yes, <color=#fb9259>freedom</color>. The kind of true liberty the noble deserves. No prying eyes, no restraints, no taboos, no burdens. Come to indulge, or to trade. The choice is yours.

speaker: Host
content: When morality and law become nothing but cudgels abused by the common man, when beauty and passion are dulled by mediocrity... only this place remains a true paradise, where you'll rediscover life's most sumptuous, most fervent pleasures...

speaker: Host
content: Including perfect love.
[CG - Solo Opening Performance]
On stage, everything is silent under a soft light. A lone figure in gold begins to sing...

The backstage is a riot of noise and motion. Footsteps and voices mingle in the air, thick with perfume and sweat. Dozens of scantily clad dancers stand to one side, their faces blank, like a line of dolls awaiting their cues.
The newcomer, Sallie, is the only one on edge. She stands tensely in a corner, eyes glued to the stage.

speaker: Man in the Shadow
content: Get ready, wait for the signal.

speaker: Sallie
content: ...The signal?

speaker: Man in the Shadow
content: The signal for the show. From the woman on stage, the Jewel of Euphoria.
[Insert Video CG] Milly strips, group dance

speaker: Magician
content: Yeehaw!! Our turn!
[Cheers, whistles, applause]

As she tosses her glove skyward, the drums erupt. The spotlight on the singer dims, and the whole stage flares to life. The curtain flies open and a riot of color floods out, instantly taking over the performance.

Snow conjures snowflakes, Selene rises into the air. The centaur prances across the stage, the magician pulls a rabbit from a hat, and a man built like a French horn blasts a tune. Everyone is in action... except for one.

speaker: Sallie
content: Ah!

The newcomer trips. The sudden glare of the lights has caught her off guard. She stumbles, missing a beat, and the swarm of bodies behind her knocks her to the floor. Her dress slips in the jostle, and she scrambles to cover herself in panic.
But when she looks up, she's met by a blast of laughter and jeers from the crowd. All she can see are flickering masks, their hollow eyeholes gaping with arrogance and greed.

speaker: Guest A
content: Well well, it's a new one. That was a pretty fall. Great pose, too. Shows just the right amount.

speaker: Guest B
content: Keep going! Want me to show you how to strip?
A few hands reach for her. She jerks away from their touch, almost screaming. The host cuts in, his voice gliding smoothly over the music to save the show.

speaker: Host
content: Oh! Looks like this lovely dancer is just dying to give us a special performance! Easy now, dear guests—don’t forget to feast your eyes on the other beauties too, or they’ll start getting jealous!
The lights and the guests' attention are quickly drawn to the frolicking dancers on the other side. In the darkened corner, Sallie hears a low curse.

speaker: Host
content: Get up! Useless piece of trash, screwing up on your first night. Don't you dare ruin everyone's fun. Dance!

speaker: Sallie
content: Ngh...

Sallie struggles to her feet. Her ankle is twisted, forcing her to kick off her shoes. She looks up, hoping to find a discreet spot to stand, only to see that the other dancers have slithered into the champagne towers flanking the stage, bathing themselves in the syrupy honey wine and slathering it all over their skin.

Piece by piece, their clothing comes off, to the increasingly frenzied cheers from the crowd. What room is left for modesty here? For decorum? Morality? Sallie feels a sharp sting of pain, but in this place, tears will earn no sympathy.
They only make the masked beasts more excited.

speaker: Host
content: Ladies and gentlemen, welcome aboard... <color=#fb9259>Euphoria</color>!
[Insert Battle]
When madness and desire burn themselves out, calm returns after indulgence runs its course. The show nears its end, and the curtain slowly falls.
The stage fills with pinpricks of light. In the gentle spotlight, the golden figure appears once more.
(A quiet solo for the finale. Adapt a short segment from the PV song, within 15 seconds, single playback; lyrics related to missing a lover and expressing love, slow and drawn-out)

speaker: Milly
content: ...Thank you. Tonight, this song is for my love far away.

speaker: Milly
content: You taught me to love this world, and you gave the jewel her light. Thank you for letting me shine.

speaker: Milly
content: May you all find your true love. May happiness find us all.

The revelry gives way to serenity. In the quiet music, the Jewel of Euphoria is bathed in a soft golden glow, her tender devotion soothing all restlessness. In the name of love, she offers them all a gentle forgiveness.
[Scene Change - The Stage at Curtain Call]

speaker: Host
content: Thank you for the dreamlike performance, for this intoxicating song. Thank you, Jewel of Euphoria, for this ode to true love.

speaker: Host
content: Well then, Milly's performance has ended, but the wonderful evening has only just begun.

speaker: Host
content: Our most honored guests—please, savor this honeyed night to your heart’s content.

He gives an elegant bow. Amid applause and lights, the beautiful dancers descend from the stage, letting the guests slip arms around their slender waists and lead them toward the bars and booths in cheerful banter.
In a corner of the stage, where the lights don't reach, Sallie is slumped on the floor. Her knees are bruised, her ankle too swollen to support her weight, but this pain means nothing to her now.
