In the distance, a lone figure glides across the mud-choked path, pristine white against the grime.

speaker: Enthusiastic Refugee
content: He's here!
The camp erupts. A surge of bodies presses forward, voices rising in desperate hope as they swarm around Saffar.

speaker: Enthusiastic Refugee
content: Look at me, Saffar! See, I've caught Mania already. It's finally my turn now, right?

speaker: Anxious Refugee
content: No, no, pick me! Look at my arm, it's way worse than hers, totally rotten! I might even turn into a Sinner any day now. C'mon, take me instead!
At the far end of the bustling crowd, Hella lingers in disguise, her sharp eyes fixed on the scene before her.
She recognizes the man. He was there at yesterday's welcome ceremony when she first arrived at the institute. One of their own.

speaker: Hella
content: ...Hey, what's going on here? What... are they doing?

speaker: Thani
content: Oh right, you just got here. You probably don't know about this yet.

speaker: Thani
content: This is one of the ways to get into the institute, a regular screening that happens once every two months.
Thani's tone is effortless, as if this were the most ordinary thing in the world.

speaker: Thani
content: That man over there in the middle is <color=#fb9259>Saffar</color>, the screening officer from the research institute. He comes here regularly to pick up people who are really sick and take them for treatment.

speaker: Thani
content: Oh yeah! The folks who came from Furor yesterday? He took them too... Are you worried about them? Aw, don't be! The institute's technology is really advanced. They'll get better in no time!
Treating refugees? Since when have the Fraser people played philanthropist?

speaker: Hella
content: Would they really be that excited just for "treatment"? No... they want something else...
Hella scans the crowd again. Amid the shoving and jostling, a tattered cloak is torn away, exposing a twisted, broken body beneath—the unmistakable marks of Mania's corruption.
Yet no fear flickers in the faces around her. Only feverish devotion, a hunger burning in their eyes.
She knows that look. It's the same desperate gaze the Syndicans once fixed upon the other side.

speaker: Hella
content: They all want to become Aurum Secretum Warriors?

speaker: Thani
content: Hehe... Well... How should I put this...

speaker: Thani
content: There's never enough food and medicine to go around. They... just want a better life.

speaker: Thani
content: For everyone here, getting infected means a chance to become a Sinner, a chance to get into Fraser...

speaker: Hella
content: Like Synex?

speaker: Thani
content: ...If there's one Synex, of course there can be a second Synex.
Thani points toward the center of the crowd.

speaker: Thani
content: Just like Saffar there. He's also someone who made it out of this place.
Hella looks toward the figure in the center of the crowd.

Saffar listens patiently to everyone's concerns, his tone gentle and his movements deliberate, without a hint of impatience. Even when faced with deformities and disabilities, his expression never wavers. Instead, he bends down to meet the refugees at eye level, treating them with unwavering dignity.

speaker: Hella
content: ...Would someone like that really be willing to come back here?
It's like seeing a Syndican who ran off to Eastside, only to return a few days later, complaining they "just couldn't get used to it there."

speaker: Thani
content: Saffar is a kind person. The elders always tell me that out of all the kids who left, Saffar's the only one who still comes back to check on everyone...

speaker: Thani
content: And sometimes he even brings extra medicine and stuff. It's because of him that things aren't as tough around here.

speaker: Hella
content: What about the others who made it into the institute? Has no one else ever come back?
Thani offers a bitter smile.

speaker: Thani
content: Hehe... I guess after they got better, they just ended up staying in Fraser. Can't really blame them, though. Everyone's had enough tough times around here...

speaker: Thani
content: After all... where else could we possibly go?
Suddenly, shouts of surprise erupt from the excited crowd. A middle-aged woman rushes to Saffar, her voice trembling with desperation.

speaker: Sandra
content: Sir! Please, I beg you, tell me about my boy... How's he doing?

speaker: Sandra
content: My boy... You picked my boy...!

speaker: Saffar
content: You are...

speaker: Sandra
content: My poor little Yuri... Is he doing all right now? Has he recovered? I-I...
The woman's voice trembles, her hands shaking so violently she can barely clutch Saffar's robe.
Some agitated refugees try to pull the woman away, only to be halted by Saffar. Deliberately, he crouches to her level, steadying her with firm yet gentle hands.

speaker: Saffar
content: I remember him. He was such a lively child... yet Mania tortured him to the brink of death...

speaker: Saffar
content: He's... fine now. And all of us will be fine, too.
Saffar stands up, his voice resonating throughout the crowd.

speaker: Saffar
content: The Farland Alliance is facing a crisis. Calamities spread chaos, monsters rampage through the streets, and DisCity keeps restricting our access to Hypercubes... We have suffered loss after loss, powerless to fight back.

speaker: Saffar
content: We need strength—desperately. And we must stand together.

speaker: Saffar
content: Do not fear Mania! Calamities won't destroy us. Challenge it. Harness it. And in return, we'll be granted extraordinary power—
With a deliberate motion, he raises his palm. The Aurum Secretum coiled around his wrist pulses to life, emitting a soft glow. The crowd stirs with admiration, their awed voices rising like a tide.

speaker: Saffar
content: My friends, the earth beneath us is scarred with countless wounds, and the sky above has long been choked by dark clouds. But never forget, no matter how long the night, dawn will always come!

speaker: Saffar
content: The Great Expo delegation has already left Fraser. They'll bring Aurum Secretum to counter DisCity's grip. As long as we hold onto patience and hope...
He takes Sandra's hand and speaks with firm conviction.

speaker: Saffar
content: Everyone will find salvation. I'm certain of it.
[Fade Out to Switch Scene: Same Background]
Hella stands silent, struck by the bitter familiarity of it all. She had heard similar words in Syndicate, more than once.
"Power," "hope," "stand together"... such familiar terms. The farland refugees lean in, starved for meaning, but all she hears is Rustfire's shackles, polished and repackaged.
Liar...
Why is it that no matter where I go, people keep falling for these stupid, empty promises...
The screening process draws to a close. Rejected refugees scatter like autumn leaves while the chosen few coalesce into an orderly line.
Hella's gaze lingers on the long queue, and an idea begins to take root in her mind.

June 23, N.F. 115
2:07 PM

Underground Maze, Inside the Aurum Secretum Institute
[Dialogue Background: Underground Tunnel]

The long line of people is led underground through a secluded entrance. The narrow corridor is claustrophobic, its walls streaked with mottled rust and grime, the air thick and damp with the scent of mildew—each breath heavy, as if swallowing spores.
Hella keeps her head low, her face half-hidden. She moves with the refugees, past one inspection checkpoint after another.

speaker: Aurum Secretum Guard
content: Beep—Beep—Inspection passed—Next.
This isn't the area where the Legion entered before... Where are they taking these people...?

The refugees trail the researchers like shadows, their faces ashen, their expressions hollow. Yet their eyes betray a strange, restless energy. One man lets out a low, grating laugh, his words slurred and incoherent under his breath.

speaker: Mumbling Refugee
content: ...Almost there, we're almost there...

speaker: Hella
content: What did you say?

speaker: Mumbling Refugee
content: Heheh... it will listen... just make a wish... it will respond...

Then he begins to hum, his voice rasping, as if his throat were lined with sand. The tune is warped, unfamiliar, some forgotten nursery rhyme from a dead people. The melody twists in the air, less like music and more like wind wailing through crumbling stone.
Hella's scalp prickles. Each note digs into her nerves, pulling them tighter. She clutches her cloak closer, but her legs betray her—her steps falter, unsteady.

Darkness thickens. The eerie tune slithers through her mind, warping her senses. The ground beneath her feet feels spongy, yielding, while the stone walls press inward, pulsing in time with her frantic heartbeat.
She grits her teeth and shakes her head violently, dispelling the vision. Her sight clears, but the throbbing in her ears remains, swelling louder, drawing her forward.
As she crosses the final threshold, the space ahead yawns open—vast, waiting.
[Black Screen]

speaker: Hella
content: What... is this?

A vast, circular chamber stretches before her. At its heart, a grotesque cocoon hangs inverted, throbbing with a slow, unnatural rhythm. Its surface glistens, a translucent membrane webbed with thick, crimson veins.
The refugees sit in a silent ring, their bodies forming a living altar. Their eyes, hollow yet feverish, are fixed in unison upon the pulsating mass above.

speaker: Hella
content: Ugh... blegh...
The air is thick with a cloying stench—sweet, yet laced with rot. Before Hella can place it, the crowd shudders to life around her.
A man lurches forward, arms raised in devotion, his gaze alight with manic fervor.

speaker: Fanatic Refugee
content: Haha... It's my turn...!

speaker: Fanatic Refugee
content: This is my wish! No more eating sandworms, no more sleep on sand... I want to live! I need to live!
Without hesitation, he presses his palm against the veined flesh of the Cocoon—
The next second, the world twists. The very air shrieks, warping as if torn apart.
[CG - Deteriorated Alchemic Beast]
The scene unfolding before her is hell incarnate.

speaker: Fanatic Refugee
content: Ah... Ah... AAAAAHHHHHH—!!!

The man's spine snaps backward with a grotesque crack, his throat tearing open in a shriek—too shrill, too alien to be anything born of nature. His flesh liquefies as it convulses, skin sloughing away in rancid sheets while his bones splinter and warp, joints popping in a nauseating chorus.
Then, his hollowed carcass splits apart, and something else claws its way out.

Fresh bone erupts from shattered limbs, organs swelling grotesquely from the gaping chest cavity. Where his face should be, the flesh churns, twisting inward before surging forward again—features mangled, rearranged, until only a shapeless, grinning maw remains.

speaker: Familiar Female Voice
content: Holy ****, this is—
Hella knows this abomination. She's seen it in Furor, in the research institute's labyrinthine tunnels. Fraser's favorite puppet, lurking at the heart of every conspiracy.

The thing lands with a wet, meaty slap, half-formed muscle still writhing as it struggles to knit itself whole. The moment its claws scrape the ground, it lunges, jaws unhinging in a roar that shakes the air.
——————

The monster's mutilated limbs thrash wildly as arcs of blood splatter the surroundings, only to fuel the crowd's frenzy. Their arms flail, voices roaring, and the chaos crescendos into a feverish storm of delight.

speaker: Fanatic Crowd
content: Amazing! The Cocoon answered his wish!

speaker: Fanatic Crowd
content: Next! Next! It's my turn now!

They are no longer human—only devotees, worshipers of suffering. They rush toward the monster in a frenzied tide, desperate to be first, their faces streaked with tears of ecstasy. Like souls clawing for salvation, only to hurl themselves headlong into hell.
The Mania radiating from the "Cocoon" presses against Hella's mind, relentless. Each pulse is a tolling bell, shuddering through her skull.

speaker: Hella
content: Ugh... Is this... "resonance"...?
In her dazed state, long-buried dark memories rip free, surging violently into her consciousness.
(Surgical Lights)
(Laboratory 1)
(Laboratory 2)

Whispers slither into her thoughts as a shrill ringing pierces her ears, sharp enough to buckle her knees. For a breathless moment, she is there again: trapped in the cold, sterile hell of the underground laboratory.

speaker: Malicious Voice
content: ...The experiment failed, but we got something else...

speaker: Malicious Voice
content: Such potent regeneration, yet with no offensive capabilities... Heh, fascinating...

speaker: Hella
content: ...Damn it...! Leave me alone...

speaker: Hella
content: ...Ugh!
She bites her tongue hard. The sharp tang of iron floods her mouth, jolting her back to reality just as footsteps echo closer.
Hella stumbles behind a collapsed piece of machinery, pressing herself into the shadows. Seconds later, a figure strides into the room through the opposite doorway.

speaker: Saffar
content: <size=24>...The number of vessels is increasing, and the Mania corruption levels are rising, but... resonance remains unstable... Most have deteriorated into <color=#fb9259>alchemic beasts</color>...

speaker: Director Hermis
content: <size=24>...No matter. Specimens like Synex are once-in-a-lifetime... Quantity will suffice...
The voices nearby reach her as if through deep water—muffled, fragmented. Most of the words slip past her, but a few cruel phrases strike like nails, piercing her skull.
What have they done? What are they planning now? Footsteps shift again. The two figures move about the room, their voices breaking apart, fading in and out.

speaker: Director Hermis
content: <size=24>Natural awakening is unnecessary... Campbell isn't trustworthy, but his tech has proven useful. By using sorcery imprints to forcibly inject Mania, we can manufacture our own Sinners...

speaker: Director Hermis
content: <size=24>...The reduced operational lifespan is an acceptable trade-off. They'll last long enough for the <color=#fb9259>Black Ring</color>'s needs...
Another roar from the crowd. Another silhouette steps forward, another body twisting, transforming.

The Cocoon's rhythm quickens, pulsing like frantic drumbeats. Malice and fanaticism coil together as whispers surge into frenzied chanting. Hella's vision blurs. Her body trembles, her muscles locking as a voice—the voice, the one she fears and hates most—scrapes through her mind.

speaker: Malicious Voice
content:
<color=#ca0c1b>Look at them, these human lab rats... They're living through everything you fled from, aren't they?
They chose this. But you... you never had a choice.</color>

speaker: Malicious Voice
content:
<color=#ca0c1b>All that suffering you tried to bury? It never left.
You thought you escaped? No... you were just given a taste of what was waiting for you.</color>

speaker: Hella
content: ...Shut up...

The chaos before her eyes bleeds into memories of the laboratory—her skull clamped in place, cold steel parting flesh, chemicals searing through bone marrow, the surgeon's gaze as hollow as a corpse's. Not memories. Nightmares. And now, those nightmares are clawing their way into reality.
Who lies on the butcher's block this time? The farland refugees? Or is it Hella herself?

speaker: Malicious Voice
content: You never escaped. You just wandered into a different lab.

speaker: Malicious Voice
content: Mania remade you... but left you powerless. Now you'll watch others die, over and over, while you cling to survival...

speaker: Hella
content: No...! I'm not your lab rat anymore! I escaped a long time ago...!

speaker: Malicious Voice
content: Oh, you know it too well. Speak. Don't run... tell me your deepest wish...

speaker: Malicious Voice
content: You still haven't realized it? "You" ceased being "you" long ago. You're just like them, another failure, another wretched monster—

speaker: Hella
content: Shut up, shut up, SHUT UP! Get away from me!!

Hella lashes out with a violent strike, unleashing a Mania-infused shockwave that shatters the surrounding illusions—their whispers dying in an instant. Light erupts outward as a ring of dark mist disperses, then vanishes into nothing.
For a single, suspended heartbeat, the hall stands utterly still.
Then—
Alarms scream. The crowd erupts into chaos. A blade of light descends from above, thunderous and unrelenting as it cleaves toward Hella.

speaker: Saffar
content: Intruder! Everyone, prepare to engage—!
The battle ends as swiftly as it began. Saffar flicks Hella's weapon aside, then pins her down in a single motion.

speaker: Saffar
content: ...She's one of the two DisCity people who went missing yesterday.
Head bowed, vision blurred by the searing pain of Mania's resonance, Hella can only listen as footsteps approach. It's the director.

speaker: Director Hermis
content: Wait, hold on.

speaker: Director Hermis
content: I've heard the shackle user and Sinners affect each other. I wonder... does that connection hold even beyond WhiteSands?

speaker: Hella
content: ...Hey! What are you talking about? What are you planning to do?!

speaker: Director Hermis
content: Lock her up. SHP-13's Sinner. She'll be invaluable to us.
[Scene Transition: Test Subject Cell]
In the haze of her consciousness, Hella feels herself being carried to someplace else. A door clangs shut, followed by the heavy sigh of someone.

speaker: Vague Voice
content: ...You shouldn't have come here...

speaker: Vague Voice
content: ...The weak, no matter how hard they struggle...

speaker: Hella
content: Ugh...

The floor beneath her is wet, sticky. When her hands press into it, the sensation is vile, like sinking into a pool of rotting flesh. The Mania in the air seeps into her being, clawing through her dazed state to burrow into her bones, gnawing at her mind like a ravenous thing.
She drags in ragged breaths, fighting against the pain. Finally, with a shuddering effort, she lifts her head.

A prison cell. The torchlight is feeble, barely pushing back the gloom. What little illumination there is reveals uneven walls encased in metal frames. Deep, frantic scratches gouge the stone—the desperate work of past prisoners who had tried, and failed, to escape.
Then—movement. A shifting in the dark. The wet slide of limbs dragging across the floor. No, it's not her imagination.
Monsters slowly crawl out from the darkness, writhing as they gradually close in.

speaker: Hella
content: What the hell...?! Get away... Don't touch me...!
Hella jerks back, but the wall is already there, unyielding against her spine.

The scrape of shackles against the ground snags her attention. Only then does she see what's wrong with them. Each creature bears Aurum Secretum shackles fused into their bodies, some jutting through shoulder blades, others driven deep into spines. The restraints don't just bind them; they puppet what's left of their twisted, no-longer-human forms.
One of them writhes forward, silent as it closes in on Hella.

speaker: Hella
content: You are...
This alchemic beast is tiny in size. With no eyes, it navigates by scent alone. Then, with unsettling gentleness, it presses against Hella's cheek.
Its flesh trembles, and from its mouthparts come fractured, guttural words, barely intelligible.
...Mo... Mom?

speaker: Sandra
content: My boy... You picked my boy...!

speaker: Sandra
content: My poor little Yuri... Is he doing all right now? Has he recovered? I-I...

speaker: Hella
content: You're... Sandra's...
The small alchemic beast doesn't stop. It nudges closer, its face nearly touching hers.
The stench of decay thickens. Hella has nowhere to retreat. She turns her face away, only to see the wall beside her riddled with scratches.

At first, they seem like mere gouges from some past violence. But as her vision sharpens, the marks resolve into something worse: uneven grooves, caked with dried blood, forming letters carved by something desperate.
<size=40>So hungry</size>　　　<size=50>Everything hurts</size> When will I get better?
They all stopped moving　 WHY 　Don't <size=50>leave</size> me here
Let me <size=40>out</size>　 I don't want this anymore, I want to leave
<size=40>How long<size=40> have I been here<size=40>　 Am I still <size=40>alive</size>? <size=40>No　 I'm not a failed product<size=40> HELP ME<size=40>
<size=40>No, I'm not a failed product<size=40></size>　　I　　I am...

speaker: Hella
content: Ngh...!
The text warps in her vision as darkness creeps inward. Voices overlap, echoing in Hella's ears—battering her consciousness, dragging her toward the abyss. She struggles, but the pull is relentless.
Suddenly, her fingers brush against something. Another set of markings, deeper than the rest, their edges sharp. They twist across the stone wall, consuming nearly the entire surface.
—Frenzied writing. A single word, carved over and over and over: a name.
With the last frayed thread of her clarity, Hella forces herself to look.

speaker: Hella
content: Sy...nex?
[Dimming Filter + Flickering Golden Light]
Strange Aurum Secretum light blooms from her fingertips. The mournful moans of the alchemic beasts fade into distant echoes as the world around her dissolves.
She seems to have touched a fragment of someone's soul. Her consciousness plunges into an endless dream—vast, weightless.
[Illusion: Synex's Past]
Softness envelops her. The sensation is warm, like sinking into an embrace.

speaker: Hella
content: Where... am I?

Hella feels herself compressed into a smaller body. An infant's perspective, able to see only strands of hair swaying gently before her eyes. A chest presses close, rising and falling in quick, uneven bursts. The heartbeat thrums against her ear, alive yet terrified.

speaker: Feeble Voice
content: Shh... there, there, don't cry... Mommy's taking you to a place where... you won't go hungry, a better, more beautiful place...
Pain seeps into tiny bones. Without Hypercubes, Mania festers, twisting through her, warping flesh into something wrong.
A sudden commotion erupts as a team of white-coated researchers approaches. The arms around her stiffen—hesitate—then, with a shuddering resolve, lift her away.
Her body suddenly feels weightless. The warmth vanishes. Cold hands catch her, steady and unfeeling.
The infant wails. Hella strains to see, but the faces blur, the reaching hands merge into a sea of strangers. Who held her? She cannot tell.
Only a whisper of blessing lingers, carried over on the wind.

speaker: Feeble Voice
content: Goodbye, Synex, my child...

speaker: Feeble Voice
content: You must live... live on for us... live well...
[Black Screen Transition]

speaker: Researcher
content: Now commencing Experiment No. 819, Fusion Attempt 5.
Argh—!
The perspective shifts. When Hella regains consciousness, she finds herself trapped in an experimental chamber.
Crimson crystals pierce her torso, forcing her body into ebullition alongside Mania. Agony follows, searing, unrelenting. This time, she is no longer an infant, no longer cradled in someone's arms.
The pain erupts from her bone marrow, spreading like wildfire. Around her, the white-coated figures observe with cold, detached indifference.

speaker: Researcher
content: It's no use. Ordinary subjects still can't withstand rampant Mania. Without stabilization, forget achieving resonance with Ash Crystals. They won't even survive long enough to awaken as Sinners.

speaker: Researcher
content: What about Aurum Secretum? Didn't those <color=#fb9259>sorcery</color> suppliers say anything useful?

speaker: Researcher
content: Those lunatics don't give a damn about survival rates. Aurum Secretum can forcibly suppress Mania, but it won't stop the mental degradation... Whatever, it may still be worth a shot. Let's try it.
The dosage increases, igniting another explosion of Mania. This time, she hears the wet, splintering sounds of bones warping, snapping from within.

speaker: Synex
content: GO TO—HELL—AAAAAAAAAHHHHHHH!!
Her limbs hum with a chorus of fractures, life surging through her in warped, convulsive waves.

speaker: Parma Researcher
content: What a rare specimen... If we increase the injection dosage further, how will it affect her regenerative abilities?

speaker: Hella
content: No, stop... Go away...!
[Transition Back to Background - Aurum Secretum Laboratory]
Her body crumples apart. Death closes in.

speaker: Researcher
content: ...Still not working. Note this down: Test Subject 819, cause of death—

speaker: Researcher
content: Wait! Something's off...
The Aurum Secretum seeps into her flesh, melting into her marrow through ceaseless, shuddering resonance.
Mania surges through her body. Pain belongs solely to the victorious—it is the proof of survival.

speaker: Synex
content: I must live... and then...
[Quick Transition to Background - Surgical Lights]

speaker: Hella
content: I must escape... and then...
[Transition Back to Background - Aurum Secretum Laboratory]

<size=40><u>Test Subject 819, Fusion Attempt 17.</size></u>

Subject has not completely deteriorated and has begun to establish initial resonance with Aurum Secretum.

speaker: Researcher
content: The M-value has surpassed the threshold, but her body hasn't fully broken down. Looks like the Aurum Secretum is effective after all.

<size=40><u>Test Subject 819, Fusion Attempt 35.</size></u>

Aurum Secretum decay cycle is approximately 720 minutes.
Increasing Mania concentration in injection solution. Continue monitoring subject's condition.

speaker: Synex & Hella
content: Aargh...!

<size=40><u>Test Subject 819, Fusion Attempt 49.</size></u>

Subject's body showing signs of deterioration. Rate of breakdown lower than physical regeneration rate.
Experiment continues.

speaker: Synex & Hella
content: Ahhh...!

<size=40><u>Test Subject 819, Fusion Attempt 127.</size></u>

High-density fusion between Aurum Secretum and subject's body achieved.
Signs of deterioration are irreversible. Subject has developed a dependency on Aurum Secretum, requiring periodic fusion.

speaker: Synex & Hella
content: Enough... stop... torturing me...

<size=40><u>Test Subject 819, Fusion Attempt 211.</size></u>

Physical deformities on subject's body continue to intensify. Aurum Secretum resonance rate has strengthened, exceeding all historical records.
<size=40><u>Test Subject 819, Fusion Attempt 356.</size></u>
<size=50><u>Test Subject 819, Fusion Attempt 585.</size></u>

speaker: Synex & Hella
content: Kill me...

speaker: Researcher
content: Wait... She hasn't returned to the suppression state! The monitoring systems are failing! Parameters erratic—initiate containment protocols, now!

speaker: Researcher
content: She's breaking loose! Cut the power! Elimin—

speaker: Synex & Hella
content: Kill me... or... I'LL KILL YOU!!
Mania forms into a tangible shockwave, shattering the observation wall. With her target locked and obstacles obliterated, she lunges straight for the blonde man standing at the rear of the crowd.
—Clang. Her claws freeze, trembling inches from his throat. Then, just as suddenly, Mania recedes, causing her body to gradually disintegrate.
Yet the man only chuckles. Deliberate, unhurried, he steps forward and raises his hand.

speaker: Adelaide
content: You're dying. How unfortunate... Your end could have been so much more meaningful. But I can offer you a way out.
The Crimebrand on his knuckles ignites as raw Mania coils at his fingertips, a malevolence dwarfing every other force in the space.

speaker: Adelaide
content: Serve me. Become my instrument, and I will make you a "hero" beloved by the masses, bathed in glory beyond your wildest dreams...

speaker: Adelaide
content: To survive, you have no other choice.

speaker: Hella
content: No... don't! Synex!!
Synex's form continues crumbling. Hella struggles, thrashing against the inevitable, but her consciousness is already unraveling, slipping away like sand through clenched fists.
The last thing she hears before the dark swallows her is a snicker, half-mockery, half-genuine.

speaker: Synex
content: ...Hah. To survive, my only option is to be your dog?
[Black Screen + Floating Points of Light]
Afterward, she left the research institute and roamed the world as Campbell's shadow operative, cleaning up the dirty affairs that her "master" couldn't allow to see the light of day.
She never resisted this fate. And so, the monster donned a mask, hid her tail, and—for survival's sake—became an obedient hound, a convenient tool.
Until fate came knocking at her door once more.
[Maybe use the Fraser City background image]

speaker: Director Hermis
content: The "Cocoon"—a mysterious Apostle matrix gifted to us by the Underground, capable of achieving maximum Aurum Secretum resonance with humans while also controlling the lifeline of all who resonate with it.

speaker: Director Hermis
content: Once resonance is attempted, successful or not, the bond is irreversible. There is no severing it.

speaker: Director Hermis
content: Test Subject 819, <color=#fb9259>Synex</color>. You are our most exceptional specimen. It's time for you to serve our city and fulfill your purpose.
<color=#fb9259><size=44>Project BR-005</size></color>

<color=#fb9259><size=44>Utilize the Underground ██, paired with a high-Mania Sinner, to trigger BR-005.

By controlling the Sinner, our city will create the first manipulable Black Ring.</size></color>
[Find some suitable WhiteSands background image to use here]

speaker: Hella
content: So this is... the memory of "resonance"... the truth about Aurum Secretum Warriors...

speaker: Hella
content: Heh... And here I thought I had it rough... Your life's even more of a mess than mine.
"Synex" is the most successful experiment, Campbell's shadow operative, the glorious Aurum Secretum Warrior.
Also a monument upon the path, she draws hopeful souls like moths to a flame.

At the end of the chaotic memories, Hella finally sees her: Synex, standing against a torrent of shattered recollections, darkness coiling around her like living corruption—twisting, grasping, reaching.

speaker: Refugees' Voices
content: Our homeland... our city... swallowed by calamity... We had no choice... ran scattered like dust on the wind...

speaker: Refugees' Voices
content: Infection followed us... death whispered at our backs... But then, hope. Shelter. Healing. Fraser... Fraser saved us...

speaker: Refugees' Voices
content: Look, it's Synex... She was one of us. She'll protect us. She'll save us...

speaker: Refugees' Voices
content: ...A hero! She's our hero!

speaker: Synex
content: ...<color=#fb9259>Hero</color>? Heh, what a joke.

speaker: Synex
content: Mania clings to me, trying to kill me. Aurum Secretum tortures me, turning me into a monster neither human nor beast. Then they came up with this great plan. Since my clock is ticking down anyway, they might as well feed me to the Black Ring, let Fraser's pompous lords wring what Hypercubes they could from my bones.

speaker: Synex
content: Everyone wanted me dead... but I survived anyway.

speaker: Synex
content: But... why?
There's not a trace of amusement on Synex's face. For the first time, she seems calm... almost numb.

speaker: Synex
content: Is the life of your <color=#fb9259>hero</color> as worthless as a stray dog's?
The contamination begins to spread, creeping up Synex's body. But she doesn't care at all.

speaker: Hella
content: ...?! Hey, you jerk! Don't go—where are you going?

speaker: Hella
content: You're the one who never bows down to fate, right?! The tough-as-nails fighter who doesn't back down?! I've been stuck in a lab too, and even I busted my way out! So don't tell me you can't do the same—fight back, damn it! Don't let those Fraser bastards win!
Hella stretches forward, fingers straining, but Synex's just out of reach.

speaker: Hella
content: I'll help you—hey! Don't you dare give up! Get your ass back here!

speaker: Synex
content: Give up?
The chaos suddenly stills. Then, the very space around Synex shudders, twisting violently.

speaker: Synex
content: Oh, please. As if I'd let my end come somewhere this pathetic.

speaker: Synex
content: Mania's been rotting through me for years. If I'm going out, I'm taking everything I can with me—

speaker: Synex
content: Since you're all so eager to send me to hell, you'd better pack a bag. Because we're going together!
[Black Screen]

speaker: Synex
content: Hey, wakey-wakey, little rat. Rise and shine.
[Scene Transition, Back to the Cell]
Blue light flickers. Some pressure digs into her forehead as her senses claw back.
Hella's vision gradually focuses on the figure before her. Malicious eyes, that mocking smile—this is—

speaker: Hella
content: Synex?! Ugh—
She jerks back, but Synex matches her movement, relentless, pressing the Hypercube against Hella's forehead.

speaker: Synex
content: Awake now? Still breathing? Can you get up on your feet?
Behind Synex, the alchemic beasts twist and coil, no longer attacking Hella. Now, they slither close to Synex, almost adoringly obedient.
(Flashback: Small CG - Alchemic Beast)

speaker: Hella
content: I saw everything. What they did to you in the lab. Fraser rounding up refugees for experiments... You're just like them. That's why you call them your "brothers and sisters"...
Her emotions stirred by the illusion cling like smoke. Hella lifts her head—Synex's smile cuts through her, radiant and razor-sharp.

speaker: Synex
content: Aww, feeling sorry for little old me? Look at you, all worked up, your cute little face red as a cherry.
Her fingers brush her cheeks, only to find them wet. Two silent streams, cold against her skin.

speaker: Synex
content: You were crying in your sleep just now, even said my name. Look at you, eyes all puffy. You missed me that much? Or...

speaker: Synex
content: Oh, I get it now. You've actually been secretly in love with me this whole time—

speaker: Hella
content: WHAT?! SHUT UP! SHUT UP SHUT UP SHUT UP!!!
Flushed with embarrassment and rage, Hella hurls the Hypercube at Synex's smirking face, only for it to be caught midair effortlessly.

speaker: Hella
content: You jerk! And I actually felt bad for you?! What a waste!
Her eyes, barely dry, well up again. Hella turns her head sharply away, stalks to the farthest corner from Synex, and drops down. She scrubs at her face with her sleeve—hard.
Tap tap. Something prods her shoulder. She stiffens, jaw locked, refusing to turn.
That thing continues to poke Hella's shoulder, unrelenting.

speaker: Synex
content: Little Hella? Little rat? Pretty cutie pie Hella— My brave little Hella who didn't even whimper when she fell on her butt—
Hella whirls, fury blazing in her glare, only to find Synex poking her with the tip of her tail.

speaker: Synex
content: Still mad?
Smack! Hella swats away the annoying tail, her teeth clenched in fury.

speaker: Hella
content: Spit it out. Exactly how are you sabotaging the Black Ring ritual? What's your real plan?

speaker: Synex
content: Hmm? Black Ring what? Plan who? My, my, such accusations...

speaker: Hella
content: Cut the bullshit! You were singing about chaos yesterday while chasing me! Brave enough to drag me into your mess but too chickenshit to own it now?!

As her mind clears, the truth strikes Hella like a blade: Synex planned this from the beginning. She manipulated the Legion, lured them underground, all to sabotage the ritual and spare herself from becoming the Black Ring's sacrifice.
And it worked. Hella, the Legion, even Hypatia—they had all been puppets in the hands of this so-called "hero."

speaker: Hella
content: Tell me everything now! Hide one more thing and I'm done helping you!
Synex narrows her eyes for a moment before she breaks into laughter.

speaker: Synex
content: Fine, you win. No more games.

speaker: Synex
content: Rebellion's no tea party, you know. Every good uprising needs its little trials. After all, what we're up against is not just one "enemy."

speaker: Hella
content: ...What do you mean?

speaker: Synex
content: Fraser has set up amplification devices around the refugee camp. Pumping Mania radiation straight into the refugees they "rescued." Turns out one Corpseborne isn't enough insurance for those cowards. Now they want spares. A whole camp full of them.

speaker: Hella
content: What...?! I thought those were Mania-blocking devices!
Synex shakes her head.

speaker: Synex
content: If they actually gave a damn about people, those city gates would've swung open years ago.

speaker: Synex
content: But don't worry. I didn't drag you into this blind.

speaker: Synex
content: The <color=#fb9259>maze</color> is not only the institute's little dumping ground for failed alchemic beasts, but also my turf. Dragons hoard treasure in their lairs, so guess what I've buried deep in mine? Something that'll make those Fraser bastards wish they'd stayed in their ivory towers.

speaker: Synex
content: When their Black Ring plan kicks off and every last eyeball's glued to me, that's your cue to slip behind them and stab where it really stings. Sound like fun?
Hella doesn't answer. Her gaze stays fixed on the ground as she poses another question.

speaker: Hella
content: ...Why me?

speaker: Synex
content: Hmm?

speaker: Hella
content: Don't play dumb with me. You've got plenty of other people you could ask. Horo or Hypatia could do this way better than me, but here you are, picking me. Why?

speaker: Synex
content: Hmm... Because it's fun?
As Hella's fury threatens to erupt again, Synex laughs heartily and clamps a hand atop her head, shoving her down with playful force.

speaker: Synex
content: Hahaha! Okay, okay, I'll stop messing with you now. For real this time.

speaker: Synex
content: The famous DisCity Legion Commander is willing to be your friend, and even the notoriously reserved Lady Campbell opens up to you. That's not something just anyone can accomplish.

speaker: Synex
content: Sure, you hit like a wet noodle, but you keep hitting. Cornered? You bite. Outmatched? You outthink. You always find a way to fight back, and you can even come up with solutions that wouldn't even cross my mind.

speaker: Synex
content: Every scheme's got cracks, but you? You're the grenade nobody sees coming.
Her fingers slowly trace across the weathered wall, Aurum Secretum radiating from her fingertips, whispering memories long buried.

speaker: Synex
content: And there's one last point...

speaker: Synex
content: No matter where they are, rats always find a way to survive. No masters, no chains—just pure, stubborn aliveness. They're free, and I like that about them.

speaker: Hella
content: ...Aren't you worried I'll just bail out?

speaker: Synex
content: Hah! If you were gonna run, you'd have bolted back in Furor. No point waiting until now.

speaker: Hella
content: Tch, the nerve of you.

speaker: Hella
content: ...Fine, count me in! But you have to let Horo and the others go!

speaker: Synex
content: Relax, that little wolf's not half as fun as you. They're just taking a scenic detour. Should stumble on the exit any minute now.
With their negotiation complete, Hella pushes away Synex's hand and dusts herself off as she stands up.
What next? Fight their way out? Hella opens her mouth to voice the question when the ground shudders violently beneath them.
The alchemic beasts grow restless. Synex's wrists jerk as the Aurum Secretum shackles tighten—her smirk vanishes, replaced by something dark.

speaker: Synex
content: Tch, these old bastards... They moved up the test explosion.

speaker: Synex
content: Sorry, sweetie, looks like I won't have time to escort you out anymore. Be a good girl and find your own way out, okay?

speaker: Hella
content: Test explosion? What does that mean? What are they planning to do now?

speaker: Synex
content: Just another simulation experiment those Fraser bastards love so much. Won't kill me, but it'll be a living hell to deal with.
Synex rises and strides toward the door, her voice still laced with amusement—though the warmth has vanished.

speaker: Synex
content: Go find help. Legion or any DisCity friends you know will do, but you need to make it fast.

speaker: Synex
content: The Cocoon will mature soon. Next time... it may not be just a drill anymore.
Without another word, she turns and walks away, her back straight. The alchemic beasts flank her, their presence a silent escort.
Hella stands frozen, her fists clenched, hands still trembling.

speaker: Hella
content: Damn it... that just makes me even more worried...!
Gritting her teeth, she slaps her cheeks hard. The sting sharpens her resolve. When she lifts her head again, her gaze is steel.
Then she runs, sprinting off in the direction Synex disappeared.
[Background - Overcast Refugee Camp]

speaker: Thani
content: Huh? When did the sky get so dark...? Gotta hurry back and help everyone bring in their laundry!

speaker: Thani
content: I hope Hella's doing okay...
[Background - Underground Experiment Site]

The site has been thoroughly cleaned. Through the open skylights, the last lingering rays of amber sunlight pierce the laboratory, pooling at the feet of Hella, who had infiltrated the ritual site long before.
Suspended in the open space above, the Cocoon looms, larger now than when last seen. Its pulsations have grown more violent, its fractured shell leaking streams of Mania.
Beneath it, a lone figure stands in silent anticipation.

speaker: Saffar
content: You're late, Synex.
Facing the stern young man, Synex merely shrugs, her hands spreading in a gesture of deliberate indifference.

speaker: Synex
content: Heh... You need a lucky hour for a suicide mission? What's the difference if I'm early or late? All that matters is that I'm here... right?
With a flick of her wrist, the shackles around her arm clink tight, along with the clasp coiled around her tail.

speaker: Synex
content: Don't worry. This dog leash is still on. I'm not going anywhere.

speaker: Saffar
content: That's not what I meant... never mind.

speaker: Saffar
content: The ritual is about to begin. Go now, they're waiting for you.
Footsteps echo across the floor. Hella holds her breath, peering through a crack between the stonework.
Saffar steps aside, no longer blocking Synex's path. With this, Synex begins walking forward.
And then, like a formal declaration of the ritual's commencement, he cedes the stage to the figure bound in shackles.
—Thud!
Synex advances, her steps measured and deliberate. Each footfall is a silent herald of fate's approach.
—Thud!

With every stride, the resonance between her and the Cocoon deepens. The Mania in the air swells, invisible flames lashing at Hella's senses. She grits her teeth, cursing quietly while choking on the searing pressure.

speaker: Hella
content: What the ****... Is this really just a test explosion?!
As if sensing Synex's approach, the Cocoon suspended in midair writhes violently. Something inside thrashes against its confines, straining to break free.

The Aurum Secretum devices at the four corners of the site let out an overloaded hum. Hella feels a prickle of awareness—eyes upon the site. She looks up and spots an observation chamber high above, filled with robed figures. Clad in white, their faces hidden behind expressionless masks, they stand in perfect rows, watching the scene below with detached scrutiny.
The leader lifts a hand. Instantly, the Mania surges. The figure in the testing area convulses, then releases a guttural, inhuman shriek.

speaker: Synex
content: Nnghh...!
The experiment isn't over. She has to keep moving.

speaker: Synex
content: Aahhh... AAAAAAHHHHH!!!

Aurum Secretum floods Synex's veins, erupting from her fingertips in jagged bursts. Her flesh splits, reforms, splits again—an agonizing cycle of destruction and reconstruction, just as it has a thousand times before.
The Mania in the air swells, oppressive and suffocating. Hella's fingers tremble. She knows it's time to go.

speaker: Hella
content: Everyone's too wrapped up in the ritual to notice me. Without Horo and the others, there's no chance I can fight them all alone... Yeah, I should just slip away in the chaos. That's the smart play...

speaker: Hella
content: Tch... Move, damn legs! Wasn't I supposed to run? I'm the queen of getting the hell out! Ugh, why can't I move an inch now?!
Everyone's attention is fixed on the Cocoon and Synex. This is the perfect moment for her to slip away.
Thump!
Synex takes another step forward, sending violent waves of Mania rippling outward. A shadow streaks past Saffar—a blur of motion—hurtling straight toward the apex of the testing site.

speaker: Saffar
content: ...?! An intruder! Is that... the DisCity Sinner?!
Hella grits her teeth, fighting against the crushing tide of Mania. Every step is a battle, her body straining as if wading through an invisible mire.
The Cocoon pulses, sensing the threat. Around her, the Mania swells, a suffocating wave that drags her back into disorientation.

speaker: Ignis
content: Move... MOVE!!
But the deeper she pushes, the heavier Mania clings—sapping her will, devouring her resolve. Her thoughts fracture; her limbs grow leaden.
The power she hoped to rely on, the Mania coiled inside her, does nothing. Against the Cocoon's overwhelming force, it's utterly weak.

speaker: Hella
content: ...Damn it... Is this really... all I've got...
Can't she even cause a tiny bit of trouble?
Suddenly, her fall is halted. Someone has grabbed her.

speaker: Synex
content: How touching. I never thought the little rat would actually scurry in here to help me...
Synex's voice reaches her ear, carrying that familiar tone of mockery.

speaker: Synex
content: But now's not the time. You've still got work to do.
Before Hella can react, an overwhelming force seizes her arm.
(Add a vibration sound effect!)
The power of Aurum Secretum erupts from Synex's body like a tidal wave, its power resonating violently with the surrounding machinery.

speaker: Institute Guard
content: This is no good! She's channeling the Aurum Secretum power!

speaker: Institute Guard
content: Subject is rioting! Abort the ritual! Stop the experiment! Suppress the subject now!!
Someone realizes Synex's intentions, but it's already too late.
[CG - Synex hurling Hella away, modified key visual]
Hella's body is hurled skyward, her world spinning wildly as the whistling wind and panicked screams below blur into chaos.

speaker: Hella
content: Synex?! What are you do—
Countless Aurum Secretum chains ensnare Synex, dragging her toward the abyss. Yet in her final moments, she lifts her head, watching Hella soar.

speaker: Synex
content: Go, Hella. Don't look back. You've got bigger things to do than rot in here!

speaker: Synex
content: Get that message out, then raise hell for me. And when you do? Kick their asses hard! I've left you all the goodies I've been stashing away...

speaker: Synex
content: Make sure they don't go to waste, okay?
Before Hella can even utter a word, the chains swallow Synex whole, and she vanishes into the metal mass.

speaker: Hella
content: ...Cough, cough...
Every inch of her body screams in protest. A throbbing pain radiates from her sprained ankle, forcing her into an unsteady limp as she drags herself forward.
The hidden passage she once used to flee the research institute lies somewhere ahead. If she can just find it again, she might make it out alive.
The exit looms before her, half-hidden in the shadows. But darkness creeps at the edges of her vision, pulling her under.

speaker: Hella
content: Gotta keep moving... This message has to get through...

speaker: Hella
content: I... must...
As her consciousness fades, a familiar figure rushes toward her, though she can no longer tell if it's real or not.
...lla......Hella...

speaker: Horo
content: Hella!
[Saffar's Dream, use any WhiteSands background]
When dry winds caressed his face, they sometimes stirred memories of home.

Every year, when the air grew crisp, the oleaster tree by his home would sag under the weight of its fruit, small and dark red, bursting with sweetness. No matter how many they ate, there were always more.
But the tree was gone now. His home had long since vanished, swallowed by DisCity's artillery fire.

The escape was a slow unraveling. Water ran low. Hard biscuits crumbled to dust in his hands. The line of refugees stretched thinner each day, their numbers dwindling as the weak collapsed into the sand. When his parents could go no farther, they pressed their last scrap of food into his palm and faded into the white dunes.
Hunger gnawed at him, sharp and relentless. Yet worse than the ache in his stomach was the certainty—this exile had no end.

speaker: Researcher
content: Huh? A refugee who actually made it here alive...

speaker: Researcher
content: Can't even speak anymore? You're too consumed by Mania. You don't have long left.

speaker: Researcher
content: Food? Even if I gave you something to eat, it wouldn't matter. The Mania's already taken you.

speaker: Researcher
content: However...

speaker: Researcher
content: There is actually a way... Do you want to live?
After enduring agony that seared down to his marrow, a group of white-coated figures crowded around him. Their voices were buzzing with excitement, talking about another successful test subject.
Metal fused with his flesh, replacing what Mania had rotted away. His stomach no longer twisted with hunger; his body was no longer wrapped in rags.
...Yet the gnawing fear of starvation clung to him. Old habits died hard—he still hoarded scraps of food like a feral thing.
Thwack! A sharp blow cracked against the back of his skull.
Someone lurked in the shadows above him. It was a small figure, probably another kid his age.
She tossed something absently in her hand as she spoke, her voice dripping with arrogance.
Hey, you've got food. Why aren't you eating it?
Hey—Hellooo—? Huh, are you stupid or something?
Only survivors get food. They need you alive for now, so relax, they don't starve you.
You really are stupid. Only survivors get food. They need you alive for now, so relax, they don't starve you.
Her lip curled in contempt, then a flicker of realization crossed her face. When she spoke again, her voice was honeyed poison.
You survived, but do you know what happened to the ones who didn't?
Hehe, they all died!
Or—even worse—they turned into monsters! Now they just wander around, eating people to stay alive. Sooo... scared yet?
...Tsk, you're no fun. Can't even freak you out.

speaker: Choice
options: There are things way scarier than monsters.

content: Hunger, disease, calamities, war... Compared to those horrors, imaginary monsters are nothing, and this place is as close to heaven as it gets.
Really? I'd actually like to go see for myself. I've never been outside. Those white coats don't let me out.
Hey, what's your name?
What a weird name—sounds like some girl's. Mine's way cooler: Synex. Now that's villain material!
Synex flicked the thing in her hand toward him. This time, he caught it. It was an oleaster berry.

speaker: Synex
content: That's your payment! Tell me more about the outside world next time, <color=#fb9259>Saffar</color>!
[Fade to black, center text]

That oleaster berry had shriveled skin and didn't taste good. Honestly, it was barely edible. But I could never forget it. After that, every time we met, Synex would bring a few of the same dried berries. At first, I assumed they were the only ones available at the research institute. Only later did I learn that she, as the facility's experimental subject with the highest resonance rate, had the privilege of choosing her own food. And yet, she deliberately picked the toughest ones.
[Scene Transition]

One oleaster berry for one story. I'm still alive, though with my low Aurum Secretum resonance, insignificance was always my fate. Meanwhile, Synex's brilliance only grew brighter. In time, she earned the right to step beyond these walls. She became a legend at the Fraser Institute, a force to be reckoned with. And so, she no longer needed my stories of the outside world.

Life went on this way. Synex would return from time to time, bringing meager snacks and hauling away trinkets and scraps in trade. One by one, the others who had entered the institute with me died. And as their numbers dwindled, so too did Synex's visits, stretching longer between each appearance. Until...
[Scene Transition: Laboratory]

speaker: Laboratory Guard
content: Damn it! Stop her! Backup! We need backup NOW—

Red warning lights strobed violently, casting jagged shadows as chaos erupted through the laboratory. With a feral snarl, Synex wrenched herself free from her shackles, the sheer force of her movement sending shockwaves ripping through the room.

A predator unleashed, she lunged onto the rubble of collapsed walls, her claws carving through the air like scythes as she descended upon the high-ranking man. Her lips were peeled back in a grotesque rictus, less a smile than a snarl of pure, unfettered madness.

speaker: Synex
content: Kill me... or... I'LL KILL YOU!!

Around her, Aurum Secretum surged in molten waves, forming an impenetrable barrier—a domain of her own making. This was not the Synex he knew. And yet, in this moment of monstrous abandon... it was as if he was seeing her for the very first time.

But she still failed. Her body crumbled like sand, piece by piece—too weak to even lift a claw toward Campbell's throat. Yet, he didn't hold it against her. Instead, he pardoned her. Drew her into the fold of the Campbells. At last, she was truly part of Fraser.
After that, Synex didn't appear for a long time. But sometimes, in the quietest moments, her voice would still whisper in my mind.

speaker: Synex
content: Is the life of your <color=#fb9259>hero</color> as worthless as a stray dog's?
[Scene Transition: Fraser Institute Exterior]
When Synex finally showed up, she brought two unwelcome visitors from DisCity with her.
DisCity origin, directly involved in the West District BR-002 incident. Affiliated with the MBCC, maintains close ties to SHP-13. A potential intelligence asset regarding the shackles.
Small and frail... yet her eyes burned with defiance. As expected, she infiltrated the institute, desperate to save Synex, only to fail.
Too weak to succeed. Too powerless to change anything.
...Just like me. We are the same.
Many came, hoping to become the next "Synex." They entered the institute, but few survived the resonance process.
They are just like me. For them, Synex's oleaster berries are an unattainable dream. This is the only lifeline within their reach. I want them to succeed. I want to help them.
After all... this is the last thing I can do.
[Black Screen Transition, Background: Fraser Institute Corridor - Day]
The young man opens his eyes.
The weight of recent days presses down like storm clouds. Forgotten memories tear through the fragile peace of his mind. Even in rare moments of stillness, they come unbidden.

speaker: Researcher
content: The DisCity Sinner has escaped, but she won't get far. We're tracking her down as we speak.

speaker: Researcher
content: You don't look well, sir... Maybe you should get some more rest?

speaker: Saffar
content: ...No, I'm good.

speaker: Saffar
content: Let's go. Time to meet our rebellious "hero."
[Background - Research Institute Dungeon]
As Saffar steps back into the research institute, the first thing to greet him is an off-key, lilting voice.

Not far away, the cocoon continues its metamorphosis. The entity inside grows more distinct by the moment, its heartbeat swelling louder. Yet the prisoner bound beneath it remains utterly unfazed, almost relaxed.
Hypatia

speaker: Synex
content: Oh...? Well, if it isn't little Saffar! These chains are practically strangling me. Be a dear and loosen them—

Synex shifts, but the chains—emerging like roots from the chamber's depths—wrench her back into place. Where the restraints bite into her flesh, cracks spiderweb across her skin, oozing a viscous fluid with a metallic gleam.

speaker: Saffar
content: You're dying.
Without another word, Saffar lifts his hand and rolls up his sleeve. The same Aurum Secretum corruption writhes on his skin, its luminous patterns mirroring hers.

speaker: Saffar
content: Aurum Secretum Warriors require regular doses to stabilize their Mania. Without it, their bodies break down at an accelerated rate. Right now, your system can't handle a full-scale insurrection. If you don't take Aurum Secretum soon, you won't survive.

speaker: Saffar
content: ...That reckless girl from DisCity is no different. She could've just run.

speaker: Synex
content: Heh... What's this? Feeling a little sympathy for her?
The young man doesn't answer, his face a mask of frost.

speaker: Synex
content: Oh, don't give me that look. Here I was, thinking we could have a nice little reunion... but I suppose you're not the sentimental type. So... let's just cut to the fun part.

speaker: Synex
content: Saffar, how about we burn it all down together?

speaker: Saffar
content: ...What?

speaker: Synex
content: Did you really think Hypercubes would be priority one after the Black Ring explodes? Fraser's first move will be marching straight for DisCity's throat. And guess who gets to be the glorious frontline sacrifices? That's right... us. Either we get fed to the Black Ring, or we get chewed up in their little war.

speaker: Synex
content: You don't want to die for nothing either, do you? So here's my offer: We blow up Fraser and the institute, and lead everyone to freedom—
Clang— Saffar's blade scrapes past Synex's shackles and bites into her throat. A thin crimson line blooms in its wake.
His hand does not waver—unnaturally steady, poised to carve deeper with the slightest shift.

speaker: Saffar
content: ...You still don't get it.

speaker: Saffar
content: You're the strongest Aurum Secretum Warrior we have. When others collapse under the weight of the world, you crush it under your feet and keep going. That's why you can't see it.

speaker: Saffar
content: What we've needed all along isn't freedom... It's the power to rewrite fate—a <color=#fb9259>hero</color>.
The Aurum Secretum shackles clink as Synex tilts her head, her laughter spilling forth, barely restrained.

speaker: Synex
content: HAHAHAHA... No way... You're actually serious?

speaker: Synex
content: I thought only brainwashed lab rats who've never smelled real air could swallow Fraser's "hero" fairytales!

speaker: Synex
content: Let's be real, what "hero" gets bred in a cage? Fattened for slaughter, then scolded for not saying "thank you" when the knife comes down? If you want to play that kind of hero, be my guest!

speaker: Saffar
content: Do you think I don't want to be one?!
Saffar raises his hand and yanks back his sleeve. His wrist is a ruin, barely held together by threads of flowing Aurum Secretum.

speaker: Saffar
content: Just one resonance nearly tore me apart... Same with that DisCity girl. Yeah, I feel sorry for her! But what else can I do?!

speaker: Saffar
content: The weak can only survive like this! None of us chose this!
He drags in a breath as if the air could steady the storm inside.

speaker: Saffar
content: Among all the test subjects... you're the only one who made it through every experiment. The only one who earned that pass. The only one who can... trigger the Black Ring, open new mines, and actually change things here.

speaker: Saffar
content: So...
He swiftly sheathes his sword.

speaker: Saffar
content: I beg you, don't throw away all those lives. Don't crush our last chance.
With those words, Saffar turns and walks away. A scornful laugh rings out behind him.

speaker: Synex
content: Coward.
He halts mid-step, spine rigid, but does not look back.

speaker: Saffar
content: ...I'm sorry.
Then he is gone. Once more, the room holds only Synex and the weight of her chains.
The shackles bite into her flesh, unyielding. Mania seethes beneath her skin, a wildfire scorching through bone and marrow.
Yet even as the agony consumes her, her lips twist into a grin. Then, laughter tears free, raw and ravenous.
[Cut to Flashback]
Death has no meaning. In this test facility, everyone dies eventually; it's only a matter of when. And only the survivors get to decide what "meaning" even is.

Once, in her agony, she looked up—high above, researchers in white coats would dispassionately observe the test subjects, watching them succumb to Mania, only uttering brief exclamations or sighs when someone either awakened or deteriorated.
Lives twisted, withered, and were reduced to scribbled notes in their records—worthless.

speaker: Director Hermis
content: Test Subject 819, <color=#fb9259>Synex</color>. You are our most exceptional specimen. It's time for you to serve our city and fulfill your purpose.
"Serve"? By giving her life away? For those who never see her as human?

speaker: Adelaide
content: You're dying. How unfortunate... Your end could have been so much more meaningful. But I can offer you a way out.
All those noble words from on high, yet in the end, they still chose to use her as a sacrifice.

speaker: Saffar
content: The weak can only survive like this! None of us chose this!

speaker: Synex
content: No... As long as one breathes, there are always choices.
She won't die here. Not like this. No matter how desperate, how ugly her struggle becomes, she will survive.
[Flashback: WhiteSands Background]
The merchant lay collapsed on the ground, his body already growing cold. She spotted the hidden envelop but left it untouched, letting the Legion find it when they arrived.
[Flashback: Furor]

Another mission complete. The enemy had fallen with resentment, their grip still clenched around an unnaturally sharp dagger. The blade hummed with whispers, a faint aura of madness clinging to its edge. Intrigued, she kept the blade for herself, never turning it in.
[Flashback: Maze Background]
She wasn't the only suitable Corpus vessel. Escaping outright had crossed her mind, but that would've been too dull. Too ordinary. What she wanted was to tear it all down.
When the girl and her companion stopped her outside the city, the gears had finally begun to turn. At last, the wildcard she'd been waiting for arrived.
[Back to Reality, Restraints CG]

speaker: Synex
content: Heheh... The prey and the hunters are all in place. This farce is just one step from its climax. Wouldn't it be such a shame to die before the grand finale?

speaker: Synex
content: This life of mine... Oh, I've got much better plans for it...
[Hypatia's Room]

speaker: Mysterious Voice
content: You should be ashamed of yourself! The Campbell name is not yours to disgrace so carelessly.

speaker: Hypatia
content: I... I am very sorry.

speaker: Mysterious Voice
content: For the next several days, you will remain at home, reflecting on your actions, and compose a thorough report on the Aurum Secretum Apostle. The Senate is eager to hear your findings. Consider this your final opportunity to redeem yourself.

speaker: Mysterious Voice
content: Hypatia... You are this family's most treasured daughter. Do not disappoint us.

speaker: Hypatia
content: I will heed your counsel with the utmost respect.
After ending the internal comms, Hypatia exhales sharply and sags against her desk, the weight of exhaustion pressing down on her.
Yesterday's infiltration could hardly be called a success, yet it wasn't a complete failure, either. The guards had arrived late enough for her to skim nearly every classified file.
She draws another steadying breath, recalling the keywords she has hastily glimpsed. Just the thought of them sends an involuntary tremor through her fingers.
The Underground, inheritance... trans-calamity communications, Project BR-005... Deliberate detonation of a Black Ring within Fraser... creation of Fraser's own Hypercube mines...
Each line is more horrifying than the last. The scale of the sacrifice—how many lives would it consume?

She had only ever known these technologies in fragments, isolated pieces of a puzzle she never imagined would form something this monstrous. A conspiracy vast enough to swallow the entire farlands whole.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Now the question is... how to get this information out...

The Aurum Secretum she carries has been completely confiscated. All communication signals are blocked—she's permitted only the internal telephone. Under house arrest, she is nearly severed from the outside world.

speaker: Hypatia
content: But there aren't many guards... An oversight? Do they assume I've no will to escape?
Indeed, the Hypatia of old would never have defied her family. Yet now, the thought lingers—who planted it there? What would she do in this situation?

In the blind spot of surveillance, she slides the chip from her palm to her wrist, tucking it into her sleeve. As she sits, her fingers brush the desk's edge, retrieving a communicator wedged deep in the crack.
A moment later, Hypatia stands up and picks up the internal telephone again.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Hello, could you please connect me to Miss Jacqueline Schneider? This is Hypatia Campbell calling.

speaker: Hypatia
content: I'm inquiring about her civilian Aurum Secretum project. If she's available, I'd appreciate a moment of her time today.
[Manor Exterior]
Shortly after, a sleek silver-white sports car drives through the gates of Campbell Manor.

speaker: Jacqueline
content: Hypatia! I rushed over the second I got your message. Oh, and just look at this car. Absolutely stunning, don't you think?

speaker: Hypatia
content: It's an exquisite design. The exterior alone makes quite a statement.

speaker: Jacqueline
content: It's our newest model. The official launch isn't even until next month! You know how my family's always dreamed of working some Aurum Secretum magic into our designs.

speaker: Jacqueline
content: But the Senate guards that technology like dragons hoarding gold. We minor nobles might as well be asking for the moon! So here I am, turning to an old classmate for help!

speaker: Hypatia
content: Hehe, the Institute has recently initiated a limited technology transfer program, an effort to collaborate with noble houses on certain... specialized breakthroughs. Naturally, you were the first person who came to mind.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Well then, shall we continue this conversation inside? You may leave the car here.
Several dozen minutes later.
A shadowy figure crouches low, slinking toward the sleek sports car. A key—the key, rightfully belonging to the car's owner—slides into the ignition.
The door swings open. Hypatia slips inside, adjusts the seat with practiced ease, and scans the controls. Her fingers tighten around the steering wheel. A slow, steadying breath. Then—
BOOM!

speaker: Manor Guard
content: Damn it, what's going on with that car... Hey, stop her!
With the accelerator floored, the silver beast rockets forward, tires screeching as it blasts through the manor gates.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Forgive me, Jacqueline... I promise I'll make time to help you with that technology sharing later. But just this once, let me borrow your car for one day!
The wheel jerks hard right. The sports car obeys without hesitation, roaring away from Fraser City.

speaker: Hypatia
content: The jamming should stop here. Please, you have to answer me, Hella!
[Hella's Dream]
Consciousness drifts in the darkness.

Trapped in an endless nightmare, she watches the Black Ring bleed into existence once again. That jagged halo of crimson once swallowed the sky above Syndicate, leaving her loved ones torn apart, while she was too weak to save them.
[Flashback: Rustfire CG and Dialogue]
Emotions long buried surge forth like a tide of blackened sludge, dragging her down, drowning her in the depths of her own dread.
The fear, the crushing helplessness—they never truly left. She had only locked them away, buried them where they festered.

speaker: Hella
content: The Black Ring's gonna blow any second. That idiot threw herself in just to get me out... I can't stop it now, but someone's gotta know what's happening! I have to do something... What else can I do now?

speaker: Hella
content: Come on, stupid brain, work!! Everyone's gonna die if you don't figure this out!!
She wants to become stronger. She must. Because...

speaker: Girl's Voice
content: I understand. I'll wait for you to become stronger, for you to come back...

speaker: Girl's Voice
content: Hella, that's a promise.

speaker: Hella
content: ...${PlayerName}, Hecate, Ninety-Nine...

speaker: Hella
content: Without you guys here... "becoming stronger" feels so impossible...

speaker: Hella
content: There's just... so much I can't handle alone. No matter how hard I push myself, no matter how strong I get... some things just don't work out. Some people... I just can't save.

speaker: Hella
content: ...Feels like I'm the only one who's still this useless... who can't do anything...
Bang!
As if a hard kick landed on her rear, her anger and frustration are instantly booted away, replaced by that infuriating, ever-grinning voice in her ear.

speaker: Synex
content: Silly, you said you had to play hero all by yourself? Ever considered ganging up on your enemies?

speaker: Synex
content: I've left you all the goodies I've been stashing away. Make sure they don't go to waste, okay?
[Waking Up] [Refugee Camp - Overcast]

June 24, N.F. 115
1:56 PM
Refugee Settlement, Outside the Aurum Secretum Institute

speaker: Horo
content: Hella? You finally woke up!
The world slowly sharpens into focus as two worried faces hover above her.

speaker: Hella
content: ...Horo? When did you get out... No, wait, how long has it been? I—
Then, the pain crashes in. Every muscle screams in protest, her wounds burn as if seared by fire, and her throat is so parched it cracks when she tries to speak.

speaker: Thani
content: Careful! ...Does it still hurt? When I found you, you were burning up all over! Your throat must feel all scratchy and dry...

speaker: Thani
content: Wait here, I'll go get some more water.
Thani rises and leaves. Hella coughs, her gaze drifting over her surroundings—she's lying in a tent in the refugee camp, wrapped in what seems to be the tent's only blanket.

speaker: Horo
content: The contamination in your body is bad. Just stay down, and don't try to move. Whatever's going on, it can wait.
A scorching hand seizes Horo's arm. Hella's voice is raw, barely more than a whisper, yet she grits her teeth and speaks.

speaker: Hella
content: I have... have to tell you now...

speaker: Hella
content: At the center of the maze, the danger Synex mentioned... Horo, you were right...

speaker: Hella
content: I saw the inheritance. They're going to set off a Black Ring! Synex is ground zero. They're dragging everyone down with them!!
[Change Perspective: Outside Refugee Camp]

The sky hangs heavy with clouds. Without warning, a squad of guards bursts into the refugee camp. The refugees shrink back, pressing into the shadows, their hushed whispers laced with surprise and confusion.

speaker: Uriel
content: The screening officers? But they were just here yesterday...

speaker: Institute Guard
content: You there, where are the Furorians who arrived recently?
The visitors clearly mean trouble. Uriel tenses, but his voice stays steady, testing the waters with careful words.

speaker: Uriel
content: Furorians? Didn't they get taken to the institute their first day here...? Who are you looking for, exactly?

speaker: Institute Guard
content: This is an order from above! Two DisCity people were hiding among the refugees, and now they're gone. You see them, you report them immediately. No hiding fugitives, got it?
Chaos erupts. Behind the clamoring crowd, a figure slips through the shadows, quickly darting in the opposite direction.
[Perspective shifts back to Hella]

speaker: Thani
content: How could this happen? Then... does that mean everyone who got picked before is...

speaker: Hella
content: I tried to stop them, but I was too weak... Synex was the one who threw me out...

speaker: Hella
content: We're running out of time! We have to move... now!
The wounds Mania carved into her refuse to heal, their pain a constant tremor in her muscles. Another wave of dizziness crashes over her, but Hella grits her teeth and forces herself to stay upright.

speaker: Hella
content: ...I'm so useless.

speaker: Hella
content: I said I'd get stronger. Left MBCC to prove I could handle the real world... but look at me. Still just a screw-up...

speaker: Hella
content: All I do is run my mouth. "Rat Queen of Syndicate"? Heh, just a dumb title to make dumbasses think I'm scary. But when it actually mattered? Got my ass handed to me, like always...

speaker: Hella
content: Synex is still trapped with those freaks... and if they set off the Black Ring, it'll be... just like last time...
A soft pat brushes Hella's back, then the scratchy warmth of the blanket settles over her. It's Horo. With surprising tenderness, she guides Hella down, cocooning her in layers of fabric.

speaker: Horo
content: Hey... take it easy. Stay down and just listen for a sec.

speaker: Horo
content: After we got separated, we were stuck in that damn maze. Couldn't reach you, couldn't find an exit.

speaker: Horo
content: But at least the enemy numbers didn't keep piling up. Then, a few hours ago, some kind of disturbance hit... and most of the maze just collapsed. That's when I saw you staggering out of the wreckage...
Through the haze of fever and fabric, Hella feels arms wrap around her—steady and gentle. Horo's voice reaches her, muffled and distant, words dissolving in the fog of her mind.

speaker: Horo
content: ...This isn't your fault. We're the ones who came too late.

speaker: Horo
content: Charging in alone to dig up the truth? That took real guts. You're already braver than most.

Hella curls tighter, fingers clutching the blankets as a sob tears free. The thick layers swallow the sound, but her shoulders shake anyway. Horo's hand moves in slow circles on her back, a silent pact to ignore the tears.
But the moment of peace doesn't last long. Commotion erupts outside, and the tent flap whips open with a violent snap as someone stumbles inside.

speaker: Sandra
content: —They're here! The institute's sweeping the camp, and they'll get here any minute. You need to go, now!

Sure enough, the commotion draws closer. There's no time to wait for her wounds to heal; they have to move now. Hella feels the blankets tighten around her as strong hands haul her upright, urgency in every motion.

speaker: Sandra
content: Thani told me you got into the institute...
A voice thick with suppressed emotion reaches her ears. It takes Hella several seconds to register who's speaking.

speaker: Sandra
content: Did you see my boy?

speaker: Sandra
content: Is he... still alive?
[Flashback: Small CG - Small Alchemic Beast]
...Mo... Mom?
[Back to Reality]
Of course she saw him. But Hella doesn't know how to answer this desperate mother.

speaker: Hella
content: ...I saw him. At the institute.

speaker: Hella
content: He... told me the Fraser people are researching something really, really dangerous. The whole screening process and the Aurum Secretum are all just a front. Everyone they drag into that facility... they're just... sacrifices. For them to get Hypercubes...
Her throat tight and dry, Hella forces out the words she must say.

speaker: Hella
content: And then he... he insisted on staying behind. Said he has to keep fighting those bastards. So...s...

speaker: Hella
content: ...He's not coming back. Not yet.
The woman's grip tightens on Hella's arm, hard enough to border on pain. Her voice trembles.

speaker: Sandra
content: Thank you... Right, he's always so brave, so kind... I...

speaker: Sandra
content: Sob...
The back of Hella's hand grows damp with tears. In this moment, any comfort feels hollow.
The clamor draws nearer, but the figure ahead halts abruptly.
Without anyone noticing, a crowd of refugees has gathered at the entrance. Their eyes lock onto the DisCity interlopers inside the tent, faces unreadable.

speaker: Horo
content: Damn it...!

As time slips away, she can already hear the guards' shouts edging closer. There's no time to explain everything to the refugees. Should she force her way through? Horo's hand reaches back toward her weapon, but she stalls, gripped by hesitation.
Someone makes the first move.
A refugee sheds their cloak, flinging it over Hella and Horo. Others surge forward, swallowing them into the crowd as it funnels toward the camp's exit.
Hella jerks her head up in surprise, only to find a pale and strained face. Sandra offers her a thin, forced smile.

speaker: Sandra
content: You helped our family in Furor. That makes you our friend.

speaker: Sandra
content: Let's go. I'll help you get out of here.
[WhiteSands, Sunset]

June 24, N.F. 115
3:02 PM

Vicinity of the Aurum Secretum Institute, Farlands

Beyond Fraser City's limits, the Legion convoy has pitched a temporary camp on the windswept dunes. Horo stands in a corner, sheltered from the wind. A howling gale reaches her ears through the communicator—someone's pushing the vehicle too hard.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...Thank goodness, I finally got through to you.

speaker: Horo
content: Sounds like you're dealing with quite a bit of trouble yourself.
The screen flares abruptly, casting a pale glow across her face as a file unfolds before her, its dense text materializing in the air.

speaker: Hypatia
content: To cut to the chase, I've uncovered information on the Black Ring project and the "inheritance."

In N.F. 90, the Senate passed a resolution to widely accept refugees displaced by calamities and war, alongside the launch of a candidate screening initiative. By N.F. 106, the Farland Alliance had formalized a friendship treaty with DisCity. Concurrently, the Fraser Aurum Secretum Research Institute pivoted its research focus to the Black Ring domain, strategically redirecting refugee flows toward remote research outposts established beyond the city's borders.

In N.F. 113, BR-002 in DisCity was successfully suppressed, leading to the formation of a new mine. During this period, Campbell forged clandestine ties with the Underground to relocate the "inheritance" to Fraser. The institute commenced contact experiments, and its previously stagnant Aurum Secretum research rapidly yielded breakthroughs. As the Aurum Secretum Institute's advancements accelerated, Project BR-005 was officially greenlit to amass sufficient military strength to subjugate DisCity.
But a Black Ring alone isn't enough. They want the means to control it—Shepherd ${PlayerName}.

In N.F. 115, Fraser proceeds with its plan to have DisCity host the 13th Great Expo. The head of the Campbell family will personally travel to DisCity in an attempt to capture Shepherd SHP-13 and eliminate the threat.
That's why my brother went to DisCity... I should have realized it sooner...

speaker: Hypatia
content: Project BR-005 is very much real. They've prepared two explosion sites: one beneath Furor, and the other at the Aurum Secretum Research Institute.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Synex... she will become the Corpseborne. But if she fails, their contingency is far more monstrous. They intend to sacrifice the countless refugees near the institute... along with the Apostle of Ashes from Furor, all to trigger the Black Ring!

speaker: Hypatia
content: Merely stopping the Corpus reception won't suffice. To truly end this, we must also destroy the "inheritance."

After a quick scan of the documents, Horo clicks her tongue in dismay. The enemy's meticulous planning spans years, while her side boasts only a handful of trained fighters—the rest are last-minute conscripts barely worthy of being called a militia.

speaker: Horo
