content: Correction: I hope you can find more reassurance in a safe location.

speaker: Schorl
content: The Black Ring has become a weapon of war, Chief. This makes you, someone who can suppress it, a strategic asset of the highest value. It is for this exact reason that the enemy targeted you with that trap, to limit your mobility. Going forward, we cannot permit you to be exposed to further unnecessary risk.

speaker: Schorl
content: And there is no cause for alarm. The situation still remains within projected parameters. EDGE contingency plans for this exact form of warfare have long been in place. Current events are proceeding within expected outcomes. It will be resolved.

speaker: Option
options: That's not the impression I got from the meeting.

content: Schorl's silence descends at the opportune moment.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...And I can't let anything happen to Hella. I can't just sit back safe and sound while she's still out there.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So if you really want me out of danger, then do something about it. Find that Black Ring. Destroy it. Get Hella back.

speaker: Schorl
content: But the two of you are not even remotely comparable in value.

In a fit of frustration, you grab the nearby report and swat Schorl with it. It's deeply unsatisfying—the black triangle just whirls in place like a disoriented top before steadying itself, utterly unfazed. Its scanning beam immediately locks back onto you.

speaker: Schorl
content: Your current condition is unstable. It is acceptable to direct your frustrations toward me, but I must advise against agitating yourself to the point of self-harm. I will amend my previous statement:

speaker: Schorl
content: Appropriate resources are being diverted to locate your friend. Given the delicate diplomatic climate, permitting <color=#fb9259>that unit</color> to participate in operations—even covertly—is a significant accommodation of your request. This action is not without its own risks, which we have accepted to provide support.

speaker: Schorl
content: Remember Sinner <color=#fb9259>Jasmine</color>? She possesses exceptional resistance to the side effects of wielding that "Rancor." After experimentation at the Ring Research Institute, the resulting technology has been discreetly transferred to Nirvana Port. That unit is now better equipped to control those weapons, as you wished.
Another moment of deathly stillness falls.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Your language module is completely screwed since the reboot. Just stop. I don't need your emotional support. Just cut the crap and stick to your "pragmatic" war logic.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You said it yourself—BR-005 is an anomaly, and so is Hella's situation. Your Observatorium is useless now. She and the shackles are your only real lead for intel. You'd better be praying she's still alive, because let's be honest... there's been no trace of BR-005, has there?

speaker: Schorl
content: ...A remarkably logical conclusion. I must admit, it is reassuring to see you analyzing the situation with such clarity.
Just as you're about to dismiss it, you receive a message.
Scored a big win? Come on, let's celebrate.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Can I still go out? Within the city's "safe zone."

speaker: Schorl
content: Of course. Your mobility is permitted, provided the individual you intend to meet is deemed secure and trustworthy, or if you would allow a security detail to be notified and accompany you. After all, I have no intention to impede your freedom or be a source of your displeasure.

speaker: Schorl
content: What do you think, Chief?
You look at the message on your terminal. The sender is anonymous, yet the identity is clear to you both. Schorl waits for your answer.

speaker: Schorl
content: A prudent choice. If your trust in the other party is not absolute, then I will ensure your safety during this "appointment."
[Scene Change] MBCC Exterior

With Schorl's "discreet" help, you leave the Bureau unnoticed. Outside, night has fallen prematurely. The distant, howling Tide of Ashes seems to whip the city with a grating wind, scouring the sky of its final light. The evening air carries a distinct chill.
You spot someone waiting for you by the roadside.
[CG] Driving Scene
A familiar sight, though she's switched to yet another luxury car.

speaker: Catherine
content: I was hoping to see you in something sharp today, and you're still wearing that? I got you those new clothes to wear, not to collect dust.
female_content: I was hoping to see you in something smart today, and you're still wearing that? I got you those new clothes to wear, not to collect dust.

speaker: Catherine
content: Does MBCC think "austerity" is a fashion statement? Don't they pay you anything?
She takes off her glasses to examine you carefully.

speaker: Catherine
content: What's with the face? Should be riding high after a win like that. Did the old fogies give you static?

speaker: Catherine
content: Get in. You look like you could use another drive to clear your head.
She smiles, slipping her sunglasses from her face onto yours before turning her gaze to the black triangle hovering at your side.

speaker: Catherine
content: And I don't mind having a third wheel along.
That's Catherine. She once took you on a joyride like this during the Great Expo. You thought little of it then, but now... now everything has changed.
Perhaps you should now refer to her by her true title—
Commander of the Nirvana Port troop, General of the 8th DisCorps Division, <color=#fb9259>Augustus</color>.
[Enter Flashback]

speaker: Schorl
content: Augustus has executed multiple assaults on the FAC, including direct attacks on our two Commanders-in-Chief. That woman possesses dangerous capabilities, commands a radical faction, and has demonstrated no loyalty to our city-state. Public recognition by DisCity is, therefore, an impossibility.

speaker: Schorl
content: If you are considering collaboration with her... Chief, I must strongly advise utmost caution.
[Exit Flashback]

The squad advances along the route of the attacked FAC Ash Outpost, destroying several more Aurum Secretum devices along the way. As they do, the sandstorm visibly begins to shift direction, retreating from FAC's defensive line and reverting to its previously predictable trajectory.

Perhaps that acting commander was right. This Tide of Ashes is no ordinary calamity—it's a weapon, engineered by the farland enemy. To neutralize it, they have to find and destroy the Aurum Secretum devices that can "resonate with the Apostles."
Suddenly, the squad's most perceptive soldier catches a hint of movement within the swirling sand. He stops dead, raising his binoculars to get a better look.

speaker: Scarface
content: There they are! So when do we get to wipe 'em out? What's the holdup? Wire Girl picked up anything yet? Our new commander still off taking a nap?

speaker: Scarface
content: Man, don't tell me the commander kicked the bucket screaming orders yesterday. If he doesn't get his act together, there's not gonna be a forward FAC outpost left to save!
female_content: Man, don't tell me the commander kicked the bucket screaming orders yesterday. If she doesn't get her act together, there's not gonna be a forward FAC outpost left to save!

speaker: Scarface
content: Ah, who am I kidding? Let 'em drop! More corpses just mean more juice for my cannon. Makes shredding those Outland mutts even sweeter!

speaker: Military Doctor
content: You're getting a bit loud there, Scar.

speaker: Scarface
content: Ooh, are we having a lesson? Right before a fight? I love it—Ouch!
The doctor kicks his weapon away and sedates him with a shot to the hip, finally quieting him down.
The lieutenant takes the communicator.

speaker: Lieutenant
content: Broken Blade Squad 3 to Command.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Minos here. What's your status?

speaker: Lieutenant
content: The Mania field is volatile. The landscape has shifted and our way forward is blocked. Our original position is no longer tenable.

speaker: Lieutenant
content: Chief, you have more intel than we do. What's your read on the situation?

speaker: Scarface
content: What the hell is this?! They just keep coming back for more! What are these things made of?! Someone tell them the party's over!

speaker: Military Doctor
content: Wait... something's off...
As the sandstorm fades, the world sharpens into view. In the distance, Siglinde can just make out the raised dunes, their forms subtly writhing against the clearing sky.

speaker: Military Doctor
content: This is...!!

speaker: Military Doctor
content: Everyone spread out! Take cover!!

speaker: Scarface
content: Urgh—!
The desert floor gives way without warning—or rather, it splits apart like a gaping mouth, devouring everything above it.
Siglinde activates an electromagnetic shield. While the squad escaped harm thanks to her alert, the comms device linking them to ${PlayerName} is dragged down into the quicksand.

speaker: Siglinde
content: ...We shouldn't lose communication like this on the battlefield. It's unprofessional to leave Command in the dark and make them worry.
As she speaks, she gets to her feet, dusting the sand from her uniform.
Then, along the arched crest of a dune bordering the vast sinkhole, she spots two figures.

speaker: Synex
content: Oops, our little secret operation's busted. So, boss—what's the plan for us lowly grunts?

speaker: Synex
content: Shall we make these problems disappear? Or can I pretty please choose the "run away" option?
Her companion, however, is already prepared, a weapon summoned forth. Resonating with the Aurum Secretum, an Ash Crystal heeds the Sinner's call, its core radiating a malevolent glow.

speaker: A.S. Warrior
content: ...Of course we wipe them out.

The Apostles' roar echoes in the distance. A new dust storm erupts, and within it, the Aurum Secretum Warrior vanishes. She charges through the swirling gloom, a specter hurtling toward the city-state she despises, and toward its rabid hounds—

speaker: Siglinde
content: Sinners wielding Aurum Secretum... are they Outlands elites? Though, judging by their reaction, it seems we've surprised each other. A fortunate coincidence, to be sure...

speaker: Siglinde
content: Looks like the campaign's first victory will be ours.
[Scene Change] Any Magnificent Hall
You listen intently, but the communicator offers only silence. Has the team lost contact? Did you send them down the wrong path? Is their sacrifice on your hands?
You need to go back. You have to—
Hey, focus.

The urgent thought shatters. You are pulled back into the shimmering glow of the ballroom, the soft strains of the waltz, and the captivating presence of the female general in crimson standing before you.
Catherine keeps one hand in yours, the other resting lightly on your shoulder. Her gaze holds a mixture of mild reproach and amusement.
female_content: Catherine keeps one hand in yours, the other resting lightly on your waist. Her gaze holds a mixture of mild reproach and amusement.

speaker: Catherine
content: That's not even your unit. If I'm not worried, my advisor, you shouldn't be. Your only job right now is to dance.
As she speaks, she deftly twists her wrist, guiding you through a partial turn to avoid a collision before sweeping you back to the center of the floor in one elegant arc.

speaker: Catherine
content: My people are strong. If I say they'll win, they will win. Consider this a victory celebration in advance.

speaker: Catherine
content: Or... do you have a problem with your partner?
Of course not. A quick glance around tells you everything: people are either mocking those fashionable sunglasses you're wearing or envying your luck for being with such a beautiful woman.

speaker: Catherine
content: That'll do. Now, follow my lead. You workaholics never know how to handle these parties, do you? Watch and learn.

You step forward under her guidance. Her hand rests on your shoulder, her face turned to yours. The scent of her perfume—a rich bloom mingled with temple incense—wafts under your nose, and her hair whispers against your cheek.
female_content: You step forward under her guidance. Her hand rests on your waist, her face turned to yours. The scent of her perfume—a rich bloom mingled with temple incense—wafts under your nose, and her hair whispers against your cheek.

content: Yet your thoughts are still far from here. With every turn she leads you through, the surrounding conversations slice through the music, pulling your attention, fragment by fragment.

speaker: Crowd A
content: Fraser has issued an urgent announcement calling for peace... but have you heard the real story? They're saying the farlands engineered these Tides of Ashes. My God, what are they even capable of now? I should've moved my assets earlier...

speaker: Crowd B
content: And what are our diplomats doing? Absolutely nothing! The shipping lanes are a mess, and I can't even get goods to the satellite towns. You know what that is? It's me, losing money. Every. Single. Day.

speaker: Crowd C
content: Really? My Eastian immigration consultancy is booming. Looking for a new investment opportunity?

speaker: Crowd A
content: Immigration? Can anyone even get out anymore? I heard that ghost unit is back at WhiteSands... yeah, DisCorps... This damned war...

Tomorrow, the city-state council will once again vote on the Wartime Emergency Resolution. And so today, philanthropists, socialites, councilors, magnates, and intellectuals have gathered here under the guise of a "ball" to exchange intelligence and form alliances.

—Yes, this is an "anti-war" gathering, and most of those present are Augustus's "enemies." Yet none of them recognize this mysterious general, who seems solely devoted to indulging in the evening's lavish pleasures.
To the rhythm of the carefree music, she pivots, using your frame for balance. The motion brings her face to yours, and your gazes lock.

speaker: Option
options: Is this your kind of scene?

speaker: Catherine
content: Better than chasing game through some manor's grounds. After the non-stop action, a night of elegance—even if it's put on—is a good change. Lets you play dress-up and listen to these aristocrats' sheltered little jokes.

speaker: Catherine
content: Call it a decadent upper-class hobby. You should try it. Could be a fun distraction.
[Enter Flashback] MBCC

speaker: Elvira
content: I know about the Andohars. Their entire wealth was built on arms dealing. They were a major factor in the last stages of the Independence War and the development of the satellite towns.

speaker: Elvira
content: I heard they weren't originally allies with DisCity; they primarily armed the metropoles. They only established ties with DisCity once the independence forces started to win, so they profited from both sides.

speaker: Elvira
content: They're not as powerful now. What's an arms dealer without an army, after all? But they're still everywhere in high society. I guess war really is good for business.
[Exit Flashback]

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I still have contamination on me. If I lose control, it could cause serious trouble.

speaker: Catherine
content: Haha, you're worried about causing trouble? Even if you did, no one would dare touch you. I promise.
[Enter Flashback] Phone Call

speaker: Max King
content: The draft resolution is facing considerable opposition. On the surface, it's certain Eastside factions trying to limit the FAC's authority. But what concerns me is that the FAC itself opposes several clauses. That's... strange.

speaker: Max King
content: They're clearly afraid of something else...
[Exit Flashback]
Lost in thought, your foot comes down on your partner's toes—for the sixth time. A breathy laugh escapes her as her hand gives your shoulder a gentle squeeze.
female_content: Lost in thought, your foot comes down on your partner's toes—for the sixth time. A breathy laugh escapes her as her hand presses slightly against your waist.

speaker: Catherine
content: Hey, relax. You're wound way too tight. No one here knows the Chief of MBCC is working with us. FAC and the 9th Agency aren't gonna talk.

speaker: Catherine
content: To this city, you're still the hero who quelled the rebellion at the Great Expo. The last thing they want is anyone finding out we're working together.
The music happens to slow down.
And you no longer feel the need to hide your true thoughts.

speaker: Option
options: But you seem like you want people to notice.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Our deal was for the battlefield—hunting the Black Ring, hitting the Outlands. It was supposed to be quiet. So why drop my name to get me here? What's your game?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Is this about sizing up your opposition? The ones blocking the mobilization order. The future obstacles. Don't insult me by pretending this is just a party.

speaker: Catherine
content: I was thinking... this is a good piece, and you're not a terrible dancer. Would've been a nice dance to finish.

speaker: Catherine
content: Pity you're not actually here to enjoy it.

speaker: Catherine
content: If you're not interested, just let go of my hand and get back to your MBCC. You can have the car you came in. The black triangle knows how to drive it. It'll take you back home.

speaker: Catherine
content: Don't force it. I don't need reluctant partners.
As she speaks, her grip on your hand loosens, a silent promise to let go.
As the music's final notes fill the room, the dance floor stirs back to life. You take the lead, guiding her through the final turn, finally in sync with her steps.
female_content: As the music's final notes fill the room, the dance floor stirs back to life. Your hand moves from her shoulder to her waist as you take the lead, guiding her through the final turn. This time, you don't miss a single step.

content: Until the music ends.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm not opposed to bending the rules. Frankly, I could use a little "extra" help myself. But this partnership only works if we're straight with each other. No more games.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I've got my own war to fight, General. I'm not just another asset for you to deploy. Is that satisfying enough for you?
She looks at you, and a smile spreads across her face.

speaker: Catherine
content: ...Not a bad lead. I'm satisfied. The floor's all yours—enjoy the rest of the ball.

speaker: Catherine
content: Just don't overthink it. Your first and foremost job tonight is to unwind. Which means this...

With a sweet smile, she casually plucks the sunglasses from your face—the very pair she gave you, along with the communication device. She simply walks away, taking your only terminal for messages from Broken Blade Squad 3 with her.

speaker: Catherine
content: ...is going back where it belongs.
Without your sunglasses, you're quickly recognized by the people around you.

speaker: Crowd A
content: Ah, if it isn't the Chief of MBCC! I knew you were a person of justice, a real peacemaker! Please, come join us!
Catherine's hand slips from yours. Her smile is the last thing you see before she is swallowed by the bustling throng on the dance floor, leaving you suddenly alone.
Over an hour later...
After several rounds of "exchanges," you've taken the measure of the ball's attendees.
Their motivations are a predictable mix: fear of financial cost, anxiety over lost business, and sheer political vendetta. You find yourself constantly courted and led back to the dance floor.

Meanwhile, some self-proclaimed activists organize anti-war protests while secretly plotting violence against public facilities, particularly FAC installations. Others simply avoid your gaze. You commit several suspicious faces to memory for a later report to the 9th Agency.
It's time to leave. The spectacle is becoming unbearable. Though you genuinely despise war, here the word "peace" is like a clay statue slathered in thick makeup—sticky, hollow, and nauseating.
The cognitive dissonance is suffocating. You excuse yourself to the restroom, splashing cold water on your face in a desperate bid for a moment of clarity.
And then, as you step out, you are cornered once more.

speaker: Anti-War Activist
content: Chief ${PlayerName}? I work over at the Council. I was hoping to ask you about the recent raid on Euphoria.

speaker: Anti-War Activist
content: I heard you were one of the people who organized the whole operation—that you were even on the front lines. But... the Sinners from MBCC are all contaminated; they can't fight. And the FAC, they don't get involved in police actions like that.

speaker: Anti-War Activist
content: So... who did you take with you? It wasn't... it wasn't those Nirvana rebels from WhiteSands, was it?
You become high on alert.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Every last one of them at Euphoria was a traitor. If you have a problem with that, take it up with the 9th Agency. Unless you're afraid to. What's the matter? You got friends there?

speaker: Anti-War Activist
content: No, no, I have nothing to do with that shadowy group! And anyway, the 9th Agency's been investigating them inside and out. There's no way the Sillage Society would dare make a move right now. You have to believe me!

speaker: Anti-War Activist
content: I'm just... I'm worried about you. I think you've been marked by warmongers. Please, please be careful.
You turn back, and that look is all the encouragement he needs.

speaker: Anti-War Activist
content: The military clique back then... they were all ambitious. Brutal. They'd always believed in rule through force. After they seized power, they brought nothing but suffering to the city-state. For twelve years.

speaker: Anti-War Activist
content: My family lived through that, persecuted by them. I haven't forgotten... I can't.

speaker: Anti-War Activist
content: Back then, DisCity expanded through bloody campaigns abroad while tightening its grip at home. They'd start wars to distract from their failures. Violence was always their answer.

speaker: Anti-War Activist
content: It took everything we had to correct those mistakes. To overthrow them, drive out those dangerous elements...

speaker: Anti-War Activist
content: But they never really left. They never disbanded. They're still drifting through WhiteSands like ghosts... It just proves they haven't given up. They're waiting—waiting for a chance to reclaim power...

speaker: Anti-War Activist
content: I've heard they have a new leader now. Last year, they forced their way into the FAC. And now... now they're using you. For what, I don't even know.
[Enter Flashback]

speaker: Catherine
content: You want to launch a full-scale rescue for a little subordinate of yours? Sure, I'll do it. Frankly, you won't find anyone else crazy enough to say yes.

speaker: Catherine
content: Don't hold it against them. A real war costs a fortune, and a B-Class Sinner like her is just not worth that price tag. Not to mention, you're going in blind. It's a terrible plan.

speaker: Catherine
content: But you? You're worth the gamble. I believe in investing in people who have potential.

speaker: Catherine
content: You'll return the favor someday, won't you?
[Exit Flashback]

speaker: Anti-War Activist
content: Chief, don't trust them. However this plays out. You can't let them take control of DisCity again. They're—

His face is a mask of worry, his words dipped in earnestness. Yet, a sliver of doubt remains. In these treacherous times, even the hands of your so-called collaborator feel perilously close to your back.
In the end, only one thing is certain...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I don't have any comment on the mobilization order. Everything I do serves one purpose. Peace or war—I'll walk whichever path gets me closer to my goal. Nothing else matters to me.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm not the ally you're looking for. There are other things I need to handle. Good day.

speaker: Anti-War Activist
content: Chief ${PlayerName}!
You shrink from his presence and walk down the corridor. But as you look up, the passage melts away, depositing you back into the overwhelming swirl of the ballroom.
Is it the stirring of your shackles that sharpens your senses? The chaotic din of the crowd, once a dull roar, now crashes upon you—each laugh, each whisper, a razor-sharp provocation.

speaker: Crowd B
content: You know, if that incident at the Great Expo never happened... we wouldn't be in this mess. Sometimes I wonder, was that the old military's doing? Is that why Fraser's peace talks keep failing...?

speaker: Crowd B
content: And this resolution we're voting on... You think those war hawks engineered this, too?

speaker: Nirvana Representative
content: Don't even get me started... The demand for Hypercubes is already stretching our production to its absolute limit. And now the Speaker expects us to play nice and make concessions to the West District?

speaker: Nirvana Representative
content: That man parlayed a single Expo incident into a reputation, and now it's gone straight to his head.

Are they discussing peace? Certainly. They speak of averting war—and like you, they profess a hatred for conflict. Yet, a subtle dissonance begins to weave through the conversation, humming just beneath their words.

speaker: Crowd A
content: The vote is just a few days away... And you know, that MBCC Chief! What if we could get him to influence Speaker King? Maybe even sit directly at the negotiating table.
female_content: The vote is just a few days away... And you know, that MBCC Chief! What if we could get her to influence Speaker King? Maybe even sit directly at the negotiating table.

speaker: Crowd A
content: Think about it, he's the hero who fought the Black Rings. Fraser could broker an introduction to the Farland Alliance. And we pitch it as a joint operation: we help them suppress the Black Ring, and in return... we get access to new mining territories. We can develop the resources together. Peacefully.
female_content: Think about it, she's the hero who fought the Black Rings. Fraser could broker an introduction to the Farland Alliance. And we pitch it as a joint operation: we help them suppress the Black Ring, and in return... we get access to new mining territories. We can develop the resources together. Peacefully.

speaker: Crowd A
content: See? Every crisis is just an opportunity in disguise...
A wave of nausea washes over you, blurring your vision. Is BR-005 acting up? You push to your feet, scanning the glittering room for Catherine.

You need to find her. To tell her your work is done, that she must honor her promise to take you back to the battlefield. Hella is still out there, somewhere beyond your sight, and every second in this gilded cage is a second too long.

Several people spot you, reaching out with polished smiles to take your arm. Their unwanted touch is a trigger. Something primal and hungry stirs beneath your skin, straining to pierce through the surface.
(use an onomatopoeia word here)
And in that exact moment, a piercing Mania alarm shreds the air, sending waves of fear through the crowd.

speaker: Crowd B
content: Mania contamination? Or robbers?

speaker: Crowd B
content: What? The alarm system malfunctioned? Seriously, how could they mess up like—
You freeze. Could the Mania outbreak... be because of you? Did you lose control of your emotions again?

speaker: Schorl
content: It was me, Chief. I infiltrated the Mania detection system here and made some minor tweaks.
The pocket on your chest vibrates slightly. It's Schorl.

speaker: Schorl
content: Your Mania levels have spiked beyond the safety parameters. I'm afraid you can't stay here any longer. And before you worry, the cause may not be emotional.

speaker: Schorl
content: I'm detecting an anomaly from the WhiteSands front line. The source could be an issue with BR-005. You should return to investigate. I believe you'd prefer that, anyway.

speaker: Schorl
content: I will inform General Augustus that you received an urgent recall to MBCC. There's no need for anyone to know about this.
You force your head up. On the second-floor balcony, a woman's gaze meets yours. She offers a faint smile and raises her wine glass in a silent toast—her expression clearly saying "you've got this."

She seems utterly indifferent to the fate of her frontline troops. Swathed in elegance and savoring fine wine, her relaxed, carefree demeanor is indistinguishable from the other high-society guests at this grotesque gala.
Another wave of nausea washes over you. You have to look away.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'll let you deal with the report to her. I need to get out of here and check in with the front line, ASAP.
Meanwhile, at the Ashes Frontline you've been worried about—
[Battlefield]

Though the Apostles roar and storms rage, even the wild laughter of the Aurum Secretum Sinner cannot drive back the DisCorps soldiers, who hold their ground behind cover, their eyes fixed on the distant horizon.

speaker: Lieutenant
content: There's no need to retreat. Stand fast, everyone.

speaker: Lieutenant
content: Command confirms reinforcements are inbound. Our mission is to buy them time.

Schorl takes you away from the chaos in Augustus's luxury car. Inside, it's a whirlwind of activity: the little triangle interfaces with the autonomous driving system, activates anti-Mania scans to stabilize the contamination spreading through your body, and tirelessly attempts to raise Broken Blade Squad 3 on the battlefield.
Nearly forty minutes after you left the ball, Broken Blade Squad 3 finally responds to your call.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: Minos, this is Iron Mask. Combat operations are complete. All objectives secured. The after-action report will be forwarded by Siglinde. That is all.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You lost contact for a while.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: It was just signal interference from the intense Tide of Ashes, nothing to worry about. Your concern should be placed somewhere else—

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: We made contact with multiple giant Apostles. Externally controlled. Their size and threat level are off the charts, far beyond anything in our records. No way this was done by Aurum Secretum Sinners alone.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: We suspect a much stronger power source is nearby. That's the key that the enemy is using to summon and control the Apostles.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: Based on the Tide's activity patterns, whatever this thing is, it's likely connected to the missing BR-005.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I see.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: One more thing.
He pauses for a moment.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: We also engaged several Aurum Secretum wielders. Captured one alive—a female Sinner. Do we transfer her to MBCC?

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: If not, I will dispose of her on site.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Keep her alive. We're critically short on intel right now. I have a lot of questions for her.

speaker: Scarface
content: Awww, c'mon, another one alive?? Where's the fun in that? My teeth were just itching to meet her!
The noisy person on the other end of the communication is quickly silenced.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: No need. The General ordered us to fulfill all your requests. I'll have her transported to MBCC as soon as possible.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: Transportation will take longer until the Tide of Ashes subsides. Please have a reception team ready. Over.
[Dance Floor]
The ball is not yet over. In fact, your departure seems to have loosened tongues, and the guests have grown noticeably more talkative.

speaker: Crowd A
content: Will you look at that? This is the great defender we're all counting on? He can barely stand up straight, and those war hawks are still trying to rope him in? How are we supposed to fight Fraser with that?
female_content: Will you look at that? This is the great defender we're all counting on? She can barely stand up straight, and those war hawks are still trying to rope her in? How are we supposed to fight Fraser with that?

speaker: Crowd A
content: I heard he's getting benched. The security departments had a big meeting over at Paradeisos, and he wasn't even there...
female_content: I heard she's getting benched. The security departments had a big meeting over at Paradeisos, and she wasn't even there...

speaker: Crowd B
content: Guess he's just another stepping stone. That current DisCorps leader is the real problem. You hear what she did? Attacked the FAC Commander-in-Chief last year. And word is, twelve years ago... back in N.F. 103? She offed the previous one, too.
female_content: Guess she's just another stepping stone. That current DisCorps leader is the real problem. You hear what she did? Attacked the FAC Commander-in-Chief last year. And word is, twelve years ago... back in N.F. 103? She offed the previous one, too.

speaker: Crowd C
content: My god. Is she trying to stage a coup? Is she just power-crazy, or is the FAC completely useless? Compared to her, MBCC is really just...

An alliance opposed to the mobilization order has begun to coalesce, with covert agitators actively fanning the flames through scandals and rumors. They whisper of atrocities from the old military's tyrannical reign, the unresolved mysteries of the N.F. 106 Observatory tragedy, the bitter rivalry between DisCity and the Outlands that sparked the one-year-long war, and fears of another Great Expo tragedy... and more.

Before long, a consensus emerges among the people: the armed forces within their own city-state seem more threatening than the hostile Outlanders poised beyond the walls. The memory of the old military's dictatorship feels closer, more visceral, than the faded history of the Independence War—and FAC's deep unpopularity is plain for all to see.
It is at this moment that Catherine returns to the hall.

Her eyes sweep across the room as though searching for someone. The wine glass in her hand has long been empty. An opportunist takes notice and glides to her side, holding two fresh glasses of fine wine.

Perhaps he is drawn by her expensive jewelry, or believes such beauty shouldn't stand alone—or maybe he recalls that she was the one ${PlayerName} left on the dance floor. Whatever the reason, his assessment is quick, and he moves to perform his version of gallantry.

speaker: Male Socialite
content: Madam, are you here alone? Allow me to introduce myself. I'm a humble businessman in the service of Paradeisos. Here's my card. And you are? I'd be honored if you'd join me for the next—

speaker: Male Socialite
content: Argh!!
A dinner knife—a flash of silver—arcs through the air and embeds itself in the back of his hand.

speaker: Male Socialite
content: What... Why would the knife... Wh-what did you do?!

Ignoring the man's choked scream entirely, Catherine strides forward without so much as a glance. As every head in the venue swivels toward her, she coolly scans the sea of startled faces, but her target remains elusive.
A tap on her sunglasses' frame activates the communicator. She listens to Schorl's message, and a soft sigh escapes her lips.

speaker: Catherine
content: Sigh... I was gone for five minutes. One phone call. And the Chief's gone already?

speaker: Catherine
content: I just needed to win that battle first. If he'd just waited, my company would be his right now.
female_content: I just needed to win that battle first. If she'd just waited, my company would be hers right now.

content: In resignation, Catherine peels off her sunglasses and rubs the weariness from her eyes. Now, someone finally recognizes her.
[Scene Change] Battlefield Frontline
The battlefield is a scar of ruin. Steel rods and iron spikes have clawed the sandy earth to shreds. A few Apostles lie pinned to the ground, their forms slowly crumbling into ash.
In the midst of the devastation, the lone Outland prisoner strains against her bonds, howling with a raw mix of rage and terror.

speaker: Aurum Secretum Captive
content: ...What is this... Is this that woman's power? Why is it here...

speaker: Aurum Secretum Captive
content: Is she nearby?!!! Where are you! Show yourself!! I'll kill you!!!

speaker: Scarface
content: Gyahahaha! That look on your face! Bet you didn't see that coming. Our boss's like a super magneto queen. She doesn't even need to show up to wreck you. She can just snap your bones from hundreds of miles away.

speaker: Scarface
content: Anywhere the Shattered Blade points, Catherine Augustus's power follows. Total annihilation. So... you scared yet?

speaker: Aurum Secretum Captive
content: Go on, kill me, you DisCity dogs!! Do it! Or I swear I'll skin you alive, grind your bones into offerings, and turn every last one of you into—

speaker: Aurum Secretum Captive
content: Ugh!!
A rifle butt smashes against the base of her skull. The Outland warrior stiffens for a single, frozen moment before collapsing into unconsciousness. Then, Iron Mask hoists her up.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: Those are words for the dead. She is needed alive for a few more days.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: Get her to Nirvana Port and prep for shipment to DisCity. Augustus wants her delivered.

speaker: Military Doctor
content: Wait, what about the others?
With a smile, she indicates the desert bandits. It was they who supplied the vessels to transport the "Aurum Secretum device," provided cover, and assisted the two Outland warriors with its escort.
[Scene Change] Dance Floor
Someone trembles as they recognize her face.

speaker: Crowd A
content: ...I remember now! I saw that face in a portrait at <color=#fb9259>the Andohars'</color> gallery...

speaker: Crowd A
content: Her name... what was her name? It doesn't matter! The uniform... I remember the uniform in the painting now. It was a DisCorps uniform. My god... she's one of them!

Catherine had long forgotten the portrait. What she'd truly wanted was an equestrian piece, a vision of herself astride a powerful horse, styled after that pre-Nightfall painting of a general she so admired.

She surveys her surroundings; today's DisCity is utterly lacking in that kind of grandeur. The crowd around her grows restless—a vortex of averted eyes, stolen glances, and hushed whispers—their dread of her presence palpable.
As it should be. The common rabble ought to fear their betters. Yet... this level of dread is insufficient. It is not yet enough.
[Scene Change] Battlefield

The desert bandits fall to their knees, their desperate hands clutching the cold, unyielding metal of Iron Mask's legs. Witnessing his mercy toward the Outland captive has kindled a fragile hope, and now they beg, their pleas torn between ragged sobs.

speaker: Desert Bandit
content: P-please!! We were just... we were just passing through! They made us do it!

speaker: Desert Bandit
content: We're done! We swear, we're done helping them! We'll... we'll help you! We'll tell you everything!!

speaker: Military Doctor
content: Alright, that's enough out of him. I'll take it from here.
The desert bandits watch, on the verge of tears, as she opens her medkit. Here is salvation: an angel tending to the wounds they suffered during their capture.
Then their angel reaches into the box. She retrieves two pistols, aiming neatly between their eyes with a smile.

speaker: Crowd A
content: But that painting... it was from forty years ago! Forty years! How is her face exactly the same... What in God's name is she?

Her declaration detonates another wave of panic, even wider this time. The room erupts into chaos; some shout for the guards while others scramble for the exits. Amidst the bedlam, Catherine merely watches, an amused smile playing on her lips as she contemplates whether to even bother answering these "youngsters."

speaker: Catherine
content: An exceptional weapon is priceless. It stays sharp because it's cared for. It's ready because it's respected.

speaker: Catherine
content: ...Is that really so hard to understand? In your grip, even a masterpiece would be reduced to scrap. A waste of a perfect gift.

speaker: Catherine
content: Just by breathing, you make my blood run hot.
[Aurum Secretum device wreckage falls]

With a deafening crash, the glass dome of the banquet hall shatters. The lights cut out completely. Countless shards rain down as a twisted mass of metal, nearly two meters wide, thunders into the floor. Iron chains that bind it whip through the crowd, unleashing wave after wave of piercing screams.
Only now has Catherine Augustus Andohar ceased her power.

She used magnetism to haul it all the way here—not taxing, but time-consuming. If she hadn't been distracted providing support to Iron Mask and his team, it would have arrived much earlier. Unfortunately, she didn't make it in time.

speaker: Augustus
content: A little trophy from our latest battle. This is what's behind the Tide of Ashes, the very weapon they're using to ravage WhiteSands.

speaker: Augustus
content: I was going to give it to ${PlayerName} as a gift. Hauled it all the way back so he could see something interesting, something to shake off the gloom. But you drove him off before I got here.
female_content: I was going to give it to ${PlayerName} as a gift. Hauled it all the way back so she could see something interesting, something to shake off the gloom. But you drove her off before I got here.

speaker: Augustus
content: So I guess you're the lucky ones who get the show instead.

With a mere flick of her finger, the iron chains groan to life, wrenching the deformed Aurum Secretum device from the crowd. It hangs, grotesque and suspended, as a shower of unidentifiable debris rains down upon the cowering crowd below.

speaker: Augustus
content: Open your eyes. Take a good look. This is what the Outlanders spent years building. They broke every law, spilled their own blood, poured their hatred into it—all so they could cross the farlands and end your lives.

speaker: Augustus
content: And you? You think you can just betray your own, drop your guard, offer a few bribes, chant "long live peace," and go on living like nothing's wrong?

speaker: Augustus
content: How arrogant... You've never known real war. You've never even truly looked your enemy in the eye. All you care about is saving your own skins.

speaker: Augustus
content: Listen up, you "peace-loving" people of DisCity. War is coming, and your army is coming back with it.

speaker: Augustus
content: That's right. These soldiers you fear—the ones with blood on their hands, shoulders heavy with sin, the so-called monsters beyond redemption—

speaker: Augustus
content: They're the ones who rotted in hell so you could prosper. And how did you repay them? You threw them away.

speaker: Augustus
content: But never forget: your shiny throne is built on our corpses. The wine you drink is spilled from lives we took.

speaker: Augustus
content: You feast on blood and flesh, and yet you dare judge my soldiers? You dare?!

speaker: Crowd
content: Aaarrrgh! HELP!!
The fury in her voice echoes, a vibration that seizes the blood. Fear shatters their composure, and the first screams tear through the air.

Jolted back to their senses, the guests scramble for the exits—a panicked crawl on hands and knees, their strength sapped, unable to stand. In the oppressive dark, they are nothing but a herd of terrified livestock.

speaker: Augustus
content: The gutter you crawled from would reject your corpse. I won't give it the chance to dirty my blade.

speaker: Augustus
content: Whatever the Outlanders can do, they can do better.

speaker: Augustus
content: Mark my words, you cowards. War is coming, and none of you can stop it.

speaker: Augustus
content: Everything we've lost... we'll take it back on the battlefield.
With her purpose fulfilled, she turns her back on the place, leaving without a second glance.
[Scene Change] Bureau
Meanwhile, you finally arrive at the Bureau.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief! Where have you been? How are you feeling?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm fine.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: How's the front line? I want a full report.

speaker: Nightingale
content: But you don't look well, Chief. You should have a medical check first.

speaker: Option
options: I'm fine. How's the battle going?

speaker: Nightingale
content: ...It's already over. They repelled the enemy and obtained vital intelligence.
You take the terminal, your eyes scanning every word of the battle report.
The stark, bloodstained numbers before your eyes dissolve into a soft sigh, then vanish entirely as the screen goes dark.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: It was just signal interference from the intense Tide of Ashes, nothing to worry about. Your concern should be placed somewhere else—
...Did that man omit the casualty figures because it was your decision? Did the strategy you chose lead to this cost?
<color=#fb9259>Why didn't he mention it earlier?</color>
The nausea from contamination surges again, and Nightingale quickly moves to offer support.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief! You need to steady yourself. These casualties are an unfortunate but ordinary part of warfare, unlike the typical operations in the city. The mission was a success. Please, trust that this is a victory.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Or... or perhaps we should withdraw from the operation? Your body isn't in any condition to handle more stress. I can submit the request right away—

speaker: Option
options: ...It's fine. I've got it under control.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The shackles' Mania fluctuations don't always connect to my emotions. I'm not that emotionally volatile. It might be coming from BR-005... Since it's been going on all night, there's probably an external cause.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Maybe the Black Ring has moved closer. Could be why my sensitivity's spiking. I'll head to medical soon to see if they can pick up any new leads.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Just need a moment to rest. I'll go by myself... I need some time alone.
You let go of her hand. As you turn to leave, Schorl stops you.

speaker: Schorl
content: Chief, try not to shoulder all the pressure yourself.

speaker: Schorl
content: We have everything under control, and the backup plans are in motion. Your direct involvement isn't a requirement for this rescue. You can withdraw at any time. Please don't feel you have to push beyond your limits.

speaker: Schorl
content: War is, unfortunately, a constant in our era. We are equipped to manage it. You can trust us with this.
You walk alone through the Bureau's silent corridor. The late hour has stilled everything but the low, persistent thrum of Mania—a rhythm that pulses in your bones.
Surprisingly, the sensation isn't unpleasant.
Compared to the gilded masquerade of that ball, this raw truth—the cruelty, the suffering—feels more real. It cannot be ignored, and you will not look away.

speaker: Langley
content: In your current state, no one in their right mind would put you on the frontlines.

speaker: Schorl
content: You can withdraw at any time. Please don't feel you have to push beyond your limits.

speaker: Hella
content: Help me...
You will not withdraw. You will take the field and finish this.
To win. To have your triumph. They started this war. They wielded the Black Ring to commit atrocities beyond forgiveness. You will defeat them, whatever the cost. You will not hesitate.

speaker: Nightingale
content: These casualties are an unfortunate but ordinary part of warfare, unlike the typical operations in the city.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Our promise... I'm sorry...

speaker: Jasmine
content: Don't mind it...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Ugh...
Another wave of contamination surges through you, forcing you to halt. You draw a sharp breath to steady yourself.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...It's the Black Ring's influence... It's close...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I have no reason to hesitate.
You step into the room and shut the door, fumbling in the darkness for the light switch.
That's when you feel it.
The air is thick, distorted. Your shackles stir restlessly as a wave of contamination seeps from the shadows. You are not alone.
You instinctively release your shackles, but you're a fraction of a second too slow.

Something crashes into your chest. Instantly, a violent shock of contamination resonates through your core, burning through your strength and hurling you back against the wall. The lights flicker on, revealing the face of your attacker.
[Hella Hug CG1] White flash fade in, sound effect, blank screen for 3 seconds

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...You're...
Hearing your voice, the "person" in your arms slowly raises her head. The sight sends a thunderous ringing through your mind.
[Hella Hug CG2]

speaker: Hella
content: Hee...
[Quick flash: CG inside the Black Ring and Apostle visual (about 0.3 seconds) with distortion effects] [Followed by white screen, then fade to black screen after 1 second, text appears]
I'M BACK

Night descends upon WhiteSands, and with it comes a storm that carries calamity and anomaly in its howling winds. It scours the desert, swallowing every shelter in its path. Merchants, bandits, and sand worms alike flee before its relentless approach.
Yet amidst this all-consuming Tide of Ashes, a single structure stands defiant upon the shifting sands. It cleaves the surging, dust-choked waves, an immovable and unyielding bastion.
The place is a ruin, a colossal steel tomb frozen in time. Within its walls, ghostly soldiers throw open the gates, forming ranks to welcome their general.
That night, her affairs in the city concluded and her desired meetings held, Augustus returns to her fortress.
As she walks through the long corridor, a smile touches her lips while listening to Siglinde's remote debriefing on the past few days.
On the other end of the line, the liaison officer's voice is composed and professional as ever, yet Augustus can immediately sense the high spirits thrumming beneath the victory report.

speaker: Siglinde
content: Thanks to your support, our frontline squad was able to adapt quickly. We repelled the enemy and secured significant spoils, completing our mission with honor.

speaker: Siglinde
content: Frankly, the FAC's combat awareness pales in comparison. They're overly defensive, their tactics are rigid, and their hesitation is costing them opportunities. It's difficult to believe they're DisCity's primary force...

speaker: Siglinde
content: General, if I may, are you still considering taking over their position? You haven't mentioned it since our breakthrough at their base. If the plan is still active, I could infiltrate their ranks, using my liaison position to gather intelligence and influence their operations from the inside.

Though her voice is measured and calm, the young liaison officer's quickening speech gives her away. Augustus recognizes the thrill coursing beneath her professional demeanor. The approach of war has a scent, a charge in the air that calls to every "Rancor" soldier's blood—a feeling she knew well in her youth.
After a moment of contemplation, she answers.

speaker: Augustus
content: Hmm... I have other plans, but your initiative has my attention.

speaker: Augustus
content: Very well. Get in close to that Commander-in-Chief. Observe him. I trust you'll see the FAC's true nature for yourself.

speaker: Siglinde
content: The mission is clear. I will not fail you, General.

Augustus ends the communication, that faint smile lingering on her lips. She enters the situation room at the corridor's end and shuts the door, sealing the howling storm outside. Now, she stands alone in this vast, empty chamber.
Yet beneath the echo of her footsteps hums a chorus of countless other voices... the whispers of the "Rancors."

speaker: Rancors
content: <color=#dg1f1f><i>The time has come <size=28><color=#7683a2>It's finally time</size></color>. The rusty scent of war <size=28><color=#7683a2>The call of blood</size></color>...<i></color>

speaker: Rancors
content: The city-state needs me DisCity needs me. The enemies are on their way, bringing back glory victory and justice homeland to us. Our courage undiminished Our resolve unextinguished, we still thirst for the demons' blood, to cement our loyalty with it to protect our city-state.

speaker: Rancors
content: Take us back Bring us back to the battlefield, General. Lead us Command us, let us kill let us die, just like... in days past.

Whenever Augustus amplifies her power through her subordinates' Rancors, she hears their voices, just as her soldiers do. And each time she returns to Nirvana Port, those voices grow clearer, sharper.
They rise from beneath her feet and emanate from the hilt at her waist, as if the entire ruined bastion trembles with whispers, welcoming her home.
Augustus always listens quietly, tracing familiar faces among them, reclaiming moments lost to time. Still listening, she moves past rows of bookshelves.
At last, she draws out a dossier—not too thick, not too slim—with writing on its cover:

<i>N.F. 62, DisCity Independence War Report

Recorder: <size=52><color=#fb9259>Big</color> Boss</size> Brock<i>

speaker: Augustus
content: ...That old fossil. Can't even file a proper war report without turning it into a joke.
She smiles to herself and opens the weathered pages.

Beneath the yellowed records, an old news clipping is pasted neatly, as if Big Boss Brock had meant to remind himself that, one year ago, DisCity's self-appointed Speaker of the City Council had died on December 26th.

At this point in the war report, words could no longer express his joy. Brock sprang up, spinning in a clumsy, ecstatic circle, bobbing and jumping around his tent while humming a wildly off-key tune.

speaker: Brock
content: We won, we won, oh YES, we won! Long live DisCity, long live the Guerrillas! Brock's command win win win—

speaker: Messenger
content: Boss!
A messenger ducked through the tent flap, his breath coming in ragged gasps.

speaker: Brock
content: Manners, rookie! You don't just enter a room, you REQUEST to enter a room! Did Dravyn teach you nothing?
The moment he was discovered, Brock spun around and snapped to attention. He scolded with feigned sternness, his face turning bright red as he desperately tried to think of an excuse.
The messenger, however, clearly couldn't wait for any of this.

speaker: Messenger
content: There's no time! Captain, you must hurry. Major Dravyn is in trouble. Andohar... And Andohar—
Immediately, Brock was alert.

speaker: Brock
content: Andohar? What's that arms dealer up to now?!

speaker: Messenger
content: Andohar's been hiding a superweapon. The Major's trying to handle it, but... he's never seen anything like that either. The Major—
Bang bang! Bang!
A series of gunshots pierced the air. Brock's eyes widened in shock. He'd know that sound anywhere—it was Dravyn's favorite weapon, a Browning M1910 from the old world.

In an instant, that brutal image consumed him again: the Speaker, gunned down from behind. Eight times. A tremor shook Brock's core, his head throbbing with a sudden, violent heat. Snatching the gun from the table, he stormed out.

speaker: Brock
content: Damn it! Don't die, Dravyn!!
[Scene Change] Armory

speaker: Brock
content: Dravyn!
Brock charged into the armory, and a rush of relief crashed over him—his friend was still alive.
But that relief shattered as he saw the officer's face, contorted with rage, clutching a gun whose barrel still smoked.

speaker: Dravyn
content: ...Look at the trouble you've brought upon us, Brock.

speaker: Brock
content: ...Huh?
The guerrilla commander in a standard-issue military uniform, huh...
Hehe. Someone at DisCorps is being very naughty, aren't they? Should I go tell on you?

speaker: Brock
content: Who's there?!
A shadow fell over his head from above, followed by a childish voice.
[Small CG 1]

speaker: Catherine
content: My name is <color=#fb9259>Catherine Augustus</color>. Of the <color=#fb9259>Andohar family</color>. You know, the arms dealer you cheated? I'm Andohar's youngest daughter.

speaker: Catherine
content: I hitched a ride in one of the weapons crates, all the way into you rebels' hideout. And now I've seen all your cards. Your gear is a decade out of date, you have zero superpowers between you, and frankly, with that scrap metal you're carrying... catching me isn't an option.

speaker: Catherine
content: If you'd rather the metropoles not find out about your little secrets, let's make a deal. I have a few conditions.

speaker: Dravyn
content: Why are you still talking to her? She's clearly not a normal human!

Dravyn seized an opening and fired two more shots. Catherine didn't even blink. The bullets halted abruptly, only inches from her body, their momentum dying as if they'd slammed into a wall of invisible mud.
It was only then that Brock's brain caught up. The girl wasn't just perched on some random crate. She was casually seated atop his prized, second-hand missile, hovering in mid-air.

speaker: Brock
content: Wait, is this magic? Brat, you—

speaker: Catherine
content: I'm 11 years old, you old fossil. I'll ask one more time: Are we making a deal or not?
She raised her hand—
[Small CG 2]
Several more missiles rose into the air, spinning 720 degrees. Brock's face went pale with terror, his eyes nearly popping out of his head.

speaker: Brock
content: Okay! Okay!! Just don't ride my missiles! How am I supposed to pay for them if they break?! Wait, stop playing with them!

speaker: Brock
content: I agree, I agree, alright?! What do you want? Dravyn, put that gun down NOW!!

speaker: Catherine
content: Heh, I've come all the way to your headquarters. Isn't what I want obvious?
[Small CG 3]

speaker: Catherine
content: Let me join the army! Teach me how to fight! Take me to a real battlefield! I can't wait to become a DisCity general!

speaker: Dravyn
content: Just kill her.

speaker: Brock
content: Hold on, HOLD ON—!

On October 22, N.F. 65, the WhiteSands Guerrillas operating outside DisCity captured a special prisoner—a young girl who had traveled undetected even by the Andohar caravan.

She possessed extraordinary abilities that defied conventional understanding. At the time, it was unclear whether she was a superhero like those depicted in television stories, or a bio-engineered weapon developed through the advanced technology of the metropoles.
Years later, such individuals would be formally classified as <color=#fb9259>Sinners</color>—a manifestation of Mania's side effects.
Likewise, history would eventually mark this day as the first encounter between the three generations of leaders from DisCity's old military era.

EDGE-05: The mobilization order failed to pass, as expected, but the margin was surprisingly wide.
EDGE-05: The "incident" at the Eastside peace ball a few days ago might be the cause. Ms. Andohar's little stunt sent quite a shock through the council.
EDGE-03: It's fine. 04 and Nirvana suffered too heavy a loss; they needed this concession. Besides, FAC's reserves are sufficient. We never planned on counting on them for this war anyway.
EDGE-03: What's the status on SHP-13? I heard there's a new development.

EDGE-07: You heard right! And it's a big one. Totally unexpected.
EDGE-07: Long story short, an <color=#fb9259>anomalous Mania contaminant</color> slipped through every one of MBCC's defenses, made direct contact with SHP-13, and... nothing happened. No incidents.

EDGE-07: It's confirmed that the contaminant's Mania profile now shows a blended signature—parts of BR-005, traces of MBCC-S-098, even echoes of SHP-13's own shackles—all in a bizarre, stable harmony. We've got an invaluable sample on our hands!
EDGE-07: This means even without live data from the Third Observatorium on BR-005, we now have a whole new way to track and analyze its condition!

EDGE-02: Hmm, quite fascinating indeed.
EDGE-02: So, was it that little Sinner's excessive longing for the Shepherd that pulled BR-005 all the way to DisCity? Or did the Black Ring use her as a conduit, and now as bait, trying to lure our Shepherd out...?

EDGE-02: ...I'm getting ahead of myself. Too much speculation. My apologies. For now, we observe. Closely.
EDGE-02: Its presence will undoubtedly affect SHP-13. Monitor him. Ensure he doesn't lose control.
female_content:
EDGE-02: ...I'm getting ahead of myself. Too much speculation. My apologies. For now, we observe. Closely.
EDGE-02: Its presence will undoubtedly affect SHP-13. Monitor her. Ensure she doesn't lose control.

content:
EDGE-07: What about 01? Any progress? Will he be ready in time?
EDGE-07: Are we drawing too much attention? Could they detect us...
EDGE-02: With his record, no news is good news. We wait and buy him time. As for detection...
EDGE-02: With our adorable Shepherd in play, I doubt it'll be an issue.
EDGE-02: Now then, let's continue observation and documentation. This war will yield very interesting data, it seems.
[Reception Room]

August 2, N.F. 115 13:00
MBCC Chief's Office
Using "city-state security" as a pretext, the newly appointed Speaker, Max King, had arranged this meeting to grant himself a formal meeting with the MBCC Chief.

Public speculation is that his failed mobilization order has dealt a severe blow to his authority, pushing him to recruit allies. But now... he's clearly unhappy, just not for the reason everyone thinks.

speaker: Max King
content: ...You're just going to keep talking to me like this?
Absolutely cheerful, you greet him with a smile and a gesture toward the seat.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Speaker King, it's good to see you. It's been a while. How are things at the council?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I heard about the struggle to get that security funding through. The mobilization order failing... that's a tough break. With all that pressure and everyone watching, just let me know if there's anything I can do to help.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And don't worry, we're completely alone here. No prying eyes or ears. You can speak freely.

speaker: Max King
content: Free? It was anything but free! I've had to invent excuses and dodge half the city just to be here! Do you know how worried I've been since the Great Expo?! So can you please, for once, be serious?

speaker: Option
options: Hmm? But I am being serious.

speaker: Max King
content: You call this being serious?!
With a flourish, he produces a mirror from God-knows-where. Held within its glass, your reflection gazes back—rosy-cheeked and radiant, seated at your desk as if touched by a sudden, glorious light.

speaker: Max King
content: Wait, what the ****! Is this place haunted for real? Why can't the mirror show it?!

speaker: Max King
content: I mean, what in the world is that attached to you? It's seriously creeping me out. Is this some kind of Mania contamination?
[Phantom Hella's portrait, hanging from Chief's neck]
You are utterly stunned by his words.

speaker: Max King
content: I'm not blind! Hey, wait a second! Did she just give me the finger?! I can't make out her expression, but there's no mistaking that!!
The Speaker's frustration mounts to a hilariously animated degree, coaxing a cheerful laugh from you in return.
As an ordinary person, Max King has never been able to see Hecate's Mania Nightmare. The fact that he can see Hella fills you with a giddy joy, as if her presence has become tangibly real.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That's perfect. I've been wanting to introduce you.
Right on cue, the shadow at your neck peels away. It spirals through the air before landing dramatically on the desk, striking a theatrical pose to match your announcement.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Her name is Hella. She's from Syndicate, and, like Hecate, she was one of the first Sinners I met.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Even now, as a phantom, I'm sure she's still deeply connected to her real self. If she's appearing like this, it has to be for a reason. Something important. That's why I've been trying to communicate with her. Max, can you hear her speaking?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It's a real shame you can't. Hella's famous for her sweet words. She's Syndicate's Ambassador of Civility, absolutely brilliant at making people smile. I know you'd like her.

speaker: Max King
content: Wait, are you seriously showing off your "daughter" to me right now?!
A few minutes later, Max King rubs his reddened hand from pounding the table. He slumps onto a nearby sofa in resignation, sprawling out ungracefully as he scratches his head.
Good grief... He actually came to discuss serious matters with him. After all that commotion, any semblance of a serious atmosphere has completely evaporated.
female_content: Good grief... He actually came to discuss serious matters with her. After all that commotion, any semblance of a serious atmosphere has completely evaporated.

speaker: Max King
content: Okay, seriously, what is your deal with Catherine Augustus?

speaker: Max King
content: The drama she caused at that "anti-war" ball? She grabbed every single headline. Now I've got everyone asking me whether the Andohars are planning a coup, or if DisCorps is making a move. And—

speaker: Max King
content: She was there as your plus-one, wasn't she? The whole city's buzzing with rumors.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: In a way, it's a collaboration.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: She needs a backchannel into city security, and I need her troops. After Adelaide stripped me of my power, seeking support elsewhere was my only real option.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Honestly, I don't believe she's truly against the mobilization order. My guess is... she sabotaged it last time because she had too many restrictions placed on her. Wasn't happy about being held on a tight leash.
Finally feeling clear-headed? Max King can't help but be amazed by the magic of a good mood.

speaker: Max King
content: ...Is working with DisCorps really the right move?

speaker: Max King
content: Look, I haven't seen war firsthand, but I know this much: you won't be fighting Mania monsters or some Underground lunatics there.

speaker: Max King
content: Those Outlanders... just a month ago at the Great Expo, you were running yourself ragged trying to protect them.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You think I'm not ready for a war? Worried that I can't handle it?

speaker: Max King
content: I'm worried about you.
He turns the mirror toward you once more.
In the mirror, you see only yourself sitting at the desk, revealing the truth that Hella isn't actually by your side.

speaker: Max King
content: I'm afraid that weight will crush you. It's because you have a good heart. And people with good hearts pay a double toll on a place like that.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Call someone "good" or "bad" these days, and all I hear is which side they're on. But I don't have the luxury to dwell on it.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: For me right now, objectives matter more than stance. A month ago, my job was to ensure the Great Expo ran smoothly. Today, it's bringing Hella home. And I'll do that, no matter what it takes.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'll do anything to get it done. If I do nothing, if there's nothing I can do... that's the real pain.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm not lost, Max. You don't need to worry.

He opens his mouth to speak, but the words are stolen by the sudden vibration of his phone. A message from his secretary: Time to return. The unspoken warning is clear—he can't linger too long. Someone is watching.

speaker: Max King
content: Alright, duty calls. Can't keep the whole cabinet waiting. Please, take care of yourself. And I mean it, if you need anything, just say the word.

speaker: Max King
content: Just don't spend all your time with your little girl. Remember, you've got friends. Real, living people who've got your back. Alright?

options: Of course, Speaker. Your orders are my command.

content: He scoffs at your joke, but seems relieved that you still have the energy to crack wise.
His smile in return is genuine, though it doesn't quite reach his eyes; relief is there, but so is a shadow of the worry that came before.
[Scene Change] Corridor
Exiting the Chief's office, Max King is immediately met by two young girls flanking the doorway—Hecate and Elvira, looking like stern sentinels.
He offers a terse nod and steps aside, a silent invitation. Hecate seizes it, slipping past him into the office to find her Chief.
Elvira remains. Falling into step beside Max King, she matches his pace down the corridor, their conversation a hushed, urgent stream of words.

speaker: Max King
content: The mobilization order's future is in doubt. While the Sillage Society has been quieter since the Euphoria incident, the public's resistance against war is far stronger than I ever expected.

speaker: Max King
content: And now, this sensationalist garbage about ${PlayerName} and Augustus? It's blatant propaganda, likely funded by the Outlands. What a mess.

speaker: Elvira
content: ......I can imagine how it must be.

speaker: Elvira
content: But because of Jele... because I was close to an Outland spy, the 9th Agency doesn't trust me anymore. They've questioned me a few times, and now they watch what I can see. I don't have access to much information now... so I'm afraid I can't be of much help. I'm sorry.

speaker: Max King
content: It's okay. Just having you here is a tremendous help.
He turns around to look back. They've rounded a corner in the hallway, but from here he can still see ${PlayerName}'s office. The door remains firmly shut.

speaker: Max King
content: My hands are tied. I can't visit often, and even out there, I'm buried in endless chatter, most of it useless. It's frustrating. To be constantly worried but unable to act.

speaker: Max King
content: That's why it's so reassuring knowing there's a smart cookie like you by his side. I'm counting on you, Miss Genius Stewart. Look after my buddy for me.
female_content: That's why it's so reassuring knowing there's a smart cookie like you by her side. I'm counting on you, Miss Genius Stewart. Look after my girl for me.

content: "Since when is the Chief your buddy?" Elvira wants to retort, but she manages to hold her tongue.
female_content: "Since when is the Chief your girl?" Elvira wants to retort, but she manages to hold her tongue.

content: Because now, everyone is in the same boat.

speaker: Elvira
content: ...I'll... do my best.
[Scene Change] Back to Isolation Cell
[Scene Change] (a cool mansion with cold color tones)

speaker: Chaotic Rusted Voice
content: ...That smell... That sound... The Outlands' dogs, right nearby, lurking, plotting... The Outlands' dogs are coming...

speaker: Chaotic Rusted Voice
content: Blood for blood... Blood for blood... General... lead us to battle, let our blades drink deep of the Outlanders' blood...

The woman removes her final piece of jewelry, hangs her sword with deliberate care, and lowers the needle onto the record. As a gentle melody fills the room, it blunts the edges of the whispers at her ears, making "them" sound less gloomy.
The phone rings. She sees the number, and her entire face lights up.

speaker: Augustus
content: Hello? So after standing me up at the ball, you finally decided to pick up the phone yourself? Go on, I'm listening. This better be good.

speaker: Augustus
content: ...Oh. I see. So your little friend's back. You must be thrilled. How is she?

speaker: Augustus
content: Hmm? Not the real one? There's a copy now? Hahaha, since when did the new era's Mania become so creative? This Black Ring really knows how to put on a show.
Her tone softens.

speaker: Augustus
content: Are you going to look for her? You must be short-handed.

speaker: Augustus
content: Fine. They're yours. Broken Blade Squad 3 is under your command now. Bring that kid home safe, and make it a clean victory.

speaker: Augustus
content: Take care of my soldiers. They're the best you'll ever get.

speaker: Augustus
content: I'll be waiting for good news.
The call ends, but the smile it brought remains, still lingering on her lips when her deputy enters the room.

speaker: Augustus
content: Look at that. All that fire and enthusiasm. You always see it in the rookies.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: Broken Blade Squad 3 is your most reliable unit. You're just handing them off to an outsider?

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: ${PlayerName} lacks proper military training and doesn't seem to fully trust you.

speaker: Augustus
content: Well, I see talent, and I allow for stubbornness. I did the same with every one of you.

speaker: Augustus
content: Now, let's see what he's truly capable of... Our focus must be on preparation. The time is almost upon us.
female_content: Now, let's see what she's truly capable of... Our focus must be on preparation. The time is almost upon us.

content: [WhiteSands]
(Environment Description)
Concealed by camouflage and cover, Broken Blade Squad 3 runs through their final pre-battle checks.

speaker: Military Doctor
content: You're telling me the enemies outside are just a distraction, and their real force is hiding inside the ash storm? No one can last more than a few hours in that kind of intensity.

speaker: Lieutenant
content: If their Aurum Secretum wielders can do it, so can we. And the Chief needs us to scout ahead.

speaker: Lieutenant
content: The shackles are still detecting the Sinner captured by BR-005. We can use them to guide us straight to that Black Ring. It's a viable strategy.
The doctor lets out a sigh.

speaker: Scarface
content: HA? Him again? That bookish guy collapses three times a day like clockwork. And he's supposed to command under fire? You really think that's gonna work?
female_content: HA? Her again? That bookish lady collapses three times a day like clockwork. And she's supposed to command under fire? You really think that's gonna work?

speaker: Military Doctor
content: Strengthening the shackle connection now will only speed up his contamination. Typical of our acting commander, always pushing it. Let's just hope he doesn't burn out before the battle's over.
female_content: Strengthening the shackle connection now will only speed up her contamination. Typical of our acting commander, always pushing it. Let's just hope she doesn't burn out before the battle's over.

speaker: Lieutenant
content: Our only focus is the mission.
After sending the final message to Nirvana Port, the man takes out a flare gun.

speaker: Lieutenant
content: Our mission objectives are clear: penetrate deep into the Tide of Ashes and locate the enemy's main force. Minos will maintain comms and provide guidance. If possible, destroy any Aurum Secretum device we encounter. This will weaken their control over the Apostles of Ashes.

speaker: Lieutenant
content: These are the commander's orders. And Augustus's orders.
After confirming the direction ${PlayerName} indicated, he fires the signal flare as promised, marking the beginning of the operation.

speaker: Lieutenant
content: Broken Blade Squad 3, move out. Complete the mission. Eliminate all resistance until victory.
[Scene Change] Farland Secret Hideout, Some WhiteSands Underground Ruins
Several advisors sit around a battered table, the air heavy with the scent of sun-baked sand, cold metal, and ancient bones—
—underpinned by the unmistakable tang of anxiety.

speaker: Farland Advisor A
content: Why would they push into the storm? Are they tracking the Black Ring? Who gave up our position?

speaker: Farland Advisor A
content: Damn it! That Underground woman Moore swore DisCity's network out here was ashes. So how did the enemy find out our location?

speaker: Farland Advisor B
content: I don't think it was a leak. It's something else.

speaker: Farland Advisor B
content: Scouts report DisCity's Shepherd is awake. Yesterday's fight sent a pulse through BR-005. It resonated with the Shepherd through those "shackles." Once that connection is made, Shepherd can just... feel where the Ring is.

speaker: Farland Advisor A
content: Sense it through the shackles...? You don't mean—

Shortly after the Black Ring outbreak over a month ago, the Aurum Secretum Institute deployed several miniature monitoring devices into the Ring through its fusion with the Apostles. Several attached themselves to Sinner Hella, providing them with critical data on the Black Ring's internal conditions.
Now, those same devices are transmitting erratic, heavily corrupted readings.
[Scene Change] Beneath the Black Ring

speaker: Farland Advisor A
content: That B-Class Sinner, Hella... The shackles have pierced into our Black Ring through her. They're still digging right now, trying to pinpoint it. It's only a matter of time before the enemy plows through the Tide of Ashes and finds us.

speaker: Farland Advisor A
content: Tch. A worthless B-Class. Negligible power, and yet she keeps gutting our most critical experiments... She needs to be removed. Permanently.

speaker: Farland Advisor A
content: The Aurum Secretum devices planted in the Black Ring... we can use them to lock onto her and force a full resonance. It won't just stop the signal; it'll turn her into a complete Corruptor. We plug the leak and maybe contaminate the shackles' user in the process... Yeah, that'll be it!
He finishes his calculations in a flash and rushes to the Aurum Secretum device, feeding the data into its core.
The red engravings at its center flare with blinding intensity. In response, a viscous, pitch-black Mania gel begins to ooze from the device—a sure sign the sorcery has taken hold.

The man can barely contain his triumph. He barks orders at several Sinners to guide the Aurum Secretum operation using the techniques taught by the Underground. But as he watches the Mania flow and the first data from within BR-005 flicker to life...

speaker: Farland Advisor A
content: Ah... Ahh... AAAAHHHHH!!!
As if obeying another command, the gel halts. It then recoils violently, expanding backward and lashing out with whip-like tentacles that ensnare the advisor in a crushing embrace.
The man is engulfed in an instant. His skin blisters and sloughs away, his body contorting and withering as a horrific stench—the very smell of death—fills the air.

speaker: Farland Advisor A
content: No, no, please!!! Help, HELP!!!

speaker: Farland Advisor B
content: What the hell is going on? Why is the Black Ring attacking us?? Could that DisCity Sinner have taken control of the Black Ring?

Off to the side, Synex munches on oleaster berries as she enjoys the show. These self-important Fraser intellectuals are a riot. One moment they're condemning Little Hella with mounting arrogance, the next they're trembling in fear. Scheming her way into this assignment has been well worth the trouble.

speaker: Synex
content: ...Fools. The arrogance, to think they could ever wield the Black Ring.

speaker: Synex
content: These are the ones who chose death over bending a knee to you. Their final act, paid for in blood. You can dump all the Aurum Secretum you want into this. Some things are just beyond your grasp.
She lifts her gaze to the points of light swirling within the Black Ring. Her close resonance with Mania allows her a faint glimpse of the chaos within.
The churning contamination outlines Hella's frail figure at its core. The girl is neither powerful enough to master the Black Ring nor has she been consumed by it—she exists in a precarious stasis.
