At the horizon, the thick fog slowly thins within the beam, unveiling a glimpse of deep blue night and stars unseen for years. And then...
A ship's horn cuts sharply through the quiet.
Once, twice, three times... blaring from the exact direction of your signal, its sound rolling clearly across the water.
In that moment, you know with absolute certainty:
It's the Rancor fleet!

speaker: Ceto
content: It is a rescue.
[Lighthouse Top]
She stumbles forward, her hands locking onto the railing with a white-knuckled grip. At the seam between light and fog, the hulking silhouettes of three steel vessels gradually solidify.

One by one, the ships' massive searchlights swing toward the lighthouse, their beams converging until they form a brilliant constellation on the water. After more than a decade of silence, rescue is finally arriving.

speaker: Ceto
content: You said... when the light was fixed, you'd let me choose one more time. To go with you, or not.

speaker: Ceto
content: Was that true?
So you've changed your mind? Not looking for an end anymore? You're asking to come with me?

speaker: Ceto
content: ...You talk too much.
She gives a small smile. It's the first time she hasn't let one of your desperate, well-meaning jokes fall flat.

speaker: Ceto
content: In this weather, with the fleet's distance, they won't reach shore before dawn.

speaker: Ceto
content: The storm and the fog will blind them. The beacon has to stay lit. All night.
She braces the flat of her blade against her forearms, wiping away the gore and contamination. Then, she moves to stand at your back once more, a shield against the encroaching monsters.

speaker: Ceto
content: Now, we'll have to survive until dawn on our own.

At the lighthouse's summit, the Tide Crawlers have completely severed your descent. The contamination surges with renewed violence; Corruptors circle ever closer, tightening the space around you like a noose.

Over the sea, the fog thickens once more, blurring the silhouette of the fleet. Thunder rumbles, twisting together with the howls of monsters. You stand atop the crumbling lighthouse—encroaching corruption at your back, and before you, only the faintest glimmer of hope.
Side by side, you wait in the dark for the coming dawn.

<size=45>July 15, N.F. 115 01:35
Operation BR-005 commences in...</size>
10 days 14 hours 12 minutes
You make your final preparations at the lighthouse summit, fortifying it to endure a night of storms and monstrous assault.
The lens is cracked. I've patched the wiring, but the batteries are shot. If we pulse the light every five minutes, we might just make it to dawn. We can't afford to waste a single charge.

speaker: Ceto
content: The window barricades are up, but they won't hold forever!

Ceto scavenges the ruins, piling movable iron grates, shattered toolboxes, and salvaged railings across the entrance—barricading every possible point where monsters might climb. From a distance, the structure looks like nothing so much as a birdcage perched high above the chaos.

speaker: Ceto
content: When that rescue team gets here... they're going to think we're insane.
Are we not?

She doesn't deny it. Instead, she rips the blood-soaked bandage from her arm, clamps one end between her teeth, and begins lashing her dagger tightly to her right hand. The cloth wraps over broken blisters, biting deep into raw flesh, yet she doesn't so much as flinch.

speaker: Ceto
content: Then watch your back. This lunatic sees red... you'll just be the next body on the floor.
You won't.
I'm not letting that blade take you.
No more words are needed. Bound by the shackles' fragile connection, you turn away and return to your posts. You throw the switch on the battery pack; she takes her position at the frontline.

The beacon flares back to life, greedily consuming the power you had so painstakingly charged. Its beam slices through the sheeting rain, and from below, a fresh wave of monstrous howls answers the light. The sound of scrabbling claws draws nearer—but behind you, Ceto stands energized, almost anticipatory.

speaker: Ceto
content: Hey, DisCity native. Remember that bet we made when you first got here?
Of course. You bet neither of us would survive the night.

speaker: Ceto
content: How about another bet? You in?
Bet on what?

speaker: Ceto
content: Miles's recipe is the prize. I bet we...

speaker: Ceto
content: ...both live to see the sun next morning!

With a guttural roar, she charges forward, surrendering completely to the Rancor. Every shred of restraint is gone; her dagger becomes a whirlwind of silver, each strike carrying the ferocity of one who fights not to survive, but to ensure her enemies die with her.
This is no longer human combat; it is something older, more savage: a primal hunger for pure destruction.
Until the tide falls at dawn
[CG Montage: Main storyline featuring battlefield scenes, Jasmine, antagonist Adelaide, Hella, and the Black Ring]
Blood...
Do you smell it? The scent of steel and blood...
The sound of bones breaking... how melodious...
Bite through them... Tear them apart. Don't hold back... You should have done this long ago.
Kill them, kill them!
[Red Flash Back to Reality]
Your vision blurs as your legs give way, dropping you to your knees. Your body is no longer your own to command.

The shackles are ready to crumble at the slightest pressure, their integrity compromised by the new Black Ring. Fresh contamination from the Sinner behind you—the one wielding a Rancor—sears through your mind like acid. This agony is a burden you willingly chose to share with her.

You try to steady your breath, but your grip on the crank slips as the last of your strength bleeds away. The navigation beacon flickers, growing dim; both the battery pack and your body are running on fumes.
Ceto notices your faltering state immediately, her own movements visibly slowing in response.
Just focus on the fight. I'll be fine... The fleet still needs the beacon to guide them. We've come too far to fail now. I'm not falling here.

You grit your teeth, forcing yourself to crank the generator for another surge of power, a pathetic attempt to prove your resilience. But you feel it clearly now: through the connection of the shackles, the Rancor's madness is gently, inexorably pulling your consciousness into its depths.

Ceto knows precisely what you're enduring, the same whispers that have been her constant companions for years. She also knows you will never speak of this pain, just as you've hidden your exhaustion and failing sight.
[Staircase]
Could you help me carry the lens up there? And don't look at me like that. I'm perfectly fine and bursting with energy after the meal.

That ${PlayerName}, who could barely walk a straight line, clutched the hard-won toolbox as he staggered toward the lantern room. He was determined to repair the navigation beacon before the thunderstorm broke.
female_content: That ${PlayerName}, who could barely walk a straight line, clutched the hard-won toolbox as she staggered toward the lantern room. She was determined to repair the navigation beacon before the thunderstorm broke.

content: She should have noticed it sooner. Temporary blindness had been a mercy. Keep pushing like this, this DisCity native's fragile physique would likely face far worse consequences. Dehydration? Collapse? Being torn apart like the other lighthouse keepers? She couldn't bear to imagine further.
Ceto, you know what I thought when I went blind in the Black Tide?
The fragile figure in her eyes paused on the stairs, turning back breathlessly:
I thought... it was so dark. An emptiness with nothing in front of you. No direction, no guide, nothing to hold onto. But that also meant...
No obstacles.
Since I knew there was nothing but the Black Tide and those monsters behind me, all I could do was swim forward. Faster. Just leave the shadows behind. There had to be land ahead. Somewhere.
Ceto despised such optimism, empty words that wouldn't fill a stomach or stop a monster. She looked up, scowling, yet her eyes fixed on the figure still pressing upward.

Those frail limbs—useless in a fight against the Tide Crawlers—clung to the rusted toolbox, carrying a weight she couldn't comprehend. Step by stubborn step, this person climbed toward what looked like an impossible hope.
So damn foolish... she thought, but swallowed the words. She had seen this kind of fool before. Watched them fall, one after another, only for new ones to rise and take their place.
Forward... tomorrow... land...
[Red Flash] [Knife Stabbing Sound]
Without a moment's hesitation, she drives the dagger into her own left shoulder.
What are you—
Simultaneously, the pressure crushing your mind eases significantly. Ceto is using pain to claw back her lucidity, deliberately lightening the burden of the Rancor that she shares with you.

speaker: Ceto
content: Keep going!
She offers no further explanation, flicks the blood from her blade, and throws herself back into the fray.
You do get a brief moment to catch your breath. But the very next second—
—BOOM!!!

The barricaded metal plates blast inward. Shattered railings tear apart, spraying debris and rain in all directions. Several monsters surge onto the platform at once, an endless tide swarming behind them.

speaker: Ceto
content: Just a little longer. The tide will fall soon.

Her voice trembles slightly from blood loss, but her grip on the knife is unshakable. You stand back-to-back in a circle of light barely two meters wide, with the abyss yawning below and a sea of Corruptors closing in.

speaker: Ceto
content: Our bet isn't over yet!
She smothers her agony, forces back the encroaching contamination with a sweeping slash, and plants herself as the final barrier between you and the horde.
Until the tide falls at dawn

The lighthouse platform has become the final stronghold, besieged by the crushing weight of the waves and the relentless tide of monsters. Rainwater, mingled with the putrid fluids of corrupted flesh, floods every crack and groove. The entire structure groans, trembling under the constant, brutal impacts.
Ceto swipes a hand across her eyes, clearing the blood that clouds her vision, and turns to the frail figure behind her.

${PlayerName}'s strength is clearly spent. The navigation beacon sputters, its light growing erratic. Cracks spiderweb across the housing. With insufficient power, the capacitors fail to hold a charge, and the beam is swallowed by the thick sea fog, unable to pierce the darkness.
Yet, you still try to force a smile.
Don't worry... I still got a B+ on the MBCC fitness test... once...

But the brave facade shatters as the platform lurches violently. Your legs buckle, dropping you to your knees. The shackles binding you both snap under the strain. The battery pack's indicator flickers, hovering just above zero.
In the dying light, Ceto's gaze falls on your hands—a raw, bloody mess of torn blisters.

speaker: Ceto
content: This won't do. The light's too weak to reach them. And the fleet isn't coming to rescue a dying person.
There has to be a way... Think! There has to be something useful that Fynn taught me!

speaker: Ceto
content: Rule Number One: Signal and Surveillance! Monitor the border without fail. Ensure signal transmission. Report all enemy movement. We are the frontline guardians. We fear nothing, and are ready to sacrifice all for the city-state!

speaker: Ceto
content: Rule Number Two: Beacon Maintenance! The light is our most reliable signal. Keeping the lighthouses operational is our primary duty!

speaker: Ceto
content: There has to be a way—
[Flashback] [Training Grounds]

speaker: Fynn
content: Alright, listen up! Today, we'll be learning Lighthouse Keeper's Code, Rule Three: Emergency Procedures.

speaker: Fynn
content: If lighthouse equipment is damaged and unable to transmit signals, immediately use semaphore to contact other outposts or Command. Semaphore is a reliable form of communication, ensuring that even if the lighthouse is inoperative, we can still relay critical information...
On the training grounds swept by a sandstorm, twelve-year-old Ceto held up a flag, nearly toppled by the raging winds.

speaker: Ceto
content: If I learn all this... I can join you, right? Then... I can go to DisCity with you?
Fynn's scabbard gently tapped the top of her head.

speaker: Fynn
content: It's not that simple, Ceto. Remember, semaphore isn't just a signal. It's the anchor that holds the keepers fast in the storm! It tells your enemies and your comrades one thing...
Fynn's withered hand suddenly surged with strength as she grabbed Ceto and thrust the flag in her hands directly into the howling wind!

speaker: Fynn
content: We are still standing!
[Flashback]

speaker: Ceto
content: Your hand! Now!
What for?
Before you can finish your question, she's already tearing strips from her tattered uniform jacket. She wraps the bright fabric around a broken metal rod, fashioning a crude distress flag.

speaker: Ceto
content: The west window's still clear. Get over there and do exactly as I say.
Rapidly, she traces symbols into your palm. You recognize them—universal signals for help. She thrusts the bloodstained banner into your arms and shoves you toward the only intact window.

speaker: Ceto
content: Memorize this signal. Repeat it, face the sea, and don't look back. You are going to execute Rule Three of the Lighthouse Keeper's Code.

speaker: Ceto
content: From now on, you are the beacon.
With no time to think, you're pushed to the western window. You raise the flag as she taught you. The first sequence begins—

speaker: Ceto
content: Wider!

Behind you, the whistle of her blade cutting the air is followed by the wet shatter of monstrosities. Something heavy slams against the tower walls. Without the shackles connecting you, there's no way to know how she's holding up.
Second sequence...

speaker: Ceto
content: Can you see... the fleet...
Not as clear as before, but I can barely make out the red warning lights on the bows of the fleet. They're approaching faster than expected!

speaker: Ceto
content: That's enough for them to see us now.
Third sequence begins. Warm liquid splatters against the back of your neck.

speaker: Ceto
content: You're losing the rhythm!
Her shout is sharp, punctuated by a suppressed groan of pain.
Fourth sequence. Your movements grow steadier, but the pace of her blade has slowed, now half a beat behind.
Tenth sequence. Her breathing has fractured into ragged gasps. The sound of steel meeting flesh grows dull, infrequent.
You almost turn; the urge to look is a physical pull. But her voice cuts through the chaos, raw and strained:

speaker: Ceto
content: Don't stop... Don't look back...
You continue sending the signals mechanically, knuckles white with tension, never stopping waving the flag.

speaker: Ceto
content: Soon... we'll see the sun...

Another crash echoes, this time with the shriek of twisting metal. The coppery tang of blood thickens in the air. A warm, thick liquid seeps around your boots. You're certain it's not from the creatures...
Fifteenth sequence...
Behind you, there is only silence now.
Ceto, how are you holding up?
No response...
Ceto?
[Injured Ceto CG] [Stirring, Heroic, Tragic Bgm]

She is still fighting. A length of steel rebar, thrust through the broken railing, has impaled her through the ribs, pinning her body in place. She uses it as a grisly prop, a final brace to keep herself upright and refusing to fall.
Even now—with the whites of her eyes flooded crimson—her gaze remains locked on the horde.

speaker: Echoes in Mind
content: Stand facing it, fight for it, and never, ever let the lighthouse beacon go out.

speaker: Echoes in Mind
content: We'll all go back together... return to DisCity in glory!

speaker: Echoes in Mind
content: From now on, you are the beacon.

speaker: Ceto
content: No... the beacon can't go out...
Her lips are cracked and bleeding. Her mouth moves with agonizing slowness, shaping words that can barely find voice.
[CG: Close-up of Injured Ceto]

speaker: Ceto
content: Go back... home...
Darkness rises like a tide, and Ceto feels herself sinking. The pain has faded, replaced by a deep, encroaching cold. A distant light glimmers, always just out of reach.
The first sounds that reach her ears are footsteps—boots striking metal, steady and clear, echoing from somewhere beyond the chaos.
[Portraits of Fallen Keepers]

speaker: Ceto
content: You all... How come?
[Consciousness World: Ceto's Life Flashing Before Her Eyes]

speaker: Familiar Voice
content: You tired?

A reply catches in Ceto's throat, emerging as silence. From the gloom before her, a figure solidifies. It's Lia, clad in her tactical gear, her Rancor in hand. She smiles, reaching both hands toward Ceto.

speaker: Lia
content: Come join me and Jay. We've been sleeping beneath the Black Tide for so long... long enough to forget all the pain.
As Lia begins to fall backward, Ceto's arms snap out on instinct to catch her.

speaker: Lia
content: You won't have to listen to the voices of the blade anymore. See? I've become just like the monsters.
Ceto lunges forward, only to grasp at empty air. Lia's form dissolves, collapsing into a pool of contaminated sludge.
Then, Sienna's figure emerges from the shadows. The flag in her hand drips black liquid with a steady pitter-patter.

speaker: Sienna
content: Where did you get all these new wounds? That must hurt so much...
Sienna's gaze is heavy with concern as it traces the fresh wounds covering Ceto's body.

speaker: Sienna
content: You gave me the last painkiller we had... but why...

speaker: Sienna
content: Why does it still hurt this much?

Sienna lowers her head, staring at the gaping hole in her chest. Ceto instinctively steps back, only to bump into something solid. She turns to find Miles standing behind her, with a dozen golden cans scattered at his feet.

speaker: Miles
content: Hey kid, you hungry? Remember these?
He nudges a can with his boot, sending it rolling to her feet. As Ceto bends to pick it up, the can suddenly splits open in her hands, a rotting fish head tumbling out.

speaker: Miles
content: The "spoils" I traded my life for... they were actually rotten long before I got them.
A wave of dizziness hits as the can grows leaden in Ceto's grip. She looks up to speak, to defend his effort, but Miles's face is already melting, distorting beyond recognition.

speaker: Herbert
content: Milly
Herbert is pinned between crushing doors, straining for a decaying family portrait floating in the Black Tide.
In an instant, the photo morphs into a rejected transfer request to return home, stamped "DENIED."
Ceto reaches out to catch it, but she's one step late. Another familiar figure appears before her.

speaker: Fynn
content: The year I found you in WhiteSands... you weren't even as tall as my sword.

speaker: Fynn
content: Everyone told me it was too dangerous to keep a child. I didn't listen. Other kids would scream at the sight of a Rancor, but you? You'd curl up next to one and sleep like a kitten.

speaker: Fynn
content: I thought you were our hope. So how could you... how could you leave them all to the Black Tide?
Fynn's hand closes around the Rancor at her waist.

speaker: Fynn
content: If that's how it's going to be, then fall in line. Don't we lighthouse keepers live and die together?
Steel shrieks against steel, sparks flying as the very space around them shudders. Fynn drives forward with terrifying strength, each blow forcing Ceto back a step.

speaker: Ceto
content: You're not Fynn...
Ceto parries "Fynn's" slash, using the momentum to pivot. She puts her entire weight into a fierce counter-thrust, driving her dagger toward the shadowy mimic.

speaker: Ceto
content: Her last wish... was for me to live.
<color=#dg1f1f>Hahahaha... Live as what? A walking tombstone?</color>
The shadow suddenly releases its weapon, impaling itself on Ceto's blade. As Ceto looks up, its features shift into the faces of her comrades, their blood now staining her hands.
Familiar, isn't it? That helplessness. Watching your comrades die, and you can do nothing.

speaker: Ceto
content: Get away from me! Don't you dare wear their faces. You're not worthy of their memory!

Ceto's blade cuts across the shadow's face. The phantom visage dissolves into black sludge, then reforms into a mirror image—a Ceto clad in a blood-drenched keeper's uniform, her pupils burning with the Rancor's crimson glow.

speaker: Ceto?
content: But I am you, Ceto. The last keeper. And you are powerless! The lighthouse? DisCity? All of it is meaningless!

speaker: Ceto?
content: So now you want to live? You've forgotten your past. But it's okay. I'll help you remember.
[Beach] [Filter] [Young Ceto]

speaker: Ceto
content: This is...

speaker: Ceto?
content: Don't recognize it? This was your first time, hahaha... Your first attempt to end it.

speaker: Ceto?
content: You were the only one left on the island. Alone. Dragging what was left of your friend to the farthest shore to bury her...

speaker: Ceto
content: I'm sorry, Sienna, for all our arguments... I promised Fynn I'd get you all out of here...

speaker: Ceto
content: There's one biscuit left. You always said... don't waste anything. Do you... want it?

speaker: Ceto?
content: Let me remind you. You ate the biscuit. Then you put your knife to your heart and lay down beside her. But the dawn came anyway. You woke up.

speaker: Ceto?
content: Hahaha... You really were born for this blade. A little blood is all it takes... to give you the strength to keep suffering.

speaker: Ceto
content: It's you... You're the one who's kept me alive...

speaker: Ceto?
content: What a perfect curse! A soul that longs for death, trapped in a body that refuses to die! You throw yourself into the hordes, praying for an end, and emerge without a scratch!
[Staircase] [Filter] [Young Ceto]

speaker: Ceto
content: I threw you away! I sank you in the Black Tide with their blades! Why did you come back?!

speaker: Ceto
content: You're never gonna let me go, are you?

speaker: Ceto?
content: Look how foolish you were then. This blade was forged with you on the battlefield, a final gift from your comrades. How could you possibly throw it away?

speaker: Ceto
content: I'll find a way anyway! I'll melt you down and feed your scrap to the sea monsters! I know what you are. You think wearing my face hides the stench, you damned Rancor? I know that pathetic whining anywhere!

speaker: Ceto?
content: That's right. I am your instinct. Your suppressed bloodlust. Your only faithful companion. And what can you do? You don't even dare to cry or laugh. Herbert taught you too well—every emotion is a liability. So you just... stopped talking.
[Inside the Lighthouse] [Filter]

speaker: Ceto
content: Ah...

speaker: Ceto
content: Ah... Ah!

speaker: Ceto?
content: You almost forgot how to make a sound! Did you think starvation was the answer? That denying this body would finally get rid of me and end it?

speaker: Ceto?
content: But I wanted you alive! I wanted you to see it all! Feel the sea breeze on an empty shore. Count supplies that will never be restocked. Tend a lighthouse for a city that forgot you! Waste away your meaningless existence!
[Lighthouse Top] [Filter]

speaker: Ceto
content: Report: Lighthouse OT-N07. One keeper remaining. No abnormalities observed. I... lost consciousness from hunger. Woke up with the taste of rancid monster meat in my mouth. No memory of eating them.

speaker: Ceto
content: Report: Lighthouse OT-N07. Rare sunshine today. Expect lighter monster activity at high tide. There are no abnormalities...

speaker: Ceto
content: Report: Lighthouse OT-N07. Sorted through the old belongings left by the others. Nothing of use. ...No abnormalities.

speaker: Ceto?
content: The keepers are gone. Your purpose died with them. So just end it. Isn't that what you've always wanted?
[Return to Consciousness World]

speaker: Ceto
content: Argh—!

Without warning, the dark shadow seizes control of Ceto's knife and—with brutal force—drives the blade deep into her shoulder. The weapon then twists viciously, grinding against bone and tearing through the flesh beneath her ravaged skin.

speaker: Ceto?
content: What a shame... The only reason I kept you alive was to feed on your despair. And now you want to live? To run away with some stray you just found? HAHAHAHAHA...

speaker: Ceto
content: What the hell do you want from me?!

speaker: Ceto?
content: What I have always wanted. Blood. Battle. I like your self-loathing, your isolation. But if you won't provide that feast... then this ends now.

speaker: Ceto?
content: This bloodlust is the true curse of the blade. And now, I'm taking my power back...!
The shadow then forces the bloodied dagger in her hand to turn, dragging it inch by agonizing inch toward her own throat.

speaker: Lighthouse Keeper
content: You never deserved to live in the first place.
[Consciousness World]
The blade hovers before Ceto's eye, its dark crimson surface reflecting her shattered form.
Within it, countless overlapping memories surface—
Her first moment on the battlefield, waking to Fynn lifting her into her arms...
Learning to wield a blade for the first time, fighting beside comrades she admired...
Her first true taste of despair, witnessing the face of war unmasked...
And the endless moments of ruin that followed.

speaker: Ceto
content: The smell of blood...
Dazed, she looks down at her body, a map of scars and fresh blood. Some wounds were carved by monsters of flesh, others by demons of the mind.
Her torn skin barely holds together the rotting flesh beneath, just as it strains to contain her splintered consciousness. Both teeter on the edge of ruin.
This time... it might be the real end for her.

speaker: Ceto
content: It's alright... I've already had a taste of it...

speaker: Ceto
content: ...What it feels like to want to live. To live for myself...
[Flashback]

speaker: Fynn
content: Everyone, starting today, <color=#fb9259>little Ceto</color> is officially a lighthouse keeper! Let's give her a proper welcome!

speaker: Ceto
content: Teach me. I want to join. I want to be like you.

speaker: Fynn
content: Now, this is an order... do not look back.

speaker: Ceto
content: ...Yes, Captain!

speaker: Herbert
content: Help me... find peace.

speaker: Ceto
content: Stop lecturing me! Push! We'll weld the door shut, and you'll be fine!

speaker: Ceto
content: Miles—!! Speed up! The tide's coming in! Hurry!

speaker: Miles
content: ...POWER—!!! TURN, YOU HUNK OF JUNK! BURN MY BLOOD TO STEAM—I'M GETTING—BACK—!!!

speaker: Ceto?
content: Why do you keep fighting? What has it ever gotten you? A number they can erase and reassign? Or just a body of scars that will never truly heal?

speaker: Ceto
content: ...Shut up.

speaker: Ceto?
content: Why persist as a walking corpse? Let go. You can finally be with them again. Isn't that what you've always wanted?
The blade draws ever closer. Ceto's vision floods with crimson as her body begins to fail, but just as she is about to collapse—
Whoosh—whoosh— A rhythmic sound rises from behind her.
[Back to Reality]
Three short... three long... three short...
It is the flag, still flapping in the wind, its sound flickering like a faint hope in the desperate darkness.

Through bloodshot, blurry eyes, she can just make out <color=#fb9259>that person</color> has not fallen. That frail, slight frame, which nearly broke upon the shore, still stands—defiant, resisting with stubborn resolve.
[Flashback]
You're still alive too. Lucky, aren't we?

speaker: Ceto
content: A nameless bastard has no right to touch the lighthouse.
Isn't a lighthouse meant to guide the lost? Right now, that's me.

speaker: Ceto
content: You're crazy.
I'll take "crazy" as a compliment. If this place is as bad as you say, a little madness might be the only thing that keeps you sane.

speaker: Ceto
content: ...And naive.
I can't stand here and judge your past. What's done is done. But I can prove myself to you. No matter what it takes, I am getting off this rock and finishing what I need to do.
Even when I was surrounded by those things under the sea, I never stopped wanting to see the sun the next morning. Far away, someone is still waiting for me. Someone who needs me.
I saw the inscriptions on the lighthouse's base. The past of the lighthouse keepers... A story DisCity doesn't even know anymore. But you still know.
You remember why they came, the duty they upheld. You're their living legacy.
Well, if it's a lighthouse keeper's specialty, we shouldn't let it go to waste.
Creating miracles is what humans do best.
[Return to Consciousness World] [Small CG: Ceto Alone]

Another, more furious attack crashes down. Ceto meets it with defiance. Excruciating pain tears through every nerve, but she grits through it, lifting her face to stare into those twin pools of crimson—eyes identical to her own.

speaker: Ceto
content: These scars... how could they be meaningless...

speaker: Ceto
content: Do you see that flag?
[Small CG: Chief Behind]
Through the chaos, the figure behind her stands unwavering, a spear-straight silhouette in a tattered coat.

With a sudden, explosive surge of strength, Ceto wrenches herself free from her enemy. Her free hand darts out, seizing the blade leveled at her chest. The edge slices deep into her palm. Blood wells, then falls in perfect, weightless drops, hanging suspended in the air.

speaker: Ceto
content: I'm not just guarding a lighthouse... I'm keeping a torch lit.
The hovering droplets of blood ignite into sudden, golden flame, and in their blaze, countless shards of memory flash into being.

speaker: Ceto
content: It's proof they ever existed.
[Small CG: Fallen Comrades Behind]

Bathed in the golden light, a legion of unyielding souls stands behind Ceto. They are a chorus of struggle, a testament of resistance, their collective will a force that lifts her and drives her forward. One by one, their faint, resolute lights converge upon her form.

speaker: Ceto
content: I'm still alive. I'm the only one left... the only one who remembers them...
Fynn's song, Herbert's family, Miles's recipe... These memories become her new marrow and blood, a fortifying strength that pulls her back from the abyss.

speaker: Ceto
content: They raised me. Their habits became mine. I am the last witness to their sacrifice!

The flames surge, flooding her entire consciousness. The countless silhouettes of fallen comrades spread like sparks upon dry tinder, igniting a wildfire that swells into a boundless, brilliant ocean of light.

speaker: Ceto
content: They pulled me from the contamination not to add another body to the grave, but to give hope one last chance to breathe. I've changed my mind, you damned Rancor. Hear this: I will live.

speaker: Ceto
content: As long as I live, the lighthouse keepers have not fallen! They stood to the end! They never deserted their post, never abandoned DisCity, never surrendered their honor!

speaker: Ceto
content: They will not be forgotten... Fragments of their will survive in me! And they will be with me forever!
Ceto shreds the shadow's disguise. As she launches her counterattack, the dog tags at her waist clash together in a violent, resonant chime.
The Rancor in her hand no longer gleams with bloody light, yet its blows fall with devastating precision, methodically driving the shadow into a corner.
At last, one shattering thrust breaks its defense completely, and Ceto presses her blade against the throat of her own destructive desires!

speaker: Ceto
content: I will live to honor the meaning of their lives. And then...

speaker: Ceto
content: I will find a meaning of my own. A voice of my own.
The Rancor flashes forward. Beneath its unwavering gleam, the shadow disintegrates into nothingness.

speaker: Ceto
content: You are the one who doesn't deserve to live!
[Back to Reality] [Eyes Opening CG]

Consciousness crashes back into her like a tide. Her blood-red pupils contract sharply; her eyes snap open. In the stark, blinding flashes of lightning, the silhouette before her slowly sharpens into focus.

speaker: Ceto
content: You're still here... Tougher than I thought.

She is a vision of gore, with shards of broken pipe jutting from her shoulder and abdomen. Yet a surge of adrenaline overpowers the agony. In one brutal motion, she wrenches a pipe free and rams it through the chest of a lunging monster, nailing its corpse to the window frame.
I told you I would be. I was waiting for you to wake up.
You are hollowed out by exhaustion, your body nearly numb. It is only when you hear movement behind you—a sound long absent—that your body reacts on pure instinct.

speaker: Ceto
content: ...The fleet?

You scrub a hand across your face, clearing the rain, only to feel the slick mix of blood and sweat seep through your fingers. There is no time for such concerns. You look up—and there, on the horizon, pinpoints of light pierce the gloom. The fleet is breaking through the Black Tide.
I can see them approaching. Looks like they've broken through the storm... Soon they'll be...
Cough!

The words die in your throat as a coppery tang floods your mouth. You double over, coughing, and a splatter of blood hits the ground. Ceto, too, has reached her limit. She watches you wipe your lips, and in return, offers a frail, pained smile.

speaker: Ceto
content: I see you now. Not a burden... but the most reliable guide in the storm. You should join the lighthouse keepers.
A lookout post with just two people? Sounds... not bad...
Ceto pushes herself upright, her bones protesting the strain. But as her fingers tighten around the hilt of her dagger, the old vulnerability—the confusion that once made her falter—simply vanishes.
The growing dawn catches the lighthouse keeper emblem on her tattered uniform, setting it ablaze with light.
You realize something fundamental has shifted within her. The blade no longer speaks for her; now, it carries her voice.
You did it, Ceto...

speaker: Ceto
content: Don't celebrate yet. It's not over.
I mean... you... you've found your voice again. You beat the Rancor...

Your taut nerves snap. The exhaustion you've held at bay for so long rushes in, an unstoppable tide. Your vision swims, the world tilts on its axis, and your body plummets toward the base of the lighthouse.
Through the descending haze, you see Ceto whirl around. Her blood-stained fingers stretch out, just brushing your sleeve as you fall...

speaker: Ceto
content: Hey! ${PlayerName}!!!
[Collapse] [Fade to Black, Unconscious]
[Heartbeat and Breathing Sounds]

speaker: Ceto
content: ...Who are you?
He never mentioned me to you?
female_content: She never mentioned me to you?

content: [Fade from Black] [Lighthouse Top at Sunrise] [Catherine Portrait]

speaker: Augustus
content: You've done well. We'll take it from here.

From below, the sounds of the landing troops and cleanup operations echo up the lighthouse. The moment Ceto's eyes find you, cradled safely in Augustus's arms, the last thread of tension holding Ceto together finally snaps. Her body goes limp as she finally surrenders to the darkness.
[Lighthouse Top at Sunrise]
Scorched awake by the piercing sun, you struggle to open leaden eyelids. The world slowly resolves from a blur of glare into a warm, bright clarity, illuminating every corner of the desolate island.
Ceto sits quietly beside you, seemingly awake for some time. Both your wounds have been neatly dressed—undoubtedly with high-grade medical supplies you'd never find around the lighthouse.

speaker: Ceto
content: Finally awake? The sun's practically baking your back.
Her tone is as rigid as ever, but you don't miss the faint, unguarded amusement at the corner of her lips.

You attempt to sit up, but barely an inch off the ground, every muscle in your body stages a mutiny. A delayed, crushing wave of pain washes over you. With a dull thud, you collapse back down, surrendering completely to the earth, splayed out like a starfish.

Sunlight cascades without restraint, warming your skin to the point of heat. The sensation is almost decadent. Gone is the chill of the Black Tide, the putrid sea breeze; all that remains is this pure, nearly scorching light. The perpetual shroud over this island has finally broken.

In the distance, the shoreline teems with methodical activity. The Rancor troops move with disciplined efficiency, scouring the last traces of contamination. The commander's voice, sharp and clear, crackles through a loudspeaker, signaling the operation's end.

speaker: Ceto
content: You won. DisCity came for OT-N07.
We both made it out alive. Our bet...
You stop mid-sentence. The recipe from Miles, the very prize of your bet, is now pointless. Its main ingredient, Tide Crawler, is being systematically erased from the world.

The bloodshed and chill of the long night have vanished, evaporated by the sun. You lie side-by-side, a wordless exhaustion intertwining with an equally profound gratitude, flowing silently between you.

This silence isn't empty, but full. It holds the taste of sunshine on each breath and the strong, steady beat of hearts beneath your ribs—a relentless reminder that you are alive, truly alive. The serenity of survival resonates more powerfully than any celebration could.
Next, I'm going to have some proper rest. A grand feast! And I'm sleeping for three days straight!
You start counting on your fingers:
First, a bowl of stew so hot it steams up the room, then honey wine so sweet it'll make your teeth hurt, and finally, a real, actual bed...

speaker: Ceto
content: I thought you had someone waiting for you. Important things to do.
You raise your hand, gazing at the power of the shackles in your palm—now faded to a dying ember, nearly gone.
Exactly. That's why I need to be at my best.
I have to be in top form... for when I go to bring her home.

speaker: Ceto
content: Home...
Her gaze drifts toward the skyline where DisCity rises, a land she has never set foot on, yet has carried on her shoulders for half a lifetime. It was her comrades' homeland. But where is her own?
What about you? The Black Tide is cleared. The lighthouse doesn't need to signal anymore. What's next?

speaker: Ceto
content: I think I'll look around.
Huh?

speaker: Ceto
content: I want to see what their loyalty and sacrifice actually bought, with my own eyes. Find a few places I actually want to go. Now that I'm free of this place... I want to see what's out there.
She holds the gleaming tags up to the sunlight, where the inscribed names seem to jostle and play, jockeying for the light.
[Shore]

The receded tide has laid bare a desolate seabed. Across the dried silt, the wreckage of the battlefield emerges: monster carcasses, scattered bleached bones, broken firearms, blades eaten by rust, and metal limbs so mangled their original forms are beyond recognition.
The Rancor ships have raised their flag, signaling their readiness to depart.
Are you sure you won't come with us? That uniform will make you a target out there.

speaker: Ceto
content: No. I was just an orphan the keepers took in. Just a lighthouse keeper. Nothing more.

speaker: Ceto
content: I'm not chasing the power in this blade. I'm looking for a new lighthouse.
She looks toward the bow of the ship, and you follow her gaze. Catherine is standing there, waving to you, waiting for you to rejoin the team.

speaker: Ceto
content: Do you trust her? That she can really help bring your friend back?

speaker: Ceto
content: Fair enough. There are no prophets on the battlefield. Good luck, then.

speaker: Ceto
content: We'll meet again, Chief of the Minos Bureau of Crisis Control. I made a deal with your general.
A deal?

speaker: Ceto
content: If you want to know, come help me.
She ignores your question and walks straight onto the mudflats, pushing aside the damp sand to retrieve a long blade, rusted and dulled beyond any sharpness.

speaker: Ceto
content: Take these Rancors left on the battlefield. Bring them where they're needed most.
The morning sunlight falls obliquely across your bodies, illuminating your repeated motions—bending down, picking up, wiping the mud from each weapon.

You do not press her for what passed between her and Augustus.
Behind you, the weather-beaten lighthouse stands its silent watch. Ahead lies an old battlefield, and a new journey.
[DisCorps Conference Room]
<size=45>Operation BR-005 commences in...</size>
5 days 5 hours 7 minutes

speaker: Scarface
content: Wait, what? They were already messing with Aurum Secretum back then?!

speaker: Military Doctor
content: The sorcery patterns are similar, but this is clearly a failed prototype. The samples we retrieved only prove someone tried to merge contamination with a nuclear warhead a long time ago—a two-pronged approach.

speaker: Augustus
content: Perhaps we can consider a bolder theory. The nuke was just a pretext. Their real objective was the Mania contamination all along.

speaker: Military Doctor
content: Talk about malicious intent. So, what do we do with these Rancors? Do we keep them?

speaker: Augustus
content: Of course. We can never have too much gear.
The Black Tide was also Adelaide's doing? That bastard...

A slender form detaches itself from the shadows, and the room hushes, as if a taut string had been plucked. The newcomer's physical injuries have healed, but the person within has grown more fractured. While all others avert their gaze, Augustus alone remains a steady gravitational force, faced with the primed explosive.

speaker: Augustus
content: Not necessarily. But if you need a target for your frustration, be my guest.

speaker: Augustus
content: If a failed Aurum Secretum experiment can cause a mess like the Black Tide, then this little excursion is about to get serious. So, what do you say? Still up for it, little Chief?

speaker: Augustus
content: Or should I get used to calling you "Commander"?
[Chief's Military Uniform Portrait]
In a cemetery outside DisCity, a new stone monument stands quietly. Its strikingly traditional design sets it in silent dissonance against the modern markers that surround it.

This monument was originally intended for the city's memorial park, but the request was denied. The applicant had wished for these names to rest far from the echoes of war, believing they belonged among the ordinary citizens they once were.

The stone has been meticulously cleaned, revealing rows of freshly engraved names. Before it, an array of offerings is spread out: hamburgers, fried chicken, the latest fashion magazines, game cartridges, cosmetics, cigarettes, and alcohol...
Only when not an inch of space remains does the visitor finally cease, leaving the memorial laden with the tokens of a life lived.

speaker: Ceto
content: It'll be a while before I can visit again. So don't you bastards go talking shit about me.

speaker: Ceto
content: I think I found a new lighthouse. I'm going to see if they've got a place for someone like me.

speaker: Ceto
content: You know I don't have much to offer. Guarding a lighthouse. Fighting... That's about it.
Words linger on her lips, but time denies them. She rises solemnly, her gaze fixed on the names etched in stone, paying a moment of silent respect.

speaker: Ceto
content: I told you we'd meet again.
At her waist, the badge of her new squad, Broken Blade, catches the light.
Success is not final. Failure is not fatal. It is the courage to continue that counts.
<size=45>Operation BR-005 commences in...</size>
<color=#dg1f1f>0:00:00</color>
[Black Screen]

speaker: Electronic Voice
content: Access Permit B95601 validated. Welcome, ${PlayerName}. You are cleared for entry into the restricted area.

speaker: Electronic Voice
content: Biometric authentication complete. Area scan is clear. The transport is now ready. For your safety, please stand clear of the platform edges during transit.
[Slow Transition] [Deep Restricted Area Background]
The elevator groans as it descends into the abyss, a deep rumble echoing through the shaft. Finally, a colossal, ring-shaped confinement structure materializes from the gloom.

Peering through the glass, you see no ordinary prisoners in the cells that line the ring. Instead, each cell seethes with raw, untamed Mania that pulses and swirls, threatening to breach its confines.

The <color=#fb9259>Deep Restricted Area</color>. Located in the deepest sub-levels of the MBCC, this facility has now been unlocked, a testament to your newly elevated clearance and the trust placed in you by EDGE.

speaker: Schorl
content: Before the shackles appeared, we lacked effective means to control highly dangerous and difficult-to-manage Sinners. For humanitarian reasons, execution was not an option. So, cryosleep technology was employed to preserve them in stasis. A practice that continues to this day.

speaker: Schorl
content: With the latest <color=#fb9259>LINK</color> technology, we can now attempt to enter their deep consciousness and awaken their minds.

speaker: Schorl
content: Due to your excellent performance during the previous incident, Paradeisos has authorized another LINK attempt. You will delve into a Sinner's consciousness to obtain the intelligence we require.
You step from the elevator and follow a track deep into the facility, stopping at last before an enormous stasis tank.
Through the semi-transparent glass, the form of a pale body is visible, suspended in liquid.
(Small CG: Tank)

Her skin is deathly white, a stark contrast to the pitch-black Mania that seeps from her, filling the container with its dark aura. Her eyelids are sealed shut, yet they flutter with a subtle, restless tremor, as if she is adrift in a dream that has lasted for decades.
Who is she?

speaker: Schorl
content: <color=#fb9259>Hilda Hartlein</color>. She was a cryptography expert working for the metropoles during the First Outland War.

speaker: Schorl
content: She is the one who cracked DisCity's supposedly unbreakable encryption and led the development of the new "Monolith" system. While she was active, DisCity's intelligence was virtually an open book to the metropoles.

speaker: Schorl
content: In N.F. 71, she was captured on the outskirts of the city after a tip-off to the intelligence department. She resisted arrest, using her power to generate an extraordinarily powerful Mania field. The casualties were devastating.

speaker: Schorl
content: Post-capture, she attempted a Corruptor transformation during interrogation. Given the invaluable intelligence in her mind, we were left with no choice but to place her in cryosleep and detain her here. She has remained in the Restricted Area for decades.
(Small CG: Tank disappears)

You review the files provided by Schorl. While they contain Hilda's biographical background and some limited information on farland intelligence agencies, historical materials from that era remain scarce, likely due to inconsistent record-keeping.

In contrast, the LINK user manual is remarkably comprehensive. It's clear that following your previous experience, the system has undergone significant upgrades across the board, with a distinct focus on enhancing your safety during the process.
What is Paradeisos expecting from this mission?

speaker: Schorl
content: We hope you can extract more information on the "Monolith" system and "Outlands Sinners." Specifically, we need to understand how the metropoles secured the allegiance of such a powerful Sinner in an era when they were exceptionally rare, and whether any secret technology was involved.

speaker: Schorl
content: Should you succeed in turning her allegiance, having her work for us upon awakening would be an ideal outcome. However, we recommend you make that judgment call based on the situation you encounter.

speaker: Schorl
content: Finally, the decision to <color=#fb9259>keep her alive</color> or <color=#fb9259>eliminate her completely</color> is also yours to make.

options: Sounds like a special kind of interrogation.

speaker: Schorl
content: Your assessment is absolutely correct. The upgraded LINK system does possess this functionality. We are very much looking forward to your performance, Chief ${PlayerName}.

As Schorl speaks, it guides you to an experimental apparatus that feels somewhat familiar. Research assistants move with quiet efficiency, conducting their final preparations, while the other end of the machinery is already connected to Hilda's containment tank.
A deep, resonant hum fills the air as the instruments within the glass chamber power up, establishing a link between your consciousness and Hilda's.
The world around you dissolves, its colors and shapes bleeding away into nothing. When your awareness sharpens again, you are adrift in an absolute, boundless darkness.
[Black Screen, Downpour]
The very air in this nearly shattered consciousness space is thick and damp, heavy with the raw scent of rainwater.
Unsteady fragments of light drift like dust motes nearby, their faint glow a fragile defense against the consuming darkness that lurks just beyond.
A primal instinct screams that danger hides within that void. Compelled, you move forward, using the drifting points of light as your guide deeper into the consciousness.
[White Interaction Point]
As you touch the luminous specks, it resonates with a soft chime, and a cascade of human voices whispers faintly from the shadows, echoing from all directions at once.

speaker: Unknown Inquirer
content: State your name.

speaker: Female Voice
content: Hilda Hartlein.
[Second Interaction Point]

speaker: Unknown Inquirer
content: What is your identity?

speaker: Female Voice
content: I will head to the DisCity University as a researcher, studying radio waves and communications.
[Third Interaction Point]

speaker: Unknown Inquirer
content: What is your actual mission?

speaker: Female Voice
content: To monitor signal intelligence within DisCity for the metropoles, decrypt secure communications, and relay all pertinent data to the Intelligence Security Agency.

speaker: Female Voice
content: <color=#fb9259>And concurrently... to prove my "value" to the city-state.</color>
(Slow fade to white, then display contamination CG)
Pushing through the weak, lingering fragments of her consciousness, you finally find purchase in the endless dark. A single, solid foothold.
(Animated CG: Contamination, gradually shaking to focus on the face)
There, you find her.

She is curled within a nest of sludge, a manifestation of pure Mania. A grotesque armor of contamination and sharpened thorns encases her body, their hostile posture a clear warning against any approach.

speaker: Chief
content: Hilda, is that you?
Her eyelids flutter faintly at the sound of your voice. But no other movement follows.
She is a spy from the metropoles; caution is a courtesy you cannot afford. You unleash your shackles against the filth blocking your path.

The shackles quickly clear the oozing Mania, but when it strikes the thorns surrounding her, it dissipates harmlessly. You realize with a start: these thorns are not Mania binding her, but a defense born from something else entirely.
Reason requires a listening ear and a coherent mind. The woman before you clearly possesses neither.
(All options exhausted)
After your futile attempts, the nearly-lost woman finally stirs. Her eyes shift, and her gaze, faint but unmistakable, lands directly on you.

speaker: Hilda
content: This is... inside my own mind.

speaker: Hilda
content: Who... are you? How did you... get in here?

options: Reveal your true identity and demand her cooperation
Make up an identity she might accept

content: Option B - Hide Identity
You step back into the desolate landscape of Hilda's mind. This time, wiser from your last encounter, you craft an identity she might trust—
A fellow spy from the Metropole Alliance who infiltrated DisCity's prison. Then, you reveal your true purpose.

speaker: Chief
content: ...The truth is, I need your memories. Your work on "Monolith" could be the key to turning the tide against DisCity.

speaker: Hilda
content: Are you telling me... the war... is still going on?
You give a slow, confirming nod.

speaker: Chief
content: The best support a child can get is from their parents.

speaker: Chief
content: Your mind, your work... they're vital. And right now, I'm your only chance to get out from under DisCity's thumb.
She falls into a deep silence. The dark Mania around her seethes in response, a turbulent mirror of her inner conflict.
You hold your ground, waiting.

speaker: Hilda
content: My memories are just fragments now. This... is the only one that hasn't completely faded...

speaker: Hilda
content: If... this broken place holds what you're searching for, then I suppose this is the only choice...

Then, with a gesture from her, the stagnant sludge convulses. It vomits forth the buried contents of this darkness: bricks and rubble, mountains and flowers, the sun, the moon, and a blanket of stars—a cosmology of her past.
Though the ground thunders with the rise of spectral ruins, her voice cuts through the cacophony, perfectly clear.

speaker: Hilda
content: Do you have any idea what you're about to walk into?

speaker: Chief
content: Whatever it may be, I'm willing to face it for the city-state.

speaker: Hilda
content: Then... let's go.
—To that inescapable, stormy night.

N.F. 71, on the eve of DisCity's independence.

With the warfront collapsing, the Metropole Alliance was staring into the abyss of inevitable defeat.

After DisCity's forces intercepted a series of nuclear strikes, it became clear that only a weapon capable of countering their anomalous power wielders could change the course of the war.

In a final, desperate gamble, the Metropole Alliance marshaled its remaining forces for a massive, surprise attack.

To shroud the operation in absolute secrecy, they turned to a team of elite cryptographers, tasking them with a new, unbreakable cipher. They called it—


<size=52>Monolith</size>.
[Radio]
The Monolith awaits. Report immediately.
[Scene Change: Mountain Path]
The evening is cloudy, with a fine, sparse rain drifting in the air.
You trudge up the rugged, muddy path toward the hilltop manor. In the distance, the purr of luxury cars echoes, but none turn onto this forgotten track.
This is DisCity's remote outskirts, where the roads remain stubbornly wild. In the failing twilight, the shadows of withered trees sway, weaving an atmosphere thick with unease.
—A perfect hideout for spies, you think.
Leaning against a gnarled tree to catch your breath, you finally manage to flag down a passing car.

speaker: Unassuming Young Man
content: Hi... you... you can see me? Are you alright?
The window slides down to reveal a man in his twenties, so thoroughly ordinary he's almost invisible. His face is the kind you forget the moment you look away.
But his presence here, now, tells you everything. You're almost certain he's another Outland spy, here for the Monolith.
A ride is an obvious advantage. And if you can turn the journey into an opportunity to gather information, infiltrating the manor will be that much simpler.

speaker: Unassuming Young Man
content: Oh... you got this telegram too. Well, it seems we're in the same line of work.

speaker: Unassuming Young Man
content: Vilensoff? Not many know about that place. If you don't mind me asking, what brings you out this way?
As he speaks, the young man's fingers stray absently toward his breast pocket. A gun? A transmitter?

speaker: Chief
content: Because I received a secret telegram.

speaker: Unassuming Young Man
content: That's it... Well, it seems we're in the same line of work.

speaker: Unassuming Young Man
content: Get in. I'll take you there. And if you don't mind, I've got some spare clothes in the back.
female_content: Get in. I'll take you there. And if you don't mind, I've got some of my girlfriend's spare clothes in the back.

content: [Scene Transition: Car Interior]
You quickly change into the spare clothes he provided in the back seat.
female_content: To give you privacy, the young man steps out of the car and turns his back to the window. You quickly change into the spare clothes he provided in the back seat.

content: The outfit is perfectly, extraordinarily ordinary, a mirror of the man himself. It's the kind of bland, nondescript attire that lets you vanish into a crowd the moment you look away.

speaker: Edward
content: The name's Edward Simmons. And you are? ...Oh, it's perfectly fine if you'd rather not answer. I understand. We're not exactly in a profession that encourages sharing.

speaker: Chief
content: My name is ${PlayerName}.

speaker: Edward
content: Hmm... Can't say I've heard the name before, but then again, that doesn't mean much in our line of work. The name I just gave you isn't the one I was born with, either.

speaker: Chief
content: You can call me "Gray Coat."

speaker: Edward
content: Hmm, can't say I've heard the codename before, but then again, that doesn't mean much in our line of work. The name I just gave you isn't the one I was born with, either.

speaker: Edward
content: Honestly, by the time we get to the manor, I doubt we'll meet a single person who's using their real name.
Despite his claim that your profession doesn't really "encourage sharing," Edward proves to be a relentless chatterbox, probing you with casual conversation throughout the drive.
You offer cautious, non-committal replies at first, but soon realize it might just be his nature. Eventually, you close your eyes, feigning sleep to end the charade.
[Black Screen Transition: Manor Exterior]
The car rumbles to a halt at the manor gates after a half-hour journey.
The manor looms, a relic of brick and stone. Under the watchful eyes of two fully armed guards, you and Edward are ushered into the main hall.
[Manor Hall]
A handful of figures are already scattered through the hall.

Some observe from solitary perches; others speak in hushed tones within small circles. In both attire and manner, every person maintains a carefully constructed plainness—a collective effort to remain unmemorable.
The most fundamental rule of espionage is to blend in.
And now that rule applies to <color=#fb9259>you</color> as well.
A glance at your own outfit confirms it... Thanks to Edward, you are perfectly camouflaged.
This is Hilda's memory. LINK has recreated the pivotal days in this manor that culminated in the birth of "Monolith."
Your objective is to unearth her secrets and extract the vital intelligence from this period.
Now, you decide to...

options: Observe the people sitting alone in corners
Observe the people gathered in groups

content: A grim-faced man with cropped hair occupies a corner. His bearing immediately sets him apart; he carries himself not like a bureaucrat, but with the sharp alertness of the room's guards, likely a soldier or field operative.
He fidgets incessantly: rolling an unlit cigarette between his fingers, his hand then straying to absently touch his collar.
In another corner, a short-haired young woman sits with unnerving stillness. Her sharp eyes have been actively scanning the room since she arrived, missing nothing.

options: Observe the people gathered in groups

content: Nearby, a circle of socialites, draped in elegant attire, is chatting with practiced ease.

speaker: Well-dressed Businessman
content: Let's be pragmatic. The outcome on the front is a foregone conclusion... The question for the Alliance now isn't if, but how we negotiate our position with DisCity.

speaker: Well-dressed Businessman
content: No one seriously believes the "Monolith" is for fighting. It's a deterrent. A... well, a rather powerful bargaining chip, that's all.

speaker: Elderly Scholar
content: Mind your tone, Mr. Johnson. This is not the place for such defeatist talk.

speaker: Elderly Scholar
content: A single setback is not a surrender. Our intelligence operations have been cultivated for decades. We have the network, the resources to wage a protracted campaign from the shadows if it comes to that.

speaker: Elderly Scholar
content: Our resolve is our greatest weapon. We must not waver. Victory in the next phase depends on it.
A modest offering of coffee and sugar is laid out for guests.
The coffee is a bitter, dark liquid made from stewed lettuce, and the accompanying sugar cubes are just cheap, questionable candies—a telling detail of the shortages.
You've only just put down the dreadful cup when you glance up. A figure now stands on the second-floor staircase, looking down upon the hall.

speaker: Hilda
content: Good evening, ladies and gentlemen. I am Hilda Hartlein. My thanks to you all for accepting my invitation.
Her voice, cool and clear as a chime, cuts through the hall. Instantly, the room freezes, every gaze drawn to the top of the central staircase.
This is your first time seeing her true form, not as a prisoner in a canister, or a soul drowning in filth.

An oversized coat hangs from her slender frame, making her seem unbearably fragile. Her skin is deathly pale, almost translucent, and her eyes hold the eerie, grayish-red hue of a specter. Merely standing seems to require a monumental effort, as if a faint breeze could dissolve her into nothing.
She offers a slow, courteous bow to the assembled crowd.

speaker: Hilda
content: I know the "Monolith" is the subject on everyone's mind. But first, allow me to provide some necessary context for this gathering.

speaker: Hilda
content: Since the Nightfall, human civilization has suffered a devastating blow. We watched nations dissolve into scattered settlements and struggling city-states, each fighting for its own survival.

speaker: Hilda
content: It was Dr. Keylan's discovery of the Hypercube that finally reunited us. It gave us a common purpose: to build DisCity and forge the City-State Coalition. We were meant to stand as a unified front, a testament to humanity's resilience.

speaker: Hilda
content: We operated on a foundation of shared knowledge and rational trade. DisCity, as the sole source of Hypercubes, was a partner—not a master.

speaker: Hilda
content: But that foundation is now being deliberately dismantled.

A strategic wartime map unfolds behind her, detailing the metropoles and their territories. Several zones are highlighted in alarming red and orange, indicating active conflicts and military stalemates. Her red-gloved hand glides over the chart, bypassing other hotspots to settle unerringly on the most critical location in the bottom-right quadrant: DisCity.

speaker: Hilda
content: There are forces among us sowing division under the false banner of "independence." They are pitting brother against sister, severing the very bonds that made us strong.

speaker: Hilda
content: They have reignited old hatreds between city-states, reducing a united front to squabbling fragments. They profit from the chaos they create, while civilians pay the price, displaced by the flames of war.

speaker: Hilda
content: We cannot, and we will not, allow this to continue.

speaker: Hilda
content: However, our efforts have been compromised. A mole within our operation has been leaking Monolith intelligence, coordinating attacks against our interests.
The room holds its breath. But no one is surprised.

speaker: Hilda
content: To mitigate the ongoing security risk, I requested the relocation of the entire project. This "safe house" was selected for its defensibility and isolation, creating a contained environment to secure the Monolith's development.

speaker: Hilda
content: Now, with the Monolith in its final testing phase, I advised my superiors that we issue assistance directives laced with critical data to "invite" all of you here.

speaker: Hilda
content: It was, of course, a calculated risk. I am operating on the assumption that our mole would find such bait irresistible, and would inevitably be drawn into our midst. This presents our best opportunity to identify, capture, and eliminate the threat.

speaker: Hilda
content: Now, if you will all remain calm and in place, we will begin the verification process.
(Show individual portraits one after another)
An uncanny silence holds the room. Hilda descends the stairs, offering nods to a few—familiar faces—while approaching others for quiet inquiries.
You watch, your focus sharpening as you note her method: she uses gloved hands to briefly touch the hems or collars of their clothing, exchanging a hushed word before moving on.
Then, her path leads inevitably to you.

The memory of the fidgeting man, his collar his tell, clicks into place. A classic place for a poison pill. In a flash of insight, you palm the small candy from your pocket and covertly slide it into your own collar.
Hilda stands before you, her face a mask of confusion.

speaker: Hilda
content: ...You're a face I don't recognize. You weren't on my list. And you... you don't carry yourself like an agent or spy.
Her voice remains soft. She reaches out, not as a gesture of affection, but of inspection, neatly straightening your collar.

speaker: Hilda
content: Your poison pill is larger than standard issue. Not an expert at concealment, are you? You must be from a different agency... or something else entirely.

speaker: Hilda
content: So, let's not waste time. Who are you, truly?
You had the look, the mannerisms—enough to pass a casual inspection. But it's painfully clear that it isn't enough for Hilda. You need a story, an "identity" that fits into this web of deceit.

Everyone here is an undercover agent personally selected by her, each with a prior history with Monolith. You, an outsider who knows none of them and has never interacted with Monolith, need a plausible role. The most logical choice seems to be...

options: I'm an undercover agent, infiltrating the DisCity Intelligence Bureau.
I'm an "anomalous power expert" sent by the metropoles.

content: The Metropole Alliance, currently facing devastating losses against Augustus and her Reaper forces, is in a desperate position. Their understanding of Mania is limited, but they recognize its potential as a weapon. This desperation creates a critical opportunity for you.

speaker: Chief
content: As you know, the Alliance has recently suffered repeated attacks from individuals with... anomalous capabilities. A new department was quietly formed to investigate these DisCity phenomena.

speaker: Chief
content: I am ${PlayerName}, the lead specialist appointed to the case.

speaker: Chief
content: We detected a significant surge of anomalous power around this estate. Given the importance of your meeting, command sent me to assess the situation.
You aren't lying, not truly. This entire manor has been steeped in Hilda's Mania from the start, where anomalies may occur at any moment.
As you expected, your mention of "anomalous power" draws a measured glance from Hilda.

speaker: Elegant Lady
content: An "anomalous power expert"? ...Have you all heard of such a thing?

speaker: Well-dressed Businessman
content: DisCity's new assets have been a strategic nightmare... It's logical that the higher-ups would seek their own countermeasures. Still... an "expert"? Unverified.

speaker: Hilda
content: Understood, Mr. ${PlayerName}. Thank you for coming and offering your assistance.
female_content: Understood, Ms. ${PlayerName}. Thank you for coming and offering your assistance.

content: As skeptical murmurs ripple through the crowd, she offers a single, slow nod. Her expression remains an unreadable mask of ice. Whether she believes you or is merely playing along is impossible to discern. Without another word, she turns and withdraws from the gathering, returning to her place on the steps.

speaker: Hilda
content: My task is to complete the final integration testing and core calibration of the "Monolith" prototype within the next three days. The mole's objective will be equally clear—to either seize or sabotage it. Therefore, I will be staying in my room, dutifully serving as bait.

speaker: Hilda
content: I am, as you know, a cryptographer. My skills are in ciphers and systems, not counter-surveillance. Many of you are far more capable in that field. The mole is one, while the innocent are many. I would welcome the assistance of anyone in this room who considers themselves blameless.

speaker: Hilda
content: If you are uncertain how to proceed, then the best course of action is simple inaction. Wait. Watch. The day the "Monolith" is erected will be eventful enough, I promise you that.
Her gaze sweeps across the room, deliberate and assessing, before finally settling on you.

speaker: Hilda
content: Let's hope our collaboration over the next few days is a productive one.
The moment Hilda departs, a tense, murmuring energy fills the room. The crowd, once a unified audience, fractures into hushed clusters, dissecting her shocking announcement.
The mundane pretense of the seminar is gone, stripped away to reveal the raw anxiety of a mole hunt that now poisons the air, evident in every nervous gesture and whispered word.

speaker: Edward
content: Ah, ${PlayerName}... so that's your real name. Do you mind if I call you Officer ${PlayerName}?
Someone you don't remember is suddenly at your side, making you jump. Has he been here the entire time?

speaker: Chief
content: A name doesn't matter much. What matters is knowing who you are and what you're here to do.

speaker: Edward
content: Meeting you truly feels like a stroke of luck, Officer. Though the rain chose such an inconvenient moment, it brought me here right to you, Officer ${PlayerName}. It's almost as if fate intended—
You cut short his sentimental speech, gesturing for him to look at several people standing nearby.

speaker: Chief
content: Do you know them?
Hilda is the bait. This entire gathering is a trap designed by her to force the agency's mole into the open.
Right now, your top priority is to gather intelligence—on Hilda, on every guest present. The source is irrelevant; the information is everything.
Just then, Edward lets out a distinctly delighted "Aha!"

speaker: Edward
content: Since arriving, I've made a point to speak with quite a few people, learn their public roles. Which one would you like to know about, Officer?

Hilda, a Sevael citizen and member of the Cryptography Department, specializes in codebreaking and engineering. Despite her talents, she has been denied promotions due to her parents' political stigma. Two years ago, she was transferred from the metropoles to DisCity, where she decrypted numerous classified communications and was promoted to senior officer. Six months ago, she was assigned to lead the secret "Monolith" project.

Manphist, a Sevael citizen and former head of the Cryptography Department, is a training instructor who was rehired after retirement. For several years, he has been undercover in DisCity. Renowned for his talent in spotting potential, he has cultivated numerous skilled spies for the metropoles.

Johnson, a Fraser socialite and director of the Wartime Economic Intelligence Center, serves as an economic advisor. A notorious playboy, he controls various financial channels and implements wartime sanctions against DisCity through economic pressure and smuggling operations.

options: Time is running short. Could you compile a report for me later?

content: Helene, a DisCity native and junior officer in the Operations Department, was referred by Hilda. Skilled in song and dance, she frequents entertainment venues to charm high-ranking officials for intelligence. As a recent recruit, she only has access to low-level information.

Edward, a Sevael citizen referred by Manphist, is trained in stealth operations and theft. Deployed to DisCity three years ago, he infiltrated the Foreign Affairs Bureau as a diplomatic assistant to gather and relay intelligence.
It's remarkable how accurate Edward's briefings are, given how concise they are. The fact that he can organize intelligence on so many people in such a short time is extraordinary...

speaker: Chief
content: This guy really does have a knack for intelligence work...
Suddenly, the crowd erupts in a crash of overturned furniture and shattering glass.

speaker: Gangster-looking Man
content: You got a death wish? Say that again. I dare you.

speaker: Caustic Middle-aged Man
content: I'll say it as many times as it takes. Her family's name is dirt. Everyone knows her parents were traitors who fled to DisCity. How do we know she's not just like them? What gives her the right to investigate us?

speaker: Gangster-looking Man
content: Go ahead and walk out. But you won't be leaving with your life.

speaker: Caustic Middle-aged Man
content: Marlo, have you lost your mind? Hilda's your boss, not your mom. Is she really worth dying for?!
A cold, furious laugh escapes Marlo. He pulls his pistol from its holster and, with a definitive crack, slams it onto the tabletop.

speaker: Gangster-looking Man
content: Let's get one thing straight: I'm not as nice as Hilda. I don't buy that "one mole hiding among innocents" crap. Far as I'm concerned, you're all suspects. Anyone tries to leave, I'll put a bullet in your head. Simple.

speaker: Chief
content: Who is he?

speaker: Edward
content: That's Marlo Bannings. I heard he and Hilda went to school together. He leads the Operations Department, has quite the reputation. But that tough act? Could all be a show, who knows...

speaker: Edward
content: The other one's embedded in DisCity's Propaganda Department. Name's... Horne, I think. Arrogant type. Looks down on just about everyone.
Before you've even finished with Edward, Marlo and Horne are already at each other's throats.

The outcome was inevitable: a desk jockey against an elite operative. Horne never stood a chance. Marlo dismantles him with brutal efficiency, and within seconds, a bloodied Horne crashes to the ground at your feet.

speaker: Horne
content: Help... help me...
His hand claws at your pant leg in desperation. But as you look down, you feel it unmistakably: <color=#fb9259>a strange fluctuation of Mania</color>.
Marlo is already moving, a tempest of rage. The slide of his pistol racks back with a sharp, metallic clack. There's no time to react.

options: I'm not going to let someone die in front of me.

content: This confined area offers no margin for error. A single bullet could spell disaster for everyone.
The calculation is instant. You surge to your feet, placing your own body as a shield in front of Horne.

speaker: Marlo
content: Out of my way!

speaker: Chief
content: He just wants to leave. You can question him or even detain him if necessary. But point that gun at him? I'll start thinking you want a witness silenced, not caught.

speaker: Marlo
content: The **** did you just say?

speaker: Manphist
content: Now, now, let's all be reasonable. ${PlayerName}'s right. We're colleagues here, are we not? There's no need for this.

speaker: Marlo
content: You might be his colleague. I'm not. Why don't you ask him what he's so afraid of that he's gotta run like a rat?
Paying no mind to Marlo's seething anger, your focus drops to the bruised form of Horne. You kneel and help the battered man stand.

speaker: Chief
content: It's alright now, Mr. Horne.

speaker: Chief
content: I know hearing there's a mole is difficult. But leaving like this just makes you look guilty.

speaker: Chief
content: If you're innocent, running is the worst thing you could do. You'd be doing the real mole's job for them.

speaker: Horne
content: You have no idea... no idea what they're like. Guilty or innocent... it doesn't matter! They'll skin me alive either way!

speaker: Chief
content: It's too late to walk away. Even if you get past Marlo, do you think Hilda will let anyone leave?

speaker: Chief
content: Fighting your way out won't work. You'd be playing right into the mole's hands. Better to just stay and wait for the Monolith to be completed. Then we all leave properly.
A film of cold sweat glistens on Horne's forehead. He dabs at it with a shaky hand, his lips quivering before he asks you cautiously.

speaker: Horne
content: You... you swear? You'll back me on this?

speaker: Chief
content: Of course. I know you're not the mole. Just keep your head. Don't let someone else manipulate you into a mistake.

speaker: Chief
content: If you trust me, we can discuss everything in detail later. Right now, let's focus on staying alive.
Horne's eyes dart between you and Marlo, wild with panic. Sweat streams down his face. You can hear his teeth grinding as he fights some internal, agonizing war.
In that moment of tension, you feel it again—that faint Mania fluctuation. Unmistakable now, it leaks from his pocket.

speaker: Horne
content: No! I won't be trapped! You're all in on it! DIE—!
Then, the air grows cold. A bone-deep chill of pure Mania prepares to tear itself free from his body.

speaker: Hilda
content: Move aside.
The command is cold, flat. A gunshot cracks the air. A bloody crater blossoms in Horne's forehead, halting the transformation instantly.
A spray of thick, black fluid hits your face, and his corpse collapses like a cut marionette, striking the ground with a sickening crunch.

speaker: Edward
content: Officer ${PlayerName}! Good heavens, that was far too close! Are you hurt? Here, let me get that for you.
During Edward's frantic attempts to clean your face, your eyes are drawn upward, to the second-floor corridor.

There, Hilda stands silhouetted at the top of the stairs, the faint wisp of smoke still curling from her gun's barrel. Her brow is furrowed in a deep, contemplative frown as she watches Horne's Mania-consumed body.
Then, she lowers the weapon and turns her gaze to you.

speaker: Hilda
content: Mr. ${PlayerName}, please come with me for a moment.
female_content: Ms. ${PlayerName}, please come with me for a moment.

content: [Hilda's Room]

Hilda's room, located at the far end of the manor's second floor, is an elegantly furnished space filled with classified documents. At its center stands a black machine, roughly half a person's height, pulsing with a cold, metallic glow.
So this is the Monolith?

The assessment is swift. It's too large to transport, not yet fully developed, and you have no intention of delivering an incomplete product to Schorl. Most pressingly, you still lack an escape plan from the manor itself.
For now, the only viable strategy is patience. Accepting Hilda's invitation, you settle into the seat opposite her.
[CG: Interrogation]

From across the desk, the details you missed on the staircase become starkly clear: the delicate tracery of blue veins visible beneath her pallid skin, her thin and bloodless lips. She resembles a figure newly risen from a grave, exuding a chill that feels less like temperature and more like the absence of life.

speaker: Hilda
content: ${PlayerName}, do you know why I asked to speak with you privately?

options: Is this about the anomalous power on Horne?

content: Thank you for the intervention with Horne. But I have to ask... won't eliminating a man like that so directly create complications?

speaker: Hilda
content: Horne's fate was a consequence of his own actions. You aren't responsible for that.

speaker: Hilda
content: However, you were there. I'm sure you observed the same thing I did. His death wasn't conventional. It was tied to an anomalous power.
Hilda's Trust +1

speaker: Hilda
content: ...You are quite perceptive.
(Paths converge)
After Horne's berserk episode, and given your self-claimed expertise in anomalous power, she's now waiting for your professional assessment.

speaker: Chief
content: The infection in Horne was superficial. It just amplified his existing emotions. Under its influence, his own anxiety and tension hit a breaking point... that's what caused his extreme behavior.

speaker: Chief
