content: You idiot! Are you trying to get yourself killed?!
With reddened eyes, Helene sits down beside him and lights the cigarette for him.

speaker: Marlo
content: Heh... after all this time... never learned to do anything but kill. Guess you could call it playing to my strengths.

speaker: Marlo
content: I've spent half my life killing. My hands are stained, my soul is stained. Can't wash it clean. When I die, hell's the only place that'll have me...

speaker: Marlo
content: Hilda, I... I've always been on the level. The ones I didn't kill, I didn't. The ones I did, I own up to every one.

speaker: Marlo
content: Remember this... I'm not the mole... I... never betrayed the city-state...

speaker: Hilda
content: ...I know. Why else would I have untied you?

speaker: Marlo
content: Heh... Heh, good... Looks like... this was part of your plan too... that's good... that's good...

speaker: Marlo
content: Among us... as long as you stay on the right path... everything's fine...
(Black Screen)
His voice grows faint, dies away, and in the void it leaves behind, a new one arises: the soft, unmistakable sound of someone reciting poetry.

speaker: Manphist
content: ...Ah, fate...
Ah, fate! You blind thrower of dice, casting us onto fields shrouded in war. Young hearts, once flowing freely like spring waters, now bewildered, trembling beneath iron hooves.
The future is a wasteland veiled in mist, a deafened horn, a silent summon. To voyage without a map, how treacherous. The destination, perhaps just an unsealed coffin...
(End of Black Screen)
Hilda gently closes his eyes.

speaker: Hilda
content: ...Rest in peace now, Marlo. The city-state will not forget you.
[Interrogation Room]
A metallic clang echoes through the room as the door swings open. The soldier chained to the interrogation chair lifts his head.

You recognize him. It's the messenger from this morning. Now, you have a name to put to the face: Shane Alvez. He's a frontline soldier, dispatched directly by the metropoles from WhiteSands with a single objective: to ensure the smooth development of Monolith.

speaker: Hilda
content: Shane Alvez... Let's drop the act. Tell us who you really are, and who you're working for.
He shoots a defiant glare at Hilda, then his eyes flick to you, feigning busywork with your notes. A contemptuous snort is his only reply.

speaker: Shane
content: In your dreams! I'm not saying a damn thing!

speaker: Hilda
content: Is that so? Then take a look at this.
With a stern expression, Hilda places several photos in front of him, informing him that his operation has completely failed and all his teammates have been eliminated.

A wave of crimson fury sweeps up Shane's neck and floods his face. His eyes bulge with uncontainable rage, and he unleashes a blistering tirade, his words devolving into a coarse, incomprehensible Outland language.
Hilda waits, a statue of patience, until his rage spends itself on the sterile room air. Only then does she utter a single, soft word: a city-state name you don't recognize.

speaker: Shane
content: H-how did you know?

speaker: Hilda
content: Language gives you away. You slip back into it when you're emotionally charged.
Hilda speaks softly, as if stirred by a personal memory.

speaker: Hilda
content: I remember that city-state. Your people needed Hypercubes and requested aid from the metropoles. After the agreement was signed, it became a subordinate city to Sevael. That was over a decade ago.

speaker: Shane
content: Ha... Haha... Hahahahahaha!

A sharp, manic laugh is torn from Shane's throat, his shoulders heaving with the violence of it. It's the laugh of a man who has just heard the world's most cruel joke, a sound utterly devoid of warmth, sharpened to a fine edge by pure hatred.

speaker: Shane
content: Yeah, you helped us back then. But how long are we supposed to pay that debt? Ten years? Twenty? For the rest of our damn lives?!

speaker: Shane
content: We grow the finest wheat in all of WhiteSands, but the moment we signed that deal, we lost all say in the price! Every industry we try to build, we have to kneel and ask the metropoles for permission!

speaker: Shane
content: A whole decade gone, and we've got nothing to show for it but wheat... No industry, no development, no future. You use Hypercube rations to keep us on a leash, forcing us to be nothing but your farmers!

This is the inevitable fate of any city-state drained by a metropole. The more one-dimensional its industry, the more anemic it becomes, until it is reduced to a mere blood bag, tethered to its master and forever unable to stand on its own. Faced with this fate—revolutionary upheaval or a slow death by bleeding—it's no wonder they become what the authorities label "separatists."
Hilda must understand this on a visceral level. As you watch her, you see her fists clench, her words becoming rigid and forced as she speaks.

speaker: Hilda
content: The metropole system has its flaws, but it remains the most effective way for human civilization to survive against the catastrophes.
Shane spits forcefully on the ground.

speaker: Shane
content: Keep lying to yourself!

speaker: Shane
content: We believed that too, at first! But what did we get? Half our harvest is taken as tribute, our children who go to the metropoles never come back, wheat prices get worse every year, and if we have a few bad harvests from disasters, they even cut our Hypercube rations the next year!

speaker: Hilda
content: That's impossible. Hypercube allocations for satellite towns are non-negotiable. No one has the authority to reduce them. Where did you hear such lies?

A violent, wheezing laugh erupts from Shane. His chest heaves with the effort, each breath a ragged rasp like a torn bellows. Yet, cutting through that grating sound, his voice is laced with a terrifying, unmistakable excitement.

speaker: Shane
content: Lies? If they were just lies, your parents wouldn't have had to run, would they?
Hilda's expression instantly turns cold.

speaker: Hilda
content: You... what else do you know?
Shane lifts his head, a defiant and twisted smile creeping across his face.

speaker: Shane
content: That person was right about you! This gets under your skin, doesn't it? You're dying to know more!

speaker: Shane
content: Fine, I'll tell you. Ten years ago, a man from a metropole came to my hometown. Said he was secretly researching the real conditions of satellite towns under the metropole system.

speaker: Shane
content: What a dedicated guy! He spent months visiting over a dozen towns like ours. Promised us his wife was a councilor who could definitely bring our situation to the higher-ups.

speaker: Shane
content: He wrote a long report detailing all the flaws and dangers of the metropole system. Warned that both DisCity and the satellite towns were sitting on a powder keg ready to blow!

speaker: Shane
content: Then, well, you know what happened... he got an arrest warrant... branded a traitor... until there was no place left for him in the metropole...

speaker: Hilda
content: Enough!
Hilda lunges to her feet, sensing the damning words about to leave Shane's lips. But his voice explodes over hers, a roar of raw defiance that drowns her out.

speaker: Shane
content: So they went to DisCity! And personally lit the fuse!!
A spasm of agony seizes him, twisting his facial nerves. The manic triumph in his smile warps, contorting into a terrifying, grotesque mask.

speaker: Shane
content: They started the war!

speaker: Shane
content: And their daughter, the one they had to leave behind... got brainwashed into becoming the metropole's most obedient, most loyal dog! Ha! Hahahaha!

speaker: Hilda
content: I said... that's enough!
Hilda's voice shakes, with a low, chilling menace that seems to darken the very air.

speaker: Shane
content: Believe what you want. Either way, you've only got two choices: believe your parents were real traitors, or admit the metropoles are actually a rotting pile of garbage.

speaker: Shane
content: DisCity's the only one who got the spine... to resist being swallowed whole by you people all this time, heh heh... cough cough.
A gleam of undisguised reverence shines in Shane's eyes, the same fanatical gleam Hilda has seen in far more repulsive things.

speaker: Hilda
content: You call that "spine"? DisCity abuses Hypercubes to warp the anomalous power and distort life itself, turning soldiers, even infected civilians, into monsters neither human nor beast, then throwing them onto the battlefield!

speaker: Hilda
content: Even if they win, what kind of twisted victory is that?!

speaker: Shane
content: You made us do it! Don't forget the Nirvana massacre. You ******* bastards have no right to judge anyone!

speaker: Shane
content: The metropoles should've fallen long ago. You people, rotten to the core, just wait to be slaughtered by DisCity!
He descends into manic laughter, vomiting fresh blood with every gasp.

speaker: Chief
content: ...Stop him! He's trying to bite his tongue!

speaker: Hilda
content: Don't you dare die!
With lightning speed, Hilda lunges forward and seizes Shane's jaw, her grip brutal and final.
(Mania Effect)

speaker: Hilda
content: Who organized your group? Who gave you the intel on the secret passages?!

As her own emotions surge, a flash of Mania responds. Black, spike-like shards erupt through her gloves, piercing deep into his jaw. Instantly, the dark sludge recognizes a host. It surges into the wound, a torrent of living shadow rushing down his throat.

Hilda recoils, snatching her hand back as if burned, but the damage is done. Mania has already burrowed upward, shattering his jaw from within and tearing his mouth apart in a grotesque, silent scream.
Under the interrogation room's pitiless white lights, his face is frozen in a monstrous, gaping ruin.

speaker: Inflammatory Voice
content: Hahahaha! How pathetic! You've been so thoroughly deceived! Hahahaha!

speaker: Shane
content: We will have... vengeance... we will be... free... we will destroy... the hegemony...

speaker: Shane
content: We will... have... freedom...

You lunge forward, catching Hilda as her legs give way. The sudden emotional shock has sent her Mania into a violent spiral; now it's turning back on itself, corrupting her from within. Through her palm, grotesque spikes writhe and spread, threatening to consume her entire body.

options: Do you have anomalous power in you?

content: You play dumb, acting as if you're seeing it for the first time.

speaker: Chief
content: Stop talking. If you can't control your power, don't use it. Take deep breaths and calm your emotions, or it will pierce right through you.

speaker: Hilda
content: It's okay... I was just... too rash. I'll be fine in a moment...
She brushes your hands away and stumbles back to the chair, her eyes fixed on the viscous, dark sludge before her.

Her gaze is a window to a private torment: the physical agony of the Mania's corruption, the sharp sting of remorse for a life lost to her own lack of control, and—most profoundly—a deep, disorienting bewilderment that threatens to consume her.
In the silence, you offer a quiet thanks to Shane for his brutal, necessary truth. Now, it's time to press Hilda further.

speaker: Chief
content: The question Shane asked you at the end. Your parents or the city-state. Which would you choose to believe?
A shadow falls across Hilda's eyes.

speaker: Hilda
content: I... don't know...
With a soft sigh, you lower yourself beside her and take her hand. Your grip is firm, an attempt to soothe the violent Mania surging through her veins.

speaker: Chief
content: I know it wasn't intentional. You were trying to stop him from killing himself. Your power just slipped beyond your control.
Hilda turns her gaze to you. Her eyes, under the influence of Mania, flicker between clarity and deep, consuming shadows.

speaker: Chief
content: But regret won't change what happened. If you truly feel responsible for what happened to him, then carefully consider everything he said. Don't let emotions cloud your judgment. Don't deny. Don't avoid the difficult questions.

speaker: Chief
content: Then... answer his accusations with action.

speaker: Chief
content: Since this was your parents' former residence, they might have left documents somewhere even the metropoles' assassins couldn't find. Didn't you say they were resourceful people?

speaker: Chief
content: The odds are slim, but I still want to search for myself. Come with me.
You hold her gaze, your invitation hanging in the air between you. Slowly, the light returns to her eyes, the lost and avoidant haze giving way to a fragile, but growing, spark.

speaker: Hilda
content: ...You're right. I... I should go look for... whatever truth is there...

speaker: Hilda
content: Thank you... ${PlayerName}. I'll go with you.
You and Hilda return to the room that was once her parents' office, now repurposed as the Monolith research lab.
From scattered details, you've pieced together that her parents defected from the metropoles, were granted asylum in DisCity as cryptographers, and ultimately settled here.
If they left anything behind, this room is the most logical place to find it. You watch Hilda quietly, noting her apparent lack of hope.
Days of relentless rain have left the air humid and cold enough to chill the bones. Black shrouds, layered over the young dead, hide their faces.
Once the final body is laid to rest, a brief funeral commences within the curtain of falling rain.

speaker: Nolaine
content: So foolish. They think breaking away from the metropoles means they're free. That they can now run their own industry, their own religion, and control their own resources. As if they can just farm and trade in peace in a world ravaged by catastrophes.

speaker: Nolaine
content: But the world is a jungle, full of predators. When a weak lamb cries for independence and leaves the herd, it doesn't get freedom. It gets eaten.

speaker: Nolaine
content: That's why... we have to stay on the right path. Even if our hand has to be iron. Even if it seems cruel. We must follow it, and guide them to follow it, too!
She casts her torch to the ground. In the flickering firelight that dances across their faces, the group moves as one—fists meeting chests in a solemn, silent salute, honoring the fallen soldiers.

speaker: Nolaine
content: To all our brothers who lost their way!

speaker: Nolaine
content: Your hate was used. Your pain was turned into a weapon against the city-state. But I still recognize you as one of us.

speaker: Nolaine
content: I hope you find the prosperity and freedom you were looking for... here in your eternal rest.
You don't see Hilda among the crowd.
Having witnessed those truths, she can no longer bring herself to participate in a ceremony that so boldly champions the metropoles' agenda.
[Cellar]
(Footsteps)
You follow the trail of Mania deep into the cellar, your footsteps the only other sound in the oppressive quiet. At the far end, you find Hilda.
She is curled in the darkness, sitting before a telegraph machine. Her fingers dance across the keys in a slow, rhythmic cadence.
The dit-dah, dit-dah-dah fills the space like a sacred requiem.

Words feel like a desecration here. Instead, after a moment of shared silence, you lower yourself to the ground beside her. Remembering the code you devised yesterday, you begin to speak with your hands.

speaker: Chief
content: What are you doing?

speaker: Hilda
content: Writing epitaphs for them.
Only now do you notice the stack of documents beside her. It's the guards' profiles.
With meticulous care, she transcribes each name, tapping them out into code. One by one, she transforms them into radio waves and releases them to the wind.
Perhaps the signals will be swallowed by Mania. Perhaps they will drift for years before any receiver finds them.
But... it doesn't matter. Someday, they will find their way home. To that place free of bloodshed and oppression.
You wait quietly beside her until the final name is sent. Then, she closes the telegraph machine, the quiet click a period at the end of her elegy.

speaker: Hilda
content: ...It couldn't have been easy to find this place.

speaker: Hilda
content: I'm fine. I just wanted to stay in a quiet place for a while.
And to secretly mourn these "enemies," away from everyone else.

speaker: Hilda
content: Here, I can hear voices from the past. When I need quiet, they keep me company.

speaker: Chief
content: Can you really hear them?
She leans in, her finger pressed to her lips. The earnest intensity in her eyes compels you. The world falls away as you still your breath and listen.
In the newfound silence, the darkness itself seems to breathe. And then you hear it—faint, indistinct voices, rising like a whisper from the void.

speaker: Girl's Shadow
content: Sis, look! The railway from the metropoles is almost here in the north. Soon you could see an art exhibition in the morning and be back with new books by afternoon.

speaker: Man's Shadow
content: Their engineers say we can redirect the underground springs to the dry regions. We'll finally be able to grow more food... feed more people in the satellite towns.

speaker: Woman's Shadow
content: Just think of how many children the medical program could save...

speaker: Man's Shadow
content: The united university is opening enrollment soon... More of our people will have a chance to study!

speaker: Woman's Shadow
content: Listen, everyone! This is our next goal. We're moving forward, one step at a time, toward the ideal city-state!

speaker: Subtitles
content: This is a crossroads for the world. In its street-side cafes, people peruse newspapers in dozens of languages, eagerly trading phrases from their homelands.

speaker: Subtitles
content: All children attend school; everyone has work and receives their rightful share. Theaters constantly debut new plays, and a laundry woman can walk proudly into a masquerade to dance with nobility.

speaker: Subtitles
content: No wars, no conflicts. People of every rank fulfill their duties, yet still have the energy to enjoy their lives.

speaker: Subtitles
content: Back then, it was the clearest vision of an ideal, an indestructible lighthouse in the hearts of countless souls.
...But what remains of it now?

speaker: Shane's Shadow
content: Why are you holding us back? Why are we the ones trapped here on the farm? Why are you stealing our future?

speaker: Guard's Shadow
content: Everyone who asked questions was taken... just disappeared. Where are they? Release them! Give them back!

speaker: Girl's Shadow
content: Why...? Why do we have to fight wars? Shouldn't we be working together? Shouldn't we be moving forward?
The silence is absolute, but her face is a transcript of a conversation you can't hear. An icy dread traces its way down your spine, and you can't stop yourself from asking.

speaker: Chief
content: What... do you hear?

speaker: Hilda
content: They ask me if I still remember what the ideal city-state was supposed to be. If I remember the person I used to be, the one who fought side by side with them for a shared future. They ask when the war will end... when the trees in our homeland will grow green again.

speaker: Hilda
content: They speak of everything... except the reason they died.

Her tone is deceptively calm, but you know better. These "voices from the past" are classic auditory hallucinations, a direct symptom of uncontrolled Mania that only emerges when a host's psyche is on the brink.

The cause could be physical—damage to the LINK—or purely psychological, with the unshackled Mania ravaging her mind. The origin matters less than the result: beneath her composed facade lies a profoundly fragile mental state.
She is just forcing normalcy, a performance as fragile as glass.
With a quiet sigh, you move to sit closer to her.

speaker: Chief
content: This question has been tormenting you, hasn't it? Why has our city-state become what it is today?

speaker: Chief
content: And sometimes you wish it were you lying in that darkness instead of them.
You listen as Hilda's breathing in the dark deepens, finding a more measured rhythm. It seems she is finally calming down.

speaker: Chief
content: To be honest, I don't know how to answer you. I'm not even sure if what we're doing is right or wrong.

speaker: Chief
content: We can only move forward until history renders its final judgment on us.

speaker: Hilda
content: ...It wasn't... like this before.

speaker: Hilda
content: I still remember when I was young, hearing about the future, from books, from my parents, from the news. Everyone said the future would be an ideal era.
She narrows her eyes, as if admiring the dust motes dancing in the darkness.

speaker: Hilda
content: Ever since the Nightfall, the metropoles have united settlements and city-states, providing aid for decades.

speaker: Hilda
content: I once saw towns on the brink of extinction rebuilt with the metropoles' help. Refugees fleeing from catastrophes would embrace each other in tears when they finally reached our gates...

speaker: Hilda
content: That same year, Sevael proclaimed to all territories that if every city-state united and contributed what it could, even the greatest disasters could be overcome.

speaker: Hilda
content: Small states are not burdens, but our flesh and blood. Resources are not barriers, but bridges between us... If we stand united, civilization's light will burn away the long night, and humanity... will rise again.
She raises her hand, reaching for a memory, a ghost—for something that was never there. At last, it falls back to her side, empty.

speaker: Hilda
content: ${PlayerName}, I believe the evidence we've seen, but I can't dismiss everything the metropoles have done for decades because of a few isolated cases.

speaker: Hilda
content: Maybe we've missed something, or something's been hidden from us... The information we don't have might explain everything.
You open your mouth, but find you have no words to offer.

You understand that these recent revelations are feeble things against the fortress of her faith, a devotion built over decades. Beginnings are always pure; memories are forever gilded. You cannot fault her for clinging to the memory of those idealistic orators and a metropole that once truly reached out to help the smaller states.
To press further now would only seed suspicion. For today, it is wiser to let the matter rest.

speaker: Option
options: I was thinking the same thing.

content: Hilda draws a deep, steadying breath, the ghost of a smile touching her lips.

speaker: Hilda
content: If the mole brought me this information, they must know even more than I do.

speaker: Hilda
content: I... won't be shaken by this. Even if it's just to learn the whole truth, I'll find that mole and make them talk.

speaker: Hilda
content: I need to know what kind of "justice" they claim to uphold while sending so many people to kill me...
Hilda rises slowly and walks through the dim light. She passes you, her form dissolving into a darkness that seems to promise no return.

In her silhouette, you see the ghosts of others you have known. They always begin this way—eyes clear, stride steady, ideals held like a shield, heads high against the sky. And so often, they end this way, too—stepping onto a solitary path, from which there is no coming back.
[Main Hall]
Amidst the devastation of the main hall, the survivors have assembled. Helene, having foraged for food and ignited a surviving stove, now beckons the others toward the comforting circle of fire.

speaker: Helene
content: Look... I have a suggestion. Instead of splitting into shifts tonight, why don't we all just stay here together?

speaker: Nolaine
content: So we can all keep a closer eye on one another, you mean?

speaker: Helene
content: I mean we can protect one another! The situation is still unclear. Staying in a group is the most logical way to ensure everyone's safety. It's obvious!
Nolaine lets out a cold snort.

speaker: Nolaine
content: Hmph, a group is just a bigger target. I have no intention of dozing off only to have my throat slit by the person sharing my fire. Separately, we stay sharp. That's how you survive.

speaker: Nolaine
content: And with today's chaos, the Monolith research can't be finished. I assume Hilda would prefer some quiet to work.

speaker: Hilda
content: The location is irrelevant to me.

speaker: Hilda
content: The Monolith's repairs are almost done; I can work from anywhere. Our priority now should be determining which arrangement is more likely to... flush out the remaining "mole."
Hilda's voice is a soft veil over steel, her words needling straight into the hearts of everyone present.

speaker: Manphist
content: Perhaps we should put it to a vote? Look, there are exactly five of us.
Right now, the vote is locked, two against two. As the fifth and final vote, the decision is yours alone—

speaker: Hilda
content: Very well. I will retrieve the Monolith files from my room.

speaker: Manphist
content: Helene and I can gather bedding and see what other provisions we can salvage.
(Black Screen)
After some time, the group has settled, each person creating a makeshift bed on the main hall's floor.
A perimeter of distrust is silently established. Individuals space themselves apart but ensure they remain visible to all.
Hilda then wheels out the Monolith prototype, centering it in the hall.
You realize that, aside from yourself, everyone else is witnessing the actual "Monolith" for the first time.

It stands waist-high, a black metal box reminiscent of a small coffin. Four screens are set into its sides, each with a corresponding keyboard. Its inner workings are partially exposed; within the unassembled core, a cluster of electronic dials glimmers faintly under the lights.

speaker: Hilda
content: Can I have your assistance to complete the final calibration process?

speaker: Manphist
content: Ah... of course. I was beginning to think you'd forgotten why you brought an old cryptographer along in the first place.

speaker: Helene
content: No trouble at all. After all, the Monolith is the entire reason we're all here, isn't it?

speaker: Nolaine
content: My expertise with mechanical systems isn't on par with Huck's, but I can manage the radio components.
Hilda nods and hands out a stack of documents to everyone present.

speaker: Hilda
content: The final calibration requires extensive parallel calculations and data entry. Please review your assigned documents thoroughly, then input the data accurately into the corresponding Monolith modules.

speaker: Hilda
content: Notify me immediately of any interface discrepancies or hardware errors during the process. I will make the necessary adjustments.

speaker: Manphist
content: Hmm... I see now... So this is the Monolith... truly an elegant design.
Leaning over the most confidential Monolith schematics, Manphist lets out a series of impressed clicks of his tongue, absorbing every detail of the revolutionary design.

speaker: Manphist
content: Not purely mechanical rotors, but integrated with the latest computing technology... hmm... yet it still contains twelve interconnected rotors internally. On demand, several can generate false data to mislead the enemy, while its cyclical structure renders brute-force decryption utterly useless...

speaker: Manphist
content: If we had had this device back then, our intelligence network would not have been so thoroughly annihilated.

speaker: Manphist
content: Augustus, that anomalous power wielder from DisCity... as long as she knows the strike coordinates in advance, her incomprehensible power can intercept anything... This alone stripped us of every effective deterrent we had.

speaker: Manphist
content: And that ghostly Reaper unit... always appearing where we were most vulnerable, tearing our defensive lines to shreds...

speaker: Manphist
content: But now... No matter. It is not too late.

speaker: Hilda
content: Once DisCity can no longer decrypt our messages, Augustus will lose her strategic advantage.

speaker: Hilda
content: ${PlayerName}... I need you to take the night watch.

speaker: Hilda
content: Though everything lies in ruins around us... this is the final push.

options: I'd like to help with the Monolith calculations as well.

speaker: Hilda
content: Thank you. I'm counting on you to keep watch.

speaker: Nolaine
content: You're versed in the ciphers too? Very well. I can share some of my work with you.
(Paths converge)

Everyone gathers around the Monolith and gets to work, the air filled with the quiet intensity of their calculations.
It's going to be a sleepless night.

A hushed quiet blankets the hall, where everyone is gathered, intent on their individual tasks. The silence is a peaceful one, broken only by the soft rustle of papers, the scratch of pens, and the methodical clicking of calculators.
Barring any unforeseen complications, you feel a growing certainty that Monolith's development will be completed tonight.
As you're lost in this contemplation, a subtle movement catches your eye. It's Hilda, offering a gentle wave, her expression suggesting she has something to discuss.
As the first grey light of dawn filters into the room, the last calibration is complete.
With a steady hand, Hilda takes the final, crucial gear and slots it into place. A soft, yet definitive click echoes in the quiet room, and a green indicator light glows to life.

speaker: Hilda
content: There. It is complete now.
A heavy silence descends. For a moment, everyone is frozen, suspended between exhaustion and the uncertainty of what comes next.
Hilda lets out a cold laugh.

speaker: Hilda
content: ...What's the matter? I expected our "mole" would have made a move by now.

speaker: Manphist
content: Hmm... This presents two possibilities. First, is the mole even still among the living? Perhaps Huck, who fell in the chaos, was the culprit after all?

speaker: Chief
content: Even if the Monolith is the target, confronting four people to steal a machine of this size would be a suicidal move.
And that's precisely why you haven't made your move yet. This prototype is simply too large to steal right in front of these people. What you really need is more detailed intelligence.
The blueprints, or perhaps the core component.

speaker: Helene
content: Oh, for heaven's sake... What "move" are you all waiting for? Just crate this thing up and ship it out! I'm so sick of this place. I want to go home!

speaker: Nolaine
content: Wait. What does this indicator mean?
A low, ominous hum fills the air as the indicator light snaps from green to a glaring red.
That familiar, chilling presence—Mania—washes over you again.
At the same moment, a piercing alarm shrieks from the Monolith. Panels on all four sides erupt in a frantic, synchronized strobe of light.

speaker: Hilda
content: What on earth...
The machine is going haywire.
The terrifying conclusion is inescapable. The crowd can only stare, speechless, as the screens dissolve into a torrent of data.
"Gexyl wz vcoebmn."
"G93ZXIgaXMgZ3VpbHQu"
"YzJCZmN1bVpQdVYrMXBveHFKaXhBdz09"
Numbers and letters skitter and swarm across the screen in a taunting dance, finally collapsing into a single, glaring string of deep red.

speaker: Nolaine
content: This... this code is...!
<color=#dg1f1f>Wklv lv qrw d jliw. Lw lv brxu judyh.</color>

speaker: Hilda
content: A Caesar cipher. Offset by three. The first lesson for every cryptographer...
<color=#dg1f1f>This is not a gift. It is your grave.</color>
<color=#dg1f1f>2:00:00</color>
Beep, beep, beep...
Two hours until the Monolith explodes...

■ Eliminated Outlands spies: Huck Burrows, Casey Abel, Marlo Bannings

■ All 30 estate guards confirmed dead. Investigation confirms they were secretly recruited by a farland resistance group, which operated under DisCity's name to conduct separatist activities and retaliate against the metropoles.

■ The estate has sustained severe structural damage. All previous entry and exit restrictions have been lifted.
■ The Monolith prototype has been compromised by the mole, currently awaiting decontamination and restoration.

Keys Obtained: <color=#fb9259><size=52><u>3</color></size></u>


Consciousness Restoration: <color=#fb9259><size=52><u>60%</color></size></u>

Unresolved Matter:

□ Among the three remaining people, who is the mole?

All eyes in the room are pulled, as if by a grim gravity, to the object at its center.
It is a thing of crude, cast-iron utility—unadorned, cold, and heavy. A palpable aura of doom seeps from its rough surface.

The silence is not silent at all. It is filled with the low, wasp-like buzz of electricity and the tight, strained breathing of the crowd. Against the backdrop of the rain, these sounds become a symphony of anxiety.
<color=#dg1f1f>1:57:03</color>
With every tiny decrement of the numbers, a minute click echoes from within, a sound so small it seems to be heard by the bones more than the ears, and it sends a visceral shiver through you.
Hilda's eyes trace the lines of the iron coffin, now monstrously changed, her demeanor unnervingly placid.

speaker: Hilda
content: I'm staying to disarm it.

speaker: Helene
content: What?!

speaker: Helene
content: Have you lost your mind, Hilda! That's not the Monolith anymore, it's a bomb! You have barely two hours!

speaker: Helene
content: The plan has failed! Our only objective now is to evacuate immediately and inform the superiors!

speaker: Hilda
content: We haven't failed yet.

speaker: Hilda
content: It's just a temporary "bomb." Once disarmed, its core functionality will remain intact.

speaker: Hilda
content: The city-state is waiting for the intelligence Monolith is meant to carry. We cannot abandon our mission at the final moment.

speaker: Hilda
content: If it explodes, we lose everything.

speaker: Helene
content: ...Insane. You're insane.
Helene stumbles backward, bumping into you.

speaker: Helene
content: You're all insane, but I'm not! I'm done with this! I'm getting out of here! I refuse to die in this damned place!
She shoves you aside and rushes upstairs.
[Room]

Helene stumbles to her desk, yanking the drawer open with a violent screech. She claws through its contents—a jumble of undergarments, dog-eared foreign magazines, and cosmetics—sending it all flying across the floor.

speaker: Helene
content: This is crazy! I only came here for a damn seminar. I am NOT going to die in this place.

speaker: Helene
content: I have to survive... I am going to make it back alive...
Soon, her frantic fingers hit the back of the drawer, finding two cold, hard objects.
She pulls them out with trembling hands: an antique brass bird whistle and an unsealed kraft paper envelope.
[Main Hall]

speaker: Chief
content: Helene, calm down!

speaker: Chief
content: The mole just made their move, and now you're demanding to leave? You'll make yourself the prime suspect!
In a burst of anger, Helene heaves her travel bag down.

speaker: Helene
content: I don't have time for your witch hunt anymore!

speaker: Helene
content: I still don't know what I did to deserve being dragged into this hellhole. Unless I've somehow slept with the mole, I am the most innocent person here!

speaker: Helene
content: You know me, Officer! You know I'm not clever enough for these kinds of games!

speaker: Chief
content: You need to face reality. I'm trying to help you.

speaker: Chief
content: I know you're terrified. I know you want to run. But you've worked with Hilda longer than I have. You, more than me, should trust her capabilities.

speaker: Chief
content: When has she ever failed to solve a puzzle?

speaker: Chief
content: Even in the worst-case scenario, I will get you out myself. But right now, you need to stay.

speaker: Helene
content: ...Ha... Pretty words.

speaker: Helene
content: In my line of work, you hear all kinds of sweet talk. "Stay with me tonight." "Marry me, you'll be the happiest woman alive." Some promises are sincere, others are lies, and I have a talent for believing the lies.

speaker: Helene
content: I'll be frank with you, Officer... Someone proposed to me. He found out my identity. He knows I'm a spy for the metropoles! And he said he didn't care. He still wanted to love me, to wait for me, to run away with me.

speaker: Helene
content: I was paralyzed. I couldn't bring myself to silence him, but I couldn't bring myself to defect, either. And that's when the orders came down for this seminar.

speaker: Helene
content: I just want... a chance to choose again...

speaker: Helene
content: Don't stand in my way. Once I'm safe, I'll burn that letter myself.

speaker: Helene
content: But if you try to stop me, I'll expose your secret right away. I mean it.
She wipes away her tears and rudely pushes past you, her high heels striking the marble floor with rapid, frantic clicks. She rushes toward the iron door, toward her gateway to freedom.
[Exterior/The Garden]
Rain pours down in sheets, but Helene doesn't wonder if any birds will respond. Her hands tremble as she raises the cold brass bird whistle to her pale lips.
Whoooo—chirrup-chirrup—chirrurup-chirrurup—
The crisp, resonant call slices through the deathly silence of the rain. It sounds like a desperate cry for help, a stark contrast to the grim surroundings.

Miraculously, moments later, wings flutter from the bare crowns of the plane trees. A few startled sparrows flee. Then, a more agile, familiar white shape dives gracefully down and lands precisely on Helene's trembling fingertips.
It is a snow-white messenger pigeon. In the dim light, its eyes gleam like two smooth black obsidian stones.

speaker: Helene
content: Good... good little bird...

Her voice breaks as she fumbles with the small brass ring on the pigeon's leg. She opens the miniature bamboo tube and, with trembling fingers, carefully rolls her note and inserts it into the tiny container, sealing it tightly.

speaker: Helene
content: Good little bird... take this to him for me. He promised to love me forever, didn't he? He said he would pluck the stars and moon from the sky for me... so let him come save me now.

speaker: Helene
content: Go, little bird, fly! Hurry, fly away—

She thrusts the pigeon upward with all her might. Its pure white wings spread against the gloomy sky like hope breaking free from despair. The bird circles once, seems to find its bearings, and flies away.
Yet in that very moment, as hope takes flight—
A dark figure stands in the doorway shadows, having been silently watching for who knows how long.
Hilda's right hand rises with absolute steadiness.
The cold wind sweeps at the hem of her dark wool coat. She stands expressionless, her face like the surface of a frozen lake. Only her eyes are alive, blood-red and predatory.
The gun barrel in her hand catches the dim light, gleaming with a cold, lethal shine.
You decide to...

options: You don't need to kill her.

speaker: Hilda
content: ...Unauthorized communication. Disclosure of classified information. She is caught in the act.
Hilda hasn't lowered her gun. But in the tense silence, you notice the faint, unmistakable tremor in her hand.

speaker: Chief
content: But she's not the mole! Even if she's guilty, she deserves a tribunal, not a summary execution!

speaker: Chief
content: Don't do this, Hilda. Think of Shane. Think of Casey. I know you don't want to live with more regrets.
Her hand moves at last, lifting slightly. The shot rings out, striking the pigeon already in distant flight.
A despairing scream tears from Helene's throat as the blood-soaked pigeon hits the ground, lifeless.
Before the echo fades, Hilda holsters her gun. She strides past the sobbing Helene without a glance and stops squarely in front of you.

speaker: Hilda
content: Since you are so certain Helene is not the mole... then enlighten me. What is your theory?
You take a deep breath.

speaker: Chief
content: At this point, identifying the real mole has become pretty easy.
First of all...

You're certain of it. Modifying the Monolith prototype into a timed bomb required inside knowledge and access. The saboteur not only survived the guards' attack but is among the small group who worked on restoring and calibrating the prototype.
(−Hilda's Trust)

No... that logic is flawed. Someone had to have modified the Monolith prototype, turning it into a timed bomb. This means the mole not only survived the guards' attack but is also among the small group who worked on restoring and calibrating the prototype.
Second...

options: The mole has a fanatical obsession with the Monolith.
The Monolith isn't actually the mole's true target.

content: This is a core motive. It rules out Nolaine immediately. Her only fixation is Hilda's protection, a goal for which she once considered killing everyone. She has never deviated from this single-minded purpose, making her an impossible candidate.
(−Hilda's Trust)
On second thought, Nolaine once considered killing everyone to protect Hilda. She has never deviated from this single-minded purpose, making her an impossible candidate.
Finally...

options: The mole is intimately familiar with The Wilderness.

content: That's it. The mole used the verses from The Wilderness as a cipher to communicate with Johnson. But Helene, who grew up in DisCity, lacks the literary education that other Outlanders have and wouldn't have read this popular work from over a decade ago. Conversely, Manphist, born in the Outlands and the most experienced and well-read among everyone, would certainly know The Wilderness like the back of his hand.
(−Hilda's Trust)

But that's not quite right. The mole used the verses from The Wilderness as a cipher to communicate with Johnson. But Helene, who grew up in DisCity, lacks the literary education that other Outlanders have and wouldn't have read this popular work from over a decade ago. Conversely, Manphist, born in the Outlands and the most experienced and well-read among everyone, would certainly know The Wilderness like the back of his hand.
The evidence points to one, inescapable conclusion.

speaker: Hilda
content: ...But doesn't that contradict your previous reasoning?

speaker: Chief
content: Sorry, I misspoke. The real mole is actually...
(Return to previous choice)
Option B: The mole is Helene.

speaker: Hilda
content: Yingying

speaker: Hilda
content: Are you thinking straight?
(Return to previous choice)
Option C: The mole is Manphist.
As one, you and Hilda fix your stares on Manphist. He looks back at you, his face the very picture of innocence.
In response to your silent accusation, he offers nothing but a resigned shrug.

speaker: Manphist
content: Ah, of course. I suppose it was inevitable. By simple process of elimination, I am the last and most logical suspect.

speaker: Manphist
content: But is it not a rather unscientific method to condemn a man based solely on that, without a single piece of tangible proof?

speaker: Manphist
content: Consider this: if guards we dismissed could orchestrate an assault, is it not equally plausible that an actor, entirely unknown to us, remains hidden within the manor's shadows?

speaker: Manphist
content: And the modifications to the Monolith... Surely, someone could have accessed the room while Hilda was absent to make the alterations?

speaker: Hilda
content: It's alright.

speaker: Hilda
content: We'll have our answers soon enough. The interrogation will see to that.
The group escorts Manphist towards the interrogation room, but he moves with an unsettling composure, as if he were the one leading the way.
His demeanor suggests not a prisoner being questioned, but an examiner preparing to administer a test.

You know his reputation as a seasoned spy trainer; he is no ordinary adversary. To extract the intelligence you need on the Outlands and the Monolith, you must first find a single crack in his impeccable armor.
Manphist sucks in a ragged breath. Gone is the scholarly composure that usually defines him, replaced by the desperate exhaustion of a cornered beast and a stubborn, lingering arrogance.
Yet, behind his glasses, those clouded eyes still hold a glint—the sharp, calculating cunning of a veteran spy.
You've hit a wall. Interrogation will yield nothing more.

speaker: Hilda
content: I understand. You did everything you could.

speaker: Hilda
content: He's an old fox who has lived on a knife's edge for decades. It would be strange if he did have any obvious weak spots.

speaker: Chief
content: What's the next step? Are you going to use more forceful methods?
With her gaze fixed on Manphist, Hilda gives you a firm shake of her head.

speaker: Hilda
content: That won't be necessary. Since he refuses to talk... I'll just see for myself.
She stands up and approaches Manphist.
(transition with sound of footsteps)

speaker: Manphist
content: Is it your turn now, Hilda? What new trick do you have for your old mentor?
Hilda stands before him, her face a landscape of sharp angles and deep shadows under the harsh white light.

speaker: Hilda
content: I do have a new method. One that perhaps you yourself bestowed upon me.
She raises her right hand, pressing two fingers to the center of Manphist's sweat-slicked forehead, then flicks her wrist.
The air doesn't crackle, yet the world bends. Reality warps silently around her touch, and from that focal point, a torrent of living darkness erupts, coiling around Manphist's head like a serpent.

speaker: Manphist
content: GAAAHHHH!!!
His scream is a brief, tearing sound, too shrill to be human. But what follows is more terrifying.

A blood-curdling sight unfolds as countless semi-transparent "intelligence strips," woven from pure Mania, are violently exorcised. They tear from his eyes, his mouth, every pore, ripped out by an unseen force.
These "strips" whip into a frenzied, swirling storm around Hilda—an ominous maelstrom of glimpsed secrets.
[CG: Mania Power]
This is the true, complete form of her power.

Anchored in the heart of the storm, Hilda remains perfectly still. As her fingers graze each spinning code strip of Mania, it halts, suspended. Then it unfurls, the distorted symbols and images resolving into sharp, legible truth.
A waterfall of secrets—scenes of trades, account numbers, the ghostly echoes of secret whispers, fragments of ambition and greed—cascades into the waiting void around, holding nothing back.
[Memory Fragment]

speaker: Fraser Officer
content: Mr. Manphist, or perhaps I should call you "Doctor." We recognize you as a true master of your craft, one who has completed many... notable operations in the shadows of history.

speaker: Fraser Officer
content: Forgive my blunt assessment, but the outcome of this war is a foregone conclusion. The Metropole Alliance is like this fish—presentable on the surface, yet compromised at its core. When the conflict concludes, DisCity's guns throughout WhiteSands will show no quarter.

speaker: Fraser Officer
content: When a great power falls, some choose to become splendid funerary ornaments... but I take you for a pragmatist. And pragmatic men become "living assets."

speaker: Fraser Officer
content: This is a "scholar visiting visa" and an "investment immigration guarantee," specially approved by the Fraser Senate. With a single signature, your designation would change from "war criminal" to "protected refugee."

speaker: Fraser Officer
content: Your expertise in cryptography, your intelligence networks, your personal connections... they are more than sufficient to establish a premier "Strategic Intelligence Division" in Fraser. It is a future we are very keen to realize.
[Return to present]

Manphist howls, a raw sound of pure terror, as he struggles to rise. But the swirling "code strips" coil around him like icy serpents, their grip inexorable and humiliating, and slam him back into the frigid metal seat.
Through the shrieking storm and his agonized whimpers, Hilda's voice cuts cleanly, cold and absolute as a final judgment.

speaker: Hilda
content: Money... A DisCity Bank bearer account, ending in 7749... A Fraser Union safe deposit box, designation Gamma-7...

speaker: Hilda
content: Power... Secret meetings at exclusive salons... The title of Chief Advisor for the "Strategic Intelligence Division"...

speaker: Hilda
content: Wine... Romanee Conti from before the Nightfall... Women... the first chair violinist from the Golden Hall... Your retirement, Manphist, is far more splendid than the "austerity" you so tearfully described.
[Continue flashback]

<color=#fb9259>ENCRYPTED COMMS</color>: The tide of war has turned, but considerable mop-up operations are still required.

<color=#fb9259>ENCRYPTED COMMS</color>: Please keep the Sevael Republic under close observation. The recent council bill rejection is a diversion; a strategic-level project, codenamed "Monolith," is advancing in secret. Please obstruct it if possible, or arrange for its complete termination.

<color=#fb9259>ENCRYPTED COMMS</color>: If successfully deployed, "Monolith" will redefine the battlefield. Its survival or elimination is now a critical variable for your upcoming arrangement in Fraser.

<color=#fb9259>ENCRYPTED COMMS</color>: We await your findings.
<color=#fb9259>ENCRYPTED COMMS</color>: I have initiated the placement of reliable assets within the departments. We now have direct access to all primary intelligence.
[End of Flashback]

speaker: Hilda
content: You recruited under the guise of mentorship, placing assets across departments to feed you intelligence. Casey, Edward, Nolaine... all of them are pawns in your game...
You glance at Nolaine beside you. She looks as if she's taken a physical blow, her face a ghastly, bloodless white.

speaker: Hilda
content: So you... willingly... became the mole who hollowed out your own home. Trading critical intelligence for a comfortable post-war life. Deserting the battlefield where you belonged!
At Hilda's accusation, a low chuckle escapes Manphist's lips. Though his voice is frail, it drips with a quiet, deliberate mockery.

speaker: Manphist
content: Don't be so rigid, Hilda. I'm retired. Your moral code doesn't apply to me anymore.

speaker: Manphist
content: You know the beauty of our business? Sell to two sides, and you're a traitor. But sell to everyone, and suddenly you're a professional "information broker"—and your market value soars!

speaker: Hilda
content: ...You are utterly beyond redemption.
Hilda stares, utterly unable to process how her mentor could be so monstrous. Manphist, however, meets her horror with a deep, unbothered laugh.

speaker: Manphist
content: If all intelligence has a price, why should the Monolith be any different?! Besides, the truth it hides is far more corrupt than anything I've done. I may have lost my conscience, but selling that? That was genuinely liberating!

speaker: Manphist
content: You have no idea, do you? Oh, of course you don't. You don't know what the metropoles plan to do with it. You're my most brilliant, yet most foolish student, handing them a knife while preaching about loyalty and justice.

speaker: Manphist
content: And now you have this... power. So you can read minds, can you? Then I don't need to tell you anything. See for yourself. Take a good, long look!
The next moment, he does the unthinkable. His own hands claw at the code strips constricting him, and with a violent wrench, he forcibly tears his own memories bare before your eyes.
[Continue flashback]
Manphist eyed the black-clad figure with deep unease. The operative, a special contact introduced by Fraser, had come bearing top-secret intelligence that required his deciphering skills.

Since entering, the man had pointedly kept his scarf and hat drawn low, obscuring his features. But a referral from Fraser was a powerful credential, so Manphist had accepted the stack of telegrams. Most contained standard fare—military movements, political appointments—but two stood out, their contents stark and alarming.

Recipient: Lighthouse Sender: Red Crossbill DisCity Reaper sample obtained. Shows minimal commonalities with Ash Crystal. Can proceed as a new research initiative. Response: Continue acquisition. Begin limited tests within military units.

Recipient: <color=#fb9259>Lighthouse</color>
Sender: <color=#fb9259>Mayfly</color>
<i>"Operation Raider" approval granted. Nuclear network now covers all key DisCity facilities with 160 units total, capable of a comprehensive strike.
Two days ago, "Black Manual" and "Briefcase" were compromised. 13 units were seized and decommissioned by enemy forces, and replacements were acquired.
Vulnerabilities persist. Requesting a more robust encryption system to secure the operation.<i>

Response: <color=#fb9259>Consider deploying "Monolith."</color>
As the final code was broken, the visitor gave a nod of clear satisfaction. He laid a "token of appreciation" on the table and turned to leave.
At the door, he paused, glancing back, and asked Manphist a question: Do you know what the Monolith is? Any information would be worth a fortune.
[End of Flashback]
Hilda's eyes fly open, a strangled gasp catching in her throat as if seized by an invisible hand.

speaker: Hilda
content: How... could this be?
Her voice is a ghost of a sound, as if her very soul recoils from the truth. Each word seems to sear her throat on its way out.

speaker: Hilda
content: It's impossible... This is madness... A plan like this would never pass the Joint Council!

And you understand. The revelation of 160 warheads—a network poised for nuclear strike—strikes you with the force of a physical blow. For such a plan to be approved, the metropoles wouldn't just be misguided; they would be utterly, criminally insane.

But the true devastation is the Monolith. The project she believed was her city-state's ultimate shield is, in fact, the key to this very plan. Unknowingly, she has built the very weapon that could end it all, becoming a silent accomplice to an unimaginable crime.
You can almost hear it: the sound of something fundamental within her shattering beyond repair.

speaker: Manphist
content: Still so naive, Hilda. The Council is just another marketplace. All their grand speeches about risk and peace? In practice, it's all business!

speaker: Manphist
content: Isn't the Nirvana explosion proof enough?
Manphist, oblivious to the shifting atmosphere, continues his lecture. Hilda, however, purses her lips, already preparing a deliberate denial.

speaker: Hilda
content: That was different. Nirvana had concentrated a massive stockpile of experimental weaponry and laboratories, including the Reapers. I understood the threat... we had no other choice...

speaker: Manphist
content: Excellent. You've just demonstrated another classic fallacy. Intelligence operatives are often deceived by the very intelligence they handle, mistaking institutional authority for moral justification.
With a smug smirk, Manphist rips away the shell, violently exposing the metropoles' true nature.

speaker: Manphist
content: No matter its military value, Nirvana was fundamentally an economic port. When the bombs fell, countless civilians hadn't even begun to evacuate.

speaker: Manphist
content: You've been fooled, Hilda.

The way he looks at Hilda has changed. He no longer watches her as a teacher observing a student, but as a cold-eyed appraiser studying precious porcelain as it cracks, silently calculating the loss in value.

speaker: Hilda
content: No... You're justifying your own betrayal...
Hilda glares back at her former mentor. His betrayal wasn't born from their corrupted environment; it seeped out from the rot within him.

speaker: Manphist
content: Justify? Why would I bother? I betrayed them because I saw the rot at the core and refused to be its next sacrifice! I defected to Fraser because they offered a better price and a higher chance of survival! But now it seems...

speaker: Manphist
content: ...Even that deal is a poor investment.
Click, crack—
His backbone erupts, vertebra by vertebra, filling the room with a series of horrifyingly crisp cracks.
Chains snap, and code strips instantly crumble to dust. The body that once housed a refined scholar swells and contorts, its form bloating and dripping with black sludge.
With a deafening roar, the enormous monster suddenly lunges—not at you, but directly toward the Monolith bomb on the table.
You and Nolaine rush toward Hilda at the same instant.

A violent explosion roars behind you. The shockwave, thick with Mania, slams into you, hurling everyone forward like ragdolls. The world dissolves into a cacophony of shattering sounds. You can't even tell if it's the building breaking apart or the snap of human bones.
(Black screen for 5+ seconds) (Dim light + debris sounds)
An unknown amount of time passes. You open your eyes to utter darkness.
A high-pitched ring is the only sound in your ears. Then, a deep, bone-jarring ache registers, radiating from the heavy weight pinning your legs and torso.

You try to move. A sharp pain flares, but your limbs respond. A collapsed sofa and chairs lie across you, but they've wedged against fallen ceiling panels, forming a fragile, triangular pocket of space around you.
Miraculously, nothing seems broken. Gritting your teeth, you carefully push aside chunks of plaster and splintered wood, slowly dragging your body out from under the wreckage.
Your palms press into the ground—and meet a warm, sticky wetness. You try not to think about what it is.
The air is thick with chalky dust and a heavy, cloying concentration of raw Mania. You try to take a steadying breath, but the moment you open your mouth, an uncontrollable cough wracks your body.
After a moment, you hear a sound coming from nearby.
${PlayerName}?
Hilda's Trust +1

speaker: Hilda
content: ...You're alright. That's a relief.

speaker: Chief
content: How are you? What about Nolaine, Manphist, and Helene?

speaker: Hilda
content: Manphist... is gone. Helene was clear of the blast radius. She should be fine.

speaker: Hilda
content: As for Nolaine, she...
You hear a faint groaning from the shadows to your left. Rubble shifts and crumbles as you discover Nolaine, trapped between two fallen support beams.
She was closest to Manphist and took the full force of the explosion to protect Hilda. Half her body is mangled beyond recognition, replaced by twisted limbs that writhe with spreading Mania.

speaker: Nolaine
content: ...Quite fitting, isn't it?
She coughs. It's a wet, gurgling sound, the noise of bloody foam churning in her throat.

speaker: Nolaine
content: You always shut me out... Hilda. Pushed me away. No matter how many of your codes I broke, you never let me in... never let me join you.

speaker: Nolaine
content: I thought you were looking down on me. So I went to Manphist...

speaker: Nolaine
content: He said I had talent... that he appreciated my skills... He wrote the recommendation... got me into the Cryptography Department...

speaker: Nolaine
content: I never realized he was just using me to get to you... I was so naive, thinking it was my own skill... that let me fight my way to your side...

speaker: Nolaine
content: I... I really wanted to go to Sevael.

speaker: Nolaine
content: I can't remember a single good day from my childhood... My stomach was always a hollow ache... even with one meal, I was terrified of where the next would come from... gunfire could erupt in the alleyways at any moment...

speaker: Nolaine
content: When I thought life was meaningless... you were the one who saved me. You showed me a city-state could be something more...
[Flashback Filter] [Alley Corner]

speaker: Nolaine
content: I knew you weren't ordinary... The kind lady who always slips me an extra half-slice of black bread at the relief station is actually a high-value Outland agent.
The little beggar tossed a wallet playfully between her hands, its ID cards and notes fluttering with each movement.

speaker: Hilda
content: ...You're more observant than I gave you credit for.

speaker: Hilda
content: So, clever girl, what's the price for your silence? A basket of bread? Or... do you plan to sell me out to those hyenas waiting for their reward at the end of the alley?

speaker: Nolaine
content: Bread? How long would that last me? And selling you out? Those hyenas would silence me right after. I'm not stupid.

speaker: Nolaine
content: I've been watching you. The way you walk, the way you observe people... it's different from the real charity workers. You avoid patrols with a skill even sharper than us street rats.

speaker: Nolaine
content: And sometimes... there's a scent on you. Not perfume. Chemicals and fire. It's faint, but I can smell it.
Her small face was flushed red, whether from frostbite or excitement, it was impossible to tell. It gave her a fierceness well beyond her years.

speaker: Nolaine
content: I don't want bread, and I don't want your life. I want... to go with you. I want to learn your skills.

speaker: Nolaine
content: This world has no good or evil, no justice, only power...! I want what you have. I want them to fear me. I want to be able to change things...!

speaker: Hilda
content: ...No. There is good and evil in this world. There is justice.

speaker: Hilda
content: You're still a child. I hope you can hold on to that belief.
She crouched down, bringing herself to eye level with the young girl.

speaker: Hilda
content: I'm from a city-state that was once filled with light and governed by justice. I came to DisCity to help it become the same.
[Fade to black for storytelling]
This is a crossroads for the world. In its street-side cafes, people peruse newspapers in dozens of languages, eagerly trading phrases from their homelands.
All children attend school; everyone has work and receives their rightful share. Theaters constantly debut new plays, and a laundry woman can walk proudly into a masquerade to dance with nobility.
No wars, no conflicts. People of every rank fulfill their duties, yet still have the energy to enjoy their lives.
Back then, it was the clearest vision of an ideal, an indestructible lighthouse in the hearts of countless souls.
[End Flashback Filter]

speaker: Hilda
content: Though war has scarred our world, I still believe that if we stand together, we can reclaim the shared ideals we once held.

speaker: Hilda
content: Give that back to me now, child. I won't bring you into our work, but I can give you all the money I have and take you somewhere safe and warm.

speaker: Hilda
content: You belong in a classroom, not on a battlefield...
[End of Flashback]

speaker: Nolaine
content: Of course... in the end... you couldn't talk me out of it...

speaker: Nolaine
content: But even now... I'm still not sure that I made the wrong choice.
Her voice breaks, fracturing into pieces, but her gaze holds Hilda's, fierce and unyielding.

speaker: Nolaine
content: You once told me... you became a spy... because you wanted the city-state to become that ideal in your heart. That kind of city-state... must have truly existed once, right?

speaker: Nolaine
content: I don't understand... When I work undercover, when I'm used by others... am I doing something wrong, or... something good? I really... can't tell anymore.

speaker: Nolaine
content: But as long as we're moving towards the right goal, we won't lose our way... right?

speaker: Nolaine
content: Hilda, you're different from me. You're smarter. You can definitely stay on the right path... because you... never lose sight of the goal.

speaker: Nolaine
content: What we're facing now... is just an inevitable obstacle on the path... that's all. We'll overcome it eventually... right?

speaker: Nolaine
content: ...And now you even have this special power. One that can see through everything and show the way forward... right?
Nolaine's breaths grow fainter, dwindling to a whisper.

speaker: Nolaine
content: Then can you tell me... which path is truly the right one?
The girl's last word hangs in the air and vanishes. Yet her eyes stay open, lingering on yours, waiting for an answer.
A long, heavy silence settles between you.

speaker: Hilda
content: ...Don't follow my example. Even with this power... there are still many things I cannot see through.

speaker: Hilda
content: In the end... haven't I lost you too?
But Hilda will never again hear a response from Nolaine.
Her figure is swallowed by the darkness. With Nolaine's death, Hilda's cold, hard shell seems to collapse, and she sinks into a deathly silence.
No response. Only the sound of heavy breathing, as if she had melted completely into the shadows.

speaker: Chief
content: This isn't your fault. Nolaine died in Manphist's suicide attack. You had nothing to do with it.

speaker: Hilda
content: ...No. This is my fault.

speaker: Hilda
content: I... was the one who told her Sevael's story... filling her head with unrealistic fantasies about the metropoles.

speaker: Hilda
content: I... was also the one who failed to stop her from joining us, who didn't guide her properly, letting her be used by Manphist and make terrible mistakes.

speaker: Hilda
content: With hollow ideals and beliefs, I led an innocent person astray... I took the life she should have lived...!

speaker: Chief
content: ...Hilda.

speaker: Chief
content: Having ideals isn't wrong. What's wrong are those cowards who manipulate others like pawns from the shadows, sending them into battle while profiting from their sacrifice.

speaker: Chief
content: Johnson sat in his position of power in the metropoles, yet he was nothing but scum who manipulated power and wealth without any morality; Manphist was a despised opportunist who'd turn at the slightest breeze, yet the metropoles welcomed him with open arms and generous rewards.

speaker: Chief
content: And then there's the hardest truth to accept: their exploitation of satellite towns, even dropping nuclear bombs on civilians to crush DisCity's rebellion.

speaker: Chief
content: They wave the banner of human unity while ruthlessly exploiting border regions and small states, using grand ideals as bait to make countless aspirational people sacrifice themselves for their cause.

speaker: Chief
content: Now that we've seen the truth... are you willing to keep being their pawn and continue down this path?
You hear a faint, dry sound in the air, like the friction of her knuckles tightening into a fist.
The silence that follows is broken only by the strain of her suppressed breath. It lasts for a long moment before she finally finds her voice.

speaker: Hilda
content: ...Is there any other way?

speaker: Chief
content: Yes. As long as we survive and get this evidence out, we can expose what we've witnessed and show the true face of the metropoles to more people. Even just a fragment of truth is enough to keep certain people awake at night!

speaker: Chief
content: Of course, if we end up like your parents, hunted by the metropoles, or completely erased...
Drawing a deep breath, you finally give voice to the dangerous, inciting thought you've harbored for so long.

speaker: Chief
content: Then let's go to DisCity... to the farlands... to places willing to hear the truth, willing to fight against exploitation and oppression, where we can truly realize our ideals of what a city-state should be.

speaker: Chief
content: A metropole like this doesn't deserve our loyalty.
A few days ago, these words for Hilda would have been unthinkable. Now, it doesn't matter anymore.

The mole is gone, the Monolith a phantom, the spy a lie. All that remains is a fool, toyed with and betrayed by the homeland she trusted so deeply. Now she is just a soul adrift, bewildered and utterly lost.
Silence stretches in the dark. When her answer finally comes, it's not the one you want.

speaker: Hilda
content: ...I don't think I can anymore...
A wave of dread washes over you. You immediately reach out, groping through the oppressive darkness toward the sound of her voice.
Your fingers find something wet first. Then, a hand rises to carefully touch your cheek. You seize it firmly in your own.
From the darkness, Hilda lets out a wry, pained laugh.
Her gloves are in tatters, shredded by the violent emergence of Mania spikes, revealing the torn and bleeding skin beneath.

This outbreak is far more severe than the last; the spikes are denser, more aggressive. Given the immense power she just unleashed against Manphist, the backlash from overexertion must be excruciating.
Right now, the shackles are the only option left.

speaker: Chief
content: I can try using another power to neutralize your contamination. No guarantees it'll work, but... are you willing to let me try?

speaker: Hilda
content: ...You're really an anomalous power expert?
"I really am. I just can't use my power because your LINK consciousness has been rejecting me," you grumble to yourself inwardly.

speaker: Chief
content: I can only try.
You've tried this before. The shackles had no effect on her then, but now...
A faint red light shimmers into existence in your hand as you cautiously reach for hers.
This time, there's no violent resistance. A small portion of the shackle's energy absorbs into her palm, but most of it simply flickers and dissolves into the air.
Yet, it's enough. The chaotic turmoil raging within her body begins to gradually subside.

speaker: Hilda
content: ...Thank you.
The flickering shackles cast a faint glow through the cramped space, illuminating Hilda's form nearby.
[Wounded CG]
She is closer than you imagined. Her head hangs low, hair veiling her features.
Sharp, solidified strands of Mania have pierced clean through her body, transforming her into a living pillar that desperately holds up the collapsed rubble.
She is the only reason this triangular safe zone exists. The space that protects you is the space her body buys.

speaker: Hilda
content: ...So you... saw it.

speaker: Hilda
content: Don't worry, it looks worse than it is... As long as one of us made it out... that's enough...

speaker: Option
options: Trust me, I'm getting us both out of here.

content: You immediately use the light to examine the collapsed surroundings.

Before the explosion, you were in the interrogation room beneath the manor. From what you can see now, the first floor directly above has completely collapsed. Escaping straight up is impossible, but...
You remember the manor's documents, the map of secret passages. A tunnel extends from this very chamber.
The switch is hidden behind the storage cabinet against the wall. You desperately try to recall everyone's positions in the moment before the blast.

Manphist was lunging toward the interrogation table when the explosion erupted from that point. Nolaine was closest to it, you were next, and Hilda was furthest away. And if your current positions—yours, Hilda's, and Nolaine's—were rearranged by the blast's force...

speaker: Chief
content: There!
Just a meter or two behind Hilda lies the entrance to the secret passage, blocked only by a few loose rocks.
When you tell her about the secret passage, Hilda's eyes widen in surprise.

speaker: Chief
content: Look, even your parents are still watching over you.

speaker: Chief
content: Don't give up, Hilda. I'm not giving up either.

speaker: Hilda
content: ...Okay.
She nods resolutely, and you immediately spring into action.

speaker: Chief
content: I'm going to try to move these rocks. It might hurt, so bear with me.
You start by clearing the smaller, movable rocks from around Hilda, working to create enough space for both of you to escape.
The stones grind against Hilda's shattered shoulder, forcing a sharp hiss of air through her clenched teeth. Yet her eyes lock with yours, burning with a silent, urgent command to continue.
Crack. An alarming sound splinters the air from the surrounding rubble. In response, Hilda calmly raises her left hand.
Those Mania strips spiral from her body once more. They whip through the dust-choked air, coiling around the unstable stones like spectral bands of steel. In an instant, the collapse is halted.
A fresh wave of cold sweat glistens on her ashen face.

speaker: Chief
content: ...I never thought that power could be used like this...

speaker: Chief
content: Hang in there! I'm almost done!
You pull and heave at the stones with all your strength. Each time the rubble shifts and groans, threatening to collapse, Hilda releases a surge of her Mania to lock the falling debris in place.

Time loses all meaning. Your world narrows to the weight of rock and the growing, throbbing pain in your hands. Your fingers are soon raw and bleeding, leaving crimson smears on every stone you manage to drag away.

Then, as you wrestle aside a final, fist-sized rock, you see the dull color of a storage box. The container is half-crushed from the explosion, but what steals your breath lies behind the shattered panel—a dark, yawning opening to a passage.

speaker: Chief
content: We've got a way out, Hilda!
[Scene Change: Cellar]
You emerge from the collapsed entrance, both too exhausted to take another step.
Still, your hand finds Hilda's. You press your barely effective shackles against her skin, struggling to calm the rampaging Mania that surges through her.
The wild crackle of Mania slowly fades from her body. In your daze, you think you hear the ghost of her laughter, but it must be your imagination.
Because neither of you has the strength left to speak.
Then, a slight movement in your hand. Her fingers trace a faint, deliberate pattern against your palm, a brief message in code.

speaker: Hilda
content: You really are... a remarkably kind person.
You rest in the cellar for a long time, until the barest shred of strength returns.
Hilda's left shoulder is ruined, and your own hands aren't much better.
The only thing that matters—the only victory—is that you're both still alive.

At some point, Hilda drags her injured body back toward the explosion site. She returns clutching a communication module salvaged from the Monolith remains. With some repairs, it could work as a radio.

speaker: Chief
content: I'm sorry, my fingers can't handle such delicate work anymore.
You watch Hilda busily working and can only spread your hands in resignation, forced to remain a helpless spectator.

She is truly impressive in this department. With just one good arm, she not only bandages your hands with practiced ease but also performs the most intricate repair work. She mentions, offhandedly, that her spy training included assembling radios blindfolded—and that she received top marks.
Hilda lets out a short laugh, her hands never pausing in their methodical dance.
Slowly, a makeshift communication radio begins to take shape. It's only then that she finally breaks the silence.

speaker: Hilda
content: ${PlayerName}, didn't you say before... you wanted to know how I transformed, and what abilities I gained?

speaker: Hilda
content: I think... if I don't tell you now, I might never get another chance...

Three Months Ago
DisCity Port

speaker: Crowd A
content: Help! Somebody, help! There's been a gas explosion! The whole area's gone! There could be dozens of people trapped in there!

speaker: Crowd B
content: Is it over?! Don't go in until it's over! We can't have more people dying!

speaker: Hilda
content: Wha... what's going on...?

speaker: Hilda
content: Was that... an attack?

She still remembers what happened minutes ago. She and her colleagues had intercepted intelligence about special military equipment being smuggled between the farlands and DisCity. Acting immediately, they had headed to the port to seize the contraband.

speaker: Hilda
content: My head... hurts...
Everything around her was in ruins. The explosion had collapsed the ground, sending her tumbling into a mining tunnel below.
Two crates of military equipment had shattered open, their contents strewn across the ground and littered over her body.

They seemed like crystals, transparent with a pink tint, as if they had been distilled from wind and sand. Tiny particles of energy orbited their cores. Freed from their sealed containers, the latent power within them began to awaken.

Shards had driven deep into her flesh during the blast. Like living organisms, they drank her blood, gradually turning bright red and growing scorching hot. A searing pain gripped her entire body as every vein convulsed and churned.
Before her reeling mind could make sense of it, an enemy lunged from the shadows, slashing a jagged blade toward her hand.
Hilda instinctively raised her arm to block. A metallic clang echoed in the tunnel, and she saw her attacker clearly—a figure wielding an eerie weapon, utterly devoid of any living presence.

In its grasp was a broken, grotesque thing, pieced together like shards of metal forged from countless battlefield souls. When it swung, the very air seemed to thin, sucking the breath from Hilda's lungs.
—It was DisCity's Reaper. Only moments before, it had been her colleague. Now, it was a horrifying soldier-like monster.
So this was DisCity's combat weapon?
It could transform a person into a monster in seconds?!
The enemy gave her no time to think, its assault relentless.

The Reaper's blade sliced her skin, and an icy chill flooded her flesh faster than the pain could register. This new cold warred against the burning heat inside her, two violent forces battling for control of her body.

speaker: Sinister Whispers
content: Give me... surrender yourself to me... she is mine... mine...

speaker: Hilda
content: ...Cough... What is... this...? Ugh! ...This is bad!
The chilling whispers spread through her bloodstream, making her very bone marrow tremble.
Gritting her teeth, she shook off her pursuer and stumbled away from the port, fleeing for her life.
Just as her consciousness began to shatter, a strip of telegraph paper seemed to materialize before her eyes.
Left, forward, don't stop.
Guided by those cryptic words, she finally escaped.
[End of Flashback]

speaker: Hilda
content: Just a tiny scratch is enough to plant this curse... If mastered on a large scale, this weapon would be more terrifying than Corruptors, capable of becoming a devastating threat. We must remain vigilant against DisCity at all times and establish proper defenses.

She later returned to the site, searching for her colleague who had succumbed to the Reaper's corruption. There, deep within the earth, she found only his exhausted corpse. Using her power, she drew forth his final, fading memories.
That harrowing experience forever colored her view of DisCity as a place of existential threat. It also explains her profound shock upon discovering the smuggling list within Manphist's memories.

Now, you finally learn the whole story of her awakening. In the era of the metropoles, Ash Crystals did create Sinners, but not through deliberate cultivation. Her transformation was a tragic accident, a fate she never chose.

speaker: Hilda
content: That code strip, appearing whenever I needed it, became my compass, helping me evade pursuit and guiding me all the way back to the safe house.

speaker: Hilda
content: For a long time afterward, I practiced using this power while learning to endure the backlash it caused.

speaker: Hilda
content: It constantly gnaws at my nerves and willpower. If I stop fighting it, I'll eventually be completely consumed by this power.

speaker: Hilda
content: But I also know this is a gift bestowed upon me. This ability is the ultimate trump card for an intelligence agent, and I will tame it and wield it.
Hilda raises a finger, commanding your attention. From the fading glow of the Monolith's remains, she draws forth a single, shimmering thread of new intelligence code.
