content: Hand you over to those DisCity people, and I'm home free.
Your legs buckle. The ground rushes up to meet you, and as your vision tunnels into nothing, someone grips your ankles, pulling you into a dark, cold corner.
[Main Hall]
If the mole orchestrated both explosions, then the blasts themselves were just a means to an end. The real clues—perhaps even the mole itself—were still on site.
You wrench your hand from Helene's grip and sprint after Nolaine through the doorway.
[Exterior]

speaker: Nolaine
content: What the hell are you doing here?! Desk jockeys like you will just get in my way!

With a flash of movement, she pulverizes a falling slab with a powerful kick, clearing the path. In the same instant, she seizes your arm, yanks you back from danger, and shoves you forcefully into the safety of the adjacent area.

options: Are you trying to destroy evidence?

speaker: Nolaine
content: Fine. If you've got a death wish, then follow me!
Nolaine's figure vanishes into the inferno. With a grit of your teeth, you plunge after her.
(Black Screen + Flames)
The world is smoke and chaos. The blast's aftermath stings your eyes, and the floor shudders with the rumble of fresh explosions nearby.
Schlick!
A muffled, sickening sound. Through the swirling ash, you see Nolaine's silhouette buckle and vanish into the gloom.
Schlick!
A second muffled sound—this one searing, personal. White-hot agony erupts in your abdomen. You glance down, dumbstruck, as a dark stain blooms rapidly across your clothes.
(Red Filter)
Your hand fumbles to stem the warm, slick flow, but your strength is already draining away. The world tilts, your vision blurring at the edges.
Through the dancing firelight, a mysterious silhouette solidifies. It calmly raises a firearm, centering it on your failing form.

speaker: Raspy Voice
content: Long live DisCity!

speaker: Helene
content: Aahh!!
Helene lets out a scream as she loses her balance and falls heavily to the ground.

speaker: Chief
content: Helene!
You quickly bend down and steady her.

speaker: Helene
content: My... my ankle... It hurts, it hurts so bad.

You look up. The others are gone. You've been left behind. Behind you, the tremor of the explosion rolls closer, followed by a wall of thick, black smoke. The fire's glow licks at the chaos, inching nearer.

speaker: Guard
content: Hey! Are you both alright?!
Through the choking smoke, the guard's silhouette turns back toward you. There's no time to think. You haul Helene over your shoulder and burst into the nearest room.
[Interrogation Room]

speaker: Helene
content: What's... all this about...? Why bring me in here?

speaker: Chief
content: It's safer. We can shelter here for a while.
You help Helene into the interrogation chair, her ankle swollen and useless.
But that's not enough. Once she's seated, you move to the next necessary step: fastening the restraints that bind her wrists to the chair.

speaker: Helene
content: Officer ${PlayerName}... really? An interrogation now? What could I have possibly done to raise your suspicions?
She gazes at you, her eyes slowly filling with tears.

speaker: Helene
content: Or is this about that letter?

speaker: Helene
content: What will you do after you get it? Kill me?
Her tears leave you frozen for a moment.
Indeed, the path is clear: interrogate Helene, seize the letter, and if needed, silence her forever. Your secret demands it.
But... is that who you are? Can you truly cross that line?
In that single heartbeat of doubt—
(Red Flash)
Schlick!
A crimson line etches the air. Understanding arrives a moment too late.
A strange weakness floods your body, the room lurching into a dizzying spiral.
Your knees buckle. In the moment of your collapse, you see Helene calmly repositioning herself in the chair.
The restraints were already undone, a fact you failed to notice. Now, a bloodied blade and a white envelope dance between her fingers, a macabre performance staged just for you.
(Black Screen)

speaker: Helene
content: I'd planned to keep using you for a bit longer. But you just had to go and spoil my plans, didn't you?

speaker: Helene
content: Promise me, never underestimate the "Hatter's" fingers again, alright?
[Exterior]
You rush to the manor's entrance, arriving just in time to see the messenger's retreating back. The crucial letter is already in the hands of the gate guard.
Faced with your request, the guard is an unyielding statue, his loyalty to protocol absolute.

speaker: Guard
content: The officer's orders are clear. All intelligence letters must go directly to her. I cannot relinquish it to anyone else.
Helpless, you can only watch as the guard turns and carries the letter into the main hall, sealing your fate.
[Scene Change: Hilda's Room]
You are escorted to Hilda's room with grim efficiency.
The questioning begins calmly, then sharpens when you offer no answers. Finally, with a disappointed sigh, she begins the formal interrogation.
The truth serum pulls you under, and your consciousness becomes a flood you cannot control. What secrets have you revealed? You may never know.
But it doesn't matter...
You think to yourself in a daze.
The next time you meet, she will have no memory of this. You will start again, as strangers meeting for the first time.

You dive through a hail of gunfire, bullets snapping past your ears, and you feel the searing heat of a few rounds grazing your body. You stagger behind a nearby chair, heart hammering against your ribs. Then, an unfamiliar guttural rasp cuts through the chaos from right beside you.
**** off! Get out of my way!
Bang. The world goes black. You never even see the shooter.
Marlo's intentions are still a mystery. It's better to play it safe and keep the guns out of his hands for now.

speaker: Marlo
content: The hell are you doing?! Give me those guns, now, or I'll—
(Sound effect: gunshots)
The moment Marlo hits the floor, a staccato rhythm of frantic footsteps echoes down the corridor, closing in fast.

speaker: Guard A
content: What's the hold-up? Are they dealt with or not?

speaker: Guard B
content: No survivors. Take the shot!
(Gunshot sound effects + red screen)
The relentless, gloomy rain has finally ceased, giving way to a rare and welcome sunrise.

speaker: Chief
content: Good morning, Hilda.

speaker: Hilda
content: Good morning.

speaker: Chief
content: Want some breakfast?

speaker: Hilda
content: Okay.
After the downpour, you scour the ruins of the collapsed annex and find the kitchen's skeleton.
From the wreckage, you salvage a few canned goods and some bread, their packaging miraculously intact. The resulting breakfast is simple: canned tomato sandwiches.
Your shelter is a wreck, the roof shattered and the floor still damp from the night's leaks. Despite it all, you and Hilda share a quiet, mutual contentment with the arrangement.

speaker: Hilda
content: It's delicious.
She takes a bite of her sandwich, then holds up a tiny device for you to see. It's barely half the size of a matchbox.

speaker: Hilda
content: The Monolith is complete. I can signal the city-state for extraction today.

speaker: Chief
content: That's a relief. I was starting to think we'd be hiking out of these mountains.

speaker: Hilda
content: Every road out of the estate is blocked. And the garage... most of the vehicles are unsalvageable.

speaker: Hilda
content: ...Let me be more precise. They've been blown to pieces. The city-state will probably send a helicopter.
You let out a sigh.
She notices your unexpected melancholy and asks with confusion.

speaker: Hilda
content: What's wrong? Don't you want to come back with me?

speaker: Hilda
content: Your contributions to the Monolith's successful development were vital. I want you there when I deliver the report.
In truth, your curiosity is undeniably there.
Could that helicopter—a fragment of the Outlands embedded in Hilda's mind—be a direct passage to their heartland?
It's a suicide mission, of course. Setting foot in the Outlands will be a death sentence the moment your identity is uncovered.
But after enduring these past few days, after wading through unimaginable carnage at Hilda's side merely to survive...
The specter of death has lost its power to terrify.

speaker: Hilda
content: Okay.
Hilda is visibly delighted.
[Room]
Before departing, Hilda asks you to pack up your room and make sure nothing is left behind.

speaker: Chief
content: ...Hmm... what should I take?
Your gaze drifts across the bookshelf until it finds the familiar spine of The Wilderness, the poetry collection from Hilda.
You carefully slide the book into your bag.
With nothing left to gather, you decide to see the cellar one last time.
[Scene Change: Cellar]

speaker: Hilda
content: ${PlayerName}? I didn't expect to find you down here.

speaker: Chief
content: Just... taking one last look at what we're leaving behind.

speaker: Hilda
content: ...Yeah. Even at the very end, I never discovered which one of them was the mole.

Her gaze sweeps nostalgically across the coffins, each one holding a classmate, a mentor, a colleague, a student...
They were all once part of her life, and now they are the part she herself had to cut away.

speaker: Hilda
content: ...But it's a meaningless question now. The Monolith is complete now. ${PlayerName} and I will leave today to deliver it to the city-state.

speaker: Hilda
content: May it be the key to our victory. May it ensure our city-state's strength and unity.
Blind with a strange, shared euphoria, we fail to hear the faint, almost silent ticking.
The warning goes unheard until we board the Outland helicopter.
Mania devours the estate first, a silent shockwave of raw force.
Then, the explosion tears the world apart.
You board the Outland helicopter, and it carries you toward the distant sunset.
You throw your body in front of Manphist, but he slams into you with the force of a freight train. The impact hurls you backward, and you crash against the wall.
(Blood Red)
A high-pitched ring fills your ears. Something warm and wet trickles down your temple.

speaker: Manphist
content: This is MY cipher machine! MIIIINE!
Before the horrified eyes of everyone, the monster's jaws unhinge. It seizes the waist-high Monolith and, with a single, brutal motion, forces the entire machine down its gaping throat.
The sound of grinding metal echoes from its gullet, a grotesque cacophony that quickly sharpens into a series of crackling ignition sparks. Then, a roaring blast erupts from inside its body.
(Explosion Sound + White Flash)
A tidal wave of raw Mania vomits forth from the depths of its being, instantly swallowing the entire estate.
The violent force crushes and tears at your body, and your world shatters into nothingness.
You clutch Hilda's brooch, its metal teeth biting into your palm. Turning your back on the manor, you walk into the roaring downpour.
A helicopter's searchlight pins you in its glare. Through the curtain of rain, you decipher the blinking message:
Survivor spotted. Did you send the radio signal?
Yes. It's you, and it has to be you.

Through the heavy rain, the world dissolves into a blur. You can only make out the DisCity soldiers surrounding you from all directions. Once they confirm you're not a Sinner, cold, standard-issue handcuffs click shut around your wrists.
Meanwhile, more troops swarm the front hall, forming a wide, cautious perimeter around Hilda. They fear the Mania radiating from her.
In the harsh lights, her silhouette seems small and achingly isolated, trapped between the soldiers and the chaotic Mania swirling around her.
Soon, sporadic gunshots crackle. They are closing in.
In response, the code strips of Mania fly from her hands, striking down her assailants with deadly precision. She feigns rage, glaring at you behind the protective wall of soldiers.

speaker: Hilda
content: ${PlayerName}. I never thought you would be the one to betray me...
She fights on, a desperate, final performance.
Glory. Dignity. Order. Loyalty.
The words she spits into the chaos are still dripping with the unmistakable arrogance of the metropoles.
As the soldiers breach the hall through flames and Mania, shouting for her surrender, a laugh escapes her lips. And she lets go. All her remaining Mania erupts in a single, devastating wave.

speaker: DisCity Agent
content: Stop her! Command wants her alive!
Throughout it all, her gaze never once leaves you.
You vaguely make out symbols forming within the Mania—shapes that feel somehow both deeply familiar and utterly alien.

speaker: Hilda
content: A full circle for a space, crescents for dots and dashes. It's a modified Morse code. Discreet, but efficient.
The symbols of the full moon and crescent moon shine brilliantly, mirroring each other in the sky.
They drift into alignment behind her, speaking only to you.
They are her final confession, hidden beneath her words.

speaker: Hilda
content:
Dream on, you DisCity hyenas.
<i><color=#fb9259>Thank you.</color><i>

speaker: Hilda
content:
I will never let you lay hands on my intelligence.
<i><color=#fb9259>It's a promise.</color><i>
Before the DisCity soldiers can take another step, she drags the glass across her neck.
In her final moments, a storm of Mania detonates around her. The world shatters; the very space you stand in begins to implode. Your LINK connection severs with a silent, violent snap.
She did ask you, personally, to end her life.
Why not just... fulfill her wish here and now?
You take a long, last look at her suspended form. Then, you give Schorl the termination order.
Your fingers close around the haft of the blood-stained hoe.
The moment you touch it, the world drowns in crimson.
A foreign will floods your nerves, and you are now a passenger in your own body. You watch as your legs carry you toward Hilda, your hand raising the hoe against her.

In that final second, you are no longer yourself. You are Shane. You are every vengeful villager. You are the pure, distilled essence of their rage and resentment. As if a thousand hands guide your own, the hoe falls. A bloody mist fills the air.
She does not speak. She does not cry out. She simply closes her eyes, a silent acceptance of the fate you deliver.
The blood is shockingly warm and sticky on your face.
When you come back to your senses, the vision shatters. Hilda and the mob are gone. Nothing remains but the phantom echo of their cheers, roaring in your ears.
(Red Flash)
Light erupts from your shackles, shattering the ghosts' blades. The spectral bonds dissolve, and you are free.

Without a second to lose, you roll forward and surge to your feet. A sharp, burning pain reminds you that a few blades found their mark with Mania already seeping into the shallow cuts. Ignoring the sting, you lunge toward Hilda and sever her ropes.

She stumbles as you haul her upright, but her gaze remains locked on the enraged ghosts. They scream, a hair's breadth away, but the shackles' light holds them at bay, a blinding barrier against their fury.
(Red Flash)

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Come with me! Let's get out of here first!
You seize her wrist and pull her toward the exit, not giving her a moment to protest.
(Scene Change)
Erratic light strobes through the corridor, casting the pursuing ghosts in jerking, nightmare tableaus. Their furious shrieks hammer at your back.
You pull Hilda along, feeling her stagger as she struggles to keep pace, but she never lets go.
The insidious Mania traces on your bodies, left by the ghosts' touch, continue to crawl over your skin like a spreading stain.

speaker: Hilda
content: Where are we going?
You don't have an answer yourself.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Anywhere is better than staying there to die.

speaker: Hilda
content: Don't you want to take a look at my heart?

speaker: Hilda
content: What kind of person I truly am... whether this is a trap, or genuine honesty... Don't you want to know?

options: You'll tell me when you're ready.
Is now really the time for this?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Some truths don't need to be laid bare to be understood. I've told you before, I'm not the kind of interrogator who has to uncover every truth at any cost.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I believe in you.
Survival comes first. When we're safe, and when you're ready... I'll be waiting to listen.
Hilda's footsteps falter. A flicker of uncertainty passes through her eyes.
You only tighten your grip on her hand. She doesn't question it; she just holds on tighter as you both run for the exit.
At the corridor's end looms a rust-eaten iron door. From behind it comes a deep, muffled hum.

You shove the door open, and the world dissolves. Howling wind and stinging, ice-cold rain slam into you. The corridor vanishes. The ghostly wails are snatched away into silence. The warmth of Hilda's hand in yours is gone; she has disappeared without a trace.
There is nothing left but you and the cold, pitch-black rain falling on your face.
As if driven by an unseen force, you step back.
The instant your legs move, the abyss answers. A web of black cracks races between your feet, darkness swelling like a tidal wave.
Hilda halts at the precipice. For a moment, she is perfectly still, like a statue at the edge of oblivion. Then, her body begins to lean back, her hollow gaze locked on you.
Her lips part, about to shape words, yet no sound comes out.
But her hand is speaking. You see her fingers tap a gentle rhythm.
"I'm sorry."
"I'm sorry."
The apology threads through the spectral howls, a needle of clarity that pierces straight to your heart.

The wails sharpen into a screech, like shards of glass in your mind. From the churning dark, a multitude of hands erupt. They seize her, pulling, clawing, dragging her down until the shadows swallow her whole.
Manphist retreats languidly onto the wall, a spectator who knew the final act all along.
With a soundless, final shudder, the great maw of the abyss closes. Hilda is gone, and the darkness settles, heavy and complete.
Sinking. Sinking endlessly. Consciousness is dragged into the abyss.
Then, a single strand of red light appears.
It's a lifeline from that young person. A chance for escape.
That person came here with a purpose, much like your own.
He is a good soul, radiant with justice, and he has helped you enact your self-punishment.
female_content: She is a good soul, radiant with justice, and she has helped you enact your self-punishment.

content: Look upon your irredeemable sins, Hilda. Look upon your shattered heart, Hilda.
That person showed you a world so similar to your own: the gleaming metropoles and weary satellite towns, the idealistic youth and the corrupt politicians, the same shadows festering beneath it all.
He offered a hand. But you were already in pieces. What could you possibly give?
female_content: She offered a hand. But you were already in pieces. What could you possibly give?

content: It is all too late now.

speaker: Hilda
content: I really wish... I had met you sooner...
With this lament, her gaze drifts once more to that light not far away.
How cruel it looks, a single, brilliant promise in this vast, consuming darkness.
A light meant to illuminate the future, not to be touched by a failure like her.
And so her hand goes limp. Her fingertips graze yours in a final, fleeting brush as she lets go.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Hilda?! No!!
You thrash downward, desperate to catch her, to pull her back. But the chasm between you only widens.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Damn it... This distance... even my shackles can't reach...
The Mania-contaminated sludge coils around her, an anchor dragging her down toward the abyss.

speaker: Hilda
content: ${PlayerName}... I won't be leaving with you.

speaker: Hilda
content: I've been asleep for too long... so long I didn't even know my own city-state was gone.
The violent surge of Mania subsides, and with it, the fury in her.

speaker: Hilda
content: In your memories, I saw familiar shadows. DisCity may be heading down the same path as the metropoles. If you truly want to stop it... you must become stronger than it.

speaker: Hilda
content: Recruiting a teammate who's always failing would be bad luck. It's better if I stop right here.

With a wave of feigned casualness, she unleashes a final, massive surge of Mania from within—not as an attack, but as a beacon, exposing her greatest vulnerability. In an instant, the greedy shadows surrounding you forget your presence. They surge toward her, a swarm drawn to a brighter flame.
In contrast, her scattered memories transform. They become code strips of the bygone era, fluttering like butterfly wings, gently surrounding you in a protective cocoon.
She vanishes from your sight. Then the sludge, the entire oppressive space. It all dissolves around you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What are you doing? Hey! Hilda!
You pound your fists against the barrier that now encases you. From a great distance, her voice reaches you, tinged with a gentle smile.

speaker: Hilda
content: If you ever speak of me to others... make it a cautionary tale. A story about someone who took the wrong path and paid the price for her foolishness.

speaker: Hilda
content: Go protect your city-state, ${PlayerName}. The new era belongs to you. Don't let it stray down our old road.

speaker: Hilda
content: As a ghost from a bygone era... this single warning is all I have left to give.
The filth crawls over her, and the familiar shackles snap shut once more. The consciousness she had fought so hard to maintain finally begins to disintegrate.
Decades of resentment and despair, shattered by a final act, complete their work. She is remade, fully, into a Corruptor, a wanderer in the eternal darkness.
When you finally break free from your cage, it is too late. You can only watch, helpless, as the last echoes of her memory slip through your fingers like smoke, disappearing into the void.
With her disappearance, the time Schorl granted you runs out.
The space begins to crystallize, then freeze, as your connection to her is irrevocably severed.

speaker: Hilda
content: Farewell, ${PlayerName}.

speaker: Hilda
content: ...There's no place for me in this new era.

speaker: Hilda
content: To be buried with the era that created me... is the only fitting end.
[Black Screen]
The illusion is gone, completely.
Hilda stands before you once more.
[Contamination CG - Animated]

Mania has morphed into cruel shackles around her body, concealing the scar on her throat. Her long hair is plastered to a face and neck as pale as marble. Her eyes—once so piercing, so deeply knowing—are now vacant, like wells that have long run dry.
Yet, as her gaze finds you—you, who have returned to this desperate place, who have fought so hard to reach her—the ghost of a smile touches her lips.

speaker: Hilda
content: Why... did you come back?

options: I told you I would help you.

speaker: Hilda
content: ...You fool... This place is dangerous...

speaker: Hilda
content: Mania could consume my consciousness completely at any moment. Soon, even this last sanctuary will be thoroughly corrupted.

speaker: Hilda
content: When that happens... not even those "memories" will be able to guide you.
She points at your body, and in response, specks of white light drift from you like luminous dust. They float through the air, settling upon her hand.
Wherever they land, the shackles binding her dissolve, melting away like snow under a warm sun.

speaker: Hilda
content: ...That time you were drinking tea in my room... you suddenly jumped up and said you could smell poison.

speaker: Hilda
content: You tried to act casual, but your expression was so serious as you searched the entire room... and you actually found it.

speaker: Hilda
content: You saved my life, and yet... I still doubted you.

speaker: Hilda
content: When I received that letter from the metropoles... you discovered I had been using you, testing you.

speaker: Hilda
content: You said we were just two tools, thrown together by circumstance... walking different paths, yet choosing to stay.

speaker: Hilda
content: I felt truly grateful.

speaker: Hilda
content: And then... you used The Wilderness to help us uncover the mole.

speaker: Hilda
content: The ideals of the past... they are both the key to the truth, and the witnesses to all that has happened.

speaker: Hilda
content: ...Then, at the very end.

speaker: Hilda
content: I entrusted everything to you... let you leave this place. To use my "corpse" and the "Monolith" to accomplish two tasks.

speaker: Hilda
content: As a result... I was tortured for years, then sealed for decades. I started out just waiting for death... but eventually, I only wanted one thing. An answer.

speaker: Hilda
content: But now that you're finally here... I find I'm no longer so fixated on that answer.

speaker: Hilda
content: I just... really wanted to see you again. That's all...
Her hand rises from the mire of contamination, stretching toward you with painstaking caution.

speaker: Hilda
content: ...No matter what... thank you. Thank you for coming back for me.

You instinctively recoil half a step, evading her touch. Her fingertips hang suspended in the air for a fractured second before falling gently to her side. That faint smile still lingers on her lips, but now it's etched with a profound and quiet bitterness.

speaker: Hilda
content: It's alright... At least you did come.
Mania ripples, a slow, consuming tide that begins to swallow the last fragments of her form.
She has failed. She has struggled. She has never truly surrendered. And yet, you are the one who let go.
Perhaps it's a subconscious alarm bell, a primal instinct for self-preservation. Or maybe a colder, more rational conclusion, that even if she wakes, her existence will be nothing but agony.
You watch Mania claim her, and within you, there is only a vast, silent hollow.
Then, the world convulses. Waves of Mania erupt in a violent storm as corruption spreads like a plague. The very space around you groans, fracturing and beginning to implode.

Suddenly, from the churning mire before you, a figure forces its way into being. Mania has sculpted her new body—a silhouette of pure, volatile energy. She lurches forward, her arms, dripping with primordial filth, locking you in a desperate, crushing embrace.
Her fingers tremble against your back as scars of raw Mania spider-web across her skin.
And in the moment of that embrace, her whisper brushes against your ear—

speaker: Hilda
content: I gave you everything. My ideals, my trust. I waited... and you never came.

speaker: Hilda
content: I told myself you must have had your reasons. But as the years turned, that waiting festered. Mania didn't just consume me... it became me.
Familiar howls twist with her whispers as her hands lock onto yours. Her fingertips are like ice, yet they burn with the last, lingering warmth of her obsession.

speaker: Hilda
content: Now you're back... but it's too late. I don't believe you anymore.
Your foreheads touch.

speaker: Hilda
content: ...This time, I will see the truth for myself.
The contamination vanishes, giving way to a storm of code strips that rustle and sway around you.
Her grip tightens, a desperate vise, and a profound emptiness yawns open inside you.

Mania assails you from all sides, ripping through your being. Before your eyes, your very essence is torn away, transforming into countless intelligence strips. They unravel, merging with the air itself, converting into a tide of radio waves.
You finally realize it. She is using her power on you!
[Shackles]
You raise your hand to release your shackles, and a flickering red light erupts, piercing through your palms. But it is not enough. It cannot halt this desperate, all-or-nothing assault.
Your memories break free in a frantic flood, stripped bare and completely exposed to her ravenous power.
The world before you bleeds away. Only her voice remains—a gentle, yet unyielding echo, resonating in the depths of your mind like a whisper from the abyss itself.
(Mania effect transitions to red text)
<color=#fb9259>Since we met, we've been deciphering each other.</color>

speaker: Hilda
content: So this is the real you—

speaker: Hilda
content: Hero of DisCity, Chief of Minos Bureau of Crisis Control, ${PlayerName}.
Alarms blare throughout the laboratory deep within the Restricted Area.

speaker: Researcher A
content: Hilda's M-Value is spiraling again! Contamination is off the charts!

speaker: Researcher B
content: The Chief's levels are climbing too, but still within the controllable range due to suppression by the shackles.

speaker: Researcher A
content: Hilda's Mania is flaring; it's creating a feedback loop to the Chief... Wait, what?! She knows about LINK?!
Faint, barely visible electrical currents ripple across Schorl. Minutes later, it speaks, its composure icy as it begins issuing orders.

speaker: Schorl
content: Continue monitoring and prepare to activate the mandatory protocol. Priority is ${PlayerName}'s safety. Regarding the subconscious incursion, if she breaches ${PlayerName}'s mental defenses, it will ultimately simplify our task.

speaker: Schorl
content: Initiate a 15-minute countdown. Prepare the suppressant injection and stand by to terminate the LINK connection.

speaker: Schorl
content: Notify MBCC to be on standby. If Mania exceeds the critical threshold, we will transport Hilda, alongside the tank, to the upper level, sever her connection to the Chief, and proceed with termination.

speaker: Schorl
content: We cannot allow her to extract any intelligence from this facility.
[Memory Space: Telegraph Background]

In the span of a few breaths, Hilda's power floods the space. Code strips unspool from your very being, cinching around your limbs and hoisting you aloft. They flutter from her fingertips like a silent, papery snow.
Your shackles and her power intertwine; your consciousness and memories knot together in a profoundly unnatural braid.

Yet she ignores the iron biting into her flesh and the corruption seeping through her veins. Her fingers, with a ghost's touch, trace the contours of your mind, coaxing your memories to unfold before her.
[Flashback Filter: Deep Restricted Area]

speaker: Schorl
content: Before the shackles appeared, we lacked effective means to control highly dangerous and difficult-to-manage Sinners. For humanitarian reasons, execution was not an option. So, cryosleep technology was employed to preserve them in stasis. A practice that continues to this day.

speaker: Schorl
content: With the latest <color=#fb9259>LINK</color> technology, we can now attempt to enter their deep consciousness and awaken their minds.
[Flashback Filter: Small CG - Containment Tank]

speaker: Schorl
content: <color=#fb9259>Hilda Hartlein</color>. She was a cryptography expert working for the metropoles during the First Outland War.

speaker: Schorl
content: We hope you can extract more information on the "Monolith" system and "Outlands Sinners." Specifically, we need to understand how the metropoles secured the allegiance of such a powerful Sinner in an era when they were exceptionally rare, and whether any secret technology was involved.
[Memory Space]

She doesn't just watch your memories; she forces you to relive them with her. Together, you see Schorl introducing you to LINK... the collective decision to select her as the target... your approach to the Sinner's containment pod. You see your past self look up, your own eyes calmly conveying the message: I will complete the mission.
She makes you an unwilling participant in this twisted retrospective, forcing you to "appreciate" the betrayal alongside her.

speaker: Hilda
content: Fascinating, isn't it? Are you afraid of the guiltiness when your lies are laid bare? Or do you fear the truth is too cruel for me to bear?
She grabs a code strip and gives it a deliberate tug, yanking you closer to her.

speaker: Hilda
content: It's really not difficult to accept. You are DisCity's hero. I am a metropole spy. We were destined to stand on opposing sides.

speaker: Hilda
content: You played your part perfectly, made me dance in the palm of your hand. I thought you were my only hope. I entrusted you with everything—the Monolith, the correction of my mistakes—believing you like a fool... waiting for a miracle that would never come.

speaker: Hilda
content: Of course you would never come back. You were always DisCity's loyal servant. Stealing the Monolith was your only objective. All that talk of correction and ideals was meaningless.
A storm finally breaks in her gaze. Anger, grief, and mockery, all crashing through at once.

speaker: Hilda
content: So why come back now? What else is left for you to take from me?

options: I came to save you. I mean it.

speaker: Hilda
content: I will not believe you again.
Her gaze locks with yours, every word measured and sharp as a blade.
The raw, near-desperate intensity in her eyes pains you. An invisible hand seems to clamp around your throat, stealing your breath and your voice. You try to form words, but only silence emerges.

speaker: Hilda
content: You still cannot control your tells. I am perfectly fine now. So why do you look at me with such pity? What are you hiding from me this time?
You instinctively recoil, but she's faster. Her hand darts out, her fingers firm as they grasp your chin, holding you in place.

speaker: Hilda
content: We have all the time in the world. I will use my power to strip your secrets away, layer by layer, until I see what truly lies in your heart...

speaker: Hilda
content: ...I will not fall into your trap again.
Her words are a soft whisper, but her fingers tighten like a vise. More code strips of your memory surge from within you, a torrent that makes your very consciousness shudder.
[Flashback Filter: Restricted Area]

speaker: Schorl
content: Welcome back, Chief. The results of this LINK session appear to be satisfactory on all fronts. You have successfully retrieved the Monolith, and the data concerning the metropoles and the Ash Crystals constitutes entirely new intelligence for us.

speaker: Schorl
content: We will now begin analyzing Hilda's brain to extract the "Monolith" within. Please rest here for the moment; you may review the findings once you have recovered.
[Flashback Filter: Laboratory]

speaker: Schorl
content: After prolonged confinement in a contaminated environment, Hilda's consciousness and memories were already fragmented. Because you continuously input new memory segments during the LINK process, her cognitive functions have begun to show signs of confusion.

speaker: Schorl
content: She mistakenly believes that the "memories" you constructed for her are her actual past, that you truly rescued her and took all her hopes away from that place.

speaker: Schorl
content: On this foundation, her mind has reconstructed memories spanning decades. In her perception, she has been waiting for you to return and fulfill your promise ever since the day you left, but her wait has yielded nothing but silence.

speaker: Schorl
content: Mania is a mutation of the mind, and memory is the vessel of consciousness. Decades of accumulated despair and breakdown erupted in an instant, causing the Mania within her to spiral completely out of control.
[Background: Mania-Contaminated Consciousness Space]
She watches in continued silence, her eyes a fractured mirror reflecting countless shattered scenes.

speaker: Hilda
content: So... even my memories are fake. This is nothing but an illusion, a construct left by your manipulation of my mind...

speaker: Hilda
content: I was such a fool.

speaker: Hilda
content: There was no betrayal, because the comrade I fought alongside never truly existed.

speaker: Hilda
content: What I want... is...

options: Stop torturing yourself with Mania. Come with me.

speaker: Chief
content: Mania will consume you completely. I want to get you out of here.

speaker: Hilda
content: ...Out? You mean to "wake up"?
She doesn't wait for your answer. Her hand rises. Her fingers find the scar on her throat.

speaker: Hilda
content: ${PlayerName}, do you know... how I survived the torture of DisCity's agents?

speaker: Hilda
content: A slit throat cannot speak, so they first infused Mania Crystals into my body, using mutation to repair the damage. Once they were sure I wouldn't die, they began... every form of physical and psychological torment imaginable.
—Thoughts of suicide had whispered to her countless times. Oblivion promised a mercy this endless torture did not.
—Yet, she endured. For the faint hope of waiting for someone to come. Forced to bear the unbearable.
But she could not let them defile her. Could not let them plunder the things she held dear: the memory of her parents, the echo of her ideals, her last, fragile hopes.
If the outside world could not be trusted, if her own mind and body were nothing but a torture ground... then let a more absolute end claim it all.
Use Mania.
The command was a silent scream, a final act of will from a voice that had been stolen.
Come. Swallow me. Encase these memories. Seal my consciousness. Lock my mind away with the heaviest chains.
And with that, she severed her final tether to the world. With a self-annihilating resolve, she extended an invitation to the darkness she had long held at bay.
Afterward... her consciousness did not fall; it willingly stepped into the abyss of Mania, and was no more.

speaker: Hilda
content: I will not fall into DisCity's hands again.
Her words are laced with an inescapable madness.

speaker: Hilda
content: You are far too valuable to DisCity. Losing you would be like losing an army... So... they will not risk harming you to stop me.

speaker: Hilda
content: The overflowing Mania will destroy this entire Restricted Area, and you will awaken with me...
As she speaks, she tightens her grip on the code strips. A jolt of electricity instantly sears through your body.

speaker: Hilda
content: I just want to leave... LINK will let them see what you are experiencing. Let them watch and listen, and consider my proposal.
You gaze at her in stark silence, your teeth gritted. In her ashen-red eyes, you see no hope—only a staring abyss, spun from the threads of ruin and a deep, devouring obsession.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If you did manage to escape DisCity... where would you go?

speaker: Hilda
content: I will return to the Sevael Republic. To finish the task once entrusted to you... the one you failed to complete...
Hearing her answer, you feel nothing but sorrow.

You used the Monolith as bait, contaminated your own consciousness with Mania to hide information, waited for decades in the cracks of memory, and finally captured me to break the stalemate... All this, just to use me as leverage to force DisCity to release you? So you can return to that metropole?
You know it is rotten to the core.

speaker: Hilda
content: But it is still my homeland.

speaker: Hilda
content: Even if it is twisted beyond recognition, even if it is rotted to the bone, I will still reshape it. I will change it. I will save it.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: A city-state does not change because of one person. You are facing an entire system, a corruption rooted in human nature itself.
And you have seen with your own eyes how they corrupt and destroy people.
Yet Hilda simply shakes her head.

speaker: Hilda
content: Nothing is beyond change... People are the variable that influences everything. People create systems, people become corrupt, people kill—so people must also be the ones to correct these wrongs.

speaker: Hilda
content: Precisely because it is flawed, we need determined individuals to cut out the sickness, to defend justice, not run from it!

speaker: Hilda
content: If the city-state is truly rotten, then I will cut it open and drain the poison. I now have the means. No one can hide the truth from me. I will use my power to see through everything!

She roars in defiance, a desperate attempt to convince herself. But the fracture in her resolve is laid bare, instantly detected by the unrelenting resentment that saturates the space. It answers with a howl of its own, coalescing and striking at her from every direction.

speaker: Chaotic Voice
content: ...Can't accept it... a lifetime devoted... for this...

speaker: Chaotic Voice
content: ...Surrender... to me... I can grant you power... to break free... to change it all...

speaker: Chaotic Voice
content: Any means necessary... survive... survive... change everything... change the city-state!!
Like moths to a flame, the tempting whispers throw themselves against the cage of the code strips, disintegrating into ash against its barrier of her power.
You watch her fight a war on two fronts, against the corrupting backlash of Mania and the grip of your own shackles. Her body trembles, swaying on the very verge of collapse.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Your war ended long ago... What we're doing now is—

speaker: Hilda
content: Shut up! I said I will not believe you!!
Her hands are trembling as they cup your face. She gazes deeply into your eyes, only to find a profound compassion within.

speaker: Hilda
content: What else do you know? What else are you hiding from me?

speaker: Hilda
content: Tell me... let me <color=#fb9259>see</color> it.

speaker: Hilda
content: ...Please...
More memories transform, becoming fluttering code strips that tear themselves from your body. They swarm outward, a frantic, suffocating blizzard that devours the space around you.
Pain lances through you—the excruciating tear of your consciousness, your very soul being ripped open.
...So let her see it all.
You hold her gaze as she plunges into the hidden corners of your mind, racing straight toward the truth you had buried in the deepest trenches of yourself.
[Flashback Filter: Archives]
Schorl led you to the cabinet housing the metropole archives. With practiced ease, it unlocked it.
You pulled file after file, but each one told the same date that marked the day the metropole vanished from all historical record.

speaker: Schorl
content: After their defeat in N.F. 82, the metropole made no efforts to correct its course. Instead, it fell deeper into corruption until it eventually fractured from within.

speaker: Schorl
content: As for Hilda herself, she endured extensive interrogation after her capture. Yet she never disclosed even the slightest piece of intelligence. Eventually, she attempted to erase her own consciousness using Mania, which led to her being forcibly placed in suspended animation, remaining in the Restricted Area for decades.

speaker: Schorl
content: What a pitiable and tragic woman. She remains completely unaware that <color=#fb9259>her homeland was destroyed long ago</color>.
[Consciousness Space]
In this moment, the entire world freezes.
In the sudden, profound silence, all feeling drains from her. You see the anger on her face melt away, leaving only naked bewilderment.

speaker: Hilda
content: ...What...is it saying?
You take a deep breath.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm really sorry for giving you these painful memories.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I can't fix this for you, and we can't let you leave DisCity to save the metropole.
Because the homeland you want to change and save was gone decades ago.
Under the scorching sun of Eastside, you clutch a gold foil ticket while standing at the entrance of a storefront. The sign above displays large letters in a Gothic font: Nightwrought.

The narrow pedestrian street is packed with visitors drawn by this famous place. The air is thick with excitement and anticipation, mingled with the unique exhaustion of working adults. Perfume, sweat, and food aromas blend into a dizzying urban scent that assaults your nose.

According to Faye, this is an "all-in-one sensory playground" that combines escape rooms, murder mystery games, TRPG, and immersive theater. Today, you'll plunge into its magnum opus, its signature production that has made countless guests scream, forget how to speak, or even flee in tears: <color=#fb9259>Cirrenfold</color>.

On Eastside's online forums, people are engaging in heated debates with all sorts of opinions, but most respect the "no spoilers" rule and simply urge other curious onlookers to experience it themselves.
[Flashback] Bureau Office

speaker: Faye
content: Chief, you're working yourself to death! This sallow face, these dark circles, and those new wrinkles on your forehead! Look at you, you're wasting away!

She'd said the same thing 52 times now, trying to sell you some health supplements or skincare products the Supply Office needed to get rid of each time. Normally, your response was always the same, which was...

speaker: Wynn
content: Hold on, hold on, don't be so quick to refuse, Chief! What Faye is trying to sell you this time is legit! Eugene and I have both been there. It's super fun, you know, that place...

speaker: Faye
content: Exactly! It's all everyone ever talks about these days...

speaker: Faye
content: "Escape the agony of real life. Dive into a world of wonder! Forget who you are and what you do. Right now, we are all residents of Cirrenfold!"
Seriously? Watching Faye's enthusiastic delivery of the line and Wynn nodding vigorously in agreement, you remained skeptical and looked toward Eugene, the most honest and trustworthy of the bunch.

speaker: Eugene
content: Things have been going smoothly at the Bureau lately, and all the major cases have been wrapped up. Chief, why not have a day out to relax and recharge for a bit?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Is it a good idea? The last time I took your bait was Belphegor. Nearly blew up the entire Eastside. You sure we won't run into another unexpected situation this time?
Faye wagged her index finger smugly, then generously pushed a ticket into your hand.

speaker: Faye
content: Promise you, you won't! This one is approved by multiple staff members of the Bureau. It's totally risk-free! You can rest easy, Chief!
[End of Flashback]

Normally, at this hour, you should be working at the Bureau... but unable to resist the spiel of the three, you finally pry yourself away from your office after being cooped up in the Bureau for so long.
They all went on and on about how wonderful it was, yet strangely, no one has offered to accompany you for a second visit.
This place seems to have drawn in all Eastsiders looking for some fresh thrills. Young students, elite professionals, and weary individuals like yourself stealing a respite from the daily grind.

Looking at the bustling crowd inside and outside the place, you suddenly get cold feet. Sure, getting out and relaxing is good for your mental and physical health, but you haven't seen this many people in so long that it triggers your anxiety, your introverted tendencies suddenly intensifying.
With a weary sigh, you withdraw your hand on the door. Maybe you should just go back to work instead...
Before you can act on your decision, a group of energetic college students swarming in pushes you through the entrance.

Darkness blurs the crowd's silhouettes as you blink to adjust your eyes. In the pitch-black corridor, the candelabra meant to indicate directions doesn't feel like a guiding torch, but rather like several cold eyes staring from the darkness.

The once noisy, laughing voices suddenly fall silent, as if a thick, heavy presence in the darkness has covered their mouths and noses. No one dares to breathe loudly, only pressing against each other's shoulders as they collectively move toward the end of the dark space.

Rumina pads over to your tiny wax figurine and bends down to pick it up, carefully brushing off the dust. Her tone is casual, as if she were just discussing the weather with you. She cradles the wax figurine in her hands before passing it to you.
What a fine little thing. You can't help but poke at the little wax figurine again, with its gaping mouth and bewildered expression.
Was this really your expression right before your "death"? You reach up to touch your own face.
You suddenly recall that unusual stiffness you felt upon waking. Does it mean... that after each "death," your dying expression will be preserved here, turned into a wax figurine by Rumina?
They might even sell it at the gift shop when you exit the game.
That would be mortifying, but the idea makes you chuckle anyway.
What concerns you most right now is the mysterious figure you saw at the end. Would Rumina answer if you asked her directly? You decide to test the waters.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Rumina, is there an NPC here with long purple hair who wears a black fitted dress?
Rumina opens her mouth, but no sound comes out. She just stands there silently, like a motionless doll.

Seon turns to Rumina, then back to you. A wisp of smoke leaking from its wick, it seems frustrated for not being able to take any side. Seeming deflated, it rests its five fingers on Rumina's hand, deciding to stay out of it.
But someone else chimes in excitedly.

speaker: Eleanor
content: I know, I know! You must have found an Easter egg! They're quite common in this kind of game! Aw, you're so lucky!
Eleanor eagerly squeezes her way in, breaking the awkward silence that has settled between you.
Rumina seems to breathe a small sigh of relief as she silently retreats into the shadows. Seon climbs up her arm to her shoulder, hopping and waving goodbye to you joyfully.
But you're not about to let her walk away that easily. You still need to confirm some information.

In this type of game, there are usually many NPCs played by actors who follow their own scripts and drive key plot developments. Only by interacting with them can players gain information in the story and enjoy a unique experience.
Eleanor hasn't encountered any NPCs like Prima, and is eagerly urging you to return to where you first met Prima to retry that route. But will you really meet Prima again? You feel somewhat doubtful.
The two of you trudge through the foggy forest unsteadily. Just like during your first round, next to a twisted, dead tree, you once again find that white figure waiting for you. It's Prima.
She slowly turns around, her expression downcast. When she sees that it's you, her eyes instantly light up, and she runs over with excitement.

speaker: Prima
content: Oh my goodness, Mr. Voyager! I thought I wouldn't see you again until after the next moonset! Are you alright?
female_content: Oh my goodness, Miss Voyager! I thought I wouldn't see you again until after the next moonset! Are you alright?

content: It seems she still remembers you.

options: Something's wrong. I seem to have forgotten something.

content: Something about the Witch... What was it again? Seeing you struggling to remember, Prima smiles with tears in her eyes.

According to Prima, after you released spiky beams of red light, both you and the shadowy figure vanished together. She was too frightened to move, only emerging once she felt it was safe. Worried you might return and not find her, she's been waiting here ever since.
Eleanor listens enviously.

speaker: Eleanor
content: Having a cute girl cry for my death... Why didn't I get such a beautiful reward for dying?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I think you prefer those strange-looking vines instead. They seem more exciting to you, don't they?
Eleanor punches your arm in annoyance, threatening that next time she'll tie you up with those vines.
Having found your lost companion and progressing in the story again, the atmosphere finally lightens as you all explore toward the town.

Eleanor turns out to be a skilled player. While you are still exploring the town with trepidation, she's turned the place upside down, chatting with each villager multiple times and extracting all their hidden information.

Eventually, even the frightening ghosts can't be bothered to appear before her. After sweeping through the town like an expert player, she's convinced she's finished her round prematurely and begins to stretch and yawn idly.
You walk over to Eleanor and examine the various items she's plundered from the villagers: letters, notes, small rings, oranges... even some villagers' clothing and other stuff...
In this type of game, ransacking everything like a bandit seems to be a perfectly acceptable behavior.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Yes?
Many of the written materials coincidentally document the villagers' thoughts about the Witch. You crouch down and start reading them.

Villager's Letter: The town hasn't been peaceful lately. Everyone says it's the Witch. To keep my child safe, I tried sending him to my cousin in the neighboring village. But... every night, the neighbors would bring my son back. I told them repeatedly he was not lost and didn't need to be sent back, but they simply wouldn't listen. After several attempts, there was nothing more I could do. What's more... I've noticed something wrong with my son. He doesn't seem like the same child anymore... I know this sounds unbelievable, but please come back and see for yourself. The child... he frightens me sometimes! Did... he...?!

Mayor's Notes: The fog in the town grows thicker each day. Unclean things lurk within it. Flowers in the forest have begun to devour people. The soil turns up putrid corpses. More and more people fall under the curse, transforming into corrupted monsters... This is the Witch's warning! The ward is crumbling. "Her" curse has seeped into every inch of the land. I know it. "She" has returned. The signs of doom draw near... For the town's peace, we must perform a sacrificial ritual immediately! Before the next blood moon falls, we must find a pure soul...

A New Interpretation of the Witch's Legend: At the kingdom's border lies a strange town shrouded in eternal fog and ravaged by disasters and curses. Legend says it's a forsaken land cursed by the Witch of Rewind. Many people leave their homes and arrive with desire and fervor, hoping the Witch could fulfill their wishes. The Witch hasn't chosen to stay willingly. People have trapped her here to harness her power. This "stolen" peace won't last forever. People must find a pure soul during the three moonrises and moonsets to quench the Witch's wrath.

Notes on the Foggy Town Written by: J. H., Traveling Scholar I've been here several days now. The fog is so unnaturally thick that it's impossible for one to tell the directions. At first, I thought this was just another ordinary remote town. But the more I know, the more I become unsettled. Tales about a Witch of Rewind prevail in the town. They say she can manipulate time and bestow peace. I initially dismissed this as mere folklore, a phenomenon not uncommon for a dwindling population whose faith has collapsed. But something is wrong. The roads at the entrance keep looping back. No matter which way I walk, I can't leave. I've observed that the townspeople all gaze up in the same direction at night... At a dark red moon. To anyone reading this: Do not enter the town after the fog rises. If you hear whispers around you, do not turn around. Run!

speaker: Prima
content: What are you reading?
Just as you're examining the writings, Prima suddenly peeks over your shoulder.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Some legends about a certain witch. Everyone in this village is terrified of her. We need to pass the Witch's Trial, and these might be our clues.
Come to think of it, Prima is also an NPC from here. Would she know something about the Witch in purple? Surely she won't be as tight-lipped as Rumina?
Prima tilts her head slightly, looking innocently ignorant.
Never mind. You sigh and return to the documents in your hands. The Witch, magic, wishes, and... the hourglass...
You find yourself instinctively looking up at the sky. You've never seen a moon shaped like this before. It's round, but somehow constricted in the middle, making it look more like...
An hourglass.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Has the moon always looked like this here?

speaker: Prima
content: Oh, I see. You're feeling homesick, aren't you? When you described the foreign world to me last time, I was absolutely fascinated! Could you tell me more about your life there? I want to hear more of your stories.
Prima stares at you intently with bright, curious eyes.

Noticing your animated conversation, Eleanor scoots over and perks up her ears to listen. The atmosphere feels perfect for a cozy chat, so you decide to share a few things, pretending you're telling bedtime stories to kids.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: My home... I suppose you could call it that. It has many floors and countless rooms. We usually relax in the common areas and celebrate holidays together.

speaker: Prima
content: Wow, you have a huge home! You never have to worry about coming back to an empty house. Someone will always leave the light on for you. I bet you never feel lonely, huh. That must be nice.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: My family... they come from all walks of life and have vastly different life stories, yet each of them is connected to me for one reason or another.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Most ordinary people fear them, but in fact, some of them are young girls just like you. They're not so different from anyone else.

speaker: Prima
content: I wish I could meet your family in the foreign world! If I could be friends with them... that would be really fun, don't you think?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: My line of work... it's a relentless job that is never done. I'm constantly being pulled into incidents that are either bizarre or dangerous.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But I can't do it alone. It takes the combined efforts of many people to resolve these deadly situations every time.

speaker: Prima
content: No wonder none of this stuff scares you.
Prima appears thoroughly satisfied. Eleanor, however, is looking utterly bored again, kicking pebbles and muttering complaints under her breath.

speaker: Eleanor
content: Why are we the ones telling stories to NPCs now? This whole thing is getting dull. Turns out these "ultra-immersive thrills" they keep advertising get boring real quick. It's always the same predictable tropes. Once you've gotten used to it, you don't feel anything.

speaker: Eleanor
content: And here I thought there'd be some mind-blowing twist or something. Ugh, I'm ready to leave. It's like those haunted houses and escape rooms that just shuffle people in and out for cheap scares. It's so boring, so predictable. Can't they try something original for once? You know, give us special powers or something...

You see. Eleanor is one of those young Eastsiders who are tired of conventional routines and like coming to places like this for a change. But perhaps because your daily life already involves so much real danger, this leisurely experience with its refreshing theatrical tricks has actually been quite relaxing for you.
If it weren't for that strange hourglass and that shadowy figure you saw.

speaker: Prima
content: So, our great adventurer, do you prefer to live life on the edge? Is this not enough to satisfy you?
Prima asks seriously, pretending to extend a microphone toward Eleanor. Taking the cue, Eleanor plants her hands on her hips and responds firmly.

speaker: Eleanor
content: Of course! I paid good money to come here for something exciting I've never seen before! Look, don't take that personally, it's just that I was expecting something more! When I saw the posters, I thought this would be the next Witch Hall!

Prima looks pensive, muttering under her breath as she tries to commit both your and Eleanor's words to memory. This chat will likely end up in her little notebook and become her source of inspiration.
You suddenly wonder what kind of story Prima herself might have. As an NPC, she must have some kind of character profile or backstory, right?

speaker: Prima
content: Me? My story... There's nothing much to tell. Every day is pretty much the same... Hehe, if you're really that curious, next time I could...
Clank!
The sound of bells rings out from the town church as a crimson tinge spreads across the sky. Prima stops in her tracks, staring vacantly up at the night sky.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Prima, what's wrong?

speaker: Prima
content: Peaceful moments are always so fleeting... It's nothing. Let's go.
Prima forces a bright smile and hurries to catch up with you two.
By the time you arrive, torches are already burning in the town square. A heavy gloom blankets the entire town. Fog obscures the moon, while howling winds whip up dust and dead leaves.
Villagers gather before the statue in the square. From the letters you found, you know this statue represents the legendary Witch who protects the town, and this is where the ritual will take place.
Eleanor weaves through the crowd nimbly like a fish, squeezing forward in search of the best spot for the "show," but ultimately fails to advance much.

speaker: Eleanor
content: Mmph... Next comes the most crucial part of the ritual, right? Hmm, there are so many people in front of the statue. Some are even kneeling on the ground...

You squeeze through to Eleanor's side. Nearby, several people who are obviously fellow players hunch excitedly over the glowing screens in their hands, snapping pictures of the statue. How did they manage to smuggle those devices in? There really are rule-breakers everywhere.
The surrounding villagers glare with anger, yet none of them try to intervene.
Prima remains silent, anxiously staring at the statue in the center of the square.
Dong, dong, dong.

Three dull strikes echo from the center of the square, making your head buzz. The sound draws everyone's attention as the crowd instinctively parts beside you. Three figures in gray cloaks lead the way with torches, dragging... someone behind them.
The person's head is covered with a burlap sack. From the clothing, it appears to be an adult woman.
You crane your neck to watch every movement on the platform. Through the gaps in the crowd, you see the woman with the burlap sack over her head kneeling before the Witch statue.
Around her, the cloaked figures behave strangely, first making several bizarre hand gestures, then dipping their fingers into some kind of pigment before drawing mysterious patterns around the woman.
Then, they begin shouting loudly.
It's a language you can't understand, each word seemingly yelled with such force that it threatens to tear their throats apart.
Responding to the cloaked figures' calls, the surrounding villagers begin shouting as well, raising various objects and banging them together in a cacophony of noise.
The chaotic, piercing sounds stab at your eardrums, shaking your heart and clouding your mind with confusion.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Um... Is this also... just acting?
Agitated by the noises, you lean close to Eleanor's ear to ask, but she just stares fixedly at the people on the platform. Is that excitement in her eyes? Or some kind of... fervor?
You turn to look at Prima, but she too is completely entranced by the ritual, her cheeks glowing bright red in the firelight.

As the preparations seem complete, the cloaked figures reveal their faces. One is the mayor, and the other, to your surprise, is the burly Butcher who was in the same room as you earlier! Why would he...
In the moonlight, you see that familiar long ax now in the mayor's hands. The blade gleams icily as he swings it down at the woman kneeling on the platform, her head still covered by the burlap sack.

speaker: Woman with Sack Over Head
content: <color=#dg1f1f><size=24>AH</size> <size=34>AHH</size> <size=44>AHHH!</size></color>
A piercing scream cuts through the chaotic noise, jolting you out of the momentary daze.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Hey!
Why doesn't anyone seem shocked by this horrifying scene? Is this also just part of the game? Are you overreacting because it's your first time?
You stare in disbelief as the villagers and fellow players around you all seem fervently immersed in this horrifyingly realistic ritual.
It's as if you're the abnormal one for not being sucked in by the performance.
But... but... this feeling... something is definitely wrong!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Out of my way!
Your professional instincts take over as you push through the crowd to the front and leap onto the circular platform.

The wound on the woman's body isn't fake, and the blood isn't just makeup! Just as you try to examine her more closely, the woman's corpse suddenly transforms into wax and melts away. You search the entire platform but find no mechanism that could create this kind of "performance."

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: There's no hidden mechanism... It's not magic or hypnosis either... This is...
There's only one explanation for this grotesque scene before you! Something you're all too familiar with... Mania!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Where are the staff? Stop this game immediately!
You shout at the crowd, but no one responds. You turn to the mayor who wielded the ax earlier and grab him by the collar, only to find his expression disturbingly strange.
You see both fervor and numbness in everyone's eyes. They have all been acting strangely since those three loud chimes. Are they hallucinating? And why are they all looking up at something above?

You follow their gazes upward to find the moon, fog-wrapped and hourglass-shaped, which seems to have flipped itself over. Its color appears deeper than you remember, with edges rimmed in an ominous crimson, resembling a half-lidded, bloodshot eye.

The moon hangs lower now, its red light seeping into every crack of the circular platform like raindrops. But instead of emitting the curse-breaking radiance promised in the legend, it turns pitch-black and viscous, reeking of rust and decay.

A tall shadow approaches the mayor. It's the Butcher. He pries your hands open, freeing the mayor from your grip. The mayor stares up at the moon, muttering unintelligibly, though you can clearly sense the fear and disbelief in his voice.
The mayor then staggers forward in despair and collapses to his knees before the Witch statue.

speaker: Mayor
content: The Trial continues... This person... is not the Witch... The ritual... must continue... Hurry, onto the next one...
At the mayor's announcement, the surrounding crowd erupts in loud, disappointed boos.

speaker: Mayor
content: I'll leave the next one to you... I have faith in you...
The mayor presses the ax heavily into the Butcher's palms. The Butcher accepts it solemnly, his eyes growing resolute.

speaker: Butcher
content: ...Leave it to me. This time, I will not fail.
The Butcher hefts the ax in his hand and begins scanning the crowd below, like a predator choosing which prey he will slaughter today.
[Scene with Red Filter]
The blood moon hangs low, engulfing the previously reddish sky in a deep crimson.

speaker: Resident A
content: Not enough... We're running out of time! Kill another one... Kill another one! You? It's you, isn't it!

speaker: Resident B
content: Don't pick me... I'm not the Witch... Please don't kill me...

The crowd grows frenzied under the pressure of the blood moon. Not wanting to be chosen by the Butcher, they push and shove one another. Some try to escape, only to be violently dragged back by others. If this continues, the situation will spiral completely out of control!

Without hesitation, light flashes from your hand. This is the weapon that gives you confidence, which also confirms that Mania has indeed invaded this space right now. You prepare yourself for battle, ready to search for the hidden culprit.
However, the enemy you must face catches you completely off guard.

The villagers who were just shoving each other chaotically now all turn toward you. Numerous pairs of red eyes reflecting the crimson moonlight stare right at you, as if pinning you to the circular ceremony platform.

speaker: Resident A
content: What peculiar sorcery! I know... You must be the Witch!
The Butcher slams his ax heavily onto the ground with a thud, a flash of long-suppressed crimson gleaming in his eyes.

speaker: Butcher
content: Don't move! That light that just appeared in your hand... what is it?

Dozens of hands pin you down. The shackles are useless against ordinary people, and you dare not display your power again recklessly. The gathered villagers whisper among themselves, pointing accusingly at you and the light in your hand.

speaker: Resident A
content: <color=#dg1f1f><i>Oh! It's you. Come to think of it... aren't you the <size=44>strangest</size> one here? Emerging out of nowhere... and even trying to stop our ritual... You must be...<i></color>

speaker: Resident B
content: <color=#dg1f1f><i>The real <size=44>Witch</size>!<i></color>
In the town square, dozens of eyes fix upon you. The predatory atmosphere, like being surrounded by a pack of wolves, sends chills down your spine.

speaker: Mayor
content: <color=#dg1f1f><i>The innocent lamb failed to quell the <size=44>Rewinding Curse</size>, which can only mean... that the <size=44>true impurity</size> remains.<i></color>

speaker: Resident A
content: <color=#dg1f1f><i><size=44>Outsider</size>... I knew it. Things have only started going wrong since you arrived... Kill him!<i></color>
female_content: <color=#dg1f1f><i><size=44>Outsider</size>... I knew it. Things have only started going wrong since you arrived... Kill her!<i></color>

speaker: Resident B
content: <color=#dg1f1f><i>I-I saw it too... He was asking around about things he <size=44>shouldn't</size> know, peeking at things he <size=44>shouldn't</size> see...<i></color>
female_content: <color=#dg1f1f><i>I-I saw it too... She was asking around about things she <size=44>shouldn't</size> know, peeking at things she <size=44>shouldn't</size> see...<i></color>

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Let go... all of you...

Before your eyes, the once-friendly villagers have transformed into aggressors with murderous glares. The players who entered the game with you have lost their minds as well, completely absorbed in this cult-like revelry. Even Eleanor, who was your companion, has joined them with disturbing excitement!
[Sudden Vibration]
Amidst the clamor, you hear an anxious female voice... A warm embrace shields you from the frenzied crowd.
Prima grips your hand tightly.

speaker: Prima
content: Don't worry. Soon, the Witch will be found.
One by one, the girl in white pries away the hands pinning you down. You wonder how someone so delicate could possess such strength.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Ugh!
Suddenly, you lose all your strength and collapse to the ground. She quickly rises to her feet and positions herself between you and the surging crowd.

speaker: Resident A
content: Why... why did he collapse all of a sudden?
female_content: Why... why did she collapse all of a sudden?

speaker: Resident B
content: No... Such a weakling can't possibly be the Witch. This is just a puppet! The real Witch is...

The moonlight and all eyes converge on a single figure. The girl in white slowly releases your hand, rises to her feet, and steps forward, shielding you behind her as she faces the crowd's fear and madness all alone.
A smile shows on her face.

speaker: Prima
content: ...Are you looking for me?
The square instantly falls silent. The crowd doesn't dare to move, seemingly waiting for a command.
Then, a piercing shriek tears through the deathly silence.

speaker: Butcher
content: <color=#dg1f1f><i>Found her!! The <size=44>Witch</size>!! It's her!!!<i></color>
An uproar. A mixture of confusion, fear, and rekindled fervor. They surge toward Prima like a swarm of locusts, seizing her roughly and dragging her toward the circular platform.
What did Prima just do to you? You try to activate your shackles, but some force seems to be suppressing them. Only the triangular mark on the back of your hand emits a faint glow.
The hem of Prima's white dress is stained with the red blood on the ground, but she doesn't seem to care.
[Insert CG]
Unlike the previous silence, the square is now like an ancient clock awoken from its slumber. The moment Prima steps onto the circular platform, black mist surges up and completely envelops her.
The red moon overhead descends slowly, drawing you closer to the end of the "three moonrises and moonsets." The girl lies immobilized on the raised platform.

speaker: Mayor
content: Let the ritual begin!
The mayor suddenly raises his voice, and the townspeople respond in unison. Some with fervent zeal, others with fearful compliance. The sound washes over everything like a crashing tide.

speaker: Resident A
content: For the town! For our peace! Offer the sacrifice! Break the curse!

speaker: Resident B
content: A sacrifice... a sacrifice must be offered! Anyone will do... It doesn't matter who...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Stop!! Let her go!!
You must stop them. This place has now become real, and you don't know if people who die here will also die in reality. This game might end up becoming the next tragic incident!
Once again, you struggle to intervene, but cannot break free from the villagers who have lost all reason.
Under the blood moon, the crowd's madness and Prima's resignation form an eerie tableau.
An invisible force lifts and manipulates Prima's limbs, her body stiffening like a puppet, dark red droplets occasionally seeping from her joints.
Light from an unknown source slices countless wounds across her body, filling the air with something thick and heavy. You know this isn't just makeup. It's the unmistakable smell of real blood.

speaker: Butcher
content: This time... there won't be a mistake!

speaker: Clergyman
content: So this is... the Trial this time...
Eleanor is screaming with excitement nearby.

speaker: Eleanor
content: Wow! What a plot twist! This is so sick!

In the center of the square, atop the circular platform, Prima's gaze toward you suddenly grows meaningful, as if she's looking through you at another presence. Finally, her head gradually droops, leaving you with nothing but a weak smile.

speaker: Prima
content: Thank you for bringing me here. Hearing your story... made me so happy...

speaker: Prima
content: Weren't you curious? This is... my story here...
[Flash briefly: Black and White Sacrifice Small CG]

Thick dark red mist envelops Prima, laden with familiar Mania, yet you're powerless to do anything! You watch helplessly as Prima's figure fades out, everything about her seemingly sucked away, gradually transforming into pure white.
You look up at the crimson moon in the sky. It seems so real, and it's growing larger and closer. This is no prop either. This is the real moon!
You smell the scent of earth, see the real trees, and feel the real wind. When did this place become so real?

The signs of doom haven't vanished. Desperate wails erupt from the crowd. They look both possessed and in utter despair as they begin slaughtering each other to find the Witch. No one pays any attention to you anymore.
Amid screams, flames light up the sky. All you hear are fleeing footsteps and the clashing of farm tools that have turned into weapons.

Eleanor has already vanished in the chaos. The Butcher clutches his ax in disbelief, his hands trembling. The name tag hanging at his waist glows brightly, the characters on it seemingly branded deeper into the surface.

speaker: Butcher
content: <color=#dg1f1f><i>No way... Not <size=44>this one</size> either...<i></color>

speaker: Butcher
content: <color=#dg1f1f><i>Then... who... should be next??<i></color>
In this hellish picture, the last thing you see is the Butcher's bloodshot eyes and his ax swinging toward you...
[Insert effect: Hourglass sand flowing to completion]
[Cycle Reversal Ritual Effect]
[Insert CG - You're Awake - SSR]
In the darkness, a book floats in midair as slender fingers turn the page.
On the page, elegant cursive letters emerge one by one.
The innocent lamb has been offered to darkness and blood. The hourglass of fate is now unstoppable. Congratulations!

speaker: Mysterious Voice
content: The brave Voyager tried to stop the ritual, only to become the next "sacrifice." The ritual failed, and in the end, no one could pass the Trial...

speaker: Mysterious Voice
content: A new hero brings new possibilities... How many cycles remain... How many paths are left...

speaker: Mysterious Voice
content: This "Mania" you speak of... where will it lead fate?
You jolt up from the darkness.
Warm, humid steam fills your nostrils, carrying the scent of wax. You look down at your intact body, then glance around at the peaceful surroundings. You've returned to the hot spring inn.
Recalling the previous chaos sends a chill of dread through your body. What concerns you more is that hourglass. It's definitely not an ordinary prop, but more like... an Aurum Secretum weapon?

Assuming everything was just part of the hyper-realistic immersive experience, you lowered your guard against Mania. You thought everything was exceptionally produced, and the actors were just that good at their roles. Now you realize, none of that was acting, probably since the very beginning!
This is undoubtedly a Mania incident with a Sinner behind it. A-Class? No. With this level of concealment, enough to deceive even you, it must be an S-Class Sinner.
You've dealt with similar situations before and can't just ignore this one. If Mania goes unchecked, everyone here will become victims... You must find a way to leave and alert the MBCC.
The path you came from has been completely sealed off. You search every corner of the inn and find no way to reopen it.
Clearly, you can't get out the way you came. You take a moment to think.

Since you were able to wake up again at the hot spring inn, it means that this extremely realistic fictional world has a functional resurrection mechanism in place. If that's the case, as an NPC, Prima might also respawn at a fixed location.
You leave the hot spring inn and plunge into the darkness of night.
Following the remembered path, you head straight for the place where you first met Prima. As you round the familiar tree, your eyes catch a shadow.
Hey, dude! Guess you've found me!
female_content: Hey there! Guess you've found me!

content: The owner of the voice turns around, revealing an overly cheerful grin, with a familiar long ax resting on his shoulder.
[Flashback: The Butcher attacking you in the previous cycle]

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...It's you?!
The Butcher tries to drape his unbearably heavy arm over your shoulder like you're his best buddy.
female_content: The Butcher unceremoniously pats your shoulder like you've been friends for a long time.

speaker: Butcher
content: Don't run away! I accidentally killed you last time. My mistake, so sorry about that! I've been waiting for you for ages.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Stop. Just stay where you are. Why were you waiting for me? Want to kill me again?
Blood still drips from the Butcher's ax as you warily keep your distance.

speaker: Butcher
content: Oh come on, no need to hold a grudge against me. I understand now. You're not the Witch, just another poor soul trapped here like me.

speaker: Butcher
content: Now that I've confirmed you're safe, I'll protect you from here on. I know how to break this curse. I just also have a <color=#fb9259>mission</color> I can't speak openly about.
He slaps his name tag loudly, as if telling you that everything is under control and to leave it all to him, then immediately waggles his eyebrows at you mysteriously.

speaker: Butcher
content: Shhh... Look over there.
Following his gaze toward the nearby field, you notice what appears to be a human-shaped shadow crouching in the darkness among the overgrown grass.
An attacker? Or some lurking creature?
