content: We don't have anything. My baby hasn't eaten in three days. Try another house.
Before you can get a word out, she begins to shut the door. You react instantly, jamming your hand against it.

Wait, I'm not asking for food. Please. I just need to know if any road to Northsnow Manor is still open. You know Shuang'er, the storyteller in town? She's up there, and she's in real danger. I'm trying to get to her.

The baby in the woman's arms starts crying, its wails thin and reedy. She pats it hurriedly, and as she moves, her sleeve pulls back to reveal a wrist that is nothing but skin and bone. Despite her frailty, she clearly knows Shuang'er.

speaker: Woman
content: Heh... You're one of those people, chasing heroes. My husband was like you. Thought if he learned a few moves, he could be a big hero and protect us all. Then the avalanche hit. He ran right into it to "save people"... When we found him, he was frozen hard as a rock.

speaker: Woman
content: Don't go up to that manor. That "heroism" you're chasing? It's just a fancy word that gets people killed.
The door slams shut with a heavy thud, its echo giving way to muffled sobbing and the baby's feeble cries from within.
[Mountaintop Cliff]
The power of Shen Wanchou's Nine-Turn Yang Pill ebbs away. Jichuan moves to regulate her breathing, only to find a heavy weakness spreading through her limbs and bones.

speaker: Yin Yansheng
content: After three breaths of my Intoxicated Dream Powder, your internal force should be scattered to the winds by now. Hehe... your vitality fades, your spirit dims. Those divine arts are wasted on a dying flame. Why not gift them to this old man instead? Consider it the last worthy deed of your existence!

His long staff quivers, its tip arrowing straight for the Zhangmen pressure point beneath Jichuan's ribs. Gritting her teeth, she forces out every last wisp of her remaining internal force and darts to the right.

speaker: Yin Yansheng
content: Stepping north seals your fate, little manor master. Your next step treads upon empty air!

At his words, Jichuan's left foot quickly recoils, her forward momentum halted mid-motion. It is almost enough. Hampered by her injuries, she is a half-beat too slow, and the long stick finds its mark, slicing a bloody line across her ankle.

speaker: Yin Yansheng
content: Tougher than this old man expected, aren't you? No matter. I'll break you down myself, bone by bone, and drain you dry. You'll make a finer tonic than any pill!

His sleeves whip outward, hurling a massive cloud of dark green poison powder directly at her face! But Jichuan, unexpectedly, does not dodge or retreat. Holding her breath in complete focus, she drives her plum branch straight through the toxic mist!

speaker: Yin Yansheng
content: Still fighting, with death staring you in the face? To become sustenance for my immortal ascent... that's a fortune you should be grateful for!

In his fury, he holds nothing back. His staff technique transforms completely. The dark ebony stick becomes a storm of overlapping shadows, like ravenous spirits clawing for prey, like writhing dragons churning the waters.

Jichuan retreats step by step, snow exploding beneath her feet. New wounds tear across her shoulders, arms, and waist, staining her white robes crimson. Yet her plum branch defense holds firm, and against this storm-like assault, she stubbornly maintains her ground within three feet of the cliff's edge.
Though her body wavers, her spine remains straight.
[Foot of the Mountain]
The door of the third house hangs half-collapsed.

As you approach, about to speak, a faint, putrid smell reaches your nose. Peering inside, you see it: in the corner of the room, on a straw mat, a grayish-blue hand protrudes from beneath a tattered blanket.
Before you can react, an aged, hoarse voice speaks from behind.

speaker: Old Woman
content: That's Old Liu. Froze to death ten days back. Nobody's got the strength left to put him in the ground.
Why?

speaker: Old Woman
content: Look around, child. Who's left in Northwild? Old folks, sick folks, the ones who can't run. The young ones either fled to other parts of Eastia, or got scooped up by those martial arts types with all their flashy talk.
Her gaze drifts to the sword at your waist, and realization fills her eyes.

speaker: Old Woman
content: Ah. You're one of them, aren't you? One of those "martial world" folks. Always yapping about being the strongest, cutting each other down over nothing. You young people... always making trouble, never fixing any.

speaker: Old Woman
content: Just last week, that inn down by the mountain pass? Couple of fighters tore it apart and smashed everything. That family'll be lucky to make it through winter now.

speaker: Old Woman
content: So, what were you gonna ask me, child? ...Hey. Where are you going?
The martial world you long to return to, the truth you seek so desperately—to these people fighting just to survive, they are nothing more than another blizzard to be weathered.

You turn and walk away. The roads after the snow prove far more treacherous than expected. Snow is churned by people and livestock, now a slush of mud and debris, frozen into a filthy, jagged sheet of ice. You slip and fall several times before fighting your way back to your feet.

You finally reach the corner where Shuang'er used to lean against the wall telling stories. It is now only broken walls and crumbling ruins, empty and desolate. The heavy snow falls steadily, inch by inch, erasing every last trace.
[Mountaintop Cliff]

Seeing Yin Yansheng's assault fail, Ji Guining strikes her pipa. The sound waves that erupt are not heard but felt, needles driving directly into the mind, granting no respite. Jichuan is already moving, her dodge calculated. She evades the full force of it, though a thin strand of hair, severed from her temple, marks how close the call truly was.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Three people, one scroll... I find myself wondering... how precisely do you intend to divide it amongst yourselves?

speaker: Ji Guining
content: You needn't trouble yourself over such matters, Miss Jiang. Once you're gone, we'll settle accounts amongst ourselves.

Jichuan twists to dodge once more, but the rock crumbles underfoot. She lurches forward, her heel skidding off the edge as she nearly plummets into the abyss. With a violent jerk, she flings herself back onto solid rock. She looks down in time to see the debris she kicked free vanish into the silent mist.

speaker: Ji Guining
content: Don't deceive yourself. That is a deadly abyss where even birds fall broken-winged. That young friend of yours... by now, is likely nothing but dust and bone.
Jichuan squeezes her eyes shut, forcing her focus inward as she channels the last of her internal force against the demonic sound's assault. Still, the color drains from her face.

speaker: Ji Guining
content: You know, I have always held a certain admiration for you. A body ravaged by affliction, yet you insist on playing the righteous hero. Such a pity that every performance must eventually reach its final act.

speaker: Ji Guining
content: Surrender the secret codex. I can grant you a swift death and send you tumbling down to join him. Compared to falling into Doctor Yin's hands, becoming one of his test subjects, or being tortured by Young Master Shen... this is already an act of considerable mercy. Don't you agree, Manor Master Jiang?
female_content: Surrender the secret codex. I can grant you a swift death and send you tumbling down to join her. Compared to falling into Doctor Yin's hands, becoming one of his test subjects, or being tortured by Young Master Shen... this is already an act of considerable mercy. Don't you agree, Manor Master Jiang?

content: The pipa's sound suddenly surges to a piercing crescendo, like ten thousand ghosts wailing in chorus. Jichuan's face turns deathly pale. Blood trickles from the corner of her mouth, and the plum branch nearly slips from her grasp.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Almost... time...

speaker: Jichuan
content: If I keep taking their attacks, I'll expose a fatal opening within ten moves.

speaker: Jichuan
content: I might as well... take the initiative.
With a flick of her wrist, she releases the scroll of the Snowquell Arts. It sails through the air in a perfect arc, landing precisely in the space between Ji Guining, Shen Wanchou, and Yin Yansheng.

For an instant, all three stand frozen, greed a raw flame in their eyes, before they hurl themselves forward simultaneously! The wind howls and snow swirls as the secret codex tumbles through the air, dancing between their crushing palm strikes and whistling blade shades.

United against an enemy only moments before, they now turn on each other with the fury of sworn foes. Yin Yansheng's poison palm slams into the small of Shen Wanchou's back; Shen Wanchou's fan blade arcs toward Ji Guining's wrist; and Ji Guining, fingers dancing across her strings, sends three sonic blades tearing through the air to find Yin Yansheng's throat.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Fight... seize it... Use those hands stained with innocent blood to claim this scroll... my personally crafted gut-piercing poison...

speaker: Jichuan
content: Use those hearts that schemed against your closest companions... to second-guess each other... How much humanity... can possibly remain...

Yin Yansheng risks his left shoulder to take Shen Wanchou's fan strike. Bone cracks, but in that same instant, his right hand shoots out and seizes the codex. He bursts into wild laughter, though his triumph barely lasts a heartbeat—

Shen Wanchou's folding fan separates again, twelve cold blades raining down like iron hail, blanketing the sky! Yin Yansheng roars, swinging his crutch in a desperate block, but his chest remains wide open. A thin blade, originally meant for Ji Guining, curves back through the air and finds his heart with a wet thud.
The Immortal Healer freezes mid-motion. He stares down at the crimson blooming across his chest, staggers a few steps, and crumples into the snow.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Your enemies... are not merely each other, and not merely me. Down the mountain, vengeful spirits await to collect blood debts. Behind you lurk allies watching like starving tigers... And in your hearts lie insatiable hunger, endless greed, and delusions of immortality...

speaker: Jichuan
content: Like scavenging flies and dogs fighting over carrion, claws and fangs bared in this bitter storm. All claim to know a secret path to heaven... yet it is nothing but another fleeting dream.
Shen Wanchou darts forward, kicking aside Yin Yansheng's still-warm corpse and snatching the codex. A flash of wild joy crosses his face, but behind him, Ji Guining begins to stir in her wheelchair.

Her lameness turns out to be all a ruse! The Princess rises with ghostly swiftness. Before Shen Wanchou can even react, she materializes before him, her fingers already dancing across the pipa's strings.

He evades the sonic blade and tries to curse, but the sound dies in his throat into a wet gurgle. He looks down in dawning horror to find Ji Guining's short sword, hidden beneath the pipa, already buried deep in his neck.
[Foot of the Mountain]

One house, two houses, three houses... You walk through half the town, and every answer is the same: there is no path. There is no hope. No one believes in heroes anymore. Maybe there is still a way to reach the manor, but if people's hearts won't turn toward it, how can such a path ever be opened?

speaker: Child A
content: ...Hello?

A thin, quavering voice, strangely clear, suddenly speaks from beside you. You look down to find a girl in a worn cotton jacket, her small face flushed from the cold. She looks up, and her eyes are bright and sparkling.

speaker: Child A
content: You... wait, you're that young hero! The one who listened to stories with me by the road that day! I remember you! Your sword! Your robe!
The child tugs at the hem of your clothes, her voice quivering with barely contained excitement.

speaker: Child A
content: A real martial arts master! Just like in Shuang'er's stories! The ones who run across rooftops and jump over walls! You're here to help us, right? Tell me you're here to help!
You open your mouth, but your mind goes blank, unable to find the words.

speaker: Child A
content: Then quick, check if I've got it! The hero stuff! Shuang'er says I do, but I... I can't see it at all!

speaker: Child A
content: She says big fists like clay pots and little fists like mine, they all got their own strength! Hiya! Pow pow pow! They can chase away all the bad things and the big scary troubles!
Big fists, little fists... Aren't these the words that old friend of Jichuan's, Mudling, left behind?
What else has Shuang'er told you?

speaker: Child A
content: So much stuff! But my favorite's her own stories. The ones about her in the martial world!
Her own stories?
You kneel beside her. Only now do you see that the child's bulk comes from layers of torn rags and old clothes, a poor padding against the cold. You pull the fabric snug around her small frame.
On the far end of the shackles, Jichuan's life force continues to fade. The decisive battle out in the snow is reaching its end.
I'd really like to hear those. The stories about her. Could you tell me?
[Mountaintop Cliff]
A fountain of crimson erupts from Shen Wanchou's neck. He crumples, his lifeblood pooling with the fallen plum petals on the ground. The scroll lands silently beside his jade-inlaid boots.
At last, the divine arts are in Ji Guining's hands. She seizes the scroll, lifts it high in victory, and tips her head back, her laughter ringing out in triumph.

speaker: Ji Guining
content: Ancestors above, bear witness! The mandate to rebuild, the restoration of my homeland... Heaven has delivered it at last into my hands! Hahaha... This is fate! Honor among heroes? Covenants of the martial world? Before true power, they are nothing but stepping stones beneath my feet!

speaker: Ji Guining
content: Manor Master Jiang, I thank you for your generous gift. Once I have unraveled the mysteries within, I shall see to it that you receive... a most modest grave. Now, let the first soul claimed by the "divine arts" serve as a blood sacrifice to my destiny!
Leaning against the jagged rocks at the cliff's edge, Jichuan is covered in wounds and breathes with difficulty. But at the sight of Ji Guining's triumph, a soft chuckle suddenly escapes her.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Hahaha... How peculiar you all are.

speaker: Jichuan
content: You hunger for power so desperately. You rely on it, trade it for hollow fame, fleeting fortune, the illusion of dominion... yet you understand nothing of what power truly is. You willingly let corruption seep into your very bones, all for the sake of a beautiful mask.
Ji Guining has no patience for the ravings of a defeated foe. With eager hands, her focus narrows to the threads wrapped around the codex, her fingers working to untie the knots.

speaker: Jichuan
content: In such a hurry... but have you forgotten? I mentioned I still have an old score to settle with you...

Before she can finish speaking, Ji Guining tears open the scroll. She doesn't even have a moment to read the script before a churning mass of inky, black energy erupts from it, its tendrils lancing straight toward her eyes.

speaker: Ji Guining
content: Aghh—! What... what is this?!
Each laugh sends pain shooting through her wounds, making it difficult for Jichuan to continue. Gathering what little strength she has left, she slowly rises to her feet.

Snowflakes fall like scattered jade, blotting out the sun and sky. She has only been watching the drama unfold at the cliff's edge for what feels like a moment, but when she stands, she finds herself buried in snow.

speaker: Jichuan
content: I am not like you, no vast networks, no reach across the martial world. I have had a few friends in this life. But there was one person... We made a promise: once we both became accomplished people, we would meet again. I had searched for her for many years.

speaker: Jichuan
content: She was skilled and kind-hearted. By the standards of this martial world, she should have become a renowned hero. Yet I had searched every corner of Northwild and found no trace of her. Guess what I discovered instead?
She brushes the clinging flower petals from her clothes, her smile fading into something cold.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Not long after my friend vanished without a trace, a number of people in the Northwild martial world suddenly displayed exceptional talent. Miraculous encounters, powers soaring overnight. Gradually, these same people carved up the martial world among themselves and became the ones who dictate its rules.

Ji Guining has now collapsed to her knees in the snow. The vile thing from the codex, having devoured her eyes, now rages through her bloodstream. It clashes violently with her internal force, inflicting an agony beyond anything she has ever known.

speaker: Ji Guining
content: My organs burning... meridians boiling... What... what have you done?!
[Foot of the Mountain]

You listen as a child speaks, her voice dripping with innocence, telling you how Shuang'er came to town ten years ago. She presented herself as an associate of the Beggar Clan, disappearing for long stretches, only to return with stories from all over Northwild for everyone. Every location Shuang'er mentioned aligns perfectly with the sects named in the criminal records.

speaker: Child A
content: You wanna know the best part? Shuang'er is amazing. Like, super amazing. She sneaked into every big martial arts place in Northwild! And she brought back these incredible <color=#fb9259>treasures</color>! From all of them! But she's so stingy. She hides 'em all and buries 'em real deep. Won't even let me peek. Not even a little peek...!
Treasures? What kind of treasures?

The child suddenly clamps a hand over your mouth, as if you're about to divulge some earth-shattering secret. Then, with a mysterious air, she grabs your hand and pulls you into a run toward the town entrance.
You follow her all the way to the edge of Ping'an Town, to the barren ground behind the candy shop, where six small mounds of earth sit crooked and askew.

speaker: Child A
content: See? Shuang'er came here lots of times! Took her forever to find 'em all and put 'em here. She said these are super duper important! Like, the most important things ever! And when she finds all of them, she'll figure out... the biggest, deepest secret in the whole entire martial world!

The closer you move, the more distinctly you feel the uneasy tremors radiating from the shackles. Below the surface, a faintly familiar presence stirs... It echoes the feeling you had when you first arrived in Northwild, during the fight at the inn.

Their power is somewhat different from DisCity Sinners... I can't quite put my finger on it, but it feels purer and more unified. Perhaps this is the "internal force" mentioned in the materials you gave me?
The six mounds before you appear randomly scattered, but a closer look reveals a deliberate design: head, torso, limbs. They are arranged to trace the outline of a small human figure.
[Mountaintop Cliff]

Ji Guining crouches on the ground, her hands desperately clamped over her mouth and nose. It is no use; pitch-black branches still force their way through the flesh between her fingers, writhing and twisting outward. Their surfaces are studded with slimy, tumor-like nodes, as if something living has taken root in her very bones and blood.
Jichuan watches her struggle with cold, impassive eyes, slowly raising the broken staff in her hand.

speaker: Jichuan
content: It took considerable time to track down those heroes from years past, one by one. To spread the rumor of a secret codex, and to lure you all here, to this manor.

speaker: Jichuan
content: I went to such lengths because I harbored a faint, almost foolish hope. That perhaps, in this filthy martial world, there might still exist half a person with a conscience. To harm the innocent would betray the very principle of justice my friend and I once swore to uphold. She would surely reproach me for it, from where she now lies.

speaker: Jichuan
content: But it seems the romantic ideals of heroism are, and always were, merely fairy tales for children. Those who believe in "ascension in one step," and those who wear the virtuous mask of a hero while they exploit the desperate... they are cut from the same cloth. For that clarity, I have you all to thank. Through your very presence here, you have dispelled the last of my naivety. It turns out...

speaker: Jichuan
content: Every single one of you deserves to die.

speaker: Jichuan
content: A single blade... can only claim a single life. Can it dismantle the very foundation of this corrupt system? This system that views the weak as nothing more than weeds to be trampled?

speaker: Jichuan
content: What I seek... is never a simple accounting of lives. I intend to tear away the gilded veil from this so-called "heroism," this doctrine of might-makes-right. I want everyone to witness the filth and decay festering beneath the principles you claim to uphold and the power you fight over.
She takes a deep breath.

speaker: Jichuan
content: What I aim to destroy is this unjust order that has plagued Northwild for decades. An order where the Great Seer is made absent, where petty tyrants rule with violence, and the lives of ordinary people are treated as less than nothing!

speaker: Jichuan
content: Today, this manor shall serve as the altar... Your greed, your hypocrisy, the inevitable consequence of your own deeds... they will be the most fitting confession and epitaph.
[Foot of the Mountain]
Next to the earthen mounds, you finally make out the mottled text on the wooden plaque. This is the tombstone of Mudling, and the mounds her scattered graves.
The ink is faded and weathered, but the brushstrokes remain vigorous. Here, preserved in wood, is the true first denunciation—

Manifesto to the World: In years gone by, atop a silent peak where snow forever lies, a young Seer's form was torn asunder, severed before mortal eyes. They sucked the marrow, devoured the flesh, plundered the spiritual meridians, all for their righteous creed. Now I have gathered what remained and found the power in those bones has never truly died. The departed soul, beholding well this body plagued and weak, has bestowed her final breath on me. This breath I now divide in twain. Yang to mend this broken shell, to steel me for the fight. Yin to merge with tainted poison, turning stolen Seer's power back upon its thieving kind. When Yin and Yang shall clash as one, with blood for sacrifice, the divine shall wake. The red plum's last testament is writ, ending only when the snow clears.
[Mountaintop Cliff]

speaker: Jichuan
content: What I demand of you is the blood debt for a child born with a gift. A child who could have grown to be a true hero. A child you... consumed, piece by piece.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Now, you will repay everything you have devoured. The stolen potential, the cultivated power, the ill-gotten reputation, the wealth and status... every last fraction of it, with all the accrued interest. Let it all be returned. Let it fill the wind and snow, let it be a benediction for the living, and a solace for the souls you buried.
[Big CG: Final Battle Long Shot]

Before Jichuan, Ji Guining's body convulses and contorts beyond control. Her spine bulges grotesquely, limbs stretching outward like withered branches. Within moments, the Princess, who once sat dignified in her wheelchair, has transformed completely into a hideous, crouching monster.

Jichuan does not retreat. Plum branch in hand, she taps it gently against the ground as she walks step by step toward the massive, grotesque creature. Her eyes reveal no fear; instead, they shine with compassion and quiet acceptance.

In her days traveling Northwild as Shuang'er, she has seen countless snow-covered vistas, yet none compare to the beauty before her now... Such a pity that this crimson and white splendor will be witnessed by her alone.
[Flashback: Shuang'er asking Xiaofeng to help the Chief before her identity is exposed]

speaker: Jichuan
content: I never imagined... that you would be the one to find me first.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: So you're sending them off yourself, I take it. Got any last words you want me to pass along to that silly boy?
female_content: So you're sending them off yourself, I take it. Got any last words you want me to pass along to that silly girl?

content: Jichuan peered into the storm beyond the dark chamber, her gaze distant. It was as if she were looking past the cold front—the herald of the final slaughter—and through layers of memory to scenes buried deep in the past.

speaker: Jichuan
content: He... was never part of my design.
female_content: She... was never part of my design.

content: She paused, suppressing again and again the chaotic force that coursed through her.

speaker: Jichuan
content: A stranger arrived at Northwild, no background, no known martial arts, no clear purpose. An uncontrollable element, walking uninvited into a scheme I spent years weaving...

speaker: Jichuan
content: When I first approached him as Shuang'er, it was to watch him, to understand what he was. To use his presence as a veil, to observe the others from within the crowd.
female_content: When I first approached her as Shuang'er, it was to watch her, to understand what she was. To use her presence as a veil, to observe the others from within the crowd.

speaker: Jichuan
content: I've encountered far too many people from the martial world. The arrogant ones, who look upon common folk as less than dust. The scheming ones, who measure all things by gain and loss. The righteous ones, whose tongues drip with virtue while their hands reach for the blade behind your back... I assumed he would be no different.
female_content: I've encountered far too many people from the martial world. The arrogant ones, who look upon common folk as less than dust. The scheming ones, who measure all things by gain and loss. The righteous ones, whose tongues drip with virtue while their hands reach for the blade behind your back... I assumed she would be no different.

content: Another surge of darkened blood interrupted her. Wiping the fresh crimson from the corner of her mouth with the back of her hand, she continued to regulate her breathing.

speaker: Jichuan
content: But he told me... that the martial world he believed in wasn't about whose skill was greater. It was a place that could hold sincerity, that could bear ideals worth bleeding for. That even a futile pursuit, fought to the last breath, still had meaning.
female_content: But she told me... that the martial world she believed in wasn't about whose skill was greater. It was a place that could hold sincerity, that could bear ideals worth bleeding for. That even a futile pursuit, fought to the last breath, still had meaning.

speaker: Jichuan
content: He said stories may be illusions, but the impulse behind them is real. Traveling a thousand miles for a single promise. Drawing your blade at the sight of injustice. Loyalty, courage, faith kept at any cost... those things must have lived, somewhere in this vast land.
female_content: She said stories may be illusions, but the impulse behind them is real. Traveling a thousand miles for a single promise. Drawing your blade at the sight of injustice. Loyalty, courage, faith kept at any cost... those things must have lived, somewhere in this vast land.

content: Once more, her gaze sharpened with resolve, fixed on the valley below and the unknown future that lay ahead.

speaker: Jichuan
content: The manor is sealed. No ordinary person can make it down the mountain alive, but you are no ordinary person. Do this for me, Xiaofeng. Wait for him at the bottom. I'll carve him a path. He doesn't need to be part of this slaughter. He only needs to live.
female_content: The manor is sealed. No ordinary person can make it down the mountain alive, but you are no ordinary person. Do this for me, Xiaofeng. Wait for her at the bottom. I'll carve her a path. She doesn't need to be part of this slaughter. She only needs to live.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Let him see for me. Let him speak for me. Let him tell those beyond these peaks how greed devoured itself, how a corrupt legacy burned to ash in a single night.
female_content: Let her see for me. Let her speak for me. Let her tell those beyond these peaks how greed devoured itself, how a corrupt legacy burned to ash in a single night.

speaker: Jichuan
content: The manor will fall. My enemies will fall. And I... will fall. But someone must remain to tell them after... that someone once tried to tear open this iron curtain of wind and snow. And nearly succeeded.
Having said all this, she appeared to have exhausted the last shred of her strength.
Maintaining Shuang'er's innocent and lively facade had drained so much of her, yet now that she was finally on the verge of dropping the act, she found herself reluctant to let it go.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Tell him... to live, and then... don't forget.
female_content: Tell her... to live, and then... don't forget.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Don't forget what?
[End of Flashback]

speaker: Jichuan
content: Don't forget that it was he who showed Shuang'er that there's still warmth left in this world.
female_content: Don't forget that it was she who showed Shuang'er that there's still warmth left in this world.

speaker: Jichuan
content: If one day the stories of heroes and this martial world fade, let it be because peace has come at last. Because no one needs heroes anymore to break the iron rules and right the wrongs.

speaker: Jichuan
content: We have generations ahead. Time enough. And if I cannot live to see that golden peace, then let this flawed, fleeting life of mine be the key that opens the door.

speaker: Jichuan
content: As for the stories after... let him tell them in my place.
female_content: As for the stories after... let her tell them in my place.

content: Her words fade, and Jichuan's eyes grow sharp, freezing the falling snow in mid-air. With the slightest raise of her plum branch, the snow within a hundred feet erupts, a white dragon soaring skyward with a thunderous roar. Beneath this same sky, a newcomer drifts into the town's familiar corner, learning to unfold a new martial world as Shuang'er once did.

speaker: Mountainfoot Storyteller
content: Esteemed audience, lend me your ears! Upon Mount Fuyun, nestled in Northsnow Manor, there dwells a young lady, frail as a willow frond, yet fierce as a winter gale. Her body, delicate enough to be snapped by a sigh, houses a heart blazing with heroic fire. The fragile plum hides a blade, and winter branches dream of spring thunder.
The wind rises. Snow spirals into waves, drawing the scattered plum blossoms into a roaring vortex atop the mountain peak. Jichuan stands at the eye of the storm, her robes billowing wildly.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Point to whole, sever the core!

The monster swings its massive branches down at her, but Jichuan neither dodges nor retreats. Instead, she guides her weapon upward; a snow dragon splits from the vortex and crashes thunderously into the attacking limb. Snow explodes outward as the colossal beast is driven back three feet.

speaker: Mountainfoot Storyteller
content: She poured her soul into the pursuit of heroism, only to find the Northwild martial world—for all their boasts of righteous men and noble deeds—teeming with vipers in heroes' clothing. The so-called "martial world"? A den of deceivers. "Honor"? A silk veil draped over greed. "Justice"? A cudgel to beat the innocent.

The monster flies into a rage and launches Jichuan high into the air with a single blow. Blood mist sprays from her lips, yet she doesn't hesitate for an instant. Spinning her plum branch once more, she peels more snow streams from the vortex. These streams transform into several snow serpents, as thick as pillars, that coil tightly around the monster's limbs and torso.

speaker: Mountainfoot Storyteller
content: Did she flinch? Did she fold? No, the master of Northsnow Manor refused to retreat a single step! If the world is thick with hollow champions, she thought, then let them be unmasked. If corruption has become the custom, then let it be purged. And so she proclaimed a grand feast for all.

The monster shrieks in agony, its cry shaking the snow around them. Jichuan is slammed hard toward the ground, but in the last instant before impact, she twists, plants her plum branch, and springs back to her feet. The blow, however, has been too fierce. The branch cracks in her hand, and her palm becomes a mangled mess of blood and flesh.

speaker: Mountainfoot Storyteller
content: No invitations were sent, yet the rumor spread like wildfire. Those hungry for glory caught the scent and swarmed the mountain paths. Those drunk on silver crawled through snow and sleet to reach her gate. Are there no true heroes left in this world? Then lift your eyes and see: Fists like thunder shake the plum blossoms; staffs like rivers sweep the snow. False idols fall, true hearts rise, and the battle is far from over!

speaker: Jichuan
content: Spirit and will as one, now!

The blizzard vortex collapses inward. Plum blossoms and shards of ice frantically converge on the point where her branch aims. The wind shrieks with a piercing howl, and the falling snow thickens, taking on an eerie blue hue.

Jichuan's face is nearly translucent, blood seeping from the corners of her mouth, each droplet freezing into a crimson pearl against the snow. But her eyes blaze with an unyielding intensity, and her weapon remains a monolith in her steady grasp.

The sounds of the festival below and the warmth of human life have faded from her senses. Yet, in the heart of the storm, it feels as though a thousand untold stories and all forms of warmth merge into a single current, flowing into her wrist.
In this moment, the very wind and snow hold their breath.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Ji Guining...

speaker: Jichuan
content: Your vaunted phoenix bloodline, your dreams of imperial heritage... in the end, nothing but an empty shell hollowed out by greed.

speaker: Jichuan
content: You are no different from the others who came to this manor. In your eyes... there is only taking, never bearing. Only possessing, never responsibility.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Fate has called in its debt. Let me be the one to end your tragedy.
The plum branch thrusts forward! A blade of pure white light carves a straight line through the frozen world, cutting through the swirling wind and snow to spear directly toward the monster's heart.

Then, in an instant, the blizzard converges. It funnels through the wound, a raging flood that scours the monster's flesh from the inside out. Ice crystals burst from its core, and with them, a hail of wood chips and black blood explodes into the air.

speaker: Jichuan
content: This battle of ours will become a legend of Northwild. That pinnacle of the martial world you so desperately sought... your name is finally carved upon it.
The howling wind slowly unravels her hair bun. Through the strands of black silk, her gaze holds a sorrowful compassion as she regards the fallen "hero" before her.

The monster writhes in its death throes, and a thick branch suddenly coils around her waist. Jichuan does not dodge or retreat; instead, she drives her plum branch deeper still. The weapon's broken forks hook into the monster's flesh like barbs, binding her and the massive creature together in an inescapable embrace.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Mudling... did you see? I have become quite the accomplished manor master.
She lifts her head toward the last small patch of clear sky at the storm's eye. With a smile, she closes her eyes and exhales her final breath.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Plum blossoms... on the other shore.
BOOM!!!
A thunderous roar erupts from the peaks of the clouds, splitting the heavens and tearing a massive rift through the heavy overcast.
In the previously silent streets of Ping'an Town, windows creak open as faces appear, one by one. An elderly man, the first to comprehend, raises a trembling hand:

speaker: Old Man
content: The... the peak! Look at the peak!
Atop Mount Fuyun, a visible shockwave erupts from the central manor, thundering outward and blasting a massive spiral void through the heavy clouds and snow that shroud the peak.
No sooner does it pass than muffled, thunder-like aftershocks begin rumbling from deep within the mountain, one rolling into the next in endless succession.

speaker: Woman
content: It... it stopped? The snow... is it lighter now?
The woman steps out, her child cradled protectively in her arms. And as if her words were a command, the years-long blizzard begins to break.

The wind's furious howl drops to a whimper; the frenzied dance of snowflakes slows, thins, and fades. For the first time in years, a fragile silence settles between the earth and sky. All around, doors creak open as people spill into the streets, their faces tilted skyward in awe.
High above, long-forgotten sunlight pierces the torn heart of the cloud spiral, pouring down like a golden waterfall.

It strikes the mountain peak first, setting it ablaze with red and gold, then sweeps down to trace the dark outlines of rooftops, to kiss the snow gathered on every doorstep, and finally, to brush its warmth across the frostbitten, upturned faces of the awestruck crowd.

speaker: Old Woman
content: The heavenly light... it really shone down. This path of heroism... it does exist after all...
At the street corner, you settle into the very spot where Shuang'er once told her tales, a crowd of children gathering around you.
Together, you and the children lift your gaze to the pristine, clear sky, a sky that the hero of your new story secured with her very life.
Hey! Done sightseeing? You're still going up this mountain or what?
A familiar voice calls out from the alley entrance. You turn, and there is Xiaofeng astride her tiger, fresh injuries marking her hands.
How are you...

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: No time for that! I cut through to get here. If we move now, we might still make it in time!
[Mountaintop Cliff]
The manor is unrecognizable now. Beams and pillars give way, corridors lie in ruins, scorch marks and ice fragments are scattered across the devastated courtyards.
The colossal creature that once ruled the mountain peak has long dissolved into the subsiding wind and scattered snow, leaving behind only this utterly broken silence.
The cliff winds spiral relentlessly, and at the vortex's heart, a figure in blood-stained white robes still stands, refusing to fall.

Jichuan props herself up with half a plum branch as blood seeps from wounds across her shoulders, neck, and torso. Her vision blurs, body heat ebbing away with her life force, until only the sound of her weakening heartbeat and the distant, endless wind remains in her ears.
As consciousness drifts, she dimly hears a familiar voice calling—
Jichuan!
[Shackles Effect]
Gathering what little strength remains, she slowly lifts her gaze. Through the bloody haze, she glimpses a figure in sturdy clothing astride a white tiger, racing toward her.

Her eyelashes flutter weakly. She wants to rush forward with joy as she once did as Shuang'er, smiling as she takes your hand, sharing the long-lost legends of the martial world and the secret origins of ancient techniques. But she no longer has the strength.

The moment that crimson spike of light strikes her, the storm she has forced herself to maintain through sheer willpower finally collapses completely. Her gathered strength transforms into chaotic torrents of air that explode outward around her, carrying away even the smile that had barely begun to form on her lips.
You push forward against the violent torrents rushing toward you, but the force violently hurls you backward, sending you crashing into the rubble.
[Manor]
Only when the last whisper of wind finally dies away do you manage to struggle free from the broken tiles. As far as the eye can see, nothing remains but an empty, deathly silence.

You stumble through the rubble. There, half-buried in dust, lies the ornate embroidery of Shen Wanchou's robe. Nearby, you find a pipa, its body shattered beyond recognition, and a walking stick, twisted into a useless shape.
You pass the snow mound where the martial artists were hastily buried. Now, a scattering of crimson petals blankets it in a tender, silent embrace.
Jichuan—
Your voice echoes off the broken walls, then quickly fades away.
Shuang'er—
Still, there is no response.

That final gust of wind has ripped the last of the plum blossoms from the branches. In the ravaged courtyard, the boughs now hold not a single speck of red; the ground below is smothered in a thick carpet of fallen petals.
As you stare up at the naked limbs, a steamed bun sails through the air and smacks you squarely on the head.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Stop wailing. You're hurting my ears.
Perched on the eaves next to a ridge beast, Xiaofeng dangles her legs and casually swings a liquor jar, its contents nearly gone.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: That girl you're looking for... when she sent me down to fetch you, yeah, she did leave a message.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Pfft, what was it again? Something about the martial world, the righteous path... real theatrical stuff, like an opera. Anyway, her last words were way too long. Who the **** can remember all that flowery nonsense!
At the sound of "last words," you waver on your feet, nearly losing your balance.
From the eaves above, Xiaofeng suddenly lets out a laugh and leaps down.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Lucky for you, you've kept a trick up your sleeve. That red thorn thing you shot out... what even was that? Whatever. Long story short, she's still breathing.
She raises her hand, pointing sharply toward the old plum tree at the cliff's edge.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: There, see that? Want to hear her finish that line? Go ask her yourself.
[Cliff]

The snow beneath the plum tree lies in rough, cleared heaps, leaving several large tiger paw prints stamped into the frozen earth. Jichuan sits propped against the tree roots, half-reclining, appearing as if asleep.
Jichuan?
She hears your voice and her eyes flutter open. She is alive. Her pupils, shaped like plum blossoms, are unfocused; they catch the light from the sky, yet remain shrouded, as if in a mist.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Is it... dawn? I can't see clearly anymore.

A thousand questions burn on your tongue. You want to ask if every shared day was part of her scheme, if she hesitated for even a single heartbeat before pushing you from that cliff. But when you finally speak, you don't ask a single one. You simply answer her.
It's dawn. The snow stopped.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Liar... I can still hear the wind.
There is no wind, only the faint, barely perceptible whisper of snow on the verge of melting. You know she won't be able to hear much longer.
It's not wind. It's the plum blossoms falling.
She pauses, a moment of stillness passing before a gentle smile touches her lips.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Then... can you listen for me? What other sounds are there?
You pause, the silence settling between you. Then, slowly, word by word, you paint for her a picture of the sights she will never see again.

Snow's melting off the eaves. Drip, drip... really slow, but steady. Birds are calling from the mountain behind us. Not larks, sparrows, chattering away, probably fighting over the last frozen berries on the branches.
And... children laughing down in the valley. It's far away, but they're definitely laughing.

speaker: Jichuan
content: ...Really?

options: Really. They all know your story now.

content: You whisper to her of the town below—their hopes, their dreams, their unbroken faith in heroes. Her wish has come true; she is now the hero she always wanted to be.
Listening, she seizes your hand with excitement, her own ice-cold and light as feathers. You gently part her fingers and lift her palm to the sky.
Can you feel it? The sun's breaking through.

speaker: Jichuan
content: ...Yes. It's warm.

That mountain across from Mount Fuyun... what's it called? The snow's melting there too. There's a stretch of rock showing at the peak. And the cooking smoke from the valley below... it's gray-blue, rising straight up until it disappears into the clouds.
You speak, sentence by sentence, while she listens with her eyes closed. Her breathing steadies and calms, as if she is on the verge of drifting off to sleep.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Young hero...
...Huh?

speaker: Jichuan
content: The truth is... my illness does have a cure.

speaker: Jichuan
content: The old doctor who took my pulse back then left me a prescription. But the ingredients were too rare... I never could gather them all. Now... I fear it is too late, yet if it is you, there might still be a chance.
She speaks in a rush, as though fearful of running out of time.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Three things are needed: a hundred-year ice lotus core from the snow-capped peaks, which must be plucked before the first light of dawn; crimson flame stone marrow from the depths of southern volcanoes, taken as the lava tide recedes and sealed within a jade box; and also...

speaker: Jichuan
content: Pearls formed from merfolk tears on a night of the full moon in the East Sea, caught while they sing. It must never once touch the earth.

speaker: Jichuan
content: If I could gather them all, this body of mine... might yet linger a while longer in this world.
The shackles clearly relay her true condition: her current vitality is merely the last flicker of warmth before the final fade.
You don't say anything, just watch her quietly. You watch the earnestness she struggles to maintain in those unfocused eyes, and the weakness she can't conceal beneath her pallor.
She mutters quietly, and there is actually a hint of hurt in her voice.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Can you not... pretend to believe me, just this once?
So where exactly do I harvest the ice lotus core? Which ice cave? How long before dawn? Should it be in moonlight or shadow?

speaker: Jichuan
content: The third ice rift on the north side of the main peak, descend a hundred meters to a ledge. It must be gathered between the hours of final darkness and earliest light, when moonlight fades but has not yet surrendered to the sun, and the petals must still be robed in dew—
She stops mid-sentence, her voice trailing into silence. She feels it then: warm droplets landing on the back of her hand, one by one.
A moment later, she musters a smile. It's wan, yet tender.

speaker: Jichuan
content: ...You fool.
She reaches out to wipe the tears from your face, but her hand falls short, her strength giving out.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Never mind. I only ever heard those places were beautiful, and I never had the chance to see them with my own eyes. I thought to trick you into going and looking for me. If you ever pass by there in the days to come, remember to write me a letter... tell me what they look like.
When you get better, we'll go together.
As if her last lingering doubt has finally been put to rest, her whole body goes limp as she settles back against your shoulder.

speaker: Jichuan
content: I'm tired, young hero.
I'll take you back inside.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Not inside... Take me to the window. I wish to see the manor one last time.

Ahead, there is nothing but vast seas of clouds and sheer cliffs, no windows to be found. Her sight has failed her completely. You choose not to correct her, instead guiding her gently toward the light.

speaker: Jichuan
content: ...It's beautiful, is it not? This place where I was born and raised.
Yeah.

speaker: Jichuan
content: The snow upon the eaves... is beginning to melt.
Yeah.

speaker: Jichuan
content: And the plum blossoms in the rear courtyard... they have bloomed fuller than yesterday, have they not?
They have. And the peach trees will bloom soon too.

speaker: Jichuan
content: How wonderful... Spring... has finally come.

Her breathing slows, growing lighter and lighter. You let her rest against you until a faint smile graces her lips, as if she is drifting into a warm dream. Only then do you carry her sleeping form inside, gently covering her with a fur cloak.
The earth is warming, yet her body turns cold. Believing she is only asleep, you tear through the dilapidated manor in search of charcoal.
At the base of the walls, beside the collapsed stove, among the scattered chests... You scour every corner. Clutching two hard-won pieces of charcoal, you finally rush back to the bedside—
The bed is empty now. Only her fur cloak remains, folded into a perfect square. On top of it lie two things:
A withered plum branch and an unsigned letter.
You unfold the letter. The strokes are crooked and wild, the final lines barely legible. The writer has spent her last ounce of strength.
Young hero,

By the time you read this, I fear I will no longer be among the living. Please, do not seek me out. For those who walk the martial world, any green hill can serve as a final resting place. The affairs of the manor have been entrusted to capable hands. The secret codex was never more than an illusion, as greed alone was the true culprit. Within the pages of Chronicles of Northwild on my desk, you will find the full account of the old cases and the brands of those involved. I ask that you make it known.

It was never my wish to deceive you or to make use of your kindness. Circumstances left me no other path. Your sincerity, time and again, broke through the impossible, and for that, I am both deeply shamed and profoundly moved. Our first meeting at the inn, the journey together through the snowy night, the peril we faced in the pine woods, the ascent up the cliff... all these became unexpected light in the dwindling days of my life. I am grateful that you were willing to trust me, one last time.
Yet what I have sought all my life was never vengeance, nor the settling of old grudges, nor the purging of corruption. What I sought can be spoken in four simple words: the world serves all.

Those who inherit power in the martial world ought to protect the common people; those born with extraordinary gifts ought to aid all living beings. This truth is simple, and yet it has been forgotten. I offer my body as kindling, to burn through this wind and snow, not to illuminate my own name, but in the hope that this flame may light the way for those who follow.

Young hero, I know you came seeking the truth of the secret codex. That scroll of blank paper was scattered somewhere during the final battle. I would counsel you to search for it no longer. Though you are not of Northwild, you were willing to draw your sword against injustice. A heart and will such as yours far surpass any divine martial art.

P.S.: If you ever pass by the old wall at the west market below the mountain, would you feed the wild sparrows that gather there for me? Among them, there may be two particularly unruly ones who always quarrel over food. I saved them during my days wandering the martial world as Shuang'er.
Jichuan
P.S.: The plum branch is yours. My mother once said that daughters should be like plum flowers, blooming fragrant even in frost. In my life... do you think I managed to become such a bloom?
At the end of the letter, there is a spot where the ink has blurred from moisture; it is still warm to the touch.

You hold the letter, standing in the empty chamber. Morning light fills the room. In the courtyard, the mist has completely cleared, and above the manor, the vast sky stretches, azure and crystal clear.
[Manor Gate]
Xiaofeng props herself against the stone lion, a grass stem tucked in the corner of her mouth. Spying you, she lifts a single, questioning eyebrow.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Off so soon?

Yeah. Should've left the first time I came down the mountain. Staying this long is already pushing it. Just wish I had more time. I finally got to Eastia, and there are old friends I won't get to see.
Xiaofeng tosses you a coarse cloth bundle. You catch it and find dried rations, a water pouch, and a hand-drawn crude map inside.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: The path down the mountain is clear. Meowy saw to that. Horse at the post station, fresh and sturdy. Call it a thank-you for letting me watch this grand show.
The show's over. Where to now?

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Me? Back to my den on White Tiger Mountain. Gonna loaf around till Eastia kicks up another fuss. Then I'll wander out again.
So you came all the way up the mountain with me just for the fun of it?

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: ...Hard to say. Watching you walk off through the snow, getting smaller... reminded me of this dream I keep having.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Bunch of scrawny kids huddled up in the mountain lord temple, kowtowing to my dusty old statue, crying, "Please, Mountain Lord, open your eyes and help us..." Didn't want you showing up in my dreams too, so, here I am.
You nod. Before leaving, you give Meowy a scratch under the chin.
Probably sounds strange, but I've got a feeling we'll meet again. Not in a dream, though.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Sure, sure. Now go. Keep yapping and it'll be dark again.
She turns and walks toward the deep forest, waving at you over her shoulder without looking back.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Hang onto that wooden branch the beggar girl gave you. It's gonna come in handy.
[Inn]
And sure enough, outside the mid-mountain inn, a chestnut stallion stands tethered to a post, its hooves pawing the ground with impatience.

You have no idea how to ride, but you attempt to mount it anyway. The horse snorts loudly and spins twice, nearly bucking you off. Luckily, it catches the scent of the tiger on you and quickly resigns itself to its fate, plodding along as it carries you down the mountain.
Wind whistles past your ears. Snowy pines blur on either side. The winding road descends, and the view gradually opens up. You see—

Streams flow again with the melting snow, their babbling crisp and bright. On sun-facing slopes, patches of grass appear in mottled hues, tender green scattered through the withered yellow. Where wild plum blossoms have fallen by the roadside, tiny buds swell on the branches.
As you pass through the small town at the mountain's base, you slow your horse to a gentler pace. Children chase one another along the street when one suddenly points at you and calls out.

speaker: Child A
content: Hero! Look, look, the Cold Egg Palms I just learned! Hi-yah! Ha!
Several unfamiliar children gather around, their upturned faces bright, each one with the same sparkling eyes as Shuang'er.

speaker: Child B
content: Mister, did you come from the mountain? Did you see Shuang'er?
female_content: Miss, did you come from the mountain? Did you see Shuang'er?

speaker: Child A
content: Shuang'er said she'd tell us stories about the manor, but she probably forgot again, took her little ratty bag, and went off adventuring. Soon as I'm good enough, I'm gonna chase her down and drag her back!
You gently pat their grubby but hope-filled faces.
You're not wrong. Shuang'er took that ratty old bag, left us all behind, and went off to live free as a bird.

She said she was heading to a place far, far away, a place where martial arts masters go to retire. Sages in the mist, smiling as they take in students, teaching a few moves, then drinking under the moon and swapping stories from the martial world.
The children don't quite understand, but a chorus of "Wow!" erupts from them.

You press your horse forward through a countryside dotted with villages, each one sending up peaceful wisps of cooking smoke. Beneath the eaves, the elderly sit soaking in the sun, their eyes half-closed in a state of quiet contentment.

speaker: Old Woman
content: Good weather we're having. Good for planting.
A soft, warm breeze moves through the wasteland. It's a sensation you never appreciate back in the DisCity, where the air offers no such comfort.
You think what Jichuan did... could it really affect the calamities here?

speaker: Schorl
content: Theoretically, it's unlikely. For a collective will to meaningfully alter calamities, it typically requires ritual frameworks or mediums, similar to Seer practices, to serve as a conduit.

Maybe the conduit was already there? Myths are conduits. Martial arts legends are conduits. Stories, lies... they're like sunlight, like air, anything that gives people hope when they've got nothing left. Maybe that's enough.
You hear the inn server as he slaps down his tea bowl.

speaker: Attendant
content: "Let me tell you the legend of Jichuan, Master of Northsnow Manor, a soul daring enough to dream of mending the world! Witnessing the rot festering within the martial world and tasting the bitter tears of the common folk, she wove herself into the bait, a gleaming lure for the wolves of wickedness. With spirit unbroken and arts divine, she swept through Northwild, purging its tainted breath until, at last, the snows relented and spring, long-exiled, returned to the land of men—"

speaker: Schorl
content: This is the story you had me transmit to DisCity for Yugu to refine.

speaker: Chief
content: This is a story of Eastia's Northwild. Let it stay here. We won't be back for a long time.
The story has begun to spread. Through word of mouth, truth and legend interweave, taking on vibrant new life.

Soon, new children will sit at street corners, raised on these tales, and seeds of heroism will be planted alongside them. Perhaps one day, some among them truly become Sinners who shield their land through acts of benevolence, or even... new Seers.
The flame of heroism burns eternal, and the martial world endures forever.
[Grassland]

You finally learn to control your horse, gently squeezing its flanks as the steed breaks into a full gallop toward the brightening dawn. Wind billows your robes, and the letter tucked against your chest rustles with each stride.
Something suddenly comes to mind, and you turn back to look in the direction of Northsnow Manor—

The manor's ruins stand quietly on the mountain peak, bathed in golden light. And in a corner where no one pays attention, that scroll, once the spark for countless greedy conflicts, hangs unrolled from the branches of the plum tree on the cliff's edge.
Mountain wind brushes past, causing the scroll to sway gently. Its surface is completely blank, revealing no martial techniques, no secrets.
Only at the very end, a line of childish, crooked handwriting appears. As if, many years ago, two children huddled at a candy shop entrance, scribbled down a promise with a charcoal pencil.
"Pinky promise, cross my heart, hope to die if I ever lie—"
"You'll be an amazing manor master, and I'll be an amazing hero!"
"We'll ride across the world together, swords in hand, to the very ends of the earth!"
Beside the words, in the blank space of the paper, a crudely sketched little bird sits near a small flower with five petals, forever frozen in time.
[Horseback Riding CG]
Night falls on Northsnow Manor. Heavy snow blankets the roof tiles, and an eerie silence descends upon the land. The strange murder from earlier that day casts a sinister pall over the vast estate.
Amidst the treetops, a slender figure, virtually indistinguishable from the shadows, watches in perfect stillness. Her deep gray eyes survey this wind-whipped, snow-bound "cage" with keen interest.
Snow buries the dead, wind masks the reek of blood... Tsk, this manor's got more secrets than a locked chest.

A <color=#fb9259>secret martial arts codex</color> pops up, causing such a grand commotion, and they don't even send this old granny an invitation? These youngsters today... Where are their manners? Their foresight? Tsk, tsk, tsk.
From the shadows, a girl in light foreign clothing emerges, drifting toward the manor's high walls like a wisp of night mist.
Thud!

An invisible force, thick as a mountain, erupts without warning, slamming into the exact spot where she is about to land. With a muffled grunt, the girl crumples, her slender form flying backward like a kite with a severed string before she lands softly in the snow several yards away.

speaker: Girl
content: Well, well... what a watchdog. Vicious thing, aren't you?

She wipes the blood from the corner of her mouth and brushes off her spotless sleeves. On the exposed parts of her arms, eerie purple-blue markings seem to have crept higher. Something beneath her skin writhes restlessly, as if struggling to burst free.

speaker: Girl
content: ...This granny's clock is ticking. Can't be swapping punches with some watchdog. I've got places to be.

The biting cold is irrelevant. She sits down in the snow, commanding the strange stirrings in her body to settle. A frontal assault would be foolish. She has neither the time nor the need for such crudeness.

Then, the girl produces an array of bottles and jars as if from thin air, arranging them neatly before her. The moment she unscrews one, a spine-tingling chorus erupts: a symphony of tiny, skittering sounds.

speaker: Girl
content: Shush now, my darlings, shush. Everyone gets a turn. If anything goes wrong, you'll each have your moment to shine.

She pricks her fingertip with a golden needle, and from the wound seeps an eerie, toxic fluid. Several small insects eagerly scramble up the jar's rim, extending their mouthparts to drink this vital sustenance.

speaker: Girl
content: Everyone calls me <color=#fb9259>Granny Goldspider</color>. Idiots. They see the gold and think that's all there is. Bless their hearts... if they only knew the variety my little darlings come in.

The girl giggles softly. Once all her little darlings have eaten their fill, she keeps one cradled in her palm. It is a silver-white spider, with limbs streaked in purple-blue and a disturbing, human-like face emblazoned across its back.

speaker: Girl
content: You're up. Go on, take a peek for this old granny. See what heroes have graced this party with their presence. Find me a strong one. Someone... accommodating.

speaker: Girl
content: And that codex, my dear, sniff it out. If those fancy techniques can actually fix this <color=#fb9259>condition</color> of mine, you and your siblings will feast like royalty. Granny promises.

Her cupped hand drifts down, opening gently against the ground. The little spider called Number One blinks once with its gleaming compound eyes, and upon touching the snow, it dissolves instantly into the night.
The little creature moves with nimble precision, scaling the high walls in moments and slipping into the manor. This time, it evades the notice of whatever hidden masters lurk within.

speaker: Girl
content: That's my clever one!

A faint glow emanates from the eerie markings on the girl's body. She closes her eyes, and before her, a different world unfolds. She now views the manor's interior from the low, scuttling perspective of the spider.
[Manor Corridor - Night]

speaker: Spider Number One
content: Doors shut tight, lights out, holding their breath like mice... Think you can fool this granny by playing dead?
The little spider slips into the first guest room, yet when it sees the two people inside, its demeanor shifts to one of disappointment.

speaker: Spider Number One
content: Oh. One of them's actually asleep.

speaker: Spider Number One
content: This little one in gray, scrawny thing... Probably can't handle a nibble. That girl beside...? Tsk, beanpole with no meat.

speaker: Spider Number One
content: Sigh. Gotta find myself one of those martial artists. Sturdy build, and plenty of cunning... moving into a shell like that, now that's what I call comfort.

The tiny spider slips through the crack beneath the door. The two people sleeping soundly inside do not know that their slight frames hold no interest for the creature, and so, unknowingly, they are passed over, escaping a hidden disaster.

speaker: Spider Number One
content: Right then. Two bland dishes, passed. Next course... don't you dare disappoint your granny.
In the darkness, the small spider pauses briefly before crawling, without hesitation, deeper into the estate. It makes its way toward the other guest rooms, drawn by the more complex auras within.

The successive deaths of her little spiders leave the girl furious. In the darkness, a single spider paces back and forth on agitated legs, even angrily shooting silk at innocent insects in the corners to vent her frustration.

speaker: Spider Number Six
content: Did I forget to check the fortune before stepping out yesterday? What's with this god-awful luck? Is this damn manor personally cursed to spite me?!

speaker: Spider Number Six
content: Crazy ones! Dead ones! Sly foxes! Filthy beasts! And a big cat who thinks spiders are playthings! Not a single decent "host" to be found! Haven't even caught a whiff of that codex, and my precious darlings are nearly all dead!
She rants irritably at the empty air, mentally marking each guest in the manor with a blood-red X. Finally, the faces of those first two pathetically weak targets reluctantly surface in her mind.

speaker: Spider Number Six
content: Fine! Fine! No choice left, is there? This granny will swallow her pride and go back to those two scrawny beanpoles! Weak as dishwater, but... better than nothing, I suppose!
She's just gathering herself to hunt for her next target when muffled sounds erupt from the silence: the thud of a struggle, the rasp of something being dragged.

speaker: Spider Number Six
content: Now what?! Is there no end to this?! Who's so blind they'd pick this moment to make trouble when Granny's already fit to burst?!
Rage burning within her, she resolves to investigate. She will sacrifice this body if it means making whoever dared to cross her pay.
Huffing with indignation, the little spider crawls and swings through her webs, racing toward the sound. As she rounds the corridor corner, a chilling scene fills its compound eyes—

speaker: Spider Number Six
content: That's... one of last night's beanpoles?!

The beanpole she just mentioned is being dragged into the darkness. A shadowy figure has a hand clamped firmly over her mouth and nose. She realizes in a flash: this beanpole is with that little one in gray!

speaker: Spider Number Six
content: Oh no, no, no! If one's in trouble, the other's in danger too! Where's that little one? Still kicking around?!
The little spider abandons all stealth, changes direction, and scurries toward the guest room at top speed.
Splat—
The legendary drift master barely rounds the corner, preparing for her grand entrance, when an elegant, thick-soled cotton boot slams down upon her.

speaker: Spider Number Seven
content: Heh... Good. Real good. You think this granny doesn't keep spares?

Having already lost so many of her tiny soldiers, she has wisely pre-positioned several backup units inside. The instant Number Six's world goes dark, her consciousness seamlessly links with another. In that same moment, Number Seven activates and takes over without hesitation.

After a lightning-fast crawl, Number Seven slides into position at the guest room entrance. It is now deserted, marked only by scattered drops of blood and Number Six's crushed remains lying in an inconspicuous corner.

She squeezes through the crack in the door and surveys her new domain. The room is empty save for the little one in gray on the bed. With a pale face, the kid seems to be anxiously awaiting the other companion's return, completely unaware of her presence.

speaker: Spider Number Seven
content: Can you even take it, little one? Look at you, paler than a ghost, weaker than last time. You're not gonna croak the moment this granny moves in, are you? How embarrassing that'd be.
The little spider approaches her target, studying the person intently; only once she has confirmed the target is unharmed does she feel at ease.

speaker: Spider Number Seven
content: Ahh, so that's it. Still got some poison clinging to you, poor little one. Neutralized, but your internal energy's a wreck... No wonder you look like yesterday's laundry.

speaker: Spider Number Seven
content: Well. No choice now. Don't blame this old granny. If you want someone to blame, blame the rest of this manor for being utterly useless...

speaker: Spider Number Seven
content: Is this what they call "kicking someone while they're down"? Heheheheh...
With no time to feel even a trace of shame for striking when her target is down, the little spider scrambles onto the bed and zeroes in on the exposed section of wrist—
[Release the shackles]
Clang!
A blinding red light erupts from the person's hand, cutting through the darkness and locking the little spider's body in place.

Her fangs do not meet the expected yield of flesh and blood. Instead, they bite down on what feels like thorn-covered brambles. An indescribable, strange power, thick with an imprisoning force, surges violently through them and into the little spider's form!
It violently repels the spider's intrusion, its vicious energy burning back through their mental link and searing the consciousness of the girl who controls the creature.

speaker: Spider Number Seven
content: What in the—?! What is this thing?!
The sudden flash of light startles the target, giving the little spider the chance to hide inside the person's clothing and wait for the next opportunity to strike...
At the base of the cliff below Northsnow Manor, falling snow silently buries the evidence of a recent plummet.
Xiaofeng, bored with guarding the unconscious person, catches a whiff of liquor and abandons her post for the nearby inn.
In that unguarded moment, a girl in deep purple embroidered shoes, adorned with silver bells, picks her way through the snow. She bends to scrutinize the figure lying there.
The person's pale lips and tightly shut eyes speak of a body still reeling from the fall.

Gently, she brushes the accumulating snow from the person's head and body. As she does, she uncovers a small spider clinging to the unconscious one's neck, its delicate legs twitching faintly. It lies barely alive, its body nearly snow-white except for the dark purple markings on its legs.

speaker: Girl
content: Oh, my precious little Seven. Look at you, all battered and bruised. Granny's heart can't take it.
The girl crouches, her fingertips stroking the little spider with tenderness. She pricks her own finger, coaxing forth a bead of blood that glows with an eerie, poisonous color.
The spider drinks, and an unearthly luminescence washes over its tiny body. It trembles back to life, nuzzling affectionately against her skin.

speaker: Girl
content: ...If it weren't for that funny power this little one's got, would this granny be out here tramping through this frozen wasteland, meddling in other folks' business? Leaving that secret codex just lying around?
After feeding the little spider, the girl's gaze drifts to the unconscious person's face. Her fingertips then hover, cautious and hesitant, just above the wrist, never quite making contact.

speaker: Girl
content: Oh ho? Tough little cookie, aren't you? Still breathing. And this face... even prettier up close.

speaker: Girl
content: Last night, when those funny spikes from your body gave me such a shock, my own aches and pains settled right down afterward. What sort of power is that...?
She braces herself for the blow as she speaks. Barely able to contain her excitement and anticipation, she quickly grabs the other's wrist.
But nothing happens. Just silence. The red light she was waiting for never comes.

speaker: Girl
content: Well now. That's odd. Not even a flicker? It was so lively last night. What, tired itself out already?

speaker: Girl
content: Body too weak to wake it up? Or maybe... not enough stimulation? Do I need to... take a little nibble?
Her grip shifts to a pulse-point check. The beat is there, but faint. She probes several key points on the body, yet detects no echo of that mysterious energy.

In the falling snow, the unconscious person's eyelashes tremble, scattering tiny, crystalline flakes. His eyes slit open, though consciousness remains out of reach. Through the swirling snow mist, all he perceives is the vague, blurred silhouette of a girl.
female_content: In the falling snow, the unconscious person's eyelashes tremble, scattering tiny, crystalline flakes. Her eyes slit open, though consciousness remains out of reach. Through the swirling snow mist, all she perceives is the vague, blurred silhouette of a girl.

content: ...Who... are you?

A hoarse voice squeezes from his throat. The girl, seeing he's awake, tries to activate her power again, but the spikes from last night remain stubbornly inert. The effort, however, nearly knocks the barely conscious young man out cold again.
female_content: A hoarse voice squeezes from her throat. The girl, seeing she's awake, tries to activate her power again, but the spikes from last night remain stubbornly inert. The effort, however, nearly knocks the barely conscious young woman out cold again.

speaker: Girl
content: Sigh, was last night just a fluke?
Her probing yields nothing. The girl shakes her head, disappointment evident as impatience creeps into her voice.

speaker: Girl
content: Just call me <color=#fb9259>Granny</color>. Look at you, head full of cotton, can't remember your own name, probably. What's the point of explaining?
He wants to ask more questions, but the dizziness from his fall leaves him too weak to speak. Instead, he can only manage to slowly raise his hand and reach forward.
female_content: She wants to ask more questions, but the dizziness from her fall leaves her too weak to speak. Instead, she can only manage to slowly raise her hand and reach forward.

speaker: Girl
content: Don't bother with thanks. Granny just brushed some snow off. If you'd gone and kicked the bucket here, all my running around this godforsaken manor all day would've been for nothing!

speaker: Girl
content: That codex those "heroes" are tearing each other apart over? It's a death trap, plain and simple. And that little girl by your side? Sharp as a blade, that one.

speaker: Girl
content: But all that... you'll find out soon enough.
Before the girl can finish her explanation, the poor soul—who had scarcely opened eyes moments ago only to endure her test—finally succumbs and lets the eyelids fall shut.

speaker: Girl
content: Asleep again? Fine, fine. You owe Granny one now. Next time... I'll come find you to collect.

speaker: Girl
content: <color=#fb9259>When that time comes... don't you dare disappoint me.</color>
Several days later, Northsnow Manor stands completely abandoned, a place of particularly desolate emptiness.

At the foot of the mountain, the inn still hums with tales concerning the fate of the martial artists who recently gathered. The girl tosses some loose change onto the counter and selects a tabloid to pass the time.

——Martial World Monthly - Special Edition——
"Northsnow Manor Treasure Heist Mystery: 
Secret Codex Lost, Heroes' Fates Revealed"

The pages introduce the martial artists who attended the gathering and depict the gruesome scenes of several deaths. The mysterious manor master's fate and whereabouts remain unknown, and the secret martial arts codex has vanished without a trace. Whispers suggest some unknown Eastian hero made off with it.

speaker: Girl
content: Tsk tsk. And they call this journalism? A steaming pile of week-old leftovers, this is. Same old names, same old rumors, not a single interesting bone in this whole sorry carcass of a paper.

speaker: Girl
content: All this fuss over some secret codex is just people scheming and backstabbing for profit. And these so-called heroes are all shine and no substance, like polished chamber pots. Look respectable enough until you get a whiff of what's really inside.
Pen in hand, she dives into the gossip article, making corrections throughout before adding two punchy lines of commentary in bold, dramatic strokes.

Looking around with a furrowed brow, she's still not pleased. She carelessly sketches a few doodles, then decisively crosses out the original headline and pens a new one. Finally satisfied, she sets the pen down.
She drains her tea in one gulp, strides over to the storyteller, and nonchalantly drops the scribbled-on tabloid in front of him. Under the stunned gaze of the onlookers, she makes her grand exit.

speaker: Girl
content: You want news? That rag you're peddling is already moldy. Granny's giving you something... fresh off the press. Still warm.

The storyteller picks up the tabloid in astonishment. Beside the names of the martial artists, she has scrawled various nicknames, and scrawled above them, in a crooked hand, is the title: <color=#fb9259>"Silent Snow, Hidden Plum"</color>.

Delightful Forest Master loved his wine and meat,
till one day he gorged and burst, a gut-spilling feat.
The Gentleman's silver needles gleamed in snow,
yet dread kept him wakeful, fear would not let go.
General Invincible, renowned in war,
met her end by ten thousand arrows and more.
Melodious Pipa smiled, her tune so sweet,
while a blood-soaked blade hid beneath her wood sleeve.
Immortal Healer hung out his shingle with pride,
yet the feared ghosts would come knocking inside.
Golden Brocade, the ever-smiling guest,
wrings tears from flesh and bone, turns sorrow into gold.

Thus it is said: <color=#fb9259>Heroic skin wraps vicious bone;
the stage performs in ghostly tone.
Withered plum reveals old crime;
Death severs guilt in time.</color>

In the blank spaces of the tabloid, nestled among carelessly scribbled doodles, a little beggar holding winter plum blossoms and a gray-clothed hero gripping a sword hilt are drawn. In the bottom right corner of the sketch sits her signature: a tiny spider.
(Scene change)
[Street]
The sky has cleared, the snow no longer bites quite so sharply, and the streets at the foot of the mountain hum with a life they lacked just days ago.

Outside the inn, Ayiguo stretches her stiff limbs. Passersby stare at her bizarre outfit—bare arms and legs in the dead of winter—casting strange looks her way. Far from being bothered, she lifts her chin in confidence, presenting herself for their admiration.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Ahhh, the weather's warming up. Time for my little darlings to wake up and smell the sun.

A few small spiders peek out from her sleeves. This batch is noticeably smaller than her previous ones. After all, she has lost quite a number. These new little darlings will need considerable time to grow.

Suddenly, Ayiguo senses something. She focuses intently and closes her eyes as Number Seven's perspective syncs with hers. Before her eyes, a patch of green grassland spreads; the little spider is perched on that person, moving toward the promise of spring.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Well, well. Look who's up and about. You've healed nicely, little one. Heading somewhere interesting, are we? Not Eastian... No, no. An outlander, then?

Her connection to the little spider grows spotty, catching only fragments of words like <color=#fb9259>"DisCity"</color> and <color=#fb9259>"Chief."</color> As the distance between them increases, Ayiguo can still sense Number Seven's location, but she can no longer eavesdrop or spy on anything of substance.
