Norma leaves. In her wake, a thin rift splits the sky. That dark figure, the one that once lurked behind her, gathers itself again, moving to strike at the order she just brought to this space...
Rules... interesting... I will make sure you never return...
The static on the other end pauses for a moment, as if at last confirming the signal has successfully gone through.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief! Thank goodness... we finally got through... Are you alright?

speaker: Nightingale
content: The signal... isn't stable. I'll keep this brief.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Actually... you've been inside the Bureau this whole time.
The moment she says this, the entire team falls silent.

speaker: EMP
content: Wait, we're WHERE?!

speaker: Murphy
content: The... the Bureau?

Everyone there is stunned into silence. But you aren't particularly surprised. That elusive sense of familiarity has been surfacing over and over since earlier. It simply hasn't been clearly confirmed until this moment.

Three Hours Ago
Inside the MBCC Ring Substance Laboratory

speaker: Researcher
content: Beginning collision experiment number eleven.

speaker: Researcher
content: Loading Ring substance.

speaker: Researcher
content: Confirmed.
Stabilizer output normal.
Collider ring preheating complete. Ramping field strength.
Sample R-07. Preparing for injection.
Polarization orbit deployed. Transfer arm calibrating.
Parameters locked. Three, two, one. Contact.
[Screen Shakes]

speaker: Researcher
content: What's going on?! Why is the field strength spiking?!

speaker: Researcher
content: Wait, the readings are off! The containment ring is destabilizing!

speaker: Researcher
content: Cut the transfer! Cut it now!

speaker: Researcher
content: Too late. The sample's breaking apart—

speaker: Alarm
content: Warning. Core parameters exceeded safety threshold.

speaker: Alarm
content: Collider ring structural integrity compromised.

speaker: Researcher
content: The experiment failed! M-values are completely uncontrollable! Not unless we can find a replacement sample!
Mania tore through the experiment center like a high-pressure valve ripped violently open, erupting beyond all containment.
But the truth was, the real loss of control had begun long before that moment.
Murphy's runaway car slammed into the Bureau's outer wall. The coin slipped from your grasp and rolled free. The brutal impact jolted open a maintenance hatch that had never been properly secured.
Behind that hatch, the backup circuits were yanked loose, their connections severed in an instant. The identification module responsible for routing samples hiccupped, triggering an error command.
The coin rolled clean through the hatch, gliding unimpeded all the way to the transfer track of the 11th collision experiment.

And at that same moment, the calibration arm, rattled by the cascading vibrations, drifted off by a few millimeters. The Mania field that should have already torn loose was delayed—by just a handful of seconds.

speaker: Researcher
content: Wait... What is that?!
And it was precisely those few seconds that sent the coin bouncing right into the ring collider.
Immediately after, a pink miasma spread along the underground facility, engulfing the entire Bureau in the blink of an eye.
(Back to present)

speaker: Nightingale
content: The Mania field is severely disrupting your perception and cognition. It's warping and restructuring the Bureau's internal layout, projecting it as the world you're seeing now.

speaker: Nightingale
content: The castle, the forest... everything around you essentially corresponds to different sections of the Bureau's underground facility.

speaker: Letta
content: Hehe... well, that just makes it even more interesting.

speaker: EMP
content: ...So we're basically people wandering around with VR headsets on, and everyone who didn't get caught up in the Mania is just watching us look like total idiots!

options: Don't worry, no one has time to laugh at you right now.

speaker: Nightingale
content: The Ring Research Institute has preliminarily confirmed that this abnormal expansion of the Mania field is linked to the influence of Sinner Murphy.
Murphy's shoulders suddenly tense up.

speaker: Nightingale
content: More precisely, the anomalous concept of her ability interfered with the Mania field. It warped what would have been a far more lethal, purer form of contamination into its current state.

speaker: Murphy
content: Phew...Oh man, I was so scared. So... so you're saying the Mania that would've driven people insane, mutated them, or just... stopped their hearts? And now the worst it does is make people get chased by coin banks and slapped in the face by slimes?
Hearing the conclusion, Murphy lets out a long sigh of relief.

speaker: Murphy
content: So that means... I actually saved everyone? That counts as doing something good, right? Hehe.

speaker: Nightingale
content: The tradeoff, however, is that the Mania field's rate of spread has also been amplified.

speaker: Nightingale
content: If left unchecked, this Mania field, with its severe cognitive distortion, risks spreading across the entire DisCity. Given enough time, all of DisCity will be shrouded in illusion.

speaker: Murphy
content: Huh...? No way... I knew it...
Murphy's brief flash of relief lasts barely two minutes before she wilts once more, like a flower starved of sunlight.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: All of DisCity?

speaker: Nightingale
content: Yes. We need to act quickly to eliminate the substance that allowed Sinner Murphy to interfere with the Mania field in the first place.
From Nightingale's end comes the crisp sound of tapping, punctuated by the rustle of turning pages, as though she is carefully cross-referencing the latest intelligence that has just come in.

options: Can you send Sinner reinforcements to the Bureau underground?

content: Nightingale goes quiet, unusually so.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Due to the Mania field's unusual properties, we can't directly intervene with it from above ground. The most we can do is slow its rate of expansion.

speaker: Nightingale
content: You'll need to locate that unstable experimental substance and neutralize its effects.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Once that's done, the Ring Research Institute will immediately attempt to recalibrate and restore the entire Mania field through an external experiment.

speaker: EMP
content: So basically, we've gotta keep pushing forward on our own.
Right. The Mania field is too disrupted right now. For the time being, we can only rely on our own strength.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Correct.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Additionally, Chief, please be aware. Mania entities still exist within the Bureau. They don't currently pose a significant threat.

speaker: Nightingale
content: However, we can't yet determine whether their threat level will escalate over time.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I see.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Also—
She seems poised to add something more, but the transmission suddenly warps beyond recognition with a surge of static swallowing her voice whole.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Murphy is... one of the key factors... but she's also... the most susceptible...

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief... you must...
The transmission cuts out, and all that remains is the hollow echo of static drifting through the empty corridor.
As everyone takes in the underground structure before them once more, it feels irrevocably changed.

The rough-hewn stone walls now seem to reveal the ghostly outlines of metal supports lurking just beneath their surface. EMP runs a hand along the stone and mutters that it's a good thing she held back earlier; otherwise, she'd definitely be on the hook for helping with the Bureau's repairs.

speaker: Murphy
content: ...I'm so embarrassed. Sniff... I came here to turn myself in at the Bureau, and now I've made this huge mess! Murphy, how could you?!
Beside you, Murphy sinks deeper into her own bitter thoughts, until at last she simply surrenders, dropping to the ground in a heap of defeat.

speaker: EMP
content: Hey, look on the bright side. Just think of it as, y'know, step one of turning yourself in.

speaker: Murphy
content: But at least the goal's clear now... We need to keep going deeper, right?
At those words, her fingers curl into tight fists, and she turns her gaze toward everyone.

speaker: Murphy
content: ...Or maybe... you should just leave me here.

speaker: Murphy
content: It's confirmed now. The Mania turned out like this because of me. And we're gonna keep running into dangerous stuff like that giant coin bank...

speaker: Murphy
content: If I keep following you guys, I'm just gonna make everything worse and drag down your combat strength.

speaker: Murphy
content: You were supposed to be dealing with the Mania, but instead you're stuck dragging around someone like me who just makes everything harder for everyone...
She trails off, her voice dropping to a murmur.

speaker: EMP
content: Okay, putting everything else aside—if you hadn't crashed into—uh, tripped and taken out that giant coin bank, we'd still be running from it right now.

speaker: Lynn
content: Yeah... But I'll admit, that final moment was... a bit unexpected.

speaker: Murphy
content: That-that was just me being unlucky again. That's all...

speaker: EMP
content: Turning bad luck into something useful? That's a talent! Just like how I clawed my way to the top of Syndicate through cheating and trickery!

speaker: Letta
content: You get scared, you cause trouble, but when things get dangerous, you still charge forward anyway... Isn't that what a friend does?

speaker: Lynn
content: R-right! How could we just leave you behind all alone? I couldn't... I-I couldn't do that...

speaker: Lynn
content: And I mistook you for someone else before! Here, this is a photo I took just now. It's yours! Think of it as a memento of... um, our f-first time becoming friends! Is that okay...?
They speak up one by one, as if they are talking about something perfectly ordinary.
Murphy stares at them, dazed, listening to every single word. It takes a long, suspended moment before she can finally accept that she didn't mishear.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The Bureau handles incidents by resolving them, not by punishing Sinners. If there's anything that needs to be said, we'll talk about it in the interrogation room once we're out of here.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're way more useful sticking with the team than wandering off on your own.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Besides... everyone here is your friend now.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Me too.
At your words, a smile finally finds its way to her face.

speaker: Murphy
content: Haha... You're all seriously weird, you know that?

speaker: EMP
content: Hehe, thanks for the compliment!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No one was complimenting you.

speaker: EMP
content: I'll take it anyway.
The tension eases at last. You cast your gaze deeper into the underground city, where that pink haze still roils and churns.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Let's get ready to move.
But now, you all know why you have to press forward—not just to clear some bizarre dungeon, but to restore the Bureau to the way it was.

speaker: EMP
content: Copy that.

speaker: Letta
content: Okay!

speaker: Lynn
content: I'll scout ahead with everything I've got!
This time, Murphy doesn't hesitate. She breaks into a light run to catch up.

speaker: Murphy
content: If this could be my everyday life... that wouldn't be so bad.
Unfortunately, she's still quite slow.

speaker: Murphy
content: Wait for me!
But what she fails to notice is that, as she dashes forward, a shadowy figure identical to her is running off in the opposite direction.
It's you... Of all people, you again...
[Scene Change: Office]
Bad luck has shadowed Murphy from the moment she entered this world. It's just her everyday reality.
In the beginning, it wasn't the catastrophic kind of disaster. More often, it's just the smallest, most ridiculous little accidents, the kind you'd feel silly even bringing up.
But somehow, they always, always picked her.
Murphy stares at the files scattered over her desk, a couple of unopened snack bags, and that familiar phone sitting right there.
Wait... is she back? Just as the celebration is about to begin in her head, a voice cuts through the air and reaches her.
Murphy, where are the materials you prepared?

speaker: Murphy
content: Oh, the materials, right... the materials...
Murphy digs through her bag, pats down every corner, and finally flips the whole thing inside out. Still, the papers she stayed up finishing last night are nowhere in sight.
...If those papers don't turn up today, don't bother turning up tomorrow either.

The person in front of her radiates a quiet, imposing authority. Murphy breaks out in a cold sweat and shoves her hand back into the bag for another desperate search. Maybe, just maybe, fortune is finally on her side; her fingers brush against something that feels exactly like a sheet of paper.

speaker: Murphy
content: —HAH! Got it! Take that, universe! The curse on me is officially broken. Today is the day my luck turns around!
Murphy eagerly unfolds the paper, only to find it's nothing but a comic strip.
Inside, there's a cape-wearing ranger, a warrior dragging a lamppost behind her, a rabbit forever on the run, a calm and collected analyst, and a worker in gray overalls.
And a little slip of paper, fluttering down.
All you ever bring is bad luck to everyone else.

speaker: Murphy
content: ...Wait, what?!
[Scene Change: Dungeon - Can use Happyzoo Restaurant background]
Murphy opens her eyes and finds herself surrounded by familiar sights. After confirming it was all just a dream, she heaves a huge sigh of relief.

speaker: Murphy
content: Oh, thank god... just a dream. For a second there I thought I'd screwed up again...
But just a few seconds later, she sees something that makes even less sense. Pink dust is swirling everywhere, and everyone caught in it is acting like they've been hexed.

speaker: EMP
content: Morning, everyone! So I've been thinking, really thinking, and I've come to a very important conclusion. I am, without a doubt, a very important person!
EMP, acting like a total drunk, just goes off and starts putting on her own little show.

speaker: EMP
content: I'm either the main character or one of those scene-stealing powerhouses who shows up and just owns the first three minutes. Honestly? Leaning toward the latter. It's more my style.

speaker: Letta
content: No, no, no. Letta is the best one! Letta can do anything now. Anyone tries to stop Letta? Squish. Flat. Like a pancake.

Letta heaves her arm upward like she's lifting something impossibly heavy, though the lantern is already back in her hand. She just hasn't realized yet; she still thinks she's exactly the same as she was yesterday.

speaker: EMP
content: Girl, you're giving off total villain energy. Can't you take some notes from me? Elegance. A little elegance, please.

speaker: Lynn
content: No, that's not right... I keep feeling like I'm supposed to run forward first, and then turn left, and then fall into a hole...

speaker: Lynn
content: But... why would I fall into a hole?

Each of them rambles on, talking away to themselves, like they've slipped into some strange alternate reality where they've become entirely different people, performing acts no ordinary mind could comprehend.

speaker: Murphy
content: Guys? What's... what's going on with you all?
Out of all of them, Murphy is the most clear-headed. When she sees her friends acting so strange, she hurries over, worried, and asks if they're okay.
You let out a sigh. The shackles flicker with a faint glow.

Crimson patterns crawl up EMP's gloves and along her sleeves. The dark haze veiling her form scatters swiftly, then, with a crisp, shattering sound, breaks apart into a cascade of shimmering motes. In an instant, clarity returns to her eyes.

speaker: EMP
content: Huh?!

speaker: EMP
content: Wha—no! I was this close to going up on stage at the DisCars! I could literally see Director Deren handing me the award herself!
Next are Letta and Lynn. One by one, you dispel the affliction that has taken hold of them.
Murphy seems perfectly fine, yet you reach out with the shackles and touch her anyway.
The moment they make contact, thin tendrils of dark mist rise from her body, unfurling and spreading like living things, as though locked in a silent struggle against the shackles' power.

You withdraw the shackles' power, and the dark mist fades with it, vanishing into nothing. Murphy stands frozen, staring at the scene before her. Even someone as slow on the uptake as she is can grasp what has just unfolded.
Yesterday, the ability deviation among the Sinners could still be laughed off as a curious little amusement to brighten the day. But today, their very consciousness has been thrown into disarray.

speaker: EMP
content: Okay, someone say something! Why did everyone just go quiet all of a sudden?
EMP wants to say something to cut through the silence, but nobody here is clueless. They can all tell that Mania's influence has gotten stronger.
And if it worsens just a little more? Will they all be lost in this realm forever?

speaker: Murphy
content: ...This is me, isn't it? This whole mess... It's gotta be my ability.

speaker: Murphy
content: But... if it really is my ability, shouldn't I be the first one going crazy? So why's it hitting everyone else instead...?

speaker: Lynn
content: ...Even if it's Murphy's ability doing this... it's dangerous, yes, but... it's not too late. There has to be a way to fix it!

speaker: Lynn
content: If everyone starts avoiding her because of this... she'd be so hurt...

speaker: Lynn
content: Just like I was...

speaker: Lynn & Murphy
content:
—I have an idea!
—So I was thinking...
After the silence has stretched on long enough, Lynn and Murphy both open their mouths at almost the same moment, only to stop themselves just as abruptly.

speaker: Lynn & Murphy
content:
—You go first!
—You first!
Lynn seems on the verge of speaking, but the words catch in her throat and she swallows them back down. Murphy parts her lips, yet in the end she only lowers her head further.
Just then, the crisp sound of footsteps rings out from the far end of the cavern. A calm, measured female voice follows.
It seems like... you could use a hand.
You follow the voice to its source and find Norma, just returned from completing her investigation.

speaker: Norma
content: This one's fairly simple to solve, actually. Think of it like noise reduction.

speaker: Norma
content: You can shield the receiver, block the transmission, or... control the noise right at the source.

speaker: Chief
content: At the source?

Norma produces a folding blackboard as if from thin air, snaps it open with practiced efficiency, and hangs it upon the wall. She then raps it sharply with her weapon, like a teacher with a pointer, commanding everyone's attention.
[Small CG 1: Norma]

speaker: Norma
content: We've confirmed that Murphy's anomalous concept has interfered with the Mania field, warping it into what we're seeing now.

speaker: Norma
content: The scope of her ability is considerable. It affects those around her, the surrounding environment, and even... Murphy herself.

speaker: Murphy
content: It's... it's not that crazy, is it?
[Small CG 2: Norma]
Norma taps the blackboard, and the image of Murphy upon it begins to shift and change at a dizzying speed.

It starts with a stumble, a fall. Then comes a flowerpot plummeting onto her head, followed by slime clinging to her, magic blasts hurtling her way, and at last, a frantic, breathless flight from some unknown creatures...

speaker: Lynn
content: So... as long as we can't find that experimental substance triggering the Mania, Murphy just... keeps going through all of this?

speaker: Murphy
content: S-sorry... I didn't mean to...
What's our best option right now, then?
Before you can finish, Norma has already pulled up her solution.
[Small CG 3: Norma]

speaker: Norma
content: That would be... <color=#fb9259>tying Murphy and Chief together.</color>

speaker: Murphy
content: ...Huh?

speaker: Norma
content: Correct.
Norma nods in affirmation, then picks up her pointer once more to resume her analysis.

speaker: Norma
content: ${PlayerName}'s shackles provide the most stable suppressive and corrective response to anomalies. They won't erase her misfortune entirely, but sustained close contact should at least reduce her interference with the Mania field to manageable levels.
Murphy goes rigid, her entire body locking up with a tension so fierce she cannot move. It seems this is the first time she has ever been in such close proximity to another person.

speaker: Murphy
content: Y-you really don't have to go this far for me!

speaker: Murphy
content: And! Chief... if my misfortune is never going away...

speaker: Chief
content: No. Leaving you unaccounted for risks even more unpredictable and dangerous outcomes.
[Scene Change]
Seeing that everyone has grasped the method, Norma packs away her full set of teaching tools.
But your mind drifts back to the feedback you felt when the shackles touched Murphy earlier, and a better idea begins to take shape.

speaker: Chief
content: Murphy's ability affects everyone around her, right? So what if we point it in the right direction instead of just blocking it?

speaker: Norma
content: You mean... targeted induction?
Norma does not consider this the wisest course of action, but you still your mind regardless and direct the shackles to fasten around Murphy's wrist.

speaker: Chief
content: Here's the plan: I'll keep a light connection, just enough to stay linked without pushing back against your misfortune. But when we're in a fight, I'll use the shackles to stimulate it.
When that happens, I need you to genuinely wish the enemy well.

speaker: Murphy
content: ...Wait, what? What do you mean?

speaker: Chief
content: We want your bad luck to work against the Mania. That's how your ability really shines.
Think of it like this, you root for an enemy to stand their ground, and they will trip instead.

speaker: Norma
content: ...Using the shackles as a conduit to direct intent onto enemy targets. The theory checks out, but it'll demand sharp focus. If your concentration slips...

speaker: Chief
content: I'll keep an eye on her.

speaker: Murphy
content: This still sounds completely insane...

speaker: Murphy
content: But... if it's you asking, Chief... Okay! I-I'll give it everything I've got!

speaker: Norma
content: Then I'd best be going as well.

speaker: Chief
content: Where to?

speaker: Norma
content: I'll continue the analysis. Time to figure out what's really happening to this space.
Murphy is happy.
All her life, people have turned away the moment she drew near as if misfortune had a face and it was hers. No one, not once, has ever said to her:

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I need your bad luck.
She tucks the photo Lynn gave her with care, nestling it close. The smile creeps up no matter how hard she tries to hold it down.
The air is still thick and damp, yet to her it carries a thread of sweetness now, a trick of the senses, light as a secret. Her feet, too, move with a newfound bounce as she walks among the others.
Just as everyone's ready to head down to the lower levels, a sound comes from far off—that horribly familiar jingling and clattering that makes your teeth ache just hearing it.

speaker: Lynn
content: Huh, that sounds familiar?

speaker: Murphy
content: ...Don't tell me that's the coin bank from yesterday!
Murphy's voice still hangs in the air when the sound surges closer, louder, more insistent. And then, cutting through the dimness, a familiar round silhouette hurtles into view.

speaker: Murphy
content: I-I-it's not actually back for revenge, is it?! I swear I didn't mean to knock it over yesterday!
Her words barely land before it springs, round body recoiling, then exploding forward like a cannonball, a racket of jingles and clangs trailing behind it as it barrels straight at your group.

speaker: Murphy
content: Eek! I'm doomed!

speaker: Lynn
content: Murphy!

Lynn seizes Murphy, who stands paralysed, and wrenches her aside. In the very next heartbeat, the coin bank hurtles past, missing the group by a hair's breadth, and scrapes along the stone wall in a blinding shower of harsh, grating sparks.

speaker: Murphy
content: Phew... that was close! Thanks... Lynn!

speaker: Lynn
content: I-it's nothing! That's... that's what friends do!
Letta has learned from last time. She steps forward in one fluid motion, swings her lantern wide, and brings it down hard against the creature's side.

speaker: Coin Bank
content: Meow!
The lantern is clearly no match for a lamppost in sheer heft, yet Letta has already grown accustomed to this unbridled style of combat.

speaker: Letta
content: Heh. Didn't think it'd actually come back for round two.

speaker: Letta
content: I was expecting one of those stories EMP's always going on about. You know, the "underdog rises up, you'll regret underestimating me" thing. With the coin bank as the tragic hero...

speaker: EMP
content: ...Pretty sure you've read just as many of those as I have, Lantern Girl.
A shriek of pain tears from the coin bank, but it doesn't stop. Head down, it pushes through the blow and drives toward you again, all momentum and fury.

speaker: Chief
content: Nice work, everyone! Murphy, you're up!

speaker: Murphy
content: R-right! I'll hit it with my best misfortune! Keep at it, guys!
Her words have barely faded when the coin bank ricochets off the wall, using the momentum to lunge back at an even more vicious angle, its body alive with the chaotic clamor of rattling coins.

speaker: EMP
content: Whoa—Murphy! Wrong target!

speaker: Murphy
content: Ack! Sorry... force of habit! Lemme fix it! Everyone... everyone is totally gonna lose this fight!
Your group falls back, fighting as you go, and only realizes where they are when the dim tunnels give way to a glittering, ornate cavern.
In here, the coin bank uses everything—pillars, steps, whatever's around—to bounce off and change direction, springing at new targets way more nimbly than something that big should be able to.

speaker: EMP
content: ****, since when does a coin bank know how to move like that?!

speaker: Coin Bank
content: Meow!
It surges forward with nothing held back, and the Sinners waver under the onslaught. But to you, this is the moment. The perfect opening, laid bare.

speaker: Chief
content: Now, Murphy!

speaker: Murphy
content: I-I got it! When it turns left... <color=#fb9259>it's gonna work!</color>

speaker: Coin Bank
content: Meow?!
The instant Murphy's words fade, your shackles release their grip on her. The coin bank, as though suddenly robbed of all traction, skids wildly and crashes straight into the wall beside it.

speaker: EMP
content: Nice! My turn!
Seizing the opening, she flips behind it in one fluid motion and looses arrow after arrow into the coin bank's back.
A sharp crack rings out as a slender fissure snakes across the coin bank's surface.

speaker: Coin Bank
content: Meoww—Wait! Wait! Stop hitting me, meow!
The whole hall suddenly goes dead quiet.

speaker: Lynn
content: ...You can talk?!

speaker: EMP
content: Why didn't you say anything yesterday?!

speaker: Coin Bank
content: You didn't give me a chance to talk yesterday either, meow! You just attacked me the second you saw me! And then you tricked me into crashing into the wall, do you know how long it took to pry myself out, meow?!

speaker: Murphy
content: ...I mean, you're the one who couldn't stop yourself. That's not on me.
Murphy hides behind you, poking her head out to chime in.

speaker: Coin Bank
content: Th-that's not the point, meow!
It lies where it has fallen, its four stubby legs paddling uselessly at the air. There is something almost pitiable in the sight.

speaker: Chief
content: Who are you? And why do you keep coming after us?

speaker: Coin Bank
content: I am the most proper, most law-abiding, most legally-minded Wealth Watcher in the whole world, meow!

speaker: EMP
content: Wow. Three lies in one sentence. I gotta hand it to you, that's a whole new level of shameless.

speaker: Chief
content: Get to the point.

speaker: Coin Bank
content: ...I wasn't trying to cause trouble for you before, meow! I've been looking for my lost <color=#fb9259>shiny!</color>

speaker: Murphy
content: Shiny?

speaker: Coin Bank
content: Hmm... now that I'm getting a closer look at you... you seem kinda familiar. Hmm... nah, must be imagining things, meow.
The huge cat-shaped coin bank gives itself a shake, its gaze shifting away from Murphy.

speaker: Coin Bank
content: That shiny is my heaven-sent investment fund, meow! I even remodeled my eyes to match it. See? Just like it, meow!

speaker: EMP
content: Even monsters get robbed nowadays? Guess things are rough all over.
You look at its eyes, and recognition clicks into place. They're the exact same as that greeting gift the Ring Research Institute supervisor gave you.

speaker: Ring Research Supervisor
content: You'll have to forgive my students. Hopeless bookworms, the lot of them. Not an ounce of field experience between them. Terribly sorry for the awkward showing!

speaker: Ring Research Supervisor
content: Now then! This is the Ring Research Institute's most prized achievement in recent months. Though I'll admit... compared to what a certain genius can whip up, it's little more than a trinket, haha... But please, accept it as a token of our goodwill!

speaker: Nightingale
content: Due to the Mania field's unusual properties, we can't directly intervene with it from above ground. The most we can do is slow its rate of expansion.

speaker: Nightingale
content: You'll need to locate that unstable experimental substance and neutralize its effects.

speaker: Chief
content: Where is it now?

speaker: Coin Bank
content: I'm not telling you...
The words are only half out when it catches the weight of your stares—everyone, fixed on it, fierce and unblinking.

speaker: Coin Bank
content: Just kidding, meow... I went sniffing around the slime village earlier, and all those slimes said it was that <color=#fb9259>alchemy geezer</color> next door who swiped it, meow!

speaker: EMP
content: Alchemy geezer?

speaker: Coin Bank
content: Yeah! The guy holed up in the workshop down below! Always waving around spoons and tongs, muttering about equivalent exchange and the Sage's Stone and turning stuff into gold, meow!

speaker: Coin Bank
content: We gotta hurry, meow. My shiny might already be his next test subject!
[Scene Change]
The way to the lower level still winds through the sprawling candy forest, yet today, the woods bear an unmistakably different air...

speaker: Coin Bank
content: Meowww! Since when are there traps here?! I've walked through this place a hundred times and never had a problem, meow... What's the deal today?!
The coin bank's pitiful wails ring out one after another, while your group, by unspoken agreement, collectively averts its gaze.

speaker: Murphy
content: W-wait! Something's off!

speaker: Coin Bank
content: Nothing's off, meow. I used to stroll through here like it was my own backyard. Those were just little accidents—
Crack.
It barely gets the words out before one of its stubby little legs steps on something. It freezes up, then carefully lifts its paw to check what's underneath.
Okay, good. Just a mushroom.
The coin bank heaves a deep sigh of relief just as the analyzer Norma left you flickers to life, as if on cue.

<size=55><color=#fb9259>Startleshroom</color></size>


A low-growing fungus found at the edges of the Mania field. Soft and harmless in appearance, yet when <color=#fb9259>stepped on</color>, shaken, or exposed to bright light, it instantly compresses the air sacs inside its cap and <color=#fb9259>blasts out a high-pressure air jet</color> to drive away approaching creatures.

speaker: EMP
content: Figures. Newcomers never know how things work around here.
EMP shakes her head, letting out a bitter chuckle. Yet her hands never pause; she seizes a vine and lashes herself firmly to the ground. The others, seeing her example, quickly do the same.

speaker: Coin Bank
content: Meow?!

The coin bank barely has time to puzzle over the strange behavior of the humans before it, then the mushroom beneath its foot bursts, unleashing a violent blast of compressed air. Prepared as you are, the sheer force of the gale still threatens to tear you from your footing.

speaker: Murphy
content: Aaaah—can't—stay up—!

speaker: Letta
content: The wind—is—so strong—!

speaker: Coin Bank
content: This—is—nuts—meow!
[Black Screen Transition]
It is not until evening falls that you finally stumble out of the forest, drained beyond measure.

speaker: Coin Bank
content: Huff... huff... Next time, someone else can be the guide, meow... I'm retired.
Beyond the bridge stretches a landscape that resembles the outskirts of some workshop, punctuated at intervals by a low, rumbling roar like furnace fire exhaling in the distance.
Gazing upon this utterly transformed area, your thoughts drift uneasily to the real Bureau, and what state it must be in now.

speaker: Letta
content: So... this is where he does his remodeling? Hmm... pretty interesting!

speaker: Coin Bank
content: Yep, meow.

speaker: Coin Bank
content: And he's the worst. The more you try to talk sense into him, the more he thinks you'd make great test material, meow.

speaker: EMP
content: ...What is this, a budget villain origin story?
Further on, a massive door looms at the end of the corridor. Through its seams seeps an unbroken crimson glow, and the faint pulse of heat radiates from the floor beneath your feet.

speaker: Letta
content: It's... kinda hot in here.
You have barely raised your hand when an exaggerated, maniacal laugh suddenly erupts from the other side of the door.

speaker: Alchemy Cauldron
content: Bwahahaha! Almost there! Just a little more! My grand work is almost complete! I shall connect to reality! I shall manifest into reality!

speaker: EMP
content: ...Yeah, someone's completely lost it.

speaker: Coin Bank
content: That's him!
The coin bank before you jolts as if electrified, its entire feline form poised to hurl itself through the door and fight to the death at a moment's notice.
The scene behind the door is even more dramatic than you pictured.
It's an alchemy workshop so vast it borders on the absurd. At its center stands a pot half a story tall, furnace fires roaring beneath it while pipes and channels spread outward like arteries.
A gigantic alchemy cauldron stands there, brandishing metal tongs and a long-handled ladle, muttering under its breath.

speaker: Alchemy Cauldron
content: The end of equivalent exchange... is the leap beyond equivalence!

speaker: Alchemy Cauldron
content: Heh heh heh... just one more step. One more.
It opens its mouth, and the rows of teeth inside shake in unison with the ladle perched on its head.

speaker: Alchemy Cauldron
content: Oh? New witnesses?
Until it spots the coin bank on the other side.

speaker: Alchemy Cauldron
content: No, wait, you're here to steal my life's work!

speaker: Coin Bank
content: That shiny's mine, meow!
The metal tongs in the old cauldron's grip lift. Clasped firmly between their tips is a gold coin gleaming with an unnatural luster.

speaker: Chief
content: Put that down.

speaker: Alchemy Cauldron
content: Put it down? Bahahaha!

speaker: Alchemy Cauldron
content: This is the key to unlocking the deepest truths! The essential ingredient to make the impossible possible! And you expect me to just hand it over?!
You frown, unsure what this oversized pot is trying to say. But one thing is certain: it's dead set on fighting you for that gold coin.

speaker: Chief
content: Murphy, get ready. Make that gold coin drop from the tongs.
The shackles flare to life just as Murphy activates her ability.

speaker: Murphy
content: You're gonna... hold that gold coin <color=#fb9259>steady</color> for sure!

speaker: Chief
content: Now!

The gold coin drops in an instant, but the old cauldron moves with impossible speed. With an eerie cackle, it flings the coin high into the air, then flicks its ladle upward, sending the coin soaring straight toward the pot's mouth.

speaker: Coin Bank
content: You absolute ******** of a cauldron, meow! Give me back my shiny!!!
The flames rage violently, and the surrounding light thickens into a syrupy crimson.

speaker: Coin Bank
content: I'll take you down myself, meow!!
With a furious roar, it rolls forward in a flash of golden light, faster than ever before.
Then, the very next second—

The workshop floor, already slick with molten gold and alchemical residue, betrays it. Rolling with too much momentum, the coin bank loses all grip, spinning out of control and skidding sideways like a bowling ball.

speaker: Coin Bank
content: Meowwww!
With a thunderous crash, the coin bank slams headfirst into the workshop's side wall.
The gold coin has already reached the pot's edge, but the sudden impact throws it off course.

speaker: Chief
content: Lynn! Your turn!
Lynn nods and sprints forward. The moment her fingers touch the gold coin, you activate the shackles, pulling her straight back to your side.
There's no time to celebrate. You activate the shackles again immediately, purging the residual misfortune from the coin.
Conventional communications can't reach the Bureau, so you're left with the crudest method possible to tell the team above ground to begin the external experiment and restore the facility.
You take out the analyzer Norma gave you, the same model stationed on the Bureau's surface level. You crank its reception power to maximum, then touch it with your shackles, setting off the alarm.

speaker: Analyzer
content: <color=#fb9259>—! Warning, parameter overflow!</color>
After several alarm blares, white light engulfs everything. You hear machinery roaring back to life from the dome above. The alchemy cauldron before you immediately senses something is wrong.

speaker: Alchemy Cauldron
content: Damn it... DAMN IT! I was so close... SO CLOSE! I refuse to accept this!
The alchemy cauldron before you leaps high into the air, then comes crashing down with colossal force.
The entire workshop lets out a sickening screech, like steel beams being wrenched apart, and then the center of the floor suddenly caves in.

speaker: Chief
content: Everyone, move! The floor's going!
Crucible stands, platforms, red-hot metal plates, and everyone too slow to brace themselves all plunge downward together.

speaker: Murphy
content: ...Ahhh!
Weightlessness hits without warning, and you plummet through a chaos of roaring noise and blistering heat.
Falling. Still falling.
A fall with no end.
She's long since grown used to the ground disappearing beneath her feet; things always slide toward disaster the moment she gets involved.
<color=#fb9259>If her bad luck were hers alone to bear, she would have stopped minding a long time ago.</color>
Murphy? Murphy...?
Time to get up. Your alarm's loud enough to wake the whole neighborhood.

speaker: Murphy
content: Mmm... Okay... Mom...

speaker: Mother
content: I've got to take your brothers and sisters to school today, so you're on your own. Be careful out there. No accidents this time!

speaker: Murphy
content: Mmm... drive safe...
But her misfortune always manages to drag others down with her.
<color=#fb9259>It was like this when she was a child.</color>

speaker: Teacher
content: Hello? Is this Murphy's mother? Murphy was hit by a flower pot during the field trip. It's just a scratch, but we'd really rather you come pick her up.

speaker: Teacher
content: ...Oh, stuck in traffic? All right, we'll take her to the community clinic nearby then.

speaker: Young Murphy
content: I'm sorry... Teacher. I caused trouble for you and Mom.
<color=#fb9259>And it's still like this now that she's grown.</color>
She spent ages preparing for the analyst interview, arrived right on time, only to find someone else's name on the list instead of hers.

speaker: Person-in-Charge
content: Sorry, the analyst applications are closed.

Murphy wanted to protest that registration wasn't even over yet, and that name on the list wasn't even hers. But then the interview room door opened, and she saw the interviewer fawning over someone who never even showed up for the written exam.
The person-in-charge quickly pulled the door shut, fished a random form out of the folder, and shoved it at Murphy.

speaker: Person-in-Charge
content: Look... reception still has an opening. Maybe try your luck there?

speaker: Murphy
content: ...Sorry for the trouble.
When something happens once, people call it a coincidence.
When it happens twice, they call it bad luck.
After three, four, five times, even she started to believe the problem really does lie with her.
Over time, she has learned to apologize first whenever trouble strikes, as if that might soften others' anger, as if owning her misfortune upfront could make it all a little less humiliating.
Another sharp crack tears through the air beside her. She was moments away from leaving this place, and now this.
A red-hot steel beam plunges down from above at an angle, grazing past her shoulder and streaking her vision with blinding sparks.
Murphy instinctively hunches her shoulders, her limbs trying to curl inward just like every other time disaster struck, making herself as small as possible. Maybe this is just how it's meant to be.
But the next moment, she feels a clear, unmistakable grip seize her wrist.
Someone is holding onto her tight, in a freefall where they can barely even save themselves.
Murphy freezes for a second, then opens her eyes to find a blurred figure before her.

speaker: Murphy
content: It's... you... ${PlayerName}.
The red light of the shackles stretches between her and ${PlayerName}, pulled taut in their plummet like a thread about to snap.
The howling wind, searing heat, and thunderous roar threaten to swallow her whole. Yet in this instant, one thing becomes absolutely clear.
Even now, ${PlayerName} refuses to let go.

speaker: Murphy
content: No...

speaker: Murphy
content: This can't keep happening...
What should have been simple unraveled into disaster. Relaxed faces shifted to weariness and frustration... She was supposed to be blamed again, pushed away again...
But not this time. This time, someone holds on no matter what, without a trace of reproach.
Murphy sets her jaw, her fingers shaking. She wants to meet this trust and the care behind it with something of her own.
With determination verging on clumsy, she squeezes the hand that holds her. She wants to protect her friends, the ones who believe in her without a single condition.
<color=#fb9259>Even if just this once.</color>

You slam into an enormous space far below. The Sinners do what they can to cushion the blow with their abilities, but the truth remains that you've just fallen from the height of a ten-story building.
You force yourself upright. Blood coats the back of your throat, and the raw scrape on your shoulder throbs with sharp, relentless heat.
But what reaches you even faster than the pain is the faint pressure of a hand squeezing back from the other end of your wrist.

speaker: Murphy
content: ...Chief...Are you okay?!

speaker: Chief
content: I'm fine. What about the others?

speaker: EMP
content: Cough, cough... Alive! Barely. Feels like someone took me apart and put me back together all wrong.

speaker: Letta
content: Hmm... nice sound on the landing. Just a little too loud, maybe.

speaker: Lynn
content: I-I'm here..! The coin's safe too!

Everyone lies scattered across the platform, but thankfully, they all manage to respond. Not far off, Lynn kneels at the edge of a fractured ledge, both hands gripping the recovered gold coin in a white-knuckled hold.
You glance back overhead. The opening you fell through has already warped into a hazy smear of red light above, as if something is slowly sealing it shut from the outside.
At the deepest point, ringed by fractured platforms and pools of contaminated sludge, the runes on the alchemy cauldron slowly begin to glow once more.
A pulse follows—agonizingly slow, yet so distinct it crawls across the skin—and the corruption tracing the device's surface flares and dims, swells and shrinks, like breathing.
The cauldron's body rotates toward you, and the mechanical arms fused to it rise with it.

speaker: Alchemy Cauldron
content: Come! Let it all melt away!

speaker: Chief
content: Watch out! The Mania concentration here's off the charts!

Before your hand can rise, the alchemy cauldron brings its full weight down on the ground. The impact sweeps everyone off their feet and launches Lynn sideways. The gold coin slips loose again, spinning toward Murphy.

speaker: Alchemy Cauldron
content: Once I smelt it down... this false, twisted little world will tear itself apart!

speaker: EMP
content: Oh no you don't!

EMP fires three explosive arrows straight at its core in rapid succession. But just before they reach the flames, the arrows lurch sideways as though seized by an invisible magnetic grip, spiraling off into crooked arcs. Then, a sickening sound of metal being chewed apart, and they disappear entirely.

speaker: EMP
content: ...Did it just eat my arrows?! How are we even supposed to fight this thing?!
Letta tries to block with her lantern, but every impact pushes her closer to her limit.

speaker: Letta
content: Hmm... not working out too well, is it...

The alchemy cauldron has clearly lost its patience. It locks onto Murphy, huddled behind the rubble, closest to where the coin has landed. With a piercing shriek, several red-hot metal tentacles lash through the air like striking vipers, aimed straight for her chest.

speaker: Murphy
content: Ah!
Murphy stares at the deadly crimson light closing in on her, her mind wiped completely blank.

In that split second, instinct takes over, and you throw yourself forward. The red-hot tentacle slices past your shoulder, opening a burning wound. You bite back a groan and wrap yourself around Murphy, using your own body as a shield.
The blow hurls both of you against the stone wall. A metallic tang rises in your throat.

speaker: Murphy
content: Ch-Chief?! Blood... You're hurt?!

In an instant, Murphy's eyes go wide, and time itself seems to halt. She sees the way your brow tightens with pain, the dark crimson streaking down your uniform and splashing into the glowing melt below.
You swallow the fire tearing through your shoulder and unleash your shackles, seizing the coin still shivering with resonance.

speaker: Chief
content: Go show it... just how... unexpected the reality it wants can be.

speaker: Murphy
content: But... if I do this... will we even make it back to the Bureau?!

speaker: Chief
content: As long as we're breathing... we'll find a way!
Murphy shuts her eyes and hurls the coin high into the air—

speaker: Alchemy Cauldron
content: Futile! Let's see... what pathetic tricks you have left!

Murphy fixes her eyes on the shocking streak of red across your shoulder. Something in that cruel, vivid color cracks her final reserve of timidity wide open. The tears hovering in her eyes are gone in an instant, overtaken by a violent bloom of purple mist.

speaker: Murphy
content: You want it so badly... <color=#fb9259>then take it</color>!
The coin veers off at an impossible angle, bending every law of physics as it shoots cleanly into the alchemy cauldron.
By all rights, the cauldron should be roaring with laughter. But one loose screw is all it takes; its entire structure buckles and breaks apart right there.
It breaks down fast, even the metal arms it once took such pride in peeling off with it.

speaker: Alchemy Cauldron
content: No... this can't be real! My calculations were... foolproof...
A final, rage-filled scream rings out as the enormous alchemy cauldron slams to the ground.
One by one, the lights flicker to life. The lava-cave illusion rapidly peels away, revealing the cold metal framework of the Bureau's underground research facility.
But the contamination lingering in the air does not disperse. Mania still presses down on the underground levels, dense and cloying, an unshakeable gloom.

What lies beneath you now is no longer false brick and molten rock, but ruined conduits and sprawling crystalline formations of contamination, still radiating heat. An absurd dream, at last, with its skin torn open.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Emergency mode switch at fifty percent.

speaker: EMP
content: What does "fifty percent" even mean?! When can you actually get in here? Chief is hurt!
As the interference fades, Nightingale's voice cuts back in. There's a rare edge of urgency in her tone.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief! Your condition... The Mania field hasn't been fully cleared yet. Please, stop all activity immediately and wait for external intervention! Do not go any further!

speaker: Chief
content: ...I'm fine.

speaker: Murphy
content: Chief...

speaker: Murphy
content: Don't move, just stay still! The wound... the wound's still bleeding...
Murphy's hands scramble to cover the bleeding burn on your shoulder, frantic. But the instant her fingertips graze the wound, she snatches them back like she's touched fire.
This... this is all too familiar.
In that instant, the space around her—freshly restored to the Bureau's true form—bleeds into another memory: a stretch of blinding, sterile white.
[Hospital]

speaker: Vague Voice
content: ...It's okay. Just keep pressure on it.

speaker: Vague Voice
content: I'm not blaming you.

speaker: Vague Voice
content: It's just... I can't go back to how things were. Not thinking about anything.
See? As long as you stay by their side, things only get worse.
(Flashback)

speaker: Murphy
content: No...

speaker: Murphy
content: No... this isn't how it's supposed to go...

speaker: Chief
content: Murphy.
You start to speak, but she doesn't seem to register your voice. Her gaze stays fixed on the blood seeping from your shoulder.

speaker: EMP
content: Hey. Don't you spiral on me now. Chief's still breathing!
Her hand retreats slowly. The trembling begins in her fingertips and spreads, reaching her shoulders before she can stop it.
You know better than anyone... People get close to you, they get hurt. Or worse.
It's always been like this. It's still like this.
How many more times are you going to watch it happen before you finally get it?

speaker: Murphy
content: As long as I'm here, it's just gonna keep getting worse.

speaker: Murphy
content: Even the shackles won't be enough. Mania's getting stronger. It's only going to get more dangerous!

speaker: Murphy
content: I know everyone's been looking out for me... But...
Murphy hesitates. In the end, she can't bring herself to finish the sentence.
Looking out for you? No. They're paying the price for what should've been yours to carry.
The Chief bleeds today. What about next time?
Are you really going to wait until someone pays the full price in your place before you let go?

speaker: Murphy
content: I can't stay with you all anymore.
Taking all the bad things on yourself... isn't that what you've always done best?
Just let go. I'll take all this misfortune off your hands. I'll deal with the mess. You'll never have to watch someone else bleed because of you again.
You... and your misfortune can't help anyone.

speaker: EMP
content: What?! What kind of messed-up logic is that?! If you hadn't done what you did back there, we might not have been able to take down that pot—

speaker: Murphy
content: But Chief got hurt.
Her voice is so faint it hardly has any strength behind it, yet it hushes every other voice in the room.
She rises slowly as the words leave her. Those perpetually anxious eyes now hold yours, steady and unwavering, like she's finally arrived at a choice she's been running from for far too long.

speaker: Chief
content: ...Do you really think walking away alone is going to fix everything?
Murphy says nothing. She offers a deep, respectful bow to everyone present, then climbs the Bureau stairs without a backward glance.
Right after, the analyzer Norma left behind blazes to life with searing red light.
The Mania fluctuations that had been dispersed across the entire area now converge at an alarming speed toward a single, narrow point.
You look up in the direction Murphy is walking. There's nothing there, but the shadows pooling on the floor continue to stretch, reaching further by the second.

speaker: EMP
content: ...Okay, I'm seeing that, right?

speaker: Lynn
content: Th-that's not Murphy's shadow...
Somewhere in the Bureau's lower depths, a laugh rings out, cold enough to freeze the blood in your veins.
Hehe...
Guess that big pot wasn't completely useless after all... The leftovers aren't exactly top-shelf, but... eh, I can work with it.
There, a shape that shares Murphy's every contour is voraciously feeding on the Mania left behind by the fallen alchemy cauldron.
Bureau members evacuate in controlled order under Nightingale's command, setting up a temporary command post just nearby.

Right now, she's locked onto the faint signal marking the Chief's coordinates. Just as the rescue passage into the Bureau is about to be forced open, the Mania field inside erupts in a violent second wave.
The buffer zone collapses, consumed in a heartbeat by the contamination's frenzied growth as it billows outward unchecked.
No time to call off the rescue team. Nightingale immediately reconnects with the Chief.

speaker: Nightingale
content: I repeat, we're picking up a new core reaction! It's forming fast!

speaker: Nightingale
content: Intensity—

speaker: Nightingale
content: —Intensity has already surpassed the previous peak!
From the deep shadows, the thing wearing Murphy's shape slowly opens its eyes.
As it raises its head, a monstrous grin stretches across its face.
There it is... all that effort wasn't for nothing after all.
You've finally come around, Murphy.

Ripping through Mania into the anomalous space is routine for Norma now. Yet the Bureau inside is in dire shape—lights strobing, walls contorting, floor and ceiling threatening to invert at any second.
Mania's corruption sends the data before her eyes into overlapping double images. She steadies herself against the wall.

speaker: Norma
content: I've placed fifteen beacons along the way and had the Chief and Murphy bind to each other to stabilize the field's distortions. And yet the Mania concentration here keeps rising...
She presses her fingers to her temples, willing the overlapping data to sharpen.

speaker: Norma
content: The concentration should drop in proportion to stabilization. Could it be that the Mania origin itself remains completely unaffected?
Just as she prepares to venture deeper, her peripheral vision catches movement in the Recreation Area.

speaker: Norma
content: ...Wait, what... is that?
On every prior visit, she'd only ever glimpsed a blurry dark shape. Not this time. Through the strobing lights, she sees it clearly now: that familiar shadow is feeding on the Mania around it.
Each bit of Mania it swallows tightens the space's distortion by another degree. And with every passing second, the shadow's form sharpens.

speaker: Norma
content: Murphy?
The signature polka dots and the wide hat and coat are identical to those of that colleague who always keeps her on her toes.

speaker: Norma
content: How did she get here? And... what... is she doing?
Norma tries calling out to her. Nothing.
She pushes back against the Mania's influence and edges toward "Murphy," only for her laptop to blare a warning from within her bag.

//Warning: Target M-value beyond threshold
//Evacuate immediately
Simultaneously in her sight, the physical readings around the figure are surging at a monstrous pace. That is no person. That is—

speaker: Norma
content: Mania?!
Mania swirls into it as though caught in a whirlpool, pouring ceaselessly into its form.
The shadow halts at the sound, and the distortion in the space goes still. It turns slowly. Its face is an abyss of black. It fixes on Norma's direction, like a predator locking onto its prey.

speaker: Norma
content: This is... a Mania entity?

She still has no idea what that "Murphy" actually is, but when the shadow's attention snaps onto her, every instinct screams. She abandons the investigation, wheels around, and runs, tearing a rift open in her desperation.

She's landed in a lava cave now, but at least it's free of Mania monsters. Catching her breath, Norma replays her ejection from the warped space. Without that spatial kick saving her skin, she'd be locked in an analyst-versus-Mania showdown right now.

speaker: Norma
content: A projection of Murphy? Or a fragment of her consciousness left behind in the real world?
Now even Norma, renowned for her cool, analytical mind, feels the edge of agitation creeping in. Confronted with things beyond explanation, all she can do is hypothesize and guess.
And, of course, the worst possibility of all.

speaker: Norma
content: This space was reshaped by Murphy's abilities. Mania would naturally gravitate toward whatever shares its origin.

speaker: Norma
content: And then... assimilate it as thoroughly as possible.
Too many variables beyond explanation. What does that Mania entity want? How is it tied to Murphy? Why take her shape? Does it harbor hostility, or some kind of... dependence?
The Murphy-shaped entity drags Norma back into her head. One thing remains solid: this warped space is dangerous, and she can't afford to let things get worse.
Her fingers hang above the keyboard, eyes fixed on the blinking cursor. A few seconds' pause, then she sets to typing with fresh determination.

speaker: Norma
content: Then I'll find the answers myself.
She closes her laptop and turns, heading toward the next monitoring model's location.
[Office]
The reception area was never quiet.
An endless procession flowed through—people reporting crimes, filing complaints, grieving lost belongings, raging about noise violations.
Murphy worked at a desk near the back, an unremarkable station where the legs wobbled, the drawer stuck at the midpoint, and the overhead light blinked sporadically.
A perfect fit for her. At least, that's what her colleagues assumed.

speaker: Colleague
content: Murphy, step away from the terminal for now, alright? Last time you touched it, we got a blue screen for half an hour.

speaker: Colleague
content: And the water cooler... she broke the dispenser button just yesterday.

speaker: Colleague
content: No way, even the water cooler?

speaker: Colleague
content: It's Murphy. You think the name's just for show?
Those words had long since lost their sting.
It wasn't that people genuinely disliked her. Not most of them, anyway. She'd simply caused enough trouble that avoidance had become second nature to everyone around her.
Murphy dropped her gaze, pulling the instant coffee she'd just prepared toward herself.
Then, with impeccable timing, the bottom of the paper cup gave way, and scalding coffee spilled over the desk and streamed onto the floor.

speaker: Murphy
content: ...I'm sorry.

speaker: Colleague
content: See? Told you.

speaker: Colleague
content: It's fine, it's fine. The rag's over there. Don't panic—wait, don't stand up! The floor's wet!
Pop.
The words had barely left her mouth when Murphy stepped squarely into the spill and went crashing backward, chair and all.
The office fell silent for a beat. Then came the stifled laughter, the weary sighs, the pointed indifference of those too accustomed to bother.
Only the colleague by the window rose to her feet.

speaker: Kiki
content: All right, that's enough. It's not like she did it on purpose.

She came over, hauled Murphy to her feet, and shoved her own tissue box into Murphy's hands along the way. The whole thing looked effortless, like she'd done it so many times it was muscle memory now.

speaker: Kiki
content: Did you hurt your knees?

speaker: Kiki
content: Good. Next time, don't fill your cup so full.

speaker: Murphy
content: ...I'm sorry.

speaker: Kiki
content: See? You're doing it again.

speaker: Kiki
content: It's not like I'm blaming you.
Murphy lifted her head and stole a cautious glance at the person before her.

Kiki was one of the few at reception who still spoke to her willingly. It wasn't pity. Kiki simply drew a clean line between misfortune and character: bad luck was bad luck, but a good person was a good person.
Over time, they fell into a rhythm: working shifts side by side, sharing discounted convenience store meals, staring blankly together at the endless paperwork on night shifts.
In Kiki's company, Murphy brightened considerably. Kiki had even bought her a four-leaf clover necklace, a small charm meant to coax better luck her way.
It felt like friendship. At least, it did to Murphy.
[Scene Change]
One perfectly ordinary afternoon, all hell broke loose on Eastside's outskirts. A Sinner riot exploded into chaos, loud and violent.

Orders collided over the comms, dispatches tangled mid-transmission, casualty figures kept climbing with every update. In the operations hall, screen after screen lit up, painting the room in a fever of blinking lights.

speaker: Alarm
content: Emergency mobilization order issued.

speaker: Alarm
content: All able-bodied personnel report to the assembly point immediately and stand by.

speaker: Murphy
content: ...Everyone? That means us too?

speaker: Kiki
content: The Suspect R you're after is hiding out at the SALVA Hospital on the west of the square—that's a well-known Sinner force.

speaker: Murphy
content: Great. I've only done first aid training twice.
Kiki said it lightly, but her hands were already flying through the supply box. Gauze, tourniquets, portable syringes...
Murphy just stood there, rooted to the spot. She worked at reception, and so did Kiki.
Their whole job was registering names and pushing paper, basically customer service with a badge. And now they were marching into the Mania site with everyone else.
...How did things ever get this bad?

speaker: Kiki
content: Hey. Stop spacing out. Take that white box.

speaker: Murphy
content: ...Oh, okay.

speaker: Kiki
content: Are you scared?

speaker: Murphy
content: ...Yeah.

speaker: Kiki
content: Me too.
But neither of them uttered a single word of complaint.
[Scene Change]
The district had come apart at the seams—smoke, fire, sirens screaming, figures fleeing in every direction, and beyond it all, Mania heaving with those sick, unsettling undulations.
Murphy's thoughts narrowed to a single thread, repeating like a prayer: stop the bleeding first, then dress the wound.
Stop the bleeding, then dress the wound. The words came easily. The work did not.

speaker: Murphy
content: D-don't move... Press down here first.

speaker: Injured
content: Gasp...

speaker: Murphy
content: I'm sorry... No, I mean, just hang on, almost done...
Kiki was just a short distance away, working alongside two other colleagues to guide the wounded behind the temporary cordon.
Everyone was simply pushing forward, throwing whatever scraps of training and instinct they had into the chaos, hoping desperately that nothing else would go wrong.
But fate is rarely so obliging.
Nearby, the door of an overturned transport vehicle suddenly gave way, and half the panel plunged straight downward, directly above the spot where Kiki stood.

speaker: Murphy
content: Kiki!
Murphy threw herself forward. The panel hit the ground with a brutal clang, its edge raking across Kiki's shoulder and back. Blood bloomed through the tear before the sound even faded.

speaker: Kiki
content: Cough... I'm okay, just grab the box first...

The gauze slipped from her fingers. The tourniquet clasp refused to catch, no matter how many times she fumbled with it. Before Murphy's eyes, the blood kept seeping through, as if it had no intention of ever stopping.
She had never known fear like this. It was not just the terror of watching a life drain away, but the deeper dread of losing her friend.
Later, reinforcements arrived. The Mania outbreak site was temporarily stabilized after higher-ranking Sinners intervened.
Kiki, gravely wounded, survived the treatment. But Murphy became a Sinner.
[Scene Change]

Kiki's wounds took two months to mend. They left a scar, but nothing that hindered her movement. Around the Public Security Bureau, many called it a blessing in disguise, a narrow escape from something far worse.
But Murphy knew the truth. All of it was her fault.

After their night shift ended, the office emptied until only the two of them remained. Murphy stood there clutching her files for a long, weighty moment. In the end, it was Kiki who broke the silence.

speaker: Kiki
content: I know what happened wasn't your fault—
But Murphy shook her head, cutting her off.
Then she reached up and unclasped the four-leaf clover necklace—the one Kiki had given her—and placed it gently back into her friend's hand.
To Murphy, this was the only way she had left to protect her friend.
[Scene Change]
The dim, yellowed old light abruptly dies.
When the maintenance lights flicker back on, you still stand in that corridor on the Bureau's lower level.
Ahead, the black fog has yet to fully disperse in the deeper reaches. And a trail of staggering footprints extends all the way into the darkest depths.

speaker: EMP
content: ...What?

speaker: Lynn
content: Murphy?...
It's Mania. It's broadcasting all her negative emotions outward.
With the Bureau's restoration comes Mania's revelation.
He gestures toward several Apostle phantoms drifting aimlessly in the distance. They appear to have lost BR-005's call, leaving them disoriented and confined to wandering along fading energy traces.

speaker: Chief
content: Come on! We're going after her!

speaker: Norma
content: ...I'm back?
She waits for a moment. No one responds.

speaker: Norma
content: ...No. I'm alone. The Chief's group and Murphy aren't here.

Only cold inorganic matter around her. Numbers pulse silently in her field of vision. Down the corridor, the emergency light hangs motionless. There are no voices, no footfalls, as the very air seems to have stopped.
She moves to the wall, crouches, and presses her hand to the corner. There, she feels a whisper of Mania activity, barely detectable.
[Scene Change]

Inside the Bureau, the Mania incursion has triggered a blackout. Electrical sparks crackle in the darkness. Mania contamination blankets the windows and chokes the corridors. The air reeks of acrid smoke.
There, amid the dark Mania, waits the shadowy figure Norma has been tracking all this time.
Norma...! What are you doing here?! You need to leave. It's not safe!

speaker: Norma
content: Drop the act. You're not Murphy.
The shadow slowly rises. A blank arc tears across its black face. Now that Norma has seen through its disguise, it abandons all pretense, radiating violet Mania without restraint.

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: Hehe... I despise people like you. You've ruined so many of my plans... broken so many traps I carefully laid...
Misfortune Incarnate before her claps its hands. Mania seals the entire space in an instant.
Along the edges, the thick Mania sets like cement, grinding every last flicker of signal into the dark silence.
This place is now a sealed abyss, a cage with no exit.

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: But this is where it ends.

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: I'll admit, you've made it further than I expected. Unfortunately for you...

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: ...these little toys of yours are barely worth swallowing.
It opens its mouth. Several wooden fragments spill out, coated in viscous Mania, hitting the ground with wet, sticky sounds.
Norma's chest tightens, but her expression stays stone-cold. One look at the debris tells her everything. Those are her beacons, destroyed.

speaker: Norma
content: If you're trying to taunt me, at least study the humans you despise so much.

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: ...Is that so? From where I stand, you're the one putting on a show.
Norma puts distance between herself and Misfortune Incarnate, but the Mania saturation is overwhelming. Data floods her vision in an explosion of numbers. There is no opening to exploit.

speaker: Norma
content: Looks like... I have to hold out a little while longer.
She straightens her glasses and watches the dark shadow closing in.

speaker: Norma
content: This is well outside my job description, Chief. Please ensure hazard pay is included in the next quarter's budget.
Norma is no fighter but an analyst. Going head-to-head with a Mania entity pushes her far past her limits. The creature's strength is crushing; she can barely hold her ground.
Mania grazes her shoulder. Pain lances through her, and she stumbles back several steps before catching herself against the wall.

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: See? Rules crumble before true power. Especially rules I've already rewritten.

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: Once I devour you, I'll grow even stronger... and that pathetic, cowardly half of "me"...

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: ...will be no more!
Misfortune Incarnate looms over her. Norma's glasses sit crooked on her face, her clothes disheveled, yet her voice remains calm and rational.

speaker: Norma
content: But this time... you won't have it your way.

speaker: Norma
content: Rules can be broken. People can change.

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: Oh?
Norma's sudden display of confidence gives Misfortune Incarnate pause. It stops a meter away, no longer closing in.

She removes her crooked glasses and slowly wipes them clean with the hem of her clothes. She holds the lenses up to the light to inspect them, then puts them back on. She even has the composure to check her handbag for damage.
She takes two steps forward. Though facing a Sinner far weaker than itself, Misfortune Incarnate retreats a cautious step.

speaker: Norma
content: My past self would have clung to those stable, reassuring numbers and followed the analysis step by step.

speaker: Norma
content: But none of that worked here. I tested, analyzed, and avoided danger. Over and over. And what did it change?

speaker: Norma
content: You're still here. The Mania is still here. The chaotic space is still here.

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: And yet you still run your mouth? Look around you... That insatiable curiosity of yours will bury you in this false space forever.

speaker: Norma
content: Heh. On that note... perhaps I should thank you.

speaker: Norma
content: Even the most distorted Mania field operates on rules. Disorder and chaos, those are the rules here.

speaker: Norma
content: I didn't see it at first. I kept clinging to order, and the space kept rejecting me for it.

speaker: Norma
content: But now, things are different.
Norma tightens her hold on the handbag, then hurls it to the floor with every ounce of strength she has.

speaker: Norma
content: <size=44><color=#fb9259>Watch this!</color></size>

Every beacon she planted, every data point she calibrated, and every broken rule she hammered back into shape all gather into this one swing. The strike cleaves through the entity's body. Spatial rifts tear across its form, locking it where it stands.

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: ...!!!

speaker: Norma
content: Surprised? While we were fighting, I scrambled every Mania configuration in this space.

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: Impossible...! You couldn't have done that, not in that little time!

speaker: Norma
content: Untangling a knot takes patience, but cutting the thread takes only a second.

speaker: Norma
content: The rules here are inherently chaotic. The moment you tried to rewrite them to suppress me, to box me in, I knew... that was my opening.

speaker: Norma
content: One more thing. If taking Murphy's form wasn't a coincidence, then I'm not the one you should be facing.

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: ...!!!
Though the strike only slows the shadow for a moment, it is enough for Norma to leap into the spatial rift.

speaker: Norma
content: I'll leave the rest of this mess to them. I've done my part as an analyst.
Her hand clamped to her chest, Murphy staggers through the passage.

The walls around her twist ceaselessly between reality and corruption. The once-linear metal corridor elongates and compresses in erratic spasms, while the overhead signs flash wildly through "B3," "Quarantine Zone," "Logistics Corridor," "Unknown Area."
She dares not turn around. She knows exactly what awaits—those already sinking beneath the weight of her growing power.
It has already happened once. It must never happen again.

speaker: Murphy
content: No... no...
She needs to get farther away, deep into a place no one can see. Some forgotten corner where all the bad luck will finally be hers, and hers only.

speaker: Murphy
content: If I could just be alone...
Ahead, the automatic door senses her approach and lets out a soft electronic chime.

speaker: Alarm
content: Identifying... Identification failed.

speaker: Alarm
content: Anomalous conceptual contamination detected.

speaker: Alarm
content: Please remain in place and await quarantine procedures.
The next second, the automatic door does not slide open. Instead, the entire slab of heavy metal lurches inward and plunges toward her head like a guillotine slipped from its rigging.

speaker: Murphy
content: Ahhh...!
She instinctively tries to dodge, but before she can even find her footing, the overhead lights explode one after another, and the fire sprinkler pipes burst right on their heels.
All she can do is clamp her hat down tight and lurch into the side passage.

speaker: Alarm
content: Warning. High-threat anomaly in motion detected.

speaker: Alarm
content: Termination recommended.

speaker: Alarm
content: Termination—
Murphy keeps her head bowed, her fingers curling tighter by the inch.

speaker: Murphy
content: ...Right. Of course. This is how it's supposed to be.

speaker: Murphy
content: This place wants me gone. Everyone around me gets hurt. So what am I even running for...
Keep moving forward. Isn't that what you've always been best at?
On the Bureau's wall, a shadow that should not exist slowly surfaces into view.
Find some quiet corner where no one can see you. Stay there.
Don't cause trouble. Don't drag anyone down. Don't make anyone stop for you.

Murphy's breathing quavers. Before her stands a figure exactly like herself. Down the corridor, the emergency lights ignite in sequence, and with every light that comes on, the shadow on the ground grows a shade darker.

speaker: Murphy
content: ...Shut up.
Why shut up?
The voice laughs softly. It sounds precisely like hers.
This is what you've been thinking all along.
Murphy doesn't want to believe it. But every word sounds like something dredged straight from her own mind.
A transmission bursts through the silence in Murphy's ear. It's Norma's voice.

speaker: Norma
content: Murphy! She's not you! She's Mania—
But before the words can finish, the dark figure swipes a hand, and the connection snaps dead. It makes a small, dismissive noise, then picks up right where it left off.
Someone like you should never get close to anything normal.
Ark
If you'd just hidden yourself away like before, Chief wouldn't be hurt. If you'd kept your distance, everyone might've already made it back safe by now.

speaker: Murphy
content: ...Don't you dare use my voice to say that.
The thick black shadow ahead sways faintly, then finally raises its head into a grin.
In that case... let's find out who this voice eventually belongs to, shall we?
Dear Murphy?
From the dome high above comes the shriek of grinding steel. Crash after crash follows, and Mania entities are before her again.
In the space of that moment, an explosion she knows in her bones detonates in front of Murphy.
The shackles' crimson light sears across the length of the corridor, sending every monster in her path flying.

speaker: Murphy
content: Why...
You simply reach out and offer your hand before her.

speaker: Chief
content: Because you think running away will fix everything.

speaker: Murphy
content: But that's how it's supposed to be!
She raises her voice at you for the first time.

speaker: Murphy
content: If I hadn't gotten close to you all, Chief ${PlayerName} wouldn't have been hurt!

speaker: Murphy
content: If I'd just run further away sooner, that thing wouldn't have gone after everyone!

speaker: Murphy
content: The Bureau turned out like this, and even this place itself wants to crush me—

speaker: Murphy
content: Doesn't that prove it?! Everything is because of me!
Her voice dies away, and the silence rushes in. Yet you, too, have something to say to the girl in front of you.

speaker: Chief
content: If everything really only gets worse because of you, then why hasn't a single person standing here left?
You shift your weight, stepping just aside, and from behind you several familiar silhouettes emerge.

speaker: Murphy
content: You all...
Murphy hesitates, then asks the question she has asked so many times before.

speaker: Murphy
content: <color=#fb9259>So... we're still friends?</color>

speaker: Chief
content: You keep saying you bring bad luck to everyone, but honestly, for Sinners... it's really not that bad.
The instant you finish, those beside you fix you with subtly pointed stares.

speaker: Lynn
content: Because... you have never, ever tried to use your misfortune to hurt anyone on purpose, Murphy.

speaker: Norma
content: Correct. Mania overflow is unavoidable. It could happen to anyone.
With the shackles' intervention, Norma patches the forcibly severed comms back through, and the channel stirs to life with a swell of voices.

speaker: Letta
content: Hehe... well... the misfortune's still a little bit of a hassle, sure, but once you get used to it, it's actually kind of fun!

speaker: EMP
content: Yeah! At this point, if you weren't around, I'd probably forget how to aim!

speaker: Chief
content: So, face Mania together with us. We need you.
Murphy stares at you, her expression frozen.

speaker: Murphy
content: Whoa... That actually worked?! Chief, did you see that?! Wasn't I amazing just now?!

speaker: Chief
content: ...Didn't you just say we'd lose even harder?

speaker: Murphy
content: Even if it means burning up all my luck for the next twenty years. No, wait, what luck do I even have?! Fine! Then I'll stake every bit of bad luck from my entire life!

speaker: Murphy
content: If this could be my everyday life... that wouldn't be so bad.

speaker: Murphy
content: Wait for me!
Dear Murphy, don't listen to them.
The incarnation of misfortune rips through Mania and surges forth, blasting your group apart across the platform without resistance.

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: Accept me. I am you. From this moment on, I will carry all your misfortune. I will savor the endless suffering in your place!
The moment its words die away, monsters pour out in a crushing tide.
You strike down every creature, yet your attacks phase through the shadow and leave no mark. Worse, each hit only seems to make it stronger.

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: Keep trying. Who knows? Maybe one of those will actually sting.

speaker: EMP
content: What the hell?! Did this thing toggle on god mode or something?! Nothing's landing!
