Murphy stares at that silhouette, so identical to her own, her fingertips trembling faintly. She can feel it: this thing is bound to her.
It knows every thought buried in the deepest recesses of her heart. It knows precisely what she needs most. And yet...

speaker: Norma
content: Listen, Murphy. Biologically speaking, it really is similar to you.

speaker: Norma
content: Misfortune surrounds you constantly, but the shackles neutralize your M-value, keeping you locked in a dangerous but stable equilibrium.
[Flashback with supplementary details]

speaker: Nightingale
content: The Ring Research Institute has preliminarily confirmed that this abnormal expansion of the Mania field is linked to the influence of Sinner Murphy.

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: Accept me. I am you. From this moment on, I will carry all your misfortune. I will savor the endless suffering in your place!
As the M-value climbs ever higher within the space, the device in your hand sounds its alarm. The Mania hangs so thick in the air that even breathing becomes a strain.
It is Murphy who breaks the silence first.

speaker: Murphy
content: I want to take a gamble.

speaker: Murphy
content: On the chance that I might have something too... something that isn't just bad luck.
The Sinners nearby stand rooted to the spot, utterly dumbfounded, their eyes fixed on Murphy.

speaker: EMP
content: Wait... are you actually serious right now?! Lantern Girl, talk some sense into her! There's no way she wins this!

speaker: Letta
content: Aha... this is getting a little too interesting. Like, so interesting it's looped back around to not interesting at all.

speaker: Lynn
content: Murphy! Please... don't do something this dangerous!

speaker: Murphy
content: Yes.

speaker: Murphy
content: Crashing into you, getting chased by monsters, ending up down here... It's true. I'm always the one who messes things up first.

speaker: Murphy
content: But I... I still want to help everyone. I want to help my friends.
Misfortune Incarnate stands at a short distance, silently observing the scene before it. The smile on its face does not fade—if anything, it deepens.

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: Heh... what's this? Grasping at straws now?

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: Sigh... You'd rather put your faith in these fragile, fleeting little things than accept the truth? You were born to stand with me. Only me.

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: The one who's truly been with you all along... has only ever been me. Your misfortune.
Murphy closes her eyes, her fingers slowly clenching into fists. It is the gesture of someone who has, at last, steeled herself for a revelation that will tear her wide open.

speaker: Murphy
content: You're nothing but a monster this Mania field spat out, feeding off my bad luck.
Her words fall away, and she opens her eyes, meeting the monster's gaze without a trace of retreat. In the same breath, her hand comes to rest upon your shackles.

speaker: Chief
content: I won't lie... I don't know what's going to happen if we do this, Murphy.

speaker: Murphy
content: Then I... should at least get one chance to see what's really left of me.

speaker: Chief
content: Don't worry. We're all with you.

speaker: EMP
content: ...Tsk.

speaker: EMP
content: Fine. If Chief's in, I'm in.

speaker: EMP
content: But I'm calling it now! If things go south, I'm the first one out the door!

speaker: Letta
content: Count me in too!

speaker: Lynn
content: I... I'll help too!
So what if the worst should happen? Then let it. A few more days in this maddening Bureau is nothing.
—Not when you'll finish this Misfortune Incarnate together with your friends.

speaker: Murphy
content: You want to become me, to strip away my very existence.

speaker: Murphy
content: Then I'll tear every last bit of it away from myself... and <color=#fb9259>give it all back to you!</color>

As Murphy speaks, she extends her hand, and threads of black come streaming forth in endless ribbons. Misfortune Incarnate before her is delirious with glee, so impatient that it seizes Murphy's hand in a vice-like grip before she can offer it.
The violet-black mist thickens, wrapping nearly its entire form in a dense shroud. Its silhouette swells and shoots upward, and its smile warps into something utterly grotesque.

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: Haha... yes... that's it!

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: Acknowledge me! Accept me! Only together with me, can you be whole—

But its voice cuts short. It realizes, with a jolt, that its own power is draining away at a terrifying speed. The mist is rushing toward Murphy instead. It thrashes wildly to break free, only to find your shackles clamped down on it, unyielding.

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: No... Why...?
It rips itself loose with a burst of force and looks down at its hands. Those hands that once passed for human now grow indistinct, regressing toward the primal form of Mania.

You've won the gamble. The Sinners wear sly grins; though not a single word passed between them, each seems more than happy to have joined Murphy in this reckless gamble: letting Misfortune Incarnate drop its guard and walk straight into her grasp.

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: What did you do?!

options: Let me spell it out for you.

content: Murphy got her ability from that accident. Not for any other reason, but because of you.

Like all Mania, you had an obsession. You wanted Murphy to grow stronger, desperately, because that would make you stronger too. But it never happened. Murphy was too unlucky. Every chance to improve just slipped through her fingers.
But opportunity always finds a way. An accident happened, and Murphy's misfortune triggered a deviation here. The deviation can alter the form of any Mania, and you used that to break free.

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: —!!

You got too greedy. Amping up the Mania wasn't enough; you wanted Murphy's body too. That's why you tried so hard to absorb her misfortune, to flood this place with Mania. You were looking for the perfect vessel. Your perfect vessel.
Too bad, you got outplayed. By the way... have you ever heard of communicating vessels?
EMP, never one for book learning, shakes her head first. You wave your hand at her, telling her not to cause any mischief.
One bottle's full of water. The other's empty. Connect the bottoms with a tube, and what happens?
Norma clearly knows. She gestures with her hand, drawing a flat, steady line through the air.

So now, the problem becomes simple. You both share the same vessel, which is misfortune itself. But the Mania stored inside is not equal. As the incarnation of Mania in this space, your reserves are practically endless.

If you hadn't let your guard down here, if you hadn't overlooked the shackles... everything would've gone exactly according to your plan. But anything that can go wrong will go wrong. You're no exception to that rule.
And my shackles are that tube. Your power is flowing uncontrollably from abundance to scarcity, until the balance between you two levels out. That's why your power is vanishing.
Murphy sways on her feet, and you rush forward to catch her. She is clearly overwhelmed, unable to contain this immense surge of power.

speaker: Murphy
content: Chief... I did it...
With the power of misfortune now absorbed, the black tendrils have vanished from around Murphy. What remains is a subtle, near-invisible shimmer of warm gold.

speaker: EMP
content: ...For real?

speaker: EMP
content: Lantern Girl, when we get back, we're buying lottery tickets. We're definitely winning!

speaker: Letta
content: But I feel like scratch-offs would be more fun.
Beside the easy chatter of the others, Misfortune Incarnate now burns with a fury born of humiliation.

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: Impossible...!
The power of Misfortune Incarnate churns and swells once again. On the opposing side, Murphy meets it with equal ferocity, refusing to yield an inch.

speaker: Murphy
content: ...This time, I'm not running away!

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: Fine! Then I'll prove it myself. Without your misfortune, you are nothing!

The maintenance platforms, barely holding together moments before, now wrench themselves out of alignment all at once. Nearly every foothold lurches in the same breath toward the most treacherous angle.
Even the Mania that had been drifting formlessly through the air coalesces under its pull, sharpening into countless slender black spines that come raining down from every direction!

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: Do you see it now?! This is misfortune!

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: It forces everything toward the worst possible outcome! And... no one can resist it!
At the very front, a single black spike drives straight for Lynn's face.
In the split second before it strikes, a warning sign, already loose, drops from above and to the side, slamming diagonally into the spike and deflecting it off its deadly path.

speaker: Norma
content: Lynn! Look out!

speaker: Lynn
content: Eh?!
The deflected spike whistles past her ear and buries itself deep into the wall behind her.
At the same moment, the metal plate beneath Letta's feet gives way, yet the fracture halts itself precisely at her heel, as if unwilling to take that final inch.

speaker: Letta
content: Hm... Time to give that pitch-black thing a taste of its own medicine. Let's see how it likes always falling just short!

speaker: EMP
content: Save the commentary, Lantern Girl!

speaker: EMP
content: This thing's trying to wipe us all out in one go!
She raises her bow and lets fly a rapid volley. Three arrows fan out across the air at distinct angles, every one of them aimed for the thickest knot of dark mist coiled upon its chest.
The black incarnation furrows its brow and waves away the arrows with a sweep of its hand. The two forces stand evenly matched, neither yielding an inch of ground.
With every step it takes, the platform splinters apart beneath its feet.
And Murphy steps forward as well. The two figures advance toward each other through the same crumbling space, unflinching.
[CG]

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: Do you really believe you can match me? Dear Murphy?

speaker: Murphy
content: Guess I'll find out.

speaker: Murphy
content: I want to see if this world will show me any path... other than the worst one.
The battle rips through the entire space, dragging everything deeper down with it.
From the corridor to the broken bridge, from the broken bridge to the warped hall, and finally crashing into that first area, the one overturned by the car, now a ruin beyond recognition.
Still, neither side can seize victory. Both have spent every last method, and neither can muster even the ghost of a proper strike anymore.

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: One day, that fear will come back to you. You will still run. You will still expect the worst to happen first.

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: And when that day comes, I will return! I will return as your deepest nightmare!

speaker: Murphy
content: ...That's a problem for another day.

speaker: Murphy
content: At least right now, I know one thing for sure. There is another possibility besides misfortune!
The incarnation sneers coldly, offering no answer. It raises a hand and forces misfortune itself into solid form, ready to hurl it straight at all of you.
From the distance, the utterly ill-timed roar of an engine cuts through the air.
Vroom—vroom vroom—

speaker: EMP
content: ...Huh?

From the far end of the darkness, two crooked headlight beams flare to life. As though tracing a route that should no longer exist, the car has wound its way through a vast, meandering circuit—threading through shattered platforms, veering around collapsed door frames, smashing through the dangling rails—

speaker: EMP
content: You're kidding me?!

speaker: EMP
content: How did it even get back here?!
The car charges forward, just as it did at the very start, barreling straight toward its target. Only this time, that target is not you.

The black incarnation folds in midair, its body bent into a lurching, broken arc. Its shell, already split through with countless cracks, finally gives way under the impact, and the purple-black mist detonates outward.

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: No—

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: This can't be!!
The car swerves drunkenly forward a short way, then screeches to a halt not far off. For good measure, the hood lets out a thoroughly undignified puff of smoke.

speaker: EMP
content: Holy ****.

speaker: Misfortune Incarnate
content: ...Why?
For the first time, it looks utterly lost.

speaker: Murphy
content: Because you've always believed... that luck only ever tips one way. Toward the worst.

With a thunderous boom, the dense purple-black mist rolls outward in all directions like a tide robbed of its center. And in kind, the misfortune and Mania that Murphy had temporarily taken into herself begin to scatter and fade.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Deep-level anomaly core confirmed eliminated. Reality restoration in progress... Wait, the underlying physical structure is collapsing!
As Mania disperses, a wave of vertigo comes crashing over you. You realize, with a jolt, that everything around you is inverted.
Thanks to the residue of Murphy's misfortune, the entire space now lies flipped, meaning every last one of you is plunging headfirst in free fall.
Until the very end, misfortune remains by your side.

speaker: EMP
content: A little warning next time?! I didn't even get to strike a cool pose—!

speaker: Letta
content: Hmm... looks like it's a diving activity now.

speaker: Lynn
content: N-no, wait! There's... there's still a cushion layer below us... right?! Right?!

speaker: Norma
content: According to my analysis, there should be.
But set against everything you've endured to get here, this is hardly more than a trifle.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief?! Chief! All personnel, deploy every maintenance airbag and buffer net on the lower level immediately! We have to catch them, no matter what!

speaker: Everyone
content: AHHHHHHHHH—!
The howling wind swallows her voice almost whole. You lash out with the crimson shackles, sending them straight through the air to snatch Murphy—the one nearest to you—mid-flight.

speaker: Murphy
content: Chief?!

options: Hold on tight! Don't let go!

content: After a fall that seems to stretch on forever, a soft white glow finally blooms below. It is the buffer netting and maintenance airbags, deployed automatically in the wake of the emergency repairs. In the next breath, everyone plummets into them with bone-rattling force.
Afterward, the Ring Research Institute spends two full days conducting a secondary sweep and structural reassessment of the Bureau's underground sector.

Faced with a report thick enough to bludgeon a person dead, Nightingale reads it through, falls into a long silence, and in the end merely sets the file down with care before turning to arrange new maintenance rotations and security shifts.
The incident is ultimately classified in a string of rigorous, officially worded conclusions.
But in the words of those who lived through it—

speaker: EMP
content: Okay, okay, listen, little mouse, you're not gonna believe this. We cleared this absolutely insane, ultra-hard secret dungeon. Under the Bureau.

speaker: EMP
content: And the place was completely cursed! Slimes, coin banks, you name it... Oh, and get this: there was this Mania thing, like, the embodiment of bad luck, and it totally had us on the ropes the whole time. Good thing I... I mean, good thing we pulled off some serious clutch plays, or we would not have made it out of there!

speaker: Hella
content: Pfft. A scrub's a scrub. You got your ass kicked, and you're still out here bragging about it.

speaker: EMP
content: Oh, right, forgot to mention, Chief was there too.

speaker: Hella
content: What?! That dummy had something this fun going on and didn't even tell me?!

speaker: Hecate
content: We were out on a field mission at the time.

speaker: Hella
content: Ugh, I don't wanna hear it! And anyway, couldn't you have just messaged me on the terminal? Obviously I would've rushed right back if I knew!

speaker: Hecate
content: Adjutant Nightingale said the comms were blocked by the Mania field.

speaker: Hella
content: Hmph. Next time something like this goes down, I'm definitely not missing it!

speaker: Hecate
content: Yeah. Next time.
[Scene Change]
In its post-incident review, the Ring Research Institute concluded that Murphy's "misfortune" was not eradicated, but rather brought into a more stable equilibrium.

Though drawn into the incident by misfortune, and though she came face to face with Mania, it was in reckoning with that Mania—and through it—that she finally found herself with something more than misfortune alone.

Of course, the institute supervisor who gifted away the experimental material was also suspended from his position. For the days ahead, he will serve as a member of the MBCC maintenance crew, helping repair the damage wrought upon the Bureau.
And so—
A long, long time later...
Oh wait, maybe... not that long after all.
For DisCity, managing to get through an entire week without incident is already an accomplishment worthy of the history books.
Anyway, on what seems like an utterly ordinary workday—though, in truth, not quite so ordinary—

speaker: Bureau Staff Member
content: Mania response detected from Sinner Murphy! Move to detain!

speaker: Bureau Staff Member
content: Attention all units, Sinner Murphy's misfortune abilities remain active! Stay sharp!

speaker: Bureau Staff Member
content: What?! The containment net short-circuited one second before deployment and tangled up three of our own people?!

speaker: Bureau Staff Member
content: Team One, pull back! Team Two, move in, now! Go, go!

speaker: Bureau Staff Member
content: Team Two? Team Two, report! ...What do you mean the tear gas all went off at once?! You can't even see what's happening on site?!

speaker: Bureau Staff Member
content: Sigh... Command, Sinner Murphy's current location unknown. Requesting immediate assistance from the MBCC Chief.
[Scene Change]
The reception office is unchanged, as it always has been. Since Kiki recovered from her injury, her life has remained much the same. Yet not entirely without change—
She has lately taken to growing four-leaf clovers, after receiving seeds sent by an old friend. The seeds, her friend claimed, came from another world and would bring good fortune.
Nightingale finishes the report at last. She lifts her gaze to ${PlayerName}, seated behind the desk with a shoulder still wrapped in thick bandages, and sinks into a long silence.
In the end, she merely sets the file down with care and exhales a sigh of quiet resignation.

speaker: Nightingale
content: I've already rescheduled the maintenance and security rotations. As for your fieldwork requests, I'll be rejecting every single one of them until your injury is fully healed.
As for the red-haired figure who vanished from the reports—
Who knows?
Maybe this time, fate will actually show a little mercy, and let her stumble upon a stroke of luck, the truly good kind, around some corner where no one's watching.

speaker: Murphy
content: Wha—?! Why did the brakes break again?!

speaker: Murphy
content: Chieeeef! Heeeelp!
[Message]
[Chat Message]

Otriana
Office - Break Room
Clutching her coffee cup in the break room, Tracy let out a groan of despair.

speaker: Tracy
content: Then what have I been drinking three times a day? Roachaccino?!
She turns to trudge back to her desk, only to freeze at the sound of a feeble, ghostly voice behind her.
<size=30>Tracy? Traaaacy...</size>

Is she hallucinating from all this overtime? Has heaven finally come to headhunt her? Tracy turns around. There, in the shadowy corner of the break room, a forlorn spirit is beckoning her over with a wave.

speaker: Evie
content: Hey, over here!

speaker: Tracy
content: Oh hey, Evie? What brings you to the contractor team? Something you need taken care of?

speaker: Evie
content: Not exactly. I heard a few people haven't clocked in for days, and now no one can reach them. All their work got dumped on the contractors. I know you guys are under a ton of pressure right now. I didn't want to pile on.

speaker: Evie
content: I was just a bit worried. You haven't been using any stickers when we chat lately. Figured you might be swamped. So I wanted to stop by and check on you.

speaker: Tracy
content: If only everyone at Otriana were as thoughtful as you...
Tracy offers a hollow smile and lifts her phone screen like a piece of evidence, the 999+ unread work messages glowing damningly upon it.

speaker: Evie
content: You're always the one checking in on me. My turn, right?

speaker: Evie
content: So, my team's been on this Eastian culture deep-dive for our new makeup line, and I came across this saying: "sending charcoal in the snow." Basically means showing up when someone really needs it!
Evie produces a paper bag from behind her back.

speaker: Tracy
content: You didn't!!!! Moonbucks? Vanilla oat milk latte with extra sugar?! Oh—
Tracy receives it like a sacred offering, cradles it in both hands, and downs a long, grateful gulp.

speaker: Evie
content: Any life coming back?

speaker: Tracy
content: Yeah... a little.

speaker: Evie
content: Sigh... Looks like these personnel issues really hit you guys hard.

No clear explanation has ever come from the company or the Public Security Bureau about those vanished employees. And really, what does it matter? Workhorses like them are only meant to quietly absorb the extra workload. They're not entitled to ask questions.

speaker: Tracy
content: So what do you do? When work gets like this, I mean.
Tracy mumbles the question between sips.

speaker: Evie
content: Me? I mean... I don't know if my thing would work for you. But if you really want to know... you have to swear you won't tell anyone.
After a quick glance left and right, Evie leans in and drops her voice to a whisper...

speaker: Tracy
content: What's with her...? It's like she's been waiting forever for someone to finally ask that. Wait, no. This is Evie we're talking about. My gold standard for a top-tier professional woman. Intellectual, poised, mature, warm. The human embodiment of grace under pressure...

speaker: Evie
content: So, on weekends, I would...

speaker: Tracy
content: You would...

speaker: Evie
content: Go full fangirl mode!!
[Workstation]
Tracy has barely made it back from the break room, not yet seated, when her computer erupts in a series of urgent chimes.
Probably more grunt work—messy, exhausting, and needed yesterday—she figures, clicking open the message window. But it's not work at all. It's from a group chat called "Family Forever."
[Chat Message 8]

Smiling, Tracy types out the words "set the world on fire." But her gaze catches the B+ on the performance review resting near her hand. She pauses, reconsidering, and backspaces until the chat box is empty again.

speaker: Boss
content: Tracy. Good, you're here. Nelson's gone MIA too. His workload's yours now. Get his files sorted and take them over.
Just a moment ago, she was happily bouncing back with her coffee; now, all the air goes out of her.

speaker: Tracy
content: Okay...
The words drag out of her, flat and heavy. She trudges over to Nelson's desk, lowers herself into his chair, and clicks open his desktop.

speaker: Tracy
content: Let's see what we've got. Spreadsheets, proposals, deck... wait. What's that?

There, dead center on the desktop, is a video file Tracy doesn't recognize. The thumbnail freezes on a blonde girl bathed in gentle backlight, the corner of her mouth lifting into a smile aimed directly at Tracy...
[Flashback]

speaker: Tracy
content: Wait, you? Fangirl mode?! Who's the idol? Guy or girl? Disian? Actor? Singer? Do I know them?

speaker: Evie
content: Shh, not so loud. I don't want to broadcast this to the whole office.

speaker: Tracy
content: I get it, I get it. Someone sees you have a life outside of spreadsheets, suddenly you're "not committed enough." Come on, you and me? Don't worry. My lips are sealed.

speaker: Evie
content: Honestly, she's just some underground idol. Super niche. You've probably never heard of her. But I figured... maybe you need something like that too. Something outside of work, that you actually like. Just a little thing to help you get through weeks like this, you know?

speaker: Tracy
content: Something I actually like? I don't think I have anything like that... Besides work, I just scroll on my phone. That's pretty much my life. But if I had to pick... then I guess I like someone like you, Evie. An angel who brings me Moonbucks.
Tracy looked up at the clock, and just like that, her smile collapsed into a cry of despair.

speaker: Tracy
content: Ugh, back to my desk... That place is literally hell! When is an angel gonna descend and save me from that nightmare?
[Workstation]

speaker: Boss
content: Still at Nelson's desk? How long does it take to sort a few files? Anyway, listen, I need all his projects wrapped up and on my desk by Friday. ...Hello? Tracy. You with me?

speaker: Tracy
content: Angel... I just saw an angel. Oh—sorry, boss!

speaker: Tracy
content: Almost done here. Just a lot of stuff to go through. Friday. Yeah, Friday's totally fine!
Once her boss leaves, satisfied, Tracy finally settles down and glances at the clock on the screen. She realizes she's just spent a full half hour staring blankly at that video thumbnail.

speaker: Tracy
content: Phanuel... Phanuel?

The name from the video title slips from her lips in an unconscious murmur. As if guided by some unseen force, her hands drag the file into her transfer list, nestling it among the ordinary work documents.

At the same time, a strange, exquisite pleasure washes over her. The world before her eyes takes on a fluffy, golden fringe. She feels blissfully adrift, as though suspended in pink clouds, her limbs entirely weightless.
(Scene change)

speaker: Host
content: She's taken over every screen, every speaker, every playlist in this city, and she's not slowing down! Phanuel is rewriting the rulebook on what an idol can be. So what's next for the girl who turned Eastside pink? Let's find out! Are you ready?

In the Bureau's Recreation Area, the TV screen is tuned to the Eastside entertainment channel, running a pre-concert promo. Phanuel's colossal posters dominate the frame, plastered across every wall of Eastside's central commercial strip.

speaker: Joan
content: ...Another one of those online celebrities, huh?
Tucked into the corner of the couch, Joan keeps her head down, absorbed in tuning an old guitar. Every so often, she glances up at the screen.

The guitar bears its history in every nick and dent along its edges, its pickguard layered with band stickers bleached pale by time. She gives the pegs a few careful turns, plucks a couple of notes, and frowns. Something still isn't right.

speaker: Phanuel
content: I hope this song brings a little happiness to everyone who's supported me!
[Play Song]

speaker: Joan
content: God, my ears are hurting... Is this what idols are putting out these days? This "arrangement" is just noise. I was writing better hooks in my sleep.
Joan's brow furrows. She pauses mid-tuning and reaches over for the remote. That's when the pre-chorus drums hit.

speaker: Joan
content: Wait...
[Theme Song Volume Increases]
Joan knows this melody by heart, so well that the next phrase arrives in her head before the singer on screen even opens her mouth. She holds up her guitar.
Mi re mi re mi re mi re mi mi mi sol mi...
The notes from her guitar and the audio from the TV land in perfect, coincidental sync.

speaker: Joan
content: You're kidding me! This is a song from my old band's album!
She keeps playing, disbelief written all over her face. One phrase, then another, then another...

speaker: Joan
content: This is straight-up copy-paste! Who steals a song and doesn't even bother to change a note?!
She pulls the TV screen around to face her, and there it is: the smile that haunts every corner of the city, now gazing directly at her.

speaker: Host
content: What do you think? Thirty seconds isn't enough, right? Don't worry, the full version drops in three days, live at Phanuel's solo concert! Fan support events are already popping up all over the city—
Over and over, the TV repeats the melody she knows inside and out, accompanied by the gleaming tagline: "A fresh original, tailor-made for Phanuel." Joan sends the remote flying at the screen.
[Throws Remote, Black Screen Transition, Office Area]

speaker: Staff A
content: I've checked for you. Chief is currently out of the Bureau. If this involves a dispute with an external entertainment company, you'll need to go through legal assistance.

speaker: Staff A
content: If you require legal help, please submit the relevant documentation first. We'll respond within five to seven business days.

speaker: Joan
content: Five to seven business days? Are you ****ing serious right now? Someone's about to steal my song and perform it at a concert in three days!

speaker: Staff A
content: I understand your frustration, but... right now we simply don't have the resources to handle this volume of personal requests from Sinners. However... if this is really urgent, we can look into speeding things up.

speaker: Joan
content: Right. By the time you "speed things up," she'll have toured all of Eastside! My work. Stolen. Monetized. Fans getting ripped off, ears getting polluted, and you're just going to brush it off as a "personal request"?
Joan remains glued to the service window, refusing to move. She fails to notice the presence behind her until the girl in the sheriff's uniform delivers a sharp elbow, pushing Joan to the back.

speaker: Jane
content: You're wasting your breath. Badgering the staff won't get you anywhere. Excuse me, are you done with her? I need my Corruptor extermination payout processed.

speaker: Staff A
content: Huh? Oh... yes, of course!
A relieved breath escapes the staff member. Her hand reaches for Jane's report, only for a palm to come crashing down onto the counter with a sharp smack.

speaker: Joan
content: You want to explain what that was about?

speaker: Jane
content: ...A reality check. Eastside's got multiple Hollow Syndrome cases still open. Even field teams and intel have been pulled to assist the city arrest team. Nobody's sitting around with free time to care about a song.

speaker: Joan
content: Wow. "Reality." So I just sit back while they gut my music, repackage it as some bubblegum pop single, and toss me a few coins? Maybe a nice little collab email? Ha. Real gracious of the system. Should I send Phanuel a thank-you basket while I'm at it?

speaker: Staff A
content: ...Ms. Jane, the base payment for your assistance on this task... has been processed... whenever you're ready to confirm...
Caught in the crossfire, the staff member speaks in a whisper so faint it could barely rouse a mosquito, terrified of sparking an explosion. Thankfully, both Jane and Joan let it drop.
Jane turns her attention to the payment check, done with the argument. But Joan, watching Jane's continued silence, lets out a cold, sharp laugh.

speaker: Joan
content: Yeah. Stick to Eastside. It suits you. Grind out your paychecks and keep your head down where the air smells like money and nothing else.
Joan heads off, guitar strapped to her back. Jane slips the signed form through the window, her gaze following Joan's silhouette until it reaches the end of the corridor.

speaker: Jane
content: I'd strongly suggest you don't do anything stupid, Ms. Joan.
Joan offers no reply. She walks out of the office area and heads directly for the A-Class Sinner detention area.
[In Front of a Detention Cell]

speaker: Joan
content: Hey. I got a job for you.

speaker: Joan
content: A big one. The kind that'll make everyone in Eastside remember your name.
[Crime Scene]

May 28, N.F. 116. A male resident of Eastside collapses without warning during his morning commute. No external trigger is identified. He loses consciousness. His face displays an abnormal, fixed smile. Following admission, his vital signs have stabilized, but he retains no memory of the event.
June 15, N.F. 116. A secondary school student loses consciousness without warning during a class break. The facial expression is identical to the first case.
June 28, N.F. 116. The third and fourth cases occur on the same day, at an Eastside commercial plaza and a community park, respectively. The onset pattern is consistent with previous cases.

Additional cases are reported. Victims are predominantly aged 12 to 25. Neither Banyan Hospital's Department of Neurology nor the Public Security Bureau's Criminal Investigation Department has identified any physiological, toxicological, or trauma-related cause. On July 3, N.F. 116, the case is officially transferred to the Minos Bureau of Crisis Control for centralized handling.
July 8, N.F. 116, A Youth Apartment in Eastside

By the time Wynn reaches the new crime scene, Eugene's team has already wrapped up the initial handover with the Public Security Bureau. Takeout bags have overtaken the apartment, spilling from the entryway into the living room, where they mingle with clothes and delivery boxes. Hardly an inch of floor is visible.
The victim, Nelson, had been absent from work for several consecutive days. According to the Bureau's preliminary assessment, he was lying unconscious for two full days without anyone knowing.

speaker: Eugene
content: Victim's already been transported. His M-value was right at the threshold when we found him, highest possible before full corruption. Vitals are holding, but mentally... not optimistic.

speaker: Eugene
content: Same as the previous cases. Unconscious, but with that weird, happy smile.

speaker: Wynn
content: People are calling it "Hollow Syndrome" online now. We're managing it, but without progress on the investigation, people are going to start asking questions we can't answer.

Both the Public Security Bureau and the MBCC are working together to keep a lid on public concern over the Hollow Syndrome. With DisCity already besieged by internal and external threats, even the faintest rumor of Mania activity in Eastside could spark an unnecessary panic. Unfortunately, the investigation isn't yielding promising results.

speaker: Eugene
content: These victims share no common threads. Different jobs. Different social circles. Different neighborhoods. Nothing links these people. As for the one thing they share, though, we haven't found any concrete evidence...
Eugene's gaze settles on the only tidy spot in the room: the desk. Its surface has been taken over by an army of pink merchandise.

speaker: Wynn
content: Phanuel. Eastside's hottest new star. These days, her face is plastered on just about every popular brand out there.
The first Hollow Syndrome case occurred during the victim's commute, as a giant roadside screen played one of Phanuel's cosmetics advertisements.

Every subsequent case has since been traced to locations within the coverage of Phanuel's pre-concert new-song promotions. And as the case count climbs, so does the percentage of victims who consider themselves among Phanuel's fans.

speaker: Wynn
content: With how hard they're pushing her right now, a couple of merch items in any young person's apartment isn't exactly a red flag. But...

speaker: Wynn
content: This? This is a lot, even for a fan.
[Chief's portrait]
But more evidence means more to work with. I don't think the Hollow Syndrome and Phanuel crossing paths is random. The last time her name came up, BR-003 was getting hit.

speaker: Wynn
content: Chief!

speaker: Wynn
content: On-site M-value scans are clear. No anomalies. We've ruled out direct contact transmission for now. Working theory right now is some other vector for Mania spread. Eugene's going to box up the evidence and bring it back to the Bureau for a deeper look.
You flip through the report Wynn hands you, then give Schorl a quick glance at it too.

options: A new type of sorcery, maybe?
Could this be connected to the Underground?

speaker: Schorl
content: Insufficient information to confirm. No subjects have exhibited full Mania corruption or transformed into Corruptors. No contamination residue has been detected at any site. If the source is a known enemy, their methodology has demonstrably evolved.

Looking back at the recent cases, both the spread and severity have been notably restrained, almost cautious. It's as if the perpetrator has switched to a completely different style. More calculated, somehow.

speaker: Schorl
content: Which is unfortunate for us. No obvious anomalies means no clear grounds to act. If this gets classified as a non-Mania case, the Bureau loses any justification to intervene in Eastside's civilian life.

speaker: Chief
content: Sounds like you'd rather we sit this one out.

speaker: Schorl
content: ...I'm only here to assist with your actions, not to offer judgments. But based on probability modeling, I'd advise holding off. Let the situation develop. We may capture more reliable leads once things become more visible.

speaker: Chief
content: And while we wait, more people in Eastside pay the price. The next victim could be a statistic you don't care about. Or it could be one of those little geniuses at the Institute.

speaker: Schorl
content: So your interest in this idol really does trace back to the Ring Research Institute.

speaker: Chief
content: Protecting the mental health of minors is a pretty basic adult responsibility.
Your eyes return to the file. The agency backing Phanuel is a name you don't recognize at all: <color=#fb9259>Mirrormoon Entertainment</color>.

speaker: Schorl
content: In the strictest sense, you don't yet qualify as an adult—
Smack. You give Schorl a slap.

speaker: Chief
content: Wynn, you and Eugene handle the on-site work. I've talked to Nightingale. She'll be at the Bureau running support for your investigation. Keep me updated through the usual channel.

speaker: Chief
content: And don't worry about me. FAC assigned a squad to watch my back.

speaker: Wynn
content: You're going somewhere else, Chief?

speaker: Chief
content: Seems like a good time to go meet this big new star. On behalf of some friends.
[Small CG: Three Threads Converge] [Muffled MV Sound]

speaker: Tracy
content: Phanuel...?
Settled back at her workstation, Tracy's fingers move on their own, pulling up that same video again.

speaker: Joan
content: God, her singing sucks.
From every screen, pink light pours out, weaving through the urban maze of streets and lanes, while the cheerful melody saturates every corner of the city.

speaker: Phanuel
content: Hi everyone! Phanuel here! This summer, I want to fill every moment with sparkle, just you and me! Ready to shine together?

speaker: Phanuel
content: Sing along with me! ♪ Even if tomorrow is a mystery...
♪ All I all I ask is for you to be with me!
[MV plays for 15 seconds] Ba, ba ba ba... Ba, ba ba ba...
(Scene change)

Late at Night
Office Break Room

speaker: Evie
content: Good evening, Tracy... oh, wait, actually, good morning. If you're here to heat up food, you might want to try another floor. The microwave here is... well...
Tracy looks up from her convenience store meal box to find the microwave emitting a burnt, acrid stench. Inside, exploded eggshells and smears of yolk are still caked onto the walls.

speaker: Tracy
content: Someone put a whole egg in the microwave?! I haven't eaten in eight hours, and this is what the universe gives me. A biohazard...

speaker: Evie
content: Want me to call maintenance?
Evie approaches with concern, but Tracy doesn't seem to notice. She simply picks up her phone and starts taking selfies.

speaker: Tracy
content: Phanuel... this is my day fifteen of overtime. No water break. No sleep. And the microwave exploded right before I came to heat up food... I'm so, so miserable. Could you maybe say something to me? Please please please...
Tracy admires her post a few times with satisfaction. Only after hitting send does she realize Evie has been standing beside her, watching the entire time.

speaker: Tracy
content: Ah! Evie! Sorry, I totally zoned out. What did you say? If it's about the microwave, it's fine, I'll just go to another floor. Stairs. Cardio. Win-win, right?

speaker: Evie

speaker: Phanuel
content: No.
Eliza flings the remote to the floor, crosses her arms, and takes a deep, steadying breath.

speaker: Eliza
content: I can see <color=#fb9259>that person</color> has been getting to you.

speaker: Phanuel
content: I'm sorry. This was my fault entirely. I've let you down. I've failed the <color=#fb9259>company</color> that made me. And I've failed my fans...

speaker: Eliza
content: Enough. I've already smoothed things over with the producer. Your segments will be cut. The official line is concert prep—grueling schedule, exhaustion, doctor's orders. You were too unwell to appear.

speaker: Eliza
content: You'll film some behind-the-scenes footage with them later, of you looking pale and frail. I'll handle the medical paperwork and the prescription records. We'll post the apology together. It'll play well. Sympathy, concern, a little pre-concert buzz...

speaker: Phanuel
content: Understood. Phanuel will face the days ahead with strength and bring love and courage to all my Cherubs.
Eliza studies the face before her with sharp, appraising eyes. Then, just as quickly, the tension drains from her shoulders.

speaker: Eliza
content: What's done is done. I'm not going to hold this over you. A face that pretty shouldn't go to waste. Everyone goes crazy for that smile of yours. Keep giving it to them.

speaker: Eliza
content: Do you know what's next?

speaker: Phanuel
content: Yes. It's ten o'clock. Time for dance practice.
In the cavernous, empty penthouse, the speakers pump out the special new track Phanuel has prepared for her concert.

Beneath the music and the beat, a faint rustle of fabric stirs from the far end of the walk-in closet. Someone lies bound at the wrists and ankles, struggling to inch forward. Sweat drips from the person's brow into the carpet, leaving a broken trail of dark stains.
Half the song later, he finally reaches the door. His bound hands fumble blindly behind his back, feeling through the narrow gap until they push it open, letting in a sliver of light.
female_content: Half the song later, she finally reaches the door. Her bound hands fumble blindly behind her back, feeling through the narrow gap until they push it open, letting in a sliver of light.

content: [Falling SFX][Small CG: Peeping POV Projection]

speaker: Phanuel
content: One, two, three, four. Two, two, three, four...
Something flickers at the edge of Phanuel's vision. She falters mid-step, her rhythm breaking.

speaker: Eliza
content: Wrong. Start over.

speaker: Phanuel
content: Two two three four...
Her dance shoes clack against the marble floor, struggling to keep up with the beat.
The figure in the shadows shrinks back further, using the cover to keep watching. Eliza notices but merely smirks and turns to Phanuel:

speaker: Eliza
content: From now on, you focus only on the concert. Everything we've built, all of it, has been leading to that moment. That's when you shine brightest. That's when you become what you were always meant to be. You will be the star that commands all eyes.

speaker: Eliza
content: Whatever <color=#fb9259>that person</color> did, or said to you, it changes nothing. You were born for the spotlight. Nothing can take that from you.
Phanuel raises her head. A perfect, polished smile stretches across her face, but behind it, her eyes grow increasingly hollow.

speaker: Phanuel
content: I was born for the spotlight...

speaker: Phanuel
content: I will command all eyes...
She keeps dancing. It's not even that hard of a practice. Still, her voice comes out thin and hollow.

speaker: Eliza
content: Forget it. Whatever happened while I was away no longer matters. You’ve already seen what became of that person.
The figure writhes inside the closet. The faint sounds of the struggle are swallowed entirely by the music.
Nngh...
Phanuel's consciousness begins to blur. She thinks she sees someone in the shadows trying to catch her attention, but her awareness is already slipping out of her control.

speaker: Eliza
content: Don't worry. We're a management company, not criminals. Once everything is finished, I'll let him go. Even if you can't see it now, everything I do is for you. For what we're building together.
female_content: Don't worry. We're a management company, not criminals. Once everything is finished, I'll let her go. Even if you can't see it now, everything I do is for you. For what we're building together.

speaker: Phanuel
content: Phanuel understands... this is the company's order.

speaker: Eliza & Phanuel
content: Yes. Let them worship you, let them give their faith to you. Guide them, liberate them... Yes. Let them worship me, let them give their faith to me. Guide them, liberate them...
An eerie fragrance seeps through the air, steadily infiltrating Phanuel's senses.
[Big CG: Close-up]

speaker: Phanuel
content: Yes. Phanuel will become everything you've ever wanted. The brightest star Eastside has ever seen.

speaker: Phanuel
content: The virtual angel will step into the real world for the very first time. A stage of light. A path to paradise. She'll lead her faithful there, all of them.

speaker: Phanuel
content: Come and find happiness with Phanuel!
Deep into the night, the office is empty and still. The whole floor sits in darkness, the lights long dead, except for the monitor on Tracy's desk still burning bright.
On the screen, an exclusive video plays, a special perk reserved for loyal Cherubs.

speaker: Phanuel?
content: Come and find happiness with Phanuel!

speaker: Phanuel?
content: C-C-C-COME AND—*A(&SYH@%$— FIND HAPPINESS HAP-HAP-HAP-HAPPINESS WITH PHANUEL?
[Small CG 2: Close-up of Face, Screen Reflected in Eyes]
On the screen, Phanuel fractures into dozens of misaligned windows—her smile, her eyes, her fingers, the hem of her skirt—all flickering in jagged, out-of-sync flashes, mirrored in Tracy's pupils.
The pink-white static begins to bleed past the edges of the frame, layering over countless smiling faces, inching closer... devouring what little remains of Tracy's awareness.

speaker: Tracy
content: Yes... I will go find happiness... with Phanuel...
[Phanuel's Mansion]
Ten hours have passed since you were bound here, completely cut off from the outside world. Phanuel's concert is less than half a day away.

speaker: Chief
content: Great. Triangle Face isn't here. Can't even chat with someone to pass the time.
You shift around, trying to make the restraints a little more bearable.

Ten hours. Since Schorl still hasn't been able to pinpoint your location, that can only mean whoever's behind this has accounted for every communication channel the Bureau has. Including the backup ones.

speaker: Chief
content: Mirrormoon Entertainment... registered two years ago. Eliza's both the owner and legal representative. Phanuel's their only artist, and the entire company's operations revolve around her.

speaker: Chief
content: What kind of goal would require Phanuel's powers and a concert of this scale? Why do they need to build her up as the absolute top of the charts, and have all eyes on her? Just what are they trying to achieve...?

You can more or less guess who's orchestrating everything. The problem is, you haven't managed to find anything that can be called a concrete clue. That said, two things are certain from how they're deliberating erasing all traces—for one, they know you very well, and for two, the concert's far from the end of their plan.
Creak. Someone has pushed open the wardrobe door while you're lost in thought.

Whoever it is, their footsteps are light. They pause at the doorway to look around before pulling the door shut. You sense a presence drawing closer from behind. Then, you feel a cold touch at your wrists.
Shh. Eliza's asleep. I told the guards I spotted a suspicious vehicle downstairs to trick them into going away.
It's Phanuel. With no light around to speak of, it takes a while before she finally finds the knot around your wrists.

options: Did you come to release me?
Aren't you afraid Eliza will find out?

content: She seems unprepared for your question, and awkwardly changes the subject.

speaker: Phanuel
content: Does it hurt? The knot around your hands was quite tight... You know, Eliza's never done anything like this before. I swear.

speaker: Chief
content: Still defending her? I've got to admit, your manager means more to you than I thought.

speaker: Phanuel
content: ...I just got my nails done, so this might take a while. Give me a minute.
The mansion is completely silent, making the rustling of fingers working at the ropes strikingly clear.

speaker: Chief
content: You do realize what will happen if you untie me, right?

speaker: Phanuel
content: Hmm... you'll feel better?

speaker: Chief
content: If I make it out of here, your concert and your career will be finished...

speaker: Chief
content: Can you really live with that?
The hands working at your bindings hesitate, then go still.

speaker: Phanuel
content: Do you remember the promise we made earlier today...? The ice cream... the taste of summer, the taste of... freedom?
[Eastside Streets]
7 Hours Before Losing Contact

speaker: FAC
content: Do you need assistance? It seems you've been waiting for quite some time.

speaker: Chief
content: No. Your presence could trigger a Mania panic in Eastside. Too many eyes are on Phanuel right now, and the case is still under investigation. Better to keep a low profile.

speaker: Staff Member
content: Coming through, coming through!
A boom mic flies straight toward your face.

You dodge in time. The crew member moves on, hauling equipment through the maze of lighting rigs. Elsewhere, camera dollies are rolling back and forth along their tracks while the director shouts something from behind the monitors. Chaotic, but it's just another day on the film set.

speaker: FAC
content: What did you say? We couldn't hear you.

speaker: Chief
content: I said stand by. I'm about to meet Phanuel!

speaker: Staff Member
content: You want to see Phanuel?
The boom mic swings your way again. You sidestep.

speaker: Staff Member
content: I had my eye on you. No badge, no credentials. How'd you sneak in?

speaker: Chief
content: I do have credentials, and I've gotten the necessary permits as well. I just need a word with Phanuel. Won't take long.

speaker: Staff Member
content: Another fan who pulled some strings, I bet. Hey, who let this one in?! How many times do I gotta say this—we're on a tight schedule! Do you have any idea how hard it was to book this slot? We can't afford any slip-ups. Come throw this fan out, now!

speaker: Chief
content: Wait, hold on—
Before you can get another word in, a concerned voice cuts through the comms.

speaker: FAC
content: Chief, are you in danger? Should we come over?

speaker: Chief
content: It's fine... I've already contacted Phanuel's manager.

speaker: Staff Member
content: Wow, how creative. Can't you people come up with something new? Hey, hello?! I said throw this fan out! We're about to roll, hurry up!

speaker: FAC
content: It sounds quite chaotic on your end. What's going on? The manager... Should we target the manager instead?

speaker: Staff Member
content: "Target"? Wait, are you here to sabotage us?! You with some competing brand or something? Do you have any idea how much money went into this ad? How much effort it took just to get Phanuel for a single shot?!

speaker: FAC
content: It sounds like you're at risk of being removed from the premises. We're ready to assist at any time, so please avoid any direct confrontation with Eastside civilians.
Why the heck did they start chatting cross-platform...? Either way, with the crew closing in to remove you, you have no choice but to pull out your credentials as Chief.

speaker: Chief
content: Actually, I'm...

speaker: Staff Member
content: Phanuel's here! I don't have time for this, so stay back, you hear me?
The long boom mic swooshes over your head and plunges straight into the crowd.

Key leader of the West District revolution. Distinguished guest of the Ring Research Institute and the Council. Acting commander of the Black Ring campaign. On paper, you're quite the big deal, yet right now, no one's sparing you so much as a glance. Meanwhile, Phanuel's been completely swarmed.
Just as you're about to make your move, a folder appears in front of you.
Just as you're about to reach out to FAC and adjust your course of action, a folder appears in front of you.
I'm Eliza, Phanuel's manager. Chief of the Minos Bureau of Crisis Control, was it? You're the one who contacted me, right?
She looks you up and down. Your uniform and the Bureau insignia, not exactly a common sight for Eastsiders, draw not so much as a flicker of surprise from her.

speaker: Chief
content: Normally, I would've summoned you directly to the Bureau. It's just that, given the nature of Phanuel's work and the fact that I have a few friends who are fans of hers, I thought it'd be worth coming to see things firsthand. Hope that's alright.

speaker: Eliza
content: Of course. It'd be my pleasure to assist. That said, I only have five minutes. I trust you wouldn't disrupt the lives and livelihoods of ordinary citizens over something as insubstantial as rumors?

speaker: Chief
content: That depends on how cooperative you are. Recently, a number of Phanuel's fans have been found in a dazed state with vacant smiles. Online, people have been referring to this as the Hollow Syndrome. Are you aware of this?

speaker: Eliza
content: Yes, and?

speaker: Chief
content: And? Phanuel's concert is right around the corner. Meanwhile, her fans are getting caught up in an anomalous incident. Don't you have anything you want to say?

speaker: Eliza
content: If these "victims" were fans of some other celebrity, perhaps that would be too much of a coincidence. But this is Phanuel we're talking about.

speaker: Eliza
content: The biggest name in Eastside. Someone whose fame reaches all the way from Paradeisos down to the West District. According to the data I have on hand, she even has a following in the Outland.

speaker: Chief
content: What are you getting at?

speaker: Eliza
content: That her fanbase is enormous. Pull ten people off the street and eight of them will be her fans. This "coincidence" provides too small a sample size to prove anything. And as far as I can tell, you don't seem to have any real evidence either, do you?

speaker: Chief
content: Looks like we haven't done enough to get our name out there, seeing as you're underestimating us. Unlike the Public Security Bureau, Ms. Eliza, I have an obligation to address any threat to DisCity's safety. Meanwhile... You don't seem willing to cooperate with us?

speaker: Eliza
content: Then, please, feel free to slap cuffs on Eastside's biggest star and haul her back to your turf for questioning. I can clear her entire schedule to accommodate you. But even you're afraid of the optics, no? You're a Chief, after all. The truth matters a lot less than how the system looks. That's just how it is, and you know it.

speaker: Chief
content: Then I must have you know I'm quite notorious for having thick skin. I wasn't planning on interrogating you, but I've changed my mind now. I'd love to see where you got this backbone from. Just who is backing you? And who are you covering for?
You're ready to press further, but a clapperboard snaps in the distance.

speaker: Staff Member
content: Cut! That's a wrap! As expected of Phanuel. First take and it's perfect. Adorable. Simply adorable. The effect's brilliant. This ad's gonna be a massive hit!

speaker: Phanuel
content: It's all thanks to how hard everyone worked. I hope that everything we've put into this will be recognized by the audience and fans.

speaker: Phanuel
content: I've also bought all of you some refreshments! I hope you'll keep loving and supporting me in the future! Hope to see you all again soon!
A black van pulls up outside the set just as those sweet parting words fade, and Eliza throws her hands up in resignation.

speaker: Eliza
content: Well, there's your five minutes. I wish you luck with your investigation. I do hope you find the truth soon and give us ordinary citizens the peace of mind we deserve.
Eliza gives a perfunctory bow, then turns to get in the car.
The van pulls away before you can even catch a glimpse of Phanuel. If the crew around you weren't cheerfully dissecting the ad, you'd almost think she hadn't been there at all.
As the van disappears from view, you put in a call to FAC.

speaker: Chief
content: Change of plans. Keeping a low profile isn't working. Get me a press pass.

Before the Concert
Media Press Conference

The press conference venue is even more packed than the film set. A long line snakes through the media check-in area, and a forest of camera tripods has claimed every inch of the front rows. By the time you arrive, there's almost nowhere left to stand.

speaker: Reporter A
content: Which outlet are they with? How come they're so late?

speaker: Reporter B
content: Probably just another nobody looking to ride Phanuel's coattails. Won't be the first, won't be the last.

Those words barely come out before a rapid burst of shutters goes off like a string of firecrackers. The entire venue blazes white, bright enough that it's blinding. Through the glare, you can just barely make out a pale figure stepping onto the stage.

speaker: Phanuel
content: Wow... so many people came. Just thinking about how I need to face a whole stadium... makes my heart race. Can you hear it? Thump, thump—

The playful opener draws a ripple of laughter from the crowd, and the mood lifts noticeably. You still haven't gotten a clear look at the stage, but the media parties have already begun firing their questions.

speaker: Reporter A
content: Phanuel, regarding the special setlist prepared exclusively for this concert. Is there anything you can share with us?

speaker: Reporter B
content: Your concert tickets sold out in seconds, and many people online are requesting that you add more dates. Any plans for that?

speaker: Reporters
content: ...Phanuel... Phanuel...
Questions pour in from every direction. Mixed with the noise of shutters, it's impossible to even tell which voice is coming from where.
Then comes a soft tap on the microphone, followed by a gentle clearing of the throat from the stage.

speaker: Phanuel
content: Thank you all for being so enthusiastic. I'll answer your questions one by one.

speaker: Phanuel
content: First is, of course, the new song prepared specifically for this concert. Since everyone's so curious, Phanuel will reveal a little something: it's going to be something quite different from anything I've done before. We're incorporating a touch of classical music into the mix, so please look forward to it!

speaker: Phanuel
content: As for adding more dates, we have no plans for that at the moment. My team and I want to put our heart into this first show before anything else.

You peer through the gaps between heads from the back of the room, trying to get a look at the blurry silhouette on stage. It's hard to find fault with Phanuel's answers, but that doesn't mean they can satisfy the reporters.

speaker: Reporter A
content: Will you be singing live this time, or will there be backing vocals? Do you think your stamina will last for the whole show? Have you done any physical training for this...

speaker: Phanuel
content: Well, that's something for everyone to look forward to! What I can say is that Phanuel has worked very hard for the sake of my Cherubs!

speaker: Reporter B
content: Some netizens have called you out for never participating in songwriting, saying you're nothing more than a pretty face doing studio covers. Would you like to comment on this?

speaker: Phanuel
content: I can understand where they're coming from, and I'm sure they're saying that because they want to see Phanuel grow. I'll keep working hard and learning from my seniors!
Even through the tedium of it all, the reporters keep pushing, hungry for any scrap of Phanuel's attention. Then, a voice cuts through the noise, one that doesn't belong.

speaker: Chief
content: Are you aware of a phenomenon called the "Hollow Syndrome?"

speaker: Phanuel
content: Hmm?
The room goes quiet. The reporters exchange glances. But before they can redirect their attention to you, a figure steps in from the side of the stage and takes the microphone from Phanuel's hand.

speaker: Eliza
content: Apologies, allow me to answer this on Phanuel's behalf. This is something we've already been monitoring internally.

speaker: Eliza
content: I'm sure everyone here knows Phanuel very well. Should she find out something like this has been happening to her fans, she'd be devastated. We'd like to avoid having that affect her performance at the concert.

speaker: Eliza
content: Please rest assured. Mirrormoon Entertainment will offer what support and assistance we can in this matter, regardless of whether there's concrete evidence showing we are responsible. Further details will be announced through our official channels.

speaker: Eliza
content: If there are no further questions, that will be all for today's press conference. Thank you all for coming.

speaker: Phanuel
content: Oh... right! Thank you all so much! I've also bought all of you some refreshments! I hope you'll keep loving and supporting me in the future! Hope to see you all again soon!
Something about that line feels familiar... verbatim, even.

speaker: Chief
content: I have one more question about the concert. I'd like Phanuel to answer this one herself.

speaker: Chief
content: Regarding the special setlist prepared exclusively for this concert. Is there anything you can share with us?
Your question draws murmurs from the crowd. Phanuel, however, doesn't seem to notice the problem, picking up naturally where she left off.

speaker: Phanuel
content: Phanuel will reveal a little something: it's going to be something quite different from anything I've done before. We're incorporating a touch of classical music into the mix, so please look—

speaker: Eliza
content: This has already been addressed. Phanuel has other matters scheduled, so we must take our leave here. Thank you all.
Phanuel is whisked away immediately. Following such an abrupt ending, the reporters are now buzzing with questions.

speaker: FAC
content: Chief, they left through the back entrance by car.

speaker: Chief
content: Follow them. There's something I need to confirm still.

speaker: Chief
content: I assumed the manager was using Phanuel's schedule and work as a shield, that she believes we'd hold back with a crowd around. But maybe we're not the ones she's trying to keep out.
[Dressing Room]

speaker: Eliza
content: Don't worry, I've already taken care of it. We'll thoroughly review every article from today's press conference before they can get published.

speaker: Eliza
content: Any outlet that doesn't play ball won't be getting a seat at future interviews. They should know what to do if they truly want the exposure that comes with Phanuel.
The call has barely ended when Eliza's phone rings again.

speaker: Eliza
content: ...Held up in traffic? And? Do you expect me to go sort out the roads myself? Call another backup styling team yourself, unless you don't want this internship anymore.

speaker: Eliza
content: Make it quick. I'll go talk to the director and producer about a contingency plan. See if I can buy you some time for this mess.
Even as Eliza strides out, the other person in the dressing room simply sits in silence, script in hand, waiting to be made up.
Two, three minutes pass. Knock, knock.
A knock comes from outside the dressing room. The person inside doesn't move.
Knock, knock.
The knocking grows more urgent. An unfamiliar voice comes from the other side of the door.
Hello, is Phanuel in? I'm a special guest on today's show. Just wanted to stop by and say hi before we start filming.
Phanuel walks to the door and cracks it open. She studies the stranger carefully, then shakes her head.

speaker: Phanuel
content: I'm sorry, please contact my manager Eliza for any inquiries—Ah?!
Before the words are even out of her mouth, the visitor slips through the gap with practiced ease, then locks the room from the inside right as the door clicks shut.

speaker: Chief
content: Don't worry, I had someone contact your manager. She should be busy dealing with your unreliable styling team right now.

speaker: Phanuel
content: Who are you? ...W-What do you want?

speaker: Chief
content: We've met before, at the press conference. Though with all those camera flashes, it's no surprise you don't remember my face.

speaker: Phanuel
content: If you have something important to talk about, maybe we should wait for Eliza to come back first?
Panicked, she tries to unlock the door and flee, but you block her way.

speaker: Chief
content: So much for an angel who heals and saves her fans. Now that there's a Mania threat before you, is hiding behind your manager all you can do? Guess the idol persona really is all an act. Wonder how your Cherubs would feel if they knew.

speaker: Phanuel
content: Phanuel doesn't understand what you mean...

speaker: Chief
content: Then tell me, what are you without that script? What would you say? What do you know about the Hollow Syndrome?

speaker: Phanuel
content: Hollow... Syndrome? Phanuel doesn't understand what you're saying at all. If this isn't work-related, please leave. Eliza said I'm not allowed to talk to anyone outside of my schedule.

speaker: Chief
content: Really? Or is it that you're just afraid? What if I could make sure your manager never finds out?
The footsteps outside draw closer. This visit was put together last second, so you couldn't really keep Eliza occupied for long.

speaker: Chief
content: Answer me, Phanuel. In your own words. Is your schedule really so packed by your own choice? Every question you answered at that press conference, everything you said in front of the camera... Was any of it really your own words?
[Close-up: Phanuel, blank expression]

speaker: Phanuel
content: Yes. Those were all my own words. Because Phanuel has never said anything that isn't. Never. Because... Phanuel has never said anything else! Those were the only things Phanuel knows...

speaker: Phanuel
content: Right, the script...
She picks up the variety show script she dropped in the commotion earlier, and reads through it carefully. Every single line.

speaker: Phanuel
content: You're right. Phanuel does have a script for every single day. I don't think I've ever really thought about it... what would happen if Phanuel wasn't following a script...?
Bang. The dressing room door swings open.
[Post-Battle]

When Eliza enters, everything in the dressing room appears normal. Phanuel is still seated before the mirror, dutifully rehearsing her answers for the upcoming interview. And yet, something in the air has quietly shifted.
Eliza stands behind Phanuel, eyes fixed on her back. One second. Two seconds...

speaker: Eliza
content: Someone was here.
[Eastside Streets]
Using the busy backstage crew as cover, you've managed to slip out through a side entrance.

speaker: Chief
content: I need to cause a little commotion. Can you buy me some time?

speaker: FAC
content: Here at the TV station? You are aware that this is the center of the city's busiest part, right? Things could get out of hand.

speaker: Chief
content: That's exactly what I need. A huge crowd.
[TV Station]
Shortly after you've left, the variety show begins filming as scheduled. Eliza seems a little agitated, hovering by the monitor the whole time.

speaker: Host
content: Come say hello to our audience!

speaker: Phanuel
content: Hi everyone! I'm Phanuel. Very happy to be here today!
Through the monitor, Phanuel's smile looks the same as ever. But Eliza knows. Something Phanuel has been holding down with all her might has just been pried loose.

speaker: Phanuel
content: Do you... like balloons? They wear colorful little outfits, and they float up so, so high, and then... BANG!!!

speaker: Reporter A
content: Phanuel, why did you suddenly walk out of the variety show set? Please give us a statement!

speaker: Reporter B
content: An insider has reported that Phanuel appeared to be in a poor mental state during filming. Is there any truth to that?
Eliza pushes through the press with Phanuel in tow. Under security's cover, she shields Phanuel from the cameras while calling the company for a pickup.

speaker: Eliza
content: Now what? If the car isn't here in five minutes, don't bother coming in tomorrow.
The voice on the other end barely gets a word in before it gets swallowed up by a wave of screams.

speaker: Fan A
content: Phanuel! Oh my gosh, you're so tiny in person! Please look over here! Can you wish me a happy birthday?!

speaker: Fan B
content: Phanuel, I've always been a huge fan of you! Can I get your autograph?! Phanuel!

The crowd spills from the front steps of the TV station all the way to the curb. The area is packed wall-to-wall. It takes the security all they have just to open up a gap barely wide enough to squeeze through.
Phanuel edges through the gap, head lowered, not saying a word all the while. Clearly, her manager has given her some kind of warning. She doesn't respond to a single question.
Phanuel, can I get a photo with you?!

A gray figure takes advantage of the chaos to push to the front. They lurch sideways and slam into Eliza. She sidesteps on instinct, but in that split second, the reporters surge forward all at once and wedge themselves between her and Phanuel.
Before Phanuel can even register what's happening, a hand clamps around her wrist.
She struggles, trying to break free, until she sees who it is. Her eyes go wide.

speaker: Chief
content: Shh!

You pull her out, going against the tide of the crowd. Somewhere in that sea of people behind you, Eliza is still calling Phanuel's name, but her voice has been all but drowned by the screaming and shutter clicks.
[The street in summer]
Steam rises off the asphalt's surface under the blazing sun. Every car that passes stirs up a hot gust that sends the shimmering heat into a rippling swirl.
You lead Phanuel across a crosswalk, then hug the storefronts and turn into a side street before looping back to the main road. It's only then that you shake off every last reporter and fan.
Phanuel quietly follows you the whole way, always staying half a step behind you. Her hat and sunglasses are doing wonders, making the two of you look like just another pair of pedestrians.

speaker: Chief
content: You're not going to ask where we're headed? Are you really okay with this?

speaker: Phanuel
content: Phanuel knows you're doing this for good reason, and I'm always happy to go along with anything!

speaker: Chief
content: Has it never occurred to you that I could be one of the bad guys? For instance... I could sell your schedule to the fans for good money.

speaker: Phanuel
content: But you won't.

speaker: Chief
content: And what makes you so sure of that?

speaker: Phanuel
content: You haven't done anything bad to Phanuel. You're the one who made me see the script for what it was. So, I tried something different, and it felt great!

Even without a camera in sight, she nods along to her own words with a smile, as if giving herself a little pat on the back. Then, she turns to you, her gaze drifting past your shoulder toward a pair of passersby.
She sees two girls around her age, holding hands and sharing a single box of ice cream.

speaker: Chief
content: Did you have any friends before you became an idol?

speaker: Phanuel
content: I think so...? I can't remember.
Her voice drops a little. As the two girls disappear into the crowd, she lowers her gaze.

speaker: Chief
content: You can't... remember? Then what about your family? Your past? Why is everything blank on your public profile?

speaker: Phanuel
content: I can't remember... I just can't.

speaker: Phanuel
content: Eliza said Phanuel doesn't need any of that.

speaker: Chief
content: And what do you need, according to her?

speaker: Phanuel
content: Everything an idol needs. Phanuel practices hard every single day, you know.

speaker: Phanuel
content: Every day, I'd memorize scripts. I have an answer for every question, one that makes sure people would like me.

speaker: Phanuel
content: And I know. You're sharp. You figured that out at the press conference.

speaker: Chief
content: Have you never thought about doing something else? Something an idol doesn't "need," so to speak?

speaker: Phanuel
content: But Phanuel doesn't know what an idol doesn't need! I was born for this!

speaker: Chief
content: Is that also something Eliza told you?
She nods proudly. Then something catches her eye, and she bounces over. It's a billboard on the street, currently playing promotional material for her concert.

speaker: Chief
content: You sure trust Eliza a lot. Most artists wouldn't trust their managers this much.

speaker: Phanuel
content: Eliza needs me. I matter. She said I'm a natural beauty, a born star... We're going to put on the biggest concert ever and become the center of everything.
Should you call her naive? Ignorant? Or simply a masterful actress? You can't say for sure.
You continue onward; only now, your grip on her wrist has tightened. Your fingertips press against her pulse, searching for any irregularity, any crack in the facade.

Phanuel notices this as well. But she doesn't resist. Instead, she squeezes back with the same force, as if she's discovered some new game. Suddenly, a shriek rings out nearby, and you both look up at once.

Across the street, a few young fans have gathered around a Phanuel billboard and are taking photos together. They strike poses with their light sticks, completely oblivious to the fact that the very person on that billboard is standing right across from them, separated only by a crosswalk and the steady flow of passing cars.

Phanuel stands at the edge of the shade, eyes fixed on them behind the sunglasses. She watches as they cheer and scream for her. Watches as they raise their phones toward the glowing billboard, their faces glowing with pure, unadulterated joy.

speaker: Chief
content: Why do you trust me so much anyway? It's not like I'm Eliza.
Phanuel's gaze remains on the fans, but she leans slightly closer to you.

speaker: Phanuel
content: Because you said something to me that no one else ever had. Just like Eliza did. She's the only one who ever told me that I was born for the stage, that I could have everyone's love and admiration.

speaker: Phanuel
content: Seems to me that you both care about me a lot.
Heartbeat steady. No irregularities. She speaks of you and Eliza the way one might of family or close friends, even though she's long forgotten the concept of either.

speaker: Chief
content: Since you trust me, I have one more question.
You come to an abrupt stop at a traffic light.

speaker: Chief
content: ...A month ago, around the time the BR-003 Observation Hub was attacked. What were you doing?
The red light counts down, second by second. The flickering numbers wash over Phanuel's face. Thirty. Twenty-nine. Twenty-eight...

speaker: Phanuel
content: I don't remember. Eliza plans everything for me. But I'm pretty sure whatever I was doing is public. You could just check my fans' posts. Why?

speaker: Chief
content: A big star who personally keeps up with her fans' posts...? Do you care a lot about them?

speaker: Phanuel
content: Yes! They write letters to Phanuel, cheer for me, and call out my name. I feel every bit of it.

speaker: Chief
content: Then, let's say your fans were being threatened and hurt right now, would you want to do something about it?

speaker: Phanuel
content: Of course!

speaker: Chief
content: And what if helping those Cherubs meant going up against Eliza?
The countdown passes its halfway point. Cars begin pulling to a stop in front of you, one by one.

speaker: Phanuel
content: I... No. There has to be some kind of misunderstanding...

speaker: Chief
content: Does this sound familiar to you—a fan smiles with pure bliss the moment they see you, then loses consciousness right after?

speaker: Phanuel
content: ...I'm not sure.

speaker: Chief
content: What do you mean, you're not sure?

speaker: Phanuel
content: I'm not sure what kind of smile you mean. Everyone smiles at every single one of Phanuel's shows. I don't understand why you'd call that a sickness...

speaker: Chief
content: Have you ever done something that felt normal at the time, but feels a little off now that you look back at it?

speaker: Phanuel
content: Eliza said it was all for my own good.

speaker: Chief
content: Just answer yes or no.

speaker: Phanuel
content: Yes...
Looks like she's not used to you being so serious.

speaker: Chief
content: Did you ever ask Eliza why she had you do those things?

speaker: Phanuel
content: No.

speaker: Chief
content: Have you ever considered that maybe Eliza has some kind of ulterior motive?

speaker: Phanuel
content: Yes.

speaker: Chief
content: Ever come across something that might be a clue, then?

speaker: Phanuel
content: Eliza always meets with someone at night to report things about me, saying things I can't understand.

speaker: Phanuel
content: And no one's ever allowed near her office... Do these count?
The countdown ends. The red light shifts to green, just as usual. The crowd moves on. Only the two of you remain in place.

Phanuel tilts her head, unsure what's gotten into you. Then, she gives your hand a little shake. When you still don't respond, she doesn't push it. She glances to the side, just in time to see a group of fans who've finished taking their photos, now walking toward you.

Unlike most celebrities, she doesn't seem concerned about being recognized. If anything, it's like she wants it to happen. Those Cherubs seem to form a pure utopia, with Phanuel being the only thing in that world. Even the star herself is caught up in their excitement.

speaker: Chief
content: What if those people all collapsed the next moment, smiles frozen on their faces forever, lost to the Hollow Syndrome? What would you do?

speaker: Phanuel
content: I don't know...

speaker: Chief
content: Stop with those scripted answers. Tell me what you think.

speaker: Phanuel
content: What "I" think...? I... I don't know...
