Catching the hint behind Mira's words, the thief stops struggling and turns to question her.

speaker: Thief
content: What do you mean?

speaker: Mira
content: The sheriff will likely detain them for two days. We still have time. If we go to my acquaintance now, we should be able to make a passable replica of the jar.

speaker: Thief
content: ...Wait, why are you being so nice? We don't know each other. Why are you helping me?

speaker: Mira
content: Perhaps... because I see my past in you. I once stole from others to survive, and did even worse things. So I somewhat understand your struggles.

speaker: Mira
content: Breaking the jar is partly my fault. Everyone makes mistakes. By helping you now, maybe someone will help me when I'm in trouble.
Yingying

speaker: Mira
content: So, think you can trust me?

speaker: Thief
content: ...As if I have other options! Lead the way.
Near the motel's back door, amidst the choking smoke, the thief stares at the stove and person in chef's clothes in silent shock.

speaker: Thief
content: So you make counterfeits right under people's noses?! And... he's the "acquaintance" you mentioned???

speaker: Chef
content: Cooking and pottery both involve fire. It's not that different. What are you staring at? Never seen a chef before? If you don't want me to do it, that's fine with me.

speaker: Thief
content: No, no, that's not what I meant...

speaker: Mira
content: It's alright, he's an outsider who doesn't know the rules here. Don't be hard on him. We're here to see you because we really need your help.
After listening to the two explain their plan and describe the original appearance of the jar, the chef pats his chest and agrees.

speaker: Chef
content: No problem. Twenty-five thousand DisCoins, and I'll make an identical one in five days.

speaker: Thief
content: Five days? That's too long! Can you please hurry... we need it in two days.

speaker: Chef
content: Sure, the more money, the faster. Fifty thousand DisCoins for two days.

speaker: Thief
content: What the hell! You can't just double the price like that! This is highway robbery!

speaker: Chef
content: Don't want to pay with DisCoins? If you can pay in Hypercubes, that's fine too.
Seeing the conflict about to escalate into a physical altercation, Mira quickly steps in to ease the tension.

speaker: Mira
content: Both of you, calm down. Let's talk about it nicely, okay?

speaker: Mira
content: I also share some responsibility in this matter. How about we negotiate a price that works for both of you, and I'll cover half of it?

speaker: Mira
content: I know making pottery is hard work, but fifty thousand is indeed a bit too expensive. Considering how long we've known each other, can you give us a discount? How about twenty thousand?

speaker: Chef
content: I can give you a discount, but with what you're asking for, I can't even break even. You should be fair, ma'am.

speaker: Mira
content: Then, can you do it for us half-price? Twenty-five thousand? Please.

speaker: Chef
content: ...Tsk, alright. For you, I'll take this loss. Come pick it up tomorrow. Mira, you owe me one.

speaker: Chef
content: Hey kid. She bargained so hard for you. Don't tell me you can't even cough up half of twenty-five thousand.

speaker: Mira
content: Sorry, this is the lowest price I can get for us. Are you okay with it?
The thief reluctantly reaches into his pockets and gathers just enough money to cover his share.
After handing over the DisCoins to the pottery-making chef, Mira smiles gently at the worried thief.

speaker: Mira
content: Don't worry. There won't be any problems. With my help, you'll definitely get through this.

speaker: Thief
content: ...Will everything really be okay?
The chef kept his promise. Early next morning, he confidently hands over the finished product.
To say there are discrepancies from the original would be an understatement. The replica looks like a completely different jar. On closer inspection, it even looks more like a thermos.

speaker: Thief
content: I mean, this is definitely not okay!

speaker: Mira
content: You can still tell it's a jar... just requires a bit of imagination. Well, it's too late to redo it now. When the merchant returns, we'll just have to make do with what we have.
The chef's product makes it hard for Mira to conceal her worries. She packs this comically shaped replica back into the original bag.
Just as she finishes packing, the disheveled merchant barges into the motel, slamming the wooden door behind him.

speaker: Merchant
content: Is the innkeeper here? I need to see the innkeeper!!

speaker: Mira
content: Welcome back, sir... Oh my, it's only been a day. How did you end up like this?

speaker: Merchant
content: Don't get me started on it. That conman said everyone in his family has a missing tooth, and wanted to knock out my tooth too! He was impossible to reason with. A total lunatic!

speaker: Merchant
content: Luckily, I had some cash on me, and that sheriff was easy to deal with. He took the money and let me out. Otherwise, who knows how long I'd be stuck in that lousy detention center!

speaker: Merchant
content: Where's my bag with the antique? Oh, it's right here...
At this moment, the still-swaying motel door gets slammed open a second time.

speaker: Sheriff
content: Hey! Why are you still here? That drunk "father" of yours realized you escaped from detention and is on his way here! I couldn't stop him!

speaker: Merchant
content: What?!

speaker: Drunkard
content: Ahhhh my son... I'm gonna knock out your tooth to bring you back into the fold! Daddy will be quick about it!

As soon as the sheriff finishes speaking, bloodcurdling shrieks can be heard from outside, getting closer and closer. The merchant's face turns livid. He grabs the bag without checking and rushes out of the motel.

speaker: Mira
content: Good. He didn't notice the jar was swapped. You should quickly...
She stops mid-sentence. Mira's reminder is unnecessary, as the thief had already slipped away amidst the chaos.
The shrieks gradually fade away, and the dust stirred by all the running settles down. The chef leisurely walks out from the kitchen, exchanging glances with the sheriff and innkeeper.
After sending off all the guests, the motel returns to its usual quietness, with only the dilapidated wooden door creaking.
Clap! A crisp hand clap breaks the silence.

speaker: Mira
content: Alright, that's a wrap. It's just us now. We can stop acting.
Mira rubs her cheeks, stiff from smiling for two days straight. As she looks at the other two, the stagnant atmosphere becomes abuzz with knowing laughter.

speaker: Sheriff
content: ...Hahaha, all that acting left me parched. Anything to drink, Mira? With ice, please!
The sheriff drops his imposing demeanor and fans himself with his hat as he lazily leans back on a chair.

speaker: Mira
content: You can have your drink, but let's talk about the door first. How many times have I told you, push the door gently when you enter! If this keeps up, the door will break, and you'll have to pay for it!

speaker: Sheriff
content: Yeah yeah... Thanks to that merchant's bribe, I can pay for ten doors.

speaker: Chef
content: Here, Mira, this is your money back to you. Get me a drink too. The usual, please.

speaker: Mira
content: Where did you find such a hideous jar? I didn't even know how to keep up with the act!

speaker: Chef
content: That's what jars for pickling meat look like! I've used it for several years now. It's practically an antique!
As they joke and banter, Mira brings out a tray and hands drinks to each of them.

speaker: Mira
content: Everything's fine on the other side?

speaker: Sheriff
content: I told him to drive that merchant as far away as possible. He really worked hard on his "lunatic dad" act the past two days. When he comes back, we'll treat him to a good meal.

speaker: Chef
content: Absolutely! We must celebrate! It's just a pity about that jar. If we didn't have to smash it, we could've made more money. Maybe it really was an antique.

speaker: Mira
content: Oh, who said we smashed it? Look here...
The innkeeper grins slyly. She points to a new cactus plant in an inconspicuous corner of the counter. The pot looks oddly familiar... it's the merchant's jar!

speaker: Mira
content: That merchant might be dumb, but he has good taste. This jar can genuinely fetch a good price.

speaker: Mira
content: If we add together Wright's bribe, the replica money, and this jar... we made triple the profit from one job!

speaker: Chef
content: Impressive! You have the sharpest eye and wit in town.

speaker: Sheriff
content: Alas, the student surpasses the teacher! We really are getting old.

speaker: Mira
content: Thanks for the compliment, but you still need to pay what you owe me. Wright, check the time. Korryn should be arriving soon.

speaker: Sheriff
content: Alright, alright. Pour me another drink. Once I finish it, I'll go get ready with little Timmy.
Sheriff Wright stretches lazily, puts his hat back on and goes to the door to greet the new guest. Behind him, Mira swiftly rearranges the tableware, her smiling eyes hiding a shifty sparkle.
..."Tuco"?
A girl's gasp echoes from the entrance. The new guest has arrived.

speaker: Mira
content: Let's see how much meat we can carve off this plump little lamb.
On an empty counter in the Tuco Palace lies a note. Seems like someone wrote it and placed it there in secret.

Tuco's food sucks and the weather's crap, but for some reason, I quite like it here. Maybe... it's because it reminds me of the old Syndicate?

The wind, the car races, and the sand that gets into your mouth from all the laughter...
Dazzle everyone with a mind-blowing hero's entrance!

Thinking about it now, those lines are pretty cool... of course, that swindler Korryn probably just made them up on the spot!

Though I only spent three days here, I learned a ton of stuff I'd never even heard of—mostly shady tricks, but some are quite useful.

For example, the yummiest part of a sandworm, or how to stroke sand foxes so they don't freak out... It might be useless trivia I'll never use, but who knows, right?!

Anyway, thanks a lot, guys! See you around!
The Legion's convoy drives deep into WhiteSands. The Syndicate girl curls up in the backseat, already dreaming.
A diary lies open on her lap, covered in scribbles and corrections, yet each word is written with utmost seriousness.

To <color=#fb9259>${PlayerName}</color>:

Hey big dummy! You're always nagging me, but when I finally call, you don't pick up? Hmph, do you even know how much fun you missed out on?!

I'll let you in on a secret: not only did I survive three days alone in WhiteSands, but I also fought off loads of desert bandits and Nirvana lackeys! Big hero Hella saved an entire village all by herself!

Actually, saying that I did it all by myself isn't quite right. The townsfolk helped me a lot! Even though they come off as kinda weird, they're actually quite decent people!
Of course, it'd be better if they tricked me a bit less!

By the way, didn't you say that if I got stronger, you'd praise me?
And Hecate too! Both of you have to praise me!

Just wait, when I return as a hero, I'll be stronger than anyone from the Legion, the city council, or Paradeisos! By then, with me watching your backs, let's see who in DisCity dares to mess with us!

Alright, this letter's about done. Horo and I are still on the road. Any more writing and I'll get carsick.
When I go back home, I'll tell you all about this one!

From the cutest, most awesome super girl in the world,
<color=#fb9259>Hella</color>

<color=#FDF9BA><i>Under the eternal Golden Rose,

you must now take this oath:</color>
Ah!!!
Yes, I swear.
Do you hereby swear that you will do everything in your power to carry forward the guidance of your great predecessors and never dishonor the glory bestowed upon your shoulders?
Yes, I will be true to my word and deed, never forgetting the compassion and justice in my heart.
Finally, do you swear before the Golden Rose that no matter the hardship, whatever the cost, you will never abandon your duty or betray your oath?
Even if...
the price is everything you hold dear?
The girl opens her eyes.
Sunlight pours through the wide window, cutting the room cleanly in half.
She stands beside the operation station. Liquid metal flows silently before her, gradually separating, merging, and realigning until it forms an integrated spiral.

Following her movements, the spiral continues to extend, assembling into an intricate yet elegant structure. The finely layered metal constructs itself tier by tier, reflecting scattered points of light.
[1 second pause, communication stone sound effect plays - use a sound similar to Schorl, not electronic]
The metal's growth halts. The girl looks toward the communicator on the other side of the room, takes a deep breath, and answers the call.
Routine report No. 8.

The latest shielding device is almost ready for deployment. Currently, material consumption remains higher than projected. We need to continue gathering data to complete the final optimization. However...
The girl breathes in deeply, slowly clenching her fist until her fingertips dig into her palm. Light streams through the floor-to-ceiling window, but fails to reach where she stands.
Regarding the calamity beyond the city walls... <color=#fb9259>That thing</color> has been acting up more and more frequently.

DisCity continues to restrict Hypercube exports, and now there are many injured people within our city. Our equipment and supplies aren't sufficient for long-term resistance against it. If we could secure support from the family, our progress would certainly be more promising. Besides, things in DisCity...

speaker: Stern Voice
content: Hypatia.
The girl is interrupted. She lifts her head as a cold light pulses from the top of the communicator before her.

speaker: Stern Voice
content: Just focus on what you should be doing. Don't forget the true purpose of our Aurum Secretum research.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...Yes, I understand.
The communication crystal flashes a few more times before going completely out. The room falls silent, leaving only the sound of the girl's suppressed breathing.

Metal components awaiting adjustment lie abandoned on the operation station. Hypatia walks to the window, her gaze sweeping across the town below before fixing on the pitch-black storm gradually approaching from the distance.
Black sand fills the sky as Mania howls through the wind, swallowing every existence caught in its path. It looms overhead like an eternal curtain of chaos, never to withdraw.
Still...
Suddenly, an incongruous bright spot appears in the darkness.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Huh? What is that...
At the center of the storm, the tiny spot of light grows increasingly visible, drawing closer and closer, and then...
[Screen shakes with white flash][Background: WhiteSands Storm]
Bang! A battered vehicle bursts out of the storm, followed by piercing screams. The girl chasing desperately behind the car grimaces in terror, her shrieks cutting through the air.

speaker: Hella
content: Wait! Wait for me! LET ME GET ON FIRST!!!
Sand howls and engine roars.

The Legion's vehicle belts ahead with a vroom at full speed, its body covered in scratches and its roof completely torn off. Passengers who should have been distributed across several vehicles are now crammed into this battle-damaged transport.
Someone in the car leans out dangerously to shout at the girl sprinting desperately behind.

speaker: Legion Member
content: Hella, faster! That thing behind you is literally gonna bite your ass!

speaker: Hella
content: HELP HELP HELP! Cut the crap and just pull me up already! Arghhhh—!!!!
Hella's legs pump like pistons until finally, with one desperate leap, she grabs the outstretched hand and gets yanked aboard shakily.

speaker: Horo
content: Everyone hold tight, I'm speeding up!

The next instant, the vehicle swerves sharply around a broken rock, nearly throwing Hella off the edge where she's perched. But the turn also gives her a perfect view of their pursuer in all its terrifying glory.

Behind them, sand and Mania have fused into an impenetrable darkness that hugs the ground, advancing with overwhelming force. Countless tiny, razor-sharp debris swirls within the massive storm, transforming it into a colossal meat grinder racing forward at over a hundred miles per hour.

This is no ordinary sandstorm. What swirls within the wind isn't sand, but tiny metal-like fragments, attracted and linked together by Mania, dancing to form a sky-darkening <color=#fb9259>black magnetic sandstorm</color> that swallows everything caught in its path.

speaker: Horo
content: Something's wrong. We've been moving sideways. We should've escaped its path by now, unless...
Visibility on the sides of the car plummets as the black sand closes in on the Legion.

speaker: Horo
content: Damn it! The storm is tracking our movements. It's <color=#fb9259>hunting us down</color>!

A massive rock hurtles past, missing Hella's head by inches before smashing the Legion vehicle's side mirror. Within seconds, metal fragments in the hurricane behind them shred the rock to pieces, reducing it to dust that blends into the raging storm.

speaker: Hella
content: NOOO! I didn't survive all those scammers and desert bandits only to die here... Ninety-Nine, Hecate, dummy ${PlayerName}, anybody—help me! I swear I'll never steal anything ever again, waaaaaah...

Debris from the storm hammers against the vehicle, stripping away patches of paint. The fragments strike with an eerie rhythm, forming whispers that penetrate Hella's ears, compelling her to look back. When she does, she hears a deeper drone from behind them.

speaker: Hella
content: What's that sound? What is... that?

speaker: Whispers in the Storm
content: Stay...
The entire vehicle strains forward in a desperate attempt to break free. Only Hella is looking back, witnessing the dense black shadow lurking at the heart of the magnetic storm.

speaker: Whispers in the Storm
content: Stay... Stay here... with us...!
With a piercing shriek, a massive boulder comes hurling through the air, flying straight toward Horo in the driver's seat!

speaker: Hella
content: Horo! Watch out—ugh!
Hella collapses limply on top of Horo. She's pushed Horo away, but couldn't dodge the boulder herself.

speaker: Horo
content: Hella?! ...Damn it!
She has no time to check on Hella and slams down on the accelerator. The engine lets out a dying roar, but that dark shadow is still slowly closing in on their vehicle.

Sunlight vanishes behind the swirling dust, plunging everything into darkness. Contamination grows thicker, distorting vision with dancing spots. The tapping sounds transform from whispers into piercing shrieks that stab painfully at the eardrums. Until...
[Transition, add a resonating sound effect of Aurum Secretum activation]

The heavy darkness is cut open, and light suddenly bursts forth. Into view comes a massive metal device of bizarre design. Mounted at the center of a small sand boat, it radiates a soft golden glow that drives back both the storm and contamination.
Several figures in black robes operate the device, their faces impossible to discern. They rotate the instrument, aiming it directly at the dark shadow at the center of the magnetic storm...
[Still frame, Aurum Secretum activation sound effect + monster roaring sound effect, possibly with the monster shadow portrait shaking]
[Still frame, Aurum Secretum activation sound effect + monster roaring sound effect, possibly with the monster shadow portrait shaking]
The metal device pulses with faint light, establishing a defensive line that shields against the Mania.

The hurricane howls around them. Horo can't make out what the strangers are shouting, but she can see their hand gestures. They're signaling for the Legion's vehicle to follow them, but... they seem to be heading deeper into the storm.
Horo grits her teeth and stamps her foot, then slams down on the accelerator to follow them, trailing the small sand boat into a narrow crevice at the base of the rock face.
[Background: Underground Tunnel]
As they enter the tunnel, the storm finally stops.
The raging black sand cannot reach inside this tunnel. The passage stretches deep into darkness, mysterious and chilly.
...But regardless, the storm has stopped. Only now can Horo spare the energy to check on the wounded on board.

speaker: Horo
content: Where's Hella? How is she?

speaker: Legion Member
content: Her injuries aren't serious, but she hasn't regained consciousness yet. She'll probably need a bit more time to come around.

speaker: Horo
content: ...Alright. What about the others?
In truth, everyone has sustained injuries to varying degrees. But the wounded simply wave their hands dismissively, indicating they are fine.

In the distance, the sand boat gradually comes to a stop. The black-robed figures onboard huddle together, muttering unintelligibly among themselves. They repeatedly glance toward the Legion's vehicle, yet cautiously avoid approaching immediately.
[Flashback][Background: WhiteSands Storm]

This mysterious group isn't made up of fighters. Their combat abilities and tactical awareness are only average, but that strange metal device of theirs can resist Mania almost as well as Hypercubes do.
Furthermore, that black magnetic sandstorm out there was also extremely unusual.
Unlike any sandstorm the Legion had previously encountered, it didn't simply sweep in one direction, but seemed to have locked onto the Legion, pursuing them relentlessly.
...Could this extraordinary phenomenon be connected to the <color=#fb9259>inheritance</color>?
[Flashback][Background: WhiteSands Market]

This photograph was recovered from the wreckage of a WhiteSands merchant caravan. The place was already wrecked when the Legion arrived. Horo discovered a bloodstained envelope hidden in a secret compartment among the cargo, which contained this photograph.
The origin of the inheritance picture was still unknown, so the Legion could only follow the caravan's trail, hoping to trace its source...
Eventually, their destination pointed to the outskirts of Fraser, a small settlement so obscure it wasn't even marked on any maps.
[Background: Underground Tunnel]
...Perhaps what she's been searching for all this time is right here.

Meanwhile, the robed figures seem to have finished their discussion, and one of them approaches the Legion's vehicle. He speaks at length, but Horo can't understand a single word. It's the dialect of a foreign race from WhiteSands.
The leader frowns and says a few more sentences. He points at the unconscious Hella in the vehicle, his tone becoming serious as murmurs of agitation spread through the crowd behind him.

Horo shifts slightly to shield Hella from view. Outland groups in WhiteSands don't all share the same attitude toward DisCity. Before any formal negotiations, she needs to determine where these people stand, and then...
[Transition for 1s, subtle sound effect of Hella waking up]
A weak groan comes from behind. Horo immediately senses trouble, but by the time she turns around, it's already too late.

speaker: Hella
content: Oww, my head's spinning... Where the heck did that storm blow us to...?
Hella groggily pulls herself up, only to find herself caught between two groups staring at her with completely different expressions.
Horo's face contorts in dismay, while the young man's expression darkens the instant he hears the Disian words, and he immediately grabs his weapon.

speaker: Hella
content: Oh no, don't tell me I've messed up again...?
The robed figures erupt into chaos, shouting in their unintelligible language as they charge forward.

speaker: Leading Youth
content: You're from DisCity! Spies! Take this!
Some hotheads in the Legion try to rise to their feet, but Horo forcefully holds them down.

The situation is still unclear. The inheritance is missing, and we still need to investigate their new weapons. This isn't the time for conflict. We can't all be captured—at least one of us needs to remain free...
...Someone who can infiltrate the enemy camp and gain their acceptance.
With a swift motion, Horo grabs Hella and shoves her off the vehicle, sending her tumbling directly into the group of robed figures behind.

speaker: Horo
content: Useless trash! Always running your mouth and ruining our plans! Should've sold you to DisCity a long time ago!
Their eyes meet, and Hella immediately understands Horo's plan.

speaker: Hella
content: You, ugh, shut it, you filthy human trafficker! She forced me into all this! Please help me...
After a chaotic struggle, the robed figures finally subdues the Legion.

They search through everything in the vehicle, not sparing even the Legionnaires' personal belongings. Finding no concrete evidence of espionage, the young man eyes them suspiciously before finally waving his hand, ordering them to be detained for the time being.
As for Hella, who rebelled against her companions...

The leading young man approaches Hella and speaks, but the stream of unintelligible sounds only results in a bewildered expression on Hella's face. Scratching his head, the youth opens his mouth again, now speaking in Disian with a peculiar accent.

speaker: Leading Youth
content: My words, do you understand? Are you with them?

speaker: Hella
content: No no no! I, I was kidnapped by them! Absolutely not with them! They, bad! Me, good!
The youth translates Hella's words to his companions, triggering another wave of collective outrage.

speaker: Leading Youth
content: So, they tricked you into coming with them... Do you know where your home is? Do you have somewhere to go back to?

speaker: Hella
content: Uh, a-am I supposed to have one...?
Hella steals a glance at Horo, who shakes her head in response.

speaker: Hella
content: ...No, I don't anymore! They were planning to sell me to some unknown town real far away. I don't remember the way back. Even if I wanted to return, I couldn't anymore...
After hearing this, the youth glares at the Legionnaires with righteous fury, then pulls Hella protectively to his side.

speaker: Leading Youth
content: Hmph, bastards from DisCity! Don't worry, you're safe now.

speaker: Leading Youth
content: Come on! You can come home with us!

speaker: Hella
content: Haha, haha... Thank you all so much...
The suspicious spies get tied up while Hella, the damsel in distress, receives an enthusiastic welcome as they escort her deeper into the passage.
She looks back discreetly, making eye contact with her crew. Though her eyes are filled with panic, she still manages to give them a stiff thumbs up while silently mouthing some words.

speaker: Hella
content: ...D-don't worry, I'll definitely find a way to rescue you all!
As they continue forward, the bright spot at the tunnel's end keeps growing in size. Emerging suddenly from the darkness, Hella's eyes can barely stay open against the piercing brightness...
[White screen transition]
When Hella opens her eyes, the first things she sees are beams of light cascading from above, and at the edge of her vision, a figure with an overwhelming presence.
[CG - Figure by the Window A]
From above, a figure stands bathed in radiance. Her silhouette is swallowed by the blinding light, making her appear hazy.

speaker: Hella
content: Hmm...?

speaker: Hella
content: Someone's standing by the window. Who is it...?
From a distance, Hella seems to lock eyes with the figure. She can't make out her face, only catching glimpses of flowing robes and long golden hair cascading down her back.
The figure by the window appears to notice Hella too. She turns her head, seemingly about to say something to Hella.
But her voice is still blurred out by the distance, dissolving into the light.
After another blink, the figure by the window has vanished. Hella rubs her eyes vigorously, and the dizziness finally subsides as her vision returns to normal.
And before her stretches a scene entirely different from what she witnessed moments ago.

Before her is a city that seems to have emerged from rock rifts. Winding paths spiral throughout, with crooked cave dwellings embedded haphazardly on the rock faces, their entrances extending outward into a collection of tents.
People move through this seemingly chaotic yet somehow orderly space, chattering away in a WhiteSands dialect that Hella can barely understand.

speaker: Hella
content: ...What is this place?
The young boy walks up to Hella, spreading his arms with a grin as he proudly announces.

speaker: Taric
content: Welcome to the safest place in all of WhiteSands, <color=#fb9259>Furor</color>, the city born out of rock rifts!

The black-robed figures remove their hoods, revealing kind, unassuming faces. They exchange greetings with townsfolk passing by, then gently nudge Hella forward while continuing their enthusiastic chatter in words she can't understand.

speaker: Taric
content: Old Rosse, over here! I'm back! Did you miss your dear Taric, old man?

The dark-skinned youth's voice booms across the distance, catching the attention of a man over ten meters away. The severe-looking man strides quickly toward them and promptly seizes the boy by his ear!

speaker: Rosse
content: ...Miss you? As if! You troublemaker, this is our last sand boat. If you wreck it, where are we supposed to get another one, huh?
After finally releasing his grip, the stern-faced man turns to Hella, his gaze piercing.

speaker: Hella
content: He-hello...?
The man's brow furrows, sending Hella into a state of panic. Her mind races desperately for something to say. Is her cover about to be blown?

speaker: Taric
content: We just rescued this girl from the DisCity traffickers! She only understands the common tongue. They probably kidnapped her from somewhere near DisCity, and now she can't get back home. Poor thing!
The crowd gathered nearby falls silent for a few seconds. In the next instant, all the Furorians are swarming around Hella.

speaker: Angry Townie
content: Those ******* bastards! Have they no shame, getting into this kind of dirty trade?!

speaker: Kind Townie
content: Are you hurt? Poor child, look how they've starved you... Where are you from, honey? How did you end up captured by the DisCity people?
Their speech is a mixture of WhiteSands dialect and heavily-accented Disian. Concerned that Hella may not understand, they slow down deliberately, carefully enunciating each word.
Though Hella still can't understand much, the concern on their faces seems genuine. Glancing over at Taric, she catches him giving her a thumbs up with an encouraging look.
But... she can't mention DisCity or the MBCC, and she needs these people to believe her. What kind of false identity should she make up? As Hella ponders this, inspiration strikes.

speaker: Hella
content: M-my name is Hella, and I used to live in a place called... uh, Tuco!
As they say, the first step is always the hardest.

The lies come more and more easily as Hella continues, her voice breaking with tears as she describes how Tuco went from a prosperous town into a barren wasteland, recounting a perfect tearjerker about a poor kidnapped child.

speaker: Hella
content: It was just a tiny town not far from DisCity, but life was decent enough. Then disasters got worse and Hypercubes became too expensive. When we couldn't pay our debts, those DisCity thugs kidnapped all of us to sell for profit...

speaker: Hella
content: Sob... Thank you all so much. If you hadn't saved me, who knows where they would have sold me off to...
Her performance is so convincing that all the townspeople listen with bitter indignation.

speaker: Taric
content: Hmph, told you there's not a decent soul in DisCity! Someone who ran away to that place told me they even detonated massive bombs called Black Rings in the city! For all we know, they might even be behind all these disasters everywhere—owww—!
A hand grabs Taric by the ear and yanks him away.

speaker: Rosse
content: Don't listen to his nonsense. Here, have some candy.

The man produces some coarse brown sugar wrapped in a wrinkled piece of oilpaper. The sugar lumps have been broken into irregular small pieces, nothing like the refined candies from DisCity, but his careful handling suggests it's a precious commodity here.

speaker: Rosse
content: Merchants don't pass through here, so our town has nothing proper to offer as a welcome gift. Still, we'll have no problem taking care of one more kid.
Huh? She recalls the maps she's seen from Horo. This place isn't that far from the trade routes... Could it be because of that strange magnetic storm outside?
Remembering her intel-gathering mission, Hella's eyes dart cunningly as she rubs them and makes her voice sound even more pitiful and distressed.

speaker: Hella
content: I've never seen anything like that sandstorm out there. It was chasing after us and was even making strange noises... Have the sandstorms around here always been like this?
The Furorians exchange glances with each other and sigh.

speaker: Taric
content: I suppose so. Those DisCity folks were foolish enough to charge right into it. It was a suicidal move.

speaker: Hella
content: What happened to the Legion... I mean, those guys from DisCity? Where did they go? Will they come back to do more bad things?

speaker: Taric
content: Those guys? They were probably taken underground. There's a special place down there where bad people get locked up.
Hella peers around, trying to spot the underground place Taric mentioned, when she feels a weight on her head. Taric ruffles her hair and leads her toward the town center.

speaker: Taric
content: Don't worry! You're one of us now. Those DisCity thugs won't ever get to hurt you again!

speaker: Taric
content: This is Granny Nysa, the best doctor you can ever find. You can go to her with any health problems. And that's Old Rosse—don't mind his grumpy face. Most of the caverns here were in fact designed by him. He's among the coolest guys in Furor!

speaker: Taric
content: And there's little curly-haired Zade over there, always waving those raggedy cards around. Feel free to mess with him a bit if you ever find yourself bored. Promise you it's fun!
In Hella's eyes, those are merely some cards printed with colorful patterns, nothing like the real stuff she's seen before.

speaker: Zade
content: Stop laughing! And they're not raggedy! These are real tarot cards and they're very valuable!

Eager to prove his fortune-telling skills, Zade pulls a card from his deck. It shows a crude drawing of something tall and skinny with an indistinguishable shape. Zade explains that this is a symbol of... um, possibly a long loaf of bread?

speaker: Hella
content: Pfft... Hahaha!

speaker: Hella
content: Oh right, I saw someone earlier standing by a window up there. She seemed different from everyone else. Is she a Furorian too?

speaker: Taric
content: Oh! You're talking about Hypatia from the lab!

speaker: Hella
content: ...Who's that?
At the mention of Hypatia's name, Zade immediately rushes over, throwing his arms up and stretching them wide to form an enormous circle.

speaker: Zade
content: Hypatia always comes down to play with us, and she brings me snacks every time. She's the most super-duper nicest person ever!

speaker: Granny Nysa
content: Indeed, she helped us build our town and kept us fed. If it weren't for the <color=#fb9259>Campbells</color>, Furor might still be nothing more than a shabby shelter today...
Campbell...? Are they talking about that girl?

Looking around, the town definitely has facilities with technology far beyond what you'd expect from a small settlement. Equipment of such caliber and quality is not seen in just any small town in WhiteSands.

speaker: Hella
content: She doesn't even look much older than me... Is she really that remarkable?

speaker: Taric
content: Of course! I mean, look!
Taric guides Hella to look up. At the top of Furor, an irregular circle of rocks seems to hang in the sky.

Looking closer, there seems to be something in the air that briefly illuminates when struck, forming a network of glittering points. Outside, the storm continues to rage, darkening the sky, yet unable to reach the city.

speaker: Hella
content: Not Hypercubes... Never seen anything like that even in DisCity! How did you guys pull that off?!

speaker: Taric
content: Hmph, with our great Lady Campbell here, what can possibly stop us?

speaker: Taric
content: She's the one who brought <color=#fb9259>Aurum Secretum</color> from Fraser, which blocks Mania and contamination. You can basically take a stroll outside during a storm with it! Even without Hypercubes, Furor stands strong thanks to this barrier...

speaker: Taric
content: With her around, this is the safest place in all of WhiteSands!

speaker: Hella
content: Aurum Secretum?
Taric continues talking enthusiastically, but Hella's attention has already been caught by something else he mentioned.
<color=#fb9259>Aurum Secretum</color>... It was probably what saved us. If this stuff is really that powerful, then...

speaker: Hella
content: Ahem, so what does this Aurum something look like anyway? Can we use it too?
Taric thumps his own chest proudly and runs back to the sand boat they arrived on, unloading an oddly shaped metal device from the cabin.
He presses something on the device, and with a soft humming sound, it slowly rotates and unfolds, emitting the same fluorescent glow as the barrier.

speaker: Hella
content: Whoa? It's actually the real deal...

Ideas start popping into her head. The Aurum Secretum's right here, should I make a move now? No, no, no, too many pairs of eyes. I still need to find a way to rescue Horo... But if I miss this chance, who knows when I'll get my hands on this precious stuff again...

speaker: Taric
content: Though production is still low now, someday it'll replace Hypercubes throughout WhiteSands, and then we won't have to fear DisCity attacking us again! With Aurum Secretum in our hands, who knows, we might even beat them!
...Attack again?

speaker: Hella
content: Wait, what do you mean DisCity attacking <color=#fb9259>again</color>...?
[Transition for 2s, attack sound effects, screen shakes]
The city's alarm suddenly goes off.

speaker: Hella
content: ?! Oh crap, don't tell me someone's actually attacking??
...No, that's not it. There's a shattering sound from high above. Hella looks up in horror, just in time to see a crack spreading in the once-solid defensive barrier.
The next moment, a sharp claw tears through the barrier. Sandy wind and Mania rush into the city.

speaker: Hella
content: Watch out! Something's breaking through!

Sand beasts and Corruptors crawl through the cracks in the barrier, wreaking havoc on the city's infrastructure. Screams, wails, and monstrous howls have replaced the bustling peace of daily life, transforming Furor into a battlefield in an instant.
The barrier overhead flickers frantically, as if struggling to once again contain the Mania outside, but each attempt is torn apart by the howling sand and wind.

speaker: Hella
content: No way! We can't fight these things! Run... Wait, what?!

Hella turns around, shocked to see that most of the residents aren't retreating. Instead, they're grabbing whatever they can find—pots, pans, and other utensils—as makeshift weapons, apparently preparing to join the fight.

speaker: Rosse
content: Everyone who can still move, follow me! Gear up! We can't let them keep destroying the barrier!
Someone hauls the Aurum Secretum device off Hella's hands. People rush past her, many pausing to ruffle her hair before charging unflinchingly into the chaos.
Another violent tremor shakes the earth. Dust rains down as deep fissures crack through Furor's rocky surface, cutting straight into the underground depths.

speaker: Voice in the Memory
content: Those guys? They were probably taken underground. There's a special place down there where bad people get locked up.

speaker: Hella
content: Oh no...! Horo!!

The situation is dire, and the Legion is still trapped underground. This is the perfect opportunity Hella has been waiting for. With everyone distracted by the chaos, no one will notice if she slips away. She can rescue the Legionnaires and they can all escape together.
But...

speaker: Voice in the Memory
content: Don't worry! You're one of us now. Those DisCity thugs won't ever get to hurt you again!

speaker: Hella
content: Sorry, but my friends are waiting for me. I have to go now...!
Screams and sobs echo throughout the city. Squeezing her eyes shut in anguish and gritting her teeth, Hella runs toward the underground cell with her head down.
The ground shakes violently once again. Nearby, Granny Nysa pulls the trembling little Zade into her arms, whispering a prayer with her rosary gripped tightly in her hands.

speaker: Granny Nysa
content: Oh dear, oh dear... Don't be afraid, little one. It'll all be over soon...
Not expecting this turn of events, you rub your temples in exasperation.
Several sand beasts break through the defenses, riding the sandy winds. Hearing the child's cries, they turn and charge toward the pair!
But seconds pass, and the expected pain never comes. Someone has blocked the beasts' attack.
The petite girl snatches a pipe from the rubble and positions herself protectively in front of them.

speaker: Zade
content: Hella!

speaker: Hella
content: You want them? You'll have to get through me first!

speaker: Hella
content: Take this! Ha! Nice, good job!
Several people work together to restrain the sand beasts, while Hella delivers a powerful blow with her pipe, knocking them down for good.

Behind them, the Aurum Secretum shield generator has been activated, creating a relatively safe perimeter for the wounded. The sand beasts blocking the retreat path are gradually being cleared. If this keeps up, everyone should at least be able to fall back to the caverns for shelter...
As Hella's mind races for a solution, she suddenly senses something wrong. The ever-present howl of the wind, somehow, has stopped.
[Transition, screen shakes]
A massive shockwave slams into Furor, shaking the entire city, knocking Hella to the ground, and completely tearing open the breach overhead.

The next moment, a vast torrent of black sand pours into Furor, blotting out the sky and sunlight. A cyclone churns above everyone's heads, and with sinister whispers, an enormous shadow slowly materializes and descends toward them.

speaker: Hella
content: ?! Is that... an Apostle of Ashes?

speaker: Hella
content: Hey! Have you got any spare Aurum Secretum weapons?!

speaker: Taric
content: We do, but...

speaker: Hella
content: Get everything you've got! This thing is no joke. Bring out all your secret weapons now, or we're all dead meat!
The townies frantically haul out an Aurum Secretum cannon. Unlike the intricate shield generator, this weapon is just one smooth barrel with a mysterious crystal embedded in its base.
Hella has no time to notice the grave expressions on their faces. She simply urges them to work together to fire the cannon.
Boom!

speaker: Apostle of Ashes?
content: ...!
The massive recoil knocks Hella to the ground. A huge hole is blasted through the Apostle's form, but the gap doesn't last long before being filled by black particles swirling in the wind.

speaker: Hella
content: It's self-repairing! Quick, we gotta strike while the iron's hot. Fire again!

speaker: Hella
content: ...Old Rosse? Taric?
No one answers. Hella turns around only to find collapsed Furorians scattering all over the ground behind her.

They're all trembling, with energy visibly soaking its way up their arms, eroding them. That's when she realizes why they hadn't brought out the Aurum Secretum weapon earlier. They can't withstand the impact of using it!

speaker: Taric
content: Cough, cough... It's okay, we can manage... another shot...

speaker: Hella
content: Are you mad?! Look at the state you're in after just one shot... You can't handle another. It'll kill you!

speaker: Taric
content: Must protect... the lab... and Aurum Secretum... Leave this to us... You go back... quickly... Run...!

speaker: Hella
content: No way! Aurum Secretum is no use now and Horo isn't here. There's no other option... I'll distract the Apostle while you guys run!
The Furorians struggle to their feet, determined to fire another shot.
A storm is brewing, with the Apostle's attack imminent. Frantic with panic, Hella forcibly yanks the boy away from the Aurum Secretum cannon. But almost simultaneously, her worst fears come true.
—From within the black vortex, an invisible gaze turns toward the two figures locked in struggle.

speaker: Hella
content: Damn it!
[Black Screen]
Shh... Don't move.
Something streaks past her at high speed. It collides with the Apostle's attack, erupting into a thunderous explosion in front of Hella.
[CG - Hypatia First Encounter A]

As Hella opens her eyes again, the dark clouds have dispersed, replaced by brilliant radiance. Golden runes encircle Hella's body. The golden rose insignia on the girl's shoulder unfolds petal by petal, transforming into a weapon in her hand.
You... do not belong here.
Formations unfold, completely suppressing the rampaging Mania. At this moment, the jade-green crystal before the girl's palm begins to glow softly, gathering energy...
Begone, return to your lair. You have no place here.
[Transition for 1s, Aurum Secretum resonating sound effect]

speaker: Hella
content: ...Hypatia?
[CG - Hypatia First Encounter B]
Hearing the voice from her side, the girl turns her gaze toward Hella.
Hmm...? You are...
[Background: City Center]
The dark silhouette within the magnetic storm grows agitated, emitting a piercing screech as it transforms windborne debris into sharp spikes that hurtle toward the blonde girl standing below.
Now, go!
Numerous uniformed figures appear on the rocky walls surrounding Furor. The Aurum Secretum devices in their hands resonate with the girl's weapon, forming a ring that nearly covers all of Furor.

Boom! An enormous energy beam, far exceeding the power of the Aurum Secretum cannon, fires forth. The dark silhouette is shredded by the light, dissolving into sand particles escaping from the city through the rift.
The crisis seems to have passed. Hella stares in stunned silence at everything that just happened, and at the girl standing not far away.

speaker: Lab Staff
content: Lady Hypatia.
Several researchers have already made their way to the lower part of the city, gathering around Hypatia.

speaker: Lab Staff
content: We're currently tallying the casualties. Multiple anchor points on the outer rock face have failed, severely compromising the barrier. Given how this may affect our ongoing project schedule, we should mobilize the whole city to prioritize repairing the barrier...
But Hypatia simply raises her hand, cutting the conversation short.

She approaches an injured person lying among the rubble. Gruesome wounds cover the victim's body, with infection spreading from the right arm across the entire chest. Despite trying to cover her mouth, the woman can't suppress the broken gasps rattling from her lungs.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Careful... easy now. Don't move, you're injured.
Hypatia kneels down gently, ignoring how her long robe is touching the ash-covered ground. She carefully places her hand over the wound on the injured woman's right arm, emitting a soft blue light.

speaker: Furorian
content: Is this... a Hypercube? No, it's far too precious to be wasted on someone like me!
Hypatia shakes her head. The Hypercube absorbs the Mania from the wound, and color gradually returns to the woman's face. Hypatia stands up and begins giving instructions to the other lab staff.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Let the injured rest. I can handle a few broken anchor points myself.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Tend to the wounded first, then repair those damaged caverns. There might still be Corruptors lurking in the city. Search thoroughly and eliminate every last one.

The crowd stirs and swarms around Hypatia to express their gratitude. Hella stands transfixed, staring at the slender girl not far from her. Though the crisis has subsided with the Apostle of Ashes' retreat, her heart still pounds violently in her ears.
That was her first time seeing Aurum Secretum in its full glory. Intricate and powerful. The Campbell heir completely dominated the Apostle, driving it away with overwhelming force.
Now, that metallic hovering weapon is resting on Hypatia's chest again, transformed back into an exquisite shoulder insignia.

speaker: Hella
content: That Campbell girl... is truly something...
...If I got my hands on Aurum Secretum, could I become that powerful too someday?
Lost in these thoughts, Hella looks up suddenly to find herself making direct eye contact with the girl at the center of the crowd.

speaker: Hella
content: ...Oh crap! I was supposed to slip away while they were distracted!
Having received their orders, the researchers have already dispersed throughout the city. Only Hella remains in Hypatia's sight. Her gaze is piercing, as if trying to see through Hella's disguise.

speaker: Hypatia
content: You over there, please stay. I have a few questions for you.
The crowd parts to create a path for Hypatia. Hella finds herself gently ushered forward by the well-meaning throng to meet their most revered Fraser scholar.

speaker: Furorian
content: This is the young girl we rescued from the DisCity people today! She was captured and almost got sold by those scum!
Hella's body freezes as she watches the legendary Lady Campbell making her way through the crowd toward her, one deliberate step at a time.

speaker: Furorian
content: That's right! She saved a few lives during the fight just now too!
Hypatia's penetrating gaze seems to see right through Hella's panic and nervousness as she draws closer. Someone gently pats Hella's shoulder, nudging her frozen body forward.

speaker: Furorian
content: Hella? Hella?
Struggling to control her expression, Hella looks up to find Hypatia already standing right in front of her.
But... unexpectedly, Hypatia merely takes Hella's wrist. A rather bloody scrape lies there, though with Hella's power, it'll heal soon enough.

speaker: Hella
content: Um... I-it's nothing, just a small scratch. It'll heal on its own soon... Ah!
Hypatia suddenly tightens her grip. She steps forward, pulling Hella away from the crowd, then leans in close to her ear to deliver the impactful sentence.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Drop your pretense. I know where you're really from...

speaker: Hypatia
content: <color=#fb9259>DisCity</color>.
[Background: City Center]

A crowbar shoots out at an angle, followed immediately by a young girl in a Legionnaire uniform. The prison gate has already been warped from the earlier attack, allowing her to pry open the lock with minimal effort.
Horo scans her surroundings vigilantly. With no guards in sight, this is the perfect moment to make their escape.

speaker: Legion Member
content: Horo, should we make a run for it now?

speaker: Horo
content: ...No, wait a bit longer.

speaker: Horo
content: Take care of the wounded and stay ready. If possible, try to get in touch with Hella. She might be able to gather different intel from inside.

speaker: Horo
content: As for the rest... we'll discuss it after we regroup.

Horo turns around slowly and gazes into the cell. The rocky wall cracked during the earlier quakes, revealing a hidden secret. There lies a concealed passage with a long stone staircase descending into darkness.

A sense of foreboding rings alarm bells in her mind. She hesitates for a few seconds, then steps into the tunnel anyway, advancing into the darkness against the bone-chilling cold emanating from the rift.
...The last time she ventured underground, her family was still by her side. But this time, she's entirely alone.
In a dark corner unnoticed by the Legion, a coin is flipped into the air, spinning several times before being snatched by a hidden observer.
The woman emerges from the shadows, gazing thoughtfully in the direction where Horo has disappeared.
A new visitor... from DisCity?

speaker: Hypatia
content: I know where you're really from... <color=#fb9259>DisCity</color>.
The girl's firm fingers around Hella's arm are ice-cold.

speaker: Hella
content: Me? From DisCity? Are you kidding?!

speaker: Hella
content: Those thugs in black are my enemies! You know... I won't even hesitate to kill them if I ever get a chance...!
Hella tries to back away as she speaks, but Hypatia pulls her away from the crowd to an empty corner.

speaker: Hypatia
content: But you arrived with those DisCity people. I saw you crossing the sandstorm together. They seemed friendly toward you.

speaker: Hella
content: Th-that's because I was valuable cargo! They were trying to smuggle me to Outlands to sell for profit...

speaker: Hypatia
content: <color=#fb9259>The Legion</color> doesn't engage in trafficking, nor do they allow strangers into their ranks. You must be one of them.
The girl drops this bombshell so casually that Hella nearly bites her own tongue in shock.

speaker: Hella
content: ?! How do you know about them...

speaker: Hypatia
content: After the BR-002 incident, some people migrated from DisCity's West District to the outer satellite towns. But one group strayed, changing their course to head deep into WhiteSands, avoiding way stations and main routes as they traveled northwest.

speaker: Hypatia
content: There's an undercover agent from the Minos Bureau in that group. A clever and cunning Sinner skilled at disguising their true identity.
No way, she knows about all that too?!
Hella tries to back away, but the blonde girl closes in again, gripping her hand even tighter until it begins to hurt.

speaker: Hypatia
content: There's something only you guys can do. I'll release your friends, but in exchange...

speaker: Hypatia
content: While there's still time, leave this place. Take everyone here and <color=#fb9259>escape from Furor</color>.
Escape from Furor? Take everyone? Why? Questions swirl through Hella's mind, but the most pressing issue right now is...

speaker: Hella
content: ****! At least try to be nice when you're asking for a favor! Let go of my hand—you're gonna break it!!

speaker: Hypatia
content: I'm sorry.

speaker: Hella
content: Enough! Let go! I won't run away. Just finish what you were saying!

She hastily loosens her grip, but then clutches Hella's hand firmly again as if afraid she might escape. This time her hold isn't painful, just resolute. Hella tries to pull away, but has to reluctantly give up when she can't free herself.

speaker: Hella
content: What's going on with Furor? Why do you want me to evacuate the town?

speaker: Hella
content: And what about that Apostle of Ashes... Weren't you able to destroy it? With that Aurum something thingy you have!
Hypatia lowers her gaze slightly and gently shakes her head.

speaker: Hypatia
content: No, that only affected part of the Apostle. You see, it's a very cunning creature. The entirety of that storm you saw is its body. If we can't destroy it in one strike, the remaining parts will regenerate, making it nearly impossible to eradicate.

speaker: Hella
content: The entire storm is its body?

speaker: Hypatia
content: Therefore, you and your companions cannot remain here either and must leave quickly. I simply ask that when you go, you take everyone from this town with you.
The girl's tone is utterly sincere. But the intimidating pressure from earlier still lingers in Hella's mind as she scrutinizes Hypatia. She begins carefully.

speaker: Hella
content: ...Is that a threat? Or a demand?
A few seconds of silence pass. Hypatia lifts her head and meets Hella's gaze directly, speaking after some deliberation.

speaker: Hypatia
content: This is... my request. As the leader of Furor, to the visitors from DisCity.

speaker: Hella
content: Oh? But I'm one of those evil bad guys from DisCity. What makes you think I'd agree?

speaker: Hypatia
content: I... have heard from my sources.
The girl's grip loosens slightly. There's an unexpected hint of a smile in her voice.

speaker: Hypatia
content: <color=#fb9259>He</color> said there's a petite Sinner in this crew venturing into WhiteSands, and that while she may appear like a brash loner, she's actually a fiercely loyal person who can't stand to see her friends suffer.
female_content: <color=#fb9259>She</color> said there's a petite Sinner in this crew venturing into WhiteSands, and that while she may appear like a brash loner, she's actually a fiercely loyal person who can't stand to see her friends suffer.

speaker: Hypatia
content: And that if I explain what's at stake and treat her with honesty, I'm certain to earn her help.

speaker: Hella
content: ...What are you talking about! Flattery won't get you anywhere! It's not like such a big crowd will just up and follow us DisCity folks without a good reason...

speaker: Hypatia
content: Your agreement alone would be a good start. Let me explain everything from the beginning.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Also, though it's rather late for introductions at this point, but...
The girl gently lets go of Hella's hand.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Pleased to meet you. My name is Hypatia. Hypatia Campbell of Fraser's Campbell family. I'm also the head of Furor's Aurum Secretum Laboratory and the inventor of Aurum Secretum instruments.
The tension surrounding them gradually dissipates, and Hella finally notices that beneath her formal exterior, Lady Campbell is nothing more than a gentle, soft-spoken girl.

speaker: Hella
content: I'm... um, Hella. Just call me Hella. I haven't got any fancy titles like yours, so just think of me as some heroic adventurer!

speaker: Hella
content: So anyway, what exactly do you need me to do?

Hypatia raises her right hand, guiding Hella's gaze upward. Beyond the shattered barrier, the sky-darkening black sand still lingers, howling and circling outside Furor like a predator watching its prey.

speaker: Hypatia
content: As you can see, the storm surrounding Furor is actually a manifestation of the Apostle's presence. It's a projection of consciousness into reality, and its behavior is heavily influenced by the Mania field. However, because it's too dispersed, it will desperately migrate toward areas of high Mania concentration, seeking to swallow and merge with them, thereby maintaining an equilibrium.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Therefore, as long as the Apostle continues lurking outside Furor, this city will continue to be in danger.

speaker: Hella
content: Um... What?

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...Ahem, to put it simply, this Apostle is easily attracted to people with high spiritual power, especially powerful Sinners—like you and your friends in the Legion. The fluctuations created when you use your special powers attract the Apostle, which is why it relentlessly pursues you.

speaker: Hella
content: ...Well damn, no wonder it kept chasing after us. So it's actually hungry for our power...

speaker: Hella
content: Wait, then if we're not here, or if we leave...

speaker: Hypatia
content: It would target the other residents in the city. After all, they also possess spiritual power.

speaker: Hella
content: What about Aurum Secretum then? Didn't you build some kickass barrier?
Hypatia shakes her head, her expression filled with dejection.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Aurum Secretum is not an omnipotent solution. The protective measures installed on the outer rock faces have been continuously eroding, and because they're difficult to recover, they eventually get devoured by the Apostle, becoming part of its body... It is <color=#fb9259>growing</color>, with Aurum Secretum serving as its nourishment.

speaker: Hypatia
content: The debris in the storm is made up of the things it has devoured. Rocks, sand, cities, passing life forms... These fragments are gathered together by the Apostle's Mania field, forming the black storm that blots out the sky.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Now it's trying to swallow Furor whole, slowly gnawing and digesting it...

speaker: Hypatia
content: Please, help Furor before time runs out.
She places her right hand over her chest and slightly bows her head, giving Hella a traditional salute that looks too formal and complicated.

speaker: Hella
content: Geez, get back up already! No need to be so formal. It's making me super uncomfortable. I never said I wouldn't help, I just don't understand what's going on here. Horo and the others are locked up somewhere below, and besides, what I don't get is...
Hella scratches her head and voices her confusion.

speaker: Hella
content: So, you seem pretty powerful to me. Can't you just help them escape yourself? Why do you need us to rescue them?
Hypatia seems about to respond when her expression suddenly changes.
Footsteps approach. Someone is humming a tune while walking directly toward the quiet corner they're in, coming with a clear purpose and making no attempt to conceal their presence.
Hypatia pulls Hella backward toward the rock wall and quickly runs her fingers over the surface, searching for something...
Click. The sound of a mechanism getting activated. A stone door slides open, revealing a passageway barely half a person's height.

speaker: Hella
content: Wow, Furor has secret passages too? That's so cool... Hey wait, don't drag me like this! And stop shoving me, I'm gonna fall...?!
[Background: Inside the Coffin]
The blonde girl forcefully shoves Hella into the secret passage. In an instant, the stone door closes, plunging the cave into darkness. Only faint rays of light filter through a few air holes.

speaker: Hella
content: Hypatia?! What are you doing!
Hypatia's hushed voice filters through the air holes.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Shh, be quiet. Don't say a word.
The light dims as the person outside blocks part of the openings. Despite this, Hella can't resist edging forward to peer through the one remaining hole...
[Background: City Center]
Hypatia stands blocking the entrance. Though Hella can't see her face, she senses that Hypatia has slipped back into that cold, rigid demeanor from before.
A moment later, a figure rounds the corner, approaching with a leisurely gait before offering an awkward bow.

speaker: Synex
content: Campbell messenger <color=#fb9259>Synex</color>, at your service. It's been a while, my lady.

speaker: Synex
content: I just visited your residence, but your servants informed me you had gone out. You've led me on quite a chase. Heh, if you needed a diversion, surely you could have chosen somewhere less... squalid?
Hypatia's hands, clasped behind her back, tighten slightly. Is she... nervous?

speaker: Hypatia
content: Just testing some new Aurum Secretum equipment.

speaker: Hypatia
content: What do you want? The Furor project is progressing well. I'll submit all the materials the family requires on schedule. No additional support is needed.

speaker: Synex
content: Is that so? Well, I've heard that... a group from DisCity has just recently arrived. What do you say? Would you like me to help you... clean up your current home?

speaker: Hypatia
content: They're just a small group of refugees from DisCity. I've already handled it. They'll be leaving tomorrow.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Did you come all this way for this trivial matter? The Campbell family's shadow operative seem to have far too much free time.
The woman who's just been called a shadow operative tilts her head slightly, speaking pretentiously.

speaker: Synex
content: Trying to dismiss me so soon? I haven't even mentioned my actual business yet. Regarding the proposal you submitted previously, <color=#fb9259>a special someone</color> has sent me to personally deliver the family's decision.

speaker: Synex
content: Of course, I'm well aware of your exceptional competence, my lady. No petty thief could ever escape your notice. But with research as important as yours, someone needs to come specifically to help clear away troubles and solve problems. For instance...

speaker: Synex
content: —Catching little mice that love to eavesdrop!
Hella clamps her hand over her mouth, desperately fighting back the scream rising in her throat.
Less than a centimeter from her face, Synex's blade has struck deep into the rock, barely missing Hella.
[Background: City Center]
The long-handled dagger plunges deep into the rock beside Hypatia. Without flinching, she reaches out and pulls the weapon free.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...Are you questioning my loyalty? Or perhaps suggesting my lab has been compromised?

speaker: Hypatia
content: Before you can give a solid answer, I'd appreciate it if you didn't damage my city so carelessly. As for other matters... there are too many pairs of ears around us. Let's continue this discussion back at the lab.
The masked woman shrugs with a grin, retrieves her weapon, and walks away with Hypatia.
Meanwhile, the little mouse who should have been exterminated...
After making sure both of them have actually left, Hella finally releases the breath she's been holding.

speaker: Hella
content: ...Almost gave me a heart attack! Ahhh!
The narrow passage prevents Hella from jumping up and unleashing a proper tirade. After furiously punching the air twice, her rational brain finally reboots.
Although... her little noggin didn't quite follow that cryptic conversation just now. But she can at least confirm two things:
[Flashback Filter] [WhiteSands Storm]

First, the strange storm surrounding Furor is undeniably an <color=#fb9259>Apostle of Ashes</color>. The city faces imminent destruction, and Hypatia wants Hella to work with the Legion to evacuate all residents from Furor.
[Flashback Filter] [City Center - Daytime]

Second, Hypatia apparently doesn't want her family to know about her plan to ask help from a group from <color=#fb9259>DisCity</color>...? Strange, aren't the Campbells supposed to be the guardians of this city?
As for the third thing...
Just now, when Hypatia confronted Synex, her tone was cold and severe, but Hella could see her hands behind her back, fingers tightly clenched and slightly trembling.
...Just like how tense she looked when she exposed Hella's identity.
[Background: Inside the Coffin]

speaker: Hella
content: Pfft, haha, so she was super nervous back then too.
Not one to speak her true feelings, huh... Reminds me of someone I know.

speaker: Hella
content: But wait a second... Where the heck am I anyway?!
Hella turns around to look at the pitch-black duct behind her. Unlike the cramped space where she can barely crouch, the passage behind her seems to stretch far into the darkness.
The stone door she used to enter the tunnel is now completely sealed... Does this mean her only option is to go deeper inside?
[Transition for 1 second, sound effect of fabric rustling and something moving in a pocket.]
Something seems to be moving in her pocket. Hella reaches in and pulls out a strange object. With five pointed tips, it looks like a star, but also resembles a tiny doll.

The next moment, the tiny doll activates with a hum and begins to glow. It jumps down from Hella's palm, slightly tilts its head, and performs an elaborate but familiar ceremonial bow with its short, stubby limbs...
So familiar that Hella realizes she just saw someone else make the exact same gesture.
...Hypatia?!
The doll bounces in a circle around Hella, then stops in front of her, nodding, as if confirming her suspicion: Yes, its operator is exactly who you think it is.
It raises its arm, hops a few steps into the darkness, and illuminates the space ahead.

speaker: Hella
content: So you want me to follow you? But it gets narrower up ahead. I'd have to crawl through... Hey, if you're so smart, couldn't you just open up that door for me instead? Please?
The doll shakes its head, then hops twice, flashing brighter to emphasize its determination. A cool breeze drifts from the darkness, its source unknown. Hella swallows hard.

speaker: Hella
content: ...So, I really have to crawl?
The doll nods. It points toward the outside, then dramatically draws a line across its throat before flopping to the ground with a plop, playing dead.

speaker: Hella
content: You—!
It's not wrong though. If Hella wants answers to all her questions, the best way forward is to follow Hypatia's directions and find her in person.
Even if it means being crammed into a duct, having to crawl on her hands and knees.

speaker: Hella
content: ...Ahhh fine! I get it!
Politely, Hella gives the tiny doll the finger, then huffily gets into position, preparing to crawl.

speaker: Hella
content: Fine, I'll crawl through this stupid pipe!

speaker: Faint Voice
content: ...Fine, I'll crawl through this stupid pipe!
The shouting echoes from far away through the tunnel, faint and indistinct.

speaker: Horo
content: ......Hella?
Hella? Never heard that name before. Is she your accomplice outside?

A beam of light shines in Horo's direction. Irritated, she looks up at the flashlight's owner, a woman casually crouching at a higher vantage point, flipping a coin in her hand while observing Horo stuck at the bottom of the trap.
Hello, there. You don't look like you're here on vacation. People around here aren't exactly welcoming to folks from DisCity.
The woman speaks, yet shows absolutely no intention of offering Horo a helping hand.

speaker: Horo
content: ...Who are you?

The woman stands high above. In the darkness, Horo can't make out her face clearly, but there's something unnervingly calm about her posture, a composure that feels out of place, as if... she already knows this darkness inside out.
[Flashback Filter]
Half an hour earlier, Horo entered the underground tunnel through a collapsed opening.

The tunnel system proved far more complex than she had anticipated. With her supplies confiscated and no flashlight, she was forced to feel her way forward in the darkness, only to accidentally trigger a trap.
At that moment, this woman, with a pair of sunglasses on her face, suddenly appeared to offer her assistance.
[End Filter]

speaker: Lysandra
content: The name is Lysandra, WhiteSands archaeologist. Just like you and your companions, I'm an ordinary passerby trapped here by the storm.
Lysandra produces a somewhat tattered ID card and dangles it in the air. Horo glimpses a woman's portrait on it, actually looking rather decent.

speaker: Horo
content: Archaeology? You came to a place like this on purpose?

speaker: Lysandra
content: Initially, I was just passing through, lying low for a while. But this place turned out to be quite interesting, so I stayed to do some digging around.
Lysandra shrugs, completely unfazed by the skepticism directed at her.

speaker: Horo
content: ...You seem quite familiar with this place?

speaker: Lysandra
content: I tried exploring on my own before, but there are too many hidden mechanisms here, and most of them use special materials that can interfere with Mania...
Lysandra points to the metal bars that have Horo trapped.

speaker: Lysandra
content: It's difficult to venture deeper alone. Fortunately, I know how to deactivate the mechanisms, and you look like you can fight. Plus, we're both curious about this secret passage.
The woman hasn't said it out loud, but Horo catches on immediately. She is suggesting they work together.

A suspicious passage and a suspicious woman. The mechanism trapping her isn't impossible to dismantle by force, but with limited knowledge, that might trigger additional traps... and possibly compromise her investigation.
But working with someone who just emerged out of nowhere? That isn't her style.
Just as Horo is about to refuse, an eerie howl echoes from the distance. Her face contorts even further as she notices how disturbingly unfazed by the sound the woman before her seems.

speaker: Horo
content: ...Now what?

speaker: Lysandra
content: Oh, someone keeps a few <color=#fb9259>watchdogs</color> here, specially trained to retrieve devices and clean up the trash.
Lysandra makes a casual gesture toward Horo. It is clear that the trash she's referring to is Horo herself.
The howls grow closer, accompanied by noisy dragging and crashing sounds. These are no mere watchdogs. They sound more like savage beasts.
The woman's voice drifts down from above behind her.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Just give up. They run much faster than you can break that trap. Reconsider my offer, will you?
The massive beast rounds the corridor corner, charging straight toward Horo. But the current Legion commander merely responds with a cold laugh.
Clang! A dagger appears out of nowhere. Horo slashes through her restraint and aims the blade at the beast looming before her.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Impressive. You sure you don't need any help, shrimp?
Horo responds merely with a cold snort. A flash of steel cuts through the air, her actions providing all the answers needed.
Another beast falls, and Horo faces her final enemy. As she launches what should be the finishing blow, her dagger fails under the strain, the blade snapping clean in half.
[Transition for 1 second, monster roaring sound effect]
Thud! A hammer tied to a rope plummets from above, striking the beast squarely on the head. It sways for a moment before collapsing completely, going still.
Horo looks up to see Lysandra at the edge of the pit, waving down at her.
The Legion leader gives a dismissive snort as she grabs the rope. But just as she is about to leap out of the pit, her foot slips. Lysandra instinctively reaches out...
Clang! In a flash, Horo knocks Lysandra's weapon away and pins her body in a counter hold.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Good reflex. You're better than I gave you credit for, shrimp.

speaker: Horo
content: And you're more shameless than I imagined, tomb raider.

Deftly, Horo snatches an identity document. Lysandra's archaeologist license. This is a pickpocketing trick she's learned from Hella. She carefully peels away the photo on the front, revealing a completely different name and face underneath.

speaker: Horo
content: Familiar with secret passage mechanisms, obsessed with ancient ruins, and now this fake license... Archaeologist? You have the nerve to call yourself that?

speaker: Lysandra
content: Self-taught archaeology is still archaeology. Hardly counts as lying.
As the broken dagger presses against her, Lysandra raises her hands in surrender.

speaker: Lysandra
content: ...Fine, at least I was dead honest about wanting to collaborate.
The woman doesn't seem to be lying. Horo slowly furrows her brow.

speaker: Lysandra
content: This place was probably built after the Outland war that happened over a decade ago. The war created one wave of refugees, and the disasters produced another.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Furor is a refugee settlement with no unified culture, no formal historical records, and not even a single ruin or artifact worth studying.

speaker: Lysandra
content: The only thing in common... is probably the rosary. Everyone here keeps a string of beads on them, which seems to represent some kind of blessing in their language.
She produces a string of beads made of different materials out of her pocket. Indeed, Horo has seen the same accessory on the people who took the Legionnaires prisoner.
Lysandra then points to the wall of the side passage, where intricate patterns are carved into the surface. These details will be easily missed in the darkness without close inspection.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Haven't you noticed? This passage is older than the dwellings above, yet its craftsmanship and engineering far surpass those crude stone caves. This couldn't possibly have been built by the Furorians. They don't even know these underground passages exist.

speaker: Lysandra
content: This place is by no means rich, yet information about it is kept tightly sealed. I'm searching for something special that might be hidden beneath Furor.

speaker: Horo
content: What's buried isn't always treasure. It could just as easily be a landmine waiting to explode.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Seeing is believing—but I need to see for myself to make that judgment.

speaker: Lysandra
content: You possess great strength, but lack the experience navigating traps and secret passages. Fighting your way through would take forever. I can help you, and we'll split the findings as is customary. We each get what we want. It's perfectly fair.

speaker: Horo
content: Horo. That's my name. Stop calling me shrimp!

speaker: Horo
content: And if you try anything suspicious, I'll be the first to throw you down to feed the dogs.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Now we've both laid out our terms. Sounds fair to me.

speaker: Lysandra
content: So, do we have a deal?
Lysandra raises a hand. After a moment, Horo lowers the knife she's been pressing against Lysandra's throat and lightly slaps her palm, signaling their deal is sealed.
Horo turns away first, ready to continue their exploration, when Lysandra's voice suddenly pipes up behind her with a belated realization.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Alright, I've explored this path before. There are quite a few more traps ahead besides the one we just passed. You'd better be careful and follow exactly in my footsteps...
Clack.

Before she can finish her sentence, the grinding of mechanical gears echoes through the corridor, followed by monsters' howls. The next second, more guardian beasts surge from the depths of the passage.
Horo turns around with a deadpan expression to face Lysandra, who's putting on her most innocent look.

speaker: Horo
content: ...Like this?

speaker: Lysandra
content: Yep, exactly like this.
Deep breaths fail to quell her rage, but Horo knows there's only one proper target for her anger—the enemy. Suppressing her frustration, she turns to face the beasts and prepares for battle.

Guardian beasts howl as they race through the passage outside, oblivious to what lies just beside them. Horo and Lysandra have tucked themselves into a small alcove branching off from the main tunnel, taking this moment to hide and recover their strength.

Horo's dagger has been completely ruined in the battle. She clicks her tongue in frustration and tosses the useless blade aside, resigning herself to fighting bare-handed, when suddenly a new dagger and a familiar-looking flashlight sail through the air toward her.
Horo looks up with a furrowed brow, just in time to see Lysandra withdrawing her hand.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Some spare equipment, in exchange for an answer. Fair enough?

speaker: Lysandra
content: You're no tomb raider, and probably not a mercenary either. Yet you're willing to risk getting blown to pieces by these traps to keep going deeper. What are you really looking for, Horo?
...For an inheritance, the cursed treasure. Who knows which lucky soul has received this precious burden this time.
Horo gives Lysandra a guarded look, weighing her next words carefully.

speaker: Horo
content: It's nothing good, that's for sure. If you value your life, stay away from it.

speaker: Lysandra
content: You think it's that thing waiting for us at the end of this path?

speaker: Horo
content: I hope not, but...
Outside, silence returns once more. The two leave their hiding spot and head back to the main passage.

speaker: Horo
content: Whatever's buried down there, inheritance or not, it's definitely nothing harmless.
A dangerously powerful energy permeates the air. As they descend deeper, the Mania grows thicker, coiling through the narrow passage, just like when Horo confronted the inheritance before.
Horo turns to find Lysandra with an unusual frown on her face, deep in thought.
