speaker: Mantis Queen
content: She awakened a mighty power long ago. She could have gotten more, but she took too many risks for "companions." She stagnated, and halted where she was.

speaker: Mantis Queen
content: One must learn to accept their deaths. How come humans become so weak after losing them?
She slowly lands in front of you and reaches out.
Already exhausted, you muster the last of your strength to unleash the shackles. The red light roars towards the monster. You have to kill it! You must!
But just as you're about to pierce her, that person changes. The mask falls off and the contamination recedes, revealing a familiar face and voice.
The light spike halts abruptly. This wasn't a conscious, rational decision, but an instinctive one... you can't harm a "companion," even if it's only a moment's hesitation.

speaker: Mantis
content: You're just like her. She also had the same expression as you.
Tsss...!
Her spike pierces your body, and your shackles shatter.

speaker: Mantis
content: Companions shouldn't be your Achilles heel. You've all been held back by illusory things for too long. Now... I'll help you.

speaker: Mantis
content: Become my companion.
You've tried your best.
But this is someone else's nightmare. It controls all the rules, just like the Illusory Moon amidst this chaos. In front of a greater determination, human faith is so insignificant.

You're pinned to the giant egg's outer wall by the cold limbs. The blood flowing out lands on the egg. It pulses excitedly, heating up and sticking to you bit by bit. Your body gradually sinks in. You weakly cast your shackles, which shatter piteously against the chitinous shell.
With a body that looks like the scholar, and donning a familiar yet unfamiliar smile, the owner of the nightmare leans in close and gazes at you.

speaker: Mantis Queen
content: Just like her, you were lured into a trap by the bait of "companions." Once you lose someone, you're easy to defeat.

speaker: Mantis Queen
content: Both of you are weak, flawed, but it's okay. I've found you. I'll be your companion.

speaker: Mantis Queen
content: From now on, together, we'll become stronger, and complete...
It affectionately sniffs your scent and licks your blood and sweat. This only stirs up your burning hatred, but even this rage gets sucked deep into the lethal gel.

The acid dissolves your spirit, and the buzzing of insects erodes your consciousness. The boundary between reality and illusion gradually blurs. Specks of light appear before your eyes, getting closer and closer and corrupting your vision, yet you can't do anything.
All you hear is a vague, floating voice that sounds like a buzzing insect. It is the voice of the Mantis.
Are you... here for your companion too?
Where is your companion? What's... their name?
Do you want... my help?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I won't be deceived... Even if you were once human, even if you mimic our language, you're just cruel monsters born from Mania. You don't understand the human heart at all. You're not worthy to talk about companions.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're not my companions...
Why do you say that? I... understand, don't I?
You're taken aback for a moment, lifting your head to see nothing but emptiness. Yet faint points of light touch you, resonating a voice deep within your heart.
Speaking slowly, as if understanding, as if learning, as if... recalling.
It's not about coming together. It's not about adding more strength to become stronger. That's not enough.
We can endure the night because we support each other. We can soar to greater heights because we strive for it.
Essentially, we are weak... It's our cherished feelings for each other that transcend all boundaries and make us strong.
People become superheroes for each other. When a superhero joins another superhero, we can conquer anything.
That’s the meaning of companionship, isn't it?
Hehe, so I... understand everything. How can you say I don't understand?
Me? Hmm... I, don't remember. But...
Our feelings, are the same. Let me think, hmm...
If I share the same feelings as you, then are we... also companions?
Would you... like to be my companion?

Flickering specks of lights, illusory voices, and strange thoughts... At this moment, you have no idea who you're talking to. But deep inside, you long to answer this question, and yearn to grasp this unfamiliar spark...
A warm current ripples around you. The specks of light tremble slightly, exciting you.
I'm so glad... I thought I wouldn't be able to find any...
My companions are here! I've finally found you all! Now, I'm going to...
<size=40>... take you home!</size>

The gel binding you suddenly explodes. Some of the gel still obstructs your vision, but you clearly hear a scream. The hard claws holding you loosen abruptly, and you vaguely see the humanoid Mutant Bug retreating and convulsing. Then...
A strong light suddenly bursts and explodes from within its body!

speaker: Mantis Queen
content: Aaaaaaaaahhhhhhhh!!!

speaker: Mantis Queen
content: Get lost! Get out! Die!! We worked so hard to get this... the Mantises worked so hard...

speaker: FAC Captain
content: A rift has appeared on the Mantis Queen's body! She is leaking a lot of Mania energy and affecting the Illusory Moon! Now! Concentrate fire and eliminate her!!

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: Visual confirmation! We see it too! The Mantis swarm is in chaos! They've lost their combat ability!

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: Now! Concentrate fire and get the captain back!!

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Don't ******* waste time on me!! Follow the orders and shoot the queen!!!

speaker: Mantis Queen
content: Aaaaaaaaahhhhhhhh!!!

Just like how the Mutant Bugs slaughtered the rescuers, a green light erupts from the rift in the Mantis Queen's chest, rising and unfurling into brilliant wings. At the base of the wings of light, a newborn rises, breaking free from the cocoon.

You want to take a closer look, but a violent wave erupts in the bug nest, rushing towards you in fury. Just as something grabs your clothes, a strong light and a powerful gust of wind instantly demolishes the entire bug nest.

A pair of strong hands yank you away. Your feet leave the ground, and you're flying away at high speed. The feeling of weightlessness almost makes you vomit. After several intense booms, a cold wind suddenly hits. The stench of the bug nest is swept away. You quickly regain your breath, and your consciousness clears...
Looking down, your legs are dangling in the air. A swarm of bugs is chasing you but can't catch up... Soaring with unprecedented lightness, you fly farther and farther from the ground.
Someone is holding you tightly, breaking you free from all constraints. Facing the wind, you soar high into the sky.

The newborn Sinner is holding you tightly, skimming past the chaos. Her slender wings of light scatter sparkles as she flies, blocking out the twisted red light of the Illusory Moon like a cascading river of light. There is never daytime in a Nightmare, but in this moment, she illuminates the whole night sky.
No, that's not her name. What should you call her?
She doesn't answer, nor does she need to. Under the mask that resembles compound eyes, you see a familiar bright and radiant smile. Her clear chirps remind you of that joyful laughter.
You fly for a long, long time, until you can't see the swarm, the contamination, or the twisted red moonlight. "Mantis" slowly , carefully placing you on the ground, gently lands in front of you.
The endpoint of the journey is the stone slate you had promised to go to. But this time, there's no camp, and no blurry figures.
There are only a few ice-blue crystallized flowers blooming around the slate, and the two of you.
You understand... You must bid farewell here after all.

options: You kept your promise. You came to see me off.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Thank you.

options: Would you like to come with me?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: We can try. Once we get out, we can form a new crew, shoot a new season of "Wilderness Trek." I have a lot of companions. I can introduce you to them. Whether it's eating bugs or something else, a lot of people will like it.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Even though we come from different eras... people will always like adventure, right? And you are the greatest adventurer.

You reach out to her. She tilts her head, as if she doesn't understand. She raises her chitinous scythe arm and waggles it a bit. Then, as if imitating you, she also reaches out to you, roughly mimicking your angle.
You choke up, unsure of how to respond. Ever since you left the gel, you can no longer hear the voice in your heart.
She seems to not understand why you're showing a pained expression. She reaches out with both arms, as if to pinch your face to make you smile, carefully avoiding the serrated edges on her own claws.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Can you... still understand my words?
She tilts her head, and her antenna-like bangs flutter a bit. You don't understand what this means, but at least she attempts to respond to you.
You make a few hand gestures.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The lifeforms in DisSea aren't monsters... they are the embodiment of collective subconsciousness...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The stronger the conviction, the greater the manifestation. There is no hierarchy in consciousness. Only when they merge and conflict does instability occur. And you broke their blockade, taking control.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You were right. There is indeed humanity in Apostles of Ashes, and they can also awaken humanity... You've proven this hypothesis yourself.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You are truly the most amazing human naturalist of all time. You are the bright little explorer who brings courage to everyone, and... our best companion, my superhero.
Seeming to finally understand that you're praising her, "Mantis" flutters her luminescent wings excitedly and emits a crisp chirp.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Can you understand my words? Do you feel happy?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Are these movements of yours... trying to tell me something?
You reach out to touch her sheathed cheek, but your hand trembles uncontrollably. Your vision gradually blurs and your voice becomes choked.

options: But I can't understand you anymore...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I can't understand what you're saying, and I don't know how to convey my feelings to you. Do you really not remember anything?

The red light of the shackles disperses the contamination clinging to her face, revealing only those fluorescent eyes. She blinks at you, showing kindness, curiosity, and perhaps confusion... Or maybe it's just a projection of your own guesses.
Those are no longer human eyes. How could you possibly understand them?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You said we'll always be companions. You said there's a possibility of communicating with the Mutant Bugs, and that we could potentially understand each other. No matter how long it takes, I want to spend time to get to know you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But I can't let go of the former you. I have so many questions to ask you, and so many things to say. If you can understand me, can you please come back?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I don't even know your name. I've forgotten all of you...
You choke up, shedding tears. You want to confide something, but this pain is now yours alone.

She tilts her head to look at you, leans in, and sniffs curiously. She licks your tears as if trying to understand you, then shakes her head vigorously as if she tasted something bitter, her little wings trembling.
After calming down, she flashes an innocent smile and reaches past your shoulder to touch something behind you...
Behind you, a name lights up on the stone slate.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Is this your name?
This name doesn't awaken any lost memories, but it lights up a warmth in some slumbering corner of your heart. You turn around, wanting to call out her name...
You've found the key to leave. You finally start to awaken from the Eternal Nightmare. The woman's smile dissolves like stardust, scattering to the wind like startled fireflies.
Your consciousness is pushed away, serenaded by the tune of gentle bug chirps.

January 9, N.F. 114
DisSea Outskirts, 
Third Broken Frontline Monitoring Station,
1.53km from the BR-000 border.
The wasteland is empty, no enemies or ambushes. In the suffocating silence, you can only hear the heavy breaths and footfalls of the guards.

In your head, however, a chaotic voice is mumbling, inciting fear and bewitching your thoughts. Don't listen to it, you think to yourself, for they are just Mania radiating from BR-000. The Mania concentration has been increasing recently, and you know why...
...The <color=#fb9259>Illusory Moon</color> is about to rise, and a new tidal cycle in the DisSea is approaching. In three days, all values are expected to reach the danger zone.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: After the return of Chief, we received more timely warnings from the shackles, allowing us to investigate the anomalies before the outbreak of the Illusory Moon and prepare for the third wave of impact.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: But don't let your guard down. Prioritize protecting Chief ${PlayerName} in this mission. We cannot afford any mishaps. If an emergency occurs, terminate the operation and return to the safe zone at once. Do you understand?

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: Yes, sir!
The soldiers respond in unison, their voices loud and resolute. Since they're guarding by your side, their deafening reply makes your heart skip a beat. You almost drop the report in your hand.

options: Thank you, do take care of yourselves, too.

content: The active period of BR-000 has an uncontrollable effect on Sinners, so you've switched your "bodyguards" to reliable FAC soldiers and...

speaker: Schorl
content: You have reached the center of this tidal anomaly. Although the value hasn't reached its peak yet, there are already signs of <color=#fb9259>temporal storms</color>. When the value reaches its peak, the following extreme phenomena might happen:

speaker: Schorl
content: Entities within the distortion field may experience temporal superposition and observation indeterminacy. Each observation may yield random results of any time state present within the distortion field.

speaker: Schorl
content: This is just a theory based on my calculation. In reality, no one has ever recorded such phenomena. The effect of the storm is beyond our current knowledge and is deemed extremely dangerous.
I didn't quite understand you. But if it's some kind of temporal disorder, can you travel through time and meet people in the past, like in those sci-fi movies? That sounds pretty cool.

speaker: Schorl
content: I can't understand you either, but the danger of this operation far exceeds the temporal distortion phenomena you've encountered in the Black Rings before. Please be on your guard at all times.
You chuckle. Well, can't exactly expect this thing to have a sense of humor.
You look up at something not far away...

It's a behemoth armor shrouded in shadow, covered with rust and scratches. Under the red glow of the DisSea tide, it's emanating intense pollution, so threatening that one simply can't stare at it for too long.

You can't tell what kind of machinery this is, what it's made out of, who made it, or why it exists. The only thing that you can be certain of is that: it doesn't belong to this era. It's like a steel colossus that has been dead for centuries, lifeless and decaying.

speaker: Schorl
content: 9 hours ago, the monitoring station confirmed that it crossed the BR-000 border and reached the outskirts of the DisSea. Its pollution level well exceeded S-Class, and all timekeeping equipment close to it malfunctioned.

speaker: Schorl
content: This is a high-risk object born in the DisSea, and the distortion it brings is rapidly increasing. We probably haven't discovered its real danger yet.

speaker: Schorl
content: Chief, please don't get any closer. You shouldn't be in such a dangerous area in the first place. There's no need for you to take such a risk no matter what your reason might be.
I told you before. And at that time, the <color=#fb9259>big shot</color> behind you agreed as well.

speaker: EDGE-01
content: I heard you applied for high-level access to the FAC and the 9th Agency for the <color=#fb9259>files on the Black Ring Expedition</color> and <color=#fb9259>classified data from a hundred years ago</color>... I'm afraid you won't hear any good news from them.

speaker: EDGE-01
content: It's nothing personal. Those incomplete records are in disarray and mostly unverified. If fallen into the wrong hands, they could endanger the very core of the city. Even your superiors don't have access to them.

options: But I already know a lot of things, through other means.

content: You stare at the cold black Schorl, recounting the vague yet clear "memories" that you've been replaying in your head and dare not forget since you woke up.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: In N.F. 21, the <color=#fb9259>DisSea Expedition</color> entered the Perishing Star restricted area. Except for Keylan, the hero who brought back the Hypercube, the other <color=#fb9259>42 people</color>, including core researchers and assistants, never left the DisSea.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Dreya the astronomer, and Man... Marguerite Nash the naturalist... I don't have access to those records, but I know these names.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: There might also be Banyan the physician, a certain mechanic, and...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: An unknown <color=#fb9259>child guide</color>.
A long silence on the other end... It's so long that you think you've crossed a line and are about to be warned, but then you hear response from it.

speaker: EDGE-01
content: Well then, tell me what you want.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I won't ask for high-level access anymore, I'm fine with what you would give to an FAC combatant; after all, I'm also part of the "Anti-Mania force." During my operation, I'll report to you any extra info I get. In exchange...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I know there's been some abnormal activity in the DisSea recently, and the Broken Frontline is strengthening its defenses. If this has anything to do with the <color=#fb9259>periodic activities of the Illusory Moon</color>...

options: I want to be <color=#fb9259>there</color> to take part in the operation.

speaker: EDGE-01
content: Alright, but there's one condition.
It surprises you with a prompt response.

speaker: EDGE-01
content: During the Illusory Moon's tidal period, Mania activities are more frequent than ever. Accidents might happen if you approach the DisSea. Therefore, the investigation must be completed before the Illusory Moon rises. Once the values reach the danger zone, you must stop the operation and return immediately.

speaker: EDGE-01
content: BR-000 is an entirely different thing from Secondary Black Rings. Your emotional responsivity is high, thus I don't know how you will be affected. If you want to get closer to the truth, you can't let your emotions cloud your judgment.

speaker: EDGE-01
content: I need you to return in one piece, physically and mentally.
You express gratitude for this unemotional concern.
I'll be back safely, and bring back some... things that are very important to me.

FAC is busy recording and collecting data on the scene, and some are keeping an eye on the contamination source. Apparently, due to something called "temporal superposition and observation indeterminacy in the temporal storm," if no one is watching this mechanical behemoth, it could jump to "another time state," or even disappear.

Sounds quite mischievous. But you have confirmed multiple times that this thing doesn't have any "driver," or remote control signal. This contamination source is a mere "machine" without any individual will. That's somewhat disappointing to you.
You thought, just like before, you would meet a Sinner, a deeply contaminated creature, or a nostalgic person.

speaker: Calm Voice
content: The truth... is right ahead... above the Illusory Moon, in the depths of the starry sky...
That's the voice of the astronomer you first met, calm just like her eyes looking at the starry sky.

speaker: Persistent Voice
content: Grouping up is truly humanity's most wonderful attribute. Even though I'm just an ordinary person, with them, I can keep going no matter how dark the night. With them, I am invincible.
A friend as warm as sunlight, an insect-loving naturalist, and your brief yet eternal companion.

Those memories were the occasional respites during your 8-month coma filled with nightmares. You constantly think of them, fearing that they are just fleeting illusions that you might forget again. It was such a big relief when you found something in the FAC's DisSea operation records that are remotely connected to those people.
But that's far from enough. You are awake now; you want confirmation; you want to find more of them... The Illusory Moon is rising again. Who will you meet this time?

Deep in your thoughts, a vague human figure appears in front of you. She stands next to the corroded, polluted mech. Even though her face is blurry, you sense that she's looking at you, without hostility.

speaker: Apparition
content: ...That earring...

speaker: Apparition
content: ...It's you... Why are you here...

options: I came, but who are you?

content: As the question leaves your lips, you suddenly realize:
You don't know this person. This is not in your memories at all!
Something has invaded your mind, peeping and imitating your emotions, planting things you don't know at all! When did it start? How long has this been going?!
Who are you?! What... are you?!

In response to you is a burst of dazzling red light that almost knocks you out. And then, a large shadow seizes all your senses. As if it suddenly came to life, the monster reveals its terrifying true face.

speaker: Roaring Mech
content: Bzzzzzzz...

speaker: FAC Captain
content: The contamination source has moved. Retreat! Protect Chief, get him out of here!
female_content: The contamination source has moved. Retreat! Protect Chief, get her out of here!

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: But Chief has passed out!!!

speaker: FAC Captain
content: What? When did that... No, now is not the time for that. Activate the shield and block the enemy. Get him out of here, quick!
female_content: What? When did that... No, now is not the time for that. Activate the shield and block the enemy. Get her out of here, quick!

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: Captain, look up!

Even the most advanced instruments failed to alert the squad beforehand. The Illusory Moon is suddenly up in the sky, as if it had always been there, still rising and expanding. There are no Corruptors, nor attacks, but due to ${PlayerName}'s fall, the red moon instantly instills fear in everyone.
Its increasingly brilliant yet viscous radiance falls upon the ground, like it's about to swallow everything it illuminates.

speaker: Schorl
content: Review completed. No miscalculations or operation errors detected, but the Illusory Moon rose 72 hours ahead of schedule.

speaker: Schorl
content: The possible reason for all this could only be...
Separated from your body and the crowded reality, your mind finally stabilizes from the initial impact. You gradually return to your senses amid the chaotic whispers.
...Time... is an illusion... and a cage...
...Give up, let go, stop clinging to your insignificance... Come face the grandeur, become one with eternity...
...Come, find where you... truly belong...
Compared to last time, the moon seems to have changed a bit: it's now split into three parts; it has grown larger, and become... even more talkative. Its voice is buzzing incessantly in your head.

options: Shut up, I'm not here for you.

content: You look at what's in front of you instead. Even without looking at the Illusory Moon, its light still stings your eyes. The immense pressure crashes you down, but you don't feel panic or wish to submit... On the contrary, you're excited.

Right before your eyes, you see everything rapidly decaying and rebuilding. Time grinds everything to dust like a massive vortex and then brings them back to life. It's too fast for human eyes to keep up. At the center of the vortex is that massive, daunting mechanical leviathan. In its shadow, you see a tiny human figure.
It's a familiar yet strange feeling, a call from someone you've never met but long to reunite—the reason why you came here.
What a relief... I thought this would be a fruitless journey, and those were just my dreams.

It's lucky that I caught the Illusory Moon this time and got to participate in this operation... It's lucky that I <color=#fb9259>came</color> here, went through some sort of temporal storm and met you.
Summoning the shackles, you take a step forward.

options: I'll take you back, let's go back together!

content: When you open your eyes again, countless specks of light are swirling and floating in the distant sky, almost like a storm is brewing.
The members of FAC and that strange mech are not here. It seems that you've been pulled into a different spacetime.
You step forward, feeling the solid rock under your feet. Everything feels real, but under the red light, the familiar feeling returns.

You see the buildings in the distance constantly changing and weathering. Although you haven't been affected yet, the spacetime here doesn't seem stable. The boundary between reality and illusion isn't so clear either.
The wasteland is not so quiet anymore. The howl of monsters is echoing. But this time it's different, you're wide awake and prepared. Defeat them, find a way out, and more importantly...
Find the "old friend" trapped by that evil moon, travel through time and bring her back.
You've walked far and fought hard in search of your 'old friend.' Now, you can finally sense her presence more clearly—she's nearby.

But that mechanical behemoth is here too, at the center of the pollution storm. And in this spacetime, it obviously has all its power. It's marching forward slowly. You can see the twisted light around it, and its pollution pouring out. Just then, you hear the howl of Corruptors.

speaker: Monster
content: Roarrrr!
You can't retreat, nor do you want to. If the person you're looking for is here, then before she leaves, you must get through these monsters.
You desperately release your power, but the monsters form a vast and never-ending ocean, the path you cut open is instantly flooded.
You're even a bit dazed. All these faces... didn't you just see them a few seconds ago? Didn't you just cut them down? How long have you been fighting? How many enemies are you fighting?
And before you know it, that behemoth armor has disappeared from your sight, even its last roar sounds far away.

speaker: Monster
content: Roarrrr!
You blast open a gap again, but lack the strength to run. Another wave of monsters is approaching, you desperately raise your hand, but your vision gradually blurs...
Just then, you hear a voice.
Don't move, save your strength.
I'll handle the rest.
The voice is calm, completely out of place in this madness, but it's surprisingly persuasive. Your body follows the instruction on its own.
You get down instantly. At the same time, a loud thud comes from behind you with a gust rushing over your head. The violent and fierce attack collides with a sturdy metal armor.
A woman clad in heavy mechanical armor leaps in front of you, the ground and your eardrums vibrating as she lands. The next moment, she swings a powerful punch with her other arm.
Boom—

The extraordinary punch, with a terrifying sonic boom and wind pressure, blasts several monsters over a dozen meters away into a wall of rock like cannonballs. Bits of rock and earth collapse, burying the monsters.
The woman does not linger in the fight. She picks you up—her mechanical arm hoists you on one side. As you get closer, she lowers her voice, just loud enough for you to hear clearly.
Cover your head!

As you shield your head with both hands, your body is pulled forward suddenly. You feel like you're being carried by a raging rhino charging into a dense forest. You see her other mechanical arm swiping back and forth, sending monsters flying like fallen leaves.

All you can hear are the silent screams, the sound of mechanical parts hitting the ground, and the thick wind. With your feet off the ground, you're rendered speechless by the jolts. Yet she presses on without slowing down, and then makes a big jump. After a dozen seconds later, your feet finally touch the ground again.
You realize that the person carrying you is not some mighty gorilla, but a woman of ordinary stature, who's equipped with two large and robust mechanical arms.

Don't fight them in the eye of the storm. Time is a tangled mess in there. When you're up against a monster, you're facing its present, past, and future selves all at once. Each and every version of it is an independent entity. You can't possibly finish them off.
But eventually all these versions of them will converge into one, so you only need to take one down, and wait for the others to die on their own.
That won't do if you're in a hurry though.
You stare at her unfamiliar yet reassuring face for a while, trying hard to memorize it, then you say...

options: I'm not in a hurry anymore.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I've found you.
The woman nods, looking towards somewhere you can't see.
Those monsters will reappear in no time. Let's leave now. The camp is not far away. I'll carry you; it's faster that way.
This time it'll be less bumpy.
She carries you in a more comfy way with her mechanical arm, then strides forward.
Oh right, you don't know her name yet, but your anxiety has long since disappeared. It's like you're finally standing on solid ground. You feel like you can follow her anywhere.
The destination of this walk is in sight—a small camp. It doesn't look like a base camp for the expedition, probably just a temporary base for an investigative squad.
But there is something in the camp that makes you hold your breath—

You see a huge <color=#fb9259>mech</color>, very similar to the behemoth you saw in the contamination. The only difference is that this one is unfinished with many half-assembled parts. Overall it's less broken, and some parts are quite new.
When you're up against a monster, you're facing its present, past, and future selves all at once. Each and every version of it is an independent entity.
Are they the same mech? Could this thing also become the center of a temporal storm in the future? Can people from this spacetime go to your era through it? What should you do?
You should ask, but... in what capacity?
You can't recognize it? You've seen the prototype at the base, it was only as tall as you then.
The woman who saved you skillfully removes her armor and stands beside you with a toolbox. Now she just looks like an ordinary woman, much less intimidating.
The question slips out, then you realize it might sound weird when you see her frown. According to your "dreams" from before, they seem to see you as some kid...?
Ow... my head, what happened, where is this? Did... I forget something? My head... hurts so bad...
The woman looks serious and examines your head. After making sure there are no serious injuries, she reaches into her pocket and stuffs a biscuit in your hand.
You have three bumps on your head. That was pretty scary for you, right? You're safe now. I'm Vanilla, your teammate, the logistician, and mechanic of the team.

speaker: Vanilla
content: I came here with a small investigation team. We set up a temporary camp here.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Yes, that's me.

speaker: Vanilla
content: The others are all out investigating. Our plan is to investigate the nearby temporal storm and evaluate its dangers.
What about you...

speaker: Vanilla
content: I'm no researcher, I'm the team's logistician, protecting the camp is my job.

speaker: Vanilla
content: All the research data, the reserves, and provisions are all here. If I left my post, monsters would swarm in and destroy all their hard work.

speaker: Vanilla
content: And you? Why did you come here all alone?

speaker: Vanilla
content: This place is far from the main camp, and it's dangerous near the temporal storm. There's no one with you?
You think for a moment.

options: There are, we came here for you.

content: I'm the guide. Finding people and places is my job, so I came to find you. And I'm not alone this time.
There are many teammates outside. I'm just... a scout. I came here to recon the place first, and then I'll figure out how to bring you back.
We can start now. I'll go scout, and we'll leave as soon as possible!
Your lie doesn't raise any suspicion, but it does puzzle her a bit. After some thought, Vanilla answers.

speaker: Vanilla
content: ...Maybe I didn't make myself clear. Let me explain again... The temporal storm has moved and taken control of this camp and its surrounding area. It's very dangerous outside. Until the storm subsides, we can't leave.

speaker: Vanilla
content: They're not the problem. The real danger of the temporal storm is that time becomes unreliable. We can no longer accurately "observe" time.
Seeing how perplexed you look, Vanilla thinks for a moment, takes out a pocket watch, and slowly explains while organizing her thoughts.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Take this pocket watch as an example. When you're looking at it, or rather, observing it, its time moves forward with you, second by second. This is reliable time. It allows you to correctly perceive the world.

speaker: Vanilla
content: But in the storm, if you fall asleep, faint, or lose consciousness and are unable to observe just for a split second, this pocket watch could jump to another random time state when you look again.

speaker: Vanilla
content: It could be the past, or the future where it's all rusty or no longer exists. I'm not just talking about this pocket watch, the whole world operates this way. If your time is no longer in sync with the world, it could destroy your mind in some severe cases.

speaker: Vanilla
content: I'm being very serious right now. Remember, it's way more dangerous than the misty mazes you usually encounter. You mustn't let yourself be in a situation where this might happen, got it?
She tries to look as stern as possible to emphasize the seriousness of the situation. You cover your eyes and loudly count to 10, then open them to look at the pocket watch.
You watch as the second hand ticks once, indicating a total of 11 seconds have passed.

speaker: Vanilla
content: I should explain more... Observation isn't just about seeing with your eyes. It's also about your consciousness and focus—what you're thinking about. That's what "observation" in the DisSea is.

speaker: Vanilla
content: ...Forget it, this might be too nerve-wracking for you.
You smile.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I think you're really strong. That big guy, you built it, right?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If we can complete it, perhaps we can break through that horde of monsters, with all the research materials and supplies in the camp!
Vanilla lifts her head, frowns slightly, but remains silent.

You squint your eyes. The bandage wrapped around her right leg is soaked with blood, and there's a stick for support. It could be a fracture, or a large open wound. Either way, it's not an injury that can heal quickly.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Hmm... It must be difficult to build such an enormous machine alone, especially with your injury. But now that I'm here...
You glance at Vanilla's injured leg.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm no good at building stuff, but I can help you collect materials. On the way here, I saw several abandoned settlements. There must be something useful there.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'll be careful and stay away from the storm or the monsters. You've taught me the ropes too—I'll run as soon as I see a monster.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I promise to only search around the camp. If something is wrong, I'll come back right away. I won't be in any danger.
Vanilla stares into your eyes, letting out a faint sigh.

speaker: Vanilla
content: ...Do you really want to leave that much?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I have to find a way out.
After a short silence, Vanilla finally budges:

speaker: Vanilla
content: Okay. I'll prepare everything for you tomorrow. Sleep now. You need rest.

options: It's okay, I'm not tired. I don't need rest.

content: You sit across from Vanilla, watching as she works. This is "observation," right?
Although you're not quite sure what the temporal storm thing is all about, it wasn't easy to get here and meet her. You don't want to fall asleep and "jump" to somewhere else.
But watching her, a sense of tranquility washes over you. You don't feel as tense, and after you loosen up, your eyes gradually...
You fall asleep.
When you wake up, your heart skips a beat the moment you open your eyes, but as soon as you lift your head, you see Vanilla sitting across from you, smiling.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Do you remember what happened before you fell asleep?
Yeah... You told me to sleep, I said I wasn't tired, and then I fell asleep...

speaker: Vanilla
content: ...<size=28>Pfft</size>.
Your eyes meet, and after a few seconds, she turns her face and chuckles.
A few minutes later, you're sipping on hot soup made from canned goods stored at the camp. Vanilla has finished the "time check" at the camp and has returned.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Nothing out of the ordinary. It seems the storm is less intense today.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Don't worry about what happened this morning, you can fall asleep. As long as I'm still here, no matter what happens when you wake up, even if time has gone wrong, I will protect you.
Vanilla takes off the pocket watch from her chest and hands it to you.

speaker: Vanilla
content: The pollution in the temporal storm interferes with comms, so I've modified this pocket watch. You can use it to contact the camp.

options: Thank you, I feel safer now.

speaker: Vanilla
content: There's more, come with me.
She leads you to the workbench, picks up the exoskeleton armor on the table, and sizes it up on you for a bit.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Try it on.

speaker: Vanilla
content: How does it fit here? Does it feel tight?
Vanilla points to your chest. The armor here is the thickest, but it's lined with soft cotton padding. The size is just right and you don't feel any discomfort.
Seeing you give an okay sign, she hobbles around you a few more times.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Is it heavy?
You try jumping a few times. The armor makes some metal clinking sounds, but it doesn't feel heavy.
But Vanilla seems to have noticed something and grabs a wrench from the table. She works fast. In just half a minute, she has finished tweaking.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Try jumping again.
You jump again, this time the armor doesn't make any sound.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Hmm... is there anywhere else that feels weird?
You stretch your limbs, trying to feel this added "part" on your body. This armor, modified by Vanilla, fits perfectly and you can hardly feel any weight.
Every part of this armor moves as if it were part of your body. No wonder it can unleash such immense power when worn by Vanilla.

speaker: Vanilla
content: That's great.
Vanilla seems to remember something and reminds you:

speaker: Vanilla
content: You can search around the camp, but don't go too far.

speaker: Vanilla
content: This exoskeleton armor is just a transportation model, it can't support high-intensity combat. But I have added a power module to it. If you encounter a tough enemy, run as fast as you can, you hear?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Loud and clear. But this was your armor, right? Did you stay up to modify it?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And if you gave me your armor, what about you then?

speaker: Vanilla
content: We have defense facilities in the camp. I never leave the camp anyway, so I don't need it.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Never? But didn't you leave the camp to save me?
She tilts her head and thinks for a moment.

speaker: Vanilla
content: You're right. Even machines go against their programming sometimes. So you have to be careful, don't put yourself in danger, or I will have to go out and find you.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Off you go. Be careful.
Upon returning to the camp, you unload the supply boxes on your back, then press the button on your arm to take off the entire suit.
The weather has gradually warmed up, you wipe the sweat off your forehead, and haul the armor and supplies onto the cart.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Just leave them here.
Vanilla pipes up from behind you, her voice as calm as ever. After such a long battle, it's hard not to feel reassured hearing her voice.

options: It's okay, I can handle it.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You already have to build the mech. Let me handle trivial things like this.

speaker: Vanilla
content: You've done a great job today.
Vanilla walks over to you, naturally taking over the cart. She's still limping a bit.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Just rest when you return to the camp. Leave the rest to the logistician.
As she speaks, she pushes the cart to the side of the workbench, then lifts the armor parts onto it.
She fishes out her tools, and repairs the armor in a swift manner. You've watched her do this many times, but you never get bored of it.

options: Where did you learn all this?

speaker: Vanilla
content: At the DisSea Observation Outpost.
Vanilla answers without looking up.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What is that place?

speaker: Vanilla
content: Just as the name suggests, it's a place that monitors the DisSea and records observation data.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Did the people at the outpost teach you mechanical skills?
Vanilla freezes for a moment.

speaker: Vanilla
content: No. I was the only one at the outpost.

speaker: Vanilla
content: There were many monitoring instruments that needed maintenance, and I learned as I went by fixing them.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Did you need to maintain exoskeleton armor and military mechs at the outpost as well?

speaker: Vanilla
content: No, but it's pretty similar to fixing monitoring instruments. I just need to connect the dots and apply what I've learned.
You might not know much about mechanics, but you do know maintaining monitoring instruments and military machinery are two different areas of expertise.
A self-taught mechanic who gets to this level of skills? It's truly impressive.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So the expedition team invited you because of your ability to "apply what you've learned"?

speaker: Vanilla
content: Not exactly.

speaker: Vanilla
content: The outpost was originally established to support the scientific expedition teams exploring the Black Ring. When the expedition team passed by, they were short on logisticians, so I joined when they invited me.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: They just wanted to recruit a logistician, and ended up with a mechanical expert.

speaker: Vanilla
content: ...You flatter me. There are others in the team who also dabble in the area, but as scientists, they have more important tasks.

speaker: Vanilla
content: I'm just helping out as much as I can as the team's logistician.
During the small talk, Vanilla has finished repairing the armor. She lifts her head to meet your gaze, her eyes carrying a gentle smile.

speaker: Vanilla
content: By the way, how do you feel about this armor after using it?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It's great, very handy.

speaker: Vanilla
content: You can drop the formality. I'm well aware that it's a suit built for transportation purposes. It has many limitations.
She glances at the sweat stains on your clothes.

speaker: Vanilla
content: I'm adding a cooling system to the armor. Is there anything else you want?
Hearing her suggestion, you make an attempt to tickle her funny bone.

options: I want a super power source.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Can you help make a pair of sturdy and powerful exoskeletal fists? I'd feel much safer.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Of course, I'm sure it will help a lot.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Maybe a set of speed-boosting prosthetics? I always felt like I wasn't fast enough when I was running away.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Sure.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Can you install a super-efficient power source, the kind that lasts a long time?

speaker: Vanilla
content: That's a great choice.
You didn't expect Vanilla to agree so easily, but seeing her clear and firm eyes, you find yourself at a loss for words for a moment.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Before you set off again, I'll have it ready for you.

speaker: Vanilla
content: It's nothing. Anyone could learn to do this.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Compared to what our scientists do, it's nothing, really.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Don't say that. I doubt anyone else in the team could build a mech on their own.
Hearing your praise, Vanilla raises her head, her expression as calm as ever.

speaker: Vanilla
content: I don't know the truth of the world, and I'm not good at fighting either. I'm not like you, so empathetic and understanding.

speaker: Vanilla
content: I'm just a logistician. This is the only thing I can help you with.

options: And you're doing an amazing job!

content: Vanilla smiles.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Thank you.
You put on your armor and wave at Vanilla, who is working on the scaffold of the mech not far away.
Hearing this, she pauses her work for a moment and looks at you.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Don't venture into dangerous areas just because I've upgraded your armor.

In order to find all the materials as soon as possible and take Vanilla out to solve the Illusory Moon crisis, exploring dangerous zones is inevitable. However, you simply nod at her without saying anything.
Fortunately, Vanilla doesn't delve too deep. She just smiles and waves goodbye.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Safe journey.
You quickly set down the supplies and then take off the armor and put it back in its original place.
You're getting better and better at these tasks. However, as the weather gets hotter, even with the cooling system that Vanilla installed for you, you're still sweating heavily.
After all this, you start looking for Vanilla in the camp. As expected, she's standing on the scaffold next to the mech, welding in the scorching heat.
Putting down her welding mask, Vanilla turns to look at you, and nods.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Welcome back.
You walk under the mech. Metal parts are all piled up here; long wires hang down from the scaffold, extending all the way to the generator in the distance.
You look up at Vanilla, her usual calm face is now covered in tiny beads of sweat and smeared oil stains, strangely amusing and adorable.
You glance at Vanilla's injured leg. Although the cast has been removed and she said she's fine, you're still a little worried about her doing such dangerous and high-intensity work.

options: Shall we take a short break?

speaker: Vanilla
content: Mmm, okay.
She casually sets down the mask and welder to the side, then sits on the narrow scaffold.
Unlike usual, she has her trouser legs rolled up, her slender calves hanging in the air, shining in a healthy color under the sun.
Now you can finally confirm that her leg injury has all healed up.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Why do you keep standing here?
Vanilla sounds puzzled, but with the light behind her, you can't see her face clearly.
This is not exactly an excuse. Since arriving at the camp, you've observed this giant mech countless times, wondering why it turned out like that in the outside world.
Or rather, what exactly happened to Vanilla over the past century? Why did her life's work turn into a source of pollution that distorts space-time?

speaker: Vanilla
content: Look at the mech...? Can you see it clearly from that angle?
With the light behind it, the mech is covered in shadow, and you can't see anything clearly.
But of course you can't tell her what you were thinking about, so you just scratch your head and laugh sheepishly instead.
Vanilla, however, was misled by your reaction, thinking that you really just wanted to see the big mechs but couldn't climb up to admire it up close.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Come, get closer.
Without giving it much thought, you walk over.
Vanilla leaps down from the scaffold, casually equips the mechanical arms nearby, and approaches you.
Before you can react, the mechanical arms have held you by your armpit, and there's a great force pushing you up. Your feet leave the ground, and you are lifted up by her.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Aah!
The sudden weightlessness catches you off guard, you close your eyes in fear, squirming a little.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Don't worry, I won't let you fall.
The mechanical arms move steadily, holding you mid-air without any shaking. After your rapid heartbeat gradually subsides, you slowly open your eyes.
Truth be told, you can't see a lot from this angle either, but you do discover something new.
Compared to when you first arrived at this camp, this huge yet intricate mech has undergone some shocking changes.
Under the light shining from somewhere, everything is illuminated.

speaker: Vanilla
content: How does it look from this angle?
Vanilla holds you up high, so you can clearly see your "work" from a higher angle.

speaker: Vanilla
content: What did you say?
You spoke too softly, Vanilla couldn't hear you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I was saying, you built such a big mech all by yourself... It's amazing. You're incredible!

speaker: Vanilla
content: Not by myself.

speaker: Vanilla
content: I couldn't have done it without you.
A smile blooms on Vanilla's face.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Yes, we're both incredible.
Since you observed it up close yesterday, you've become even more motivated to finish the mech.

You've explored and scavenged the relatively safe areas nearby, but the materials you gathered are still far from enough. Looking at Vanilla who's busy at the nearby workbench, you decide to try something new this time.
Without looking up, Vanilla simply waves goodbye to you.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Okay, be careful out there.
Vanilla lifts her head, the smile on her face is warm and firm.
You arrive at a crossroads, the sight of which makes you feel somewhat familiar. You realize this seems to be the place where you were rescued by Vanilla.
Unlike before, you now have experience dealing with monsters, and the armor made by Vanilla herself. You are somewhat tempted, thinking whether you can explore further.
Of course, you don't recklessly venture into the area, instead, you take out the telescope attached on your waist.
Although you were mentally prepared, you still gasp after you look into the telescope.

The monster you just fought is one of the most difficult ones to deal with so far. The fight wasn't easy at all. But now you see the same monsters in hordes. You can't even count their number at a glance.

Behind the monsters are those twisted glimmers and the storm, the gigantic shadow within the storm is barely visible. It resembles a leviathan patrolling its territory, blocking everything from approaching.
Just then, the pocket watch hanging on your chest suddenly vibrates—it's Vanilla.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Can you hear me?

speaker: Vanilla
content: You're taking longer than usual. Where are you? Did you run into trouble?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No, I just saw something.
She falls silent for a while.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Okay, as long as you're not in danger. I think it's better for you to come back now. We can talk when you're back.
Vanilla's voice gives you peace of mind. After hanging up, you take a deep breath and start analyzing the situation.
It seems that the military mech you and Vanilla are building is indispensable. Without it, you can't possibly break through the blockade of the monsters.
Now that you've collected enough supplies. It's time to head back.
After dinner, under the light of the campfire, Vanilla is repairing the damage on your armor.

After the sun sets, the temperature gradually drops. If not for the heat provided by the campfire, the chill would strip away all your warmth. The crackling flames, accompanied by the chirps of insects, paint a peaceful scene before your eyes...
But you are distracted, thinking about the sights you saw today and racking your brain for a foolproof way to break through.

speaker: Vanilla
content: You've been to some very dangerous places, haven't you?
Vanilla knocks at the horrifying scratches on the armor. Her tone remains flat, but you can detect a hint of worry.

options: I'll protect it better next time.

content: Vanilla shakes her head; that's not what she wants to hear.

speaker: Vanilla
content: What happened?
You don't immediately answer her, but your gaze unconsciously drifts toward the mech on the other side.

options: How's the progress on the mech?

speaker: Vanilla
content: If we calculate by working hours, it's about 75% finished.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...In that case, it shouldn't take too long, right?
Hearing your words, Vanilla stops her work and raises her head to look at you.

speaker: Vanilla
content: You seem anxious. What happened?

speaker: Vanilla
content: That day over the call, I remember you said you saw something?
Even Vanilla, who isn't very sensitive, has noticed your mood.
It's just her usual tone and way of speaking, but seeing how causally she brings it up, it unexpectedly evoke your desire to confide.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...I saw monsters, lots and lots of them.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And behind them, there's the light and storm, and the shadow within it... All of them seem to be preventing someone from approaching...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It's not just that. This entire space, it seems to be created to trap someone. Leaving here isn't as simple as I thought.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Honestly, I'm not so sure anymore.
Vanilla quietly listens to you. After a while, she walks away from the workbench, and sits down next to you.

speaker: Vanilla
content: That's some useful intel, with this, we now have an accurate assessment of our enemy.

speaker: Vanilla
content: We just need to make the necessary adjustments and ensure the improved design can handle those issues.

speaker: Vanilla
content: As long as we keep making progress on the mech at our current speed, and be well-prepared when we set out, there's nothing to be anxious about.
There's no sentimental comfort, nor any ingenious strategy. She just gave a simple analysis of the current situation and solutions to the predicament.
Strangely, these words bring comfort to your mind.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm glad you're here...
Vanilla nods quietly.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Speaking of, you're always so calm. I don't think I've ever seen you get anxious.
As you speak jokingly, you gaze at the peculiar scenery in the distance.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Aren't you afraid of this place?

speaker: Vanilla
content: Not really, because nothing really changed for me.
Vanilla answers in her usual calm tone, but her words make you tense up a bit.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Nothing changed?

speaker: Vanilla
content: Yeah.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Before I joined the expedition, I worked at an outpost near the DisSea and lived there alone for ten years.

speaker: Vanilla
content: There's no difference between here and the outpost.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Out there, there are no temporal storms, or abnormal timestream. People come and go, and things change. I would have thought...

speaker: Vanilla
content: ...For ten years, I looked at the same scenery every day: the desolate DisSea beach, the silent storm, the same sunrise and sunset. Same everything for ten years.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Humans can no longer change the world, for the world has been changed by the Perishing Star, and humans are now the ones being changed by the world. Everyone has the same look in their eyes, and to them, every day is the same.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Those travelers came from all over the world, but they all had the same look in their eyes, just like mine. Those were the eyes dyed by this desolate scenery. Each of their days was just like the last.

speaker: Vanilla
content: If there is such a thing as eternity, that must have been it...
Vanilla looks up at the sky, her voice soft and ethereal.

speaker: Vanilla
content: So whether it's the outpost, or this camp, it's all the same.

speaker: Vanilla
content: All I see is an unchanging scenery. There's no sign of humans, and no sight of the future. Disasters seem to be imminent, yet they never arrive.

speaker: Vanilla
content: It's as if time has stopped itself, and the world has stopped changing.

speaker: Vanilla
content: When I think like this, the temporal storms, and the chaotic time just can't scare me anymore.
Vanilla calmly recounts her experiences. The desolation has given her resilience, rationality, and wisdom.
But she seems to have forgotten how to embrace change.
How long have you been in this storm?
She thinks for a moment before answering.

speaker: Vanilla
content: I lost count.
...Do you want to leave with me?

speaker: Vanilla
content: You said you want to leave. I just want to help you.

options: What about you? Do you want to leave?

content: Vanilla doesn't answer, her expression as calm as ever.
You've always believed that you could bring her back, but right now, you're not so sure anymore.
This is a storm of Mania. How can someone, who has no hope for the future nor desire to change, break through this storm?
As the temperature drops day by day, the mech is finally about to be finished.
After working hard for the day, you sit again by the campfire, the warm glow of the fire illuminating her face.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I've thought about it for a long time, you said you can't imagine what the "future" looks like.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I, however, daydream about the future quite a lot. It's kinda amazing. Would you like to hear it?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Consider it... a silly fantasy of a child.
Sitting next to you, Vanilla nods with a smile.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: In my future... the expedition team successfully completed their mission and saved humanity.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: We've found a way to deal with the disasters. Civilization has a chance to be rebuilt.

speaker: Vanilla
content: That sounds great.
Vanilla smiles. You don't know if she's really imagining the scene you're describing or just agreeing with you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The disaster of the DisSea disappeared, and people rebuilt a city here.

speaker: Vanilla
content: A city? I've always lived in the outpost, I've never been to one.

speaker: Vanilla
content: What does a city look like?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It's enormous. It covers dozens of kilometers.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: From the outskirts of the DisSea, to your former outpost—it's all part of this city.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: We live there with many, many people... It will become the largest city in the world.
Vanilla listens, then ponders for a long time.

speaker: Vanilla
content: ...The largest city outside the DisSea? In this pollution?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Is it hard to imagine?

speaker: Vanilla
content: It is. Even Keylan, our daydreamer, would be taken aback to hear these things.

speaker: Vanilla
content: ...But you talked about it with such passion, and gave so many vivid details. You must have spent a long time imagining that future.

speaker: Vanilla
content: You make it sound like it'll really happen.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Humanity is saved, and civilization grows once again... Everyone in the expedition team would love to see that... Yes, they definitely will.
Vanilla pauses, smiling but looks slightly apologetic.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Me too, I guess... I'm not sure.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That's okay.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Just like how you can't imagine the future I talked about in this short amount of time, it took me a long time to understand your "unchanging" life and scenery.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Change always takes time. It's just that some changes take longer than others.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Even if everything else in the temporal storm hasn't changed, you've already changed.

speaker: Vanilla
content: What do you mean?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You joined the expedition team and came here.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If you had stayed at that outpost, I wouldn't have met you.

speaker: Vanilla
content: I'm not like them. They're... people who believe they can change the future. That's something I never imagined myself doing. I'm not that kind of person.

speaker: Vanilla
content: ...I just couldn't refuse them when they invited me.
She speaks calmly, but a genuine smile appears on her face.

speaker: Vanilla
content: But maybe change is about going with the flow sometimes. Who knows?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: There's one thing I hope will never change.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I want to be with you all forever, including going to the future.
On a chilly morning, you two finally finish adjusting the mech.
You bring the research materials of Vanilla's teammates, and stuff the rest of the space with as much food and medicine as possible.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Are you ready?
Vanilla's voice comes from above the mech.
White fog comes out of your mouth. You give her a thumbs up, signaling that you're ready.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Let's go, then.
The night has fallen. You and Vanilla set up a temporary camp on the safe high ground.
Perhaps the shadow hidden in the temporal storm has noticed your plan, the monsters you meet on the way here are much more difficult to deal with than before.
You take out the telescope and gaze at the center of the temporal storm from a distance.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Anything new?
You shake your head. As expected, nothing has changed.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Feeling nervous?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: We've come so far. What's there to be nervous about?

speaker: Vanilla
content: So... about the fight, do you have any plans?
You've thought of different tactics for the final battle, including igniting a large bomb to lure the monsters away, or passing through the monsters stealthy...
But soon you realize that most of your plans are impossible.
So you grin and say:

options: It's not much of a plan, really.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Just like we discussed before—we'll go full speed to shake off the monsters and avoid unnecessary fights... and then break through the temporal storm and leave.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: We've prepared so much in advance, I'm sure we'll make it.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Yes, you're right. We've made all the preparations, and done everything we can.
Vanilla smiles faintly while looking at the temporal storm.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Well then, let's roll.
Your long journey finally reaches the end.
You've found a gap amid the horde of monsters and break through the encirclement with the modified high-speed mech, shaking off those monsters. The temporal storm is right ahead of you.
The journey of crossing the temporal storm, for some reason, feels so long.
You two gallop across the wasteland, relentlessly marching forward... You journey across boundless time, from the past to the future, as everything rapidly falls away behind you two.
Even time can't catch up with you. The future is right ahead.
You're suddenly attacked by something. The violent jolts almost topple you over. It seems something has pierced the mech.

speaker: Vanilla
content: No way... What could catch up with my...
You look up to see a huge shadow above the mech.
The surface of the object above you is so decayed that you can't see its color; it's full of rust and scars... and standing atop it is a dark and ominous figure.

The monsters that appear multiple times in the same spacetime, the never-ending supplies... Now it finally makes sense to you. The ominous storm distorts spacetime, and this is where the past and future intersect.
You finally recognize the figure in front of you.
What you see subverts everything you know. Stunned, you turn your head in disbelief to look at the person beside you.
They look the same and pilot the same mech. But now, the Vanilla beside you is turning blurry.

speaker: Vanilla
content: You... are...
The shadow completely covers the mech, the despairing future swallows the past.
Both of the mechs and pilots gradually overlap, merging into one.
It feels like ages since she was swept into the center of the temporal storm, but Vanilla finally hears a familiar voice.

speaker: Faint Voice
content: <color=#7683a2>Those who went to investigate the distortion field haven't returned. Something's not right; we need to go take a look. We'll leave it to you here, Vanilla.</color>

speaker: Faint Voice
content: <color=#7683a2>There's still some distance to the danger zone, but space-time distortion is a trap, no one can predict what will happen. If we don't come back in time, you should pack up and return to the main camp as soon as possible.</color>
Before she can respond, another voice takes over.
<color=#7683a2>I can't leave, there's still a lot of equipment to fix. Don't worry, I can guard the camp. I'm good at waiting.</color>
It's her own voice, Vanilla sees another "her" waving goodbye to her companions. It's like she's watching a movie that records her unremarkable days.

speaker: Vanilla
content: I know these... I did the same. I stayed and waited for them to come back.
She keeps waiting.
One day, two days.

Three days, four days, five days... how long has it been like this? "Vanilla" quickly notices something out of the ordinary: defeated and broken monsters reappeared, used supplies being restored... The time around the camp is jumping, overlapping, and disordered.

speaker: Vanilla
content: <color=#7683a2>...Has the distortion field moved here? Looks like I'm the one being trapped now.</color>

speaker: Vanilla
content: <color=#7683a2>Heh, good thing the others left the camp, they should be safe.</color>

speaker: Vanilla
content: <color=#7683a2>Keep it up, scientists, keep heading toward the future you yearn for. The life of a logistician in exchange for all your safety, it's totally worth it.</color>

She calmly accepts her fate. Just like her days in the outpost, she tinkers with the mech to pass the time, and watches the same unchanging scenery every day. She's already used to living and waiting in this eternal stillness.
...Until someone else desperately breaks into the temporal storm to find her.
Yes, it's this moment. There's a commotion outside the camp, ${PlayerName} made a mess back then too.
"Vanilla" wears her armor and enters the storm, hoping to find the person in danger as soon as possible.

But the person who came is not ${PlayerName}, instead, "Vanilla" saved two of her teammates; one was already dead, the other severely injured. Shocked, she looks at their bloody wounds and feels a heart-wrenching pain.

speaker: Vanilla
content: <color=#7683a2>Why did you come back to an abandoned camp? The temporal storm is still here; it's dangerous.</color>

speaker: Injured Teammate
content: <color=#7683a2>...Because you're still here...</color>

speaker: Injured Teammate
content: <color=#7683a2>Don't worry, I'm not the only one who came, the others will be here soon... Oh right, time is distorted, you might have to wait a bit...</color>

speaker: Injured Teammate
content: <color=#7683a2>Don't worry, as long as you're here, everyone will definitely come... to take you back...</color>

speaker: Vanilla
content: <color=#7683a2>...Stop talking. Let's patch you up first before it's too late.</color>
"Vanilla" moves the teammate to the sickbed in the camp. After spending a dozen hours treating his wounds and watching over him, he's finally out of danger. She closes her eyes exhaustedly.
When she opens her eyes again, his bandages have disappeared, the sewn sutures have rotted and snapped, the infection has accelerated, and her companion died in front of her.

speaker: Vanilla
content: ...This is not my time. I never experienced this... If I knew things would turn out this way, I would have...
She knows what "Vanilla" would do. The other her buries her fallen comrades and sits quietly in front of the graves for a long time.

speaker: Vanilla
content: <color=#7683a2>As long as I'm here, everyone will come back... You said that the temporal storm is a trap, so "I" am now the <color=#fb9259>bait</color> in the trap...</color>

speaker: Vanilla
content: <color=#7683a2>...I'm the logistician, I'm supposed to stay put. You're the ones who are supposed to change the future... You shouldn't have gone this far for me.</color>
She stands up, looks at the camp, then at the forever half-repaired, damaged "mech." It can at least resist some dangers in the storm, perhaps it could bring her out of here faster.

speaker: Vanilla
content: <color=#7683a2>I can't stay here any longer. I... have to do something.</color>
"Vanilla" can no longer remember how long she's been trying to leave.

She's been pushing herself to the limit, working around the clock without any sleep. But the instant she dozes off, she finds herself engulfed by the currents of time, thrown back to where she started, or sometimes, even further back.
Her efforts are always easily erased, every step she takes is meaningless. Trapped in an eternal limbo, she can never reach the future.

speaker: Vanilla
content: <color=#7683a2>...It's just probability. This time the jump was short, only going back 30 minutes.</color>

speaker: Vanilla
content: <color=#7683a2>Given this is a rift of eternity, then surely not much time has passed on the outside. I can try as many times as I can bear.</color>

speaker: Vanilla
content: <color=#7683a2>There's still time...</color>
As usual, she adjusts her armor and sets off again.
The mech treks across the wilderness, relentlessly marching forward... She journeys across boundless time, from the past to the future, as everything rapidly falls away behind her.
She mutters to herself, unable to think of anything else.

speaker: Vanilla
content: <color=#7683a2>Almost there... almost done.</color>

speaker: Vanilla
content: <color=#7683a2>This time... time is on my side...</color>

As time continues to leap forward little by little, she's gradually shrouded in Mania, and the polluted mech becomes the center of the storm. Guided by Mania, the mech marches on, and eventually stops in front of Vanilla. The story has reached its end.

speaker: Vanilla
content: <color=#7683a2>I... made it out...</color>

speaker: Vanilla
content: <color=#7683a2>Where... should I go...</color>

speaker: Vanilla
content: <color=#7683a2>Who... am I...</color>
Vanilla stands in front of the decayed mech. The separated timelines intersect and gradually merge. The audience from the past finally reaches the finale in the future.

speaker: Vanilla
content: ...In the center of the storm, time is a tangled mess. My present, past, and future selves—each and every version of me may appear as an independent entity.

speaker: Vanilla
content: So that's it... Like you said, anyone can leave, change, and reach an ending they've never imagined... This is the end of the mechanic, the real Vanilla.

speaker: Vanilla
content: And I'm just a shadow from the past, a phantom in the storm, an existence that was only momentarily anchored by that child.
She gently caresses the mech she crafted with her own hands, which has now become weathered and decayed.

speaker: Vanilla
content: I'm but a fleeting moment of coincidence in this eternity, and will eventually meet a quiet end...
With a blinding red light, the illusion is broken, and Vanilla finds herself bound in the polluted metal.
The Illusory Moon is squirming in the sky. The red light falls and turns into pollution, and that child is fighting desperately.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Grab my hand and come with me! Don't be shaken! You're still alive and well. Let's leave this place together!

Vanilla is momentarily taken aback. Can he still be called a "child"? He's much taller now, and his gaze has hardened. He's suffered a lot of injuries as well. If it wasn't for that earring, Vanilla wouldn't recognize the little guide at all.
female_content: Vanilla is momentarily taken aback. Can she still be called a "child"? She's much taller now, and her gaze has hardened. She's suffered a lot of injuries as well. If it wasn't for that earring, Vanilla wouldn't recognize the little guide at all.

content: Is this also the effect of the temporal storm? To think that she can witness such an incredible miracle... And on the face of that miraculous person, there seem to be trails of tears.

speaker: Vanilla
content: So you've also seen everything too... I'm not the Vanilla you're looking for. The real Vanilla has already—

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That was an illusion! A trap created by the Illusory Moon, DisSea, and Mania to blind you!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It was the same for Dreya and Mantis. Those bastards like to peek into your minds, make use of your wishes or weaknesses. It's trying to trap you, to keep you here forever.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'll take you out. I won't leave you here!
What is ${PlayerName} talking about? Vanilla's not deceived by any red moon. She's very clear-headed now, surprisingly.
She sees the twisted moonlight wrapping around ${PlayerName}'s body. The red light has dyed his eyes crimson. His voice is wild and hoarse, his expression filled with immense pain.
female_content: She sees the twisted moonlight wrapping around ${PlayerName}'s body. The red light has dyed her eyes crimson. Her voice is wild and hoarse, her expression filled with immense pain.

content: The polluted mech roars loudly, trying desperately to push ${PlayerName} away, yet not to harm this person at the same time.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The polluted mech seems to be preventing someone from approaching...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This temporal storm, it seems to be created to trap someone...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I enjoy spending time with you.

speaker: Injured Teammate
content: As long as you're here, everyone will definitely come... to take you back...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: <color=#dg1f1f><size=44>I will take you back!</color></size>
Countless memories flash through in her mind, but the mechanic quickly sorts them out. She notices a sinister scheme amidst the anomalies.

speaker: Vanilla
content: ...The temporal storm is a trap, and "I" am a separate illusion within it, a bait in the trap. Is this... a coincidence?

speaker: Vanilla
content: The trap doesn't just trap me. It also traps the people who come to save me...

speaker: Vanilla
content: And the one who created this fake Vanilla to lure that child is... <color=#fb9259>you</color>...

She looks up at the Illusory Moon in the sky. It writhes and twists, its evil pulsations radiating greed. It eyes its prey, peering into his heart, grasping at his wishes and weaknesses... It wants to trap ${PlayerName}.
female_content: She looks up at the Illusory Moon in the sky. It writhes and twists, its evil pulsations radiating greed. It eyes its prey, peering into her heart, grasping at her wishes and weaknesses... It wants to trap ${PlayerName}.

content: Vanilla's body is merging with the mechanical remnants. The long years of memories are gradually corroding her thoughts, but she does not fear.

speaker: Vanilla
content: So... what would the real Vanilla do in this situation?

speaker: Vanilla
content: Would she succumb to her creator and fulfill the duties it gave her, or...
Smiling, she looks at the rusted mech, clenches her fist and raises her hand.

The mech creaks as it raises its arm high. A powerful force gathers at its front—it's the century-old temporal storm. It's now suppressed and controlled by a strong willpower, and turning into light in the rusty palm.
With a punch, the dazzling light instantly disperses the Illusory Moon's red light wrapping around ${PlayerName}.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Just like how my ten years at the outpost allowed me to master mechanics, my future self who has experienced eternity can also... master time.

speaker: Vanilla
content: I'm close to that future now. Once I get there, I can use her power to send you back.
As the power converges in her hand, Vanilla's body quickly weathers and decays, just like her creation that has experienced countless temporal jumps over the unimaginable long period of time.
I don't want you to become like that！ We're leaving together! I came here for you. I won't leave without you.
Since this is a temporal storm, come with me to my time. I'll be with you no matter how many times we have to jump. We'll get there someday! You did the same thing!
You can't just stop here. Keep going, you can go even further into the future!

speaker: Vanilla
content: Heh, you might have grown up, but you're still a child at heart.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Don't rush. Those who seek the future must have eyes to see the present clearly, you need to see your own path.

She takes off her goggles and puts them on your face. It blocks out the red light of the Illusory Moon, and the whispers in your head finally recede. Your restlessness fades, your breathing steadies, and you gradually see the face of the person in front of you.

speaker: Vanilla
content: I'm different now. I'm no longer stuck in place. I embarked on a journey of my own, and reached... a decent endpoint.

speaker: Vanilla
content: Perhaps the scenery hasn't changed much, but my future is far from finished, it'll keep going.

speaker: Vanilla
content: You will take it with you, and go far.
With the goggles adjusted, the broken lens refracts the chaotic time within eternity. She's smiling, but rapidly decaying.

speaker: Vanilla
content: I've never seen other sceneries, so this desolate view is everything to me. But my teammates have always believed that the world can be changed, and the scenery you brought back far exceeded our expectations.

speaker: Vanilla
content: I like the things that you told me about—the future city, the life you love, your new companions, and all those hopes you have for the future. Thank you for bringing these incredible memories here to see me.

speaker: Vanilla
content: It's time to go back now. Go back to your time. Go on your own journey, and into your own future.

speaker: Vanilla
content: This... is the meaning of our journey...

You don't know when she let go of her hand, her voice and figure gradually fade. At the same time, you feel something familiar from behind you while your head gradually clears. You know what this means.
—It's that stone slate. Vanilla's name must be on it, and lit up now to send you back. Everything is rapidly receding in your wake. She has harnessed the power to send you back to your time.
