But this only fills you with panic, you walk toward her with all your might, trying to catch the figure disappearing into the storm.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You can't stay here. Don't die, come with me! Vanilla...!
You want to dive deeper into the contamination. Your shackles are charged up, ready to unleash their power, when suddenly a burst of blue light pierces your vision.

speaker: FAC
content: Chief!

The light pierces your body and mind, instantly robbing you of all your strength. You fall to the ground as everything before you shatters. Vanilla is gone when the light fades. It takes a long time before you regain consciousness and realize...
You're back, to the "present time," the future of N.F. 114. The members of FAC are guarding you nervously, clearly there are more elites than before.
Schorl floats before you, observing... or rather, scanning you.
You quickly realize what has happened. Despite your exhaustion, your anger ignites in an instant.

options: Did you use the "Rules" on me?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I was so close to bringing her back! She's trapped in the DisSea. The Illusory Moon has caught her, and will continue to torment her!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Send me back. Someone is in the storm. I'll bring her back.

speaker: FAC
content: The temporal storm has ended, Chief... there was no one else but you. You're the only one the Illusory Moon was attacking.

speaker: FAC
content: Those things you saw were all illusions created by Mania to deceive you...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: She wasn't an illusion! They all existed at one point!
You struggle free of his grip and rummage in your coat, looking for the gift she gave you. You carefully tied it well on you so as not to lose it. Now you need it to prove that she's real.
...But you search everywhere, and there's nothing.

speaker: Vanilla
content: That's the real Vanilla. I'm... just a shadow from the past, a phantom in the storm.
You finally lose all your strength, the fatigue and pain accumulated completely overwhelm you. Supported by an FAC soldier, you collapse, covering your face.
After a while, you hear some footsteps that cause a slight commotion from the crowd, but they quickly fall silent. Someone has arrived.

speaker: Paradeisos 01
content: Although the operation had many incidents, they were expected, and the emergency plan was effective. Good work, Chief. I believe you've collected some valuable information in this operation.

speaker: Paradeisos 01
content: So... who did you meet this time?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The logistician and mechanic of the expedition team... Vanilla.

speaker: Paradeisos 01
content: Vanilla... that's a name I've never heard of. Thank you for bringing it back.

speaker: Paradeisos 01
content: They chose their own paths without any regrets. They don't need anyone to save them.

speaker: Paradeisos 01
content: Yet, we now remember them again despite death and the passage of time—that's the greatest purpose of your journey.

speaker: Paradeisos 01
content: Do you want to see them again?
Surprised, you look up at him. The man remains emotionless, calmly looking at you and waiting for your answer.

speaker: Paradeisos 01
content: Good. Set out again when your emotions can't cloud your judgment anymore, and you're able to face all of this with a clear head.

speaker: Paradeisos 01
content: You'll be ready once your emotions can't cloud your judgment, and you're able to face all of this with a clear head.
He turns to leave. It seems he came here just to say these words. A few guards open up a protective shield for him, but he refuses.

speaker: Paradeisos 01
content: The Illusory Moon is receding, we'll recover the relics of the expedition team later.

speaker: Paradeisos 01
content: With <color=#fb9259>that</color> here, this place is very safe.
You gaze at the menacing mech that was originally covered in contamination. Its pollution is long gone.
Above the mech, some Hypercube flowers have bloomed. The soft blue glow blocks out the red light of the Illusory Moon, quietly embracing you all...
And within the cluster of flowers, there's a glint of light. It might have worn out a bit, but you recognize it nonetheless...
It's the pocket watch that the mechanic gave you.

15:15, May 30, N.F. 114
Intelligence Center, FAC HQ

speaker: Comms
content: Warning! Monitoring Station 1 of the Broken Frontline has been <color=#fb9259>attacked</color>! I repeat, Monitoring Station of the Broken Frontline has been attacked!

speaker: Comms
content: The nature of the attack is unclear, but all lighting equipment is failing. We can't see anything!

speaker: Comms
content: We're hearing noise... scary noise... Please send reinforcements!!
The radio interference is getting more piercing. The HQ's screen is showing what's happening on the frontline. As the FAC soldier said, it's pitch black.

speaker: Comms
content: <color=#fb9259>Darkness</color>... We can't find the way... Can't get out... Going to be trapped here forever...
A significant portion of the frontline personnel are giving incoherent responses, clearly showing signs of mental disorder.

speaker: Comms
content: My leg... my leg! It should have recovered... but how come I can't stand up anymore...

speaker: Comms
content: Why... in this place... But they already died when...

speaker: Comms
content: There are too many of them... We can't win... Go away, arghhhh!
A brief burst of gunfire is heard, but it's quickly drowned out by a chilling growl and the sound of viscous liquid dripping.
After that, everything goes silent. The calls are never answered again.
15:19, May 30, N.F. 114, four minutes after the arrival of a new DisSea tide, contact with DisSea Monitoring Station 1 is lost.

20:21, May 30, N.F. 114
MBCC Chief's Office
Schorl, the <color=#fb9259>support</color> given to you by Paradeisos during <color=#fb9259>desperate times</color>, is floating noiselessly before you.

speaker: Schorl
content: The <color=#fb9259>unknown contamination</color> leaking from BR-000 has now fully covered Monitoring Station 1 and is spreading to Monitoring Stations 2 and 3.

speaker: Option
options: Should I head to the frontline?

speaker: Schorl
content: We would advise against that.
The voice from the device is void of emotions.

speaker: Schorl
content: FAC HQ has already launched a rescue. Currently, six frontline combatants have been saved with no physical injuries, only varying degrees of mental distress.

speaker: Schorl
content: Two of them are still conscious and have reported about the situation inside the contamination. So far, the threat posed by this DisSea tide appears significantly lower than previous ones and remains manageable.
Seemingly observing your reaction, the mechanical voice pauses briefly before speaking again.

speaker: Schorl
content: We understand how you feel and recognize your need for certain information. We are equally eager for news about the expedition, however...

speaker: Schorl
content: There's a very high chance that the DisSea tide is a trap designed for you. Your contact with the contamination might escalate the situation.

speaker: Schorl
content: Based on the current situation, we hope you can keep your distance from this DisSea tide and observe with patience.
The machine isn't lying. Your previous encounters in DisSea have already taught you painful lessons.
Dreya, Marguerite, and Vanilla all unknowingly became <color=#fb9259>bait</color> for the DisSea to capture you.
You can't make the same mistake again. Knowing full well they're gone, you shouldn't let the enemy tarnish their sacrifice.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I accept your advice and share your view. That said, I wish to keep up with the operation and be informed of all new developments. I want to reserve the right to participate in discussions on any emergencies.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Will Paradeisos... no, that man you represent, accept this proposal?
After a moment, Schorl gives its answer, coldly.

speaker: Schorl
content: Of course. He had expected this from you since the tide started to rise.

02:48, May 31, N.F. 114
MBCC Chief's Bedroom

You've been closely monitoring the frontline situation for over ten hours. Overall, things are looking optimistic. The contamination hasn't spiraled out of control, and more trapped individuals have escaped the mutated area.
But you can still feel the subtle connection between you and the DisSea. It's constantly influencing your mind, tempting you to venture into the contamination.
You set up several Hypercube shields in your bedroom.
Eleven hours have passed since the DisSea tide outbreak. You close your eyes.
The moment your consciousness returns, you feel enveloped by a heavy and viscous substance.
Sleep hasn't eased your fatigue. Instead, you find it hard to breathe.
Darkness.
It seems your retinas have completely lost their function. You see nothing but <color=#fb9259>endless darkness</color>.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Where am I?
You ask vigilantly out of instinct. But no response comes from the darkness.
You grope around in the dark for a long time, touching some familiar objects: a military Mania detector, Hypercube shields, and so on.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No, that's not right.
You were just in your bedroom. You haven't gone to the DisSea or come into contact with the contamination.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So, is this a dream? Has the Illusory Moon captured me again?
Enduring the unpleasant darkness, you stand up.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Looks like the only choice I've ever had is to face it.
As you reach this conclusion, the previously silent darkness begins to change.
Sounds reemerge in this space. A strange writhing noise in the darkness, the drip of liquid, and howls that seem to come from a wailing monster not far away.
Unperturbed by these oddities, you contemplate a crucial question instead.
As if hearing your question, several specks of <color=#fb9259>light</color> near you suddenly come into sight in the endless darkness.
Compared to the darkness itself, the light is so faint that it may well go out at any moment, yet it's so conspicuous against the pure darkness.
You have no other choice now. Going near a trap is better than going nowhere.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Stay cautious and be aware of the situation. I'm here to seek the truth, not to step into a trap.
Thinking this, you stride forward, wading through the darkness.
On your way to your goal, an unusual noise draws your attention.
<size=28>...We can't... we can't win...</size>
It's not a noise from a monster, but a human's mutters and pants.
Indeed, a person lies on the dark, viscous ground. Although it's partially covered in dirt, you still recognize the FAC uniform he's wearing.

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: So dark... Can't see... anything...
His face is ashen and his lips are trembling, muttering incoherently.
You reach out, and the moment you touch the armor, your hand passes through it like it's incorporeal.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I can't touch him? Is it because the DisSea has only captured my mind?
As you look for an explanation for this strange phenomenon, the FAC member on the ground suddenly props himself up and stands with difficulty.
A small <color=#fb9259>flame</color> emerges out of nowhere, fluttering in front of him as if leading him away.

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: Can't see... Can't go back...
You glance at the direction where the flame appeared and continue on.
You walk through the darkness for a long time. The spark illuminates the vague outline of a camp which resembles an abandoned campsite rather than an FAC structure.
Is someone there?
A figure approaches with a limp. It's a tall warrior in standard FAC armor.
I'm the captain of squad G83. Did you follow this flame here too?

speaker: FAC Captain
content: I got separated from my squad and sustained some light injury, but luckily I found this camp.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: There are medical supplies here... I'm looking for a splint. Hold on for a second, we'll retreat together.
The captain has a deep voice, but his breathing is shallow. He speaks as he comes closer to you, making out your face with the flame.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: You... you're... the MBCC's Chief?! Why are you here? Have they sent reinforcements?

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Hold on, where are your subordinates? And the guards? You shouldn't have come here. It's too dangerous here... I'll escort you out right away!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Keep going in this direction and you can leave the mutated area. As for me, I have to look into something. Don't worry, I'll be fine.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Then I'll go with you.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: I'll be ready as soon as I find a splint. Please give me a sec.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...That won't be necessary. I'm pressed for time. And I should be back soon if nothing unexpected comes up, so don't worry about me.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Then I'll wait here for you.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Please return as soon as you finish your investigation, and I'll escort you out.
The captain is determined. It's pointless to continue refusing.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Alright. I'll come back as soon as I can.
You turn around to press ahead.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Wait!
The captain calls out, produces a dim Hypercube, and tosses it to you.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: I don't know what your mission is or why it's worth risking your safety... but...

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Take care, and good luck.
You step into yet another dark swamp and see an increasingly bright light ahead, possibly the source of those strange flames. Without hesitation, you continue forward.
After a few steps, a sense of intense, reality-distorting danger suddenly washes over you. You're being watched.
Darkness obscures your vision, making it impossible to pinpoint anything's location, but you can hear eerie growls and smell a strong stench.
After a few seconds of standstill, the thing moves. It strikes from behind, piercing your body so fast that you cannot resist.
You turn your head, and the last things you see are two <color=#dg1f1f>blood-red eyes</color>.
You jerk awake from the nightmare and hear Schorl's toneless voice.

speaker: Schorl
content: We detected your psyche nearing the danger threshold and initiated the <color=#fb9259>emergency revival protocol</color>.

speaker: Option
options: I was captured by the DisSea in my dream.

content: You waste no time and immediately explain the situation to Schorl.

speaker: Schorl
content: I see. It seems we've underestimated the danger of this phenomenon.

speaker: Schorl
content: I've reported the situation. Paradeisos will adjust the response strategy accordingly. In the meantime... please enhance your protection and keep your mind as stable as possible.
You wake up and find yourself once again enveloped by the omnipresent darkness.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...What happened? Why am I back?
You remember reporting the situation to Schorl and analyzing various possibilities. You should be awake now and away from this somber dream.
But the next moment, you slip into a slumber and return to the darkness.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Is something wrong with my memory? Could it be I have never woken up?
As your mind clears up gradually, you quickly dismiss the thought.
This is the dreamscape twisted by the phenomenon. Reality is on the other side.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I see. So I'll always end up back here.
It's only a matter of time before Schorl notices the issue and wakes you up. You can choose to wait right here, or...

The nearby sounds become increasingly <color=#fb9259>rich</color>. Crying that feels too close to your ear, dreadful monster growls... More sounds pour into your ears. Crisp ringing of metal bells, unintelligible murmurs, human sobs...
Crossing through the darkness, you gradually make out the dim flame in the distance.
Despite its dimness, it's bright enough to illuminate this unnatural darkness. And the pitch-black terror accentuates its warmth and stability, evoking an irresistible longing, especially for you.

speaker: Schorl
content: Keep your distance and observe with patience.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I know how to handle it.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But there's something I must do.
As you find your resolve, something turns its gaze upon you in the darkness.
The shackles' red light flickers, readying you for battle.
After walking for what feels like an eternity, the unknown monsters pestering you along the way gradually vanish. You begin seeing some fine ropes tied to the trees in the woods.
The ropes are wrapped with old cloth strips and attached to rusty bells. In the windless darkness, only your passing makes them ring softly, as if signaling a boundary or a warning.
The feeble light that draws you here floats just beyond a few ropes, almost within reach.

In the darkness, the sparks reveal a small clearing, where a few dry branches on the ground form a not-so-round magic circle less than a meter wide. The lines are crooked, the pattern simple, leaving its specific meaning unclear.
You break off a twig and throw it into the center of the circle. Nothing happens. You erase part of the circle with your hand. Everything remains the same.
It seems there's no mysterious power to this thing. Someone was probably just doodling here with a stick dipped in water.

The dead branches, the hanging bells, the circle, and the faint sparks that illuminate the darkness... This resembles some kind of mysterious ritual to keep the monsters away. It's not the FAC's style, and you can't imagine any scholars from the expedition coming up with this.
The drawing hasn't dried yet, with blurry footprints within and around it. The person who drew the circle was here not long ago but seems to have left in a hurry.
...Are they really gone? Your senses in the dream feel particularly sharp, detecting some kind of presence from the darkness behind you.
You turn toward the unlit spot, following your intuition into the darkness, your hand tightly gripping the shackles.
Sure enough, having walked less than two meters, you hear something.
If this crude trap was indeed made for you, its maker probably wouldn't come out to meet you until you fell into it. Anyway, it's just a dream...
You walk straight into the center of the circle, stretching out your body exaggeratedly. And then, just as you wish...
Ia! Cthugha!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What?

A shrill cry pierces the darkness. Sparks burst out of the circle on the ground while the surrounding bells ring loudly, besieging you. Startled, you turn to the ringing bells and immediately realize they're a decoy.
Behind you, a massive club as tall as a person suddenly breaks through the darkness and lands right on your head.
Die, monster!
Aaahhh—!!
You dodged the attack, and the figure stumbles and topples past you.
The attacker seems unable to wield the heavy club, losing balance and falling to the ground with a cry.
No, no, no! Stay away from me!

Failing to get up, the person desperately scrambles backward. The courageous determination just now has completely evaporated, and she now tries to hide from your gaze in the darkness, nearly sobbing.
But the floating flames quietly gather around her, dispelling the shadows and revealing a petite figure.

It's a short and frail girl with a pale tear-streaked face. She wears a strange robe and no shoes, her legs covered in mud and wounds. The long torch she holds is probably the weapon she used to attack you.
She trembles violently, cornered against the roots of a tree, curling up into a ball.

speaker: Girl in Strange Clothes
content: No... Get away, monster... If you dare come a step closer, I-I'll...
Monster? Is she talking about you?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm not a monster. I'm a human, just like you. Take a good look at me with the light, okay?
Yet she gasps in fear and shrinks even smaller.

speaker: Girl in Strange Clothes
content: You're covered in <color=#fb9259>red spikes</color>... You're a monster! Back off! Don't talk to me. I won't fall for your trap!

speaker: Girl in Strange Clothes
content: I can see. Even if you're cloaked in human skin and speak the human language, I can tell. The holy fire will guide me. I'm not... I'm not blind!
At this, you instinctively search for her eyes...

Her eyes are too pale and dim. Although her gaze occasionally falls on you, it just seems unfocused. She's waving the torch frantically to keep you away, seemingly without any idea where you really are, as if she can't see you.
Is she blind? Or visually impaired? It appears she can only roughly discern your location by sound.

speaker: Girl in Strange Clothes
content: The holy fire will purify you, and the Pyromater will punish you, I... I'm not afraid of you! I have people coming to help me!

speaker: Girl in Strange Clothes
content: They're all elite scientists who know how best to deal with you! They'll be here soon. I'm their important guide. If anything happens to me, you're done for! We clear?!

speaker: Girl in Strange Clothes
content: So go away and grovel back to your own god. Stop bothering me! Back off!
You raise your hand to catch the torch swung at you, effortlessly removing it from her hands. Shocked, the girl tries to get up but collapses heavily to the ground.

speaker: Girl in Strange Clothes
content: No, no... I don't want to die here...

speaker: Girl in Strange Clothes
content: Captain! Helen! Where are you? Help me!
You stop approaching but instead step back a little and begin softly.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I won't come any closer without your permission. I just want to talk to you.

speaker: Girl in Strange Clothes
content: Go away!
You hold back the shackles and squat down to meet her eyes.

speaker: Option
options: Are the red spikes still there?

content: Still wary, she doesn't answer, but there's a hint of consideration in her expression, as if she's trying hard to tell.

speaker: Girl in Strange Clothes
content: ...Where did you hide those spikes of light? Are you... a shapeshifter?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This is how I've always looked. Those spikes are just a weapon I use for self-defense. Just like you need the torch, I need something to protect myself too.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But we're not enemies. I'm not going to hurt you, so I've put it away.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If you promise not to hit me with the torch again, I'll give you back your weapon so you can feel safe, okay?
You say as you squat down and offer her the torch. The girl doesn't take it, her pale eyes warily staring in your direction.

speaker: Option
options: Just now, you said you have companions?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Where are they? Did you get separated from them?

speaker: Girl in Strange Clothes
content: ...Like I'll tell you.

speaker: Option
options: I'm also looking for some friends. A team of scholars.

content: She sits up abruptly.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It consists of a calm, knowledgeable girl who loves stargazing, a girl who loves to laugh and knows a lot about biology, and a mechanic who doesn't talk much but is in fact very kind...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: They're all very nice people and brilliant scientists. They should be around here too.

speaker: Girl in Strange Clothes
content: <color=#fb9259>Dreya, Marguerite, and... Vanilla...</color>

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Just like you, I'm looking for them too. If you're a guide, can you show me the way?
She relaxes her tense body, "looking" in your direction.

speaker: Girl in Strange Clothes
content: ...Are you also part of the <color=#fb9259>expedition</color>?

speaker: Girl in Strange Clothes
content: But I've never heard your voice...
You hesitate. As you deliberate for an answer, she props herself up slightly, fumbling in front of her as if looking for something to support herself. You offer her the torch.
But the girl doesn't take it. Her bony hand reaches toward you, trembling as it lands on your cheek. At the moment of contact, you freeze.
Unlike others in the dream who pass right through you, her fingertips rise and fall repeatedly, every touch incredibly gentle and clear in the silence.

Cheekbones, eyelids, eyebrows, the tip of your nose, the corners of your mouth... She carefully traces the contours of your face with her hands. The gaze on you remains hollow, yet you see emotions slowly exuding from her eyes.

speaker: Girl in Strange Clothes
content: I've never heard your voice, but somehow... I recognize you. You feel familiar... just like everyone else...

speaker: Girl in Strange Clothes
content: ...How strange. How could I mistake you for a monster? It never happened with anyone else on the team before...

speaker: Girl in Strange Clothes
content: I'm so sorry. I can't see very well, and being here all alone for far too long really made me paranoid... I hope I didn't hurt you.
The flames illuminate her face. She smiles at you, but tears are streaming down her cheeks uncontrollably.

speaker: Girl in Strange Clothes
content: Haha, don't worry. I'm just too happy, so happy. I...

speaker: Girl in Strange Clothes
content: ...Ever since splitting up with you guys, I've been terrified.

speaker: Girl in Strange Clothes
content: It's so dark here and monsters are everywhere. I'm so scared. In my dreams, bad things often happen to you guys, so you can never return... But thankfully, you...

speaker: Girl in Strange Clothes
content: You're still alive... How wonderful...
Her voice dwindles and her hands rest on your chest feebly to support herself as she bows her head and sobs.
Before you even realize it, you've raised your arms around her, as if ready to embrace her tightly, as if you're also overwhelmed by a certain surging emotion...
You pause and withdraw your arms, only putting your hands on her shoulders.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're fine now. I've found you, and I'll protect you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're a member of the expedition too, right? I'm often out on missions. I don't think we've met before. What's your name?
You hold her up by her trembling shoulders and ask gently.
Your words have soothed her. Slowly, the girl stops sobbing and squeezes out a funny smile.

speaker: Girl in Strange Clothes
content: I'm Hestia. What about you?

speaker: Hestia
content: I must remember your name and your face, so I won't make the same mistake again.
She wipes her tears and smiles. Reaching out with both hands, this time she presses her warm palms on your face boldly, cupping your cheeks and tracing your ears with her fingers.
And then as Hestia touches your <color=#fb9259>earring</color>, she freezes for a moment.

speaker: Hestia
content: This earring...

speaker: Hestia
content: It's you?!
Her smile vanishes, her face flushes, and her eyes widen. She shoves you with both hands, surprisingly pushing you down to the ground.

speaker: Hestia
content: You little punk, are you playing me for a fool?!
The next instant, the long torch is swung up again and this time lands square on your forehead. With a buzz in your head, everything goes black...
[Flash]
Your eyes snap open. Before you, Schorl is performing a scan on you, pulling you back to reality.

speaker: Schorl
content: You just fell into a dream of the Illusory Moon again.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...I made primary contact with some people.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If I can go back, I should be able to get useful information.

speaker: Schorl
content: Your speculation is correct. Paradeisos has yet to find a way to solve this problem. When your mind is weak, you might get captured again.

speaker: Schorl
content: You may continue <color=#fb9259>exploring</color>, but please don't be ensnared by the Illusory Moon again.
You look at your hands. Your forehead doesn't hurt, but the touch and the warmth you felt when patting her back still linger in your palms.
In that interwoven dream, people existing in reality couldn't touch you. If the girl could touch you, it can only mean...
That was just a <color=#fb9259>trap</color> to lure you in.
You clench your fists and teeth.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm aware of the situation. Next time... I won't fall for that again.
You don't have to wait long before your next return. After reporting and confirming new survivors for almost twenty hours, you're finally sent back to rest.
And the moment you lie down, you're back in that somber dream.

Someone touches your forehead gently. You open your eyes slightly and see Hestia sitting by your side, her gaze wandering. She probably hasn't realized you're awake, her expression somewhat concerned and uneasy.
You cough softly. She immediately withdraws her hand and puts on an annoyed expression.

speaker: Hestia
content: Why did it take you so long to wake up?

speaker: Hestia
content: You passed out for a long time. I tried and tried but couldn't wake you up. You freaked me out!

speaker: Hestia
content: Nonsense. How could I knock you out with your thick skin?

speaker: Hestia
content: ...Besides, you tricked me first. You changed your voice and pretended to be an adult. Think you could fool me just like that because I can't see?

speaker: Hestia
content: Nasty little punk. I'll tell the captain about this when we get back.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Fine.

Your voice hasn't changed, nor has your appearance. But in her eyes, you've obviously become that <color=#fb9259>child guide</color> once again. No matter who you meet, you're always playing the same role of a person you don't know.
...It doesn't matter anymore. Knowing this is an <color=#fb9259>encounter</color> under the Illusory Moon, you won't be led by the nose again. You stand up and look around.

speaker: Option
options: Do you know how to get back to the expedition?

speaker: Hestia
content: ...What get back? Just wait here.
Hearing your voice from above, she seems a bit irritated and stands up too.

speaker: Hestia
content: Listen, little punk. I know we'd barely talked before, but now that we've decided to stick together, let's get a few things straight.

speaker: Hestia
content: I'm Hestia, the priestess of Stor Town, the oracle of the Pyromater, and the prophet of Nightfall. I have two hundred followers under me, and more importantly, a pair of eyes that can see through darkness.

speaker: Hestia
content: Never fooled by illusions, they allow me to see the truth in darkness. God has guided me here to enlighten the lost lambs, and it's your expedition who's asked me to stay and provide assistance.

speaker: Hestia
content: Got it? I'm your guide, so treat me with respect and trust. Heed the priestess's advice, for only I can lead you out of this forbidden land alive.
She stands up to you defiantly, while you recall how not long ago the priestess was scared into a teary mess just because her torch got snatched.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: OK.

speaker: Hestia
content: Hmm, keep that in mind.
Then, she begins listening carefully to the surroundings and even lowering her voice a bit.

speaker: Hestia
content: Monsters lurk everywhere except this spot. We're safe here.

speaker: Hestia
content: I've set up an alarm with bells. Stay near the magic circle and nothing will happen to you. Don't run around, and keep your voice down. Too much noise will attract them.

speaker: Hestia
content: I still have plenty of food here. Enough to last until they come for you.
Hestia pats that little battered messenger bag she carries.

speaker: Hestia
content: So, who were you with? How did you get separated from them?

speaker: Option
options: I came alone to find you.

speaker: Hestia
content: What?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No other adults are coming. We have to go find them ourselves.

speaker: Hestia
content: Stop talking nonsense!
Conscious of her raised voice, Hestia pats her chest and speaks more softly.

speaker: Hestia
content: Even adults may not be able to take down the monsters around here, what can two kids do? We'll be eaten alive the moment we step out!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Aren't you a powerful priestess? Use your magic circle to get rid of the monsters.

speaker: Hestia
content: The priestess is not adept at combat. I can only guide the way, leading you away from danger. This forbidden land is governed by the most atrocious deity. Those who do not heed the oracle will surely be...

speaker: Option
options: Do the scholars believe what you say?

content: Interrupted by you, Hestia pauses, flushing instantly.

speaker: Hestia
content: W-what...? Don't they also call you "Guide"? You're even younger than me, yet you always lead everyone around with your gibberish... If they can believe you, why can't they believe me too?

speaker: Hestia
content: The Pyromater Sect of Stor Town is well-known in the deserts. I have followers everywhere. Do you think you can convince every one of them I'm a liar?
She says and knocks her torch against the ground, mustering a semblance of fragile authority.

speaker: Hestia
content: I have already informed the captain of the situation. The priestess has accompanied you guys on your journey for too long. I must rest. That's why I stayed behind to wait for the expedition's return.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: OK.

speaker: Hestia
content: Such a safe hideout is hard to come by around here, so don't wander off. Stay here and wait for the adults to get us.

speaker: Hestia
content: I'd rather it be anyone else but this little punk... What a nuisance.
She obviously doesn't like you too much, but it doesn't matter. You're more than happy to keep a distance.

speaker: Option
options: Since it's safe here, you should stay.

speaker: Hestia
content: Huh?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I can protect myself. That red light you were so afraid of is my weapon. It's got me covered. I came all the way here with its help, I'll have no problem carrying on.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Since I'm a guide too, I should find my own way out.

speaker: Chief
content: Hey, you! Wait!
She stops you with her torch hastily, but you stride right over it.

speaker: Hestia
content: Wait a second!
Her panicked call stirs an eerie echo in the darkness. Shuddering, the girl stands up and bumps into your back, grabbing onto your clothes.

speaker: Hestia
content: I... I'll go with you. You're too reckless. I must keep an eye on you so you don't die and make everyone sad.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Okay.

speaker: Hestia
content: I am not scared!!
You don't persist, letting her clutch the hem of your clothes while you lead the way, grateful that your mind still remains calm.
Stay calm. This is just a trap... You remind yourself.

speaker: Hestia
content: Don't walk too fast. Stay close to me.
She stays half a step behind you, gripping your arm tightly. Her hands are cold and tremulous.
She frowns and pokes you with her torch.

speaker: Hestia
content: Show some respect. Don't push it.

speaker: Hestia
content: I know this darkness better than you do. A reckless fool like you is bound to run into trouble sooner or later.

speaker: Hestia
content: Just don't beg me to save you when a monster jumps out of the darkness and drags you away...

speaker: Option
options: What kind of monster? What does it look like?

content: Hestia takes a deep breath and begins to describe that so-called monster.

speaker: Hestia
content: It is... the physical manifestation of divine malice, the embodiment of fear without a fixed form.

speaker: Hestia
content: If I must describe it in words, well... It's entirely black, covered in a viscous liquid, like a beast that has been skinned.

speaker: Hestia
content: Pain and fear drive it mad. It cannot die, or should I say, it's already dead. That's why its howl... sounds like someone crying...
As she depicts it with chilling details, the girl's breathing grows shallower.
Suddenly, you hear a subtle noise in the air, like a whimper or a painful groan, which makes one's hair stand on end.
Wooo... Awooo...

speaker: Hestia
content: Its... its eyes are red... blood-red... Once you've seen them, you can never erase them from your memory...
The sound draws nearer, quickly becoming deafening. Meanwhile, two blood-red specks of light flit toward you in the darkness.
The girl's face is filled with terror, her entire body trembling uncontrollably.

speaker: Hestia
content: It's... It's...

The monster reveals itself right before your eyes. Just as Hestia described, its eyes are blood-red, and its black body is constantly twisting and morphing, with a petroleum-like viscous fluid dripping from it, leaving filthy traces on the ground.
The girl evidently senses the terrifying presence.

speaker: Hestia
content: It's here... Run!!!

speaker: Monster
content: Ahh... Wooo... Awooo...
You weave through the narrow valley while the monster follows you like a shadow, its eerie howls never ceasing.
Heavy footsteps shake the ground. Pieces of rocks and soil keep falling upon you.

Turning around, you see the monster's massive body squeezing through the valley, rolling toward you. Like a black torrent, it tears down the protruding grass, wood, and stones from the valley walls, engulfing every inch of land in its path as it surges toward you.
In the pitch-black darkness, only those red eyes flicker constantly, always fixated on you two.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This thing sure is a handful.
The monster's steps grow closer. It will catch up eventually. But there's no time to think, and all you can do is run as fast as you can.

speaker: Monster
content: Ahhh... Awooo...
The monster squeezes its massive body through the narrow valley, its black claws almost reaching you.
The quaking of the ground significantly slows you down. It's only a matter of time before you get caught.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What's Schorl doing... Why hasn't it woken me up yet?
You try to tell yourself to stay calm, but the situation is making you extremely nervous.
Swish—
While you're distracted, a fierce attack strikes, grazing your back.
You feel something being drawn out from your back. Intense burning pain follows, almost making you scream.

speaker: Hestia
content: No!
The shackles' red light flickers, instantly forming spikes that fly toward the monster behind you.
But the attack that would have killed most Corruptors simply sinks into the monster's body silently like a rock dropping into the ocean.

speaker: Monster
content: Hiss... Hah...
The monster lets out a mocking scream, its huge red pupils staring straight at you, the rotten stench of decay assaulting your face.
The pain in your back becomes increasingly unignorable, burrowing deep into your body together with fear, blurring your vision.
In a daze, you see several hands cling to your body.

speaker: Deranged Scholar
content: ...I can't die here. I haven't reached the truth yet... Guide me, show me the way... Take me where the moon rises, beside the abyss... to see the Perishing Star that fell...

speaker: Contorted Mantis Queen
content: My companions... Our companions... I can't leave them behind... Let go of me. I must go back. I can't lose anyone else...

speaker: Rusty Machine
content: I'll just stay here... I'm already used to it. I'll accept any outcome... But you...

speaker: Rusty Machine
content: Why did you come? You know it's a trap. You know you can't change anything...

speaker: Rusty Machine
content: And the meeting alone causes you unbearable pain...

Shadows of the departed surround you and non-human arms climb onto your body, entangling your limbs. Their gruesome corpses force you to face the past while fear consumes your body and consciousness voraciously.
You try to escape, but the illusion morphs into a faceless girl with a torch whispering indistinctly, grabbing and pulling at you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Back off!
Fear takes over all thought. You want to retreat, afraid to see another dead face. But that person doesn't let go.
She lunges at you again, this time raising her weapon high, smashing it at you.

speaker: Hestia
content: Wake up!!
A burst of sparks. It stings your eyes, changing the scene in your vision abruptly.
Before you, an ashen-faced Hestia raises her torch and smashes it down behind you repeatedly, each hit eliciting a scream. Startled awake, you realize you're entangled in the monster's tentacles.

speaker: Hestia
content: Let go! Let go!! Let go of him!!!
female_content: Let go! Let go!! Let go of her!!!

content: Her tearful attack lacks strength, but the monster seems to suddenly weaken, howling as it releases the tentacles binding you. Dodging the sparks, it quickly retreats into the darkness, the massive impact shaking the ground.
Before you register what you see, she drags you up from the muddy ground.

speaker: Hestia
content: What are you waiting for?! Run!!
While the monster is temporarily hiding, the two of you keep running until you both exhaust your strength and must take a break in a cave.
Hestia sits collapsed on the ground, both her legs and her hands holding the torch still shaking, but she doesn't stop grumbling.

speaker: Hestia
content: ...You idiot... Idiot!!

speaker: Hestia
content: I've told you the monster can't be killed. Why must you push your luck? That red light of yours is useless. You're even shorter than me. Did you really think you could take on that thing?!

speaker: Option
content: ...Thanks for saving me.

speaker: Hestia
content: There won't be a next time! I'll let you die if it happens again! Sob...
The girl gasps for air, her hands and legs shaking violently, tears streaming down uncontrollably.

speaker: Hestia
content: I, I'm out of strength. The monster will catch up soon. We're really going to die this time, aren't we? Oh no, what should we do...
It's hard to believe she just ran up to you and beat up that monster she feared so much and actually drove it away.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Well...
This whole time, you've been constantly reminding yourself to stay rational and see Hestia as a trap set by the Illusory Moon instead of a companion. You've been keeping your guard up against her.
But now, it seems you might have misread the situation. To defeat that monster, you need her help.

speaker: Hestia
content: What?
At the mention of an <color=#fb9259>idea</color>, Hestia scoots closer as if grasping at straws.
But considering it comes from that <color=#fb9259>little punk</color>, she seems somewhat hesitant.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I've thought of a way to deal with that monster.

speaker: Hestia
content: Are you insane? Going to get yourself killed again?!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Just hear me out...
Despite her skepticism, this still gives her a glimmer of hope, so she moves closer...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Although my attack didn't work earlier, you managed to hurt it. Why do you think that is?

speaker: Hestia
content: Don't know, just luck I guess...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Because you were being brave just now.

speaker: Hestia
content: Brave? Me?
The girl looks incredulous, then asks.

speaker: Hestia
content: Let's just say... I was being brave. But what does that have to do with hurting the monster?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It makes all the difference.
It concerns the root of this darkness, where we need to go, and...
You lean forward slightly, moving closer to the girl.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And how we... defeat that monster!
Boom—
As the detonator blows the supporting branches apart, the ground collapses instantly, revealing a hollow.

speaker: Monster
content: Wooo... Awoo!
Growling, the monster tumbles into the trap you've set up in advance.
Spikes of red light form in the air, sharp tips impaling the monster's massive body, firmly pinning its upper half exposed outside the trap.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It worked!

speaker: Monster
content: Awooo... Wooo... Awooo!
The monster's black body struggles violently, trying to break free from its restraint and crawl out of the trap.
The ground shakes intensely, and the painful growls almost pierce your eardrums.
The girl peeks out from a cave nervously, her body supported by the long torch.

speaker: Hestia
content: What... what should I do?
The monster's struggle drains you significantly, but you still turn your head.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Remember what we talked about... What we agreed upon!

speaker: Hestia
content: What we... talked about...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Marguerite once told me that the emotions of nearby humans could influence creatures in the DisSea, causing them to change.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If you fear it and believe it immortal, it'll become especially powerful and truly unbeatable.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: On the contrary, if you face it bravely, it'll become nothing more than an ordinary monster, many of which our expedition has defeated before.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Red eyes, black body, inconsistent form, covered in thick, sticky liquid.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Look, it might just be a monster you've imagined, materialized by the DisSea to incite fear in you and make you believe you can never win.

speaker: Hestia
content: Then... What should I do?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It's simple.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Vanilla's left me some equipment. We can use it to set up a trap.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Also, Dreya's said that the red moon enhances monsters' power. Now that the sky has turned cloudy, the clouds will soon shroud the moon and weaken the monster.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: When the time comes, I'll restrain it with my red light. As for you, just hit it with your torch or a stone. Whatever you can manage, just do it.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Above all, do not be afraid. Muster your courage and trust that we can defeat it.
Facing the massive monster, the girl now has something just the right size in her hands. This is probably the largest stone she can lift.

speaker: Hestia
content: It's impossible, I can't do it... It was pure luck last time. I can't do it. I'll get killed...

speaker: Hestia
content: What courage... It's all nonsense. You liar! I'm not doing this, I...

speaker: Monster
content: Roar!!!

speaker: Hestia
content: Ahhh!!!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The moon is shrouded. Go!
Indeed, you made up that theory about the clouds and the red moon. But right now, they become the last straw that snaps the girl's nerves.
The girl's face flushes and her eyes brim with tears. She lifts the stone high above her head with both hands.

speaker: Hestia
content: Back off!
The small stone arcs through the air, seemingly carrying a bright, warm flame, and lands on the monster feebly.
The hit clearly lacks force, yet the monster explodes into sharp cries.

speaker: Monster
content: Awooo!!!
The flame kindles the liquid darkness and the fire rages on rapidly. The monster flips and turns in the fire, dwindling.
Eventually, its massive body burns out completely and vanishes, leaving only a faint burned smell in the air.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Phew...
You let out a long sigh. After countless challenges, you finally defeated the monster you once thought invincible.
You come next to the girl, patting her on the shoulder.
But she just stands there silently for a long time.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What's wrong? Are you still scared...
Before you can finish, Hestia suddenly speaks up.

speaker: Hestia
content: We...

speaker: Hestia
content: Won?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Yeah, we won beautifully. If only you could see it. The monster turned into a big firework at the end. Whoosh, and it vanished in the fire...

speaker: Hestia
content: Has it really... disappeared?
Tears swirl in the girl's eyes. Her body is so weak she can barely stand. Even the torch she never parts with falls aside.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Why are you crying? We won...
The moment you touch her, the girl dives into your arms and bursts into tears.

speaker: Hestia
content: (Crying loudly)

speaker: Hestia
content: What kind of plan was that? I really thought I was going to die! Idiot! You stupid, arrogant little punk! I'm never listening to you again!!
Her cotton-light punches bounce off you. You can no longer hold back your laugh.

speaker: Hestia
content: Don't laugh!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: We're still alive. Two kids have beaten the big monster and uncovered the truth behind this darkness. We don't have to be afraid anymore!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Let's go, Hestia! Back to the expedition! We'll tell everyone that both of their little guides are super amazing! Everyone will be proud of you!
Hestia grabs your hand and musters all her strength to get up, but her legs give out and she sits back down on the ground, her face turning beet red.

speaker: Hestia
content: My legs... have given out. I can't walk...
Hearing you laugh again, she starts poking you with her torch angrily. You laugh so hard you're bending over and letting her jab you repeatedly.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Alright, alright, my bad. Want me to carry you?

speaker: Hestia
content: Like you can, you runt. I'm taller than you... Woah!!
You laugh as you lift her up. Hestia wraps her arms around your neck, screaming in surprise and indignation by your ear, but her crackling little sparks reveal her joy.
The flicking glimmer can't pierce through the distant night, but is still enough to briefly illuminate a short stretch of your journey together.
Carrying Hestia on your back, you tread through the darkness. The bells on her jingle, the sound much softer now.
Under her guidance, you find a safe place to rest. The fire provides you with light, warmth, and protection. Since entering the mutated area, you've never felt so at ease.
Hestia sits beside you. She may be tired or still nervous, as she's placed her torch beside her and is hugging her knees quietly.

speaker: Hestia
content: ...Not anymore, we won.

speaker: Hestia
content: I just didn't expect... that such a terrifying monster could be defeated by us two kids. I'd been so scared for so long only for it to turn out this easy...
You smile. After all, that monster was a projection of her fear. As long as she herself faced up to it, of course it was nothing more than a paper tiger.
But you decide against giving her this lecture.

speaker: Option
options: Of course, you are the great priestess.

content: Her face turns red again, poking in your direction with the tail end of her torch.

speaker: Hestia
content: Stop mocking me! I know you don't believe what I say!
But her angry poke misses. You can't help but laugh out loud.
The smile disappears from the girl's face. She withdraws her torch feebly, her voice becoming somewhat downcast.

speaker: Hestia
content: I... I guess you all know that I'm no priestess.

speaker: Hestia
content: If the Pyromater's oracles were real, the world wouldn't have ended up like this...
You watch her quietly. Under the firelight, the girl's eyes reflect a dim color, as if looking into a distant past.

speaker: Hestia
content: I've mentioned Stor Town before, right? That place... is sort of my hometown. It's a rundown small town in a desert.

speaker: Hestia
content: It's not far from here and has suffered many disasters. Folks in that shabby place don't know much about the world. Even in that sorry state, all they knew was to beg for the Pyromater's mercy instead of getting out. In the end, only around four hundred people survived with "her blessings."

speaker: Hestia
content: ...My whole family died too. I was the only one left. A frail, nearly blind kid who'd had no education whatsoever. I wasn't able to snatch even just a few bites of food. Nothing but death awaited me.

speaker: Hestia
content: But I didn't want to die. If those stupid fire believers could live, why should I have to die... So I told them that these eyes weren't blind but meant to reflect the form of God. That I didn't see demons in my dreams every night, but divine oracles bestowed upon me by God.

speaker: Hestia
content: Of course they did. I'm timid and sensitive enough to sense those things. These eyes can't see the normal world, but the bad and ominous stuff? Never miss it.

speaker: Hestia
content: Besides, I'm smart enough. Whatever kind of <color=#fb9259>priestess</color> they wanted, I could play along. Those folks suffering out there were dying for a god to protect them.

speaker: Hestia
content: Those stubborn scholars from the expedition were the only people who cared to ask all those questions, and then there's you...
Another poke from the torch, this time gentler, just enough to express her annoyance.

speaker: Hestia
content: ...It wasn't all lies, though. I did predict a few disasters and save Stor Town from hell more than once.

speaker: Hestia
content: In return, I only asked for food and protection, plus a bit of respect... It's a fair trade, isn't it?
She says slightly sheepishly, shrinking a little as if fearing your judgment.

speaker: Option
options: You've made the best out of your situation.
...Having to lie constantly must be exhausting.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Life's tough out there. It's already an achievement for a kid at your age to survive...

speaker: Hestia
content: ...Hmph, you're a kid too, only with better luck. Of course, I know I'm awesome.

speaker: Hestia
content: Ha... These days, people are ready to kill to survive. Deceiving others isn't that hard for a kid who has nothing. I can do it for the rest of my life.

speaker: Hestia
content: But... I still ended up here at last.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Aren't you the revered priestess? Why would Stor Town and your believers let you go?

speaker: Hestia
content: Let me go? Haha, they sent me here.
She laughs, her voice becoming cold.

speaker: Hestia
content: I did predict a few disasters and saved the townsfolk a few times, but the luck of a blind little liar would eventually run out at some point.

speaker: Hestia
content: I got really anxious and worried that time and told them to leave quickly if they wanted to live. There was only so much I could do, but back then, I truly hoped they could live.

speaker: Hestia
content: Heh... How stupid. The priestess was supposed to wield divine power to save her believers. How could she leave them to fend for themselves?

speaker: Hestia
content: The mayor said since I had proven my power, I could definitely save everyone... So they tied me up and brought me here.

speaker: Hestia
content: No matter how I pleaded and apologized, they wouldn't listen. My "believers" tied me up, kicked me out of the vehicle, then prayed in the direction where the "mighty god descended", saying that...

speaker: Hestia
content: Stor Town sent the most devout <color=#fb9259>Priestess of Fire</color>, who would nourish the flames with her own power and life, all to appease the <color=#fb9259>god</color>'s anger.
You freeze, clenching your fists involuntarily.

speaker: Hestia
content: Haha... You're not angry, are you? Don't be mad, they've already received their punishment.

speaker: Hestia
content: How would sacrificing a fake priestess stop the disaster? If God really existed, it would only anger them! How could they be so dumb?

speaker: Hestia
content: Haha, maybe their god has already unleashed their fury and blown up that shabby town? Serves them right!
She laughs unnaturally, her body convulsing. She doesn't look like a child of her age at all and even seems a little hysterical. It only makes you sad.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You left Stor Town and escaped from the Pyromater Sect. What you found here wasn't any god...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But that expedition you like.
She still staring into the void, yet her gaze softens.

speaker: Hestia
content: ...Just a bunch of fools. They're even more gullible than the folks in Stor Town.

speaker: Hestia
content: When they first found me, I was on edge all the time. To survive, I had to cling to this sliver of hope. I made up so many lies, tried to be helpful, and said nice things, all because I was afraid they'd abandon me too and leave me to die.

speaker: Hestia
content: But they never wanted anything from me, never asked me to prove myself or be useful... They were indeed quite careless, taking in a kid full of lies emerging out of nowhere like that.

speaker: Hestia
content: It's really dangerous here and resources are more than scarce, yet they were willing to spare their medicine on me, share their food, and waste bullets to protect me. Even though they didn't believe in my made-up god, they never exposed me either.

speaker: Hestia
content: Where did they get the courage? Did they really think they could survive? That they could save me, save everyone, save the whole world?

speaker: Hestia
content: ...What a bunch of fools.
The girl's voice dwindles.

speaker: Option
options: You seem to really like those fools.

content: She doesn't respond, and after a long while, she nods slightly.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Why did you split up? You're alone here.
Hestia doesn't answer.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Did you run into danger and get separated?
Still, no response.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Hestia, what happened? Tell me.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This path is too dark and bumpy to walk alone, but now we're together. I'll help you find them.

speaker: Hestia
content: ...No. It was me... I ran away from you guys.
Silence. For a long moment, all you can hear is her low breathing.
After a while, she begins softly.

speaker: Hestia
content: <color=#fb9259>The Perishing Star sinks into the abyss. The abyss connects to the dream. The dream brings back echoes. The echoes tell you to follow the moonlight and reach the stars...</color>

speaker: Hestia
content: That day you told everyone that, saying if we set off when the moon rose, we could make it out of the maze and find the real path.
Her grip on the torch tightens and she curls up, muttering to herself as if entranced.

speaker: Hestia
content: How happy they were... Collecting data, calculating the moon phase, and conducting experiments, thinking they could finally escape the temporal loop and uncover the truth behind the Perishing Star and the disasters.

speaker: Hestia
content: But only I saw it... At the end of the path, at the edge of the dead city, under the Illusory Moon, lay an indescribable source. The truth you wanted to witness was absolutely unbearable. The redemption you sought would only hasten the end.

speaker: Hestia
content: If only you'd blurted out some gibberish as I would... to stop them from going on that journey with no return, from approaching that twisted, disgusting... that thing...

speaker: Hestia
content: It's... the real god...
Illusory Moon, Perishing Star, dead city, source? Under the guide's direction, did the expedition take action? Where did they go? Did this really happen, or is this also part of the trap?

Regardless, you've never been closer to the past. Hestia's hollow gaze is fixed in one direction. Following her gaze, you see only darkness, but you're certain something else lies beyond that. You grab her hand eagerly.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Did they go there? That way? Can we still catch up with them now?
She jerks awake, but also seems suddenly irritated. Hestia shakes off your hand.

speaker: Hestia
content: I've told you not to go. Will you ever listen to me?!
Taken aback, you realize it's too late to try to calm her now. She gets riled up.

speaker: Hestia
content: I've said it so many times. Don't go, you'll die. Why won't you listen? Even if I used to lie for a living, sometimes I do tell the truth. Why can't you trust me just once?

speaker: Hestia
content: Have you forgotten all the trouble we've gotten into just because you must wander around and do your investigation? You never listen. And they're just like you. They insisted on going. What could I do?

speaker: Hestia
content: I could only run! Was I supposed to just die with you? I'm not part of the expedition anyway. I don't share your great purpose!

speaker: Hestia
content: I'm not some great scholar or brave guide. I've never been to school. I don't have any noble ambition or courage. I'm constantly scared by my own nightmares. I can't understand your ideals or find the same motivation.

speaker: Hestia
content: All I've ever done is try to survive. I tell whatever lie I must tell and use whoever I must use. I'm just a selfish, useless, blind parasite. A liar who's abandoned those who have helped me.

speaker: Hestia
content: I was never part of the expedition, just a coward. Every step I've taken following you guys has been exhausting...

speaker: Hestia
content: I really... can't go on anymore...
Unable to say another word, she bows her head deeply, leaning against the torch. The young guide who's been staring into darkness her whole life is already broken in body and spirit.
You finally make a decision.

speaker: Hestia
content: ...Huh?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Let's not go to look for the expedition. We'll turn around. I'll take you away from here, to a truly safe place, away from all dangers. A place where you can finally live at ease.

speaker: Hestia
content: But what about them...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: They told me to come and get you. They gave me these powerful red spikes so I can protect you.

speaker: Hestia
content: You're lying.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But if they knew I was here, they would say the same thing. They would want me to take you away.
Hestia freezes. You hesitate for a moment, but finally take her hand and gently embrace this girl who's been hurt countless times.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The world is cruel enough. Even those adults in Stor Town didn't find the courage to face the disaster and pushed a child like you into the fire...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So, you shouldn't feel ashamed of your fear. The expedition would never look down on you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: They refused to leave you behind because of their principle. They let you go because they heeded your warning. They knew the path ahead was dangerous, so they wanted to keep you out of it.

speaker: Hestia
content: Then why did they still go...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Probably to look for a better world... A world where children worry about nothing and aren't forced to be brave in a place like this. A world where adults protect children and allow them to grow up safely.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You know, that's just the kind of people they are.
Although she doesn't answer, you feel her nod slightly in your arms. She's gradually calmed down.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Besides, you're in fact incredibly brave. A real coward would either hide at the camp or run far away, yet you've come to this place and set up this magic circle, waiting for them to return in the dark despite being terrified.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If I hadn't come, you would have already gone after them, right?
Hestia flushes again. It seems you're right.

speaker: Hestia
content: ...I don't know. I'm not that brave. Even if I really went to find you guys, it would be because...

speaker: Hestia
content: I no longer have the courage to be alone...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I think "too scared to be alone" and "wanting to return to your important ones" mean the same thing to you now.
Her body trembles slightly.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But we're just kids now. We're not strong enough to protect ourselves. If we died recklessly on the way, it would only bring them more sorrow.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It's not a kid's job to save the world. We just need to grow up properly so we can follow them on the same path later.

speaker: Hestia
content: ...Hmm.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Let's go back. Before coming to find you, I've already figured out the exit. Once we're out, we'll immediately go find capable adults to rescue the expedition.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You've been scared for too long on this journey. From now on, I'll protect you. I hope you won't be tormented by fear anymore.
She nudges you, wiping the tears from her face, crying and laughing at the same time.

speaker: Hestia
content: ...Stop trying to sound like an adult.

speaker: Hestia
content: You're even younger than me. How come you never seem scared?
Saying nothing to her half-joking question, you simply take her hand and keep walking, glad that she can't see your expression right now.
In the boundless darkness, two small figures walk hand in hand, one leading the way while the other follows.
Guided by the flames, fear no longer troubles them despite the darkness.
The little torch gives you a poke.

speaker: Hestia
content: You're the scared one. See how cold your hand is. There, hold on tight, my hand is warm.

speaker: Hestia
content: I'll give you some courage.
Holding hands, the two of you tread in the darkness with the dim flames, but you're no longer afraid.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: We've arrived.
Thanks to your memory and the flickering flames along the way, you return to that initial abandoned camp.
Hestia steps forward, carefully identifying the surroundings with touch. Dry food, water, and some defensive gear. Up close, you see plenty of remaining items here.

speaker: Hestia
content: ...This was the expedition's last camp on the outside. They decided to enter the forbidden zone from here, and that's when I ran away.

speaker: Hestia
content: But when I left, everyone was packing up to move. How come there are still so many supplies left here...
Maybe they are meant for you.
You wanted to say, but seeing her expression now, you think that won't be necessary.
You'll let her reminisce a bit longer before you set off again. Just then, a familiar voice comes not far away from the darkness.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Chief!
Probably glimpsing the light, a figure limps over. It's the FAC captain.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: You finally came back. I almost went off to look for you. We could have missed each other.
Hearing the stranger's voice, Hestia grips your hand tightly, shrinking back behind you.
So this is what she looks like when meeting a stranger for the first time. You'll have to tease her later.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: She's...? Did she release these sparks?
He looks at Hestia, then at the strange sparks floating around her.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Is she a <color=#fb9259>Sinner</color>?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But she's a little timi... Ahem, a little cautious. Please take good care of her.
Hestia's hand pinches you behind your back. The soldier catches this small gesture.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: You two seem quite close, Chief.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Thank you, young lady. It was your little sparks that saved my life. Now it's my turn. Don't worry, I'll keep you safe.
He deliberately removes his helmet and leans down slightly toward the girl while keeping a reassuring distance, speaking gently.
Hestia looks at the stranger, then at you, hesitates for a moment, and finally reaches out to shake the soldier's hand before quickly retreating behind you.

You're certain the soldier indeed makes contact with the girl at that moment and doesn't notice anything unusual. He seems relieved to have gained trust, stands up straight, and resumes his solemn demeanor before posing the question.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: You're back from your investigation of the incident. You must have made some significant progress, right?

speaker: Option
options: This girl was a member of the expedition.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Regardless of how she managed to appear before us, the current overlap of our spacetime brings us unprecedentedly close to certain key events back then.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The expedition is now venturing deep into the DisSea for the first time, approaching the Perishing Star. Perhaps they're walking toward death, or perhaps closer to the truth. For us, this is also a rare chance to approach the historical truth.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So, Captain, there's one thing I must ask of you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Take this girl, Hestia, out of the mutated area. Please ensure her safety at all costs.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Could she be...

speaker: Option
options: She is the cause of the phenomenon.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This darkness is the materialization of Hestia's inner fear. Her staying here will only worsen the contamination. I need you to take her out of the mutated area, to a safe place.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Only when Hestia is completely at ease can this phenomenon possibly come to an end.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Of course, I will protect her. It's my duty. But Chief...
He must have seen through your thought and wants to stop you. In response, you reach out to him. In that instant, your hands pass through each other, surprising the soldier.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That's right. What you see now is merely a projection of my consciousness. You don't need to take me back or worry about my safety. We don't exist in the same dimension.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: My body is at the MBCC, under strict supervision by Schorl from Paradeisos. If I encounter any danger or severe contamination, it will wake me to prevent harm. And as long as the phenomenon persists, my consciousness will be brought back here against my will time after time.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That's why I must act, and I am the best suited to do so.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The biggest help I most urgently need from you is to protect this girl and take her away.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: ...Understood. I will follow your orders.

speaker: Hestia
content: Wait, I... don't understand what you're saying.
The girl interrupts your conversation, clutching your clothes tightly. She sounds more confused than uncertain, hoping you can help her understand the situation.

speaker: Hestia
content: What do you mean by "take her away"? Where are you going then?

speaker: Hestia
content: What Chief? What Sinner? Aren't you ${PlayerName}? Why are you talking like an adult?

speaker: Hestia
content: Didn't we agree to get out and wait for everyone? You said this is not a job for the kids, that we should seek help from reliable adults...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm not that <color=#fb9259>little guide</color> you know.

speaker: Hestia
content: ...What?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The little guide you know is with the expedition now, leading them deeper into the darkness.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And I'm not a member of the expedition.

speaker: Hestia
content: But... the expedition... All those things you've told me, you...
She grabs the hem of your clothes, but struggles to reach your face. She can't figure out your height just from hearing your voice.

speaker: Hestia
content: You're not... ${PlayerName}...?

speaker: Hestia
content: But the things you've said, and that earring... No way I can be mistaken, you...
Holding her shoulders, you pull away slightly, finding it so hard to do and say these things at this moment.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...All these are mere illusions. The Illusory Moon creates these false images that lure and trap us with the desires in our hearts.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: We must not be deceived by it. Remember our purpose and those who are truly important to us.

speaker: Hestia
content: ...No, liar.
The girl suddenly tenses up, her expression shifting from unease to anger.

speaker: Hestia
content: Liar! You are abandoning me and running back to them, right?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I want to get you away from danger and fear. I want you to leave the DisSea safely.

speaker: Hestia
content: I don't care!
Hestia grabs you, tears welling up again. It seems you always make her cry.

speaker: Hestia
content: Don't go... We've just managed to escape. Just listen to me once, okay? Don't go back. Just don't go. You'll die...
By the end, the anger in her tone has vanished and she's almost pleading for you to stay.
You remain silent for a long while, then kneel before her on one knee. You remove your earring, guide her hand to touch your face, and then release the shackles at the slightest intensity.
Hestia trembles.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Remember what you feel now, Hestia, this is who I am. An adult venturing deep into the darkness with a weapon to stop this phenomenon and follow the expedition.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm not that friend of yours, but I respect and admire those you love just the same.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This time, you've shown me the way, one that leads unprecedentedly close to the truth. I don't want to waste it. Like you, I'm eager for them to return.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But I can't take you further into it. I can't let you close to that fear again.
Hestia's eyes are fixed on you, as if those sightless eyes can suddenly see right through you. After a while, she smiles.

speaker: Hestia
content: Scared, aren't you? You're afraid... Haha... I know it... You're lying...

speaker: Hestia
content: You're scared to be with me... Every time we get close, you'll pull away... You're afraid to face me, I know...

speaker: Hestia
content: Why? You don't hate me, so why? What are you really afraid of?

speaker: Schorl
content: This is just a <color=#fb9259>trap</color>.

speaker: Schorl
content: They are long dead. This is just a trap to stir up your emotions.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I just want to make it possible for you to finally leave the DisSea, this place imprisoning you.
You must stop talking to her. You look at the FAC captain, who either understands how you feel or is simply obeying orders. He holds her back.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Keep her safe.
Hestia doesn't struggle this time. In front of the two of you, she seems to understand any resistance is useless. She simply clutches her torch tightly, her hollow eyes staring straight at you.

speaker: Hestia
content: Heh... Liar...

speaker: Hestia
content: I'm not leaving. This time, I won't run away no matter how scared I am. I'll stay here and wait for you.

speaker: Hestia
content: ...So you're not allowed to run away either.

speaker: Hestia
content: Come back to me, coward... You must come back to me.
You leave the camp alone, followed by a tiny flame that has appeared out of nowhere, heading to the heart of the DisSea.
The journey seems endless. You walk past the valley where you fled with Hestia and the "magic circle" where you first met her.
The further you go, the denser the surrounding darkness becomes. With each step, you feel like you're stepping deeper into a swamp, sinking slowly.
The light and warmth from the flicking tiny flame dwindle. The darkness tries to snuff it out, but it stubbornly reignites again and again.
You make a circle with your hands and hold the tiny flame in your palms, protecting it in front of your chest.
The darkness washes over you again and again, cold, viscous, and suffocating. That dim Hypercube given to you by the FAC captain has slowly fallen apart and turned into dull dust.
You feel increasingly tired and drowsy, with only the flame in your embrace providing the last bit of light and warmth.
At some point, the relentless dark tides finally recede.
A blinding red moon rises from the horizon. Even the darkness cannot contend against it, disappearing without a trace.
You open your eyes. Under the blood-red light, a vast, dilapidated, humid city instantly fills your view.
In this eerie red city, vague yet familiar figures weave through the crumbling, decaying buildings.
Driven by an inexplicable impulse, you advance mindlessly, coming to a broken pillar.
You lift the algae off it and wipe away the sticky silt. A name that stirs your heart appears on it.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: <color=#fb9259>Maria City</color>...
You traverse the ruined city. In the thick fog, your mind gradually blurs as if you're falling asleep. You're dissolving amid the indistinct voices, unable to recall the reason why you're here.
But the spark is right next to you. You can barely hear someone's voice in your ear.

speaker: Hestia
content: You're scared to be with me... Every time we get close, you'll pull away... You're afraid to face me, I know...

speaker: Hestia
content: Why? You don't hate me, so why? What are you really afraid of?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Maybe. Maybe I really am afraid. I'm worried you'll end up like them. I'm scared to watch it tear you to pieces again.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But if it's just venturing alone by myself, I can bear it... I'm a grown-up now. I won't be a coward again.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That's why I have to come back... I've had enough...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm tired of falling into traps over and over again, tired of it using you guys to torture me. I tell myself to "stay rational and don't fall into traps", and it makes me sick every time I say it.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What really happened back then... What's the thing that destroyed you all and came back to haunt me... I've gotten so close this time. That's why I'm here. I must see the truth and identify my true enemy.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I can't be fooled by it anymore.
Your consciousness blurs further. Whispers from the surrounding shadows turn into vague noise. Only the blood-red moonlight remains in sight.
Fooled? Heh heh heh... No...
A voice objects, but it sounds comfortingly familiar.
No... This is not a trap. No one has lured you here... Everything happened because your heart desired a response...

And you are destined to return... Even if you know the journey is perilous, even if you want to personally escort that girl out, even if... Heh, no, from the moment you entered the dream, you've been destined to come...
It's not about courage or cowardice, or those trivial missions...
Poor child, you're just too sad, too lonely... You simply miss home, so sooner or later, you must come home...
An obscure figure appears in your mind.
...Me? Miss home?
Yes... Every time you fall into a nightmare, every time you return to the Illusory Moon, you're brought here by your own longing...
You miss home, so you come back... You miss your family, so you meet them...
Meet who?
The ruins of the city are behind you. Your legs move on their own and you walk on the desolate, gray shallows alone.
No, you're not alone. Human-like specters hover around you. You gaze at them blankly, trying to make out their faces, which are unrecognizable yet familiar.
They seem to want to say something to you, or are just muttering to themselves.

speaker: Blurry Shadow
content: It's down here. Now we're sure... It's at the bottom... We must... continue... We can't stop diving...

speaker: Blurry Shadow
content: We've found it... ██... after so much... sacrifice... Giving up at this moment... is not an option...
The voice sounds familiar yet incoherent. The person seems to be crying.

speaker: Blurry Shadow
content: Still... holding on... even if we'll no longer be... what we were... but...
You want to touch that shadow, but she disappears into the mist in the blink of an eye and is nowhere to be found.

speaker: Inquisitive Shadow
