content: Wait, tell me more about the meaning of your language. What you saw beyond the boundary on the other side...

speaker: Inquisitive Shadow
content: I believe in your wisdom. I think you've returned to this side of the shore because you have a message to convey...

speaker: Inquisitive Shadow
content: So... give me the prophecy and the revelation.
The shadow poses the question loud and clear into the mist, but fails to get the desired response, instead descending into chaos and merging into it.

speaker: Troubled Shadow
content: No, I see no pattern... The model is proven wrong again. All the calculations have gone to waste...

speaker: Troubled Shadow
content: This makes no sense. Is there an error in the data...? Yes, that must be it. Something went wrong during the collection in the dive. That has to be it...

speaker: Troubled Shadow
content: If not... What's the point... of everything we've done?
Muttering hysterically, the shadow stands frozen, clutching its head in agony.
The next moment, with a pop, she explodes like a balloon, blending in with the mist around her.

speaker: Quarreling Shadow
content: Why are you looking at me like that? Can't the great scholar understand the idea of power? Or is it humanity you can't grasp? No... You all must know...

speaker: Quarreling Shadow
content: We've come so far together, yet you've never trusted me... What else is there to say?
An agonized screech. The shadows overlap, mauling and obliterating each other.
You simply watch them. The voices and feelings are so familiar, as if... you're always meant to be here.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: My... family...
Yes, your family. You're finally getting closer... by their side, at last. Are you satisfied now?
Joy dispels the pain and despair. Among the shadows of these revenants, you feel at peace.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Yes.
Haha... No, too soon...
There is one more of them. The real reason you came here. It's neither rational nor emotional, neither about fear nor determination...
It's because you've finally heard its call... finally grown up and waited till this day...
So, go on...

The figures all stand up and raise their hands. Slowly, you look toward the direction they're pointing at and step forward, feeling a warmth you've never felt before. Blue light flashes, and is shattered in an instant by red light.

You cross the shallows and walk toward the deep sea. The surface of the sea begins to boil. Something rises from the abyss. In the sky, rings of light ripple outward, the concentric circles surrounding the central red moon.

Moonlight reflects off the water, paving a red path of light. Gladly, you move forward, your consciousness gradually dissolving into the deep sea, in a blissful embrace where all imperfections and insignificance are accepted.
Go... Meet... your real family...
You walk toward the splendor at the end of the light path, like an infant returning to the womb.

<color=#fb9259>??-06</color>: Emergency! A major shock occurred in the Illusory Moon zone. The phenomenon area is shrinking but its intensity is skyrocketing. SHP-13's Mania index has surpassed the threshold. Forced revival has failed!
<color=#fb9259>??-07</color>: The readings were stable until a moment ago. Can the FAC verify the cause of the sudden change?
<color=#fb9259>??-06</color>: No, the wave charts are a mess. But the frontline squads have entered the mutated area and are doing their best to stop the Mania.

<color=#fb9259>??-03</color>: I see... Schorl is retrying the revival protocol. Use as many Hypercubes as needed. Do whatever necessary to bring him back.
<color=#fb9259>??-03</color>: There's only a 15-minute window. After that, disposal will be mandatory.
<color=#fb9259>??-06</color>: ?!
female_content:
<color=#fb9259>??-03</color>: I see... Schorl is retrying the revival protocol. Use as many Hypercubes as needed. Do whatever necessary to bring her back.
<color=#fb9259>??-03</color>: There's only a 15-minute window. After that, disposal will be mandatory.
<color=#fb9259>??-06</color>: ?!

content: <color=#fb9259>??-03</color>: This is different from previous instances. If No. 13 breaks down now, it will be a real catastrophe.

Inside the shield room, the shackles' red light pierces through the devices, canceling out the Hypercube energy. Amid the intense clash of red and blue light, ${PlayerName}'s face is almost contorted and the body is twisted into an extremely painful posture.

speaker: Schorl
content: ...Order received. The first and third Observatoriums have joined the operation and are currently recording and analyzing the data.

speaker: Schorl
content: Target one, the search for SHP-13 is still ongoing. We've encountered significant obstacles.

speaker: Schorl
content: Target two, the phenomenon's singularity coordinates are confirmed. It has made a move.
The girl jerks her body up, but the irrepressible fear turns into a fearful shudder, almost crushing her body.

speaker: Hestia
content: <size=44>That idiot!!!</size>
The boundless darkness is suddenly surging, filled with cries, laughter, and the bloody sound of flesh getting torn apart.
Hestia's stomach churns. She grabs her torch and stands up, only to be yanked back by a pair of broad hands. She then hears a series of gunshots.
A muffled sound, followed by a powerful gust sweeping past from behind. A terrifying thing is hit and sent flying, landing in the distance.
The clash of metal. Heavy breathing. Liquid dripping onto the ground.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Don't wander off! The situation has escalated. The monsters have multiplied and Mania is intensifying rapidly. It's not safe here anymore. I'm taking you out now.
Hestia's voice trembles, out of fear, or emotions.

speaker: Hestia
content: No, I, I need to find him. That idiot got caught. He's trapped. It won't be long before he's taken away altogether. Then he'll...
female_content: No, I, I need to find her. That idiot got caught. She's trapped. It won't be long before she's taken away altogether. Then she'll...

speaker: FAC Captain
content: It's impossible! You can't do it under the current circumstances. We simply can't get through this high-risk area on our own. We must leave immediately and contact support so they can send reinforcements.
The man's voice also sounds tense. He has already forgotten ${PlayerName}'s explanation about the dream and Schorl's revival.

speaker: Hestia
content: It'll all be too late by then!
She can't push away the tall soldier, but as she struggles, a flame lights up, forcing the man back.
The fire stretches between him and the girl.

speaker: Hestia
content: Huff... huff... What is this? Where did this... <color=#fb9259>fire</color> come from?

speaker: FAC Captain
content: ...Listen, kid, you need to stay calm.
The flames burn through his damaged armor and sear an old wound, making him gasp.
Hestia hears it, and probably also smells the burned flesh. She instinctively tightens her grip on the torch, the realization of hurting someone filling her with panic.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Using this kind of power near DisSea is very dangerous. Mania might backfire on you. Chief's not here, nobody can help you control it.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: I've promised Chief to protect you. Please trust us. The FAC will surely bring Chief back.
The man speaks earnestly. Hestia gradually calms down, realizing he's right. Her consciousness is indeed slowly growing heavy and murky.

She witnesses a horrifying scene. The Illusory Moon expands rapidly. The dark sea churns. The ghosts of the dead city howl. Even the breath of the soldier in front of her fades, as if he never should have existed before her.
Once she calms down, a single strong thought remains in her heart, compelling her to make an immediate decision.

speaker: Hestia
content: ...By then, it will be too late.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Wait!
The FAC soldier approaches, but she raises her torch, and a wall of fire suddenly rises between them, even scaring away the monsters growling around them.
Under the glow of the fire, the girl's pale face now appears exceptionally solemn.

speaker: Hestia
content: You... can stay here, or go back, but don't go on further. The flames will stop you and also protect you.

speaker: Hestia
content: ...Thank you.
She steps back, leaving the camp left by the expedition for her, heading deeper into the DisSea. Gazing past the numerous chaos blocking her way, she steps into the darkness.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This spark is your strength, as well as your courage.
Hestia takes a deep breath, steadies her trembling body, and walks into the darkness.
She treads alone in the dark wilderness, losing track of how long or how far she has gone. The mere act of advancing in the somber mire is exhausting all her strength.
Likewise, she can no longer clearly recall those restless ghosts hindering her in the darkness.

speaker: Worshipper
content: Go and confess that you've disrespected God with blasphemous thoughts, and now you'll atone for your sin in exchange for Stor Town's safety.
In a daze, the girl finds herself back in the town center. Below the circular <color=#fb9259>altar</color>, the townspeople's faces are twisted as they make desperate and cruel prayers.

The worshippers cry and shout, their faces filled with different emotions: fear, despair, anger... but not a shred of <color=#fb9259>reverence</color>. Countless filthy and horrifying hands reach out to Hestia, almost drowning her.

speaker: Worshipper
content: If you're a real <color=#fb9259>priestess</color>, sacrifice yourself to God. If you're a fake <color=#fb9259>priestess</color>, then give your life as atonement. Choose your fate.

speaker: Worshipper
content: You're just a blind <color=#fb9259>kid</color> who can't survive without us. You should fear us, please us, beg for our protection! Because we are the brave and strong <color=#fb9259>adults</color>!

speaker: Hestia
content: Don't touch me!
She swings her torch, and the fire rises instantly, dispersing the stubborn shadows around it.

speaker: Hestia
content: What kind of <color=#fb9259>adults</color> are you? You pathetic cowards who could only rely on a <color=#fb9259>kid</color> when disaster struck, why should I fear you? You're nothing to me!
The nightmarish shadows catch fire and turn to ash. Finally, she can catch her breath.
Time is running out. Hestia quickly steadies her breath, steps over the ash leaning against her torch, and presses onward. This is how she's come all this way.

speaker: Hestia
content: I'm no longer afraid of you... I need to keep going... I'm going to find those who are most important to me...
Following her closely, barely audible whispers emerge from the darkness.

speaker: Indistinct Whisper
content: Those... who are most important to you?

speaker: Indistinct Whisper
content: Heh heh... Are you talking about... them?
[Scene change]
The ground suddenly collapses under her feet. Hestia slips and tumbles down, feeling a sharp pain in her ankle as she falls onto a pile of mess.

Several figures approach. This feels familiar... Yes, it was when she first got banished from Stor Town and left to die in the forbidden zone. There, she met the expedition at her last breath and was taken in by them.
Tears instantly fill her eyes. Hestia struggles to her feet, wanting to call their names, eager to tell them all about her terrifying journey to reach them. But the figures speak first.

speaker: Ethereal Figure
content: No one asked you to come <color=#fb9259>search for</color> us...
She hears the dark, eerie echo, so malicious it makes even her heart shiver.

speaker: Ethereal Figure
content: You're a liar. Nothing you say is true... You're always planning to escape and slow us down, aren't you?

speaker: Ethereal Figure
content: Say something! Admit all the lies you've told along the way, all the things you've done, how you've betrayed us selfishly and ungratefully!

speaker: Ethereal Figure
content: You're weak and useless. You've never been one of us, just a burden, a parasite. The expedition doesn't need you. Crawl back!

speaker: Hestia
content: ...I don't need you to tell me that.
She gasps for air as something heavy presses down on her. She stands with great effort, with the torch the only thing keeping her upright.

speaker: Hestia
content: I know I'm not worthy of them. I will apologize... but not to you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: They refused to leave you behind because of their principle. They let you go because they heeded your warning. They knew the path ahead was dangerous, so they wanted to keep you out of it.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You know, that's just the kind of people they are.

speaker: Hestia
content: They would never say such things. They are nothing like you. Of that, I'm sure!

Trembling, she lifts the torch, its fire rising to dispel the gloom on her. After letting it burn for a long while, Hestia wipes her tears. Time is running out. She continues on, using the torch to support herself.
Don't look back. You must not look back. Muster the courage. You must move forward.
She repeats this to herself over and over, relying on this nascent, fragile courage to keep going.
And above the darkness, in the sky she cannot see, the red Illusory Moon waxes, watching over the girl from high above.

speaker: Indistinct Whisper
content: Yes... Don't look back. You must not look back. Go and find the real them.

speaker: Indistinct Whisper
content: You will reach the <color=#dg1f1f>truth</color>...
[Scene change]
How long has it been? The ground under her feet is no longer muddy, but like a stretch of shallows. Hestia's mind is cloudy, but her vision is clear. She sees a red bloody path extending forward.
Under the red moon, in the crimson seawater, dozens of ashen, bloated bodies float in disarray, their faces frozen in the last moments before death.
Yet Hestia can hear their voices.

speaker: Ghastly Figure
content: You were right... That thing... No one should approach or see it... It's a path of no return...

speaker: Ghastly Figure
content: So everyone is dead now... This is the outcome you foresaw, <color=#dg1f1f>Guide</color>...

speaker: Ghastly Figure
content: Why did you come here? Do you want to... change something?
She doesn't have the strength to answer and simply continues walking.
Ahead stands a familiar figure bathed in red light.

speaker: Little Guide
content: You know it's fake, so why are you still so scared? You're even more skittish than before, Hestia.

speaker: Little Guide
content: Back then, all you needed to worry about was your own survival. What are you afraid of now? Your fear is so deep... It has bred this vast darkness.

speaker: Hestia
content: ...I'm afraid they might die.

speaker: Little Guide
content: Heh heh... I'm afraid that can't be helped.
${PlayerName} laughs, a dark red viscous liquid welling up in those eyes, forming two streaks of bloody tears that stream over the unchanging smile.
Hestia sees it. Instinctively, she runs forward, dropping the torch to support ${PlayerName}, who immediately turns into a splash of red water, spattering all over Hestia.

speaker: Little Guide
content: You know you can't stop them. That's who they are. They'd risk it despite knowing the danger, like moths flying into a flame. You can't change them.

Hestia stands dazed, drenched in the crimson hue. She stays there for a long time before picking up the torch from the blood-red shallows. The torch has been extinguished, and darkness is creeping up the shadows.
Hestia leans on the torch, forcing herself to go on, each step harder than the last. Her eyes are hollow and her body shakes with each step, either from fear or from the cold.
But she never stops. She keeps going, and slowly, the dim sparks around her begin fluttering.

speaker: Hestia
content: They don't need to change...

speaker: Hestia
content: I like them the way they are. I like watching them press forward, even if I can only watch from behind, I'm still pleased.

speaker: Hestia
content: The one who needs to change... is <color=#fb9259>me</color>...
The sparks are multiplying, gathering at the top of the torch, flickering constantly.

speaker: Hestia
content: I've always lived in fear. I don't mind living that way even when I grow up. Everyone fears something.

speaker: Hestia
content: But <color=#fb9259>courage</color> is something you must reach past your fear to grip.

The flames burn brighter and brighter, illuminating the gnawing darkness, dispersing the silt covering her ankles. Hestia walks forward, over those familiar, fearful scenes, advancing despite shivering.

speaker: Hestia
content: I've finally grasped my courage. There are many things I want to do. I... won't stop here!
In a place invisible to her, the illusion begins sinking back into the darkness. The path beneath her feet is turning smooth.
After a long silence, a distant, indistinct voice comes through the darkness.
...Good. Fear can no longer stop you. Come... I shall return your eyes...
The voice is so lofty. She can almost hear a disdainful sneer.
I invite you... to face the truth...
The darkness fades like a tide. The blood-red light obscures everything.
At the end of that red light, an indescribable, colossal being casts a nonchalant glance.
The red moonlight casts long shadows. Her shadow writhes and whispers to her.
Ancient memories begin to revive. This is the first <color=#fb9259>glimpse</color> of this world she has, which will reign over her deepest instinct ever since.
Gone is the past. The doom is near.
The searing stars shine, boiling and trembling.
Rising from the ocean depths, descending from the starry sky.
Omnipotent, omnipresent.
Rising it is, and rise it will, returning us to the blissful gloom.
Hestia opens her mouth but is unable to utter a word. She wants to step forward but her body is frozen. As if only now realizing her grave mistake, she questions why she's returned.
The frail human girl trembles, clutching the torch, but the flames in it are just like her brief and futile determination.
Extinguished easily.
You finally understand... Hestia...
For you... courage... is the poison...
The shadows in the chaos disappear. The horrifying echoes fade as the fearsome creatures scatter, vanishing into the wilderness.
Not because someone has defeated them, but because the only prey has finally been completely devoured, and the remnants can no longer sustain the attention of Mania.
The empty shell of her remains in a gazing position, but can no longer see, hear, or feel anything.
The tears have dried up, and she can no longer move a step forward. Finally, Hestia kneels under the Illusory Moon, letting the red light permeate her hollow eyes and body.
The night is so heavy and vast, requiring no effort to crush the brave scholars or the young timid soul.

speaker: Shattered Voice
content: It's okay now... We've found you. You're not alone anymore...

speaker: Shattered Voice
content: We will survive. Not just here, but when all of this is over, we'll go out into the bigger world, and everyone will live happily together...

speaker: Shattered Voice
content: Welcome to the expedition, Hestia. If you want... would you like to become a guide too?
Memories flash through her mind and then shatter, weathering and fading quickly.

The girl raises her hands slowly. In Stor Town, she was trained countless times to raise the holy fire against disasters. In the expedition, she held up the torch many times at the camp, hoping her loved ones would soon return safely.

speaker: Shattered Voice
content: This fire is your power...

speaker: Shattered Voice
content: Your torch... lights up the way home for everyone...
But the torch by her side through the years has also turned to ash. Her hands are now empty.

After Nightfall, humanity has lost the world. Only fear spares the insignificant humans a possibility of life, teaching them reverence, guiding them to flee. God favors Hestia, and fear is the wisdom and gift bestowed upon her.
And this is the consequence of abandoning it.
Because she's realized even that brave little punk fears something, she dreams of having courage. And this is the outcome.
Darkness crawls up her tattered body and swallows her consciousness, returning everything to silence. The end is right here... At that moment, she laughs dryly.

The dregs of her courage, or despair, turn into overwhelming madness. When death finally comes, proving the long struggle meaningless, Hestia experiences liberation from fear for the first time. Love and friendship didn't save her, but destruction does.
Finally free, she reaches out to the brightness she can no longer see.

speaker: Hestia
content: The torch... is still here...

speaker: Hestia
content: I'll light it...
The final spark falls into her palm, burning down her arm like a sprout growing from the roots, blooming. The broken, empty shell quickly <color=#dg1f1f>burns out and vanishes</color>.
Then it transforms into a <color=#dg1f1f>torch</color>, disappearing in an instant.
[Fade out]

speaker: Hestia
content: ${PlayerName}, you know... Before today, I never liked you.

speaker: Hestia
content: The first day I was brought back to the camp, I saw you, another kid coddled by the crew. It made me so jealous and reminded me of fighting over a piece of bread with other kids when I was little. Or maybe I just didn't like losing.

speaker: Hestia
content: Later, I competed for the guide's position with you. To convince everyone, I made up so many nice tales, but they laughed it off each time. The routes you suggested were always bold and dangerous, yet everyone followed without protest.

speaker: Hestia
content: The things I'd never dared to face in my life, you never averted your gaze from. You pointed out the path directly, leading the team forward without looking back.

speaker: Hestia
content: You're even younger than me. Why weren't you ever afraid?

speaker: Hestia
content: I couldn't do it. I could only follow behind you, trying to catch up while sulking.

speaker: Hestia
content: Looking back now... I wish I'd talked to you sooner.

speaker: Hestia
content: Then I would have known that courage alone isn't enough. Like today, watching you fall worried me so much.

speaker: Hestia
content: ...Don't you ever do this again.

speaker: Hestia
content: Press ahead bravely, but stay fearful at heart. Don't forget the dangers even if the goal is in sight. From now on, you are the only guide.

speaker: Hestia
content: Just like I need you, you need me too.

speaker: Hestia
content: I'll help you once more, for the last time. Consider it... <color=#fb9259>a thank you, for giving me courage</color>.
[Open eyes special effect]
You wake up.
Opening your eyes, you find yourself lying on the shallows of the DisSea. Tiny sparks hover in front of you, emitting comforting light and warmth quietly.
No answer. The little sparks draw a few circles, then drift in a certain direction. In a daze, you get up to follow them.

The red moon in the sky is glaring, yet now all you can see is the tiny dim light in front of you, the faint warmth makes you forget the long, intrusive darkness... Somehow, you feel you're no longer alone.
Yes, you're no longer alone... Continuing walking, you hear sounds. The wind, footsteps, and finally the vague, gentle whispers around you.
Where the sparks shine, some people come to your side before you notice.

speaker: Blurry Figure
content: Oh... What a fruitful journey. The calculations are correct and the theory has been proven. We've finally located the Perishing Star and established a base...

speaker: Blurry Figure
content: Who'd have thought? We've just taken the first step after all these years, and it's led us straight to our goal... Let's go back and celebrate. Celebrate the truth that's right before us. Uh, no...

speaker: Blurry Figure
content: First, let's celebrate that we've all come back alive and managed to find the way back...

One after another figure emerges, joining this returning crew. Someone takes your hand habitually, and another person pats your shoulder. You want to see their faces clearly, but your vision is wet and blurry while your heart is filled with a strange yet familiar warmth.
The Illusory Moon fades. The dreadful darkness is behind you. People move in the same direction, gradually forming a returning path.
The sparks along the path grow bright and dazzling, clarifying your mind.

speaker: Blurry Figure
content: I followed the spark here... Thank you, little guide... I'm glad you're here to show us the way...
You look around but don't find the person you're looking for.
The specters of the crowd pull you forward. You can feel the stele waiting for you ahead.
But somehow it feels like you've missed something.
No answer. She's not in the crowd, not ahead on the road, not at the stele.
You turn around. The flames you've passed along the way all feel strangely familiar. You want to go back to confirm it, but...
Someone rushes up to you from behind, embracing you.

speaker: Hestia
content: Pfft... Haha...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Hestia?
The girl blinks, not answering. But her eyes sparkle and her body gradually fades into the light.
And the light that belonged to the torch is now held up high in her hands, burning silently in the air.
In the blink of an eye, the joy of reunion turns to ice.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No...

You turn back, searching for those burning flames. Perhaps you can find the residue. Perhaps you can still deny that dreadful guess. You don't care if it means staying here forever. You want to go back. You must go back.
But the guide won't allow it.
Hestia pulls your arm, dragging you back to the original path, giggling as if mocking you for straying. Her pace hastens, and you simply cannot resist the pull of the frail body.
In the end, the two of you are running. The sparks fall to the ground, blooming into a field of flowers. The specters following you along the way gradually stop, waving at you as if it's a farewell.
The path is bright, warm, yet short, quickly coming to an end. Waiting for you there is the nameless stele, the exit of the dream.
And your last companion lets go of your hand.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Hestia!
Hestia doesn't leave you. Even as the light erases her silhouette, she's still jogging after you, smiling and waving at you until she disappears. She says something.

speaker: Hestia
content: <color=#7683a2>Don't worry...</color>

Thirteen minutes and twenty-eight seconds after the MBCC's Chief went out of control, Mania subsides, and the DisSea's Illusory Moon is observed to have disappeared.
The fourth anomalous tide ends. BR-000 has regained peace for now.

All missing persons have been found, with no casualties. Those survivors who were brought back earlier are also recovering from their mental disturbance. No one has suffered any permanent physical or mental damage. After rehabilitation at the hospital, they will be discharged back to the DisSea frontline.
[Banyan Hospital - Ward]

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: I can't remember what exactly happened in the dream. Or maybe I don't want to remember... It still spooks me out...

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: The only thing I remember is a few small flames. I think someone told me to follow them to get out of the phenomenon...

When Mania broke out, the last survivor to escape the mutated area ran into the reinforcements entering the zone. Guided by him, the troops soon reached Monitoring Station 1 safely.

However, the other information he's provided is yet to be verified...
[FAC HQ - Background]

speaker: FAC Captain
content: I requested support immediately, but when we rushed to the site, we failed to find that abandoned camp despite rigorous search efforts. That child named Hestia was also nowhere to be found.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: The Ring Research Institute says it was a Mania-induced illusion, kind of like a daydream... I'll take that explanation. After all, the phenomenon is gone now. Chief has been at the MBCC this whole time. Once he wakes up, we can hear his side of the story and find out.
female_content: The Ring Research Institute says it was a Mania-induced illusion, kind of like a daydream... I'll take that explanation. After all, the phenomenon is gone now. Chief has been at the MBCC this whole time. Once she wakes up, we can hear her side of the story and find out.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: But... if all of that was real, then Chief...

Three days later, the MBCC's Chief also regains consciousness and is confirmed to be free of significant physical or mental issues upon examination.

According to his account, a member of the expedition has been identified. Named Hestia, she is a Sinner whose ability is telepathic ignition. The spiritual energy she yields during this process can disperse Mania to a certain extent.
Hestia is suspected to be spiritually gifted and highly sensitive to Mania fluctuations. Similar cases were recorded in a few regions during the first few years after Nightfall. Her exact age and real name are unknown. Further information to be added.
female_content:
Three days later, the MBCC's Chief also regains consciousness and is confirmed to be free of significant physical or mental issues upon examination.

According to her account, a member of the expedition has been identified. Named Hestia, she is a Sinner whose ability is telepathic ignition. The spiritual energy she yields during this process can disperse Mania to a certain extent.
Hestia is suspected to be spiritually gifted and highly sensitive to Mania fluctuations. Similar cases were recorded in a few regions during the first few years after Nightfall. Her exact age and real name are unknown. Further information to be added.

content:
During Chief's coma, the vast data recorded by Schorl has been transferred to the Ring Research Institute, Banyan Medical College, and other core Paradeisos authorities.

The fourth Illusory Moon tide has ended. But for humanity's operations in the DisSea and the exploration of the expedition's history a century ago as well as the truth behind the Perishing Star, this is only the beginning.
[MBCC Medical Room]
You open your eyes and see Schorl floating before you.

speaker: Schorl
content: The people behind me are more than relieved to see that you're unharmed, Chief.

speaker: Schorl
content: This Illusory Moon tide was very unique. You were able to remain rational in the depths of Mania and bought precious time on the most dangerous frontline. It's the first time humanity has retrieved this amount of invaluable <color=#fb9259>data</color>.

speaker: Schorl
content: EDGE-01 has specifically asked me to relay his sincere salute to you, saying your growth compared to a few months ago has exceeded his expectations. He's expressed his gratitude.
You don't answer or look up, just staring at your hands.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What purpose will these data serve?

speaker: Schorl
content: We're still in the preliminary analysis phase, but based on the current findings, not only can they reveal the truth behind the Illusory Moon tides, but they may also completely change the strategies for future operations in the DisSea.

speaker: Schorl
content: Before the mystery of the DisSea is solved, the Illusory Moon tides will not cease. But by the next cycle, you will definitely receive better protection. The overall approach in the DisSea might also shift from defensive to offensive, with humanity taking the initiative to unearth the truth.

speaker: Schorl
content: This is all thanks to your contributions. Well done, Chief.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...I'm exhausted. I'd like to be alone for a while.

speaker: Schorl
content: Of course. I came to say goodbye to you. The operation has come to an end. At your request, I will leave the MBCC, in honor of our mutual trust.

speaker: Schorl
content: Farewell, Chief.
Finally, you are alone in the room.
The bedding is warm. The aroma of the bouquet on the desk is soothing. As sunlight pours in, you find that you've regained all your senses. Everything feels warm and bright.
You will no longer return to that dark dream. You can only struggle in vain trying to grasp that slowly fading memory.
You've also walked in that cold, suffocating darkness, with only a single light beside you.
You've tried countless times to catch up to it, to hold it tightly in your hands, not wanting to lose that fragile, perplexed, yet stubborn fire.
You want to ask if it was trying to tell you something by flickering so vigorously. At that moment of departure, what did she really say to you?
Luckily, you finally remember...

speaker: Hestia
content: <color=#fb9259>Don't worry, you're the guide... We will always follow you...</color>
[Back to the Room]
You finally unclench your tight fist, but there's no spark in your hand, only a red mark.
It's not a burn scar, only a bloody mark left by your nail from the too-tight grip.

10:30, October 24, N.F. 114
Chief's Office
After four months, you hear news about the DisSea once again.
<color=#fb9259>Schorl</color>: The Illusory Moon tide is about to rise again. After four challenging operations, humanity seizes the initiative this time.

<color=#fb9259>Schorl</color>: It is confirmed that the DisSea Expedition Team did break through the convoluted outskirt of the dead zone. Traversing perils, they reached the Maria City ruins, where the Perishing Star descended, and established an enduring research base there.

<color=#fb9259>Schorl</color>: During the fourth investigation, our Observatorium retrieved crucial timespace coordinates by tracking Chief ${PlayerName}. It turned out that the current tide's epicenter lies unprecedentedly near the heart of the DisSea.

<color=#fb9259>Schorl</color>: Soon, we will be following in the pioneers' footsteps, tracing their lost research findings with the chance to uncover truths entombed within the dead zone.

<color=#fb9259>Schorl</color>: MBCC Chief ${PlayerName}, the shackles bearer, will continue to lead the charge with backing from all departments.

<color=#fb9259>Schorl</color>: In addition, the following modification will be implemented to our approach this time:

<color=#fb9259>Schorl</color>: During the last Illusory Moon tide, ${PlayerName}'s connection to the Moon was further intensified. Once the tide reaches its climax, ${PlayerName}'s mind would inevitably connect with the Black Ring, resulting in direct consciousness contact with the Mania illusion and triggering severe mental contamination.

<color=#fb9259>Schorl</color>: Though we cannot completely block the influence of the Illusory Moon, we can reduce its risk coefficient, hence converting this perilous link into a controlled tool and gaining a chance to probe deeper.

<color=#fb9259>Schorl</color>: Over the past five months, the Ring Research Institute has developed a safety protocol:

<color=#fb9259>Schorl</color>: By limiting the shackles' activity, we can suppress the Illusory Moon's corruptive influence on the investigator, thereby safeguarding ${PlayerName}'s sanity.
<color=#fb9259>Schorl</color>: Furthermore, separate researches have also managed to mitigate the risks from restricted shackles use:

<color=#fb9259>Schorl</color>: The Mania beings that emerged during each contamination peak, formerly identified as contamination sources, have now been revealed as echoes of the expedition members who perished in the dead zone. Their consciousness melded with the Mania, reawakening whenever ${PlayerName} returns to the DisSea.

<color=#fb9259>Schorl</color>: While the underlying mechanism remains unverified, and we cannot rule out the possibility of this being a trap orchestrated by the Black Ring, there is one certainty—

<color=#fb9259>Schorl</color>: Every time ${PlayerName} falls prey to mental contamination and ensnared by the DisSea, these entities would attempt to guide ${PlayerName} back to reality.

<color=#fb9259>Schorl</color>: Therefore, as long as ${PlayerName} makes contact with a contamination source, even if ${PlayerName} faces a crisis afterward, we can utilize the source's coordinates to rescue ${PlayerName}'s consciousness in time.
<color=#fb9259>Schorl</color>: In other words, the very people you seek, Chief ${PlayerName}, are your safety net.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...This tide's contamination source is closer than ever to the heart of the Black Ring, you said?

speaker: Schorl
content: Correct. It is remarkably close to the impact site of the Perishing Star. Essentially, the intelligence we could gather this time might be groundbreaking—we may finally uncover the truth about the Perishing Star.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I understand, and I will do it. There's just one more thing I need to ask...

options: Is there any possibility of bringing them back?

speaker: Schorl
content: Given our current research findings, we can only guarantee the safe return of your consciousness. As for retrieving anything from the Mania of nearly a century ago, there have been no successful cases so far.

speaker: Schorl
content: I regret to inform you that the closer those explorers got to the epicenter, the lower their survival chances became. This may not sound rational, but...

speaker: Schorl
content: Just think of it as a dream, Chief.

speaker: Schorl
content: Your task in the DisSea is to address the anomalies, collect intelligence, and uncover information about the expedition. Changing the past is no walk in the park.

speaker: Schorl
content: From the very beginning, they chose a path of no return. They marched bravely to their end, gambling everything for even the faintest glimmer of hope and possibility in the darkness.

speaker: Schorl
content: Their expedition has become history, whereas your expedition is to venture through that history to reclaim the lost possibility.

speaker: Chief
content: ...I see.
While the words are conveyed in Schorl's typically mechanical manner, you somehow discern a trace of that man's presence within.

14:30, October 24, N.F. 114
Observatorium
An Observatorium staff member leads you to a room filled with an array of scientific instruments.
According to them, the protective equipment in this room can effectively shield your mind during the tide—a far more reliable method than previous attempts.

speaker: Researcher
content: Chief, everything's set.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Okay.
Following the researcher’s instructions, you lie down and watch as equipment emitting a blue glow slowly descends.

speaker: Schorl
content: Your expedition is to venture through that history to reclaim the lost possibility.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Let's get started.
After a few minutes, your consciousness starts to blur. Your eyes gradually shut as you slip into a boundless dream.
You wake up in an endless sea, its boundaries nowhere in sight.
The water surface above you recedes, the moonlight tinged with a red glow devoured by the darkness below you, growing increasingly obscured.
There is no suffocation, no panic even—just an eternal descent. The frigid, murky water envelops you, numbing all sensation and emotion.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The DisSea, the contamination source, the expedition...

A few fragmented words flicker through your foggy mind—they're your crucial mission here. Yet, you find your body out of your control, trapped in this everlasting descent like an insignificant grain of sand in the vast ocean.
After an unknowable time, you discern whispers emanating from the depths below.
Who could it be? Your targets—the members of the expedition? You can't be certain; those whispers are too distant and muffled to make out.
You try to turn toward the source of the sound, but your body remains beyond your control.
Gradually, that sound draws closer, carried into your ears by the seawater.
The currents shift, turning your body along, and at last you catch sight of the source of the whispers.
[Small CG 1 Section 1]
Instead of the familiar figures you expected, before you lies a vast, bottomless void.
Some soft, tentacle-like appendages reach out to drag your body down as the space around you slowly constricts. Above, the red glow becomes even more distant until it vanishes entirely.
Something's wrong—there's a presence in the void. You cannot descend any further. You must break free to search for your targets.
[Small CG 1 Section 2]
Your attempt proves futile. No matter how desperately you try to move, your body remains unresponsive. Then, it suddenly dawns on you that perhaps, a "corpse" is never meant to move.

You have been deceased—your limbs bloated and contorted in the sea water, your organs reduced to liquid. Carrion worms tunnel into your ears alongside the whispers, only to seep out through your eye sockets.
[Small CG 1 Section 3]
The whispers draw closer, growing more complex, while worms writhe and gnaw through your brain, devouring what little is left of your nerves.
Soon, you will fall into the utmost darkness, joining that presence in eternal demise.
At that moment, a wholly distinct voice—light but clear—pierces through the maddening whispers and resonates within your soul.
...Are you... afraid of this place?
Before you can answer, a hand reaches down and grabs you. Upon the touch, warm life-ness flows back into your body.

You find a mysterious being before you—neither fully human nor wholly otherworldly—enveloped in a faint white light, along with numerous ethereal white little creatures. Her true form remains veiled from your sight.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Not here...
...I see... Then... follow me...
Let me take you out...
Her voice envelops you in tranquility and solace, drowning out the fear instilled by the whispers from the previous darkness.
When you glance back, the tentacles that once ensnared you have already vanished without a trace.
Guided by the luminous white being, you ascend gradually, drawing ever closer to the surface.
The intensifying light from above casts a surreal glare on everything surrounding you.
Here seems to be where the darkness ends. She releases your hand, letting your body drift upward with the waves.

options: Are you not coming with me?

content: [Big CG 1 Section 1]
You want to return, to grab her hand and take her away from the icy waters. Yet she does not respond to your intentions, merely waving goodbye as she watches you drift upward.
Your consciousness gradually slips away, dissolving into the ethereal white light.
Your eyes snap open, only to realize everything that just happened was nothing more than an illusory dream.
You find your clothes clean and dry—proving that the encounter was but a dream, and that you haven't even touched the sea.

You find yourself in a small boat on the water. The sea is calm, with no sign of the colossal corpse from before. In the sky—the Illusory Moon is no longer glaringly bright but a faint presence in the heavens, as if observed through a veil of mist. As you look at it, for the first time, there are no maddening whispers echoing in your ears.
Is this the protection Schorl mentioned? It seems that you have anchored at the target space. The memories of that "dream" earlier are already blurring into a distant haze.
Perhaps it was simply a transitional phase during your entry into the realm, a "dream within a dream" before this space settled—something that never actually occurred.
The mirror-like sea surface reflects the red moonlight. Occasionally, bubbles and white shapes flicker beneath, vanishing in mere moments.
As you ponder what lies hidden beneath the surface, suddenly—
Following a tiny splash, a black ball breaches the surface. Startled, you lose your balance and stumble back into the boat.
As your eyes regain focus, you see a glass panel at the front of the ball, and behind it, a pair of bright eyes.
You and the owner of those eyes stare at each other, locked in this awkward and bizarre silence for almost a minute.
Finally, the woman moves. She swims closer, seizes the gunwale, and elegantly vaults into your boat, landing before you.
Then, she removes the black ball on her head, her diving mask. In the moonlight, her long hair cascades down like a waterfall, revealing a delicate, fair face.
She scrutinizes you intently, her eyes as serene as still waters. You hear only steady breathing—no words escape her lips. There is something oddly familiar and reassuring about this moment.
A gut feeling tells you that she is one of the people Schorl mentioned—your companion, your "safety net," the target you must establish contact with in the mission.
After a moment of silence, she finally speaks.

speaker: Woman in Diving Suit
content: You didn't need to come.
She pauses before resuming her speech.

speaker: Woman in Diving Suit
content: No need to come looking for me. I'll go back once my work's done here.
Her manner appears aloof, yet you sense no hostility in her. She simply comes across as a socially awkward person, merely attempting to convince a companion to leave away from danger.

options: Try to come up with something

content: As you consider how to break the ice and gather more information about these waters, a shout reaches your ears from the distance.

speaker: Forthright Male Voice
content: Hey—over here—
You look up and see a small submarine approaching your boat.
The submarine stops before you. Two men get out of the vessel and engage you in conversation face to face.

speaker: Forthright Male Voice
content: How's the salvage going? Need any help...? Hold on, is that our little guide? What are you doing here?
The man speaking seems to know Pylgia very well and sees you as a child, just like everyone else here before.

speaker: Forthright Male Voice
content: You here for Pylgia too? Well, come on into our sub.
Like always, you follow them into the vessel as the "little guide" again, and manage to gather more insights into the expedition.

After a grim crisis several months ago, the expedition tracked the flames to the DisSea Border, where they set up their base camp. The team members assigned to investigate the DisSea and the Perishing Star have assembled submersibles and boats, already undertaking several diving and salvage operations.

speaker: Forthright Male Voice
content: ...Our mission this time is to retrieve the data collectors deployed during the last moonrise, and bring 'em back to Shin.

The Shin he mentioned seems to be the ocean scientist on their dive team. As for the two before you, there’s Ragnar—a robust, bearded middle-aged man who pilots the submarine—and Dale, a lean young man who, like Pylgia, works as a diver.

speaker: Ragnar
content: Who knows what's up with this damn sea? Only when the moon's out does that huge hole show up at the bottom. Then we gotta chuck the collectors down there during that tiny window and haul 'em back up when the moon rises again. It's a pain, I swear.

speaker: Ragnar
content: Ugh, honestly, this is ridiculous. The job's super urgent, but they just wouldn't cough up more help...

speaker: Dale
content: Usually, Pylgia handles the collector retrieval on her own, but this time we got a tighter deadline, so Shin sent Ragnar and me to help out.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: She's been doing this all alone?

speaker: Dale
content: Yes, Pylgia's our best diver. There are many tasks that only she can take care of.

speaker: Ragnar
content: You said it! She's a total champ in the water—better than any sea monster out there. Nothing can even keep up with her! Hey, Pylgia, is it true you can talk to deep-sea critters?
Pylgia offers no verbal response, standing alone in a far corner and letting an awkward silence permeate the air.
Seemingly well-acquainted with Pylgia's character, Ragnar displays no unease and continues talking in a relaxed manner.

speaker: Ragnar
content: This mission's a big deal. Those collectors mean a lot to Shin's crew. We'll be counting on you to lead the way once we dive in, you good?

speaker: Pylgia
content: Actually...
Pylgia wants to speak, but hesitates for a few seconds before finding back her voice.

speaker: Pylgia
content: You didn't need to come. I can handle it here.
Her tone lacks any trace of arrogance, nor the firmness expected in a refusal. Perhaps, she is simply concerned about the safety of her companions.

speaker: Dale
content: Things are different this time. All our collectors are down there—it's too many for you to manage alone.

speaker: Ragnar
content: Yep, right on the money. Those scientists keep yapping about how the seabed shifts with each tide, so we gotta grab all the collectors now—no chance you could handle that on your own.

speaker: Ragnar
content: If we lose even one of those precious gadgets, we'll never hear the end of it from the folks on shore!
Faced with the barrage of words from the two men, Pylgia remains silent, only casting a gloomy glance at the porthole.

speaker: Pylgia
content: ...I'll go check outside.
With that said, she opens the submarine's top hatch and climbs out.
Seeing Pylgia leave, Ragnar looks rather relaxed.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Should we... take that as a yes?

speaker: Ragnar
content: Yeah, it takes a bit of time to figure out how to work with her, but she's actually pretty reasonable—just not the most expressive person.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Is really the heavy workload that you're here to help?

speaker: Ragnar
content: Haha, a sharp little one, aren't you? Truth be told, we're mostly here 'cause we're worried about her.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Worried? But you said she's the best diver you have.

speaker: Ragnar
content: That's true, but things aren't safe beneath the surface lately. Last month, a three-person squad went on a mission and disappeared—haven't heard a peep so far.

speaker: Ragnar
content: Since our first dive six months ago, monster sightings have quadrupled. Pylgia's a pro at this, yes... but she's still human. If she keeps going solo like this, with no one watching her back during missions...

speaker: Ragnar
content: We're worried that one day she might run into a monster and...

speaker: Dale
content: Ahem... Ragnar.
A noise emanates from the hatch as Dale adeptly interrupts the talk. Shortly after, Pylgia enters.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Equipments are all set. We can go now.

speaker: Ragnar
content: Right, time to hunt.

speaker: Ragnar
content: Pylgia, you handle the port side. Dale, you got the starboard. As for our guide... help me watch over this, will ya? Just keep an eye on this pressure gauge and give me a heads-up if anything seems off.
Following Ragnar's gesture, you spot a large set of levers and panels.

speaker: Ragnar
content: Let's roll!
The engines roar to life as seawater fills the ballast tanks, allowing the submarine to descend.

speaker: Ragnar
content: We've reached the designated location. Pylgia, set up the first security perimeter.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Roger.
Through the monitor, you see Pylgia holding a metallic portable, flips the switch, and places it in the water.
To your surprise, the device hovers at where it's deployed instead of sinking, emanating an ethereal blue glow.

speaker: Ragnar
content: You mean the alarm? Oh, just a gadget the tech team cooked up using some glowing blue crystals.

speaker: Ragnar
content: This is also part of the job—we've got some sketchy stuff happening down here lately. If any weird creatures swing by, it'll set off an alarm to give the surface teams a heads-up to clear out.

Through the device's dial, you catch sight of the shimmering blue crystals Ragnar spoke of. Although their crystal structure resembles that of a Hypercube, their appearance is vastly distinct—more like flowers blossoming on a plant.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I thought we'd run into some monsters on our way down.

speaker: Ragnar
content: Heh, hold your horses. Won't be long.
[Switch Scene]

speaker: Pylgia
content: Eleven o'clock, evade.
Ragnar wrenches the helm hard to starboard. Less than two seconds later, a grotesque creature—deathly pale with limbs that seem grafted from various sea creatures—glides right past the porthole.

speaker: Ragnar
content: Pylgia, Dale, keep an eye out! These things are quick—I'm ready to fire at any second!

speaker: Dale
content: Copy that.

speaker: Ragnar
content: Pylgia, do you copy? ...Pylgia? Pylgia!
Something is fast approaching, another one from the left side.
You rush to the porthole, only to find Pylgia utterly motionless as another pale creature charges towards her at a terrifying pace.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Watch out!
You can't help but shout out, trying to warn Pylgia of the creature's attack. However, clearly seeing the approaching threat, she makes no attempt to dodge—instead, she stretches her hand.

In the next moment, an astonishing sight unfolds before you: the creature slows down as if restrained by an invisible force, eventually suspended right in front of Pylgia. They fall locked in an uncanny standoff.

Then, an impossibly high-frequency, almost imperceptible piercing sound reaches your ears. Influenced by this seemingly illusory noise, the creature—which had been charging forward in a frenzy moments ago—begins to retreat as if "persuaded" by Pylgia.
Suddenly, Dale's voice cuts through, interrupting the sound.

speaker: Dale
content: Pylgia, clear out!
Before you realize it, Dale has already moved to Pylgia's side, his sharp underwater weapon firing straight through the creature.
The creature writhes violently, letting out a blood-curdling shriek. In the meanwhile, countless inhuman eyes emerge from the darkness, all fixed on the submarine.

After Dale kills the first monster, more surge forth from the dark waters, forcing you into a desperate battle. Ragnar had no choice but to fire one of the submarine's only two torpedoes, barely managing to break free from the swarm.
As the battle ends, you glance at the pressure gauge and find the descent speed higher than expected.

speaker: Ragnar
content: (Pants)...
After such a narrow escape, even Ragnar, a seasoned pilot, is now gasping for breath.

speaker: Ragnar
content: Pylgia, you alright?

speaker: Pylgia
content: I'm fine.

speaker: Ragnar
content: Good. But don't freeze up like that again—if Dale hadn't jumped in fast, you might've been in serious trouble.

speaker: Ragnar
content: If we run into more of them, give me a heads-up ASAP. I'll shoot right off the bat. I'm not letting them get near us again.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Don't need... to fire...
For some reason, Pylgia's voice is breaking up, and with the radio static added, you are unable to discern what she is trying to say.
You check the monitor and see that she continues to swim alongside the submarine as before, nothing unusual.

speaker: Ragnar
content: What did you just say? Couldn't catch it.

speaker: Pylgia
content: I said...
She pauses for a long moment, only to force out two words.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Never mind...

Following the earlier battle, the monsters' sightings have not diminished—they have become more frequent somehow. Even when repelled, they simply withdraw into the shadows, biding their time for another opportunity to attack.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Something's wrong with the pressure gauge readings. We shouldn't be descending this fast. Is it the monsters' doing?

speaker: Ragnar
content: It's okay. We'll be fine. This won't happen again, probably...
Ragnar, his eyebrows knit in a frown, has completely forgotten that he had asked you to give warnings. He steers the submarine while attempting to reassure you, the only "child" on the team.

Disregarding Ragnar's comforting, you focus on recalling the monsters' traits. The first one you encountered was hideous in appearance but not inherently aggressive—Pylgia even managed to pacify it initially.

Nevertheless, as the battle persists, the newly appearing monsters become increasingly fearsome. They exhibit nothing but hostility towards any movement, launching attacks at every chance when their numbers amass.
Has the combat heightened their aggression? Or perhaps...
Thud—
An abrupt loud thump startles you out of your thoughts, and you turn to Ragnar at the helm.

speaker: Ragnar
content: Damn it! A monster on the port side!
At Ragnar's call, Pylgia immediately swims to check.

speaker: Pylgia
content: No creature spotted. Just a reef.
As Pylgia shines her searchlight, you all look over. The "monster" reveals itself to be nothing more than a deformed coral rock.

speaker: Ragnar
content: Shoot... Alright.
Ragnar mutters under his breath, but the tension remains unbroken both inside and out. The frequent battles have left everyone on edge.

As the searchlight beam moves away, everything outside fades back into darkness. In the porthole, you catch a glimpse of yourself—a child sporting a red neckerchief, referred to by the expedition as the "little guide."
Yet when you look down at yourself, both your body and clothes appear completely normal—being the same adult in this realm as you are in the real world.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So, this place does have the truth about my past...
Your past self, the expedition's fate... Your mind starts to wander as you recall Ragnar's earlier joking about "being taken by sea monsters."
The previous nightmare of falling into the vast void... Could that be a forewarning of things to come?
The darkness answers not, akin to the bottomless pit from your dream, only mirroring your unsettled silhouette.
Silence reigns, with only the persistent static from the radio filling the space. The ambiance becomes oppressively dense, making it hard to catch a breath.
Knock, knock...
A rhythmic tapping comes from the porthole.
You glance up to see Pylgia, floating there in full diving gear. Silence falls again between you, but this time, through her diving mask, her gaze is steadier as if trying to calm your unease.
Capturing your focus, she gracefully glides away a little, unveiling a cluster of white, softly bioluminescent plankton floating into the spot she previously occupied.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Are they trying to... greet me?
Pylgia nods at you. Then—maybe it's just your mind playing tricks—the white creatures begin to move, arranging themselves into a playful smile.
You rub your eyes in disbelief, yet the luminous smile has already vanished. The plankton revert to their original state, swimming aimlessly around Pylgia.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: They seem... fond of you?
Pylgia gently touches one of the luminous beings with her finger and answers with certainty.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Yes, because I can understand what they're trying to convey.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So you really can understand these deep-sea creatures? What are they saying?
Pylgia falls silent, seemingly contemplating her response. Meanwhile, the white creatures position themselves above her head in a dotted line that strikingly resembles an ellipsis.
Faced with Pylgia's prolonged silence, you decide to break the ice discreetly.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I wish I could understand what these little ones are saying too...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Once we complete our mission and leave this place, could you teach me how to talk to them?
This time, Pylgia responds with a firm nod.
The submarine rocks slightly in the turbulent currents. Pylgia casts a glance downward and waves at you.

speaker: Pylgia
content: We're approaching the target location. I'll go find a suitable spot to dock.
Pylgia returns to her duties, but not before giving you a nod that seems to say, "See you soon."
In this brief private moment, you glimpse a spark of life beneath her reserved facade.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Being a child sometimes does work wonders...
You smile and then glance back to where the luminescent creatures were, only to find that they have vanished without a trace.
Under Pylgia's guidance, the submarine descends to the white sandy seabed, swaying gently.
While Ragnar and Dale, relieved and convinced their mission is half complete, see only hope, what you see outside is the stark opposite—an omen of anything but a safe return.
Beneath you stretches a vast void of infinite darkness, the submarine anchoring right at its edge.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This is... the place in my dream.

speaker: Ragnar
content: Still no sign of the collectors?

speaker: Dale
content: No... Pylgia, what about your side?
After scouring for more than ten minutes, the team has only located a few collectors at their designated spots, with the rest having disappeared without a trace.

speaker: Pylgia
content: The seabed terrain changed earlier than expected. I've checked all our marked locations. Nothing there.
There's an unusual unease in Pylgia's voice over the radio—a clear sign that even she has lost control of the situation.

speaker: Pylgia
content: There's only one possible area left...
All four of you simultaneously turn to gaze at the vast void.
For the past ten minutes, you have all silently agreed to ignore its existence.
Anyone in their right mind can sense something down there—something so terrifying that none of you dare to voice the worst possibilities.

speaker: Pylgia
content: The collectors are... probably down there.

speaker: Dale
content: ...The Maw of the Abyss... We've got some serious trouble here.
The Maw of the Abyss—this is the first time you've heard your team members name this enormous void. Dark, cold, harboring untold dangers, devouring all... Truly, no name could be more fitting.

speaker: Pylgia
content: ...We should go back.

speaker: Ragnar
content: ...I understand your worries, but...
Ragnar, upon hearing Pylgia's proposal, showed an uncharacteristic hesitation.

speaker: Ragnar
content: Those collectors are the dive team's life. Shin's whole crew is counting on them! If we go back empty-handed, this mission, no, the expedition would be pointless! Sorry, but I really can't give them up...

speaker: Pylgia
content: But...
Pylgia's voice carries even more concern.

speaker: Pylgia
content: We've never dived down into the Abyss before. We're clueless about what lies in there.

speaker: Pylgia
content: ...I can feel it. It's dangerous.
When the champ diver, known for being fearless all the time, uses the word "dangerous," the tension in the air grows even thicker.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Maybe... when the next tide comes and shifts the terrain again, the collectors might resurface from the Abyss, and then...

speaker: Dale
content: The odds are too low. We can't afford that risk.
Dale's voice, somewhat hoarse, comes through the radio.

speaker: Dale
content: Resources are stretched thin. The tech team won't be able to manufacture another batch of collectors for us.

speaker: Ragnar
content: ...We can't just sit back and watch six months of everyone's work go down the drain...

speaker: Pylgia
content: ...I'll go.
Pylgia pauses for a moment as if steeling her resolve.

speaker: Pylgia
content: I'll go alone. You guys take these collectors we've gathered back to base.

speaker: Ragnar
content: What are you thinking, Pylgia? We're the ones insisting on going in there. We can't let you go in on our behalf, especially not alone!

speaker: Ragnar
content: I've been at this gig for ages—can't let a lady dive into that death trap alone. We'll go together. Trust me, it's always better four than one.

speaker: Pylgia
content: But...

speaker: Dale
content: We trust your instincts and skills, but there's no way you can retrieve all of them on your own. I know how capable you are, but you need help.
After a long moment of silence, you hear a soft sigh through the radio.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Anything goes south, turn back. Don't push yourselves...
You've been descending through the dark pit for what seems like an eternity, yet haven't come across any substantial danger.

Conversely, the area beneath the Abyss is eerily silent, with only darkness enveloping everything. The deeper you descend into this void, the stronger the feeling that something horrifying is watching you. A nameless dread permeates both the inside and outside of the submarine.
The pressure gauge readings skyrocket, anxiety gnawing at your mind, your nerves growing increasingly taut.

speaker: Ragnar
content: We're descending... way too fast...
Ragnar's teeth are chattering. This seasoned pilot is behaving completely out of character, constantly glancing over his shoulder with an expression so nervous that even makes you feel uneasy.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Found them. Twenty yards ahead, port bow.
Pylgia's voice somehow remains remarkably calm.

speaker: Ragnar
content: What? For real...? We found them just like that?!
A small ledge juts out from the chasm wall. In the submarine's searchlight beam, you can make out the silhouettes of about a dozen metal objects.

speaker: Dale
content: No, something's wrong! The collectors... they are damaged!
Panic saturates Dale's voice. You hasten to the porthole to witness it firsthand—the thick metal shells of the collectors are severely cracked.

Even more astonishing is the giant tear at the center of every collector, as if something had violently ripped them apart, leaving the delicate instruments exposed to seawater without protective shells.

speaker: Ragnar
content: Stay back!
Ragnar's voice rises to a piercing pitch as he yells out the command.

speaker: Ragnar
content: A trap... This is a trap! Must be some monster ambushing us... Pylgia!

speaker: Pylgia
content: I don't see any.

speaker: Ragnar
content: There must be!
Ragnar's voice rises even higher, becoming painfully shrill.

speaker: Ragnar
content: Ever since we descended, I've felt it—something's been watching me... It's right around here!
Ragnar's mental state is palpably frantic, and equally unsettling is Dale's labored, erratic breathing transmitted through the radio.

speaker: Dale
content: These shells are made of tough alloy... What kind of monster... could tear this apart...?
Both Ragnar and Dale are on the verge of breakdown—a highly uncommon situation for such seasoned sailors. You take the radio from Ragnar, hoping to get a response from Pylgia.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Pylgia, are you sure you don't see anything?

speaker: Pylgia
content: No...
Pylgia speaks in her usual monotone voice.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Ragnar and Dale don't seem normal. We must go back. Pylgia, can you take the collectors?

speaker: Pylgia
content: Got it.

It's taking some time for Pylgia to carry all the collectors alone. Before you, Ragnar rambles in an unintelligible tongue, his eyes bloodshot with foam frothing at his mouth. Outside, Dale mutters incessantly while swimming in agitated loops around the submarine.

The tension and unease persist, and you too begin to sense something is amiss—a disquieting feeling of numerous watching eyes. Drawing from your past experiences, you suddenly realize what the problem is:
Human emotions manifest in the reality of the DisSea. Therefore at this moment, the unrestrained fear of Ragnar and Dale is awakening something that should never have existed.

speaker: Dale
content: It's coming... It's here!
Outside, Dale suddenly starts pounding violently on the hatch door.

speaker: Dale
content: Let me in... Let me in!! Open up!!

speaker: Pylgia
content: Watch out!
Pylgia's voice comes through the radio before you start to speak.

speaker: Dale
content: Ugh!!!
Before you can even say or do anything, a massive tentacle emerges from the darkness, violently piercing Dale's chest.
Under the pale searchlight, a red mist explodes in the water. Dale lets out an agonized scream as the tentacle drags his limp body into the darkness at an astonishing speed.

The seafloor suddenly begins to shake violently, unleashing a profound, deafening rumble. As white sand cascades away, the rocks beneath shift slowly, revealing myriad viscous, black-and-white crystalline objects.

speaker: Ragnar
content: Dale?!
Ragnar stares in disbelief as the killing unfolds just before him. In the darkness, a bone-chilling grinding sound reaches your ears.

speaker: Ragnar
content: I gotta get out... Gotta get out of this hellhole... I... I...

speaker: Ragnar
content: AHHHH!!

speaker: Pylgia
content: Reef ahead, watch out!
Under Pylgia's warning, the submarine narrowly maneuvers through a maze of mysterious skeletal remains and rocks.
But there's no time for respite—the colossal creature trails closely behind, resembling a leviathan of flesh and bone, smashing through everything in its path.
The massive impacts echo through the Abyss, like the tolling of a demonic bell, signaling impending doom.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Ragnar, we need to surface now! No way we can get rid of it in the Abyss.
But Ragnar appears entirely impervious to your words, his entire body stiff as he holds the depth helm at its utmost limit. His bloodshot eyes dart repeatedly to the pressure gauge.
However, when you divert your attention to the pressure gauge, the reading hasn't diminished in the least—instead, the needle is quivering violently towards the right.
You finally realize that as your companion's sanity fractures, some indescribable force is dragging your submarine—tons of solid steel—relentlessly deeper into the Abyss.
You have lost track of how long this deadly game of cat and mouse with the monster has lasted.
Suddenly, Ragnar beside you turns his head toward you with an unnaturally stiff motion, his cracked lips parting into a smile.

speaker: Ragnar
content: Dale?
You come to the realization that Ragnar isn't looking at you but at the porthole behind you.
You spin around to find a black diving suit pressed against the window. Its loose metal helmet sways in the current, repeatedly tapping against the submarine.
Pylgia drives her harpoon into the diving suit, forcefully prying it away.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Move the sub! That's not Dale; it's...
Before Pylgia can finish, a massive tentacle sweeps past, cutting off her warning. That fleeting moment reveals "Dale" in his entirety.
His body is inexplicably fused to the monster's tentacle, the diving suit distended with an unknown substance, making him look like a swollen water balloon.
At the same time, the impact kills the engine, and the screech of grinding metal threatens to rupture your eardrums.

speaker: Ragnar
content: Hahaha... So this is the way out...
All color has drained from Ragnar's pale face as he stares transfixed at the tentacles, his hands having long since abandoned the helm.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Go, it's catching up!
There's an unusual urgency in Pylgia's voice. But you don't need her warning to know the monster is breathing down your neck.
But Ragnar has completely lost his mind. He slumps in the pilot's seat, his face buried in his hands, emitting nothing but hoarse laughter.
As the submarine remains motionless in the water, the sound of breathing and static crackles through the radio. Outside the porthole, Pylgia glances back, her eyes indiscernible in the darkness.

speaker: Pylgia
content: I'll hold it off.
In the boundless dark water of the Abyss, Pylgia raises her searchlight high and blasts a piercing beam directly into the giant creature's face.

The monster, having lurked in darkness since time immemorial, recoils from the intense light. Its strike, originally aimed at the submarine, goes wide, colliding with the rock wall with such force that the entire Abyss appears to tremble.
Shortly after, it notices the tiny figure that dares to provoke its might, unleashing its pale, slimy tentacles to lash viciously at Pylgia.
Pylgia dodges the lethal strike with incredible agility, yet there's no respite for her as more putrid tentacles come crashing towards her, one after another.

options: Try to snap Ragnar out of it

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Wake up Ragnar! Pylgia's holding off the monster. Start the engine, right now!
The submarine violently shudders as tentacles outside exert unimaginable force, hurling the vessel deeper into the Abyss. The impact throws you to the floor.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: We can't... let her effort go to waste...

speaker: Ragnar
content: Go to waste... Ha... Hahaha... Don't you get it yet?

Ragnar turns his head with mechanical stiffness to gaze at you sprawled on the floor, his mouth stretching into an impossible grin, nearly reaching his ears, as black ooze seeps from his eyes, nostrils, and gums.

speaker: Ragnar
content: It's all in vain... There's no escape... We're doomed... No... no...

speaker: Ragnar
content: It's been so many times... You knew it...! The moment we entered this... we... we were already dead...
Ragnar—no, this isn't Ragnar anymore. Some entity has seized control of his consciousness. It knows your history, cognizant of your countless futile struggles in the DisSea.

speaker: Ragnar
content: You can't save her... or anyone... You never... belonged here...

Outside the submarine, Pylgia persists in her battle with the monster. Despite her unparalleled speed underwater, she's but a raft in a tempest, destined to be engulfed by the monster's relentless assault.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Ugh...
A muffled grunt of pain comes through the radio.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Pylgia!
Pylgia offers no response. All you can hear is the endless rambling of "Ragnar" by your ears.

speaker: Ragnar
content: This is... our... end...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Pylgia, where are you?!
There's still one torpedo left on the sub—maybe you can use it to blast through the tentacles, but there's only writhing darkness wherever you peer. You can't even discern the target to strike.
Your hands tremble as rage and frustration scream to burst out of your chest, yet with nowhere to be vented.
Once again, a companion vanishes before your eyes. And once again, you are utterly powerless to stop it...

speaker: Pylgia
content: ...I'm fine.
Suddenly, Pylgia's weakened voice crackles through the radio.
The familiar figure appears outside the porthole. Harpoon gripped tight, Pylgia navigates through the onslaught of attacks as dense as a fishing net, turning the battle into a deadly dance.

speaker: Pylgia
content: I... can try to hold it off for a while longer.

speaker: Pylgia
content: If Ragnar couldn't make it, at least there's you...

speaker: Pylgia
content: Start the engine and get out of here.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Get Ragnar and the collectors back... please.
Pylgia isn't dead yet, but like every companion before her, she is willing to sacrifice her life to light a path through the darkness.
But you refuse to let it end this way again—even if just this once, you want to save someone.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: There's still a way. We can make it back together!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I won't let you go... Not any of you!
You must save Pylgia, and Ragnar, even though he is being possessed by something... Wait, or perhaps Ragnar is the key to all this.

He's slouching in the pilot's seat at the moment, his blood-red eyes locked on you in an unblinking gaze. If emotions can shape reality in the DisSea, maybe by stopping him from spreading fear is the way...
You grab the spare oxygen tank and smash it against Ragnar's head. Without a moment to react, his body shudders violently upon the impact before he collapses unconscious.
Almost instantly, the monster outside freezes mid-motion, like data running into an error. It hangs suspended in place, even the shrill screams falling silent.
However, the peace lasts only a moment before the creature resumes its movement. Yet this time, you unmistakably sense that its speed and strength have significantly waned.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Pylgia, listen up. I'm taking the tiller now. We can still counterattack... There's still a chance.
You drag the unconscious Ragnar aside and take the pilot's seat, your hand fiercely gripping the torpedo launch button.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: There's one torpedo left. All we need is to find an opening...
Pylgia grasps the situation almost instantly. After taking a few breaths, she speaks with unwavering determination.

speaker: Pylgia
content: I'll lure the tentacles away. Aim at me.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What? But what about you?

speaker: Pylgia
content: Trust me.
It's undoubtedly a plan bordering on madness. However, with only one torpedo remaining, you have just this one chance to strike.
You have no choice but to trust her—perhaps she is the only one in the world who could pull this off.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Okay... I trust you!
You restart the engine and turn the submarine around, your fingers clenched tightly on the torpedo launch button.

At the same time, Pylgia charges forward at an incredible speed, her harpoon paving the path ahead. In this instant, she resembles an unstoppable marlin as she dives headfirst into the tangle of tentacles.

She moves too fast and dives too deeply for the tentacles to catch up with her. As they pursue and jostle against each other in their chase, they inadvertently form a small pocket of space around Pylgia at the center.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Now!
Following Pylgia's signal, you press the torpedo launch button, your heart caught in your throat.
The gap between the tentacles is too narrow, and at such a high velocity, even Pylgia cannot feasibly alter her course. The torpedo will strike her, propelling her body directly into the monster.

But in that split second, Pylgia executes an impossible maneuver—she springs upward at the final instant, as the torpedo streaks past her in a flurry of bubbles and currents, descending deep into the tangle of tentacles.
The next moment, your vision is engulfed in the glaring explosion.
[Explosion]

The explosion unleashes a devastating shockwave, its force immediately hammering the submarine. The metal vessel tumbles in the powerful currents as you are tossed around the cabin like a rag doll in a spin cycle.
You struggle to your feet, pushing through the ringing in your ears and the throbbing headache, and stagger towards the porthole.
Outside lies pitch darkness, the submarine obstructed by drifting monster remnants. You reach for the radio.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Pylgia, are you okay? Answer me!
The ringing in your ears drowns out all other sounds. You can't make out anything.
Where is she? Did she escape the blast? Is she hurt?
Questions flood your mind as you call out her name, again and again, your heart racing with desperate worry.

speaker: Pylgia
content: I'm... fine...
At last, you discern Pylgia's voice. Enveloped in a gentle white radiance, she's fast approaching your location.
Accompanied by her side, white luminescent particles surge forth from behind her—the same plankton you have met before, beyond the Abyss, in... a not-so-distant dream.
They saved you before, and once again, they have helped Pylgia achieve this miraculous escape.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You made it!

speaker: Pylgia
content: We made it, together.
Pylgia's voice retains its usual composure yet is tinged with a hint of a smile.

speaker: Pylgia
content: But, it's not dead.
A deep growl echoes from below. The explosion only managed to drive it back. You're not surprised—a monster that colossal wouldn't be easily vanquished.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: At least we've bought some time to escape.
You try to keep your voice light to reassure Pylgia... and yourself.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: There's no time to waste. Show me the way, Pylgia. Let's... get out of the Abyss.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Mmm.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Obstacle ahead. Watch out.
