You alter the course of the submarine just in time, giving Pylgia a quick confirm through the radio.

The injured monster's growls draw nearer, yet there's little you can do. All that remains is to trust in Pylgia's guidance and pray that the impaired submarine can carry you to safety before the monster catches up.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Ragnar... Is he okay?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Not good... Looks like he's been possessed by something...
He seems trapped in some terrible nightmare. His eyes are shut tight, his face alternating between terror and eerie grins as he mumbles incomprehensible words.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Dr. Banyan will cure him. I'm sure...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Let's get out of here first.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Okay.

speaker: Ragnar
content: It's coming... The monster... will die... no escape...
Ragnar's condition deteriorates further. Something squirms beneath his skin, and his delirious mutterings become increasingly coherent.
But you don't have the luxury to worry about him now. Maneuvering through the darkness saps your energy and mental acuity, demanding continual vigilance against the monster's abrupt assaults.
Never in your life have you wished so desperately for a vessel to move faster.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Incoming... from the left!
You execute an immediate maneuver, evading the monster's onslaught.

Through the porthole, you catch sight of the monster's incomplete form, marred by the explosion. However, its fractured tentacles and mangled shape have not impeded its pursuit—if anything, the damage has rendered it even more fearsome.
Its damaged tentacles reach out, catching the rear propeller. The entire submarine lurches to a stop, nearly ejecting you from the pilot's seat.

speaker: Pylgia
content: I'll lure it away!
Pylgia tries her old trick again, raising the searchlight high to draw the monster's attention.
But this time, the monster ignores the glowing "insect" before it, focusing all its attacks on the submarine instead.
With a bone-chilling screech of rending metal, one of the propellers is torn clean off, as more tentacles coil around the submarine's stern.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The sub will be immobilized at this rate!

Pylgia knows full well how dire the situation is. Realizing the monster won't target her, she opts for a more audacious approach—forsaking evasion and defense to mount a full-scale assault with her harpoon.
With a single shot, the tiny harpoon severs a tentacle thicker than Pylgia's entire body from the submarine's tail fin.
However, it's far from killing it—the monster has too many tentacles.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This isn't working. We need to hit its vital point.
However, the monster's body remains entirely shielded behind countless tentacles. There is no torpedo remaining, and Pylgia is no longer able to divert the monster's attention.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Let me be the bait. You find an opening to strike.
Pylgia catches your intention in no time.

You shut down the rear engine and activate the lateral propellers, rotating the helm to its limit. The submarine executes a full 180-degree turn in the water, compelling the entangled tentacles to coil along with it. Unable to retain their grip, the tentacles briefly lose their grasp on the vessel.
The submarine's bow now faces directly at the monster's body.
The steel vessel charges forward at full throttle, ripping a path through the monster's fleshy tentacles.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Now!
Surrounded by drifting plankton, Pylgia's figure transforms into a white meteor, plunging swiftly through the breach in the tentacles and directly towards the monster's exposed body.
The breach created by the submarine's collision lasts mere seconds before the tentacles reconstitute into a new barrier, engulfing Pylgia as she charges in alone.
For what seems like an eternity, you hear nothing but silence through the radio—except for the sickening squelch of myriad putrid, slimy tentacles coiling around the hatch.
But this will not the end for the two of you—not here, not now.

The monster's piercing shriek cuts through water and steel, but this hellish sound now rings like sweet music, heralding victory. The entwined tentacles convulse and withdraw, their barrier crumbling away.

You finally behold the monster's true form—a fusion of fish fins and scales intertwined with the razor-sharp claws of crustaceans. Pervaded by bloodless, decaying flesh, this creature appears to be a grotesque patchwork of every terror the deep sea has to offer.
A colossal breach now gapes through the center of the monster's body. You can even see charred fragments of flesh drifting around its periphery.
And through that hole, you find that familiar spare figure.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Pylgia!
The tiny harpoon thrusts deep into the monster's head. Then, as the tip expands, she rips off an entire section of shell and tissue.
Despite the monster being gravely injured, the figure exhibits no sign of slowing, darting around it at a dizzying speed akin to a razor-sharp blade, leaving a tempest of shredded flesh in her wake.
The monster is unable to match her speed in the slightest, its tentacles thrashing frenziedly yet unable to land even a single hit.
You start the engine, your target crystal clear this time—the monster's head. The submarine is just a few dozen meters from the monster, which is close enough for you.

Once again, the steel vessel transforms into a weapon, hurtling directly at the cornered mass of flesh. The weighty hull drives into the monster's body as the high-speed propellers rend through its tender innards.
[Fade Out to Switch Scene]
Seconds later, the submarine drills out from the other side of the monster. Just as you expected, its massive body shatters and slowly sinks back to where it came from—the dark Abyss.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: We did it!
In a distance, Pylgia swiftly swims towards the submarine. The insidious monster has at last been silenced. This triumph is one shared between the two of you.

speaker: Pylgia
content: No more monsters... Let me guide you back.
The path back is now unobstructed, and together you will return to the expedition with both your injured companions and the crucial data collectors.

speaker: Ragnar
content: Hehe...

Behind you, a hollow laugh emanates from your "companion." He was controlled by something from the Abyss, but with the monster vanquished, a glimmer of hope catches you that he may revert to his former self.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Ragnar, you're awake. We can go back now. The monster has been killed...

speaker: Ragnar
content: Hehehe... killed... the monster?

speaker: Ragnar
content: Isn't it... still right there...?
Ragnar directs your attention to the porthole. Following his gesture, you only see Pylgia swimming towards you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That's not the monster. It's Pylgia.
You offer the radio to him, let him speak to Pylgia directly. However, he only spares a glance at it before pivoting back to you with an unsettling grin.
Only now do you realize that the radio is entirely muted, with nothing but silence emanating from the speaker.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It must've been damaged during the collision... Pylgia was just talking to me...
Pylgia has returned to the submarine's side, and through the glass you see that familiar figure. You turn back to Ragnar, gesturing toward her.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Look, she's back. Don't...
You freeze in place, your words faltering in your throat.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Pyl...gia...?

speaker: Pylgia
content: I'm here. Everything's fine now.

speaker: Pylgia
content: ...Is there... anything wrong?
[Big CG 2 Section 2]
A calm voice responds to you. You stiffly turn your head. As she's always done, Pylgia remains hovering there, gazing at you in silence.

Beneath her tattered diving suit, her bared skin is eerily pale, almost translucent, as if enveloped in an otherworldly white glow. The suit clearly no longer shields her from the crushing pressure and frigid cold that would be fatal to any mortal, yet she remains there, her usual calm demeanor making her seem impervious.
There's no mistake—this is Pylgia, the Pylgia you know so well, and also the white figure you first encountered when you entered this "dream."

speaker: Ragnar
content: Too late... It's too late... I told you... the monster never died... they're everywhere... everyone is a monster!
An excruciating pain seizes your chest, causing your legs to give way. Only by leaning against the porthole do you manage to remain upright.
In this position, you finally see Pylgia's true form in its entirety.
(CG3)
Beneath her human torso, several chitinous tentacles—much like those of the monster you killed—stretch down, disappearing into the darkness where your eyes cannot follow.
In your despair, you raise your gaze, only to see Pylgia's sorrowful eyes that hold unspoken words.

speaker: Pylgia
content: A monster... huh...
Pylgia can no longer be considered human by any measure. She has long since transformed into a monster. That dream was a forewarning—everything you have done has been futile.
From the very beginning, you were destined to fail in saving her...
At the moment reality becomes clear, something within your mind abruptly fractures.
The pressure gauge's needle spins wildly. The world lurches in tandem. Infinite darkness floods into the battered, leaking submarine, devouring you in a heartbeat.
That sorrowful figure reaches out to you at the last moment, yet you are already engulfed by overwhelming regret, sliding inevitably into the deepest, farthest dark.
Your last shreds of sanity form into a few fragmented words.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Abyss... fear... dive...
Soon, even this vestige of cognition is devoured. Your final recollection of reality is Ragnar's frenzied wails.

speaker: Ragnar
content: Sinking... sinking again... I knew there's no escape... We're all going to die here...
As the darkness dissolves the submarine, you plunge into the cold, formless waters.
You failed to save Pylgia, and let her become a "monster."
The Abyss has turned your pain and regret into a trap to drag you down into its depths.
When did it all begin?
Was it when the monsters surrounded you, or was it the moment you chose to dive deeper...? Or perhaps, was it the first day you set foot in the DisSea?
Temporary Leader
You are now merely carried along by the currents, devoid of eyes, form, and all senses, powerless to stop this everlasting drift.
You shouldn't even exist.
How long has it been? Perhaps an eternity, or maybe just an instant—you cannot tell, for time has lost all meaning here... But then, you stumble upon something.
Unable to see it, you can only vaguely sense something breaking apart. Then, abruptly, the world is illuminated once again.
You finally have a clear view of where you are—an infinitely vast and desolate darkness, yet in certain places, distant and faint stars still exist.

What lies there? You are uncertain, but you yearn to find out the answer. However, stripped of form, you cannot steer your course. You are once again driven by chaos, drifting towards an uncharted horizon.
In an imperceptible space behind you, an aged monocle shatters, dissolving into invisible dust.
You remain devoid of control, drifting wherever chaos takes you.
At some point, a girl's silhouette emerges within your sight. With a pair of transparent wings and a tangible form, she seems strong enough to soar against the tides of chaos.
She flies about anxiously, seemingly in search of something.
Eventually, her gaze settles upon you.
She alights beside you and folds her wings, letting them dissipate into particles of shimmering light.
Light enters you once more. Gradually, you begin to sense your own existence: hands, feet—you regain a physical form, no longer a mere grain of sand drifting along the currents.
You turn around the very moment when your senses return to you, but the girl is nowhere to be found.
All that remains is a tiny green insect, emitting incomprehensible rustling sounds as it longingly circles around you before vanishing once again into the darkness.
With your body reclaimed, you are finally free from the pull of chaos, able to move on your own.
But you have no memories, no ability to think—you don't know where you're meant to go, only wandering aimlessly.
Until you come to a halt before a statue.
Soon, you realize it's not a statue but a woman standing still.
Having sensed your presence, the woman slowly opens her eyes, seeming to understand your predicament through a single glance.
Without warning, her solid form begins to crumble, flesh dissolving into dust to reveal a skeleton of forged steel beneath.
As the dust disperses, all that's left at the core of the steel structure is one withered heart.
When you pick up this last remnant of her being, the heart transforms into light once again and flows into your body.
Long-buried memories surge forth—you now remember who you are, recalling everything that has brought you here.
As you recover these memories that should never have been lost, you turn back, only to find the steel bones have corroded away. Nothing remains.
You still cannot leave.
The darkness is absolute, the void endless—you can't even be certain an exit exists at all.
But then, in the distance, you spot a flame—a feeble one that could flicker out at any moment, yet it fills you with a familiar warmth.
It takes you a long time, and at last, you reach the flame.
A girl stands there, cradling a torch in her arms, smiling at you.
Firelight begins to radiate from her body as she extends her hand towards you.

In this reality as cold and dark as the deep sea, you slowly discern a colossal, malevolent presence behind you, lurking at the bottom of the Abyss, its existence so overpowering that fear verges on palpable.

Inexplicably, your memories resurface—of your former companions, of Pylgia. You failed to save her. You failed to save any of them. Your bitter regret manifests as tentacles entwining around your body and mind, attempting to drag you further into the depths.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Is this... what you want?
You murmur the question, uncertain whether you are directing it towards yourself, or the presence lurking at the bottom of the Abyss.
You hear a deep resonance, like meaningless, jumbled whispers, or the final breath of a dying being.
It offers no answer to your question. How could it answer your question? From the very beginning, all it ever wanted has been to drag you deeper into the depths.
In desperation, you gaze at the entrance of the Abyss. It's now so distant that only a tiny speck of light remains.
No. There's more than one speck of light.
You struggle to lift your head, watching as the other light speck grows larger, traversing torrents of death and sorrow to reach your side.
The exact scene that you once saw in a dream.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Pyl...gia...
Accompanied by echoes tinkling like wind chimes, luminous plankton emerge one by one, resembling stars strewn across the darkness, drawing closer to you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Pylgia... Is that you?

Memories of her flood back to you—from the dream you had when you first came, to the initial distance between you at your first encounter, then to the trust and mutual reliance you forged while fighting alongside each other.

She is your companion, and what Schorl referred to as your "safety net" in the dream. Regardless of the perils you encounter, she would always find and save you. Perhaps this is the memory etched into your very soul, as well as an inexorable fate intertwining you and them.
You reach out towards the luminous being, but upon the touch, a vision flashes through your mind—Pylgia's face, contorted and marred by the taint of the Abyss.
The truth hits you again: This fate brings not only meetings but partings too—unbearably painful partings. You refuse to accept this imminent parting, your body instinctively recoiling.
As you flinch, the luminous beings that were approaching you freeze in their tracks. Time creeps by, and then a voice reaches your ears.
You are... scared... Did I frighten you?
Because I am... a monster...
That voice bears deep sorrow and loneliness, echoing hollowly with an inhuman resonance that breaks your heart.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No... I'm not scared of you. No matter what you've become, you're always part of the expedition, a cherished companion.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: My duty is to meet you all, to bring back lost hope and possibility. Every encounter... has been meaningful, and they are all memories I hold dear.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It's just... I just...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm afraid of losing you again... just like how I lost them...
...I'm not leaving. I'm still here.
Though her voice still carries a hint of hesitation, the white beings no longer waver, approaching you once again.
Follow me. I'll take you back to where you belong.
Trust me one more time.
More white creatures emerge beside you, gliding through the water, showing you the way.
You no longer reject her kindness. Following the guidance of the luminous beings, you swim towards the surface.

With the luminous beings guiding your path, the once terrifying darkness dissipates in their gentle light. You feel something warm pulling you gently, your body moving toward the surface as your mind finally breaks free from chaos, returning to clarity.
When you realize it, you find yourself before a familiar stone slate. Only a few luminous beings remain beside you, beckoning you forward. You know that just a few steps ahead lies the exit.
But you can't bring yourself to leave like this. Though the luminous creatures have been guiding you all the way, you still haven't seen Pylgia herself—your precious companion.
You refuse to accept such an unspoken farewell. Looking back, you see specks of white light marking your path, forming a faint trail. Could she be hiding at the other end?
After what feels like an eternity, you find her at the path's end—Pylgia, now covered in barnacles and appendages, hiding in the depths of the shadows.
She senses your presence. A brief glimmer of light flashes across her pale pupils, only to fade away instantly.

speaker: Pylgia
content: ...Why are you here?
She remains shrouded in darkness, seemingly attempting to hide her long-mutated form.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Go back. Just follow the light to leave... Go back to everyone else.

speaker: Pylgia
content: You have fulfilled your duty. There's... nothing left here worth staying for.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No.
You shake your head, taking several steps closer.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're still here. How can I just leave?
She lifts her face, one so pale it borders on translucence, her bloodless lips slowly parting. After a long silence, however, only a few words slip out.

speaker: Pylgia
content: But I've... become like this. Are you... not afraid?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm not.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But I'm worried... You said you were still with me, that you hadn't left. But you never showed up again, not even when I reached the end of the path.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If I leave now, will I... never see you again?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Sorry... I'm just being childish, I guess.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You all have your own paths, and your fates are already sealed. I just... I just can't accept it...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Even though a hundred years have passed, you all have to face this cruel end again... and I... I can't do anything... I'm just a bystander, just... just a child you keep sacrificing your lives to save...
Pylgia remains still and listens to you in silence, not much different from her human days. This was how she used to listen to the voice from the Abyss.

speaker: Pylgia
content: You mean... we... everyone in the expedition died?
You feel reluctant to answer, but your expression gives everything away.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Mmm... For humans, death is the farewell that's hardest of all, I understand.

speaker: Pylgia
content: You're suffering because you can't save us, right?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Yes.

speaker: Pylgia
content: But we were people from a century ago.

speaker: Pylgia
content: We were never meant to live in your time.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Not even... you guys in the expedition?

speaker: Pylgia
content: To be honest, I've never fully grasped many of the thoughts humans have.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Civilization, duty, dignity... Choosing these won't change the laws of life.

speaker: Pylgia
content: All life equally becomes part of the cycle—birth, predation, reproduction, sickness, death, and at last, becoming nourishment for other life.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No, not like that. You are all heroes.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This shouldn't be the end for you, at least not here... dying in agony like this, being devoured, burned... And now even you've been taken by this cursed Abyss...

speaker: Pylgia
content: Then, what do you think our end should be like?

speaker: Pylgia
content: The world outside is no different. When the disaster strikes, everyone must fight with all they have just to survive.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Some had already changed, even before joining the expedition or entering this death area.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You mean...

speaker: Pylgia
content: Yes. From the very beginning, I could feel that I was different from others.

speaker: Pylgia
content: I could understand the language of sea creatures and survive in storms and whirlpools. I know the sea even more than the fish.

speaker: Pylgia
content: But I found it more and more difficult to understand my own "kind." I didn't know who I was... or how to live with them.

speaker: Pylgia
content: When I became like this, the world looked different to me again.

speaker: Pylgia
content: You see, it's not all bad. At least now, I can have a proper conversation with you.
You recall your initial encounter with Pylgia. Back then, she always maintained a distance from her companions, never initiating conversations.

Just as she says, only after being contaminated by Mania and losing her human side, she has at last unburdened herself of inner turmoil, capable of accepting her true self and expressing who she truly is.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But Mania... This power is twisted, different from naturally formed life...

speaker: Pylgia
content: It is different, indeed.

speaker: Pylgia
content: No dead human should be able to talk to another soul after a hundred years, right?

speaker: Pylgia
content: Perhaps humans after Nightfall are changed by what you call... Mania, and have found a new path of evolution. They may have broken free from natural forces and entered a broader, unknown cycle of life.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Whether it is me or the other members of the expedition, we make our choice by our own will, becoming the next form of life.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Our consciousness hasn't faded—we're still doing what we find meaningful... From this perspective, we never truly die.
Pylgia gazes into the distance, her pale eyes gleaming with light.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Like me, they have been here all along, hoping to be your strength rather than a source of guilt, given our destined parting...

speaker: Pylgia
content: That, I believe, must be the meaning behind our reunion.
With Pylgia's words, you close your eyes as memories of all the encounters surge forth.

While sifting through these fleeting encounters for their faces, you finally understand that the memories need not be painful—what fills them are mostly moments that have captured their gentlest, most beautiful sides, not death, nor parting.

Perhaps they never truly left, lingering deep within your soul all along. At that moment, you feel an immense weight lifting from your heart. At last, you are freed from the anguish of their recurring deaths.
Pylgia smiles gently.

speaker: Pylgia
content: No need for thanks. We're companions.
Your heart has returned to peace. Looking up, you see a blue light flickering in the distance—probably Schorl reminding you to go back.

That consists of your mission: the Abyss within the DisSea, the presence at its depths, the intelligence on spirit and substance, the hypotheses on human transformation... and above all, the story of the expedition.
You must bring them all back to reality.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Let's take the submarine back. It carries the findings everyone fought so hard for.
Without you needing to say a word, Pylgia already catches your mind.

speaker: Pylgia
content: It's time. I'll see you off.
In a shared comprehension, neither of you utters another word. You both harbor the same wish—that this farewell could wait just a little longer.
You return to the submarine. Everything feels so familiar—the scarred hull, the pressure gauge, and Ragnar, still unconscious beside you.
The submarine's power system is completely dead, but Pylgia remains outside the porthole, guiding countless white plankton to carry you upward.
As you draw closer to the surface, the long-dead radio mysteriously crackles back to life.
This is... hiss... please respond... repeat... this is... hiss... Please answer...
Pyl... Rag... Dale... do you copy...
Rescue is coming your... we...
Whether owing to the distance or other interference, the voice on the radio emerges urgent yet fragmented, laden with static. Nonetheless, you discern some crucial information.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Pylgia, did you hear that? It's the expedition! They're looking for you!

speaker: Pylgia
content: Mm... I heard it.
Suddenly, you notice that the submarine's ascent begins to slow.

The water churns violently, as though attempting to prevent something from passing. Your fears and anguish have already been soothed, so you know that the obstruction does not stem from this battered submarine.
That leaves only one possibility.
Unknown to you, Pylgia has been undergoing a disturbing transmutation.
Barnacles cover her entire body in a dense mass, and new appendages visibly thrust out from beneath her skin, stretching into the deeper darkness.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Pylgia, your body...
[Sound effect: sharp alarm]
Before you can finish speaking, a sharp noise pierces the air. You turn around and find the submarine has passed by a pre-installed alarm.
Monster... hiss... detected... alert... triggered... hiss... your position... watch out...
The once encouraging radio transmission now sounds painfully jarring. The "monster" they speak of is none but Pylgia herself, mutated beyond recognition.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That's not a monster—it's Pylgia!
You shout into the radio, but it proves all futile. Your signal can't possibly reach the people on the surface.
Watch for... hiss... mines... kill... we're coming... save... hiss... hang... there...
Anxiously, you rush to the porthole, only to find Pylgia's condition has grown even worse.
More appendages tear through her skin, revealing not blood but pale, rotting flesh beneath. Countless appendages writhe frantically toward the Abyss, yet their roots remain anchored in Pylgia's body.
With each inch of ascent, the appendages create more resistance. They're now stretched taut like steel cables, threatening to tear Pylgia's body apart.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Looks like... this is as far... as I can take you...
You know this scene all too well—the Abyss has found Pylgia's fears and bound her here, just as it once did to you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Don't be afraid. They just don't know it's you... I'll explain to them right now!
You try again and again to reach your companions' frequency on the surface, but the radio emits nothing but static.

speaker: Pylgia
content: I... can't go back anymore.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The expedition will accept you. They will!

speaker: Pylgia
content: I know... I... trust them...

speaker: Pylgia
content: But that... would be painful... and take too much unnecessary effort...

speaker: Pylgia
content: They would set aside... missions more valuable than life itself... to care for me... to "cure" me.

speaker: Pylgia
content: That's not... what I want.
Pylgia's body has been stretched to its absolute limit, unable to rise even an inch further.
She keeps her promise, escorting you until the very end. However, eventually, she ceases her struggle, descending into the Abyss like a kite bereft of its only thread.
[Big CG 1 Section 2]

speaker: Pylgia
content: Go. Bring Ragnar and the collectors back to them.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Go back... to them.
Before you can utter a word, Pylgia expends her final vestige of strength to give the sub a tender push.
(CG2)

Watching as Pylgia drifts further and further away, you desperately wrestle with the helm in futile attempts to reach her. But the battle-worn submarine has long since stopped responding to your commands.
As the entrance to the Abyss slowly seals off, she fades into the darkness along with the countless appendages writhing around her.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Pylgia!
You cannot accept this. But as the Abyss closes, the entire sea trembles. The depths where Pylgia is now sealed have become forever beyond reach.
The turbulence carries nameless emotions that wash over your consciousness. Foreign memories surface endlessly, feeling as real as your own experiences.
In this torrent of lost memories, you gradually drift away from yourself.

speaker: Mother
content: Did you sneak off to the beach again?

speaker: Mother
content: How many times do I have to tell you? The sea isn't safe right now. Why can't you just listen?

speaker: Mother
content: What's so good about the water anyway? Why don't you go make friends with children your age instead? Don't make things harder for me...

speaker: Father
content: ...Your mother's right. I know you're always finding excuses to go to the beach, but, well...

speaker: Father
content: At least try not to make people think you're a freak...

speaker: Colleague A
content: Once this mission's over, I'm gonna quit.

speaker: Colleague B
content: You're leaving too?
The young diver overhears her companions' conversation when she walks past a corner of the cabin.

speaker: Colleague B
content: ...Yeah, I understand. This job is tough as nails. The disasters escalate every darn year. I'm not even sure how much longer I can keep going myself.

speaker: Colleague B
content: But come to think of it, what's the plan afterward? I mean, yeah, this gig is risky, but it pays well. Don't you have two kids counting on you?

speaker: Colleague A
content: Dunno... I'll just wing it... Wish I had Pylgia's talents.
Unaware that the very person they're discussing is nearby, they continue their conversation with bitter smiles.

speaker: Colleague B
content: Yeah, I hear ya. Just a few years in the job, and she's already outshining us old-timers at such a young age... Quiet as a mouse on land, but underwater, she's quicker and sharper than the lot of us. Sometimes I swear she... she's...

speaker: Colleague A
content: Not quite like a human, right?

speaker: Colleague B
content: Hey, you're the one who said it. Don't pin this on me if anyone hears.
Their voices fade into the distance, but the young diver remains rooted to the spot, lingering there for a long time.

speaker: Expedition Member
content: How's the mission going? Do you need more hands?
An expedition member stops the young diver with genuine concern on her face. But she just stands there, seemingly struggling to find the proper response.

speaker: Expedition Member
content: The contamination in these waters is getting out of hand, and there are monsters poppin' up all over the place lately. We're all just worried about you, you know.

speaker: Pylgia
content: I know.

speaker: Expedition Member
content: Alright, you're a stubborn one, aren't you? I get it, you're a pro underwater and all, but you should know that... it's usually the best swimmers who end up drowning...

speaker: Expedition Member
content: You skipped your routine checkup with Dr. Banyan, right? You're well aware of what's happening with the rest of the crew on this expedition.

speaker: Expedition Member
content: These missions keep you away for weeks at a time. I'm afraid one day I'll see you again and... not even recognize who you are anymore...
The senior colleague trails off awkwardly, catching herself.

speaker: Expedition Member
content: ...Never mind. I'm the one being totally blunt, rambling on about all these dreary stuff.

speaker: Expedition Member
content: Remember, if you need any help, tell us right away.

speaker: Pylgia
content: ...I know.
After an indeterminate passage of time, the currents finally subside. Light once again filters through the porthole as you breach the surface.
With leaden limbs, you struggle to pry open the hatch and climb atop the submarine, scanning your surroundings.
There is no trace of the expected rescue, no expedition team—just the Illusory Moon shrouded in misty shadows, and that small boat drifting silently below.
Everything remains exactly as it was when you first arrived.
Only Pylgia will never again emerge from beneath the water in her black diving suit... Your connection to her is now too distant to sense.
You stare numbly into the water below. The Abyss has sealed itself shut, and you have returned to the true DisSea. The Illusory Moon tide must be nearing its end.
Perhaps this was how she fell to the Abyss in the original history. Where she left behind this battle-scarred submarine, along with the companions and collectors she gave her life to protect.
The story has simply come full circle.

You have gathered crucial intelligence, witnessed the depths of the DisSea, and verified the feasibility of Project Nightmare. The mission is completed beyond expectations, and you will soon make your safe return.
Despite Pylgia falling into the Abyss and being taken by that thing again... wasn't this all anticipated in the calculated result?
Yeah, you've made it, and you've done everything you could. Stop punishing yourself for it.
You knew from the start you couldn't bring her back. Even Pylgia herself said it wasn't your fault. There's no need to be so sulky.
A strange voice comes from behind. You refuse to turn around, eyes locked on the water below.
Your face is reflected on the water's surface.

speaker: Reflection in the Water
content: No one's. The life or death of those who existed a hundred years ago was never yours to decide.

speaker: Reflection in the Water
content: She ventured into the DisSea, faced the unknown, and sought a new path for life amid the Mania. Doing so, she chose her own destiny, and your role is simply an observer through it all.

speaker: Reflection in the Water
content: All you need to do is watch and then leave, carrying the buried truth into the future, and singing the praises of her name and greatness. This is where your true mission lies—preserving her legacy.
Is that really how it is?

options: No... I'm going back to save her.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That thing has been coveting Pylgia. It killed her companions and trapped her at the bottom of the sea.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I've seen far too much of things like that, and I know too well of its wicked intentions. It plans to trick her, corrupt her, torture her... It will destroy Pylgia, then mock the insignificance of her very existence.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm not accepting it... I can't let her suffer like this!

speaker: Reflection in the Water
content: Not accepting it? Why? What gives you the right?

speaker: Reflection in the Water
content: You know she chose to stay. It's her own accord.
The words hit you like a powerful blow, leaving your mind reeling.

speaker: Pylgia
content: No need to come looking for me. I'll go back once my work's done here.

speaker: Pylgia
content: ...I'll go check outside.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Don't need... to fire...

speaker: Pylgia
content: You are... scared... Did I frighten you?

speaker: Pylgia
content: Because I am... a monster...

speaker: Child's Reflection
content: She was always quiet, struggling to fit in with crowds, avoiding others' gazes. Even when her uniqueness was labeled as abnormal, she couldn't defend herself—she didn't even know how to speak out.

speaker: Child's Reflection
content: Afraid of rejection, concerned about burdening others, she had no choice but to hide her abilities. Yet each time she denied to accept herself, it was only a reminder to herself: See? You really are a monster.

speaker: Child's Reflection
content: Wasn't she so pitiful?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Shut up.

speaker: Child's Reflection
content: She's content to stay, even though it means becoming a monster. There in the Abyss, she no longer has to worry about others' judgment or feel lost. Pylgia has made peace with the "monster" she sees in herself. The Abyss accepts her, giving her freedom.

speaker: Child's Reflection
content: And this "rescue" of yours—where would you take her? What would you turn her into? Would you force her back to "normal"?
No... that's not how it is.
This is not what you want.
...Then what do you WANT?
Your sight is tinged red, your ears echoing with a deafening buzz. The underwater illusion grows murky as you resist its tempting whispers, and another voice begins to take hold of your mind.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm going. I must go...

speaker: Child's Reflection
content: Heh... Heheh... Yeah, you're just so stubborn, arrogant, and full of yourself...

speaker: Child's Reflection
content: But you're nothing here. The Abyss belongs to <size=42><color=#fb9259>It</color></size>. Without Pylgia, you can't dive any deeper, and the entrance to the Abyss is completely sealed. There's no way forward—where do you think you can go to save her?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...I know where to find It.

A blue light flickers by—a warning—but you choose to ignore it. Something shatters at the brink of your consciousness, and your perceptions grow increasingly sharp, as if breaking free from an eggshell to breathe for the first time.
You turn around to look at Ragnar. Though still unconscious, his body looks different somehow under the red glow.
A black viscous liquid seeps from his body, flowing and coalescing into slick tentacles that drag his body towards the shadows.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I know the way...
You walk up, kneel before him, and raise your hands. With his neck in your grip, you exert all your strength, trying to force your way into his body.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The Abyss links to Mania, and Mania is the mind itself... That thing once possessed Ragnar by invading through a mental connection. The pathway to the Abyss is right here!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Take me to her!

Ragnar's eyes snap open—where white should be, there is only sticky blackness. "Ragnar" lets out a piercing shriek, his body thrashing wildly as tentacles whip about, splashing black fluid everywhere.

speaker: Ragnar
content: <color=#fb9259>□□□□□don't touch□□□□□□□□□□don't touch!!</color>
Black tentacles pierce through you. Without your shackles, you are completely powerless against this type of monster.

speaker: Child's Reflection
content: Heheheh... Pitiful... how pitiful that you don't even have any power. You've been coddled too much, weak and delicate. You can't even push open a door, let alone reach <color=#fb9259>The Thing</color>.

speaker: Child's Reflection
content: You only dared to barge in when cowering under the blue light with all connections cut off. You could never win... You have no power!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Then give me power!
Above the sea, the Illusory Moon's radiance surges, casting blood-red circles upon the churning waters—like pupils, also akin to shackles.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Give me back my power... Give me back my shackles!
The pointed ends of your shackles pierce into "Ragnar's" body, and a crimson rift emerges. He convulses violently as more tentacles surge from the rift, attempting to ensnare you to death.
Yet, beneath the blinding red glow, the shackles' sparse spikes have turned unprecedentedly resilient, pinning numerous tentacles to the ground, rendering them entirely immobilized.
Under your control, the shackles tear open the crimson rift, revealing the entrance to the Abyss behind it. Without hesitation, you plunge in.
Only blood-red moonlight remains behind, along with dust dancing in its glow, as if the rift has never existed at all.

speaker: Little Guide
content: Heheh... heheheh... Good, so this is your power, your true heart.

speaker: Little Guide
content: Use it to find the one you cherish, and your enemy—the vengeful spirit of the Abyss... Go forth to intimidate it, expel it, and force it back to where it belongs.

speaker: Little Guide
content: Let it die in peace, and never touch what belongs to us again.
In the freezing seawater, you use the shackles' power to steady yourself, descending alone into the depths in search of that familiar white figure.

This time, you are no longer the captive of the Abyss. You are an intruder, your mere presence stirring terrifying echoes in the eerily silent Abyss. Moans, whispers, howls, and growls—these noises resemble the prelude to death for the living, yet also akin to the eruption of long-decayed corpses.
You are a rolling mass of thorns, ceaselessly shredding any who dare to attack.
Your very arrival heralds destruction, marking a confrontation between two different powers that throws these waters into absolute chaos.
As you dive deeper, the being beneath the Abyss finally takes notice of you.
The mountain-like corpse trembles as lifeless nerves and spines manipulate rotten flesh, its malevolence taking form. In an instant, a dark colossus obstructs your entire view, impeding your passage.
This is the response It offers to you, a tiny intruder.
Dazzling moonlight illuminates the darkness immemorial. Besides its gigantic body, the blue warning light you have been deliberately ignoring is shinning resiliently.
The spikes of your shackles surge forth in full force, crimson thorns cutting through the water as they thrust towards the colossus.
But the gap of power between you is still far too vast.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Ugh...
The moment you touch the dark colossus, it feels like being slammed against a reef by a dense, viscous tide. One single round of confrontation is enough to nearly shatter your consciousness.
In a daze, you hear voices that should not exist.

speaker: Dale
content: Get away... Get away! Monster... Why me... I never wanted to die!
Countless agonized, wailing faces emerge on its body. Among them, you recognize some familiar faces.

speaker: Ragnar
content: No escape... Once you've come here... there's no leaving... It will find you... everyone will meet their end here...
A myriad of human despairs have been woven into this monster's form, as the being beneath the Abyss employs their faces to spread its horrifying malevolence to the world, and to you.
You cannot tolerate this desecration of your companions. Your rage briefly rallies your consciousness as you pour every last ounce of strength into raising the spikes of your shackles once more.
All faces flow as one, their features melting into black ooze, releasing a deafening shriek.
The shriek shatters every attack from your shackles as endless chaos floods into your empty vessel. At the next moment, darkness tears you into fragments.

You have lost. This is the Abyss's territory. The moment you regained a fraction of power, you walked right into its trap, your ignorant defiance earning nothing but its nonchalant glance. What's truly pathetic is that you couldn't even endure its mildest counterattack.

In the deep sea, darkness coalesces into contorted human silhouettes, encircling and gradually closing in on the lone, lingering crimson light. The foremost figure, carrying the most chaotic malevolence, drags numerous appendages crafted from dense darkness beneath its warped shape.

A mere touch would suffice to utterly obliterate your consciousness. However, for some inexplicable reason, the figure comes to a halt—like a dam teetering on the brink of collapse, restraining the tide of darkness behind it.

speaker: Dark Figure
content: Why... did you... come back...
You are long past the point of resistance. At this moment, any action is deprived of its meaning. Your only remaining option is to answer the dark figure's question.
Right... why? Why did you come back?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: For... Pylgia...

speaker: Dark Figure
content: Why?
The figure asks again as black tides wash over it repeatedly. You hear something breaking.

speaker: Dark Figure
content: She... doesn't need... salvation...

speaker: Child's Reflection
content: Heh... Heheh... Yeah, you're just so stubborn, arrogant, and full of yourself...
Indeed. "Salvation" is too presumptuous a word—nothing but illusory shackles forged for self-satisfaction.
Pylgia said she neither wanted pity nor wished to be a burden to her companions. So what did you come for?
Follow me. I'll take you back to where you belong.
Trust me one more time.
The crimson light flickers within the dark tide as your consciousness is peeled away, layer by layer. The last thorns protecting you crumble to dust.
In your consciousness, only one pure, blazing emotion remains burning—a feeling far less weighty than salvation, simpler than duty or mission.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I just... want to see her one more time.
Suddenly, specks of white light appear in the dark tide. Their mere presence radiates warmth, constructing a solid dam that shields both you and the dark figure before you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I remember her face... her name... Pylgia... I want to see her.
The white light specks spread through the darkness, gradually unveiling the dark figure before you.

speaker: Dark Figure
content: Is this... really worth it...?
[Big CG 3]
The thick darkness peels away from her body, the coral shatters, and she breaks free from the monstrous shell. At last, that familiar face emerges before your eyes once more.
In truth, she yearned to see you all too. But she had lived as an outcast for too long, missing too many chances along the way.
Until this moment.
At last, she stops hesitating and running away. For the first time in her life, she is resolute in her choice.
She reaches out her hand amid the dazzling white light, and your silhouettes entwine. Together, you look up, gazing past the terrifying being of the Abyss towards the distant surface of the water.
This is her answer.
Through the vast Abyss, the radio once again receives a clear signal.

speaker: Man's Voice
content: Hello... Hey, Pylgia, can you hear me?

speaker: Pylgia
content: Yes.

speaker: Man's Voice
content: Finally! Where are you, Pylgia? Do you need help?

speaker: Pylgia
content: The submarine is returning. We'll reach the surface soon.

speaker: Man's Voice
content: Thank goodness. How's everyone? How's Ragnar and Dale, they alright? And the collectors?

speaker: Pylgia
content: The collectors... are brought back...
After a brief silence, a rustling sound comes through, followed by a woman's voice.

speaker: Female Voice
content: Don't blame yourself. I'm the one who misjudged the situation here.

speaker: Female Voice
content: Whatever happened, Pylgia, I'm just glad you made it back. We owe you.

speaker: Pylgia
content: I couldn't have done it alone.
You can feel the warmth of Pylgia's palm.

speaker: Female Voice
content: You mean... little guide's with you?
As the hatch swings open, an elegant woman comes into view. Much like you, she seems surprised by your presence.
But soon, she regains her composure, a gentle smile spreading across her face.

speaker: Unfamiliar Woman
content: Even in these waters, you've managed to work another miracle. I really wonder where your limits truly lie.

speaker: Unfamiliar Woman
content: The next deep dive operation is coming up soon. Maybe I should reach out to the base and see about "borrowing" you?
Should you ask for her name? As you ponder this, your vision starts to blur. Schorl's blue light seems to warn you that the tide is receding—it's time to bid farewell.
You feel someone tugging at your clothes. You turn around to find Pylgia.
Pylgia appears taken aback by her own action. Once out of the water, she has returned to her usual reserved self.
But now you understand her a little better. As everything fades into the distance and time runs short, with farewell approaching, you gently take her hand.
No longer choked by pain, you can finally utter the words that must be spoken.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I promise.
Pylgia nods. In the intensifying light, her lips part and close. Even though her voice is no longer audible, you still make out the words spoken.

speaker: Pylgia
content: I will... be waiting for you... Goodbye...

content: <color=#fb9259>??-01</color>: One last thing, please pass this message to ${PlayerName}.

speaker: Schorl
content: I see. I've uploaded your report. This information is invaluable.

speaker: Schorl
content: Also, I've been asked to share some good news with you.

speaker: Schorl
content: The Mania Flux in the DisSea gradually settled after the Illusory Moon tide completely receded. But this time, unlike in the past, the singularity didn't vanish along with the tide.

speaker: Schorl
content: Deep in BR-000, at the heart of the DisSea, the Mania entity that formed a connection with you remains active to this day. To put it in less technical terms...

speaker: Schorl
content: You didn't lose anyone this time, Chief. Your companion is still waiting for you in the past.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Is that so...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That's wonderful, truly is...
None of it was futile. You no longer need to dread moving forward. The path ahead is no longer only about powerless loss.
Your expedition has already begun, and the path will guide you to them. This time, it will be more than just despairing farewells.
You have found the way, and you have rekindled your resolve—also your power! Everything can change now! You want to change!
And after this...

speaker: Little Guide
content: Hehe... Hehehe...

speaker: Schorl
content: What's the matter?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...No, it's nothing.
In that instant, something flashes before your eyes.
And then, even this memory sinks into the depths of the hazy dream.

10:30, February ■■, N.F. 115
DisSea Monitoring Station, FAC
A massive machine hums in the center of the room.
Around it, dozens of MBCC medics and FAC researchers are busying at their stations.
They're supporting the person slumbering within the machine—the MBCC Chief, now taking a deep dive in another Illusory Moon tide.
The efficient team works together seamlessly, clearly well-trained for their job. Yet despite their professionalism, their faces are still tinged with apprehension and concern.

speaker: MBCC Medic
content: Can this... really help the Chief?

speaker: FAC Researcher
content: In what regard?

speaker: FAC Researcher
content: If you're talking about resolving the anomalies or finding crucial clues for your Chief, then the answer is no.

speaker: FAC Researcher
content: But it can monitor vitals, hormone levels, M-Value fluctuations, a dozen parameters. If anything spikes beyond the threshold, the embedded Hypercube inhibitors will kick in and pull your Chief out of the illusion.

speaker: FAC Researcher
content: This project took three research teams one full year. The budget was astronomical. I won't claim it's foolproof, but at the very least, we've done everything in our power to minimize the risks.

speaker: MBCC Medic
content: Thanks for all that hard work.

speaker: FAC Researcher
content: At least we don't have to risk our lives in the DisSea... But honestly, as dangerous as it is, I still envy your Chief.

speaker: FAC Researcher
content: The Expedition Team... they're the greatest heroes in human history. I read so much about them as a kid. Their stories inspired me to become a scientist.

speaker: FAC Researcher
content: If possible, I'd really love to meet them in person...
[Scene Transition] CG

speaker: Black-Haired Woman
content: Alright, open your mouth.
The woman before you leans in with a gentle smile.

speaker: Black-Haired Woman
content: Don't worry. Everything's fine now.
Her voice is kind and gentle. You open your mouth without thinking.
After checking your mouth, she gently brushes a hand across your cheek and parts your eyelids.

speaker: Black-Haired Woman
content: No bleeding in the mucosa... Alright, let's check your torso next. Don't worry, it won't hurt.
The woman takes out a stethoscope and puts it on, tucking a few stray strands of hair behind her ears.
She unbuttons your jacket and warms the chest piece in her palm before pressing it against your chest.

The process feels slow and tedious. You don't dare move, and the people around you seem to be holding their breath. Only when she withdraws the metal probe and removes the stethoscope do you finally voice your question.

speaker: Black-Haired Woman
content: Hmm? No, I'm not.

speaker: Black-Haired Woman
content: Compared to Banyan, I'm not even fit to be her intern.

speaker: Black-Haired Woman
content: But when you spend enough time at sea, you tend to pick up a few useful skills.
The woman puts her medical tools away, but her gaze never leaves you for a second, and she still wears that gentle smile.

speaker: Black-Haired Woman
content: Back to you, little guide. Your body is healthy. At least from what I can tell with the tools on board.

speaker: Black-Haired Woman
content: ...After going through something so horrific, you're still standing here, unharmed. It's nothing short of a miracle.
Upon hearing that, the hushed crowd around you erupts into a small cheer.

speaker: Captain Edmond
content: And it's not just one miracle, Shin. Pylgia made it back in one piece too.
You follow the crewman's finger and see a familiar figure. Her hair is still damp, but the tattered diving suit and grotesque limb growths from your memory are gone.
Meeting your gaze, Pylgia smiles and waves. After all you've been through together, just one look is enough. You have no doubt this is the Pylgia you know.

speaker: Shin
content: Don't worry, Pylgia's in good shape. Ragnar has been treated too. He hasn't regained consciousness yet, but his vitals have stabilized.

speaker: Vikmar
content: Too bad Dale didn't make it back...

speaker: Captain Edmond
content: No one will forget their sacrifice, but we have more important things to do.

speaker: Laura
content: All collectors have been recovered and the data analyzed. Time's running out... We should start the salvage operation immediately before this tidal cycle ends.
They're talking over each other, but based on their words and Pylgia's presence, you're fairly certain that this is a time node adjacent to the previous singularity.
It's clear that they're planning a dive for some kind of salvage operation, and your heart sinks at the realization.

speaker: Shin
content: We're close to the target coordinates...
The woman called Shin finishes packing her tools and stands up. The noisy crowd falls silent the moment she speaks, waiting for her orders.

speaker: Shin
content: We stick to the plan. Vikmar and I will deploy the salvage equipment. Sigmund and Laura will stay at the Abyss entrance to assist us.

speaker: Captain Edmond
content: Wait, this is a risky mission... Pylgia, you know these waters better than anyone. If you go with Shin, we'll feel more at ease...
All eyes turn to Pylgia. She frowns slightly and opens her mouth to speak, but the woman dressed as a researcher doesn't notice her hesitation and jumps in.

speaker: Laura
content: With your and Shin's experience, I'm sure you can handle whatever comes up. I know it's a lot to ask, sending you back down after you just barely escaped with your life, but...

speaker: Pylgia
content: It's fine, I can go. But...
Everyone looks at you in surprise. Clearly they weren't expecting an objection. Perhaps this isn't the kind of thing their guide would do.
The middle-aged researcher looks annoyed that her important discussion was interrupted.

speaker: Laura
content: The Perishing Star salvage mission is critical. You can say our entire Deep Dive unit was created for this sole purpose. Now that the target is right here, there's no reason to turn back...

speaker: Shin
content: Laura...
Shin raises a hand, stopping the researcher. She then turns to you and asks in that same, gentle tone, without any sign of impatience.

speaker: Shin
content: Can you tell us why? Why shouldn't we go down?
You can tell that she's treating you like a child.
Noting the crew's mixed expressions, you take a deep breath.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It's extremely dangerous under the sea. There's a terrifying entity in the Abyss, something beyond our comprehension. It can twist the entire environment and inflict irreversible mental contamination on anything that enters its domain.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I don't know how to fight it... I don't think humanity has the technology or means to deal with something like that. We only made it back alive because...
You glance toward Pylgia in her human form and swallow the words on the tip of your tongue.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Because we were lucky. But I don't think we'll be that lucky again.
The crew falls silent, including Shin. After a long moment, the researcher named Laura speaks up begrudgingly.

speaker: Laura
content: ...Pylgia, is it true?
Pylgia doesn't speak, just nods silently.
The crew stirs.
Shin's eyes are downcast. She seems to be pondering the current situation. The crew's gazes rest on her, their hopeful inquiry carrying the inescapable weight of responsibility.
But that burden doesn't make her hesitate for long. She looks up, pale blue eyes shining, and gives her answer with her usual gentle smile.

speaker: Shin
content: I believe in our guide.

speaker: Shin
content: The research matters. But the fact is, Dale and the others are gone. If the Abyss is as dangerous as what we just heard, the risk of going there is beyond our control. Even if we could bring something back... I... I cannot accept results paid for in lives.

speaker: Shin
content: Our little guide and Pylgia are our companions. When it comes to the dangers in the Abyss, they have more say than any of us. I think we can all agree on that, right?
Shin glances around the room. The crew's silence serves as their answer.

speaker: Shin
content: We've already retrieved the collectors. That's more than enough for now. So...

speaker: Shin
content: It's time we go home.
The crew exchange looks. This isn't what they had hoped for.
In the end, it's the captain-like man who breaks the silence.

speaker: Captain Edmond
content: What are you standing around for?

speaker: Captain Edmond
content: Back to your posts! Turn the ship around. We're...

speaker: Captain Edmond
content: Going home!
At the captain's command, the crew quickly breaks up and leaves. Only you and Shin remain.

speaker: %u
content: Don't you have work to do?

speaker: Shin
content: Thanks to your reminder, there's no dive to prepare for. So no, I don't have anything urgent on hand.

speaker: Shin
content: You don't like my company?

speaker: %u
content: I just... I'm fine. And I'm not a child. I don't need a babysitter...

speaker: Shin
content: Hmm, I know. You're a tough adult... I'm glad you're okay.

speaker: Shin
content: You should get some sleep. If all goes well, we'll be back at camp by the time you wake up.

speaker: %u
content: No, I don't need to rest...
The illusion won't let you leave that easily. Sitting around is not a wise choice.
You throw off the blanket and try to sit up. Shin notices your movement and places a protective hand over the bed to prevent you from bumping your head.

speaker: Option
options: I'd like to look around. Is it okay?

speaker: Shin
content: Alright. It's a good idea to meet everyone.

speaker: Shin
content: Come with me.
On the deck, you immediately spot Pylgia tinkering with some diving equipment.

speaker: %u
content: Pylgia!
You wave at Pylgia. She looks up, notices you, and waves back.

speaker: %u
content: How are you feeling? Is everything alright?

speaker: Pylgia
content: I'm fine.
The conversation feels familiar, except this time you're the one asking.

speaker: Shin
content: Don't worry, Pylgia's in even better shape than you are. Her suit was shredded, but she came back without a single scratch.

speaker: Shin
content: She gave me a big fright! I checked her over many times before I was convinced enough to let her go...

speaker: Pylgia
content: ...It's all thanks to our guide. Without him, I wouldn't have made it back.
female_content: ...It's all thanks to our guide. Without her, I wouldn't have made it back.

speaker: Pylgia
content: I feel well. Not like in the Abyss. And I don't... want to go back to being like that again.
Pylgia, you still up there? Come give us a hand!
Pylgia gives you an apologetic look. There are too many secrets between you, too many things unsaid, but now isn't the time.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Wait for me at camp... And thank you for keeping my secret.
You nod at her, and she quickly disappears below deck, her steps much lighter than before.
The ship's passageways branch out in all directions, and Pylgia is nowhere to be seen. The captain is huddled with a tall, lanky young man, going over ship operations.

speaker: Captain Edmond
content: How's the hull holding up? And weapons?

speaker: Sigmund
content: Weapons are fine. But there's this weird noise from the engine room. I suspect a leaky pipe. I'll take a look in a bit... Hello Shin, what brings you here?

speaker: Shin
content: Showing our guide around.

speaker: Sigmund
content: Hello there! I'm Sigmund, first mate. This is Captain Edmond.

speaker: %u
content: Hello... I hope I'm not interrupting anything?

speaker: Sigmund
content: Not at all! Just some routine checks. We're almost done.

speaker: Captain Edmond
content: Haha, what's this? Getting nervous in front of your mentor?

speaker: %u
content: ...Mentor?

speaker: Captain Edmond
content: Yep. He was one of Shin's grad students. Signed up the moment he heard about the expedition. Dragged his mom along too. That's Laura, our researcher.

speaker: Shin
content: We'll let you get back to it.

speaker: Captain Edmond
content: See you around, kiddo!
In the wheelhouse, you see a lean young man hunched over the controls, absorbed in his work. He doesn't seem to have noticed your arrival.

speaker: Shin
content: This is Vikmar, our helmsman and navigator...

speaker: Vikmar
content: Ah! Oh... i-it's you, Shin...

speaker: Shin
content: Don't be fooled by his face. He's top of his class at the maritime academy and a veteran with ten years of experience piloting large cargo ships.

speaker: Shin
content: We haven't had a single accident since he took the helm. Pretty impressive, right?

speaker: Vikmar
content: I-it's the auto-navigation and steering systems doing all the work. I-I didn't do much...

speaker: Shin
content: But you're the one who keeps those systems running.

speaker: Vikmar
content: W-well, I suppose so... but th-there's still a lot I could do better...
The shy young man's ears turn red. He nervously wrings his hands, unsure what to do with them.

speaker: Shin
content: Don't stress yourself out. You're doing a great job. I know you'll get us home safe.

speaker: Vikmar
content: R-right... I'll do my best...

speaker: Laura
content: We're good on medical supplies, and we have enough fresh water and food to last for a while... Sigh...

speaker: Reid
content: I know it's hard to give up after all that preparation. But honestly? When Shin decided to turn back, I felt relieved... I had a bad feeling about this trip from the start.

speaker: Laura
content: But we were so close...

speaker: Laura
content: Oh, there you are, Shin.

speaker: Reid
content: Hehe, first time I've seen Shin with a kid. You two look like mother and son!
female_content: Hehe, first time I've seen Shin with a kid. You two look like mother and daughter!

speaker: Shin
content: This is Professor Laura, my senior colleague from university. Thanks to her, we've made a lot of headway in marine research in the forbidden zone...

speaker: Shin
content: And this is Reid. He's in charge of guarding the lower decks.

speaker: Reid
content: Yeah, it's pretty spooky down here. Any second now, monsters are gonna jump out of the shadows and... RAWR!

speaker: Shin
content: Alright, Reid, cut it out. Do we have enough supplies for the return journey?

speaker: Reid
content: Don't worry, we're fully stocked. We're finally going home...
You push open the door to find Ragnar curled up on the bed, his back toward you, his body trembling uncontrollably.
You take a few steps forward and hear him muttering under his breath, spitting out meaningless syllables.
As you get closer, you notice traces of dried black ooze still clinging to his skin. Your heart clenches with dread.
Then, the slime begins to move. Tiny tendrils writhe and squirm, like the feelers of some deep-sea creature.
Ragnar's delirious murmurs grate on some unbearably jarring frequency. You feel an inexplicable pain in your skull, but you can't tear your eyes away.

speaker: Shin
content: Are you okay?
Shin's calm voice jolts you from your trance. When you look back at Ragnar, the black slime and maddening murmurs are gone.
You shake your head hard, trying to clear that strange feeling from your mind.

speaker: %u
content: I'm fine... Let's go.
You and Shin complete your tour and return to the deck.
Beyond the rails, there's nothing but the gray sky and sea. The ship charges forward at full speed. A briny ocean wind whips at your face, but does nothing to dispel the gloom weighing on your heart.

speaker: Shin
content: Still thinking about Ragnar?

speaker: Option
content: No...
Rather than worrying about Ragnar, you're more affected by the stress of the illusion itself. You've been through this several times now. Even with no immediate danger, your nerves remain on edge.
Shin quietly studies you for a moment, then suddenly speaks.

speaker: Daoxuan
content: Oh right, I introduced you to everyone on the ship, but I never got to introduce myself.

speaker: Shin
content: I'm Shin, the oceanographer of the expedition, and the acting ship doctor for now. If we're short on hands, I can also handle the helm and navigation.
She leans in, her pale blue eyes twinkling. For her mature, refined bearing, the affectionate way she speaks to a child doesn't feel out of place at all.

Your brief time together has given you an initial impression of Shin. She has an effortless warmth, and as Reid said, she is like a mother, a natural leader who can understand and support her companions.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Oceanographer? You study things in the sea?
You try your best impression of a curious child.

speaker: Shin
content: Well, pretty close. I study marine life that began mutating after the Perishing Star fell.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Mutated marine life... you mean, those "monsters"?
Thinking of Pylgia's condition, you continue to probe, hoping to get a sense of her attitude.

speaker: Shin
content: I don't think "monsters" is an accurate term.

speaker: Shin
content: They don't fit into any biological taxonomy from before the Nightfall. Labeling them as hostile "monsters" before we fully understand them... that might destroy our chance of resolving the crisis.

speaker: Shin
content: Before joining the expedition, my work focused on studying these new life forms. My initial findings suggest that they share an extremely close connection with us humans.

speaker: Shin
content: That theory isn't exactly popular in academia... which is why I decided to join the expedition. There's no better place on this planet for my research than the waters of the forbidden zone.
Shin gazes out over the endless sea, and you see a tinge of forlorn longing in her eyes.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm sorry... for cutting off your research like this...

speaker: Shin
content: No, you don't need to apologize. You saved Pylgia. You're probably saving the rest of us too.

speaker: Shin
content: As long as we're alive, our research can continue at any time. Patience and caution are the two things we can't afford to forget right now... And in that regard, you did great.

speaker: Shin
content: Once we get back and analyze the data from the collectors, perhaps we can start another...

speaker: Radio
content: Shin... ■■■... something's wrong... the wheelhouse... ■■... ■■■...
A sudden crackle from the radio cuts your conversation short. The message is garbled, broken by harsh static, but you can still make out the sound of ragged, desperate gasps.

speaker: Shin
content: Vikmar?

speaker: Radio
content: Navigation... ■■■...

speaker: Shin
content: The signal's jammed. I can't hear you. Stay calm, I'm on my way.
His voice is drowned out by the static. Shin clips the radio back to her waist without switching it off and wrenches open the door to the cabins.

speaker: Shin
content: We'll have to continue our chat later. Now back to the wheelhouse.
You nod and hurry after her.
The emergency lights flicker and buzz overhead. You race through the corridor, footsteps hammering a frantic rhythm against the metal floor.
But soon, you feel your steps grow sluggish.
What starts as a faint tug quickly becomes a struggle, as if you're trudging through a heavy marsh. Every step requires tremendous effort.
The thick, damp air is mixed with a faint, foul odor that invades your lungs with every quickening breath.

speaker: Shin
content: Ugh, that smell...
Drip.

Something wet and sticky drips from the ceiling onto your head, mingling with the sweat on your forehead as it trickles down to your brow. The stench hits you full force: the reek of rotting fish, concentrated several times over.
Someone steadies you just in time and wipes the filth from your forehead with a sleeve. You look up into Shin's concerned eyes.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It's left by a crawling deep-sea creature. Something's already gotten inside the ship.

speaker: Shin
content: Sure. The comms signal... it's gone.
You both know what that means, but neither of you says a word. You simply quicken your steps in tacit understanding. Squelching footsteps echo eerily in the corridor, leaving a trail of pale ooze.
[Scene Transition: Still in corridor]
The door of the wheelhouse is spattered with sticky globs of gunk. Caught in the slime are the shredded bits of a uniform, smeared with dark, wet blood.
Thud, thud-thud, thud. An irregular pounding comes from behind the half-open door.
Shin catches your eye and raises a finger to her lips. Stay quiet. Shielding you with her body, she grasps the handle and slowly pushes the door open.
[Black Screen Horizontal Wipe]

speaker: Captain Edmond
content: Mmph—help... help!
[Show Wheelhouse]

Captain Edmond is half-collapsed beside the console, his upper body strangled by a gelatinous creature. Thick slime smothers his mouth and nose as he desperately swings a wrench, trying to knock away the writhing mass gripping his face.
On the other side, Vikmar is slumped over, his helmet cracked. A shattered comms device lies in pieces near his hand.
Shin immediately understands. She moves to Vikmar's side to ensure he's safe from further harm.
You rush to the captain, grab the wrench from his hand, and bring it down hard on the mass crushing his chest.

The mass convulses, and a thick, tar-like substance spurts from the gash. Seizing the moment it loosens its grip, you grit your teeth and yank the thing off the captain's face, flinging it against the wall.
Shin immediately understands. She moves to the captain's side as you approach Vikmar.
She grabs the wrench from his hand and brings it down on the mass crushing his chest.
The mass convulses, and a thick, tar-like substance spurts from the gash. Seizing the moment it loosens its grip, she yanks the thing off the captain's face and flings it against the wall.
It splats into an indescribable pulp and slides down the wall, before lying still in a puddle of its own ooze.
The captain, breathing freely again, scrambles back to the helm. Vikmar has also come around.

speaker: Vikmar
content: Thank goodness you're here, Shin...
He starts to thank her, but the relieved sigh on his lips suddenly morphs into a gasp of horror.

speaker: Vikmar
content: I-it.. it's...!
The puddle of flesh on the ground is twitching. Tiny lumps bulge from its surface, pulsing like a heart. In the center of the mass, a new maw is taking shape.

speaker: Captain Edmond
content: You've got to be kidding me!

With a roar, Captain Edmond lunges at the unholy creature, trying to pin it down with his weight. But the monster, revived with greater strength, hurls him across the room into the console. Then, slick with its own ooze, it charges straight at you.

speaker: Shin
content: —Watch out!
Shin throws herself in front of you without a second thought, raising her arm as the monster opens its gaping maw.
That brief moment is enough. The creature visibly falters; the next second, Captain Edmond is on it, bringing the wrench down on its head.
Splat.
The second blow smashes it to pieces. It twitches twice, then melts away into a puddle of black ichor.

speaker: Captain Edmond
content: Phew... Are you alright?!

speaker: Shin
content: I'm fine. How about you? Are you okay?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm fine. Thank you, Shin. I...
As you stare at the puddle on the ground, a dull ringing fills your ears.
[Contamination Effect]
Waiting... waiting for you...
[Red Flash]

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What was that...
Captain Edmond has returned to the console, his expression grave. Vikmar crouches nearby, carefully wiping the slime from the panels to prevent it from fouling the main systems again.

speaker: Vikmar
content: T-they're really trying to stop us from leaving, aren't they...?

speaker: Captain Edmond
content: Don’t overthink. There's no proof that they're that smart. One just happened to slip in and cause some trouble. We'll fix the equipment. Things will be alright.
Shin calmly walks over to the console and examines the flickering navigation readings. Her dress is soiled by the ooze, but she offers her handkerchief to the captain first.

speaker: Shin
content: You should wipe your face, Captain. The comms are jammed, so you'll have to brief the crew in person. They'll be unsettled to see you like this.

speaker: Captain Edmond
content: ...The news itself is enough to cause panic.

speaker: Shin
content: Which is why we need you, Captain. Immediately notify the crew: every hatch, entrance, and exit must be guarded by at least one armed crew member at max alert. Tell Pylgia to reduce her dive radius and be ready to return to shore at any time.

speaker: Captain Edmond
content: Right. Leave it to me.
The captain cleans his face, straightens his clothes, and strides out of the room.
You look at Vikmar. Terror is still written all over his face. At the sound of Shin's voice, the big man shudders.

speaker: Shin
content: Don't worry, we'll make it back safely.

speaker: Shin
content: The anemometer shows the wind speed dropping in the southwest, and the barometer readings are low. This combination usually means a local cyclone or some other disturbance ahead.
She lightly taps several flashing indicators on the screen, then glances at the humidity readings.

speaker: Shin
content: Humidity's still rising; sea foam's dense on the surface. There's a strong upwelling, probably from a sudden change in terrain... or large creature activity. Either way, we avoid areas with abnormal wind speeds or intense surface glare, and follow the sea lanes with stable pressure and sparse foam. Not so hard, right?
Vikmar stares intently at the numbers, his fear slowly giving way to focus.

speaker: Shin
content: The captain is out there to give hope and confidence. I am here to read the signs of the sea. As for steering the ship... can I entrust that to you?
Vikmar stares at Shin's hands. These hands, used to flipping through research papers, had just fought a vicious battle. Now, with these reassuring hands, she's entrusting him with the helm.
He thinks for a moment, then nods firmly.

speaker: Vikmar
content: I... I can't promise I won't make any mistakes, but I'll give it my all.

speaker: Shin
content: Don't worry. As long as we're at sea, there are innumerable ways to reach our destination. Instruments are just aids. What matters most is experience, and...
Shin walks over to you and gently pats you on the back.

speaker: Shin
content: Sharp eyes.
There's no room for two in the crow's nest. Shin stays below, watching as you climb up alone.

The radar has fallen deathly silent, its antenna pointing stiffly into the ashen sky. You think of the console inside, indicators blinking wildly, needles jittering. All navigation, detection, and comms systems are failing, one by one.
Only your eyes are still working.
You gaze out over the endless sea. The horizon is a murky blur, the fog bearing down on the water like a heavy net. You see no stars, no sun, only the grayish black of a low, oppressive sky.
You hold your breath, forcing yourself to pick out some difference, a silver lining, a glimmer of light that could mark the destination for your voyage.
Time seems to stretch on. Sweat trickles down your spine. Your knuckles turn white from clenching too hard, and your shoulders ache from prolonged tension.
Then, you see it, the true form of a distant shadow—a patch of water that undulates gently against the current, surrounded by waves going the different way.
It must be land! You look down in excitement, eager to share the good news with Shin on the deck below, when a strange dizziness suddenly crashes over you.
[Distortion Effect]
Waiting... waiting for you...
Your vision begins to distort. You blink hard, trying to stay sober, but in the corner of your eye, that patch of water slowly splits open.

You see something slowly emerging from the rift. It is one with the sea, its form indescribable, its size unknowable. You can only instinctively feel that it has countless twisted limbs and chaotic, disordered eyes.
The land on the horizon is completely obscured. All you can see is the ancient, colossal being, looming with a nameless malice. Moving, coming for you, eroding your very consciousness...
Darkness engulfs you, dragging you down into the bottomless deep.
You don't know how you survived the ordeal.
When the final impact passes, the unspeakable being finally dissolves.
But you find no relief. Its voice still echoes in your ears.

speaker: Discordant Whisper
content: Do not resist... do not flee...

speaker: Discordant Whisper
content: Sink... return...

speaker: Discordant Whisper
content: Your name was carved in the deep long ago...
You cover your ears and scream. A ringing fills your ears, and then, everything falls silent. You look up in disbelief. In the distant fog, a ship is floating peacefully.
