Its outline is blurred and tattered, yet its shadow seems strangely real, almost familiar. You want to tell Shin, but only then do you realize: you're no longer on the radar platform.
Like the ship, you're floating above a dark land. The ocean breeze brushes past vaguely, carrying the faint scent of brine.
You've been through this before. In an illusion like this, there's only one choice to make.
Having endured endless chaos, you press forward through the darkness. You can see the ship clearly now.
It seems to have been drifting here for an eternity. The hull is worn and stained with rust. A broken masts sways noiselessly, and a signal flag hangs limply from its pole.
You climb over the side and step onto the deck. The rusted steel groans beneath your feet. Your arrival seems to have roused something. Faint sounds can be heard from somewhere deep within a cabin.
Human voices.
Broken whispers, like a group of people huddled together, talking in a hidden corner.
You hold your breath and slowly creep toward the voices. Their words become clearer.

speaker: Whispers in the Cabin
content: <color=#fb9259>Something like that shouldn't exist...</color>

speaker: Whispers in the Cabin
content: <color=#fb9259>We're lost... No one's steering...</color>

speaker: Whispers in the Cabin
content: <color=#fb9259>...He's not coming back... G-got swallowed... by that thing...</color>

speaker: Whispers in the Cabin
content: <color=#fb9259>We have to find it... It's still hiding on the ship...</color>
The voices are a frenzied jumble of suffocating terror and despair. You hear ragged breathing, quiet prayers, and what sounds like muffled sobs.
But the strange thing is...
[Inside the Cabin]
You push the door open. The cabin's in ruins. No one's inside. And yet... the whispers don't stop.
In your ears, above your head, under your feet. Everywhere at once, yet nowhere to be found.

speaker: Whispers in the Cabin
content: <color=#fb9259>Quiet! Don't let it hear us...</color>

speaker: Whispers in the Cabin
content: <color=#fb9259>We can't keep hiding. We have to fight back!</color>

speaker: Whispers in the Cabin
content: <color=#fb9259>Kill it! Or we'll be next!</color>

speaker: Whispers in the Cabin
content: <color=#fb9259>It's... too late... This is its lair!</color>
Cold wind gushes in through the shattered portholes, sweeping through the ship's hollow husk. It carries that familiar salty stench, and with it, one final warning:

speaker: Whispers in the Cabin
content: <color=#fb9259>Run! Get out of here!</color>
Run!
The metal beneath your feet begins to give way. Fog swarms in from all sides, and you can barely see a thing.
You get your bearings as best as you can, then dash out of the cabin and start sprinting in the direction of the shadow from your memory.

speaker: %u
content: <color=#fb9259>Forty degrees west by southwest</color>, I'm sure of it. The shadow I saw... it was land. The place the malice didn't want us to reach.
Shadowy figures keep emerging in the fog ahead, but you don't slow down.
You shut your eyes and plunge headfirst into the fog, forcing yourself to keep running.

speaker: %u
content: Land... the land is ahead...

The air you drag into your lungs grows cold. The chill spreads from the soles of your feet to the base of your skull. A low hum, a drone of whispers, begins to buzz in your ears. You feel something slithering around your arms and ankles, trying to hold you back.
You don't even look. You picture only the foggy sea from your memory, clinging to the image like a lifeline and refusing to let go.
But the mental corruption gets worse.
The fog seeps into you with every breath. Whispers drone on in your ears, drowning you like incessant tides. More and more shadows coil around your body, bogging you down.
You begin to stumble, your movements getting sluggish. The location of the land blurs in your mind.
Just as you're about to lose control completely, a familiar, steady voice cuts through the noise.

speaker: Firm Voice
content: Wake up!
[White out back to reality]
[Shin's portrait, out of focus]

speaker: %u
content: Shin...?

speaker: %u
content: Land... forty degrees... west by southwest...
Summoning your last bit of strength, you look at the person before you and take a step in her direction. Then your knees give out, and you crash heavily to the ground.
The medical bay isn't far away, but she slows her pace, her steps steady, knowing what you're going through.
Shin holds you in her arms, afraid of startling you in your nightmare.

speaker: %u
content: <color=#7683a2><size=36>So many eyes... limbs... I can't see...</size></color>

speaker: %u
content: <color=#7683a2><size=36>It's... talking to me?</size></color>

speaker: %u
content: <color=#7683a2><size=36>...Abyss... wake... stay...</size></color>
Your eyes are screwed shut as you relive the nightmare, instinctively curling into her embrace and clutching at her clothes.
Your body is cold, your clothes drenched in cold sweat, but Shin doesn't flinch. She only holds you tighter.
You feel yourself sinking into a warm, soft embrace in the darkness.
The hands supporting your shoulders pat you gently, calming you down.

speaker: Shin
content: It's okay now. You did well...
She stops outside the medical bay. In the empty corridor, she buries her face against your frail shoulder and takes a deep breath.
You feel something wet land on your cheek. You can't tell if it's rain, water, or a tear.

speaker: Shin
content: Hah... You made it — very well.
[CG Background: Ceiling]
You wake up to the harsh glare of the ceiling lights and the faint smell of disinfectant.
The medical bay is quiet, save for the low hum of equipment and the distant sound of sea wind against the portholes, reminding you that you're back in reality.
A sudden coolness on your forehead brings you back to your senses. Someone is dabbing away your sweat with a towel, their touch slow and gentle.
Not yet used to the cabin's temperature, you turn your head stiffly to look at the person beside you.
[Shin's portrait]

speaker: Shin
content: You're awake? I checked you over. Everything looks fine. You probably fainted due to psychological and mental stress.

speaker: Shin
content: But I'm not a real ship doctor. It would be best to have someone more qualified examine you again once we're back on the land.
Your voice comes out hoarse. You've barely formed a syllable before she's smiling and holding a cup of water to your lips.

speaker: Shin
content: I know. <color=#fb9259>Forty degrees west by southwest</color>.
She carefully supports the back of your neck, helping you drink the warm water. Feeling a little embarrassed, you look away.

speaker: Option
options: I can manage on my own.

speaker: Shin
content: I almost forgot. You did say you're an adult.
She chuckles softly and places the cup in your hand without fuss.

speaker: Shin
content: You were talking in your sleep. Your lips were chapped from the sea wind, but you just kept going. And you weren't just talking about land. What did you see... in your dream?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I saw...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It was huge, and very old... And it was sinking...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Everyone was trying to escape, but it was too late...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It came from the bottom of the sea and quickly vanished...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But where it went, it left behind so many desperate cries for help.
You speak haltingly, your voice trailing off. Memories rush back like a tide, heavy enough to crush your chest.

Shin never interrupts you. She listens quietly until you've finished speaking, before picking up the towel again and gently dabbing the last traces of cold sweat from your brow. Then, she takes your hand and envelopes it in hers.

speaker: Shin
content: You've been through a lot.

speaker: Shin
content: And you gave us the right direction.
Her voice is as warm as her hands, firm with an unswerving conviction.

speaker: Shin
content: The radar just came back online. Based on my earlier analysis of currents, pressure, and refraction... there is unusual terrain forty degrees west by southwest. The currents there are stable, with minimal temperature shifts. It's our best chance for survival.
Hearing her speak with such calm confidence, you quietly let out a sigh of relief and feel your nerves ease just a little.
Shin notices your tension. She leans in close, so her eyes are level with yours, and speaks in a quiet voice.

speaker: Shin
content: You held on until the very last moment. You remembered the direction. You even faced off... the corruption.

speaker: Shin
content: You're very brave.
This isn't the tone one uses to comfort a child. There's no exaggeration, no perfunctory praise. Every word is slow and earnest. She's showing you genuine acknowledgement.
You give her hand a gentle squeeze to let her know you're alright. In the gentle scent of disinfectant and sea breeze, the air feels peaceful and serene. But the next second...
The entire medical bay lurches.

The ceiling jolts, and the light swings violently. Medicine cabinets and equipment racks tumble to the floor with a deafening crash. The tremor comes from the bottom of the hull, as if something enormous just rammed into the vessel.
Shin springs to her feet, scanning the room with vigilant eyes before opening the medical bay door.
A fragmented broadcast crackles over the PA system. You hear Vikmar's terrified cry.

speaker: Vikmar
content: S-something's wrong! In the wheelhouse... there's something in here...!
The broadcast breaks off abruptly, snapped by some invisible force. Only the jarring static echoes through every cabin.
Shin turns to look at you on the cot. You're conscious, but you haven't recovered enough strength to face this sudden crisis alone. She doesn't hesitate long.

speaker: Shin
content: Stay close to me. Can you do that?
[Scene Change]
Half-carrying, half-supporting you, Shin carefully guides you past the toppled shelves and shattered glass and through the lurching corridors.
This is more violent than before. The walls groan in agony with each shudder of the hull, the entire vessel straining against some unseen force that threatens to tear it apart.
Dark red emergency lights flash ahead, casting broken shadows across the cracked metal walls.
You stay close to Shin, relying on her strength to keep moving forward.
[Wheelhouse Entrance]
The captain and several crew members have already gathered outside the wheelhouse.
[Impact/Vibration]

speaker: Captain Edmond
content: Vikmar! Can you open the door? Vikmar!!
The captain slams himself against the door, but it doesn't budge. A dark red fluid seeps through the panel, trickling down the seams and dripping onto the deck with a wet, sickening patter.
The door, corroded by the ooze and warped by force, has turned the wheelhouse into a chamber of despair.

speaker: Whispers in the Cabin
content: Land... there's land ahead...

speaker: Whispers in the Cabin
content: Only I... only I can get us there...

speaker: Vikmar
content: Aaaaaahhh! Don't come near me! Aaaahhh—!!!
Vikmar's terrible screams mix with the incessant pounding, drilling into everyone's ears and fraying their nerves.
Shin and you hurry over to the scene.

speaker: Shin
content: Where's the breaching axe?
The crew seems stunned. Shin asks again, her tone stern.

speaker: Shin
content: Where's the breaching axe?!

speaker: Captain Edmond
content: Around the corner, by the stairs.

speaker: Reid
content: I'll get it!
Reid quickly returns with the axe, but as he stands before the door, his hands begin to shake uncontrollably.
Forcing open the cabin door might release unknown contamination and threats from within.
What will he find inside? Vikmar's half-eaten corpse? Rotting things from DisSea? Or...

speaker: Shin
content: Break it down!

speaker: Shin
content: <size=52><color=#fb9259>Save him!</size></color>
Shin's orders carry an unshakeable resolve. The axe comes down at her command, hitting the cabin door that separates them from the unknown horror.
One swing. Two. With the third strike, the lock shatters. The door teeters open.
The panel crashes to the floor. There's no one inside.
[Emergency Alert Flashing]

speaker: Alarm
content: Warning. Vessel has deviated from course.

speaker: Alarm
content: Warning. Obstacle twenty meters ahead.

speaker: Alarm
content: Final warning. Impact in ten seconds. Ten. Nine. Eight...
The shrill alarm echoes in the empty room. But somehow, the only thing you can hear is the frantic spinning of the ship's helm.
Through the viewport, you see a colossal shadow bearing down on the small research vessel. Is it an iceberg? Or a reef?
No, it can't be... Because it's moving.
[Screen Shakes]

speaker: Laura
content: Watch out! Brace yourselves!
[Intense Shaking]
The next second, everyone is thrown from their feet. Your back slams hard into a wall, and with a crash, a metal shelf collapses on top of you.

speaker: Shin
content: No!
Fighting through the pain and nausea, you force your eyes open with sheer willpower.
The entire ship has nearly capsized, seawater pouring in through the portholes. And now, the only person still standing is Shin.

In the raging storm, she's gripping the helm with all her strength, her feet barely touching the ground as she struggles to anchor herself in place. In this moment, her fate and the ship's fate have become one.
Finally, the ship stops tilting at a most perilous angle and slowly settles back amid the screech of tortured steel.
The cabin falls silent. The only sound is the howling wind and crashing waves outside.
A deathly silence hangs over the crew. You can't tell if it's the shock of surviving the disaster, or...
You look at Shin, who has fallen to her knees from exhaustion. She must have hit something just now, for blood is trickling down from her temple.

speaker: Captain Edmond
content: Where the **** is Vikmar?!

speaker: Reid
content: Vikmar...
The captain slams his fist into the wall. You feel the metal shudder behind your back. All that's left is the sound of his heavy breathing.
No one dares to say another word.
Shin's portrait
Shin slowly rises to her feet and staggers toward the spot where Vikmar had once stood.
Only a puddle of thick black ichor remains, pooled around the tattered pieces of his uniform.

Slowly, she sinks to her knees, drenching the hem of her dress in the black ichor. But she's not done. She reaches her hands into the puddle as well, the tar-like liquid dripping from her pale fingers.
Then, she carefully picks out the scraps of cloth that are still recognizable—the only pieces left of him—and gently cradles them to her chest.
Tumultuous emotions wash over the survivors: anger, fear, confusion... And amidst it all, she realizes that you're the only one watching her.
Shin's expression (can we get a close-up?)
Shin gives you an almost heartbreaking smile, and says softly, like she's comforting a child.

speaker: Shin
content: Maybe he's just missing. We... we can't give up hope yet.
Blood drips from her face, vanishing into the black puddle beneath her.
You should go help her, but something holds you back. You can't bring yourself to disturb this moment; the scene before you seems to forbid any intrusion.

The deck lies in wreck. Half the equipment that once packed every corner is gone, while the rest lies smashed to pieces. Several crew members huddle around Captain Edmond, their voices shaken as they count the survivors.

speaker: Captain Edmond
content: Is this everyone? Where are the others? Weren't you supposed to be wearing tethers?!

speaker: Crew Member
content: It was no use... The wave was too big. Once they went overboard, the line snapped before we could pull them up... We only made it because we were clinging to the mast.
The crewman is soaked to the bone and looks like a mess. Contamination from the sea has spread across his body. He may have survived, but not unscathed.
The captain breathes heavily, fists clenching and unclenching at his side.
He's your captain. And at times like this, everyone needs him more than ever.

speaker: Captain Edmond
content: You survived... that's what matters.

speaker: Captain Edmond
content: I'll check the other sections. There might be more who went overboard.

speaker: Captain Edmond
content: Find a way to reach Pylgia. See if she can find any sign of our people underwater.
You go to the edge of the deck and call out.

speaker: %u
content: Pylgia!
Before long, a familiar figure surfaces from the water.

speaker: %u
content: Thank goodness... you're all right. Did you know about the commotion just now? Any changes underwater?
Pylgia nods, then shakes her head.

speaker: Pylgia
content: There's something in the water.

speaker: Pylgia
content: But... the water's murky... Too many... formless things.

speaker: Pylgia
content: I almost caught up to it, but it disappeared. I only saw a blurry shadow.
It's rare to see Pylgia on edge. She seems to be blaming herself for losing the culprit that attacked the ship.

speaker: %u
content: Don't worry about the monster for now. The collision threw some of the crew into the sea. Captain Edmond wants you to bring them back.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Yes, I saw them. Found two, they're back on deck. But the others...

speaker: Pylgia
content: I'll keep looking. At least, I'll bring back the bodies.

speaker: %u
content: Be careful out there.
Pylgia raises a hand and makes a wiping motion across her face, as if to brush away her unease for your sake. She gives you a faint, strained smile.

speaker: Pylgia
content: I will... come back safe.
The next second, she disappears beneath the waves.
You head below deck. The power's out, and you can only rely on the weak beam of a flashlight to check your surroundings.
The boiler room is in shambles. Stacks of supplies, meant for longer trips into the DisSea, have been smashed to bits.

speaker: Reid
content: Hey little one, don't come in here. There's nowhere to stand. I'm just grabbing some spare weapons. You stay there.
As you stare at the black ichor sprawled across the floor, that voice pierces your mind once again like a needle.
It's you... I've been... waiting for you...

speaker: %u
content: I... I'm not...
You are me... you are the Abyss... you are darkness...

speaker: %u
content: I am not!
You finally shatter the illusion, and the noise clawing at your head recedes. At this moment, a flat, mechanical voice speaks in your mind.

speaker: Schorl
content: Chief, we're detecting abnormal fluctuations in your mental link. All indicators have reached critical thresholds. We advise you to leave immediately.
Facing the ghostly blue orb that shouldn't exist here, your response comes without hesitation.

speaker: %u
content: No, I can't leave yet.

speaker: Reid
content: W-who are you talking to?
Reid asks nervously in the dark, his flashlight sweeping in your direction.

speaker: %u
content: It's nothing, I... I just spooked myself.
After steadying the guard, you continue your mental conversation with Schorl.

speaker: %u
content: I can't leave. They need my help... Besides, we haven't gathered any useful information. It's too early to go back.
Schorl falls silent. After a moment, it responds.

speaker: Schorl
content: Understood. We respect your judgment, but retain the option to sever the link by force. Please proceed with caution.
You refuse to give up on Sigmund. Bypassing the blocked corridor, you search room by room, until finally, you stop at a locked cabin door.
A rustling sound comes from behind the door, punctuated by ragged, heavy breathing. In the beam of your flashlight, a dark, unknown liquid seeps through the door, slowly consuming the panel...

speaker: Reid
content: Sigmund? You in there? Open up, you need help...

speaker: Sigmund
content: Go away! I told you, there are monsters here!

speaker: Reid
content: Open the door! We can take care of them together!

speaker: Sigmund
content: You haven't seen them only because they haven't found you! Get out of here! Leave me alone! I'd rather die in here with these things...

speaker: Reid
content: **** it! Knew this axe would come in handy. Here, hold the light for me.
You take the flashlight from Reid. He raises the emergency axe and hacks down at the door lock.
But the moment you break down the door, the figure huddled in the corner howls, spreading his arms wide as he lunges toward you.

speaker: Sigmund
content: Stay away from them!!
Time seems to stop.
Countless slimy tentacles erupt from the surrounding darkness, piercing the first mate's body.
He freezes. His face begins to melt, then his torso, his legs, and finally his arms.
In an instant, he dissolves before your very eyes, leaving a man-shaped puddle on the floor. Only the outline of his outstretched arms remains, vaguely reminding you of his final protective gesture.
The black ichor pools at your feet. The scene is horribly familiar.
The power to destroy people with fear, to twist reality through the mind... just like what happened to Ragnar several months ago.
Ragnar... That's right. How could you have forgotten about him? He was the first person on this ship to be crushed by fear. You placed him in a room, as if that would keep the problem contained.
But fear... fear cannot be contained. You must cut it off at the source. You must stop the tragedy from happening again. You must...
You must find Ragnar.
The flooded passages wind like a labyrinth, but you don't need to recall which room is his. Some dark intuition guides you, pulling you toward the only destination.
Finally, you stop at that door.
Ragnar is in the doorway. Once, he may have been a reliable member of the expedition. But after the being in the Abyss drove him mad, none of that matters anymore.
The man you see now is nothing more than an empty, pathetic shell, a trap meant to drag everyone down into the Abyss.
The door isn't locked. You push it open.
The attack you braced for never comes. In fact, the room is exactly as you saw it last time.
No monsters, no strange black ichor. Only a hunched figure sitting by the iron cot, his back turned to you.
How deceptive. His body no longer shows any sign of mutation. You may even mistake him for any other harmless patient.

Why didn't you see it sooner...? Humans are fragile. A little fear, a little pressure... that's all it takes to crush them, turning them into puppets of the Abyss. But that same fragility became the disguise that fooled everyone, making you overlook the one threat you should never have ignored.

speaker: Ragnar
content: Hehe... Hehehe...
Ragnar notices you and slowly turns around. His eyes are two pitch-black voids. His mouth is split into an uncanny grin as a dry, raspy laugh escapes from his throat.
It's laughing at you. Mocking you from the husk of your former teammate. Mocking the blind, weak fool you are...

speaker: Ragnar
content: Too late... It's too late... I told you... the monster never died... they're everywhere... everyone is a monster!

speaker: Pylgia
content: Go. Bring Ragnar and the collectors back to them.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Go back... to them.
Countless images flash through your mind: your encounter with Pylgia in the Abyss, the tragedies aboard the research vessel, Vikmar's disappearance, Sigmund's death...
These memories fill you with overwhelming regret and anger. And that anger catches flame, turning into an unquenchable thirst to kill.
You grab the emergency chisel propped against the door. Your body, overtaken by fury, takes one step forward, then another.
And still, he holds that eerie posture, his hollow, lightless eyes boring into yours, his mouth agape in silent derision.
You can almost hear him saying...

speaker: Ragnar
content: You can't do it, can you?
No. You'll show him. You'll prove him wrong. You raise the chisel high over your head. Soon, you'll sever the root of this tragedy...
Stop!
Just as you are about to strike, you hear an urgent shout from behind. Soft arms wrap around you, holding you fast and stopping you from landing the final blow.
In an instant, your body freezes, as if plunged into an icy ocean.
But how could you let something so weak stop you?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: He's the source of contamination on the ship! He's the one who killed Vikmar and Sigmund!!
You're the only one who saw through his disguise. You're righteous. You're good. You must save everyone...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: He brought the monsters from the Abyss onto the ship! He led the thing from the water back here!!
Think of those who died. They died because you're foolish, because you're weak! If only you had killed him sooner... if only...
Do you still remember their eyes? Do you remember how they looked at you before they died? You must not forget...
I BELIEVE IN YOU...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I believe... I will not forget... I believe in myself...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I will...
TEAR HIM APART TEAR HIM APART TEAR HIM APART TEAR HIM APART TEAR HIM APART TEAR HIM APART...
Once, twice, three times... The thick, sweet tang of blood fills your nostrils.
Blood sprays into the air. The droplets hang there, morphing into countless faces, crying, screaming, sprouting infinite hands that pull you into their embrace.
You're face-to-face with them. They open wide their pitch-black eyes, open their crimson mouths...
For us. For us. Save me. Save me. SAVE ME SAVE ME SAVE ME...
You are doing the right thing... YOU are all doing the right thing.
KILL HIM. KILL HIM. KILL HIM.
You strike again. This time, something splashes onto your lips. A soft, sweet, juicy morsel. It tastes divine.
[Gray Background with White Text]
Your desire is finally sated.
[Back to Normal]
You collapse to the ground, completely drained. You're caught by the person who first tried to stop you.
She holds you in her arms, human warmth seeping through the damp fabric into your body once more. You feel at peace.
...No, it's the warmth of blood.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Shin...?

You jolt upright, only to find her a mangled mess of flesh and blood. You want to grasp the hand that's holding you, but you don't dare, for you can see white bone showing through the gashes on her arm.
They're all stab wounds, your marks left on her with your chisel.
The metallic smell of blood, so comforting moments ago, now makes you want to throw up.

speaker: Shin
content: It's okay... We're here, it's okay...
Impervious to the pain, she gently lifts that hand and rests it against your cheek.

speaker: Shin
content: You just... lost control. You didn't mean it. I know.

Your companions have gathered around, shouting something, but the words barely register. You stare blankly as they scramble to bandage Shin's wounds. You reach out your hands, trying to help... but you realize they're the hands that attacked her.
You come back to your senses, fumbling for a piece of gauze, anything to pass along, but Shin takes your hand first, her fingers cold from the loss of blood.

speaker: Shin
content: I'm glad... I could do something for you...
Twenty minutes later, all the survivors are gathered in the wheelhouse, including you and Ragnar.
The cramped space now holds a dozen people, bodies pressed against each other as you force the thin air into your lungs and let it out in careful breaths. You are the only souls left on the ship.
No one dares to speak. The loudest sound in the frozen air is the dull thumping of hearts against ribs.
The collision has stopped, but Pylgia, still concerned, stays underwater to keep watch.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...I tried to do the bandages. Is it... okay?

You keep your head down, too guilty to meet her eyes, and busy yourself with dressing Shin's injuries. The cuts look terrible, but thankfully, they're just flesh wounds. A child's attack can only do so much harm.
But still, you're gnawed by doubts.
Here, trapped in this lonely vessel on the dark sea... has your mind become so fragile that a simple taunt from Ragnar could drive you to madness?

speaker: Shin
content: Thank you.
Shin interrupts your brooding. With a faint smile, she rises gracefully, smoothing the creases from her dress. Her composure seems to dispel the suffocating dread in the air.

speaker: Shin
content: We've cleared the danger zone. If we keep going in the direction you gave us, we should, in theory... reach land soon.

speaker: Shin
content: "Mantis"
Her voice is steady, but sorrow passes in her eyes.

speaker: Shin
content: "Mantis"

speaker: Shin
content: I didn't realize he was under so much pressure. I killed him...

speaker: Captain Edmond
content: Don't blame yourself, Shin. It wasn't your fault.
Your gaze drifts to Ragnar in the corner. He leans against the wall, his eyes vacant, a dry, broken laugh rattling in his throat.
Again, words spill from your lips, almost beyond your control.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: We've already found the source of all this, haven't we?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: We can't let this happen again...
Before you can finish, Shin's hand presses gently on your shoulder.

speaker: Shin
content: I've checked. Ragnar's body is fine, but he's lost all response to external stimuli. In other words, he no longer has any negative emotions that can be manipulated.

speaker: Shin
content: I know what you're worried about... but this isn't the time to bloody our hands with a crewmate's life. It's for everyone's sake, not just his.
A brief silence fills the wheelhouse.

You survey the room. Captain Edmond has taken the helm, his expression grim. Reid, who witnessed Sigmund's end alongside you, clutches a safety axe and stands guard over Laura silently, like he's trying to atone for something.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But...
Your voice is raw, forced from the back of your throat. You've seen too many tragedies, lost too many important companions. You're... running out of courage for another gamble.
Shin takes your hand, her palm warm and steady.

speaker: Shin
content: If we let fear overcome reason at a time like this...

speaker: Shin
content: I don't know for sure what would happen, but I have a feeling it would be a fate worse than death... and you probably understand that better than any of us.
Noticing your silence, Shin offers a familiar smile.

speaker: Shin
content: The expedition's faced impossible odds before. And every time, we pulled through by supporting each other.

speaker: Shin
content: This time, it'll be no different.
After a moment, Pylgia's fragmented words crackle through the silent radio.

speaker: Pylgia
content: You... saved me...

speaker: Pylgia
content: This time... I'll continue to believe in you...
Every eye in the wheelhouse turns to you, some confused, others hopeful, but all filled with trust.
You close your eyes, your chest heavy yet warm. That dark feeling of despair seems to have lifted a little.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'll get us out of here, but...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Until we're truly safe, no one can let their guard down.
Weapons clutched tight, the crew watches Ragnar with wary eyes, isolating him in an empty corner of the room.
Through the portholes, the shadow of land is much closer than before. But you know the real danger never comes from above the waves.
Temperatures at sea change drastically. Soon, your breaths fog in the frigid air.
The room grows colder by the minute. Shin shivers in her thin, damp clothes, yet she drapes the only blanket over Laura.

speaker: Shin
content: Your injuries are worse. Stay warm.
Laura was in the lab during the collision and was struck by fallen instruments. She's barely managing to stay conscious.

speaker: Captain Edmond
content: The temperature's dropping too fast... At this rate, the injured won't last until we reach shore.
The crewman you met earlier in the lower cabins hobbles forward, leaning on a metal pipe.

speaker: Crew Member
content: It's the boiler room. I saw it during the crash, but didn't have time to fix it... I'll handle it now.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Your leg...?

speaker: Crew Member
content: Just a sprain. It's nothing.
To prove his point, he lifts the pipe and hops on the spot, but the twitch in his face gives him away.
Even so, he's still in better shape than most of the survivors.

speaker: Captain Edmond
content: Alright. But we need one more person, for safety.
Reid stares down at the axe gripped tightly in his hand, face rigid, but never moves to stand. The captain gives his shoulder an understanding pat and makes the call.

speaker: Captain Edmond
content: Shin needs to tend to the wounded. Our guide will keep us on course and watch for threats. I'll go with two of our repair crew.

speaker: Captain Edmond
content: Reid, I'm leaving the wheelhouse to you. Keep everyone safe.
Reid looks taken aback. Then, he nods with resolve.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Wait, the lower decks... they aren't safe. The comms are down. What if you run into danger? How do you call for help?
The captain takes the metal pipe from the crewman and waves it confidently.

speaker: Captain Edmond
content: Tapping signals. The ship has a metal hull. The sound carries. We tap on the walls down there, you'll hear it up here.

speaker: Captain Edmond
content: That's a sailor's wisdom for you. Don't underestimate our crew!
They head out without further ado. The crewman turns in the doorway and waves.

speaker: Crew Member
content: Hang in there. We'll be back soon.
Soon, clear tapping sounds come from the metal walls. Those left behind begin their long, silent vigil, nerves stretched taut.
The sea is calm. Right now, you want nothing more than to see that familiar figure break the surface.
You miss her face, the way she could soothe your troubled soul despite her clumsiness with words.
You've helped each other through so many hardships. But on this voyage, you barely spent any time together, busy with your separate duties...
You have no comms, no way to reach her. All you can do is wait.
The metal tapping has been coming from the same spot for some time, when a low exclamation breaks the silence.

speaker: Reid
content: Hey, is it... getting warmer?
Shin looks up, her lips blue from the cold. She pulls a stiff hand from where she'd tucked it for warmth and feels the air.

speaker: Shin
content: Yes, it is... Looks like they succeeded. They'll be back soon.
A voice suddenly comes from the other side of the room.

speaker: Laura
content: Who? Who's coming back? Sigmund?
Laura's gaunt face peeks from under the blanket. She had received emergency treatment, but her condition hasn't improved much in just a few hours.

speaker: Laura
content: Gasp...
She groans in pain. Shin pulls back the blanket to see that the movement has reopened Laura's wound; fresh blood seeps through her clothes.

speaker: Shin
content: Don't speak, and try to lie still. Your bones are broken. You need to rest.
Shin gently tears clean clothing into strips and bandages the wound. As the room gets warmer, Laura's mental state improves considerably, and everyone breathes a sigh of relief.
Shin gets up and walks toward Ragnar, opening her notebook for his check-up.

speaker: %u
content: Don't get too close. Let me do it.
You stop Shin from touching Ragnar and mimic the procedures she used when she first examined you.
Body temperature, breathing, pulse... You even remember to pry open his mouth and eyelids, checking the mucosa for any anomalies.

speaker: %u
content: ...Everything's normal.
Unlike the others in the room bearing some injury or other, he doesn't even have a scratch. Based on the examination alone, Ragnar is "healthier" than any of you.
These results make you wonder if you were wrong. Perhaps Ragnar has been abandoned by the Abyss. Or maybe... you really were thinking too much.
Shin records Ragnar's results in her notebook. The room has settled down considerably.
After checking on Ragnar, Shin returns to Laura, curled up in the blanket, trembling.

speaker: Shin
content: How are you feeling? Are you in pain?

speaker: Laura
content: No... I'm fine...
Laura sniffles, but the tear tracks on her face betray her.

speaker: Shin
content: Do you... remember something?
Laura hides her face in her hands, then jerks her head up again. She struggles to contain herself, trying to preserve the reason and dignity expected of an expedition member.

speaker: Laura
content: I... you told me... Sigmund, my boy... he's already... he's not coming back...
Shin gently wraps her arm around Laura's trembling shoulders. Her silent embrace shatters the façade that the woman had struggled so hard to keep up.
First come quiet sobs, then low whimpers, until finally, she can hold herself back no more. Clinging to Shin, she cries her heart out.
Everyone sees her as a serious, capable researcher. But now, she is only a mother who has just lost her child.
After a long while, the crying eventually subsides. Shin gently strokes Laura's back, her voice soft as a whisper.

speaker: Shin
content: Perhaps... Sigmund hasn't truly left us.
Laura snaps up her head, a glimmer of hope flickering in her eyes before dimming again. She knows these are just words of comfort.

speaker: Shin
content: In the legends of the old era, when heroes die, their souls live on in people's memories for eternity.

speaker: Shin
content: Before the Perishing Star fell, scholars like you and I would have dismissed that as a wishful tale. But in this forbidden zone, we've seen too many things that defy our understanding...

speaker: Shin
content: Now, I find myself wanting to believe in such stories. Perhaps Sigmund is standing beside you right now. You can no longer see him, but he's watching over you in his own way.

speaker: Laura
content: Thank you, Shin... Thank you for telling me... such a beautiful story...
But Shin shakes her head. She is smiling, her eyes filled with tenderness, but she seems to be looking past this small wheelhouse at somewhere far away.

speaker: Shin
content: Don't thank me. Humanity is so very tiny, compared to the sky and the ocean.

speaker: Shin
content: And yet... when these tiny creatures come together, they somehow find the courage to face the darkness, to overcome their fear of the unknown... What an incredible power that is...

speaker: Shin
content: I should be the one thanking all of you. For letting me see...
She says no more. Pressing her lips together, she doesn't continue the topic.
The rhythmic tapping continues. Reid is visibly relaxed, even in the mood to joke.

speaker: Reid
content: Sounds like they're in good spirits.
But Teto, the communications officer, has gone pale.

speaker: Teto
content: By my calculations, they should've been back long ago...
Clang... clang...
Clang clang... clang...
You close your eyes, listening to the rhythm of the metal pipe.
Clang clang clang clang...
Each strike is heavier than the last, the tempo quickening.
CLANG.
After one last, sharp clang, the tapping comes to an abrupt halt.
Come out from there... Don't hide...
Face... the darkness... the fear... Face... yourself...
You shudder violently, instinctively moving to shield Shin and Laura.
The light in the wheelhouse goes out.
In the darkness, a familiar, nauseating feeling washes over you. You hear the writhing of something wet, feel the gaze of countless eyes from the shadows...
You have no time to think. Cold, clammy tendrils have coiled noiselessly around your limbs, dragging you into the dark Abyss...
Once again, you narrowly escape the darkness. When you open your eyes, the first thing you see is Shin's worried face.

speaker: Shin
content: You fainted again...

speaker: Shin
content: Don't be afraid. They'll be back soon. We'll make it to shore. Banyan will heal you. No one can hurt you...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No... something's wrong! Listen!
You struggle to get up, pointing at the door.
The clanging draws closer, very, very slowly.
So slow, it couldn't be a human walking...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: They've been gone too long.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The banging is louder than when they left... but why haven't they come back?
Everyone senses something deeply wrong with the sound. Yet it continues approaching, one clang after another, a deafening clamor that splits your skull.
Clang... clang...
Clang clang... clang...
Clang clang clang clang...

speaker: Crew Member
content: D-don't scare us. If it's not them coming back...
Her voice cracks with tears.

speaker: Crew Member
content: <color=#fb9259>Then what's getting closer to us now?</color>
The banging gets closer. Soon, you realize, it's not just coming from outside the door!
Frenzied clanging bursts from all the metal walls.
Every pipe is screaming. Every steel plate is quaking. The entire ship seems to groan in agony, grating on your nerves.
Then, suddenly, the banging stops.
Something huge has stopped at the door. The next instant, the walls are shaken by violent slams.
THOOM! THOOM!
This is nothing like the sound of the metal pipe. Only something enormous can make these booming sounds.

speaker: Crew Members
content: Aaaahhh!
The crew shrieks. Laura's fragile nerves finally snap, and she clings to Shin in terror.
Whatever the thing... It is right outside.

speaker: Shin
content: Stay calm! We can't let them in!

Shin shoves Laura to a nearby crewmate, then grabs an iron chain and wraps it around the door handle. But it's not enough. The thing outside starts crawling fast, the sound of its wet, grimy steps reverberating across the walls and ceiling as it barrels toward the front porthole.

speaker: Ragnar
content: Hehehe... Hahahahaha...
Ragnar has somehow gotten to his feet, eyes transfixed on the door as peals of maniacal laughter burst from his throat. But no one has time for him right now.

speaker: Shin
content: The window!
The crew member holding Laura musters her courage and leaps toward the window. But the moment she reaches for it, the darkness outside coils around her injured arm and yanks her violently through.

speaker: Injured Crew Member
content: Aaaahhh!!
She lets out a blood-curdling scream, desperately clawing at the window ledge, her fingernails screeching against the metal, leaving bloody streaks.

speaker: Injured Crew Member
content: Help me! Somebody help me!

speaker: Laura
content: Don't let go! Someone, anyone, help us! HELP US!!!
The next second, the window slams shut. The darkness devours her whole, leaving only a few bloodied fingers rolling across the console.

speaker: Laura
content: Ah... Aaaahhh... AAAAHHHHH...

speaker: Pylgia
content: What's going on?!
Screams, pounding, and scraping against metal fill the air, drowning Pylgia's urgent cries from the radio comms.
The comms officer picks up the radio with trembling hands, but doesn't know what to say.
His whole body is shaking, threatening to seize up.
You struggle to sit up, yelling, trying to steady him.
But Teto doesn't seem to hear you. He stares blankly at the writhing darkness beyond the porthole, hesitantly bringing the radio to his lips. He forces out a warning, word by word.

speaker: Teto
content: Don't... come back... Out... side... there's...

speaker: Pylgia
content: What? There's what outside?

speaker: Teto
content: There's... Gaaaarghhhh!!!
Black tentacles erupt from his mouth, silencing his words. His body bloats like a balloon stuffed with leeches before bursting with a sickening pop.

speaker: Ragnar
content: Hahaha... Haha... HAHAHAHAHA...

As he watches his crewmates burst one by one, Ragnar's laughter grows louder, shriller, almost piercing your eardrums. He admires the scene like a detached spectator before a mural of hell, every last shred of his sanity gone.

speaker: Reid
content: No! This can't be happening...
Reid has snapped. Clutching his axe, he starts toward Ragnar.

speaker: Reid
content: He's... he's turning... Can't let him live...

speaker: Reid
content: I'm... I'm gonna kill you! This is all your fault! If it weren't for you... I should've killed you from the start!!

speaker: Shin
content: Stop! Reid, guard the helm!

Shin grabs another metal rod and jams it into the door handle. The battering outside weakens for a moment. She stops Reid and turns to restrain Ragnar, trying to secure the wheelhouse's last line of defense.

speaker: Shin
content: He's not turning! It's safe in here for now. We just have to keep that thing out!

speaker: Shin
content: Reid! Do you hear me?

speaker: Laura
content: Sigmund? Is that you, Sigmund?
With Shin overwhelmed, Laura suddenly rises from where she'd been sitting on the floor and stares at the door with vacant eyes.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Don't go there! That's not Sigmund outside, it's...
Her gaunt face brightens with a tender smile, as if enchanted by the softened knocks on the door. You try to call her back to her senses, but it's clearly futile.

speaker: Laura
content: My dear boy, you really are alive... I was wrong... I shouldn't have been so hard on you...

speaker: Laura
content: You've always been... my pride and joy...

speaker: Shin
content: Stop her!
Hearing Shin's cry, you drag your broken body over and desperately try to hold her back. But Laura moves like a soulless puppet, taking one step after another toward the door.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Stop! He's not there!
But her strength is shocking, and your arms are growing sore. Blood seeps through her makeshift bandages, yet she seems to feel neither pain nor weight as she forcibly drags you along.

speaker: Laura
content: My boy's crying for help... How can I ignore him...

speaker: Laura
content: My boy... Mommy's coming...
You don't know what she's seen. But the instant she touches the door handle, her body dissolves like the others, melting into a puddle at the door.
Your hands pass right through her, and you tumble to the ground, collapsing onto the black ichor.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Darn it!
You slam your fist on the floor, helpless. But the unfolding horror doesn't grant you a moment's rest.

The porthole shatters, and black ichor seeps in from every crack. Like living things, they transform into writhing masses of tentacles, churning and squirming as they close in on Reid, who is still standing guard over Ragnar.

speaker: Shin
content: Reid! Watch out!

speaker: Ragnar
content: Hahahaha... I saw it... It is coming for me! Hahaha!!!

At the sight of the black ichor, Ragnar's laughter turns more manic as he babbles in some unknowable tongue. He throws off Shin, who is trying to restrain him, and begins crawling toward the black ichor, dragging his bonds behind him.

speaker: Shin
content: ...Ahhh!
Reid had been standing in a daze. At Shin's cry, his whole body shudders, yet he remains oblivious to the tentacles slithering up behind him. Instead, he turns to look at the two of you.

speaker: Reid
content: I... I must...

speaker: Reid
content: Aaaaargh! I don't care! To hell with this ******* world! Just DIE!!!
He raises the axe high and brings it down on Ragnar with all his strength.
The first blow takes off Ragnar's left arm. The black ichor instantly reforms the limb.
The second blow takes off the right side of his body. The black ichor once again repairs the gaps.

speaker: Ragnar
content: Haha... Hahahaha!!!
Ragnar's maniacal laughter never ceases, as if mocking Reid's futile attempts. Shin stares at the scene, paralyzed. There's nothing she can do to stop this.

speaker: Reid
content: Why... why won't you DIE?! AAAARGH!!!

speaker: Shin
content: ...No! —Reid!!
The third blow takes off Ragnar's head.

speaker: Ragnar
content: Guh...
The laughter that had tormented you stops abruptly as the severed head rolls across the floor.
Ragnar's headless body collapses into a pool of black ichor, which coils around Reid's legs as if possessed of a mind of its own. But Reid just stands there, motionless, a mournful smile on his lips.

speaker: Reid
content: I promised... I'd keep you safe... I kept my word... Captain... Heh... Hehe...
Black tears stream from Reid's eyes as torrents of dark ichor gush from his body, rushing toward you and Shin, the last two survivors left.
Unable to bear the mental strain anymore, your mind erupts in a deafening roar.
The moment before the black tide engulfs you, a flash of blue light tears your consciousness from your body. The world around you shatters like glass.
The last thing you see is Shin, sitting stunned on the floor, black ichor spattered on her face and soaking through her clothes.

speaker: Shin
content: Why... how did this happen...
She presses her hands to her eyes, to her face. Her crew, her companions, all dissolved into nothing before her very eyes. She is powerless, the darkness closing in to swallow her whole...

speaker: Shin
content: Sob... sob...
You seem to hear her crying. You see her clutching your broken body. You struggle to reach for her, but you only drift farther and farther away...
[Scene Change]
Your heart jolts as you open your eyes in the room at DisSea Monitoring Station.

speaker: Schorl
content: Chief, we detected signs of mental breakdown and forcibly extracted you from the illusion. How are you feeling now?
You look at the emotionless black triangle and feel an unexpected sting of envy. You lie back down without hesitation and let out a long exhale.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Well then, I suppose I owe you one.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Send me back.
Schorl falls silent for only a moment before restarting the connection.
Eerie red and black intertwine as you plunge once more into that violent sea of alien hues.
Before being consumed by the sea of madness, you feel your feet hit the solid steel of a deck again.
Bloody, chaotic footprints wind from the deck toward the inner cabin, each dark red smear like a gaping wound.
You take a deep breath and follow the trail inside.
[Scene Transition]
The corridor ahead is empty, thick with the stench of rot and damp. Broken lights dangle from the ceiling, their flickering bulbs casting twisted shadows across shattered glass.
The clock on the wall has long since stopped, its fractured hands pointing crookedly toward the bottom right. At least four hours have passed since you left.
Your heart sinks as you realize that in those critical hours, you've clearly missed too much.
Suddenly, you hear a noise in the darkness. Someone is climbing up the rope ladder on the side of the ship.

speaker: %u
content: Pylgia?
Pylgia notices you at almost the same time. She's in rough shape. Her diving suit is torn, her skin ghostly pale from being submerged for too long. Several ghastly wounds mar her flesh.
You don't know what she endured down there, but seeing her like this brings back many terrible memories.

speaker: Pylgia
content: I got caught up underwater... What happened on the ship?

speaker: %u
content: ...We were attacked. I was forced to escape the wheelhouse. I have no idea what it's like in there now.

speaker: Pylgia
content: I see. Let's check the wheelhouse first.
Pylgia nods, gripping her harpoon tight.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Don't be afraid. This time, I'm here.
You follow her, dragging your battered body, ravaged by the unforgiving sea, toward the wheelhouse.
It doesn't take long to reach your destination. There are no monsters at the door, no crewmates. Only horrifying dents in the metal, proof that the attack wasn't a nightmare.
[Small CG 01]
Black, human-shaped stains cover the floor. The crew members who were still fighting when you left—including Captain Edmond—are all gone.

In the empty wheelhouse, only one person remains. Shin leans against the console, her face and chest smeared with blood. Blood is still gushing from an appalling wound in her abdomen, soaking her white shirt crimson.
Beside her, various items are haphazardly piled together:

Reid's axe is jammed into a metal groove beside the helm, its dull blade propping up a bent metal pipe, the makeshift crutch of a wounded crewmate. Together with the broken railing, they brace the helm, keeping it from slipping.
Laura's safety goggles, the ones she always wore during experiments, are now wedged into a crack in the console, watch over the approaching shore with her final will.

On the other side, pieces of clothing, drenched in blood and black ichor, are torn into strips and knotted into ropes. Tied to the helm from anchor points across the console, they hold the helm in place, ensuring the broken vessel stays on course.
Every item bears a familiar memory of its owner, a record of life's final act of will.
And Shin assembled this makeshift fortress on the verge of death, with the last dregs of her strength.

speaker: Shin
content: Who's... there? Is someone... still alive? That's great...
You and Pylgia rush forward almost simultaneously.
Pylgia tosses her harpoon aside and grabs the sputtering helm, holding it steady through gritted teeth.
You catch Shin's swaying body, carefully helping her sit against the wall.
Only now do you get a clear look at her injuries. Her abdomen is torn open by a deep, jagged wound. You can even see the warm pulse of her gut, threatening to spill out.
Blood flows steadily from her wounds, pooling with the black ichor on the floor and soaking your clothes.
Panic seizes you, your hands shaking uncontrollably as you desperately try to push her warm insides back where they belong.
You rip strips from your own clothing, rolling them up to dress the gash, doing everything you can to stanch her wound.
Tears and blood blur your vision, but you never stop working, praying you won't lose another companion.
In your daze, a cold hand touches your face.
[Small CG 02]

speaker: Shin
content: Is that you... my little guide?
You wipe away your tears and see Shin open her eyes. So much blood loss has left her gaze hollow. She can't even see you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It's me... it's me, I'm back...
Even the usually collected Pylgia has lost her composure.

speaker: Pylgia
content: What happened? Why are you...

speaker: Shin
content: I'm sorry... I couldn't save them...

speaker: Shin
content: I don't know... why it had to be them... Why am I the only one left...? What did I... do wrong...?
Undisguised grief and anguish wash over the face of this beloved leader, who has witnessed her trusted companions vanish one by one.
The Shin you remember was always calm, able to understand everyone's feelings and forgive their mistakes. But now, trapped in the shadow of her own failure, she feels like a stranger.
You gently take her blood-stained hand, your voice equally choked with emotion.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You've done enough, Shin. They fought to get us this far... We have to live, we have to keep going. For them.
Shin trembles at the sound of your words.
She slowly closes her eyes, then opens them again, whispering in a faint yet determined voice.

speaker: Shin
content: You're right... We still have a chance...

speaker: Shin
content: At least you're still here... At least... the ship hasn't gone off course...

speaker: Shin
content: Can you...
She struggles to turn her head, trying to look out the window.

speaker: Shin
content: Can you help me see... is this... the right direction...?
Outside, veiled in a thin mist, the shadow of land draws closer. In these terrible circumstances, it's the only good news there is.
Shin's final decision, made while she was dying, kept the ship from drifting off course and preserved your last ray of hope.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The course is right. We'll reach land soon.

speaker: Shin
content: That's... good...
Tears flow from her vacant eyes, streaming through dried blood to form two dark red streaks down her cheeks.
Still, she forces the corners of her mouth up into the smile you and Pylgia know so well.

speaker: Shin
content: Perhaps I need... to rest for a while...
The horrific wounds, the endless mental torment... what Shin has gone through is beyond the limits of human endurance.
She can't hold on any longer. Her body goes slack, and she leans into your embrace, barely able to sit up.
As her body grows heavier, you wrap your arms tightly around her shoulders, panic and helplessness rising again. But in this moment, she uses her last bit of strength to grip your arm.

speaker: Shin
content: Promise me...
In her dilated pupils, nothing but desperate, fervent pleading remains.

speaker: Shin
content: Take this ship... to land... Please...
With these words, Shin collapses in your arms, unconscious.
Pylgia reclines a chair in the wheelhouse, and together you carefully lay Shin on it.
Shin's breathing grows peaceful, and before long, she falls into a deep slumber. She's simply too exhausted.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You should tend to your wounds, Pylgia.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Okay.
She sits down on the floor in front of you and unzips her diving suit, revealing horrific wounds that look like something had chewed through her flesh.

speaker: Pylgia
content: You were right... That monster from before... it might have been following us the whole time.

speaker: Pylgia
content: The water was unnaturally dark... I couldn't really see it, but I could feel it watching me.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Every time it got close, the static on the radio would spike. So I tried to hunt it down, drive it away, but...

speaker: Pylgia
content: I couldn't defeat it... It had so many... shadows, like tentacles. It took me too long to break free... By the time I made it back, it was already too late.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Even now, I can't be sure if it's gone.

speaker: Pylgia
content: More likely, it's still following us... waiting for the next chance to strike.

speaker: Pylgia
content: I shouldn't have stayed underwater for so long... No, maybe I shouldn't have left the ship at all. If I'd stayed...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No, even if you'd been here, you couldn't have stopped what happened. If anything, you're alive and well. That's the better outcome.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Besides, there's no point dwelling on it now. Shin entrusted the ship to us. What matters most is bringing her back alive—along with the collectors, and… everyone’s legacy.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I don't know if the monster is still out there... Maybe we should use some kind of bait to lure it away? No... it's too dangerous to go alone. We can't risk it.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: We're so close to land. If we can just hold on a little longer, we'll be rescued. Shin will also...
Pylgia stares at you in silence. Rather than comforting her, your words are meant more for convincing yourself.
Fog seeps in through the shattered porthole, and you can't stop yourself from shivering.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Are you... cold? There should be medicine and supplies left in the medical bay. Warm blankets too. I'll go get them.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm coming with you!
Your overwrought nerves make the words fly out of your mouth. You can't bear the thought of losing someone else.
[Black Screen]
You feel a sudden chill as Pylgia wraps her arms around you.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Don't worry. I'm here.

speaker: Pylgia
content: You're not alone.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Shin didn't just entrust all this to you alone. I'm here too.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Trust me, it's going to be okay. And I trust you just the same.
[Fade from Black]
She awkwardly reaches out to wipe the dampness from your face.

speaker: Pylgia
content: I never doubted... that you could do this.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm sorry... Thank you... Pylgia.
As Pylgia leaves the wheelhouse, you take your place at the helm.
You turn your gaze back to the ocean. Throttling up the engines, you steer the ship into the dense fog.
The ship slows down. Before long, you find the shore.
In the pale gray fog shrouding the sea, there's a small gap where it meets the land.
A beach. The sand nearly indistinguishable from the heavy fog.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Pylgia, it's a beach! Quick, get the lifeboats ready! We can finally...

speaker: Pylgia
content: ...I checked when I went to the medical bay. It must have been from the earlier attack... the two lifeboats have crashed into each other. One has a hole through its deck, the other's bow is shattered. They're both useless...

speaker: Pylgia
content: We'll have to drop anchor offshore and send out a signal. Hope the expedition team can come and pick us up...
Pylgia's words are like ice water, dousing what little relief you felt from surviving the ordeal.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What do we do now...
With the fuel running empty, you can't afford to search for another landing site.
A mountain looms on the nearby shore, unmoved, its giant shadows seeming to mock you: so close, and yet so far.
In this desperate moment, a crazy idea comes to your mind.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Perhaps we could just run the ship aground? Beach it on the shore?

speaker: Pylgia
content: ...Are you sure?

speaker: Pylgia
content: If we can't keep the ship balanced, it will tip over and break apart. We might not survive the collapse.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Fifty-fifty. We burn all the fuel and go full speed ahead. If we hit the beach before the ship breaks apart, we'll live.
You try to sound confident.
Pylgia silently watches Shin beneath the blanket. The painkillers are wearing off, and her body involuntarily curls up.
Though she's still unconscious, the deep furrow of her brow and the sheen of sweat on her forehead speak of the pain Shin is enduring.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Okay, I trust you.
You don't hesitate. Firing up the engines again, you aim straight for the beach.
As the ship gathers speed, red grounding alarms blare from the radar. You ignore them, using Reid's axe to jam the helm in place before pulling Shin into a corner with Pylgia.
The ship is tossed around as rocks graze the bottom of the vessel. You grab the nearest handrail, bracing for the more violent impact to come.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Three... two... one... now!
[Vibration Effect]
The impact hits on cue. Through the long, brutal quaking that threatens to tear your insides apart, you and Pylgia hold on to each other, shielding Shin's body with your own.
[Black Screen, Vibration Ends]
At some point, the shaking stops.
You don't know when... you must have passed out. But when you open your eyes, the world is perfectly still.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Did we make it?
You try to get up, but your legs give out. Pylgia catches you. Shin, shielded beneath her, is also unharmed.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Yes, we're fine. We can get off the ship now.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The expedition team's got to notice a crash like that. Hopefully they can find...
[Special Effect]
You look up through the broken porthole, and freeze.
You don't know where you are. You don't know when the expedition team might find you. But you realize... something else has found you first.
The mountain beyond the fog, the colossal shadow blotting out the sky and sun... at this moment, it opens its eyes.
[Special Effect]

speaker: Pylgia
content: What... is that...

This isn't some abstract metaphor, but the reality unfolding before your very eyes. The mountain and earth tremble and split open, revealing dark hollows within, crystals glittering with otherworldly sheen.
Eyes. Countless, grotesquely massive eyes.
The sunken pupils slowly turn, like black holes that devour all light. Just looking at them paralyzes you, roots you to the spot.
And when those eyes finally stop turning, you find yourselves caught in their gaze.
A single, void glance is all it takes to shatter your will with distorted, overwhelming horror. You're flooded by negative emotions beyond your control.
Regret over your choices. Agony in your body and mind. Despair of facing the invincible... Mad whispers you cannot comprehend, pouring in like water from a burst dam.
[Blur]

And then you realize... you know this thing. It's the gaze that's been hunting you. The ocean depths you once descended into... A part of the Abyss that you and Pylgia barely escaped from, at such a terrible cost.
[Color Shift, Distortion]
You open your mouth, trying to tell Pylgia to run, but no sound comes out.
On the mudflats, the cliffs, even the waves behind you, more eyes are slowly opening. The land you imagined never existed. That distant shadow was a trap from the start, set specifically for you.
And now, it is here. The mountain, the land, the false shores—they're nothing more than a small fraction of the great torso of the unfathomable thing beneath the Abyss.
This time, it's not just Pylgia. Shin, too, has become a victim of your foolish acts.
Do you really think you're the expedition's "little guide"?
You're wrong. How many times have you been deceived? You're nothing but a toy for these unknowable things. Every choice you make only hastens your companions' deaths...
<color=#dg1f1f>With your own hands, you've sent everyone on this ship down the path to madness and death... a path of no return.</color>
[Distortion Vanishes, Fade to Black + Chaos Effects]
Countless eyeballs twist and merge, morphing into black tentacles that crush the last few intact portholes and bore into the wheelhouse.
You no longer have the strength to fight, nor the will to resist. This is your punishment for daring to defy the Abyss. Your verdict for killing your companions.

speaker: Shin
content: This... isn't your fault.
[Big CG: Shin's Sacrifice]
A frail figure appears in your view. Shin, who was unconscious moments ago, is now standing before you.

speaker: Shin
content: You've done... well...

speaker: Shin
content: No matter how hard we try... there are some things humanity... can never overcome...
You can't make out her face. The darkness writhes behind her, but she stands firm, shielding you with her body.

speaker: Shin
content: But fate... won't abandon us forever...
The bandages you wrapped for her fall away. Her gentle face begins to dissolve in the eerie red light.
The palpable malice eats her body away, but her voice is as soft as ever.

speaker: Shin
content: Live on, my dear guide... As long as you're alive, there will always be hope...

speaker: Shin
content: I believe in you... You'll lead everyone... to the right...
Shin crumbles before your eyes, dissolving into a human-shaped puddle.
In the next instant, darkness surges like a tide, sweeping away the last trace of her existence.
Shin is gone. And with her goes the infinite torso of the Abyss, the shadow of the false land.
Only you and Pylgia are left in the wheelhouse. Those horrific memories carved into your soul are like phantoms that never existed.
But you know, with despair, that they aren't phantoms. The shattered portholes, the dead control panels, and the congealed alien matter are all proof.
Now, where is the ship supposed to go? You don't know. The fog has lifted, yet all you can see is the endless ocean. There are no stars to guide you, no landmarks to show the way.
Of course, even if there were, you wouldn't dare trust them again. You can only drift aimlessly with this ship across these loathsome, unending waters, waiting for inevitable death.
[Fade to Black, Show Schorl]
Deep in your consciousness, a blue light flickers. Ah, that's right. You won't die here. Unlike the crew, you always have an escape route. The illusion can't truly kill you.
Then why fight at all? Why make any choices? Everything you've done has been proven wrong.
Or perhaps your presence here is a mistake.

speaker: Pylgia
content: No fuel... We need to prepare for a long drift.
Pylgia's voice reaches your ear, cutting through your muddled thoughts.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Even without power, the tides will eventually carry us to shore. It's just a matter of time.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Don't be afraid. I'm still here. Even if it's just the two of us, I promise I'll get you back.

speaker: Pylgia
content: As long as we're alive... there will always be hope.
She glances at the broken, drafty portholes, then extends a hand to you.

speaker: Pylgia
content: We can't stay here. We'll freeze. Come with me.
Pylgia is the only one speaking in the wheelhouse, but it takes a long time for her words to penetrate the fog in your mind.
She wants to take you away. She hasn't given up. She's fighting this destined end?
But what's the point?
The blue light flickers incessantly in the depths of your mind. Your body is as stiff as a stone statue, leaving Pylgia's hand suspended in the air.

speaker: Pylgia
content: We... can't let Shin's sacrifice be in vain.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Do you remember what happened in the Abyss? When I wanted to give up being human... you didn't give up on me... If it hadn't been for you, I would never have made it back.

speaker: Pylgia
content: So... trust me, and believe in yourself. Don't give up, okay?
Her voice is almost pleading by the end, bringing a moment of clarity to your murky mind.
You could give up and walk away. But what about Pylgia?
If you leave now, would you ever see her again? What would become of her fate?
You don't know, but you don't have the slightest courage to find out.
In your daze, you grasp her outstretched hand. Her damp palm still carries human warmth.
You let her lead you toward whatever unknown awaits.
You settle down in the ship's dining room.
There's a decent supply of food, a furnace for warmth, and most importantly, doors, windows, and walls that are still mostly intact.
Compared to the flooded lower decks, this is the best long-term refuge Pylgia could find.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Tonight's dinner is canned tuna in oil.
Pylgia passes you a heated can clasped with tongs.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Careful, it's hot.
You have no appetite, but you can't refuse her kindness. And you know you have to eat.
So you repeat the slow, robotic motion of putting the fish into your mouth.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Do you know why tuna fish are clever?

speaker: Pylgia
content: Because they spend so much time in schools.
Your mind has become so numb, it takes you a while to realize Pylgia just told you a joke.
It's not very funny, and Pylgia doesn't make a good comedian, but you laugh anyway.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That was a good one, Pylgia... Thank you.
Time passes, and food is running out. You're forced to leave the dining room from time to time to search for supplies in other parts of the ship.
At first, Pylgia says she could go alone and asks you to wait in the dining room. You wouldn't hear of it.
(Scene Brightens)
Crack!

Pylgia breaks apart a chair from the wheelhouse and feeds the pieces into the furnace. As the fog rolls back, temperatures have plummeted. You're burning through fuel faster than you get through food. Soon, you've stripped the upper decks of almost everything combustible.
She finishes her work and returns to your side. The two of you wrap yourselves in the only blanket you found in the medical bay, huddling close for warmth.
Wood crackles in the furnace. You clutch her hand tightly.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Try to get some sleep.
She tries to soothe you, but you no longer dare to rest. You mustn't fall asleep. As long as she allows, you'll hold on to her hand to make sure she won't suddenly disappear.
Schorl keeps flashing in the depths of your mind, but you don't want to respond.
You're afraid that if you leave, you'll never come back... that you'll never see her again.

speaker: Pylgia
content: The ship probably won't hold out much longer...
This morning, a loud crash came from the lower decks. Pylgia determined that the ship's hull is giving way.
Eroded by fog and seawater, paint has peeled from the upper deck, revealing metal rusted beyond recognition. It's only a matter of time before the keel and waterproofing fail.
Frankly, it's a miracle the ship's held together this long, after everything it's been through.

speaker: Pylgia
content: I was looking through Sigmund's shipping manifest yesterday. It lists some spare submarine parts in the cargo hold below.

speaker: Pylgia
content: The fog isn't as bad in the lower decks. Maybe those parts are still usable. We could try fixing one of the lifeboats...
Honestly, you don't see the point of this.
Neither of you knows much about mechanics. Even if you did, how long would it take to assemble a submarine...?
And what then? With no fuel or destination, where would you even go? How long could a tiny lifeboat last in this fog anyway?
But you can't bring yourself to say no to Pylgia, who refuses to give up.
[Heavy Fog Effect]
The fog has already crept into the corridor, thicker here than outside. Emergency lights flicker disturbingly, like some dangerous signal luring you deeper into the ship's guts.
You clutch Pylgia's arm, refusing to let go for even a second. She's forced to clear the obstacles blocking the corridor with one free hand.
The thick fog is tinted red by the lights, blurring her silhouette. Metal groans now and then from the decks below, dredging up horrific memories that swarm your mind.

speaker: Pylgia
content: It's just metal breaking from fatigue. Don't worry, there's no one down there.
Sensing your distress, Pylgia comforts you while struggling to clear the path. For some reason, her voice sounds far away.
Inexplicably, a crushing wave of frustration and helplessness rises in your chest, and before you can stop it, a question you've been holding back for days finally breaks free.

options: How can you still keep going?

content: Pylgia stops what she's doing. After a long moment, she slowly begins to speak, her voice hazy in the thick air.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Because you're still alive... Because you're important to me.

speaker: Pylgia
content: You're the one...who saved me from the Abyss. When I wanted to give up, you... gave me the will to live again...

speaker: Pylgia
content: My life, my body... it no longer belongs to me alone. It's something we fought for together. I can't just throw it away.
[The thick fog intensifies, Pylgia's portrait changes to a more blurred version (either white or black is okay).]

speaker: Pylgia
content: So... if you need it now... I want to be... the person you can lean on...

speaker: Pylgia
content: ...The cargo hold is just ahead. Come on, stay close to me.
She turns and waves, her smile melting into the swirling fog.
You lose track of how long you've been in the lower decks.
For two amateurs, repairing a lifeboat proves a near-impossible task. Your progress is painfully slow.
Sometimes, you catch glimpses of a taciturn mechanic's face, only to realize it's just a hallucination. If she were here, these problems would be solved effortlessly.
The next moment, you find yourself desperately wishing they were all here. At least these problems would be easy.

speaker: Pylgia
content: I'll check the boiler room... hopefully there's some coal left.

speaker: Pylgia
content: If we're lucky, I might find some food in the rooms nearby. Or at least something edible...
The food and fuel you brought down are long gone. Prolonged hunger and cold have drained your last strength, yet you still force yourself to stay awake.
You're so weak that your mind is clouded. You barely register what Pylgia is saying.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Rest well, save some strength. I'll be right back.
[Cut to Black Screen]

You can't remember how long you've stayed in the darkness, or if you even slept. But when you open your eyes, the familiar warmth beside you is gone. There's no power, no fuel, only a chilling darkness.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Pylgia...? Are you... there?
[Metal Pipe Clang 1]
No answer. In the deathly silence, you only hear the distant, muffled crack of metal breaking.
You finally remember what Pylgia told you, that she was going to the boiler room to search for fuel and food.
But isn't it taking too long?
[Metal Pipe Clang 2]
The wait in the dark stretches on forever.
You have nothing else to do but think and remember... The horrific, nightmarish memories, and beneath them, the lurking truths that you dare not confront.
The metallic clanging is getting closer.
[Metal Pipe Clang 3]
The metal clanging outside gets louder. You can no longer ignore it.
You're certain it's not a hallucination. Mixed in with the racket, you can hear the sounds of water and footsteps.
Those sounds grow louder, closer, until they come to an abrupt stop right at the door.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Pyl...gia? Is that you?
There's no reply. Perhaps your voice is too weak.
But then you hear it. Something latching onto the door. A terror unlike anything you've ever known seizes your heart.
Who is standing out there...?
[Red screen effect, followed by black screen for 3 seconds]
Nothing happens.
The sounds are gone. The metallic clanging, the water, the footsteps... you can't hear any of them anymore.
You open your eyes. The door to the cargo hold is ajar. But outside, there's nothing there.
After that day, Pylgia never came back.
You leave the cargo hold and head down the corridor toward the boiler room, searching for any sign of her.
Fog is everywhere. The faint blue glow from your earring is the only light you have. You wade alone through the flooded passages, calling her name again and again.
The only answer is the sound of distant waves.
[Black Screen Transition]
Hope slowly dies in the cold seawater.
You wander through a maze of passages, past one empty room after another, searching every dark corner.
Your throat is hoarse; you can't manage another sound. The fog corrodes what's left of your mind, leaving only a numb, hollow shell.
In the end, only instinct drives you onward in mechanical, meaningless repetition, searching the endless dark for a companion who no longer exists.
The blue light hasn't flickered in a very long time.
[Black Screen Transition]
An unknown obsession has taken root in your heart.
You can no longer hear Schorl, but you don't feel lost. The Abyss extends into a vast emptiness, echoing with nothing but your own persistence.
In your absurdly long search, you finally begin to realize that <color=#fb9259>you are going down</color>.
The passages and cabins from your memory are stretched, twisted, and reassembled, merging together in grotesque ways. No matter how far you walk, you can't find an exit back to the upper decks.
<color=#fb9259>You are heading into the Abyss.</color>
Your legs have soaked in seawater for so long that they've grown swollen and heavy, like rotting wood in a swamp that could crumble at any moment.
Then, your body begins to rot. Your spine can barely support your weight, and you tumble to the ground.
Cold seawater flows over you, dissolving your body and consciousness. Soon, you'll melt into a puddle of shapeless ichor, just like...
Just like what happened to them. To your companions.
Are you going to give up here?
Your fists furiously slam into the ground, the pain bringing your mind back to clarity as the bodily hallucinations recede like a tide.
Just as Shin said, the source of it all is down there. How could you possibly run? Even if it means death, you have to face the truth.
The fog has lifted without you noticing, and a pale gray figure stands at a corner not far away. You can't make out her face, but her silhouette and voice feel achingly familiar.
Well done, child... You have managed to overcome despair.
I believe you can reach the deeper truths.
She disappears at the end of the passage.
You snap back to consciousness. Scrambling through the water, you chase after her.
You round the corner, and more shadows surround you.

speaker: Anxious Shadow
content: Don't go there... Don't go!

speaker: Anxious Shadow
content: You'll be devoured... You'll become a monster...

speaker: Option
options: Every passerby wears a genuine smile, their eyes bright with hope for tomorrow.
