content: You wade through the murky shadows. They reach for you with desperate hands, blocking your path uselessly, only to be torn apart by your slightest touch.
Before a sealed door, a sorrowful shadow waits.

speaker: Sorrowful Shadow
content: I was wrong...
She seems to be confessing, or waiting. Confessing her stubbornness and prejudice; waiting for a child who will never again respond to her unspoken love.

speaker: Sorrowful Shadow
content: I was so foolish... I loved you so much... You were... the best child in the world...

speaker: Sorrowful Shadow
content: But I just... I just...

speaker: Sorrowful Shadow
content: I didn't want you to be a hero... I didn't want you to carry this... weight... I just wanted you...

speaker: Sorrowful Shadow
content: ...to live...
The sorrowful shadow blurs, and with her weeping, melts into the darkness.
Two shadows are locked in struggle at the center of the room.
One appears to be holding some kind of weapon, hacking at the other shadow again and again.

speaker: Furious Shadow
content: It's all your fault! Why?!

speaker: Furious Shadow
content: You got everyone killed! I couldn't protect them... It's all your fault!
No matter how deadly, his attacks are all in vain.
The deranged shadow is shredded, only to reform moments later. The slaughter has repeated countless times, until your arrival.
Only when you draw closer do you hear his frenzied whispers amid the roars and destruction.

speaker: Deranged Shadow
content: There's no escape... She planned it all... It was over... the moment we stepped onboard...

speaker: Deranged Shadow
content: The Abyss is among us... It's too late...

speaker: Deranged Shadow
content: We're all going to... die...

speaker: Weary Shadow
content: That's not the right direction... You're wrong... We're all wrong...
A shadow leans feebly against a door that feels painfully familiar.
Old and weary, he is the last keeper of the ship, guarding the door with pointless determination.

speaker: Weary Shadow
content: ...This intuition... it's saved me many times... Trust me... we can't walk to our doom like this...
As you draw closer, the shadow's neck suddenly bursts open, gushing liquid darkness.
He spins around, mustering his last strength to grab something, and lunges at you on pure reflex.
But when he sees what's before him, you feel the crushing shock and despair from the depths of his soul, even though his features are obscured.

speaker: Weary Shadow
content: Why... you... What do you... want to do?!
Life drains from him. He collapses in exhaustion, his body dissolving.

speaker: Weary Shadow
content: Whatever... None of it matters anymore...

speaker: Weary Shadow
content: There's nothing left on this ship... worth staying for...
The shadow vanishes without another sound. The path forward is now clear.
Every murky shadow tells a tragic end.
The malice from the Abyss, the true culprit of the tragedy, the truth you've long suspected but dared not—would not—confront... It's enough. You've seen more than enough.
But you will go on. You must go on.
Blinding white light floods your vision. You find yourself on an unfamiliar, clear azure sea.
Spacing out?
A white shadow extends a hand. Unlike the murky shadows you met before, this one is hollow. A puppet performing scripted scenes regardless of your response.
I know this is your first time at sea. It's natural to feel a little scared.
But don't worry. We have the wisest scholars with us, the bravest captain and sailors on these seas.
The torch of human civilization is in our hands... We'll solve the mystery of the disaster and bring a future full of hope.
[Scene Change]
In the biting winds, civilization and humanity—love and hope—proved so fragile.
"Future" became a joke. In the brutal present, survival was the only problem to solve.
It was a blizzard no one saw coming. No scholar could explain how, at summer's end, the research vessel became trapped by sea ice. Everyone was stranded.
Four long months passed. No rescue, not even a word from the outside world. Supplies long exhausted, hunger turned the finest of humanity into the most primitive of beasts.
The same hands meant to hold "the torch of human civilization" were now covered in fine bite marks.
This is a necessary sacrifice.
They spoke these words while slurping the last drops of marrow from finger bones.
...He's already dead. There's nothing we can do to change that.
Be rational, my child. We have... no other choice.
[Scene transition, a mental space]
She was the most rational of them all.
She had a deceptively gentle façade and the foresight to see things through. Patiently, she waited as bloodthirsty instincts consumed every soul less rational than she was.
She witnessed the entirety of the bloody feast, yet remained true only to herself. And thus, effortlessly, she survived to the end.
Then, she beheld the final prize.
From the desperate madness of her former companions, upon their corpses bereft of sanity or reason, a strange new life was born, glimmering with a radiance entirely alien to humankind.
That was the Apostle they spoke of—and the one true goal of their voyage.

speaker: Shin
content: It is a species far more beautiful than humanity.

speaker: Shin
content: It accepted everything, absorbed everything. Empty ideals, pretentious virtues, or the most primitive fear and despair... It embraced them all.
You don't know when the pale gray figure you've been chasing appeared silently by your side.
Shin, the expedition's oceanographer, the woman synonymous with compassion, understanding, leadership... all those positive words.
Now that you see her again, she's no different from when you first met her. Calm, patient, confident, like the perfect mother one could only find in a storybook.
But you know she's nothing like the woman you met on the ship. You take a wary step back.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Was this your true purpose all along? Did you... KILL them?

speaker: Shin
content: When I joined this expedition, I expected to see a repeat of the past, the same drama of betrayal and slaughter I remembered from before.

speaker: Shin
content: But things were different this time.

speaker: Shin
content: Everyone on the crew... Dreya, Marguerite, Vanilla, Pylgia... even the two children who guided us on the way... everyone on the ship was so brave, strong, and rational.

speaker: Shin
content: Without their efforts, we never would have come so close to the truth. In them, I saw that humanity still carried a spark.

speaker: Shin
content: And that's precisely why I find it so regrettable.
[Insert special effects + more intense BGM + Shin changes pose or form]

speaker: Shin
content: You had the courage to come this far, to stand before the greatest of truths, to witness a more powerful form of life and new possibilities for evolution. One more step, and you could transcend the narrow confines of human perception.

speaker: Shin
content: Why do you insist on covering your eyes and shackling your feet?

speaker: Shin
content: Why cling so stubbornly to the concept of humanity? You embark on this journey, merely to understand the Perishing Star so you can fight it; so that humanity can endure to pit their feeble flesh against greater beings.

speaker: Shin
content: Why not cross that line? Why not abandon your weakness and become a grander form of life?
Even though you'd guessed the truth, hearing her say it aloud hits you with a nauseating chill so intense it's almost unreal.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You let the monsters into the ship...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You assigned everyone's tasks, pushing their minds to breaking points.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You drew its gaze to this ship. You misled me into searching for land that never existed.

speaker: Shin
content: Yes. It gazed upon this ship, and every soul aboard.

speaker: Shin
content: It embraced them, welcomed them into its vastness... But they were ungrateful. They were terrified. They fought desperately to escape, even tried to harm it.

speaker: Shin
content: A pity, but thankfully, things turned out as they should have. Except...

speaker: Shin
content: Only I...
She covers her face, as if about to weep.

speaker: Shin
content: Every one of them was chosen. Every one of them earned its gaze.

speaker: Shin
content: Why am I the only one left behind?

speaker: Shin
content: I worked so hard to plan everything. I arranged every detail, just to reach it. But in the end, I'm the only one left behind, unable to reach the other side.

speaker: Shin
content: What am I still missing?

speaker: Shin
content: You can give me the answer, can't you, my little guide?
You stare at her smile, fists clenched. She's still smiling, like always, like a gentle, patient mother.

speaker: Shin
content: Because you don't need my help. You don't need to abandon anything, or even endure physical death, to arrive at this place.

speaker: Shin
content: I never misled you. It was your will that brought everyone here.
She crouches down and strokes your hair. Her soft touch and tender words, once so comforting, now stir your deepest fears.

speaker: Shin
content: After all, <color=#fb9259>you came from the other side</color>.

speaker: Shin
content: Take me to it, my little guide. Only you know the way.
The false ocean melts away like fresh snow, and warm, damp chaos returns in its place.
And with it, her human disguise is torn away.
Countless slimy tentacles writhe and coil from behind her, beneath her dress, all around you, seizing you before you can even struggle.

speaker: Shin
content: From the moment I first saw you, I knew you didn't belong here.

speaker: Shin
content: You may be unaware of it, but I know. There's an unbreakable umbilical cord connecting you to it. You're the agent of its will, an angel walking among men...

speaker: Shin
content: Every time I held you, I felt myself embracing the Abyss. That feeling... it was so hard to let go.
Soft biomass flows across her features, and you can no longer see her eyes.
Her fingertips brush across your face as she lets out a long sigh.

speaker: Shin
content: I don't know why you forgot the Abyss, why you chose to stand with humanity. But look... you suffered so much pain and fear on this journey. All because you resist, because you're fixated on loss and sacrifice.

speaker: Shin
content: Let me guide you.
The tentacles tighten, suffocating you.
You try to struggle, but they seal your mouth and nose, binding your limbs.

speaker: Shin
content: In the outside world, we're as weak as ants. But in this new world brought by the Perishing Star, all our inner frailties and shadows will be accepted, shaped into something beautiful and strong—Apostles born in the forbidden zone from emotions in the collective subconscious of humanity.

speaker: Shin
content: Don't grieve, don't fear. The crew is waiting for you on the other side, in new forms, as higher beings...

speaker: Shin
content: And you... you have always been closer to the Abyss than anyone. If you open your mind to the cycle and evolution of life, to your origin and destiny... if you let go of your fear, accept it, embrace it... you'll become the greatest of all the transcended...

Her voice, her burning breath, fills the small prison of tentacles.
You try to struggle, to bite, to kick, to tear yourself free.
But Shin restrains your every move. You feel your soul consumed by anger, but more than that, fear.

speaker: Shin
content: This... must be <color=#fb9259>LOVE</color>.

speaker: Shin
content: See? An emotion that I tried so hard to deny and conceal when I was human, now spoken so easily after transcendence.
In Shin's impossibly warm embrace, you feel your body... melting.

speaker: Mira
content: I once wanted to let you go, to let you leave this place... What was it that stopped you from going back?

speaker: Shin
content: Well, it doesn't matter anymore... This is the guidance of fate. You and I were destined to meet again.

speaker: Shin
content: And this time, I won't let you go.
The ringing in your ears drowns out her whispers. Everything that was you rapidly dissolves—the expedition team, humanity's fate, your existence and memories...
Until at last, only endless darkness and crimson remain.
[Scene, Abyss] (Black scene is sufficient)
You are falling.
Your body is melting, your mind blending into the black Abyss.
A strange sense of comfort fills you with a deeper dread.
It was you who led the crew into the Abyss. They trusted you, depended on you, and you delivered them into the Abyss's maw.
You didn't want to do this.
You never want to, so why... Deep down, are you really connected to the Perishing Star...
Countless red lights appear before your eyes, their dying screams echoing in your ears.
The red light tears through a corner of the Abyss. Through the filthy, twisted ripples, you see a distant Illusory Moon. A familiar, eerie laughter rings in the depths of your mind.

Hehe. You should've listened to me from the start. I invited you, offered you my power. You could've devoured it by becoming me, but you... you're always so stubborn. So arrogant. So sure of yourself. Yet when it matters most, you falter...
That's why you couldn't even defeat that half-dead wretch... You were crushed...
The shackles shatter, and the vortex below sucks you in. Abyssal filth overwhelms your vision, blocking the light. As its laughter fades, the Illusory Moon vanishes too.
You reach out, struggling with all your strength, and several twisted figures coalesce from the chaos.
[Corrupted DisSea group portraits with black gradient]
They look so familiar, so comforting. They reach out to you...
Many hands seize you at once, clawing up your arms, licking and tearing at your skin, yearning to merge with you, to become one.

speaker: Companions
content: I don't want to die...! You're our guide! Take us back!!
You scream in terror, but no sound comes. You try to flee, but in your path stands a woman, arms wide open, pulling you into her embrace.
She holds you tight, shielding you from every attack, soothing your fear with gentle whispers. Her voice trembles with ecstatic joy.
It's alright, don't be afraid. You have always been closer to the Abyss than anyone. Don't fear the unknown, don't fear sacrifice.
This is the guidance of fate. You and I were destined to meet again. This is its greatest gift to me... Come, my guide, let us go together...
Only YOU know the way back.
You are It...
Create a proper earring pendant visual effect; the previous ones were all terrible. Use an earring image or small model, whatever works, just make a decent one.
[Sound effect: a single piano note, see if there's any classical/thematic note available, stretch it out—]
[White flash] Full black screen, 2 seconds, pay attention to sound effects, add ambient sound of an empty environment without music.
You are consumed.
Or perhaps you've fallen through a rift.
There is no light. No sound. No one. You feel no ground beneath your feet, no walls, no ceiling. You're suspended, adrift in a vacuum, or the deep sea, or...
[Faint piano sound, slow, distant, emphasize the sound effect]
The notes are pensive and far away, like the sigh of a long-lost friend. You pull yourself up shakily and follow the sound...
[Fade to full white screen, exit after 1 second]
You follow the music through the Abyss, walking through an endless void until you lose track of time.
When you finally stop, you see it: a piano not far away. An ordinary piano, the kind you'd imagine when you hear its sound.
But the melody... it feels so familiar, so dear. You would never forget the tune, even if your consciousness were reduced to dust.
You want to take a step closer, to see who's playing, but your feet refuse to move. As if humans can only come this far, and no further.
But the pianist senses your presence. The music stops. He looks up, toward you.
A pure white silhouette. A... person you cannot discern.

speaker: White Figure
content: ...Why are you here? I told you I would stay. You don't need to come looking...
He stops. He gazes in your direction for a long while.

speaker: White Figure
content: ...I mistook you for someone else. I thought you were ■■.

speaker: White Figure
content: Are you lost?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I want to go back, but...
You open your mouth, but no sound comes out. Your body trembles as a force presses on your throat. It isn't from this void, but from within you...

You watch as every vein in your body swells and burns red, your boiling blood growling like a wild thing trying to burst free. You watch as your skin stretches taut, cells crisscrossing into frigid blue grids, every triangle cold and precise, sealing everything like a coffin.
You never knew such terrifying forces dwelled within you. What chills you to the bone is how they're tearing you apart, pulling you in two different directions, and you can't control either one.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...How do I go back?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Back... to where?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: After going back... what will I become?
The figure watches you being ripped apart. He says nothing, doesn't move. After a long moment, he turns impassively back to the piano keys, like he's contemplating what to play next.

speaker: White Figure
content: ...Who knows? That's your problem.
He raises his hands.

speaker: White Figure
content: You have to find your own answers.
[Sound effect, followed by faint red light effect]

He presses a black key. A jolt runs through your body as your heart starts pounding forcefully in your chest, drowning out the roaring in your blood. It beats steady and fierce, the heat gathering in your palms before pulsing back through your veins, rejoining your circulation.
Next, he presses a white key.
[Sound effect, followed by faint blue light effect]

The ice coating your skin melts away, the patterns receding toward your head. The terror subsides, and you realize there's nothing here to fear. Clarity returns to your thoughts, forming your name, coalescing into your swaying earring.
You look up at him again. Through his ethereal white glow, you glimpse a smile, strange, yet somehow familiar.

speaker: White Figure
content: Don't be afraid. They've always been a part of you. Learn to use them, then find your own way.

speaker: White Figure
content: Find the answers yourself. No one can make your choices for you.
The man bows his head; the question seems to require a great deal of thought. You can hear the space around you beginning to crack.
Red and blue seep into the pure white domain, breaking it apart. The piano and the man, the only things untouched, drift farther away. He seems to give up on his thoughts and smiles at you.

speaker: White Figure
content: ...I suppose it's time to go back. It was good to see you, ${PlayerName}.
The next moment, countless rays of light burst from the cracks, engulfing the piano and the man who helped you.
The pure white illusion shatters, and time resumes its course. You leave the rift, returning to the flow of time.
Brilliant red light blazes in your hands, turning into numerous sharp spikes that slice through the tentacles entangling you.
The tentacles don't yield, but in the next moment, their assault is deflected by a radiant blue light.

speaker: Shin
content: Hmm? What's that?
Despite you severing her tentacles and breaking free, Shin shows no sign of anger.
Now, with light dispelling the darkness, you finally see her true form. At the center of writhing tentacles, the woman still stands with elegant poise.
Countless pupils gaze at you, at your earring and shackles. For the first time, something resembling intrigue and apprehension crosses her corrupted face.

speaker: Shin
content: They can tear through my domain... Wherever that power comes from, it is deeper than the Abyss we know... They're dangerous.

speaker: Shin
content: Be a good child and give them to me, won't you?
She holds out a hand, her voice a gentle murmur as she approaches step by step.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Dangerous? Good.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It takes a dangerous power to kill a monster like you.

speaker: Shin
content: A monster?
She gives a bitter, disappointed smile.

speaker: Shin
content: When ants look upon humans, they must think the same thing... What a shame. I thought you would understand.

speaker: Shin
content: But it doesn't matter... It's an adult's responsibility to show a lost child the way.
Beyond the blue barrier, a dense mass of tentacles writhes and coils, ignoring the shackles' strikes and trying to breach your small sanctuary.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Sorry, but I was born a rebel.

speaker: Shin
content: Do you feel no fear?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Of course I do. But it's in facing fear that we find courage, and the will to fight.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I can tell you that in the future, humanity never reaches the "enlightenment" you're hoping for. A hundred years from now, your god hasn't conquered everything as you wished.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The way I see it, strength isn't about power, or species, or form. It's the will to always follow your heart and make your own choice.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Just like you chose to betray humanity, I'm choosing to seek the truth with my own eyes and decide where I stand by my own will.
Red and blue converge once more, forming a pillar of light that impales the heavens.
You know that no matter how far away, your final companion, the one cut off from this darkness, will know where you are.
[Special Effect Big CG Insert]
[Special Effect Big CG Insert]
A pale figure descends from the sky, her sharp harpoon ripping through the darkness and severing dozens of tentacles in its wake.
Monstrous appendages sprout from her body, her near-transparent skin glowing gently in the chaotic darkness.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Sorry I'm late.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No, I'm the one who should apologize.
Seeing Pylgia's inhuman form once again fills you with warmth and sadness.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I let fear get the better of me. That's why I was dragged in here... Thank you for saving me again.

speaker: Pylgia
content: ...Don't mention it. We're companions.
You and Pylgia stand together. To leave this place, there's only one thing left to do.
Defeat the monster blocking your way. Defeat...
Shin.
Shin's power is immense, but she isn't the Abyss itself. She can't inflict upon you the deepest despair, the kind you've already endured once before.
As the red light of your shackles impales her abdomen, through the wound you had bandaged yourself, her body is pinned to the ground, her tentacles thrashing wildly in vain.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Looks like humanity won this time.
The filth slowly recedes from her face, and you see those sea-blue eyes once more.
But this time, she looks at Pylgia, then at you, before breaking into a sardonic smile.

speaker: Shin
content: Humanity...? Hahaha...

speaker: Shin
content: You... you two... you're perhaps the furthest thing from humans in this world.
She gazes at the red and blue light around you, laughing derisively.

speaker: Shin
content: This inconceivable power of yours is proof enough.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No.
Your denial is swift and resolute. You know power. You've wielded many kinds—some yours, some not—and because of this, you know one thing with perfect clarity.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm merely using it. I'm not tempted by it. I'll never deny my worth as a human... just for the sake of power.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Whatever its source, in human hands, power is just a means to achieve our goals.
Her tentacles make a last-ditch attempt to strike, but Pylgia notices and pins them to the ground with her harpoon.
In the red light of the shackles, her tentacles continue to dissolve, her body disintegrating.
As the tentacles of her god are about to abandon her, she finally shows a rare expression of fear.

speaker: Shin
content: No... wait...
She reaches desperately for the retreating tentacles, only to watch them melt into black ichor.

speaker: Shin
content: Wait! Please, don't leave me!

speaker: Pylgia
content: Watch out!
At her plea, you see the crumbling tentacles pause. Then, they suddenly reverse course, surging frantically back into her body!
If Pylgia hadn't shielded you, you would have been swept up in the retaliating tentacles.
But it seems Shin wasn't trying to attack you.
The torrent of tentacles rushes into her body, just like... what happened to the crew on the ship.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Careful, she's... fusing... with the Abyss...
Through the wild thrashing of tentacles, you barely make out Shin's voice.

speaker: Shin
content: Ah... ah... So... that's how it is...

speaker: Shin
content: It would not accept me... because I never truly felt fear... or sorrow...

speaker: Shin
content: Then I must thank these two children... for granting me... true fear.

speaker: Shin
content: Yes... I am afraid. Afraid of living out a human life in mediocrity, unable to reach my ultimate ideal.
[Use Phase 3 art as CG? Preferably with some motion, some camera movement.]

Shin lifts her head, dark ichor streaking down her face. Although the wounds from your shackles haven't healed, you can sense an unmistakable shift in her. She's completely different from the foe you just fought.
From her emanates a pressure that could overwhelm the entire ocean, just like...
Just like that monster from the Abyss.

speaker: Shin
content: Thank you, my little guide... Thanks to you...

speaker: Shin
content: I finally... reached...
Pylgia decisively steps in front of you.

speaker: Pylgia
content: She's fused... with that thing. No... we can't beat her. I'll hold her off, you have to get out.
But Shin shakes her head.

speaker: Shin
content: No need to be alarmed, children. You've helped me, and for that, you have my sincerest gratitude. Now, all I want is to return to its side.

speaker: Shin
content: Besides, I think... the reason you exist... is because it, too, wants to touch humanity. It wants to understand... So, you must keep trying.

speaker: Shin
content: Go. Understand, comprehend, experience... When the time is right, I will personally return from the Abyss... to welcome you.
Her body slowly sinks into the darkness, leaving only a pair of pale blue eyes that watch you with the same gentle warmth as before.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'll defeat you again, no matter how many times it takes... I'll protect everything I love, until I've destroyed the source of your existence...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...the it you keep speaking of.

speaker: Shin
content: ...Is that so?
In this moment, something you've never seen before passes over her disappearing face: confusion and sorrow.

speaker: Shin
content: I shall be... looking forward... to that... day...
With those final words, her eyes dissolve into the wind.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Cough...!
You're pulled out of the water. It takes a long time to readjust after leaving the deep sea. The air is so unfamiliar it's almost suffocating.

Your last remaining companion keeps you afloat. She slowly parts the waters, pulling over some floating debris and pushing you on top of it with her last bit of strength. She cups your face with both hands, keeping you from slipping back under the waves.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Hold on tight, don't let go... It's over now.
Pylgia tries to give you some warmth, but her skin is as cold as the sea. Her touch is your anchor, connecting you to a world you are sensing anew.
The Illusory Moon is gone. A gray, overcast sky hangs low, pressing down against the leaden sea. Cold, briny. Your senses return one by one to the rocking of the waves.
The nightmare is over. You have escaped the Abyss.

speaker: Pylgia
content: ...Yes, we're back.
She grasps your hand and forces a wan smile.
Then, you hear a distant shout.

speaker: Distant Figure
content: Hey—! Can you hear us?
A small boat appears on the rolling waves. Someone's waving frantically. You can't make out their face, but you know...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...It's the expedition team... They found us, we're saved...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Pylgia... we can go home. Together...
The hand you're clutching suddenly feels wrong. Cold and soft, almost boneless. This is not the hand of a human.
At some point, her skin has turned transparent again, veins visible underneath. Coral-like tendrils branch from her body, swaying gently with the waves.
And below the surface, the dark waters conceal her shifting form.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No... It's not supposed to be like this... We both made it back, so why won't she let you go?! Is it Shin? Is this her doing again?!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Pylgia, hold onto me! Don't go! We escaped the Abyss together, it won't control you!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're human! You have friends, they're coming for you now!! Don't listen to her!
I told you I'd be back...
Pylgia looks at you, then at her own body. At last, she raises her arms and wraps you in her embrace.

speaker: Pylgia
content: ...It's alright... I know who I am, and it won't drag me down. This is my own choice...

speaker: Pylgia
content: I'm choosing this body. It's the only way I can slip quietly into the Abyss... to bring our companions home...

speaker: Pylgia
content: Do you remember them? You don't want them to be trapped in the dark forever, do you...?
[Flashback Sequence]
You remember the ones imprisoned in the Abyss.

Not the fanatic Shin, but the others... the ones who, even after endless torment, after losing their bodies, their voices, their dignity and reason, still fought to awaken you from your trance. The ones who exhausted everything they had to give you a ray of light.
They boarded that ship of death, setting sail for the Abyss to rescue you and Pylgia, lost at sea. They knew nothing of what awaited them, and even if they had, they would never have regretted it.
Neither you nor Pylgia could ever abandon them.
You're still for a long moment, before slowly raising your hands to hold Pylgia tight. You don't want to let go, but you know... this is farewell.

speaker: Option
options: Can they... can they still be saved?

speaker: Pylgia
content: Of course... They're so strong, they fought so hard. You saw it... They just need someone to lend them a hand. I'm the best choice.

speaker: Pylgia
content: It's too dangerous. We both know it wants you more than anyone else. Your presence would only excite it, and that would make things harder.

speaker: Option
options: Then I'll let the others know.

speaker: Pylgia
content: If you tell them, they'll get worried. They'll come after me. And I don't want to lose anyone else...
Her pale smile becomes infinitely gentle. As if in response to you, her inhuman skin gains a touch of warmth, like a final comfort, a reluctant farewell.

speaker: Pylgia
content: Don't be afraid, my child... This time, no matter what I become, no matter where I'm taken, I'll never forget where I belong, and I won't give up on returning to my companions.

speaker: Pylgia
content: ...Because you've already shown me the way home. I've walked that path once. I won't forget it again. And I'll never be alone.

speaker: Pylgia
content: I'll bring them back, just like you brought me back. When I do... you'll be there to welcome me home, won't you?

speaker: Pylgia
content: Now... my brave guide, lend me your courage, and wish me... a safe journey.

speaker: Option
options: I'll come for you... Wait for me.

content: [Scene darkens, 2 seconds] Process sound effects

Her hands tighten one last time, then suddenly let go. The waves give a gentle push, and you're taken away from her warm embrace. The cold sea wind jolts your eyes open. The dream shatters. Before you, the surface of the ocean is empty, the waves having erased every trace of hers.
The debris carries you on, until you fall into the arms of others.

speaker: Rescue Team
content: Got you!

speaker: Rescue Team
content: Good heavens, what are you doing out here alone? Don't you know how dangerous this place is? The sea's claimed enough lives! You're our important guide. What if something happened to you?

speaker: Option
options: I... the Deep Dive unit, they...

content: The rescue team pauses, exchanging glances. Their expressions grow heavy, and they struggle to find their words.

speaker: Rescue Team
content: So it was for Shin and the others...

speaker: Rescue Team
content: Listen, ${PlayerName}, the truth is...
[Background slowly darkens]
You're brought back to shore and awakened by Schorl. But for the next several nights, until the Illusory Moon tide fully recedes, you find yourself dreaming of this place.
Here, you see the small station built by the expedition's Deep Dive unit. You learn...
[Slowly fade to black]

During the third week of an Illusory Moon cycle, Deep Dive Unit One was conducting a routine mission to retrieve equipment when they encountered an accident. Three divers—Pylgia, Ragnar, and Dale—lost contact.
Two days after Unit One went missing, Deep Dive Unit Two departed on a rescue mission. Seven days later, their vessel lost contact. The entire crew of eleven, including their leader, Professor Shin, never returned. Multiple rescue attempts by other teams were fruitless.

One month later, all fourteen members of the Deep Dive units were declared dead.

The Deep Dive station, having lost its equipment, vessels, and most importantly, its people, was abandoned.
The expedition team erected a memorial beside the station, carving on the tombstone the names of the Deep Dive unit members.

Their sacrifice serves as a warning:
The time has not yet come.
Do NOT chase the Illusory Moon.
Do NOT approach the Abyss.
Only the young guide refused to accept the truth. He insisted that he could hear the Deep Dive unit's voices, that Pylgia was still searching for her companions, that they would all come home.
female_content: Only the young guide refused to accept the truth. She insisted that she could hear the Deep Dive unit's voices, that Pylgia was still searching for her companions, that they would all come home.

content: ...Every day, he went to the leaden shore, waiting beside his companions' graves for the departed to return.
female_content: ...Every day, she went to the leaden shore, waiting beside her companions' graves for the departed to return.

content: [Fade in to Small CG 1]
You keep watch at the station and find that woman's notes.
The journal is filled with arcane language and theory, enigmatic models and formulas, too complex for ordinary minds.
Perhaps it also hides a madness beyond normal perception.
[Small CG 2, Focus on Tombstone]
Or perhaps all of this is just a nightmare fabricated by the Illusory Moon to deceive you.
Perhaps... somewhere in your subconscious, you want those days of darkness, that crushing despair... to be nothing but a dream. Something conjured by your proximity to the Abyss.
Everything before you grows thin. This tide cycle is nearing its end. Next time, you'll wake in another corner of history.
Just as you think this, the comms device in the small shack crackles to life.
[Static sound effect]
Uh... her notes? I'm not sure. Maybe you guys should...
Okay then. I'll just grab whatever I find. You guys can figure it out.
The voice gets closer. It's not coming from the radio, but...
[Small CG 3] Medium Shot
Someone's coming up the slope. A young man with wild hair that looks like a messy bird's nest.
He stumbles as he walks.
It's way too complicated. I don't understand it. You guys find the answers. I...
[Small CG 4] Allow sufficient pause time
[Pause 1s]
[Small CG 5] Pause for two seconds, sound of ocean waves
This is your first meeting after a long goodbye. As the Illusory Moon fades, your consciousness recedes.
[Screen dims]
Until the very end, you never get a clear look at his face.
Since your last dream, the Illusory Moon's tidal cycle has shifted. It's a subtle change, yet regardless of such intricacies, it has returned.
And you, beneath the Illusory Moon, plunge into the dream once more.

Your consciousness sinks, slowly descending into an unseen embrace that feels less like welcome and more like consumption. Then, a foul, damp stench intrudes your nostrils—the brine of sea, the cloying thickness of blood that will never dry.
The remains of a city, or rather... a city's dream. How beautiful.
From the depths of darkness, a voice drifts toward you, so familiar it turns your stomach.
The world sharpens. Derelict buildings sprawl before you, their hollow frames leaning into twisted, unending streets.
And there, among the ruins, stands that woman. Her gaze finds you, tender as a wound.
The moment the words leave your mouth, their meaning slips away from you. Were you affirming her reality... or giving shape to the feelings she stirs within you?

speaker: Shin?
content: The origin of all, and the secrets of all...
As she murmurs, the ruined buildings around you shiver in a subtle tremor.
She tilts her head, as if listening to whispers meant for her alone. Behind you, the darkness contracts, tightening like a throat. Your retreat dissolves.
It takes so little. A few syllables in that familiar tone, and your fury blooms again, hot and helpless as ever.
Why am I here? What do you want? Is this another scheme of yours?!
Silence is her only reply. She turns and moves toward the distant bend, her steps striking the broken ground with a clarity that feels like an intrusion.
Her silhouette thins like smoke dispersing, and through its fading form, the ruins emerge: solid, yet wrong. Present, yet impossible.
Don't run from me!
Rage hurls you forward, fingers outstretched for that spectral form, but she dissolves before you arrive.

In the moment of her disappearance, her hand lifts one final time. A pointing finger, aimed at the labyrinth's core, where twisted ruins stand sentinel. It is not a warning. It is an invitation. Sincere.

speaker: Shin?
content: My dear, fate is guiding you. You are destined to return to the origin, to return to my side. Go and see the shape of truth...

speaker: Shin?
content: Now that you're here, don't be so eager to wake yet...

Beneath your feet, the ground speaks: hard, cold, rough with the texture of years untouched. Dilapidated walls lean within arm's reach, their facades long stripped away to reveal stonework sealed for ages.

Decay varies from structure to structure, yet every collapsed doorframe hangs frozen mid-swing as if pushed open in desperate haste. Every shattered window faces the same direction. Through those hollow gaps, you see the quiet debris of ordinary lives.
If this is Maria City, where the Perishing Star fell, then the disaster struck in an instant. The people here tried to flee the moment it happened. But...
You cross a fallen doorframe and step inside. Dimness swallows you. The air is stagnant, thick with dust that hangs suspended, as though even time refuses to let it settle.
Tables and chairs keep their positions, patient as mourners. But the tableware has abandoned them, scattered across the floor in fragments.
On the wall, a damaged clock points to a frozen hour. It is not alone. On tables, inside cabinets, tucked into corners—every timepiece you find has stopped. All at once. All at the same moment.
The street constricts with each step, buildings leaning inward like conspirators ready to seal their trap. Then, without warning, the space exhales, opening wide again.

The layout shifts without reason, but the stench only deepens: rotting, briny, suffocating. Drag marks score the ground in every direction. They seem chaotic at first, but on closer look, they all point the same way.
You attempt to stop, but the <color=#fb9259>silence</color> has already stopped you first. No footsteps. No breath. Only the damp kiss of mist against your skin.
The moment you sense it, the ruins ahead begin to move.
Shadows writhe within them, contorting into shapes that almost resemble human forms. Hollow faces twist in what should be screams. But there is only silence.
Then the wave takes form. They surge together, a torrent of forgotten things, and rush forward to swallow you whole.
You elude them at last—the shambling things that hunt these ruins. But the air remains troubled, thick with currents you cannot name.
The earth itself has forgotten its solidity. It moves beneath you now, like some viscous liquid.
Something inside you finally gives. The shattered streets lift and turn before your eyes, rearranging themselves with terrible purpose—an invisible architect completing its design.
Your legs forget their strength. You fall. And the darkness welcomes you home.
[Fade Out] Switch to Inner World
Time loses itself. When you finally wake, mist wraps everything—a veil between you and the world that was.

The scene breathes familiarity, but wrong. Broken doorframes sink into black mire, their surfaces now etched with uncanny patterns. Fallen signposts rise like craggy peaks. The concrete beneath you has dissolved into flagstones stretching endlessly. And within the fog, phosphorescence flickers.
At the corner you just passed, phantoms gather. Clusters of them. Standing still. Vacant.
Before you can comprehend, the phantoms converge. They drift toward you as one, bodies pressing together, mouths spilling familiar murmurs that coil through the air.
[Raise the field of view, and add some red visual effects.]
You step back. They rise to meet you in all directions. The ground births them, the fog exhales them. And now they scream, a chorus of shrieks that drive into your skull like spikes.

speaker: Strange Phantoms
content: Welcome... Welcome... Welcome to □□□...

speaker: Strange Phantoms
content: You are... You are □□□□. To join... To join □□□□□, you must...
You turn and run. But the world is thick with them. Most merely exist, indifferent, unaware. Except—
Where they fall, they leave behind something worse. Phosphorescence pools. Stone cracks, weeping liquid light. And from the residue, limbs twist into malformed beings, shrieking as they lunge.
Then silence. The shrieking dies. The limbs dissolve. And you stand alone again, in this desolate world without end.

options: Try to find a way out

content: With every step, the world peels further from recognition. Flagstones wind beneath you. Crumbling monuments lean like tired sentinels. Grotesque statues line your path, their hideous faces repeating—one after another, after another—until your senses blur into numbness.
It feels like walking through a reflection. Maria City, yes, but seen through something that should not exist.
Then you see it. Among the rubble and dust, a copper coin on a red cord lies waiting.
You bend. Your fingers close around it. The moment skin touches metal, a bell chimes, crisp and sudden, echoing in your ears. The sound is soft, yet impossibly clear.
Is it... the coin?
Can you understand what I'm saying?
The copper coin offers no answer. You pat yourself down, searching for sense, wondering if this place has finally undone you.
You stare at it. A moment. Then another.
Whatever purpose it holds, whatever meaning hides in its stillness, you do not know. But your fingers close around it anyway. You clutch it tight. And you press onward.
A ruined stele appears without warning.

You step closer to examine it. Then the light begins. Crimson, vast, it spreads from beneath the stele like spilled blood finding its way. An ominous presence washes over you, rooting your feet to the ground.
Behind the stele, something moves. A massive, nameless figure crawls into view. Its back is turned to you, limbs twisted at wrong angles yet moving with horrifying grace.
Its neck begins to twist. Turning. Turning. Turning.
Then the eyes. Crimson. Glowing. Staring into you.
Your efforts find their mark. The red light explodes outward, and in that violent blossoming, the monster and the stele rupture together, vanishing as though they never were.
Rubble scatters. Beyond where the stele stood, a new place unfolds before you. You are certain you have never been here before.

You search the remnants carefully. The creature, you realize, was somehow bound to the stele, perishing the moment it shattered. And the red light's source turns out to be a crimson crystal flower, broken beneath the stone.
Before you can study it further, a sound drifts from somewhere distant. Another bell.
It echoes through the space, from somewhere far away.
Someone else? In this world? The question answers itself. There is only one way to know. You go.
You stop in your tracks. The space ahead fractures into nothing, the ruined street ending where a familiar stele stands.
Beneath it, red crystal petals bloom in impossible abundance. Crimson light fills the air, pulsing slow and steady, like a heart that has always beaten here.
From that sea of flowers, an aura reaches for you. It seizes something deep—the soul, perhaps.
Then the red crystals rupture. Before your eyes, their glow peels away, and with it, the presence that has coiled inside you since the beginning finally recedes.
You are waking now. Leaving this world. Leaving the nightmare behind.
You almost step forward. Then your periphery catches something. At the edge of the dispersing ruins, two silhouettes stand in silence.
Their faces remain hidden. You cannot tell if they watch you, if they even see you at all. Yet something stops you cold. Familiarity. Deep and wordless and undeniable.

One of them tilts their head ever so slightly and murmurs something indistinct. The words escape you. But the voice... the voice echoes somewhere beneath thought, in the place where recognition lives before understanding.
The bell fades. The world dissolves. When you open your eyes again, only a heavy memory remains.

speaker: Shin?
content: Go on... Go back to your struggle. You'll return. You always do. You can't stay away...

speaker: Shin?
content: ...This city... lives in all of you.
[Black Screen]
Thump.
This place of death... who does it claim...
Thump. Thump. Thump.
It gathers souls... forgets their name...
Rhythmic beats pulse through the darkness, ancient and sorrowful, as though crossing centuries to reach you. Each one lands like a stone dropped into deep water.

You force your eyes open. Fog clings thick, but through it, you glimpse figures in white at the far end, moving with the slowness of ritual. The foremost carries a white funeral banner that sways with each step as they chant.

They fade into the distance. Then the flakes begin. White and soft as snow, they drift onto your body, your face. You reach up, only to find ashes. Burnt paper offerings, crumbling between your fingers, scattering on the wind before you can hold them.
[Inner World]
The fog lifts, but this is not the Bureau's lounge. Above you stretches a sky the color of sickness: gray-green and heavy. Before you lies a barren earth twisted and crumbling.
You're back. Again.

But you remember leaving. You remember escaping those ruins, returning to the Bureau, and submitting to the full weight of their medical examination. Sleep deprivation, they said. Mild anemia. Nothing severe.

Schorl promised to find the records on <color=#fb9259>Maria City</color>, the place Shin named. And now, with a new Illusory Moon tidal cycle approaching, the Ring Research Institute has prepared to monitor.

You know the rhythm now: sleep brings the DisSea nightmare, pulled by the Illusory Moon's tide. But never like this, never so precise. Last time, you wandered through ruins to arrive. This time, you have fallen directly into the twisted, breathing depths where nightmare lives.
So... is this that woman's doing after all? As if hearing the thought, her laughter curls through your ears.
You shake your head, brow tight. You will not give her the satisfaction. No matter how many times it takes, you will leave. You will return to where you truly belong.

But the darkness has already heard your resolve. It answers with squirming movement. The aberrations you fled before have not forgotten your scent. The phantoms remember your shape. And tonight, they are more excited. More hungry than last time.
[Faint Red Light Flickering]
The whispers withdraw, but the darkness itself becomes a witness. From its depths, invisible eyes open because of you, because of something you did, something you still do not understand.
You clench your fist, feeling the power of the shackles in your palm. You must use your only weapon with care.
You recall the stele and the red Hypercube flowers at the dream's end. It functioned like a boundary marker. To escape again, you need to find another.
Tinkle...
As if in response, the distance answers. Crisp metallic chimes ring out, cutting through the quiet. You listen closer, and a melody takes shape.
If the melody springs from something like a bell, then fortune smiles. But fortune is a stranger here. It could also be a monster wearing the shape of music. You must stay vigilant.
You clench your fist, feeling the faint power of the shackles, and take a deep breath. Following the sound, you proceed with caution.
Tinkle... Tinkle...
Exploration has bled you dry. Stamina gone, reserves emptied, but worse than the weariness is the loss of certainty. There is no safe path anymore. Not one.
The fog thickens ahead, swallowing everything beyond a few steps. And through it, those gazes cling to you, impossible to shake. They follow no matter where you turn, as well as the chime.
I cannot waste away like this. I must find a way forward. There is no other choice.
Ding—
Just then, a soft rustling reaches you from the side. Straining to see, you make out a hunched figure moving through the mist.

The figure wears a patchwork of brightly colored clothing and walks with a limp. Yet the damp fog, which clings to everything else, seems to have no effect on them whatsoever; they maintain their slow but steady course, heading somewhere with clear intent.
They know the way.
[Add a transition] (If no additional background image is available, add a fog effect and remove the fog afterward)

After following the figure for a while, the fog begins to thin at last, and the path resolves before you. The unsettling gazes no longer press in from all sides, and even the ringing in your ears gradually slows before fading into silence.
It worked...
Yes, your choice was right. Following the figure led you out of that perilous fog. You can breathe easy, at least for now. So then, what next?

Do you look back, hoping to glimpse what that fog truly was? Do you scout ahead, searching for a sign of where to go? Or do you simply stop and take a break? After all, this ordeal has left you utterly drained, your thoughts growing hazy at the edges.
What is going on...
You make your choice, but your body refuses to obey. Instead, it continues forward with unsteady, floating steps, trailing after the white figure ahead. Onward, onward—
Panic jolts through you. You struggle, thrash against the invisible grip, but your legs keep dragging forward. One step, then another. And then...
The path grows increasingly crowded; more figures materialize beside you, appearing from nowhere. They move as one, silent and blurred, all heading the same direction.
When you glance down, you see your own hands turning to mist, just like theirs. A leaf caught in the current, and the river will not let go.
No... Something's going wrong. I have to get away from them...

You fight. You thrash against the pull, but your feet refuse to halt, dragging you forward step by helpless step. Your body turns translucent, your breath comes in ragged gasps, and your consciousness flickers at the edges.
...Stop! Stop!
The cry tears from your throat, but your body doesn't hear. It doesn't belong to you anymore. And then, something peculiar cuts through the haze—

Stone lions line the roadside as the procession shuffles past them, blind. But you see. Crimson threads wrap around each lion, thick as rope, and their loose ends trail across the ground, coming to rest at your feet.
That's it. You can't stop moving. But if you must march, then at least you can...

options: Reach for the red threads and trip yourself

content: ...Ungh!
In an instant, the torrent of figures crashes over you like floodwaters, threatening to pull you under.

options: Hold tight to the red threads

content: You grip the threads with everything you have and fight your way toward where they lead.

Just as your sanity begins to fray and your strength gives out, you stumble free. The tide releases you. You collapse, gasping, heart hammering against your ribs. But slowly—blessedly—your body remembers it belongs to you again.
Pant... Pant...
You look around. The ruins have opened into a clearing, and you stand at its center, surrounded. Stone lions tower around you like silent sentinels, their bodies rising as high as buildings.
Red threads bind their eyes, layer upon layer, the trailing ends hanging down like weeping wounds. Their mouths are wide open, locked in grins that hold no warmth.

You stumble back, heart lurching, and crash into something solid. A stone statue tumbles to the ground before you, scattering rubble. You stare at its face, frozen—it wears your expression. Your terror. Your wide, uncomprehending eyes.
These statues... Could they be...?!
Fear grips you. You lash out with everything you have, your shackles screaming through the air, but the stone lions don't even scar. And still, they laugh.
The shrill laughter rises and falls in waves, each one driving deeper into your consciousness, shredding the edges of your sanity.

options: I have to get out of here!

content: You spin to flee, but every path is sealed. Stone lions block every exit, towering and mocking. And among them, standing perfectly still, is a figure in white.
Bright clothing. A familiar limp. The same one who led you here.
Hitting them won't work... They helped you... You must give something in return...
You accepted their help... so you have to pay the price...
His voice is hoarse and grating, scraping against your eardrums like a saw through wood. Before you can think, the words spill from your mouth.
Then what would it—
Tinkle, tinkle, tinkle, tinkle...!
Before all the words leave your mouth, chimes shatter the silence in the distance, sharp and urgent. They cut you off. But it's already too late.

The figure lifts its head. And for the first time, you truly see: Peeling paint, not bright clothes. Crumpled folds, not wrinkled skin. Crude scissor cuts, not a human shape. And hollow, pitch-black eyes, lifting to meet yours.
<color=#fb9259>—It's a paper effigy.</color>

speaker: Paper Effigy
content: You want to know?

speaker: Paper Effigy
content: You want to know? You want to know? You want to know? You want to know?
The bell rings on frantically. The paper effigy shuffles closer, muttering under its breath.
But you can't back away. Behind you, the blood-stained stone statues wait, their grins still leering down at you from every angle.

speaker: Paper Effigy
content: If you want to know, then... ASK FOR IT. DEMAND IT. BEG FOR IT!!
In your dreams!

speaker: Paper Effigy
content: Sssss—
Your shackles lash out. The paper effigy shrieks—a thin, tearing sound—and shatters into fragments. You don't hesitate. You slip past its remains and run, desperate for escape.
But despair crashes down moments later. The path ahead is gone. Erased. In its place stands a wall of impenetrable darkness, waiting for you to step into its depths.
Behind you, the fragments stir, reforming. One becomes two. Two becomes four... The resurrected effigies drag their bodies across the ground, pulling themselves toward you.

speaker: Paper Effigy
content: You'll never find your way out alone. Beg me, and I'll show you the path. All it takes is a single plea—

speaker: Stone Lion
content: Hehehehehe...
Around you, the paper effigies and stone statues multiply. And with each passing moment, your limbs grow heavier. Heavier. As if your very flesh is turning to stone from the inside out.
You have to move. You have to escape. Whatever these things are, they're pulling you under, and if you stay any longer, you'll become one of them. Trapped and frozen forever.
I will not... let you keep me here!

Your body fails you mid-motion. You crumple, and the moment you strike the ground, you hear a dull, heavy thud of stone meeting earth. You force your head around, muscles screaming, only to see a swarm of paper effigies and red-threaded lions closing in—
Tinkle—!
A single bell note rings out, pure and sharp, and the fog recoils. Pale blue spectral flames erupt from the ground before you, cold fire roaring skyward.

The paper effigies ignite instantly, curling and shriveling like dead leaves in a furnace, and from their burning forms comes a sound that might almost be screaming. You look up, eyes wide, gaze traveling past the flames—
Mao, fei, bi, hong, he, yi, zhen, li, dui...

A mask conceals the upper half of the woman's face. Only her pale lips remain visible, shaping a mantra that means nothing to you. Each syllable falls deliberately as if the words themselves have weight.
She moves toward you, unhurried, stepping through the spectral flames as though they were solid ground. One side of her robe is dark with stain, but the fire does not touch her.
Heed my command... Let the fire take you.

The bell rises in her hand. She flicks her wrist, and the ringing swells, becoming something vast. The spectral flames leap to obey. They burn away the fog that has plagued you since the beginning. Those cold, watching eyes are gone, and the paper effigies curl and crumble to ash in the space of a heartbeat.

speaker: Paper Effigy
content: Screeeeech—
Her hands form another seal. In an instant, the red threads on the lions ignite. And when the last thread snaps, the stone beasts shatter completely.
The screams rise from the wreckage, anguished and terrible. The flames crackle and hiss. But gradually, inevitably, both fade into utter stillness.
Pant... Pant...
In that stillness, you see the woman slowly turn her head toward you.
Her skin holds no color, bloodless as bone. Long black hair spills down her back, drifting lazily in the fog, and the bell in her hand sways with each gentle movement.
Tinkle.
The familiar mask on her face catches your attention. Perhaps... she was part of the expedition too?
But then why the Eastian robe? Is the bell in her hand the source of those warning chimes? Has she been the one helping you all this time?

She approaches silently, making no sound at all. Her hand reaches toward you. Her sleeve drifts close, nearly brushing the tip of your nose. And you see her fingers: slender, yet vivid red like blood. Golden runes pulse across her skin, alive with light.
She doesn't notice your tension—or if she does, she gives no sign. She steps closer still.
The spectral flames still cling to her, flickering softly. As she draws near, tiny sparks drift free. They fall onto your hands, and you find them ice-cold.
You edge away, a quiet resolve settling over you: you would ask for nothing in this place ever again. Every kindness, it seems, comes with a hidden toll.
Her hand is cold. When you grasp it for leverage, it doesn't move at all, and she hauls you to your feet as if you weigh nothing.
You stay where you are, wary, your grip on the shackles hidden but ready. Still, she demands no price.
She lets go and retreats a single step. Her head tilts, just slightly—studying you, perhaps, though you can't be sure. Then, slowly, her lips part.
The divination did not lie... Here you are.
She gives a stiff nod, then lifts the bell in her hand and gives it a soft shake, as if to say there's nothing to fear.
Do you wish to leave?
I can be your guide... out of here.
You can't read her; her voice gives nothing away. But she saved you, and she's asked for nothing. Maybe that means something. Maybe... she's different from the paper effigies after all.
...You know the way out of here? Can you show me?
She nods once more, then turns and walks away.
As she recedes, the dispelled shadows rush back together, like ripples smoothing into stillness, but in reverse. Eager. Hungry. It seems her protection extends only to those who walk beside her.
She must sense you lingering, because she stops just ahead. Firelight flickers across her slender shape; the bell chimes, gentle and steady. In all this madness, she alone shines.
She is waiting.
With no better path in sight, you draw a breath and go to her.
Assured of your company, she presses on. Her bell pulses slow and deep, each chime pushing back the dark like ripples on black water.
—Clink.
Your foot strikes something. You look down and find the copper coin from before. This time, its reverse face stares up at you, and a sudden unease crawls over your skin.
Tinkle, tinkle, tinkle... The bell grows distant. She's pulling away. No time to think. You snatch the coin, pocket it, and hurry after her.
Tinkle... Tinkle...
Footsteps and bell chimes weave through the strange rock forest, echoing off stone again and again. The same scenery scrolls past until time blurs to nothing. Then, finally—
That's...
Hypercube flowers bloom ahead, a familiar sea of crimson. And there, standing silent among them, is the realm stele that marks the exit. She did not lie. The way out waits.
After so long wandering this eerie city, your limbs have gone numb. Wasting no time, you approach the realm stele and reach out to touch it.
A dark fog seeps from nowhere, coiling upon the stele like breath on glass. The monster guarding this place is coming. You step back, shackles loose in your grip, ready.
She glances down at you—vigilant, coiled—then up at the dark fog taking shape in the air. A long moment passes. Slowly, she lifts her hand, and the bell rings once again.

speaker: Dark Shadow
content: Aaarrrghhh—
Pale blue flames surge from the ground, swallowing the dark fog whole. In moments, it crumbles, scattered, gone without a trace.
You never expected the battle to end before it began. The stone stele before you glows softly now, beckoning you to leave.
...Thank you.
If you hadn't rung that bell to warn me, or shown up when you did... I'd probably still be lost in this ghost city.
You wished to leave.

You gaze at her, this expedition member whose name you never learned. Her bell has accompanied you all this way, chiming through every shadow. Now you are about to wake from this nightmare, while she...
Will you... come with me?
She looks at your outstretched hand. A long silence. Then she shakes her head, a faint smile touching her lips as if bidding you farewell.
The stone stele's glow brightens. You let your eyes close, but you carry her with you. Once you wake, you will find her name in the archives. You will remember her.
You open your eyes, but the nightmare is still there. Something is wrong. Your hand, the one pressed to the stele, is no longer just yours.
Golden runes crawl over it, identical to the woman's. They spread without pause, consuming you.
Hands, feet, neck, face... They creep over your eyelids, and the moment they do, the world dissolves. Light fragments, pulling you through a kaleidoscope of broken colors.
My body... It's becoming the same as hers?!
[Flashback]
Hitting them won't work... They helped you... You must give something in return...
[Flashback Transition]
Gaze upon the dead, and they shall look back. Listen to the dead, and they shall hear you. Speak to the dead... and they shall answer.
[End of Flashback]
The pieces begin to fall into place, all pointing toward an answer you refuse to believe, and yet, it is the only one. Slowly, you turn to look at her once more—
So... you're just like those things...
You... grant my wish... and then... I pay the price. I become like you...
Crimson light bathes her. The red Hypercube flowers do not fade with the shadows; instead, they bloom around her, thriving. Phantoms writhe in the darkness, twisting within that intense, eerie glow.
Her lips still hold that gentle curve. You once thought it a parting smile. Now it feels cold. Mocking.
She knows you cannot leave.
You never gave anything for free... It just wasn't the time to collect yet.
Gradually, you can no longer see. No longer hear.
—Clink.
The copper coin slips from your pocket and falls to the ground.
You should stop asking. Stop seeking answers. The final price... is more than you can pay...
But your body is already corrupting, hollowing. A foreign, twisted consciousness floods in through the gaze, wrenching the question from your lips:

options: Are you a guide of the void?

content: Her shadow tears itself across the ground, stretching beyond reason, as though her very soul is clawing free of its mortal cage. You know she is speaking, but the sound never reaches you. Only a smear of color where mouth and teeth should be, opening and closing.
Heh... Do you see me as dead?

Her shadow tears itself across the ground, stretching beyond reason, as though her very soul is clawing free of its mortal cage. You know she is speaking, but the sound never reaches you. Only a smear of color where mouth and teeth should be, opening and closing.
Me? I am... a resident of this city.
Her words drift down like feathers, soft and weightless, yet when they land, they crush the last shred of your consciousness.

speaker: Whispering Phantoms
content: You saw us. You spoke to us. You asked, and we answered.

speaker: Whispering Phantoms
content: Now... you are one of us.

<size=50><color=#dg1f1f>       </color>YOU<color=#dg1f1f>      </color>HAVE<color=#dg1f1f>       </color>REACHED<color=#dg1f1f>       </color>YOUR<color=#dg1f1f>       </color>LIMIT<color=#dg1f1f>       </color><color=#dg1f1f>       </color><color=#dg1f1f>       </color><color=#dg1f1f>      </color></size>
Reason breaks. Consciousness scatters. Crimson flowers and spectral flames consume your sight.

The symbols that have haunted you—those half-glimpsed runes at the edge of thought—begin to twist and writhe through this phantasmal landscape. And with your last remaining thread of awareness, you finally read them:

<color=#dg1f1f>Offer no glance to the departed.
Lend no ear to the abyss.
Speak no question to the spirits.</color>
The bell rings again, its chimes sinister and close. Through the haziness, you see her shaking it again, this time advancing with the phantoms at her side.
Your desperate resistance buys you only a sliver of space to retreat.
Pant... Pant... Pant...
You gasp, lungs burning. Pushing your shackles to their limit has left you even weaker—your mind more scattered, more fragile.
[Screen Shakes]

The figure before you stands bathed in crimson light, slowly consumed by the sea of flowers. And the gazes, the same ones that have haunted you from the darkness, break free from their fetters and resurface once more.
They are everywhere. Malicious. Mocking. Covetous. Prying. In that instant, you feel as though all the malice in the world has fixed its eyes upon you.

speaker: Phantoms
content: Life and death... a single breath between. A whisper tears the veil. You know this.

The voices whisper, sliding past your ears like silk through a keyhole. And from the darkness, mist the color of bruised teal writhes toward you, winding around your body and seeking any passage into the fragile fortress of your mind.
Offer no glance to the departed. Lend no ear to the abyss. Speak no question to the spirits...
You recite the warnings like prayers, blood-written and desperate. You press your palms hard against your ears, shutting them out, shutting them all out.
But still, they seep through.

speaker: Phantoms
content: Fight not... Your feet carried you here. Fate carries you home.

speaker: Phantoms
content: Find your own road back. Follow what calls... O soul, return!
[Flashback]

speaker: Shin?
content: My dear, fate is guiding you. You are destined to return to the origin, to return to my side. Go and see the shape of truth...
[End of Flashback]
Your heart convulses, and your shackles shatter their last restraints. Savage crimson thorns burst from your flesh, spearing through you, nailing you to the moment of your undoing.
Agony lances through every nerve. The world bleeds black as your knees find earth. And in that darkness, you feel them coming—the shadows, viscous and cold, surging forward to swallow what remains.
Tinkle—!
[White Screen Shakes]

A bell rings. Clear as ice, sharp as a blade. White light erupts through the darkness, and the very fabric of this nightmare trembles. The crawling horrors crack, splinter, and fall away like sheets of painted glass.
Let the flood wash all stain, cleanse the crossing to the beyond...
[CG Begins]

Within the glimmering haze, a figure takes shape: a woman in a cyan robe. She holds a silver bell aloft, swaying as she chants, her voice a quiet stream through the chaos. Her sleeves drift like wings resting.
And from her, light emanates, not harsh, but purifying. The air itself grows still around her, as if heaven and earth have agreed that here, in this small space, only what is sacred may remain.
The height of Yang, to Yang be called; the depth of Yin, let Yin be thralled...

Life flows back into your limbs. Your vision sharpens, the world resolving from chaos into form. The headache, the nausea, the creeping madness... all of it dissolves in that gentle radiance, leaving behind a sense of relief you had forgotten you could feel.
She turns toward you. A few strands of long hair sway gently beside her cheek, revealing a pair of clear, cyan eyes.
...Who... are you?

At the sound of your voice, she slowly moves toward you. The silver bell at her waist sings with each step, soft and clear, and with every chime, the darkness that has pressed so long upon your heart finally loosens its grip.
Dazed, you watch her crouch before you. She takes your hand.

speaker: Woman's Voice
content: You're awake. No need for fear. I'm here.

The sharp sound of tearing bandages gives way to the gentle pressure of a fresh dressing. Then, through the thin fabric, you feel another's warmth, solid and real. Only now can you be certain: you have finally left that place where only ghosts wander.
A deep relaxation settles into your bones. Reaching out, you loosely grasp her sleeve and catch the faint, bittersweet scent of medicine clinging to her.
Wait... Those clothes?!
[Transition for 1s, screen violently shakes]

You spring up, but your body isn't listening. You stagger back, steps wild and uncoordinated. When your foot hooks on something, there's no stopping the fall. You hit the ground hard, tailbone first, the sharp pain a sudden, brutal clarity.

speaker: Daoist
content: Such alarm, young friend. Whatever for?
The voice calls out once more, and a cold sweat slicks your body in an instant. Before thought can become action, you hear the approach—the wet, squelching tread of her shoes against the mud.
Pain lances through your head as you force your blurred eyes to focus, to lock onto her. There is no error. That is an Eastian robe, identical to the one that woman wore.

The memory of bells chimes in your ears, bringing with it the return of the sinister whispers and that putrid stench. Against your limbs, something begins to creep, writhing and tightening, a phantom grip trying to drag you back to that place.
You thrash wildly at the empty air, legs scrabbling against the ground as you fight to push yourself backward. But for all your desperate efforts, you've barely managed to move half a meter.
Then she stops before you. Her shadow falls, swallowing you whole. There is nowhere left to run.
Don't... don't come any...
The sound that tears from your throat barely resembles your own voice anymore.

She lowers her gaze, studying you for a long, thoughtful moment. Then something shifts in her eyes. She raises her fingers in a delicate pinching gesture and begins to speak, her words slow and deliberate.

speaker: Daoist
content: Yin energy clings to you. Your spirit's gone to pieces. I fear some evil work. Not good. Not good at all.
As she speaks, her hand reaches out and closes firmly around your shoulder.
The hand doesn't budge. Instead, she uses your own momentum against you, flipping you over completely. An arm hooks under your armpit, scooping you up and tucking you against her side like a parcel.
Her arm digs painfully into your chest. Your legs kick helplessly in the air, but the struggle only makes her grip tighten further.

speaker: Daoist
content: Keep squirming, young friend, and I'll have to make you less comfortable.
She raises the other hand and waves it in front of your face. From nothing, golden threads kindle across her palm, glowing, gathering.
No, you won't let her have you. Not completely.
You coil inward—arms folding, body curling—and writhe against her grip, desperate to slip loose.
Nngh...

speaker: Daoist
content: Still stubborn. Very well, don't blame me for what comes.
Her hand cuts through the air, forming a seal. Then, pressure. Invisible, omnidirectional, crushing in on you from everywhere at once.
She adjusts you against her side like someone shifting a bag, and the casualness of it makes your stomach turn. You are nothing to her but weight. Her voice rises:

speaker: Daoist
content: According to The Scripture of Purifying the Heart, to dispel nightmares, one must press the philtrum with the left hand twenty-seven times...
Twenty-seven?!

speaker: Daoist
content: ...And recite the heart-purifying incantation and beseech the Divine's protection...

Suddenly, she stops. With a slow shake of her head, her expression shifts to one of grave alarm. Her hand gropes behind her back, finally producing a rolled booklet. With a sharp flick of her wrist, it unfurls with an audible swoosh, and she starts flipping pages in a desperate hurry.
...Don't tell me you forgot the incantation.
Smack. The booklet is slapped hard against your lips. The musty odor of decaying paper invades your senses, thick and suffocating.

speaker: Daoist
content: Nonsense. The phantoms in your dreams must've scrambled your wits, young friend. Hence this babble.

speaker: Daoist
content: This incantation, that incantation... what does it matter? Sincerity is what counts. As long as it saves you.
With that, she simply stuffs the booklet back behind her, clears her throat, and reaches toward the area beneath your nose.

Her murmuring drifts into your ears—first, fragments about "Lord of the Great White," then an invocation: "spirits of heaven, spirits of earth." And then... all those murmurs give way to a humming tune.
All the while, her thumb works against your philtrum in erratic, pounding jabs. Barely ten presses, but each one feels strong enough to drive your teeth through your gums.

You gather yourself to protest, but her voice cuts off. In the same breath, a small bottle appears in her hand, and its contents splash across your face. Ash-tainted water hits you, and your whole body shudders.
Cough... cough cough... Are you done yet?! Sto—

speaker: Daoist
content: Wisdom pure and clear, spirit at peace... Begone!
[White Flash]

Warmth blooms from your philtrum, gentle at first, then rippling through your limbs like thaw after deep cold. Your mind sharpens, suddenly clear. The whispers, the phantom touches, the creeping dread—all of it withdraws like a retreating tide.
You blink. Desolate ruins resolve before you. Wind moans through broken stone, hollow and gloomy, but now the sound brings only stillness. Only peace.

When did she set you down? You're seated now, cross-legged on the ground. The talisman water still drips from your chin, cold against your skin. And there she is, watching you with that pleased, squinty-eyed smile.

speaker: Daoist
content: There we go. That's twice now I've lent you a hand. Surely you can drop your guard and hear me out?
She rests her chin on one hand and extends the other toward you, but gently now, without command. Her palm simply waits, open and patient.

You're still foggy, but your hand lifts on its own, finding hers. Her palm is cool against your skin, soft. And beneath it, a pulse ticks gently against your fingers. Not a ghost. Not a corpse. Alive.
She draws you up, steady and sure, until you're standing.

speaker: Lichen
content: I'm <color=#fb9259>Lichen</color>. Young friend, do you remember me?

You free your feet from the sucking mud and kick loose rubble aside. The handkerchief Lichen gave you works across your face, scrubbing away grime, but it can't erase the ashy taste of talisman water still clinging to your senses. At least your head feels clearer. A little.

You raise your eyes to the ruins. They stand silent, hollow. In the distance, white fog unfurls, curling through cracks in the brickwork like breath, like something alive. Something watches from within, a gaze thick with ill intent.
And through it all, one person wanders utterly unconcerned.
[Lichen's portrait]

speaker: Lichen
content: The Dao dwells in breath, the heart neighbors the void. In stillness, illumination; in illumination, eternal tranquility...
The cyan-robed Daoist moves through the endless fog, leisurely as a dream, her soft chanting accompanied by the gentle ring of the bell. Wherever the sound reaches, the mournful wails simply cease.
Wisps of low gray cloud drift near her. She notices them, smiles, and flicks her sleeve. The gust disperses them like thought. She walks on, untouched by mud, unmarked by the mire.
Then, as if feeling your gaze, she turns. Her eyes find yours, transfixed as you are. And her serene expression breaks, blooms, and becomes a smile meant just for you.

speaker: Lichen
content: Mm... Where the bell chimes, evil spirits retreat. Everything within a hundred meters is as safe as can be.

speaker: Lichen
content: Hehe. Look at that face. "This doesn't make any sense." What, seeing's still not believing? You won't accept that Daoism has its own divine arts?

speaker: Lichen
content: Do I really have to drag you to the Tianyi Sect and make you learn a few tricks before you see the light?
You say nothing. Instead, you slide half a step back until the cold wall presses against your spine.

Divine arts. Right. You've seen strange things before—demons, monsters, things wearing friendly faces. You haven't forgotten. You won't be fooled by a pleasant smile and a clean robe. And you're certainly not about to start asking questions like some trusting fool.
She doesn't seem to mind your silence. She simply continues talking, unhurried, as if she has all the time in the world.

speaker: Lichen
content: I came on urgent business; knew I couldn't go it alone. Cast a divination, seeking aid, followed the signs... and they led me straight to you, young friend. What I didn't expect was...

speaker: Lichen
content: ...that the good kid everyone praises so highly would sneak out of camp, wander into a forbidden zone, and end up sprawled out in the mud. Took some doing to wake you, I'll have you know.

speaker: Lichen
content: So what's the story? Our famously clever little guide, sharp as a blade—lost? Were you sleepwalking? Homesick, maybe?
She leans down, hand reaching for your head. You dodge.
The question is out before you can stop it, and you immediately regret it. The recognition in her eyes is unmistakable.
She cocks an eyebrow, gaze sharpening as she studies you through narrowed lids. You lick your lips and offer nothing.
To your relief, she doesn't push. Just a small, knowing smile, and she picks up where she left off.

speaker: Lichen
content: A foreign name can't be that hard to remember... This is the last time I'll remind you. Forget it again, and I might just be heartbroken.

speaker: Lichen
