content: This humble one's surname is Li, given name Xianling. I go by Lichen. Disciple of the Tianyi Sect, seeker of the Dao from the Eastern Continent, and part-time consultant for a certain expedition.

speaker: Lichen
content: Same as you, I'm a special guest, invited by the scientists.

speaker: Lichen
content: That's right. The ■ Nation on the eastern coast. Tens of thousands of miles across the sea. Fastest voyage takes well over ten days, and if the weather turns, well, fish gotta eat. So you see...
She reaches for your head again. You try to dodge, but the wall is right there. Your head thumps against it just as her finger connects with your brow.

speaker: Lichen
content: To meet you here, of all places? We must be kindred spirits. Blessed by the heavens.
Your eyes trace her features, her clothing. There's something familiar about them; she looks like the Eastians you've known.
Which means... if this truly is the expedition era, the early N.F. 20s... then you've encountered others like her before...

speaker: Yingying
content: Eastia? Where's that?
A time before Eastia, before the city-states, when their people were divided into nations... the Eastern Continent?
You could ask. The questions burn on your tongue. Instead, you hold them in. You watch her in silence, spine against the cold wall, refusing to come closer.

speaker: Lichen
content: That look... Are you thinking, "Why'd the scientists bring along some mystical charlatan spouting nonsense"?
...You said no such thing. You have no desire to converse with her. But then you see her pinch her fingers together, assuming an air of enigmatic wisdom.

speaker: Lichen
content: Hmph, rude little one. Show some respect. The Dao of Heaven is in disarray—Yin and Yang all thrown off balance—those fancy Western formulas of the expedition aren't half as useful as my Daoist arts. Take just now, for instance...

speaker: Lichen
content: Without the pure chime of my bell, you'd probably still be weeping away in that nightmare.
...You weren't crying.
That was—
You try to recall that blurry and dreadful dream, yet find no words to describe it. She watches you with keen interest for a moment before her expression turns serious.

speaker: Lichen
content: From the look of it... you just entered the <color=#fb9259>Void of Yin</color>, didn't you?

speaker: Lichen
content: That's what the Tianyi Sect calls it. The <color=#fb9259>Realm of Yang</color> and the <color=#fb9259>Void of Yin</color>—two sides of the same ruins. The little curly-haired one came up with a name too, but it was such a mouthful I forgot it. Helen and her lot have a simpler Western way of putting it: <color=#fb9259>reality</color> and its shadow, <color=#fb9259>dream</color>.

speaker: Lichen
content: When that baleful star fell from the heavens, every living thing in this lakeside town vanished overnight. In their place, things unseen and unspeakable gathered slowly. Beyond reality. Within dreams. And built themselves a city of ghosts and spirits.

"Ghosts and spirits"... She means the Manic Entities, doesn't she? The ones that wore false faces and tried to take you. It's not a bad word for them. They were insubstantial as smoke, yet touched with something deeply uncanny.

speaker: Lichen
content: Ghosts and spirits commune with heaven and earth. Transcend past and present. Omniscient. Omnipotent. Close to the Dao of Heaven itself. So... the slightest stir on their side ripples through all things on ours.

speaker: Lichen
content: This is the ruins of <color=#fb9259>Maria City</color>. We, the living, dwell on its Yang side. Ghosts and spirits keep watch in the Void of Yin. The baleful star bridged the two. And the expedition... they came seeking that hidden path.
<color=#fb9259>Maria City</color>... This place again.
...Have you been to the Void of Yin too? Did you find an entrance?

speaker: Lichen
content: I was just about to ask you the same thing.

speaker: Lichen
content: The Realm of Yang and the Void of Yin are two separate worlds. Ordinary people can neither see nor touch the other side. Force your way in recklessly, and you only invite disaster. I've dreamed of it once or twice. Not even sure those were real. But you...

speaker: Lichen
content: Only a rare few with extraordinary gifts, and the right fate, can enter the ruined city, close their eyes, take a nap, and slip right into the Void of Yin. I'm green with envy, I tell you.
Envy? You stare at her, incredulous. Those twisted stone statues, those paper effigies—each one more disturbing than the last. You couldn't even tell what they were. Human? Object? Dead? Alive?
You breathe deep and look at her again. Really look. The patterns on her robe are nearly identical to what the "dead" wore. The one in your dream who commanded shadows to attack you.
Coincidence? It can't be. Then what is she really after, coming here for this <color=#fb9259>Void of Yin</color>?

speaker: Lichen
content: Alright then, tell me: what did you see in the Void of Yin just now, young friend?

speaker: %u
content: Someone who could control ghosts... Someone dead.

speaker: %u
content: The clothes that person wore… looked a lot like… yours.
You let the final word hang in the air, heavy with intention, and watch.

speaker: Lichen
content: ...Looked like mine? Could it be...
Lichen's eyes brighten, alive with interest. She leans in half a step, sleeves drifting with the movement.

speaker: Lichen
content: You saw my shifu?!
...Shifu?
She doesn't answer you, already lost in her own joy.

speaker: Lichen
content: I knew it. She's here. Right here. All that searching, it wasn't for nothing!

speaker: Lichen
content: Here, let me give you a proper introduction. My shifu's name is—ah, never mind, you won't remember it anyway. Point is, she's the grandmaster of the Tianyi Sect. Great mystic of the ■ Nation, Eastern Continent.

speaker: Lichen
content: Decades ago, she was already performing divinations and exorcisms for the people online. Training an exceptional disciple, namely, me. Amassing tens of thousands of fans... I mean, devoted believers.
...They had online influencer scams in this Eastern Continent a century ago?

speaker: Lichen
content: You're thinking something rude again, aren't you? That my shifu's a fraud just like me? Uh-uh. Different. She has real talent.
Did she just admit... she really is a fraud?

speaker: Lichen
content: Years before the Nightfall, my shifu had already divined the <color=#fb9259>Perishing Star</color>'s arrival.
Your reaction clearly delights her. She gives her head a slow, dramatic shake, then carries on with her tale.

speaker: Lichen
content: The prophecy came true. Calamities swept the land. A few years later, my shifu vanished without a word. Her followers believed she'd passed on. But recently, she started appearing in my dreams. In the dreams of many others.

speaker: Lichen
content: She said nothing. But I know... she is in the Void of Yin. She has attained the Dao of Heaven. Transcended life and death. And she wishes for us to find her.

speaker: Lichen
content: Well? Interested? Come find her with me. The divination is never wrong. You, young friend, are the one I must rely on for this journey. I'll be the advisor, you be the guide. I'll ward off your misfortune; you lead the way. What do you say?

speaker: Lichen
content: Once we find my shifu, the good karma will be first-rate!
She pats your shoulder, leaning close. And in her eyes, you catch a flicker not of fear, but of something rawer. Longing... perhaps?
You've seen that look before. In someone else's eyes.
No. You force the thought away. Here, now, in this place, dwelling on <color=#fb9259>her</color> is dangerous. It will only sink you further.
I have no interest in good karma, and I have no plan of going back. I don't want to get tangled up in things I can't understand. No wish to take that kind of risk. Ever again.

speaker: Lichen
content: The greater the risk, the richer the fortune! For seekers of the Dao like myself, glimpsing truth through danger? That's the blessing we dream of.
Easy for you to say. That place can cost you your life.
If you want to know what I learned there, what it taught me, it's this:
Stay far away. Never dream of asking them for anything. One wrong word, and there's no turning back.
I will never go back to that place—
The bell at her waist draws your gaze like a moth to flame. You try to look away—command yourself to—but your eyes won't obey. Your hands are shaking. You didn't even notice until now.
Silence hangs above you for a long moment. Then, soft as breath, a sigh.

speaker: Lichen
content: ...But where in this world is not dangerous?

speaker: Lichen
content: These are not fortunate times. Anyone with aspirations must steel their resolve. Be ready for sacrifice.

speaker: Lichen
content: Look at you—this expedition, venturing into ruined towns and abandoned cities. Was that all just to stay safe?
Words fail you. What could you possibly say? To her, you're just a child who wandered off from the group and stumbled into Maria City like a fool. If you tried to explain...
...No. You stop yourself. You don't owe her an explanation.

options: I don't want anything from this place.

speaker: %u
content: I don't seek danger. I don't seek what I can't get. I just want to leave.
She gazes at you quietly for a moment, then lets out a soft chuckle.

speaker: Lichen
content: ...Alright. I'll stop pushing you.

speaker: Lichen
content: No matter how gifted you are, young friend, you're still a child at heart. Knowing fear is a good thing, especially in a place like this. I can tell you've been through far too many frights.

speaker: Lichen
content: Rest assured. There is still one last safe place in this world.
Mid-sentence, she pulls a long hairpin from her hair. A casual gesture, unhurried.
Behind her, a scratching sound begins, faint at first, then insistent. Like claws on wood. Like something trying to get out. Fog seeps from the shadows ahead, taking shape.
She doesn't turn. Just lifts her hand, sleeve falling back to reveal her wrist, and flicks.
The hairpin pierces the forehead of the monster formed from fog.

speaker: Lichen
content: Stay by my side. I'll keep you safe.
The last glimmer of the paper talisman dies, swallowed by the fog. For a long second, there is nothing, only quiet, only gray.
Then sound returns: a bell's crisp chime, and Lichen's voice, warm with laughter.

speaker: Lichen
content: I know. Children fear such things. The path to my shifu must be crawling with ghosts and spirits. I shouldn't force you to brave such dangers.

speaker: Lichen
content: Then again... staying in the Realm of Yang may not be any safer. And leaving you alone would only worry me. Why not come with me for a while? I can keep them at bay. I promise, none of them will get close to you.
Her hand extends toward you, waiting.

You follow the line of it—that same hand that just destroyed a monster like it was nothing. Her face is calm, almost lazy, but her posture is impossibly straight. Mist curls at her feet, and for a heartbeat, she looks like something out of a legend. A Daoist immortal, come down from the mountains.
You swallow hard. You don't trust her. But right now? She's your best chance at getting out of this alive.
You leave her hand hanging in the air. Instead, you draw a breath and give her a single nod.
Her lips curve. Without a word, she folds her hands behind her back.

speaker: Lichen
content: Then I'll take that as a yes, young friend.

Agreement or not, the chill won't stop. It crawls up your back, bringing with it memories: the dead city from your dream, the flagstones slick with something wrong, the chimes and whispers that threaded through the air like poison.
And... her. The ashen one. Dressed just like Lichen.
You shake yourself, and find Lichen already turned, facing the mist and smiling at whatever lurks within.

speaker: Lichen
content: Alright. Let's be off. Time waits for no one.

Unlike before, she is no longer the leisurely figure trailing behind you with an air of calm composure. Now, she strides forward with swift, resolute steps, heading toward the deeper shadows among the ruins.
You are left behind. Seizing the opportunity, you reach out and attempt to summon your most familiar weapon.
Red sparks in your palm and dies. Scatters like embers in a wind that isn't there.
Your hand closes on emptiness. You look up; she's vanishing around a crumbling wall. The chill that's been creeping now settles deep.
You bite down hard and force your heavy limbs to follow.

speaker: Lichen
content: When one seeks to decipher the will of heaven, this vessel is utterly indispensable—
Ta-da!

speaker: Lichen
content: The N.F. 22 flagship communication terminal, procured just before I joined the team. It houses the foremost divination software: Ziwei Diviner app! Motion-sensing capabilities, AI-driven analysis, high-performance computation, and fully certified by the Tianyi Sect and the Eastern Continent University Institute for Spectral Phenomena!

speaker: Lichen
content: Simply inscribe your query, bestow it a vigorous shake like this, and the prognostications are impeccably precise. One may even request a granular analysis. I have secured the premium subscription, look!

Her fingers stab at the screen with mounting force, frustration creasing her brow. The longer you observe, the less convinced you are that she knows what she's doing. She catches your look and says casually:

speaker: Lichen
content: Hmm, the signal is tenuous here... No matter. It shall suffice.
When you found me earlier, didn't you say you divined my location yourself?!

speaker: Lichen
content: But I did. I personally shook the device to cast the hexagram. How is that not performing the divination myself?
She shoots you a wink and gives the terminal a little flourish, smug satisfaction radiating from every inch of her.

speaker: Lichen
content: I'll install it on your device later. Once we get out, you may proclaim yourself a master diviner. Your patronage is assured.
Back here again.
The ruins are a labyrinth, but at least the buildings are real. Solid. Unlike your progress, which has somehow landed you at this same broken pillar for the fourth time.
You're running on empty. One hand slaps against the cold stone for support while the other digs into your shaking knee. You can't seem to catch your breath.

And the monsters won't stop. They slither out of shadows, teeth and claws and wrongness, and Lichen deals with each one like it's nothing, but it's not nothing to you. Every appearance grinds down what's left of your composure. You're close, too close to breaking.

speaker: Lichen
content: Sigh, still can't find the way out? Just as that one said, the more souls wandering the Realm of Yang, the more tangled the path becomes... Heh. A clever snare. Either we all lose our way together, or we're picked off one by one.
She starts chuckling, as if admiring a well-crafted puzzle.

speaker: Lichen
content: Spirits don't win with force. They win with cunning.
Behind her, in the shadowed corner, something stirs. A mass of darkness writhes, wet and slow. You open your mouth to warn her—
Slash!
Her fist clenches—backward, without looking—and golden light erupts from nowhere. The monster is simply gone, crushed into nothing.

speaker: Lichen
content: We can't linger. If we don't find my shifu before dusk...

speaker: Lichen
content: Well, a perfect chance to try that little trick.
Your question hangs in the air, unanswered. She's already pacing, already pulling out an array of curious objects, already lost in her own excited murmurings. To her, you've ceased to exist.

speaker: Lichen
content: Where the Yin energy pools, spirits cling...

speaker: Lichen
content: With blood as the lure, the body as the bait, they shall find their anchor.

In the span of a breath, she's arranged it all: a ritual formation laid out with casual precision. Above, clouds swallow the sky, drowning every last ray of light. But the red threads still glow, an eerie crimson defiance against the dark. At the center, a bottle. And from it rises the sickly-sweet scent of blood.
Lichen...? Lichen!
She finally registers that you're there, but doesn't stop. Instead, she simply turns and gives you a gentle smile.

speaker: Lichen
content: That look again. You never seem at ease around me, young friend. I told you I'd keep you safe. Is my word so hard to trust?
But look at what you're doing...
The monsters she crushed like bugs were terrifying. But not as terrifying as her—the way her eyes gleam now, the strange cheerfulness in her voice.

And it's not just her. Behind her, inside the formation, something is happening. Dark mist gathers, churns, lives. Whispers spill out, fragmented and wrong. Your chest tightens. You can barely draw air. Does she not see it? Or—
She waves a casual hand toward the roiling dark and says, almost proud:

speaker: Lichen
content: Well, since you asked... This place is thick with phantoms, and phantoms can bridge the gap between worlds.

speaker: Lichen
content: So, according to Volume 999 of my shifu's Whimsical Musings, why not just open a ghost gate and "invite" them over for a proper chat?
You're luring them out on purpose?!

speaker: Lichen
content: To commune with all things is to know the true Dao of heaven and earth. Professor <color=#fb9259>Shin</color> also found the practice fascinating. She has a sharp eye for such things.
...You're on her side? You actually agree with her—

speaker: Lichen
content: ...Agree or not, it matters little. It's just an old saying—

speaker: Lichen
content: If I learn the truth at dawn, I can die content by dusk.
The formation is now alive. Threads pulse with growing rhythm, and you realize with horror that you have no idea when this began, or how.

She stands at its heart, serene, as violent winds tear at her clothes. The bell swings in frenzy, its ringing accelerating until it's not separate chimes but one endless, piercing shriek that flays your senses.
The terror returns. It sinks into your marrow, your blood, your breath. You can't let this continue. You won't. You have to stop her.
Stop! Just... stop! You think just because you call them, they'll give you answers?!
Don't bargain with spirits! Don't ask them for truths! They always demand a price!!

speaker: Lichen
content: A price? Then let them come to collect. If they can, I'll gladly owe them one.

speaker: Lichen
content: But if they can't... well, they'll have to concede defeat.

Her words hang in the air, then the bottle explodes. Light floods everything, impossibly bright, throwing her face into stark relief. The ruins before you rip apart as reality itself twists and warps, revealing something beyond: darkness so profound it feels solid, pierced by chaotic, flickering light.
From that tear, they come. Phantoms unlike any before—bodies twisted into shapes of pure agony, faces frozen in eternal screams. They lunge at you with shrieks that should shatter your soul...
[Transition for 1s, screen shakes, white flash effect]
And they stop. Right there. Right in front of you.
Whoosh—!!!

Crimson flames roar upward, consuming the spectral figures in a heartbeat. One moment they're there, the next, ash drifting on scorched air. Beyond the fire, through the wavering heat, Lichen catches your eye and offers you a smile.
Then she turns to face the rest of them. And that gentle smile hasn't changed at all.

speaker: Lichen
content: With my body as the offering, the dead shall be ferried... Open—!

speaker: Phantom
content: Waaaaahhh—!

The phantoms wail all around her, a chorus of torment. She doesn't seem to hear. Her steps are slow, deliberate, almost lazy. She even pauses from time to time, tilting her head to observe the phantoms restrained by her red threads, as if selecting which one to keep as the ferryman for her own crossing.

She finally stops before one and raises her hand. Several wooden swords shoot through the air and pin the creature in place. It convulses a few times before letting out what can only be described as a blood-curdling shriek.

speaker: Phantom
content: Arrrggghh—!
The creature's agony is palpable, but Lichen feels nothing for it. Her brow stays smooth. There is only intensity in those eyes, a fire fixed on her target. Then she snaps:

speaker: Lichen
content: By my lineage, by my true name, I bind you. Ghosts and spirits, answer me true. Tell me—

speaker: Lichen
content: The one I seek... where does she dwell? The path I must walk... where does it lead?

speaker: Lichen
content: Answer!!

The command leaves her lips, and something answers. Something cold wraps around the back of your neck, thick and slithering, crawling down your spine like a parasite. Behind Lichen, several masses of dark fog are closing in fast—
[Red Flash or Multiple Slashes]
Several threads spring up from thin air, coiling around their limbs and necks. One sharp tug, and they are torn to pieces in an instant.
She pivots on her heel, not sparing you so much as a glance.

speaker: Lichen
content: Fret not. I promised you safety. Not one of these phantoms will touch you.
True enough, she has swept your surroundings completely clean. But...
At the heart of her formation, the dark mist grows ever denser. More and more spectral figures emerge from within, lunging toward her.
You can't let this continue! You have to stop her!
You stagger toward the center of her formation, but the threads trip you before you can reach her—

speaker: Lichen
content: Huh?! Wait— Young friend, no!
[Transition for 1s, screen shakes, white flash]
The world lurches, then spins. Pain—searing, white-hot—erupts from your back and chest, flooding your senses until your limbs go numb. The chaos of sound collapses into a single, infinite shriek.
Through the blur, you see Lichen reaching out toward you—
And then, darkness.
Your eyes snap open on a gasp, as if breaching the surface after nearly drowning. Your lungs are searing caverns, each breath laced with the metallic tang of rust.

You're lying on a familiar flagstone path, its cool, smooth surface a stark contrast to the unfamiliar, crumbling steles that enclose you. The air shimmers with that same phosphorescent glow, casting everything in a sickly light.
You're back. Again.

A dull throb pulses at the base of your skull. Pressing a hand to it, you try to anchor yourself, scanning your surroundings for a clue that bridges the gap between now and the moment you blacked out.

speaker: Lichen
content: So, according to Volume 999 of my shifu's Whimsical Musings, why not just open a ghost gate and "invite" them over for a proper chat?
There was no other way. Stopping her ritual wasn't a choice; it was survival. She warned it would destroy your world, and you believed her.
But justification won't carry you out of here. Right now, survival means moving.
Ding—
A soft clink sounds beneath your foot. You glance down and find it: a single copper coin.
The last time it appeared... you were alone. And in danger.
Your gaze snaps up. Across the ruins, you spot a broken stele and move.
Just as you duck behind it, a dense, dark mist rolls in from the distance. It drifts directly to the spot where you woke, hovers there with terrible patience, then leisurely drifts away.
You look down at the coin in your palm.
Are you... helping me?
The copper coin, of course, says nothing. It never has. But the instant you ask the question, it slides from your palm and lands face-up.
Face-up...? You stare at it. A coincidence? It could be. But you've learned one thing here: almost nothing is truly lifeless.
You toss the copper coin. It barely leaves your palm before landing face-up. Again.
That's the confirmation you needed. No more doubt; this is how it speaks to you.

options: This place is dangerous, isn't it?

content: Of course, face-up again.
The copper coin lands face-up, again. You breathe a sigh of relief.

You know nothing of this coin's origin. Everything in this world fills you with unease. And yet this small piece of copper has helped you more than once. For now, you have no choice but to trust it. At the very least, it guides you away from danger.
Not toward it.
That alone is enough to steady your heart.

options: Which way should I go now?

content: The copper coin slips from your fingers. It hits the stone with a soft clink and spins. Once. Twice. Then it wobbles, slowing, until it rests at a sharp angle.
You raise your eyes. The flagstone path lies before you, narrow and endless, disappearing into the void.
You steel yourself, pocket the coin, and walk. Behind you, the mist closes like a curtain, all the while concealing the faint but persistent bell chimes in your wake.

You've lost count of the steps. The flagstone path stretches endlessly, uneventful, but your body has stopped pretending. You brace against your knees to rest, and the moment you double over, your stomach lurches.
Gasping, you open your palm.
The coin lands face-up. Your chest tightens, but you don't argue. You pick up the coin, steady it on your thumb, and prepare to flip again.
How much farther to the exit?

You close your mouth the moment the words leave it. Too complex. The coin can't answer that. You grip it tightly, searching for the right question. For a moment, you almost wish you could just talk to it.
The thought hits like a slap. That's what she would do.

options: Can this path lead me out?

content: You toss the coin. It hangs in the air—just for a moment—then falls.
—Face-down.
Patience. You have to be patient. The coin knows this place—has seen its dangers—and yet it has never pulled you toward the darkness. That must count for something. You choose your words carefully.

options: Are you trying to lead me away from the monsters?

content: The coin lands face-up, the motion decisive.
But we can't just keep running forever. I need to leave.

options: Do you know the way out?

content: The coin lands face-down, but not before that familiar hesitation, that almost-imperceptible pause in the air.
Then... what now? Do you just wander this world forever? Is there anyone who might know the way out?
Who could possibly be so eager to help you?
If avoiding danger won't solve the problem, then there's only one option left: You have to walk toward it.
Her silhouette rises from the darkness of your mind, unwelcome but undeniable. At this dead end, she has become your only inspiration.

options: I'll have to do it her way.

content: As if reading your thoughts, the coin slips from your fingertips, landing face-down with a soft clink.
I know it's dangerous, but...
If I don't ask them, will I be trapped here forever?
You flick your wrist. The coin arcs, strikes stone, and spins.
And spins. And spins. Longer than it should. You wait, heart pounding, but it refuses to stop.
...Answer me!
A childish shout tears from your throat, and the coin freezes mid-spin.
Then, impossibly, it stops right on its edge.
...I'll take that as a yes.
Then that's the only choice I have, right?

No need to flip the coin. You already know the answer. You grip it until its edges bite into your palm and turn, only to freeze. A stone statue stands directly before you, so close you could almost touch it.
You're certain it wasn't there a moment ago.
Its eyes are sealed shut, its expression serene, as if carved mid-prayer. Brows low, gaze lowered toward some unseen altar. You steady yourself with a breath and force your feet forward.
Please show me a way out.
A moment passes, and nothing stirs.
Have you been so frightened for so long that you can't recognize a simple statue anymore? The thought almost convinces you. Almost. You start to turn away—
Crack. Crack. Crack.

The statue moves. Slowly, joint by joint, it rotates to face the distance. Through the haze, your breath catches. More statues. One after another, identical and still, stretching endlessly into the fog.
At the far end, the last statue turns. Its finger is extended toward a stone stele half-swallowed by mist. Wisps curl around it like breath, and from within pulses a faint, rhythmic red glow.

speaker: Stone Statue
content: What you seek lies ahead...

speaker: Stone Statue
content: Make an offering, and the world shall bend to your desire...
The corner of the statue's mouth twitches. It's just a flicker, a suggestion of a smile. You blink, and it's returned to that same serene stillness, eyes lowered as if it never moved.

You force yourself toward the stone stele. The flagstone path gives way to dry earth, but it doesn't feel dry beneath your feet. It feels soft. Alive. Each step sinks slightly, as if the ground itself is tasting you, drawing you in with cautious, greedy hunger.
Mist rises with each step, thick and cold, erasing the world behind you.
It curls around your arms, your throat—not damp, not airy, but strangely solid. Like the soft, cold fingers of a corpse tracing your skin.
You take a deep breath and touch the stele. The cold stone warms, then burns, and you press harder through the pain.
I want to leave this place.

At the sound of your voice, the mist freezes. Then it sinks, retreating low to the ground. The whispers begin. Fragmented at first, broken syllables scattered through the air, then they find one another and cohere into words.
It's you... You're back...
...Seeking our aid once more...
The mist parts for her. She emerges at last, taking form piece by piece.

First, the hem of her robe, trailing thick, viscous filth. Your gaze travels upward, past the golden patterns writhing across her neck, past the shadowed hollow where her face should be, to the mask that obscures it completely.
She reaches out. Her fingers stop inches from your nose, but you feel nothing. No warmth. No scent. Nothing.
Your heart slams against your ribs. You do not dare touch her.
Tinkle—
That's...?!
Tinkle, tinkle—
A bell. But brighter, crisper, with a hint of urgency. It does not come from her.
She only watches, smiling, as if the sound means nothing at all.
Did they answer your call?
Every nerve in your body fires at once. You stumble back, your hand closing around the copper coin so tightly you feel its edges bite into your palm, pressing toward bone.
Hehe... A wish fulfilled, a debt incurred. So it begins...
The ground shudders beneath you. Then they erupt—massive tentacles, stitched crudely from ghostly limbs, writhing and reaching with nauseating, wet squelches.

Your strike forces her back just one step. The mist around her boils, twisting inward, and from its depths emerge countless faces, their human features stretched into something else. Slowly, they turn toward you as one and speak:

speaker: Phantoms
content: Heaven's balance does not tilt. To seek is to owe. To receive is to render. Lay down your spirit... and the scales shall be made whole...
Hilda
Your mind whites out. Your body forgets how to stand. Your knees slam into the ground.
Through the pain, you grit your teeth. You drag yourself forward. One step. Two. The words that tear from your throat come out broken and halting.
I never asked for this. You're the ones keeping me here...
And now you want... you want me to... pay...?!

speaker: Phantoms
content: To grasp without offering... is to mock the laws of heaven...!
The voices curdle. What whispered now screams, fury boiling through each syllable. The mist ripples, convulses, and then splits. From the tear, a spectral figure launches itself at you—
[Transition for 1s, screen shakes, copper coin (metallic) sound effect]
The copper coin flies from your chest, blocking the blow, only to be swatted aside like nothing. The dark mist swallows it without a sound.
No... Not here... You can't fall here...

You spread your fingers wide, dragging strength from somewhere deeper than muscle. From your palm, a small red barb tears free, its glow faint but burning. You thrust it forward as the next phantom lunges.
...Back off!

The phantom stumbles back, its form unraveling at the edges, but only for a moment. It recoalesces, thicker now, more present than it was before. A shriek tears from it, aimed at the air itself, then it charges at you again with renewed fury—
[White Flash]
By the clarity above, by the sanctity below... disperse, defilement!
Fire tears through the sludge, burning away the dark. Through the rift, daylight scatters, and within its shattered rays, a figure takes form.
A wind reaches you, carrying the copper taste of blood. Then light finds her face.

Lichen. She lands before you, standing tall. The silver bell in her hand blazes brighter than memory, its chimes urgent and alive. But she is as pale as death. A trace of dark red at her lips. Her robe is black with fire's kiss.
She looks down at you. And offers only a smile.

speaker: Lichen
content: No need to fret. I told you I'd keep you safe, young friend.
The phantoms go still. A breath of silence, then their cries ignite. Fury, raw and ancient, floods the air.

speaker: Phantoms
content: Insolent... Insolent! We will unmake you. Stitch your flesh to agony and hang your soul in the void, where both life and death cannot find you...!
And with it comes the malice. It rushes in from everywhere at once, a tide of pure hatred that presses. Your skeleton sings with strain, bones creaking beneath the weight of countless graves.
[Dark Mist effect prior to this line; white flash followed by the dark mist disappearing]
The filth withdraws. It seeps away from you, coalescing into more shadows and tendrils as they all turn toward Lichen.

speaker: Phantoms
content: A mortal soul dares tread the realm of the dead. You break a law written in the bones of the world... For this trespass, the sun shall forget your name...!

speaker: Lichen
content: ...The Realm of Yang and the Void of Yin are two separate worlds. Ordinary people can neither see nor touch the other side. Force your way in recklessly, and you only invite disaster.
—Ever since Lichen appeared, you were never their target. The truth hits like a blade.
You're already moving, staggering toward her through the crushing dark. There's still time. You can still push her out!

An instant before your fingers can find hers, Lichen lifts her hand. A shimmering curtain descends between you, a silent ward that drinks the chaos of the malevolent energy and leaves only stillness at your feet.
Through the translucent veil, she glances back with a soft smile. Then, she turns away, a solitary figure walking into the screaming dark to meet the ghosts alone.

speaker: Lichen
content: Wretched things. You exist only to be unmade. What right have you to demand anything from the living?

speaker: Lichen
content: If you would take by force... then come!
Her finger slices through the air, a final, brutal stroke that bisects the ghost before her. The spirit dissolves, but her victory is marred by a fresh line of red blooming across her finger.
She ignores the pain and brings the bloodied hand close to her chest, her focus unbroken. Without a moment's hesitation, her fingers begin to fly, weaving mystic seals for whatever comes next.

speaker: Lichen
content: Golden light, come forth and shield me!
A wooden sword, launched from her sleeve, flies true, beating back the shadows. But victory has a price. For every ghost dispersed, a burn sears itself into her flesh.
<color=#fb9259>This is the city of the dead, and it punishes the living.</color>
Then, the tide turns. Several phantoms disengage from the fight, their heads swiveling as one. Their crimson eyes find you.

speaker: Lichen
content: Thunder, descend!
Lightning answers her call, descending in righteous fury to strike down the ghosts.
The cost is immediate and terrible. Her body convulses, racked with pain as a mist of blood erupts from her flesh.

Then, a new horror. A massive ghost crashes against the barrier she left to guard you. The air thrums with impact, golden light washing across the surface in waves as it strains to contain the assault.

speaker: Lichen
content: Blood-oath sworn, the heavens heard. Banish the restless, break the curse. By my command... yield!
[Multiple Red Slashes]

Crimson threads spin through the air, finding their marks among the distant phantoms. Trapped in her web, they become reluctant soldiers, forced to raise their hands against their own brethren to keep you from harm.

speaker: Phantoms
content: The price... You will pay the price...!
Beneath her feet, the contamination burns hotter, thicker flames crawling upward as rivers of crimson flow down.
Sweat and anguish blur your vision, but her suffering remains impossibly clear. Every wound that rips across her flesh with each incantation is seared into your memory.

speaker: Lichen
content: By my command... yield!

The specters shriek, a chorus of damned voices as they devour one another. Below her feet, the flames rise hungrier, stripping away skin to reveal the raw flesh beneath—flesh that blackens even as you watch.
Just stop! Every time you command them, they hurt you!
You beat against the invisible wall, desperate and useless. Through the haze of heat and smoke, her silhouette flickers, a candle flame struggling against the storm.
Blood pours from her, painting her entirely in red. But she does not flinch.
Stop it!
You hurl yourself against the barrier. It groans under the impact, and the ache settles deep into your bones.
Stop... You'll die...
One more time. One more time. The wall is weakening—you can feel it giving.
Below her, the flames dance wildly, blazing ever fiercer. And within them, her silhouette flickers like a dying ember.
Stop... Stop!!!
[1s pause] White flash + barrier shattering SFX
At first, the barrier fights you: a solid, unyielding wall that makes every muscle scream. But the moment you break through, it transforms, wrapping around you like a gentle last breath.

You crash into her frail back. The overwhelming stench hits you first: blood and charred flesh. Her clothes are soaked through, sticking to your skin with warm, wet adhesion. Then the anguish comes, far more violent than any physical pain, surging through your chest as your arms close around her.
Your fingers search for something, anything, but find no patch of unharmed skin. Trembling, they sink helplessly into the torn flesh at her waist.
[Release the shackles]
Crimson spikes burst forth around Lichen, winding tight, but they do not bind her alone. You hold her through it, gasping as the same piercing, bone-deep pain surges through your own body.
She looks down, studying the shackles wrapped around her waist, then raises her gaze to you. Despite her deathly pallor, despite everything, she smiles.

speaker: Lichen
content: Stop? No...

speaker: Lichen
content: With you fighting so fiercely for me? It would be unforgivable if I didn't win, and win beautifully.

speaker: Lichen
content: Trust me. Just watch.
In the fleeting stillness, she gathers herself. Energy flows from her once more, and the flames at her fingertips burn ever fiercer.
Her right hand sweeps gracefully through the air. Wooden swords emerge from her sleeve, arcing outward to embed themselves in the ground, a ritual formation taking form.

In her other hand, the silver bell hums without cease. Stained with her blood, it glows brighter, pulsing like a second heart. Between them, her fingers weave seals before her chest—one by one, slow and deliberate.

speaker: Phantoms
content: Never... You will never escape this place...!!!
In an instant, all the shadows twist and shriek, lunging toward you—

speaker: Lichen
content: Lin, bing, dou, zhe, jie, zhen, lie, qian, xing!
The bell rings out. Blood and lingering flames merge as one in the air. Its resounding peal transforms into a golden disc, cleaving diagonally toward the monsters!
[Screen Shakes + White Flash]

speaker: Phantoms
content: Aaaaahhh—!!!
[Transition Effect] White transition fading to white background?
A blinding white light erupts with a thunderous roar. Around you, the shadows convulse violently, writhing as if in their death throes. Then, with one final, bitter reluctance, they reach for you.

speaker: Phantoms
content: Pay... Pay...

speaker: Phantoms
content: We will make you pay us... in time...

Then, like an ebbing tide, they recede. The flagstone path crumbles and reforms, cracks seal themselves shut, and the dense, chaotic contamination disperses into white mist—revealing at last the true form of Maria City beneath.
Every taut nerve in your body finally loosens. You collapse to your knees, gasping for breath.
Pant... Pant...
But beside you, there is nothing. No sound. No words of comfort. No relieved laughter of having survived. Just silence.
[Enter Small CG 02]
Ninety-Nine keeps swinging her huge sword, blazing a bloody trail amid the monster.
It's fixed on the epicenter where the shadows finally broke. A figure stands there. Someone departed. For one fleeting moment, she is Lichen's mirror.

Then she flickers, and the vision shifts. An older woman now, clad in a weathered Eastian Daoist robe, her features gaunt but peaceful. Her hands are clasped serenely before her, a posture of quiet dignity.
Is that the shifu she spoke of?
Her shoulders tremble ever so slightly, but enough. Enough for the phantom to waver in response, shifting back to its previous form.
You reach for her sleeve, but Lichen raises her hand faster. Your fingers close around nothing.

speaker: Lichen
content: ...Fear not.
She raises her hand. The last wisp of crimson flame dances at her fingertips, and she presses it gently toward the phantom's heart.
The flames catch. They spread in silence, consuming the lingering shadow. Then, the ruins fall still. No sound remains. Only the wind sweeps through, carrying away what the fire cannot hold.
[Exit Small CG 02]

Her hand finally falls. You hesitate—just a breath—then reach out and take her fingers in your own. The blood on them is still wet, warm and sticky against your skin. Her bones feel like ice, so fragile you fear they might snap at the slightest pressure.
For a moment, she is elsewhere. Then she blinks, returns to herself, and squeezes your hand briefly before letting go. Above you, a familiar chuckle drifts down.

speaker: Lichen
content: Victory is ours, young friend. Is that not worth a smile?
The silver bell hangs in the air, its earlier radiance faded to a soft glow. As the wind sweeps past, it chimes softly.

speaker: Phantom
content: Hisssss... Hisssss...
From behind the wall, a spectral form lunges. Lichen steps forward, and with a sharp gesture, summons a volley of wooden swords.

speaker: Lichen
content: By divine mandate, reveal!
The swords punch through the ghost. It shrieks, its form convulsing as it tries to escape.

In its final second, the chaos resolves into a single, horrifying image: a human face, perfectly smooth and featureless except for two bottomless pits of black staring directly into your soul before it vanishes.

speaker: Lichen
content: Don't look.
She yanks you behind her.

Though Lichen has driven the monster back, the victory feels hollow. The Realm of Yang itself seems to recoil; the ground beneath your feet no longer feels solid, but warps with a subtle, queasy undulation.
From the depths of this distortion, the phantoms come. They emerge one after another, an endless tide pursuing you from behind.

speaker: Lichen
content: By flame and blade, be slain. Turn to dust and fade!

speaker: Phantom
content: Aaahhhhh—!
The agonized scream still hangs in the air when another figure emerges from the mist—a hazy silhouette that doesn't walk, but glides low along the ground.
The next moment, with terrifying speed, it coils tight and springs at you.

speaker: Lichen
content: Over here!
She sweeps a wall of mist behind you, a desperate barrier against the horde. Her hand finds yours, grip fierce and unyielding as she drags you toward a low wall.
For one fleeting second, the thunder of footsteps behind you stumbles. Then the pursuit resumes, a furious stampede that shakes the ground and promises no escape.

speaker: Monster
content: Roaaarrr—
[Red Flash]
The mist soon shreds apart. You hurl yourselves behind the wall just as razor-sharp claws rip through the space where you stood.
We can't keep this up. They're after me. I'll draw them off, and you—
Lichen presses a finger to her lips. Her other hand moves with practiced stealth, producing several paper figures from her sleeve.

speaker: Lichen
content: Heaven and earth, lend me your striders... Go!

The words barely leave her lips when the paper figures twitch to life. These tiny, wobbling things tumble onto the ground and immediately begin burrowing. Within seconds, only a few small holes remain.
The rumbling beneath your feet stops. Then, impossibly, it shifts direction, rumbling away.
A tug at your sleeve. Lichen grins, gesturing for you to peek.
Over the wall, you watch the monsters circle in confusion before scattering, each chased by a little hopping paper figure that leads them farther and farther until they vanish.
Silence, at last. Safe in her shadow, you breathe in the sharp scent of blood and the bittersweet tang of medicinal elixirs. Your heart gradually settles, and your breathing slowly steadies.

speaker: Lichen
content: There. That little diversion trick should keep them busy for a while.
She turns, and for the first time in a while, the tension in her face melts away. Her hand rises, then settles gently on your head. This time, you don't pull away.

speaker: Lichen
content: Fret not. They weren't sent for you. These little phantoms are all from my shifu, her way of disciplining a wayward disciple.

speaker: Lichen
content: I committed the ultimate transgression, you see. Had the nerve to use some arcane tricks against her. She must be absolutely livid.
Her voice carries laughter, light and easy, but her lips barely move, frozen in that same faint smile she wore moments ago. The one she wore when she drove back her own "shifu" to protect you.

options: ...Did you hurt her badly just now?

content: You look worried.

speaker: Lichen
content: Oh, it's nothing, really! I've been tinkering with exotic arts and mystical trinkets since I was small. Every time I got caught, she'd chase me from the peak to the foothills. She's long accustomed to it. She knows when to stop.

speaker: Lichen
content: Once her temper cools, all will be well. For now, your situation is more...
A faint sound from behind cuts her off. Lichen spins, hand tightening around the bell—muscles coiled, ready.
But it's only the wind, stirring the paper talismans left by the wall.
She watches, waiting. The thin mist thins further, revealing nothing. Only then does she lower her eyes, the tension slowly leaving her shoulders as she looks away.

speaker: Lichen
content: ...Your situation is more pressing. Once you're safely settled, young friend, I'll find her and make amends.
She pulls out a talisman paper and a small vial streaked with bloodstains. She tries to wipe it clean on her sleeve, but the marks linger. She offers it to you anyway, along with an apologetic smile.

speaker: Lichen
content: Such a timid soul, and yet you stood in front of me... You're a good child. I'd hate to leave you here alone. If you wandered into the Void of Yin again and got frightened, I'd never forgive myself.
...In truth, your concern has always been for her.

But now, as she pours water, her sleeve slides back, just enough to reveal the dark crimson wounds blooming on her skin. For the first time, you lower your head like an obedient child and simply listen.
She notices your gaze. With a small, subtle motion, her sleeve falls, hiding away the wounds.
...I'm not that timid, actually. The Void of Yin isn't so frightening. Not everything there is hostile.
Before I met you, there was a copper coin. It would protect me.

speaker: Lichen
content: ...A copper coin?
You nod. Lichen is taken aback for a moment, then lowers her head.

speaker: Lichen
content: It hasn't crossed any line yet, so what's there to worry about...
What did you say?

Her words slip away, too quiet to reach you. You ask her to repeat them. Her head snaps up, gaze fixed on you. A long pause stretches between you. Then she smiles, warm and a little wondering, and says:

speaker: Lichen
content: Well, you're here now. That changes things.
Before you can press further, the paper talisman in her hand ignites and dissolves into the water. In the same motion, the cup is at your lips, warm and fragrant with herbal ash.

speaker: Lichen
content: Here, drink. If that coin has chosen you, then count it as another ally by your side.

speaker: Lichen
content: Alas, my methods have always been... sweeping. Grand gestures and bold strokes. Using arts you don't understand would only frighten you. That would never do.
Her shoulders sag. Her gaze drops, and something dark flickers across her face. Then it's gone. She looks up with a smile and speaks gently to comfort you.

speaker: Lichen
content: I'll find my shifu. At worst, I'll take a thorough scolding. Now that she's ascended, her heart must be far more magnanimous. She won't be too hard on me.

speaker: Lichen
content: But first, let's get you out of this city and back to the camp. With you, me, and the coin together, we should be able to break through this spectral maze.

speaker: Lichen
content: That way, you can rest easy.
...What about you then? You're still going to look for her?

speaker: Lichen
content: Mm-hmm.

speaker: Lichen
content: I began this search alone anyway. If I lose my way, I'll simply cast another divination. The path will reveal itself.
...But can she really find her shifu?

Your shifu is now a denizen of the Void of Yin, beyond our reach. Earlier, just asking about her nearly pulled me into the abyss. We barely made it back. And now, even this realm is more dangerous than before.
You're just one person...
...The copper coin warned me, many times. Don't speak with the dead. Maybe that's what you'd call the Dao of Heaven. If you break that rule... the consequences could be worse than we can imagine.
She hears you out. Not a flicker of hesitation crosses her face, and when she answers, her voice is steady.

speaker: Lichen
content: Would that not be a gift? If speaking with spirits leads me to a new world, I would walk that path gladly.
Words fail you. You don't know what to say, but she doesn't seem to notice. Her voice lifts, growing brighter, more spirited.

speaker: Lichen
content: This "abyss" people speak of—these "demons and devils"—they are merely shadows cast by fear. The common folk keep their distance, but how many have truly looked beyond the dark?

speaker: Lichen
content: If everyone clung to rules like that old relic, trembling at every shadow, they might as well entomb themselves in a museum and be done with it.
The words spill faster, faster. Her eyes slide away, fixed on something distant. She's murmuring to herself now, gone again.

speaker: Lichen
content: The Dao of Heaven has shifted. Life and death blur. Yin and Yang fall out of balance. What room is left for all these rules? We have witnessed enough disasters. It is time someone sought new fortune amid the chaos. After all, fortune often lies within misfortune.

speaker: Lichen
content: I will seek it. I will use it... Since she is already here, since someone has already crossed the boundary between life and death, then...
She catches the tension in your face. Her words trail off, unfinished. A soft sigh escapes her, and she smiles, warm and understanding.

speaker: Lichen
content: Ah. There I go again. You are already the timid sort, young friend, and here I am rambling.

speaker: Lichen
content: But there is nothing to fear. With your help, I am stronger, but I will manage on my own, as I always have. Who knows? Going solo might let me truly spread my wings.

speaker: Lichen
content: It would not be right to rely on a child, anyway. Go on back now. When you are older, I will take you on another adventure. It is settled.
She raises a hand, patting your back gently. You look up, and all you see is blood, dark crimson staining her shoulder.
If you leave her alone, there's no telling how far she'll push herself. And she won't listen to persuasion. So there's only one choice left—
She raises her hand and flicks you on the forehead.

speaker: Lichen
content: Are you going to listen to me or not?
You're not the only one who angered your "shifu." She was chasing me before you stepped in. With the old lady this furious, you really think she'd just let me walk away?
If we're going to apologize, wouldn't it be more sincere if we both went together? And if her anger doesn't cool, do you really think these ghosts will just let me leave in peace?

speaker: Lichen
content: Hmm... You do have a point...
Her brow furrows slightly, as if mulling something over. You quickly press on.
Besides, even if I tried to leave this city, who knows how long that would take. What if I fall asleep on the way? Then I'd have to face your shifu alone.
This is the honest truth. With your current body and strength, you have no confidence that you could make it out of Maria City on your own.
But with you by my side, I wouldn't be afraid. Not even if I fell asleep again.
I trust you. You'd wake me up, just like you did the first time.

speaker: Lichen
content: Mm... No, no, that will not do! I cannot let you walk into danger again. What if something goes wrong?
You think fast. You know exactly what she likes to hear, so you tell her.

options: But I have you, don't I?

content: The arts you used just now were incredible. That copper coin is nothing compared to you. One swat from a monster and it'd fly off who knows where.

speaker: Lichen
content: Young friend, you mean to say...
I can't feel at ease unless I'm with you. Sending me back, relying on that coin... none of it's reliable. Staying by your side is the only way I'd feel safe!
Your words work like a charm. She nods enthusiastically.

speaker: Lichen
content: ...Well reasoned. Well reasoned indeed! It has been ages since I met someone so perceptive. You truly have more spirit than those stuffy old pedants.

speaker: Lichen
content: Then let us be off! I am truly delighted. After all, the divination foretold it: you, young friend, would be my greatest blessing on this journey.
She produces a heap of tools all at once—odd shapes, strange symbols—and thrusts them into your arms before you can react. Their names and uses tumble out of her in a breathless rush.

speaker: Lichen
content: I am here to protect you, yes, but the road ahead is long, and you are already weary. If your eyes grow heavy and you slip into slumber, only to wake in the Void of Yin... well. That would be rather troublesome for me, too.

speaker: Lichen
content: We cannot have you walking in empty-handed. Preparation is key. Here, take these—
The first thing she places in your palm is a small jade fish, smooth and cool, so cool it reminds you instantly of her fingertips.

speaker: Lichen
content: This is a Yin-Yang fish pendant. The Yin half goes to you. The Yang half stays with me. This way, I will always sense where you are. If something stirs, give it a shake, and I will pull you back.

speaker: Lichen
content: Here, take this gourd as well. Something small is sealed inside. When you need it, pull the stopper, and it will shield you. Do not worry, I have trained it. It listens. And...

speaker: Lichen
content: If the Yin energy grows too heavy, take these elixir pills. A few when you are well will not hurt; they stir the blood and mend the flesh. Just do not overdo it, or you will burn from within.

speaker: Lichen
content: Oh! I almost forgot the most important thing...
With exaggerated solemnity, she produces her terminal, lights up the screen, and waves it before your eyes like a sacred offering.
But don't give me everything. You need to keep some for yourself. I'll be careful there.
Besides... if all else fails, I still have the copper coin.
At this, her brows furrow and she bites her lip.

speaker: Lichen
content: Eh... Mmm... I mean, you are not wrong, but that old coin can only flip up or down. It's just a rigid and dull thing that cannot answer the hard questions... Use my Ziwei Diviner app instead!

speaker: Lichen
content: See? On one hand, an ancient relic. On the other, modern high-tech. Clearly superior, would you not say? Besides, you told me yourself, young friend, that I'm the reliable one.
...But this thing isn't even connected to the internet. How's that different from a paperweight?

You glance down at the armful of paper talismans and treasures she's pressed upon you and decide to keep that thought to yourself. Instead, you accept the terminal, now sealed with one of her papers, and hold it carefully. Supposedly, the paper talisman will allow you to bring it into your dreams.

speaker: Lichen
content: One last thing. If you see my shifu again, do not fixate on apologies. You cannot weather her temper alone. When the time comes, remember—
She waves the little white fish in her hand.

speaker: Lichen
content: I will bring you back. And then, together, we will go and make amends.
...Mm, you have my word. But while I'm asleep, no rash moves. You promised me.

options: I'm counting on you to protect me.

content: Her eyes crinkle into a smile.

speaker: Lichen
content: But of course. Trust in me, and fear not.
You clutch her gifts to your chest, wondering if any of them will truly follow you into that ghost city.
But for now, you walk. A stretch, then a rest. Her pace has slowed noticeably. Her strikes against the monsters come heavier, slower.
You hold her hand and match her step, listening to her ramble, her silly jokes landing soft in the quiet.
If you didn't know why she'd slowed, you might almost enjoy this. Taking it easy. Being with her. But you do know.
And then, during one rest, your eyes slip closed. And you're falling—into the dream again...
[Scene Transition]
You open your eyes to the Void of Yin, just as you knew you would. Lichen's treasures rest in your arms, now veiled in a thin gray haze.
The copper coin has also returned, silent and present.
The bell's song pulls you forward, past the final flagstone, to the foot of a stone bridge.
Before it, a polished tablet where cyan characters shift and flow until, slowly, they resolve into meaning:
<color=#00ae9d>To cross over is to let go.</color>
You step onto the bridge.
And there she is, a pale cyan figure leaning against the railing, nearly one with the stone. As if she has always been here. As if she has been waiting for you.
You're close enough now to trace the embroidery on her clothes. But the bell's chime doesn't grow clearer. Only more fractured, more scattered.
You stare at her, and with each heartbeat, she feels more known. Time slips, and you don't know how long you've stood here.
She hasn't seen you. Her slender shoulders droop, face tilted down, one hand pressed to her waist. Through her fingers, cyan light drifts—slow, aimless, like breath escaping.
You can't see her face. Can't know if she's in pain.
It reminds you of Lichen, standing before you and parting the dark mist with that faint smile. You never knew how much pain she carried. You still don't.
A suspicion rises. No, it's always been there. You've just stopped pretending not to see.
You step closer. Your lips part, hesitant, trembling on the edge of sound—
But <color=#fb9259>the name</color> catches, staying locked behind your teeth. You can't say it. You can't.
She only turns her hollow mask, just slightly, toward you.
...You again.
Have you come... to ask something of me... again?
You shake your head and come to a stop before her.
I just came to see you.
Your fingers find one of Lichen's elixir pills. You set it on the railing beside her, hoping, though you don't know if hope means anything here.
If just looking at you counts as a favor... then if you need it, consider this payment.
The moment it's set down, a sheen of moisture blooms across its surface.
She lifts her hand. The elixir pill thins to mist and threads through her fingers, and the glow bleeding from beneath her ribs seems to slow.
...This is enough. You don't need to give me anything.
You stare at your empty palm. The bittersweet smell, her smell, stays with you—sharp and familiar.
I just want to look at you. That's all.
She offers no reaction, as if the very concept of your words is something she can't comprehend.
A long moment passes. Then she rises, wordless, and drifts toward the bridge's far end where the fog pools thick and white.
You follow. Only your footsteps echo, sharp against the emptiness, soon swallowed by the mist until even you are lost in it.

You follow. Then, the path simply falls away, and your footsteps vanish into a silence so complete it seems to swallow sound before it's even made. You are adrift among floating stone steles, their surfaces etched with alphabets turned to dust by time.

She glides ahead, a fixed point in this formless place. She never turns, never questions your presence. And truth be told, the reason eludes you, too. But deep within, a question, fragile as a held breath, is beginning to form.
Will you let it surface?
Or does the greater terror lie not in breaking the rules, but in what the answer might reveal?
High above, the drifting fish begin to glow, one by one, like paper lanterns kindled by the dusk. Their song follows—long, plaintive notes that hang in the air like a farewell.
Then, her voice returns, soft at your side.
[CG]
No joy nor grief finds release... bitter lament stretches long...

Pale phantoms drift into view, their forms frozen in gestures of grief: some prostrate, others hunched as though bearing the weight of the sky. A few bury their faces in their palms while ash and earth slip through their fingers like hourglass sands. Others cradle small, brittle bodies, limbs as thin as winter twigs.
Their anguished wails rise and become rain, a gentle drizzle that passes straight through you, leaving only a chill behind.

You cannot understand their words, only to see rolling green hills stretching endlessly toward a horizon that offers no solace. Beneath them, new graves are heaped upon old, layer after layer, so quickly that even wild grass cannot take root.
She moves ahead. You quicken your pace, watching her. Her mask betrays nothing, and yet, with each phantom she passes, her head droops a little lower, as if bearing the weight of every single one.
Alas for years misspent... obsession clings, stubborn and strong...

She reaches for them. Those monstrous fingers extend with impossible tenderness, and as they do, tiny embers kindle across her body, drifting from her skin and floating toward the specters on the wind.
One by one, all that sorrow and anguish begin to recede, flowing away like water. Soon, a river stretches between you and them, wide and deep and ever onward, carrying their grief into the distance.

Something tender swells in your chest, a feeling that presses against your ribs, urging you to weep. But your thoughts are growing hazy now, and even that impulse softens, blurs, becomes distant and unreal.
You look ahead. Her silhouette is fading, growing so faint that one more step might let the current take her too.
You stop.
[CG]
She finally turns to look at you, her lips curving into the faintest of smiles.
...Fear not.
—Suddenly, you remember again.
Why you followed her through all of this. The question that you have been wanting to ask.
You reach for her. That blood-red hand, the same one that once dealt you nightmares—you grasp for it now. But your fingers, human fingers of flesh and bone, pass through her palm like smoke.
Her hand rises, and she traces a gentle arc through the air.
[CG]
Warm ashes of a bygone dream... a single lamp illumes the vain...
Old friends, scattered and lost... a solitary form, wrapped in pain...
One by one, the swimming fish gather around you. They press close, their forms warm and luminous, encircling you in a silent embrace.
This fleeting life now ferried o'er... the mortal realm fades from thought...
Hand in hand, I bid thee farewell... from my home, forever I am brought.
Gently, they lift, carrying you away from that river woven of sorrow and death.
You instinctively reach down. Your hand grasps at emptiness, trying to hold onto something. But then, from the air behind you, a muffled voice drifts forward.

speaker: Vague Voice
content: <size=28>From dream's deep, return; by light's edge, the gates unseal... </size>From dream's deep, return; by light's edge, the gates unseal!
But you still have questions for her. Questions that only she can answer.
Questions you would pay any price to ask. Questions worth bearing any curse.
The words leave your lips, and the last fragment of your sanity scatters like ash in a wind you cannot feel.
<color=#00ae9d>To cross over is to let go.</color>

Your body grows ever lighter. You drift upward, reaching, grasping, but your fingers close only on scattered fragments of light. The fish talisman slips free from your arms, swimming through the air toward her.
Her mask turns slightly, tilting as if to welcome its return. And in that instant, finally, you see the eyes beneath it.
They are not the eyes of a monster. Not the eyes of a vengeful spirit. Just Lichen's eyes.

Those eyes watch you as you rise. They grow smaller, more distant, but they do not look away. The light around her dims. She stands like a tall, slender stele, merging into the boundless void and the shattered garden of stones that surrounds her.
—That is the last thing you see.

speaker: Lichen
content: ...From dream's deep, return; by light's edge, the gates unseal... From dream's—

speaker: Lichen
content: Oh, you're finally awake... Settle!

Your eyes are forced open, yet the cold mist of the dream still clings to you, seeping through your skin. Only when something pokes your forehead again—insistent, familiar—does consciousness begin to trickle back.
Lichen is right there, her eyes meeting yours. You grasp her sleeve. Your grip tightens, and your hand slides down until you find her wrist—warmth, pulse, the steady rhythm of life.
She pauses, startled by your desperation, then reaches out to feel your forehead before finally letting out a sigh of relief.

speaker: Lichen
content: You were gone so long this time. Even the Yin fish lost its thread halfway... You really had me worried.

speaker: Lichen
content: What happened?
She looks you up and down, but can't find what she's searching for.
I think it should be fine.

speaker: Lichen
content: When?! Did she do something to you?
But the little fish swam over to her. So I don't have it on me now.

speaker: Lichen
content: Whew... I was afraid she'd try to keep you there again like last time...
You shake your head.
I didn't ask anything I shouldn't have. So she didn't ask anything of me.

speaker: Lichen
content: Ah... Well done, young friend. Smart and steady. That puts my mind at ease.

speaker: Lichen
content: But how did the Yin fish end up with my shifu...? Did she subdue it, or...

speaker: Lichen
content: Given where things stand now, can we still use the Yang fish to trace it...?

Seeing you safe, she relaxes, shoulders softening. Then, as if flipping a switch, she resumes counting on her fingers, muttering under her breath. Her face cycles through expressions: puzzlement, concentration, and the occasional furrow of deep thought.
You watch her for a while, taking in her ever-shifting yet radiant expressions. At last, you break the silence.

speaker: Lichen
content: Hmm?
I don't think I know you as well as I should. Tell me about your shifu.

speaker: Lichen
content: Hmm... To be honest, my memory's a little blurry. I wasn't that old when she left, and it's been so long. What I remember best is getting scolded whenever I got into trouble.

speaker: Lichen
content: I am grateful she predicted the Perishing Star, though. I didn't believe her at the time, but she kept me pinned at home the day of the Nightfall. At least that spared me the worst of it.

speaker: Lichen
content: Oh, did I never mention? Shifu is actually a distant relative of mine. The Tianyi Sect? Family business. Kept behind closed doors, just between us.
Lichen winks at you. You open your mouth to speak, but the words catch in your throat. It takes a moment before you finally manage to ask:
...Did it hurt? Letting her go?

speaker: Lichen
content: It was alright. Grief comes, grief goes. Those who seek the Dao learn to let go. Every year on her death anniversary, I bring some treats to her grave and let her have a sniff. Filial enough, I think. As for mourning... I'm nothing compared to her fans online.

speaker: Lichen
content: Honestly? I think Shifu suffered more from her prophecies than anything. When the Perishing Star came, and she lost her mind... in a way, it was a mercy.

Is it the Eastian way? Or simply the mark of a generation that knew how to let things go? Life and death and parting—she touches each one with such gentleness, such ease, as though they were ordinary as morning light. And suddenly your own sorrow feels like a stone you have carried too long.
I thought... you couldn't let go. That's why you pushed yourself to come here. To bring her back...
Your words amuse her. A soft laugh escapes, and then she's sweeping you into her arms, holding you tight. Her hand finds your hair and ruffles it with reckless affection.

speaker: Lichen
content: You are worried about me? Oh, you—such a good kid! So precious!
Hey...! Stop messing my hair up!

After a bit of playful tussling, she finally stills. But she doesn't let you go. Instead, she draws you closer, tucking you into her arms for warmth. Her chin comes to rest atop your head, and together, you gaze out at the hazy ruins in the distance.

speaker: Lichen
content: Truth be told, my Daoist arts aren't all that refined. My divination's barely accurate. I prefer the odd and unconventional, all in good fun, never digging too deep. Forget comparing me to Shifu; I might not even outdo that copper coin of yours.

speaker: Lichen
content: It was only after the Perishing Star fell that my hodgepodge arts slowly started working. More convincing by the day. More people came seeking help. Bit by bit... I actually became a proper Daoist.
Was it the shift in the Mania field that triggered her awakening? Her Mania power? Though she'd probably never heard of it.

options: Because the Perishing Star changed the Dao of Heaven?

speaker: Lichen
content: There's a theory that says the great calamity threw heaven and earth out of balance—Yin and Yang in chaos, evil spirits running wild. That's what gave my unorthodox methods power. Enough to overwhelm the orthodox ones.

speaker: Lichen
content: There's some truth to it. But it's too stiff. I don't care for such a lifeless explanation.

options: Then what do you think it is...?

content: She gazes into the distance, her eyes growing ever more pensive.

speaker: Lichen
content: I believe the Daoist arts make no distinction between righteous and wicked, good and evil. The Dao of Heaven is chaos; we'll never be able to fully grasp it. Arts that fulfill the wishes of the believers... those are good arts.

speaker: Lichen
content: ...And what <color=#fb9259>people believe in</color> will have power.
You pause, struck by her words.
Yes. You have heard this theory before. Not in DisCity. Not from anything resembling science.
But somewhere far from here and now—nearly a century later, thousands of miles away in <color=#fb9259>Eastia</color>—someone, it seems, has proven it true.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Hypercubes don't exist in Eastia. Facing the Apostle, people could only rely on their faith in the Sun Shot legend. In other words, they were fighting the product of collective will with their collective will.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: When the Great Seer crafted the Almighty Bow, she was activating this immense spiritual power. No matter how many times she failed, she always had that faith. This, Yanyan is surely capable of.

options: Is this wisdom from the Eastern Continent?

content: She smiles and waves the question away.

speaker: Lichen
content: Figured it out myself. Haven't published a paper yet.

speaker: Lichen
content: Before the Nightfall, even with all the conflict and war, people still clung to "science." Those who came to me or my shifu were mostly looking for entertainment. No one truly believed in the Daoist arts, so the arts never took hold.

speaker: Lichen
content: But after the Nightfall, everything changed.

speaker: Lichen
content: That baleful star, and everything it brought, could neither be explained nor stopped. Science, common sense, all of it useless. Everything people once believed in was uprooted and swept away. And in its place, irrational faith captured their attention.

speaker: Lichen
content: Praying to gods. Worshipping Buddha. Embracing the supernatural. The more mysterious and incomprehensible, the better. That way, the slightest miracle could be taken as divine intervention, a flicker of hope.

speaker: Lichen
content: ...As if believing in something—finding the right method, praying to the right being—could restore the world to its former grace. As if what was lost might still return.

speaker: Lichen
content: You see, fortune and misfortune go hand in hand. It was that sorrowful faith that granted our arts their power.

In this silent, labyrinthine city, the two of you are barely more than specks, adrift among endless stone corridors. Yet when you look up at her, you see it: the vast heavens, the twisted stars, the whole sprawling cosmos reflected in her eyes.
Then her smile fades. Her gaze sharpens, unbent by anyone or anything. She is looking at something you cannot see. Something far beyond.

speaker: Lichen
content: That is why I must see my shifu. She has become an icon to hundreds of followers, and they hope she will truly rise from the dead, just as they long for their own loved ones to return.

speaker: Lichen
content: And if... my shifu can truly return from the Void of Yin, then the path I seek will finally have its answer.

speaker: Lichen
content: And you, young friend, would no longer have to fear losing anyone.

You watch her. You cannot stop watching her—those cyan eyes, the small mole between her brows, the gentle curve of her smile. You keep watching until your knuckles blanch white. Until your nails bite crescents into your palms.
She notices. Gently, she pries your fingers open. Only then do you feel the sharp, waking pain of flesh remembering itself.
You look away.
...The place you're going is really dangerous. Aren't you afraid at all?
It's too dangerous. It's really dangerous there. I don't want you to go. What if you run into something even your divination can't foresee?

speaker: Lichen
content: Cross each bridge as it comes. I've studied so many mystical arts precisely to have more ways to handle situations like this.

options: What if those don't work either?

speaker: Lichen
content: Then I'll adapt and wait for the right moment. The path will reveal itself when the time comes. I'm patient; I can wait for my chance to act.

options: What if the path never reveals itself?

content: What if you actually die this time?
What if all your resolve means nothing?
Your barrage of questions comes like stones cast into still water, but her smile does not ripple.

speaker: Lichen
content: Then that, too, shall be my destiny, a fate I've sealed with my own hands.
As if sensing the weight her words would carry, she pulls you closer the moment she finishes speaking, still smiling.

speaker: Lichen
content: It's not so frightening, really. Don't let appearances fool you. This humble Daoist is more meticulous than she seems. I've made all the necessary preparations. Look—
[Big CG 02]

She tucks a strand of stray hair behind her ear, and in the same motion, an Eastian rune drifts lazily through the air before hooking itself onto her earlobe. With her peculiar arts, she has made herself a curious little earring.

speaker: Lichen
content: Artifacts, talismans... I've got plenty more on me. Enough to save my life several times over! And with you, my auspicious star, by my side? Everything will be just fine.

speaker: Lichen
content: Once I meet my shifu, I'll kneel and pay my respects properly. While I'm at it, I'll put in a good word for you—

speaker: Lichen
content: You've helped me so much on this journey, young friend. Perhaps you could earn yourself the title of "honorary disciple"? Then I would be your senior.

She beams with pride, tilting her head to invite you to touch this little creation of hers. Her smile is radiant, like sunlight breaking through a century of clouds, warming you where you stand. A moment you will carry forever.
But you don't reach out.
You don't dare.

...You fear that the instant your fingers meet her, she will dissolve. That the boundary between dream and reality will shatter, and you will fall back into that other space, that other time, so recently visited, where you truly touched something. And it was not this.
[Big CG 03-04]

You have reached out before. You have truly touched her face. In the depths of that lonely darkness, the sensation traveled through your fingertips—cold, rigid, immovable—and pierced straight into your heart like a shard of ice.

It could only be the body of someone long dead. A hollow shell, her soul long scattered, held together only by runes sprawling across her form, dark Eastian Daoist arts pulsing beneath the skin. You know who cast the spell.

—Only one person would so arrogantly trample the boundaries of life and death. Only one would so cruelly enslave the remains of the departed. Only one would so mercilessly... deny even herself any peace.
You know what your palm touched was real. You know this is how her story ends. And yet, the questions only multiply—
How did it come to this?

Was she lost in the ruins, no way forward, no way back? Did Shin's whispers lure her into the abyss? Or did the forbidden path demand too much? Too many questions. Too many answers. Until the price came due.

Now adrift in this cold tide of death, what does she feel? Is she still that same girl, open-hearted and free-spirited, as you remember? Or has she become like the countless phantoms she once guided onward? Lost, anguished, lingering without end. Does she know now? That her pursuit of transcending life and death was nothing but a fool's dream, even after a hundred years? That the path she sought was merely a tiny flicker of light beneath the boundless night sky, gone in an instant, as though it never was?
All her life, she read the signs and asked the heavens. She believed in omens, in fate, in you—her auspicious star. So before she began this long journey—
Did she already know how it would end?
...And if she knew, did she still choose to walk toward it?
—These are questions you must not ask. You know the rules of the Void of Yin. <color=#fb9259>Offer no glance to the departed. Lend no ear to the abyss. Speak no question to the spirits.</color>
But even so... even so...
Is there still time... for me to do something for you?
Her lifeless eyes lifted slightly, meeting yours for a moment before lowering again. A soft chuckle escaped her.

speaker: Lichen
content: Heh...
You spoke after all, breaking the taboo. Yet, fortunately, no punishment came.
It seemed, that time, even the Void of Yin had no answer to give.
[Return to the Surface World]
A cool breeze sweeps through you, clearing the haze from your thoughts. You come back to your senses just as Lichen shivers before you, her eyes lighting up.

speaker: Lichen
content: Ah, I've found the Yin fish. It's near. Will you stay here, or come with me, young friend?

speaker: Lichen
