content: The trouble yonder seems still for now, and I'm rested. Either way, I can take you with me, or leave a ward for your keeping.

In the distance, dark mist rolls in like tidal waves, devouring the light above you inch by inch. Your tiny shadows are swallowed whole. The paths through the ruins twist and turn, just as chaotic as fate's crossroads.
Lichen has already risen. She gazes toward the road ahead, the one that was always waiting for her.
She looks just as she did long ago, sitting by her window, watching distant mountains burn, watching endless incense smoke curl at her doorstep.
...But you cannot accept it. Not yet. Not this.

speaker: Lichen
content: Ah, that gladdens me even more. The elders in my sect always said a restless soul like mine would surely bring some calamity one day, if left unwatched.

speaker: Lichen
content: Hehe, but those fools never saw that I would meet you, young friend.
She crouches before you, taking your hands in hers. Your fingertips meet, warmth against warmth.

speaker: Lichen
content: If I do wander too far, just call my name. Whenever you call, I will answer.
As your fingers part, delicate threads of light linger between your fingertips. For one heart-stopping instant, they hold, and then they scatter, dissolving into the air like an illusion.

speaker: Lichen
content: Fear not. I will return to you.
You answer her in the silence of your heart.
—You will. I will bring you back.

The Yin-Yang fish talisman guides your steps until you stand before a mass of thick, churning fog. It surges and rolls like a living thing, yet the air around you is perfectly still. Not a whisper of wind reaches your ears.
Lichen stares into that ominous gray, her chest rising and falling in shallow, careful breaths. Her fingers tighten around the jade pendant until her knuckles blanch.

speaker: Lichen
content: This is the place. No doubt about it.

The moment she steels her will, the gray-white fog holds still, just for an instant. Then it begins to turn, spiraling inward like a slow, silent whirlpool. At its heart, a figure takes shape: a faded robe, indistinct at first, then slowly gathering into form.

speaker: Lichen
content: ...Shifu. I finally found you.
Her tone is certain as she slowly paces forward, one deliberate step.
Wait! That's—
But the figure that forms before you is not the elderly Daoist Lichen described. It is her. The mask, the one you know too well.
Yet she appears more real now than she ever was in the Void of Yin. Every thread of her robe stands out with impossible clarity. Light plays across her mask's smooth surface.
—You are not <color=#fb9259>seeing</color> her. She <color=#fb9259>exists</color> within your consciousness.
In an instant, the silence shatters into a thousand whispering fragments: broken prayers tumbling from unseen lips, each one burning with fevered devotion.

The words find your ears. They burrow, insects with hard shells and tiny, jointed limbs that scrape against tender flesh as they force their way deeper. Into your skull. Into your mind. And there, in the fertile dark, they birth new things—countless eggs that pulse and squirm, already hatching.

speaker: Eldritch Voice
content: Incense unending... the divine gaze falls...

Around the phantom, hazy figures materialize from the gloom. They throw themselves to the ground, foreheads pressing into dust, worshipping. And as they bow their heads, they hurl clots of dark, viscous matter toward the one who stands at the center.

speaker: Eldritch Voice
content: Beseeching the sacred writ... pardon from the turning wheel...
Pale blue flames ignite at her feet, crackling softly at first, then building into a fierce, hungry roar.

She does not move. Her mask shows nothing: no joy, no sorrow, no pain. The fire climbs. Her robes char and curl, falling away to reveal pale flesh beneath. In the heat, skin begins to peel from her ankles, slowly, strip by strip.
Then, a myriad voices rise as one—

speaker: Eldritch Voice
content: Flesh given to the Dao... shelter your servants... The underworld awaits... all shall be rendered...

speaker: Eldritch Voice
content: All... shall be rendered...!
No... No... Don't go... That's not...!
You open your mouth, but all sound is swallowed by an overwhelming hollowness.
The phantom lifts her masked face, just slightly.
Around her, the devotees freeze. A tableau of worship arrested mid-prayer. Then, in a motion too synchronized, their faces turn to find you.
[Transition 1s]
<color=#dg1f1f>But they have no faces.</color>

speaker: Lichen
content: ...Heh, these are indeed the arts of the Tianyi Sect. Step back, young friend.

speaker: Lichen
content: Let me handle this.

Lichen's hands flash through a rapid series of seals, her fingertips dancing with practiced precision. From her sleeves, thunder paper talismans tear through the air, each one finding its mark square in the foreheads of the lunging specters.

speaker: Lichen
content: Sky overturns, earth submits; drive the thunder, race the clouds... Break!
Thunderclaps rupture the swarm in rapid succession, each blast a hammer of light against the dark. The phantoms scream as their forms unravel, their shadows bleeding away under the relentless glare.
When the last echo fades, only the acrid scent of scorching remains, hanging heavy in the air. Sparks of lightning, scattered and dying, flicker one final time before surrendering to the mist.
Lichen stands frozen, her chest rising and falling in quick, shallow breaths. At the far edge of her vision, the figure waits—still, shrouded, wreathed in thin mist.
Her throat moves. A swallow, small and quiet. Then a step. Another.

Her fingertips meet the mist. They gray instantly, as though the color itself is bleeding out of her. One more step and she crosses over. One more step and her wish is fulfilled. But every instinct in you screams:
—Don't let them meet!

You grab her sleeve, mind racing for words to hold her back. But if words fail, you have one last resort: the Prohibition. All this time, you've been drawing on the Mania seeping from the Void of Yin, channeling power desperately to release the shackles. Pouring everything you have into stopping her.
And now, in a way you never wanted, your wish is coming true.
[White Flash]
Clink—!
A crisp, resonant chime of one copper coin suddenly rings out from deep within the mist.
Bzzzz— Clank, clank—

speaker: Lichen
content: This sound... It's...!!
A deep lurch runs through the earth, as though the ground itself is being pulled by countless dragging chains. From far below, a grinding chorus rises, iron singing its slow, terrible song.

The mist parts, torn asunder, and from the rift steps a figure clad in ancient bronze. Chains trail beneath its feet. Upon its back, a coffin rests. The thing is ink-black, bound in red threads, covered in paper talismans that seem to writhe.
What is this now...?!
It moves toward you. Each step is a labor. Its spine bends low, almost to breaking, crushed beneath a weight it was never meant to carry. And yet it continues. It has no other way.

speaker: Coffin Ghost
content: Ohhh... ohhhhh...

A muffled roar forces its way up from somewhere deep within the monstrosity. It raises one enormous hand, palm streaked dark red and black, fingers thick as roots. Lichen stands forgotten. The hand closes around the masked figure's neck in the mist, gripping tight.

speaker: Lichen
content: —Stop!
She raises her hand. From above, swords of living lightning rain down, each one piercing the dark specter's body with blinding precision.
[White Flash]
It wails, a sound that tears through the air, and staggers backward, wounded. But through it all, that massive hand never once loosens its grip on the silent figure it holds.

The mist recoils, surging away to reveal what it had hidden: a dark, profound rift, yawning like a wound in the world. One by one, the malevolent entities are dragged back, pulled back to wherever they came from.

speaker: Lichen
content: Wait! Let her go!!
Lichen!
You lift your foot to move, and the world stops. A voice, ancient and deep, rises from the depths of your own mind. Each syllable falls like a hammer. Each blow cracks something inside your skull.
Mmph—!
Reality ripples. Through the distortion, Lichen's form reforms, and for a heartbeat, she wears that face. That mask.
Then the fragmented words emerge. They drift loose on the air like scattered petals, until they gather into a single, screaming line of red before you.

<color=#dg1f1f><size=60>Offer no glance to the departed.
Lend no ear to the abyss.
Speak no question to the spirits.</color></size>

<color=#dg1f1f><size=60>Offer no glance to the departed.
Lend no ear to the abyss.
Speak no question to the spirits.</color></size>

The rift convulses, folding in on itself like a wounded thing. It seals with a soundless finality, swallowing the copper coin that has turned into the coffin ghost, the phantom in the ghost's grip, and that warning. All of it, gone.
Lichen rushes toward the last shimmering traces, and crimson flames leap from her fingertips.

speaker: Lichen
content: Heaven and earth overturned; Yin and Yang reversed!
The rift does not yield quietly. It lashes out, a violent surge of crimson flame that throws her backward. She can only watch as the Void of Yin's tear seals shut completely.

speaker: Lichen
content: ...Nngh!
Are you alright?

You catch her before she falls. Carefully, you lift her sleeve; beneath it, the wound that had only just begun to mend has torn itself open again. Blood wells, trails down her wrist, falls in slow drops to the mud below. But...
She laughs.

The sound is fractured, unfamiliar, echoing through the mist like something that does not belong to her. Around you, the rift has sealed. The evil spirits have withdrawn. Lichen stands at your side. And yet the air grows colder. The light withdraws. The world holds its breath.

speaker: Lichen
content: ...After all this, just a little more... and still they try to stop me... every single time...

speaker: Lichen
content: It's unfair...

speaker: Lichen
content: I will show you...

The last echo of laughter fades into a heavy silence. A shadow passes over Lichen's features, her playful demeanor gone. She starts forming hand seals, and from the space between her fingers, golden runes flow. It isn't until you see them that the connection is made:
The other "Lichen" bears these very same symbols.
A spike of raw alarm shoots through you, and your grip on her tightens.
That monster didn't hurt your shifu. I saw it. It fled into the Void of Yin with her. Your shifu's still out there. She's safe. You're the one bleeding right now.
Let's stop for a moment. Let me tend to your wound, and then we'll figure out the next move. Okay?
Your words fail to ease the tension.

speaker: Lichen
content: The Dao I seek is right before me, yet you'd have me retreat for the sake of safety? Hah... Do I look that faint of heart?

speaker: Lichen
content: Worry not. Since that coffin ghost appeared... the one commanding the copper coin must be near. They will protect you.

speaker: Lichen
content: I will not be staying. My mind is still racing, and besides... I still have to go after my shifu.

She reaches up to pat your head as usual, but her movements are stiff, mechanical. Her gaze is locked on the distance, the exact direction the coffin ghost fled, deep into the ruined city. Flames flicker to life among the runes on her fingers, and on the air, faintly, you hear the drone of chaos.
A cold spike of dread pierces through you. Without heeding the danger, you grab her hand and force it down, crushing the flames in your shared grip. You have to stop her.
The motion finally breaks her trance. Slowly, she turns to look at you.

speaker: Lichen
content: Why are you still trying to stop me?
A single glance from her sends a chill through you, her tone ice-cold. You grit your teeth and hold your ground.
...The Void of Yin is too dangerous. You won't survive it. Last time you forced your way in, the backlash nearly killed you. And now you're alone...

speaker: Lichen
content: But I brought you back, did I not? This time, I will do the same for my shifu.
Lichen's gaze darkens, the light in it guttering like a candle in a void. You search her eyes desperately, looking for a trace of her—the one you know.

But that familiarity is a trap. It only shows you the other "Lichen" reflected in this one. The fearlessness and irreverence, the resolve and obsession, the wildness teetering on madness—they've always tangled in her, separated not by the barrier between the two worlds but merely by a fleeting thought.
...You have to hold her back. By any means necessary.

options: You can't do this alone. I have to come with you...

content: Your grip on her hand tightens slowly, as you channel your strength into the shackles.
The Mania here is too thin to summon the red spikes, but it's enough for her to sense something at work. Enough for her to feel the strange, unusual connection blooming between you.

speaker: Lichen
content: This is...?
...Seems like some kind of spell. It protects me from time to time when I'm in the Void of Yin.

Last time you forced your way in, you barely made it a few steps before the Void's backlash tore into you. I panicked and somehow threw up this spell to shield you. You're deep enough in the craft, so you must've felt it, right? Without it, we'd probably both be dead.
This is the real <color=#fb9259>key</color> to crossing between worlds. If you want to enter the Void of Yin and bring your shifu back, rushing in alone won't work. You need me.
She says nothing. Her gaze drops to your clasped hands, resting there like a weight. What she's thinking, you cannot tell.
You take a deep breath, withdraw the shackles, and soften your voice:

speaker: Chief
content: You said it yourself: "Cross each bridge as it comes." In plain terms, every problem's got a solution, and you just need the right one, right? I'm that solution. Or at least, better than you going solo.
She offers no response.

speaker: Chief
content: And if that's not enough, you also said to adapt and wait for the right moment. Whether it's finding your shifu or chasing the Dao of Heaven, there's no rush. The more impatient you are, the further you'll be.

speaker: Chief
content: Maybe we wait here for the others? Once everyone's regrouped, our odds get a lot better. Don't you think?

Silence stretches between you. Then, finally, she looks up. Her eyes travel from your intertwined hands to your face, and when they lock with yours, a faint smile curves her lips, encouraging you to continue.
You steel yourself.

speaker: Chief
content: ...If you're really that anxious, I'll go. I'll find her for you. Right now.

speaker: Chief
content: I know that place. I can catch up. I'll try to reason with that copper coin, and if that fails... I'll help your shifu take the monster down. My "spell" works better in the Void of Yin. I'll bring her back to you. I promise.

Will this even work? You catch the faint shadow that passes through her eyes. Annoyance? Suspicion? Or are you just seeing things, hoping and fearing in equal measure? Regardless, you keep holding her hand tightly.
Then she laughs—soft, almost fond—and tilts her head back. When she speaks, her voice is leisurely, amused:

speaker: Lichen
content: ...No wonder my divination said I would meet a sage and have my wishes granted. It seems the prophecy was true. You have guided me through confusion time and again, young friend. Every word you speak holds truth.

speaker: Lichen
content: Blinded by a single leaf... Yes. I was so desperate to find my shifu, so eager to break into the Void of Yin, that obsession clouded my sight. I didn't even notice...
She's still smiling, but her eyes are cold. They narrow as they trace over you with an interest that feels less like recognition and more like appraisal.

speaker: Lichen
content: You are the remarkable one, young friend. Such power, such wit and nerve, such insight and magnanimity...

speaker: Lichen
content: Since when did our guide grow into someone I barely recognize? You no longer resemble that "child" at all.
She raises her hand as if to pat your head again, but her fingers trail along the side of your face instead. They press gently against your skin, tracing the shape of the bones beneath.
You stiffen at the touch, every instinct screaming. Then you force it down. You puff out your cheeks, straighten your back, and let your voice climb higher, sweeter, deliberately childish:
But there's a condition! You have to promise to stay here. Don't run off before I'm back. Wait for me. Because...

...I-I scare easy. If something happens, I can't make it back alone. I need someone up here to pull me out, to yank me back the second things go wrong. You've got Daoist arts, right? Only you can do that!
She watches you for a long moment. Finally, her gaze seems to soften, and she nods.

speaker: Lichen
content: Hehe... You speak truly, young friend. I was too narrow-minded.

speaker: Lichen
content: Perhaps following your lead is the wiser path.
She withdraws her hand seals and steps back, her expression settling into something almost calm. Did you manage to reach her? The breath you've been holding loosens, just slightly.

This is for the best. She has to stay behind. If she ventures deeper into the Void of Yin, she'll only break more rules without a second thought. That place belongs to the dead, governed by the rules of the phantoms. And if something happens to her there...
You can't foresee the consequences. That uncertainty is what truly terrifies you.

This is for the best. Lichen understands now. She can't go alone. And once you leave her sight and head in—whether you find the copper coin, the coffin ghost, or the other "Lichen"—you'll deal with it.
Instinct screams beneath your thoughts: You must not let the two Lichens meet. No matter what.
You've figured it out. You have a plan. Then a finger presses against your chest. Its tip blazes, heat scorching the entire index finger red-hot.
A vermillion rune materializes from thin air, slamming into you like a brand. It merges with your flesh, sinks deep, and leaves no trace behind.
This is...?

speaker: Lichen
content: A protection talisman. Keep it close... The enemy you face this time is no small matter. With this, I can offer you some safety for a while longer, just as I did before.

You open your mouth to ask, but she reaches out first. One finger presses gently against the space between your brows. Then, the world bleeds away, slowly sinking into darkness like ink spreading through water.

speaker: Lichen
content: Go now, young friend. I will be waiting for your answer.
In this vast expanse of nothing, her cyan eyes remain fixed on you—watching, ever watching.
Creak... Clang... Scrrrch...

The coffin ghost never looks back, only a relentless sprint forward. Its claws strike the ground like iron hooves, each impact sending a low tremor shuddering through the earth. On the coffin board strapped to its back, faint runes writhe and ripple in the dappled light.

The ground beneath you appears deceptively solid and flat, yet every step you take sinks into a wet, sucking mire. It slows your progress, a sickening familiarity to it—a phantom pain from Maria City. Could the boundaries between the Realm of Yang and the Void of Yin have warped and merged again?
Once more, that cold, dark voice echoes from the depths of your mind:

speaker: Shin?
content: Fragile minds trace and retrace boundaries... but boundaries are just cages the weak build for themselves...

speaker: Shin?
content: Cast off fear. Transcend limits. Then, reach the end you seek. And see what's been hidden all along...
You refuse to dwell on those words any longer. Gritting your teeth, you call out to the coffin ghost.
You don't have to run! I'm not your enemy! I just want to confirm something with you—
The coffin ghost hesitates. Its footsteps falter, and it begins to turn.
Then, they strike.
Shadows launch from Lichen's gourd—paper figures, springing to life.
You snatch one from the air. It writhes in your grip. A crimson gash splits open across its face like a mouth, and it clamps down hard on the webbing between your thumb and forefinger.
Mmph—!
At the sharp pain, you fling it away. Your skin is unbroken, but the sting pulses with sickening reality.
More of them cling to the coffin ghost like a swarm of leeches, shrieking as they tear into it with frenzied hunger.
No! Stop!
The ground writhes beneath you, gripping your ankles, pulling you down. You fight to tear free. Ahead, the coffin ghost buckles, its spine bending...

speaker: Shin?
content: Twist. Merge. Reshape. Yes... yes... To be bound by form is to never taste that supreme sweetness...

speaker: Coffin Ghost
content: Ngh... Ahhh...
...Until, with an agonized howl, it snaps.
A gale of fury explodes outward. Mad with pain, the monstrosity swings its iron chains wildly, friend and foe forgotten.
You dive. A strike clips past you, smashing the earth into a deep crater where you just stood.
The near miss is enough. Lichen's gifts ignite. Talismans and implements rocket from your body in a blinding cascade, hurling themselves at the shrieking ghost.

speaker: Coffin Ghost
content: AAARRGHH!
It meets the assault head-on. Crimson flame blooms across its form, consuming it. It charges toward you, then a leap—
[Red Flash, Add Phantom Effect After This Line]
And it hangs, suspended mid-lunge, as if something has caught it by the throat.
Below, the ground has given birth to something dark. Arms of black mire coil around the coffin ghost's legs, anchoring it.
The sludge stretches, thinning grotesquely as the ghost thrashes. Within that straining darkness, you swear you hear it: ghostly wailing, muffled moans. Yet the grip holds, relentless and iron.
...Could this be Lichen's doing as well?
The hesitation costs you. The coffin ghost whirls its arm, iron chains screaming toward your face—
You brace for impact, knowing you won't make it. Instead, your body folds in a sharp drop that shouldn't be possible. The iron chain screams past, grazing air where your nose just was.
You didn't move. Something moved you.

A vermillion glow emanates from your chest. It was the protection talisman that forced the dodge that your body could never have performed otherwise, just as Lichen had commanded those phantoms before.
So it works on the living too? She really...
There's no time to dwell on it. While you are dodging, the coffin ghost has already shredded the dark arms. It pivots, coiling for another strike.
The charm Lichen gave you erupts with blinding golden light, slamming straight into the ghost—
[Screen Shakes + White Flash]

The black coffin strikes the earth with a thunderous crash, sending dust spiraling into the air. The coffin ghost dissolves with its form unraveling into nothing. One by one, the red threads fall, crumbling to white ash before they settle.
When the air clears, only a single copper coin remains, lying still in the dust.

You pat yourself down: all the artifacts and talismans Lichen gave you have been destroyed in the battle. Even that terminal's screen is nothing but static now, truly reduced to a piece of scrap metal.
...Perhaps that's a mercy.
You step forward. The silence wraps around you, deep and watchful. Only the soft scrape of your shoes against the ground.
Now it's just us. Can we talk for real this time?
You bend down and pick up the copper coin.

I'm not here to speak for her. I didn't come to demand you return anyone. The opposite, actually, I came to the Void of Yin alone because I didn't want her meeting... the one you just took. That thing.
You rub the copper coin between your fingers. Its surface still feels cold against your fingertips, yet devoid of any presence.
Is it still resisting you?
I've never thought of you as an enemy. Every time I've walked this place, you've kept me from danger, steered me away from the dead, and made sure I never paid their price.
And of course, one of them... is <color=#fb9259>Lichen</color>.
That "Lichen" wandering the Void of Yin... is that what she's becoming? If she keeps walking this path?
That's why you tried so hard to pull that "Lichen" back. You don't want her to end up like that either... do you?
A familiar, crisp clink rings out. For the first time in a while, it lands face-up.
...I see.
Something's clearly wrong with her... A broken taboo?
She forced her way into the Void of Yin to find me. Didn't realize she was being corrupted by its power...
And if the two of them met, the one here and the one out there, that'd make things even worse, wouldn't it?
The copper coin lands face-up once again.
So my instinct was right. But now what...?
What is that phantom? Why does it exist beside Lichen?
You flip the coin again. It wheels through the air, turning end over end—
And lands on its edge.

speaker: Chief
content: What's stopping you now? Did I break another rule? Is this not something I'm allowed to ask?

speaker: Chief
content: Or... do you not know either?

speaker: Chief
content: Then let me ask something else. What are these places—the Realm of Yang and the Void of Yin? Lichen called them "reality" and "dream," but it's more than that, isn't it? Everything I've seen in the Void... that is real too.
You keep tossing the copper coin, but every question meets the same silence. Every answer balanced on a blade, refusing to fall. A wall that will not yield.
But there is one question. One question buried beneath all the others. One question you cannot leave unanswered.

speaker: Chief
content: Is there still time? Can I still bring her back? ...What else can I do?
This time, more than ever, you need it to land face-up. You need a sign, a simple yes.
You flip the copper coin. It shudders in the air, and then—
[Transition + White Flash + Dark Mist Effect Begins]
Its burnished gold surface flakes away, melting into a viscous liquid that drips down in eerie silence.
It hits the ground with a dull, final thud, charred beyond recognition. Face up or down? The question is meaningless now. It's just a lifeless object.
It seems Lichen wasn't entirely right. Even in the Void of Yin, not all questions can be answered.
The answer, it seems, is yours to find alone.
A cold, eerie black aura seeps from the coin's remains and drifts forward like smoke. You follow its trail, and there, at the far end of your vision, lies the black coffin.
The phantom that Lichen has been chasing rests within.
The coffin sits ahead, shrouded in desolate silence, still as stone, like nothing more than an ordinary vessel for the dead.
But you know what lies inside.
The chase ends here. The path meant to transcend life and death. The taboo that the living should never touch. And the one question only you can answer.
Your footsteps echo in lonely solitude. No enemies block your path, no companions offer comfort, and even the phantoms have faded into nothing. No one remains to guide you.
...But perhaps the "Lichen" within is still as gentle as when she bid you farewell? Perhaps you could still ask her for help?

As long as the power stops overflowing. As long as it stays away from the living Lichen. You want her to be safe, and you're willing to pay the price. The question now is: what must you offer for "her" to accept?
You take another step. It's right in front of you now.
The black coffin waits in absolute silence. Not a breath escapes. But you could swear you hear laughter, and your hand lifts toward it—
Clink—
You freeze. The rusted copper coin is still in your hand. You've been turning it over and over without realizing, as if seeking its guidance, as if replaying its warnings on an endless loop.

speaker: Chief
content: Offer no glance to the departed. Lend no ear to the abyss. Speak no question to the spirits...
<color=#dg1f1f>But it's rusted through, rotted away. It can no longer guide you. There's no point in relying on it anymore.</color>
The copper coin clatters to the ground. This time, you don't pick it up. You step over it and press on, until your hand finally rests upon the pitch-black coffin lid.

Incantations cover its surface, carved deep into the wood. Paper talismans layer over them. Red thread winds through the talismans, strung with thousands of cold copper coins. And binding it all together are iron chains as thick as a fist.
Layer upon layer, seal upon seal. Together with the heavy lid, they press down on whatever lies within—airtight, impenetrable, not a single crack left unsealed.
Your hands find the edge of the lid. You begin to push.

A child's palm is thinner than the coffin lid itself. You barely stand half its length. Even with your adult body, you doubt you could move it an inch. Pushing harder is futile. Perhaps you should stop and think of another way.
<color=#dg1f1f>No. You can do this. You just used this very body to evade the monster guarding the coffin.</color>
<color=#dg1f1f>Of course you can... Keep going.</color>

Something takes hold of you, an inexplicable confidence, a force not your own. Your arms grow warm as strength far beyond a child's capability floods through you. The copper coins on the coffin begin to tremble. They corrode before your eyes. Red threads snap. One by one, the seals fall away.
CRRRACK—!
You gather yourself and push. One final, forceful shove. The iron chains that bound the coffin snap apart, crashing down, then crumble to ash in an instant.

The black wood shifts, revealing a thin crack like a pitch-black eye slowly blinking awake. Your mind buzzes. Another scene overlays your vision. Distant sounds flood your ears. The world splits in two.
[Scene Change: Maria City]
...Little guide? Little guide?
Inform the medical department to bring Horo to the interrogation room...
female_content: A strangely familiar voice reaches you, distant and near all at once. Your vision swims, but you can just make out a young man with disheveled, slightly curly hair. He half-kneels on the ground, cradling a child in his arms, gently patting the girl's face and calling out to her.

content: ...Wait. That child... is you?
You passed out? Your consciousness entered the Void of Yin while your body remained behind? Then what... what is all this?
Your gaze drops. Through the haze, you see a blurry torso and blurry hands. Standing over a dozen meters from the unconscious "guide"... You are not the guide.
Then <color=#dg1f1f>who</color> are you right now?
It's no good; the kid won't wake. We've tried every path into the mapping layer. Your copper coin's shattered. If Lichen really is behind this...
□□, could you go talk to her? See if you can get through?
Hmm... Looks like there's no convincing her now.
—Shing.

The blade clears its sheath. Your attention snaps back to the scene before you: A figure stands between the two and <color=#dg1f1f>you</color>. <color=#dg1f1f>You</color> cannot see clearly, only the tip of a sword, leveled directly at <color=#dg1f1f>you</color>.
And from the pommel, a copper coin dangles.
<color=#dg1f1f>You</color> open your mouth to ask, but the voice that emerges is not yours. A familiar one.

speaker: Lichen
content: <color=#dg1f1f>Tossing coins like it's the holiday season? You think that will stop me?</color>

speaker: Lichen
content: <color=#dg1f1f>Too late, old man.</color>

speaker: Lichen
content: <color=#dg1f1f>...That "child" will give me the answer soon enough.</color>
[Scene Transition: Back to the Coffin-Pushing Scene]
This question, too, never leaves your lips. Something tears you away. A violent force rips you from that body, hurling you back through the cold Void, back before the black coffin.
Your hands press against the lid, legs braced. Every muscle in your small body is fully committed to prying it open.

Your body does not listen. It moves anyway. When you heave with everything you have, fire streaks across your arms, and your little hands shove aside a coffin lid many times your own weight. It slides off completely, crashing to the ground.
THUD!
<color=#dg1f1f>...You did it. Well done.</color>

You have no voice, and no one answers. The fire burns on. Your vision warps; crimson patterns trace themselves across your skin like a silent, spreading stain. You grip the coffin and pull yourself in—
And you finally see her. A familiar face, peaceful beneath that mask. She slumbers as all the death-destined do: undisturbed, eternal, serene.
But the moment your eyes trace her features, the world lurches violently. A deafening cascade of fragmented whispers claw their way into your mind.
[White Flash]

speaker: Fanatic Voice
content: Master Lichen! I had the dream! I finally had the dream! A little immortal child came to me and said my mom's at peace in the world below, and we'll see each other again soon!

speaker: Fanatic Voice
content: You were right. Heaven doesn't want offerings, just faith! I came here day and night, burned 888 sticks of incense. I was always so scared my mom was being bullied down there, too scared to even eat. Now... now I can finally rest easy!

speaker: Fanatic Voice
content: Another one... Another one gets a vision in their dream. So there really are gods watching over us? Then why not me? Why won't she visit me? Or just... just let me go be with her!

speaker: Fanatic Voice
content: Hey, easy there, lad. Half the people here are in a worse spot than you. Knock over that incense, and you're not just dealing with me. You're dealing with everyone. And their fists.

speaker: Fanatic Voice
content: Look on the bright side, though! You came around, didn't you? You do it right, stay faithful, and getting a dream's just a matter of time!

speaker: Fanatic Voice
content: Me? I've never actually met her. But everyone who's gotten a reading from her swears she's the real deal. I know someone who lost everything—family, home, the whole lot. Then they had a dream. Gave 'em the will to go on. They've put their life back together. They're here every day now. I just tagged along one day and stayed.

speaker: Fanatic Voice
content: It's not like it costs you an arm and a leg, right? So why not try? These days, who doesn't have someone they're desperate to see again? And if it works? Jackpot.

Adrift in this boundless sea of fervent praise, a swirling white light coalesces before your eyes. It fills your vision, drowning out the world. You cradle your aching head, blinking again and again, desperately trying to make out something—

speaker: Fanatic Voice
content: Faith... brings answers... I'm faithful... I have to be faithful...

speaker: Fanatic Voice
content: Master, guide me... Please... Master, guide me...

Joy, longing, excitement—all the bright, hopeful things gather in these murmurs. They swell and intertwine, an emotional tide so potent it threatens to overflow, to crystallize into obsessive fanaticism. Then, you remember her words:

speaker: Lichen
content: I believe the Daoist arts make no distinction between righteous and wicked, good and evil. The Dao of Heaven is chaos; we'll never be able to fully grasp it. Arts that fulfill the wishes of the believers... those are good arts.

speaker: Lichen
content: ...And what <color=#fb9259>people believe in</color> will have power.
A sudden surge of fear jolts you half-awake.

speaker: %u
content: You've been manipulating them... Cultivating their faith. You want to...

But there's no time to worry about others now. Crimson flames crawl up your limbs, binding you, commanding you. The fire's source burns deep in your chest, where her fingertips once pressed. The <color=#fb9259>protection talisman</color> is blazing.

speaker: %u
content: This... is no protection talisman...
Shared senses. Memory resonance. Guiding a child's body to defeat the coffin ghost... All of it is her Daoist arts, still working through you.

speaker: %u
content: You've been controlling me... Using me like a puppet, just like one of those phantoms...

speaker: Lichen
content: Go now, young friend. I will be waiting for your answer.

speaker: %u
content: You letting me come down here... It was your plan all along.
[Clatter]
The terminal slips from your grasp. It hits the ground, and in that instant, its white screen flickers. Against all odds, against all reason, it powers on.
[White Flash]

content: [White Flash + Return to the Inner World]
She knows. She has sensed what you hide, what you intend. Is that why she no longer holds back?
Your body betrays you. It bends forward, stiff and unwilling, moving toward the figure in the coffin. Against your will, your hands slide beneath her shoulder blades and waist, lifting her body up.

You know where "you" are taking her. You know, and the knowledge is a scream trapped in your throat. Resisting is like trying to hold back the tide; all you can force through clenched teeth is a handful of broken words.

speaker: Chief
content: ...You can hear me, can't you, Lichen?

speaker: Chief
content: Stop. Please... stop. That's not your shifu. Bringing her out serves you nothing.

speaker: Chief
content: No matter how you made your followers believe in <color=#fb9259>resurrection</color>... those who have crossed into the Void of Yin follow a different <color=#fb9259>Dao</color>. What you seek... you cannot have...

<color=#dg1f1f><size=60>Offer no glance to the departed.
Lend no ear to the abyss.
Speak no question to the spirits.</color></size>

speaker: Chief
content: What you want is beyond your reach... Don't force this...

Your pleas fall empty into the coffin's depths. The rune burns against your chest as you continue cradling "Lichen's" body, inching it outward, millimeter by agonizing millimeter. As the figure in your arms emerges, the frozen air itself begins to stir.

A chill wind rises, drawing spectral flames toward the black coffin. The thick lid groans, cracks spider-webbing across its surface. An invisible seal is weakening, fast. Through your daze, you glimpse ruins on the other side.
The sealed rift has reappeared. And there, on the other side, stands Lichen, calm and still. A talisman pinched between her fingers.

speaker: %u
content: ...Stop, Lichen. Stop.

Your body fights—every fiber screaming resistance—but all it can manage is a tremor. You watch, helpless, as Lichen on the other side draws another paper talisman to ignite it. Instantly, your body goes weightless, as if about to lift off, to slip from this space entirely.
Is this sorcery to pull you back? Or does she intend to use you—to drag "Lichen" with you to Maria City? If they actually meet, if they come face to face, they'll—
[Flashback: Corpse Hair-Brushing CG]

speaker: %u
content: ...No. I can't let them meet.
There must be something beyond her control. Think.
There's still time. You have to stop this!
[Release the shackles]
Crimson light bursts. Shackles erupt from your body, piercing through you and "Lichen" at once. The illusions scatter, and with it, the world falls still.
Your feet hit the ground—heavy, real. Slowly, you reclaim your breath. Then your body heat. Then your sense of smell. The fire talisman on your chest has died; whatever held you has finally let go.
You loosen your arms from around "Lichen." The shackles settle. The light piercing her body softens, gentling until it matches the peaceful expression on her sleeping face.
Calm, serene, and yet... stubbornly unrepentant. You don't know what to feel.
The crimson glow of the shackles around your waists fades. Now you can see her clearly. Unlike the Lichen on the other side, this one bears far fewer scars.
You let out a sigh.
I understand what you wanted.
As for me... I'll explain everything when I return.
For now... let me say goodbye.

Perhaps you should reach out. Perhaps, one last time, you should touch her face. Perhaps, deep down, you secretly hope—the way the living always hope—that the dead could awaken and find some happy ending.
You never believed in resurrection. But how easily can anyone suppress that deeply human longing? That stubborn, foolish wish of the heart?
Then, you step back. Slowly.
<color=#dg1f1f>Your wish has been fulfilled.</color>
The Yin-Yang fish mask has opened. At some point, you don't know when. And "Lichen" opens her eyes.
They are wide, unblinking. They scan the sky of the Void, slow and deliberate. A smile forms at the corners of her lips. In that instant, fear seizes your heart.
—Those are not Lichen's eyes. Not the eyes of the dead. This person... she does not belong to this world.
Blue and crimson intertwine in her gaze. Divine and demonic. Yin and Yang. All separated by a single thought.

speaker: Lichen
content: I see... So this is the truth you witnessed in the Void of Yin...

speaker: Lichen
content: My "shifu" was merely a phantom of my own longing. In both the Realm of Yang and the Void of Yin, all things are illusions born of the heart... Even I could not escape this.
She sits up, slowly turning her neck. Crack. Crack. Crack. Each one a distinct sound in the silence. Only then does she glance down at the shackles still faintly encircling her body.
Comprehension hits you instantly.
She used the very bond that held you together as her road here. It was, and always had been, her goal.

speaker: Chief
content: This is no place for you. Go back, please, while you still can...

speaker: %u
content: Any later... and you really won't have the chance...
She turns to face you, her gaze holding yours for a long, breathless moment. Finally, a smile crosses her lips, familiar yet horribly stiff.

speaker: Lichen
content: It is alright. Thank you for guiding me here, young friend... The divination was not wrong. You truly are my auspicious star.

speaker: Lichen
content: Now then... will you enlighten me once more?
She draws closer, that faint smile still in place.
You have nowhere left to retreat.
Her fingers, cold as stone, press gently against the side of your neck. The touch is almost tender until it isn't. They tighten, grip firm, and begin to pull you toward her.

speaker: Lichen
content: You, who wear that child's skin, standing before me yet not truly here... Who are you?
[Fade to Black]

speaker: Shin?

speaker: Shin?
content: You have but to do as she did... and chant its name...

In the Void of Yin, blue-black mist coils around you as loose stones slip silently into the abyss below. The woman's fingertips brush your skin. You lock eyes with her, and find her pale cyan irises holding a deep, flickering crimson light.
In the next heartbeat, chaos floods your mind, a deafening roar of voices. Your body, no longer your own, is dragged inch by relentless inch toward the void.

speaker: Pleading Voices
content: Can you hear us...? You can hear us. I know you can...

speaker: Pleading Voices
content: If our sins are forgiven, will we finally be free?

speaker: Pleading Voices
content: Our families... our home... please, show us the way...

speaker: Pleading Voices
content: You can grant our prayers... we know you can...

speaker: Pleading Voices
content: Please, Master... Please, gods, watch over us... Please, we beg you...!
Within the churning currents, a more substantial figure materializes.

The figure turns to face you, features blurred and voice strange.

speaker: Woman's Voice
content: But do not lose your way... Come. Come to Maria City. Here, you shall find the path to <color=#fb9259>vanquishing evil</color>...

speaker: Woman's Voice

[Chengxiao's while silhouette]

A cold touch yanks you sharply back to the present. Lichen's fingertips are slowly tracing the shell of your ear. A burning ache prickles across every place her fingers graze.

Your thoughts spiral deeper into chaos as an invisible grip tightens around your throat, choking away every last whisper of sound.

speaker: Lichen
content: What is the matter? Did you really knock your head hard enough to forget what just happened? Do you not even recognize me?
Can you no longer recognize her? Is the one in front of you even the same person you know?
[Quick cut to memory filter + surface world background + Lichen squinting smile portrait + two silhouettes on the side (the devotee portrait from the end of the previous chapter)]
She schemed through every step of the journey, twisting people's deepest desires to her advantage.
[Quick cut to memory filter + corpse hair-brushing CG]
She made you think the expedition had corrupted her, only to exploit you.
[Quick cut back to present, show Lichen corrupted no-mask portrait]
Now that she has finally reached the <color=#fb9259>Void of Yin</color>, what more does she want from you?
The corner of Lichen's mouth tugs upward. Is that meant to be a smile? Yet that face, no matter how you study it, bears no resemblance to anything still alive.
You wrench your arm upward, twisting free of her wrist. Your heel digs deep into the mud as you kick yourself backward.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You went through all this trouble to lure me down here, just to enter the Void of Yin...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But I have no power, and I'm definitely not your "auspicious star." There is nothing I can do for you.
Behind her, specks of pale blue luminescence surface from the darkness, bobbing and sinking like fish swimming through unseen depths.
[Flashback to soul-guiding CG]
It is them. These are the very fish that once guided you safely out of the Void of Yin.
Could you rely on them to escape again? Though you have no idea how to communicate with them...

speaker: Fish
content: <i><color=#7683a2>...Please...</color><i>

speaker: Fish
content: <i><color=#7683a2>...our... wish...</color><i>
<color=#fb9259>And yet, every word they speak rings clear in your mind.</color>

speaker: Fish
content: <i><color=#7683a2>...Please, gods...</color><i>

speaker: Fish
content: <i><color=#7683a2>...grant... our wishes...</color><i>
As each word sharpens into clarity, the flecks of light begin to shift, slowly drawing out human silhouettes. They flicker and sway, indistinct as reflections upon a river's surface.
In the next breath, the phantoms rush toward you.
The hazy figures shudder violently and then scatter back into luminous specks. But they do not leave. Instead, they gather again in the air, weaving into a ribbon of light that glides toward Lichen.

speaker: Lichen
content: By decree of Shangqing...
The incantation has scarcely left her lips halfway when the ribbon of light winds itself around her arm. It constricts, then slips beneath her sleeve.
She freezes in place, lowering her head as if listening intently.
You take the opening to brace your hands against the slimy, softened earth and force yourself to your feet. Something hard grazes your fingertips.
A <color=#fb9259>copper coin</color>!
Lichen raises her eyes and lets her gaze trail across the glowing ribbon wound obediently around her arm, then smiles.

speaker: Lichen
content: Why run? These things answer to me now.
In a flash, the copper coin sears with heat, nearly hot enough to melt through your skin. Just like before, a dire warning.
As you suspected, even these drifting fish are on her side. Who is left for you to rely on?!
Gritting your teeth against the pain, you grip the copper coin hard, spin around, and sprint into the darkness at full speed.
Behind you, she turns and walks after you, bells at her waist swaying gently, ringing step by step.
Run. That's all you can do now. Keep running.
[Inner World - Aberration 2]

At last, the familiar stone stele comes into view. Yet your eyes find more than just the path out of this nightmare. Stretching between you and the distant exit lies a sprawling field of ashen gravestones, jutting from the earth at crooked angles.
Before each one, small clusters of shadowy figures stand in silence. Your fingers tighten unconsciously. They share the same hue as the ribbon of light those drifting fish became.
Their heads hang low, hands clasped before their chests, bodies tilting forward ever so slightly as faint murmurs slip from their lips.
It looks almost like an act of worship.
The copper coin sears without warning. You fail to hold back a muffled groan.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Mmph...!
In near-perfect unison, the shadowy figures all turn to face you.
You hold your breath and clench the copper coin tight. Even as your palm sizzles from the heat, you dare not loosen your grip.
(Transition 2s)
One by one, the shadowy figures at last turn back. The whispered murmur rises once more.
You release a slow, careful breath. The copper coin in your hand gradually cools.
It seems you must not draw their attention... That leaves only one path forward: to search for the true exit without disturbing their vigil.

options: Hold your breath and proceed carefully

content: You are closing in on the way out.
Then you hear it again.
[Empty scene + bell sound effect]

speaker: Lichen
content: Following the <color=#fb9259>copper coin</color> will get you nowhere.
[Empty scene 1s + footsteps & bell]

speaker: Lichen
content: And where exactly do you think you'll run to? It's no different from doing nothing and waiting to die.
The chime draws nearer. She will find you soon; it is only a matter of time.
<i>The copper coin... She seems fixated on it. Perhaps you could use it to lure her attention elsewhere.
You grip the coin in your palm, your thumb tracing its charred, blackened face.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm sorry...
The coin flies from your palm, arcing through the air past the tombstone you crouch behind. It disappears into the haze beyond and strikes the ground with a faint, ringing chime.

speaker: Distant Specters
content: <i><color=#7683a2>Aaarrghh!</color><i>
You yank your body back and shrink entirely into the darkness pooling behind a gravestone.

speaker: Lichen
content: Heh...
The footsteps falter for a moment, then move off into the haze. The rustle of cloth reaches your ears, then a quiet laugh somewhere far off. And finally, all falls still.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Phew.
You slowly peek out and gauge the distance to the stone stele far away. Now is your moment. She has moved away. Find the real exit while you can.
[Screen flash + vibration + sound of stone shattering]

All around you, tombstones explode without warning. Debris flies past, sharp shards slicing across your cheek. The ghostly green silhouettes shatter into points of light before they can even utter a sound, dissolving into the air.
[Heavy vibration + dust and smoke effect]
You land flat on your back amidst the shattered stones, a jagged point piercing your shoulder. Warm, thick blood glues your clothes to your skin.
And there, through the swirling dust that has yet to settle, Lichen's silhouette grows steadily clearer.

speaker: Lichen
content: That boy always loved it when we played this game.
female_content: That girl always loved it when we played this game.

speaker: Lichen
content: I'd always pretend I couldn't find him, just to make him happy.
female_content: I'd always pretend I couldn't find her, just to make her happy.

content: She sinks into a crouch before you, head tilting, a smile playing at her lips. It is almost the same look she wore the very first time you met.

speaker: Lichen
content: But playtime is over. No more hide-and-seek.

Her hand reaches toward you, pausing in the air just before your face, then drifts down to your collar. Through the fabric, her cool fingertips press hard against your collarbone and suddenly grip with terrible force.
[Single vibration + character portrait zooms in]
She lifts you as though you weigh nothing. Your legs kick at empty air while your hands grasp desperately at her wrist.
There, just behind you, the last stone stele marking the exit stands in silence.
There is nowhere left to run.
Sweat drips from the hair matted to your brow, seeping into your eyes. The sting threatens to blind you, yet you force yourself to hold her gaze.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You already used me to get in here. You got what you wanted.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I told you, I'm done with you. And I meant it.

speaker: Lichen
content: Yes. I've tasted the power of that <color=#fb9259>thing</color>. It's extraordinary, truly... The way it can draw the mind and spirit... That is exactly what I need.

speaker: Lichen
content: So why not lend that power to me once more?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: "Lend"? Is that what you call it? The way you command those ghosts, the way you just controlled my body?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And what would you do with it? Drag your shifu back from the dead?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: There's no way you can bring the dead back. What you've been looking for doesn't even exist. Just look around. There's nothing but monsters in the Void of Yin! Your shifu is dead! She died a long time ago!
A smile tugs at the edges of her mouth. She pulls your hands closer against herself. The two of you are nearly touching now, but her body offers no heat, only an unsettling cold.

speaker: Lichen
content: Of course I know she has long since passed. What I saw was nothing more than a phantom, shaped by my own obsession.

speaker: Lichen
content: Looking at it another way, that's a puzzle solved for me.

options: If you knew it was just your obsession...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Your shifu's death... is that all it ever was to you? Just some puzzle to solve...? I thought...
Your voice dwindles to a whisper, and yet the smile on her face only grows deeper.

speaker: Lichen
content: Shifu drove herself to madness and death trying to prove there is a way to cross the boundary between life and death, to stand against the calamity. And she never once regretted it.

speaker: Lichen
content: So if someone can finally find an answer, I think that would give her peace.

speaker: Lichen
content: And such a way... it may not be out of reach after all.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If you already knew what you saw was just born out of your delusion, then stop. Let it go.
Your voice swells with rage, but the smile on her face only deepens in return.

speaker: Lichen
content: "Delusion"... Heh. Yes, you're right. To be honest, after all these years, I can barely remember her face anymore.

speaker: Lichen
content: But one thing I do remember. Even as she lost her mind, even at the end, she never stopped searching for a way to transcend life and death, to stand against the calamity.

speaker: Lichen
content: And that way... it may be more than just my delusion after all.

speaker: Lichen
content: <color=#fb9259>"Believe, and it shall be."</color>

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Believe, and it shall be... Those specters that blocked our path, they showed up because you led people to "believe," didn't they?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But whatever they are now, you can't exactly call them alive. This whole transcendence of life and death is just nonsense.

speaker: Lichen
content: If they can be put to use, does it really matter whether they're truly "alive" or not?

speaker: Lichen
content: Speaking of which, what does that make you, I wonder? Hiding inside a child's body the way you are?
You press your mouth into a hard line, giving no reply. The grip at your collar seems to cinch ever tighter.

speaker: Lichen
content: It's alright. Whatever you are, I don't mind. As long as you're willing to help.

speaker: Lichen
content: After everything we've been through together, do you still not trust me?
You meet her gaze at last, and it dawns on you. You recognize that look in those eyes. You saw it long ago, before you ever entered the Void of Yin.

speaker: Lichen
content: <i><color=#7683a2>If I learn the truth at dawn, I can die content by dusk.</color><i>
Her grey, bloodless lips stir again.

speaker: Lichen
content:
Fear not.
<i><color=#7683a2>Fear not.</color><i>

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I... don't trust you...!
Not a single mark appears where your shackles should have bitten. Instead, a deeper, more terrible power pours back into you through them, grinding your insides and splitting you apart from within.
You try to lock your eyes on Lichen's face, yet her features are melting, sliding down in sluggish rivulets.
Your tongue swells, filling your mouth. Broken words scrape past it and fall from your lips. Even you cannot make sense of what you are saying.
Your limbs turn soft and useless. Your arms fall to your sides, swing once, then hang motionless.
[Empty scene 1s + switch special effects]

Your awareness is torn free from your body. Drifting in a daze, you rise and gaze down upon the entire space. Only now do you truly see: the ground beneath your feet was never ground at all. Beneath the scattered slabs of grey stone lie heaps of twisted, blackened limbs, piled layer upon layer.

Bare arms, thighs, slick and shapeless half-torsos... They all extend from the same darkness, crawling in different directions, clutching at anything within reach. It is as though the unspoken words of the dead still animate their flesh and bone, driving them endlessly onward.
And at the center of this vision, a child, utterly pale, is gripped by the collar by a woman whose face is just as grey and cold.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Li... chen...
Those ashen, fractured lips of the child do not stir. Words are no longer within his reach. Only this faint whisper echoes gently in the deepest part of your joined awareness.
female_content: Those ashen, fractured lips of the child do not stir. Words are no longer within her reach. Only this faint whisper echoes gently in the deepest part of your joined awareness.

content: The grip across your chest slackens. The child drops from her hand.
[Vibration + special effects / character art disappears]
Your back sinks into the cold, clinging softness of flesh. Slick limbs swarm toward you all at once, stroking your arms and legs, weaving through your hair. Their touch is ravenous yet eerily tender.

Your vision sharpens at last: Lichen stands above you, gazing down, and takes another step closer. You drag your body backward once more, desperate to escape her and the torrent of twisted, overwhelming Mania force surging from her.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Back off!
After that furious shout, all strength drains from your limbs. It feels as if your bones have been pulled clean out, and you fall limply onto your back.
She pauses and studies you closely, her fist tightening in silence. The power slowly recedes but remains coiled around her form, its taint still gnawing at your senses.
She seems to waver for a moment, then tries to edge another step closer.
<b>Why did you stop?
<i>A ghost? The Illusory Moon? Or something else entirely?!
Your breath catches in your throat again. You stare hard into Lichen's eyes. The voice is clearly pushing her forward, coaxing her nearer. If she obeys...
But you are completely drained.
Lichen only offers a small smile and shakes the copper coin free from her sleeve, the one she had been hiding all along.

speaker: Lichen
content: Oh? Finally decided to speak up? Did you just now figure out this burning little coin is completely useless against me?

speaker: Lichen
content: Looks like your definition of playing by the rules is quite flexible.

speaker: Copper Coin
content: We made a promise to find the answers together. You're on the verge of succeeding. Of course I intend to see this through.

speaker: Copper Coin
content: Though... a phrase comes to mind. "To fall short at the final step."

speaker: Lichen
content: Enough with the riddles. What are you trying to say?

speaker: Copper Coin
content: This child doesn't have much time left, judging by the looks of him...
female_content: This child doesn't have much time left, judging by the looks of her...

content: Lichen offers no reply, her eyes appraising you in silence. The ghostly green ribbon of light wrapped around her arms begins to churn.

speaker: Copper Coin
content: Or are you planning to simply kill him? What you're after is inside his body, after all.
female_content: Or are you planning to simply kill her? What you're after is inside her body, after all.

content: Lichen's grip tightens around the coin, thumb digging into its edge.

speaker: Lichen
content: And who said I would stoop so low?

speaker: Copper Coin
content: "So low"? You've come this far. You've done what needed doing and plenty that didn't. So who exactly are you putting on this virtuous act for?

speaker: Copper Coin
content: What, now of all times you want to earn some good karma? Pray to the heavens—
The copper coin is crushed in two. Fragments of rust sift through her fingers like dust, too pitiful to make the slightest sound.
A faint wisp of smoke rises from her palm, winding briefly between her fingers before drifting away.

speaker: Lichen
content: ...Huh?
While her eyes remain on that curling wisp of dark smoke, you seize the moment and drag yourself toward the stone stele.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Get me... out of here...
In a flash, thick black fog surges upward from behind the stone stele. A chorus of countless voices erupts within the mist, rushing toward you and hurling you back against the cold stone.

speaker: Departed Souls
content: <i><color=#7683a2>To leave... you have to leave something behind...</color><i>

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Fine, whatever you want... just get me out!

speaker: Departed Souls
content: <i><color=#7683a2>Yes... yes...!</color><i>

speaker: Departed Souls
content: Then give it to us...!
The dark fog twists in an instant, thickening into a slick, pitch-black mass that lunges straight at you.
<i><color=#7683a2>By the stars I walk; ghosts wail, gods tremble! All foul spirits, seized and delivered to justice!</color><i>
A blade slices through the creature, scattering it into countless flailing limbs. White radiance spills through the widening crack, growing more brilliant with each breath.
Your fingers stretch toward it, nearly brushing its glow, when something seizes your ankle and wrenches you back.

speaker: Departed Souls
content: Pay us... pay the price... give it to us!
The grip on your ankle loosens, just barely. Before you can even think to pull away, sharp nails extend from its fingers and slash down toward you.
[Red screen flash + severed limb & blood splatter sound effects]
Lichen stands behind you, her left hand trembling uncontrollably, dripping blood from the blow she took in your stead.

The blackened, rotting limbs latch onto the fresh wound with something close to rapture, burrowing deeper, merging with her flesh. From that unholy union, new skin and sinew, slick and crimson, finally begin to sprout.
She looks at you one last time, her eyes lingering, then turns to confront the creatures. Her hand tightens into a fist as she wrestles with the part of herself she no longer recognizes.

speaker: Lichen
content: You want a price?

speaker: Lichen
content: Fine. Come and take it!
The limbs come flooding toward her all at once.
You don't look back. Finally, you cross through the white light and return to the other world.
[CG] Eyes open
The fog in front of you suddenly dissipates. Only then do you catch the gleam of a sword cutting through. As though the fog had been lingering only to be banished by it.
Little guide... Little guide?
I think he's back. Xiansheng, come take a look?
female_content: I think she's back. Xiansheng, come take a look?

content: Worry not. It's going to be fine.

The figure before you sports a mess of curly hair and leans in uncomfortably close. A few paces away stands a long-haired man, his sword already returned to its sheath. He glances sideways at you, his gaze pausing on your face for a beat, then looks away.
All that reaches you is a low, quiet laugh.
[Realm Stele]
The woman turns the broken half of a copper coin idly between her fingers. Its sharp edge scrapes across her skin with each pass, but draws no blood at all.
That blood-red hand has lost all semblance of humanity. It gleams as if forged with golden veins that trace every place the creatures fed.
She flips the half-coin over and holds it up, broken edge raised, toward a shadow standing before her.

speaker: Lichen
content: So, this is how you've been showing up in the Void of Yin. <color=#fb9259>Anchoring the soul to an object.</color>

speaker: Lichen
content: Lyu Buzhou. All those myths and legends I gathered across the land, I shared every last one with you. I assisted your research. I helped you build that Ziwei software. And you? You kept the most crucial discovery to yourself.

speaker: Lichen
content: Never trusted me, did you? You always think so highly of yourself.
The shadow before her wavers but offers no words.
Her hand drops to her side, and with a careless flick of her fingers, she sends the coin spinning into the mud. It sinks slowly, swallowed without resistance.

speaker: Lichen
content: No matter. Person or object, it makes no difference now. Here we all are, in the Void of Yin.

speaker: Lichen
content: And even without that person, I've already found <color=#fb9259>another path</color>.

speaker: Long-haired Man
content: I'll deal with these creatures. Check on him first.
female_content: I'll deal with these creatures. Check on her first.

content: A paper talisman shoots past the long-haired man's shoulder, catching the creature mid-leap and nailing it to the ruined wall beyond.
Someone tugs your clothes from behind. You react before thinking and yank away.

speaker: Curly-haired Young Man
content: Ah!
His right hand loses its hold, but as you scramble to your feet, his left finds your free hand without missing a beat. He pulls, and you land squarely back on the makeshift cushion of his coat.

speaker: Curly-haired Young Man
content: ...Sorry. I've got two hands, you know.
Messy hair hides half of his face, leaving his expression a mystery. Apology or sarcasm, you honestly can't tell. In your confusion, your hands move on their own and take the water bottle from him.

speaker: Curly-haired Young Man
content: You're in rough shape. Take a breath. Can you still speak?
Pain throbs dully under your ribs, turning even the simplest breath into torment. Still, questions press against your tongue, demanding to be asked.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Who... who are you people...

speaker: Curly-haired Young Man
content: Xiansheng, he doesn't remember us. His cognition may be affected.
female_content: Xiansheng, she doesn't remember us. Her cognition may be affected.

speaker: Curly-haired Young Man
content: Maybe you should take over. I think I'm just making him mad.
female_content: Maybe you should take over. I think I'm just making her mad.

content: Before you can blink, Chengxiao dusts the talisman residue from his fingers with a casual shake and exhales something between a snort and a laugh.

speaker: Long-haired Man
content: He'll be fine.
female_content: She'll be fine.

content: Silence settles over everything. Only the ash of spent paper talismans drifts down like snow. The long-haired man approaches from a distance, his steps nearly soundless.

He stops before you, catches your gaze, and offers a gentle smile. Then he gestures toward your arm. You follow his eyes and notice, for the first time, the shallow red scratches running along your left forearm.

speaker: Long-haired Man
content: Let me patch you up first.
The curly-haired man rises without a word, giving up his spot across from you. He walks over and settles beside Lichen, who lies motionless nearby.

The long-haired man lowers himself before you. His hand lifts your injured arm with care as he pulls a cotton swab from the kit on the ground. He dips it in iodine and touches it gently near the wound, letting you feel the coolness before he begins.

speaker: Long-haired Man
content: My name is Lyu Buzhou. I'm a scholar on the expedition team specializing in Eastern Continent mysticism. I used to teach at the Spectral Phenomena Institute at Eastern Continent University. Though everyone here calls me Chengxiao. It's my Daoist name, and rather easier on the ears.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Daoist name... so you're a Daoist too? Then you and Lichen...

You study his clothing more carefully this time. He is Eastian, unmistakably. Yet it's his voice that snags at you, each word sounding more familiar than the last. A name almost leaps from your lips, but Chengxiao nods before you can speak it.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: That's right. That <color=#fb9259>copper coin</color> was me.

speaker: Copper Coin
content: Why did you stop?
Those words surface in your mind again, their intent still unclear, and reflexively you try to yank your hand away.
But he saw it coming. His hold on your wrist is calibrated perfectly: just enough to keep you there, never enough to hurt.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: I scared you back there, didn't I? Forgive me. I had to say what I said to buy enough time to get you out. Had you remained in contact with her any longer, I doubt you would have lasted much past that.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Worry not. I'm nothing like that one over there, who willingly shed her flesh to go drifting about as a ghost. I'm here to bring you back.

He finishes his sentence, and only then does he slowly ease his grip, as though giving you every chance to bolt. You watch him, wary. If you had to name his expression, you'd call it earnest. That only makes it more confusing.

Still, that small flash of tension aside, he has been helping you every step of the way. You waver, then let the tension drain from your arm. A faint smile crosses his face as he returns to tending the wound.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: ...Just some superficial cuts. Likely from the gravel on the ground. They should heal in a day or two.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Your pallor, on the other hand, gives me far more cause for concern. Have you forgotten everything that happened before you came here?

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Do you remember how you arrived in Maria City at all?
There's no honest answer you can offer, so you let him keep his assumption. Feigning memory loss seems useful. It might loosen his tongue enough to give you the answers you're after.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It's... a little fuzzy...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Then... how did you two end up here?
Chengxiao glances at you and smiles briefly. Your avoidance seems to roll right off him. He bows his head and goes back to the wound, explaining as he cleans.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: We had arranged for you to lead the first survey of Maria City three days ago. But you disappeared without warning just before departure, and the plan has been suspended ever since.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Leaving camp without authorization is strictly forbidden, to say nothing of entering Maria City alone. The consequences would be severe. All of this was covered in the very first safety briefing.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: You're still a child, little guide, so one could at least say you don't know any better. But a certain someone, having lived for decades, has always been far too bold for her own good. Briefings skipped, yet not a single prohibited thing left undone.
Chengxiao changes tack, his voice now lilting and theatrical, cryptic yet casual. He's clearly mimicking the way someone else speaks.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: "I'll go look for our little guide first. And while I'm at it, I can have a look around. Two birds, one stone, wouldn't you say?" Those were someone's exact words.
You raise an eyebrow and glance up. His face is deadpan, completely unreadable. Joke or not, he's giving you nothing.

speaker: Curly-haired Young Man
content: Professor...

speaker: Chengxiao
content: She even made you cry just a few days before departure, too. What sort of grown adult fakes their own death to tease a little kid? And so convincingly, not a single tell. No sense of where to draw the line with these things.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: The moment I suggested you might have been frightened enough to run off into Maria City, suddenly she's full of enthusiasm, going on about how she's your "big Daoist sister." So I said—

speaker: Curly-haired Young Man
content: Professor, your sound waves are interfering with my readings. Can the niece stories wait? Or you could walk ten meters to the left. There's a tree over there you can tell all of this to.

The Eastian man finally falls silent. You glance back and find the curly-haired young man hovering just behind you, sweeping a small, strangely shaped device around the back of your skull. It emits a rapid string of beeps.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: How's the situation?

speaker: Curly-haired Young Man
content: Hmm... the readings have barely stabilized, but they're not holding steady. I suspect it's caused by consciousness dissociation between the <color=#fb9259>Material Plane</color> and the <color=#fb9259>Reflection Plane</color>...

speaker: Chengxiao
content: The names Li Xianling told you would be the Realm of Yang and the Void of Yin, I imagine.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: The academic community has yet to settle on unified terminology. Only we in the Eastern Continent use those names. The Realm of Yang is simply the reality we inhabit. The Void of Yin, by contrast, is more like a separate mental plane built from human memories and obsessions.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Time and space flow erratically within the Void of Yin, and no reliable means of entry has been discovered as of yet. But Maria City appears to have been actively pulling anyone who enters it into the Void of Yin.

options: And what do you mean by "consciousness dissociation"?

speaker: Chengxiao
content: The Void of Yin and the Realm of Yang can influence one another. The deeper people's obsessions run in the Realm of Yang, the stronger the shadows grow in the Void of Yin, which in turn eats away at the mind. The reverse holds true as well. Once the corruption runs deep enough, the boundary between consciousness and body can no longer hold.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Which is precisely why I have always reminded you: <color=#fb9259>Offer no glance to the departed. Lend no ear to the abyss. Speak no question to the spirits</color>.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: In more scientific terms, the psychological hazards posed by the Void of Yin include, but are not limited to: mental disorientation, memory loss, and sensory disorder.

speaker: Curly-haired Young Man
content: ...Obsessive behavior.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: ...And obsessive behavior.
Chengxiao hesitates briefly, then murmurs his agreement in a low voice. He looks ready to steer the conversation elsewhere, but you cut in before he can begin.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Obsessive behavior... So from the moment Lichen entered this city, she was already slowly turning into what she is now? Dead set on entering the Void of Yin no matter the cost...

speaker: Chengxiao
content: And now she has remained there. In a sense, she has become something that defies definition, something that has crossed beyond the boundary of life and death.

He tilts his head back and gazes at the sky. It's riddled with jagged fissures of pale green light, some wide, some thin as thread. Peering through them, you catch hazy snatches of the world within: the Void of Yin, still visible through the wounds.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: To upset the balance between two realms entirely on one's own. Well done, Li Xianling.
His eyes drop to your bandaged forearm. He gives your wrist a gentle flex, checking it over, then smooths your sleeve back into place over the wound.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: There. Do be careful on the way back, and mind you don't knock it against anything.
[Vibration Sound Effect]
The terminal Lichen left behind flickers to life, its screen glowing as a familiar symbol surfaces.
Chengxiao straightens up and scoops it from the ground in one easy motion, his fingers already moving across the display.

speaker: Ziwei App
content: Authorization confirmed. Switching to manual override. Retrieving backend data.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: ...As I thought. More and more people across the Eastern Continent are reporting strange dreams.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That thing... I wouldn't trust it too much.
An eyebrow arches on his face. He doesn't seem pleased with what you just said.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: This is a scientifically developed application built on aggregated data. It has undergone extensive safety testing.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: It is meant to provide sound guidance, steering users toward safe and controlled behavior, while intercepting any dangerous actions on their part and alerting the central database so a human operator can take over.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Yeah, but just now Lichen asked it whatever she wanted and it answered, no questions asked. Forbidden arts and all.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You think objects can get messed with by this city too? Same way people do?
Chengxiao drags his thumb along the rim of the screen, feeling it out. Then his mouth tightens, he locks the device with a tap, and meets your gaze with a smile.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: I think I'll leave those questions for the expedition's scientists to puzzle over.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: For now, the priority is getting you out of here alive.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: There is much I'd like to ask you, once we're back.
You purse your lips and look away, sneaking a sidelong look at his face. He belongs to the same Daoist sect as Lichen... What is he trying to find out?
Not getting an answer from you, Chengxiao smiles and rises.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: No matter. We'll have enough time later.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: The researchers back at the camp have pinpointed the nearest safe zone based on the signal. Head there and rendezvous with them. I'll handle things here.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: ...Including the one on the ground.
While speaking, he casts a sidelong look toward Lichen's prone form.
The curly-haired man is already packed and waiting, hands resting on his bag strap, quiet at your side.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Am I going with you?
He gives a nod. Only then does it strike you: through all of this, you've never thought to ask his name.

speaker: Curly-haired Young Man
content: Name's Keylan. Assistant. Here to help.

speaker: Keylan
content: Don't worry if it doesn't ring a bell. It's a big team. Just remember the important people.
...<color=#fb9259>Keylan</color>?

[Quick flashback: an empty black-and-white piano room and one with a white figure playing, rapid color flashes with layered sound effects] [Finally settles on descriptions of him from the expedition members in the Nightmare]
A dull ache spreads through your skull. Your thoughts turn sluggish, and strange images flicker past your eyes. You desperately hold onto them before they slip away.

speaker: Mantis
content: ...my name isn't Mantis; I study Mantises... it's those dark flying creatures over there. That idiot <color=#fb9259>Keylan</color> calls them DisSea cockroaches...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Ah, you're that guy—
The curly-haired young man flinches like he's been shocked. A painful pause stretches out before he twists toward you, lips twitching into a strained excuse for a smile, and mutters under his breath.

speaker: Keylan
content: Sorry. Didn't mean to drag you down to my level.

speaker: Keylan
content: They're Mantises... We have to remember.
The smile he wears is barely holding, but the feeling behind it reaches you before you can guard against it. Your own lips curve upward in response, even as a weight sinks slowly through your chest.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...You're right. I'll remember.
You take the hand he extends and move naturally into place beside him.
