...Yes, that's right. How could you ever forget someone who's walked this road with you?
You trail after Keylan, your thoughts still clouded and your steps unsteady.

You blink hard and glance down. Beneath your feet, the asphalt with its faded crosswalk lines is cracking open, pried apart by stone slabs. Thick, dark fluid oozes through the gaps and seeps around the edges of your shoes.

speaker: Keylan
content: Maria City's assimilation rate with the Reflection Plane... fifty-four percent...

speaker: Keylan
content: Ah!
[24 Quick Cut to the Surface World - Distortion + White Flash]

Light detonates in front of you, ripping the world clean in two. On one side, the broken remains of Maria City; on the other, the forest of steles from the Void of Yin. A blinding white seam sizzles where they meet.
From that seam, the phantoms begin to pour through, one after another.
They are nothing like ordinary ghosts. Dark cyan mist seeps from the holes in their forms, and though no sound escapes, every wound seems to scream.

speaker: Voices of the Phantoms
content: <i><color=#7683a2>To receive is to render. To seek is to owe... Your wish has been granted... But ours... what of ours?!</color><i>

speaker: Voices of the Phantoms
content: <i><color=#7683a2>Has he paid the price? Has he paid the price? He has...</color><i>
female_content: <i><color=#7683a2>Has she paid the price? Has she paid the price? She has...</color><i>

speaker: Voices of the Phantoms
content: <i><color=#7683a2>But that doesn't count! Not yet paid... still not enough... not enough...</color><i>

speaker: Voices of the Phantoms
content: <i><color=#7683a2>Give us... give us... Pay your price!</color><i>
You drop hard onto your knees, palms sinking into the black ooze.
They crowd in, a mass of tangled forms passing through each other, their fingers clawing at the fissures between the emerging stone slabs, creeping nearer and nearer.
You. Only you. They're here for your life alone.

speaker: Voices of the Phantoms
content: <i><color=#7683a2><b>Give us... give us what must be paid...

speaker: Voices of the Phantoms
content: <i><color=#7683a2><b>Bones, blood, your name... any of it will do...

speaker: Voices of the Phantoms
content: <i><color=#7683a2><b>Give it to us! Give it to us!

One hand presses to your chest, cold fingers burrowing into your skin. Another climbs the nape of your neck, twisting into your hair and pulling your head back hard. You can see only the grey sky hanging over Maria City now.
Beneath you, the ground goes soft and yielding. Your pulse thuds in your ears. Beat by beat. Heavier and slower each time.

speaker: Keylan
content: They've crossed over again... Xiansheng!
[White flash, then rescue CG]
A blast of sword wind shoots past your ear from behind. You have no time to turn before something wrenches you back with brutal force.
It's Chengxiao's hand, clamped around your collar, dragging your whole body clear of the grasping phantoms.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: His <color=#fb9259>price</color>... has it not already been...
female_content: Her <color=#fb9259>price</color>... has it not already been...

content: The black fog freezes in place, its wild churn suddenly still. But only for a breath. Stung into rage, it comes roaring back, rushing at Chengxiao from every direction at once.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Cough... cough, cough...!
A violent cough rips through you, and your lungs sear with the effort.
The dark fog ahead has been blasted apart, but beyond it, fresh waves of the same sickly haze bleed through the sky's thin cracks, gathering their strength.
Chengxiao holds the line between you and them, his outline traced in eerie green flame. He raises his blade and points the way.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Follow this path straight ahead. It will take you to the rendezvous point. I suggest you don't linger.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Can we... even keep going...? I don't think we'll last much longer like this.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Those things were after me. If we run into more of them...

speaker: Chengxiao
content: You needn't worry about that. They know that your <color=#fb9259>price</color> has already been paid by another.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: His <color=#fb9259>price</color>... has it not already been paid by another?
female_content: Her <color=#fb9259>price</color>... has it not already been paid by another?

content: Another <color=#fb9259>price</color>. Paid by "another" on your behalf.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What about you?

speaker: Chengxiao
content: ...I left something with Li Xianling. I won't be leaving just yet.

A thread of urgency runs through his words, enough to make you study him more closely. Faint streaks of dark corruption stain Chengxiao's arm, marks eerily similar to the ones that had eaten into Lichen before.
You turn toward her body, meaning to check your suspicion, but a jarring splash of color stops you cold.
Her hand has turned a vivid, blood-red, and blurred golden runes drift across its surface like living talismans.
[Red screen flash + severed limb & blood splatter sound effects]

speaker: Lichen
content: You want a <color=#fb9259>price</color>...?

speaker: Lichen
content: Fine. Come and take it!
[24 Transition Flashback End]
So the person Chengxiao talked about is...

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Go.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Wait! ...I left something down there too.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: What did you leave? I can retrieve it for you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But how are you planning to get down there? Lichen destroyed the coin. If you force your way in like she did, you'll be affected too.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I can go in and help you find it. I just need to fall asleep to enter the Void of Yin. I don't need a coin.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: I have other tools. And the fact that even the coins could barely hold out down there is precisely why I cannot allow you to go charging into the Void of Yin in a <color=#fb9259>child's</color> body.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But I have a way to find Lichen, and it'll be fast.
Chengxiao's brow lifts at your words. He looks ready to cut in, but instead presses his lips shut and waits for you to finish.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: She only just entered the Void of Yin, and Maria City is already like this. If we leave her down there, things here are only going to get worse.
All around you, the ghostly green cracks in the sky keep widening. The phantoms' faint shrieks leak through from the realm beyond.
You shift your eyes meaningfully toward his arm.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That thing you lost is affecting your body too, isn't it? That's why you can't leave. With the cracks spreading, the anomalous activity spiking, phantoms crawling out of every crack... can you really hold out here?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And it's just Keylan and me on the road. No telling what might happen along the way. What if neither of us makes it?
Chengxiao looks down and sighs quietly.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: If it will truly set your minds at ease, then stay by my side for the time being.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: I will try not to take long. Retrieve what is mine, assess the situation, and then I'll stop. We leave together after that.
He raises his palm, and threads of talisman light leap from his fingers, weaving a protective circle at your feet that pushes back the roiling darkness encircling you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Since we're staying, let me try to find Lichen.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: She... promised me.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: You still wish to go after her.
Your mouth opens, ready to push back, but no words form. There's honestly nothing to deny. Still, the certainty in his voice lands like an accusation, and you feel the heat of unjustified guilt.
After a pause, Chengxiao breathes out a small laugh and looks down, murmuring to himself.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: She really does have a way with people. Even after everything she's done...
He turns to face you again, the last trace of amusement gone from his expression. His voice, when he speaks, is entirely serious.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Are you not afraid of her?

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Manipulating faith. Commanding phantoms. Nearly getting you killed just now. All of that was her.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But wasn't it also Lichen who paid that price for me just now?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The person you mentioned is her, isn't it?
You look over at Lichen's body. But Chengxiao doesn't follow your gesture.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It's not the first time she's done something like that... I had a part in what she has become too.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: If you believe this is your burden to carry, there is no need.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: A price, simply put, is nothing more than bearing the consequences of one's own choices.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Whether it was choosing to come to Maria City, attempting to bend the hearts of the living to cross the boundary between life and death, or paying that price on your behalf... every one of those was a decision she made herself.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: That being the case, these are the fruits of her own making. Hers alone to bear.
He pauses, and his tone eases, growing almost gentle. Still, what he says next lands heavy, dragging something inside you lower.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: All of it has nothing to do with you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...You're not wrong about that.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But back then, it was my choice to enter the Void of Yin in her place. And my choice to help her cross the boundary between Maria City and the Void of Yin. Those were decisions I made myself.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You said it yourself. You make a choice, you pay the price. If I do nothing now, isn't that just me running away from it? Even those phantoms couldn't sort out how the price should be paid in all of this.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That's exactly why I can't just leave her behind.
Chengxiao's expression stays mostly neutral, hard to read. Then, unexpectedly, a smile breaks through.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: The two of you really are rather alike...

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Go on, then. Try your luck down there.
So... that leaves one practical problem. How are you supposed to fall asleep?
You clamp your eyes shut, but after everything you've just been through, your brain is racing, offering not a shred of drowsiness.

Chengxiao regards you with a knowing look, as if he'd expected this all along. His fingers move swiftly through a sequence of seals, and with each motion, your eyelids droop further. Maria City melts away before you, bleeding steadily into the Void of Yin.
You're back in the Void of Yin. The moment your eyes open, your breath catches in your throat.
Pale cyan figures stretch in every direction, heads bowed in fervent prayer, as though awaiting an answer. The whole realm now resembles an immense ritual ground.
These things again... Unlike the creatures near the statues or the steles, they were born from Lichen herself.

speaker: Departed Souls
content: <i><color=#7683a2>Three kneelings... nine prostrations... O soul... return...

speaker: Departed Souls
content: <i><color=#7683a2>Three kneelings... nine prostrations... O soul... return...
The phantoms chant their prayers, mouths working the same sounds until the words fray into meaningless noise.
You hold your breath steady and weave cautiously among them, careful not to draw a single glance.
Solid footing is scarce, but now that you know what squirms beneath that sludge, you would rather leap from stone to stone than let your feet sink into it again.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Yes?
Whispers, thinner than all other sounds, reach you. They sound as if they're drifting in from another world, one far more distant and yet somehow more real than this one.

speaker: Weeping Voice
content: <i><color=#7683a2>I'm sorry... I'm so useless...

speaker: Weeping Voice
content: <i><color=#7683a2>Wait for me... I'll go beg the masters again... I'll beg the gods again... I'll give them whatever they want...
Each footfall presses a damp, sodden sound from the ground, like stepping through a layer of tears. The voices sharpen, syllable by syllable.
Around you, the pale cyan figures multiply, lining both sides of the path ahead. You walk through their gathering, and a coldness crawls slowly up your spine.
<color=#fb9259>Offer no glance to the departed. Lend no ear to the abyss. Speak no question to the spirits.</color>
You drill the warning into your own mind while keeping your eyes locked on the path ahead.

speaker: Departed Souls
content: <i><color=#7683a2>Three kneelings... nine prostrations... O soul... return...

speaker: Departed Souls
content: <i><color=#7683a2>Three kneelings... nine prostrations... O soul... return...

speaker: Departed Souls
content: <i><color=#7683a2>O soul... return... wish... granted...!
Their limbs start to extend, drawn out longer and longer until they dangle limply into the dark sludge.
Then their torsos buckle and fold, contorting in ways that hurt to witness. Their mouths keep moving, gnawing at nothing.
Mindless as insects, they scuttle toward you at startling speed.
[Show monster portrait, zoom in]
[QTE Button]
[Show monster portrait, zoom in]
[QTE Button]
[Show three monster portraits, zoom in]
You've run out of safe footing. Your heel sinks onto something fleshy, a hand or a foot. The phantoms' hollow gazes snap to you instantly.

speaker: Departed Souls
content: <i><color=#7683a2><b>You dare... stand in our way...!
[Screen shake + portrait zooms in]
By the stars I walk; ghosts wail, gods tremble! All foul spirits, seized and delivered to justice—
A rush of flame licks past you, drawing a line of fire that sends the phantoms reeling backward.
Amid the crackling heat, there's a brittle snap at your back, like dead wood splitting.
You spin around and find yourself staring at a familiar face, one that doesn't look quite as you remember.
[Chengxiao portrait]
He still bears Chengxiao's form, but a hard mask now covers his eyes, and dark fissures coil up his arms, cinching the fabric of his sleeves. The fate waiting for him speaks for itself.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: What is it? You think I'm one of them?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: How did you get down here? I thought Lichen had the coin.
He lifts an arm and offers you a full view of his form. Unlike Lichen, the figure before you is something nearer to a half-seen silhouette.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: I was able to assist you before because I had sealed my soul within the coin. But Li Xianling shattered it. My soul escaped and became trapped here in the Void of Yin.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So that's what you left behind. Without your soul, of course you can't leave.
A nod. His tone remains light, almost dismissively so.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: On the bright side, I can now be of proper use to you down here.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: I am well aware of what Li Xianling said about my coin. That it could only flip up or down, that a single swat from a monster sent it flying, that it was nothing compared to her spells.
Those last words were yours, actually. But you have no intention of owning up to that.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...I've seen it for myself now. You're the stronger one, clearly.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Telling people exactly what they want to hear... did you pick that up from her as well? She and her silver tongue... Do not let her be a bad influence.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: To be fair, her spells are still stronger. She'll use just about anything.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: That one, forever resorting to unorthodox methods, burning through her own spells in the process. Do not let her be a bad influence.
Your gaze falls. That vision of her blood-soaked hand cuts through your thoughts again, and your chest tightens in response.

speaker: Phantom
content: Hsss... Haaa...
Not far off, the phantoms Chengxiao struck back are writhing, their form slowly knitting back into clarity. The broken limbs littering the ground have begun to squirm, crawling toward the torsos.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Watch out, they are getting back up.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: No need for concern.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: These souls are still quite weak. So long as we refrain from disrupting their ritual, they will not attack.
It's not like you wanted to disturb them. You just had nowhere else to go.
The grumble is still settling in your chest when his lips curve upward, and he throws a question back at you.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Have you not already conducted the experiment yourself?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Conducted the experiment? I've been running for my life down here.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: This is part of the experiment.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You... you've been tagging along as a coin this whole time, and all the while I was your test subject? Some professor you are...
Your accusation lands, but he takes it without a trace of guilt.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: "Test subject" is not a derogatory term. A pity we are in a place like this, or the work might have earned you some extra school credit.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Besides, I was watching over you the entire way. And you came out just fine, did you not?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...I've heard that line from Lichen too. Birds of a feather, I guess...
His reassurance doesn't land. A phantom up ahead suddenly raises its head, and your muscles jerk, ready to flee, before you even decide to move.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Stand still.
A steady hand clamps onto your shoulder and keeps you rooted where you stand. Only then do you sense it: something thick and frigid gliding just past your heel.
Seconds drag by before the presence retreats into the distance. You lift your gaze and find Chengxiao's masked face above you, the corner of his mouth tilted faintly upward.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: I am watching.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Right.

Your fingers gradually uncurl, and you track the phantom as it moves into the distance. Its drifting motion mirrors the cyan fish exactly. Then again, why wouldn't it? They have always been the same thing.

speaker: %u
content: These phantoms... they're all turned from those spirit fish, the ones Lichen was controlling.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: They appear to be the wishes of the people, gathered and shaped by Li Xianling. When many pray in the Realm of Yang, these wishes take form here in the Void of Yin. The stronger their faith, the more human these things become.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: In turn, they repeat their rituals of worship here, over and over. Whether this is mere mimicry of the living, or whether some other purpose drives it... I have only speculation to offer at present.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: I cannot draw any conclusions without further study.
He looks at you while he says it, then lets his eyes drift back toward the contorted cyan figures in the distance.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: But if you wish to try...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I don't.
You shut it down immediately. Chengxiao must have seen it coming, because the moment the words leave your mouth, a laugh slips out from him.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Honestly, I kind of wish you'd just read the fortune like a proper Daoist priest right now...

speaker: Chengxiao
content: I already did. The divination says one thing only: engage them in prolonged combat, and death is certain.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Yeah, I figured that part out.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Which is precisely why knowing what will happen is not enough. One must understand why.

The phantoms he'd mentioned as subjects for study keep murmuring their ceaseless prayers, bowing their heads to the empty air. With each bow, the color of their forms becomes a little brighter than before.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: It seems Li Xianling is conducting something of an experiment herself... She has finally learned to pursue knowledge through proper methods. A pity she has applied them in entirely the wrong place.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Their appearance is growing increasingly aberrant. If they continue this ritual unchecked, the consequences may well defy imagination.
Chengxiao sighs.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Though I must admit... I bear some small responsibility for what has come to pass.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Your responsibility...?

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Which is why I had to come and see for myself what she was truly after.
He seems intent on avoiding a direct reply. You tighten your lips and decide not to push further.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Alright. And we need to find a way to get your soul back, too.
He smiles and gives a nod.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Then I shall be counting on you.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Naturally, she had no intention of letting me spoil her plans. She summoned a number of souls to waylay me and used the opportunity to slip away.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I know how to find her.
—<color=#fb9259>Shackles</color>.
You extend your hand, and a subtle pulse stirs at the center of your palm, threading outward into the deeper dark. You let it guide you, stepping forward into the unknown.
The cyan silhouettes multiply as you press on, packed ever tighter, yet none acknowledge you. They simply cycle through the same ritual: kneel, pray, bow.
You and Chengxiao move through them with practiced discipline, adhering to the safest rule: don't look, don't listen, don't ask. Shut them out as completely as you can.
As you walk past, one of the phantoms suddenly leans in close.
Its outline sags before you, loose and shapeless, the shoulders and arms pleated with deep folds that look ready to slump into nothing.

speaker: Phantom
content: <i><color=#7683a2>...Could you... hear me...

speaker: Phantom
content: <i><color=#7683a2>...Could you... tell them... I'm still waiting... I can keep waiting...

speaker: Phantom
content: <i><color=#7683a2>...Please... let our wish be granted...
<color=#fb9259>Offer no glance to the departed. Lend no ear to the abyss. Speak no question to the spirits.</color>
The figure bows low before you, a deep and solemn kowtow, and then it is gone. But the sound of its weeping remains, soaking slowly into your thoughts like water through cloth.

speaker: Faint Voice
content: <i><color=#7683a2>Mom... does it still hurt...? Why do I keep dreaming you're hurting...? Just like that day... you curled up so small...

speaker: Faint Voice
content: <i><color=#7683a2>Let me see you one last time... come tell me yourself... please...?

speaker: Faint Voice
content: <i><color=#7683a2>Just one last time...
You don't know these people, or the ones they mourn. But the weight inside their voices, that you know intimately.
The desperate begging, the wailing, the prayers born from hopelessness: you've seen and heard them all before. And yet, is there really nothing you can do...?
A thick, wet footfall sounds at your ear, and Chengxiao steps up beside you.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: It would seem these are souls who perished in a fire. The Eastern Continent has seen several major fires in recent years. The largest among them claimed hundreds of thousands of lives in a single night.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Were you... there?

speaker: Chengxiao
content: That one, I did foresee.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Then did you try to do anything? Before it happened?

speaker: Chengxiao
content: I contacted the local authorities. They dismissed it as baseless nonsense. "Your reputation lies in ruins," they said, "and now you stoop to spreading rumors..."
Chengxiao lifts his palm toward the floating green specks. They orbit his arm in a few slow loops, then veer off into the distance.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: But the "rumors" spread all the same. The people panicked, and so the authorities sealed the city. When the fire came, no one could get out.
The note of weariness in his words vanishes like the scattered green sparks, replaced by his usual cool composure.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: So you see, prophecy is a thing that cuts both ways. Believe it or not, the outcome is no different. The old saying goes that the will of heaven must never be revealed—not because revealing it invites divine punishment, but because revealing it changes nothing. The fate has already been written.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Do you believe in it, then? Prophecy.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Lichen told me your shifu came to you both in a dream, said you'd find a "god" here. Is that why you're here in Maria City?

speaker: No, no. I don't care about the truth or falsehood of gods or games. Those are from the work. I've seen all sorts of absurd things at work. Plus, you've paid me well.
content: I believe in the fate that prophecy reveals. But what concerns me more is causality. Everything that happens has its reasons.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: I want to know what has been sending us these dreams, and why.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But if you believe fate is already set, what's the point of knowing the process? Is it just academic curiosity?

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Fate may be beyond changing. But the process can still offer insight. Should something similar come to pass again, at least one would know what to expect.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But what if one day, something you learn from the process turns out to be exactly what you need to change something?

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Then I would call it a welcome surprise. But that is not why I came.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: The laws of causality exist for a reason. Wanting to change everything, that is Li Xianling's way. She can scorn the price for breaking those laws all she likes. The price will find her regardless.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: You have seen it yourself. Those who attempt to cross the boundary between life and death become nothing more than these wandering phantoms in the Void of Yin, trapped in endless suffering. She is already well down that road.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: What, do you think I'm a rather poor excuse for an uncle?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...No. You're right. I've lived through everything you said myself.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But I'm still curious. You foresee it all, and you can't change a thing. Can you really live with that? Like with that fire.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Are you asking because you want to know if I can live with it? Or because you cannot?

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Then what is it you wish to change?
Your lips part, but you find yourself staring at his face with nothing to say. No answer has formed. You simply cannot bring yourself to speak.
While the silence drags on, several pale green shadows begin to drift toward him.
Chengxiao lifts a finger to his lips, hushing you. Then he opens his arms wide, as if welcoming them.
That's right: just don't interact. Offer no glance to the departed. Lend no ear to the abyss. Speak no question to the spirits. Follow the rules and nothing will go wrong.
So you do nothing. You only watch as the ghosts gather around him and hold him close. He stands among them as he truly is in death, silent and still.
After a while, the phantoms scatter. Chengxiao smiles.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: See? Everything will be fine.
You want to answer him, to pull your lips into a smile, because you're supposed to feel at ease.
But the gesture won't come. So you turn your face aside instead and look up toward the distant path the phantoms took.
[Altar Background]
It's an ocean of cyan lanterns, stretching endlessly, bathing everything in a light that feels more like a warning than a welcome.
[Altar - Upper Half]

speaker: Praying Voices
content: <i><color=#7683a2>May wishes find their end... may longing find its anchor... may souls find their vessel...

speaker: Praying Voices
content: <i><color=#7683a2>May wishes find their end... may longing find its anchor... may souls find their vessel...
Guided by the shackles, you step deeper into the lantern sea, the air thick with low, indistinct chanting.

Lichen should be here. But everywhere you look, there are only the soul lanterns, cyan and countless, suspended at every height and swaying softly. They stretch from where you stand to the very limit of sight.

You can't help but study each lantern as you pass. They're made of paper, and the pale cyan glow within throws wavering human silhouettes across their surfaces, flickering frame by frame like a shadow play.
The faces bear no eyes or noses, only a split where a mouth should be, stretched open in what might be a grin.

Figures kneel and slam their heads against the ground. Once, twice, three times... Their skulls have already collapsed, no longer recognizable, just swollen lumps of ruined flesh. They feel nothing and carry on anyway, bowing until those lumps flatten entirely and stick to the earth.

Candles burn in their bare hands, the fire climbing and consuming each finger in turn. The hands dissolve slowly, like tallow, meat and bone blending into a shapeless drip of grease. The flames, nourished, only rise higher.
Each figure has a bowl set before them. With small blades, they gash their palms and let the liquid trickle out, but the bowl never fills. Their hands are no longer hands, just unrecognizable ruin.
In that lantern, you see yourself.
Faceless, but unmistakably you: same frame, same clothes. He kneels low before the stone statues and monsters you've seen along the road.
female_content: Faceless, but unmistakably you: same frame, same clothes. She kneels low before the stone statues and monsters you've seen along the road.

content: His spine is curved into a posture of submission you've never worn, skull hanging heavy under an unseen burden.
female_content: Her spine is curved into a posture of submission you've never worn, skull hanging heavy under an unseen burden.

content: Abruptly, his head snaps toward you.
female_content: Abruptly, her head snaps toward you.

speaker: You?
content: <color=#dg1f1f><i>It's your turn...

speaker: You?
content: <color=#dg1f1f><i>Make your offering... and your wish shall be granted...
[White Flash]

speaker: Chengxiao
content: ...Don't touch anything here.
A hand bats your arm down softly. You snap out of it and notice, with a jolt, how close your hand had reached toward the lantern.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: That is where we need to go.
You lift your eyes in the direction he's looking. From the crown of every lantern, fine red threads stretch upward, all of them arcing toward a vast sphere suspended at the heart of the lantern sea.
The closer you come, the harder the shackles tug, until you're standing right before the stone sphere.
Countless crimson threads are lashed around it, and the giant heart beats with a slow, steady rhythm, as if alive.
Overhead, a wound in the fabric of the world yawns open and snaps shut, over and over. With each pulse, it breathes out a gust of damp, decayed air that hits your skin.

speaker: Chaotic Voices
content: <color=#dg1f1f><i>Without rules... nothing holds its shape...

speaker: Chaotic Voices
content: <color=#dg1f1f><i>Let... everything... return to the right path...

speaker: Chaotic Voices
content: <color=#dg1f1f><i>Do not walk toward... the ending... you fear most...
Something speaks, and the sound crawls into your brain like a damp parasite, sliding past every defense.

speaker: Chaotic Voices
content: ...rules... right path...

speaker: Chaotic Voices
content: ...ending... fear...
...Are these words meant for you?
In your daze, the logic feels sound: uphold the rules of the Void of Yin, restore the proper order, and only then...
<color=#dg1f1f><i>Your wish shall be granted.
[Transition 1s + sound of a sword being drawn]

A shrill screech of metal grinds through the whisper, reducing it to a formless hum. You snap back to awareness. Chengxiao is gazing down at the blade in his grip, its edge gleaming cold under the cyan lantern light.
His head hangs low, as if listening to something.
Around him, an unsteady surge of Mania begins to coil and churn. You edge a careful step toward him.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Chengxiao?
He doesn't answer right away, his hand gripping the hilt tightly.
Then, after a few seconds, he pulls in a deep breath and lets his fingers fall loose.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: ...Mm. What is it?
He draws himself upright again, still not meeting your eyes, his attention locked on the sphere ahead. But the surge of Mania has quieted. For the moment, at least.
You shake your head, rattling the last of the hum from your skull, and force your eyes to lock onto the sphere.
It rests in the tight grip of a pedestal, and the base is buried deep into the sludge below. Both are cast in the same cold, hard grey stone, much like the steles you first saw in the Void of Yin.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This doesn't look like something Lichen could have made.
Perhaps she used those wishes and corrupted the wandering dead, but this stone sculpture is anchored in something far older.
A string of unfamiliar cyan glyphs drifts above the pedestal's surface.
<color=#11F0F0><b><i>Will and longing are born entwined, tethered to form.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Li Xianling... you've really taken it this far...

speaker: Chengxiao
content: You've gone too far... and I couldn't stop you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What does it say? What is she actually trying to do?

speaker: Chengxiao
content: This is the "truth" the Void of Yin has left for us.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Guide people to repeat the ritual, strengthen their faith, and they will manifest here in the Void of Yin as wandering souls.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Then, with an artifact to bind and stabilize those souls, one can bring something new into being.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: And as for the artifact... we have one right here in front of us.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So that's why she's been controlling those phantoms. That's why she came here. She wants to gather all those phantoms and fuse them into something stronger...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But could something like that really bring a person back from the dead...?

speaker: Chengxiao
content: No.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: What Li Xianling truly wants is to create, with her own hands, a divine savior, a god that can save the world. Something to stand against the calamities.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But how could anything made from these wandering souls be a savior?
After all, almost everything in the Void of Yin is, in one way or another, a creation of Mania.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Of course it couldn't. It would be nothing more than a monster, no different from the <color=#fb9259>calamities</color> themselves.

Tied to the <color=#fb9259>DisSea</color>, a monster no different from the <color=#fb9259>calamities</color> themselves... Something stirs at the back of your mind, a half-formed recollection of a similar being that you know far too well...

speaker: Du Ruo
content: <color=#fb9259>Apostles of Ashes</color> are products of concentrated Mania, a material projection of collective consciousness. They manifest themselves in this world, in the forms of disasters and Wraith Beasts.

If what's forming is truly an <color=#fb9259>Apostle of Ashes</color>, and it breaches Maria City with no Hypercubes to counter it, the result would be annihilation on a scale the people of that age could never endure.
Everyone here will die.
<b>You have to stop its birth now!
Your fingertips barely graze the sphere when glyphs erupt, multiplying and elongating into unrecognizable forms. They twist and knot together like a swarm of insect legs gnawing at each other.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: "Will and longing are born entwined, tethered to form"...

speaker: Lichen
content: ..."When form is masterless, every desire seeks its own path."
She raises her eyes to the pillar, where the same cyan glyphs flicker in frantic bursts.
A sound descends from overhead, a visceral thrum as if drawn from the lungs of something enormous and ancient. It swells, louder and louder.
The sphere shudders, convulsing against its pedestal as though fighting to tear itself free. From within the black maw of the void, a shape becomes darker and more solid by the second.

<color=#11F0F0><b><i>Will and longing are born entwined, tethered to form. 
When form is masterless, every desire seeks its own path.
Every soul lantern goes dark in the same breath. Absolute blackness crashes down around you.
Then the void pulses, swelling in rhythm with your own heartbeat, turns into a form of pure chaos. It's something beyond anything you've ever witnessed, and it hurls itself at you.

Your last blow lands, and the chaos before you begins to lose its shape, scattering into the dark. The sphere cracks and breaks free from its pedestal. A soft cyan glow seeps back into the air, casting its light over the wreckage.
Beneath the ruined stone platform, a slab grinds slowly aside, unveiling a passage leading down.
[Transition 1s]
Then the shadows inside the lanterns begin to move.

They draw themselves into thin, sinuous threads and slip through the tiny holes at the top of each lantern. Streaming between you and Chengxiao, they pour past like a silent river, cascading into the entrance at your feet and flooding the dark passage below.
The shackles thrum with increasing urgency. Lichen is inside, nearly close enough to touch.
You step forward, and instantly, fingers lock tight around your wrist, stopping you cold.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Stop!

speaker: Chengxiao
content: This is beyond us now. I'm sending you back.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Lichen is right down there. We can still make it!

speaker: Chengxiao
content: The wicked being that will come next is beyond your ability to handle.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That's not just some wicked being! It's something way worse than any of them.
You clench your jaw and claw at his fingers with your other hand, trying to peel them off. They don't move, not even a fraction.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If we let her finish making that thing and it gets loose in Maria City, it's over. We have to stop her now—
The air thickens with chaotic whispers again, seeping in from every side and pressing closer around you both.
<color=#dg1f1f><i>Without rules... nothing holds its shape...
<color=#dg1f1f><i>Let... everything... return to the right path...
A subtle tremor runs along the rim of Chengxiao's mask. From somewhere deep inside, two points of dark red light flicker to life.
His breathing turns ragged and loud. Where his hand grips your wrist, a wave of Mania surges upward.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Let go. If you won't help, then I'll go myself.
You tear your arm away with a violent jerk, and this time his grip breaks. Stumbling from the force, you steady yourself and immediately dash toward the passage.
[White flash + sword swing SFX] Cut to CG
The hiss of a blade slicing through the air reaches you. Cold steel settles across your shoulder.
The mask moves aside, and the eyes beneath lock onto yours.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: This ends here.
[Standoff CG]

speaker: Chengxiao
content: This ends here.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: You have already intervened once, and made an attempt to destroy the altar. Yet you were unable to eliminate them entirely.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Those phantoms have already been scattered. Now we just need to find Lichen—

speaker: Chengxiao
content: That line of "truth" has a second half.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: "When form is masterless, all longings seek one of their own."

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Which is to say, without a vessel to bind them, those phantoms will only grow more restless. They will seek out the next tangible form to latch onto.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Such as... a human.

The phantoms pour past you in a frenzy, flooding the passage ahead. You watch the river of pale cyan, and a cold weight sinks through your chest. They're hunting for a living vessel to latch onto. Any of you could serve, including Lichen.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So there's no way out at all, then?! They accounted for everything!
You aren't sure who you mean by "them." Is it the presence that whispered from the altar? Is it fate itself? The answer feels irrelevant. You're past the point of caring.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: These rules they've set... are they even right?! You heard those voices too, didn't you? And you're just going to accept that? Is this what you would call fate?!

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Yes. You have seen it for yourself, and you have made your attempt. It is time to recognize when to yield.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Rules exist for a reason. They are not so easily crossed.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: I had thought you would prove different from her in the end. That you would understand the cost, respect the weight of the rules, and know when you had reached your limit. Unlike her, forever lost in her own delusions.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: If you are just as obstinate as she is, then I will send you back.
His arm lifts again. Your fist tightens as you fix your gaze on the blade suspended in the air, its edges limned by swirling crimson fire and dancing sparks.
You track its arc, waiting for the strike aimed directly at you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Nngh...!
You reel backward, your gaze racing across his form, hunting for any gap in his movements.
When his blade sweeps toward your flank, it falters, just a fraction of a second, enough for you to throw your arm up and block.
Trap or not, you have no time to second-guess it.
Crimson light erupts through the gaps in your fingers, slamming into his blade as it descends.
The strike is deflected, the sword tip skidding wide, but Chengxiao holds his ground. He just watches you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Neither of us wants to actually hurt the other. So why are we wasting time?

speaker: Chengxiao
content: We needn't, if you are willing to stand down.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Stand down...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're telling me to stand down. But what about your own soul?

speaker: Chengxiao
content: This is precisely the consequence of me breaking the rules.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Those who dwell in the Realm of Yang have no business meddling in the Void of Yin. Yet I spoke out. I provoked her. I allowed her to seize my coin, and in doing so, I revealed to her that a physical object can be used to anchor a soul. For that, I must pay the price.

speaker: Copper Coin
content: <b>Why did you stop?

speaker: Chengxiao
content: I scared you back there, didn't I? Forgive me. I had to say what I said to buy enough time to get you out. Had you remained in contact with her any longer, I doubt you would have lasted much past that.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That's exactly why I can't just follow the rules of this place and stand here watching you...
You look at the face beneath his mask, knowing it will one day be buried by the weight of years.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...end up exactly like what I'm looking at right now.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The way you are now... it's not just from losing part of your soul.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If that monster is created, you'll die here. You'll end up just like Lichen... trapped in Maria City, stuck somewhere between life and death.
He lets out a quiet laugh.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: If you already know how this ends from having seen the future, then there is even less reason to waste time here.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...You knew it the whole time.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: I do not know who you truly are. I only know that you are not that child, for that child never possessed the power to bring Li Xianling into the Void of Yin.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: What I also know is this: time and again along this journey, you clutched that coin tightly in your palm, wishing for nothing more than to escape this world.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're right. Ever since I got to Maria City, all I've wanted is to get out.
Trapped inside a child's body, eroded by the Illusory Moon, drained of almost everything, you've reached the point where even your shackles feel like a cage.
What has Maria City, the Illusory Moon, this whispering presence in your head really done to you? Broken your flesh? Unraveled your sanity?
Or turned you into someone ruled by <color=#fb9259>fear</color>, too afraid to take another step?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And for that, I turned to things I don't even understand.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The world I come from doesn't have ghosts or gods. Everything I've seen along the way is all just creatures born of Mania.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But somehow I keep believing in them more and more... That they're something else. Beings that bridge heaven and earth, like Lichen says. That if I just listen, they'll show me the way.
Meeting his stare, you advance into the surge of Mania radiating from the sword. The sludge grips your feet, but you leave your mark with every step.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And while I did that, I watched the people around me sink deeper and deeper into this place, one by one...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Being trapped here forever, I can live with that. But doing nothing? That I can't accept.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I refuse to accept it.
[White flash + sound effect]
He pulls the sword free from the sludge, but this time it slides into its sheath. His face hardens, and he offers you no further words.
You take a step toward the entrance, then another. The blade's whistle, a sound that once steadied you and once terrified you, never comes.
And so you leave it all behind, the grieving cries sweeping you forward as you race toward the tunnel's end.
[Change Fraser's corridor to green]
There is no end in sight, and the way back has vanished. You are walking through what feels like a long dark casket.
Phantoms stream past you, and their lament echoes from wall to wall, a chorus of quiet, endless weeping.

speaker: Phantom
content: <i><color=#7683a2>A place to rest... a place to rest...!

speaker: Phantom
content: <i><color=#7683a2>Give me a place to rest...!
Shrieks of terror flood in from the darkness behind, only to be caught in the cramped stone chamber, ricocheting endlessly off the walls.
Lichen gazes at the pillar in front of her. Its crown has been shattered, and a web of hairline fractures snakes down its length. Still, the pale cyan light radiating from the stone intensifies.
Chunks of debris tumble down and strike the ground at her feet. She doesn't even flinch.

speaker: Lichen
content: ...Heh.
She lifts her hand and swirls her fingers through the air. The drifting cyan phantoms hesitate, just for a heartbeat, then rush inward, gathering fast at the center.

speaker: Phantom
content: <i><color=#7683a2>Aaaaaaaah!

speaker: Phantom
content: <i><color=#7683a2>Aaaaaaaah!
Whoosh!

A paper talisman slices through the air and slaps onto a phantom's head, burning it to ash in a heartbeat. A second one follows right behind, flying toward the rift and cutting off the phantoms streaming out.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Even when none of this concerns you... even when you already know how it ends for us...

speaker: Chengxiao
content: You still cannot bring yourself to do nothing...
...Bang!
The paper talisman gives out, fluttering wildly before it detonates and blasts the leading phantoms apart. But the reprieve is brief; more of them come clawing through the rift, a relentless flood.
Chengxiao staggers backward. His arm, caught in the explosion, is already darkening.

speaker: Keylan
content: Xiansheng... is your hand alright?

speaker: Keylan
content: Xiansheng? Xiansheng?

speaker: Lichen
content: ...Lyu Buzhou?

speaker: Lichen
content: So, what does the divination say?
Her voice carried a smile as she plucked needles from the potted pine on his windowsill. The Daoist texts said the pine was resilient, weathering frost and snow, evergreen and unfading.
She drifted closer and studied the hexagrams on the table with a show of keen interest. In truth, she didn't care at all what they foretold.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Whatever the hexagrams say, you intend to go regardless. Am I wrong?

speaker: Lichen
content: Hmm... <color=#fb9259>"Flames dye the heavens, and the divine draws near; the spirit is slowly steeped, until the divine dwells within; the dragon soars too high and learns regret, and what descends into darkness shall not return."</color>...

speaker: Lichen
content: And someone looked at that and called it a terribly ill omen?

speaker: Lichen
content: For those of us who seek the Dao, a glimpse behind the curtain of heaven is about the best thing you could hope for in one lifetime.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Then perhaps you ought to have cast the divination yourself. Though I confess some doubt as to whether you still recall the method.
Lichen shook her head, still smiling, and pressed her palm against the coarse paper. Pine needles slipped from between her fingers and scattered across the surface.

speaker: Lichen
content: And what would be the point? The heavens and I have never seen eye to eye on much.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Heh. Let the others hear you speak that way, and they shall have fresh cause to label you a heretic.

speaker: Lichen
content: "Baleful star," "wretched"... Trust me, I've been called worse.

speaker: Lichen
content: You know what I really can't stand, though? Sitting around doing nothing. Letting my backside gather moss up on that mountain.

speaker: Lichen
content: So? Have you decided yet?

speaker: Keylan
content: ...Xiansheng?

speaker: Chengxiao
content: ...I'm fine.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: ...So that is how it is...

speaker: Chengxiao
content: <color=#fb9259>The spirit is slowly steeped, until the divine dwells within</color>...
He had meant to follow, partly to keep a watch on Li Xianling. That girl put too much faith in the unorthodox and would walk herself right into the fate the hexagrams had laid out. As for himself...
He once believed that clinging to the rules and reasoning through each step would eventually reveal a way out.
But when had the rules started to trap him instead? The more he struggled to see clearly, the tighter they bound him, barring him from taking a single step forward.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Heh. It seems I, too, have wandered too far.
From the moment he stepped into that ocean of lanterns, the <color=#fb9259>voice</color> had been guiding him, patient and insistent, telling him to set things right and push no further.
It demanded he face the "truth," yet prevented him from chasing it?

speaker: Chengxiao
content: You guided us here. You have already written the ending for us. Why go to the trouble of this charade? Unless you fear what else we might uncover.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: It would seem the divine is not so very divine after all.

Chengxiao casts a glance around. Keylan is still at it behind him, jabbing at the receiver in his hands, straining to catch a signal from camp. The device spits back nothing but static and error tones.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Step back a little.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: I would like to see for myself—

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Exactly what our esteemed "god" is so worried about.
He pulls in a long breath and murmurs an incantation under his breath. The markings on his arm darken, and through the mist, ghostly flames flicker to life.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Above and below, in all realms of the dead...

speaker: Chengxiao
content: <i><color=#7683a2>...no fiend shall disobey this command!
[Chengxiao's corrupted character art]
In front of the ruined tunnel entrance, the shadow wavers briefly, then thickens into something more solid. Then, he steps forward.
At last, you arrive at the end of the passage.
A stone chamber opens before you. In its center, a pillar lies toppled, its surface etched with strange, twisting patterns. You recognize the same motifs that marked the base of the shattered sphere.
Since you tracked the trail all the way here from that place, these two structures might once have been a single piece.
Which means what you shattered back there was only the top half...

speaker: Chengxiao
content: You have already intervened once, and made an attempt to destroy the altar. Yet you were unable to eliminate them entirely.
You force yourself to stay calm. It changes nothing. You'll battle it out once more if you must. Whatever this "ritual" is, you are going to stop it.
[Lichen's portrait]
Lichen stands facing away, her clothes fouled beyond recognition by mud and gore. Her eyes are fixed upward, fixed on her great creation: the enormous, expanding shape of darkness looming ahead.
The thing has grown truly colossal now, its shadow stretching across the ground, all the way to your feet.
You can't see her face. Having finally witnessed this power, what fills her eyes? Pride, envy, or something closer to the fervor of a pilgrim?
She hears your footsteps halt behind her and lets out a soft laugh.

speaker: Lichen
content: So you've finally come around? Here to lend me a hand?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This is your shifu?

speaker: Lichen
content: Of course not.

speaker: Lichen
content: Shifu worried herself sick over the Perishing Star. Always worn down, always tired. Could barely walk a few steps without stopping to catch her breath. She never looked anything like this.
She looks down at her palm, and her voice drifts for a split second, almost unmoored, before snapping back into something cold and absolute.

speaker: Lichen
content: Shifu, or the so-called "Celestial Master," whoever they want to call on... hah.

speaker: Lichen
content: When it comes down to it, begging gods and bowing to masters is never going to get you as far as counting on yourself.

speaker: Lichen
content: Anyway, this is what people believe in. A real "god" is nothing more than mortal faith given shape.

speaker: Lichen
content: Turn that kind of power against the calamities, and it would be almost too easy.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're trying to harness the Void of Yin, but that power is just going to swallow you whole in the end—

speaker: Lichen
content: That sounds awfully preachy. Who's been filling your head with that?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Nobody told me what to say or do.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm standing here because I can't just stand by and watch you keep going down this road.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You use people's faith, but can you even hear what they're really asking for? The last thing they want is to summon a monster.
She lets out a quiet chuckle.

speaker: Lichen
content: What they're really asking for...

speaker: Lichen
content: Two years ago, I went southwest to collect stories about prophetic dreams and walked right into a massive earthquake. I ended up staying for three months.

speaker: Lichen
content: Anyone with any clout in the area had already cleared out. No help coming from them. But somehow, everyone pinned their hopes on me, just one traveling Daoist. And wouldn't you know it, cheering people up with my little tricks? That's kind of my specialty.

speaker: Lichen
content: Wooden sword to ward off evil, gourd to cure what ails you. But you know what everyone wanted most? Incense. Any idea why?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What exactly are you trying to say?

speaker: Lichen
content: We'd dig people out of the rubble one by one, and then we'd have to put them back in the ground. But the earth was split wide open. Where was there even room to bury anyone? It was slow enough already with those beat-up shovels and pickaxes, and this was the southwest in July, hottest and muggiest time of the year...
Your stomach lurches. She sees the look on your face and smiles, her reddened eyes locking onto you as she presses the question again.

speaker: Lichen
content: So tell me, then. What is it that people really want?
With a sweep of her sleeve, she shows off the immense form looming at her back, her expression verging on proud.

speaker: Lichen
content: When you get right down to it, peace and a steady world. Isn't that all anyone ever asks for? So I'll give them exactly that.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: With that thing? You think you can control it? You can't even keep these scattered phantoms in check right now.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If it ever breaks out of Maria City, slips free of you, Chengxiao, from everyone's control, it could kill tens of thousands of people in the blink of an eye.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're standing closer to this power than anyone. You have to feel that.

speaker: Lichen
content: "Will and longing are born entwined, tethered to form"...

speaker: Lichen
content: Sure, you destroyed the pillar. But the principle still holds. A physical anchor can stabilize belief. See? I really am still a woman of "science."

speaker: Lichen
content: Something to draw them all together... how hard could that be to find?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: There's nothing here that could—

speaker: Chengxiao
content: ...without a vessel to bind them, those phantoms will only grow more restless. They will seek out the next tangible form to latch onto.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Such as... a human.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Stop! Don't you—
You launch yourself off the rubble. But she's faster, her hand already raised. Red ribbons whip from her sleeves and streak toward the scattered phantoms, cinching tight around their ghostly forms.
Golden light races along the ribbons, and with every pulse, the outline of the "god" sharpens into greater clarity.
[Monster silhouette appears]
The Benevolent Mother looms above, gazing down upon you both.

Her face is hidden behind copper coins strung together with red threads, and it's precisely this concealment that stirs the imagination: how holy, how radiant must the visage beneath be, surpassing all that human eyes have ever beheld.
It feels as though merely kneeling in devotion, bowing your head, and offering your all would earn her forgiveness for every sin and the granting of every wish.

speaker: Whispers
content: <color=#dg1f1f><i>Yes... she will grant your every wish...
[Red flash]

speaker: Whispers
content: <color=#dg1f1f><i><b>It... will grant your every wish...

speaker: Whispers
content: <color=#dg1f1f><i><b>All you have to do... is give yourself... to It...
[White flash]

speaker: Lichen
content: Heh.
The edge of her mouth tugs upward, and a ghost of a laugh slips out, so faint you almost miss it.
Her fingers carve glowing seals into the air, and crimson-cyan fire roars to life in her hand as she utters the spell to command the specters.

speaker: Lichen
content: Lord of the abyss, bow your heads and guard my gates!
Behind Lichen, the black mist thickens and knots with the votive force, churning like the breath of something colossal stirring awake.
She faces you, her tone like frost.

speaker: Lichen
content: Go back.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And if I don't?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What then? You'll use your power, your monster, to kill me too?
She doesn't seem angry. Her face now looks nearly identical to the phantoms you've seen in this world: pale, stiff, incapable of forming any expression.
The "god" at her back rises again. Lichen regards you with cold detachment. The hidden meanings beneath her words and glances are lost to you now. Perhaps they always were.
Maybe she's ready to crush the obstacle standing before her, just as she once cut down those phantoms for your sake. To her, both are equally effortless.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Do whatever you want to me.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But I'm not leaving, not until I get you out of here.
The space resounds with furious roars, as if answering your refusal to yield.

The sheer force of it blurs your sight. Lichen's silhouette melts into the black mist. You draw a slow breath and tighten your fist. Red sparks glimmer in your palm, fragile as candle flames in the thick fog pressing in on all sides.
But you will not turn back. Not here.

speaker: Apostle of Ashes
content: <color=#dg1f1f><i><b>AAAAAAH!
The monster raises its hand, blade held high. Lichen's form follows in perfect sync, as if pulled by the same strings.
[Red Flash + Special Effect]
The executioner's blade meant to end you falls, but its edge meets Lichen's shoulder instead. A shudder runs through her body, and the ribbons binding her cinch deeper.

speaker: Lichen
content: Silence...!
The monster jerks sharply in rhythm with the bell at her hip, then, impossibly, falls still. But under its fluttering robe, the black muck keeps writhing, waiting for the next chance to strike.

speaker: Lichen
content: ...Go back.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You really can't control it yet, can you?
She stands, her shoulders still trembling. She doesn't turn your way.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Lichen...
You walk toward her. The nearer you draw, the more savagely the Mania surges, eating away at your mind and dulling your senses.
Your resistance is nearly spent. If she chose to act now, you'd have no strength left to defend.
She could do it again, just like before: hoist you up, wrap her hands around your throat, and crush your bones.
But her hands are no longer pale. She wouldn't even need force. A flick of her fingers, and those beast-like claws would pierce your throat without effort, opening the path for the horror behind her.
(Transition 2s)
But when you stand close enough to touch, she does nothing.
You rest your hands lightly against her waist. Under your palms, Mania churns.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You've always wanted me to tell you everything I know, haven't you?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You've always wanted to borrow the power of my shackles, right?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Then see for yourself.
You release your shackles, and <color=#fb9259>memories</color> unfurl before you.
[Sun Crow Apostle - Ten Scorching Suns] Memory Filter
Everywhere you look, the land is barren and bleached. Figures stand alone or in pairs on the split, desiccated ground, with nothing but sparse, withered grass pushing through the cracks beside them.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Harbinger rose, seen in east sky... All lives perished, with ten suns high...

speaker: Du Ruo
content: ...The real Sun Crow came fiercely and suddenly. There were no preordained omens from the myths, no poisonous trees, no floods or Wraith Spirits, only countless suns in the sky scorching the earth and terrorizing all living things.

speaker: Yanyan
content: ...When I was a child, the great drought brought by the Sun Crow dried up the fields, and its little monsters hurt people everywhere... I still remember how Grandma's house was set ablaze. It was terrifying...

speaker: Sealer
content: The calamity has escalated. Several allied states in Eastia have been victimized by the ten suns as well and had to abandon their cities due to the extreme heat. Something major seemed to have happened in DisCity too, cutting off trade completely. We can't import Hypercubes anymore, and our reserves are...
[End of Flashback]
The dark cyan void of chaos unfurls before you once more, devouring every color your memory holds. In the distance, the twisted monstrosity continues to swell.
Lichen wavers, and her knees slam into the ground. She throws out her hands to break the fall, sharp debris slicing her palms, but no sound escapes her.
To see so many calamities yet to unfold, all in a single instant, is more than any soul can endure. Yours included.
You drag in a deep breath and fight to steady your shaking voice.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What you just saw... that's what happens a hundred years from now. In your homeland. And in DisCity, where I come from.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That thing you created... it's a monster, just like the Sun Crow. In the future, we call them the <color=#fb9259>Apostles of Ashes</color>.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: They're born from the collective consciousness of humanity. The very "wishes" you've been gathering together. And all they do is consume everything in their path. No mind. No control. Completely impossible to use.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Again and again, they're the ones who bring the calamities. Your homeland was almost destroyed because of them. And even...
She keeps her head down and says nothing. Pushing her further would be dangerous now.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But look. The monster didn't destroy Eastia completely. Someone managed to hold it back. Your homeland is still there. It's just that—

speaker: Apostle of Ashes
content: <color=#dg1f1f><i>—!
The monster behind you stirs and begins to rise. Power surges up from beneath your feet, and sheer, primal terror grips your chest.
Perhaps because it has just been born, it lacks the overwhelming power of the Apostles of Ashes you have faced before. But even so, it is more than capable of crushing you both.

...No matter what, Lichen has to be taken out of the Void of Yin first. If she can be brought back to her senses and the balance between the Realm of Yang and the Void of Yin restored, the monster might remain trapped here. There's still a chance to escape Maria City.
You lift your hands to her face, and your fingertips meet the slick, sticky warmth of blood.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: There's still time.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You made me a promise, remember? You said you'd come back to me. I can still believe that, right?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: We're getting out of here. Together.
Each word grates past your throat, raw and parched. You can't tell anymore whether you're trying to persuade her, or yourself.
Slowly, she lifts her hand and closes it around your wrist with a gentle hold. At last, you feel a flicker of warmth.

speaker: Lichen
content: Mm. I saw it all.

speaker: Lichen
content: Monsters beyond imagining. Disasters with no end in sight. People crying out with everything they have, and still no answer from the gods... A hundred years, and nothing's changed.

speaker: Lichen
content: A hundred years, and it's already pushed the Eastern Continent back to savagery. Neighbor eating neighbor just to survive.
She sees it now, right? The path she clung to, creating a god to redeem the world, was only ever a mistake.
Then, she lets out a soft laugh.

speaker: Lichen
content: But I saw something else, too. No matter how many times those disasters descend upon us, there's nothing to be afraid of.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...What?

speaker: Lichen
content: Because people have faced them again and again—and defeated them, again and again.

speaker: Lichen
content: Isn't that what you showed me?
She pushes herself upright and lifts her gaze again to the Apostle looming above.

speaker: Lichen
content: You said it yourself. It's the same as the monster you showed me, isn't it?

speaker: Lichen
content: Then you were right. It has to be stopped, to be taken down...

speaker: Lichen
content: And that's the last good thing it'll ever do.

speaker: Lichen
content: I'm going to show the world that there really is a way to <color=#fb9259>vanquish evil</color>. And human hands are all it takes.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Vanquish... evil...

speaker: Shin?
content: <color=#dg1f1f><i>The origin of all, and the secrets of all...

speaker: Eastian Envoy
content: The Perishing Star falls, calamities descend... Our <color=#fb9259>ancestors</color> had long foretold the era of great disasters and recorded the true method to <color=#fb9259>subdue demons</color> in legends.

speaker: FAC Officer
content: ...It's a Sinner, one <color=#fb9259>fused</color> with the Apostle of Ashes.

speaker: Lichen
content: Years before the Nightfall, my shifu had already divined the <color=#fb9259>Perishing Star</color>'s arrival.

speaker: Woman's Voice
content: Just as I foresaw, the <color=#fb9259>baleful star</color> has fallen, erasing all in its wake and bringing ruin without end. You have witnessed it, all of it...

speaker: Woman's Voice
content: But do not lose your way... Come. Come to Maria City. Here, you shall find the path to <color=#fb9259>vanquishing evil</color>...

speaker: Woman's Voice
content: <color=#fb9259>You</color> will surely uncover it, and pass it down through the ages, shield those who are yet to come...
If the prophecy holds true, if the one who foretold the Perishing Star's fall was indeed Lichen's shifu...
Then who was it that first uncovered the path of the <color=#fb9259>seers</color>?
She has made a disaster she can't exploit, so she turns to opposing it, subduing it, and finally... merging with it. Does she need so badly to prove that mortals could stand against calamity?!
Everything you went through, was it prophecy fulfilled or myth being written?
Then should you never have stopped her?
The thought that flashes through your mind in that moment chills you to the core. Who is <color=#dg1f1f>tempting</color> you now? Who is <color=#dg1f1f>manipulating</color> you?
You fight to cast the idea aside, but your sight blurs further. Past and future unfold simultaneously before your eyes:
Blaze, blizzard, deluge, thunderclap, houses crumbling, crowds crying, pitiful pleas swallowed into oblivion. Blurred figures press toward the heart of the chaos, like one person, like many, like...
[Lichen's white silhouette]
Within the roiling chaos, Lichen's silhouette sharpens by degrees. For a dizzying instant, she looks just as she did when you first laid eyes on her.
[24 Transitions back to the original background + Lichen's corrupted no-mask character art]
You grab her sleeve and hold tight.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: A hundred years from now, people gave everything they had, and no one ever really controlled an Apostle of Ashes. You saw it! So how could you possibly—

speaker: Lichen
content: That was the path they had to walk, in their time.

speaker: Lichen
content: And now, this is my path to walk.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This was never your responsibility!
You look up. What did you think you would see? The eyes of a zealot, wild and unhinged?
Instead, her stare is perfectly calm, bright and lucid. Maybe it has always been this way.

speaker: Lichen
content: "Responsibility"? I never had anything like that.

speaker: Lichen
content: Seeking the Dao and all that, let's be honest, I was never really a Daoist. Raising the dead? That was always a lie.

speaker: Lichen
content: But there's one thing I never lied to you about.

speaker: Lichen
content: Fortune and misfortune, two sides of the same coin. The calamities brought ruin, but they also gave the Tianyi Sect its power. People burn incense for you, and you'd better earn it. I'm not one of those high and mighty "gods." That much conscience, at least, I still have.

speaker: Lichen
content: I don't want the world, or you, to spend your lives afraid of losing anything more.

speaker: Lichen
content: If you don't believe me, that's fine.
Her eyes move past your shoulder, and she offers a slight, quiet nod to someone behind you.

speaker: Lichen
content: You saw it too, didn't you?

speaker: Lichen
content: That people can stand against the calamities with their own two hands. It was never just some delusion of mine.
Then she lowers her head once more, looking into your eyes.

speaker: Lichen
content: Thank you.
She brushes your hand aside effortlessly and turns her back to you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Don't—
Two arms lock around your waist and wrench you backward.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Chengxiao?!
Chengxiao clamps his arms around you, his shredded clothes whipping up and momentarily veiling your eyes.
Has it finally reached him too? Is he so desperate to drag you away, back onto the "right" path? Instinct screams at you to fight free, and then...
You notice his gaze. It is locked forward, unblinking, fixed on that single point. He speaks only these words to you:

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Go.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Don't look back.
You turn your head anyway. Just like every hopeless, stubborn fool of a human would.
[Small CG]
The Apostle of Ashes rends a gash in the void above. And so, in this purgatory that transcends life, death, and time itself, a heaven and an earth are born.
She walks between them, step by step, into the black, churning tide of rubble and severed limbs.

speaker: Lichen
content: Apostle of Ashes... Mania... Is that what you call them in your time?

speaker: Lichen
content: They're a mouthful. Sounds exactly like something the little curly-haired one would come up with. I can barely make sense of them.

speaker: Lichen
content: Doesn't matter. Anything that won't let people live, I'll cut it down.
All around her, the wishes of the living and the dead resound in endless refrain: grant us peace, bring us together, give us shelter, let us rest.

She's heard it all before. She never believed the creature before her could understand anyway. That's the nature of gods, isn't it? They are forever beyond the reach of those mud-soaked hands stretching toward the sky.
What you finally grasp, in the end, is only those next to you.

speaker: Lichen
content: A hundred years isn't enough? Then give it another hundred. The universe is vast, time is long. That day will come.
Whatever comes, steel or flood, she will meet it in kind. If a god cannot be made, she'll simply try another road. Until the Dao she seeks is found, this body will not yield.
She pulls her feet free and advances again, allowing the grasping hands to flay her skin piece by piece into the mud.
Until at last, she lifts her gaze.
[Big CG]
The rift above splits wider, unveiling the sky behind it. Light spills through and illuminates the face of the being looking down upon her: gentle, merciful, the face of her shifu.

It was like the first clear day after a deluge brought by the Perishing Star, when the first beam of sky light split the dark clouds and struck the dry, spotless crown of the Celestial Master's statue. Months of relentless rain had never once dampened that stone.
Her shifu held her hand and guided her up the mountain to witness the miracle. Young Li Xianling only stared blankly at the statue. Its shadow swallowed her.
A god that never weeps, and a shifu like this: was there any difference at all?

speaker: Shifu?
content: <color=#dg1f1f><i>...You did it... You have done so well...

speaker: Shifu?
content: <color=#dg1f1f><i>...Just as I knew you would. You were always the bravest of them all...

speaker: Shifu?
content: <color=#dg1f1f><i>...I have heard your wish... Everything you have ever wanted is right here...

speaker: Shifu?
content: ...As long as you believe it... As long as... you believe it...
A fierce wind tears through, lifting the veil of copper coins. But a god has no form. In her eyes now, there is only the surging tide of humanity and the slow turn of ages.
The fate that person brings a hundred years from now, she only caught the briefest glimpse of it, not nearly enough to grasp its meaning.
Across that barren waste, fire sweeps the plains and frost cloaks the mountains, yet silhouettes rise into the sky one after another, gripping torches that are also swords, all aimed at the heavens.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: <i><color=#7683a2>What if you actually die this time?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: <i><color=#7683a2>What if all your resolve means nothing?

speaker: Chengxiao
content: <i><color=#7683a2>I fear this so-called means to vanquish evil... may prove to be yet another trap laid by the Perishing Star itself.</color>

speaker: Chengxiao
content: <i><color=#7683a2>...Are you really resolved on this?
Truth be told, Li Xianling still doesn't have the answers.
One thing, however, is clear.

speaker: Lichen
content: Well, that's a pity...

speaker: Lichen
content: I have never believed in gods.
The bell chimes one final time, piercing through the clamor and hurling a challenge at the divine, one that will resonate across a century.

And then, before your eyes, like every arrogant fool who has dared to face a god,

her body is pierced clean through by the god's merciful hands.
<color=#dg1f1f><size=40>And swallowed whole.

speaker: Vague Voice
content: <i><color=#7683a2>Among lonely graves... Yin and Yang in ceaseless churn...

speaker: Vague Voice
content: <i><color=#7683a2>Come, then go... no soul may stay...
The pale crowd chants in unison, rocking the sails, herding you step by step backward.

speaker: Vague Voice
content: <i><color=#7683a2>The living stop here... the dead take the river...

speaker: Vague Voice
content: <i><color=#7683a2>All earthly ties are severed... turn back... and find no shore...

Their features are lost to you. The voices alone remain, thick with a viscous, clinging sorrow, and it seems to dissolve the shapes of them. Their forms are dripping slowly, bleeding into the water below.
Clop. Clop. Clop.
A wooden knocking sounds from nowhere.
Clop. Clop. Clop.
Then...
[Lichen's white silhouette]
There she is, standing tall among the surging crowd. Her cyan sleeves catch the air with effortless grace, impossibly vivid amidst the wash of pale figures.
She turns to you and offers a soft, quiet smile.
Then, without hesitation, she walks straight ahead.
<color=#7683a2><i>Why? Why won't she stop? Why is she walking so fast?
<color=#7683a2><i>Why does it have to be this way?
But even these thoughts soon dissolve. Ash drifts down from all around, and the river quickens, forcing you backward once more.
[White flash transition back to the Surface World]

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Pant... pant...
You jolt upright, heart pounding, an urgent need to search driving you. Your gaze darts wildly, sweeping every corner for—
Lichen.
She lies nearby, her body left too long on the cold ground. When you touch her, she feels rigid and cold as timber.

You extend your trembling hand, the shaking beyond your will. Fear has seized your body before your heart can catch up. You hover your fingers near her cheek. There is no breath, no heat, no heartbeat. Only stillness.
You move your hand down to her waist.
Nothing comes through from the other end of the shackles.
[Vibration + sound effect]
Furious, you snatch at her robes and yank her body upright from the ground.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Get up... Get up!
Her body sags against your chest, a dead weight. You keep shaking her shoulders with almost violent force, your fingers sinking deep into her cold skin.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Get up!!!

You knew she was mad! What made you think words would work? What were you waiting for? You should have hauled her back, no matter if she saw you as an enemy or a hindrance from then on. You knew damn well she was mad!
[2s transition + fabric rustling]
Her arm slides off you, her hand dropping lifelessly into the mud.
You knew it all along.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Lichen.

You catch her limp arm and try to drape it back into place, but your small shoulder won't hold it, and it slips down again. You try once more, then again, until her fingers are coated in fresh mud that hides the dried blood.
