Impossible. There must be something you haven't checked, some pulse still flickering, no matter how faint. There must be something.
You bury your face against her chest. The fabric, stiff with dried blood, scrapes your cheek, and the only sound reaching your ears is the drumming of your own heart.
The cold, metallic reek of her blood fills your senses, nearly making you retch. You pull her closer. Her chest grows warm and damp where you press against her. So why can't you hear anything at all?
Across Maria City, the cyan fissures pulse, then close. Under the grey sky, the bare concrete buildings stand silent, as if nothing ever happened.
(Transition 2s)
A hand settles lightly on your shoulder, and the warmth of that touch slowly brings you back.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: You're back?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Chengxiao...?
In a daze, you grasp his hand, and your palm recognizes the familiar slick, icy sensation at once.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You... went into the Void of Yin in this body?

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Not to that extreme, no.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Still, a journey like this exacts its toll, one way or another.
He pulls his hand back as though it were nothing, and tugs his sleeve down to hide the mark blooming dark across his wrist.
And you can do nothing. Just as before.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Your divination was right. Every last bit of it was right.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I thought I could talk her down and stop her. But I couldn't. Every time I tried, I just pushed her further.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The fact that I'm here at all already proves the ending was set. It was only ever a question of when.
A torrent of words spills from your chest, carrying a conviction so firm it feels alien on your own tongue.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So it was all inevitable, wasn't it?
Chengxiao looks at you for a long while. He doesn't nod. Only a soft sigh escapes through his nose.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Perhaps it was.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Though after all of this, I find myself wondering... most people who seek out divination are really just looking for someone to tell them they made the right choice. And fate, perhaps, is simply the place people arrive at after walking the road they had already chosen for themselves.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: People, even when they know better, can't bring themselves to betray their own hearts.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Venturing into the Void of Yin, pursuing its secrets, standing against the calamities... she had made up her mind about all of it long before we ever set foot in Maria City. Even if it meant surrendering herself to evil, it was, as she put it, no terribly ill omen.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Had she done anything less, she would not have been the person I know.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: The same applies to me. Willing or not, here I am all the same. Is that not proof enough?

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Whether you were present or not, we would have ended up standing before that so-called "god" regardless. The outcome has nothing to do with you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Nothing to do with me...
He gives a single nod, draws himself upright, and turns his gaze toward the far horizon.
Maria City lies quiet now, so still it feels strange. Only a faint tremor hums beneath your feet. With the Apostle sealed inside the Void of Yin, this is nearly the end of all things.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I still can't leave.
The faint light catches Chengxiao's glasses, flashing and hiding whatever lies behind his eyes.
<i>Are you still not turning back, even at this point?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Truth is, there's a lot I still want to ask her, to ask both of you. Even if that chance is gone now.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're both Daoists, aren't you? And pretty good at reading fate. You must have seen your own endings long before I ever showed up.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So why did you still set out? Why...
<i>Why did it have to be this way?
(Flashback)

speaker: Lichen
content: That was the path they had to walk, in their time.

speaker: Lichen
content: And now, this is my path to walk.
[End of Flashback]
At last, you understand her.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Because...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If you weren't here right now... or I guess, for me, if you had never <color=#fb9259>been</color> here... my world wouldn't exist. I wouldn't be here at all.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What would that world even look like? I don't know.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So even knowing how it ends...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No. Precisely because I know how it ends for you all, I want to see it through with you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This has everything to do with me.
Even if this is all but a dream.
You breathe in deep, raise your chin, settle your shoulders back, and look straight at him.

speaker: Mechanical Sound
content: And if you two really are the ones who left behind a way to suppress the Apostle for Eastia...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Even with Lichen gone, merged into the Apostle... that'll only hold it for so long. It's going to break loose eventually, and when it does, your expedition is in for a whole lot worse.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I don't know if we can actually do this...
No Almighty Bow. No power drawn from the mass. Only a single person who has made peace with her own ruin, suspended somewhere between life and death.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But we have to take that monster, and whatever's inside it—
Your mouth opens, and the sound that slips out is almost a sigh. You grit your teeth and manage to push the words through.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: We put it down for good.
Chengxiao doesn't move. The wind slips through the space between you, catching the edge of his sleeve and lifting it for just a moment.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: ...No matter how I read the hexagrams, it seems I truly cannot divine what lies beyond the boundary of my own fate.
Chengxiao breaks into an unexpected laugh.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Thank you. Now I can set out with an easy mind.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Ah, and when you see Li Xianling, do be careful not to mention you assumed she was dead. She would make quite the scene afterward.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You... believe Lichen is still alive?

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Believe? It would be more accurate to say I do not.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Li Xianling has had a gift for finding loopholes ever since we were children.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Once, she was caught mocking the Celestial Master's statue. She turned right around and, in that pompous old classical style, declared she was simply offended that anyone would dare imprison the great Celestial Master in the mortal realm with something as earthly as stone.
A brief laugh escapes him, then his hand snaps shut, the mud still clinging to his fingers leaving dark, wet marks pressed into his palm.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: So, I do not believe she would allow herself to be killed by the very thing she holds in the greatest contempt.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Look.
You lift your gaze and realize the fissures in the sky never truly sealed. They've been pulled taut into a single seam, its light quivering as if someone is wrestling to keep it closed.
The sound of pattering footsteps draws closer.

speaker: Keylan
content: Data checks out. The anomalous fluctuations in the Reflection Plane are being suppressed. How long that'll hold, though...

speaker: Chengxiao
content: It will suffice. The creature will not emerge again until we find it.
Chengxiao lowers himself into a crouch. He takes out a paper talisman and a short blade, then draws the edge across his fingertip. Blood beads and falls, winding into a formation on the ground.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: This formation will send me into the Void of Yin, to where my soul is. It will take some time. You may have to wait a while for me.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So entering the Void of Yin takes a ritual this complicated...

speaker: Chengxiao
content: One could force one's way in, I suppose. But I cannot bring myself to adopt her methods. Proper preparation is always preferable.
[CG]

speaker: Chengxiao
content: You see? People truly do not change.
In the dim light, he looks at you with a knowing smile, waiting. But as ever, he already knows what you will say.
He reaches out his hand toward you.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Are you ready?
You lower your gaze to your open palm. Beneath the skin, your veins throb with a quiet, rhythmic pulse.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm ready.
[Chromatic Passage]
Once again, you return to the Void of Yin, and the dark passage is still the first thing to meet you. It lies in total silence, only a cold wind rushing up from its depths.
Fear no longer holds you.
You extend your hand and let the shackles be your only guiding light.
[Surface World - Anomaly]

The ritual is complete. Now he only needs to step into the formation and fuse with the half of his soul still trapped within the Void of Yin. To set foot in the underworld through the arts of righteousness: it is the most perilous of all forbidden practices recorded in the Daoist texts. Even Li Xianling has no knowledge of it.
Perhaps, the instant his soul is made whole, he will grasp a sliver of survival. Or perhaps he will stay in the Void of Yin forever, neither alive nor dead.
<i>Should he cast one more divination?
He rummages inside his robes, but the three copper coins he uses for divination are gone. Some wandering phantom must have swiped them during the chaos.
No matter. There have already been more than enough surprises along the way, and his final fate won't be altered by this. And yet, amidst all of that...

speaker: Lichen
content: You saw it too, didn't you?

speaker: Lichen
content: That people can stand against the calamities with their own two hands. It was never just some delusion of mine.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Heh.
Golden light ripples to life beneath his feet.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Keep monitoring the camp's signal. If you get a response, don't wait for us.
He opens his mouth, but no sound escapes. His feet are leaden, rooted to the spot.
Sensing it, Chengxiao offers an apologetic smile and taps Keylan lightly on the shoulder.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Don't worry. We'll catch up soon enough. We'll all make it home together.

speaker: Keylan
content: ...I understand. I believe in you.
Chengxiao only smiles and offers no reply.
A moment later, something seems to occur to him. He retrieves his terminal and passes it to Keylan.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Ah. One more thing before I go.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Tell those who still come seeking answers from the heavens to stop putting their faith in gods and immortals. The great Celestial Master of the Tianyi Sect died long ago on the path to saving this world. And never once looked back.
No sooner does the terminal land in Keylan's grip than it vibrates violently, almost tumbling to the ground.
When he lifts his head again, Chengxiao's silhouette is already fading, consumed by the fissure.
[Altar Lower Half - Damaged]
The immense form stands at the chamber's heart, quivering almost imperceptibly. The copper coins tremble in response, countless as eyes that blink and stare.
A voice, soft and unhurried, floats through the air, fading to a whisper by the time it finds you.

speaker: Shifu?
content: <color=#dg1f1f><i>You've come...

speaker: Shifu?
content: <color=#dg1f1f><i>You...
It suddenly thrashes as if grappling with an invisible force, its limbs twisting and seizing midair, barely able to hold its human semblance.
Beneath you, the black sludge swells and bubbles. Those limbs rise sluggishly from the depths, their fingers locking around your ankles, dragging you back.
With each step forward, those fingers burrow into your flesh, peeling away strips of skin. Viscous fluid rushes into the wounds. So this is what she suffered, like being scorched from the inside.
You clench your jaw.
[Red Flash]

speaker: Lichen
content: But I saw something else, too. No matter how many times those disasters descend upon us, there's nothing to be afraid of.
[Red Flash]

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Nngh!

speaker: Lichen
content: Because people have faced them again and again—and defeated them, again and again.
[Red Flash]
<i>Faster... you must... keep going forward...

speaker: Shifu?
content: <color=#dg1f1f><i>Persist in your folly...

speaker: Shifu?
content: <color=#dg1f1f><i><b>...and the price will be steep...!
A tide of black, viscous tentacles erupts from beneath its robes, reeking of decay. They lash against your arms and legs and wind tight around you.
A blade flashes before your eyes. The dark hands grasping you are severed in a single sweep, black mist bleeding from the stumps.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Wrong target.
Chengxiao moves before you, his body a shield. He raises his sword, the blade still stained with blood from the ritual, now running in slow rivulets down the steel.
The golden light reaches the Apostle and instantly becomes rope, winding around it in tightening coils.
The monster convulses. Something rips through it from the inside, and white light erupts as a gaping hollow tears open in its body, black mist roiling at the torn edges.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Go now.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: There are people waiting for us.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Right.
A howling gale blasts outward from the hollow. You push into the light and rush headlong toward the Apostle's core.
[Rumble + White Flash]
Chengxiao stands alone before the thing wearing his shifu's voice and face.

speaker: Shifu?
content: <color=#dg1f1f><i>Why... do you point your blade at me...

speaker: Shifu?
content: <color=#dg1f1f><i>Do you still mean to... defy the will of Heaven...?

speaker: Shifu?
content: <color=#dg1f1f><i>...You were always the most sensible one... the one who knew his place...
No answer came. Her footsteps gradually faded into the distance.

speaker: Lichen
content: Anyway, I've saved you a ticket and a spot on the expedition. Whether you show up or not, that's on you.
He turned the copper coin between his fingers, its surface burnished by years of handling.
She almost reached the front door, then hesitated mid-step, turned on her heel, and made her way toward the back.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Taking the back trail down, are we?

speaker: Lichen
content: Beats those front stairs. You keep them so polished they might as well be waxed. I almost took a tumble on my way up.

speaker: Lichen
content: Besides, turns out there's actually a new trail through the back hills now.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: We have taken in more children of late. I imagine they've worn it into the hill with all their running about. No one can keep them in hand. Each one harder to catch than the last.
Li Xianling burst out laughing and pushed the door open. Sunlight flooded through the gap, throwing her silhouette across the floorboards.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: We will meet again there.
Behind him came the rustle of fabric. He imagined Li Xianling giving him a casual wave—her version of a goodbye.

Her footsteps trailed off toward the back hill. When they were young, the adults had forbidden the children from taking that shortcut, insisting it was too dangerous, prowling with wolves and bandits. Li Xianling, of course, had never listened and had spent years goading him into breaking the rule with her.
In hindsight, it makes no difference. Front hill or back, both paths eventually led down to the clamor of the town streets.
Just like this moment right now.
Chengxiao runs his fingers slowly along the flat of the blade. His own face stares back from the steel, and for a fleeting second, it looks almost unfamiliar.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: What is taken must be repaid, and what is sought comes at a cost. Without rules, nothing holds its shape. Everything the sect taught me, I remember every word.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: But if that is so, then those who keep to the path are owed a good end, and those who stray will reap what they have sown. Every fate is already settled in your eyes.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: If the best outcome is always assured, no matter what, then why send those voices to guide us along the way at all?

speaker: Chengxiao
content: ...Perhaps because even you cannot control it. The ending may be fixed, but what we learn along the road, and how we choose to walk it... those remain beyond your reach.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: And that matters to you, doesn't it?

speaker: Shifu?
content: <color=#dg1f1f><i>The human... heart...

speaker: Shifu?
content: <color=#dg1f1f><i>The human heart... is fickle above all... never to be...

speaker: Shifu?
content: <color=#dg1f1f><i>...trusted...
[Screen shake + flash]
The void inside the Apostle's form gapes ever wider. Its voice fractures into broken shards, until at last it can no longer weave those gentle, tempting words.

speaker: Discordant Whispers
content: <color=#dg1f1f><i><b>Foolish... arrogant... self-righteous mortals...

speaker: Discordant Whispers
content: <color=#dg1f1f><i><b>Destined... destined for ruin...!

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Heh. Indeed...
[24 Transition to white screen + Lichen's corrupted, no-mask dark silhouette]
Her blurred silhouette stands at the center of the creature, hemmed in by twisting, thrashing limbs that still carry the faint suggestion of human forms.
Draped across her is the heart of everything: a shapeless monster that drains the sorrow and desperate prayers of humanity to keep itself from unraveling.
At your presence, the limbs rage anew. Screams pour into your ears, and the black mist rises to blind you.
[Empty scene 2s + black corruption]
[White flash + bell SFX, then transition into awakening CG]
Her bound hands can no longer raise the bell high, but the chime continues. Every time the black mist swells and threatens to bury the road ahead of you, the bell scatters it. Again and again.
And through the clearing haze, you can see it plainly now: how those limbs pierce straight through her chest, clawing frantically for something, hope, perhaps, or the price for it.
Yet from a human body, only flesh and blood can ever be taken. And what use is any of that, if the person simply refuses to fall?
You move toward her step by step, just as she once advanced here step by step. Stubborn and unyielding. Never stopping.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: ...Such is the human heart. You can calculate every outcome down to the last detail, and still they will hope, at the final moment, for fate to bend just a little. Even if what comes next is more than they can bear.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: You have fed on their offerings, their prayers, their fears, their hopes. You, who have nourished yourself on the hearts of mankind, must now bear the price of them.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Those are the rules you yourself set down.
He lifts his sword and levels it at the creature once more. Black tentacles whip around the blade and drag him forward with savage strength.
His sword arm holds fast, unmoving. The only sound is the crack of bones giving way.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: When all is said and done... I am only human...
He wrenches the blade around with a violent twist and slashes straight for the monster's face.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Obstinate to the end. You have brought this on yourself.
[White Flash + Sword Strike SFX]
[24 Transition to Chief Mini CG]
The shackles inside you shiver with a subtle hum. At your back, a blade catches the light; through your chest, the bell's chime resounds. And in that instant, a lightness floods through you.
So you break into a run.

speaker: Shifu
content: Li Xianling. Trespassing on the sect's forbidden grounds not once, not twice, but repeatedly. And speaking irreverently of the immortals. And Lyu Buzhou, you knew of this, said nothing, and even mapped out her route for her...

speaker: Shifu
content: Every complaint the sect has about the two of you all lands on my desk...

speaker: Li Xianling
content: Oh, come on, Shifu! Think about it. If I actually found the immortal, that'd be a huge win for the sect, right? Total honor and glory. Shouldn't that cancel out a few little rule bends? Rules were made for people, not the other way around!

speaker: Lyu Buzhou
content: Shifu, the classical texts do state that rules ought to adapt to the shifting demands of the times and the needs of the people.

speaker: Lyu Buzhou
content: ...After all, immortals, humans, and beasts are fundamentally different by nature. Surely it stands to reason that one cannot measure them all by the same yardstick.

speaker: Li Xianling
content: Wait, Lyu Buzhou! You think I didn't catch that? You better believe when I finally meet an immortal, I am not telling you a single thing about what they look like!

speaker: Shifu
content: Enough, enough, both of you! ...Fine. I will go and make your apologies myself.

speaker: Shifu
content: Truly, I never needed either of you to bring glory to this sect.

speaker: Shifu
content: If the world could settle into something a little more peaceful, and you two could remain just as you are right now... that would be more than enough for me.
Perhaps, to some greater being, humanity is nothing but frantic ants, blind to all but the road ahead, never realizing that their every step leads only to ruin.
Yet what makes them human is this: when a crossroads rises before them, they choose the manner of their own destruction.
With prudence or obstinance.
With hubris or valor.
With faith or doubt.

speaker: Ziwei App
content: Transmitting data... Warning. Warning: large-scale emotional fluctuation detected among users. Warning. Warning—

<i>　　　I do believe...　　　　　 <size=38>I want to believe...</size>　　　　<size=50> Please, heavenly immortals, bless us...</size>
　　　<i><size=52>No... I can't believe it...</color></size> <size=50>This is... Clearly, this is...</size>
　　　　　　　　<i>But even in this form... <size=38>you must still be merciful,</size> <size=52>right...?</color></size>

　　　　　　<size=38><i>If the immortals are indeed real...</size> then why have they never listened...? 　　　Please, bless us...
<size=52><i>Then why do they make us suffer...?!</size>
　　　 　　　<i><size=52>I can only... I can only believe...</color></size>
<i><b><size=50>I can only believe in myself now...!
The black mist shrieks and scatters. The shapeless mass crumbles again, writhing desperately as it tries to pull itself together.
Nothing blocks your path now, not ahead, not behind.
<i>Is now the time to say sorry?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: In a hundred years, the calamities, the Mania... we haven't beaten any of it. Just failure after failure. Losing people, over and over. You, and them...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But... I still want you to see.

speaker: Lichen
content: Then let me borrow your eyes a moment. Let me see that even fate itself can't bring the mortal world to ruin.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It's all because you were here. I'll remember that you were here.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Fate has laid its course plain before us... I ask only that it hesitates, if only for a moment, on my account.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Even if that's the only reason I'm standing here right now.
There is only one thing left to do.

You look into her eyes, truly look into them for the first time. Not at a lying Daoist who spoke nothing but deceit, not at a pitiful madwoman poisoned by the abyss, not at a lost soul wandering and waiting to be rescued.
You look at Li Xianling and reach out your hand.
[Hand-Holding CG]
She seizes your wrist and clings to it, dragging it toward her chest with all her remaining strength. The ribbons wound around her arms cut deeper into the flesh that still marks her as human.

speaker: Lichen
content: Fear not.
Then, between your pulse and hers, thorns of bright crimson blossom into being.
[Full CG Awakening - Split]
The shackles drive through her chest, splintering her earrings and blasting apart the dark mist massed at her back.
She hears her heart tear open once more, cleft in two, pulsing against the shackles.
But nothing could be better than this. Because this body will never be hollow.
[White Out]

speaker: Faint Voice
content: <i><color=#7683a2>Gods? Immortals? Come on. You really think there's any of that out there?

speaker: Faint Voice
content: <i><color=#7683a2>You ever see a god pick up a shovel? Put food on your plate?

speaker: Faint Voice
content: <i><color=#7683a2>Hey, don't say that. Better to believe in something than nothing at all...

speaker: Faint Voice
content: <i><color=#7683a2>You know what they say. Human will can conquer heaven itself. I still remember the year that the rogue god went on a rampage. Not a single blade of grass left standing. Lives lost beyond counting. But heroes rose up, stood their ground, and struck that wicked god down atop the clouds.

speaker: Faint Voice
content: <i><color=#7683a2>The heroes may be long gone now, but if you're as brave as they were—not afraid of the dark, not afraid of thunder, not afraid of the things that bare their claws in your dreams—then they'll watch over you too. Right there in those same dreams. ...Hey, what'd you kick me for?

speaker: Faint Voice
content: <i><color=#7683a2>...What do you mean I'm feeding the kids lies? It's been thundering every night for a week. I told them a little story, and now they sleep through it without crying. Tell me what's so wrong about that.

speaker: Faint Voice
content: <i><color=#7683a2>Oh, enough with all this talk. Let's just focus on getting by...

speaker: Faint Voice
content: <i><color=#7683a2>Gods, heroes, whatever you put your faith in, doesn't really matter, does it? At the end of the day, everyone's just looking for a little peace of mind.
This is where a myth ends. And where another begins.
You lie on the ground and let the voices drift softly into your ears. Are they from a century ago, or from a time much closer to your own? You cannot tell.
In this moment, you do nothing but listen.
Hymns of praise, rising year after year.
[Surface World - Safe Zone]
At last, the quiet, unchanging sky of Maria City appears before your eyes.
A hand extends toward you.
Chengxiao pulls you up from the ground and, with a smile, dusts off your shoulders.
The wind threads through the ruins, and time begins to move again. Only the body lying still nearby remains unmoved.
The breeze sweeps over the wreckage, torn apart and stitched back together, and your gaze crosses the broken ground to settle on her.
Is it because you've only just come back? Your vision blurs. You cannot see her face, only the hem of her robe stirring gently in the wind.
Behind you, a voice tinged with warmth reaches your ears.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Go on.
You walk toward her, dragging your steps on purpose.
When she found you that first time, weren't you lying just like this in the mud, perfectly still? What had she done then? Shaken a bell and chanted some nonsense incantation, hadn't she?
You crouch down. The bell rests between you, its clapper choked with mud, silent. You gently brush it aside.
No response.
You clasp her cold wrist and pull her arm across your shoulder, hoisting her onto your back. She weighs less than you imagined, even for a child's frame.
You lift your head. The man before you is still watching with that same soft smile. Did he see this ending coming too? And even knowing it, can he still face it with something like peace?
The answer doesn't matter anymore. Slowly, you walk toward him.
[Transition 2s]
...Heh.

speaker: Lichen
content: Am I heavy?
Your heart trembles. You bite down on your lip and force your spine straighter.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Not at all.
The words have barely left you when the weight on your shoulders vanishes. A rustle of fabric sounds beside you, soft and stirring, so achingly familiar that your tears almost drop.

She bends down, bringing her eyes level with yours, and studies you with earnest care. Then she reaches out and wipes your cheek, but the blood on her fingertips only smears across your skin. She offers you a sheepish smile.

speaker: Lichen
content: Well. After all that, I still needed you to carry me back. That's just embarrassing.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: One might hope a certain someone would take a lesson from this.

speaker: Lichen
content: A lesson? Honestly, it could've gone a lot worse. You know me. I bounce back.
She stands, wobbling for a moment before steadying herself.
Her hand lifts, fingers reaching for the spot just below her ear, but there is nothing left to find. Only tiny specks of dust float between her fingers in the light.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Well? The sacred relic of the Tianyi Sect's did the trick, didn't it? A good thing I insisted you bring it along.

speaker: Lichen
content: What's with that tone? I didn't know you were so proud of the old sect.

speaker: Lichen
content: Have to say though, I didn't expect it to be that useful. Hmm... think I could order them in bulk?

speaker: Chengxiao
content: And do what, exactly? Stock up enough to storm the Void of Yin a hundred more times and fling the gates of the underworld wide open?

speaker: Lichen
content: Don't tempt me. I might just try it.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Utterly hopeless.
Chengxiao shakes his head, his voice tinged with resignation.
Yet something in the unseen world compels you to turn around. Even as you walk step by step toward the light, those whispers have already rooted themselves deep within your mind.
<color=#dg1f1f><i>Turn back... look back...
<color=#dg1f1f><i>Everything you treasure... everything you love... it's all here...
Two dark silhouettes flicker behind you.
No human could resist such a call. But...
[Tremor]
Lichen staggers, and you immediately brace her with your shoulder. She hesitates for just a moment, then wraps her arms around you in turn.
[CG]

speaker: Lichen
content: Well, look at that. Turns out I still need you to keep me upright after all.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: You seem to be recovering remarkably fast. Right back to your old self, I see.

speaker: Lichen
content: What can I say? This one's my auspicious star.
She grins brazenly, still leaning into you, though the burden on your shoulder has lightened just a bit.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Go back and recover your strength first. After that, you owe the expedition team an apology. And you'll need to send a message back to the sect explaining the situation. You've stirred up quite a commotion across the Eastern Continent. They will have certainly sensed something amiss by now.

speaker: Lichen
content: Just a message? What about telling them what we actually found? A chance to clear our names for once.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Clear our names? You mean tell them that after the Man-Fiend incident, two disciples of the Tianyi Sect, Lichen and Chengxiao, very nearly succumbed to corruption, and only narrowly escaped with their lives thanks to the aid of some mysterious stranger from the West...

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Surely you don't actually believe you've succeeded.

speaker: Lichen
content: You really know how to kill a good mood, you know that?

speaker: Lichen
content: Hey, speaking of which, where's the little curly-haired one?
A familiar figure bounds up in the distance, rushing a few steps your way before skidding to an abrupt halt. That messy head of curls whirls around in a circle, directionless.

speaker: Lichen
content: What's he doing all the way over there?

speaker: Chengxiao
content: I told him to go on ahead. It seems he's been waiting for us all the same. Though I suspect he's keeping his distance for fear we might be phantoms.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: This works out rather well. We can each go with a partner.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: And don't think you can change the subject. You will sit down and write that letter to the sect, properly. I will not have you sending the elders into apoplexy again.

speaker: Lichen
content: We'll see.
The words stop short. A hand comes to rest lightly on the crown of your head.

speaker: Lichen
content: We've been going on about things you couldn't follow again, haven't we?
You blink, realizing you had drifted off entirely. You didn't hear a word.
You were too absorbed in the weight resting against your shoulder, the gentle heat of aging sunlight, and the sound of their voices, still warm and bright, before time could wear them thin.

speaker: Chengxiao
content: Let us head back. When you return, get some proper rest, won't you?
Lichen clears her throat, presses her fingers together, and speaks in a slow, lilting cadence:

speaker: Lichen
content: The hour is most auspicious. Allow me to cast one last divination for you. Let me see... our little auspicious star...

speaker: Lichen
content: Tonight, your dreams will be nothing but sweet.
So let the story pause here for now.
Now, grip the hand in yours and move forward. Don't look back. The whispers and phantoms behind you have lost their power to harm.
If all of this was really fated, then we will meet again at the end.
[Black Screen 2s]
[Chief's Lounge]

Following the conclusion of the latest Illusory Moon tide, ${PlayerName}, Chief of the MBCC, regained consciousness after the nightmare's grip released. The Bureau immediately conducted a full medical evaluation. The findings confirmed that the Chief's physical and mental faculties showed no irregularities.

The precise cause of the anomalous fluctuations observed during this Illusory Moon cycle remains unresolved. Nevertheless, the Chief managed to retrieve a considerable amount of highly valuable research data during the mission. These documents have now been transferred to the research department, and a thorough analysis has commenced.
[DisCity Central Library]
After the incident concluded, the Chief filed a formal request to review historical records pertaining to the expedition, archived at the DisCity Central Library.
[Verifying clearance level] Access granted
[CG]

<color=#fb9259>Lichen</color>, birth name Li Xianling, was formerly a Daoist priestess of the Eastern Continent. In the years after the Perishing Star fell, she journeyed across the Eastern Continent, gathering folklore and documenting anomalous phenomena associated with it. Her work focused on investigating the potential connection between human spiritual activity and the Perishing Star.

In ▉▉, she volunteered for the expedition and subsequently served as an advisor representing the Eastern Continent, offering specialized support to related operations.

She went missing in ▉▉ during Operation ▉▉. When exhaustive search efforts failed to locate her, she was officially declared <color=#fb9259>deceased</color>.
[CG]

<color=#fb9259>Chengxiao</color>, birth name Lyu Buzhou, was a researcher of mysticism at the Eastern Continent University. His academic career centered on religion, belief systems, and the human psyche. After the Perishing Star fell, he turned his focus to the spiritual and psychological anomalies emerging across various regions in the disaster's aftermath.

He joined the expedition in ▉▉, thereafter contributing his expertise as a mysticism researcher of the Eastern Continent.

He went missing in ▉▉ during Operation ▉▉. When exhaustive search efforts failed to locate him, he was officially declared <color=#fb9259>deceased</color>.
[Daoist Temple]

[Records on the Tianyi Sect, compiled by Eastian scholars]

Eastian scholars report that the <color=#fb9259>Tianyi Sect</color> ceased to exist many years ago. Its esoteric arts are nonetheless widely acknowledged as the foundation of <color=#fb9259>the seer legend</color>, though later seized and restricted by the seers who followed. The <color=#fb9259>seer</color> practices now current in Eastia are largely imitations and adaptations derived from the Tianyi Sect's original methods.

The original creator of these arts vanished long ago, with some accounts claiming they fled Eastia in fear of the disaster and were never seen again.

After several calamities, related records were further scattered across Eastia, making complete recovery nearly impossible.

Following investigation and review, only a handful of annotated fragments have been recovered. Though these surviving pages contain references tied to <color=#fb9259>the seer legend</color>, the lack of definitive dates, authorship, and complete context precludes any verification of their authenticity at present. Consequently, they do not qualify for formal archival inclusion.

Nevertheless, considering that these fragments were discovered by chance among a batch of old books slated for mass incineration, and that they still possess a degree of preservation value, transferring them to DisCity for safekeeping within the Bureau's database may be the more prudent approach.

[On the Calamities of Primordial Chaos, Volume IV]

...Practical observation confirms that so-called calamities are Wraith Beasts coalesced from human consciousness, and that they disintegrate when that same consciousness crumbles. If this principle can be harnessed to exert reverse control over the force of <color=#fb9259>collective will</color> to its maximum extent, it may be possible for human beings, in their mortal bodies, to oppose calamity itself.

...To accomplish this, three elements are essential: the people, the ritual, and the vessel.

Neatly written annotation: The sect has already run small-scale trials, though the method appears quite limited at this stage. Firstly, crafting the vessels requires specific materials. While those they used bear a broadly similar structural makeup to the artifacts we uncovered in the Void of Yin, their efficacy is far inferior. What accounts for this disparity requires further study. Another challenge is finding someone capable of presiding over the rituals and subduing the Wraith Beasts. As I noted before, formally conferring a title upon such individuals is equally essential. I sent you several name proposals earlier. You read them and never replied. Hastily scrawled annotation: All that beating around the bush just to say we need to go back into Maria City for another look? I'll join the next expedition. As for the names... the ones you came up with are all so uninspired. "Priest" sounds like something out of the West, and "Ritual Officer" lacks any sense of mystery. ...What if we called them seers?
[Sun Crow CG]

In N.F. 106, a devastating drought fell upon Eastia. The following year, the Apostle of Ashes known as <color=#fb9259>Sun Crow</color> manifested. The seer <color=#fb9259>Xu</color> gave herself to the Apostle, merging with it entirely and succeeding in containing its rampage.
[Sun Crow Background]

In N.F. 112, the Tide of Ashes struck Eastia, destroying several city-states and submerging large areas of land. The next year, the Apostle of Ashes <color=#fb9259>Sun Crow</color> broke its seal, and by N.F. 114 it reached DisCity, trying to enter the DisSea. At the same time, Eastia sent a delegation to DisCity seeking cooperation.

In the end, with help from Eastian Sinners <color=#fb9259>Yao</color>, <color=#fb9259>Du Ruo</color>, <color=#fb9259>Yanyan</color>, and all of FAC, ${PlayerName}, Chief of the Minos Bureau of Crisis Control, successfully eliminated the Sun Crow Apostle.

The operation also gathered more critical data on the Apostles of Ashes for DisCity and established friendly relations with Eastia. The data will be used in future operations against the Apostles of Ashes.
[Bureau]
In N.F. ▉▉▉, two S-Class Sinners advanced upon the DisSea perimeter. The Bureau acted immediately, establishing preliminary containment of both targets and securing their successful detention.
The profiles of the two Sinners are as follows:
[CG]

Sinner <color=#fb9259>Lichen</color>, ID S-396. Corruption level: high. Psychological condition: relatively stable. It should be noted, however, that the subject's soul and physical body are not synchronized on the same frequency. If not for the subject's ongoing self-suppression achieved by burning her own soul, her physical body would constitute a major threat.
[CG]

Sinner <color=#fb9259>Chengxiao</color>, ID S-159. Corruption level: high. Psychological condition: relatively stable. It should be noted, however, that the subject's soul and physical body are not synchronized on the same frequency. If not for the subject's continuous self-binding through ritual sorcery, his physical body would constitute a major threat.
[Chief's Office]

Since their admission into custody, neither Sinner has caused any harm, whether within the Bureau or beyond it. Their anomalous conditions have remained largely within controllable parameters.

Given that both Sinners are classified at the extreme threat level, the Bureau will maintain ongoing observation and documentation of their respective states.

[MBCC Daily Report]

No unusual activity reported today.
All is well.
[Black Screen]

<size=62><b>The End
City Beyond Tribulation</color>
[Transition 3s]
[Chief's Lounge]
You slide the two thin files into an archival envelope, seal it shut, and ready it for return to the Central Library today, where it will be locked away once more.
The little black triangle peeks cautiously around the doorframe, observing you for a while before drifting slowly to your desk and giving a fawning little wag.

speaker: Schorl
content: The Illusory Moon's cycle shifted without any warning this time. You had to face two S-Class Sinners all on your own, and you didn't just walk away in one piece. You brought back a goldmine of intel. I shouldn't be surprised, Chief. But I still am.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No, not just two. There was someone else. We had to pair up to get out, so there should've been four of us. He was...
[Keylan's character art fades to black]
But his features and the sound of his voice are already starting to blur.
...Don't worry if it⬛⬛⬛... ⬛ big team... ⬛remember⬛important⬛.. Don't ⬛⬛...doesn't ring a bell.

speaker: Schorl
content: He was...?
It darts up to your face in an instant, activates recording mode, and begins bobbing eagerly, brimming with anticipation.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Sorry. I can't remember.
The little black triangle droops with a soft beep, but it seems to console itself quickly enough, twirling around on the spot.

speaker: Schorl
content: You've clearly overclocked yourself. Go get some proper rest. The full report can wait until you're awake.

speaker: Schorl
content: A brain like yours doesn't just lose things. I'm sure the important bits are all in there.
But in the end, you let it down.
Try as you might, the face and name of the third person you met in that dream never come back to you.

30 Days
Until the Trial
The door slams shut behind you. You sit in front of the notorious Eastside murderer.
Demon raised his head and looked at you for a second.
The faint aroma of blood lingered in the air. Perhaps his wounds had not completely healed from the recent surgery.
Demon Schilder, I have some things to ask you.
Demon raised his head again, as if sizing up prey with his eyes.

Not long ago, this man had been on the run. It took a sixty-hour chase to catch him, and after he was caught, the Bureau removed more than 300g of shrapnel from his body. Moreover, he was given a lethal dose of sedatives just four hours ago.
Even so, he still exuded a terrifying presence. You could feel that Demon was someone who could seriously hurt you.
I'm not your enemy.
There are some things I need to know. It is my responsibility to protect the Bureau's Sinners, including yourself.

speaker: Demon
content: ...You want me to thank you?
There was no hint of gratitude in his voice.
Think about your situation, Demon.
A lot of people want to kill you. Only the Bureau can protect you. You better cooperate.

speaker: Demon
content: Let them try.
Demon didn't even bother to lift his head in the face of these threats.
You knew Demon would be uncooperative. Someone warned you a few hours ago.

speaker: Comissioner
content: These are all the files on Demon Schilder.
Documents piled high on the desk before you. Across the desk, the commissioner beamed at you.

speaker: Comissioner
content: Chief, Demon Schilder must be handed over to the City Council. His execution is long overdue and should have been carried out eight years ago.

speaker: Comissioner
content: He averted justice eight years ago and killed a dozen city councilors since.

speaker: Comissioner
content: He is a crazed murderer. His execution will undoubtedly appease public anger.
The commissioner paused, observing your reaction. After a while, he continued:

speaker: Comissioner
content: We've arranged a trial for him in thirty days. We brought you these case files and evidence.

speaker: Comissioner
content: You can investigate and interrogate Demon as you wish. We believe you can get to the bottom of things...
The conversation continued for another while. Near the end, the commissioner stood up to say goodbye. Suddenly, he seemed to remember something, and took out a small box from his briefcase.

speaker: Comissioner
content: Oh right. I almost forgot this.

speaker: Comissioner
content: If Demon refuses to talk, show him this.
Inside the box was a dainty bracelet.

The City Council provided all the information needed for this interrogation. Although it was unsettling that they were interfering and demanding to execute one of the Bureau's Sinners, they did present a strong case supported by evidence.
Unless you uncover extenuating circumstances about the case, your superiors won't intervene. The only path awaiting Demon would be execution.
We have to talk about your case.
options: We have to talk about your case.

content: Demon squinted at the files in your hand.

speaker: Demon
content: The City Council gave you these?
His voice dripped with contempt at the mention of the City Council.
Yes.
Hearing your answer, Demon sneered coldly and stopped responding.
test
test
test
test
test
test
You picked up the first file.

Former Special Task Force Vice Captain <color=#e45515>Finn</color> fell from his apartment balcony on December 24th, 105. In addition to injuries sustained from his fall, there were also knife wounds all over his body. We presume that he was interrogated and tortured before his death.
You did this?
The case had ample evidence. Witness testimonies, the recovered murder weapon and even video footage from the victim's home all proved Demon was the murderer.

speaker: Demon
content: That's right.
Demon confessed so easily.

speaker: Demon
content: He owes me.
Why did you torture him?

speaker: Demon
content: To extract info about my next prey. And also...

speaker: Demon
content: ...to make some money along the way.
Sounded like Demon harbored a deep grudge against Vice Captain Finn.
Demon answered so bluntly that you couldn't think of what else to ask. So you picked up the next file.
Councilor Dole Young's body was found in the Eastside sewage system on October 17th, 105.
Fatal wound to the head, presumably caused by blunt force. The victim's skull was completely crushed, while his spine and ribs suffered multiple fractures. Did you do this?

speaker: Demon
content: Yes.
Demon gave another blunt answer.
Did you hurt him to extract information about your next prey as well?

speaker: Demon
content: No.

speaker: Demon
content: I just wanted him to die as painfully as possible.
Shadows loomed over Demon's face, clouding his expression.

<color=#e45515>Sedgwick Hendrold</color>, head of the City Council Security Department, was injured by an assailant on April 7th, 106 on Eastside's Saint-Saëns Avenue. When the ambulance arrived, he was pronounced dead at the scene...
You stopped talking. Those icy eyes already gave you the answer.
You breezed through a dozen cases in a few minutes. Demon's answer was the same for each one.
You understand why the City Council pressed you so hard to hand over Demon—the twelve deceased were all city councilors, and all were brutally tortured before they died.
Do you feel guilty when you commit murder?

speaker: Demon
content: Guilty?

speaker: Demon
content: I was simply crushing some maggots.
Demon's voice was cold and indifferent.
You still haven't figured out his motive. You couldn't imagine what he had gone through to reach his current state of mind.

speaker: Demon
content: Revenge.
His answer was crisp, heavy, and ominous, like a deadly undercurrent.
You could tell he wasn't lying when he spat out that word.
What did they do?
This time, Demon did not answer you.
There was a long pause. Demon didn't answer, so you picked up the last file.
Councilor <color=#e45515>Abel Schilder</color>, the first of Demon's victims. On July 6th, 104, Demon killed him in full view of the public.
You weren't expecting much from Demon's next answer. It would probably be another absent-minded confession.
But things turned out differently from what you expected. When Demon heard the name "Abel," his face changed.
You suddenly noticed something. Abel Schilder, Demon Schilder... the two shared the same surname. The dots were starting to connect.
test
test
test
test
test
test
test
Abel was your foster father?
Demon wore a strange expression on his face. You couldn't tell if it was sadness or rage.

speaker: Demon
content: It's been eight years. I didn't expect anyone in Eastside to still remember him.
Eight years cannot erase murder.

speaker: Demon
content: Who knows? Eastsiders forget easily.
So you killed him?

speaker: Demon
content: That's right.
Why? He was your foster father. Were you exacting revenge on him, too?
The file stated that Demon had been a Syndicate member as a teenager, but was later adopted by Abel. Thanks to Abel's support, Demon found a job at the FAC.
Abel was clearly his savior.

options: Question Demon's motive for murdering Abel

content: Demon closed his eyes. When he opened them again, the cold and ruthless expression returned.

speaker: Demon
content: Eight years ago, Abel mutated into a Corruptor after he was struck by an Mania weapon during a campaign speech.

speaker: Demon
content: At the time, I was the Captain of the Special Task Force. Eliminating Corruptors was my responsibility.
Demon's tone remained flat, as if talking about something that had nothing to do with him.
However, you acquired new information. The City Council made no mention of Mania weapons.
Eight years ago, Eastside, Mania weapons... all these unrelated pieces of information were jumbling together. The truth was becoming harder and harder to decipher.
There is no reason for the City Council to withhold such important information. Do you have evidence? Or any relevant witnesses to prove your claim?

speaker: Demon
content: Listen...
Demon suddenly interrupted you.

speaker: Demon
content: Don't waste your time.

speaker: Demon
content: I'm not interested in playing this childish detective game of yours.
Demon's patience was wearing thin.
You didn't know which question triggered him, but too many unresolved issues remained. The interrogation could not end yet.

options: Why do you hate the City Council?

content: Shadows loomed over his gaunt, lowered face.
Answer me.
The Bureau is not affiliated with the City Council. I'm not your enemy.
If you keep refusing to cooperate, I won't be able to help you even if I uncover extenuating circumstances about this case.
One month from now, the City Council will hold a secret trial. Once you are convicted, the City Council will immediately take you away to be executed...
A cold laugh echoed in the darkness. Demon glared at you, then closed his eyes.
By now, the interrogation was basically a closed case. Demon confessed to the murders, but refused to mention any further details. There wasn't any more information or evidence.
Except for the commissioner's strange box.
test
test
test
test
test
test
Do you recognize this thing?
Demon didn't open his eyes.
You waited for a while, but Demon didn't respond. You opened the box and took out a bracelet, which clinked crisply in your hand.
Demon opened his eyes.

speaker: Demon
content: Ve...
Demon mumbled something quietly, but you couldn't hear clearly.
What did you say?

speaker: Demon
content: Where... did you find that?
A sense of indescribable dread filled the room.
The ominous aura made your scalp feel numb. You subconsciously gave the answer.
The City Council...
Demon's body suddenly stiffened, and his face contorted like a terrifying beast.

speaker: Demon
content: Give me...
You shivered in fear. Your instinct told you to flee, but your legs went limp.

speaker: Demon
content: Give it... to me!
There was a painful ripping sound. Torn strips of cloth fluttered and tinged the air with the scent of blood as Demon lunged towards you.
At the same time, you heard a soft metallic sting. It was the sound of something sharp piercing the skin.
Demon fell to the floor with a thud.
Nightingale stood behind you, tranquilizer in hand.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Group 1, please update the data. The subject needs twice the amount of sedatives as before. Group 2, take the subject back to his cell.
As Nightingale spoke, guards lifted Demon onto a stretcher.
Demon hadn't completely lost consciousness yet. He fixated his eyes on the bracelet in your hand, his pupils gradually dilating.

speaker: Demon
content: I want to... kill...
Before he could finish, the guards carried him out of the interrogation room.
This was how Demon's interrogation ended.

15 Days
Until the Trial
You went down the hall to Demon's cell.
Several guards were waiting there.

speaker: Guard
content: The evidence is ready. The suspect, Demon Schilder, is awake. You may start your interrogation.
You nodded to the staff, then took a deep breath as you faced the cell door.
The cell door was already open. Yet Demon wasn't inside.

speaker: Guard
content: Chief, watch out!
You sensed something was wrong. You spun around, only to face Demon's glaring eyes.
Before you could react, a searing pain enveloped your head. You blacked out and lost consciousness...
What are you doing?
Let go... Chief...
Put down the gun... let him pass...
You opened your eyes to a peeling ceiling. Your arms and legs were so tightly bound that you could not move an inch.
You groggily remembered what happened. You were planning to interrogate Demon in his cell, but he attacked you.
Demon was still dozing off in his chair. It seemed like he was exhausted from running away while injured.

speaker: Demon
content: ...Awake?
Demon seemed to hear the sound of you struggling and opened his eyes. He brought you a glass of water.
You wanted to refuse, but your parched lips and dry throat thirsted for water.

speaker: Demon
content: You're dehydrated.
Your parched lips throbbed in pain. You realized Demon was right and drank the cup.
After that, Demon fell silent again. It didn't seem like he was going to explain what was going on.
As you wriggled your body, you realized that your personal tracker was still on you. The Bureau would be able to track your location.
Demon heard your movement and squinted at you.

speaker: Demon
content: Don't move.
Demon's eyes were bloodshot. His voice was threatening, but also reeked of indescribable exhaustion.
He was in a fragile state. His usual threatening and ferocious demeanor had been stretched to the limit.

options: Ask him why he kidnapped you

content: You've already achieved your goal and escaped from the Bureau. Why do you keep me around?
You want to kill me?
The dim light cast dark shadows over Demon.
After a long silence, his dry and ominous voice spoke up again.

speaker: Demon
content: I can spare you...

speaker: Demon
content: Don't get in the way of my revenge, and I'll let you go.
Revenge. It wasn't the first time Demon mentioned this word.

options: Who do you want to take revenge upon?

speaker: Demon
content: You don't need to know...
Ding—
A sudden noise from the water pipe in the corner interrupted Demon. Probably some alarm was triggered. Demon stood up, high on alert.
People might be on their way to rescue you.
The people you want to exact revenge on, are they the deceased city councilors? What did they do?
Demon ignored you, walked across the room and opened the curtains. He peered out the window and quickly came back to you.
Did they frame you?

speaker: Demon
content: Shut up.
Demon's facial muscles twitched slightly, but he didn't answer your question. Perhaps he was unsettled by the alarm and was planning to leave.
You should stall some more time for your rescuers.
Are you going to keep fleeing?
It's been eight years. You're killing more people and becoming more notorious. Yet nobody knows the truth. They only see you as a killer. They fear you, despise you...
Look at the situation you're in now. You're hiding left and right, running out of options... How much of your plan for revenge has been realized?

speaker: Demon
content: Shut up!
Demon leaned down and grabbed you by the collar.

speaker: Demon
content: You know nothing!
Then tell me what you want to do!
The anger that had been suppressed for eight years poured out.

speaker: Demon
content: They must pay for Abel's death!
Are you saying that the City Council was responsible for Abel's death?

speaker: Demon
content: Isn't it obvious?

speaker: Demon
content: Eight years ago, Abel entered the election to repeal the Western District Security Law...

speaker: Demon
content: Aside from those maggot councilors, who else had the motive to kill him?
Demon's face contorted from the murderous rage that had built up for many years.

speaker: Demon
content: They bribed Finn, one of my former subordinates, to let thugs armed with Mania weapons into the venue.

speaker: Demon
content: Abel turned into a Corruptor, so I had no choice but to kill him. I had to kill... my father.
Demon's voice quivered when he uttered the word "father."

speaker: Demon
content: They scapegoated me for everything...

speaker: Demon
content: The most ridiculous thing was that everyone believed the City Council's words. Just because I'm from... the Syndicate.

speaker: Demon
content: In that case, I could only use the Syndicate's methods to resolve the problem...
Demon inched up close to you, spitting out each word with relish.

speaker: Demon
content: Everyone who had anything to do with this must die.
Demon finally released the rage that he had nowhere to vent for eight years.
He gasped for air after spitting out everything in one breath. His bloodshot eyes were filled with rage but also helplessness.

speaker: Demon
content: Help me?
Demon laughed coldly.

speaker: Demon
content: How will you help me? Declare war on the City Council?
You're a Sinner from the Bureau. If what you said is true, I have the responsibility to protect you.
Only by staying alive can you bring the real culprits to justice. If you keep fleeing like this, you'll die sooner or later... It's not too late to come back to the Bureau with me.
Demon raised his head and took a deep gulp of air, gradually calming down.

speaker: Demon
content: ...Eight years ago, perhaps I would've believed you.

speaker: Demon
content: But not anymore.

speaker: Demon
content: I know you're just stalling for time to wait for help. I won't give you any more chances.
You struggled to get up, trying to defend yourself.
As you wriggled and writhed, the bracelet you wanted to use for questioning slipped out of your pocket and fell to the ground.
Demon's pupils shrank abruptly. Though this was the second time he saw the bracelet, he still couldn't conceal how shaken he was by it.
You remembered the question you wanted to ask during the interrogation, as well as the question that came up when you were browsing the files.

speaker: Nightingale
content: If your guess was correct, the bracelet given to you by the City Council belonged to her.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Abel's biological daughter, Demon's sister.
Vera Schilder
Demon looked at the bracelet on the ground in silence.
Is she important to you?

speaker: Demon
content: She is my family... my little sister.
Demon's expression gave the answer you were looking for.
He picked up the bracelet gently from the ground.
He raised his hand as dim rays of light shone through the curtains. The white bracelet swayed slightly. There was a gentle look on his face that you've never seen before.
Where is she?

speaker: Demon
content: I... don't know.

speaker: Demon
content: I'm a fugitive, while she's a councilor's daughter. I can't go meet her.
As for the bracelet the City Council gave...

speaker: Demon
content: I can only think of one explanation. They kidnapped Vera to use her to threaten me.
Is that why you escaped the Bureau despite your injuries?

speaker: Demon
content: Vera is the only family I have left... I must find her.
Demon clutched the bracelet in his palm and turned to you. His expression was unprecedentedly calm.

options: I will help you find her.

content: This time, Demon didn't refuse right away.
The Bureau has sufficient manpower and a well-developed intelligence network. Finding Vera won't be difficult as long as you can provide the appropriate information.
I'm not your enemy, Demon. Come back with me. You shouldn't shoulder all the burden by yourself.
Demon didn't respond. He just stared at you quietly.
Thankfully, the hostility had vanished from his eyes.
After a long time, Demon responded.

speaker: Demon
content: Thank you...
Demon walked to the window and opened the curtains. Blinding sunlight poured in from outside, and for a moment you couldn't open your eyes.

speaker: Demon
content: I've met people like you. None of them survived.

speaker: Demon
content: Good people don't live long in DisCity, but murderers like me can survive until now.
Demon opened the window. A grassy breeze diluted the musty odor in the room.

speaker: Demon
content: This is a battle I must fight alone.
Wait...

speaker: Demon
content: You have impressive men working for you. They will find you.
Demon leaned on the window sill. He covered his wound with one hand and gazed out the window.
Was he just going to leave like this? In his current state of health, it would only be a matter of time before he got caught.
You can't just leave like this! The City Council will sent their troops to arrest you. If you land in their hands...
You hadn't noticed that the old wooden door had been open for some time. A man in a hat stood by the door.

speaker: Mysterious Man
content: Cough...

speaker: Mysterious Man
content: Sorry, I didn't mean to interrupt your conversation.
You can't just leave like this! The City Council will sent their troops to arrest you. If you land in their hands...
You hadn't noticed that the old wooden door had been open for some time. A man in a hat stood by the door.

speaker: Mysterious Man
content: Cough...

speaker: Mysterious Man
content: Sorry, I didn't mean to interrupt your conversation.

speaker: Demon
content: Who are you?!
Demon immediately became vigilant. He didn't notice the man's arrival either.

speaker: Mysterious Man
content: It doesn't matter who I am. What matters is what I heard. It seems that in fifteen days, a show trial will be held against you.

speaker: Mysterious Man
content: I have a plan to break the game... do you two want to hear it?
The man smiled faintly. He didn't wait for an answer, but took off his hat and walked in.

speaker: Mysterious Man
content: I think you do.

10 Minutes
Until the Trial
You and Demon entered the courtroom.
The commissioner, the FAC official, and the City Council's chief judge were already in their seats. As high officials of various departments, they were all familiar faces to you.
The man in the hat was also present, but he didn't seem to be welcome.

speaker: Comissioner
content: Why is the 9th Agency getting involved? This isn't your style.
The man didn't respond to the commissioner's hiss, but he tipped his hat to you in respect.

speaker: 9th Agency Staff
content: Long time no see, Chief. Are you all prepared?
Fifteen days ago, you met him for the first time. The man claimed that the 9th Agency he represented could help.
At the time, he simply said he would provide extra evidence and information to help you win the case.
To your surprise, the most mysterious spy agency in DisCity got personally involved and placed one of their own in the jury.
You were planning to chat before the trial, but the judge began striking the gavel.

speaker: 9th Agency Staff
content: Seemed like some people couldn't wait.
The judge was a bigwig in his sixties or seventies from the municipal court. He didn't give you a chance to chat, and began to speak.

speaker: Judge
content: Defendant Demon Schilder, accused of killing thirteen high officials including Abel Schilder and Dole Young, will be tried by this court.

speaker: Judge
content: Court is in session.
The strike of the gavel echoed throughout the courtroom.

speaker: Judge
content: The commissioner began to speak.
The commissioner adjusted his spectacles. You recognized him. A month ago, it was this rising star from Eastside's legal world who gave you the files and Vera's bracelet.

speaker: Comissioner
content: Ladies and gentlemen, since this is not a regular court, and everyone is familiar with this case, I will summarize the details in a short and concise manner.
The commissioner waved the files in his hand.

speaker: Comissioner
content: Taking the case of former Special Task Force Vice Captain Finn as an example, the fingerprints and the murder weapon can be perfectly matched, and the surveillance footage from the victim's home recorded the entire crime.

speaker: Comissioner
content: All the other cases had similar circumstances. He didn't accidentally leave behind evidence of his crimes, he flaunted them on purpose to spread fear.

speaker: Comissioner
content: The crimes committed by Demon Schilder have had an extremely egregious impact. The City Council, and indeed all the citizens of Eastside, cannot accept him to be simply taken under MBCC custody.
The commissioner paused, looked around, then gazed at you and Demon with his head raised.

speaker: Comissioner
content: On behalf of the City Council, I demand the MBCC to hand over Demon Schilder to be publicly executed.
After the commissioner finished his cold statement, the entire room went silent. Everyone looked at you with malice.
Frowning, Demon tried to speak several times, but couldn't bring himself to open his mouth.
Before he could finally talk, the judge noticed his intentions.

speaker: Judge
content: Defendant, it's not your turn to speak.
Even though the commissioner said nothing else, and the jurors were all curious about what Demon had to say, the judge did not give Demon a chance to defend himself.
Perhaps Demon's trial eight years ago was also like this.

options: Help Demon get a chance to speak

content: Was this the case eight years ago, too? The defendant doesn't even get a chance to speak? This doesn't seem like a proper trial.
If you want the Bureau to hand him over, we have to at least hear what he has to say.
The judge frowned. He didn't expect you to talk back. After a while, he spoke again.

speaker: Judge
content: Defendant Demon, what was your motive for killing the thirteen victims?
Under your pressure, the City Council backed down. The judge took the initiative to "question" Demon.
Demon's eyes showed a hint of panic. It was obvious that his past trauma had a profound impact on him.
You put a hand on his shoulder.
Don't worry. I'll help you.
Demon took a deep breath and shifted his gaze to the commissioner.

speaker: Demon
content: Twelve of them...
Demon's voice was barely audible.

speaker: Comissioner
content: What did you say?

speaker: Demon
content: Eight years ago, the twelve of them murdered Abel...

speaker: Demon
content: I killed them to exact revenge.

speaker: Comissioner
content: Oh?
The commissioner wiped the corners of his eyes somewhat dramatically and continued.

speaker: Comissioner
content: Are you saying that it wasn't you who shot and killed Abel Schilder in Rose Hall eight years ago? And that it were the twelve deceased whom you killed later?

speaker: Demon
content: No... I was the one who shot Abel.

speaker: Comissioner
content: Then did those twelve instruct you to kill Abel?
The commissioner interrupted Demon several times, throwing in various theories to disrupt Demon's testimony.

speaker: Judge
content: Objection overruled. The commissioner is just doing his job.
Demon glared at the judge, but failed to change his mind.

speaker: Judge
content: ${PlayerName}, control your Sinner.
The court's malicious intent was disgusting. There was no hint of justice in this trial from beginning to end.
Fortunately, you were well prepared. As long as you set the pace, you could break the game.
Don't be distracted by his questions. Tell only necessary information.
Demon looked at you, and began to speak again.

speaker: Demon
content: I shot Abel because he had already mutated into a Corruptor and was attacking innocent civilians. I had no other choice.

speaker: Comissioner
content: That is to say, you admit to shooting and killing Councilor Abel Schilder, your foster father, on July 6th, 104?

speaker: Demon
content: During his speech, thugs armed with Mania weapons burst into the hall and attacked indiscriminately.

speaker: Demon
content: Abel was hit... though he didn't die on the spot, he quickly mutated and lost his consciousness...

speaker: Comissioner
content: I'm sorry, everyone.
The commissioner interrupted Demon again.

speaker: Comissioner
content: Since we mentioned Abel Schilder, it's necessary to reiterate the details of that case.

speaker: Comissioner
content: On such an important matter, the defendant's account will inevitably omit certain details, which will mislead everyone's judgment. Allow me.
The commissioner looked around. Nobody objected. He cleared his throat and began to speak.

speaker: Comissioner
content: On the night of July 6th, 104, the victim Abel was giving a campaign speech at Rose Hall when four thugs barged in and committed a massacre. Security personnel later shot and killed them.

speaker: Comissioner
content: While the victim was being escorted to safety, Demon used a 9mm pistol to shoot the victim six times in the head. The victim died on the spot.

speaker: Comissioner
content: The murder weapon was recovered at the scene of the crime. Eyewitness testimonies, fingerprints, DNA testing, and bullet analysis all point to the fact that you're the killer, Demon Schilder.
The commissioner ended his long monologue with a smug smirk.

speaker: Demon
content: I already said that Abel had turned into a Corruptor and was attacking innocent civilians...

speaker: Comissioner
content: It's true that according the report, Abel Schilder's body showed a high degree of mutation. The four thugs were also indeed armed with Mania weapons...

speaker: Comissioner
content: However, eight years ago, Mania weapons were extremely rare. In all of Eastside, no agency other than the Special Task Force could access such dangerous weapons.

speaker: Comissioner
content: Coincidentally, the defendant Demon was the Captain of the Special Task Force at the time... Back then, nobody except for senior Special Task Force members had access to Mania weapons. Isn't that right?
The commissioner looked over at the FAC official.
The FAC official frowned silently for a while.

speaker: FAC Official
content: Early Mania weapons were indeed accessible to the Special Task Force.

speaker: FAC Official
content: After the incident, the FAC conducted an internal investigation, which concluded that four Mania weapons were missing from the inventory.

speaker: Comissioner
content: I think the truth is clear. Defendant Demon Schilder stole the Mania weapons and gave them to the thugs.

speaker: Comissioner
content: He also sent away Special Task Force members responsible for guarding the venue to allow the thugs to enter without hindrance...

speaker: Demon
content: Where's the evidence?
Demon interrupted the droning commissioner.

speaker: Comissioner
content: All the case details come from the Special Task Force's internal testimonies.

speaker: Demon
content: Testimonies?

speaker: Comissioner
content: In the absence of other conclusive physical evidence, oral testimonies are sufficient to make a conviction.

speaker: Demon
content: I have some "conclusive physical evidence."

speaker: Demon
content: The fake document where Finn forged my signature is in Room 1102 of the West End Apartments.

speaker: Comissioner
content: It's pointless of you to mention a random name and address like that.

speaker: Demon
content: Haha... are all Eastside commissioners as incompetent as you?

speaker: Demon
content: The name belongs to the person you just mentioned, former Vice Captain Finn.

speaker: Comissioner
content: ...Are we going to wait here for several hours for someone to fetch it?

speaker: Demon
content: It won't take that long.

speaker: Demon
content: ...Are you scared?
Sweat drops formed on the commissioner's forehead.
However, the bang of the gavel put an end to the confrontation.

speaker: Judge
content: The evidence mentioned by the defendant had not been submitted to the court beforehand.

speaker: Judge
content: Therefore it cannot be used in the trial.
The atmosphere in the courtroom instantly dropped to the freezing point.

speaker: Demon
content: ...When did you ever give me the chance to submit evidence?

speaker: Judge
content: The rules of the courtroom haven't changed for twenty years. You should've read it up before you came, Demon.

speaker: Demon
content: I remember... eight years ago, you sentenced me to death...

speaker: Judge
content: That's right.

speaker: Demon
content: I should've paid you a visit a long time ago.

speaker: Judge
content: You have no more chances.
The judge rejected your request to submit evidence outright, ending the fiery confrontation.
Demon stopped arguing, and just stared coldly at the judge. He no longer had any hope for a fair trial.
Demon's attempts seemed to have failed, but you still had to try.
Abel was Demon's foster father. From what we know, they had a good relationship. Demon has no reason to kill him...

speaker: Comissioner
content: On this point, we also have contradicting evidence.
The commissioner spoke up again.

speaker: Comissioner
content: We obtained the defendant Demon Schilder's transfer records from Eastside Bank.

speaker: Comissioner
content: On June 29th, 104, Demon's private account received a huge payment from an anonymous account.
The commissioner looked at the judge.

speaker: Judge
content: Defendant Demon Schilder, please explain where this payment came from.
Demon kept silent, without any intention to answer.
This was a question you could not answer for Demon. You didn't know anything about it.

options: Tell Demon not to give up

content: Don't give up.
Even if they don't accept our new evidence, there must be flaws with their existing evidence... we still have a chance.
Under your coaxing, Demon's attitude seemed to thaw.

speaker: Judge
content: Defendant, answer the question.
The judge urged him to answer again. A look of annoyance and disgust flashed on Demon's face.

speaker: Demon
content: ...I don't know.

speaker: Comissioner
content: You don't know? So you cannot explain where this payment came from?

speaker: Demon
content: I only have one personal account, and my sister Vera took care of it.

speaker: Comissioner
content: Are you saying that Vera instructed you to kill her biological father?

speaker: Demon
content: Shut up!
Demon immediately sprung up in anger—Vera was his last family member. He couldn't allow anyone to frame his sister like that.

speaker: Comissioner
content: Thank goodness Miss Vera is under our care. Otherwise, I highly suspect you'd try to hurt her, too.
The City Council was finally showing its true colors.

speaker: Demon
content: I knew it... you took Vera...

speaker: Comissioner
content: Miss Vera has requested our protection since January 105. She is hiding from your murderous pursuit.

speaker: Demon
content: Where is she?!

speaker: Comissioner
content: I'm sorry, but in the interests of Miss Vera's safety, she will not be testifying in person today.
The commissioner took out a thin plastic bag.

speaker: Comissioner
content: But before the trial began, we attained her testimony, which proves all your crimes in the past eight years.

speaker: Demon
content: Impossible!
Demon roared.

speaker: Demon
content: Vera is a family, there's no way she would...

speaker: Judge
content: Watch your tongue, Demon Schilder.
The judge's voice was like a bucket of ice-cold water dousing out Demon's flames of rage.
With Vera in their hands, Demon didn't dare fight back.
You realize that the City Council's trump card was Vera. They were holding her hostage to coerce Demon into pleading guilty.

speaker: Judge
content: The testimony states that you plotted to murder Councilor Abel Schilder. Defendant Demon, how do you plead?
Demon's eyes were bloodshot, and his tightly clenched jaw made a horrible grinding noise.

speaker: Demon
content: ...plead guilty.
His words were engulfed by utter hatred and unwillingness.

speaker: Judge
content: You're accused of murdering twelve city councilors. How do you plead?

speaker: Demon
content: I... plead guilty.

speaker: Judge
content: You forced the victim Vera Schilder to take the blame for Abel's murder, and tried to murder her every chance you got in the past eight years. How do you plead?
The trial was heading towards the worst possible outcome. If this went on, Demon would surely be doomed.
You said you'd help him... you promised... but under the circumstance...

speaker: 9th Agency Staff
content: My apologies. Allow me to interrupt.
The man from the 9th Agency suddenly spoke up.
The judge's face went dark. He didn't expect someone to interrupt him at the most critical moment.

speaker: 9th Agency Staff
content: I'd like to ask... Commissioner, when was this testimony recorded?
The commissioner looked at the judge in slight confusion.

speaker: Judge
content: Two days ago.
The judge didn't dare hide that fact in front of the agent from the notorious 9th Agency.

speaker: 9th Agency Staff
content: Who conducted the questioning and transcription of the testimony?

speaker: Judge
content: This was a matter of utmost importance, so I completed the entire procedure myself.
Faced with the current situation, the seasoned judge grew impatient. He just wanted to answer the spy's questions quickly and finish the trial.

speaker: 9th Agency Staff
content: Oh? How strange...
The man put on a teasing tone.

speaker: 9th Agency Staff
content: Five hours ago, my men raided a secret Black Water outpost. You should know what I mean by Black Water.

speaker: 9th Agency Staff
content: We found quite a few corpses there. Just now, we conducted DNA analysis and confirmed the identity of one of the bodies...

speaker: 9th Agency Staff
content: Councilor Abel Schilder's daughter, Vera Schilder.
Hearing this, Demon stiffened, and his eyes became listless.
His teeth chattered, but he was unable to say a single word.

speaker: Judge
content: That's... impossible...

speaker: 9th Agency Staff
content: I advise you not to lie about her date of death. Miss Vera has been dead for at least six years.

speaker: Judge
content: No... no... that's not...

speaker: 9th Agency Staff
