content: Are you trying to say that you were unaware of Miss Vera's death? Or that Black Water concealed the information? Who is your contact with Black Water? Would you like to come to the morgue with me?
The judge finally fell silent, his face turning ashen. He knew it was useless to say anything now.
In just a few words, the trial took a one-eighty degree turn - all thanks to the man from the 9th Agency.
He wore a faint smile on his face.

speaker: 9th Agency Staff
content: The trial for the murder of Eastside's city councilors is hereby suspended. Defendant Demon Schilder shall return to the MBCC for confinement.

speaker: 9th Agency Staff
content: The main goal now is to investigate the fraud committed by the City Council and weed out Black Water's infiltration... Lord Blake, please come with me.
Emerging as the victor, he slowly strut over to the judge and gestured for him to leave.
You realized now that the conversation seven days ago and his offer to help was part of a well-planned scheme. The 9th Agency took advantage of both you and Demon.
The entire trial was just a cover for the 9th Agency to overthrow the City Council.

speaker: Demon
content: Why...
Demon's voice was hoarse. He should be the center of attention at the trial, but at this moment, the courtroom was chaotic. No one noticed him except you.
He sat frozen on the floor, his voice trembling.

speaker: 9th Agency Staff
content: I'm sorry for your experience, Demon.

speaker: 9th Agency Staff
content: But your trial has concluded, and we have more important things to attend to...

speaker: Demon
content: What did Vera do... why did you do this to her...
The judge looked over. His face was grim, but he still forced himself to croak in defense.

speaker: Judge
content: It had nothing to do with me...

speaker: Demon
content: You said... you transcribed her testimony...

speaker: Judge
content: Did you really believe that?

speaker: Judge
content: It wasn't my decision alone to hand her over to Black Water. We lost contact with her afterward.
But you dared to use her name to fabricate evidence?
The judge's face turned ashen.

speaker: Judge
content: Nobody wanted her dead... It's just that I didn't expect Parma to act so boldly.

speaker: Demon
content: ...It's not important anymore.
Everything happened so quickly. You saw everything, but there was no time to stop it.
Demon broke free from the heavy shackles and pounced on the judge. The next moment, the judge's head fell to the ground with a thud.
It took a full five seconds for everyone else to realize what happened. Demon slumped to the floor like a puppet cut from its strings. His pupils lost focus, as if his soul had left his body.
Eight years later, Demon committed another murder in public.

speaker: 9th Agency Staff
content: Um...
Sorry. I couldn't stop him.
And your investigation?

speaker: 9th Agency Staff
content: It's fine. We got enough justification already. Anyway, thanks for your cooperation.
He glanced at the commissioner paralyzed in fear on the floor, and then at Demon.

speaker: 9th Agency Staff
content: Demon is an unstable pawn. Please be careful with him.

speaker: 9th Agency Staff
content: A murder in broad daylight is not easy to placate. You must deal with it appropriately, otherwise you won't be able to stop people from talking.
I will take care of it.

speaker: 9th Agency Staff
content: I trust your judgment. Oh, by the way...

speaker: 9th Agency Staff
content: Miss Langley says hi.
The man tipped his hat in respect one last time and left. Next, the FAC official took a deep look at Demon and left silently as well.
In the hall, only you, Demon and a roomful of carnage remained.

MBCC Temporary Mission Log
Time: ██/██/112
Location: High-risk zone, the Rust upstream.
Goal: Find Vera Schilder's remains.

speaker: Guard
content: Corruptors detected. Number: 4, distance: 10 meters... Chief!
Several black shadows sprung out from the ruins.
Bang—

Demon grabbed the Corruptor who jumped out first by the throat and slammed it to the ground. The sharp edge of his shield snapped its neck. The headless Corruptor twitched a few times and then stopped moving.
Find cover and shoot!
Under the cover of firepower, two Corruptors found it hard to advance and were quickly riddled with bullets.
Yet the last Corruptor dodged the guards ahead and lunged towards you.
Demon was the first to react. He used his shield to slam the Corruptor into the nearest concrete pillar, causing it to vomit out its internal organs.
The buildings in the Rust's no-man's land had long fallen into disrepair and simply could not withstand such an impact.
The dilapidated six-story building came crashing down.

speaker: Guard
content: Chief... zzzz... can you hear me? Chief! Please respond!
I can hear you. I'm fine.
Demon dusted off the debris from his body, stood up, and stared at you without saying a word.
...Demon is fine, too.

speaker: Guard
content: We will be there... in twenty minutes... please wait where you are... please don't move...

speaker: Demon
content: Those sounds probably alerted all the Corruptors in the area...
Demon didn't continue, but you knew what he meant. To wait where you were equaled waiting for death.
We need to keep moving. With him around, we won't be in grave danger.

speaker: Guard
content: But...
You knew he wanted to say that the person next to you was the gravest danger of all.
But there were no other options now.
I'll go to the destination first. You guys go back to the pick-up point and wait for me.

speaker: Guard
content: ....Copy that.
You turned off the radio headset and waved to Demon.
They don't seem to trust you.

speaker: Demon
content: They're right.
No matter what he said, Demon's personal abilities were trustworthy. Though the mission had been marred with countless dangers, it was reassuring to have Demon around.
Though he became thinner and gloomier after the trial, he was still the former Captain of the FAC Special Task Force renowned throughout the city.
We still have a mission to complete.
Demon did not deny it this time. He raised his shield and walked up to you. He had applied to take part in this mission himself.
There was only one goal to the mission—to find the remains of Demon's sister, Vera Schilder.
You pushed open a corroded iron door and entered a sanatorium.
The foul odor of dead bodies mixed with the putrid stench of mold, seared your eyes. In the corridor ahead, there were more than a dozen decomposed corpses on the floor.
There were Corruptors, and there were humans.

speaker: Demon
content: This was the place.
Two months ago, agents from the 9th Agency came to this place. They found what they wanted.
However, some also died here.
When agents from the 9th Agency asked the judge to "identify the body," I thought...
They should've brought Vera along.

speaker: Demon
content: That's not their responsibility.
Demon crouched down and prodded the severely decomposed corpse of a combatant.

speaker: Demon
content: No risk of becoming a Corruptor...
He took off his cloak and put it over the corpse.
The elevator had long been out of use. You went all the way up the stairs and finally came to the door of the room you were looking for.
The dust in front of the door was thinner than in other places. The whole corridor was covered with footprints, especially in front of the door to this room.
You knew you were in the right place.
Demon put his hand on the doorknob. For the first time, you saw hesitation and withdrawal on his face.
Shall I wait for you outside for a bit?
Demon shook his head and twisted open the doorknob.
The room behind the door was only about eight square meters in size. There was a small skeleton curled up on a gray bed by the window.

speaker: Demon
content: Vera...
He limped over and knelt down in front of the bed. His movements were so gentle, as if fearing to wake up the sleeping girl.

Demon wanted to say something, but couldn't open his mouth. He crouched beside the bed as sunlight leaked through the cracks of the abandoned building, illuminating the dust flying among the shredded beams.
The time passed bit by bit, but Demon said nothing. The bloodcurdling shrieks of the Corruptors were getting closer and closer. You had to remind him.
We should go now...
Demon turned around and looked at you.

speaker: Demon
content: Hmm...

speaker: Demon
content: I know.
He packed the bones into his backpack piece by piece. He also took the dusty notebook by Vera's pillow.
After finishing, he got up and walked towards you.

speaker: Demon
content: Sorry to keep you waiting.
Demon forced a smile. He looked so fragile, with gaunt eyes seeping nothing but exhaustion and sorrow.
All around you, the shrieks of the Corruptors grew ever denser.

speaker: Demon
content: Let's go.
You and Demon traversed the crumbling ruins for quite some time. Corruptors were appearing more and more frequently.
Luckily, your destination was already quite close. You could already see the lights of the Syndicate.

speaker: Demon
content: Be careful! Behind you!
Linda stands there thunderstruck, mouth hanging open.
Demon turned sideways and knocked down the Corruptor behind him. Squeezed between the ground and the shield, its head exploded, spurting foul-smelling gray liquid onto the ground.
A shard from the Corruptor's skull sliced open his hand, leaving a bloody wound.
This wave... is temporarily over. Thank you, Demon.
Contrary to your joyful relief, Demon dealt with his wound calmly, but without a hint of relief or joy in his voice.

speaker: Demon
content: Things are bad.
What are you worried about?
The guards have arrived at the pick-up point. We are very close to the borders of no man's land...
With your strength, we can definitely evacuate successfully. What are you worried about?
Demon looked up at the sky. The city lights tinted the hazy clouds ominously yellow, blocking out the stars.

speaker: Demon
content: Yes, very close...

speaker: Demon
content: And that's the worst possible thing.
Gazing at the lights of the Syndicate neighborhoods, you suddenly realized what Demon meant.
The Corruptors will follow us all the way to the city...

speaker: Demon
content: A lot of people will die.
I'll alert the FAC right away! They'll send help!

speaker: Demon
content: There's no time.

speaker: Demon
content: How far is the nearest residential area?
You glanced at the satellite map.
2.5 kilometers away...
The distance is too short. By the time the FAC gets here, the streets would be awash with blood.

speaker: Demon
content: They won't make it in time.
Demon quietly removed his backpack and took out the notebook. He then gave the backpack to you.

speaker: Demon
content: Please bury Vera for me.
He put the shield on the ground and pulled out the dagger from his waist.
Have you gone mad?!

speaker: Demon
content: I will try to slow down the Corruptors.

speaker: Demon
content: Go find the Bureau's guards and evacuate nearby residents. Wait until the FAC arrives before clearing things here.
Demon raised his head to look at the debris around him.

speaker: Demon
content: The Syndicate has lost too much already. Someone needs to protect what's left.
You'll die...

speaker: Demon
content: The whole thing started with my selfish desires. I have no excuse to flee.
There was no regret in his voice, only relief.

speaker: Demon
content: For someone like me, dying here is the easy way out.
There are Bureau staffs nearby. I'll bring them to help you.

speaker: Demon
content: It's no use. There are so few of them that they won't even be able to form a line of defense.

speaker: Demon
content: They'd only distract me here.
But...

speaker: Demon
content: Go!
Demon scowled again, but unlike in the past, you weren't frightened.
Wait for me. I'll be back.
Watching the "Chief" who restrained him leave, a smile appeared on Demon's face.

speaker: Demon
content: Don't come back. It's not worth it.
He muttered to himself, shaking off the blood from his left hand.

speaker: Demon
content: I'm all alone again... this is for the best.

speaker: Demon
content: This is for the best.

speaker: Demon
content: After all... I couldn't protect anything.
Weak monsters always hunt in groups, otherwise they wouldn't be able to kill their prey.
They are ignorant, short-sighted, and beholden to their instincts.
That's why they're easy to control.
That was the knowledge Demon had summed up back at the Special Task Force. To this day, the same logic still applied.

speaker: Demon
content: Ahhh!
Demon roared and slammed into the Corruptor in front of him. The slender monster snapped into two, its blood and guts spilling onto the ground in a sticky mess.
The shrieks around him did not stop. This was the terrifying thing about Corruptors. They didn't fear death.
They were beholden to their instincts.

speaker: Demon
content: Come at me... you monsters...
In the darkness, endless waves of Corruptors surged forth, baring their fangs and claws to pounce on the lone warrior, before being torn to bits and washing away downstream.
In this carnival of slaughter, everything that moved became a sacrifice.

speaker: Abel
content: Vera, come.
The man waved to the little girl. Beside him stood a boy.

speaker: Abel
content: From now on, he is your older brother. Be nice to each other.
The little girl came over, but the boy stepped back instinctively. He didn't belong here. He was just a gangster from the Syndicate who jacked Abel's car, and he... killed people before.
But the little girl still walked over and took his hand.

speaker: Vera
content: Demon, my brother!
She smiled sweetly.

speaker: Vera
content: Let's go home together!
Swish—
The sharp claws left bloody gashes on Demon's face. He woke up with a start, and just for a moment, he lost focus.
The wounds on his body were increasing, and his eyes became a bit blurry.

speaker: Demon
content: That was just a mirage from the past.
Demon kept warning himself. It was dangerous to be distracted during battle, and the Chief needed more time to evacuate the townsfolk. He couldn't fall down just yet.
Thanks to the power of Sinner, his left hand healed, leaving a shallow scab.
Demon tore off the scab. The pain stimulated his numb nerves, bringing about much-needed sobriety.

speaker: Demon
content: I won't make this kind of mistake again.

speaker: Vera
content: Demon, you need to eat...
Scars zigzagged across the boy's naked torso. He blushed and quickly put on his shirt.

speaker: Vera
content: What's that on your body...

speaker: Vera
content: Daddy says that you used to have a hard life, and that your former daddy beat you. Guess it's true...

speaker: Vera
content: But don't worry! My daddy is the best daddy in the whole wide world! He never scolds me unless I eat something bad and get a tummy ache.

speaker: Vera
content: I'll protect both you and Dad. From now on, no one will dare bully you!

speaker: Vera
content: Demon, are you leaving?
The boy nodded somewhat awkwardly. He deliberately chose such an early hour to leave, because he didn't know how to face parting with them.

speaker: Demon
content: I'm going to the Eastside Police Academy. Abel... Dad is very busy. I should learn something to help shoulder his burden.

speaker: Vera
content: I know...
The little girl sounded a bit aggrieved.

speaker: Vera
content: But I don't want you to go.
The boy smiled and patted her head.

speaker: Demon
content: Don't worry. I'll be back soon.

speaker: Demon
content: I'm sorry, Vera. I came back too late...
Demon touched the notebook in his breast pocket, muttering to himself.
It was the last part of his body that had not been soaked with blood.

speaker: Demon
content: Vera, I should have had a chat with you before I committed all these crimes...
Demon stood upright in the pool of blood. He was exhausted, and even the armor on his body became heavy from the bloodstains.
He needed to rest, if only for a little while. Perhaps he needed to chat with someone, even if it were a hallucination.
Demon closed his eyes, entering a world of boundless darkness.
A young man with a backpack slung over his shoulder knocked on the door hesitantly, but no one responded. When he twisted the doorknob, he found that the door was unlocked.
The house was dark.
Bam—

speaker: Vera
content: Happy birthday!
The lights in the house suddenly lit up, and colorful ribbons rained down from the ceiling. A young girl stood behind him with a cake in her hands.
The young man turned around, a warm smile on his face.

speaker: Demon
content: Thank you...
As he removed the ribbons stuck to the girl's head, he nodded towards the man on the sofa.

speaker: Abel
content: Cough cough...
The man stood up from the sofa. He aged a lot these past few years. But seeing his adopted son return home, the wrinkles on his face seemed to smooth out.

speaker: Abel
content: I have good news.

speaker: Abel
content: It's not confirmed yet, but based on your recent performance, you should be promoted to Captain of the Special Task Force next month.

speaker: Vera
content: Really?!
The young girl's eyes widened in surprise.

speaker: Vera
content: You're the best big brother in the whole wide world!

speaker: Vera
content: Demon, I heard that someone... wants to hurt Dad... Is it true?
The young man was tired, but after hearing the girl's anxious question, he still answered with a smile.

speaker: Demon
content: Yeah, Dad stepped on a few toes this election.
The young girl's face filled with worry.

speaker: Vera
content: What do we do...

speaker: Demon
content: Don't worry, I'll protect him.
After a silent pause, the girl forced a smile.

speaker: Vera
content: Yes, Demon, I believe you.

speaker: Demon
content: You shouldn't have believed me.
Demon used his last bit of strength to snap the neck of the Corruptor in front of him. He finally succumbed to exhaustion, falling to his knees in a pool of blood.
The surrounding ruins dissolved, and Demon returned to the tiny eight-square-meter room.

speaker: Demon
content: I let you down...
Vera's remains rested there silently, unresponsive to Demon.

speaker: Demon
content: I'm a coward, a good-for-nothing piece of trash... I don't deserve your trust...

speaker: Demon
content: I couldn't protect Abel, and I couldn't protect you...
A finger pressed the man's dry, chapped lips.
Behind him, a pair of arms wrapped around his neck, and the cold touch made him feel familiar and at ease.
The next instant, Demon stood up suddenly and let out a bloodcurdling roar.

speaker: Demon
content: Ahhhhhhh!!!
Demon lifted the Corruptor who had snuck up on him in midair. Its shattered spine and innards washed away the dreamlike hallucinations.
The notebook in his breast pocket fell out, landing on the last page.
Dear brother, I hope you are well.

It's been a year and I still don't know what this place is. Every day, new faces come and old faces disappear. Every day, I look out the window, hoping to find you in the crowd, but I'm also glad that you're not among them.

Please forgive me for thinking this way... It's probably because I haven't seen you for so long.

Today, when I saw the sunset outside the window, I remembered the first time we met: Dad and I took you home, and we walked along the path in front of our house. You didn't speak, so I could only admire the scenery along the way. There was a beautiful sunset that day, just like today.

Sorry, I may not be able to survive much longer.

I don't know what others think, but I want you to know that no matter what you're doing, no matter what they say, I believe you. I will always... be grateful to have met you.

May you spend every day in peace and happiness.
Your sister Vera
The man raised his head, tears running down his cheeks.

speaker: Demon
content: Ve... ra...
He uttered that name one last time. All the dreams and memories disappeared.

speaker: Demon
content: Thank you...
Corruptor corpses piled high all around him, and the terrifying shrieks gradually fell silent.

speaker: Demon
content: I... I did it...
There was nothing left. Corruptors, violence, promises, warmth, his once beloved and trusting family...
Everything scattered to the freezing night wind along with the Rust.
Demon smiled and closed his eyes. He slumped to the ground, his armor landing with a dull thud.
...Wake... up...
Demon... Demon...
Demon! Wake up!
I told you I'd be back...
You can't die yet!

Postcard content:

OwO has found my hometown! Hmph, such a dummy clapper like you must be having a hard time in Syndicate without me. You must be missing OwO and OwO's lion dance very much!
Wait for me! Oh, I have very good news to tell you in person, and that's important!

She clearly asked an adult to write it for her. A photo is attached to the back of the postcard, in which OwO lifts the lion head proudly in front of an ethnic village. The golden writing on the plaque at the entrance reads Goldionville.
You look down at the prideful lion dancer in the photo, then look up at the girl before you who's covered in dirt rolling on the ground, picking a fight. You sigh.
This is what the alarm was referring to... "An extremely dangerous Sinner is causing trouble on the street"?
Staring at the petite figure making a scene in the crowd not far ahead, even the fully armed guards lower their weapons a little awkwardly.

speaker: OwO
content: I'm sure about it this time! It must be that jackass with the hat!
Standing in the crowd, OwO scans the gathering pedestrians and points at a lucky spectator.

speaker: OwO
content: You seem sneaky! Did you steal my lion head?!

speaker: Hooligan
content: Did you just call me a jackass?!

speaker: OwO
content: Hump! Why are you getting mad if you know you're innocent? It must be because you're feeling guilty!
OwO roars in the direction of the hooligan, bursting out a string of golden sound waves.
Luckily, the hooligan dodges it agilely, though toppling a water bucket in front of someone's house behind him.

speaker: Hooligan
content: I didn't do it! I said it's not here, that whatever freaking head of yours!

speaker: OwO
content: The lion head! A big, beautiful lion's head! How can you not know it!

speaker: OwO
content: I don't care! Liar, liar, liar! Your nose will grow if you lie!
She seems to be aiming at a flowerpot on the windowsill on the second floor of a building this time, shattering it with a furious roar.

speaker: OwO
content: I lost it here! If you don't tell me where it is, I'm not leaving!
She sits down on the ground, arms akimbo. The surrounding residents dare not get close to her or make eye contact, lest they become the next unlucky target of her suspicion.

speaker: Pedestrian A
content: What's this thing she's making a fuss about? Is it some expensive toy?

speaker: Pedestrian B
content: Who cares what it is. All I know is that this little girl wrecked a lot of our things.

speaker: Pedestrian C
content: Whose kid is that? She needs to be disciplined! We already told her we'd never seen it but she insists on harassing every resident here... Just shut up.

speaker: Pedestrian D
content: Didn't someone call the police already? Why aren't those publicly-funded idiots from DisCity here to arrest her yet?
Cough...
Being the leader of publicly-funded idiots from DisCity, you've observed enough to have a grasp of the situation here. You make your way through the crowd.

speaker: OwO
content: Hmph, no one can hold me back now. I won't give up if I don't find the lion head!

speaker: OwO
content: Just be nice and give it back to OwO, or I will... Eh?
She watches the changeless uniform and leather shoes approaching her and realizes she's seen them before.

speaker: OwO
content: You're...
She looks up and finally recognizes the face in front of her.

speaker: OwO
content: Little clapper!
OwO grabs onto your thighs as if clutching a lifeline.

speaker: OwO
content: The guys behind you are... the bunch of assistants who follow you!

speaker: OwO
content: Good timing! I order you guys to make them hand the lion head back to OwO! Right now, immediately, at once!
She grips the hem of your jacket and looks up at you with red-rimmed eyes, only to hear a cold and resigned answer.
You've abused your special power and disrupted public order. You'll have to come with us, Sinner.

speaker: OwO
content: Abused my special power?! Disrupted public order?!

speaker: OwO
content: How dare you, you mere clapper! You dare to defame OwO, the fabulous, genius, number one lion dancer in the entire universe?!

speaker: OwO
content: Why don't you obey my order? Help OwO look for the lion head!
The girl who was just making a scene in the middle of the street is now punching and kicking the air in the interrogation seat.
You used your special power casually and arbitrarily on the street just now. Are you going to deny that?

speaker: OwO
content: Hmph!
Or... Have you actually never heard of the rules and regulations concerning Sinners?

speaker: OwO
content: I don't talk to cowards who won't stand up for OwO!
She puffs her cheeks and turns her face away, uninterested in the topic of Sinners.
...Are you sure you lost your lion head in Syndicate?

speaker: OwO
content: I'm not answering you. You're not gonna help me find it anyway. You even took me away and locked me up! Bleh!
She sticks out her tongue and turns to face another direction rashly.
It looks like if you don't cheer OwO up first, the conversation won't go anywhere.

options: I can only help you if you answer my questions.
I was helping you by getting you out of there.

speaker: OwO
content: Huh?! You've gotten cocky since the last time I saw you! How dare you negotiate terms with OwO?

speaker: OwO
content: Huh?! You've gotten cocky since the last time I saw you! How dare you bend the truth in front of OwO?
...Well, you see, we haven't seen each other in a while.
During these days, other than the message on the postcard, I learned nothing about the corruption of your special power and your physical condition.
I don't know how and where you've been, what you've experienced. How am I supposed to help you... help the genius, pretty, world number one lion dancer deduce her lion head's whereabouts?

speaker: OwO
content: Hmm...
The improvised speech is a bit too lengthy for OwO. She considered for a long while before glancing at you a little skeptically.

speaker: OwO
content: It seems to... make a little bit of sense?
Then can the genius, pretty, world number one lion dancer tell me what exactly happened to you while I was away?
How did you get home? What did you encounter on the way? How come your special power seems to have intensified a lot in just a few months?

speaker: OwO
content: Must I answer so many questions just to find the lion head? That's annoying!
Well...
You glance at the half-blank Sinner file on hand and feel a little helpless. The little clapper has a job to do too.
All these questions are necessary for reconstructing how the lion head got lost. Um, right, it's all for the lion head.

speaker: OwO
content: Hmm... Alright, for the lion head! In that case, OwO will begin with how I found the way home!
She finally steadies her fidgeting limbs.

speaker: OwO
content: You know it, right? When I was escorting Stella home, I ran into some really, really bad guys!

speaker: OwO
content: OwO beat them heroically! I gained power! I became a... What's it called again... A...

speaker: OwO
content: Exactly! That's it! It sounds a bit lame though...

speaker: OwO
content: Hold on... Did the lion head get mad and run away because I didn't name it properly?

speaker: OwO
content: OwO wants to name it after I learn about more names, but it seems like we can't wait until then! What should I call it? ...Li-li? On-on?
The conversation is deviating from the original direction. You can only be patient and keep guiding her in the right way.
You beat the bad guys and became a Sinner. What happened next?

speaker: OwO
content: And then? Ohhhhhhh! And then, I used this ability to help a super big caravan! They saw OwO defeat the bad guys and said OwO is the strongest unbeatable superhero in the universe! Awesome like a thunderbolt !

speaker: OwO
content: <size=32>And very coincidentally, the caravan, which seems to be called something... something... they actually know where OwO is from! And they even traded with people there! They saw OwO's lion head and said it must be a specialty there, the Goldionville!</size>

speaker: OwO
content: But you certainly didn't expect... the bad guys who attacked the caravan to set us up! They had several very powerful guys to hunt down the remnants! And then!

speaker: OwO
content: Of course, OwO was not afraid of those guys! OwO pulled out the lion head! And transformed into the invincible super lion dancer! Then swish, swish, swish! Golden light and blue light explode together! I...
Hold on!

<size=29>The exhilarating swishes echo in the interrogation room. That blue light must the energy from Stella. It seems that OwO's Mania power is more than ever, probably because she got some kind of enchantment from the Apostle of Ashes. It's giving you a headache. Suddenly interrupted, OwO seems unamused.</size>

speaker: OwO
content: Why did you stop me? I just got to the most exciting part!
Because it's too exciting, I want to zoom into these "swish, swish, swish" parts. Please explain them in detail so I know how to compliment you concretely!
Your ample interrogation experience has turned you into a great improviser. Handling OwO should be a piece of cake for you.

speaker: OwO
content: Mmm... The details are not particularly important, but since you asked... Alright.

speaker: OwO
content: I suppose you understand that it's already a splendid achievement that OwO is the sole chosen inheritor of the art of lion dance! But... but even a genius has flaws.

speaker: OwO
content: OwO...

speaker: OwO
content: Has always hidden behind others.
OwO's voice sounds a bit muffled. She looks down at the hem of her patchwork skirt. On her waist, the longevity lock loaded with blessings jingles softly as she fidgets.

speaker: OwO
content: Every time something bad happens, OwO always gets tucked behind others. Whether it's Deren or the other assistants under you, everyone always stands in front of OwO.

speaker: OwO
content: But that one time, OwO and that group of powerless people faced those bad guys on our own.

speaker: OwO
content: I didn't know them, but something bad had just happened to them, and they treated OwO with so much trust and kindness...
She gets serious uncharacteristically, looking into your eyes seriously.

speaker: OwO
content: I want to become someone who can stand in the front! I want to be like Deren, you, and those assistants under you, to stand in the front!

speaker: OwO
content: What's that word, in...pendent?
Independent?

speaker: OwO
content: Right! I want to be independent just like everyone else. Suddenly, OwO feels like the power within me has become even stronger!

speaker: OwO
content: OwO can protect Stella! I can protect you guys too! I can protect everyone in the Drifter Camp!

speaker: OwO
content: I wanted to tell you guys this, that's why I...!
She holds her breath, looking slightly aggrieved with her reddened face.
That's why you came back to Syndicate, right?
test
test
test
test
test
test
The good news you wanted to tell me is that you now have power as strong as a Sinner's, and you're independent now, am I right?

speaker: OwO
content: I... OwO doesn't know much about Sinners and all that. I just want to show off and look cool, I didn't know... something like that could happen...
Suddenly deflated, she pouts her lips and darts her gaze away.
What happened?

speaker: OwO
content: Wh-when I arrived in Syndicate, I-I took a break around there... Then, I was just...
You were just?
The usually high-spirited OwO looks uncharacteristically embarrassed and hesitant now.

speaker: OwO
content: I was just distracted for a second, and when I turned around, it, it was already...
The lion head was already gone?

speaker: OwO
content: Hmm... It's all your fault! I wanted to make the coolest comeback! And now I've even lost my lion head! Not! Cool! At all!
Didn't you lose it yourself...

speaker: OwO
content: I don't care! If you'd helped me just now, I would have already found it!

speaker: OwO
content: It's all your fault because you just had to drag me back and ask me a million questions... Ah, hold on!
She looks as if she's just found out about some shocking news.

speaker: OwO
content: Th-the questions you asked have nothing to do with finding the lion head!

speaker: OwO
content: Waah... The lion head, my lion head... The thief has probably already turned it into a dish by now... Sob...

speaker: OwO
content: Sob... I order you! Go and look for the lion head! Right! Now!
...What happened to being independent?

speaker: OwO
content: Mind your attitude when you talk to the genius lion dancer! Don't forget your place!
Yes, yes. I'm the little clapper who's in charge of cleaning up messes.

speaker: OwO
content: Go, find the lion head! Off to Syndicate!
I've still got a lot of work to finish...

speaker: OwO
content: Exactly, the little clapper's work is to help me find the lion head! Off to Syndicate!

She blew her nose, hopped off the interrogation seat before you could protest, and walked out of the room pompously. To save the Bureau from being bombarded by thunderous roars, you have no choice but to follow her.
It looks like the little clapper is forced to play house with the lion dance star before you find the lion head...

speaker: Pedestrian A
content: Why is that little girl back again? Isn't that person behind her the one who arrested her last time?

speaker: Pedestrian B
content: She didn't come to wreck more things, did she? I've run out of flowerpots she can smash...

The minute you and OwO return to the neighborhood she wreaked havoc in, you receive many weird looks. But OwO is unbothered by these complaints as she now has her whole mind focused on finding her lion head.

speaker: OwO
content: It's about this big, this long, this wide...
She gestures animatedly in front of an old woman passing by.

speaker: Old Woman
content: I'm sorry, sweetheart, but I have poor vision. I'm afraid I haven't seen the world's most glamorous and beautiful lion head you describe.
OwO doesn't get discouraged and continues to knock on the next door.

speaker: OwO
content: I passed by that charcuterie across the street carrying it! I went in for a look, and when I came out, the lion head was already gone.

speaker: Resident
content: No, never seen it! There are too many drooling kids passing by the charcuterie every day. How can I remember every single one of them?
Another door is slammed shut in her face. OwO grimaces indignantly at it.

speaker: OwO
content: I-I wasn't drooling! You're the one drooling! Bleh!
Did you ask the charcuterie?

speaker: OwO
content: OwO is not stupid, of course it was the first place I went to. I asked many, many times, but every time, they said they haven't seen it! Then they kicked OwO out.
How is that possible? The lion head is so big and eye-catching. Even if someone had stolen it, they couldn't have stashed it right away. Someone must have seen it...
True, the lion head is so big and eye-catching. Someone must have seen it.

speaker: OwO
content: Hmm?
OwO tilts her head, holds up her two pigtail buns, and follows the voice.

speaker: OwO
content: Who's talking? Like hiding, don't you?!
Hehe, I'm just an old tramp who picks up trash around here...
A hunchbacked old man in ragged clothes strolls out of the hidden bin with a fawning smile on his face.

speaker: Old Tramp
content: Are you looking for the world's most glamorous and beautiful lion head that's about this wide and this big?
The old man simply repeats what OwO just described to someone else, and she immediately falls for it.

speaker: OwO
content: Have you seen it? Where is it? Where is it!

speaker: Old Tramp
content: Obviously, that little punk stole it. That kid has no parents to watch over him. He goes around picking pockets every day and survives on help from the neighbors.

speaker: Old Tramp
content: That dumb kid must have thought that lion head was some rare treasure and nicked it.

speaker: OwO
content: The lion head is indeed a super rare treasure!
OwO argues vehemently, still not realizing the oddness in the old man's words.
This is all just your guess, right? Did you really see him take the lion head?

speaker: Old Tramp
content: Ahaha, why don't you go and see for yourself? That's the only clue you have now. Isn't it better than hovering around here like a headless chicken?

speaker: OwO
content: I'm a headless lioness, not a headless chicken!
From what you're saying, you know where this thief is now?

speaker: Old Tramp
content: Of course...
The old man smiles and holds out a hand, palm up, lifting it at you twice.

speaker: OwO
content: What's that? A secret code for the address?
OwO frowns and imitates the old man's gesture, trying to crack the mysterious message in it.
...How much?

speaker: Old Tramp
content: Not much, five hundred.

speaker: Old Tramp
content: Tsk tsk, you don't want to upset this little girl here, do you?
It's pointless to waste more time with someone like him, so you eventually take out five hundred DisCoins. The old man grabs the money with one hand and shows you the way with the other.
You take out the exact amount of DisCoins from your pocket and put the money in the old man's palm. He doesn't hesitate to take the money with one hand and show you the way with the other.

speaker: Old Tramp
content: Ahem. Walk straight to the end and you'll find a hidden alley. That kid likes to hide all his loot in that godforsaken corner.
Counting the cash, the old man staggers back to the end of the street. OwO is still pondering his hand gesture.

speaker: OwO
content: So, what does that gesture even mean? What did you just give him?
Nothing, leave this kind of trivial matter to the clapper. Let's go and have a look at this place he told us about.

speaker: OwO
content: Right, the thief. Let's go catch the thief!
You've distracted OwO effortlessly. She now walks triumphantly ahead, while you are still skeptical about this clue you traded with five hundred DisCoins.
Then again, as suspicious as that old man was, he was right about one thing. That boy is the only clue you have now.

speaker: OwO
content: I see it! OwO's lion head!
Just as you reach the beginning of the alley, OwO shouts excitedly and jogs deeper into it.
You quickly catch up with her, but are suddenly blocked by OwO who stopped short not far from her destination.
Why stop here? Where's the lion head you saw?

speaker: OwO
content: Shhh!
OwO yanks your sleeve to stop you from making any sound. You follow her gaze and see that behind a pile of scrap, OwO's lion head is bobbing up and down rhythmically.
Beneath the lion head is a filthy, short, scrawny body that looks like it's going to get crushed by the head.
The body beneath the lion head is strenuously maneuvering the lion head to squat down and hop up, making tender grunts whenever he exerts himself.

speaker: OwO
content: Is he... imitating me?
They're the most basic up and down movements and very poorly attempted, but OwO's eyes can't help chasing the lion head up and down.
That old man didn't lie. It's indeed here...
Normally, OwO would have lunged over yelling "Right! The old man said he's the thief!" But right now, OwO doesn't seem to even hear you.
She focuses entirely on watching the clumsy performance, her eyes brimming with excitement and curiosity.
You don't interrupt her and only peek at the boy's dance with her through the gaps in the scrap.

speaker: OwO
content: One, two, three, four...
Counting the beats softly, OwO seems even more nervous than the lion dancer himself.

When OwO said "imitating me", you thought she meant copying the overall format. But after a while, you realize the boy alters his moves according to a certain pattern. You seem to have seen this choreography before...
This is...?

speaker: OwO
content: This is the performance OwO did in the movie! He's seen OwO's movie!
OwO tries her best to lower her voice but fails to conceal her surprise.

speaker: OwO
content: It's coming, the most important final pose!
The small hand clutching your sleeve tightens.
Under your anticipating gaze, the boy tries hard to remember the steps, hops left and right hesitantly, then lifts the lion head over his head toward the sky.
The pose is done. You finally make out the boy's face too. On the small face covered in dirt, a pair of eyes stares at the lion head, glistening with anticipation.
He holds his breath and stays in that pose for five seconds, ten seconds, half a minute...

speaker: OwO
content: What’s he waiting for?
Didn't you choreograph this lion dance? Shouldn't you know?

speaker: OwO
content: Oh, but the dance ends here. In the movie, that's the moment when OwO gains the lion head's power and turns into a superhero!

speaker: OwO
content: Hey, don't tell me you've never watched OwO's lion dance movie! How come you don't know what happens next?
Ahem, of course I have...

speaker: Boy
content: Liar!!
The boy suddenly cries out furiously, interrupting your chit-chat.

speaker: Boy
content: Nothing happens! It's all just a lie!
Before you can react to the boy's sudden rage, he lifts the lion head high and is about to smash it to the ground...

speaker: OwO
content: Ahhh! Stop, you stinking thief!

OwO screams and lunges out almost instinctively. Luckily, with her Mania-enhanced physical abilities and agility gained from years of lion dance practice, she manages to catch the lion head in that precarious moment.

speaker: OwO
content: Do you even know what you're doing?! This is the one and only extraordinarily glamorous and beautiful lion head in DisCity!
OwO is covered in dirt from the fall, but she only grabs the lion head and examines it carefully while cursing.

speaker: OwO
content: You're lucky it's not damaged. Otherwise, I'm definitely taking you to Goldionville where you'll work your butt off to make me ten lion heads to compensate for my loss!

speaker: Boy
content: You... You're...
The boy seems shocked by OwO's sudden appearance. He looks at OwO, then at you who come out from behind the heaps of scrap, then back at OwO.

speaker: Boy
content: You're that... from the movie...

speaker: OwO
content: Hehe, at least you're not blind! That's right, I'm the world's number one genius lion dance que...

speaker: Boy
content: Liar! You're that big fat liar from the movie!

speaker: OwO
content: Huh?!
OwO chokes on the words "Lion Dance Queen," and the anger almost making her jump.

speaker: OwO
content: You, you, you! You thief!

speaker: Boy
content: Liar!

speaker: OwO
content: Stinking thief!

speaker: Boy
content: Big fat liar!

The boy may look scrawny, but he speaks with a loud voice. It's the first time OwO has argued with someone even louder and more stubborn than herself. Feeling both anxious and aggrieved, she stomps behind you.
Trapped between two quarreling kids, you feel like your head is close to exploding.

speaker: OwO
content: OwO is not a liar! Waah!

speaker: Boy
content: That's exactly what you are! "Lion dance brings you the power to return home"? It's all crap!

speaker: OwO
content: I didn't lie! I did find my way home! Sob... Say something, little clapper!

speaker: Boy
content: Then why didn't I find it?!

speaker: Boy
content: I copied what you did, with your lion head! I did the exact same thing! Then why did nothing happen?

speaker: Boy
content: I got nothing! No darn power! No home! No friends! No Mom! No Dad!
The boy yells at you two at the top of his voice.

speaker: Boy
content: Liar! Both you and your lion head are just a lie!
OwO seems in shock. Tears still streaming down, she hugs her lion head tightly and stares at the boy blankly with red eyes.

speaker: OwO
content: You, you...
She asks, the question punctuated by her uncontrollable whimpers.

speaker: OwO
content: You... want... to go home?
Seeing the stupefied OwO, the boy turns his face away in frustration, biting his lip.

speaker: Boy
content: Yeah... But I don't know... I can't find it.
When he finishes, he seems to have completely lost the mood to yell at OwO. He slumps beside the pile of scrap and bows his head dejectedly.

speaker: OwO
content: I, I'm not a liar! I really do have the lion head's power. I'm very powerful.
Though still teary, she seems to have restored most of her pride. OwO pokes her head out from behind you and takes a tentative step toward the boy, hugging her lion head.

speaker: OwO
content: I'm... the world number one extraordinarily powerful Lion Dancing Queen OwO!
She pats her own chest with one hand. The boy frowns and stares at OwO, probably guessing what she's getting at.

speaker: OwO
content: I'll help you find your home!

speaker: OwO
content: If I could find my home, I must be able to find yours too! Right, little clapper?
Huh? Oh, Yeah!

speaker: Nightingale
content: It's a considerably long ride to your destination from the MBCC. We have stationed staff on standby at the stops along the route. Please contact them in time if you need anything.
After another five minutes of reminders, Nightingale finally ends the call for now.
An adult who always walks straight into danger alone is taking two half-fledged kids to an unknown village outside the city. You suppose this trip does warrant Nightingale's concerns.
Though you've retrieved the lion head, your work as the clapper slash chauffeur slash guardian is not done yet. You can't really let the two of them go on this unknown journey back home on their own.

speaker: Boy
content: My name is Bagley.

speaker: OwO
content: Bugley? Bergley? Um, not as cool as OwO which both sounds good and is easy to remember!

speaker: Bagley
content: Hmph, what kind of name is OwO anyway? It's more like an interjection! My name has a meaning!
Clearly unaware of your resignation and worry, the two initiators of this trip keep bickering non-stop.

speaker: OwO
content: OwO means OwO! Well, explain the meaning of your name then!

speaker: Bagley
content: I don't remember.

speaker: Bagley
content: When I was only a baby, my parents hid me in a caravan's truck as a stowaway, so I ended up in DisCity alone. I didn't have a chance to learn our language.
Bagley leans by the car window and looks out to the boundless white sand.

speaker: Bagley
content: I only know it was a caravan heading toward the southeast of DisCity. My home must be in that direction.

speaker: Bagley
content: It's a part of the desert where grass grows. Beautiful violet flowers bloom along the road too.
Bagley stops after that. Perhaps that's all he can remember...

speaker: OwO
content: What's so special about grass in the desert? OwO can even beat bad guys on the sand!

speaker: Bagley
content: Is that some fake movie plot again?

speaker: OwO
content: It's not from a movie, it's a true story! It happened on my way home, all of a sudden!

speaker: OwO
content: A bunch of bearded men appeared out of nowhere!
OwO clears her throat and speaks in a deeper voice, imitating the tones of the bearded villains.

speaker: OwO
content: Ahem, you kid over there. Right, I'm talking to you! The one with the lion head who looks super badass!

speaker: OwO
content: Hand over Starbeast now and we'll spare you!

speaker: Bagley
content: I'm pretty sure they didn't say "super badass"...

speaker: OwO
content: Pff, I'll never lie about such a thing! Anyway, I chased them away with my lion head!

speaker: OwO
content: Just like this, I held the lion head and stood in front of Starbeast, saying to myself secretly...

speaker: OwO
content: I must become an inpendent hero!
Independent...

speaker: OwO
content: That's right! I must become a dependent hero!

speaker: OwO
content: Then, with a swish, a warm golden ray of light poured down from the lion's head.

speaker: OwO
content: In that moment, the lion head became so light, as if it was weightless! Also in that moment, it felt like a voice was talking to me in my head!

speaker: Bagley
content: What did it say?
Bagley was looking out the car window, but he turns back now, captivated by OwO's story.

speaker: OwO
content: It said...
As if going to leak an incredible secret, OwO leans into Bagley's ear.

speaker: OwO
content: It said, "OwO, scare them away with your loud voice!"

speaker: Bagley
content: Did it work?

speaker: OwO
content: Of course, it's the lion head's power we're talking about! Swish! My power hit those bearded men and toppled them over!
Bagley stares at the lion head, his eyes bright with the light of anticipation once again.
Sensing the enthusiasm in her only audience, OwO immediately renders a dramatized, exaggerated retelling of her journey back to Goldionville.

speaker: Bagley
content: So... You didn't lie, you really found your way home with the power of lion dance?

speaker: OwO
content: Of course. The lion really brought me home, no kidding!

speaker: OwO
content: I saw all kinds of lion heads back home! They come in different colors and patterns. There are also some lion cubs suitable for a stick like you!

speaker: Bagley
content: I'm not a stick! I just... have a smaller appetite!

speaker: OwO
content: That has to change! Being a lion dancer is physically demanding! You must eat plenty, sleep well, and train diligently!

speaker: Bagley
content: If my native culture was as cool, I certainly wouldn't mind eating and sleeping well!

speaker: OwO
content: You're interested in lion dance? Good taste! Do you wanna be the prodigy OwO's lion tail? I'll consider it if you call me Master!

speaker: Bagley
content: Who says I want to be your apprentice? My native culture might be even cooler than yours!

speaker: OwO
content: Nothing is cooler than lion dance in this world! If you think there is, that's because you've never seen an eye-dotting ceremony!

speaker: Bagley
content: Eye-dotting ceremony?

speaker: OwO
content: A ceremony where you draw the last few strokes on the lion head to wake the lion! The dots drawn in different positions have different meanings!

speaker: OwO
content: When I was very little, I once heard my dad and his friends chant a rhyme over drinks. I think it goes like this...
OwO can't even get the word "independent" right, but when it comes to lion dance, it's as if the knowledge flows through her veins, and she recites the rhyme unthinkingly.

speaker: OwO
content: First dot on the left eye, brilliant as gold. Second dot on the right eye, shiny as silver. Third dot on the brow, the lucky star is forever bright above. Fourth dot on the mouth, the world finds peace and prospers...
Amid the repeated chant of blessings, the off-roader carries the three of you through the boundless white sand, heading southeast.
OwO has turned into quite a chatterbox with her new companion, sharing with him her childhood memories of Goldionville and what she saw during her last visit.

speaker: OwO
content: Did you know that lion costumes come in different colors? Gold, black, blue... They all have different meanings.

speaker: OwO
content: Around this time of year, Goldionville is the most festive. You can see lions with all kinds of different eyes dancing in various places at the same time!

speaker: OwO
content: This festival is called the New Year in Goldionville! With the lion's power, we kick out all the bad stuff and welcome the auspicious, lively new year!
Speaking of Goldionville's New Year, OwO jumps up and down excitedly in the car, as if she's really seeing those endless red lanterns and firecrackers she's describing.
Bagley listens to OwO's sharing enviously, but still seems a bit confused.

speaker: Bagley
content: If the festival is so much fun and so exciting... then why did you come back?

speaker: Bagley
content: You went through so much and finally found your wonderful home. If I were you, I would never leave again.
The boy's innocent curiosity brings out that question you never get the chance to ask. You wait for OwO's answer quietly, but she seems truly baffled and begins thinking as she thumbs her chin.

speaker: OwO
content: Hmm, why did I come back... To tell everyone I'm already an inpendent grown-up now?

speaker: Bagley
content: You can do that by sending letters and postcards?

speaker: OwO
content: Right, so there must be a reason why I have to come back...

speaker: Bagley
content: Ah, look!
Bagley's surprised shout interrupts OwO's thoughts.

speaker: Bagley
content: Violet flowers by the road! The flowers that grow around my home!

speaker: OwO
content: Ah! How tiny it is! It's really there! Stop the car, little clapper!

speaker: Bagley
content: We're here! We've found it!
Before you stop the car properly, Bagley jumps off eagerly and lunges toward the tiny flowers on the roadside.
Several slightly shriveled violet flowers peek out from the sand, the sandy wind brought by the disaster almost draining the last bit of life out of them.
Perhaps it's really a lucky miracle that leads Bagley here to see these flowers. After all, they're really hard to notice in this desert.

speaker: Bagley
content: Yes, this is it! I was stashed at the bottom of the truck when I left with the caravan. I remember seeing this flower outside the village!
This is the closest Bagley has been to his home in so many years. He's too thrilled to speak properly, scrambling to straighten those wilting stems.

speaker: Bagley
content: The village must be nearby. I'm sure!
You and OwO follow Bagley off the car, but stay silent. You both have already spotted the so-called village.
It's an utterly quiet ruin under the curtain of sand.
Unlike in Bagley's memories, there are no oases here, let alone villagers who work in them.
The cracked land and dry weeds are all there's left in this empty reality.
Bagley must have seen what you've seen as well. But he simply bows his head and focuses on protecting the small flowers, mumbling repeatedly.

speaker: Bagley
content: I've finally found it! It's right here! I'm home!
You and OwO look around the abandoned village and knock on almost every one of the dusty doors, but you don't find any trace of life here.
Bagley doesn't follow you into the village. Perhaps he can't bear ruining those only memories he holds, he just stays outside the village, squatting there and guarding those flowers.

speaker: OwO
content: Bagley...
Even OwO, who's always bubbly, doesn't know how to break it to Bagley that no one lives in his village anymore. She can only hold the lion head and slump beside Bagley.

speaker: Bagley
content: OwO, I'm sorry...
Just when OwO is still debating how to tell Bagley, the boy stares at the flowers blankly and begins.

speaker: OwO
content: If it's about stealing the lion's head, forget it. I've gotten over it.

speaker: Bagley
content: No... I shouldn't have called you a liar... The lion head's power indeed exists.

speaker: OwO
content: But... But it seems like OwO didn't help you find anything at all.

speaker: Bagley
content: It's not your fault. It's not the lion head's fault either. Just that my home...
Bagley's shoulders shake dejectedly, his teardrops landing on the violet petals.

speaker: OwO
content: Eh, s-s-stop crying!

speaker: OwO
content: Maybe they've just moved somewhere else and haven't got the time to find you yet!

speaker: OwO
content: Look, there isn't even a drop of water around here. This is no place to live in!
OwO is used to receiving consolation but has never consoled others before, so her improvised excuse is pretty clumsy.

speaker: Bagley
content: I was sent away to DisCity to escape the disaster. Where else could they have moved to other than DisCity? Why haven't they come look for me? Why has no one told me anything...
Whimpering, Bagley refutes OwO's flimsy assumption.

speaker: Bagley
content: I don't need your pity... There are no disasters to hide from in OwO's home. You came back to DisCity because you like it here. They're both your homes. But it's different for me...

speaker: Bagley
content: I don't like DisCity! I just want to go home, even more than you do. This place is all I have, but...
A little stupefied, he looks up at the sandy wind decaying his birthplace, and his tears overflow uncontrollably.

speaker: Bagley
content: But even this place is no more...
OwO follows Bagley's gaze and looks toward the empty village, still a little bewildered.
Even though she has pushed open every door in there and witnessed up close the desolation and silence, she still can't comprehend Bagley's sadness.
Her home in DisCity will always welcome her with the heater and snacks, and every family in Goldionville has warmly received the girl who protected the caravan.
Indeed, she doesn't understand what it's like to lose her home. Getting ambushed by the bearded men trying to snatch Starbeast is already the biggest challenge she's ever faced in her life.
But she can somehow understand... Back then in DisCity, when she stood alone and watched the other kids, she understood that the congested feeling that made her want to cry was called loneliness.
OwO turns back and walks toward you sullenly, burying her head into your coat.

speaker: OwO
content: Can't! Do! It! OwO can't cheer him up. Who knows there's something even the lion dance genius can't achieve?
Should the little clapper go and clean up the mess now?

speaker: OwO
content: Don't make me ask!
OwO's voice sounds dull and she seems sulky.
I know a way to cheer him up, but I shouldn't be the one doing it.

speaker: OwO
content: Why?
OwO looks up from your coat, the tip of her nose still red.
Because he's OwO's friend.

speaker: OwO
content: ...OwO's friend.
She repeats the words a few times, then finally nods firmly.

speaker: OwO
content: That's right, OwO should do it!
She rubs her face on your coat again. Once she collects herself, she holds out a hand to you palm up and lifts it twice.

speaker: OwO
content: Tell me how!
The sandy wind has dried Bagley's tears. With two pale tear stains on his face, he sits beside the violet flowers and stares blankly at the village far ahead.

speaker: OwO
content: I know a story about your village. Want to hear it?
The chatty girl hovers over to sit beside Bagley again. Bagley doesn't answer.

speaker: OwO
content: No answer means yes!

speaker: OwO
content: Did you know this flower is called pearly? Does this name ring any bells with you?

speaker: Bagley
content: I've heard of it before...

speaker: OwO
content: Because Pearly is also the name of this village!

speaker: Bagley
content: That sounds... right.
Bagley can't remember it very clearly.

speaker: OwO
content: That's right, pearlies are unique to this village. They've grown here since a long, long time ago.

speaker: OwO
content: Not only are they beautiful, but they are also the raw material of a useful dye!

speaker: OwO
content: The villagers introduced this dye to DisCity, and DisCity introduced it to the rest of the world.

speaker: OwO
content: Even now, pearlies are used to make colorings in many places!
Bagley seems a bit bewildered by this information about his home. He never knew that this tiny flower he held so close to his heart grew in other places as well.

speaker: OwO
content: Goldionville was named after the big golden lion who guarded the village and brought good auspices.

speaker: OwO
content: People from your village must have named the village after these tiny flowers because pearlies brought them hope! That's the tradition and culture of your village!

speaker: Bagley
content: Pearlies, and the Pearly village...
Bagley keeps repeating this strange yet familiar name a little glumly, touching the fragile petals tentatively.

speaker: OwO
content: It was the hope of the village, and it will be your hope too!
OwO grabs Bagley's hand and guides him to touch the petals boldly.

speaker: OwO
content: See, your touch won't damage it! It may look shriveled, but it's in fact very tough! Look how it survives this harsh environment and lives on with everyone's hope!

speaker: OwO
content: Pearlies are super tough flowers! The Pearly village is a super awesome dye manufacturer!

speaker: Bagley
content: The whole world uses this dye... Which means... like me, there must be some people traveled to different parts of the world, with this flower!

speaker: Bagley
content: Wherever there's the pearly dye, there are pearlies and the hope of the Pearly village!

speaker: OwO
content: Exactly! The hope of the Pearly village is everywhere! Your home is not gone, it's only turned into these pearlies and now they bloom in many different places in the world!
The two kids get excited with the talk and both stand up to take a better look at this ancient village.

speaker: Bagley
content: Do the flowers remember the villagers?

speaker: OwO
content: Of course they do! Just like OwO's lion head must remember OwO!

speaker: Bagley
content: Then do they remember my mom and dad too?

speaker: OwO
content: Yes! OwO's lion head was passed on to me from my great-great-great-grandfather. It remembers everything!

speaker: Bagley
content: How do I find these flowers in DisCity?

speaker: OwO
content: Find them? Aren't they right here before you? We can bring them back and grow them ourselves!

speaker: OwO
content: Do you remember what you asked me? If it's so nice back home, why did I come back to DisCity?

speaker: OwO
content: You're right. I like it there. I like the people there! I like the neighbors, Deren, and little clapper!

speaker: OwO
content: Although I left home, I don't feel lonely at all!
OwO smiles at you and pats the lion head in her arms.

speaker: OwO
content: The lion head is the seed of Goldionville. Wherever OwO brings it to is home!

speaker: OwO
content: If I want it to be DisCity, then DisCity it'll be...
OwO dances with the lion head on the sand, screaming recklessly. Her shrill, childish laughter blends into the sandy wind, somehow turning into a pleasant sound.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: DisCity it'll be. I'll take it back to DisCity.
Bagley carefully digs out a whole pearly plant from the sand and cups it in his palms.

speaker: Bagley
content: I must plant the pearly in a sunny place.
They laugh and play, chasing each other in this desolate desert. You only begin to head back once these two little ones are both completely exhausted.
In the rear-view mirror, you see the two of them try to stay up and bicker despite their sleepy eyes, one holding the flower and the other hugging the lion head.

speaker: OwO
content: My lion dance is no doubt cooler than your dye.

speaker: Bagley
content: You literally just lost your lion head.

speaker: OwO
content: Mind your attitude when you talk to the genius pretty lion dancer. I may consider teaching you a move or two if I'm in a good mood.

speaker: Bagley
content: As if I want to learn it. I'll be busy with planting the flowers and making dye.

speaker: OwO
content: And you'll give me some for the eye-dotting ceremony.

speaker: Bagley
content: Ha, that will depend on the price you offer.

speaker: OwO
content: I've got my awesome little clapper who knows everything. He's the one who told me about Pearly. You can't fool me.
female_content: I've got my awesome little clapper who knows everything. She's the one who told me about Pearly. You can't fool me.

speaker: OwO
content: Little clapper, pay up! I need to dot the eyes for my extraordinarily gorgeous lion's head!

speaker: OwO
content: First dot on the left eye, brilliant as gold. Second dot on the right eye, shiny as silver...

speaker: OwO
content: Third dot on the brow, the lucky star is forever bright above. Fourth dot on the mouth, the world finds peace and prospers...
Bagley has already fallen asleep. OwO closes her eyes drowsily, mumbling something in her dream. She hugs her lion head even more tightly than when she's awake.

speaker: OwO
content: Little clapper... I've remembered it...

speaker: OwO
content: That word...

speaker: OwO
content: In... de... pendent...

speaker: OwO
content: Zzz... Zzz...

██, ██, N.F.113
MBCC Headquarters,
Chief's Office

speaker: 9th Agency Member
content: So, you believe that Nirvana, or perhaps someone behind them, was the driving force behind the two Rustfire crises in N.F. 104 and N.F. 113, correct?

speaker: 9th Agency Member
content: What a dangerous speculation. But it's not surprising that you would think that way.

speaker: 9th Agency Member
content: After all, you yourself got entangled in it. Even death could be exploited…

speaker: %u
content: It's not that complicated. All I want is the truth.

speaker: 9th Agency Member
content: The truth, huh…

speaker: 9th Agency Member
content: How many of those who chase the truth at all costs can actually afford its price?

speaker: 9th Agency Member
content: And what do you plan to do once you find it? Make the big shot who pulled the trigger on you pay in blood?

speaker: 9th Agency Member
content: Easy, it's just a joke.

speaker: 9th Agency Member
content: Regardless, the puppet master won't be an easy opponent...

speaker: 9th Agency Member
content: Please pay close attention to your new guest.

speaker: %u
content: I will...

You know who the man is warning you about. That S-Class Sinner from the FAC who turned up following an abrupt staff transfer. In fact, you've been on your guard since the day Rahu arrived at the MBCC.

speaker: 9th Agency Member
content: It seems you've already figured it out.
The official from the 9th Agency takes out a well-sealed document from his briefcase and places it on the office desk with a smile.

speaker: 9th Agency Member
content: This is what you're looking for... The 9th Agency won't prevent you from probing for the so-called truth. But remember…

speaker: 9th Agency Member
content: Stay safe.

speaker: Rahu
content: State your purpose.
Under the bright light, the woman's face is shrouded in shadow.

speaker: Rahu
content: You call this a routine interrogation?
Rahu looks around. The cramped interrogation room is filled only with the hum of cold surveillance equipment and halogen lamps.

speaker: %u
content: You've accepted your transfer to the MBCC and you're an S-Class Sinner. Undergoing this form of investigation is your duty.
Rahu looks into your eyes, and after a moment, a cold, emotionless smile appears on her face.

speaker: Rahu
content: Yes, <color=#fb9259><size=40>Commander</size></color>.
You take out a document envelope labeled with Rahu's name and place it on the table.

speaker: Choice
options: Tell me about your experience at the FAC.

content: Rahu glances at the envelope on the table.

speaker: Rahu
content: Why ask if you already know?

speaker: %u
content: Files often contain omissions and errors. I'd like to hear your version.
Rahu doesn't waste more time and begins to talk about her past.

speaker: Rahu
content: I was born in Syndicate, and was recruited by the FAC in N.F. 102. I'd worked for the FAC for a total of 11 years since.

speaker: Rahu
content: Until last week. The higher-ups thought I could be of more use here.
Rahu doesn't seem too pleased when she mentions the higher-ups' decision.

speaker: %u
content: Is that all? Can you go into more detail?

speaker: Rahu
content: What kind of detail?

speaker: %u
content: For instance, the reason you joined the FAC.

speaker: Rahu
content: Reason?
Rahu laughs, as if it's an unwarranted, foolish question that's been asked too many times.

speaker: Rahu
content: Ha... To survive.

speaker: Rahu
content: Life in Syndicate is more dangerous than in the FAC.

speaker: %u
content: As far as I know, the FAC doesn't often recruit from the West District. How did you come on their radar?

speaker: Rahu
content: A squad was carrying out a mission in Syndicate at the time. I met their captain, who referred me to the raw recruit camp for trial training.

speaker: %u
content: And the captain's name is?
Rahu pauses for a moment, then casually says.

speaker: Rahu
content: I don't remember.

speaker: %u
content: Really?
She's lying.
The file states that after completing her training, Rahu joined that captain's squad. For almost two years, they participated in over twenty operations together.

speaker: %u
content: As far as I know, you were part of that captain's squad up until the squad was wiped out in N.F. 103.

speaker: %u
content: You've repeatedly demanded the truth about the DisSea catastrophe from your superiors. You've even gone as far as barging into the FAC executives' office and making a scene. Cost you two demerits on the record.

speaker: %u
content: Now, tell me again you don't remember the name of that officer?
Rahu doesn't respond and just stares intently at the file in your hand for a long time.
After a long silence, she suddenly begins.

speaker: Rahu
content: Post-traumatic stress disorder... I've received treatment from the FAC.

speaker: Rahu
content: What I don't need to remember, what I shouldn't remember, I don't. This is better for me, and for everyone else.
Rahu's statements are consistent with the records in the file.
Clearly, the counter-interrogation training she received at the FAC wasn't wasted. Dwelling on this topic is pointless, and might even result in accusations of veteran persecution.
But you know she's not telling the truth, or at least not all of it. You casually flip through the file, trying to move past the previous topic.

speaker: %u
content: I'm glad you were able to move on from that experience.

speaker: Rahu
content: ...Glad?
Rahu questions, and you can detect a barely noticeable hint of anger in her tone.
Even though she's the one who brought up things like "having received treatment" and "better for everyone," her irritation at your words still peeks through the careful concealment.

speaker: %u
content: We're not enemies here, Rahu. We're now colleagues who are about to begin a long-term working relationship.

speaker: %u
content: Your eleven years at the FAC have proven your loyalty and capability. As long as you can clear up the minor flaws on your record, I would naturally be grateful to have such an excellent subordinate.
You explain. Meanwhile, you abruptly stop flipping the file, landing on the last page.

speaker: %u
content: In July N.F. 113, you left the FAC headquarters to go to Erica Villa. What for?
Taken aback by your sudden change of topic, Rahu hesitates slightly, but quickly recovers.

speaker: Rahu
content: Vacation.

speaker: %u
content: That's not a vacation spot for ordinary people.

speaker: Rahu
content: ...It was a private matter. I'm not answering that.

speaker: %u
content: You were there to meet someone, weren't you?

speaker: %u
content: You went to Erica Villa behind the back of your colleagues at the FAC, and there you met a certain big shot...

speaker: Rahu
content: Haha, I underestimated you...
Rahu's snicker interrupts you.

speaker: Rahu
content: The intelligence unit of the MBCC is quite something. What a bold move.
Rahu's smile disappears without a trace, leaving only a cold stare.

speaker: Rahu
content: But you better keep your subordinates in check. Don't overreach yourselves.
The threat in her words is clear, and you respond calmly.

speaker: %u
content: That's none of your concern. My sources are quite reliable.

speaker: Rahu
content: The 9th Agency, right?
You ignore Rahu's almost provocative question and continue with the previous topic.

speaker: %u
content: What was your real purpose for going to Erica Villa?

speaker: Rahu
content: Why don't you ask your reliable sources?

speaker: %u
content: I want to hear it from you.

speaker: Rahu
content: They sent out a distress signal on the public channel. I received it, and then I went. It's as simple as that.

speaker: %u
content: Before responding to the distress signal, did you know a high-ranking official from Paradeisos was in Erica Villa?
Rahu looks directly at you, as if she's scrutinizing you for your motive. After a few seconds of silence, she suddenly bursts into laughter.

speaker: Rahu
content: Haha, will you take no for an answer?

speaker: Rahu
content: Of course, I did. If the Paradeisian official wasn't there, why should I care if they were dead or alive?

speaker: %u
content: So you went for the Paradeisian official in the first place? Why?

speaker: Rahu
content: To butter them up so I could leave the FAC. Why else?

speaker: %u
content: You'd been serving in the FAC for over ten years, why the sudden switch?

speaker: Rahu
content: It wasn't sudden. I'd been wanting to change jobs for a while.
Her tone no longer carries the tension of someone being interrogated, but is instead filled with casual mockery and indifference, as if she sees through you.

speaker: Rahu
content: Indeed, I had served in the FAC for over ten years and participated in hundreds of operations, big and small. Since BR-002, my colleagues came and went. Those older and younger than me have all died, none of them had a good end.

speaker: Rahu
content: I want to live. Those mercs working as bodyguards for Paradeisos make it to retirement alive, why can't we FAC soldiers do the same? Have we not shed enough blood already?

speaker: Rahu
content: A job from a Paradeisian bigwig can't be that bad.
Rahu leans back slightly and you hear the creaks of the chair.

speaker: %u
content: What about your squad? You just left them behind like that?

speaker: Rahu
content: Not all of us are saints, ${PlayerName}. FAC soldiers are nothing more than ordinary people who feel lucky to survive another day.

speaker: Rahu
content: Having been through so many brutal battles, it's only natural that one would want to plan ahead.

speaker: Rahu
content: Not to mention that I don't owe them anything. I'm not irreplaceable to them either.
Rahu's voice is cold, and the facts she states are consistent with the records. Ethically speaking, she indeed had no obligation to stay in the FAC forever.
But something just doesn't sit right with you. Logically, what she says makes sense, but it doesn't exactly match her character.
These words seem like a bastion built of countless lies, so deliberately designed and seamless that it's virtually impossible to spot a crack.
Whoever this designer is, they must possess unimaginable power. Such means and power can't be found everywhere in DisCity.
The big shot from Paradeisos, the puppet master behind Rustfire, and the opportunity Rahu has mentioned. These elusive fragments are beginning to overlap in your mind.

speaker: %u
content: Did that Paradeisian official accept your proposal?
Rahu seems stumped by the question, caught off guard without a well-prepared response.

speaker: %u
content: Now you're here in the MBCC, not by the side of that big shot.

speaker: %u
content: Have you been abandoned?
Rahu's expression gradually turns icy.

speaker: %u
content: Or, is this the good job that big shot has offered you? Transferring to the MBCC?

speaker: %u
content: Let's see... You're an experienced and powerful combatant, an elite who can be entrusted with important tasks anywhere.

speaker: %u
content: Why give up such a capable assistant and send you to me?

speaker: %u
content: To kill me? No, too inefficient. To watch me? Possibly.

speaker: %u
content: But why would that big shot ignore the 9th Agency and directly monitor me instead? Is it about Rustfire? Or maybe it's related to the attack I suffered at the Drifter Camp...

speaker: Rahu
content: Hahaha...
The cold, abrupt snicker interrupts you.

speaker: Rahu
content: I've seen many like you who thought they could see through everything and grasp the truth.

speaker: Rahu
content: Guess what happened to them?
Rahu's smile is overlaid with a shadow.

speaker: %u
content: Are you threatening me?

speaker: Rahu
content: Consider this a threat if you will.

speaker: Rahu
content: Your curiosity is too brazen, whether it's about the truth or that big shot... Your thoughts are practically written all over your face.

speaker: Rahu
content: Stop deluding yourself that you can pursue the truth. Know your place, you're only the chief of this little bureau. Or else, you risk your life.

speaker: Rahu
content: You've been doing well so far. Stop now, and they might overlook this little misbehavior.

speaker: Rahu
content: But if you insist on pushing further, well...
Rahu looks up, her eyes flashing with a dangerous light.

speaker: Rahu
content: DisCity is built on the bones of those who betray and cross the line. No one can protect you, not even the 9th Agency.

speaker: Rahu
content: You're dealing with that kind of big shot.
Rahu's tone is incredibly calm, but what's hidden beneath the calm surface makes your hair stand on end for a moment.
You take a deep breath, trying to calm yourself.

speaker: %u
content: Thank you for your advice, Rahu.

speaker: %u
content: I think I can tame my curiosity. I can get the information I need without crossing the line.

speaker: %u
content: At least I won't end up like Conrad Cage.

speaker: Rahu
content: ...Conrad?
You catch a complex emotion flickering in Rahu's eyes at the mention of this name.

speaker: %u
content: Don't you know?

speaker: Rahu
content: I'm not sure what you mean by that.
Her face no longer changes, all emotions hidden behind those cold eyes.

content: Rings a bell, doesn't it?

content: Ten years ago, you belonged to the same squad. He was absent due to injury, and you were the only survivor of the battle.

speaker: %u

content: What happened to him?
Rahu interrupts you.

speaker: %u

content: According to the FAC, Conrad has been affected by Mania and is facing serious mental issues.

speaker: %u

speaker: %u

speaker: Rahu
content: And what does this have to do with me?

speaker: %u
content: Relax, you're not under suspicion yet. However...

speaker: %u
content: However, Conrad's treatment isn't going well. He's undergone rigorous psychological training in the past, which is now working against him. He specifically refuses treatment from doctors and has even shown highly aggressive behaviors.

speaker: %u
content: A professional institution has contacted the FAC, claiming they can take over him and provide him with appropriate treatment. However, the FAC hasn't accepted the offer yet.

speaker: %u
content: They're seeking help from us, an organization experienced in dealing with those infected with Mania... Perhaps because they know that you've recently been transferred here.

speaker: %u
content: Of course, I completely understand if you don't want to go. All I can do is try to get Conrad's version of the truth. Hopefully that'll at least help the FAC's medical department analyze the cause of his mental disorder...

content: I'll go.
Rahu's answer is curt but firm.

speaker: %u
content: Great.

speaker: %u
content: This is your first field assignment in the Bureau. Break a leg.
