options: True. I haven't seen nearly as much as you have.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But I've never met an Undergrounder who couldn't bear to hurt a human. Even with Thorn's gun in your face, you refused to harm him. You even went out of your way to protect him in secret, right there in the heart of the contamination.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Thorn was convinced that you killed Rust because he recognized something of "Rust's" on you. So I don't see a problem if I draw a different conclusion from the same clue.

speaker: Stranger
content: That's a rather... unconventional line of reasoning, Chief. Shouldn't you be presenting me with scientific evidence?
He hands the documents back to you.

speaker: Stranger
content: Since you have the autopsy report, you should also have access to "Rust's" biological data from the time of his death. Even better if the 9th Agency still has his physical examination records from recruitment.

speaker: Stranger
content: Compare all of it to me as I am now, and you'll find—

speaker: Stranger
content: From a purely biological standpoint, Rust and I are two entirely different individuals. We don't even share a blood relation.
He's not wrong. You don't rush to agree, however. You simply hold his gaze, watching.

speaker: Stranger
content: Still not convinced? Then let's discuss something else. An agent of his caliber must have left behind a few connections, wouldn't you say? Informants, friends, enemies... and that partner of his, so eager to avenge him.

speaker: Stranger
content: You could always invite them here to identify me in person. Let's see who else—besides you—would ever accept that I've simply... inherited "Rust's" identity.

speaker: Stranger
content: Though, if you do go through with it, I'd need your protection. Can't have that partner charging at me again.
Your stare doesn't waver. After a moment, he lets out a weary sigh.

speaker: Stranger
content: Alright. It seems you're holding onto other compelling evidence, Chief, to be this certain in your identification.
Looking into his eyes, you start to speak, pace deliberate.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're right. There are gaps I can't explain. I've never seen his face, never known his whereabouts. When I checked with the 9th Agency, they admitted their star agent preferred to work alone. No one knew the details.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: "Rust" left no trail. So when new questions came up, I had no choice but to ask you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Bullets and rifle butts can't fake a death. Whoever brought me to the Drifter Camp in N.F. 112 must have used some kind of Mania sorcery. And in N.F. 113, while I was out, I was moved around more than once, by his hand. And then there's you...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I know the person in this world who understands "Rust" best isn't Thorn. Isn't Langley. Isn't anyone from Rustfire... It can only be you. As for why, you're going to tell me.
For the first time, the glib, slippery tension that could have sustained your duel indefinitely crystallizes into silence. He looks at you, and his gaze is suddenly a honed edge.

speaker: Stranger
content: ...Who told you that?
There it is. The expression you were waiting for.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Then let's trade answers. I mean you no harm, and "Rust" was once a comrade I trusted. If the truth is what I suspect, then honesty helps us both. But the more you dodge and hide, the more you look guilty.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And once my suspicion latches onto someone... it tends to become a headache for them.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No matter how many times you change your face, your voice, your identity... no matter how well you hide, you won't shake me until I get a satisfying answer.
For a long moment, neither of you moves. Finally, the tension leaves his shoulders, and he leans back.

speaker: Stranger
content: Then it seems I have no choice but to tell you everything...

The man holds your gaze as he raises a hand to his collar. He loosens it, then deliberately draws his lapels apart, revealing what has been carefully hidden all along: the base of his neck, his collarbones, his upper chest.

speaker: Haha, writing about the honorable deeds of heroes is a crime in your eyes, huh?

content: Thick, ropy scars cover every inch of his exposed skin. They resemble the marks of Black Ring corruption you've seen on Hella. These, however, are more extensive, and gouged far deeper. What lies beneath them isn't flesh and blood, but a seething, formless chaos. Stare too long, and you feel your own mind straining at the edge, threatening to tumble in.
The man's face shows no pain. He watches you, calm and assessing, as if what he's bared is not a mutilation carved into his own body, but simply bait on a hook.

speaker: Stranger
content: Judging by your reaction, you've seen something like this before. This is what happens when a human fuses deeply with a Black Ring, complete with its curse... and its blessing.

speaker: Stranger
content: The ability I gained is simple enough: bodies are merely vessels I change at will, and I can always transfer my consciousness through the Black Ring.

speaker: Stranger
content: Whenever a body is destroyed beyond repair—when it dies—my consciousness returns to the Black Ring. It waits until the Ring connects to a suitable replacement... Say, when someone is infected with Mania and their mind collapses, but their body has yet to twist into a Corruptor...

speaker: Stranger
content: My drifting consciousness seeps through, claims that hollow, ownerless shell as my own, and is reborn in another body... Sound familiar?

speaker: Stranger
content: Yes, that <color=#fb9259>Parma</color>, the Undergrounder who gave you quite some trouble, used a similar trick. You might ask the 9th Agency how many times they had to kill him before he finally stayed dead.

A sharp, intentional malice emanates from him, and you register every edge of it. Still, you choose stillness over reaction. The urge to discover what fuels his venom outweighs the instinct to avoid it.
He notes your momentary slip and the iron control that instantly corrects it. A smile of genuine approval touches his lips before he yields to your order.

speaker: Stranger
content: The "Rust" in your reports is at least the third body I've used. It seems to have belonged to a fallen 9th Agency agent, likely "Thorn's" actual partner when he was alive.

speaker: Stranger
content: I grew rather fond of it. Convenient, and it came with a wealth of useful knowledge and skills. When it was destroyed in N.F. 113, I was... genuinely reluctant to let it go.

speaker: Stranger
content: Come to think of it... before I claimed that body, could he have been one of those dear <color=#fb9259>Rustfire comrades</color> you still think about?
[Shackles Effect]

You rise, and your shackles lash out on pure instinct, piercing through his body. The sensation is startlingly vivid this time. Through the psychic link, you can feel the wet, tearing resistance of muscle and fascia.
Yet none of that agony reaches the man's face. He is still smiling, the expression welded onto his corpse-pale features, his gaze locked on you without a flicker.

speaker: Stranger
content: There we are. You shouldn't be so quick to count me among your own, Chief... My ties to the <color=#fb9259>Underground</color> run far deeper than you realize.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: There's no point in being vague with the timeline. If you were truly using Rust's body, then at the very least, we can confirm one thing: the person killed by the Undergrounders at BR-002 was you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So what exactly do you mean by your "ties" with them? When did you enter Rust's body? What triggered it? Who were you before that, and what have you done since becoming "Rust"?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Don't try to dodge by unsettling me. Answer me. Tell me the truth.
You try to pull your shackles back, to reassert control of the interrogation... but it seems you're already behind.

The luminous barbs of your shackles protrude from wound after wound across his skin. You try to pull them back, but meet a faint, grotesque resistance. It's a sickening tug, like drawing a blade from clotted mire.

speaker: Stranger
content: Heh... I've given you quite enough intel. Now, it's your turn to answer a few <color=#fb9259>little questions</color> of mine.

The fissures across his body glow ever brighter, bleeding crimson light. An indescribable presence saturates the room. Suddenly, you can no longer be sure—is this still the interrogation room? Is this reality? The air thickens with something viscous, clogging your senses.
...All you can perceive is the man before you and the chaotic aura shrouding him, growing more vivid, more glaring with each second.

speaker: Stranger
content: Who I am now bears no resemblance to "Rust." Before my candid confession, there should have been no clues, no evidence, no one who could have connected me to him... except you.

speaker: Stranger
content: So steadfast in your conviction, completely unmoved... Why?

speaker: Stranger
content: Chief... Why are you so certain that I am Rust?

Something is wrong. Your body tenses to leave, to shout a warning, but a turbulent wave of familiarity crashes over you, pressing you back into the seat and guiding your tongue. You grapple with it, fighting the magnetic pull to give him your raw, unguarded truth.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Those who know me would say I can be... confident. Unreasonably so, sometimes.

speaker: Stranger
content: Now it's your turn to be evasive? No matter. Just as you seem to have a knack for seeing through me, I'll study you just as closely. I'll uncover everything you wish to hide.

The man offers a polite nod before his gaze drops to the spikes piercing his body. He lifts a hand, his fingers brushing lightly against one of the shackles' barbs. Red light erupts, and a piercing ring floods your ears, instantly silencing the interrogation room's alarm.
Your senses blur into a formless haze. It feels less like an assault and more like a return, to something gentle, known. Like home. Like... a Black Ring. His face tells you he feels it too.

speaker: Stranger
content: The shackles... I failed to account for them during the manhunt a few days ago. That's how I ended up in your hands... But now that I think about it, the look on your face when you caught me was rather interesting.

speaker: Stranger
content: In that moment, did you see anything through the <color=#fb9259>shackles</color>?
You bite back a verbal response. Yet within, his question finds its mark, provoking an answer that forms against your will.
[Flashback: Chapter 9 Shooting CG, Chapter 10 Chief's Speech CG, Chapter 13 Chief Lying in Coffin CG (solo, without Don)]

speaker: Stranger
content: ...It's come this far already? It seems your shackles have grown considerably since we last met two years ago. You've personally entered and destroyed two Black Rings since then, haven't you?

speaker: Stranger
content: Did you <color=#fb9259>devour</color> them, just like before? BR-005? BR-002? Or did you take them all? Did EDGE not stop you? Or perhaps I should put it this way...

speaker: Stranger
content: After such a feast, how have you changed? Who exactly is ${PlayerName} now? The Chief of Minos, or the <color=#fb9259>shackles of Mania</color>?

His hands suddenly clamp down on the spikes impaling him. A corresponding jolt lurches through your consciousness, followed by a wave of visceral nausea. The Sinner before you distorts, dissolving into a chaotic, humanoid mass that writhes hungrily to devour the shackles themselves.

speaker: Stranger
content: Please, tell me the truth. "Rust" received interrogation training. He can spot a lie. Don't try to deceive me.

speaker: Stranger
content: Otherwise, no matter how powerful your shackles may be, I might just do something drastic... and hurt you at any cost.

His grip tightens. The shackles blaze white-hot, burning through his leather gloves, melting the skin of his palms, searing into something deeper—his very essence. It is not only the uncanny Mania that presses down on you with menace, but the raw intensity burning in his eyes.
Holy hell! If I'd known you packed this much firepower, I'd have dragged you everywhere! Just imagine how invincible we'd look together—the invincible EMP with an ace like you!
[Flashback]

speaker: Thorn
content: Chief?!
Yet every time, he held back his attacks. With you, with Thorn—even at the cost of his own advantage.
[Exit Flashback]

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...There's no need for you to worry. Even cautious as they are, EDGE isn't concerned about my shackles. That should tell you they have it under control. And... threatening me won't work. If you could so easily "hurt" someone, you wouldn't have been caught and brought here.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Your actions are far more honest than your words, Mr. Many-Faced Agent. When it comes to you, I'd rather trust my instincts.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And my instincts tell me there's no need to treat you as an enemy, or a prisoner. We didn't have to speak like this.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Tell me about yourself. What you've been through, what you're fighting for, what weighs on you now, and why you keep hiding the truth from us.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If you're not the Agent "Rust" I thought you were, then tell me your real name. I want to hear it from you.

speaker: Rust
content: ...You're not going to use your shackles to see for yourself? You clearly have the power.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The power to pry into someone's secrets? I don't know if I even have that. And even if I did, I wouldn't use it lightly. Besides...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If you really are "Rust," as I hope you are, then you're my friend.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I won't do that to a friend.

The oppressive chaos gripping your shackles dissolves. The uncanny feeling saturating the space evaporates, leaving only the sterile chill of the interrogation room. The Mania alarm has remained unanswered long enough that flustered voices now clamor beyond the door.
...How strange. That confrontation felt like an eternity. Yet snapping back, only seconds have bled away. And the man opposite you—
The violent fissures that scarred his form have subsided. He sits poised, collar neatly adjusted, his gaze steady upon you.

speaker: Rust
content: My apologies, Chief. That was an ill-timed jest. I'm glad to see you haven't changed, still the most dependable <color=#fb9259>friend</color> a Sinner could ask for.

speaker: Rust
content: As for the matter of "Rust"... perhaps we could save that for another time? That little scuffle took more out of me than I'd care to admit. I'm afraid this body of mine is at its limit. Shameful, I know, that even I have my frailties.

speaker: Rust
content: After all, you've already placed your shackles on me. The interrogation can resume whenever you wish.

The commotion beyond the door pulls your attention for a second. When you look back, his expression has reset. The smile is a placid, unreadable mask. The interrogation is over. You draw your shackles back, the movement slow and final.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Before that, I have one last question.

options: You're the Rust I know, right?

speaker: Rust
content: ...Heh. If seeing me reminds you of him, then by all means, use that name.

speaker: Rust
content: It was only ever a spy's temporary codename, but... to be remembered by you, I'm sure that "Rust" would be pleased.
[Door Closes, Black Screen]
It turns out, you never get him back into that room.

That night, an entire surveillance grid goes dark. Not disabled, but utterly and physically destroyed, in perfect synchronicity before a single alarm can sound. The scale of it is impossible, far beyond the Sinner's known methods. The entire Bureau is left reeling.
By the time repairs are complete, his cell is empty. The only recovered footage is a brief clip of him casually walking out the Bureau's front doors. He glances up, finds the camera—
—and turns to wave you goodbye.

August 28th, N.F. 115
West District Second Mine - Field Clinic

A commotion stirs through the work area. A group of young miners is half-carrying, half-dragging a wounded colleague toward the exit. Rumor ripples through the crowd: a rookie, first descent, took a hit of raw contamination to the shoulder. The injured man's face is corpse-pale. Yet, the miners around him look even more terrified.

speaker: Rookie Miner
content: Hey, buddy! You with us? Whoa, easy, easy, the blood's getting everywhere!

speaker: Rookie Miner
content: This is all on me, man. I was yapping away, wasn't paying attention, and now you're hit... I'm so sorry!

speaker: Rookie Miner
content: Just hang tight, okay? I'll grab you something to eat. Specialist's almost here... Lavina!

speaker: Lavina
content: Alright, who let their guard down this time?

A red-haired woman strides briskly toward him. Her clothes are plain but neat, and her bright voice carries easily. The lines on her face speak not of weariness, but of a life fully lived, making her warm smile all the more infectious.

Lavina looks even more spirited than he remembers. After the High Tower Black Ring fell, he heard she had left the West District to follow Rustfire and establish contact with the satellite towns. She must have rushed back recently to assist with the post-war reconstruction. Caring for others has always been her calling, after all.

speaker: Lavina
content: New around here, aren't you? What's your name? Been at the Drifter Camp before?
No time to invent a name. He gives her his old partner's codename instead. "Thorn's" cover has always been airtight; it won't be compromised.

speaker: Lavina
content: "Thorn"? Hmm... don't think I've heard that one. You just started?

speaker: Lavina
content: Ah, never mind. Something about how you talk reminds me of my old friends at Rustfire. Must be my imagination.
Of course it does. He spent so long at the Drifter Camp that deliberate effort is required to mask his old habits. He must still be careful not to let her keen intuition pick up on anything.

But this same familiarity also makes it easier to draw out information. Lavina moves through her work while detailing safety protocols, covering procedure after procedure. She chats without a second thought, but he listens with intent, quietly committing every word to memory.

speaker: Lavina
content: Hm? Asking after Nirvana? Hah, trouble-makers, always will be. Can't drop your guard around them. But it's a sight better than it used to be.

speaker: Lavina
content: Not all city folk are bad, you know. We've got good friends across the river, too. Even a certain... official, low-profile but quite the big shot, has secured us a lot of resources. Things are smoother now. You just focus on working safe.

speaker: Lavina
content: Long as you follow the procedure and watch out for each other, you'll be fine.
As she speaks, she ties off the bandage with a practiced knot and pats his shoulder—a gesture both cautionary and encouraging.

The restless pain she once carried has settled into a quiet calm. Time has softened the sorrow from her brow and etched gentle laugh lines at the corners of her eyes... He can't help but feel genuine happiness for her, seeing this change.
Just as the thought settles, someone else lifts the tent flap and steps inside.

speaker: Lavina
content: Samuel? Weren't you over at Nirvana's sorting things out? What brings you back?

speaker: Samuel
content: ...Matilda's managing it. It's fine. Someone from Decontamination is looking for you. You should go; I'll keep an eye here.

speaker: Lavina
content: Ugh, they really need to be more careful. I'm on my way.

speaker: Lavina
content: Oh, and—
She turns back with one last reminder.

speaker: Lavina
content: Thorn, follow the protocols next time. If I see you in here again, you'll get an earful from me, promise.
The tent flap falls shut. Only Samuel and the "injured worker" remain, and the air grows still.
Samuel looks over. The "newcomer" waits on the cot's edge, wrapped in a coarse cloak, his hair intentionally mussed.

speaker: Samuel
content: ...You make friends quickly.

speaker: Rust
content: Comes with being a Syndican.

Rust offers a grin, the kind worn by miners through the dust and ash. The smile doesn't have time to settle before the old man's hand clamps onto his wrist and deftly retrieves a pass concealed beneath the rough fabric.

speaker: Samuel
content: Syndicans in the mine don't steal. This is Lavina's pass. You lifted it while she was treating you? Quick hands.
Rust stays silent. He's acutely aware of Samuel's weapon, already drawn and leveled at him from beneath the fabric of his cloak.

speaker: Samuel
content: Word came that someone suspicious had slipped into the shafts, asking questions. That's why I returned early, to meet you. And you even timed it for when I was away. Well-informed. Professional, I take it.

speaker: Samuel
content: Nirvana's lackey? Or an Outland scout? Who sent you, and what do you want?

speaker: Rust
content: Hmm... I'm curious. Who tipped you off?

speaker: Samuel
content: Don't play games. People like you disappear without a trace. Rustfire still has people who can arrange that.

Samuel is the same as ever—sharp and cautious. Crossing paths with him always invites complications. That's precisely why Rust confirmed personnel schedules before he made his move, timing his visit for when Samuel would be away at a meeting. And yet, here they are.
No matter. Adapting is part of the job. The real question is how: concoct another story on the fly, or use the secluded setting to neutralize the problem quietly?
As Rust weighs his options, the light from the entrance flickers. Someone stands at the doorway, holding the tent flap half-open. Before Rust can make out the backlit face, he recognizes the voice.
Sorry, Samuel. He's one of mine.

speaker: Samuel
content: ...Chief ${PlayerName}? Then this is...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Well, not exactly "one of mine." More like an escapee I couldn't keep tabs on.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Made a bit of a scene saying he was looking for an old friend. Since I care about that friend too, I thought I'd tag along.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: A Rustfire intelligence operative—"Rust." Sound familiar, Samuel?
Samuel's hand goes still. Rust catches the brief, distant flicker in his eyes.
It looks, for a moment, like grief.
[Black Screen]

"'Thorn' is Rust's informant and an old friend from the Outlands, also a Sinner."
"He came to DisCity but couldn't locate Rust. He refuses to believe his friend is dead and insists on investigating the truth."
"It's been too long, and information is scarce. If possible, we'd like Rustfire's assistance. This is the only place Rust left any trace."
—Samuel accepts your fabricated story immediately, without a shred of doubt.

speaker: Samuel
content: In the autumn of N.F. 113, he supplied us with a great deal of intelligence. Without any single piece of it, we likely couldn't have extracted you from the High Tower Black Ring.

speaker: Samuel
content: But I only officially rejoined the organization after the Black Ring fell. Before that, I never had direct contact with him. It wasn't until we compiled the list of the fallen that I even learned his codename.

Though he never met "Rust" in person, Samuel had once compiled a detailed record of every Rustfire member lost in BR-002 over those nine years. Using that, he mapped "Rust's" network—contacts from the Drifter Camp, comrades from Rustfire, scattered Syndicate informants, rival gang affiliates, and more.

The result is a substantial list of leads, which Samuel provides in the hope it will help you learn more about the man you seek.

As you walk the streets of the West District together, your "person of interest" doesn't flee this time. He stays close, cooperating without protest. Perhaps he has finally grasped a few basic truths:

First, if he wants to operate under Rustfire's watch in the West District, working with you is the fastest way. And second—
Just how determined you are to get answers.
[Scene Change] Syndicate Streets

The West District streets, still under reconstruction, thrum with chaotic life. The crowd packs the sidewalks so tightly that the roasted meat bun stalls are doing a roaring trade. Everyone is too busy chasing their next meal to spare a glance at two slightly out-of-place figures seated nearby.
The bun in your hand is delicious, but mixing work with food always dulls the pleasure, especially when the intel you're reviewing only grows more irritating by the minute.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Fake ID, fake ID, fake ID... ALL fake?! Seriously? You spent years here and couldn't make one real friend? Not a single person you could be honest with?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: All those people who still ask about you, who still care... What they're missing is just a character. A performance. Charming lines, rehearsed sincerity... all to play with their feelings. Tch. And these?!!
As you speak, you slide several frayed, handwritten notes from the folder. Each is a personal IOU.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Didn't the 9th Agency approve a budget for you? How do you still owe people money?

speaker: Rust
content: A field agent's budget only covers the basics. I did some research—if you want to build a reliable informant network using money, the real trick is to reverse the dynamic.

speaker: Rust
content: You see, people are far more motivated to chase down a debt than to collect a payment. Financial ties, it turns out, bind tighter than sentiment.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...You sound like someone from Whitestone. Quite the achievement, single-handedly tanking the 9th Agency's reputation.

speaker: Rust
content: That said, I do believe you have a far greater talent for this work than I ever did.

speaker: Rust
content: You were the one who spread the word to bring Samuel back, weren't you, Chief? Laid a neat little trap, then swept in just in time to save the day.
A practiced smile rests perfectly on his face.

speaker: Rust
content: I'll admit, it was well done. But why go through all the trouble?

speaker: Rust
content: You've already put your shackles on me. Could've tracked me and picked me up anytime. I was actually curious why you waited so long to come find me.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I just wanted to see what interesting moves you'd make on your own.
You glance at him.

The wound on "Rust's" shoulder clearly isn't from any work accident. Before meeting the workers, he must have already gone down into the mine for his own purposes. Has his objective shifted to BR-002?

But if that were all, he could have simply slipped away afterward. Why go through the trouble of posing as a newcomer and seeking treatment? Gathering intel wouldn't require such theatrics either. Unless...
You'd like to believe he genuinely misses his old friends, but asking directly would never yield an honest answer.

Your terminal vibrates—an update on the joint Black Ring search mission. You skim it. No immediate intervention required. You still have time to humor the stubbornly evasive agent sitting across from you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This place you picked is probably the busiest shop on the street, right? Strong reputation, heavy foot traffic, been here seven years. Prime informant material.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Not on Rustfire's list, so the owner isn't one of theirs. You developed him yourself back when you were with the 9th Agency? He must know more about you than most.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'll go have a word with the owner later.
He spreads his hands, offering a gesture that hangs between yielding and daring you to proceed.

speaker: Rust
content: Already checked the kitchen. The old owner's gone. All new staff.

speaker: Rust
content: He was in poor health. Whenever we met, I'd bring him the specific medication he needed. Even if his body survived the High Tower Black Ring... he wouldn't have lasted two years without his meds after "Rust" died.
His tone remains as detached as ever, devoid of any sorrow. But his eyes tell a different story: they've softened noticeably.

speaker: Rust
content: He was an interesting man. Bottom-rung Syndican, but proud. If I'd tried to trade medicine for information outright, it would've wounded his pride. He'd have slowly shut me out.

speaker: Rust
content: But if I borrowed five hundred from him first, then said "Can't pay you back yet—take this medicine as interest" whenever he came to collect... he'd grumble and curse, but he'd take it. Even slipped me extra food now and then, treating me like the broke fool I was pretending to be.

speaker: Rust
content: And while we were chatting about this and that... I'd coax out quite a bit of intelligence.

His gaze settles on the roasted meat buns on the table, freshly made, generously stuffed and fragrant. The agent has ordered a dipping sauce with an unusual mix of ingredients to go with them. The flavor is quite good, actually. You've eaten them all.
Food steeped in memory has a way of softening hearts. The pointed exchanges from moments ago no longer seem to matter.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If you cooperate when we go back to the Bureau, I might even keep ordering takeout for you.

speaker: Rust
content: Please, spare me. I've told you everything I can. The rest... let's call it privacy, shall we?

speaker: Rust
content: I've nothing against you personally, Chief. But given how much EDGE values you, who knows what they've put in you? I'd rather not have an audience listening in.
As his smile fades, so does the nostalgia in his eyes. He pushes the buns back toward you.

speaker: Rust
content: The one who loved these was "Rust" of the 9th Agency. That body is gone. This is a new vessel, so time to develop new tastes.
You're still searching for the right words when your terminal buzzes. A message from the 9th Agency cuts through the silence:

New lead, and a major breakthrough!

We've tracked Underground movements. They haven't pinpointed BR-003, but are actively investigating the other Black Rings. Interception team preparing to deploy. Exact coordinates...

speaker: Rust
content: See? Duty calls. An urgent dispatch from the 9th Agency, I presume.
It clicks immediately. The breakthrough is his design. This is a game, and like you did with Samuel, Rust is now moving you across the board.
Dragging him to MBCC is an option, but too blunt. Without understanding his driver, he'd escape again.
Letting him go to trace the shackles later feels like falling into a prepared script. He's likely arranged for that, too.
...Confrontation, then? Right here, with all cards on the table?
He reads your hesitation, your silent debate. A soft chuckle escapes him before he voices a proposal that changes the entire equation.

speaker: Rust
content: There's still time. Why not take a walk with me, Chief?

speaker: Rust
content: These streets are where "Rust" once lived. If you want to find out the man he was... this is the place to do it.
You have the time, and so you see no reason to refuse.
[Scene Change]

The two of you walk through the dusk-lit streets, the afterglow deepening around you. No matter how much the West District has changed, for all these years the sunset has painted these streets in the same crimson hues.
It also lends a flush of warmth to his pale face, making him look, for a moment, a little less different from those around him.

speaker: Rust
content: This place has changed so much. For the better, too.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The Ash Campaign destroyed many parts of the city. Otherwise, you'd be seeing something even more impressive.

speaker: Rust
content: The tensions with Nirvana and Eastside... they're still there, aren't they? Have you been mediating this whole time?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I can't take that much credit. It's mostly Matilda and the rest of the Executive Committee doing the heavy lifting.

speaker: Rust
content: Miss Cavendish is quite reliable, yes. But without the Bureau's "back channels," I doubt so many of those "Rustfire rioters" would have avoided prosecution and regained their freedom.

speaker: Rust
content: I heard Mr. Donald moved to a satellite town? Do the two of you still keep in touch?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: We do, just not as often. Everyone's busy.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But you could visit them. Don would be happy to see you. Samuel mentioned you two crossed paths back in N.F. 113.

speaker: Rust
content: Heh, that was the old "Rust." I'm not that free. Making it to the West District is already pushing my limits. I'll just have to pick up news about them while I'm here.

speaker: Rust
content: Lavina and Samuel are doing quite well, it seems. Just now, "Mama Lavina" mentioned she had a video call last week with a kid who just returned to the Bureau.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Hah, it must be her. She's been studying, but after running around outside for a bit, she came back having forgotten how to write half her characters. Then she just went on and on about needing to call Lavina and catch up with her.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But her health isn't great. Ever since she came out of the Black Ring, she's needed constant rest. She sleeps for long stretches, and no one can figure out why.

speaker: Rust
content: Once your consciousness has merged with a Black Ring, breaking free is no simple task. It takes everything you have.

speaker: Rust
content: But she made it back. That's what matters. My guess is she sleeps so long because she's trying to find someone in her dreams, to go back for them. Once she finds who she's looking for, she won't need to keep at it. She'll perk right up.

speaker: Rust
content: Or perhaps... there's a simpler explanation. You've assigned her such a heavy course load that little Hella has no choice but to fake an illness to escape her studies?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Hiding from Raven? She's running a proper Syndicate Academy now, and enrollment is booming. It's been two years already. Time changes a lot of things.

speaker: Rust
content: Is that so?

speaker: Rust
content: ...I guess it really does.

He smiles, but his pace gradually slows until he stops in the middle of the street. The sunset bathes him in gold as the crowd flows past, their faces bright with genuine laughter, a stark contrast to his own stillness. He simply stands there, watching.
You stop as well and turn to face him. Just as you're about to speak, your terminal buzzes again. You let out a quiet sigh.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...I know you're the one who fed them that intel. Send me on a wild goose chase so you could slip away, right? Thanks for the assist—still frustrating as hell, though.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Being honest wouldn't kill you. You obviously came back because you missed them. I really don't get what you're so set on hiding.
He holds vital intel. You carry a heavy debt to him. After all this time, you've finally found him. The questions are pressing, yet...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Forget it. Even if you don't say anything, I'll find out what I need on my own. But don't think you can run. Once I'm done here, I will find you. Doesn't matter how many times you die, how many shells you swap, what mission you take next.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This isn't about work. Or any official interrogation. It's about you—
You don't get to finish. A sharp shout from behind cuts through the conversation.

speaker: Shop Owner
content: Hey—!! Was that—was that your order just now?

speaker: Shop Owner
content: This sauce... this sauce... is it yours?!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Uh... It's a friend of mine...

speaker: Shop Owner
content: I knew it! It's "Rust," isn't it! That old-school ratio—I'd know it anywhere! Two years, not a word, and my old boss griped about the money he owed right up 'til the end! Is he ever gonna pay up or what?!

This sparks a fierce tirade from the shop owner—phrases and grievances that must have been passed down from his late boss. You add a few corroborating comments to keep the rhythm going, then smoothly slide him some new details: Rust went to a satellite town, looking for work to earn some money.

speaker: Shop Owner
content: ...Honestly, just knowing he's alright is enough. He was a regular, you know? My old boss thought about him for two whole years, came up with new dishes he never got to try. If you see him... tell him to visit. I can at least try to cook a few of the old ones.

speaker: Shop Owner
content: But most importantly, he still owes us! Fifty DisCoins!
With a light laugh, you send the shop owner off, then glance toward Rust.
An agent with his people skills should know how to read a room. And if he somehow misses it, Samuel already spelled things out plainly enough.

speaker: Samuel
content: If you hear anything about him, good or bad, let us know.

speaker: Samuel
content: He'll always be a friend of Rustfire.
He absorbs your words in utter silence, waiting for you to finish before he finally offers a reply.

speaker: Rust
content: ...You certainly have a way with words. Whether it's winning people over or pulling intel out of them. A real professional.
Bzzz— Your terminal vibrates again.

speaker: Rust
content: Go ahead and take the mission, Chief. I've held you up long enough. What I have left to say... it's honest. And it won't take long.

speaker: Rust
content: I may carry traces of the Underground, but I'm not your enemy. Everything I do is to repel the Black Rings, to stop the fanatics spreading them. If our goals align, I'm willing to lend a hand when I can.

speaker: Rust
content: Tell EDGE to be careful. You've successfully recovered BR-002 and BR-005, but BR-003's existence is exposed. The enemy will move soon.

speaker: Rust
content: What they're after is BR-003's true core: that inheritance fragment that has successfully merged with the Corpus... So don't get attached to whatever benefits the Black Ring offers. Deal with it quickly, while EDGE still has a weapon like you on the field.

speaker: Rust
content: But when you're out there... remember: at the final moment, don't use your shackles to make contact like before. Don't let "instinct" tempt you into accepting it. That... wouldn't end well. You're strong enough as it is. Any further, and you'll be stepping into dangerous territory.

speaker: Rust
content: Leave it to EDGE. Just like with BR-002 and BR-005, destroy the Black Ring, recover the "fragment," purify it, and seal it away. Guard it well. As long as it's not taken, there won't be a problem.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...You could've told me all this sooner, you know.

speaker: Rust
content: An agent doesn't hand over information freely. Intel is worth more than one's life. I had to build trust carefully—with you, and with every organization behind you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So you're saying you didn't trust me before? Or are you telling me you suddenly trust everyone behind me now?

speaker: Rust
content: I've always trusted you... and I will never trust <color=#fb9259>them</color>. But now, I believe it doesn't matter who stands behind you. It won't be a problem.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...That's a lot to take in. I need some time to process this.

speaker: Rust
content: That's fine. If it's hard to trust me, just pass the message along.

speaker: Rust
content: Tell my former supervisor at the 9th Agency, or... let the EDGE technology buried inside you hear it clearly. They'll make the call.

speaker: Rust
content: Also, there's something I'd like to ask of you. Consider it... an exchange of favors.
He pauses for a long moment, as though gathering his thoughts with exacting care. Then, slowly, he begins—one request at a time.

speaker: Rust
content: First, for Samuel: at 85 East Street in the Drifter Camp, second floor, third compartment. Under the third floorboard on the upper left, he'll find some detection manuals. Have him use them at the mine. If anything unusual comes up, run a patrol sweep immediately. That's the only way to root out the truly dangerous ones in time.

speaker: Rust
content: With it, there's also a sealed letter. It's a will that "Rust" wrote to "Thorn" ahead of time. But the death came too suddenly... I never had the chance to deliver it. I'll have to ask you to do it for me.

speaker: Rust
content: Tell Thorn not to blame himself so much. "Rust" fell fighting the Underground. He never had any regrets, and for his partner, he had nothing but gratitude.

speaker: Rust
content: Rather than revenge, "Rust" would prefer Thorn to visit the cemetery when there's time. Bring a few bottles of good wine, and some roasted meat buns from the old shop.

speaker: Rust
content: Also... everything you noted he owed during your visit earlier, please help settle it all.

speaker: Rust
content: My apologies for the cost. Rust's survivor benefits should still be valid. See if you can claim them to cover the debts.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Why are you asking me to do all this?

speaker: Rust
content: Why... I suppose even I didn't expect that "Rust," two years gone, would be lucky enough to make such a stubborn friend.

speaker: Rust
content: It's your fault, you know. For being so stubborn. For insisting on pulling him back here, making him revisit every regret, live through such a happy day... only to face another painful goodbye.

speaker: Rust
content: It's too much for him to carry. So please, take responsibility and see it through for him. He would be truly grateful.
That wasn't your question. Yet his answer is so disarmingly sincere that it catches you off guard, and you let him continue without interruption.

speaker: Rust
content: ...Thank you. The Black Rings are a terminal illness of our time, but you've shown me that a cure might be possible.

speaker: Rust
content: Thank you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Keep this in mind: no matter where you go, how many times you die, what body you use, or what your mission is... you are my friend.
He listens with genuine attention, his expression softening into a smile meant just for you.

speaker: Rust
content: Then... let's save the rest for next time. Don't worry; with the shackles, you can always find me.

speaker: Rust
content: ...I wish you all the best, Chief ${PlayerName}.

In the following days, you successfully root out several Underground scouts lurking in the BR-005 ruins. Other operatives closing in on the archives to steal BR-003 intelligence are neutralized as well. Bolstered by timely intel from an anonymous source, every operation proceeds smoothly.

Back at the Bureau, as you're weighing your next move regarding the "interrogation," you receive an unexpected update: an intelligence access request filed a few days ago has been approved. The file from the 9th Agency, marked top-secret, arrives.

[9th Agency Top-Secret Archive Excerpt-0]

No Security Classification  Not for Public Disclosure
—Experiment and Surveillance Records of Underground Fugitive S-247.
He bids farewell to the warm sun, the bustling streets, to those who pursued him and those who showed him kindness—returning, at last, to a place even more familiar.

speaker: Undergrounder C
content: To sabotage our plans with such precision... I knew it had to be you.

speaker: Undergrounder C
content: You returned unusually fast this time. Was it the Fifth Black Ring that reshaped you?

speaker: Undergrounder C
content: ...And arrogant as ever. You still dare to come here—and alone, no less.
He opens his eyes, and is greeted once more by the people he knows all too well.

speaker: Rust
content: But of course. You are the very reason I cling to this wretched existence.

<color=#7683a2>[9th Agency Top-Secret Archive Excerpt-1]
The origins of Subject S-247 are untraceable. Current hypothesis suggests he may be an anomalous entity spawned from Black Ring influence.

<color=#7683a2>The Agency employed advanced interrogation techniques, including psychological induction protocols from Banyan Medical College and deep-trance hypnosis, to extract information.
The resulting data, however, proved too fragmented and contradictory to synthesize into a credible history.
<i>The shackles appear to... resonate with certain memories. To be honest, I rarely looked back before this. I can hardly recall things clearly anymore.<i>

<i>Every time I wake up in a fresh body, I feel something has slipped away, while something else... has seeped in. It makes a certain sense. The flesh is just a vessel for memory. A vessel I can never hold onto for long.<i>
<i>But one thing never changes. Every single time I retrace this fragmented path, I always see the same things.<i>
<i>It always starts with a Black Ring. And it always ends as a joke.<i>
[Scene Change] [Flashback] BR-001
<color=#fb9259><size=50>N.F. 89, DisCity Carnival</color>
<color=#fb9259><size=50>The BR-001 Outbreak</color>

speaker: DisCity Visitor A
content: AAAAAHHH!! What is that?? The amusement park is... is... MONSTERS!!

speaker: DisCity Child
content: Mommy... Daddy... Waaaaaah—
That day, fear and despair had spread like wildfire, assimilating all prey too weak to flee and transforming them into Corruptors. Humans, helpless, had run only in vain.

Yet against the tide of fleeing crowds, several figures in black raincoats were striding calmly forward, their faces upturned in worship of the twisted red glow that rose above. Amid the cacophony of wailing dirges, it slowly unfurled into the shape of a ring.

speaker: Underground Scout
content: A wild fragment... To unleash such power without guidance, without any Mania catalyst...

speaker: Underground Scout
content: The Ring... As the prophecy foretold, the halo descends... This is divinity's true face. A miracle born from a mere fragment... Can we replicate such grace? How? The park is sealed now. We...
When he turned to ask, his companion offered no reply. Instead, he found the other crouched low, prodding at a creature nestled among the debris and rubble.

speaker: Underground Scout
content: ...How's this little swine still breathing? Scraps the spawns overlooked?

He crouched and seized the child's head, forcing it to turn. The child didn't cry or flinch; he was hollow, like a shell from which the soul had been emptied, the dried tracks of salt tears still visible on his cheeks.
Was he six years old... or only five? The child lay curled in a hollow, completely motionless, clutching a bloodstained adult shoe to his chest.

speaker: Underground Scout
content: Brain not fully formed? Consciousness too faint to register, I suppose. Leave it. It'll be dead in days.

speaker: Underground Elder
content: ...I'll take him back.

speaker: Underground Scout
content: Hah? Oh, spare me, you senile fool! Has the Overground stench rotted your mind? Why waste breath on that thing?

speaker: Underground Elder
content: ...Alive all these days, and can bear the Ring's gaze... This one is favored. Might be of use.

speaker: Underground Scout
content: ...Since when do swine and mutts earn the Ring's favor? Fine. Have it your way. You always have a soft spot for strays.
<i><color=#7683a2>...Don't call me that...</color><i>
<i><color=#7683a2>Favor...? I want no part of its curse...</color><i>

speaker: Underground Scout
content: Come here, brat. That's it, come. No one's coming for you. Come with us, to the Underground sanctuary. There's a god down there who can keep you safe.
<i><color=#7683a2>It took everything... Why would I seek its shelter?</color><i>

speaker: Underground Elder
content: If you wish to live... come with me...
<i><color=#7683a2>...Was it because... I didn't want to die?</color><i>
<i>That was my first encounter with a Black Ring. I didn't die there... I was taken, by ones from the Underground.<i>
<i>For the next decade, they became my family.<i>

<color=#7683a2>[9th Agency Top-Secret Archive Excerpt-2]
Subject S-247 was captured in N.F. 106 from the observatory ruins, found within the wreckage of the Black Ring. He exhibits an exceptionally high tolerance to Black Ring contamination. All corruption-based experiments to date have failed to fully degrade or terminate the subject.
He retains a semblance of sanity: the barest, most tenuous level of cognitive cohesion.

<color=#7683a2>Analysis of internal tissue samples confirms contamination from multiple distinct Black Ring signatures:
- Most Recent: BR-003
- Earliest: BR-001
- Peak Concentration: BR-000, or a contaminant nearly identical to BR-000
- Trace Amounts: BR-002

Home, to him, had always meant darkness, confinement, oppression, and gloom. He had been hidden away in a small drainage trench, kept out of sight of the believers who flowed to and from ■■. They, too, were hiding in this sunless sewer city, sheltering from the sinful light of the world above.
Down there, a person's world was only as wide as their vision. But that hadn't mattered much.
For the brat, it was enough simply to have a "home." Wherever his "family" was, that had been his "home."

speaker: Underground Elder
content: Five centimeters taller, a thousand hymns sung... It's been a thousand days. You scrawny mutt, you must be eight by now.

speaker: Underground Elder
content: Useless brat! Eight years old and you still don't act like a proper believer!
...Then why not just throw me out?
Those words earned him a slap across the face.

speaker: Underground Elder
content: Still using that filthy Overground swine-speak, are you? When you speak to me, you speak like a proper human!

speaker: Underground Elder
content:
Throw you out? I could just as easily kill you. But if you're gone, who's going to pay back the seven hundred days of food I wasted on you?
Catch!

speaker: Underground Elder
content: ...Memorize every step. I fought hard to get you this chance. Do this right, and you can finally scrub that Overground stink off for good. I'll bring you into ■■, and you won't have to hide in the outer ditches anymore...

speaker: Underground Elder
content: Do it right! It's the only thing you're good for. Mess this up, and I'll get myself some real dogs instead, and butcher you to feed them!
<i><color=#7683a2>Just like that, I was back on the surface. A thousand days later, I saw the sun again, sent to execute my first "mission."</color><i>
<i><color=#7683a2>The "god" wanted to open a door that would not yield to it. So it ordered me to steal the key.</color><i>

N.F. 104
Inner Bay, West District, DisCity
Before the Mine W-31 Negotiation

speaker: Child in the Memory
content: ...Help... Help... me...

speaker: Mine Guard
content: Hey! Where'd you come from, kid? You're nothing but skin and bones. An Outlander? My goodness... you're white as chalk! And you're freezing!

speaker: Mine Guard
content: Get in here. Come on, quick now. Don't you go dying on me.
<i><color=#7683a2>It had been so long since I'd seen the "swine" the Undergrounders always talked about. I'd forgotten we smelled the same.</color><i>
<i><color=#7683a2>The old man said this was my only use: to make the Overground swine open their doors. And they did.</color><i>
<i><color=#7683a2>...They were kind to me.</color><i>

speaker: Rustfire Worker B
content: Doni wrapped up the first round. Final meeting's next week. Things are looking good for us!

speaker: Rustfire Worker C
content: Don't get comfortable. Nirvana didn't like any of it. Who knows what they're planning? Double the patrols in the mine. Watch for anything odd.

speaker: Mine Guard
content: We're on it, we're on it. Got eyes everywhere—even the kids are on lookout. Nobody's slacking. Even this little one new here knows the job.
<i><color=#7683a2>He clapped my shoulder. Called me one of them.</color><i>

speaker: Mine Guard
content: Rustfire's carrying the whole West District's hope. We won't lose to anybody. Right, kid?
<i><color=#7683a2>The Overground people were happy. Hopeful for a bright future ahead. They wanted me to celebrate with them. They were kind.</color><i>
<i><color=#7683a2>They didn't know my real "mission."</color><i>

speaker: Underground Scout
content: Map's set. Duty roster and keys are ours. Good work, runt. Knew I had an eye for talent. You're a real piece of work. Your reward's waiting back home. Hahaha.

speaker: Underground Scout
content: "We humans should... help each other... especially a child... we can't leg—leave them... to die."

speaker: Underground Scout
content: "Humanity... great..." Pfft— HAHAHAHAHAHA!!!

speaker: Underground Scout
content: They're priceless! Once we plant the inheritance in the mine tonight, our job's done. Then... let's see what those swine dig up when they start tearing each other apart. Heh. They'll never know what hit them.
<i><color=#7683a2>I had completed the task they gave me, but I didn't feel happy at all.</color><i>
<i><color=#7683a2>I didn't understand their plan, but I felt a deep, cold dread.</color><i>

speaker: Child in the Memory
content: What... do you want in the mine?

speaker: Underground Elder
content: ...To confirm the prophecy's truth. To prove the divine power. To recreate a miracle.

speaker: Child in the Memory
content: ...Recreate... a miracle?

<i><color=#7683a2>I learned the truth later. A seed called the "inheritance" was buried in Mine W-31. The Underground believers wanted to recreate the amusement park's miracle. To prove it could happen anywhere, through devotion alone.</color><i>
<i><color=#7683a2>They succeeded.</color><i>

<color=#fb9259><size=50>November 28, N.F. 104

Inner Bay Mine W-31, the BR-002 (First) Outbreak</color>

<color=#7683a2>[9th Agency Top-Secret Archive Excerpt-3]
EDGE's analysis of pre-outbreak data from Mine W-31 confirmed the presence of an unidentified Mania substance, which matched the signature of the Underground object known as "the inheritance." This signature was later identified at the BR-003 and BR-004 sites. The N.F. 104 incident provided EDGE with its first empirical confirmation of the inheritance's true threat potential. The vector of its introduction into Mine W-31, however, remains officially undetermined.

Following the reconstruction of the West District, authorities restored relations with Rustfire. But most witnesses to the W-31 incident are now deceased, leaving no conclusive evidence as to how the Underground breached security and brought the inheritance into the mine.

<color=#7683a2>Hypnosis conducted on S-247 has recovered fragmented information. Analysis suggests the Underground used a child to gain the workers' trust, and that S-247 participated in this operation, sustaining significant trauma within the Ring...
This hypothesis provides a plausible explanation for his subsequent extreme actions to sever ties with the Underground. Furthermore, his prior familiarity with BR-002 likely influenced his later assignment to surveillance and experimental duties. However, notable inconsistencies remain within the timeline of events described in his account.

<color=#7683a2>The final report determined that his narrative could be attributed to symptoms of a memory disorder, or that this Underground entity was still attempting to deceive us. Consequently, his account was ruled inadmissible as evidence.
Time might be disordered. Memory might become jumbled. Even emotions might be fabricated. But when it came to the Black Rings, everything was absolute.
From the first moment he truly stepped inside a Black Ring, every event was seared into his memory, undimmed to this day.

speaker: Corpus 002
content: ROARRRR—

The black casket had consumed human hearts and birthed monsters. It devoured every struggling worker, swelling endlessly. If a mere human caught a glimpse of it, the fear in their heart would tear open into a bloody maw, devouring them alive before fusing them into its flesh.
Yet, in that bloody hell, it was only a temporary master. Above the Black Ring, a true monster lurked.
[Transition, fade in Sister's portrait, hold for 2 seconds]

speaker: Shepherd???
content: Heh... Look at you, so satisfied after your little feast. Full now?

speaker: Shepherd???
content: Now, it's my turn.

speaker: Halved Corpus
content: ROARRRR—!!

With a thunderous roar, a colossal crimson light sheared the Corpus in half at the waist. Instantly, the abyss found its new master, and the world snapped into terrible clarity. There was the sky's light, the crimson Illusory Moon, and silhouetted against it, a minute figure.
She was Death incarnate, beyond all things. Her very manifestation maddened every faithful soul who had remained to witness the miracle.

speaker: Underground Scout
content: We did it... We did it!! The sacrifice has been awakened and offered to the Shepherd! She draws closer to godhood!

speaker: Underground Scout
content: Please, transcend all that exists! I... have no regrets in this life!

speaker: Halved Corpus
content: Roarrrr!! DIEEEE!

The sacrifice, now reduced to half a body, was driven by an astonishing will to survive. It must live. It must escape the terrifying monster looming above. It would devour anything it could on its desperate flight—it must survive. Its gaze fell upon the ant-like followers at its feet.

speaker: Underground Elder
content: Is it my turn now? Hehe... To become a part of her... I... have no regrets.

speaker: Child in the Memory
content: ...No... NOOO!!
Someone grabbed the old man around the waist, tackling him aside as the deadly blow narrowly missed its mark.

speaker: Underground Elder
content: Brat, you—?!!

speaker: Child in the Memory
content: They want you dead! I won't let them!!

speaker: Child in the Memory
content: We have to live! Everyone has to live! Don't let it eat you! Don't die here! I—
Words failed him. His mind was chaos, his body a crucible of rapid mutation. Only one thought burned through the storm:

It was happening again. That hideous crimson halo was coming to take everything from him, a second time. He refused. He would not die here. In response, his corrupted flesh began to unnaturally coalesce, forging a new power that allowed him to take away anyone he hoped to save.
Back then, he still hadn't understood that people could hold vastly different "stances."

speaker: Mine Guard
content: You... It was you... You led them here... Kid... who are you?

speaker: Mine Guard
content: A Nirvana spy?!!
Schlick—

speaker: Child in the Memory
content: ...Cough!

Driven by Mania, the miner drove his iron pickaxe deep into the boy's neck, puncturing vital tissue. At eight years old, he encountered his first genuine "death." As the countless hateful gazes bore down on him—a moment etched permanently into his memory—he grasped his position for the first time, and with it, his identity.
Agent, mole, spy... or, stripped to its vilest essence: traitor.
He had it coming.
<i>That was the second Black Ring I witnessed. I should have died there. But I didn't.<i>
<i>I survived, in the most unnatural way.<i>
[Scene Change: Background 953]

speaker: Priest
content: His condition stabilized? Heh... the experiment actually worked. So even inferior believers who fall short of Parma's caliber can withstand the Ring's blessing...

speaker: Priest
content: Hm. Could it be because he was already altered inside the Ring? Become what they call a "Sinner"? An excellent finding. Our potential just expanded...
<i><color=#7683a2>Who...? What did you... do to me...?</color><i>

speaker: Priest
content: Give thanks to fate, brat. You weren't even qualified for the "experiment." But it took pity... and someone offered a sacrifice to place you upon the altar.

speaker: Underground Elder
content: Esteemed Priest... I beg you, please, save him! He can still be saved, can't he? The same happened with Lord Parma, didn't it? He survived again and again...!

speaker: Priest
content: That man claimed the Second Black Ring was all your doing. Said you were willing to offer yourself for the miracle. That one day, you would serve it like Lord Parma... He offered his own arm to prove his loyalty. Heh.

speaker: Underground Elder
content: He's no Overground swine! He only wore their stench to infiltrate them! He's clever! Devout! Sings the hymns every day—every single day! He guarded the inheritance with his life. That's how he was stabbed!

speaker: Underground Elder
content: He's still young! He'll... he'll be of greater use in the future, I swear! Save him! I'll offer my arm... my whole body if you ask! Please!

speaker: Priest
content: From now on, you are a reserve of the execution squad. Go. Prove your ability... and your devotion.

speaker: Priest
content: Don't let us discover your <color=#fb9259>grandfather</color> dared to lie to a priest.
[Scene Change: Underground Space (202 color change)]

speaker: Underground Elder
content: ...What are you staring at? This arm had been acting up for years. Good riddance.

speaker: Underground Elder
content: Don't keep coming back here. You've been blessed with a miracle, accepted into ■■. Don't you have training? You were born low, and even with a new body, they'll still call you an "Overground swine." Sharpen your skills, or they'll toss you back down here.

speaker: Underground Elder
content: ...The priest says the next Black Ring will be larger. More critical. It will take a decade to prepare... By the time you return to the Overground, you'll be grown. Not just a scout anymore. You'll be frontline.

speaker: Underground Elder
content: Make something of yourself, brat. The sky's the limit...
...There will be another one?

speaker: Underground Elder
content: Of course.
Without hesitation, the old man gave his answer. The fanaticism in his eyes burned brighter than ever as he gazed with eager, heartfelt sincerity at his reborn "family."

speaker: Underground Elder
content: Don't hold me back next time. Just watch your own back. To die within a Ring... would be my highest honor. It spared me because it values my devotion, giving me another chance to offer myself.

speaker: Underground Elder
content: Don't waste your worry on me. Focus on your training and studies. I'll manage just fine with one arm.

speaker: Underground Elder
content: When the next Black Ring descends, I'll be right there with you.
...Okay. I'll wait.

He waited, studying the most deranged sorcery and following the most fanatical Sophos. One by one, those around him were granted revelation, achieved epiphany, or found their release. Yet the "awakening" the faithful promised never arrived for him.
He understood nothing of their fanaticism, their hatred, or their sacrifice. And in the sunless depths, he simply waited, while the twisted time slowly crawled into its tenth year.

speaker: Priest
content: The time has come. Steel yourself; this will be a brutal struggle. Even the Overground swine must have learned something from the last miracle.

speaker: Priest
content: But it matters not. We have prepared far longer than they have. Time is on our side. And besides... the swine always find a way to tear themselves apart.

speaker: Underground Elder
content: Move out. Ten years... this is the moment we've waited for.
He waited, until he accepted the sacred mission. Yet the promised awakening still eluded him. That steadfast faith had never arrived.
In its place, he had found only doubt, accumulated over years of hollow waiting. And that doubt... led the faithless into shadow. There, he found others of ignoble mind.
[Scene Change: Use any new underground contamination background]

speaker: Bai Yi
content: ...Heh. What I'm planning is a death sentence. Never thought anyone else would be stupid enough to join.

speaker: Bai Yi
content: You ready to die?

<color=#7683a2>[9th Agency Top-Secret Archive Excerpt-4]

In N.F. 106, during a post-battle sweep of the Navigator Observatory ruins, operatives from the 9th Agency located the sole surviving Underground entity within a contaminated sector.
Designated S-247, he was retrieved for experimental analysis to pinpoint vulnerabilities in Parma-like entities. The project resulted in substantial breakthroughs.

<color=#7683a2>EDGE analysis indicates the Mania corrupting S-247 contains multiple distinct consciousnesses.
The Underground likely used a method to bind these consciousnesses together within his body, with the Black Rings enhancing the effect. This may explain the notorious resilience of certain Underground elites; until all entangled consciousnesses are depleted, they can regenerate via the Black Rings.

Further experiments reveal a key difference from chaotic polymer forms like Parma: S-247's consciousness aggregate is dominated by a single primary will, which suppresses all other chaotic elements. He appears to have undergone a profound transformation within BR-003, achieving a unique equilibrium with his Sinner physiology.

<color=#7683a2>Undoubtedly, he is a twisted creation of the Underground. During the 83rd round of experiments, the Research Institute accidentally pushed Subject S-247's fragile body to the brink of collapse. Following assessment, they recommend immediate disposal to eliminate future risk.

How he had survived was lost to him. During that chaos, he had withstood intense contamination from the Black Ring, weathered frantic assaults from the "Overgrounders," and endured the sheer fury of the Underground's Mania sorcery. Still, he had lived.
Could even this be a blessing from the Black Rings? The notion that he, as one of its blessed, would always be protected and cling to life? What a laughable thought.
<i><color=#7683a2>No matter. We succeeded. At least the Black Ring was taken away, never falling into that woman's hands. The prophecy was wrong. Their efforts were for nothing...</color><i>
<i><color=#7683a2>Heh... A failure doesn't deserve to be called a god. She was never a god, only a monster. The people of ■■ will awaken. The lies end here. The sacrifices end here.</color><i>
<i><color=#7683a2>Next time, he will do it again. As many times as it takes, he will stand in their way. This is his true purpose.</color><i>

<color=#7683a2>However, Langley Blackett of the 9th Agency offered him a chance: an experiment.
She would transfer the Underground creation into a new, more "reliable" body, testing whether the vessel could influence his humanity. Concurrently, the process would serve as a stress test for her own Sinner power.

Success would yield a potent weapon against the Underground and the Black Rings, permissible under heavy surveillance.
Failure, conversely, would measure her Causality's efficacy against such Underground entities.

In her assessment, the odds favored the former.

<color=#7683a2>The evidence was written on his broken form. Found in a wretched state, S-247 bore the marks of dozens of lethal Underground sorceries, his life nearly extinguished by them. And the final proof lay strewn around him: the bodies of his former kin.

Regardless of his past, this defector had drawn his line, in blood.
The slaughter was finally over. He could no longer remember how many times he had died, nor how many he had slain. It no longer mattered. He won. Now, time to celebrate.

speaker: Underground Elder
content: I should never have saved you! Not once, never! I should've let you die right there! I should've killed you myself!!

speaker: Underground Elder
content: How could you do this?! You are my—
<i><color=#7683a2>Maybe it's better this way. No more hesitation. No regret. Just forward, with no way back.</color><i>
<i><color=#7683a2>Everything, after all these years, comes down to this one answer: the only true faith for a man who believes in nothing.</color><i>
Urgh... AAAAHHH—!!

speaker: The 9th Agency Report
content: From that day on, he became the Underground's mortal enemy.

<color=#fb9259><size=50>N.F. 106
Navigator Observatory - Surface Ruins</color>
<i>The third Black Ring. And still, I'm alive.<i>
<i>Though... this might be what death feels like, anyway.<i>
His memories were adrift, scattering and sinking in a disordered tide. Only those anchored to the Black Rings remained constant.
How he wished he could tell ${PlayerName}. The vigilance he had once upheld was now matched by a desperate hope: that ${PlayerName} might glimpse the truth through the shackles.
—With these thoughts filling his mind, he opened his eyes. In the silence, shadows drew near, pulling him back from his memory.

N.F. 115
The Rust
A handful of Underground assassins emerge from the shadows, silent puppets at their heels. Only one steps forward to speak.

speaker: Undergrounder
content: ...Arrogant as ever. You still dare to come here.

speaker: Rust
content: But of course. You are the very reason I cling to this wretched existence.

speaker: Rust
content: Shouldn't you all be minding the Third Black Ring now? I'm touched you'd make time for me.

speaker: Undergrounder
content: You interfered... You leaked our intelligence to the Overground. Uprooted the seeds we'd sown. Years of planning, undone because of you.

speaker: Undergrounder
content: You created risks where there should have been none.

speaker: Rust
content: Heh. Well, I did learn from the best.

He is ready for a fight; he always knew they would come. Just as he understands the Underground, his old friends from there understand him just as well. They know he always returns to where it all began.

Can he win? Hard to say. This body’s been put through too much; it’s close to its limit. If he dies… at least the shackles on him will finally break.. Might even spare that person the trouble of worrying and chasing after him every day.
At least he has said everything. He has readied himself for battle, coming back to life once again to take his place at the gambling table.
Then, his foe speaks, and the words stop him cold.

speaker: Undergrounder
content: ...You could still come back.

speaker: Rust
content: ...Back to where?

speaker: Undergrounder
content: Home.

speaker: Undergrounder
content: There are those willing to plead your case before the priest. Even the Sage has agreed to hear you out... All you have to do is come back.
[Scene Change: MBCC]

A calculated interference drowns out the shackles' connection. Your search leads you from one empty location to the next, only to find pieces of flesh he left behind. By the time the emergency transmission from the monitoring station reaches you, far too much time has already passed.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Not BR-005... He's near the Rust? Same fluctuation pattern as last time?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I see. I'm on my way! To the BR-001 ruins, now!
[The Ruins]
Time itself appears to freeze within the ruins. The churning roar of the contamination nearly drowns out the memory of that whispered offer.

speaker: Rust
content: ...Why would you want me back? I'm not exactly a free man now.

speaker: Rust
content: Besides, I thought your creed had no room for forgiveness. For traitors, least of all.

speaker: Undergrounder
content: Did you tell them where the Holy City lies? Did you sell the Shepherd's secrets?

speaker: Undergrounder
content: ...Exactly. Those wretches have not found the gate to ■■. Not a single believer has fallen by your hand... That proves your conscience is not entirely lost.

speaker: Undergrounder
content: The Third Black Ring was the work of that Bai woman. You were deceived. Captured by that Spider, tortured, brainwashed... They caged you in a body not your own, tried to twist your faith with a swine's memories, and forced you to dance on their strings.

speaker: Undergrounder
content: Even then, you did not sell out your kin... That is why some of us cannot bring ourselves to forsake you.

speaker: Undergrounder
content: Many remember what you sacrificed for us. Many refuse to let that memory die. Cutting you loose... proved more difficult than we thought.
<i><color=#7683a2>...Don't say that.</color><i>

speaker: Undergrounder
content: We already killed you once. Shattered that filthy puppet-shell; broke the Spider's chains. The role is over. Will you not finally wake up?

speaker: Undergrounder
content: Cast off the memories that fog your mind. Reclaim your faith. The Underground shows no mercy to traitors, but you're different.

speaker: Undergrounder
content: You were merely led astray. Blinded by base instinct, by sentiment... It is... understandable. We can look past that.

speaker: Undergrounder
content: Every misstep you took was born from love for them.
<i><color=#7683a2>...You never cared.</color><i>

speaker: Undergrounder
content: The Third Black Ring is no longer hidden. Our Shepherd's power grows, and the Sages are prepared. When the moment comes, <color=#fb9259>she</color> will rise from the Underground and scour the world clean of all opposition.

speaker: Undergrounder
content: Come back. It is not too late to atone. Serve, redeem yourself, and walk the path of greatness once more. The Holy City will receive you. Return to ■■, or at least to the old man's side.

speaker: Undergrounder
content: He remembers little now. But he still asks for you.
It's a trap. He knows this all too well. They repeat the same lines every time, each one a blade aimed at the same exposed nerve.
...And yet, how he loathes it.
His pulse thunders in his ears. His voice speaks before his mind can intervene, repeating the same futile, damning question yet again.

speaker: Rust
content: ...If I went back... what awaits me?

speaker: Rust
content: Are you all still down in that hole, lining up to offer yourselves to the Black Rings... to her?
The figure before him offers no answer, only lifting their chin in haughty pride.
Of course. About this, at least, they never lie.

speaker: Rust
content: ...Hah. Damn it all.

speaker: Rust
content: It sure sounds like home...

speaker: Rust
content: Ugh... Stubborn fools are the worst!

speaker: Undergrounder C
content: Argh!

This is a strike years in the making. His hesitation ends; his resolve snaps forward with a speed his foe could never predict. Though they share the same resilient curse, Rust holds the darker pedigree—he has died more times and been reforged more cruelly in the Black Rings' endless agony. In that fleeting advantage, the traitor's attack finds its mark in the old friend's chest.

speaker: Undergrounder C
content: Fool... This chance we fought to give you, and you—

speaker: Rust
content: I've worn too many skins to remember who you are. My apologies.

speaker: Rust
content: The Black Rings' <color=#fb9259>blessing</color> is the only reason I'm still breathing. So you see... that leaves me with just one simple purpose in life.

The thought of that face tightens Rust's grip. He unleashes a deeper, hungrier power. Why merely kill and let his foe collect a prize from the Black Rings again? True mercy is a cleaner end: to consume him utterly—flesh, spirit, all of it—leaving nothing to return.

speaker: Rust
content: You were so eager to throw your lives away. Might as well die by my hand. Consider it your final contribution to the Black Rings. A noble sacrifice, wouldn't you agree?

speaker: Rust
content: Now, now, don't look at me like that. You know what I am.

speaker: Rust
content: I'm used to it by now.
He ignites the Mania within. The zealot's form liquefies under its heat, and the molten residue is absorbed into Rust's being.

speaker: Undergrounder C
content: Heh... Hehehe... She will come soon... bearing the shackles of rebirth... to guide us toward transcendence...

speaker: Undergrounder C
content: But you... You...

speaker: Interwoven Memories
content: Traitor!! Ungrateful wretch!! Blasphemous vermin!!!

Their venomous curses wash over him like a balm. Yes, this is for the best. Give him no room to question, no reason to falter. He has chosen to be a traitor, and their hatred is the finest prize he can collect. No matter how many bodies he wears or whose memories tangle with his own, that will never change.
At last, Rust dissolves the man's consciousness and flesh, imprisoning and plundering everything he once was. The killing is complete, sealed with an embrace.

speaker: Rust
content: ...Rest here... Don't go to that place. Don't become fodder for monsters...

speaker: Rust
content: You have made it far enough...

He lays down the only remaining raincoat and buries it in a shallow grave. The night falls quiet once more. He has bestowed death upon an unfortunate old friend, and lived on himself, again. And now...
It is time to bear the madness the dead have left behind.

speaker: Mine Guard
content: Bastard... Traitor... You're the one who should be dead... Die with us...

speaker: Underground Elder
content: May the Mania consume you... May the Black Rings claim you... And I... I curse you forever...

speaker: Underground Elder
content: In life and death, may you never know peace...

It is always like this. New flesh and blood, once absorbed, shatter the delicate equilibrium inside him. His consciousness tears apart, only to be crudely kneaded back together—a bloody, aberrant mess that plunges him into brief, howling chaos.

Dying and returning to the Black Rings now would be such a waste... This vessel hasn't given out yet. Stubborn thing. Might as well push it a little further. It's not my first time being hunted. No room for sentiment.
He staggers upright, willing his leaden legs to carry him on.
As long as I'm breathing, I have a role to play. The choice was made long ago. No turning back now. Keep moving. See it through... There's only this one path I can take, anyway...
Someone else is coming, and they look familiar... An old friend, perhaps?

speaker: Thorn"?
content: ...That Undergrounder again?! Chief! Be careful!!
Ah... A gun rises in the newcomer's hand, its aim steady on his chest. Another life-taker, then. Yet a strange familiarity washes over Rust, and without thinking, his shoulders loosen.

speaker: Blurred Figure
content: Hold on, don't shoot! He's not an enemy!
A second blurred shape pushes down the raised gun. In a frantic rush, they close the distance and grasp his hand—so rotten that it's seeping with contamination.

speaker: Blurred Figure
content: Rust, are you alright? Just hang on, I can help you. The shackles might stabilize your condition. Let me try, okay?
[Release the shackles]
A red light drives into him, an unexpected warmth laced with calm, power, and an unshakeable will. If anything in this world can tear apart a body cursed by the Black Rings, this is surely it.
But wait... Wake up. He should know this. He must remember who the master of this power is.

speaker: Rust
content: ...The shackles...

speaker: Rust
content: You're... the <color=#fb9259>Shepherd</color>...
The blurred shape in front of him sharpens into clarity. There. This is the end he has chased across a lifetime. The single purpose for which he has refused to die.
[Flashback]

speaker: Shepherd???
content: ...Good. The "shackles" have been well-fed. One step closer to your "god"...

speaker: Shepherd???
content: Congratulations. Your sacrifices weren't in vain.
[Exit Flashback]
Rust smiles, dazed, and slowly closes his hand around the one extended toward him.

speaker: Rust
content: Finally... I found you...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Ngh—!!

speaker: Thorn"?
content: Chief?!
His hand closes over yours. His living flesh spreads rapidly, a warm, invasive weave across your skin. You feel it burrowing into your veins, a current of death rushing toward your mind.
