You look down and meet his eyes. Rust's smile is sincere, his crimson gaze holding yours with an absolute, fervent resolve. It is not hate that burns there, but something far more consuming.

speaker: Rust
content: It's because of you... They're all so stubborn because of you...

speaker: Rust
content: As long as you're alive, nothing can change... So...

speaker: Rust
content: I've waited so long for this. Can you please just die?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Wait, you—

Does he not feel it? Even as he corrupts you, the color drains rapidly from his own flesh. His life is bleeding away. The shackles have instinctively triggered their protection. Every inch closer he presses only drives him further onto Death's scythe.

speaker: Rust
content: Please... just die...
His voice fades, yet his hold on your hand is unyielding. He clings to you, to the very shackles burning in your palm, and with a desperate stubbornness, draws you nearer.

You shout the restraining order. Spikes of light rip through his already shattered body once more. He coughs up blood, yet his smile only widens. His grip is not relenting, pulling you ever closer. The crimson spike from your palm is already buried in his chest.
And through the shackles, his consciousness touches yours again. From somewhere deep within the chaos, you hear a faint voice.

speaker: Rust
content: <size=30>Now... I can finally... die...
In that single, shattering moment, you finally see his true purpose. And then... pure, unthinking fury takes you.
[Release the shackles]
<i><color=#7683a2>This is it, then?</color><i>
<i><color=#7683a2>...Finally.</color><i>
[Bright Hospital Bed - Syndicate; Use the Eastside daytime one if it doesn't look comfortable enough]
Sunlight streams through the windows, illuminating a spotless room. A stark contrast to the filth that haunts his nightmares.
For a moment, he believes he's still dreaming, or that death has claimed him once more.
Then he turns. ${PlayerName} is right there, sitting beside the bed. The instant their eyes meet, the expression on that face hardens into undisguised anger.
Only then does the memory rush back... So he brought him back.
female_content: Only then does the memory rush back... So she brought him back.

speaker: Rust
content: ...As expected. You found me again, Chief, and so quickly. A promise made, a promise kept. I'm impressed.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You've been out for a week. I was starting to wonder if you'd wake up at all.

speaker: Rust
content: Are you angry? Ah... now I remember.

speaker: Rust
content: My apologies. I seem to have mistaken you for someone else and acted... rather uncouthly. I hope I didn't hurt you?
You glare at him.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm not the one wrapped up like a mummy in a hospital bed, after all.
You glare at him.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: An "agent" who can't be left alone for five minutes without getting himself killed? I'd be surprised if you could so much as scratch me.

speaker: Rust
content: Haha... Don't worry. Thanks to Mania, this body heals rather quickly. I'll be back on my feet in no time. Please, don't mind it.
To hell with that. You do mind it—a lot.

options: Heals quickly, so that gives you license to throw your life away?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The way you fight out there isn't how a disciplined agent operates. Do you have a death wish?

speaker: Rust
content: ...But death doesn't mean much to me. Sooner or later, the Black Rings will bring me back.

speaker: Rust
content: Besides... I did tell you. The disciplined agent you remember died two years ago. The "Rust" you see now... different body, different person. Perhaps a little more unhinged. Sorry to disappoint.

speaker: Rust
content: Maybe next time I come back, I could choose a form you'd prefer?

speaker: Rust
content: Whatever you like. I could return as a woman, if that suits you better.
[1 second of empty scene] Add a shattering glass sound effect to indicate the Chief's composure is breaking.

options: ...Does death really mean nothing to you?

speaker: Rust
content: Well, it's happened more than once, and I've tried a few ways. I'm quite used to it by now. Maybe next time, you can let me fully experience what it's like to be... erased by the shackles.

A memory stirs within his body. It's the phantom echo of the shackles that had pierced him not long ago. He had felt it all with perfect, excruciating clarity: through his chest, between his ribs, the impossible nearness to his beating heart... a most peculiar, intimate violation.
While those shackles leave other Sinners unharmed, they ravage a body like his. And yet, the pain had left behind a craving for more.

speaker: Rust
content: Quite a remarkable power, really. If you wanted, you could tear me apart without much effort. In theory, you could even keep my consciousness from returning to the Black Rings. After all, the shackles have quite the appetite, even greater than the Rings...

speaker: Rust
content: ...Heh. That might even count as a release. Not the worst way to go, honestly...
His words hang in the air, met only by a heavy, rigid silence. You let the quiet stretch for a long, deliberate moment before finally speaking.

options: ...I've said it before. Don't talk like that.

content: ${PlayerName} is furious. Rust doesn't need to guess; the air itself is thick with it. Since his body hasn't died, the memories from not long ago are still perfectly clear.
[Enter Flashback: The Battlefield at the End of Phase 3]

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What nonsense is that?! Don't you have things you must do? Weren't you the one who threw away your past just to keep moving forward? Weren't you supposed to be stubborn as hell?!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Then stop talking about dying! Open your damn eyes! You've cheated death over and over. This time is no different! No matter how much it hurts, you keep living! Even if it's just out of pure spite! You still have debts to pay, so get up!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Don't you dare use my hands to find your way out. I won't kill you. If you're going to drag me into this, then here's my answer—

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: LIVE! YOU ARE NOT ALLOWED TO DIE!!
[Exit Flashback]
Silhouetted against the dying sun, your face is lost in shadow. But the shackles within him sing with your fury, a clear and violent signal.
And in that moment, he finally understands the terrible weight of his words.

speaker: Rust
content: ...Sorry. That was a poor joke.

speaker: Rust
content: I won't say it again.

Is it the bandages and the hospital bed, the undeniable image of frailty? His trademark composure, usually so effortless and infuriating, is completely stripped away. For the first time, he looks capable of genuine reflection.
...Or perhaps it's no act. His eyes are open but unfocused, seeing nothing in this room. This raw, unguarded emptiness feels less like an act and more like the truth of him.

speaker: Rust
content: ...I've been unfair to you. I always believed I was resolute in my purpose, but now I see... secretly seeking death only proves there's a part of me I never acknowledged. A rather pathetic part.

speaker: Rust
content: But you have my word: even if I don't exactly cherish my life, I'm not so eager to accept death, either.

speaker: Rust
content: After all, dying just means my consciousness returns to those nauseating Black Rings. One moment of carelessness, and I'd be dissolved, absorbed... devoured. The thought alone is unbearable. I'd fight with everything I have to escape alive. I'd crawl out if I had to.

speaker: Rust
content: Perhaps that's the only thing that's kept me going this long.
He doesn't look at you. His focus retreats to the bandages swathing his hands. The unnatural, ashen grey of his skin persists, and the wounds visible beneath the gauze are stark and bloodless.

speaker: Rust
content: ...I lost any real sense of being alive a long time ago. I've lasted this long only because of the Black Rings' <color=#fb9259>curse</color>. So... I have only one purpose left.

speaker: Rust
content: To repel the Black Rings and to stop the fanatics spreading them, whatever it takes. For that end, I'm willing to be your ally. I will support you. And I will protect you... because you matter.

speaker: Rust
content: But I can't promise you—nor can I pretend—that I'll cherish my life. The path I've chosen is dangerous. I could die at any moment, become trapped in a Black Ring, and have to claw my way back for who knows how long.

speaker: Rust
content: ...And by the time I'm back, a person's entire lifetime may have already passed.
Another long silence settles. At last, his gaze shifts, finding you once more.

speaker: Rust
content: Chief, use your shackles on me. Your power seems able to glimpse memories even I can't see clearly. So do it now; see as much as you can while you have the chance.

speaker: Rust
content: In my case, the concept of "life" is quite unpredictable. If I can leave you with something of value, that alone would be worth celebrating.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Don't talk like that. Don't act like your life means nothing.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're not alive just for some great "cause." And your life is not just about you alone...

speaker: Rust
content: Sorry to disappoint. But some people are just that stubborn.

speaker: Rust
content: After all... it's the only thing they can hold onto.

He stops you with a smile, offering his hand. The meaning is plain: use the shackles on him. It is indeed the most efficient way. No surveillance needed, no lies to untangle, no suspicion to hold. Besides...
It seems he can still find the dark memories—the ones he fled, the ones he buried. He offers them to you, trusting you to use them well. But...

speaker: Rust
content: Why not? Isn't this exactly what you need most?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What I need, I'll find on my own. Besides, I've had people test it.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The shackles can't peer into someone's soul. They've never shown me what I want to see. That time I saw those memories... that was actually you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: People like you, with ties to the Black Rings... It seems you can channel your thoughts through Mania in reverse, feeding them into the shackles. Into me. After realizing that, I can't help but wonder one thing...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Why was it that the memories strong enough to reach me weren't about duty, or the mission, or the path, or the Black Rings—all the things you're always going on about—but the past you keep saying you've let go of?
Seeing the look on his face, you can't help but laugh out loud.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You didn't even realize it yourself, Mr. Agent? Haha. If you care that much about the people you left behind, stop pretending you don't.

speaker: Rust
content: ...There you go again. Once you've made up your mind about something, you can be rather unreasonable.

options: I don't need to be reasonable.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Call it a hope, then. Mine, and others'. That you'd value these bonds as much as we do.
You place the torn letter of will in front of him—a farewell that Thorn refused to accept.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I didn't tell him anything. The 9th Agency followed confidentiality protocols, too.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But after what happened at the Rust, I think he's pieced it together.
[Enter Flashback]

speaker: Thorn
content: ...I know he's not an enemy. I just...
[Exit Flashback]

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Thorn asked me to tell you: "The living don't write farewells. If you have something to say, say it to my face."

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And the shop owner, Samuel... and everything else you've tried to leave with me? I'm not accepting any of it. I'm not the one who owes them, the one they want to see. You're still here, so go take care of it yourself.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Say what you need to say to them yourself. Whether you're in a different body, whether you stay silent or out of sight... you might find fewer people care about those things than you think.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Maybe... there are more people out there who don't care where you came from or what you've become. They just want to know how you're doing now.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It doesn't matter how many faces, voices, bodies, or memories you've worn. These past years—every time you threw yourself into the fray—it left a mark. You changed things. And people remember.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: After all that... do you still think being alive isn't real? That death is something you can just treat lightly?

speaker: Rust
content: ...I see.
He remains silent, head bowed, as if physically weighed down by his thoughts. Time stretches before he finally answers, his voice soft.

speaker: Rust
content: ...I don't have an answer. Not yet. Maybe... we can talk about it next time?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Every time you say that, you vanish at the first chance. Is that the plan again?
He smiles awkwardly.

speaker: Rust
content: Heh, no, not this time. I really do want to think it over. After all... I've never looked at it this way before.
He tilts his head back, gaze fixed on the ceiling as he searches for something true.

But then, the world intrudes: the warmth of sunlight, the faint aroma of bedside flowers, the softness of the blanket, the rhythmic drip of an IV, the sterile bite of disinfectant, even the deep, long-forgotten ache in his bones. These sensations—so vivid, so mundane—rush in like a tide, washing away his still-forming thoughts.

The "spy"—who has been wound tighter than a spring for lifetimes—finally lets his guard down. A deep, bone-weary exhaustion claims him. He wants to keep talking to ${PlayerName}, but a warm, reassuring drowsiness pulls him under completely.

speaker: Rust
content: ...Give me some time, Chief. This question... it might actually matter.

Outside the door, a nurse catches your eye and gestures you over. Schorl appears in the doorway. If it's here, it's either that they've set their eyes on Rust, or there's a big job for you. Given the timing, it's likely something has flared up in Fraser again. Either way, your time here is up.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The staff will look after you. Get well soon; there are people waiting for answers. And don't think about running away. MBCC has the room secured, and the bed's fitted with restraints. I'm not making the same mistake twice. You—
The words die on your lips. His breathing has deepened, eyes shuttered, his expression softened by an unfamiliar, unguarded smile.
With a soft sigh, you gently pull the blanket to his shoulders and let yourself out, the door clicking shut behind you without a sound.
[Hospital Ward, Night]
Rust is telling the truth. That night, escape is the furthest thing from his mind. He surrenders to sleep, and it takes him deeply.
In that depth, the inescapable shadow of the Black Rings is finally absent. In its place come older dreams... memories worn smooth by time.
[Flashback]

speaker: Underground Elder
content: Brat... you understand me? Quit... quit your crying. You're already lucky. The Black Ring didn't take you... and lucky again, that I found you.

speaker: Underground Elder
content: Come here. Dry your face. You'll eat what I eat. I brought you here... I won't let you die.
[Flashback Scene Change]

speaker: Underground Elder
content: You want a name? Then I'll go ask the priest—
<i><color=#7683a2>No. You give me one.</color><i>
<i><color=#7683a2>You took my old name. You owe me a new one.</color><i>

speaker: Underground Elder
content: ...What a pain. You're not some Overground swine. What do you need a name for...

speaker: Underground Elder
content: ...Alright. I'll call you ■■■. Was my kid's name. Take it.
[Memories Overlap]

speaker: Mine Guard
content: That name of yours is a mouthful, little Outlander. Can't have everyone stumbling over it every time.

speaker: Mine Guard
content: How about a nickname? Makes things easier. Neighbors will remember it.

speaker: Mine Guard
content: You'll be here a long time. Think of it as a new start. How's ■■ sound? Or pick one yourself.
[Memories Overlap]

speaker: Thorn
content: ■■■■?! Thank god you're back! It's ■■. You remember me?

speaker: Thorn
content: ...Right. Codenames now. I'm "Thorn." Got it? And you're "Rust." We both work for the 9th Agency. Partners.

speaker: Thorn
content: "Rust"... does the name ring any bells? That's what everyone calls you.
[Scene Change]

speaker: Shop Owner
content: ...Honestly, just knowing he's alright is enough. He was a regular, you know? My old boss thought about him for two whole years, came up with new dishes he never got to try. If you see him... tell him to visit. I can at least try to cook a few of the old ones.
[Scene Change]

speaker: Samuel
content: If you hear anything about him, good or bad, let us know.

speaker: Samuel
content: He'll always be a friend of Rustfire.
[Chief's portrait]

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I want to know your real name.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No matter where you go, how many times you die, what body you use, or what your mission is... you are my friend.
[Back to Reality]
On this rare night free from nightmares, he wakes long before dawn. For a timeless stretch, he simply stares at the ceiling, his thoughts unmoored and drifting.

speaker: Rust
content: ...This won't do.

His hand comes up, pressing against the fissures marring his body... Good. He hasn't slipped too far. He can still hear it—the distant call of the Black Rings, the susurrus of voices whispering from beyond the chaos.
A sound he hasn't heard in a long time. If only it had come earlier... the shackles might have heard it, too. A cruel twist of fate.
<i><color=#7683a2>...Right on schedule.</color><i>

speaker: Rust
content: Heh... Time to get moving.

Rust pushes himself up and retrieves a small, concealed device. Only a select few official hospitals can handle a case like his. He had scouted each one long in advance, preparing for exactly this moment.
Well, well. Right on cue, here comes his informant.
[Scene Change] Outside MBCC Gate
Hey there, handsome. Wanna settle your tab before skipping town?

He turns. The assassin in white is already there, leaning against the doorframe. No one saw her approach. With her preternatural speed, she slipped past every surveillance system once again, proving it a hollow joke just like the 9th Agency's house arrest.

speaker: Bai Yi
content: Bailing you out last week wasn't cheap. Doubling my fee this time sounds perfectly reasonable, don't you think? Need my help again?

speaker: Rust
content: By all means. The 9th Agency is covering it. Name your price.

speaker: Rust
content: Your only concern should be whether you'll live long enough to spend it.

speaker: Bai Yi
content: No sweat. I'm quick on my feet. Even if that woman shows up, she won't catch me. But you...

speaker: Bai Yi
content: Didn't you say you'd wait for them and never run? What's with the sudden change of heart?
Rust pauses, then smiles.

speaker: Rust
content: I'd never run from the Undergrounders. But now... there's someone far more intimidating.
If he stays any longer, leaving may become unthinkable, in every sense of the word. But... that must wait. For now.

speaker: Rust
content: Call it a tactical retreat. I did leave him a note, after all.
female_content: Call it a tactical retreat. I did leave her a note, after all.

content: [MBCC Office]

Your drawer is open, the cameras are blind. That man used his last "escape" to case the place—this time, getting back in was effortless. Five Hypercubes are missing from the count. And he even had the nerve to leave a message on your desk.

<i>Dear Chief,

A job came up on short notice that requires some traveling. Forgive me for not saying goodbye in person. My remaining time here must go toward settling other personal debts. And if I delay any longer... well, leaving might become difficult in more ways than one.
So, my apologies. Please don't exhaust yourself using the shackles to track me down. I've copied the MBCC's contact information. Once I arrive, I'll be in touch.

I've also borrowed a small sum for the trip. I promise to repay it with interest—along with that answer I still owe you.

Rust<i>
You crush the note in your fist, then fling it to the corner.

—He guessed you would react this way. Rust smiles, the expression tinged with reluctance, as he turns from you and the fragile sense of life he'd briefly held. He steps into the DisSea Black Ring, letting its depths absorb him, returning to the inescapable road he must walk alone.
But the promise he leaves behind... this time, he means it.
<i>No matter the body I wear, the deaths I endure, or the years that slip by... I will repay every debt I owe you.<i>

Rookie, I've heard that you've been gathering info on Mania, Corruptors, and DisSea. I believe you've already noticed the truth is related to your past. Your intelligence work seems to have met a bottleneck, which is normal, since some things are not accessible to you yet. I'll give you a little hint though: Go ask the Sinner you've recently detained. NOX, the living person closest to the truth of DisSea. Good luck, rookie.

speaker: NOX
content: The end is still far away from you... Do you need saving too?
Saving? No one needs your saving here.
Just as you enter the interrogation room and sit down facing NOX, she throws out a somewhat strange question.
This is an interrogation, Sinner NOX. I ask, you answer. This is your duty.
NOX does not respond. You've expected this.

Based on your past interrogation experience, this guarantees a tough interrogation, especially when interacting with this kind of Sinner, who's unresponsive with a fractured mind, but extremely powerful and aggressive.
But this is no excuse to back down. You open the file on the desk—It's the best starting point for this interrogation.
test
test
test
test
test
test
NOX shows no response to what you're doing, not even sparing a peek at the documents on the desk.
Do you know about the Sinner Grim Reaper?
NOX's pale pupils remain lightless.
The Ghost of DisSea, Night Terror, Calamity Witch... You must have at least heard of one of these?
These figures from urban legends, or should I say, horror stories, have been around for almost thirty years. Do you really have no idea at all?
Your victims must have said something with their last breath, no?

speaker: NOX
content: ...You want to hear it?
I need to know.
Dark gray mist pours out from NOX's body. The interrogation room is suddenly filled with many desperate, throaty cries.
Stay away.
Don't kill me.
Kill her!
Kill me...
Several seconds later, the wails surrounding your ears subside. Cold sweat has wetted the back of your shirt.
Your anxiety isn't only caused by your fear of NOX's mysterious ability, but also mostly induced by the unignorable fear and despair in those cries.
Can I interpret that as you're admitting you're indeed the Sinner Grim Reaper?

speaker: NOX
content: I've never called myself that, but...

speaker: NOX
content: ...I like that name.
NOX doesn't deny her identity as the Sinner Grim Reaper.
Since N.F. 84, the authorities have received in total 639 sighting reports of the Grim Reaper. Among them, 511 cases are free of injury records and 27 cases have been closed.
The culprits for the remaining 101 cases are still unidentified. Were all these unsolved cases...
Your doing?
NOX's hollow eyes resemble an unperturbed lake surface. With her mental state, it may be a bit difficult to understand the concept of a case.
The victims come from everywhere in Syndicate and Eastside, including regular civilians, merchants, gangsters, and even FAC officers.
Let me help you recall: the Red Falcon's former leader Usman, Eastside energy business owner Rovi Dante, the FAC's Task Force member Dustin Hertz...

speaker: NOX
content: Names are meaningless.
NOX interrupts you.
If you didn't even know their identities, what was your motive?

speaker: NOX
content: Because I heard the voices in their hearts. I heard the calls...

speaker: NOX
content: They wanted to survive.
What NOX just said somehow stirs up anger and anxiety within you.
You killed them because they wanted to survive?!

speaker: NOX
content: I was saving them.

speaker: NOX
content: The barrier has to be removed, in order to resist the summoning of DisSea.
Without passion, without obsession, NOX says that in an icy tone.
It's exactly because you've studied NOX's Sinner ability, what she's saying now sounds even more twisted and eerie.
test
test
test
test
test
test
test
You still remember clearly the conclusion of the report:

...The assessment report from the Research Institute has validated our hypothesis: the subject's body simultaneously shows multiple traits of Sinners and Corruptors...
...
We are unable to accurately describe her Sinner ability. But one thing is certain: Through a particular means, the subject can rob a dying person of their vitality in the form of an abstract idea and transform it into the foundation of her own existence. Current theories cannot explain the mechanism of this ability.
...
Based on existing information, the subject severely undermines safety and poses potential threats, therefore it is not recommended to use her in battles at this stage.
"Through a particular means, the subject can rob a dying person of their vitality in the form of an abstract idea and transform it into the foundation of her own existence..."
Saving is only a lie.
In essence, your ability is to rob others of their lives.
NOX falls silent for a while.

speaker: NOX
content: Individual souls are too feeble. The only way is to cling onto... us.

speaker: NOX
content: The craving for life and the resistance to death... Our collective will.
Us? She refers to herself as us?
Insane assumptions have occupied your mind. What if NOX is not one person, but a group of people...

speaker: NOX
content: But this is wrong... I...
While you're absorbed in analyzing the situation in your mind, NOX's state is showing significant changes.
She's mumbling to herself, struggle and confusion flicker in her eyes.

speaker: NOX
content: This is the only way to evade death... It's also... our promise...
The slight resistance vanishes quickly and completely, and the cruel icy stare is locked on you once again.

speaker: NOX
content: You are... Very dangerous.

speaker: NOX
content: We, must save you!
Heaps of dark gray mist flow out of NOX's body. Instinctively, you sense danger.
You immediately stand up and apply the shackles. A power strong enough to subdue any Sinner coming from the depths of your mind surges toward NOX.
But the moment it touches NOX, those terrifying wails once again ring in your ears, pierce through your ear drums, and reach directly into your consciousness...
I don't want to die!
Help me!
I don't want to become like that...
Mon... ster...
You stand in the center of a large factory with a fractured left leg, surrounded by corpses. The broken tibia has ripped open the skin, yet you can't feel any pain at all.
You don't know why you're in the middle of an escape in this place. Like muscle memory, those words surge to your throat, and you say them like fulfilling a duty.
Kill those damned traitors... Kill them...
Kill everyone in sight...
Intense cough interrupts your mumbling. Coagulated blood clots fall onto the ground. The air is filled with a pungent rusty smell.
The club belongs to me...
Don't you dare take it away from me!
The bloodshot conjunctiva colors your vision red, but you still see the useless leg being wrapped by a layer of wriggling black silt.
The entire left leg gets covered rapidly.
Facing this unsettling sight, the previous thirst for blood and vengeful desire are overwhelmed by fear.
No! No! Don't come near! I don't want to die!
Get off me!
You stab the dagger hard into your left leg, trying your best to scrape off that damned silt. But it's engulfed the knife-holding hand, slithers along the arm, and charges at you.
Back off! Back off!
I don't want to die...
Somebody help me...
As if answering your plea, a shadow emerges in the dark. She's looking at you, but at the same time seems like she's looking at something else.
No, I don't belong here... Are you here to take me away? Or...
Swish—
In place of her answer, you hear the sound of a sharp weapon slicing through a body.
Your vision tilts gradually. Everything in your sight is spinning.
When you come back to consciousness, the shadow has already disappeared. You hear the wind and your own heavy breaths—You find yourself running in a dark alley.
Damn it, damn it! Where are the sheriffs?
Where are those idiots when you need them?

Lacking regular training, your body finally reaches its limit. You lean against a lamppost and support your chest with your right arm in a cast. You bend down and gasp for air, your heart almost leaping out of your chest.
You decide to stop running. There's gotta be a way to deal with this.
The cast on your right arm hides your secret weapon, the gift given to you by that guy dressed in gray two years ago.

You've made it through several assassination and revenge attempts with it. Be it perfectly equipped assassins or Sinners with mysterious powers, there hasn't been one person who could survive after being hit by it.

<size=32>It does come with a strange side effect though—ever since a certain assassination attempt, it's fused with the nerves of your right arm, undetachable no matter how hard you try. But now as you're gripping it, the pounding of your heart is gradually slowing down.</size>
Only in times like this, I'll be glad I still have this thing with me...
I'm not gonna die here. This time tomorrow, I'll still be a rising star in Eastside's business scene. No one can drag me down!
From under a street light not far away, a lanky shadow spreads to your feet.
Here you are...
Simon paid you to kill me, didn't he?
The shadow approaches step by step without responding.
Whatever sum that pauper offered you, I'll pay you ten times more.
Whether it's power or status, as long as you can name it, there's nothing I can't buy.
The shadow is still silent. The face as pale as that of a corpse is gradually exposed under the dim street light.
Wait! I have an agreement with the Reagan family. You can't kill me...
You feign fear as you back away, discreetly aiming the cast on your right arm at her.
Die!
Twelve dark red light beams pour onto the woman in front of you.
You have to admit that, although it's the worst to have to do it yourself, you still feel extremely relieved as you're pulling the trigger.

You've already thought up a plan to deal with the aftermath in your head—call the esteemed councilor to explain the situation and ask him to take care of it for you. It's only a matter of money, anyway.
Then you'll go home and take a hot shower. It'll be all over.
The dark red light is sliced up by a weirdly shaped weapon. The woman before you is completely unharmed and continues to walk toward you.

You pull the trigger in vain, and nothing comes out of the barrel anymore. You want to run for your life, but that weapon seems to have drained all your strength. Legs going limp, you kneel on the ground.
Puff!
The right arm wrapped in the cast flies up high. At that moment, for some reason, you suddenly feel relieved.
At least, finally gotten rid of it...
You feel a sharpness piercing into your chest, and something warm is drawn out of your body.
Everything before you is gradually becoming corrupted by darkness. You can't see anything, but can only feel your consciousness being dragged, heading toward the next icy death.
The cold you're feeling slowly fades away.
It's already December. Why? Did Mom pay the heating bill without telling me?
But you're still starving.
How strange, where did Mom go?
Mom!
You shout loudly. No one answers you in the pitch-black house. Mom must have gone out.
So hungry.
Tortured by intolerable hunger, you start pacing aimlessly in the house.
In the dark, you smell an aroma from the kitchen.
That's right, Mom left me something to eat in the kitchen.
You rush into the kitchen hurriedly, stuffing your mouth with the food on the floor.
Flesh mixed with fat slides down your esophagus, into your stomach, yet you don't feel satisfied at all. For no particular reason, you suddenly feel sad.
Mom... Sob... Mom...
You're crying, but your hands and mouth do not stop.
Before you notice, a woman is already standing in front of you.
Mom...?
Are you here to... pick me up...?
I'm all alone... I'm scared...
I don't want to... turn into that...
No... No, this is not me!
You scrape inside your own throat desperately, trying to fish out everything you've just swallowed.
How can I be eating this! It's... They're contaminated... contaminated...
But even though you've reached all your hand into your throat, you still don't get any abnormal feelings.
You grab the kitchen knife on the side and cut open your stomach with all your strength...
But only viscous black silt wriggling and turning into monsters... Corruptors.
...Corruptors!
The moment you recall this, a sharp pain shoots up your skull, impaling your spirit like a dagger.
This is all an illusion... I... I've come here to...!
You're walking by a lakeside that seems to extend infinitely. As the humid wind blows in your face, the intense headache surprisingly makes your mind unusually clear.
You're ${PlayerName}, the MBCC's Chief. You've been interrogating the Sinner NOX, and she attacked you...
You're very likely to be inside an illusory space constructed by her spirit—shadows are lurking everywhere around you, letting out meaningless moans.
I don't want to die...
I must live...
Why only me...
That's not enough...
I need more...
You realize the surrounding shadows have noticed your existence.
A healthy soul.
He's not one of us...
female_content: She's not one of us...

content: I want him...
female_content: I want her...

content: Sensing danger, you endure the headache and the chaotic thoughts in your head and begin running desperately. You enter a building to evade the shadows' attack.
Following a strange sense, you and the shadows circle each other for a long while, and finally you hide into a ward.
Weirdly enough, here in this place, the headache and the feeling of chaos you were having have all vanished.
On the bed, a young girl dressed in white is staring out the window at the red moon and mumbling to herself.

speaker: Maiden
content: Will there be sunshine tomorrow...
With a slender and frail figure, the girl has pale blonde long hair. A starkly different presence from the crowd of shadows out there, she seems like a misfit in this somber, twisted world.
You have a premonition that she knows the way out of here.
Excuse me, do you know...
You walk toward the girl's bed. Hearing your voice, the girl turns back, indigo eyes looking particularly bright.
But the moment she looks at you, the shadows' roars stream in from outside.

speaker: Maiden
content: Are you here to visit me?

speaker: Maiden
content: But they don't seem to welcome you...
Countless black shadows tear down the ward's room and swarm toward you, dragging your body until darkness devours you.
The lights in the interrogation room have driven out darkness. You lean against the back of your seat, feeling an inexplicable exhaustion.
Before you realize it, a full team of armed operatives has surrounded you. Leading the team, Nightingale is looking glum.
NOX has already been taken away. Having noticed you've woken up, Nightingale's expression grows softer.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, you passed out just now.

speaker: Nightingale
content: The Sinner NOX attacked you. We must take some measures...
You shake your head wearily.
I'm fine.
I think, I've already found out how to crack this problem.

speaker: Nightingale
content: ...In other words, NOX's body houses tens of thousands of souls of the dead.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Numerous minds have fused together and lost their essential sanity, leaving only the last bit of survival instinct to drive their actions.

speaker: Nightingale
content: And that girl...
She's the only person I've seen not appearing as a shadow in NOX's spiritual space. What's more, the shadow's activity is suppressed around her as well.
She's very likely the core that many of the dead attach to, the original owner of that body.
The Grim Reaper NOX is undoubtedly an immense threat to other Sinners and even to the MBCC.
But if we can confirm that girl—NOX's main personality—is not a threat, then we can try to guide her to regain control over her body.

speaker: Nightingale
content: I understand what you mean, but...
Nightingale is a little hesitant.

speaker: Nightingale
content: This is already the fourth attempt to connect to NOX's consciousness. Repeated contact with a highly contaminated Sinner like her will be a massive burden on your mind.
I have my own judgment.
Nightingale gives a sigh.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Lakeside Residence was a sanatorium built in N.F. 61 which served patients with chronic illnesses, located in the scenic area three hundred meters from the south coast of DisSea. Much data was lost after the explosion of DisSea, so we couldn't retrieve information about the girl.

speaker: Nightingale
content: But based on your description, her ward should be in the intensive care area on the sixth floor. The fire escape on the first floor's west side leads straight there. You can evade attacks from most of the shadows if you take that path.

speaker: Nightingale
content: But above all, remember who you are—${PlayerName}, The Chief of MBCC. Please never forget this.

speaker: Nightingale
content: And...

speaker: Nightingale
content: Best of luck to you.
On the other side of the glass, NOX is as silent as a corpse. You take a deep breath and wrap up your mental preparation.

options: Use the shackles to create a link

content: <size=31>Damp wind blowing in your face, you're back to that lakeside. Like the past few times, the dead's messages lingering here are flying toward you like air blades, attempting to occupy your mind—but thanks to the repeated self reminders in the preparation, you immediately recall your identity and objective.</size>

The gathering shadows have never left, still loitering around. You sneak into the sanatorium swiftly and carefully pass through the lobby and corridors following Nightingale's hints, not startling any of the shadows.
Finally, you arrive at the door of the young girl's ward.

speaker: Maiden
content: Come in.
The girl's voice pierces through the door. Without hesitation, you push open the door and enter.

speaker: Maiden
content: You're the new caretaker, right?
You close the door behind you. After what happened last time, the ward has become shabbier. Some shadows remain in the ward, but luckily they're much more tamed than the ones outside.
To avoid rousing these irrational, grudging souls, without batting an eye, you start pretending to be the caretaker the girl has mentioned.
Do you need anything from me?

speaker: Maiden
content: The previous caretaker had cleaned before leaving. I'm not hungry either...

speaker: Maiden
content: You can take a break for now. I'll let you know if I need anything.
After a wordless moment, the girl casts her glance outside the window again, but all she finds there are the red moon and incessant roars.
Not sure if caused by the cold or fear, the girl's body has been trembling the whole time.
How long have you been here?
The girl turns back.

speaker: Maiden
content: Six years.
The girl pauses, then murmurs.

speaker: Maiden
content: ...So it's already been six years.
Your condition...

speaker: Maiden
content: Systemic muscle fibrosis caused by abnormal crystal hyperplasia in soft tissues—according to the doctor.

speaker: Maiden
content: I don't understand it fully either, I only know it's very, very rare. It's said that there have only been two cases in the whole DisCity.
It must have caused you a lot of inconvenience.

speaker: Maiden
content: Indeed, a few years ago, I couldn't even stand up on my own...

speaker: Maiden
content: But it's improved a lot, now I can walk around in the ward with the caretaker's help.
The girl's smile is cheerful, although the actual situation may not be as hopeful as it sounds.
You scan the surroundings and find that the bouquet on the nightstand has already withered. Beneath the flowers, a thick pile of letters stands out particularly.
Are those from your friends?

speaker: Maiden
content: Yes, most of them are from my friends from school.

speaker: Maiden
content: Here.
Without a hint of annoyance, the girl smiles and passes the letters to you.

speaker: Maiden
content: ...Read them yourself.
Sensing your hesitation, she passes the letters to you casually.

speaker: Maiden
content: It's fine, I don't mind.

speaker: Maiden
content: It's been too long, I don't quite remember what they wrote.

speaker: Maiden
content: These past two years, my eyes... haven't been able to see very clearly. Could you read them to me, please?
You smile and take the letters, unfolding the paper.
However, the content of all the letters is covered by some kind of somber dark gray mist, as if something is stopping the girl from recalling the past.
Unable to read the blank letters for the girl, you hold up the stack of letters silently. After a long while, the girl lowers her head, a little disappointed.
They... Your friends have never visited you here?

speaker: Maiden
content: They have.

speaker: Maiden
content: They brought those flowers.
On the bare stems, several scattered dried petals and leaves are hanging.

speaker: Maiden
content: They used to come more often, but recently...
The girl has grown even sadder.

You notice the shadows in the ward becoming more active gradually, floating around in the room aimlessly. Every time a shadow passes through the girl's body, a shiver arises in her, and the room grows even chillier.

options: Try to expel them with the shackles

content: The shackles' power manages to stun the stirring shadows. They've retreated to the dark corners of the ward.

speaker: Maiden
content: ...It's fine, really. Sometimes I feel frustrated too, worried I may never see them again.
A smile reemerges on the girl's face, apparently completely oblivious of the shadows' existence and your actions.

speaker: Maiden
content: But as long as I can still see the sunrise, I can keep going.
Sunrise?

speaker: Maiden
content: You've never seen it, have you?
The girl seems a little excited.

speaker: Maiden
content: A warm morning sun that leaps out of the lake.
The girl glances at the slightly dry pale blonde hair lying on her shoulder.

speaker: Maiden
content: They don't look alike anymore... But in the past, it looked just like the color of my hair.

speaker: Maiden
content: Every time I see it, it cheers me up and makes me believe I will live on. Suddenly, my illness, all the medicine and all the treatments don't seem that scary anymore.

speaker: Maiden
content: It's a pity the weather hasn't been very nice these days, otherwise you can see it too. It's really pretty!
The girl looks out the window again. In the pitch-black sky, besides the icy red moon, there's nothing else.
I'm sure you'll get to see it, the sun always rises. When it does, I'll take you to see it.
You comfort the girl.
But there's no sun in this dark, hopeless place.
Have you ever thought about... leaving this place?

speaker: Maiden
content: Leaving?
The girl looks confused.

speaker: Maiden
content: I must stay here to nurse my illness...
You've stayed here for a long time. Have you never thought about going out for a walk sometimes?

speaker: Maiden
content: But the doctor said...

speaker: Maiden
content: No, it seems that I... That's true, why haven't I...

speaker: Maiden
content: I really miss my friends a lot. Now that I can move around... I should go visit them...

speaker: Maiden
content: How weird... How come I can't even recall their names...
As the girl is mumbling to herself, the shadows in the corners have become agitated again.
They lean into the girl's ears and whisper unsettling words.

speaker: Black Shadow
content: Must live on...

speaker: Black Shadow
content: Don't want to go back...
The girl's wavering thoughts create cracks on the already worn walls of the ward. More shadows are swarming in, charging at you, the intruder.

You try hard to suppress them with the shackles, but the number of shadows has far exceeded what you can handle. Under their tearing and biting, your headache and chaotic thoughts, which should not happen in this ward, suddenly reappear.
Time is running out, you must ask the critical question—this is also the most crucial purpose of your visit.
I have a question for you.
The girl turns her head, looking confused. The colors in her indigo eyes are fading, you must hurry up.
If there's a way that will allow you to live properly, enable you to move freely, and free you from being bound to the sickbed.
But the price is that you must kill others, take their lives, will you do it?

speaker: Maiden
content: How can I do that!
The girl shouts out her answer.

speaker: Maiden
content: That is not right, Mr.
female_content: That is not right, Miss.

speaker: Maiden
content: How can I take others' lives in order to... to...
The girl's face is flushed from her emotions, and she sounds a little incoherent. Her answer gives you confidence that what you're doing is indeed right.
But what she says next makes your heart tighten.

speaker: Maiden
content: Hold on... I think I've had certain dreams... I...

speaker: Maiden
content: I killed many people in those dreams... They didn't want to... But still I...

speaker: Maiden
content: That's not right... How could I... That's not right...

speaker: Maiden
content: That's not right, I don't want that, I must leave this place...

speaker: Maiden
content: Argh!
The girl is screaming. On the corners of the ward, cracks suddenly appear out of nowhere, and shadows are rushing in from all directions, shouting next to the girl's ears.

speaker: Dark Shadow
content: I don't want to die!

speaker: Black Shadow
content: You can't leave!

speaker: Black Shadow
content: We've made a promise!

speaker: Black Shadow
content: Kill him... Kill him!
female_content: Kill her... Kill her!

speaker: Maiden
content: I don't want that!
The girl struggles and gets up, shakes off the shadows next to her, and staggers out of the ward through the door.
You didn't expect the question to cause such a big stir. You want to stop the escaping girl but instead get dragged by countless shadows, rendering you powerless.
With the girl gone, the small ward collapses within seconds. All the memories, except for the letters you're gripping tightly, are buried in darkness.
You release the shackles' power with all your might, and the shadows dragging you get blown away, wailing.
You begin to fall.
Fall...
Fall.
You fall through the deaths of countless people, witnessing all the past memories and deaths.
Longing, bitterness, pain, despair. All emotions vanish with death, turning into endless madness.
But as you keep falling, the dark gray mist on the letters in your hands is slowly fading too. You see the girl's stolen life, see the countless blessings, and see... a name.
You need to save her, you need to help that girl take back her own life.
An indefinite length of time has passed since the initial collapse.
In the surroundings, there are only ruins and boundless darkness.

speaker: Shadow
content: Quick, wake up, get out of here.
The young girl opens her eyes and props herself up on the rubble, struggling.

speaker: Maiden
content: What is... this place?
DisSea.
Before her, a blurry shadow is making some weird noise.

speaker: Maiden
content: That's not how DisSea looks like...

speaker: Black Shadow
content: Have you forgotten?
Ice-cold memories flood the girl's mind. She kneels on the ground, tears flowing out of her gradually whitening eyes.

speaker: Maiden
content: The caretaker... and the doctor... They've all...

speaker: Black Shadow
content: There's no time to get sentimental. Look around you.
The girl looks around. The ruins are packed with countless bizarre creatures.

speaker: Maiden
content: This is...?

speaker: Black Shadow
content: Humans.

speaker: Black Shadow
content: Or perhaps I should say, most of them used to be humans.
The girl takes a few steps back fearfully.

speaker: Black Shadow
content: You want to live on, don't you?

speaker: Black Shadow
content: If you don't run now, you won't get another chance.
Without a second thought, the girl follows the shadow's advice.
It's strange. Not long ago, she was still being tormented by her illness and could barely walk without the caretaker's help.
But under that blood-red moon, she's running faster and faster, as if even pain can't catch up with her anymore.
Even so, there's no time for celebration. The surrounding monsters keep multiplying, and her fear is almost overflowing from her chest.

speaker: Maiden
content: I can't die here. I must get out...
The girl keeps running like mad, until she's coughing up blood in her breaths, until she can't feel her limbs anymore, until her heart stops, and all that remains is that small but firm will of hers.

speaker: Maiden
content: I want to watch it once more... The sunrise...
But even the firmest will will eventually get obliterated by the cruel reality.
The run is too long, so long that the girl has forgotten how much time has passed. She finally collapses over a stretch of rubble.
This spot is not very different from her starting point.

speaker: Black Shadow
content: Haha...
The shadow's hysterical laughter rings near her ears.

speaker: Black Shadow
content: Hahaha!

speaker: Black Shadow
content: Hahahaha!
Lying on the ruin, the girl still keeps groveling forward, as if not hearing that irritating laughter.

speaker: Black Shadow
content: You're alive, only you're alive. Why should it be you?

speaker: Black Shadow
content: You're a Sinner, yet you're so weak... If we were you...

speaker: Black Shadow
content: You can't make it out on your own.
The girl's arms are slightly bent, leaving a dark red trail on the rubble.

speaker: Black Shadow
content: Are you really so desperate to live on?

speaker: Black Shadow
content: Good, because we are, too.

speaker: Black Shadow
content: Accept us and become our vessel... Let's continue to live together.
The girl's body freezes for a second. Then, as the endless exhaustion and darkness overwhelm her, she blacks out.

speaker: Mutated Youngster
content: Somebody help me...

speaker: Mutated Youngster
content: I don't want to become like that...

speaker: Mutated Youngster
content: I don't want to die...
In the dim kitchen, the inhuman monster is whimpering hopelessly.
NOX raises the longsword in her hands. Her motion is too ruthless and smooth, as if she's already done this a thousand times.

speaker: Mutated Youngster
content: Mom...?

speaker: Mutated Youngster
content: Are you here to... pick me up...?
NOX pauses. She doesn't know why she's here and what exactly she's doing.

speaker: Mutated Youngster
content: I'm all alone... I'm scared...

speaker: Mutated Youngster
content: I don't want to... turn into that...
Clank!
When the longsword falls on the ground, NOX's pale gray eyes are full of agony and doubts.
At that moment, the shadow that she could never get rid of, once again appears before her.

speaker: Black Shadow
content: Kill him, and take him in.

speaker: Black Shadow
content: Just like before.
NOX stumbles backward, not responding to the shadow's provocation.

speaker: Black Shadow
content: You need to live on, like we do, so does he.

speaker: Maiden
content: This is... not living... at all...

speaker: Black Shadow
content: You must do it.

speaker: Black Shadow
content: We've made a promise.
The girl backs off desperately, but the shadow won't let her go.
Dark gray mist spurts out of the girl's body, tightening around her limbs.
Driven by the shadow, the girl picks up the longsword again. She's fighting it with her instinct, the longsword halting mid-swing in the air.

speaker: Maiden
content: I... can't...
The shadow finally covers the girl's eyes. The longsword rips through the air, and the teenage boy stops crying.
Yet the girl can be heard crying in the dark.

speaker: Maiden
content: Somebody help me...
Just like in the past, no one answers her.
The girl has lost track of time waiting in the dark.

speaker: Maiden
content: How strange, where am I? Why... am I here?

speaker: Maiden
content: I should... stop them, but... on my own, I can't do anything...

speaker: Maiden
content: Somebody help me...

speaker: Maiden
content: Who... am I...?
In the hopeless wait, her memories are starting to dwindle. Darkness is coming near, and the girl is like ashes from the remains of a fire, gradually losing brightness.
Until a beam of light breaks up an opening on the edge of the darkness. Someone's voice rouses her.
Don't give up, I'm here!
A figure is desperately squeezing into this darkness, bringing in light that is faint yet impossible to ignore.
The light illuminates the girl's sick and extremely scrawny body, as well as the countless horrible shadows crawling all over her.
I know it's painful, but... don't give up!
You want to see the sunrise, don't you? Remember? I've promised to take you out, to see DisCity's sunrise!
I'm here to fulfill my promise!
The girl looks up mechanically at the person approaching her.
Grab my hand! We'll get out of here together!
Amber!
Amber, the name in the first line of every letter. A symbol of the morning sun and hope, it rekindles the light in those pale gray eyes.
She reaches out a hand, brilliant white light shooting out from that tattered body.

speaker: Amber
content: Nino

speaker: Amber
content: Finally... you're here.
The shadows clinging onto Amber are fleeing from her body hysterically, raucous wails shaking the entire darkness.

speaker: Black Shadow
content: You can't do that, we've made a promise!

speaker: Black Shadow
content: You can't fight against DisSea on your own!

speaker: Black Shadow
content: I don't want to die, we must stay together if we want to live!

speaker: Amber
content: But this is not living at all.

speaker: Amber
content: I want to live in earnest.

speaker: Amber
content: Even if it's just for once, I want to watch the sunrise again...

speaker: Amber
content: I've had enough of you.
Amber grips that hand.
The white light expels the darkness, and the nightmarish shadows are nowhere to be seen.
Amber gives a dazzling smile.

speaker: Amber
content: Let's go.
The target has... broken free... from the constraints...!
Ensure the Chief's... safety...
Unit 3... has failed...
We can't hold her off!
You wake up from the happy illusion only to find a complete chaos all over the place.
The dizziness has not completely passed. You force yourself to get up.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief...
Nightingale is usually calm, but right now her voice is filled with shock and bitterness.

speaker: Nightingale
content: NOX destroyed the constraints, we...
We couldn't stop her.
Broken Frontline, DisSea

speaker: Nightingale
content: NOX... is right ahead.
You've already been chasing after Amber for two hours. Just now, she's crossed the Broken Frontline and entered the deepest part of DisSea.
The shackles connecting you to Amber are also reminding you that she's right there.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief...

speaker: Nightingale
content: That place is an area absolutely forbidden for the living. You... shouldn't go there.
You point at the safety cable for transporting goods on the side, offering your solution.
Tie that around me. Once I give the signal, you'll pull me back.

speaker: Nightingale
content: I understand you don't want to give up on any Sinner.

speaker: Nightingale
content: But this... will only cost you your life for nothing.
You know the shackles can defend against the Black Ring's corruption.
Also, I've promised Amber I'd take her to see the sunrise. I don't have a habit of breaking promises.
Nightingale is staring into your eyes without speaking a word for a while.
At last, she ties the cable around you silently.

speaker: Nightingale
content: If you notice anything unusual, please send the signal at once.

speaker: Nightingale
content: You must not... hesitate.
Pressing on the cable around your waist, you trudge in the mud along a ford.
Amber!
The more you go forward, the more faded the colors of all the surroundings seem, only the cold red moon above is becoming more and more clear and blinding.
As you advance, more and more figures emerge around you. They're standing still, staring at the blood-red moon-adorned sky blankly.
Under the sky, something is gradually peeling off from you.
Fresh... Fresh...
Memories of the living...
As if smelling something, the dazed figures are flaring their nostrils greedily, mumbling.
Amber!
Without hesitation, you continue shouting the girl's name and advancing the best you can, but the silt under your feet and the unknown filth hidden in it are hindering you.
Stumbling, you fall into the lake. Colorful ripples spread across the water surface.
I remember now.
I was alive once too.
We've been dead for too long...

You stand up. Mysterious colors keep spreading into the water. You notice you've forgotten the meaning of the mumbling crowd behind you and the line of fortifications appeared out of nowhere, but you must keep going.
You've lost track of time walking, until you finally see that familiar figure.
Amber, I'm here.

The object around your waist makes you uneasy, and your body and mind are both growing heavy. You're not sure why you're wearing such a burdensome thing on you, but your instinct tells you to never remove it.
There's no sunrise here. You must go back with me.
Amber turns back slowly.
There's not a hint of Amber in those eyes.
Hahahaha!
You hear frantic cackles from behind. After swallowing the colors peeled off from your body, those who're following you are showing blatant malice in their eyes.
We've told you, we've told you!
She died a long time ago!
With her memories and all of our deaths, we created an illusion of DisSea.
We've already deceived the rules, deceived DisSea, and yet here you are!
The moon above you is hanging lower and lower, staring at what's happening on the lake coolly.
You finally understand what the red moon signifies—the real DisSea, the cold rules, the start and the end of the Mania, and the final fate of everyone.
Those who're infected with the Mania belong to DisSea after they die. There are no exceptions.
You've killed her, you've killed us.
And you're about to kill yourself.
Seeing that you've chosen death yourself, I guess you no longer need these living memories.
They're ours now!
The faces of the surrounding figures are growing more and more distorted, developing flesh lumps and fangs like Corruptors. They're crowding around you.
Some are tearing at the steel cable behind you and some are catching the spreading colors on the lake surface.
Even more of them are coming toward you.
You must run... You should send someone... a signal...
To whom? What's the signal? What is... this place?
Should I go back? Go back where?
You try your best to think, but the answer never comes.
No, I can't go back, Amber is still here...
You can't understand what the clamorous crowd is saying.
Your consciousness is growing heavier and big chunks of blanks appear in your memories, like rocks eroded by the wind, turned into colorful sand and scattered into the lake.
The colors have finally touched the girl in front of you.
${PlayerName}?
The girl turns back. Her eyes have regained clarity and brightness.

speaker: Maiden
content: Why are you here?
Are you... Amber?
I'm here... to take you back... to see the sunrise.

speaker: Maiden
content: You shouldn't have come here.
I can't... break my promise.
Follow me... Hurry up! Time is running short.
Crack!
You hear the sound of metal shattering from behind.
Amber is looking at you, tears streaming down her cracked cheeks, dripping down into the lake.

speaker: Maiden
content: I thought... there would perhaps be a little bit of time left, even if it's only one day... At least I could see them... and the sunrise...

speaker: Maiden
content: Well... now is not the time for this.
A dazzling smile reemerges on the girl's face.
She stares into your eyes and solemnly says that name that makes you feel both strange and familiar.

speaker: Maiden
content: ${PlayerName}.

speaker: Maiden
content: Thank you.

speaker: Maiden
content: Thank you, for making me recall everything about being a human.

speaker: Maiden
content: Even though I've done so many... unforgivable things...

speaker: Maiden
content: Thank you... for coming to me when I was feeling the most hopeless...
You don't understand what the girl is saying, but an instinctive worry makes you grip her hand.

speaker: Maiden
content: Since many years ago, this place has been my destined home. This is an inevitable truth no matter how I try to defy it.

speaker: Maiden
content: I should have known better. That would have prevented so many mistakes from happening.

speaker: Maiden
content: But at least there's still something I can do now.
The surrounding monsters have already lurked next to you, but all of your attention is on the girl before you.
She grips your hands tight.
You open your mouth but are at a loss of words.

speaker: Maiden
content: I can't protect you, but perhaps... she can.

speaker: Maiden
content: Live on, live well.

speaker: Maiden
content: Farewell...
The girl's figure shatters and turns into starlight, brightening up the sky.
Amid that, the monster holding the longsword once again emerges.
It's a nightmare too long and too desperate. When you wake up, Amber is carrying you and walking toward the Broken Frontline.
Even though her skin is ice cold, you feel relieved for having survived the disaster.
Are we... safe now?
Amber doesn't say a word, and only keeps moving forward silently.
On the Broken Frontline, Nightingale is impatiently ordering the others to drop the cable.
Behind them, the warm, golden morning sun is slowly rising.
Amber, it's the sunrise.
Amber?
You look up. No reaction can be seen on the ashen face, as if everything before you, even the sunrise she's been longing to see, has nothing to do with her.
It is an ice cold, empty vessel named NOX.

At long last, the tumultuous DisCars crisis is coming to an end, all thanks to you, Deren, and OwO. You take a team of soldiers to search every nook and cranny of Dillywood, in case that formidable force is lying in wait in some dark corner.
The host of the DisCars ceremony has booked five venues for the special occasion. Now, surrounded by a cluster of gigantic buildings, you can't help but heave a sigh.
This is gonna be a long night.
You move your head from side to side to ease the soreness in your neck, and step through the gaping hole created by the Apostle of Ashes to investigate the complex in the back.
Excuse me, coming through...
The moment you step into the alley, you hear a stream of footfalls coming your way.
Then you see a familiar figure approaching you.

speaker: Deren
content: Ah, Chief!
Deren catches her falling hat and strides toward you.
Without saying anything further, she grabs your hand and starts running, dragging you along, much to your surprise.

speaker: Deren
content: What a coincidence! Us meeting again here and now!
Hold on!
What are you doing?
Before you can get an answer, you hear a confusion of voices coming from behind.

speaker: Producer A
content: Miss Deren, please stop running for a minute! Take a look at this new contract. I'm sure you'll be happy with the terms!

speaker: Producer B
content: We'll double whatever they offer you, as long as you sign with us!

speaker: Reporter A
content: Miss Deren, could you tell us why you've decided to attend this ceremony? And is the person running with you the star of your next movie?

speaker: Deren
content: Sorry! But I can't answer any questions right now!

speaker: Reporter B
content: How about you, mister? Do you have something to say?
female_content: How about you, miss? Do you have something to say?

content: You can't think of anything to say while you're running your heart out.
Right at this moment, you catch sight of a hill of rubble ahead. That's the place where you fought the Apostle of Ashes.
You speed up and get ahead of Deren, pulling her instead. The two of you slip into the dilapidated building.

speaker: Deren
content: (Pants)...
...Care to explain, Miss Big Director?

speaker: Deren
content: Hehe... I used to be, um, quite famous.

speaker: Deren
content: Well, you know, the DisCars ceremony has been delayed. Those guys are not gonna go home empty-handed... so they have been vying to sign me or get me on interviews.

speaker: Deren
content: They're like bloodhounds. They know exactly where to find me.
Deren puts her hand on the nape of her neck, a look of resignation on her face.

options: I might have a solution to your conundrum.

speaker: Deren
content: Really? What is it?
Follow me.

speaker: Deren
content: Hey, where are you taking me?
Just follow me. You'll find out.

speaker: Deren
content: This is... your solution?
The MBCC headquarters is a high-security facility. No ordinary folks can get in without permission from me or one of my superiors.
If you agree to be detained and stay here, not only will you be rid of those nuisances, but you will be protected. Two birds with one stone, don't you think?

speaker: Deren
content: So, simply put, free food and accommodation, right?
...Yeah, you could put it that way.

speaker: Deren
content: Hmm, sounds great.
Deren plunks herself down on the chair in the interrogation room, seemingly at ease. She looks up at you with a smile on her face.
...Aren't you gonna resist a little?

speaker: Deren
content: Resist? Why would I?

speaker: Deren
content: I'm a Sinner, and you are the Chief of the MBCC. Me being detained here is a matter of course.
...You have a point.

speaker: Deren
content: Plus, here, I get free food and accommodation. Out there, I have to fend for myself, while hiding from my pursuers.

speaker: Deren
content: It's an easy option. Wouldn't you agree, Chief?
You can't figure out what's going on in the head of this happy-go-lucky Sinner before you. Is she really ignorant of how the relationship between the MBCC and Sinners works, or...
Is she just playing dumb, biding her time?
Once you've decided to stay, it won't be easy to back out.
All Sinners, once detained by the MBCC, must take orders from me, no questions asked.

speaker: Deren
content: Well, I'm aware of that.
Deren narrows her eyes at you. The way she is now speaking reminds you of your first conversation with her, where you had a hard time deciphering her words.

speaker: Deren
content: Taking orders from you, not taking orders from you... Doesn't make much of a difference to me. At least I can live comfortably here.
Surely a famous director like you can easily find a place to live comfortably?

speaker: Deren
content: Hmm, I need a change of scenery, if you really need an explanation.

speaker: Deren
content: And there is no place in the entire DisCity more special than the MBCC headquarters, where I can "stay close to you".
I don't suppose you want to make a movie about Sinners, do you?

speaker: Deren
content: That actually sounds like a great idea.

speaker: Deren
content: No one has ever made a movie like that before.
Then what? Submit it to the DisCars and win half a dozen trophies?

speaker: Deren
content: Oh my, wouldn't that be fantastic.
Deren waggles her eyebrows at your question, or more specifically, at the mention of the DisCars.
You exchange glances and chuckle.

speaker: Deren
content: You said the MBCC headquarters is a high-security facility. Your words, not mine.

speaker: Deren
content: Would anyone understand a movie about an organization that has never dared to show its face in public?

speaker: Deren
content: Oh... wait a second...
Deren strokes her chin, her face a study in contemplation, as if ready to deliver some devastating news.

speaker: Deren
content: Understand or not, that's not even our first concern. Whether it would be allowed to be released, that would be the real issue.

speaker: Deren
content: Those guys...
Deren tips her head back slightly, signaling you to look at the roof above the two of you.

speaker: Deren
content: They would never allow a movie like that to be screened in the DisCars.

speaker: Deren
content: What else could it be?
Deren starts counting on her fingers while murmuring to herself. After a while, she shows her hands with the palms facing out.

speaker: Deren
content: I can give you ten reasons, at the very least.

speaker: Deren
content: But I won't elaborate on them; I don't want your interrogation report to be rejected.

speaker: Deren
content: Haha... You're so amusing.

speaker: Deren
content: What do you mean, even if it's my movie?

speaker: Deren
content: It's exactly because it's my movie...

speaker: Deren
content: They'd be more strict, more unreasonable, in vetting it.
Deren falls silent. Her eyes are shielded from view by the brim of her hat, so you can't see how she is feeling inside.
They put restrictions on your movies, forcing you to make changes to suit their taste... Is that the reason why you loathe them?
You twirl the cap of your fountain pen, pull it out, and put it back on with a click, a sound not unlike that of a clapperboard.
At the sound, Deren lifts her eyes to look at you, shaking her head.

speaker: Deren
content: I don't loathe them.

speaker: Deren
content: I just find them... very boring.
Deren stretches and rests her head on her hand, looking as if she is about to fall asleep.
You didn't use to hate the DisCars so much, did you? You attended a few DisCars ceremonies before you quit directing, if I'm not mistaken.

speaker: Deren
content: Alas, everyone has a living to earn, my dear Chief, even a talented director.

speaker: Deren
content: I have to say I'm not as assertive as I used to be.

speaker: Deren
content: Have you heard that I didn't attend the DisCars ceremony where my award was presented? That's right before I quit directing.
I heard. Nobody held it against you. Quite the opposite, a lot of people thought you had...
Character.

speaker: Deren
content: Character?

speaker: Deren
content: That's something I do not have.

speaker: Deren
content: It's just a flawed choice made by the immature me.

speaker: Deren
content: As for the audience and judges...
Deren's smiling eyes have narrowed into slits. Their brilliance is mostly trapped behind the heavy eyelids.
She snickers, closing her eyes for a second.

speaker: Deren
content: They only saw what they wanted to see, or what they were tricked into seeing.
Why didn't you attend the ceremony then?
The DisCars are the most prestigious awards in the entertainment industry, right?

speaker: Deren
content: But the movie they submitted for consideration in my name didn't deserve them.

speaker: Deren
content: Even though the audience, judges, and everyone else thought it did.

speaker: Deren
content: I didn't think so.

speaker: Deren
content: So I didn't attend it, because it was their party. It had nothing to do with me.
Deren sounds breezy. It's as if she doesn't think much of the highly-regarded awards.
I've never seen a director who doesn't want to join the "party" with audiences.
Something went wrong in the production of the movie?

speaker: Deren
content: How very observant of you!

speaker: Deren
content: How about I tell you a little story, Mr. Clapper. And then you can tell me what is real, and what is false...
female_content: How about I tell you a little story, Miss Clapper. And then you can tell me what is real, and what is false...

content: Deren narrows her eyes at you again. The smile she gives you is strangely familiar.

speaker: Deren
content: In the open sea drifts a lifeboat, which holds a woman, a tiger, a dog, a monkey, and a hippo.

speaker: Deren
content: Threatened by the mere existence of the tiger, the dog, monkey, and hippo gang up to get rid of the tiger. And when the big cat asks the woman for help, she says,

speaker: Deren
content: "You have to go so the rest of us can live."

speaker: Deren
content: But she tells herself, "You have to go, for your own sake."

speaker: Deren
content: Well, take a guess, which is true? Is it what she says to the tiger, or what she says to herself...

options: What she tells herself is true.
What she tells herself is false.

speaker: Deren
content: That's what most people would guess.

speaker: Deren
content: Thinking outside the box... I like that.

speaker: Deren
content: But the truth is, it doesn't matter what you believe. It's what you do that matters.

speaker: Deren
content: So... the woman jumps into the sea with the tiger, never to be seen again.
You... I mean, she... disappears with the tiger, but the lifeboat and other animals are intact, right?

speaker: Deren
content: Correct. The dog, monkey, and hippo, now sure of their safety, start celebrating, like they have received <color=#fb9259>The Invitation to Dance</color>, and it didn't matter if they were dancing of their own free will or if they were forced to.
Are you saying...

speaker: Deren
content: Yes... it's not all that complicated... The movie submitted for consideration was not the version I edited.
Deren puts it lightly, but you catch on immediately.
Even OwO, a newcomer to the film industry, understands the importance of direct involvement in editing. It's the only way of ensuring your story is accurately presented.
If the task is assigned to someone else, some of the ideas you wish to present will inevitably be missing in the final product.
And if you're unlucky enough, the theatrical version can have an entirely different message than the director's cut.
What kind of message did you want to get across in your version?

speaker: Deren
content: Mmm...

speaker: Deren
content: I don't remember.
Deren hangs her head, deep in thought. After a while, she looks up at you and shrugs her shoulders before giving you a non-committal reply.

speaker: Deren
content: It's been changed so drastically that I'm not even sure I could recognize it now.

speaker: Deren
content: I don't understand why people are still so obsessed with a movie that has nothing to do with me.

speaker: Deren
content: Maybe because they are just... bored.
Deren must be lying. She can't have forgotten what the original version of the movie is about...
You muse, as you look at Deren, who has closed her eyes.
Deren seems to have lost interest in continuing this discussion about her movie. You decide to call it a day and end the questioning.

speaker: Luvia Ray
content: Hmm, how should I go about this?
You're walking past the lounge area when you catch sight of Luvia, dressed in her new white coat, gesticulating in front of the TV.

speaker: Luvia Ray
content: "Failure, how I like the word!"

speaker: Luvia Ray
content: "The story of humankind is one about failures, one failure after another."

speaker: Luvia Ray
content: "This keeps us trapped in the draft phase, our lives merely endless rehearsals for a show that will never be staged."
Luvia mimics the actor on the screen, reading out the actor's lines.
Then it hits you: Luvia is in show business. She might know something about Deren's movie.
From what Deren said during yesterday's interrogation, you've inferred that the movie is called The Invitation to Dance. It is banned, probably due to the DisCars incident.

Plus there's a lot of irrelevant information about the name on the internet, so it's extremely difficult for you to even come by some appropriate review. But Luvia might know a thing or two about this high-profile movie in her field.
You come up to Luvia.
Sorry to bother you, Luvia, but do you have a minute?

speaker: Luvia Ray
content: Oh! It's you, Chief.
Luvia is delighted to see you.
I have some questions about the film industry to ask you, if it's not too much trouble.

speaker: Luvia Ray
content: Em? No problem at all! You might not believe it, but these days I have no trouble landing movie roles.

speaker: Luvia Ray
content: Please go ahead... what do you want to ask me about, Chief?
At the mention of the name, Luvia's eyes brighten.

speaker: Luvia Ray
content: Of course I have! She's the master of absurdness, the youngest winner of the DisCar for Best Director.

speaker: Luvia Ray
content: Her movies have a mysterious, outlandish feel to them, but they can be romantic at the same time. They are thought-provoking and open to interpretation. My point is... she's an extraordinary director.
Luvia smiles at you sheepishly, fiddling with the hem of her clothes.

speaker: Luvia Ray
content: I... I'm a big fan of hers.

speaker: Luvia Ray
content: Truth be told, I knew she was coming to the MBCC, so after her interrogation that day, I tracked her down and asked for her autograph.

speaker: Luvia Ray
content: Ta-da!
Luvia whips out a notebook from her pocket and opens it to the back. On the page is written Deren's name in paint.

speaker: Luvia Ray
content: One of my dreams is to play a role in one of Deren's movies, even if it's just a minor one.
So... you must know about the movie that won her the best director award?

Luvia turns around and starts rummaging in the drawers of the TV cabinet. After a while, she turns back to you, a thumb drive in her hand. As she hands it to you, she waggles her eyebrows, looking all mysterious.

speaker: Luvia Ray
content: I'm a fan. Of course I know about the movie. But this is only the theatrical version. Apparently there is a director's cut—that's what they say on the internet, but no one has ever seen it before.

speaker: Luvia Ray
content: Let's watch it together, huh? I'll explain those bits you don't understand.
You insert the thumb drive into a USB port; you select and play the movie.
You dim the lights and sink into a beanbag chair. On the screen, intricate dark-colored patterns fade in, slowly transporting you to another world.

It is a POV shot. You are seeing through an unseen character's eyes, as if you are the character. In front of you, a pale, delicate hand flips open a roster book, then runs a red fingernail down a list of run-of-the-mill names.
The fingernail stops at an illegible name, and the pale hand takes your invitation.
Some time later, the pale hands make a welcoming gesture and push open a door that gives out an eerie red light. You enter the ballroom.

The ballroom is dimly lit. Next to the dance floor is a row of long chairs, seemingly out of place with their surroundings. Feeling lost and having no one to talk to, you walk over to sit down on one of the chairs.
Music comes on, which sounds to your ears like an impatient, irritated voice rushing you. Then a girl in a white dress stumbles into the room.
The girl comes over and sits beside you. You notice the plainness of her dress, and when you look down, you also notice a few inconspicuous white patches on the hem.

speaker: Girl in White
content: Sorry, I'm still a bit nervous.
She leans sideways toward you and whispers.

speaker: Girl in White
content: "Dancing among the clouds, lapped by the waves, but they weave a web of thorns."

speaker: Girl in White
content: I don't know if this is working. But they've told me I'll be happy.
