The camera moves upwards to show the girl's face, delicate and graced with a gentle smile. She is staring at the dance floor.

speaker: Spooky Female Voice
content: Please come to the center of the dance floor, this lady in a white dress.

speaker: Spooky Female Voice
content: Someone will come, to accept you, help you, protect you, and...

speaker: Spooky Female Voice
content: Love you.

speaker: Spooky Female Voice
content: Go dance with him!
The eerie door opens again, and in walks a man whose entire face is shadowed. He comes up to the girl and bows slightly before her.

The music has turned cheerful and joyous, but somehow it sounds like an old train running on rusty rails, or notes played by filthy hands on a broken-down piano to your ears. In the dance floor, the two figures—one in white, the other in black, start twirling.
Slowly, the girl's long hair becomes up-do, while her white dress turns yellowish-gray. You hear the sound of cups and dishes breaking, followed by the shrill cry of a baby.
The smile on the girl's face is gone. Her face is now tear-stained and devoid of feeling.
The girl looks beyond her partner to where you are seated. She opens her mouth to say something, but nothing comes out.

The camera cuts to the dancers. The man places a wilted rose in the girl's pocket and takes her hand. They bow to the audience. Then comes another close-up of the girl's face. Her hair has come down, and she is wearing a sweet smile.

speaker: Guest
content: Everyone can find happiness! Every dream can come true!

speaker: Guest
content: How wonderful!
Murmurs of approval go around the circle, loud enough to drown out the whimpering sound.
No one knows where the sound is coming from, or where it might end up.
The camera pans over the crowd. Their faces are blurry, but each seems to carry a ghost of a smile.
You raise your hand. It seems that you have something to say, but before you can say anything, the eerie door opens once again.

speaker: Pale-faced Boy
content: Cough cough... Excuse me, is this seat taken?
The camera pans back to the seat that the girl occupied not long ago, and you see a pale-faced boy.
His neck, wrists, waist, and ankles are entangled in strange-looking vines. The vines look alive. A closer look shows that they're squirming, slowly making their way into his body.

speaker: Pale-faced Boy
content: I heard them talking outside.

speaker: Pale-faced Boy
content: Is it true that everyone can find happiness, and every dream can come true?
You don't know the answer, so you neither shake nor nod your head.

speaker: Pale-faced Boy
content: I hope that the people I love can live on... even...

speaker: Pale-faced Boy
content: Skin, organs, bones... they've come together to create me, and they'll come together to create them...

speaker: Pale-faced Boy
content: It's just that I don't know if I can last until... the dance is over.

speaker: Spooky Female Voice
content: Come on, kid, come and stand in the center.

speaker: Spooky Female Voice
content: They'll come, to help you, to protect you, to take care of you...

speaker: Spooky Female Voice
content: And the ones you care...

speaker: Spooky Female Voice
content: Your dream will come true.
The pale-faced boy stands up, nods at you, and walks into the dance floor.
He is flanked by two white-robed people in the dance floor, each wearing a face mask. You can't see their faces clearly, with the face masks and the red shadow covering their upper faces.
They take the boy's hands, lift him up, and lay him flat in mid-air, before putting him back down. A bizarre dance is afoot in the dance floor.

speaker: Pale-faced Boy
content: ...I'm so hungry. Are you hungry too?
From God knows where a black mass appears on the boy's top and starts expanding. It's located above his abdomen; slowly, it takes on a blood-curdling shape.
Then another black mass appears, then another... After a while, the masses become transparent and disappear entirely, like a magic trick.
The vines binding the boy are growing thicker and wilder. They're on the verge of tearing his tiny body apart.
But the boy is oblivious to all this. Standing on his feet again, he bows to the audience, as the music comes to an end.
He's still alive. He'll survive...

speaker: Guest
content: What a tough kid! How persistent!

speaker: Guest
content: You'll find happiness! All of you!
The guests murmur in appreciation and take off their hats as a gesture of respect.
A smile spreads across the boy's gaunt, pale face. He is clutching two dying roses in his hand.
The flowers are wilted, but their thorns are still sharp and tough. They've punctured his palm, but no liquid flows out.

Just like what happened with the girl, a close-up of the boy's face takes up the entire screen. He's smiling, seemingly content. Then the crowd breaks into rapturous applause, beating out a rhythm with their palms.
You are applauding too, you realize.

speaker: Guest
content: Are you truly wishing him well?
...Are you really?
Your hands are trembling. You are antsy; that much is clear.
You are seized by an overwhelming desire to leave the room, but you don't know how.
Amid the rhythmic applauding, a work song starts playing. But it's not a typical work song; it's rhythmic but lifeless.

speaker: Young Woman in a Suit
content: Are you okay?

speaker: Young Woman in a Suit
content: If you need help, just let me know.
The voice belongs to a young woman. She's wearing a suit, and is now sitting beside you.
She lays her hand gently on your wrist, and she sounds concerned.

speaker: Young Woman in a Suit
content: This isn't my first time here. If you're not feeling well, I could take you outside for a walk.
The young woman pulls you to your feet, eliciting a collective gasp of surprise from the guests. They start whispering, and some even retreat to the far side of the room out of fear.
You and the young woman head for the gate, cutting through the dense crowd and the harsh and dizzying light.
Light and shadow weave an intricate pattern on her. It looks like a suit of armor worn over her business suit.
...Or a tangle of ropes that bind her.

speaker: Spooky Female Voice
content: The ball has not ended yet. Please don't leave!

speaker: Spooky Female Voice
content: You can't leave!

speaker: Spooky Female Voice
content: Our expectations, our expectations of you... You must meet them this time!
The spooky voice rings out in the ballroom. As if encouraged, galvanized even, by the voice, the guests, who have been giving the two of you a wide berth, start closing in.
They start murmuring, but whether they're murmuring among themselves or to the two of you, you are not sure.

speaker: Guest
content: You can't leave! You're not allowed to leave!

speaker: Guest
content: The ball has not ended yet. You can't leave!

speaker: Guest
content: You're the star.

speaker: Guest
content: You're our hope.

speaker: All the Guests
content: You're a good kid.
The guests come at you and tear you away from the young woman.
Then they carry her into the dance floor, and put her in the center.
They take away the notebook in the young woman's pocket, remove the watch from her wrist, and change her flats for a pair of high heels.
The young woman's anxious eyes search the crowd, and they spot you.

speaker: Young Woman in a Suit
content: Leave! Get out of this place!
These are her last words to you.
She starts dancing in the crowd. Her black suit comes apart and becomes dark-brown overalls, and the overalls come apart and become a white gown.
Her clothes stop changing. Her eyes are no longer following you; she's looking at her partner, who is leading her step by step to the gate she has longed for.
With every step she takes, a rose petal falls. The petals come from the three roses pinned to her clothing over her chest.
The camera follows the young woman's footsteps out of the gate. The gate closes, and the screen goes black.
Is it over?

speaker: Luvia Ray
content: Of course not! Just hold on, wait for it.
Ten seconds later—or maybe a longer period, red light bursts through the screen.
Sprawling rose bushes and rose petals fill the entire screen.

Lying on the blanket of rose petals are the girl in white and her dance partner, with two cute babies between them; the pale-faced boy surrounded by his six siblings; and the young woman, who has changed out of her business suit and into a long soft-looking garment, lying against her dance partner's chest, holding his hand.

It's a romantic scene accompanied by romantic music. A breeze is ruffling their hair and clothes. From a distance, they all look happy. Then the camera pans closer; they open their eyes to look at the POV character, or you the viewer.
The next second, with the breeze still blowing, they close their eyes, as well as the window into their minds.
The end.

speaker: Luvia Ray
content: What do you think? What do you think? It's very thought-provoking, right?
Luvia can't wait to know your opinion on the movie.

speaker: Luvia Ray
content: It is really romantic and extremely bizarre. The mysterious door, the unconventional camerawork and dialogue, the romantic dances, and the sadly beautiful final scene.

speaker: Luvia Ray
content: There are some places I can't quite wrap my head around, but that's probably because I'm not quite there yet, not savvy enough, not perceptive enough.

speaker: Luvia Ray
content: After all, this is the movie that won so, so many DisCars. Deren knows how to capture romance on the screen; that's the consensus. And I'm sure of it.
Luvia stares at the rolling credits, her fists clenched.
Every character in the movie seems happy at the end. But is that the message of the movie? Are they really happy? Have their dreams come true in the end?
You don't have definite answers to these questions. The movie feels jarring throughout. It feels as if someone's trying to force a set of ideas on you.
Haha... do you really think so?
A voice intrudes. You look toward the doorway. Deren is leaning against the doorpost, looking at you and Luvia.

speaker: Luvia Ray
content: De... Director Deren!

speaker: Deren
content: Is that movie really that good, that awesome in your eyes?

speaker: Luvia Ray
content: I do, I really do. What they say on the internet is right. You have great taste and extraordinary skills, but...

speaker: Deren
content: Yes?

speaker: Luvia Ray
content: But as for my personal opinion of Miss Deren... I'll wait until I've known you better—if I have the privilege of spending time with you, that is.

speaker: Deren
content: Haha... You're so adorable.

speaker: Deren
content: Then, what about you, Chief? What do you think?
Deren turns her attention to you, looking you in the eye. You have no choice but to answer her question.
I'm not a professional. But speaking as a layperson, I think it's a great movie.
It deserves all the awards it won.
It's a great movie. No doubt about it. And it deserves all the awards it won.
And you... you're a great director. I've seen your genius at work.
Deren clears her throat, a smile playing about her lips.

speaker: Deren
content: You're not just saying that, are you?
I mean it.
There is one thing, though... The characters in the movie seem to have something more to say when they come around.
Does that mean... there's going to be a sequel?
Your question wipes the smile off Deren's face. She pulls down the hat to shield her eyes, making herself unreadable again.
Luvia looks at you, then at Deren, concerned. You give her a gentle wave of your hand, a gesture that tells her everything is all right.

speaker: Deren
content: That's not gonna happen. I'm under detention, Chief. Where would I find the time and money to make a sequel? But I'm okay with it. My film-making days are behind me.
She chuckles, pats you on the shoulder, and with a wave of her hand, turns to leave, ignoring your calling after her as she walks away.
You rush out. Outside, you find a notebook on the ground. The movie's name, The Invitation to Dance, is written on the cover.
What? Someone took Deren away?
Who? Who took her away without my permission?
In the past few days, you've been studying Deren's notebook, justifying it as a way of better understanding one of your Sinners.
This is the last thing you want to hear—that one of your Sinners has been taken away without your permission, when you've just arrived at work sleep-deprived and bleary-eyed.

speaker: Nightingale
content: A councilor from Eastside asked for her. That is a very high ranking official, higher than you, Chief. So... we couldn't stop it.

speaker: Nightingale
content: And... Sinner MBCC-S-014 counts as one of the "Elite Sinners", thus is entitled to temporary release from detention.
Nightingale gives you an apologetic smile and hands you the terminal she's holding.
A live interview is being shown on the screen. The miniature image of a burning fire next to the title indicates that the interview has drawn a large audience.

speaker: Reporter A
content: Miss Deren, it's been some time since your last appearance at a DisCars ceremony. Could you tell us why you've decided to come back?

speaker: Deren
content: They invited me, so I came.

speaker: Reporter A
content: Do you have anything to say about the ceremony being delayed?

speaker: Deren
content: It's delayed, not canceled.

speaker: Reporter B
content: Is it true that you didn't submit a movie for consideration this time?

speaker: Deren
content: It's true. Because I haven't made any.

speaker: Reporter B
content: Why? We like your movies. They are refreshing, a mixture of romance and absurdness.

speaker: Deren
content: Why haven't I made any new movies? Haha... Haven't got around to it, I guess.

speaker: Reporter C
content: Are you happy with your old movies?

speaker: Deren
content: What's important is whether you're happy with them.

speaker: Reporter C
content: What do you think about the title "the Queen of Absurdness"?

speaker: Deren
content: I'm no queen of any kind. I'm just a director who makes movies she enjoys making.

speaker: Reporter D
content: Miss Deren, I have a question for you...

speaker: Deren
content: Ask away.

speaker: Reporter D
content: You've been out of the public eye for five years. Have you been collecting material for a movie?

speaker: Reporter E
content: You've finally agreed to attend the DisCars ceremony, and it's been delayed due to a singular event. Could you share your view on this event? Are you considering turning it into a movie?

speaker: Reporter F
content: Do you plan to attend future DisCars ceremonies?

speaker: Reporter
content: Miss Deren, would you please answer my question? Miss Deren...

speaker: Deren
content: Whoa, whoa... Slow down! One at a time...
Deren maintains her smile. She squints her eyes to face the passionate crowd.
An array of microphones, like fearsome truncheons, are stuck up close to Deren's face, each carrying a nameplate.

speaker: Deren
content: I'll answer your questions as best I can.
Deren is cornered. There seems no hope of escape.
Deren sighs and takes small steps backward.

speaker: Reporter
content: You sighed, because you feel the film industry is hopeless?

speaker: Reporter
content: Is this the reason why you went into hiding for so long?

speaker: Reporter
content: You've come out of hiding, because you want to bring the film industry back to life?

speaker: Deren
content: Haha... I'm flattered that you think I can pull off such a feat.
Deren's face grows solemn, as inexplicable emotions churn inside her. Something deep in her psyche seems to be stirring, threatening to break free of the restraints her rationality puts on it.
Don't be tempted.

speaker: Deren
content: Who?
On the count of three, turn around and run southwest.
With the familiar voice reverberating in her head, Deren smiles, raises her head, and speaks into the bank of microphones.

speaker: Deren
content: Sorry, but I have to digress a little. I have an announcement to make.
One...

speaker: Deren
content: Which is...
Two...

speaker: Deren
content: How should I put it...
Three...

speaker: Deren
content: I'm off. See ya!

One minute she was scratching her head, pretending to search for words. The next she was off like a runaway horse, avoiding street signs and roadblocks as she goes. Shortly, she disappeared without a trace.
Silence descends on the crowd of reporters, but it is short-lived, presently replaced by an uproar.

speaker: Reporters
content: Why is she running away?

speaker: Reporters
content: Is she off to save the film industry?

speaker: Reporters
content: I don't think so. I think what she is trying to say is that no one can touch her in this profession.

speaker: Deren
content: Chief, are you experiencing a feeling of déjà vu?

speaker: Deren
content: Or a flashback, like in a movie.
Taking Deren by the hand, you dash around in a maze of narrow alleys, and finally slow down when you have lost the reporters and bodyguards.
Are you saying I'm the star of a movie?

speaker: Deren
content: Of course. You'll always be the star of my eyes.
Then please tell me how to "act" right now, Director Deren, because I have a bellyful of questions.
You lead Deren into a narrow cul-de-sac that ends in a high wall.

speaker: Deren
content: Oh my, why get so serious all of a sudden?

speaker: Deren
content: I'll answer your questions honestly. I'm not gonna mess with you, as I did with those boring idiots.

speaker: Deren
content: You.

speaker: Deren
content: Just kidding... I know you're asking who took me away from the MBCC.
Deren leans against the wall, arms crossed. Specks of dust alight on her shoulders. It brings to mind the image of a long-forgotten wooden box collecting dust in a dark corner.

speaker: Deren
content: It's an old friend, he is...

speaker: Ringtone
content: Beep,beep.
A shrill ringing of the phone interrupts Deren. She fishes out her communicator, takes a look at the screen—her assistant is calling her, and gives you a sheepish smile.
Deren answers the phone. A penetrating voice comes through.

speaker: Assistant
content: Good Lord, what have you done! How could you run away in the middle of an interview?

speaker: Assistant
content: Do I have to remind you who got you out of the MBCC? I guess I have to. It's Councilor Walter!

speaker: Deren
content: I know, I know... But he said that as long as I showed up, I could say as I pleased, and do as I pleased.

speaker: Assistant
content: Didn't you work with him before? Why would you put him in an awkward position? Don't you know he holds sway in the business world and on the political scene?

speaker: Assistant
content: He's the one who financed this DisCars ceremony. You'd better not get in his bad books, or he...
Deren jerks her head away from the communicator. She furrows her brow and jams a finger in her ear.

speaker: Deren
content: Okay, okay... I'll listen to you. I'll attend the ceremony. I promise.
Having put her angry assistant's mind at ease, Deren turns off the communicator.
For a moment, it seems that the brick alley is buzzing as the assistant's voice fades away.
So... if you don't give interviews, or attend the ceremony...
He'll pull out?

speaker: Deren
content: I guess so. You heard my assistant.

speaker: Deren
content: I've long since lost interest in that kind of stuff, but I know...

speaker: Deren
content: A lot of people depend on that for their livelihood, and it's not gonna cost me anything, right? So, I'll go and do their bidding.
So... that movie of yours, did you agree to have it edited by someone else, because you didn't want people to lose their jobs?
Deren is struck dumb by your words for a moment, but then roars with laughter.

speaker: Deren
content: Haha... You sure are different. Did you pick up something?
You shrug and motion for her to follow you.
You leave the alley and soon arrive at a factory, from within which noises come gushing.

speaker: Deren
content: What is this place?
Deren seems confused, looking around.

speaker: Deren
content: So, this is my punishment for leaving the MBCC without saying goodbye to you, to be thrown into a factory to do hard labor?
Now I understand why you could win the best director award.

speaker: Deren
content: Enough with the praising. I'm getting tired of it.

speaker: Deren
content: Why did you bring me here anyway?
You show Deren the notebook you found the other day.

speaker: Deren
content: Looks like you've done your research.
You're my Sinner now, and as Chief of the MBCC, it's my responsibility to...
Have a thorough understanding... of each and every one of my Sinners.
Deren narrows her eyes at you, incredulous.
You open the notebook and read from it.
"The dancers behind the door, they tried bravely, they struggled sadly, but in the end, they accepted their fate."
"Maybe it's because they felt helpless, maybe there's no reason at all, or maybe it's because they didn't care anymore."
"But little did they know the cost of accepting their fate was destruction."
"Then... who should cry out for the voices they hide in their hearts?"

speaker: Deren
content: Oh my, it's embarrassing to hear my stuff being read out loud by someone else.
The movie Luvia showed me... it's been so heavily edited that it feels off to me.
But, no matter how deceiving editing techniques can be, the director's true intentions are always revealed in the eyes of the actors.
You left this notebook for me on purpose, didn't you?

speaker: Deren
content: I just wanted to see how much you could discover. I have a feeling that you've discovered more than I expected.

speaker: Deren
content: Chief of the MBCC, you're really something.
You pass Deren the notebook, and she takes it. She runs her hand over the cover, looking as if she is connecting with her younger self.
Those labels that the internet and media desperately try to put on you are not who you really are. They are just, labels.
They don't define you or your movies.
The movie you wanted to show the world is not a romance movie, or one of those feel-good movies.
It's a profound movie intended for the audience to hear the cry of those who break the bonds of fate.
Unfortunately, the movie, like the director, is unfairly labeled. It's been altered, and its message has been distorted.
The boom of machinery shutting down issues from behind the closed gate of the factory, lingering in the air between the silent Deren and you.
The gate opens, unleashing a wave of workers. The two of you, standing among the moving crowd, are like two drops in the ocean.

speaker: Deren
content: What you just said is all true. But... it is what it is.
Now there is a steady stream of workers that separates you from Deren. She gives you a childlike smile, just like the one she gave you in your first encounter.

speaker: Deren
content: Making movies takes money. My movie was no exception; a lot of people invested in it.

speaker: Deren
content: I did want the world to see my movie, to see my ideas being realized on the screen.

speaker: Deren
content: But you can't always get what you want. If it was the director's cut that had been used, it would've never been accepted, and the efforts of everyone involved in making the movie would've gone down the drain.

speaker: Deren
content: I couldn't let that happen.
The sun has set low, and the temperature has dropped. Thin clouds form as you breathe.

speaker: Deren
content: The movie won universal acclaim after it was screened in the DisCars. Everyone was celebrating.

speaker: Deren
content: I'm the only one who was angry. I wasn't angry with them, because they hadn't done anything wrong.

speaker: Deren
content: I guess... I was angry with myself.

speaker: Deren
content: I was angry, and tried and failed to justify to myself what I had done. Then in my chaotic mind, something exploded into existence and split into many shadows—fifty of them, maybe. They took over my mind and started dancing.
Deren opens her arms and starts twirling like the dancers in the movie, making a full circle around you.

speaker: Deren
content: The dance was replayed over and over in my mind. And over and over, the shadow figures died before my eyes.

speaker: Deren
content: I wanted to do something for them, so I shot some short films and got on talk shows that I had previously avoided.

speaker: Deren
content: But what I said on the talk shows and through my short films was nothing more than a drop of water in the ocean, vanished without a trace.
Deren is standing with her back to you. You can't see her expression, but you can hear the helplessness and frustration in her voice.

speaker: Deren
content: So... that's that.

speaker: Deren
content: I accepted reality. That's not the end of the world.

speaker: Deren
content: They sold out, they partied... As for me, I stopped making movies. What I earned is enough to last me a lifetime.
You're looking at Deren's back. As she delivers the last remark, she shrugs slightly, and perhaps... proudly.
You step forward to stand beside her. When you speak again, your tone of voice is strangely detached, just like Deren's.
Accepting reality... Doesn't it mean you can't change it? Doesn't it mean you can only sit by and do nothing?
Deren seems surprised by your words. Then she chuckles, and narrows her eyes into slits, looking at you intensely.

speaker: Deren
content: Sounds like you know something that I don't.

options: Do you want me to tell you?

speaker: Deren
content: I'm intrigued, to be honest.
This factory has been around for a long time. Its name, Jaminet, is quite new though. It was adopted only three years ago.
Jaminet is also the surname of the man who manages the factory. But he is not the head of the factory, not in name at least; his sister is.
He was supposed to inherit this factory after his sister died. But he didn't want to; instead, he kept his title as vice president.

He hires special workers—a girl who ran away from home to escape being forced into marriage, a youngster who was forced to sell his organs to support his younger siblings, and many other members of the underprivileged who quarreled with fate.
Deren has an aha moment as the last of the workers walk out of the gate in twos and threes.

speaker: Deren
content: This is?

speaker: Deren
content: The young woman in a suit at the end of the movie?
If her brother hadn't changed the name, I wouldn't have been able to find this place.
I talked to him a while back. He still remembered the day you met.
Deren looks at the nameplate, which looks much newer than the exterior of the factory. She nods, recalling.

speaker: Deren
content: I remember too.

speaker: Deren
content: His sister's journal was the inspiration for the movie.

speaker: Deren
content: I found it in a junk shop.

speaker: Deren
content: Every item in a junk shop has a story. I really enjoy spending time there, looking for inspiration.
Deren takes you by the arm and leads you to the narrow flowerbed of roses under the nameplate. The two of you sit down on the edge, and she starts recounting the story about the journal.

speaker: Deren
content: At first, I thought it belonged to a man, because it was full of notes on such subjects as finance, business, and politics. I only realized that it belonged to a woman when I came to the part where she complained about her mother, who had sent her to piano and violin lessons, instead of letting her stay in school with her younger brother.

speaker: Deren
content: That's also when I realized that I was just as bigoted as her mother.

speaker: Deren
content: The journal was a detailed account of her experiences and thoughts. I read through it in one night. In the pages, I saw a brave spirit who with every fiber of her being decried the injustices of her fate.

speaker: Deren
content: She dreamed of starting a business, and her brother supported her. But her parents wouldn't allow it.

speaker: Deren
content: Her wings were clipped before she could learn to fly.

speaker: Deren
content: She was forced into marriage with a family friend. As a married woman, she lived in a grandiose mansion, where she put her frustrations into words. In the end, she died in childbirth.
Your shackles start throbbing violently, a signal that Deren might be losing control. But you don't want to stop her from continuing.

The words in the journal have been etched on Deren's mind. That night, she read through the journal in the two hours between 5 p.m. to 7 p.m. And connected through the shackles, you can feel how the words are making Deren feel.
Now, the words have come alive, recreating the world of their writer before you and Deren again and again.
She was powerless but brave.

speaker: Deren
content: When the final moment of her life came, she became a heroine to herself.
You reach out your hand, locking eyes with Deren. She gives a wan smile before putting her hand on yours.

The moment her hand touches yours, the shackles on your wrist come into contact with her hand. Presently, red thorns twist and turn, coming together to form an image of a young woman. Time freezes, as the image bursts into flames and burns to ashes.
The ashes fall, and time starts running again, as if nothing had happened.
The movie should've ended differently. The characters should've voiced their true thoughts at the end.

speaker: Deren
content: I know. But there's nothing I could do about it. That's the ending the audience wanted to see.
The movie came up in my conversation with Mr. Jaminet.
Well, long story short, Mr. Jaminet changed the name of the factory because of the movie.

speaker: Deren
content: Really? But it's not unusual for a factory to be named after the person who runs it, right?
You point at a spot above her hat. She tips her head back and sees another word, surrounded by roses, before the word Jaminet on the nameplate: MISS.
Mr. Jaminet told me, although trapped in an unhappy marriage, his sister never gave up on her dream; she still wanted the world to hear her voice, and that's why she kept a journal.
After she passed away, the housekeeper sold the journal by accident, but as luck would have it, it ended up in your hands.
Mr. Jaminet saw his sister in the young woman in a suit who appears at the end of the movie... and countless other females just like her.
The ending was not exactly what he had expected, but he still thought it was a beautiful one. I understand why he felt that way. The young woman in the movie is not dead, after all.
Deren throws up her hands and sighs.

speaker: Deren
content: I didn't give them enough credit. They must have gone to some trouble to salvage those shots from God knows where to make the final scene.
But this "beautiful" ending was what inspired him to revive his sister's dream, and let the world see his sister for who she was.
He changed the name of the factory and hired people like those in the movie, unfortunate but strong, while making his sister the permanent head of the factory.
You stand up and plant yourself before Deren.
Sorry, I shouldn't have brought you here. It was out of line, even if you did leave this notebook for me.

speaker: Deren
content: No need to apologize. You can take me wherever you like, like when you took me to the MBCC.
Cough cough... that's not what I meant.
What I meant to say is... Don't let yourself be bound by what others think of you. Don't let yourself be defined by the label they gave you. Break free and be yourself.
Because you, Director Deren, are no ordinary person.
Deren rests her chin on her hand and looks up at you, a smile blossoming on her face.

speaker: Deren
content: You're right. I'm a vicious person detained by the MBCC, an avoided-at-all-cost Sinner.
Well, Miss Sinner, would you like to peel off all the labels attached to you in front of everybody and let them see the movie that you've wanted them to see all along?
Deren is confused for a moment. She looks from you to the notebook in her hand and catches on to what you've just suggested.
She takes your extended hand and stands to her feet. She is wearing a mischievous grin on her face.

speaker: Deren
content: I didn't expect you, Chief of the MBCC, to come up with such a crazy idea.
I hang around with lunatics like you, so...

speaker: Deren
content: Thanks for the compliment. Lunatic... I quite like the moniker.
Gone are the last vestiges of daylight. In the dimness, you see the world reflected in Deren's eyes, bright like a star.
The days fly past. The long-awaited DisCars ceremony rolls around, and the whole Eastside comes alive.

In the days leading up to the ceremony, there has been much hype in Dillywood about Deren's new movie. It comes as no surprise that a large number of reporters have gathered outside the main venue for the ceremony.
But they are not in luck. They won't be able to see the director they are here for, since she is at the back entrance with you.
What is with you and back entrances?

speaker: Deren
content: Well, it's quieter. I'm sure you don't want to get stuck in the crowd, surrounded by a bunch of blinking cameras, right?

speaker: Deren
content: Relax. You're safe with me. I know my way around this place, though last time I was using this route to get out, not get in.
On the way here, you and Deren have avoided reporters that seem to have popped out of nowhere.
You and Deren walk into the hall and take your seats. The ceremony is heating up. But you soon realize that...

options: There's no escape from the inevitable...

speaker: Deren
content: Have mercy on me, Chief. You're not gonna stand by and watch me suffer, are you?
Deren leans toward you ever so slightly and whispers in your ear, while maintaining her smile for the cameras.
The host seems hell-bent on taking advantage of the hype surrounding Deren, asking for her opinion before announcing the nominees for each award.

speaker: Host
content: Let's see... The next one is for Best Makeup.

speaker: Host
content: Any thoughts on this, Miss Deren?

speaker: Deren
content: Makeup, or more broadly, the combination of makeup, costumes, and props, is indispensable to a great movie, though the Award for Best Makeup might not sound as important as the others.

speaker: Deren
content: Most often than not, how a character looks can mean the difference between alienating an audience and drawing them in, so...

speaker: Host
content: Well said, well said indeed. Now... without further ado, here are the nominees for achievement in makeup.
The protracted presentation of the awards ends, and the much-anticipated screening of upcoming movies begins.
The audience applauds and cheers, but not with excessive enthusiasm, at the end of each of the movies that come before Deren's.
The opinions given on the movies are contrived and stilted; they sound like work reports ghostwritten by some Eastside Sinners in a rush.
You understand why the audience is getting impatient. Deren's movie is the last to be shown.
We're next. Are you ready?

speaker: Deren
content: I can't wait.
A great cheer goes up from the crowd when the host announces that the next movie to be screened is Deren's.
You follow Deren onto the stage, asking the projectionist to sit offstage, and take over as a temporary projectionist.

speaker: Deren
content: Looks like everyone is looking forward to my new movie.

speaker: Audience
content: Absolutely!

speaker: Audience
content: That's why we are here!

speaker: Deren
content: Thank you for your support. I'm honored.

speaker: Audience
content: We'll support you forever!

speaker: Deren
content: Making movies isn't easy. The director's vision and skills are important, but a movie couldn't be made without input from the rest of the crew.

speaker: Deren
content: They also have dreams, and they also turn their dreams into reality when a movie is made.

speaker: Audience
content: Bravo! Now show us the movie!

speaker: Deren
content: And film editing is not as easy as you might think.

speaker: Deren
content: Even when they have a clear idea about how a storyboard should look and what shots should be selected, film editors still have to cut footage and piece the strips of footage together.

speaker: Deren
content: It can be the dullest job in the world if you don't have a passion for it.

speaker: Deren
content: But film editing can also change how a movie turns out, and even decide the message it conveys.
The screen behind Deren remains black. The audience has lost their patience, urging her on with shouts.

speaker: Audience
content: What's with this long speech? Just show us the movie!

speaker: Audience
content: Yeah, show us the movie!

speaker: Audience
content: Miss Deren, show us how you've outdone yourself again!

speaker: Deren
content: Do you really want to see it now?

speaker: Audience
content: Yes. Right Now!

speaker: Deren
content: Are you sure?

speaker: Audience
content: Don't keep us in suspense!

speaker: Audience
content: Of course we are!

speaker: Audience
content: One hundred percent!
Deren turns off the microphone, walks to the center of the stage, and gives a smile, her eyes sweeping around the room.
Then she bows low to the audience.

speaker: Deren
content: All right. Please enjoy...
You press the play button. The screen in the back flickers, and then an eerie red light spreads across it. Everyone is taken back to five years ago, to when the movie was first released.
There are murmurs in the crowd. "Isn't this supposed to be a new movie?" "Isn't this the movie from five years ago?"
Slowly but surely, everyone in the audience comes to realize that the movie they are watching couldn't be more different from the one from five years ago.
The shots are the same, but the way these shots have been edited and presented is different. Now they convey something entirely different.

speaker: Deren
content: My best work. This is the movie that I wanted to show you five years ago.
As the movie plays on, the audience starts getting antsy.

speaker: Deren
content: Please stay where you are. The movie is not over yet. Okay?
Deren raises her hand and uses her power on the crowd. Their faces are frozen in different expressions.
You see the image in Deren's head: Rose petals falling from above and landing at the audience's feet.
More petals fall and gather around the many pairs of feet, keeping them from moving. The audience will not be released until the movie ends.

Chaos reigns. The audience watches, as the girl in white, tear-stained and helpless, screams at them, as the pale-face boy pulls out the vines that have sunk into his flesh, as the young woman in a suit burns down everything around her, sucks every bit of redness into her fountain pen, and uses it to write down her wildest dreams on a giant piece of paper.
Deren reaches out and takes your hand. She leads you up onto the stage. And the two of you bow to the crowd.

speaker: Deren
content: Thank you. Thanks to everyone who worked on this movie back in the day.

speaker: Deren
content: Thanks to everyone who helped me in making this movie possible.

speaker: Deren
content: Thanks to those who inspired me.

speaker: Deren
content: Thank you for making me become a "lunatic" again.
With that last sentence, Deren turns to you.

speaker: Deren
content: I didn't walk the red carpet five years ago. Would you do me the honor of walking it with me?
Absolutely. After all, I did play a small part in reviving this great movie.

speaker: Deren
content: You played much more than a small part.
Deren takes your hand. And with the big crowd watching, the two of you walk the red carpet and head toward the exit.

speaker: Deren
content: You're the star of my eyes.
█/12 12:35 PM, at the MBCC cafeteria.
Little do you expect to meet Donald again in a place like this.

speaker: Donald
content: I'd always heard the chatter among those Sinners about MBCC's great grub, and it's no tall tale...
There's Donald, clutching a juicy roast pork knuckle in one hand and a whole jug of fresh juice in the other, his face shining with grease.

speaker: Donald
content: Honestly, the chef's magic here... A little buzz and who'd need a capture team, right? The Sinners outside would queue up in a heartbeat.
As he speaks, Donald flashes a thumbs-up to Kelvin and Ignis working their wonders in the nearby kitchen.
Soon after Donald polishes off that pork knuckle in no time, he shouts towards the kitchen:

speaker: Donald
content: A bowl of noodles next, I reckon. Then, surprise me with dessert, and I'll be on my merry way.

speaker: Donald
content: Gotta have the ice cream, it's a hit here at MBCC, right?
Once Kelvin delivers the dishes ordered by the "guest," she scoots back to the kitchen, then slyly peeks out to glance over at you.
Obviously, the other Sinners are just as curious about the bold blonde guy who shamelessly scrounges for meals from the Bureau. They huddle in groups nearby, murmuring and gesturing towards him.
And when you glance back at Donald, the table's feast is gone, devoured. There he is, slumped contentedly in his chair, leisurely picking his teeth with a satisfied grin.
How's the West District's big hero starving like this? Hope no one's been messing with you?

speaker: Donald
content: Ha, no way. Been all over the place, up to my neck in tasks. Eating? Barely had the time.

speaker: Donald
content: You're a real pal... If you ever need a hand, just give me a shout. I can't promise I'll always come through, but you'll always have my loyalty.
Nah, don't mention it, it's just a meal.
A busy bee like you wouldn't make a special trip just to my place for a free meal, would you?

speaker: Donald
content: Belch... You know me too well.
Donald flicks the toothpick into the bin and gets to his feet.

speaker: Donald
content: Of course, I've come to you for some serious business to discuss.
What serious business?
Donald scans the surroundings, then sidles up to you, speaking in a hushed tone.

speaker: Donald
content: It's too crowded here, let's find a quieter place to chat.
...Okay. I'll sort out a spot.
Follow me.

speaker: Donald
content: No...

speaker: Donald
content: Is this where you Bureau folks usually talk shop?
No one ever comes here normally.

speaker: Donald
content: Exactly, right? Who'd be sane and bored enough to hang out in a spot like this?

speaker: Donald
content: Plus, I'm well aware that your MBCC interrogations of the Sinners are always recorded.
Relax, I've already disabled the cameras beforehand.

speaker: Donald
content: Should I be singing your praises or something?... Cheers, you've really thought of everything.
You're welcome.

speaker: Donald
content: Talk about getting cocky... Really, what I'm talking about isn't so hush-hush, let's not stand on ceremony...
Who had the bright idea to hole up somewhere out of sight again?
Oh, that was your call, Mr. Donald.
And remember, you're quite the "persona non grata" now. You've still got that juicy bounty from Nirvana hanging over you.

speaker: Donald
content: Me... well... you've got a point. But I can't shake the feeling this isn't the first time we've seen this happen.

speaker: Donald
content: ...You know, this "serious business" actually ties back to Nirvana.

speaker: Donald
content: Of course, it's that blasted bounty. Nirvana's got eyes and ears everywhere, and guess who they've targeted now. I'm solo, up the creek without a paddle, so here I am, begging for your help...
Stop pulling my leg. With your smarts and network, Nirvana couldn't catch you in a million years.

speaker: Donald
content: I'm dead serious... Yet, you've got a point, if I'm set on laying low, they won't lay a finger on me.

speaker: Donald
content: But, you know, it's kind of tricky... They've really "zeroed in" on me.
They came after you? You're saying...

speaker: Donald
content: First, I need to make one thing clear to you.
Donald slightly straightens up, his expression unusually serious.

speaker: Donald
content: Did you catch the news about the "psych patients" cropping up in the West District for the last half-year?
You shake your head.

speaker: Donald
content: Makes sense you're out of the loop. You've just woken up, after all.

speaker: Donald
content: In a nutshell, for the last half-year, BR-002 has been spreading Mania non-stop in the West District, impacting quite a few people.

speaker: Donald
content: The good news is, these folks are faring better than the earlier victims of Mania. They're mainly dealing with intense mental burnout, but it's not life-threatening, at least not for now.

speaker: Donald
content: With prompt medical care, they'll bounce back completely, and it won't mess with their lives going forward...
But the West District as it stands, we're not equipped to help them, are we?

speaker: Donald
content: That's right. The West District, as things stand, isn't equipped to tackle this issue.

speaker: Donald
content: The city's just starting to rebuild, and the only dependable medical center is SALVA Hospital. But, the patient count is just too high...

speaker: Donald
content: Right now, we've got more than two thousand serious cases on record, way more than what SALVA can cope with.

speaker: Donald
content: Then there's the mild cases... We can't do a mass check-up right now, but a safe guess? Several tens of thousands.
Donald's revelation sends a shiver down your spine.
This is a tough one... With these numbers, even the Bureau is overwhelmed.
But, I might be able to use my political clout to get the Eastside's big shots to chip in with donations. Then, we can set up a medical team in the name of humanitarian relief...
Watching your earnest offer to help, Donald gestures dismissively.

speaker: Donald
content: What you've done for the West District is no secret to anyone. But this, this doesn't require your intervention.

speaker: Donald
content: The West District is broke, sure, but once the Hypercube trade kicks off, money won't be an issue. We've got this covered.

speaker: Donald
content: It's actually something else we could use your help with, something trickier.
What do you need me to do?

speaker: Donald
content: Well, it's quite the tale...
Donald takes a moment, then goes on:

speaker: Donald
content: You know how it is, there's been a flood of folks from Eastside recently. Some on business, others just showing off, and naturally, people from the West District looking for treatment for the Mania-induced disease.

speaker: Donald
content: The issue cropped up right there. A few so-called "doctors" snatched up a "classic case" before they went back to Eastside...
At this juncture, there's a mix of resignation and appeal in Donald's eyes.

speaker: Donald
content: The lady's name is... Margaret, she's my aunt.

speaker: Donald
content: I'm hoping you can help me get her back.
Listening to Donald, you piece together who Margaret is.
Right now, there's pretty much just one likely candidate behind such actions.
Nirvana...

speaker: Donald
content: That's right, they're from Nirvana.

speaker: Donald
content: They're actually from Banyan Fourth Hospital in Eastside, a hospital specializing in mental health.
Hmm...
They're planning to use Margaret as leverage, to draw you out, isn't that the case?

speaker: Donald
content: I can't see any other reason for this.

speaker: Donald
content: How did they manage to single out my aunt from more than two thousand patients? They really pulled out all the stops, fooling the neighbors in the Drifter Camp and whisking her away, claiming it was for treatment.
These folks are relentless, aren't they?
But this is a bit of a tough spot.
If I go straight to the top brass and lean on them, I might just scare them off. Who knows what kind of dirty tricks they'll pull then.

speaker: Donald
content: I know that much. But since I've sought you out, it means I've already figured out a way.

speaker: Donald
content: Even though Nirvana pulls the strings at Banyan Fourth Hospital, not everybody there is their puppet.

speaker: Donald
content: I'm acquainted with a doc from there—turns out, he's just the right person to tackle our present troubles in the West District...
You instantly catch on to Donald's plan.
You mean, I can get close to him by offering him a chance to treat patients in the West District, and use that as a cover to sniff out news about Margaret, correct?

speaker: Donald
content: Haha, you always make things straightforward!
But is this plan solid?

speaker: Donald
content: Trust me, I know this guy. He's steered clear of Banyan Fourth's riffraff for years, always getting the cold shoulder from Nirvana's crowd.

speaker: Donald
content: You can totally rely on his medical expertise and moral integrity. Choosing him is a sure bet.
Donald looks like he's got it all figured out.
Okay, I'm on it... What did you say his name was?

speaker: Donald
content: Das Arz. He's the chief psychiatrist at Banyan Fourth Hospital these days. You'll likely catch him during working hours with a simple appointment.
You note down this doc's details and then glance up at Donald.
Come to think of it, a shrink from Eastside Psychiatric Hospital... and one under Nirvana's thumb. How'd you even get in touch with him?

speaker: Donald
content: You know me, Donald, the walking Rolodex, pals everywhere. Knowing a shrink isn't exactly a shocker, is it?
Donald muses for a second, then remarks:

speaker: Donald
content: Oh, and a heads-up, the guy's not exactly Mr. Nice, tends to rub people the wrong way with his talk... Just don't mind that, he's actually alright at heart...
Right, I've got a handle on this.

speaker: Donald
content: Good as long as you know what you're doing...
Donald starts to speak, looking like he's got more to add, but he appears to be holding back a bit.
Out with it.

speaker: Donald
content: Ha, yeah... right, there's no point in mincing words with you.

speaker: Donald
content: Anyway, it's not like me to ask for help much, but this time... I really do need your hand in this.

speaker: Donald
content: I'm asking you, please.
█/13, 5:24 PM, at the entrance of Banyan Fourth Hospital.
Why are you here too...
A blond man donning an eccentric mask cautiously peeks from behind a decorative tree near the hospital's front gate.
Didn't you tell me you couldn't show your face in Eastside and asked me to step in for you?

speaker: Donald
content: A true man stands with honor and sits with dignity; why be afraid?
How about you remove that mask before talking?

speaker: Donald
content: Ah, well...

speaker: Donald
content: I'm just worried about you going into the "den of demons" by yourself, you know.
Donald's voice comes from behind that ludicrous mask, prompting you to instinctively press your hand against your forehead.
Where in the world did you get that mask?

speaker: Donald
content: That purple-haired young lady from your Supply Office handed it over.

speaker: Donald
content: I requested some disguise gear, and she demanded payment. I asked if there could be a discount...

speaker: Donald
content: It's all good, it's all good. The main thing is it keeps me incognito, and it works out the same.

speaker: Donald
content: Company's arriving... Quick, go handle it.
Meanwhile, at the hospital's front gate, a towering nurse is heading your way.

speaker: Nurse
content: You're the Chief of MBCC, aren't you?
The nurse comes to a halt before you, and it is then that you fully sense the intimidating presence of this psychiatric hospital nurse.
He towers over Donald by half a head, his muscles almost ripping out of his nurse outfit.

speaker: Nurse
content: Okay.
The towering nurse takes a brief look at Donald by your side.

speaker: Nurse
content: Is this individual part of your entourage?
...That's correct.

speaker: Nurse
content: There was no mention of a plus-one in the appointment.
Thinking on his feet, Donald blurts out:

speaker: Donald
content: I'm the bodyguard!

speaker: Donald
content: It's not too much to have an aide along when our MBCC Chief is out and about, is it?
The nurse gives you both a once-over and appears to be fine with that answer.

speaker: Nurse
content: Okay, come with me, I'll escort you to Dr. Das.
The nurse, towering and unyielding like a steel colossus, ushers you into the hospital.
You keep a cautious distance between yourselves. Stepping through the main entrance, you lean in and murmur to Donald:
I can't believe he bought it that quickly, and didn't even rib you about your wacky get-up.

speaker: Donald
content: Isn't that a testament to how spot-on my disguise is?
...I guess it's just that we've become numb to the bizarre.

speaker: Nurse
content: Banyan Fourth Hospital, an esteemed psychiatric hospital with a storied past, also deals with patients impacted by Mania with erratic M-values.
As you walk, the nurse occasionally chimes in with snippets of the hospital's lore.
Well, that sounds a lot like what we do at MBCC...

speaker: Nurse
content: But they're worlds apart.

speaker: Nurse
content: We're in the healing business, a hospital. You guys run a containment facility for the Sinners. Our roles are fundamentally distinct.
The nurse seems utterly oblivious to the concept of "a joke," glancing back at you as he walks.

speaker: Nurse
content: Moreover, under normal circumstances, we don't take Sinners.
Why?
You ask instinctively.

speaker: Nurse
content: Their destructive power when they go berserk is too great, hard to control...

speaker: Nurse
content: The patient activity zone is just ahead.
As the nurse speaks, his stride noticeably quickens, prompting you to pick up your pace to stay in step.
Here, in this section, you can see patients in hospital gowns, huddled in twos and threes, either standing or sitting.
A few just stand there, unmoving; others make odd, indistinct sounds. Some even seem to be having animated conversations with thin air, gesturing enthusiastically.

speaker: Nurse
content: The activity zone is a unique feature of our Fourth Hospital. It allows patients to partake in cultural pursuits, almost like they're living a normal life outside...
Ding-a-ling...
The abrupt ring of a bell cuts off the nurse's speech.
Grabbing the personal device fastened to his belt, he hit a key and asks in a deep, echoing tone:

speaker: Nurse
content: What is it?

speaker: Noise
content: The patients in the lab are having a meltdown... we can't hold them back...

speaker: Nurse
content: Understood, I'm on my way.
With a swift click ending the call, the nurse pivots back to you.

speaker: Nurse
content: Apologies, got an urgent matter, stay put here.
Then, before your eyes, this behemoth of a man, well over six feet, takes off in giant strides, barreling out like a truck at full throttle.
After rounding a bend, he disappears, his footsteps lingering in the halls like rumbling thunder.
Did the nurse... really just ditch us here?
What's our next move?

speaker: Donald
content: Next move? Hang tight. You've got no clue where the doctor's office is, do you?
Even then, we're in the midst of the mental hospital's patient zone...
Surely, nothing can go wrong, can it?

speaker: Donald
content: With me here, what's there to be scared of?
It's not fear, really, but there's something unsettling about these patients...
Donald moves in closer to you, murmuring softly:

speaker: Donald
content: You're right... They're mostly innocent civilians, oppressed by Nirvana and imprisoned here under the guise of "unstable M-values."
It's only after Donald points it out that you notice the clear scars on them, some even missing parts of their bodies.
Yeah, if we get the chance, we should definitely rescue them too...
But, there's something I've been wondering.
You pivot, your gaze settling on Donald.

options: How come you know this place so well?

content: You even know the doctor, and you're clued up about the patients' situations...
Someone from the West District knowing this much about the Eastside's mental hospital...
You haven't been here before, right?

speaker: Donald
content: What's that? Networking, man, networking, get it?
Donald gives his chest an exaggerated pat.

speaker: Donald
content: A guy as badass as me, I fit in anywhere...
Just as you're about to retort, a voice unexpectedly echoes from behind:

speaker: Patient A
content: Isn't that... Isn't that the great hero?

speaker: Donald
content: Cough, cough...

speaker: Patient A
content: Hey, it's me—the Emperor of Paradeisos. You don't know who I am anymore?
Donald stands rooted to the spot.

speaker: Patient A
content: Stammering and not responding to me, have you turned against me? You're guilty of treason against the crown! Off with your head! Execute every last one of them!

speaker: Patient A
content: Guards, come here! Arrest this rebel!

speaker: Donald
content: No, no, no...
Donald, with a sense of resignation, turns around and puts on a strained smile.

speaker: Donald
content: How could I not know you, Your Imperial Majesty?

speaker: Patient A
content: Just as it should be. Assist me well in my grand endeavors, and you'll be handsomely rewarded... Wait, what's going on with you? You look... different.

speaker: Patient A
content: Has it really been that long? When did you grow such a long beard?

speaker: Patient A
content: Hey everyone, check this out! Our hero's back, and he's sporting a beard now!
"The Emperor of Paradeisos" rings out loudly, stirring the patients in the activity area who, sensing the commotion, hurriedly converge.

speaker: Patient B
content: Is that you, the great hero?
The situation has reached a point where Donald can't hide anymore. He takes off his mask and offers a slightly embarrassed smile.

speaker: Donald
content: It's me. Little Spud, long time no see. Everything good with you lately?

speaker: Patient B
content: Terrible, just terrible. Drenched daily and still no sprouts. Those jerks from the Underground keep chopping me up, I must be delicious... Wait till I sprout, they're in for a toxic surprise!

speaker: Patient C
content: Hurry up and poison them. If those lab coat guys don't bite the dust soon, I'll be the one done in. They're zapping me with lightning like it's a game.

speaker: Donald
content: They're zapping you with lightning?

speaker: Patient C
content: How would I know? Once you were gone, I turned into the human lightning rod. If I don't get zapped, someone else will...

speaker: Patient A
content: It's all on me... I gave the order for the mole to tunnel, and that's how those rebels found us... I've put him in danger...

speaker: Patient B
content: Hey, big hero, when are you planning to get us out? If this keeps up, I'm going to be cut down to nothing.

speaker: Donald
content: We're almost there...
Donald's eyes take on a determined glint.

speaker: Donald
content: Hang tight, I'll get you guys out soon, cross my heart.

speaker: Patient B
content: But how soon is "soon"? You've been away forever...
Patients buzz around Donald in a noisy throng, firing questions left and right. Out of the blue, the "Paradeisos Emperor" snaps to attention, his head jerking up.

speaker: Patient A
content: Trouble's brewing, we've got company! Troops, heed my call—fall back!
With the "Paradeisos Emperor's" shout, the patients disperse like leaves in the wind.
The nurse's unmistakable heavy tread draws nearer, and Donald quickly slips his mask back on.
Once done, Donald shoots you a somewhat sheepish look.

speaker: Donald
content: Like I always say, I thrive wherever I go... Not just hot air, right?
So, you did stay...

speaker: Donald
content: Hush—here comes the nurse.

speaker: Donald
content: Let's focus on the task at hand. I'll fill you in once we're back, but for now, let's head over there.

speaker: Nurse
content: Over here.
The nurse opens the office door. You and Donald step inside, and then he withdraws, quietly shutting the door.
The doctor, perched at his desk, continues writing without glancing up.
Hi, I'm ${PlayerName}, Chief of MBCC. We had a meeting booked for this afternoon.

speaker: Doctor
content: Das Arz.
The doctor introduces himself, but his hands keep busy the whole time.
An eerie quiet settles over the office.
You pause briefly, realizing the doctor isn't going to continue speaking, and then you begin:
I'm here to ask if you would consider treating...

speaker: Das
content: The patients with Mania from the West District, I know.
Well... what do you...
The doctor briefly lifts his gaze to meet yours.

speaker: Das
content: No treatment.
I've been told you're a highly skilled psychiatrist...

speaker: Das
content: When I say no treatment, it's not that it's beyond my ability.
Don't worry about the costs, MBCC and the Eastside's charities have got it covered...

speaker: Das
content: It's not a question of money.

speaker: Das
content: I mean it when I say no treatment—absolutely none.
Das's icy and rigid manner catches you off-guard for a moment.

speaker: Das
content: Better to ask your "bodyguard."
Turning, you find Donald scratching his head, taking off his mask, his smile carrying a hint of resignation.

speaker: Donald
content: Das, meet my friend, the savior of the whole West District, you...

speaker: Das
content: A fugitive, yet you have the audacity to show up here... You're after the patient from the West District, right?
The doctor halts his writing, looks up, and raps his pen sharply on the desk.

speaker: Das
content: She's locked in the hospital's subterranean quarters—right where they kept you. Under 24-hour surveillance, your chances are nil.

speaker: Das
content: Also, don't count on any assistance from my end.
As he speaks, the doctor shoots you a brief look.

speaker: Das
content: So, you're the Chief of MBCC, aren't you? I'm at a loss about why you're in his corner, but you've definitely been duped.

speaker: Das
content: This "guard" of yours? He's a former patient of mine—a real ticking time bomb. He pulled a fast one and escaped the grip of the hospital. No one knows how he did it.
The doctor gets to his feet, sifts through a file cabinet next to him, and passes over a file to you.

speaker: Das
content: In case you're doubting, this is his medical history. Have a look, and it'll all make sense.

speaker: Das
content: By all rights, I ought to be alerting the hospital's security at this very moment, to snag this wanted criminal back into custody for some much-needed therapy.

speaker: Das
content: But I am simply a doctor. My role is to treat and save lives, not to engage in your political conflicts with Nirvana.

speaker: Das
content: However, a word of advice: The Fourth Hospital is a legitimate medical facility, supported by Nirvana.

speaker: Das
content: Think carefully about the consequences if you decide to go against them.
Das shifts his attention away, settling back at his desk and diving back into his work.

speaker: Das
content: You're probably not here for medical advice, right? If that's the case, we've got nothing to talk about.

speaker: Das
content: Please close the door as you leave.
With a courteous nudge from the nurse, you and Donald are promptly shown the door of the doctor's office.
Looks like this is going to be tougher than we thought...
Once out of the hospital, you and Donald hop into the car heading back to the Bureau.

speaker: Donald
content: Chances are, Das has run into some trouble himself...

speaker: Donald
content: He tried quitting last year, handing in his notice to the Fourth Hospital. But here he is, still stuck there...
He did give us the scoop on Ms. Margaret's location, though, and even snagged your file on his way out.
We didn't come back empty-handed, at least.

speaker: Donald
content: Ha, always looking on the bright side, huh?
Got that from you, didn't I?
You take a quick look at the medical file you are holding.
Things have shifted, so we might need to cook up a fresh plan.

speaker: Donald
content: Easy does it. Let's break down the info we've got first.

speaker: Donald
content: We'll find a solution, for sure...
█/14, 2:41 AM, Chief's Office.
You flip through the files Dr. Das had handed over, back in the office.
This looks like a regular Eastside medical chart, but the details here... they're anything but ordinary diagnosis and treatment.

Name: Donald   Gender: Male   Age: █
Medical Record Number: █████████
Diagnosis: Donald, a Sinner from West District and the leader of the notorious "Rustfire" terror faction, was heavily tainted by Mania during the BR-002 event. Marked by Hush for survival, he narrowly escaped death.
From N.F. 104 to N.F. 105, he was repeatedly manipulated and tasked with handling Rustfire operations, causing IV mental trauma. Resistant yet unadaptable, he failed to undergo the puppet conversion, leading to his transfer to our institution for advanced treatment.
Currently, Donald is grappling with intense schizophrenia, has lost all speech, and shows no reaction to the outside world. As a high-value S-Class Sinner, he's a prime candidate for advanced experimental research. Following top-level directives, he's been moved to Lab B4 for continued study and intervention.
As you keep turning the pages, what comes next is even more shockingly eye-opening.

Medical Log:
On █/█/106, initiated participation in the power augmentation trials for the Sinners.
On █/█/106, attempted external stimulation through electrocution, acid exposure, extreme heat, and cryogenic methods. The subject nearly died three times without any notable rise in the M-value.

On █/█/107, the patient showed subdued brain activity, failing to produce vital emotional reactions. The only notable spike in mental activity was observed during what appeared to be dreams about the BR-002 incident. These spikes are detrimental to the patient. While this has left him unable to resist for an extended time, it has also severely hindered the project's timeline.

As of █/█/107, the patient will be transferred to psychiatric care bi-weekly. This decision by Lab B4 aims to partially rehabilitate the patient's mental health, anticipating improved outcomes in future experiments.

As of █/█/108, Lab B4 has concluded that the patient no longer holds research value. The request for his benign processing was overruled by senior management. Considering the patient's inability to function independently, permission was granted to step up psychiatric interventions. Nonetheless, constant supervision by an assigned officer is mandatory. In case of any irregularities, both the patient and any related staff will be subject to benign processing.

speaker: Donald
content: Why are you still up so late?
Donald wears a smile, but his hands are far from idle. He nonchalantly flings the document onto the topmost shelf of the office bookcase.

speaker: Donald
content: There's no use reading that.

speaker: Donald
content: These medical records, crammed with bureaucratic speak, won't really tell you what's happening at the Fourth Hospital. If it's the truth you're after, better to come see me directly.

speaker: Donald
content: Oh, worried you'll hurt my fragile emotions?

speaker: Donald
content: It's fine. I have always had a knack for moving on. It's been ages, hasn't it...

speaker: Donald
content: Alright, quick now, we've got to head back to Eastside at dawn. Any burning questions? Ask away.
Donald pulls up a chair and positions himself in front of you.
He looks completely at ease, almost as if he has genuinely moved on from the past events.
After a brief moment of thought, you voice your first question.

options: What's the real deal with Banyan Fourth Hospital?

speaker: Donald
content: It's part of Nirvana.
Donald answers, cutting to the chase.

speaker: Donald
content: The mental hospital? It's just a smokescreen. On the surface, the Fourth Hospital seems to be a part of the Banyan system, but in truth, Nirvana pulls all the strings.

speaker: Donald
content: What they really do there is run human experiments and secretly take care of the dirty work—those "issues" Nirvana can't sort out in the daylight.

speaker: Donald
content: Folks like Das? They're just part of the show, handling what they claim to be their "core business"—it's all for show for the people of Eastside.
You know, you kept some cards close to your chest during our last chat.

speaker: Donald
content: Well...
Donald scratches his head, appearing slightly embarrassed.

speaker: Donald
content: I was worried you might let your justice radar go off the charts. What if, in a moment of rage, you end up leading a charge into the Fourth Hospital, taking everyone out?
Do you really think of me like that?

speaker: Donald
content: Hey, I'm just messing with you. Look, I'm mainly here to ask for your help. It wouldn't be cool to keep pitting you against others, right?

speaker: Donald
content: Totally my fault! From now on, I'll spill the beans immediately on anything that comes up, no more hiding!
...Alright. Moving on.
What's been your journey like since then?

speaker: Donald
content: What happens next after going through that?
I just saw that the B4 Lab has labeled you "no longer holds research value"...

speaker: Donald
content: Ah, that bit.

speaker: Donald
content: I was still locked up in the lab's infirmary afterward, though they hardly took me for experiments anymore. Guess they really got bored of me, huh?

speaker: Donald
content: Dr. Das would drop by now and then, giving me meds and doing some physiotherapy.

speaker: Donald
content: Then... the game changer happened.
Donald cracks a secretive grin, leaning in a bit.
The game changer?

speaker: Donald
content: You bet! It was Samuel.

speaker: Donald
content: Guess what? An old-timer from the West District, posing as a cleaner, managed to infiltrate Nirvana's turf solo... and, incredibly, he located me.

speaker: Donald
content: Then, we teamed up, united in purpose, delivering the final blow... Though, really, it was his hustle, back and forth, that leaked the info and kicked up a whole lot of fuss.

speaker: Donald
content: Oh yeah, and there was that self-proclaimed poet lady. Don't know how, but she ended up at the Fourth Hospital and, believe it or not, she waltzed past the guards and slipped into the underground facility.

speaker: Donald
content: She filled me in on Julien building Drifter Camp, and even said Rustfire is back in action. Man, was I thrilled to hear all that—it was like a spark lit up in my brain...

speaker: Donald
content: Can you believe it? The sickness just vanished right then and there, and never came back. It's no wonder they say "good news beats the best medicine"...

speaker: Donald
content: But I'm not knocking Dr. Das' skills. Without his care and his round-the-clock guard against the Fourth Hospital's endless "experiments," I probably wouldn't have made it.
As Donald shares his story, his smile never wavers, remaining ever-present.
It's tough to picture his nightmare of an experience, and yet when he talks about it now, it sounds as carefree as discussing the weather.
But, reality might not be as laid-back as he lets on.
So, you really started to heal mentally, way after Samuel rescued you, huh?
Seeing Donald's face twist into what looks like a grimace of discomfort, you press on:
Back then, even after he stumbled upon you, he couldn't talk to you. You "had lost all speech, and showed no reaction to the outside world."
And Dr. Das couldn't shield you anymore, especially now when he's barely hanging on himself.
So, those days of being locked up and tormented went on till N.F. 112, didn't they?
As you fire question after question, a hint of resignation creeps into Donald's smile.

speaker: Donald
content: You know, I figure... it's not really important to split hairs over it.

speaker: Donald
content: The hardest times are over, and I've moved on. Why get bogged down counting every bit of pain I've been through?
In that moment, as Donald utters those words, his face radiates pure sincerity, free from any shadow of doubt in his eyes and brows.
It hits you all at once—maybe you've been too obsessed with "revealing the truth."
Sorry...

speaker: Donald
content: Hey, hey, hey, no need to say sorry, it's all good... Eesh, cut the formal act, you're making my skin crawl with these goosebumps.
Donald keeps waving his hands off. Confronted with your sincere apology, he oddly appears rather uneasy.

speaker: Donald
content: Back to the main point, huh? Got more questions? Fire away, ha...
Donald lets out an exaggerated yawn.

speaker: Donald
content: Seriously, it's this late and you're not sleepy? I'm beat.
You think for a second and then come up with another question.
Why did you have Raven go back to Drifter Camp and spread the news of your "death"?
Donald straightens up, an air of secrecy about him, and responds:

speaker: Donald
content: How about this—if I say I instantly knew that "great poet" was all talk, no show, would you buy it?
...Yeah, I'd buy it.
You lock eyes for a moment, and after a brief silence, you both start laughing out loud.

speaker: Donald
content: Hahahaha...

speaker: Donald
content: This is the first time I've realized how thrilling it is to talk smack about someone behind their back, hahaha...
While chuckling, Donald continues to explain:

speaker: Donald
content: Back then, I figured, this lady was a real yarn-spinner; gaining trust in Drifter Camp wouldn't be easy for her. If she started saying I was alive, she'd likely be shown the door right away.

speaker: Donald
content: But you know her, she's decent at heart and as a Sinner, if she got into Drifter Camp, she could really make a difference.
Is that why you cooked up this whole story for her?

speaker: Donald
content: She did most of the work; I just added a few touches. But who knew it would go so well—the "great poet" got in without a hitch, calmed things down at Drifter Camp, and really stepped up later...

speaker: Donald
content: In hindsight, that strategy was spot on. If the "great poet" had spread the word about me being alive and let Drifter Camp know I was in Nirvana's clutches...

speaker: Donald
content: Better they're skeptical. If they actually bought it and stormed Nirvana's stronghold, it'd be a suicide mission. That would've been a real disaster.
You nod thoughtfully and go on to ask:
Once you were back on your feet, teaming up with Samuel on the outside...
Given your skills, did the idea of escaping ever cross your mind?

speaker: Donald
content: Naturally, it did.

speaker: Donald
content: Back then, I was marked by a Hush. And the odds of not getting snagged again after my escape were pretty slim...

speaker: Donald
content: But what really keeps me up at night are the folks I left behind at the Fourth Hospital.
You think Nirvana might go after Das and the crew in revenge?

speaker: Donald
content: Yes.

speaker: Donald
content: And it's not just a chance, it's a guarantee they'll strike back.

speaker: Donald
content: Letting Das treat me was only so I'd be of some use in their experiments. If I got fully healed and slipped away, Das would be in deep water, no doubt about it.

speaker: Donald
content: Das has always been butting heads with them, plus he's got a lot of dirt he shouldn't... With Nirvana's no-holds-barred tactics, it's a toss-up if he'll make it out alive.

speaker: Donald
content: That's why I chose to stick around a bit longer.
Donald is all smug.

speaker: Donald
content: Turned out to be a classic case of "not seeing what's right under your nose." Those folks at the Fourth Hospital never caught on that I was just playing crazy, hahaha.
You mean to tell me you played the madman till N.F. 112 and never got busted? That's incredible!

speaker: Donald
content: Well, how else would I bag the title of a top-notch actor... Obviously, a lot of it was down to Samuel and Das playing along.

speaker: Donald
content: Get this, I once faked my own death. Boy, did I nail it. Those Fourth Hospital guys actually carted me off to the crematorium...
So, what happened next?

speaker: Donald
content: What else was there to do? Played the zombie.

speaker: Donald
content: Gave those jerks the fright of their lives; ended up in the hole for a month.

speaker: Donald
content: Post that, escaping wasn't high on my to-do list.

speaker: Donald
content: Ah, it's not like I didn't try, I just couldn't find a way out...
So, how did you manage to break free in the end?
Donald gestures with open hands.

speaker: Donald
content: Frankly, I'm not too sure.

speaker: Donald
content: Suddenly, one day, I got this order from Paradeisos and next thing I know, I was being hauled off to the Executive Committee.
Any idea who signed off on that order?

speaker: Donald
content: It's Hush X's signature on the Transfer Order, but who knows if she's the one behind it.
You're not worried about a hidden plot?

speaker: Donald
content: Why worry? There's nothing to fear.

speaker: Donald
content: Doesn't matter if it was X or someone else, the bottom line is they got me out, right?

speaker: Donald
content: Looks like that Paradeisian is probably in our corner, aiming to throw a wrench in Nirvana's plans.

speaker: Donald
content: If Paradeisos's really in lockstep with Nirvana, singing the same tune, then we're really out of luck.
You nod in agreement. Interestingly, Donald's view echoes what you've always believed.
As you ride that thought, you suddenly have an epiphany, a smirk naturally forming on your face.

speaker: Donald
content: What are you thinking about? What's with that sudden devilish smirk?
Donald gazes at your face, clearly baffled.
I'm thinking... if Paradeisos isn't all on the same page, then maybe, if I blow the lid off some things, the higher-ups won't necessarily rush to their rescue, huh?

speaker: Donald
content: Whoa! Planning to rat people out, huh?
Yep, that's right. I'm gonna spill the beans.
Eastside is at a crossroads with public sentiment shifting. A bunch of politicians are on standby to declare their stance.
Imagine the fallout if we dig up the past squabbles between the Fourth Hospital and Nirvana now. You know what's gonna happen, right?
Or, we might just decide... to keep it under wraps.

speaker: Donald
content: You mean...
Right, exactly what's on your mind.
Some cards are more intimidating in hand than on the table...

speaker: Donald
content: That's a clever strategy... It neither tips them off nor backs them into a corner. It also lets us play hardball.
Donald gives his leg a hearty slap and jumps up.

speaker: Donald
content: Okay, that's the plan!

speaker: Donald
content: I'll get in touch with some old pals, and cook up something big for the Fourth Hospital...
Seeing the fire in Donald's eyes, you can't help but gesture towards the clock.
...Maybe take a look at the time?
It's pretty late. You sure your friends will still be up for a chat?
Donald gives a lighthearted laugh, ruffling his hair.

speaker: Donald
content: True, true, time to hit the hay.
He turns and stretches out, yawning widely.

speaker: Donald
content: Better get some sleep yourself, you know. All these late nights could take a toll on you.
Appreciate your worry, Mr. Donald. Though, I've caught up on plenty of sleep not long ago...

speaker: Donald
content: Haha, you've got a point there.
█/16, 3:12 PM, Dean's Office, Banyan Fourth Hospital.
Led by the burly nurse, you and Donald enter a new, unknown office.
Take a seat, please.
The Dean's responsibilities aren't limited to the Fourth; he also manages the First and Second Hospitals, along with the Banyan Medical College. He's stretched pretty thin...
So, I'll be taking care of you this time around.
Just to introduce myself, I'm Jones, the appointed director at the Fourth Hospital.

speaker: Jones
content: What's the occasion for this visit from the Chief of MBCC, if I may ask?
The director of the Fourth Hospital is lounging back, hands clasped together, sporting a laid-back grin. He seems totally unaware of the bombshell you're about to drop.

speaker: Jones
