You had worked tirelessly to make it possible, eliminating every conceivable diplomatic risk with the Outlands, rallying support from the FAC and relevant departments at Banyan Medical College, and laying down a web of classified protocols to ensure nothing would leak and no public disturbance would arise.

The Fourth Hospital claimed the rapid approval was simply because "someone in EDGE has your back," but the sincere help they lent you along the way was never a pretense. They were genuinely concerned, and you are thankful for that.
...You are almost certainly doing something foolish.
The light switches on. Jasmine does not lift her head. She does not scream, does not surge into another attack.

Her limbs are locked in custom anti-Mania restraints. After being shackled for so long, she has abandoned all resistance, only shrinking back another inch the moment you step inside, curling further into the narrow, cold metal chair.

The interrogation room is the cell that holds her, but she has sealed herself into something even smaller still, despising your approach. On the other side—behind monitors, outside the room—your subordinates are on full alert.

News of the Banyan Fourth Hospital incident had circulated everywhere. Nobody dares expose you to danger again. Between conducting a multi-officer interrogation and limiting her movements, you chose the latter, hoping it might disturb her less.

—Of course, such considerations mean nothing to her. In the shadow of her unkempt hair, Jasmine's glare locks onto you, dark and malevolent, tinged with a faint red gleam. This reunion is hard to breathe through.
After a long, drawn-out silence, you rise from your seat in the "safe zone" and step toward her, halting just before she can recoil. You indicate her wrists, chafed and inflamed beneath the cuffs.

speaker: %u
content: If it's bothering you, I'll take them off.

speaker: %u
content: It's just the two of us here. It's okay.
Seeing no resistance, you take another step closer and kneel down beside Jasmine, your hands moving to unfasten the tightest of her shackles.
She watches you for a long moment, then lowers her head and leans in, sniffing. At last, the ghost of a smile touches her lips.

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...You've washed... So many new scents on you now... Heh...

speaker: Jasmine
content: Trying to cover up that <color=#fb9259>stench</color>?
Your hands pause.

It seems she has indeed grown much calmer, her sharpness and cunning restored. She has enough composure left to test you, to provoke you, to hurt you, like a fox playing with a discovered trap, pressing just enough without ever going too far.
You don't answer. You keep working. Click. The first shackle comes free. She snatches her hand back at once, avoiding any chance of your touch.

You don't push. Instead, you ease back a little, lowering your gaze while still half-kneeling before her. You know she only has to glance down to see you. In this shift of height, you have become the one being scrutinized.

speaker: %u
content: I did go to the battlefield. I've seen war now, Jasmine.

speaker: %u
content: It kills. It destroys. It tramples everything that makes us human, enemy and ally alike. I threw myself into it to protect the people I love, and in just a few days, there was nothing left inside me but hate. Hating others and being hated back. Bleeding and making others bleed.

speaker: %u
content: Finding something I truly believe... it wasn't easy. I tried my best. But there were still sacrifices I couldn't stop. Mistakes I can't take back. Shadows I'll carry for the rest of my life. You were right. Once you've been through something like that, nothing ever goes back to how it was.

speaker: %u
content: But I don't want you trapped in the cruelest part of it.
You lift your head and meet her eyes.

speaker: %u
content: I'm not asking you to forgive me. I just want you to live. Whether it's the Mania or the war, there are treatments now that can ease your suffering, stop it from getting worse.

speaker: %u
content: If you can't stand the touch of anyone from DisCity, then I'll find your friends, people you actually trust. We can send you back to the farlands. There will be kind people there who'll look after you.

speaker: %u
content: I have no right to wish you happiness. But this city has already put you through so much pain. Don't let us cage you again. Don't go back to that cold lab. Don't...
[Flashback: Jasmine being carried away]

speaker: %u
content: ...Don't let the people you hate destroy you all over again. You fought so hard to survive that war. You shouldn't be heading toward an ending like that again.
Jasmine offers no response to any of your proposals. She only listens as you speak, and gradually, she stops recoiling. Her eyes rest on you, unguarded, without pretense.
She looks at you. Looks, and looks. And then, slowly, her hand rises, inching toward your cheek, and—

Her hand closes around your throat. You force down the shock, offering no sound, no struggle. Behind your back, your hand signals the surveillance camera to keep your people back. Stay calm, meet her eyes, don't let the conversation break, you keep telling yourself. You know, in this moment, you absolutely cannot look away.

A moment later, Jasmine smiles. She respects your courage, even if the rigid set of your muscles and the frantic pulse beneath her fingers tell her everything. She giggles, and at last her hand releases its brutal grip, softening into a gentle caress over the reddened skin of your throat.
After the long monologue you've carried alone, Jasmine finally speaks.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Heh... Why say all those things I can't understand? Chief... You're clearly just <color=#fb9259>afraid</color> of me.
Her fingers trail up, following the line of your jaw to your cheek, cool against your skin. They read every shift in your face, all while she wears a teasing smile.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Treatment? What's treatment? Strapping me down? Needles? Pills? Until I can't scream anymore, can't fight back? And if I'm too stupid to learn, just toss me back in the water to sleep and never let me wake?

speaker: Jasmine
content: Hehe, I know how it works. That's exactly what those white coats think. I can see it in their eyes. They're scared of me, sick of me. But they have to come see me anyway.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Heh... You Disians are all the same. Just like those soldiers who came at me with their blades... You're no different.

speaker: Jasmine
content: "Such a nuisance. She's an enemy. Why won't she just die already?"
She plays it up, her smile steeped in undisguised contempt and loathing.

speaker: %u
content: The war is over. This isn't a battlefield. There are no blades here meant to kill. I'm not your enemy. I want you to live.

speaker: Jasmine
content: You're not my enemy? How strange... You're certainly no family of mine!
She draws nearer, her hands mapping your face in fine, careful detail. Smiling, she reads your features the way one might hold up a head torn loose on the battlefield.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Not an enemy, not family... Then what are you to me? Why can't you just let me go?

speaker: %u
content: Your pain tears me apart too. I can't let go.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Don't talk like you know me!
She pushes you away with sudden force.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Where I came from, where I've walked, everything I've seen, heard, breathed in... how much could you possibly know? What right do you have to decide how I should live?
Then her expression shifts again. She leans in close to your ear and breathes, sly and teasing.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Or... why don't you grant my wish?
You know exactly what she means by "wish."
[One-Second Flashback: The Great Expo Closing Ceremony, where Jasmine, manic and blood-soaked, flanked by FAC in black]
And in turn, she reads your answer in the tight, strained silence.

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...You won't, will you? I knew it from the start. So why even bother?
She arches back, extending her limbs in a languid stretch.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Sigh... I'm sorry, Chief. Truth is, I do understand. You've always belonged to their side. Looking at me hurts you. Getting close to me scares you.

speaker: Jasmine
content: If I weren't so awful, picking up Sibilla's tricks, using my pain to make you feel sorry for me, to make you care, you'd never have to waste so much of yourself on me.

speaker: Jasmine
content: It's only because you're so kind that you can't bear to see me like this. Sigh... Let yourself off the hook. Let me go too. You don't have to force yourself to love me.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Your love is too big, Chief. You love too many things. You can't let go of me, but you can't let go of my enemies either... So just take it all back.

speaker: Jasmine
content: I don't need that kind of love.
She tries again to push you off, but this time, it doesn't work.
You catch Jasmine's thin hand, holding it fast, refusing to let go. Her expression flickers from surprise, then disgust, then fury. She struggles, but still you do not release her.
You know you are doing something foolish.

speaker: Doctor
content: Whether this is out of kindness, duty, guilt, or some other need to help her... don't set your hopes too high, Chief.

speaker: Doctor
content: There are wounds in this world that can't be healed. Some lives won't let you in. Jasmine's past is too heavy; taking her on will be far harder than you imagine. To prevent more serious consequences from unfolding, I will always advise you to cut your losses while you still can.

speaker: Doctor
content: Otherwise, sooner or later, you will regret this.
His face is grave as he speaks. You realize he isn't talking only about Jasmine anymore. To a doctor's eye, you, too, are slipping into the role of a patient.
Still, your mind is made up. You keep your grip firm around Jasmine's hand.

speaker: %u
content: ...I know you think it's worthless. Hate me if you want, but I won't let you go.

speaker: %u
content: You owe me a few things too.

options: Remember the promise we made before the "celebration"?

content: [Flashback] Lap Pillow CG

speaker: Jasmine
content: Take me to the celebration, and I'll come back to you after it's over. Just as promised.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Once the closing ceremony ends... I'll follow you anywhere.
[Back to Interrogation Room]

speaker: %u
content: Thanks to MBCC, you made it to the celebration. The closing ceremony's over. Time to keep your word now.

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...You sly thing... sneaky fox... How dare you...

speaker: Jasmine
content: That was all a lie! Fraser's people taught me to do that! They told me you could get me to the closing ceremony, said you were a soft-hearted fool. That's the only reason I picked you, got close to you, played sweet for you... None of that counts! I was lying!
She shoves you, hits you, her nails carving bloody lines across your skin. But you cling on, refusing to let go.

speaker: %u
content: If a promise can be kept, it was never a lie. I believe you meant every word, Jasmine.

speaker: %u
content: Last time, the war got in the way. You said the most beautiful promises are always the easiest to break in wartime. But the war's over now. Your blades are under control. There's no better time than now, Jasmine.

speaker: %u
content: One at a time. I remember all of them.

speaker: Jasmine
content: You...

speaker: %u
content: You said in DisCity, the only meat you ever ate was sandworms, and they tasted awful. You wanted to try the amazing food I mentioned.
She stiffens. But you keep going, your eyes locked on hers, each word deliberate and steady.

speaker: %u
content: ...You said if DisCity had celebrations or fireworks, you'd like to see them too.

speaker: %u
content: And rain, snow... summer, autumn, winter. If there were more good people around me, you'd like to meet them too. You wanted to make more friends.

speaker: %u
content: I remember every single thing you said. Your future doesn't belong in a cage, Jasmine. Promises have to be kept; that's where you're meant to go. See it all first, then I'll set you free.

speaker: %u
content: ...I want you to be truly free. I'll do whatever it takes.
She looks at you, her lips parting slightly. Words rise and fall away. There are several times she almost speaks, only to press her mouth shut again. After a long moment, she slowly lowers her gaze.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Why do you remember all that...? It was all foolishness, lies... things that can never come true...

speaker: Jasmine
content: You should've just forgotten...

options: ...I won't forget. Because you haven't either.

content: Her long hair falls forward, veiling her face from view. But slowly, the rigid tension in Jasmine's spine eases, and her body, as if in a daze, leans just slightly toward you.

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...I know. I know you mean well, Chief. Thank you...

speaker: Jasmine
content: I don't believe that my hometown is gone anymore. Even after the movie ends, Goldionville must still be around. Someday, I will go back to find it.
She looks up, her eyes holding a genuine warmth you haven't seen in so long.

speaker: Jasmine
content: I'll do as you say. I'll stay by your side. Just like we promised.

speaker: %u
content: ...Jasmine...
The weight pressing on your heart lightens, and without thinking, you reach for her hand.
—Only to find she has already taken yours. Her touch is startlingly cold.

speaker: Jasmine
content: But before that... I have one more wish.

The dancer rises, her waist bending like a reed as she takes your hand and sweetly reels you in. Her eyes have turned, now slick with cunning, and her voice climbs tenderly around you, drawing you into her hold.

speaker: Jasmine
content: There are some people I'd love to meet. The ones who visit my dreams, over and over... <color=#fb9259>The Shattered Blade</color>. That's their name, right?

speaker: Jasmine
content: I know they're friends of yours. And I know you can find them. Won't you take me to see them, Chief?
Every muscle in your body locks tight.
[Flashback]

speaker: Nightingale
content: General Augustus departed WhiteSands with the main Shattered Blade force in mid-September. Their return date remains uncertain. Nirvana Port is currently under the supervision of that adjutant with the iron mask. The good news is, he didn't turn down your request.

speaker: Nightingale
content: The Shattered Blade has shared their latest Rancor suppression technology with MBCC. That's exactly how we were able to safely separate Jasmine from her dangerous blades. It's been highly effective in controlling the Mania exposure she's experiencing.

speaker: Nightingale
content: It's rather surprising, honestly... That was their core proprietary technology. They turned down the Ring Research Institute more than once. Yet now they've agreed to share it with us... Chief, how did you manage to convince them?
[Interrogation Room]
Jasmine leans against your shoulder, her hand trailing downward to rest lightly over your heart. She narrows her eyes.

speaker: Jasmine
content: I know what worries you. I promise I won't hurt them. They're your friends, after all. And you're such a good person, Chief... Your friends must be wonderful too.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Didn't you say you wanted me to step out into the world? Meet more good people? Let them be the ones, then.
Beat by beat, she listens to your heartbeat with narrowed eyes, a familiar smile slowly creeping across her lips.
(Flashback)

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: That Outland woman... I remember her. The Great Expo, the closing ceremony. Augustus infiltrated the FAC command convoy, and not even their on-site security caught on. But that Outlander did, precisely.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: Hell of a fixation. No chance in hell of winning, but she just kept coming, like a rabid dog that won't let go. Even had the nerve to turn our own blades on us... Heh. Suits Rancor perfectly, I'll give her that. Corrupted to this point, she'd be better off not waking up at all. Pitiful.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: So go on, then. Try and fix her, Chief. Fix her. Keep her on a short leash. And don't let her try anything that stupid again.
[Interrogation Room]

speaker: Jasmine
content: Take me to them, please? Jasmine will be so good. I won't do a single bad thing. I trust them, just like I trust you.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Chief... I have only this one wish. Please, I'm begging you.
She blinks, doe-eyed and innocent, her smile honeyed as melting frosting, overflowing with dependence and trust in you. It is a smile you know intimately.

The eve of the Great Expo—that was when she last smiled at you like this. Even steeped in hatred and pain, she can still put on this smile. Discordant, untimely, it remains carved upon her face like an indelible epitaph.
You know she is lying to you again.
But these broken hands, once released, will fall straight into nothingness. You can only grip them tighter.

speaker: %u
content: The Shattered Blade is out on a mission. I can't reach them right now. Once they return, I'll take you to meet them.

speaker: %u
content: Until then, you'll accept treatment. You'll stay with me and keep our promise. Okay?

speaker: Jasmine
content: Really?! Chief, you're the absolute best! It's a promise now. You can't take it back!
You have put on a false mask of your own.

speaker: %u
content: We'll both keep our word.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Thank you... thank you, Chief...
She nestles her head lightly against your chest, a happy, satisfied smile gracing her face as she takes in the heavy beat of your heart.
(Flashback)

speaker: Doctor
content: Jasmine's past is too heavy; taking her on will be far harder than you imagine... Sooner or later, you will regret this.
[Black Screen]
You're doing something foolish, that much is certain. But... you just can't let go.
After the promise was made, the suffocating tension dissolved completely. Jasmine has clung to you at almost every waking moment since. It's been a gentle, peaceful stretch of time, much like now.
[Bureau]

A captivating scent fills your office. There on the coffee table, in a shallow dish, sits a freshly made meal. The beef is braised to a melting tenderness, its rich sauce catching the light with a tantalizing sheen.
Jasmine is helpless against the temptation. Without a glance at the cutlery nearby, she reaches out and carefully plucks a piece, holding it up to her mouth.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Ahm—mm...! Hot, hot, hot!

She springs to her feet from the heat, both hands waving wildly to fan her mouth. She refuses to spit the meat out, so she just blows out quick, desperate breaths instead. They say a cat's tongue can't handle anything hot, and Jasmine appears to be no different.

options: Why not let it cool down a bit first?

speaker: Jasmine
content: But then it won't taste the same. I've never had anything this good out there, you know. Whatever I caught myself was always raw, and whatever the desert bandits gave me was always cold. Hot like this... that's where the real flavor is.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Oh, won't you have a bite too, Chief? Here, I'll cool it off for you. Give it a try!
Using both knife and fork, she stabs a piece and bounds over to you. She blows on it carefully, several gentle puffs to cool it, then presents it to your lips with a beaming smile.

This is what your days have become. She's like a changed person, sweet-natured and eager to please. Even when her actions are plainly meant to curry favor, that innocent smile makes them disarming, utterly irresistible.

More astonishing still is that even beyond your sight, she's shed the violence of her past, no longer so quick to react. She's even begun to willingly reach out to people besides you—Disians, of all people.
[Scene Change] Flashback Filter

speaker: Wynn
content: Chief, Chief! You have to hear this! I was delivering files around the departments today, and Jasmine followed me the whole time! Looking around, peeking at everything, it was the cutest thing. She's exactly like my cat. She even rubbed her cheek against my hand! Like this little nuzzle for attention!

speaker: Wynn
content: Oh, I've totally figured out what snacks she loves by now. Next time I'm bringing a whole bag! Hm... where should I take her wandering next?
[Scene Change] Flashback Filter

speaker: Eugene
content: The day before yesterday, she slipped into the crawlspace above the garage maintenance room. How on earth did a fully grown woman climb that high and fold herself into a space that tight?

speaker: Eugene
content: And the creepier part is... she stayed up there the whole day, dead silent. No one had any idea. Then, some guy on night shift happened to glance up, and two glowing eyes blinked right back at him. Now the Bureau's got another ghost story...
[Scene Change] Flashback Filter

speaker: Nurse
content: Look, I know she's doing a lot better now... but she can't just go tearing off wherever she feels like it! Those regular checkups still need to happen! She's way too fast. I can't even catch her! Chief, can you please do something...
[Scene Change] Flashback Filter

speaker: Doctor
content: Hmm... Her aggressive tendencies have vanished entirely. She's more willing to communicate, shows better self-regulation... I have to admit, this far exceeds anything I expected. It's genuinely striking. As a case study, I'd love to dig deeper...

speaker: Doctor
content: ...Chief. You didn't do something, did you? Have your shackles evolved further? Why not accompany her back to Banyan sometime? We'd be happy to provide a full examination, on the house...
[Door Opens] Back to Present

It's a good thing. You've always wished she could feel the kindness of more people, could open her eyes and truly see those around her once again. And Jasmine, as though she understood your unspoken hopes, has done exactly that.

One by one, the "promises" are being kept. Even when your work piles up and keeps you, even when your thoughts are elsewhere weaving other plans, she never urges you, never stirs up a fuss. She simply stays at your side with a smile, gazing at you.
Still, that taut string hidden deep in your heart refuses to loosen.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, here's the report from the Outland Affairs Bureau. There's been an update on those desert bandits you asked us to track.

You page through the file. Jasmine had passed through the hands of several bandit crews back then. All of them had been questioned, and all of them had come clean about how they stumbled on her, tricked her, used her as a weapon against sand beasts and competing gangs. Now and then, they'd feed her a few DisCity sheriffs to toy with, as a prize.

But the promises were never real. DisCity was never the destination. And no one could speak to her past: where she had come from, whether she still had family, what had hollowed her out into this. The bandits had never bothered to learn.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...That's all there is?

speaker: Nightingale
content: I'm afraid so. The Ash Campaign hit the bandit groups hard as well. Those who had direct contact with Jasmine back then are nearly impossible to find now.

speaker: Nightingale
content: And in any case, the bandits only valued her combat strength. To them, she was just a mentally unstable refugee from the Outlands, someone easy to string along... They never cared what she'd gone through, so they can't offer any useful information. As for the rest...
She pauses, following your gaze toward the corner.

In the corner of the office, Jasmine is perched silently on the coffee table. She watches the two of you, perfectly still except for her hand, which inches the glass before her ever closer to the edge, a fraction at a time. By now, it teeters at the table's rim, a sliver of it already suspended over nothing.
The instant she catches your gaze, her hand retreats. She looks up at you with big, dewy eyes, the very picture of blamelessness.

speaker: Nightingale
content: ...Chief, Jasmine really has come a long way. Perhaps you can let yourself ease up a little. You don't have to carry so much tension.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Just leave the files here. I'll go through them more carefully in a bit. If any new leads surface, I'll need you to follow up on them again.
Nightingale sighs. In the end, she says nothing more, only setting the files down on your desk in silence.
The moment she exits the room, Jasmine springs to your side.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Hehe, desert bandits are so dull... Didn't the adjutant lady bring anything else?
You know exactly what she wants to hear.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The report says the Shattered Blade's mission is still ongoing. You know how it is out there, Apostles crawling everywhere, disasters at every turn. These things take time.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: We'll wait together. If you're getting bored, how about you tell me some stories? About the world out there?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Where you've been, who you've crossed paths with, how long you spent in each place, anything strange or wonderful that happened... Whatever you can recall, I want to hear all of it.
Jasmine studies you for a long moment, and an impish smile spreads across her lips.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Mm... I don't really remember. Nothing worth talking about anyway. Oh! I hear Wynn out there! Gonna go play with her!

speaker: Jasmine
content: You're busy anyway. I'll do what you want and go meet more of my "friends."

She leans back, rolls away from your grasp, and bolts out the door quick as a fox. Moments later, peals of happy laughter echo from outside. It's Wynn and some other staff members, their voices warm with affection. Everyone adores Jasmine, cares for her, believes in her, overjoyed by her "recovery."
—Only you know the truth.
[Switch Scene]
Each night, you let Jasmine have the bed while you lie on the sofa nearby. In the deep hours of the night, her painful moans reach you again.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Nn... nngh... Stay away... no!
You turn to her at once and take her hand in yours.

options: Jasmine! Wake up! I'm right here!

content: Her eyes snap open, and she shoots upright in the dark. Her pupils, wide and shaking, are fixed on some nightmare beyond your sight. Sweat-soaked but deathly chill, she pants, and those rapid, broken breaths cut through the dead quiet, squeezing your heart tight.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Jasmine, it's just me. You had another nightmare. Are you okay? Should I call the doctor?

You lift a hand to wipe away her sweat, only to startle her. Jasmine jerks away, scrambling back against the wall, hands fumbling frantically in the corner. You know all too well what she's reaching for. Those savage blades.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Your blades aren't here. This isn't the battlefield. You don't need weapons here.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The nightmare's over, Jasmine.
She gazes at you for a long while. When you finally lower your hand, still poised awkwardly in mid-reach, she softens just slightly, returning to the present. A dry chuckle escapes her.

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...I'm fine, Chief. It wasn't a nightmare... It was a sweet dream...

speaker: Jasmine
content: I dreamed I was back at the celebration. I was dancing, seeing everyone I wanted to see. All of them...
[Flashback: Small CG - Burning Village]

speaker: Jasmine
content: Heh... such a sweet dream... You shouldn't have woken me. That's where I'm supposed to be...
She curls into herself, arms wrapped tight around her body, her laughter dwindling into near silence.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Jasmine, that's...

speaker: Jasmine
content: Go back to sleep, Chief. I'll sleep too... The celebration's still waiting for me... in my dreams...

She bundles the bedding and climbs off the bed, steering clear of you. She weaves drowsily around the tables and chairs that belong to Disians, drifting like a sleepwalker, until she sinks into a cold corner of the room. The blanket goes over her head. She shrinks into a tiny, shadowed knot.
You can only watch.
You cannot bear to leave, but you cannot move closer. This is the fractured reality that tears between you. In waking life, the chasm filled with pain is impassable. But at least in dreams, it isn't.

Now you can join her in those nightmares. They are so vivid now. The moment your eyes close, you are back on that battlefield you fought so hard to forget. The vast spiral, the blood spilled, the hatred swallowed. Yours and not yours alike, they coil around you, grinding everything to dust beneath your feet.
So you try to abandon sleep. It brings its own rewards: by day, you can focus your mind on tracing Jasmine's past. By night, you can keep watch and pull her back from the nightmares in time.

Time is slipping away. You must find answers. You must carve out a path for her before a darker ending arrives. You have to go deeper into her past, sifting through shattered, chaotic memories for any fragment of possibility.
After countless dead ends, you finally find a crack.
—It's a call coming in from Nirvana Port.
[Switch Scene]

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: We finished analyzing that pair of Rancor blades you sent over. They've been reforged, with heavy damage across both, but the material composition, manufacturing batch, and Mania signature all left traces. Enough to make a match.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: They belonged to the last batch of Rancors, manufactured N.F. 92. Issued in stages to six battalions. Three of those were later deployed to different overseas bases. All three went silent starting N.F. 102.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: Cross-reference with that woman's age, and it lines up with the RNH Battalion. They fought through the one-year war after BR-003, from N.F. 106 to 107.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: Without central command from DisCity, the RNH wandered. Scavenged their own supplies, fought their own battles. They covered too much ground and passed through countless settlements. Hard to pin down an exact location.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: Report's in your hands now. If you want to help her find her roots, go do it yourself.
The report is thorough. It sets out a clear perimeter within the blighted wasteland and pinpoints several sites of interest. This could be enough to lead you to Jasmine's homeland.
You should thank him, but your instinct pulls another question from your lips.

options: ...Is the RNH Battalion still with the Shattered Blade?

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: No. Their gear was already obsolete the year they deployed. And during their time fighting alone out there, losses were catastrophic. By the time Augustus pulled them back, there wasn't much left to salvage. The battalion was disbanded and merged shortly after.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I meant the soldiers under its command. The ones who survived. Any of them still out there? Where are they now?

options: I want to talk to them.

content: The line goes stiff with silence. When Iron Mask finally speaks again, his voice has dropped, low and grim.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: The support you asked for, we already gave it. Whether we should have or not, the Shattered Blade delivered. What's left... you can't reckon with, and you can't collect. This stops now.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: If you still want to do something for that Outland woman, sort it out inside your own Bureau.
You try to keep him on the line, but a commotion of some sort has broken out on his side.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: ...Go back. This doesn't involve you.
Those words are not meant for you. You can tell Iron Mask has stepped back from the microphone. Beyond him, another voice reaches you, distant and unclear.
Someone else is there, imploring Iron Mask about something, and they refuse to be dismissed.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: Ten minutes. And this stays sealed between the two of you only. Clear?

A few more muffled words come through. Then you hear the receiver being set down, two sets of heavy footfalls crossing, one retreating and the other approaching. Someone else reaches the communicator and lifts the receiver.
A stranger's voice greets you, gravelly and strained.

Chief of the Minos Bureau of Crisis Control. My name is Arkin, Logistics Task Force, Shattered Blade. Before we came back to Nirvana Port, I was with the RNH Battalion, one of the old DisCorps overseas units.

speaker: Arkin
content: I'm grateful you'd even ask about my old unit. Whatever you need to know about the RNH Battalion... if I remember it, it's yours.

options: ...Walk me through every combat operation RNH ever carried out.

content: After a long, deep breath, Arkin answers your question.

N.F. 106, the year of the Great Expo. Under the cover of "peace," a small faction of Outlanders colluded with the Underground and detonated BR-003. From that flashpoint, a new city-state war ignited, and the news tore across thousands of miles to reach the RNH Battalion.

It wasn't because DisCity's communications were working. They'd been severed from the homeland for years. But that didn't slow the war's spread.
Almost the same time the conflict erupted, the RNH camp came under assault. Unlike the abandoned soldiers of DisCity, the Outlands had been preparing for total war from the start. The pretext they broadcast for mobilization was that "DisCity deliberately triggered BR-003, unleashing disasters and seeking to wield Mania to once again dominate and exploit the farlands."

The ranks of the RNH Battalion were filled with the young, men and women in their twenties and thirties. A great many had endured the BR-001 disaster in N.F. 89. After joining the military, they only understood more clearly the true cost it had demanded. They knew DisCity could not survive a Black Ring. The lie filled them with fury. "DisCity could never detonate a Black Ring. We're the ones who bore its real cost. You twist the truth. You're the criminals here!" "What's become of the city... the Black Ring, the Mania... what the hell have you bastards done?! Where's my mom? How's everyone...? I want to go home. I want to go home..." "...How DARE you?! Outland filth. You will PAY for this!!"

Stoked by hatred, the war sank swiftly into a blood-soaked stalemate.
Every settlement in view was manufacturing guns and bullets. The enemy hid war criminals inside civilian hospitals, sent the elderly, the frail women and children out to the roadsides swathed in bandages, pleading for rescue. When DisCity soldiers approached, the bombs sewn into their cloaks would ignite without warning. That was how Arkin lost his leg, the same death trap that took his comrades.

This stray remnant force refused to surrender. If DisCity ever mounted a counteroffensive, their position would also serve as a critical passage. They believed their homeland's main force might still come. The RNH Battalion resisted with their Rancors, sustaining themselves on the spoils of battle, down to the very last soldier.
...Until every threat in the region was at last annihilated.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...So you're telling me everything RNH swept through were military targets? Hidden in villages, in towns?

speaker: Arkin
content: I'm certain of it.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And the civilians? All of them are enemy combatants in disguise, waiting to strike?

speaker: Arkin
content: Everyone in RNH died that way. Every last one except me.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...But you said RNH was short-handed, cut off from command. What intel were you operating on? How did you make those calls? And what if you got it wrong?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Did you expect the Rancors in your hands to tell you who to kill and who to spare?
Bang!

A metal fist slams hard against a desk on the other end of the line, cutting the conversation short for a moment. Mentioning the past has easily reignited his long-buried hatred. You can feel the fury rolling off him through his breath alone.
When Arkin speaks again, he has barely wrestled his emotions back under control. His voice has grown even rougher.

speaker: Arkin
content: ...We've seen too many cunning, vicious Outlanders. Their "clever little tricks" got far too many of our people killed. That woman may act tame around you...

speaker: Arkin
content: But she's holding a Rancor weapon in her hands, blades she took off our fallen comrades... She even set her sights on General Augustus. That... I can't let that stand.

speaker: Arkin
content: You earned our trust and respect in the Ash Campaign, Chief. From the General to the adjutant, the Shattered Blade considers you one of us.

speaker: Arkin
content: ...I'd hate to see all that thrown away over some Outland Sinner with a questionable background.
There is no pretense in his words. They carry a warning, but even more than that, a plea. This veteran is earnestly begging you not to cross that line, not to side with the "enemy."
...<color=#fb9259>Enemy</color>. That word again. Like the unrelenting nightmares of recent nights, it sends a fresh spasm twisting through your stomach. You hold it down.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...I reached you precisely because I want to settle her "questionable background."

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: She's lost her memory. Mania destroyed her mind completely. I had to use EDGE's technology just to reach her subconscious. And there, I found some clues. Strange ones. They might connect to her past. I need to know if any of it means something to you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Deep in her subconscious, I saw a village on fire. A celebration that never ends. And a song, from the Outlands.
[CG: Burning Village, Screen Dims]
Let flame ignite the candles bright, not scorch the seedlings in the light.
Let arrows fly to strike the mark, not pierce a grandmother's tender heart.
Let parades roll through fields so wide, yet never steal dreams from inside. Let fireworks gleam in skies above, but never burn the homes of love.
O traveler, when you join a celebration in a foreign land... leave blades of slaughter behind.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You've been there. How much do you remember? What happened at <color=#fb9259>that woman's</color> village? At that celebration?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Was it the same as what you told me? Just another filthy military outpost, fake civilians, a staged celebration, all of it a trap meant to kill you?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Answer me.

speaker: Arkin
content: Urgh... bleurgh!!

The only reply is a fit of harsh, convulsive vomiting. The handset on the other end tumbles to the floor as the man goes down. The retching drags on for a long while, tangled with weeping, until someone hauls him off. When the receiver is picked up again, it's Iron Mask who speaks.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: He was there. He knows what he did. Bring him back. If he has a shred of conscience left, he'll face me and answer for it!

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: Ten minutes are up, Chief. That was the last exception I'll make for you. This ends here. Goodbye.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You know he's guilty! Are you shielding him from me? Or are you no different from that guy yourself?

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: My duty is to keep the Shattered Blade in line. Not to play the saint for you.
[Transition, visual effect, sound effects: crushing sound, sharp static]

A sharp burst of static cuts your question short. The receiver has been crushed. Through the crackling noise, you can barely make out Iron Mask's breathing. It's tight, strained, muffled behind the metal slits of his mask.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: ...The General left DisCity in N.F. 103. While those fools triggered the Black Ring and dragged everyone into war, she was still out there, crossing the lands, weathering the Mania storms, searching for the soldiers they abandoned.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: Even merchants know when to steer clear of danger. Augustus never took a detour in her life. From Eastia to the farlands, she'd go dark for weeks, for months. And you're asking if she knew about that ugly war? Hah.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: If she'd been there, it wouldn't have ended like this. The Black Ring would never have erupted. The year-long war would've been finished in a single day. Those shameless Outlanders wouldn't have dared lift a finger in the first place. Don't you think so?!
Rage, loathing, disdain, and another deep feeling beyond any outsider's reach. Together, they catch fire inside this soldier, rigid and unyielding as forged steel.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: Listen, Chief of Minos. I don't fulfill your requests to earn your goodwill. Not out of guilt toward anyone. Not to shield anyone either.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: We at the DisCorps claimed our seats in hell a long time ago. Your judgment means nothing to us. I help you only because the General saw something in you, nothing more.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: You want to study Rancors? Play your little hero game inside your own Bureau? Do as you like. I can work with that.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: But leave Augustus out of it. And stay out of her way.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: Whether it's the DisCorps or that Outland woman, the moment they took up a Rancor, they became something different from you. You still have the sense to keep your distance from war. You'll never understand what those weapons really mean.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: If you insist on interfering, on fighting for that Outlander's justice... then by all means. Bring her to <color=#fb9259>Nirvana Port</color>. Make it soon. I'll be here.
He lets out a cold laugh.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: I'm curious to see... how you'll handle the consequences when that day comes.
The dead silence freezes time itself. It drags on, and on, until you grow weary of this standoff. You no longer know what meaning there could be in repeating this same confrontation.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Jasmine isn't a "Rancor." She doesn't belong on a battlefield. She's nothing like you people.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm returning her blades to the Shattered Blade. They'll be delivered immediately. Take them and go. As far from here as you can get.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And don't ever come near her again.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: A sound decision. I'll be waiting for your update.
[Scene Change: Chief's Room, Late Night]
That night, ${PlayerName} comes back very late.
Finding Jasmine already lying down and deep in sleep, he returns to the "sofa" beside her, his glowing tablet in hand, and taps away at it long into the quiet.
female_content: Finding Jasmine already lying down and deep in sleep, she returns to the "sofa" beside her, her glowing tablet in hand, and taps away at it long into the quiet.

content: When the sounds from across the room at last stop and the glow goes out, Jasmine, in the darkness, opens her eyes.

${PlayerName} has fallen asleep, head drooping. She rises, steps on tiptoe across the cold tiles, and creeps noiselessly to his side. Imitating the way ${PlayerName} always does it, she taps at the machine still resting in his hands.
female_content: ${PlayerName} has fallen asleep, head drooping. She rises, steps on tiptoe across the cold tiles, and creeps noiselessly to her side. Imitating the way ${PlayerName} always does it, she taps at the machine still resting in her hands.

content: The screen lights up again. She sees several little squares: some photographs, some strange drawings. She peers closer—
She can't make sense of it. It's a jumbled mess to her.

She is about to keep browsing when a soft noise stops her cold. She jolts and skips back a step. ${PlayerName} stirs faintly, brows knitting together, and a few indistinct words fall from those lips. But in the end, the Chief stays asleep.
How rare. All this time, he's never once taken his eyes off Jasmine. Has so many sleepless days finally caught up with him? Is he dreaming right now?
female_content: How rare. All this time, she's never once taken her eyes off Jasmine. Has so many sleepless days finally caught up with her? Is she dreaming right now?

content: That only makes it better. Jasmine slips close again—

speaker: Jasmine
content: What's troubling you, Chief?

speaker: Jasmine
content: If you can't sleep, I'll stay right here with you.

Another few indistinct murmurs escape ${PlayerName}. Jasmine presses closer still, ghosting her fingertips along the cheek and earlobe. She let her words drift into the Chief's ear like a breath, threading them into those dreams, coaxing answers out:

speaker: Jasmine
content: You were gone alone for so long today... Did the Shattered Blade come back?

speaker: Jasmine
content: Is my wish going to come true soon?

${PlayerName}'s eyes snap open with a violent start. A hand pushes Jasmine away, palm blazing, glowing with the threat of something ominous about to break loose. Jasmine feels a spike of primal fear, her body poised to bolt.

But just before the force can fully unleash, his eyes focus, and he sees her. The moment he registers it's Jasmine, his expression shifts into something even more terrified than before. He wrenches his hand back as if electrocuted, scrambling backward to put space between them. His voice emerges ragged and shaking.
female_content: But just before the force can fully unleash, her eyes focus, and she sees her. The moment she registers it's Jasmine, her expression shifts into something even more terrified than before. She wrenches her hand back as if electrocuted, scrambling backward to put space between them. Her voice emerges ragged and shaking.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Sorry, Jasmine... I was dreaming. I didn't realize it was you...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Sorry... that was my fault. I'm sorry...

${PlayerName} tries to stand but collapses back onto the sofa, his hand coming up to cover his face. His breathing is harsh and unsteady. The terminal hits the floor and glows to life again. By its light, Jasmine sees it now: his lips are frighteningly pale, cold sweat soaking his brow, the frantic hammer of his heart almost audible.
female_content: ${PlayerName} tries to stand but collapses back onto the sofa, her hand coming up to cover her face. Her breathing is harsh and unsteady. The terminal hits the floor and glows to life again. By its light, Jasmine sees it now: her lips are frighteningly pale, cold sweat soaking her brow, the frantic hammer of her heart almost audible.

content: He's lost weight. Jasmine's never seen him like this, with his eyes hollowed out and bloodshot. How many nights has it been since he last slept well? After every smile he gave her, every gentle moment... was his face always like this beneath it all?
female_content: She's lost weight. Jasmine's never seen her like this, with her eyes hollowed out and bloodshot. How many nights has it been since she last slept well? After every smile she gave her, every gentle moment... was her face always like this beneath it all?

content: Jasmine knows what hatred feels like. She remembers love and longs for it. But this expression is something she's never witnessed before. She freezes in place. A long silence passes before her body stirs. Without realizing it, she steps forward and slowly, gently wraps her arms around the person before her.
${PlayerName}'s body tenses for a moment.

speaker: Jasmine
content: It's okay, it's okay... You still have Jasmine. I'm here with you...
She strokes the Chief's back in slow, gentle beats, easing the chaotic heaving of that chest little by little.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Tomorrow... I think it's supposed to be sunny...

speaker: Jasmine
content: We could go outside. Maybe... you could come with me, Chief?

speaker: Jasmine
content: I've explored every corner of the Bureau already, but I don't know what's fun out there yet. Maybe... you could pick a few places?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...What do you want to do, Jasmine?

speaker: Jasmine
content: I'm not clever enough to think of anything. You tell me, Chief.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Spring is almost here. The sunlight will be beautiful. By then... there might be performances in the city. All kinds of them...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: There'll be music, lights, good food, and shows... People from everywhere, dressed up in pretty clothes, singing and dancing together. Like a celebration.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Hehe. Wynn told you about that, didn't she? It all sounds lovely. I'd love every bit of it. And since it's what you want, how about we go see them all?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Of course. I just want you to be happy.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: As long as you can be happy...
The smile slips from Jasmine's face. She gazes at you for a long while before her voice finally comes.

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...Why are you crying, Chief?
Are you crying?

No. It's just the remnants of that nightmare. Iron and blood. Fire and ash. Blistering heat and the stink of rot. You hear the roars and the wails. Sacrifice and hatred churning together, stirred up again and again with vicious intent, bleeding outward until they solidify into a vast, oppressive spiral.

That's nothing but a dream, the aftermath of your brief time at war and the suffering others described. But your soul, the ones and the things you truly hold dear, none of them were ever swallowed by that war.
You are lucky. You took everything back just in time, so you still had the chance to escape the battlefield. To run far, far from it all.
But what about them?

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: Whether it's the DisCorps or that Outland woman, the moment they took up a Rancor, they became something different from you. You still have the sense to keep your distance from war. You'll never understand what those weapons really mean.

He was right. You don't know how to do right by Jasmine, don't know what you can get back for her, don't know how to bring her away from all this. Your face is dry, your eyes dry. You haven't cried. It's not your turn yet.
But Jasmine reaches up anyway and brushes her fingers across your cheek. For the first time, those luminous, fawn-like eyes of hers cloud over with a haze you cannot quite see through.

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...You shouldn't cry for me. The times I lashed out, the nightmares, all the lying, running off, picking fights... I did all those terrible things, but none of that was ever your fault. I don't hate you. I never did.

speaker: Jasmine
content: I know you're such a good person. You're the kindest. If anyone should be sorry, it's me...

speaker: Jasmine
content: I'm sorry, Chief. I lied to you, I used you, I never listened. I took your kindness and threw it back at you. And I made you so, so sad.

speaker: Jasmine
content: But... I really do like you. I always have. Your love isn't something worthless. It's the best thing anyone's ever given me.

speaker: Jasmine
content: I don't know what happiness really is. But if you see it as so precious, then I want you to have every last bit of it. So please, don't cry. Smile for me, okay?

speaker: Jasmine
content: I love seeing people smile the most...
You force out a smile and draw her in your arms, burying the look that follows.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Promise me one thing, Jasmine. Whatever you choose to do, wherever you go, whatever happens, let me stay beside you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I won't get in your way... I have no right to ask you to let go. And I can't pretend I can ever make up for everything you've lost.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But if there's something, out beyond your celebration, here in the waking world... if there's anything still worth holding onto, even a little... tell me.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Even if it's just the faintest hope, as long as you're willing... I want you to be happy.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Sleep now, Chief... Tonight, I will watch over you. Sleep. Have a sweet dream...
As you feel the rhythm of her breath and the beat of her heart, exhaustion and drowsiness, held at bay for so long, finally wash over you like a tide.
You fall into another dream.

In the dream, the bloodstained blades are sent out of the Bureau on schedule. You watch as they're locked into a suppressant casing and placed inside an armored transport. Past the port checkpoint, through the sandstorm, they'll finally return to the place they were always meant to be.
And Jasmine accepts it calmly. She lets go of the inseparable blades just like that, shedding nine years of fixation. She doesn't even bother to look again.
She stays beside you. She tells you not to worry. She's right there when you fall asleep, just like tonight.
...Tonight, she watches you as you drift deep into sleep. She sees your brow smooth out at last and thinks to herself—maybe, just maybe, you're finally having a good dream.
Jasmine reaches toward you, but pulls her hand back before it can land.

speaker: Jasmine
content: It's enough if you are happy... Your love is precious.

speaker: Jasmine
content: From now on... save more of it for yourself...

speaker: Jasmine
content: I'm sorry...

Three days after the Rancor blades were sent away from the MBCC,
Sinner Jasmine fled the Bureau. Her absence went undetected for two whole hours. Not a single alarm was raised.

Passwords, monitoring gaps, security zones, corridor schedules, patrol movements, even the psychological vulnerabilities of every staff member she interacted with... This "pitiful patient," supposedly "mentally broken" and "cognitively degraded," had quietly mastered it all, then leveraged every piece of it with surgical cunning.

Her final choice was the medical waste collection vehicle. She hid herself within its contamination isolation chamber and escaped. The timing was immaculate.

She had stockpiled her own prescribed sedatives, dissolved them into your tea, and left while you slept soundly. She knew precisely when you would finally let your guard down.
The entire Bureau was thrown into shock.

speaker: Wynn
content: So... all that time Jasmine spent following me around... it was just to get out? Is she going after the Shattered Blade by herself? What's going to happen to her?

speaker: Eugene
content: Hold on. No matter how well she plays it, her Mania sensitivity readings are off the charts. The second she steps into WhiteSands, the Ash Apostles' fields will scramble her sense of direction completely. She won't be able to find her way. She knows that. She knows she can't reach the Shattered Blade alone.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...She knows. She's known all along.
So she planned it all from the start...

Your knuckles whiten, cold sweat sliding down your skin as your gaze stays locked on the external comms. One channel has been silent. Too silent, for too long. Nightingale reads the implication before anyone else does.

speaker: Nightingale
content: ...The transport carrying those Rancor blades was headed for Nirvana Port.

speaker: Nightingale
content: It underwent final inspections at the port last night before departure. They flagged a medium-risk anomaly, which held it up for three hours. Did she slip in during that window? Or did she... cause that delay herself...

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief!
[Scene Change]
She crawls out of the upturned transport and staggers blindly into the WhiteSands. The wind flays her skin; the Apostles' thunderous roars scramble her mind, turning every direction into nothing.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Here in the waking world... if there's anything still worth holding onto, even a little... tell me.
There is... there is. Everything you gave me. Thank you for being so kind to me. For giving me so much.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Whatever you choose to do, wherever you go, whatever happens, let me stay beside you.
I'm sorry. I never learned how to hold onto anything good. I hope... it won't hurt too much.
The celebration isn't over. I have to go back. I have to...

She's close now. So close. The Rancor, clutched tight for nine long years, finds its way back into her hands. It feels its companions somewhere near. The blades will show the way, leading the wandering dancer across seas of spilled blood, through the long years, back to the stage she never truly left.
This time, she will not dance alone. She can feel it—
Up ahead, <color=#fb9259>familiar faces</color> from that year already stand waiting on the stage, ready to join her and complete the celebration that never ended.

At Nirvana Port, the watch has changed shifts. Arkin stands guard over the shipping lane toward DisCity, but all he sees is a sea of fire. That phone call was just the cure his peace needed; it stripped away every last shred of it, and now every nightmare has awakened again.

speaker: Arkin
content: ..."Leave blades of slaughter behind"... Heh... That's not how they used to sing it...
The rust-coated Rancor rifle trembles in his grip. Mania leaks free. Behind him, soldiers are falling in, all brothers-in-arms bound by the same shared nightmare.
Now that same irresistible scent reaches them all: the gore of a past massacre, an invitation no battlefield specter can ever refuse.

speaker: Arkin
content: ...Yes. You're right.

speaker: Arkin
content: ...Following orders is a soldier's sacred duty. Eliminating the enemy is all that matters.

speaker: Arkin
content: Everything you said... it's all true... but...
He looks toward the distance, and a smile creeps onto his lips unbidden.

speaker: Arkin
content: Look... She's here.
The shadow of Nirvana Port reaches outward, like some waking creature, like a long runner rolled out to greet a guest.

Before it, a thin figure approaches, unsteady on her feet. She seems so small, and yet so achingly familiar. It is as though this long-dormant grave has been waiting for her alone, waiting to be stirred back to life.

speaker: Jasmine
content: I'm finally out... Heheh... This is right. I'm back...

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...Now, let the celebration begin...
She raises her Rancor. They all raise theirs. The long-lost weapon has at last returned to the place it has yearned for day and night. And after all this time, she feels a true heartbeat at last.
At that time, you don't yet understand. The deeper a Rancor is pulled into the battlefield, the less meaning attachment and possession can ever hold.
Only through taking can their hearts be awakened.

23 Hours After Jasmine's Escape

WhiteSands
The Bureau's armored pursuit vehicle tears through the pale expanse of WhiteSands. The ash density hasn't eased, the sandstorm hasn't broken, and together they bleed the speed from your chase.
You can only hope it drags Jasmine down just as much, that it keeps her from reaching Nirvana Port so quickly.

speaker: Eugene
content: Chief! We've got the transport driver on the line. He never saw who hit him, woke up on the side of the road with the truck dead. He's less than 30 klicks from Nirvana Port.

speaker: Eugene
content: Those Rancor blades are gone.

speaker: Wynn
content: Is she at the port yet? Has she made it? Chief, I keep calling but the Shattered Blade won't pick up—

speaker: Nurse
content: Jasmine escaped? That... that doesn't make any sense. She's been doing so well, taking her meds, fully engaged in rehab. If something was seriously wrong, there's no way she could've kept up that act. Where... where did she go?

speaker: Doctor
content: A madwoman with her wits intact... That level of intelligence, that will... it only makes her more absolute in rejecting any attempt to reach her heart. She's far more dangerous than we gave her credit for. It's... it's just tragic.
[WhiteSands Background, Nighttime] Screen Shakes, Driving Scene

Inside the vehicle, you're seething with frustration. This is your 16th attempt to contact Nirvana Port through the heavy communication interference; this time, it finally goes through. A cold voice answers from the other end.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: Hello.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: She is here, with her blades. This is your idea of returning that Rancor?
A storm of noise rises in the background. You catch the clash of metal, the bark of gunfire, and from some far-off place, barely audible—

speaker: Jasmine
content: Hahaha...
It's Jasmine! Your heart clenches in an instant.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Stop her, please! There has to be something at the port! Augustus must know some way to contain Rancors! Just get those blades off Jasmine. Separate her from them. They're the ones in control, not her.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm almost there. The shackles can calm her. She'll listen to me. She still has her mind. She can still be saved.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Jasmine isn't DisCity's enemy. She's a civilian. She's innocent! Uris, don't hurt her!
You beg him, your words tumbling out near-incoherent, but all you get back is the coldest possible reply.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: That's not our problem. If she wants to make herself the enemy of the Shattered Blade, we've got standing orders for enemies.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: Pick up the pace, Chief. Show up now, and you might still catch the closing act.
The line goes dead. A curse tears out of you, raw with fury, as you dial the next number, then another, reaching for every name you can think of.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Nightingale, get me FAC, or EDGE, or Ring Research, anyone! Put a leash on the Shattered Blade! Get them ordered to stand down!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Banyan Medical, sedatives, high-potency sedatives, whatever they've got! Authorization for high-level Sinner deployment, now! Don't let them slow me down! Hello? Hello?! Can you hear me?! Damn it!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: <size=50>Eugene, faster!!</size>

Over quicksand, through the storm's lashing heart, the armored pursuit vehicle at last breaks into the eye and barrels through Nirvana Port's guardrails like a thing possessed. You boot open the scarred and splintered door, stepping out to meet the guards closing in to inspect.

And to your surprise, they do as you say. One look at you, and understanding settles over their faces. Someone opens their mouth, then thinks better of it. They clear a path and let you through. The weight of it only deepens the dread coiling in your gut.

You storm into Nirvana Port. Alarms howl along every turn, security measures slamming shut in sequence, yet it feels orchestrated, a baiting trail. The path is littered with fresh, brutal slash marks, drawing you toward the heart of the fortress.

Jasmine's unhinged laughter echoes amid the gunfire and the ringing clash of metal. You cannot tell if it is near, if it bleeds through the shackles, or if your imagination has finally broken its leash. Before your eyes, fragments of nightmare unspool.

[War CG Montage]
[War CG Montage]
[War CG Montage]
[Final Flash: Two CGs of Jasmine Being Taken Away]
[Final Flash: Two CGs of Jasmine Being Taken Away]

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: There's still time... I have to make it!
[Black Screen, Sound of Door Being Rammed]
You burst from the cramped passage onto an open-air platform. The sky is dark, but one glance down and you see her.
There, Jasmine stands in the center of a clearing. She's unhurt, but exhaustion weighs on every line of her frame. She sways on her feet, her long hair and dress soaked in a vivid, glaring red.
It's not her blood.

speaker: Soldier
content: Cough... Ahh!!

At her feet and all around her, soldiers lie fallen. Five, six, seven of them, breath shallow, life fading. The ground is strewn with the shattered fragments of Rancors. From the broken edges, the masterless Mania leaks forth, mingling with blood, spreading slow across the earth.

Farther back, a dozen or so Shattered Blade soldiers stand in loose knots, their faces etched with bone-deep weariness. Weapons in hand, yet they do not stir—spectators or corpses, it is impossible to tell—jutting stark and strange in the hush of this quiet arena.
At center stage, Jasmine trembles. She laughs, a frail sound spiraling steadily into madness.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Heh... hehe... Ahahahahahaha! So weak... SO WEAK!!

speaker: Jasmine
content: Is this all DisCity's blades can do? Rusted out? Gone dull? Every last one of you, so pathetic! Lining up one by one, just begging me to snap you in half?!

speaker: Jasmine
content: You wish! That celebration isn't over. Now it's your turn to take the stage, and just bleeding won't cut it!

speaker: Jasmine
content: Cry! Scream! Get on your knees and beg. We've been through all that! Pick up your weapons! Keep going!

She cries out, raising one of her blood-drenched Rancor blades and leveling it at the "audience" a few meters away. Where the blade points, no fire of rage ignites. The soldiers remain eerily calm, and from among them, another figure steps forward.

speaker: Soldier
content: ...My turn.

He hefts his axe, accepting the "duel." In an instant, Jasmine's drained body ignites again. The Rancor blades drag her forward, hurling her at her opponent as she hacks down on him like a raging storm.
Stop them. They must be stopped. Your feet stir into motion, but no sooner do you turn than a hand lands hard upon your shoulder, barring the way.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: Careful, Chief.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: This is a fight between Rancors. At this point, walking in means death. The General sees something in you. I'm to keep you breathing.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: Not that you'd stop them anyway.
Isn't this on him too?! Fury rises to your lips, but before the words can break, your eyes catch what Iron Mask carries on his other side.
A veteran soldier, his body half-drowned in blood, arms and legs swaying with the lifeless weight of the unconscious. From his collar, a rusted dog tag slips free, bearing a name—
He's beyond saving. This is Jasmine's vengeance; this is the brutal battlefield you've relived countless times in your nightmares. But what truly shakes you goes deeper than that.

When you look at Arkin's face, you see no hatred, no pain, no fear, no regret. There's just an eerie smile, hollow and desolate like the stillness of ruins. You then turn your gaze at the Shattered Blade soldiers below, only to find them wear the same expression.

Challenger and onlooker alike, none of them mean to kill her. No fear, no fury, no resignation. They simply watch and wait, as if the figure before them isn't an enemy who slaughtered their comrades, but something else entirely. Kin, at last recognizing each other.
The bizarre inversion of it sends a wave of dizziness through you.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: You don't get it? Of course you don't. In this world, only Rancor understands Rancor. We understand her hatred. A life for a life, simple as that.

His words are cold, his gaze fixed on the scene below. In the arena, the two Rancors launch into another charge. Jasmine's Mania spills from her blades, shrieking as she drives forward. The soldier on the other side surges to meet her with gathered force, his face still utterly calm.

Just as her blades are about to crash against his axe, with half a step between them, he looks into Jasmine's eyes and suddenly smiles. The same smile as Arkin's. He opens his mouth and murmurs, barely audible.

speaker: Soldier
content: You... did good.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Ahhh!!!

The instant their weapons meet, the Mania on his axe gutters out. Jasmine's blade shears straight through the soldier's weapon and into his body. Blood sprays into the dancer's eyes. She reels back several steps, her shock blasting through the shackles straight to the top of your skull.
And then you hear it too: the resonance of the Rancors echoing through her mind, and theirs.

speaker: Rancors
content: It's from RNH... I remember now... No, don't remember. I've seen people like that before I've hurt people like that before. They're coming to stir up trouble again they're finally here to collect what's owed.

speaker: Rancors
content: Don't feel sorry for her don't hurt her. We're not done hating yet we've done enough evil already. I stayed alive for today I kept breathing for this. Time to settle every score that was left open...

speaker: Rancors
content: Back to the fight back to the fight back to the fight back to the fight back to the fight back to the fight back to the fight back to the fight back to the fight back to the fight BACK TO THE FIGHT!

Accumulated derangement, the longing for death... Under Mania's influence, they curdle into a frenzy that denies everything. The impact knocks you off balance. Iron Mask catches you before you fall. Yet the soldiers, Iron Mask included, remain utterly still, their faces expressionless, as if they'd seen this coming all along.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Are those Rancors... brainwashing them? Or do they actually want...

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: There aren't many DisCorps soldiers left alive. They've been running on fumes a long time now, held on 'til Augustus came, held on 'til now... Truth is, most of them ran out of fight a while back. If anything, we should be the ones thanking you.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: Thank you for delivering us a spotless victim. You proved her innocence. Laid bare the weight of their sins. Handed them the perfect judge to send them all to hell.
...Judge? Perfect? Meaning... both sides get exactly what they want?
The deathly numbness in his voice sets your blood on fire.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Are you kidding me?! There's only Arkin left from RNH. What do the rest of them down there have to do with Jasmine? What, you're all going to relive their traumas together? Run the past back, swap the ending, and call that atonement?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: To hell with that! You just can't put down the Rancors. Spent your whole lives blind to everything but the battlefield. If the guilt's eating you alive, then march your asses to a military court and face a real verdict! She is not your way out. This is just more torture for her!

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: Waking up is the torture!

His metal prosthetic pins you against the narrow corridor railing, the force nearly wrenching your arm out of its socket. Through that cold iron mask, you feel his anger, something you've rarely ever sensed from him.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: You pulled her out of cryosleep, stood there running your mouth about bringing her back to the living. When you did all that, did you ever stop and think how she's supposed to live on?

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: Dragging a ghost back takes a lot. If you can't keep at it and you can't tame her, then let her go. None of us can stop her. So just watch, Chief.
The Mania markings on his neck smolder with a pent-up burn, and his Mania bleeds into you. Rage, hatred, agony, obsession—a torrent of violent emotion, and none of it is meant for you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...You can't keep at it, and you can't tame them. You believe these soldiers of yours can never come back, so you're letting them go... You made this decision by yourself...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Or are you doing this while she's gone, to settle old scores before she returns?
At last, a ripple cuts across the stagnant water.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Heh... There it is. You can't face her. You don't want her stained by the sins from your past. You want to keep her in the light. You think she's like you. That she couldn't carry it either.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...So this is how you look after her soldiers, <color=#fb9259>Adjutant</color>.
You say your piece. Then, with little resistance, you shoulder past him and rush down.
[Scene Change: Jasmine's Portrait]
Another "enemy" falls, but Jasmine has no time to celebrate. She stumbles backward, hunched over, frantically scrubbing at her eyes as if the blood were acid instead. She's whimpering, trembling.

She's terrified. Through the blood haze, the soldiers of DisCity close in around her, with weapons in hand, but no intent to kill. Calm madmen lining up to bare their necks. For the first time, they truly frighten her.

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...Again... It's happening again!! You have weapons. Why won't you fight?! Are you insane?!
Silence is her only answer, save for the Rancors' resonating whispers, swelling ever more rabid in her mind.

speaker: Rancors
content: Go on. Don't stop now. Who's next? Do us this honor. We can be your enemy too. We've all walked the same battlefield.

speaker: Rancors
content: This is what you wanted this is what we prayed for. We hate you we know how you feel. Go on. We're all the same.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Drop the act! You've always wanted me dead, haven't you?! Then come on! I'm standing right here! Come at me!
She's nearly breaking under the weight of those whispers. Just then, she hears the one voice that's real.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Chief...?!
She thinks she's hearing things until she looks up and sees you. Joy ignites her face for an instant, then gutters out just as fast.
The moment she realizes you've entered the battlefield too, your foot setting down on the spreading blood, her expression turns ashen. Jasmine snaps her blades up and screams at you to stop.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Not one more step! I'm having fun. Don't ruin this for me...

She attempts a savage, mocking smile, but it reveals nothing save her own collapse. The battle has dragged on too long; her strength and will are both nearly spent. Even her voice comes out trembling.

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...Why did you come here, you fool... It's dangerous, and this has nothing to do with you. How many times have I lied to you now, and you still worry about me?

speaker: Jasmine
content: But you don't have to. I'm strong now, not like last time. I won't lose again... See? I've already won.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Once I've swept the stage clean, I'll come back. You can punish me then, okay?

speaker: Jasmine
content: Just wait a little longer... The celebration's almost over. All of DisCity's blades are here, every last one... I'll finish it soon. Just have to break them all...
She looks around. Yes, this is her celebration, taken back at last. Look, everyone's so happy. Everyone but ${PlayerName}.

Fallen at her feet or waiting in silence, some of them wear fresh uniforms, some in clothes worn thin by time. Even faces from years back have come, all of them an audience who once watched her dance.

From that first celebration to this one, every last person has been bleeding, bearing blades, watching her with smiles. She scans each face—the living, the dead—all of them knowing this is the finale. Jasmine wants to smile too, but...

One by one, slashes and bloodied scars grow on those smiling faces. The faces of "enemies" and the faces of her people slip apart and slide together. The blades in her hand burn. The gleeful celebration song dissolves into keening. Suddenly, she cannot see how long the road ahead truly is, how much longer she must walk before the celebration ends.

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...Why are there so many... It's still not over? How much longer... Do I have to kill every last one?

speaker: Jasmine
content: My celebration... is this really what it was?

Jasmine's smile crumbles, her spirit suspended on a gossamer thread. For more than ten years, she confronted the wound without flinching, and now she stands at last at the source of it all, only to find the awakened past flaying her inch by inch.
As though her pursuit had never been about righting what was wrong. As though what they hunted, all along, was only the death the battlefield had long owed the ones who lived.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No... this isn't right... You don't want this. Killing only hurts you... You just wanted to protect your celebration. You wanted to break the blade that destroyed your home...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Put the blades down. Please. This fight is not giving you anything but more pain. The nightmare can end. We'll find another way. Destroy the Rancor for good. Hold the guilty to account. See a real celebration...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Come back with me, will you? Don't let the thing that hurt you destroy you all over again... It shouldn't end like this...

You call her name softly, walking toward her through the weight of Mania and the reek of blood. But the eyes Jasmine turns on you hold nothing but hollow confusion. You're the only outsider here. Every one of her "enemies," every "foe" here, is closer to her heart than you are.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: You pulled her out of cryosleep, stood there running your mouth about bringing her back to the living. When you did all that, did you ever stop and think how she's supposed to live on?

What's left that could still ignite something in her? Justice, happiness, a future—things already stripped from her, denied beyond reach. Do they hold any value anymore? What could possibly make her turn and look back toward this shore? You wrack your brain, your skull pounding.
Then, as if pitying your desperation, someone behind you brings the answer.
[Black Screen]

speaker: Voice From Behind
content: You started a fight and didn't invite me?
[Transition 2s]
Familiar footsteps. A familiar voice. It's someone you know well.
This time, there isn't the faintest trace of a smile on her face.
[Silhouette Transitions to Augustus's Portrait]
The general strides past you, and in that moment, you are frozen where you stand, your body gone cold. The dozen or so Shattered Blade soldiers ahead are no different.
At last, their gazes pull free of Jasmine, only to flinch away from their commander by instinct.
The one they answer to has returned. A pall of fear settles over them all.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: ...Why did you come back?

speaker: Augustus
content: Got an emergency call. Nirvana Port's in trouble, they said. Told me to get back now. I didn't think I'd come home to... this.

An expression you have never seen before rests on Augustus's face. She takes in the scene: a manic Outlands Sinner, debris and remains littering the ground, Rancor after Rancor broken open and bleeding corruption.
At last her gaze finds you. A single glance at your expression tells her all she needs to know. She laughs, cold.

speaker: Augustus
content: Chief ${PlayerName}'s right. This fight means nothing. A waste of breath.
A handful of soldiers who followed her back step quickly between you, shielding you and shutting you out at once. You try to speak, but her eyes never return to you.
Augustus turns toward Jasmine.

speaker: Augustus
content: If it's revenge you want, at least point it at the right target.

Jasmine's entire body jolts. The confusion and vulnerability she showed you only moments earlier have vanished. From the moment Augustus entered, her gaze has been fixed on the general. A smile reclaims the dancer's face.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Heh... I knew it. This whole thing felt off... because you weren't here.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Should've just said so. All I need to do is kill you. So let's—Nngh!
