She lunges to attack, only for her twin blades to wrench hard in the opposite direction, tangling her stride. She knows this force at once. It's Augustus's magnetic field manipulation, the same power she witnessed at the Great Expo.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Let go of me, coward! What's wrong? You scared? Scared to fight me?!

speaker: Augustus
content: Fight you? Heh... Stray cats really don't learn. Have you forgotten already? At the Great Expo, when I used my power, you couldn't even last a minute.

speaker: Augustus
content: Besides, I don't waste my time on fools who let their own blades puppet them around. You want to face me? Then clear your head and come at me like a real warrior.
She steps through her subordinate's blood and enters the inner circle, studying Jasmine with cold scrutiny.
Then Augustus lifts her still-sheathed sword and levels it at the enraged dancer.

speaker: Augustus
content: Rein in your Mania, Outlander. You follow the rules, and I'll give you my word. No powers, a fair duel with just this sword. Which means...

speaker: Augustus
content: You might actually get a shot at my head.

Iron Mask and every Shattered Blade soldier stiffen at once. But Augustus doesn't spare them a single glance. Her eyes stay fixed on the blood-crazed Sinner before her, a smile of pure contempt spreading across her face.

speaker: Augustus
content: Unless, of course, you're too afraid to face me without <color=#fb9259>DisCity's Rancor</color> doing all the work.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Heh... Hehe... Ahahaha! You snake! Fine, come on! I'll gnaw you to death with my own teeth if I have to!
Jasmine speaks through clenched teeth, but the wild Rancor in her grip slowly begins to subside. Something in Augustus's eyes eases, just a fraction.

speaker: Augustus
content: ...There we go. Now show me what you've got.
The two S-Class Sinners lock eyes. Their powers gradually recede, suppressed by the weight of a greater will. The raging Mania around them quiets, and everyone holds their breath.

The instant the magnetic field lifts, Jasmine launches forward like a bullet. Her blades slice past Augustus's face, only to be guided aside by the DisCity general's sword. In a smooth deflection, it slides and turns her strike away.
(Production note: Record several battle sound effects, edit as needed, and sync to corresponding narration. This line should be deleted from final version.)

Chop, slash, sweep, thrust. Jasmine's attacks are ferocious and blunt, reckless with abandon. In a few exchanges, Augustus has caught her rhythm. A casual feint, a flick of her cloak, and Jasmine takes the bait.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Ugh!
Duped by the sweep of the cloak, Jasmine staggers and crashes to the earth. The first exchange is done. For all her fury, her claws have not once grazed the composed hunter before her.

speaker: Augustus
content: Get up. Again.

Her tone of command only stokes the flames higher. Jasmine's eyes burn red as she springs up and surges forward again. The second round begins: their movements now too swift to follow, only crimson phantoms flickering around Augustus's form. Metal shrieks against metal in rapid, stinging bursts, sparks flashing through the air like lightning.

Augustus will not be broken; she is the perfect target for vengeance. At last, Jasmine can pour out her fury without restraint. The battle climbs in intensity, and the atmosphere among the Shattered Blade soldiers presses down heavier with each beat.

Not long ago, they hung their heads in silence, awaiting Jasmine's execution. Now their beloved general is threatened, and their hands tighten once more around their Rancors. Murderous intent seeps through the ranks, but Augustus pays it no heed.

She reads the stillness inside the storm and thrusts with precision, striking Jasmine clean in the chest. Jasmine lets out a violent cough and staggers back, her berserk offensive collapsing with a single hit. The blade, even now, remains sheathed.

speaker: Augustus
content: Go on.

speaker: Jasmine
content: GAAAAAHHHHHH—!!!

Another round, and another. Her attacks descend like a frenzied storm, only to be broken, again and again, by the simplest slash as metal shrieks its lament with every blow. A spent assassin on the edge of ruin hurls herself against a composed general fresh from her victorious return.

Murderous rage and hatred devour the last of her strength, ignited into a blaze until at last, the fire burns itself out. Jasmine drops to her knees, staring in confusion at the Rancor in her hands. Nothing remains but exhaustion, defeat, and a hollow void.
Augustus's shadow falls over her. The "enemy" is overwhelmingly strong. Jasmine couldn't wound this woman, not even a scratch.

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...Can't break... her blade... I can't break it...

speaker: Jasmine
content: Why...

This is the second time. How many years have passed? The beginning of everything, the fount of all her suffering, stands here before her now. A chain of cause and consequence this long ought to have its end. The celebration's close requires this woman's severed head to mark its grave, and yet Jasmine cannot lay a finger on her.
...And still she is made to suffer that gaze from on high.

speaker: Augustus
content: Are we done? Or take a breath and keep going?

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...Hahaha... Is this some kind of joke? I'm not a joke... None of us is a joke...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Jasmine, don't...
Her breathing grows ragged and disordered. Her fragile mind can no longer hold the Mania back. It seeps through the widening cracks, and the Rancor blades begin to thrum with a low, pulsing hum.

speaker: Jasmine
content: It's not meaningless... I came all this way, I made it here... I survived for the celebration, and it's not over yet...
Augustus studies Jasmine without a word. Her eyes drift past the dancer's shoulder to you, then settle on the fallen soldiers strewn across the ground. A sigh escapes her, nearly imperceptible.

speaker: Augustus
content: Last chance. Put the blades down, or I'll break them for you.

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...You're the one who should be broken!

The Rancor is set loose. In that moment, she wants nothing but to bring down the woman before her. She gives herself willingly to the blades, becoming their puppet. The duel collapses, her power spirals out of control, and years of bottled madness erupt in a roaring surge toward Augustus.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: General!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Jasmine, no!!!

In the same breath, the Shattered Blade soldiers erupt into motion. A dozen fighters with a dozen weapons surge to Augustus's side as one, pushing forward to meet the crazed Outlander. They know killing her means damnation, but they do not waver for a second. Gunfire cracks through the air.
The Rancors decided their own end long ago.
[Black Screen]
Yet the death match never ignites.
There is no bloodshed, no collision. Every blade and bullet hangs suspended in the air, their wielders locked motionless alongside them.
A crushing magnetic power commands the field. Augustus stands at the center between the two frenzied forces, surrounded by Rancor weapons hovering in stillness. The quiet that falls is absolute.

speaker: Augustus
content: I said a fair duel. Are all of you deaf...? You dare defy my order?

Her magnetic power wrenches the weapons and flings them hard, throwing the berserk combatants to the earth. If this ground is a battlefield, it must kneel to her command. Her patience has at last run dry, and she wields terror to drive reason back into them.
The battle between the Rancor wielders is over. You can rest easy now. Except...
Just now, Augustus wasn't the only one trying to stop the fight.
[Shackles Effect]

Your hand is outstretched, a harsh red light blazing from it, aimed at the center of the battlefield. Both S-Class Sinners turn to look at you at once. In that most perilous moment, you released the shackles on pure instinct. But the shackles can only bind one person at a time.
And the person you restrained is—
The red light of the shackles cuts through Augustus. She holds steady, unshaken, yet even so, this grants Jasmine her first, and only, chance.
One of the curved blades sweeps across the DisCity general's shoulder, a strand of her hair falling away. Blood slowly surfaces, darkening the fabric of her epaulette.
Jasmine, too, stands frozen.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Haha... Haha... You deserved that... You deserved it...

speaker: Jasmine
content: I'm not alone. I have Chief on my side. As long as he's here, I won't lose. Chief, I—
female_content: I'm not alone. I have Chief on my side. As long as she's here, I won't lose. Chief, I—

content: She never meant to drag you into this. She's always kept you out of her battlefield. But now that you've truly barged in, she realizes that she's so happy. So impossibly happy. She doesn't yet understand this feeling. She just wants to turn around and look at you.
Then, in a heartbeat, all that joy twists into a scream of horror.

speaker: Jasmine
content: NOOO!!
[Violent impact, screen shakes, bone-breaking sound effect]
You're thrown down from behind. Your arm twists into a grotesque angle, searing pain tearing through every nerve. The hand that unleashed the shackles goes instantly numb.
You turn your head and meet Iron Mask's bloodshot, red-rimmed eyes.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: ...You use the shackles on her again, I'll snap your neck.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: Now shut your mouth!

You are pressed ruthlessly into the earth. White sand mingled with blood fills your mouth and nostrils; no restraining order can leave your lips now. Barely meters beyond, more than a dozen muzzles turn as one and train themselves on you. Behind each sight, eyes seethe with rage.

speaker: Jasmine
content: No! He has nothing to do with this! I'm the one you want. Let him go!! Nngh—!
female_content: No! She has nothing to do with this! I'm the one you want. Let her go!! Nngh—!

content: Steel plates and iron bars bear down on her with crushing weight. Even the twin blades in her hands twist into restraints, flipping around to lock the Outland Sinner firmly in place.
It's that person's power.

speaker: Augustus
content: Let him go, Uris. All of you, stand down.
female_content: Let her go, Uris. All of you, stand down.

speaker: Augustus
content: ...Leave him to me.
female_content: ...Leave her to me.

content: The weight pinning you down lifts with obvious reluctance, but you can't rise anyway. Pain and blood loss keep you flattened against the ground. You hear slow footsteps approaching.
That most dependable "comrade" who once fought at your side picks up her sword. Despite the shackles, she walks toward you, step by step.
Jasmine struggles desperately, but it's useless. Augustus doesn't spare her a single backward glance. The general has abandoned her old foe and now stands before you.

speaker: Augustus
content: ...Your arm's broken... Does it hurt?

speaker: Augustus
content: How could you be so foolish? Using the shackles on me here... You really could've gotten yourself killed.

You understand. Shackling the commander, becoming a clear threat to her, is the Shattered Blade's greatest taboo. The trust you've shared exists only because you fought side by side through the direst of circumstances.
And that instinctive move you just made shattered it completely. The Shattered Blade never spares an enemy of Augustus.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You said you didn't want the battlefield defiled. You wanted to return honor to Shattered Blade.
Hearing this, Augustus smiles.
She's glad you remember those words. But the shackles are still on her, which means you don't truly trust her.
...Then let it be that way. Augustus closes her eyes. When she opens them again—

speaker: Augustus
content: Honor...? You mean mercy? Justice? Righteousness? Kindness, understanding, seeing the other side's pain... No. That's you. That's who you are.

speaker: Augustus
content: You're such a fool, Chief... Who talks about conscience to a war?
There is something wrong with her expression. You try to ask, but a deafening boom interrupts. Several lengths of steel rebar graze past your body and drive deep into the earth.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Chief!!
Augustus doesn't look back. After all this time, she finally draws that sword, her eyes fixed on you, yet every word she speaks drives clean into Jasmine's nerves.

speaker: Augustus
content: I am a general of the DisCorps, commander of every last Rancor. What they do, all of it, is on my orders. If I had a shred of mercy in me, that woman wouldn't be out here right now, hunting vengeance like some rabid dog.

speaker: Augustus
content: So you don't want her dead? Then why did you let her onto the battlefield? Why did you stand by while she provoked me? Were you just hoping for the best? Can you afford the price if you're wrong? Or is it that her life doesn't really matter to you?

speaker: Augustus
content: But it does matter, doesn't it? You even used your shackles against me, just to protect her...

speaker: Augustus
content: Good. This is easier. Treating you as an enemy makes things much simpler...
Augustus turns slightly, glancing at the blades in Jasmine's hands, then at Jasmine herself. A chill crawls down Jasmine's spine for no reason she can name.

speaker: Augustus
content: That Rancor says you never left that celebration. That it's still going, even now. Then allow me to... liven the mood.
She slides the sword through your hair, the edge shearing away a few strands, then draws it slowly across your throat. Jasmine's pupils blow wide in an instant.

speaker: Augustus
content: Don't worry... I'll make it quick.

speaker: Rest in peace, monster.
content: ...ARRRGGHHH!!

A fire catches within Jasmine. She struggles like a woman possessed, pouring all her remaining strength into breaking loose. The blades forgotten, she hurls herself past Augustus and throws her body in front of yours as a living shield.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Jasmine...

speaker: Jasmine
content: No... You can't let her... She's insane. She's a monster... She means it...

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...It's happening again. It always happens... I shouldn't have let you come. I should've driven you away the second I saw you... Not again. I can't let it happen again. I can't lose you too...

Her whole body shakes. For too long, far too long, war and enemies meant nothing but vengeance in her eyes. So long that she'd forgotten what they truly were at the beginning: absolute <color=#fb9259>fear</color>.

The fear of being stripped of everything. The fear of losing what she loves. It all comes rushing back now, vivid and visceral, a chaotic mess churning through her mind. She shields you desperately, clinging to you the way she once held onto those she couldn't keep, unwilling to move even a single step away.
Augustus doesn't move. At some point, her sword found its sheath again. She stands a single step away, watching the two of you. In the end, she doesn't take that short step.

speaker: Augustus
content: ...There. That's better. Hate me. Fear me. When the killing urge comes, come find me. But only challenge me when you're ready to lose everything. That's the attitude war demands. No more fooling yourself with hope.

speaker: Augustus
content: Pitiful Rancor. I am your one commander, and your one enemy. I will give you everything you seek. Even death, if that's truly what you want.

speaker: Augustus
content: But be clear about this... There are more than just enemies on the battlefield. There are also fools like him, clinging to you, refusing to let go. He threw himself in front of me for you this time. But if he does it again, I promise you, his end will not be gentle.
female_content: But be clear about this... There are more than just enemies on the battlefield. There are also fools like her, clinging to you, refusing to let go. She threw herself in front of me for you this time. But if she does it again, I promise you, her end will not be gentle.

speaker: Jasmine
content: You vile bastard... shameless coward... If you lay a finger on him...
female_content: You vile bastard... shameless coward... If you lay a finger on her...

content: She curses helplessly. The woman she hates most has already turned away, walking back toward her troops. Her back is wide open, every cell in Jasmine's body screaming at her to charge and run her through.

But the body in Jasmine's arms is going cold. He's badly hurt. Jasmine presses frantically at the wound to stop the bleeding, and in her panic, ${PlayerName}'s face blurs with the faces of her people. She can't breathe. Her heart pounds like a war drum as if she's alive again, truly alive.
female_content: But the body in Jasmine's arms is going cold. She's badly hurt. Jasmine presses frantically at the wound to stop the bleeding, and in her panic, ${PlayerName}'s face blurs with the faces of her people. She can't breathe. Her heart pounds like a war drum as if she's alive again, truly alive.

content: War stripped everything from her. Justice, happiness, love, a future, all ground to dust. Everything she once believed in was denied, annihilated. But war gave her one thing, carved into the marrow of her bones: the pain and fear of loss.
That is it. Only through taking, and being taken from, can a Rancor's heart truly awaken.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Don't you dare think you've won!! I'll kill you. I swear I'll kill you one day!!

speaker: Augustus
content: When you're truly ready to let go of everything... anytime. I'll be waiting.
Augustus moves forward without a single backward glance. As she passes the abandoned pair of Rancor blades, she raises her hand and breaks them apart.
Then she walks toward her silent soldiers and leads them back into the shadow of their bastion.
The crimson light from the shackles cuts through Jasmine, breaking her assault and crushing the Rancor's corruption in one clean stroke.
Reason has returned to her. She keeps her head bowed, every inch of her shaking.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Do you hate me now, Chief? Because I... wouldn't listen?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...No. I could never hate you, Jasmine.

speaker: Jasmine
content: You don't hate me? Then why...

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...Because... you're taking her side?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm not taking anyone's side. But Jasmine... I can't watch you suffer like this anymore.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Don't let the Rancor take you. Don't let it destroy you again. Come back with me. We can—
You try to move closer, your voice earnest and pleading, desperate to soothe her. But your words can no longer reach her.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Haha... I knew it. I knew it! All the same... I'm such a fool. You're all the same...
Augustus is the first to sense something wrong. Killing intent. Her hand closes around the hilt of her sword, every muscle going taut.

speaker: Augustus
content: ...Enough. ${PlayerName}, get out. Now—

speaker: Augustus
content: Uris, get him out of here!
female_content: Uris, get her out of here!

content: But it's too late. Jasmine turns and looks at you. This time, finally, her heart and her eyes hold you, and only you.

speaker: Jasmine
content: I SHOULD HAVE KILLED YOU FIRST!!

She spins around, dragging the Rancor blades with her and turning them on you. Hatred and despair far heavier than vengeance erupt alongside her Mania, and somehow she breaks free of both Augustus's control and the shackles.

speaker: Augustus
content: ${PlayerName}, move!!
Augustus draws her sword and thrusts straight at the crazed Jasmine, dropping every last trace of hesitation and mercy.
But Jasmine's blades are faster, more desperate. She charges at you from less than ten steps away.
Five steps. The killing intent hits you like a physical force. She means it. You can see the hatred in her eyes with absolute clarity.

speaker: Soldier
content: No... hold your fire! Too close, we'll hit the Chief!
Three paces. The wind off her blades stings your nerves. Your body finally registers death's warning, only for raw fear to seize you and lock every muscle in place.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: Move! ${PlayerName}!!
You can't die on her blades. Not here. You throw every ounce of strength into retreat, forcing your body backward, desperate to gain even a single step of distance. You have to move, for everyone!
You manage it. Then, at once, regret floods in.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Cough!
A rapier pierces through her body.
It's Augustus.

She seizes the opening, that single step you fought so desperately to create. With you finally clear, she unleashes her power. Two steel lances shoot in from opposite sides, impaling Jasmine's hands and completely neutralizing the strike meant for you. The Shattered Blade soldiers open fire on instinct.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No!!

Before your very eyes, bullets rip through that fragile, shattered body. Not a sound escapes her. Her blades fall from your throat as though, at the very end, she mustered what little strength remained and turned it away from your vital points.
She slides down against you, blood drenching you both. You sink to your knees and hold her. There is no use in calling out now.
The dancer's pupils slowly lose their focus, like scattering fireworks, taking in every Disian's face standing around her.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Hehe... Hahaha... Look... a celebration... a celebration that lasts forever...

speaker: Jasmine
content: Enjoy it... It's all yours now...
The fireworks scatter into nothing. In death, she binds her enemies to the celebration's eternal curse.
[Black Screen Transition]

General Augustus slew the frenzied avenger with her own hands, saving her soldiers and her ally.

Yet her battlefield lies stained, her blade dishonored. The glory she newly claimed and the vow she made are all reduced to ashes. And you, together with every Rancor soldier standing there, are witnesses to it.
Even years later, it remains a nightmare for all of you. The cursed celebration never ends, not even in death.

Jasmine's blade comes straight for you, but you can't move away. If you take even a single step, Augustus's sword will pierce through this berserk Outland Rancor wielder. She could end everything, but that's not what you want.
The Sinner before you, her eyes wild with rage, was never meant to be here.

speaker: Jasmine
content: DIE!
Her hatred pierces you before the blades ever do. Somewhere between the pain and the fear, a hazy answer flickers into mind.

She never accepted you. Never wanted to let you in. But now, everything is different. Now, you are her <color=#fb9259>enemy</color>. By truly stepping onto her battlefield, you've finally earned your place.

speaker: Augustus
content: Stop!!
Trapped on this battlefield, suffering for so long, she's questioned fate over and over, and always received the same answer. But now, perhaps, you can finally give her an answer no "enemy" ever has.
You step forward, reaching out to her, arms open wide. In that moment, Jasmine's eyes go wide.

For the briefest instant, the hatred in her gaze shatters under the force of shock. Then follows a maelstrom of confusion, doubt, terror, resistance, and regret. She can't process it. She tries to pull back, but she's already too close. There's no escaping now.

Momentum carries the twin Rancor blades forward. They slice easily through your coat and bite into skin. The edges carve through flesh, exposing the sinew and bone of your shoulder. Blood spatters across Jasmine's face. Her whole body jolts.

speaker: Jasmine
content: AAAHHHH!!!
A scream tears from her throat. She flings the Rancor blades away as if they seared her palm. The weapon spins through the air and buries itself deep in the white sand.
At last, you summon every last shred of strength and catch hold of her. No time to register the pain. You pull her tight against you.
Augustus rushes over. Judging by her face, things aren't looking good. But you can't black out now, not after coming this far. Time to strike while the iron's hot.

speaker: Augustus
content: Let go, ${PlayerName}. She's not someone you can control. Those blades have already marked you as the enemy. Leave this to me. I'll handle both the Rancor and its wielder.

speaker: Augustus
content: Let her go! She's too far gone. You're going to get yourself killed!
Her enemy's voice is so close, yet Jasmine can no longer make out Augustus's face.
${PlayerName}'s blood keeps pouring out, sticking him and Jasmine together. The metallic stench is overpowering. After all these years, fear finds Jasmine again. She shakes violently.
female_content: ${PlayerName}'s blood keeps pouring out, sticking her and Jasmine together. The metallic stench is overpowering. After all these years, fear finds Jasmine again. She shakes violently.

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...No... let go... let go of me... why...
Your consciousness blurs at the edges, but the weight in your chest finally eases.
For the first time, you feel you have truly reached her.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Haha... It's okay... Everything's okay now... I came to deliver the blades. So... mission accomplished, I guess...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Augustus... Catherine. That Rancor is yours. Take it... Take your soldiers... to a battlefield worthy of real glory.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: She doesn't belong on any battlefield... I'm taking her back.
You feel the one in your arms flinch.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Jasmine doesn't belong here. She'll never be your enemy again... And if she needs an enemy... I'll be enough.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: From now on... I'll bear everything she carries.

Your words have struck something deep within her. Augustus makes no answer. She gazes at you both in silence, then raises her eyes to the soldiers gathered before her, who seem still bewildered and uncertain.
The general of Rancors smiles.

speaker: Augustus
content: What kind of battlefield is this... All these Rancors, and not one of you has half the spine of a person who walked in here empty-handed.

speaker: Augustus
content: ...If this is your decision, ${PlayerName}, then good. Very good... Hold onto that will. Bear her well, and get off my ground.

speaker: Augustus
content: ...Don't ever come back.

She sheathes her sword and moves forward, past the two of you, toward her soldiers. Along the way, she collects the discarded pair of Rancor blades—gathering everything, everyone—and retreats deep into their bastion.
You're left where you are. Jasmine trembles uncontrollably, no strength left to chase after the Shattered Blade. She's so broken she can't even pull free from your arms.

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...Let go... Let go of me... Don't do this...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...I'm sorry, Jasmine... I'm so sorry...
The calls of your MBCC subordinates reach you, and at last, ease settles in. You slacken, your hold gradually releasing. The sounds recede. Before your eyes, a blur of light begins to glow.

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...You... what's wrong? Hey... Hey!! Wake up!! Chief... CHIEF!!
[Black Screen] Sound of a body collapsing
[Both major branches converge here - Black Screen Transition]

The sandstorm dies down. The MBCC transport vehicle tears away into the distance. Neither side impedes the other, but no one exchanges another word either. It's clear enough now that each has their own road ahead.
Nirvana Port is finally empty of outsiders.
Augustus returns to the command room and sets aside her sword. The expedition was a long one. She brought a few back with her and sent some others on their way. There's much to deal with now.
Behind her, the soldiers who caused the incident stand in a line. They deliver their report as protocol demands, but their voices are a shade too quiet.

speaker: Soldiers
content: General. 32 severely wounded. 29 face a high risk of permanent disability. All have been sent for emergency treatment. 54 Rancor weapons confirmed destroyed, exact count still being tallied. The Mania attached to them likely transferred to that woman's blades.

speaker: Soldiers
content: The MBCC didn't take the weapon. Quartermaster's already on site. Containment will take some time, but we'll handle it.

speaker: Soldiers
content: General...
Augustus keeps her back turned. Her silence alone is torture; the soldiers dare not lift their heads.
After a long, heavy pause, she finally speaks.

speaker: Augustus
content: ...Is it really that unbearable, serving under me? You had to go find yourselves a "judge" from outside... What, without her coming to collect your lives, you couldn't even stand being alive?

speaker: Soldiers
content: General, we...

speaker: Augustus
content: You fools!

speaker: Augustus
content: Feeling good about yourselves, are you? Playing martyr? You thought that made things right with her? Washed away your sins, gave you release? Open your eyes! Look at what she's become!

speaker: Augustus
content: That woman broke a long time ago. There's nothing you can give back to her. All you did was stain her hands again and betray me one more time. That's it. Nothing else!

speaker: Augustus
content: I told you I'd carry everything for you. I told you I'd lead you back to the battlefield, follow you into hell. So why wouldn't you wait? Can't keep up with me anymore?

speaker: Augustus
content: Or do you think I can't carry it? That I'm not worthy?

speaker: Soldiers
content: That's not true!
They scramble to explain themselves, but a thunderous crash cuts them short. Augustus drives her sword deep into the concrete floor. Cracks spider out from the impact. Every voice dies.
The general's blade strikes no one. Her true rage is only buried in the ground. The soldiers know, and their regret only cuts deeper.

speaker: Augustus
content: ...Anyone who wants out, go register. The rest of you, get back to cleaning up the battlefield.

speaker: Augustus
content: As for those fools... treat the ones who can be saved. The ones who can't... bring them back to me.

speaker: Augustus
content: ...I'll send them off myself.
The general dismisses her soldiers. She goes to the cemetery, then returns, walking alone through the ruins.
She does this every time she comes back from a long journey.

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: It's on me. I failed to stop them.

speaker: Augustus
content: ...You wouldn't have stopped them. You're no different from them.

speaker: Augustus
content: This one's on me. I kept you all waiting too long. I came back too late...

speaker: Iron-Masked Man
content: General...

Augustus walks on in silence, the wind and sand coursing through the military port as they have for decades without change. Uris recalls it well that 12 years ago, when she came back, it was no different.

A general who was far too young for the battlefield. A color too brilliant against the grey ruins. The one sword that remains forever sharp amid the Shattered Blade. She should have rushed forward into the future without a backward glance, yet she chose to gather up the broken blades and stay behind, anchored to what was.

Should one mock her for such pride? Nirvana Port's shadow rests upon Augustus, as does the Rancors' wails she vowed to shoulder. So immense a burden that even one as iron-willed as she might find herself crushed and consumed by it.
Augustus tilts her head upward. DisCity cannot be glimpsed from this place. Whatever she beholds beyond remains unknown.
Then, all at once, she laughs. One swing of her sword sends a wind that splits sand from sky. The horizon cracks open with light. It's always like this. She turns and gives a casual wave of her hand.

speaker: Augustus
content: Let's go back. I just said it, didn't I? The battlefield doesn't deal in conscience. I only look at victory. And what comes next.

speaker: Augustus
content: The debts of the past... I'll settle them all in time.
Right. What's the hurry? She's pointed out the road ahead. The price still owed is waiting down that path, too. She just needs to keep walking.
She is a general. She will carry it all.
After a night spent riding out the storm, by the time you finally arrive at the Bureau, your wound has already become severely infected.
[Scene Change] Operating room. Perhaps reuse the ceiling perspective from CH1, with Mania visual effects, red pulsing, etc.

speaker: Nurse
content: Fever, infection, and Mania contamination?! How did you let it get this bad?!

speaker: Nurse
content: A wound from a Rancor weapon, and no emergency treatment at all? What were you people thinking? Even the Shattered Blade should have—

speaker: Eugene
content: ...I'm sorry. Shattered Blade delayed me. I couldn't reach Chief in time.

speaker: Eugene
content: No... if only we'd caught up to Jasmine sooner, none of this...

speaker: %u
content: I was being reckless... I put Shattered... Nirvana Port in a tough spot. They offered treatment, but I decided... I wanted to get back as soon as possible...
Staying there any longer would only put Jasmine's mental state at greater risk. She needed to be taken away from Nirvana Port as quickly as possible, away from anything that might trigger her.

speaker: %u
content: I'll be fine... They patched me up enough, and my... Mania resistance is high. I can take it. Just...
Your consciousness grows hazy. The words you speak sound far away, as if they belong to someone else.

speaker: %u
content: <size=36>Just</size><size=35>...</size> <size=34>please</size> <size=33>check</size> <size=32>on</size> <size=31>Jasmine</size> <size=30>for</size> <size=29>me.</size> <size=28>I'll</size><size=27>...</size> <size=26>leave</size> <size=25>her</size> <size=24>in</size> <size=23>your</size> <size=22>hands</size><size=21>...</size>

speaker: Nurse
content: You don't even need to ask! Chief, worry about yourself right now. Save your strength. We're prepping for surgery. Let me administer the—

speaker: Jasmine
content: Stay Back!

Jasmine violently slaps the nurse's hand aside. She reacts with fierce alarm to the sharp needle coming near you, arching her back like a lioness guarding your bed, utterly oblivious to how terrified and fragile she appears.

speaker: Jasmine
content: He went to that place and this is what happened... Those Rancors did this. Those Disian blades hurt him... Not a single good person here. No one can be trusted... Anything I have, you people just take and take and—
female_content: She went to that place and this is what happened... Those Rancors did this. Those Disian blades hurt her... Not a single good person here. No one can be trusted... Anything I have, you people just take and take and—

speaker: Jasmine
content: STAY BACK!! Don't you dare touch him!!
female_content: STAY BACK!! Don't you dare touch her!!

speaker: Nurse
content: What are you saying?! Chief needs surgery right now! His fever's already at 41! Do you want to watch him lose a limb?!
female_content: What are you saying?! Chief needs surgery right now! Her fever's already at 41! Do you want to watch her lose a limb?!

content: The words jolt through her like an electric shock. All the color drains from her face, and though no sound escapes her lips, she refuses to step back.

speaker: %u
content: Jasmine...
You force out a thin, broken whisper. It reaches her.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Chief!
In an instant, she snaps back to herself, pressing close and gripping your hand. The rest of the world falls away.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Does it still hurt? Here... let me hold you. I'll draw the fever into me, then it won't burn you anymore. ...Is that a little better?

speaker: Jasmine
content: I'm right here. Jasmine's right here. I won't let any of them near you again, not one step closer. I won't let anything hurt you ever again. Your face is so pale... Would you take my blood? You can have all of it. Please...

Before you, Jasmine's silhouette blurs and sways like a mirage. Her eyes, flooded with tears, hold yours with an aching urgency. Hatred has been washed clean from those depths; what remains is vast, unguarded fear and sorrow. She cannot bring herself to step away, afraid that one blink is all it would take to lose someone she holds dear again.
Through you, who is she really seeing? How many beloved faces has she watched disappear in agony, ripped from her grasp one by one?

speaker: Jasmine
content: Please... say something. Just tell me what to do. Anything... please...

You ache to answer her. But the fever and the relentless pain consume you whole. Your body and mind are slowly coming undone, drifting away from each other. Your sight goes dark at the edges, and then everything fades.

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...Don't close your eyes. Please... please don't close your eyes... Chief!

speaker: Jasmine
content: Get away! I told you, stay back! Mm—!
A hand grabs Jasmine and spins her around. Fury flares in her chest, ready to ignite, only to be smothered by a rebuke far sharper than the one she was about to deliver.

speaker: Wynn
content: Enough, Jasmine! Scratching and clawing around him like that won't fix anything. Chief's practically foaming at the mouth! Here, feel this. Colder than your hands, right? If you want him to wake up, then use the fever patch. You won't let us touch him? Fine. You do it!
female_content: Enough, Jasmine! Scratching and clawing around her like that won't fix anything. Chief's practically foaming at the mouth! Here, feel this. Colder than your hands, right? If you want her to wake up, then use the fever patch. You won't let us touch her? Fine. You do it!

content: Something ice-cold slaps into Jasmine's palm. She flinches, and her vision clears just enough to see a familiar face. It's someone who works with ${PlayerName}. The girl grips Jasmine firmly by the shoulders, holding her steady.

speaker: Wynn
content: I know you understand me, Jasmine. You're not actually a cat. You're smart. So listen. Really listen! This wound would've killed any desert bandit by now, and Chief's in worse shape than they are. That field first aid of yours won't save him.
female_content: I know you understand me, Jasmine. You're not actually a cat. You're smart. So listen. Really listen! This wound would've killed any desert bandit by now, and Chief's in worse shape than they are. That field first aid of yours won't save her.

speaker: Wynn
content: He needs surgery. Surgery. You know what that means? A whole team working on him, real experts. And we are running out of time! So you are going to help, right now!
female_content: She needs surgery. Surgery. You know what that means? A whole team working on her, real experts. And we are running out of time! So you are going to help, right now!

speaker: Wynn
content: You're not the only person who cares about Chief. He matters to all of us. If we waste any more time, he's going to die. And if <color=#fb9259>he dies</color>, I will <size=45>NEVER</size> <size=50>EVER</size> forgive you!
female_content: You're not the only person who cares about Chief. She matters to all of us. If we waste any more time, she's going to die. And if <color=#fb9259>she dies</color>, I will <size=45>NEVER</size> <size=50>EVER</size> forgive you!

content: The words hit like a thunderclap. Jasmine stands frozen, rooted to the spot. After a long silence, she speaks, her voice hollow and dry.

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...He's going to die...? He won't come back? Even he will...?
female_content: ...She's going to die...? She won't come back? Even she will...?

content: She glances at Wynn, then at you, and suddenly all the strength drains from her body.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Sob... no... no, please... My blades. Where are my blades... Say something... Someone save him... please save him...
female_content: Sob... no... no, please... My blades. Where are my blades... Say something... Someone save her... please save her...

content: Whimpering, she reaches out blindly. The ice pack slips from her grasp and hits the floor, leaving her hands empty, clutching at nothing. She curls in on herself, covering her eyes, unable to look at you or draw close. Slowly, she edges backward, trying to disappear into the shadows.

speaker: Jasmine
content: It's all my fault... What am I supposed to do...? My blades aren't here... I don't know what to do...
A flicker of panic crosses Wynn's face too. She quickly takes Jasmine's hand, then opens her arms and pulls her into a tight embrace.

speaker: Wynn
content: What good are those blades supposed to do? Here, I'll teach you. The doctors will handle the surgery. Your job is to hold Chief's hand. Give him strength. Help him pull through. Okay?
female_content: What good are those blades supposed to do? Here, I'll teach you. The doctors will handle the surgery. Your job is to hold Chief's hand. Give her strength. Help her pull through. Okay?

speaker: Wynn
content: Well, it's... it's not really that bad. The doctors here are amazing. Chief's body might, maybe, possibly, probably be stronger than it used to be? And more than anything... what you feel for Chief is the real miracle right there.

speaker: Eugene
content: ...That's all made-up TV drama stuff. Surgery requires a sterile environment. Ow!
Wynn kicks him sharply in the shin. The nurse is back too, jumping into the conversation with a huff.

speaker: Nurse
content: The attending physician just called. He's on his way, and he said if Jasmine wants to stay, it might actually be better. Could be a real opportunity. We just need to manage the sterilization.

speaker: Nurse
content: But once the surgery begins, ${PlayerName} may bleed. There could be emergencies. We can handle all of that, but it won't be easy to watch. Can you stay calm through it?

speaker: Nurse
content: If you have another outburst then, you could really hurt ${PlayerName}. Can you keep yourself under control? Do you trust yourself to do that?

She turns to Jasmine, all traces of their earlier argument gone. Her gaze is steady and grave now, fixed on Jasmine's eyes. She is waiting for an answer, one that comes from a responsible human being.
[Black Screen]

speaker: Nurse
content: BP, heart rate... defibrillator on standby, compression device ready, prepare for intubation...

speaker: Nurse
content: Is the patient still stable?
[Black Screen]

Jasmine doesn't remain inside. She makes the choice to leave the operating room herself, but she doesn't wander far. She stays just out the door, where she crouches low, her spine pressed against the seam of the doorframe.

Wynn settles an arm around her shoulders, soothing her with a low, steady voice. Eugene keeps vigil close by, relaying requests back and forth over comms—water, blankets, medicine to calm Jasmine's nerves.

speaker: Wynn
content: It's okay. It's going to be okay. They've handled far worse than this. He'll pull through...
female_content: It's okay. It's going to be okay. They've handled far worse than this. She'll pull through...

speaker: Jasmine
content: I'm sorry... I'm really sorry...
The Rancor is gone. Her hands can no longer grip the blades. This time, someone else reaches for her icy fingers instead, gripping them hard, holding on with all their strength.
(Surgery Sound: Beep————)
[Black Screen]

Three Days
After Returning the Rancor

You open your eyes. The surgery is behind you now, with no surprises, no complications, a success as assured as the sunrise. You even managed a few untroubled dreams, the first in what feels like forever.
The visitors are many. FAC veterans, the Bureau's youngest Sinners, even friends with their pets in tow. You have seen a whole spectrum of people, one after another.
It wears on you a little, if you're honest. But every single visit is rooted in pure goodwill, so you welcome them all without complaint.
You hope, more than anything, that Jasmine sees it, that she can feel even a fraction of that warmth.

speaker: Doctor
content: We're still trying not to trigger her. While you've been out, Jasmine's had Wynn and the others keeping her company. She's talking to a few people now, even expressing her needs on her own... She's working on reconnecting. It's a world apart from where she was.

speaker: Doctor
content: She actually asked for more treatment options. Said she wants to get better faster... Whatever you call it, she's searching for ways to quiet the pain that don't involve revenge. And she's stopped pushing everyone away.

speaker: Doctor
content: You did it, Chief. That's no small thing.
...Did I?
You glance back. Jasmine is there, tucked into the corner of the sofa. She's drawn up so small, so tight, until her eyes find yours.
Eyes meeting, no words spoken yet, she gets to her feet. And then she comes to you, compliant, as if drawn by an invisible thread.
[Black Screen Transition]

One Week
After Returning the Rancor

One by one, the promises between the two of you are being kept. Sunbathing in an Eastside park, visiting hidden-gem eateries deep in the alleyways, catching glimpses of what the Outlands settlement streets look like from a distance. She says she's happy, but she always keeps herself a little apart. Perhaps she still can't quite handle being around crowds.

Every time Wynn returns from a shopping trip, she brings Jasmine clothes and accessories, insisting that now she's put down the blades, Jasmine ought to look her best. Jasmine only picks out a soft silk loungewear top. She slips it on, rubs the fabric against her cheek, and smiles, saying she really loves it. She knows exactly how to make Wynn happy.

Most of the time, she stays in your office while you work, keeping you company. She no longer acts out for attention, no longer stirs up mischief. She's friendly and polite to everyone now. She doesn't push water glasses off your desk anymore, doesn't sneak glances at your terminal or files.

She still wakes in the middle of the night, haunted by nightmares, but when you call her name, she no longer struggles or tries to flee. She makes an effort to stay within your sight and calm herself down. The next day, she seeks out the doctor for treatment on her own.
The words she says to you most often are:
...Alright. I'll do as you say.
All of the hatred and the self-destructive pulse seem to have been wiped away, as if by someone's hand. Yet you find it hard to feel any relief.
You know the wounds are far from healed.

Two Months
After Returning the Rancor
[Bureau, alarm blaring, panicked shouting]
The alarm blares without warning. People rush through the corridors, searching for someone. You step out and stop a nurse.

speaker: Nurse
content: I'm not entirely sure. Jasmine said she wanted to spend some time with other Sinners, so I brought her over. It was going fine at first... everyone chatting and laughing.

speaker: Nurse
content: Then EMP got excited and said she wanted to throw a welcome party, a little event. She asked Jasmine to dance... and then suddenly, this.

speaker: %u
content: ...A "celebration."
You rush out immediately.
Through the swirling chaos, you trace the shackles' pull until you arrive, alone, at an empty warehouse.
No answer comes from the darkness. You know she's there, but flipping on the lights too abruptly might trigger her. You decide to try a different approach.

speaker: %u
content: That's strange. The shackles are pointing straight here, but nobody's around... Is she up high? I can't reach the shelves unless I stretch... let me just—

speaker: %u
content: Ah—ow, ow, ow...
A figure darts to your side in a flash, seizing your hand to check the old wound, only for you to catch her in return.

speaker: %u
content: Got you.
A tremor runs through her, yet she can't bring herself to fight or flee. She simply stays still in your grip, her body folding inward, shrinking.
The damp chill of her palms meets your fingers. Something tightens in your chest, and regret washes over you all at once.

speaker: %u
content: ...I'm sorry. It was meant to be a joke. I didn't mean to frighten you.

speaker: %u
content: I'm fine. You've been taking such good care of me. I was just worried.

speaker: %u
content: Are you okay, Jasmine? What happened back there...

speaker: Jasmine
content: I'm good...
After a moment, she goes on.

speaker: Jasmine
content: I'm sorry... I've caused trouble for you again. They mentioned a celebration, and I just...

speaker: Jasmine
content: No... it's not the celebration. It's not that. I'll try. I'll try harder. I'll get over this. I'll keep moving forward, I promise...

She lowers her head even further, her hands scratching at her skin uncontrollably. The dim corridor light catches scars both new and old. She scratches hard as if punishing herself, or perhaps holding something back.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Take me to the doctor... You can freeze me if you want. I don't need to wake up again... I don't want to cause any more trouble. I can't... keep going like this...
You can't find the words. Instead, you take her hand and press it firmly into your palm. A long moment passes before you force yourself to speak, the words coming out strained.
You know the truth: nothing you offer can mend what came before. She's simply remembering what it feels like to lose.

Fear swallows everything else. It's what made her let go of hatred, and what now makes her bury it inside herself, sharp edge turned inward. You've only dug deeper, uncovering wounds she'd hidden even from herself.

speaker: %u
content: This is just a small injury. I'm not going to die. And none of it is your fault. I didn't think it through. I never should have let you see something like that again.
You want to tell her you regret it.

The pain is a massive, roaring thing inside her. It howls for an exit, but finds none. And so, rather than watch her bury it deeper into herself, you'd rather she turn that blade on the world outside, let her hate the cruelty of it all, or let her hate you.

speaker: %u
content: If you're angry, then yell at me. Hit me if you have to. Lie to me, use me, manipulate me... I don't care. Throw all of it at me. I can take it.

speaker: %u
content: ...I'll be here. I'm not going anywhere.
She gazes at you, lost in a daze. The sealed chamber of her heart cracks open again at last, yet what escapes is a flood of bewilderment, fear, and restless doubt.

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...You... Why are you so kind to me?

speaker: Jasmine
content: You could've just let me go. You should've left me alone. Why do you keep holding on? If you hadn't followed me that day, I never would have—

speaker: Jasmine
content: Even if I died, it wouldn't have anything to do with you...
You remember it clearly. Just a few months ago, inside that interrogation room, when the air between you was still charged with friction, she asked you much the same question.
...That's right. Why? When did it all begin?
You hold Jasmine's gaze, and the nightmares flash before your eyes. Fear, rage, hatred, madness, the helplessness of loss, the agony of powerlessness...

speaker: %u
content: ...We're the same...
[CG Flash: Hella suffering in war]

You can bury them again and again, but seeing Jasmine always pulls them back to the surface. They stitch themselves into fresh nightmares, whispering the same truth: the war was real. It crushed everything in its path. This chapter cannot be erased.

speaker: Jasmine
content: You're lying... You're a Disian...

speaker: Jasmine
content: You're a Disian... and you're telling me we... are the same?

speaker: %u
content: You're right. I spoke out of turn. I'm sorry.
Gently, you pull her into your arms.

speaker: %u
content: We're not the same. But I have pain I can't shoulder alone either. Wounds I can't heal by myself. That's why I want you to get better.

speaker: %u
content: People heal others to heal themselves. Walk beside someone long enough, and somehow, you end up moving forward too. Like right now...

speaker: %u
content: Holding you through this... it feels like someone's holding me, too.
Her expression is hidden from you. A long stillness stretches between you before she finally speaks, her voice barely above a whisper.

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...Can it really be healed?

speaker: %u
content: I don't know, Jasmine. I don't know...

speaker: %u
content: But if it ever hurts too much, if you can't take it alone anymore... then give some of it to me...

speaker: %u
content: As long as you're alive. As long as you still want to be. Even if the road ahead is nothing but wasteland... someone will walk it with you, waiting for the flowers to grow back...
Does she understand? You don't know.
All you feel is a pair of trembling hands climbing up to your shoulders. And then...
...She holds on tight.
[Black Screen Transition]

A Long Time
After Returning the Rancor

So much has happened since then, both good and bad. Jasmine has long settled into her own room by now, the one filled with plushes from Wynn, and a little cat she's taken in. She no longer needs you there every night to feel safe.
So tonight, when she shows up at your bedside, fully dressed, quietly waiting for you to wake, it surprises you.
Once you're sure this isn't a dream, you reach out and take her hand.

options: Did you have a nightmare? Are you alright?

content: Her hand isn't as cold as before, but she still seems dazed. It takes a long while for her to speak.

speaker: Jasmine
content: I... had a dream.

speaker: Jasmine
content: I dreamed I was on stage... and I had to dance. A different kind of dance.
Her gaze is far away. Her words come so very slow.

speaker: Jasmine
content: No blades to hold. No cannons... I was at another celebration. It felt familiar, but strange too. So many eyes on me... family, guests, strangers... You were there as well, sitting with the Disians, waiting for me to dance...

speaker: Jasmine
content: But it's been so long... I've forgotten how to dance without those blades in my hands... If I stepped onto that stage now, everyone would just laugh...
A long pause. Then Jasmine lifts her eyes to yours, hesitant and uncertain.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Would you... watch me? Just... think of it as practice?
Jasmine holds your gaze as she retreats, step by slow step, to the very center of the room.

The night light is pale and thin. If you let your eyes blur, it could be moonlight slanting in, a bonfire's glow that holds the two of you within its quiet circle. Her hands rise upward, as though greeting the sky itself. Her body, soft and fluid, moves like a stream catching the moon's rippling shimmer.

There are no blades, no bloodshed, only an audience of one. The dancer closes her eyes, following a beat no one else can hear, searching through the splinters of memory to gather back the steps she thought she'd lost.
Through wind, through dust, across impossible distances, she journeys on until she reaches the buried end of time.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Let flame ignite the candles bright, to greet the seedlings in the light.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Let arrows fly to strike the mark, to hear what a grandmother's blessings impart.
[Switch Scene]

speaker: Nightingale
content: ...Chief, a confidential letter for you. It's from the farlands.

speaker: Nightingale
content: It was routed through internal channels, so security isn't an issue. But... yes, no signature.
It's not really a letter. There's no message inside. The sender seems to have nothing to say to you.
Or perhaps they believe you'll understand without needing words.
You look down at the "letter" in your hand.

speaker: %u
content: ...Notify Outland Affairs and the 9th Agency. Tell them they can call off the search.

speaker: %u
content: I know where it is. I'll find a time to go myself...
[DisCity Night View]

speaker: Jasmine
content: Let parades roll through fields so wide, and drift into sweet dreams inside. Let fireworks gleam in skies above, illuminating homes built with love.
[Scene Change: Nirvana Port]

The general of DisCity returns from another far-flung expedition. The city-state's newest war proposal goes straight into the trash, discarded without ceremony, before she makes her way back to the cemetery beyond Nirvana Port.
Dozens of new headstones have sprung up across the burial ground. Some were raised over bones she carried home herself. Others mark fresh graves, dug in the aftermath of the latest conflict.

She finds the stone bearing Arkin's name. The ones lined up beside it belong to the same group of fools who followed him into the fire. She couldn't bring them back. Maybe they wouldn't have wanted her to. Maybe they'd even call it a decent way to go.
The general gazes at them for a long, long time. Then she walks up and gives each grave a solid, brutal kick.
After that, she crouches down and leaves a few belated photographs at Arkin's grave.
[Outlands Outskirts] Apply photo/print filter
In those photos, past windswept sands, across a thousand miles, at the buried end of all things lies a valley. A battlefield long forgotten.

The years have worn everything down. Homes, fields, craters, bones... The lost village is nothing now but scattered rubble. No one ever raised a monument. Perhaps the photographer thought it would ring hollow.

So instead, she carried a pair of blades to this place—nearly shattered, barely holding together—and planted them among the ruins, at the best vantage point in the whole ruins. If there were ever celebrations here, this would have been center stage.
The blades stand there now, center stage. And then...
[Background continues, remove photo/print filter, apply dreamlike, hallucinatory filter]

From the dust, green shoots emerge. They follow the cracks along the steel, climbing, reaching upward. A new bud trembles on the verge of blooming, and it almost catches the echo of joyful voices cheering from below the stage.

speaker: Villager A
content: Jasmine... Jasmine...

speaker: Villager B
content: The celebration is right around the corner! Harvest came in full this year. And those guests from way back have come around again...

speaker: Villager B
content: They still remember the celebration. They remember your dancing... And they brought gifts, too. Said they've been meaning to return the kindness all this time.

speaker: Villager C
content: They brought gifts? Well, that makes them our friends!

The flowers bloom. Green leaves spill over the stage, burying the shattered Rancor blades, washing the devastation clean. Perhaps the fires of war never truly ignited. Sunlight breaks through the sandstorm once more, and face after face emerges through the calamity to join the celebration.

People wipe the blood from their faces. They throw their blades aside and embrace with wild laughter, drink deep, dance together, shouting at the top of their lungs in their mother tongue and in Disian:

speaker: Villager C
content: Come on, Jasmine! The celebration is starting!
[Office]
The dance ends without warning. There is no smile, no graceful bow, only a puppet whose strings have been severed. She stands hollow, adrift, in the dim room of a foreign land.

speaker: Jasmine
content: It's over...

speaker: Jasmine
content: When the celebration ends... there's really nothing left at all...

speaker: Jasmine
content: There's nothing left, Chief... None of it can ever come back...
Wordless, you step forward and gather her into your arms.

speaker: %u
content: That was a wonderful celebration. I will never forget it.

speaker: %u
content: None of us will...
Slowly, you feel dampness spread across your chest. Soft sobs reach your ears, and then at last, she breaks into full, unrestrained weeping.

speaker: Jasmine
content: ...Aah... aaaaaah...

Through the battlefields, through the nightmares, torn open by hatred and terror, the celebration, frozen in time, has at last reached its end. So much was stolen from her. She has been chasing it for so long. And now, only now, does she take the first step, recovering the first treasure she lost so long ago.
You hold her close, as tightly as you can.
The one who lost her home finally sheds her broken smile and finds her tears again. Her heart, stitched together from fragments, remembers how to grieve at last.

speaker: Jasmine
content: O traveler, when you join a celebration in a foreign land...

speaker: Jasmine
content: Brush the dust from your sleeves, raise your cup high. Let us toast this meeting. Let us savor this night. And before you depart, full of good cheer, look forward to the year ahead.

speaker: Jasmine
content: Another year... and another after that. Dear friends from afar... may we gather again.

speaker: Jasmine
content: At the next celebration, may I find you there.
[Deep Within WhiteSands]
The horizon is a blight of black debris, the air seething with violent Mania energy. Through the shroud of sand, two figures are barely visible, locked in a fierce struggle.
The enemy's power is absolute; a lapse in focus would mean death. The woman, however, shows no fear, her entire being focused on a relentless, vicious assault.
So what you want is... my arm?

In the chaos of the storm, a massive boulder slams into her, crushing her to the earth. As the monster channels more power into the stone, its weight multiplies, and the sickening creak of her collarbone echoes beneath the crushing force.
Hahaha! You're full of surprises! This is my kind of fun!
She mocks, the words barely spoken before she shoves the immense rock away and launches herself back into the fray.
Her next strike finds its mark. She drives her claws deep into the monster's flesh and savagely rips its arm from the socket.
An agonized roar rips from the monster as it uses its other arm to fling her away. She tumbles through the air before smashing into a far-off dune.
The giant Apostle of Ashes does not give chase. The turbulent Mania fades, and a heavy silence falls over WhiteSands.
Moments later, the sand shifts. The woman's head pops out, and she spits vigorously.
Ptooey ptooey! Now that was a rush. Sure, I lost the fight, but winning an arm? I'd call that a fair trade.
She scrambles free, snatches the torn limb, and tears into it with ravenous hunger.

A soft wind blows across the dunes, and in response, several Alchemic Beasts poke their heads from the sand. They scuttle from their holes to scour the battlefield, meticulously collecting the scattered particles of Aurum Secretum left behind.
The footage freezes. The officer stops the recording and zooms in, ensuring every person in the room has a perfect, clear view of the woman's face and the horrific act she is committing.
[Inside the Search Vessel]

speaker: 9th Agency Officer
content: Report to MBCC: Initial verification is complete. The woman in the footage is Synex, a former shadow operative for the Campbell family. We have confirmed her involvement in dozens of serious crimes linked to the Campbells.

speaker: 9th Agency Officer
content: An arrest warrant was issued ten days ago. While initial intelligence placed her in WhiteSands, her movements were elusive. Our searches yielded only fragmentary clues until approximately one hour ago, when we captured this relatively clear footage.

speaker: 9th Agency Officer
content: The footage confirms our initial theory. She is in WhiteSands to hunt Apostles of Ashes and extract Aurum Secretum. Both she and her Alchemic Beasts feed on the particles produced by these Apostles.

speaker: 9th Agency Agent
content: ...Beyond these basic facts, I'd like to offer you a further analysis of the situation, if I may.

speaker: 9th Agency Agent
content: Recently, we've detected significant Apostle of Ashes activity near the coordinates in the footage. If our target is hunting them, her camp is likely in that vicinity.

speaker: 9th Agency Agent
content: Furthermore, Alchemic Beasts are not long-lived, and our target shows no ability to heal them.

speaker: 9th Agency Agent
content: The ones accompanying her are clearly in the final stages of their lifecycle, with severely diminished mobility. Creatures in that condition couldn't travel far. A nearby camp would explain the concentrated activity we've observed.

speaker: 9th Agency Agent
content: That concludes our evidence and analysis. We await your instructions: to continue direct tracking, or to focus our search for her lair in WhiteSands. End of report.
The communicator flashes blue—signal received—just as the vessel status monitor blinks a warning red.

speaker: 9th Agency Agent
content: Hmm? Something's wrong.

speaker: 9th Agency Agent
content: I'll go check it out. All of you stay right here.
[WhiteSands Exterior]
The hatch hisses open, and a scorching, sand-laden blast strikes the agent full in the face. Staggered, he instinctively stumbles back a few steps.

The entire stern of the search vessel is split open by a colossal tear. Through it, the desert winds howl, whipping sand into the compartment. The metal hull, once impregnable, is now a wound of twisted shards, its edges jutting inward like rusty fangs.

speaker: 9th Agency Agent
content: The hull was reinforced just weeks ago... How is this even possible? What could have done this?

speaker: 9th Agency Agent
content: Sand beasts? No... impossible. Nothing out there has this kind of destructive power.
The agent crouches down to examine the torn metal edges more closely.
At that exact moment, a powerful force strikes from behind. Before the agent can react, sharp claws pin him against the torn metal floor.

speaker: Synex
content: Well, well. You managed to track me down, but skimped on the security measures. How... disappointing.

speaker: Synex
content: Seems the 9th Agency doesn't value your lives very much. Your training doesn't seem too thorough, either.

speaker: Synex
content: Oh dear, what a predicament! You came to investigate all alone, only to be ambushed by the big, bad monster. Should you call your friends to join our little party?

speaker: 9th Agency Agent
content: Intruder! We need backup now!

speaker: 9th Agency Officer
content: It's Synex! Quick, take her down!

speaker: Synex
content: Hahahaha! You? Here? You think you can catch ME?!
Her form vanishes, leaving only her wild, echoing laughter in its wake.

Close combat is Synex's domain. She blurs through a storm of gunfire, closing in on each arriving crew member. With every fluid motion, her claws find their mark, precisely piercing another operative's arm.
This isn't combat. It's a bloody hunt.

speaker: 9th Agency Agent
content: Damn it! At this rate...
[Inside the Sand Ship]
The agent staggers back into the cabin and frantically punches a code into the control panel.
The indicator light shifts from red to green—distress signal sent. But they are deep in WhiteSands territory; reinforcements are at least twenty minutes out.

speaker: Synex
content: Oh, there you are!
The cabin door bursts open again. Framed in the doorway stands the woman, now drenched in blood. The agent can only stare, all strength to fight back gone.

speaker: Synex
content: What's that on the panel, a distress signal? Hahaha! Go on, tell me. Who's coming to hunt me down this time?
A gleeful smile on her lips, the woman grips the agent's throat and effortlessly hoists them into the air.

speaker: Synex
content: What about you? Should I keep you alive until help arrives? ...Hmm, guess what kind of mood I'm in today?

speaker: 9th Agency Agent
content: Cough... cough...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Synex, let him go.

speaker: Synex
content: Hmm...?
At the sound of your voice, Synex freezes. She drops the agent and scans the room, her gaze finally locking onto a communication device.

speaker: Synex
content: Oh, it's ${PlayerName}. How unfortunate that our reunion happens over a distress call, of all things.

speaker: Synex
content: I don't mind sparing these pathetic lives. But, my dear MBCC Chief... what will you offer me in return?

speaker: Option
options: A life for a life. What do you say?

speaker: Synex
content: Yours? And what exactly would I want with your life?

speaker: Option
options: We can help treat the aftereffects of your Aurum Secretum infection.

content: Her expression freezes in shock, but it lasts only a second. Soon, her cunning red eyes narrow.

speaker: Synex
content: ...You've found a clever angle. Let's hear it.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I know why you attacked. The agents on the search vessel captured footage of you and located your camp, the one you share with the Alchemic Beasts. You're protecting them.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But you've misunderstood. We aren't your enemies, and we never mean to harm the Alchemic Beasts in your care. I know your condition. You need regular doses of Aurum Secretum to survive. That's why you hunt the Apostles.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Come to DisCity. The Bureau can provide proper treatment. We can find a way to extend your lives.

speaker: Synex
content: Let me get this straight. I release these poor saps, and in return, DisCity welcomes us "monsters" with open arms and a miracle cure?
From the other end of the line, Synex suddenly erupts into raucous laughter, her voice distorting from the volume.

speaker: Synex
content: HAHAHAHA!! Do you high-and-mighty types order your lies in bulk? Adelaide fed me the same line, back in the day.

speaker: Synex
content: But thanks for the offer. I won't be taking it. Keep your fancy new leash. Maybe you should try wearing it yourself.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm not lying to you, Syn—
Your words fail to reach her. A sharp explosion blasts from the communicator, the screen flashes crimson, and the speaker dies into a deep, hollow hum.
[MBCC Office]
Nightingale, log the coordinates of that distress signal and notify the relevant departments. I need more intel, and I need it fast.
If necessary, I'll go to WhiteSands myself.

speaker: 9th Agency Agent
content: The intel collection on target Synex is complete, Chief. Here is the operation report for your review.

speaker: 9th Agency Agent
content: As you predicted, we found extensive evidence of combat between humans and the Apostles of Ashes in the heart of WhiteSands. Several sites contained scattered Aurum Secretum fragments. By analyzing the age and distribution of these traces, we've pinpointed the target's encampment. The coordinates are on the final page.
What about the search vessel? Did you find it? Were there any survivors?
The agent shakes his head, his expression darkening.

speaker: 9th Agency Agent
content: No... we went back to check. The ship was completely empty.

speaker: 9th Agency Agent
content: Not only were there no survivors... but everything on board—resources, files, equipment—was torn to shreds by that woman. ...There was nothing left to return to their families.
...I see. Thank you for your efforts. I'll add this to the records.
As the agent departs, you massage the bridge of your nose and turn your attention to the report.
To your surprise, it contains more leads than you expected. Synex isn't even trying to conceal her whereabouts; finding her will be the easy part.
...The real problem is what comes next. When you find her, a brutal confrontation is inevitable.
[Flashback: Hella vs Synex Confrontation CG + Restraint CG]

speaker: Nightingale
content: ...Chief, I must advise against this. Reviewing the intelligence and combat footage, this operation presents a significant level of risk.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Are you certain you want to proceed without any Sinners?
Aurum Secretum's effects on Sinners are still too unpredictable. And... given Synex's history of wariness and hostility, arriving without a show of force might make her less likely to attack.
Just like she did with Hella back then.

After all, she was the one who came to your and Hecate's aid at the edge of the Black Ring. In a way, this explains the peculiar friendliness she shows you now... or whatever this particular interest of hers might be.
I'll have a tactical team on standby for immediate support if it's needed. Besides, I still have the shackles.

speaker: Nightingale
content: ...Understood. I trust your judgment, Chief. Please proceed with extreme caution.
[WhiteSands]
On the day of the operation, WhiteSands is unnaturally still. Not only have the sandstorms ceased, but the very traces of Mania that usually permeate the air have vanished entirely.

speaker: Escort Soldier
content: We've got a new lead, Chief. Look here.
Through the binoculars, the withered oasis in the distance looks like a forgotten grave. Broken logs lie stacked by a dried-up riverbed, reminiscent of a traveler's long-dead campfire.
Nearby, several dark creatures crouch in kneeling postures, while others twist and writhe on the ground, their forms so distorted it's impossible to discern their actions.
Are these bizarre movements just a part of their existence? Lowering the binoculars, you are lost in thought.
If the Alchemic Beasts are here, this is the place. They don't seem aggressive, but that doesn't confirm our target's presence.
Synex rarely travels without them. If they're here, she's likely in that camp.
I'm going in.

speaker: Escort Soldier
content: Chief, it's our duty to protect you. Please allow us to accompany you!

Hold your position within firing range. Do not advance any closer. Synex isn't like our other targets; she'll kill anyone who bores her without a second thought. If you get too close, there will be too many of you for me to protect.
With your backup team in position, you jump from the sand ship.
As you slowly approach the camp, an even more disturbing scene unfolds before your eyes.
Synex is hunched on the sand, crouched over the hollowed-out husk of a dead Alchemic Beast—its body glittering with infused Aurum Secretum.

She gnaws at the shell, then delicately licks up the crumbling Aurum Secretum fragments. The act is a horrifying contradiction: part savage tearing, part intimate kiss. She works methodically, from the head down the neck and chest, devouring the shell inch by inch until nothing remains.

Encircling them, other Alchemic Beasts sit in a macabre audience, their severely distorted bodies hunched forward, struggling to maintain their kneeling position. Their vacant eyes are fixed ahead, as if attending a sacred, solemn ritual.
As she swallows the Aurum Secretum, traces of frenzy ripple across her skin, a visible sign of the power being digested and resonating within her body.

speaker: Escort Soldier
content: Chief, we have Synex in our sights. Her energy signature is rapidly expanding. We need to interrupt her feeding immediately! Permission to open fire.
...Ungh!
You are on the verge of giving the order when a sharp resonance lances through your mind like a blade.
You grit your teeth, enduring the agony, and as it subsides, you find yourself staring directly into the eyes of an Alchemic Beast across the expanse.

speaker: Synex
content: ...Hmm? Oh?
Synex has sensed the connection, too. She lifts her head, her gaze piercing the distance to find your exact position. A faint, knowing smile flickers at the corner of her mouth.

The Aurum Secretum she just consumed now flows beneath her skin, forming shifting, golden patterns. You can feel the violent Mania radiating from her, a field many times stronger than during your last encounter.

speaker: Escort Soldier
content: Danger! Cover the Chief!
The warning from your communicator is instantly drowned by the eruption of heavy gunfire.
The specially enhanced bullets find their mark, ripping bloody wounds across Synex's body, yet she remains utterly unfazed, charging directly toward you.

speaker: Synex
content: Haha... hahaha! Stationed soldiers at a distance, did you? Oh, your ammo's a bit stronger now, but it's still pathetically weak!

speaker: Synex
content: ${PlayerName}, you don't seriously think these bullets can hurt me, do you?
You raise your hand with lightning speed, but her ferocious strike is faster.
What—
The powerful blow connects with your chest. Under the crushing force, a deafening ring in your ears swallows all other sound, and the world before you fades to black.
[Black Screen]
You have no idea how long you've been unconscious. In your dreamlike state, strange noises begin to emerge...
Coo coo...
Mmm... coo?
Mmm... coo coo coo coo...
[WhiteSands Cave]
You open your eyes to find a grotesquely twisted Alchemic Beast staring at you, its head tilted to one side.
What... is this?
As far as you can tell, you're in a cave. Synex has bound your limbs tightly, and several Alchemic Beasts stand guard around you, likely left behind as your captors.
The Alchemic Beasts remain silent, tilting their heads in unison. You suddenly realize their gaze is fixed on something behind you.
According to the reports, deeply mutated Alchemic Beasts lose all cognitive function. They're no different from wild animals. Trying to get information from them would be a waste of time.

speaker: Synex
content: Well, well! My little trophy is finally awake.

A woman's voice echoes from outside. Synex saunters in, the soft swish of her dress accompanying her approach before she crouches directly in front of you. Her hand reaches out, gripping your jaw and forcing your gaze up to meet hers.

speaker: Synex
content: Did you sleep well?
You notice her tail swishing gently behind her, a clear sign of her amusement.

speaker: Synex
content: Our little encounters are always so... rushed. Never any time for a proper chat. I was hoping to see what you're really made of. But you're so... disappointing. Maybe that rumor is true after all. The Devil Wears Gray Coat is nothing without the shackles?
I told you before, Synex. The Bureau's goal was never to lock you up. We're trying to find a cure. To help you, and others like you, survive.
Synex's grip tightens incrementally, her eyes savoring every twitch of pain that contorts your features.

speaker: Synex
content: I've killed a lot of people. DisCity executives, Fraser hounds, government spies... You can't possibly think I'd walk out of a Bureau cell alive.

speaker: Synex
content: Oh, wait. I forgot. You have your own little Luminaris Society, don't you? The "Ring Research Institute." That's the real plan, isn't it? Hand me over to them. Let them dissect me, experiment on me... see how your Hypercube tech stacks up against Aurum Secretum for your next war.
Killing you solves nothing. We know Aurum Secretum was developed by the Underground and Fraser. In the end, test subjects like you are victims, not criminals.

Settling a score with you is the least of our priorities. We have bigger things to deal with: the BR-005 incident, the true nature of the Famine, arranging rescue for the other test subjects... That's just the start of the list.

But I suspect you don't care about any of that. So let me give you a more personal reason. You "helped" us outside the Black Ring, and you're Hella's "friend"... so I will do everything in my power to keep you alive.

speaker: Synex
content: Ohhh, aren't you clever? Using my sweet little Hella as bait.

speaker: Synex
content: I take it back. Even without your shackles, the Devil Wears Gray Coat still has a silver tongue.

speaker: Synex
content: Sure, I want to live. But if survival means becoming your pet, I'd rather take my chances in WhiteSand. Fighting Apostles, causing trouble... occasionally kidnapping a Chief for fun. Now that's a fulfilling existence.
If you don't care about your own life, what about the others? The other test subjects? Have you considered what they want? Maybe they actually want to survive.

speaker: Synex
content: Them? Survive?
Synex throws her head back and laughs, a sharp, mocking sound as if you'd just told the world's most hilarious joke.

speaker: Synex
