For me... it's kinda like how people feel about the White Tiger Mountain Lord. The way they believe in them and trust them. I've also got people who care about me, people who expect things from me.
It's heavy sometimes. Yeah. But... for the ones who believe in me, I'll carry it.
You meet Xiaofeng's eyes.
Maybe it's the same for the Mountain Lord. Doesn't mean you gotta get all tangled up with everyone. Maybe it's just... you grab an offering when you're passing by and lend a hand when it's easy.
Even if you're not really thinking about it... to the folks living down below, that's a miracle. A god reaching down and touching their lives.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Tch. Sappy nonsense.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Ugh, I knew we'd never see eye to eye. You humans are all the same. Maybe you can't throw a punch worth a damn, but every single one of you can talk circles around anyone. One slip and I walk right into it...

Xiaofeng polishes off the last piece of jerky, brushes her hands clean, and rises to her feet. You cannot see her face, but those fluffy ears of hers twitch once, then again. You swallow any teasing words before they can escape. You have finally reached this "deity," and you refuse to undo that now.
Together, you walk with Xiaofeng toward the edge of the venue, where Nightingale stands waiting.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, the ship back to Eastia is ready.

Xiaofeng summons the white tiger to her side. The majestic creature takes its place behind her, its fur now decorated with seven or eight red strings—bright little knots tied by the eager hands of a few young Sinners. The effect is at once regal and completely absurd.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: What? You jealous? Wanna tie one on yourself? Something to remember us by in case you miss us.
You step forward, but rather than tying something on, you toss a bundle her way. Xiaofeng catches it without effort.
Then, Mountain Lord, please watch over me from now on.
I'll pass. The Mountain Lord's protection's a little too good. I'd need to give a way better offering.
You step forward, but rather than tying something on, you toss a bundle her way. Xiaofeng catches it without effort.

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: This is...?
It's silvervine branches. You have had them gathered specially—whole stems, still intact, tied together in a neat bundle with red string.
Consider it a keepsake. Take the main road next time, okay? This visit was too rushed. I couldn't show you around properly. But DisCity's got plenty worth seeing.
Besides, you like stories, right? Operas? I've picked up a few over the years. Why settle for secondhand when you can hear them straight from the source?
So... if you ever feel like swinging by DisCity again, come find me. Anywhere you wanna go, I'll show you.
Xiaofeng hesitates for just a moment. She offers no words, but after a few strides, her hand lifts in a lazy wave over her shoulder. That's her own way of saying goodbye.
The bundle of silvervine swings at her side, and the little golden tiger claw on her pinky sways with the motion, catching the light and scattering it in brief, bright glimmers.
A tiger's roar rings out as the golden gleam fades along with her retreating silhouette. You know exactly what she means:
Until we meet again.
[Flashback Fragment: Market Below the Mountain]
The sun danced in her cup, the light rippling with a gentle tremor. She had been staring at it for a while now.

This was her first time descending to the world below. She'd heard the girl speak of this place often enough, but that was years ago now, before the bitterness of their parting had settled in. She hadn't been back to the White Tiger Temple since that day, and she hadn't seen that herb-gathering girl again.

The food on the mountain was bland, and no matter how carefully she tried, she could never get the meat to sear quite right. Eventually, she'd decided to throw on her cloak and go down, slipping into the human market just to scratch that particular itch.

The mortal world buzzed around her, a thicket of overlapping chatter. In the span of a glance, she knocked back a mouthful of liquor and propped her head in her hand, listening to the spinning of yet another tall tale.

speaker: Villager 1
content: I heard that the tiger came right off the mountain and ripped those bandits to shreds! Ate 'em up, one by one! Tsk, tsk, tsk... Blood everywhere, nasty stuff!

speaker: Villager 2
content: Shh! Keep your voice down, will ya? The gods are always watching, and the White Tiger Temple's right there! You're gonna bring a curse down on us, bad-mouthing the Mountain Lord like that...

speaker: Villager 1
content: Hey, it's a tiger! Tigers eat folks. That's just how it goes! But you gotta admit, the trails up there have been way safer lately. Do you think...
She let out a short scoff and washed the last bite of meat down with her liquor. She was just pushing back from the table when a familiar voice cut through the din.

speaker: Herb-Gathering Girl
content: That's a load of nonsense! The deity would never eat people!

speaker: Villager 1
content: Wha—you... Don't go spouting off, girl. What, you see it happen yourself or something?

speaker: Herb-Gathering Girl
content: Yeah! I did see it myself!
The girl, usually so gentle of speech, abruptly lifted her voice. Never before had she spoken with such volume; though it quavered, she compelled it to steadiness.

speaker: Herb-Gathering Girl
content: It was her... The Tiger Deity saved me! She chased off those thieving scoundrels. The White Tiger Mountain Lord's not just some old story. She's real, and she's a real deity!

speaker: Villager 2
content: But... it's still a tiger...

speaker: Herb-Gathering Girl
content: Who cares if she's got fur or not! If she's doing good and saving folks, then she's a proper deity!

The girl stubbornly pressed on with her argument. Meanwhile, the figure beneath the cloak pursed her lips slightly and rose amid the commotion, only to be halted by the restaurant owner demanding payment.

speaker: Restaurant Owner
content: Let's see here... one plate of marinated beef, two cups of liquor... that'll be one qian of silver! Say, I don't recognize your face. You got a name, traveler?
The cloaked figure stopped short.
Her eyes found the White Tiger Temple at the entrance, where incense offerings had been thriving these days. A cluster of villagers moved to and fro, fixing a new couplet above the gate.

She let out a soft chuckle. The flowing black characters on the red paper meant nothing to her. She could not read a single stroke, but she had heard people recite the words before, whenever she slipped down the mountain for a taste of liquor.
Untamed roar echoes across the peaks for those who pray. The mountain lord guards all who dwell below, where the gale reach.
It honored the Tiger Deity, the Mountain Lord.
What a shame, then, that no such deity guarded those heights. Deep in the mountains there was only a white tiger, and a woman the tiger had raised, mistaken by all for the Mountain Lord.

Humans fascinated her. So fragile, so fleeting—barely able to cling to life on their own—so they prayed to gods and ghosts, begging for a helping hand. And yet they never begged for much. They just handed their wishes and their hopes over to something bigger than themselves.
"Not seeking glory or a name in history, only peace, good fortune, and a life free of worry."

Wish after wish, prayer after prayer, they braided themselves together. They took shape in the roast chicken sold at the corner, the liquor pooled in clay bowls, the gold trinkets woven into hair, the red strings knotted around wrists.
They became all those scattered lights burning across the world below the mountain—the brilliant, chaotic tapestry of mortal life.
The roaring gale... Xiao... Feng... Heh, I like that.

She still would not say she liked humans, nor did she wish to play the benevolent deity. But the world below was lively, and she did not mind visiting from time to time... And perhaps, on occasion, she might lend a hand to a few little ones who ventured down the mountain alongside her.
The woman raised her hand and lifted back her cloak. Born and raised by white tigers, she had no name. But since she was entering the mortal world, she might as well do as mortals did—

speaker: Xiaofeng
content: Just call me <color=#fb9259>Xiaofeng</color>.

MBCC
Chief's Office

You're enjoying a pleasant day at the Bureau. Work has wrapped up for now, and Wuhuanzi has just brought you fresh tea, the boiling tea still making wisps of steam in the teapot. Sipping the piping hot brew, you leisurely while away the final moments of your workday.

speaker: Chief
content: Hm? What's this...

You glance down at your tea. Emerald buds settle in a loose pile at the bottom of the cup, and among them, a single tea stem floats upright in the water. You remember hearing from a Sinner that a standing tea stem is a sign of good luck.

speaker: Chief
content: Good luck is welcome, of course. But honestly, I'd be perfectly content if the next few days stayed as peaceful as today.
Maybe you could leave early today, take a stroll around the grounds. Nightingale mentioned the flowers around the Bureau are in full bloom, and you haven't had a chance to see them yet...
Just as you're making up your mind, a series of panicked screams and a deafening engine roar suddenly assault your eardrums.
Instinct kicks in and you dive right. The next instant, a car smashes through a wall of the Bureau building, blasting a gaping hole into it!
Cough, cough... Oh no, oh no, they're gonna make me pay for this again, aren't they...
You're still holding that steaming cup of tea, eyes widening in shock. After a moment, a familiar mop of red hair pokes through the hole in the wall.

speaker: Murphy
content: Hey there, Chief... Looks like we've... run into each other again.
(Transition)
Some ten minutes later, you bring this uninvited guest to the interrogation room.

To accommodate this guest with such unique abilities, Nightingale has called for an urgent reinforcement of the interrogation room and removed all sharp objects that might turn hazardous under Murphy's influence.
You silently pray that aside from that gaping hole in the wall, no further damage will be done today.
You refill your own tea and pour one for Murphy as well.

speaker: Murphy
content: Wow, Chief, this tea stem in your cup is standing up! Could this be... the rumored sign of good luck? Does that mean I'm your lucky star today?

speaker: Chief
content: Good luck? All I see is the Goddess of Bad Luck I just saw off making her grand return.

speaker: Murphy
content: Heh heh heh... Well, it's also possible that my arrival scared the tea leaves so badly they're all standing up! Pretty impressive, huh?

speaker: Murphy
content: Hold on... hold on! I... I was just trying to lighten the mood, you know! Actually, I've just returned to my job at the Public Security Bureau's information desk. You see, I'm a perfect, law-abiding citizen!

After the previous incident, Murphy completed a simple registration and vanished. The city arrest team managed to track her down several times despite considerable difficulty, but every attempt to detain her ended in some sort of mishap. Somehow, she always slips out of the Bureau's grip.

speaker: Chief
content: Didn't you go home after registering with the MBCC? Why have you been wandering around again? I've been getting a ton of Mania alerts, and every single one turned out to be you.

speaker: Murphy
content: Ahaha... Well, something went wrong with my car again... If it hadn't run out of power and fuel, I bet it would have driven itself all the way to WhiteSands!

speaker: Murphy
content: So after I got the car fixed, I figured, if I couldn't go back to Eastside... I could just become a delivery person or something in WhiteSands instead! Thought I could at least make a living!

speaker: Chief
content: I've always admired your optimism...

speaker: Murphy
content: Then a few days later, I found out that my arrest order had apparently been retracted! So I went back to Eastside...

speaker: Murphy
content: Though my coworkers seem to look at me a bit differently now... well, overall, my life hasn't changed that much compared to before!

The little disaster magnet is just as oblivious as ever. You let out a helpless sigh. The arrest order was retracted because you had confirmed Murphy's identity and verified that her special power posed no threat to public safety, aside from the harm she caused herself.

options: So what brought you to the Bureau today?

speaker: Murphy
content: Hmm, I just wanted to drop by and catch up with you and everyone else?
You raise your hand expressionlessly once more.

speaker: Murphy
content: Okay, okay, I get it!
She fidgets nervously, poking her fingers together as if trying to figure out where to begin.

speaker: Murphy
content: Okay then... Be prepared for the long story.
You nod, gesturing for her to begin.

speaker: Murphy
content: During those few days I was hiding around WhiteSands, I actually discovered a pattern to my bad luck!
You point in the direction of the wall Murphy just crashed through.

speaker: Murphy
content: Hey... No, I'm serious! This time was just an accident! Let me tell you all about it...
[Insert Flashback]

speaker: Murphy
content: Spilled milk three times, broke my charger twice... but I won a third prize in a lucky draw! Sure, it's only a third prize... but that still counts as good luck, right?

speaker: Murphy
content: Computer crashed three times, replaced two hard drives... but today, before it rained, I actually remembered to bring in my laundry! That's a first!

speaker: Murphy
content: Hmm... Before, my life had been filled only with bad luck, but somehow I won a prize just a while ago?! A PRIZE! That had seriously never happened in my entire life!

speaker: Murphy
content: Could it be...

Murphy scribbled away in her notebook. As she meticulously documented every trivial detail of her daily life, she seemed convinced she had uncovered the ultimate secret behind her luck. Even in the dim, suffocating cubicle, she became fired up with enthusiasm.
[End of Flashback]

speaker: Murphy
content: So, my guess is... my natural bad luck must have evolved!

speaker: Chief
content: ...I'm pretty sure that's just the normal everyday experience of the average person?

speaker: Chief
content: Rather than your bad luck evolving, I think you've simply started noticing that good things happen to you too. How long have you been experiencing this?

speaker: Murphy
content: ...Since my car sent that shadowy impostor flying last time?

speaker: Murphy
content: ...Oh! Wait, could I have... transferred all my bad luck to that thing last time? That's why my own luck seems to have improved a teeny tiny bit?
(Flashback)

speaker: Murphy
content: And there's more! I've also noticed that... after a few unlucky incidents, I'll get some good luck!

options: Have you been reading too many light novels?

speaker: Murphy
content: But it's true! Chief, you have to believe me! I've been keeping track... On average, three days of bad luck will trigger a small lucky event. After a whole week of bad luck, something really good will happen!

speaker: Murphy
content: Like... one time a car splashed dirty water all over me, then I broke a chair, and the very next day I bought the sweetest watermelon ever! Like, it was delicious! The kind that splits right open with just a tap!

speaker: Murphy
content: This has happened so many times! Look, I wrote it all down in my notebook!

You take the notebook Murphy hands you. The title was written with a highlighter in big letters: On the Pattern of Good Luck and the Pity System of Bad Luck. Below it, she's even carefully calculated the frequency of lucky events.

speaker: Chief
content: Wow, this looks like some kind of research paper... So, you seem to believe your bad luck and good luck follow a pattern, with some form of conversion and exchange going on between the two?

speaker: Chief
content: Like some sort of points system you see on shopping websites. Collect enough points and you can redeem a prize. Is that what you mean?
Murphy nods vigorously, her eyes brimming with hopeful anticipation as she looks to you for approval.
You consider your response carefully, and decide not to comment on her peculiar theories or her so-called pattern of good luck for now.

speaker: Chief
content: ...Alright, let's say it's true. If your luck's gotten better, then that's great, isn't it? Did you come all the way to the Bureau just to brag about it?
The corners of Murphy's mouth droop noticeably.

speaker: Murphy
content: No... Obviously... I came because lately, the pattern seems to behave strangely...

speaker: Murphy
content: Two weeks ago, I got what has to be the angriest complaint call ever! This old lady was impossible to deal with. My coworkers all call her the <color=#fb9259>Cranky Old Lady</color>. She's practically become a legend at the information desk...
[Scene Change]

speaker: Cranky Old Lady
content: Hello?! Anyone there? Did you all kick the bucket?! I pay taxes so you people can fix those ramshackle walls, not sit around the office gathering dust!

speaker: Cranky Old Lady
content: How many times have I told you?! That wretched dog on the next street starts howling at three in the morning every day! Like its owner just died! Are you going to do something about it or not?! If you don't, I'll go hang myself right outside your office!

speaker: Cranky Old Lady
content: Say something! What, cat got your tongue?!
[Scene Transition]

speaker: Murphy
content: She was basically calling every single day, complaining about late-night road construction keeping her up, or the neighbor's dog barking...

speaker: Murphy
content: I had to listen to her rant while also helping other citizens at the information desk. The moment I was a little slow to respond, she turned on me too, calling me a lazybones who only knew how to take taxpayers' money. I remember thinking maybe I should've just called in sick that day...

speaker: Murphy
content: To ease the awkwardness, I asked if she wanted to grab some water and take a breather before continuing to yell at me. Next thing I knew, she just... stopped shouting and hung up.

speaker: Murphy
content: And then my supervisor heard the recording. He thought I showed amazing patience and handled it brilliantly. He actually held me up as the model complaint call operator and gave me a huge bonus.

speaker: Chief
content: Isn't that great? Sounds like you've unlocked your secret talent.

speaker: Murphy
content: I know, right? I thought I had never been blessed with better luck too! But after that... the information desk started getting more and more complaint calls. And my supervisor would transfer all the toughest cases straight to me...

speaker: Chief
content: I see. So you became the complaint call specialist.

speaker: Murphy
content: Exactly! Anyway, after that, my life changed completely all of a sudden! The little bits of good luck I was getting got rarer and smaller, and work kept getting harder.

speaker: Murphy
content: Until yesterday... It was supposed to be a lucky day for me, but Cranky Old Lady called again! This time she was complaining about the streetlight outside her place being too bright and keeping her awake... But I'd literally just walked past that very spot the day before and tripped because it was too dark!

speaker: Murphy
content: ...If she hadn't made that call two weeks ago, I never would've gotten recognized by my supervisor or become stuck with all those awful complaint calls. If only she hadn't called that day...

speaker: Murphy
content: So instead of giving her my usual "Thank you for your feedback, we'll look into it," I stood my ground and firmly explained that there was absolutely nothing wrong with the streetlight's brightness.

speaker: Murphy
content: I don't even remember what else I said, but I was so worked up. Probably went a little overboard... When I finally came to my senses, all my coworkers had stopped working and were just staring at me, and my supervisor called me into his office for a lecture...
As she speaks, Murphy's head droops lower and lower. Faint traces of Mania gather around her, forming a rain cloud above her head.

speaker: Murphy
content: My supervisor asked if I'd been under too much stress lately and needed some time to recharge. And that's how <color=#e88490>unlucky Murphy</color> earned herself a special day off.

speaker: Murphy
content: I wanted to clear my head, so I went for a drive. Next thing I knew, I ended up around here. Chief, I feel like I'm slipping back to how I was before I met you. What am I supposed to do...

speaker: Murphy
content: You... you told me if I ever needed help, I could come to you. You meant it, right? You'll help me this time too, right?

Murphy stares at you with pleading eyes. Seeing her in such a pitiful state, you can't bring yourself to scold her any further. With a wave of your hand, you disperse the rain cloud hovering above her.

speaker: Chief
content: Of course. A promise is a promise.

speaker: Chief
content: While I don't believe good luck appears in any predictable pattern, let's analyze the situation under the assumption that your theory is true.

speaker: Chief
content: Based on your records, the frequency of lucky events has dropped significantly over the past two weeks, from an average of once every three days to once every four to five days.

speaker: Chief
content: If we quantify the exchange rate between your bad luck and good luck, it's as if... the threshold for triggering good luck has suddenly been raised, right?
Murphy looks at you with teary eyes, as if she's just found her kindred spirit, nodding vigorously.

speaker: Murphy
content: You must know a way to fix this too, right? Just like how you handle Mania!

speaker: Chief
content: Don't look at me like that. I'm not some god of fortune. I can't just fix your "good luck probability" like that.

speaker: Chief
content: Normally, this theory does help you stay optimistic. But when you encounter an unlucky streak... like right now, this same theory gives you unrealistic expectations for good luck. So when things don't turn out the way you anticipate, you end up feeling even more dejected and disappointed.

speaker: Chief
content: You're not really upset about that cranky old lady. You're frustrated because your bad luck hasn't been properly "converted" into the good luck you're expecting...
You continue taking notes while observing her expression. Then, you suddenly realize something and stop writing.

speaker: Chief
content: ...It sounds like this theory itself is the root of the problem. Your mindset is affecting how you see things. Couldn't you abandon this theory altogether?

speaker: Murphy
content: Actually... I don't want to. This is my hard-earned good luck, after all...
Though you remain completely unconvinced by her theory, you know such good luck is indeed hard to come by for Murphy—even if it might be nothing more than a fancy illusion.

speaker: Chief
content: I understand. I'll stop by your workplace later and see if I can offer some advice.
You decide to give it a shot anyway.

speaker: Murphy
content: Hurray! I knew you wouldn't give up on me, Chief!

speaker: Murphy
content: I thought I might lose my job because I was too frustrated, then I might lose my apartment because I couldn't pay rent, and I might end up hauling all my stuff to crash at the Bureau... Haha...

speaker: Chief
content: ...What kind of horror story is that?

You can't help but recall what it was like when she came to the Bureau for her examinations. The constant downpours were actually the least of your problems. Glassware and ceramics were broken on a daily basis, and every so often, a few light fixtures and chunks of wall joined the casualty list.

You'd be walking around in casts every day, constantly on edge, all while enduring Nightingale's unspoken complaints and the other Sinners' resentful stares... Just thinking about it sends a shiver down your spine.
<size=44><color=#fb9259>Murphy definitely cannot move into the Bureau again!!</color></size>

speaker: Chief
content: Alright, for the smooth operations of the Bureau, and for my own safety at work...
Have to find a way to help this Goddess of Bad Luck as soon as possible.

Two Days Later
Public Security Bureau Information Desk
After your last meeting, you contacted the Public Security Bureau's Information Desk, where Murphy works. With their permission, you spend a full workday observing her at the office.
Murphy is indeed behaving a little strangely. She's constantly distracted when answering calls, unable to stay focused.

Specifically, she's destroyed one power strip by spilling water on it, leaned back too far in her chair and fallen over four times, spaced out mid-conversation and caused the caller to hang up eight times.
Her luck-altering special power hasn't disappeared. If anything, it's gotten stronger. You can feel it now, a dark cloud hanging over the entire office.
And there, right beneath the gathering clouds, sits the Goddess of Bad Luck herself, scribbling something in a notebook with a ball pen.

speaker: Chief
content: What are you writing down?

speaker: Murphy
content: N-nothing...
You say nothing and simply look down at her.
Within seconds, Murphy, head hung low like a guilty kitten, respectfully hands over the lined notebook with both hands.

You flip through the pages. Back in the interrogation room, you only glimpsed her notes about good luck. You didn't notice that, besides trivial everyday events, she's also been keeping track of things happening at work in detailed logs, organized by dates.
First call today: Four minutes twenty seconds in, the caller heard my joke but didn't laugh... Unlucky!
Third call today: One minute five seconds in... the caller suddenly dropped the heavy topic and started talking about her cat. Lucky!
Ninth call today: Two minutes fifteen seconds in, the conversation suddenly died, and neither of us could think of anything else to say... Unlucky!
Was suddenly craving walnuts during lunch break today. Tried cracking one twice but failed, then accidentally hurt my finger... Super unlucky! :((((
You keep turning the pages. The rest reads pretty much the same.

speaker: Chief
content: These things you've been noting down...

speaker: Murphy
content: Huh? Wh-what about them...
She lifts her head slightly, looking at you with an anxious, insecure expression.

options: Aren't they a bit too trivial?
Are these things really worth noting down?

speaker: Chief
content: That entry about walnuts is at least understandable. But the ones about "the dead conversation" and "the sudden cat talk"... most people wouldn't even remember things like that. Yet not only did you record them, but you also categorized them as lucky or unlucky.

speaker: Chief
content: You didn't use to obsess over these trivial things. Look, at the beginning of this notebook, you only recorded important things in your life, right? But starting from a certain point, you suddenly began logging every single detail, good or bad, no matter how minor.

speaker: Chief
content: The human brain naturally filters out unimportant details. We jot down things that matter, so we don't forget. But now you're trying to care about everything. And worse, you're forcing yourself to judge if each one of them is good or bad. This will only stress you out for no reason.

speaker: Murphy
content: Chief... So you're saying that these things I've been writing down have nothing to do with luck, and that I should just... stop judging them...

speaker: Murphy
content: ...But if I stop doing this, how else am I supposed to figure out the pattern behind good luck?!

speaker: Chief
content: Observation and judgment are both subjective activities. Have you ever considered that maybe this so-called <color=#fb9259>pattern</color> doesn't exist at all?

speaker: Chief
content: Here's what we'll do. Starting with the next call, you focus on your work, and I'll keep track of what happens during that time.

speaker: Chief
content: But I won't be judging if anything is a good or bad sign, and I won't be noting down any "lucky" or "unlucky" events.
Murphy nods, tentatively accepting your idea. Once she collects herself, the Mania clouds surrounding her finally dissipate. You pull over an office chair and sit down beside her.

Over the next hour, Murphy dutifully handles one complaint call after another, while you meticulously document every detail of her conversations, matching the same level of thoroughness displayed in her own records.

speaker: Chief
content: Honestly, recording all this is no easy task. No wonder she was almost at a point of burnout.

speaker: Chief
content: Done. Take a look.
Murphy obediently sets down the receiver and takes the notebook, reading through each entry. Her expression shifts from eager anticipation to gradual disinterest, until finally, she even yawns.

speaker: Murphy
content: It's so... boring? They are all just trivial things that don't matter.

speaker: Chief
content: That's exactly my point. Even according to your own theory, the good luck and bad luck you're experiencing now can only be considered the smallest bills in fate's currency.

speaker: Chief
content: Rather than desperately collecting these small bills, obsessing over their values, wanting to use them to exchange for something else...

speaker: Chief
content: Why not think of them as tiny coins you're saving in a giant piggy bank? Whenever something happens, good or bad, just toss it in and don't think about it again. That way, you'll feel a lot better, and nothing will get in the way of <color=#e88490>real good luck</color> when it finally arrives.

speaker: Murphy
content: I mean, you've got a point, Chief...
After hearing your words, she tilts her head and slumps forward onto the desk. Her right hand picks up a ball pen and attempts to spin it, only to drop it on the desk again and again.

speaker: Murphy
content: But... it's just not that simple for me.

speaker: Murphy
content: A long time ago, I didn't use to think about my luck at all. I mean, what difference would it make? I was still the same unlucky girl anyway.

speaker: Murphy
content: But once I've learned that good luck really does exist, I can't help but hope for it! It's like... spending your whole life in darkness, then suddenly finding out about the sun!

speaker: Murphy
content: ...Well, I'll give it a try! Stop overthinking... Yeah! I can do that!

She forces a bright smile, but the pen slips from her hand again and clatters to the floor. Scrambling to pick it up, she bumps her head on the desk as she straightens back up, letting out a soft "Ow"!
She clearly hasn't fully grasped the concept, and her agreement sounds halfhearted. Still, it's progress. You smile at the unlucky girl, watching her live up to her reputation in real time.
Ring, ring, ring!

speaker: Murphy
content: ...Oh, the phone. Hello, Public Security Bureau Information Desk and Service Center!

speaker: Grateful Citizen
content: Hello! Oh, yes, this voice! I remember you!

speaker: Murphy
content: Huh? Oh! You're the gentleman who called about the public safety concern! I remember now! You told me how unlucky you were. You always had thugs hanging around your shop while your business kept losing money...

speaker: Grateful Citizen
content: Yes, yes, that's right! You fell off your chair during that call, choked on your water multiple times, and then your computer crashed, and I had to wait for it to reboot!
Not sure if it's a good thing to be remembered for those reasons... Murphy rubs her face awkwardly.

speaker: Murphy
content: We've already submitted the issue you reported last time. Have you encountered another problem?

speaker: Grateful Citizen
content: Hahaha... Don't worry! The problem from last time hasn't been sorted out yet, but I'm only calling to thank you!

speaker: Murphy
content: You want to thank me... even if it hasn't been sorted out?
Alarms blare in Murphy's head. Is this genuine gratitude a sign of good luck, or just another trap leading to bad luck?

speaker: Grateful Citizen
content: After that call, I thought to myself, wow, there are people out there way unluckier than me who still manage to smile through their job. Compared to you, I suddenly realized my situation wasn't so bad after all!

speaker: Grateful Citizen
content: So I just let it all go! And guess what? Barely two weeks later, I was thinking of closing my lousy shop. Then those punks showed up again. I thought to myself, to hell with it, I don't care, I'm quitting anyway!

speaker: Grateful Citizen
content: So I just grabbed all that unsold junk cluttering my shop and hurled the whole pile at them!

speaker: Murphy
content: Huh? And did you get... beaten up by them?

speaker: Grateful Citizen
content: Beaten up? No way! Some kid nearby was filming a vlog or something. He caught the moment I threw out all that stuff!

speaker: Grateful Citizen
content: He edited it with some epic music and called me "the furniture store J. Chan" who taught those nasty kids a lesson. By some miracle, that video went viral!

speaker: Grateful Citizen
content: All that inventory I couldn't move for three years sold out in less than half a day. Now I even have to restock every day!

speaker: Grateful Citizen
content: Um, hello? Did the line cut out? Anyway, just wanna say I really appreciate your help, miss. Keep up the good work. Oh, I've got a customer, gotta go!
Beep... Beep... Beep...

The call ended. Murphy remains frozen, receiver still pressed to her ear. Several seconds pass before she lowers it back into the cradle with a heavy look on her face. She turns to face you, her expression utterly deflated.

speaker: Murphy
content: Chief, you said earlier that those events were just the normal everyday experience of the average person... that they didn't count as bad luck...

speaker: Murphy
content: But even someone I've only spoken to once over the phone could tell how unlucky I am. He even used my bad luck to feel better about himself.

speaker: Murphy
content: Fine, fine! Fate's already forsaken me anyway! He's right, I am indeed the unluckiest person in the whole world... Sob... Nobody better try to steal that title from me...
The Mania field around her begins warping again. Near the office ceiling, dark clouds of bad luck start gathering.

speaker: Chief
content: Well... that just set us back to square one.

speaker: Chief
content: If I want to pull her out of this, I need another theory. One that can explain her bad luck in a way that's convincing, but won't make her despair. Something different from her own good luck theory...
Watching Murphy's M-value climb, you quickly usher her out of the office.
[Scene Change]
At a coffee shop outside the Public Security Bureau, you hand Murphy a hazelnut latte to help calm her down. On the table sits a collection of board games, and one in particular catches your eye.

speaker: Chief
content: Let's play a game about good luck and bad luck.
You pick up the somewhat worn board game and give it a little shake in Murphy's direction.

speaker: Chief
content: The rules are simple. You roll the die to get your planes out. Each time you roll a six, you can launch one plane from your base. After that, you roll each turn and move your planes along the track based on the number you get.

speaker: Chief
content: If your plane lands on the same spot as mine, the one that was there first gets knocked back to the base. Whoever gets all their planes to the finish point first wins. Ready?
Murphy picks up the die and nods hesitantly.
You both pick up the die and begin. Ten rounds pass. You've already launched two planes, while Murphy, who hasn't rolled a single six, can only watch helplessly as your pieces race around the board.

speaker: Murphy
content: Chief, that's not fair! Why'd you pick a game that's all about luck? You know mine's terrible.

speaker: Chief
content: Look, the probability of rolling a six each turn is one in six. Now that ten rounds have passed, by that logic, the die owes you at least one plane.

speaker: Chief
content: When I first started playing this game, I used to think the same way. After all, it's no fun watching everyone else's planes out on the board while yours are still stuck at home.

speaker: Chief
content: But that's not how it works. A die only has six sides. It has no memory, no record of your previous rolls. No matter how many times you've failed, the odds of rolling a six next time are still just one in six.

speaker: Chief
content: Besides, rolling a six isn't the only outcome that matters. Launching a plane late can sometimes save you from getting knocked back. Each roll doesn't just determine a single stroke of luck, but an entire chain of <color=#fb9259>unknowns</color> you'll face afterward.

speaker: Chief
content: Try letting go of your resentment over the past rounds. Treat this die as the reality you're facing, and roll it again.

speaker: Murphy
content: Let go of the resentment...
Murphy gives the die an indignant squeeze, then gently strokes it a few times to show she forgives it.

Her next rolls still aren't sixes, but your planes don't make it into the fast lane either. Murphy's planes launch over the following rounds and, by sheer coincidence, knock yours back several times. In the end, she wins the game.

speaker: Chief
content: Congrats on winning. Feeling any better now?

speaker: Murphy
content: Thank you, Chief. This is the luckiest thing that's happened to me in days.

speaker: Chief
content: I didn't just invite you here to play a game. That theory of yours about good luck is like a gacha game with a pity system. You thought enough bad luck would guarantee eventual good luck. But reality is actually more like rolling a die, isn't it?

speaker: Chief
content: Gacha games have pity systems because someone programmed those odds. Life doesn't work like that. It's more like a die with far more sides, and it's completely out of anyone's control. No one can promise you what you'll roll next.

speaker: Chief
content: The one thing I can say for certain is that your Mania can influence the die, but it won't always go the way you want. And it definitely doesn't work like a machine that follows strict rules.

speaker: Chief
content: Your luck hasn't changed. Your mindset has. The Murphy who was constantly unlucky was the exception. What you're dealing with now is actually closer to what normal people experience every day.

speaker: Chief
content: You were used to being constantly unlucky, so days where good and bad mix together feel strange to you. That's why you insist on defining it and discovering the pattern behind it, exhausting yourself. My advice: Learn to accept your new life and adapt to it.

speaker: Murphy
content: Accept, adapt...
Murphy fiddles with the die, repeating your words without fully understanding them.

speaker: Murphy
content: Chief, I'm not sure I get it... but then again, maybe I do! You mean I should accept whatever result I roll, and no matter what the number is, treat it like an unknown worth looking forward to. Just like the game we were playing.

speaker: Chief
content: I'm glad you've figured it out once again. I hope the "lesson" you've learned this time can last longer.

speaker: Murphy
content: Oh, but it will! Look, Chief. To prove I mean it, I'll cross out all my old notes now!
She picks up her notebook as she speaks and starts scribbling over her previous entries, crossing out each record she's marked as good luck or bad luck.
Suddenly, her pen stops. She stares intently at one of the entries.

speaker: Murphy
content: Cranky Old Lady... the lady who yelled at me and cost me that unlucky commendation... The last time she called was three days ago! But according to my old records, she used to call every single day...

speaker: Murphy
content: Why hasn't she called in so long... Did something happen to her?

speaker: Chief
content: I remember you mentioned that you said something harsh to her during that last call. If I were her, I wouldn't call back either.

speaker: Murphy
content: ...Could this be my fault?

speaker: Murphy
content: Then next time she calls, I must control my temper and apologize to her. I'll explain why I acted that way last time and reflect on my own behavior... That's the right thing to do, right, Chief?

speaker: Chief
content: As long as you can stay rational and stop overthinking all that stuff about good luck, bad luck, and pity systems, I'm confident you'll handle it just fine.

speaker: Murphy
content: Yes, I'll definitely do my best! And thank you for everything you told me today, Chief. I'll write it all down in my notebook and commit it to memory!

speaker: Murphy
content: Honestly, I still feel a little lost... But I believe everything is going in the right direction. With your help, Chief, I won't be afraid anymore!

speaker: Murphy
content: And that big stroke of good luck I've been waiting for so long must be on its way too!
After everything that's been said, she's still waiting for good luck?
You're still a little skeptical about her renewed understanding of luck. But at least you've seen a glimmer of hope that her understanding might still be corrected.
The next time you hear from Murphy, two weeks have passed.

She tells you she's been waiting for Cranky Old Lady to call these past two weeks, and she never picked up whenever Murphy tried calling. She wouldn't even mind if the woman just showed up in person to chew her out, but that hasn't happened either.
She even broke protocol by accessing the bureau's call records to confirm that none of her colleagues have received any calls from that number either.
And so, in hopes of getting the chance to apologize in person, she drags you onto the streets of Eastside.

speaker: Chief
content: But are you sure wandering around aimlessly like this will help you find her? You don't even have her personal information or address, do you?

speaker: Murphy
content: The Public Security Bureau's system has an old ID photo she uploaded before... I, uh, took a picture of it. But the address on file is outdated, so we'll just have to search for her ourselves.

speaker: Murphy
content: From her previous complaints, I know the general area where she lives. There's a fruit stall downstairs where she always ends up buying rotten persimmons, and a giant billboard on the roof that blocks out all the sunlight in her room... I remember all these details!

speaker: Chief
content: So you know the general area, but can you really find the exact location with those vague descriptions?

speaker: Murphy
content: That's exactly why I enlisted your help, Chief! Without you, I'd probably just end up getting lost in Eastside!

speaker: Murphy
content: Let me see... There it is! Look, right over there!

You follow where Murphy's pointing and, miraculously, there it is. A fruit stall piled with overripe persimmons at the corner across the street, and atop the same building stands a massive Quinn billboard.

speaker: Murphy
content: I knew it! My luck's finally turning around! Let's go, Chief!

speaker: Chief
content: Wait, watch out for the car!
With that confident announcement, Murphy immediately bolts toward the other side of the street. You quickly yank her back, barely avoiding a dump truck turning out from a blind spot.
After that, you grab the unlucky star's arm as you search for a crosswalk, finally arriving at the fruit stall a few minutes later.

speaker: Murphy
content: Good morning, Rotten Persimmon Lady! Does this old lady in the photo... happen to live in this building?

speaker: Rotten Persimmon Lady
content: ...What rotten persimmon?! I only sell fresh fruit here!

speaker: Rotten Persimmon Lady
content: This photo... Oh! That's the old lady who used to live on the second floor. She moved out a couple of days ago. Try looking for her in the neighborhood east of here.

speaker: Murphy
content: She... she moved?! Do you... happen to have her address? I really need to reach her. It's important!

speaker: Rotten Persimmon Lady
content: Why would I have it? Do you even know her, anyway? She never talked to any of the neighbors. We wouldn't have even known she was leaving had we not seen the movers!
The "Rotten Persimmon Lady" looks Murphy and you up and down, apparently deciding if you're some suspicious characters. She then continues.

speaker: Rotten Persimmon Lady
content: If you really want to find her... Look, there's a bus stop over there. Ride four stops. Ask around there with your photo.

speaker: Murphy
content: Awesome, thank you!
Following the fruit vendor's directions, you and Murphy arrive at the bus stop. Murphy runs her hand over the bus schedule with a wistful and longing expression.

speaker: Murphy
content: This brings back memories... You know, Chief, I just realized I haven't taken a bus in ages...

speaker: Murphy
content: I have a bunch of younger siblings, and the family car couldn't fit everyone, so I always had to take the bus to school.

speaker: Murphy
content: But there was always something wrong with that bus. Broken AC, a leaking tank, or we'd run into road work... It never made it to the destination without a hitch...

speaker: Murphy
content: I was always late, and I felt so guilty every time... I brought bad luck to everyone else on the bus. But now you're here with me, so maybe today will be a little luckier.

speaker: Chief
content: We're only riding four stops. What could possibly go wrong?
At that moment, the bus pulls into the station. You and Murphy sit down, but after just two stops, a rear tire suddenly blows out. You're forced to get off the bus along with the other passengers.

speaker: Murphy
content: Of course... I'm still a hopeless jinx.

speaker: Chief
content: ...We still have some ground to cover. We can grab two shared bikes here and bike the rest of the way.
You bring Murphy over to a few rental bikes. She crouches down to examine the bright yellow paint, then runs her hand over the handlebars, that same wistful expression crossing her face.

speaker: Murphy
content: You know, Chief... I just realized I haven't ridden a bike in ages either.

speaker: Murphy
content: After I gave up on buses, I saved up and bought myself a beautiful bike. I loved riding it... It made me feel so free and happy. Finally, I didn't have to feel guilty about delaying other people's trips.

speaker: Murphy
content: But then I accidentally crashed into a pedestrian and sent him into the bushes... I had to sell the bike to cover his medical bills. I haven't ridden a bike ever since...

speaker: Chief
content: Okay, stop. Can you please not bring that up right now? I've got a really bad feeling about this.

You and Murphy bike normally for a while, but the peace doesn't last. A few minutes in, you suddenly hear Murphy shout from behind—then a blur shoots past you. It's Murphy, screaming as she barrels downhill completely out of control.

speaker: Murphy
content: Why won't the brakes work?! Chief!!! HELP!!!

A cacophony of crashing noises echo from the bottom of the slope, followed by a rising cloud of dust. When it settles, you spot an overturned bicycle lodged in the bushes, its rear wheel still spinning in the air.
You grit your teeth and force yourself to stay positive, then pedal down to the bottom of the slope and pull Murphy, sprawled on the ground and covered in leaves, to her feet.

speaker: Chief
content: Well, at least you're not hurt. We've had more than our share of mishaps, but we should be close to our destination now. We can just walk there from here.

speaker: Murphy
content: You know, Chief...

speaker: Chief
content: ...Don't tell me you haven't walked anywhere in ages either.
Hearing that familiar opening line, you instinctively take two wary steps back.

speaker: Murphy
content: No, no! Look, over there! I think we actually made it to our destination!
[Scene Change]
You follow Murphy's gaze. Sure enough, there's a familiar bus stop standing by the roadside, and not far beyond it, a cluster of run-down, low-rise apartment buildings.

You and Murphy park the bicycles by the roadside and start asking around in the residential buildings with the photo. But your luck seems to have run even drier this time. Not a single resident here has ever seen that cranky old lady.

You search from morning through noon and into the afternoon without a single lead. To make matters worse, Murphy somehow gets targeted by someone's dog, and after a relentless chase, the two of you end up cornered in a dead-end alley.

speaker: Murphy
content: Why does this have to be so hard... I just want to find Cranky Old Lady. We've already made it this far. Why is the home stretch so impossible...
These obviously can't be called coincidences anymore. You sense Murphy's emotions beginning to spiral, her Mania stirring restlessly in response. You quickly reach out to calm her.

speaker: Chief
content: Murphy, calm down a little, okay? These are nothing more than some small obstacles. Don't stress yourself out.

speaker: Vicious Dog
content: Woof, woof!

speaker: Chief
content: Watch out, it's coming this way again!

speaker: Murphy
content: Ahh! Stay away!!
In a panic, Murphy tears off one of her accessories and hurls it into the distance, hoping to divert the dog's attention.

But as luck would have it, a black cat suddenly leaps down from a tree by the wall and snatches Murphy's accessory from under the dog's nose! The cat flicks its tail smugly, then darts toward a distant corner, jumps over a wall gracefully, and vanishes.
Robbed of its prize, the dog makes to give chase, only to be stopped by its owner's distant shout. With a few reluctant barks, it finally retreats.

speaker: Murphy
content: ...Wait! Did I just... Oh no, that was one of my lucky charms! I need to get it back!

Without hesitation, Murphy rushes over and scrambles up the wall. You follow close behind. The barrier is old and weathered. Through one of the cracks, you lock eyes with someone in the garden behind it.
Who's out there?! How dare you skulk around and steal bricks from my wall?!
Somehow this resident looks familiar to you, but before you can place it, Murphy blurts out.

speaker: Murphy
content: There you are! Cranky Old Lady!

speaker: Cranky Old Lady
content: Watch your tongue! Hold on... I know that voice. You're that girl with rotten luck, aren't you? How on earth did you find me here? Even my own son doesn't know where I live.

speaker: Murphy
content: Um, I didn't find you... A black cat led me here. Whew... Finally! I was so worried something bad had happened to you!
Getting a good look at how disheveled and dust-covered you are, and with the teary-eyed Murphy next to you, the old woman lets out a sigh, suddenly speaking more kindly.

speaker: Cranky Old Lady
content: ...Your unusual luck and your unusual methods. Look at the state of you both. Ran into all sorts of trouble getting here, didn't you? Come on, get down from that wall already. Come sit in the garden.
Murphy agrees cheerfully and positions herself on top of the wall to get ready for the jump. And just as you expect, she lands flat on her face.
[Scene Change]
After you've washed your faces and dressed your wounds, the old lady leads you both into the shabby garden to sit down. She even pours each of you a glass of water.

The property is not only old, but also clearly long-neglected. The wiring and plumbing have fallen into disrepair. The house is poorly furnished. And the plants have been dead for ages. It's obvious it had been abandoned for years, and has only recently regained a resident.

speaker: Old Lady
content: You shouldn't have come. An old woman like me isn't worth all the trouble you went through.

As she speaks, the old lady explains why she moved here. It turns out she was diagnosed with cancer some time ago. Not wanting to burden her family, she decided to hide away in this abandoned family property where no one could find her.

As for all those complaint calls to the Public Security Bureau, they were a result of her new, lonely life. During that time, lodging complaints gave her some purpose. And Murphy, who listened so patiently, in fact offered her some semblance of companionship.

speaker: Old Lady
content: Never imagined the first person to find me would be you, the girl I used to pester every single day. So how have you been, you poor thing? Still as unlucky as ever?

speaker: Murphy
content: Oh, you bet! Just look at all these cuts and bruises. Got them when I was searching for you everywhere.

speaker: Old Lady
content: Sigh... You see, I never got much of an education in my life. Didn't make any money when I was young, and now that I'm old, those predatory schemes went and swindled me out of what little I'd saved. I used to wonder, why am I the unlucky one? Everyone else gets to be rich. Why not me?

speaker: Old Lady
content: Then came all kinds of disasters. My husband passed. I even had to see my own children go... Now I have only one son left. Heh. Turns out I'm the one who outlived them all.

speaker: Old Lady
content: So many years passed, and I never got rich, but my health held up well enough. And by now... I've actually stopped dwelling on all that.

speaker: Murphy
content: Why did you stop?

speaker: Old Lady
content: Because there's no point. I've been unlucky most of my life. Thought I finally got to enjoy some peace in my old age, but here I am, suffering from a terminal illness. How do you make sense of that? You can't. It's just fate.

speaker: Old Lady
content: So listen, my dear. People with luck like yours and mine must learn to come to terms with life. Whether times are harsh on you or not, life goes on. Whatever it throws at you, try to take it. There's no reasoning with it, but once you make peace with that, you'll find life a lot easier.

speaker: Murphy
content: But that's... that's not fair at all...
The words leave Murphy visibly shaken. She wants to say something comforting, but can't come up with anything. The old lady notices her struggle and smiles, continuing on.

speaker: Old Lady
content: You said you came to apologize. Thank you, my dear. But as you see, whatever you said to me is nothing compared to what fate's dealt me. Besides, all you did was give me a bit of attitude. No need to keep blaming yourself.

speaker: Old Lady
content: You've got nothing to apologize for. Stay a little longer if you like, then go on home and live your life. You've still got plenty of unlucky days ahead of you to get through, okay?
The old woman turns to refill your tea. Murphy lowers her head, lost in thought, processing what she's just heard.

speaker: Murphy
content: Am I really going to stay unlucky my whole life...? Could... her illness be caused by my bad luck as well...?
Despite everything, she's spiraling once again. A faint trace of Mania begins gathering around her once more. You gently pat her hand, trying to dispel the dark clouds closing in.

speaker: Chief
content: Everyone has their own fate. Trust me, your bad luck can't be transferred so easily through a phone line. That much I can guarantee.

speaker: Chief
content: Other people's life experiences don't necessarily apply to you. Be curious about them, but you don't have to agree with everything they tell you. That said... "making peace with things" and "not blaming yourself"—those two points I do agree with.
[Scene Change]
You stay with the old lady a while longer before heading back with Murphy. She follows behind you wordlessly, then suddenly stops.

speaker: Murphy
content: I... I forgot something at the old lady's. I need to go back real quick.

speaker: Chief
content: Alright. Hurry back.
With your permission, she turns and jogs back toward the garden.

Just then, you sense a sudden surge of Mania. The Mania field that's been lingering around Murphy like rain clouds suddenly stirs violently and uncontrollably. Through the shackles binding you to her, you feel a tremor run through you.

speaker: Chief
content: No... Murphy's Mania is flaring up again! Stop, Murphy!
But your voice is quickly drowned out by a deafening explosion...
[Scene Change]
One hour has passed.
Two hours have passed.

You and Murphy sit across from each other in silence, unsure how long you've been waiting outside the emergency room. The nurses passing by all seem uncertain of the situation, refusing to share any concrete details.

On her way back, Murphy stepped on an old, faulty cable in the garden, making it explode. Fortunately, Murphy managed to shield the old lady in that instant, but the woman's frail body could hardly withstand the blast. The garden went ablaze instantly, and now its owner's fate is still unknown inside the emergency room.

speaker: Murphy
content: I'm so sorry... It's all my fault... If I hadn't gone back, she wouldn't have...

speaker: Chief
content: Don't blame yourself for everything. That faulty wiring was an accident waiting to happen. You might have even lessened her injury by protecting her in that moment.
Even so, Murphy remains consumed by guilt. You take her hand, and together you wait for the final outcome.
After what feels like an eternity, the light above the emergency room finally changes color. The door opens, and you seem to be witnessing a miracle.

The old lady you both feared was beyond saving walks out on her own feet, supported by a nurse. Despite her haggard appearance, one arm in a cast and the other clutching two X-ray films, there's an unexpected vitality about her.

speaker: Murphy
content: Cran... Ma'am! You're okay... I thought you were...
Murphy throws herself into the old lady's arms. Seeing this, the weight that's been pressing on your chest finally vanishes.

speaker: Old Lady
content: Oh goodness... You nearly knocked me over! And stop saying those things that may bring bad luck. I'm fine. I'm not that fragile!

speaker: Old Lady
content: You know what, that explosion was actually a blessing in disguise! Sure, it broke my arm, but when the doctors ran their tests, they found out that the cancer diagnosis was a mistake. They'd mixed up my scan with someone else's! Turns out I've been perfectly healthy this whole time!

speaker: Murphy
content: The explosion... was a blessing in disguise? How is that even possible? Hold on... The cancer was a misdiagnosis?! That's amazing! You're okay! Does this mean... my bad luck finally turned into good luck?

speaker: Chief
content: No... For most people, this would simply mean that there was medical malpractice and the hospital now owes them compensation.

speaker: Old Lady
content: Oh, you're indeed my lucky star, darling!

speaker: Old Lady
content: Now I don't have to count my remaining days, and I don't have to avoid my own son anymore. Of course, this is no bad luck. It's the greatest blessing I've ever received!
As she speaks with a big smile, tears are streaming down her face at the same time.

speaker: Chief
content: Well, these two... certainly seem to be on the same wavelength.

speaker: Chief
content: Maybe this really is a blessing in disguise after all.
You watch as Murphy and the old lady hold hands, chatting happily for some time. Eventually, the woman's son arrives, and you and Murphy take your leave.
[Scene Change]

speaker: Murphy
content: An explosion and a broken arm certainly sound like a huge disaster to me. But the old lady still called it good luck... And she thought I brought her that blessing?

speaker: Chief
content: After all, whether something is good or bad isn't just about objective facts. There's also the subjective judgment of those who experience it. This event we just went through is simply more dramatic than most.

speaker: Murphy
content: Whether something is good or bad is subjective... Do I really get to decide... if it's good luck or bad luck?
She looks down at her hands, studying her palms before turning them over to examine the backs, as if contemplating the two sides of a coin—good and bad, fortune and misfortune.

speaker: Murphy
content: ...I've learned about so many different things these past few days. Your perspective, the old lady's perspective, the pity system, the aeroplane chess, the black cat, the die...

speaker: Murphy
content: The meaning of good luck and bad luck... I think I'm finally starting to get it! For real this time!
You give her a thumbs up in encouragement. She responds with a determined smile.

speaker: Murphy
content: I need to go home and really think about this. Figure out how to handle the bad things that happen to me, and how to live with these everyday events that have a lucky side and an unlucky side.

speaker: Murphy
content: Chief, next time we meet, you'll see a completely transformed Murphy! I promise!
She thumps her chest twice with brimming confidence.

speaker: Chief
content: Sure, I'm looking forward to it.

speaker: Chief
content: But it's getting late. Let me take you home. And just to be safe... we'll go on foot.
Her smile suddenly freezes, and her legs tremble slightly at the prospect of the physical ordeal ahead. Meanwhile, you stride forward leisurely as she wails in protest behind you.

After what happened at the hospital, you keep close tabs on Murphy. You learn that the old lady, whose bad luck turned out to be a blessing, later sent Murphy a commendation banner. With such recognition from a citizen, Murphy begins progressing steadily at her job.
One evening, you receive a photo from Murphy. It shows two tickets to an amusement park.

Chief! My boss gave me these two amusement park tickets! Hehe, I only got praised thanks to your help, so please, let me thank you properly! Are you free tomorrow? Let's go have a fun day out together!
You see no reason to say no. You wrap up your remaining work and clear your schedule for tomorrow.
[Scene Change]

speaker: Murphy
content: Good morning, Chief!

speaker: Chief
content: Good morning. You look energetic. I take it the trip here went smoothly?

speaker: Murphy
content: Pretty good! The taxi driver only got lost for like fifteen minutes, the subway was delayed for another fifteen, and I only sprained my ankle a little on the walk here. Nothing major!

speaker: Murphy
content: I promised you that you'd see a brand new Murphy, didn't I? Look, I wrote down everything we're going to do. Whatever happens today, I'm going to check all the items on my list with a smile!
Murphy waves the notebook in her hand. The page she has open reads: Itinerary - Amusement Park Day with Chief.

speaker: Chief
content: You even made an itinerary? Let me see...
#1: Try the park's famous strawberry sundae with Chief...

speaker: Murphy
content: You forgot to turn on the freezer last night and all the ice cream melted? No worries! Do you guys have bowls and straws? I'll just buy one and drink it like a milkshake.

speaker: Chief
content: Isn't the texture too thick? Maybe dilute it with some water.
#2: Get a unique balloon from the balloon vendor...

speaker: Murphy
content: Chief, look! The balloon ribbon got completely tangled in my hair! That makes a pretty cool hairstyle, huh?

speaker: Chief
content: ...Let me untangle it for you.
#3: How can an amusement park trip be complete without some great pictures? We must take some pics with the mascots...

speaker: Murphy
content: Sure, the dozen pictures we took all came out blurry... but at least this one of me falling on the ground is clear! I'm putting it on my desk!

speaker: Chief
content: Send me those image files. I can perhaps salvage a few of the blurry ones...
#4: Go to the water park and try the water seesaw.

speaker: Chief
content: Isn't that for kids? Are you sure two adults can even fit on it?

speaker: Chief
content: Come to think of it, why is the roller coaster the only thing not on this list? Most people come to the park for these thrill rides.

speaker: Murphy
content: Th-thrill rides, huh...
Murphy turns her head away sheepishly.

speaker: Murphy
content: You know how I am. If I got on a roller coaster, I'd probably end up getting everyone else hurt...

speaker: Murphy
content: I mean... I do really want to try them, but let's just stick to the other stuff for now.

speaker: Chief
content: ...Okay.
After that, you visit some other attractions, checking off items from Murphy's list one by one. By evening, as you head back toward the exit, you come across a little girl crouched by the side.

speaker: Murphy
content: Hey there, what are you doing here?

speaker: Lost Child
content: I... don't know where Mommy and Daddy went. Do you know where the guest services desk is? Mommy and Daddy told me to go there if I got lost, but I can't find it anywhere.

speaker: Murphy
content: Guest services... Um, I'm not great with directions, but it shouldn't be too hard to find. Let's look for it together, alright?

speaker: Lost Child
content: Okay!
Reassured, the girl joins you. The three of you begin following the signs toward the guest services desk.

But somehow, no matter how carefully you follow the directions, you can't find any trace of your destination. You only encounter more signs pointing in the opposite direction. Walking in an endless loop, you seem to keep barely missing the guest services desk.

speaker: Lost Child
content: Mommy and Daddy must not want me anymore... That's why I can't find it... Boohoo...
As she speaks, the little girl crouches down on the ground again, covering her eyes as she sobs.

speaker: Murphy
content: Hey now, don't cry! We're just a little unlucky, that's all. Trust me when I say I know all about it!

speaker: Murphy
content: Oh, I know! Let me tell you about all the unlucky things that've happened to me! Lots of people find these stories comforting!
Drawn in by Murphy's promise, the girl obediently lowers her hands and sniffles.
[Insert flashback, monologue, young Murphy's portrait]

speaker: Murphy
content: Ever since I was little, I've been super unlucky. There were a lot of kids in my family, and I was just the most ordinary one. I didn't get much attention.

speaker: Murphy
content: Well, what could I do? I wasn't the cutest, and I wasn't the most likable either. Whenever they talked about me, they'd say I was the most sensible and easygoing child. I figured... that was at least a compliment, right? So I kept it up!

speaker: Murphy
content: But later on... things got worse. My exam scores were always one point short of the university cutoffs. I was the only one in my entire dorm with a different major. And when I took the civil service exam, I got assigned the job with the most unattractive package.

speaker: Murphy
content: Everyone around me treated me like a walking disaster. They all kept their distance, terrified my bad luck would rub off on them. And then things got even worse... I contracted a <color=#dg1f1f>very strange illness</color>! I finally made a friend at work, but because of me, something terrible happened to her...

speaker: Murphy
content: So after that, I didn't even have anyone to talk to anymore. I had to constantly worry about causing problems for everyone around me. And even now, I don't have a single friend!
[End of flashback monologue]

speaker: Murphy
content: ...So? See, I'm way unluckier than you, right? Now that you've heard all that, do you feel a little better?

speaker: Lost Child
content: Um...

speaker: Lost Child
content: All these bad things must make you feel really sad. So why aren't you crying?

speaker: Murphy
content: ...Cry?

speaker: Lost Child
content: If I were you, I would've cried my eyes out.

speaker: Lost Child
content: But you're not crying, and you're telling me all this to make me feel better... Are you holding back your tears? That must be really hard...
The girl's small hand reaches up to touch Murphy's eyes. Suddenly, her vision blurs. The smile on her face finally crumbles, twisting into something even more pained than a crying face.

speaker: Murphy
content: Wow... Do kids these days all sound like they're grown-ups?

speaker: Chief
content: Murphy, your bad luck might have accidentally comforted people in your work at the Public Security Bureau, but when you bare your wounds to others like that... it hurts you too, doesn't it?

speaker: Chief
content: The bad luck you had as a child, and the Mania you contracted as an adult... none of it was your fault. These are real scars you carry, not hardships that should be brushed aside, and they don't need to become entertainment for others. If those things still sting, then let it all out.

speaker: Chief
content: Curse them as harshly as you want. This isn't the office. You don't have to worry about who's listening. Just let it all out.

speaker: Murphy
content: Cough...
Murphy fumbles for words, her voice trembling. She glances at you, then at the girl, before finally tilting her head back to stare up at the sky.

speaker: Murphy
content: ...I want to ride the roller coaster.

speaker: Chief
content: ...Now? Where's this coming from?
Murphy looks like she's about to burst into tears. Her M-value isn't particularly high right now though, so riding the roller coaster shouldn't be dangerous.

speaker: Chief
content: Alright then. My job today is to make sure you have a good time, after all.
The little girl beside you tugs at your sleeve, asking cautiously.

speaker: Lost Child
content: I want to ride the roller coaster too, but Mommy thinks it's too dangerous and won't let me. Can I come with you?

You glance at the roller coaster in the distance. It's not particularly tall, so it shouldn't be too dangerous. You steal a quick look at the figure behind you. Even if something does go wrong... you should be able to handle it.

speaker: Chief
content: Alright then. I'll accompany you two brave ladies on this roller coaster ride.
You head back to the thrill ride area. Fortunately, the girl's height clears the 1.2-meter mark. She's tall enough to ride.

After the staff completes their checks, the roller coaster slowly begins its ascent into the sky. Eastside's night view unfolds before you. The car pauses briefly at the peak, then plunges into its thrilling descent.
As the wind roars past your ears during the dive, you hear the girl beside you let out a raw, cathartic scream.

speaker: Murphy
content: Screw you, bad luck! Screw you, Mania! And screw my boss for dumping all the annoying tasks on me! You can all go to hell!!

speaker: Murphy
content: I want friends too! I want people to care about me too! I want to be happy every single day too!

speaker: Chief
content: So that's why you suddenly wanted to ride the roller coaster. You're really letting it all out.

speaker: Lost Child
content: My stupid parents don't even care about me! They just want to be all lovey-dovey... Screw... Mmph!

speaker: Chief
content: Uh-uh, you shouldn't say that.
Amid the roaring wind and the screams of the other riders, you clamp your hand over the child's mouth to cut her off. Having finished their own venting, the two turn simultaneously to look at you.

speaker: Chief
content: Sigh... Alright, my turn.

speaker: Chief
content: Screw you, Black Ring! Screw you, the Underground! I'll eliminate all of you!

speaker: Murphy
content: That's the spirit! Woohoo, screaming at the sky from way up here feels incredible!
As if "something" has been eavesdropping on your conversation, the roller coaster grinds to a halt with a loud creak before Murphy can even finish her sentence, leaving you suspended in midair.

speaker: Murphy
content: Oh no, we're... screwed. I knew it. I never should've gotten on this thing.
Fortunately, you've stopped at a relatively low point on the track and are right-side up, so you can all still breathe alright.
More and more visitors notice something's wrong with the roller coaster and gather below to watch. Among the onlookers, the child spots two familiar faces. She tugs on Murphy's arm.

speaker: Lost Child
content: That's... Mommy and Daddy! I found them!

speaker: Lost Child's Mother
content: Oh my goodness, how did you get up there?! Somebody, please help get my child down right now!!

speaker: Roller Coaster Operator
content: We're very sorry! Everyone, please remain calm and stay still! There's been a minor system error. I'll reset it right away... Just a moment!
A few minutes later, with a hum in the tracks, the roller coaster starts moving again. You make it back to the starting point unharmed, your aerial adventure finally over.
Back on solid ground, the lost child rushes into her anxious parents' arms. She pounds her little fists against them a few times before bursting into tears.

speaker: Lost Child's Mother
content: I'm so sorry for all the trouble. Thank you both for looking after her. Sweetie, say thank you.

speaker: Lost Child
content: Thank you for taking care of me. Sorry for the trouble.

speaker: Murphy
content: Not at all! She's such a sweet, empathetic kid. If anything, I should be thanking her.
Murphy waves her hand bashfully, then crouches down and whispers something into the girl's ear.

speaker: Murphy
content: Those things I told you about are all in the past. But now? I've met this gentleman here, and so many other people just like me. These days have been the luckiest time of my entire life!
female_content: Those things I told you about are all in the past. But now? I've met this lady here, and so many other people just like me. These days have been the luckiest time of my entire life!

speaker: Murphy
content: So, keep being the awesome girl you are, okay? Your bad luck won't last forever. Our lucky days are still waiting for us down the road, right?

speaker: Lost Child
content: Mmm!
Murphy watches the family walk away, her gaze following them into the distance. Perhaps reminded of her own past, she seems quietly moved.

speaker: Chief
content: Feel better after screaming it all out? If that's not enough, you can cry like she did, you know.

speaker: Murphy
content: Chief, what are you talking about? I didn't even dare to cry like that when I was little. Now that I'm all grown up... isn't it a bit too late for that?

speaker: Chief
content: Well, growing up didn't make your bad luck go away or solve your problem, did it? Both the unlucky little girl and the unlucky big girl have the right to cry about it.

speaker: Chief
content: Since you can't change it, you might as well face it with a smile. But complaining works too. So does crying. Who says adults aren't allowed to cry?
You say and open your arms, offering her an embrace.
She throws herself into your arms and finally bursts into tears.
Murphy cries in your arms for a long time. When she finally stops, the sky is already dark.
You head toward the park's exit, retracing the path you took on the way in. Behind you, fireworks bloom across the sky. You both stop to watch as brilliant colors shine upon your faces and eyes.

speaker: Murphy
content: How beautiful... I knew today would be my lucky day. I'm so happy I got to come here with you, ${PlayerName}.
She takes out her notebook and begins jotting down something carefully.

speaker: Chief
content: Recording your good luck and bad luck again?

speaker: Murphy
content: Well... yes and no! This time I'm not going to write down everything, and I'm not going to categorize them as good or bad either! I just want to note down the happy moments I had today.

speaker: Murphy
content: Maybe from now on, I'll keep doing it this way... Let the insignificant details fade away, and only record the things that make me happy! That way when I look back, I can feel more at ease.

speaker: Chief
content: Good idea. And if someday you feel like letting it all out again, you're always welcome to come find me at the Bureau. Just remember to give me a heads-up. We've already gone over our repair budget.
Murphy puffs out her cheeks and shoots you a look.

speaker: Murphy
content: Chief, remember that piggy bank metaphor you mentioned before? You said good luck and bad luck are both just little coins dropped inside.
As she speaks, she traces the shape of a piggy bank in the air with her hands.

speaker: Murphy
content: I'm ready! From now on, I'm only going to save the good luck! As for everything else... who cares if they're good or bad? A thing is good if I decide it is!

speaker: Murphy
content: Since my bad luck is everywhere anyway, I might as well just pretend it's nowhere at all... right?
She says and sticks her tongue out at you playfully.

speaker: Murphy
content: Everything went according to my itinerary today! We checked off everything on the list! I'm really, really happy. Thank you, Chief!
After bidding you farewell, Murphy leaves clutching her notebook, waving at you enthusiastically the whole way.
Once the red-haired girl's figure finally vanishes from sight, two figures emerge from the shadows.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Looks like we won't need to execute Plan B after all.
[Insert Flashback]

speaker: Chief
content: You mean I should take Murphy back to the Bureau for supervision if she fails to meet the standard?

speaker: Nightingale
content: Yes. Her ability is quite unique. If her mental state can't be stabilized, the resulting bad luck will pose a serious threat to civilians around her.

speaker: Nightingale
content: You can meet with Murphy today as planned. I'll secretly observe her mental state and behavior. I'll bring sufficient backup to subdue her, should it come to that. If she fails to meet the standard by the end of the day, we'll have no choice but to bring her back to the Bureau.
[End of Flashback]

speaker: Nightingale
content: When it comes to guiding Sinners and placing your full trust in them, no one can beat you, Chief. I admit I was wrong to doubt you.

speaker: Chief
content: To be honest, I'm surprised at how far she's come in such a short time too.
Perhaps, in some mysterious way, "fate" finally smiled upon her and lent a hand.

speaker: EMP
content: Hey, hey, hey, what about me? So I came all the way here for nothing? I spent the whole day watching you two eat delicious snacks and go on rides, while I was stuck on standby munching stale bread. Is that even fair?

speaker: Chief
content: Not having to fight should be a good thing, no? Don't tell me you were actually hoping for some action?

speaker: EMP
content: I don't care! I came all the way to the park, so either let me throw some punches, or come with me again tomorrow to play. I deserve some kind of reward!

speaker: Chief
content: I'll pass. The park just barely survived the Goddess of Bad Luck. Having the Archer Queen show up right after would be too much for them to handle. This isn't the Bureau, after all.

speaker: EMP
content: ...Uh, worst joke I've ever heard!
At EMP's remark, all three of you burst into laughter.

speaker: Chief
content: Alright, alright. Since we're already here, let's stay for the fireworks at least. There are food stalls nearby too. My treat—eat as much as you want.
Despite everything, this could have turned out so much worse.
You hope Murphy's Mania can treat her with more kindness from now on.
And perhaps more mercy from "fate"—which has been so exceptionally hard on her—too.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, we failed.
Failed? How could that be?
Uh, wait, failed in what?

speaker: Nightingale
content: Don't worry, Chief. Nothing crucial.

speaker: Nightingale
content: It's about the investigation into Whitestone Industries. It's basically failed.
Has any investigator been attacked?

speaker: Nightingale
content: No, the investigators are all fine. It's just that the progress with the investigation into Whitestone Industries isn't fine.
