content: It will only... bring you... the present you... even more pain.

speaker: Serpent
content: Ha...

speaker: Serpent
content: Why... Why?!

speaker: Serpent
content: Happiness... happiness is a luxury, something out of a sweet dream.

speaker: Serpent
content: I've tried so hard to find happiness for myself. But still, I can't have sweet dreams, can't experience true happiness!
Serpent makes many more dashes for the park. Each time, she is knocked down and dragged out.

speaker: Serpent
content: I just...

speaker: Serpent
content: Just...

speaker: Serpent
content: I just want to be happy... Forever...!!
Serpent lies outside the gate, too spent to pick herself up again. She stares blankly at the gray skies, as the sound of snakes, rats, and all sorts of insects crawling gets closer and closer.
Her emotions, her feelings, her obsession... all are being conveyed to you through the shackles, the whole kit and caboodle.
You clench your teeth, eyes red, feeling everything she has been put through.
Serpent is now lying at the edge of the Rust in the darkness surrounding Endless Carnival, motionless like a corpse but burning with desire for happiness.
You're about to wake Serpent up when you hear a sound that makes your hair stand on end.
It's the flapping of wings. You sense that Serpent is aroused by the sound, who raises her head and looks ahead...
Ahead is something you've seen before. Looks like it's been drawn here by Serpent's obsession. It releases some kind of crystal-clear liquid from its wiggling mouthpart.

speaker: Chief
content: Marv?! It's releasing Ambrosia! Serpent, get out of here...!

speaker: Serpent
content: Sweet... so sweet...

speaker: Serpent
content: I like the taste... Is this... my happiness...?

speaker: Marv
content: Hehe... Happiness, happiness, this is... happiness, you like it.
The next second, you and Serpent are transported by Marv to a pure white Realm of Dreams.
Serpent is still sitting on the ground seiza-style, murmuring about the taste of happiness, indifferent to the new landscape.

speaker: Marv
content: Strange, very strange...

speaker: Marv
content: Obsession, so intense, but... it's blank...

speaker: Marv
content: You have no happiness! Nothing! No food for me! You have no happiness, not at all!
Serpent freezes for a second before turning to Marv, her movements stiff and unnatural.

speaker: Serpent
content: What... did you say?

speaker: Marv
content: Your dreams, blank, blank! No happiness! Hahaha! You have no happiness! I'm so hungry...

speaker: Serpent
content: I've been looking for it for a long, long time, but I've failed. I wish I had it...

speaker: Serpent
content: But you... you wanted to eat my happiness?!

speaker: Marv
content: That's something you do not have.
The shackles throb violently, a sign that you're in the presence of a powerful Sinner.
Due to her own obsession or the influence of Endless Carnival, Serpent's Mania level is off the charts.

speaker: Serpent
content: Perhaps, your death can bring me happiness.
Serpent's snake appears on and wraps itself tightly around Marv. Serpent runs a finger over her captive's chest to where its heart lies and taps on the spot gently.

speaker: Serpent
content: It'll take only a moment, and you'll feel very happy too.

speaker: Marv
content: No! Please don't do this! Let me go, I'll give you happiness! Let me live! Live! Happiness!!
Marv stops flapping its wings and falls onto the ground in the white landscape. Squirming, it spits out a lump of sticky substance which gives off a sickly sweet smell.

speaker: Marv
content: My heart, it's Ambrosia. Take it, it'll make you happy!

speaker: Serpent
content: I was brought here after I drank this. Do you really think... I'll fall for it again?

speaker: Serpent
content: But, I accept your surrender.
Serpent squeezes Marv's heart, which then turns into a small bottle, and walks out of the white landscape.
You recognize it. It's the Bottle of Dreams!

speaker: Serpent
content: I... I have no happiness.

Serpent is in a deranged state of mind upon leaving the Realm of Dreams. The two of you, still linked through the shackles and now back at the gate to the amusement park, see a circus and its wagons drifting past in the bowels of the Rust.
Bringing up the rear is a crowd of Mania-infected monsters in different shapes and forms. They march toward a contaminated, eerie-looking red entrance, disappearing the moment they go through it.

speaker: Serpent
content: Monsters, just like me...
Serpent roams the streets alone once again, Bottle of Dreams in her hand.
She wants to continue her pursuit of happiness, but the blankness of the Realm of Dreams unsettles her no end.

speaker: Serpent
content: No one here... is happy.
Everywhere she looks, tribulations and miseries meet her eyes.
In a dark alley, an elderly woman is on her knees, pleading to a young man standing in front of her.
The voices stops Serpent in her tracks, who looks at them from a distance.

speaker: Old Woman
content: Please, have mercy! I can't lose this job. I've got a disabled family member and small kids to support!

speaker: Young Man
content: My hands are tied. I did everything I could! I could've just killed you, you know.

speaker: Young Man
content: Go now! Before it's too late. My boss might be here at any minute!
What is taking you so long?
You want to die too?!
A door is violently pushed open. A potbellied man walks out of the building into the alley.

speaker: Young Man
content: Boss, I... I will kick them out right now!

speaker: Boss
content: It's been ten minutes! If you don't want this job, just say the word!

speaker: Boss
content: You can't even handle a simple thing like this. Do I have to do it myself?!

speaker: Young Man
content: No, of course not. I'll do it now, right this second!
The young man wrenches himself free from the old woman hugging his legs, and, ignoring her tearful pleadings, pushes her over and over again.

speaker: Young Man
content: Go now! I can't save you. If you stay, I'll die too. And I don't want to die!

speaker: Serpent
content: It turned out that these corners where the brilliance of Eastside cannot reach... are as bleak as Syndicate.

speaker: Serpent
content: These dark alleys in Eastside are like black holes, sucking in those who are abandoned by happiness.
Serpent watches as the scene unfolds before her eyes. Her tone is even when she makes the remark, as if she were telling a story.

speaker: Serpent
content: You poor thing...

speaker: Serpent
content: My method of finding happiness doesn't work for me, because I'm a monster. You're a human; it might work for you...

speaker: Serpent
content: Then, do you want happiness...?

speaker: Serpent
content: Let me tell you, all of you, how to find happiness, okay?

speaker: Old Woman
content: Who... Who are you?

speaker: Old Woman
content: It doesn't matter who you are. Help me! Save me! Please!

There is a mountain of garbage in a corner of the alley. In the mix are glass bottles that have broken in half. They once held expensive alcoholic beverages and were thrown away unceremoniously as soon as the contents had been consumed.

speaker: Serpent
content: Good, good... When you're one of the downtrodden, when you're trapped in the depths of despair...

speaker: Serpent
content: Weep, be angry, be sad... and after all that, take action.
Serpent is still murmuring, her words mingled with the old woman's crying and the young man's mumbling.
You see Serpent... or you. You are tied together by the shackles. You share each other's emotions and sensations.
You can feel it: you and Serpent take hold of the old woman's hand and guide it toward a broken bottle.

speaker: Chief
content: Serpent, don't do it! That won't help her!

speaker: Chief
content: That won't solve her problem. It won't make her happy!

speaker: Serpent
content: Take it easy. Don't be afraid. This is just a story. Or you can think of it as a show!
The old woman, holding the broken bottle, turns to face the potbellied man, who is still ranting and raving not so far away. Serpent urges the woman on, her voice trembling slightly with excitement.

speaker: Serpent
content: Yes, just like this, go get your happiness!
Piercing shrieks and shrill cries intertwine. Soon enough, a pungent smell fills your nose.

speaker: Old Woman
content: No, No... What happened?!

speaker: Old Woman
content: I didn't want to do this, I didn't... It's her. It's her...

speaker: Serpent
content: Great, you did it! You took care of everything once and for all. Aren't you feeling better now?

speaker: Serpent
content: Feeling happy now, huh?
Serpent does a little dance of exultation, whereas the old woman falls on her knees, her face as white as a sheet, shaking all over and making no response to Serpent's question.

speaker: Serpent
content: What's wrong? ...You don't seem happy. How can that be...? But you're shaking...

speaker: Serpent
content: I get it... The happiness you just experienced was short-lived, not enough to offset your past sufferings.

speaker: Serpent
content: Hmm... Try this then!
You watch as Serpent produces the Bottle of Dreams, hands it to the old woman, and holds her shaking hands stable as she drinks the contents.

In Serpent's Realm of Dreams, a pure white landscape where Marv's heart resides, a painting with moving images appears in midair, which features the old woman and a kid, both smiling. Serpent is standing in front of the painting, admiring it in silence.

speaker: Serpent
content: Is this happiness? Her happiness...?
Serpent gazes at the painting, lost in thought. After a long while, she suddenly brightens up, like a kid who's just given candy.

speaker: Serpent
content: I get it now! I totally get it!

speaker: Serpent
content: This is how I'm supposed to find happiness!

speaker: Serpent
content: I should do what Marv did. I should help people by letting them drink Ambrosia and bringing happiness to them! This way, there will be happiness in my Realm of Dreams!

speaker: Serpent
content: I should decorate it with all of your happiness... This is the way for me to find happiness! My Realm of Dreams won't be blank anymore!

speaker: Serpent
content: So...

speaker: Serpent
content: Let me bring you happiness, okay?

speaker: Serpent
content: Drink it, and you'll enter a place of endless happiness and sweet dreams.

speaker: Serpent
content: This is your reward. You deserve it.
As the voice bounces around in your head, Serpent is walking toward you.
She opens her arms, as if to embrace you.
You raise your head slowly...

speaker: Chief
content: Stop bewitching me.
You now know the ins and outs of Serpent's story, about the Bottle of Dreams and about Marv.

speaker: Chief
content: Time to bring down the curtain, Serpent.
You can't indulge her any longer.
The mist around you clears; the dark gray walls of the interrogation room come into focus. The two of you have never left.
The floor is now scattered with what looks like magic props used in a circus. No idea how Serpent has managed to pluck them out of thin air.
You're grabbing Serpent's wrist, and she is holding a bottle of pink liquid, trying to force-feed it to you.

speaker: Serpent
content: You are awake...?!

speaker: Serpent
content: It was so close...

speaker: Serpent
content: If you had waited for one more second, you'd be experiencing... my "happiness" now.

speaker: Chief
content: You are a powerful Sinner, Serpent.

speaker: Chief
content: But... You have been put under my shackles.
Still grabbing her wrist, you pull her closer and look straight into her greenish-gray eyes.

speaker: Choice
options: Is this the last bottle of Ambrosia?

speaker: Chief
content: The Bottle of Dreams is still working, isn't it?

speaker: Serpent
content: Haha... Yes, it is... Because I still need happiness, because I still want to make you happy!
Serpent smiles, tears welling up in her eyes. This gives you a sense of déjà vu. That was how you met before the interrogation.

speaker: Chief
content: Why are you crying? I sense you're getting weaker, and your psyche is being eroded.

speaker: Chief
content: Are you... under the control of the Bottle of Dreams, Serpent?

speaker: Chief
content: Tell me where it is. I'll save you, Serpent.
Serpent shakes her head. Her hand holding the bottle, which you're holding up by the wrist, goes limp.

speaker: Serpent
content: You won't find it... Unless you enter the Realm of Dreams... to search for happiness.

speaker: Serpent
content: Can... can you really...

speaker: Chief
content: If that's the case, I'll do as you wish.
You guide her hand and down the pink liquid.
The sickly sweetness spreads out in your mouth and travels down your throat. Your scalp goes numb.

speaker: Chief
content: You are my Sinner... Whatever I tell you to do, you shall follow.

speaker: Chief
content: Now let me... into the Realm of Dreams.
The white landscape stretches in every direction, too bright to behold.
You take tentative steps forward. But with every step you take, the white landscape shudders, and some pieces of it fall off.
From the other end of the shackles come faint vibrations. You sense that she's still alive.
You also sense that she's asking for help.

speaker: Chief
content: There's no time left...

speaker: Chief
content: Don't let the Bottle of Dreams consume you!
Though Marv has been eliminated, its heart, the Bottle of Dreams, has become integrated with Serpent.
Serpent's obsession with happiness has allowed Marv's heart to latch onto her Realm of Dreams like a parasite.
It has to be fed constantly, or it'll start torturing its host ceaselessly.

speaker: Chief
content: Darn it!
You make a determined dash in the direction your shackles have pointed you.
The white landscape crumbles away, as black masses of sludge rise up to chase you like moths after light. Finally, you see Serpent ahead.

speaker: Chief
content: Serpent! Wake up!

speaker: Chief
content: Stop yourself from sinking!
Thud! Thud!
Your viscera contract viciously, and then an excruciating pain sweeps over you.
You see that Serpent has curled into a ball, howling and howling.

speaker: Serpent
content: Stop devouring... Stop!

speaker: Serpent
content: Every dream ends. I have... I have no happiness left... None at all...

speaker: Serpent
content: Nobody can save me... I...
The last piece of whiteness falls off. The white landscape is gone; in its place is a void of dark redness.
Serpent's eyes open abruptly, looking deep into yours.

speaker: Serpent
content: I'm going to be buried in pain...
All of a sudden, an avalanche of black sludge comes rushing down and swallows you up.
The black sludge makes its way into your mouth and your ears, suffocating you.
A myriad of pained voices howls in your ears.
"Get lost, you monster!"
"Ah? Why are you still alive?"
"You're just a tool for making money!"
"The world would be a better place without you."
"So disgusting!!"
You clamp your hands over your ears and close your eyes.
You force your legs to move, running desperately in the direction you are sensing.
You're getting closer and closer to her—you can sense it. But right before you can touch her, a huge winged monster rises up behind her.

speaker: Serpent
content: Can you... bring me happiness?

speaker: Chief
content: Wake up, Serpent!
Red thorny tentacles penetrate the all-encompassing darkness, spread to where the girl is, and ensnare her like snakes.

speaker: Chief
content: Don't let Marv and the Bottle of Dreams control you!

speaker: Serpent
content: Chief...?
All around, the howling voices are still tormenting your ears, as the gigantic black Marv runs through Serpent's body again and again to attack you.
It floats about, giving cries of joy and pain, and subjects Serpent to the sufferings the owners of those pained voices once went through.

speaker: Serpent
content: Painful... so painful...

speaker: Serpent
content: Make it stop...!

speaker: Serpent
content: Give me... your happiness!!

speaker: Chief
content: Serpent, I do not have a realm of dreams. You have no access to my happiness here.

speaker: Chief
content: You knew this, and you still brought me here... Why?

speaker: Chief
content: Isn't this... a cry for help?

speaker: Chief
content: It's torturing you, and it feeds on happiness, and you brought in someone whose happiness can't be accessed here.

speaker: Serpent
content: Yes, yes!!

speaker: Serpent
content: I've tried everything I could...

speaker: Serpent
content: But you don't recognize my happiness. I'll be tormented by pain forever!

speaker: Serpent
content: Tormented forever and ever!
Serpent acknowledges her pain and gives up her chase for happiness, and having seen this, Marv's shadow advances on you frantically.
You lunge forward, pick up Serpent, and roll to one side to avoid its attack.

speaker: Chief
content: Calm down, Serpent.

speaker: Chief
content: I cannot enter a Realm of Dreams after drinking Ambrosia, because all my happiness is rooted in reality.

speaker: Serpent
content: How can there be any happiness in the real world?! Under all the happiness... it's overrun with sufferings!

speaker: Chief
content: There is happiness, Serpent...

speaker: Chief
content: All my happiness and joy are on the other side of the shackles.

speaker: Chief
content: Everything I've been through since I woke up is a bundle of tribulations. My life would be nothing but pain if not for those... Sinners. They're my only source of happiness and joy.

speaker: Chief
content: They can't be recreated in the Realm of Dreams, because they're unique. That's why I'm not able to fall into a dream after drinking Ambrosia.

speaker: Chief
content: You're my Sinner too... In this place, I can't acknowledge the happiness you've collected. All I can do is share your pain.

speaker: Serpent
content: Share my pain...?

speaker: Serpent
content: You're not even willing to acknowledge my pain...

Black Marv picks itself up from the floor and soars into the air again, shrieking and screaming, a pink light blinking in its eyes. You also notice the same pink light on Serpent's chest. That's the light of the Bottle of Dreams!

The pink light blinks out, and Marv becomes more vicious, as if it has absorbed the power of the Bottle of Dreams. Serpent, on the other hand, seems to have had her energy sucked out, and she falls into your arms.
You carry Serpent on your back and, with great difficulty, dodge oncoming attacks.

speaker: Chief
content: Listen! I've never, ever denied your pain. And I've never expected you to accept or forget everything you've been through.
As you roll out of the way of an oncoming attack while protecting Serpent, a compact music box falls out of your pocket.

The music box, a ubiquitous item in the amusement park, starts playing music as a funny-looking circus spins on top. You brought it to the interrogation room and intended to give it to Serpent as a gift.
Serpent hears the music and opens her eyes slowly. Marv's attacks halt for a second. You seize the opportunity by reactivating the shackles to cut off the Bottle of Dreams' control over Serpent.

speaker: Chief
content: Serpent, do you know why you were rejected by the Carnival, even though you think you are a monster?

speaker: Serpent
content: W-why?
Serpent's quivering voice reverberates around the Realm of Dreams, sounding like she's about to cry.

speaker: Serpent
content: Because I am not allowed to be happy... even as a monster?

speaker: Chief
content: Because you're NOT a monster!

speaker: Chief
content: You are in great pain, but you are still a human. In fact, pain is what makes a human more human.

speaker: Serpent
content: But it's too painful, everyone is in pain. I don't want this... I don't want this!
Serpent curls up, and Marv breaks the restraint imposed by the shackles and turns into a black sludge, clinging to Serpent to drag her under.
Ignoring the sludge, you quickly thrust your hand in it, and grab Serpent to prevent her from sinking.

speaker: Chief
content: If you don't want this, you don't have to.

speaker: Chief
content: Like I said, I don't deny pain, but I don't glorify it either.

speaker: Chief
content: Because pain is pain, and it should be ameliorated with compassion and love.
Serpent looks up at you, tears still streaming down her cheeks, once again that kid wailing outside the gate of the amusement park.
You open your arms, just like she did, as if to extend her an embrace.

speaker: Chief
content: You told me everything about yourself, wanting me to experience what you think is happiness.

speaker: Chief
content: But that's not true happiness. True happiness comes from <i>love<i>, all the love you've been missing, under all the unavoidable shadows. Love can give you the strength to endure pain, to conquer sorrow.

speaker: Chief
content: And they gather to become happiness for you.
Perhaps because of your welcoming body language or your words, or both, Serpent's crying subsides. The black sludge stops churning and slowly retreats. And then she falls into your embrace.
The sky and ground stop shaking. The white light shines through once again.

speaker: Serpent
content: But I... I am already in this shadow of darkness.

speaker: Serpent
content: I've missed so much of this "love" you've been talking about, and that's because I don't know what it really looks like.

speaker: Serpent
content: My journey ahead is still paved with suffering.

speaker: Chief
content: Mine too, Serpent.

speaker: Chief
content: The first thing I learned about this world was all its danger and suffering. But I know that... danger and suffering are only one part of this world, and of me.

speaker: Chief
content: Do you remember what I said about why I won't fall into a dream after drinking Ambrosia?

speaker: Serpent
content: I do...

speaker: Serpent
content: You said your happiness is lying on the other side of your shackles.

speaker: Chief
content: Yes. And now, you're there too.
You shake Serpent's hand which you've been holding and give her a gentle smile.

speaker: Chief
content: Since both our futures will be full of suffering, why don't we search for love and happiness under that suffering, together?

speaker: Chief
content: From now on, you and I are tied together... Whether you still want to find happiness or not, whether you're able to find it or not.

speaker: Chief
content: So at least... let me share your pain in our journey ahead.
Serpent looks at you, tears budding in the corners of her eyes once again.
This time, the Realm of Dreams doesn't shake or shatter.
Serpent leans closer and rests her head on your shoulder, her breathing deep and rhythmic, as if she is about to fall asleep.

speaker: Serpent
content: Will you help me find true happiness...?

speaker: Serpent
content: If I stay by your side... I can find true happiness?

speaker: Chief
content: I don't lie, nor do my shackles.

speaker: Serpent
content: Uh, that's wonderful...
Serpent picks up her weapon and stabs herself in the heart.

speaker: Serpent
content: Save me then, Chief...
She places your hand on the gaping wound.
It's damp, warm to the touch, giving you the chills, and your fingertips feel the vibrations of a rhythmic heartbeat.
You activate the shackles, guide them down the open wound, and aim them at the object clinging stubbornly to the wound—a small, black moth.

speaker: Marv
content: Ahhh!!!
The white light gets brighter and brighter in the realm until you can see nothing. The only things you feel are the warmth of Serpent in your arms, and her strong heartbeat.
You stare at the remaining pieces on the table, lost in thought.
You've smashed the bottle in the Realm of Dreams to save Serpent. Only one piece remains. You now have no way of finding any clue linked to the bottle.

Everything you saw in the Realm of Dreams has vanished with the realm itself. The procession of monsters, the festooned circus wagon, the entrance where red contamination concentrates... You have no way of untangling their secrets now.
At least you now know that Marv was not created by Serpent with her power, but by someone else.

speaker: Chief
content: Who created this monster? Even the residues of its power were strong enough to control an S-class Sinner...?
The interrogation has ended, but more questions have arisen; it gives you a headache.

speaker: Chief
content: Baby step, baby step... Serpent is one of us now.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Speaking of which, can you please keep a rein on this Sinner of yours?

speaker: Chief
content: N-Nightingale?

speaker: Nightingale
content: Serpent, Sinner No. 948, turns training sessions into circus shows without permission, and repeatedly terrorizes other Sinners and staff members with her snake.

speaker: Nightingale
content: She has also been rude to others multiple times... And justifies her action by saying that she just wants to know if they love her. Don't you think you should do something about it?

speaker: Chief
content: Sigh...

speaker: Chief
content: I'll be right there. Adjutant, could you find it in your heart to tell her you like her very much?

speaker: Chief
content: That would help quiet her down a bit.

█Number: FAC-M-136-I
█File: Sinner's Arrest Report

A Sinner was arrested by the MBCC Arrest Unit in the latest locale where the myth of Mad Shears appeared. The arrestee was barely conscious at the time of arrest and is presumed to be Adela, an S-Class Sinner at large.
Adela is a suspect in a series of attacks on Sloane Street. Although no video evidence is available, it's believed that she's capable of mental interference. She's extremely dangerous and must be detained immediately.

*Annex—Performance in Serving Term (PERF):
The Sinner has been detained. An interrogation by the MBCC chief is urgently needed. Furthermore, MBCC supervision of the Sinner should be strengthened to keep her dangerous behavior in check.
You walk into the interrogation room. Seated at the table is Adela the Sinner. She looks up at you with a smile on her face.
She looks harmless, with her gentle smile and slight build. Appearances can be deceptive, however. You know how dangerous she is.
You put the PERF report and evidence bag on the table and sit down across from Adela. You notice that she's looking at your face with interest.

speaker: Adela
content: Oh, nothing. It's just that you look familiar.

speaker: Adela
content: I have a feeling that I've seen you before, but I can't place you. Have we met before?
You don't remember meeting Adela.
I guess this is our first meeting, Miss Mad Shears.

speaker: Adela
content: I was mistaken, then. Sorry!
You don't remember meeting Adela, but...
I'm not sure. Maybe we met on Sloane Street, where I was attacked by a mysterious being and lost the memories of that day. Have you been to Sloane Street, Miss Mad Shears?

speaker: Adela
content: Sloane Street? Yet another place I've never heard of.
Adela remains calm, unruffled by your accusatory tone. But she didn't contradict you when you called her Miss Mad Shears.
You're dealing with a seemingly cool-headed individual with a streak of madness.

speaker: Adela
content: You must have brought me here for a reason. Why don't you tell me how I can be of help, Chief?
You have so many questions about the Fog Alley attacks and Mad Shears herself.

None of the Fog Alley attacks was captured on film, and the victims and other people who had been on the scene, affected by the Sinner's power, couldn't remember what he or she looked like. The only thing the Arrest Unit had to go by was the reported sightings of Mad Shears. Despite the lack of information, they were able to apprehend Adela, who was losing control of her power at the time of arrest.
But you have a more urgent matter to deal with at the moment.
In a matter of days, S-Class Sinner Adela attacked eleven people, including MBCC staffers and Sinners. Ten of them have suffered mental impairment to various degrees.

speaker: Narration
content: You glance at Adela out of the corner of your eye. She's still wearing that gentle smile of hers. You have a hard time reconciling the harmless-looking woman in front of you with Mad Shears in the urban myth, or with the dangerous Sinner in the PERF report.

speaker: Adela
content: You don't look well. They're important to you, aren't they? And you're worried about their well-being?

speaker: Adela
content: You don't have to worry. They're not in any danger. They'll sleep it off, and when they wake up, they'll be as good as new.

options: Their well-being is none of your concern.
I'm not here to talk about them.

content: Here in the MBCC, everyone understands what they've signed up for. I've done everything in my power to protect them against Mania, and they're forever ready to face it when it's necessary.
What I want to know is why you attacked them.
I know you didn't do it to break out.

Many of the detained Sinners have tried to break out of the MBCC, but Adela hasn't been one of them. She didn't run away after her attacks. Instead, she sent the victims to the lounge area and stayed on the premises.
Why did you do it then?

speaker: Adela
content: Why? I was just trying to help them.

speaker: Adela
content: Their hair was too long. They carried it everywhere they went. It weighed them down.

speaker: Adela
content: It upset me to see them like that. So I cut the troublesome hair off to make them feel more comfortable. I didn't mean to cause any trouble. I'm sorry about that.
Adela sighs. She sounds sincere, even though her explanation is absurd.

speaker: Adela
content: Oh sorry, I forgot to explain it to you.
She brushes a stray lock of hair from her eyes, her smile never fading.

speaker: Adela
content: Your hair grows rapidly if you carry a lot of worries in your mind. The more worries you carry, the longer the hair.

speaker: Adela
content: I was just trying to help them get rid of their worries.
I have no idea what you're talking about.

speaker: Adela
content: Maybe only those who hold the shears can see the rapidly growing hair, but...
Her gaze is still on you, but her smile is gone.

speaker: Adela
content: I did make some mistakes in the past and got some people in trouble. But I won't make the same mistakes again.

speaker: Adela
content: I want to trim away other people's worries. It's always been my responsibility, and mine alone.
You don't fully understand what she's saying, but you've taken notice of a useful piece of information in her gibberish.
You said you want to trim away other people's worries?
Was that why you attacked those Sloane Street residents trapped in thick fog? To trim away their worries?

options: Produce the report on the Sloane Street attacks

content: It's discovered that all the Sloane Street victims suffered from memory loss, as have the MBCC staffers who you attacked.
Are you still claiming you're innocent?
You look into her eyes, trying to see if they betray anything.

speaker: Adela
content: I have no idea what you're talking about. I don't remember going to Sloane Street. I don't know anything about that place.
You've interrogated many Sinners. You know a liar when you see one. The eyes of the woman in front of you betray nothing; she seems very genuine.
Maybe she is a highly accomplished liar? Or maybe she's successfully trained herself to remain calm in whatever situation?
You can't decide which. You need more clues.
test
test
test
test
test
test
You have Adela's suitcase brought into the interrogation room. It's an important piece of physical evidence collected at the time of her arrest.
The lock on this exquisite suitcase is intact. When Adela notices how it's not been forced open, she gives you a compliment, still wearing her trademark smile.

speaker: Adela
content: You're quite the gentleman.
female_content: You're quite the lady.

content: I don't deserve such a compliment. I didn't open it, not because I didn't want to, but because I didn't get around to it.
Mind if I open it, Miss Adela?

speaker: Adela
content: Do I get to say no?
Still smiling, Adela gives a small wave of her hand.

speaker: Adela
content: Be my guest.
When you open it, you're greeted by a faint scent of lavender. Everything inside is neatly organized: clothes, toiletries, papers. The owner must be a very organized lady, you think to yourself.

speaker: Adela
content: As you can see, nothing out of the ordinary...
The papers catch your attention. They might bear some useful information.

options: Take the papers out of the suitcase

content: A business license for a hair salon in Ashby Village, receipts for furniture purchased in the Central Business District, a lease on an apartment on Sloane Street...
These papers—some old, some new, have been tucked away in one of the compartments.
Do you have anything to say about this?

speaker: Adela
content: You mean the papers? I have this old habit of saving receipts and stuff. They might come in handy. That's what I thought anyway.

speaker: Adela
content: Now I realize I might be wrong. They take up space in my suitcase, and I haven't found a use for them yet. I've never got around to throwing them away. Now I have a big pile of them.

options: I'm not asking about your habit.

content: Ashby Village, the Central Business District, Sloane Street, which I mentioned just now...
Do you know what these places have in common? The answer is the myth of Mad Shears.

speaker: Adela
content: Really? I didn't know that.

speaker: Adela
content: None of the names you just mentioned rings a bell.
Don't play me for a fool. Your power is unique. No other Sinner in all of DisCity can do what you do.

Adela looks unperturbed. You've met your share of accomplished liars in the past, and you've always been able to spot a crack or two in their veneer. The same can't be said of the woman in front of you.
Or maybe she is telling the truth. If that's the case, then the only possible explanation...

options: Did you erase your own memories?

speaker: Adela
content: We all have troublesome memories. I'm no exception.

speaker: Adela
content: Maybe I did go to those places. Maybe I did erase those people's troublesome memories, and mine as well. Either way, I have no recollection of any of it.
Adela remains unperturbed—disturbingly so, for some reason.
It makes no sense. Why would you do that to yourself?
A faint smile crosses her lips. And then she starts explaining.

speaker: Adela
content: Whenever I get the chance, I listen to my beloved customers' troubles and remove those troubles for them afterward, so that they can carry on with their lives worry-free. That's my calling.

speaker: Adela
content: After I free them of their unpleasant memories, including the memories of me, I do the same to myself.

options: What do you gain from all this?

content: Adela closes her eyes. She opens them moments later and answers your question.

speaker: Adela
content: Inner peace.

speaker: Adela
content: I gain inner peace. I'm free of worries.
It's ridiculous.
Are you telling me that every time you experience something unpleasant, your solution, your only solution, is to erase the memory connected with that experience?
You're getting worked up. Adela doesn't react strongly. She leans forward ever slightly, a concerned look on her face.

speaker: Adela
content: You look upset. Did I cause it?

speaker: Adela
content: Do you need my help?
Her words of concern send a chill down your spine. The fire of anger that was burning inside you just a moment ago has been instantly doused.
You blurt out your refusal.
I don't need your help. I don't want to have my "unpleasant" memories erased.

speaker: Adela
content: Are you sure?
She smiles, somewhat ruefully.

speaker: Adela
content: What a shame.
The brief exchange gets your adrenalin pumping. You can feel the shackles vibrating inside you.
Fortunately, Adela doesn't make further moves to escalate the situation. Now there's a brief silence.

You take a moment to calm yourself down. You now realize that your line of questioning is getting you nowhere. How do you expect to extract any useful information from someone who erases their own memories?

options: Go through the contents of the suitcase for other clues

content: As you go through the contents of the suitcase, Adela looks at you with a ghost of a smile on her face. Both of you remain silent.
You find a bunch of keys in a hidden compartment.
The keys are covered with rust. There's a tag attached to the key ring. On it are a few vaguely identifiable words.
12 Dorset Street, Apt. E.
Do you remember this place?
You've asked the question in a somewhat offhand manner, only expecting "I don't remember" or "It doesn't ring a bell" as an answer from her.
Your interest is piqued when Adela doesn't answer you right away. You look up and see her expression has changed slightly.
But it only lasts a second. And then she delivers what's become something of a catchphrase for her.

speaker: Adela
content: Doesn't ring a bell. Sorry.
Why did she hesitate? Why does she keep the keys? The address must hold great significance for her, you think as you run your finger over the piece of paper, which has grown soft with age.
These are the only keys in your suitcase. They're rusty, but you didn't get rid of them. They must mean something to you.
Dorset Street is where the myth of Mad Shears originated. Maybe that's where you lived before you became Mad Shears.

speaker: Adela
content: What does it matter where I lived before I became Mad Shears?
I don't know yet. It's worth checking out, don't you think? As part of the investigation.
I hope you can accompany me on this trip. Your participation is essential.
Adela shakes her head, her smile now tinged with resignation.
It's night. You and Adela are in a neighborhood crisscrossed by poorly-lit streets, searching for 12 Dorset Street.

speaker: Adela
content: Your plan is to visit an apartment that's probably laid vacant for more than ten years?
You nod.

speaker: Adela
content: Why did you take me on this trip, instead of one of your people? I'm Mad Shears. People speak about me with dread.

speaker: Adela
content: There won't be any witnesses here if you're attacked.
Gathering evidence is only one part of this investigation, and always has been. What I really want to know is what happened in your past that turned you into who you're today.
That's why I took you with me. It's a calculated risk.
Besides, Mad Shears doesn't attack people for no good reason. She only attacks those who have too many unpleasant memories, right? So I guess I'm not in mortal danger.
Adela smiles at your reply. The two of you continue to search for 12 Dorset Street in the dimness, and soon arrive at the destination.
In front of you is a dilapidated apartment building.
Here we are. Do you remember this place now?
You receive no response. You feel as if you were talking to yourself.
You come into the dark hallway. You click on your flashlight and shine it on the letters on the doors. Apt. E is at the end of the hallway.
You take out the keys found in the suitcase and insert them one by one into the lock. The lock is rusty, and so are the keys. You give each key a good wiggle before moving on to the next one.
Finally, by trial and error, you unlock the door and push it open.
Cough... Cough...

You're assaulted by a cloud of dust, so thick that you have to close your eyes for a second, so thick that the beam of your flashlight hardly penetrates it. And there's a musty smell lingering in the air.
Clack!
The bulb overhead buzzes into life. Dim light fills the room. You find your bearings and look to Adela. She is dusting her gloved hand with a handkerchief.
The electricity is still on. Who's been paying the utility bills?

speaker: Adela
content: Nobody. It's just a trick I used to save money, as many ordinary folks in Eastside do. I'm a bit surprised that the circuit is still working, though. We're in luck.
Adela leaves the room and returns shortly with some cleaning tools. She must have found them in the common area you just walked past.

speaker: Adela
content: Let me clear a space. It might take a while. Just bear with me.
Adela sets to work, with surprising efficiency. She takes out bags of trash, which end up next to the trash can downstairs. Soon, there isn't a speck of dust anywhere in the room.
It has taken her half an hour, and the room that sat neglected for years has been transformed. She has even put an antique-looking table and chairs, old as they might be, in the center of the room.
On the table is a faded tea set and a kettle of hot boiled water.

speaker: Adela
content: This is the best I could manage. Wish I had brought some loose tea leaves. We'll have to make do with only water; I don't want to bother the neighbors at this hour. Hope you don't mind.
I didn't know you had to be good at housekeeping to be a hairdresser.

speaker: Adela
content: Not every hairdresser.
Adela smiles.

speaker: Adela
content: It's usually just me in the shop. No employee. So I have to do everything myself.
Adela opens the window to let in the cool night air. It mitigates the musty smell in the room.
I feel like a guest invited here for tea or whatever beverage is on offer, and you're the thoughtful host.

speaker: Adela
content: (Chuckles) It's nice of you to say that. But I know what you're implying.
Adela gives a smile that doesn't reach the eyes.

speaker: Adela
content: I just did something I'm good at, to make it a bit more comfortable for you. I have no memory of any of the objects here. This is just like any old apartment to me.
Don't worry. I'm gonna help you remember. It's an essential part of my plan, after all.

speaker: Adela
content: Well, how are you gonna accomplish that?
Adela regards you with interest, her eyes twinkling with amusement and anticipation.
You can see other people's worries when you're holding your shears. That's your power, right?
My instinct tells me that you must have had many memories connected to this place. You erased them, because they made you sad. I want to see them, but I'll need your help to do that.
Adela is reluctant. She looks slightly uneasy.
Didn't you say that ridding people of their worries is your calling? Well, it's my worry, not knowing what happened in this room so many years ago.

speaker: Adela
content: It's just... I just don't think you'd see anything pleasant.
I don't mind. I'm used to seeing unpleasant things.
Adela sighs and gives in.

speaker: Adela
content: All right then, if that's what you want.
Adela holds out her hand. A pair of shears, black with long blades, materialize in a pool of dim blue light.
You grab the handle of the blades, and in the process, feel Adela's skin. It's cold to the touch.
In the blink of an eye, the room changes.
Hair is everywhere, twisting and bending as if it has a life of its own. It's in every corner, it's floating, it's all you can see.
You don't scare easily. You've seen many horrific things in your life. Still, the sight before you sends your heart palpitating.
This is what you see?
Adela responds with a mirthless smile.
You take a moment to collect yourself. And then you summon up the courage to reach out your hand.
You see a girl. She's sleeping. Someone is pounding at the door. She wakes up with a start.
She gets out of bed and switches on the light. It's three in the morning, according to the clock on the wall. When she opens the door, a woman collapses into her arms.
The girl glances at the hook that's used as a key holder. No keys are there.

speaker: Girl
content: Did you lose the keys again?
The girl half drags, half carries the woman to the bathroom, where, upon entering, the woman sinks down by the toilet and vomits into the bowl.
The vile stench of vomit is overwhelming. It stinks out the apartment that the girl took great care to spruce up during the day.

speaker: Girl
content: Mom, you must stop drinking. Or you'll ruin your body.

speaker: Mother
content: What did you say?
The woman says in a cold, shrill voice.

speaker: Mother
content: Don't you dare lecture me. You'd better keep your mouth shut.

speaker: Mother
content: I'm your mother. You literally owe me your life.

speaker: Mother
content: If it weren't for you, I'd still be with the ballet company, and I wouldn't have to degrade myself just to keep food on the table.

speaker: Mother
content: If I don't do this job, you'll starve, you ungrateful brat. So don't you dare lecture me!
The girl has tuned her shrieking mother out by this point. She's thinking about her next-door neighbor.
This irritable overweight neighbor is bound to come knocking on their door tomorrow, demanding an explanation for the racket coming from their apartment at three in the morning.
For some reason, the girl is amused by the thought.

speaker: Mother
content: What's so funny? You don't approve of what I do, is that it?

speaker: Mother
content: Answer me. Tell me what you're unhappy about.
The woman keeps up her ranting and raving. The girl doesn't talk back. She looks up and gives her mother a gentle smile.

speaker: Girl
content: Sorry, Mom. It's my fault. You must be tired. Let me get you to bed...
It's a heart-wrenching memory, which inspires in you a sense of vicarious pain.
Adela looks at you, as if curious as to how you're reacting to what you've seen. You meet her gaze.
Can you recall anything about the girl?
Adela shakes her head.

speaker: Adela
content: I have accessed a great number of unhappy memories. Nothing special about this one. It could belong to anyone in Eastside, or even in DisCity.
It's all right. You have quite a collection of unhappy memories here. Let's check out some more.
Maybe some of them will help you remember.
The sun is about to set. The woman is still sleeping.
The girl is making oatmeal at the stove. She adds sugar to the oatmeal and brings the dish to the table. The aroma is delightful.
A while later, her mother shuffles out of the bedroom and slumps into a chair at the table.
After two servings of oatmeal, some color returns to her mother's face.

speaker: Mother
content: Hmm...

The girl clears the table, brings out her mother's mirror and cosmetics, and put them on the table. They can't afford a dressing table, so the dinner table doubles as one. Her mother starts putting on make-up, getting ready for work.

speaker: Mother
content: It's in moments like this that I feel it wasn't such a big mistake to have kept you.
The girl doesn't say anything in response. She goes over to the sink, turns on the faucet, and starts doing the dishes.

speaker: Mother
content: Anyway...
The woman seems to be in a good mood. She's not in the habit of initiating conversations.

speaker: Mother
content: Have you given thought to your future career?

speaker: Girl
content: Not really.
The girl doesn't want to discuss what kind of career she wants with her mother. She doesn't see the point.

speaker: Mother
content: What do you mean not really? You can't sit around on your ass indefinitely. You have to contribute.

speaker: Mother
content: You have my looks. You can be a movie star or a model. Don't waste the good looks.
Taking to her daughter doesn't seem to distract the woman from the task at hand.

speaker: Girl
content: Hairdresser.
The girl gives a random answer, partly out of a desire to shut her mother up about the subject.

speaker: Mother
content: What did you say?

speaker: Girl
content: Hairdresser, I want to become a hairdresser.
The girl repeats her answer, with more determination in her voice.

speaker: Mother
content: Hairdresser? Why? Hairdressing is not a lucrative job.

speaker: Girl
content: I want to live a happy life. And you don't need to earn a lot of money to live a happy life. I'll be able to make my customers happy as a hairdresser, and if they're happy, I'll be happy too.

speaker: Mother
content: Instead of daydreaming about how to make strangers happy, why don't you spend some time thinking about how to make your mother happy? And your mother is unhappy, because she has no money.
The girl has nothing more to say to her mother. She knew the conversation wouldn't end well.

speaker: Mother
content: You're useless.
Having done her makeup, she rises to her feet and leaves for work.

The girl listens as her mother's footsteps recede and eventually disappear. She smooths down her hair, which hasn't been trimmed for some time and has grown somewhat unruly, picks up a curl of hair between her index and middle fingers of one hand, and mimes clipping it with the other.

speaker: Girl
content: Snip, snip, snip...

speaker: Girl
content: Worries, colorless memories... Make them all disappear.
Adela's expression doesn't change, but you can feel her hand trembling slightly through the shears.
You know she's not as composed as she makes herself appear to be. You press on, accessing another of her memories.
The girl's mother looks different. Radiant even. She has even taken out the brand shoulder bag which she saves for special occasions.

speaker: Girl
content: Are you not going to work?

speaker: Mother
content: I took the day off.

speaker: Mother
content: I have a date, with William.
The girl has heard her mother talk about the man more and more often over the past two months. And whenever she talks about him, she goes all smitten.
The girl has met William a couple of times. He's not as likable as her mother is making him out to be.
He's a patron of the place where her mother works. They've grown closer over time. Now they spend time together even on her days off.
The girl looks away from her mother's happy face, not interested in hearing about her mother's love life, and busies herself tidying up the room.

speaker: Mother
content: You don't want to know where we're gonna meet?
The girl ignores the question. Her mother volunteers the answer.

speaker: Mother
content: We're going to the Belphegor.

speaker: Girl
content: Oh...
It is an unusual rendezvous for her mother.
Not discouraged by her daughter's lack of enthusiasm, the woman continues to talk about her beloved.

speaker: Mother
content: I still feel like I'm in a dream.

speaker: Mother
content: William proposed to me yesterday. It still feels so surreal.
The girl's heart lurches at the news. A question comes out unbidden.

speaker: Girl
content: Did you turn him down?

speaker: Mother
content: What?! Why would I want to do that?

speaker: Mother
content: If I had turned him down, where would I find another man as handsome, considerate, and rich?

speaker: Mother
content: And he doesn't think of you as a liability. He's even promised to send you to one of those fancy boarding schools after we get married. You should be happy to have him as a stepfather.
The girl looks up, her neck stiff, her face expressionless.

speaker: Girl
content: I'm not going to any boarding school, fancy or not.
Her mother pauses for a second. And when she speaks again, her voice is piercing as usual.

speaker: Mother
content: Where else would you go?

speaker: Girl
content: You go live your happy life. I can take care of myself.

speaker: Mother
content: You're talking nonsense. You're my daughter. It's my responsibility to take care of you. I can't just...
The woman trails off, her eyes on her daughter's face.

speaker: Girl
content: You're the one being taken care of.
Smack!
The girl's cheek is burning with pain.

speaker: Mother
content: You want me to choose between you and him? You don't like him, so you're pushing him out of my life. Is that it?

speaker: Mother
content: Haven't I sacrificed enough for you? Do you want to ruin the rest of my life too, you ungrateful brat?
Her mother's shrill voice gives the girl a headache. Still, the girl responds with a soft voice, like she's talking to a baby.

speaker: Girl
content: You don't have to make a choice, Mom. Go to him.

speaker: Mother
content: What?
Looking at her understanding daughter, the woman is lost for words for a moment.
Anger fills her chest. The words that next come out of her mouth cut like a knife.

speaker: Mother
content: Get out! Get out of my house! I don't want to see your face ever again!
Without a moment of hesitation, the girl gets up and leaves the apartment.
When she steps out onto the street, the last of the light has faded, and a cold fog is rolling in to engulf the world around her.
She wanders around aimlessly. Seen through the fog, everything seems distorted—the trees, the buildings, the pedestrians. Her hair is growing fast, trailing behind her like a black ribbon.

speaker: Girl
content: Cut it off, and everything will be all right again...
She holds out her hand and feels something coolly metallic in her palm.
Snip, snip, snip...
You let go of the blades. The room returns to normal.
Adela's chest is heaving. It's obvious that seeing into her past must have been taxing on her.
She keeps her eyes closed, as if relishing those memories of pain and regret.
Those are your memories. That's how you got your power.

speaker: Adela
content: I erased them. Now they've come back to me.
She opens her eyes, which are now devoid of gentleness and composure. She gives you a weak smile.

speaker: Adela
content: Thank you for helping me recover these memories that I erased.
You erased your memories and your mother's, didn't you?

speaker: Adela
content: Yes.
Why did you do that?

speaker: Adela
content: I had no choice.
Her voice is uncharacteristically impatient.

speaker: Adela
content: You would've done the same thing if you were me.
But...

speaker: Adela
content: My mother and I, we both got what we wanted.

speaker: Adela
content: She wanted happiness, and I wanted her to have it without having to feel guilty about leaving me behind. So I erased our shared memories of us arguing, of us hating and hurting each other.

speaker: Adela
content: And I got my peace.
You lost each other.

speaker: Adela
content: I didn't care. My mother wouldn't have cared either.
Adela looks at you.

speaker: Adela
content: I made the right choice.

speaker: Adela
content: And you don't have to feel sorry for us.
Her voice is cold and distant.

speaker: Adela
content: It's about time we ended this farce of an investigation.
Adela turns around and makes for the door.
You grab her by her wrist.
Adela turns to face you. She doesn't look angry, but when she speaks, it's in a cold voice.

speaker: Adela
content: What else do you want from me, Chief?
How you want to proceed from this is entirely your business. It's just that I haven't got the whole picture yet. I have something to show you, and I want to hear your thoughts afterward.
You produce a tape. It's a recording of an interview with a man who has an intimate knowledge of the tenants of Apt E.
Does Adela really not care about her mother?

speaker: Javis
content: Kelly? You mean Mary Jane Kelly?

speaker: Javis
content: That name sure brings back a lot of memories. She liked to sit where you're sitting now.
It's early. Only a couple of patrons are in the bar. The waiter answers your questions while polishing glasses with a cloth.

speaker: Javis
content: Poor woman...

speaker: Javis
content: Kelly was once a promising ballerina. But as is the case with many young women in Eastside, fate was not kind to her. She was involved with a seedy man, who abandoned her when he found out she was pregnant. She lost her job, and at one point, she was close to becoming homeless.

speaker: Javis
content: She kept the baby.
The waiter stops polishing the glass in his hand for a second and looks to the doorway.

speaker: Javis
content: I still remember the first time I met her. It was raining that day, and she didn't carry an umbrella. She rushed into the bar soaking wet. She was desperate for a job.

speaker: Javis
content: So she started working here. At first, she only danced and sang on the stage. Later on, some patrons would pay for her to sit with them.

speaker: Javis
content: Life was not easy for her, or for many of us for that matter. And Kelly was—uh, how should I put it, headstrong.

speaker: Javis
content: One day, this man came to the bar.
The waiter clucks. It's not hard to see his disapproval of the man he's about to describe.

speaker: Javis
content: His name was William. Nothing happened at first. He was just one of the many patrons. But soon, he hooked up with Kelly.

speaker: Javis
content: He was the account executive of Phantom Entertainment. He was loaded, and handsome; he used to be an actor. He knew how to please a woman with sweet talk. Kelly fell for him in a big way. She was drawn to men like that.

speaker: Javis
content: Things seemed to be going well between them. There's one thing that bugged William though, which is Kelly's daughter. She was nothing like her mother, personality-wise. She was smart and independent. Sometimes, when I observed the way they behaved around each other, I couldn't help wondering if she was the mother and Kelly was the daughter.

speaker: Javis
content: William and Kelly's daughter met each other a couple of times. I could see that he didn't like her. So Kelly was stuck in the middle.

speaker: Javis
content: On the day William popped the question, he also brought up the subject of Kelly's daughter. He offered to send her to a fancy boarding school, which was just his way of getting rid of the inconvenience. There's a lot going on Kelly's face when she heard this. I thought that she would just storm out of the bar.
The waiter shakes his head.

speaker: Javis
content: But she didn't. She slapped the man across the face. She loved her girl, though she sometimes came off as cold and aloof.
What happened next?

speaker: Javis
content: Well...
The waiter sighs.

speaker: Javis
content: What happened next was a bit confusing.

speaker: Javis
content: When Kelly came to work the next day, we asked about her daughter.

speaker: Javis
content: Her reaction was strange. She looked at us in confusion and said, "Daughter? What daughter?"

speaker: Javis
content: We all thought she had had a fight with her daughter. That happens between mother and daughter. But from that day on, we never heard her talk about or mention her daughter.
And she married William?

speaker: Javis
content: No, she didn't.

speaker: Javis
content: They broke up. Right here in this bar, on the next night after his proposal. It's like the plot of one of those cheesy soap operas produced by Phantom Entertainment.

speaker: Javis
content: She chose her daughter in the end, it seemed.

speaker: Javis
content: She continued to work here for some time and then quit. I've never heard of her since.

speaker: Javis
content: I guess the whole experience must have made her realize that she had to find a different means of livelihood, if she wanted to give her daughter a normal childhood.

speaker: Javis
content: I'm just glad that she made the right choice in the end, immature as she was.
That's the end of the recording. You look up at Adela. Her face is a blank mask.

speaker: Adela
content: Why did you play me this?

options: I think that there might be a misunderstanding between you and your mother.

speaker: Adela
content: Misunderstanding? I don't think so. I would have been a burden to her on her journey to happiness if I hadn't cut myself off her life. I bet she had a comfortable life without me, whether married or not.
You and your mother had a difficult relationship, but I believe that it could have been mended. I have faith in the special bond between mother and daughter.
You eliminated that possibility by erasing her memories of you, even though she hadn't planned on leaving you in the first place.

She cared about you. She gave up what she thought would bring her happiness for your sake. If you hadn't erased her memories of you, she would have had a chance to make up for her mistakes; and you robbed her of the right to carry on with her life while burdened with the unpleasant memories.
You made the choice for her without asking what she wanted. You hurt her, and yourself.

speaker: Adela
content: It doesn't matter to me whether she had planned on leaving me or not. I'm past caring.
Adela cuts you off before you can say anything more. Her voice is cold as ice.

speaker: Adela
content: Those memories of mine, they don't feel like mine, they feel like somebody else's.
The long, black blades of the shears gleam dangerously, reflecting Adela's grim face.
At that very instant, a voice, soft like velvet, whispers in your ear.

speaker: Adela
content: Let's put an end to this.

speaker: Adela
content: You are kind and strong-willed. You always try to save those in trouble. But you don't have to worry about me. I have a quicker way to resolve my troubles.

speaker: Adela
content: I'll leave here and continue with my peaceful life, undisturbed and untroubled. I've left my past in the past.

speaker: Adela
content: We'll forget everything that happened today. It'll be like waking up from a dream...
Adela raises the shears, Mania energy swirling around its blades. You're the target.
You use the shackles on her just in the nick of time. The shears freeze in mid-air.
You're not one to give up, even when faced with strong resistance.
You say you want to live a peaceful life.
What is a peaceful life? Enlighten me.
Adela doesn't respond. She looks calm, but something is stirring below the surface.
Erasing every painful memory to restart your life over and over again, is that your definition of a peaceful life?

speaker: Adela
content: You don't agree?
No, I don't. That's escapism.
You're using the full power of the shackles to restrain Adela.
You're kind to those around you. You form bonds with them before erasing their memories of you without any hesitation. You did this to your mother, and now you're trying to do it to me.
It's cruel...
Now linked through the shackles, you and Adela see a shared memory that she has once removed.

speaker: Adela
content: ...This is the second time you've fallen in front of me.

speaker: Adela
content: ...You keep making a big mess of yourself, and I have to work overtime to tidy you up.
You're the one who saved me.
Thank you. Sorry for troubling you.

speaker: Adela
content: No worries. I just wanted to make you feel as comfortable as possible in my home. The most important thing was to get you to sleep well.

speaker: Adela
content: Now that you came to my little salon, you're my "customer."

speaker: Adela
content: What's that?
The fast-returning memory has thrown Adela into emotional turmoil.

speaker: Adela
content: Let go!
I won't. Stop running away from your past anymore, Adela.
You can't expect to have a meaningful future if you keep running away from your past.
Let's chat about something, Adela.
Like you always do.

speaker: Adela
content: What do you want to chat about?
Anything.
I'll listen to whatever you want to tell me. Just like what you did for me before.
Adela smiles. After pondering for a moment, she speaks up again.

speaker: Adela
content: ...I don't have anything in particular that I want to talk about. Let's just pick a topic that you want to hear.

speaker: Adela
content: ...Let me tell you the story of Mad Shears.

Her fingers brush behind your ears as she gently fixes your hair. The shears return to that intimate distance. One snip after another, your hair tips fly amidst the gleams again, but this time, you don't shudder.

speaker: Adela
content: A long time ago, there was a lucky little girl who didn't have any worries. She lived a peaceful life and liked it very much. She thought everyone was like her.

speaker: Adela
content: But that wasn't the case. Life was not good for everyone, and slowly, the people she loved sprouted long, long hair. Hair that could not be cut off. Hair that suffocated the soul.

speaker: Adela
content: Everyone lived in pain, and could only vent their discontent through words.

speaker: Adela
content: The girl wanted to help. She listened to them, took care of them, and did all that she could. Sometimes, their symptoms could be soothed by a cup of black tea, and other times by tears. But ultimately, there was no cure.

speaker: Adela
content: The girl finally realized she could do little. Those were other people's worries, which they can't let go of so long as they remember them.

speaker: Adela
content: So the girl prayed to gain the power to help people forget, and was bestowed a pair of magic shears.

speaker: Adela
content: Worrisome hairs are condensed and severed with each cut, vanishing forever into the ether. The people she loved no longer wallowed in resentment. They forgot everything that worried them, and regained their joyful smiles.

speaker: Adela
content: The girl's wish came true. She thanked the magical shears, and vowed to protect everyone forever.

speaker: Adela
content: ...That's the story of Mad Shears. Everyone lived happily ever after.
Mania energy pours forth from inside Adela's body, as her hair, feeding on her worries, grows wild.
You have no time to lose. Drawing on the power of the shackles, you strain to keep her from slipping further into madness.
It's natural to long for a worry-free life where every intimate relationship is perfect.
But nothing is perfect in life. We've all got to learn to live with whatever life brings us, the good and the bad.
I understand why you want to run away from your past. Because it weighs you down, it suffocates you. So you run and run, until it's become second nature to you.
But running away from your past will get you nowhere.
I know it'd be presumptuous for me to say this, but please, for yourself, and for those around you, stop running away from your past and give yourself another chance.
Try again, try to face the past, and start life anew with the people you care about.
You want to pull her to your side, but the intense disorientation caused by the shears makes it impossible to do so.

speaker: Adela
content: It's fine. Don't worry about me, Mr. Inspector. No one will get hurt...
female_content: It's fine. Don't worry about me, Miss Inspector. No one will get hurt...

speaker: Adela
content: I'm a hairdresser who trims away worries. Dealing with this kind of thing is my forte.
Under the aim of countless guns, Adela lets go of your hand gently.

speaker: Adela
content: Goodbye, ${PlayerName}.

speaker: Adela
content: Whether it's Adela or Mad Shears... You don't have to worry about me any longer.
The first rays of light come in through the open window and chase away the fog. Finally, the Mania energy dissipates along with the fog.
Adela's body goes limp. She's falling to the ground.
You step forward and catch hold of her.
The memories of what happened on Sloane Street over those two forgotten days and nights have come back to you, clear as day.

speaker: Adela
content: Mr. Inspector...
female_content: Miss Inspector...

content: Adela's voice is weak, but not without warmth.

speaker: Adela
content: You haven't changed. Still an interfering busybody.

speaker: Adela
content: You've got a real knack for sticking your nose where it doesn't belong.

options: I just wanted to do the right thing.

speaker: Adela
content: You did it.

speaker: Adela
content: You helped me recover those forgotten memories and made me realize I've thrown away so many precious things in my life.
You'll get them back.

speaker: Adela
content: I wish it were that easy.
Adela's voice grows weaker and weaker. Finally, she closes her eyes.
I'll help you get them back...

You're in a hair salon bathed in sunshine coming through the giant French windows. You're there with Adela. Ever since the Dorset Street investigation, her power has been kept in check with the help of the shackles. As a result, the number of attacks has decreased dramatically. But you know that that's not the end.

speaker: Adela
content: So this is your surprise for me?

You told me that you had stayed in the MBCC headquarters for too long and you were starting to feel claustrophobic. I figured that spending some time away from that place might make you feel a bit better. So, here we are.

speaker: Adela
content: Thank you, for doing this for me. I appreciate it.
The hair salon is located in a bustling pedestrian zone of Eastside, but for some inexplicable reason, there are no customers in the shop.
Adela doesn't seem deflated. She continues to wipe down the already-spotless table.

options: Sorry, I should've done some promotions.

speaker: Adela
content: It's okay.
You feel a bit awkward, but quickly relax when you see a woman coming in. You come up to her.
Welcome. New shop, twenty percent off for all customers.
She is middle-aged, with slightly disheveled hair. Lines have found their way onto her face, but it's not hard to see that she must have been a beauty in her younger days.
She looks at you in confusion, her hand holding a coupon for a free haircut.
She's the person you've been waiting for.

speaker: Adela
content: Welcome. Please come in and have a seat.
You turn around and glance at Adela. She looks calm, but you're sure that she recognizes the woman. It's her mother; it's impossible that she doesn't remember what her mother looks like.

speaker: Kelly
content: Oh, okay.
Adela comes near you and gives you a meaningful look. You shrug, and after a long second, she sighs with resignation.

speaker: Kelly
content: I've lucked out. See? A coupon for a free haircut.
Adela has left to get her tools ready. Kelly leans sideways and whispers to you. There's a playfulness about her demeanor that belies her nearly-fifty years.

speaker: Kelly
content: She's a good girl, I can tell. Very warm and friendly.

speaker: Kelly
content: Lucky you. Landed a beautiful and competent girl like that.
You wave your hand in embarrassment. You're about to set Kelly straight about the relationship between you and Adela when she returns with her tool kit.
Not saying a word, Adela removes a pair of scissors from the tool kit and starts trimming Kelly's hair.
Normally, Kelly, who has little tolerance for disrespectful behavior, would complain aloud about the hairdresser cutting her hair without asking her first.

But it feels different today. As she looks at the hairdresser's reflection in the mirror and feels her gentle fingers weaving in and out of her hair, she's overwhelmed with an inexplicable feeling of familiarity and security.
A while later, as if to break the silence, Kelly speaks to Adela.

speaker: Kelly
content: You know what? I used to know a girl who also wanted to become a hairdresser.
There's a slight pause in Adela's moving hands. She looks up at the woman's reflection, and nods with a smile on her face to show that she's listening, trimming the woman's hair all the while.

speaker: Kelly
content: I didn't understand back then what's so good about being a hairdresser.

speaker: Kelly
content: Now I do. A good haircut can put you in a good mood. A good hairdresser makes all the difference. I misunderstood the girl.

speaker: Kelly
content: Not really. It's just that the kids in the nursery are a headache for me.

speaker: Kelly
content: I wash their diapers, I get up before it's light, day in, day out. They run around all day like a bunch of monkeys. They're really doing my head in.

speaker: Kelly
content: You might not believe this, but I used to be a ballerina working for a big ballet company in Eastside. The world was my oyster back then. Even after I left the company, there was no lack of attention from men. Now, look at me, slaving away in a nursery.

speaker: Kelly
content: I don't know what I was thinking when I took that job. Those little Misters and Misses, they're the bane of my life.
Despite her continual complaints, it doesn't seem to you that she hates her job that much, judging by the expression on her face.
Adela is working away on Kelly's hair. Bits of hair are drifting onto the floor.

options: Have you heard about Mad Shears?

content: Your question takes Kelly by surprise. Confused, she answers your question.

speaker: Kelly
content: Mad Shears? Who's that?
Adela is also surprised by your question. The muscles of her hand holding the scissors tense, and her work slows down a bit.
For some reason, you're amused by Adela's reaction. And then you go on to explain the story of Mad Shears to Kelly.
It's a famous urban myth going around in Eastside. It's rumored that this Mad Shears can trim away other people's worries by removing the memories they don't want to face.
You can seek her out. Maybe she'll help you get rid of the worries you're having because of your job.
Kelly pauses for a moment and gives an embarrassed smile.

speaker: Kelly
content: I don't think that's for me...

speaker: Kelly
content: Those little monkeys give me hell, but I love them. That was just a bit of a complaint, that's all.

speaker: Kelly
content: Sometimes, I feel like, um, I had a kid once. It's a very strange feeling.

speaker: Kelly
content: I'd have made a terrible mother. I don't deserve to have a kid.
Kelly sounds despondent. And Adela has just finished her job.

The general shape of Kelly's hair hasn't changed much. All Adela did was cut off some split ends and make some small adjustments here and there. But the effect is obvious. She now looks a few years younger than before she had the haircut, and much more pleasing to the eye.
Kelly looks at her reflection and fingers her hair. For some reason, tears well in her eyes.

speaker: Adela
content: Are you not happy with the haircut?

speaker: Kelly
content: No, it's not that. I love the haircut. It suits me.

speaker: Kelly
content: The girl I mentioned earlier, she used to cut my hair in this style. It was years ago, and I've never changed my hairstyle since then. I have the feeling I knew her very well, but I just can't remember her name. It's very strange.
Her voice breaks. Realizing that she might have made a faux pas, she starts apologizing.

speaker: Kelly
content: Sorry, forgive me for talking nonsense. It seems to be a side effect of getting old, talking nonsense.
Kelly wipes the tears from the corners of her eyes. And self-consciously, she adds:

speaker: Kelly
content: I've been told that I have a tendency to ramble. I've been working on it, and I've been doing a decent job.

speaker: Kelly
content: I don't know what's wrong with me today. I can't seem to shut up around you.

speaker: Adela
content: Don't worry about it. I'm glad that you shared your story with us.

speaker: Adela
content: After all, it's part of my job as a hairdresser to listen to my customers' troubles.

speaker: Kelly
content: Thank you.
Kelly stands up slowly and walks toward the door.

speaker: Adela
content: Thank you for your business.
Kelly turns her head to look at Adela.

speaker: Kelly
content: Oh, thank you. You did a great job. I'll come back for your services again.
Adela nods, wearing a warm smile on her face.

speaker: Adela
content: Look forward to seeing you again.
Adela's eyes follow Kelly until she's out of sight. Adela then turns around to face you.
You look at her, feeling somewhat guilty.

options: I shouldn't have sprung this on you. Sorry.

speaker: Adela
content: You have nothing to be sorry for. I should thank you, if anything.
I just did what I could to help.

speaker: Adela
content: Despite the fact that you relish interfering in other people's business, enjoy making decisions for them, and use the shackles on them whenever you see fit.

speaker: Adela
content: Because of you, I can no longer erase my worries as easily as I did before. Because of you, I have to face the void in my heart and even the past I once left behind.

speaker: Adela
content: I feel exposed because of you, Mr. ${PlayerName}.
female_content: I feel exposed because of you, Miss ${PlayerName}.

content: You don't know how to respond to Adela's accusations.
Sorry...

speaker: Adela
content: Hair grows and grows, until it becomes a heavy burden. I've seen it happen to many, many people, and I've also seen their desire to be free of it. And then you showed up and told me you didn't want to get rid of it, because it's important to you.

speaker: Adela
content: I didn't understand at first. I didn't understand why you didn't want to have your worries erased for your peace of mind, or why you put yourself in harm's way and went to extraordinary lengths to catch me.

speaker: Adela
content: And after you detained me, you delved into my past and forced me to face what's really troubling me.

speaker: Adela
content: I had been running away from my past, and in the process, I had lost something precious.

speaker: Adela
content: Fortunately for me, you were always there for me every time I got lost.

options: I looked into your past, and I knew you wanted to stay.

speaker: Adela
content: Ah, before I knew it, my "peaceful" life had been turned upside down, and I didn't get to leave.

speaker: Adela
content: I still have the hairs associated with you, but I don't find them irritating. They feel like a reassuring weight that anchors me.

speaker: Adela
content: I feel that it's okay to keep them this time.
Adela looks at you, her eyes full of gentleness.

speaker: Adela
content: So...

speaker: Adela
content: Mr. Inspector, let me accompany you on the journey ahead, me with all my newly-recovered worrisome memories.
female_content: Miss Inspector, let me accompany you on the journey ahead, me with all my newly-recovered worrisome memories.

speaker: Angell
content: When you look up from this angle, you can see the sky through the narrow gap between the high walls of the alley. Despite its small size, the sky appears incredibly blue and vast.

speaker: Angell
content: I don't normally have the chance or desire to gaze upon the sky like this, but today, I realize it's quite nice.

speaker: Angell
content: The only thing that makes this feel less comfortable is the rock against my upper back. But that's okay, I've grown numb to the pain.

speaker: Angell
content: A flock of white birds fly across that tiny gap, free and unrestrained. In the meantime, my life is slowly draining away.

speaker: Angell
content: I always knew this would happen eventually, one way or another. After all, tomorrow is not guaranteed in this line of work; my life could end anytime and anywhere, nothing surprising.

speaker: Angell
content: My vision starts to blur, a sign of hallucinations due to extreme weakness.

speaker: Angell
content: I hear jumbled footsteps that appear close one moment, and distant the next.

speaker: Angell
content: Out of nowhere, I think of the goldfish in the corner of the living room, their blood-red tails swaying in the water before my eyes.

speaker: Angell
content: Some say that before death, one sees what they can't let go of, and the person they want to see the most.
...Angell? Angell!

speaker: Angell
content: Seems like it's true.
What happened?! Stay with me...

speaker: Angell
content: Because just before I fall into complete darkness, I see your face.
In a corner of the MBCC cafeteria, you sit opposite Angell at a rather inconspicuous dining table.
Between you are a few empty plates that were filled with side dishes, along with a stack of bowls.
Since it's not mealtime, there aren't many people in the cafeteria, but Angell still receives some curious gaze from the people who pass by.
However, she remains calm and composed, like she usually does, and finishes her sixth bowl of red bean soup, unfazed by the unfamiliar surroundings.
Finding Angell unconscious in a Syndicate alley nearly sent you into a panic. You hastily rush her back to the MBCC for urgent medical care.
Fortunately, the physical examination showed that she simply passed out from extreme hunger, and she was fine after some glucose.
When was the last time you ate...?
Angell eats quietly, even elegantly, but her speed is astonishing. As her bowl empties once more, you push your untouched bowl of red bean soup towards her.
