She accepts without hesitation, simply nodding her thanks.

speaker: Angell
content: Can't remember, but it's been quite a while.
Angell brushes off the question, clearly unwilling to dwell on this topic.
Okay...
After she devours another bowl of soup, you offer:
Do you want more? If it's still not enough, I can cook some more...

speaker: Angell
content: Thanks, but it's okay.
She sets down her spoon and the empty bowl.

speaker: Angell
content: I'm full now.
She looks at you, then at the empty bowl in front of her, and smiles with a hint of nostalgia.

speaker: Angell
content: Your red bean soup tastes amazing, just like always. I never thought I'd have it again.
She smiles at you across the table, reminding you of the time back at the safe house. You smile back at her.
Nonsense. I'm right here. You can always tell me when you have a craving.

speaker: Angell
content: ...Thank you.
After expressing her gratitude once more, Angell gets up, ready to leave, but you hold her back.
Angell, wait.
I know you're more than capable of getting out of the Bureau whenever you want, but would you mind if we talk a bit more elsewhere? It's just the standard procedure around here.

speaker: Angell
content: What procedure?
Despite not knowing what you mean by "procedure," Angell follows you, heading deeper into the Bureau.
Angell takes a seat in the interrogation room, scanning the shackles hanging from the armrests, various security devices in the room, and the video camera in the corner that's been turned off.

speaker: Angell
content: Is this where you usually interrogate Sinners?
She sounds indifferent, showing no emotion, but you can't help feeling nervous. Worried she might misunderstand, you hurriedly explain.
Don't worry. There are no guards outside, and I didn't put the shackles on you. This is just the standard procedure for all new Sinners.
Just think of it as us finding a quieter place to talk, okay?
Angell's gaze softens as she looks back at you.

speaker: Angell
content: I'm alright, but you seem really nervous.
Angell leaves you speechless for a moment, then the corner of her lips curls up. Seemingly in a good mood, she initiates a new topic of conversation.

speaker: Angell
content: You want to talk, let's talk.

speaker: Angell
content: Let's start with... how did you find me?
You didn't just stumble upon her, of course.
After sending you back, Angell vanished completely like a raindrop fallen into the deep waters of the dark web.

It's difficult for ordinary people and the authorities to reach the deeper ends of the dark web. You found nothing despite using every possible means and searching through every channel you could think of.

But yesterday, you saw a post about "Angell's whereabouts" on the surface of the dark web. You took your chances and bought the information from them, and that's how you found Angell, who had passed out on the street.
Someone was selling your intel on the dark web yesterday. Is it because you made too many enemies in the kidnapping mission, and they wanted revenge?

speaker: Angell
content: ...It could be.
Angell doesn't seem too surprised, merely nodding thoughtfully.
She doesn't question who provided the information, but you couldn't tell her even if she did. The poster used a disposable account, and you couldn't find any useful information from it.
Speaking of which...

options: Could you help me with something?

speaker: Angell
content: What?
You open a file and push it across the table to Angell.
test
test
test
test
test
test
This is the operation report for the entire case.
I couldn't see many things clearly when they were happening, but I'm beginning to piece them together while reviewing the case and writing the report.
There are still some details I'm not too sure about. Could you help verify them?
Angell glances at the report and says without hesitation:

speaker: Angell
content: Yes, I can.
Alright, let's start with the background of this case.
With the reconstruction of the West District underway, the gangs found it increasingly difficult to survive, forcing them to flee to this mysterious dark web created by some unknown figure.
The dark web's covert and intricate nature allows them to carry out a series of attacks on key figures in the West District, including me, making it difficult for the authorities to respond quickly.
Angell narrows her eyes, holding back what she wants to say and letting you continue.
This was our analysis at first, but as the operation unfolded, we realized we had overlooked a very important force—
The masterminds hidden in the deeper area of the dark web.
Angell nods slightly in agreement.

As you said before, people like us only have access to the surface of the dark web. So, at first, I assumed that the first round of the counterattacks I secretly organized using your account had eliminated all the enemies.

But then you told me about the deeper area of the dark web, and the results of the operation showed that there indeed was a hidden force—the real gang leaders and the Hypercube company who are upset by the new mines.
They were the real masterminds and financiers. The people we caught before were just thugs and minions.
We didn't realize they were behind the scenes and almost let them slip away. If it weren't for your covert assistance, we would never been able to solve the case.
Angell's gaze flickers.
You flip through the report and point to the "Joint Operation" section.
You put news about me on the dark web, asking those who were interested to come find you with their offers. But selling me for a good price wasn't your real intention, was it?
Since there's nothing to hide anymore, Angell admits openly.

speaker: Angell
content: No. I leaked your information to bait them.

speaker: Angell
content: Those people were so eager to get rid of you and the news threw them off. They were worried you'd be rescued, so they hastily recruited some people to make a second assassination attempt.

speaker: Angell
content: They were ill-prepared. That's why they gave themselves away, and finally gave you the chance to solve the case.
You nod with a smile.
And that's not the only time you've helped me.
Angell looks at you, surprised and puzzled.

speaker: Angell
content: What do you mean?

I'm talking about the time you went out every night and came back injured. You never told me what you were up to, but come to think of it, you must have been dealing with those who wanted to kill me, right?

speaker: Angell
content: ...Yes.
For protecting me all this time.

speaker: Angell
content: No need.
Angell shakes her head, but her gaze softens.

speaker: Angell
content: I was just doing what the client wanted. The instructions were very clear: kidnap and guard the MBCC Chief until delivery, no killing involved.
You ponder for a moment, a new doubt crossing your mind.
Was that job from a gang?

speaker: Angell
content: Yes.
Isn't that strange? Those people clearly wanted me dead.
...Perhaps the job was tampered with?

speaker: Angell
content: It's possible.

A dark web case is inherently far more challenging to tackle than typical cases, and this time we even found out about the dark web's deeper layer. What exactly is this dark web? What encryption technology does it use? When was it developed, and by whom?
Angell goes deep into thought for a moment.

speaker: Angell
content: I only know that the technology used by the dark web is extremely bizarre and highly secure, making it difficult to crack... I know nothing about its origins and creators.
Then, who do you think has the ability to interfere with the jobs in the deep dark web?
After a brief silence, Angell lowers her gaze.

speaker: Angell
content: No idea. I'm just a contractor who only cares about completing the jobs.
I see.
Angell moves in her seat to adjust her posture, and you catch a glimpse of a few wounds under the hem of her clothes that weren't there before.
I've got everything I need. Now, let's talk about you.
What happened to you? How come you passed out on the streets?

speaker: Angell
content: I had no money, couldn't afford to eat.
Such a candid and straightforward answer leaves you momentarily speechless.
This is not an easy thing to admit openly, but Angell shows no sign of embarrassment.

speaker: Angell
content: This job has caused me a great deal of trouble. Though you might have caught all the gangsters, many others took this opportunity to seek revenge. Many of them were also hitmen.

speaker: Angell
content: They thought I had betrayed the dark web and turned to the authorities. I know a lot of their secrets, so those guys are trying to get rid of me.

speaker: Angell
content: I've been followed closely by them 24/7. I couldn't withdraw money, or go back to the safe house to get food...

speaker: Angell
content: That's why I ended up like that.
Despite her light and matter-of-fact tone, you can imagine the hardship she went through.
...Did that job affect your credibility on the dark web?

speaker: Angell
content: Not really. No one cares about credibility there. After I deal with those guys, business will only get better, because I've proven myself.

speaker: Angell
content: Besides, it's not like I betrayed my client. I did exactly what the job asked me to do. They wanted me to protect you by kidnapping you, they will thank me for it.
Good.
The conversation winds down. Angell stares at you for a bit.

speaker: Angell
content: Anyway, thanks for searching for me and the meal. Once everything is settled, I will repay you.
You understand the meaning behind her words—she doesn't plan to stay at the MBCC.

speaker: Angell
content: What do you mean?
Well, you've got nowhere else to go right now, why not stay here for a couple more days?

speaker: Angell
content: ...Is this how you want me to repay you?
Yeah. I happen to be on a break at the moment, so you could join me for a bit of a holiday.

When you were living together, you had been trying to show her the beauty of the sunlit world by picking certain jobs for her, but you also wanted to take her out on the streets to experience the life of ordinary people.
This is something you've always wanted to do since you first met her, but you never had the chance. And now, this might be the perfect opportunity.
She always says she's meant to lurk in the shadows, but once she feels the sun's warmth and witnesses the flourishing lives under the sunlight, perhaps she will change her mind.
She frowns, likely sensing your intention.
However, perhaps due to your help this time, or because she's gotten used to you planning things for her, she cannot bring herself to refuse.
Noticing her silence, you give a sly smile.
Alright, since you're not saying anything, I'll assume you agree.
I'll plan our trip for the next couple of days.
Fresh and organic veggies! Have a look!
The new farmers' market in West District today welcomes a new stall and its two owners. You and Angell, each sitting on a small stool, have occupied a prime spot at the entrance.
Under a canopy supported by four sticks, a variety of fresh, dewy vegetables are laid out. You got up at dawn to fetch them from the farmers.
Tomatoes, cabbages, potatoes, cucumbers, carrots! We have all you need!
Dressed in casual clothes and a straw hat, you energetically call out to potential customers, all the while watching the people as they come and go.
After the Rustfire incident, the West District's economy is slowly reviving, which has led to the emergence of large markets like this.
Despite the simplicity of the stalls and the occasional troublemaking thugs in the area, the market remains lively and busy.

It's early morning, yet the market is already bustling with customers and vendors, their enthusiastic shouting filling the air. Everyone's eyes are filled with anticipation for a better life, a sight you've never seen in the West District before.

speaker: Angell
content: You do this on your break?

A calm, deep voice comes from beside you, prompting you to turn your head and look at Angell. Unlike you, who has blended into the bustling market, she stands by your side like a shadow, still carrying the black bag with her blade.
Why not? Just peddling some vegetables. Compared to what I do at MBCC, this is definitely a break.
Besides, I've always wanted to experience the life in West District.
All we have here are trivial daily matters, no assassins or mercenaries seeking revenge. The biggest danger is probably someone slipping on a banana peel or some rotten vegetables on the ground.

speaker: Angell
content: Really...
After what you said, Angell gradually relaxes, lowers her guard, and starts to observe this new environment.
She looks at the customers and vendors, listening to them chatting, gossiping, or haggling, her eyes filled with curiosity and interest, seemingly fascinated by everything happening around her.

You smile without saying anything, and continue calling out to attract passersby. Right now, you blend in perfectly with the hundreds of ordinary people bustling about for their livelihoods in the market.
Who could have guessed that the two people running this little stall are a former fearsome hitman on the dark web and the hero of the West District.
Despite sitting at the perfect spot and your voice going hoarse from shouting, not many people have stopped by your stall for some reason.
As you take a moment to rest your throat and drink some water, a lady stops in front of your stall, and you immediately put down the water bottle to greet her:
Hey there, want some tomatoes? Some of the freshest ones you can find around here! Look at the size, and the color!

speaker: Middle-Aged Woman
content: ...Hmm, not bad. Give me two of these, and some cabbage as well.
She holds the tomatoes in her hand, scrutinizing them from all angles before finally nodding her head.

speaker: Middle-Aged Woman
content: I'm buying a lot here, how about a discount?
She raises her head with the imposing look she uses when haggling with vendors, but as soon as her gaze locks with Angell's, she backs away a little, quickly putting down the tomatoes.

speaker: Middle-Aged Woman
content: Hey!

speaker: Middle-Aged Woman
content: ...I changed my mind. You can keep them.
You immediately grab the lady, attempting to salvage the deal.
Of course, I'll give you a discount. How about I round it down for you?
She seems tempted by your offer, but after sneaking a glance at Angell again, she shudders and pushes your hand away, hurrying off while muttering in fear.

speaker: Middle-Aged Woman
content: Oh dear, is she trying to kill someone with that look?
Angell turns to you, somewhat puzzled.

speaker: Angell
content: ...Is she talking about me?
Probably...

speaker: Angell
content: What's wrong with my expression? This is my serious face, and many clients liked it. Why isn't it working here?
Her puzzled expression amuses you. You wave your hands, sitting back down and stretching lazily.
Forget it, nothing's wrong with slow business. It's nice to get some sun.

speaker: Boy
content: Granny, you're back!

speaker: Old Lady
content: Sigh, that stingy butcher... We're all neighbors here, and he wouldn't even help butcher a chicken...

speaker: Boy
content: Ah...

speaker: Old Lady
content: Don't worry. I'll keep asking around. You'll definitely have your chicken soup today.
You look towards the fruit stall next to yours. The stall owner, an old lady, is holding a tied-up chicken, while her grandson stands beside her, looking dejected.
Hello there, can I help you with anything?
The old lady walks over, holding her grandson by the hand and slightly lifting the chicken in her other hand to show you.

speaker: Old Lady
content: Sigh, one of our relatives has sent us a chicken, and I thought a chicken soup would be perfect for my grandson here, so I went to ask the butcher to handle it for me.

speaker: Old Lady
content: But he refused to help because the chicken wasn't bought from his shop.
That's unfortunate...
She hesitates as she looks at you and Angell, somewhat embarrassed.

speaker: Old Lady
content: Um... Could you help me butcher this chicken?
You turn around and ask Angell.
Angell, do you think you can help out?
Angell answers with her actions instead—she swiftly draws a gleaming blade from her bag, staring intensely at the chicken in the old lady's hand, chilling the air around her.

speaker: Boy
content: Ahhh! She's so scary. Granny, forget the chicken! I wanna go home... Wahhh...

Just as you are about to take the chicken from the old lady and hand it to Angell, the grandson starts crying. He snatches the chicken from his grandma and runs back to his stall, cowering in a corner and trembling as he stares at you and Angell.

speaker: Old Lady
content: Huh? Sigh, this kid... Please don't take what he said to heart. Sorry for taking up your time...
Most likely feeling apologetic, the old lady picks out a generous amount of vegetables from your stand without haggling. You pack a full bag of vegetables and hand it over with a comforting smile.
It's alright. Are you sure you don't need help with the chicken?

speaker: Old Lady
content: Thank you, but don't worry about it. Oh, and I've been watching you for a while; this peddling business isn't as easy as it looks.
The old lady continues as she takes Angell's hand and pats it. The latter seems a bit uncomfortable but doesn't pull away.

speaker: Old Lady
content: When I first started my stall, I couldn't sell anything either, but it got better over time. Keep at it. My stall is just over there. We're friends now, ask away if you need help.
Of course, thank you very much.
After finishing the conversation and watching the old lady return to her stall, you are soon drawn to the commotion not far away.
The nearby vendors and customers all drop what they were doing and walk over; you also grab Angell and approach the crowd to see what's happening.

speaker: Hooligan
content: Stop talking and pay up!
You squeeze into the crowd. A few arrogant hooligans come into view, snatching a few crumpled bills from an emaciated man's hand.
The leader scoffs contemptuously, then frowns and curses after counting the money.

speaker: Hooligan
content: That's all you have?! What the **** do you mean?

speaker: Hooligan
content: We work hard here every day to maintain order and keep this place safe. You think it's easy?

speaker: Elderly Man
content: This is all the money I've earned these past two days. My wife is sick and I have to take care of her, please have mercy...
The old man pleads pitifully.

speaker: Hooligan
content: Did I ask? I don't ******* care even if she dies! Just give me my money, you hear?!
With new markets and profits, the rats that once lurked in the shadows now emerge. These troublemakers are some low-level thugs who couldn't even join a gang in the past.
Now that almost all of the gangs are gone, they seem to think that they can finally take over and rule the West District.

These thugs have grown accustomed to dominating this place, and the people of the West District have endured oppression for so long. Even though times have changed, the influence of gangs still lingers, and people are still too intimidated to fight back.

speaker: Boy
content: Baddies! Stop bullying him!

Suddenly, a young but sharp voice breaks the silence. You look down and see the boy who Angell had scared earlier; he has let go of his grandma and made his way to the front of the crowd, his face reddened as he yells at the thugs.

speaker: Hooligan
content: Get lost, you little brat.
The thugs ignore the boy, shoving him impatiently. He tumbles to the ground, scraping his palms and knees.
Seeing this, his grandma rushes over, positioning herself in front of her grandson like a lioness guarding her cub, and begins cursing at them.

speaker: Old Lady
content: Protection fee? Nonsense! What did you protect?!

speaker: Old Lady
content: When the West District was in trouble, none of you scum was there. Now that the Black Ring is gone, you're out here pushing us around again.

speaker: Old Lady
content: Let me tell you, times have changed. Those gangs have all been wiped out, and now you're just a bunch of nobodies. You don't get to boss us around anymore!
Hearing the old lady's words, murmurs ripple through the crowd, with many nodding in approval, their faces no longer as terrified as before.

speaker: Hooligan
content: You ************* wanna mess with me?!
Hecate

speaker: Hooligan
content: I'm going to teach you a lesson, and show you who runs the West District these days!

Just as the leader of the thugs is about to strike, his bat is suddenly sent flying by someone. The crowd only catches a glimpse of a silver flash before Angell's blade is already inches from the thug's throat.
You quickly ask the spectators to step back a bit to prevent them from getting hurt, and to give Angell room.
Careful now, everyone step back a little...
Before you can finish, Angell has already kicked those guys out of the market's fence. They scream as they fly over your heads, crashing onto the newly paved road outside with a dull thud.

These lowlifes may lack other talents, but they are experts at fleeing for their lives. From the brief "fight" just now, they also realize that Angell is clearly not someone they can mess with, so they immediately turn tail and bolt.
After a brief silence, thunderous applause and cheers erupt around you and Angell.
Even the little boy who was scared of her gets up from the ground, runs over, and grabs the hem of Angell's clothes, his eyes sparkling with admiration.

speaker: Boy
content: Wow! You're amazing, miss...
Angell is obviously taken aback by his reaction. Unsure of how to respond and afraid of frightening him again, she only averts her gaze, frozen in place.
You step forward with a smile to rescue her by taking the boy's hand and sending him back to his grandma.
But before you two can catch a breath, the cheering subsides, and the customers at the market, along with the vendors, rush over to support your business.
The two of you busily collect money and bag vegetables. The once hard-to-sell vegetables are quickly swept up by the eager crowd, leaving not even a single leaf behind.
Good, good, we can close the stall early.
You count the money you've just collected and are quite pleased with today's earnings. You hand half of it to Angell.
She looks at you, puzzled.

speaker: Angell
content: What's this for?
Your pay for the day.

speaker: Angell
content: But I did nothing.
It's not all about the goods in business, advertising is important too.
You handled those thugs skillfully; that was great advertising.
You pack everything up, throw away the empty boxes that were used to store the goods, and put the stools, cloth, and sticks into a corner. You stretch leisurely afterward.
Alright, everything's sold out and now we've got some money, let's go enjoy life.

There aren't many people at the cinema on a weekday afternoon, with only six or seven viewers scattered in the vast place. As you and Angell take your seats in the back row with drinks and popcorn, the movie begins.
The film being shown is a recent blockbuster, an epic story adapted from the incidents of Rustfire and Drifter Camp.
The movie starts with a wide shot of a city in ruins, with a massive and intimidating Black Ring floating above it.
Your eyes light up. Pleasantly surprised, you tug at Angell's sleeve.
Wow, look at that Black Ring, it's pretty well done. Looks like they really invested in the CGI for this movie!

speaker: Angell
content: ...Okay.
Angell glances at you and nods in agreement under your expectant gaze.
The movie's reaching its climax. As one of the witnesses of the story and character inspirations for the movie, you feel like you're revisiting those indelible memories.
The journey was fraught with many hardships and difficulties, but now that it's all in the past, looking back on those times brings a sense of reflection and relief...
Everyone's efforts and perseverance bear meaning, and those sacrifices were not wasted. Darkness will fade, and the hopeful future that once seemed unreachable will eventually come.

Just like what you saw at the farmers' market today, the West District still has a long way to recovery, and various problems remain. But now, people no longer remain silent in the face of oppression and choose to stand up and fight back.
They all truly believe that the era of despair has become the past, and the future of this place will only get better.
As you contemplate, many amusing anecdotes from those tough times also reemerge in your memories.
In the movie, the group of protagonists overcomes obstacles and vanquishes their enemies along the way, making for a thrilling journey to witness.
Hold on, this part is way too exaggerated and idealized...
We were in such a mess back then; everyone was wounded and scattered. It was far from heroic.

In the most critical moments of battle, a character keeps cracking jokes to lighten the mood, drawing not only eye rolls from his companions on the screen but also a few muffled laughs from the audience.
Hahaha, that line does sound like something he would say...

Immersed in the movie, you find it difficult to suppress your comments with someone sitting next to you. As you enthusiastically share your thoughts, you turn and notice Angell looking at you as well.
You smile, a bit embarrassed, and lean in to whisper.
Sorry, you can't focus because I'm talking too much?

speaker: Angell
content: No.
Angell pauses, then adds.

speaker: Angell
content: Your commentary... is very interesting.
After saying this, Angell slowly turns her head back to focus on the movie, the light from the screen flickering on her profile.

At the end of the film, a once sunless alley is finally bathed in light, and the laughter of children dispels the dreadful silence. The last shot lingers on a small white flower blooming amidst the dark mire.
The screen fades to black, and the lights in the cinema come on, leaving a long list of credits rolling.
With the soothing end credits music playing, the other viewers slowly exit, leaving just you and Angell in the now empty cinema.
Feeling stiff from sitting for so long, you stretch and turn to Angell with a smile.
What do you think of the movie?

speaker: Angell
content: Why do you ask?
After overcoming all the hardships, these people finally live happily and comfortably in the new West District. Sounds pretty good, don't you think?
Angell is smart. She picks up on what you're trying to say, but she shows no reaction and simply replies softly:

speaker: Angell
content: Yeah, but I'm not like them.

speaker: Angell
content: From the very beginning, they had their goals and beliefs. They wanted to bask in the sunlight, and to achieve that goal, they tried their best to break free from the darkness.

speaker: Angell
content: At the same time, there are also people like me on the fringes of the world, who don't see themselves in that picture.
What kind of life do you want?

speaker: Angell
content: The life I have now is good enough. I've already chosen my path.
What made you lose your desire for the sunlight? How did you become who you are today? And why did you make such a choice?
You have many questions, but looking into her tranquil eyes, you suddenly don't know where to start.
There's a moment of silence between you two, Angell is the first to break it.

speaker: Angell
content: I've heard that in your world, people like me are considered criminals that need to be captured and shackled, is that true? I'm not too sure.
...Yes, if you don't mind.
Her eyes darken.

speaker: Angell
content: But I won't stay at the MBCC.
I know.
Let's turn this into a commission. I put the shackles on you, and you tell me about your past.

speaker: Angell
content: What do you mean?
We have a bail regulation here. Under this regulation, I have the authority to determine whether a Sinner can be released on bail by evaluating their cases and current condition.
As for the shackles, think of them as a form of security. I won't use them to control you or restrict your freedom.
Angell thinks for a moment, then nods.

speaker: Angell
content: Sure.
The crimson glow of the shackles fades, and Angell remains impassive. You pull back your hand.
Alright, let's start from the beginning.
How did you end up in this profession?

speaker: Angell
content: ...I was once just an ordinary Syndican.
Angell falls silent, then begins to share her past with you for the first time.

speaker: Angell
content: I was born into a humble family. We led a simple life in a small rented place. We weren't rich, but we didn't have to worry about food and clothing. Although we couldn't afford luxurious meals, my mother would often make sweet red bean soup.

speaker: Angell
content: One night, my parents were caught in a gang shootout on their way home. They were hit by stray bullets and died on the spot, covered in blood. I was still very young at that time.

speaker: Angell
content: With my parents gone and little savings, I couldn't afford the rent. I had no choice but to leave our home and look for ways to make a living.
So you joined the dark web to make a living?

speaker: Angell
content: Uh-huh.

speaker: Angell
content: In the early years, I had been everywhere in Syndicate and tried many different jobs. But it turned out I was only good at fighting, killing, and doing dirty work for other people.

speaker: Angell
content: For a long time, I was living hand to mouth, barely scraping by. And one day, I heard about the dark web and how people could make money there, so I registered an account and became a contractor.
As Angell recounts these old stories, her gaze becomes distant.

speaker: Angell
content: Back then, I just wanted to earn more money so I wouldn't starve to death, that was it.

speaker: Angell
content: But as I got more jobs, I also made more enemies. To stay alive, I had to stay vigilant at all times.

speaker: Angell
content: I couldn't leave my house, nor stay in the same place for more than two months. My blade was always within arm's reach. The curtains in my house had to stay drawn at all times, or the windows had to be painted black...

speaker: Angell
content: It was during that time that I slowly lost my sense of taste, forgot what an ordinary life looked like, how to find joy in beautiful things, and began eating merely to survive.
What kind of life was that? The safe house ensured her safety, but it also became her prison.
You can't help feeling sorry for her.

speaker: Angell
content: When I was in the safe house, I occasionally reminisced about the days when I lived with my family, but those memories felt so distant, like they belonged to a past life.
So you thought about the past... have you tried going back to living a normal life?
Angell smiles, her voice carrying a hint of resignation.

speaker: Angell
content: I tried, but you can see how that turned out.

speaker: Angell
content: After landing a few big jobs, I was able to establish myself on the dark web. Over time, I earned enough to buy a new identity and start a new life.

speaker: Angell
content: And I did that. I went to a new place with good security and privacy.

speaker: Angell
content: I stopped going on the dark web. I still had to be constantly aware of my surroundings and hide my identity, but I could occasionally get out of the house.

speaker: Angell
content: There was a small restaurant near my place. They had red bean soup, so I would sometimes go there to get some.

speaker: Angell
content: I thought I could live out the rest of my life quietly like that, but it only lasted for three months or so.

speaker: Angell
content: Some people from the dark web found me. They thought that red bean soup place was one of my hideouts, so they killed the owner and his family, ruined that beautiful restaurant.

speaker: Angell
content: The only survivors were a tank of red goldfish.
And you brought them back with you? Are they the same ones you keep in the safe house?
Angell shakes her head.

speaker: Angell
content: That was many years ago. Those goldfish all died, but since then I have been keeping a tank of goldfish.
Her tone remains flat, but your heart feels heavy.
Sorry for bringing up these sad memories again. It must have been difficult for you.

speaker: Angell
content: Rather than sad, "liberated" might be a better word to describe what I felt.
Liberated?
You look up in surprise, confused.

speaker: Angell
content: During the days of living on the edge, I longed for the peace I once had, and each night I dreamed of wonderful things.

speaker: Angell
content: But during that seemingly peaceful time, I was always thinking about how to hide my identity and flee my past. My dreams were consumed by my life on the dark web as well.

speaker: Angell
content: After that incident, I realized that I had become a shark accustomed to the deep waters.

speaker: Angell
content: I can't respond to kindness from others, fearing I might harm innocent people. I'm too sensitive to malice and hostility due to my Mania; I might overreact instinctively and accidentally hurt someone.

speaker: Angell
content: But now, none of that really matters anymore.

speaker: Angell
content: Because I've finally fully adapted to the dark web and I can live well here. The dark side of the city always exists, but there's no need to worry or flee because I can survive on this side. The darkness is no longer my enemy; it has become my "haven."

speaker: Angell
content: This is my past.
Angell recounts her past calmly, like an unfeeling onlooker. Her tone and expression reveal no sadness or regret.
What should you say to her?
Stunned by her story, you're at a loss for words, even though you're usually so eloquent.
Should you tell her you understand her, that the past is behind her, and she should keep hope alive? Or maybe ask her to trust you and step into the sunlight together?
None of them feels right, because she doesn't need comfort or encouragement.
You still want to convince her, yet after learning about the blood and tears she endured in the past, everything you say feels weak and inadequate.
Angell watches you quietly, as if she has already seen through you.

speaker: Angell
content: ...${PlayerName}.

speaker: Angell
content: I know you're used to saving and helping people. When you see someone stuck and suffering in the abyss, you try desperately to pull them out like it's your responsibility.

speaker: Angell
content: But not everyone needs or yearns to be saved. You can't save everyone.

speaker: Angell
content: I know you've more than once asked me to go back with you into the sunlight.

speaker: Angell
content: You can try to persuade me, or show me the beauty of your world again and again, my answer still remains the same.
Having said that, Angell quietly waits for your reply. You see a hint of helplessness in her eyes, but also her determination.
The screen has turned pitch-black, seems like the movie's credits have already ended at some point. With no music in the background, all you can hear is your breathing in the silent cinema.
...I see.
After a long while, you let out a sigh and nod.
I'm still trying and asking these questions only because we've never had the chance to truly talk about it.
I knew how you might react, but I still had a glimpse of hope that maybe I could persuade you.
But now that you've told me how you feel about this, I won't insist.
You're right, perhaps I've been too caught up in the so-called "savior" role, but I hope you will understand and forgive me for being stubborn and selfish.

I've always believed no one is meant to live in the shadows, and that deep down, everyone yearns for the warmth of the sun. I thought you didn't want to come with me because you don't trust this side of the world.
I thought that if I tried harder and proved myself worthy of your trust, I could ease your worries and pull you out of the mire.
But now it seems, that's not the case.
I was wrong.
You pause, then look back at Angell, flashing a broad smile.
I respect your decision. I won't impose my own beliefs on you anymore.
Since you can't accept this kind of life, I won't go against your wishes and force you to stay.
After finishing your sentence, you get up from your seat.
Let's go, the movie has ended for a while now.
As night deepens, the bustling MBCC detention area gradually quiets down. Even the night owls have retreated to their rooms, now fast asleep.
Angell is lying on the bed in the temporary room you've arranged for her, unable to fall asleep.
Days are passing by, living this lie, Not knowing what we're looking for. Gray, these walls are gray and there's no sky. There is no hope, there is no soar. I know somewhere there must be more.
The familiar lyrics and melody echo in the headphones. Normally, this song would lull her to sleep quickly, but not tonight.
Her brain refuses to rest, her thoughts uncontrollably drifting back to the time she spent with you, the memories replaying over and over in her head.
...Haven't started cooking yet. Just about to make the red bean soup you asked for.
Do you know any doctors? Or a safe underground clinic? You should still get it checked. The wound is deep, it might get infected.
I'll miss the time I spent with you.
Sometimes you just stumble upon a chance that brings you into the sunlight, where you can meet people who need help or have good intentions.
If my offer doesn't sound bad... come with me.
The next second, her thoughts drift from the safe house to the cinema this afternoon.
But now that you've told me how you feel about this, I won't insist.
I respect your decision. I won't impose my own beliefs on you anymore.
Since you can't accept this kind of life, I won't go against your wishes and force you to stay.
Angell knows how frequently she fails to convey her thoughts.

She's not talkative, and doesn't believe that "talking" has any function beyond exchanging information. She speaks as little as possible at work already, and there's little need for her to express her emotions and feelings.

However, over these past few days with ${PlayerName}, she seems to have spoken much more than she has in her entire life. Normally, when she's by herself, she can go two weeks without uttering a single word.
The opinions or feelings of others mean nothing to her, so she doesn't care if her words cause any misunderstanding.
But after meeting ${PlayerName}, she worries about whether she can fully and accurately express herself for the first time.
There have been others who wanted to "save" her, but most of them only told her that the bright world could offer her protection and allow her to live an ordinary life in peace.
They never considered whether someone like her could truly get used to, and live a good life under the sun. However, Chief has thought of everything.
He's different.
female_content: She's different.

speaker: Angell
content: Maybe I didn't make myself clear.
Angell sighs and turns. She doesn't want to upset you, or cause even the slightest misunderstanding because she can't express herself.

speaker: Angell
content: I should explain tomorrow...
Angell doesn't remember when she fell asleep.
The safe house is shrouded in a misty, soft light. She sits on the couch as you come in, with shopping bags in hand.
As usual, you complain about her living habits and the mess she's made in the house, and surprisingly, you suggest cleaning up together for the first time.
Just as she's about to take the broom, Angell is jolted awake by a sudden alarm.
She stares at the unfamiliar ceiling for some time before remembering that she is leaving MBCC this morning, just as she said before.
After washing up, Angell leaves the room and walks towards the MBCC gates. The corridor is empty due to the early hours.
Just as you promised, no one is there to stop Angell as she leaves. It's quiet, and she senses no danger, but she hears her own heartbeat, pounding and quickening.
Her anxiety peaks when she sees you waiting at the gate from afar, and she stops in her tracks.
You hear her footsteps and walk towards her.
Angell feels the weight in her hands and looks down, noticing a thermal bag. It appears somewhat bulging and blocky, and feels warm to the touch.

speaker: Angell
content: This is...?
I bet you're leaving on an empty stomach since it's still early. I packed these from the kitchen. All your favorites. You can eat them on the way.
Oh, and there's this...
You fish out a key from your pocket and hand it over to her.
This is the key you gave me. You can stay there when you go back.
I've been cleaning that safe house, but I didn't touch anything in your room. The goldfish you left with me are all alive and well. If you're staying in the safe house, I can send them back.
I've already topped up your electricity account. It should be more than enough to last a couple of years.
If there's an emergency, you can still use your backup generator. I've charged it and put it in the bottom drawer of the living room cabinet.
Also, that broken microwave in your kitchen, I've asked someone to fix it. It's working fine now.
I've stocked the fridge with fresh ingredients. You can make something simple. If you don't feel like cooking, there are also ready meals and instant food you can heat up in the microwave.
I've written down the reheating instructions for each item on memo papers and stuck them on the boxes.

Oh, I also wrote down a red bean soup recipe and put it on the fridge. Since you like it so much, you can try making it yourself. The instructions are detailed, so you shouldn't have any major issues if you follow them step by step.
Hmm... I guess that's everything? I was going to tell you all this when you returned to the safe house, but I never thought you'd go out of your way to avoid me.
You try to lighten the mood since Angell hasn't said anything, but she takes it very seriously and begins to explain:

speaker: Angell
content: I wasn't avoiding you. I just couldn't go back because of those loose ends. I didn't want to risk bringing them home.

speaker: Angell
content: But now that it's almost over... I'll head back.
That's good to hear.
Relax. I was just messing with you.
You give a comforting smile, but she grips the key tighter, and pauses for a moment before she continues:

speaker: Angell
content: I'm okay. There's just something I want you to know.
Sure, I'm listening. Take your time.
Reassured and encouraged by the look in your eyes, she continues.

speaker: Angell
content: It's true that what I said in the cinema yesterday was my lifelong beliefs, but I choose not to stay not because I dislike you, or hold something against you.

speaker: Angell
content: On the contrary, I cherish the time we spent together in the safe house, and I've never held a grudge against you for hiding things from me.

speaker: Angell
content: You showed me a different world and things I've never seen before. It was a great memory.

speaker: Angell
content: Before I met you, I hardly ever took orders. I used to spend time investigating the targets to make sure I could bring myself to do it. A simple kidnapping job is quite rare on the dark web.

speaker: Angell
content: It was nice to have you picking orders for me. I actually like those odd jobs that can help people, but I could never find them on my own before because browsing and filtering through all that malicious information always tired me out.

speaker: Angell
content: I did have my own selfish reasons back then. I didn't want you to leave. Even though I knew we didn't belong to the same world and I couldn't stop you from returning to the sunlight, I still wanted to stay with you a bit longer.
It was a lovely memory. Whenever I think back on those moments, they always warm my heart.
You unconsciously smile and nod.
That was a rare, peaceful time for me too. Even though I knew it couldn't last, I didn't want it to end either.
So, I was actually a bit sad when you decided not to come with me, but I do feel better now that I know you cherish that time as much as I do.
Angell sighs softly.

speaker: Angell
content: The dark side of the world will always exist, and the darkness in my heart can't be erased. I couldn't come with you because I was afraid that a monster like me, or the dangers around me, might hurt you.

speaker: Angell
content: ...I was also afraid that after being exposed to too much warmth and kindness, I wouldn't be able to continue living in the shadows.
She pauses for a moment, then looks at you seriously again.

speaker: Angell
content: But this time, I want to thank you properly in person. I'm grateful for everything you've done, and I'm happy that we met.

speaker: Angell
content: In the past, my way of reminiscing about the past involved only red bean soup and goldfish, but you and that interesting job have given me a new idea—I could do what I'm good at and cut through the darkness to guard those who live under the sun.

speaker: Angell
content: I'm happy with myself as I am now, just as you are proud of your way of life. I hope to receive the blessing of a dear friend.
Angell remains as calm and composed as ever, but this time, you feel the sincerity and hope in her every word.
It's like she's finally laying her heart bare before you. Suddenly, you also feel an indescribable feeling in your heart.
So, you take a deep breath and look into her eyes, and say to her earnestly:
I understand how you feel.
Your body somehow turns into a small wooden cutout, and is placed onstage.
I'm content now that I know you don't actually dislike those people and that kind of life.
I didn't mean to show you the "life under the sunlight" to change your lifestyle.

I just wanted you to see a different kind of life and possibilities, so you'd know that here, there are people who will protect and support you, just like how you've been protecting me from the shadows.
If you ever feel tired in the shadows, you can come out to bask in the sun. I will always be here waiting and welcoming you.
As you speak, you're also watching Angell's reactions.
She loosens her grip on the strap of her bag, and her face relaxes as if a massive burden has been lifted from her heart, bringing her a sense of relief.
After getting to know her, you realize that this cold assassin isn't emotionless, she's simply much more reserved compared to most people.
Despite her habit of hiding and suppressing her feelings, you can begin to recognize them in the subtle details, such as her slowly relaxing eyebrows and the faint curve forming on her lips.
But you're wrong about one thing.
You intentionally put on a stern face, changing the subject.
Sure enough, Angell raises her eyebrow slightly, confused but patiently waits for you to continue.
I'm stronger than you think. Those things in the shadows have been trying to get rid of me forever, but they've never succeeded. So trust me, you can't hurt me.

And you're not some monster either. You're one of the strongest people I've ever met. As you said, shadows will always exist, but if everyone living in there was like you, it would actually be a good thing for all of us.

I also believe that, someone as strong as you can always find the strength to live in the darkness no matter what, and the warmth and kindness you feel will only fuel your determination to go further.
Angell seems touched, and you smile softly. The sky has lost its morning glow at some point, revealing a clear blue behind the golden clouds.
I shouldn't keep you here any longer. I've truly said everything I wanted to say this time.
You can go back to your life. I won't bother you anymore in the future. Just take good care of yourself, alright?
Well then... Goodbye, Angell.
You wave goodbye at her, but she holds you by your wrist as you turn back.

Angell parts her lips urgently, but averts her gaze the moment your eyes meet. It's like she has something to say but fails to find the words. Instead of rushing her, you simply enjoy this rare sight of her struggling with herself.
After a long time, she finally lifts her head like she's ready to risk everything, and says earnestly.

speaker: Angell
content: I don't want you to stop bothering me.
You raise your eyebrows. You're trying to "force" her to say this, but hearing it from her still catches you by surprise.
You clear your throat, adjust your expression, and nod solemnly.
Okay.
It seems your prompt and brief answer leaves her puzzled and uncertain. Angell hesitates for a moment before asking another question to make sure.

speaker: Angell
content: You... do understand what I mean, right?
Yes, I get it.
To reassure her, you continue:

On second thought, you're really bad at doing chores. I can't but worry even if you follow the recipe step by step. Making a mess is one thing, but what if you somehow blew up the kitchen or caused a safety hazard?
How about I drop by the safe house sometime and teach you in person? That should be much safer.
Angell doesn't feel upset because of your slight teasing. On the contrary, she simply nods.

speaker: Angell
content: You're right.

speaker: Angell
content: You're always better at doing chores.
On a similar morning, you experience a similar farewell.
You watch as Angell walks into the distance once again, but this time with a completely different feeling.
You can barely contain your smile thinking about how she awkwardly said that she didn't want you to stop bothering her.
Perhaps this is why a proper goodbye is so important—it makes reunions something worth looking forward to.

speaker: Vague Voice
content: You...
Your consciousness returns, and you realize you're in an entirely white space. Time and space are distorted here, and only a translucent figure in the distance comes into focus.
You open your eyes wide, but still can't see the almost shattered figure clearly, nor can you hear her voice clear.
She approaches you, seemingly smiling. Her familiar smile makes your heart race.

speaker: Girl in the Dream
content: ...Come here... my...
She responds to your question, her lips moving as if saying something. But no matter how hard you try, you can't hear her.
Sensing something, the white shadow also reaches out to you. Just before your fingertips touch...
[Scene Transition: Chief's Office. Transition, screen shakes, alarm sound]
Opening your eyes again, all you can see in your blurry line of vision is a glowing object. Your comms is ringing sharply, giving you a headache.
You lay your head back on the desk, but the familiar figure from your dream appears before your eyes again. This is not the first time she has appeared.
For some reason, you've been plagued by the same dream recently. The white shadow repeatedly appears in your dreams, approaches, then dissipates as you awaken.
Why? Is it Mania? Aftereffects from a mission? Or...
You've forgotten a lot of things; thinking it over is no need. It's better to pull yourself together and face the upcoming work.
[Transition, ringing again]
You hear a noise again—someone's ringing the doorbell.

options: Get up and open the door

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, it's Nightingale. Regarding the dark web operation, we have made some new progress.

speaker: Nightingale
content: In recent days, a hacker named <000> has been extremely active on the internet. The virus she created is able to force its way into operation systems and take over control. It's extremely dangerous.

speaker: Nightingale
content: More importantly... we have detected Mania on the virus. Chief, we've discovered that this hacker is a Sinner and is likely connected to the dark web.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Yes. That's why we need you to interrogate her personally this time.

speaker: Nightingale
content: This Sinner has been captured and delivered to the Bureau at the moment. Chief, please be careful during the interrogation.

speaker: Nightingale
content: And...

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, you sound very tired. Please don't overexert yourself and get some rest after work.

speaker: %u
content: Now... let's go meet this troublesome guest.
You feel stilled upon seeing the girl.
It's not that she looks any special. In fact, she doesn't stand out that much; she seems just a typical Eastside fashion girl.
You feel nothing weird, but more a strong sense of déjà vu... you feel like having seen her somewhere before.
Hi... What a slowpoke. I've been waiting for you for a long time.
Of course! I've been snooping on you through the web for months, but this is our first time face-to-face.
Remember? I've saved you several times.
The girl with cat ears winks at you, hinting at something.

speaker: %u
content: You are...
Bingo!
Nice to meet you. You can call me 000. From now on, I'm a Sinner under the MBCC's care.
Your Intelligence Department is really impressive. They immediately found my hiding spot from just a small bug I left behind.
So, you've cracked quite a few of the Easter Eggs I hid online. Impressive! Too bad I don't have any prizes on hand, so consider this a verbal high-five.
You stare at the girl in front of you—since you've entered, her gaze lingered on you only for a few seconds before turning away to observe the room.
The sense of déjà vu grows stronger. This conversation seems to have happened once before, but you have no memory of it, and your mind is spinning.
You hear a crisp, sudden sound... 000 snaps her fingers in front of you.
Hey, focus please? Get on with your questions. I am about to go pick out my bed soon.
You realize you've been staring at her for too long... long enough for her to notice and look back at you.
Her reminder makes your mind a bit clearer. Putting aside the sense of déjà vu, you get down to business.

speaker: %u
content: ...Nice to meet you, Sinner 000.

speaker: %u
content: I hope you will cooperate with this interrogation. I do have quite a few questions for you.
test
