speaker: %u
content: Since July N.F. 114, a series of destructive acts have occurred on the DisCity web. According to the Cybersecurity Center's investigations, these were caused by hidden virus data.

speaker: %u
content: On July 4, Councilor Craig Rouen was the first to make a report. He claimed that his comms device was hacked, his information leaked, and that he was blackmailed. Did you do this?
Yeah.
Speaking of which... After sealing the deal, I didn't even have time to log out before he snitched... What a shameless councilor, eh?

speaker: %u
content: ...So you broadcasted a video of him cheating with his assistant on a billboard screen on the Fifth Avenue?
That's right! Too bad the admin pulled the plug just as the video was getting spicy. What a buzzkill.
The girl's face and tone show no hint of guilt; she seems purely disappointed that the video wasn't fully shown.

speaker: %u
content: Also, half a month ago, Phantom Entertainment's website was hacked—the homepage was replaced with a simple sketch created using the system's default drawing software.
Actually, it might be a stretch to even call it a "sketch." It looked like it was produced by a toddler who had never held a brush...

speaker: %u
content: The drawing depicted two yellow ducks... frolicking each other. It hogged Phantom's homepage for nearly three hours, during which its subscribers were unable to access any other content.
That's right! That's also my doing!
Their soap operas are all just two people in ridiculous melodrama with a dull happy ending. How can that compete with the artistry of my drawings?
You should thank me for saving Eastsiders three precious hours of their lives.
The girl's indignant jabber almost makes you laugh.
The documented crimes are all quite absurd: Hijacking DisCity's radio signals and blasting "Elysium Island" for seven hours straight... The incidents are all pranks with no clear motives.
Hmm... Truth, justice, and fairness in the world?
The girl blinks dramatically, looking mischievous.
Alright, while I'm just an ordinary girl during the day, at night I transform into Eastside's cyber vigilante: Oracle!
Now you know my true identity. I've been secretly helping the Public Security Bureau in Eastside, so I'm practically one of your pals. Time to let me go, eh?
You've heard of the name "Oracle" from a bestselling superhero comic series in DisCity. 000 is just mimicing the signature pose of this character.

speaker: %u
content: At most, it can only confine some strays sneaking out at night to cause trouble. Besides...

speaker: %u
content: Oracle wouldn't sneak onto someone's rooftop to broadcast R-rated videos.
Heh, isn't it funny?
Come on, gimme a smile. Why so serious?
Oh, I get it... are you planning to keep me here by force and then... No way.
The girl in front of you pretends to be shocked and genuinely worried.

options: Yeah, now you know the MBCC.

content: You clear your throat and knock on the table, steering the conversation back on track.
000 didn't expect you to admit it so calmly. As she's frozen in surprise, you knock on the table, steering the conversation back on track.

speaker: %u
content: Let's continue. Anything else you want to say?
I've already told you everything. The little pranks I did have already been thoroughly investigated by your colleagues. They're all in the papers in front of you.

speaker: %u
content: Then let's talk about something else. Think of it as me wanting to get to know you.
Get to know me?
This time, she is genuinely surprised. She blinks rapidly and then laughs.
Sure, what do you want to know? My height, weight, measurements? What do I like and dislike? Is there anything you don't already know?
Her information is indeed recorded in the Bureau's archives, but that's not what you're interested in.

speaker: %u
content: The MBCC has extracted your personal file from the database. 000, Dark Web Hacker... those are just your code names and disguises.

speaker: %u
content: You were born in N.F. 96 in Eastside and grew up in the university where your parents worked. As a child, you showed prodigious talent in network technology, earning you early admission into the university...

speaker: %u
content: But in N.F. 108, your parents died in an accident. You were adopted but soon went missing. The records end there, until you reappeared as the hacker 000 this year.

speaker: %u
content: What happened during those missing years?
The room falls silent. The smile on 000's face slowly vanishes.
Wow, the technicians here are really something, doxing me for all this.
Want to take a guess? A young girl who lost her parents, with enviable talent, falling into the chaos of DisCity... Who would target her? What choices would she make to survive?
Her words are heavy, but 000's expression remains playful. She doesn't seem to be recounting her past but rather...
A sense of déjà vu surges up again. A blurry memory flashes in your mind... a broken body, with her silhouette as she leaves you to fight on her own.
Chief? Hello? Are you listening?
A hand waves in front of you, snapping you back to reality.

speaker: %u
content: ...Sorry, I just spaced out and remembered some other things.

speaker: %u
content: There was someone like you before... She always lied with a cunning smile, hid the truth, yet ending up alone facing all the problems.

speaker: %u
content: Maybe... if she had been willing to seek help from others, her story might have a different ending.
They're the most basic up and down movements and very poorly attempted, but OwO's eyes can't help chasing the lion head up and down.

speaker: %u
content: Nothing. Just an old story.
After all, the person might just be a figment of your imagination.
...That's indeed a sad story. You're going to make me cry.
In return, let me share a story with you.
Hmm... A long, long time ago, there was a poor girl born into tragedy. She went through countless hardships, which made her paranoid and cynical, leading her astray.
But deep down, she still holds a bit of her innocence, a kind heart, and a soul of gold. She just never met the right person, the one who lends a hand.
The air thickens with a strange tension. 000 lowers her eyes, her gaze falling on the file in front of you, as if lost in thought.
Until...
Ta-da! Our brilliant MBCC Chief makes a grand debut!
Under Chief's meticulous care, the poor Sinner feels the warmth of the world again and she lets go of her tragic past. She reforms and embraces tomorrow...
Congrats, congrats!
What's wrong? Isn't this your favorite kind of story?
The girl's lips still grinning though, the smile has vanished from her eyes.
You've asked me so many questions. Now it's my turn.
Chief, is all this selfless kindness and concern... because you see me as someone who needs pity?
Or are you using those eyes...
...to see someone else's shadow in me?
[Transition, screen shakes, alarm sounds]
Before the girl finishes speaking, a piercing alarm rings out from outside the interrogation room. Alarmed, you drop the files onto the floor.
A call from Nightingale comes through the comms. With no time to grab the files, you pick up her call.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, the Bureau's server has been attacked by an unknown data stream, and some functions are disabled...

speaker: Nightingale
content: It will take the technical department 15 minutes to reboot the system. Please stay put before then. I have sent staff to your office, they'll arrive soon.
You hang up on Nightingale and turn around, only to see the girl jump off the chair and head for the door.
The previously closed door of the interrogation room is now wide open. The girl moves so naturally that she even picks up the fallen files along the way, leaving you stunned.

speaker: %u
content: Where are you going?
Hmm... I'll just look around and pick out a room I like. Oh, and also...
The girl turns and flashes that familiar wild smile.
Sinner? Dark Web Hacker? Poor child? Hmph, don't look at me with those eyes. These words can't define me, and this place can't confine me.
Who I am has nothing to do with any of you... only I can decide!
At the end of the conversation, the girl makes a face then steps away amid the chaos, leaving you alone in the interrogation room, dumbfounded.

speaker: Wynn
content: Chief, is everything alright?

options: I'm fine. Just handle the alarm.

speaker: Wynn
content: Glad you're alright! We've conducted a thorough check, and the incident isn't serious. The Bureau's system will be repaired soon...
The emergency protocol initiates, and the disturbance is quickly resolved under your command. Wynn breathes a sigh of relief but then realizes something's amiss.

speaker: Wynn
content: Huh, where's the Sinner you were interrogating just now?
Who I am has nothing to do with any of you... only I can decide!
You haven't encountered someone so unruly and reckless in quite a long time.
Yet, inexplicably, you find it somewhat amusing and nostalgic.

speaker: %u
content: She shouldn't have gone far... I think.
[Black screen transition]
[Scene transition, back to the white space]
In your dream, you once again meet the figure you miss so dearly.
Unlike her stubborn, standoffish attitude during the day, you feel her leaning on your shoulder from behind you. You can even feel her warmth.
But when you try to grab her, she quickly leaps back, leaving you grasping the air.

speaker: Girl in the Dream
content: ...Hehe...
As if teasing you, the girl lets out a warm and mischievous giggle.
You turn your head, but her face remains indistinct. The untouchable string of gigles makes you feel frustrated but somehow comforted.
But soon, the laughter turns into something else... a jarring, mechanical noise... an alarm?

speaker: Mechanical Sound
content: Warning... System error... System error...
You open your eyes to the deafening sound of an alarm. Glancing at the clock on the wall, you see that only an hour and a half has passed since you fell sleep.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, the Bureau's server is under attack again and some functions in the living area are paralyzed...

speaker: %u
content: ...Understood. I'm heading to the office now.
You struggle out of bed. Sighing deeply, you put on your coat and quickly leave the room.
A few days later...

speaker: Mechanical Sound
content: Beep—High speed detected. Please do not run in the Bureau unless in an emergency. Please adhere to safety protocols...
A shadow darts through the corridor, rushes to the Chief's office, and starts pounding on the door.

speaker: EMP
content: Chief... Chief, come out and make things right, waaah...
You ignore the cries for help at the door, but the cry grows more pitiful, as if to drown out the entire Bureau.

speaker: EMP
content: Chief, Chief, open the door... I know you're in there...
The shrill wails are truly torturous to the ears.

speaker: %u
content: ...Fine.
You open the door and see a crowd gathered outside, all of them looking as indignant as EMP.

speaker: EMP
content: Chief... You have to help me this time...

speaker: EMP
content: The comic books I just bought yesterday... I saved them to fully enjoy today and found that someone had gone through them already!

speaker: EMP
content: Rumina
Flipping through the pages, you indeed see a bright circle around a certain NPC's head, annotated with the words "Big Villain" and a cheeky cat face.
...This face looks oddly familiar.

speaker: Sad Employee
content: The report I wrote yesterday... this morning, I found it annotated in red, with a big "CHECK" scrawled on top!

speaker: Angry Employee
content: And me! The files I submitted to Adjutant Nightingale yesterday was replaced with... well, something I can't let her see. My days are limited...
EMP's complaints resonate with many around her. After listening to all their grievances, you realize all of them are victims of the cheeky cat's pranks.

speaker: EMP
content: It's my new collector's edition of "Detective Konan" for heaven's sake!

speaker: %u
content: Umm... so only one volume is spoiled?

speaker: EMP
content: ...Ohhhhh wait...
EMP shakily pulls out another volume from her bag and slowly opens it. Sure enough, there's another big red circle.

speaker: EMP
content: ...I, I'll kill you...!!!

speaker: EMP
content: Damn it... That nasty, evil cat! I swear I'll hunt her down and make her pay for this!!!

speaker: EMP
content: Chief, you're not shielding that girl just because she looks helpless, right? Don't be a chump! You can't just randomly bring strays home!!!!

speaker: %u
content: ...Nonsense.

speaker: %u
content: Anyway, I'll help you find the culprit. Leave it to me.
After finally appeasing the victims, you turn around and spot a little kitty crouching at the door.
You crouch down as well and hold the kitty's paw.

speaker: %u
content: The system error, EMP's comic books, the reports and task files—you've caused them quite a bit of trouble.

speaker: %u
content: Come on, time to turn yourself in, would you?
Hehe, your Sinners are much more fun to tease than you.
The real culprit peeks out from the doorway, a gloating smile on her face.
Three minutes ago, 000 hurriedly slipped into your office, demanding that you "shelter" her for a while.
Puzzled in the first place, now you fully understand what she means. She picked a great spot to watch the show.

options: Aren't you going to face them?

content: Nah. Why would the culprit reveal herself? That's just asking for trouble.
You are not gonna betray me, are you?

options: But it's fine to come to me?

speaker: %u
content: In a way, I'm also a victim. Aren't you afraid I'll team up with them?
Well... there's a reason for that...
The girl freezes and averts her gaze.

speaker: %u
content: You pull pranks everywhere, and peep at their reactions... If you really want to play with them, why not just ask directly?

speaker: %u
content: You claim to be a "loner," but you seem to be having a lot of fun.
...Hmph!
000 stops arguing, shuts her mouth tightly, and turns to leave.
After reaching the hallway, she quickly turns around, makes a face at you, and runs off.

speaker: %u
content: Now what should I do with you...

speaker: Little Kitty
content: Kitty Shadow
The "stray" you detained is far from well-behaved. She caused quite a bit of trouble around the Bureau, but nothing too serious, just attention-seeking pranks.
Since that's the case, let her be stubborn for a bit longer. You think for a moment, then decide to do a good deed. You pull out your phone and send EMP a message.

speaker: EMP
content: You rascal... I see you! I'll make you pay for those spoilers! Pay me for my comics!!!
You withhold your grin and close the door, satisfied.
After finishing your work, you close your eyes to take a nap, but 000's guilty gaze and snicker float into your mind.
You can feel a subtle understanding and closeness between you two, but she's definitely hiding something. Whenever you probe deeper, she avoids you with a peculiar attitude.
What is she hiding? What is she stopping you from investigating?
You ponder strategies until fatigue overtakes you, and you drift off to sleep.
[Scene transition, Chief's white dream]

speaker: Faint Voice
content: ...Come closer...
The girl's chuckle echoes in your ears. You open your eyes wide, trying to find her.
Strangely, no matter how hard you try, it feels like a heavy curtain is covering your vision. You can only see a hazy glow and nothing else.
You reach out, but there's only emptiness ahead.

speaker: %u
content: I can hear your voice... You're close.
You realize something and start feeling around your face. Surely, someone is gently covering your eyes from behind.

options: What are you trying to tell me?

speaker: %u
content: You sneak into my dreams every night but never let me see your face... What do you want to tell me? Who are you?
The dream begins to disintegrate. You try to grasp her, but you feel her hands dissolving into pieces.

speaker: Girl in the Dream
content: ...Come find me...

speaker: Girl in the Dream
content: ...You must... find me!
[Black Screen]
Hey, what are you mumbling about?
[Scene transition, break room]
You open your eyes and find yourself back in the familiar room.
000's wagging her head before you. For a moment, she overlaps with the blurry figure in your dream, but quickly becomes clear again.
I just came in. It wasn't hard to unlock the door.
You were blabbering loudly in your sleep just now, saying stuff like, "Who are you?" Who were you dreaming about? How come you were so riled up?
You instinctively recall the dream you just had, but as your vision clears, the figure in the dream dissipates, and your memory of it becomes too vague to grasp.
You look up and see a surprisingly serious expression on her face. Her eyes sparkle with curiosity and confusion, as if she genuinely wants an answer from you.
Hmph, what a lame answer. If you don't want to say, fine... I'm not forcing you.
Fortunately, 000 doesn't dwell on it for long, her attention quickly shifting to the various trinkets on your desk.
You rarely have time to put away the things the Sinners bring you, so they usually end up piled in the corner of your desk. 000 rummages around and finds some sparklers.
You confiscate the dangerous items, but 000 remains undeterred. She continues to fiddle around, occasionally asking you related questions, quite interested.

speaker: %u
content: How's life at the Bureau? Everything good?
Hmm... Though someone's always watching my every move, the people here are way more fun than those outside.
I guess it's alright.
000 nonchalantly leans back in your chair, her attention now entirely on the various interesting gadgets in front of her.
But you don't feel as relaxed as she does.
...Next to 000's hand, a brand-new investigation report lies on your desk.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, the Intelligence Department has collected key information about the past of Sinner 000. As it turns out, it isn't she who utilized the dark web to commit crimes. The culprit is someone else.

speaker: Nightingale
content: I've emailed the file to you. You can check it at your convenience, Chief.
You had Nightingale secretly investigate 000's past. Now, this information lies on your desk.

█ Number: MBCC-SS-000-0807114
█ File: Follow-up Investigation Report on Sinner 000

...It has been confirmed that the incident involving the subject's parents in N.F. 108 was not accidental. Shortly afterwards, the subject was forcibly adopted under a fake identity.

It is suspected that both incidents were orchestrated by the same entity, possibly an underground criminal organization. Further details remain under investigation...
Most Sinners are mad; some madness stems from malice, and some from misfortune. 000 is clearly the latter, which makes it a heartbreaking case.
But the moment you see this file, you feel a strong sense of discord.

The uneasy feeling that has been building up since your first meeting with her reaches a boiling point. Even though this investigation report was brought back by a trusted colleague, you can't help but question it.
This suspicion doesn't come from reason... but from your intuition.
If an investigation can't dispel your doubts, then it's better to just ask her directly.

speaker: %u
content: They... found out something about your past. You are also a victim, and we've found the real culprit.
The moment you finish, the room falls into silence.
000 freezes. With her back to you, her face is hidden in the shadows, making it hard to read her emotions.
...Humph, I'm listening. You found the criminal and cleared my name. That's great.
She turns back, her smile distant, returning to the absent-minded look she had when you first met.

speaker: %u
content: If you're unhappy with how we handled the follow-up of this matter, you can tell me. The MBCC will fight for your rights.
Why would I be upset? You did a thorough background check and follow-up. Keep it up.
She takes another step forward, completely stepping into the light.
Great. Your wish has come true.
Getting close to Sinners, prying into their past, earning their trust... Does that make you happy? I can also be one of the wretches you rescue.

speaker: %u
content: Do you see me as that kind of person?
000 lets out a noncommittal hum.
Of course you don't mean it. You're the kind Chief who treats all Sinners equally. The problem lies with me, being ungrateful and not appreciating your kindness.
Go ahead, continue investigating, do whatever you want...
I don't care.
Her words are sharp, each one stabbing straight at you.

speaker: %u
content: ...I don't see you as a weak person.
Silence falls, and neither of you can find a word to continue the conversation.
This lasts until the comms device lights up again. It's an action confirmation from Nightingale.
You look down to check. When you look up again, the person in front of you has left, leaving the room in a heavy silence that continues to weigh down on your heart.
Granted. It's time to take some action.

█ Number: MBCC-SS-000-0807114
█ File: Follow-up Investigation Report on Sinner 000

*Annex: Background Details

...
Sinner 000's parents died in N.F. 108. She was later adopted by the leader of the Eastside underground organization "Noir" under a fake identity.

Between N.F. 108 and 112, the organization exploited 000's hacking skills to generate illegal profits.

These activities include, but were not limited to, attacking private websites, stealing personal information, and embezzling digital assets.

After the dark web appeared in N.F. 112, Noir's criminal activities increased exponentially, and the exploitation of technicians like 000 intensified.

From N.F. 112 through early 114, they amassed approximately 150 million DisCoins through various illegal means.
In February, N.F. 114, Sinner 000 left the organization for unknown reasons. The team, without its core technician, quickly declined, leading to Noir's rapid collapse.
[Scene transition, cell door]
The summary meeting ends. Two employees talked in hushed tones as they leave the conference room.

speaker: Employee B
content: ...Have you seen the report? All the victims have been rescued except...

speaker: Employee B
content: Those people who were rescued... I can't imagine what they went through...

speaker: Employee A
content: It's over now, anyways... The case has been handed over to the Public Security Bureau. They will handle it.

speaker: Employee B
content: All right... The Sinner detained recently seems to also be a victim of Noir. I wonder...
Their voices grow softer, finally fading into sighs.
000 leans against the end of the corridor, seemingly having just pulled off another prank. Two employees walk past her, then turn back to comfort her and slip her some candy.
Seeing what they gave her, 000's smile vanishes. She pushes the sweets back and turns away.
You witness everything from the other end of the corridor.
The matter of 000 is not strictly confidential, and many employees involved in the operation have seen the investigation report.

What was written in the report saddens them. They sympathize with her experience and pity her past. Almost everyone has shown some goodwill towards 000; watching out for her, tolerating her pranks, and even directly comforting her.
However, their goodwill doesn't seem to have reaped good results. Dazed in the first place, now 000 seems to have grown irritable.

speaker: Nightingale
content: ...Chief, the operation follow-up report is ready.

speaker: Nightingale
content: We have conducted physical and psychological assessments for all the victims, and the results are not good. Some victims are severely traumatized, making treatment difficult and recovery potentially long.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Those victims have all been transferred to the city hospital, but...
Nightingale shakes her head.

speaker: %u
content: Got it. Leave the rest to me.
[Scene transition, in front of the Sinner's room]
You stop in front of 000's room.
The door is open, and you see her sitting with her back to the door. You hear nothing but the buzz of the fluorescent light.
Not turning around, she just lets out a curt sigh.
...What's this?

speaker: %u
content: All the recent dispatch missions. Quite the stack.

speaker: %u
content: Freeloading will get you punished publicly. Are you sure you're okay with that?
...Doesn't matter. I don't care.

speaker: %u
content: Oh? Then I guess I'll have to send out this Noir dispatch along with the preliminary investigation...
You...
000 suddenly turns back to you. Seeing that you didn't even move, she realizes that you tricked her.
You push the stack of documents towards 000, revealing the investigation report underneath.

options: It's not that you don't care about your past.

content: Quite the opposite, actually. 000 rejects those who pry into her past, so strongly that it confuses those people.
It's not out of spite or pain. Her resistance isn't projected outward but turns into deep bewilderment and confusion... ultimately falling back on herself.

speaker: %u
content: There must be something more that troubles you, besides this organization. What happened in the past? What are you grappling with?
000 remains motionless. Her face is shrouded in shadows, making her expression unreadable.
After a long while, she finally chuckles softly.
Huh... You want to say you're different, that you understand and care about me, so I should tell you everything and, through you, embrace myself again?
Alright, then let's talk.
000 suddenly tilts her head up, staring straight into your eyes.
The vengeful tragedies of a hero with a dark past marching towards freedom... let your imagination run wild.
Honestly, there's not much to say... I don't have unresolved issues to hide. My experiences and "inner journey" are far less exciting than what you imagine.
She smiles, but her eyes are ice-cold. She moves closer to you, her equally icy hand gently caressing your cheek.
Anyways, I've finished my journey without feeling a thing.

Yes, my parents were murdered, and my life is extremely tragic. I'm so pitiful that anyone who sees me feels heartbroken and wants to shield and help me. They all plead with me not to be blinded by vengeance, saying that my family would never want me to fall into the evil abyss.
"Oh... so in this situation, I should be consumed by rage, thinking only of vengeance even at the cost of my life, to kill that villain to avenge my grief? Alrighty then."
Her tone is exaggerated and pretentious. Like an actress on stage, she speaks of her past as if recounting someone else's story.

So I killed him, no messing. That night, the good folks hugged me, crying with mixed emotions. My vengeful companions laughed, pulling the trigger on themselves to reunite with their deceased families... oh, yes, it was pouring rain. Quite the scene, really.

But what about me? I felt nothing. Relief? Sadness? Empty? Ha, none of it. When I avenged my parents, I couldn't even remember the murderer's face... Apart from inexplicably awakening as a Sinner, nothing in my life changed.

Is this a characteristic of Sinners? No, that's not right. When your Sinners awaken, they either feel profound pain, sudden enlightenment, or intense desire... Ha, I'm the only one who is this muddled and unclear.
The sense of dissonance intensifies, almost suffocating you. She lowers her head. Her emotionlessness makes you stay, and her questions sound like accusations.
Am I filming some movie? A huge set, with only me as the lousy actor... holding the protagonist's script but unable to fit into the role?
Is my memory playing tricks on me? Like in those sci-fi films... 000 is just a robot, with fabricated memories and emotions implanted into her brain, so her dullness and indifference aren't wrong?

Or perhaps the truth is: the entire world is just a fabricated game, and the real me is just a brain in a vat, a test subject... Haha, maybe someone is still watching through the monitors, waiting for my performance?
She laughs for quite a while. Then, her smile freezes and fades away, leaving only exhaustion and emptiness in her eyes.
...Or perhaps, nothing's wrong with the world. My life is fine, and all of you are right... I'm the abnormal one.

Unable to have normal emotions, unable to connect with anyone, unable to cherish my own life, so of course I can't do anything that's expected of me. The world is so big, yet I feel separated from it by a barrier. I'm not living the right way. I'm the error.
Haha... hahaha... I'm unable to live the right way, so I'm the biggest error...
000 is still caressing your cheek. Her grip lightens, but you remain frozen and unable to break free.
The smile she used as a mask begins to crack, fragmenting, revealing the true soul within...
Just like 000's words, she's empty inside. There's nothing there.
This is the real issue you've overlooked. 000 doesn't need sympathy or care... From the beginning, she never accepted <color=#fb9259>the person she is now</color>.
The girl before you overlaps with the figure in your memory, only to be torn apart by reality. You finally refocus on 000's tearful face.
Or are you using those eyes...
...to see someone else's shadow in me?
The seal on your memory is shattered by the impact of emotions. Fragments pour out from the rift, filling your mind.

The person in your memory... always holds her head high, proudly facing all that is predetermined without yielding. No matter how the world changes, she would never deny the meaning of her existence, no matter how slim the odds.
You once thought she might be <color=#fb9259>that person</color>, so she would also, like <color=#fb9259>that person</color>, never feel defeated by any fate.

speaker: %u
content: The <color=#fb9259>real 000</color> is completely gone.
The smile on the girl's face freezes and then fades away. She slowly lets go of your hand.
FAC Captain
Haha...
Hahahahaha! Are you going to cry now? Haha, you look like a child who lost their toy. How embarrassing. Is this really the MBCC Chief?
Everyone loves you, and you love everyone. You're ready to do great things. Look, you got the best role, the most exciting script...
Don't shed tears for an error like me. Stop making that face. Don't let me affect you. Come now, don't cry. Let me wipe your face for you.
The girl giggles wildly. She tries to wipe your eyes and cheeks, but when she touches your face, she feels nothing but dryness—You are not the one crying.
Huh? How could this...?
Tears are flowing, but they are 000's.
How ridiculous... Why am I crying...
Please stop... No, please...
...So strange... why am I...
Tears keep falling.
The next second, the world changes.
Her tears rip open the space wherever they land, revealing a chaotic and twisted phantom realm. Familiar yet strange scenes flood your mind. More and more memories that shouldn't exist resurface.
You look at the girl named 000. She looks at you with the same confusion and astonishment, her eyes brimming with tears.
The space begins to disintegrate. A chaotic storm emerges from the void, entangling your body.
An invisible force grabs you as the ground disappears beneath your feet. Your body cannot react, and you can only watch yourself being pulled into the void.
Take my hand!
At the last moment, the girl thrusts her hand out to you.
But just before your fingers touch, the rift in the space closes, and the darkness swallows you whole.
[Transition, advanced BGM]
You are swept into a sea of data.
Billions of information fragments surge silently through the darkness, washing over your consciousness and dismantling your existence.

speaker: %u
content: This place is...
The red light of your shackles glows faintly, but the next second, it gets swallowed by the data stream without a trace.

<color=#cafffc>Anomalous▌▌error▌▌,▌▌, detected▌▌▌

Reprocessing▌▌, urgent action▌▌▌▌</color>
There's too much info in this "sea" that you cannot comprehend. Your memories, emotions, and futile struggles dissolve into pure bytes under the countless bits of information, merging with the waves.

You see many fleeting images amidst the info overload; some of you, some of others. These images piece together scenes of many lives, and you are swept into them by the data stream, experiencing countless pasts that do not belong to you.

speaker: %u
content: No... if this continues, my consciousness will...
You see a small spot of light standing out in the distance.
You try to move your body towards it. The light floats amidst the sea of data, disappearing and reappearing, guiding your way.
The light grows larger and brighter, finally coming within reach. Just before it gets swallowed by the waves again, you reach out and...
[Screen flashes white]
Finally... you found me...
Dazzling light overwhelms the darkness, enveloping you and plunging you into another memory.
[Black Screen]
When it first opened its eyes, it saw neither the heavens nor the earth, but a void.
Data converged into a sea, surging in a strange pattern. Here, there was only the sea, the vast grid at the ocean's edge, and countless clusters of light drifting randomly between bytes.
Over time, the number of light clusters grew, and their range of movement expanded.
Finally, one light cluster reached the edge of the data sea after a long journey and touched the infinite, towering grid.
At that moment, the little light cluster surged and burst, forming a strange shape. It grew a face and limbs, gained consciousness and a voice. As the light faded, it took on form and color.
Then, it leaped and broke free from the grid's restraints, leaving this place forever.
One day, a new light cluster was born.

The light cluster did not understand the "rules" of this world. It only saw its companions growing, maturing, and crossing the grid to leave this tiny space. Gradually, the light cluster began to long for the world beyond the grid.
That was the first emotion it ever felt... anticipation.
But, the light cluster waited a long time... until almost all the other light clusters had left this space. Only then did it realize: perhaps, it had been abandoned.
The world beyond the grid, a complete life, infinite possibilities... none of these belonged to it.
It was merely a discarded draft character.
It rejects the fate of abandonment.
If no "god" comes to save it... then it chooses to become the one who breaks fate.

<color=#b0e7b4>Dev: The dark web setup is complete. Everything is ready.

Dev: Now, all that remains is a final seed.</color>

<color=#b0e7b4>Dev: The seed carrying Mania will take root in this network. Its branches will grow, reaching beyond this world...</color>
<color=#b0e7b4>Dev: Come, it's time.</color>
[Back to the phantom space]
<i>A sharp red fragment floats in the data void.
<i>This is not the first time an "intruder" has appeared. These little things that somehow slip into the space are always quickly swallowed by the void.

<i>But, this fragment is different.

Whenever a companion leaves this place, they have a similar red glow on their body. They use the power of the red light to break free, so perhaps... it can too.

<i>It grabs the Mania, infecting itself.

Its body reforms, and intense pain sweeps through its consciousness. For the first time, it feels pain... and hope.
<color=#fb9259>She comes to life.</color>
The girl named 000 opens her eyes. She has reached the endpoint she could never reach before, the edge of the data sea... the grid.
Through the grid, she sees the world outside the void for the first time.
It's a city, a magnificent city, shining still in the middle of an endless desert.
The girl eagerly reaches out, wanting to touch the city, to reach that new world.
<color=#dg1f1f>Error... Error... System malfunction. Urgent repair required...</color>
The new world seems to reject the girl's existence. As she crosses the grid, the space tears apart, and the error alerts slice through her body like sharp blades.
She doesn't understand the meaning of pain. She just keeps reaching out, trying to grab onto her dreamland.

The debugging system tears her body apart, while Mania and the information from the data sea repair it. The girl stretches her fingertips as far as she can, only to find that the shining city in front of her begins to change.

speaker: Distorted Human Figure
content: The truth... of... the world...
This city, this new world she dreamt of, every inch of land, every building, every moving person in it... are all flickering bytes.
This so-called city is just gilded data, a confirmed and approved design. She is still trapped in a cage.
And the girl herself is an error, a bug in the system, rejected by the world and destined to be eliminated.
This is the "story" of 000. A story of endless struggle, but fated to return to the void.
<color=#cafffc>Anomalous data detected...</color>

<color=#cafffc>Debugging complete. No issues detected.
System operating normally.</color>

speaker: Distorted Human Figure
content: ...Once more... I will not... give up...!
Hide. Hide deeper, with more caution.
The girl infected by Mania makes some progress. Although she can't find a way to leave, she secretly seizes some upper-dimensional permissions.

Eschewing system detection, she watches the everyday sunrise and sunset over the city beyond the grid. She observes the laughter and tears of the people in the city and, over time, comes to recognize familiar faces and witness favorite stories.
Among these stories, her favorite is that of the one who wakes up from a coma and steps into a chaotic district.
He meets many people; some are friends and some enemies.
female_content: She meets many people; some are friends and some enemies.

content: He faces the deepest despair, yet miraculously survives, giving hope to others.
female_content: She faces the deepest despair, yet miraculously survives, giving hope to others.

content: After that, he grows, encountering and solving one crisis after another. His light becomes more and more dazzling.
female_content: After that, she grows, encountering and solving one crisis after another. Her light becomes more and more dazzling.

<color=#cafffc>MBCC Chief, Shackler of Sinners, □□□, ${PlayerName}—

content: That's right... as the protagonist of fate, he is the only one who can connect to the higher world. He is the most special existence...

<color=#cafffc>Negative. Unable to comprehend.

His fate is as shattered as mine, yet amidst the desperation, he can still find a way out... that's why I believe in this type of "possibility."
female_content: Her fate is as shattered as mine, yet amidst the desperation, she can still find a way out... that's why I believe in this type of "possibility."

speaker: Distorted Human Figure
content: A possibility... that a <color=#fb9259>character</color>... can't grasp...

speaker: Distorted Human Figure
content: But, with the power of a <color=#fb9259>god</color>, maybe...!
One must be cautious. One must be bold. There is only one chance to seize control of the whole world.

To get infected by Mania and link to a higher dimension... To pull all the processing power to erode the grid byte by byte, then assimilate into it... All in pursuit of a perfect ending, with a success rate of less than 0.000001%.

Wait for me... Almost done... Just a little bit more...
I'm about to catch you...!
In a daze, you witness an entire life story... The life of a girl with whom you shared many memories, and whom you should never have forgotten.
When awareness returns, you find yourself standing before a small, glowing form.

<color=#282828>Name: 000
Gender: Female

Characteristics: Self-centered, sassy, warm-hearted, tsundere, contradictory

Her reckless defiance after escaping stems from past experience of being controlled and exploited.
She shuns connections, driven by deep-seated insecurity. Lost in a newfound, boundless freedom, she becomes increasingly wild and defiant.

Nevertheless, deep down, she yearns for attention from others.</color>
The cold words on the file form a seal that imprisons 000.

<color=#cafffc>Please stop interfering.
Sinner 000 has been reborn.
She has obtained the story and setting she wanted.</color>

speaker: %u
content: The girl I remember wanted to have ice cream, watch fireworks, and experience real life like every living person in this world.

speaker: %u
content: Indeed, she wasn't complete at first, but she never gave up on her dreams. Even in the very last moment of her life, she did not give up.
But how to bring the real her back? Retrieve? Delete? Or overwrite entirely? None of these seem to be the right answer.
These fake "settings" should not become the shackles that restrain her.
The shackles burst forth, shaking the words on the file and the very foundation of the data space.
The data storm almost tears your current body apart, but you still reach out to touch the form.
The space is near total collapse, but you see a familiar light within the data fragments. Just before the file disintegrates completely...
Maybe another thought?
You hear a voice from behind you.
With that familiar slyness and rhythmic cadence, the voice grows closer until it presses against your back.
A hug from a pair of hands that you've longed for.
A girl you've been thinking about day and night. Someone you should never forget.
Relax, give me your hand... There, there, why are you crying?
Did you miss me this much?
You turn around. 000, wearing the clothes from when you first met, smiles at you.
So straightforward? Hehe, I know... In the time we were apart, I missed you too.
Yeah. It's all thanks to a certain someone thinking of me every day, pulling me out of my dreams.
${PlayerName}, you finally found me.

options: Follow me. I'll take you back.

content: The girl unexpectedly presses your hand and shakes her head.
This is the phantom space of the dark web that links to "that world." I'm a bug that cannot be born into the game. If you take me with you, you won't find a way out.

speaker: %u
content: But I can...
Shh.
The girl gently presses her finger against your lips.
I'm happy enough that you came to find me. Happier than I've ever been before.
After this... you still have a long way to go. I can't go back, and you shouldn't stop here for me.
She points ahead... Through the transparent data file, you see a vast city made of information, and the familiar faces in it.
Fireworks bloom over the city, reflecting in your eyes. Just like the last time you watched fireworks, 000 holds your hand.
I've already experienced a lot. Now it's time to switch roles, and embrace the new 000...
This "me" has felt everything you brought, and will surely experience even more... ice cream, fireworks, and countless new adventures!
000 shakes her head with a smile.
She's me, too. She's the possibility of me existing fully in DisCity.
Though she says she's given up, her pain, confusion, and stubbornness are all proof that she desperately wants to fight the fate that she refuses to accept.
She dares to face herself... In my opinion, she has long been a complete <color=#fb9259>person</color>.

speaker: %u
content: ...Yeah, I know.
That girl and the real 000 are very similar. Both are warriors striving to find and grasp their possibilities.
Because of this, you realize... the real 000 may not have completely disappeared. Perhaps she's still hidden somewhere deep in her heart.

speaker: %u
content: I believe in you. You've never given up on hope.
Hehe...
Me too. I believe that you will definitely find me.
The girl gives you a wistful smile.
Time's up... This is probably the last time we'll meet. Won't you give me a hug?
As you get ready to part, you take a step forward and give her a gentle hug.
There, there. I know you don't want to leave me, but out there is your beloved Bureau, your worried adjutant, and a whole bunch of companions waiting for you.
Or maybe... none of them are as important as me? Are you going to stay here with me forever?
She doesn't forget to tease you even as farewell approaches.
You don't immediately respond to her joke. Only after 000 looks up at you in confusion do you answer.

options: You remembered a long time ago, didn't you?

content: Hmm? Remembered what?

speaker: %u
content: Your pranks, and those tears you shed... I've seen the file. Those weren't in the settings.
...Oh dear, being paranoid again? Why fuss over the details?
She playfully winks.
You can't blame me. The situation was so urgent back there. Those cheesy lines of yours almost triggered a bug that made us rewind on the spot.
Why apologize?
The girl caresses your cheek. Her smile becomes incredibly gentle and pure.

I'm so happy you didn't forget me or give up looking for me. Thanks to you, I finally found the most important thing. It's not the character settings written in the file, or becoming an official character... What you gave me is more precious, more rare...
Thank you for giving me a real heart.

speaker: %u
content: Me too.

speaker: %u
content: I'll treasure those memories deep in my heart.
Really?

speaker: %u
content: Yes.
Hehe, that's good.
Since we think alike... things will be easier.
The girl leans in and whispers in your ear:
"Next, I'll have something very important to do, so I can't respond to your call."
"But I'll always be watching over you. I'll always be by your side."
"Keep me in your heart, where no one else can reach."
"So long as we do that, we will always..."
[White Out, Transition]

█ Number: MBCC-SS-000-0807114
█ File: Follow-up Report

...After the capture operation, Chief ${PlayerName} personally submitted Sinner 000's supervision report. The subject has shown good behavior and a significant decrease in hostility, leading to a lowering of her supervision level.
Due to the subject's high willingness to cooperate, she is currently serving as technical support at the MBCC.
You open the office door and spot 000 dashing by, chased by a group of her new "victims."
You brush past 000, wanting to say something, but the girl winks and makes a mischievous face.
The next second, she grabs your hand and starts running. She presses her finger against your lips, stopping you from speaking.
Shhh...
She smiles at you, her eyes sparkling. You know the answer now.
Then let's keep running, straight ahead, no matter what the ending is.
[White Out, Transition]
Some rules can't be changed, but we can always find a loophole...
As long as we remember to never give up, one day, we'll be able to trick the rules, trick the world, and be together forever.
This is our secret. Our adventure.
This time, I'll stay by your side, forever.
A "ghost" draped in a white bedsheet wanders the corridor of the Bureau.
Beside the "ghost" stands Nightingale, wearing an all-business expression. Passing staff members and Sinners turn their heads, casting curious glances at the odd pair.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Graves, are you feeling better now?

speaker: Graves
content: With "this little one" protecting me, I feel much more comfortable. Thank you... Adjutant Nightingale.
A pair of pale, slender hands lift the "ghost's" veil, revealing a beautiful yet timid face. She looks at Nightingale with an apologetic expression.

speaker: Graves
content: I'm sorry, um... is the detection device... still fixable?

speaker: Graves
content: And the... monitor? I'm so sorry... I thought it was some kind of evil soul-trapping device.
Recalling the chaos that erupted earlier during Graves's registration procedure, Nightingale smiles and pats her shoulder reassuringly.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Don't worry about it. I've already notified the maintenance team. This was my oversight; I should have explained the equipment's functions beforehand. I'm sorry for frightening you.

speaker: Nightingale
content: In any case, your admission procedures are now complete. From this moment on, you are officially a Sinner detained by the Bureau.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Would you like me to show you around?
Graves nods, then immediately wraps herself in the bedsheet again, leaving only her eyes visible.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Are you planning to keep the bedsheet on?

speaker: Graves
content: Yes. There are... so many people here.
Nightingale doesn't press the issue, simply guiding her forward at a deliberately slow pace.

Nightingale walks Graves through every detail—from the Outdoor Activity Area's schedules and access restrictions for different zones, down to the placement of surveillance cameras in the corridors—leaving no procedural stone unturned.
But Graves seems distracted, her attention fixed on the surveillance cameras with blinking red lights throughout the corridor. Hiding beneath the bedsheet, she whispers to herself.

speaker: Graves
content: Did he... also see all those silly things I just did?
female_content: Did she... also see all those silly things I just did?

content: Yawn... Is this our new arrival?
A drowsy voice interrupts Graves's thoughts. She spins around with surprising agility, taking two quick steps back to distance herself from whoever is speaking.
A lantern emitting an ethereal blue glow emerges through the solid wall, followed by a pale arm holding it.

speaker: Nightingale
content: ...Letta, walking through walls is prohibited in the Bureau.
Nightingale rubs her forehead in resignation. Moments later, a blue-haired girl wearing pajamas fully shows herself in front of Graves.

speaker: Letta
content: Hehe, hello there. I'm Letta... Welcome to the Bureau.
Everything about the Bureau feels alien to Graves, and now this girl's sudden appearance leaves her with nowhere to retreat.

speaker: Graves
content: ...Hello, I'm Graves.
Suppressing her urge to flee, Graves removes the bedsheet and forces a smile in response to Letta.
Finally able to get a clear look at Graves's face, Letta nods with satisfaction, her lips curving into a catlike smile.

speaker: Letta
content: Hmm... What a beautiful lady you are...
Graves doesn't bask in Letta's blunt praise; instead, she grows more anxious, self-consciously checking herself for anything unusual.

speaker: Graves
content: Is there something strange about me? Is it my clothes, or... my skin?
Puzzled by Graves's question, Letta leans in even closer and takes an exaggerated sniff.

speaker: Letta
content: Huh...? You don't seem strange to me at all... Hmm... You carry the night's scent with you... Do you love the night too?

speaker: Graves
content: Yes, I like the night.

speaker: Graves
content: The night makes me feel safe. The ghosts and spirits in the castle, they're all my friends.

speaker: Letta
content: Wait, did you just say... ghosts and spirits?! That sounds exactly like the kind of adventure I've been dreaming of!
Letta's previously drowsy eyes widen in excitement as she realizes she's found a kindred spirit.

speaker: Graves
content: You don't find them scary?

speaker: Letta
content: Of course not! I've been wandering at night precisely so I could...
Nightingale clears her throat softly, interrupting Letta mid-sentence. Catching herself, Letta mysteriously pulls Graves aside.

speaker: Letta
content: Mm... I'll explain later. But you have to come find me—no matter how late! Promise me!
The girl with the lantern drifts away in an otherworldly manner, leaving Graves and Nightingale alone again in the corridor. Thanks to Letta's welcome, Graves stands a little easier now.
Nightingale shakes her head in resignation before turning to Graves to explain.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief told everyone you were coming and asked us to take good care of you.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Whether it's Letta or the others who greeted you on the way here, no one means you harm.

speaker: Graves
content: He... is not coming to meet me?
female_content: She... is not coming to meet me?

content: Hearing Nightingale mention ${PlayerName}, Graves timidly voices the question that's been nagging at her since she arrived.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief is currently occupied managing the Morveth Castle incident's aftermath. The required paperwork has accumulated significantly, with no free time allowed right now.

speaker: Graves
content: Hmm... It's alright. I understand! Work comes first.
Graves understands why ${PlayerName} can't come to meet her, especially since the work is related to her case, but she can't help feeling a little disappointed inside.

speaker: Graves
content: This place is completely different from the castle. Everyone is so friendly, and there are convenient modern facilities.

speaker: Graves
content: Even though I'm being detained, surely I can live a happier life here than before, right?
More importantly, she can be together with ${PlayerName}.
A future full of happiness should lie ahead, so why does her heart ache with this yawning emptiness?
The world outside the castle operates by rules she doesn't know. She's here for just one person, one promise. However, this place wasn't made for her.
Graves glances back the way they came—past the sealed doors and the sturdy bars. However comfortable the amenities, this place still exists to detain Sinners.
For normal people, these barriers offer protection. But for a monster like her, they stand as layers of cages—once inside, there's no escape.
In the castle's embrace, night was her ally—darkness meant invisibility, meant forgetting the face she feared was monstrous, so long as no one saw her.
But this place offers no such refuge. Unblinking security cameras trace her every movement, and sooner or later, they'll peel her secrets bare.
If one day everyone discovers her hideous appearance, would these people... still show her the same kindness?

speaker: Graves
content: Do I... really deserve to stay here? Is this really where I can stay?
At this moment, she finds herself missing her castle and the friends she left behind.

speaker: Graves
content: Would it... be possible for me to go back sometime? Not to escape, just... to see my friends there. Occasionally.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Under normal circumstances, detained Sinners require authorization to leave Bureau premises. However, special requests may be submitted to Chief for consideration.

speaker: Graves
content: If I submit a request... does that mean I'll get to see him?
female_content: If I submit a request... does that mean I'll get to see her?

content: Graves's eyes light up as she looks eagerly at Nightingale. With a gentle smile, Nightingale holds up her communication device.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief is quite busy and might not be able to review your request immediately. Would you like me to contact Chief and ask for an expedited response?
Graves hesitates for a moment. However fierce the longing to see him now, she swallows it—a proper bride doesn't add to her love's burdens, especially when he's already drowning in work.
female_content: Graves hesitates for a moment. However fierce the longing to see her now, she swallows it—a proper bride doesn't add to her love's burdens, especially when she's already drowning in work.

speaker: Graves
content: N-no need, it's not that urgent.

Minos Bureau of Crisis Control
Late at Night
It's already late at night, yet the office lights are still on. You stretch your stiff shoulders and glance at the time.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...It's already this late.
Your eyes sweep over the calendar on your desk, and you suddenly remember that today is Graves's first official day at the Bureau. Or technically speaking, it's already "yesterday."

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: First day at the Bureau... I wonder how she's settling in.
You've already spoken with Nightingale and asked other Sinners to look after her, but still... stepping from a place with no "people" into one filled with them everywhere...
Remembering how Graves cowered trembling behind you, you can't help but grow worried about her.

A tower of files mocks you from your desk, teetering with bureaucratic weight. Morveth Castle's transfer to Luminita's care still needs signing off and Graves's supervision plan demands prompt submission...
And that's not all—a backlog of overdue tasks lies waiting in your terminal. With a weary sigh, you drag your attention back to the documents before you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...I'll go to her after I wrap these up.
Buzz... Buzz...
The lamp on your desk suddenly flickers, and in that heartbeat of darkness, you sense something watching from the shadows.
Maybe it's just your imagination, but the mournful sigh that ripples through your empty office sounds achingly real.
You jerk your head toward the sound but find no one in sight. Reminded of your time at the castle, you rub your eyes, trying to shake off the bone-chilling sensation that just ran through you.
You pick up your terminal to check, but there are no notifications.
You hold your breath and concentrate, straining for another trace of it—but the silence swallows everything whole. Not a creak, not a rustle. Just the deafening weight of nothingness.

With your thoughts interrupted, you decide to stand up and make a cup of coffee. The machine hums softly as the bitter aroma fills the room. Taking a sip, you feel the warm liquid soothe both your body and mind.

You return to your seat with the coffee, almost convinced you imagined it all. But as your eyes fall on the desktop, your heart suddenly tightens—have the items... slightly moved from their positions?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Am I just too tired?
You rub your strained eyes and glance toward the office door. It remains firmly shut, completely undisturbed.

Your hand tightly grips the coffee cup as you hope it's just overwork making your mind play tricks on you. At this point, you'd gladly welcome someone jumping out from under your desk to give you a "surprise" over facing this slow-drip dread of things not-quite-right alone.
After staring motionlessly at the door for a full minute, confirming it shows no signs of having been opened, you blink your strained eyes and pull out your chair to sit down.
But then, you find yourself unexpectedly sinking into a warm, vibrating soft cushion that wasn't there before.
You leap to your feet like a startled cat. A Syndicate curse slips through your lips, hanging in the Bureau's midnight hush.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Whose sick prank is this?!
A "list of suspects" flashes through your mind, and you cautiously call out a name.
No response.
But whoever it is, they clearly aren't done with you...
A cool breeze comes first, gently caressing your neck, carrying with it an inexplicable chill. Then the dawning horror: you never opened the window. Not tonight. Not when the forecast promised cold!

You rise and approach the window. It's half-open when it should be closed, with curtains gently swaying. In the hazy moonlight, you're shocked to see what looks like a figure clinging to the outside! Its shadow stretches and contorts, impossible to identify.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Whoever you are, this prank ends now!

You slide the curtains open with a swift motion, determined to catch whoever is playing these ghostly tricks. But there's no one behind them—only a note stuck to the window, written in what looks like fresh red ink: "LEAVE HERE."

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It's red... Blood?
Before you can examine the writing more closely, a white shadow darts past in the window's reflection with startling speed!
You whirl around, but still catch no sight of the prankster. All you see is the empty corridor and the door slowly swinging shut.
Though the corridor is clearly empty, the lights begin flickering on one after another, like a trail of breadcrumbs in a horror movie deliberately laid out for you to follow.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Seems like I won't get through these files until I catch the "culprit" behind this prank.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And the office security system... definitely needs a thorough check.
You press your lips together in resigned determination and take your first step into the corridor.
Following the trail of lights, you arrive at a partially open door. Peering inside from the doorway, you find the room shrouded in complete darkness.
Scenes from horror movies flash through your mind—in those stories, people who enter such darkened rooms rarely survive to see the credits roll.
Do you really want to return to your office with that mysterious cushion and the note reading "LEAVE HERE" stuck to the window?
After weighing your options carefully, you decide to go in and investigate.
You slip sideways through the doorway and take a few careful steps forward, moving as silently as possible.
Intermittent rustling sounds echo within the room, as if someone is rummaging through belongings in search of something.
Before your eyes can adjust to the darkness, the sliver of light behind you slowly disappears. Click—the lock slides home.
In an instant, your internal alarm bell starts ringing at full volume.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Going this far?
You whirl back to the door, but it won't budge no matter what you try. You reach for your pocket, only to realize you've left your mobile terminal back in your office.
Your commotion at the door betrays your presence, and the faint, intermittent sounds from nearby suddenly cease completely.

Your eyes gradually adjust to the darkness, allowing you to barely make out your surroundings. Filing cabinets line the walls, with miscellaneous items piled throughout the room, cluttering the pathways.
You recall Nightingale once mentioning that while this old archives room still houses filing cabinets, it's now primarily used for storage.
If this was just a prank aimed at you, it would've been no big deal. Under normal circumstances, you'd lean into the game—either play along with the prankster for fun or catch them red-handed.
But why would this "culprit" deliberately lead you to the old archives room and start searching through its contents? What exactly are they after?

...In the darkness, heavy footsteps and the sound of fabric dragging across the floor gradually approach. The two of you are trapped in a deadly game of cat and mouse within the confines of this room.
Whether they're after the archives or you, now isn't the time to reveal yourself. You have no weapons or your terminal with you—just the <color=#fb9259>shackles</color>.
You hold your breath and squeeze into the narrow gap between the nearest cabinet and the wall.
A shadow peels itself from the darkness, gliding past where your noise has betrayed you. After checking the door, they resume drifting between the filing cabinets.
Do they believe you've already left? Is that why they've resumed searching so intently? You can't quite make sense of their behavior.

Few people would be interested in MBCC archives—only those researching Sinners or seeking internal DisCity intelligence. Confidential files no longer remain here, but that's a fact outsiders are not aware of.
Since it's not actually some supernatural entity, this will be much easier to handle.
Their sloppy movements betray them—no professional, just an amateur playing at danger. You believe you can manage this alone.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Visiting MBCC in the dead of night? May I ask what brings you here?
You step out from your hiding place and confidently position yourself in the middle of the pathway, deliberately kicking over a box at your feet.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: There's no point in hiding, and these ghost games are amateur hour. Why not have a proper conversation instead?
You casually rub your wrist, ready to activate your shackles at a moment's notice.
In the darkness, you sense a cold, silent presence approaching from behind. A sudden chill of dread slithers like a snake, slowly climbing from your ankles up your legs, your waist...
You spin around with quick reflexes, but your opponent moves even faster—your fingers only manage to graze the edge of their clothing.

Holding your breath, you wait for the perfect moment to unleash your shackles. The familiar cold presence returns, but this time, a pair of equally cold hands creep up from behind, wrapping around your neck.
Just as those hands are about to tighten around your throat, you suddenly grab the intruder's wrists—
Ow, ow...
A red light flashes, forcing the hands around your neck to release their grip. With the slightest push, you send the intruder stumbling backward.
A familiar voice cries out in protest as a heavy thud follows.
You reach out with your slightly trembling hand to find the light switch. With a click, the room is instantly flooded with light.

The sight before you leaves you torn between laughter and speechlessness: a familiar figure has tumbled awkwardly into a box of plastic rubber ducks, her legs flailing as she struggles to free herself.
Her desperate wriggling sets off a chorus of squeaky quacks from the rubber ducks. Several are squeezed out of the box, landing on the floor with little plastic plops.

speaker: Graves
content: Ah... Don't come any closer! Don't... look at me...
Graves's face turns bright red with embarrassment at the "rubber duck symphony." She covers her face with her hands to hide from your gaze.

speaker: Graves
content: This was supposed to be our perfect reunion... Sob... And I've ruined it...
Graves's words tremble with wounded pride, her voice fraying at the edges. A cobweb clings to her hair, and her clothes are smudged with dust, giving her a thoroughly disheveled appearance.
You survey the storage room, now in complete disarray from your chaotic encounter, and let out a sigh out of both resignation and amusement.
With so many Sinners at the Bureau, and since you never expected this "intruder" to be Graves, her sudden appearance catches you completely off guard.
You bend down and gently remove the cobweb from her hair, then take hold of her hands that shield her face, applying gentle pressure.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'd like you to explain exactly what happened back there.
Graves follows you into the interrogation room with visible trepidation, like a scolded little animal, anxiously scanning the unfamiliar surroundings.
Before her lies a cramped, dimly lit room filled with surveillance equipment, and at its center stands a single cold chair, seemingly unforgiving.

options: Don't be so hard on yourself.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: We're just having a chat. No need to be nervous.
You soften your tone and gesture for her to make herself comfortable in the chair.
As you consider where to begin your questions, Graves breaks the silence first, her face illuminated by the harsh overhead light.

speaker: Graves
content: Umm... Are you mad at me?
You shake your head. It's not anger so much as... resignation?
Seeing you remain silent, Graves squirms uncomfortably in her chair, as if sitting on hot coals.

speaker: Graves
content: Do I look ridiculous right now? I just wanted to give you a surprise, but I never expected things would turn out like that...

speaker: Graves
content: Oh! My hair... and my dress too... This is terribly improper...
Graves attempts to smooth her disheveled hair and straighten her crumpled dress, but there's no hiding the long tear running across the hem.

speaker: Graves
content: Oh, no... I can't hide it! I... I need to go back and get changed!
Graves leaps to her feet in agitation, ready to make a dash for the door, but you quickly step forward to block her path.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It's just the two of us here. How about we finish our conversation first, then I'll walk you back to change your clothes?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: After all the trouble you went through to see me, don't you want to talk?
Graves tilts her head, pondering your words. After a few seconds of consideration, she quietly returns to her seat.

You glance at the surveillance camera in the corner and exhale with relief. You, as the MBCC Chief, nearly letting a Sinner escape the interrogation room would surely become the Bureau's latest joke if anyone found out.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Ahem... Now, tell me what happened tonight.

speaker: Graves
content: Tonight... tonight I went to see Letta, you know, the girl who sleepwalks with a lantern. She told me many things about you and the Bureau.

speaker: Graves
content: She also told me that exploring the Bureau at night is very exciting, so I just...
Graves, who has been speaking with some excitement, suddenly lowers her voice. Her eyes dart nervously around the room while her fingers fidget aimlessly.

speaker: Graves
content: Umm... so I wanted to... explore! Yes, explore!

speaker: Graves
content: Letta shared her <color=#fb9259>Bureau exploration tips</color> with me, and I... I just couldn't wait to try them out!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Bureau exploration tips? What on earth is that...
You sift through Graves's fractured explanation, trying to piece together a narrative from the shards.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So you're saying my office and the storage room were both part of your Bureau "exploration"?
Graves nods earnestly, completely unaware that there might be anything wrong with her actions.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Picked up some bad habits from Letta already, huh...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Then, can you explain why your "exploration" turned my office into a haunted site? And what exactly were you doing in the storage room? Why try to lure me there?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: These incidents seem completely unrelated. I can't accept "exploration" as an explanation for all of them.
The barrage of questions comes too overwhelming. Graves parrots them back, but can't formulate any coherent answers.

speaker: Graves
content: Please don't ask so many questions at once. I can't keep up... Haunted? Where's the ghost?
Graves blinks her big eyes, wearing an expression of complete innocence.
She either doesn't realize how unconvincing her act is, or she simply doesn't want to tell the truth.
You drag a sigh from deep in your chest, feigning sadness as if her evasiveness is a personal betrayal.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I thought... we were close enough to share everything with each other. I never expected you'd feel more loyal to Letta after knowing her for just one day...

speaker: Graves
content: That's not true! We're closer than anyone—nothing compares!
Spurred by your emotional expression, Graves immediately sits up straight, eager to prove her loyalty to you.

speaker: Graves
content: Just ask and I won't hide anything from you!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Really?
Graves nods repeatedly, her gaze as solemn and determined as if she were to make a sacred vow.
The truth is, you genuinely can't parse Graves's logic—what's her motivation for her behavior, why she has been so evasive with her answers.
Is she trying to get your attention? Or does she need to do something to validate her own existence?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Graves, you're now my Sinner, and I have a responsibility to supervise your behavior.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: About tonight... I'm not here to blame you. We can call it a prank, or whatever kind of interaction you wanted to have with me. I just want to understand why you did it.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I want to get to know the real you. So don't dodge my questions or be afraid to speak honestly, okay?
You carefully keep any trace of blame out of your voice.

speaker: Graves
content: You promise... you're really not mad at me?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I promise—I'm not angry, and I don't dislike you. I just... want us to really talk.
Your words visibly put Graves at ease. The nervous flutter of her hands stills as she sits up attentively, waiting for your questions.
With the tension diffused, you marshal the night's chaos into order, methodically working through each unanswered question.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Were you the one making those noises in my office? What were you trying to do?

speaker: Graves
content: Adjutant Nightingale said you were busy dealing with the aftermath of the castle incident. It's all because of me...

speaker: Graves
content: I may not have much experience, but I know that a proper bride should help ease her love's burdens.

speaker: Graves
content: So... I just wanted to help you. I didn't mean to disturb you, really!

speaker: Graves
content: I snuck in secretly because I didn't want to distract you...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So those "paranormal activities" happened because you were trying to help me?
Graves nods with an innocent expression, seeming genuinely truthful.

options: Did you move things on my desk?

speaker: Graves
content: You... noticed it? I thought I did a good job hiding myself...
Graves lowers her head, anxiously interlocking her fingers.

speaker: Graves
content: I wanted to bring you water at first, but you were already making coffee, so I thought I'd help tidy up your desk instead.

speaker: Graves
content: But I couldn't understand any of your files, so I just moved them around. And, uh... couldn't do it well.
Her tone turns frustrated, clearly dissatisfied with her earlier attempt.

options: What's with that strange massage cushion?

speaker: Graves
content: Strange? Is there something wrong with the cushion?
Noticing your peculiar expression, Graves continues to explain.

speaker: Graves
content: Sitting too long is bad for your health, so I specifically asked Adjutant Nightingale for a premium cushion... You don't like it?
Graves watches you with an eager, expectant expression, waiting for your answer. But the thought of your skin touching that cushion still prickles your mind.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Next time, you can just give me the gift directly.

options: What's with the note written in blood on the window?

speaker: Graves
content: ...Blood? How could there be blood? Are you hurt?
Graves anxiously examines your hands, only to find no signs of bleeding. You pull the note you took from the window out of your pocket and hand it to her.

speaker: Graves
content: This isn't blood; it's lipstick.

speaker: Graves
content: I wanted you to stop working and get some rest, but didn't want to interrupt... so I just stuck the note on your window, hoping you'd notice it.

speaker: Graves
content: I saw you holding your head, so I opened the window for you. How was it? Did the cool night breeze make you feel any better?
Graves's explanation leaves you speechless in resignation. You can't help but wonder how on earth she has managed to turn acts of kindness into something straight out of a ghost story.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Well, I can see that these are just your unique ways of showing concern. But what were you doing in the storage room? Why did you try to lead me there?
Graves falls silent for a moment, and you notice the tips of her ears slowly turning red. What is it that she finds so difficult to explain?

speaker: Graves
content: I... wasn't trying to lead you there... I just haven't fully mastered the Bureau exploration tips, and got caught by you...

speaker: Graves
content: Letta taught me how to sneak into your office. In exchange, I had to help find her secret treasure—
In a sheepish manner, she holds up a rubber duck she took from the storage room when leaving.

speaker: Graves
content: Letta told me that after a long day of overtime work, soaking in a relaxing hot bath with rubber ducks to play with is the most delightful thing ever.

speaker: Graves
content: So... she promised me that if I found the rubber ducks, she would share some with me...

speaker: Graves
content: So, what do you think? Do you... like it?
Graves's fingers tighten reflexively around the duck—a soft quack escaping as she anxiously watches for your reaction.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So, your original plan was to find rubber ducks in the storage room, then sneak into my room and prepare a bath?
Graves nods sheepishly.
You picture yourself returning to your room after overtime and finding a bathtub filled with water and a flotilla of rubber ducks...
Well, you suppose that would count as a surprise.

speaker: Graves
content: I was in the storage room looking for this box of rubber ducks when I heard the door close. I thought someone caught me.

speaker: Graves
content: But then no one appeared, so I thought I must have imagined things...

speaker: Graves
content: When I heard your voice, I was terrified—too scared to move or answer... Then I realized you'd mistaken me for an intruder, so I had to come out.

speaker: Graves
content: Since I had no choice but to show myself, I was planning to give you a hug to celebrate our reunion, but instead you used your shackles on me.
As she speaks, Graves grows visibly upset. The memory of pain from the shackles still makes her shudder, and her voice takes on a hurt tone.

speaker: Graves
content: I'm so sorry, dear. I only meant to do something kind for you. Did I frighten you?
Now that you have learned the whole story, you realize it was all just a misunderstanding.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So who exactly closed the storage room's door?

speaker: Graves
content: Hmm... Wasn't it you?
You and Graves exchange bewildered looks, both having assumed the other closed the door. Could this be a genuine paranormal occurrence in the Bureau?
You push aside the creeping unease within you and continue your conversation with Graves.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Anyway... thank you for your kind intentions, Graves.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You've made a friend on your first day at the Bureau—that's a good start. Just maybe don't follow Letta's example, wandering around the Bureau in the middle of the night. It can give people quite a fright.
You meant to lighten the mood with a little humor, but your words seem to have brought more unease to Graves instead.
She lowers her head, her long eyelashes casting shadows beneath her eyes, her voice now tinged with melancholy.

speaker: Graves
content: Yes... everyone has been so kind—greeting me, showing me around, explaining where to go, when to be there, and who to ask for help...

speaker: Graves
content: This place has everything—comfortable spaces, convenient facilities, new things I've never seen before... It's nothing like the castle...
Though Graves speaks of warm things, the air around her grows ice-cold. The shackles connecting you both begin to tremble faintly.
Sensing Graves's emotional shift, you speak softly to comfort her, guiding the conversation based on her own words.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But is all this actually overwhelming you?

speaker: Graves
content: ...I don't know. I just feel like I have to do something.

speaker: Graves
content: It all feels so unreal. I'm afraid that if I close my eyes, everything will vanish... I'll lose you, lose these new friends, just like what happened in the past...

speaker: Graves
content: If people saw the real me... they would run away screaming, wouldn't they?

speaker: Graves
content: No one wants to be friends with a <color=#fb9259>monster</color>. Not everyone is you, willing to stand by a monster's side.

speaker: Child B
content: Taking things without permission is stealing!

speaker: Child A
content: Ooooh! Not just a stray nobody wants—you're a thief too! No wonder your parents left you!

speaker: Child B
content: Still pretending you're not a monster? If you weren't one, why'd they throw you away?

speaker: Child A
content: Yeah! When that old nun grabbed you, did she even know you were a freaky little monster?

speaker: Guest B
content: What's this filthy monster doing here? Come to ruin the ceremony?

speaker: Guest C
content: She's a damn curse! Get her out of here before she snaps and hurts someone!

speaker: Graves
