A long, tense silence fills the room. Ceto leans forward, her gaze as dissecting as it was during your first encounter. You hold it, unblinking. An eternity seems to pass before she finally reclines in her chair. No words are spoken, but you know this is her silent consent.

Almost immediately, communication from the officials is restored to the Bureau. This time, it bypasses your earpiece entirely, channeling directly to Nightingale. A moment later, the red eye of the surveillance camera flickers back to life.

speaker: Official
content: Are you here to offer an explanation? Regarding your unauthorized actions and blatant disregard for instructions, I agree that we need a serious discussion.

Sorry to disappoint, but I won't be apologizing. I've said all I need to on the matter. Going in circles with Ceto is a waste of time. She won't give you the answers you want, and she won't get what she needs.

As long as this trust crisis persists, this deadlock will get us nowhere. The only way through this is with verifiable truth. And for that, I have a proposal. One that serves everyone's interests and is far more efficient.

You rise and cross to the corner, your eyes lifting to confront the camera's sterile curve. You know they're there, watching, waiting for this exact show of defiance. But the thought is a distant one, a fact that no longer holds any power over you. Let them have their moment.
Yes, it's what you're thinking. Experiments have proven that the shackles can resonate with a Rancor. I can use that to explore the wielder's mindscape—to a point.

However, the Mania contamination levels on a Rancor are extremely high. Safe resonance requires the wielder's stability and cooperation. That's why the procedure is officially "not recommended." You don't have the authority to order it.
But if I volunteer and willingly accept all consequences, that changes everything. You question my judgment, but keep me on this case. Isn't this the move you were waiting for?

speaker: Official
content: I'm sure I don't know what you mean. We do not involve ourselves in other departments' classified research, nor have we guided your actions in any way. However, city security is our paramount concern. Your proposal does have our attention.

speaker: Official
content: What do you require now?
That Rancor fragment. Your so-called "evidence."
The voice on the line slips back into its ingratiating pleasantness, a clear signal that your strategic dance has entered a new phase.
[Blank Screen]

Against a pristine white backdrop, your consciousness is violently wrenched downward into the depths. All your senses are submerged in a slowly flowing liquid; sound blurs into a dull roar, and images drift like phantoms around you.
Suddenly, quick footsteps shatter the blur. A little girl, clutching something to her chest, dashes past, leaving only a glimpse of her defiant, retreating form.
I don't need help. I can do this myself!
Is this the hostage Ceto was protecting? As you watch the girl disappear into the distance, instinct compels you to give chase.
Mmph...!
Are you alright?!

As if weighed down by the heavy object in her arms, she loses her balance and falls before she can get far. Your heart lurches as you rush to her side, but she simply sits up, stubbornly wiping her face with her sleeve before turning to look at you.
Ceto...?!
You freeze in your tracks, your heart skipping a beat. This girl—struggling with an enormous metal gear—is not the hostage.
You are witnessing Ceto's own story, a memory from her childhood.
The scene feels hauntingly familiar. Wind, carrying the stench of the Black Tide, seeps through the hatch door, rattling the metal hinges. Inside the lighthouse, a dim, amber glow bathes everything.
What's unfamiliar is the meager smell of unappetizing food hanging in the air, and the sight of exhausted adults around a makeshift table, forcing scattered conversation.

speaker: Miles
content: ...Festivals back in the city... the square would be packed. When I was a kid, I'd buy bags of those candies. You know, the sour ones that turn sweet. I'd sell them for double the price. Made a killing.

speaker: Sienna
content: You’ve got quite the business savvy. I remember those. Dirt cheap, and even the strictest moms would buy a few for their kids without thinking twice.

speaker: Herbert
content: Right, they sold them in the old parts of the city. My wife lived on them when she was pregnant with our daughter. Kid loves them too. One of those would stop her crying every time. Haha...

Though the details of these memories have faded, an unspoken understanding lingers in the cadence of their voices. They are bound by a collective nostalgia for a shared place and time—a deep-seated longing for a homeland. This longing is the ember that keeps them fighting.

Ceto sits apart from the others, a silent observer clutching her Rancor. The concept of "warm memories" is foreign to her; she cannot fathom how a simple thing like candy could ignite such joy in their eyes.

speaker: Herbert
content: You always sit so far away. Tired of hearing our old DisCity stories? Can't blame you.

speaker: Ceto
content: No.

speaker: Herbert
content: With a face like that, don't bother being polite. We tell the same old stories, probably getting half of them wrong by now. You must be bored with it.

speaker: Ceto
content: ...It's fine. I've never been to DisCity. I can't tell which stories are old. Don't worry about me.

speaker: Ceto
content: They were never my stories to begin with.
Herbert settles beside her, a tin-can cup in his hand. His gaze moves from her unreadable poker face to her hands, which are meticulously polishing the Rancor. A weak, bitter smile touches his lips.

speaker: Herbert
content: You think you have no home, that you're rootless? Sigh... That's why when Fynn said she wanted to give you that blade and bring you into the lighthouse keepers, I asked her to reconsider...

speaker: Ceto
content: Are you saying I'm not worthy of it?

A rare confusion crosses the girl's face. She looks up at the person next to her, whom she deems her family, her polishing stilled. Instinctively, her grip tightens on the handle, and she pulls the blade closer to her chest—a clear, wordless refusal to surrender it.

speaker: Herbert
content: It's not about worth, Ceto. We fight to protect our families back in DisCity. But you... you have no one there to protect.

speaker: Herbert
content: Standing guard here is tough. These blades take a piece of you. But it's worth it to keep our families safe. For you, it's just pure sacrifice. Nothing in return. What's the point?

You watch as Ceto's gaze travels the room, skimming over each battle-scarred Rancor before settling back on the one in her arms. Herbert's logic remains just out of reach, and her voice is tinged with pure confusion.

speaker: Ceto
content: I just want to join you. Isn't that enough? Can't I fight with you? Am I still not good enough?

speaker: Herbert
content: How to put this... Right now, you see the uniform, the training, the salutes. You hear us talk about glory and heroes. You see the supplies from the rear. So you think the lighthouse keepers are cool.

speaker: Herbert
content: But the real fight... it's ugly. Without something precious to anchor you, to protect, you won't last. We're not just fighting the monsters. We're fighting these blades, too.

At the man's earnest words, Ceto pales and presses her lips into a thin line, as if recalling the Rancor's first awakening, the surge of negative emotion and bloodlust that had crashed over her like a black tide. Even so, she stands her ground.

speaker: Ceto
content: I can handle it. Fynn... you'll all be there to help me.

speaker: Herbert
content: In the heat of battle, there's no time to think... Ah, forget I said anything, Ceto. Don't take an old man's worries to heart. It's just... you're my daughter's age. Kids your age should have candy in their mouths and a grin on their faces, not weapons in their hands.

Herbert pats Ceto's head, slips something into her palm, and stands to walk away. She remains still, her gaze fixed on his retreating form. Only after a long moment does she uncurl her fingers to see what he's left behind—
A cellophane candy wrapper, crumpled beyond recognition, its patterns long since faded.

You know his warning didn't deter her then, but years later, it would ring with the weight of prophecy. And watching this stubborn girl bite her lip, you can already see the shadow of what she had become: the Ceto who had lost everything and lived only to seek her own death.
Stop... the bleeding's no use... Save the supplies... You'll need them for the journey back... Ceto... you're young... you have to live... survive to the end...

The wounded girl presses a rag—so filthy its origin as cloth is unrecognizable—against her companion's wound, heaving with all her strength. But life continues to seep through the fabric, unstoppable as a tide. The soldier's clouded eyes drift with immense effort, a final, cold sigh escaping the corner of her mouth.

speaker: Ceto
content: ...I know. Don't worry, I'll fight. Till the end.
Marina... Marina... Don't be scared... I'll kill them all... I'll keep you safe... Just... just you being safe in DisCity is enough...
No! Marina! Get away from her! Monsters! I'll kill you! I'll kill every last one of you!

Ceto, her own arm bound in makeshift, stained bandages, stands over the delirious soldier sprawled on the planks. She watches, motionless, as the wounded keeper's body is seized by a sudden, violent tremor, then falls into a final stillness.

speaker: Ceto
content: Rest now, old-timer. I'll finish what you couldn't.
Ceto, how much blood have I lost? Must be a lot... Guess... this is it...

speaker: Ceto
content: ...Don't talk.
Hah... It's fine. I'm not scared to die... Just can't accept it... So few of us left now... What if we can't hold?... If this place falls... my family in DisCity...

Ceto no longer needs to follow her comrade's struggling gaze to know where it points, as she once did every time. And neither do you. Across the chasm of separate timelines, this knowledge is a shared, grim certainty: they are all looking toward DisCity.

speaker: Ceto
content: Don't think about that. We'll hold. I will make sure of it.
That's... a comfort... With your word... I can go now... If only... I could dream of DisCity one more time... see them again... that'd be enough...

The fellow keeper's breath grows fainter, yet his eyes remain fixed, wide and unseeing. You watch as Ceto's fingers twitch, hesitate, then slip behind her to retrieve something from a hidden pocket. She holds it near his nose—
It's a candy wrapper, folded and refolded so many times its scent must be a ghost of a memory. Yet, sensing her intention, the faintest of smiles touches the dying keeper's lips.
Smells like... DisCity... Ah, this is nice... I think... I can dream of them now... Thanks, Ceto...

After a moment, the candy wrapper lies still, no longer stirred by any breath. Ceto retrieves it, her hands automatically folding it back into its familiar shape. But her fingertips keep worrying its edges—a gesture partly of remembrance, partly an unconscious search for a feeling that's unknown to her.

speaker: Ceto
content: DisCity, DisCity... What is it like, really? Your home... is it really that good a place? Worth your lives? Worth your last thought... this desperate wish to go back?

speaker: Ceto
content: If I can guard this place... if I can make it out alive...

speaker: Ceto
content: ...I'm going to see DisCity for myself.
To see that home they never made it back to, that place they were willing to die protecting.
The scene is familiar, yet the perspective is new. You watch as Ceto's fingers find the candy wrapper, her gaze turning towards the direction of DisCity.
Suddenly, a searing light obliterates the vision. You squeeze your eyes shut against the glare. When the white-hot burn fades, it reveals an unfamiliar, bustling scene—WhiteSands.
This must be a memory from after she left the lighthouse, the period you know least about, and likely the most crucial to understanding her current motivations. You focus, determined to miss nothing.

speaker: Merchant
content: Hey! Why's that kid always staring at my stuff? She planning to steal something? Listen up, this merchandise is straight from DisCity! You don't want to mess with someone who can move these kinds of goods.

speaker: Man
content: Oh, I'm sorry! She doesn't know any better. Can't teach her no matter what I do! I'll beat some sense into her right now! You hear me? What the hell are you staring at!

The man's curse, thick with a WhiteSands accent, lands at the same moment as his fist. The girl, a skeleton in tattered rags, has no means to defend herself. The blow sends her frail body swaying violently, a breath away from collapsing into the sand.

Yet she makes no sound. No sob, no scream. Her eyes remain locked on the stall, where cellophane candy wrappers refract the desert sun into a painful glare. It's a light that would make anyone flinch, but she doesn't look away. She doesn't even blink.

speaker: Man
content: I said, stop staring! Are you ******* deaf?! I've told you, looking at those is useless! Stop dreaming about going back to DisCity! A place like that doesn't want the likes of you!

The merchant's face darkens at her silence. The man raises his fist again, the threat now a rapid, guttural stream of Disian. This, finally, she seems to understand. Her eyes—glossy with tears she'd held back for so long—blink, and a single one escapes, tracing a path down her cheek.

speaker: Little Girl
content: Back to DisCity... Back home... I want to go home... No, I can't go home...

Those eyes have been shimmering the entire time, whether from the pain or the glare of the sun, it is impossible to say. Even as the man fists a hand in her hair and begins to drag her away, her gaze remains locked on the stall of DisCity candy, her lips moving in a silent mantra.
Fresh from Ceto's earlier memories, the parallel is unmistakable for you. And a moment later, you see Ceto's own muscular arm snap around the man's throat like a vice.

speaker: Ceto
content: ...She said she wants to go home. You hard of hearing?

The man's eyes drop to the stones and the long chain now scattered on the sand at Ceto's feet. His bravado shatters. He understands, now, that he is being deliberately provoked. His words become a nervous, sputtering excuse, his eyes desperately scanning the crowd for an ally who does not appear.

speaker: Man
content: Home... right! I'm her dad! We were just leaving! C-could you let me go? I'm taking her home right now!

speaker: Ceto
content: Hey, kid. Is he your dad?

speaker: Man
content: O-of course I am! She's just a kid, she doesn't know what she's saying! Don't listen to her! Mmph!
Ceto ignores the man entirely, her grip tightening to a conclusive silence. Her eyes shift to the sobbing girl, whose terrified whimpers are answer enough.

speaker: Ceto
content: Right. So if I said I was your dad, you'd believe that too?

speaker: Man
content: You...!

Seeing he's met his match, the man wastes no more time. A blade flashes in his hand as he lunges. Ceto doesn't flinch. She moves like a storm, catching his wrist, twisting until a sickening crack prefaces his howl. Her boot then crushes the same hand he used to beat the girl, a brutal and final punctuation.

speaker: Ceto
content: Tch. This is the best you've got? The only thing you're good at is running away. Now get lost.

speaker: Ceto

After a few terse questions to confirm the girl shows none of the familiar symptoms, Ceto finally allows herself a shallow sigh of relief.

speaker: Ceto
content: ...They lied. You're fine. Don't listen to their crap. If you want to go home, go.

speaker: Little Girl

speaker: Ceto
content: Bullshit. If you've got a home to go to, you go. Before you regret not going.

speaker: Ceto
content: Enough. I'm taking you home. No one will stop you with me. If anyone asks, the dirty thing was mine. Stop crying. A kid like you should have candy in your mouth and a stupid grin on your face, not sobbing in the sand.

You can see it in her eyes: Ceto's mind is made up, her plan fully formed. Her expression remains stern as she pulls the little girl along, snatches a handful of candy from the nearby stall, and stuffs it into the child's hands before leading her away.

The merchant, clutching the mineral Ceto left as payment, is ecstatic. You watch the two figures—one tall, one small—retreat into the distance, heading the same way Ceto's comrades had gazed with their dying breath. Toward DisCity.
"If you've got a home to go to, you go. Before you regret not going." Her words hang in the air. Were they for the little girl, or a belated message to her fallen comrades?

You're now almost certain that her determination to return the child—the regret she's trying to make amends for—isn't really about the girl. The child is a mirror, reflecting fragments of Ceto's own past.

Ceto has never lied about her purpose. She genuinely intends to take the girl home. This is simply her method: a stubborn, pragmatic act of exploration and amends. Her harsh exterior is a shield, protecting the innocent child from the world's prejudice against Rancors.
Since I promised not to let her down, there must be something I can do.
You open the evidence bag from the officials and retrieve the so-called "Rancor fragment," the alleged threat to the city-state's security. Connecting it with your shackles, you begin the scan...
Unlike Ceto's dagger, the fragment lies inert in your palm. No Mania fluctuations. No triggered memories. Just as you suspected. The conspiracy is a fiction.

speaker: Official
content: A truly... illuminating glimpse into a tragic past. As a DisCitizen, I'm very grateful for such... dedicated service from those soldiers.

Cut the act. You used me to validate your fake "evidence" and get a free look into DisCorps's past. Must be quite the accomplishment for you. Who ordered it? What's the real play, using a Rancor as a scapegoat now?

speaker: Official
content: Heh, as expected of the great hero of the East and West Districts. Your deductions are... more creative than most.

You can hide behind that smile. But know that there are others who take a much dimmer view of anyone playing games with Rancors. They won't ask nicely. If you value your position, or your skin, you will ensure the child's safety and return supervisory authority over Sinner Ceto to the MBCC.

speaker: Official
content: Of course. This appears to have been a... regrettable misunderstanding...
And...
You cut him off, your tone leaving no room for negotiation.
Your report will state this was a failure of trust, not security. Your paranoia and heavy-handed policies are what created this conflict.

The lighthouse keepers were manipulated by their own loyalty into sacrificing themselves for pointless foreign campaigns, and now we treat the only survivor as a threat. Who will be left to protect DisCity when the next crisis comes? That is the security breach you should be worried about. And it's one we can still fix.

speaker: Official
content: You're right, Chief.
You return after a brief absence, carrying a terminal, a tracker, and monitoring gear. Ceto's gaze falls on the new restraints laid before her, and a cold smirk twists her lips.

speaker: Ceto
content: Here to "trust" me again, is that it?
It was the best I could do. Even after clearing your name, you're still an S-Class Sinner with a "record." Letting you near civilians... these were the only terms they'd accept.

speaker: Ceto
content: Let me near civilians? What are you talking about?
Ceto studies you with wary uncertainty, her brow furrowed in the same way it was when the girl rejected her "impulsive" offer of help. She is weighing your every word, probing for your true motives.
Exactly what it sounds like. The deal is this: you can return the girl home yourself, but you must wear the tracker and leave DisCity right after. In exchange, they drop the charges.
You get to see her home. Make amends for your own regrets. Close that chapter for yourself. The catch is, I'm your guarantor. I take full responsibility for you. And I step in if I have to.
Ceto's lips twitch at the word "regrets." The vulnerability of it clearly unnerves her, yet she offers no denial. In this silence, you sense a newfound trust.

speaker: Ceto
content: A deal this good... What's the real cost? Or... What did you trade for this?!

Whoa, whoa, whoa! Do I look like someone who deals in bribes? Don't overthink this. You fought for this city-state once. Today, you protected one of its kids. That's the only currency that mattered. It's that simple.
You earned this trust, Ceto. You. Not your Rancor. You proved that even when pushed, you control the Rancor; it doesn't control you. That's what I used to argue your case.

You gently push the files and devices aside, locking your gaze with hers. It is a gesture that sweeps away all calculation, leaving only raw honesty. For a moment, Ceto seems disarmed, meeting your eyes with an unblinking steadiness.
Those labels don't define you. You know who you are. Everything you've done... it's never about destruction. It's always about protection. From the very beginning.

As for whether DisCity is still worth protecting for you... I want you to see for yourself. Go find the home that the girl wants to go back to so badly. See the homeland the lighthouse keepers fought for.
At least to me, it's not just a name on a map, and it's not the prejudiced place you've seen. What it really is... I trust you to find that answer yourself.

After a long hesitation, Ceto finally raises her hand in silent acquiescence. You circle the table and step closer than you have since your reunion—close enough to hear the soft rhythm of her breath—as you remove her restraints and secure the devices in place.

speaker: Ceto
content: ...Thanks.
Don't mention it. I know you've got a list of problems in DisCity. I just crossed one off for you.

speaker: Ceto
content: ...Heh.

She looks up, and for once, her smile is genuine, stripped of all its usual sarcasm. A soft beep from the monitor confirms it's active. She rises, rolls the stiffness from her shoulders, and gives you a gentle, deliberate nudge.

speaker: Ceto
content: Not a bad play. But don't think for a second I'll follow your script.
There is no script. My only plan is trusting you to write your own.

You share a final, knowing smile as she walks out of the interrogation room, silhouetted against the light from the hall. The device clings to her like faithful shadows as she departs to explore her DisCity, her "anchor," and her "belonging."

Beep, beep, beep... A rhythmic electronic pulse underscores your work, an ouroboros of sound looping endlessly as you flip through documents. In the corner of your screen, notifications bloom and vanish in a silent, frantic dance.
Wynn stands by your desk, her eyes flicking toward the chiming terminal. She tries to contain her curiosity, but the relentless beeping wears her resolve thin.

speaker: Wynn
content: Chief, those alerts are so... rhythmic. And they're not stopping at all. Are you sure it's okay to just ignore them?
They're just periodic updates from Ceto's tracker. Basic telemetry and a visual feed. The system will flag any Mania fluctuations or unusual movement automatically.
Your attention drops back to the report on the Rancors and lighthouse keepers. Wynn, however, remains captivated by the slideshow of images auto-advancing on the screen.

speaker: Wynn
content: It's so... still. Is it lagging? Or is nothing really happening? Oh, wait, there she goes! Chief, even without sound, you can see a whole story in this!

speaker: Wynn
content: It's like a flipbook! Way more interesting than a live feed. It kind of feels like... you're following along on someone's trip!

Following along on someone's trip... The phrase pulls your gaze to the screen. The footage is choppy, a silent film stripped of context, yet you can still trace the narrative woven through its distinct scenes—the shifting backdrops, the subtle changes in posture, the quiet emotions flowing from one frame to the next.

Wynn's comment echoes the fragments you have collected over these past few days: a silent, stuttering reel of "Ceto's DisCity tour." It is a catalog of moments that have, more than once, offered a fleeting respite from the tension of the looming war.

speaker: Ceto
content: Mission's done. Took a little longer than I figured, but... it went smooth.

speaker: Ceto
content: The family said they spent everything they had looking for her. If they'd given up hope, they'd have moved on by now.

speaker: Ceto

You listen silently to her words—still terse, blunt, and somewhat stiff. Yet, though only a few hours have passed, the Ceto navigating the streets of Eastside is no longer a complete stranger to this city.

speaker: Ceto
content: You made this happen. Thanks, ${PlayerName}.

Ceto?

speaker: Man's Voice
content: But... this is your favorite candy. My Lily is... so thoughtful, worrying her daddy will cry... Ahem...

speaker: Child's Voice
content: Are you crying now, Daddy? Don't cry, your eyes will get all hurty... Eat the candy! It'll make your eyes better!

speaker: Man's Voice
content: No, Daddy won't eat it... I'll keep it right here. For when I miss you and Mommy so much it hurts, then I'll eat it. Lily, remember: no matter how far I am, I'll always be thinking of you. Always protecting you.

speaker: Man's Voice
content: Be good for Mommy. I promise I'll do everything I can to come back to you. Quickly!

The conversation has ended, the family has left, yet Ceto remains, anchored in place. Her eyes narrow slightly, as if gazing at a distant, brilliant glare, perhaps the way sunlight catches on cellophane. Her profile is still, weathered and unchanging as a reef stone shaped by coastal winds.
What do you see now?

Silence stretches, but as Ceto resumes walking, the tapestry of DisCity's streets unfolding behind her once again, you can almost feel the gears turning in her mind. She isn't refusing to answer; she is assembling her thoughts. And when she finally speaks, her voice is decisive.

speaker: Ceto
content: I saw what you, Fynn, and the others talked about. "Something worth protecting." And... "a reason to fight."
Is that what you were hoping to see? Has DisCity... given you the answers you were looking for?

This time, there is no hesitation. She lifts her gaze, looking squarely into the monitoring device as if seeing through it, across the distance, directly to you—the person who once described DisCity to her from within the lighthouse.

speaker: Ceto
content: Yes. I have my answer now.

Behind her, the city pulses: a flow of rushing crowds, the rhythm of blinking neon, the living, breathing entity of a metropolis and its people. With the ghost of her comrades' homeland at her back, Ceto now strides forward, her path clear, moving toward the city gates, toward the end of the promise you secured for her.
...Maybe we'll meet again soon. When we do, Ceto, I hope you've found a place to call your own. And something worth protecting.
Whatever that place is. Whatever that something turns out to be.

speaker: Herbert

speaker: Herbert

speaker: Herbert
content: In the heat of battle, there's no time to think... Ah, forget I said anything, Ceto. Don't take an old man's worries to heart. It's just... you're my daughter's age. Kids your age should have candy in their mouths and a grin on their faces, not weapons in their hands.

speaker: Man's Voice
content: A storm is coming. I can't just sit here and watch our savings run out. You know how it is. The worse things get, the more we need to fall back on. I need to protect you both. That's why I have to go. That's my fight!

speaker: Man's Voice
content: No, Daddy won't eat it... I'll keep it right here. For when I miss you and Mommy so much it hurts, then I'll eat it. Lily, remember: no matter how far I am, I'll always be thinking of you. Always protecting you.

speaker: Man's Voice
content: Be good for Mommy. I promise I'll do everything I can to come back to you. Quickly!

A young father, a tearful mother, a child clinging to her mother's leg, her small face confused by the grief of a parting she cannot understand. These are the moments treasured like candies, carefully preserved in their shimmering wrappers.

Is this what Fynn and Herbert sought to protect? When Herbert left this city for the outpost—the lighthouse before the Black Tide, where Ceto met him—had he, too, carried the memory of a scene like this?
What are you looking at? What do you see now?

speaker: Ceto
content: I saw... a different kind of lighthouse keepers. No special weapons. No combat training. Not even a soldier's resolve. Just the most ordinary people.

speaker: Ceto
content: Family? DisCity? It's all temporary... Even without a Rancor's voice in their heads, the battlefield will still break them. That hell will swallow them whole and spit out monsters!
She closes her eyes, clenching her fists.

speaker: Ceto
content: But I'm not like them. I'm a Sinner. I crawled out of the Black Tide. That cursed blade lost its hold on me long ago.

speaker: Ceto
content: I'm stronger, much stronger than those ordinary people. I can fight to the last breath. I can kill the things they can't. I can protect what I decide to protect.
Even if she cannot prevent tragedies like what befell the lighthouse keepers from ever happening again, she can still fight to ensure they happen less often.

speaker: Ceto
content: I know where I have to go. Back to that hell, the battlefield. I was born in it, forged by it. It's only right that I'm the one to wipe it from the earth. End it once and for all.

speaker: Ceto
content: For everyone, past or future, who just wants to go home... Let my life be the price! Let them have a home to return to. That... is what I will protect!

Ceto opens her eyes. The battlefield stretches before her; the weight of her weapon rests solidly in her hand. This world is one of sharp, unforgiving edges, a pressure that should be suffocating. Yet she finds it comforting. Familiar. It is a reality she can command.

speaker: Ceto
content: One.

She kills the monster before her and takes a step forward. The act no longer feels like sinking into a hollow, bottomless swamp. Now, each kill delivers a clear, tangible feedback—a purpose solid enough to count, one by one.

speaker: Ceto
content: Two.

Another creature falls with a dying howl as other Rancor soldiers carve a path through her flanks. She presses onward. Here, killing is survival. Fighting is survival. And for the first time, both survival and combat hold meaning.

speaker: Ceto
content: Three.

Forward. Always forward. The soldiers form a living barrier against the endless surge of monsters, like the cliff face once battered by the Black Tide. This battlefield is far from DisCity, but she knows with absolute clarity what lies behind this defense line.

speaker: Ceto
content: The more I kill... the longer I hold... the more I can protect. Fynn, Herbert... ${PlayerName}. Is this what you all believed in?

speaker: Ceto
content: ...Ha. So this is what it feels like... to fight for something worth protecting.
Perhaps she has finally found it: a homeland, a place of belonging. Her new "lighthouse."

speaker: Justice Fan
content: You people need help! Who even defends a maniac who sent a bunch of people into a coma?!

speaker: Die-Hard Fan
content: You're the ones who're crazy! Can't you see she was being used?!

speaker: Janitor Lady
content: Oh dear, doesn't anyone feel bad for that pretty face? Can I sweep up those flyers?

Reporters with cameras of every shape and size thrust their lenses into every contorted face they can find, while beyond the crowd, ordinary passersby look on with no idea what's happening.

The janitor picks up her broom and works her way through the gaps, sweeping the litter into a pile. She has no idea whether this <color=#fb9259>Phanuel</color> everyone keeps going on about has done something good or something terrible. speaker: Janitor Lady
content: Sigh... What a mess...
At the same time, a black sedan glides silently through the VIP entrance on the other side of the venue, unnoticed by anyone.

speaker: Phanuel
content: Posters of Phanuel... banners... and so many people. They all came for Phanuel.

speaker: Phanuel

speaker: ${PlayerName}

After the livestream

speaker: Phanuel
content: Chief, how did I do today?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What do you think?

speaker: Phanuel
content: I think... it went pretty well? I showed everyone a day in my life at the Bureau, just as you asked, and I didn't say anything I wasn't supposed to.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That's true. You didn't say anything out of line. Though there were a few moments when your <color=#fb9259>real thoughts</color> slipped through.

speaker: Phanuel

speaker: Phanuel
content: It's fine... as long as no one touches it. Compared to the pain everyone else went through, this is nothing.

speaker: Phanuel
content: Do you not have other orders for me, Chief?

content: Of course! Today's mission for Phanuel is to deliver a retirement statement and put the chaos to rest.
[Scene Change] Camera flashes, press conference venue

At the press conference venue, media representatives and fan delegates have already taken their positions. Cameras of every size are aimed squarely at the stage, lens caps off, as everyone waits for Phanuel to step out.

Public Security Bureau guards have been posted on either side of the stage, ready to hold back any fan who gets too worked up. You walk onto the stage as part of the accompanying staff and take a quick look at the crowd below.

Reporters in the press section are checking their voice recorders. Meanwhile, fans in the back rows are leaning forward for a better view. Then there's the Public Security Bureau officers, who are pulling the perimeter tape taut. You speak up, just clear enough to reach the very last row.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Phanuel will be reading a statement at today's press conference. Once she is done, she will be escorted back directly by MBCC. There will be no Q&A session.

speaker: Reporter 1
content: No Q&A? Then what are we even here for?

speaker: Reporter 2
content: You just don't get it. Grab a few juicy shots, slap one photo at the top, and you can make up whatever you want. The more sensational, the better.

[Camera Flash Effect]

The curtain parts. Guards close in around Phanuel and slowly escort her into the venue. The cameras erupt all at once, becoming a blinding sea of white. She, however, doesn't even blink, having long gotten used to it.
The moment Phanuel appears, fans surge forward in a frenzy, only to be held back by the wall of guards.

speaker: Justice Fan
content: Get out of the industry, Phanuel!

speaker: Die-Hard Fan
content: We'll be waiting for you, Phanuel!

The shouts of the two factions clash, neither drowning out the other. Phanuel doesn't look at either of them. She keeps her head down and walks onto the stage she hasn't stood on in a long time, one step at a time, and even takes a moment to smile at you.
She picks up the microphone and turns toward the angry fans, bowing deeply. Her back bends lower and lower, as if she might fold herself in two.
The venue, still ringing with jeers just moments ago, falls silent. Her presence alone has dissolved the crowd's anger. The banners in their hands grow heavy, slowly sinking toward the ground.

You glance down at the PR statement in your hand. This is the version the Bureau, the PR team, and Phanuel herself signed off on. Every sentence has been stripped down to the conclusion, nothing more.
Phanuel looks down at the same statement.
<i><color=#7683a2>"To all members of the media and my fans, hello. Thank you for being here today."</color><i>

speaker: Phanuel
content: To all members of the media and my Cherubs, hello. Thank you all... for coming to see me, even in this heat.
You look up. Didn't she say she'd read it over ten times? And she's gone off-script on the very first line?
<i><color=#7683a2>"Regarding the recent events and the harm caused to the general public, my fans, and the families of Hollow Syndrome patients, I sincerely apologize."</color><i>

speaker: Phanuel
content: Regarding the recent events and the harm caused to the public, and to everyone here... I honestly don't know how I'd ever make things right.
You frown. Again, the first half follows the script, but she made up the second half. The focus has shifted from a formal apology to a promise of making amends.

<i><color=#7683a2>"The case is still under investigation, and it will take time for the truth to come to light. However, public discourse has strayed so far from the facts that I felt compelled to come forward and make a statement."</color><i>

speaker: Phanuel
content: The case is still under investigation, and it will take time for the truth to come to light. Though I've lost my memories, and can't provide any further leads...

speaker: Phanuel
content: I still felt like I needed to come forward and set an example for everyone who believes in me.
The first two deviations could still be chalked up to nerves, but this line makes it clear: Phanuel isn't stumbling over the words. She's deliberately rewriting the script.
But what is she trying to do?
<i><color=#7683a2>"I will permanently retire from the entertainment industry and will cooperate fully with the relevant authorities during the investigation."</color><i>

speaker: Phanuel
content: Phanuel has decided... that I will no longer take the stage.

speaker: Die-Hard Fan
content: No! Phanuel! We still want to see you!

speaker: Die-Hard Fan
content: No, Phanuel! How am I supposed to go on without you?!
Phanuel's announcement sends the crowd into a frenzy. You speak into your earpiece, issuing a warning.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Phanuel, stick to the script.
No response. Clearly, she has completely forgotten your agreement. You keep a close watch on the situation, ready to deploy the shackles at a moment's notice.
<i><color=#7683a2>"Thank you all for your support. I also hope everyone will approach this matter rationally, and that no unnecessary conflict will arise from it."</color><i>

speaker: Phanuel
content: I've heard your voices. Thank you so much for the love and support you've given Phanuel. I hope you'll all find happiness!

speaker: Phanuel
content: So please, don't fight over Phanuel. Your love has reached me. Every last bit of it.

speaker: Phanuel
content: To everyone who has ever cheered for Phanuel, everyone who has ever believed in Phanuel... you are proof that Phanuel has lived!
Phanuel's performance is flawless. Even the tears fall at precisely the right moment. One, then two, gently tracing two curves down her cheeks.

speaker: Die-Hard Fan
content: Phanuel! Don't cry! We'll always believe in you!
The statement has lost its purpose. You crumple it up and toss it in the trash.

speaker: Justice Fan
content: What's crying gonna do? Her tears aren't saving the victims!
Phanuel doesn't argue back. She simply bows her head, absorbing every word of the criticism. Her shoulders tremble faintly, but her bandaged hand still holds the microphone steady.

speaker: Phanuel
content: I know. Many people want me gone. And I will be.

speaker: Phanuel
content: But if someday, when you think of Phanuel... it makes you even just a little happy. That would be enough.
Phanuel manages a slight smile, as though even that costs her something. She is radiant under the stage lights. Angelic.

speaker: Die-Hard Fan
content: Phanuel, we just want you back!

speaker: Justice Fan
content: You're gonna forgive her, just like that?! Hey, stop pushing...

speaker: Fans
content:
Fly high, Phanuel! The Cherubs will follow you to the ends of the world! 
Fly high, Phanuel! The Cherubs will follow you to the ends of the world!
Phanuel has twisted the cold, calculated PR language into a genuine apology and confession. The restless pulse of Mania stirring through the venue confirms it: Phanuel is using her ability.

Somewhere along the way, the two factions in the crowd have merged into one. They gaze up at Phanuel with reverence, their emotions wholly in her grip, as the swelling tide of cheers slowly drowns out every voice of dissent.

She's effortlessly shifted the narrative from "Phanuel is guilty" to "Phanuel is a victim too." What was supposed to be a retirement press conference has become, in every sense, Phanuel's comeback tour.
You don't deserve this!
A furious roar cuts through the crowd's sobs. A figure radiating Mania breaks through the security line.
Their cap tumbles to the ground as they sprint forward, revealing a pair of bloodshot eyes, locked right on Phanuel. The sharp blade in their hand gleams coldly.
You don't deserve to be forgiven!
[Red Flash, Screen Shakes, Blood Effect]
The guards lunge forward, but they're half a step too late. The blade goes through the crowd, closing in on the stage.

Yet Phanuel doesn't move out of the way. She looks frightened, but it also looks as though she's been waiting for this very moment. The fragile smile at the corner of her lips hasn't faded. The tears are still on her face.
As the blade closes in, she shuts her eyes.
[Shackles Effect] Black Screen + Red Flash + Screen Shakes
Tears, a smile, vulnerability, anguish—every expression had been readied and waiting. But the pain that should have followed never came. So, she opens her eyes.

The dark crimson shackles have intercepted the attacker. The blade, however, still finds its mark, slicing through the sleeve of the gray figure. The tip punches through the fabric and into the flesh. Vivid red spatters across the hem of Phanuel's dress, dripping drop by drop onto the floor.

speaker: Phanuel
content: Ch-chief...

speaker: Chaotic Crowd
content: AAAHHH!
The venue erupts into chaos. The fans snap out of Phanuel's influence, screaming as they scramble for the exits.
I'll never forgive you! You destroyed my family!
The guards pin the attacker to the ground, but that doesn't stop his roaring. The reporters freeze for just a moment, then the camera flashes erupt all at once.
You turn sideways, using your injured shoulder to block the nearest camera lens, and with it, the shock on Phanuel's face that she hasn't had the chance to hide yet.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Did I ruin your plan, Phanuel?
The burst of camera flashes makes her pupils contract sharply, snapping her back to herself. She composes her expression almost instantly, and swiftly reaches over to steady your injured shoulder.

speaker: Phanuel
content: You're hurt, Chief. We need to get that bandaged right away...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You didn't move out of the way just now.

speaker: Phanuel
content: I just... the shackles held me in place. I couldn't move.
Phanuel didn't step back as the blade closed in. Her right shoulder shifted forward, just barely, a movement so slight that most wouldn't have noticed.
But not you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You leaned in.
The smile on Phanuel's face falters, just a little.

speaker: Phanuel
content: ...I didn't.
You stare at her. Watch as she denies it out of habit, watch as she lies. In this moment, your silence weighs heavier than any accusation could.
The screams from the crowd, the camera shutters, the shouts of the guards all blur together. Amidst it all, she stands rooted to the spot, pinned there by your gaze.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That blade was supposed to be your perfect curtain call. Too bad it missed.

speaker: Phanuel
content: What are you talking about, Chief? Phanuel is really scared of pain, how could I...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That's a lie. If you were, why would you hurt yourself during a livestream just to win sympathy?
Your accusation strikes Phanuel speechless. The smile she had been forcing just moments ago finally begins to slip.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You went off script from the very first line. I'm not sure what you were after, but I did think it'd be fine to let you have your say within reason. Until you scrapped the speech entirely, that is...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You don't actually care what happens to your fans, do you? You just enjoy the attention and the love they give you. Otherwise, why would you use your power on them again?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You said you needed my orders, that you wouldn't know what to do otherwise. And yet, here you are, still fighting for yourself despite receiving none.
The noise of the crowd grows distant. Phanuel looks up at you, and for the first time, she's truly panicking. She realizes the ending she's written has been thrown completely off course.

speaker: Phanuel
content: Phanuel... didn't mean to...
She instinctively lets go of you and tries to step back, but you raise your injured hand to grab her wrist. Your grip is firm, leaving no opportunity for her to run.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Don't run, Phanuel.
Phanuel's thoughts are unravelling, to the point where she can't string together a sentence. She yanks her arm hard, trying to wrench herself free from your grip.

speaker: Phanuel
content: It's time... for Phanuel's curtain call, Chief... Let go...

The usual calmness in Phanuel's voice is gone. She struggles, desperate to get out from under the cameras. Your wound sends a sharp sting through your arm, but you don't let go. You pull her back in front of you, taking that same angle to block the camera lens.
It's only when she sees your wound bleeding again that Phanuel settles down.

speaker: Phanuel
content: Chief, your hand...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That's exactly why I'm saying it now.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: All this time, I couldn't quite wrap my head around just what you're playing at. But I've got it now.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: <color=#fb9259><b>What you want... is a life where everything comes easily. Isn't that right?
She freezes. Her body's strength drains from her, and her clenched fist slowly uncurls, falling slack at her side.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You can abandon an identity. You can start over with new memories. But habits don't lie. You remembered to find the camera, to manage your expression, and every PR line and manipulation trick your manager ever taught you.
The blood soaks through the fabric and drips onto the floor.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: <color=#fb9259><b>You never actually lost your memory.
The words hit Phanuel like a physical blow. A shudder runs through her. Her mouth opens, but her voice doesn't come out. That perfect face, that fragile expression, all gone.
You step closer and lower your voice.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And not just this time...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The last time you <color=#fb9259>reset your life</color>, too.
[Eastside] - Past [Flashbulb Effect] + Flashback Filter
<color=#FFC9F3><i>To love the spotlight, to crave love and attention... Is that really so strange?</color>
A white room. A sharp, acrid smell. The steady beeping of machines. This place is...

speaker: Blurry Face
content: ■■, what do you know about what your parents did? Were you involved?

speaker: Blurry Face
content: Did you really lose your memory? Or is it just a convenient excuse to dodge the public's scrutiny?

speaker: Blurry Face
content: The case is still under investigation. Do not release any images of the individuals involved!

speaker: Blurry Face
content: This is a hospital. The patient hasn't recovered yet. You need to leave!
Her heart won't stop pounding. Her temperature is climbing. Those faces and voices from her memories are nothing but a blur now. What remains is noise and chaos.

It all dissolves into strings of scrambled code, flooding her vision. What follows is a searing headache, causing her to clutch her head and scream. Through the tears, something stirs inside her—a strange, roiling power clawing its way to the surface.

speaker: Girl
content: I'm sorry... I really can't remember...
Streaks of tears mark her face as she manages a smile, confused and apologetic. Somehow, the strange power within her reaches out and smooths away those scrambled codes filling the space.

speaker: Blurry Face
content: If she can't remember, then that's that... She's just a child, after all.

speaker: Blurry Face
content: Exactly. Her parents might be criminals, but that doesn't mean she's one too. Stop putting a child through even more trauma!

She doesn't understand what is happening. All she knows is that whenever she smiles, the people around her suddenly become warm and kind. Slowly, she finds herself drawn to that feeling of being pursued by the spotlight, of being embraced by a crowd.

She can't tell whether those words mean well or harm. All she knows is that when people talk about her, look at her, it fills the emptiness in her heart. It soothes the restless power stirring within her.
A smile. That was the gift she received in the wake of that upheaval.
[Scene Change] - Hypnotherapy Room
<color=#FFC9F3><i>How long has it been since she last saw darkness like this?</color>
She opens her eyes to a calming blue. The rich scent of incense drifts through the air, easing her nerves.
Within that soft light, a counselor in a white professional suit sits at her side.

speaker: Counselor
content: Phanuel, can you hear me?
Phanuel blinks slowly, adjusting to the haziness.

speaker: Counselor
content: Good. Relax a little. Take a look at the lights in the room, and feel the chair against your back. You're at the Bureau now. You're safe.
Right. This is the Bureau.

It has been a few days since the press conference. In that time, the Chief has not pressured her further, and has instead done exactly as she hoped, giving her directives and keeping her schedule filled.

speaker: Phanuel
content: I'm sorry. I still can't remember anything.
She's lying.

speaker: Counselor
content: There's no need to apologize. I'm here to check in on how you're feeling, not whether you've recovered some of your memories, after all. Now then, any heart palpitations, ringing in your ears, nausea, or noticeable physical pain?

speaker: Phanuel
content: I'm a little tired, I guess...

speaker: Counselor
content: Fatigue is worth noting too. Your breathing quickened a few times just now. You don't have to tell me what it was about, but can you tell me what it felt closer to: is it fear, resistance, or sadness?
Phanuel blinks, as if trying to recall the dream she just had.

speaker: Phanuel
content: Hmm... if I had to say, probably nothing at all.

speaker: Phanuel
content: At least Phanuel got a good night's sleep out of it though!
The counselor chuckles, and logs the day's notes on the terminal.

speaker: Phanuel
content: Maybe... It's okay if I never get my memories back, and it's time to start a new chapter? "The Angel Idol Phanuel's Rebirth: My Days as a Model Student at the Bureau"?

speaker: Counselor
content: That's all for today. If you experience any nightmares, auditory hallucinations, or strong reactions to certain words going forward, please inform me or any other medical staff right away.

speaker: Phanuel
content: Got it! Hehe, Phanuel has finished this morning's schedule already. As expected of me! Now I need to find Chief and ask him to add something new to my itinerary.
female_content: Got it! Hehe, Phanuel's finished this morning's schedule already. As expected of me! Now I need to find Chief and ask her to add something new to my itinerary.

content: The girl seals away her past in the black box of memory, as fate pushes her forward, shedding one <color=#fb9259>unimportant</color> thing after another.
What she doesn't know is that the flowers, the applause, and the adoration that so easily fall into her arms were never free. Fate has simply hidden the price tag from her, for now.
And so she took the easiest path. One with no responsibilities to shoulder, no mistakes to own, nor the need to decide where she was headed.

<color=#FFC9F3><i>She simply leaves everything to fate. Even as that path slowly tilted off course, leading her further down the point of no return, she still believed she had finally found the life she always wanted.</color>
[Eastside] Past + Flashback Filter
<color=#FFC9F3><i>This is all it takes to have everything? Then... I don't see why not.</color>
Her smile was what brought her into the public eye. It was the beginning of her next life. A woman arrived with a business card, and became her foster mother.

She found tutors for her, arranged every last detail of her daily life—skincare, posture training, food and lodging, vocal and dance lessons... She didn't need to think about anything. All she had to do was work through each item on her daily schedule, and countless people would love her.

Her life has become far more comfortable than anything she had ever known, so much so that she genuinely forgot about the parents she had never been close to, and the dull past that came with them. Or, perhaps, young as she was, she had already read the danger in Eliza's eyes.

speaker: Eliza
content: From today, your name is <color=#FFC9F3>Phanuel</color>. Whether or not you remember your past, I don't care. If anything, it's better that you don't. You're going to become Eastside's brightest star, the idol of thousands.

speaker: Eliza
content: Your future is bright. You will become a superstar. All you have to do is be a good girl and do as you're told, and that smile of yours will get you everything... Am I clear?
What was Eliza to her? A mother? A superior? A caretaker? Perhaps all of the above. After all, she tended to her every need, gave her a life free of worry, and raised her to the clouds.
Her past was wiped clean by a mysterious power. An idol cannot have a stain on their name, much less if that stain is their parents.

She did forget everything about the past, if only briefly. But as the power within her settled, those scattered memories came back to her, piece by piece. By then, however, she could no longer speak of them. Even if she remembered, she must forget again.
<color=#FFC9F3><i>After all... a lie can only be held together by countless more.</color>
[Scene Change] Bureau Cafeteria / Recreation Area?

speaker: Wynn
content: Oh wow, Phanuel! It's so rare to see you here. Have you finally figured out how to eat fish?!
Phanuel has been locked in a staring contest with the fish on her tray. Upon hearing Wynn's voice, she looks up with an awkward smile.

speaker: Phanuel
content: Yup... Chief said the Bureau isn't a daycare, so I need to learn to take care of myself. Look, my task for today is to "eat a whole fish on my own without choking on a bone."
She holds up the schedule and shows it to Wynn with a grin. That said, both Phanuel's expression and the untouched fish on her tray say plenty about how out of her depth she truly is.

speaker: Wynn
content: Ugh, I swear, Chief really needs to learn that some things must be done one step at a time! Next time, I'll ask the kitchen to swap it out for a fish with fewer bones!
Wynn pulls a chair over to sit beside Phanuel and rolls up her sleeves.

speaker: Wynn
content: I'm great at this sort of thing, so let me teach you the ropes! If anything, nothing makes me happier than being able to help you, Phanuel!

speaker: Phanuel
content: Then... I'll leave it to you!

Unfortunately, somewhere down the line, Wynn became practically enthralled from being up close with Phanuel. And so, the "teacher" became a caretaker, picking out every bone for Phanuel before she could even touch it.

speaker: Wynn
content: Phanuel, your smile is so beautiful...

speaker: Phanuel
content: Thank you, Wynn. Here, this is for you.
She holds out a CD with "To Wynn" written on it, along with an adorable little doodle of an angel throwing a peace sign. Wynn clutches it like it's the greatest treasure in the world and skips away.

Reading people, managing her image, deploying small and harmless calculations to keep her fans' affection intact... These have all become instinct for Phanuel. Because to her, seeing everyone's smiles is the only way for her to know for sure that she did well.

She once craved the worship of adoring crowds. But when the flowers, the applause, and the love finally came pouring in, her heart remained hollow. Why is it that the tiniest glimmer of her light can make these people overjoyed?

As Wynn's footsteps fade, Phanuel drops her angelic smile and tries to make an ordinary one instead, something plain but real. She tugs at the corners of her mouth a few times, but her face refuses to relax, so the resulting expression is strange, to say the least. She gives up.

She sighs and looks down at her tray. The carefully deboned fish sits there, so neatly arranged it almost feels like an act of flattery. She pokes at it idly, picks up a piece, and brings it to her lips.
A stray bone pokes out from the flesh. Phanuel wrinkles her nose.

speaker: Phanuel
content: Oh no, what do I do? Wynn worked so hard on this...
The old Phanuel would have tipped the whole tray into the trash without a second thought. Now, however... she stares at the offending bone.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: These gifts were found when we searched your home. I assumed they would be things that mattered to you, but their condition seems... less than ideal.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You shouldn't treat other people's feelings like something you can just throw away.

speaker: Phanuel
content: Well... if Chief says so... food made with love should be eaten with gratitude.
The girl mutters to herself. It sounds both like a complaint and an excuse. She reaches out and carefully pinches away the bone, something she once would never have touched.
<color=#FFC9F3><i>The steamed fish tastes pretty ordinary. But it's not bad, either.</color>
