speaker: Summer
content: But it's not exactly accurate to call it a substance. It's a by-product created when the imaginary number sequence of will invades reality.

speaker: Summer
content: It contains extremely powerful mental power and can even influence substances in reality.

speaker: Summer
content: Humph, for sure. This is also the idea behind the Ring Weapon's design, using the purest spirits as its core to provide bottomless firepower!

speaker: Summer
content: Sigh... It's a shame that before the Ring Weapon was put into mass production, the project got called off. Otherwise, with this weapon, the FAC could have long eliminated all traces of whatever Mania super easily.
It looks like the fragment inside you hides even more secrets you're unaware of.
You must eradicate its influence. Otherwise, it may awaken anytime and corrupt your mind completely.

options: How do you stop mental contamination?

speaker: Summer
content: Spiritual contamination is only a phenomenon, an outcome.

speaker: Summer
content: Essentially, it is the result of mutual interference and compression of the boundaries of the spiritual and physical dimensions.

speaker: Summer
content: To stop it completely, you need to eradicate the source of Mania—the Black Ring.

speaker: Summer
content: Except that someone already tried that long ago.

options: Was it during the BR-000 incident?

speaker: Summer
content: No, even earlier than that.

speaker: Summer
content: When the Perishing Star struck, someone already came up with this solution.

speaker: Summer
content: But until today, no one has succeeded.

speaker: Summer
content: Though existing Black Rings have been successfully removed, new Black Rings keep popping up.

speaker: Summer
content: People keep turning into Sinners under their influence, one after another.

speaker: Summer
content: The Black Ring is probably only the result of mass occurrences of a certain phenomenon, and its impact is irreversible.

speaker: Summer
content: Now, what do you think is the thing that causes a Black Ring to occur, Chief?
Summer throws the question at you.
You think of the black box brought to the negotiation venue, the thing that turned Zoya into the Black Ring's ground zero.
The thing that lives inside your body now.
An answer slowly forms in your brain, the one you reject the most.

speaker: Summer
content: Correct, it's the inheritance.

speaker: Summer
content: I'm lucky enough to have seen the residue of that thing. Only a few picograms of it... can generate an infinite amount of energy.

speaker: Summer
content: I'm very positive that it's something that absolutely, definitely does not belong in this world.

speaker: Summer
content: If I find it... If I find it, the source of the disaster, the truth of the world will be presented right before my eyes.

speaker: Summer
content: How I wish to see it... I wish to see it so much!

speaker: Summer
content: Don't you want to see it, Chief? To find out what the secret hidden beneath the filthiest soil is?

speaker: Summer
content: Oh... Seriously? Don't lie to me, Chief.
I only saw it in a dream, it looked like... a white box.

speaker: Summer
content: And inside it? Is there anything inside the box?
As soon as you mention the white box, Summer seems really intrigued.
There seems to be... a fragment inside.

speaker: Summer
content: Hahahaha... I see, I see!
As if having an epiphany, Summer suddenly laughs loudly.

speaker: Summer
content: Thanks for telling me that, Chief. But one must not lie.

speaker: Summer
content: If you saw it with your own eyes, then admit it. Don't make up some dream like that.

speaker: Summer
content: Otherwise... things may end up terribly for you.

speaker: Summer
content: No wonder... your aura feels so familiar, Chief.

speaker: Summer
content: It feels like the lab at Parma...
Summer leans into you, her warm breaths brushing against your ear.

speaker: Summer
content: Dear Chief, how do you explain the thing about the Black Ring in Keylan Square? The records show that no one was sent to clean up the site after its disappearance.

speaker: Summer
content: It should be the most valuable research material, yet there has been no news about it in the FAC, the Legion, or even the Research Institute.

speaker: Summer
content: The only possible explanation is that... the MBCC has taken it.

speaker: Summer
content: Half a month ago, I infiltrated the MBCC's intranet, but I didn't find any information about the inheritance.

speaker: Summer
content: That's why I'm sure that...

speaker: Summer
content: The inheritance, is inside you, right now.
She points at the tip of your nose with her index finger.

speaker: Summer
content: When I first saw you, I thought you were just an ordinary person, someone who shared my interest in anime.

speaker: Summer
content: ...The shackles and the Black Ring's fragments. These are areas out of reach of ordinary people.

speaker: Summer
content: What has been presented before me only lead me to believe that you're the ideal vessel for the truth!
Summer expands her armor and walks toward you slowly.

speaker: Summer
content: What kind of answer can I find on you?

speaker: Summer
content: When the source of Sinners, the source of Mania, and the source of the Ring all combine into one, what will be the outcome... I'm really looking forward to that.

speaker: Summer
content: Will it be coexistence or destruction? Let's go, Chief, explore the truth and mystery of the world with me!
Summer's expression has grown frantic, as if she's completely lost her sanity.
You want to put the Bureau in the emergency mode to temporarily block Summer's ability.
But right after you press the button on the control panel, you find that nothing happens.

speaker: Summer
content: I've already told you, I've infiltrated the intranet half a month ago. Why wouldn't I have the Bureau's admin rights? You've truly underestimated the power of Infinite Knowledge, Chief.
You want to forbid her actions with the shackles, but before you can say more than one word, a tranquilizer shot is stuck in your leg.
You...

speaker: Summer
content: Let's go! Let's go! Chief...

speaker: Summer
content: Let's begin our experiment!

speaker: Laplace
content: The Chief of the MBCC and S-Class Sinner Summer have gone missing.

speaker: Laplace
content: Okay.

speaker: Laplace
content: The first target is deduced to be the ruins of the Laboratory of Parma.

speaker: Laplace
content: Yes, this is the outcome I've been anticipating.

speaker: Laplace
content: Welcome back, my genius.
You wake up.
You reach out your hand, and what you feel is the touch of cold steel. You seem to be locked in a ring-shaped experiment apparatus.
This is a prison cell someone has built especially for you. You try to use the shackles, but notice they've been blocked by some kind of power.
Looking out the glass window on the wall, you see the familiar Parma Ruins.
The apparatuses are visibly worn, old like the ruins, but the young girl is operating them skillfully, as if she's always been conducting experiments here.
Seeing that you've woken up, she only waves at you, then carries on with her operation.

speaker: Drone
content: Cleaning routine, set-up completed...

speaker: Drone
content: Transporting route, set-up completed...

speaker: Drone
content: Solution mixing, in progress, 73% completed. Fully completed in approximately 3 minutes.
Dozens of drones are transporting objects along the route she's set up and cleaning the devices. Everything is working in perfect order.

speaker: Summer
content: Alright... The preparation is done. A3, turn off the fractionator and fractionating column.

speaker: Drone
content: Command confirmed, ready to execute.
Before you, Summer has been completely taken over by her thirst for knowledge. She's giving commands to the drones calmly to ensure the smooth execution of the experiment.
You knock hard on the metal prison cell imprisoning you, hoping Summer can free you from it.

speaker: Summer
content: Stop struggling, Chief.

speaker: Summer
content: With your power, it's impossible to break it. Moreover, with this thing here... you can't use the shackles on me now.

speaker: Summer
content: I'll let you out when it's time. If you're too bored, have a go at this.
Summer presses a button and an 11x11 Rubik's cube drops before you.

speaker: Summer
content: Why? You're the ideal candidate for the inheritance. Don't you know your own worth?

speaker: Summer
content: This is a necessary step toward the truth, toward saving the world!
In the desolate Parma Ruins, only the mechanical buzz of the drones can be heard.
Like those monsters in the Black Ring?

speaker: Summer
content: As someone qualified for the inheritance, you don't have to worry about such things.

speaker: Summer
content: If my assumption is correct, nothing's gonna go wrong... Even if you hug it in your arms and give it a kiss.
Summer answers your questions as she mixes solutions of various colors together, gives the mixture a shake, and sets it down.

speaker: Summer
content: Amazing, this is the most stable state I've ever seen.

speaker: Summer
content: Parma is the right choice, after all.

speaker: Summer
content: Hmm? ...You don't even know that, being the Chief of Minos and all?

speaker: Summer
content: The inheritance was initially stored right here, in the Laboratory of Parma.

speaker: Summer
content: I couldn't find it here back then... But now, my wish is finally coming true!

speaker: Summer
content: Great! I'm a step closer... to the truth.

options: I can't believe you're no different than Parma.

content: Has your intention always been... to steal the inheritance?

speaker: Summer
content: Steal? No, no, what an awful way to put it.

speaker: Summer
content: To be honest with you, I don't care where the inheritance is. All I care about is that I get to study the mystery of this inheritance.

speaker: Summer
content: Next, we'll test the compatibility of the bearer and this stuff.

speaker: Drone
content: Inspecting experiment environment... Result: Good. Experiment can begin immediately.
Summer is operating the experiment panel, and a pale blue solution starts filling the glass prison cell you're in.
What is this?!

speaker: Summer
content: Oh? This is the inheritance catalyst number three concocted by me. All the raw materials were obtained from regular purchasing channels in the Bureau.
You want to distract Summer and seize this chance to stop her with the shackles, but this proves somewhat difficult for you, having just awoken.

speaker: Summer
content: Hey... Relax. For someone like you, this won't be a great burden to your body.

speaker: Summer
content: It may just... hurt a little.
The solution is growing in volume. You feel as though you're back to that boundless abyss, countless hands tearing at you hysterically.
Viscous, painful, and maniacal emotions are pouring into your mind, the origin of the mystery has once again opened its door to you.
But this time there are no terrifying Corpsebornes or sad departures.

speaker: Summer
content: The emotions are stable, prepare to increase the dosage.
The solution keeps increasing. You must think of a way to escape from this glass prison cell. Even if it's for the truth of the world, one shouldn't attempt something like this.
The metal prison cell is unusually hard. It's impossible to break free of it with bare hands.
Your gaze shifts to the Rubik's cube Summer has thrown in. You grip the cube and smash it on the metallic surface.
Sadly, it's only a most ordinary Rubik's cube.
The reaction wrecks it easily and the color cubes shatter everywhere. One piece of it cuts your hand and a small amount of blood drips into the solution.

speaker: Summer
content: Chief—Don't attempt any dangerous moves! Just wait patiently!

speaker: Summer
content: Next, it's time to uncover the truth and save the world!
Uncover the truth and save the world...?
That's one of the iconic lines from The Age of Youth.

speaker: Summer
content: Come on, come on, come on, come on, come on!

speaker: Summer
content: The truth... is waving at me on the other side!
You know that Summer wants to replicate the inheritance's initial form through simulation.
And you had the luck to see what was on the other side.
There lies only pain, darkness, and despair.
What's hidden on the side where the inheritance lies may not be the truth.
Suddenly, you hear a fine noise in the massive Petri dish you're in.
The frequency of the noise starts getting faster, and its volume bigger.
As if gaining its own consciousness, the solution is eating through the metal prison cell aggressively.
Visible cracks begin appearing on the incredibly hard steel. The pain plaguing you is also dwindling.

speaker: Drone
content: Warning, pressure in the container is dropping continuously.

speaker: Drone
content: Warning, stability of the container cannot be sustained.

speaker: Summer
content: There are... errors?

speaker: Summer
content: No way... It shouldn't turn out like this! The solution should have fused with the inheritance and generated new power...

speaker: Summer
content: Again, let me try that again! It shouldn't have turned out like this!

speaker: Summer
content: I must be able to turn this curse... into infinite energy!
The situation looks just like when Summer hits a bottleneck in the anime.
The inheritance won't bring you the truth. It only brings destruction!

speaker: Summer
content: No!

speaker: Summer
content: I was... so close to making it! So close... to making it!
She's panicking and seems helpless, yet she can only keep endeavoring endlessly to search for the unknown truth.
Our little genius seems very troubled.
A familiar voice is echoing on the experiment site.

speaker: Summer
content: How did you find me?
Through those two videotapes, of course. Our genius is still careless as always.

speaker: Summer
content: ...But I've made sure to delete all my records of use.
It's hard to locate you, but it's easy to locate him.
female_content: It's hard to locate you, but it's easy to locate her.

speaker: Summer
content: My patience is limited. Seeing that we were once colleagues, I don't want to harm you.
Not bad, you've become much calmer than before.
Your past self would have already fired at me.
Haha, enough of that.
How about we make a deal? A deal about the truth.
Why, you're not interested?

speaker: Summer
content: Go on.
The initial test on the MBCC's Chief, Parma's remaining members, and the ceaseless reports on the dark web. These three things combined give you nerves, am I right?

speaker: Summer
content: Of course, I'm the hero who's going to save the world. I can't sit back and watch the world go into an even bigger crisis.

options: The world going into a crisis?

content: I've never heard about this.
We're talking about you, my dear Chief. As the bearer of the inheritance, who wouldn't be curious about your body?
That's why the deal is really simple. There's only one term.
Come back to the Research Institute with me, Summer.

In return, I can provide you with protection on behalf of the Research Institute. You'll regain freedom at the same time, no longer trapped in the MBCC's birdcage. And you'll receive way more generous research support.
As for this guy, once we're back, I'll let you study him with state-of-the-art equipment instead of a tacky metal can like this.
female_content: As for this one, once we're back, I'll let you study her with state-of-the-art equipment instead of a tacky metal can like this.

content: Consider my offer, my little genius.
Summer's expression is serious, looking like she's mulling over the man's words.
We've missed the good timing. Right now, the FAC needs his power, and even that old hag at the 9th Agency has her eyes fixed on him. It's hard to get in touch with him through ordinary means.
female_content: We've missed the good timing. Right now, the FAC needs her power, and even that old hag at the 9th Agency has her eyes fixed on her. It's hard to get in touch with her through ordinary means.

content: As he speaks, he sticks out his fingers and gently knocks a couple times on the experiment equipment imprisoning you.
But the Research Institute will find a way to make him disappear, turning him into your permanent research material.
female_content: But the Research Institute will find a way to make her disappear, turning her into your permanent research material.

content: We're all passionate about the truth, but the Research Institute treasures a one-in-a-million genius more.
Summer, did you know? Everyone at the Research Institute... is looking forward to your return! There are many interesting projects waiting for you!
It'll be so much more fun than watching anime in that shabby place all day!
Let him out, we should go now.
female_content: Let her out, we should go now.

content: The mysterious man beckons to Summer.

speaker: Summer
content: Laplace, you're still so boring.

speaker: Laplace
content: What did you say...?

speaker: Laplace
content: This time the Research Institute will be fully in charge. Parma's tragedy won't happen again.

speaker: Laplace
content: As long as you come back and make your mark, you'll be the next Keylan, esteemed and praised by all.

speaker: Laplace
content: The process doesn't matter. Once you achieve the right results, you'll be the Hero.

speaker: Summer
content: You're still as shallow as always. Hero to me is not a title or a name.

speaker: Summer
content: It's the one thing that I find the most interesting and must keep living up to!

speaker: Summer
content: I will find the solution with my own powers. Your Research Institute... Ha, you'd better step aside this time. I will never trust you guys again, ever.

speaker: Summer
content: I will keep fighting and carrying out my own research while sticking to my initial intention.

speaker: Laplace
content: If we pair your formula with the endless seeds in the Research Institute!

speaker: Laplace
content: We'll soon obtain power comparable to that of a Black Ring!

speaker: Laplace
content: Why? Why don't you understand? There are so many more truths waiting for you! Why do you choose to waste your time here?

speaker: Summer
content: Haha, blame it on your wicked tricks. Selling all my research findings to Parma, no hero will make such a despicable act!

speaker: Laplace
content: Fine... fine! Go on lying low, go on being an underachieving loser then! I shall triumph over you, so the world will know that even without Summer... research on the Ring can still continue!

speaker: Summer
content: Isn't that beyond your reach, considering your capability, Laplace?

speaker: Laplace
content: It looks like we've run out of room for talk again, Summer.
The solution filling up to your waist still keeps stimulating the Black Ring fragment in your body, like numerous ants nibbling at your nerves.
You want to stop the conflict between the two as soon as possible. Summer knocks on the container, signaling you to stop.

speaker: Summer
content: Just wait for me patiently, Chief.

speaker: Summer
content: A battle is coming up next. It's the safest choice to stay in there.
Before she finishes her sentence, a laser beam is shot toward where you are. But before it touches that cage imprisoning you, it's blocked by Summer's drone.

speaker: Laplace
content: Haha... I'm impressed. Even though our combat team members hasn't carried any metal equipment on them, you've still spotted them.

speaker: Laplace
content: Attention, capture her alive!

speaker: Soldier
content: Understood. Everyone, be sure to control the laser intensity.

speaker: Laplace
content: Come on, show me... just how much your Ring Weapon has improved in the past two years.

speaker: Laplace
content: Fire!
At Laplace's command, countless bullets are sprayed toward Summer.

speaker: Summer
content: Activate defensive stance.
At her command, all the drones within the area immediately form an enormous shield before her and you.
Sparks are flying everywhere, and the defensive shell can barely block all the laser beams shooting at you.

speaker: Drone
content: Warning, high temperature detected. Defensive shell will melt in approximately five seconds. Please take cover in time.

speaker: Drone
content: Time remaining: four seconds.

speaker: Soldier
content: Keep firing! She won't last long!

speaker: Drone
content: Time remaining: three seconds.

speaker: Soldier
content: Copy that! Keep up with the attacking rate!

speaker: Drone
content: Time remaining: two seconds.

speaker: Laplace
content: Is this the truth you're after? How ridiculous... You're going to bring shame to the Ring Research Institute.

speaker: Summer
content: So what... if I do? I don't want anything more to do with the Research Institute anymore anyway!

speaker: Drone
content: Time remaining: one second.

speaker: Summer
content: I see that the Research Institute hasn't raised its standards. It's easy to spot a weakness in such an overly regular attack pattern.

speaker: Drone
content: Shield melting, please take cover.
Summer looks fearless and doesn't even react to the drone's severe warning.

speaker: Soldier
content: Has she lost her mind?! How can we capture her alive like this? Cease fire, now!

speaker: Summer
content: Reform battle formation!
The moment the shield melts, Summer gives her command and pushes out the already damaged drones to block the last round of attack.

speaker: Summer
content: A2, A4, A6, A8, A10, switch to attack mode, quit defense formation.

speaker: Drone
content: Command accepted, preparing to change battle strategy.

speaker: Summer
content: B3, B6, B9, B12, switch to tracking mode, prepare to eliminate specific targets.

speaker: Drone
content: Command accepted, preparing to eradicate threats.
The drones begin adjusting their combat forms, locking onto one hidden enemy after another.

speaker: Summer
content: Full system locked on, clear area!
With a snap of a finger from Summer, brilliant blue flames shot out from the Ring Weapon.
Boom—
Amid intense explosions, the offense-and-defense dynamic on the battlefield reverses within a second.
Laplace's lackeys have their armor blown away by the immense firepower. Despite having taken over the bunker, they can't resist the intense bombarding by the Ring Weapon.

speaker: Summer
content: Yield, Laplace. If you leave now, I can pretend none of this has happened.
Laplace is laughing hysterically, putting on a strange glove. With a wave of his hand, all of Summer's attacks are ceased entirely.

speaker: Laplace
content: Looks like our genius has learned quite a few lame jokes in the Bureau.

speaker: Summer
content: If Parma hadn't been destroyed, you would have become one of them long ago, wouldn't you?

speaker: Laplace
content: Haha, hahaha... Parma? What could I have gotten from Parma?

speaker: Laplace
content: Let me show you the latest technology from the Ring Research Institute! Those Ring Weapons and drones of yours, they are no more than toys in the face of it.

speaker: Laplace
content: I don't want to play hero with you anymore. Recognize the difference in strength between you and us, and come back, Summer.
A brilliant blue light is gathering in Laplace's palm. You sense danger instinctively.
After he's put on that glove, all you can feel from Laplace is... a fear that can destroy everything.
Just like what you felt in that battle with the Corpseborne.
You look at Summer. Under his attack, there won't be any chance of survival even if Summer fights back with all her might.
The only hope is to use the shackles to amplify Summer's ability so she can resist Laplace's attack.
The entrance to the abyss, the origin of mysteries, the beginning of disasters. What actually lies there? You close your eyes gently, feeling the guidance your body receives.
The truth is right before your eyes, yet you can't reach it. It's quiet under the dead silence.
You finally activate the shackles successfully. The blue solution has brought you endless suffering, but it's also given you unimaginable power.
The shackles pierce through the solution and split into countless blood-red thorns, spreading from the metal container covered in cracks.

speaker: Summer
content: Chief... You...
Noticing the sudden changes behind her, Summer scrambles over to stop you.
But the power no longer brings you pain. It reassures you instead.
No haggard figures, no painful emotions, only power in its purest form.
It passes through the steel and firmly connects to Summer.
Unlike extremely painful emotions, it doesn't long to devour, doesn't crave each other, and doesn't thirst for blood, flesh, or souls. It simply exists.
It wants to help others, wants to become their hero.
It's the purest emotion, as well as part of Summer's truth.
Only, sustaining this state is extremely demanding on your spirit.
You force yourself to steady the shackles and give Summer your final order.

speaker: Summer
content: Humph, I knew it. How will my truth possibly be defeated?
The shackles pierce through the solution and split into countless blood-red thorns, spreading from the metal container covered in cracks.

speaker: Summer

No haggard figures, no painful emotions, only power in its purest form.
It passes through the steel and firmly connects to Summer.
Unlike extremely painful emotions, it doesn't long to devour, doesn't crave each other, and doesn't thirst for blood, flesh, or souls. It simply exists.
It wants to help others, wants to become their hero.
It's the purest emotion, as well as part of Summer's truth.
Only, sustaining this state is extremely demanding on your spirit.
You force yourself to steady the shackles and give Summer your final order.

speaker: Summer
content: Humph, I knew it. How will my truth possibly be defeated?
The shackles pierce through the solution and split into countless blood-red thorns, spreading from the metal container covered in cracks.

content: Humph, I knew it. How will my truth possibly be defeated?
Summer turns back and smiles at you.

speaker: Laplace
content: Those bizarre tricks of yours... are no match for the great invention by the Ring Research Institute! Hahahaha...

speaker: Summer
content: No wonder the battle scenes were so poorly made in the second episode... You can't even imagine how I'd look when I destroy Parma.

speaker: Summer
content: This time, take a good look at how I butcher a whole team of villains on my own, and do a remake when you get back!
The two sides pull the triggers at the same time. The blinding light forces you to keep your eyes shut.
An unfamiliar ceiling, the edge of an unfamiliar bed, and unfamiliar curtains.
And...
An unfamiliar person.

speaker: Summer
content: How are you recovering? Chief?

options: I guess I just got burns.
I thought I was gonna die.

speaker: Summer
content: Thanks to my perfect control of firepower.

speaker: Summer
content: I was trying really hard to control the firepower!

speaker: Summer
content: Blame it on Laplace, he was the one who went too far.
I still think the person who locked me in a metal can was the one who went too far.

speaker: Summer
content: No clue. All the surveillance equipment has been destroyed by fire.

speaker: Summer
content: And I didn't find any trace of him.

speaker: Summer
content: Ugh... I was so sure I would succeed the first time! If he hadn't held me back, I probably could have done it!

options: Can you give me a heads-up next time?

speaker: Summer
content: Uh... nope.

speaker: Chief
content: Why?!

speaker: Chief
content: I almost died in that experiment.

options: What happened to that thing inside me?

speaker: Summer
content: While you were asleep, I did a complete and comprehensive physical examination on you.

speaker: Summer
content: Eh... What's that expression supposed to mean?

speaker: Summer
content: Come on, it was handled by the drones—of course I didn't touch you or anything.

speaker: Chief
content: And what's the final conclusion?

speaker: Summer
content: There's good news and bad news. Which one do you want to hear first?

speaker: Summer
content: I strongly recommend you start with the good news.

speaker: Summer
content: Your body is in good condition, Chief!
And what's the bad news?

speaker: Summer
content: The bad news is that... um, that thing still exists inside your body.

speaker: Summer
content: If you overuse the shackles or get too close to a Black Ring... I can't guarantee what will end up happening.

options: So just the same as before.

content: You chuckle drily, thinking of it as running a lap... then returning to the starting point.

speaker: Summer
content: I was wondering, Chief... if I apologize to you solemnly, can you pretend what happened today was just a dream?

speaker: Summer
content: Everything is just as it was before. Nothing happened. Don't look into anything. There are certain things that can put you in great danger the more you know about them.
At least for now, your body apparently hasn't gone through any actual abnormal changes.
But you must make Summer go into the confinement cell, and she won't be allowed to have chocolate for a while. She'd better be prepared to face the consequences of doing such a thing to the Chief.
You look down at the unfamiliar hospital bed and suddenly recall something very important.

speaker: Summer
content: Ah...

speaker: Summer
content: Let's wait a bit longer.

speaker: Chief
content: This is a kidnap case aimed at the Chief, Sinner Summer.

speaker: Chief
content: If we go back too late, your punishment won't be as simple as going into the confinement cell.

speaker: Summer
content: Well, then... At least wait till after we finish watching the ending of The Age of Youth.
Summer begins blinking excessively at you.
Usually, when she does that, it means she's up to something.

speaker: Chief
content: Where are we going to watch it?

speaker: Summer
content: Downstairs, of course.
Loud noise can be heard from the hallway. Apparently, this is no desolate place.

options: Why isn't there a new videotape for The Age of Youth this time?

speaker: Chief
content: Did Laplace give it to you beforehand?

speaker: Summer
content: No.
Summer shakes her head and motions you to look out the window.

speaker: Summer
content: We're going to shoot it real-time this time!
Just as you're still wondering how Summer, who's very weak physically, carried you upstairs, Summer has already changed into a new outfit.
She's taken off her jacket from the Research Institute and changed into a suit, a small flower clipped to her chest.

speaker: Summer
content: The graduation ceremony is about to begin. Shall we go together, Chief?

speaker: Summer
content: That's the third episode of The Age of Youth—Graduation.
The two of you walk to the playground with all the other students.

speaker: Summer
content: Chief! Here, here!

speaker: Chief
content: I'm not wearing a school uniform, what if the security guards notice me and kick me out?

speaker: Summer
content: Haha, no worries. I'll tell them you're my parent.

speaker: Summer
content: After all, this is the last day at school. Even the strictest security guard... will surely grant the students' wishes.

options: Why did you decide to come here all of a sudden?

speaker: Summer
content: Because I still don't have the important life experience of graduation.
You almost can't believe your ears.
No graduation? Then how did you get into the Ring Research Institute?

speaker: Summer
content: Like... they just asked me.

speaker: Summer
content: They asked me if I wanted to do research on things related to the Ring substance.
And you said yes just like that?

speaker: Summer
content: Of course, that's the Ring substance we're talking about! Although it didn't end up well between me and them...
You're suddenly speechless. Apparently, a genius's world is indeed different than that of ordinary people.

speaker: Principal
content: Testing... Testing...?

speaker: Principal
content: Can you hear me?
On the makeshift podium, someone who looks like the principal is testing the mic. Once he shows up, the noisy students soon all stop talking.

speaker: Summer
content: I guess... it's beginning now.

speaker: Principal
content: Eileen!

speaker: Eileen
content: Present!

speaker: Principal
content: This is for you. I hope that in the future... you will still think of your schoolmates and all your teachers here.

speaker: Principal
content: You've finished your journey here. But soon enough, you will set off on a new journey.

speaker: Principal
content: You had good academic achievements and diverse hobbies. If you keep working hard and always apply your thinking... you will certainly find a path best suited for yourself.

speaker: Eileen
content: Thank you... Thank you, Principal!
The girl receives her graduation certificate, looking both overjoyed and sentimental.

speaker: Principal
content: Next... Ronnie!
The boy named Ronnie walks up to the podium steadily.

speaker: Principal
content: I remember when you first came, you were the most mischievous boy here. It seems like... time really does change a person.

speaker: Ronnie
content: No, it's all because of your guidance.

speaker: Principal
content: Hahaha... You've even grown to become a smooth talker too! Here, for you! Those who can adapt to the surrounding environment will always be the winners.

speaker: Principal
content: I'm looking forward to your future achievements, Ronnie!
The students go up the podium one after another, receiving the proof of their three years of study.
The summer wind in June is hot. Even though it's almost evening now, the setting sun is still radiating warmth.
The two of you are standing at the front of the procession. Listening to the principal's graduation speech, Summer suddenly grows sentimental.

speaker: Summer
content: Well, to be honest with you, I envy these kids a lot.

speaker: Summer
content: They have healthy bodies, unlike me who's always been sickly... I couldn't do anything on my own. All I could do was sit in the classroom and work on questions.

speaker: Summer
content: It was bearable at first, when my classmates could still talk to me about the questions I was working on. But as I moved on to tougher and tougher questions, everyone in my class treated me like a weirdo.
At the time, you didn't have... any friends in your class?

speaker: Summer
content: Hmm... I guess you can say I had one.

speaker: Chief
content: And who's that?

speaker: Summer
content: Anime.

options: It has to be a person.

speaker: Summer
content: Then... I didn't have any, indeed. But... back then, anime was my only friend.

speaker: Summer
content: That invincible high school girl is everything I long for. She has her youth, her adventures, her friends, and her wonderful daily life. She's given me my infinite imagination and courage.

options: Perhaps that's the price of being a genius.

content: No one truly understands them.

speaker: Summer
content: That's why the ending of The Age of Youth must be like this: having saved the world, the genius high school girl returns to her friends and has her graduation, putting a perfect full stop on her hero adventure.

speaker: Summer
content: But... even if she comes back to school, she has no friends here, so she'll make do with the Chief.
While you are discussing the ending of the third episode, the names of all graduates have already been called.
The students there are all leaving to take pictures with their graduate certificates. Only you and Summer are left in the ceremony venue.
Summer seems a little hesitant, so you propose the idea to her.

speaker: Summer
content: Hmm... I guess we can, but let me put on my glasses! What do you think? Do I look more like a high schooler like this?
But just as you want to step into the crowd, you receive a call from Nightingale.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, how are you doing?

speaker: Chief
content: I got injured, but it's nothing serious.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Is the Sinner Summer still under your control?
Summer glances at you, a little uneasy.

speaker: Chief
content: Yes.

speaker: Nightingale
content: The MBCC's search unit will arrive at your location right away, please stay where you are.

speaker: Chief
content: Copy that.

speaker: Summer
content: Sigh... In the end, this is not a ceremony a Sinner can attend.

speaker: Chief
content: I'm sorry.

speaker: Summer
content: Hahaha... No need to apologize for something like this, Chief.

speaker: Summer
content: I simply find it interesting. I want to experience things I've never experienced before.

speaker: Summer
content: If something is interesting enough, I'll do it. But the situation this time is special, I'll let it be...

speaker: Summer
content: This is the way I, Summer, do things in my life.
The graduation ceremony at dusk has come to a perfect end, and you get in the car going back to the Bureau.

speaker: Summer
content: Come to think of it, what happened today can only count as a drill.

options: How intense are the regular fights?

speaker: Summer
content: The crisis threatening the world is even bigger than I thought.

speaker: Summer
content: During the battle with Laplace, I felt a strange power.

speaker: Summer
content: I was lucky to have you by my side, Chief, so I was able to completely offset his power. That's why... you're my necessary catalyst for saving the world.

speaker: Summer
content: Ah... No, companion.

speaker: Summer
content: So, let's go back. Go back to the MBCC.

speaker: Summer
content: I don't need help from those deceitful people at the Ring Research Institute.

speaker: Summer
content: No matter what challenges I face, I have to write my own story, find the truth, and save the world in my own way.

speaker: Summer
content: Write the perfect ending for The Age of Youth.

speaker: Summer
content: Why aren't we allowed to bring anything into the confinement cell, Chief?

options: What kind of confinement cell will that be?

speaker: Summer
content: But... I want to eat chocolate.

speaker: Chief
content: Don't even mention your chocolate.

speaker: Chief
content: Do you still remember what happened last time?

speaker: Summer
content: Ahem! That was an accident! An accident!

speaker: Summer
content: As I've said, invention always involves accidents!

speaker: Summer
content: ...Ugh, I can at least order some at the Supply Office, can't I?
You can, but you'll need my final approval.

speaker: Summer
content: Sob... Damn it, I can't ask Nightingale to tweak the quantity for me this time.

speaker: Summer
content: If it causes delays in my invention, I won't be able to meet the standards in The Age of Youth, which means I can't save the world. You'll be liable for that! Hey! Don't you run away!
Teary-eyed, the genius inventor watches you leave the confinement cell.
But eventually, in the approval form for the chocolate purchase order, you increase the volume discreetly...
Perhaps this can somewhat compensate the girl for not being able to have her graduation this summer.
The lights in the interrogation room are turned off. Someone is murmuring in the darkness.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: You shall endure hardships and surpass all stelae in this world. You shall meet the golden falcon, and the winged traveler will guide you to the light. Where there is light, there you shall be.
You find this poem oddly familiar.
When you walk in, Oak Casket nods to greet you.
She sits in a relaxed posture in the interrogation chair, gently gazing at you as though she is the one in control of the interrogation room.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: You're here.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: What do you seek from me this time?
Oak Casket's tone is calm and unperturbed, yet you can feel a sense of distance.
Your support, or something along the lines.

You gently flip open the folder, revealing several pictures of the ruined Romanesque Hall after the explosion of the Black Ring. You slide it forward, but Oak Casket only glances at it before returning her gaze to you.
The Rustfire crisis in West District is over now. The people of West District and the Eastside City Council hope to start the reconstruction of Syndicate as soon as possible.

We also deeply regret the severe damage the Romanesque Hall suffered during the battle, but we've already planned to repair it, and... construct a monument for those who lost their lives in the disaster.
Now, we need someone who has the required knowledge to assist us in our work.
We believe there aren't any other better candidates than you.
You thought Oak Casket would agree to repair the hall and the surrounding stelae despite her look of disdain. But to your surprise, Oak Casket voices her refusal.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Regretfully, there isn't much I can do.
But... no one knows the number of stelae in Romanesque and the list of the deceased better than you do.
If there are any procedural concerns, I will assist you.
You try to persuade her in a soft voice, but Oak Casket remains cold-faced and adamant.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: The living caused the death of the deceased, and they build the stelae and create the archives to comfort themselves.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: They believe that by doing all this, they can atone for their sins and gain the forgiveness of the deceased.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Then they can bid the past farewell and continue to live in this world burden-free.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: I refuse to participate in that.
Having said that, Oak Casket leans back in the interrogation chair, signaling the end of the conversation.
You've misunderstood me.
You sigh and patiently explain to Oak Casket.
We are not doing this for our own sake, nor to comfort ourselves... but to always remember the pain inflicted by this disaster...

The Romanesque Hall preserves the dignity of the deceased after death and resolves their final regrets. It is one of the most precious places in Syndicate, and also one of the important witnesses of this disaster.
That's why we want to rebuild it.
Oak Casket's attitude softens a bit. She stops refuting you.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Yes... Where they are is the best place in the world... They are the most wonderful, peaceful, and reliable friends...

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Alive, they were the heroes of Rustfire, the refugees of the Drifter Camp, and my good neighbors. After their death...

speaker: Oak Casket
content: They returned to Romanesque. I dressed them up the best I could and listened to the words they left in the last moments of life.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Answering their murmurs, I resolved many of their regrets... but there were always some I couldn't settle...
Can you tell me more about these regrets?
Oak Casket smiles.
She lifts her finger deftly, as if some invisible souls are lingering in the blank space of the interrogation room, lamenting their regrets to her.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: They take on many forms. A child complained he had never seen his parents. A man couldn't get over his hatred for the gang who murdered his family. An old woman said she hadn't had one good thing in life and that her life was pointless...
Is this related to that unresolvable regret?
Or... is this one of the reasons you refuse to help us?
In the silence, you can hardly hear her breathing.
After a while, she bends down slightly, leaning in closer, her unevenly colored eyes eerie in the dimness.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Answer me...
Her voice is icy, like a question from the dead.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Do you believe that... the future is always hopeful?
I believe in hope, just like I believe you're trying to help those who have lost hope.
You hold her gaze and tell her your choice.
Oak Casket sighs deeply, leaning back in the chair.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: You're stubborn, aren't you?

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Then let me tell you a story.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Have you heard this story about a falcon and three pockets before?
No.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: This is a story told to me by a priest a long time ago. I've heard it dates back to before Nightfall.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: When people first came to this world, the golden falcon opened the way for them and gave them three pockets: One filled with wealth, one with power, and one with hope.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: The falcon told them the pocket of wealth could be found where merchants gathered and the pocket of power could be found in war.
I guess the pocket of hope was the hardest to find.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: You're always smart at times like this.
Oak Casket smiles and continues while gazing at you.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: It's a pity that the priest... died before he finished telling this story.
Is that priest the one whose regret you couldn't resolve?
Oak Casket doesn't answer your question. Instead, she starts reciting that strange poem softly into the darkness.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: You shall endure hardships and surpass all stelae in this world...

speaker: Oak Casket
content: You shall meet the golden falcon, and the winged traveler will guide you...
She mutters emotionlessly, sounding more like she's mocking the poem than praying.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Those who have lost hope... can't even resolve their regrets.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Chief, where do you think we can find the pocket of hope?

options: I may not find it now.

content: I once found the pocket of hope with my own hands.
Perhaps the pockets of hope have become scarce in our world now, so much so that the regrets and the deceased you've ever encountered have never seen hope.
But the world has already started to change.
One day, the pocket of hope will appear before everyone's eyes.
Perhaps the pocket of hope doesn't exist in our world now.
But there are always people resisting this terrible world, striving to bring the pocket of hope back to this world.
Maybe we're indeed the unlucky ones. Maybe the world after Nightfall is just so terrible that hope no longer exists naturally.
But as long as we persist, one day, the pocket of hope will appear before everyone's eyes.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Do you think it is something that everyone can have?
Oak Casket is watching you, her eyes gleaming with interest.
Yes, as long as they're willing to persist.
I've been through countless hopeless situations... Yet I'm still standing here, instead of lying beneath a gravestone in Romanesque.
I believe that as long as you face it, one day you'll find a way to resolve even that unresolvable regret.
Oak Casket remains silent.
But from the other end of the shackles, you feel a tiny ripple of Mania.
It's impossible to fully convince her of a hopeful future within such a short conversation. But you want to at least show her the possibilities.
I have a suggestion, Oak Casket.
You take the spread-out file, remove the photos on it and put them in your pocket, then draft an application on the paper.
If I can't persuade you from the living's perspective, then we'll let the dead decide.
For the first time, some semblance of surprise emerges on Oak Casket's expressionless face.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Let the dead decide? How are you going to conduct this judgment when you can't even communicate with them?
I will sign a document permitting your return to the Drifter Camp for the reconstruction of Romanesque's stele garden. And I'll accompany you as your supervisor.
We'll resolve that regret together.
Upon hearing your proposal, her mismatched eyes radiate an almost hysterical brilliance.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: ...You're very bold, Chief.
You haven't seen her like this in a long time. The messenger of the dead who mocks the living recklessly.
If the dead approve of me... I hope you will too, and cooperate with us to rebuild West District.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Haha... After peeking into death, are you reaching to the message between life and death now too?
She looks at the application you handed over, a neat signature already printed after the supervisor's name. Oak Casket picks up the pen on the desk and signs her own name.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Very well, I accept your proposal.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: I will do my best to assist you, but you must touch the gravestones of Romanesque and listen to the whispers of the dead, and you can't leave even if it becomes too much for your mind to bear.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Don't disappoint me.
As you exit the interrogation room, Oak Casket looks much more pleased than before.
You complete the application as quickly as possible, but Nightingale is still concerned.
You reassure her that Oak Casket has helped you many times before and that she'll do the same this time. Finally, Nightingale relents.
Romanesque Hall

The stele garden now looks starkly different than it did when you first came here. Most of the stelae have collapsed, and the white marble blocks scatter among the weeds. Some graves have cracked, revealing the coffins.
When you walk into the stele garden, a crow flutters its wings and flies away from a stele. You notice a bunch of black vines climbing on the stele, with a small yellow flower blooming on it.
What kind of flower is that?
Seeing the flower, Oak Casket's gaze sharpens. She squats down next to the vines and gently caresses the small flower.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Raven
You listen carefully, but the stele garden is like a frozen space, without even a whisper of wind.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: This is an oak flower. Or rather, an oak flower that's been branded.
But these vines are not even branches of an oak.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: This is the branding effect. These vines grew from an oak coffin, so its flower is a duplicate of an oak flower. The person buried under this stele was a gardener who was fond of plants.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: There is an oak tree behind the stele garden. Half of it was blown away by the explosion of the monastery, but it still survived.
Because of this gardener?

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Yes, he cared for every plant within his sight and dreamed of living in a forest, even though he never saw a real forest in his life.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Before his death, he asked me not to use dried wood for his coffin. He wished to become one with these plants.
Did he die in this war as well?

speaker: Oak Casket
content: No... much earlier than that.
Oak Casket smiles gently.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: He died in a gang fight.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: He was the monastery's gardener. The monastery had some peaceful days until a gang threatened them and made the place their hideout for some big shot.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Soon, the fact that the big shot was hiding in the monastery was discovered. Other gangs besieged the monastery, and many people died in that siege.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: At that time... when I returned to the monastery... he was on his deathbed.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: He was the first person I laid to rest.
Did he leave behind any regrets?

speaker: Oak Casket
content: He was worried about that oak tree behind the monastery.
As dusk falls, you look toward the back of the stele garden in the twilight. There is nothing there, only vast and empty darkness in the distance.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: It didn't survive the last war. But I kept part of it.
Oak Casket spreads her hand to reveal an acorn in her palm. She places the acorn next to the small flower, watching it.
You walk along the path of the stele garden, fixing the damaged tombstones along the way. Oak Casket seems to remember every tombstone owner and the locations of all tombstones and coffins.
A nearly worn-out hat sits on a tombstone. Oak Casket gently removes the hat and starts mending it.
Is this hat yours?

speaker: Oak Casket
content: No, it belonged to a little girl named Nasha. The one buried here was her best friend. That child was sickly her whole life. Nasha probably worried that she would catch a cold from the wind and rain here.
...Did the child die of illness?
Oak Casket shakes her head slightly.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: The gang took her away. Two days after they brought her back, her mother found her in a reaction pool at the Drifter Camp. I made her a wig and a mask so that she could look like herself in departure.
Her gentle, sad gaze falls on the tombstone again, where the little girl's name is engraved, but the name has long since faded.
...What about Nasha? Hasn't she come to replace this hat? It looks... quite old.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: She can't come anymore.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: That's her tombstone.
Following Oak Casket's gaze, you see another newer tombstone behind the hat bearing Nasha's name and date of death.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: A conflict broke out when the Executive Committee came to clear the Mania contamination. An incendiary bomb hit her room.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: The fire burned for three hours before it was extinguished. Nasha's family asked me to help find the remains in the ruins. When I got there, there was nothing but charred debris and ashes from the fire.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: The fire swallowed the residential building. I heard cries from both adults and children. The firefighters were stuck outside the block. By the time they got in, the flames had reached the roof.
You can almost visualize the fire from Oak Casket's description. The sky is dyed red. The flames blend into the sunset, like a flock of bright red sparrows struggling to escape.

Not far from Nasha's tombstone, there is a cluster of dilapidated stelae. You stop there and find that the greater part of the nearest tombstone has been blasted away, leaving only a small broken stub. The ground has also been damaged, revealing half a medicine bottle shallowly buried in the soil.
Half of the glass bottle is shattered, spilling shiny buttons and broken glass bits all over the ground.
What is this?

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Stars.
You remain silent, quietly waiting for Oak Casket's elaboration.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: His name was Humar. He was bullied from a young age for having white hair and skin. His mother gave birth to him in a basement and he was kept away from sunlight for many years.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: People told him that his mother went where the stars were, so he started collecting these stars. Later, someone told him that the Drifter Camp was in a high and starry place and that when the night was clear, you could even touch them, so he came. Only eight years old, he came carrying his only belongings.
She picks up the bottle and carefully puts the buttons back into the remaining half of the bottle.
There are so many buttons. He must have spent a long time collecting them.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: I collected some for him, but he didn't want them. He only kept the ones he collected himself.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: I still remember his expression at that time. He liked those buttons but couldn't accept them... His eyes were wide open. It was quite amusing.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: He asked me where I got so many stars, so I took him where I found the buttons. The morgue in the monastery.
Then what happened next?

speaker: Oak Casket
content: After that, he became my playmate.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: When I was a child, I often went to the morgue by myself. It was the quietest place in the monastery. I brought him to the room, thinking it would scare him...

speaker: Oak Casket
content: But he was just envious of me, for I could have such a big room all to myself... Oh dear.
Oak Casket lets out a soft gasp. You step forward to help steady the glass bottle, catching the stars almost spilling out.
Oak Casket's gaze travels from the glass bottle to you. The light from the bottle is reflected in her pupils, warming up her gaze as she looks at you.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: One night, he appeared in the morgue again, but this time... he was unrecognizable.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: He was tricked into climbing a high-rise building in Syndicate to pick stars, and ended up falling.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: His final regret was only a bottle full of buttons.
Oak Casket rises and walks into the cluster of broken stelae.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Most of the people buried around here were from the monastery... These people fell into eternal slumber because of the living.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: You see, the dead won't hurt you, only the living will.
Her tone is calm, as if she's merely stating an objective fact.

You want to object and tell her that's not true, that there are many trustworthy and good people among the living. But perhaps because the wind in the graveyard is too quiet, somehow you can't bring yourself to speak.
The two of you proceed in silence for a while until Oak Casket stops in front of a somewhat weathered tombstone. She stares at the stele for a long time without saying a word.
Whose tombstone is this?

speaker: Oak Casket
content: I don't know.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: But what remains here... is the regret I cannot resolve.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: I've resolved the regrets of the dead from all walks of life. Those who passed away in accidents, those who chose to go because they couldn't see hope...

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Yet I've never truly understood the message the person lying beneath this tombstone has left me.
You reach out your hand toward Oak Casket.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: I'm afraid it's difficult. She didn't leave much information.
Oak Casket is much gentler in the Romanesque Hall than in the interrogation room.
Give it a try.
This time there are two of us. We should be able to hear more.
She looks into your eyes, as if she's glimpsing through something you don't know. In the end, she takes off her gloves and covers your eyes.
The chill of Oak Casket's palms still remains over your eyes. Your vision is blank.
Gradually, a warm light arises, dispelling the chill in your eyes.
You find yourself in a meadow under the warm sunlight. It's a beautiful sunny day.
Perhaps because the tombstone has stood there for too long, you can't make out clearly what you're seeing. You can only vaguely see a girl reciting something under a tree.
Her voice is so soft that you can't hear what she's reciting. You turn to look at Oak Casket, who's also straining her ears to listen.
What is she reciting?
Oak Casket doesn't respond.
Meanwhile, the figure of an adult approaches and joins the girl in her recitation.
Like a melody, the peaceful and warm voice floats in the air with the sunlight. The light about the girl grows brighter and brighter.
Hardships... Traveler... Light...
These words somehow ring a bell.
Wanting to hear more clearly, you strain to step forward, but end up stepping into a sea of white light.
The two of you have returned to the stele.
The link of the shackles still remains, so you feel the repressed emotion from Oak Casket almost as soon as you come back.
Why? The sun was so warm and mellow.
Did you just see the same things as you had previously?
Before we came, we made an agreement that you would do your best to assist me.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: ...This time, I could hear her recitation.
You sense the emotion coming from the shackles, guiding Oak Casket.
The poem she recited... I only heard a few words, but I'm certain I've heard it somewhere before.
Do you remember?
Oak Casket falls silent again, but through the shackles, you can feel what she's feeling... Something like contempt or anger... Or perhaps... sadness.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Such a foolish and despicable poem...

speaker: Oak Casket
content: I've forgotten about it.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Do I need to recall it, Chief?
Her tone is somewhat harsh, but you feel that her sadness outweighs her anger.
You don't want her to be stuck in this kind of pain, so you shake your head slightly.
You stand next to Oak Casket for a while until the emotion on the other end of the shackles subsides.
You said that everyone sleeping here was connected to the monastery.
Are there any other people from the monastery still alive? Or people related to the monastery. They may know something.
...If remembering will cause you pain, then let me find these answers.
After a moment of silence, Oak Casket finally answers you.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: There's a doctor who's closely related to the monastery... but I'm not sure if he's still alive.
It's okay. Let's try to find him.
Before leaving the stele garden, you look back. The land where the oak tree once grew is empty.
There's still not a breath of wind in the stele garden. The tombstones are gray, just as those stars sealed in the glass jar are.
The journey isn't peaceful. You pass collapsed houses and ruins while Oak Casket remains unusually silent. The only thing that alleviates your unease is the faint, unique fragrance on her.

You keep wondering what the little girl was reciting, and what the light represents. The recitation sounded like a prayer from someone from the monastery, but Oak Casket's unusual reaction tells you that this is no simple prayer.
Thinking this, you look at Oak Casket walking ahead of you.
She seems to never want to stop for the scenery around her, yet she's the messenger who always stops and turns back to listen to those who can't go on.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: What's the matter?
Noticing that you haven't kept up, Oak Casket turns around and asks simply.
Nothing... I'm just a little surprised by the lack of signs of habitation here.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: This place...
Oak Casket looks at the flat land around her with a calm expression that doesn't give away any emotions.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: It's because this place is a mass grave.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Initially, stray dogs would forage around here in packs. No one wanted to be near here.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Later, to curb Mania, this place was hastily buried and covered up. But even though the smell was gone, most people still avoided this area. Only until recently... After the war ended, people began to remember this place after Romanesque's been destroyed.
Only then do you see some recent mounds on the land originally covered with weeds. Not far away, someone is erecting a plank of wood in front of a mound as a makeshift gravestone.
As the man plants the plank into the earth, he keeps muttering something, his voice drifting in the air along with the flickering phosphorescence.
You shall endure hardships... Meet the golden falcon... Traveler will guide you to the light...
You finally understand why those words in the vision sounded so familiar.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Perhaps you have.
You were reciting it when I entered the interrogation room.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: You shall endure hardships and surpass all stelae in this world... You shall meet the golden falcon, and the winged traveler will guide you to the light...

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Now you want to ask: Where did you learn about this poem?

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Well... This is an elegy that reminds the dead to let go of all suffering and prays that they can travel to the beautiful and peaceful land of eternity.
Have you heard someone recite it?

speaker: Oak Casket
content: More precisely, someone recited it for me.
But you just said this is an elegy for the dead...
Before entering the interrogation room, you looked over the investigation report on Oak Casket.

She was born during Syndicate's most chaotic period. Orphaned since a young age, she was adopted by a priest from the monastery. When she was about thirteen, the monastery was destroyed in a gang fight, and the priest died that year.
Ever since then, the teenage girl has disappeared from the official records.
How many deaths and departures must she have witnessed over all these years to become what she is now?

speaker: Oak Casket
content: You're looking very earnest now. Are you that eager to delve into my past?
As the Chief of the Bureau, and as your friend, I want to know.
Oak Casket gives a slight smile, but it doesn't melt the frosty chill on her face.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Very well... I'm looking forward to your response to this story, little one.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: It took place when this mass grave hadn't been covered up yet.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: At that time, I was one of the hundreds of corpses in the pit. But I was not dead. I was thrown in alive.
The smell of blood stung her nose. The little girl struggled to open her eyes.
So stinky. So disgusting. I want to get out of this place.
But she couldn't move. Rigid bodies were lying on top of her limbs, belly, and shoulders. The body she was leaning against was also slowly turning cold.
She finally realized what was happening. She looked up and saw the gray sky several meters above.
The gravely injured girl was lying at the bottom of the pit helplessly.

speaker: Little Girl
content: I'm still alive...
Weak and with her throat parched, she could only make a faint noise.

speaker: Little Girl
content: Please... Help me...
Soon after, footsteps came from above the pit.
Two figures stood at the edge of the pit and noticed the little girl at the bottom with her eyes open.

speaker: Little Girl
content: Father... Doctor...

speaker: Little Girl
content: Help me... Help me, please...
They seemed to be muttering something. A moment later, another body was thrown down.

speaker: Old Priest & Doctor
content: You shall endure hardships and surpass all stelae in this world. You shall meet the golden falcon, and the winged traveler will guide you to the light...
Hearing the words, she watched more and more bodies being thrown into the pit. Dirt was being shoveled onto her head, covering her view.

speaker: Little Girl
content: You shall meet the golden falcon, and the winged traveler will guide you to the light.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: What's the point? He told me to seek the light when he cast me into the dark.
Oak Casket recalls placidly, her voice gradually merging with the little girl's in the vision. A rough guess arises in your mind.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: The living believe their prayers can cleanse the souls of the dead, helping them find relief. They cover up their sins with such grandiose rhetoric, as if they can earn forgiveness from the dead just like that.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: This poem won't bring light. It's just an excuse for the living to absolve themselves and alleviate their guilt.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Once they finish reciting the poem, the death of the deceased has nothing to do with the living anymore.
Oak Casket looks at you composedly.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Alright, little one, you got your story...

speaker: Oak Casket
content: In return, can you give me a guiding answer?
You can't find the strength or words to argue with her anymore. After all, what words carry enough weight to comfort who was once discarded by the living?
Oak Casket shrugs. Without taking one last glimpse at this land, she walks straight ahead.
You remain silent all the way, following Oak Casket to an old residential building.
The building is on the verge of collapse, the exterior wrapped in a mess of electrical cables. You climb the narrow staircase to the first floor and knock on the door, but no one answers.
Are you sure this is the place?

speaker: Oak Casket
content: I can't be mistaken.

Oak Casket produces a thin slice of metal out of nowhere and slides it through the door gap effortlessly, like performing surgery. When the door opens, the entire frame shakes like it may collapse at any moment.

As soon as the door opens, a stench hits you. Several rats squeal and scurry past you. The living room is filled with all sorts of garbage, from which a bunch of flies take off and try to land on you.

You walk through a dark corridor. The light should be on, as you can hear the hum of electricity in the light bulb, but it's not lit. Perhaps it's stayed on for too long. The faucet is stuck with rust, and occasionally you can hear water dripping.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Hmm, he's still alive.
What?
Oak Casket draws the curtains of the room open. With the faint morning light filtering in through the window, you see a person lying on the bed.

Half of the body is shriveled up under a faded old quilt, revealing only a dried and wrinkled face and sparse white hair. If it weren't for his breathing, you'd almost mistake it for a dried-up skeleton.
Is this the doctor?
Oak Casket doesn't speak and simply nods. Her expression remains indifferent. You can't tell what she thinks of this situation.
You lean in toward the doctor, trying to wake him up.
Excuse me, Sir.
The doctor doesn't move. You smell the stench of bedsores. He must have been paralyzed for quite some time, and with no one taking care of him, his bed reeks of excrement.
Is this... nutritional fluid?
You see a half-used bottle of liquid lying on the bedside table, guessing it might be what's keeping him alive.
He's neither dead nor alive, cut off from all possibilities of communication.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: What a shame. He's worthless in his state.
...What?

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Isn't he? In his current state, he can't even speak clearly.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: But if he died, we could at least learn something from him through my ability.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: The dead are honest while the living are furtive. The dead are tranquil while the living are restless. The dead are eternally peaceful and loyal; as the root of all evil, the living create nothing but chaos.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: You see, I like the dead a little more than the living.
Oak Casket's eyes somewhat soften as she says this.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Given his condition, only death can grant him relief.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: What's the point of clinging to life in such a body in this world? The living don't need him, but the dead would surely welcome a new friend breaking free from worldly ties.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Let's send him off.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: He'll like it.
Oak Casket's words give you chills, and you finally regain your composure.
Whether someone should live or die, that's not your decision to make.
If death was indeed a form of relief, then you wouldn't know so many lingering regrets from the dead.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: That's because they didn't know the beauty of death when they were still alive.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Compared to living such a life in such a world, death is the true salvation.

options: Compared to life, death is a simpler choice.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Perhaps you have.
But not everyone wants to be saved by death.
Just as you said, living such a life in such a world... is a much harder and painful choice than death.
But he's still chosen to live.
If a person truly wants to die, he will let you know at the necessary moment.
This is also... my response to your past.
Oak Casket stares at you for a moment, then suddenly walks over to the doctor, and pulls something out of her pocket.
Startled, you want to stop her, but then realize that Oak Casket has only pulled out a handkerchief to wipe the grime off the doctor's face.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: If you have something to say, now's the time.
But the doctor only opens his mouth and breathes laboriously.
You have no choice but to search around the small living room, trying to find some other clues. But all you can find are a few books and a notebook in the plainly furnished room.
Oak Casket just stands by the door, waiting pensively.
Before leaving, you change the doctor's nutritional fluid and clean up his bed. Suddenly, you notice that his eyes are open. He's staring intently at Oak Casket's back, his mouth moving.
You lean in and hear him mutter a word.

speaker: Doctor
content: ...Light.

speaker: Chief
content: What light?
The old doctor doesn't answer, as if uttering that word has taken all his strength. He closes his eyes again.
You catch up with Oak Casket, who seems to be avoiding something. You can barely keep up with her.
You have many questions, but at least one thing is certain: That incomprehensible regret on that stele has something to do with Oak Casket.
By the time you return to the stele garden, the day is already bright.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: I've decided to terminate this collaboration.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: I'm not yet skillful enough to interpret a regret from that long ago. Perhaps letting it go would be best for all of us.
She looks at the old site of the mass grave not far away, which has long since been covered up. Oak Casket's gaze looks as if she's staring into an abyss.
You flip through the doctor's journal, a thin volume that's somewhat old. Luckily, it contains the information you're looking for.
It is what Oak Casket has missed over the years, what she still needs to see now.
...You told me about the legend of the falcon before, but you didn't finish.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: You turn out to be quite a talker, you know.
The pocket of wealth is found where merchants gathered and the pocket of power is found in war...
The pocket of hope lies in utter pain.
Because hope is most elusive to the living. It hides in the places the living are least likely to go near.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: You sure have many original ideas.
That stele... is related to you, isn't it?
Oak Casket says nothing and falls silent.
That stele's regret is all blurry now, but it has persisted for so long. I can only imagine how intense it originally was.
Why can't we persist a little longer for him too? Give it another try?
Isn't it your wish that all the deceased ones can leave this world without any regrets?
You spread the notes you found at the doctor's apartment and lay them out in front of the tombstone.
The handwriting on the notes has faded, some of the ink smudged due to moisture. Only the word light is still clear, as if someone has retraced it carefully.
You respect our contract. Our agreement hasn't reached an end yet.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: This is why I hate dealing with the living.
Oak Casket stands there quietly. Though a little hesitant, she doesn't stop you from getting near her.
You reach out to her slender body as cold as her words. You cover her eyes.
Incessant whispers echo in your ears, clinging to your nerves, bringing you pain.
Oak Casket seems to want to pull your hand away, but you hold hers instead.
It's okay, Oak Casket, I'm not afraid.
You hold her hand firmly until the temperatures of both hands gradually even out, becoming equally warm.
You begin to recognize the voices in your ears. Two old voices.

The moment you recognize them, the power of the shackles becomes more intense than ever, and your vision has never been more clear. There is light in front of you, and it keeps brightening until you can see everything clearly.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: Why is light always granted to those with an uneasy journey? Why is life always granted to those with a bitter soul...
Oak Casket's voice trembles slightly.
The moon shines upon the stele. The little girl sits under the wooden board, reciting the poem she's copied by the moonlight.
When she looks up at the person approaching her, you finally make out her face. It's a young Oak Casket.

speaker: Old Priest
content: What are you doing here, Nona?

speaker: Young Oak Casket
content: I'm reading the poem you taught me today, Father. But there are many words I don't know.

speaker: Old Priest
content: Let me see.

speaker: Old Priest
content: The golden falcon... Oh, that bird is the sun's companion. Do you remember that funerals are usually held before dawn?

speaker: Young Oak Casket
content: I remember.

speaker: Old Priest
content: The dead live in a different world than the living. But when the falcon arrives, it means the sun is rising.

speaker: Old Priest
content: Let's read it together.

speaker: Old Priest & Young Oak Casket
content: The wanderer in the wilderness no longer carried the burden of the past. The golden falcon asked her: Where came you? She said: I do not recall the way I came. Dawn is near, as is the end of everything.

You see the light getting brighter. In that white light, a younger doctor appears, along with some people from the monastery. They gather around the young Oak Casket, reciting the unfinished poem together, as if completing a devout worship.

speaker: Crowd
content: You shall endure hardships and surpass all stelae in this world. You shall meet the golden falcon, and the winged traveler will guide you to the light. Where there is light, there you shall be.
The pages turn. The fire colors the full moon red.
The gangsters' roars and gunfire end the quiet world.

speaker: Doctor
content: Father, Nona is not dead. There's still hope for her...

speaker: Old Priest
content: Her injuries are grave. With our current supplies and equipment, we can't save her...

speaker: Doctor
content: But she's not dead yet! She's looking at us from the bottom of the pit! Maybe she can survive this...

speaker: Old Priest
content: Those scoundrels are coming soon! They've finally found an excuse to attack the monastery, and they will surely take Nona away, dead or alive! Don't you know what they're going to do to her?!

speaker: Old Priest
content: Instead of being infected with Mania in those experiments... it's better... to surrender her to hope...

speaker: Old Priest
content: The blessing has long abandoned us... but still, I wish... she could see hope... see the light...
The pages turn again.
The doctor sat in front of the stele, which looked less dilapidated than it is now.

speaker: Doctor
content: Nona... Father... did you meet again in the afterlife?

speaker: Doctor
content: Give him a beating. Stay mad at him. He was still repenting to you until his last breath.
The doctor seemed to be remembering something, his eyes reddening again. Finally, he sighed.

speaker: Doctor
content: I'm the only one left in the monastery. I'll come to pray for you both often, until the day I can't anymore.

speaker: Doctor
content: You must go where there is light.

speaker: Doctor
content: You shall endure hardships and surpass all stelae in this world. You shall meet the golden falcon, and the winged traveler will guide you to the light. Where there is light, there you shall be.
Countless praying rituals flash before your eyes. The young doctor turns into a middle-aged one, then into an old man. In the end, only the unvisited grave is left.
As all the chants blend into a unison, the regrets intensify, until the vast light reaches its limit.
Slowly, the light goes out.
You remove your hands covering Oak Casket's eyes.
Nona.
Oak Casket nods. There is a gleam of resignation and indulgence in her eyes.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: This was the name the priest gave me, as I was adopted on the ninth day of that month. But Nona is dead.
Her hand gently traces the inscriptions on the stele. You can now vaguely make out a number that had been scratched out. It's the number nine.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: You guessed right. This is Nona's stele.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: I suppose this is the cenotaph they erected for me after they threw me into that mass grave.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: I used to think... that this cenotaph was like an elegy they recited for me... that it was nothing more than an excuse to absolve them of their guilt...
No, they...
Oak Casket interrupts you.

speaker: Oak Casket
content: I'll settle this once and for all.

speaker: Oak Casket
