<color=#fb9259>Anon</color>: I'm only interested in that Chief because I heard she's an expert in the field of Mania. I have no other intentions.

<color=#fb9259>Anon</color>: The Ring Research Institute is hard enough to get into, and coming from a satellite town means I practically have no chance. But even so, I don't want to give up... Finding ways to defend against disasters is a topic that concerns every researcher.

<color=#fb9259>Anon</color>: Please rest assured, I'll keep any information about her confidential, and I promise I won't do anything that could harm her in any way.

content: On the screen, the stilted explanations continue popping up, each line bearing an excessive seriousness. You stare at the words, the corners of your mouth tightening slightly.
They seem quite... stubborn. It's hard to tell whether this is naive single-mindedness or a calculated facade.
Suddenly, a notification flashes at the top of the chat window. The next moment, you see they've disabled their anonymity setting.
A strange profile picture appears, and a new username catches your eye.
Archivist 19260817
You catch yourself holding your breath. Dropping anonymity voluntarily? Do they truly mean to get candid, or do they have an ulterior motive?
Regardless, this unexpected act of frankness still causes a slight tremor in your otherwise guarded composure.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: I believe you. But if you're so interested, why not contact the MBCC and try to schedule a meeting with Chief in person?

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: ...Maybe someday.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: I'll try when I'm truly ready.
You stare at the brief reply, your expression darkening slightly.

Just as the 9th Agency reported, they're extremely cautious. They clearly take an interest in "Chief," yet the moment you suggested a meeting in person, they immediately retreated behind their defenses.
But on the other hand, you don't think they're particularly calculating either, like right now...

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: Alright, then just join Chief's fan club for now. It's the fastest way to get the latest updates about Chief.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Is that so?

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Okay. How do I join?
Hook, line, and sinker. They even meticulously arrange ways to stay in regular contact with you, and decide on a "secret code."
Even the 9th Agency agent silently observing nearby can no longer suppress a smile.

speaker: 9th Agency
content: At the 9th Agency, such amateur tradecraft could get an agent sent back to the academy by the superiors.
You merely raise an eyebrow without responding, your gaze fixed on the now-silent chat window on the screen.
That marks the end of the first exchange. It went smoothly, yet it feels like you've merely lifted the corner of an unknown curtain, revealing even more elusive shadows behind it.
Who exactly is this mysterious <color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>? Are they really a cautious, budding independent scientist? Or is it all a carefully crafted facade?
And why are they so eager to collect information about Black Rings, Mania, and you?

speaker: You
content: Keep this account active and continue monitoring.
This chess match is far from over. To unravel these mysteries, you need to maintain contact with them and find the answers through careful probing.
Early February, N.F. 114
After that, things keep going surprisingly smoothly.

Due to security concerns and to keep your cover identity as the "fan club president," you can't discuss sensitive technical subjects with "Archivist 19260817," yet your communication has continued constantly.
Rather than research topics, they seem more interested in DisCity lore, and are especially fascinated by stories of Chief's adventures.

When they ask about Chief's recent activities, you cherry-pick a few headline stories and attach some blurry "snapshots." When they're curious about Chief's past, you share some half-true media stories to satisfy their curiosity.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: I heard Chief personally interrogates Sinners? Is that true?

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: More or less.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Is he really as... invincible as the rumors say? Is he really that resourceful?
female_content:
<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: I heard Chief personally interrogates Sinners? Is that true?

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: More or less.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Is she really as... invincible as the rumors say? Is she really that resourceful?

content: You give an affirmative answer and also helpfully make up quite a few details as evidence. Watching the "typing..." notification flash repeatedly above the chat box with no new text appearing, you can't help but laugh out loud.
You can almost picture them on the other side of the screen, eyebrows furrowed in disbelief, fingers hovering hesitantly over the keyboard before finally cautiously typing out a response.
Gradually, your conversations extend beyond discussions of Chief and research, as Archivist begins voluntarily sharing tiny details of their daily life.

For instance, when equipment readings suddenly spiked during an experiment last month, Archivist got so excited thinking they'd made a breakthrough that they even drafted an outline for a paper. But moments later, they discovered it was only caused by a loose connection.
And two weeks ago, they spent forty-eight hours in the lab trying to verify a hypothesis. Having forgotten to eat, they ended up fainting from low blood sugar.

Mysterious tiny paw prints on lab reports, new buds sprouting on the windowsill, a sudden rush of inspiration... whether it's moments of happiness or frustration, or even just some insignificant feelings, you seem to be the first person they talk to when something happens.
Before you realize it, you've come to know many things they like.
You know that when they leave the lab, they prefer to eat alone at a café on the street corner.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Whenever I'm done with the experiment, I go there and sit for a while. From that corner seat, I can watch the sunset through the window. It's like a burning, orange ball of fire. It's beautiful.
You know that in their spare time, they like to reorganize all their documents and books in the most practical order.
<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Today I reorganized all my documents again. After sorting them by category, they're much easier to find now.
You know they love the aroma of freshly brewed herbal tea. They say the rising steam makes them think of flower fields in spring.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: I always brew a cup of herbal tea when I'm doing my reading. The aroma helps me concentrate.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: I've never actually seen a real flower field, but I imagine it must be as dewy and vibrant as the steamy, freshly brewed herbal tea.
Then a few days ago, they suddenly sent you a photo.

It's a small white flower defiantly emerging from a crevice in the rock. A slender finger gently caresses the blossom, its delicate petals unfurling in the desolate crack, looking so lonely yet remarkably resilient.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Remember the herbal tea I told you about? This is what it's made from.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Someone suggested picking it to make tea, but after thinking about it, I refused.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Blooming from a rock is way cooler than becoming a cup of tea, don't you think?

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: You're always sharing photos with me, so I thought I'd send one to you today.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: I hope it cheers you up a little.
That day, when you drag your exhausted body back to the Bureau after finishing a field assignment, the moon is already high in the night sky.
You rest on the couch for a moment, then pull your device from your pocket and log onto the dark web as usual. You find an unread message in your inbox.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: I heard Chief has been out on missions lately?

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: Yeah. I went along too. Could barely keep up.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: Haven't received many messages from you these past couple of days. Have you been busy as well?
You've just set down your device to get ready for bed when the screen lights up again, the reply popping up almost instantly.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Recently... there have been some changes to my research project, requiring more of my attention. I'm managing well enough.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: What about you? Have you been out taking photos again?

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: Something like that. Though things were so chaotic today I nearly took a fall and almost smashed my camera.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: No way?! That sounds dangerous! Are you alright? You're not hurt, are you?

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: Don't worry, I'm fine. All the photos are saved. I'll pick out some good ones, touch them up a bit, and pack them into a zip file.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Pack them?

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Like when I group my experimental records?
These weird comparisons always put a smile on your face. Archivist is such a nerd, but inexplicably, that's kind of cute.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: Yes, think of it as some kind of research record.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: Just like you said, categorizing and organizing them makes everything easier to find later.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: I see, that's an interesting way to put it.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: ...If I ever get the chance, I'd like to visit DisCity myself. To see where you live, and all those scenic spots you've mentioned.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Perhaps... I might even have the opportunity to meet that legendary Chief, together with you.
The yearning in their words reaches you through the cold screen, and you can clearly feel the sincerity behind.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: In that case, I sincerely extend an invitation to you. You have the welcome of DisCity and the MBCC.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Are you speaking on behalf of Chief's fan club?
You smile and gently type out a reply.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: On behalf of the fan club, but also myself.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: You're welcome in DisCity. Once your project wraps up, I'll throw a celebration party for you.

They quickly respond with a smiling emoji and say nothing more. As the chat falls still, you lean back against the couch and swipe your fingertips across the screen, switching to another conversation.
<color=#fb9259>9th</color>: Chief, the tracking report from the tech department is ready.

<color=#fb9259>${PlayerName}</color>: Any findings?

<color=#fb9259>9th</color>: The signal source has been located on the outskirts of DisCity, in a small satellite town. It's primarily an agricultural production area with almost no unusual activities.

<color=#fb9259>${PlayerName}</color>: ...Understood. Continue monitoring.
You stare at the report from the 9th Agency. Everything appears harmless. Nothing is out of the ordinary. It's almost surprising, and it raises your suspicions.
From your interactions so far, you've already formed a mental image of this mysterious "independent scientist."

<size=50>A young girl</size> under twenty years old　　<size=40>Perhaps just of age?</size>
　　　　　<size=50>Privileged background</size>　Have received top education
　　　　　　　　　　　Intelligent　Almost a <size=50>genius</size>
　　　　　　　　Small social circle　　Seems to have <size=50>few friends</size>
　　　　　　　　<size=50>Research scholar</size>　Passionate about her work
　　　　　　　　　　　<size=40>Inexperienced</size>　　<size=40>Immature</size>　　<size=40>Just starting out</size>
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　...
　　　　　　　　　　　　　Independent?　　<size=50>Lonely?</size>
You stare blankly at the screen until it goes dark, then instinctively tap to wake it.

"Archivist 19260817" seems to be nothing more than an ordinary girl sitting before a screen, playfully joking with you, the two of you separated by thousands of kilometers yet connected by data between two worlds.
She still skitters around certain topics. She's never revealed her location or the specifics of her research, yet she is eager to share anything outside of these subjects.
Those restrained, polite texts are like a cautiously extended hand—yearning for connection and conversation, yet hesitant of complete honesty. Is this truly a trap, or perhaps...
...you're lonely enough to entrust all your thoughts and feelings to a stranger on the dark web?
A message notification interrupts your thoughts. A long block of text suddenly appears in the chat window.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Have you...

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Have you ever considered that maybe... you could distance yourself a bit from him, from ${PlayerName}?
female_content:
<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Have you...

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Have you ever considered that maybe... you could distance yourself a bit from her, from ${PlayerName}?

content:
<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Don't get me wrong! I'm not trying to speak ill of Chief. It's just that you're always chasing after him. It must be exhausting for you too.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: I just want you to be more mindful of your own safety.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: He's always risking his life in the most dangerous places, resolving those terrifying crises. But you're just an ordinary person... I don't want you to get caught in the crossfire and get hurt.
female_content:
<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Don't get me wrong! I'm not trying to speak ill of Chief. It's just that you're always chasing after her. It must be exhausting for you too.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: I just want you to be more mindful of your own safety.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: She's always risking her life in the most dangerous places, resolving those terrifying crises. But you're just an ordinary person... I don't want you to get caught in the crossfire and get hurt.

content:
<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: But I also understand that all those obstacles are not a reason to give up. Just like I wouldn't give up on my experiments easily.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: So, it's okay. My experiments often go wrong too, but if you persist, you'll eventually find the problem and reach the solution...

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: ...
The "typing..." message keeps flashing at the top of the chat window, but the next message never arrives.

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: What's wrong?

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: ...Nothing.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: I've just... run into some trouble lately. Makes me wonder sometimes...

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Will I ever truly find the answer if I keep going...?
Hmm...?

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: You sound a bit sad?

<color=#fb9259>Gray</color>: Is something troubling you? If you'd like to talk about it, I'm here to listen.
A reply pops up quickly. But just as you make out the first few characters, the message is immediately deleted.

After a moment, she responds with just a brief "thank you," then subtly changes the subject. You don't press further, simply following along with some trivial updates. When it's finally late enough into the night, you say "good night" to each other.

You set down your device and finish your nighttime routine. Then you return to your room, turn off the lights, and lie down in bed. The room is silent and it's all dark out. Only the sound of your own breathing fills the air.
Just as you're about to close your eyes in the darkness, the device on your bedside suddenly lights up, the cold white glow jarring in the quiet night.
It's a lengthy message. This time, she doesn't delete it.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: ...I'm sorry. You were clearly just concerned about me, yet I behaved so rudely.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: I don't know who I should share this with, or if I should share it at all... It's not about my research, but my... family.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: My family has always been strict and demanding with me. "With great ability comes great responsibility"—that's been drilled into me since childhood. My father was harsh, and my mother constantly reminded me that as the youngest child, I had to work even harder to be the best and never be outshone.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: My older siblings are all exceptional, and very... independent. They've never seemed unsure about anything. I've always wanted to prove myself too, to show everyone that I'm not just a spare.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: I tried so hard to adapt, pushed myself to my limits, but honestly... it was exhausting. I was afraid I might never measure up to my family's standards.
Her messages appear line by line with brief pauses, still somewhat cautious.

<color=#fb9259>Archivist 19260817</color>: Later, someone I deeply respected returned to my life. He told me I didn't have to follow in my siblings' footsteps, that I should pursue the research I enjoyed, as long as I believed it was meaningful.

She tried to tell them the truth, that this place was doomed, that staying meant death. But they didn't respond with anger. Instead, she received a piece of bread wrapped in rags, a crumpled wildflower from a child, and words of gratitude.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...${PlayerName}, it's been a long time.

Hypatia holds her breath, her trembling finger tapping open the long message she had missed.
Archivist 19260817, I hope this message finds you well.
You sit in the Bureau's lounge, typing out each character slowly.

You've rewritten the opening several times, yet nothing seems quite right. Your fingers hover over the delete key, tempted to erase everything and start again. In the end, you just shake your head and continue writing.

As I write this letter, DisCity is blessed with beautiful weather. Sunlight streams through my window. The warmth filters through the trees and the window frames. A gentle breeze rustles the leaves. I can hear my companions' shouts from the corridor.

　　But soon enough, those shouts will turn into laughter. They'll come bursting into my office with smiles on their faces, then drag me out to join them in whatever shenanigans they're up to.

　　How I wish you could witness this too.

　　How I wish I could be by your side.
You pause briefly. The computer screen glows faintly before you, its light reflecting on the desk and in your eyes like a thin mist, casting a looming shadow over this moment of tranquility.

Archivist 19260817, I've known for a while now. You've been hiding things from me. That's probably why you chose to keep your distance, isn't it?

　　But the truth is, we both have our secrets. I'm sorry. I've lied to you too.

　　I was never a fan of ${PlayerName}. Frankly, I don't think that pretender is as competent as the rumors say.

Lately, I find myself thinking often of my days in West District.

　　Back then, West District was a poor and nasty place. Everyone was drowning in despair. Yet they still claimed those ruins as their only home, fighting to survive amid the violence and poverty.

Bread shared over rubble, people supporting each other during war... I was constantly struck by their resilience and compassion. They weren't powerful, yet they seemed more remarkable to me than any hero.

　　But there was only so much I could do to help them.

　　Time and again, I could only watch helplessly as West District's wound festered anew, as its people struggled desperately to survive through the pain.

Your fingertips pause briefly on the keyboard as your chest tightens. You're transported back to your early days in Syndicate, when the unrest of Rustfire was rampant, and you were just a helpless outsider being swept away by the deluge of chaos.
You take a deep breath and keep typing.

Back then, I truly felt powerless. So powerless that all I could do was witness others' suffering without being able to help.

　　But I refused to give up like that.

Because I witnessed how hard they tried. I saw how, even when they had nothing, they still lit up the stoves and cared for one another.

　　That made me believe that even ordinary people, no matter how weak they are, can still do something. Hardship may not change overnight, but we're not condemned to simply accept whatever fate deals us.
You press Enter to start a new paragraph as the image of someone who left home to go on an adventure surfaces in your mind.

Like a friend of mine from the MBCC. After what happened in West District, she decided to journey to WhiteSands to train herself. She only just set out recently.

　　She told me that because she felt too weak, she wanted to find a way to become stronger.

I deeply admire her choice. It also reminds me of Chief.

　　Chief never shoulders everything alone. He has deep faith in his friends and values them above all else.

The man doesn't respond, only fixing her with a cold stare that cuts like a blade.
female_content: The woman doesn't respond, only fixing her with a cold stare that cuts like a blade.

content: The moment their eyes meet, Hypatia flinches. She feels that gaze pierce straight into the depths of her soul, tearing open every hidden sin, exposing everything.

She had secretly imagined different scenarios for their first meeting: fighting side by side against an Apostle of Ashes, or simply sitting together in a small park in DisCity, sharing the herbal tea she's brought.

She had imagined many possible encounters, but never one like this, where they are physically so close, yet somehow feel light years apart. In the less than half a meter between them stand the opposite beliefs they represent and a past they cannot erase.
...But this is exactly the judgment she deserves. Someone who has committed such a grave crime should receive no empathy.

speaker: Hypatia
content: I know I have so much I should confess. It's too late for explanations now, but... since this is just a dream, please, indulge me just once.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...I'm sorry.

speaker: Hypatia
content: I've been lying to you since the moment we met. I'm not from a satellite town, nor am I some independent scientist. Hypatia is one of the Campbells, who stand against you. I'm your enemy.

speaker: Hypatia
content: DisCity possesses the latest Mania research data. So... I secretly infiltrated the dark web, using it to get closer to you, gathering everything I could find about the MBCC's Chief, that Black Ring expert.
Her throat tightens, fingers unconsciously gripping the hem of her clothing.

speaker: Hypatia
content: I did wonder... if I should have just told you the truth from the beginning.

speaker: Hypatia
content: But I have a sister in DisCity. I knew that under these circumstances, my actions would make me a "Fraser spy," putting both you and me in danger. So... I dared not say anything or suggest a meeting, let alone come clean.
She lowers her gaze, the corners of her lips trembling slightly, as if fearful of each syllable leaving her mouth.

speaker: Hypatia
content: When I first met you, I had already arrived in Furor. It was my first time being so far from home. I was confident I could accomplish something meaningful here and prove my worth.

speaker: Hypatia
content: But Furor... the disasters in the farlands were simply too devastating.

speaker: Hypatia
content: This is a desolate place where the violent sand constantly blots out the sun. People lose their homes and lives to sandstorms and Mania mutations, perishing without a trace.

speaker: Hypatia
content: I thought if I could just gather more firsthand data, I could buy a little more time, secure a glimmer of hope for this place... but my efforts alone were too feeble. I failed again.
She never discovered that the inheritance had never been removed. It remained hidden beneath Furor all along, drawing Apostles to it.
The white light pours down from the ceiling, wavering in her increasingly tearful eyes.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...Those days when I chatted with you were the most precious memories of my entire life.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Thank you for telling me I was resilient and brave. Whenever I was about to give up, it was you who made me believe that perhaps there was still hope, that perhaps I truly could accomplish everything I wanted.

speaker: Hypatia
content: You told me not to fear or give up. You said if I must keep going, I shouldn't go alone. That I should find someone who could watch my back, and fight alongside them. You told me I would never be alone.

speaker: Hypatia
content: And in the end, I did meet someone.
Who did you meet?
The sudden voice cuts Hypatia off. Her body freezes, as if drenched in ice water, the words congealing in her throat.

speaker: Aren't you curious why the guests left Elysiland? You can see such a place with your own eyes.
content: Who did you meet? Why don't you continue?
Fear and despair intertwine in Hypatia's eyes, reflecting the man slowly rising from his seat and advancing toward her, like the approach of doomsday.
female_content: Fear and despair intertwine in Hypatia's eyes, reflecting the woman slowly rising from her seat and advancing toward her, like the approach of doomsday.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: All of this... is nothing but excuses you tell yourself.

speaker: Hypatia
content: No... no! That's not... I...

Hypatia's body involuntarily shrinks back, her hands clutching the edges of the chair tightly. She shakes her head desperately as tears begin to fall, her words as powerless as bare hands trying to hold back a storm.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: "No"? Then why come to me with this confession? You kept insisting you would bear all the risks, yet in the end, it was never you who suffered the consequences.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If someone like you deserves forgiveness, then what about Furor? What about those innocent people in the farlands? Who would speak for them, stand up for them? To Fraser, their lives don't matter, not in the slightest.
The man's shadow stretches in the light, casting an oppressive gloom over Hypatia's entire body. His gaze is calm, detached, utterly indifferent, yet more cruel than any display of rage or hatred.
female_content: The woman's shadow stretches in the light, casting an oppressive gloom over Hypatia's entire body. Her gaze is calm, detached, utterly indifferent, yet more cruel than any display of rage or hatred.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And you have the audacity to mention the messages I wrote you. I did tell you to "find someone who can watch your back," but what did you do to her?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This friend who trusted you, helped you, and followed you into the direst dangers...
The man's lips part slightly. His voice is deep and dragged out.
female_content: The woman's lips part slightly. Her voice is deep and dragged out.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: <color=#fb9259>Hypatia Campbell, you're the one who pushed her into the deadliest peril.</color>

Amid the emotional turmoil, her surroundings suddenly distort. The walls collapse like quicksand, replaced by a vast emptiness resembling a square where a trial awaits. Hypatia kneels alone at its center, like a condemned prisoner to be interrogated.

speaker: Mother
content: This marriage is a complete failure... I had hoped you might amount to something, but you can't even compete with those illegitimate brats. You can't even hold onto what's handed to you...

speaker: Mother
content: If you can't lead the family, I might as well disown you!
Her father's towering figure stands like a silent mountain, hands clasped behind his back, looking down at her authoritatively.

speaker: Father
content: I have no need for useless children. Those who cannot provide value have no right to inherit this family name.
Her elder siblings gather together, their gazes contemptuous as they point their fingers at her, whispering and mocking.

speaker: Eirene
content: So this is my "sister"? Heh...
She desperately tries to defend herself, but her feeble words only sound more laughable and hollow amid their cold, mocking laughter.

speaker: Horo
content: The black box from afar and those strange experiments... You discovered them early on. So why didn't you investigate? Why didn't you give a warning sooner?

speaker: Horo
content: Did you get carried away after finally making a friend in real life? So much so that you forgot your responsibilities?

speaker: Hypatia
content: Huh?! No, it's not like that...
The next instant, more apparitions appear, bombarding her. Countless strange yet familiar faces emerge, painful wails and angry accusations blending into overwhelming clamor.

speaker: Furorian
content: <color=#dg1f1f><i>Lady Hypatia... You're a Fraser noble, so you'll never understand... The source of the Black Ring is the source of all suffering in the farlands. You cannot change it... You yourself are a part of it...

speaker: Furorian
content: <color=#dg1f1f><i>Farewell... We're happy to give our lives...

speaker: Hypatia
content: No... come back, please come back...!

Hypa runs after the apparitions, but only grows increasingly distant from them. Beyond the far-off crowd, a lonely, slender figure slowly emerges. She stares directly at Hypatia, her gaze filled with disappointment.

speaker: Hella
content: Hypa... it's so dark, so cold here... I've waited for you for so long...

speaker: Hella
content: But until the very end, you never came back to me...

Hearing each sentence is like feeling a piece of flesh being carved out of her body. Pain clogs her chest, as if an invisible hand is choking her throat. Her voice catches, reduced to nothing but broken, intermittent whispers.

speaker: Hypatia
content: I'm sorry... I'm really sorry...
Hypatia curls up on the ground. She doesn't dare lift her head, unable to face the shattered visages of those she has failed and betrayed.
Hypatia.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I know your pain. I understand your struggle. You've carried too much for far too long. None of this was ever meant to be shouldered by you alone. I'm ready to share your burden and your suffering, as your friend.
Through the tears, Hypatia sees the man. His expression seems genuinely understanding and sympathetic. Hypa reaches out a trembling hand, trying to grasp the sleeve of the apparition.
female_content: Through the tears, Hypatia sees the woman. Her expression seems genuinely understanding and sympathetic. Hypa reaches out a trembling hand, trying to grasp the sleeve of the apparition.

content: But the man steps back, evading her hand.
female_content: But the woman steps back, evading her hand.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You knew who I was and that I'm a Black Ring expert... so why didn't you tell me the truth? Was it guilt? Or were you too ashamed to talk?!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If you had just been honest with me sooner, I would have rushed to Furor. BR-005 wouldn't have detonated and things might have turned out differently. All those people wouldn't have had to die!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Why didn't you say it? Why did you hesitate?!
<size=45>Why didn't you confront your brother and the Luminaris Society sooner?
<size=45>Why didn't you figure out the truth behind Aurum Secretum sooner?
<size=45>Why... didn't you confess everything and ask him for help when you first learned ${PlayerName}'s true identity?
female_content: Why... didn't you confess everything and ask her for help when you first learned ${PlayerName}'s true identity?

speaker: Hypatia
content: You're right. I've had so many chances, but I didn't seize even one of them...

speaker: Hypatia
content: What should I do... What can I possibly do now... Please, I beg you, don't leave...

Guilt, confusion, and remorse churn in her heart like tides crashing against a crumbling sea wall. Her breathing becomes ragged as sobs burst from her throat uncontrollably, scalding tears streaming down her face.
Until...
Pain, anger, indignation, guilt... these are all pieces of your heart too. Ever the perfectionist, aren't you? Unwilling to forgive yourself even in your dreams.
You want forgiveness. You want to confess your sins to them... but is this the only reason you dream of them?
The voice gradually transforms, turning from faint sighs into gentle yet beguiling whispers.
No, what you truly desire is simply for one of them to point you in the right direction.

speaker: Adelaide
content: Just like right now, as you call out to me.

speaker: Young Hypatia
content: Sob...
Back then, she was once again locked in a cramped room for failing to meet her mother's standards. The shadows on the walls loomed over her as the stifling air suffocated her.
Hypatia curled up in the corner, quietly sobbing, when the door was gently pushed open. A sliver of light slipped in from outside, like salvation falling through a crack.

speaker: Young Adelaide
content: Crying again? There, there. Everything's fine now.
The boy, whose features still bore traces of childishness, stepped over that beam of light as he entered. He crouched down and reached out his hand, gently wiping away his sister's tears.

speaker: Young Adelaide
content: One day, you'll have to face challenges beyond your abilities and shoulder burdens that should never have been yours. And fate is cruel. You'll so often find yourself alone.

speaker: Young Adelaide
content: But fortunately, siblings are meant to share each other's pain.

speaker: Young Adelaide
content: Come with me... As your brother, I can at least walk alongside you for a while.

She looked up in a daze, her young heart enveloped by such warmth for the very first time. In that moment, it almost seemed to her that this hand and this figure were the only things left in this world.
So she followed him out, her gaze firmly fixed on his thin yet resolute silhouette. It was the only time she depended so entirely on someone, making her most tender memory.

However, in the blink of an eye, the boy turned around, a shadow suddenly falling over his limpid features. His smile remained, but something had changed. Beneath that warm exterior now emanated something chilling.

speaker: Adelaide
content: You don't need to worry, Hypa. Just do as I say. Isn't that how it's always been between us?

speaker: Adelaide
content: No matter what happens, I'll always be by your side, protecting you and guiding you... Listen to me, and everything will be so much easier.
Hypatia releases her hand and lifts her head to look directly at her brother's face.

speaker: Hypatia
content: ...But you've changed. You're no longer the person who once led me out of darkness.

speaker: Hypatia
content: I won't trust you anymore.
Since when? The family member she once trusted completely has already gone on a different path.
The man gives a faint smile. His figure begins to fade away, his smile becoming indistinct in the growing light.

speaker: Adelaide
content: ...Is that so? Then... who do you plan to follow now?

speaker: Adelaide
content: Besides me, who else could promise to never let go of your hand?
A startled dove takes flight from the windowsill. Hypatia's eyes snap open.
An unfamiliar ceiling comes into view. She lies on a bed in an inn, her chest still heaving from the suppressed cries in her dream, her pillow and sheets already soaked with sweat.
Next to the bed, scratchy news broadcast from the radio pierces her eardrums.

speaker: News
content: BR-005 has successfully detonated and continues to spread toward the border. The Tide of Ashes is still expanding, and Apostle of Ashes activity is surging. They are expected to strike the DisCity defense line again in several days.

speaker: News
content: Farland authorities state that the war is evolving as planned...
The anchor's indifferent voice and the clamor outside her window form an impenetrable barrier, trapping her within.

Hypatia hugs herself tightly, slowing her breathing to conserve energy. Constant fleeing has left her body extremely weak. Her eyes unconsciously fall on the communicator at her bedside, and she reaches out to turn it on.
Beneath the cracked screen, ${PlayerName}'s profile picture sits quietly against a black background, like a disconnected void.

speaker: Hypatia
content: Tell me... What should I do...
Just then, an unfamiliar voice drifts languidly through the air.
Poor child, are you feeling lost?
Hypatia whirls around, but the room is empty, except for a dove perched by the window, its red eyes gazing at her coldly. In the next instant, it takes flight.
Something quivers in Hypatia's chest. She rushes out after it without a second thought.

On the street corner below, the dove quietly lands on a woman's fingertip. Against the light, her white dress looks incongruously immaculate amid the surrounding chaos. The dove flutters its wings on her fingertip, like a gambling chip not yet cast.

speaker: Mysterious Woman
content: Oh, I only came looking for the missing genius Aurum Secretum researcher, but now I have a little lost dove in my palm. Now... what should I do?

speaker: Mysterious Woman
content: War is coming. If we delay any longer, peace won't reach the battlefield in time.
<size=50>One week before the outbreak of the War of Shattered Blade.
<size=50>The DisCity spy "Peace Dove" has successfully made contact with the key figure of Fraser's Aurum Secretum research, <color=#fb9259>Hypatia Campbell</color>.
August, N.F. 115. The destruction of BR-005 turned the tide of war.

The Farland Alliance was forced into a full retreat. For DisCity, it was more than a victory; it was the moment they seized decisive strategic superiority.

At the center of it all was General Augustus. Her legendary military success granted her unprecedented influence.

Now, the city holds its breath. Will Paradeisos appoint her to a higher office? Will she seek new battlefields?

The rumors are a constant hum, yet the profound reverence for her—or more accurately, for pure, unassailable strength—never wavers.

You, too, once felt that reverence.

Having stood with her, breached the Black Ring, and rescued Hella, you placed her on a pedestal.
But perspectives shift. And in the space of a few short days, yours began to change...

September 1, N.F. 115
Bureau Office
After BR-005, the MBCC mailroom has been nearly buried. Not in debris, but in gifts from General Augustus.

They have been pouring in daily—gourmet food, vintage wine, and tailored suits, punctuated by endless invitations to galas and yacht parties. But the most absurd by far is one piece from her personal collection: a hulking metal horse statue.

Reportedly salvaged from the BR-005 battlefield, she found the metal horse "very cool" but had no space for it in a Nirvana Port undergoing reconstruction. In a stroke of what she called generosity, General Augustus decided to let you display it for a few days.
You try to follow her reasoning.

speaker: Augustus
content: So, do you like my gift? Any fun plans for the weekend?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: How does a General have this much free time? Some of us are chained to our desks. You get to relax; I get to burn the midnight oil.
Hearty laughter echoes on the other end of the terminal.

speaker: Augustus
content: Hahaha! After all we've been through, you still don't see it? Life can end in an instant. That's not a reason to hide in your office; it's a reason to live.

speaker: Augustus
content: Especially for a workaholic like you... you might just drop dead from exhaustion one day, who knows?
You maintain your composure; a few provocative words from her are no match for your current equanimity. Adjusting your mindset, you respond with measured dignity.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Thanks to the endurance training from your unit, I'm good for a few more all-nighters. Now, if you'll excuse me, duty calls.

speaker: Augustus
content: Hmm... brushing me off like that... Could it be...
Her contemplative tone gives you pause. Overtime is a convenient excuse, but you know the truth is more complicated. You are, after all, facing the most formidable woman in DisCity.

Is it politics? A conflict of interest? Or are you simply wary of being swept up by her overwhelming charisma? With your comrade-in-arms chapter closing, you haven't yet found the new script for your relationship. You wonder if she has, either.
Regardless, she speaks up.

speaker: Augustus
content: Could it be you're sulking because <color=#fb9259>I</color> was the one who pulled little Hella out of the Black Ring, stealing <color=#fb9259>your</color> heroic moment?

speaker: Augustus
content: Don't take it to heart. After all, in this world, the strong call the shots—
Jump
CLANK! You ended the call and blocked her number in one furious motion. Your terminal smashes against the wall, a victim of your fury.
The damage she inflicts isn't physical; it's a slow burn of pure frustration. You'll die from rage long before overwork claims you. Did you ever truly respect her? Really??
As the thought echoes in your mind, an elegant hand appears in the doorway, calmly retrieving the device you just condemned.

speaker: 9th
content: Even the most durable device has its limits, Chief. And with reconstruction costs being what they are, our budget for replacements isn't quite what it used to be.

speaker: 9th
content: I'd advise taking good care of this one. It's about to become extremely useful.

Seeing an old friend should be a rare pleasure, and a part of you is genuinely glad—his survival is a relief. The expected thing would be to exchange pleasantries, to fall into that easy rhythm. But you can't.
The crisis is far from over, and the 9th Agency is at the very epicenter of it all. An intelligence agent shouldn't have time for casual visits. Which means this is anything but casual.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It's good to see you in one piece. But... you don't just drop by for a chat at a time like this. What's wrong?

speaker: 9th
content: You always did cut straight to the heart of the matter. You're correct. A concerning situation is developing within the city-state. The 9th Agency is preoccupied with external threats, leaving us stretched too thin to address it properly.

speaker: 9th
content: So, I've come to seek your counsel. And, if I may be so bold, to ask you to leverage your... unique rapport with <color=#fb9259>a certain individual</color>.

speaker: 9th
content: Naturally, I'm referring to the most prominent, politically sensitive, and frankly, sleep-depriving figure right now: <color=#fb9259>General Augustus</color>.
He hands you back the terminal you just threw. A single prompt glows on the screen: a data transfer request.

After the Ash campaign, DisCity's "savior," General Augustus, never bothered to leave. Instead of leading her Shattered Blade unit back to Nirvana Port, she has embedded herself in the city's elite social circuit. Or, more accurately, the elite now curate their events specifically for her.

<size=40>Activity Log 1:</size>
<color=#fb9259>N.F. 115/8/29</color> Attended a celebration banquet hosted by Public Security Bureau Chief Ford, a man previously suspected of involvement in the Euphoria case.

<size=40>Activity Log 2:</size>
<color=#fb9259>N.F. 115/8/30</color> Attended a covert meeting at the Jacknal Estate. The purpose is unknown. The owner, Penn Jacknal, is a suspect in Hypercube smuggling operations.

<size=40>Activity Log 3:</size>
<color=#fb9259>N.F. 115/8/31</color> Made a high-profile appearance at a joint reception hosted by the Harrington and Frank families, where she reportedly made shocking statements about conventional trade with the Outlands.
The report further notes a trail of suspicious financial transactions and regulatory violations, as multiple institutions have bent their own rules to accommodate her.
To the public, Augustus is a war hero basking in well-earned glory. But beneath the surface, her presence is a destabilizing force, sending shockwaves through the city's power structures.

speaker: 9th
content: As you know, the General promised to return to Nirvana Port to regroup and await further orders. The agreed-upon deadline, however, has come and gone, with no sign of her departure.

speaker: 9th
content: Her troops are still here. And what's more, she's using her victory as political capital, maneuvering through every sector of the city, expanding her influence. Her intentions... are unclear.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Augustus is bold, I'll give her that. Maybe even flashy. But she's always been straightforward with me. Is that really how the 9th Agency sees her? Or is this the view from... higher up?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Are you telling me she's being labeled a threat? That you think she's making a power grab?

speaker: 9th
content: ...Chief, you must understand. Compared to the long history she has written, your time with her has been but a brief chapter.
You read on, confusion giving way to disbelief, then to stunned silence. The revelation on the screen is impossible. Your eyes lock on the words, refusing to process them.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...What is this?!

speaker: 9th
content: Every detail there is a verifiable fact, a matter of historical record. We've fabricated nothing. DisCorps were vital allies in our recent fight; that is true. But it seems the General has not entirely left her... shadowed past behind. She is playing a deeper game.
His focus remains locked on the intelligence in your hands. A solemn undercurrent now runs through his tone.

speaker: 9th
content: The General holds a unique interest in you. We need you to use that. Learn what she is truly planning. If our concerns are misplaced, then we will all rest easier. But if they are not...

speaker: 9th
content: ...Then DisCity may face a threat far more dangerous than anything the Outlands could muster.
After a moment of hesitation, you set aside the other reports in your hands and accept the mission.
[Scene Change: Interrogation Room]

The next day, against all reason, she comes. Catherine Augustus Andohar—the general who repelled the great enemy, the leader of the Shattered Blade, DisCity's most celebrated figure—has accepted your discourteous "invitation." She forsakes a dozen high-society galas to descend into your austere, oppressive interrogation room.
That chair has held countless notorious Sinners. Yet none occupy it as she does. She sits with an air of poised imperiousness, not as a guest in your domain, but as its sovereign.

speaker: Augustus
content: So this is where you finally decide to ask me, after playing hard to get for so long? Charming.

speaker: Augustus
content: Off the battlefield, your sense of decorum is... remarkably flexible.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Thank you for accepting MBCC's invitation, General Augustus.
Hearing you address her this way, she raises an eyebrow.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This isn't a formal interrogation. Just a routine inquiry. Since you've been at WhiteSands for years, you're likely unaware of the recent policy changes in DisCity.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Being a Sinner is no longer a crime. Pass our psychological and ability assessments, get an MBCC safety certification, and you can move freely in public. You'll have the full rights of any DisCitizen.

speaker: Augustus
content: Hmm... Acceptable. Not much different from how things are now.

speaker: Augustus
content: Well then, let's see what the Chief of Minos can do with a suspect like me. The rumors flying about you are... fascinating.
A mere two hours ago, you could have dismissed her methods as unprofessional. Now, that luxury is gone.

options: Ask why she's staying in the city

speaker: Augustus
content: Isn't this the great DisCity? All my family's mansions and estates are here. Am I not allowed to come home? Or is a general not permitted to take a vacation?

options: You call bringing an entire stationed military unit a "vacation"?

speaker: Augustus
content: My troops have weathered storms for years and just won a war. They deserve to enjoy the peace. Is there a problem with a commander looking after her own?

options: But the places you've been visiting are suspicious.

content: test
test
test
test
test
test
test
It's the same classified document from the 9th Agency, cataloging all her contacts with numerous high-ranking officials.
Subsequent verification has linked a significant number of these individuals to active investigations for wartime betrayal and systemic corruption.
She listens, her eyes locked on yours. As you speak, her gaze sharpens from casual attention to a blade's point of focus.

speaker: Augustus
content: Is there a problem with my social calendar? Does our austere Chief find my taste in associates too... lavish?

options: It's who you're meeting with that concerns me.
It's why you're meeting with them that concerns me.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I have friends who've briefed me on these people. I know their backgrounds. By associating with them, you're only tarnishing your own reputation.

speaker: Augustus
content: Oh? And was that... your friend the Speaker who told you that? Or perhaps the friend who happens to be the former Speaker's... illegitimate daughter?
Her gaze is a physical pressure, and her tone, sharp enough to cut, sends a jolt of ice down your spine.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Who my sources are isn't the point. What are you playing at, Augustus?
Augustus gives a soft chuckle.

speaker: Augustus
content: What do you think? You've investigated me so thoroughly. Or perhaps... your real interest isn't in me at all, but in the <color=#fb9259>DisCorps</color> standing behind me?

speaker: Augustus
content: Go on, then. Tell me what you've uncovered.
A new edge enters her voice. Your body reacts as if to a physical threat—muscles coiling, your grip on the files turning into a defensive clutch.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...After DisCity's independence, your faction rode the momentum of the Independence War to an overwhelming election victory. Within two years, you'd pacified the satellite towns, bringing security and prosperity to the entire periphery.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But soon after, the DisCorps under <color=#fb9259>Dravyn's</color> command twisted. He waged brutal campaigns abroad while enforcing an iron grip at home... He led this city into a long, dark era.
A cold sweat pricks at your hairline as you lay out the information. Augustus doesn't interrupt; she merely observes, her eyes alight with undisguised amusement.

speaker: Augustus
content: And what does that history lesson have to do with me? Didn't your files mention I was asleep for most of it?
Indeed, for DisCity in the fight for independence, a Sinner who could control magnetic fields was a priceless strategic asset, one capable of tipping the vast military scales against the metropoles.
To preserve this power and stave off Mania corruption, Catherine Augustus Andohar was placed in cryosleep shortly after independence, following the liberation of several key satellite towns.
By the time she awoke, it was already N.F. 103, long after DisCorps had been reorganized into the FAC. But... is she truly as disconnected from it all as she seems?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The records are clear. He gave you medals and promotions outside the chain of command. He personally led you into battle, and rumors suggest he was grooming you as his successor.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: To treat your war-induced Mania intensification, he personally ordered EDGE to develop cryosleep technology, all to ensure you would survive until a cure could be found.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That man is regarded as the greatest dictator in DisCity's history, a figure who's still controversial today. And you... you were like a daughter to him.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Are you saying you knew nothing about what he was doing? That you have no responsibility for it?

speaker: Augustus
content: "Like a daughter"... Hah! If that old grouch heard you say that, he'd be spinning in his grave!
She dismisses the most insignificant point of your accusation with a light laugh, yet her voice retains a strange, almost fond warmth.
Mid-laughter, her eyes find yours. The warmth vanishes, replaced by a focus so intense it feels like a physical pressure.

speaker: Augustus
content: Go on. I'm listening.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Marshal Dravyn's prestige from the Independence War gave him immense power. But that power corrupted him. It concentrated in his hands until he became a tyrant.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: By the end of his first term, slow reconstruction was turning people against him. Facing electoral defeat, he refused to step down. He rigged the vote and forced his way back into office, becoming the longest-ruling dictator in DisCity's history.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: His solution to internal strife was external war. He plundered abroad and crushed dissent at home. Corruption was rampant. The city-state kept rotting... until the DisSea Explosion in N.F. 84 finally forced his hand.

speaker: Augustus
content: Continue.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...After the explosion, the Black Ring returned. Mania catastrophes were everywhere. Dravyn had no choice but to cooperate with EDGE. He ceded authority, merged the military into the FAC, a united front against the Mania.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: He "stepped down" as Speaker to become the FAC's first Commander-in-Chief. The title changed, but his grip on power didn't. Not until the Eclipse Operation failed in N.F. 103. After that disaster, with public outrage and the FAC broken... the Marshal finally fell. He died in bitterness and obscurity.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: —That's the official record. The rumor is he couldn't live with his failure. That he took his own life.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And you woke up in N.F. 103. After Dravyn's death, when EDGE appointed Adrian Sterling as the new Commander-in-Chief, you refused his orders. You took a faction of DisCorps and left the city.

speaker: Augustus
content: It's been a long time since anyone has recounted this story to me. Go on.
The words die in your throat. A different kind of cold, one of pure dread, seizes you, locking your jaw and making speech impossible.

options: What are you trying to accomplish by coming back now?

content: She holds your gaze, relentless and silent, until the question evaporates from your mind and all that remains is the slow, suffocating weight of her attention.

speaker: Augustus
content: Are you afraid of me?

speaker: Augustus
content: Heh, you should be, boy. Do you really think I can't do anything just because we're on your turf?
female_content: Heh, you should be, girl. Do you really think I can't do anything just because we're on your turf?

speaker: Augustus
content: Perceptive. That's more like it. You should be, boy. Do you really think I can't do anything just because we're on your turf?
female_content: Perceptive. That's more like it. You should be, girl. Do you really think I can't do anything just because we're on your turf?

speaker: Augustus
content: Your pathetic security system can't even detect a killing intent this clear.

Bzzt— Blackness ensues as the Mania field kills the lights. The Sinner's restraints disengage immediately. In the heartbeat that follows, cold metal shrieks as it clamps around your wrists and ankles, chaining you to the chair.
Your struggles are useless. Across from you, the architect of this chaos lounges in her seat, a motionless silhouette in the dark—a sated predator observing its captive prey.

speaker: Augustus
content: Curious? Let me give you a demonstration of how we used to handle interrogations back in the tyrannical DisCorps era.

An unseen force lifts your chair, and you with it. You glide helplessly through the oppressive dark, drawn directly toward her. Augustus remains seated, merely planting a foot against your chair to halt your approach with nonchalance.

speaker: Augustus
content: I've completed my registration. I haven't misused my powers. By the book, you have no grounds to interrogate me. Besides, you've been "too busy" to see me.

speaker: Augustus
content: So why the sudden change of heart?

speaker: Augustus
content: Still holding back? Look around. The surveillance is offline; this is our private little space now. I can do anything I want to you, and we have all the time in the world for a... heart-to-heart.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Your recent behavior has raised concerns. After our victory, a lot of dubious elements have resurfaced. Instead of keeping your distance, you're meeting with them. People are naturally questioning your intentions.

speaker: Augustus
content: Oh? And what does that have to do with you?

speaker: Augustus
content: Didn't you solemnly declare you'd "only fight Mania and only go to Mania battlefields"? It's only been a few days, and now you're dabbling in political scandals again?
Her questioning leaves you speechless.
Indeed, you have no official reason to be involved. She truly hasn't misused her abilities, you no longer report to the 9th Agency, and the MBCC has no stake. So... why are you risking her wrath?
Doubt flashes through your mind, but now is not the time to waver. Augustus demands an answer.

options: Tell her about your mission first

content: You press your lips together, offering only silence. To your surprise, a spark of genuine amusement lights her eyes.

speaker: Augustus
content: Not talking, hmm... Let me guess. Did someone put you up to this? "Expressed their concerns"?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Some reliable people are concerned about your intentions. They asked me to look into it.

speaker: Augustus
content: They told you quite a bit, didn't they? To be careful around me? To stay away? Or perhaps... to deliver a warning?

speaker: Augustus
content: <color=#fb9259>Who</color> told you to probe me like this?
Her voice drops to a glacial temperature. An unseen magnetic force wrenches your chair forward, slamming you into the direct, cutting line of her stare.

speaker: Augustus
content: How did the person who gave you this "mission" describe me? Rebel, usurper, thug, heir to a dictator, returning aspirant... what else?

speaker: Augustus
content: Then, did they tell you this...
The cold leather of her glove closes around your jaw. With irresistible force, she yanks you forward, pulling your ear to within a breath of her mouth.

speaker: Augustus
content: The second Commander of the Independence Army, the first democratically elected Speaker, the first FAC Commander-in-Chief—<color=#fb9259>Marshal Dravyn Steel</color> did not commit suicide.

speaker: Augustus
content: He was killed by his <color=#fb9259>most trusted subordinate</color>... These ambitious jackals waited until the old Marshal was in his twilight years, then made their move to seize his fading power. They delivered the final blow to the already weakened FAC, ensuring it would become nothing more than EDGE's puppet.

speaker: Augustus
content: They left that part out, did they? Good. Then you should hear it from me. And we can discuss... other things, too.

speaker: Augustus
content: Like what we really did. To our own people, to others... Not just numbers in a report. The real stories. The kind they'd never dare mention now, during DisCity's glorious triumph. It's far too shameful.
[Jasmine Flashback]

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: <color=#dg1f1f><size=44><i>Don't touch me!</color></size><i>

You deploy the prohibition. It's the first time you've used that command on her. For a single, heart-stopping moment, you see it: a flash of pure, unadulterated murderous intent in her eyes, there and gone, but utterly real.

speaker: Augustus
content: So that's how you use those shackles... Heh. No wonder so many were desperate to bring you back.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Mmph—!
The crimson spikes lance through her frame, forcing her to release you. But the hovering shards of metal ignore the command, darting forward to clamp over your mouth, silencing you utterly.

speaker: Augustus
content: Go on, then. Let's see what else you can do...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If you want to talk, then tell me this: Why do treasonous, irredeemable remnants of the DisCorps have such close ties with the current Commander-in-Chief?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Back in N.F. 103, when the FAC was at its weakest, why didn't your "arrogant and disloyal" faction—you included—seize power? And who had the strength to exile you all?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And... what were you really angry about just now? This "mission"... What are you using me to fight against?
No answer comes, but the pressure pinning you down slackens by a fraction. Augustus opens her mouth to speak when suddenly—

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief!
The door bursts open as Nightingale interrupts the conversation.

speaker: Nightingale
content: General Augustus, this is a serious misunderstanding. Please, allow me to explain.
Her grip doesn't yield. Instead, she settles back against the chair, tilting her head in a cool, appraising stare directed at your adjutant.

speaker: Augustus
content: I must say, I never imagined DisCity would treat a victorious general like this. What's the saying? "Kill the goose that lays the golden eggs"? Though, your Chief here has no way to restrain me.

speaker: Nightingale
content: You have my sincere apologies. The 9th Agency inadvertently implicated you during their investigation into the Sillage Society. There have been individuals with ulterior motives attempting to approach you since your victory. Our intention was only to advise caution.

speaker: Nightingale
content: However, a person of significant authority has vouched for you. All official suspicions have been cleared. We only need to complete some paperwork to formally restore your freedom.
Augustus holds her in a cold, silent stare for a protracted moment before the force field restraining you finally dissolves.

speaker: Augustus
content: So it's that little spider... Too busy to keep tabs on me personally this time? Heh...
She scans the documents, and you both see it: the cited author's name—
<color=#fb9259>Barry Orwell</color>—the Council's recording clerk who publicly challenged her at various wartime gatherings.
A slow, knowing smirk spreads across her lips. But your mind is already elsewhere, grappling with a far more critical implication.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What do you mean, "cleared"? My interrogation isn't finished. This is far from over.
Nightingale's face loses all color, her words catching in her throat. Before a single syllable can form, Augustus's voice slices through the tension.

speaker: Augustus
content: It means someone in higher places wants to stand behind me and ride the wave of my success. Well, I suppose I should humor them...

She frees you from the chair's magnetic grip. The clatter of fallen metal pieces is the sound of the interrogation being forcibly concluded. Then, as if flipping a switch, she is all soft smiles and soothing gestures, gently straightening your clothes.

speaker: Augustus
content: My apologies for misunderstanding you. It's been a complicated time. I may have been on edge. I hope I didn't frighten you.

speaker: Augustus
content: Perfect timing. I have a banquet to attend. You should join me. Consider it my way of making amends. I'll even let you get a good whiff of the sweet scent of power.
She moves to leave, but as she passes you, she leans in close enough for her shadow to fall across your vision, dominating your field of view.

speaker: Augustus
content: After all, weren't you ordered to keep a close eye on me?

September 2, N.F. 115
Eastside District 3, Augustus Mansion (formerly Peace Mansion)
Victory Celebration Banquet for the Ash Campaign
Since last year's attack on the Viers Mansion, the historic Peace Mansion has emerged as the district's most prestigious venue for elite gatherings. Tonight, it is a monument to extravagance.

Gold and silver horse statues stand beside blooming flowers. Bottles of fine wines gleam under the light as rare blue feathers adorn legendary swords and armor, all competing for attention. The air is thick with the cloying scent of perfume, a fragrance so potent it stings the nose.

In every corner, wealth is immolated in a desperate race to express adoration for the General's victory. The guests have collectively decided this is the style she prefers—a questionable assumption, at best.

They are here to celebrate her triumph, but the true cause for revelry is the mansion's renaming. Several distinguished elites have even swallowed their pride, trading formal wear for blue military attire. It is as if, from this day forward, "Peace" has been superseded by a more glorious name: Augustus.
Yet, beneath the celebratory veneer, the air crackles with a faint, restless anxiety.

speaker: Guest
content: Are we really safe with her here? She's not like the others... And it wasn't long ago that we...

speaker: Guest
content: Shh! She's a woman of grand ambition, not some petty tyrant. And anyone who can't see which way the wind is blowing is a fool. It's just like the Independence War. Stake your claim now or get left behind.

speaker: Guest
content: Unlike that idiot Max King, he's really... Oh! Look, she's here!
The star of the evening makes her entrance. General Augustus descends the grand staircase, her opulent gown a seamless part of the bejeweled tapestry of political and business elites below.
In a deliberate irony, the guest of honor herself has forgone her signature, flamboyant military regalia, rendering the banquet's meticulous martial theme a case of profoundly misguided flattery.

All eyes follow her as she glides through the crowd, not to greet a dignitary, but to stop before a decorative suit of armor in the corner. You watch, helpless, as she "invites" you out from your hiding spot behind it and decisively links her arm with yours.

speaker: Augustus
content: You're early. Excited, aren't you?
She smiles with intimate familiarity, as if she has entirely forgotten that you two nearly came to blows in the interrogation room just yesterday.

speaker: Augustus
content: It's <color=#fb9259>Catherine</color>.

She hasn't just forgotten; she's orchestrating a scene. Deliberately, she steps closer, her hands coming up to straighten your posture with a proprietor's air. Under the weight of the crowd's gaze, she begins to adjust you.

speaker: Catherine
content: We went over this last night. Still can't get your tie straight?
female_content: We went over this last night. Your hair's come loose again.

content: With a knowing smile, she focuses on your collar, standing so near that her presence is a physical force. A mere downward glance captures the intimate details: the silk of her hair, the sweep of her lashes, the elegant line of her nose, and her vivid red lips...
female_content: With a knowing smile, she tucks the stray hairs at your temples behind your ears. Her wrist brushes your cheek, carrying with it that familiar, subtle fragrance—a scent that irresistibly draws your gaze back to her face.

content: She has always been radiant, but at this proximity, the fearsome general reveals an unexpected tenderness. Her fingertips brush against your throat, a touch so light it forces you to tilt your head back, a futile attempt to escape her overwhelming brilliance.
female_content: She has always been radiant, but at this close distance, surrounded by her fragrance, the fearsome battlefield commander unexpectedly reveals an unfamiliar tenderness. It doesn't take her long to arrange your hair, but then her fingertips trail lightly down the curve of your ear. A jolt of sensation sparks through you, forcing you to turn your head away from her intense scrutiny—

content: —only to be met by the stares of the crowd, their faces now a mask of envy and admiration.

speaker: Guest A
content: What a stunning pair, the heroes of our city! You simply must grace the cover of our magazine. We'll arrange our finest photography team for you.

speaker: Guest C
content: Beyond that, the General's heroic deeds will surely be recorded in the history books, celebrated for generations, just like Keylan... Oh, I can already picture the illustrations!

speaker: Guest B
content: "Augustus Breaching BR-005"—The Frank family has already commissioned DisCity's most renowned artist to capture the moment. The masterpiece will be delivered to your residence the instant it's complete.

The flattery finds its mark. The valorous general leans against you, shaking with laughter as she pulls you into the spotlight. The socialites, usually so cunning, now spew the most absurd praises, which she accepts with regal grace.

This is the treatment Catherine Augustus Andohar now commands in DisCity. Bathed in this cloying, suffocating adoration, only she could accept it as her natural birthright. You, however, dragged along like a royal consort, can only squirm in misery.

options: We had a "good time" last night?

speaker: Catherine
content: Heh. Just giving the fools a little show. Don't you think their reactions are amusing?
The fools in the audience savor every moment of her staged scandal, their faces plastered with sycophantic glee.
She answers with a smile, her grip a silent command not to leave.
Just then, a distinctly prominent voice cuts through the chorus of sycophantic praise.

speaker: Wilton
content: General, your presence truly honors this gathering. And of course, your esteemed companion as well.

The man offers a respectful bow in your direction. You recognize him from a memorial reception. <color=#fb9259>Wilton Stewart</color>, a prominent conservative councilor who was outmaneuvered by Max King twice—first in an election, then in the recent war. Now, he is swiftly repositioning himself for a new gambit, a man not to be underestimated.
The crowd instinctively parts, granting the host the coveted space before the General, a privilege he accepts with natural ease. Noting your empty hands, he smoothly continues.

speaker: Wilton
content: I have a treasured vintage, imported from the Campbell Estate. Might it be to your taste?

speaker: Catherine
content: Hmm... a bit too dry for me. I prefer something sweeter.

speaker: Wilton
content: Of course, right away. And you, Chief of the MBCC? Any preferences?

speaker: Wilton
content: I must say, I never dreamed both heroes of our city-state would grace us with their presence tonight. It's an immense honor. Please accept my personal gratitude.

speaker: Catherine
content: Hehe, you're as accommodating as ever. But our little ${PlayerName} doesn't drink this kind of stuff. Let's talk about something else.

speaker: Catherine
content: If I recall, you invited me here to discuss something important. Something about my garrison?
Wilton freezes mid-gesture, shooting a furtive, almost guilty glance in your direction.

speaker: Wilton
content: Well... I had hoped to be better prepared, to discuss this in the privacy of your residence. And since Chief ${PlayerName} is honoring us for the first time, surely there are more interesting diversions. My collection room, or the gallery?
As he elaborates on his generous invitation, his eyes steal another look in your direction. Catherine, having missed nothing, allows a knowing smile to form.

speaker: Catherine
content: Should I call you a coward, or just blind? Can't you see? ${PlayerName} came here with me. That makes this person no outsider... and I don't appreciate that kind of treatment.
Wilton freezes for only a moment before a sudden understanding dawns, his face brightening with unmistakable delight.

speaker: Wilton
content: Oh! Oh, of course! How foolish of me. You two are steadfast allies, comrades who have faced death together. That makes you both my most honored friends! Please, right this way—
He eagerly leads you both toward another man.

speaker: Sernie
content: General Augustus. And... Chief ${PlayerName}.
Bowing to you, he shares a swift glance with Wilton, and his own defenses finally come down.

speaker: Sernie
content: I am Sernie. As for my background... heh, let's just say it's not the most important detail tonight. What is important is the word on the street, that General Augustus's troops are still lodged in a hotel.

speaker: Catherine
content: The finest hotel in Eastside.

speaker: Sernie
content: Naturally. The wealth of the Andohar family is truly remarkable.

speaker: Sernie
content: However... for a distinguished hero of the city-state to lack a proper garrison within our own walls... it would make DisCity a laughingstock if word got out.

speaker: Catherine
content: Well then, enlighten me. Where do you believe the DisCorps's new garrison should be established?
They immediately take the subtle depth in her smile for encouragement. Sernie clears his throat and seizes the opportunity.

speaker: Sernie
content: The FAC was fundamentally built around the DisCorps, integrating numerous other departments. And there's no question that you and your Shattered Blade are the rightful heirs to that legacy. You never should have been separate entities to begin with.

speaker: Sernie
content: We are at war now. The FAC can no longer confine itself to internal affairs. If your forces were to fight side by side, with close coordination, it would tremendously enhance the security of our entire city-state...

speaker: Catherine
content: That's not for you to decide, is it?
As Sernie smiles, you observe a ripple effect; one by one, the faces behind him mirror the expression.

speaker: Sernie
content: It's not my decision alone, but the will of the people. The calling of our era. These are extraordinary times; DisCity needs a wartime leader to guide us all and usher in a new age.

speaker: Sernie
content: The Commander has grown old. Set in his ways. I believe there is no one in all of DisCity more suited to the role than you.

speaker: Sernie
content: The business sector, the city council, and even... certain voices from Paradeisos all want you to step forward. Or, at the very least, have your forces take a definitive position on the garrison. Should you show interest, many would eagerly clear the path for you...

speaker: Catherine
content: Well then... I thank you both for your... consideration.

Her smile deepens as she raises her glass in a toast of agreement with the two men, wholly ignoring the tension in your arm. It is the signal they have been waiting for. A palpable wave of relief washes over the crowd, and the room slowly fills with the hum of laughter and animated conversation.

speaker: Guest B
content: You know, looking back, this war hasn't been all bad. The whole West District situation has made the economy stagnant for years, but the General's forces have turned it all around overnight. The Outlands took quite the beating this time. And the war reparations... care to guess the figure?

speaker: Guest C
content: Heh, the reparations are nothing. The real prize is BR-005. They deployed all those Apostles of Ashes... and after suppressing them, there are supposedly no mines? Impossible. Mark my words, a new great Hypercube rush is about to begin.

speaker: Guest C
content: If that's true, with General Augustus at the helm, our shipping lanes will be secure, trade will flow, and our military power will be completely revitalized! It's time to cast off the shackles of history and forge a new world order...

At this moment, victory has finally descended upon DisCity. The air is thick with intoxicating flattery, a tribute the flushed and excited crowd offers up like courtiers to a newly crowned queen. The hall vibrates with a shared fantasy: the spoils of war and a glorious future for all.

The fear is gone. Now, from the shadows of high society, countless hands reach for her—like putrid, grasping flesh drawn to a gleaming blade. They rejoice that its edge no longer presses their throats, and celebrate as it is now poised to conquer the world for them.

speaker: Wilton
content: There is... one more small matter...

speaker: Wilton
content: It's just that recently, the Speaker and that 9th Agency have been talking about investigating asset transfers, Outland dealings... How should I put this... don't you think they're going a bit too far?

speaker: Wilton
content: Not all financial transactions are suspicious! Some are just delayed settlements. If this continues, innocent people will be caught in the crossfire. The war is over. We should be unified, not creating division. All I'm saying is...

As the man stammers his excuses, a wave of nausea washes over you. You look away, only to find the entire room is doing the same—a sea of carefully neutral masks, all ears intently trained on the General, waiting. A roomful of scum, all cut from the same rotten cloth.
In response, Augustus offers only the ghost of a smile, an answer as ambiguous as silence.

speaker: Augustus
content: You'll have to ask my dear Chief about that. The Euphoria investigation was his initiative, after all. Better stay on his good side, hmm?
female_content: You'll have to ask my dear Chief about that. The Euphoria investigation was her initiative, after all. Better stay on her good side, hmm?

content: Wilton's gleaming eyes immediately snap to you, fixing on you with a look of desperate, calculating eagerness.

speaker: Wilton
content: Thank you so very much—
His face lights up with delight, and he launches into a torrent of words. The flood of filth that was meant for Augustus instantly gushes toward you.
Just as you reach your limit and move to brush his hand away, Augustus leans close to your ear once more, an intimate, possessive gesture, like someone jealously reclaiming what is hers.
He leans in, his face greasy and shining, provoking a violent wave of goosebumps across your skin. The sensation is more violating than a Corruptor's attack.
Just as you reflexively move to brush his hand away, Augustus leans close to your ear once more, an intimate, possessive gesture, like someone jealously reclaiming what is hers.

speaker: Catherine
content: Well, I've enjoyed myself long enough. I still have somewhere to be with my dear ${PlayerName} for the second round.

speaker: Sernie
content: Huh? Leaving so soon? But we still have so much to discuss about the garrison...

speaker: Catherine
content: I said, it's long enough.

A slight chill falls over the moment. Sernie, catching the signal at once, swiftly pivots the conversation. And so, Augustus smiles at him again. A generous smile, the kind given to a well-trained dog for performing a trick.

speaker: Catherine
content: It's such a lovely evening. I want to show him my private collection. Sorry, but this time, I want it to be just the two of us.
female_content: It's such a lovely evening. I want to show her my private collection. Sorry, but this time, I want it to be just the two of us.

content: At these words, the guests fall silent, then—spurred by the quick-witted—erupt into applause.
