They shower you with cheesy praises, from "feast for the eyes" to "kindred spirits," lauding the DisCorps-MBCC alliance and the union of its two heroes.

speaker: Guest C
content: Have a wonderful night!
Then, to rowdy cheers, Augustus downs her wine and flings the empty glass into the throng. In the chaotic scramble for the souvenir, she links her arm with yours and makes her escape.
[Exit and get into the car]
[Exit and get into the car 2]

You are in yet another of the General's luxury cars, cruising through the heart of the bustling city. But this time, your stomach churns with a violent dread, every nerve on edge. In the driver's seat, Augustus is the picture of relaxation, as if it were all just the norm.

speaker: Catherine
content: Phew... remind me, who was that person again?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: A key figure in the Council's conservative faction. Wilton Stewart. Distant relative of the former Speaker. And the other one, Sernie, seems to have connections that could help you... stir the pot with the FAC.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: They're trying to provoke you into seizing FAC territory for a garrison station and using the opportunity to usurp power and expand your influence.

speaker: Catherine
content: Oh, right. See? Bringing you along was a brilliant move. Very clever. Make a note of them.
Keeping track of such people feels like a stain on the mind, yet you commit their faces and names to memory regardless.
With a general as unpredictable as her, you can never know when she might finally be swayed by their honeyed words and decide their schemes have merit.

options: I had no idea you enjoyed these kinds of events.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Is the <color=#fb9259>second round</color> going to have the same stench? Don't you find it all a bit disgusting?

speaker: Catherine
content: Not at all. I come from a military arms dynasty. I've been used to it since I was a child.

speaker: Catherine
content: Wherever there's money and power, people will always claw their way in. So much naked ambition in one place... of course it feels dirty to you.

speaker: Catherine
content: But as you climb higher, your world will only get more crowded. So much praise and flattery, so many schemes and desires... Especially here in DisCity. You'll be put on a pedestal and constantly subjected to the worst of human nature.

speaker: Catherine
content: Better get used to it now. Build up your immunity. I'd hate to see the day our noble Chief gives in to temptation and is wracked with guilt over it.

options: I could always choose to keep my distance.

speaker: Catherine
content: Haha. How do you expect to change the world while avoiding the battlefield? Besides... you can't escape anyway.

Augustus stretches her arm into the slipstream, her hand riding the howling DisCity wind. Behind her extravagant sunglasses, her gaze is fixed on the road ahead, yet seems to look through it into some vast nothingness. The glittering city lights slide over her face, streaking past so that light and shadow perform an ambiguous dance across her features.
In the lull between the rushing wind and the engine's hum, her soft words are almost lost:

speaker: Catherine
content: You've had a long night. Let me take you home.
[Scene Change: MBCC Office]

September 3, N.F. 115, 10:00 AM
MBCC Chief's Office
Before you can fully piece together the clues from the previous day, an uninvited guest arrives at the MBCC office.

The visitor is <color=#fb9259>Kane Diesel</color>, a media professional known for covering politics. You have no personal recollection of him, but his name comes with a referral from a friend of Max King. After a moment's deliberation, you grant him entry.
The moment he sits down, he gets straight to the point.

speaker: Kane
content: There's a lot of chatter in the city-state about Augustus taking over the FAC and restructuring the military. Chief, what's your take? Is it even feasible? Credible?
Is he referring to the Rancor troops formally relocating back within DisCity? Your instincts go on high alert, but you keep your expression perfectly neutral.

options: ...That's well above my pay grade. No comment.

content: Kane raises an eyebrow.

speaker: Kane
content: Really? Your department works with both sides more than almost anyone. Any shake-up would land directly on your doorstep. You can't tell me you're not concerned.

speaker: Kane
content: Or is it... an uncomfortable topic? Given your... close relationship with General Augustus?
You shoot a glare at him.

speaker: Kane
content: Sorry, I mean no offense. It's just, when people see you two at the banquet together last night, they'll talk. It's only natural.

speaker: Kane
content: And that obvious favor she shows you... That's a significant opportunity, isn't it?
What are you implying?

speaker: Kane
content: Look, setting aside the historical baggage and just focusing on power, the city-state is desperate for military strength right now. Combat departments are on the rise. They've been held back by the FAC's bureaucracy. But this? This could be a chance to reshuffle the entire deck...

speaker: Kane
content: Right now, General Augustus is in a league of her own. She's the talent the city-state needs, and the one most likely to claim the largest piece of the post-war pie. Align with the right faction, and you catch the prevailing wind.

speaker: Kane
content: Her iron will, her decisiveness—her exceptional abilities in every regard. She reminds me of Marshal Dravyn in his prime. Setting aside the historical baggage, she's destined to be the brightest star of our future.

"Setting aside the historical baggage"—he's said it twice now. The hypocrisy is glaring; it's clear the "baggage" is the very reason he's here. He's backing the dictator's heir, betting she will seize power just as her predecessor did.
The realization turns your stomach, but he prattles on, utterly oblivious to your disgust.

speaker: Kane
content: The only question is her next move. Chief, given your rapport with her... have you heard any whispers about her plans, or...
As he talks, he closes the distance between you. Memories of last night's banquet assault your senses, and you feel the last of your patience shatter.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Back off. The mind games you play with her won't work on me.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You want to use the post-war chaos and her momentum to dismantle the FAC, don't you? Start at the garrison, send a signal, and slowly encroach? You see her ambition as a lever you can pull, luring her into your web.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Let me be clear. I may be "fortunate" enough to have her attention, but I will never support her seizing power. I'll stand in her way. That's what a real friend would do!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You should trust that General Augustus will make the right decision on her own. If she chooses to favor you, my interference won't sway her. Likewise, her ambitions have no influence on me. There is simply no connection between us.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I apologize, but I have a considerable amount of work to attend to. Please see yourself out.
You fire back with a directness that leaves Kane speechless. But his stunned expression is short-lived, quickly replaced by a look of unmistakable relief.

speaker: Kane
content: That's a big relief... You really are as upright and trustworthy as he described.
He dips his head briefly, and when he looks up, the Editor-in-Chief is a different man. His expression sobers, his gaze sharpens, and he fixes you with an unnervingly direct stare.

speaker: Kane
content: I apologize, Chief. That was a test. The current political climate is dangerous. Had you shown even the slightest agreement with my earlier suggestions, I would have had to end the conversation here.

speaker: Kane
content: But now, I'm beyond glad to see we share the same objective: we must firmly oppose this regression. Augustus has to be stopped.
While explaining, he produces a second terminal and swiftly initiates an encrypted link. The screen flickers to life, revealing a face you find familiar.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: We met at the peace ball before the war... You're the Council's recording clerk who opposed Augustus even during wartime. <color=#fb9259>Barry Orwell</color>, is it?
Barry nods, his expression deeply troubled.

speaker: Barry Orwell
content: The DisCorps's occupation of FAC headquarters will be a blatant declaration of ambition. Whether they intend to subjugate the FAC or merge with it to reconstitute the military, the outcome would be earth-shattering. Such a move absolutely requires proper procedural deliberation.

speaker: Barry Orwell
content: But her current behavior, the circles she frequents... it's deeply concerning. If she continues to surround herself with these opportunistic sycophants, the General will inevitably follow her predecessor down the same path. Power is a trap.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Are you disappointed in her current actions?

speaker: Barry Orwell
content: ...Disappointment would be easier to bear. I must admit, the city-state needs her strength now. And I also... still hope that what she said back then was sincere.

speaker: Augustus
content: So what if I try to seize power later? Then stand up to me like you are now. Show some backbone against intimidation. Unite and drive me back. It's that simple. That backbone is exactly why I chose you.

speaker: Augustus
content: Have you already forgotten the courage you just showed?
A shared, reflective silence falls between you, solidifying into an unspoken alliance. It's you who finally breaks it, after a long moment.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...I feel the same way.
You recount your observations from the banquet and voice your concerns.
Augustus is, by nature, forthright and passionate; you refuse to believe she would stoop to such underhanded schemes for power. If she had wanted that, she could have seized it long ago.

Yet, you cannot be sure how many sycophants now cling to her, drawn by her influence. These opportunists, with their honeyed words, could slowly corrupt her judgment, blind her to reality, and ultimately exploit her until they drag her down into the abyss.

speaker: Barry Orwell
content: I'll continue my media campaign, speaking frankly and exposing those parasites clinging to her. But as she herself pointed out, that alone isn't enough. I must also find a way to stop her.

speaker: Barry Orwell
content: So please, you must speak to General Augustus yourself. You have considerable influence over her. She admires your integrity. Go to her with those qualities. Warn her. Prevent her from falling into the same traps.

speaker: Barry Orwell
content: Thank you... I hope she'll lead the DisCorps down the right path this time. That is the only way to heal the wounds that divide us.
The communication ends. You sink back into your chair, absorbed in your thoughts. Throughout it all, your visitor, Kane, has been watching you with an unwavering focus.
He is the one who finally breaks the silence.

speaker: Kane
content: I fully understand your position now, Chief. I have several old friends in the Council. When the time comes, an alliance with them will make our work much smoother.

speaker: Kane
content: ...I didn't expect you to be so resolute. Without you, I fear the General would have fallen under their influence much sooner.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Me?

speaker: Kane
content: Oh, think nothing of it. I'm counting on you to persuade the General. If you need any assistance from me, just say the word.

Kane takes his leave. As he goes, he casts repeated glances back your way, his expression that of a man who has staked all his hopes on a single card. And after today's conversation, you have to admit, your own perspective has begun to shift...
[Scene Change]

September 4, N.F. 115, 10:00 PM
Eastside Suburbs, Nameless Bar

Your destination is not a luxurious mansion or a high-society venue, but a secluded old house at the end of a quiet, suburban Eastside street. The area is nearly deserted; the few pedestrians are ghosts in the night, and the lone parked sedan is deliberately inconspicuous.

As you ascend the steps, the door swings inward before you can even knock. A woman of modest yet unmistakable elegance greets you. She seems to have been expecting your arrival, and she immediately begins to apologize.

speaker: Owner
content: I'm sorry, we're closed for the evening. If you could please...

speaker: Voice from Inside
content: Since he found his way here on his own, he deserves a reward. Let him in.
female_content: Since she found her way here on her own, she deserves a reward. Let her in.

content: You recognize that voice. The owner offers an apologetic smile and gestures for you to enter.

Stepping inside is like crossing into another world. Candlelight flickers, its glow refracting through the liquor bottles to cast intimate, colorful patterns across half the room. Vintage music drifts from a mobile terminal, the only concession to the modern era in a space otherwise devoid of electricity—a small sanctuary untouched by DisCity's relentless progress.
The booths, which should be filled with patrons, stand completely empty. The only occupant is a familiar figure seated at the bar.

She wears a floor-length red dress, her long hair flowing over her shoulders. Catherine gently swirls her glass, her expression hidden in the play of shadow and dim candlelight. You approach and take the seat beside her.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I asked Iron Mask where I could catch the <color=#fb9259>second round</color>. He gave me this address. Told me to come alone, keep a low profile. I think I managed.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Not a bad spot at all.

speaker: Catherine
content: Right? It's peaceful. With our reputations, finding a little privacy is a battle in itself.

options: You could've just come to the Bureau.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Last I checked, you said the interrogation room was very private.

speaker: Catherine
content: Please. Your place has ears behind every wall. It's an iron cage. Who'd want to stay for fun?

speaker: Catherine
content: If I ever did set up shop there, I'd have to gut the place first. Give it some actual taste.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: With that metal horse you sent me?

speaker: Catherine
content: Hah. Alright, enough circling. You never seek me out without trouble on your heels. Go on, I'm listening.
As if on cue, the owner serves you the house special. You take a small, deliberate sip, using the moment to collect your thoughts.

options: Do you remember Sernie? Or Wilton?

speaker: Catherine
content: Who?
A smile touches your lips. Whether it's the drink or the vibe, a wave of relaxation washes over you, and you wave a dismissive hand.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Never mind. They're nobody.

options: What about Barry Orwell? Ring a bell?

speaker: Catherine
content: Oh, that daring recording clerk.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: In your current wave of public admiration, his book, The Dark Side of DisCity: Rule of Shadow, was nearly out of print before the war. Now, it's shot to the top of the bestseller list.
Surprise flashes across the general's face.

speaker: Catherine
content: So... congratulations to him?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: "Congratulations"? This wasn't your doing? It's exactly your style, anonymously buying up copies and flooding the districts. You nearly scared the poor clerk to death. He thought it was a threat.

speaker: Catherine
content: Oh come on, he's got a spine! Shouldn't a critic with that much talent find a real audience? I'm sick of all this praise. I needed something with more bite. Let all the bootlickers get a taste of it, too.

speaker: Catherine
content: Want me to send you a copy? Aren't you quite interested in that sort of history?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Already bought it. Let's talk about something else.

options: Discuss official FAC business with her
Actually enjoy talking about anything with her

content: Without a moment's hesitation, you sit beside Augustus and launch into the speech you've been mentally rehearsing, your tone solemn and convinced.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I know all about those people and their real intentions... And I know that you're actually... But when it comes down to it, the point is...

Even you begin to find your lengthy monologue a bit tedious. To your surprise, Augustus—notorious for stirring up trouble—doesn't interrupt. She simply listens, quiet and attentive, before suddenly bursting into unfiltered laughter.

speaker: Catherine
content: Look at you, so serious. You and <color=#fb9259>Adrian</color> are cut from the same cloth.
That name... Is it the Commander-in-Chief?
The conversation flows effortlessly, wandering from her Nirvana Port to your Minos, from WhiteSands to Syndicate. Time slips away unnoticed, the well of topics seemingly bottomless.

speaker: Catherine
content: Heh, quite the talker... just like <color=#fb9259>Victor</color>.
Victor? The name rings a bell from Barry's bestselling exposé.
In her hand, the ornate glass sways gently, its ice cubes clinking a soft accompaniment to the faint smile on her lips.

speaker: Catherine
content: You know <color=#fb9259>Adrian</color>, don't you? FAC Commander-in-Chief, technically your former boss. Let me tell you a secret...

speaker: Catherine
content: He's had that old man demeanor since he was twenty.
She laughs, eager to tell you more.

speaker: Catherine
content: Meticulous and rigid in everything, except when he argued with Dravyn. That's when his voice would hit a new peak. And when those two went at it, only Victor could ever pull them apart.

speaker: Catherine
content: Victor... the legendary messenger who picked up skills from all over. He could speak anyone's language—talk to saints like a saint, devils like a devil. Even the most troublesome soldiers were putty in his hands.

speaker: Catherine
content: With that masterful talent for heart-soothing, if he'd had a shred of malice, the Independence Army would've crumbled from the inside.

speaker: Catherine
content: Dravyn should count himself lucky to have had those two. With that stubborn, radical streak of his, he'd have been a real danger without someone to rein him in.
The General's fingers tap a light, rhythmic pattern against her glass. A certain softness in her gaze suggests the drinks are beginning to take effect.

speaker: Catherine
content: Me?

speaker: Catherine
content: I was in charge of stirring up trouble. Gave them something new to argue about, kept things from getting dull.

speaker: Owner
content: Heh...
A soft laugh escapes the owner. As she collects your nearly empty glasses, she gently asks her most distinguished regular.

speaker: Owner
content: What would you like this time?

speaker: Catherine
content: That's up to him.
female_content: That's up to her.

content: Catherine brushes the triviality aside. Instead, she turns to you, tilting her head as her gaze meets yours, and poses her question.

speaker: Catherine
content: Enjoying the stories? Well, now it's your turn. Tell me about yourself, and the people you keep around. I'm all ears.
The answer rises to your lips instinctively, an almost reflexive openness, but you bite it back just in time.
There is something else, something more important, you need to say.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That day in the interrogation room, you asked why I'd take a mission to investigate you if I wasn't interested in politics.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I didn't have an answer for you then. But I think I do now.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You have a... magnetism. A power to make people feel seen, to inspire loyalty. And that's precisely why I can't ignore the shadows that might lurk beneath.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That "sweet scent of power" you mentioned? To me, it stinks. And it's dangerous. You're too sharp not to see through their depravity. So why entertain them? Are you buying their flattery, or do you have your own game?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The more I respect you, the more it unsettles me. And yet... I remember fighting at your side. A part of me wants to silence these doubts, to prove the general I admire is real.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Even now, tonight... I still hope the Augustus I've come to know isn't a facade. I want to trust you.

options: Instead of becoming your enemy someday.

content: She listens in absolute silence, her gaze locked with yours. The eye contact holds, stretching the moment, before she finally breaks it with a soft, downward smile.

speaker: Catherine
content: That question... is one you'll have to answer for yourself.
She listens quietly, her eyes holding yours. Seeing your unwavering gaze, a fond warmth lights her expression. Then, she reaches over and playfully ruffles your hair.

speaker: Catherine
content: Since you put it that way... fine, I'll indulge you.
And so, that is how DisCity's most illustrious General Augustus spends a peaceful night in an obscure, nameless bar, doing nothing at all.
[Scene Change]
Three days later, you see her again—this time, on television.
[Sound of TV being turned on]

speaker: Reporter
content: General! General Augustus! A moment, please! The rumors say the Shattered Blade is officially relocating to DisCity. Congratulations! Could you share more—

speaker: Catherine
content: Oh? And who told you that?

speaker: Reporter
content: Eh? Well... it's common knowledge by now! It's a well-deserved honor for our war heroes, and something the public has been hoping for.

speaker: Catherine
content: "Honor"? If that's what we're calling it now, DisCity's standards have certainly fallen. You can keep your rewards. My troops and I will find our own fun.

speaker: Reporter
content: Huh... Your mindset seems to have changed, General. Has someone been... influencing you? Could it be the Chief of the MBCC...?

speaker: Catherine
content: Heh. Think what you want. I do have a few friends, and with them around, it's hard for me to stray from the right path even if I wanted to.
[Scene Transition: Back to Chief's Perspective]
As the interview concludes to the sound of audience applause, you switch off the screen. You turn off the screen just as a call from an old friend comes through.

speaker: 9th
content: A positive outcome, it seems. If this encourages General Augustus to settle into her role, it could bring stability back to the situation.

speaker: 9th
content: After all, should another major conflict arise, she remains our most indispensable military asset.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Something about it feels off. She was just performing, playing with the public. All that serious investigation on our end, and she treats it like a game.

speaker: 9th
content: That sounded almost like a complaint between friends. Does she enjoy teasing you in particular, Chief?

speaker: 9th
content: But you can rest assured, Chief. While General Augustus may be headstrong, she is never disingenuous. Her respect for you is entirely authentic. She would never truly deceive you, at least according to my superior.

speaker: 9th
content: Thank you for helping to guide her back, Chief ${PlayerName}.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I had nothing to do with it. That was definitely all an act on her part. Next time we meet, I'll be having a serious conversation with her...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But before that, we have other guests to attend to.
Outside the window, a car swerves through the rain, accelerating violently to cut you off. Then, vehicles from behind and the side slam into position, sealing you in a moving trap.
Through the downpour and the glare of headlights, the dark muzzles of several guns stare back at you.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief!

Your eyes dart, taking in the situation: you're trapped on a high-speed elevated highway. Three hostile vehicles have you pinned from the front and rear. The only possible exit is the guardrail, and beyond it, a sheer drop of dozens of meters.
In that case, there's only one option...

options: Ram them out of the way!

content: CRASH!! The impact shunts the enemy car sideways, grinding it to a halt. Your reinforced Bureau vehicle shudders but holds, while the attacker's hood crumples, engine spewing black smoke.
Their doors fly open. For a final stand or a frantic escape, it's irrelevant. Shadows detach from the darkness, quickly pinning them down.

The Shattered Blade soldiers move with lethal grace, neutralizing the attackers before they can even react. One assassin receives special attention: Iron Mask seizes him by the throat and slams him onto the ruined hood.

speaker: Attacker
content: Easy... I-I was just a hired gun! I didn't know the target, or that they were connected to DisCorps!

speaker: Attacker
content: Please, spare me! I'll tell you everything!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...They couldn't even send professionals? How insulting.
Nightingale's expression, however, is etched with deep concern—not for the present danger, but for what this attack implies about your future safety.

speaker: Nightingale
content: ...Will attempts like this become a regular occurrence?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Let them come. None of them is a real threat. I don't need the Shattered Blade to protect me either. Your efforts are wasted on me. Frankly, for all I know, you might be the ones drawing this trouble to my door.
You shoot a glance at Iron Mask, ready with your usual taunt. But the barb dies on your lips as he remains silent this time.
His body is rigid, a coiled spring, and the surrounding soldiers have fallen into an unnerving silence—their combat stance. Something is wrong.

You track his gaze. A luxury car accelerates from the far end of the road, screeching to a halt nearby. Augustus emerges and strides directly toward you. Her eyes sweep over you, confirming you're unharmed, then shift to her adjutant. Iron Mask is already at attention, his report prepared.

speaker: Iron Mask
content: He wasn't the only target. Of the 11 councilors who voted against the second mobilization, three are now detained on fabricated charges. Also...
female_content: She wasn't the only target. Of the 11 councilors who voted against the second mobilization, three are now detained on fabricated charges. Also...

speaker: Iron Mask
content: <color=#fb9259>Barry</color>, the recording clerk, was attacked at home. He just came out of critical condition.

speaker: Barry Orwell
content: Thank you... I hope she'll lead the DisCorps down the right path this time. That is the only way to heal the wounds that divide us.

Iron Mask passes a comm device to Augustus. A familiar voice crackles over the line. It's the Shattered Blade's doctor, reporting Barry's status. They arrived later than planned, but not too late to save him.

speaker: Military Doctor
content: The assassin was reckless. They were clearly going for the kill.

speaker: Augustus
content: Do we know who's behind this?

speaker: Iron Mask
content: Those who wanted you to replace the FAC. They're panicking since you backed out. They're likely trying to find out who influenced you.

speaker: Iron Mask
content: Wilton, Sernie, and all guests from the banquet two weeks ago are under Siglinde's surveillance. Also, regarding the attempt on the MBCC Chief...

speaker: Iron Mask
content: Of the recent suspicious visitors to the Bureau, the magazine editor <color=#fb9259>Kane</color> is the prime suspect.
—Kane? The same man who presented himself as part of Augustus's opposition, with his cautious probing, his righteous counsel, and his talk of placing his hopes in you?

speaker: Kane
content: Oh, think nothing of it. I'm counting on you to persuade the General. If you need any assistance from me, just say the word.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...What's this about? He came to MBCC with Barry and urged me to speak out against you.

speaker: Iron Mask
content: He was testing your allegiance. Kane is an actor. His public criticism of Augustus is a cover to infiltrate opposition circles, including Barry's. His media outlet is secretly funded by Wilton's group.

speaker: Iron Mask
content: You're unfamiliar with how these vipers in silk suits hunt. We are not.
The iron lump has finally remembered to talk back, but you're in no mood to engage.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So they're systematically identifying opponents and eliminating them? Using these... underhanded methods? And these people are loyal to you? They want you in power? Why?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Wait... If that's the case, did you infiltrate their circles to uncover their real agenda?
You look to Augustus for an answer, but she gives no sign of having heard. The headlights behind her backlight her uniformed silhouette, throwing an immense, long shadow across the ground.

speaker: Augustus
content: Excellent... All these people... Not a single one can be missed.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...What do you want to do?

speaker: Augustus
content: Hmm, did I worry you? My apologies.
Her face remains unreadable, shrouded in shadow.

speaker: Augustus
content: MBCC personnel, guard your Chief well. The shooter was an amateur, but who knows what else is waiting in the dark.

speaker: Augustus
content: Well then, I have matters to attend to and won't be seeing you for a while. Take care of yourself, Chief.

speaker: Augustus
content: When I return, you'd better be in one piece. Understood?
She offers no answer. A contingent of soldiers insists on escorting you back to the Bureau, while the rest depart with her. For a long time afterward, you receive no news from the Shattered Blade.
The first day passes. Then the second. The third. The fourth...
On the fifth day, you finally find your answer splashed across the news.

<i>Early morning, September 12, N.F. 115: Wilton Stewart was abducted from his estate. No valuables were taken, but all transaction records from his associated accounts were illegally accessed.
Early morning, September 12, N.F. 115: Sernie Parker vanished. Paradeisos issued a notice confirming his office had been ransacked, every document seized.
Early morning, September 12, N.F. 115: Kane Diesel's magazine office was violently broken into. Kane himself disappeared, while detailed records of his political funding sources were systematically leaked online.
Early morning, September 12, N.F. 115: Disturbances were reported around the Andohar family estate. Witnesses observed numerous armed forces entering and leaving the property.

<i>All evidence from these incidents points directly to the Shattered Blade that has remained in the city.

2:00 PM, September 12, N.F. 115: 
Catherine Augustus Andohar stormed the city council with her forces and seized control of the entire building.
<i>It is in this moment that the people of DisCity feel the chilling truth: the shadows of the past have returned, shrouding their city once more.

September 12, N.F. 115, 02:00 PM
City Council
At the chairman's podium, Augustus flips through the agenda, glancing at one page, discarding the next. The pages litter the ground around her feet like fallen leaves.
Armed soldiers of the Shattered Blade stand in formation behind her, their weapons raised and trained on the captive councilors.
The sight is eerily familiar.

speaker: Max King
content: Augustus! That's enough!
She lifts her head, her gaze slow and deliberate, finding the Speaker of the City Council. His face is a mask of fury, his own body a shield for the trembling officials he protects.

speaker: Augustus
content: ...Save the heroics, Speaker. They don't deserve it. They're neither your comrades nor noble councilors. They can't even be called law-abiding citizens.

speaker: Augustus
content: These are scavengers. Parasites. The shadows lurking beneath your beloved city are vast. Step aside and let me clean the gutter. You keep your hands clean.

speaker: Max King
content: ...I won't allow it. The war is over. Your emergency powers are revoked. You don't get to bypass the law and execute your own brand of justice!

speaker: Max King
content: You should be DisCity's protector. Drop your blade and return to the order you should be upholding!

speaker: Augustus
content: And I believe cutting out the tumor is the fastest way to restore that order and protect your city-state. My methods are just more effective.

speaker: Max King
content: Your "effective methods" are a slippery slope! Today it's them, tomorrow it's anyone you please! Your violence has no oversight, no guarantee of justice.

speaker: Max King
content: This system—these rules—were built over the years for this exact reason! This simply can't be replaced by violence or individual action. No one's strength, no one's wisdom, is enough for that burden!

speaker: Max King
content: Stop this, General Augustus! We fought side-by-side in the war. I know the soldier you are—honorable, noble! Don't prove the rumors right! Don't stray down this wrong path!
Without a word, Augustus strikes open the iron box at her feet. The lid flies open, and she upends it, scattering a pile of "evidence" before Max King.
It's a collection of intelligence, a dossier of slander. But it is the final photograph—Adrian, pale and still in a hospital bed—that makes his eyes widen in raw shock.

speaker: Max King
content: ...Are you threatening me?!

speaker: Augustus
content: Not me. This is a gift from your many, many "well-wishers." Hoping to help me bring you down.

speaker: Augustus
content: Every single piece of this "evidence" could work perfectly within your precious legal order to democratically destroy you. Ironic, isn't it?

speaker: Augustus
content: The "order" you defend doesn't want a righteous man, Speaker. It prefers someone ruthless and insolent like me.
She borrows a light from one of her subordinates and drops it to the ground. Right before Max King's eyes, she watches the slander curl and blacken into ash.

speaker: Augustus
content: My patience has limits. I've waited. I played the long game. Gathered evidence, filed reports, and delivered it all on a silver platter to the courts.

speaker: Augustus
content: And poof. It vanished. Buried carefully. The witnesses I "exposed"? I had to send my own people to protect them from being silenced... by your "order."

speaker: Augustus
content: You want to know the real tragedy, Speaker?

speaker: Augustus
content: Even after I held my nose and wallowed in their muck... even with the ruthless methods I'm employing now... I still couldn't see the whole picture. I barely scratched the surface.

speaker: Augustus
content: What a vast web... How deep it goes... You've seen the real battlefield of guns and fire. Now open your eyes to the one in the shadows. Where they kill without spilling a single drop of blood.

speaker: Augustus
content: While you cling to your principles, what have our enemies become? Do you really think your sacred, inviolable "faith" is a weapon that can win this war?
His eyes track the photograph as it curls and blackens in the fire, his stare unbreaking. A long silence hangs in the air. Then, his jaw tightens, and he lifts his head.

speaker: Max King
content: I know the corruption is terrifying. I swim in it every day. I know it better than anyone... And so do you, General.

speaker: Max King
content: You want to solve this the old DisCorps way, with brutal, efficient violence to enforce your own will. But you're smart enough to see it. The shadows hold more than one kind of monster...

speaker: Max King
content: Look in the mirror. Marshal Dravyn's shadow is already falling over you. Doesn't that scare you, General?

speaker: Augustus
content: ...You really are as ${PlayerName} said. Upright. Brave. A true comrade. Honestly, I worry a bullet with your name on it is waiting in the wings.

speaker: Augustus
content: The DisCorps might have to keep you on a leash for your own good.

speaker: Augustus
content: Take him away.

speaker: Soldier
content: Roger that!

speaker: Max King
content: You...! Let go of me!!

With the Speaker dragged away, the remaining councilors are a portrait of pure fear, trembling, cowering, faces drained of color. Augustus's focus shifts to an abandoned camera left aside. It shudders, then lifts from the ground, floating on a wave of magnetic energy to stop directly in front of her.

speaker: Augustus
content: ...Well then. It took me years to reclaim my blades. The war with the Outland can wait. A different battle needs fighting first... and I have all the time in the world.

speaker: Augustus
content: Hyenas... maggots... beasts of the Sillage Society. You've trampled lives, stolen the city's noble cause, and manipulated the loyalty of better men and women. You've embedded yourselves like parasites, sucking this city dry for far too long.

speaker: Augustus
content: But now... the troop of ghosts has returned from hell. The time for reckoning is here. And I will see to it... until the end!
Her declaration sets the city ablaze. As the reality of the imminent storm dawns on its citizens, a select few begin to prepare.
[Scene Change]

speaker: Elvira
content: This is what power does to people. She just realized she could use violence, that she could dispense her own justice, and that she could bypass any opposition... so she did. That's the inevitable logic of power.

speaker: Elvira
content: She found the formula to convert violence into authority. And in that, she found what feels like total freedom. Heh. It's Dravyn's playbook all over again... History doesn't just repeat itself; it follows a script.

speaker: Elvira
content: Chief, you need to step back. Your integrity used to be an asset in her eyes, but now it might just be a thorn in her path.

speaker: Elvira
content: Use the goodwill she still has for you. Stay close, and stay quiet. Telling her what you really think now is just volunteering to be her next example. Wait. As long as she's willing to listen to you, there's a chance.

speaker: Elvira
content: If you challenge her directly, I fear you'll be crushed by her, just like the others.
[Scene Change]
Most people feel utterly bewildered.

speaker: Civilian
content: Dravyn's... heir? The stories are true? She's taking power? What were those days even like? Surely Paradeisos won't just stand by and let this happen?

speaker: Civilian
content: They probably will. Paradeisos only intervenes when Mania flares up. As long as the streets are quiet, they don't care who's in charge. Rumor is they've already shaken hands with the General. The Speaker is an outdated concept, after all.

speaker: Civilian
content: ...So what do we do? How long will this last? What happens to us now...?
Only a rare few have not forgotten their anger.
[Badly injured but still raging at the camera]

speaker: Barry Orwell
content: Justice?! Don't you dare call this justice!! This is the raw exercise of power, masquerading as law! If she can shred the legal code to punish her enemies today, she will turn it on any one of you tomorrow! This is not justice; it is the birth of a tyranny!

speaker: Barry Orwell
content: You can hear me, right, Catherine Augustus Andohar?! I will not be your prop! I will not be the "victim" you use to justify breaking our world to your will! I reject your so-called justice! Do you hear me?!

speaker: Barry Orwell
content: You... you hypocrite! You stood where I stand and told me to have faith! You spoke of a better system, of change! So tell me, how are you any different from Dravyn?!
[Cut to EDGE]

EDGE-03: Are we certain intervention is unnecessary? Multiple departments are concerned this could trigger unforeseen social instability.

EDGE-05: Necessary? This appears to be another routine power transfer in the lower levels. There's no risk of triggering a Mania crisis. The structural weaknesses from Dravyn's era won't resurface.
EDGE-05: Moreover, from a purely practical perspective...
EDGE-05: DisCity currently relies on her forces for security, doesn't it?

EDGE-02: Hmm... We have two members here familiar with her. Any observations?
EDGE-02: 01. You must have anticipated this situation.

EDGE-01: Well... Rational analysis tends to prove unreliable when applied to her. The margin for error is substantial.
EDGE-01: That said, I concur with 05's assessment. The probability of a significant crisis remains low.

EDGE-01: Based on intuitive observation, both the duration and impact of this disturbance should remain contained. Wouldn't you agree?
EDGE-01: ...Given your understanding of her.

EDGE-06: ...
EDGE-06: My assessment is irrelevant. Run your own calculations.
[Switch Scene]
But you can't keep up with her.

The Shattered Blade sweeps through the city like a storm of steel; there are simply too many to arrest, too many to process through interrogation. The only way to dominate this new battlefield is with sheer, overwhelming speed.
At her former residence, before the tightly shut doors, only Iron Mask stands guard, as if he has been waiting for you, and you alone.

speaker: Iron Mask
content: She's not here.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: When will she come back? I've been here quite a few times. Knowing her, she wouldn't stay away from you all for long.

speaker: Iron Mask
content: The General is occupied.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The situation is getting very dangerous. She needs to know. If you don't think I'm the right one to tell her, then you should.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You... You're the Rancors. You're Augustus's most trusted allies. It's your duty to steer her right.

speaker: Iron Mask
content: ...You're mistaken. Rancors are not her "most trusted allies." We are her swords, shattered blades, collected from across the world.

speaker: Iron Mask
content: To control a frenzied weapon, a commander cannot show weakness. More than trust or dependence, we need her strength. Unrivaled.

options: And you're not afraid she'll end up isolated?!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Whether they're with the Sillage Society or not, they targeted Barry to deceive her. To isolate her, so they can manipulate her later.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Would you really let your commander charge into the battlefield alone, too stubborn to listen?
Iron Mask remains silent, but his gaze lingers on you.

speaker: Iron Mask
content: We obey our commander, support her, and trust her. Absolutely. As for what you mentioned...

speaker: Iron Mask
content: If you care that much, then you should be the one to do it.
[Switch Scene]
Once more, you return empty-handed. But waiting for you back at the MBCC is a figure you never expected to see.
[Empty Scene for 1 second] Display portrait

speaker: Commander-in-Chief
content: ...The FAC doesn't involve itself in political struggles. What she's doing won't last much longer. This will be over soon.

speaker: Commander-in-Chief
content: But if you still insist on seeing her...

speaker: Commander-in-Chief
content: Then I'll give you these. Just some old things that should have been discarded long ago.
You accept the stack of aged letters. The pages are filled with a script you quickly recognize as an antiquated cipher, a language within a language.
Yet even through the unreadable code, the emotion is palpable—in the angry press of ink that has scarred the paper, and in the stark, familiar signatures that mark each page.

<size=40><i>
—Dravyn

—Adrian
You read through the letters, the silence in the room broken only by the rustle of old paper. When you finish, you lay the stack heavily on your lap before raising your eyes to meet the elder's gaze.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No matter where she's gone, or what she believes now... I'll find a way to reach her. I promise.
[Switch Scene]

speaker: Iron Mask
content: He's been here many times. Are you really not going to see him?
female_content: She's been here many times. Are you really not going to see her?

speaker: Augustus
content: No.

speaker: Augustus
content: We'll talk after this is over.

speaker: Iron Mask
content: I see.
Iron Mask lowers his head.

speaker: Iron Mask
content: But he doesn't see it that way.
female_content: But she doesn't see it that way.

content: A message from the MBCC is presented to her. Augustus accepts it, her eyes swiftly parsing the text within.
<i>I've found a quiet place for the <color=#fb9259>next round</color>. I'll be waiting.<i>
[Scene change] Several days later

September 17, N.F. 115, 09:00 PM
Eastside Suburbs, Nameless Bar
You step back into the bar. The amber glow, the soft melody—everything seems unchanged, yet holds in a new silence. The stool where Augustus sat last time is empty.
This time, the owner welcomes you with a gentle smile, offering a glass of Augustus's favorite cocktail.

speaker: Owner
content: A spark of life returns to their dull eyes. The dying embers of their old dreams reignite, kindling a new flame of hope that spreads among the townsfolk.

speaker: Owner
content: She's always been cautious about her affairs. She finds me directly. Never leaves a thread for me to pull. I'm sorry I can't be of more help.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Sigh, it's strange. She used to pester my office daily. Now the silence is... louder than I expected.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I suppose the great General Augustus is ascending. Soon, she won't have time for old distractions.

speaker: Owner
content: Heh...

speaker: Owner
content: It's only... she was saying something similar not long ago. That "once the war ended, the Chief of Minos became a ghost. A fair-weather friend, tossing allies aside once the fighting's done."

options: My loyalty was never in question.

content: Smiling, she offers you another glass.

speaker: Owner
content: It may not be my place to say, but I believe she keeps her distance precisely because she values the connection so much.

speaker: Owner
content: She's afraid of losing you.
The small terminal happens to be tuned to today's breaking news.

speaker: Augustus
content: Hyenas... maggots... beasts of the Sillage Society. You've trampled lives, stolen the city's noble cause, and manipulated the loyalty of better men and women. You've embedded yourselves like parasites, sucking this city dry for far too long.

speaker: Augustus
content: But now... the troop of ghosts has returned from hell. The time for reckoning is here. And I will see to it... until the end!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...So entangled with all that power. It's a side of her I never had to see.

speaker: Owner
content: But she's also the same hero she's always been.
She stares into the terminal, the candle's flame flickering a silent dance in her eyes.

speaker: Owner
content: ...They're hailed as heroes, but only when the city needs them. They're polished up and put on the front line, a shield against the bullets in the name of glory.

speaker: Owner
content: And when the war is over? The same voices that praised them now cry for "reflection," and spit on the very monuments they built.

speaker: Owner
content: This time, at least, she is powerful. Too powerful to be cast aside. She can now remind them where a hero truly belongs.

speaker: Owner
content: Well... I imagine the general would say...

speaker: Owner & ${PlayerName}
content: "Who? Why should I care?"
You speak in perfect unison, and your smiles lock. As you take another sip of your drink, a pleasant tipsiness starts to wash over you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...I think I understand why she likes this place. Out there, it's all turmoil and chaos. But in here... it's a safe harbor.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If possible, I'd like to become a regular here, too.

speaker: Owner
content: The honor would be mine. And with you here, I'm certain the general would find her way back more often.
A laugh escapes you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Yeah... I have plenty of ideas for how to make her visits "voluntary."
BAM! The door slams open. Augustus stands there, her face livid as she glares at you both.
A furious roar answers you, followed by the deadly hiss of steel leaving its scabbard.

speaker: Augustus
content: Stay away from him!!
female_content: Stay away from her!!

speaker: Owner
content: Argh—!

She flings her sword, guiding it toward you with her magnetic power. On the counter, a dozen bottles of aged liquor shatter, their contents coalescing into several Underground Puppets that lunge your way.
Augustus scans the room for more weapons, but finds only the small music terminal—nothing of the iron or steel that she can command.

speaker: Augustus
content: ${PlayerName}!!!
Your shackles barely deflect the first attack. It's not nearly enough. Augustus still stands at a distance from you, but for her, that's well within range.

You yank the bag from your side and shake it violently, scattering all the "secret weapons" across the floor—bullets, knives, forks, all made of metal. Augustus freezes for a split second, then understands. Her power engages.
The Puppets surge. Two forks hook into your collar, yanking you backward from the assault. You stumble, falling directly into Augustus's waiting arms.
You look up. A few other knives hover in the air between you and the Puppets, holding them at bay.

speaker: Augustus
content: Hold them back! Buy some time!
[Release the shackles]
Your shackles buy you three seconds. Just enough. You feel Augustus's grip tighten, her body tense. Then, a powerful energy explosion erupts.

speaker: Augustus
content: Take them down!
CRASH! A luxury car plows through the wall, instantly crushing three Puppets. Right behind it, a squad of Shattered Blade soldiers storms the ruined bar.

speaker: Soldiers
content: Roger that!
[Action sequence]

The chaos is swiftly subdued. The Puppets are neutralized, their threat extinguished in a flurry of efficient violence. The owner is hauled from the wreckage of her collapsed and contaminated liquor cabinet, her gaze finding you with a desperate plea.

speaker: Owner
content: Catherine... I...

speaker: Iron Mask
content: Take her away.

Around you, the soldiers conduct a methodical inventory of the aftermath: the faint taint of the Underground sorcery, the lingering residue of the Sillage, and the trails of covert communications. Throughout it all, Augustus remains a constant, tense presence at your side, never straying more than a step away.

speaker: Augustus
content: ...When did you know?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: When Clerk Barry was attacked. Your reaction wasn't just about my safety. You were furious that innocent people were getting hurt... and shaken by someone's betrayal.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That's when I realized your anonymous bulk-buying of his book wasn't a joke. It was a shield. You didn't want to publicly endorse him, and this bar was the only loose thread.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm the one who pulled it. I stumbled onto the truth and had no idea how dangerous that was.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And being here just confirms it...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Everything in this place is non-magnetic. She'd rather polish silver than have a single piece of steel. Candles over electric lights. She was never on your side.
You feed her the facts like a steady drip, your voice a firm anchor as Augustus pulls the fragments of her composure back together.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: After Barry was attacked, you figured it out too, didn't you? That's why you never came back... Were you planning to handle her yourself? Did I get in your way?

speaker: Augustus
content: ...If you knew she was suspicious, why come here alone?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I bet that you would come for me.

speaker: Augustus
content: You gambled with your life? Have you lost your mind?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Yes. I specifically gambled that you would protect it.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content:
Even with your power grab underway, you don't want me dead. You don't want me ending up like Victor.
That's good. Because I don't want to end up like Adrian either, slowly pushed out of your life.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Neither of us wants to see you on that battlefield alone. Not like Dravyn.

speaker: Augustus
content: ...That old man. What did Adrian tell you?
You bite back the words—that the Commander-in-Chief called her an arrogant, annoying brat. Some truths are better left unsaid.

The Commander-in-Chief brought letters spanning two decades. They told a story: of two men mourning fallen comrades, raging against betrayals. Then, the gradual emergence of differences leading to the Marshal's complete isolation. Adrian's final, confidential letter never even made it to his desk.

Barry's documentary is incisive, but it's no substitute for the living accounts, for walking the same paths. Only then can you glimpse the true past and peer through the rift into this city's deeper truth.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I used to think the strong craved power. But watching you... I've realized it's not that simple. Power also craves the strong.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Even those in the shadows need a figurehead to clear their path. Those who failed to kill you now covet your influence. They'll try to seduce you, break you, or own you. It's a trap designed specifically for prey like you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You see it, don't you? The same web that caught Dravyn is laid right at your feet. Do you really plan to walk into it?

speaker: Augustus
content: ...Don't underestimate me. There's no web I can't tear apart, no dead end I can't breach.

speaker: Augustus
content: I'm just disgusted by the enemy's shamelessness. This is the most revolting battle I've ever fought.
Augustus's gaze sweeps over the wreckage: the splintered bar, the glittering carpet of glass, the void where the owner once held court. A silent storm of emotions passes over her face.

speaker: Augustus
content: This was a good place. Whenever the outside world sickened me—when I had to stop myself from slaughtering those maggots, when I was in a foul mood and couldn't find you... I'd come here. Have a drink. Chat with her. It helped me breathe.

speaker: Augustus
content: They wouldn't even leave me this one small sanctuary.

speaker: Augustus
content: ...I can't kill her. She's Brock's niece, his only living relative.

speaker: Augustus
content: I held her when she was born. The Independence Army raised her together. Before my cryosleep, she gave me flowers. Her parents were imprisoned for opposing Dravyn... I have to look after her. But more than that...

speaker: Augustus
content: Whenever I grew tired of this new era, I'd come here to remember. It's the last place left from the old days. And those worms found even this... corrupted even her...

speaker: Augustus
content: You see, ${PlayerName}, how clever my enemy is. They flatter me to lower my guard, then target everyone around me to isolate me. They won't even grant me a moment's peace.

speaker: Augustus
content: This is DisCity, the world's glittering peak. A throne of money and power everyone scrambles for. And it doesn't matter who sits on it. Victor, Adrian... Dravyn... it's all the same.

speaker: Augustus
content: ...Quite the battlefield, isn't it? More treacherous than the war you just fought. I intend to win, but I can't keep my hands as clean as you'd like.
The candlelight flickers, and though her face remains shrouded in shadow, you feel you have finally traced the contours of the person within.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The victory the Independence Army bought with their lives was stolen and twisted. Now history's repeating. You can't stand it. You want to crush these enemies, but you're terrified of walking Dravyn's same path... Am I right?
Her silence is confirmation enough.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You've always been a warrior who defies fate. I'm in no position to judge your chosen battlefield... Let's just say I want to understand more.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: As you said, this is the center of the world. It gathers all the wealth, dreams, glory, and filth. It has its own rules. The higher you climb, the darker and more dangerous it gets. It's a suffocating mess.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If a great general plans to break this cycle by carrying the entire city-state on her shoulders... I have to wonder...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Back then, you commanded an army and bore all their suffering and sins. Now you want to command the greatest city-state, which means carrying all its prosperity and corruption... Can one person really bear that weight?
Your eyes have adjusted to the dark, and now you can truly see her. The bloodstained ferocity has drained from her gaze, leaving only a deep, serene blue that lingers in the shadows.

speaker: Augustus
content: ...I can answer that, wise Shepherd. I've asked myself the same thing countless times.

speaker: Augustus
content: I've never feared taking power or stepping onto this shadowy battlefield. I swear I'll be victorious. I won't fall to any enemy, and I won't compromise who I am.

speaker: Augustus
content: But I'm not foolish enough to fight alone. I'll have extraordinary warriors as my mind, my blade, and my shield. And you... you will be my shackles and my scabbard.

speaker: Augustus
content: All of you make me stronger. Far superior to those cowards. Victory will be mine. That's the resolve I bring to this fight.
As she speaks, the serene blue of her eyes slowly churns with a gathering storm.

speaker: Augustus
content: ...But it's all so tedious. So shameless. How can it be this ugly? There are no warriors willing to die for this city, no souls with the resolve to face death without flinching.

speaker: Augustus
content: Nothing but self-serving vultures. No principles, no convictions. Having to maneuver among them... it turns my stomach.

speaker: Augustus
content: This battle isn't worth my passion, and today's DisCity isn't worth my soldiers' lives. Only a stubborn fool like Dravyn would cling to it so desperately, not letting go even at the end.

speaker: Augustus
content: Rather than worrying that power will corrupt me, you should worry I'll lose all patience with this farce and flip the entire board.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...It sounds like you're the one worried you might do that.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: For someone about to charge into battle, you're being unusually cautious. That's not like you, General.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But now I know what I can do for you.
You sit up straight and grasp the empty scabbard she left in your hands.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No one in this world can stop you from fighting. But I hope one day you can leave this battlefield you hate. Let your subordinates or allies win your victories for you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I can't do that for you. I have my own battles to fight.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But I will protect you. If DisCity's blade ever starts to break—if you ever verge on rampage—I will find you. I will stop you. I'll do whatever it takes to make you stand down... even if it means following the path you took when you killed Dravyn with your own hands.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Your sword once cleared a path for me. So from now on, no matter what battlefield you march onto... as long as I hold this scabbard, I won't let you become something you'd despise.

speaker: Augustus
content: ...Heh, well said.

speaker: Augustus
content: What a speech...
She composes herself, rises, and helps you to your feet. After straightening your clothes, she leads you from the battle-ravaged quiet of the bar into the silence of another car.

The engine stirs, and you plunge into the night. No Shattered Blade soldiers follow; this journey is for you two alone. The vast cityscape streams past on both sides, a familiar tableau—just like your first meeting, just like every encounter yet to come.

But tonight, your vision has changed. The dense high-rises no longer just cradle countless lights; they trace the edges of a massive silhouette. It looms like a primordial beast, bearing festering wounds a century old, its body slowly swelling with a breath like the eternal rhythm of tides.

And against this colossal shadow draped across your path, everything else diminishes—the car carrying you, the General's sword, your seemingly resolute promise—all of it shrinks into fleeting smallness, like a sigh dissolving into the wind.
[Scene Change] MBCC
The journey ends where it so often does: she returns you to the familiar grounds of the Bureau, a place that has come to feel like home.
With a final word of farewell, Augustus watches you step out.

speaker: Augustus
content: I have my soldiers, and I will eventually claim my battlefield. But you...

speaker: Augustus
content: A scabbard doesn't need to kill. With you here, the Rancors will never bend, never corrode, never run wild. So... you have to stay alive.

A small smile touches her lips. She takes off her hat and places it on your head, pressing the brim down to steal your vision. You expect this to be like all the times before—her signature prelude to a tease, a final, flippant gesture to lighten a heavy moment.

But this time is different. Blinded by the fabric and shadow, you feel her hand firm on your shoulder, pulling you close. She leans in, and her voice, a low vibration in your ear, is unnervingly deep.

speaker: Augustus
content: ...Stay alive. Whatever comes, you won't have to face it. I promise you that.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Then I promise you, too.

options: Even on different battlefields, I'll be watching.
You have my word. As your scabbard.

content: Is that a smile? You can't be sure. But you feel the brief, telling pressure of her grip on your shoulder before she releases you. Only then does the car pull away, leaving you in its wake.
[Scene Change: Eastside]

The steel storm does not immediately subside. It rages on, a tempest unleashed after years of pent-up fury, scouring the city streets. In its wake, many vanish; many more flee. Only after days of unrelenting terror does the Shattered Blade abruptly withdraw.
Then, some of the vanished are returned to their homes, dazed and silent. Others are found bound at the prison gates. Many bear notes affixed to them.

<color=#fb9259><i><size=40>
"To our gracious hosts, thank you for the warm welcome. I simply had to return the favor with a surprise party of my own.
You all played your parts well. My thanks for the participation.

I'll leave the cleanup to you, the esteemed 'city-state.' I'm sure your experts will know exactly how to handle the legal aftermath."

<color=#fb9259><i><size=40>
"After all... I might just come back on a whim."

speaker: Nightingale
content: The higher-ups have dispatched additional personnel to assist with our workload. It's a significant show of support. We have been given strict instructions to alleviate your administrative burden, Chief, and to ensure you maintain a healthier work-life balance.
Despite your deep bewilderment, you accept the unprecedented directive:

<i><size=40>
Your scheduled duty is limited to 8 hours per day, 5 days per week, with compensatory leave for any overtime.
You are allocated 40 days of annual leave, with permission to be absent when the workload is light.
Oh, and one more thing.
No external department can task you with assignments without proper approval.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Am I dreaming? What kind of prank is this? Who signed off on this... an angel?

speaker: Nightingale
content: ...It's authentic, Chief. We have already begun rerouting several assistance requests from the 9th Agency. The directive comes directly from <color=#fb9259>EDGE</color>.

EDGE-03: Is this really your solution to quell the unrest? An EDGE seat carries significant weight. It must be granted through consensus and with extreme caution.
EDGE-07: The original candidate is already paralyzed with fear. Acting now is damage control. We can't allow her to create greater complications.
EDGE-03: But this is coercion. Her terrorist acts, mimicking Dravyn's methods, were likely orchestrated precisely for this purpose. Yield once, and this tactic will repeat indefinitely.
EDGE-03: We still possess the capability to stop her. For now, at least.

EDGE-02: If you're referring to the shackles, I suggest keeping those two separated. In the current situation, trying to restrain her might result in even SHP-13 being swayed to her side. The cost would far outweigh any benefit.
EDGE-02: The current arrangement isn't so bad, is it?

EDGE-05: Precisely. DisCity requires her protection, and we cannot risk her turning her blade toward the upper echelons at this juncture.
EDGE-05: If she has grown weary of the theater below and wishes to play at our level, so be it. The strategic advantage remains ours.
EDGE-05: Much like when we established the FAC, or reorganized EDGE... would you not agree?
EDGE-05: Besides, 01 still possesses the means to redirect her focus when necessary.

EDGE-05: Have you circulated new intelligence regarding the missing overseas troops again?

EDGE-01: In a manner of speaking.
EDGE-01: However, she also made it clear she has no interest in wasting time with our "pointless deliberations." For her first meeting, she asked me to deliver only two statements on her behalf.

EDGE-08 [Proxy]: The blade has returned, now hanging above your heads.
EDGE-08 [Proxy]: You'd better all watch your steps.
The Dark Side of DisCity: Rule of Shadow [Revised Edition] [Unpublished]

<size=40>Historical analysis indicates the corruption of the Independence Army was a multifactorial process.

Economically, both the demands of warfare against the metropole coalition and the subsequent need to rebuild the city-state under trade blockades required immense capital and resources.

<size=40>Following key military successes, the Independence Army's influence expanded, drawing corporations and wealthy industrialists into its orbit. These alliances provided necessary financial support for the war and initial reconstruction.

Through their involvement in rebuilding, these allied groups steadily consolidated control over the city-state's critical economic infrastructure.
Contemporary records suggest neither Dravyn nor the Army's command possessed the administrative experience to perceive the systemic risk.

<size=40>This, truly, was the origin and root of everything.
Yet, compared to the dramatic political shifts, personal betrayals, and fallen heroes that followed, these mundane economic origins were largely obscured in the historical narrative.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If DisCity's blade ever starts to break—if you ever verge on rampage—I will find you. I will stop you. I'll do whatever it takes to make you stand down... even if it means following the path you took when you killed Dravyn with your own hands.
...Haunted by that person's strange words, Augustus returns home. She seeks solace in the pages of a book, but as she reads, the lines begin to blur, lulling her into a peculiar dream.

?? ??, N.F. 103
Cryogenic Chamber, ???? Laboratory
...It hurts...
Where am I...? EDGE?
Her body was a foreign, leaden weight, and it took a monumental strain of will just to try sitting up.
Ugh, these side effects are bad... That baldy's cryogenic tech is complete garbage... He'd better hope his tech didn't fry a single nerve...
Finally, she managed it.
Outside the cryogenic chamber, there were no researchers or military officers waiting.
Instead, she was met with a sea of blood.
...Did they forcibly awaken me...? What happened?
Is this a battlefield? Where is the enemy? When did the war begin?
Who are you?!

speaker: Iron Mask
content: I'm the new Rancor wielder.
<color=#7683a2><i>...Another replacement?
<color=#7683a2><i>But... he explicitly promised he wouldn't use those again...
<color=#7683a2><i>Did Dravyn send you?

speaker: Iron Mask
content: The Marshal is in a dire situation. He awakened you in hopes you might be of use.

speaker: Iron Mask
content: This is his order to you.
A top-secret directive awaited the awakened one, its encryption a cypher unused since the fires of the Independence War had cooled.

<size=40>[Excerpt 2]
From a contemporary historical viewpoint, Dravyn's political era effectively concluded with the Eclipse Operation in N.F. 103.

The operation was a catastrophic and strategically meaningless defeat, resulting in significant FAC casualties in the DisSea. The public outcry prompted an official investigation by EDGE.
Though it was largely overlooked at the time, the majority of the lost personnel were remnants of the former DisCorps. While Dravyn had previously survived numerous political challenges, the circumstances of this event created an inescapable predicament.

<size=40>Dravyn Steel, then FAC Commander-in-Chief, was politically isolated and subsequently died. The official cause of death was listed as complications from long-term depression. Contemporary accounts speculated it was a suicide driven by despair and the prospect of prosecution. More conspiratorial narratives alleged an assassination framed as a form of retribution.
The consensus among analysts is that for an authoritarian leader of his stature, only death would have compelled him to cede power.

<size=40>However, all these theories are difficult to reconcile with his documented, resolute character. The evidence suggests he was too formidably entrenched to be easily eliminated by external forces.

<size=40><color=#fb9259><i>
The Rancors are yours now. Wage war as you see fit.

<size=50>I only demand victory.
</color></size>
...What kind of order is this supposed to be?
Where is Dravyn?

speaker: Augustus
content: Where is he?!

<size=40>[Excerpt 3]
The Marshal's career reveals a consistent pattern of tactical pragmatism.

Willing to sacrifice conscience and moral boundaries, he pursued victory at all costs, using success to justify every means. This approach characterized the campaign to counter nuclear assault, the suppression of dissenting city-states, and the neutralization of internal opposition.

<size=40>Confronted with an untenable situation, his response was operationally consistent. He authorized proscribed protocols, demonstrating a systematic disregard for collateral damage.
This calculus was applied universally, to adversaries and his own forces alike.
[Enter Flashback]

speaker: Parma
content: What's past is past, Marshal. What you need now... is help. Power.

speaker: Parma
content: So take it. Summon it again. The Sage's power is already in your hands. It chose you once. It won't let you die. Wield it. Defend your throne like you defended your city.

speaker: Parma
content: Where is that conviction now? Weren't you the one who said all power is justified if it serves your cause? Look at yourself, trapped, desperate... Isn't this your only option?

speaker: Parma
content: ...You said you refused to surrender, didn't you? So then... why hesitate? Heh heh... heh...
[Exit Flashback]

<size=40>[Excerpt 4]
Did no one try to stop him? The historical record suggests otherwise.
One does not achieve such stature by acting entirely alone against all counsel. A hero forged in the fires of the Independence War could never have been a mere isolated fanatic.

<size=40>And indeed, he was not alone. There were many who stood with him.
Shared ideals brought them together; a common enemy united them; collective suffering forged their bond.

But then victory arrived. The hardships ended, the enemy scattered, and the founding ideals were, on the surface, achieved. And with that, everything changed.

<size=40>We see the first fractures: internal division and collusion with the old power structures. The parasites of the former regime taught these new heroes how to feast, subtly pulling them into the same corrupt currents.
Those who refused to partake were methodically removed.

Victor was the first to fall, a man of political genius but no military skill, cleverly reassigned to the front lines where he "perished in combat."
The opposition chose their target well; without his unifying influence, the military's integrity began to crumble.
The steadfast Adrian held his principles to the end, but what was the purpose? A loyal advisor, once stripped of trust, is rendered useless.

<size=40>As for his family...

All eyes inevitably turned to the Steel family. Each member represented a potential vulnerability, a point of pressure. They shared Dravyn's blood, but few, it seems, could share his formidable vision or his resolve.

speaker: Schorl
content: Greetings, General Augustus. Your vitals indicate severe stress from the forced awakening. For your physiological stability, I must insist you return to the cryogenic chamber.

speaker: Schorl
content: Please rest assured. The city-state's security architecture remains optimal. Our military assets have been successfully realigned toward catastrophe prevention, and lingering societal instabilities are being systematically resolved. Progress is incremental, but with a more powerful EDGE, we will guide it to the correct path.

speaker: Augustus
content: It was you... you used him. You repurposed the entire DisCorps under the guise of catastrophe prevention, consolidating your control... The FAC program was just another one of your schemes...

speaker: Augustus
content: You set him up as a figurehead, stripped him of any real power, and then spent nineteen years backing him into a corner!

speaker: Schorl
content: Violence and power are a mechanism, not an objective. All actions have been calculated for the preservation of the collective. The DisCorps restructuring was a necessary measure. I regret that more optimal solutions were not computationally viable. But regarding Marshal Dravyn...

speaker: Schorl
content: He was provided with multiple viable paths. The one he selected led to his own termination.
Magnetic force erupted with her fury, pinning Schorl. The black triangle jerked and spasmed against her unyielding grip.

speaker: Augustus
content: Stop hiding behind this cold, logical garbage! Show yourself and face me! COME OUT!!

speaker: Schorl
content: Logically—bzzt—this interface is no different—however, if a familiar form facilitates your compliance—
Despite its reluctance, EDGE complied with her demand, projecting the face of someone familiar before her eyes.

speaker: EDGE-01
content: Hello, General Augustus. It's been thirty-one years since we last met.

speaker: Augustus
content: What happened after I went under? In N.F. 84... No, even before that... what happened between you? How did it all come to this?

speaker: Augustus
content: Were all the oaths we swore back then just... a pile of bullshit?!
His smile was a cold, detached thing, utterly foreign to the one she knew.

speaker: EDGE-01
content: I posed that same question to him once. I no longer trouble myself with such concerns.

speaker: EDGE-01
content: I recommend you also de-prioritize these concerns. Technical and logistical support remain available to you, should you require it.

speaker: EDGE-01
content: Or... would you prefer if I called you little Catherine again? Would that help soothe your emotions?
A blue light flashed, and in its wake, both his projection and the black triangle unraveled, vanishing without a trace.
[Scene Change: FAC Interior]

<size=40>[Excerpt 5]
Dravyn was not personally motivated by material gain. However, years of suppression by the metropoles fostered a deeply ingrained DisCity-centrism, a strategic vulnerability that proved highly exploitable.
The interests standing behind him, seeking to wield his authority for resource acquisition, consistently provided him with rationalized justifications for their campaigns.

<size=40>
In the era before the DisSea Explosion, the cause was the liberation of metropole colonies; this was used to legitimize the suppression of city-states that resisted DisCity's hegemony.
Following the explosion, the threat of Mania became the new justification, with the argument being that since DisCity had borne the primary impact, all of humanity was obligated to support its lead in combating the catastrophe.

<size=40>Consequently, with the commander's own focus shifted, the institution that revered and followed him was inevitably corrupted in turn.
It must be remembered that the former DisCorps was a highly systematic and methodical apparatus—a perfect machine for the dissemination and amplification of its leader's ideology.

<size=40>
The sword that a power forges for external dominance will, in time, be turned inward.

speaker: Lieutenant
content: General Augustus... Do you remember me?

speaker: Lieutenant
content: I see... Not as Lieutenant... but by my real name. I... I'm honored, General. And ashamed.

speaker: Lieutenant
content: This is the sword you entrusted to the Major. Now, it should return to your hands. The Eighth Division... I'm the only one left. Returning this to you is the only purpose my survival has left.

speaker: Lieutenant
content: What is our next objective, General? A civil war? Just as Marshal Dravyn said? Or are we to bleed another city dry, all to fund his political purges? How many more must we kill?

speaker: Lieutenant
content: ...I apologize, General. That was insubordinate. Seeing you again... it brought everything back.

speaker: Lieutenant
content: It makes no difference... Civil war or campaign, just give the order. Tell me who to kill. I can no longer hold a gun with pride anymore, but fighting for you... that I can still do.

speaker: Lieutenant
content: Seeing the fire still in your eyes, General... It's a relief.
[Scene Change: Cabinet Meeting Room 2]

<size=40>[Excerpt 6]
Is history unjust? One cannot help but wonder, watching the endless repetition of malevolence.

<size=40>
And yet, history possesses a certain grim fairness. Those who dare to abandon Justice... often find themselves collectively condemned, cast into the abyss.

<size=40>
But who, in the end, is fit to deliver the final verdict?

The young general finally reached the old commander's throne. The audience hall stood vast and empty, a void of such scale it bordered on absurdity. The round council table of her memories, with the many chairs that had once surrounded it, was gone. Only the solitary seat of authority remained.

The old man upon it was as motionless as stone. It was only the sound of her footsteps that made him stir, his body trembling slightly as he turned toward the young figure before him, awakening from his long trance.

He was awake now, but his face was so aged she barely recognized him. In the years unknown to her, Dravyn seemed to have borne the weight of mountains. The man who was once iron-hard and formidable now sat with a broken spine beneath his burdens.

speaker: Dravyn
content: ...You're late... I didn't teach you to keep a battlefield waiting...

speaker: Augustus
content: ...How did you get so old?

speaker: Dravyn
content: Me? Heh... I don't even remember what I looked like before old age claimed me.

speaker: Dravyn
content: You, on the other hand, look exactly as I remember.

His clouded eyes, sunk deep in wrinkled furrows, trembled unsteadily before they slowly, painstakingly found their focus on the young general. He studied her in silence for a long moment before he finally spoke in a hushed voice.

speaker: Dravyn
content: Has it really been that long...

speaker: Augustus
content: Why did you wake me?

speaker: Dravyn
content: I woke you...? Ah, yes... because we agreed to...

speaker: Dravyn
