content: When the shadow of war returned... you would be the blade to meet it. To bring us victory.

speaker: Dravyn
content: That time is now, Augustus... War is at our doorstep again. Defeat the enemies. Bring back victory, for me. Only you can do it.
Augustus remained silent for a moment before speaking deliberately.

speaker: Augustus
content: What war? DisCity is thriving. Its satellite town network is a deterrent. No foreign power would be so foolish.

speaker: Augustus
content: Dravyn... what war are you talking about?

speaker: Dravyn
content: It's here. In this very city... The battlefield is everywhere...

speaker: Augustus
content: Then point me at your enemy. Where are they?

speaker: Dravyn
content: Where aren't they...? Beyond this room... everyone. Everyone is the enemy. Can't you see?
His eyes widened slightly, staring into some unseen distance. His hunched frame leaned forward slowly, as if his very soul were being drawn out, and his gaze filled with a bitter, consuming hatred.

speaker: Dravyn
content: The enemies I thought I'd defeated... they just changed their faces after the war. Those I believed were my allies... once they left the battlefield, they put on new masks.

speaker: Dravyn
content: They smile to my face, and the moment my back is turned, they plot. All of them. Just waiting for a crack in the armor, a sign of weakness. They don't want to serve this city; they want my chair.

speaker: Dravyn
content: And the people... short-sighted, foolish, greedy, selfish! So easily led to break what they should be protecting... And assassins?? The Eclipse Operation's failure is my fault? We built this city from ash and sacrifice. And this... this is their gratitude?!

speaker: Dravyn
content: Is this my judgment? Or this city's? After all I've sacrificed to hold it together... what is the purpose of this... this Mania?

speaker: Dravyn
content: Oh yes, of course, I've known all along. That too is part of the enemy's conspiracy...
The old man continued to mumble incoherently under his breath.

speaker: Dravyn
content: The Underground Mania, the shackles, the Shepherd... All lies. Waving a flag for "humanity" while they send my last loyal soldiers to die... burn my bridges...

speaker: Dravyn
content: EDGE has fallen... into their hands, corrupted by those depraved hounds. Even... even he has turned...

speaker: Dravyn
content: Or... was it always <color=#fb9259>his</color> plan...?

speaker: Dravyn
content: It was him all along... All that talk of fighting catastrophes, building the FAC together... Hah. Noble words. A disguise. It was just a slow, deliberate transfer of power. A trap to erode my authority!

speaker: Dravyn
content: He called himself a scientist. Said he understood my vision!

speaker: Dravyn
content: We had an agreement. To correct our errors. He said there was still time. For <color=#dg1f1f>nineteen years</color> I compromised. I trusted him. And this is when he moves against me?! <color=#dg1f1f><size=44><i>Then he will regret it!!</color></size><i>

speaker: Dravyn
content: This is MY DisCity. I took over the command, and I'm not giving it up. The victory I want will come, one way or another!

speaker: Dravyn
content: Augustus, I am the one who woke you! So take up your blade and cut down every last one of my enemies! Go! Forge more glory!

speaker: Dravyn
content: Only the shock of victory can crush these scheming vermin. Only undeniable strength forces obedience. Seize that victory; it is your purpose!

The aged marshal grew more fervent with each word, his voice swelling as if chasing the ghost of his former glory. He leaned forward, eagerly extending a hand toward Augustus, his sole audience member in the empty hall.
But he was met with utter silence.

speaker: Augustus
content: ...But this is not a war.

speaker: Augustus
content: What you're asking me to do is just clear the path, for you and you alone.

speaker: Augustus
content: You only want my blade to guard your throne.
Her answer was swallowed by a wave of unhinged laughter.

speaker: Dravyn
content: HAHAHAHA! Since when did an Andohar preach to me about justice? Do you think I don't know who you really are?

speaker: Dravyn
content: You were born in a metropole. Your house built its fortune on war. Your loyalty was never to a flag; it was to war itself. So why not fight for me? I am giving you a battlefield of your own. Isn't that what you've always wanted? That has never changed!

speaker: Augustus
content: ...You're right. No one has my loyalty. And I don't fight for banners...

speaker: Augustus
content: But did you give that same order... to my soldiers?

speaker: Augustus
content: When you asked them to trust you, ordered them to die for you, did they know what they were really dying for?

speaker: Augustus
content: If Victor were here... what would he say?
He fell silent. Did that name still hold meaning for him? Did he still remember the comrades who had once pulled him back from the abyss?

speaker: Dravyn
content: Victor was murdered... I am avenging him.

speaker: Thank you, I'm feeling fine... May I ask where Miss Stewart is?
content: And Adrian? You stripped his rank yourself. You cast him out.

speaker: Dravyn
content: Was he ever loyal? He always challenged my authority. Stood against me like a stone wall when I needed him most. That man... that bastard... he became an enemy long ago.

speaker: Augustus
content: Who told you that? Your inner circle? Lapdogs who only know how to pledge loyalty? Or just a bunch of... bootlicking sycophants?

speaker: Augustus
content: Do you really believe their loyalty? Or just the lies that comfort you?

speaker: Augustus
content: Where are all those eager voices now?

speaker: Dravyn
content: The ones I could trust are all dead!!

speaker: Dravyn
content: You've never held command. You've never sat in this chair. You've never seen a real battlefield! Those enemies are undying ghosts... they can't be routed, can't be purged, more persistent than war itself...

speaker: Dravyn
content: This war permits no innocence, but they refused to see it! Adrian, Victor... neither of them could understand!

speaker: Dravyn
content: For this city—for all we've sacrificed—if I fail now, all those people's deaths will mean nothing! This is necessary! Can't you see that?!

speaker: Augustus
content: ...I don't see it. And I don't want to. Haven't you already left behind what was truly necessary?

speaker: Augustus
content: Those who give their lives for DisCity must not be betrayed by it. Those who fight for you must not be abandoned by their commander.

speaker: Augustus
content: Brock entrusted you with the Independence Army. He told you to remember. But look around now, Dravyn...

speaker: Augustus
content: Who's still standing by your side?
A long silence settled between them. Augustus held the old marshal's gaze, watching as the final embers of passion guttered and died within his eyes.

speaker: Dravyn
content: ...I see. So you, too, will stand against me...

The old man turned away and shuffled back toward the hall's only remaining chair. This was the commander who had once been the very embodiment of invincibility in her eyes. How could he have been reduced to this? How could a figure of such power become so diminished?

speaker: Dravyn
content: It seems... even you believe I've already lost...
Dravyn seemed to have aged years in moments, again, left with nothing but two things to which he desperately clung:
The dilapidated chair that only resembled a throne, and the Mania Rancor in his hand that was never a true blade to wield.
He clutched them as if they could anchor him, but time surged anyway, a torrent rushing through the spaces between his fingers.
[Flashback 1]

speaker: Augustus
content: Take care of my troops. They're my pride.

speaker: Dravyn
content: You have my word.

speaker: Dravyn
content: It doesn't matter. At least you still understand me... For victory, I would pay any price. Bear any burden.

speaker: Dravyn
content: I will not yield... I will not allow DisCity to fall to <color=#fb9259>them</color>... This blight upon the city, this rot threatening my command... I... will not... abandon this post... I will not retreat...

speaker: Dravyn
content: Even if I must stand alone...
[Flashback 2]

speaker: Augustus
content: Well then, goodbye. I'll be waiting for the day I wake up.

speaker: Dravyn
content: I'll be waiting for that day too.
Mania spilled from his gun barrel, unfurling like crimson petals and injecting his withered frame with a deceptive, frenzied vitality.

With this, Dravyn Steel descended into madness, fully merging with the Rancor. He was the second commander of the Independence Army, Eastside's first democratically elected Speaker, and the founder and first Commander-in-Chief of the FAC. He was the sole hero who had led DisCity from nuclear devastation, and in Andohar's eyes, its most tenacious and obsessive warrior. Now, he was none of these things, and he was mad.

In his final moment of lucidity, his gaze drifted down from his perch, and he recognized the figure before him one last time—just as he had futilely tried to distinguish friend from foe for the past thirty years.
<i>Ah... it's that brat. She's back... Well then... he should at least force a smile.

speaker: Dravyn
content: ...I should have woken you sooner... but back then...

speaker: Dravyn
content: I believed I could give you a better world...

Dravyn stood upon his throne as he always wished, transformed into a weapon, and left before him the sharpest general of the Independence Army—the one he had personally summoned back from the past—now slowly raising her sword against him.

speaker: Augustus
content: ...Then why don't you just come back... you old jerk...
It was not a difficult battle.
It did not take long to kill a hero in his twilight years.
Augustus walked out of the hall alone. The sun had just dipped below the horizon, its final afterglow staining the distant sky.
Yet she could no longer tell what time of day it was, or even what year.
[Scene Change: Street]
Walking through the streets, she saw the same crowds who had once lined the roads celebrating victory and praising heroic soldiers now angrily demanded peace and justice, calling for a reckoning.

speaker: Civilian
content: My grandfather was just an innocent Outlander, and you killed him! You ****ing murdered him!! Don't you dare hide behind your DisCorps uniform and call yourselves heroes! We know what you did! You're not soldiers; you're butchers! Go to hell!!

speaker: Civilian
content: All this time... we lived beside them. We broke bread with them. To think such monsters were walking among us... I can't... I can't bear it. How do you live next to a demon?!

speaker: Terrified Civilian
content: Stay back! Get away from me! Please... don't kill me!
[Scene Change: Banquet/Hall]

Walking through the grand halls, she recognized the same parasites who were supposed to have been expelled by the Independence Army. They had merely changed their skins, and there they were, still clinging to the top. These were the ones who, after seizing a precious blade, had instigated wars for profit and slipped away unscathed. And now, they raised their glasses in celebration of a new era.

speaker: Upper-Class Guest
content: A toast! To the final exorcism of the old era's demons, and to the unequivocal correction of past errors! With the city-state firmly back on its proper course, we can finally usher in a future of stability and progress. An era of peace, led by our own steady hand!

speaker: Fraser Caravan
content: Of course! A new dawn has arrived. Let peace line our pockets, and prosperity build our legacy! To wealth, and to a future where business can truly flourish!
[Scene Change: Base]
Back on the battlefield, the soldiers she had once taken pride in were still there, waiting for her.

speaker: Despairing Soldier
content: General... is it really you? All these years... What happened to us? Tell me I wasn't wrong. We had to fight. DisCity... it would have fallen without us, wouldn't it?

speaker: Despairing Soldier
content: They told us... the enemy was at the gates! That the whole world wanted the Hypercubes we had. We were just securing resources... pre-empting the threat. People die in war; it's a cost we've accepted! I did it for our home... for our city-state! What was I supposed to do?!

speaker: Despairing Soldier
content: So then... was it wrong? Was I wrong? When did it... change? Or... was it always like this? Have I just been... a murderer all along?

speaker: Despairing Soldier
content: Then why did they pin medals on my chest?! Why did they call me a hero?! You were the ones who told us! That to fight for DisCity was the highest honor! That to kill for its future was glorious! I didn't—! I never wanted this! Not like this!!

speaker: Despairing Soldier
content: General... I only ever wanted to serve my city-state. Now... after all of it... is there really nothing waiting for me but hell?

Their glory was erased, their faces awash with confusion, helplessness, fear, and shame. The once-sharpest blades had proven the most brittle; those who had burned their lives for their beliefs now watched as those convictions shattered at reality's slightest touch, crumbling to dust.

So easily broken, so thoroughly abandoned, they were left to rust on meaningless battlefields. They were swallowed by the very war they served, living a fate worse than death, rejected even by hell itself.
What are you fighting for?

speaker: Scarface
content: It wasn't like that, Lily... Your brother's no murderer. I'm a soldier. A hero... It was the only way to keep you safe... Everything... it was all to keep you safe...

speaker: Scarface
content: GYAHAHAHAH!! Yes!! A hero!! Anyone who lays a finger on you deserves death! Every last one of those bloodstained hounds will die!! Those rabid dogs will never get near you!! Not even me!!!
Why are you broken?

speaker: Military Doctor
content: ...I don't need vindication, treatment, salvation, or anyone's forgiveness. There's only one thing I want to know...

speaker: Military Doctor
content: General, will you return to the battlefield? Are you still going to hunt those bastards down and make them pay?

speaker: Military Doctor
content: I will follow you with my Rancor to the ends of the earth, and we will slaughter every last one of them.
Why can't I die?

speaker: Lieutenant
content: ...Why do you still try to save me? What's left to salvage in a demon?

speaker: Lieutenant
content: Death would be a mercy. Just let me bear my punishment! I carry hell with me wherever I go anyway!
Why can't you just come back...?

speaker: Iron Mask
content: The Marshal said that if he fell, I was to follow you. That you would seize victory for him.

speaker: Iron Mask
content: ...I know you will. He had waited long enough. Bring him the true victory he was owed.
Victory? What kind of victory?
She had been awakened merely to officiate a funeral, one that felt far too long, arriving after her thirty-year absence.
A funeral for the very ones she had once believed were unbreakable.
[Grave]

speaker: Augustus
content: We said when I woke up, I'd either help him fight his wars or give him a proper send-off.

speaker: Augustus
content: ...Never pegged the old grouch for the sentimental type.

speaker: Commander-in-Chief
content: The Eclipse Operation did cripple the Underground, but the Mania spread is irreversible. Paradeisos has ordered me to take command of the FAC. But one man is not an army.

speaker: Commander-in-Chief
content: Will you stay? The Commander's title is yours if that's what it takes.

speaker: Commander-in-Chief
content: After all, countless good soldiers have died to protect this city-state. Brock was one. Dravyn was another.
City-state... Before her slumber, this word could stir the blood of countless people. Now, it failed to cause even the slightest ripple in her heart.
Augustus lowered her head, her gaze falling upon the name etched into the tombstone.

speaker: Augustus
content: Old man... you served him longer than I did. You knew the man he was...

speaker: Augustus
content: Tell me... what changed him into this?

speaker: Augustus
content: Was it Mania? That same crystal flower that took Martin, Tom, Joe, Vennon, and his entire squad... Did it finally claim him, too?

speaker: Augustus
content: Or was it that Undergrounder, "Parma"? Did he put a curse on him?

speaker: Augustus
content: Tell me... where should I point my blade? Who is my enemy?

speaker: Commander-in-Chief
content: Dravyn was not a man to be broken by Mania. No matter what changes, every choice he ever made, in his eyes, served a single purpose. And he never regretted it.

speaker: Augustus
content: Heh, you're right... The man was as stubborn as rust. All he cared about was protecting DisCity.
She tilted her head back without a word, her gaze fixed on the sky—or perhaps on the colossal form looming beneath it—for a long, silent moment...

speaker: Augustus
content: ...So in the end, he was defeated by this... great city-state?
Adrian jolted alert, his hand flying to his gun.

speaker: Commander-in-Chief
content: ...When I accepted this rank, I accepted the duty that comes with it.

speaker: Commander-in-Chief
content: Do not force my hand, Augustus. Do not make me your enemy.
Those words drew the first hearty laugh from Augustus since her awakening.

speaker: Augustus
content: Hahahaha... Relax, old man! What's a general without her blade? I can't even make sense of the last thirty years. Now's not the time!

speaker: Augustus
content: Those soldiers shipped off to the farlands for "resource acquisition," the people fed lies about justice and honor... and the units deliberately transferred to weaken the DisCorps...

speaker: Augustus
content: After DisCorps fell, they were abandoned too, weren't they? How many units? Where are they? How many still draw breath? I'm going to find them back.

speaker: Augustus
content: My precious Reapers... shattered, rusted, and scattered to forgotten corners of the world. I won't let them wait in vain... I will find every last one, and bring them home.

speaker: Augustus
content: And then...
The razor-sharp edge returned to her eyes.

speaker: Augustus
content: I'm not you, Adrian. This isn't my city-state. I don't pledge to flags or thrones. My loyalty is only to the blade in my hand.

speaker: Augustus
content: When I return, this city-state had better give me a reason to stand down. If it doesn't... you'll need every gun you have to stop my blade from claiming what it owes.

<size=40>In late N.F. 103, Catherine Augustus Andohar—General of the Eighth DisCorps Division and the Independence Army's most elite soldier—abandoned DisCity. Her forces were a shadow of their former selves, their supplies nearly exhausted.

<size=40>The fracturing of DisCorps awakened old ambitions in the farlands. Enemies who had long coveted the city-state began to stir once again, and three years later, they succeeded in detonating a catastrophe at the world's very heart. The war that followed was brief, ending in a year, but it left in its wake the enduring blight of the Black Rings and catastrophes that scarred the globe.

With the end of the Marshal's iron rule, history's shame and glory were buried together. Grand ideals were dismantled, replaced by the seductive rallying cries of those now in power. Society found its solace in pleasurable apathy and decadent revelry. Under the glow of the Black Rings, madness marched steadily toward death.
<size=40>But Augustus no longer cared.

<size=40>She had forsaken the city-state. For over a decade since, she and her loyal subordinates have walked only the brutal, bloody path of warfare—far from prosperity and light, on a perpetual expedition toward hell.

speaker: Rancor
content: ...Are you going to stop us or judge us? Haha... Salvation? Where can we return to? A soldier's lover is their enemy!

speaker: Rancor
content: Bloodlust is glory, violence is justice, ignorance makes us unyielding, and hatred... hatred is the finest quality of all! It ignites our blood, circulating endlessly... endlessly! It is my eternal life! Brat, do you dare defy me?!

speaker: Rancor
content: Then strike me down, crush me, defeat me, destroy me, kill me countless times! Let the slaughter forge you countless times until you wield our remains to slay your enemies! Your strength is what we seek. Come!
[Slashing Effect]

This was the fate of the mightiest soldiers. For their convictions, they wielded the Rancors to kill. And when those beliefs were shattered, they were devoured by the very blades they carried, becoming mere instruments of war. Augustus conquered them. She tamed them. But more often than not, when she could not save them, she broke them all and laid them to rest.
They were beyond salvation. So many were beyond salvation. And this cursed funeral was nowhere near its end.

speaker: Dravyn
content: They don't understand... You don't either... not yet... but...

speaker: Dravyn
content: When you truly hold power, when you reach the summit... on that day, you'll be no different...

speaker: Rancor
content: If you come for me, if you wish to save me, then bring us redemption through war! Comfort us with the blood of the enemy! Fight for vengeance, fight for DisCity! Or...

speaker: Rancor
content: Tell us who your enemies are, and we shall fight for you!!

speaker: Rancor
content: Take us with you, General. The Rancors desire you. Take us to hell back to the battlefield!!

speaker: Dravyn
content: ...Do not come back...

speaker: Dravyn
content: Catherine... never... come back...
[Empty scene for 1 second, fade to black, then sudden screen flash]

speaker: Augustus
content: ...That's only you! Pathetic losers!

speaker: Augustus
content: I swear, no matter what enemy I face, once I step onto the battlefield, I will not retreat. I will not falter. I will not surrender. I will rise every time I fall—until victory is won, or I meet a glorious death!

speaker: Augustus
content: I. Will. Never. Become. You!!!

She charged headlong into the abyss, her mortal legs wading through swamps of flesh and blood. Let the shadows of war envelop her. Let the frenzied souls of the dead tear at her flesh. This was what she had been born for!
Lost time could not be reclaimed, so she pursued death itself to recover the fallen. She had awakened now, and this time, she chose her own battlefield.

speaker: Augustus
content: Soldiers of DisCorps who were abandoned and have lost your way... let your Rancors shut up and listen to me.

speaker: Augustus
content: From this moment, I am your only commander. You will follow my orders, and mine alone. You will fight only on the battlefields I choose.

speaker: Augustus
content: And in return... I will bear the weight of your sins. I will chart your path forward. I will restore your glory.

speaker: Augustus
content: You will not be asked to compromise your duty. You will not be ordered to make pointless sacrifices. You will have your justice, your honor, and your win. All of it. Every battle you fight under my command will be honorable, with not a single blemish on your victory!

speaker: Augustus
content: ...My exploited, broken, abandoned soldiers... Your hell ends now. Come with me. It is time to return to the world of the living.

speaker: Augustus
content: My blades—in victory or defeat, in life or in death—will always be human.
<color=#7683a2><size=40>The general plunged into hell, while history marched on regardless.

<color=#7683a2><size=40>Perhaps her blade would carve a path to power's pinnacle, reclaiming glory through violence.
Then, like all who came before, she would have that very strength corrupted, her iron will hollowed out, swinging her blade against the chaos until she finally fell from her throne.

<color=#7683a2><size=40>Perhaps her conquest would cower the dead and smother the embers of past wars.
But for the hatreds sown too deep to root out, she could only conquer on. Every land she crossed would be stained by her influence, as she herself became stained with blood.

<color=#7683a2><size=40>Or perhaps...
The general would fall in battle, lost on the road home, meeting the same meaningless end as the countless souls she had once reaped.

Born for war, to die in battle would be the most fitting and natural conclusion—before her strength could carve a path into even greater torrents.

<color=#7683a2><size=40>Or maybe...

Perhaps someday, in a distant future, by the slimmest chance imaginable...
<color=#3877E0><size=40>Even one who had lived an entire life by the blade would meet a truly unremarkable end.
[Cemetery] (Return to present day)

speaker: Augustus
content: Heh, I came back after all, you old bastards. Angry enough to climb out of your graves?

speaker: Augustus
content: Now that everyone's here, I can show you something good.
For years, the names of the two previous commanders have rested in silence upon their tombstones. As she looks up, a faint gray silhouette emerges from the short distance, moving toward her.

options: I came to see the blade that returned.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I heard that an exceptional weapon is priceless. It only stays sharp because it's cared for.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Still not broken yet? Need any tending?

speaker: Augustus
content: Don't worry. Everything's fine.

speaker: Augustus
content: Now the blade can finally return to its scabbard.
Thunder rumbles within the dark clouds. Rain pours over Eastside, sending the city into a dreary haze.

Police lights flicker beneath the shadow of the trees before the manor. Reporters have completely surrounded the place, cameras in hand. At the center of it all, a middle-aged maid is being escorted into a police car.
Through the jostling crowd, you catch the eye of a frazzled-looking sheriff.

speaker: Sheriff
content: You're late, Chief. The maid's already confessed.

speaker: Chief
content: I read the report on the way. I'm only here to confirm the situation. This makes three cases now, doesn't it?

speaker: Sheriff
content: That's correct... Shipping tycoon Porto, banker Leighton, and now young Humbert. All of them died under bizarre circumstances, yet in each case, someone came forward immediately with a confession.

Strange cases have been cropping up across Eastside recently. Last month, shipping tycoon Porto suffered brain death due to a malfunctioning nutrition pod, and the resuscitation failed. Banker Leighton, on the other hand, died of a heart attack after mistakenly ingesting NSAIDs.
As for this case, which occurred early this morning, the Humbert estate owner's only son was found dead in his bathroom. A garter stocking was pulled tight around his neck.

speaker: Chief
content: The ones who confessed... do they all have grudges against the victims?

speaker: Sheriff
content: Porto's gardener had a daughter who was used as a test subject for his nutrition pods. Leighton's chauffeur had a son who was driven to jump off a building over debt. As for today's case...

speaker: Sheriff
content: Years ago, young Humbert drove after drinking and killed a college freshman in a hit-and-run. Due to damaged surveillance footage and the reported vehicle being stolen, the police never pressed charges.

speaker: Chief
content: And the victim was that maid's only daughter.

speaker: Sheriff
content: Precisely. She confessed to the crime without hesitation. Strangely enough, though, she refuses to reveal how she did it, no matter what we ask.
Technically speaking, none of these cases fall under MBCC jurisdiction, but...

Something feels off. The victims in all these cases were wealthy elites with long histories of committing vile acts, none of which were ever brought to justice. The perpetrators were all people they had wronged, and somehow, each one devised an incredibly sophisticated plan to bypass security and got close to their targets...
As if they were following a <color=#fb9259>script</color> someone wrote for them.

You step into the bathroom. It seems there should be crystal chandeliers hanging from each corner of the ceiling, but right now, one lies shattered, and another spot is empty. Freshly starched shirts and aprons are scattered across the floor along with some undergarments.
Honestly, at first glance, this could easily pass for the scene of an accident. But then, you catch a faint glint in your peripheral vision as you examine the area once more.

speaker: Chief
content: This is...
[Scene Change: A Room, Night]

Click. A woman flicks on an old floor lamp as she enters, casting a dim, amber glow across the room. The air carries the scent of aged paper, beeswax, and the faintest fragrance of bitter orange flower.

Strange collectibles can be found on the desk—butterfly specimens, acorns, and several worn dice. A well-thumbed book bound in dark red leather lies facing down. A slender hand picks it up, fingertips trailing across the words on its pages.
A chandelier, fishing lines, and a perfectly timed accident... Not a bad piece of work, wouldn't you say?
The wind stirs the curtains. An uninvited shadow appears in the room.

This, however, doesn't surprise her. She slowly closes the book and returns it to the shelf, then reaches for a crystal wine glass. She then leisurely pours wine into the empty glass, all while smiling in the direction of the shadow.
A visit at this hour... Did you come to share a drink with me before bed? My dear detective, ${PlayerName}.

Looks like there's no point in hiding anymore. You step out from the shadows and seize her slender, delicate wrist in one swift motion. Since she is holding the glass with that hand, the wine spills, just as expected.

speaker: Chief
content: This time, we'll be having a chat at the Bureau, <color=#fb9259>Clementine</color>.

In the interrogation room, Clementine sits with perfect composure, not showing even the slightest hint of discomfort. Two cups of hot tea have been set on the table between you. Through the rising steam, a faint smile plays on her lips.

speaker: Clementine
content: It's been a while, ${PlayerName}. You look terrible. Have you not been sleeping well?

options: You have no clue how much time I spent looking for you.

content: The last reported sighting of her came from the surveillance team stationed outside Clementine's home. She vanished within the burning Mania, and shortly after, news of the Redwood arsonist's death broke out.

speaker: Chief
content: After we parted that day, Banbury Manor caught fire under unknown circumstances. Charles Banbury, the "Carl" from your book, was confirmed dead in the flames.

speaker: Chief
content: The Redwood fire case was reopened, and the investigation resumed. The Public Security Bureau followed the trail and uncovered numerous old cases that had been suppressed in the same way. I promised you I would see the investigation through to the end, that I would deliver justice for everyone...

speaker: Chief
content: But you broke your promise.

You've spent so long worrying about her. This reunion really should be a touching one, but seeing her sit across from you now, acting as though nothing happened at all, you can't help but feel extremely annoyed.

speaker: Clementine
content: Now, now, there's no need to look so stern. Why don't we talk about something more interesting?

speaker: Chief
content: The only thing I'm interested in right now is the final step of your vengeance.

speaker: Chief
content: How did you kill Carl, and how did you escape the fire? What have you been doing all this time you've been missing?

speaker: Clementine
content: Hehe... What are you talking about? Didn't the authorities already state that it was an <color=#fb9259>accident</color>?

She clearly has no intention of telling you what really happened that day—not how she dealt with the assassin, how she breached the layers of security to reach Carl's residence, how she ended his life...
Nor how she vanished in the sea of flames, letting the fire consume every trace of evidence.

speaker: Chief
content: So even you didn't expect to make it out of that "accident" alive?

speaker: Clementine
content: Yup, it was just a stroke of luck. An old friend came to my rescue, so I barely made it out. I just wanted to give myself a little vacation for once to rest and recover, since I'm always being hounded by deadlines. That's not so strange, is it?

speaker: Clementine
content: You should try to relax every now and then too. Investigating cases can be interesting, but don't let it become an obsession.

speaker: Chief
content: That's ironic, coming from someone who always writes protagonists that eagerly throw themselves into trouble to solve other people's problems.

speaker: Clementine
content: True. And in the world of stories, good people are always rewarded. You're much like one of those lucky protagonists who were blessed by fate.

speaker: Chief
content: I'll have you know that there was no such thing as fate or good luck. Accidental fires are dangerous, and that artificial rainfall cost me three months' worth of salary.

speaker: Chief
content: I'm putting this on your tab. Don't even think about running off before you've paid me back.
Clementine looks both surprised and amused. She raises her teacup and gently clinks it against yours.

speaker: Clementine
content: Thank you, ${PlayerName}.

speaker: Clementine
content: I knew you're one to keep your word. I trusted that... Even if I'm not around, you'd still honor our agreement and see the investigation through to the end.
She leans forward, her gaze clear and filled with genuine curiosity.

speaker: Clementine
content: But I'm still curious about something, Chief. How did you find me?
test
test
test
test
test
test

speaker: Chief
content: These cases weren't originally under my jurisdiction, especially since all the suspects seemed to have a death wish. They all confessed to their crimes on the spot.

speaker: Clementine
content: If that's the case, the cases should have been closed right then and there.

speaker: Chief
content: You seem to have forgotten that I've been a devoted reader of yours for quite some time now. The medical malpractice case, the drug poisoning case, and now this stocking murder case... Shouldn't they all seem rather familiar to you?
You flip through the case files and stop at a photo of the crime scene from the stocking murder case.

speaker: Chief
content: Here—there's a thin fishing line strung between the chandelier hook and the ventilation window handle.

speaker: Chief
content: Those lights may look nice, but they're notoriously unreliable. If one breaks, another's bound to follow. When someone finishes using the restroom and opens the window to air it out, the stocking would come falling down along with the fishing line.

speaker: Chief
content: Most people would assume the clothesline goes on empty hooks, but what if it was attached to that light instead? What if that light was only held to the ceiling by that single rope?

speaker: Chief
content: When the victim stood up to open the window, the rope went slack. The chandelier came crashing down, its falling weight yanked the stocking upward, and then—
You mimic the motion of a neck snapping.

speaker: Chief
content: The method is identical to the one in that old book on your desk, no?

speaker: Chief
content: I joked about how some of the methods in your books were practically a how-to guide for criminals, that you've probably had a hand in Eastside's rising crime rate... but I never imagined you'd actually get directly involved in helping them.

speaker: Clementine
content: It seems you've been quite devoted to your research. To think you've even read my earliest work.

speaker: Clementine
content: But... what if they're simply a fan of mine who used a method I'd written about? Would that make it my responsibility still?

speaker: Chief
content: If that were all, I probably wouldn't have suspected you so quickly.
You spread out the case files. Red circles mark numerous sections across the pages, with lines connecting clue to clue, mapping out a series of crimes.

speaker: Chief
content: Every suspect in these cases is an ordinary citizen from the lower class. At first glance, they appear to have no connection to the victims, but upon investigation, it turns out they'd all been wronged by the deceased. After exhausting every legal avenue with nowhere to turn, they resorted to murder.

speaker: Chief
content: Even so, their targets were heavily protected. Given these suspects' limited means, they should never have been able to get past those defenses...

speaker: Chief
content: ...But they succeeded anyway. I've met with them, and nearly every single one of them used methods far beyond their own capabilities. They carried out their vengeance with remarkable sophistication.

speaker: Chief
content: The timeline starts shortly after you disappeared and runs up until last week. What made them all choose to act within this specific window? Can that really be a coincidence?
You press Clementine, but she remains unfazed.

speaker: Clementine
content: It's just a coincidence, of course. There wouldn't have been enough time. Even I need considerable effort to craft such sophisticated crimes in my novels.

speaker: Clementine
content: But if you insist on pinning this on me...

speaker: Clementine
content: Perhaps Redwood gave them hope. They realized that injustice is only addressed when it becomes a scandal. Taking such desperate measures isn't so strange given their circumstances, wouldn't you say?
For a fleeting moment, you catch what looks like a sly glint in Clementine's eye. However, in the next instant, her expression returns to one of detached indifference.

speaker: Clementine
content: Why couldn't it be a miracle of love? Maybe that gave them the power to achieve vengeance against all odds?

options: Alright then, is this also a coincidence?

speaker: Chief
content: You can dismiss everything I've said so far as speculation, but how do you explain this?
You pull out a slightly creased card and hold it over the teacup on the table. After a moment, a string of numbers appears on its surface.

speaker: Chief
content: The maid had a card sewn into her collar. If it hadn't been exposed to the steam, no one would have ever found this hidden message.

speaker: Chief
content: Once is a coincidence. Twice, however, is proof.

speaker: Chief
content: Blank cards like this were found at every crime scene. The method used to reveal them appeared in your novels, and they all contain your contact information. That's when I knew for certain that you're alive, and that you're the one orchestrating these three cases, Clementine.
The room falls silent.
After a long pause, soft applause begins ringing.

speaker: Clementine
content: You're as sharp as ever.

speaker: Clementine
content: Through observing the scene alone, you managed to reconstruct the methods used. Most importantly, you found decisive evidence, leaving the mastermind with no room for denial.
Her cavalier attitude irritates you.

speaker: Chief
content: Why use this method to help people get vengeance? I don't understand, there should be better methods available.

speaker: Chief
content: I'll see Carl's case through to the end, and I won't give up on any of these either. Even if they're not related to Mania, I can still help investigate and vindicate these injustices.

speaker: Chief
content: Why do you find it necessary to force yourself, and all those other victims, down the path of crime? I—

speaker: Clementine
content: Pray tell, then, Chief—what exactly can you do?

speaker: Clementine
content: You might be able to help them track down the criminals and expose the crimes. But you know as well as I do that those bastards, who deserve the death penalty, will keep getting shielded by their connections and walk away with a slap on the wrist.
Her smile vanishes completely in the face of your questioning. The warm atmosphere of your reunion dissipates in an instant, as if it had never existed at all.

speaker: Clementine
content: Public opinion can be manipulated. The truth can be buried. And even if a conviction is secured... retribution would fall on those poor souls who dared to resist, long before the perpetrator walks free.
She leans back in her chair and tilts her head up slightly. The steam clears, revealing a hollow, emotionless gaze.

speaker: Clementine
content: DisCity is vast, and there are more souls holding grievances than anyone can count. Not everyone can make it to your office door, much less survive long enough to see justice done.

speaker: Clementine
content: The Redwood case alone took ten years. How many decades can ordinary people afford to lose?

speaker: Clementine
content: Besides... think about our current situation. You're not just here to catch up with me, are you? Someone ordered you to find Carl's killer. Oh, and to apprehend the mastermind behind those three cases.
You're left speechless. Everything she said is true.
Seeing this, Clementine's voice softens, regaining its gentle warmth.

speaker: Clementine
content: I'm sorry. I didn't say all that to condemn you.

speaker: Clementine
content: Quite the contrary, in fact. I very much admire your sincerity and integrity. You possess something beautiful—something I stopped believing I'd ever see again long ago... Your very existence brings hope to those still struggling in the dark.
Clementine reaches out, her fingertips brushing across your cheek tenderly.

speaker: Clementine
content: But not everyone seeks the light.

speaker: Clementine
content: That's just how this world is. There are good people like you who charge ahead stubbornly, no matter how battered and bruised you get... and then there are utterly irredeemable bastards like Carl.

speaker: Clementine
content: But most ordinary people are caught in between. They're too kind to avoid being trampled, but too powerless to fight back.

speaker: Clementine
content: There are people you and the law cannot help... so I'll help them instead.

speaker: Clementine
content: Hatred can only be dispelled by blood. Just passing judgment on the villains isn't enough, considering how much they've lost.

speaker: Chief
content: Have you thought about the consequences?! This is nothing more than mutual destruction! Their lives will be completely ruined afterward—

speaker: Clementine
content: Their lives were already ruined.

speaker: Clementine
content: After everything they've been through, do you really think they can just go on with life as if nothing had happened?
Clementine's voice sounds distant. She's talking about others, but you hear something deeper in her words—a profound grief.

speaker: Clementine
content: They have nothing left but hatred and rage.

speaker: Clementine
content: Those who come to me are all like that. That's why they're willing to step into my stories, take up the blade, and become its protagonist.

speaker: Clementine
content: For them... this is the only way to live.

speaker: Chief
content: ...And then what happens?

speaker: Clementine
content: Hm?

speaker: Chief
content: Criminals need to serve their time and atone, but life goes on. What happens after they're released? How are they supposed to live the rest of their lives?
"What choices will they have then?" The words almost slip out, but you stop yourself.

speaker: Clementine
content: What happens after? The fact that even an outsider like you, Chief, can feel the anguish of the characters in this story... I think that shows it has served its purpose well enough.

speaker: Clementine
content: As for me...
Clementine's smile turns distant. She's sitting right across from you, yet she feels impossibly far away.

speaker: Clementine
content: Imprisonment, punishment, whatever it is, go ahead and follow your procedures. Don't worry. I knew the risks when I made my bet.
[End of Interrogation - Scene Change]
The interrogation ends. Clementine admitted to assisting the suspects in all three cases, yet you feel no satisfaction whatsoever.
You open the comms.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, did the interrogation go smoothly? You look troubled.

speaker: Chief
content: The interrogation went about as I expected. Clementine is willing to accept the consequences, but she's not truly repentant. Given her current state, we can't let her leave the Bureau, much less hand her over to the Public Security Bureau.

speaker: Chief
content: Nightingale, keep a close eye on Clementine's condition. Pay special attention to anyone she might be in contact with, and monitor her behavior when she interacts with the other Sinners.
After giving Nightingale instructions, you sit alone in your office, anxiety still gnawing at you. You open the recording again—the one you've listened to countless times already.
Ma'am, you've been drawing quite a bit of attention lately. This doesn't seem like your usual approach.

speaker: Clementine
content: You mean before I "died"?

speaker: Clementine
content: Give me a little more time. A sudden death takes its toll, even a staged one.
Time... of course. We've always valued talented partners, but we also value those who know when to exercise restraint. That is the foundation of a lasting partnership.
We simply expect satisfactory results. Don't keep <color=#fb9259>her</color> waiting too long.
You've lost count of how many times you've listened to this conversation, yet some of the words and tones in it still leave you deeply unsettled.

The person in the recording must be the old friend Clementine mentioned—<color=#fb9259>the Sillage Society</color>, an organization that operates in the shadows of the city-state. They were the ones who gave Clementine Mania, the power to exact her revenge, and now they're inviting her to plunge into the abyss alongside them.
The society is trying to recruit Clementine, yet she's hesitating for once.

She vanished, only to reappear out of nowhere, and then she used these acts of revenge as a message to show that she's still alive. But why? Is it a cry for help? Or is she really just doing what she claims... enacting justice in her own way?
[Flashback]

speaker: Clementine
content: Their lives were already ruined.

speaker: Clementine
content: They have nothing left but hatred and rage.
[End of Flashback]
Clementine's novels are still on your desk. Both the popular and obscure ones. Were the people in her stories really just characters meant to serve a tale of vengeance?
[Flash portraits of the train passengers from the main story]

You turn to the case file at your side. The victim list for the Redwood arson is painted in stark red, while the survivor column holds only a handful of names. And even those were buried in WhiteSands years ago, leaving Clementine as the only one left.
Perhaps the person whose life was destroyed, who has nothing left but hatred and rage... is Clementine herself.
You can't let her fall to the darkness. You have to do something.
You can only hope it's not too late.

Two weeks later
Somewhere on the outskirts of Eastside
The car leaves the city, winding through overgrown paths before finally coming to a stop in front of a dilapidated building.
You step out and open the door for her, but she remains seated. Despite her attempt to hide it, the surprise on her face as she takes in the view outside doesn't escape your notice.

speaker: Clementine
content: Is this your idea of punishment?

speaker: Chief
content: Call it a surprise. Spoiling it ahead of time would ruin the fun, wouldn't it?

This is the site of the old Redwood Orphanage. The ruins sit in silence atop a low hill. The fire has left the building unrecognizable—bricks and stone are showing through crumbling walls, and the gaping hollow windows look like empty eye sockets, staring out into nothing.

speaker: Chief
content: The crimes of Carl's family are still being looked into. There might be new leads here that the search team overlooked.

speaker: Chief
content: I think you can help with this. Consider it a chance to make amends. Can you accept that?

speaker: Clementine
content: The MBCC certainly has an unconventional approach to discipline. Haven't I already told you everything you needed to know?

speaker: Chief
content: It wouldn't hurt to go over it again, would it? Think of it as field research for your new book. I heard you've been gathering material lately.
Clementine steps out of the car. For a brief moment, nostalgia flickers in her eyes. Before long though, her composure returns, that practiced smile sliding back into place.

speaker: Clementine
content: My, keeping tabs on me, are you? Did that child called Wynn tell you that? Are you helping her press me for my manuscript?

speaker: Clementine
content: A seasoned author works at her own pace. You don't need to worry about my progress, Chief. Besides, aren't we here on business?
She won't speak unless asked, and when you probe, she acts surprised. Clementine keeps everything locked away inside, all while maintaining that unbothered facade.
Without another word, she turns away and walks toward the ravaged building alone.
You hurry after her, signaling the security detail behind you to spread out. If there are any traces of the Sillage Society, they'll alert you immediately.

speaker: Chief
content: Ever since the Banbury family fell, many have been eyeing this land. The redevelopment plan is being voted on right before the Eastside residents. There shouldn't be any issues this time.

speaker: Clementine
content: That means this place will be torn down, huh...

speaker: Chief
content: Yes. This is your last chance to go inside.
Clementine closes her eyes. Years of rain have carved streaks down the charred walls, like tears running down a face. She gently traces them with her fingers.
After a long moment, she looks up. Birds are flying peacefully above the trees overhead.

speaker: Clementine
content: The smell of smoke... is gone. Aside from the fire, will anyone even remember what happened here?

speaker: Chief
content: If you're willing to talk about it, I'll make sure to remember. Anything goes.
You seize the opportunity, but she merely gives you a quiet smile and a knowing glance, as if she'd casually cast a line and baited out your true intentions just like that.
You make a quick recovery, keeping your expression serious.

speaker: Chief
content: This is also for the investigation. You were there, so you'd know more about Redwood Orphanage than any of us.

You expect her to dodge the question again, or perhaps throw you another puzzle and watch you struggle for answers. However, all she does is pause for a moment before walking straight toward the desolate, debris-strewn foyer.
[Scene Change: Interior]
Clementine's steps are light as she spreads her arms wide, just like a gracious host would when welcoming a guest into a home she's lived in for years.

speaker: Clementine
content: This was the reading room. Annie would play with her teddy bear here. The shelves were filled with fairy tales donated by kind souls, and there was a bean bag chair in the corner.

speaker: Clementine
content: The filling was buckwheat. On sunny days like this, we'd take it outside to air it out. It smelled wonderful—like a wheat field at harvest.
It is indeed sunny today. You can almost smell the scent she's describing.

speaker: Clementine
content: Come, feel this.

Clementine takes your hand and guides it to a series of notches carved into the doorframe at varying heights. There are markings beside them, but they've long since faded. You glance at her questioningly.

speaker: Clementine
content: This is where we'd measure everyone's height. It was an annual tradition, and the children always looked forward to it.
You trace your fingers along the marks. The highest line on the doorframe barely reaches your chest.

speaker: Clementine
content: The orphanage was always short-staffed back then. I was the oldest, so I helped look after the younger children too.

speaker: Chief
content: It's hard to picture what you were like back then. Did you put on a stern face to keep everyone in line, or did you run around and play with them?

speaker: Clementine
content: A bit of both. Some thought I was too quiet and serious. Others said I was full of clever schemes and good at getting people to do what I wanted.
She leads you to a side room. This must have been the kitchen. The stove beneath the window is covered in a thick layer of ash, and a few small bowls sit stacked beside it.
Clementine crouches down, moves the bowls aside, and taps the floor. She quickly locates a hollow brick and lifts it onto the stove.

speaker: Clementine
content: With this brick, any of the older children could climb right through the window.

speaker: Clementine
content: There's a small grove just outside. On nights when the moon was bright, we'd sneak out. Since we're pretty much in the countryside, we could go fishing, catch rabbits, or head to the nearby campgrounds for bonfire nights.

You gaze at the small patch of blue sky visible through the window. For a moment, you can almost see young Clementine, bathed in moonlight, perched on the windowsill. There, a world of wonder and freedom lay just beyond her reach.

speaker: Clementine
content: Now you know what kind of child I was.
She narrows her eyes with that signature half-smile of hers. You can't help but smile back.

speaker: Chief
content: The caretakers never caught you?

speaker: Clementine
content: A few times, they did. When too many of us tried to sneak out at once, the old Director would stand right here in her faded blue apron. She'd tell us to slow down, and not to kick up dust into the bowls.
Clementine stands behind the door, her toes lightly scuffing at the ashes on the floor.

speaker: Clementine
content: But that one time... only that one time, she told us to run faster.
[Flashback Filter: Fire Background]
She turns around and takes a deep breath. You wait quietly, giving her space.

speaker: Clementine
content: Well, I've told you enough about this place. Let's move on.
She beckons to you and starts moving forward once more. You pass through the ash-gray main building and reach the courtyard.
[Scene Change]
The sun is blinding. She suddenly stops in the shade. Before you lies a scene of vibrant life—a stark contrast to the desolation you've seen so far.

The old tree in the courtyard is split. One half is grotesquely charred and has withered, while the other is bursting with new life. Its branches sag heavily toward the ground, nearly concealing an old tire that once served as a swing.
Clementine leads you beneath the tree, pushing aside the thorny branches. The soil is soft, so she was able to dig up a metal box with ease.

speaker: Clementine
content: It's still here, just as I thought.

speaker: Clementine
content: A time capsule. We read about them in a book and decided to bury one. We promised to come back and open it together when we grew up.

speaker: Chief
content: You going to open it?

speaker: Clementine

You push through the torrents of Mania surging from Clementine, inching closer and closer until you finally grasp her hand.

speaker: Clementine

Mrs. Jones is the queen of the Redwood Kingdom, the grumpy William is a kindhearted police officer who struggles with words, the mischievous Alison is an enigmatic mage, and the young adventurers each possess their own special talents.

speaker: Clementine

<i>The days that followed felt surreal. Almost like someone had pressed a fast-forward button.

The orphanage was gone, naturally. The case was stated to be an accident, but that figure from that day haunted Clementine's thoughts, robbing her of sleep night after night.

People came in droves—angry, pitying, morbidly curious... Their gazes would inevitably drift toward her, meeting her eyes before awkwardly looking away.

<i>She seemed to have matured overnight, yet she was still so young. So powerless.

The adults sought the truth behind the fire, boarding a sand ship called the Praeva, and then... they never came back.

Clementine was an orphan once more.

<i>Justice and law could no longer be trusted. If she wanted to find the truth, she would have to seek a different way.

And so, she began weaving stories once more.

She created countless false names and identities for herself—a fallen Eastside noble, a private detective who specialized in dirty work, a smuggler with ties to the black market.

Through these disguises, she slipped into the underworld and slowly began to uncover leads.

<i>A name from the list of the orphanage's former sponsors.

An organization concealing the darkest secrets buried in the depths of Eastside.

They profited off of and covered for each other. To them, both human lives and money are but numbers. There were countless more tragedies like Redwood, all swept under the rug.

<i>But those forces were too deeply entrenched. Someone as insignificant as her could never hope to touch the true culprit. She nearly lost her life just trying.

Then, in her darkest hour, someone extended a hand.

She had already lost everything. So even if the price was her life... it would still be worth it, wouldn't it?

She picks up her pen once more—not to weave fairy tales for children, but to pursue vengeance. She becomes the characters in her own stories, spinning webs with her words to ensnare her prey.
But sometimes, in her dreams, an endless road would appear.

At first, the surroundings are familiar. There are the friends and mentors she sees regularly, her editors at the publishing house, the streets she knows, her home, the shops and restaurants she frequents.
She walks faster and faster, almost breaking into a sprint, while a distant voice echoes endlessly in the back of her mind.
Run faster. Faster!
Until everything falls into silence and darkness spreads without end. The voice grows louder, clearer. It's Clementine's own voice.
Run faster—save the children trapped in those rooms before the flames swallow the hallway.
Faster—chase them down, they're just by the wall near the flames. You could have caught the culprit right then and there.
Run faster. Faster. Grab the Director's sleeve at the dock, muster the courage to ask just one more question. "Where are you going? What are you going to do?"

Clementine stumbles forward, step by step, until her fury burns to ashes and her guilt erodes to sand. In the end, even pain itself grows numb. Nothing remains but dying embers and fading sparks.
She continues to burn in defiance, walking forward, as the world around her turns hollow and pure...

speaker: Chief
content: You don't seem surprised about Outland having its own special shipping manifests... Tell me, why would a corporate leader who insists they've never been involved in such things seem so unsurprised, and on top of that be able to tell the manifest is fake?
Eirene narrows her eyes and glances at you.

speaker: Eirene
content: You tricked me?

speaker: Eirene
content: Looks like we're the same kind of people... We would do unscrupulous things in order to achieve something...

speaker: Chief
content: I only dare to speak to you like this because... Councilor Enoch told us a couple of things when he found out we were investigating this.
Eirene shows a hint of panic but quickly returns to how she was before.

speaker: Eirene
content: That voice recorder was given to you by Enoch, right?

speaker: Eirene
content: That's right. Quinn does have some dealings with Outland, but they all... happen under the authorization of Councilor Enoch.

speaker: Eirene
content: If you can find the real shipping manifest, you'll see Enoch's stamp all over it.

speaker: Eirene
content: That does not indicate that I directly trade with Outland.

speaker: Eirene
content: The goods moving between Quinn and Outland have to be inspected by Enoch before they are released.

speaker: Eirene
content: Why?

speaker: Chief
content: When we requested to inspect the cargo, Councilor Enoch was so nervous that we had to bring up the name of the 9th Agency to continue with our inspection.

speaker: Eirene
content: Sigh... I guess name-dropping the 9th Agency does work miracles.

speaker: Eirene
content: Enoch probably gave you the recorder to safeguard those goods... I never thought I'd be the one sacrificed some day.

speaker: Chief
content: So let's be open about it, Miss Eirene.

speaker: Chief
content: Enoch has handed three shipping channels to Quinn, which correspond to three different Outland states.

speaker: Chief
content: He didn't just want to transport Hypercubes; he wanted the DisCity to trade other industrial products with Outland as well.

speaker: Chief
content: To support Outland, the DisCity usually asks them to trade the equivalent production materials or household goods.

speaker: Chief
content: But during this investigation, it's been found that the metals used for trading... seem to be unsatisfactory both in terms of weight and density.

speaker: Eirene
content: Fraser City's precious metal salvaging operations have always been hazardous and luck-dependent. It's normal to have some margin of error.

speaker: Chief
content: Regretfully, Enoch's camouflage is not convincing enough.

speaker: Chief
content: DisCoins of the same weight can be considered as a precious metal too in a sense. Am I right, Miss Eirene?

speaker: Chief
content: Besides the DisCoins, we found something else that's interesting.

speaker: Chief
content: After Enoch handed over the freight channels to Quinn, Quinn suddenly raised its tax rate by 5% and actively took part in various charitable activities.

speaker: Chief
content: Meanwhile, in the Fraser City shipping manifest, the Campbell family's tax income on the goods was lowered by 5%.

speaker: Chief
content: That means that each month, Fraser City has 5% more money for various purposes, including the military...

speaker: Chief
content: Coincidentally, that year saw an abnormal trend in desert bandit activity in the unruled areas in WhiteSands. It heightened tension with the DisCity.

speaker: Chief
content: Do you still insist it's a mere coincidence, Miss Eirene?

speaker: Eirene
content: Looks like you've done your homework.
Eirene sighs and leans back weakly.

speaker: Chief
content: Quite a lot actually, and it means we have a very high regard for your ability.
Hearing your praise, Eirene smiles coldly.

speaker: Eirene
content: My ability...?

speaker: Eirene
content: Relying on myself and my so-called special ability alone, it's impossible to build a business empire like Quinn.
The interrogation room falls silent after Eirene said that. As the dust in the shimmering light is about to come to a standstill, she opens her mouth again.

speaker: Eirene
content: Quinn has infiltrated many aspects of the DisCity, be it the economy, daily life, technology... and even defense.

speaker: Eirene
content: But all of this is thanks to the "help" of my father, Bryce Campbell.

speaker: Eirene
content: Besides him, who else could possibly create a business empire in such a short period of time? Not even his own daughter will be able to do it.

speaker: Eirene
content: My father had me build a business empire in Eastside. He wants to turn Eastside into his own supply warehouse...

speaker: Eirene
content: He asked me to tamper with the freight trade. He even told me who to bribe.
A bitter laugh that seems like a sigh comes from Eirene. She props herself up and leans back in her chair with a lonely look.

speaker: Eirene
content: Perhaps you're not aware, but Enoch is the only person I bribed based on my own judgment without listening to my father, and he ended up being my downfall.

speaker: Eirene
content: I was not unaware of the danger these things would bring to the city and myself.

speaker: Eirene
content: But... I had no other way. I couldn't come up with a better way.
Eirene averts her eyes and stares at a tile under her feet.
The strong woman at the peak of Eastside's business empire is currently showing signs of vulnerability.
She's like a canary that escaped the cage but couldn't break free from the chains on her feet, landing here helplessly.

speaker: Eirene
content: My father used every available means to ascend to the position of the current head of the family in only eight years.

speaker: Eirene
content: And amongst those means was his own family... I was able to survive, but probably only because I once had a close match with him in chess.
Even you have heard Bryce Campbell's name here and there. His methods are described in the intel at great length.
The master of a city with a fearsome reputation. But who would've thought he would be this vicious to his own daughter?

options: Why don't you try to break free from his control?

speaker: Chief
content: Now that you're in Eastside, you should have plenty of opportunities to do so.

speaker: Eirene
content: You think I haven't tried?

speaker: Eirene
content: I tried, and I realized it's safest being a pawn.

speaker: Eirene
content: So what?

speaker: Eirene
content: Even now that I've awakened as a Sinner, he does not show a shred of fear.

speaker: Eirene
content: He would only tell me that now I have the ability to open up Syndicate's market as well.

speaker: Eirene
content: In the hands of those gangs lie a significant number of resources.

speaker: Eirene
content: So what...

speaker: Eirene
content: Would you really use such a terrible power against your own father?

speaker: Chief
content: Even though he threatened your life?

speaker: Eirene
content: In this father-daughter relationship, I'm the only one being soft-hearted.

Eirene's confession means that the largest business in Eastside and its related conglomerate capable of intervening in the Hypercube industry... are colluding with Outland. This is no trivial matter. You decide to suspend the interrogation and take some time to think.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Do you believe her words?

speaker: Nightingale
content: Then why did you...?

speaker: Chief
content: What I don't believe is her objective... Even if Bryce has such a long reach, having been in Outland for so long, it would be impossible for him to control Eastside completely without any flaws. But she said that everything was orchestrated per her father's instructions...
You look at the DNA test report at the bottom of the pile. It was intended to be your trump card against Eirene's lies, but now it seems a bit pointless.

speaker: Chief
content: She's smart. I don't believe a Sinner of that caliber would get manipulated that easily. Even if it's her father.
You think for a bit before including the interrogation in the report and immediately sending it to the 9th Agency.
Your report clearly points out the danger of Bryce and the need to investigate since he can manipulate even a Sinner. There may be a hidden force comparable to Sinners backing him.

Moreover, you believe that since Eirene voluntarily disclosed the truth, she stands to defect. You apply for a permit for the Sinner to go outside, wishing to take Eirene back to Fraser City with you.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, the permit to leave has been approved. You may take Eirene...

speaker: Nightingale
content: What's this?
Placing a pile of documents on your desk, Nightingale immediately notices that transparent chess piece.
Eirene sent it. I think it belongs to a chess set.
The rich sure are obsessed with these exquisite objects.
The chess piece made of transparent crystal is reflecting a dazzling light. Though it looks a bit bizarre, you're able to appreciate it somehow.
You pick up the documents on the desk, consider briefly, and decide to put that chess piece in your pocket.

speaker: Nightingale
content: 98% of the routes in WhiteSands are controlled by the Campbell family. Although they're all being monitored by the FAC currently, considering you're taking Eirene with you... Chief, the FAC advised that you bring a larger team.
I'll think about it. But first, I have to invite Miss Eirene to come with me.
In the room, Eirene sits in the same posture as she did when you first met her, her gaze focusing on the chessboard on the desk.

options: Sorry to interrupt you, Miss Eirene.

content: Eirene remains silent. You suppose you've got her permission, so you walk into the room and stare at the state of play on the desk with her.

speaker: Eirene
content: Please speak plainly if you want anything, Chief.

speaker: Eirene
content: I don't think you've squeezed out time from your busy schedule just to rack your brains over this endgame with me.
As far as I know, it's still possible to win during the endgame in chess.
I've long heard about your gift for chess, Miss Eirene. Don't you want to reverse the situation in this endgame?
Eirene finally lifts her gaze from the chessboard and looks at you.

speaker: Eirene
content: Go ahead, state your purpose.
Thank you for your cooperation last time. Based on our investigation, we've judged that Bryce Campbell has become more dangerous and he may be in touch with other Sinners besides you.
That's why I'm taking a trip to Fraser City for the investigation, and I hope you could come with me.

speaker: Eirene
content: ...What are you talking about?
Eirene frowns and seems unable to comprehend the meaning of your words.

speaker: Eirene
content: You're inviting Eirene Campbell, Bryce Campbell's daughter, to go back to Fraser City with you?

speaker: Eirene
content: I can't tell whether you're overconfident or simply out of your mind.

speaker: Eirene
content: Aren't you afraid that my father and I may take advantage of your arrival and launch an attack on the DisCity?
There's a hint of sarcasm in Eirene's tone. She lifts her hand and pushes a black piece near the opponent's king.

speaker: Eirene
content: Chief, do you want to lead this endgame toward a victory... or a failure?
You sit in the chair facing Eirene and produce the permit to leave and the transparent chess piece.
It all depends on which path you decide to take, Miss Eirene.
You're now a Sinner detained by me. As long as I wish, you can't defy my orders. But I won't go as far as that for now. The MBCC needs you and is going to help you.

speaker: Eirene
content: Ha... For now, you said.

options: I know you're trying to break free from him.

content: Eirene lapses into silence. Her two hands on the desk are clenched, to the point her fingernails are turning white.

speaker: Eirene
content: In that case... Let's have a game of chess, Chief.

speaker: Eirene
content: In the past, whenever I felt lost, I would play a match with my father.

speaker: Eirene
content: Thinking about the steps helps me clarify my mind and see ahead clearly.

speaker: Eirene
content: I hope you won't turn me down.
But I'm not good at chess.
That's an understatement. In fact, you only just went through the rules of chess as you were investigating this chess piece today.

speaker: Eirene
content: That won't be a problem. A player pays the same respect to every opponent.
You nod and scoot forward slightly to begin a game with Eirene.
But you're certain you have no chance of winning at all.

speaker: Eirene
content: Hehe...
...What's so funny?

speaker: Eirene
content: What you just said reminds me of my own words when I played chess with my father for the first time.
Smiling, Eirene looks at you and turns the chessboard to set the white pieces before you.

speaker: Eirene
content: I said, "You're too good, father, you'll defeat me in seconds."

speaker: Eirene
content: Then he moved the white pieces to my side, and told me that... "In any case, making the first move means victory."
Gestured by Eirene, you pick up a white piece and consider for a good while before deciding to move the white pawn two squares forward.

options: Are you taking advantage of me?

speaker: Eirene
content: Hmm, a very steady first move.

speaker: Eirene
content: You must be joking... Taking such trivial advantage of you won't do Quinn any good.

speaker: Eirene
content: But that game indeed ended quickly.
Eirene's fingers brush against a piece gently, pick it up, and set it on the chessboard sharply.

speaker: Eirene
content: My father didn't treat me as a beginner at all, and kept attacking mercilessly, even ignoring the position of the king.

speaker: Eirene
content: He taught me with this ruthless match that a businessman ought to have the decisiveness to kill without hesitation, and...

speaker: Eirene
content: The resilience to never bow down and give up no matter how bleak the situation is.
Though I'm no businessman, I'll try to struggle for a bit longer.
It seems to me that you lost that game but won Mr. Bryce's recognition.

speaker: Eirene
content: Who knows? I only remember bawling my eyes out.
A child's pride is much more stubborn than we think. A trial like that is indeed quite cruel.

speaker: Eirene
content: You think that's cruel?
The woman before you picks up a piece, the black rook, and pushes a white piece on the board gently with it. The white piece standing there falls immediately, tumbling on the board.
Eirene sets the black piece on that square and gives a self-mocking laugh.

speaker: Eirene
content: My father has given me many more trials after this checkmate.
The night has fallen. Under the moonlight, the sand of WhiteSands appears even more desolate.

Not far away, an enormous structure is docked near the fine quicksand. It's a WhiteSands freighter. It's so close to the quicksand, looking like it may get pulled at any moment into these seeming feeble swirls that can devour everything.

speaker: Desert Bandit Boss
content: Unload as many of the goods as you can, but our primary target is that girl!

speaker: Desert Bandit A
content: Boss, it's just a girl, wouldn't this be overkill? How can she make it out of WhiteSands alive without this ship?

speaker: Desert Bandit Boss
content: Humph, do you think she's the same as those pampered fat cats around you?

speaker: Desert Bandit Boss
content: She's a Campbell! She can escape WhiteSands with her eyes closed!

speaker: Desert Bandit Boss
content: Moreover... This time, someone is paying a fortune to make her...
The desert bandits exchange a look and burst out in disgusting laughter.
Daisy
Frightened of the desert bandits? No, it's the person paying a fortune that she's frightened of.

speaker: Maiden
content: Daddy...
The desert bandits are approaching this hold. The girl grips the handgun tightly, trying hard to calm down.

speaker: Maiden
content: White... E3.

speaker: Maiden
content: NO!!! I'm not waiting for anyone! NOBODY IS COMING!

speaker: Desert Bandit B
content: Boss! There's a hold below!

speaker: Desert Bandit Boss
content: That's for storing ropes, a person won't fit in there. But just in case, take a look to see if they've got anything valuable hidden in there!

speaker: Desert Bandit B
content: Alrighty!
The desert bandit lifts the plank at the entrance and jumps down, but the moment he turns, he faces the black hole of the barrel.

speaker: Maiden
content: Take this!
A gunshot sounds. Without splashing out much fluid, the desert bandit exits the chessboard before he can even notify anyone.

speaker: Desert Bandit Boss
content: That girl is right below! Fire!!

The girl keeps her crouching position and fires back at the converging enemies the best she can. The bullets going in the reverse direction carry determination, piercing through the desert bandits trying to get close to her.

speaker: Desert Bandit Boss
content: Don't ******* just shoot through the entrance! Aim at the deck! Fetch me those weapons!
A large machine gun shining in an eerie red light is carried there by several desert bandits. The moment the boss pulls the trigger, the bullet rips through the hard deck and barely misses the girl.

speaker: Maiden
content: What the h*** is that?! If this goes on...
With a clack, the girl's handgun stops, leaving only a few strands of smoke in the air.

speaker: Maiden
content: Damn it!
Hearing that the gunshots below have stopped, the boss gives a wicked laugh and pulls the ring off the hand grenade.

speaker: Desert Bandit Boss
content: I wanted to let you keep your pretty face, but I guess you want a taste of my favorite trick... Hehe, hahahaha!
The hand grenade rolls into the hold. The smell of the burning detonator and overwhelming fear have paralyzed the girl's nerves. For a moment, her head is swimming.

speaker: Desert Bandit Boss
content: You're pretty tough to have held us off for so long. You're indeed a Campbell.

speaker: Maiden
content: That's right, because I'm a Campbell...

speaker: Maiden
content: At the very least... I won't let this warship that carries our honor fall into the hands of your sort!
At that moment, the girl has already made her decision. She crawls out from the ruins of the stairs and begins executing every step of her strategy.
She tries her best to steady her mind and picks up that hand grenade with shaky hands, gripping it.

speaker: Maiden
content: Let's hope you're powerful enough to at least blow up the next two holds.

speaker: Desert Bandit Boss
content: You sure fight hard, but is it harder than my ****? Hahahaha!
The girl ignores the cackling desert bandits on the deck, focusing only on the dwindling hiss.

speaker: Maiden
content: Just... catch this!
At the final moment, she throws the hand grenade backward and leaps behind the iron petition.

speaker: Desert Bandits
content: For ****'s sake!
Boom!
The hand grenade embedded with a bizarre crystal is several times more powerful than regular ones. It's almost blown up the whole deck, and a few neighboring holds have completely collapsed.

speaker: Desert Bandit Boss
content: Argh! Find that girl first! Even if I have to break this ship up, I must throw her ashes in this WhiteSands!!

Furious, the desert bandit picks up an iron bar randomly and swings it violently. But wherever they search, they don't find any signs of life in these ruins. Only a puddle of fluid mixed with filth keeps spreading little by little.

speaker: Desert Bandit A
content: Boss! There's a secret passage leading upward!

speaker: Desert Bandit A
content: It seems to be... leading to the cockpit!

speaker: Desert Bandit Boss
content: What?!
The desert bandits immediately run back to the rails to confirm the situation. As expected, the ship has already been launched, and the front half is almost sinking into quicksand!

speaker: Desert Bandit Boss
content: You ****! If I must die on this ship, you'll **** die with me!!
The boss snatches a gun and kicks the cockpit's door open.
Trembling, the girl is operating the control stick with one hand, her other hand resting on a red button. The liquid dripping from her fingertips gathers on the button, as if she has dyed it red.

speaker: Maiden
content: Buried in quicksand... or buried in flames...

speaker: Maiden
content: I... Cough, I do have mercy for you... I'm letting you choose.

speaker: Desert Bandit Boss
content: Shut the **** up! Do you know who paid to have you killed? Bryce Campbell!

speaker: Desert Bandit Boss
content: And you're still guarding his ship like a ******* idiot?! Stop it, now! ****!

speaker: Maiden
content: OwO

speaker: Maiden
content: I... Eirene Campbell... will protect the Campbell family's honor with my life.
The girl presses the button gently.

In the last conscious moment, she sees the desert bandits' contorted faces, and feels the deafening and pungent explosion, just like the gun salute her father fired at the Campbell family's coming of age ceremony.

speaker: Maiden
content: Congratulations, you're a grown-up now, Eirene.
Fortunately, the girl doesn't end up dying or getting swallowed by quicksand.
