She's let many down, but as long as that one person recognizes her, everything's worth it.

speaker: Eirene
content: Chief, it's your turn.
E-M-P! Mess! Can you hear me?
And you're still absorbed in the ending of the young girl's story.
Excuse me... But that story was too...

speaker: Eirene
content: It's not a story, it's a trial given to me by my father.
I know, but still... it sounds a bit unimaginable.

speaker: Eirene
content: I remember I've told you, he's able to sit on his throne now because he's trampled over his own family many times.

speaker: Eirene
content: If I died, it would only prove that I wasn't qualified to stand next to him.

speaker: Eirene
content: But fortunately, not only did I survive... but my ability also awakened.
That was when you became a Sinner!

speaker: Eirene
content: Yes... I've heard of two ways parents react to their child turning into a Sinner.

speaker: Eirene
content: They either become even more protective and refuse to let the government take their kid, reluctant to lose them.

speaker: Eirene
content: Or they throw the kid out like a piece of dirty rag, afraid of having the slightest connection with a Sinner.

options: Then... which reaction did you get?

content: Eirene shrugs, skillfully placing a chess piece where one of yours stands, devouring it. You recognize the piece, it's the queen.

speaker: Eirene
content: I guessed right. The one who bought the desert bandits to ambush me on the route was indeed my father.

speaker: Eirene
content: His intention was clear. If I died, he'd pretend he'd never had this daughter, and if I lived... it'd prove that I was still useful.

speaker: Eirene
content: That's why when I lived... when I became a Sinner, he was gratified.

speaker: Eirene
content: He told me to feel proud of myself... because he was going to send me to the DisCity to lay the foundation for his great plan.

speaker: Eirene
content: That was the second time he said that. The first time he told me to feel proud of myself was the only time I defeated him at chess.
As you're talking, Eirene has once again besieged your pieces. There's nothing worth analyzing on the chessboard, Eirene has simply been devouring all your pieces ruthlessly.
In other words, you've established Quinn at your father's will?
You move your piece one step to the side. You've decided to struggle a bit more and open up the spot so that you may bring the king out.

speaker: Eirene
content: Correct. He'd planned the entire roadmap for me. As long as I followed his instructions, nothing could go wrong. Then again, what he'd planned was not easy to achieve either.

speaker: Eirene
content: But I'm a Campbell, after all. Perhaps I was born with... a rebellious instinct in me.

speaker: Eirene
content: I thought I could undermine him slowly. I didn't expect to... fail completely.
Eirene lowers her gaze and stares at the chessboard, her thoughts undecipherable.
That's also why I hope you can come with me to Fraser City.
As the chief, I can't let a Sinner fall under someone else's control. As your acquaintance... I think you're too competent to be controlled by him.
Also, I'd like to clarify that the shackles... are in fact not a form of control...
Tak! You hear the crisp sound of a piece falling, and the corner of Eirene's mouth is slightly lifted, interrupting your sentence.

speaker: Eirene
content: Checkmate.
What?

speaker: Eirene
content: I'm sorry, you lost, Chief.
On the chessboard, the king you've racked your brains to move out has been blocked by Eirene's queen. You're stuck.

speaker: Eirene
content: This is speed chess. As a beginner, you did pretty well playing against me.

speaker: Eirene
content: But still... Thank you, Chief. My mind feels a lot clearer now.
You stare at the chessboard occupied by black pieces and feel perplexed. Is she genuinely confused?
In that case... what's your answer?

speaker: Eirene
content: I'll come with you... Indeed, I should break free from the control.
Eirene picks up the permit on the desk and smiles at you.

speaker: Eirene
content: Whenever you're ready.
There are no windows in the sand cruiser's cockpit. You can only observe what's going on outside through the navigation panel.
Sailing off that towering wall, the surrounding structures are beginning to dwindle in both height and number. The sand is stirred up by both the wind and the oars, slowly covering the sky.

speaker: Eirene
content: No. It's just that I've realized that this sand cruiser... looks like the one owned by my family at that time.

It's indeed a copy manufactured based on the Campbell family's ship. The trade terms with Fraser City contain a blueprint of the sand cruiser. And if I remember correctly, Quinn also owns a sand cruiser manufacturer, doesn't it?
Miss Eirene, I thought you must know? This sounds more bizarre than me thinking you may have motion sickness.

speaker: Eirene
content: Excuse me. This ship is a pretty old model. I thought you would use a newer sand cruiser produced by Quinn, it'll be much faster.
...This is just to pay Fraser City some respect.

speaker: Eirene
content: We're still about thirty minutes away from the unruled areas of WhiteSands. Would you like to play some more chess with me, Chief?
Within thirty minutes, can I reach a level where I may be able to last a few turns with Mr. Campbell?

speaker: Eirene
content: You're certainly an idealist.
That's enough time for you to defeat me five or six times, Miss Eirene.

speaker: Eirene
content: Wouldn't it be fun?
Eirene shrugs and looks at you with amusement.
She's literally just told you that horrifying story not long ago, yet there's no trace of fear on her face, even though she's going to see her own family who once tried to murder her.

speaker: Eirene
content: Perhaps that's the secret behind the Campbells' successes.
Eirene seems to have read your mind.

speaker: Eirene
content: The business world is a battlefield. Affection plays no role here.
After that, the conversation ceases between you and Eirene.
On the navigation panel, the color outside the window has turned into an endless stretch of white with no other colors. You realize you've probably crossed into the unruled areas.
You're going to face that businessman deemed cruel and ruthless by many... Bryce Campbell.

speaker: Vibrating noises
content: Boom...
What's that?

speaker: Eirene
content: It's from a sand cruiser... Are there others following you?
No, our main purpose this time is not a violent confrontation.

speaker: Navigator
content: Chief, several old sand cruisers have just appeared out of nowhere on our route!

speaker: Navigator
content: Moreover... They're approaching us, looking ready to fight! We're already within their shooting range!

speaker: Eirene
content: They're Campbell's freighters, Chief.

speaker: Eirene
content: Although these are old models, with their number and the weapons equipped on them, they can deal a fatal blow to us.
As they're speaking, some obscure shouts from the outside are reaching the cockpit.
Those people are chanting Bryce's name and asking the MBCC's chief to get lost or kiss Bryce's feet.
This operation has been disguised as a regular trade visit. We've been betrayed.
As you're still frowning and considering what to do, dense gunfire is already blasting around you. The next round of bombardment may hit the cabin.
Eirene...
You raise your head to look straight at her.
Feeling your gaze, she laughs softly.

speaker: Eirene
content: If you trust me... let me sail it.
I also hope you can trust my decision.
Eirene bypasses you and walks straight to the navigator's seat to begin operating the panel. Her movements are smooth and without any hesitation.
The freighters on the other side are still attacking, but under Eirene's navigation, your ship begins dodging and retreating.

speaker: Navigator
content: Is... is this route safe? We haven't tested if there's quicksand...

speaker: Eirene
content: A Campbell can escape WhiteSands with their eyes closed.

speaker: Eirene
content: Have you never heard of this saying?
Without stopping her hands, Eirene winks at the navigator.

speaker: Navigator
content: Excuse me...

speaker: Eirene
content: ...Hmm, you're very young, after all.
Under Eirene's navigation, your sand cruiser begins sailing in another direction. Although the Campbell freighters are chasing after you closely, you haven't been hit so far.
Eirene navigates so skillfully that it's as if this ship were the one that had been through fire and water with her back in the day.
Thanks for navigating the ship, hang in there. Other armed crew members, please follow me to the deck...
Those guys have been quiet for a while. Who knows what they're up to next.

You lead a group to the deck to check the stern of the ship. You've guessed right. While you weren't aware, they tied a rope to the stern of the ship and are now jumping onto your freighter one by one.
Stop them. We can't let them get inside the cockpit!
You command the team to disperse and strike back at the intruders.

speaker: Eirene
content: Watch out, the freighter at ten o'clock is shooting at you guys! Hold on tight!
Eirene's voice comes from the PA system on the ship. You throw yourself to one side and lie down behind a container.
Boom!!
As a deafening explosion sounds, the entire ship shakes violently for a while as if it's grabbed by a giant invisible hand.
When the smoke clears up, you finally realize your ship has been hit.

speaker: Eirene
content: Ugh... Apologies, Chief. I couldn't dodge that one hit.
Eirene's voice sounds a little feeble as well, perhaps because she bumped into something with the shock just now.

speaker: Eirene
content: It must have been a seasoned gunner. They changed the trajectory at the moment it was fired... That was insane...
But before you can recover from the shock, a second shell has already been fired.

speaker: Eirene
content: Chief! Take cover!!
The static noise in Eirene's voice is gone. The ship has stopped and she's come out of the cockpit.
With a severe look on her face, she raises her hand toward the incoming shell.

speaker: Eirene
content: I won't let you have your way again.
The shell explodes in mid-air. Debris and sparks bloom in the air, falling down on the deck, making cracking noises.
It's Eirene's special ability.

speaker: Eirene
content: Chief, you can order me.

speaker: Eirene
content: Otherwise, both you and I may not make it back alive.
What do you mean?!
Eirene gives a wry smile and points at the ship facing you.

speaker: Eirene
content: He... came himself. The one firing the shells is him.

speaker: Eirene
content: Everything I know, I've learned from him. I can never win against him.

speaker: Eirene
content: Unless... you agree to let me use my ability.

As you're talking, more shells keep flying toward you. All of them are blocked by Eirene in mid-air, but it's not difficult to tell that your opponent is set on wrecking this ship, even though some of his own people are on board.

speaker: Eirene
content: Chief, that's our only way out.
You clench your fists and dig your fingernails into your palms, but your hands have long been numbed by firing the gun, so you don't feel any pain at all.
You know you're facing a cutthroat situation, but you don't want to let Eirene use her power. Despite everything, the person on the other ship is her father, and she... has at least once revered him.

options: Allow Eirene to use her power
Not allow Eirene to use her power

content: But I won't allow you to attack him with your special ability. Just block all his shells.
You can't use your special ability on humans.

speaker: Eirene
content: What...?
I mean you can only use your special ability to stop the shells. Leave the rest to me.
You turn around and gather the remaining crew members to escort you back to the cockpit.
The climate in WhiteSands is special. Is there a storm coming soon?

speaker: Navigator
content: Yes, in about three minutes.
Good. I'll ask Eirene to reserve a time interval in three minutes. You guys seize this chance to aim at the opponents and...
Get rid of as many of them as possible.

speaker: Navigator
content: ....Copy that.
You grab a sniper rifle from the weapon rack and gesture for the other crew members to follow you.
The sky is getting dark, but you're not sure whether it's due to the smoke from the gunfire or the gathering clouds.
The wind is becoming stronger. The dark smoke resulting from the shells exploding in mid-air by Eirene's power is diffusing in the air bit by bit.
You squat and lean against the lookout, the rifle in place. The soldiers behind you are ready and waiting for your command.
Everything you see now is through the small window of the rifle scope.
You're waiting, waiting for that person to appear before the storm...
Everyone, aim at two o'clock...
A blur of black barges into your sight from the edge of the window.
The figure leans half of his body forward, as if wanting to operate the artillery.
You know this is the best and the last chance you'll get.
Ceaseless gunshots are echoing in the comms, and you see the target falling down slowly amid the converged gunfire.
The shells closing in on the ship have dyed the sky red. But as if blocked by something, they stop flying and instead are struggling, contorting, and exploding in the sky.
Eirene's power is indeed terrifying.
...Did we succeed?

The wind is still blowing, clearing up the obstacles blocking your sight. Fortunately, the opponents have stopped attacking. A smear of red is dripping down the enemy's artillery. Finally, you let out a sigh of relief.
Your hands are still shaking. After you get down from the lookout, you remove the magazine and pass the rifle to the soldiers while mocking yourself for trembling so badly.
You give a slightly resigned smile and walk to Eirene.
Eirene is standing at the bow of the ship, but her eyes keep avoiding the ship carrying her father.
I'm sorry. The most I could do was not let you be the one to do it.

speaker: Eirene
content: ...I understand what you mean.

speaker: Eirene
content: I just can't believe that he... really died, just like that.

speaker: Eirene
content: Perhaps... he was really getting old.
On the gap blasted open by the shells at the stern, a piece of hard steel has been sliced off, dangling and moaning like a frail old man.
Unstable to withstand the wind, it finally falls with a thud.

speaker: Eirene
content: Let's go, Chief. Let's go and witness the beginning of a new era for the Campbells.
Sure, but first we should do a quick cleanup to preserve all the evidence. I suppose the Campbells are all difficult to deal with, just like him.

speaker: Eirene
content: In that case, I'll let you know...
Eirene walks back, and turns back to wink at you when she reaches the other end. The previous sadness in her seems to have all vanished.

speaker: Eirene
content: There are at least ten other tricky Campbell children like me in Fraser City.
Your father... was a virile man.
Once the sandstorm calms down a little, you prepare to go to Bryce's ship with a few crew members and Eirene.
From afar, the gold watch on the wrist of that wrinkled hand drooping from the artillery is still glistening even in this gloomy weather.

speaker: Eirene
content: It's indeed... him.
...You didn't have to come.
Eirene shakes her head and says thanks to you, then turns around to walk toward the cockpit.

speaker: Eirene
content: I'm just here to take one last look at him... I'll wait for you in the cockpit, Chief.
You watch Eirene enter the cabin, take a deep breath, then begin handling the dead body lying over the artillery.
Although your bullets missed, the navigator's didn't. The filth oozing out from the wound is pooling around the other cheek, dying the still-open eyes a different color.
This is...?
You put on a pair of gloves and gently pull the body's eyes open, examining them carefully.
His eyes have been tampered with?

The liquid is flowing into the eyes in a weird direction, as if it's seeping in. When you look more closely, you find that the two eyes are looking to the left and right in a strange way, as if they haven't been properly installed.
A layer of cold sweat breaks all over your back: this isn't Bryce!!
You force yourself to calm down and mentally go through all the events in order...
Eirene... you've led me here.
From the very beginning, the person who lured you to this area to fight the freighters and told you that your assailant was Bryce... has been Eirene!
Now that you're sailing on an unrecorded route because you've been attacked, without Eirene's help, you certainly won't be able to make it out of here.
You leave two people here to take care of Bryce and walk out of the cockpit gloomily.
Chief? You're already done... taking care of him?
A clear voice sounds in a dark corner. A grim white light is turned out with a click, illuminating both you and her.

speaker: Eirene
content: Why the long face? You can't be mourning for that man... can you?

speaker: Eirene
content: Don't worry, he's long gotten his hands dirty... with many things, including the blood of his own kin.
Since the start of the chess match, you've been planning all of this, haven't you?

speaker: Eirene
content: Haha... Chief, I recall I already told you this when we first had a heart-to-heart.

speaker: Eirene
content: Businesspeople... always seek to maximize their profits.

speaker: Eirene
content: In chess, there's an opening known as the Queen's Gambit. It's a very risky move, so few are willing to use it. Those who do are mostly highly skilled... or simply arrogant.

speaker: Eirene
content: Obviously... I am both.

speaker: Eirene
content: I made myself a pawn and rushed to you during the opening... I was glad you didn't block me in the middle, you let me come to the end smoothly... Now, I've turned the pawn back into the queen.
You do have masterful chess skills, but this is not what I want to hear.
State your request plainly.

speaker: Eirene
content: I like talking business with smart people.

Eirene leans back and sits in the leather chair in the cockpit. Ignoring the faint smell of gunpowder and blood, you find that she does look like the kind of CEO ready to sign a contract you've seen on TV.

options: Is this another plan instructed by Bryce?

content: This is... indeed ruthless.

speaker: Eirene
content: Haha... First of all, I believe you understand the current situation. That's why you came to me alone.
Yes, I must admit I need your help to get out of here.

speaker: Eirene
content: But the truth is that you can also threaten me with the shackles and make me escort you out without harming you.
I want the truth more than that.

speaker: Eirene
content: You can also use the shackles to...
I've said it before, Eirene. I've always firmly believed that the shackles do not exist to suppress your freedom.
Eirene rests her elbows on the armrests and crosses her two hands, staring at you intensely.

speaker: Eirene
content: Alright. Since you have a clear understanding of your situation and are so merciful, Chief, I'll be upfront with you.

speaker: Eirene
content: My request is simple: be my cover in Syndicate.
Be your cover in Syndicate...? You do want to get involved in the private mines, after all!
It seems like you've already begun your moves in Syndicate... Bishop is indeed working with you, am I right?

speaker: Eirene
content: Yes, this lucrative business has been getting divided by Syndicans little by little for a long time. How can the Campbells just sit back and watch? That's the Hypercube we're talking about!
Eirene lifts a hand, as if giving a business talk.

speaker: Eirene
content: But as you know, those gangsters, those Sinners loitering in Syndicate... are no pushovers.

speaker: Eirene
content: Besides... I need the name of an official entity. I don't want to taint Quinn's reputation.

speaker: Eirene
content: The chief of the MBCC, my friend... you're the most suitable person.
I don't seem to have the right to say no.

speaker: Eirene
content: Haha, of course you do, Chief.
Eirene covers her mouth and chuckles, then lifts her hand again. In the silence, you hear the clicks of numerous guns being loaded.

speaker: Eirene
content: But if you choose to say no, you leave me with no choice but to hold a grand farewell party for you and me.
You and me?

speaker: Eirene
content: The poor chief of the MBCC died in a desert bandit attack when he took his Sinner to WhiteSands. They both died under gunfire.
female_content: The poor chief of the MBCC died in a desert bandit attack when she took her Sinner to WhiteSands. They both died under gunfire.

speaker: Eirene
content: But only you will really die, as for me... I will be reborn in Syndicate. My past will be erased, I'll build another empire with a new identity.
Syndicans, especially those gangsters, won't trust a newcomer blindly.

speaker: Eirene
content: As long as they can't tell I'm a newcomer, it'll be fine. That can be achieved easily, Chief.
...Enoch. He'll forge a new identity for you.

speaker: Eirene
content: You're indeed very smart, Chief. Sadly, you're always one step behind me.
You take a deep breath, and breathe out while shaking your head. You give her a faint smile the way she does.
When I was reading the rules of chess, I learned about a move... called castling.
Although I indeed lost to you in that game... I may not lose this one.
You walk to the chair facing Eirene and sit down, staring at her eyes of different colors.

speaker: Eirene
content: Oh? Your growth is so rapid... A pleasant surprise.

speaker: Eirene
content: You do implement your strategy very... decisively, Chief. Now I'm glad you're not in business.
When we first found that batch of goods, we had our reservations. In fact, I checked the shipping manifests between Fraser City and the DisCity in the past eight years.
Indeed, I couldn't retrieve the records from several years, but just from the available data from the first few years, I could observe some irregularities.
Eirene frowns slightly and signals you to continue with her gaze. It feels like the two of you are back to the interrogation room.
Like with most Outland cities, the trade between Fraser City and the DisCity mostly involves exchanging household goods and energy with precious metals.

But starting eight years ago, the household goods and energy exported to Outland have been decreasing each year. Lately, it's been found that the imported precious metals have been gradually replaced by DisCoins of the equivalent weight...

As far as I know, during this period, Fraser City didn't suffer any large-scale diseases, natural disasters, or arable land degradation caused by industrial factors, so there hasn't been a decline in its population.
Then... what caused the reduction in the exported energy and household goods? Where... did this amount of DisCity cash come from?
Eirene still wears the same poised expression, but her palms are pressed together. Like white sand, the pale color resulting from the pressure on the muscles and joints has covered her fingers.
My guess is that... Fraser City has probably switched owners through some unspeakable means. And its new owner is Quinn's CEO who holds the massive cash flow in her hands, Miss Eirene.

speaker: Eirene
content: Your thoughts are... very cruel.
Yes, it makes me instinctively want to believe your story.
But luckily... even in the face of a master, my chess skills are not exactly horrible.

speaker: Eirene
content: ...Haha... Hahahaha!
This is the first time you've seen Eirene lose her cool. Though half of her pretty face is masked by her hand, when the laughter stops, those eyes are sending you an obvious warning.

speaker: Eirene
content: You're right, Chief. Fraser City has indeed switched owners in a ruthless way.

speaker: Eirene
content: When I awakened as a Sinner, Bryce initially wanted to control me and use me for his great comeback plan.

speaker: Eirene
content: But just as you've said, how can an ordinary man subdue a Sinner? Besides... isn't Bryce exactly the type who doesn't give a damn about his own family?

speaker: Eirene
content: Perhaps I should put it this way... Our relationship completely fell apart in that explosion in WhiteSands.
Eirene's voice is dull. She raises her head and looks around the cabin to find that logo projected above the control panel. The Campbell family's coat of arms.

speaker: Eirene
content: Or perhaps even earlier? When my mother passed away having never earned a legitimate place beside him, all he did was come to play chess with me. It was the only game I've ever won against him.

speaker: Eirene
content: But I don't want to become the next Bryce.

The image on the projected screen suddenly changes from the coat of arms to somewhere like a monitoring room. On the screen, a blond old man is sitting in a wheelchair and staring at the empty chessboard before him blankly.
Is that Bryce?!

speaker: Eirene
content: That's right. I couldn't bring myself to kill my dear father just like that... He still has to witness how I'll become the Campbells' pride.
What have you done to him...?!

speaker: Eirene
content: He's old and he treasures his life... He almost never questions whether the pills he takes every day are really going to make him live longer.

speaker: Eirene
content: But what does that matter, Chief?
Eirene's tone has regained its usual coolness, questioning you.

speaker: Eirene
content: You don't think you'll be able to beat me just because you have this information, do you?
Of course I can't. I know that.
But it puts me in a state where I can assess the trade between us more... fairly.

speaker: Eirene
content: What state?
You straighten up and lean forward, shortening the distance between you and Eirene.
Based on the assumption I've mentioned, when I invited you to Fraser City... I also requested armed protection from the 9th Agency.
Before we boarded the ship, a team of armed guards has been placed in different parts of the sand cruiser.
Otherwise, why would I dare to come to meet you alone?
You see Eirene frown. Obviously, she didn't expect you'd hidden help on the sand cruiser.

speaker: Eirene
content: Ha... I thought you said the main purpose this time wasn't a violent confrontation?
I meant not with Bryce Campbell.

speaker: Eirene
content: But this is pointless, Chief. Without me, you guys can't make it out of this desert.

While you pretended to be dodging the freighters' attacks, you damaged the sand cruiser's communication and positioning functions. But you probably didn't expect that every member sent by the 9th Agency has their own positioning device on them.
All I need to do is survive until they make it here, that's it. Please do not underestimate the 9th Agency.
Eirene lowers her hand, the smile on her face deepening. She's watching you like you're a precious gem.

speaker: Eirene
content: I really admire you, Chief.

speaker: Eirene
content: I did... underestimate you.

speaker: Eirene
content: But unfortunately...
Eirene stands up and comes behind you. She places her hands on the armrests of your chair, almost encircling you with her body.

speaker: Eirene
content: I, Eirene Campbell, belong to the Campbell family. I've been the Campbell family's head for the past eight years.

speaker: Eirene
content: I've watched sand cruisers come and go, float and sink, since I was a child.

speaker: Eirene
content: The weight of goods and the number of people a sand cruiser is carrying... I can tell these just from the speed it's going at, the draft, and the area of the sand it's stirring up.
Eirene's voice rings by your ear, as if whispering to you. Her warm breaths are spraying on your ear, but you're feeling an icy chill on your back.

speaker: Eirene
content: Still, I do really appreciate you.

speaker: Eirene
content: Since the moment you accepted my invitation despite not knowing all the rules of chess...

speaker: Eirene
content: Perhaps... you'll make a pretty good opponent.
What do you want?
Eirene sits back into the chair facing you, reaching out a hand to you with amusement.

speaker: Eirene
content: You already know my plan, and I understand your ideas.

speaker: Eirene
content: Right now, it's safe to say... we're at even strength.

speaker: Eirene
content: In that case... I'd like to have another game of chess with you.
What kind of chess?
Several rays of sunlight shine through the gap shattered by the shells, cutting up the shadows between you and Eirene and forming a chessboard on the coffee table.

speaker: Eirene
content: I'll return to the MBCC with you and accept your detention arrangements. I know that according to the rules, they won't ask me to give up Quinn just like that, so I'll still have the time and rights for my personal activities.

speaker: Eirene
content: What do you think? Will you accept my challenge? The chief of the Minos Bureau of Crisis Control who refuses to control me with the shackles... The chief who's competent enough to be my opponent.

speaker: Eirene
content: Well... I look forward to finding out who'll come out the winner in this even match.
If we're no longer bound by the rules of chess, then I guess, there can be more outcomes than just victory or loss.
You grip Eirene's extended hand. Her warm palm grips yours and pulls you forward...

speaker: Eirene
content: Very well... Let's find out together.

O dazzling morning star,
Shine beside the moon,
May you never lose your glory.

Stood above the stars,
Crossed the clouds in the far north, 
Sat on the peak of towering mountains.

On the verge of falling,
It was prophesied to fall from the heavens
Into a world of falsehood destined to vanish.
The communicator device is beeping, and three text messages in a row are sent to you.
You tap on the latest one. It asks you to the interrogation room ASAP. A Sinner has turned herself in and specifically requested to see you.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Long time no see, my little monster.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Why the look? Do you not miss me at all?
Could you explain to me what happened to him, Miss Stargazer?
In the interrogation room, the exotic Sinner fiddles with the chains on her wrists. She seems to find being confined here a new and fresh experience.
At the door, several staff members are carrying a fainted person out of the room. He looks ghastly pale as if he had been shocked.
She glances in the direction you are pointing at, unconcerned.

speaker: Stargazer
content: I thought you're already used to it.

speaker: Stargazer
content: You know full well. This kind of thing always happens wherever I go.
Stargazer waves her hand nonchalantly. The trinkets and chains on her body make a jingling noise, which adds a touch of eeriness to the interrogation room.

speaker: Stargazer
content: They were interested in my prophecy skills.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Seeing as they were your colleagues, I prophesied for them.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Too bad they thought my prophecy was a joke, and tried to "teach me a lesson." But...

speaker: Stargazer
content: Hey, am I really that frightening?
The staff members hiding outside the door behind you seem to be afraid of her and wishing for her to leave immediately. After a few grunts, they leave reluctantly.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Although my prophecies are not for free, seeing them making an exhibition of themselves could count as the fee, I guess.
Stargazer gives you a wink.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Of course, you're different, little monster.
You ignore her stare and sit in front of her.

options: Why did you insist on seeing me?

speaker: Stargazer
content: Of course it's because I've missed you.
...Thanks for your concern.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Little monster, are you questioning my sincerity for you?
That’s not what I meant...

speaker: Stargazer
content: Hehe... You used to be so bold. Now you can't even take a joke.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Never mind. The reason I came to see you... is to tell you a new prophecy.
Stargazer's lips curl up into a knowing smile, just like when you first met her in WhiteSands.
You can tell me, but as you know, I'm not... one to believe in prophecies.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Alright, alright.
Stargazer's smile grows deeper as she waves her right hand and brings a tarot card out of nowhere.

speaker: Stargazer
content: My poor little monster...

speaker: Stargazer
content: How should I tell you... this huge canvas known as fate...
Stargazer places the tarot card in front of her while gently shaking her head toward you.

speaker: Stargazer
content: The tower rises over the zoo. Vultures, scorpions, jackals, hounds, vipers, monkeys...

speaker: Stargazer
content: They howl under the tall tower and dance in the mud to declare this sinful world...

speaker: Stargazer
content: And you hang above this tower, tottering like the morning star...
What are you trying to say?

speaker: Stargazer
content: A great catastrophe sweeping the world...

speaker: Stargazer
content: Little monster, the world you love will inevitably come to an end because of the catastrophe.

options: The world will end one day.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Then... why don't you go to the Realm of Truth with me? I have been looking for it for a long time. Until recently, I finally found its entrance seems to be stirring around you. You should be able to sense it too.

You frown. You have seen the Dreamflower with Stargazer, so you have a rough idea of where it came from. DisSea has been unstable lately, but you can't be sure that it's related to the so-called "truth" that Stargazer is mentioning.
As a human being born to this world, I have the right to choose to die with this world. I will not run away from death, Miss Stargazer.
As you should know, such words of bewitchment don't really work on me.

speaker: Stargazer
content: It's not bewitchment. It is a prophecy. It's your... future path. You are destined to follow me.
As Stargazer says this, she picks up and shows you the second tarot card with her golden finger claws.
On the card, a thorny moon glows brightly in the sky. The animals that Stargazer just mentioned are gathering below, with their necks upturned, roaring vigorously.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Haha... it's the Moon upright.

speaker: Stargazer
content: You will embark on a journey filled with confusion and uncertainty... Everything will feel like being covered in the shadow...

speaker: Stargazer
content: The pale glow carries sharp thorns that will make your spine and heart ache.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Oh, my poor little monster. You need me, sweetie.

options: My journey has always been filled with those things.

content: Stargazer quietly looks at you as if expecting you to say something.
But I won't back down. Sorry, Miss Stargazer. I know it's rude to interrupt your prophecy. Please continue.

speaker: Stargazer
content: That's one of the things I like about you, my little monster.
Stargazer places the second card on the right side and draws a third one.
The moment she sees the card, Stargazer sighs and gazes at you in compassion.
If you got something to say, just say it.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Five of Cups. You will fall into the abyss of darkness. Alone and helpless, terror and sorrow will surround you and gnaw at your body and soul like ants eating flesh...

speaker: Stargazer
content: You are destined to walk through each and every painful hardship in your future journey.
Well, doesn't seem like any of these cards bring happiness.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Indeed, indeed... but you have me, my little monster.

speaker: Stargazer
content: I was able to make you suffer, then rise from the ashes in WhiteSands... Naturally, I can also save you from this false world and guide you to the path of truth.
Where is that path? How can you be sure that the truth lies at the end of it?

speaker: Stargazer
content: All you have to do is follow me... My powers won't deceive me. You are very important to me.

speaker: Stargazer
content: My companion, you are the key to the Realm of Truth.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Endless darkness lies beneath your blue pupils...

speaker: Stargazer
content: But, there is a hidden path to the truth in them...
You look to the side and the dark screen reflects your eyes, where a hint of its turquoise hue can be seen.

speaker: Stargazer
content: The Dreamflower shall return to the Void, and you shall give this false world the ending it deserves! You... shall unlock the truest Enlightenment!
Alright, Miss Stargazer. I don't have the time or energy to play along with your prophecies.
But if you tell me this so-called "path of truth" is near DisSea, I'd be happy to hear more about it.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Hehe... Perhaps it is?

speaker: Stargazer
content: The path of truth lies in where your sight goes. That's why I've been so infatuated with you.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Why... my little monster?

speaker: Stargazer
content: Behind those eyes as blue as the ocean and sky, is deep and empty darkness...

speaker: Stargazer
content: Yet I found a path towards the truth in that darkness... Though the Dreamflower returned to the Void, I am still searching in this false world... Could your body be the Realm of Truth? Could your soul be... the key?
Stargazer laughs as her voice starts to tremble.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Hahaha... This world feeds everyone with foolishness and mistakes, which ultimately transform into sin inside one's belly.

speaker: Stargazer
content: When evil rises and gnaws at their brain and spirit, people become blinded by falsehood.
I think I can see clearly right now.
Stargazer looks at you, her purple eyes as bright as the moon, twinkling with a hint of insanity.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Yes, I know you won't lose your way... After all, you are the darling of WhiteSands, welcomed even by the Void.

speaker: Stargazer
content: But here, even you will be overwhelmed by the hostile glares of all those scums.
I won't be.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Trust my prophecy... My little monster.

speaker: Stargazer
content: I'm here to save you.
I think I'm safer now than I was in WhiteSands.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Little monster, in this chaotic world, everyone has moments when they can't see their surroundings clearly.

speaker: Stargazer
content: And here... There is neither sunshine nor starlight.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Not to mention clear moonbeam.
Stargazer holds out her hand as if invoking the descent of the gods.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Yes... I can feel it...

speaker: Stargazer
content: Your worries emit the same salty smell as the desert.

speaker: Stargazer
content: But you need not be afraid...

speaker: Stargazer
content: Only absurdity and falsehood will devour souls.
Stargazer's words make little sense, but they carry a power that cannot be ignored.
It chokes the spirit like an unforgiving tide that rises with the moonlight, forcing one down a path of no return.

speaker: Stargazer
content: A journey filled with confusion and deception... A cast of vile and callous villains... Ultimately, you will be trapped in the lofty tower...
Is this the ending of your prophecy?

speaker: Stargazer
content: Yes... and they shall all come true.
I was able to survive WhiteSands last time. I can overcome this prophecy, too.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Then, time and fate will tell.
Sometimes, time and fate cannot escape the manipulation of humans.
You reach out and flip over the middle card, placing it before yourself.
A fourth tarot card appears on the table, which has been covered by the card you just flipped over.
Please explain this, Miss Stargazer.
Stargazer looks at the fourth card on the table and laughs soundlessly.
She picks up the card gently, squinting her eyes.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Just like you said... Time and fate cannot escape the manipulation of humans.

speaker: Stargazer
content: You have put this card in your future, with your own hands.
And what does this card represent?

speaker: Stargazer
content: This flag and scythe couldn't be any more obvious.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Someone has drilled a hole, draining the contents inside and leaving but a dry shell.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Death... this hollow and fragile oak barrel represents a bleak death!
The path I take may not be your so-called "path of truth." I'm also well aware that this path is filled with dangers and thorns, and that at its end is the end of everything.
But these hardships will become my armor and sharpen my blade.
I will not let these so-called prophecies slow down my journey. Thank you for your advice, Miss Stargazer.
Stargazer cackles shrilly, sending a chill down the spine of everyone present.
The others still glare at her with a mixture of fear and malice.
What breaks this stalemate is an urgent order from the superior.

speaker: FAC Liaison Officer
content: Chief! There is an urgent request for help from the Broken Frontline in DisSea.

speaker: FAC Liaison Officer
content: A well-equipped team has attacked the base station near BR-000! That's the weakest point of the shield...

speaker: FAC Liaison Officer
content: We've also detected a sharp spike in M-value at the Frontline. Either there are Sinners assisting the attack, or... the attackers are already Corruptors.
So much for the interrogation. I'll be right over.
You glance at Stargazer. She still sits calmly before you with a smile on her face.
You pack up your things and turn to leave. An exotic scent seeps into your nose, putting you into a dizzy stupor, and you hear a voice from the distance.

speaker: Stargazer
content: O Morning Star, O Morning Star...

speaker: Stargazer
content: Why do you fall from the sky, nine days and nights...

speaker: Stargazer
content: The journey of confusion and uncertainty is about to begin... my little monster...

Below a base station outside BR-000, you put on your breathing mask. Blue dust floating by your cheeks goes in and out of the filter as you breathe. The monsters' roars coming in from a distance add to the already tense atmosphere.
After receiving the call for help, you immediately brought a small group of police officers toward the frontline.
Yet you were greeted by dozens of plainly dressed corpses and silent guardsmen.
They were the ones who tried to attack the Broken Frontline.
The leader of the group, wearing an FAC uniform, steps forward to answer your question.

speaker: Cole
content: I'm Cole, the bo... the Captain here. Err, I mean the person in charge. They usually call me Boss.

speaker: Cole
content: Those on the ground said that the government had taken away their resources for survival and made life a living hell for them. They were convinced that the government's resources are kept under the shield of the base station.

speaker: Cole
content: They said... they're here to take back what belongs to them.
It is true that there have been rumors like this.
But I don't think that should be a reason to kill them off.
You frown and look at Cole.

speaker: Cole
content: They said something was installed on the base station that made them unable to sleep, so they attacked us with a bunch of believers or just troublemakers.

speaker: Cole
content: They claimed that we set up the base stations here to prevent civilians from approaching and to evict them.

speaker: Cole
content: They may be dressed up as civilians, but hidden under their clothes are knives and guns.

options: Explain why you're here and the rules

content: I'm the Chief of MBCC. I was asked to support when I received news that the M values here were rising and there were possible attacks of Corruptors or Sinners.
To avoid Mania to spread any further, you should've dealt with them only after I determined whether their M-value has reached the critical point.
Besides, even dead bodies might spread Mania contamination.

speaker: Cole
content: You are... the chief of MBCC?
Cole touched the Hypercube pyramid before his chest, and took a few glances at you.
Yes.
You ask the FAC officers to maintain order with the frontline personnel and begin looking at the bodies for possible infections.

speaker: FAC Officer
content: Chief, the force field shield from the base station shows signs of being attacked.

speaker: FAC Officer
content: But it doesn't seem like mania weapons were used.

Hearing this, you leave the body you're checking and start to survey the Broken Frontline's base station shields. They seem more likely to be worn by the blades and guns of Syndicate's gangsters and Outlanders.
Weird...
The Broken Frontline is the weakest protection for BR-000. The distressing atmosphere of DisSea is almost breaking through the shields and drowning all of you, nauseating and anguishing.
Ordinary people will not come to a place like this for such reasons. And these marks and the wounds on the corpses are clearly from the same weapons.
The wounds on the corpses were not caused by an FAC weapon. You are not...

speaker: Cole
content: You're kinda smart, huh?
The moment you turn around, the barrel of a cold gun is pressed against your forehead. The men you brought are already under their control without making a sound.

speaker: Cole
content: From what I've heard from these corpses, the base stations are managed by some MC thing, and you happen to be the chief.

speaker: Cole
content: Be a good kid and open this thing up.

speaker: Cole
content: Or else... you'll become a part of that pile.
The base stations keep death and contamination away! There's nothing that you want inside!
Opening it up will only make your infection worse!

speaker: Cole
content: So... you're not gonna cooperate?

Cole signals his men with his eyes. Since your arrival, those men have been hanging around your officers. Once they receive the cue, they skillfully stab into the fragile gaps of the protective suits, killing all your officers.

speaker: FAC Officer
content: Ahhhhhhh—!
The metallic smell of blood rushed in all of a sudden. As if felt the smell, DisSea rose a wave of fear and suppression that filled the air in a second. It is suffocating.
You!
Before you can say anything, your lost balance and felt dizzy. Your palms and knees are grazed by the gravel. Cole slammed you hard on the ground, looking down at you while stepping on the rubble.

speaker: Cole
content: Tough, eh? Let's see how long you can last.
Cole turned around and fired several shots in quick succession at the Broken Frontline.
Stop it!
The bullet pierced Cole's palm but you saw no blood. Instead, a thick, reeking liquid came out...
You've become a Maniac!

speaker: Cole
content: Ah... having wandered in DisSea for so long, how could I possibly not gain the devil's favor?

speaker: Cole
content: But I am very fond of this power...

speaker: Cole
content: Are you afraid, Chief of the MBCC?
This power is beyond your control and you will only end up being infected further until finally being corrupted by it.
Cole kicked the gun out of your hand. With a single swing, he slammed you onto the shield.
Despite the pain, you drew out your gun, ran toward Cole, and pressed it against his chest.

speaker: Cole
content: Ha... The chief from MBCC has some guts. I'll give you that.

speaker: Cole
content: But unfortunately, you won't be able to kill me now.
Cole gave a sinister expression and thrust himself toward you.

speaker: Cole
content: Come on, shoot me. Oh, that's right... You, Chief, just said we need your approval before killing anyone, no matter who it is.
You look at the twisted face of Cole. The black liquid splashed on his protective suit. The Hypercube pyramid on it is quickly turning red and getting smaller. He is beyond saving.
Cole took advantage of your hesitation and brutally slammed your head against the base station.

speaker: Cole
content: It doesn't matter if you don't cooperate. We were planning on taking this step anyway.
The sharp pain from your scalp extended to your tailbone. Cole tossed you to the ground by your hair.

He ordered his men to take up guns or even small artillery and begin bombarding the Broken Frontline. The cracks in the shield got bigger and made a crunching sound. The force field covering DisSea is starting to weaken.
Stop!!!

Your wounds are giving you tearing pain, but they're the least of your problems. You press the communicator, requesting immediate support from HQ. In the meantime, you grab a weapon from one of the corpses, giving Cole a flurry of attacks.

speaker: Cole
content: Hah! That doesn't even tickle!

speaker: Cole
content: Are you really the chief or something? How about you let me take your place!
Cole took on your attacks and got close to you quickly, putting one hand around your neck. He picked you up and crushed you against a nearby abandoned statue.

speaker: Cole
content: Hahaha...hahaha!!! Do you feel my power!

speaker: Cole
content: Why not save your strength? Once we make a hole in it, I need you to lead the way... Or I guess I could just kill you right now.
Being strangled, the air in your throat is escaping, and your vision starts to get blurry.
A flash of bright color walked into your sight, when you thought you were about to die from strangulation on this abandoned statue.
Look who's deep in prison, trapped in the tower...
My poor little monster, fear no more...

speaker: Cole
content: A woman?
Cole looked up at the woman standing on the statue, but her hood covered her eyes so he couldn't see clearly.

speaker: Cole
content: That's your backup? Just this woman?

speaker: Stargazer
content: It's just some howling animals...

speaker: Stargazer
content: I am more than enough.

speaker: Cole
content: How dare you...
Before Cole could finish, several black light balls exploded in his face, causing him to let go of his hands.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Hmph, get a taste of the other side.
A tarot card flew out of her hand into the shield that they have been frantically bombarding.

The card seemed to freeze the cracked base station for a while, and many shield pieces were shaken off from it. Through those little gaps, everyone saw the dark and crimson interlaced with little blue lights, like the pastel blue sapphire.

speaker: Smuggler
content: Boss! Hypercubes... it's Hypercubes!!!

speaker: Cole
content: Hahahah! I knew it! There are a great many Hypercubes stored inside!
Seeing the blue color, Cole's eyes turned red. He didn't seem to care about the blood flowing from his head at all and crazily rushed toward the gaps.
No... *cough, you can't. You're already...

speaker: Stargazer
content: Where are you going, my little monster?
The woman standing on the high ground leaps down and grabs onto you to look at the surge of people and black smoke on the other side of the station.
They are like bloodthirsty leeches that are greedily sucking in the slightest bit of scent coming from DisSea.

speaker: Stargazer
content: The smell of Hypercubes, the smell of death, the smell of money...

speaker: Stargazer
content: To these outlaws, money outweighs life.
I know... that they are Hypercube smugglers from Outland.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Oh? You knew already, my little monster?

speaker: Stargazer
content: But it seems like they won't last long.
No, *cough... We can't let them open the shield!
The Hypercubes in Syndicate are all contaminated by Mania! If they live on them, they must have long been infected!
We knew that there has always been a group of ghost-like smugglers in DisSea... Never thought I would meet them here...
Their M values have passed the critical point. If they get any closer... they'll turn into Corruptors!

speaker: Cole
content: Piss off! I'll do it myself, you trash! Hahahahah!
Losing his mind, Cole pushed his man viciously away.
The abandoned statue behind him is covered with sharp debris, but Cole did not care at all about falling on it. All he could think about are Hypercubes.

speaker: Stargazer
content: They deceived you and you still want to save them?

speaker: Stargazer
content: They are greedy and cunning... donning themselves in sheep's skin to deceive the innocent.

speaker: Stargazer
content: They are cruel and ignorant... digging their own graves.

speaker: Stargazer
content: You destroyed people like them when you were at WhiteSands. Why do you want to help them and even... save them now?
That's not helping them.

speaker: Stargazer
content: The tower has been erected. No one can escape the punishment of the world. People like them will not be able to live until the end.
But in the face of a catastrophe, everyone is equal.
If the station is destroyed, the crisis in DisSea will escalate! Many more will die!
I can't possibly...!
What are you doing?!

Stargazer lifted you by your collar and pinned you against the statue. You were startled and instinctively tried to use the shackles. DisSea was surging, as if it's waiting for you to release the shackles in excitement.
The fluctuations of the shackles hummed in the depths of your mind, calling you to be alert to DisSea's temptations, and to... the person in front of you.

speaker: Stargazer
content: My divination, my prophecy...  will not be so easily broken.

speaker: Stargazer
content: The outcomes are inevitable, Chief. There's nothing you can do to change them.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Of course... you can choose to bind me with your shackles and take the helm of your own destiny.
It's a strange sight. If it isn't for the tension between you and Stargazer, some eccentric artist must be willing to paint this scene for you.
While the armed mob of raspy-voiced miscreants try to break through the shield at the beleaguered base station, a tense face-off quietly unfolds on the abandoned statue nearby.

speaker: Stargazer
content: There are two paths before you, my little monster.
Stargazer is smiling, but you can sense the veiled threat in her tone.

speaker: Stargazer
content: My prophecies are coming true one by one. A lost path, a cast of villains, a disaster... death will soon come up next. You can choose to either seek my help, or to resist...

speaker: Stargazer
content: For example... To avoid dying here, you can bind me with your shackles and let me handle those who have mutated into monsters.

options: Is this your prophecy or a conspiracy?

content: You must know that if I use my shackles here, I'll be swallowed by DisSea. After what those people and you have done, the shield is already on the verge of collapse.
Stargazer smiled and pulled you deeper into her embrace.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Isn't that good?

speaker: Stargazer
content: A skimmer can't trap fine grains of sand, just like this world can't trap you and me. We can walk into the Mirage of Truth together...

speaker: Stargazer
content: You can no longer go back, little monster.
Stargazer pressed against your ear. Her warm breath grazed the tips of your hair, making you shudder.

speaker: Stargazer
content: No matter how hard you struggle, it will all descend.
I just don't believe in prophesied fate, nor do I accept arrangements by others.
I can resolve everything, whether it's them... or you.
Stargazer pressed her head to the side of your neck and giggled as if she heard something funny.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Hahaha... Oh my little monster, are you trying to amuse me?

speaker: Stargazer
content: In this world, everyone indulges in the jubilance of falsehood. They discard the weak and grovel for wealth under whatever pretext, before finally drowning in the reality they've woven.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Only you... You appeared in my dream, in the purest of places, and you've put aside everything in your way... You have the desire to seek the truth.
Stargazer stared at you deeply, as if to find the path to truth in your eyes.
Why did you choose me?
Because I appeared in your dreams? Or because I witnessed the Dreamflower's slumber with you?

speaker: Stargazer
content: I think that's more than enough reason... little monster, you're a special one.
I cannot accept such a reason.
Even if this world is false, it has bestowed upon me responsibility... And for that, I will not abandon it.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Every day... every day... you are surrounded by lies.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Do you think your companions have kept no secrets from you?
Stargazer spun the crystal ball in her hand. The dark mist inside twisted and turned, gradually spreading to form a wasteland.

speaker: Strange Roars
content: Roarrrr...!! Ahhh...!!
Unable to get to the treasures behind the shield, the Hypercube smugglers screech in frustration.

speaker: Cole
content: Outta my way, morons! You dumb ****!

speaker: Cole
content: There's no **** way you can get these without me!

speaker: Cole
content: These are all mine alone! You won't even get close to my ****!

speaker: Smuggler A
content: ***! These are mine! No one can **** take them away, ****, not even you!

speaker: Smuggler B
content: Hell no!! Hell no!!
Restrained in place, you can only watch as they grow ever more berserk.
Are you using your powers? They wouldn't be killing each other otherwise!

speaker: Stargazer
content: Indeed, perhaps it is divine will that our kind can peer into people's hearts...

speaker: Stargazer
content: Thus I did gain some kind of power by peering into a corner of the Void.

speaker: Stargazer
content: However... the desires of the human heart are all too easily exposed.

speaker: Stargazer
content: You say that I used my power to make them fight?
Stargazer brought the crystal ball before you. You saw the dark mist rolling inside it, but felt no fluctuations from her power.

speaker: Stargazer
content: I don't need to use any powers at all... Just whisper a few words in their ears, and they will reveal their rawest desires like an open book.

speaker: Stargazer
content: There are countless people like them in this world. They are everywhere around you! Why do you think they fear me and want you to suppress me?

speaker: Stargazer
content: Think about those around you, my dear. Why have they fallen? Why do they avert their gaze from me?
You remembered how the people looked at you and Stargazer back at the WhiteSands shelter and Syndicate black market. You recalled their eyes, filled with awe, fear... and hatred.

speaker: Stargazer
content: They've hidden many things from you. That's why they feel guilty.

speaker: Stargazer
content: All those people in that city... Surely you aren't naive enough to believe that they are all your friends?

options: You're right. I don't trust them.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Mankind is prone to holding blind faith. Once they realize they've put faith in a false made-up deity, the world will march towards destruction.

speaker: Stargazer
content: The shattering of the deity will bring devastating damage. You'll be riddled with scars, little monster.
No one can live in this world in one piece, Miss Stargazer.
You can't guarantee that I'll be unscathed even in the Realm of Truth.

speaker: Stargazer
content: No, you can trust me!
Doesn't your unshakable trust in the Dreamflower count as blind faith as well?

speaker: Stargazer
content: What an unexpected answer.
There is no such thing as unshakable trust in this world.

speaker: Stargazer
content: That's right. There isn't.
But there is unshakable bond.
The bond may be between people, or between someone and something.

It's true they're not completely loyal to me, but when it comes to "protecting", we can temporarily put aside our doubts, calculations, and disdain to each other, and form a type of unbreakable "trust."
Stargazer lowered her head, obscuring her expression.

speaker: Stargazer
content: You have a way with words... even if these words are filled with blind ignorance.
I don't care why the Dreamflower chose me, but I know why destiny chose me here in this reality.

speaker: Stargazer
content: O you who have been blinded...

speaker: Stargazer
content: Haven't you ever considered... that you, who is created by this world, are also a false one?
What did you say?
Stargazer's face is now as cold as the moon rising over WhiteSands. You've never seen her so serious before.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Oh my little monster... My dear Chief of MBCC...

speaker: Stargazer
content: Are you... someone who really, truly exists here?
Her whispers rang in your ears, but before you could ask her what she means, she loosened her grip on you.
You can suddenly breathe smoothly again. The pungent DisSea air floods your nostrils, plunging you into a fit of coughs.
Cough...

speaker: Stargazer
content: In that case, let me ask you one more time.
With a flick of her wrist, the last star card drawn in the interrogation room appeared in Stargazer's right hand.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Will you continue to bear this false and invisible destiny, or will you join me on the path of truth?
With a card in hand, Stargazer approached you step by step. The awe exuding from her body inadvertently made you take a step backward...
Oh no...!
Misjudging the statue's proportions, your foot landed in the air and you fell backward.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Don't run, my little monster.
The person in front of you reached out and grabbed your collar, leaving you suspended above the ruins.
Her sharp fingernails scraped across your cheeks. Amidst the stinging pain, you felt a small stream trickle down your face.

speaker: Stargazer
content: You despise my prophesying game and want to overturn my predictions. Yet now, your life is literally in my hands.

The Broken Frontline's shield shattered. Bearing the full brunt of DisSea's contamination, the infected attackers rapidly devolved into Corruptors. As their consciousness dissipates, Hypercubes no longer attract them. They turned to... you.
As madness eclipsed greed, they now thirst for your blood more than they did for Hypercubes.

speaker: Stargazer
content: They're coming, and they'll devour you if I let go. If you use your shackles... I'll be quite happy. Let's answer DisSea's calls together. They'll embrace our truest selves, just like the Dreamflower...

speaker: Stargazer
content: So, will you become my companion?

speaker: Stargazer
content: I'll save you from being devoured by the ants, and from hanging on the branches...
Thank you for your kind offer, but...
The jacket sheathing your arm slipped off, revealing the pistol in your hand that you have been hiding.
I choose to overturn the prophecy by myself.

speaker: Stargazer
content: What are you doing?!
You clench the hand gripping onto you and press the muzzle of your gun against it.
You pull the trigger without hesitation, making Stargazer lose her grip immediately.
The gunshot reverberates painfully in your ears and brain. You watch your surroundings whirl by as the Corruptors' noises become clearer and clearer.
I won.
You're not sure if you managed to say this out loud, but you did your best to express it during your fall.

speaker: Stargazer
content: So this is your answer?
I have the right to shoot in defense against a Sinner's threat.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Don't you... have an easier way?
Are you trying to direct me to use my shackles?
I don't know what you're plotting, but I have my own principles... In other words, I don't think it's the right time to use the shackles.
Stargazer's usual smile has gone. She looks at you coldly as she speaks.

speaker: Stargazer
content: In that case... Farewell, little monster.
Stargazer let go of her grip, and you were immediately immersed by the weightlessness of falling.
As you slammed into the rotting bodies, you caught a glimpse of Stargazer's eyes before the surging Corruptors completely enveloped you.
They are madly purple, just like the door at the end of the path to the Realm of Truth.
The monsters instantly overwhelmed the fallen one.
The soaring M-value has transformed all the greedy, brutal thugs into Corruptors. Their avarice is on display for all to see.

speaker: Stargazer
content: How hopelessly ignorant...

speaker: Stargazer
content: In the face of truth, falsehood, and your so-called responsibility...

speaker: Stargazer
content: ...You end up choosing death.
Stargazer jumped down from the ruins and coldly watched the incoming Corruptors howl as they besiege their prey.

speaker: Stargazer
content: The prophesying game always exposes the ugly desires and feared truths of humans.

speaker: Stargazer
content: I should've gotten used to it by now.

speaker: Stargazer
content: It's a pity that, in the end, you cannot be my...
Stargazer turned away. Her face filled with disappointment, as if she has seen a half-eaten apple.
She waved her hand and cast her power to exacerbate the monsters' cravings, like giving her little monster a funeral in her own way.
But just as she left, gunshots rang out from the pile of monsters behind her.

speaker: Stargazer
content: What...?
Stargazer froze for a bit, and she turned around to see a gap in the encirclement, broken through by a single pistol.
From that small, dark gap, a strong force shot through and bound Stargazer with fearsome strength.

speaker: Stargazer
content: It's... the shackles...!
Stargazer could feel her own power frozen as the thorn-like force pierced her wrists and neck.
The caster of this force is standing amidst the seething monsters.
He is riddled with wounds, and the pitch-black liquid seeping into his eyes obscures his vision. Yet he stands tall without flinching, and says to Stargazer—
female_content: She is riddled with wounds, and the pitch-black liquid seeping into her eyes obscures her vision. Yet she stands tall without flinching, and says to Stargazer—

options: Protect me. Don't let me die.

speaker: Stargazer
content: You used your shackles...? Aren't you afraid...!
Sinners cannot disobey orders from the shackles. Stargazer's hand twitched gently and began to attack the Corruptors around you.
Of course I'm not afraid...
You gaze towards the pitch-black DisSea, where shapeless screams are beckoning you to come.

I shall be the one to decide who takes part in my destiny, when and how they take part, and where my grave shall be... I know at least that I won't be there just yet. My shackles and Sinners... are my strongest weapons.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Hahaha... In that case, I can only... obey your command.
You brandish your pistol, slaying the frenzied monsters alongside Stargazer.
Though without Stargazer's exacerbating power, the thugs were desperados to begin with, and they've only grown more violent after mutating into Corruptors.

speaker: Stargazer
content: There are people like these everywhere in this world.

speaker: Stargazer
content: No one can guarantee that they won't become such a monster after exposing their innermost desires.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Your so-called protection is also shielding them.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Without shackles or Sinners, you'd die from their bites.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Are you still going to persist even if the truth is so ugly?
Stargazer's expression changed slightly upon hearing your answer.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Oh? You finally had an epiphany after a visit to the gates of hell?
You turned and pointed your gun at Stargazer. Locking your gaze onto hers, you pulled the trigger. The bullet grazed her hood and hit the Corruptor sneaking up behind her square in the forehead.
I will not shield them.
Stargazer uses her power to restrain the monsters who are still writhing forward despite having their hands and feet pierced by you. She then motioned for you to continue speaking.
You walk over to the restrained Corruptor with your gun raised, shut your eyes and fire into its vital organs.
The crisis is resolved as the last Corruptor is wiped out. Calm finally returns to the chaotic Broken Frontline. You gaze at the once again tranquil DisSea as you speak to Stargazer.
Like I said, I'm well aware that this path is filled with danger, and that at its end is the end of everything.
This world is filled with crises, but I'm already an integral part of it.
Stargazer's crystal ball began to spin, but there's no longer dark mist swirling inside.
Like grains of sand from WhiteSands, the pure white particles gathered little by little, emitting a faint glow.

speaker: Stargazer
content: What are you thinking about?

speaker: Stargazer
content: You're clearly able to repudiate all arrangements given to you, then why do you still linger in this world?

speaker: Stargazer
content: You're someone who can reach the truth. I've been hardly able to find any companion in this world, except for you.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Thus, even if you awaken to a chaotic haze, and your body is but a false shell, I still wish to go with you.
Stargazer watched you shoot all the Corruptors she restrained. After you wiped out all the Corruptors, she came forward to gently wipe the stains off your face.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Little monster... you are both an executor and a guardian.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Both a pioneer and a nostalgic.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Who... are you exactly?
I don't know.
But perhaps that's why I accepted this arrangement and destiny.
I shall explore this world as an executor, a guardian, a pioneer, and a nostalgic.

speaker: Stargazer
content: Even if this world is false?
Even if this world is false.
You say that my body is but a false shell, that you can't see my soul, and that endless darkness lies beneath my eyes.
Then can I assume, after all the lies and suffering I've encountered are devoured, drowned out, and broken down by this abyssal body...
...A soul of my own will then be born?

speaker: Stargazer
content: A soul will be born?
A twisted expression dawned on Stargazer's face, as if she had just witnessed something incredible.
You shrug and look around, spotting your tattered, blood-soaked jacket.
You walk over and take out something from the inner pocket—Stargazer's final tarot card that represents death. Yet behind that card, you find another one...

speaker: Stargazer
content: Still think you've won?

speaker: Stargazer
content: Even if you've bound me with your shackles now, in essence, you did not overturn my prophecy.

speaker: Stargazer
content: You will still...
I won.
I won, Anarkia. I overturned your prophecy.
You say the name softly and smile at Stargazer's stunned expression.

speaker: Anarkia
content: Hahahahaha!

speaker: Anarkia
content: Well played! Overturning my prophecy, changing destiny!

speaker: Anarkia
content: Alas, I am so curious...!

speaker: Anarkia
content: You always manage to surprise me, little monster!

speaker: Anarkia
content: You've won this game, little monster. The victory is yours.

speaker: Anarkia
content: I saw through this world and found the Realm of Truth. You discovered my real name and you're determined to change your destiny.

content: I've decided to stay by your side, little monster...

speaker: Anarkia
content: I'm just too curious!

content: When a false body gives birth to a real soul, what will be its ultimate fate?

speaker: Anarkia

speaker: Anarkia
content: The flesh, blood, skin, and thoughts of humans are all one mask upon another, used to create a facade of truth.

speaker: Anarkia

speaker: Anarkia
content: You accept the falsehood of your existence, yet still strive to seek the truth...

speaker: Anarkia
content: Dragging along your false shell of a body, you seek your true soul...

content: I must thank the Dreamflower for helping me find you... Hahahaha!

Etti?

speaker: Etti
content: Zzz... Zzz...

speaker: Etti
content: No... You can't break the rules...!

speaker: Etti

speaker: Etti

content: Here, I'm just a regular...

content: Tell you everything?

speaker: Etti

speaker: Etti

speaker: Etti

I can already guess what you've done. I'll give you a chance to confess on your own. I'll be lenient if you cooperate.

content: Huh? This quick?! Hey, are you doing this on purpose?

speaker: Etti
content: ...The God of Fate really knows how to screw us over.
"Fate always likes to play tricks on people."
You shrug under Etti's displeased gaze.

speaker: Etti
content: Oh well. You already said the sun will set earlier, so I'll accept this. It's dark already, so it's too late.

speaker: Etti
content: In any case, it's our first time at this bazaar, and there's a lot we're unfamiliar with. It might not be useful to set up a stall so quickly anyways.

speaker: Etti
content: Let's just take a look around today. We'll set up the stall tomorrow if need be.

speaker: Etti
content: But it's dark now. It might be dangerous to just brashly barge into the bazaar. I want to scout the situation inside first.
Etti motions for you to bring over the dice.
Etti puts the dice in her hands, shakes them gently, then casts them in your direction.
You reach out to catch the dice. When you look down at your palms—it's a critical success.
"Etti the Mage jumps onto a building next to the alley to get a bird's-eye view of the whole bazaar."
"As she expected, the bazaar is a den of chaos. The people rushing to and fro are all quite mysterious. She can tell that most of them are just here to eke out a living."
"They aren't threats to us, but probably won't have any useful information."

speaker: Etti
content: "They aren't threats to us." Affirmative. But "probably won't have any useful information" means there's still a possibility.

speaker: Etti
content: Well... since "fate" didn't shut me down, that means... we can safely go in for a look.
After thinking for a moment, Etti leads Hella and Ninety-Nine into the alley.
The alley is completely empty, but Etti scrutinizes each and every intersection with extreme care. Even Hella can't help but mimic her and look left and right.

speaker: Etti
content: Let's see, what shops are around here?
"The most common shops at the bazaar are those selling food and potions, such as brown bread made from easily-grown brown rice, and healing potions with a dash of magic."
"There are also a few mysterious-looking shops scattered in the depths of the bazaar."

speaker: Etti
content: I'm curious about that shop to the right. It has a blue sofa in front of it.

speaker: Etti
content: Shall we go over and take a look?
Holding onto a sign on the wall with one hand, Etti stands on her tiptoes on the stone pillar as she calls out to you below.
You raise your head and take over the dialogue.
"As the adventurers look for shops that might offer some clues, they hear a voice in the alley."
You slip your hand into your pocket and gently press the comms device in there twice.
After some clangs and gasps from a nearby alley, you finally hear a female voice.
Oh! My lost little lambs, what do you seek?
Oh, just look at your timid and piteous little eyes!!
Why don't you come serve me—the great, noble, and powerful West District Overlord, EMP. Perhaps I can help guide your fate...
The familiar voice stutters at first, but becomes smooth and eloquent as time goes on. Everyone can tell what she's doing.

speaker: Hella
content: Pfft... I'm a hundred percent sure she added those lines herself. What nonsense...

speaker: Etti
content: Oh? The West District Overlord? How interesting... I wasn't expecting to gain anything today, but...

speaker: Etti
content: It seems that fate has pointed out a fairly obvious route for us.
Etti leaps forth and lands beside you with a faint smile.
"Although the adventurers are bit wary of this voice, the important thing right now is to gather clues. Hence they decide to go meet the West District Overlord."
You turn away your face somewhat nervously and nudge Hella and Ninety-Nine, who are behind Etti.

speaker: Hella
content: Hmph! So what if she's the West District Overlord? She's probably nowhere near as smart, witty or lovely as Hella.

speaker: Hella
content: Don't worry, Mage Etti! Go exchange info with her if you wish! I've got you covered!

speaker: EMP
content: Ha! You've got her covered? Can you even jump high enough to touch her staff?

speaker: Hella
content: Hmph! Is your IQ number even as big as her shoe size?

speaker: EMP
content: How dare you!!
A gust of wind blows by. The "West District Overlord" had emerged from the alley, making her grand debut before you.
Like Hella, her face is brimming with delusions of grandeur.

speaker: EMP
content: Listen up, dwarf! I have clues about the legendary castle!

speaker: EMP
content: This is a priceless clue that even money can't buy! Prostrate before me if you want it!

speaker: Etti
content: Your clue is about the legendary castle?
Upon hearing EMP's words, Etti steps in front of Hella and stares at EMP.

speaker: EMP
content: Y-yes. Why? Are you interested?
EMP gulps and shoots a nervous glance at you.
You make a fist to encourage her.

speaker: EMP
content: Well, young lady, I see from your eyes how deft and determined you are. I can tell that you have great talent. Want to strike a deal with me and become my sworn sister?

speaker: Etti
content: Me? How did you realize that I'm the most perfect Mage in the world who wields unparalleled control over fate and destiny?
EMP freezes, at a loss for words.

speaker: EMP
content: Well... I didn't realize that actually...

speaker: Etti
content: Really?! You didn't??
Etti fixes her gaze on EMP, as if EMP is about to say something critical.

speaker: EMP
content: Am I... supposed to?

speaker: Etti
content: Prepare for battle, my friends.

speaker: Hella
content: Haha, yessir!

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: All right. Who shall we attack?

speaker: Hella
content: This Syndicate swindler in front of us, of course!

speaker: Etti
content: How dare you play such tricks right under my nose... You actually have no idea whether the clue in your hands is real or not!

speaker: EMP
content: Wh-what?
"Etti the Mage thinks that EMP the West District Overlord is not sincere in working with her and is full of lies, so she decides to attack."

speaker: EMP
content: I was not asking to work together with her!
"Thoroughly intimidated by Etti's presence, EMP skips for one turn."

speaker: EMP
content: Huh?! Isn't that cheating?!

speaker: Etti
content: It's fate, my dear.

speaker: Etti
content: Ninety-Nine! Use your berserk skill!

speaker: Etti
content: Now, hehe... Hella, you can start putting your thieving skills to good use. Go get us some clues.
Etti finishes prepping all the skills, brings you to the middle, and casts the dice.
The dice roll gently on the ground and stop on the number 1.

speaker: EMP
content: ...A-a-a critical failure?! Hahaha...
"Uh... uh... Ninety-Nine the Barbarian attacks EMP viciously, but EMP manages to dodge her huge sword!"
"Plus, EMP uses the rebound force from the giant sword to attack everyone in the adventurers' team—her real identity is a Bard!"
EMP takes out her bow and arrow and leans forward in a horse stance. She points her bow to the sky, shouting—

speaker: EMP
content: You... you forced me to do this!

speaker: Etti
content: Tsk, quite the troublemaker, isn't she?

speaker: Etti
content: If you don't want to die here, get as close to me as possible!

speaker: Etti
content: I'm going to cast a defensive spell!
Too bad the God of Fate didn't take Etti's side this time. The group falls into silence after seeing the number on the dice.
"E...EMP unleashes a hail of arrows, p-piercing through Mage Etti's defensive spell..."
"Even though EMP the West District Overlord loses her ability to move, the adventurers are also forced to halt their quest because of their heavy injuries..."
The dice hit the ground heavily. EMP's legs go limp and slumps to the ground when she sees the number on it.

speaker: EMP
content: It's a... critical success! P-please have mercy... At the very least, s-spare the face!

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: Taste my boiling rage!
