A flash of red dashes by. Wielding her blade, Ninety-Nine appears behind EMP.
But EMP doesn't get completely defeated just yet!

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: She dodged the attack!
"Having acquired excellent dodging skills from her years surviving in the West District, EMP manages to escape Ninety-Nine's fatal strike!"

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: Etti, watch out! She's coming for you!

speaker: EMP
content: Hahaha! Messenger of the dragons my butt! Taste my triple-stacked flash arrow! Pew pew pew pew pew!

speaker: Hella
content: You Syndicate swindler! Who puts all the points into dexterity just to dodge attacks?!

speaker: Hella
content: Etti, watch out!
Wielding her water pipe, Hella steps in front of Etti to protect her.

speaker: Hella
content: Mages shouldn't get involved in melee combat! Watch me destroy your flash arrows!

speaker: Etti
content: H-Hella?
The light from the flash arrows suddenly becomes blindingly bright. Everyone can't help but cover their eyes.
When the light subsides, you see Etti and Hella standing side by side. Perched on Hella's nose is a pair of oversized sunglasses.
You recognize them as the pair she got from the staff when she left the interrogation room.

speaker: EMP
content: Where... where did those sunglasses come from?!

speaker: Etti
content: It's a treasure from my vault—my Dark Abyss Conjoined Lenses!

speaker: Hella
content: They're sunglasses.

speaker: Etti
content: Dark Abyss Conjoined Lenses.
"Because Etti swiftly gives Hella a pair of sunglasses..."

speaker: Etti
content: Dark Abyss Conjoined Lenses!
"...Dark Abyss Conjoined Lenses, Hella the Rogue not only dodged EMP the Bard's attack, but also used the lenses' reflection to destroy EMP's remaining stamina!"

speaker: EMP
content: Huh?! I'm gone, just like that?! I still have a lot of lines left...
Huh?

speaker: EMP
content: Ah... never mind, never mind. Cough cough...
EMP holds her forehead dramatically, spins on the spot, then kneels onto the ground.

speaker: EMP
content: As I meet my demise... I want to ask you...

speaker: EMP
content: Mage Etti, how on earth did you know... that I didn't know if the clue was real or not...?
Etti adjusts her hat and vest, clears her throat, and walks back and forth in front of EMP.

speaker: Etti
content: Your acting was 99% perfect, but... that missing 1% gave it away.

speaker: Etti
content: You refused to hand over the clue to me directly, meaning that you didn't acknowledge that I'm the most perfect Mage in the world who wields unparalleled control over fate and destiny.

speaker: Etti
content: In other words, you had no idea whether the clue was real or fake. You just wanted someone to help you identify its authenticity for free.
After finishing her speech, Etti looks back confidently and flashes EMP a haughty smile.

speaker: EMP
content: S-so... that's why! I-I was too weak!

speaker: EMP
content: B-but, I really do have a clue about the castle!

speaker: EMP
content: I'd like to offer it to you for free! B-but... will you let me join your adventure squad?

speaker: Hella
content: But aren't you dead...?
<i>"Um... When EMP the Bard was choosing her skills, she chose one that "automatically recovers 1 HP after being severely injured, but can only be used once every fifty turns."</i >

speaker: Etti
content: That's such a stretch of a skill... Has it been fifty turns already?
Ahem, the game master says it is so, therefore it must be so.
"But whether or not to let her join the adventurer's team is up to you three. Please discuss it carefully."

speaker: Hella
content: Aghhhh, these skills are so complicated! I-I don't care anymore! Just let Etti decide!

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: Yeah, let Etti decide.
Befuddled by EMP's complicated skills, Hella shrugs off all responsibility and pulls Ninety-Nine aside to sit down.
Now solely in charge of the decision, Etti smiles smugly with a hand on her hip.

speaker: Etti
content: Of course you're welcome to join. But...

speaker: EMP
content: B-but what?

speaker: Etti
content: You must give us the clue for free, and... tell us when, where, and how you got it!
EMP nods immediately, sits down on the ground, and explains in detail how she got her clue.

speaker: Etti
content: I knew it! It's the shop with the blue sofa to the right! I could tell at first sight that it's no ordinary shop.

speaker: Etti
content: With that being the case, let's head out now! The sooner we find more clues and reach the castle, the sooner we can get rid of the darkness!

speaker: EMP
content: I agree!

speaker: Hella
content: Mhmm, how can I miss out on saving the world? Right, Ninety-nine?

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: Mmm, that's right.
"Having added a new member to the team, the adventurers set off to find the merchant who sold EMP her clue."

"They march forward fearlessly in the darkness of night, unafraid of what lies ahead, be it danger or deceit... I'm sure they'll overcome all hardships, grasp the direction of fate, and bring light back to this world... .”
The comms device in your pocket buzzes. Walking behind everyone else, you take a peek at it.

speaker: McQueen
content: Sorry, my little gray wolf. Though I promised to take part in this exciting play with you...

speaker: McQueen
content: I really couldn't bear to let my little apple get off work late.

speaker: McQueen
content: I put your clue under the sofa cushion by the door. Thanks and bye!
Your hands quiver somewhat after reading the message.

speaker: Etti
content: Huh? This seems to be an art gallery? But the door is locked, and there doesn't seem to be anyone inside... Did we come here for nothing?
"The door... is indeed locked. The adventurers are a bit shocked, but they calm down quickly."

speaker: Etti
content: Huh? What's the situation here...
"EMP is not the brightest of the bunch..."

speaker: EMP
content: ...Never mind, you're the game master. Whatever you say.
"The adventurers realize that since this... er, clue-peddling merchant... gave EMP a clue to begin with, he or she probably also anticipated the adventurers coming back for more."
"So the clever adventurers figured that the merchant either left more clues within sight, or... didn't leave at all."
Etti strokes her chin and thinks for a while, then orders Ninety-Nine to take Hella off the sofa and begins to search.

speaker: Etti
content: This blue sofa has always been outside, so people of the bazaar are used to it. But to us who are here for the first time, it's a pretty obvious tip-off!

speaker: Etti
content: To send a message through something that most locals have tuned out while knowing it would stick out to newcomers is a clever idea indeed.
In the gap between the sofa's cushions and back, Etti fishes out an old piece of paper with her fingers.

speaker: Etti
content: But... this clue is a bit weird...
The three others scuttle over curiously to look at the paper in Etti's hand—it depicts a drawing identical to the one that EMP has.
It's a giant dragon soaring forward with its wings spread and head raised high. However, this one is facing the other direction. Both drawings are symmetrical to the central axis.

speaker: Hella
content: Hey look, there's a poetic verse in the bottom right-hand corner of each one. Are they clues?

speaker: EMP
content: Huh? You can recognize poetry...? Ouch, why are you kicking me?!

speaker: Etti
content: Let me see...
Etti puts the merchant's clue below EMP's clue, piecing out a complete poem...

speaker: Etti
content:
"The hometown that I kissed is the place the wind blew cold."
"The dragon's head always faces the light, which is the way that I must go."

speaker: EMP
content: Ahhh... I sort of get it, but don't get it at the same time.

speaker: Hella
content: Just admit that you don't get it. There's no such thing as sort of...
The team stares at the identical dragons and falls silent again.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: The place the wind blew cold... is that referring to the direction of the wind?
Ninety-Nine asks this as she tucks the hair lifted by the night breeze behind her ear.

speaker: Etti
content: Wind... direction... symmetrical dragons...

speaker: Etti
content: I get it now!
Etti picks up two wooden sticks from the ground and smears them with some drool that had fallen when EMP and Hella were fighting.
She sticks the two pieces of paper symmetrically on the sticks, then holds them up with a loose grip.
The wind blows by, turning the sticks around and moving the dragons' bodies. Everyone sees the dragon's heads swaying in the wind, pointing out the way forward.

speaker: Etti
content: I knew it! The legendary castle is that way!
Etti jumps up in excitement with both hands up high.

speaker: Etti
content: It must be a dark, dangerous castle full of traps! Only a castle like that can imprison light and be worth it for me to conquer!
Your shackles twitch instinctively. You look at Etti's glowing eyes and frown slightly.
"The adventurers deciphered the merchant's clue and learned of the legendary castle's location."
"It is a dangerous path laden with hardships and obstacles. The adventurers might be devoured by the darkness with the slightest misstep."
"But the adventurers believe in themselves—and also their companions."
Etti's gleaming eyes gradually return to normal. She looks at the others behind her, then at you. Then, without saying a word, she beckons for you to follow her and sets off.
"Just like that, the four adventurers chosen by fate—Etti the Mage, Ninety-Nine the Barbarian, Hella the Rogue and EMP the Bard—sets off towards the darkness to restore the light."
Deep in the night, you bring the adventurers to a remote corner of Eastside. A house almost completely shrouded in darkness appears before everyone's eyes.
"The adventurers can't see the entire castle clearly in the darkness of night, but the ominous roars carried out from inside by the wind betrays its gloom and terror."
There are messy stones and broken barbed wire everywhere. The teams stop outside the fence to discuss what to do.

speaker: Hella
content: Etti? Why don't you say something? You always have the most ideas. Tell us how we should attack and give that "Dreadlord" a surprise!

speaker: Etti
content: ...I don't know.

speaker: EMP
content: You don't know? E-e-e-even you don't know?

speaker: EMP
content: Th-then what's inside must really be...
Etti sighs, puts back her previous expression, and pats EMP.

speaker: Etti
content: What I mean is, the mystery is what makes it exciting.
Half of Etti's face is immersed in the darkness of the night, while the flickering neon lights nearby cast an eerie glow on her face.

speaker: Etti
content: Dragons are fearless, mighty, dominating creatures...

speaker: Etti
content: As a messenger and representative of the dragons, I have no fear of the unknown! Fear itself should fear my might!

speaker: Etti
content: As for you...
Etti opens her arms to her companions, as if wanting to hug and restrain them at the same time.

speaker: Etti
content: My dear companions... and guides of fate... since you are with me... you must be strong enough and worthy of accompanying me.
Before Etti's smile disappears, she picks up her staff and leads everyone towards the "castle" step by step.

speaker: Etti
content: I hope my God of Fate has arranged the most exciting battle for me in this legendary castle!
The "castle" gates creak open.
There are no ghosts, no monsters, or any other spooky scenes from their imaginations—just endless darkness that seems to devour something new with each step they take.

speaker: Hella
content: I don't like this place...

speaker: EMP
content: This is worse than seeing ghosts or monsters...

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: This environment can make people agitated.
"The boundless darkness makes the adventurers realize that if all the light gets devoured one day, every corner of the world will end up like this castle."
"And all the people who came here bravely did so to prevent that from happening."
"The adventurers' courage and kindness transform into rays of light, bursting out from their chests to illuminate the darkness..."
"And they finally see the light-devouring, darkness-spreading Dreadlord inside the castle..."
A pale light resembling the one in the interrogation room switches on. Under this light, everyone sees... the Dreadlord.
The "Dreadlord" sits in the center of the magic circle, holding a... picture book.

speaker: Dreadlord
content: "Hmph hmph hmph╭(╯^╰)╮"

speaker: Dreadlord
content: "Puny adventurers!"

speaker: Dreadlord
content: "I know why you've come! However! To get the magic box, you must defeat me first!"

speaker: Dreadlord
content: "Yet defeating me is an impossible task!"
In the face of the "Dreadlord's" provocations, Etti slowly opens her eyes, like a dragon fixating on a treasure.

speaker: Etti
content: Did you know, dragons are often considered the last and strongest of the great beasts.

speaker: Etti
content: So... a Dreadlord is nothing by comparison.
With a swish of her cape, Etti stands in front of the Dreadlord with her head raised high and begins to arrange the adventurers' attack order.

speaker: Etti
content: Rogue, take the lead in the first round and neutralize all the traps around the Dreadlord!

speaker: Hella
content: Hehe, leave it to me!

speaker: Etti
content: Barbarian, you're next. Deal a painful blow to the Dreadlord with your berserk skill!

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: Okay.

speaker: Etti
content: Bard, when it's your turn, keep releasing your flash arrows and paralyze the Dreadlord for at least two rounds.

speaker: EMP
content: No problem. I got it covered!

speaker: Etti
content: Finally, give me one minute.
Etti raises her staff and slams it hard on the floor.

speaker: Etti
content: I will turn this place into a frozen tundra!
The dice of fate starts to spin.
Under the command of such an outstanding Mage, the four adventurers' consecutive attacks gradually put the seemingly invincible Dreadlord into a losing position.

speaker: Dreadlord
content: D-despicable! Just you wait!

speaker: Dreadlord
content: Um, hey, God of Fate? I remember that I had a siege crossbow?

speaker: Etti
content: Huh? But isn't that for knocking down the city wall? No way... would the Dreadlord have something like that?!
Hehe. If the God of Fate says it is so, then it is so.

speaker: Dreadlord
content: You four scoundrels! Taste this!
The Dreadlord rips open the picture book, revealing a sketch of a powerful siege crossbow.

speaker: EMP
content: Oh my gosh! That thing will turn us into minced meat!

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: Things... aren't looking good.

speaker: Hella
content: Etti...!! Think of something!
Grinning, the Dreadlord aims and shoots the powerful crossbow at the four adventurers!
The adventurers have no time to react! The crossbow strike leaves them scattered and riddled with scars.

speaker: Dreadlord
content: Impossible! They should have been defeated by now! Why are they still alive?
Failing to hear any announcement of the adventurers' defeat from the "God of Fate"/game master, the Dreadlord becomes quite flustered.

speaker: Etti
content: Ha... Haha!
With the support of her staff, Etti gets up slowly, dusts off her face, and stares defiantly at the Dreadlord.

speaker: Etti
content: You think I'd come face you off unprepared?

speaker: Etti
content: Sorry to disappoint you—I already cast a defensive spell on my companions long before we came in.

speaker: Hella
content: Ha, so... your Ultimate won't kill us!

speaker: EMP
content: It hurts, but I bet you didn't expect us to survive! We can still fight!

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: Hmph! I will make you taste my wrath!
In the face of these circumstances, the Dreadlord silently lowers her head, as if deeply aware of her precarious situation.
Excellent... Truly outstanding adventurers.
A cold, female voice suddenly echoes from behind the Dreadlord, sending a chill down everyone's spines.
Everyone stares into the dark vortex. After a while, a green-haired woman emerges and takes the place of the Dreadlord.

speaker: Dreadlord
content: It's already quite impressive that you were able to defeat my "doppelganger"...

speaker: Dreadlord
content: Though I really want to defeat you, I realized there's something I want to do even more.
The real Dreadlord lifts up her hand and points at Etti.

speaker: Dreadlord
content: Your teammates are feeble, but you're a hundred times stronger than them... How about ditching them to join me?

speaker: Dreadlord
content: Darkness and dragons have always been best friends. If we join hands... this world is ours.
After hearing what the Dreadlord said, Hella can't help but blurt out...

speaker: Hella
content: What are you plotting?! There's no way Etti would listen to you! Right?!

speaker: Etti
content: Yeah! Why would I listen to you?

speaker: Hella
content: Look!
Etti approaches the Dreadlord step by step, her radiant eyes gleaming.
The Dreadlord frowns and looks at Etti in puzzlement.

speaker: Etti
content: To join you and stand by your side...

speaker: Etti
content: What an uninteresting proposal... How can you face your enemies with such thoughts?
A bit unnerved by Etti's words, the Dreadlord sneaks a glance at you.

speaker: Dreadlord
content: Oh? Then... what would you consider to be interesting?

speaker: Etti
content: If I were in control of this game, what would I do?

speaker: Etti
content: I... would sacrifice all my companions to the darkness.

speaker: Hella
content: What?!

speaker: EMP
content: Huh?!
Etti laughs, somewhat maniacally.

speaker: Etti
content: Then... I'd mix all of you together to create a stepping stone to world domination!

speaker: Dreadlord
content: Wait! Chief...!!
Etti doesn't wait for the Dreadlord to finish speaking. With a sudden wave of her hand, the surrounding darkness springs to life and consumes her, then rushes towards everyone else!
Etti! Stop!! What are you doing? Are you trying to create another Aesthia?!

speaker: Etti
content: No... of course not.

speaker: Etti
content: But you're not completely wrong.
As Etti manipulates the darkness, you can't see her expression clearly.

speaker: Etti
content: From the moment I stepped in here, I knew... that it was me who devoured the light.

speaker: Etti
content: I know what this place is... But now, it's nothing but pitch darkness... Before, whenever I opened the door, I'd see all the different game worlds he made.

speaker: Etti
content: Grandpa would assume the role of different NPCs and take me into the game world... No matter how lonely I was outside, I wouldn't be alone when I came here.

speaker: Etti
content: But I almost lost those warm memories... Even when I regained them, I'd soon forget them again whenever happier memories appear... What should I do?!
More and more darkness springs forth from under Etti's feet, ensnaring the white light above her head. Light is about to vanish completely.

speaker: Hella
content: Tsk, you're so much trouble! I don't want to play anymore! If you think it's better this way... then just cast me to the darkness.

speaker: EMP
content: Yeah, if you like this ending better, just pretend that we adventurers lost and you became the Dreadlord. You win!

speaker: Etti
content: You're... not scared of losing?

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: It's okay to lose. I lose to Hella and Chief all the time. It's just a game. Having fun is what counts.

speaker: Etti
content: None of you get it...

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: I get it. Memories are what keep a person going. They fuel one's life and actions.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: But I'm doing fine right now. I haven't forgotten, nor will I ever forget. Yet I will also make myself happy.
Etti's hand trembles. She bites her lower lip, as if trying to hold back her emotions.
Yet the next second, the darkness still devours everyone except you and Etti.
Etti, don't make this a repeat of the Isle of Sky. Total control will only make you lose control!

speaker: Etti
content: Lose control...? But I already have complete control over this place, and also mastered your weakness—these people.
The surrounding scenery begins to change. You're suddenly surrounded by the red spiritual world, while Etti's eyes look the same as they did on the Isle of Sky.
It's a look that only a gamemaster can have—one that exudes total control.
I see...
It's a pity, because like you said, I'm the "God of Fate."

speaker: Etti
content: Ha! So what?
Fate... will always set you on the right path.

speaker: Etti
content: That's true! But... I've always relished deviating from the path set for me by fate.

speaker: Etti
content: Of course, I also respect fate...
With a wave of her hand, Etti takes out a star-speckled die.
You recognize it as Etti's special die. You can guess what Etti wants to do, so you take out your own pure white Chosen One.

speaker: Etti
content: You should know the rules already, but I still want to make it clear to you...

speaker: Etti
content: I control this place. Even if you win... I will find a way to subvert you.
Now that I wield fate itself... I believe the God of Fate will stand by my side.

speaker: Etti
content: All right. Good luck to you, then.
With a flick of her wrist, Etti casts the die into the air. You also cast your die, and the two collide.
The pair of dice gradually slow down. You can feel your heart beating faster and faster.
The spiritual world's sea of red flowers gradually expands. The power of Mania is growing stronger and stronger...
The pair of dice lands softly on the ground, marking the end of the duel between fate and power.

speaker: Etti
content: Dear God of Fate...
The gleam in Etti's eyes brightens, and her smile gets ever more eerier.

speaker: Etti
content: You were born to be subverted.
Everything suddenly quiets down. The thick darkness quickly envelops your whole body, eroding your mind and senses.
In your last moment of consciousness, you feel a powerful gush of Mania rushing towards you.

speaker: Etti
content: Goodbye, dear Chief.
Yet when the shudders and ringing in your ears subside, what you had expected didn't actually take place.
Slowly, you try to open your eyes...
Basking in the soft light, you spot the one smiling mischievously before you.
You better explain this to me...

speaker: Etti
content: Aww, why so serious?

speaker: Etti
content: I-I was just joking around...
Just joking around?!

speaker: Etti
content: What, you want to put on airs and lecture me about rules now? This "interrogation" of yours was nonsense from the very beginning!

speaker: Etti
content: You want to get back at me because you got humiliated on the Isle of Sky? You want to use this game to "give me a taste of my own medicine?" Hmph, should I call you brave or naive?

speaker: Etti
content: Plus, you're not a very professional game master. You're always trying to find ways to counter me. It's already quite magnanimous of me to hold out this long before exploding.

speaker: Etti
content: So I wanted to show you how to control the game like a professional game master!
What about everyone else?

speaker: Etti
content: Don't worry, they're here...
Etti waves her hands, and the dark shadows dissipate instantly. Hella, Ninety-Nine, and EMP are all sitting on the ground in confusion.

speaker: EMP
content: Ah... ah!! I'm still alive!! Hahaha!! That's great!

speaker: Hella
content: You're so loud!

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: ...Is it all over?

speaker: Etti
content: Yeah, sort of...

speaker: Etti
content: Oh wait, there's one more person...
Etti takes you to the attic. When you open the door, you see your mild-tempered adjutant sitting at the desk, smiling kindly.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, Etti, if possible, when we get back to the Bureau, I want you to tell me in detail what... the... heck... happened!
After Nightingale leaves the attic, both the mighty dragon and unyielding fate sigh in relief.

speaker: Etti
content: Don't be so cocky next time. Judging from this sloppy game of yours, you have a long way to go before you can challenge me.
...The Isle of Sky aside, I do have a real treasure. Since you did clear the level, it's yours to keep. I guess this can count as having completed the game on my part.
To Etti's surprise, you give her the handmade book that Nightingale left behind.

speaker: Etti
content: Is this... my grandpa's handmade book?

Yeah. Sorry, I didn't mean to read something he left you on purpose. At the time, you were clutching it tightly, and we moved it aside to let you sleep better. However, it accidentally flipped open in the process.
It was then that I found a hidden compartment at the end of the book.
The hidden compartment seems to have remnants of the Dragon of Genesis' power. I'm guessing there's a gift inside that your grandpa wants you to have once you're truly able to "control everything."
Etti goes to the last page of the book and gently taps on the handmade wooden cover. The muffled sound tells her that there is a hidden compartment.
She opens the compartment to find a letter that has been there for a long, long time.
Etti opens the letter and reads it in silence for a long time.
She doesn't speak again until the dawn light emerges in the horizon.

speaker: Etti
content: Actually... I panicked when I came back into this house. I thought I had lost my memory again from being immersed in my own game.
Etti gazes at the letter in her hands, then folds it up and puts it in her shirt pocket.

speaker: Etti
content: But... thank you for being willing to trust me, tolerate me, and for letting me know...

speaker: Etti
content: That when memories are overlaid by trust, happiness, and sincerity, they are not forgotten... They are simply tucked away like treasures.

Etti, I assume that by the time you read this letter, you've already completed the game I made?

Did you have fun?

I believe you must be quite happy, and that you also have trusty friends by your side. Am I right?

Hehe... If this is the case, then you can safely tuck me away into the deepest, darkest corner of your heart. I'll guard you against fear and loneliness...

...Until you turn all this darkness into joy.

—Guardian of Darkness - Genesis Gamemaster - Black Dragon - Old Wach

speaker: Wynn
content: Sigh, this is my first field mission with the task force. I thought I'd witness the Chief capturing a Sinner in action.

speaker: Wynn
content: How did I get myself into this?

speaker: Chief
content: Wynn, how is everything going here?

speaker: Wynn
content: Uh, it needs a bit more time to complete the generation of data.
Wynn fiddles with the analyzer in her hands, while complex data strings crawl over the display panel.
At the same time, the members of the MBCC's city arrest team are placing one heavy bag after another in front of you.
Not surprisingly, such a peculiar scene draws the attention of passersby in the West District.

speaker: Pedestrian A
content: What are these government people doing here?

speaker: Pedestrian B
content: Looks like they're collecting garbage.

speaker: Pedestrian A
content: So many of them, just to collect garbage? Have they gone nuts?

speaker: Pedestrian B
content: I don't know. Maybe some department has gone bankrupt and has come to the West District to make money.

speaker: Pedestrian C
content: Tsk tsk! The Scrap King of the West Side is going to face some stiff competition.

speaker: Pedestrian A
content: Exactly. Can't believe they've come all the way here to steal jobs...
The members of your team are well-trained. Still, the ongoing conversation around you is starting to make them feel embarrassed.
Fortunately, right at this moment, Wynn's analyzer completes the generation of data.

speaker: Wynn
content: Chief, we've got the results!

speaker: Wynn
content: Let me see... Hmm, among these 517 test samples, there are 136 with M-values in the "slightly higher than normal" range and 171 with M-values in the "trace amount" range.

speaker: Wynn
content: The rest are... harmless?

Wynn, somewhat puzzled, takes out the instruction manual for the analyzer. After a quick flip, she finds the ranges for "slightly higher than normal" and "trace amount," which are ±5 and ±1, respectively.

speaker: Wynn
content: Have we been played?
Wynn looks around, taking in the steel bars, steel plates, and timber that surround her. She can't help but voice her doubts.

speaker: Wynn
content: These contaminated materials look just like... just like, uh...
Building materials? These are the words you're looking for, right?
A familiar voice helps Wynn find the words she's looking for. You turn around and see a dark figure standing among the members of the city arrest team.

speaker: Wynn
content: Yes, yes, just like building materials.

speaker: Raven
content: Then you're wrong.
With a flourish, the woman points at the pieces of cement brick, steel, and wood scattered all around her.

speaker: Raven
content: These are not building materials.

speaker: Raven
content: They are the pieces of Syndicate's shattered past, the ruins of its former glory...

speaker: Raven
content: They are a reminder of the ravages of Mania that once plagued this piece of land, a flower that withered only yesterday...

speaker: Chief
content: They are building materials.

speaker: Chief
content: The contamination level is very low; it doesn't pose any serious danger, but I have a feeling that all this was staged.

speaker: Chief
content: Like someone made them and put them here, probably to lure us here.
Your eyes never leave the "poet" who just appeared out of nowhere.

speaker: Raven
content: You might be right. These do look like old building materials, but that doesn't mean they can't be put to good use.

speaker: Raven
content: See? The bricks are still in one piece, the wood hasn't rotted through, and the corrosion of the steel is not serious.

speaker: Raven
content: I can't see why we can't reuse them to build shelters that will protect some Syndicans from the elements...
Caw... Caw...
The familiar bird call interrupts Raven's speech. Clearly, it doesn't come from the black crow on her shoulder.

speaker: Wynn
content: What's that?

speaker: Raven
content: To shelter Syndicans from the elements, isn't this their intended purpose?
Caw... Caw...

speaker: Chief
content: Wynn, check the bag next to you.

speaker: Wynn
content: Sure... Will do...
Raven tries to reach out and stop her, it seems, but it's too late.
The moment Wynn opens the bag, a black—no, a gray crow, stained such a color by concrete dust, flies out.
It lands on Raven's shoulder.

speaker: Gray Crow
content: Caw... Caw...
Bang—
The crow caws twice and explodes, turning into a puddle of ink that stains Raven's shoulder black.
The members of the city arrest team turn in unison to look at the heavy bags of building materials they just carried over.
Sure enough, all of them are stained with suspicious ink marks, without exception.

options: It's time for us to talk, Raven.

content: The red light from the shackles flares up. The S-Class Sinner doesn't make any move to dodge; she simply tucks a strand of hair behind her ear and says with mock regret:

speaker: Raven
content: Ah, so close. What a shame.

speaker: Raven
content: If you were a bit slower, it would have been a happy ending for all of us.
The red light from the shackles flares up. The S-Class Sinner doesn't make any move to dodge; she simply tucks a strand of hair behind her ear and says with mock regret:

speaker: Raven
content: Ah, so close. What a shame.

speaker: Raven
content: If you were a bit slower, it would have been a happy ending for all of us.
The red light from the shackles flares up. The S-Class Sinner doesn't make any move to dodge; she simply tucks a strand of hair behind her ear and says with mock regret:

speaker: Raven
content: Ah, so close. What a shame.

speaker: Raven
content: If you were a bit slower, it would have been a happy ending for all of us.
Although it's not the earth-shattering battle Wynn has conjured up in her head, she gets her wish to see the Chief in action.
(Scene change)

speaker: Chief
content: It's been a while since we last met. You've given us folks at the MBCC quite a task...

speaker: Chief
content: Do you think that Syndicate is too peaceful now, and that has made it difficult for you to strut your stuff?

speaker: Raven
content: Exactly.
She gives a smile, raising her eyebrows playfully.
Her shameless honesty leaves you speechless. After a while, you manage to get out a sentence:

speaker: Chief
content: You know, you didn't need to pull a stunt like that.

speaker: Chief
content: If you wanted those things relocated, you could have done it without our help.

speaker: Chief
content: Instead, you went around defacing public property and then reported a possible contamination incident to the MBCC to get us out there. Why did you do that? To pull a fast one on us?

speaker: Raven
content: No no no, you're wrong.

speaker: Raven
content: I had to do that. I wouldn't have been able to get you to notice this matter otherwise.

speaker: Chief
content: You went through all that trouble, just to get my attention?

speaker: Chief
content: I heard you fell from a high place. Did you hurt your head or something?
The state your once-reliable former ally is in prompts you to cast a concerned glance at her.

speaker: Raven
content: Hahahaha...

speaker: Raven
content: Funny.

speaker: Raven
content: You're right about one thing, though. My injuries did have something to do with my trying to get your attention.
Raven makes an effort to lift her right arm, but it comes up only to the height of a standard chair's armrest.
You see, under the purple shawl, the white bandages wrapped around her upper arm. Those must be the injuries she suffered when she helped you escape.

speaker: Chief
content: Sorry, I didn't know it was this bad.

speaker: Raven
content: Haha, that's all in the past. Don't worry about it. They're not as bad as you might think. Making life a little bit difficult for me; that's all.

speaker: Raven
content: My aim is not as precise as it used to be when I use my abilities, and my staying power has declined too.

speaker: Raven
content: This is why I couldn't agree with you when you said, "You could have done it without our help."

speaker: Raven
content: I couldn't, sadly. So, I need a reliable ally. And I want it to be you.
You look Raven in the eye. You sigh with resignation.

options: What do you want me to do?

speaker: Raven
content: I want...
Raven pauses for a moment, and then smiles, as if suddenly remembering something.

speaker: Raven
content: I want to build a new school over there, one that truly belongs to the children in Syndicate.

speaker: Chief
content: What about the people from Rustfire? You didn't ask them for help?

speaker: Raven
content: That architect friend of mine did promise to help me out...

speaker: Raven
content: Unfortunately, he won't be able to keep that promise.

speaker: Raven
content: It would be inconsiderate to make any of the remaining members of Rustfire feel bad about themselves, given their current circumstances.

speaker: Raven
content: Besides, they have enough on their plate right now. It wouldn't be right to ask them to drop their things and help me instead.

speaker: Raven
content: You're the only person I can count on now. Please, help me, for the sake of the future of the children in Syndicate...
Raven's eyes are surprisingly clear and sincere, and a bit misty, as if on the verge of tears.
Still a great actor, you think to yourself. This time, however, you consider granting her request.
Fickle as Raven is, she seems serious about building a school.
Despite the asking-for-your-help farce she put on, no serious damage has come out of it, except for wasting your time and some of the MBCC staff's.
Building a school should not prove too difficult a task for the MBCC construction team, but you have a nagging feeling that there will be trouble down the line.
You take a deep breath, ready to have a good talk with Raven.

options: I'll help you build the school.

speaker: Raven
content: You agree to help me?
The first word has barely come out of your mouth when the Sinner before you grins from ear to ear, no longer the damsel in distress on the verge of tears.

speaker: Chief
content: Tell me why you're so obsessed with building a new school.

speaker: Raven
content: It's simple. Children are the future of the West District. Education is essential for the rejuvenation of this land.

speaker: Raven
content: You're looking at her...

speaker: Raven
content: Yes, it's yours truly. I'll teach them.

speaker: Chief
content: You'll need more than one teacher.

speaker: Raven
content: You have no faith in me, one of the best journalists in Syndicate, a model member of Rustfire, the greatest poet in Syndicate?

speaker: Raven
content: Besides, when I was a member of Rustfire, I taught those homeless kids for a while. So, even though I don't have a certificate, I'm a skilled teacher—a versatile one even.

speaker: Chief
content: I heard the kids you taught... they all ran away when you went to Eastside.

speaker: Raven
content: Ehh...

speaker: Raven
content: Ah, I heard a lot of Sinners locked up in the MBCC escaped while you were asleep.
Noticing the unpleasant look on your face, Raven quickly changes the subject.

speaker: Raven
content: Ah, let's stop belittling each other. We have the future of Syndicate to think about.

speaker: Raven
content: As the saying goes, "If the skin is gone, so will be the hair attached to it." Without a school, there's no way of persuading Syndican adults to become teachers here, and Syndican kids to become students.

speaker: Raven
content: Once we've built a school, there will be a place for them to be. By then, Rustfire will have been done with their things. I'll ask Lavina and others to come over, and then we'll have a teaching staff.

speaker: Raven
content: And there will be no shortage of students. We can bring the kids from the Homeless back to attend school here.

speaker: Raven
content: After hearing what I just said, don't you feel that a school is all we need to bring hope back to Syndicate?
You nod, but as you do so, you realize something's missing.

speaker: Chief
content: Have you contacted any publisher? Have you applied for ISBNs? Do you need my help?

speaker: Raven
content: Well...
Raven doesn't seem to know how to face your concern for her. She simply looks away, avoiding your eyes.

speaker: Chief
content: What are you going to teach the kids before other teachers join you? Only poetry writing?

speaker: Raven
content: Give me some credit. I grad... studied in a proper university in Eastside. I did give the curriculum some thought, but at the moment, I don't have a budget for textbooks.

speaker: Raven
content: While I was at the Drifter Camp, I wrote dozens of textbooks and composed hundreds of poems, but that alone took me several years. It will be difficult to write all the remaining ones from scratch...

speaker: Raven
content: So, I'm planning to try a much faster method this time.

speaker: Chief
content: A faster method?

speaker: Raven
content: Yes. I'm going to "borrow" some textbooks from Eastside and change them up a bit. And then they'll be used as our textbooks.

speaker: Chief
content: Your moral compass is quite flexible on such matters.

speaker: Raven
content: Scholars learn and borrow from each other. There is no shame in that.

speaker: Raven
content: I also plan to have more illustrations added to the "borrowed" textbooks. The Syndican kids are smart, but they're not very big on words.

speaker: Raven
content: Once we switch to illustrated textbooks, the kids will be over the moon. Maybe I'll incorporate my masterpieces into the illustrations, so that literature can have a second life on this land...
Raven grows more excited as she explains her plan for the school, her eyes sparkling and her hands moving around.
Looking at the "poet" in front of you, you can't help but wonder, These Rustfire guys never change.
Even if there's only a glimmer of hope, they'll chase it with all their heart.

speaker: Julien
content: Hope is something precious. It holds a lot of power even when it's irrational.
Yes, indeed. She wants to bring hope to the children, even if that means she has to give up everything she has.

speaker: Chief
content: So, do you have a name for the school?

speaker: Raven
content: Of course, I've had it for a long time. It'll be called...

speaker: Raven
content: The Syndicate Academy!
Raven shouts out the name of the school, her "injured" right arm lifted high above her head.

speaker: Chief
content: Didn't you say that you were injured?
Her right arm comes back down quickly as if shocked.

speaker: Raven
content: Ouch, ouch, that really hurts. I was too excited just now to notice the pain...
You know without a shadow of a doubt that she can't be trusted to oversee the construction of the school alone.

You, heaven on earth! What kind of curse

Once cast an ominous shadow over you?

A thousand years of oppression

Stained your brilliance with blood and pain

Until your wonderful stars washed the stains away with their tears.

speaker: Construction Worker
content: Hey, Miss Poet, get down from the rooftop. We need to get working now!

speaker: Raven
content: I'm coming... I'm coming. I was reciting the poem to boost your spirits before you got started on the day's work.

speaker: Construction Worker
content: You can say whatever you want. Just as long as you don't show up at our construction site every day.

speaker: Raven
content: That wouldn't do. The sight of you working under the night sky is so inspiring, and your burning soul is so dazzling!

Scenes like this have quickly become a daily occurrence. Whether it's due to the habits she acquired while working as a reporter or her genuine concern about the progress of the construction work, no one can say for sure.
Every now and then, Raven can be seen having a "friendly conversation" with the construction team sent by the Bureau.
Fortunately, the members of the construction team are worldly enough to not be greatly affected emotionally while dealing with a Sinner.
Of course, although she occasionally fools around, Raven is never idle.

speaker: Raven
content: Why are you here this late? There isn't enough work in the Bureau to keep you busy?
Before you can say anything, Raven thrusts a thick file folder into your arms.
You open the folder and take out the papers. A quick glance tells you that it's written in that overly flamboyant style of hers.
The Syndicate Academy, where the children in Syndicate find hopes and dreams!
Say no to war, say yes to peace! Reject ignorance, embrace knowledge!
With the full support of the MBCC Chief! What are you waiting for? Enroll now!

speaker: Chief
content: What is this?

speaker: Raven
content: Isn't it obvious? It's a recruitment brochure.

speaker: Raven
content: The school is in Syndicate. So it's written in a style befitting Syndicate!

speaker: Chief
content: Why did you decide to write this thing all of a sudden?

speaker: Raven
content: Yesterday, while inspecting the school, I stumbled upon this classroom. It's basically finished; I put some desks and chairs in the room to see how it looked.

speaker: Raven
content: You know what, the classroom is quite big, big enough to hold at least fifty desks and chairs, almost as big as those classrooms I saw during my schooldays in Eastside.

speaker: Raven
content: Then I thought to myself, "Since I've got the desks and chairs, why not get the podium and blackboard in as well?"

speaker: Raven
content: See? We've got everything here except for the students.
Raven points to the empty desks and chairs in the classroom, then waves the thick stack of recruitment brochures in her hand.

speaker: Raven
content: Just wait and see.
The next day...
A few curious kids are often seen milling around outside the Syndicate Academy.
They watch from a distance at first, and Raven pretends not to notice them.

Slowly, as if in a game of Statues, they sneak closer and closer, so as to take a better look at the building. More than once, while Raven is examining the content of the textbooks, she finds the kids looking in from behind one of the windows.
And then, Raven turns her head toward the window suddenly. Caught by surprise, they duck out of sight as one.

speaker: Raven
content: It's fine. Kids don't have much patience. Just wait, and they will come to us. Now, show me the textbooks.
You open the trunk, take out the textbooks, and hand them to Raven.
Raven flips through them one by one.

speaker: Raven
content: Hate to admit it, but these are quite well-written. They won't need much tweaking, except for this one...
Raven extracts the history textbook from the stack and places it on the table.

speaker: Ica
content: Miss Raye.
The sudden voice interrupts Raven, and the kids, with their minds made up, have come out of hiding.

speaker: Raven
content: Oh my, how nice of you to greet me. I rarely hear people call my real name these days; it feels strange, to be honest.

speaker: Ica
content: We, um...

speaker: Raven
content: Want to attend school here?

speaker: Ica
content: Not exactly. We just want to learn poetry writing from you. Your poems inspired us a lot in the past.
Raven is rendered speechless for a moment, a rare thing to witness, but she quickly regains her composure.

speaker: Raven
content: Hahaha... Of course you can come and learn how to write emotive poems from the great poet of DisCity, as long as you attend school here.

speaker: Ica
content: Can I, um, only take classes in poetry? Because I heard your other classes... are a bit...

speaker: Raven
content: A bit what? And who said that?
Raven raises her eyebrows, and the children exchange glances of amusement.

speaker: Raven
content: Won't tell, huh? Well, let me take a guess then... Remarks of this nature can only come from...

speaker: Crache
content: I said it.
A shadow slithers out from the base of one of the walls and takes on human form.

speaker: Raven
content: Well, if it isn't the naughty dropout who made a habit of skipping school! Now you think you're good enough to criticize your old teacher?

speaker: Crache
content: I read the textbooks you left behind from cover to cover several times. Some of the content is just too difficult for kids of their age; not the right teaching materials.

speaker: Raven
content: Oh, you a fan of my writings?
Raven gives a teasing smile.

speaker: Crache
content: You rotten bird!

speaker: Raven
content: By the time I started teaching the kids from the Homeless, it had been a good decade since I graduated from middle school. Could you blame me if I didn't get the difficulty level right for all the materials?

speaker: Raven
content: This time is different, though.
Raven points at you; you're unloading textbooks from the Bureau's vehicle.

speaker: Raven
content: With the help of the MBCC Chief, we can't go wrong with the textbooks this time!

speaker: Raven
content: Disian, mathematics, history, social studies, science... Anything that can be taught will be taught here.

speaker: Raven
content: I can help you transform yourselves into a new generation of Syndicans who will carry the torch of hope for Syndicate.
Raven's earnestness seems a bit too much for the leader of the Homeless.

speaker: Crache
content: Well, I'll take your word for it this time. These books are from Eastside, right?
Crache's eyes scan the room and land on the glossy cover of the history textbook on the table. They linger for a few seconds before looking away.

speaker: Crache
content: <size=25>Do history textbooks from Eastside record the troubled history of Syndicate?</size>
A bell rings out. You check your watch. It's 2 p.m. on the dot.

speaker: Construction Worker
content: Sorry, did we disturb you? We were installing a school bell; it went off by accident.
You make a gesture that says it's not a problem. And then Crache leaves you and walks toward the other end of the school campus.

speaker: Crache
content: It's almost time, Ica. It's time for the combat skills class.

speaker: Ica
content: Ah... Okay, boss.

speaker: Crache
content: And your classes... I'll look forward to them a bit, just a bit.
Crache walks away and waves goodbye without a backward glance.

speaker: Raven
content: Safe journey. Remember to come when school starts. I'll be waiting for you here.
Raven waves at the receding backs of the homeless kids until they disappear around the corner.

speaker: Raven
content: What a sharp-witted kid... I'll have to give her extra homework.
Raven sighs. She opens the textbook in front of her.

speaker: Raven
content: In N.F. 84, the BR-000 appeared following a large explosion in DisSea, and left an impact so profound that it's difficult to eliminate its effects even today.

speaker: Raven
content: Syndicate was originally called the West District. According to the West District Order Management Regulations, the region was left to the local violent gangs for self-government.

speaker: Raven
content: Thanks to the Hypercube discovered by Dr. Keylan, DisCity was established. Also thanks to the Hypercube, DisCity grew into a megacity, the only one on the continent, attracting countless immigrants and ushering in a prosperous era.

speaker: Raven
content: These are some snippets from the textbook. What do you think?

options: I think it's suitable for children.

speaker: Chief
content: Syndicate doesn't feature much in it, don't you think?

speaker: Raven
content: They obscure Syndicate. Whenever Syndicate comes up, it's referred to as DisCity. Worse still, in some cases, they stigmatize it.

speaker: Raven
content: This is not the kind of history that we should teach the children in Syndicate.

speaker: Raven
content: Where there is light, there must be shadow. You can't have one without the other... I will not let the efforts of generations of Syndicans go down the drain.

speaker: Raven
content: Their sacrifices, their achievements, deserve to be remembered.

speaker: Raven
content: To instill hope and faith in children, hope for a better future, faith in the light ahead... This is my aspiration.

speaker: Raven
content: Or it was, up until that incident...
Raven seems lost now; she's always been confident and determined.

speaker: Raven
content: Join me, Chief of the MBCC. I need your help and advice.
Raven extends her hand to you.
The creaking of a door...
With a creak that makes one's teeth tingle, Raven pushes open the door to the study.
You find yourself in a room jammed full of photos, clippings, magazines, so numerous that they fill up at least a dozen shelves of varying sizes.
This room is one-quarter the size of the MBCC's archive room.

speaker: Chief
content: Are these...
You take a notebook from one of the shelves, shake off the dust, and open it.

speaker: Raven
content: These are all records about the history of Syndicate, from N.F. 81 to N.F. 114, some by me, some by others.

speaker: Raven
content: I've tried my best to collect the epic tales of every Syndican hero; I don't want any of their stories to be buried and never see the day of light.

options: When did you start collecting them?

speaker: Raven
content: Some time after I arrived in Eastside, I guess. My family moved to Eastside when I was a child.

speaker: Chief
content: That explains why you look sad in some of your childhood photos.
The few photos of a gloomy young Raven stand out on the photo wall.

speaker: Raven
content: Yeah, Eastside is just for show; it's actually quite boring.

speaker: Raven
content: The boredom wasn't relieved until, on TV, I saw how those heroes stepped up in times of crisis; they were like a fire in the dark.

speaker: Raven
content: That's when I found the goal I wished to pursue.

speaker: Raven
content: Ever since then, I had been jotting things down as a hobby. And just like that, more than a decade passed.

speaker: Raven
content: Maybe because life in Eastside was too boring for me, or maybe because I wanted to visit my childhood hometown...

speaker: Raven
content: I ended up becoming a writer for Yagyu's newspaper; I wrote articles for their official account.

speaker: Raven
content: Hahaha... The funny thing is, while I was working in that place, I realized that no one could match me when it came to sensationalism and writing eye-catching news.
Raven holds up a finger, words pouring out of her mouth as she excitedly recounts her glorious past.

speaker: Raven
content: One year later, in N.F. 103, the newspaper sent me to Syndicate. But it wasn't the Syndicate I remembered from my childhood.

speaker: Raven
content: Ruins were everywhere, war was widespread, devastation as far as the eye could see...

speaker: Raven
content: It was then that I saw that fire in the dark.

speaker: Raven
content: Yes. You're quick on the uptake, aren't you? Anyway, I became an embedded reporter, living off them... no, I mean, reporting on their activities.

speaker: Raven
content: It was a troubled period. The relationship between the miners and Nirvana was extremely tense; Nirvana planned to do away with the mining machines, and the miners wouldn't hear of it.

speaker: Raven
content: The miners fought back. They went all out, eventually stopping that arrogant Nirvana from going through with their plan, at least temporarily, and forcing them to the negotiation table.

speaker: Raven
content: Of course, I wasn't idle either. I put up banners for them, wrote slogans, and even helped them drag back a couple of machines.

speaker: Raven
content: That's a great story, right?
You nod.

speaker: Chief
content: That's not the end of it, though.

speaker: Raven
content: Ah, the hero defeats the villain, and the faint light turns into a blazing fire, illuminating the inky night.

speaker: Raven
content: But even the fiercest fire is no match for torrential rain. That's exactly what happened to our heroes. After the W-31 incident, a Black Ring appeared, and the leadership of the organization disappeared in mysterious circumstances.

speaker: Raven
content: After I returned to Eastside, I tried hard to publicize their heroic deeds, hoping that they could be remembered.

speaker: Raven
content: However, as you must have known, in Eastside at that time, articles about Nirvana would be removed from circulation as soon as they were published.

speaker: Raven
content: They would invite the writers for "coffee," to give them some "friendly advice."

options: How many times were you invited?

speaker: Raven
content: Well, let me put it this way... More times than I'd been home. I could walk around the Eastside Public Security Bureau's office with my eyes closed.
Raven shrugs, a nonchalant look on her face.

speaker: Raven
content: The heroic deeds I recorded posed a threat to them. Sure enough, they soon made their move against me.

speaker: Raven
content: I became a target for DRD, Nirvana's special department, because I knew too much about the W-31 incident. They pinned such charges as "endangering Eastside's public security," "repeatedly disrupting public order," "spreading false information" on me.

options: What did they do to you?

speaker: Raven
content: I was fine. Just a few scratches here and there. They were nothing; they couldn't break me, not at all.
Raven dismisses your concern with a wave of her hand. She looks relaxed, describing her ordeal like it's no big deal.
But it couldn't have been easy on her. Nirvana's secret department would never let their enemies go with only a slap on their wrist.
Do you confess?

speaker: Raye
content: Haha, writing about the honorable deeds of heroes is a crime in your eyes, huh?
Your brain isn't working well, it seems. You guys, teach her a lesson about how to make a proper confession.

speaker: Raye
content: Ah, do your worst. It'll only strengthen the case that those people are heroes!
Take her away. Give her some alone time to think things over.
Do you confess?

speaker: Raye
content: I've recorded... their heroic deeds...
Oh my, I've never seen anyone so foolish.

speaker: Raye
content: Haha, hahaha...
Why are you laughing? Have you gone mad?

speaker: Raye
content: Yes... I record stories of heroes...

speaker: Raye
content: In those stories... dirty rats like you... play a part too. You're there to make the heroes appear even more noble by comparison...
Crazy woman.
Beat her to within an inch of her life, but don't let her die.
Do you confess?

speaker: Raye
content: ...Hahaha, you're afraid of the heroes of Syndicate... afraid that you're going to be burned by Rustfire...
You still have the strength to yell? With your broken ribs and all.
Lock her up. I've had enough of this crazy woman.
The ordeal doesn't seem to have broken her spirit. She is a true fighter.

speaker: Raven
content: Have you found something interesting in the notebook?
When Raven draws closer to take a peak, you quickly turn to the next page.

speaker: Chief
content: Just some records. What gave you the idea of becoming a teacher, anyway? You don't strike me as the kind of person who might be interested in teaching.

speaker: Raven
content: You have a point there. If DRD had let up a bit on their effort to make my life miserable, maybe I wouldn't have thought of becoming a teacher.

speaker: Raven
content: They couldn't do anything about me, so they sent me to a detention center on the border between Eastside and Syndicate.

options: The conditions there must have been appalling.

speaker: Raven
content: They were. But that's only half of it. The worst part about the whole experience was that I got no one to talk to. Even the person who delivered my meals wouldn't get near me.
She had it tough. She had to endure the appalling conditions while still recovering from serious injuries.

speaker: Raven
content: Here is the thing about not having anyone to talk to. It prevents me from sharing my beautiful poems with other people.

speaker: Raven
content: If I can't share them, how is the name of Raven, the Great Poet of DisCity, supposed to spread throughout the world?!
Raven bangs on the table, and dust falls from the shelves around you.
Typical Raven.

speaker: Raven
content: There was one saving grace, though. The window was not very high. I could reach it if I put something under my feet.

speaker: Raven
content: Through the window, I always saw this group of Syndican kids giving the guards hell.

speaker: Raven
content: They mocked these guards, every day without fail, or threw rocks and made faces at them.

speaker: Raven
content: Haha... it was quite satisfying. Because of the West District Treaty, all the guards could do was chase them away, angry as they were. Even at their angriest, they only dared to fire shots skyward.

speaker: Raven
content: So, every day, I'd sit on the window ledge, cheering the kids on, waving at them.

speaker: Raven
content: ...I don't know when exactly, but one day, one of the kids appeared on the other side of the iron bars.

speaker: Raye
content: What's your name?

speaker: Miles
content: Miles, and yours?

speaker: Raye
content: Raye.

speaker: Miles
content: How long have you been locked up here, Raye?

speaker: Raye
content: Over a month now. They brought me in because I spread stories of heroes.
I cast a glance at the wall covered with the horizontal and vertical lines I had carved. And I saw my opportunity.

speaker: Raye
content: Hehe... Can you do me a favor? Just a small one.

speaker: Miles
content: No.
Tsk tsk, the kid was sharp.

speaker: Raye
content: Hahaha... Come on, I just need you to get some notes out of this place for me. It's an easy task.

speaker: Miles
content: No.

speaker: Raye
content: Not even if the notes are actually poems written by the most famous poet in all of Syndicate? This is a once-in-lifetime opportunity for you to earn a place in the history books.

speaker: Miles
content: No.

speaker: Raye
content: Seriously? What's the matter? Don't tell me that you've lived in Syndicate all this time and never heard of my nickname name—Raven?

speaker: Miles
content: No.
The kid on the other side of the bars shakes his head.

speaker: Miles
content: And... I don't want to be a Syndican; I want to go to Eastside.

speaker: Raye
content: Ah, what's so good about that rotten place? The lights at night can blind you!

speaker: Miles
content: At least I won't starve over there.

speaker: Miles
content: ...But my friends told me that if you want to survive in Eastside, you'll have to know how to write.

speaker: Raye
content: Lucky for you, you've come to the right person. Miles, I want to apologize, because I've kept a big secret from you.

speaker: Raye
content: Well, actually...

speaker: Miles
content: Actually what?

speaker: Raye
content: Actually, I'm a teacher.

speaker: Miles
content: What's a teacher?

speaker: Raye
content: You don't know? A teacher is someone who passes on knowledge, teaches you how to write. A teacher sometimes teaches a poem or two to the students too.
I emphasized the word "write." When he heard it, his eyes brightened and started seeing me in a different light.

speaker: Raye
content: Did you get today's poem out yet?

speaker: Miles
content: Yeah, I posted it on their front door when the guards weren't watching.

speaker: Raye
content: Bravo! I knew I picked the right person! Now, let's start our lesson.
I struck a deal with this Miles kid. I taught him to write, disguised as a teacher, and he helped me get my poems out of this closed-off detention center.
This is how the lesson went: I taught him the pronunciations of a few words, and then I wrote them down on a piece of paper and passed the paper and pen out of the window.
On that memorable day, Miles didn't start writing right away when I passed him the paper and pen.

speaker: Raye
content: What's the matter? Are today's words too difficult for you?

speaker: Miles
content: It's not that... Um, can you finish Heroes of Syndicate first?

speaker: Raye
content: Cough... cough...
That was something I came up with on the spot the day before, to get him to help get my poems out. As a good "teacher," how could I say no to a student's request?

speaker: Raye
content: Sure thing. Let's pick up where we left off yesterday. Remind me where we were yesterday.

speaker: Miles
content: Julien the Fate Challenger!

speaker: Raye
content: All right, let's talk about another hero of Rustfire then. This one is called the Thunder Halberd!

speaker: Miles
content: Wow, that name sounds badass...

speaker: Miles
content: Miss Raye...

speaker: Raye
content: What's the matter?
Miles was practicing writing on the other side of the window. Although his handwriting was still crooked and oftentimes illegible, it was much better than when he first started.

speaker: Miles
content: I think Syndicate isn't so bad after all. I want to stay.

speaker: Raye
content: You don't want to go to Eastside anymore?

speaker: Miles
content: No, I don't. I used to despise Syndicate, thought it was a decrepit place.

speaker: Miles
content: I don't think so now, after hearing you tell me about what it has been through, what it used to look like, and how countless people have fought on its behalf.

speaker: Miles
content: Plus...

speaker: Miles
content: It would be selfish of me to think only of filling my own belly. I want all my friends to have enough to eat.
I looked out of the window at Miles, who was absorbed in copying out my poetry.
I knew those were just the words of an innocent kid, but I saw the fire of resolve in his eyes when he said them.
I couldn't help but think, "If only I were a real teacher. Then I could teach him even more things, better things."
"If everything went right, maybe he could one day become a poet and write poems for me."
And then something went wrong. It hit when I least expected it. Somehow, my poetry was discovered by the guards of the detention center.
I was stripped of what few privileges I had been allowed. They took away my pen, ink, paper... They also kept Miles from making contact with me.
If they thought that was enough to shut me up, they had another thing coming.
I kept on writing. Since I had no way of getting my writings out of that place anymore, l left them where they were.
I looked for brick, plaster, anything with color in it, and turned it into my pen.
When I used up these items, when I couldn't scrape any bit of plaster from the walls of my cell...
I bit my own fingertip bloody and continued writing the heroic tales of Syndicate with my blood.
I wanted those heroes to be remembered, I wanted them to serve as an inspiration for future generations; I wrote for Miles, and for myself.
My body grew weak with each passing day due to oxygen deprivation and blood loss. My eyesight was failing fast.
Even the words I wrote down were crooked. They looked like crows in my failing eyesight. The whole thing was absurd...
Right before I closed my eyes and lost consciousness, I saw the words on the wall spout wings and fly out through the gaps between the iron bars one by one.
When I regained consciousness, I found that the words on the wall were gone, and there were crows in the cell. They were circling around a piece of paper on the floor, cawing.
They seemed to know I was awake; one of them picked up the piece of paper in its beak and flew over to drop it in my hand.
I opened the note. On it was the crooked handwriting that I had grown so familiar with...
"Thank you, Miss Raye."
They thought they could stop me from writing poetry; it's laughable.
My will was a crow that had long since flown out of her cage.

speaker: Chief
content: That's how you became a Sinner, and that's also when you decided to become a teacher.

speaker: Raven
content: That's right. From that point on, the prison staff could do nothing about me. That's when Raye stopped talking, and Raven started speaking.

speaker: Raven
content: With no evidence whatsoever against me, they had to let me go.

speaker: Raven
content: After my release, I put my newfound power to good use. To get back at those bastards, I went to a lot of trouble in Syndicate and Eastside. Of course, my power grew stronger with each of my life-and-death adventures.

speaker: Raven
content: I saw Donald, who was treated as a traitor back then, in that psychiatric hospital. He begged me not to tell Julien that he was alive, but I ignored his plea.

speaker: Raven
content: Soon afterward, I joined Rustfire and became a capable member of the organization. That gave me a chance to witness the changes in Syndicate.

speaker: Raven
content: Oh by the way, I also tracked down the DRD members who had tortured me and gave them a good beating.

speaker: Chief
content: After that, you joined the Executive Committee as an undercover agent, right?

speaker: Raven
content: Yes. And the next part of my story is about my encounters with you and your MBCC.
Epic stories of heroes, great individuals who worked tirelessly to change Syndicate for the better, battles against oppression...
These must be the kind of history that Raven wants to record.
You walk over to Raven's desk and pick up the textbook with the word "History" written on the cover. This is the revised textbook that she has been working on.
You open it, expecting to be awed by the poet's masterpiece.
But you don't find what you expected.
With the exception of the first page, where the events that transpired in Syndicate in N.F. 81 are recorded, the rest are blank.

speaker: Chief
content: Why is it mostly blank? You changed your mind about telling the stories of Syndicate to your students?
Raven opens her mouth, but nothing comes out.

speaker: Raven
content: I didn't.

speaker: Raven
content: I told the stories of Syndicate to someone before.

speaker: Raven
content: I told him about the hypocrisy of Eastside, the craftiness of Nirvana, the injustice of the W-31 incident; I gave him hope with stories about heroes.

speaker: Raven
content: He died.

speaker: Raven
content: Miles died.

speaker: Raven
content: He hated Eastside, hated Nirvana, hated all enemies of Syndicate.

speaker: Raven
content: In a foolhardy act, he stole a weapon from a Rustfire soldier, jumped over a fence, and got shot in the head by a bullet.

speaker: Raven
content: It was my fault. If I hadn't filled his head with all those stories and ideals, he would've stayed in Rustfire as my first student.

speaker: Raven
content: ...I remember clearly that that was the only time I ever got angry with Julien; I blamed him for the failure to keep the kid safe.

speaker: Raven
content: But I was not only angry at him; I was angry at myself too.

speaker: Raven
content: Children have a right to the truth, but the truth can be too heavy for them to bear.
Raven hands you her wrinkled press pass.

speaker: Raven
content: In Syndicate, there are already too many kids like that; they act on what their guts tell them.

speaker: Raven
content: Ica wants to avenge his parents' death, because they were captured by the executive officers and died in a detention center.

speaker: Raven
content: Crache hates all adults indiscriminately, because she was sold to Yagyu.

speaker: Raven
content: I still love the stories of heroes who fought the dark forces, but what kind of stories should I pass on to these children?
You step forward and hold Raven's trembling hands.

speaker: Chief
content: But I hope that in tomorrow's class, you'll give the children another chance to choose.

On the first day of school, Raven insists on giving lessons in the new classrooms at first, but gives up the idea after being told by the construction workers that there are a lot of air pollutants in these newly renovated rooms.
The safety of the students is far more important than where they should be taught.
So Raven sets up tables and chairs in the playground outside the teaching building.
You look around at the children. They're of different ages. Some appear to be about eight or nine years old, while others seem to be about fifteen or sixteen years old.
Raven has the Sinner standing in the nearby shadows to thank for such a good turnout.
She's sent, albeit with mock reluctance, all the kids from the Homeless to the Academy.
You also see something else that pleases your heart.
An enrollment application form that bears a name written in large, crooked letters...
Hella.
But the applicant is not present. Maybe she's afraid of you? You can even imagine what she would say if she saw you here.

speaker: Hella
content: Hey, what are you doing here? You're not here to laugh at me, are you?
You smile, replace the applications, and weigh them down with a stone. Then you find a seat in the back row and sit down, as if you were a parent of one of the students.
Almost five minutes into the first class, and the podium remains unoccupied.
However, in the next instant, a dark shape rushes into the room and takes up its place behind the podium.

speaker: Raven
content: Sorry, sorry I'm late... I lost track of time while preparing the best teaching materials for my dear students.

speaker: Raven
content: Listen to me. You gotta stay calm, no matter what happens here. All right?
The students look at Raven with suspicion, not knowing what she's going to do.

speaker: Student A
content: Miss, what's going to happen? Is it going to explode?
A bold student raises his hand and asks his question.

speaker: Raven
content: Well, how should I put it... I've prepared a surprise for you.

speaker: Raven
content: An explosive surprise.
As if on cue, a black crow appears above a student's head, flapping its wings.
The crow circles around a few times, drops a stack of textbooks on the student's desk, and flies away.

speaker: Crache
content: Heh, rotten bird, showing off again.
The shadow in the corner complains, but it doesn't sound angry.
The students watch in awe as a group of crows swiftly complete the delivery of the textbooks.
Such an ostentatious way to have books delivered. But that's just Raven being Raven.

speaker: Raven
content: All right, my dear students, let's get your first class at the Syndicate Academy started.

speaker: Raven
content: My name is Raven, like the name of the black bird. Of course, you can call me by my other name if you prefer...

speaker: Raven
content: Raye.
The class proceeds smoothly. You listen with interest. Whether it's because Raven is well-prepared for the class or because she's using a textbook from Eastside, you're not sure.
Time flies, and it's time for the students' first history lesson.
Before the lesson starts, you run into Raven in the corridor, who is carrying a lesson plan.

speaker: Raven
content: If I said I didn't make preparations, would you believe me?

speaker: Chief
content: I wouldn't.

speaker: Raven
content: If I said I'm fully prepared?

speaker: Chief
content: I wouldn't either.
Raven chuckles.

speaker: Raven
content: Looks like we're getting more and more in sync with each other.
Raven walks up to the podium in long strides. You stand to the side, watching the goings-on in the playground.

speaker: Raven
content: All right, my dear students, take out your history textbooks. Let's begin our first lesson on Syndican history.

speaker: Raven
content: We won't start with the year N.F. 81 today, the year when Syndicate was created. Instead, we'll talk about the year you are most familiar with first.
Raven turns around, and draws a horizontal line with chalk on the blackboard to create a timeline.

speaker: Raven
content: The year I'm talking about is N.F. 98, my dear students. Check your textbooks and tell me what happened that year.
Raven adds a dot on the timeline.
Raven closes her eyes and waits for the answer among the rustling of pages being turned.

speaker: Student C
content: Miss, there isn't anything written about that year in the book!

speaker: Student A
content: Yeah, it's blank.
The few students who can read have flipped through the entire textbook without the help of a dictionary, but they can't find any major events recorded for the year N.F. 98.
Raven asks the students to sit down, turns the pages for a second, and makes a slightly exaggerated gesture.

speaker: Raven
content: Ah, look at me, I must be getting old. How could I have misremembered the year?

speaker: Raven
content: My mistake. Let me see...

speaker: Student D
content: Miss...
A hand goes up.

speaker: Student D
content: Miss, I know... what happened... I think I know, although it's not written here.
After the initial surprise, she looks at the student encouragingly.

speaker: Raven
content: Tell everybody what you know then, loudly.

speaker: Student D
content: Well, actually... I learned it from my older brother. He told me that there was a very powerful organization in Syndicate during that period, called...

speaker: Student D
content: Rustfire!
There is a stunned silence when the name is uttered.

speaker: Student A
content: Did Rustfire exist back then?

speaker: Student B
content: Is he making this up?

speaker: Student C
content: I don't think he is. I heard that Donald joined the organization around that time...
Raven taps on the table to silence the students.
Then, with a flourish, she tears the blank page from the textbook, accompanied by a satisfying sound...
Raven lets go of the page. Carried by the wind, it flies away.

speaker: Raven
content: Well done. You've given an excellent answer.

speaker: Raven
content: History is all about personal experiences. If some of you witnessed or experienced a particular event, then this particular event must have happened.

speaker: Raven
content: If you don't agree with a certain written account, or if you have something to add to it, it's up to you to decide what to do about it. You can tear it off, if that's what you want to do.
You observe Raven's facial expressions closely, trying to figure out what she's up to.
Raven plows on with her questions.

speaker: Raven
content: So, what significant event occurred in N.F. 103?

speaker: Student B
content: I know. The Eclipse Operation!

speaker: Raven
content: Exactly. You found this piece of information fast. Good job. You can sit down now.
He doesn't.

speaker: Raven
content: What's the matter, kid? You've given your answer. Why are you still standing?

speaker: Student B
content: Miss, there's nothing about Syndicate in this textbook. It's all about the city on the other side.

speaker: Raven
content: Oh? Really?

speaker: Student B
content: That year, my whole family was out of work. My dad, mom, sister, me... and my neighbors as well. But Rustfire came to our rescue.

speaker: Student C
content: Our family too!

speaker: Student D
content: Our family too!
Several students stand up, echoing him.
Raven smiles, tearing off another page from the textbook.

speaker: Raven
content: So, what significant event occurred in N.F. 108?

speaker: Student D
content: The Reconstruction of Rustfire!

speaker: Student B
content: And the return of Syndican Hero Donald to Rustfire.

speaker: Student D
content: Wait a second. I heard he betrayed Rustfire.

speaker: Student B
content: You got it wrong. Donald was injured; he didn't betray Rustfire. And he got a cool nickname too, the Thunder Halberd!

Raven goes on to pick out a dozen more years. When she asks about the significant events of each year, she always gets answers from the students; some even offer their own opinions. They're eager to share what they know about this or that historical event.
The bell sounds for the end of the spirited discussion, with pages of paper floating in the Syndican sky. In the end, only the covers of the history textbook remain.
How do you like the surprise the children gave you?

speaker: Raven
content: Haha, you were right; they did deserve a chance. These students saved me. They're orphans, but they have hope for a bright future, even though they know the dark truth of the past.

speaker: Raven
content: They're fully aware of the circumstances they're in, but they never complain. They all hope that their life history will be remembered by others.

speaker: Raven
content: It delights me to know that the most bright flowers can be found amid fire and ashes. That makes it all worthwhile.

speaker: Raven
content: Everyone can see their future clearly, and the future of the West District has never been brighter.

speaker: Raven
content: The past is in the past, however painful it has been. It's time for us to look forward to the future.

speaker: Raven
content: Ah, but before we do any of that, can you reimburse me for the money I spent on the history textbooks?

speaker: Raven
content: I'm gonna write another set of textbooks and have a few hundred copies made. Would it be okay if I put the expenditure under your name, the honorary principal of the Syndicate Academy?

speaker: Student A
content: What class do we have tomorrow?

speaker: Student C
content: Have your head gone all muddy from spending too much time on math? It's poetry, of course.

speaker: Student A
content: Right. Math is really difficult. I'm lucky to have Miss Lavina as my math teacher; she's very patient with me.

speaker: Student C
content: Both Miss Raye and Miss Lavina grew up in that era. I can't believe that they're able to give us lessons after experiencing those horrible things...

speaker: Student A
content: Yeah... I want to become just like Miss Raye. Someone who searches for light in the darkness! It sounds so cool.

speaker: Student C
content: Give me a break. I don't want to go back to those days when we never had enough to eat.

speaker: Student A
content: Hehe, just saying. Like Miss Raye said in class before, "To forget is akin to betrayal."

speaker: Student C
