content: Only by remembering the painful days of the past will we know how to strive for a bright future!

speaker: Student A
content: By the way, do you know who that person sitting in the last row is? A friend of Miss Raye's?

speaker: Student C
content: More than just friends! I hear that the two of them always have meals together, and ride in the same car!

speaker: Student A
content: Really? Are they... ouch!
Before he can finish his sentence, a piece of chalk hits him on the forehead.

speaker: Raven
content: What were you two gossiping about over there?
The two naughty students are visibly shaken.

speaker: Student A
content: Cough... Miss Raye, we, uh, were just talking about how amazing you are!

speaker: Student C
content: Yes... we were.

speaker: Raven
content: Hehe... Is that so? Then you two recite "To the Future" to me.

speaker: Raven
content: There will be punishment if you even make a mistake or miss a word. That's my proudest work after all.
In the land of Syndicate, I witness both hope and despair.
Indulging in darkness, yet searching for light.
Writing poems, and becoming a poem.
In honor of the flames rekindled amidst the rust,
the winds howling amidst the forest,
In honor of the birds fluttering their wings in the storm, the flowers blooming in the mud.
In honor of dreams...
In honor of hope...
In honor of...
...the future

speaker: Crache
content: I hear this poem isn't a finished product.

speaker: Crache
content: Is that true? And if it is, when are you going to finish it?
The leader of the Homeless steps out from the shadows and smiles at the teacher known for her unconventional teaching methods.

speaker: Raven
content: Oh, about that? I'll get around to it when I get around to it.

speaker: Raven
content: There will be more tales about heroes in Syndicate in the future. That will certainly keep me busy.

Walking through familiar streets at a well-known hour, she goes against the flow of the crowd. A quick left and 50 meters more, and there's the Fifth Avenue. There stands the nerve center of Eastside—the towering Eastside TV Station.
A pale figure blends with the crowd, face blank, watching those who, glued to their phones, push their way upstream against the crowd.
The world spins in a listless haze, the clamor of the crowd mingling with unsettling noises.
Gradually, these sounds grow clearer, ringing distinctly in my ears.
Ting-a-ling...
Oh, there you are...
Are you here... to destroy me?

speaker: Eleven
content: Indeed, I am.
But haven't you already ruined enough lives? Isn't that enough? All I have left is... just this little bit of strength...

speaker: Eleven
content: Even a little is unacceptable. This is the root cause... It'll just lead to more of those unwanted problems.
Eleven strides against the crowd, moving swiftly. The jostling shoulders of pedestrians make her wince in pain, but she doesn't stop.

speaker: Eleven
content: It's time to stop; the last call at three in the morning has already ended.

speaker: Eleven
content: I'll make sure no one remembers that there ever was a show or a phone call like this.
Oh? Then what, exactly, is this we're doing right now...?
Eleven makes her way to the base of the TV building, uncovering a hidden black terminal in a nook.
As long as we both exist, there will always be another call coming in at three in the morning...
Another "host" will emerge...
The world will continue to be flooded with sounds you'd rather not hear!
Change is beyond your reach. Forever.
Clack.
The line goes dead on the terminal, echoing with a busy signal. The black device in her grasp turns into a shadowy mist, ascending into the heavens.

speaker: Eleven
content: ...This isn't the real deal.
Eleven gazes upward, the city's neon blaze hiding every star from view.
Yet, she remembered a sky brimming with stars here—that time on the highest rooftop, falling fiercely as if racing the stars.
She extended her hand, but it met only the empty air.

speaker: Eleven
content: Wait, this isn't right...?!

speaker: Eleven
content: That's not me!! I recall... that moment... he had held my hand!
female_content: That's not me!! I recall... that moment... she had held my hand!

content: An instant of reflection, and the atmosphere around begins to warp, something's off.
Eleven's breath catches in terror, feeling as though unseen hands are lifting her, propelling her from the ground floor to the rooftop!

speaker: Eleven
content: Could it be... is it... Mania??

speaker: Eleven
content: Could the real thing... actually be hidden here?

speaker: Malicious Voice
content: Didn't I say you should be laying on the compliments thicker? The more you suck up, the bigger your payoff. Got it?

speaker: Disdainful Voice
content: Controversy fuels fame; it's your chance to shine. Seriously, you're a fan of this, right? This is how you show your affection?

speaker: Eleven
content: ...And it's happening again, making me see all this stuff.
Images that flit across the sight are a mix of the known and the unknown.
They rake up the past Eleven was trying to put behind.
Beep beep beep—
A red alert pops up on your screen. You click to see a red dot blinking on the Dis map.
"Major spike in M-value in Eastside's south! Dispatch now to stop the surge!"
This again?
You check the time on your computer. Seeing it's the dead of night makes your eyelid flicker.
Feels like the Mania in Eastside's gotten worse lately...
But are we all okay, mentally?
Never mind, just the usual grind—more overtime, endless work, and the relentless call of duty.
You snap the file shut, organize it, and head out in your car to the designated spot.
Exiting the Bureau, the guard at the entrance salutes and hands you half of his wife's packed lunch—just a basic sandwich with a runny egg.
The further you drive, the more familiar the surroundings become.
You only twig it when that massive building looms up at your destination.
Trouble at the TV tower again? Don't tell me it's...
The moment you step out of the car, your phone goes off—and it's not just yours. All around, everyone's phones are ringing simultaneously.

speaker: Passerby A
content: Hello? Hello? Anyone there?

speaker: Passerby B
content: What's going on here?

speaker: Passerby C
content: Hello? Bad reception?
Your eyes fix on the terminal, an unknown caller ID lighting up. You swipe the green answer button.
With only the buzz of static filling your ears, you stay wordless, juggling the call while using your real ID to get through the television station's doors.
As you enter the elevator, the phone call's chatter slowly diminishes, giving way to a clear, feminine voice.

speaker: Female Voice Over the Line
content: Head to the roof.
You hit the top floor button, settling into a quiet wait.
Eleven, is that you?
Stirring up a storm here, who else could it be but you?
Looks like we're about to cash in on that goodbye you tossed my way.
How about we discuss a matter, what do you say?
It seems every time we meet, it's during my overtime hours...
How about you hop over to my bureau? Then, our meet-ups wouldn't exactly be overtime, right?
Or maybe you're actually keen on getting back to the TV station, to keep hosting that Call at 3 AM show?

speaker: Female Voice Over the Line
content: Yeah... I've been thinking...

speaker: Female Voice Over the Line
content: You see... I long to hear those voices, yearning for everyone to hear mine...
There's a brief pause on the line, her voice returning, distant and ethereal.

speaker: Female Voice Over the Line
content: To fill this world once more with...
The elevator doors part, casting a weak glow from the energy-saving lights dangling before them, leaving the hallway cloaked in shadows.
There's an unmistakable sense of dread as you stand there. Behind that door to the rooftop, a fearsome Mania energy is lurking, suffocating the air with its ominous presence.
Got it, loud and clear.
You quickly hang up and, with a swift motion, fling the door wide open—
On the empty rooftop, a swirling mass of dark energy wraps tightly around Eleven. She's motionless, eyes closed, seemingly unconscious.
In her grip, there's a terminal, clearly not hers, a bit on the older side. The signal light is still glowing, hinting at an active call.
That was you on the phone just now, right?
But, weirdly enough... it feels like I'm the only one who can hear that voice.
That old trick? I've seen it before in worlds warped by Mania.
Seriously, you don't expect me to fall for that line again, right?
Your eyes are locked on that vintage terminal, with your hands clasped behind you, glowing red, creeping ever closer to Eleven.

speaker: Female Voice Over the Line
content: It's not the same... We're different, in every way...

speaker: Female Voice Over the Line
content: I long for the world to... just once more... just once more...
Eleven!
The lights on that vintage terminal flicker, betraying its unrest. You catch this lapse, casting forth scarlet shackles that wrap tightly around the hands of the one deep in sleep.
Suddenly, a tidal wave of grief overwhelms you, sending a shiver through your body, like falling into a frozen abyss.

speaker: Eleven
content: You're not getting away from me.
Across the shackles, Eleven's eyes flutter open. Your strength stirs her to consciousness, igniting her spirit of defiance.

speaker: Eleven
content: Just vanish... vanish forever, I command you!
Eleven activates her powers, causing the vintage terminal in her hand to break free and rise, as if battling against an unseen force, into mid-air.
The dark mist that has been circling her now rushes towards it, wrapping it in a swirling embrace.
One by one, cracks spread across the terminal's body, punctuated by sharp snaps of breaking. The stubborn red light, which has been flickering all this while, at last fades to darkness.
Eleven, along with the old terminal, collapses to the ground. She lies there, breathing heavily, staring at the terminal with an expression that is a mix of confusion and unreadability.
Thankfully, it didn't lead to anything major this time.
You walk over, slip the terminal into an evidence bag, and then pivot to face Eleven.
So, Miss Eleven, how about...

speaker: Eleven
content: Can you please take me back with you?
Huh?

speaker: Eleven
content: It seems... everything's been taken care of. I had faith in your abilities...

speaker: Eleven
content: There's nothing left for me here now.
Eleven props herself up against the wall, gradually standing up. She brushes off the dust from her clothes and then offers her hand to you.

speaker: Eleven
content: Being a Sinner, it's only expected... that I be held in tight custody.

speaker: Eleven
content: Here... I no longer have a haven.
When you take her hand, the feeling of being linked by those shackles just moments ago is still palpable, undeniable.
Ease up, things here aren't as tough as you're imagining.
At least... you won't be left starving.
Did you get a chance to eat dinner?
Eleven seems unexpectedly taken aback by your question, hesitating briefly before giving a dismissive shake of her head.
Here you go. Go ahead, have a bite.
You hand over the sandwich to Eleven.
My colleague's wife whipped this up. She's got a magic touch, you know—turns even a basic sandwich into something scrumptious.
Guiding Eleven, you step off the elevator.
By the front doors, that video wall you'd glimpsed in the Otherworld remains lit up, as vivid as ever.
On the screen above, a feed cycles through show highlights, timetables, and a handful of bulletins.
Starting today, our regular broadcast "Call at 3 AM" will be on hiatus until further notice. We apologize for any inconvenience and appreciate our audience's patience.
The woman in front of you sits elegantly in the interrogation seat, looking like she could be about to start a TV show.
She greets you with a warm smile as you walk in.

speaker: Eleven
content: Great to meet again, Chief ${PlayerName}.
You hold the latest updates in your hands, looking at the woman before you, her smile gentle and reassuring, as you quietly take a deep breath.

options: It's only been a few hours since we last met.

speaker: Eleven
content: You look a little on edge, is everything alright?

speaker: Eleven
content: Why so tense? We both saw it, didn't we? The ultimate threat... it's been dealt with, and now I'm right here with you.
The ultimate threat? Are you talking about that vintage terminal, or something else...?
I caught sight of the announcement when I was returning from the TV station.
They've put your radio program on an indefinite hiatus...

speaker: Eleven
content: Hmm, I know that.

speaker: Eleven
content: I was the one who went to negotiate that personally.
You went there in person?

speaker: Eleven
content: Right... To be honest, I've been ready to come here for a while. The world beyond... there's no need for it to bear my mark.
Your mark...
You sift through the documents next to you, the ones you had put together before stepping out.
So, that's the reason... you wiped the memories of people who got those 3 AM calls?
Eleven appears unexpectedly taken aback that you dug up this info, hesitating for a moment.

speaker: Eleven
content: You... how on earth did you know?
I'm the head of the Minos Bureau of Crisis Control. Once I learned that this radio station was behind the Mania Event, investigating it thoroughly was a given.
Just doing my job...

speaker: Eleven
content: You've got a point there.

speaker: Eleven
content: That late-night radio show at 3 am... When I was the host, I had one clear goal: to hear out our audience, to offer solace for their daytime hurts, or calm the emotions that night couldn't quiet.

speaker: Eleven
content: I had intended for it to be a show that warmed hearts. Obviously, it didn't turn out as planned.
Eleven keeps smiling, but her eyes lower to the floor, almost as though she is mustering up the bravery to speak those hard truths.

speaker: Eleven
content: Whispers of the weird, swirling rumors, unyielding control of narratives, and constant public condemnation—they've all weighed heavily on me. Ultimately, I couldn't be the beacon of warmth I intended; instead, I turned into a perpetrator in this maelstrom of voices.

speaker: Eleven
content: With the root of all this chaos gone, it's a welcome change.
Eleven's voice trails off for a moment before she shrugs nonchalantly.

speaker: Eleven
content: Indeed, the airwaves are silent, and that final vintage terminal is no more... Call at 3 AM is a thing of the past.
Yet... out there, it appears someone is still getting those calls.
As you speak, a frown forms on Eleven's brow.

speaker: Eleven
content: No way.

speaker: Eleven
content: I might not have the strength to take down that terminal, but now that you're here...

speaker: Eleven
content: With your abilities, there's no way it could have gotten away...
Yet, here's the reality.
You push the tablet in front of Eleven, the swiftly scrolling entries on the screen leaving her momentarily flustered.

Post-investigation, searches for <color=#fb9259>"Call at 3 AM"</color> plummet, and you notice that memories of involved individuals are being deliberately wiped. You task the intelligence team to help erase any leads and manage the fallout.
However, moments ago, searches for the term surged back up, gaining traction fast. The rumors now spreading are eerily alike the previous ones.

<size=42><color=#7683a2>[Dismyth Forum][Discussion Board]</color>[Call at 3 AM Strikes Again]</size>

<color=#fb9259>Anonymous Poster</color>: The midnight calls are back! If you're up at 3 a.m., you could get a call from an unknown caller... A lady will share a story and pose a question.

<color=#fb9259>Anonymous Poster</color>: You've got to pick up, you've got to respond! Anyone who hangs up or gets the answer wrong ends up mysteriously dead!

speaker: Eleven
content: What... what did it do?!

speaker: Eleven
content: It's obviously been ruined already...
Yet, inside, the echoes of Mania are unmistakable. And... just before I got to the skyscraper, it seemed like everyone around, myself included, got this eerie, silent call.

speaker: Eleven
content: That's not right, that call was meant for you and you alone...
But, if I'm not mistaken, the voice on the other end of the line was supposed to be "someone else," wasn't it? And... at that moment, you were supposed to be out cold.
You lock eyes with Eleven, but she's the first to break away, conceding the silent battle.

speaker: Eleven
content: Sorry, I should've been upfront with you from the start.
Better late than never, right? This is exactly why we're here now.

speaker: Eleven
content: At the outset, when the world was ending and we fused together, a piece of power escaped... leaving my abilities fragmented...

speaker: Eleven
content: Moreover... it's constantly rekindling their eerie memories of calls received at 3 AM.

speaker: Eleven
content: I truly hope they could erase these memories... For anyone who's called in or listened to that broadcast, those memories are anything but fond.

speaker: Eleven
content: Dragged into a surreal realm, morphing into creatures with freakish heads, forced to utter words against their will, echoing the masses.

speaker: Eleven
content: I've been on its trail, determined to obliterate it... to regain my strength, and also... to extinguish the "Origin."
Eleven stares intently at the vintage terminal within the evidence bag, as though anticipating its indicator light to suddenly blink on again.

speaker: Eleven
content: However, I realized that without this part of my power, I can't control it, nor can I erase it. It overpowers me, attempting to use me once more for its old tricks.

speaker: Eleven
content: I... I deceived it, claiming that my current power and emotions are insufficient to create another world... but... with someone else's strength added, it surely could...
She raises her head, looking at you somewhat sheepishly.

speaker: Eleven
content: I used that terminal to call you... My plan was for us to take it down together... but I had no idea it could still reach out to so many people...
Ah, now it makes sense...
Back in the elevator, I figured out it wasn't you on the call, but both of you stem from the same Mania force.
Moreover, I had already found out about your efforts to erase information regarding this radio station, which led me to take a gamble, thinking I had won.
You bring the evidence bag to the center, questioning Eleven.

speaker: Eleven
content: Lock it up...
Lock it up?

speaker: Eleven
content: Ah, there's got to be a room around here, a kind of fortress that can totally shut out that Mania. If we stash it in there, we can make sure it doesn't mess with anything outside.

speaker: Eleven
content: Give it enough time, and these whispers will... well, they'll just disappear. People forget all about spooky stories and shows like this.

speaker: Eleven
content: The world is full of fascinating things and sounds that are constantly changing, but they all fade away in time.
Are you really going to go through with this, knowing your powers might never come back?

speaker: Eleven
content: My power... it's not exactly something to be proud of, right?

speaker: Eleven
content: It's brought nothing but trouble to everyone... and it's not like it can make my current predicament any better.
After finishing, Eleven hangs her head, shutting down further conversation.

speaker: Eleven
content: What should we try...?
One more use, and I'll unleash the power of these shackles. I'm convinced it'll lead us to some clues.
Eleven's face betrays a moment of doubt.
Don't worry, I'm here. I don't think... it could really create another world.
Upon hearing you, Eleven gives a small nod, lifting the fractured terminal to her ear.
Noticing she's set, you lift your right hand, triggering the power of your shackles.

speaker: Eleven
content: ...Ahhhhh.

Suddenly, there's a noise from the handset of the terminal. Panic creeps into Eleven's voice, uncontainable. That's when you see how ghostly pale she is, biting her lips as though she's hearing something ominous.

speaker: Eleven
content: Why... why not? Is it impossible to change anything, ever?

speaker: Eleven
content: Hey hey, I didn't...
Eleven's emotions spike, her fingers turning white from gripping the terminal so hard. The room starts to distort, responding to her rising panic, with the Mania sounds assaulting your ears.

speaker: Eleven
content: This isn't on me! It's all of you... you've always ignored what I had to say!

speaker: Eleven
content: You're the ones who cast me aside... because I was too weak... it's on me...

speaker: Eleven
content: If that's the case, then I'll just—!
Eleven! Drop it, let it go!

Eleven makes no move to stop you as you latch onto the terminal, but pulling it away is no easy task. The device exerts a powerful pull, freezing you in place, as the room distorts and tightens around you, your consciousness fading.
In the midst of this turmoil, you catch a sinister whisper on the other end of the line—a voice bubbling with anger and ill intent.
A story, with a question.
What I'm really wondering is... Eleven, have you actually... found the voice you've been searching for?
(The hum of electricity intensifies, climaxing in a blinding white flash.)
(The hum of electricity intensifies, climaxing in a blinding white flash.)
Suddenly, the buzzing stops dead. At that moment, the spinning world around you comes to a standstill, your feet at last touching solid ground.
The streets are well-known, but the crowds are unrecognizable. Night falls with a heavy mood, casting an oppressive air over the streets.
Lights shine bright against the deathly stillness.
Next time, I'll think before I speak... Who knew I'd eat my words this fast, actually bringing a whole new world into being...
You can tell immediately this is like the world Eleven had made, but it's clearly a lot less powerful.

The end of the road in sight is shrouded in darkness, not a speck of light. The only path you can see is teeming with people in business attire, all hurrying past you towards the only skyscraper in sight.
It's just you left standing in the throng of people; Eleven is gone.
Out of the blue, someone grabs your arm from behind.

speaker: Passerby A
content: You...

speaker: Passerby A
content: You... work...
Look, man, if there's something on your mind, let's talk about it. True, I'm on the job at the moment, but...

speaker: Passerby A
content: Can't skip it; work's an obligation; I have to get to work...!

speaker: Passerby A
content: Time's up... You should be heading... to work too...
Like those you've encountered in the other Mania worlds before, this odd-headed man in a suit grips your arm, the other hand stiffly pointing to a skyscraper far away.
But... my work isn't there...

speaker: Passerby A
content: Can't put off work... need to start right away...
Its grip tightens, almost yanking you forcibly towards the office tower.
...So, work over there...
I'm on my way, heading there now...
After all, it's not like I have anywhere else to go.
You're caught in the thick of the crowd, as crammed as sardines, all shuffling towards that tin-can of a building.
As you move, you're piecing together the puzzle of your current situation, step by step.
Eleven's lost power now clings to a vintage terminal... Blending her residual might with my shackles, the story of Call at 3 AM is spread anew...
Could it be, these whispers and the feelings they evoke have birthed another realm like this?
But why tread the same path again? To whom does that vintage terminal belong? Is all this just to keep the memory of "Call at 3 AM" alive in everyone's mind?
You look up at the skyscraper looming so close by...
Back at the TV station... What's lurking in its shadows?

As you step into the building, the thought of sneaking past the snarling turnstile without ID crosses your mind. But to your surprise, when the tide of people sweeps you to the front, the facial recognition system mirrors someone else's face, not yours.

speaker: A Robotic Tone
content: Access granted. Welcome aboard, Eleven.
It hits you then. When you engage your shackles, you find Eleven's position coinciding with yours... Somehow, you and Eleven have become one and the same.

options: Could this be another spooky tale...

content: All I can offer is... my sincerest apologies... It wasn't fair to you... I'm truly sorry...
female_content: Honestly, this is the first time I've ever faced anything like this...

speaker: Eleven
content: No... It feels like a fragment of my mind is now intertwined with yours...
female_content: Same here... I've only known how to disconnect, never to become one with another like this...

speaker: Eleven
content: It's kind of enchanting...
female_content: But, I actually feel it's more like a part of my consciousness has connected with yours...

content: Like making a phone call, isn't it?

speaker: Eleven
content: It's hard to say for sure...

speaker: Eleven
content: Considering it's my power, who's to say it isn't the birth of a brand-new urban legend?
But I think it's just a partial merging of minds, kind of like we're on a phone call.

speaker: Eleven
content: You see... I genuinely couldn't feel you were there. I assumed I was alone in the crowd heading to the building, until just a moment ago when it hit me...
It looks like we only hear each other when we're both aware.
So, where are you hiding?
The shackles suggest you're close by, maybe right in my spot.
While talking, you head to the well-known second floor. Around the corner, you spot an elegantly dressed full-length mirror.

speaker: Eleven
content: Huh? Do I... see you?
I feel the same...
As you move towards the mirror, it reflects two images—you and Eleven.
Eleven is right in front of you, casting a silhouette that enshrouds you.

speaker: Eleven
content: Does it feel like... you've turned into a guardian angel on my back?
Through the mirror, you watch Eleven raise her hand, and you do the same. Yet, as you attempt to move beyond her, to stand in front of her, you realize you're unable to.

speaker: Eleven
content: It's still a realm born from my abilities, my fixation... So, I guess I'm the one in control, right...
Probably a good thing, actually. You know this TV station better than me, so it makes sense for you to lead.
While you both are taking it all in, a ruckus suddenly breaks out on the third floor.

speaker: Employee A
content: Work! Work! Work builds value, brings happiness, and realizes dreams!!

speaker: Employee B
content: Work... Argh... Argh... Argh... Survive, then slave away...

speaker: Eleven
content: That's my old workplace up there!
Let's head up and check it out!
Eleven guides you to the third floor, and what you see is startling—

The office is teeming with people. Even though it's way past midnight, nearly everyone's glued to their desks. Amid the brightly illuminated cubicles, a symphony of footsteps and chatter fills the air.
The workers, with their bizarre head, labor mechanically but with fervor, making you almost believe in the "upbeat and dynamic corporate culture" illusion.

options: Is this the norm at the TV station...?
Is this the onset of a Corruptor outbreak?

speaker: Eleven
content: First time at the TV station, huh? Because of varying show times, there are always people working, even in the dead of night.

speaker: Eleven
content: This is especially true for the current events team. At critical times, they're practically on call around the clock.
Ruthless company... MBCC at least shells out for extra hours.
...Or offers compensatory leave.

speaker: Eleven
content: These fabricated realms use reality as a blueprint for their virtual spaces, likely because they're also shaped by my memories.

speaker: Eleven
content: Yet, it's odd... My show is a late-night broadcast. It's not typical to have so many people sticking around...
Eleven!

A sharp, woman's voice slices through the air, aimed directly at you. A group of employees hurry over, encircling something that looks like a microphone. But as they part, you're shocked to see it's not some prop they're hoisting up—it's a person's severed head.
Just then, this "Mic" emits a jarring, pressing sound, demanding attention.

speaker: Eleven's Boss
content: Look at the clock! Why are you still loafing around?

speaker: Eleven's Boss
content: The show's kicking off soon, you better get to the studio! How do you youngsters even manage to snooze through this?

speaker: Eleven
content: The show...? Hold on, wasn't my show put on hold...

speaker: Employee B
content: Come on, Miss Eleven! It's nearly 3 in the morning!

speaker: Employee A
content: You know, Miss Eleven, you've become the star broadcaster of our station recently. Your live shows have a huge fan following!
You find yourselves encased by a sea of employees, being guided further into the heart of the building. Passing along the corridor, you once more notice the reflection of two figures in the glass.
Eleven's face is unsmiling, her features hidden in shadow, enigmatic and unclear.

You trail behind Eleven into the broadcasting room. There's just a microphone in front of you, a thin script, and onlookers from behind a nearby glass. The producer, with a microphone-head, appears to be speaking, but the silence glass muffles any sound.
In the absolute hush of the room, your own voice is the only sound you hear.

speaker: Eleven
content: Feeling a bit nervous?

Eleven takes her place at the mic, expertly thumbing through the script and fine-tuning the volume. The instant she settles in, she seems to be in her element—her actions smooth and effortless, compelling enough to make your heart race just watching her.
There's an unmistakable tension, seeing how you've set things up. Everything is precise and well-planned, it gives off a vibe like "we're on the brink of something major."
I've been through much rougher patches. It's just your tight, professional setup that's making it seem like we're on the brink of something momentous.

speaker: Eleven
content: It's all a bit of a façade, kind of like how a news host fills time until the end credits roll.

speaker: Eleven
content: Being a radio host, you don't have to be seen; this stuff is... just for their eyes.
Eleven looks up briefly at the soundproof glass. Outside, the crew is still huddled around the producer with a microphone-head.
Yet, you're truly a pro at this, aren't you? You seem to love what you do.
Eleven's hand hesitates, her face clouding over.

speaker: Eleven
content: Indeed... But when it turns into something unsettling, a harbinger of danger...

speaker: Eleven
content: If liking is all there is, then it loses its purpose.
You're about to respond, to challenge her, but at that moment, the indicator light flashes on.
Eleven swiftly regains her composure, leans towards the microphone, and speaks gently.

speaker: Eleven
content: "Maybe you've wrapped up a busy day, or perhaps you're still mulling over the fatigue of today..."

speaker: Eleven
content: "Welcome to Call at 3 AM. This is where you can talk about your worries, open up about what's on your mind, or share a slice of happiness."

speaker: Eleven
content: "The night has settled in. Regardless of how your day went, I'm always here... ready to hear what you have to say."
Eleven gently unfolds the introduction for today's show. Her voice, processed and overlaid, turns into signals, broadcasting through the city on radio waves.

speaker: Eleven
content: So, let's bring in our first listener's call—
Following a few busy signals, the line finally connects to the studio.

speaker: Listener B
content: Hi there... Am I on... Call at 3 AM?
A soothing voice whispers in your ear, reminiscent of the comforting warmth of a winter sun, casting a glow around you.

speaker: Eleven
content: Yes... that's right! I'm Eleven. Is there anything on your mind you'd like to share?

speaker: Listener B
content: You know... there's this thing that's been on my mind for quite some time. I've been going back and forth on it, with no one around to bounce ideas off. I guess... maybe I could run it by you?

speaker: Eleven
content: Absolutely, I'd be more than happy to lend an ear and share your burden.

speaker: Listener B
content: So, here's the deal... I've been invited by one of my classmates to the school's anniversary dance, which is happening soon. Can you believe it? It's my first-ever invitation!

speaker: Listener B
content: People have always said I'm not that attractive, my family included. That's why I usually play it safe with just T-shirts and jeans...

speaker: Listener B
content: But, for the dance, dresses are a must, aren't they? So, I went ahead and chose a couple of dresses online that I thought might work...

speaker: Listener B

Being the kind soul as I always am, I took him in and signed him to a year of service with all the necessary welfare. I also promised him a journey to the fabled paradise of DisCity afterward...

Dear, I can hear you snickering.

Désir is gone, but it's never truly lost.

Yet, he failed my trust. He fled with a good portion of our supplies. By the time this letter reaches you, he should be near the border. I trust you know what to do, right?
Hail and well met, my partner in justice. Yours, Vautour Bleu
Vautour Bleu's letter ends abruptly, very much in line with her style. She seldom speaks her mind directly, instead leaving others to decipher her true intentions through carefully placed hints.
If things turn out well, you owe her a favor. Otherwise, you've simply misinterpreted her meaning. So sophisticated.

speaker: Chief
content: Partner in justice... No such heroic character would stand by and watch someone suffer a merciless fate, even if it's some desperado on the run.

speaker: Chief
content: Using people as bargaining chips. Is this the trade you want, Vautour Bleu?
After careful consideration, you decide to accept this deal. After all, this is in DisCity, not Désir. Even if she is indeed plotting something, you're sure you can handle it.

speaker: Chief
content: Nightingale, notify the Border Bureau. We don't know what this man stole from the caravan yet, but he's unlikely to enter the city through legal channels. Conflicts is probably imminent.

speaker: Chief
content: Get our operatives ready. Let me know immediately once you locate him.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, are you going there yourself?

speaker: Chief
content: How else can I verify what we're dealing with if I don't? Don't worry. Vautour Bleu may be shrewd, but I don't make bad investments either.
Despite that, a shadow of doubt still lingers in your mind.
Vautour Bleu is a merchant for whom profit always comes first. So what drives her to reach out to you, share what she knows, and propose this deal? What does she really want?
You try to recall your time in Désir for clues, but the more you think, the less you figure out. Vautour Bleu's like a mirage in WhiteSands, ethereal, but potentially lethal if touched by.

speaker: Chief
content: Looks like we'll have to deal with it anyway, no matter how suspicious it is... Sitting here overthinking won't do any help.

speaker: Chief
content: You won't expect me to go easy on someone like you, would you? Business is war, Miss Merchant, and vice versa.
WhiteSands stretches endlessly to the horizon. The blazing sun pours shimmering heat waves above the scorching sands. No living creature would dare traverse these dunes at this high noon.
Except this man. He's clad in desert gear stolen from the merchant caravan, its thick insulation layer and cooling circulation system allowing him to survive the lonely trek across WhiteSands.
His pack, once bulging with supplies, now hangs nearly empty. Only one last bottle of water and a few hardtacks remain.

speaker: Lyman
content: Hah... hah... How many days so far? Guess... 19?

speaker: Lyman
content: That truck we stole wasn't half bad. Beat up here and there though, still ran fine. Wouldn't have abandoned it if it hadn't run out of fuel.

speaker: Lyman
content: Been walking for ages, are we? Lost track of time. Going on foot is slow, but we're used to it, aren't we, Evelo? Just like when we marched against desert bandits and disasters back then.
The man stops to adjust his pack as if still carrying some heavy burden, tightening the straps across his shoulders. The grotesque scar on the back of his hand is clearly visible.

speaker: Lyman
content: No weapons, no commanders with a functioning brain... and of course, no Hypercubes. We used to envy DisCity's FAC so much. Heard each of their soldiers got plenty.

speaker: Lyman
content: But what could we do? Our poor little town kept gambling on our lives, one after another. After you all died, it didn't take long for the whole party to fall apart... Hah, that's when I finally saw my chance to escape.

speaker: Lyman
content: I ran into that woman called Vautour Bleu and her caravan. Said she could take me to DisCity to live that "good life," but only if we make a deal first.

speaker: Lyman
content: To hell with her deal, f*** liar. That woman never planned to go to DisCity. She thinks I'm easy to fool around, huh? Ain't she the most useless one in the caravan?
His body and mind teeter on the edge of collapse, his legs driven forward by nothing but hollow hope and burning hatred.

speaker: Lyman
content: I stole their car, got us water and food, even their cargo. Took that navigation device off the car too.

speaker: Lyman
content: Once I reach DisCity, I'm gonna sell this gear. That should give us enough money to settle down there.

speaker: Lyman
content: If only we'd had gear like this back then... It'd probably have cost an arm and a leg, but at least Belmar would survive.

speaker: Evelo
content: That's right. Keep moving, Lyman. You must make it to DisCity. Do it for us.
He rubs his eyes, and through the writhing heat wave, he sees a few swaying familiar silhouettes. They wave to him, and one approaches, reaching out as if to help him up.

speaker: Belmar
content: Go, Lyman. We can't make it to DisCity, but you will. See that promised land for all of us.

speaker: Lyman
content: ...You bastards.
Lady Hypatia.

speaker: Lyman
content: Just don't go yet... Stay with me, a little longer...

speaker: Guard
content: Sir, we've got someone at the checkpoint. He's from WhiteSands.

speaker: Comissioner
content: Just one person? Not with a caravan? That's a restricted zone. How could he make it through?

speaker: Guard
content: Confirmed, it's just him. No anomalies detected in the surrounding area, his M-value within the safe range. Might be a refugee who got separated from the group.

speaker: Comissioner
content: It could also be a disguised Corruptor, or a spy from Outlands... Stay alert. Let's go and have a look.
At the foot of the border wall, Lyman lifts his head in a daze, confronted by the towering barrier that cuts off everything beyond.

speaker: Lyman
content: So this is... DisCity...

speaker: Lyman
content: Here, our dreams... we're finally here...
Before he becomes aware of the situation, several heavily armed soldiers appear and surround him.

speaker: Guard
content: Name? Age? Where are you from?

speaker: Lyman
content: ...Ly... Leonard. 30 years. I'm an... engineer. I'm from DisCity... was sent to Désir for a commission... I was heading home to visit my family when the desert bandits attacked.

speaker: Lyman
content: No matter what happens, time always takes on the same appearance in my hands. Yesterday, today, tomorrow, every day... nothing ever changes.
He recites the details of the fake identity Vautour Bleu forged for him two weeks ago.
Having no idea what kind of place Désir is, he can only dodge the guard's questions about its details by playing up his exhaustion and mental confusion.

speaker: Lyman
content: I'm an engineer from DisCity! My family's waiting for me!

speaker: Guard
content: We'll let you through once we verify your identity. Hold out your hand.

speaker: Lyman
content: What...
He watches stupidly as the guard takes his hand, collecting fingerprints and a blood sample to match with the database. An ominous chill crawls up his spine.

speaker: Guard
content: Sir, your DNA profile says your name's Lyman. You're no engineer. You're an active Outland soldier.
Clack. The familiar sound of guns being loaded pierces the air as multiple black barrels point simultaneously at Lyman.

speaker: Guard
content: Hands up! You are under suspicion of espionage and illegal entry. You are under arrest by the DisCity Border Guard!

speaker: Lyman
content: That's impossible! She promised me, she said she'd set it up for me... No, I-I'm not Lyman. My name is Leonard! I'm an engineer from DisCity!

speaker: Lyman
content: Look, this is our company uniform. This proves for me!

speaker: Guard
content: Who do you mean by she?

speaker: Lyman
content: She... Sh-she's...
Lyman still hasn't gotten over his grueling journey. He stares around in confusion, his muscles still twitching from the memory of constant exertion, eventually going into spasm.
Lyman collapses to his knees. When he raises his head, all he can see are the cold gun barrels pointed at him from every corner of the area.
That's when his dignity crumbles.

speaker: Lyman
content: Please, please... Mercy please! Just let me in! I'm not a spy. I spent a whole month crawling through WhiteSands to get here!

speaker: Lyman
content: I swear I mean no harm to DisCity! I just want a life. A life with no Mania and disasters!

speaker: Lyman
content: Y...you can lock me up, Sir. Do me investigation, as long as you want! Just please don't send me back. I can't go back to that hell!
Lyman gazes hopefully at the commissioner's pampered face, so different from the weathered, battle-worn features of even the highest-ranking officer he's ever seen.

DisCity's prosperity and peace are laid bare before him in the most visceral way. He's willing to cast aside every shred of his ego, begging this official for just a touch of the magnanimity befitting such a great city.

speaker: Comissioner
content: I regret to inform you, Mr. Lyman, that your actions constitute illegal entry. Moreover, your military status complicates matters as it interferes with Outland political protocols.

speaker: Comissioner
content: Therefore, we will deport you after notifying your home city. Until we're ready for that, you shall remain here.
The commissioner's hollow, bureaucratic sympathy crushes Lyman's last bit of hope, his features contorting with horror and despair.

speaker: Lyman
content: Deport me? No, I'm not going back. I'll die there! There's nothing there but suffering!
If I'm going to die... If I'm going to die anyway...!
He leaps up in a frenzy, breaking free of his restraints and charging toward the checkpoint.

speaker: Guard
content: Watch out! He's forcing through!

speaker: Comissioner
content: Stop him! Snipers, get ready.
Deaf to all warnings, Lyman fixes his eyes only on the barrier ahead, a fragile obstacle that seems so easy to break through.
It's there. Right there.
Everyone's dreams and hopes. The oases and springs that carried him through WhiteSands. Lying right there.
Let me through. Just let me through...!
Stop!! Stop there!! Don't...
BANG—!
Vautour Bleu's pen slips, slicing through the letter paper with a sharp, piercing scratch.
Both pen and paper, her loyal companions in the past two weeks, are now ruined, like a sign of something imminent.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: ...Ruined, after all.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Looks like the ending won't change no matter who's holding the pen.
With a soft sigh, she discards the spoiled paper and pen, deciding to abandon the letter altogether.
As the haze dances and fades before her eyes, she thinks she sees those long-lost young faces from her memories.
Those hopeful souls who once journeyed with her to DisCity, they too perished along the way.
There will always be gamblers willing to bet their lives on hollow dreams.
And yet...
And yet.

speaker: Assistant
content: Boss, is everything alright? You don't look well.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Nothing. Just reminiscing about the past. Anything new?

speaker: Assistant
content: Yes. In fact, we... we've been surrounded!

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Look at you, boy, you're practically shaking. It's not the first time we get a run-in with desert bandits.
Catching Vautour Bleu's indifference, the assistant lowers his voice anxiously.

speaker: Assistant
content: No, this time it's not just some petty bandits. It's the FAC from DisCity! They're saying... you're involved in sneaking some Outland deserter into DisCity!

speaker: Assistant
content: They've hit you with some serious charges, like um... motivating illegals and disrupting Outland relations? They want to take you in for questioning!

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Oh? The FAC from DisCity?
A flicker of surprise crosses Vautour Bleu's face, but it quickly gives way to bitter realization.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: For them to come now, it must be about that incident. I was even counting on that kid. To change the ending of the story...? Just being naive I am, heh.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Well then, a deal is a deal. It's time for me to hold up my end of the bargain.

speaker: Assistant
content: Boss! Are you really going? But if you leave now, the caravan...
The split second of bitter realization vanishes, and right in the next moment, her characteristic self-assured smile returns to her face.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: No need to worry, boy. They just want me to assist with their investigation. I'll be back once it's done. While I'm away, continue along the route as planned.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: You might not get the best deals without me doing the talking... But think of it as a chance to practice. I don't expect you to make a fortune anyway. Just try not to lose money while I'm away.

Night has fallen. In the dim light, the caravan crew sit around their campfires, some clutching ladles and spatulas, others holding bowls and spoons, all glaring viciously at the FAC operatives standing in their midst.

It almost seems one word from Vautour Bleu would send her people charging in with their makeshift weapons. And it is in this tense atmosphere that the caravan's owner approaches the FAC operatives with graceful tardiness.

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: Vautour Bleu, correct? We might need you to go with us to DisCity, and assist with our investigation.
In the flickering firelight, the FAC soldier's face is expressionless like a machine and the voice that comes out is also utterly flat.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Sure thing. Cooperating with the authorities is the sacred duty of a humble merchant like myself. Though I must admit that I'm quite curious, how did you manage to find me?

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: That's not a question we can answer. But you have the right to ask the person in charge once we arrive in DisCity.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Sometimes being flexible might serve you better, sir. That Chief of yours at the MBCC knows how to play the game.
She raises a hand to quiet her restless crew, her smile remaining as gentle as ever.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Well then, shall we go, little bloodhounds?

The FAC's vehicle looks even fancier than customized cargo trucks. This is no doubt the result of Vautour Bleu's regular "contributions" to the officials. The big shots in DisCity clearly want no harm to come to her.
Once inside, Vautour Bleu helps herself to a cocktail from the fridge, which is clearly not a regular item in an FAC vehicle. She settles down to enjoy the drink with perfect composure.

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: As per our superiors' orders, we won't restrict your movements. However, we strongly advise that you remain sober until the investigation officially begins.

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: We wouldn't want you to be so intoxicated that you'll conveniently forget the true identity of Lyman, that Outland infiltrator, before the questioning even begins.
The FAC soldier sitting across from Vautour Bleu speaks stiltedly, his tone and gaze vigilant and hostile. To him, she's clearly nothing more than a common criminal disturbing the city' order.
But these low-ranking soldiers' standoffish attitude fails to intimidate Vautour Bleu a bit. She lounges in the leather seat languidly, playfully swirling her glass at the soldier.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Easy, young man, this level of hospitality won't cloud my judgment. Besides... I'm already here to honor our arrangement. Relax, your boss won't be disappointed.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: But what about you all... This can't be an easy assignment, can it? You get no supplies out here in WhiteSands, only annoying desert bandits and disasters. And you have to sit here ramrod straight for days on end... Isn't it exhausting?

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: That's none of your concern. The FAC is well-stocked with Hypercubes. We've never feared desert bandits or disasters.

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: Besides, we've deployed top-tier equipment to expedite your transit to DisCity. In no more than three days, you'll be handed over to the Bureau.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Oh? So I'm an important witness, aren't I? Am I in the VIP lounge now? Haha.
Vautour Bleu lets out a derisive laugh.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: How very fitting of the mighty DisCity.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Back then, it took me three whole years to trek this same journey...
Western WhiteSands, Territory of House Noailles

speaker: Edna
content: Ladies and gentlemen, I have sorrowful news to announce.

speaker: Edna
content: Three months ago, we lost contact with my husband Alden Noailles and my son Joel. We've been trying to find their whereabouts since then, but to no avail.

speaker: Edna
content: Worse still, the suspension of our business during these three months has placed us in severe financial difficulty.

speaker: Edna
content: Two months ago, defending against the disaster depleted most of our Hypercube reserves. Yesterday, a new disaster began looming and is now approaching us. We... I must face reality.
Her voice trembled before she can even finish, dissolving into quiet sobs.
Most of the caravan's core members had joined that trading expedition three months ago, and none had been heard from since. Losing so many elite members at once left the family's caravan leaderless.

Now, the remaining members and relatives were overwhelmed by the profound grief of losing their family, friends, and leaders, as well as anxiety about their future. The disasters, the Hypercubes, the fate of their caravan...

speaker: Emma
content: What... what do we do now? Will our family split? I don't want that...

speaker: Old Hugh
content: Nonsense! Whoever wants to leave may go ahead. I'm staying right here with the lady and the family!

speaker: Emma
content: Me too! ...But even if we stay, can we really protect them? We're almost out of Hypercubes...

speaker: Old Hugh
content: Why don't we go to DisCity? It's the largest city there is. There's bound to be plenty of business there! We could set up a new trade route and start fresh together.

speaker: Landon
content: Easy for you to say! DisCity is on the other side of WhiteSands! Who's gonna lead us? The master and young master are both missing. Who else could guide us through?
The room fell in awkward silence. A name lied on everyone's tip of tongue, but no one had the heart to speak out.
Lady Madeleine, the eldest daughter of the Noailles. A natural-born businesswoman whose talent surpassed her brother's, she had already been handling multi-million contracts while still in her teens.

Yet she had never been into it. A lover of art, fine cuisine, flowers, and the pleasures of life, she had declined the offer to lead the caravan many times before. Could they really ask her to shoulder such a heavy burden that would overwhelm even the best leader?
Outside the door, the girl pressed her forehead against the wood, listening to the family servants volunteering to share the burden of leadership. She clenched her fists, then slowly relaxed them.

In the shadow of the ornately carved door, a symbol of her family's glory, the girl composed herself, carefully arranging her face until it mirrored her father and brother's casual optimism. Then she pushed the door open, determinedly.

speaker: Madeleine
content: Everyone, enough. I will take it over. I will lead everyone to DisCity.

speaker: Biber
content: Madeleine...! Are you sure about this? Don't push yourself. Once I'm old enough, I could also lead us to DisCity!

speaker: Landon
content: That's right, Miss. We're an old and useless lot, but we can still...

Madeleine raised her hand to silence the words from her servants. Seeing the mixture of concern, hope, and disbelief in their eyes, she adopted a more serious tone and her expression grew more resolute.

speaker: Madeleine
content: I mean every word I said. It's settled. Though I can't guarantee success in leading all of us across WhiteSands, I can never be so heartless as to leave you all here to die.

speaker: Madeleine
content: Now, let me assign our jobs. Emma, Landon, take inventory of all sellable goods and pack them up. Make sure our packs are as neatly as possible.

speaker: Madeleine
content: Hugh, I know you have a copy of the map that Father and Brother carried with them. Bring it to me tomorrow morning.

speaker: Old Hugh
content: Yes, yes, of course! At your word, Miss!
As she gave one order after another, the reception room grew lively again. Not only were those called upon bubbling with excitement, but the rest all began picturing a future.

speaker: Servant A
content: I've heard DisCity is the largest Hypercube producer, and the safest city too! Once we get there, all our troubles will be behind us!

speaker: Madeleine
content: True, but to reach DisCity safely, we must plan our route as carefully as possible. We have a long journey ahead.

speaker: Servant B
content: Have we got enough supplies for the trip? We can always trade along the way! That's what we do best. Come on everyone, let's show them what we're made of!

speaker: Madeleine
content: Yes, that's definitely our strength. I'll plan our route based on our inventory, and if we work together as one, we will reach DisCity.
Seeing how her attitude and words successfully dispelled the gloom hanging over the room, Madeleine secretly let out a sigh of relief.

At last, she knew her strategy worked. Just as her vision of the future ignited hope in their eyes, their renewed spirit and optimism now shone like an oasis in the boundless deserts, showing her the way forward.
Hope and dreams would guide them to the promised land. That will be the day. That must be the day.

speaker: Old Hugh
content: Um, Miss... Have you thought about, well, using a different name?

speaker: Madeleine
content: Why? Is something wrong with my name?

speaker: Old Hugh
content: The merchant caravans in WhiteSands are all roughnecks like me. Your name... may sound too soft for other traders to take you seriously. And better not go by Noailles either. We don't want those debt collectors coming after us.

speaker: Madeleine
content: ...Then how about, Vautour Bleu.
The girl's gaze rested quietly on her half-finished desert landscape. Paints were a luxury in their harsh journey, so she could only mix whatever colors she had left for the painting.
A vulture, against the blue sky, gorging itself on a corpse in the sand.

speaker: Old Hugh
content: Vautour Bleu... A blue vulture! What a majestic name! Those desert bandits won't even dare come near you!

speaker: Merchant
content: Have you heard about Vautour Bleu? That lady boss is really something, young but ruthless. Her people burned down every single one of Red Claw's depots when their talk didn't go well. Didn't leave them a single straw.

speaker: Drunk Patron
content: Now everyone around here has to go through her for goods. She's good, way too ******* good at this.

speaker: Merchant
content: More than that. Do you know how much her caravan makes in a single run? At least this much. And you know what's the real shit about her?

speaker: Merchant
content: While others have no choice but to surrender their goods to desert bandits, she's found a way to trade with them! Good thing her caravan is still small. Otherwise, she's prolly gonna take over the whole WhiteSands!

speaker: Drunk Patron
content: No shit. No matter how big her business is, when disasters strike, everyone's got to run and hide. No one can stand that.

speaker: Drunk Patron
content: Look at the Noailles. They were basically on the throne just a few years ag—Ow! Who the hell hit me...

speaker: Landon
content: Miss, the sandstorm is gaining on us. We have three hours at most! Even if we run now, I'm afraid half of the caravan won't make it!

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Get the supply trucks over here. We don't have enough Hypercubes left to protect all vehicles, prioritize these ones and our crew. As for the cargo, save what we can and leave the rest.

speaker: Old Hugh
content: Miss, but these goods are everything we have! If we lose them, we'll have to start over again from scratch!

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Don't be silly. I will never choose some cargo over you guys' lives!
But Vautour Bleu's stern words couldn't stop the stubborn old servant.

speaker: Old Hugh
content: We still have some Hypercubes left on the trucks. I've checked. Get two of our best drivers to take the trucks west, and we'll be able to slip past the storm's flank!

speaker: Old Hugh
content: We'll regroup at the next stop after the storm passes! If we can save these goods, we can rebuild everything!

speaker: Old Hugh
content: I've spent my whole life behind the wheel dodging disasters like this. Today's the day I show the storm what I've got.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: This isn't just some ordinary sandstorm! Hugh, you can't throw your life away! Hugh—!

speaker: Biber
content: Miss, me and the boys found a mining site. Looks like it's covered by quicksand, but we're thinking of checking it out.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: No. You can't go.

speaker: Biber
content: Madeleine! I know you're worried about everyone after what happened to Hugh, but we can't keep going on like this!

speaker: Biber
content: We're already running low on goods, and even you can't conjure merchandise out of thin air! If we secure that mining site, we'll have a new source of supply!

speaker: Biber
content: Even if it's not a Hypercube mine, any mineral vein we find would make our days so much easier.

speaker: Biber
content: I'll just take a quick look! I promise I'll come back in one piece!

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: ...He never came back. It wasn't until that moment that I truly understood how desire leads us all to our doom.

speaker: Edna
content: Madeleine... Don't... don't blame your brother. He just so wanted to be a grown man.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: ...I know, I just can't... keep going, Mom.

speaker: Edna
content: Madeleine, oh, Madeleine...! My dear daughter...
A headstone carved from sand and stone marked this crude grave.
Leaving her mother's favorite flowers from homeland, Vautour Bleu gathered a handful of sand and slowly poured it onto the gravestone.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Landon, how many of us left?

speaker: Landon
content: Thirty.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Hah... We started out with fifty. Lost almost half of us in such a short time.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Was it worth it? All of this just for a few crates of goods and some useless minerals!

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Answer me, Landon! Was it worth it?!
She lashed out uncharacteristically before her mother's grave, her old servant silently accompanying her aside. Tears running dry, she regained her composure, rising once again from the ground.
The sunset bled crimson across the sky.

No one called her Madeleine anymore. Lady Noailles, sister, daughter... One by one, her old identities have faded away. Now, she stands as Vautour Bleu and Vautour Bleu only, who devours everything, including the remains of her enemies.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: ...Let's go. We can't delay any longer. We must reach DisCity as quickly as possible, whatever the cost.

At last, after two years and two hundred eighty-seven days, with more than half of the crew gone, bereft of all families and her most trusted staff, Vautour Bleu led the remaining crew to DisCity's border.
Around the evening bonfire, an unusual silence fell over the camp. Their eyes fixed upon the towering city walls in the distance almost reverently, each mind painting pictures of what lay beyond.
Vautour Bleu negotiated with DisCity's border officials, securing the precious entry permits from their hands.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Alfie, this is your share of the profit. It's less than we hoped for, but perhaps we could borrow some textbooks first, then think about getting you into a school later...

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Jake, you lost your leg for our caravan. I swear I'll take care of you for the rest of your life...

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Everyone, our funds are just enough to secure the investor entry permits for each of us.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: For what's next, we'll have to plan that out after we enter DisCity. And for now, let's get some sleep. We'll cross the border at sunrise.

Unlike Vautour Bleu, who had witnessed the commissioner's greed and arrogance, those who remained at the camp still held onto their fantasies. They encouraged one another, counting the DisCoins just issued like precious gems.

speaker: Alfie
content: I'll just start with a book then... The books in DisCity must be nice and cheap! Maybe I can even buy one, and when I'm done reading it, I'll buy a next one...
Soft murmurs wove dreams of a better life in DisCity. But soon, they shattered beneath the sudden boom of gunfire.

speaker: Jake
content: What's that? Someone fired a gun?! ...It's from DisCity!

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Stay calm! Everyone stay calm! It's not aimed at us!

speaker: Jake
content: But DisCity... Isn't it supposed to be a safe zone? Do they have wars here too?
The question floored Vautour Bleu. Her knowledge of DisCity proved just as limited. Not until now, as she heard the gunfire, did she grasp the true meaning behind the commissioner's cryptic warning.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: No, it's not a war. Just a shootout between gangs. It'll be over soon. DisCity's FAC isn't to be trifled with. Everything will quiet down quickly. By the time we enter the city tomorrow, things will be good.
She desperately shielded their fragile dreams with hollow words of comfort, yet in their eyes, she saw it—the dreams already fell apart.
Now welcomed into DisCity as the FAC's "honored guest," Vautour Bleu notices how Syndicate has changed from total chaos like a decade ago.
Though traces of war can still be seen in the rebuilt district, it has at least become a place where people can lead normal lives.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Heh... You know what, when I first came here ten years ago, this place was overrun with gangs and guns.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Several of my companions were lured away by them and disappeared ever since. Others tried sneaking to Eastside along the Rust, but of course they got arrested.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Then there were those who were so disappointed by DisCity trying to return home, only to find their homeland already destroyed.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Yet I... I can't do nothing then. I couldn't stop any of it, couldn't save anyone.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: <size=26>...The DisCity dream. Heh, what's the good of living here?</size>

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: Of course you wouldn't understand. People like you can't even imagine how many Hypercubes we've spent in mopping up Syndicate. West District would be even better if fewer opportunists with no sense of morals like you are slippin' in.
The FAC soldier's cold remarks faze Vautour Bleu not. She lets out an amused sigh, her expression showing nothing but casual indifference tinged with nostalgia, without a trace of shame.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Hypercubes, you say... Yeah, some can ride down the road, while others must risk their lives just to sneak through the mud. Some even drown in that... And that's not even a shortcut, that's just the only path left.
Her thoughts drift to the man who fled from their caravan. He must have collapsed right on DisCity's border. The DisCity dream may be no good, but he couldn't even afford the luxury of bethinking it.
Yet why does she still offer him a chance to dream? Even after Désir crumbled, even after the DisCity dream was proven false once again.
In a daze, Vautour Bleu glimpses a familiar silhouette through the vehicle's window. The figure that once appeared among datura flowers, behind the sheer curtains, and in sandy air.

speaker: Chief
content: We meet again, Miss Vautour Bleu.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Good afternoon, my dear Chief. This is my first time being a guest... at your MBCC.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: This interrogation room feels rather empty. Did you not receive the art pieces I sent you? You should put some here, to add a touch of artistic charm to the space.
The woman before you lounges in the interrogation chair as if it were a plush sofa, teasing you with a smile. She behaves just like a casual visitor she claims to be.

speaker: Chief
content: I see. If you like it, next time you visit, I'll have them placed here. All of them, I promise.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Next time, heh... Quite optimistic, aren't you? Already hoping for our next meeting when we're not even done with this one.

speaker: Chief
content: A little hope won't kill you. You must've been hoping for something too when you sent those packages to me, am I right?

speaker: Chief
content: So I'd say being optimistic drives us both forward, isn't it?

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Driving forward? Haha... That's rather a punch line, little Chief.
She laughs, responding to your words with appreciation and humor, but her next words are not what you expected.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Very well, I'll say yes to our next meeting. Though I'm afraid I won't be able to send you so many souvenirs next time.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Those lovely bloodhounds you've sent my way will certainly put a damper on my business. Having the cops sniffing around isn't good for one's reputation in WhiteSands, you know.

speaker: Chief
content: Surely the marvelous Vautour Bleu revered by the whole WhiteSands won't be fazed by that, I guess? After all, judging by the variety of gifts you've sent, your business does stretch far and wide.

speaker: Chief
content: I imagine you have connections even in the most obscure small towns we've barely heard about? For example, the hometown of one of our recent guests.

speaker: Chief
content: I hear they're struggling with resources there and need Hypercubes to fight off disasters. You're their lifeline. Surely this little setback won't affect your business with them.
Vautour Bleu appears completely oblivious to your implied meaning, merely shaking her head slowly with a tinge of reproach and forgiveness in her eyes.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: These business connections you speak of... are as strong as they are fragile. Never mind pressure from a big player like DisCity, even a slight increase in the price or one missing shipment...

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: And they'll crumble in the blink of an eye. That's why for merchants like us sailing in WhiteSands, the most valuable trait is knowing how to play safe and not to go too far.

speaker: Chief
content: Oh? Then, if a merchant is willing to risk double the trouble with the FAC to pass along the message, that must be some seriously important info to her, correct?
You lock eyes with her, pushing for one last time by playing along with her. But she looks the other way again.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Perhaps? But unfortunately, I lost that kind of courage to take risks long ago. I might have sold it off cheaply, right along with any hope you spoke of.
She sounds cooperative, but she's misinterpreting and digressing every question, deliberately avoiding the topic that you both know lies at the heart of this conversation.
Her continued evasion only strengthens your certainty that you're on the right track. Time to bring everything into the light.

speaker: Chief
content: Is that so? But I'd say, I think you're never short of courage or hope.

speaker: Chief
content: I doubt anyone else would go to such lengths to tip me off about Lyman and act all casual about it like you did.

speaker: Chief
content: Without this letter, you wouldn't be facing accusations of disrupting Outland relations, and your business would certainly remain unaffected.

speaker: Chief
content: ...Or are you still going to insist that I'm reading too much into this?

You take out the letter and slide it toward her. Though you've been handling it carefully, time has washed away its warm fragrance, leaving only the cold ink on it, frigid like the air in the interrogation room.
She responds with only a brief silence before casually averting her gaze, letting her eyes drift lazily across your face.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Maybe. After all, I'm just a humble merchant who happens to know a bit too much about DisCity. I was worried the guy who escaped from my caravan might cause trouble here, so I filed a report just in case. Just trying to leave a good impression, Chief.

speaker: Chief
content: Very well then, Vautour Bleu the humble hawker, in that case, please stay in character and answer a few questions from this lowly chief.

speaker: Chief
content: Since you're so well-versed in DisCity's capabilities, you must know that Lyman's identity as an Outland soldier is sensitive, even though he's a deserter. You must have been aware of the potential danger.

speaker: Chief
content: Yet you still informed me about him in your letter. I don't suppose your business has gone so bad that you're planning to spend winter in the MBCC?

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Why not? At least here I won't wake up with my mouth half-filled with sand.
Vautour Bleu laughs at your words. She remains perfectly composed... even starting to look around the room.

speaker: Chief
content: Because the Vautour Bleu I know is a woman of action. She spearheaded the establishment of Désir, planted the datura flowers, and even in the final moments, she was still devising plans to save the townspeople.

speaker: Chief
content: If she were the type to bow to circumstance and give up the fight, she'd never have saved Primrose and the others. She wouldn't have taken them in to begin with.

speaker: Chief
content: On the contrary, she always believes there's still a chance to make things right, especially when it comes to her companions.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: ...Sounds impressive this lady. But what does any of this have to do with Lyman and our current topic?
Vautour Bleu mulls over your words, a slight smile playing on her lips. She shifts in her seat, as if settling in to hear your further analysis.

speaker: Chief
content: Lyman is a deserter from Outlands and a temporary member of your caravan. But above all, he's an illegal immigrant. Everything he's done has been for one goal: to get into DisCity and live a better life.

speaker: Chief
content: When I saw his background, I thought if Désir were still there, you would have taken him in without hesitation. And even with Désir gone, you'd still see him as one of your own.

speaker: Chief
content: That's why you tipped me off about Lyman beforehand. You knew better than anyone that even if he managed to reach DisCity's border alive, someone with his sensitive background would never manage to get in.

speaker: Chief
content: You wanted me to save him before the Border Bureau could find and deport him. That was your real purpose. Just like... that deal we made back in Désir.

The vivid memory conjured by these words seems to bring back the ethereal scent of datura. This elusive fragrance, as intangible as the woman before you, had deceived yet also protected everyone there.

speaker: Chief
content: You may be a ruthless merchant and leader, but you cherish every life in your care. I don't think it's all just about profit. You truly feel responsible for them.

speaker: Chief
content: You just... want to keep everyone safe in this eternal present, where their dreams are neither fulfilled nor broken.

speaker: Chief
content: You'd rather have them run endlessly like hamsters in a wheel than face the cruel reality of their shattered dreams.
A brief silence falls. You did hope these words would move Vautour Bleu, or at the very least create an opening you could exploit further.
But she remains perfectly at ease, the curve of her smile unchanged.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Hmm...? How interesting. The MBCC's Chief isn't here to condemn someone, but to plead their case instead.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: If that's what you want to believe, I won't object. Since you've decided I'm such a good person, shall we end our little chat here?

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Time is money for a merchant, you know. My caravan has been idle for days while I'm cooperating with this investigation. Who knows if my crew has already run my business into the ground by now?
She says and makes to get up and leave. You can see your best chance at uncovering her true motives slipping away, yet you stay put and just watch her calmly.

speaker: Chief
content: Answer one last question before you go.

speaker: Chief
content: Why me?

You've always known Vautour Bleu carries a secret. It's the reason why even though she genuinely cared about everyone in Désir, she kept a distance from them and never let anyone close, always solitary and evasive.
Neither vague possibilities nor concrete examples can make her open up now. You decide to give it one last try. This time, you're putting yourself in the bet.

speaker: Chief
content: You have plenty of connections in DisCity who would be willing to help if you only asked. Why did you seek me out and send those hints to me? What did you see in me?
Vautour Bleu stills for a moment. Her gaze returns to you, studying every nuance of your expression with an almost tactile scrutiny.
Then, perhaps sensing your earnestness and knowing she can no longer hide from your questions, she gives a wry smile. For the first time, her expression grows placid and candid.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: What did I see in you... Perhaps, as you said, it's possibility and future. A different future.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: You're a revolutionary, a savior, and Syndicate's hero. You're different from the others. You care about everyone's lives, and you care about their dreams.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Since our last farewell, I've often wondered... If I had met you earlier, could those dreams I dismissed unavail have had a different ending?

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Maybe you would have noticed the signs earlier and stepped in sooner... Those who had gone missing might have come back...

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Maybe you could have convinced them not to value the cargo over their own lives, stopped them from chasing rumors to their doom...
She lowers her gaze, her voice almost a whisper. Though you don't know who these people are, you hold back the question and simply listen. You understand that this is exactly what she needs.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: And then there's the people of Désir. You might have brought the doctors and helped Sheila get better. You would have stood up for Primrose and saved her from her worthless foster parents...

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Such a shame... Daydreams are only beautiful because they can never come true. I couldn't save them... and you were never there to make their dreams happen.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: Those marked for death would have died anyway, died chasing those fantasies, died at the doorstep of their dreams... It was true back then, and it remains true today.
...It remains true today? So that's what this is about.
Her words suddenly reveal the fundamental misunderstanding between you. You calmly raise your hand to interrupt Vautour Bleu who is deeply immersed in her emotions.

speaker: Chief
content: Wait, I think there's been some misunderstanding between us. From what you're saying... you think Lyman is already dead?

speaker: Chief
content: In fact...
You turn on your comms device in front of Vautour Bleu and play a clip from the surveillance footage.
In the footage, Lyman is wearing a clean, loose shirt, his hair and beard neatly trimmed, with bandages wrapped around his head.
He sits in a circle with around fifteen others of varying ages, while someone who appears to be a teacher stands in the center, giving a lecture.

speaker: Night School Teacher
content: Alright, while the official history dates Syndicate's founding to the establishment of Eastside, Syndicate actually existed for an even shorter time. Lyman, can you tell us when Syndicate was truly established?

speaker: Lyman
content: ...Huh?

speaker: Classmate
content: <size=26>Page 322, A5...</size>

speaker: Night School Teacher
content: Nice try, Lyman. I wish Syndicate had existed back then too, but at that time, we didn't even have DisCity yet.
The whole class breaks into good-natured laughter.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: He's... still alive.
Unlike his once-haunted look in the caravan, Lyman appears shy yet relaxed on screen. This warm, harmonious atmosphere matches exactly what others once described to her...

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: And... he's smiling.

speaker: Chief
content: Yes, he's still alive, and he's not just smiling. He's learning and stepping closer to his future.

speaker: Chief
content: You see? Perhaps the ending isn't always as tragic as you think. Maybe there's still hope. Even if we can't change the past, there might still be a future we can shape.
She gazes at the screen transfixed, as if peeking into another timeline where things could have been different.

speaker: Madeleine
content: Hmm... Mom, what do you think of this house? It has a big garden where we could plant your favorite flowers and trees. The air would be fresh, and we could pick fruit together then.

speaker: Edna
content: Good taste! Then at your word, my little lady!

speaker: Biber
content: Oh, nice, so this is DisCity. Not quite as big as I imagined it would be! Haha!

speaker: Madeleine
content: Biber, stop shouting on the street. People are staring.
On the bustling street, she hears someone calling her name from behind.

speaker: Old Hugh
content: Miss Madeleine, wait, wait for me!

speaker: Landon
content: Miss Madeleine—!
She turns around to see her old servants all rushing toward her.
It's a season of brilliant sunshine and blooming flowers, a time when birdsong fills the air and everything feels like a fresh start.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: ...Haha.
The woman smiles. And for once, it's nothing like her usual calculated expressions. This smile is genuine and beaming, her blue eyes bright and clear like they've just been rinsed with fresh water.

speaker: Vautour Bleu
content: What a relief. I thought he was shot dead by the DisCity Border Guard.

speaker: Chief
