<color=#dg1f1f>For our friend, companion, and leader, ${PlayerName}.</color>

speaker: Andrew
content: What are you doing here?

speaker: Albert
content: What do you mean? Of course I must be here for this very important day.

speaker: Albert
content: Everyone in the clinic is here. We're all happy for Eve.
People gather next to the surveillance window outside the rehabilitation room, talking in hushed tones.

speaker: Nurse
content: Good. Yes, just take it slow. First, try to support your body with the strength of your arms...

speaker: Eve
content: Mmm...
Eve strains to hold onto the rehabilitation equipment, slowly removing herself from the wheelchair.

speaker: Benna
content: All right. Then I wish that in this life, Eve can leave the factory, and live a long, happy and peaceful life.

speaker: Bass
content: You're not wishing for Shanna? Benna forgot again!

speaker: Benna
content: How could I forget? The one who chatted with me... the one who I watched grow up... is Eve.

speaker: Bass
content: Bass hope Eve can make new friends! Friends smarter than Bass, so Eve won't be troubled! If Eve is happy, Bass is happy!

speaker: Eve
content: It hurts... where the prosthetic pulls...
Eve grits her teeth, her face already pale.

speaker: Nurse
content: It's a good sign you're feeling it. Keep going, Eve.

speaker: Andrew & Albert
content: You can do it, Eve...

speaker: Polly
content: I wish that in my next life, I'll meet Eve again! By then, we will be complete, healthy and well.

speaker: Maresa
content: Bone still remembers its promise with Eve.

speaker: Maresa
content: He wishes that he can go for a walk with Eve... and be Eve's puppy again.

speaker: Polly
content: Go for a walk... That sounds nice. It'd be great if we could all go together.

speaker: Eve
content: We said we'd... all go for a walk together...
Eve is already drenched in sweat, but she has only moved a finger's distance away from the wheelchair.

speaker: Nurse
content: Just a little more, Eve. You can do it... Just a bit more!

speaker: Andrew
content: How's it going? Has she stood up?

speaker: Albert
content: Do you think it's that easy? Eve's nerves have been dormant for years. It's already a miracle that she can feel anything!

speaker: Andrew
content: Then what are we waiting for here?

speaker: Albert
content: Tsk, can't you just shut it for a minute.

speaker: Albert
content: Of course, we are waiting for a miracle!
Eve.
Their wish is for you to experience tomorrow outside the factory.
It's a tomorrow that belongs to you, and one that you'll witness on their behalf.
Because of you, this family without blood ties exists.
If you move forward, the family members in your memory will also move forward.
You are their hope and continuity for the future.
Let's go. I'll take you away from here.

speaker: Eve
content: Tomorrow... I still have many, many tomorrows...

speaker: Nurse
content: Ah! Eve...
It's only for a brief moment, yet everyone sees it. Eve leaves the wheelchair.
Although she quickly falls back into the wheelchair, for that one moment, the entire clinic held their breath for her.

speaker: Eve
content: Did... did I do it?
Bass and Benna have said it, you're the smartest. I believe you will find your motivation.
Once you do, you'll be able to stand up and walk out of the factory, enduring the pain.

speaker: Eve
content: Stand up...
Go and make the lies come true. Create a better world with the accumulated tomorrows.
This is my motivation. What's yours, Eve?

speaker: Eve
content: Walk out...
Tell me your answer when I come back.
No matter what your answer is, this time, I will support you.

speaker: Nurse
content: Eve, why are you crying? Did you get hurt just now?

speaker: Eve
content: No, I'm fine...

speaker: Eve
content: I did it. I found my motivation...

speaker: Eve
content: Those beautiful lies... One after another, they motivated me and all those who couldn't protect themselves. I see a new tomorrow now...

speaker: Eve
content: But Polly and the others... they can't see it...
Just the act of getting up has drained all of Eve's energy. She clutches the notebook in her wheelchair.

speaker: Eve
content: ${PlayerName}, you'll come back, right?

speaker: Nurse
content: Eve, are you sure you want to leave the clinic?

speaker: Eve
content: Yes, I'm a Sinner of the MBCC. I can only meet the person I'm waiting for over there.

speaker: Nurse
content: If that's your decision, sure. Be careful! It's not particularly safe out there. Take care.
Eve nods with a smile. The doll in her hand swells up to an enormous thing to fend off some contamination for the nurse.

speaker: Nurse
content: ...Well, it seems like I'm the one who needs to be more careful.

speaker: Nurse
content: Besides waiting for that person, what else are you going to do when you're back?

speaker: Eve
content: Of course, there's still a lot I want to do...

speaker: Eve
content: I'll continue my rehabilitation in the Bureau.

speaker: Eve
content: Then, I want to see if I can help with the mechanical maintenance there.
The sky over Syndicate is all gray. Eve lifts her head, trying to find a hint of blue.
As she's gazing at the sky, lively noises come from not far away.

speaker: Childish Voice
content: Give me back my plane! I found it!

speaker: Childish Voice
content: Nah, nah, nah, I won't give it back!

speaker: Nurse
content: It's the group of kids we recently took in... They're causing a ruckus again.

speaker: Nurse
content: Right, I heard one of those boys got separated from his mother at the border of the Rust and Eastside when he was a child.

speaker: Nurse
content: Could he be the child of the Maresa you mentioned before?

speaker: Eve
content: How old is he?!

speaker: Nurse
content: He looks around twelve or thirteen. Do you want to meet him?

speaker: Eve
content: ...No. He'll be fine staying here with you guys.

speaker: Eve
content: They've moved on, so I should too.
Clutching her small diary, Eve heads in the direction of the MBCC with her toys.

speaker: Eve
content: I'm sure you'll come back. I still have so many things to tell you.

speaker: Eve
content: You listened to my story at the factory, but I haven't had the chance to get to know you yet.

speaker: Eve
content: They've told me a lot of things, all about your past as a hero.

speaker: Eve
content: But I also want to hear the story of the gray cloth doll when you were just an ordinary person.

speaker: Eve
content: The next time we meet, please tell me.

speaker: Eve
content: Your lies and your ideals...

speaker: Councilor
content: I've heard that during the recent operation against the Sun Crow Apostle, you collaborated closely with the Eastian delegation.

speaker: Councilor
content: Then this shouldn't pose a problem for you, I presume.
Early in the morning, a councilor visits the Bureau office, placing a stack of documents on your desk.

speaker: Chief
content: It's been a week since the battle with the Apostle. Everything is back to normal, and the delegation has already returned to Eastia.

speaker: Chief
content: Why bring up these old matters now?

speaker: Councilor
content: It's true the delegation has returned, but aren't you aware?

speaker: Councilor
content: One of them has turned back.
The councilor opens the folder, revealing the title page with the sharp font: <color=#fb9259>Du Ruo's Visa Application</color>.

options: Du Ruo is back in DisCity?
I'm not aware. When did this happen?

speaker: Councilor
content: You better not be playing dumb. After infiltrating DisCity's military operations, the Outland state is now sending an envoy here again under the guise of an academic visit... I shouldn't need to spell out the conflict of interest in this situation.

speaker: Chief
content: ...You suspect she has an ulterior motive?

speaker: Councilor
content: At the very least, we can't rule out the possibility that she is a spy. The discord between states can't be so easily mended, but we also can't break the superficial peace so soon after the Apostle operation. So, we can only ask you a favor.

speaker: Councilor
content: This is at Ambassador Du Ruo's own request. She's willing to undergo an assessment by the MBCC, and if she fails your evaluation, she agrees to be expelled.
The councilor leaves the documents behind and specifies the time to escort the ambassador to the Bureau for an entry assessment.
Before leaving, the councilor pats you on the shoulder.

speaker: Councilor
content: You have the authority to approve her application, but you should be well aware of the outcome DisCity desires.

speaker: Councilor
content: Find a diplomatic excuse to send her back to Eastia. DisCity entrusts this task to you.

The interrogation room is kept at an apt temperature. Inside, the returning scholar is already seated and waiting. No handcuffs have been put on her, and the M-value detectors used against Sinners have been turned off.
At least on the surface, DisCity has shown considerable courtesy to this foreign dignitary.
Noticing someone entering, Du Ruo looks up, her eyes meeting yours.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: They say reunions are rarer than farewells. But here we are, reunited so soon.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: I hope you're well, Chief. How have you been recovering from the Sun Crow's backfiring against the shackles?
She speaks placidly as if it's the most ordinary small talk.

speaker: Chief
content: I feel normal, and so do the shackles. Thank you for traveling all the way to inquire about my health.
You say emphatically, testing her attitude.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Is that so? Glad to hear it.
She doesn't lead the conversation to a new topic as you expected, simply nodding in relief. The interrogation room falls into awkward silence once more.
Du Ruo doesn't seem uncomfortable with the unusual silence. Her gaze lingers on your face before leisurely moving to the visa application in your hands. She smiles.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Is that a reunion gift you're holding?

speaker: Chief
content: I think you know better than I do what this is.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Oh, you're throwing the question back at me. You've gotten more cunning in just a week, Chief. Looks like I'll have to come up with more sophisticated lies in the future.

options: Is the academic visit a lie too?

speaker: Chief
content: The crisis has been averted, why return to DisCity? Why didn't you contact me before coming back?

speaker: Chief
content: From the moment the delegation first set foot in DisCity, all of you have been on the 9th Agency's watchlist. You knew this from the start, yet you still chose to take the risk alone.

speaker: Chief
content: Why did you specifically request me to conduct your entry assessment?
She doesn't answer and just leans forward slightly, observing you closely.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Chief, are you anxious? Or are you angry?

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Even in the face of the Sun Crow Apostle, you've never shown such emotions. What's different now?
She leans in a bit closer.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Are you upset because I didn't tell you before coming back? Or, are you... worried about me?

options: You're overthinking. I'm just doing my job.

speaker: Chief
content: You should know full well that DisCity will not let you in its border again.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: That's why I'm not seeking DisCity's opinion. I specifically volunteered for an evaluation by the MBCC's Chief, ${PlayerName}.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: ...Didn't you want me to come back?
She seems eager for your response, but you can't tell if she's jesting or being sincere, so you steer the conversation back to the visa application.

speaker: Chief
content: This isn't about what I want personally. No one would have approved this flimsy application.
test
test
test

test

My account of DisCity's epic victory against the Sun Crow to the Eastian audience has been met with great enthusiasm. Interest in DisCity's culture is surging in my homeland.

Following the recent breakthrough in my Eastian mythology studies, I am seeking a chance for an academic visit to deepen my knowledge of DisCity's mythology and broaden the scope of my work.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Yes, I kept the handwriting elegant and the tone tactful. What could be the problem?

speaker: Chief
content: Of course, there's a problem...

speaker: Chief
content: It's only been a few days since the delegation left DisCity. Even the fastest transport couldn't have taken you through WhiteSands back to Eastia with your Sun Crow myth and then doubled back to DisCity.

speaker: Chief
content: Having fought alongside you for so long, I can tell you're the biggest non-believer among the delegation of these so-called myths. You even actively disproved and debunked the legends many times.

speaker: Chief
content: What you want to collect isn't just DisCity's myths.

speaker: Chief
content: DisCity was only established after Nightfall. As an emerging immigrant state, it doesn't have a rich history or culture like Eastia.

speaker: Chief
content: Here, you can only study the declining mine factories, new urban technologies, and...

speaker: Chief
content: Black Rings, Mania, Hypercubes.
These are the core of DisCity's secrets, and this is the conclusion you least want to reach. At the mention of these terms, the atmosphere in the interrogation room drops to freezing point.
She has listened to your scrutiny of her application. When you voice your suspicions about espionage, she finally opens her eyes.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: I remember you liked listening to my stories. Would you like to hear one now, for old times' sake?

speaker: Chief
content: You haven't responded to my question yet.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: The answer is in the story.

speaker: Chief
content: A myth?

speaker: Du Ruo
content: A true story.
She takes out an Eastian-style incense burner.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: The story is a bit long. Do you mind if I light some incense? It helps clear my thoughts.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Don't worry, it's just ordinary incense. I promise not to mix in anything weird.
Amid the rising plumes of smoke, she begins.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Since the beginning of my memory, my parents had already sent me to the academy.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: The Eastian continent has a long-standing civilization that even Nightfall never interrupted. In our education system, the teachers enlighten us by retelling all kinds of mythological stories. The myth of the Sun Crow myth is one of them.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: But after hearing the myth of the Sun Crow from my teacher for the first time, I was skeptical. Why would people worship something that brought nothing but disasters to humanity?

speaker: Du Ruo
content: The teacher didn't answer my question. He simply said, "Just remember what's written in the textbook."
Du Ruo chuckles softly, shaking her head a little wryly.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: It'll probably surprise you. I wasn't exactly a model student in my childhood. The more the teacher said that, the more I refused to accept it.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: I dismissed the myth as superstition and tried to prove that the Sun Crow was not a god, but just a Wraith Beast. Then, starting with a series of skeptical viewpoints, I began my research as a mythologist.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Over the years of research, I read some books and also made some friends.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Some friends, like me, did not believe in myths, but they sacrificed their lives to protect those ignorant beliefs.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Some friends would choose the greater good over personal beliefs in a heartbeat, and dedicate decades of anonymous effort to it.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: And some friends... You've already met them.

options: The seer inside the Sun Crow?

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Yes, it was Xu and the others who saved Sunset Town from the ten-sun calamity. They showed me that even after reading all these books, what I was seeking was just the shallowest part of the myths.
She speaks with rare candor.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: It turned out that miracles really did exist. They were created by my late friends... by people.
You've never seen Du Ruo get so serious before. She's fighting to suppress her emotions, but you can still easily sense the fluctuations of Mania in the air.
This was clearly not an easy past for her. She takes some time to adjust her breathing.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: You call me a non-believer, and that's true. I only believe in the truth built by humans with their blood and sweat.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: But you're wrong about DisCity not having its own myths.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: For those who have witnessed devastation, the construction of such a prosperous city under the disasters is a myth in itself.
The room quiets down, and the incense in the burner just happens to burn out. But Du Ruo's new interpretation of mythology still lingers in the interrogation room like the scent of the smoke.
Perhaps it's only at this moment that you truly understand her identity as a mythologist.

options: Did you really come for the DisCity myth?

speaker: Du Ruo
content: If you don't believe me, why not join me on my academic visit?

speaker: Du Ruo
content: It just so happens I need a guide to show me around DisCity and to help me understand the local customs. How do the people here view the disasters they've overcome and their current lives? And how do they live with the potential threat of Mania?

speaker: Chief
content: Are these also part of the myth?

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Of course. Just like the idea that mere mortals can shoot down the sun with their faith, to Eastia which lacks the protection of Hypercubes, these seemingly mundane daily experiences are as dreamy as a legend or a hope...

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Will you join me in writing this DisCity myth? I'm sure you're a highly anticipated character in this story.

speaker: Chief
content: ...Do your fellow townspeople like this sort of thing?

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Sure. I, for one, do. Give me a chance to write you into this story. Will you indulge me just for once?
She resumes her usual teasing demeanor, tapping lightly on the visa approval with her index finger.

speaker: Councilor
content: You have the authority to approve her application, but you should be well aware of the outcome DisCity desires.

speaker: Councilor
content: Find a diplomatic excuse to send her back to Eastia. DisCity entrusts this task to you.
Despite your so-called right of approval, in reality, you can only choose between an unconditional expulsion and the burden of full responsibility.

speaker: Chief
content: The aim of this academic visit can only be a cultural exchange, as you've clarified. Anything related to the city's secrets is off-limits, and you must stay away from all the sensitive areas listed in the application...

speaker: Chief
content: These are the only rights the MBCC can secure for you.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: So, I've passed your entry assessment?

speaker: Chief
content: Although you're a habitual liar, I'm still willing to bet on your passion for mythology. Besides, I'll accompany you throughout the academic visit to keep an eye on you.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Aren't you afraid of upsetting those big shots?

speaker: Chief
content: You don't need to worry about that. The MBCC will draft a special entry agreement for you. Just follow the rules and focus on writing your myth.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Hmm, bossy. You know, you're pretty charismatic, even as someone from DisCity. Don't forget you still owe me an answer, Chief. Can you tell me now?

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Chief, did you... want me to come back?
She lowers her voice, staring at you with a foxy grin.

speaker: Chief
content: Then you also owe me an answer. You couldn't have doubled back from Eastia to DisCity in just a few days. Why lie in the visa application?

speaker: Du Ruo
content: I see...
She hesitates for a moment. You seem to catch a fleeting hint of disappointment on her face.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Then let's consider us even on this matter.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: See you on the streets of DisCity, fellow traveler.
It's nighttime in Eastside. Towering skyscrapers stretch endlessly into the depths of the streets.

Colorful advertisements play non-stop on the glass curtain walls, featuring TV show trailers, movie promotions, and the pop songs in rotation. The area is filled with a constant hum of the crowd which stimulates the eardrums together with the loud music.
Du Ruo stands in the middle of the street, tilting her head back to take in everything. It takes her three full minutes before she lowers her head to ask you a question.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Chief, is there an event happening here?

speaker: Chief
content: There's no event. This is just how this place always is, considering it's one of the busiest streets in Eastside.
Hearing this, Du Ruo looks up to scan her surroundings again, taking her time before she's willing to move on. Seeing her barely concealed excitement, you feel somewhat relieved.

Half an hour ago
Outside the MBCC
The vehicle escorting you and Du Ruo for your academic visit to Eastside has arrived, but it's surrounded by a group of unfamiliar guards.

speaker: Policeman
content: Chief, Miss Ambassador, please wear this when you go out.
He hands you and Du Ruo a small earpiece, through which you hear the councilor's not-so-friendly voice.

speaker: Councilor
content: Chief ${PlayerName}, it seems you've made a rather significant decision on your own.
This is clearly about your approval of Du Ruo's entry.

speaker: Chief
content: The MBCC has submitted Du Ruo's entry agreement. It specifies her range of activities and forbids her from visiting any sensitive area.

speaker: Councilor
content: Yes, we have received it. But the council wants to supplement it with some necessary measures.

speaker: Councilor
content: All of your subsequent actions will be monitored by the council and the 9th Agency. We hope you will cooperate if there are any instructions.

speaker: Councilor
content: Should there be any violation, we might take the envoy back to the City Council with force for a reassessment of her entry permit.

speaker: Chief
content: Force? This is a senior official from Eastia. What are you planning?

speaker: Councilor
content: Whatever it is that we're planning to do, you would take full responsibility, wouldn't you, Chief?

speaker: Chief
content: You...
Just as you are about to argue further, Du Ruo suddenly grabs you.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: I see. I will do as you ask. I also appreciate this opportunity you've given to me to understand your culture.
You see she has obediently put on the earpiece and doesn't seem offended, so you can only follow suit and comply with the council's arrangement.

The earpiece feels somewhat uncomfortable in your ear. Half a step ahead of you, Du Ruo is strolling and looking around leisurely. You were worried these regulations would ruin her mood for the tour, but it seems you were overthinking.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Were all these buildings constructed on desert ruins?
She looks at a tall building beside the road. The trailer of a recent comedy movie is playing on its glass facade.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: I've heard that to withstand disasters, most buildings in Eastside use a shear wall structure?

speaker: Chief
content: I'm not too familiar with these details, but I can ask someone at the Bureau for you when we get back.

speaker: Chief
content: Yes, I've heard it can counteract quicksand during construction.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: I see... Standing here today, it's like a monument to human wisdom and effort.
Du Ruo seems to be attracted by something else and continues forward. You follow her gaze to a shop not far away that sells small building-shaped pendants with the word Eastside engraved on them.
You're just about to comment on the questionable design of these souvenirs when you hear Du Ruo say...

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Chief, I want to take some of these back to Eastia.

speaker: Chief
content: ...I finally know who's buying these things.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Oh, don't look so embarrassed by your own city's souvenirs. You remind me of that saying: One who dwells among orchids does not know the fragrance.
You have a feeling that's not a compliment. But before you can ask her, a jarring electric noise explodes in your ear.

speaker: Policeman
content: Warning. Shopping on the roadside is not allowed. Please immediately return to the main street.
You turn to Du Ruo, but she immediately complies with the instruction and moves back to the middle of the street.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: I also happen to want to check out other places.

She doesn't seem discouraged by the warning, continuing to walk at an unhurried pace. Soon, she stops in front of a 4D advertising screen as wide as two buildings which was once heavily promoted by the developer as a selling point.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: I've read about this technology in books. Seeing it with my own eyes now, I wonder... did Zhou dream of becoming the butterfly? Or did it dream of becoming him?

speaker: Chief
content: Is this an ancient saying from Eastia?

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Yes. It means it's hard to distinguish between dreams and reality. Just like how I'm standing right in front of this screen, yet I'm uncertain if what I see is real.

speaker: Chief
content: That sounds a little exaggerated.

speaker: Chief
content: From a technical standpoint, DisCity is indeed at the forefront of the world.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: I've also heard that you can construct swimming pools in the desert, and make highly immersive theatres and museums.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: These things that only exist in books... are actually realized here... DisCity truly is a miracle amid disasters. If only there were more miracles like it.
Her expression as she surveys the surroundings is one of envy and amazement, from which you can somehow also read a sigh for other hardships in the world.
Just then, a passerby holding a selfie stick squeezes in between you.
Your outfit... You must be from the Outlands, right?
I thought so when I passed by just now! Hey, I'm doing a live stream. Mind saying hi to my family?

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Live stream? I've heard of it. It's one of DisCity's representative cultures.
Du Ruo raises her hand experimentally.

speaker: Streamer
content: Exactly! You gotta try live streaming when in Eastside. Come on, look at the camera with me...
Du Ruo taps on the various buttons on the live stream interface curiously. A variety of funny filters with flowers, kittens, and puppies appear on her face.
You watch her with amusement. Suddenly, Du Ruo turns around and grabs you, pulling you into the frame.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Chief, join us.
Zzzt! Another warning pierces through the earpiece, the jarring sound of electricity making your head spin. Du Ruo also stops in her tracks.

speaker: Policeman
content: The envoy is to immediately cease interaction with the residents of DisCity. I repeat, the envoy must cease interaction with the residents of DisCity at once.

speaker: Policeman
content: This is the second warning. If a third warning occurs, we will take forcible measures and escort Ambassador Du Ruo back.

speaker: Streamer
content: Hey, why are you guys so quiet suddenly?
You and Du Ruo say nothing but simply nod apologetically to the passerby and silently retreat to the main street. The person abandons you, grumbling in confusion.
Du Ruo becomes somewhat silent. She's still observing everything around her with curiosity, occasionally striking up a conversation with you, but no longer deviating from the set path.
At this rate, even if you stroll down this street ten times from end to end, it might still not be satisfying.

speaker: Chief
content: Wandering casually like this won't do for your academic visit, will it?

speaker: Du Ruo
content: I thought I'd have the chance to chat with the people of DisCity on the street, but it seems like a pipe dream now... Nonetheless, being able to witness all this is already a great gain.
She doesn't want to make things difficult for you. But the more she's like this, the more it reminds you of the things she said and makes you feel even more indignant for her.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: You call me a non-believer, and that's true. I only believe in the truth built by humans with their blood and sweat.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: For those who have witnessed devastation, the construction of such a prosperous city under the disasters is a myth in itself.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Of course. Just like the idea that mere mortals can shoot down the sun with their faith, to Eastia which lacks the protection of Hypercubes, these seemingly mundane daily experiences are as dreamy as a legend or a hope...

speaker: Chief
content: Du Ruo, wait for me under that billboard.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: What, have you prepared a surprise for our date?

options: Yes, I want to give you a hand.

speaker: Chief
content: Take off your earpiece first. I'll be right back.

speaker: Councilor
content: Chief ${PlayerName}, do you know what you're doing?
You've only walked a few steps away when a reproach immediately comes through the earpiece.

speaker: Chief
content: Of course. I'm testing her credibility for you.
The councilor clearly didn't expect such a reply, and before he can continue to object, you quickly defend yourself.

speaker: Chief
content: I haven't gone far away, and her actions have been within a controllable range. Instead of being so on edge all the time, why don't we deliberately lower our guard?

speaker: Chief
content: If she indeed takes the bait and does something against DisCity's interest, we'll have a legitimate reason to detain her.

speaker: Chief
content: If she acts normally, we can play along and support the enthusiasm of a visiting scholar from Eastia.

speaker: Councilor
content: ...What's your plan?

speaker: Chief
content: You guys pretend to drop all defenses, but secretly guard all exits in the area. I'll take her to visit the surroundings of an insignificant Black Ring ruin, but we won't get close.

speaker: Chief
content: If she attacks me or shows any inclination to approach the Black Ring ruin during our time alone, you can immediately take your forcible measures.
Even you don't completely buy your plan, but fortunately, you know very well how to muster a firm tone and just fake it till you make it. After a long silence, the councilor finally responds.

speaker: Councilor
content: ...Considering your loyalty to DisCity all this time, we agree to your proposal.

You breathe a sigh of relief and turn back to see that Du Ruo is still waiting at the same spot. To your surprise, the usually resourceful and strategic scholar seems somewhat awkward and uncertain amid the hustle and bustle.
You've never fully let down your guard around her so far. For you, this is also the moment of truth.
You manage to bring Du Ruo to an abandoned high-rise in Syndicate.

The old street lamp at the base of the building flickers on and off, struggling to light up. The staircase is covered in large patches of rust. Accompanied by creaking noise, you and Du Ruo ascend to the rooftop.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Chief, what is this place?

speaker: Chief
content: Look far to the right.

Moonlight shines over a vast stretch of dark rooftops of the uninhabited area. In the distant sky, lights start to come on one after another. At the end of the lights, the Statue of Keylan stands tall.
Du Ruo is somewhat dazed.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: I never thought I'd be able to see Keylan Square with my own eyes...

speaker: Chief
content: With all your talks about the miracles of DisCity, I thought this might be one of the places on your bucket list.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Of course, the story of Keylan has inspired so many... After all, in the face of disasters, human power is so insignificant. It wasn't until Keylan that countless scholars began to believe that the laws of the supernatural could also be conquered.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: He isn't just a beacon for DisCity. Even in the other states, he is a sacred and legendary figure...
Overlooking Syndicate's night view, Du Ruo's voice dwindles, almost as if she's whispering a sigh of admiration.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: ...It's a pity that I have to leave soon and won't get to see the fully restored statue.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Next time, I'd like to bring a tea table and a good teapot. We'll each have a cup, watching the moon and Keylan over the tea till the sun rises.

speaker: Chief
content: Must we wait until next time? It might be even harder for you to gain entry next time...

options: Why don't you stay if DisCity pleases you so much?

speaker: Chief
content: Remember that question I haven't answered? Whether I want you to come back to DisCity. You have my answer now.
A trace of surprise flashes across Du Ruo's face, but it quickly disappears into a smirk and a pensive look.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Oh my, Chief, are you trying to abduct me? No way, I still have to go back.
She sighs exaggeratedly, gazing toward Eastia.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: The Sun Crow calamity took a severe toll on all of Eastia, especially my hometown, Sunset Town. I promised Xu and those friends who sacrificed themselves in the disaster that I would pass on the myths and faiths for them, even though they were all lies.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: People have defied the impossible to rebuild a city on the ruins of Sunset Town and named it Sunsink City. They are in dire need of individuals with strong spiritual power now. I can't just abandon my hometown when it needs me the most. I can't just part with my past promises.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: That's what we Eastians are... A bunch of fools. Home is both the origin and the end.

speaker: Chief
content: I guess this is the end of the academic visit, then. It's time to say goodbye again. Who knows when we'll meet next.
The topic has somehow drifted from the romantic ideals back to the discouraging reality. She lowers her head, moving imperceptibly closer in your direction.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: In that case, why don't I abduct you back to Eastia?

speaker: Du Ruo
content: There's no Statue of Keylan or neon-lit skyscrapers, but Goldionville's lion dance and Sunsink City's tea ceremony are worth checking out.

speaker: Chief
content: Your hometown needs you, and mine needs me too. There's plenty of trouble to deal with at the Bureau.
You try to play along with her joke, but when you look back at Du Ruo, you realize... she might not have been joking just now.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Can't you come with me? Can you really call DisCity... your hometown?

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Do they really need you, or just your shackles?
Severity, earnestness, anxiety... You capture these rare emotions on Du Ruo's face.

speaker: Chief
content: Where did that come from all of a sudden?

speaker: Du Ruo
content: It's not exactly sudden. I've noticed for quite some time. ${PlayerName}, the people of DisCity trust you no more than they trust Eastia.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Though you bear the title of Chief, you actually have little power. You only got roped into the battle against the Sun Crow or my entry approval and had no say in anything. All this hometown you keep talking about wants is just...
She grabs your wrist and activates her power. She's not attacking you. On the contrary, the shackles within you seem to be summoned, mobilized, and connected to something.

speaker: Chief
content: What are you doing...

speaker: Du Ruo
content: I'm looking for the answer in your heart. Is such a hometown really worth it?
The shackles sense the approach of powerful Mania and start to pulsate uneasily.

speaker: Chief
content: Du Ruo, stop. Once the shackles and the Sinner are connected, it can't be undone.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: I can stop, but first, answer me.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: I consider Eastia my home because I was born and raised there. It's a place that has given me beautiful memories, a safe haven that gives me a sense of belonging.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: But does DisCity offer you unconditional shelter? Does it feel like a mother to you, too?
It may not be intentional, but Du Ruo's words hurt. You don't know where you were born and raised. You have no past, no place to call your safe haven.

speaker: Chief
content: ...No comment.
You try to pull your wrist away, but her grip only grows tighter.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Is it because even you can't justify why DisCity is your hometown?

speaker: Du Ruo
content: During the battle with the Sun Crow, even in the presence of the Outlanders, they were unwilling to trust you fully. If I'm not wrong, your situation during the previous Black Ring operations was even worse.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: What has DisCity done to you? Surely, they must have gone further than using your shackles?

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Has your so-called hometown threatened you, or even deceived you...

speaker: Chief
content: That's none of your business.

speaker: Chief
content: According to our entry agreement, you're not supposed to get involved with any information related to the Black Rings or Mania.

speaker: Chief
content: Du Ruo, you've broken the agreement.
Under her questioning, you've slipped up and revealed an emotional weakness. In that moment when you both waver, the shackles connect successfully. A red spike of light forms between you and Du Ruo.
She looks at you through the spike, her expression weary.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Sorry, I shouldn't have probed in such a manner. It must have been hard for you.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Keylan Square is enough material for the DisCity myth. The academic visit has been fruitful. Thank you... I'm a bit tired. Let's go back.
On the ride back, you both remain silent. The earpiece carries the councilor's voice, congratulating the Eastian ambassador on an eventful visit to DisCity.
Your time alone didn't result in the anticipated escape or injury. Instead, you shackled an Outland Sinner, which is a pleasant surprise for the council. But neither you nor Du Ruo are listening.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: I'll be returning to Eastia in three days.
This is the last thing you hear from her at the end of her academic visit.
The next day
Nightingale knocks urgently on your office door, handing you an emergency report from the council:
Database access has been hacked by an unknown sorcery.
Seeing the adjutant's hesitant look, you immediately have a bad feeling.

speaker: Chief
content: Where's Du Ruo?

speaker: Nightingale
content: Surveillance cameras showed that Du Ruo never left her room since returning from her academic visit. We only just discovered...

speaker: Nightingale
content: She's gone.

speaker: Chief
content: How much time do we have left?

speaker: FAC
content: Based on our estimates of Eastian vehicles, suspect Du Ruo could enter another state's territory in six hours.

speaker: FAC
content: If we can't catch up, we'll just have to wait for the higher-ups to issue a formal query.
You follow the FAC squad deep into the heart of WhiteSands. The sensation from the shackles becomes progressively clearer.

speaker: Chief
content: It won't come to that. Six hours is enough.
You point the squad in a rough direction and the ship speeds ahead.
Looking out through the observation window, the vast WhiteSands stretches endlessly. You can only rely on the thermal radar to search for nearby life forms.

speaker: FAC
content: Look, there's something here!
The helmsman shouts in surprise, and you look over.
On the radar, a new red dot is approaching step by step toward you, until a blurry figure also appears outside the observation window.

speaker: FAC
content: This is...
Before you can ascertain the situation, the sand under the ship starts churning.

speaker: FAC
content: Quicksand?!
At this moment, your shackles give you a definite response. The shadow in front of you is not the Sinner you're sensing.
The small range of quicksand expands rapidly, drawing the sand in a hundred-meter radius toward your location like a vortex.
The wind whips up sand and stones. The severe turbulence causes malfunctions in the cabin. Lighting and instruments fail one after another while alarms blare inside the cramped cabin.

speaker: FAC
content: Leave the cabin, quick! Get out! Or you'll be buried by the sand...
Before the soldier can finish his sentence, the sandstorm already crashes into the cabin. You suddenly find yourself in complete darkness.
The suffocating sensation brought by the quicksand knocks you out.
You don't know how much time has passed when you finally regain consciousness.
In a daze, you realize you're lying on something hard.
A slight ache in your shoulder blades makes you turn to the side, and at the same time, you smell a familiar fragrance in the air.

The bright light is blinding, forcing you to squint. Surrounding you are the canvas of a crude tent. Against the light, you see another figure inside the tent. She's sitting beside a weathered rock stump, resting her head on her hand while fiddling with a compass.
Hearing the noise from your side, she turns her head, still wearing that same roguish smile you saw on her face when you first met.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Calling my name even when you blacked out. Do you miss me that much?

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Yeah, I was just walking home when suddenly I heard a huge noise behind me. I turned around and saw... haha... a huge ship sunken into WhiteSands. And just like that, I found you there.

options: Could you make up something more believable?

speaker: Du Ruo
content: So, what do you want to hear? I can go along with anything. Say, I set up a trap and waited for you to jump in?
Du Ruo smiles enigmatically, leaving you somewhat puzzled.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: What do you mean by this? Be more specific.

speaker: Chief
content: Everything. Hacking the database, leaving DisCity early, saying those things to me next to Keylan Square. And also...

speaker: Chief
content: Coming back to DisCity after defeating the Apostle. Was it really just for the DisCity myth?
You struggle to sit up from the stone bed. Your palm feels a sting as it supports you on the edge of the bed. You probably injured it from falling on the ship, but you can't worry about that now.

speaker: Chief
content: Now is not the time for jokes. If you don't return to DisCity, diplomatic tensions may rise between DisCity and Sunsink City or even the whole Eastia.

speaker: Chief
content: The FAC is versed in quicksand combat. They will soon be able to locate us. You will be taken away.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: And what if I don't let them find us?
She deliberately starts toying with the compass by her side.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: I know DisCity is technologically advanced, and I've always been curious if your technology really does have the upper hand against Eastia's mystic arts.

speaker: Chief
content: What is that?

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Something that allows those soldiers to discover our coordinates but not us. Although I only know the basics, it's enough to cause a little trouble for your ship.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Come back to Eastia with me, Chief. You don't have to worry about any diplomatic crises. WhiteSands is ever so perilous. Let's just pretend you and I both went missing during the chase. Neither DisCity nor Eastia would have enough reason to confront each other.
She doesn't shy away from her plans at all now. Instead, she approaches you calmly to treat your wounds.
But as she comes closer, you instinctively move away.

speaker: Chief
content: You haven't answered me. Are you really here to steal DisCity's secrets?
Those hands poised to heal you hang in mid-air.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: So you still don't trust me.

speaker: Chief
content: Not only do I trust you, but when the council doubted the purpose of your visit, I fought for you for a chance to prove yourself. But my trust alone can't explain your unusual betrayal.

speaker: Chief
content: From the initial visa application to the betrayal now, I no longer know when to trust you.

speaker: Chief
content: You took me here and made DisCity believe I'm dead, and then? Are you going to take me to Eastia just like you said that day next to Keylan Square? And after that, what do you plan to do? Force me to spill the truth about the Black Rings?
Listening to your questions, her smile grows increasingly cold.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Don't trouble yourself to tell me about the Black Rings. I saw everything after hacking the database.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: I saw everything about BR-002, BR-001, and BR-004. Saw how you were deceived, tested, used, and even abandoned.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: But in the end, you still doubt me for the city that did all that to you.
Du Ruo smiles bitterly and takes a deep breath, her lips forming a tight line.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: The reason why I came back, why I went on that visit with you and got shackled, why I hacked the database, why I left early to set up this complicated trap in WhiteSands... You really...

speaker: Du Ruo
content: You really don't know?

speaker: Chief
content: You should know full well that DisCity will not let you in its border again.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: That's why I'm not seeking DisCity's opinion. I specifically volunteered for an evaluation by the MBCC's Chief, ${PlayerName}.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: ...Didn't you want me to come back?

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Will you join me in writing this DisCity myth? I'm sure you're a highly anticipated character in this story.

speaker: Chief
content: ...Do your fellow townspeople like this sort of thing?

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Sure. I, for one, do. Give me a chance to write you into this story. Will you indulge me just for once?

speaker: Du Ruo
content: ...It's a pity that I have to leave soon and won't get to see the fully restored statue.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Next time, I'd like to bring a tea table and a good teapot. We'll each have a cup, watching the moon and Keylan over the tea till the sun rises.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: In that case, why don't I abduct you back to Eastia?

speaker: Du Ruo
content: There's no Statue of Keylan or neon-lit skyscrapers, but Goldionville's lion dance and Sunsink City's tea ceremony are worth checking out.

speaker: Chief
content: Huh? So all of this was for...

speaker: Du Ruo
content: I wish you could have seen through my intentions as easily as you did those inconsequential lies.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Then I wouldn't have had to personally verify your situation in the database.

speaker: Chief
content: The hacking of the database, that was for me too?
You feel somewhat incredulous. The situation is a mess, and your wrist throbs with dull pain. Your silence prompts Du Ruo to come closer.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Let me check the wound on your wrist first.
She sits beside you, takes out a small bottle of ointment, and dips her fingertip in it, her motions as gentle as her tone.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Come with me to Eastia, Chief.

The sandstorm continues, the wind constantly hitting the shelter's canvas. Some time has passed since Eastia's recent espionage against DisCity, and the prime suspect is sitting right in front of you, the concern in her eyes genuine.
Just as you're unsure how to begin...
Suddenly, you feel a familiar throbbing in your palm.
You can clearly sense that the throbbing isn't just from one set of shackles, and it comes from a distance... You're certain this sensation isn't from Du Ruo.

speaker: EMP
content: C-H-I-E-F!!!

speaker: Hecate
content: Shhh. There's nothing here either... Could something really have happened?

speaker: Hella
content: Hey, don't just poke around aimlessly. It's easy to get lost in WhiteSands! ****, Nightmare, keep an eye on them!

speaker: Ignis
content: Giving us all this trouble again... If he dares end up in any accident, I, I won't forgive him easily.
female_content: Giving us all this trouble again... If she dares end up in any accident, I, I won't forgive her easily.

speaker: Kelvin
content: Nothing will happen to Chief. Maybe it's just a loss of signal? I believe in Chief, and I believe we'll find Chief.

speaker: Nightingale
content: The location should be around here. The device is working normally.

speaker: FAC
content: Good, I'll send people to continue the search.
The scalding heat of the shackles and the coolness of Du Ruo's medicinal herbs intermingle to give an unexpected calming effect.

speaker: Chief
content: Du Ruo, can I ask you a question?
The question comes abruptly. She looks up in surprise.

speaker: Chief
content: Say your birthplace couldn't provide you with shelter or leave you with any fond memories, and you met friends like Xu whom you fought and grew together elsewhere. In this case, where would you consider your hometown?

speaker: Chief
content: Or let me put it another way. When both places needed you, how would you choose?
She pauses the moment the answer is about to slip out.

speaker: Chief
content: Maybe you misunderstood why I did what I did for DisCity.

speaker: Chief
content: Just as a myth may not be about gods, a hometown means more than just the name of a place.

speaker: Chief
content: What really lies behind that... You were the one who taught me this.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: ...It's the reality built by people.
Du Ruo understands at last. She applies the last bit of ointment on you and stands up to pick up the compass.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: It seems you've made your choice.

speaker: Chief
content: Like I've said, there's plenty of trouble to deal with at the Bureau. I need to go back.

speaker: Chief
content: Wherever they are, I will be there.

options: I want to stay in DisCity.

content: You and Du Ruo lock eyes, neither of you looking away. After a long while, Du Ruo sighs deeply.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: I don't agree with your choice.
She raises her hand to the compass, her fingertips moving the pointer.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: But I respect a friend's judgment.
The compass starts spinning rapidly. After dozens of turns, it comes to a complete stop. The faint glow on the disc fades away.
At the same moment, the shelter's invisible barrier is shattered by the Nightmare. The FAC soldiers and the MBCC guards arrive together.
The Sinners also rush toward you, standing before you protectively, responding to the call of the shackles.
The FAC soldiers raise their guns and encircle Du Ruo. Her gaze sweeps over the rows of gun barrels, calm as usual.
Before the soldiers act, she speaks first.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Thanks to Chief's selfless rescue, I was able to escape from the sandstorm.

speaker: FAC
content: No one asked about that. Do you have nothing to say about the hacking of the database?

speaker: Du Ruo
content: I came all this way in pursuit of the Eastian traitor who stole the data. So the FAC hasn't caught it either?
The FAC soldiers are somewhat confused by her diversion. Indifferent to their reaction, Du Ruo smiles, her gaze traveling through the crowd to you.

options: Go along with her final lie

speaker: Chief
content: I can vouch for Du Ruo. WhiteSands is fraught with danger...

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Come back to Eastia with me, Chief. You don't have to worry about any diplomatic crises. WhiteSands is ever so perilous. Let's just pretend you and I both went missing during the chase. Neither DisCity nor Eastia would have enough reason to confront each other.

speaker: Chief
content: The traitor who hacked the database went missing during the chase.

speaker: Chief
content: Tomorrow?
On the other end of the phone, the councilor's tone is jubilant.

speaker: Councilor
content: Yes, she leaves tomorrow. The departure documents for Ambassador Du Ruo will be delivered to the MBCC later today. After she leaves the Bureau, please vet her residence to ensure the Outlander doesn't leave behind any traps.

speaker: Chief
content: She just returned from WhiteSands yesterday. Isn't this arrangement too hasty?

speaker: Councilor
content: Her stay in DisCity was supposed to be a temporary one. Moreover, we've demonstrated enough generosity by letting her return to Eastia without holding her accountable for the hacking of the database.

speaker: Councilor
content: Trust me, Chief, there's no need for further discussion. Before making the decision, we consulted Ambassador Du Ruo herself, and she had no objections.
When you come to verify this with Du Ruo, she's bending over to light incense. Baggage scatters around the room and an open suitcase lies half-packed on the floor.

options: Have you decided to leave tomorrow?

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Yes. Will you miss me?

speaker: Du Ruo
content: After this departure, we probably won't meet again in a long time.
This room in the Bureau has particularly good lighting. It's because she said upon arrival that Eastians needed to bask in the sun every day to gather spiritual energy.
Du Ruo stands in the light. Smoke gathers around her occasionally and quickly dissipates again.

speaker: Chief
content: I will make some arrangements so you can come to DisCity anytime.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Thank you, Chief.
Shrouded by lingering smoke, the room falls silent for a moment.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Can I take something from here as a keepsake? I couldn't get that pendant from Eastside that you disliked.
You look around and find nothing you can give her.
She shakes her head.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: I want this.
Du Ruo opens the window, pointing at a branch outside.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: In old Eastian, breaking a willow branch is symbolic of a reluctant farewell. Could you break off a branch for me?

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Just a small one is fine.
You do as told. Du Ruo takes the branch cherishingly.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Thank you... Seeing this branch, I'll remember the experiences we shared in DisCity. It'll make the long journey home less tedious.

speaker: Chief
content: Are you sure you don't want to stay for a few more days?

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Why would you want me to stay?
The branch turns in Du Ruo's hands for a while before going still.
The sun rises higher. Du Ruo stands quietly in the room.
Tomorrow, the sun will still shine into the room, but the person living here will be thousands of miles away.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Chief?
She presses you for an answer deliberately.
Before you can speak, someone knocks on the door.

speaker: MBCC Staff
content: Is this Du Ruo's room?

speaker: MBCC Staff
content: These are your departure documents. Please keep them safe.
The MBCC staff member hands over the envelope to Du Ruo briskly and excuses himself.
Seeing your awkward and embarrassed expression, Du Ruo laughs and sighs, then continues to empty the room.
Dust floats in the air. Passing items to each other, you and Du Ruo begin packing up the luggage wordlessly.
Books, clothes, travel documents.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Will you give me a hand like this again in the future?

speaker: Chief
content: That depends on whether you're thinking of crossing DisCity's line again.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: What counts as crossing the line?
Leaning in suddenly, her voice is so soft it's almost a whisper.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: What if I want to learn more about Mania?

speaker: Chief
content: I can answer your questions as long as they're within the permitted range.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: What if I simply want to chat with you?

speaker: Chief
content: I'll pick up your call.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: What if... I can't make it to DisCity anymore?

options: I'll go to Eastia to see you.
The councilors would probably be happy.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: You know, you're weird. Is it really necessary that we meet?

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Are you implying that you won't be happy?
This time, she doesn't wait for your reply and simply retreats to a safe distance contentedly.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Alright, no more teasing.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Before our next meeting, I'll remember today, and how much you don't want me to go.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: As a mythologist, once all of this dies down, I will certainly make frequent visits to DisCity. I will also come to see you, if that's what you want.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: So, go make those arrangements for me, Chief. In exchange, I'll leave this with you.
She takes out an Eastian-style thread-bound book with no title on the cover.

speaker: Chief
content: What is this?

speaker: Du Ruo
content: My myth book.
She opens it to the first page and hands it to you.
A nation stood, bearing the name of Dis. The atrocity of the god begot the rampage of calamities. One with no fear stepped forth.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: There once existed a state named Dis, which suffered frequent disasters from the god's wrath. Then, a courageous person stood out.
Wronged and affronted, harmed and maltreated. A foreign one came with a deserter's plan. The hero refused, sworn to slay the god.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Misunderstood and defamed, this person endured endless hardships and unfair treatment. An Outlander tried to take this person away, yet the hero chose to stay and kept fighting the disasters.
A fine line of writing lies at the bottom. The ink looks the darkest. It appears to be a fresh remark.

speaker: Chief
content: So, what about this sentence? What does it mean?
Once again, she smiles slyly.

speaker: Du Ruo
content: Take your time to guess, Chief. We Eastians are very subtle.
"Only now do I realize one cannot quell the mountains and seas."
The MBCC command room remains brightly lit deep in the night. The message that woke you from your sleep thirty minutes ago glares on the large screen on the wall.
JXU0RjYwJXUyMDI2JXUyMDI2JXU4MEZEJXU2NTM2JXU1MjMwJXUyMDI2JXUyMDI2JXU1NDE3JTBBJXU2NTUxJXUyMDI2JXUyMDI2JXU2NTUxJXU2MjExJXUyMDI2JXUyMDI2JTBBTEw=
The rapid tapping of keyboards by the network technicians weaves an impenetrable web, casting a heavy shadow over the hearts of everyone present.
You stand quietly to the side with your arms crossed, your fingers tapping rapidly in anxiety.
So, has the message been deciphered?
You finally can't help but ask.

speaker: Technician A
content: Please wait, almost done...
The technician's eyes remain glued to the screen in front of him, his hands never stopping. A few seconds later, the deciphered message is projected onto the large screen.
Can you... see... this... help... help me... L.L...
This is... a distress signal?!
Lore-Ley.
This name immediately springs to your mind—the instigator of the Elysiland incident who was found and taken away by the Underground.

Since returning empty-handed from Lore-Ley's residence, you've continued your search for her and the Underground. You devised many tracking plans and strategies, but the Underground is vigilant like always, leaving no breakthroughs.
Just when you were getting nowhere, you receive this distress signal from Lore-Ley.
Another technician's voice rings out at the same time.

speaker: Technician B
content: Chief! We've pinpointed the location of this message to an abandoned building on the outskirts of the city. The exact coordinates have been sent to your terminal.
OK.
You throw on your coat and quickly head out.
Special Task Force Unit One, come with me immediately!
The team's fragmented footsteps echo alongside the eerie dripping sounds and electrical buzz in the pitch-black ruins.
Tracing the source of the sounds, you come to and push open a tattered, half-closed door. When you shine your flashlight into the darkness, you can't help but gasp at the scene before your eyes...

Lore-Ley lies limp in a puddle of dark, dirty water on the floor, her head hanging weakly. Her tangled hair is plastered across her face, soaked to the point where you can no longer tell its color. Yet she still tightly clutches a cable pulled from the corner of the wall.
At the edge of the puddle, a severed wire hangs from the ceiling, still sparking with electricity from its broken end.
Perhaps noticing your footsteps, or perhaps sensing the light, she musters her last bit of strength to grab the corner of your coat.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: I feel... awful... Chie...
You sit at your desk with a furrowed brow, rereading Lore-Ley's detailed examination report. These few sheets of paper have weighed heavily on your mind like a boulder these past days.
When you found Lore-Ley in the abandoned building a few days ago, you immediately used your shackles to temporarily stabilize her condition, then rushed her to the MBCC for treatment.
Although her life is not in danger, the examination revealed that she is suffering from an extremely rare type of congenital hydrophilia...
This rare condition causes her muscles to weaken, and her skin cannot be exposed to air for long. She must stay immersed in water.
Now, with the aid of your shackles, she can leave the water temporarily to walk around, but must keep her skin humid. After consulting medical staff, you learn this condition cannot be totally cured.
However, these are not the only matters troubling you.
Accustomed to Lore-Ley's erratic and bold persona in the virtual world, you're surprised to find that she is completely different in real life.
Finally attaining freedom though, she somehow avoids meeting with people.

She almost never appears in the Recreation Area or Outdoor Activity Area, and always finds excuses to avoid group training and Sinner social events. If someone comes to sit with her in the cafeteria, she immediately picks up her tray and leaves, bewildering both the other Sinner and cafeteria staff.

During hypnosis and psychological therapy, Lore-Ley hinders her treatment by refusing to speak to the hypnotist and psychiatrist. Only when communicating via computer or comms does the situation slightly improve.
Continuing like this is not an option. For the sake of her treatment and future, you decide to talk to her face-to-face.
You ponder for a moment, then open the chat window on your comms device and send Lore-Ley a message.
<color=#fb9259>${PlayerName}</color>: How's your recovery? How are you feeling these days?
The moment you send out the message, your comms device pings with a reply.

<color=#fb9259>L.L.</color>: Great! I can move around and try a lot of exciting things now! 
<color=#fb9259>L.L.</color>: Thank you for saving me. 
<color=#fb9259>${PlayerName}</color>: You're welcome. 
<color=#fb9259>${PlayerName}</color>: By the way, are you free this afternoon? Can we have a talk face-to-face?
This time, she doesn't reply as quickly. Half a minute later, a short reply appears.
<color=#fb9259>L.L.</color>: Sure.
When you enter the interrogation room, Lore-Ley has already been waiting for a while. Under the watch of two unfamiliar staff members, she keeps her head lowered in wary silence.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: ...Hello, hello! There you are!
Only after you tell the staff members to leave does she finally relax a bit. She lets out a big sigh of relief and greets you warmly.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Is there something important you needed to discuss with me face-to-face?
Since she asked so directly, you skip the pleasantries and cut to the chase:
I hope you can assist us in wrapping up the recent events.
A hint of confusion gleams in her eyes.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Me...? Are you asking for my help?
Yes.
The Elysiland incident involves the Underground, but we have limited information. However, you've had direct contact with them.
I was just worried that experience might be a traumatic memory for you, so I wanted to wait until you feel better before asking for your help.
Upon hearing that she could be of help, she becomes thrilled, nodding vigorously at you.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Absolutely! Just let me know what you want.
After returning from Elysiland, I got your address and went to your place right away.
But unfortunately, you were taken away by the Underground before I could reach you.
What exactly did they want you to do, and why did they use dark web technology to help you hatch up the Elysiland?
Hearing the word "Underground," Lore-Ley purses her lips, her face ashen.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: What other reason could there be? They noticed my power and wanted me to spread Mania for them on the dark web.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: I didn't think too much at the time. I thought nothing mattered as long as I could create a utopian "Elysiland."

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: To them, the bigger the Mania explosion in Elysiland, the better. They want exactly what you don't want.
You squint your eyes, recalling how Lore-Ley almost wanted both you and her to go down with the island.
Lore-Ley nods, looking indifferent.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Yeah, I turned them down.
Why?
Lore-Ley mimics you and squints back at you with interest.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: What do you think?

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: If it were the old me, I probably would have agreed, but now...
Lore-Ley picks up a small cup of water and pours it on herself.
The water drips from her clothes and forms a small puddle around her feet.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: I think now... I'm more interested in the real world.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: I also want to see with my own eyes what this so-called real world truly looks like. What is it that makes people willingly give up the happiness, excitement, and perfection of the virtual world to return here?

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: ...But that doesn't mean I've given up on the online world.
Lore-Ley extends her hand to you. You smile and shake it, showing that you remember your past agreement.
So, is this the reason they "abandoned" you?

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Yeah, that's right.
But your power should be very important to them, right?
Lore-Ley strokes her chin.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: They think I won't be interested in the real world for long. They say that based on my personality, I'll soon return to the dark web... to them.

options: Do you want to go back?

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Right now, of course not. You haven't taken me to experience those happy things you mentioned yet.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: But after that... it's hard to say.
Lore-Ley lifts her chin up, flashing her signature smile.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: So, make sure to do your best!
It's about time to take you out for a trip, but...
Hearing your words, Lore-Ley sits up a bit awkwardly.
This morning, I heard someone say she wanted to chat with you, but you ran off after just a few words. She's worried she might have offended you somehow.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: It's not like that! I...
Lore-Ley tries to refute but can't find the words, her face flushing under your gaze. You don't badger her, and patiently wait for her to gather her thoughts.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: I haven't interacted with the real world for a long time. All my communication was done online, so I don't know how to do it.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Sometimes, even though I've thought about what to say, as soon as I look up and see the other person's eyes, my mind goes blank.
Lore-Ley gestures to you, trying to explain her self.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Mmm... it's a bit like what I saw online before, where if you don't write for a long time, you get "writer's block"?

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Do you get what I mean?
Lore-Ley lowers her head, sighing in frustration.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: There are many interesting people in your Bureau. I'd really like to become friends with them in real life. But in my current state... it's hard to avoid misunderstandings...
This is the first time you see Lore-Ley so dejected.
No rush.
Integration and adaptation take time. Just start trying little by little, and I'll help you.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Hmm...
She mutters a muffled response but continues to look down. You ponder for a moment.
You mentioned in your message that you can "move around and try a lot of exciting things now," right?

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Yes, why?
Tomorrow's a day off. How about we hang out to see the real DisCity together? Wouldn't that be exciting?

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Huh? That's what you mean little-by-little?
Well, I thought the Elysiland owner might prefer a more thrilling approach, don't you?
The weekend weather is splendid, with the clear skies carrying not a wisp of cloud. Even the gentle breeze is adorned with the faint scent of newly bloomed flowers.
Noon is the busiest time of the day, and the streets teem with bustling crowds. Despite having to regularly soothe herself with water, Lore-Ley doesn't want to miss any of the views before her.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: I read online before that the human eye has a higher resolution than any camera, and it's true! Look at the foliage under the sunlight! Such a beautiful green! Online pics can't compare to the real thing at all!
At first, she trailed behind you timidly, but now she's running around like an excited critter bursting with curiosity for everything around her.
She skips along under the shade of the trees, where light specks fall through the canopy and sparkle on her feet with each step.
Even a trivial thing like this is enough to make her happy for quite a while.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Hmm... If feels a bit suffocating to walk under those tall buildings. This isn't what they call "megalophobia," is it?

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Look! The birds are standing in a row on the wire... Ah, they all flew away.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: A leaf has fallen off the branch over there! I can definitely catch it before it hits the ground!
She would suddenly stop and inhale the floral scent in the air, then eagerly share with you the subtle differences between the flowers on this street and the last.
She would also crouch by the greenery to touch the soil, buds, and cement pavement on the other side, then carefully compare their differences.
She sniffs her soil-stained fingers and reflects to herself.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: It feels slick and cool, but it smells like this? It's different from what I imagined...
Hearing her mumbling to herself, you squat down beside her and rub some soil with your fingertips.
If it were a rainy day, the smell would change again.
Your childish actions draw curious glances from onlookers, but you don't mind. You listen to her intently and respond accordingly.
Immersed in her own world, Lore-Ley is talking a lot more. After years of being confined in a tub, things that are ordinary to most people are a brand new experience for her.

This might be the first time in her life she can truly step into, observe, and explore this vast world. You want her to experience as much as possible during this meaningful opportunity, and not let any of her expectations fall short.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Change again? To what? I often saw people online say they like the "smell of soil after the rain," but what kind of smell is that exactly?
Hmm... I guess it's a moist smell?

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: What does "moist" smell like? Is it the same as the smell of wet clothes?
She continues to ask, but this question stumps you. You're not sure how to answer, so you awkwardly scratch your head.
Uh... It's hard to explain in words. How about we wait for a rainy day and then come out to smell it together?

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Sure, I'll remember that!!
She nods vigorously, her smile bright and vivid. She summons her cute little manta ray and solemnly jots down the promise between you and her.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: ...Huh? Could that be...!
Attracted by something else, Lore-Ley gasps and dashes across the street by herself, quickly disappearing into the bustling crowd.
Wait...
You venture into the crowd after her, looking around until you finally see that tuft of light blue hair by the window of a pet store.

As you approach, you see Lore-Ley gazing intently at a puppy behind the window. She glides her finger against the glass, and the white furball chases her finger back and forth, wagging its tail happily.
Looks like it really likes you.
Hearing your words, she flashes a bashful smile.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: I've watched a lot of cat and dog videos online, but I've never seen them in real life. They seem even livelier and cuter than in the videos.
Want to take a look? Maybe you can even pet them if the staff allows.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: ...Really!?
Her eyes light up as she looks at you, brimming with joy and anticipation. You smile and nod.
Of course.
The pet store owner kindly agrees to your request. After cleaning your hands and clothes as requested, you're allowed into the activity area.
In a sunlit corner of the activity area, you sit quietly and observe the girl play happily with the puppy.
The puppy energetically barks and jumps, eagerly fetching the ball again and again. Lore-Ley can't help but laugh when the puppy licks her fingers.
After a while, the puppy gets tired and falls asleep on Lore-Ley's lap. Lore-Ley strokes the puppy's white fur, murmuring to herself.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: So this is what touching an animal feels like. Warm, dry, fluffy, and very soft... so different from my skin, which is always cold and slippery from the water.
You watch her quietly look at her lap, not knowing what she's pondering about. So you decide to ask.
What are you thinking about?

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Ada also had a puppy like this one.
Ada?
Lore-Ley snaps back to her senses, as if realizing what she just said. She stops petting the puppy for a moment, but the puppy whines and she continues.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Ada... was a friend I met online a long time ago.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: I met her through a game. Her username was "Ada - Top Future Designer of the Universe." We were on the same team several times. Her skills were on par with mine, so we became familiar with each other over time.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Gradually, we started to talk more, and discussed things beyond gaming. She shared her life and the things happening around her with me.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Like what she had for dinner, the weird trees and clouds she saw in the street, the stress of graduating, her favorite stars and cartoons, and her dream of becoming a top designer...
Lore-Ley's lips curl into a faint smile. For her, those memories are as soft and cute as the puppy resting on her lap.
She seems to be a brave, honest and interesting person to have written her dream in her username like that for everyone to see.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Yeah. Ada was straightforward, confident, and generous.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: No matter what kind of injustice or discomfort she encountered, she would boldly express her feelings and then bravely resist.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Once, she told me she had a big fight with her parents because they were too controlling. They meddled in everything, and she had no personal space.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: I told her that my parents don't really interact with me that much now, and I kind of envy her for having that kind of attention.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: She seemed unable to understand my point of view. It was the first time I mentioned my health condition to her...

The moisture on Lore-Ley's body has gradually dried up. She wants to pour the water in her bottle on herself, but is unwilling to leave the critters in the activity area, so she just takes a sip of water instead.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: She apologized, saying that she didn't realize what situation I was in. Then she sent me a picture of the puppy she just adopted.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: She told me the puppy was named Cabbage, and had just turned one year old. He had a heart condition, but was well cared for and took his medicine regularly.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Cabbage was very bubbly and knew how to cheer people up. Everyone who met him liked him.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Ada said she would send me videos of her playing with Cabbage every day. Seeing their joy made me happy, too. She said if I ever felt lonely, they would be my friends.
What happened after?
Lore-Ley flashes a bitter smile and shakes her head.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Nothing. I lost contact with her a long time ago.
The puppy that resembles the one in Lore-Ley's memory senses her melancholy. It opens its eyes and goes forward to lick her cheek.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Our last chat was probably in the summer five or six years ago. I still remember the last message she sent me. She said she was going on a family trip and would send me photos when she got back.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: But after that, her avatar never lit up again. I never saw Cabbage again.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: But isn't that how online friends are? You connect randomly and hit it off quickly, but as time passes, or as your shared interest fades, the connection naturally breaks.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: After all, a "friendship" built on an internet cable can't be that strong.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: But I do miss those times. I felt like I had a faraway friend. Sometimes when I reminisce, I wonder how she is now, and whether she realized her dream of becoming a designer...
You purse your lips.
Why not try contacting her again?

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: What...?
Lore-Ley looks at you, somewhat surprised.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Are you saying...
In your current state, finding Ada's contact info shouldn't be hard, right?
You make a typing gesture, but she seems a bit startled by your suggestion and hesitantly waves her hands.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Th-that might not be a good idea... Isn't it a bit too sudden...
What if she wants to know how you're doing too, but just hasn't found the chance or courage to take the initiative?
You don't want to live in regret forever, do you? Don't you want to change things?
Lore-Ley bites her lip and falls silent for a while before speaking softly.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: I know her. If she wanted to do something, she'd definitely do it right away...

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Maybe we just weren't fated to be...
But that's just your guess, right? You still have to ask her directly to get a definite answer, don't you?
Just like how you got a definite answer from the guests before bringing them to the bottom of the sea.
Lore-Ley pouts at you, deep in thought. Having no intention of letting her back out, you continue to push her.
Whether one wants to create, maintain, or keep a connection, one side must bravely take the first step.
After an intense internal struggle, Lore-Ley finally nods as if she's made up her mind.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Then... I'll give it a try. I can... find her social media account and make a call.
She takes a comms device out of her pocket, activates her power, and quickly finds Ada's number from the vast sea of information on the internet. With trembling fingers, she presses the dial button.
Beep—Beep—
Her heart beats intensely to every ring, and the sweat of her palm almost makes her drop the device.

speaker: Ada
content: ...Hello?

The call finally connects. Seeing Lore-Ley's panicked expression, you know she must have recognized the voice. But the background on the other side is very noisy, full of boisterous clamor and clanging.

speaker: Ada
content: Who is it? Hello?
The voice on the other end grows impatient, and Lore-Ley, flustered, casts a pleading look at you.
