You gently squeeze her little finger and make a "relax" gesture to Lore-Ley. Under your encouraging gaze, she gradually calms down, takes a deep breath, and bravely speaks.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Hello, is this Ada?

speaker: Ada
content: Yes. Who is this?

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Um... I'm L.L., do you remember me?
Ada clicks her tongue, her voice full of wariness and irritation.

speaker: Ada
content: I don't know anyone named L.L., and I'm not interested in buying anything. Go bother someone else...

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Wait, wait! I'm not selling anything! We met online in a game a long time ago. My gamertag was L.L.! We used to chat every day! You showed your puppy and said we could all be friends!

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: We haven't been in touch for a long time... I just wanted to know, are you... doing okay?
Lore-Ley pours out everything she wants to say in one breath. Her shoulders rise and fall intensely, as if she's used up all her strength.
The other side listens to Lore-Ley and falls silent for a moment.

speaker: Ada
content: I don't know why you're calling me. We're not friends, and whether I'm okay or not has nothing to do with you. Don't call again.
There's a noticeable change in her attitude. She seems to recall Lore-Ley but hangs up quickly as if avoiding something.
Beep, beep, beep...
Lore-Ley stares at the coldly beeping comms device, somewhat at a loss.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: ...I knew this is how it would end.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Online friends are just online friends, after all. Without ever meeting offline, it's wishful thinking to be real friends...
As she wallows in the pain and disappointment of rejection, you carefully recall the brief call, troubled by the noise in the background.
How noisy the background was when you called her? It sounded like people were arguing.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: It did sound a bit noisy... I also heard a loud clang. Not sure what it was.
Was something getting smashed?
Lore-Ley's expression changes a bit.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Did something happen on her end? Could she be in danger? Is that why she didn't answer me directly?!
It's possible...
Lore-Ley, can you locate her based on that phone call just now?

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Yeah.
She nods and closes her eyes as she holds the device. Countless data flashes before her eyes.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Found it! She's very close! It's a neighborhood about two kilometers from here!
Okay, let's head over there.
I've already agreed to send him away! What more do you want!?
I'm going right now! Happy?
A shrill voice echoes from the hallway. You quickly pull Lore-Ley behind the bushes of a small flower bed.

The next second, a young woman emerges from the hallway. She angrily hangs up the call and rams the device into her pocket. In her other hand, she is carrying a pet carrier and a large, bulging canvas bag.
When Lore-Ley sees the young woman's face, she lets out a small gasp and nods at you. It's definitely Ada!
But when her gaze shifts to the woman's protruding belly, Lore-Ley's eyes widen in surprise.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: She's...?
You gesture for Lore-Ley to be quiet and wait until the pregnant woman walks a bit further before quietly trailing behind her.
That's Ada, right?

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Yeah. She's grown a lot, but I can still recognize her... What she's holding? Could it be Cabbage?
I know it's not good to make you follow and track someone with me... But she's your friend, right?

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Friend... Yes, I want to be her friend.
Then let's follow her... and don't tell Nightingale.
You follow Ada down a block. She storms forward furiously, seemingly clear about her destination. Finally, you see her enter a pet store.
You and Lore-Ley exchange a puzzled look and follow her inside.
You go to a corner, pretending to browse the pets while secretly keeping an eye on Ada.

speaker: Store Manager
content: Good afternoon. Buying something for Cabbage? We just got some new pet shampoo. It's on sale now, wanna get some?
The store manager greets Ada warmly. It's obvious that she's a regular customer at this store.

speaker: Ada
content: ...I'm afraid I won't need it anymore.
Ada sighs and places what's in her hand on the counter. She unzips the pet carrier and takes out a white puppy.
The puppy is clearly well-cared for, with bright eyes and neatly groomed snow-white curls.
However, his left front leg is shorter than the others, making it hard for him to walk. He hobbles over to lick the store owner's hand affectionately.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: What happened to Cabbage's leg!? He didn't have an injury before!
Lore-Ley covers her mouth, whispering in surprise. You signal her to stay calm and continue listening.
A melancholy Ada gently strokes Cabbage, but soon she sneezes, her face bright red. She takes out a mask in exasperation and puts it on tightly.

speaker: Ada
content: You know, ever since I got pregnant I've become allergic to Cabbage. My family knew and has been urging me to give him away.

speaker: Ada
content: The symptoms weren't too severe at first. I just sneezed occasionally, so I was able to hold off their pressure. But these days, it's impossible.

speaker: Ada
content: Cabbage has been with me for so many years. He's long been like family to me. Plus, he has a heart condition and injured his leg. How can I trust others to take care of him? Will they care for him as I do?
Seeing Ada break out in red patches, the store owner quickly takes Cabbage and puts him on the counter, then gives some ointment to Ada and leads her to a breezy area near the entrance.

speaker: Ada
content: The whole house has been in chaos for days. They threatened that if I don't send Cabbage away immediately, they'll get rid of him themselves.

speaker: Ada
content: I've been arguing with them every day over this, but it really can't continue like this...
She touches her belly.

speaker: Ada
content: After all, since I've decided to have this little one... I have to be responsible for it.
The store manager stays silent for a moment, then sighs.

speaker: Store Manager
content: So... what are you planning to do?

speaker: Ada
content: I know this might be a bit presumptuous, but... can I leave Cabbage here for a while? I'll look for someone to adopt him, and I'll cover all his expenses before that happens...

speaker: Store Manager
content: Money's not the main problem. I'm worried that given his health problems, it would be hard to find him a new home. Most people want a healthy puppy, right?
The store owner looks at the puppy on the counter and whistles loudly. The puppy, oblivious to his future, responds happily, wagging his tail and turning in circles.

speaker: Store Manager
content: But don't worry, I'll take good care of him. I'll also keep an eye out for a new owner...
Wow! What a cute puppy! He can even spin in circles!
You suddenly hear a young voice ring out. A child rushes up to the counter like a whirlwind, her eyes sparkling as she gazes at Cabbage.

speaker: Girl
content: Sir, miss, can I hold this puppy? I really like him!
After being momentarily stunned, Ada smiles and nods, letting the store owner carefully place Cabbage into the little girl's arms.

speaker: Ada
content: Of course, but please be careful and hold him steady. His legs have some problems.

speaker: Girl
content: Yeah, I'll be careful.
The girl teases Cabbage while giggling.

speaker: Girl
content: Miss, what's the puppy's name?

speaker: Ada
content: His name is Cabbage.

speaker: Girl
content: Wow, what a cute name! Just as cute as he is!

speaker: Girl
content: Miss, I heard that you're looking for a new home for him?

speaker: Ada
content: Yes. I'm pregnant, so I can't continue to take care of him. We need to find him a new owner who can.

speaker: Girl
content: Ah, I see...
The girl nods thoughtfully as a couple walks in.

speaker: Woman
content: How many times have I told you not to run so fast? Look at you, you're all sweaty.
The woman bends down lovingly to wipe the sweat from the girl's forehead as she reprimands her. The man, carrying many shopping bags, nods in agreement.

speaker: Man
content: Yes. You're making Mommy worry.

speaker: Girl
content: Sorry, Mommy and Daddy. I saw a really cute puppy, so I just had to rush in.
The girl proudly lifts the puppy in her arms up to the couple.

speaker: Girl
content: Look! His name is Cabbage. Isn't he cute? He's looking for a new home. Can we take him home?
The man's gentle expression freezes when he notices the puppy's missing foreleg. His face darkens, and he becomes stern.

speaker: Man
content: You can have a pet, but definitely not this dog!
The girl seems startled by her father's sudden change. She takes a while to respond, pouting in confusion and dismay.

speaker: Girl
content: Why?

speaker: Man
content: Can't you see he's crippled!?

speaker: Girl
content: So what? I really like him. I'll take good care of him!
As the girl argues with her dad, she casts a pleading look at her silent mother, but doesn't get the support she wants. The woman sighs, avoiding the child's gaze.

speaker: Woman
content: You say you'll take good care of him. Maybe you can do that for a day, a week, or even a month. But what happens after a year or two?
The woman squats down and lovingly strokes the girl's head, trying to comfort her.

speaker: Woman
content: Taking care of a sick puppy is as time-consuming and demanding as taking care of a sick person. You're still young. You can't fully comprehend these responsibilities...

speaker: Girl
content: But, I can do a lot of chores now! I can definitely take good care of him! Just let me...
The girl wants to argue more, but gets cut off.

speaker: Woman
content: Sweetie, don't be stubborn. No matter how much you love him or promise to never abandon him right now, you'll get tired of him over time.

speaker: Woman
content: You'll have to spend a lot of time taking care of him. You might not have time to go out with other kids or watch TV or play. Instead, you'll have to stay with him for his treatment. Is that what you want?

speaker: Woman
content: Plus, you'll need to buy him medicine, take him to the vet... your pocket money might not be enough. You won't be able to buy your favorite snacks and toys like now. Is that okay with you?

speaker: Woman
content: And the harsh truth is, no matter how well you take care of him, his condition won't improve. He'll be like this for the rest of his life. He won't be able to go outside to run and play with you...

speaker: Woman
content: Are you sure you won't resent him someday for these issues? Are you sure you won't see him as a burden and regret your decision?
The woman rambles on with her reasons, barely caring if the girl understands. She exchanges looks with the man, as if recalling a painful memory.
The girl finds herself unable to answer her mother's questions and lowers her head in frustration.
The man steps forward and lovingly pats her shoulder.

speaker: Man
content: Mommy and Daddy have been through this. We know how tough it is.

speaker: Man
content: Listen to Mommy and Daddy. Choose a healthy puppy, and grow up happily with it. You have so many choices. Why choose one that might make you regret it in the future?
The girl clenches her fists. She looks at the puppy, then at her father, making a final plea, but eventually slumps her shoulders in defeat.

speaker: Girl
content: Okay...

speaker: Man
content: Thatta girl. Our good girl.

speaker: Man
content: There there, don't be sad. Come, we'll get your favorite snacks from the supermarket, then Daddy will pick out the best beef and make your favorite stew!

speaker: Girl
content: R-Really?
Hearing these words, the girl's eyes light up instantly. She seems to forget all her previous disappointments.

speaker: Man
content: Of course. When has Daddy ever lied to you?
The woman pats her daughter's head with a smile.

speaker: Woman
content: Since you want a puppy so much, have you thought about which breed you want?

speaker: Girl
content: Huh? Do different breeds have differences besides their looks?

speaker: Woman
content: Of course! Like their temperament, habits, and so on. Different breeds of puppies are very different from each other.

speaker: Girl
content: I see...

speaker: Woman
content: Why don't we go home and do some research together? After all, choosing a puppy to join the family is a big decision!

speaker: Girl
content: Sure! Mommy, you're the best!
Ada and the store owner watch the family leave in silence. Only Cabbage continues to wag his tail eagerly, unaware of why he was suddenly left behind.
The woman's words, though harsh and heartbreaking, are grounded in reality. But you feel more regret and pity for the puppy, and start to worry about his future.
The atmosphere is so silent that you almost forgot you had a companion.
Lore-Ley?
You call out to her but get no response. She hangs her head in silence, her hair drooping down and covering most of her face.
What's wrong? Are you feeling unwell? Come, let's go and hydrate you before they notice us.
She doesn't answer you. After a long silence, she slowly utters some jumbled words.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: When I was young, they treated me with the same gentleness and patience... Ha, I almost forgot.
...What?
You don't immediately understand her, but instinctively feel a wave of unease.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: You can't believe it, can you?

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: What a coincidence. Those two... are my parents.
For as long as she could remember, Lore-Ley had never left that small room.
A white bathtub, tiles with little dolphins, a ray of sunlight peeking in from the window, the scent of bath lotion, a tub full of water and splashing sounds... these made up her entire world.
Though she never met anyone else of her age, Lore-Ley could still vaguely sense that she was somehow different from others.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Mommy, why am I always in the bathtub?

speaker: Mother
content: Because you're a little water fairy that lives in water.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: When can I get out of this tub?

speaker: Mother
content: When you grow a little bigger and stronger.

speaker: Mother
content: When you grow up, you can make friends and play with other kids. You can go on adventures and travel to faraway places like in the picture books, and see many different things.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Wow! It's great to grow up!

speaker: Mother
content: Then you should eat well every day to grow up quickly, okay?

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Sure!

speaker: Mother
content: Alright, sweetie. Do you want to know what Mommy saw when she went downstairs just now?

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Yeah!

speaker: Mother
content: Well, the peach blossoms have bloomed... the first ones this spring! They are small pink flowers with five petals and a tiny center...
Back then, little Lore-Ley wasn't tall enough. Even if she stretched out her arms, she couldn't reach the window above the tub.
She couldn't push it open to see outside, to see if there really were colorful flowers and bustling crowds like her parents said.
But what does it matter? After all, she would grow up one day.
Until then, she had the company and love of her parents, endless stories, and many rubber duckies and plastic fish.
That little room was her castle, and that little bathtub was her throne. She was the queen of her own world.
For Lore-Ley, freedom was the distance from one end of the bathtub to the other. As time passed year by year, her body grew, and her heart grew as well. Freedom became so much smaller.
She began to realize that growing up wasn't as wonderful as she once imagined...
Her illness didn't improve, but the weariness on her parents' faces grew. They appeared in front of her less and less each day.
The room was quiet. From the bathtub, Lore-Ley watched the sun rise and set outside the window. Finally, when the sunlight almost vanished completely, the door opened from the outside.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Daddy!

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Did you finally get off work? You must be tired! Did you see anything interesting outside today?

Leaning on the edge of the tub, Lore-Ley smiled expectantly at the man at the door. But all she got in response was a brief and weary "Mmm." He didn't seem to want to chat, and only made a stiff remark.

speaker: Daddy
content: It's your birthday today, right? Happy birthday. This computer is our gift to you. It should help pass the time. Play around with it yourself.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Thank you...
Before she could finish speaking, the door slammed shut in front of her once more.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: ...Daddy!

It's okay. Daddy had a hard day at work. I should be more considerate of his feelings. Plus, he remembered my birthday and gave me a gift. Isn't that something to be happy about? She comforted herself with these thoughts.
After finally sorting out her emotions, Lore-Ley started to fiddle with the small black machine. When she randomly pressed a button, the screen lit up.
The internet was a world much bigger than she had imagined. Lore-Ley met many different people through it.
At first, she thought she had gained freedom. Every day in the virtual world was fresh and exciting, surrounded by fascinating people.
But ultimately, she was still different from everyone else.

Other netizens could meet offline and become real-life friends, but Lore-Ley couldn't leave the tub or this room. Thus, no matter how the wonderful online relationships she formed, they all eventually fade away.
But the info on the net updated too quickly. For Lore-Ley, who had never encountered such variety, the stimulation was overwhelming.
She barely had time to feel the pain of losing friends before being drawn into another whirlwind of information.
Temptations from the dark corners of the internet began to erode her mental world. She became increasingly dissatisfied and irritable.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Today's steak is so salty! Gross! Take it away!

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Why don't you take me for treatment? Don't say it's incurable! Have you given up so easily!?

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Ha, why are you looking at me like that!? Do you know how painful it is to be trapped in this stupid tub every day!? I can't even walk! I can't make friends! I'm not happy at all!

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: As my parents, is it not your duty to spend time with me, talk to me, and fulfill my needs? If you didn't want this responsibility, why did you give birth to me at all!?
As she watched her parents leave the room without a word, Lore-Ley felt as if she had achieved some kind of victory. She smugly mumbled to herself:

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Now they must realize their mistakes! It won't be long before they come to apologize and start paying attention to me again. Then we can happily live together like when I was little!

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: I'm sure it will be like that!
However, the next morning, all she got was a note left behind in an empty house.

Lore-Ley, sweetie.
Forgive us. This is the last time we will be addressing you in this way. We're deeply sorry, but we can't no longer bear these endless days of mutual torment. We understand your pain, truly we do, but we've done everything we can. Believe us, every time we see you, we feel just as much pain and despair as you do.
You might feel we owe you, but the care and effort we gave you over the years, we hope, should be enough. We want to move forward, free from the hopeless burdens. Please don't hate us.

On the back of this note is our bank account details, with our savings. Every month from now on, we will deposit a living expense for you. Take care.
Lore-Ley stared blankly at the note in her hand.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: ...To everyone, I'm just a burden, a drag. I should have realized long ago... what am I still hoping for?

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Stop it. Let it all end.
As she mumbled to herself, she filled the bathtub to the brim, and slowly submerged herself.
As the water submerged her head, she no longer heard the voice in her heart or any outside noise. Only the steady chimes of computer messages persisted.
After telling her story, Lore-Ley exhales deeply and laughs in self-deprecation.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: For a long time after that, I still hoped they would return to me. I thought blood was the only connection in this world that couldn't be broken.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Their money arrives on time every month, but I realized that it's just a thick firewall they use to completely block off our kinship.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: It's fine. After seeing them live so well, I no longer cling to any shred of false hope. They definitely don't want to see me again.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: So now, I have no connection with anyone in this world.
Her lips curl slightly, forcing a grimace of a smile.
What is there to do at this point? Nothing can be changed. Both consoling her or questioning that family seems meaningless.
Suddenly, an idea pops into your head when you look back at the white puppy.

options: Do you want to adopt that puppy?

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: What...?
Lore-Ley seems confused by what you're saying, so you repeat yourself.
Lore-Ley, do you want to adopt that puppy?

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Me... adopt?
Yeah. You have the ability to take care of him now. The key is whether or not you want to take on this responsibility.
Lore-Ley hesitates. She glances at you, then the puppy, then the door her parents left through. She seems to vaguely understand your intention.
But before she can respond, Ada approaches you both and interrupts your conversation.

speaker: Ada
content: Um, excuse me, I overheard you... Are you thinking about adopting Cabbage?
Lore-Ley lowers her head in a bit of a panic, not daring to look Ada in the eyes.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Y-yeah, I'm considering it...

speaker: Ada
content: Well, adoption does require careful consideration.
Ada looks at the puppy on the counter, her tone full of pity.

speaker: Ada
content: Cabbage was born with a heart condition and later had an accident that disabled his leg. He's fragile and can't move freely, so he really needs meticulous care.

speaker: Ada
content: It's a heavy responsibility. You must be fully mentally prepared before taking it on.
After listening to Ada, Lore-Ley gazes at the puppy on the counter in silence. She ponders solemnly for a while, then makes up her mind and lifts up her head with a look of determination.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Ah, I see. Let me adopt him. I'll take good care of him, just like you did.

speaker: Ada
content: R-Really?! You really want to adopt him?!
Ada exclaims happily, and Cabbage, influenced by his owner's emotions, raises his head and howls.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: I know how troublesome a lifelong incurable disease can be. But even so... I want him to be cared for.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: I hope my promise... can maintain the link between me and him, and between me and you.
Ada's eyes brighten, glistening with tears.

speaker: Ada
content: Since you're serious about adopting him, let me tell you the details about taking care of Cabbage!

speaker: Ada
content: Even though Cabbage is ill, he's very warm and cheerful! He's not dangerous at all. He loves people, so if anyone wants to play with him, you can let them...
Ada says this as she puts her large canvas bag on the table and unzips it to reveal an array of medicines, bowls, dog food, cans, blankets, and plush toys.
You seize the moment to pick up the puppy from the counter.

speaker: Ada
content: ...This is his heart medicine. One pill in the morning and one at night. Just mix it into his food. He needs a monthly visit with the vet for his heart and deworming...

speaker: Ada
content: This is the card of the vet who usually treats him. He knows Cabbage well.

speaker: Ada
content: This is the food that Cabbage usually eats. He prefers chicken and beef vegetable flavors. This is his favorite beef jerky treat. You can give it to him as a reward every now and then, but not too much, as it can cause indigestion...

speaker: Ada
content: This is Cabbage's shampoo. His skin is sensitive and prone to allergies, so just stick to this brand.

speaker: Ada
content: These are his favorite plush toys, and this is the blanket he sleeps with. His bed is at the bottom, I can't pull it out right now...
Lore-Ley listens intently, meticulously recording every detail on her comms device.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Okay, I've noted everything you said. I promise I'll take good care of Cabbage.
Lore-Ley takes the big bag from Ada solemnly, as if literally taking on a heavy responsibility.
Ada seems to realize something. She scrutinizes Lore-Ley's face, then hesitantly asks.

speaker: Ada
content: By the way, your voice sounds familiar... May I ask, are you L.L.?

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Yeah, um... sorry for bothering you earlier, I...
Lore-Ley panics. Her eyes dart around as she looks to you for help, but in the next moment, Ada bows to her.

speaker: Ada
content: So it really is you... I'm sorry.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: ...Huh?

speaker: Ada
content: You called me, and I was harsh to you.
Ada explains with an apologetic expression.

speaker: Ada
content: I never had the chance to explain to you... I cut off contact because Cabbage had an accident while I was traveling. That's when his leg got injured.

speaker: Ada
content: I recognized you in that call. I was arguing with my family about Cabbage at the time, so I was feeling irritable. Plus, your sudden call reminded me of Cabbage's injury, which is why...

speaker: Ada
content: I'm really very sorry. Can you forgive me?

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: It's okay... I understand how you feel.
Lore-Ley smiles and gently shakes her head. Ada also smiles at her, a hint of nostalgia in her eyes.

speaker: Ada
content: You're still as easygoing as ever.

speaker: Ada
content: I still remember how I used to tell you everything, no matter how trivial. Whether I was complaining or bragging, you would always respond patiently.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Yeah.
Recalling the past, Lore-Ley relaxes and playfully winks at Ada.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: I remember you said you wanted to become a great designer. Did that dream come true? Or was it just one of your boasts?

speaker: Ada
content: Of course it came true. It was never just a boast! Though I later realized the job was less glamorous and more tiring than what I imagined, I don't regret it.

speaker: Ada
content: And you? What about your wish?
Ada looks teasingly at Lore-Ley, but the latter tilts her head in confusion, seemingly unable to remember.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: My wish...? Did I tell you my wish?

speaker: Ada
content: Of course you did! I still remember it.

speaker: Ada
content: You said you wanted to be like other people and leave the bathtub. You wanted to see the outside world and have real friends, just like everyone else.
She smiles first at Lore-Ley, then at you and Cabbage.

speaker: Ada
content: Hmm... It seems like it's all come true now. That's great.

speaker: Ada
content: You seem happier now than you did back then.
As you leave the pet shop, Ada calls out to you.

speaker: Ada
content: L.L.! Can I visit you and Cabbage?
Lore-Ley looks at you and shakes her head in dismay.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: The place where I live now has some restrictions. Usually it's not open to other people. But...
She pauses, mustering up courage.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: But if you want, we can go back to chatting online! I'll send you pictures of Cabbage!
Ada doesn't press further and simply nods.

speaker: Ada
content: Alright. Let's use our old accounts to get in touch. It's been a long time since I logged in, but I still remember the password.

speaker: Ada
content: ...It's getting late. You should head back soon. It's almost Cabbage's mealtime. Don't let him go hungry!
She waves vigorously at you from under the tree.

speaker: Ada
content: Have a good one! Don't forget to send me pictures of Cabbage, videos as well! As many as I used to send you!

speaker: Cabbage
content: Woof, woof!

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Cabbage! Slow down!
As you watch the blue-haired girl chase after the puppy with the prosthetic limb, you feel all the weariness from work dissipates.
Neither you, Lore-Ley, nor Ada ever imagined that Cabbage could regain the ability to move freely through technology and the efforts of everyone at the Bureau.
Cabbage probably never expected to rediscover the joy of running freely himself. He now charges through the corridors of the Bureau, indulging in his hard-won freedom.
Lore-Ley is also diligently fulfilling the promise she made to Ada at the pet shop, caring for Cabbage with great patience and attention.
This is her first time raising a pet, and also her first time taking responsibility for something.
Though lacking experience, her strong sense of responsibility drove her to seek help from Ada, you, and other Sinners with pets when she faced difficulties.
Finally, through her persistent efforts, everything fell into place.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Ah! Excuse me! Please stop Cabbage!
She calls out to a pair of Sinners up ahead, who responds earnestly and blocks off the paths at the end of the corridor after assessing the situation.

speaker: Luvia Ray
content: Got it! You can count on us!

speaker: Serpent
content: Mhmm, no puppy can escape from my grasp...
As Ada said, Cabbage might just be the most charming puppy in the world. He captured so many hearts since coming to the MBCC.
Whenever someone at the Bureau had time, they would come play with him and chat with Lore-Ley along the way.
As time progresses, Lore-Ley is no longer the timid soul she was when she first arrived.
She's now an assured and outgoing person who confidently expresses herself with others face-to-face. Her lively online persona is showing in real life.
In addition to Ada, Lore-Ley also found more like-minded friends in the real world.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Thank you so much!

speaker: Luvia Ray
content: No worries! Happy to help!
Lore-Ley thanks them and takes Cabbage from their hands. She lifts the playful little dog to her face, affectionately pressing her nose against his.

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Didn't you hear what Dr. Iron and Miss Eureka said? This new prosthetic leg is still experimental. If something goes wrong, you could fall and get hurt!

speaker: Lore-Ley
content: Have some patience! Take it slow, little by little. There's plenty of joy and freedom waiting for you in the future!

speaker: Nirvana Employee
content: ...And so, this group of criminals who fled to WhiteSands has been apprehended. However, the leader of their town somehow found out about you and specifically requested that the Chief of MBCC oversee the extradition process.
In your office, an employee from Nirvana is explaining the specifics of this request to you.

speaker: Nirvana Employee
content: Therefore, the Council hopes you can spare some time to make the trip... There won't be much required of you, and FAC will handle all security arrangements. Your presence alone would be greatly appreciated.
You glance at your work schedule and find that you do have some free time coming up. The task itself sounds simple enough to be treated as a nice little getaway to unwind.

speaker: Nirvana Employee
content: That couldn't be better. On behalf of Nirvana, we really appreciate your understanding...
You wave a hand, cutting off his pleasantries. While you have to play nice and work together with Nirvana for Paradeisos's sake, you've never really liked these people, not deep down.
Is there anything else? If not...

speaker: Nirvana Employee
content: Just a moment, please. There are a few other matters I'd like to bring to your attention.
You knew it—these Nirvana people always have ulterior motives. They don't go away that easily.

speaker: Nirvana Employee
content: Here's the situation: we've recently learned that an Eastside fugitive has fled to that same town. According to reliable sources, this individual is a Sinner with dangerous abilities.
Do you have any identifying information?

speaker: Nirvana Employee
content: Yes, we do. Her name is Parfait, and she refers to herself as Eastside's "investment guru." You may have heard of her.
Yeah, I've heard of her. But I've always been curious, what exactly did she do to get on your radar?

speaker: Nirvana Employee
content: Six months ago, Parfait used various methods to fabricate massive amounts of false information about Hypercubes. This scheme resulted in catastrophic financial losses for hundreds of investors and caused irreparable harm to the Hypercube market's stability.

speaker: Nirvana Employee
content: Truth be told, we consider her the most damaging financial criminal DisCity has ever seen...
Alright, I get it. I'll keep an eye out for this Parfait when I'm there... But don't get your hopes up too high. She may well be gone before I arrive.

speaker: Nirvana Employee
content: Of course, we completely understand. We knew this would take time from the very beginning. Honestly, just having you keep an eye on the situation is already an enormous help to us.

speaker: Nirvana Employee
content: Here's Parfait's complete dossier. We're not expecting you to arrest her. If you could just gather some firsthand intelligence when convenient, we'd be extremely grateful...
Couldn't get a single useful lead in the end...

The sand ship's engines roar to life as it prepares to depart. You close Parfait's dossier, thinking back on the past few days. You had asked about her—both deliberately and in passing—but turned up nothing useful.
Forget it...
You slip the dossier back into your bag. The business trip isn't particularly long, but despite what the Nirvana employee claimed, the days have been packed with plenty of work to keep you busy.
When it was finally over, you deliberately booked passage on a civilian sand ship for the return trip, even put on a bit of a disguise, all to avoid any work talk during the journey.
Only after you adjust your hat and mask, settling into your seat, do you finally exhale in relief. At last, some proper downtime.
Excuse me...

Your seatmate shows up just as the sand ship is about to depart, rushing to reach you. Despite the hurry, she carries herself with grace—polite, courteous, even elegant. But something about her demeanor strikes you as a little... practiced.
This is your first time paying your own way on a civilian sand ship, and you didn't splurge on first class or business class. For the next few hours, this stranger will be your closest companion.
You shift aside to let her pass, taking the opportunity to discreetly size her up.
Thank you.

She squeezes past you and settles into her seat with perfect posture, taking a moment to smooth any wrinkles from her clothes. Then she lowers her tray table and begins unpacking her bag: a stack of financial newspapers, a mysterious paper-wrapped parcel, a tiny bottle of aromatherapy oil, an exquisite traveling tea set, and—of all things—a hand-crank coffee grinder.
With practiced efficiency, she arranges everything on the small tray table. Then, unfolding the parcel, she tips a handful of coffee beans into the grinder and begins turning the crank.
Excuse me, do you have any hot water... Wonderful, thank you.

You watch, utterly mesmerized, as she accepts hot water from the attendant, filters her fresh coffee grounds, and somehow still flips through the newspaper while she waits. The rich, nutty aroma leaves no doubt: these are premium beans.

As the coffee finishes brewing, she lifts her porcelain cup with deliberate grace. Even performing this elaborate ritual in the cramped space, she maintains an effortless elegance. You can't help but be impressed.
Somehow, you find her face familiar.
Would you like some?
Apparently catching your curious gaze, your seatmate gives you a smile and lifts her coffee pot.
That coffee aroma is impossible to resist... Just one small sip wouldn't hurt, you think.

You pull out a paper cup from the passenger amenity kit. Though everything about her screams refinement, she doesn't bat an eye at your flimsy drinkware. Instead, she pours you a careful half-cup with a smile.
You're not reckless enough to accept a drink from a stranger you've met for barely ten minutes. You shake your head in polite refusal.
She doesn't press the matter, simply offering a courteous smile in response.
Still, the brief exchange breaks the ice. The more you study her features, the stronger that nagging sense of familiarity grows, until curiosity wins out.
Are you from DisCity? Or...
Eastside.
She finishes her coffee and quickly wipes the cup clean before putting it away.
I've spent some time around WhiteSands for work, and now I have a few matters to attend to in Eastside. So, I'm on my way back.
So, what do you do for work?
Just a bit of financial investing here and there.
Finance? Wait, you're not some big shot from Eastside, are you?
No, no...
She demurs, quickly waving her hand.
I've been fortunate to receive such kindness from my fellow investors in Eastside, and while they've generously referred to me as an "investment guru," I'm afraid the title is far too flattering...
Truthfully, my passions lie more in the realms of art, cuisine, and fashion. Rather than a financier, I suppose you could say I fancy myself a "professional hedonist."

Your gaze flicks unconsciously to your bag holding the dossier. Now you're certain. That's why she looked familiar. This passenger sitting right next to you is none other than the fugitive you've been chasing.

You booked a civilian ship ticket precisely to avoid trouble, yet here it is, coming to you anyway. Well, if that's how it is, you'll play your part. A few more hours of keeping her calm and unsuspecting, and this journey will be over.

speaker: Parfait
content: To actually meet a kindred spirit aboard a sand ship... what extraordinary luck this is.

Parfait presses a hand to her chest and sighs wistfully, with the look of someone who regrets not meeting you sooner. All that mental gymnastics you've done in the past few hours, scrambling to keep up with her art theory tangents, has apparently paid off.
Not at all, I just happen to know some friends who work in the arts.

speaker: Parfait
content: Oh, you're far too modest. Your depth of knowledge and cultural refinement couldn't possibly come just from knowing some friends. Some of your insights on music and fine arts are truly remarkable. I must admit, they leave me in awe.
You offer an awkward smile. There are quite a few artists in the Bureau, and you've mostly picked things up through osmosis. A few more hours of this, and you'd be fresh out of borrowed knowledge.
But of course, you can't possibly explain any of this to her.

speaker: Parfait
content: Speaking of which, I actually came back specifically for this year's Spring Concert. A fine gentleman as yourself surely wouldn't miss it, would you?
female_content: Speaking of which, I actually came back specifically for this year's Spring Concert. A fine lady as yourself surely wouldn't miss it, would you?

content: ...I suppose so.

Unfortunately, you've never even heard of this Spring Concert, and barring any surprises, your schedule wouldn't allow it anyway. Right now, all you can do is offer a vague reply and hope the conversation moves on.

speaker: Parfait
content: That would be absolutely wonderful!
The sand ship begins to slow down. Through the window, dock workers materialize in the gloom, their signal batons cutting bright arcs through the darkness as they guide the vessel home.

speaker: Parfait
content: It seems our time together has come to an end... Well, I've never once wished a sand ship voyage could last longer. Oh, before you go... might I offer you a ride back? I'd be happy to accompany you.

speaker: Parfait
content: My business partner will be arriving shortly in my extended Wraith. I had the interior custom-designed by the finest artisans. No expense spared, of course. And I always keep my personal wine selection on hand. Would you...

You watch Parfait extend these lavish offers from her economy-class seat, strangely charmed by her enthusiasm. There's no artifice in her expression but genuine excitement at the prospect of sharing something wonderful with a new friend.

Still, you politely decline. After all, you've just uncovered that this so-called investment guru has an accomplice. The Bureau's operations department needs to be alerted—and reinforcements dispatched—immediately.
Thank you, but I have plans with a friend.

speaker: Parfait
content: I see... What a shame. But that's quite all right. So long as we're both in DisCity, I'm certain our paths will cross again.

speaker: Mission Operative
content: Will her accomplice really show up...?
You sit in the Bureau's vehicle, watching Parfait through the window. She hasn't moved from her spot in the parking lot for nearly an hour, luggage at her side.

Every few minutes, she tries her terminal again, but each call fails to connect. Around her, the lot empties. The wind picks up, sharp with the late-hour chill, but still, no one comes for her. By now, she's hugging herself against the cold, shoulders hunched.
Forget it. Let's close the net.
The car slowly pulls up, and you roll down the window, waving at Parfait. She's still shivering in the cold, her nose red and on the verge of running.
Need a ride?
The biting wind has left her half-numb, her thoughts sluggish. When she looks up at her unexpected rescuer, her face lights up with nothing but pure, unguarded gratitude.

speaker: Parfait
content: Thank you so much...
Once inside the Bureau's walls, even Parfait couldn't fail to recognize you forever, and the moment of realization finally comes.
Now she sits in the interrogation chair, no longer the shivering, miserable figure from the parking lot, but once again displaying the elegant composure you first encountered.

speaker: Parfait
content: Who could have imagined my first encounter with the distinguished MBCC Chief would be quite so... undignified? Though I must admit, there's a certain charm in the unexpected. Perhaps one day, this will serve as a rather entertaining story over cocktails.
With that said, her face shows not a trace of embarrassment. She simply leans forward in her chair, hand outstretched toward you.

speaker: Parfait
content: Allow me to introduce myself properly. I am Parfait Medici, Executive Director and Investment Advisor at Tulip Holdings. It's an honor to make your acquaintance, Chief.
Parfait smiles, her hand lingering expectantly in mid-air as she waits for your response.
Your reputation as the investment guru certainly precedes you. I've been hearing about your impressive track record for some time now.

You're the orphaned heir of Robert Medici, a wealthy merchant who lived abroad. Since your return to DisCity in N.F. 108, you've become one of high society's most prominent figures. Through your accomplishments in finance, the arts, and other pursuits, you've earned a reputation as the epitome of Eastside aristocracy.

speaker: Parfait
content: You're too kind. As I mentioned before, it's all far too flattering...
Your "but" cuts through Parfait's modest deflection.

Ever since you disappeared from Eastside's public eye six months ago, your reputation as the "investment guru" has taken a steep nosedive. Even Tulip Holdings, where you're employed, is struggling with bankruptcy rumors right now.

speaker: Parfait
content: ...That's simply the way high society operates. No matter how earnestly I tried to connect with everyone, it's impossible to win them all over in the end.
Parfait sighs, her voice laced with quiet resignation.

speaker: Parfait
content: Indeed, Tulip Holdings faced some unfavorable press six months ago when I was in the Outlands overseeing a significant business transaction that demanded my full attention. Regrettably, this meant I wasn't able to address the situation as promptly as I would have liked.

speaker: Parfait
content: As you can see, my enemies naturally took advantage of the circumstances to amplify rumors and distort the facts. I'm afraid that's also why my business partners felt compelled to withdraw... Of course, I understand the decision completely. Had I been in their position, I might have done the same.

speaker: Parfait
content: However...
Parfait lifts her head, the gloom vanishing from her expression, replaced by the polished confidence that only comes with success.

speaker: Parfait
content: Now that Parfait has returned to DisCity, where her loyalty lies, the rumors will naturally fade away, and this entire situation will be resolved smoothly. Rest assured, the investment guru would never allow her investor friends to suffer any losses.
Is that so?
Parfait's response is confident and thorough, but the dossier from Nirvana tells a completely different story.
test
test
test
test
test
test

You pull out a stack of files: surveillance photos, intelligence reports, all the damning evidence. The top photo leaves no room for doubt—there's Parfait, leaning from a helicopter door, scattering Hypercubes by the handful.

Six months ago, you announced the discovery of an Outland Hypercube mine. However, there's still no visible progress on any mining operation. It appears your actions were nothing more than fraudulent market manipulation, with serious consequences for both Hypercube trade and DisCity's economy.

speaker: Parfait
content: I must say, that seems a rather uncharitable remark. My return to DisCity is precisely to bring back the latest updates on the Outland Hypercube mine.
But the Hypercube situation was just the beginning.
You flip through the files, pointing at the photos as you continue.
After that incident, all of Eastside—from government officials to affected corporations—began investigating you. Some now question whether your entire identity is legitimate.

"Contrary to initial assumptions, Parfait is no aristocratic orphan but a West District slum native with a history of fraud. Notably, her emergence coincided precisely with Eastside's bank counterfeit currency case. With her Sinner status now confirmed, we assess she likely employed her abilities to facilitate these crimes."
For just a moment, you catch what looks like a crack in Parfait's composure, but by the time you study her expression again, that fleeting hitch is already gone.

speaker: Parfait
content: Might I ask if these files—or more precisely, these unflattering reports—came from Nirvana?
Parfait gives a slight smile, seemingly unfazed by your response.

speaker: Parfait
content: This assertion about disrupting the Hypercube market is merely Nirvana's side of the story. After all, if there truly were no Hypercube mine in the Outlands, how would an ordinary investor like me have acquired such a substantial quantity?

speaker: Parfait
content: If you consider it thoughtfully, the discovery of an Outland Hypercube mine is undoubtedly an unequivocal boon for all of humanity with no conceivable drawbacks.

speaker: Parfait
content: The only ones who might oppose this—who would see their interests jeopardized—are Nirvana. After all, their corporate supremacy hinges entirely on their monopoly over Hypercubes. So...

speaker: Parfait
content: Naturally, they will resort to any means to undermine me, even exploiting my status as a Sinner, not just to attack me personally, but to tarnish the credibility of all the capital under my name.
After delivering that impassioned speech, Parfait pauses for a moment, looking deeply into your eyes.

speaker: Parfait
content: Please tell me, Chief. Surely in today's DisCity, being a Sinner isn't still a crime, is it?
Before you can finish whatever comes after "No," Parfait quickly interjects with an exclamation.

speaker: Parfait
content: Exactly. Just look at today's DisCity: whether among traders, the FAC, the Council, artists, or even Nirvana's own circle, Sinners can be found in every sphere of influence.

speaker: Parfait
content: It's already N.F. 115, and yet some still resort to exploiting antiquated Eastsider prejudices, to employing such crude and outdated tactics simply because I've challenged their monopoly. It's utterly absurd, don't you think?
Your status as a Sinner isn't the issue here. It's whether you've ever used your abilities for illegal activities.
Based on the intelligence and evidence from Nirvana regarding the counterfeit currency case, everything indeed points to your involvement.

speaker: Parfait
content: Really?
Parfait tilts her head, her expression the perfect picture of innocence.

speaker: Parfait
content: But from my perspective, what they refer to as "damning evidence" appears to be little more than malicious speculation built on thin air.

speaker: Parfait
content: It is true that I have dined with individuals from the West District who may be connected to counterfeit currency distribution. But let me be clear: these were not private gatherings. On the contrary, invitations to Parfait's Dinner Party have always been extended publicly, as a matter of record.

speaker: Parfait
content: My guests represent every industry and district in DisCity, including, I might add, a number of my detractors—the very people now circulating these rumors. If their own logic were to be followed, wouldn't that implicate them just as readily in this accusation?
Parfait isn't wrong about this. When it comes to the counterfeit currency case, Nirvana only gave you circumstantial evidence, nothing concrete enough to challenge her claims.
Your silence doesn't go unnoticed. With a satisfied brush of her sleeves, Parfait meets your gaze, utterly self-assured.

speaker: Parfait
content: After all, this is neither a court of law nor the office of the Financial Inspection Team. Arguing over whether the evidence is comprehensive here seems rather pointless, don't you think?

speaker: Parfait
content: Frankly, if Nirvana truly had solid evidence, they would never have circumvented the proper channels by using you to detain me. Nor would they have wasted all this effort on their smear campaign against me.

speaker: Parfait
content: In fact, I would welcome the opportunity to face them in court and let them accuse me of identity fraud and counterfeiting. I'd be more than prepared to countersue for defamation and anti-competitive behavior.
So you came back specifically to take legal action against Nirvana?

speaker: Parfait
content: What? No, no, no. I have no interest in wasting my time on something like that.
Parfait quickly waves off your speculation.
Why not? One successful lawsuit could easily restore your reputation and save Tulip Holdings. Wouldn't that be worth it?

speaker: Parfait
content: Hahaha, you've got it all wrong. Personal reputation lawsuits are pure bad debt. Even if I exhaust myself winning, the returns are negligible. It would only wear down the investors' patience without meaningful gain.

speaker: Parfait
content: What truly matters to investors, after all, is profitability—the potential for future returns. That's precisely why I've dedicated the past six months to advancing Hypercube's mining operations in the Outlands.
But you did come back after all. Couldn't you set the record straight while you're here?

speaker: Parfait
content: There's really no need for that. A touch of doubt can actually strengthen trust over time. Once the Hypercube shipments arrive, those making a scene now will surely be eager for a piece of the cake. Why indulge in pointless debates?

You have to admit, Parfait's arguments are compelling, airtight even. The kind of flawless logic you'd expect from a financial magnate. But the sharper her reasoning gets, the louder your instincts scream: This woman is hiding something big.
After all, by her own explanation, she shouldn't even be in DisCity right now.
Then what's the real reason you came back?

speaker: Parfait
content: For the Spring Concert, of course!
At the mention of the Spring Concert, Parfait's face lights up, her professional demeanor melting away as her eyes sparkle with childlike excitement.

speaker: Parfait
content: Didn't I mention this to you on the sand ship? It's the most prestigious event for musicians across all of DisCity, and even the Outlands. This annual celebration has practically become DisCity's cultural emblem.

speaker: Parfait
content: And to think, Maestro Euragio announced at the start of the year that this Spring Concert would be his final public performance... My friends and I promised to attend together six months ago. I simply couldn't bear to disappoint them.

Watching Parfait's expectant expression, you find yourself inexplicably amused. In all your years dealing with DisCity's swindlers and criminals, you've never met someone who manages to be both cunning and naive at the same time.
After all, she's a major economic suspect specifically flagged by the higher-ups. There's no way you can let her attend some concert.
...Well, I'm afraid I'll have to disappoint you.
Parfait goes still. The eager anticipation in her expression instantly hardens into wariness.

speaker: Parfait
content: I... don't understand what you mean.
As per regulations, the MBCC is responsible for monitoring Sinners suspected of criminal activity to protect DisCity from further harm.

speaker: Parfait
content: You... you must be joking. How could I possibly cause any...

Just to clarify, MBCC operates differently from the Public Security Bureau and Financial Inspection Team you're familiar with. Unlike those agencies, we don't permit bail. Also, we maintain detention authority over Sinners until their charges are fully resolved.
You catch a single drop of sweat glistening on Parfait's forehead.
I want to believe what you've told me, so I won't be sending you to Nirvana. But... the higher-ups have you flagged. I can't just let you walk out of here.

Here's the plan: with so many people looking to settle scores with you anyway, think of this as protective custody. You'll stay at the Bureau while we verify the intel together. Once everything checks out, you're free to go. Fair warning though, this could take some time.

speaker: Parfait
content: For... how long?
If all goes well, ten days to two weeks.

speaker: Parfait
content: Can I go out at all during that time?
Strictly speaking, absolutely not...

speaker: Parfait
content: Wait!
Parfait, until now the picture of unshakable poise, suddenly shakes her head in a frantic manner.

speaker: Parfait
content: Hold on, hold on... but the Spring Concert is next week!
You keep your professional composure, though duty clearly weighs on you.
Can't you watch the livestream?

speaker: Parfait
content: No, no, no... a livestream is an entirely different matter altogether!

speaker: Parfait
content: A maestro's farewell performance, with the most extraordinary lineup in years. If I couldn't witness such a masterpiece in person, I'd carry that regret with me forever. Just the thought of missing it would leave me wistful for years to come...
Parfait looks utterly shattered. You didn't expect such a casual probe to hit so hard, and now you're starting to have your doubts.
Would an "investment guru" like her really crumble over a simple concert? Something doesn't add up, so you decide to dig deeper.
If it's that important to you, I could make an exception for that one night. But you'd be under full surveillance the entire time.

speaker: Parfait
content: Do you mean it?
Parfait looks up at you pitifully, her eyes even shimmering with unshed tears.

speaker: Parfait
content: But... one night simply won't be enough. First, I'll need to secure tickets, considering presales ended ages ago. I'll have to reach out to someone from the box office directly.

speaker: Parfait
content: And then there are the friends I've invited. It's already been half a year since I left, and it would feel terribly unkind if I didn't make time to see them in person...
That's it! You're now finally closing in on Parfait's slip-up. There's no way her return to DisCity at such a delicate time is just about some concert.
The real reason must be hidden among the people she plans to meet this week.

speaker: Parfait
content: Chief, please... this is really the one thing I couldn't bear to miss. After the concert, I'll gladly assist you with all you need, anything within my ability. You have my word.
I see...
You make a show of reluctance, though your mind is already working—you'll need to monitor Parfait closely during this time and catch her in the act.
Still, you can't agree too quickly, or she might get suspicious and figure out your real intentions.
As it turns out, I could use your help collecting some intel.

speaker: Parfait
content: Please, go ahead! I'm more than happy to share everything I know! I won't hold back a single detail!
So, about six months ago, right during your most active period, I received an anonymous letter while on official duty.
Whoever sent it did me a real favor, but I'm sure they're sitting on far more valuable information. The problem is, I've spent half a year digging and still can't track them down.
I was thinking someone with your financial success and connections might be able to help uncover some leads?
Parfait's smile falters for just a heartbeat before she catches herself, her face lighting up again with practiced brightness as she answers.

speaker: Parfait
content: Leave it to me. Once the concert's over, I'll reach out to my entire network to help you investigate this thoroughly!
I appreciate it.
And you'll need to share your schedule with me. I have to accompany you wherever you go... I hope you understand.

speaker: Parfait
content: Of course. Please rest assured, I will not let you down.
At last, Parfait relaxes, her breath escaping in a long sigh of relief. This outcome isn't perfect, but one you can both live with.
With your permission, the first stop on Parfait's itinerary is an upscale gallery in Eastside.
The moment you step inside, the murmur of wealthy patrons follows you, their whispers curling through the space like smoke.

speaker: Passerby A
content: Isn't that Eastside's investment guru? What's she doing back here? And the person next to her is... the MBCC Chief?

speaker: Passerby B
content: It's about her Tulip Holdings, obviously. She has to come back for the investigation anyway. If she doesn't clean up her own mess, she's totally gonna go bankrupt.

speaker: Passerby A
content: Shh, she's coming over... Hello there, Parfait! Long time no see. What have you been keeping yourself busy with lately?
Parfait approaches with a bright, practiced smile. Whether she's oblivious to the gossiping whispers or just playing innocent is impossible to tell.

speaker: Parfait
content: Oh, Richard, it truly has been too long. I've been much the same, keeping rather occupied with the development of the Outland Hypercube mine.

speaker: Richard
content: I recall this Hypercube mining venture has been going on for about half a year now, hasn't it? How's the progress coming along?

speaker: Parfait
content: Everything is going quite smoothly. If all continues as planned, I anticipate having the first shipment prepared by March of next year.

speaker: Richard
content: Splendid! Once this Outland Hypercube trade route is up and running, Tulip Holdings will be absolutely gilded. Now Miss Parfait, as a personal favor to an old friend, you really must reserve me a distributor position.
His syrupy enthusiasm turns your stomach, but Parfait doesn't even blink. She shakes his hand smoothly as she replies.

speaker: Parfait
content: Of course, I could never forget my old friends here in Eastside.

speaker: Richard
content: That's wonderful to hear. You have my sincerest wishes for your venture's success, and do keep me apprised of any favorable developments, won't you?

After exchanging a few more pleasantries, the two impeccably dressed patrons bid Parfait a performatively reluctant farewell, waving as they withdraw. But the instant her back turns, their expressions melt into something oddly amused.

Not that you're surprised. From the moment you and Parfait walked into this Eastside gallery, you became the center of gravity—Investment Guru Parfait, miraculously returned, and the MBCC Chief, side by side. An irresistible spectacle.
Even now, murmurs ripple through the space, eyes flicking your way constantly.

options: Who were those two just now?

speaker: Parfait
content: That man is the Executive Director of the McLenn Foundation. I've crossed paths with him at a few dinner gatherings. Strictly speaking, I suppose you could consider him a competitor of mine... After all, they have rather close ties with Nirvana.
Then why did you spend so much time talking with them?

speaker: Parfait
content: Well, I'll admit the social etiquette in Eastside's high society can be rather tedious. Still, I do believe it's essential to uphold a certain level of decorum.
Even while talking to you, Parfait keeps smiling and offering gracious nods to acknowledge the crowd around you both.
Having to smile through all that passive-aggressiveness... That must be exhausting.

speaker: Parfait
content: Oh, it isn't so terrible, really. Not everyone is like that. I've been fortunate to make some genuine friends here...
As she talks, her eyes light on who she's looking for in the crowd. She waves enthusiastically to a man and a woman standing nearby.

speaker: Parfait
content: Hans, Ava?! Oh my goodness, it's been so long! ...Please excuse me for just a moment. I must pop over and say hello to my friends.
Clearly, these two must be the genuine friends Parfait mentioned. But you don't plan to wait around like she asked. You're here to watch her, after all.
However, just as you're about to follow Parfait to hear exactly what she plans to discuss with her "genuine friends," a voice calls out from behind you.

speaker: Richard
content: A pleasure to meet you, Chief.
You turn, and there he is: the same man who was talking with Parfait earlier. He flashes you a beaming smile, leaning in a little too close as he strikes up conversation like you're old friends.

speaker: Richard
content: You see, our dear investment guru is always like this, effortlessly gliding between celebrities and tycoons...

speaker: Richard
content: Allow me to introduce myself. I'm Richard McLenn, Executive Director of the McLenn Foundation. As far as I know, you rarely grace social gatherings such as this one. And arriving as the renowned Miss Parfait's companion... makes it all the more unusual.

speaker: Richard
content: If I may be so bold as to ask, do we find ourselves graced with your presence for some particular purpose?
You resist the urge to roll your eyes. This is, after all, where Eastside's elite mingle—no sense in making enemies needlessly. So you force a perfunctory smile and explain.
I've got some confidential business to handle. Running into Parfait was just a coincidence.
Richard arches a brow, his expression knowing. He's likely already pieced together that you're here to watch Parfait. But since you shut it down first, he's too tactful to press the issue further.

speaker: Richard
content: I see... Though I have to admit, I'm quite curious whether our dear investment guru will get what she's after this time.
Now that piques your interest.
You mean...?

speaker: Richard
content: The Spring Concert tickets, naturally. It's the premier social event of the season that virtually all of Eastside's elite will attend. This would be such a convenient opportunity for Miss Parfait to... reacquaint herself with old friends she hasn't seen in ages. Unfortunately...
Unfortunately?

speaker: Richard
content: Unfortunately, VIP seats are impossible to come by these days. Tulip Holdings is mired in crisis, and the investment guru herself is drowning in scandal. Well... let's just say she shouldn't expect many warm welcomes. I do fear she'll find herself leaving empty-handed.
Seeing that his words have piqued your interest, Richard continues in a lowered voice.

speaker: Richard
content: I'm sure you're aware of Parfait's questionable background. In her early years, she was quite inseparable from certain Syndican circles, and even during recent years, she's been using her so-called "Parfait's Dinner Party" as an excuse to bring all sorts of suspicious characters into establishments far above their usual standing.

speaker: Richard
content: The Eastside consensus these days is that Tulip Holdings' remarkable financial reports in its early years were... shall we say, purely due to her shady dealings with Syndicate gangsters. Money laundering, if we're being blunt.

speaker: Richard
content: How fortunate, then, that your decisive interventions completely restructured those organizations. Syndicate has entered a new era, and that, quite coincidentally, severed her original revenue streams. That's why she announced her plans to "develop an Outland Hypercube mine" six months ago.

speaker: Richard
content: A shame, of course. The investment guru's golden reputation is now completely tarnished. And once panic selling begins? Well. No fund, no matter how pristine, survives a full-blown stampede.
You have no interest in this tedious mix of slander and flattery, offering noncommittal hums and nods while stealing glances at Parfait, who is deep in animated conversation with her two friends.
But the man's too wrapped up in his own enthusiasm to notice your half-hearted responses, riding high on whatever point he's trying to make.

speaker: Richard
content: Any real businessman can spot that Outland Hypercube mine of hers for the folly it is. Meanwhile, our West District operations have already begun actual extraction. Naturally, we Eastside investors have been... keen to participate. Yet somehow, Rustfire maintains such exclusive control, and we've never found a way in...

speaker: Richard
content: Chief, given your... exceptional rapport with the West District, we were hoping you might facilitate an introduction... Consider it our way of contributing to our sister district's reconstruction efforts.

The second he says it, you almost snap. Another Eastside opportunist eyeing the West District's Hypercube mining, just like the dozens before him. Every last one has been a vulture, circling for profit, never lifting a finger unless there's something in it for them. You've grown so sick of it.
Eager to get over to Parfait's side, you offer a perfunctory response.
This could be tough to set up. I'll ask around, but I can't promise anything concrete.

speaker: Richard
content: I'll be counting on you, then. By the way, Spring Concert VIP tickets are quite hard to come by, but I happen to have some connections in that circle. Would you like me to have someone send a few your way...
Without waiting for Richard to respond, you wave your hand dismissively.
I have to go now. Excuse me.
You escape Richard's attention and weave through the gallery, taking the long way around before finally approaching Parfait's group.
As you arrive, the young man among them continues chatting with infectious enthusiasm, his excitement and joy appearing completely genuine.

speaker: Hans
content: ...And then I met the artist himself in the auction house's VIP room. You'll never believe this: the genius behind that masterpiece is barely twenty years old, just some ordinary Syndicate kid like any other street rat you'd pass without noticing.

speaker: Parfait
content: Hans, you know what I always say. Art doesn't care where you come from. Real talent and beautiful virtues can shine through in anyone, no matter their background.

speaker: Hans
content: Come now, I couldn't disagree more. How many generations does it take Syndicate to produce a talent like this? And let's be honest, without connoisseurs like ourselves to recognize his worth, those Syndicate paupers would probably be selling his masterpieces as wrapping paper...

speaker: Ava
content: Honestly, you two... Must you argue about this every time? You're giving me such a headache...
The elegantly dressed woman beside them interrupts Hans and Parfait's endless debate.

speaker: Ava
content: Parfait, I was so sorry to hear about your partner's disappearance and those dreadful debts. How is Tulip Holdings faring?

speaker: Hans
content: Just rest assured, Ava. This is Parfait we're talking about—the so-called investment guru for good reason. When have you ever seen her fail?Business ups and downs are always temporary...

speaker: Ava
content: You should know both the Financial Inspection Team and Nirvana have Parfait under close watch now. And I've heard that your uncle's been spreading rumors to depress Tulip's stock while quietly accumulating shares on the secondary market... At this rate, they might completely edge Parfait out.

speaker: Parfait
content: Don't worry about me.
Faced with her deeply concerned friend, Parfait maintains her characteristic confidence.

speaker: Parfait
content: This stage does need some tactical adjustments, but I've already mapped out all the next steps for the business strategy. Once next quarter's financials are out, the pressure should ease on its own.

speaker: Parfait
content: But let's not dwell on that now. Ava, any updates on those tickets I mentioned?

speaker: Ava
content: Of course I wouldn't forget.
Ava reaches into her handbag and produces a black matte ticket bordered in gold before handing it over to Parfait.

speaker: Hans
content: Holy ****, a VIP ticket?! a VIP ticket?! How on earth did you score one this late?

speaker: Ava
content: It's from my father.
For a moment, you catch a flash of shock and embarrassment on Parfait's face that she fails to hide.

speaker: Parfait
content: I... I really shouldn't take this.

speaker: Ava
content: Why not? You know these events aren't really my sort of thing. After last month's breakup, I'm hardly in concert-going spirits anyway. Father practically insisted I take it. If you hadn't returned, I likely would've passed it along as a favor to someone else.

speaker: Hans
content: Oh? Since when have you disliked these events?

speaker: Ava
content: Oh, quiet you! This is a prime seat. You'll be right next to Sheffield from the Financial Inspection Team, Prosecutor Eddie, and my father...

speaker: Hans
content: Well, I'll be damned, Parfait, this ticket is practically tailor-made for you.Her old man's the primary investor behind Tulip Holdings, isn't he? You two really should have a proper chat.
Parfait's gaze flickers anxiously, her words tripping over themselves.

speaker: Parfait
content: Oh, but that's... that's not quite... what we agreed on. We said regular tickets would be fine. And actually, I was hoping to bring a few friends along. Just one ticket wouldn't be enough...

speaker: Hans
content: Enough about the regular tickets. When you were on top, you could parade your dodgy entourage through the cheap seats and they'd still hail you as the investment guru for being unconventional. But this isn't the time for stubbornness.

speaker: Hans
content: Look at these absurd rumors circulating about you now—"Tulip Holdings involved with illegal Syndicate operations?" Tch, half of Eastside can't claim clean hands themselves...

speaker: Hans
content: But to call you some Syndicate con artist, always lurking in the slums? That's what truly disgusts me. The sheer lack of thought, as if someone of your caliber could ever be mistaken for their gutter trash.
The smooth-talking socialite you've been watching finally drops his carefree act. His playful expression fades as he gazes at Parfait, his voice uncharacteristically earnest.

speaker: Hans
content: Listen, Parfait, whatever people are saying out there, we believe in you. Ava, me, all of your friends. That's not changing. You're not getting through this crisis alone. Count on that.

speaker: Ava
content: Exactly. Your first priority now is maintaining calm with both the Financial Inspection Team and Nirvana, while reassuring investors and partners. Which is precisely why you need this ticket more than anyone else.
Ava presses the ticket firmly into Parfait's hand.

speaker: Ava
content: Oh, by the way, Hans and I have a dinner engagement later with Sheffield and his group. Would you like to join us?
Parfait falls silent, the VIP ticket clutched in her hand as she offers a bitter smile. Having noticed your arrival since a while ago, she glances instinctively in your direction.

speaker: Parfait
content: Oh, no thank you... but I'll have to pass for now.
Her two friends turn to look at you in unison. The warm concern they have shown Parfait melts into perfectly practiced smiles. Hans even inclines his head in a polite greeting.

speaker: Hans
content: Well then, we won't keep you any longer. See you at the concert.
As they pass by, you catch Hans murmuring to Ava in a hushed voice.

speaker: Hans
content: See, stop worrying. She's even got the MBCC Chief on her side now. Parfait is more resourceful than we gave her credit for...
You watch the two wealthy young people walk away until they disappear from view, then finally approach Parfait.
Hey, what's going on? You've got your ticket, but you still look pretty down.
Parfait's face is etched with bitterness.

speaker: Parfait
content: But I... from the very beginning, I wanted to bring my friends along with me.
She holds up the gleaming gilded concert ticket, furrowing her brow as she lets out a long sigh.

speaker: jojo
content: No matter how amazing a VIP ticket is, it can't fit more than ten people...
...More than ten people?
Parfait stands frozen in place, silent for a long while. Her fingers twist absently through her hair, disheveling what had been a carefully styled arrangement.
I could help?

speaker: Parfait
content: But how? At this point... even regular tickets are impossible to come by...
That Richard you just spoke with came by earlier, trying to give me some tickets.
He looks pretty gullible. Want me to go ask him for you?

speaker: Parfait
content: Really?!
Parfait's head jerks up, her eyes lighting up for just a second before she catches herself. The hope vanishes as she narrows her eyes, leaning back with new suspicion.

speaker: Parfait
content: Wait, what do you want in return?
You know how it is in my line of work. We're a naturally curious bunch. And I have to say, I'm particularly interested in these "more than ten friends" you're planning to invite.
How about this: you share who they are, and I'll help you out. Sounds good?
The moment those words leave your mouth, Parfait's expectant expression shatters, suspicion flooding in to take its place.

speaker: Parfait
content: Then... then please don't trouble yourself over this. I'll figure something out on my own...
With the West District business wrapped up smoothly today, you're now left with half a day to spare, and you already know how to spend it.
Parfait's evasiveness about her past—and those mysterious friends of hers—has only sharpened your curiosity. If she won't talk, you'll find the answers yourself.

Based on what you've learned from days of investigation and grilling Eastside reporters for leads, it takes you several hours to locate a run-down apartment building. By the time you match the address in your notes to a faded door number, night shadows stretch long across the hallway.
It's a typical wooden apartment door you'd see anywhere in the West District—plain, weathered, and indistinguishable from any other.
The narrow hallway is choked with debris and layered in dust, yet the space before this door stands conspicuously swept clean. Someone's been here recently.
You knock. Seconds stretch into silence. When no answer comes, your hand drifts toward the handle.
Clack!

The lock gives way—whether from years of decay or forced entry, you can't say. Just a gentle twist, and the latch releases with a shudder. Something metal drops into the shadows as the door groans open.
Clank!
The metallic clatter ricochets down the concrete corridor. Flustered, you spin around, only to discover someone standing right behind you.
You quickly raise both hands to show you mean no harm, but it's already too late.
Don't move!
A sharp shout jolts you upright. Within moments, neighbors begin to cluster around, drawn by the disturbance and already buzzing with speculation.
What's going on? Did someone break in?
Doesn't look like it...
So another one of those Eastside ************s? Great, just what we needed. Has nobody ever taught you people it's rude as hell to barge into folks' homes uninvited?

The hallway lights have been dead for years, leaving the late-night darkness thick enough to hide the neighbors' faces. Not that you need to see them clearly. The rolling pins and kitchen knives in their hands tell you everything you need to know.
Just tie them up and send them to the Executive Committee...
Send 'em my ass! Hell, how many have we sent there this month already? Screw talking. Just rough 'em up and throw 'em out on their ears. That'll make 'em learn to stay gone.
What's all the racket? That home got broken into again?
An elderly man shuffles up the stairs, his flashlight beam trembling ahead of him between raspy coughs. As he speaks, the surrounding commotion gradually dies down.
Now listen here, don't you Eastside meddlers got anything better to do than creep around at this hour pulling this kinda nonsense!

How many times do we have to tell you? There's nothing here for you. But you never listen, just keep forcing your way into that home in the middle of the night. And now look at you, caught red-handed again.
The flashlight's glare blinds you for a moment. You wince, instinctively closing your eyes.
You know what they say—enough is enough. If I let you off easy this time, you'll just... Wait a minute. Do I know you from somewhere?
Hey, I've seen you on TV... Hold on, aren't you that, uh... what's the name again? Right, the MBCC Chief!
Apparently, your reputation in the West District still carries weight. When the neighbors realize who you are, they quickly untie you and usher you into the elderly man's apartment.

speaker: Rayden
content: Sorry about that, Chief. Just a simple misunderstanding, that's all. We've had some shady sorts skulking about after dark lately. Got everyone on edge, you see... Cyllis, be a dear and fetch the Chief some water.
The elderly man across from you—Rayden, you've since learned—sits with a polite but slightly embarrassed air, sighing between apologies. It's clear he's the one calling the shots in this building.
It's alright. However you slice it, me breaking into a place at night is pretty suspicious behavior.

speaker: Cyllis
content: Have some water, Chief.
The girl who first found you walks over from the kitchen, carrying a glass.
Thank you.
You accept the water and fake a sip—old habits die hard. They might be simple-hearted West District locals, honest as the day is long, but you've been burned too often to drop your guard now.
Speaking of which, I've been wondering something. Were all the people who broke in here at night before Eastsiders?

speaker: Rayden
content: Who said that?!
Old Rayden stiffens, his gaze whipping around before zeroing in on a burly young man, the same guy who threatened to "rough you up" earlier.
No, no, I was just talking nonsense...
Before the young man can finish, Cyllis silences him with a stern glare.
The people before me were probably all from Eastside, but I think there's been a misunderstanding. They were basically just reporters or investigators.
