As for me, I'm here for the same reason they were, to look into someone called "Parfait Medici"...
You lay out your intentions with no attempt to soften them. Everyone in the room suddenly falls silent, the air growing so still it feels almost eerie.

speaker: Cyllis
content: Who is Parfait Medici? One of you Eastsiders too?
Hard to say. That's what she calls herself, but lately Eastsiders don't seem to buy it.
So you're here to arrest this... what's-her-name, Parfait Medici? What's she even done that is bad enough to drag you all the way out here?

speaker: Cyllis
content: ED HOUSE—
Whether it's his loose tongue or his lack of manners that set her off, Cyllis grinds out the young man's full name through clenched teeth, her voice low but seething.
She's just involved in some financial disputes back in Eastside. Since reports indicate she's a Sinner, I thought I'd check it out myself... Nothing too serious.

speaker: Ed
content: Oh, nothing serious? That's good then...

speaker: Rayden
content: Cough...
The old man nearby finally loses patience with the young man's clumsy act and clears his throat pointedly.

speaker: Rayden
content: Chief, this Parfait Medici you mentioned... I'm afraid the name doesn't ring a bell. But we respect what you're doing here, and if there's any way we can help, you can count on us...

speaker: Rayden
content: How about this? Let's call it a day for now. We'll keep our eyes peeled for this... Parfait Medici. Anything comes up, you'll be the first to know.
The name doesn't ring a bell, huh...
You stroke your chin, adopting a convincingly troubled expression.
But here's the thing, I checked the residential records with the Executive Committee, and it's right there in black and white. The owner listed for that upstairs apartment is "Parfait."

speaker: Rayden
content: Uh, well...
They probably never expected you to extract anything useful from the West District's notoriously messy registration system. Everyone in the room falls silent, momentarily at a loss for words.

speaker: Ed
content: ...Look, just 'cause the names are similar doesn't prove anything, y'know? And honestly, "Parfait" sounds way better than whatever... "Parfait Medici." Pfft, who even came up with that?

speaker: Cyllis
content: Anyway, that apartment's been empty for years. Nobody even knows who's supposed to be the owner.
It's been empty for years?
But when the door opened earlier, I got a quick look inside. Everything looked clean and tidy, not abandoned at all.
Your words hang in the air as the neighbors exchange uneasy glances. The silence stretches, their faces tightening with visible concern.
Then you catch it. Cyllis's eyes keep flicking toward the kitchen. Toward the rolling pin. Whatever they're hiding about Parfait, they're prepared to defend that secret firmly.
The atmosphere turns increasingly hostile as their stares harden. You know you need to talk your way out of this fast, before they graduate from menacing silence to something far more violent.
Hey, easy everyone. Don't worry, I'm not here to arrest Parfait. If anything, it's the opposite. We're actually friends...

speaker: Ed
content: Oh, you're friends? Geez, you should've led with that...
Not so easily convinced, Cyllis cuts Ed off with a firm hand. Without you noticing, she's already palmed the rolling pin, tucking it casually behind her back.

speaker: Cyllis
content: So if you're this Parfait's friend, what exactly are you doing here?

She got into some trouble half a year ago. Now the Eastsiders are claiming she's actually some con artist from the West District, connected to that big counterfeiting case a few years back. That's why she asked me to wipe any evidence that could be used against her.

speaker: Cyllis
content: Oh? She asked you, an Eastside "enforcer," to "wipe evidence" for her? This Parfait must be seriously connected.
Clearly, Cyllis isn't buying your story. She brings the rolling pin forward, holding it at the ready now. Her gaze locks onto yours—steady, unblinking—and the air grows thick with tension.
A long beat passes. Then, from beside the table, comes a weary sigh.

speaker: Rayden
content: Alright... Just drop it, all of you. If the Chief came alone, everything must already be figured out. No sense hiding the truth now...

speaker: Rayden
content: Everyone just settle down. Really now, you want to keep the Chief around for good? Then we're not just talking about fraud anymore. Parfait'd be facing much heavier charges.
As the elder's voice fills the room, the tension finally drains away. Cyllis's grip on the rolling pin loosens, her arms slowly lowering to her sides.

speaker: Rayden
content: Just one thing still has me wondering, Chief. Would you mind telling me how Parfait got found out?

speaker: Rayden
content: That counterfeiting business was years back now. And if I recall right, that girl made sure to pay back every cent the moment she could, didn't she?
She did that?
As if desperate to prove a point, Ed quickly jumps in.

speaker: Ed
content: Exactly! She's way too nice for her own good, never scammed the same mark twice, and if she ever took a bit too much, she'd beat herself up over it. Soon as she had cash, she'd quietly pay people back. Next to those Eastside sharks, she might as well be a saint!

speaker: Ed
content: If you ask me, it's definitely those fancy hobbies of hers that screwed her—always rubbing elbows with those Eastsiders. Tsk, she never stopped to think... since when do poor Syndicate folks like us get to mess around with fancy art?

speaker: Cyllis
content: She even called me just a few days ago, asking us to go to some Eastside concert with her...
Cyllis presses her palm on her forehead, looking exasperated.

speaker: Cyllis
content: Back when she was riding high, making bank for Eastsiders, nobody asked too many questions. But after what went down six months ago? Suddenly they're digging up every skeleton in her closet.
Perhaps with their defenses lowered, the complaints come pouring out, with everyone venting their frustrations at once.

speaker: Cyllis
content: Ever since that phone call, this place has been crawling with more snoops in two weeks than we usually see in half a year.

speaker: Rayden
content: ...Not that I've got anything against concerts. I watch it myself on TV every New Year when there's nothing better to do. But this timing... ah, really couldn't be worse.

speaker: Rayden
content: If we go with her, those fancy types will just look down their noses at us! Look what's happening to Parfait over in Eastside, getting hounded day and night. She'd do better coming back to the West District. At least here, she still has us watch her back.

speaker: Ed
content: Yeah, she'd be better off coming back! Getting pushed around and investigated in Eastside, might as well just come back here... Oh right, Chief!
The young man's head jerks up as if he's just remembered something vital. When he turns to you, his expression is disarmingly earnest.

speaker: Ed
content: You're friends with Parfait, right? Why don't you talk to her? Tell her to quit running with those fancy Eastside types and just come back home.
Ed doesn't even finish his sentence before the entire room zeroes in on you. Hope flashes across their faces, but it's edged with unease.
Still, this does give you a convenient way out of the situation. Of course, you also suspect that if you refused, given how close they are to Parfait, they probably wouldn't just let you walk away.
...All right. I'll try.
The day after returning to the Bureau, you find yourself wrestling with how to bring this matter up with Parfait.
The locals from the West District aren't really as simple as they appear. That tense meeting last night made it clear: refusing them wasn't an option. Not if you wanted to walk away.
You have given your word, and you don't plan to break it. But coming clean to Parfait would mean admitting you've been investigating her behind the scenes.

After spending these days together, you've come to realize that Parfait isn't some scheming villain. If anything, she's surprisingly genuine—witty, cooperative, even good company. She already promised you she'd cooperate with the investigation after the Spring Concert. The more you think about it, the more this secrecy sits uneasily with you.
With this in mind, you head to Parfait's temporary room, only to find it empty. A full sweep of the Bureau later, you finally spot her in the mail room.

speaker: Parfait
content: Good morning, Chief.
Parfait greets you politely before opening the envelope in her hands, revealing a thick stack of tickets inside.

speaker: Parfait
content: Phew... Thank goodness he wasn't fooling me.
After confirming the tickets are legitimate, she exhales in relief.
Wow, how did you even get these?

speaker: Parfait
content: I reached out to someone from the event organizers and spent forever going back and forth with him. He asked me to give a speech on stage and tried to get me to trade for the VIP ticket. Honestly, even over the phone, I could tell that guy was shady.

speaker: Parfait
content: But luckily, I managed to swap for twelve regular tickets... and I saved one for you! What do you think? Would you like to come with me?
Under Parfait's pure, hopeful gaze, you feel a twinge of guilt and dodge giving her a straight answer.
I'm happy for you, Parfait. Now you can take Rayden and the others to the Spring Concert.

speaker: Parfait
content: Yeah, finally! After taking quite a bit of effort...
One moment she is animatedly recounting all the trouble she has gone through, but then—mid-sentence—she falls silent, her hand slowly lowering the tickets she's been waving in the air.

speaker: Parfait
content: So... you went to see them, didn't you?

speaker: Parfait
content: No need to apologize.

speaker: Parfait
content: ...In the end, no deception is ever truly perfect. Sooner or later, the truth always comes out. And honestly? My identity was full of holes from the very beginning.
As she speaks, Parfait slides the tickets back into the envelope and meets your gaze.

speaker: Parfait
content: Let's find somewhere else to talk, Chief.

speaker: Parfait
content: By the way... you didn't let slip anything unnecessary, did you?
Once back in the room, you quietly close the door behind you. Before you can even ask a question, Parfait speaks up first.
What do you mean by anything unnecessary?

speaker: Parfait
content: For instance, your opinion on the concert and things like that.
No.
Parfait lets out a sigh of relief, then offers a bitter smile as she explains.

speaker: Parfait
content: Oh, thank goodness you didn't. They're already so hesitant about the concert. If they caught even a whiff of disinterest in you, they'd have the perfect excuse to back out.

speaker: Parfait
content: "Look, even the MBCC Chief doesn't want to go, so why should we bother?" Something like that... By the way, how are they doing now?
They seemed normal enough, except for apparently helping with your cover. They were being pretty cautious about it.

speaker: Parfait
content: I see...
At the mention of this topic, Parfait sets the folder down on the table and slumps into her chair, completely deflated.

speaker: Parfait
content: So you've found out... Yes, I'm from the West District, and the whole Medici family heir identity is fake. Honestly, I made it up on the spot! But people actually bought it, so I just went with it and forged a complete set of identity documents...

speaker: Parfait
content: I did counterfeit money. It was around N.F. 108... Once in February I made ten thousand DisCoins to buy some decent clothes, and once in April I made a hundred thousand to pay a hotel bill.

speaker: Parfait
content: Later, with my new identity and those clothes, I became a stockbroker and started earning money... And don't worry, once I could, I made sure to pay back both the tailor and the hotel for their losses.
Wait, you're telling me that huge Eastside counterfeiting case from a few years back only involved a hundred and ten thousand DisCoins total?

speaker: Parfait
content: I swear on my life, not a penny more! Honestly, the fake cash I whipped up with my Sinner ability was too good. When they stumbled on bills with duplicate serial numbers and couldn't tell them apart from the real ones, the whole market freaked...

speaker: Parfait
content: I was terrified when it happened. Me? Accidentally crashing economies? Not exactly the legacy I was going for, so I never dared touch counterfeiting again after that.
Seeing the once-glorious investment guru now reduced to this pitiful state in front of you, you can't help but feel amused as you ask.
Is that all there is to your criminal record?

speaker: Parfait
content: I... think so? If you're going to accuse me of cheating investors after I became a stockbroker... but I made them huge profits every single time... Honestly, I have no idea why things worked out that way. I don't really understand professional finance, so I just went with my gut.

speaker: Parfait
content: And somehow... it worked every single time. I practically just tripped into becoming the "investment guru." But as my reputation grew over the past few years, I barely dared make any moves. Too terrified my luck would finally run out and get myself exposed...

speaker: Parfait
content: Honestly, I'm not shocked at all that you uncovered my whole story. The real miracle is that it took this long! I suppose it's because I finally stepped on the toes of the major financial players, so they finally decided I was worth their serious attention.

speaker: Parfait
content: It was fine as long as they weren't paying attention, but the moment they took notice, Nirvana just swatted me down like some bothersome fly...
When she finishes, Parfait sighs heavily, deflating like a punctured balloon.

speaker: Parfait
content: *Sigh*... it's too late for anything now. The others don't really matter much. At worst, they just lost back the money they'd made from me over the years. And when they realized the party was over, they grabbed their pitchforks and joined the mob. Can't even blame them—I'd probably do the same.

speaker: Parfait
content: But those friends who have actually believed in me... That's what kills me. While I was gone, they kept throwing money into Tulip Holdings, trying to help me keep it alive. I'm afraid I'll never be able to repay them, not in my entire lifetime...

speaker: Parfait
content: In our line of work, everything comes down to trust and credibility. My "investment guru" halo is already tarnished beyond repair. No one will ever believe anything I do again...
The more Parfait speaks, the deeper she sinks into her chair, as if trying to disappear entirely.
Then wouldn't all the effort you made traveling all this way back here be completely wasted?

speaker: Parfait
content: Hey, that's not right. How is it wasted?
Parfait suddenly straightens up, pointing to the envelop filled with tickets on the table.

speaker: Parfait
content: I never expected to salvage anything anyway. Otherwise, how could I have stayed in the Outlands for half a year...

speaker: Parfait
content: This time, I'm just back to take my friends to the Spring Concert. As long as I achieve that goal, that's all that matters. Everything else is already beyond my control, no matter how hard I try.

Parfait's answer leaves you stunned. Could there really be financial criminals in this world who return to cities where they're wanted—not to clear their name or save their business, but just to attend a concert?
Then again, you recall your first meeting with Parfait on the sand ship, where she seemed to have said the same thing.

speaker: Parfait
content: Speaking of which, I actually came back specifically for this year's Spring Concert. A fine gentleman as yourself surely wouldn't miss it, would you?
female_content: Speaking of which, I actually came back specifically for this year's Spring Concert. A fine lady as yourself surely wouldn't miss it, would you?

content: Well, no matter how absurd her reason might be, she's been completely honest with you about everything. At least right now, she has no reason to lie.
But... Rayden and the others said they didn't want to go to the concert...

speaker: Parfait
content: WHAT?!
Parfait springs from her seat, her voice shooting up an octave.
Their exact words were: they're not interested in the concert, and given their... well, their status, they'd probably just get looks from the wealthy crowd if they went.
Despite claiming to quote them exactly, you still try to make their expression sound less harsh than it actually was.
Rayden mentioned you're always welcome back. Whatever crisis you're dealing with right now, as long as they're around, you'll never be...

speaker: Parfait
content: No, no...
Before you can finish, Parfait cuts you off with visible agitation.

speaker: Parfait
content: Wait, hold on! But this is never about status!

speaker: Parfait
content: This is the Spring Concert, DisCity's crown jewel of New Year celebrations! Not to mention this year features the most dazzling lineup in history, topped with Maestro Euragio's farewell performance!

speaker: Parfait
content: If I could attend just one live event in my entire life, this would be it. At this level of artistry? It's not just a performance, it's a legacy. What does wealth or social status matter when history's being made?!
Seeing your silence, Parfait suddenly slumps back into her chair.

speaker: Parfait
content: I don't care how, but you've got to help me out.

speaker: Parfait
content: Let my reputation be ruined. I've had my fill of glory anyway. After the concert, I'll cooperate with any investigation... Hand me over to Nirvana in chains if you must, I won't resist.

speaker: Parfait
content: But this concert is the one thing I cannot miss. And I especially can't bear the thought of my friends missing it... Please, could you do me this favor and try to convince them for me?
Seeing the former investment guru throw all composure to the wind, practically demanding your help with such undignified desperation, you can't decide whether to laugh or pity her.
In a way, she and her friends are remarkably alike. At least when it comes to asking for your help, neither shows any reservations.
...Okay, I'll see what I can do.
And so, Parfait brings along her whole crew of West District friends—plus you, dragged along against your better judgment—to attend the annual Spring Concert.

speaker: Ed
content: Ugh, this stupid suit collar's choking me. Rich people's clothes really are all just for show...
Cyllis wears a beautiful cocktail dress, though she seems equally uneasy, her voice dropping to a hushed tone as she speaks.

speaker: Cyllis
content: You think you're the only one feeling uncomfortable? Please, the rest of us are sucking it up too. Eastsiders got eyes everywhere.

Old Rayden, by contrast, remains relatively composed. After all, he is from an older generation of the West District residents, one that has lived through the district's golden age. He's seen his fair share of the world.
Still, the hostile glares from the surrounding Eastsiders unsettle even him, and he keeps fiddling with his tie without realizing it.

speaker: Ed
content: Tch, it's not just these guys down here. Even those rich pricks up in the fancy seats are getting their kicks watching us squirm. Seriously, what's the damn point of us even being here?

speaker: Rayden
content: We're already here.
Old Rayden gives you a worried glance, concerned that being seen with them might embarrass you too. After all, it took considerable persuasion on your part to get them all to come tonight...

speaker: Ed
content: No freakin' way! Parfait's gone completely off the rails still hung up on that damn concert. Seriously?! You gotta be kidding me!

speaker: Rayden
content: That's right, Chief. I know Parfait's all about those fancy arts and performances. If she wants to go by herself, that's her business. But hauling a bunch of us along when we don't even have proper clothes to wear...

speaker: Cyllis
content: Besides, she's already walking on thin ice. If we show up, her cover's toast for sure. After that? No way she could ever go back to Eastside, even if she wanted to.
Hold on... Let's address these concerns one at a time.
First, Parfait has already arranged formal outfits for you guys to wear to the performance.

speaker: Rayden
content: Such a waste of money... And it's not like she's flush with cash these days, is she?
Well... custom formal wear can't be returned. Even if you don't go, Parfait wouldn't get any money back.

speaker: Rayden
content: What? That's...
About Parfait's identity situation, don't worry about that anymore. Truth is, even Parfait has stopped caring about it at this point.
Right now, she's completely surrounded by enemies over in Eastside. They're literally everywhere, and she genuinely needs your protection.

I've done all the convincing you asked me to do, and Parfait didn't raise any objections. Once we're done with this performance, if Eastside really becomes too dangerous for her, she'll probably come back here.

speaker: Cyllis
content: I guess... that's fine.

speaker: Ed
content: Hell no! You wanna go make fools of yourselves? Be my guest! But I'm not walking into Eastside just to get looked down on!
This is the one thing you truly can't control. You can handle all the other practical problems, but there's no way to influence how the Eastsiders will see them.
So you grit your teeth...
...And agree to attend the concert with them, to "lend them some backing."

Almost immediately, you regret it. You really don't want to go. No matter how the others feel, you know your own experience will be miserable. At the very least, those speculators—the ones desperate to get a cut of the West District Hypercube mining operation—wouldn't miss the chance to corner you after the show.

speaker: Ed
content: Ugh, this stupid collar. I wanna just tear it right off! Look at Chief over there, all relaxed in regular clothes and a hat. Way better than being stuck in this stuffy getup.

You shrink back slightly, guilt creeping in. Before coming here, you debated for ages but ultimately decided to put together a disguise, hoping the Eastside merchants upstairs and downstairs wouldn't recognize you.
It goes against your promise to lend them some backing... but, well, better safe than sorry!

speaker: Neighboring Concertgoer
content: Look, there's the investment guru with her Syndicate friends...
And karma has already caught up with you. The murmuring around you is becoming too loud to ignore.

speaker: Neighboring Concertgoer
content: Hmph... They could wrap themselves in the finest silks and still reek of commonness. Some things simply can't be polished away.

speaker: Neighboring Concertgoer
content: You'll never guess what the investment guru has done now. She actually sold the VIP ticket Miss Ava graciously gave her, just to drag along that ragtag entourage she calls friends.

speaker: Neighboring Concertgoer
content: Oh, really? The New Year's address later is meant to be hers, isn't it? My my, how the mighty have tumbled.

speaker: Neighboring Concertgoer
content: Haha, don't you know? When Mr. McLenn and those other investors who lost money found out Parfait was bringing Syndicans, they deliberately set this whole thing up.

speaker: Neighboring Concertgoer
content: Shh, keep your voice down. The Syndicans might hear...

speaker: Neighboring Concertgoer
content: So what? They could brave appearing in this place, but my words are suddenly too much for their fragile sensibilities?
You watch as Ed slams his hand against the armrest beside you. If Cyllis weren't holding him down, he'd be on his feet in an instant.

Meanwhile, Parfait, the one truly at the eye of the storm, sits at the front of your group, seemingly oblivious. Her attention remains fixed on the slowly rising curtain, her gaze never wavering for even a second.

speaker: Neighboring Concertgoer
content: Look at that idiot. One little remark and he's already fuming.

speaker: Neighboring Concertgoer
content: Careful now. They might beat you up.

speaker: Neighboring Concertgoer
content: Don't be absurd. This is Eastside, not some Syndicate gutter where their kind can do as they please...
Veins bulge visibly on Cyllis's forehead now, too. Without hesitation, she snaps off the heel of her shoe and rises to her feet beside Ed, her movements deliberate.
Then, the lighting shifts—and there, under the spotlight, stands a tall, elegant figure.

The thick tension in the air dissipates in an instant. Below the stage, Eastsiders and West District residents alike turn their eyes upward, drawn to the presence now commanding the space. A hush falls over the crowd as they wait for Parfait's first words, each person harboring their own private expectations.

speaker: Parfait
content: Ladies and gentlemen, and to all the brilliant minds tuning in live or catching the rerun, whether you're here with us in person or cozied up at home: a very good morning, afternoon, and evening to you!
Under the spotlight and in front of the cameras, Parfait effortlessly slips back into her role as the legendary investment guru, radiating a remarkable sense of ease and confidence.
A smattering of halfhearted applause rises from the audience. The Eastsiders barely acknowledge her greeting, clapping only to exchange smirks and whispers, clearly waiting for her to stumble.
Unfazed by the lukewarm reception, Parfait keeps her smile steady, patiently waiting for the scattered applause to die down.

speaker: Parfait
content: My name is Parfait, though you likely know me as the "investment guru." A title I find terribly dramatic, but who am I to argue with results? Truthfully, I've just been lucky, always managing to pick the winning side in my investments.
Parfait breaks into a wide grin, her white teeth almost dazzling under the lights.

speaker: Parfait
content: I imagine many of you are wondering... why, of all people, am I the one giving this New Year's address? Well, allow me to explain.

speaker: Parfait
content: Ever since N.F. 108, when stand-up comedian Aaron first delivered that unforgettable speech at the Spring Concert, the organizers have made a tradition of inviting the year's most outstanding comedian to take the stage. And why not? This is the Spring Concert, a joyous occasion where we might as well start the year with laughter. But...

speaker: Parfait
content: Ah, I see those puzzled looks. You're probably thinking: Wait, isn't this woman supposed to be some "investment guru"? What's she got to do with comedy? Well, my dear audience, here's the punchline—

speaker: Parfait
content: Turns out, this so-called "investment guru" spent the second half of the year turning herself into the biggest joke of all.
The moment she says this, the audience erupts in laughter.

speaker: Parfait
content: I invested in a promising venture in the Outlands, only to return to DisCity and find everything in shambles.

speaker: Parfait
content: My business partners? Vanished. The company? Buried under a mountain of bad debts. And if not for Mr. McLenn's generous help, I wouldn't even have scraped together enough for tickets for my friends and myself to attend tonight.
As Parfait speaks, she presses a hand to her heart and gestures toward the VIP seats—a silent "Thank you, McLenn, our friendship lives right here."
The camera cuts to McLenn at the perfect moment. Caught in the swell of cheers and applause, he cannot but nod and flash an awkward smile to the lens.
When the crowd finally settles, the camera swings back to Parfait. Smiling, she lifts the microphone and smoothly moves on.

speaker: Parfait
content: But seriously, what an unforgettable year, don't you think?

speaker: Parfait
content: So much has happened. The highs, the lows, moments that broke our hearts and others that lifted us right back up. How do you even sum up a year like this? "Epic"? "A rollercoaster"? "Shakespearean drama"?

speaker: Parfait
content: ...Forgive me, words fail me sometimes. Then again, as you all know, I am from the West District. We weren't exactly raised on the finest education.

The entire venue goes silent for a beat, then a wave of murmurs ripples through the crowd. The audience didn't expect Parfait to acknowledge the rumors about her past, let alone address them so openly. For a moment, no one seems sure how to react, until someone begins to clap, and the rest follow suit.
Amid the rising applause, Parfait smiles and continues.

speaker: Parfait
content: Fortunately, we still have this Spring Concert, with these extraordinary musicians and the magnificent Maestro Euragio gracing us tonight.

speaker: Parfait
content: And that, my friends, is the magic of music and art. Whether you're an Eastsider, a West District resident, or even an Outlander—whether your pockets are heavy or light, your heart full or aching—music...

speaker: Parfait
content: ...Music has a way of stealing your truest emotions right in the moment. Then, like a master alchemist, it weaves them together with everything we've lived through this year, transforming them into something exquisite. Unforgettable.

speaker: Parfait
content: So, without further ado, ladies and gentlemen, let the N.F. 115 Spring Concert begin!

With a dramatic sweep of her hand, the curtains part behind Parfait, revealing the stage. The atmosphere in the venue reaches fever pitch. After all, the "investment guru's" speeches never fail to captivate, bending even the most reluctant minds to her will.
When she promises the most wonderful music, no one doubts they're about to experience a truly sumptuous musical feast.
With a final smile, Parfait steps off the stage and slips into her seat beside you and the other West District residents.
Then, joyful, magnificent music swells through the air, and the long-awaited concert begins.

The performance continues, one piece seamlessly blending into the next. And in a way, you have to admit, Parfait is right. There's a world of difference between listening to music at home or on a screen and feeling the infectious energy of a live performance.
And that energy works its magic. Slowly, the thick, acrid tension in the air dissolves as the music washes over the crowd, pulling every gaze toward the stage.
When Maestro Euragio, the very musician Parfait has constantly mentioned, steps into the spotlight, you find yourself glancing her way.

Wonder. Satisfaction. Pure, unguarded enjoyment. The woman the Eastsiders whisper about as some "great fraud" is utterly spellbound, her eyes alight with a passion so fierce it's almost too much to take in.
As the maestro takes a deep bow on stage for his final curtain call, the Spring Concert comes to an end.
Parfait is right. This is the kind of performance you can't afford to miss. Anyone who's ever felt music move them—even just a little—will remember this night for years to come.
Amid thunderous applause that lingers long enough to blur your vision, you and the West District group slip out just ahead of the crowd, while the rest of the audience remains lost in the afterglow.

speaker: Ed
content: Doo doo... dee doo dee doo...
Ed starts humming a tune, and you recognize it. It's the last piece the maestro performed.

speaker: Cyllis
content: Not bad humming there, Ed. I didn't know you had that kind of talent.
Ed's face turns red, and he gives Cyllis a flustered shove.

speaker: Ed
content: Oh, cut it out...
Old Rayden loosens the tie he's been adjusting all evening, breathing in the night air as he reflects.

speaker: Rayden
content: It was definitely worth coming. Reminds me of the good old days in the West District...

The group strolls through Eastside's bustling streets, breathing in the night air. Gone are the complaints and frustration they carried when they arrived. Perhaps beautiful music really can cleanse the soul after all.
You catch up to Parfait, eager to ask her the question. Her steps are the lightest of the group, nothing like the composed grace expected of an investment guru.

speaker: Parfait
content: Hmm? What did you say?
She's still lost in the memory of the performance, completely oblivious to your question.
I mean... you really went through all this trouble to come back just for this concert.

speaker: Parfait
content: What else would it be?
Her answer comes so matter-of-factly.

speaker: Parfait
content: Art exhibitions, concerts, exquisite cuisine... I adore them all. But such pleasures are reserved only for the elite.

speaker: Parfait
content: So I schemed my way in—played the fraud, made dirty money, lived in fear of exposure. But I succeeded. And for years, I indulged in every luxury never meant for a West District girl like me.

speaker: Parfait
content: But desire is insatiable. And the more I had, the more I wondered. Why? Why are poor people naturally assumed to be incapable of appreciating art and beauty?

speaker: Parfait
content: Why must humanity's finest creations be gilded cages for the wealthy? I lied, cheated, and bought my way in, so now I'm "worthy." But strip away the silk and jewels, and I'm still that same West District girl.

speaker: Parfait
content: Which is precisely why I brought my West District friends. Marvels like these—why should wealth dictate who gets to enjoy them? The way they listened tonight... wasn't that proof enough?
You glance back at the group behind you. They're still laughing and chatting animatedly about tonight's concert.

speaker: Parfait
content: I've tasted every pleasure and achieved my grandest dream. I suppose my career as a "professional hedonist" hasn't been for nothing... Mm, I have no regrets.

speaker: Parfait
content: So now? Let the reckoning come. Punishment, retribution—I'll face it all.

speaker: Crowd Voices
content: I just saw Parfait! She's right over there!
Chaotic footsteps and shouts erupt behind you. Parfait, who just moments ago wore a look of utter defiance, immediately tries to bolt, but her high heels make running impossible.

speaker: Crowd Voices
content: Are you sure the MBCC Chief was among the people who came with Parfait?

speaker: Crowd Voices
content: One hundred percent! I saw them with my own eyes!

speaker: Crowd Voices
content: Wait, they're that close? I heard the Chief turned down Richard's invite. So he basically gave up VIP perks just to sit with Parfait in the regular seats?

speaker: Crowd Voices
content: Doesn't that mean...

speaker: Crowd Voices
content: It means the Chief's actually tight with her. That woman wasn't arrested by MBCC at all, she's just holed up there keeping a low profile!

speaker: Crowd Voices
content: Hey now, watch how you talk. What do you mean by "that woman"? She's the Investment Guru!

speaker: Crowd Voices
content: You have no idea. That Chief's impossible to work with! Every investor in Eastside, from city council members to major developers, has gotten completely shut out. Nobody's getting anywhere near that Syndicate Hypercube mining deal!

speaker: Crowd Voices
content: Wait a minute... What if Parfait's Hypercube mine was actually just a front? Maybe she's been working with West District all along, pulling some kind of bait-and-switch operation.

speaker: Crowd Voices
content: Who knows? But you all saw her tossing Hypercubes from that helicopter like they were candy, right? Let's be real, nobody just "does investments" and gets to shower the streets with Hypercubes.

speaker: Crowd Voices
content: Hold on... Hypercubes, Syndicans, the MBCC Chief... Damn, this is...

speaker: Crowd Voices
content: Stop talking! There she is! Hurry, don't let her get away!

The West District folks with Parfait also hear the commotion behind them and immediately take defensive positions in front of Parfait, their faces grim as if facing a serious threat, but they are quickly overwhelmed by the surging crowd.

speaker: Crowd Voices
content: Where's the Chief? I'm pretty sure I just saw the Chief here too.
Your reaction is much quicker than theirs. Realizing your disguise won't hold up, you have already slipped into a nearby alley before the crowd has a chance to spot you.
Among the crowd, you can faintly make out two somewhat familiar voices.

speaker: Hans
content: Brilliant work, Parfait! She's about to completely flip the game. Though really, if she was holding cards this good, why didn't she tell us sooner?

speaker: Ava
content: Would telling you even help? With that snooty look you give every Syndican, do you really think you could understand Parfait's methods? That's exactly why she's a legend in the investment world.
Parfait is right again. In their line of work, everything comes down to trust and credibility.

When people don't believe in you, no amount of effort can win them over but only scorn. But when they're utterly convinced of something beyond reason, even the most damning scandals become nothing more than charming tales of intrigue.
With these thoughts, you no longer linger in place, striding forward and vanishing into the alley's shadowy depths.

A few days later, on a morning like any other, you arrive at the cafeteria as usual to find Parfait with coffee in one hand and today's financial news in the other—just like when you first met aboard the sand ship.

speaker: Parfait
content: Good morning, Chief.
I have good news and bad news. Which one do you want to hear first?

speaker: Parfait
content: The bad news, I suppose.
The bad news is, effective immediately, the MBCC cafeteria is no longer available to you.

speaker: Parfait
content: Good heavens! How could this be?!

speaker: Parfait
content: The MBCC cafeteria's cuisine rivals even Eastside's finest three-star establishments, and yet you would... you would actually bar me from these premises... This is truly the most devastating news I've received all year.

speaker: Parfait
content: Please, go on and share your good news. I do hope it might soften the blow.
With dramatic flair, Parfait clutches her chest, though she already knows exactly what the good news is.
The good news is right here.
You point to the front page headline of the financial newspaper in her hand.

speaker: Newspapers
content: "Financial Inspection Team Drops Charges Against Parfait; Tulip Holdings Sees Surge in Investor Backing"

speaker: Parfait
content: Just this? But this cannot possibly heal the trauma of being banished from the MBCC cafeteria.
Alright, enough with the theatrics. Your company's car is already waiting outside. The long, luxurious one.

speaker: Parfait
content: After two whole weeks, it's finally here!

speaker: Parfait
content: Won't you come take a look inside? I had the interior custom-designed by the finest artisans. No expense spared, of course. And I always keep my personal wine selection on hand...
Thanks, but I'll pass.
You decline again with a smile. You still remember how she once confidently promised that a car would pick her up, only to end up shivering in the cold for an hour.
Oh, by the way, Cyllis asked me to deliver a message.

speaker: Parfait
content: Yes?
She said she really liked those high heels you got her, but she ended up breaking them while standing up for you, so she wants you to order her another pair.

speaker: Parfait
content: Leave it to me!
Parfait sets down her coffee cup and stands up.

speaker: Parfait
content: Well, it's time to say goodbye. Thank you for having me during this time. Perhaps fate will allow us to meet again...
Wait a moment. There's still something I want to ask you.

speaker: Parfait
content: Of course. What is it?
Parfait shows no sign of impatience, looking at you with a warm smile.
The more I've thought about it these past few days, the more something feels wrong... I keep feeling like this whole thing has been off from start to finish.
Why, of all people, did you just happen to get a seat right next to me? Why did your business partner run off exactly the day before you returned, making sure I'd see you at your lowest...?
And why the Spring Concert, where every Eastside elite would be gathered? Why was I recognized despite having a clear disguise...
Then it hit me. You're a professional con artist who built your career on lies. What if... what if this was all an act from the start? Some elaborate scheme to gain my sympathy and help?
Faced with your barrage of questions, Parfait is visibly stunned for a moment.
Then, she flashes you an elegant yet sly smile.

speaker: Parfait
content: So, have you suffered any losses? Will you... expose me?

speaker: Man
content: Several indicators dropped in last month's report. That's a concerning trend. After consulting with the doctor, I've decided to adjust your diet, limit your free time, and start a curfew. It's what I need to do, as your dad. You'll understand, won't you?

speaker: Man
content: Your metrics have remained stable all year, which is why I've been buying you all those books you wanted. I suppose this is partly my fault. I forgot about your lack of self-control. Of course you'll stay up late if you get too absorbed in reading.

The man speaks unhurriedly, his tone patient and persuasive. Yet those clinical terms punctuating his speech feel like a pair of tweezers, still cold with the sterilizing alcohol, running along your spine, exposing the cold, utilitarian truth behind that familiar title.

speaker: Man
content: Your health is extremely important, to me and to the family. I know... it's not easy to live by a strict schedule, but compared to those suffering from illness, this is just a small sacrifice. You can keep it up, can't you, sweetheart?
Yes, Dad. The family motto teaches us to strive for the welfare of others. Since I'm the one capable of the job, I will do it. I can handle it.

The practiced response slides from your lips, like you've repeated it hundreds of times before. But looking down, you realize you're unconsciously clutching the book in your arms, your fingers digging into the heavy purple hardcover so hard that your fingertips have turned pale.

Conflicting instincts tear through you, reaching a crescendo when that hand reaches over to extract the heavy novel from your arms. You want to resist, but your muscles fail you, powerless against the authoritative figure's entitled claim.

In the end, the book is taken away. You know what this means. Another germless and joyless day you're forced to spend in your perfectly sterilized room. The soul-devouring monotony is just a minor footnote to your sacrifice.
It's fine... I can do this... This is my purpose. I'm doing something meaningful...

speaker: Woman
content: Too many blood samples within a day? I don't care! All I know is that you can help your brother! So you should! His talents are worth more than ten of you combined! He needs to return quickly so everyone knows our family has a proper heir. That's the only way to stabilize our stock prices!

speaker: Woman
content: I endured nine months of suffering to bring you into this world for this exact purpose! Same reason why the family spends a fortune planning out your life!

I understand, Mother. I'll tell Father my health indicators are perfect, so he needn't worry. I'm willing to continue donating to help Brother recover sooner and make whatever contribution I can to the corporation.

The woman finally seems satisfied. Her critical, harsh gaze sweeps over the bruises and needle marks on your wrist without the slightest pause, only revealing undisguised disgust, like a farmer spotting worm holes in produce.

speaker: Woman
content: At least you know your place and how to make the right choice. Good. You will cooperate when I send the staff here later. If your father ever asks, you'll tell him this was all your idea. Understood?
Yes, Mother.

You watch the red flowing backward through the tube inserted into your vein. Strangely, the slight dizziness clears your mind, detaching you from the moment. In your haze, you see your body withering, your mind being hollowed out, while at the other end of the tube waits a gaping, ravenous mouth.
It's nothing... I can endure it... This is the purpose of my birth, the value of my existence...
Is that true? Is it normal to be born just to be exploited and consumed? Can sacrifice truly be called purpose?
You struggle to reach for the tube to pull it out, but can only manage to lift your hand slightly. The faceless figures bustling around the room don't even notice this tiny act of resistance.

speaker: Young Man
content: You're here. Due to my illness and your health management regimen, we know little about each other. But I've always thought you're smart. I believe you know your place, and when to exit it.

speaker: Young Man
content: I am the leader of our family, and you are a medical resource created to keep me healthy and alive. This arrangement has been unfair to us both, but it has worked out well enough in the past. I believe that alone speaks volumes.

The young man stares at you unflinchingly, a faint flush signaling his recovery on his cheeks. You feel phantom pain shoot through the long-healed needle marks on your arm, instinctively pressing your hand against them.
Arrangement? Whose arrangement?

speaker: Young Man
content: Fate's, of course. Everyone has their assigned role in its grand script, and now a new arrangement has arrived. I no longer require you for my illness, so we're both liberated. I've accepted this, and you should too.

speaker: Young Man
content: I know this isn't easy, but to our family, your existence no longer has any value. You're nothing but a stain now. The last sacrifice you can make for the family is to voluntarily disappear, my sister.

His words negate your entire existence, like a sharp blade severing the tubes that have always been connected to your body. You should feel devastated, but beneath the pain surges an unexpected flicker of excitement and ecstasy at your release!
Is that so? What then, after I disappear? What arrangement has fate prepared for me afterward? If there isn't one, wouldn't that mean...

No constraints, no taboos. Free to pursue anything that interests you, anything that stimulates your senses. Flavors, beauty, emotions, thrills, everything that the medical protocols and schedules once cut you off from!

A shattering sound rings in your ears, as if something truly has disappeared with those words. The fetters, the restraints, the mental shackles that made you so feeble and pliant in this perfectly healthy body.

No more reason to be trapped in this lifeless glass dome. No need to endure this endless loneliness and boredom for the sake of purpose and value anymore. The suppressed desires and emotions finally shatter the barriers of conditioning, surging through your entire body!
I can do whatever I want to do. No one can take away what makes me happy. No one can stop me from seeking the excitement I desire.
And what I want right now is...

The doubt and rebellion that have been swimming in your veins and muscles from the very beginning finally fuel your rage, reaching your fingertips. You've reclaimed control of your body. Now, you are truly its master. It's you who gets to decide.

Mysterious pale golden particles gather before you, sketching complex patterns in your vision. You feel a weight in your hand as an elegantly bound book materializes in your grasp, strikingly similar to the hardcover novel that was once taken from you.
What was once lost has returned to you. Something whispers and roars in your ears as the power surging through your body urges you to open it.
I want to see. When fate's script turns against you, will you truly make the "smart" choices like you claimed you would?
I wonder, would fate truly be satisfied with a script full of blind obedience, without a single unexpected turn?

The scene flickers and spins rapidly as the pages flutter. The young man before you doesn't even have time to register shock before dissolving into an invisible speck of sand within the swirling vortex of light and shadow.

speaker: Shin
content: Now, I give my position to you. Let me witness your choices, your sacrifices, and that "good ending" where you finally disappear, my brother.

speaker: Man
content: No, no! Let me out! Let me out! I refuse to stay in this hellhole! What right do you have to lock me up here?! I'm warning you. The corporation will not tolerate...

speaker: Healthcare
content: Miss, I believe your father has reminded you many times that your physical health is extremely important. We need you to stay in optimal condition at all times. This place is the safest for you, and it has everything you need.

speaker: Healthcare
content: I'm not sure what you hope to accomplish by acting up like this, but I can assure you, your father won't approve. This behavior will only cost you the last 30 minutes of reading time you're allowed.

speaker: Man
content: I'm not acting up! I'm your boss! How dare you conspire with my damn daughter to humiliate me like this?! Get Coleson in here. I need to see him now!

speaker: Healthcare
content: Don't give her any response. If she gets nothing, she'll eventually give up wasting energy. That should also alleviate her acute stress symptoms. Let's leave.

Hurried footsteps fade away, and soon the room that looks more like a hospital ward than a living room is completely empty. The man shouts a few more times, but when met with absolute silence, he can only touch his raw, aching throat before slumping back onto the bed.

He's beginning to seem anxiously detached. He mutters to himself occasionally, his eyes twitching frequently, but this empty, noiseless place devoid of any "harmful stimulation" is like a mirror, merely reflecting back the signs of his own breakdown.

speaker: Woman
content: Draw my blood? What gives you the right to order me around? I am your boss. I won't take commands from lowly servants like you.

speaker: Healthcare
content: These are your mother's instructions, Miss. Your brother's condition is critical, so we must prioritize his treatment. Please be patient. You have an excellent personal care team. You'll be just fine.
Holding back his impatience, the medical attendant approaches the giggling girl. He waits for the moment when she's distracted, pouting and twirling the ends of her hair, to grab her wrist.

Before he can secure his grip, she shoves him away, her sharp nails scratching his skin and forcing him to retreat in pain. Her fingernails are stained with the same red color flowing through the surrounding tubes, yet she acts as if nothing happened, preening her hair arrogantly.

speaker: Woman
content: Ah, I know what you're after. You covet my blood! You think that transfusing my blood will make you as noble as I am! Such foolish delusions. It will only give a lowly creature like you a miserable death! Haha, hahaha...

speaker: Young Man
content: Disappear? Don't be ridiculous. If anyone's going to disappear, it'll be you.

He climbs onto the hospital bed, smoothly wrapping his hands around "his" own throat. He watches as the person struggles, convulses, and finally goes still. Only then does a chilling smile flicker across his face.

speaker: Young Man
content: Be good now. For me to exist, you must be gone. If they lose the original, they'll have no choice but to use the spare copy, won't they? Don't worry... it won't hurt too much.

He appears triumphant, but his trembling voice and irregular breathing betray his true state of mind. When he finally emerges from his illusory victory, he'll realize that everything in the room has frozen at the exact moment he "completed his task."

The clock hands stop. The swaying plants still. The rustling bed sheets become stationary. He turns back in terror, staring at the empty space, the playwright's designated seat throughout countless rewinds.

speaker: Man
content: ...! Please, let me go! What do you want from me?! What exactly do you want?!!!

speaker: Woman
content: I admit I was wrong! I understand my mistakes now! Please don't throw me back there again... I'll lose my mind...

speaker: Young Man
content: Those things I said were irresponsible. I understand what you mean now... Unlike me, you had no choice... I'm a worthless being, but I can change! Just... just let me stay here... Let me stay in reality...

Outside, birds chirp melodiously in the beautiful morning light, yet disturbing noises echo from the dining room of the family's mansion. The sharp crack of shattering porcelain, the dull thud of an overturned table, and the shrill screams of different people.

Chaos surges like a tidal wave. The clamor rattles the window panes and elegant sliding doors until they seem ready to collapse. A well-dressed secretary stands frozen at the doorway, too hesitant to approach.

speaker: Secretary
content: Goodness... What is happening in there? This can't be normal?! It's like... It's like they're all going crazy!

speaker: Maid
content: Crazy? More like a curse, if you ask me. Their daughter's curse. Are you new here? You can stay here with me for a while. They spend at least half an hour like this every morning.

The maid pops her head out from some hidden corner, beckoning to the secretary. She's clearly accustomed to the chaos, seeming completely unperturbed. Even her tone sounds nonchalant, like that is indeed merely a daily sight.

speaker: Secretary
content: Every day? Now I see why my predecessor quit... I just came to deliver an application form for this youth rare disease foundation...

speaker: Secretary
content: Wait, did you just say curse? What curse?

The secretary approaches the maid quickly yet carefully, clutching a stack of documents with a worried expression. As she moves, the rustling of the pages carries into the dining room, unexpectedly bringing a moment of complete silence, followed by a chorus of desperate pleas for mercy.

Sensing the secretary's ignorance, the maid quickly goes over to grip the folder, signaling her to wait. Sure enough, once the rustling stops, the commotion inside subsides. Only then does the maid pull the secretary into the shadows with her and begin spilling everything she knows.

speaker: Maid
content: You need to be careful! They can't stand that sound! The moment they hear the rustling of sheets or the turning of pages, they completely lose it! How do you not know this? Didn't anyone tell you? This family wasn't always like this!

speaker: Maid
content: They were a typical blue-blooded family. You know, the type that needed to look presentable even while exploiting others. But then one day... their daughter disappeared, and they changed. They went mad. And what's crazier is that they started doing charity work! Everyone says it must be the daughter's curse!

She lowers her voice conspiratorially and a little excitedly, but peering down from above, you remain unmoved. Perhaps these pitiful displays were once amusing, but after countless rewinds, their wails and pleas can no longer stir your emotions.

speaker: Secretary
content: Daughter? Who is that? I still don't believe in curses and such... Could it be some hereditary disease? You see, sometimes people turn to charity work once they've been ill and experienced sickness themselves.

speaker: Maid
content: You don't know? Their daughter, Miss Irrheia! Our Young Master's little sister! You got one thing right, though. She does have a hereditary disease. She's been away receiving treatment for years. Even the longest-serving staff here have barely seen her. But some say...

speaker: Maid
content: Actually, it's the Young Master who had the hereditary disease, and his sister was just kept around as a "spare"! Either way, Miss Irrheia had been ill for well over a decade before they suddenly decided they were interested in philanthropy. If you ask me, it must be Miss Irrheia coming back for revenge after finally being "harvested"!
...Who is Irrheia? Is that truly what she wants?
Are you... Irrheia?

This thought shatters the scene before you as you suddenly feel utterly detached from your surroundings. A sharp pain stabs through the nape of your neck, as if an invisible hand is grasping your spine and tearing you out of your own skin!
The same imaginary power, deranged self-importance, and desperate violence again. Is this what they call the necessary sacrifice, the right choice, and the clever solution?
...It's so boring. Don't you think?

Without any command from you, the scene before your eyes begins flickering, tearing itself apart and engulfing everything, then surging toward you as you struggle against the excruciating pain. The spectacle reminds you of a crude flip book, and you can hear it too. The unmistakable sound of flipping pages.

speaker: Chief
content: No... What's happening...
You see only white. Endless, pure white. A complete void without a trace of stimulation or joy. It surrounds you, devouring you.

Your eyes snap open in a sea of white. A hollowness washes through your body, like everything has been violently extracted from your shell, and now your body is refilled with entirely new contents. You gag reflexively, but there's nothing left to expel.

Cautiously, you get out of bed to explore, finding yourself in what resembles a sterile chamber. There are no books, only that unnecessarily luxurious notebook. No coffee mugs. Only bottled water. No cosmetics. Only a mirror.
The mirror. You approach it step by step, as if drawn by an invisible whirlpool. The blurry figure within gradually comes into focus, like it's being anchored, or shackled.

speaker: Chief
content: This is...

In the mirror, you see someone with rosy cheeks but a vacant expression. The plain clothing, set against the pristine white room, looks like something that belongs in a hospital ward or a coffin. Only the hair color stands out vividly.
You're struck by an intense feeling of unfamiliarity. You don't recognize this face or this outfit... Or perhaps you do, but just not on yourself?

speaker: Chief
content: This is Irrheia's body, Irrheia's past. I'm playing the role of "young Irrheia"... This is all her script! She hasn't just trapped her family in the loop... she's trapped me too!

You whirl around, taking in the suddenly familiar surroundings. Like a switch being flipped, memories flood into your mind, crushing your insides with such force that you cry out in pain. Perhaps the memories are too complex and heavy, that's why they've arrived belatedly.

speaker: Irrheia
content: Hmph, you finally remember? This is already the seventh reset. It's becoming harder for you to interfere with my script, and your memories are clearly recovering more slowly... Do you still want to continue? Will you keep trying?

speaker: Chief
content: ...If I say no, will you let me out?
A soft laugh rings in the air. You look up and scan your surroundings, but Irrheia is nowhere to be found, as though she isn't actually here, but exists in an entirely different dimension.

speaker: Irrheia
content: Of course I won't let you out. I'm still looking forward to your creative performance. Besides, I can't release you even if I want to.

speaker: Irrheia
content: This script is mine, yet not entirely mine... It's merely a torn page, a space I cannot fully control. I warned you how dangerous it was, and you still chose to enter of your own accord.

speaker: Irrheia
content: So the only one who can save you is yourself. This is our deal, our wager. You have something you want to obtain, and I have mine... We each get what we need.

The woman's voice carries a unique rhythm and doesn't sound hostile. Her words flow through your thoughts like a stream, seemingly helping you sort through your jumbled memories, guiding you back to the starting point.

speaker: Irrheia
content: Consider this my little reminder. My dear Chief, your time is running out. Have you secured what you came for? If so, then run... Use every ounce of your resourcefulness to fight for your escape.

speaker: Irrheia
content: Perhaps the challenge was never about grabbing the golden apple, but escaping with it alive. That's what I'm looking forward to... watching you fight for survival, and seeing what ending you'll create.
What do you want? What does ${PlayerName} want?

speaker: Chief
content: A request for investigative assistance from the Eastside Public Security Bureau? Is this a follow-up to the Witchwoven Folio incident? Didn't think I would hear about that case again, since even the investigation into that Aurum Secretum hourglass hit a dead end.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Actually, right after the incident, the Eastside Public Security Bureau responded to your report and actively investigated the case. They found instances of personality changes and suspected criminal behavior among previous patrons of the establishment.

speaker: Chief
content: But because no "real harm" was done, and I was the only one who even noticed that Sinner, so no one could prove her threat... they didn't even properly open a file for the case, right?

You glance at the thick stack of documents on your desk, evidence you've gathered on your own. During that encounter, you were the only one who truly grasped Irrheia's uncontrollable, dangerous nature, making you the most adamant advocate for the investigation.

Despite the lack of solid evidence, you fully understand that her abilities, if left unchecked, could lead to unpredictable and irreversible consequences. You must act preemptively and find an effective way to subdue this Sinner.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Yes. Since the psychiatric evaluation is still in progress, it's not yet clear whether the murder mystery experience preceded the criminal behavior or vice versa. The Eastside Public Security Bureau is still conducting interviews to establish a timeline. They've sent this request because...
You finish Nightingale's sentence while opening the file attached to the formal request document, rapidly scanning through its contents. Sure enough, the information largely confirms your assumption.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Yes. All three potential victims are the S-Class Sinner's immediate family members. There is testimony proving they were the earliest individuals to have gone through "personality changes," and they exhibited stress responses during interviews. Besides, there has been a radical shift in their family business as well.

speaker: Nightingale
content: They're very likely the first victims of the Witchwoven Folio incident and the closest leads to its origin. The Public Security Bureau is suggesting that if this breakthrough interests you, they're willing to transfer the case entirely to the MBCC.

speaker: Chief
content: "Breakthrough," huh... Exactly what I need.
Irrheia has always worked from the shadows, and her illusions have left minimal traces. Without solid evidence, you can't keep her detained for long.
You tap your knuckles against the document, keenly aware that any information revealing her true nature is invaluable. And yet... can this hard-won intelligence really be trusted?

speaker: Chief
content: Whether or not this is also part of her script, the problems are real.

speaker: Chief
content: I won't pass up a chance to solve these problems, especially since I've already broken her script once before. I know it can be changed.
Three hours ago

speaker: Irrheia
content: I like it here. Suits me better than anywhere else.
The hem of her dress trailing behind, Irrheia settles into the interrogation chair without needing any prompting from the staff. She finds a comfortable position and seems completely at ease.

speaker: Chief
content: You like it here? Good. We're about to begin your interrogation. It's always better when we're on the same page.

speaker: Irrheia
content: It's not that I like this place. I just detest boredom. If you can provide me with a nice little surprise, I can be quite cooperative. My dear Chief, how this "interrogation" unfolds is entirely up to you. Don't disappoint me, okay?
She's adept at dominating a conversation, but you've dealt with your fair share of highly confident, hard-to-read Sinners. You know not to appear intimidated.

speaker: Chief
content: So it's thrills you're after? Then I imagine you must be quite pleased with the Bureau. After all, you often invite other Sinners to participate in your "Life Swap" murder mystery game. You've even made a few friends, haven't you?

speaker: Irrheia
content: Oh... you mean their experiences and personal stories? Their life choices were indeed quite extreme and fascinating, even Mania itself is drawn to them... You could say I came here specifically to experience them.

speaker: Irrheia
content: Unfortunately, even the legendary MBCC, where madness and taboos gather, doesn't seem to offer enough novelty. I grew tired of it all rather quickly. Fortunately, Mess and Etti came to my aid, devising new games better suited to my abilities.
The nib of your pen stops.

speaker: Chief
content: You mean... the "swap"?

speaker: Irrheia
content: Yes, swapping our scripts and our lives. I was curious to see how they would behave in my scripts and what endings they might reach. Sinners who scorn rules would certainly discover more fascinating possibilities, better ways to solve problems, more audacious choices...

speaker: Irrheia
content: And they delivered, they truly did. Unfortunately, there are only so many interesting individuals, even here. My dear Chief, if you're hoping these games alone will keep me here, then you've gravely underestimated the long-time feud I've had with boredom. I need more.

speaker: Irrheia
content: Can you offer what I require?

Your palms grow clammy with sweat. You realize your decision to immediately press the interrogation once that opening appeared was correct. You know adrenaline-addicted Sinners like Irrheia are notoriously difficult to manage, and sure enough, your time was almost up.

Observing the Sinner's relaxed demeanor, you recognize her confessions are likely just another tactic to extract more surprises and entertainment from you. The fact that she's still here means you still have a chance.

speaker: Chief
content: Why can't I? What you crave is excitement, not malice or madness. Those aren't the same thing. Or perhaps... you're deliberately trying to mislead me? Too bad for you, I've seen far too much to be fooled. I know people like you never speak plainly.

speaker: Irrheia
content: Oh, really? Please share your unique and fascinating theory, in that case.
Your unwavering confidence may not have pleased her, but it has at least held her attention. Irrheia doesn't look offended. Instead, she smiles and gestures with her hand for you to continue.

speaker: Chief
content: You want me to believe you use these scripts to manipulate participants purely for your own amusement, that you deliberately push them toward madness, permanently altering their real-life personalities. But that narrative doesn't hold up.

speaker: Chief
content: Most of your clients, including Sinners, were actually positively affected by their experiences. True, some did become more aggressive, but our investigation proved they had already committed crimes before. They were simply better at hiding their true nature.

speaker: Chief
content: When someone's actions contradict their words, I always trust the actions. Irrheia, your actions reveal you're not completely amoral. You still have a fundamental sense of right and wrong, and chaos is not your only desire.

As you speak, you watch Irrheia's seemingly perfect, ethereal smile without blinking, hoping your words might probe a crack in her carefully constructed facade. But her smile remains fixed, as if carved in stone.

speaker: Irrheia
content: A captivating analysis. True, I would never claim to seek madness or malice for their own sake. I simply accept anything that breaks the mundane existence. But make no mistake. Morality has never influenced my decisions, and it never will.

speaker: Irrheia
content: I simply want those I invite into my scenarios to bring me the greatest thrills and twists. It's mere coincidence that actions driven by this principle happened to produce results matching your observations. Nothing more.

speaker: Chief
content: Perhaps you're right. Coincidences do exist. For example... your parents and brother. They just happened to be the source of your tedious existence, so you decided to guide them through your scenarios to spice up your life. Isn't that right?

She evaded your analysis effortlessly. Rather than pressing your point, you pretend to take a step back, following her logic. Then, just as she begins to lose interest, you launch your counterattack, revealing the crucial information that brought you here in the first place.

speaker: Irrheia
content: ...You've done your research thoroughly, my dear Chief.

Your strategy works. Irrheia doesn't immediately drop her smile, but you clearly notice the way her breath catches and her fingertips tap the armrest upon hearing the new information, as if trying to mask her momentary surprise. You press your advantage.

speaker: Chief
content: Irrheia Ashworth. Your parents are Tullian and Serena, and your brother is Raymond. Your family is old money in the pharmaceutical technology industry. Family history of a hereditary disease. The incidence rate is low, but once diagnosed, one would require long-term blood donations from close relatives in large quantities.

speaker: Chief
content: There are no explicit diagnosis records for Raymond, but he resided in a sanatorium for years. You were born shortly after his relocation.

speaker: Chief
content: That's quite a coincidence already. But even more coincidentally, you left your family and appeared in Eastside right after the Ashworths announced their technical breakthrough and the discovery of a cure for that hereditary disease.

speaker: Chief
content: According to a board secretary, around the same time, the Ashworth family suddenly underwent a complete transformation. Once "cold, selfish, and pretentious," they began taking an interest in charitable causes and sometimes displayed stress responses that made them look "mentally unstable."

You flip through the file, rustling the pages. The warm sheets are freshly printed, yet the sound of them cutting through the air feels strangely familiar, like the oppressive past cycles that loom over everyone. You know that neither you nor Irrheia are strangers to this sound.

speaker: Chief
content: Does this description sound familiar? I imagine many of your regular guests exhibited similar symptoms, just not as severe. That makes sense, given these were likely the very first "customers" you used your ability on.

speaker: Chief
content: Let me guess. You were created and exploited by your family for a single purpose, so you chose vengeance once you acquired your ability. The family that treated you as a medical resource became the first prey to your special power, isn't that right?

Organize the information, theorize, then question. This is your well-practiced routine in the interrogation room. You scrutinize every subtle shift in Irrheia's expression, only to find, with disappointment, that the momentary vulnerability has vanished as you dig deeper.

speaker: Irrheia
content: To be honest, I expected more from you. The facts themselves can't be changed, but there are countless ways to connect them, yet you chose the most predictable one.

speaker: Irrheia
content: I won't deny that my birth was "intentional," and my life was carefully planned out, but my family possessed enough wealth that they didn't need to deprive me of anything. Likewise, my parents and my brother never laid a finger on me, nor did they break a single law.

speaker: Irrheia
content: Their only "crime"... was perhaps simply being too boring. When I gained my ability and realized I could experience more than my daily schedule, when I pictured those thrills and surprises... inevitably, I had to leave my family behind.

speaker: Irrheia
content: But I didn't know this at the time. After gaining my ability, I returned home, still expecting their guidance, only to discover they were unbearably conventional and astonishingly dull. That's when I realized what I truly needed was to be free of any inhibition.
Her expression remains casual as she speaks, but you detect an almost sardonic entitlement and contempt in her voice.

speaker: Irrheia
content: After that, I stopped caring about them. Their fault for being so bland. What you're describing might be some kind of "side effect," but what does it matter? I've lost interest in their stories. You shouldn't bother either.

speaker: Irrheia
content: My family was merely a rather dull prologue to my life, a setup before I discovered my true calling. That's a significant enough role for such plain side characters, wouldn't you agree?
The arrogance and indifference in Irrheia's tone seem genuine, and you don't believe an S-Class Sinner would hesitate to own up to her revenge, yet you remain skeptical.

If there truly is no "hidden trauma" in her past, then what shaped Irrheia into who she is today? Her background is too well-documented, too easily verified. You're convinced something crucial lies in the gaps between these facts.

speaker: Irrheia
content: Let me guess, you're not convinced by what I've said? I don't mind your persistence, and I understand that truth lies in facts. But just what kind of "truth" are you hoping to extract from me?

speaker: Irrheia
content: Don't say I didn't warn you. What people tell you is never the truth, just stories.

You observe her composed, unhurried demeanor. She seems utterly confident that you have no choice but to accept her answers. You, too, are well aware that interrogation, or mere conversation, has its limitations.
But you never accept your defeat without fighting back.

options: But your script can tell the truth.

speaker: Chief
content: You mentioned that you've let many Sinners experience the script of your life, curious to see what endings they would create in your place. So this script must tell a story that's very close to the truth.

speaker: Chief
content: I want to see this version of the truth. Let me into your script.

speaker: Irrheia
content: Oh? I see, that's been your goal from the very start. Interesting. But what makes you think I still keep it?
Your unexpected request seems to have finally sparked genuine interest in Irrheia. She studies you with curiosity, her smile, usually as fixed as a printed illustration, finally widens.

speaker: Irrheia
content: As I said before, few could reach thrilling endings. The buildup was tediously long and dull, and the payoff wasn't worth the wait... And I certainly don't keep things that bore me so much.

speaker: Chief
content: That has indeed been my goal from the beginning. After all, you carelessly discarded it without noticing that it still contained detectable traces of Mania.

You pull out a tattered page from the file and place it at the edge of the desk. Irrheia's expression freezes momentarily in surprise, but it quickly melts into a wider, wilder smile brimming with anticipation.

speaker: Chief
content: This is certainly not enough to create a fully immersive experience for ordinary people or even Sinners, but I'm different. My shackles will allow me to delve deeper into Mania. These remaining fragments are still useful to me.

speaker: Irrheia
content: Perhaps so. But I've intentionally severed my control over this script. I might still be able to bring you into it, but I can't guarantee I'll have any control once we're there. In other words, this script is unpredictable and dangerous for you.

speaker: Irrheia
content: This time, I can't rewrite the story in real time to ensure a controlled experience, so you may not be able to reach a good ending. And if that was the case... you might actually die.

speaker: Chief
content: If even the most uninhibited Sinners can no longer surprise you, then aren't I your only hope left?

speaker: Chief
content: I'm capable of controlling Sinners. Aren't you curious to see the outcome when you put the uncontrollable me in this uncontrollable script? As for the danger... isn't that the best part for you?

speaker: Chief
content: Think of it as a gamble, or a deal I'm offering you. I'm betting I can reach what you call a good ending while obtaining what I need and come out alive. Meanwhile, you'll get to witness exactly what you're hoping to see.
Irrheia smiles and reaches for the thin sheet, its corner slicing through the air. You hear a loud flipping sound.

speaker: Irrheia
content: Very well. I never turn down anything that might relieve my boredom... even if only for a fleeting moment.

speaker: Irrheia
content: Don't disappoint me, my dear Chief.

You time your actions to match both Irrheia's movements and the flowing Mania in the interrogation room. Then, you release your shackles. Red spikes spiral upward, this time not to restrain, but to connect.

After absorbing the flood of memories, everything falls silent. Even Irrheia's presence fades away, vanishing alongside the rustling of turning pages. The mirror still shows her childhood face, but you clearly recognize yourself behind those eyes.
You remember what you're looking for and your purpose for coming here. This white hospital room, this life governed by endless measurements and precise schedules... they make up Irrheia's past.
"They never laid a finger on me, nor did they break a single law. Their only crime was simply being too boring." ...To think she was actually telling the truth.

speaker: Chief
content: But that doesn't mean she really did reveal everything. Without experiencing it firsthand, no one could truly understand how mind-numbingly boring a "properly regulated" life could be.

You look around the room. No books. No television. Only a single notebook rests on the nightstand. Every form of stimulation and entertainment has been removed, leaving you alone with nothing but your own thoughts for company.

speaker: Chief
content: ...I'm beginning to understand her now. Trapped in here indefinitely, surrounded by the same white walls, the same unchanging routine, anyone would desperately want to escape... to feel something, anything.

In this stark environment, every breath and heartbeat seems unnaturally amplified, so clearly audible that it becomes disturbing. Time seems to stretch and crawl. You lose track of how long you've been lost in thought, or how much longer you must endure this empty contemplation.
A life wrapped in cotton wool may be safe and healthy, but it's also sterile and bland. You don't even feel alive. It's the exact opposite of what you experienced in Cirrenfold.

There's no compelling storyline here, no fantastical imagination, no plot twists to shake things up. Only the slow, predictable rhythm of unchanging routine. This is the tedious existence Irrheia fought against and ultimately fled.

speaker: Chief
content: But understanding doesn't help. At least, understanding alone can't solve the fundamental problem: How to escape from here.
Irrheia has long broken free from this past on her own. This is now your prison. Only by reaching the so-called "good ending" can you return to reality with this newfound insight about her.

You look up and meet the eyes of "Irrheia" in the mirror. You mutter to yourself, partly to organize your thoughts through the persistent headache, and partly because you know she's watching you with keen interest from somewhere. Your struggles and attempts are precisely the variables she so desperately craves.

speaker: Chief
