content: She hates anything mundane, predictable, or uncreative. She loves excitement, change, and novelty. So the strategy should be to follow the residual instincts in this body, guess her "previous" choices, then stay as far away from them as possible... That approach should work.

speaker: Chief
content: But after seven resets, I'm still trapped here. That means something's not working. Maybe I'm not deviating enough from her choices? Just how different must the choices be to break this cycle?

You need to keep trying, but as Irrheia warned, each failure erodes your consciousness further. Your time is running out. You struggle to concentrate, but the mental fog grows thicker by the moment, like dragging your thoughts through cold mud.

speaker: Irrheia
content: More fascinating possibilities, better ways to solve problems, more audacious choices...
The "good ending" in her mind comes down to these three elements. And they represent not only my way out, but also my realization of what she truly desires...
This should be the only goal and the only approach.

You gaze around the desolate, lifeless hospital room where endless white threatens to smother every thought. You understand that within this place you return to after each reset, hidden in this suffocating whiteness, lies a gap into Irrheia's soul.
And only by reaching her most profound desire can you hope to break this endless cycle.

options: And you'll break the cycle thoroughly

content: You stand up decisively, push the door open, and walk out. The inertia of the script makes each step a struggle, but it's exactly this exhausting trudging sensation that confirms you're moving toward something entirely different from the predetermined story. The right path.

speaker: Young Man
content: ...Irria? What are you doing here? Who brought you?

You thank the nurse who mistakenly thinks you're just being a caring sister, and enter the obviously cozier suite. You don't expect a welcome, but your wretched brother's unkindness still manages to surprise you.

Not only does he get your name wrong, but he also makes no effort to hide his irritation. Only after his gaze passes over the IV drip steadily feeding into his arm does he seem to remember his role as a brother.

speaker: Chief
content: My name is Irrheia. No one brought me. I came on my own.

speaker: Young Man
content: On your own? You? Irrheia, I don't know what you've heard from the person who brought you here, but it's all lies. Neither the family nor I have ever wronged you. If you're smart enough, you should...

speaker: Chief
content: I'm not smart, nor do I wish to be. Pragmatism only works when circumstances already favor you.
Ignoring his condescending lecture, you slowly approach him, then suddenly leap onto the bed, using every ounce of strength to pin him down by his chest and clamp your hand firmly over his mouth!

speaker: Chief
content: Take you, for instance. Always on the high ground, waiting for them to feed you the sacrificial blood. You even have the audacity to complain about the taste. But circumstances will never be in the sacrifice's favor, no matter how long I wait.

He's the older brother, and you're in the body of his younger sister. But ironically, the disease that exploits you has left him weak, while the strict regimen designed to facilitate that exploitation has made you strong. You've pinned him down with surprising ease.

speaker: Young Man
content: What... are you... doing...

speaker: Chief
content: I want to break this scripted, controlled, meaningless routine! I want to break free from the indoctrinated ideals of sacrifice and duty! I want to shatter this damned cycle where I'm used as a mere disposable blood bag!

speaker: Chief
content: A life that can only be sustained by sucking another's blood should not exist! No one is born to be exploited and consumed! All this talk of sacrifice and duty is complete nonsense! You can't take my life away with these manipulative tactics anymore!

You stare into his panicked, terrified eyes, knowing full well this isn't the actual person who oppressed Irrheia for years, but a mere phantom. Yet your words aren't false. They flow from your lips naturally, like an instinctive, reflexive response.

You no longer have to fight against this body. Every movement has become effortless and fluid, as if someone else is guiding your hands to make the same motions, adding their strength to yours, just as Irrheia once did.

Is this what Irrheia truly wanted all along? Had she wished to see through the deception sooner? To make her escape sooner? Or even shatter these constraints and confront these people who twisted her life with tedium and control earlier?

speaker: Young Man
content: Who... who are you really... You're not my sister...!

speaker: Young Man
content: No one has taught her these things. How could she possibly know any of this...?!

He struggles with every ounce of his strength, suddenly unleashing a surprising burst of power that sends you flying off him. You crash hard onto the floor and see him scramble to the edge of the bed and slam his fist on the security alarm!
BEEEEEEEP!

The piercing alarm cuts through the air and seems to slice right into your skull. Your vision explodes with dark spots, and you barely make out the uniformed personnel rushing into the room. But before they can even grab you, the entire scene begins to crumble.

speaker: Chief
content: ...A reset?!

A wave of excruciating pain washes over you, followed by a loud thud. Your mind finally shuts down like a power outage, plunging into a complete blank. Before you can even feel the relief, one final thought flashes past your mind.
Where did it go wrong this time?

speaker: Chief
content: Ow... my head hurts... This reset feels nothing like what happened in the murder mystery game. It's like I actually died...

It sounds extra convincing coming from someone who has literally set one foot into the coffin multiple times. Too bad the room is completely silent, with no one to respond to you. You rub your temples and sit up in the sterile white void. Reluctantly, you start reviewing what happened once again.

speaker: Chief
content: She was right after all. This fragment of the script is completely beyond her control. She can't guide me or rewrite the story like she did in Cirrenfold. I'm afraid even the reset trigger here doesn't follow Irrheia's logic.

speaker: Chief
content: If that's the case, it could explain why even though I deliberately followed Irrheia's suggestions and intentionally broke the usual patterns to show her different outcomes, I still got reset.
After everything you've experienced, you're no longer the blank slate you were when you first awoke. The Sinners have shown you many kinds of entertainment.

In video games and murder mystery games, an illusion is often the manifestation of its creator's obsession. To succeed, you must outperform the owner of the obsession. If Irrheia doesn't govern this place, but the Mania lingering in her consciousness does, it'll only make this principle more true.

speaker: Chief
content: But... how exactly do I meet the criteria for success here? If Irrheia herself isn't providing the clues... then perhaps what matters is her earliest desire, from before she was contaminated by Mania?

speaker: Chief
content: It can't be about escape. She's already accomplished that herself. What does "better" really mean in this context? Not earlier, not madder either...
Then...
Is "better" really what she needs?

speaker: Chief
content: Well... I don't have any better options anyway.
You don't let the fleeting insight slip away. Of course, it's just a hunch. You're far from certain. But at this point, you have no reason to hesitate. You'll test your theory boldly.

So you lie back down on the bed and dutifully play the role of an obedient "medical resource." You allow yourself to be nurtured to the perfect condition. Time stretches unbearably when you take no action of your own, but you wait patiently.

Day after day of exercise, medication, and examinations, interspersed with tutoring and reading time doled out as rewards. You become so cooperative that even your family is astounded, and even after learning you've been cast aside, you simply obey instructions and leave home to live independently.

speaker: Boss
content: The figures didn't look so good last month! I know it's not easy to consistently produce high-quality content, and players grow bored quickly, but that's just how this mystery game business works. Your script gotta grab enough attention!

speaker: Boss
content: You know how these Eastsiders are these days. They're all empty inside and craving virtual thrills. That's how we make money! We gotta satisfy the customers, Irrheia. Put in the hard work and you'll push through it, right? I know you can do it!

speaker: Boss
content: Just be more mindful next time, okay? Your previous work The Charming Snake's Dream was very popular, but that doesn't mean you can just follow it with The Silly Panda's Bamboo Wish! We pulled the first one exactly because people got tired of it, remember?

speaker: Chief
content: Got it, Boss.

On your way home from work, you receive a lengthy message from your boss. You mechanically react with a thumbs up and reply with a "Got it" before switching back to the email tab to finish your daily report. The single word "script-writing" summarizes your entire day. Write, delete, repeat.

This is the best job you could find. You work nine to five. You get the weekends off. You can make ends meet. You get meager bonuses. Your boss's favorite activities are counting profits and pressuring employees. No endless Corruptors to kill or Black Rings to absorb.

speaker: Chief
content: Wait, two more seconds until I can clock out... I won't make this light. Whatever. Got another hour to wait before I can buy the discounted sandwiches from the convenience store near my apartment.

Bustling crowds come and go around you, the same people passing you by at the same time every day. They hurry along with eyes fixed on their phones. Nobody so much as glances at you, an employee of a murder mystery game parlor commuting in a witch costume.

This is daily life in Eastside. When technology occupies everyone with cheap thrills, the dazzling spectacles eventually become dull. Overstimulation numbs the senses, leaving people desperately craving new identities, new lives, and new roles to play.

You're no different, except your witch costume changes nothing. Art imitates life, and your life consists of clocking in, working, then clocking out. Occasionally, you catch the news broadcast, and that has inspired you to write The Dancing Beauty of the Great Expo.

speaker: Boss
content: DisCity Independence Day is next week and we need to cash in on that! Be prepared to work overtime. Please reply if you've seen this message.

speaker: Boss
content: Let's take a vote on this year's team-building event. I personally recommend option 1. It's cheaper and just as effective.

speaker: Boss
content: We're adjusting the lunch subsidy policy. Only those scheduled for the day shift will be eligible. Off-duty employees and office support staff will no longer receive it. It'll start this month. Don't be alarmed when you get your paycheck.

It's as if you've really spent years within this story, until you've become just another featureless face. Even your witch costume doesn't make you stand out from the rush hour Eastside crowds. And you finally get the proof you've been waiting for.

speaker: Irrheia
content: My dear Chief, what are you doing? Yes, nothing, just playing by the rules... Do you think this will impress me? Hah, no one wants to watch such a boring story. It's so repetitive and uncreative.

The voice suddenly rings out, as if someone is whispering in your ear, hair brushing past your ear before vanishing. She maintains that ethereal, smiling tone, but the fact that she's spoken first should be some kind of indication.
And this is exactly what you've been waiting for. You straighten your posture within the crowd, as if you've anticipated her "appearance" all along.

speaker: Chief
content: I don't find this boring. True, this is not an "interesting" life, but it's peaceful. If my Sinners could live like this, I'd be happy for them.

speaker: Irrheia
content: Oh? You seem quite content to waste your life away here. Fine then, I can certainly gift you this boring existence if that's what you want.

speaker: Irrheia
content: But doesn't this mean you choose to lose the bet? What a shame. Have you finally realized you stand no chance of winning? It seems your unbridled creativity and unyielding pride have been worn away completely.

speaker: Chief
content: I do hope to retire early someday and live a stable life away from danger. But... I never said I planned to spend my whole life here. Indeed, I'm quitting.

speaker: Irrheia
content: Quitting? Are you begging for mercy now? Do you think I'll spare you just like that?
You keenly detect a hint of disappointment in her tone. For someone usually so inscrutable, this is already a rare display of emotion. It gives you more confidence to proceed with your plan.

speaker: Chief
content: Of course not. I remember you said you couldn't control this place, and I'm not giving up yet. I'm attempting to stay in the game by saying "I quit" to the version of you that controls this place.

speaker: Irrheia
content: ...Has the boring life worn away your sanity as well?

speaker: Chief
content: I'm simply trying to guess what you truly want. At first, I realized you weren't lying. After gaining your power, you saw through the Ashworth family's hypocrisy and arrogance. You recognized how they deceived and exploited you.

speaker: Chief
content: But someone who has truly broken free wouldn't voluntarily return here time after time. The very existence of this script is itself a clue pointing toward the answer. On the surface, it appears I'm trapped here, dying repeatedly, while you can quit whenever you please...

speaker: Chief
content: But in reality, the one dying has always been "Irrheia," your past self. Each of our attempts, which are really your attempts, to find a "better outcome," is the prison itself.

speaker: Chief
content: I understand you. Every time I escape a plight, I too can't help but wonder: Why couldn't I see through it earlier? I could have done better. But this refusal to accept what happened also traps us in the past.

speaker: Irrheia
content: All these pretty words, but you're just rearranging the connections between facts. The result is still the same. If you truly understand as you claim, then you shouldn't want to quit. You should keep trying, shouldn't you?
You swivel your chair and look up, searching for Irrheia's position in the air above you. You know you can't actually make eye contact with her, but you want her to feel the weight of your sincerity.

speaker: Chief
content: No. I won't keep trying, because I already know what you want. I also know that if everything presented in this script is true, then there could never be a so-called "better" ending.

speaker: Chief
content: No one could have done better than you did in those circumstances, Irrheia. You endured such a past. You were deceived, brainwashed, exploited, and ultimately discarded. Yet you broke free from those chains entirely on your own, still existing as yourself independently.

speaker: Chief
content: I've tried, and so have many other Sinners. Even with our ability to cheat, to reset, and retry with memories from the previous rounds, we still couldn't do better than you. No one in the world could. You should have been freed from here long ago. You deserve it.

speaker: Irrheia
content: Is flattering me your new strategy? Then you're likely to be disappointed. Save your sugar-coated bullets. This alone won't be enough to sway me. Keep trying the wrong approach, and you might really remain trapped here forever.
You're unfazed by this half-hearted threat.

speaker: Chief
content: This isn't flattery. It's simply the truth. If I've truly misread the situation, and you've long gotten over this, then let me pay the price for my presumption. But I'm not saying all this just to get myself out of here.

speaker: Chief
content: I don't want you to remain trapped in this impossible what-if scenario, tormenting both yourself and others. Irrheia, you never did anything wrong as a child. She was already so brave. Please stop denying her and killing her, will you?

speaker: Irrheia
content: The one who killed her... was never... me...

Irrheia is still in denial, but her voice draws out and breaks off unnaturally, finally vanishing into the spatial fissure, as if she's restraining something. Soon after, she vanishes completely once more, resuming her role as a mere spectator.

Yet you know that even in Irrheia's absence, the part of her long trapped in the past remains. It's the very thing she's been struggling to suppress. The fracturing space before you confirms everything, as the room rapidly collapses.

The illusion begins to unravel, and you're thrown into a weightless vortex, the world spinning violently. Instinctively, you try to close your eyes to steady yourself, but you force them open again. In the shattered mirror fragments, you glimpse what appears to be young Irrheia's face.

speaker: Young Irrheia
content: Is that true? Are there really no "better" and "smarter" choices than the ones I made?

Her childish face is etched with exhaustion. Her gaze is both vacant and defiant, as if she's shouldering a burden that should never have been hers. She stares right into your eyes, her lips barely moving, like it's taking all her courage to force out the words.

You've experienced many failures yourself. You know what will help her break free isn't some hypothetically perfect alternative, but rather an affirmation. That at least under those specific circumstances, she already did her best.
In that moment, she freezes, her tense expression finally relaxes, and her lips curve into a smile. A smile of long-awaited relief and peace.

The fissures collapse all at once, mirror shards raining down around you. The hospital ward, the sanatorium, and the room all vanish completely. You're thrown out of the illusion, a sudden release of pressure in your chest as you awaken in your own body in the real world.

speaker: Irrheia
content: How does it feel to return safely to reality? Pleasant, I imagine. After all, you got everything you wanted, and claimed your victory. Now you understand me better than I understand myself.

Your vision gradually comes into focus as the wavering shapes before your eyes solidify into Irrheia's perfectly composed form. She still rests her chin lightly on her hand, a smile playing at her lips, as if she has no objection to your actions in her script, or is even appreciative of them.

speaker: Chief
content: There's an old saying in Eastia: "Those in the midst of a situation often see less clearly than bystanders." And another: "A single leaf before your eyes can hide an entire mountain." Some problems simply cannot be seen from where you already stand. That was true for you, and true for your childhood self as well.
This is why you're always extraordinarily patient with Sinners. Because you know that sometimes they simply need someone to help them see clearly.

speaker: Irrheia
content: You don't see danger in me, but "problems"? What about my vengeance against my "family"? My uncontrollable power and my attitude?

options: Those are also just some of your problems.

speaker: Chief
content: I never said I was interrogating you for your crimes. This interrogation is indeed part of the follow-up investigation into the Witchwoven Folio incident, but you're not the one who appears as a potential perpetrator.

speaker: Chief
content: You may remember I mentioned that some customers were indeed negatively affected by your murder mystery games. But our in-depth investigation revealed that they already had criminal tendencies, and most had secretly acted on them.

speaker: Chief
content: The Public Security Bureau discovered this pattern. When they added the Ashworths to the list of suspected victims, they simultaneously placed them on the list of potential perpetrators. And you are very likely a victim of that family's abuse.

speaker: Irrheia
content: Me, a victim? The S-Class Sinner, the culprit who triggered a chain of incidents on a whim?
She seems amused by your words, her lips curving up mockingly. Her smile reveals both piqued interest and teasing disbelief toward your claims.
You don't react to her teasing. Instead, you pull out a note from the back of your folder and push it toward her. The note contains signatures from many different Sinners.

speaker: Chief
content: Yes, I am talking about you, and all these Sinners would agree too. Every one of them has spoken in your favor, even though you erased much of the information in that script you could still control.

speaker: Chief
content: And after experiencing it personally, I found that they were absolutely right. Only by being in that position could I understand how difficult it was to break free on my own, and how difficult it was to maintain restraint once I had power.
You pull out another stack of documents filled with data and charts. The impassive printed text sits above a collection of distinct signatures.

speaker: Chief
content: Perhaps you never intended vengeance, much less to do good, but you did save children like yourself. The freely available technology and the charity foundation have made treatment more accessible and reduced the practice of breeding donor children.

speaker: Chief
content: Just like how your thrill-seeking activities ultimately gave lost and bored city-dwellers a sense of belonging, while exposing those who had already strayed from the right path.
Your sincere words don't seem to affect Irrheia at all. She regards you with mockery, like she's watching a child who has just proudly proclaimed their belief that kindness is human nature.

speaker: Irrheia
content: So, you're saying that I'm a good person, huh? You've almost convinced me. So what's the Bureau's policy toward a kind soul like me? Surely you won't keep me detained here any longer?

speaker: Irrheia
content: Since you've confirmed I haven't done anything evil and that I pose little danger, shouldn't you just let me go now?
Hearing that, a gleam flashes past your eyes as you realize you've caught the crux of the matter.

speaker: Chief
content: But the MBCC's condition for releasing a Sinner is for them to be implanted with the shackles, to keep them under my supervision. As long as you meet this condition, you're certainly free to leave.

speaker: Chief
content: So, will you allow me to give you the shackles?
The smile on Irrheia's lips widens, as though she's been waiting for these exact words.

speaker: Irrheia
content: My dear Chief, you seem quite confident in your powers. Well, I don't mind a little conceit.

speaker: Irrheia
content: Very well. Then let me see just how much of my power these famous shackles of yours can actually restrain. I only hope... you won't regret this.
She extends her hand toward you invitingly, like an immortal witch awaiting a kiss on her hand. You round the desk and approach her, reaching out your hand as you gather your power.

speaker: Chief
content: More than the supervisory function, I've always valued the perceptive power of the shackles more. I certainly have faith in them and won't regret this. After all, once the shackles are "truly" implanted, I can guarantee you full freedom.

speaker: Chief
content: Both inside and outside the illusion... so long as you release me from this illusion as well.
The previously composed Irrheia suddenly jerks her head up, instinctively trying to withdraw her hand! But it's too late. You immediately seize her wrist and activate your power!

Crimson thorns burst out, each one piercing into Irrheia's fair skin, like the blood drawn from her countless times in childhood, splattered all over her body, like a grotesque, bloodthirsty tree sprouting wildly from her flesh!

The root-like thorns pierce into the very core of everything, shattering the space around you! You watch as the woman's skin, long hair, and clothing dissolve into pale golden sand, flowing ceaselessly into an enormous hourglass at the foundation of this space!

speaker: Chief
content: <color=#dg1f1f>If you won't give me freedom, then I'll have to seize it myself.</color>
The sand constructing the scene disperses. Your soul tumbles with a thud, fitting perfectly back into your body. You look around. To your surprise, you find yourself back in your own office.

Irrheia is right across from you, having just withdrawn her hand from the hourglass. The Aurum Secretum device shakes intensely, the swirling sand making a howl-like noise. You can still see irregular red light spikes pulsing and fading like heartbeats.

speaker: Chief
content: Did you really think the story would unfold smoothly according to your script, culminating in a classic, clichéd "happy ending"?

You instinctively activate the shackles. When the surroundings seem stable with no disruption, you confirm this isn't yet another layer of illusion, but reality. You lift your gaze to look Irrheia directly in the eyes.

speaker: Chief
content: Then you've certainly underestimated me. Perhaps you should spend more time studying The Secret History of the MBCC published by that tabloid.

Irrheia is neither flustered nor angered by your sarcasm. She leans forward slightly against the desk, casually brushing her cascade of hair once, seemingly unconcerned about your confrontation mere seconds ago.

speaker: Irrheia
content: Oh? What makes you say that?
Her amused tone reveals she isn't genuinely asking for an answer, but simply taunting you loftily, demanding that you respond to her challenge. And you're ready to take her on.

options: Because it would have been too predictable.

speaker: Chief
content: I never believed in that tragic past you showed me. After all, you let me restart too many times, enough for me to explore every corner, noticing the elements in your script that resembled other Sinners' stories.

speaker: Chief
content: If you didn't draw inspiration from The Secret History of the MBCC, then someone must have fed you with those stories, resulting in this script full of recycled ideas and familiar plot twists.

speaker: Irrheia
content: My, that's a rather harsh critique. Did you not enjoy this story? That's surprising. Isn't this exactly the kind of stereotypical narrative that everyone seems to love?

speaker: Irrheia
content: Dark family drama corrupts the innocent girl to become a Sinner, turning her into a madwoman in the attic, who is then redeemed by the wise savior and reclaims her own happiness. The gimmick, the melodrama, the heartwarming ending. It has everything.
Irrheia pretends not to get your meaning, but you refuse to dance around the subject with her any longer.

speaker: Chief
content: This has nothing to do with whether I enjoyed it or not. I'm not your customer, and I'm not going to write you a review for cashback. I came to you seeking an honest conversation, but you tried to deceive me with a clichéd story you've cobbled together.

speaker: Chief
content: As I've told you, my reality has always been stranger than fiction. I can spot the slightest incongruity in even the best story. And if this is your carefully crafted script, then maybe you're in fact not that good of a creator.

speaker: Chief
content: Though I shouldn't be surprised. Of course an Eastside white-collar worker with an ordinary lifestyle would believe that her own boredom is the only authentic reality. Your script is boring because you are a boring person surrounded by boring things.
This isn't the first time Irrheia has tried to deceive and manipulate you with her custom-made illusions and stories. You're deliberately provoking her, mocking her frivolous love for novelty.

speaker: Irrheia
content: ...Heh, perhaps you're right. Perhaps this is the root of everything.

She simply waves her hand. The notebook opens on its own, countless pages filled with cursive writing fluttering and interweaving as they turn rapidly. Surrounded by all these different universes, Irrheia acknowledges your criticism thoughtfully.

speaker: Irrheia
content: I noticed the bottleneck long ago. I turned out new scripts, tried new themes, cast new NPC actors, and even deliberately guided the actions of those more "creative" players... but nothing worked.

speaker: Irrheia
content: The thrills in my scripts grew fewer and faded faster. Everyone's choices became predictable... I discovered that even the one thing that could pull me from that void of emptiness was beginning to fail.

speaker: Irrheia
content: I certainly didn't want to return to that numbing existence, so I began searching for new variables, and I managed to find you. But perhaps... you're just a timely, pleasant surprise, while the real problem lies elsewhere.

One by one, pages detach from the notebook and scatter everywhere, then rearrange themselves in some unknown order before slipping back into the spine. You suspect Irrheia might be taking inventory of her past creations.

speaker: Irrheia
content: Nothing new under the sun. I've witnessed countless people let their choices be shaped by their experiences. The same applies to my own works as well, hence the loops and repetitions... the recycled ideas and clichés...

speaker: Chief
content: By bottleneck, do you mean your scripts were declining in quality and no longer felt thrilling to you or provided escapism? Did you start creating these scripts for this reason in the first place?

speaker: Chief
content: The manipulation and real-time adjustments in your scripts are just extensions of your creative process, aren't they? But is the person sharing all this with me the real you, or just another improvised character you've created, another "witch" in your story?

speaker: Irrheia
content: Looks like you've become quite the murder mystery game expert. Indeed. A rich girl who was used as a human blood bag for years, then returned with her superpower for revenge? Such a trendy character concept. I might have made it up myself.

speaker: Irrheia
content: Perhaps the real me is actually just a nine-to-five office worker who writes scripts, occasionally putting on costumes and acting out roles just to earn my performance bonus.
Irrheia smiles noncommittally, seemingly pleased that you're following her rhythm. But you won't fall into her rhythm.

speaker: Chief
content: Yes, I could certainly take guesses, but why would I? I don't care which parts of you are real and which are not. As Chief of the MBCC, I'm only concerned with your safety under Mania, and whether you're using that power to influence others.

speaker: Chief
content: Just like you only care about these so-called thrills. They're the reason you create your scripts, manipulate events, and exhaust yourself trying to escape the MBCC. As long as something keeps you entertained, you couldn't care less when exactly I saw through your act.

speaker: Chief
content: And now, I've successfully planted the shackles within you. From now on, whenever you abuse Mania with harmful intent, I'll know immediately and be able to intervene. This is what I want, and I've already achieved it.

You open your palm, revealing crimson light flickering between your fingers. Irrheia stares at it, seeming to contemplate your true intentions behind all this. From this moment, the dynamic between you finally begins to shift.

speaker: Irrheia
content: Fine, fine, put away your victory trophy. No need to flaunt it in my face. Though... I don't mind it when you're being a show-off. It's fun to see you like this, my dear Chief.

speaker: Chief
content: I'm not like you. I don't wear different masks. Whether inside or outside your scripts, I'm just myself. That interrogation might have been staged, but my words weren't.

speaker: Chief
content: I promised that if you allowed me to give you the shackles, I would grant you freedom. I'll keep my word. I'll even help you break free from what's been eating away at you all this time. Boredom.

speaker: Chief
content: In truth, I've always preferred to build trust with Sinners, and that begins with mutual understanding. I called you to my office for this reason. We need to clarify what we each want and be completely honest with one another.
You gesture with an open palm toward the notebook placed between you.

speaker: Chief
content: Before you dragged me into that scenario of yours, I thought we'd already achieved this. We discussed how you used the emotions that erupted in your scripts to fill the emptiness of your reality.

speaker: Irrheia
content: The more extreme the content, the more vibrant the medium, the emptier ordinary life feels once the screen goes dark. I was tired of those packaged experiences that never reached the core or the flesh, even though I was the one creating them. I needed something that could truly move me.

speaker: Irrheia
content: So I played the Witch, making my customers fight for their lives, cry out in pain, find their courage on my stage... The stories were fake, but the emotions were real. For some fleeting moments, I felt ignited by their emotions, borrowing their racing heartbeats to feel alive again.

speaker: Irrheia
content: Yes, all stories eventually end, which is precisely why one should seize the present experience. The virtual thrills and connections may fade away, but isn't that better than spending an entire lifetime numbed by emptiness and absence?
You repeat Irrheia's words, raising your eyes to meet hers.

speaker: Chief
content: I don't fully agree with your philosophy, but I understand you and trust your motives aren't dangerous. I thought that script... the one about being honest about your past, offered a deeper form of connection.

speaker: Chief
content: But it is just another script you've cobbled together. No one knows how much of it is real. I'm curious, what are you really looking for in all this? Do you truly believe these repetitive scenarios can give you what you need?
Irrheia freezes momentarily, then lets out a quiet laugh. She taps a finger between the pages of the notebook, then slowly withdraws it, like treating a toy she's tired of.

speaker: Irrheia
content: A script is just a script. As for its meaning to me... isn't that already clear to you? It's full of possibilities and can be replayed endlessly. Once I introduce new variables, it can generate new excitement and save me from boredom.

speaker: Chief
content: Yes, it is clear to me. But what's clearer to me is that they're becoming less effective for you. Have you considered how much longer these predictable scenarios can deceive your clients? Or how much longer they can deceive you?

speaker: Chief
content: When you finally realize you've completely run out of inspiration and nothing stimulates you anymore, what will you do then? What will become of your scripts?

speaker: Irrheia
content: Yes, what should become of them...

Under your persistent questioning, Irrheia lowers her eyes to the hefty notebook and falls into deep thought. You don't interrupt her, but you can sense Mania flowing and swirling, gathering strength in dark undercurrents.

Suddenly, she throws up her hand, and the surging Mania splashes in all directions. You can almost feel its spiraling trajectory like a sandstorm, reminiscent of what you've experienced in WhiteSands, as white grains whip past your cheeks! You barely stop yourself from activating the shackles!

speaker: Chief
content: What are you...!

But you stand transfixed by the scene before you. The Mania isn't whipping up sand grains, but the pages containing whole universes from the notebook. They swirl around Irrheia, being crumpled and torn apart!
She's actively withdrawing the Mania power she has infused into the notebook! The pages aren't being destroyed by outside force, but by their owner!

speaker: Irrheia
content: These scripts are merely props, and creating them is just one way I amuse myself. Now that I know I'm not even that good at it, and I have you, a constant variable who always manages to surprise me...

speaker: Irrheia
content: So what if I stop making them?
Irrheia picks up the notebook's empty shell and casually tosses it behind her, clearly relishing the undisguised shock on your face.

speaker: Irrheia
content: Don't look so surprised. You know perfectly well that I only write these scripts for fun... But these thrills are fleeting. Once they get old, no one cares about them anymore.

speaker: Irrheia
content: So what if I tear up these scripts that no longer entertain me? What does it matter if I find something even more exciting and stop creating altogether? The only thing I ever want is to pursue new thrills.
You collect yourself, not wanting her to see you waver as your mind races, weighing whether you should see her opinion, even more radical than you anticipated, as a good or bad thing.
Meanwhile, Irrheia watches you with obvious interest, savoring every reaction of yours with joy.

speaker: Irrheia
content: My dear Chief, are you feeling nervous right now? Don't worry. After seeing so many Sinners' stories, I understand why you're always probing each Sinner's inner world, searching for their deepest obsessions...

speaker: Irrheia
content: Because obsessions are our anchors. Surveillance and perception aren't infallible. You prefer to nip the problems in the bud, but for things beyond your control, you can only rely on these anchors to restrain and limit them.

speaker: Irrheia
content: People with fewer, more abstract obsessions are more dangerous to you, like me. You've been provoking me all this time, pushing me to admit my scripts have become useless... but my scripts are my anchor.

The carefree, almost languid-looking Witch finally bares her fangs, closing in relentlessly with razor-sharp words, making your heart clench. No wonder she's dubbed the Witch of Rewind. She knows human nature like a supernatural being who's been alive for centuries.

speaker: Irrheia
content: Without it, what else can you use to control me? Unless... you already know the answer. Go ahead then, say it. What's your trump card? What's this antidote you've found?

But as you look up at her eyes, unusually bright with excitement, you feel unexpectedly calm. What glimmers in her eyes is clearly anticipation, not hostility. She doesn't want to defeat you, but is only curious about your response in a plight.

Just as she did in all those scripts and loops you've been in before, she casually flicks her fingertips while relentlessly pressing her questions. What she seeks has always been the same: change, thrills, surprises.

She's right. People with fewer obsessions are harder to control. But someone with desires as simple and direct as hers doesn't actually care how you deliver what she wants. Stories inevitably end, but experiences alone are real.

speaker: Chief
content: Just as I know your past was never a mediocre script that needed rewriting, neither is this reality. The one trapped in loops isn't me. It's you. What imprisons you in endless boredom isn't reality, but the loops themselves.

Irrheia tilts her head back slightly, as though she's just read an absurd plot twist. Her lips curve into a smile, though she doesn't speak. A more genuine, expectant smile gradually reaches her eyes, tinged with both playful mockery and curiosity.

The scripts, the manipulation, and the narrative control are all just the Witch's attempts to stave off boredom. Yet these safe, "controlled" experiments only trap her in a vicious cycle of increasing monotony.

speaker: Irrheia
content: Interesting. Do continue, my dear Chief. Let me see what other fresh theories you've developed.

speaker: Chief
content: I believe you already know. These scripts which you can rewrite, enrich, and reset may be safe and convenient, giving you endless opportunities to explore, but no matter how many times you try, they can never give you that soul-stirring excitement you're seeking.

speaker: Chief
content: Because choices you can undo at will are never truly impactful. They can't crack your shell or leave any lasting impression. Deep down, you already know that some things are precious because you only get one chance at them.

speaker: Chief
content: Didn't that Outlander's death shake you precisely because of this reason? If it had merely been the "permadeath" of a character, would it still have affected you so deeply?

For the first time, all expressions vanish from Irrheia's face. This should make it appear stiff like a mask, but with that thin veneer of a smile stripped away, you realize this might be her true, pensive face.

speaker: Chief
content: Seeking thrills in these scripted cycles will never be truly satisfying. If you are determined to escape this boredom that ensnares you, I suggest you shed your armor, step out of these cycles into reality, and experience the world firsthand.

speaker: Chief
content: You could even leave Eastside behind, travel to distant places, and see other parts of the world, like the Outlands. It may not be easy or entirely safe, but I guess danger is rarely boring, isn't it?

Her fingertips tap against her cheek. Her gaze sharpens for an instant, then quickly softens again. Her smile has returned almost imperceptibly, but it's like still water disturbed by the wind, ripples spreading underneath.

speaker: Irrheia
content: ...How strange. Compared to all the cycles I've experienced, your life has surely been shorter and less substantial, yet you consistently do and say the most unexpected, truth-revealing things. Why is that?

options: Perhaps because reality is always stranger than fiction.

speaker: Chief
content: During my first murder mystery game, you asked me if my complex experiences had made me unable to understand ordinary people's boredom and aspirations. I think there may be some truth to that.

speaker: Chief
content: I've certainly had some... extraordinary encounters that most people will never experience, or even imagine. That's how I learned that stories need to be logical, but reality doesn't. The truth is, reality always catches you off guard.

speaker: Chief
content: I wouldn't call all these experiences pleasant, but I've certainly never been bored. If that's the kind of life you're after, I believe nothing can stop you from changing your path now and stepping out of Eastside, this cocoon you've been living in.
Irrheia listens quietly, her fingers still resting against her cheek. The rhythmic tapping pauses for a moment.

speaker: Irrheia
content: Stories need to be logical, but reality doesn't... So reality always triumphs over stories. Is that why those of us who seek solace in stories are doomed to emptiness and ruin?

speaker: Chief
content: Not at all. I don't think reality is inherently better than fiction. Sometimes people need the safe, accessible escape that virtual entertainment provides. What I'm trying to say is, if simple stories no longer satisfy you and instead drive you toward the extremes...

speaker: Chief
content: Then perhaps the real issue lies in your reality itself. Stepping out to experience more of reality might help you find what you're truly seeking. And when you eventually return to stories, those real experiences can enrich them.

speaker: Irrheia
content: Oh? So you'd let me return to stories and scripts? You were the one who called my scripts mediocre and goaded me into abandoning them all. Now suddenly you're not worried about how dangerous and uncontrollable they are?

speaker: Chief
content: I am. Even the scripts you find unbearably dull are still dangerous enough for ordinary people with weaker minds.
At this point in the conversation, her tone no longer sounds provocative and has become more playful, so you also decide to be frank.

speaker: Chief
content: But that doesn't mean I don't care about your quality of life as a Sinner. I want ordinary people to live safely, but I also want you to be happy. That's the real reason I think you should go out and explore.
You sigh, rummage through your desk, and pull out a plain notepad normally used for recording key details during interrogations. You slide it across to Irrheia.

speaker: Chief
content: I'd even encourage you to record what you experience. They could make excellent material for your work. I never expected you'd actually tear up your notebook... So please, take this one instead.

speaker: Chief
content: If you trust me and choose to step out of your shell into the real world... then I think you'll find a notebook useful. Remarkable events blur together easily in memory, but stories last forever once they're told. And don't worry, you'll have plenty of readers at the Bureau.
Irrheia stares at the notepad, her expression darkens momentarily, then she suddenly smiles. It carries a hint of mischief, as if she finds your suggestion amusing.

speaker: Irrheia
content: You really are full of surprises. I have to admit, when you first walked into my shop, I never expected you'd be so... reckless, but fun. What's in it for you, encouraging me like this?

speaker: Chief
content: No matter who you really are, I know your sole motivation is seeking twists and escapism. And now, I want you to break free from the endless cycle and the prison of boredom too. Our goals are the same.
She doesn't respond. The interrogation room falls into momentary silence as you wait patiently. Finally, Irrheia leans forward, reaches for the notepad, and opens it.
You expect her to examine it for some hidden trick, but she simply turns to the first page, takes one of your pens, and writes a single line.

speaker: Irrheia
content: "Real twists and surprises are found in reality."
The elegant cursive writing trails in a long final stroke, like the opening line of a new script. You can't help but look up at her.

speaker: Irrheia
content: Since you've brought me so many surprises, I suppose I'll try this theme you've suggested. Even though I love chaos and surprises... perhaps you're indeed the one true variable in my life?

speaker: Irrheia
content: As for that notebook... I'll leave it with you. You've written the opening act of this script, and for the rest... I'll continue writing it until I've experienced the vast world you spoke of.

Yet another lengthy field assignment is finally over. You drag your exhausted body and push open the door to your lounge, ready to black out. But before you sit down, your eyes are drawn to an open notepad on the desk. It doesn't belong to you.

speaker: Chief
content: The writing, the format... A script? Has Irrheia returned?!

You flip through several pages and discover they contain an incredibly detailed account of your recent field assignment. The writing is lyrical and accurate, capturing even your exact words and the decisions you made.
There's no signature on the script, but the familiar cursive handwriting clearly belongs to Irrheia.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, I was just coming to find you... Copies of this script seem to be circulating throughout the Bureau. They're being distributed as a murder mystery game prop. It's now a popular form of entertainment among Sinners.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Although the sensitive information has been censored or altered, the Intelligence Security Department has still flagged it as a Level B risk. Also, a note appeared on my desk with Sinner Irrheia's handwriting. It says...

It's been a while, my dear Chief. I've explored all the places you recommended before returning to DisCity. Syndicate, WhiteSands, Fraser, the farlands... they were indeed wonderful, but still not as interesting as being by your side.

I hope you've kept my room for me. After skipping work to cooperate with your investigation and taking this extended unpaid leave, my boss has already fired me. There's no place for a jobless person in Eastside, so you'll have to take responsibility for that.
You fold up the note and shake your head with a smile.

speaker: Chief
content: I knew she would come back. As for this script... fine, let her be, seeing as no real sensitive information was leaked, and the circulation is limited within the Bureau.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...What's going on? Have we been sitting here long, or is it just me?
After countless missions, the smooth ride in the back of the car has become a second office. But today, the stillness is different. It has nothing to do with your driver's expertise.

speaker: Nightingale
content: My apologies, Chief. We've hit unexpected congestion. I've already notified the team on-site and advised them to prepare a contingency plan in case of your absence.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: My absence? A traffic jam this bad? Can't we get traffic control to clear a path?

You roll down the window. A cacophony of car horns assaults your ears, but underneath it, something else prickles your investigator's instincts. Protesting, shouting, arguing, the shove and scuffle of a crowd. The very air feels charged and unstable.

Compelled, you step out and scan toward the source of the commotion. Through the crowd gathered on either side of the road, you make out a promotional banner stretched between buildings. It hangs now, pulled crooked and askew.

speaker: Nightingale
content: That's Rollins's group. They promote "DisCity Primacy"—anti-Outland, advocating for relocated settlements under centralized control. His secretary has been canvassing across Eastside, collecting signatures.
Noticing the subtle furrow in your brow, Nightingale steps out from the passenger seat and closes the distance. She leans in, her voice a murmur at your ear, translating the banner's message.

speaker: Nightingale
content: But Rollins's exclusionism has drawn opposition, mainly from immigrants and those close to them. They're not large in number, but today a registered protest march happens to be passing through this same street...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Just a coincidence? Feels more like a clash waiting to happen...
What seems like a coincidence is just another tremor in DisCity's ideological cold war. It's no accident that the authorities are holding back, reluctant to step into the line of fire.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Precisely. That's also why direct intervention would be difficult... And honestly, I doubt either side would listen to us right now.

You frown, looking through the gridlock to the disorder ahead. You don't need your friend in the Speaker's office bending your ear with complaints to feel it firsthand: the turbulent undercurrents that have swirled around DisCity's foreign policy since the Great Expo.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I get it. When emotions run high, reason doesn't stand a chance... But I don't believe there's nothing we can do.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, we must be cautious. Any move you make could be amplified or twisted by others...

You are no longer the fringe official you once were; you now understand the weight your influence carries. Yet, as an expert on Mania, you also know how easily a tide of unchecked emotion can unravel the very fabric you seek to mend.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Given the choice, I'd stay out of political games. But the MBCC can't ignore a conflict this volatile, not when it risks triggering a Mania outbreak.
Nightingale seems about to say more, but you simply pat her shoulder and plunge into the stalled traffic, navigating toward the heart of the commotion.

speaker: Young Female Voice
content: I-I understand how you feel, but I can't just leave! This is my responsibility. Our supporters are counting on us to—

speaker: Angry Male Voice
content: How could you possibly understand how we feel?! You get paid to push us out, to hand your boss a political win! <size=45>Get out! Get out of our neighborhood!!!</size>

speaker: Arrogant Male Voice
content: Linda, stop wasting your breath on them! You represent the councilor as his secretary, so act like it! This is the golden chance to make our stance clear!

speaker: Linda
content: But... I...

Weaving through the traffic, you take in the confrontation. The two groups are squared off, a wall of tension between them. Positioned uneasily at the front of Rollins's side is his young secretary. She looks utterly out of her depth, pushed forward but frozen, all color gone from her face.

She is still green, lacking the steely resolve of the men behind her. With both sides at a breaking point, her hesitation is a fatal pause. The immigrants read it as defiance, and a shove sends her stumbling!

speaker: Angry Male Voice
content: If you won't leave, we'll make you! We're not scared of your councilor. We've got nothing left to lose anyway!

A roar of approval swells behind him, and the crowd surges. Linda's scream is swallowed by the chaos as she clutches her folder like a lifeline. The rest of Rollins's staff scatters, and the standoff explodes into a frantic, shoving brawl.

The eruption was faster than you'd ever anticipated. Teeth gritted, you shove your way into the fray. With a handful of other concerned bystanders, you wedge between the sides, arms raised, a human buffer against the chaos.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Everyone, stop! You'll regret this! Stop it! Violence solves nothing!

speaker: Crowd
content: Get out! Get out of here!!

speaker: Crowd
content: You are the ones who should get out of DisCity, filthy Outlanders!!!

At first, your desperate buffer works. The immediate clash eases. But the momentum behind the crowd is a force of its own, a tide of raw emotion that keeps pushing, oblivious to the fragile line trying to hold it back. Within moments, you are swept apart.

Amid the chaos, a pained cry cuts through from one of the peacekeepers, likely hurt. But the sound doesn't register. The crowd is beyond reason now, past caring for those who tried to make peace, or even for themselves.

You try to push toward the injured person, but the crowd tosses you like flotsam in a current. Helpless, you're shoved forward until you're suddenly face-to-face with the secretary. She's also pinned by the crush of her own "supporters," frantically fumbling for her terminal.

speaker: Linda
content: This is going all wrong...! Someone... Can someone help us... Right, the councilor! I'll call the councilor...!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Ms. Linda, I don't think that's going to help...

speaker: Linda
content: He... hung up... Why would he...?

You let out a sigh as you watch Linda, lost and waiting for a hero who doesn't exist. Then it clicks: she isn't just caught in this—she's the cause. Pull her out, and the storm might lose its center. Steeling yourself, you move to shield her, pushing firmly toward the edge of the mob.

speaker: Linda
content: Ah! What... What is that?! Did Keylan send it to guide us?!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What are you—?!
Linda clutches at your coat with a sharp cry. You assume stress has taken her, but then you follow her pointing hand skyward. There, against the chaos, hangs an unexpected guide.

It is a dove. A snow-white dove of peace, so stunningly pristine it seems to have alighted from an oil painting. Something glints in its beak, and it scatters a trail of shimmering particles, like powdered light, impossible to look away from.

It beats its wings with fluid grace, gliding toward you as if drawn. After circling overhead, securing your gaze, it drifts purposefully away as if beckoning you toward the right path. It feels like a miracle made manifest.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Does it... want us to follow? A bird can fly, but we...

All doubt stills in your throat as something even more miraculous unfolds. Where the dove flies, heads turn as one, gazes lifting like a tide. The simmering anger in the crowd softens, then dissolves, and the conflict simply... unravels.
It is like the legend of a saint parting the sea. Before you, the dove's shimmering dust drifts downward, laying a path through the chaos—a corridor of calm, untouched by conflict.
Confusion remains, but you act. Gripping Linda's hand, you press forward, meeting no resistance. She murmurs in awe as you walk, but your focus is on the luminous dust coating your fingers.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: A faint Mania reaction... A Sinner? But this ability... Forget it. Now isn't the time!

Worried the miracle won't last, you push all thoughts aside. With Linda's hand tight in yours, you quicken your pace, then break into a final, desperate sprint—bursting free just as the crowd begins to close in again.
[Make a grand entrance]
Oh my, do be careful, Chief ${PlayerName}. And you as well, Ms. Secretary. Rushing about like that, you might have gotten hurt. Daniel, did you perhaps fly a little too eagerly?

You brace for impact, but instead, you're caught. A pair of steady, gloved hands halts your fall. Silk brushes your cheek, and the air fills with a deep, tender fragrance, soft as feathers. In surprise, you look up—

Before you stands a woman dressed in elegant pale gold and white, a gentle smile on her lips as she steadies you and Linda. Several paces behind her, watchful figures in black stand poised—her guards, you assume.

Yet her gentle reproach isn't for them. Perched on her shoulder, the dove opens its beak and coos softly, feigning innocence. It is the very same bird that moments ago parted the crowd like a miracle.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're the one who saved us? You're a Sinner, and you know who I am?
I am indeed a Sinner, but I haven't saved you just yet, Chief. The commotion continues, and emotions are still high... This isn't quite the moment for introductions.
Allow me to address the conflict first. Afterwards, we can make proper acquaintances. Shall we?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're planning to use your power on all these civilians? In their current state, exposure to Mania could have severe consequences.
My power? Oh, there's no need for concern. I understand all too well that power can only bring temporary calm. Lasting peace must be nurtured through genuine understanding.
She guides you and Linda behind her, smooths the edge of her glove with a subtle tug, and turns. Her smile is soft, yet carries a resolve that feels like a promise.
Please, don't worry. Facilitating cooperation and compromise, even in the most hopeless clashes of interest, is my profession. It's what I do best.

speaker: Linda
content: What... What are you going to do?

To your surprise, it's Linda—the perpetually flustered secretary—who gives voice to the question hanging in your own mind. She clutches the woman's sleeve, gazing up with a look of desperate hope, like someone reaching for a lifeline in deep water.

To listen carefully for what each side truly needs, and to help them find common ground through dialogue. At its heart, peace and negotiation are simply about conversation. It's not as difficult as it seems, dear.
Peace and negotiation...? The dove, the black-clad guards, and a recent call from an old friend. You feel the pieces click into place, and the woman's identity sharpens in your mind.

speaker: Margaret
content: Everyone, my name is Margaret. I once served as DisCity's Outland Affairs Officer in Fraser. I understand the concerns on both sides. Could we all pause for a moment, and simply listen? Would you grant me that?

This is the peacemaker who once orchestrated the defense against Fraser's takeover of the new Hypercube mine. Now, with practiced grace, she steps into the fray, her dove Daniel rising beside her. Together, they command the crowd's focus and begin to calm the storm.

She stands unwavering before the heat of their stares, with confusion, fury, and skepticism washing over her. Yet her voice stays calm, her words flowing like a clear stream, finding their way into every listening heart.

speaker: Margaret
content: My friends, in Fraser I witnessed countless conflicts rooted in differing interests and beliefs. Everyone wants to protect themselves, to secure what benefits them—and there is nothing inherently wrong with that. It is human nature to seek advantage and avoid harm.
At her words, cheers erupt from Rollins's side, while the immigrants seethe, barely containing their fury. Yet Margaret remains unshaken, raising both hands in a calming, steadying gesture.

speaker: Margaret
content: But first, let's ask ourselves: is there truly a conflict of interest among us right here? Looking around, I see no outsiders, only fellow Disians. And that reminds me... I am truly home again. It brings me a sense of peace.

speaker: Margaret
content: Isn't that what you see as well?

speaker: Crowd
content: Of course it is!
A ripple of laughter runs through the assembly. Some faces burn with shame, but not a single voice rises in dissent.

speaker: Margaret
content: Thank you. Let me say this clearly: since we are all Disians, what stands between us is not conflict, only disagreement. We are brothers and sisters. No one should be driven away for holding a different view.

speaker: Margaret
content: Some believe origins should determine rights. Others disagree. These are differing perspectives, and fortunately, DisCity's system allows every voice to be heard.

speaker: Margaret
content: In Fraser, the Senate silenced the farlanders. In the end, they lost not only trust but the Hypercube mine as well. DisCity will not repeat that mistake. Whether you support Councilor Rollins's proposal or oppose it, you have every right to speak.
You hear Margaret's voice grow firmer, her firsthand account stilling the crowd. But then another voice cuts in, slashing through the calm she has so carefully woven.

speaker: Angry Male Voice
content: But we don't have a councilor who represents us! Our voices never reach the ones in power!

speaker: Margaret
content: Are you so certain? Who says a future councilor cannot come from among you? Do not be afraid to speak up. In DisCity, there will always be people like me ready to ensure your voice is heard, so that true dialogue can take root.
Margaret turns to the young immigrant with an encouraging smile. Then, with a glance over her shoulder, she motions for Linda to step forward.

speaker: Margaret
content: For example... this young lady right here.

speaker: Margaret
content: Indeed. Ms. Linda, you never came here to silence anyone, did you? Everyone is seeking a platform. Your role is to gather voices, and I imagine you wouldn't mind gathering theirs as well?

speaker: Margaret
content: In DisCity, decisions are forged through debate. Councilor Rollins has always been confident, never one to shy from a challenge. I believe opposing voices will only strengthen his resolve, and that of his supporters.
Linda freezes, her eyes fixed on Margaret's serene profile as if beholding something divine. It takes her a long, suspended moment before she gathers herself and hurries to comply.

speaker: Linda
content: Y-yes! Neither Councilor Rollins nor any of us fear a fair challenge! We will prove that our beliefs are sound, that they align with the interests and voices of all Disians!

speaker: Linda
content: If you're willing to share your views with me, I'll make sure they reach the councilor!

speaker: Crowd
content: They've said it themselves... This is a real chance...

speaker: Crowd
content: Right! Well said! We're not afraid of any challenge! No matter what pretty lies some might spin, the people of DisCity will see the truth!
Guided by Margaret, Linda's rhetoric becomes unexpectedly polished. She strikes a public stance that earns nods from the immigrants while placating the hardliners among her own.

You watch from the sidelines as Margaret defuses what could have become a large-scale riot with practiced ease. This DisCity's Outland Affairs Officer, you concede, has more than earned her reputation.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This is my first time seeing a DisCity Outland Affairs Officer in action. I'm impressed, Ms. Margaret.

With the conflict expertly defused, you and Nightingale move to disperse the crowd and restore order. Margaret soon finishes her final instructions to Linda and rejoins you to resume your conversation.

speaker: Margaret
content: As long as one listens earnestly and engages in genuine dialogue, a temporary peace isn't so difficult to achieve. I haven't done anything remarkable, Chief. I'm certain you could do the same.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No need to be modest. What you pulled off was nearly magical. If I hadn't watched it myself, I might have suspected your Sinner power was at play.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But I have to admit, I didn't expect DisCity's peace ambassador to Fraser to be an unregistered Sinner.
Your probe catches Margaret off guard for a moment. But she shows no offense, answering instead with a touch of apology in her tone:

speaker: Margaret
content: Oh, how careless of me! I neglected to mention the most relevant detail. My apologies, Chief. Allow me to reintroduce myself: I am Margaret Kervoz, formerly classified as an S-Class Sinner.

speaker: Margaret
content: I was stationed in Fraser prior to this and never registered with the MBCC. Under protocol, my first task upon returning to DisCity is to report to you.
She turns and extends her hand toward a guard, but he pointedly ignores the gesture. Instead, he steps past her entirely and places the folder directly into your hands.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This is... an interrogation request? Naming you as the subject?

speaker: Margaret
content: Yes. All pertinent details should be inside. I'd prefer not to discuss the matter further here, where there are too many prying eyes.

Though the guard's act borders on insolence, Margaret's serene smile never wavers, warm and steady as a spring breeze. She shows no hint of displeasure—if anything, her expression turns thoughtful, her attention settling quietly on you.

speaker: Margaret
content: To be truthful, the MBCC was my first stop after arriving. But I was told you were away on duty, and I understand your current equipment isn't suited to fully restrain an S-Class Sinner. I didn't wish to place your staff in a difficult position, so I decided to find you directly.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're being awfully cooperative about this. You're hailed as a hero in DisCity, but the first thing you have to do after returning is ask me to shackle and interrogate you... Don't you think it's unfair?

You don't need to read the request to sense the dissonance. Officially, DisCity has welcomed the farlands' independence and the ownership transfer of the Hypercube mine with open arms. But you suspect Margaret's true position is like her elegant attire—
Splendid at first glance, but on closer look, dulled by the fine dust of a long and weary road. And if the higher-ups want her interrogated, they must already suspect the gilt is wearing thin.

If you can sense the treachery at play, Margaret is certainly no fool. Yet her smile remains seamless, as if she holds no bitterness toward DisCity's leadership for discarding her the moment she became inconvenient.

speaker: Margaret
content: Of course. I've always believed that a sincere voice has nothing to fear from scrutiny. This interrogation is simply another form of dialogue between us. I'm not afraid, so I see no injustice in it.

For all her genuine warmth and deliberate courtesy, you detect something immovable at her core. She might offer more cooperation than any Sinner before her, yet you know this interrogation won't be a simple exchange of questions and answers.

...In N.F. 115, on the eve of <color=#fb9259>the Great Expo</color>, she utilized classified networks to relay critical intelligence from Fraser concerning the Aurum Secretum Warriors. Due to administrative system failures during the <color=#fb9259>Speaker Election</color>, the transmission was delayed, preventing the intelligence from achieving its intended strategic impact...

...Via internal reassignments within the Luminaris Society, she identified anomalies related to <color=#fb9259>BR-005</color>, though insufficient time precluded direct intervention. Concurrently, Fraser initiated a <color=#fb9259>pre-war purge</color>, resulting in the continuous exposure of informants. Operational focus shifted to the rescue and relocation of compromised operatives...

...She spearheaded the sabotage of Fraser's <color=#fb9259>Unity Gala</color>, exposing their strategic manipulation of the farlands and creating significant diplomatic rifts. However, the <color=#fb9259>Farland Alliance</color> subsequently declared independence, and the BR-005 Hypercube mine recovery operation ultimately failed...

You set down the thick stack of documents: Margaret's complete service record, transcripts of the intelligence she transmitted during her years undercover in Fraser, and surveillance logs from other DisCity operatives assigned to monitor her while she was stationed there.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Margaret. First daughter of the <color=#fb9259>Kervoz</color> family, a founding house of DisCity and Paradeisos nobility. Diplomatic envoy to Fraser, philanthropist, art connoisseur, salon hostess, S-Class Sinner...
Your fingertip traces the aliases and titles scattered through the pages, finally settling on the signature at the bottom of a classified dispatch.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Senior Agent, <color=#fb9259>Peace Dove</color>.

DisCity's entire intelligence network in Fraser was built almost single-handedly by her. For years, a continuous stream of high-value intelligence flowed back, securing DisCity a decisive strategic advantage.

Winning over the farlands and securing the BR-005 Hypercube mine in WhiteSands was to be her final, crowning mission, but she failed. It gave her political enemies the opening they needed, allowing them to frame it not as a setback, but as deliberate betrayal, and demand this investigation.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But what's her gain in this? She's Paradeisos elite. Her record as an agent is spotless. She has fame, money, and influence. What could Fraser—or the farlands—possibly offer her that DisCity hasn't already?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Calling it betrayal... doesn't add up, for Fraser or the farlands. And everyone makes mistakes. Ordering a serious interrogation over this just makes the higher-ups look like they're grasping at straws. Almost funny, really.

...The old foxes at the top couldn't have missed this. Yet they ordered the interrogation anyway, even burned her classified Sinner status just to hand you the case. You, of all people. What do they see in you?
There's only one answer: your <color=#fb9259>shackles</color>.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Margaret knows who I am. Naturally, she knows what they're after. And she still agreed—even made it clear to me that she isn't afraid...
This is a political duel between Margaret and her political enemies, and you stand between them. Your shackles could dig for her secrets, or defend her truth.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: We'll see who's running the game, and who's just another piece on the board.

You organize the documents, making your final preparations before the interrogation. You steel your resolve, for whatever is to come, and to show those who sought to use you that you are not their instrument. You are here by your own judgment.
You will be no one's pawn. Your power serves one purpose alone: to find the truth, and to judge what is right.

You pull out a chair and sit, lifting your eyes to meet Margaret's. A faint, knowing smile rests on her lips, her posture perfectly poised. From her refined makeup to the elegant line of her dress, she is an image of flawless, unassailable grace.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Morning, Margaret. Hope the Bureau didn't treat you too poorly for your first night here.

speaker: Margaret
content: Good morning, Chief. I rested well, thank you. Though... and I hope this doesn't come across as rude... I would still very much prefer this to be my only stay here.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This interrogation room's for finding answers, not making things hard. Ms. Margaret, if you're honest with me, and you're innocent, we'll both get what we need.

speaker: Margaret
content: How reassuring. It seems we share the same goal. I couldn't ask for better. If only my so-called colleagues in Fraser were half as agreeable, my work would be far simpler.

speaker: Margaret
content: I've always believed honesty enables dialogue, and dialogue enables mutual peace. But as my presence here suggests... not everyone shares that belief. It appears quite a few "friends" hold rather different convictions.
Margaret's face breaks into a genuine smile. The polished, diplomatic distance vanishes at once, replaced by a warmth and ease you didn't sense in her yesterday.
Sinners brought to the interrogation room are typically guarded, defensive. Margaret is only open. You can't quite decipher her angle, so for now, you keep probing.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Maybe those who aren't honest themselves assume openness is just another act? Or maybe it's like me. Do this job long enough, and you get professionally suspicious.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Most people avoid talking about their failures, but you brought yours up yourself. When someone breaks the pattern, I have to wonder... what are you hoping to gain?
Your direct question catches Margaret off guard for a second. But there's no sign of panic, only a light, amused laugh as she raises a hand to her lips.

speaker: Margaret
content: Then I'm afraid you've misread me. You're someone even the steely Langley speaks well of, and you've seen my file. I'm sure my little secrets are already laid bare before you.

speaker: Margaret
content: I assumed my maneuvering wouldn't escape your notice, so I chose candor, hoping it might earn your goodwill... and perhaps an earlier release. I didn't expect it would work against me.
Her openness in admitting her own calculations surprises you. However, it's the mention of your former superior's name that truly catches your attention.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Really? She "spoke well" of me? I didn't take Madam Langley for the type to discuss work with friends. Not many Paradeisos nobles choose to get their hands dirty. Is that what connected you two?

speaker: Margaret
content: Hmm... To be honest, it's difficult to say if Langley and I are friends. Even if I claimed we were, her answer might differ. We have differing perspectives, after all. Friction is inevitable.

speaker: Margaret
content: I suppose we are peers, more than anything. Kindred spirits, in a way. The sort who might lend a hand if circumstances allow—to one another, and to those who follow, like yourself.

Margaret rests the tip of her fan lightly against her cheek, considering your question. Her sincerity feels genuine, and her decision not to invoke her ties to Langley earns a subtle shift in your regard.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Mind if I ask what kind of friction? Just so we're clear. Are we talking "I'm a Fraser spy and she wants me dead," or more like "we disagree on which foot to put through the door first"?

speaker: Margaret
content: How humorous you are! But rest assured, I am no spy, nor have I ever accepted a single coin from Fraser. There's no need to trouble Langley and that gun of hers.
Your teasing draws a soft laugh from her. Sensing you've started to lower your guard, she meets your lightness with a playful quip of her own.

speaker: Margaret
content: Simply put, she sometimes finds me too naive, and I occasionally find her too pragmatic. Surely you've had similar... disagreements with her?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I imagine she sometimes sees me as a child throwing a fit. But you as well? You both came of age in turbulent times. You traveled the farlands with your father, an Outland Affairs Officer.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Oppression, independence, expansion, stability... DisCity has gone through a lot, and so have its people. It's only natural that she and I see things differently. But the DisCity you witnessed... shouldn't it be closer to the one Madam Langley knows?

speaker: Margaret
content: In Langley's words... perhaps I am too much of a dreamer. I know, no matter how much changes, chaos and conflict remain the themes of this city, of this world. And yet, I still believe...

speaker: Margaret
content: It is precisely because the world is this way that peace must remain our common pursuit. Our most fundamental one.
A flicker of bitterness crosses her smile, there and gone. What remains is a fierce, unmistakable resolve.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This "too naive" dream of yours... Is it peace?

speaker: Margaret
content: Yes. It sounds like such a grand word, the sort an Outland Affairs Officer should champion. But to me, it has always been something... much more personal.

speaker: Margaret
content: It's been a long time since I've spoken of what it truly means. Since you ask... would you care to hear it?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I can't think of a reason to say no. But may I ask... why tell me?

You watch Margaret weigh her words carefully, as if gathering her courage. For once, the unflappable Outland Affairs Officer seems less than sure. And in that vulnerability, you know this is where the real story begins.

speaker: Margaret
content: Because I've heard how you stabilized the West District and reopened the Hypercube mine. How you thwarted an Outland spy ring from undermining DisCity, and prevented BR-002 and BR-005 from causing far greater harm.

speaker: Margaret
content: None of that was easy, and yet you've come this far. My own work in Fraser has been... fraught. But whenever my spirit wavered, word of your deeds would find its way to me. It lifted me.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're talking about... me?
Margaret nods, her expression earnest.

speaker: Margaret
content: Yes, you. You showed me I am not alone in believing this road leads somewhere hopeful. We may have started in different places, seen through different eyes, but we've both witnessed what the Black Rings and war leave in their wake. We both want it to end.

speaker: Margaret
content: Traveling with my father changed me for the rest of my life. It showed me the suffering of ordinary people—something one never sees in Paradeisos—and it showed me the power of peace, of words.

speaker: Margaret
content: Truthfully, my father rarely prevailed against entrenched interests, and he faced constant danger. But on those few occasions he succeeded... countless lives were spared from war and torment.
Her voice holds a note of wistfulness, of memory held close. For a moment, you can almost see the girl she used to be, deeply moved by something she was too young to fully grasp.

speaker: Margaret
content: I wanted to be like him. That is why I returned to Paradeisos, why I left again for Fraser. Every path I've walked has been for that simple purpose. But such an ideal... it is delicate. Fragile.

speaker: Margaret
content: Sometimes I waver. I wonder if I truly am too naive. You may not realize it, but your actions have mended my missteps and encouraged me to keep going. For that, I must thank you.
