As a DisCity Outland Affairs Officer, her eloquence is no surprise. But her eyes speak more plainly; they are brimming with emotions too layered to name. You can feel their weight, the depth of her regard for you.
Faced with such an unguarded confession, your cheeks flush. You clear your throat, gently breaking the moment.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You'd never even met me. For all you knew, I could've been some glory-seeker playing hero, someone who didn't care about peace at all.

speaker: Margaret
content: Have you forgotten? I am not merely an Outland Affairs Officer, Chief. Since going undercover in Fraser to investigate Outland collusion with the Underground... I've seen my share of arrogant foxes and greedy hyenas.

speaker: Margaret
content: In diplomacy or covert work, any partnership requires common interest. Who comes out ahead in the end... well, that comes down to skill. I may not look it, but there are few who can match me.
As if sensing your bashfulness, Margaret gives a soft chuckle, a flicker of mischief in her gaze. She deftly dismantles the tender atmosphere she had just spun.
It's a considerate pivot, yet one that feels just as honest. You decide to match her openness with your own.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I understand your ideals. What I don't understand is why you became a secret agent. You could've followed your father's path. Just be a proper Outland Affairs Officer. Wouldn't that have served the same goal?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: When you call yourself naive, it's only relative to other agents, isn't it? I know you've had blood on your hands. I've read that you've been forced to leave people behind. Why choose to carry that?
The question lands like a touch to a bruise. Her expression tightens—a subtle, involuntary flinch—and she looks down, lost in a memory or a thought.

speaker: Margaret
content: To be honest... I thought the same for a long time. I refused to join Langley's 9th Agency. I told her I wanted no part in that kind of work.

speaker: Margaret
content: Back then, I believed an ideal peace could only be won through ideal means—that anything less would stain it beyond recognition. But that... pristine little conviction of mine didn't last long.
A shadow settles in her eyes as she says it, darkening her features.

speaker: Margaret
content: I wonder... if you recall the previous <color=#fb9259>Great Expo</color>.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...You mean the one where <color=#fb9259>BR-003</color> broke out?

speaker: Margaret
content: Yes. I was an Outland Affairs Officer stationed in Fraser at the time. I had spent years laying the groundwork, carefully persuading them to attend. I truly believed it would mark a new beginning for peace.

speaker: Margaret
content: But when I returned to DisCity with the delegation, ready to celebrate what we'd achieved... the Black Ring took everything. I didn't even have time to grieve. I was quietly conscripted, granted special clearance to become an advocate for weaponizing the Black Ring.

speaker: Margaret
content: I never believed the rhetoric, that weapons of deterrence could bring peace. But if not me, it would have been someone else. I swallowed my anger and told myself that at least with me involved, I could set limits. Soften the edges. Find room to maneuver.

speaker: Margaret
content: I fought to impose strict conditions on its use, then leveraged that to reduce stockpiles of weapons designed for mass civilian casualties. I told myself... some things cannot be done with clean hands.
A ripple of weariness passes over her features, betraying the real scars beneath the carefully constructed mask of history. This isn't a performance. This is something true, painfully so.
The shadow of regret remains, unhidden, in her expression. But as you extend a gesture of understanding, her smile resurfaces, graceful and composed once more.

speaker: Margaret
content: Thank you. When it was over, I declined their offer to stay. Instead, I requested a transfer back to Fraser. DisCity's vision of peace had... diverged too far from my own. I thought Fraser might be a better stage for what I hoped to achieve.

speaker: Margaret
content: What came after... well, you can read it in my file. An Outland Affairs Officer is always viewed with suspicion in Fraser. But fortunately, I had an excellent role model who helped me find my footing, barely.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: There's nothing "barely" about your record. From infiltration to building a network, every move was impressively precise. You became DisCity's most valuable asset in Fraser. But that's exactly why any slip-up makes them suspicious.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The farlands gained independence, Fraser was denied the Hypercubes, and it ended peacefully—an outcome that still favored DisCity. Even if it was your "slip-up," holding it against you seems... pretty greedy.
You understand, perhaps too clearly, the choices pressed upon her, the wars she gave everything to. Something tightens in your chest, a deep and genuine ache of empathy.
Noticing you've taken her side, Margaret seems to soften. A true smile touches her eyes, and her tone lifts, lightened by a hint of relief.

speaker: Margaret
content: I'm so glad we see it the same way. I had a feeling we might. But there are always those who miss the bigger picture, people who see nothing beyond their own gain, yet insist on meddling and throwing everything into chaos.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You sound like you've been through this before. Is this not your first interrogation?
She pauses, her cheeks puffing out just a touch. For a fleeting moment, she looks almost girlish, making no attempt to mask her flash of petulance.

speaker: Margaret
content: Naturally... Both DisCity and Fraser have too many nobles and officials blind to the common people. To them, casualty figures mean nothing. The only numbers that matter are the ones in their accounts.

speaker: Margaret
content: We lay our plans so carefully, negotiate a result... only for the hyenas to come snapping at our heels, eager to overturn the table. It happens far too often. Just thinking about it makes my blood boil.
In this moment, the woman before you seems a world apart from the flawless DisCity Outland Affairs Officer you first met. This is simply Margaret: vivid, human, and real. You can't help but smile.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So you do get angry.

speaker: Margaret
content: I'm only human, Chief. Peace is... a little hobby of mine. A private indulgence. Destroying it is like trampling a garden I've lovingly tended. Of course, I get angry.

speaker: Margaret
content: But such frustrations pass. What truly pains me is friction with kindred spirits. Working toward the same goal, yet getting in each other's way, unable to accomplish anything... That is what I find truly regrettable.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Are you saying... you and Madam Langley have had that kind of friction as well?
You ask out of genuine curiosity, expecting a lighthearted story. What follows is anything but.

speaker: Margaret
content: No, I'm referring to the recent farland independence. Sigh... I was quite fond of the young Campbell girl. Such determination and talent. I even arranged a suitable position for her within the Farland Alliance...

speaker: Margaret
content: But I didn't expect her cleverness to become a double-edged sword, leading the farland people away from the path I had envisioned. If this continues, it will be difficult for me to offer them further assistance. Theirs will become a road of thorns...
Margaret speaks with such casual candor that it takes you a moment to register the full gravity of what she's said.
You stop her, your mind already rewinding, scanning for anything you might have missed.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The farland independence? The young Campbell girl... You mean Hypatia? Adelaide's sister? You arranged a position for her in the Alliance?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Are you telling me that all of this was part of your plan from the beginning?
She meets your gaze, her gentle sincerity unwavering. There is no guilt in her eyes, only a steady, open calm.

speaker: Margaret
content: Yes. I have no reason to hide it from you. Many details unfolded in ways I had not foreseen, but the outcome still aligned with my design. For that... I am reasonably satisfied.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...You're admitting it, just like that? Nothing else you want to explain to defend yourself?

Your thoughts snag for a moment. But on reflection, she never truly tried to cover her motives. She was open about her ideological rift with DisCity's leadership, and clear that her role in Fraser was more than a simple posting.
But what unsettles you most isn't her staggering confession. It's your own reaction: your first impulse wasn't to report her; it was to listen.

speaker: Margaret
content: I could explain, but do you truly need me to? I imagine even from the fragments my old colleague shared, you can already piece together the full picture.

speaker: Margaret
content: Yes. Fraser's role as the puppet master was exposed. The Farland Alliance gained independence. A people struggling to survive now have a Hypercube mine to call their own. This is the situation I engineered.

speaker: Margaret
content: What I did has certainly harmed DisCity's interests. It could be called "treason." But all I wanted was for the Hypercubes the farlanders paid for with their lives to belong to their comrades and their children.
Margaret holds your gaze without faltering, her eyes clear with conviction and trust. Even now, she maps the journey her heart has taken and offers you a place beside her.

speaker: Margaret
content: I wanted the newly discovered Hypercube mine to belong to an independent third party—one that desires peace—to help stabilize the standoff between the two powers. Not Fraser the oppressor, nor DisCity with its overflowing reserves.

speaker: Margaret
content: Chief, if you were in my position—the farlanders' struggle before you, the oppression of Fraser and DisCity behind you—what would you choose?
Caught in the tide of the moment, the answer almost slips free, but you bite it back. She doesn't press.

speaker: Margaret
content: I won't press you or rush your answer. I'm simply doing what I have done from the start: laying myself bare before you, hoping to earn your support. Because I believe that if I am to change anything... you are my only hope.

speaker: Margaret
content: But in the end, this is only my side of the story. Whatever you decide, I will understand.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're openly telling me you want to win me over. Aren't you worried I'll see it as manipulation and report you on the spot?

speaker: Margaret
content: I believe honesty is the only path to trust, just as I believe peace is the only soil in which civilization can flourish. If you truly give me no chance at all... I will accept that graciously.

speaker: Margaret
content: If you believe I should be punished for the goals I've pursued and the things I've done, then so be it. This was my decision, and I do not fear paying the price.

She watches you fall into reflection and makes no move to pull you back. The stillness grows heavy, measured only by your indecision. You weigh her confession again and again, still uncertain whether to accept it as truth or reject it as artifice.
Perhaps you need to step outside the emotional current Margaret has drawn you into, just for a moment. To think with a clearer head.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...You're right. Your motives, your actions, their consequences—everything I've heard is only your side. I need more information before I can decide.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But it's been a long time since you've returned to DisCity, and I shouldn't keep you here. How about this: you accept the shackles, I grant you clearance to free movement, and we both give each other some time?
Lamia

speaker: Margaret
content: Chief, you still remember your promise and truly intend to keep me here for just one night. It's very considerate of you. I certainly won't refuse.

With a playful quip, she slips off her gloves without pause and offers her hand in an unshielded gesture. Your fingers meet hers: only warmth, only steadiness. Just what you have already begun to believe.

Crimson spikes of light shimmer into existence. You reach through the connection and feel only the same calm gentleness she projects—a silent confirmation that the woman before you is precisely who she seems: clear-hearted, devoted wholly to good. By every measure, you should help her.

speaker: Margaret
content: Hehe... I never expected the shackles to feel quite like this. It's as though you're always by my side, cheering me on. How reassuring.
Yet as she rises with fluid grace and moves past you, a knot tightens in your gut:
Could someone of her caliber—a DisCity Outland Affairs Officer and veteran spy—truly be so transparent? Would she so easily hand you the power to decide her fate?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Oh, right, the cameras...
As your gaze shifts, it catches on the surveillance equipment, and you remember the recording. You hesitate, weighing the choice.

Leave it, and Margaret's political enemies could seize the footage at any moment, stripping you of room to maneuver. Delete it, and you've effectively taken her side, limiting your options just as surely.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, has the interrogation ended? IT just reported a malfunction in the surveillance equipment. The footage from the second half wasn't recorded.

speaker: Nightingale
content: We should have notified you immediately, but the alert itself was... delayed, for reasons currently unexplained.
Well, there's the answer. How convenient the system chose now to fail. You shake your head, wondering: could the timing really be so perfect?

speaker: Butler
content: The requests for a visit have been filed as usual, Miss Margaret. I have also taken the liberty of preparing a list of those families who customarily send their regards but whose correspondence was... notably absent this time.

speaker: Margaret
content: Thank you, Anderson. You can't imagine how I missed home while I was in Fraser. Not just the comforts, but you, having everything in perfect order without my having to say a word.

Margaret surveys the butler's work with a small, approving nod. She sets her terminal aside—it's frozen under the weight of incoming messages—and picks up her fan, leafing through the stack of letters at her leisure.

speaker: Margaret
content: How strange. I missed DisCity so terribly... yet it appears DisCity did not miss me in equal measure. Some of its people, at least.

speaker: Butler
content: You were missed deeply within this house, Miss Margaret. Your older brother and little sister spoke of you daily.
Margaret's cultivated composure melts away at the old man's by-the-book answer. A soft, frustrated puff escapes her, and she raises her fan like a shield.

speaker: Margaret
content: Spoke of me? I can believe that of my brother, but don't you start polishing my sister's words. She detests trouble. If she isn't privately blaming me for stirring a scandal, I shall count myself fortunate.

speaker: Butler
content: House Kervoz does not falter, and your sister is not one for short sight. A temporary parting alters nothing of substance.

speaker: Margaret
content: Quite right. These comings and goings cannot shake our foundations. Those who fled at the first sign of difficulty will come scurrying back when the wind changes... And in any case, it's not as though I am wanting for connections.

She lifts the list, entirely unbothered that these "old family friends" now treat her like poison. The petulant tenderness reserved for family falls away, and in its place rests a quiet, confident smile.
As if on cue, an urgent ringtone pierces the silence. The number is unregistered, yet Margaret answers without a moment's hesitation.

speaker: Linda
content: H-hello? Is this Ms. Margaret? It's Linda. You gave me your number. I-I'm not sure if you still remember me...

speaker: Margaret
content: Of course I do, dear. You kept your head when everything was in chaos. That left quite an impression. Now, tell me, what can I do for you?

The old butler closes the door softly and withdraws with a bow. Alone now, Margaret rests her chin in one hand, fanning herself with the other as she speaks to the young secretary, her voice warm and unhurried.

speaker: Margaret
content: You have something to share? Linda, you are still young. Discretion is everything in our world. And truly, you seized that opportunity yourself. You owe me nothing. There's no need to feel obliged...

speaker: Margaret
content: Oh? Councilor Rollins has heard about the incident and intends to target me in today's interview? Tying me to the Farland Alliance and the Hypercube mining disputes... Yes, that would stir public sentiment nicely for him...

speaker: Margaret
content: Let me think... Hm? There's more? Something worse? One moment, let me see...

Margaret's fan goes still. Her fingertips skim the terminal screen, light as a dove's wing, as she scrolls through the chat logs Linda sent. Her expression doesn't darken; instead, her smile deepens, thoughtful and assured.

In moments, she makes her decision. Switching screens, she begins activating her network. Light shifts fluidly across her pupils as she works with practiced ease, all while remembering to send a calming word to Linda, who has grown anxious in the silence.

speaker: Margaret
content: ...Don't worry, dear. I'm handling it. You were right to bring this to me. To others, it would simply be buried. But there's no need for fear. I understand what you wish for, and I will see it done properly.

speaker: Margaret
content: But you must understand... you've placed yourself in danger. Never do something so brave and so reckless again. Go to the address I'm sending you. Someone there will keep you safe. Once this is over, come work for me. All right?

The call ends with a soft beep. She cross-references a few last messages from her network, tying up every loose end. Only then does she set the terminal aside and rise, unhurried, allowing herself a slow, elegant stretch.

speaker: Margaret
content: To think the breakthrough on "that person" would come from here... Linda really is a clever girl.

speaker: Margaret
content: Quick, principled, and capable of thinking for herself... Wasted on Rollins. Fortunately, when this is settled, she'll have a place far more suited to her gifts.

speaker: Councilor Rollins
content: The Hypercube mines are not just resources; they are the strategic lifeblood of DisCity! To cede them under any guise of "peace" is nothing short of betrayal!

speaker: Councilor Rollins
content: DisCity has the strength and the resolve. We are the power here, and we must act like it! This so-called "peaceful diplomacy" is a farce. It is handing our future directly to the Outlanders!

speaker: Councilor Rollins
content: I would ask those so-called "diplomats": do they have any conception of how many Disian lives a single Hypercube mine could sustain? Lives that are being gambled away!

speaker: Audience
content: Well said!

The man stands before the studio's illuminated world map, his voice fervent, his gestures sharp and precise. The host beside him nods in steady agreement, while the audience—visible only as a sea of virtual avatars—responds with rolling waves of applause.

speaker: Margaret
content: He's reaching his crescendo, I see? Quite effective. One would expect nothing less from a councilor riding a wave of popularity. This is how one commands attention. Don't you agree, my old friend?
Offstage, Margaret glides to the producer's side. Her tone is measured, carrying a note of appreciation and curiosity. She shows no sign of anger at having been publicly denounced.

The producer watches as she moves through the backstage with natural elegance, pausing to thank the assistant who led her in—earning a flustered blush for her warmth. The producer can only laugh and offer a fond, teasing reprimand.

speaker: Producer
content: You've been away from DisCity for years, and the moment you return, you drop a bombshell on my show. "Old friend"? Margaret, be honest, am I walking into one of your beautifully laid traps?

speaker: Margaret
content: Still the worrier, after all this time. I know you're concerned that I, fresh from interrogation, should not be appearing publicly. But as you can see, I come and go freely.

speaker: Margaret
content: The questioning was merely a formality. Chief ${PlayerName} of the MBCC was... quite agreeable. We had a refreshing conversation.

speaker: Producer
content: Who's worried about you? I'm worried about my ratings! Ugh, fine, we're in too deep now. Places! Three... two... one... Go, go, go!
With a reassuring pat on her friend's arm, Margaret straightens her hem under the producer's direction, then turns and walks onto the set—smiling, composed, into the thicket of cameras and light.

speaker: Margaret
content: Councilor Rollins, your perspective on "strength" and the "peaceful diplomacy" aligns remarkably well with that of Fraser's elite. By your own logic, perhaps you would make a more suitable envoy to them than I.
Inside the studio, the host catches the producer's instructions through her earpiece. She turns in surprise, only to meet a gaze that is both calm and piercing.

speaker: Host
content: Councilor, your questions are indeed profound. And it seems fortune favors us. Tonight, we have the perfect guest to address them!

speaker: Host
content: Ladies and gentlemen, please welcome: the Peace Ambassador, former key diplomat of the Fraser mission, Ms. Margaret!

speaker: Audience
content: The Peace Ambassador? The one from the headlines? No way they actually booked her! This show is pulling out all the stops! And she's absolutely slaying! So elegant!
The virtual audience erupts. Rollins is visibly thrown; though he quickly regains his composure, Margaret has already taken control of the narrative.

She approaches Rollins with deliberate steps, a composed smile on her lips. Her pale gown is elegance itself, the very image of a model DisCity Outland Affairs Officer. The scene unfolds with the weight of a slow-motion frame, her presence and command washing over the studio.

speaker: Margaret
content: My thanks to the production team, and my particular thanks to Councilor Rollins for his courage, for agreeing to discuss these pivotal diplomatic matters with me directly. These are, in fact, the very questions that occupied my every moment during the Fraser negotiations.

speaker: Councilor Rollins
content: No thanks are necessary, Ms. Margaret. Facing challenges head-on is the Disian way. And I'm more than happy to give you the floor to... explain the "merits" of your work in Fraser.

speaker: Councilor Rollins
content: That is, assuming you can provide a compelling reason for why you stood idle while the farlands formed their little alliance, and walked away with our most critical Hypercube deposits!
Rollins's style is aggressive, striking at weaknesses and pressing without pause. He knows his audience eats it up. Yet even through the storm of jeers, Margaret stands unshaken.

speaker: Margaret
content: Because DisCity's strength affords us the rare privilege of playing the long game, of securing advantages that endure. Councilor, you speak often of DisCity's power...

speaker: Margaret
content: But if I may be frank, do you truly comprehend what that power entails? We have the MBCC. We possess enough Hypercubes to shield every Disian, with even a surplus for trade. That is the foundation of peaceful diplomacy. That is the confidence behind every negotiation.

speaker: Margaret
content: You label peaceful diplomacy as betrayal. Does that make every Hypercube export an act of treason? Then let me ask you this: why imply the entire cabinet are traitors? Why suggest Disians are left unprotected? Are you, Councilor, seeking to undermine public trust?

Her tone stays gentle, yet her reasoning is sharp enough to draw blood, stirring murmurs through the virtual audience. Rollins falters for a heartbeat, but quickly regains his footing and pushes forward.

speaker: Councilor Rollins
content: I'm undermining trust? Don't let her twist my meaning! Yes, we have reserves, but that is no reason to gift them to the Outlanders!

speaker: Margaret
content: "Gift them," Councilor? Mining rights aren't quite like handing out campaign cookies. Once given, they can't be taken back.
Seizing the opening in Rollins's words, Margaret turns to the audience with a poised smile, addressing them directly and drawing an immediate swell of cheers in return.

speaker: Audience
content: Not cookies? What are they, then? Bread?

speaker: Margaret
content: Think of it as an apple tree growing on open land. We want the apples. Our troublesome neighbor wants them too, to fill their belly and grow strong enough to threaten us. But our home is quite far away, and the one living right beside the tree... happens to be our neighbor's loyal friend.

speaker: Margaret
content: So, if you were in this position, how would you secure those apples... keep them from that neighbor... and prevent them from gathering strength to strike us?
A chorus of voices rises from the audience, but before Margaret can build on the connection, Rollins cuts in, his expression stern.

speaker: Councilor Rollins
content: Please, let's not reduce grave strategic concerns to children's parables! The "neighbor" you so lightly reference is Fraser, DisCity's greatest enemy. The blood they've spilled cannot be compared to some... playground squabble over fruit!

speaker: Councilor Rollins
content: The Great Expo, BR-005... That hatred is what fuels our fight! Ms. Margaret, you make it all sound so tidy. Is that because your own sense of outrage was... softened... during your time among them?
Rollins's vicious attack fails to unsettle Margaret. She answers with flawless composure:

speaker: Margaret
content: How could it be? It is precisely because I spent so long in Fraser that I agree with you on this: Fraser is our greatest threat. And that is exactly why we must strike at the root of their power and drive a wedge between them and the farlands.

speaker: Margaret
content: If the farlands gain true independence, Fraser loses its direct access to the Hypercube mine. And we hold the leverage, and the technology. In time, the farlands will see that DisCity is the more reliable partner... perhaps even choose to join with us.

speaker: Margaret
content: This path demands no further sacrifice of DisCity's youth. Yet the apples, and the tree itself, will become ours. Let Mania rage elsewhere. DisCity will stand secure, a beacon drawing talent and prosperity from every corner of the world!
Her delivery is straightforward yet compelling, a quiet force that soaks in like a soft rainfall. Behind the scenes, the crew's eyes lock onto the rising metrics, faces brightening with excitement.
Rollins scans the room. The audience's response tells him everything: he's losing. A flicker of panic crosses his expression, but he steadies his voice and makes one final, desperate play.

speaker: Councilor Rollins
content: Hmph, an elegant theory. But it's built on promises you can't keep. Can you guarantee that the farlands' Hypercubes will ever end up in DisCity's hands?

speaker: Margaret
content: No, of course I cannot. Just as you cannot guarantee that a war would secure the mine, or that every soldier sent would return home to their family. What I can promise is that my colleagues and I will devote every resource, every effort, toward a lasting solution.

speaker: Margaret
content: From the day we took office, peace has been our compass. We seek to safeguard not only DisCity's interests, but the life and property of every Disian. We will never balance one life against another.

speaker: Councilor Rollins
content: You...!

At Rollins's silence, Margaret's expression softens with a knowing smile. She shifts her stance, turning to address the lens directly, prepared to end on a note of undeniable victory, one that defends her history and proclaims her vision.

speaker: Margaret
content: Peace is an abstract ideal, and because of that, the work to achieve it is often misunderstood. Much like my friend, Chief ${PlayerName} of the MBCC, faced when first dealing with the West District and Sinners.

speaker: Margaret
content: So I am deeply grateful for this chance to share the principles that guide me. Peace is a delicate equilibrium. It asks something of everyone—so much given, with returns that often feel distant, intangible.

speaker: Margaret
content: But look at the West District now. ${PlayerName} has shown that peace alone can give without taking, that it nurtures true prosperity, and harmony that includes everyone. That is the precedent we've begun. And that... is the future we are building together.

A measured pause allows her statement to settle. Then, with elegant formality, she bows. The audience answers with roaring applause, and the host steps in, deftly wrapping the broadcast with closing remarks.

The broadcast cuts, and the virtual audience blinks out. Amid the crew's cheers, Rollins approaches, his expression stony, for a perfunctory handshake. He's clearly eager to leave, but Margaret's grip tightens almost imperceptibly, holding him in place.

speaker: Councilor Rollins
content: ...What now? Looking to humiliate me a little longer?

speaker: Margaret
content: Humiliate you? That was merely a spirited exchange of ideas. You held your ground admirably. In fact... it seems almost a waste for someone of your skill to remain merely a piece on "that one's" board.

Rollins's eyes snap to hers, a flash of shock and suspicion crossing his face as he searches for her intent. But Margaret remains unshaken, leaning in to whisper something close, her tone weighted with implication.

speaker: Margaret
content: Do give my regards to your... patron. Tell him I'm touched by the attention he's paid me since my return. My reciprocal gift is nearly prepared. He should... await it with anticipation.
Rollins shoots her a sharp, wordless look, then turns and strides away. Margaret doesn't need a reply; she already knows the message has been received.

speaker: Producer
content: I knew betting on you was a winning move! You were absolutely stellar! The numbers are through the roof. Half the audience thinks the whole segment was scripted because it was too perfect!

speaker: Producer
content: Look at these trends! "#SoThisIsADiplomat," "#StarAmbassador"... they're everywhere! And that closing bit where you wove in the Chief? The Chief's credibility gave the whole exchange wings; it's gone completely viral!

speaker: Margaret
content: Oh, don't flatter me. Even from afar, I know how the feeds tend to amplify things. I won't take all that praise to heart. If my words reached even a few people and planted a small seed for peace, that is more than enough.

The producer rushes into the studio and thrusts her terminal under Margaret's nose, words spilling out in an excited rush. Margaret's reaction remains measured, so much so that the producer gives her arm a light, teasing pinch.

speaker: Producer
content: You're impossibly humble! But real talent can't stay hidden. You have no idea how much goodwill you've just banked. The public is completely charmed!

speaker: Producer
content: ...Even that celebrity couldn't resist. He showed up not long after you went on air and hasn't looked away since, hanging on your every word. Your charm really is something else...
female_content: ...Even that celebrity couldn't resist. She showed up not long after you went on air and hasn't looked away since, hanging on your every word. Your charm really is something else...

content: The producer gestures toward the edge of the set with a knowing nod, dropping her voice to a whisper. Margaret follows the direction, and meets a familiar pair of calm, gray eyes. Only then does her smile soften into something real.

speaker: Margaret
content: He's been here all this time? Goodness, I had no idea he'd come. And I invoked his name so freely... I do hope he isn't cross.
female_content: She's been here all this time? Goodness, I had no idea she'd come. And I invoked her name so freely... I do hope she isn't cross.

speaker: Producer
content: The Chief's been nodding along the whole time. Does that look cross to you? Honestly, who could ever stay upset with you? I'll leave you two to talk. Oh, and if the moment feels right, put in a word for an exclusive interview for me, won't you?
Margaret only smiles at the insinuation, offering no reply. Once the producer and crew have cleared the set, she finally gestures for ${PlayerName} to join her from the doorway.

speaker: Margaret
content: I only shared my schedule with you because I was concerned it might become an inconvenience for you. I never imagined you would come in person. And to think I was speaking so freely about the West District and peace right in front of you... Goodness, my cheeks are burning.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Why? Your address was masterful. I couldn't have said it better myself. You won over nearly everyone watching.
You walk over and stand beside her, your gaze steady on her face. She meets your eyes, her smile noticeably warmer than the polished poise she showed on air.

speaker: Margaret
content: Thank you. As confidently as I spoke, the truth is, I couldn't be certain how it would land until I saw the response. Nor could I be sure whether there was still soil here fertile enough for my convictions to take root.

speaker: Margaret
content: I've never doubted it was the right path. But as I'm sure you understand, being right doesn't mean one will be welcomed, nor does it guarantee acceptance.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But you've already earned that acceptance. Before tonight, no one had personally stepped forward to refute the hardliners or explain the reasoning behind the headlines.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You made a distant concept like peace feel tangible. You showed the silent majority that there is another choice. I believe they won't let you down, just as Linda didn't.

speaker: Margaret
content: You truly think so, Chief? I'm so glad that you can see those glimmers of hope on the road ahead, too...

Margaret's face lights up, touched. She turns to you, her hand lifting toward yours, but her eyes sweep across the map behind her, and her expression visibly dims. Her thought hangs, unfinished, her voice fading away.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What's the matter?

speaker: Margaret
content: Forgive me. This map... it reminds me of the global briefings I used to compile each day. Even in Fraser, there are many who long for peace, yet their voices never register on maps like this.

speaker: Margaret
content: Fraser is now under the control of the appeasement faction, and they seem to have paused their strategy of gradual encroachment, for now. But we can't be certain their ties to the Underground have been fully severed. They could be incited again at any moment...

speaker: Margaret
content: The newly formed Farland Alliance is a coalition of disparate voices. Whether it can mature into a stable third force remains to be seen; it will face many trials. And should it fail... the cost will be measured in civilian lives.
Sorrow touches her brow, softening her gaze. Her voice is measured, each phrase imbued with a quiet, compassionate ache that reaches deep.

speaker: Margaret
content: At every address, I present myself as certain, convincing my audience that peace is within reach. But in my heart, I know the path to that ideal is never smooth.

speaker: Margaret
content: Even DisCity, seemingly solid as bedrock, churns with undercurrents. The West District is progressing, yet the lure of Hypercube profits remains potent. And that's without mentioning officials being slowly corrupted in the shadows, or the ever-present whispers from the dark web...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That is a sobering picture. But I imagine you didn't return to DisCity and step into the spotlight just to give up, did you?
She pivots to face you, shaking her head with quiet conviction. The trace of worry lifts instantly; her poised smile returns, bright and fearless, like a clearing sky.

speaker: Margaret
content: Of course not. I accepted the interrogation because, compared to giving up, I have far more important work to do. I intend to return to <color=#fb9259>Paradeisos</color> and reconnect with old friends, to visit the <color=#fb9259>West District</color> where you once stood your ground, and to speak with the leadership of <color=#fb9259>Nirvana</color> and <color=#fb9259>Quinn</color>.

speaker: Margaret
content: But most of all, I wish to meet you and your companions: the courageous Ms. Cavendish, the brilliant Ms. Stewart, and perhaps, if fortune allows, the Speaker of the City Council himself, "your steadfast Max King."

speaker: Margaret
content: I have always believed that success lies in human endeavor. Peace must be sustained by all who share the vision, and people are the heart of that effort.

speaker: Margaret
content: And I believe that on this path, I will have many friends walking beside me. Such as... you.
It is almost a perfect appeal for peace—impeccably paced, drawing listeners into her world and bidding them to believe alongside her.
Your gaze locks with hers, full of quiet anticipation. Her eyes, a clear and guileless blue, hold all their hope in you—only you—as if the thought of refusal had never even crossed her mind.

options: Of course I'll stand with you.
Why should I stand with you?

content: A spark brightens Margaret's eyes, but before her smile can fully form, you press forward.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That's the answer you were counting on, isn't it? Ms. Margaret, your performance tonight was masterful and perfectly tailored, for my ears alone. It probably never even occurred to you I might say no.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You know me well, after all. You know what I value, what I fight for. But what made you so sure... that I don't know you just as well?
You raise your palm, giving a small, deliberate wave before her eyes. Fine crimson thorns flicker across your fingertips, slicing through the compassionate atmosphere she had so carefully woven.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Don't forget. I'm the one who put the shackles on you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I know the answer you want to hear. But I'm not going to give it to you. Ms. Margaret, your performance tonight was masterful and perfectly tailored, for my ears alone.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It probably never even occurred to you I might say no. You know me well, after all. You know what I value, what I fight for. But what made you so sure... that I don't know you just as well?
You raise your palm, giving a small, deliberate wave before her eyes. Fine crimson thorns flicker across your fingertips, slicing through the compassionate atmosphere she had so carefully woven.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Don't forget. I'm the one who put the shackles on you.

speaker: Margaret
content: What could you mean? Of course I remember the shackles. They're a testament to the trust between us, aren't they? You aren't suggesting... this has all been a one-sided delusion on my part?

Confronted by your sudden edge, Margaret brings a delicate hand to her lips, her eyes gleaming with a practiced, almost theatrical surprise. Your pointed words wash over her, leaving no visible trace.

Someone greener, like Linda, might have been disarmed by Margaret's unshaken composure by now. But you refuse to let her righteous confidence diminish your own. You meet her with a smile just as poised, just as carefully empty.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Yes. I imagine you do have some... misconceptions about what the shackles can do. Not that I blame you. The classified reports that reach your level would naturally emphasize their more tactical applications.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Controlling and enhancing Sinners, for example. But in my day-to-day work, I rely far more on a function deemed of little strategic value: emotional perception.

speaker: Margaret
content: I must confess... this is the first I'm hearing of it. You clearly possess unique insight. But I still fail to see what this novel capability has to do with me. Would you be so kind as to enlighten this rather slow pupil?

Her feigned confusion is just a performance. Keeping the dialogue flowing while gathering intel is one of her signature moves. But you were already prepared to lay your cards on the table, so if she wants to hear it, you have no problem spelling it all out.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Let's start from the beginning. Since our "chance encounter," you've been carefully crafting an image: gentle, kind, impeccable. You even realized perfection alone might seem unnatural, so during the interrogation, you raised the stakes, letting slip that you, too, have your own small, selfish motives.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: All of it was tailored to win me over, designed after careful study of who I am. And I'll admit, you played the part beautifully. But you're no machine. You could suppress the urge to use your power to deceive me, but you couldn't disguise your own heart.

speaker: Margaret
content: I'm not sure I follow. Perhaps... it's simply because I wasn't lying to begin with? One can hardly deceive oneself when there's nothing to hide.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If you'd known someone could feel your emotions—read your joy, your pain, your anger—and use them to gauge your sincerity, you would have tried to mask those, too. Just like... you are now. A pity you found out too late.

Without breaking eye contact, you close the distance between you, stepping pointedly into the space where Margaret held the stage. The studio lights still shine, hot and glaring. In their focus, you feel undeniably centered.

Margaret's face shows nothing, yet for a woman of her words, even a pause can speak. You reach deliberately through the shackles' connection and touch an unfathomable quiet. You know you've hit the mark.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Let me be frank. From the moment you walked out of the interrogation room, I've been verifying everything you told me, while keeping you under surveillance. Not just your movements. The shackle connection, too.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It didn't take long to see that your words and your heart don't align. You treat people as instruments. When Linda risked her life to deliver a message to you, you were pleased. But when she confided her troubles? On the surface, you seemed moved. Inside, you felt nothing.

speaker: Margaret
content: I understand what you mean... After so long in Fraser, I grew accustomed to maintaining composure, to being the pillar others lean on. Perhaps the sands there wore my heart thin. Thank you for the reminder. From now on, I'll—
She is, above all, adaptable. She is quick to offer something that resembles self-reflection while skillfully evading real accountability. You cut the act short.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So it was for her own good? You truly valued her? Then tell me, did you show the same kindness, the same appreciation, to the Campbell girl?
Margaret's composure cracks for a split second. That, she clearly didn't expect.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Is this your version of kindness? Guiding them, mentoring them, only to lead them down paths they may one day regret, all to serve your own ends? They trusted you, and you repaid that trust with manipulation?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What you truly relish is the thrill of bending others to your will with words alone. Take tonight—an unscripted speech, a dramatic reveal. In one stroke, you neutralized a rival, earned favors from a friend, and captivated an audience.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: For your grand return to DisCity's political stage, the opening act couldn't have gone smoother. No wonder you were so pleased standing here. And every time I played along, every time you felt you had a little more leverage over me, it only added to your satisfaction.
You gesture toward the empty seats of the virtual audience, then turn back to Margaret. Her face is now swallowed in shadow.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Every emotion of yours revolves around your own ambitions. You spare nothing for the "people" you so love to invoke. And this peace you cherish? It's a carefully curated garden, an order that exists only because you control it.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And anyone who dares trample your pristine order? They vanish like pests, for reasons that conveniently have nothing to do with you. Tell me, how are you any different from Councilor Rollins?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're both the same, arrogant elites who treat lives as weeds to be cleared. You sit in polished rooms trading empty phrases, and presume yourselves fit to decide the fates of countless others!

You were never much of an actor. Now the last trace of that empty smile vanishes. Your voice is stripped of pretense, exposing Margaret's true aims. The performance is over. There's nowhere left for her to retreat.

speaker: Margaret
content: ...I suppose I have my old colleagues to thank for your insights. I had hoped they would be more... discreet.

speaker: Margaret
content: It wasn't just me. They knew precisely how you would react. You see, this is exactly why I took the time to study you, to adapt to you. It was all in service of building a proper foundation of trust between us, so we might work together effectively.

As the last of your accusations fades, Margaret finally raises her gaze. The inviting warmth is gone, her expression now distant and composed. You suspect this detachment might be nearer to her real self.
She acknowledges her actions, but her tone stays cool, untouched by your anger. It still carries the same guiding authority, still firmly in control.

speaker: Margaret
content: After all, if we scrutinized everyone's motives at every turn, humanity would remain forever divided. In peaceful diplomacy, cooperation requires nothing more than common ground. I knew you would find certain details... unpalatable, so I took the liberty of filtering out the noise for you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Is this how you people dress up deception? With such refined language? And the living, breathing people affected by every decision you make... I suppose they're just noise to be filtered out too?
No offense touches her expression. The curated warmth she had offered you is gone, but curiously, her patience endures. She lets out a slow, measured breath.

speaker: Margaret
content: Why do you despise these political games so much? I understand you believe every life is precious, that you hate the thought of a single word deciding who lives and who dies... But why won't you consider the other side of it?

speaker: Margaret
content: It may sound abstract, but this is the very heart of DisCity's diplomacy—an alternative to conflict. Negotiation will always cost fewer lives than bloodshed. Surely you don't share Councilor Rollins's view that it's all meaningless?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Of course not. But you're conflating the issues. Enough with the sophistry.

speaker: Margaret
content: I am not being sophistic. I have never once lied to you, my dear Chief. From the very beginning, I have simply been presenting information in a way you could accept, hoping to earn your trust.

She looks nothing like someone whose mask has just been stripped away. Her tone still carries the righteous conviction of a DisCity Outland Affairs Officer. It dawns on you that perhaps this part of her isn't a performance after all.

speaker: Margaret
content: I want you to see my pride as a DisCity Outland Affairs Officer. I want you to understand that political maneuvering can be the most effective path to peace. And I say this not because I've never witnessed war, nor because my special power lets me speak of such things lightly.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Does it not?
Your irony collides with her sincerity and loses its edge, swallowed whole by her quiet conviction.

speaker: Margaret
content: Of course not. My power awakened in the midst of chaos. My father had brought me along on a diplomatic mission to the farlands. The local officials were useless, deadweight collecting their pay while doing nothing. The people took up arms themselves, raiding government supplies to survive and waging guerrilla resistance against DisCity.

speaker: Margaret
content: As a DisCity Outland Affairs Officer, my father bore the brunt of the attack. Some of the insurgents were wounded when our guards fought back. All I could think was... it didn't have to be this way. There had to be a better solution, a way to resolve things without bloodshed. Let me try. I can do this!
Margaret's gaze drifts into the distance, as though retracing that pivotal moment. This time, even your shackles cannot detect a single flaw.

speaker: Margaret
content: Mania answered my desire. It gave me the chance to negotiate, and I made them understand that DisCity had not come to conquer. I convinced them to serve as escorts for our delegation during our stay, in exchange for supplies. No one else was hurt.

speaker: Margaret
content: A girl from the guerrillas wove me a tapestry by hand to thank me. I had never seen such ornate, exquisite patterns. It left me in awe—and in sorrow. Those hands could have created art and wealth, but conflict had forced them to hold a weapon instead.

speaker: Margaret
content: I grew up listening to sermons about peace, but when those hands unfurled that tapestry, I saw for the first time the shape of the peace I truly wanted. It is a delicate balance that demands meticulous care, a complex weave where not a single thread can be out of place.

Her voice lifts a fraction, charged with a fervor that is felt more than heard. This philosophy of peace is familiar, but the rawness beneath it is new. This may be the closest she has ever come to being truly, undeniably herself.

speaker: Margaret
content: To smooth it out, to maintain it, one must walk the knife's edge between power, desire, strength, love, and hate. Arrange them like puzzle pieces until they fit together seamlessly... How difficult, and how exquisite!

speaker: Margaret
content: Ever since then, I have devoted myself to this exquisite work of art. And I told you honestly, you are a vital thread in this perfect tapestry. So tell me, where did I lie? Where did I twist my words?
The moment Margaret drops the act of the gracious noble lady, a harder truth surfaces. In her pale eyes, a keen, almost daunting intensity begins to burn.
But your guard is already raised. You refuse to be carried off by her rhetoric again, to be led into the maze of her logic. You meet her gaze and don't look away.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: A work of art? It looks more like a trophy to me! This is sophistry! You dress up personal ambition as a universal virtue. You disguise a need for control as selfless devotion!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You do it because you know raw "honesty" wouldn't win you support. And no matter how you phrase it, I can still hear the condescension in your every word!
You step closer, reach past her shoulder, and tap the map behind her.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That tapestry only seems like a wonder because you've never lived at the bottom! You don't even realize there's a girl behind every tapestry, because you're always here, in studios like this. Your back to the big picture, your eyes on the abstract!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Everything you say is armchair strategy. Words don't outweigh action. And when negotiations fail, you don't pay the price; the people you never see do. Do you care? I don't think so!

The sound of your finger striking the map cuts through the studio, punctuating the collapse of her rhetoric. At this proximity, you stare her down, daring her to react. But she only lowers her lashes a fraction, showing perfect, unshaken indifference.

speaker: Margaret
content: It seems words alone will not move either of us. But... what does that change?
She lifts her eyes to meet yours, her voice soft and measured—almost coaxing, like a teacher steering you to the answer.

speaker: Margaret
content: We've laid our cards on the table. Trust is no longer relevant. Negotiation, in the traditional sense, has run its course. What remains is simply a choice. And what choice do you truly have?

speaker: Margaret
content: Perhaps my vision of peace contains an element of self-satisfaction. But you're not a fool, ${PlayerName}. You know that for those unseen people you care about, peace—even an imperfect one—is preferable to war and ruin.

speaker: Margaret
content: You could expose me, yes. And then? You might gain momentary satisfaction, but what follows? The farlands' stability is fragile. In all of DisCity, I may be the only one both willing and able to steward it to a lasting peace.
She lays out the underlying logic of her scheme, a stratagem hidden in plain sight. In that gentle, instructive tone, she could almost convince you she has your best interests at heart.

speaker: Margaret
content: And let's be frank, as you yourself noted, DisCity needs a unifying figure. Someone to rally the moderates, counter the extremists, and carry the banner of peace. Remove me, and this delicate balance collapses.

speaker: Margaret
content: And your character would never allow that. Not as the Chief of the MBCC. Not as the hero of the West District. Not as the vanguard against the Black Rings.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Blood... blood...

speaker: Margaret
content: Mockery? My dear Chief, I've never held any ill will toward you. Can you not see this as trust? Even admiration?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Because you only use "trust" and "admiration" as tools. It makes people want to break that so-called trust, to expose you, even if it triggers a crisis.
Margaret laughs. She looks at you the way one regards a child throwing a tantrum—her tone assured, almost indulgent.

speaker: Margaret
content: But you won't. If that were your goal, you could have filed the interrogation report and taken me by surprise. You didn't. Because you know, I was never your enemy.

speaker: Margaret
content: Whatever my methods, the future I'm working toward is one you also desire. But those behind this interrogation? They want something else entirely. They move in the shadows of DisCity's upper echelons, brewing chaos, amassing power...

speaker: Margaret
content: Everything we've worked to build, they would dismantle without a second thought. Rollins is merely their tool. Hand them the weapon, and the peace we've nurtured will be utterly undone. That is why you haven't acted on impulse.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I see it now. The ones using this interrogation to undermine you, scrap the accords, and send troops to seize the Hypercube mine... they're your political rivals. And my "old friends."

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You saw this from the beginning. You knew once I uncovered the truth, I could never side with them. That's why you never flinched. You've been in an unassailable position all along. Am I wrong?

When she reads you, her gaze holds a glint of satisfaction, as though silently praising your acuity. You meet it with a detached recitation of her schemes, laying each calculation bare and stripping away the gentle veneer she uses to obscure them.

speaker: Margaret
content: I'm not the only one in a strong position; you are as well. Truly, this needn't feel like a loss. Compromise is the essence of diplomacy. You'll come to understand that... though, in truth, you already grasp it quite well.

A low chuckle escapes her as her hand comes to rest on your cheek. Your muscles lock, but you don't retreat. There's a claiming softness to her touch, deliberate and exact, less a caress than a calibrated signal of approval and guidance.

speaker: Margaret
content: It brings me genuine pleasure to see someone like you rise in DisCity. Sharp, principled, and effecting real change. But as I once learned, you will too: in times like these, to get things done, one cannot be too delicate about how it's achieved.

speaker: Margaret
content: I, fortunately, had no choice at the time. But if your hands must remain clean, you can always learn to make use of those whose hands need not be. To achieve what you wish, and thwart the schemes you despise. Someone like... me.

Her words soften into a purity that feels almost enchanting. The flawless, inviting smile she wore when you met her returns, and with it, her unshakable composure. In this moment, she is unmistakably the Margaret who seems to hold all the strings.
Move aside, please! I've got to get offstage, there's an urgent situation.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're not wrong. I could indeed use you to achieve my goals and handle the people I need to. And the leverage I'd use? You handed it to me yourself.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: After all that, you still think you can draw me in with that rhetoric? If I were foolish enough to accept, the question of who ends up using whom... remains to be seen.

You step back, coldly brushing her hand aside, and pull out your terminal—still recording—giving it a deliberate little wave. True, even in the midst of crisis, she can weave an intricate web, guiding you step by step with her rhetoric, narrowing your perspective and your options...
Anyone else might have fallen for it. But not you. You've been on guard against her from the very beginning. Margaret wants to force a decision on her terms, and you refuse.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're quick on your feet. Even after being exposed, you still tried to guide me, dangling a common enemy, making it seem like I had no choice but to side with you.

speaker: Margaret
content: ...You are sharper than I anticipated. But tell me... which part of what I said was untrue?
She pulls back her hand and lifts her fan, masking her expression. Behind it, her eyes stay cool and controlled.

speaker: Margaret
content: You've been at the center of every major incident in DisCity lately. Whether this faction exists, how great a threat they pose, you know far more than I do here in Fraser. Even if I had remained silent, would you have truly chosen to look the other way?

speaker: Margaret
content: Whether through peace or purge, our destination aligns. I see no reason we cannot walk the path together. Setting everything else aside, Chief... this is a sincere proposal. A proposal for cooperation.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Cooperate? I'm the one holding proof. I decide your fate, and the farlands'. Why should I cooperate on your terms? Why should I choose from the options you've laid out?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I have no intention of becoming your next Rollins or Linda. I'm taking a third path. I'll move the pieces, and just as you suggested, I'll make proper use of you.
Margaret's brow furrows ever so slightly.

speaker: Margaret
content: You mean...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I can choose not to expose you. I might even help you deal with this faction. But I will be in control. All the intelligence you've gathered—I want everything. And from now on, you share any new information with me immediately.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Every move you make must be reported. No tricks. I'll be watching constantly. The moment I catch you, your interference with the interrogation and your personal agenda will be exposed. Don't even think about exploiting your position again. I won't allow it.

For a moment, it seems you've finally struck a nerve. A shadow falls across her face, and she goes silent.
But before you can deliver the line you had prepared—something about her sincerity being nothing more than lip service—she raises her head again.

speaker: Margaret
content: I accept your terms.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Don't think hollow promises will work this time. I know your type, people who thrive on control. Having someone else call the shots must chafe. But that won't make me ease up. Not one bit.

speaker: Margaret
content: I know this path won't be easy. But as you said, you hold the leverage, and the shackles. By any measure, control rests with you. And as a DisCity Outland Affairs Officer, I never swim against the tide.

speaker: Margaret
content: Besides, you don't crave power for its own sake. This is simply your way of letting me understand what Linda and the others felt, isn't it? If enduring this proves my sincerity and earns a true partnership with you, I have no reason to refuse.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Then prove your sincerity over time. If it even exists.

You watch as Margaret, still smiling, sees right through your intent. You sharpen your tone, but she shows not a hint of displeasure. Instead, she offers a slight curtsy, takes your hand in hers, and presses a kiss to the back of it—feather-light and startlingly sincere.

speaker: Margaret
content: I will. The files will be in your hands shortly. For our time working together, I hope you will offer your guidance. And please, do not forget... our goals have always been aligned. I long for your trust.
You hold her gaze for a long moment, studying her until you are certain she has truly accepted all your demands this time without rhetoric or evasion. Only then do you turn and leave.
You do not look back as you leave. And so you do not see Margaret's eyes beneath the brim of her hat, half-hidden behind her fan, gleaming with undisguised interest.

speaker: Margaret
content: ...How trying. First, that little Campbell girl, and now your precious SHP-13. Not one of them seems content to follow a script. Both insist on seizing the master's chair.

In the dim room, Margaret speaks into her communicator. Her words come faster than usual, and her feathered fan flutters with restless energy. The servants have long since been dismissed; for now, only her voice fills the quiet.

speaker: Margaret
content: Sigh... Every last one of them would rather be the player than the piece. But DisCity's stability requires balance above all; it cannot endure their... spirited improvisations. To think of my designs unraveling over a whim... it is genuinely disquieting.

speaker: Margaret
content: Would it be so difficult to simply walk the path I've prepared? It isn't as though I mean them any harm. I've selected each piece with care, crafted the most elegant plans... Wouldn't they thrive better under guidance than fumbling in the dark?

speaker: Communications
content: That is just how children are. Quick to grow, and unpredictable by nature. But isn't that exactly why their potential remains boundless?

speaker: Communications
content: When we selected them as anchors for our design, these were the very qualities we sought. And besides, they have not yet fully defied our expectations.
Margaret's fan stills its restless flutter. A soft laugh escapes her as she nods in quiet agreement.

speaker: Margaret
content: You're right, of course... Any surprises from anchors of this caliber are... ultimately incidental. The larger design remains intact. Our timetable proceeds.

speaker: Margaret
content: The peace we have envisioned will come to pass.
The line falls silent for a moment, as if transmitting data. Margaret's eyes scan the information appearing on her terminal, and a smile of quiet certainty spreads across her face.
It is an electronic map, an aerial view of the land below. Scattered intelligence markers dot the terrain like the lit windows of a residential area in an age of peace.
Now then, onward to the next move.

In the final snowstorm that sweeps across Northwild, Jichuan walks alone to the farthest end she can reach. Sustained only by the last remnants of life the shackles can give, she goes to a place where her passing burdens no one.
//Fade in from black to cave
The cave's damp chill seeps through her clothes and intertwines with the suffocating pain churning in her chest. Like a spider's web, it binds Jichuan's life to this moment, to this place.

speaker: Jichuan
content: So this is what death feels like...

Outside the cave, the wind's wailing blurs into a distant hum. Her vision grows hazy. It feels as though the whole world narrows to nothing but her faint breathing, a flickering flame on the edge of going out.
Her life force ebbs with every breath. Her limbs become heavier and heavier. The pain in her body begins to fade, as if gentle hands cradle her, carrying her somewhere deeper and quieter.

speaker: Jichuan
content: This is as far as I go, huh...
Her voice is barely a whisper, heavy with exhaustion finally released, each word growing fainter and slower than the last...
//Black screen blink effect
//BG: Ancient Chinese-style interior

Jichuan stirs awake in a surge of warmth. An unfamiliar yet reassuring power moves through her limbs and chest... The last time she felt this vital, this alive, was in her childhood—before Mania claimed her and she fell terminally ill.
She blinks her eyes open. What meets her gaze is no longer the cold cave but warm, traditional furnishings.
Sunlight streams through the windows, and nearby, the soft bubble of boiling tea water fills the quiet.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Is this... a dream?
She reaches out, attempting to grasp the sunlight before her, when she suddenly realizes her body feels lighter than it ever has before.

speaker: Familiar Voice
content: Chuan'er? You're awake.
A gentle push swings the door open, and a familiar voice drifts in on a warm breeze.
Jichuan props herself up in disbelief, unable to look away from the person now entering the room.

speaker: Familiar Voice
content: What's with that look? Still dreaming, are you? I made pumpkin porridge. You said you wanted some yesterday. Come, try it while it's warm.

speaker: Jichuan
content: ...Mother...?
To Jichuan, the word feels so foreign that it leaves her throat hoarse the moment she speaks it. She rubs her eyes.

The woman in front of her looks down, her gaze settling on Jichuan's face with a soft, tender warmth. A slight smile touches her lips, and the delicate crow's feet at the corners of her eyes mirror Jichuan's memory exactly, down to the smallest detail.

speaker: Jichuan's Mother
content: Oh my, how did your voice get so hoarse from just sleep?
As if sensing Jichuan's unease, the woman sits down on the edge of the bed. She takes Jichuan's hand and cradles it inside her warm palms.

speaker: Jichuan's Mother
content: Your hands are so cold. A bad dream? Tell me, what did you dream about?
Jichuan seems unused to the warmth of being held. She watches those hands gently rubbing hers to chase away the cold, and tears spill from her eyes without her ever feeling them start.

speaker: Jichuan
content: I... I dreamed so many things. I dreamed the snow at the manor fell heavier and heavier, burying everything. I dreamed... that I tried with everything I could to make it stop...

speaker: Jichuan
content: That you and Father, my friends, and everything I believed in and fought to protect all faded away into that endless white.

speaker: Jichuan's Mother
content: Silly child, it's spring now. It's all right... Everything will be all right.

speaker: Jichuan's Mother
content: If you're cold, just put on more clothes. I'll have your father prepare some pickled ginger later. You can have it with the pumpkin porridge. That'll warm you up.
Her mother wraps Jichuan in her arms and gives her back a gentle pat, just like she did back when Jichuan was small.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Father is here too?

speaker: Jichuan's Mother
content: Silly girl, still foggy from sleep, aren't you? This is our home. Where else would your father be?

speaker: Jichuan
content: Home...?
//Sound effect of door opening

speaker: Jichuan's Father
content: "You two little ones better grow up healthy and strong. Don't let all my hard work go to waste..."

speaker: Jichuan's Mother
content: Listen to your silly father, talking to those seedlings again. Can you believe it? A master herbalist who can't even keep two little vegetables alive...

speaker: Jichuan's Father
content: Badmouthing me to Chuan'er again, are you? Let me tell you, these are specially cultivated varieties. They grow slowly, but they're full of nutrition!
Straightening up in the courtyard, the figure turns toward Jichuan, his face illuminated by that same warm, gentle smile.

speaker: Jichuan's Mother
content: Perfect, then. We'll use your most nutritious little seedlings to nourish Chuan'er and settle her nerves.

speaker: Jichuan's Father
content: What's this? Something scared my Chuan'er? Tell me who it was, and I'll give them a proper talking-to!
As he speaks, he rolls up his sleeves, revealing the thin, scholarly arms beneath. Jichuan can't help but laugh.

speaker: Jichuan
content: And this talking-to of yours, Father... will it be an hour long, or two?
Seen right through by his daughter, her father takes it in stride with good humor, scratching his head sheepishly before turning his attention back to those pitifully small seedlings.
Seeing Jichuan's smile again, her mother finally eases. She turns toward the earthen stove in the corner.

A vegetable garden, a thatched cottage, a home... Bamboo medicine baskets scattered across the courtyard give off the fragrance of various herbs, blending with warm spring sunlight and the comforting scent of everyday life. Jichuan has never truly lived this way, but she knows exactly what this is...

speaker: Jichuan
content: <i><color=#7683a2>When I was little, my parents told me that once the snow at Northsnow Manor stopped falling, once the people below the mountain no longer suffered... we would go together to a place no one knew... tend a garden, water the flowers, and live a life free from the world's troubles.</color><i>

speaker: Jichuan
content: <i><color=#7683a2>How could I ever forget... This was my parents' dearest wish while they were still alive...</color><i>

Dazed, Jichuan sits down by the stone table as her mother presses a bowl of hot porridge into her hands. The bottom of the bowl scalds her, but she doesn't feel it until the heat shocks her back into awareness.

speaker: Jichuan's Mother
content: Oh dear, my fault! I should have warned you it was hot. Did you burn yourself? Shall I get some ointment... Chuan'er? Chuan'er?

speaker: Jichuan's Mother
content: Oh... you're crying again? That's twice this morning already.

speaker: Jichuan's Father
content: "Snow melts from icy peaks, first turning into jade. The river, fed by clearing skies, begins to flow with spring." Chuan means river, and a river is made of water. Let her cry a thousand times if she wishes.
Helplessly, Jichuan wipes her face, then glances at her fingertips, now red from the burn.

speaker: Jichuan
content: I'm fine. I just... I don't know what's come over me. Everything feels like a dream, and yet the warmth, the pain... they're far too real...

speaker: Hecate
content: I should be in that freezing cave, quietly slipping away from this world. By now, I should have already—
Chuan!

The voice reaches her before its owner does. Then a small figure bursts into the courtyard from outside, carrying a bamboo pole. The instant she recognizes who it is, the bowl of porridge nearly slips from her hands.

speaker: Jichuan
content: By now, I should have already died.
The figure fails to catch her whispered words. She lifts her head, innocent smile in place, tilting it as her gaze meets Jichuan's.

speaker: Mudling
content: What are you muttering about? Is it a new plan for us to roam the world together?

speaker: Jichuan
content: Mudling... Why are you here too?
Her face is so close, vivid and real. Jichuan reaches out, wipes the dirt from her cheeks, and she feels it again: the warmth of living skin under her fingers.

speaker: Jichuan
content: I see now... Of course you'd be here. Whether this is a dream or reality no longer matters.

speaker: Jichuan
content: <i><color=#7683a2>I understand now. This is a place where the departed reunite. And the departed... include myself.</color><i>
She lowers her head to drink the porridge, using the motion to hide the tears welling in her eyes. The warm porridge slides down her throat and flows gently through her.
She takes another spoonful, then another. It settles in her stomach, and as it fills her, warmth spreads through her chest too.
Mudling sits beside her and takes a bowl of hot porridge from her mother's hands, slurping it eagerly.

The four of them gather around the stone table in quiet contentment. Her parents chat about daily clinic matters while Mudling chimes in enthusiastically—not quite grasping everything, but eager to join in.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Your straightforward words seem to shatter the invisible wall between you. After a moment of silence, Dove steps aside, opening the door to her room.

Jichuan cradles the warm bowl in her hands, lost in thought, gazing at her dear family and friend around her—all of them long dead. Then she suddenly recalls the old folktales she once read about the world beyond.
The wicked meet their end and descend into darkness; the virtuous depart and reunite with loved ones beyond...
Her heart settles. She blows away the rising steam, tips the bowl back, and downs the last of the pumpkin porridge in a single, final gulp.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Mudling, now that you've finished eating, time for practice!

speaker: Jichuan
content: Father, I'll help you in the fields once we're done training.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Mother, can we have rice cakes for lunch?

speaker: Jichuan's Mother
content: Would you like some dried fruit in them?

speaker: Jichuan
content: Yes!
She grows accustomed to this vibrant body, embracing the garden blooming with life around her. Her voice turns brighter, each word ringing with newfound clarity.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Mudling, I met quite a few martial masters in my dreams last night and learned a new sword technique that can break formations. Care to try it out with me?

speaker: Mudling
content: I can't believe you've been sneaking in extra training behind my back! I've been getting stronger too, y'know. No way I'm falling behind! Check this out!

The two of them tumble across the courtyard in a playful brawl, caring little for proper form. Her parents shake their heads helplessly, letting them roughhouse from the eaves all the way up to the rooftop.

speaker: Jichuan
content: This move is called <color=#fb9259>Shadows Aslant</color>!

speaker: Mudling
content: Then try my <color=#fb9259>Sea Dragon's Ascent</color>!

speaker: Jichuan
content: I'll counter it with my own <color=#fb9259>Snowdrift Blitz</color>!

speaker: Mudling
content: Hah! You let your guard down! My Beggar Staff Technique's unbeatable!
Jichuan draws the plum branch staff, Bent Jade, from her side and swings. Mudling snatches a bamboo pole to parry. Their banter stays playful, but genuine technique flows through every move.
The bamboo pole grazes Jichuan's cheek. She bends backward to dodge, tilts her head up, and glimpses something white falling from the clear sky.
A single snowflake drifts down, landing on the red mole between her brows.

speaker: Mudling
content: Huh? That's weird. Spring's already here, isn't it?
Mudling stops as well, leaning closer to see. But the snowflake melts at once from the warmth of Jichuan's skin, disappearing without a trace. Overhead, the clear sky shows no sign of change.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Perhaps... we were just seeing things.

Jichuan offers reassurance, yet her expression grows distant. In that brief moment of contact with the snowflake, she feels her heart skip a beat. Something from the depths of her consciousness—some connection—stirs within her.
For reasons she cannot name, someone comes to mind... A name buried deep in her heart, from a distant, foreign land...
//BG: Chief's Office, DisCity MBCC

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, a new report just came in from Eastia.
Several days have passed since your return from Eastia, yet that bitter snowstorm refuses to let you go.
You have thrown every resource at your disposal, reaching out to every Eastian faction you can find, all for one purpose: a single trace of Jichuan.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This time... nothing again?
One look at Nightingale's expression, and you already know the answer.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Thanks. Just leave it there.

Reports on Jichuan's whereabouts pile into a small mountain on your desk. You pore over each one, attempting to feel every faint lead through the shackles... Day after day, you turn up nothing. Nightingale watches you in your exhausted state, her lips parting, but she thinks better of it.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I know what you're thinking. All signs point to the possibility that Jichuan might not be alive. Don't worry, I'm not blind to it. Eastia's just as concerned about the situation in Northwild; they won't just let her disappearance go unanswered either.
You rise from your seat and walk to the window, your gaze settling on the withered plum branch in the white porcelain vase. That branch is the only trace of her you managed to bring back from Eastia.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But I trust what the shackles are telling me... Jichuan is alive.
The withered branch offers no answers to your hopes. You let out a sigh and reach for the porcelain vase, readying yourself to change its water.
But just as your fingertips brush the vase, you see it: at the very tip of the branch turned toward the sun, a tender green bud, no bigger than a thought, begins to push through.
//Sound effect of communicator
Just then, your terminal emits an urgent chime.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief... this is from Eastia. They found Jichuan!
//Black Screen
Help... help me...
Help me...
//BG: Ancient Chinese-style interior

All night, the blizzard rages without reprieve. Fierce winds slam heavy snow against the window frames, and beyond the house, the world lies buried in a vast white desolation. Even the tender spring greenery, barely beginning to sprout, now smothers beneath the drifts.
The hearth fire crackles, yet it fails to chase off the lingering chill. Wrapped in her cloak, Jichuan stares out the window, her brow deeply furrowed.
Help me...

The fragmented cries for help echo over and over in her ears. Though as faint as a flickering candle, the voice pierces the howling storm with perfect clarity, gripping her heart. She reaches for her coat.

speaker: Jichuan's Mother
content: Chuan'er, where are you off to?

speaker: Jichuan
content: I heard someone calling for help. They may be in danger. I should go and see.

speaker: Jichuan's Father
content: There's no one for miles around the house. You must have misheard. It's likely just the wind.

speaker: Jichuan
content: It wasn't the wind. I heard it clearly. It was a human voice, very faint.

speaker: Mudling
content: ...Chuan, come on, at least wait till the storm lets up a little. This weather's just too weird. Something about it feels... off.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Precisely because the weather is so unnatural... I have a feeling something terrible is about to happen.
