Jichuan's determination is plain for everyone to see, and they all realize there's no point in trying to stop her.

speaker: Jichuan's Father
content: Then dress warmly. I'll have some ginger soup ready for when you return.

speaker: Jichuan
content: ...Alright!
She pushes open the door. A frigid gust carrying swirling snow rushes in, forcing a shiver from her.
She takes a few steps forward, then cannot help glancing back.
Her father, mother, and Mudling stand by the window, watching her with concern. The house glows warm with candlelight, and she knows they have lit them for her.
...Help... Please, someone...
From afar, the cry for help sounds again. Jichuan turns her gaze forward, walking without hesitation toward the source of the voice.
//Black Screen
No longer hindered by her illness, Jichuan moves swiftly through the wind and snow, her movements nimble and sure.
The wind and snow obscure her vision, but fortunately the cries for help never cease, growing clearer with each step.
Whoosh—
Another slicing gust screams through the air, and Jichuan nearly collapses.
Half her legs vanish into the snow. The cold, piercing to the bone, drills into her marrow while icy water seeps down her collar, shaking her teeth into a frantic chattering.

speaker: Jichuan
content: The branches along the path have all sprouted buds... It's already late spring, yet this cold snap feels deeply unnatural...
Just as Jichuan begins to ponder further, cries for help pull her from her thoughts.
Help... Someone help us...

The voice is right beside her now. Jichuan's head snaps up, and only then does she realize she has reached the village at the mountain's foot. Before her stands a crude wood shed, its roof sagging dangerously under the weight of accumulated snow.
Cries for help pour continuously from within. Jichuan hurries forward.
As she draws closer, she sees that the shed's doors and windows are completely sealed by waist-deep snow.
Miss Jiang! Help! Please, the snow's gonna bury us alive!

speaker: Jichuan
content: You know me? Stay calm. I'll have you out in a moment!
Jichuan reaches out to clear the snow blocking the door. It should only take a moment...
Crack!
The wooden planks of the shed's roof groan, straining under the unbearable weight. From inside comes the woman's scream.

speaker: Jichuan
content: You'll be all right. There's still room. Grab this!
Jichuan slips her plum branch through the wooden boards and yanks the trapped woman into the clearing.
No sooner have they escaped than the shed crashes down with a thunderous roar. Frightened cries fill the air.
Only now does Jichuan see that the woman is holding a baby. The infant's face is pale, its breath shallow, numbed by the long cold.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Don't be afraid. I'll get you both somewhere safe. Are your legs hurt? Can you walk?

speaker: Disaster Victim
content: I can... I can still walk...

speaker: Disaster Victim
content: Miss Jiang, there are a few more families up ahead, all old folks, real frail. They were crying for help just a bit ago, but now... now they've all gone quiet...

speaker: Jichuan
content: Don't worry. I'll get them out.

speaker: Jichuan
content: I passed an inn on my way here. It's still in good shape. Should hold through the storm. Take the child there and wait it out.
After settling the woman, Jichuan turns and moves deeper into the village.

But the deeper she goes, the more desperate the cries for help grow. Not only people trapped in houses, there are also those pinned under collapsed beams, clinging to their last breath, and others clutching the bodies of their loved ones in numb grief, refusing to let go.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Everyone, stay calm! If your home is still sound, shelter inside. If it's damaged or unstable, make your way to the inn north of town. Watch your step in the snow and keep yourselves safe!

speaker: Jichuan
content: We're running low on supplies to keep warm. If any household is short on necessities, let me know. I'll do everything I can to secure more.

Jichuan moves tirelessly through the tottering wooden houses. Even a healthy body would break down from such relentless effort, yet she never pauses, pulling one trapped family after another from beneath the heavy snow.
But one person's strength is nothing more than a drop in the ocean against a disaster of this scale.
As she rushes from place to place, a desperate cry reaches her ears from nearby—

speaker: Female Disaster Victim A
content: My baby... my baby! She's not breathing...

It's the woman Jichuan rescued first. Without Jichuan's martial skill, the woman struggles through the deep snow with her child, only now making it to the inn's entrance—still exposed, not yet safe inside.
Something inside Jichuan finally snaps. She stumbles toward the woman on unsteady feet. Yet hope remains: she can see the child still clings to life.

speaker: Jichuan
content: She's all right. She'll be all right. Here... give her to me.
Jichuan reaches for the child to treat her, but the woman clutches her daughter tight, unwilling to let go.

speaker: Female Disaster Victim A
content: No, no... She's cold. She's so cold...
The woman's terrified expression pierces Jichuan's heart. She does not press further. Instead, she places her palm on the child's chest and slowly channels her life force into the tiny body.
Finally, redness returns to the child's skin. A faint cry rises from the bundle in the woman's arms.
Clutching her child, the woman weeps with joy. She drops to her knees before Jichuan, bowing again and again in gratitude. Jichuan reaches down to lift her up, but her movement suddenly freezes.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Cough! Cough, cough, cough!
A mouthful of dark, congealed blood spatters across the white snow. Then familiar agony tears through her organs, seizing her insides in a vicious grip.
The villagers freeze at the horrifying sight, too shocked to move.

But no one is more terrified than Jichuan herself. She knows this pain all too well. The "contamination" that has shadowed her for years now gnaws again at her life force from within, devouring her bones, her blood, and her warmth.
She stares at her hands, the ones that just channeled her energy. Those same hands, which restored life to an infant, now rapidly lose their last trace of warmth.
Seeing her about to collapse, a small child among the villagers darts forward and catches her.

speaker: Child
content: Miss, you're so cold... Are you sick too?

speaker: Jichuan
content: This... this isn't an illness. It's a countdown I cannot escape, no matter where I run.
The child fails to grasp what she means. Jichuan forces a smile, wipes the blood from the corner of her mouth, and pats the child on the head.

speaker: Jichuan
content: I'm fine. It's cold out here. Go find somewhere warm to shelter. Where are your parents?
The child points into the distance, where countless makeshift stretchers lie shrouded in white linen.
Jichuan gathers the child into her arms, sharing what little warmth lingers in her body.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Perhaps... this strange world has been unfair to us all.
Is this truly the afterlife? Then why must she live through this helplessness all over again?
The child senses Jichuan's distress, presses closer, and clings to her in an anxious search for comfort.

speaker: Child
content: Miss... will the snow ever stop?
Jichuan gives no answer. Instead, she simply takes the child's hand.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Come. I'll find you somewhere warm to stay.
The snow always stops eventually. But this crumbling town, these people, her body... they may not last until the skies clear.
//Black Screen
//BG: Mountain path
You've been trudging across the slippery mountain path for what feels like ages. Your legs have gone from aching soreness to a numb, dull throb.
An Eastian child, just past ten years old, is leading the way ahead. She knows these mountain paths intimately, and despite her youth, her steps stay sure and steady.

speaker: Bao
content: Young hero, we're almost there... You holding up okay?

speaker: Bao
content: You know, I never would've guessed someone who looks as delicate as you could round up so many big shots to help find Shuang'er.

speaker: Bao
content: Are you, like... some kind of legendary sect leader or something...?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I just happen to know quite a few people, that's all.

speaker: Bao
content: Oh... Wait! Your foot's bleeding!
You freeze for a moment and look down. The black boots are so sodden with snow that no bloodstains are visible, yet the footprints trailing behind you stain the snow a vivid red.
Your feet have been frozen numb for so long that you fail to notice when the soles rip open.

speaker: Bao
content: That looks bad! Wait here, I'll go down the mountain and get help...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It's nothing, just a scratch. Finding Jichuan is what matters.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Didn't you say we're almost there? Come on, let's go. We've come this far.
Bao hesitates, then pushes forward, though you catch her easing off her pace ever so slightly.

speaker: Bao
content: It's just up ahead. The cave's super hidden. I only found it 'cause I tripped while digging for wild veggies. And when I peeked inside, I was like, whoa! Isn't that Shuang'er from town, the one who's always telling those epic stories!

speaker: Bao
content: Oh right, I'm supposed to call her Jichuan. I only learned later that Shuang'er is actually the crazy amazing manor master!

speaker: Bao
content: When I first found her, she'd mumble sometimes, calling for her mom and dad... Then she kept saying it's so cold, save them... I didn't really get it, so I just stayed with her.

speaker: Bao
content: We're here!
Bao suddenly stops and lifts a hand, brushing dead wood and weeds aside. There, concealed in the mountain wall and blurred by wind and snow, lies a narrow cave entrance.
You duck inside. The cave feels slightly warmer than the outside world, yet the air holds a damp, musty smell laced with a faint trace of medicinal herbs.
Bao, who has been leading the way, steps aside. At once, your gaze lands on a slender figure sprawled on a pile of dry grass nearby.

She lies covered in a small, worn padded coat, the one Bao must have left for her. Beneath it, her white dress is soiled. One hand rests on the coat, withered and rough, the fingertips touched with an unnatural, ashen pallor.

You crouch slowly beside her. By the faint daylight seeping through the cave entrance, you lean closer to that pale face. Your fingers gently push aside the tangled strands of hair, and there it is—the red mole between her eyebrows, the one you know so well.

You have pictured this meeting with Jichuan a thousand ways. Perhaps she has already found a cure and still dresses as that Beggar Clan girl, ready to tease you. Perhaps she is full of life again, hiding behind a curtain, pretending to be a reclusive martial arts master.
But instead, you find her broken in a way you have never witnessed before.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It's her.

A whirl of emotions floods through you, yet all you can manage are these few words as you gently tuck the old coat around her. She lies so still, so deathly quiet, that you are afraid to check if she is even breathing.

speaker: Jichuan
content: ...The snow... have to save them...
Jichuan's voice is barely a whisper. But even that is enough to answer the question weighing on your mind for so long—she is truly alive.
You reach out and take her wrist, so emaciated it feels like nothing but skin and bone, and through your shackles, you attempt to forge a connection.

speaker: Bao
content: How's she? Is she gonna be okay?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Not good. She's hanging on by a thread, fighting the Mania corruption inside her with nothing but will. But I can feel that will slipping. I need to steady her mind first.

speaker: Bao
content: Oh... Th-then... is there anything I can do?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I need you to head outside to an open spot and keep watch. I've already called for a medical rescue team. You'll have to guide them here.

speaker: Bao
content: You got it! What about you?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Her consciousness is trapped. She doesn't even know how bad it is. I have to go in and find her. Wake her up.
//Black Screen
The shackles' connection pulls you into Jichuan's mental domain. Before you can even steady yourself, a violent snowstorm engulfs you.
Wherever you look, blinding white fills your vision and blots out the sky.
Adrift in this vast expanse, you have no idea which way to go.
A stove fire flickers inside the inn, its flames trembling in the biting wind—flaring bright, then fading—threatening to go out entirely.

Jichuan sits cross-legged on the cold brick floor, her palm pressed against the chest of an elderly woman before her. Strands of luminous white internal force are being ripped from her meridians, flowing through her fingertips into the old woman's body.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Cough...
A dull blade might as well be carving open her blocked meridians, again and again. Cold sweat streams down her temples, runs along her cheeks, and seeps into her collar.
Stifled groans and coughs fill the air around her. Still, she does not dare stop, not for a single moment.

speaker: Female Disaster Victim B
content: Miss Jiang... please, child, you must rest... This old bone's lived her share. Don't you go wasting yourself on me...

speaker: Jichuan
content: Be at ease, ma'am. Just a little longer, and the pain will pass.
As she speaks, she grits her teeth and forces out more of her internal force.

This is already the eighth person Jichuan treats without rest, but still, countless wounded cry out in agony around her. Her body sways unsteadily, and when the metallic taste of blood rises in her throat, she forces it back down.

speaker: Female Disaster Victim B
content: You've done more than any soul could ask, Miss Jiang... If it weren't for you, we'd all be frozen stiff by now.

speaker: Female Disaster Victim B
content: Don't push yourselves further for us... Our lives were never ours to keep. It's the heavens' call, not yours.
Jichuan steadies her voice, keeping it calm and controlled.

speaker: Jichuan
content: I'm fine... Cough... Every person who survives gives the rest a little more hope to hold on.

speaker: Female Disaster Victim B
content: Someone like you—young, skilled, noble—you shouldn't be trapped here, waiting to die with hopeless souls like us!

speaker: Female Disaster Victim B
content: Go home, child. Your parents must be waiting by the door.
Clouded eyes brimming with tears, the old woman holds Jichuan's gaze with quiet resolve. She keeps her voice low, ensuring the others in the room cannot overhear.

speaker: Jichuan
content: There's no noble or common here. I have parents waiting for me, and so do your families. Don't they hope just as much to see you safe and sound?

Jichuan forces herself to hold her head still, to keep her gaze from drifting toward that distant window glowing with warm lamplight, the light her parents leave burning, always waiting for her return.
But the old woman's words—go home—wrap around her like a tender spell.
Go home... Yes, she has a home now. A home with warm tea and hot meals, with a cherished friend and a beloved family. And here... here remains an endless frozen world and a crowd of strangers.

speaker: Jichuan
content: <i><color=#7683a2>If this truly is the afterlife, then why must I endure such purgatory all over again... If only...</color><i>
Her healing hands never stop moving, though her thoughts drift away to that warm little house, to the hot soup her mother has waiting for her.

speaker: Jichuan
content: <i><color=#7683a2>What if none of this was ever real...</color><i>
A cruel, coldly rational thought flashes through her mind: perhaps all this suffering is mere illusion, her efforts no more than grasping at shadows.
Yet a cry immediately yanks her back from that brief lapse.

speaker: Female Disaster Victim A
content: Miss Jiang! My baby... she's crying again, and I don't know why...
Jichuan's hands reach out before her mind catches up. She draws the child into her arms, gently patting her back.
The heat against her fingertips makes her heart clench.
The clamoring thoughts in her mind fall away like a receding tide, leaving only one behind.

speaker: Jichuan
content: <i><color=#7683a2>But what if... what if this is real? What if these people are all truly alive?</color><i>
//Black Screen

speaker: Jichuan's Father
content: Chuan'er? Slacking off here again, are we? Have you finished memorizing the medicinal herbs I assigned?

speaker: Young Jichuan
content: Mm... soon.

speaker: Jichuan's Father
content: Oh-ho! So you've snuck my roasted beans again!

speaker: Young Jichuan
content: You're so stingy, Dad... I'll buy you a new bag next time I go down the mountain.

speaker: Jichuan's Father
content: Hmm? What's the matter? Why do you look so bothered reading a storybook?

speaker: Young Jichuan
content: Well... the hero in the story had a falling out with a friend. But I think both of them have a point...

speaker: Young Jichuan
content: The hero has been through so much hardship in the martial world that he wants to retreat from it all. But his friend says he's just being a coward...

speaker: Young Jichuan
content: I feel bad for the hero, but I also don't think he should just hide in the mountains forever...

speaker: Young Jichuan
content: Dad, do you think he should go into seclusion, or keep wandering the world with his sword?

speaker: Jichuan's Father
content: Hah... you've got me there, sweetheart. I can't make other people's choices for them.

speaker: Young Jichuan
content: What if it were you?

speaker: Jichuan's Father
content: The latter, of course.

speaker: Young Jichuan
content: Why?

speaker: Jichuan's Father
content: Hmm... how to put this so you'll understand...

speaker: Jichuan's Father
content: Alright, take these beans on the plate. See this bowl with a hundred beans? If you shared them with ninety-nine other people, how many would each get?

speaker: Young Jichuan
content: If I share with ninety-nine people, everyone gets one bean, and I'd have one left for myself.

speaker: Jichuan's Father
content: What if you only shared with ten people?

speaker: Young Jichuan
content: Then everyone would get ten beans!
Her father scooped up all the remaining beans from the plate and pressed them into young Jichuan's hands.

speaker: Jichuan's Father
content: But if you took these and hid yourself away, you could keep all a hundred beans just for yourself.
Young Jichuan watched the beans stacked in her palms, thoughtful. Then she returned them all to the plate, taking not a single bean for herself.

speaker: Young Jichuan
content: Then I won't take any, so I can share with a whole hundred people!
//Black Screen
//Back to the inn
The raging snowstorm lashes the inn's weathered door, each gust a volley of steel blades forged from ice. The wooden bolt groans and creaks under the strain, on the verge of giving way.
Within the inn, firelight shudders and flickers across anxious faces. Dozens of elders, women, and children huddle in the shadows, their silent worry fixed upon the girl standing before the flames.
Jichuan returns the infant, whose fever has now broken, to the mother's waiting arms. She lifts a hand to her own mouth and wipes the fresh blood from her lip. It is done. She has made her choice.

speaker: Jichuan
content: <i><color=#7683a2>True or false, what does it matter? So long as there is the faintest possibility that suffering may unfold, I am bound to stand before it. This is the path my parents set beneath my feet, and the vow I made with Mudling: to become true martial heroes.</color><i>
She approaches the precarious wooden door, pulling it open just a sliver.
The storm outside gathers strength. Loose tiles plummet from the inn's roof, their landing smothered by the thick, forgiving snow.
The room does not comprehend this sudden act. Bewildered gazes linger on Jichuan's back, searching for a reason that is not there.

speaker: Jichuan
content: This storm has caged you long enough. To linger here awaiting its mercy is to surrender what little warmth remains. Now, I alone may hold the means to break this impasse.

speaker: Jichuan
content: What I do now may be like casting a candle into a river, futile in the eyes of reason, reckless in the eyes of prudence. Yet Heaven and Earth granted each of you this singular breath, and every life is as precious as the finest jade, never carved twice.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Though unworthy, I will offer my own steps to melt the ice that bars your way. With this resolve, I go now to carve a sanctuary for those who cannot yet raise a hand to shield themselves.
With that, she gives the infant in the woman's arms one final, gentle stroke upon the cheek. She exits the inn and presses forward, alone, into the teeth of the raging storm.
//Outside in the snowstorm
Even having channeled her internal force as a preemptive shield, Jichuan reels the instant she sets foot outside. The vicious wind shows no mercy.

Illness and cold conspire now, a united front ripping through meridians and scraping against her organs. She forces her pace to slow, allowing the fragile architecture of her body a single breath to recover.
She presses on toward the town center, where the storm's fury only intensifies. Walls groan and waver on the brink of collapse, while snow discharges from the rooftops in muffled, percussive thuds.
She enters the eye, and immediately, a low, stifled groan escapes her. Blood beads and trails from the corner of her mouth.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Ice worms at the viscera, fire ants along the sinew... I have grown rather familiar with this pain. It would seem Heaven's playwright has but one tired act, staged again and again.
She presses a hand to her chest, suppressing the ache. A light flick shakes the snow from her plum branch, and she aims it at the dark, oppressive sky.

speaker: Jichuan
content: I believe the soul endures beyond the flesh. I believe the wheel turns, that all beings are granted a new beginning, and that threads severed too soon may yet be knotted anew in another dawn.

speaker: Jichuan
content: And yet this world answers with the same unyielding judgment, afflicting the innocent, harvesting hope before its fruit can sweeten, and spinning mortal sorrow into a circle without end.

speaker: Jichuan
content: This bitter cycle of endless parting, of impossible reunion... Let it befall me alone.
Her words fade into silence as the plum branch sweeps through the air. Internal force surges with the motion, etching intricate runes into the space before her.
The runes scatter outward, a spiraling weave that expands to form an immense array, large enough to envelop the entire town.
From this pattern, a luminous white barrier surges upward. The wind and snow crash furiously against the light, yet find themselves unable to penetrate even an inch.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Ngh...! What a pity. I left in such haste... In the end, I never did taste my mother's rice cakes again... Cough!
The barrier shines so brilliantly, sheltering the entire town, yet it cuts Jichuan off from her paradise, from home.
From the shelter of the ruined walls, the townsfolk begin to emerge, one by one. They fix their wide, shocked eyes on the barrier before them.

speaker: Male Disaster Victim A
content: A plum branch draws the array, golden light shields every soul, and the storm can't get through... Th-this is straight out of the tales of martial heroes. It's the Plum Immortal Calming the Snow!

speaker: Male Disaster Victim B
content: But there ain't no immortals in this world... She's just a girl, barely more than a child. She shouldn't have to...

Jichuan offers no explanation, nor does she glance behind her. The hand that grips the plum branch trembles without cease. Her face is pale as paper now, each breath more labored than the last. She feels it acutely that her life force is bleeding away with every shred of internal force she spends.
Yet she cannot retreat, not even half a step. She cannot pause, not even for a moment.
Behind her stand countless fragile lives, the mortal world she is sworn to protect at any cost.

speaker: Jichuan
content: I did not imagine this solitary stand would weigh heavier than the clash for the codex upon the manor cliffs.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Perhaps it is because I knew, back then... that spring mountains awaited at my back, and trusted hands to catch me should I fall. Even had I failed at the final step, the flame would have remained to greet the dawn I longed to see.
Heaven and earth fade into white. There in the center of that vast, desolate snowscape, Jichuan's frail body sways on the verge of collapse.
She lifts her gaze toward the mist-veiled horizon and murmurs to herself.

speaker: Jichuan
content: I never found the moment to tell that person... Though I cherish the warmth of spring, the brilliance of living light... I have come to understand that winter's snow, for all its solitude, holds a quiet radiance all its own.

speaker: Jichuan
content: I'm told there is no snow in DisCity. Whatever ill wind gave rise to this storm... I hope only that the next snow to fall descends upon a joyous day, soft as cotton down, stirring only tender thoughts of homecoming and reunion.

Her hands grow so heavy around the plum branch that she can no longer lift them, not even a fraction. But she clenches her jaw. Her knuckles turn white, her fingertips tremble without end, and she does not let go.

speaker: Male Disaster Victim A
content: Miss Jiang! Please, you gotta stop! Don't go throwing your life away for folks like us!

speaker: Male Disaster Victim B
content: How could we ever repay a kindness like this? We ain't worthy of such a sacrifice...

The pleas behind her fade beyond hearing now. With the last shred of consciousness she still holds, she wears a peaceful smile. She will not let her parents and Mudling worry too much when they find her.
Her awareness fades further. She staggers, sways, and then her strength abandons her. She drops heavily to one knee, the plum branch plunging into the frozen earth with a sharp hiss.

speaker: Jichuan
content: How wonderful... The snow... it seems lighter now.

Bit by bit, the light fades—from ashen gray to murky gloom—until only endless darkness remains. Jichuan seems to see that familiar window again, warm and glowing. Her parents and Mudling smile and wave, beckoning her home.
She tries to lift her hand to wave back, but her fingers are too heavy. The snow has risen past her waist unseen, crept over her chest, and now swallows her whole.
//Black screen for a while
BOOM!!
//White flash cuts to a ray of light
Just as the snow is about to swallow Jichuan completely, a thunderous roar tears through the heavens.
A bolt of lightning rips the pallid clouds apart, and golden radiance pours down from above, striking the small snowdrift that buries her.
A golden rift splits open within the beam of light. Through it, a pair of hands reaches out and grasps Jichuan's hand—still visible above the snow—with a firm, unyielding grip.
I'm sorry. I should have come sooner.

Your consciousness was a mess of blizzards and mountain trails. You know I'm terrible with that kind of weather and terrain. If you hadn't disguised yourself as Shuang'er to guide me, I wouldn't have even found the manor's entrance.
//Intense BGM plays, Chief's portrait appears, snowy landscape background

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So, what should I call you this time? The little beggar girl, the manor master, or...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Jichuan, the one who fought the cold eating away at her body until the very last moment inside her own consciousness.

Jichuan is pulled free. She stares at the figure before her, consciousness still hazy, still confused. She blinks and shakes her head hard. The figure does not vanish; it only sharpens, growing clearer by the moment.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Why are you here? What... is all of this?

You do not wait for her to finish. The shackles pierce through, linking palm to palm. The excruciating pain that wracks Jichuan's body begins to recede, and the haze that clouds her mind slowly sharpens into clarity.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: After you left the manor, I never stopped looking for you. Everyone in town was searching too... Do you remember Bao?

speaker: Jichuan
content: Of course... A girl just past twelve. Among all the children who came to hear my stories, she alone would linger behind and pester me with endless questions.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: She's the one who found you in that cave. She took good care of you, and when she heard I was searching, she did everything she could to reach me.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Bao found me... Then I am still alive?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're still alive. Do you remember Aunt Liu from town? Chen, the blacksmith? And that inn server who was always ducking under the tables?

speaker: Jichuan
content: I remember them all. After my parents passed, their friends from every corner of the land came to the manor of their own accord, to watch over me, to teach me. But I was a restless, wayward child. I had no patience for classical texts and formal instruction. I would slip down the mountain whenever I could and lose myself among the townspeople, under the name Shuang'er.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Yeah, the townspeople all pitched in. They had Eastian merchant caravans send aged wheat all the way to DisCity, just so they could ask me to bring back their martial heroine of Northwild.
The snow keeps falling, but as Jichuan turns to look at the people behind her, their faces sharpen in the cold wind. One by one, they come into focus.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This isn't the afterlife. It's the final vision your mind created while fighting off death. It's everything you couldn't let go of, everything you couldn't escape from in those last moments. Your regrets, your attachments, your obsessions... All the deepest bonds of your life are here.
In disbelief, Jichuan touches the snow upon the ground and feels, to her surprise, a gentle warmth. A dazed, wondering smile crosses her face.

speaker: Jichuan
content: No wonder I lost my way here... But what of you?

speaker: Jichuan
content: Is your presence here a true thread connecting to the waking world... or merely the projection of one I hold most dear?
Her question is so sincere that, for a moment, it leaves you without words.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Well... Our brilliant manor master is a strategist of exceptional wisdom, isn't she? Once you wake and return to reality, I imagine you'll know the answer well enough.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So wake up. The rescue team will arrive soon to get you proper treatment. Spring hasn't come to Northwild yet. You promised you'd see it with me. Don't go breaking your word now.
You reach out your hand to her, but she only shakes her head in refusal.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Now that I understand the nature of this realm, no storm can lead me astray again. But I cannot leave with you just yet. There is something I must do first.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Do not worry. This time, I will not break my word. Wait for me outside.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Allow me to see you off first—

With a single thought, she drives the plum branch into the snow. It takes root in an instant. The shoots grow visibly, thickening and strengthening as flowering branches spread outward until the canopy covers the entire town, a shelter against every wind, every frost, every drop of rain and flake of snow.
The flowering canopy lifts you too, raising you toward the edge of this world. Through the dense tangle of plum branches, you see her serene smile receding into the distance.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Your mind's fully stabilized now, but your body still isn't ready to wake completely. I'll find a way to deal with the Mania contamination.

speaker: Jichuan
content: I will leave that to you!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Don't mention it. Then it's settled. See you in reality.
//BG: Paradise Cottage
When Jichuan returns to that cottage, everything remains exactly as she left it. Within the flickering candlelight, three figures gaze out at her with tender eyes.
This is all she has left to do, to see them one last time. But Jichuan does not cross the threshold. She remains outside the cottage, standing still and quiet.

speaker: Jichuan's Mother
content: Are you leaving now, my child?

speaker: Jichuan
content: Yes, it is time. I have made a promise to another, and many things are yet to be finished.

speaker: Jichuan's Father
content: The road ahead is long and winding. Walk with care, and guard your own well-being. That is what matters most to us.

speaker: Jichuan
content: I understand. Father, Mother... please take care as well.

speaker: Mudling
content: Chuan! You better work twice as hard, once for you and once for me, and become the greatest hero this world's ever seen!

speaker: Jichuan
content: ...Pinky swear! On my honor, I shall become a hero worthy of the name, and wherever injustice darkens the land, my hand shall rise in your place!
//Black Screen
//BG: Cave
//Communicator rings

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I found Jichuan. Her mental state's stable. I've got the Mania contained, so it won't spread any further through her system. But physically, she's in rough shape. Still not out of the woods. We need to loop in Banyan Medical College for a joint consult.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Copy that, Chief. The rescue team has just linked up with our Eastian informant, Bao. They'll be arriving at your location shortly.
You watch the gradual steadying of Jichuan's breath and let out the sigh you have been holding.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You've never been to DisCity, have you? Wake up soon. I'll show you around myself.
//BG: Hospital room entrance

Outside the emergency room, harsh fluorescent lights sting your eyes. Their stark white glare mingles with the thick reek of disinfectant, pressing down on the waiting area until the air feels suffocating.

After what seems an eternity, the glaring red light—Emergency Treatment in Progress—suddenly blinks out. The door swings wide. The doctor pulls off his mask, exhaustion carved into every line of his face, and walks straight toward you.

speaker: Doctor
content: Chief. Good news: the shackles you left inside her body did their job. They absorbed most of the corruption for her.
Your nerves stay stretched tight. You know, with sinking certainty, that a but is on its way.

speaker: Doctor
content: But she's been pushing her abilities past their limits for years. Her body gave out a long time ago. She was only managing through Eastian medicine. Most of her internal organs have deteriorated past the point of recovery. Honestly, it's remarkable she's made it this far.

speaker: Doctor
content: At this stage, life support is the only thing keeping her going. How long she holds on, whether she regains consciousness... that's out of our hands now.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...I understand. Thank you. For everything.
//Entering the hospital room
Inside the hospital room, machines keep their steady beep. Jichuan lies upon the bed, tethered by various medical lines. You take a quiet seat at her side.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Jichuan... just rest for now.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Don't worry about a thing. Everyone's going to be here waiting. You just focus on holding on, alright?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I've still got that plum branch you gave me. Soon as you wake up, we'll plant it together...
You know she probably cannot hear a word, so you do the only thing you can: you sit quietly at her bedside and keep a silent vigil.
Beep—Beep—Beep—
Night settles deeper, and the world narrows to the steady hum of the monitor and the whisper of Jichuan's breathing, so faint you strain to catch it.
Days of exhaustion finally overtake you. Resting against the edge of the bed, you let sleep pull you under.
//Black screen. Only the monitor's steady beeping remains.
Consciousness seeps back, and you find yourself in the interrogation room.
The metal table and chairs are familiar. The cold lighting is familiar. Only one thing is unexpected—Jichuan sits in the interrogation chair.
She wears her usual plain white dress, her face relaxed and serene, her gaze upon you perfectly calm.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Do not be alarmed. I sought you out of my own accord. That little chain you left within me is a curious thing. I thought if you could enter my consciousness, perhaps the current might flow both ways. I made the attempt, and here we are.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Though I confess, I did not imagine your dreamscape would take this form. What manner of place is this?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This is an interrogation room in DisCity. I use it to look into Sinners' pasts, ask questions, and get answers.

speaker: Jichuan
content: I see. Then I am ready for that!
She even takes a moment to adjust her clothes with formality, accepting this space with surprising ease. A hint of excitement even flickers through her bearing.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Shall we begin the interrogation? What would you ask of me?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're lying in a hospital bed right now, hooked up to more tubes than I can count. Why would I interrogate you like this? I just want you to wake up. Soon.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Besides, I've already filed my report on everything that happened at Northsnow Manor. There's nothing left to investigate. No loose ends.

speaker: Jichuan
content: If you have no intention of questioning me, then allow me to question you instead!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Question me???

speaker: Jichuan
content: Since you are here, you shall answer. First inquiry—
She gives you no time to react.

speaker: Jichuan
content: As "Chief of the Bureau," what duties fill your days? What rhythm governs your time, and by what means do you keep counsel with the world beyond?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Detaining anomalies, managing case files, handling crises... Basically, if it involves the order and safety of Sinners, it lands on my desk.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: My schedule's all over the place. Depends on whatever's happening that day. Overtime's a thing, vacation's a thing, though working through vacation is... also a thing.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Most of my communication goes through a "terminal." I can get you one set up if you want. That way, you can skip the carrier pigeons and letters and reach me wherever you are.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Do you truly take me for some relic of a bygone age? I at least know the concept of electronic correspondence.

speaker: Jichuan
content: It is only that the region I called home was plagued by frequent calamities, and thus lagged behind much of Eastia in such developments. And with all these years spent in seclusion at the manor, devoted to recovery, I never had cause to form connections elsewhere...
You prepare to offer words of comfort, but to your surprise, she shows no trace of sadness. A bright smile already graces her face as she moves on to her next question.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Second inquiry! Beyond your duties, have you pastimes to ease the hours? Do you share your leisure with friends?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I wouldn't say I have hobbies exactly, but I keep up with whatever's popular around DisCity. Games, movies, manga, stuff like that. Given the classified nature of my work, most of my friends are Bureau staff and Sinners.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Outside the Bureau... I've got a few connections. Met plenty of people while I was handling missions in Syndicate and Eastside.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Eastside, Syndicate... I recall now. My teacher always stressed the importance of knowing the wider world and its geography. Those are DisCity's eastern and western districts, are they not?

speaker: Jichuan
content: What did you do there? Did you also don the guise of a wandering hero, investigating Mania from the shadows?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What I did in the eastern and western districts? That's... a long story. We can save it for another time—

speaker: Jichuan
content: I wish to hear it.
She cuts you off mid-word. Her gaze settles on you, calm and impossibly steady.

speaker: Jichuan
content: I wish to hear it now.
The playfulness vanishes from Jichuan's tone entirely. In its place settles a quiet earnestness.

speaker: Jichuan
content: I want to know where you came from. Your past, your path, all that has shaped you... From Eastia to DisCity, we have walked together all this while, yet I have never had the chance to truly know you.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Would you... tell me now?
The word "now" falls from her lips with deliberate weight, and her smile holds something close to a plea. As though this moment is the only one you will ever have. Miss it, and there is no other.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Don't talk like that... You're going to wake up.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm not just going to share my life story with you now. I've still got so much work ahead, so many problems I'm going to need your help with. Oh, that reminds me!
You push yourself to rally, putting on the look of someone who has just landed on a brilliant idea.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You know, so many Sinners are just like you. I met them while I was out on missions. And now they've joined the Bureau. They come with me on new investigations all the time!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So it'll be the same for you. I've been thinking... you'd be way better suited for strategy and coordination than frontline work. There are quite a few Sinners at the Bureau I think you'd really click with.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Might I meet them as well?
Jichuan appears swept up in your enthusiasm, pulled into the vision of the future you are sketching before her.

speaker: Jichuan
content: What manner of people are these comrades of yours? I have little experience with Disians. I fear I may prove clumsy and bring you trouble instead.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You won't. You'll fit right in.
You start to think it over in earnest, summoning their faces to mind one after another.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: A lot of them are like you, deep down, holding onto something they refuse to let go of, no matter how rough the road gets. Steady and determined.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Then there are the ones who seem like they don't take anything seriously. Honestly, some of them are a real handful. But when it actually matters? More reliable than anyone. They pull through when you least expect it.

speaker: Jichuan
content: That sounds rather familiar. Is that not Xiaofeng to the letter?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And there's more. Some carry a lot of secrets. They've got their own way of doing things, keep to themselves... like they're standing just at the edge of the world...

speaker: Jichuan
content: They sound like the eccentric heroes from a storyteller's tale! They must be fascinating.

And so you keep going, telling her more and more. You tell her about past missions thick with danger, about how the West District has changed, about the troublesome Sinners at the Bureau who never give you a moment's peace, and about the many Eastians you have met along your path.
Watching her listen with such rapt attention, a memory surfaces: your first meeting. Back then, it was she who talked without end, introducing you to the martial world she knows inside and out.
You have no idea how long you speak, as time in dreams is always blurred. At last, just as you begin listing Summer's high-tech inventions for the third time, she smiles and says:

speaker: Jichuan
content: Dawn is approaching. You will wake soon, I think.

The air between you grows suddenly heavy. Dawn breaks outside, and soon you must return to your work, to your friends. But Jichuan lies in that hospital bed, and who can say when she will have the strength, or the chance, to speak with you like this through the night again.
You try to hide it, but she catches the sorrow lingering in your eyes.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Do not grieve. I know my own body better than anyone. We have both done all that could be done.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This doesn't have to be goodbye. I've pulled you back from the edge so many times before. I know there'll be a next time, and another after that—

speaker: Jichuan
content: Young hero... listen to me.

speaker: Jichuan
content: Life and death are currents beyond our command. Should I fall into slumber and never wake... do not let it burden your heart. And do not let despair take root because of me.

speaker: Jichuan
content: That plum blossom I gave you... tend it with care. When it blooms, that shall be me, still beside you.
Gentle as her words are, each one finds its way to pierce your heart.
//Sound effect of the monitor
Beep... Beep...
The monitor's rhythmic beeping bleeds into your awareness, and with it, the edges of the dream begin to blur and distort.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No, wait! I'm not done!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That's right! I never showed you around DisCity. I promised I would.

speaker: Jichuan
content: When was this? I do not recall.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: When you were unconscious in the cave. That's right. DisCity's got this old street with Eastian charm, full of specialty shops tucked away everywhere. A bunch of people from the Bureau love going there. You could tell them what's authentic and what's fake.

speaker: Jichuan
content: I have journeyed all the way to DisCity... and you would take me to Eastian shops?
Beep—Beep—Beep—
The drone of the ventilator swallows your voices whole, and your words begin to scatter into incoherent rambling.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Then we skip the shops. I'll pick a nice day and take all the Sinners from the Bureau out for team building. Do you know what team building is?

speaker: Jichuan
content: Going out to enjoy yourselves together?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Yes! Do you like hiking? There's this hill outside the city. From the top, you can see all of DisCity. Or maybe you'd want to try an amusement park? You've never left Eastia, so you've probably never been to one...
Beep—Beep—Beep—Beep—

speaker: Jichuan
content: All that you have named... I wish to see every one of them.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Then we'll see them all! We'll go to so many places together, help those who need it, stand up when something's wrong...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Don't you want to know how the manor is doing? Once you're better, we'll go back. Together.

speaker: Jichuan
content: All right. We will go together.
The interrogation room starts to blur at the edges, and Jichuan blurs with it, her colors slowly draining away.
The world around you dissolves into obscurity. The ventilator's drone swallows every other sound. You watch Jichuan's lips form words, but none of them reach you.
Allow me to call you "young hero" one last time, just as I did when we first met.
Young hero, until we meet again.
//Black Screen
//Back to the hospital room
After that long night of conversation, Jichuan never visits your dreams again.

The days blur into one another. Your Eastian friends—the ones who help you search—keep sending messages, asking after her condition. You can only reply with the same brief words, repeated each time: "Still under observation."
Gradually, everyone at the Bureau grows used to it: the Eastian girl in the ICU, suspended in her unending sleep.

You have no choice but to plunge back into the relentless grind of work. The moments you can spare for her bedside dwindle and shrink. Only in the deepest hours of night do you slip away to her room, where she lies unchanged, still and silent, showing no sign of waking.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Just how long are you gonna keep sleeping...
//Black Screen
//The Rust
This is the Rust's border. You have been fighting here for days, locked in a grueling, unrelenting battle.

Corruptors come in massive, endless waves, pouring through the blockade line without pause. The air is thick with smoke, choking and acrid. The battlefield roars with the sound of clashing steel and inhuman cries. Your unit fights on, mired in a desperate struggle that shows no sign of ending.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief! The Sinners are en route with reinforcements. They'll be on site any moment!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Copy.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: All units, pull back and tighten the line! Hold position and wait for backup!

You sweep your gaze across the battlefield, swallowing the anxiety that burns in your chest as you coordinate your forces with every ounce of focus you have. Just then, a new frequency cuts into your combat terminal.
Southeast flank, the air stirs wrongly. Enemy forces may seek to encircle us. Dispatch a squad to intercept without delay.

The Corruptors at the front are all bluster, fierce but lacking substance. Send two defensive specialists to anchor the center and blunt their advance. As for your position, Chief... leave that to me.

In the very next breath, a figure in white tears across the battlefield like the arc of silver wings. Her blade moves with lethal grace, carving through the chaos, and wherever she passes, the Rust's Corruptors collapse.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I told you to coordinate from the rear. What are you doing out here?

speaker: Jichuan
content: I insisted on coming. My pulse is steady today, and I have strength enough to spare. The physician rarely grants such leave, you know. If I do not move soon, my joints may well forget their purpose.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Oh? Well then, if I don't let you stretch your legs properly today, I'd be a pretty heartless Chief, wouldn't I?

speaker: Jichuan
content: Do not think to slacken your own efforts now! We made a promise, did we not? To face this world together, standing side by side. Hiding behind me would make a liar of you!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That's rich coming from you. You've been faking symptoms to trick me since the day you woke up. Don't you think you're in a pretty bad position to lecture anyone about honesty?

speaker: Jichuan
content: Then to be known alongside you as the <color=#fb9259>Gray-White Twin Deceivers</color>—why, I would count that the greatest fortune of my life.
Inside the porcelain vase on your office desk, the plum branch defies all reason and puts forth fresh, delicate buds.
[Is the Speaker of the City Council Driving DisCity's Future Off a Cliff?]

speaker: Anchor A
content: Speaker Max King was spotted vacationing at a seaside resort with a mysterious Outlander woman. Analysts say the trip could signal a growing alignment with Fraser. Professor, what's your take?

speaker: Professor B
content: It's a rather unusual move. Our analysis suggests that he's sending a clear message with the public display: Pledge your allegiance, and even someone from Fraser can earn a place among DisCity's elite. We've seen this playbook before in his grandfather's era.

speaker: Anchor A
content: You mean Ronald King and the former Commander? Ms. Maris's alliance would decide which side gained the satellite town's support. Rumor has it those two old friends on the establishment side spent their lives competing, yet neither ever won. Ms. Maris never took a side.

speaker: Professor B
content: My deepest respects to Ms. Maris. She never let political winds sway her convictions, dedicating her entire life to the fight against Mania. It is high time DisCity's politicians study the examples set by their predecessors. After all, only by learning from history can we build a better future!

speaker: Anchor A
content: For more on Ms. Maris, stay tuned for our special feature, The Life of Maris Andre. We'll be right back after the break...

speaker: Anchor C
content: This tip comes from an arms-dealing family descendant, and the truth may come as a shock to some of you: In the age of Mania weapons, the Andohar family is nearing bankruptcy. General Augustus’s lavish lifestyle, military expenses, and image maintenance have finally caught up with her.

speaker: Anchor C
content: Because of this, she is reportedly exploring new revenue streams. According to an insider tip, Shattered Blade commemorative coins and autographs of the General herself are already in production... with the first limited release consisting of 40,000 sets!

speaker: Anchor D
content: This is not an easy thing to admit, but yes, my friends, Marshal Dravyn was my biological grandfather. You only need to look at my gray eyes and hair to see the connection. My grandmother often told me stories of the time he spent at her estate during ceasefires many years ago.

speaker: Anchor D
content: The attic was prepared specifically for the Marshal. My grandmother was the daughter of a manor owner, a true country girl at heart. She loved climbing trees and scaling walls. That's why there's a little balcony up there. That's where they would always meet in the moonlight...

speaker: Anchor E
content: Don't miss today's juicy scoop! Why has the West District remained out of reach for so long? And which Paradeisos factions are so formidable that even the Cavendish family has to tread carefully around them? Drop me a couple of coins and I'll break it all down for you...
You turn off the screen displaying a diagram illustrating the Kervoz family's romantic histories, rubbing your aching eyes.

speaker: Chief
content: ...What was I watching?

speaker: Nightingale
content: Since the return of the DisCorps, the public's interest in conspiracy theories has been on the rise, fueling the popularity of this kind of "debunking" content. People no longer place their trust in textbooks or official records. Instead, they seek to challenge established narratives, expose the corruption of the ruling elite, and uncover the true history of this era.

options: This is what they call history?
This is what they call the truth?

speaker: Nightingale
content: Many believe so. Judging from the current situation, the movement has clearly spiraled out of control. Sensationalized, fabricated stories are flooding even mainstream channels, and the misinformation they spread is seeping into every sector.

speaker: Nightingale
content: The MBCC received a request for assistance claiming that Mania influence was behind this phenomenon, but our investigation has found no such connection so far. It may simply be an excuse to borrow the bureau's manpower due to their own staffing shortages...

You silently scan the report in your hands. It involves a wide range of parties. Besides the Public Security Bureau, municipal departments, and the military, even a few voices from Paradeisos have called for this matter to be addressed...

speaker: Chief
content: ...Not a bad reason to get involved, actually.
You think it over, then turn off the screen in front of you, standing up.

speaker: Chief
content: I'm heading to EDGE.

speaker: Chief
content: ...That's the current situation. Regarding this request for assistance, the MBCC's own archives contain limited documents, and this case clearly entails cross-referencing a large amount of DisCity's historical records.

speaker: Chief
content: We're all aware of how much of a hassle data access requests can be. Given the scale of this investigation, broader access clearance would help ensure a smoother process.
Schorl takes in your request, the light beams across its surface flickering.

speaker: Schorl
content: The scope of information you're interested in spans quite a range of categories, Chief, and the access permissions involved are... let's call it a labyrinth. My current module set isn't really built to navigate that gracefully. Fortunately, there's a dedicated institution designed to field requests like yours.
Just as you mentally prepare to have your request brushed off once again, Schorl's response takes an unexpected turn.

speaker: Schorl
content: EDGE has granted you a special information security clearance, so you'll now have high-level access to the <color=#fb9259>DisCity Central Library</color>. Beyond borrowing books or films you might enjoy, you'll be able to pull extensive backups of EDGE data.

speaker: Schorl
content: You'll also find exceptional professionals there who can provide the help you need. I'm confident they'll earn your trust.
You receive an incomplete dossier on your personal device.

speaker: Schorl
content: Celine Fabius is a scholar of considerable renown in academic circles. She also serves, by EDGE's commission, as our city-state's specially appointed <color=#fb9259>chronicler</color>, in charge of collecting, recording, enriching, and preserving our history from every conceivable angle.

speaker: Schorl
content: Her family holds deep roots in Paradeisos, which has left her with no shortage of connections. Yet despite her abundant resources, she maintains the integrity and restraint expected of a chronicler and witness. Quite admirable, if you ask me.

speaker: Schorl
content: The professor's grasp of DisCity's history—as well as the social, economic, and political currents beneath it—runs deep. Her standing is unimpeachable. I do hope she'll provide the assistance you require.

speaker: Chief
content: This dossier lists her as a Sinner from Paradeisos, but why is almost every field left blank here?

speaker: Schorl
content: Her ability is non-combat in nature, so she poses virtually no threat. She is effectively no different from an ordinary person, which is why registration was never required. Perhaps you could use this opportunity to establish contact with her.

speaker: Chief
content: Non-combat ability? What exactly does it do?

speaker: Schorl
content: Apparently, she has an <color=#fb9259>excellent memory</color>.

A few days pass. Just as online armchair historians drop their latest bombshell—that Speaker Max King is actually Speaker Stewart's secret illegitimate brother—you receive a notification that the historian is already waiting in the MBCC interrogation room.

With a cascade of jet-black hair and ice-blue eyes, the scholar before you sits with a calm gaze and composed demeanor. Her hands rest lightly on a blank notebook in her lap, as though she were here for a book club meeting rather than an interrogation.

speaker: Chief
content: Nice to meet you, Ms. Celine. Thank you for accepting our invitation. Allow me to introduce myself: I am ${PlayerName}, Chief of the Minos Bureau. I apologize for receiving you here, but please understand this is not a formal interrogation. It'll be just a routine interview followed by a simple registration.

speaker: Chief
content: Afterward, we will move to a proper conference room to discuss the fabricated historical accounts that have been circulating online.

speaker: Celine
content: Please, don't trouble yourself. This room is fine. Seeking historical truth and correcting the record are simply part of my work. I'll do everything I can to assist with your investigation. My apologies for the delayed registration. I've been tied up with my work at the library.
She offers a polite bow, her smile gentle and humble.

speaker: Celine
content: Shall we begin, then?

speaker: Chief
content: According to our records, you're a member of Paradeisos's renowned Fabius family and have served as Head Librarian of the Central Library for the past decade, overseeing DisCity's official historical records. Is that correct?

speaker: Celine
content: I see you've done your homework thoroughly. Yes, as the library's historian, my work primarily involves gathering historical materials, overseeing the library's day-to-day operations, and compiling and cataloguing records into the central system.

speaker: Celine
content: Over these past ten years, we have compiled a comprehensive history of DisCity, tracing events from Nightfall to the present day. The latest volume will be published shortly. If you happen to be a history buff too, Chief, I do hope you'll pick up a copy.

speaker: Celine
content: And if buying books isn't quite your thing, you're always welcome to register for a library card. A small deposit is all it takes, and you'll have access to a full century of DisCity's history.
Though she sounds perfectly sincere, the DisCity history sitting on the public shelves is not what you are after. As for the data you actually need, you're not certain she can provide it.

speaker: Option
options: Is that how the library keeps its lights on?
You really live up to your reputation as a celebrated scholar.

speaker: Celine
content: Hehe, running a library is unimaginably costly, while the budget Paradeisos provides isn't always enough to cover all the costs. Most of the time, we simply have to come up with ways to pay the bills on our own.

speaker: Chief
content: Can't you apply for more funding?

speaker: Celine
content: That would require convincing people that the library's efforts in preserving history and educating the public are more urgent than the industrial crisis, Mania research, or even the Outland War.

speaker: Chief
content: Or that it matters more than the birthday dinner party some official's mistress is throwing.

speaker: Celine
content: ...You've got a nice sense of humor, Chief.
Her eyes crinkle as a warm smile spreads across her face.

speaker: Celine
content: I'm grateful that you share that view. But it's all right. We've long since made our peace with it.

speaker: Celine
content: This profession existed long before Nightfall. A historian's job is to faithfully document every historical event, to devote oneself to recovering scattered records. And yet, more often than not, we are only allowed to write what pleases those in power, or worse, compelled to fabricate false evidence.

speaker: Celine
content: People need these record keepers to preserve their history, yet they also fear the power of their pens. Poverty, persecution, and even exile are common occupational hazards. Survival becomes especially difficult during times of transition. In fact, the pre-Nightfall records we possess today were once fragments passed down through this river of blood, preserved in the same arduous manner.

speaker: Celine
content: Nightfall changed the world beyond recognition, yet our duties of investigation, documentation, compilation, and research remain unchanged. Instead of the tyrants of the past, Mania is now our greatest adversary. As for poverty, oppression, solitude, and temptation, they are obstacles that have never vanished, and never will.

speaker: Celine
content: Even so, many of my colleagues gave everything they had, risking their lives to preserve the precious few records that survived, gathering them through whatever channels they could find so that others might one day read them.

speaker: Celine
content: And so, securing funding through various means, keeping the library running, and honoring the sacrifices of those who came before, that is the call of duty the library and I must answer in this age.

speaker: Celine
content: Academics are deemed "useless" by many. What a shame. If only these history books were worth as much as Hypercubes...
You shake your head at her words.

speaker: Chief
content: You're being way too humble. What you do is remarkable.

speaker: Chief
content: During several major incidents in the past, the historical materials provided by the library played a crucial role.

speaker: Chief
content: Records about the DisCorps, the metropoles, and even the origins of the West District and Nirvana... Without the help of you and your colleagues, we never could have resolved some of those issues so quickly.

speaker: Chief
content: That said, most of this information is locked away in the archives, and ordinary people can never access it. That seems somewhat at odds with what the library stands for.

speaker: Celine
content: My, that's quite a pointed question, Chief.
Not seeming offended by your remark, she simply smiles and explains.

speaker: Celine
content: History is an immensely complex subject. Verified facts, disputed interpretations, and even embellished conjectures are often intertwined. Releasing them all without distinction could easily lead to misuse and misinterpretation, ultimately pushing the public further away from the truth.

speaker: Celine
content: There's an old saying in our field: "Let history be the judge." Many perspectives must stand the test of time before they can truly become part of history. That is why I do not insist that everything be immediately made available to the public. While I wish to reveal the true and accurate account of history, I also feel a responsibility to safeguard against its more chaotic aspects.

speaker: Chief
content: But that also leaves the public in the dark, vulnerable to all kinds of misinformation. Which is exactly the problem we're facing right now.

speaker: Celine
content: ...Sigh.
She lets out a slightly theatrical sigh.

speaker: Celine
content: I've been keeping a close eye on this situation as well. It's disheartening to see some of my colleagues get caught up in it. The pressures and temptations of this era can change people, and even historians are not immune to such influences.

speaker: Chief
content: Are you suggesting a certain expert might be pulling the strings behind all this?
She blinks.

speaker: Celine
content: I'm not sure what sort of expert might be behind this, but it would certainly take a great deal of calculation to construct arguments that appear so sound and credible, and that have spread so rapidly and so widely. Isn't that why you came to the library, Chief? Because you had the same thought?

speaker: Celine
content: To be frank, I've been racking my brain over this myself... As a historian, the spread of such fabricated records both irritates and saddens me. However, the library is already understaffed, and we simply don't have the resources to conduct an investigation of our own.

speaker: Celine
content: Therefore, I'm very glad to hear the MBCC is willing to take this on.

speaker: Chief
content: There are plenty of young, intellectual minds in the Bureau, after all. I'd hate to see them led astray by this kind of misinformation.
As you speak, you put an investigation report on the desk.

speaker: Chief
content: We sifted through a massive amount of data and identified several videos that stood out as particularly suspicious. They cover a wide range of topics, but a number of them feature historians affiliated with the library.

speaker: Chief
content: Our conversation has told me everything I need to know about where you stand. You carry yourself with the dignity and integrity of a respectable historian. And I believe you're just as determined as we are to find whoever is behind this.

speaker: Celine
content: Hehe... Then I'll gladly accept your trust, Chief.
She nods with a smile, her gaze skimming over those videos before settling on a particular name.

speaker: Celine
content: Chief, have you heard of the name Maris Andre?

speaker: Chief
content: That woman who will soon be posthumously awarded the DisCity Leader Medal for her efforts against Mania? Of course I've heard of her.

speaker: Chief
content: A civilian hero who aided in the Battle of Glory of the Rust, helped establish multiple anti-Mania facilities, and even contributed to the development of Mania detection technology during the MBCC's early days. There's even a biography of her in the Bureau's library. I have no idea how long it's been sitting there.

speaker: Celine
content: But regretfully, <color=#fb9259>Maris Andre never actually existed.</color>

speaker: Celine
content: Of course, this has nothing to do with Mania. Someone has simply wielded their academic influence and fabricated her existence.

speaker: Celine
content: Records about her follow a single linear timeline. They are thorough, but not flawless. Nearly every milestone in her life traces back to pre-existing Mania-related events. Her birthplace, related artifacts, portraits, and even her biography only appeared in the public eye after those key events had been established.

speaker: Chief
content: How can you be so certain? Couldn't these so-called flaws be a result of incomplete historical records?

speaker: Celine
content: Because... N.F. 103 was a remarkable year. It was the year when the Eclipse Operation failed, the BR-003 crisis erupted, and a humble historian awakened her special power. Yet in this historian's mind, no one by that name ever returned from the Rust since.
Your breath catches.

speaker: Celine
content: Oh... Did I surprise you? You invited me here because you had questions about our history, didn't you? And I'm only answering them honestly.
She smiles softly, lowering her gaze. Something in the air has shifted.

speaker: Celine
content: My approach differs slightly from that of other historians. What others record with pen and paper, I can remember after a single glance. And that includes not only the documents indexed in the Grand Library's system, but also the highly classified files that never see the light of day.

speaker: Celine
content: Your question about access to the Grand Library's archives was rather tactful, but I could sense the frustration you experienced from these restrictions.

speaker: Celine
content: There's no need to worry. I understand, truly. You seek access to more historical data, and I wish to correct the flood of false information spreading through society. That gives us common ground for a meaningful partnership.

speaker: Chief
content: What exactly do you mean by partnership? Are you saying you can help me get higher clearance?

speaker: Celine
content: I'm afraid not. If Paradeisos hasn't granted you that clearance, it isn't my place to overstep. After all, I'm just a humble civil servant.
She effortlessly shifts the responsibility back onto EDGE, resting her chin in her hand, a mysterious smile playing at her lips.

speaker: Celine
content: But I can certainly put in an application on your behalf, along with a letter of recommendation. That may help things move along a little more smoothly.
Your heartbeat quickens.

speaker: Celine
content: All I ask in return is that you help me bring Maris Andre's puppet master to justice. A fair trade, wouldn't you say?
She extends a gentle invitation, waiting patiently for your answer.
She already knows it'll be positive.

speaker: Chief
content: Sure, but there's one thing I don't quite follow. If this has nothing to do with Mania, why come to the MBCC?
At that, she gives you a knowing wink.

speaker: Celine
content: For one thing, you've piqued my curiosity, Chief... I'm about to begin compiling a historical record of the West District, and I was hoping to arrange an in-depth interview with you.

speaker: Celine
content: And for another, I imagine the Bureau is considerably better staffed and funded for this sort of thing than the library.
So that's what it all comes down to, huh...
Rain drips from the man's disheveled hair as he squeezes sideways through the ajar door, clutching a crumpled coat against his chest. The door hinge groans, refusing to budge.
Unbelievable. They're right on your doorstep the second the electric bill's due, but ask them to fix a door, and suddenly they've got a million excuses!
Still grumbling, the man squeezes through the gap. He produces several thick books from the unfurled coat, makes room for them on the desk, then whips out an old gas lamp.
The moment he turns the lamp on, two massive, looming silhouettes stretch across the wall.
Ghosts!!!
With a dull thud, the man crumples to the floor.

speaker: Figure in the Dark
content: Oh my... Perhaps we went a little too far with the prank.
The two silhouettes step forward. One of them reaches out and pokes at Morton's hair, which is as messy as a bird's nest.

speaker: Chief
content: Did he actually faint from fright?

speaker: Celine
content: Hmm... I don't think so. More likely from low blood sugar induced by hunger... Could you help me get him onto the couch?
Celine and you haul Professor Morton onto the worn-out couch, then feed him some leftover bread crusts found in the back of the fridge, softened with some warm water.
In the meantime, Celine calls the power company and settles the overdue bill. A little while later, the lights flicker on at last, and the man on the couch stirs slowly back to consciousness.
