In the meantime, Celine calls the power company and settles the overdue bill. A little while later, the lights flicker on at last, and the man on the couch stirs slowly back to consciousness.

speaker: Morton
content: You... you're...

speaker: Chief
content: I'm ${PlayerName}, Chief of the MBCC. This is the Bureau's archivist. Sorry for letting ourselves in. The door was open, and no one answered, so we took the liberty. You must be Professor Morton?
Morton eyes the two of you with quiet suspicion, his gaze shifting back and forth through the cracked lens of his glasses.

speaker: Morton
content: That's right. MBCC... Sure, I've heard of it. Can't say it has much to do with me, though. What brings you here?

speaker: Celine
content: Please excuse our intrusion, Professor Morton. We have some questions regarding Maris Andre, and we were hoping you could enlighten us.
You step forward, cutting off Morton's lingering gaze at Celine, and nudge the plate of toast on the coffee table toward him.

speaker: Chief
content: You passed out from low blood sugar just now, so we made you something in the kitchen. Hope you don't mind.

speaker: Morton
content: Hey, don't worry about it. If anything, I should be thanking you. Sorry about that. Must've given you a scare.

Muttering to himself, he pushes up from the couch and reaches into his pocket out of habit, fishing for a cigarette, but the lighter produces nothing more than a spark. He gives up and stuffs another piece of toast crust into his mouth instead.

speaker: Morton
content: Right, you said there was something you wanted to know about Maris?

speaker: Celine
content: Yes. I've been reorganizing some historical records lately, and came across a few inconsistencies. You're one of the leading experts in this field, so I asked Chief to bring me here.

speaker: Chief
content: Everyone we asked said you rarely show up to events and don't own a phone, preferring to spend all your time on your research. It took quite a bit of effort to track you down... but now we truly see what a devoted scholar you are.
Morton seems rather pleased with all the flattery. Chuckling, he gestures to the side, and Celine settles onto a stool nearby, producing a notebook and pen with practiced grace.

speaker: Celine
content: According to your book, Maris of Glorie, in the N.F. 50s, the metropoles launched an aid program in DisCity, sponsoring children from reputable families or those who showed academic potential. The true purpose was to train spies for their eventual infiltration into DisCity.

speaker: Celine
content: And yet, Ms. Maris came from the slums and didn't meet the selection criteria at the time. So how exactly was she chosen?
The seasoned academic chuckles, then begins sincerely.

speaker: Morton
content: A historical event must be read in the correct context. To understand that, you have to know DisCity's social climate at the time. The wealthy families were well aware of the metropoles' scheme, so many of them found substitutes for their chosen children. It was entirely plausible that Maris went in someone else's place.

speaker: Celine
content: I see. Then, to prove that, shouldn't we also verify exactly who she replaced?

speaker: Morton
content: You're right. It took me six months of digging before I made any headway. She took the place of a merchant's son, and it was around that time she adopted the surname Andre. All of this will be included in the new edition of Glorie, which is coming out next month.

speaker: Celine
content: I see. Thank you for clarifying. My next question concerns a patented technology developed by Ms. Maris during the early stages of Mania detection research, which also earned her the honorary title of...

speaker: Morton
content: I covered that report in the book. Chapter seven.

You're quite surprised. Morton has a thorough answer ready for every question about Maris. He's also able to defend the flaws in his theories. You can't fathom just how much time and effort must have gone into making the fabricated story seem so impeccable.
There is no doubt he is indeed an exceptional historian.

speaker: Celine
content: Yes, the report is quite clear. However, the patent number begins with "RE," indicating it was resubmitted at some point. According to the patent office's records, Ms. Maris's name was not listed on the original submission.

speaker: Morton
content: Consider yourself lucky you're not in academia, young lady. You'd have made a fool of yourself.
Morton leans back into the couch, settling into a more comfortable position.

speaker: Morton
content: Under the guidelines of the time, the "RE" prefix denoted a supplementary submission, not a reapplication.

speaker: Morton
content: Reapplications were subject to a time limit, and supplementary submissions were not. Therefore, regardless of who the initial applicant was, the fact that Maris was a co-applicant on the patent is beyond dispute.

speaker: Celine
content: But... when this application was first filed, Ms. Maris hadn't even been born yet.

speaker: Morton
content: That changes nothing. Maris popularized anti-Mania infrastructure. She was the one who completed the puzzle of modern anti-Mania technology. Her name deserves to be on the patent.
Attributing a predecessor's work to someone born later by manipulating the guidelines... That simply makes no sense.
You furrow your brow, meaning to speak up, when Celine gives a quiet nod.

speaker: Celine
content: I see, Professor Morton. Compared to outright fabrication, facts altered by exploiting loopholes are indeed far less noticeable.

speaker: Morton
content: What do you mean?
Celine sets down her pen and paper, then draws a stack of documents from her bag.

speaker: Celine
content: Before coming to see you, I did some research on Glorie. It turns out that the birthplace of the famous Maris Andre is surprisingly poorly documented. Luckily, I found the records I needed in several satellite towns a few dozen kilometers away.

speaker: Celine
content: Suppose there was a leader who was born in the slums, handpicked by the metropoles, and trained to become a spy. After witnessing the suffering of her homeland, she turned against the metropoles and ultimately led her hometown to become a satellite city of DisCity.

speaker: Celine
content: Suppose there was a soldier who, after holding the line against countless disasters, enrolled in university, only to return to the battlefield before graduating... and ultimately gave his life during the Eclipse Operation.

speaker: Celine
content: Suppose there was a researcher who treated countless Mania patients with crude equipment, collecting invaluable data and samples. Believing herself no more than an amateur, she donated it all to the authorities free of charge. She later died from prolonged Mania exposure, never living to see her name on the patent.

speaker: Celine
content: Professor Morton, as a historian, what future would you say awaited them?
Morton's hands grip the edge of the desk, knuckles whitening. He says nothing.

speaker: Celine
content: You seem hesitant to give an answer, Professor. Then, allow me. Their stories were buried under dust, and many years later, they share one common name... Maris Andre.

speaker: Morton
content: Shut up!

speaker: Chief
content: Sit down!
You loom over him, drawing your gun.

speaker: Chief
content: Maris Andre is so famous and influential that one wrong move could jeopardize the public image of the city's authorities. That's the only reason you're still sitting comfortably at home having this conversation instead of being dragged away in handcuffs. Are we clear?

You never get the chance to put what you learned during your shooting lessons at the Bureau to use. Morton keeps his eyes fixed on Celine, and it becomes clear that her impeccable manners frighten him far more than the barrel of your gun.

speaker: Morton
content: She was real. Of course she was real! Just look at all the evidence!

speaker: Morton
content: Because of her, civilian anti-Mania movements have flourished, and donations for DisCity's heroes have been pouring in. Isn't all of that thanks to her?! You two have benefited from this too. So why are you...

speaker: Chief
content: So you're admitting this book of yours is just a bunch of lies, then?

speaker: Morton
content: Lies? You've got to be kidding me! Ninety-nine percent of the events in the book actually happened. I didn't make any of them up!
Morton glares back with bloodshot eyes, like a bull ready to charge.

speaker: Morton
content: It fills in the gaps in DisCity's modern history. Every Disian should read it! Say whatever you want. Ten years, twenty years, even a hundred years from now, this book will remain a cornerstone of historical scholarship!

speaker: Morton
content: People will never forget what she went through. Her legacy will live on in them. No matter the era, her light will always guide them forward...

speaker: Celine
content: That's one way to glorify deception, Professor Morton. If your only goal was to pass on "her legacy," why didn't you just write a novel instead? Why should any of us willingly wade through dry, tedious historical facts?

speaker: Celine
content: You're simply satisfying your selfish intellectual desire.
Celine closes her notebook and looks up.

speaker: Celine
content: You're simply satisfying your selfish intellectual desire.
Celine closes her notebook and looks up.

speaker: Celine
content: You deem ordinary people ignorant, so you use your expertise to exploit that weakness and deceive them. You believe your seemingly noble cause can justify deception, the erasure of truth... all for this so-called "gain."
With his darkest thoughts laid bare so effortlessly, Morton finally seems shaken.

speaker: Morton
content: You... just who are you?!

speaker: Celine
content: Take a closer look, Professor.
Morton finally gets a good look at his interviewer who has been standing behind Chief all along.

speaker: Celine
content: Take a closer look, Professor.
Morton finally gets a good look at his interviewer who has been standing behind Chief all along.

speaker: Celine
content: Take a closer look, Professor.
Morton finally gets a good look at his interviewer who has been standing behind Chief all along.

speaker: Celine
content: Take a closer look, Professor.
Morton finally gets a good look at his interviewer who has been standing behind Chief all along.
Through the thick lenses of his glasses, his wary, suspicious eyes gradually widen, and his fingers begin to tremble. Finally, he recognizes that face.
A deathly silence hangs over the dim room. All that remains is his feeble, mumbling voice.

speaker: Morton
content: After the rerouting in WhiteSands, Glorie fell into decline. Developers complained about the poor soil conditions and kept pushing prices down. The locals received barely any compensation and were on the verge of being forced out of their own homes.

speaker: Morton
content: If Glorie could become something special... If it were more than just another unremarkable little town in WhiteSands, its fate would have been entirely different.

speaker: Morton
content: It was around that time that those people came to me with a photocopied set of handwritten notes...

speaker: Morton
content: Biographical research is my specialty. I know of countless people like that... It's what I've dedicated my life to studying! So many people are forgotten simply because their stories aren't exciting enough, or because of their flaws. They're too ordinary to be seen as heroes, so no one wants to talk about them!

speaker: Morton
content: All I needed... was one opportunity to bring Glorie's history to light. People would remember these stories, this town, and those nameless heroes...

speaker: Celine
content: Professor Morton.
She leans forward to steady Morton, who is overwhelmed by emotions and on the verge of collapsing, her voice settling back into its usual calm, gentle tone.

speaker: Celine
content: Your book does contain fabricated sections, but as you said, over 90% of it is genuine history. Once properly revised, it will still be a remarkable work. As a fellow historian, my respect for your academic expertise remains unchanged.

speaker: Celine
content: I know you've poured every penny into your research, persevering through countless hardships. Your dedication is admirable, and that's why I believe you were simply led astray by temptation.

speaker: Celine
content: We historians are rarely tempted by mere money or fame. The truly dangerous lures are ideas disguised as grand ideals, historical missions, or the pursuit of truth.

speaker: Celine
content: Poverty cannot kill our conviction, but arrogance can.

speaker: Celine
content: But what matters is that now we both know it is wrong. Professor Morton, would you be willing to hand over the documents those people gave you? We will follow this lead and pursue those behind it. Once this is all over, these precious records will be preserved, joining the endless river of history.
She's tactfully pointed out Morton's weakness without sounding overly critical of his mistake, and she's now even making an offer he cannot possibly refuse.
For a while, Morton trembles harder under her gentle gaze. At last, deflated, he shuffles to the bookshelf and retrieves a safe.

speaker: Morton
content: Here's the original manuscript. The information in the hidden compartment is all true. If they hadn't shown me those records and made me believe I was Glorie's only hope, I never would have accepted their offer...
He clutches the safe with both hands, as if lifting those sheets of paper has drained every last bit of strength he has.

speaker: Morton
content: Once these documents are in the library... will I still have access to them?

speaker: Celine
content: Rest assured, Professor Morton. I have great respect for your work. When all of this is behind you, if you still wish to pursue the truth, you'd be welcome to join us at the library.
He hands the case over reluctantly, drawing a long breath. And somehow, he seems to stand a little straighter now.

speaker: Morton
content: Thank you, Ms. Celine. It was once my dream to work at the Central Library, but I never quite measured up, so I ended up becoming an independent researcher...

speaker: Morton
content: I'm grateful for your leniency, but... there are still a few things I should probably disclose to you.
With a calm, resolved expression, he bends down and lifts the cushion of the worn couch. Beneath layers of plastic wrapping, you see stacks of glaring banknotes.

speaker: Morton
content: When they paid me, they marked every bill and filmed the entire transaction. After all, accepting the money would prove that I had become their accomplice.

speaker: Morton
content: But sitting on it every day was like being burned at the stake. I never dared touch a single bill. Take it. Perhaps it'll give me some leverage when I'm put on trial.
When you come out of Morton's home, the overcast skies that have hung over Eastside for days have finally cleared, and the sun is shining brightly.

speaker: Chief
content: I didn't expect you to forgive him so easily.

Celine steps over a glittering puddle on the ground deftly. The wind catches her skirt and veil, as though the two of you have been gently swept into a passing cloud. You hear her voice without seeing her face.

speaker: Celine
content: Moore

speaker: Celine
content: Though, today's events remind me of someone I once knew. The response that person gave in the end was quite different from Morton's. Would you like to hear it, Chief?

speaker: Chief
content: What did this person say?

speaker: Celine
content: He said that as long as people's lives improved, he didn't care if his name was erased from the library's records. He believed the welfare of the living was far more important than lifeless knowledge preserved on paper.

speaker: Chief
content: ...And what became of him?

speaker: Celine
content: His reputation was utterly ruined. His name was removed from every work he had authored, and he vanished completely from academia. But the people he had helped never forgot him. He remained in history in another form.
She pauses beside you. Perhaps it is the weather, but you could almost swear that detached smile of hers looks genuinely warm and bright for a moment.

speaker: Celine
content: Which response do you prefer, Chief?

options: That unnamed figure was indeed brave.
An ordinary person like me doesn't really think about this kind of thing.

speaker: Celine
content: At its core, history is a collection of objective facts. Its keepers must possess an impartial heart, a commitment to truth, and the resolve to leave an honest account for future generations.
B: That unnamed figure was indeed brave.

speaker: Celine
content: To many, history is no different from mere tales. We look back on history in search of lessons that can guide us toward a better life. So... being able to achieve that goal directly would indeed be a tempting idea.
C: An ordinary person like me doesn't really think about this kind of thing.

speaker: Celine
content: Pfft, that's indeed a very "Chief-like" answer. I think I could use a little bit of that frankness myself. That would definitely help me get over some past troubles that still haunt me.
(Convergence)
You can tell she's just giving you a polite answer. Someone as tactful as her would never reveal her true feelings under these circumstances.
Against the fading light of the setting sun, she lifts the photocopy in her hand and holds it out toward you.

speaker: Celine
content: Chief, I doubt we can stop the upcoming memorial events for Maris Andre with what we've gathered today alone.

speaker: Celine
content: You may have heard of the Pierce family of Eastside. They built their reputation through collecting and restoring historical artifacts, but after a change in leadership in recent years, they've expanded into commerce. They have strong connections within the city's elite circles.

speaker: Celine
content: This mark here matches their family crest.
Her finger points to a faint imprint in the bottom-right corner of the photocopy. It's a logo composed of several shields.
You recall seeing this family name in the investigation report. In three days, they are hosting a banquet to celebrate the inauguration of the Maris Andre Memorial Hall.

Over the years, the Black Rings have become a unit we use to measure time: N.F. 89, BR-001. N.F. 104, BR-002. N.F. 112, BR-004... But before them, there was another way to define an era.
In N.F. 68, she kindled the first light amid the ruins. In N.F. 72, she saved more than twenty thousand lives. In N.F. 76, Mania detection technology was born...
Today, countless barriers shield us from Mania. Yet this unsung hero spent her entire life reminding us that, in the face of disaster, humanity's final line of defense has always been our resolve to stand by one another.
This is not the story of a single hero. It is the story of humanity itself.
This film is dedicated to every brave soul who walks through the ashes.
— Maris Andre

As the text on the screen fades away, thunderous applause fills the elegant, ornate memorial hall. The chandelier gradually lights up as the guests raise their glasses in unison, their expressions sincere, some even teary-eyed.

speaker: Pierce
content: Let us raise a toast to the subject of our documentary, Ms. Maris Andre, and to every unsung hero among us.

The young aristocrat raises his glass to the guests. Ever since inheriting the family enterprise a year ago, he has abandoned the family's traditionally low-profile approach, using the media to showcase its collection to the public. He has also been doing everything he can to secure a place in the city's high society.

speaker: Celine
content: I'd like to take a look at the calligraphy and paintings over there. Shall we, Chief?
Her calm, gentle voice remains unperturbed by the excitement buzzing around her. Celine loops her arm through yours and leads you toward the exhibits that caught her eye.

The Pierce villa is vast. After winding your way through its endless corridors, you arrive at the memorial hall just as the opening ceremony draws to a close. The guests disperse like a school of well-fed fish, each drifting at their own pace through the currents of history, admiring the grand portrait of Ms. Maris behind low-reflection glass with solemn reverence.

speaker: Curator
content: The layout and arrangement of the memorial hall are truly well thought out. It chronicles Ms. Maris's life while painting a vivid picture of the Disians' everyday life at the time. Ms. Maris was truly the symbol of that era...

speaker: Pseudo-historian
content: Indeed. She witnessed DisCity's growth from its infancy, through its roaring golden age, into the global powerhouse it is today...

speaker: Painter
content: General Augustus is immortalized by Breaching BR-005. Likewise, Ms. Maris deserves a painting of her own, Silent Night Walk. The painting on that wall is my tribute to her. I never had the chance to meet her in person, but in my heart, she is a goddess bearing a lantern, lighting the way for a world ravaged by Mania.

speaker: Writer
content: "Ms. Andre's gaze was ever piercing, always insightful. There burned within her eyes an indestructible flame." A line from the biography Maris of Glorie. What a masterpiece! If you look closely at the painting, you can actually see the light of her lantern reflected in her eyes.

speaker: Editor-in-Chief
content: Oh, that reminds me. Where is Professor Morton?

speaker: Pierce
content: Ladies and gentlemen! You are all distinguished figures in your respective fields, and dear friends who share my passion. So allow me to speak from the heart...
The hall buzzes with voices, but these individuals stand out in particular, speaking loudly and confidently.

speaker: Chief
content: I'm afraid these people all play a part in fabricating the image of Maris Andre. That painting doesn't even show her full face. Are they afraid of getting caught using a real person's face as reference?

speaker: Celine
content: They kept the face blurry because they were not trying to make a portrait of a real person, but a "symbol of an era."

speaker: Celine
content: The painter creates the image, the writer shapes the persona, the media stirs public empathy, and the curator pieces together these fabricated fragments into a coherent narrative. That is all it takes to make a hero. Human beings have always been good at creating idols.

speaker: Celine
content: It's a shame that the only genuine antique in this entire hall is that crystal chandelier. Everything else is a forgery. It seems Mr. Pierce has just enough sense to know that the real treasures are best kept hidden.

The crowd suddenly parts. Pierce approaches, champagne glass in hand. As he draws closer, you can clearly see that huge ring on his thumb, a striking piece fashioned in the shape of a three-sided shield.

speaker: Pierce
content: Are you... Chief ${PlayerName}? It really is you! I thought I had the wrong person from across the room. And you are...

speaker: Chief
content: Nice to meet you, Mr. Pierce. This is the Bureau's archivist.

speaker: Pierce
content: A pleasure to meet you! There were so many guests at the peace banquet last time that I never had the chance to speak with you. I hear the MBCC keeps you quite busy... Are you here because you're interested in Ms. Maris's life, or is there some other matter you wish to discuss?

speaker: Chief
content: We've been archiving some old files lately, and many of them are from unidentified periods. I heard the memorial hall would be exhibiting materials from the Independence era, so I thought I'd come take a look ahead of time. Please don't feel the need to make any special arrangements for me.

speaker: Chief
content: Though I must say, the exhibition downstairs seems rather sparse. I've already taken a full tour and seen most of what's on display.
This is a script you and Celine worked out in advance. Given the Pierce family's eagerness to mingle with the upper echelons, you can easily get his attention this way.

Fortunately for you, Celine rarely appears in public, so she isn't easily recognized. With nothing more than a change of clothes, she can pass herself off as your assistant. After all, if her identity were exposed here, it would be no different from announcing your true purpose out loud.

speaker: Editor-in-Chief
content: Get the cameraman over here! This could be tomorrow's headline.

speaker: Pseudo-historian
content: I seem to recall the Chief's dance partner last time was that rather imposing general. But it's not the same person this time...

A crowd begins to gather. Pierce's smile deepens. He waves a server over, murmurs a few words, then turns and gestures for you, one of DisCity's most talked-about public figures these days, to join him.

speaker: Pierce
content: What matters to society matters to me. As witnesses to DisCity's history, the Pierce family has always valued its bonds with those who seek the truth.

speaker: Pierce
content: Indeed, there are some limitations as to what we can display downstairs. If you'd like to see some rarer exhibits, Chief, please follow me.
Pierce leads you both upstairs courteously. You spend nearly ten minutes navigating the labyrinthine corridors before he finally stops before a pair of heavy redwood doors.

It is a lavish study, its decor appearing as though it had been salvaged from some grand old building and carefully reassembled here. Books and folders line the shelves in neat rows. Though the origins of the antique furnishings are unknown, they all appear exceedingly luxurious.

speaker: Pierce
content: You're looking at my family's private collection, Chief. Though we're still in the same building as the memorial hall, this area is subject to much stricter security measures, as it houses a far more important collection.

speaker: Pierce
content: This area is equipped with the finest climate control systems, allowing us to safely incorporate these artifacts into our daily lives. Any single piece you see in this room could easily become the centerpiece of an exhibition at any public museum.

speaker: Chief
content: A collection of this size must have taken considerable money and effort to maintain.

speaker: Pierce
content: Haha, naturally. Three generations of my family's dedication are preserved in this room. Quite a few pieces were acquired through... special means. You'll never see such pieces on the open market. My ancestors were content simply to collect, but I believe these treasures deserve to be admired by more people.

speaker: Pierce
content: Is there any particular piece that catches your eye, Chief? I'd be happy to give you a proper introduction.

Wine is served, and you settle into the seat across from Pierce for a rather diplomatic conversation. Celine wanders around the room before stopping at the shelves, and within moments, she is completely absorbed. Judging by her reaction, she must have taken an interest in a few items from the collection.

speaker: Chief
content: Mr. Pierce, please excuse my assistant. She works best without an audience, so kindly let her be. Now, do tell me more about your family. That ring on your thumb has caught my attention.

speaker: Pierce
content: Heh, you have a keen eye, Chief. It bears my family's crest and motto, passed down for over a century. The three shields symbolize collection, scholarship, and legacy...

speaker: Pierce
content: And this motto is an old saying that predates Nightfall, meaning "Faithful to Memory." It reflects the way my family has always approached history...

speaker: Celine
content: And wouldn't it be ironic if the Pierces turned out to be fabricators of history?
Celine's voice comes from behind. She strides over, cradling an open book which belongs to the collection here. When she stops in front of you both, a cold glint flashes in her eyes.

speaker: Celine
content: Desertification along DisCity's borders is severe, so livestock are a scarce resource. Most books there are made from a local plant fiber renowned for its exceptional strength. You can imagine how difficult it would be to find a notebook bound with leather cord in a satellite town.

speaker: Celine
content: After DisCity's mining districts fell into decline, Syndican literature entered a golden age. Memories of Grace River was never intended as an elegy for the DisCorps. Just because Grace River later became known as the Rust—and rust is associated with metal—doesn't make the book a legacy of the Shattered Blade.
Celine flips through the pages with increasing speed. Pierce grows visibly restless, his eyes darting to you questioningly. You spread your hands and feign innocence.

speaker: Celine
content: Chief, with such unreliable sources, I'm afraid it's impossible to establish a timeline for our cases that are undeniably real.

By now, even a fool can tell that you are not here for a friendly conversation. Pierce's smile has turned rigid. He stops a passing server, rises from his seat, pours himself a glass from the tray, and makes his way toward Celine.

speaker: Pierce
content: I've long heard that the MBCC is home to many talented individuals, but today is the first time I've had the pleasure of meeting one. How long have you worked in the archives, Miss? If you hadn't spotted those flaws, I might never have realized these were forgeries. The Pierce Museum could certainly use someone of your caliber.

speaker: Pierce
content: And of course, I would offer something in return for taking your capable assistant off your hands, Chief. I'm aware that certain parties aren't exactly fond of you or the MBCC, and I happen to have some insight into the forces behind them... I know you prefer to confront your opponents openly, but having a better understanding of them is never a disadvantage.
Celine looks almost amused. She pretends to consider the offer seriously before beginning to haggle with you.

speaker: Celine
content: What do you think, Chief? I never imagined my expertise would lead to so many career opportunities. My current research doesn't require much funding, but... surely the Bureau could use a few more comfortable chairs?

speaker: Chief
content: If all you want are new chairs, there's no need to switch jobs. I can splurge what's left of this year's budget on furnishing the archives.
Nightingale isn't here anyway. No one can stop you from making empty promises.

speaker: Celine
content: Then... what about the offer that gentleman just made? One more friend in the shadows is better than one more enemy in the light, wouldn't you say?

speaker: Chief
content: I'd much prefer friends in the light, though. The shadows make it difficult to tell friend from foe, and the last thing I want is to hurt an ally by mistake.
She picks up her glass, pours the wine into your empty one, then raises her now-empty glass in a toast toward Pierce.

speaker: Celine
content: What a shame, Mr. Pierce. Granted, I do have the patience to sift through your mountain of mostly forged documents to find the few genuine records, but your current offer simply isn't tempting enough to make me give up my comfortable chair at the Bureau.

speaker: Celine
content: My apologies. I'm afraid I can't raise a glass with you today.
A vein throbs on Pierce's forehead. He deliberates for a moment, then seems to make up his mind. Turning away, he retrieves a glass case kept safe behind layers of tempered glass.

speaker: Pierce
content: Given the Chief's generosity toward the Bureau's employees, it's only natural that you would be reluctant to give up your current position, Miss. How about this...

speaker: Pierce
content: These are authentic records from the early Black Ring operations. They contain experimental logs and research data on Mania patients from that era. These documents are priceless materials that have never been revealed to the public.

speaker: Pierce
content: With your expertise, I have no doubt you could craft a research report that would shake the entire academic world. And of course, you would receive full credit for it.
Not only is this the original document behind Morton's incomplete copy, but it also contains previously unpublished materials found nowhere else. This is truly an invaluable discovery.
Then again, neither you nor Celine are ordinary people. Pierce's bribe would certainly have no...

You glance over at Celine, only to find her eyes practically glowing as she stares at the documents in Pierce's hands. She looks exactly like a child who has just spotted a lollipop, practically drooling.

speaker: Chief
content: Ahem!
Your cough brings Celine back to her senses. She tears her gaze away, though not before stealing several longing glances back at the documents.

speaker: Celine
content: Mm... Ahem... That does seem like an irresistible offer. What do you think, Chief?

speaker: Chief
content: I believe Mr. Pierce has proven his sincerity. Perhaps you should just accept it.
The moment Celine takes the glass case, an urgent call comes through. Pierce's expression changes.

speaker: Pierce
content: What... the Public Security Bureau? An inspector... are you sure?
He wheels around to face you both, the fawning look in his eyes gone, replaced by flustered anger.

speaker: Pierce
content: Chief, I know I'm just a nobody compared to someone as important as you, but I came to you in good faith. And this is how you repay me? By sending people to sabotage my exhibition?!
Celine tilts her head ever so slightly, her gaze settling on the hand he's pressing over the box, as though she's spotted something interesting.

speaker: Celine
content: I see... Mr. Pierce, you accuse us of sabotaging your exhibition.

speaker: Celine
content: But you know full well those exhibits downstairs are embarrassingly flawed, and yet you've still chosen to display them. You can see that the face in that painting has been deliberately obscured, and yet you still call it "the symbol of an era."

speaker: Celine
content: Sabotage? Is it even worth the effort? It seems to me your project is already coming apart on its own.
Pierce's expression darkens, but Celine gives him no chance to respond. Her gaze drifts back down to the glass case he's clutching.

speaker: Celine
content: That said, unlike everything downstairs, what you have in your hands is genuine. At least for now, it is still priceless.

speaker: Celine
content: When you took it out just now, I noticed the ink along the edges. Given the temperature and humidity in this room, I'd estimate you have about a year before the ink begins to bleed.

speaker: Celine
content: Wild papyrus has long gone extinct. I know of a company capable of developing a substitute fiber, but... for certain historical reasons, they would never be willing to work with a family that has betrayed the motto "Faithful to Memory."

speaker: Celine
content: Is that why you seemed so desperate? You're in such a hurry to find its next owner before it becomes a worthless stack of paper. That's the real reason you were so eager to receive Chief today.
She has barely finished her sentence when an alarm goes off. You can faintly hear the guests' shocked cries and frantic footsteps downstairs.

speaker: Pierce
content: What do you want exactly?!
Celine does not answer right away. She simply raises her hand, and every sheet of paper in the room seems to tremble simultaneously.

These pages have rested quietly in this elegant collection room, their deterioration slowed to a near standstill by carefully controlled temperature and humidity. Having been spared the devastation of war and the ordeal of concealment under harsh conditions, many of the documents remain in remarkably good condition.
And yet now they tremble in unison, as though straining against their cage in search of a new guardian.

speaker: Celine
content: Many of the manuscripts in your collection were painstakingly crafted by people I knew personally. Your ancestors left them buried in dust for years, and now they are being unearthed only to support a deceptive scheme.

speaker: Celine
content: Whether you like it or not, I will return them to the descendants of their authors. I suppose I should thank your family for leaving you with at least a modicum of dignity.

speaker: Pierce
content: I see... I see. You've been conspiring together, trying to silence the truth about Maris! That is what this is really about. I won't let you get away with this. I swear...
Finally realizing his opponent's true goal, Pierce lets his anger get the better of him and lunges straight at you.
Even without any help from the Sinners, you think you can handle this pampered brat on your own just fine.
Thump!
A dull, numbing pain shoots through your fist. Pierce lets out a sharp cry, clutches his face in agony, and crumples to the floor with a miserable wail.
The sound of their employer taking a beating reaches the security team outside. They storm in and move to pin you both to the ground.
(Gunshots, smoke)

speaker: Nightingale
content: MBCC! Get on the ground and do not resist! You are under arrest!

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, are you alright? My apologies. The Public Security Bureau's operation was compromised, so we were delayed.

speaker: Chief
content: I'm fine. Your timing couldn't have been better. Don't let Pierce get away!

speaker: Chief
content: Where's Celine?!

speaker: Celine
content: Cough, cough... I'm... cough... here.
The smoke clears just enough to reveal Celine, eyes red and face smudged from the tear gas. She's clutching the glass case to her chest. The same one Pierce nearly smashed moments ago.

speaker: Celine
content: Tell everyone to be careful! Cough... Every piece in here is precious. Even the fake ones! Oh no, no, no... No more tear gas. Or at least don't aim it at the collection. It will corrode the items!

Dazzling lights still shine in the villa well into the night, though the guests have long since fled. The grand portrait of Maris Andre still watches over the disordered banquet hall in silence. Her face, deliberately obscured behind a veil of mist by the artist, now seems to carry a trace of mockery.

speaker: Pierce
content: Stop, stop! Do you have any idea who you're dealing with?!

speaker: Pierce
content: I am the head of the Pierce family! Just let me explain... This is all a misunderstanding!

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, we've got the guest list from the reception. The Public Security Bureau's media department will handle the follow-up interrogations. Professor Celine's arm was injured by broken glass. She's been taken to the hospital.

speaker: Chief
content: Good work. What will we do with the documents and antiques found here?

speaker: Nightingale
content: The Public Security Bureau is conducting a thorough investigation. Under a special requisition order from the library, the entire collection in the Pierce estate, including the potential forgeries, will first be transferred to the Central Library in Paradeisos.

speaker: Chief
content: Everything?
As if she's already expecting your surprise, Nightingale gives a small nod of confirmation.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Yes, Chief. Everything.
I can't tell when exactly this started. But no matter how I fall asleep, the lessons from my childhood always appear at the beginning of my dreams...

speaker: Old Professor
content: Today, you will embark on your journey into the study of history. Before we begin, there is one thing I hope you will always remember...

speaker: Old Professor
content: As historians, we must face our own ignorance with honesty, and never let bias or sentiment cloud our judgment. We will always question our findings, always remain objective and independent, and pursue the truth at any cost.
My name is Celine Fabius. I am a Disian. When I was six years old, my family discovered that I possessed an extraordinary memory. I could memorize the contents of any book after just a single glance.
So, at a very young age, I entered my grandfather's private academy, studying alongside people many years my senior, all of us learning what it meant to become true scholars of history.
By modern medical standards, it would be considered a disorder. But for someone like me, someone who had always loved history, it felt less like an affliction and more like a calling.

speaker: Older Student
content: She can memorize anything after reading it just once... She doesn't even know half the words yet... So this is what they call a genius, huh... I'm so jealous... Why would someone like her choose such an unprofitable field of study...

speaker: Mother
content: If this is where your passion lies, then pursue it. It won't be an easy path, but you will become a remarkable historian. We will always be proud of you.
(Flashback to the ceremonial hall or the private school)
My grandfather had many students under his tutelage and nurtured countless accomplished scholars. I can still picture every one of their faces, even now. Well, it is my special gift, after all.
Lucie, Theodore, Davy, Sasham, Qiu Qiu, Morton, Pierce...

History flows like a river, forever rushing onward. In the fleeting span of a single lifetime, to seek the truth of this world is a great endeavor—a journey with no clear destination and no easy way home.

speaker: Lucie
content: I know the history of the farlands that I have compiled does not please the authorities. That is why I can no longer remain in DisCity, or these records will never see the light of day. Goodbye... I am returning to the farlands, and I will find my own way to continue chronicling history!

speaker: Theodore
content: I passed the civil service exam for the Public Security Bureau. Turns out knowing DisCity's local customs inside and out actually comes in handy. Maybe I'll work my way up the ranks someday, who knows. Wish me a happy graduation, genius...

speaker: Davy
content: All our works can be destroyed in an instant. Not only by disasters, but by human hands. If humanity is so willfully blind, why should we continue striving to preserve these records?

The next time Lucie's name appeared, she had already been officially labeled a "terrorist." She often ventured deep into the disaster zones of the farlands in search of firsthand historical records, living among the contamination and Corruptors.

Theodore joined the Department of Communications and married a beautiful woman. After rising through the ranks of society, he advocated for a public data censorship bill, turning against his former colleagues.

As for Davy, he lost both legs during an operation in DisSea, but fortunately survived. In the end, he found his way back to the library, where he worked as a chronicler while quietly searching for the true meaning of history.

One by one, they threw themselves into that great river. Before I knew it, I was the only one left where I had begun. I was an observer who never waded into its waters, merely watching and recording it all.
And so, the names in her memory grow ever more numerous, and ever more vivid.
Those who record their own distorted version of history...

speaker: Morton
content: Biographical research is my specialty. I know of countless people like that... It's what I've dedicated my life to studying! So many people are forgotten simply because their stories aren't exciting enough, or because of their flaws. They're too ordinary to be seen as heroes, so no one wants to talk about them!

speaker: Morton
content: All I needed... was one opportunity to bring Glorie's history to light. People would remember these stories, this town, and those nameless heroes...
Those who scorn history, yet go on to make it...

speaker: Celine
content: He said that as long as people's lives improved, he didn't care if his name was erased from the library's records. He believed the welfare of the living was far more important than lifeless knowledge preserved on paper.

speaker: Celine
content: His reputation was utterly ruined. His name was removed from every work he had authored, and he vanished completely from academia. But the people he had helped never forgot him. He remained in history in another form.
Those who cherish history, yet never hesitate to use it to their advantage...

speaker: Pierce
content: These are authentic records from the early Black Ring operations. They contain experimental logs and research data on Mania patients from that era. These documents are priceless materials that have never been revealed to the public.

speaker: Pierce
content: With your expertise, I have no doubt you could craft a research report that would shake the entire academic world. And of course, you would receive full credit for it.
Those who call themselves observers of history, yet still find themselves swept up in it...
<size=42><color=#7683a2>[Ongoing Request] Reward Offered: N.F. 101 DisCity Prison Inmate Registry | Nirvana Port Surveillance Footage | Authentic Historical Records</size></color>

<color=#7683a2>Thousandhand_marf</color>: Got a chronological surveillance recording from the port depot. Also have a digitized smuggling ledger from August N.F. 101. Certified scans. What's your offer?

<color=#7683a2>Keluge</color>: My grandma left me a stack of letters from her old army buddies. All from before N.F. 100. Will you pay for these? Look, there are tons of them. [Image][Image][Image]

<color=#7683a2>Nailwind</color>: Everything you're looking for is restricted data, you know. My dad works at Nirvana. I can plant a virus on his device and sneak it all out for you.

<color=#fb9259>codename_ce</color>: I don't accept tampered footage or recompressed files. Scanned copies are worth less too. DM me.

<color=#7683a2>Mamaguagua</color>: Found the registry you want. The person you're looking for did enter the prison during N.F. 101 and got exiled in N.F. 102. The prison was demolished by the end of that year.

<color=#fb9259>codename_ce</color>: Did they leave behind any notebooks or diaries?

<color=#7683a2>Mamaguagua</color>: No chance. Even if they did, anything like that would've been destroyed the moment it was discovered. But I dug deeper, and the chronicler in charge of the prison records at the time was Harden Pierce. He died of a heart attack two years ago. His grandson inherited everything.

<color=#7683a2>Mamaguagua</color>: Total trust fund brat. Squanders his father's money throwing banquets and parties, trying to buy his way into Eastside's upper circles. Nobody's really interested, though. The Pierce family never had the kind of old-money pedigree that crowd actually cares about.

<color=#fb9259>codename_ce</color>: Thank you. Your information has been valuable. Payment will be transferred to your account within 8 hours.

<color=#fb9259>codename_ce</color>: Have a nice day.

The dark web is a remarkably useful tool. It offers access to all kinds of information unobtainable through legitimate channels. It is almost ironic that the most unfiltered truths reside in the darkest corners of the internet.
Celine's gaze drifts slowly down the screen, the scattered threads of the story weaving together in her mind.
[The Truth Behind the Battle of the Rust][Maris Andre Memorial Hall Opens Soon: Rare Historical Documents on Display for the First Time!][Could Maris Andre's True Family Name Be Pierce?]

The scheme is so shallow and flimsy that it's almost laughable. Its influence is far too limited to draw in enough important figures. In that case, why not add a little fuel to the fire and turn it into a major scandal?
In the climate-controlled vault, Chief and Pierce exchange pleasantries in the background as she drifts closer to the carefully preserved collection.
Behind the familiar strokes and sharp writing on the page, their faces emerge from the depths of an unforgettable sea of memories.
Humanity continues to repeat the same history, making the same mistakes again and again. Civilization is a glorious yet fragile thing, one that can collapse in an instant.
If destruction is inevitable, then what is the point of continuing to record all this?
And yet...
We ask you that remember us.

speaker: Celine
content: I will, my dear friends. I'm here to bring you home.

A few days later, the forgery case surrounding Maris Andre is finally exposed. The Public Security Bureau launches a crackdown on several illegal media outlets, and the investigation even uncovers leads pointing to Outland spies and an intelligence smuggling operation. The 9th Agency is currently celebrating their good fortune, reaping the rewards without lifting a finger.
It is around this time that you hear of Celine's discharge from the hospital and receive an enormous parcel from the Central Library.
"Thank you for your assistance during this operation, Chief. Enclosed is the highest-level access I can grant. The doors of the Central Library are always open to you."

This is your first visit to the Central Library. Nestled within a secluded garden with United University behind it, it stands across from the Ring Research Institute, yet the two are worlds apart in terms of size and public attention.

You take the elevator to the heart of the library. Shelves rise all the way to the ceiling, arranged in chronological order and stretching on like an endless scroll. Hovering rails connect them, while dim light falls across the uneven spines, revealing gaps where volumes once stood.

speaker: Chief
content: The modernization of the DisCity Army... Escalating political and military tensions... Border budget in crisis... Refugee influx from WhiteSands doubles in the same year...

speaker: Chief
content: Nirvana's unmanned mining project... Bid evaluation records... EDGE external summit minutes...

These sensitive documents sit openly on the shelves like bestsellers. Yet you feel like a parched man cast into the ocean, or a blind man standing beneath the blazing sun. As a layperson, you simply cannot find what you seek in this vast sea of information.

speaker: Chief
content: Even with access, I can't make sense of the system. If I want to borrow anything, I'll still need her help... How cunning.
The deeper you go, the more towering the shelves become. Rounding a corner, you spot a familiar figure.

She is perched on a lift chair, sorting through some documents, hovering around the N.F. 115 section. From a distance, she looks like a pink bookmark about to be swallowed by the vast sea of files. Only when she spots you does she slowly drift back down.

speaker: Celine
content: Welcome to the library, Chief ${PlayerName}. You must have received my gift.

speaker: Chief
content: Yes, nearly two hundred books, including the A Brief History of DisCity series, bestsellers, popular novels, science primers... Our little library's collection has grown by more than half. The kids all love them.

speaker: Chief
content: And this is my first time venturing this deep into the Central Library and seeing the archives for myself. It's truly impressive. Though I can't help but wonder what methods were used to gather all of this.
You study her face, still as gentle as ever, and begin laying out the information you have obtained over the past few days.

speaker: Chief
content: We were only investigating the forgery case concerning Maris Andre at first, which was supposed to be nothing more than a minor public order violation. Yet we ended up drawing out the Pierce family and even Outland spies.

speaker: Chief
content: The 9th Agency walked away with a huge prize, and every other department got something out of it as well. But if you ask me who came out on top, it was the Central Library. You ended up acquiring a substantial portion of the Pierce family's collection for free.

speaker: Celine
content: Quite a few talented individuals from the Pierce family have served this library. As Head Librarian of the Central Library, I will never forget the considerable contributions made by these collectors.

speaker: Chief
content: Never forget their contributions, huh... That's a lovely way to put it.

speaker: Chief
content: The Maris Andre forgery case is a scandal to the public, a lead for the Public Security Bureau, and a windfall for the 9th Agency. But to you, it is the perfect pretext.

speaker: Chief
content: With that pretext in hand, you could apply for a special warrant and have the entire Pierce estate collection seized, including any potential forgeries. The Public Security Bureau is busy with its investigation, the media is having a field day on the front pages, and here you are, sitting quietly in the library, waiting for everything you've been searching for to be delivered straight to your door.

speaker: Chief
content: Did you have fun setting up the trap, Professor Celine?
Celine's smile fades, but her gaze remains gentle. Perhaps it is just your imagination, but she seems to be reading something in you, tracing every detail with her eyes, committing it all to memory.

speaker: Celine
content: They all say the MBCC's Chief is exceptionally intelligent. I suspect there is more to your reasoning. Can I hear the rest?

speaker: Chief
content: That's all I have. The rest is just speculation.

speaker: Chief
content: You were looking for the manuscripts the Pierce family had kept hidden, while my attention was drawn to the shady dealings behind the wave of "debunking" stories. And how fortunate we were to have the renowned Head Librarian volunteer as an expert advisor. Now that it's all over, I suppose I owe the library a favor.

speaker: Chief
content: As for whether you've had any covert dealings with the 9th Agency, my guess is... not yet. But the windfall you brought them could very well lead to a new connection. Am I right?
You pause for a moment.

speaker: Chief
content: There's another thing... You've mentioned the lack of funding and dwindling visitors a few times, but the Central Library is, in fact, an important facility under Paradeisos. Surely you have students, colleagues, and other connections you could rely on as well. Why did you decide to handle the Maris Andre case personally?

speaker: Chief
content: What's hidden in those manuscripts from the Pierce collection that made you so eager to obtain them? And why did it have to be <color=#fb9259>you</color> who acquired them?

speaker: Celine
content: Smart, honorable, highly perceptive... I just wonder whether a mind like that can remain unchanged...

speaker: Celine
content: ...Fine. I owe you an apology. Please forgive me for approaching you the way I did. I tried to make it up to you by granting you a rather high level of access.
She holds her faint smile and extends a hand in invitation.

speaker: Celine
content: It's your first time here, Chief. Let me show you around while I offer you my explanation.
You step onto the hovering device and let it carry you to the shelves. You watch as she pulls out a red-covered book and opens it.

speaker: Celine
content: This is the Nightfall Chronicle, a detailed account of the upheaval that swept through human society in the early years after Nightfall. It documents everything from daily life to the collective mindset of society at the time. It is an extraordinarily valuable historical record. Its author, Barney, lived through the N.F. 20s. He was already in his sixties when the Perishing Star fell, yet he still traveled across multiple cities, leaving behind millions of words of documentation.

speaker: Celine
content: Transportation was largely paralyzed back then, and contamination was spreading across the land. But the hardships never slowed him down—not until Mania claimed him and his wife in their sleep, turning them into Corruptors. After his death, much of his work was destroyed as hazardous material. Barely 10% of his records have been salvaged.

speaker: Celine
content: To recover this remaining fragment, Lucie dug through five graveyards. She was exposed to too much contamination in the process, and passed away not long after.
You've seen this document in Morton's photocopy. But this is the first time you've heard of Lucie, the name of the chronicler.
The book retriever drifts slowly along the shelves. Further ahead, Celine draws out another book, this one with a black cover.

speaker: Celine
content: After the N.F. 30s, DisCity developed rapidly under the colonization of the metropoles and entered a golden age. This journal meticulously documents the daily lives of Syndican miners.

speaker: Celine
content: But it wasn't recovered until the late N.F. 90s. Filled with verifiable facts and supported by documented accounts of Nirvana's exploitation of its workers, it circulated widely through Syndicate for a time, only to be swiftly branded a "collection of lies," banned, and destroyed.

speaker: Celine
content: Theodore spent five months digging through government databases before finally identifying his name. He was called Ramboll Wade, a cobbler who was so insignificant, yet so influential.
She pauses for a moment, clutching the book to her chest. The book retriever carries you both onward to the next shelf.

speaker: Celine
content: This one was compiled by Davy Buerz and contains records about the Pioneer unit of the Ring Research Institute. From the N.F. 80s onward, the abilities of Sinners gradually became known to the public, and among some of them, a brief yet fervent worship of Mania, and even the Black Ring, took hold.

speaker: Celine
content: The Pioneer unit ventured into the unstable parameters of the contamination zones, carrying an early model of the Hypercube shield, and documented the changes in various Black Ring indicators.

speaker: Celine
content: According to their records, the changes in the Black Ring indicators formed distinct patterns that they could only describe as "moods," ones that even seemed to respond to human behavior. The discovery sent them into a frenzy. They classified it as a biological phenomenon rather than a purely physical one.

speaker: Celine
content: We now know that Black Rings are not independent living beings. Much of the knowledge surrounding Black Rings has since become classified information. As for this book, which contained outdated methods, incorrect conclusions, and views contrary to accepted doctrine, it was banned shortly after its publication.

speaker: Chief
content: And the people involved...

speaker: Celine
content: Most of them have passed away. Only Mr. Oliver is still alive, spending his remaining years as a long-term patient at Banyan Medical College. Alzheimer's has taken away most of his memories.

speaker: Celine
content: The Ring Research Institute funded multiple editions, and after countless revisions, we were able to preserve a redacted version for internal use. We send Mr. Oliver the latest revision each time. What you're holding is the first edition, the one that was scheduled for recall and destruction.

She stands before the towering shelves and speaks of every book like an old friend, introducing you to each chronicler who brought these documents back. As she speaks, the unfamiliar names take shape, until they feel like people standing right in front of you.

The shelves stretch endlessly upward, with light and shadow shifting across them. The figures of these people emerge and fade among the rows of books, like leaves drifting along the great river of history.
Finally, she brings you to a pile of uncatalogued documents, and gestures toward the files just transferred from the Pierce estate.

speaker: Celine
content: These were all recovered from the Pierce family collection. Generations ago, their ancestors were collaborators of the library who handled a considerable number of documents.

speaker: Celine
content: Documents deemed "incorrect," "dangerous," and marked for destruction.
Every era pursues its own version of the "truth." Harden Pierce understood this and did all he could to preserve the truths that could never be spoken aloud.

speaker: Celine
content: That was why they preserved some of these truths and kept them hidden until now. They were all meticulous. They knew exactly what it would mean if any of it ever came to light. But the generation that inherited them used them to produce blatant forgeries for profit.

speaker: Chief
content: The humanities have been in decline for a long time now. Priceless collections lose their value the moment they're moved into the library.
A wry smile crosses her face. She lowers her eyes.

speaker: Celine
content: The Pierce family itself has a rich history, yet its current head hasn't a shred of historical sensibility. Better it all pass into my hands than be squandered by someone like him.

speaker: Celine
content: I dislike conflict, but I refuse to watch my colleagues' life's work gather dust.

speaker: Chief
content: So you decided to take over the collection. Because you knew that if it remained in the hands of that wastrel, not only would the distorted history twist people's understanding of the past, but the sensitive documents his family had fought so hard to preserve would also be exposed, scrutinized, or even destroyed.

speaker: Chief
content: You want to protect these documents, but every manuscript and dataset here has a traceable code...
Unconsciously, your voice drops to a near whisper.

speaker: Chief
content: Is that why you came to me? Can I help?
She smiles, then extends her hand toward you.
A pulse of Mania spreads from her palm, and with it, the shackles take hold.

speaker: Celine
content: Chief, I didn't come this far alone. I have many friends, mentors, and students. Most of them have been far less fortunate than I am, yet they continue to walk this path all the same.

speaker: Celine
content: I was blessed with the gift of memory. The least I can do is put it to meaningful use.

She raises her hand like a seer performing a ritual, and the sheets of paper in the room all rise and swirl in orderly streams, sweeping past her eyes one by one. A hurricane suddenly erupts in this space where time has long stood still.

The pages let out a soft shriek as ink flows into them. Words and materials from different eras sweep past your eyes. History rearranges itself in a nonlinear order. Words are connected by nothing but logic.
Prayers whispered beneath the eclipsed moon, a land deed from the metropoles, a list of the deceased in WhiteSands, a secret military order from a forgotten era...
Every symbol breaks free from its cage, flowing joyfully into the river of history she commands, dissolving in it.

speaker: Celine
content: They can destroy written records or grind stone carvings to dust, but they will never take what is etched in my mind.

speaker: Celine
content: Text can be lost or altered. But everything I have committed to memory has remained perfectly preserved.
Mania stirs your emotions through the shackles. You recall what she said in Pierce's study, that many of those manuscripts were painstakingly crafted by people she knew.
That is why she wants them. They are not merely a stack of records. They are proof that those people once lived.

speaker: Chief
content: ...Would that do?
She smiles and nods.

speaker: Celine
content: Thanks to your help, the library was able to recover so much invaluable data. <color=#fb9259>On my own</color>, I doubt I could have ever uncovered the conspiracy behind it all.

speaker: Chief
content: Save the flattery, Professor Celine. I'm already well aware that we're caught in the same web.

speaker: Chief
content: Next time you need help, just ask. No need to go through all that. I don't appreciate being manipulated... but I also can't leave you to do this alone.

speaker: Chief
content: Besides, you can tell me more about them, too. Not just what is written in the books, but who they actually were. I'd like to hear about that.
She chuckles and walks over to the documents about to be destroyed, running her fingers gently over them as though saying goodbye to some old friends.

speaker: Celine
content: You know, sometimes I find myself wondering... Chief, what if one day, for some reason, I lost my memories?
Her tone remains as gentle and casual as ever, but her smile doesn't reach her eyes.
You take a deep breath.

options: That happens to be my specialty.
We'll go and find them back.

speaker: Chief
content: As it happens, I lost my memories by accident as well. If that day ever comes, at least you'll have someone who understands what you're going through.

speaker: Chief
content: I'm no chronicler or scholar, so I can't help you preserve documents. But I am a Mania specialist, and your ability is fundamentally tied to Mania. As long as the shackles remain intact, I'll do everything in my power to preserve it.

speaker: Chief
content: If that day ever comes, we'll do what the chroniclers do. Piece the fragments of history back together.
I have encountered so many people in the river of history.

<color=#e5b2cc><i>Those who record their own distorted version of history...
Those who scorn history, yet go on to make it...<i></color>
Those who cherish history, yet never hesitate to use it to their advantage... Those who call themselves observers of history, yet still find themselves swept up in it...
And those who remember history... and continue to move forward...

speaker: Celine
content: ...Heh. Then... it's a promise.

speaker: Chelsea
content: I'm so bored... I want alcohol. Hey, the lad over there, yes, you! Get me a bottle of wine, bro, the best one you can get!

speaker: Chelsea
content: I'll pay you fair. As much tip as you want.
Before you even walk into the interrogation room, you hear the person yelling at the top of her voice from inside.

speaker: Chelsea
content: I normally pay by carats, or... you want to be paid by pounds? Well, whatever. It's not that much money anyway.
Chelsea reclines in the chair for the interrogatee, looking bored stiff without the slightest hint of nervousness, as if she isn't under arrest but here on vacation.
As soon as you enter, the staff hurries away with a quick bow to you, as if you're their lifesaver, while Chelsea waves and greets you warmly.

speaker: Chelsea
content: Hey! Isn't this the Chief?! Welcome! Welcome!

speaker: Chelsea
content: Would you be interested in sharing a glass of N.F.82 Campbell's with me?
Alcohol is strictly prohibited in the interrogation room.

speaker: Chelsea
content: Well, what a dull life it must be here then.

speaker: Chelsea
content: Chief, listen. I'll pay ten, no, twenty times the price! Just for one sip of wine from you. How does that sound?

speaker: Chelsea
content: If you're willing to feed me the sip of tea yourself, I'll pay a hundred times the price!
Forget it. It'll never happen.

speaker: Chelsea
content: Well, how about both of us take a step back. You'll be my sugar baby, and when I get back to my mansion, you'll have a whole cellar of choice wine to choose from.
Chelsea keeps mentioning her offer to be your "sugar mama" ever since she arrived at the MBCC.
You've already gone from being slightly irritated at first to being able to turn her down with a straight face.
And you can't go back to the Countess' Court until the investigation is over.

speaker: Chelsea
content: Aww... What a ruthless Chief—

speaker: Chelsea
content: But exactly the way I like about you! Heh heh—
Chelsea instinctively reaches out toward you, yet with her hands restrained, she can't go any further.
The sight of her hands and your poker face finally prompt Chelsea to sit up straight. Seems like she finally realizes this interrogation isn't a joke.
test
test
test
test
test
test
You place a thick pile of files in front of her, all filled with accusations against Countess Chelsea.

speaker: Victim 1
content: "She offered to be my sugar mama, and I... I refused. But she bought the company I work for, replaced everyone with staff she hired, and took all my work. Whatever I say, they would only ever reply—Please be the Countess' sugar baby."

speaker: Victim 2
content: "She wants me to be her sugar baby, and I said yes. But then I scratched my arm one time, and she told me she bought me a new arm and could install it anytime. Who in their right mind would do such a thing?!"

speaker: Victim 3
content: "Wh-What am I to her? It's not me that she likes!"
Several victims accused you of harassment, imprisonment, and causing great physical and psychological trauma. What do you have to say for yourself?

speaker: Chelsea
content: Th-That's not harassment!

speaker: Chelsea
content: I like them, so I wanted to be their sugar mama and wanted them to be happy. That's all.

speaker: Chelsea
content: And some of them said yes! How can that be imprisonment—? I mean, I don't understand why anyone would give up such a happy life for something else out there—it's so dangerous out there!
Chelsea furrows her brows, looking very frustrated, not feeling guilty at all about what she's been doing.
You're speechless. She doesn't seem to get that her so-called "happy life" is just drowning someone with money with no regard for what they think.

speaker: Chelsea
content: All I want is to be nice to them, but they keep cursing me and rejecting me. Hmm. Yeah, guess I wasn't doing enough of it.
Why would they accuse you?

speaker: Chelsea
content: How should I know...

speaker: Chelsea
content: Well then... How about you try being my sugar baby, Chief?

speaker: Chelsea
content: You won't know until you try, right?
Chelsea looks excited while the cuffs on her hands clank as she moves.

speaker: Chelsea
content: Chief, I have a question for you.

speaker: Chelsea
content: What gem color do you like, Chief?
You pause at hearing this question completely irrelevant to the interrogation, failing to keep up with her jumpy train of thoughts.

options: This has nothing to do with the interrogation.

speaker: Chelsea
content: Come on! These cuffs are just too plain. They'll definitely look better with gems on!
She looks as if she's pondering some serious questions, staring at the cuffs, but it turns out she's thinking about adding gems to them...

speaker: Chelsea
content: Look, Chief! I've got a lot of gems! How about I give them all to you to put on your cuffs?

speaker: Chelsea
content: Aww! Chief's so cold...

speaker: Chelsea
content: But I like it.

speaker: Chelsea
content: So... to show you my affection, how about I give you a few gems to put on the cuffs?

speaker: Chelsea
content: Then you won't have to use cuffs that look so boring for all the other Sinners!
As Chelsea speaks, a string of sparkles shines in her hand. After the glow fades, several gems of various colors and excellent quality appear on her palm.

options: Please don't use your ability in the room.

content: Or I'll use the shackles when necessary.

speaker: Chelsea
content: Come on! I just want you to have a better life. These gems are worth a lot of money. With them, you won't have to live in this crappy, tiny place anymore!
The Bureau is certainly no match for the Countess' Court, but I have no reason to leave here.
Hearing your rejection, not only does she not get upset, but she even smiles and leans forward.

speaker: Chelsea
content: Come on! Don't be so cold. Look, I can even let you and everyone else move into my mansion, with all the gourmet free to enjoy. Much better than this crappy place the Bureau has.
Sinners are not allowed to leave the Bureau without permission from the supervisors. Please be cooperative with our investigation.

speaker: Chelsea
content: Oh, are you worried that your bosses won't be happy about it? No worries, I know what to do. I'm really good at this...
You take a deep breath and fixate your gaze on her. Seeing that you're slightly agitated, Chelsea shrugs.

speaker: Chelsea
content: Let me just say one more thing...

speaker: Chelsea
content: I adore you with the utmost sincerity, Chief. If you're willing to be my sugar baby, I'll treat you especially well.

speaker: Chelsea
content: I'll love you as much as I love Sitri. I won't let you suffer a tiny bit. I'll buy anything you want!
She talks about getting a sugar baby as if she's just buying a toy.

speaker: Chelsea
content: Sitri... Sitri... Oh, Sitri is my favorite cat—I have a huge bunch of cats in my backyard... They're all su-per cu-uute!

speaker: Chelsea
content: So? Are you tempted yet?
Thanks, but I'm more interested in finding out the truth behind the cases.
Chelsea bursts out laughing and tilts her head toward you to gaze at you, looking even more intrigued.

speaker: Chelsea
content: Cases. Those can hardly be called cases, right, Chief?
Well, why don't you take a look at this, Countess Chelsea?
