Serpent Eye wants to requisition you to protect the current Deputy Speaker of the City Council.
The Deputy Speaker plans to give speeches in Eastside soon. Just recently, he's received a death threat.
Despite having left her position for years, as an elite in the industry, Cinnabar's instinct kicks in quickly.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: Does the intelligence have any clues yet?
No. The guy sends threatening letters to Reagan's personal terminal every day, using virtual IPs. The intelligence hasn't been able to trace any useful information.
After thinking for a moment, Cinnabar promptly gives her professional advice.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: The person sending the threats is good with technology, shortwave communication equipment and an EMP device will be necessary. Hmm... We must also beware of remote bombs...
Looks like you're all ready.
Cinnabar lifts her head and looks dazed for a moment.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: ...I'm a Sinner. I work for you, I shouldn't go outside for personal matters.

Since the assassination of a councilor by a Maniac eight years ago, MBCC has been obliged to provide security support for any events involving officials. Of course, only when the organizer requires it. It won't be a personal matter if we send you.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: Serpent Eye is capable of protecting Reagan. I shouldn't be needed.
Cinnabar seems hesitant, perhaps not yet prepared to meet her old teammates.
My initial response to Alyosha was this: "Are you sure she can pull off such an important mission? Don't forget she's a Sinner who requires constant supervision."
But Alyosha said, "Cinnabar is different from the other Sinners!"
And these résumés on the desk—who do you think sent them?
Give your colleagues the trust they deserve. They very likely fought for this mission, for you.
Maybe they've long forgiven you. It's just that you haven't forgiven yourself.
After a brief moment of silence, Cinnabar's eyes are filled with determination.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: If this is truly what Alyosha and the others wish for... then I shouldn't let them down again.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: I accept this mission.
Then it's all set. By the way, out of MBCC's supervisory duty, I must accompany you throughout. After all...

speaker: Cinnabar
content: I understand.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: Rest assured, I will obey the rules.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: Rest assured, I will remain in your sight.

speaker: Female Stranger
content: Hello! If you don't mind, may I have your contact please?

speaker: Cinnabar
content: I... Ugh...
As you come backstage, you happen to see a female staff leaning close to Cinnabar.
Bewildered, Cinnabar shoots a helpless look at you.
Excuse me, I have an important task to discuss with her. Can I borrow her for a minute?

speaker: Female Stranger
content: Her?!
The staff leaves in shock. Cinnabar lets out a sigh of relief at last.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: Thank you.
Don't mention it. The speech will begin in 20 minutes, are you ready?

speaker: Cinnabar
content: Serpent Eye is still doing the last round of security checks. They'll then take over from me here, and I'll be in charge of on-site staff deployment...
She's barely finished her sentence as you hear footsteps in the corridor. A man in his fifties is striding toward you.
Broad and strong, the man is more than a head taller than you and wears several terrifying scars on his face that will scare off most people. As he approaches, Cinnabar immediately stands up.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: Captain, is everything okay on-site?
From Cinnabar's slightly nervous tone, you learn his identity—the man before you is Alyosha.

speaker: Alyosha
content: Security check on the 172 audience members is complete. The EMP device has been set up on site as well.

speaker: Alyosha
content: Besides, there are five of Reagan's VIPs. Serpent Eye is not responsible for their security check.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: Can they at least... Never mind.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: I'll keep an eye on them.
Cinnabar says no more and simply lets out a sigh. It's not their place to question anything with political motives behind it.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: Captain...

speaker: Alyosha
content: Yes?
Alyosha interrupts Cinnabar's question with a frown, as if unwilling to utter even one word irrelevant to the mission. Cinnabar bows her head like a child who's done something wrong.
I believe in your ability, Cinnabar. You seem all tensed up, try to relax a bit.
Alyosha turns to look at you. His gaze is piercing, like a big cat zeroing in on its prey.
Also sensing his hostility toward you, Cinnabar steps forward to put herself before you.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: Captain, the Chief is here to assist us.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: Captain, please don't... treat my friend like that.
Alyosha narrows his eyes and glances at Cinnabar, then at you. A few seconds later, he turns and walks away wordlessly.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: I'm sorry, Alyosha... is not very sociable.
Don't be sorry, I can see that he's very responsible. You can never be too careful, right?
Reassured by your understanding, Cinnabar smiles. She glances up at the clock, then turns around to knock on the door of Reagan's lounge.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: Mr. Reagan, it's about time...
Before Cinnabar finishes, the lounge's door is opened.
Crowded by bodyguards in black suits, a well-dressed man walks straight in the direction of the stage without even sparing you two a single look.
Cinnabar signals you to follow Reagan to the venue with her.
Cinnabar grips your hand, and you two follow Reagan to the venue.
You take the first seat on the left side of the front row. As the security manager, Cinnabar stands beside you.
On the stage, Reagan begins his speech.

options: Sit down and listen to the speech

content: It is apparent that Reagan is an excellent public speaker. His logic is clear, his emotions compelling and his speech convincing.
For the better part of an hour, he presents the plight faced by certain blocks in Syndicate, and the efforts he has made in order to solve the problem.
Toward the end of his speech, Reagan begins to give his thanks to those who support his project.

speaker: Reagan
content: ...These benevolent gentlemen have endorsed my Home Reconstruction Project and built a new community for the Syndicans that have lost their homes.

speaker: Reagan
content: They have won respect from all Syndicans, as well as admiration from me.

speaker: Reagan
content: Now, let us welcome them onto the stage, and allow me to have the honor to personally award them with the Medals of Benevolence issued by the City Council!
Greeted by passionate music and loud applause from the audience, several well-known Eastside real estate tycoons—the VIPs Alyosha has mentioned—stroll onto the stage from the VIP lounge.
Do you know these people?
Prior to being taken in by MBCC, Cinnabar lived in Syndicate. If the truth is really as Reagan said, Cinnabar is likely to know these people.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: I don't know them.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: Also... I've never heard of any Home Reconstruction Project. But I've heard that a recently constructed residential block has collapsed due to its weak foundation, and many have died in the accident... Hold on, something seems wrong with him!
You follow Cinnabar's finger and look toward the stage, one of the developers' faces is ashen, his lips are trembling, and he's striding toward Reagan.
Clack!
Before Cinnabar even has time to rush forward, the developer pulls out a pair of handcuffs from his clothes and cuffs himself and Reagan together.

speaker: Developer
content: I'm so sorry, Mr. Reagan... Please don't move, I beg you, please do not move, or we'll both die! That guy's installed a bomb on me...
After a brief confused moment, screams explode across the entire venue. An immense panic descends on the audience within seconds.

People are screaming and jostling against each other. You hear a child's cry from behind, but the moment you turn around, you are pushed onto the floor by the mass of people scrambling toward the emergency exit.
You try your best to get back up, but a pair of stomping feet on your back prevents that. Right at that moment, you feel a hand grab your forearm firmly.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: Hold onto me, don't let go!
Hearing Cinnabar's voice, you react immediately and clutch onto her arm, helping yourself to your feet.
The two of you wade through the flow of people and soon reach the base of the stage. You hear loud, raucous noise coming from the stage.
You try your best to get back up, but a pair of stomping feet on your back prevents that, and the following flow of people seems to have no end.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: Hey!
Against the icy blue screen, Cinnabar shields you from the crowd, facing you with her back. Turning to you slightly, she reaches out an arm.
You react immediately and clutch onto her hand, helping yourself to your feet.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: ...Are you hurt?
I'm fine. You need to stop what's happening on the stage!

speaker: Cinnabar
content: Don't worry, I'll handle it. You should get out of here first.
Cinnabar wraps her left arm tightly around most of your body, pushing the shield forward with her right arm to divide the crowd.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: Hold onto me, don't let go!
The two of you wade through the flow of people. You've lost track of time, until you finally hear loud, raucous noise coming from the stage.

speaker: Synthesized Voice
content: ...Reagan, you have only one choice: allocate funds at once to compensate all the families of the victims who died in the collapse of the buildings in Pasture Block.

speaker: Synthesized Voice
content: Take this as your final chance of atonement, or I'll blow you and this vermin up.
A synthetic voice comes out of the speaker attached to the developer's collar. He unbuttons his suit jacket to reveal the communication device beneath and the bomb around his waist.

speaker: Developer
content: I... I can give back the money I've taken, please don't kill me, I have kids...
Reagan stares at the developer coldly and remains silent.

speaker: Synthesized Voice
content: You have two minutes to decide.
Reagan still hasn't spoken.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: There is a fifteen-minute delay on the live TV broadcast, and everyone in the control room works for Serpent Eye... The attacker must be on site now.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: The attacker needs to observe everything on the stage at all times. The back rows near the exit are crowded with people, you can't see the stage clearly from there...
As Cinnabar reaches the end of her analysis, you meet each other's gaze, then each begins immediately to scan one half of the venue with unspoken coordination.
Soon, a trembling figure squatting under a desk captures your attention. The scrawny body is shaking violently, as if immobilized by fear. But in fact, he keeps peeking up at the stage all the while.
Your eyes meet. He quickly looks away even as you see a chilling light flash over his gaze.
The fourth seat in the sixth row, under the seat!

speaker: Synthesized Voice
content: Time's up. Repay the dead with your lives!

speaker: Cinnabar
content: Launch the EMP!

Through the shortwave communication equipment, the Serpent Eye team receives the order. They immediately launch the EMP device. The strong EMP shock causes all electronic equipment to fail at once. Darkness falls upon the venue.

The next moment, Cinnabar leaps past the crowd, takes hold of the arms of the attacker who's about to escape, and subdues him on the floor. The detonator falls out of his hand and is stamped over by the crowd, turning into scrap metal.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: Target captured!
Half a minute later, you hear the sound of the uninterruptible power supply turning on, and the venue is lit up again.
You quickly make your way to Cinnabar, and find that the person being pressed on the floor has a rather youthful face—the attacker is a teenager.
Well done, Cinnabar!
Several Serpent Eye members come over to pass some nylon ties to Cinnabar, with which she efficiently ties the attacker up.
Once her hands are free, Cinnabar's first reaction is to search for something in the busy crowd. When she sees that you're safe, she finally breathes a sigh of relief.
On the stage, Alyosha breaks the handcuffs with a pair of hydraulic tongs. Reagan rubs his reddened wrist with an undecipherable expression, then suddenly pulls out the gun from Alyosha's holster.
Bang! Bang!
As the gunshot dies down, the developer is found lying on the floor. His body twitches a few times, then goes completely still.
Reagan, having just killed a person, draws in a deep breath, lets it out slowly, and gives a perfect high society smile as he turns to Alyosha.

speaker: Reagan
content: Care to explain?

speaker: Alyosha
content: I'm really sorry.
Alyosha's face is ashy, but Reagan simply pats him lightly on the shoulder.

speaker: Reagan
content: I don't need someone who apologizes all the time.

speaker: Reagan
content: I prefer doers who deliver solid work.
He shoves the handgun back into Alyosha's hand, glances down once at the attacker on the floor, then makes for the emergency exit, escorted by two bodyguards.

speaker: Attacker
content: You son of a bitch, come back, I'm going to kill you! Even if we die, all of us Syndicans will come back to haunt you!
On the floor, the attacker is cursing while straining to lift his head. Reagan halts his steps and turns around, but not to respond to him.

speaker: Reagan
content: By the way, Cinnabar.
Reagan is smiling. For some reason, the smile feels very unpleasant.

speaker: Reagan
content: Who'd have thought, after two years of rolling in the dirt in Syndicate, even after you turned into a Sinner, you're still impressively good...

speaker: Reagan
content: Eastside is hungry for talents... Who knows? Even a filthy street rat like you might be useful somewhere.
Having said that, Reagan leaves without turning back again.
Within a few minutes, the audiences have all been evacuated under Serpent Eye's instructions. Those who remain are shrouded by an unsettling silence, only the attacker is still cursing hysterically.
Alyosha doesn't say a word as he comes slowly in your direction. He hasn't replaced his gun in his holster. The heavy footsteps make your chest feel tight.

speaker: Attacker
content: Go to hell, you spineless bastards!
The attacker is wriggling frantically on the floor. Alyosha stops in front of him.

speaker: Alyosha
content: Cinnabar, hold him down.
Everyone present understands Alyosha's purpose, but no one objects, except Cinnabar.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: Captain...
Bang!
Alyosha doesn't let Cinnabar finish and simply pulls the trigger. But as the gunshot rings in the air, the attacker is still alive. Terrified, he has shut his eyes. The bullet drops before his face.
Blue light is floating around the attacker. Cinnabar has expanded the shield and protected him.

speaker: Alyosha
content: CIN—NA—BAR!
The muscles on Alyosha's face are twitching.

speaker: Alyosha
content: This is the client's order... Hand him over to me.
Cinnabar passes her eyes over the young attacker on the floor, grits her teeth, and lifts her head to face Alyosha.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: I can't do that.
The shield still separates the two of them.

speaker: Alyosha
content: Do you have any idea how much it's cost Serpent Eye to make this happen?!
Alyosha takes a deep breath and suppresses the anger that threatens to explode any second.

speaker: Alyosha
content: Whatever happened in the past, I can overlook it. Now, get out of my way, don't make me say it a third time.
The surrounding Serpent Eye teammates are all staring at Cinnabar, but no one says anything.
If you don't help Cinnabar, no one will.
You don't have the right to kill him, Alyosha.
Alyosha doesn't budge, doesn't so much as look at you once. His gaze remains on Cinnabar still.
The attacker no longer poses any threat. According to the law, he must be trialed in court. Lynching is...

speaker: Alyosha
content: Shut up!
Alyosha growls at you. He looks furious, like a raging lion.

speaker: Alyosha
content: You're just an outsider, you have no business meddling in Serpent Eye's affairs!

speaker: Cinnabar
content: He is not an outsider.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: She is... not an outsider!
Alyosha is suddenly wide-eyed. For a moment, shock overpowers anger.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: The Chief has always been by my side... The Chief is my friend.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: She has been helping me and taking care of me... She is my... Friend! She's important to me!

speaker: Alyosha
content: So... you mean to say you're willing to betray Serpent Eye again for this friend?!

speaker: Cinnabar
content: I don't want to betray Serpent Eye, Alyosha, I've never once thought of that...

speaker: Cinnabar
content: Loyalty, courage, and determination... These are what Dad, José... and you have taught me. I've never forgotten them.
Cinnabar's chest is heaving intensely.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: But have you ever considered that, besides these, there are other more important and righteous things in the world?

speaker: Cinnabar
content: What's more important than a client's order is morality, justice, and the lives of innocent people...

speaker: Alyosha
content: For these obscure ideas, are you going to give up your career and Serpent Eye, stay in that shitty place, and work a job with no future, till the day you... die?

speaker: Cinnabar
content: I'm really sorry for what happened two years ago... but I do not regret it.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: To strive for these so-called obscure ideas, I'm willing to...

speaker: Alyosha
content: Enough.
Alyosha interrupts Cinnabar. He stands still before her, the anger has vanished from his eyes, leaving behind only weariness on his face.
After a long silence, he moves the handgun away.

speaker: Alyosha
content: Suit yourself.
Ignoring the sadness in Cinnabar's eyes, Alyosha turns around and heads toward the exit. The heavy footsteps echo in the empty hall like distant thunder.
If you let him go like this, Cinnabar will probably never get to meet him again.
Hold on, Alyosha... Cinnabar has always cared about your team, cared about you.
Alyosha comes to a halt.
When she learned you'd phoned me, her first reaction was to ask: "How is Alyosha doing?"...
When you feel ready, have a talk with her. Give her a chance, and give yourself a chance too.
Alyosha starts a little at that. Before leaving, he turns back to look at you with a complex expression, but no words come out of him.
After everyone from Serpent Eye has left, Cinnabar retracts the shield.
Expanding the shield for such a long time has worn Cinnabar out. Having retracted the shield, she leans her back on the wall and slowly slides down onto the floor.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: I'm fine.
She doesn't sound fine at all.
Alyosha probably just needs some time.
You step up and steady her wobbly body.
Cinnabar lifts her head, her eyes are full of tears, and her body is shaking uncontrollably.
You sigh and pat her on the shoulder.
Cinnabar lifts her head, her eyes are full of tears. Suddenly, she wraps her arms around you. You can clearly feel her whole body shaking.
You sigh and pat her on the back.
Whatever happens, I'm on your side.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: ...Thank you.
Two months have passed since the attack at the speech.

A lot has happened within these two months: The attacker has been detained, the Syndican block's residents have received compensation, several developers have gone bankrupt... The incident has a fairly satisfying ending.
Except for...

speaker: Cinnabar
content: The search warrant concerning Reagan still hasn't come through yet?
Reagan's background is far more complicated than we imagined. It's already a miracle to have been able to bypass him and compensate the Syndican residents.
You understand Cinnabar's concern. After all, as long as Reagan is still in power, Serpent Eye can suffer retaliation anytime.
I'll give another call to Serpent Eye.
You've already phoned Serpent Eye several times. As you've expected, no one picks up this time either.
You've lost touch with Serpent Eye.
Watching your perplexed face, Cinnabar begins to comfort you instead.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: Take it easy, I'm sure they're fine.
Three days later
Alyosha?!
Nightingale looks at you quizzically, unsure why you seem so agitated by the call from this Alyosha guy.
You take the phone from Nightingale.
Captain Alyosha? I haven't been able to reach you by phone. How's everything going for you?

speaker: Alyosha
content: Serpent Eye's number has changed.

speaker: Alyosha
content: Get Cinnabar on the phone.
That's just typical of Alyosha to not give you any respect, but now is not the time to be petty.
When Cinnabar learns that Serpent Eye is on the phone, she drops everything and rushes to your office.
Cinnabar takes the phone from your hand, pauses, and turns on the speaker.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: How have you been, Alyosha? Did Reagan give you any trouble?

speaker: Alyosha
content: Serpent Eye isn't working with City Council now.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: Is it because of what happened last time? I'm sorry...

speaker: Alyosha
content: Don't make stupid guesses.

speaker: Noise
content: You still haven't finished your drink, Captain. Who are you talking to on the phone? But it can't be Cinnabar?
Raucous noise comes from the other end of the phone.

speaker: Alyosha
content: ...If you've got any questions, you know where to find me. I happen to be... free now.
Alyosha hangs up without hesitation.
Cinnabar holds the phone in the air for a long while before putting it down.
I'll go with you.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: Um...
Cinnabar seems hesitant.
You don't want me to go?

speaker: Cinnabar
content: That's not what I mean.
You only mean to tease her with the question, but she's taking it seriously.
I hope it's not because you're annoyed at me following you around?

speaker: Cinnabar
content: How can I be annoyed at you!
To your surprise, Cinnabar is flustered at your obvious teasing.
To prove that she treats you as a confidant, Cinnabar insists that you go with her to meet her family.
You agree with pleasure, and go with her to the meeting spot hinted by Alyosha, an old depot on the border separating Eastside and Syndicate.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: Serpent Eye was founded here. Thirty years ago, Dad... my father, Alyosha, and the others rented this place to use as their quarters and training arena.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: This is the origin of Serpent Eye.
Boisterous chatter can be heard from inside the building.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: Let's go inside.
As the door is pushed open, you are greeted by a sweet wine fragrance and animated chatter.
The depot is furnished like a bar. Under the warm light, the place looks cozy and welcoming everywhere.

speaker: Serpent Member A
content: Hey, Cinnabar, I see you've even brought someone with you.
The seniors are drinking around the long table. As they spot Cinnabar and you, they drag the both of you close hospitably and sit you down at the table.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: This is my current employer, the Chief of MBCC. You've met during the last mission.
Two empty vodka bottles stand in front of him, and the third one is already half-finished. He can surely hold his liquor.

speaker: Serpent Member B
content: Haven't you had too much to drink? The headache's gonna kill you tomorrow morning.
Catching the sarcastic remark of his comrade, Alyosha slams the glass loudly on the table and spits out two words—

speaker: Alyosha
content: F**k off.
You make your way to Alyosha and say hi. But he pretends he doesn't see you and says nothing back, continuing to down his alcohol. The third bottle is almost empty too now.
You return indignantly.
Recalling how Alyosha has behaved in the past, you still feel intimidated to talk to him directly, so you turn to the friendly Serpent Eye members next to you.
What's happened to your captain?

speaker: Serpent Member A
content: Oh, don't mind him. That's our boss for you. He was over the moon when he knew you guys were coming, but once you came in, he went back to being an ass.

The crowd is giddy with chatter and laughter, shooting ceaseless questions at Cinnabar about her life in the past few years. It's obvious that their friendliness toward you is courtesy of Cinnabar, because they really adore her.

speaker: Serpent Member B
content: Tell us more about your life these two years, Cinnabar.

speaker: Serpent Member B
content: Alyosha has sent someone to get updates, but he's kept his mouth shut this whole time.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: Since the City Council began hunting me down, I've lived in Syndicate.
Cinnabar has helped civilians dodge gang attacks a few times in Syndicate. She's saved plenty of people.

speaker: Serpent Member A
content: Cinnabar is a star wherever she goes. She's always been like this since she was little.
Oh? Since she was little?

speaker: Serpent Member A
content: You don't say.
The veteran is obviously preening himself.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: My childhood... was nothing special. My father passed away early, I was raised by the seniors of Serpent Eye.

speaker: Serpent Member B
content: Cinnabar's pa was our comrade, we all risked our lives for the higher-ups in those days. After retiring in N.F. 84, we were re-hired as a mercenary unit. The first two years, we picked up jobs on the Broken Frontline that others didn't dare touch...

speaker: Serpent Member B
content: That geezer was always babbling about the big money we were going to make together, but then he went down first in DisSea...
Reminiscing the past, the veterans of Serpent Eye are getting teary-eyed.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: My father's gone, but I'm here to take his place at Serpent Eye.

speaker: Serpent Member B
content: Oh yeah, look at you. You graduated top of your class from the police academy, but you didn't even try to get one of those fancy civil servant jobs... You could have at least joined the real army of FAC. What are you doing here rolling with geezers like us anyway?

speaker: Serpent Member A
content: Oh boy, if it hadn't been for Cinnabar, none of us would have survived DisSea, let alone won the contract to protect the City Council.

speaker: Serpent Member B
content: But even protecting the City Council is risking life and limb, one misstep can mean death. If anything happened to Cinnabar, how could we face her pa on the other side?
Seeing the old men starting to worry for themselves again, Cinnabar tries to reassure them at once.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: Everything I have has been given to me by Serpent Eye, Serpent Eye is my home... It's only natural that I come back...

speaker: Alyosha
content: Enough!
Having been silent the entire time, Alyosha stands up abruptly and makes for the exit.
People in the bar are all searching each other's faces for some clue of what just happened. Cinnabar seems particularly mortified, uncertain what she's said has upset Alyosha.
Didn't you say you were going to talk to Cinnabar? She's already said so much, have you got nothing to tell her?
Alyosha stops short and turns to stare straight at Cinnabar, then croaks with a wave of drunken anger.

speaker: Alyosha
content: Serpent Eye is your home?! Then what is that place you're staying in?

speaker: Alyosha
content: You'd rather stay in that shitty place like a prison and be ordered around like an inmate than come home?!
Alyosha is growling at Cinnabar, but you know full well whom his accusations are really meant for.

speaker: Alyosha
content: I see you've long forgotten...

speaker: Cinnabar
content: I have never forgotten anything.
Cinnabar stands up and begins to counter Alyosha earnestly while holding his gaze.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: If Serpent Eye hadn't given me the education I had and taught me the important values in life, I wouldn't have grown up to be the person I am today.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: When I first joined Serpent Eye, if it hadn't been for the protection from José, Don... and you, I would have died.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: It's exactly because Serpent Eye has always protected me, I want to be like you, to protect everyone in sight...
At that moment, Cinnabar's voice sinks.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: Those unrealistic ideals of mine and the stubborn urge to protect others probably all come from my admiration for you guys.
Alyosha looks stunned and at a loss for words. After a moment, he finally continues a little indignantly.

speaker: Alyosha
content: Then who is it that you want to protect now? Don't tell me it's this kid who keeps you in chains?

speaker: Alyosha
content: The person who feels the need to monitor you even when you're having a private gathering! Who won't set you free, wanting to trap you in that shitty place for the rest of your life!

speaker: Cinnabar
content: You've misunderstood. I'm a Sinner. As you know, this identity is the main reason why the City Council wanted to hunt me down in the first place. Leaving MBCC at this juncture will only cause unnecessary trouble.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: The Chief is also not the person you've described, but a reliable employer and my confidant whom I trust my life with. The Chief only came with me because I insisted.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: The Chief has never forced me to stay in MBCC, it's my own choice.
Alyosha opens his mouth, but struggles to speak even a single word. Perhaps he's already accepted the truth, and is only grappling mentally with his pride.
With no good counter-responses, an utterly baffled Alyosha returns to his corner and flops back into the seat, raises the bottle, and then downs all the remaining content in it.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: Yes.
Alyosha's eyes widen.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: The Chief is a very important person to me.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: It's my own choice to stay in MBCC.

speaker: Alyosha
content: But this kid... and you...
Perhaps the alcohol is finally kicking in, as Alyosha is mumbling incoherently, struggling to form any meaningful sentences. Cinnabar keeps her head low and simply smiles vaguely.
With no good responses, an utterly baffled Alyosha returns to his corner and flops back into the seat, raises the bottle, and then downs all the remaining content in it.

speaker: Serpent Member B
content: You can't expect your kid to always stay by your side when she's grown up. You should learn to let go, old man.
As the Serpent Eye members begin cracking jokes, the atmosphere is pleasant and amicable again.

speaker: Serpent Member B
content: To celebrate Cinnabar's homecoming, today's drinks are all on Alyosha!
Alyosha, who's already collapsed on the bar from all the drinks he's had, is currently snoring and has no means to object.
Boisterously, people are beginning to give toasts. You can feel several pairs of scheming eyes gathering on you.

speaker: Serpent Member A
content: Since you're our dear Cinnabar's friend, allow us to treat you to a few more drinks!

speaker: Serpent Member A
content: Since you're our dear Cinnabar's good friend, allow us to treat you to a few more drinks!
The other Serpent Eye members agree unanimously.
There seems to be no way out. it's probably disrespectful to refuse the drinks from these geezers, but if you accept them... you very likely won't find your way home today.
The second you lift your hand, Cinnabar takes the glass from you smoothly, and drains it.
Just as you're about to refuse politely, Cinnabar beats you to it, lifts your glass, and drains it.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: Does anyone else want to toast the Chief?
A somewhat strange smile emerges on Cinnabar's face. This is the first time you've seen her like this.
Strangely, witnessing Cinnabar's behavior, the geezers from Serpent Eye begin to search each other's faces. An odd trepidation can be seen in all of their eyes.

speaker: Serpent Member A
content: Are you kidding me? You're being overprotective.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: I have nothing against responsible drinking. But are you sure you plan to drink responsibly? I know you guys too well.

speaker: Serpent Member A
content: Nonsense... Haha...

speaker: Serpent Member B
content: Challenge accepted. Who knows, maybe she's gotten rusty these two years. In any case, she can't outdrink all of us on her own, can she?

speaker: Cinnabar
content: Try me.

Just like that, the high-spirited crowd kicks off the drinking contest. Soon after, the loudest ones are already collapsing. Cinnabar returns to your side, she looks very calm, without even the slightest hint of flush on her face.
How... how can you hold your liquor so well?

speaker: Cinnabar
content: Finishing the drinks a client gets offered is part of the job of a bodyguard too.
Cinnabar glances at the clock on the bar.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: I remember you still have some unfinished work.
You don't want to stay here a bit longer?
Cinnabar turns back to look at the geezers. Her gaze is warm and affectionate.

speaker: Cinnabar
content: There will be a next time...
Clank!
A loud thump interrupts your conversation. Apparently, Alyosha has woken up and fallen onto the floor. Cinnabar wants to help him up, but her hand gets slapped off.

speaker: Alyosha
content: I'm not that old.

Alyosha makes his wobbly way to your side. Thinking he might want to force you to drink, Cinnabar is ready to stop him. To your surprise, he simply looks at you, and looks at Cinnabar. He shakes his head and lets out a long sigh.
After that, he pats you heavily on the shoulder, twice.
You understand the meaning behind this act—he's accepted you.

speaker: Serpent Member
content: Woohoo!
Seeing that, the Serpent Eye members immediately begin to cheer and whistle. Alyosha's meaning is clear—he's accepted you.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Excuse me, Chief? Has my application been approved?
The boy in the chair asks as soon as the door of the interrogation room slides open.

speaker: Chief
content: I'm very sorry. Your application cannot be approved at this time.
You sit down and gaze at the mountain of folders on the table before you.
Many Sinners' files have tested your patience before, but this boy in front of you, Kawa-kawa, truly has too many violation records.
Yet each case seems so... Uncharacteristic for a Sinner.
You really want to ask the Public Security Bureau why so many minutiae count as "violations".

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: I still have important work to do in WhiteSands. How about we give each other a break and stop wasting each other's time.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Alright, Chief?
The blue-haired boy probably thinks the thick stack of files on the table are his applications, so he's trying again.
Kawa-kawa guided the investigation team during the WhiteSands operation. He led the sand ship in the right direction and came to your rescue just in time before the ruins collapsed.
Yet now it seems there are some problems with this talented guide.
Moreover... He doesn't seem to know what's going on.

speaker: Chief
content: First of all, are you aware of your current situation? As in, the reason why you're held here.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Of course I'm aware!
His face glows with confidence.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: I recently used my power to make some more beacons. I could've hurt myself by using my power like that.
It seems that he has no idea that he'd be detained as a Sinner.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Also, other people don't seem to like me very much...

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Not really... It's just that... I don't know how to describe it...

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: I wanted to befriend them, but for some reason, no one really gets close with me...

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Some even came up to me and asked, "Are you actually a scapegoat for someone else?"

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: That's why I've been submitting so many applications. I really have a lot of mapping work to do.

options: This boy has no idea about the situation he's in.

content: It seems he won't be able to integrate with the other Sinners for a while.
The boy has no record of using his Sinner power to hurt others.
He doesn't belong here. He shouldn't even be in DisCity. He only belongs to the boundless WhiteSands.
We'll talk about all your cases later. It seems that I should first explain to you the purpose of this facility.
The MBCC's duty is to detain and manage Sinners. We have both the obligation and capacity to prevent the worst scenarios from unfolding.
Upon hearing this, the blue-haired boy frowns.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Chief, I really wish you used simpler words.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Tell it to me in a way that's easy to understand, like when I told you that people get eaten if they get too close to sandworms.

speaker: Chief
content: In DisCity, Sinners have to stay here for interrogation. because Sinners are dangerous.
For a moment, the boy seems to get it, but he is soon overcome with new confusion again.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: But... I've never done anything that can harm others. I just want to finish mapping WhiteSands and then mark the safe routes with beacons.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: I'm trying to protect others, just like what we were doing in WhiteSands. Why do I need to be locked up?

options: You're doing it the wrong way.

speaker: Chief
content: You're doing things in a way that violates official regulations and creates chaos for other agencies.

speaker: Chief
content: The chaos you've created has done more harm than good. It takes a lot to clean up after you.

speaker: Chief
content: Take a look at this.
test
test
test
test
test
test
The screen in the interrogation room begins to play a video.

speaker: Chief
content: You repeatedly entered the official base station in WhiteSands without permission and misappropriated supplies for personal use. By law, you're guilty of theft and trespassing.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Theft? Trespassing? I'm not sure I know what that means...
The boy's amber eyes show no sign of panic. It seems he has long taken these things for granted.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: If you're talking about the food and water at the base station, I did use some of it, but isn't that really normal?

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: People living in WhiteSands always help each other out. I saw that no one has used those supplies for a long time. Some boxes are almost even buried.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: If someone is in urgent need of food, isn't it necessary to use the supplies?

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Many people aren't familiar with the WhiteSands and they get lost, while I know where the base stations are and how to get to them safely. It's only natural for me to help them.
Kawa-kawa has mentioned "many people". And many in WhiteSands who need help don't live in shelters with stable shields.
Some are homeless refugees, but others are the desert bandits who you were so close to eradicating.

speaker: Chief
content: According to our investigation, many of those you've helped are desert bandits. You've handed over valuable government resources to the desert bandits who sowed chaos in WhiteSands.

speaker: Chief
content: This is also the most important reason for detaining you. Abetting desert bandits is a serious crime.

options: You helped those who shouldn't have been helped.

speaker: Vautour Bleu appears completely oblivious to your implied meaning, merely shaking her head slowly with a tinge of reproach and forgiveness in her eyes.
content: But... They're not like those scary bandits... Chief, quit saying stuff that I don't understand!

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: All I know is that, if someone is dying of thirst in WhiteSands, I have to give them water to drink.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: I know my way around WhiteSands, but others don't. If I didn't help them, they wouldn't have survived till sunset.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: The people who arrested me are just like you. All you talk about is the law.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: To make things worse, they knocked over my water flask! That whole big flask of water, all gone! Do you know how many people that amount of water could've saved?

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: I shouldn't have helped you back in WhiteSands!
The boy seems to be quite angry.
You take a deep breath, your mind whirring. It seems you've underestimated the boy's lack of common sense. You must tone down your expectations even more.

options: Can you tell me about those people?

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Uh... why do you suddenly ask that?

speaker: Chief
content: So that I can brief our operatives. According to you, everyone in WhiteSands helps each other out, so maybe we won't have any conflict next time we run into those "friends" of yours.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: You promise? It'd be really nice if there are fewer conflicts. But everyone dresses pretty much the same in WhiteSands. There's just a few types of desert uniforms.

speaker: Chief
content: Did their clothes have any insignia? Or were they carrying... certain weapons?

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Ah! Now that you mention it, I remember I did meet a group of travelers whose cloaks were buttoned with dagger-shaped pins.

speaker: Chief
content: Are these the guys?

You press the remote control. The screen is still showing surveillance footage, but the scene has changed to a sand cruiser anchored in WhiteSands.

speaker: Chief
content: Take a close look. Are the people on the left side of the screen the travelers you helped?

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: I think... It might be them. But I can't see their faces clearly, so I'm not sure.
You remain silent, waiting for the images to change.
The video begins to play. Several cloaked figures with long knives and submachine guns climb onto the main deck of the cruiser with hook locks.

speaker: Crew Member
content: Wh-who are you?
A crewman steps out of the bridge to see what's going on, but he is greeted by a hail of bullets.
Kawa-kawa's stomach twitches when he sees the crewman's body slump over by the bloodstained porthole.
But the boy holds back from vomiting on the spot. The footage dissolves into static as the bullets pulverize the surveillance cameras.

speaker: Chief
content: This video is from a month and a half ago. Desert bandits attacked a sand cruiser in WhiteSands. By the time the patrol team received the distress signal and rushed to the scene, no survivors were found.

speaker: Chief
content: There were twenty-three crew members in total. The desert bandits snatched away everything they could take, sparing not even the crew's personal belongings.

speaker: Chief
content: The cruel environment of WhiteSands may unite those living there, but it can also make them cruel.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: No... no! How can this be?
What he believed to be good deeds have reaped horrific results. The boy is deeply confounded.

speaker: Chief
content: I'm just stating a fact. Not everyone in WhiteSands is as kind or eager to help others as you are.

speaker: Chief
content: People who slaughter innocents without batting an eye like these desert bandits make strict laws necessary.

options: Some people don't deserve your kindness.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Then what... what should I do?
The rehabilitation is beginning to pay off. However, the boy won't be able to accept everything all at once. You can see the denial, confusion, and a hint of unease in his eyes.

speaker: Chief
content: Next time someone asks you for help, at least ask them a few questions about their background.

speaker: Chief
content: If you encounter any suspicious individuals who might be desert bandits, alert us right away. The patrol team in WhiteSands will go and catch them.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Alright, I'll listen to you. Then what if I...

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Wait a sec.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: What did you just say? Next time?
The boy's crestfallen eyes suddenly flash with exuberance.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: So you've agreed to let me out?

speaker: Chief
content: However, the MBCC will soon organize another cleansing operation against the desert bandits. I will put you on the task force.

speaker: Chief
content: If things go well, I'll arrange for you to continue data collection along the way. You'll also be able to place your beacons.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Awesome!

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: There's an area of WhiteSands that I'm almost finished mapping! I just need one more round of data collection to complete it!
As the boy cheers, the brief interrogation comes to an end.
The boy is soon taken out of the interrogation room, while you return to your office. At least on the surface, everyone is happy with the outcome.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief... should we believe him so easily?

speaker: Nightingale
content: The cleansing operation has entered the final stage of planning. Isn't it too risky to include such an unpredictable element?

speaker: Nightingale
content: Relevant agencies are already working overtime to analyze the weather data of WhiteSands for this operation.

speaker: Nightingale
content: With experience from the last operation, we do not necessarily need a navigator.
You understand what Nightingale is getting at. There had been too many blunders in the previous WhiteSands operation.
With regards to the upcoming WhiteSands operation, it is only natural to try and minimize unpredictable elements as much as possible.

options: He is first and foremost a geologist.

speaker: Chief
content: He is a navigator second, and a Sinner last.

The data from the beacons, combined with the strange forecasting model, are indeed more accurate than the research institutes' forecasts, no? He claims to be a geologist, and so far, there's no evidence to disprove that.

It's just like what the boy has always insisted. A search of his carry-on luggage has revealed many research materials on the geology and climate of WhiteSands, as well as hundreds of WhiteSands maps with surveying data.
To most people, those maps all look exactly the same.
Among the materials, there is a thick notebook documenting a very complex dynamic theoretical model.

speaker: Chief
content: After reviewing the theoretical model, the only conclusion the research institutions can draw is that it's a model that tries to predict the weather changes in WhiteSands. However, without enough real-time data to back it up, it remains of dubious value.

speaker: Nightingale
content: That theoretical model does hold some value, but we can't rule out the possibility that Kawa-kawa is an accomplice of the desert bandits. Like you said, he claims to be a geologist.
Nightingale emphasizes the words "claims to be" extra hard.

speaker: Chief
content: But is there any other, better way? If the forecasting system used by the fleet can avoid sandstorms, we naturally wouldn't need a navigator.

speaker: Chief
content: As for socializing him with reality, he has to personally experience things to truly understand the ways of the world, no?

Five days later, 130 kilometers east of DisCity
The bridge of the sand cruiser Thoth

speaker: Sandship Captain
content: We can't go any further! The engine's cooling system has been completely clogged by white sand! If we don't stop now, the engine will be totally scrapped!
The howling sandstorm hammers the bridge relentlessly. Alarms are going off all over the ship. The crew members have all suspended their work, and are now gazing towards you in anticipation.
To pursue the desert bandit remnants, the navigator's warning has been ignored. That's a huge mistake.

speaker: Chief
content: Everyone, brace for impact! Put the maintenance team on engine repair right away!
In an instant, the bridge hums with activity again. The crew shouts out their instructions, while the tremoring hull regains stability as the engine grinds to a halt.
The sand cruiser is stuck.

The only sound left on the bridge is that of the whirling sand whipping against the windows. The radar screen shows only static, and all GPS signals are lost. Even the bow has vanished completely into the raging white sands.
WhiteSands is once again showcasing its devastating might, but fortunately, the cruiser's Hypercube shield is doing its job. Things are safe as long as one stays off the deck.

speaker: Sandship Captain
content: Commander, what is your next order?
The captain's question snaps you back to reality. The crew and task force members all await your response.

speaker: Chief
content: Before the sandstorm subsides, the cruiser will remain in place and undergo repairs.

speaker: Chief
content: ...If necessary, we might have to stay here for a few more days.
The worst case scenario has happened. You don't want your crew to risk their lives.

speaker: Sandship Captain
content: All posts have heard the order. Issue a damage report right away!
As for the task force...
You look at the Sinners and task force members behind you.
Go back to your cabins and get some rest. After the cruiser is fixed, we must speed up our mission progress.
Some show disappointment, while others just shrug it off and follow your order quietly.
Just a few hours ago, the task force carried out a triumphant raid against a group of desert bandits.
To lure out the big fish, you deliberately asked the force to let a few bandits escape. The "sudden" sandstorm, however, disrupted your plan.
The fleeing bandit ships have sensed the sandstorm coming before you have. The sand cruiser plunged headfirst into a sandstorm that could have been avoided...

speaker: Sandship Captain
content: Commander, the damage report is ready.

speaker: Sandship Captain
content: Due to continuous operation during the sandstorm, the ship's air filtration system has been completely destroyed. Consequently, the engine is also damaged.

speaker: Sandship Captain
content: Luckily, the maintenance team says they can fix these two problems. They just need some time.

speaker: Sandship Captain
content: But the most critical issue is our fuel and water supply...
If I remember correctly, this ship should be carrying enough supplies to last a month.

speaker: Sandship Captain
content: Indeed.

speaker: Sandship Captain
content: But...
The captain seems exasperated and helpless.

speaker: Sandship Captain
content: Since the sandstorm paralyzed our air filters, a large amount of white sand blew into the cargo hold through the pipes. The storage tank in the hold was open for some reason, so the white sand got into our water and fuel supply.

speaker: Sandship Captain
content: The fuel might still work after filtering, but as for the water...

options: How many more days can we manage?

speaker: Sandship Captain
content: By conservative estimates, the remaining intact water tanks can last us up to five days.

When traveling in WhiteSands, aside from resisting bad weather, it's also crucial to prevent white sand from mixing with supplies. This is especially true for white sand that has been whipped up by a sandstorm.
But five days... Returning to DisCity the same way right now will take three days with the sand cruiser's current speed. And that's not counting the engine repair time and possible speed drops...
If requesting help from WhiteSands patrol... The sandstorm has jammed the comms system. Even if we get in touch, it'll take a while for any rescue team to arrive this deep into WhiteSands.
But one thing is certain. We must not sit here idly.
Find out why the storage tanks were open in the first place. I'll find a solution to the supply issue.

speaker: Sandship Captain
content: Understood. I'll deal with it right away.
Hecate, come with me.

speaker: Hecate
content: Okay.
The blue-haired girl quietly follows you as always.

Compared to the busy bridge, the cabins allocated to the task force seem a little deserted. Even though you've ordered them to rest, most of the task force members are reluctant to stay around the cabins.
As for the reason...

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Chief! I felt the ship's engine stop! Are we already at the storm harbor?
Kawa-kawa has shed all traces of depression since boarding the ship, and has been happily dishing out WhiteSands survival tips to everyone he meets.
The task force members in the adjacent cabins were the first to suffer. After several force members locked their doors, Kawa-kawa turned to target the regular crew members.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: The scale of this sandstorm is huge! What a rare treasure trove of data! I did a simple calculation just now.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Hmm... The sandstorm will probably last another ten hours. As long as we don't enter its core zone, there isn't much risk...

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Um, chief? You followed the route I gave you and avoided the spots I marked, right?
When it comes to WhiteSands, Kawa-kawa's acumen immediately increases a hundredfold.
Yes, the sand cruiser steered clear of the spots you marked on the route. However, the scale of this sandstorm is a bit bigger than expected.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: What? A sandstorm appeared at the storm harbor?

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Why...?
For a split second, an expression of disbelief blankets the boy's face, as if he's been betrayed.
You feel a bit guilty for lying to save face.
But soon, he snaps back to normal.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: There must be something wrong with my calculations. Are the coordinates data wrong? Or maybe it's the wind speed data?
After muttering a few words to himself, Kawa-kawa dashes out of the cabin.
You grab the boy quickly before he almost knocks over Hecate by the door.
I suspect that I may have copied the wrong coordinates data. I'm going to the bridge to collect new data.
At this point, it's no longer necessary to calculate the sandstorm data. I have other things to ask you about.
Actually, the ship has ventured into the heart of the sandstorm. We are currently trapped by the storm and cannot move.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: How could this be? Did we turn too late?
No, it was because we were too focused on chasing the bandit ships. They led us into the storm.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: B-but... I clearly warned a while back that based on the beacon data, the area will be hit by an extra large sandstorm!

options: There's nothing wrong with your forecast.

content: If we had followed your instructions, we might still be sailing ahead. But we couldn't miss this opportunity, otherwise those desert bandits might have escaped.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Sigh...
The boy looks disappointed.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Then why did you come find me?

Our fuel and water supply have been contaminated. We only have enough for less than five days.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: What?!

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Why didn't you mention something so important at the very beginning?
You're a little shocked by the momentary panic on the boy's face.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: There are a total of 53 people on this ship. It's a big project to find clean water for so many people! You should have told me at the very beginning!
At that, Kawa-kawa breaks free from you and runs out of the cabin without looking back, his footsteps echoing along the corridors.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: I'm going to make some preparations for going out...

speaker: Sandship Captain
content: Commander, I checked the surveillance footage of the cargo holder from beginning to end. No outsiders have entered.

speaker: Sandship Captain
content: The water and fuel tanks were contaminated because the crew forgot to close the valves during their inspections...

speaker: Sandship Captain
content: I deeply apologize for such a serious mistake. As the captain, I am willing to take full responsibility.
The mistake has already been made. We must now focus on correcting it as soon as possible. We need everyone's help on this.
The comms conversation ends. Having been disrupted by so many unexpected events, you can't help but sigh.
Eighteen hours later. Ten o'clock in the morning.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Everyone! Hold on a bit longer! We'll be arriving at the shelter soon!
Kawa-kawa is now setting up beacons on the dunes. Having received permission, the boy is stopping the hovercraft at regular intervals to stick a newly assembled beacon into the dunes.

speaker: Task Force Member 1
content: Heck, where does he get all that energy? Does he never get tired at all, with such a huge bag on his back? How many beacons has he set up?

speaker: Task Force Member 2
content: Around twenty or so. Haven't you figured it out yet? It's the same reason you feel like a duck to water in Syndicate.

speaker: Task Force Member 1
content: ...In WhiteSands, he is the true boss.

speaker: Task Force Member 2
content: It's so hot... I'm melting from just sitting inside the ship...
And this is after Kawa-kawa got special WhiteSands suits for everyone.
You can feel that the boy is wholeheartedly contributing his knowledge to the task force. He even reminded everyone to set off in the early morning when the temperature is the lowest.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Done! Let's go!

speaker: Kawa-kawa

options: How long will it take to get to the shelter?

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Soon. It'll be a few more minutes if the hovercraft is going at full speed. I've installed all the spare beacons in my bag already, so I won't be stopping anymore.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Look! Up ahead! That's the shelter I was talking about!
The hovercraft speeds over a small slope, and a fortress-like building comes into view.
It's similar to the sanctuary you encountered on your last mission. This particular fortress even has some traces of green.
Yet the heavy machine guns and sentries based there immediately confirm your worst expectations. There are even a few mania weapons.
Park it behind the cliff over there!

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Huh? Why stop the hovercraft here? Why not go directly to the shelter?
I'm afraid your traveler friends won't welcome us.
You don't have time to explain to the boy in detail. The hovercraft is less than 500 meters from the fortress, which means you've already entered the heavy machine guns' firing range.
You cast your shackles and take over the steering wheel from Kawa-kawa.
After taking over the hovercraft's steering wheel, you swerve it to the far right.
The sentries on the towers have noticed the approaching hovercraft, while the people in the fortress are quickly gathering.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Chief, what are you doing?
After veering out of the machine guns' firing range, the task force members leave the hovercraft and begin to observe the fortress's forces from the cliff.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Don't assume the worst of them... I rescued someone before and brought him to this settlement.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: They were quite nice. They gave me food and water before I left.

Ordinary shelters don't have powerful machine guns like the ones on the towers. Also, this fortress doesn't have the yellowish shield common to other shelters.
You remember the shield that saved you from being devoured by sandworms last time.
The figures on the towers even set up several rocket launchers. Even the seasoned task force members frown worriedly upon seeing those heavy weapons.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Wait! They might just be a bit spooked by strangers.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: I'll go tell them that we just want some fuel and water. I helped them before, so they'll definitely help us back!

He has to experience some things for himself. Plus, this will show if he's a desert bandit or not.

speaker: Hecate
content: What if he flees?

speaker: WhiteSands Resident
content: Who is it?!

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Hey, it's me! Do you remember me? I visited this place last time!

speaker: WhiteSands Resident

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Our ship broke down and needs water and fuel. Can you spare some for us?

speaker: WhiteSands Resident
content: Ship? What ship?
The person who appears to be in charge takes the binoculars from his subordinate and observes the cliff, but you've hidden the hovercraft well. Binoculars alone won't be able to spot it.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: So, I'm navigating for a sand ship, but we got stuck in a sandstorm and need water and fuel.

speaker: WhiteSands Resident
content: So you say there's a sand ship nearby? Is it a merchant ship? Where did you anchor it?

content: Oh, not a merchant ship. Strictly speaking, it's a battleship.

speaker: WhiteSands Resident
content: Battleship? A battleship?!

content: Yup! A big battleship like the V-170.

speaker: WhiteSands Resident
content: Are you talking about the MBCC's fleet? Damn it! You brought them here?!

speaker: WhiteSands Resident
content: Great! We can finally avenge the boss today! Brothers, attack!

speaker: WhiteSands Resident
content: And he's a Sinner! Kill him! Shoot! Shoot him!

The desert bandits continue to shoot for several minutes before ceasing fire.
The panicked boy holds up the beacon and activates its shield to resist the shooting. You quickly send the task force members to attend to him.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: No, but...

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: How could this be... Why...

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: I just wanted to ask them for some water... And I helped them before...

You pat him on the shoulder. This is probably the first time someone has responded to his goodwill with bullets and malice.
He had firmly believed that everyone in WhiteSands is honest, kind, and eager to help others. Now he knows that he is terribly mistaken.

options: Do you remember what I told you?

content: Some people don't deserve your kindness.
The boy lifts his head in a daze, mouthing the words you just said.
Soon, the fear fades from his eyes. One gains the most profound insight after a brush with death.

content: Chief, you're right. I...

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: I apologize for my reckless and immature actions.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: I was too naive...

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: I thought that life always came first in WhiteSands. I assumed that everyone here puts saving lives as their top priority...

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: I'm sorry... I'm really sorry...

speaker: Hecate

speaker: Hecate
content: Can you stand up? We still have work to do.

content: Yeah. Don't worry about me.

speaker: Kawa-kawa

speaker: Kawa-kawa

Kawa-kawa tries repeatedly to cover the other task force members with his shield, but the desert bandits are obviously well-stocked in ammunition, and have even begun to use mania weapons.

You notice the boy repeatedly observing the fortress's defenses with his binoculars.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: I noticed something several times now. Look, Chief.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: My hunch was right. That thing at the top of the tower is a beacon I had put in WhiteSands.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Although they changed the color, I can still feel a faint connection to the beacons. They must be using that as a shield!

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: I was wondering why so many beacons in this area went missing! I thought the sandstorm blew them away, but they were actually removed by these desert bandits!

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: And to think that I already helped them install multiple beacons here to resist the sandstorm... They are so greedy!

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Chief, I want to regain control of these beacons and cut off their firepower.

content: Around three hundred meters.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: All of them.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: I'll first activate the beacons near the heavy machine guns and the mania weapons. Will the task force be able to use the opportunity to approach the fortress?

speaker: Task Force Member 1
content: I think it's no problem. The shield seems fairly strong.

speaker: Task Force Member 2
content: Fairly? He's practically unscathed after getting pummeled by bullets!

content: Understood.

content: Well done. You're a proper Sinner now.

content: Double-check all their straps! Confiscate all weapons and bandage up the injured!

speaker: Task Force Member 2

speaker: Task Force Member 2
content: Any other commands, Chief?
