The hearty victory makes everyone forget WhiteSands' scorching heat, but it seems the good luck isn't here to stay.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Chief! The beacon network is warning that a massive sandstorm is rapidly approaching!
How much time do we have?

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: It's too late. The hovercraft won't be able to leave. We have to take cover where we are.

After all you've been through in WhiteSands these past few days, particularly the recent battle, you now have complete trust in the young geologist in front of you. Kawa-kawa's calculations are impeccable.
...Hecate! Get a team to move the bandits to the cellar! I'll tell the guys over at the hovercraft to go directly into the fortress's dock.
Luckily, the walls and living facilities here are well-maintained and sustained minimal damage. The sand ship's supplies can last us a few days. We just have to wait out the sandstorm here.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: What about me? What about me?
The young desert researcher seems to be expecting orders from you.
You point out anything we've missed right away.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Okay! No problem!
Two days later, the sandstorm is still raging.
Hiding in a flimsy wooden building of an oasis shelter is completely different from hiding in a sturdy sand ship. Even in the cellar, one can feel the full fury of the storm above.
The dilapidated cellar door suddenly opens from the outside, and wind mixed with white sand gushes in. A tightly bundled figure jumps down, closing the wooden door behind him.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: I'm back!
The boy holds a supply box high above his head. The task force members greet him with warm smiles. They have long grown accustomed to his ways.
Though this young, self-proclaimed geologist is socially awkward and lacks common sense, he is one to be trusted in times of crisis.
What's more, in the few days spent with the task force, the boy's common sense is also rapidly developing.
In the past few days, many things in the fortress were blown away by the sudden sandstorm before they could be packed away.
The reserves in the cellar were low, so Kawa-kawa constantly went up to the surface to find supplies, saving everyone from starvation.
He refused to let anyone help him, citing the risk of getting lost in the sandstorm for those unfamiliar with the desert.
Everyone can only shrug and let him show off his prowess.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Just as the data predicted, the sandstorm has already started to shrink. It will recede almost completely by tomorrow.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: I checked all the beacons. They're all tightly fastened to the fortress wall. Speaking of which, I really have to thank them.
Kawa-kawa glances at the desert bandits in the cellar corner, who have their hands tied behind their backs.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: They placed so many beacons in the oasis, and the center of this sandstorm just happens to be here. The data collected from this storm is priceless!

speaker: Chief
content: Did yesterday's signal go out?

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Don't worry! As long as no one from the sand ship took down the beacon I set up, the information must have reached the captain.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Oh, right! I found some food to share with you all!
Everyone's eyes lit up as soon as they heard the word "food." They've been eating nothing but compressed food for the past two days.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Hehe... I found some good stuff.
Kawa-kawa puts down the supply box, squats down and starts rummaging through his backpack.
He fishes out a few scrawny lizards with one hand, and some scorpions with broken tails with the other.
Some task force members almost shriek out and faint.
You recall that during the first WhiteSands operation, Kawa-kawa mentioned eating grilled scorpions, which according to him, taste like chicken.
You realize now that it wasn't a joke.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Of course! This is a rare delicacy of WhiteSands.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Although there's not much meat on them, they're very delicious when grilled and seasoned!

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Animals and insects are much more perceptive than humans.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: During a sandstorm, you can easily find them hiding together, especially in the corners of buildings.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: I found these in the dock.
With that, he skillfully lights a fire before everyone's gawking eyes.
He slices open the lizards and scorpions with a small knife and sprinkles them with fine salt. He then skewers them with dead branches and holds them over the fire.
Though unsettling to look at, the delicious aroma of grilled meat soon wafts throughout the cellar.
Like a gourmet chef, Kawa-kawa fans the flames with his hat to control the heat.
He cooks like this for around five minutes.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: It's ready! Who wants to take the first bite?
One must admit that the grilled lizard skewers look much more appealing now.
The lizards' fat has turned golden brown from the open fire, while the lean meat has become like jerky.
Even so, no one dares to take a skewer from Kawa-kawa.
You, however, disregard the uneasy atmosphere by the fire. You not only take a lizard skewer, but a scorpion skewer as well.
You take a bite. Kawa-kawa has grilled them with the perfect amount of heat. The skin is crispy, while the meat inside is tender and juicy.
The scorpions, on the other hand, are crispy and succulent all over, especially when seasoned with fine salt. You can't help but give a big thumbs up in the direction of the desert bandits.
For the past two days, everyone had only compressed biscuits to feed on, which were as bland as a mouthful of sand.
After hearing your praise, the task force members can't help but salivate.
Hecate makes the first move. Then, one after another, everyone scrambles to grab the skewers by the fire.
Soon, the task force members can't stop praising the food. The boy smiles happily.
Ten hours later, Oasis fortress tower
The sandstorm subsides, just as Kawa-kawa has predicted.

After three days of tense nerves, the task force is finally able to get a good night's sleep. Kawa-kawa, however, says he's not tired, and that he'll take the final night shift for the task force. He wants to keep an eye on the beacon data in case another sandstorm comes.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Chief, why are you still awake?

speaker: Chief
content: Someone needs to watch the desert bandits in the cellar. But don't worry, I asked Hecate to go.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: I'm used to it. For many years, when I was surveying in WhiteSands, I could only do research when the temperature dropped at night.
The boy sits cross-legged atop the tower as he talks, with a thick notebook and map on his lap, and a fire next to him to keep him warm.

speaker: Chief
content: What are you working on this time?

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: I'm pulling the data on the previous sandstorms from the beacon network and putting them into the model.
You can see the fatigue on the boy's face, yet something is spurring him to keep working on the data.
You sit down next to him by the fire. You take a portable terminal out of your pocket and hand it to the boy.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: What's this?

speaker: Chief
content: An application for a transfer order I just wrote. When we get back, I'll start the formal approval process.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: You're going to transfer me to... the task force?

speaker: Chief
content: Your Sinner power is very special and can protect others well. Coupled with your performance in battle, I don't think there should be any obstacles in getting the approval.

speaker: Chief
content: Also, don't you want to return to WhiteSands to continue your surveying work? By joining the task force, I can regularly arrange for you to go to WhiteSands on missions.

speaker: Chief
content: After this transfer order is approved, you can use all the supplies in the WhiteSands base station.

speaker: Chief
content: Think of it as a fringe benefit. But you have to promise me one thing.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: A-and what is that?

options: You have to promise not to escape.

content: Kawa-kawa takes a deep breath, then hugs the terminal in his arms, trying his best to stop shaking with excitement.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Thank you.

speaker: Chief
content: No need to thank me. Remember what I said? I'm just trying to the best of my ability to repay you for the kindness you've given to this world.

speaker: Chief
content: Your contributions to WhiteSands' routes shouldn't just be respected by us, but by everyone.

speaker: Chief
content: If it weren't for the beacons you set up, the sand ship would've struggled to navigate WhiteSands. The task force would've also had a hard time reaching the oasis.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: ...Thank you, you're very kind too. My dad would've been proud to hear this.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Yes, my dad. My grandpa, also. Three generations of my family have been surveying and mapping WhiteSands.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: They would've all been thrilled to hear this.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: After all, this is the first praise I've ever gotten for our work.

speaker: Chief
content: That notebook in your backpack, and that forecasting model... Did your dad leave you those?

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Yeah, those are my dad's valuable research materials. But... I haven't seen him for almost a decade.
The temperature of WhiteSands at night is totally opposite to that of daytime. Kawa-kawa tightens his scarf and adds some more wood to the fire.
The firelight illuminates the boy's face, but you can't tell what he's thinking.
You wait for the boy to continue on his own, asking no questions.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: I never met my grandpa, and my mom died giving birth to me. As for my dad... He only returns to the shelter once in a while. Sometimes, I wouldn't see him for a whole month...
The boy smiles sadly.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Growing up, I was quite unpopular in the shelter. You know what they called me? The "idiot's son." That father of mine was a lot of trouble.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Every time he came back to the shelter, he told me he was working on a great cause.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: But he was so sly, he never told anyone else about what he was doing. He never let the townspeople know that he was mapping WhiteSands, or that he dreamed of finding safe passages and harbors there.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: I told him I wanted him to just stay in the town and be like everyone else's fathers. I wanted him to take my hand and go to the grocery store at dusk.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: This continued until I was six. I haven't seen him since.

options: Did anyone else see him since?

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: No one has seen him since. Every day, I sat on top of the crate at the entrance of the town, waiting for him as always. It was the path he'd take to come home.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Sometimes I thought that maybe I'd feel better if he really died in an accident.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: But you know what? When I was eight, I got a package from him.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: He didn't put any letters in the package, but I knew he was the one who sent them. Only he would send those fancy research materials to such a little border town.

options: And they're the manuscripts you have on hand?

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: That's right.
The boy takes out the manuscripts from his luggage. The dozens of handwritten pages have yellowed from the years, but there are no signs of damage. They have been perfectly preserved by Kawa-kawa.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: I thought about it for a long time. Why did he send me these materials? The townspeople told me not to think about such useless things. They laughed at me and said that if I did, I'd become an idiot just like him.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: But I just couldn't help thinking about my dad's "great cause."
You couldn't figure it out, so you tried to chase after him, right?
The boy freezes in surprise.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: ...How did you know?

options: That's what they call souls in sync.

content: The boy's actions have always been upright. Coupled with his current situation, it wasn't hard to guess.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Amazing! Just like Stargazer!

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: You're right. And it wasn't hard to follow my dad's trail. There was a beacon set up only a kilometer away from the shelter.
So you followed the beacons, one by one, into WhiteSands.
And on that journey, you awakened your Sinner power.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: That's right. Looking back at it now, it was actually extremely risky. I went into WhiteSands with just enough food and water for less than a week.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Then, unsurprisingly, a few kilometers into WhiteSands, I encountered a massive sandstorm.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: You should know what it's like to see a beacon shining brightly in a sandstorm when you can be torn to shreds anytime.
You've faced the full horror of sandstorms, so you can easily visualize the scene.
You remember the despair, fear and powerlessness you felt when Stargazer rescued you last time. Those feelings almost suffocated you, and the boy was probably in an even worse situation at the time.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: I could only follow the beacons, one after another, on and on.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: I didn't know how long I had been walking. I didn't know which direction I was heading. That was, until I reached a harbor at the very last beacon.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: I knew I was saved.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: At that moment, I understood firsthand what my dad's "great cause" meant. I realized what this cause could bring to others.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: I realized that I should devote my life to this cause, for there is nothing greater than saving the lives of others.
The wind around you dies down completely. All you can hear is the crackling firewood by you and the boy.
I checked some information on your grandpa. He was a well-known geologist who devoted his life to forecasting sandstorms. And your dad was your grandpa's best student.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: The theoretical model for forecasting sandstorms was created by my grandpa. But the model requires massive amounts of dynamic data to function.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: And in WhiteSands... Whether it's exploring or setting up a beacon network, the work is hard and thankless.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: I heard that no one supported my grandpa's project, so he and my dad had to finish the model themselves.
You've reviewed the files and inventions of Kawa-kawa's grandpa. The forecasting model is actually very accurate, but it threatened the vested interest groups of DisCity.
If safe transport routes are established in WhiteSands, Nirvana's status will be severely hit. In the worst case scenario, Hypercube prices may crash...
So the authorities promised him the most cutting-edge research equipment in exchange for staying in WhiteSands forever.
This is the reason why Kawa-kawa's family had been living in WhiteSands for generations. To keep the precious research resources, Kawa-kawa's grandpa had no choice but to accept such a deal.
But obviously, the boy is not yet ready to touch upon such realistic issues.

options: The awakening of every Sinner's power is related to the Black Rings.

content: Many of them call their powers a curse, and have caused much misfortune wherever they go.
But Kawa-kawa, you're different. You've done things that many others haven't been able to. You've made good use of your power, bringing happiness to others with your "curse." You're very lucky.
Of course, all those years of surveying, mapping, and setting up beacons in WhiteSands isn't something that can be easily surmised by luck.
The boy has perseverance unimaginable to most, but at the root of the matter is the unshakable faith he inherited from his forefathers.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Yes... I was awakened during that sandstorm. My mind has changed since then.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: I no longer thought of my dad as the "idiot" that others sneer at. As for myself, I feel like I should do even better than my dad after gaining this power. Only...

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: I followed all those beacons in WhiteSands, searching all the way. In my seven years of searching, I finished every geology book and figured out every piece of data and model in those manuscripts...

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: I thought that maybe my dad was testing me, and that he'd come back to me if I completed the test.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Or maybe he just had too much work, and that he'd come back early to meet me if I helped him complete part of it.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: But I was wrong.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Half a year ago, I walked across half of WhiteSands and found my dad's last beacon. There ought to have been another beacon a kilometer away, but I didn't see it.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: I looked in every direction but found nothing. I was finally convinced that it was the last beacon my father had set up.

options: You didn't find any other information?

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: No.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: The beacon stood alone amid the dunes. I stayed by that beacon for a week, thinking that maybe my dad left for a run, and that I'll bump into him on his way back.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: But it's just like when I was six years old, I sat at the entrance of the town, waiting for him. In the end...
You gently touch his head.
...That day will come.
Maybe your dad will follow your beacons to find you.

speaker: Kawa-kawa
content: Sob...
The knot in his heart that had stayed there for seven years finally unravels with the wind.
Your dad and grandpa would be proud of you.
The data terminal in the boy's hand falls to the ground. The data finishes uploading to the beacon network. After a five-second countdown, the beacon network of the oasis resumes functioning.
The beacons around you light up one by one. From the high tower, they look like blue fireflies illuminating the dark desert.
They link all the way to the night sky, merging with the stars.
It's as if a second Milky Way has spread out across WhiteSands.
Levy, you've gone too far!

speaker: Levy
content: That'll be 73,500,200 DisCoins. Since we're relatives, keep the two hundred. But that private sand boat you've just bought will be mine. Be sure to clean up the trash on the boat. I'm kind of a neat freak, you know.
Levy, you! I...
We're... family, after all, how could you...

speaker: Levy
content: Crying won't get you anything, dear cousin. Grow up. This is a board meeting with so many people watching. Aren't you ashamed?

speaker: Levy
content: Hey, don't rub it with your dirty hands. Two hundred DisCoins are not enough to pay for pink eye treatment.

speaker: Levy
content: And don't give me that kicked-puppy look. You've gotta get me that money even if it means pawning your last pair of pants...
Shut up! I won't let you humiliate my father any more!

speaker: Levy
content: Oh, don't you worry, Chaddy. I won't make you pay your father's debt. If he dies, I'll be your guardian. I must do my part for the family, mustn't I?

speaker: Levy
content: Aaahhh!
In the interrogation room, Levy swings his arm in a cast nonchalantly.
You should avoid moving it if you want it to heal soon.

speaker: Levy
content: Relax. Back in the day, I once broke my leg in a fight and went clubbing as soon as I got the cast. It healed just fine after.

speaker: Levy
content: Hehe, speaking of which, why do you care so much about me?

speaker: Levy
content: Curious? About what?
About how an ordinary boy could crack the metacarpal bone of a Sinner with Endura Tendency...

speaker: Levy
content: Nonsense. How could he hurt me? I fell on my own!

speaker: Levy
content: I slipped and fell, knocking my hand on the step. It has nothing to do with that boy.
Then why did you ask to see him after that fall cracked your metacarpal bone?

speaker: Levy
content: It's only natural that an uncle would want to see his nephew who's strayed into questionable territory. Or do you think I'd seek revenge on a kid?
Based on what I know of you...
Yes.

speaker: Levy
content: ...You're right. I'm going to sell Chaddy to a private Hypercube mine as a coolie to cover my medical expenses...
Levy said that menacingly. When he saw your icy expression, he began to explain gleefully.

speaker: Levy
content: Tsk, look at you. I'm joking! Have you got no sense of humor?

speaker: Levy
content: And why does it look like you're interrogating me? Shouldn't you be questioning Chad instead? I'm the victim!
Levy pointed at his injured arm a little indignantly. He's obviously a little careless with his movement, as it seemed to tug at his wound.

speaker: Levy
content: Ouch...
After his brief "performance", he noticed your indifference to his exaggerated acting and decided to initiate small talk.

speaker: Levy
content: By the way, Chief, do you know what's the best part of getting wrapped in bandages?
What?

speaker: Levy
content: Look, the nurses wrote their good wishes on it. Things like get well soon, speedy recovery, etc.
Levy raises his bandaged arm.
Not everyone gets this kind of privilege.

speaker: Levy
content: I know, I know. I'm hot and loaded, after all. It's normal the nurses are being particularly nice to me.

speaker: Levy
content: But it's not like these words can actually help my injury heal faster. If I were a little more antisocial, I would even think they were being annoying.
What are you trying to say?

speaker: Levy
content: Nothing. I just think people are obsessed with seemingly useful but practically meaningless things.
What's meaningful to you then? Taking revenge on your nephew?
Levy raised an eyebrow.

speaker: Levy
content: Please, I thought we were over that? Besides, what can I gain from being petty with a child... You, on the other hand.

speaker: Levy
content: Sitting here and interrogating me. It doesn't get more meaningless than that.
He leans over from the chair, looking you up and down like examining a product.

speaker: Levy
content: Hmm, well, I guess that's quite an achievement, at least.

speaker: Levy
content: Hey, why don't you tell me how it feels like to sit there?

speaker: Levy
content: When you sit in that chair, the Sinners must tell you whatever you want them to tell. You've got the MBCC and even the entire government behind you, and the infallible shackles.

speaker: Levy
content: It must feel amazing. Power is the most luxurious addiction, you see.

speaker: Levy
content: Be careful though. Not every Sinner is harmless like me. You're very powerful, but even someone like you can't watch their back all the time.

speaker: Levy
content: If you run into a murderous psycho one day, no power or special ability can save your ass.
The mockery in Levy's words is blatant. But you know a thing or two about dealing with people like him.

options: Ignore the mockery and take back control

content: Be direct, Levy. I know full well what power my position grants me, and I accept the risks and the price that come with it.
But you... I can tell you don't like to be here, do you? Cooperate with me and help me understand the cause and consequence of the incident, then I'll let you go.

speaker: Levy
content: Haha, interesting...

speaker: Levy
content: You hate me, but you tell yourself: he's a Sinner. He might be useful some day.

speaker: Levy
content: That's exhausting. If someone disgusts you, you should simply punch them in the face like my little nephew did.
You didn't respond to his provocation but produced the evidence instead.

This is Chad, right? The one who hit you.

speaker: Levy
content: I told you, he didn't do it. I fell on my own.
Levy grumbled as he took a glance at the photo, then at you.

speaker: Levy
content: Sigh, I was shocked too. Didn't think that kid would really dare to do it.
What do you mean?

speaker: Levy
content: I mean, Chad is the son of my cousin. I watched him grow up. Growing up, he's always followed me around, calling me Uncle Levy.

speaker: Levy
content: I was heartbroken that this should have happened.
If you were that close, why would he attack you?
Levy frowned.

speaker: Levy
content: Because of... a minor dispute over some property.
Minor dispute?
Did you know that after the Public Security Bureau arrived and subdued Chad, they found a gun on him?
Had he been a little more reckless, it wouldn't have been just a fistfight. He would have shot you.

speaker: Levy
content: Nonsense. Chad has always been a decent kid. How would he possibly want to shoot me?
Levy looks taken aback. Apparently, he was unaware of this.
Then why did he carry a gun to the board meeting?
I'm afraid this is no minor dispute.

The document says that the two parties have been disputing over property worth dozens of million DisCoins recently. But for a family of wealthy entrepreneurs in Eastside, it doesn't sound like that much of a big deal.
Your cousin didn't file for bankruptcy protection?

speaker: Levy
content: Bankruptcy, huh? He just bought a villa with three balconies, a private pool, and a central thermostat. You can't imagine how cozy that house is. Even I'm getting envious... Ugh, I digress.
Levy looks like he's holding back something. He must be hiding some secret.
After a slightly dramatic sigh, Levy finally begins.

speaker: Levy
content: Frankly, I know Chad too well. That boy is always broody and alarmingly quiet. He's a good kid.

speaker: Levy
content: Even if puberty screwed up part of his brain, I bet he wouldn't come up with the idea of carrying a gun.
So you're saying someone put him up to it?

speaker: Levy
content: Do I have to spell it out? You don't know my cousin. The fourth shareholder of Fort Limited with two companies and a large assembly plant under his name. Sounds like a respectable fella, yeah?

speaker: Levy
content: Tsk, in reality, being a respectable fella means "acting respectable and leaving all the dirty deeds to others."

speaker: Levy
content: He won't even hesitate to use his own son. He feels no such thing as guilt.
You mean your cousin is the true culprit?

speaker: Levy
content: Hey, don't give me that doubtful look.

speaker: Levy
content: At first, I thought Chad hit me because he didn't like the way I talked to his dad, but I didn't know about the gun... What a shame, I've always spoiled that kid.
Hey, that's a little too much, drama queen.

speaker: Levy
content: If you can't tell how heartbroken I am, then at least look at my arm. Do you know how hard it's been to relieve myself in the past few days?
Levy swung his injured arm once again.
I've been shot by a gun before. No need to remind me of how it feels.

speaker: Levy
content: But Chad, my little nephew, he suffers worse pain. He has such a kind heart, but now he's been misled by his dad and his gang of so-called friends.

speaker: Levy
content: At first, I thought it was fine even if you wouldn't let me see him. A few days in the cell will help calm him down. At least he'll know he shouldn't act on impulse again.

speaker: Levy
content: But I swear I didn't know about this. Now if I don't go and have a chat with him, he may really cross into criminal territory.
It's very hard not to take your eagerness to see your nephew as a potential plan of revenge.
Or, as you've said, perhaps you want to use Chad to take revenge on his father.

speaker: Levy
content: But he's my family! Do you really not trust me?
I've looked into your background, which has led me to believe that you don't deserve my trust.
The people in your family took over your deceased parents' property when you were a teenager. But in just a few years, your family all either fled or died. Things didn't end up well for them.
Claiming someone is your family doesn't sound reassuring at all.

speaker: Levy
content: That hurts... And you can't be saying these things without proof. Rich folks like us are exposed to more threats. You can't just blame everything on me, it's unfair.

speaker: Levy
content: Moreover, my nephew... He's so young and innocent. I can't bear watching him misstep and become my cousin's hired gun.

speaker: Levy
content: I mean, Chief, isn't it your hobby to save poor Sinners from their plight? Or does my pitiful nephew not deserve your saving just because he's not a Sinner?
My saving? He's under no death threat.

speaker: Levy
content: Oh, of course, I know Chaddy's life's not in danger. It's only a metaphor.

speaker: Levy
content: But imagine, a young man trapped between his father and his uncle. His father has been teaching and forcing him to shoot his uncle. How will he know how to handle such a messed-up situation?

speaker: Levy
content: Now is probably the darkest moment of his life. He has no one to rely on, no one to listen to him. God knows what kind of despair he's in.

speaker: Levy
content: If I don't visit him and help him sort things out, he may just stray onto the wrong path and end up a scoundrel like me.
So far, we've found no evidence his father may have manipulated him to do it.

speaker: Levy
content: All the more reason to see him then. You won't make any progress if you don't ask him directly.

speaker: Levy
content: If you're that worried, why don't you come with me? Haven't you got the shackles? What can I do with that thing on me?

speaker: Levy
content: Aha, I know you're reasonable.
From what you know about Levy, he wants more than just to cheer his nephew up.
You're not someone who'd waste energy on something that doesn't benefit you... You're manipulative and vengeful, and you don't work for nothing. That's your style.

speaker: Levy
content: So, when are you gonna bail me out? I'm getting really bored at the Bureau.
Sorry, even as your uncle, I have no say over that. Even if we put aside the other crimes you've committed before...
female_content: Sorry, even as your uncle, I have no say over that. Even if we put aside the other crimes you've committed before...

content: Though no one was hurt, instigation of arson is a crime. I'll investigate whether you were involved in this. If that's the case, then you'll face a criminal charge way worse than Chad's.
Get ready to serve in the Bureau for the rest of your life, my good nephew.

speaker: Levy
content: Hahaha, you've really made progress with your sense of humor.
You come into the interrogation room. The young woman who is about to be interrogated is drumming her fingers on the armrest of her chair, impatience writ large on her face.
You put the evidence bag on the table. That's when her patience runs out.

speaker: Uni
content: I came all the way down here. And you locked me up in this messy room?

speaker: Uni
content: Sorry, but I don't have the time to tidy it up for you.
She sounds insincere and sardonic.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Nice to meet you, Uni.
You take a quick look around the room, with its spotless floor and walls and neatly arranged table and chairs. It could not, by any stretch of the imagination, be called messy.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Well, this is an interrogation room. I don't think we should make it fancy, as long as it fulfills its purpose.

speaker: Uni
content: This room lacks symmetry, is what I'm saying. The lighting, the furniture, even your haircut... It just makes my skin crawl.

speaker: Uni
content: Your eyes, though, are a different story. They're beautiful. Have you ever considered adjusting the other parts of your face to make them go better with those eyes?
The way she's looking at you...
It's an appraising look, as if you were a piece of furniture for sale. It has never left your face since you entered the room.

options: Are you speaking as a cosmetic surgeon?

content: Uni is a cosmetic surgeon who owns an underground clinic. She is little known by the general public, but well known in certain Eastside circles.
She may be one of the wealthiest doctors in all of Eastside. Rumor has it that in the past two years, her services have helped many people get on the fast track to stardom.

The cosmetic surgeon, who is now sitting in front of you, doesn't strike you as a go-getter who has made it. This might be attributable to the fact that she has an aura of sullenness, which is accentuated by the way she talks and her general attitude.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I hear you can change your clients' faces according to their exact requirements. With the right price, they can get a perfect new face that will catapult them into stardom and change their lives forever.

speaker: Uni
content: That's about the size of it. I have surgical skills, they have money. It's a two-way street. And it's fun to fulfill their so-called desire to advance with my hand.

speaker: Uni
content: It's a legit business. Are you interested, Chief?

options: It's your clients that I'm interested in.

speaker: Uni
content: My clients? They get a ticket to success for a reasonable price. If you think about it, it's quite a bargain for them.
Uni runs her appraising eyes from your chin to your lips, and finally to your eyes.

speaker: Uni
content: It's a win-win situation, really. I get paid, and my clients leave the clinic happy with their new looks.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Not all your clients, I'm afraid.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Some of them didn't get to leave.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Do you remember seeing these people?
