This explains why all the gangs are striving to come up with all sorts of plans and why they've become exceptionally active after discovering Golan's whereabouts.

speaker: Chief
content: But isn't it more dangerous to wander alone in Syndicate? Why not stay with the Iron Gang? At least you wouldn't have to face any threats alone.

speaker: Golan
content: Chief, this is not how you survive in Syndicate.

speaker: Golan
content: A living Sinner from a gang is much rarer than any resource or weapon. That's why from that day on, I became a moving target in the gang brawls who everyone wanted to test their strength with. The Iron Gang has never seen a peaceful day since.

speaker: Cub
content: Boss lady, this way! Please take a break here. I'll go and chase those guys away!

speaker: Golan
content: ...Don't go, Cub. We're better off hiding here. They'll give up sooner or later.

speaker: Cub
content: No way! They all think they're good enough to try us now. If we don't teach them a lesson, they won't stop pestering you!

speaker: Cub
content: Don't worry. You stay here. I'll handle it quickly.

speaker: Golan
content: At that time, every day was a struggle.

speaker: Golan
content: On one hand, I thought about how to use this new power to eliminate all of the Iron Gang's enemies. On the other hand, I was afraid. I feared that all the people I cared about would falter on the battlefield, that to protect one meant to sacrifice another...

speaker: Golan
content: I tried to become a proper heiress, but I failed. I neither had the resolve to kill nor was smart enough to solve problems otherwise.

speaker: Golan
content: In the end, all I brought to the family was trouble, and I made the Iron Gang an easy target for other gangs.

speaker: Fynn
content: Gradually, I began to want to escape... but every time I thought about running away, I felt extremely guilty. I even began to think if I hadn't taken that hit for Mom, I wouldn't have been in so much pain.

speaker: Golan
content: But when I snapped out of it, I felt like the most unforgivable scumbag in the world for having that thought.

speaker: Golan
content: Gaining such a formidable power should be a good thing. But why did it make me so sad...

speaker: Chief
content: That's why you moved into a rented home and tried to live like an ordinary person. That was the best solution you could think of to free you all.

speaker: Golan
content: Yes... I thought this would protect them, but I was too naive. I didn't know that those people wouldn't believe I had fled and would even use it as an excuse to provoke the Iron Gang.
Golan stops in her tracks, looking back. The small courtyard where she talked with Brenna is no longer visible, but she's still staring intently.

speaker: Golan
content: But I dare not go home, because I haven't gotten any stronger. In fact, no one expects anything of me. As long as I return, everyone will still do their best to protect me, just like what you heard a moment ago.

speaker: Golan
content: But... but every time I see the suppressed exhaustion in my mom, and the increasing injuries on Cub, Joy, and Sunny, I just can't face it...

speaker: Golan
content: Chief, am I in so much pain because I'm too weak?
Having spilled the deepest secret in her heart, Golan doesn't feel relieved. Instead, she feels overwhelmingly powerless.
This is the destination she wishes to reach, the home she wants to guard but finds no way to.
She may not have intended to confide in you, but the confession itself no doubt requires a great deal of trust. You want to do something in return for this precious trust.

speaker: Chief
content: If you no longer want to face this, the MBCC can take care of it. Solving the Mania weapon riot and retrieving Sinner Golan are two separate tasks. I can have someone take you back to the Bureau first, and then the MBCC will handle this gang fight.

speaker: Chief
content: If you want, this doesn't have to be your responsibility. Let it become the MBCC's job.
Your earnestness pays off. Golan's expression finally lightens a little.

speaker: Golan
content: Thank you, Chief. But no need.

speaker: Golan
content: I started this conflict, so I should also be the one to end it. I don't want so many people to die for me. I must repay my debt. I must help them.

speaker: Golan
content: Otherwise, even if I return to the MBCC, I will never find closure.
At last, guilt and indebtedness push her toward her lonely fight. This deepens your worry for her.

speaker: Chief
content: Then...
Boom!
A shoddy incendiary bomb blows off the low wall and instantly plunges the entire block into a sea of flames.
Golan watches it happen with a frown.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief! The situation has changed. The fight has escalated. Please retreat ASAP! Our team is breaking through the perimeter. A vehicle is waiting at the meeting point to pick up you and Golan.

speaker: Chief
content: Copy. Golan?
No response.
You turn around to see no one, only a slender figure advancing through the flames, eventually disappearing in the direction where the fight sounds the most chaotic.

Syndicate
Margaret Street
Iron Gang Territory
The already narrow street is now crowded with weapon-wielding thugs, all eyeing today's target with undisguised greed and ferocity.
Gangsters from various gangs have all assembled with their weapons, ready to go full force against the besieged Iron Gang. Finally, the long-brewed fight breaks out.

speaker: Cub
content: No good, boss, we're surrounded. All passages to Margaret Street are packed, and the underground exit has been barricaded.

speaker: Brenna
content: Cub! Go seal off the back alley. No one is allowed through.

speaker: Brenna
content: Everyone else, grab your toughest weapon and charge with me! Today we'll show them what you get when you come look for trouble on Iron Gang's turf!
Brenna leads her underlings forward. When the main target finally enters the scene, the mob immediately directs their firepower at the Iron Gang.

speaker: Joy
content: There's someone on the roof! Watch out for arrows! Send two guys after me upstairs to... Argh...

Attacks from the shadows prove far more efficient than direct confrontation. The Iron Gang has no choice but to switch to a defensive stance while their path gets hampered by stealthy attacks from the mob.
Gritting her teeth, Brenna manages to carve a bloody path through the brawl while protecting her people, yet she struggles to fend off the ambush.

speaker: Enemy Thug
content: Die! Let today be your death anniversary! Hahahaha...
A sneak arrow flies toward the woman who's resisting fiercely while being pinned down and unable to fend it off.
Just before the arrow hits her, it gets blocked by a mechanical parasol emerging out of nowhere and ricochets onto an enemy nearby.

speaker: Golan
content: Mom!! Are you hurt?

speaker: Brenna
content: I'm fine... Why are you here? I told you to leave!

speaker: Golan
content: I said I wouldn't run away this time. I never thought about abandoning everyone. I was just too naive before... But this time, I'd rather die fighting on this battlefield.

speaker: Brenna
content: ...And you're still naive now. Get over yourself. The Iron Gang can't possibly die out here.

speaker: Golan
content: I admit I'm naive. But dear boss Brenna, that naive girl has now saved you twice on two separate occasions!

speaker: Golan
content: If you still won't let me fight as part of the Iron Gang, then I'll just fight on my own against our common enemies. That way, you can't stop me!
Golan opens her parasol, and with a sweep of the tough canopy sends two reckless thugs out of the way with their screams.
Brenna stares at Golan next to her and suddenly realizes she seems to have grown taller.

speaker: Brenna
content: ...Alright. If you've come prepared, show me what you've got.

speaker: Golan
content: Let's do this together!
As the enemies turn on each other to seize Golan, the girl fights alongside her mother, ripping open a gap in this scorched iron barrel of a battlefield.
Golan's appearance enlivens everyone's morale, reversing the course of the previously losing battle.
Three months of training and the determination to protect her gang allow Golan to exceed her potential in this battle, seizing the attackers' attention.

speaker: Enemy Boss
content: Excellent! This is the weapon we need! She was completely clueless with her power before. I even planned to throw her into the underground arena for a couple of months to train her.

speaker: Enemy Boss
content: Now, it seems she has indeed become the finest weapon. My brothers! Whoever captures her today will never have to worry about money or status anymore!

speaker: Enemy Thug
content: Boss, no one dares to get close to her... We simply can't die our way through...

speaker: Enemy Boss
content: Are you ******* kidding me?! Bring out our Mania weapons!

speaker: Enemy Boss
content: It's a bit of a waste to use my treasured possessions on this lousy gang. But in exchange for a living Sinner, it'll be more than worth it, hahahaha!
When the enemies bring out the Mania weapons, Brenna's pupils shrink, and her underlings are petrified as if they're looking at a monster. Everyone instinctively looks toward Golan.

speaker: Brenna
content: Everyone!! Gather up!!
Golan tries to stay calm in the face of the Mania weapons, but her trembling hands betray her fear at that moment.

speaker: Enemy Boss
content: Do you bastards have some kind of special gene that turns you into Sinners? Let's do an experiment. See how many precious Sinners I'll get after wiping out the Iron Gang with these weapons!
The hysterical, bloodthirsty mad dogs raise their old weapons coated with Mania Crystals. Contamination immediately oozes out of them.

speaker: Brenna
content: Be careful, everyone! Panic will only benefit them. Stay calm and keep your guard up!

speaker: Sunny
content: Pro... Protect the boss! Let's fight them!

speaker: Joy
content: We can't let these scumbags hurt the boss and the boss lady!

speaker: Enemy Thug
content: ****, trying to run? You'll be the first then!
The Iron Gang underlings at the front simply cannot withstand the onslaught of the Mania weapons. Any resistance only leads to severe injuries under their power.
Once again shocked by the ruthless battlefield, Golan clenches her teeth to suppress her fear and charges with her parasol to the front to tackle the Mania weapon-wielding mad dogs.

speaker: Golan
content: Slow down! Get behind me! I'm a Sinner. Those things can't hurt me!
The taste of blood fills her mouth, but she still rushes over to put herself before Joy and Sunny, opening her parasol to block an attack.

speaker: Golan
content: Joy, take Sunny and run! She's too skittish for this. Take her somewhere safe! Now!
The remaining attackers block the way of all the Iron Gang members. She can withstand the Mania weapons, but she can't stop their detrimental impact on non-Sinners.
The Mania contamination makes the mad dogs even more frantic and the attackers even more reckless.
Golan tries her best to shield her comrades behind her, pointing the parasol at anyone trying to approach while struggling against the contamination of Mania radiation.

She seems unaccustomed to a battle of this scale. Having only had control over her Sinner abilities for a mere six months, Golan can do nothing but exhaust her power, unsure if she'll collapse the next second.

speaker: Joy
content: Boss lady... You must go now... Forget about us... This thing is too dangerous, you must take cover...

speaker: Golan
content: I won't leave you guys behind. Stay with me... Stay awake!

speaker: Joy
content: It seems... we really can't make it this time. You go first, we'll come right after you... Argh...

speaker: Sunny
content: Hurry up... Go, boss lady... It's too dangerous here...
The instant Golan is about to give in, the usually timid Sunny suddenly shoves her aside and headbutts the thug in front of her.

speaker: Sunny
content: Don't you dare... hurt... Golan!

speaker: Golan
content: Don't!
Not expecting someone to charge from under the Sinner's protection, the thug is caught off guard and stumbles back several steps. Sunny also faints from the strong impact.

When the thug recovers from the hit, he makes to pick up a brick and smash it on Sunny's head furiously. In that critical moment, Golan staggers over, grabs Sunny in her arms, and dodges the attack in a tumble.
The overwhelming impact blackens your vision, but you manage to save Golan and Sunny in your arms.

speaker: Golan
content: Cough... Cough cough... Chief... It's you?

speaker: Golan
content: Didn't I tell you not to come...

speaker: Chief
content: Your mother told you the same thing, didn't she? If this is how a Sinner from the Bureau behaves, don't expect their Chief to be any better.

speaker: Chief
content: Don't worry, I won't interfere with your decision. Consider me as... another party on the battlefield, handling things according to my own rules.

speaker: Chief
content: Come on, the Iron Gang's fight isn't over yet. Your important ones... still need your protection.
Golan gently settles the Iron Gang underling behind a barrier and immediately gets back up, gazing at the chaotic battlefield firmly.

speaker: Golan
content: I won't rely on others anymore... nor will I leave you guys behind... Not anymore... This time, I will hold on...
They have neither Mania weapons nor the same level of hysteria.
The Iron Gang is no match for those lunatics. The hysterical opponents no longer differentiate between friends or foes, beating any target they catch with a murderous intention.

speaker: Enemy Thug
content: Kill... Kill them!! Kill them all! Mine!! Weapons!! All mine!!!

speaker: Golan
content: Watch out!!!
In a flash, Golan opens her arms and protects a comrade. With no time to pick up her parasol, she instinctively holds her comrade in her arms, exposing her own back.
With a dull noise, the enemy's club hits her on the back of the head.
Golan's head swims. Weakness and rage take over her mind with a buzz as uncontrollable tears from the pain overflow from her eyes.
Seeing Golan take the hit, the thugs let go of the targets in their hands and all begin to close in on her.
Golan staggers to her feet just to see her subordinates desperately holding back the thugs to get them away from her, but they are soon knocked down by the bloodthirsty opponents.

speaker: Golan
content: Bastard!

Golan roars, her rage piercing the sky. Her sanity seems to have left her as she picks up whatever is next to her, a brick, a stick, an iron pipe, a broken knife... and throws them at the thugs while backing off.
She retreats to the side of the Iron Gang members, not letting the attackers come any closer to her comrades.

speaker: Golan
content: You're looking for the Sinner, aren't you? Come on then! All of you! Let's find out which one is the most powerful weapon, me or that piece of junk in your hands!

speaker: Golan
content: I won't let them sacrifice themselves for me. I'll make sure they all survive. You're the ones who should die. I'll take them home... Yes, home... Just like before... when I wasn't a Sinner... I'll never let you hurt my family again...

speaker: Golan
content: I've said I won't run away ever again... I won't let you succeed. I won't let the Iron Gang disappear. I'll win this fight. I'll beat all of you pieces of shit, *******...
Golan fights tirelessly, until her hands are covered in blood, yet she feels no pain. She has forgotten pain.

Her mother has fallen. So has Joy and all the young and old underlings who call her boss lady. It's almost her turn now. But not yet. She keeps struggling to stay on her feet, until she can't anymore...
The setting sun disappears behind the horizon and the afterglow colors the whole sky.
At last... Golan can't hold on any longer.

speaker: Enemy Boss
content: Yo-ho! Tie up all this garbage from the Iron Gang and take them away!

The attackers wave their flags as they plunder the spoils on the battlefield. Golan feels near-dead, but seeing them drag the barely alive members of the Iron Gang across the gravel path, she still tries with all her might to pick up the broken mechanical parasol and stagger over.

speaker: Golan
content: I've warned you! Don't...
Her labored effort is met with a crisp bullet. Blood immediately seeps out of her arm.
Whoosh!
The shackles emit a red glow. The mechanical parasol springs open with rage.
The already tattered canopy shoots a massive wave of energy at the enemies while the ribs expand into a transparent energy shield, guarding Golan and the Iron Gang behind it.
The attacking thugs are blown away by the sudden impact. Golan looks up and sees you standing beside her.

speaker: Chief
content: It's about time. Golan, you've done very well.

speaker: Chief
content: You've held on for a very long time, pushing beyond your limit... You're incredible.
Having held back her tears until now, Golan freezes for a moment, then bursts out crying upon realizing that the explosion of power was due to your use of the shackles.

speaker: Golan
content: ...Why? This isn't my power... This isn't my power!

speaker: Golan
content: Why... am I still so weak... In the end, I can only narrowly protect everyone relying on your power. It's true... I can't protect anyone at all...

speaker: Golan
content: I don't want to be... a damsel in distress who needs rescue all the time. I want to protect my important ones with my own hands. I don't want to rely on others!
Tears stream from Golan's red-rimmed eyes. She seems forever trapped in the walls that besiege her.

speaker: Chief
content: There's no shame in it. You did protect them with your own power.

speaker: Chief
content: Without your strong desire to protect your family, the shackles wouldn't have been able to summon the power within you. You own the power. The shackles are just a key to unlock it.

speaker: Golan
content: ...If it weren't for your shackles, I couldn't have done it.

speaker: Chief
content: No one is perfect or omnipotent in this world. You can't possibly solve every problem by yourself all the time, nor do you have to.

speaker: Chief
content: If you're not yet strong enough, gather all possible power to guard those you wish to protect. You can face it alone when you finally find enough strength in yourself.

speaker: Chief
content: Golan, do you wish to prove your strength, or to protect your family?

speaker: Golan
content: I want... to protect my family...

speaker: Chief
content: Then the method isn't so important, is it? I believe those you wish to protect would want to stand against the hardship together with you. Your mom... and your friends in the gang... They must want that, don't they?

speaker: Golan
content: I guess so...

speaker: Chief
content: So, Golan?

speaker: Golan
content: ...Yes?

speaker: Chief
content: This is a formal question: Do you require my assistance in this battle?
Tears once again stream down as Golan nods.

speaker: Chief
content: Warning! The Minos Bureau of Crisis Control is investigating a Mania weapon riot in this area. As the Chief of the MBCC, I now instruct you to put down your weapons and cooperate with the investigation.

speaker: Chief
content: Sinner Golan, according to the MBCC Sinner Management Regulations, you have violated the rules regarding public behavior and will soon be detained.

speaker: Chief
content: According to the DisCity Mania Weapon Control Act, individuals here involved in illegal possession and use of Mania weapons must also cooperate with the Bureau's interrogation.
Under the night sky, police lights surround the chaotic alley, casting bright colors onto the injured faces on the battlefield.

speaker: Enemy Thug
content: I have no idea about this riot or the Mania weapons... Who saw them? Did you see them?

speaker: Enemy Thug
content: Um... No...

speaker: Enemy Thug
content: Are these cops so bored they have to put on drama on the Iron Gang's turf at this hour... Do they want a proper fight with the Iron Gang or what?

speaker: Enemy Thug
content: I know... And isn't that girl from the Iron Gang the Sinner you're looking for? Take them all back. I bet they've got more of those hiding in the gang!

speaker: Enemy Thug
content: But that's the Iron Gang's heiress! If they let them whisk her away like that, it'll be a scandal for Iron Gang in the whole Syndicate!
Despite some of them constantly adding fuel to the fire, the gangsters here are all used to this kind of situation.

speaker: Chief
content: All related individuals, put down your weapons and cooperate with the investigation! As for Sinner Golan and those in possession of Mania weapons...

speaker: Golan
content: It's me.
Clack!
The warm-toned headlights shine deep into the crowd. At the end of the light beam, Golan drops the weapon in her hand, stretching her hands toward you in a gesture of surrender.

speaker: Chief
content: Sinner Golan has been captured. Next, the MBCC will conduct a rigorous search in this area for possession and use of Mania weapons. I encourage any individuals involved to turn yourselves in to the MBCC.

speaker: Enemy Boss
content: Damn... Did she just... get caught by the cops? Since when do they intervene in gang business?

speaker: Enemy Thug
content: What's going on? Is she outta her mind? Those two...
The arrest team captures Golan easily. The gangsters whisper among themselves as they see her walk toward the police car without looking back.
Two underlings run over to grab her.

speaker: Cub
content: Boss lady, wait... I'll go get the boss, she'll save you...! Just wait!

speaker: Joy
content: Boss lady, don't go... You promised to let me follow you wherever you go...

speaker: Golan
content: You guys better stop picking fights every day, or sooner or later you'll end up a Sinner like me, and then you'll meet me in the Bureau.

speaker: Sunny
content: Boss lady... don't leave me behind...

speaker: Golan
content: I'll come back to visit you when I have time... Now get going, won't you?!
The three of them linger on the spot. Golan turns back to look at the injured crowd of the Iron Gang.
At the forefront of the crowd, Brenna's still standing there, a relieved smile crossing her blood-stained face.
This is the most reassuring outcome her mother hopes to see.
In that moment, Golan understands her mother's past and present intentions. She turns to sit in the car.

speaker: Brenna
content: Did you all see that? The Sinner you were fighting over is no longer with the Iron Gang. From now on, I won't show any mercy to anyone coming at us.
As the car leaves the scene, Golan looks through the window at her mother's back. She seems to be shielding her from the thousands of enemies, all by herself.

speaker: Golan
content: It's different from what I imagined. I wasn't strong enough to protect my family on my own. But turns out, that's not too bad either. Maybe your method is indeed more effective...

speaker: Chief
content: Yes?

speaker: Golan
content: Even though in the end, I'm still a powerless deserter, at least I protected my family in this way, and... I feel more at ease than before.

speaker: Chief
content: You fled from your family, from the MBCC, and now from that battle all for one purpose: To protect the Iron Gang and not let your Sinner identity affect them. Even if it means giving up your status in the Iron Gang and becoming a traitor and a deserter. But you did it. And in doing so, you've proven your strength.

speaker: Chief
content: Moreover, as the war escalates, it'll only involve even more greedy violence and affect more innocent people. I guess that's not what you want to see. It's better to admit your own weakness and escape once and for all. Just leave the problem to someone stronger, like the MBCC.

speaker: Golan
content: Damn... I've never thought of that solution.

speaker: Golan
content: Uh... I mean, being Chief is really something else, huh? One moment you're strong, and the next you're weak. So what really am I?

speaker: Golan
content: Anyway... Thanks.

Two weeks after the heist
MBCC visitation room

speaker: Cub
content: I'll go first!

speaker: Joy
content: No, I'll go first.

speaker: Cub
content: No.

speaker: Joy
content: No, I'll go...

speaker: Golan
content: Alright! Just take turns and stop fighting!

speaker: Cub
content: Big news, boss lady!

speaker: Golan
content: What's wrong? Did those guys try to mess with us again?

speaker: Joy
content: No, they wouldn't dare anymore.

speaker: Cub
content: Right! Ever since you turned yourself in heroically that day, those losers started suspecting a trick. I mean, they can't believe a gangster would willingly go to the cops.

speaker: Joy
content: Then when they found out you could go on missions with the cops and come home from time to time, they became even more convinced... They now say you're playing both sides, dealing with the cops while bringing business to the Iron Gang... Who'd dare mess with someone like that?

speaker: Cub
content: As the story spreads... Nobody dares to come look for trouble anymore... Now those who knock on our door are looking to do business... We've in fact grown stronger than before!

speaker: Golan
content: Damn! I knew luck's always on the Iron Gang's side!
The visit ends, but Golan still has that silly happy look on her face. She doesn't even notice you walking past her.

speaker: Golan
content: Hehe, it's a bit bizarre, but I think I've gotten used to it.

speaker: Chief
content: What's bizarre?

speaker: Golan
content: It's just, inexplicable things tend to happen in our family.

speaker: Chief
content: Such as?

speaker: Golan
content: My ancestors were fishermen who sold fish for a living. But because the poker face ran in the family, someone got them into the debt-collecting business. That turned out well and business was good, so they gained some followers. Somehow, the group kept growing and eventually turned into a gang...

speaker: Golan
content: I thought that was the end of it... but then I got into the Bureau... and now they think I'm playing both sides and have protection from the cops? Wow, our family business is still going strong...

speaker: Chief
content: ...Tell Nightingale to arrange for more staff to monitor the Iron Gang's territory more closely.

speaker: Chief
content: Just to make sure their family business doesn't go too strong.
With a soft thud, you close the folder containing Dove's file and related information. The preliminary investigation has yielded so little information that you feel like you've read nothing at all.

speaker: Chief
content: I guess that's normal... Information on Outland Sinners has always been hard to come by. Looks like I'll have to wait for tomorrow's interrogation to learn more about her.
You set the reviewed documents aside, rubbing your fingertips together.
The flimsy file mirrors Dove herself. An innocent facade that somehow feels elusive and even a little off.

speaker: Dove
content: Yes, I am a Sinner, and yes, I forged the letters. Maybe you see that as an unforgivable crime...

speaker: Dove
content: But I really don't know anything about the Mania or any truth of this town! I have my own reasons for doing all this!
Reasons... You've heard all kinds of pretty excuses from people who wanted to justify their actions. You won't be fooled easily by her crude attempt at explaining away her deeds.
And yet... something about her tear-filled eyes lingers in your memory, leaving you with the nagging feeling that the pain glimpsed beneath the surface isn't entirely an act.
Could there really be some unknown motive behind her series of cruel deceptions in the town? Something you've yet to uncover?

speaker: Nightingale
content: Excuse me, Chief. We've just received a visit request for Sinner Dove.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Like the previous times... we need your response as soon as possible.
Nightingale's telling hesitation gives you a good idea of what to expect.
Taking the visit request form, you glance at it and find exactly what you expected. You can't help but let out a weary sigh.

speaker: Chief
content: ...The same person? I'll give him credit for being persistent.
You're too familiar with the name on the request form by now. The background check shows that he's a merchant who brokers deals between DisCity and Outlands and often travels in WhiteSands.

speaker: Chief
content: I hear he's been bragging at dinner parties about having found a new gold mine? Well, at least he knew better than to state his true purpose on the visit request.

speaker: Chief
content: Disasters and storms are common in WhiteSands, making regular electronic communication equipment highly vulnerable to damage. High-end devices are only affordable for the wealthy, so most people still rely on the old way to communicate: by mail.

speaker: Chief
content: He wants to exploit this situation by using a Sinner's abilities to forge letters and scam people... Should I call that gutsy or just shameless?

speaker: Nightingale
content: Sinner Dove's condition is stable and her special power is low-risk. And considering that her previous offenses didn't result in any serious harm, she's likely to be granted bail or at least permission to leave the Bureau.

speaker: Nightingale
content: The man must have noticed this and sees her as a money-making tool he can manipulate. That's why he wants to establish contact with Dove early, so he can put her to work the moment she's released on bail.
While Nightingale's deduction seems sound, you shake your head.

speaker: Chief
content: If this was truly just one merchant's scheme, it would be simple enough. We can just decline the request. But why would a mere merchant happen to know the exact details of a Sinner's special power...

speaker: Chief
content: And how convenient that this visit request, which normally requires multiple levels of internal approval, lands on my desk the day before her interrogation? Not to mention how brazenly he's advertising his intentions.

speaker: Nightingale
content: You mean to say... DisCity's higher-ups are involved, and this scheme to exploit a Sinner's powers for profit isn't just some merchant's random idea?

speaker: Nightingale
content: I understand now. I'll handle it appropriately. Would you like me to reschedule Dove's interrogation tomorrow?
You look at the visit request and Dove's file laid side by side before you, pause for a moment to think, then reach out to pile them into a single stack.
No doubt, this business plan isn't just illegal but is also morally reprehensible. Under normal circumstances, no amount of pressure could make you complicit in such corruption.

But this man has appeared at an almost perfect timing. His plausible yet sinister scheme bears some unexpected resemblance to Dove's own actions in Désir. Perhaps it could serve as a touchstone to reveal her true nature.

speaker: Chief
content: No need to change it. We'll proceed with the interrogation tomorrow as scheduled.

speaker: Dove
content: It's been a while, ${PlayerName}. You look so much more commanding than you did in Désir, and way cooler too... I almost didn't recognize you!
The girl taps the toes of her shoes against the floor and smiles modestly, her ever-present messenger bag resting on her knees pressed demurely together.

Truth be told, the farewell between you two in Désir was far from pleasant, which makes her current composure and friendliness seem oddly suspicious, like a carefully laid trap waiting for you to slip in.
But you're no longer the green interrogator you once were. In response to her calculated move, you reply calmly.

speaker: Chief
content: It's been a while, Dove. You... don't seem much different. I take it you're adjusting well to life at the Bureau?

speaker: Dove
content: Well... life in DisCity has turned out quite different than what I expected. It took some getting used to at first, but everyone's been so warm and kind to me. Thanks to them, I've really settled in.

speaker: Chief
content: That's good to hear. As it happens, I've just received a routine report from the Drifter Camp. It seems like the other folks from Désir are starting to settle in as well.

speaker: Chief
content: The authorities have provided basic necessities, but they need to be self-sufficient to truly survive. It also helps them break free from the false dreams certain individuals had once woven for them.

speaker: Dove
content: Drifter... Camp...? I didn't know such a place existed in DisCity. Though I'm not sure what it's like there, if you say so, ${PlayerName}, I can finally put my mind at ease.
Dove keeps her head tilted as she listens intently, and even as you make those pointed remarks, she merely pats her chest to show her relief.

speaker: Dove
content: As they say in the books, each new day brings a fresh start, and everything will get better. I believe that as long as everyone stays grounded, they'll find happiness. I'll be cheering for them here in the Bureau too!

speaker: Chief
content: Well, I've heard that while some people demanded to return to Désir and wanted their old lifestyle back at first, quite a few have found jobs now. They're truly making a fresh start.

speaker: Dove
content: That's wonderful! Everyone is so resilient and brave! As for those who are still reluctant... ${PlayerName}, could you give them more time? I believe they're not weak. They're just still processing everything.

speaker: Dove
content: Even I sometimes think back to my days as a mail carrier in Désir... After all, it was our shared home filled with so many wonderful memories together. ${PlayerName}, please be more patient with them, will you?

Her optimistic outlook and sincere concern reveal no cracks despite your probing words. To any observer, she would appear to be nothing more than a kind-hearted girl who gives everyone her unreserved support.
...Or rather, she's very good at playing such a character. Even though she knows you've seen her hidden side before, she's confident she can keep up the act. In that case...

speaker: Chief
content: Do you miss your days as a mail carrier in Désir? Even though Désir didn't have too many residents, constantly going back and forth delivering mail must have been quite demanding.

speaker: Chief
content: Looks like being a mail carrier gave you quite a sense of accomplishment. Is that why you can't seem to let it go?

speaker: Dove
content: Heh, ${PlayerName}, you've got that right. Though if I have to go into more detail, we may get sidetracked...

Your more direct question has been deflected effortlessly. The atmosphere shifts subtly yet suddenly, as if someone is gently tightening the very trap you've stepped in, snickering at the capture of their prey.
Dove's smile fades as her voice grows soft and slow, as if preparing to tell you a tale from long ago.

speaker: Dove
content: Actually, my parents were mail carriers too. Ever since I was little, I watched them work tirelessly delivering mail for everyone back in our hometown.

speaker: Dove
content: I was born far from DisCity, in a remote village. Back home, resources were scarce and everyone was poor. We were constantly plagued by all sorts of disasters.

speaker: Dove
content: Even basic survival depended on messengers like my parents, who kept communication flowing throughout the community... As for me, being a sickly child, I was mostly confined to our home.

speaker: Dove
content: Sounds kinda sad, doesn't it? But I never felt that way at all! My parents would bring back books and stories from the outside world, so I could explore it myself through text, even when I couldn't leave home.
She straightens her posture and meets your gaze, her eyes showing just the right amount of determination.

speaker: Dove
content: They taught me that mail could spread knowledge and communicate human emotions. It carries thoughts and hopes, connecting separated souls, villages, and cities across vast distances.

speaker: Dove
content: Being a mail carrier is a noble calling. That's why I always dreamed of becoming one just like my parents.

speaker: Dove
content: E-even though delivering mail meant facing countless dangers, even attacks from monsters...
She lowers her head, her body and voice trembling slightly as if recalling the pain once inflicted upon her.

According to the infirmary's report, the Mania contamination in Dove's body does match the characteristics of a Corruptor infection. So far, she doesn't seem to be lying, but this only makes that weird sense of inconsistency you feel from her even more inexplicable.

speaker: Chief
content: I can see being a mail carrier means a great deal to you. Actually, what I wanted to discuss today is related to your work...

speaker: Chief
content: Someone wants to bail you out and hire you as a mail carrier on the Outland routes... You'd be happy to accept the offer, wouldn't you?
You nod with feigned understanding, casually mentioning the merchant's visit as bait while carefully observing Dove's reaction.
Sure enough, Dove's dejected expression instantly vanishes, her pupils dilating with joy as if what she's just heard is too good to be true.

speaker: Dove
content: ...Really? Can I? Yes, of course I'd love to accept it! I'll work hard to be a good mail carrier and deliver letters to everyone, just like I did in Désir!

speaker: Dove
content: This is what I learned from my parents! They passed this noble calling on to me, and I won't let them down!
Her eyes sparkle with anticipation as she instinctively clutches her messenger bag. Her words overflow with genuine admiration and respect for both her parents and the profession.

In Désir, she was equally inseparable from her messenger bag, which you know was filled with intercepted letters she opened without permission. They were both evidence of her forgeries and a symbol of the trust she betrayed.
Indeed, Dove's enthusiasm seems genuine, as does her devotion to letters, and that's precisely what contradicts her actions in Désir. Unless... A theory begins to form in your mind.

speaker: Chief
content: You seem so excited. I wonder if it's because you can return to your profession and fulfill your noble calling... or because you can go back to deceiving more people with forged letters?

speaker: Dove
content: ...I knew it. Even if you didn't bring it up at first, you still remember what happened. You still think I'm just a dishonest, bad person.
Dove flinches at your pointed question, but quickly straightens up and meets your gaze with determined resolve.

speaker: Dove
content: But... back then in Désir, I truly didn't know what else I could do. I just wanted to protect everyone's feelings from the cruel reality...

speaker: Dove
content: I know what I did might be wrong, but I was just trying to do what my parents taught me, to help everyone live better lives by delivering heartfelt messages. If I have to pay the price for that... then so be it.
In the interrogation room, her desperate defense trails off into a heavy silence charged with emotion. The girl lowers her gaze hopelessly, waiting quietly for your response.
But unfortunately for her, you won't give her the sympathy and leniency she's fishing for.

speaker: Chief
content: Dove, the very act of forging letters contradicts your claims about a mail carrier's duty of delivering heartfelt messages. No amount of glorification will change that fact.

speaker: Chief
content: I think... you've told me all this just to win my sympathy and absolve yourself of your crimes.

speaker: Dove
content: No, that's not it... I'm not lying, I swear I'm not!
As if shocked by your ruthless words, Dove's face crumples with hurt as her eyes instantly well up with tears, glistening in the light.

speaker: Chief
content: Just now, you described Désir's situation as the cruel reality, which shows you were somewhat aware of the truth behind, or at the very least, you knew its condition was deteriorating.

speaker: Chief
content: But you didn't expose the truth to give the others a chance to escape, nor did you follow Vautour Bleu's example of believing in and protecting this illusion until the very end...

speaker: Chief
content: You were simply being a bystander who took no active action. Don't you see how that contradicts the image you've been trying to craft for yourself: someone sincere, kind, and strong?

speaker: Dove
content: No, you're wrong! ${PlayerName}, I know you've been prejudiced against me ever since that day... but why must you think of me as such a terrible person?
Her meek expression cracks momentarily, but she quickly masks it with a show of panic and hurt. Seeing her still adamantly denying everything, you decide to approach this from a different angle.

speaker: Chief
content: In Désir, you voluntarily took up the role of a mail carrier. Just now, you were happy to be able to deliver mail again. You said it was because that job brings hope to everyone.

speaker: Chief
content: You didn't hesitate to violate your code of conduct and deliver fake letters in order to protect the townsfolk's feelings. In other words, you're saying you were willing to do something wrong because it was for their own good.

speaker: Dove
content: Yes, it pained me to... forge those letters too. If I hadn't seen everyone's smiling faces when delivering the mail, I couldn't have kept going... What's... what's wrong with that?

speaker: Choice
options: No, there's nothing wrong with that.

speaker: Chief
content: Delivering mail does let you get close to the recipients and see their joy firsthand. For you... that meant watching them continue to believe in you and the beautiful dream you'd woven.

speaker: Chief
content: But for someone as kind as you, when you saw their smiles from the false hope given by you, did you never once think about what would happen when their dreams finally shattered?
Dove opens her mouth to explain, but after several failed attempts, she falls silent. You seize this moment to elaborate on your theory.

speaker: Chief
content: Maybe you never considered the consequences, or you did but chose to ignore them. Either way, that was not the behavior of an honorable messenger who would violate her own principles for the sake of people's trust and happiness.

speaker: Chief
content: Which means your true motive for creating and delivering these fake letters is questionable.

speaker: Dove
content: W-what other motive could I have? What could I possibly gain from this?

speaker: Chief
content: True, you might not have gained any material benefits from this. But what if your satisfaction was purely psychological?

speaker: Chief
content: For instance, many compulsive liars simply enjoy the sense of superiority that comes from deceiving others. They revel in watching their victims fall from grace, finding pleasure in their pain and suffering. It makes them laugh with delight.

speaker: Dove
content: ${PlayerName}, is this really how you see me... Why?
Her hurt expression is so innocent, but you remain unmoved.

speaker: Chief
content: I'm simply trying to find a motive that fits your actions. If deceiving people with fake letters wasn't your means to an end, but the end itself, then it explains everything.

speaker: Chief
content: Your real motive for becoming a mail carrier was simply this: to deceive the townsfolk with fake letters, reinforce their fantasies, and ensure their suffering would be even greater when the town finally collapsed, all while securing a front-row seat to watch it unfold, wasn't it?
Having laid out your final conclusion, you watch Dove intently, studying every nuance of her expression and reaction.

speaker: Chief
content: Even an S-Class Sinner wouldn't have been able to maintain Désir's facade forever. You knew that all along, didn't you?

speaker: Chief
content: But knowing it would all come crashing down, you still delayed people's escape, sabotaged others' efforts, and kept them trapped on a sinking ship.

speaker: Chief
content: Pure altruism alone can't explain your contradictory actions, but one mixed with ill intentions can. Unless you have an even deeper, more compelling reason that might convince me?
You deliberately pause here, giving Dove time to think. You are indeed anticipating a better explanation or a more convincing reason she might have to justify her actions.

speaker: Dove
content: ...Yes, you're right! I forged those letters for my own pleasure. I just loved watching those pathetic weaklings succumb to my lies.
But in the end, all you get is the shattering of her gentle, harmless facade. All her carefully hidden thorns now point directly at you.

speaker: Dove
content: Oh, how very smart you are! Yes, your guess is exactly right! You've got your answer! Are you satisfied now? Should I give you a prize, great Chief of the wonderful DisCity?
Her long-suppressed emotions explode in a torrent of bitter mockery. She fixes you with a look both defiant and sneering, having completely abandoned her pretense.

speaker: Chief
content: Satisfaction isn't what concerns me. What I want to know is why you did this. What could you gain from it?

speaker: Dove
content: Ha! You want to know why I deceived others? Because I was the one who was lied to first! My parents lied to me. They promised they'd come back, but they abandoned me and died delivering mail!

speaker: Dove
content: All that talk about being needed by everyone. They were both liars. They died for nothing! The villagers were all spineless cowards who only wanted to hear good news. No one even cared if anything was real or fake!

speaker: Dove
content: They treated my parents' deaths like some kind of joke. They even kept me in the dark while shamelessly forging letters in my parents' voices, trying to get me to tell them where our money was hidden!

speaker: Dove
content: They destroyed my trust and trampled on my dream. All I did was write a few fake letters to get back at them. Merciful enough, wasn't I?
Like a dam breaking, she pours out all the truths about her past that she had kept hidden. Having nothing left to lose, she admits to all your accusations without further denial.

speaker: Chief
content: But from what you're saying, all of this happened before you came to Désir. The townsfolk there had nothing to do with it.

speaker: Dove
content: True, they had nothing to do with it. But they have no one to blame but themselves, for they were as blind as those villagers, failing to see what was right in front of them!

speaker: Dove
content: This is WhiteSands we're talking about. How could they possibly get replies so quickly? And the envelopes and paper always looked the same, arriving perfectly intact! Yet they still bought it. What does that tell you?

speaker: Dove
content: It proves that those people in Désir wanted to be fooled! They were the ones clinging to the lies, refusing to wake up. They didn't care if the letters were real. They just wanted to comfort themselves with falsehood!
A contemptuous smirk curls her lips as her voice grows as cold and heavy as the night of WhiteSands.

speaker: Dove
content: You see? No one cared if the letters were fake. All everyone ever cares about is themselves. It's the same in my hometown, Désir, or anywhere else. So I didn't do anything wrong. What could I possibly have done wrong?
Beneath her cracked facade, you see a shattered core like a burnt-out firepit. It's as cold and lifeless as her voice now.

Others' contempt shattered Dove's fantasy of the messenger's job. She began using fake letters both for revenge and to test people, until each successful deception trapped her deeper in the pessimistic cycle.
Faced with Dove's mocking expression, you find yourself at a loss for words.

speaker: Chief
content: So, what you've said earlier, about your devotion to being a mail carrier, was that all just a lie too?

speaker: Dove
content: It was real once, but not anymore. I'm not foolish enough to be deceived twice.

speaker: Chief
content: So you didn't mean it when you said you were willing to take up the job as a mail carrier on bail on the Outland routes?

speaker: Dove
content: What kind of question is that?

speaker: Dove
content: Unless I can go back to fooling those gullible idiots with fake letters, I refuse to waste my life like my parents did on such a thankless job!
Dove remains contemptuous, her refusal unwavering. But you've already prepared your next move for exactly this kind of response.

speaker: Chief
content: Oh? As it happens, a like-minded merchant has just requested to see you. He wants to use your skills to forge letters and sell them to Outlanders for profit.

speaker: Chief
content: Isn't this exactly what you're looking for? In that case, I'll arrange a meeting for you.

speaker: Dove
content: ...I've been perfectly honest with you, and this is your answer? Aren't you supposed to be the good guy, the hero Chief of DisCity?
Now it's Dove's turn to study you with suspicion, trying to guess your true intentions. But you simply meet her gaze calmly, letting her distrustful eyes pass over you.
Though Dove presents herself as a hopeless nihilist, you know that for a dream to shatter, it must first have existed. Moreover, the way she spoke about her parents shows that she still cares.
Perhaps that shattered dream can still move her. You're not ready to pass your final judgment yet. You hope this merchant might be the fuel needed to reignite the dying embers in her heart.

speaker: Dove
content: Hmph, I can't tell what exactly you're up to, but if it involves delivering mail...
She blinks, her suspicious expression vanishing as she puts on her sweet innocent smile once more.

speaker: Dove
content: Ahem... then I would be more than happy to help, Chief.

speaker: Merchant
content: Oh, Chief of the MBCC, it's a pleasure to meet you. It's been no easy feat to secure an audience with you.

speaker: Chief
content: Given the special status of Sinners, our visit approval process must be stringent. This is for the protection of both parties involved. I trust you understand.
In the meeting room, the merchant brazenly scrutinizes both you and Dove, behaving so arrogantly that he's barely trying to hide the powerful connections backing him.

Whatever this merchant and his backers might be plotting, he does have legitimate trading credentials in WhiteSands, and the background check confirms his extensive knowledge of Outlands' current situation and trade networks.

speaker: Merchant
content: And this must be... Miss Dove?

speaker: Dove
content: Hello, sir. I'm Dove. It's a pleasure to meet you.

speaker: Merchant
content: Young, pretty, and obedient. Perfect. In our line of work, trustworthiness is key, and a young lady like yourself... Tsk tsk, you'll be quite a valuable asset.

speaker: Merchant
content: Your Chief must have already briefed you about why I'm here, yes?
Under his appraising gaze sizing her up like merchandise, Dove shows not the slightest hint of displeasure, the perfect curve of her smile never faltering.

speaker: Dove
content: Yes, Chief has already told me. Actually, this is my first time meeting someone like yourself, a big-time trader who works across WhiteSands and Outlands.

speaker: Dove
content: Before meeting you, I was worried I might be unqualified. Someone like me who knows nothing other than delivering mail... could I really be of any help to you?

speaker: Merchant
content: Haha, you sure are humble! Miss Dove, you're quite different from your Chief here. You're very pleasant and down-to-earth.
Dove's practiced flattery has the merchant beaming with satisfaction. He nods approvingly, his tone growing even more pompous.

speaker: Merchant
content: No need to sell yourself short. You might think delivering mail is just a trivial job, but that's because you don't know the inner workings. In today's market, there's quite a profit to be made there.

speaker: Dove
content: Really? I'm afraid I don't quite understand... I know so little about business matters...

speaker: Merchant
content: Ah, you'll understand once I explain! I'm confident this business of mine will interest you, as long as you don't have... other reservations!
The merchant shoots you a meaningful glance. Rather than a mere suggestion, it's an unmistakable warning forbidding your intervention.
You smile back at him, pretending not to have noticed his boastful attitude.

speaker: Chief
content: My duties require me to be present throughout your meeting, but within reasonable bounds, I will respect Dove's personal choices.

speaker: Merchant
content: Well, it'd be fantastic if you could keep your word, Chief.

The merchant doesn't hide his distrust of you and the Bureau, attempting to drive a wedge between you and Dove. But this plays right into your hands. You'd be even more pleased if he could be more blatant.
After all, you've brought Dove here just so the merchant can provoke her with his contemptible arrogance, to stir whatever spark of the messenger dream that might still remain in her heart.
You don't think that Dove has chosen to stay in this profession after all her disillusionment purely out of malice and vengeance. The merchant is simply your pawn in this psychological gambit.

speaker: Dove
content: Chief ${PlayerName} is very kind, and we Sinners all trust him. If I have to make any decisions, I should certainly consider his opinion!
female_content: Chief ${PlayerName} is very kind, and we Sinners all trust her. If I have to make any decisions, I should certainly consider her opinion!

speaker: Merchant
content: Consider his opinion? Hah! I'm afraid your Chief knows nothing about business!
female_content: Consider her opinion? Hah! I'm afraid your Chief knows nothing about business!

content: Whether or not Dove perceives the hidden agendas between you and the merchant, she maintains her gentle yet firm demeanor as she steps in to smooth over the tension.
Oblivious to your true relationship with Dove, the merchant grows agitated at her convincing display of loyalty. He waves his hand dismissively, eager to regain control of the conversation.

speaker: Merchant
content: Let me tell you something: you don't realize how much sway DisCity holds in Outlands and WhiteSands unless you're a businessman!

speaker: Dove
content: Hmm... I've read in books that DisCity has brought hope for humanity's survival. That's why many people in Outlands look up to its prosperity.

speaker: Merchant
content: Oh, they don't just look up to it! Those country bumpkins from Outlands would risk their lives just to sneak into DisCity!
Frustrated by Dove's naivety, the man decides to spell things out.

speaker: Merchant
content: But those backwaters are dirt poor and isolated. Some of these so-called cities can't even match up to a satellite town of DisCity! Things like personal devices, internet... Tsk, they've got none of those!

speaker: Merchant
content: They still rely on people running around on foot to deliver messages. These so-called mail carriers... belong in a history textbook if you ask me! If they want to know what's happening in the outside world, they can only rely on merchant caravans like ours!

speaker: Merchant
content: Sometimes we do help deliver mail on the side. But who'd want to waste time tracking people down and delivering these trivial messages? Hah! It's not worth the costs even for those expensive handicrafts! That being said...
He pauses deliberately, giving Dove a chance to fill in. Playing along, she claps her hands with an expression of sudden realization and chimes in excitedly.

speaker: Dove
content: If I could use my ability to forge reply letters... we could easily trick them into supplying us with these handicrafts and make a fortune!

speaker: Merchant
content: Hmm, you're quite sharp. It's always a joy to talk to someone with business acumen. So you get it now, right? If you work for me, all you'll need to do is write a few letters. No need to wear yourself out delivering mail.

speaker: Merchant
content: I've seen plenty of fools risk their lives on their mail routes through WhiteSands. Some of them never made it back alive. I'm known for taking good care of my staff, and I won't let you do anything that stupid.

speaker: Dove
content: After all, one doesn't meet someone with your insight and vision every day, sir.

speaker: Dove
content: All it takes is forging a few letters. It's a great way to save costs and avert risks. If someone else had thought of such a brilliant method, they would've made a fortune off the Outlanders by now.
Her flattery really strokes the merchant's ego. He clears his throat before correcting Dove in a pretentiously serious voice.

speaker: Merchant
content: That's not all! Don't forget about all those village chiefs in Outlands! These leaders also have to spend money on our good news just to keep their ignorant masses happy!

speaker: Merchant
content: Letters may be old-fashioned, but they have their uses! They're tangible proof, and word spreads quickly through a village! Sign one off with someone's relative's name and you've got the whole village fooled!

speaker: Dove
content: I see, you are really well-versed in this subject. I totally overlooked that. Since letters are so valuable, shouldn't we charge down payments from those Outlanders?

speaker: Dove
content: And after they pay us, we'll promise to deliver letters regularly! That way we can easily cut and run whenever we want! I mean, even if we don't... who knows how long these Outland villages will even last?

The two discuss their schemes enthusiastically as if you weren't there. You observe silently as their conversation sinks deeper into moral depravity, crossing one line after another, yet Dove seems perfectly at ease with it.
What you see makes you question your judgment. Were you wrong from the start? Is there even any point in trying to test Dove's true nature?

speaker: Merchant
content: Exactly! It's almost like these Outlanders are delusional! They're just a bunch of lowlifes who might not even live long, yet they dare to dream about living in DisCity, chasing their ridiculous DisCity dream!

speaker: Merchant
content: Haha, do they really think they deserve it? The DisCity dream belongs to us, the people of DisCity. Only businessmen like us who profit off Outlands deserve to be real idealists!

speaker: Merchant
content: Those Outlanders should be grateful we let them be DisCity's cash machine!

speaker: Dove
content: ...You're absolutely right, sir.

Dove keeps smiling and agreeing with the merchant's increasingly outrageous statements, though her enthusiasm has notably dimmed. The merchant remains pleased, making a show of modesty with a wave of his hand while barely containing his smugness.

speaker: Merchant
content: Miss Dove, you're smart enough to know how to play the game. I can tell we're going to have a wonderful partnership!

speaker: Merchant
content: Tell you what, I've been wanting to get into this business for a while now. I've tried working with some local messengers before... but they were all too rigid and frankly just dumb! No wonder Outlanders are dirt poor!

speaker: Dove
content: ...Did they all decline your offer?
You might be imagining it, but Dove's voice is sounding a bit tremulous. Yet when you pick up on this subtle change and turn to look at her face, you find only her usual radiant smile.

speaker: Merchant
content: You bet they did! Every single one of them spouted nonsense about their duty and code of conduct and all that... like writing a few fake letters would kill them. A messenger's professionalism? Can you eat that? Does it pay?

speaker: Merchant
content: I met this idiot in WhiteSands once. Now that was memorable. Half of this messenger's body was already buried in the sand, yet he was still grabbing at me. What did he say again...

speaker: Merchant
content: Oh! He was telling me not to worry about him, he was dying anyway, and just take the letters and deliver them... What else? Oh right, he said the whole village was waiting for this letter that could save lives.

speaker: Dove
content: ...So, did you end up delivering that poor soul's letter, sir?

speaker: Merchant
content: Like I would! I just walked away. He kept calling out and begging until I couldn't hear him anymore! Hah, it was so stupid it made me laugh. Their whole village wasn't worth half of the deal I just made.

Perhaps emboldened by your silence or pleased by Dove's apparent approval, the merchant grows increasingly unrestrained, his gaping mouth spewing nothing but selfishness and greed he takes such pride in.

speaker: Merchant
content: A month later when I passed by again, there wasn't a single living person left in that town! You know, I kinda regret just walking away like that. I should've looted whatever valuables were left!
The merchant's cruel laughter bounces around the meeting room like a dropped ball that no one moves to catch, echoing until it finally sinks into dead silence.

The person who has been playing along and catching the ball this whole time suddenly falls silent, head bowed. You instinctively turn to Dove, and this time you see her clenched fists trembling uncontrollably.

speaker: Dove
content: How dare you... How dare you?!

speaker: Merchant
content: Wahhhh!

Raw, unbridled rage surges through the other end of the shackles, so intense it makes your breath catch. The Sinner's rage, suppressed throughout the entire conversation, has finally reached its breaking point. She's about to lose control!

Countless letters shoot out of her messenger bag, sweeping through the meeting room like a hurricane. The swirling letters overturn the desk and chairs, then, at their master's command, all aim at the man cowering on the floor!

speaker: Dove
content: How dare you look down on that messenger?! How dare you call him stupid?! Do you really think everyone is as greedy, shameless, vicious, and cold-blooded as you?!

speaker: Dove
content: People... scum like you shouldn't be allowed to exist in this world!

speaker: Chief
content: Dove, stop! You can't lose control again!
But Dove, consumed by rage, pays no heed to your intervention, only inching closer toward the merchant.
If she actually harms him, as a Sinner, who is already in a precarious position, she will suffer irreversible consequences. You must stop Dove before she completely loses control.

speaker: Dove
content: Let go of me! Let, nngh...!
Crimson thorns pierce through her fragile frame, but Dove, usually submissive to the shackles, now erupts with a burst of powerful resistance.
To prevent Dove from breaking free, you're forced to unleash the shackles once more. This time, with your firm determination, you finally seal away her special power with the shackles.

speaker: Dove
content: You money-grubbing scum! You're nothing but a parasite feeding off people's hard-earned savings!

speaker: Dove
content: How dare you look down on that messenger who sacrificed his life for his duty! How dare you open your filthy mouth to judge all the messengers who deliver hope to everyone!

speaker: Merchant
content: Ahhh, stay back! Don't come near me!!! Guards! Where are the guards?!

speaker: Dove
content: Drop the act! You're nothing but a cowardly, greedy cockroach obsessed with forgery. You make me sick just looking at you!

Without her special power, Dove is just a frail girl who cannot break free from your restraint. All she can do is let out a barrage of furious screams that tears through the air and through her mask of gentle grace.

speaker: Dove
content: Messengers... are people who deliver emotions and connect souls. Any one of them is a hundred times more noble than you!

speaker: Dove
content: Calling yourself an idealist... Don't you dare sully that word!
Surging rage twists Dove's delicate features as her words, sharp as needles, seem to pierce not only the merchant but herself as well.
After that, she falls silent, though her chest still heaves heavily. Through the shackles, you sense the undisguised turmoil of emotions, and your suspicions are finally confirmed.
For all her apparent indifference, a small flame of her dream still burns within Dove's heart, even if she refuses to acknowledge or face it.

speaker: Merchant
content: Huff... huff... Well, well! So this is how the Bureau manages its Sinners?! What were you thinking, letting this unstable monster meet with me?!
The merchant finally snaps out of his shock, jumping up and venting his terror and rage. Still trembling with fear, he only dares to accuse you both while standing behind the couch.

speaker: Chief
content: I deeply regret this incident. As Chief, I take full responsibility, and according to the Bureau's regulations, Sinner Dove will be placed under confinement.

speaker: Merchant
content: Confinement? She just attempted murder and you're only locking her in a cell?! First you failed to protect your business partner's life, and now you're covering for the culprit?!
You cut him off firmly.

speaker: Chief
content: Allow me to correct you, sir. You've misunderstood something. Dove will be disciplined for acting without permission. It has nothing to do with whether or not you were her target.

speaker: Chief
content: Furthermore, I never promised you any business cooperation. The Bureau has no interest in dealing with a businessman who discriminates against Outlanders and runs illegal operations like yourself. Nightingale, please escort the gentleman out.
Ignoring the merchant's reaction, you use your communicator to summon Nightingale waiting outside.

speaker: Merchant
content: Hey, don't forget who sent me here! Don't get too big-headed just because you're Chief. You should know your place...

speaker: Nightingale
content: Sir, visit time is over. Please come with me. I'll show you the way out of the Bureau.
You've heard such threats countless times before, and your capable adjutant will handle them appropriately. Leaving the merchant's empty threats behind, you lead Dove out of the meeting room.
On the way to the confinement cell, she follows you in unusual silence, head bowed and completely docile.

speaker: Chief
content: I thought you said idealism was dead and pointless. Deceiving others with forged letters to feed your vanity and sense of superiority, isn't this the way of life you've chosen?

speaker: Chief
content: If that's the case... why did you get so worked up? Where did this rage come from? You know that for a Sinner, negative emotions are both a source of power and a poison that corrupts the body and soul, don't you?
You speak at a measured pace, but the questions you've thrown at Dove are like stones dropped into a bottomless pit. You don't hear a single echo, even as you reach the confinement cell.

speaker: Choice
options: It's okay if you don't have the answers now.

speaker: Chief
content: After all, I guess you're not sure either. Perhaps some alone time will give you a chance to think these questions through.

speaker: Dove
content: ...Wait!
Having kept her silence all this time, Dove finally calls out to stop you. You turn around and wait for her question, but what she says at last seems both relevant and irrelevant at the same time.

speaker: Dove
content: I offended the guest and caused such a mess... Is this really it? Just confinement?

speaker: Chief
content: According to the regulations, this is sufficient punishment for a single instance of rash behavior. Sticking to the rules is my duty as Chief.

speaker: Dove
content: Regulations? Duty? You talk about these things, but do you think that bastard will care about any of that? Aren't you afraid he'll...

speaker: Chief
content: I will act according to my principles. As for whether others follow them or not, that's beyond my control and won't affect my decisions.
She falls silent and walks into the confinement cell of her own accord. You close the door and turn to leave, but you can feel her lingering gaze following you.
Life in the Bureau runs like a train on its predetermined tracks. Most days are regular and uneventful.
After doing her confinement time, Dove returns to her room and resumes her normal life. No one approaches her about the incident again or demands she face any additional consequences.

Chief's special attention also fades away with those consequences. In the bustling Bureau, that day's events were nothing more than sparks ignited on the tracks when a train rounds a bend, deserving no one's special notice.
The pages of her life don't cease turning. She follows a routine, reads books she never had access to before, and occasionally, when the mood strikes her...

speaker: Dove
content: Oh, don't sigh like that. I read that it may drive good luck away. If something's bothering you... I'm all ears. Don't worry, it'll be our little secret!

speaker: Dove
content: You can't tell that Sinner you admire her because you're staff... Why not try writing a letter? You don't have to put your name in it. If your feelings are sincere, it'll surely move her!

speaker: Dove
content: Would you like me to deliver your letter? It's no trouble at all. No, thank you for trusting me! Just wait here, I'll make sure to bring back a reply...
Dove waves goodbye with a smile, her skirt billowing as she turns the corner. But instead of going to her supposed destination, she heads straight to her own room.
The moment the door closes, she instantly wipes the smile from her face and casually tosses the letter onto her desk.

speaker: Dove
content: It's just another boring letter, but I suppose it's better than nothing. Now, how should I respond to this admiration in the idol's voice...
She smooths out the paper and envelope with practiced ease, taps the pen against her lips for a moment pensively, then, having made up her mind, slowly lowers the nib...

speaker: Dove
content: You're nothing but a cowardly, greedy cockroach obsessed with forgery. You make me sick just looking at you!

speaker: Dove
content: Messengers... are people who deliver emotions and connect souls. Any one of them is a hundred times more noble than you!
A drop of ink drips from her idle pen, blooming into a dark stain on the blank paper. The sudden invasion of memories grips her wrist like a vice, making it impossible for her to start writing.
...It happens again. After struggling briefly, Dove lets out a resigned sigh, puts down her pen, and crumples the ink-stained paper before tossing it into the corner.
Though Dove has been trying her hardest to avoid remembering that day, she knows she can't run away from these memories.

speaker: Chief
content: I thought you said idealism was dead and pointless.

speaker: Chief
content: If that's the case... why did you get so worked up? Where did this rage come from?

speaker: Dove
content: Yeah, why? Why don't you tell me? Why should I know?

She seems to be speaking both to someone in her memories and to herself. The question that has been haunting her all this time resurfaces, tearing her between conflicting thoughts until she's left completely at a loss.

speaker: Staff Member
content: Really? You'll do that? Thank you! Thank you so much! I had no idea being a mail carrier was such a noble profession... You've really helped me out of a tough spot!

speaker: Staff Member
content: I don't think this job exists in DisCity anymore. Isn't it some kind of ancient occupation? Oh, sorry, I must sound really ignorant... I'll make sure to learn more about it!

speaker: Dove
content: A noble... profession...
Perhaps the letters she always carries with her are guiding her, or perhaps the girl's gratitude has stirred something deep within her heart.
By the time Dove snaps out of it, she's already cleared away the envelopes and paper meant for forged letters, leaving only fresh blank sheets waiting silently on her desk.

speaker: Dove
content: Could this be... an answer?

The girl stares down at the blank paper that seems to be both guiding and questioning her, hesitating for a long while. Slowly, the intermittent scratching of her pen breaks the silence as more and more crumpled drafts gather at her feet.
After countless revisions, the neat and firm writing finally appears on the envelope...

speaker: Dove's Letter
content: "To Mom and Dad"
She draws in a deep breath and, mustering her courage, picks up her pen.

speaker: Dove's Letter
content: You'll never guess where I'm writing this letter—DisCity. But it's really not that fancy of a place. There's this Bureau here, and their Chief is kind of a control freak who can be mean to me sometimes, calling me a liar.

speaker: Dove's Letter
content: Although... fine, that's the truth! But did he have to point it out right to my face? Even if he's always right about everything, that's not very nice!
female_content: Although... fine, that's the truth! But did she have to point it out right to my face? Even if she's always right about everything, that's just not fair!

content: Contrary to her usual efficiency in forging others' letters, Dove is taking her time with her own letter. She opens up her heart hesitantly, carefully choosing each word as she reveals the true feelings she's kept hidden for so long.
Her words are neither diplomatic nor mature. In fact, they're simply a sulking child's complaints meant only for her parents.

speaker: Dove's Letter
content: To be honest, back in Désir, I really got a thrill out of deceiving people. It made me feel so superior and powerful. I even wanted to keep doing it forever.

speaker: Dove's Letter
content: A mere letter could make them laugh and cry, stirring up joy and despair... and I was the only one who knew it was all fake! The letters, the smiles, the tears. Everything was just a lie! Haha!
Watching others fall for her deceptions, Dove convinced herself that becoming a deceiver meant she could never fall victim to lies again.

speaker: Dove's Letter
content: It wasn't until that person scolded me that I started to realize I was wrong. The truth is, I've been lied to all along too.

speaker: Dove's Letter
content: By myself.
She forged letters to take revenge on the villagers in her hometown, because they relied on the mail carriers to bring back messages while carelessly dismissing their sacrifice.

She also used lies to punish the people of Désir, for they never once saw through her deceptions and only proved her bitter, disillusioning assumption repeatedly: No one truly cared about a messenger's idealistic mission.
But in truth, the one she really wanted to get back at might have been someone else entirely.

speaker: Dove's Letter
content: I wanted to trick myself. Maybe the DisCity dream was real? Maybe the messenger dream too? Maybe someday someone would tell me our dedication to our job wasn't all in vain, that my mom and dad were worthy of respect.

speaker: Dove's Letter
content: Maybe you're just held up somewhere, like it was written in those letters Uncle and Aunt showed me. If I just wait a little longer, you'll come back and tell me this was all just a joke, just a little test to help me grow up faster...

speaker: Dove's Letter
content: But why won't you come back? I've deceived so many people and told so many lies. I've become such a terrible child. Why won't you come back already?
Her parents abandoned her to pursue their career. And with the truth concealed by the villagers' fake letters, she refused to believe that her parents were already dead.

speaker: Dove's Letter
content: Shouldn't you be scolding me right now, like you used to? Tell me it's wrong to lie, that it's a crime to forge letters. Tell me a good child should face reality with courage instead of hiding behind lies like a loser.

speaker: Dove's Letter
content: But I'll never hear those words again. You're never coming back...
The nib of her pen digs deep into the paper as she scribbles on and on, each word like a liberating cry.

speaker: Dove's Letter
content: Mom, Dad, why did you just leave like that... Why did you leave me alone...
She's scribbling so hard that the pen skids off the edge of the paper. The sound of writing filling the room stops abruptly.
She hunches over the desk like a cold plaster statue. Only her trembling fingers gripping the pen reveals the tempest raging within her.

The air seems to freeze, and time becomes a hazy blur. The girl stares at her messy handwriting for what feels like an eternity before finally gripping her pen again, letting the words flow out like a stream.

speaker: Dove's Letter
content: I know I was wrong. I understand I've done so many unforgivable things. But I... all I wanted was for you not to suddenly leave me behind.

speaker: Dove's Letter
content: Don't choose your noble calling over me. Dove doesn't want to be the thing you throw away.

speaker: Dove's Letter
content: I'll apologize, I'll atone for my actions. So please, just come back to see me one more time. Just once is enough. I just want to say goodbye...
...Even though she knows it's impossible.
Dove sets down her pen and meticulously folds the letter. She takes out an envelope and slips in the paper skillfully, sealing it carefully before finally standing up.
But then she halts at her next move. She stands still as an indescribable disoriented feeling washes over her, making her want to laugh suddenly.

speaker: Dove
content: Right... How will I even send this letter? Find a mail carrier? ...But I am the mail carrier.

speaker: Dove
content: Nowhere to send it, and no chance of ever getting a reply... Should I end up using my special power on myself, forging replies to fuel my own delusions?
This letter has nowhere to go, just like her who's finally stepped out of her web of lies. There's no place left for her in this imaginary wonderland that's long collapsed.
At that moment, a familiar voice cuts through the loneliness and desolation binding her, reaching out like a helping hand to her lost soul.
Chief's POV

speaker: Chief
content: Dove?
The girl before you seems completely unaware of your presence until now, her eyes going wide with an uncharacteristic startled look.
Not wanting her to feel like you're intruding on her vulnerable moment, you take the initiative to speak first, keeping your tone casual but direct.

speaker: Chief
content: Don't get the wrong idea, I'm just doing my routine patrol and happen to see you heading out. ...Got something to attend to?

speaker: Dove
content: Ah... N-nothing.
She nervously tries to hide the letter behind her back, but you didn't come here to let her keep concealing her problems.

speaker: Chief
content: Don't worry, I won't open any letters without permission unless they're going out of the Bureau. There's no need to hide it from me.

speaker: Dove
content: ...Of course you don't need to read the letters, Chief. Not when you have those almighty shackles. What secrets can we Sinners possibly keep when you can just use them on us?
Understanding what your words implied, Dove narrows her eyes and puffs up her cheeks in a pout.

speaker: Dove
content: You already know what I'm trying to do, don't you? So why even bother asking?

speaker: Chief
content: Because I think that once you've sorted everything out, you'll need someone to confide in. Someone you can be completely honest and open with.
Compared to the Dove who put on an innocent disguise to achieve her goals, her true self might be more difficult to deal with.
But you know this means you're closer to the real her than anyone else has ever been. What you both need now isn't empty pleasantries, but complete honesty.

speaker: Chief
content: I'd say I'm a pretty good candidate for that role, don't you think? After all, I've been waiting for your answer for quite some time now.
