Your straightforward words seem to shatter the invisible wall between you. After a moment of silence, Dove steps aside, opening the door to her room.

speaker: Dove
content: ...Come in.
You follow Dove into her room. Limited by the conditions here, the furnishings look quite different from her room in Désir, yet you can still see echoes of that study in this space.
This time, you sit down by the desk as told by the host. Dove carefully smooths out the creases in the letter before placing it on the desk between you.

speaker: Dove
content: It's all because of your strange questions. These past few days, I haven't been able to sleep or read properly anymore.
She complains, mustering a cheerful tone. You simply listen quietly, waiting for her to ready herself to open up.
You don't have to wait long. Soon, Dove stops fidgeting and looks you in the eye with a seriousness you've never seen in her before.

speaker: Dove
content: Chief... No, ${PlayerName}. I want to tell you I'm angry because I can't forgive those people who look down on messengers.

speaker: Dove
content: But deep down, I know the last person I can forgive is myself.

speaker: Dove
content: My parents were gone. My mail carrier dream shattered. I discovered that everything I used to believe in, the letters, the books, even the words themselves... were nothing but elaborate lies...

speaker: Dove
content: I watched as my world crumbled into a pile of unrecognizable mess I couldn't piece back together. But what did I do as I watched it all happen?
Dove takes a deep breath, trying to steady the tremor in her voice.

speaker: Dove
content: ...Nothing. I was so afraid of getting hurt again that I couldn't even look at the fragments, much less try to piece them back together.

speaker: Dove
content: All that pessimism and detachment were just concealment for my own weakness. Looking at it now, I'm no different from those who willingly believed my lies, reluctant to face reality.
She lowers her head, gently tracing the recipient's name on the envelope with her fingers, her eyes dim with sorrow.

speaker: Dove
content: Even if I understand my mistakes now, even if I want to atone for them... what then? I've already lost everything. I don't even have anyone left to write to.

speaker: Dove
content: For someone like me who's lost hope and faith in everything, if I can't even rely on lies, what meaning could the future possibly hold?
Dove withdraws her hand. You watch as her delicate fingers tremble in the air, hovering uncertainly before finally coming to rest on her lap, where she clasps her hands tightly together.

speaker: Choice
options: I can't say I fully understand what you're going through, but...

speaker: Chief
content: But have you ever thought... perhaps you could write to me?

speaker: Dove
content: ...You?
She looks up at you, her voice feeble and filled with doubt and uncertainty, but you catch a fleeting glimpse of hope in her eyes.

speaker: Chief
content: Yes, but not just me. The Bureau will make a fair judgment about your past crimes, and until you complete your necessary rehabilitation, we'll be here to support you every step of the way.

speaker: Chief
content: We'll help you break free from the mire of your past, help you find more people to write to, and let you see for yourself all the things still worth believing in.

speaker: Chief
content: Dove, you're no longer that housebound child whose understanding of the world came only from the words others brought back to you. You've seen more now, and you know better what's worth believing in.
You fix your gaze on her wavering eyes and strengthen your tone.

speaker: Chief
content: Rising anew from ruins, sprouting from scorched earth, gaining formidable strength from pain and suffering. This is what it means to be a Sinner.

speaker: Chief
content: Dove, you can do this. Because you've already won once before.

speaker: Dove
content: C-can I really? Delivering emotions, connecting hearts... I've strayed from my dream for so long. I'm afraid I won't be able to stay the course...
The girl mumbles self-deprecating words and shrinks back. You can almost see that sickly child she once was, clutching the doorframe, yearning to step outside yet paralyzed by fear.
Now it's your turn to extend a hand to her.

speaker: Chief
content: It's normal to be afraid, to have doubts, to feel uncertain. Even the most committed idealists cannot be sure they are on the right path from the start.

speaker: Chief
content: It's no big deal to get lost from time to time, because Dove, I've never seen anyone more devoted to the mail carrier profession than you. I know you can find your way back.

speaker: Dove
content: Don't be ridiculous. How many mail carriers can you have met? Besides, I've been on the wrong path for so long...
She protests in a slightly choked voice. This makes you smile, and with gentle words, you take the hand of that child standing by the door, slowly guiding her out.

speaker: Chief
content: It's all right, we've got plenty of time. There's no need to rush.

speaker: Chief
content: We'll be right beside you as you find your way back to the beginning, just like when you first learned to read and write, when you first learned to believe in the power of words.

speaker: Dove
content: ...${PlayerName}...
A teardrop falls onto the envelope, blurring the recipient's name. You know these overwhelming emotions won't subside quickly, so you keep your promise in silence, staying quietly by her side.

These fragments of her dream and faith have been forgotten for too long, but both you and Dove, who has chosen to gather them up again, believe that one day these pieces can be shaped back into her mail carrier dream again.

speaker: Dove
content: ...This letter is for you. I know you're busy and might not have time to write back... but I'll keep waiting.
At long last, Dove regains her composure. She grabs the letter from the desk and presses it into your hands decisively. The letter feels heavy and warm.

speaker: Chief
content: I promise I won't keep you waiting for too long.

speaker: Chief
content: Oh right, and I've got some good news for you.

speaker: Dove
content: Good news?
You smile at her bewildered expression and continue slowly.

speaker: Chief
content: Remember that merchant whom you met with? I heard that after he was escorted out of the Bureau, he couldn't keep his mouth shut and kept spewing insults about Outlanders.

speaker: Chief
content: Somehow he ended up in the immigrant district and got jumped by some guys. They gave him quite the beating.

speaker: Dove
content: Somehow?
You think of Dove's face when she acts innocent and gives your best shot at an impression.

speaker: Chief
content: Yeah, somehow. You know, these things just happen sometimes.
She watches your hammy performance for a moment before bursting into laughter.

speaker: Dove
content: All right, dear Chief who clearly has nothing to do with that. I'd love it if you could include a story about some crooked merchant and the hero who punished him in your letter.

speaker: Dove
content: In exchange, I can tell you a story... about a frail girl's journey through WhiteSands.

speaker: Chief
content: Deal.
You rise with a smile, carefully tucking away her letter. This time, she walks you to the door to see you off, and you both know that a new day is about to begin.
NOT for the Faint-Hearted! Chilling Truth Unveiled: Ghost Sightings in Demolition-Bound Complex
"IT" LINGERS! Disturbing Incidents Plague Urban Renewal Project: Midnight Curse Reported
DEMOLITION HALTED BY SUPERNATURAL FORCE? Horrifying CCTV Footage Emerges—And Experts' Shocking Response...

speaker: Real Estate Developer
content: Absolutely not true! Never heard of anything like that!

speaker: Real Estate Developer
content: Is the Bureau seriously blocking our deal with Miss Luminita just because of some baseless tabloid stories?

speaker: Real Estate Developer
content: I understand that you have your concerns, but let's not forget this renewal project is a top priority approved by the government. We can't afford any delays.

speaker: Real Estate Developer
content: The rumors about the haunted old neighborhoods are really hurting our project's reputation. As per our signed agreement, Miss Luminita is obligated to use her expertise as a haunted property inspector to address these rumors.

speaker: Real Estate Developer
content: I've mentioned this multiple times in our previous calls. I strongly urge the Bureau to expedite Miss Luminita's leave permit. Let's put an end to these unnecessary obstacles and time-wasting!
Beep—Beep—

After finishing her report, Nightingale places the documents from the developer on your desk one by one. Alongside the property inspection agreement, the developer has included a structural hazard assessment report for the old neighborhoods.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, I've verified the report's contents. While I suspect some deliberate exaggeration in the wording, the district has indeed experienced several accidents due to deteriorating infrastructure and does present significant safety hazards.

speaker: Nightingale
content: During our previous communications, the demolition contractor was evasive when we pressed for details. But judging by the contents of this structural hazard assessment alone, their attitude could be seen as... honest.
Whether it's honesty or pressure tactics, only they know for sure. If they really cared about resident safety, they wouldn't have waited until now to send us this report.
Any updates on the investigation into those haunting rumors in the old district?

speaker: Nightingale
content: Apart from several residents claiming to have witnessed supernatural events, we haven't come across any solid leads. We're still tracking down the source of these rumors.
You give her a nod. Tracking down the source of rumors is always challenging, and the current situation still lies within your expectations.
Fortunately, you have another person directly involved in this matter right here.
You push aside the documents on your desk and pull out Luminita's profile that you were reviewing earlier. Picking up on your intention, Nightingale continues speaking.

speaker: Nightingale
content: As you requested, we've been conducting a parallel investigation into Sinner Luminita. Every single "haunted property" she's handled as a real estate agent has tested positive for abnormal Mania residue, without exception.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Due to the large number of properties involved and the complexity of the transactions, a more detailed investigation will take additional time. Allowing Luminita to leave the Bureau before the results are complete would indeed pose unnecessary risks.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Regarding the real estate developer's request, should I continue to refuse it on your behalf?
No need. The fact that they can keep contacting us shows they've got some powerful supporters backing them up.
But you're not about to let anyone pull your strings. You want to hear how the Bureau's resident "expert" in haunted property deals explains these ghost-infested old houses.
Nightingale, please move up Luminita's interrogation schedule. I need to speak with her in person before meeting with the real estate developer.

speaker: Luminita
content: Well hello there, Chief! Finally remembered I exist? You locked me up here and then not a peep from you—I was beginning to think I'd been left in the dust!
As you enter, Luminita, seated in the interrogation chair, brightens up. She eagerly greets you before you can say anything, her words light and cheerful.

speaker: Luminita
content: So? You've come to see me today—does this mean you've finally made up your mind about "that thing"?

speaker: Luminita
content: Buying a house, of course! What else could it be?

speaker: Luminita
content: Remember what I told you just two weeks back? These drops are just normal market fluctuations, and prices will definitely bounce back in six months. Those properties I mentioned last time are all hot listings! Whoever hesitates is lost, Chief. You gotta act fast!

speaker: Luminita
content: Of course, buying property is a big decision that deserves careful consideration. But with me on your side, you don't need to worry about prices at all! If the budget is a bit snug, I can find you something even cheaper. I remember there's one at... the crematory out east...
I appreciate you helping me keep an eye out for properties, but I'm afraid that's not why I'm here today.

speaker: test
content: "Yingying"

speaker: Luminita
content: I'm just your friendly neighborhood agent here! No hard sell, no nonsense, just me nudging you because I've got your back. Owning a home equals peace of mind, Chief. As dedicated as you are to work, sleeping at the office isn't the dream, right?
Luminita mutters and grumbles with a show of complaint, but there's no actual trace of displeasure in her voice. She has clearly anticipated your refusal all along.
You observe her reaction and decide to play along with her conversation, gradually steering toward your actual intention.
If we're talking about dedication to work, I can't hold a candle to you. I bet there are fewer than ten people in the entire Bureau who don't have your business card in their pocket.

speaker: Luminita
content: Just a force of habit... I swear, I wasn't being pushy at all. They practically grabbed my cards themselves!
I understand. I just didn't expect you'd refuse to give yourself a break even while at the Bureau. Is the real estate market that rough out there these days?

speaker: Luminita
content: Not really. My business usually does quite well. In real estate, it's all about experience and connections, you know.

speaker: Luminita
content: I'm sure you've done some digging into my past. Grew up poor and lied about my age to get jobs, so I started in this business early and do have some connections. Even though I work solo in this gig, it's not really hard for me.

speaker: Luminita
content: But...
Luminita taps her cheek with her fingertips, looking noticeably disinterested.

speaker: Luminita
content: Ever since I landed here, selling houses has been one tough nut to crack!

speaker: Luminita
content: Folks around here probably grab my cards just to be nice. Everyone follows your example, Chief—they're all such workaholics they might as well start moving their beds into the office!

speaker: Luminita
content: I can't develop new clients, and I'm not allowed to contact anyone outside. You know, I still had a pile of deals to be closed when I was brought in here.
You avert your gaze, pretending not to notice Luminita's teasing remarks, and continue with your questions.
Seems like agents face the same problems regardless... I thought things might be different for someone specializing in haunted properties like you.

speaker: Luminita
content: Business is business—the fundamentals never change, and everyone's racing against time. It's just that with haunted houses, profits and trends come and go much faster. Gotta hustle extra hard to keep those earnings flowing since this gig puts food on my table.
If it's such a grind, why did you specifically choose to go into the haunted house business?

speaker: Luminita
content: Oh, it's all pretty much the same. Every line of work is tough.
She waves her hand nonchalantly, using an exaggerated sigh to brush off your question. Given Luminita's social acumen, she must have picked up what you were really asking.
Let me cut to the chase. Haunted houses are considered taboo and notoriously difficult to sell. Don't most agents steer clear of these properties?

speaker: Luminita
content: Ohh, so that's what you're asking about...
Luminita puts on an expression of sudden comprehension, adjusting her posture. As she moves, the keys beneath her trench coat make a crisp clinking sound—almost like smug laughter.

speaker: Luminita
content: That's exactly why they're just your average agents!

speaker: Luminita
content: The haunted house business has its risks, sure, but there's a lot more money to be made.

speaker: Luminita
content: I'm not just raking in cash from sales, but also from all those thrill-seekers over in Eastside who flock here for a good scare. Believe it or not, sometimes just selling tickets because of a house's haunted reputation brings in a small fortune!

speaker: Luminita
content: Oh, and if you're interested in seeing for yourself...
As she speaks, she pats her pocket. With a quick flick of her wrist, a pristine business card materializes between her fingers, which she promptly thrusts before your eyes.

speaker: Luminita
content: Once I'm out of the Bureau, hit me up anytime—whether you're house hunting or just curious about haunted spots. Bring your friends, and I'll hook you up with a nice discount!

speaker: Luminita
content: Sure, finding real haunted houses is like striking gold these days. But if you're up for a spooky encounter, just swing by my way. I'll make sure you meet a ghost or two!

speaker: Luminita
content: And I'll bump your deal to the top of the list, just for you! You can count on it!

options: There's no rush for my personal deal.

content: You take the business card but don't pocket it, simply placing it next to the documents on the table. Then, you slide the real estate developer's property inspection agreement toward Luminita.
It's too soon to talk about you leaving the Bureau, and my personal deal can wait. Right now, we've got a major case on our hands—and they're asking for your involvement specifically.
There have been some rumors about the old district marked for the government's urban renewal project, and the real estate developer in charge of the project...

speaker: Luminita
content: They're in charge of demolishing the old district, and now they want me to hold up my end of the deal—by proving the area isn't haunted and those houses aren't cursed. Right?

speaker: Luminita
content: I remember it. This is a real estate developer with some bigshot backer we're talking about, after all. And they're generous—just the initial deposit is nearly half a year's income for me.

speaker: Luminita
content: No wonder you moved up my interrogation. It's because of this situation, right?
With a theatrical flair, Luminita flips through the agreement with a rustling flourish, not bothering to read any of its contents, before casually tossing the document aside.

speaker: Luminita
content: When old buildings seem haunted, it's usually just aging infrastructure or some malfunction. These situations are super easy to fix!

speaker: Luminita
content: With my touch, haunted hellholes turn into dream homes overnight. Only catch? I don't do remote work yet—I'll need to be there in person.
From how you're describing it, were all those "haunted houses" you've handled just cases like this?

speaker: Luminita
content: Hmm... Pretty much.

speaker: Luminita
content: It's not like ghosts are that common anyway! Living people without homes carry WAY more resentment than any ghost ever could.

speaker: Luminita
content: But anyway, Chief, when do you plan to let me out to handle it? It's a major urban renewal and demolition project after all, and delaying too long will only create more trouble for the Bureau, right?
She crafts her words with meticulous care, gently probing your position. Despite her intentionally courteous manner, you remain unmoved.
After multiple rounds of exchange, you are growing increasingly convinced that Luminita is not as cooperative in this interrogation as she appears to be.
Luminita, you can stop probing my position. I know you want to leave the Bureau, but I'll be perfectly clear with you: given our investigation's findings, that's not going to happen easily.

You've been hiding critical information while only sharing trivial details. So let's start with this: Those properties you handled—were they already "haunted houses" to begin with, or did they only become "haunted" after they fell into your hands?

According to the investigations on the completed property transaction, every "haunted property" handled by Luminita shows evidence of meticulously removed Mania residue. Based on the nature of this Mania, Corruptors may have been present at these sites for extended periods.
Furthermore, testimonies from several of Luminita's fellow agents have indirectly confirmed the suspicion.
"Only Luminita can find, handle, and sell those properties successfully." Your fellow agents speak highly of your skills, but many of them share the Bureau's skepticism about your methods.

Based on evidence gathered from these properties, you're now under serious suspicion of sheltering Corruptors. We suspect that you intentionally used them to fabricate haunted houses and fraudulently profited from the scheme.
Luminita, do you have anything to say in your defense?

speaker: Luminita
content: ...Whoa, you just got real serious all of a sudden. I was expecting you to say something actually important.
After a brief silence, Luminita shrugs her shoulders and spreads her hands with complete indifference, as if the accusations mean nothing to her.

speaker: Luminita
content: Alright, you got me. I checked all the boxes. But what's that really proving?

speaker: Luminita
content: That I'm a genius at using Corruptors to fake supernatural activities and market "haunted" houses? That I was born for real estate? Look, what I did didn't hurt anyone or cause any real damage.

speaker: Luminita
content: If my little tricks qualify as "fraud," then half the Eastside real estate agencies belong behind bars. Would certainly save you the trouble of running around collecting statements from those agents in town.
Setting aside the consequences of what you call "little tricks," simply gathering Corruptors already constitutes a serious prohibited offense.

speaker: Luminita
content: This sort of... minor violation should be nothing new for the MBCC Chief... Hey, don't look at me like that. I'm just joking.

speaker: Luminita
content: Look, I know I've broken some rules, and that's why I've been cooperating with your investigation. But let's be clear: even with my record, that has nothing to do with the developer's property inspection request.

speaker: Luminita
content: I've never even been to that old district. Not once!
If you've never been there, how could you be so certain that the "hauntings" were caused by aging facilities rather than Corruptors?
A tense silence suddenly envelops the interrogation room, your words lingering in the air. Luminita narrows her eyes, scrutinizing you closely, the once casual smile on her face fading away.

speaker: Luminita
content: I was just talking off the cuff. No need to get hung up on word choice... So what you're implying, Chief, is that you suspect I'm behind the haunting rumors in the old district?
I'm just pointing out a possibility. After all, our investigation shows that staging fake hauntings has been your standard practice in your haunted property dealings.

speaker: Luminita
content: That was for profit before—to sell houses. But what would I gain from doing it this time? Sabotage the demolition so I never receive my final payment from the client? Does that make any sense?

speaker: Luminita
content: You're giving me way too much credit, Chief. Is overthinking everything just a professional habit in law enforcement?
Maybe. A lot of times I wish I was just overthinking things.
Currently, we have no evidence linking you to the hauntings in the old district, but at the same time, we can't entirely clear you of suspicion.
The investigation into your past activities remains incomplete. To mitigate potential risks, the Bureau will need to maintain certain restrictions on you...

You purposefully pause. Luminita's expression stays composed, showing no immediate reaction to your words, but the subtle tightening of her posture betrays her underlying nervousness, allowing you to catch a crack in her facade.
Don't think this deal will be your ticket out of the Bureau, Luminita.

speaker: Luminita
content: So... what are you going to do about the developer's request?

Since you yourself raised the possibility of Corruptors causing these paranormal events, our top priority before demolition begins will be detecting and eliminating any Mania influence. This is exactly the kind of situation the Bureau specializes in handling.
If the scans detect any anomalies, the demolition will be halted and postponed. And given your history of using Corruptors to fake hauntings, you can expect a much deeper investigation.

speaker: Luminita
content: And if there are no issues?
We still have other options to handle it without requiring your involvement.
You deliberately maintain a stern tone while carefully observing Luminita's reaction. Her expression visibly stiffens with each word.

Just when you expect her mood to deteriorate further and reveal her true motives for pursuing this request, she suddenly bursts into laughter, reverting to that same carefree, joking demeanor she displayed at the beginning of the interrogation.

speaker: Luminita
content: You're right—you definitely should scan the area first. That old district's so isolated, Corruptors could've easily wandered in. Seen it happen plenty of times before.

speaker: Luminita
content: Still, I'd recommend letting me check the property myself after you've finished your part.
Luminita's abrupt shift in attitude momentarily catches you off guard.
Why do you have to go there?

speaker: Luminita
content: It's not like I absolutely have to go. Besides, weren't you the one who brought up this request thing, Chief? I know the Bureau doesn't just let Sinners walk around, but...

speaker: Luminita
content: Special cases require special treatment, you know? I signed the property inspection agreement, so if I don't show up to finalize it, the developer could claim breach of contract and bleed the Bureau dry.

speaker: Luminita
content: Just look at this penalty clause—it's multiple times the commission! I wouldn't just lose the money; I'd be paying out of pocket. That would ruin my name in the business!

She reopens the property inspection agreement that was set aside, her finger repeatedly circling the violation penalties on the last page—a pointed reminder of her shrewd, profit-driven nature as an agent.
Luminita's reasoning sounds plausible enough, but this vague, one-size-fits-all explanation might just be her way of talking in circles to shut down further questions.
As you ponder the details of Luminita's behavior during the interrogation, something feels off. A question that's been bothering you since the beginning comes creeping back.
If you're only in real estate for the money, why go through the trouble of faking haunted houses? Normal properties would be much easier to sell.
Someone with your talents doesn't need cheap haunted house stunts.

speaker: Luminita
content: Not really, Chief. Every industry's its own world with layers you wouldn't see. You've never been in real estate; you don't know how things actually work.
Sure enough, she brushes you off again.

Meeting your gaze, Luminita smiles slightly, almost as if she can read your thoughts. In the tense silence between you, it dawns upon you that this interrogation has hit a wall—you lack the evidence needed to challenge her claims.
You need an opening to make her slip up and reveal her true intentions.
You produce the document you have prepared in advance. When Luminita reads its contents, a flicker of suspicion crosses her face, only to be quickly masked by the same nonchalant smile.

speaker: Luminita
content: ...Wait, what? So this whole time, you were just trying to scare me?

Think of it as standard procedure. But you're right about one thing—the Bureau is getting tired of the real estate developer's constant pressure. Sending you in would be the quickest way to resolve the situation.
However, in exchange, I'll be accompanying you the entire time.

speaker: Luminita
content: So, Chief... you sure you're not in the market for a house?

On the way back to the detention area, Luminita hastens her steps to move ahead of you. While walking backward to maintain eye contact, she seamlessly transitions back into her salesperson persona, dispelling the serious atmosphere of the interrogation room within seconds.

speaker: Luminita
content: The old district inspection will only take half a day at most. How about I show you some properties with the rest of our time? Even if you're not buying, it doesn't hurt to look, right?
...You really don't need to focus so much on me as a potential client.

speaker: Luminita
content: It's not just about selling to you! I treat all clients without homes equally—that's my core principle as an agent!
Fortunately, the path isn't long, and Luminita's unyielding sales pitch, which allows you no breathing space, finally comes to a halt as you reach a fork in the corridor.

After saying goodbye, she hurries away with quick, long strides. You watch her figure disappear and begin to breathe a sigh of relief when you suddenly notice something odd—your pocket feels unusually bulky.
You reach into your pocket and a thick stack of business cards comes tumbling out all at once, scattering across the ground.
Cafe in Eastside 7:00 AM

speaker: Luminita
content: Sorry for the wait! Did you have any trouble getting here? I've picked out some great properties based on your needs, all very budget-friendly. Take a look and see what you think!

speaker: Client A
content: Um... Do you have more affordable options? I've had some big career changes lately, and this might be a stretch for me right now.

speaker: Luminita
content: Oh, don't worry at all! My job is to find you the right fit. Now, take this one—top floor, north-facing, quirky layout. It's outlived three owners, and the price has dropped like a rock. Could be your lucky break?

speaker: Client B
content: The price works for me, but what's the place actually like inside? And the neighborhood? My last place had a leak. That endless dripping totally ruined my sleep.

speaker: Luminita
content: Then you absolutely can't miss this one! After they found human remains in the plumbing, all the pipes were completely upgraded—whisper-quiet now. You'll sleep like a baby, guaranteed!

speaker: Client C
content: I'm not superstitious or anything, but all these houses you've shown me are haunted... I actually prefer living alone, so I might need to think this through.

speaker: Luminita
content: You'll never know if it's right until you try it! And guess what? I've got this great deal—just 100 DisCoins for a one-month trial. And extending for a few more months is no problem at all.

speaker: Luminita
content: Those ghosts were respectable, salaried tenants in life—the kind who always mind their manners and don't damage property. Honestly? You might end up getting along great!
As the bell chimes crisply, signaling the departure of the final client, Luminita downs her drink in one gulp, lets out a deep exhale, and crumples into the couch.

speaker: Luminita
content: Whew—finally finished! Thanks for sticking with me through all this, Chief.
You've got... quite remarkable sales tactics.

speaker: Luminita
content: You're too kind! But hey, this job puts food on my table—gotta bring my A-game.
When you say "putting food on the table," you mean by selling houses at rock-bottom prices?
You pick up the three housing contracts signed today and casually flip through their contents.
You've closed plenty of deals, but all at below-market prices. Unless you got these properties for free, I don't see how you're making any profit.

speaker: Luminita
content: Don't you remember? I also make money from haunted house tours.

speaker: Luminita
content: Besides, these clients who rush to buy houses all have their own struggles. If I can help them, why wouldn't I? I just want them to have a place they can call home.

speaker: Luminita
content: Once they sign the papers and have a home...
She puts on a thoughtful expression and gradually lowers her voice. You wait attentively for her to continue.
To your surprise, she suddenly breaks into a wide grin, snatches the contracts from your hand, and starts using them as a makeshift fan.

speaker: Luminita
content: It'll be easier for me to make money when they're trapped in a contract! Hey, don't give me that look. I'm just kidding!

speaker: Luminita
content: Anyway, shouldn't we be heading to the old district? If we don't leave now, we're going to be late.
Distracted by Luminita's change of subject, you glance down to check the time.

By the time you look up, she's already packed everything and is standing before you. Her rapid-fire stream of urgings leaves no room for a response, and before you know it, she's all but shoving you out of the cafe in a hurry.
Old District in Eastside 5:00 PM

The demolition zone earmarked for redevelopment sits in Eastside's most economically depressed area. Gray, cracked walls have been painted over multiple times, while small advertisements plaster every surface, left uncleared for who knows how long.

You and Luminita arrive on time at the residential building where you're scheduled to meet the real estate developer. To your surprise, the surroundings are unnervingly quiet. Despite it being near dinner time, there's not the slightest hint of human life anywhere.
Where are all the residents?

speaker: Real Estate Developer
content: As you know, this is a top-priority project for leadership, but it's been delayed by complications. Many property owners here don't have the full context like yourself, which has led to misunderstandings and... less-than-ideal cooperation.

speaker: Real Estate Developer
content: We had no choice but to assist the residents with relocation last month.
"Assisted them with relocation"? The Bureau wasn't informed about any of this before today.

Did you secure proper approvals before acting? Were residents given full resettlement plans and compensation? By protocol, you should have shared this information with us when you requested this meeting.

speaker: Real Estate Developer
content: This is just reasonable flexibility—unless the Bureau's sudden demand for Mania testing doesn't count either?

speaker: Real Estate Developer
content: The tests came back clean, but you never know where there might be some residual contamination. Getting owners out early was a safety precaution, for their own good.

speaker: Real Estate Developer
content: Besides, this back-and-forth with you has already set us back. We simply don't have time to report everything according to "protocols" anymore. I hope you understand.

While talking, the developer shows utter indifference toward their regulatory violations in forcibly relocating residents, almost treating such actions as standard procedure. This demolition project is clearly not as legitimate as they've publicly claimed.

speaker: Luminita
content: Honestly, the early relocation works in my favor. Makes it much easier for me to go in and check things out!
Just as you're about to speak, Luminita—silent until now—suddenly cuts in. She shifts subtly between you and the real estate developer, steering the conversation away and leaving you sidelined.

speaker: Luminita
content: By the way, what's the full story behind these haunted building rumors? The more details I know, the faster I can wrap this up.

speaker: Real Estate Developer
content: They're just baseless rumors—what details could there possibly be? This area is slated to become a commercial district, and this haunted nonsense is seriously scaring off investors. We're bleeding money over superstitions.

speaker: Real Estate Developer
content: And we still can't find the source of these rumors... If you ask me, it's probably those stubborn homeowners who won't budge.

speaker: Luminita
content: Hmm, that's entirely possible. I've staged a ghost or two myself when dealing with tough clients in the past.

speaker: Luminita
content: But don't worry! I'll make sure to take care of all these "ghosts" for you today. Your demolition schedule won't get derailed on my watch.

speaker: Real Estate Developer
content: Good. I hired you because I trust your expertise in evaluating supposedly haunted properties. Don't disappoint me, Miss Luminita.

speaker: Luminita
content: Naturally. You pay, I perform—that's the deal. Shall we begin? After you.

The real estate developer strides toward the residential building, pointedly ignoring you. Luminita trails behind him, maintaining the same eager smile she had when meeting with her clients this morning.

Something undeniably shady lurks behind this demolition project, and the developer isn't even pretending otherwise. Yet Luminita doesn't seem surprised in the slightest. Does she already know the truth—or does she just not care, so long as the job gets done and she gets paid?
You hear her calling for you from up ahead. Temporarily setting aside your suspicions, you follow them into the residential building.

The rusty bedroom door creaks open. Before you can make out the room's layout, the overhead bulb explodes in a shower of sparks. Then, at the edge of your sight, an eerie shadow materializes on the far wall.
Having learned from past experiences, you immediately cover your ears. Almost simultaneously, a piercing scream cuts through the air.

speaker: Luminita
content: Geez, you've got some pipes on you.

speaker: Luminita
content: Relax, there's nothing to be afraid of. There, see for yourselves.

Luminita strides past you and the cowering developer, pulling a flashlight from her coat. The beam cuts through the dark, exposing the shadow's true nature—human in outline, yet completely motionless, more like a stain on the wall than anything supernatural.

speaker: Luminita
content: See those hook holes up there? There must have been a coat hanging here for years without being moved. That's why a human-shaped mark is left on the wall.

speaker: Real Estate Developer
content: Ahem. C-clearly... people who'd live in a place like this didn't care about housekeeping at all.

speaker: Luminita
content: It's an old building, after all. What we've seen so far—flickering lights from bad wiring and that damp smell from water trapped between walls? Just standard wear and tear.

speaker: Luminita
content: But spot that shadow in the dead of night, and it could easily pass for some vengeful ghost hovering at your bedside... Haha, don't you think so?

speaker: Real Estate Developer
content: Now that we've confirmed there's nothing wrong here, let's move on to inspect the next area.

The real estate developer, having barely regained his composure, makes no effort to hide his impatience. Clearly unwilling to linger, he turns on his heel and marches out, leaving you and Luminita trailing a step behind.
Faint footsteps echo from the corner. You turn around—in the dim light, what appears to be a shadowy figure quickly slips around the turn.

speaker: Luminita
content: Chief, wrong turn. We need to go this way.
I know, but I thought I saw something over there...

speaker: Luminita
content: Hmm? What did you see?
You look back toward the corner, only to find it completely empty now. Nothing is there except a ceiling light buzzing with poor electrical contact.

speaker: Luminita
content: Your eyes must be playing tricks on you. Don't go scaring yourself!

speaker: Luminita
content: We still have another floor to check. Faster we move, faster we're out. Chief, if you're really that scared, just stick close and don't fall behind.
Before you can respond, she grabs your sleeve and practically drags you in the opposite direction, as if even one second lingering near that corner might cause her to work overtime.

Her sudden urgency leaves you bewildered. You stumble forward from the force of her pull, instinctively trying to look back. But before you can fully turn your head, you feel another sharp tug on your sleeve.

speaker: Luminita
content: But our progress today has been much faster than I expected! At this rate, once those rumors are cleared up, this place should be ready for demolition soon, right?
Based on what we've seen so far, that should be the case, as long as nothing unusual comes up.
You seem quite concerned about the demolition?

speaker: Luminita
content: Of course! I won't get the final payment for this commission until the demolition officially begins.

speaker: Luminita
content: Besides, I'm sure the Bureau wants this demolition over with too, right?
You don't immediately answer Luminita's question.

Despite obvious signs suggesting the real estate developer's shady dealings with the demolition, this technically falls outside the Bureau's jurisdiction. And given how deteriorated these buildings are, swift demolition is probably the right call.
With no Mania residue found here and these "hauntings" debunked, the Bureau has no reason to oppose the demolition project moving forward.

speaker: Luminita
content: Yeah, you have no reason to oppose it.
She nods, naturally equating you with the Bureau, seemingly confirming something to herself through this classification. You sense something off in her tone and are about to press further...

speaker: Real Estate Developer
content: How much longer do you two plan to waste time over there?

speaker: Luminita
content: Coming! Sorry for the hold-up—right behind you!
Luminita trots quickly after him, her face instantly resuming its standard radiant smile. That thoughtful expression from moments ago seems almost like it was just your imagination.

The rest of the inspection unfolds without a hitch, with Luminita effortlessly debunking every supposedly paranormal incident you encounter. Slowly, the real estate developer's tense posture relax, his initial unease giving way to relief.
Maybe trying to salvage his pride after his earlier jumpy display, the developer grows much more talkative, venting his emotions and no longer concealing his true opinions about the old district.

speaker: Real Estate Developer
content: I knew it! There's no such thing as ghosts in this world, and even if there were, what are the odds they'd all haunt MY turf? Now it's time to squeeze those holdouts and find out who's been feeding these rumors.

speaker: Real Estate Developer
content: Their greed just never ends. Holding out for more money, then pulling this crap? Guess they don't even want the pittance we're offering anymore...
Just as you turn into a corridor, before the real estate developer can complete his sentence, a precariously dangling light bulb above suddenly plummets to the ground, shattering into pieces.
Then comes the second bulb, the third, continuing all the way to the end of the corridor. Darkness surges in like a flood, engulfing your entire field of vision within seconds.

speaker: Real Estate Developer
content: How many times is this going to happen? The same old trick again. Miss Luminita, I suppose this is another case of unstable voltage, right?

speaker: Real Estate Developer
content: ...Miss Luminita?
The expected reply never comes, leaving only complete silence surrounding you. You turn around.
Luminita is gone.
Bang!

All the open doors throughout the building suddenly slam shut in unison, the rotten floor beneath your feet shuddering upon the tremendous noise. Footsteps, alternating between light and heavy, materialize out of thin air. In the pitch-black darkness, shadowy figures seem to dart past, their shrill laughter echoing around you.

The darkness heightens your senses, making everything around you feel contaminated with dread. A sharp ringing fills your ears as your heart pounds like a drumbeat echoing throughout your body. A chill slowly creeps up your spine.

But what troubles you even more is that since these disturbances began, the shackles connecting you to Luminita have grown extremely weak. This usually indicates the safety of the Sinner is threatened—not a good sign at all.
This realization overrides your instinctive fear. You need to find her quickly. As you prepare to move, a hand suddenly grabs the hem of your coat with desperate strength.

speaker: Real Estate Developer
content: Oh no... there really are ghosts... Hey! Where are you going?

speaker: Real Estate Developer
content: You do know what you're doing, right? Just get me out of here first! Once we're safe, I'll pay you however much you want!
My responsibility to the Sinner comes first. I need to check on Luminita's condition.

The Bureau has already screened this place for Corruptor risks, and I haven't detected any abnormal Mania fluctuations. If you're afraid to leave on your own, find a safe spot and wait for me to return.

You shake off his grip, but barely take a step before his hand clamps around your arm again. From the cracked walls comes a shrill, skittering laughter—mocking your struggle, sending a chill down your spine.

speaker: Real Estate Developer
content: Don't push it! You brought this Sinner here, and now she's run off because she clearly knew there was something wrong with this place. When they start looking for someone to blame, you'll also be in line!

speaker: Real Estate Developer
content: Should've known better than to trust some two-bit agent. Takes the money and can't even do the job right! **** it...
His barrage of offensive words shows no signs of abating. You have borne this man's shameless behavior for far too long, reaching the limits of your tolerance.
You know exactly how this demolition project really works, and who'll take the fall when it's over.
I don't have time for this. Let go!

speaker: Real Estate Developer
content: You... Ouch!
Exhausted by his shameless arguments, you use a swift, practiced movement to break free from his grip and immediately head deeper into the corridor.

Within moments, the developer's footsteps echo behind you. You have no energy to worry about him now as you focus all your attention on the fragile shackle connection, trying to pinpoint Luminita's exact location.

The aged floorboards groan under your weight as indistinct laughter and whispers echo through the air. You feel your way forward in the darkness, unable to see clearly, but you sense something lurking in the shadows, its gaze fixed on your back.
The shackles lead you to a narrow door at the far end of the corridor. Without hesitation, you slam it open.
Luminita!
You can hardly call this a room. It's cramped, disordered, and crammed with dust-covered, decrepit furniture.
Luminita lies collapsed in the center, surrounded by grimy couches with stuffing protruding out. She shows no response to your call, appearing completely unconscious.
Other sounds emerge in the room, twisting and crawling along the walls and floor, breaking intermittently as they echo around you.
Home... is gone... what now...
...Why... did you take... my... our...
You pay no heed to the raspy whispers that surround you and instead rush forward to check on Luminita.
But in the next instant, something seizes your ankle. You instinctively whirl around to look.

Before you can make out its form, the massive dark shadow instantly constricts your limbs, then your neck, mouth, and nose, gradually robbing you of breath and consciousness. You hear the anguished cries of the real estate developer, who is also succumbing to the same mysterious assault.
The shackles within your body pulse in response to Mania. A Corruptor? No—you recognize this power all too well.

You grab at the thing coiled around your neck. As you release your shackles, darkness engulfs your vision. Simultaneously, a flood of foreign memories floods your consciousness, infiltrating your mind through the connection of the shackles.

speaker: Grandmother
content: My, where have you been wandering to come home so late? Go wash up, dinner's ready.

speaker: Luminita
content: I wasn't wandering! Just... fell asleep on the bus and missed my stop...

speaker: Luminita
content: Grandma, listen! Those demolition people came again. They were handing out stuff in the neighborhood and told me to bring one home for the adults.

speaker: Grandmother
content: Let me check... Oh, this? Just put it with the old newspapers. I already signed a demolition contract.

speaker: Grandmother
content: Lumy, we'll be moving to a new home soon.

speaker: Luminita
content: Huh? But didn't everyone say those people were scammers who just wanted to steal our homes?

speaker: Grandmother
content: That was before they changed management. The new developer's made it clear to us. This demolition is a government decision meant to improve people's living conditions.

speaker: Grandmother
content: This contract's got all the proper stamps, the compensation money will come right to us on time, and our new home will have better conditions and location than here. They've even got night buses there, so you can play outside till the stars come out and still get back safe...

speaker: Grandmother
content: Goodness, why am I explaining grown-up things to you? Off to wash those hands now—your dinner's going cold!

Bam. Bam. Bam. The hammering at their door shattered the quiet of their home. Before they could react, strangers poured inside—shouting, shoving, and smacking an official demolition permit onto the table before the grandmother and granddaughter.

speaker: Demolition Staff A
content: Stop wasting time. You're holding up our work. Pack up and get out now.

speaker: Grandmother
content: This wasn't our agreement... The relocation date hasn't even come. This is against the law. I will report you!

speaker: Demolition Staff B
content: Your "relocation date" means nothing. Demolition day is today. That contract's signed, stamped, and legally binding—go cry to a judge. Should've read the fine print, grandma. Only person to blame is you.

speaker: Demolition Staff B
content: You've got half a day to pack. Once the machines start rolling, we won't be liable if your brittle old bones get crushed!

speaker: Luminita
content: Mister, my grandma's really old... M-my parents usually deal with this stuff, but they're away working. So we don't really understand all this...

speaker: Demolition Staff A
content: You think the kid's telling the truth? If the property's really under the parents' names, this could get messy, and that's not the kind of report management wants to hear.

speaker: Demolition Staff B
content: Truth my ***! Two people live here—that's it. Last time we fell for the "helpless kid" act, but this little schemer's full of tricks. Probably learned it all from the old hag.

speaker: Demolition Staff B
content: Get out of the way, now!

speaker: Grandmother
content: She's just a child, she doesn't understand... Please, we'll go—we'll go right now. Lumy, sweetheart, hold Grandma's hand...

Her grandmother had never taught her such lies. But at that moment, the old woman said nothing—only gripped her granddaughter's fingers and placed her own frail body between the child and those intimidating men.

speaker: Luminita
content: Grandma... I wasn't smart enough. What do we do now...?

speaker: Grandmother
content: Oh, don't cry, sweetheart. None of this is your fault. Grandma will find us a new place to stay... Here, Lumy, help me read this address. These old eyes aren't as sharp as they once were. Ah, I really am old...

speaker: Landlord A
content: No, absolutely not. An old woman and a kid living off a pension? Can you even pay rent on time? Look, don't waste your breath. I'm not running a charity here. No means no.

speaker: Real Estate Agent
content: To be frank, with your... situation, options are limited. But there are workarounds—if you're willing to cover some "extra fees." Standard rates won't apply here. I'm sure you get what I mean.

speaker: Landlord B
content: You need to be out by next week at the latest! Clear out quickly. I have urgent plans for this place.

speaker: Grandmother
content: Could you possibly give us a few more days? Next week is far too soon, cough cough... We won't have enough time to find another place.

speaker: Landlord B
content: Not my problem. That's just how things are. If you don't own property in Eastside, you'd better get used to situations like this.

speaker: Luminita
content: Excuse me! Please wait.
Late at night in their rented room, the gravely ill elderly woman couldn't stop coughing. Luminita brought her warm water and painkillers with practiced ease, all traces of her past panic gone.

speaker: Luminita
content: Don't worry, Grandma. I've kept copies of our lease agreement and all the bills. I talked to the landlord—she can't just break the contract and throw us out without a reason.

speaker: Luminita
content: According to the agreement, we can stay for another month. Before then, I'll definitely find...

speaker: Grandmother
content: Lumy, my child, it's all my fault. I'm so sorry.

speaker: Luminita
content: No, Grandma, this is not your fault.
Her denial never reached her grandmother's heart. The old woman just muttered weakly, her clouded eyes glued to the ceiling, drowning in guilt and worry.

speaker: Grandmother
content: A house is what makes a home, and now our home... is gone... Oh, Lumy, how will you manage now?
Home... is gone...

The Mania fluctuations are suppressed by the shackles. The voice that was echoing throughout the room suddenly becomes clearer, blending with the old woman's words from the memory, prompting you to react swiftly.
You pull off the thing wrapped around your body—a pitch-black curtain. From below comes the clinking of a chain, Luminita's weapon of choice, the other end firmly gripped in her hand.

speaker: Young Boy
content: Luminita, are you okay?

A child crouches beside Luminita, whose face has drained of color, anxiously checking on her. Behind him, there's a hole in the floor—and beside the tiles, a tape recorder whirs, endlessly looping the whispers that had filled the room.

speaker: Young Boy
content: Stay back! I'm not going to let you hurt Luminita!

The real estate developer lies unconscious on the floor nearby. Fortunately, he's only fainted from fright and has no visible injuries. After confirming the situation is under control, you turn your attention back to the wary child standing protectively in front of Luminita.
You're one of the residents' children, aren't you? Are you creating these hauntings to stop the old district from being demolished?

speaker: Young Boy
content: I-I don't know what you're talking about.
The boy's denial comes out shrill, unnatural. His eyes lock onto yours—too wide, unblinking—as if sheer intensity could force you to believe him.
His behavior says enough, especially paired with everything else you've noticed: darting shadows, the prickle of unseen eyes, and voices and footsteps that seem to follow you from every direction...
If none of this is actually caused by Mania, then everything is just like the tape recorder on the floor...
...the kind of "ghost-staging tricks" Luminita has mentioned.
Are there other children in the building?

speaker: Young Boy
content: No...
For a "haunting" this elaborate, there must be more people involved than just you. Did Luminita put you all up to this?

speaker: Young Boy
content: It wasn't Luminita's fault! It was our idea, she was just trying to help us!

speaker: Young Boy
content: Those mean people started it first. They kicked us out, even though this is our home...

The child doesn't get to finish—Luminita's hand yanks him behind her for protection. She staggers upright, breath ragged, but it's not the shackles weighing her down. Her current weakened state seems more like she has been attacked by something.

speaker: Luminita
content: Cough... When did you figure it out?
I got suspicious after meeting the developer. Then I noticed people still in the building, and you kept changing the subject while probing my stance on the demolition—that's when I knew.
But I never imagined you'd go as far as faking an attack, even using your power on yourself just to sell the act and leaving yourself this vulnerable.
You were trying to make it look like a Corruptor attack, weren't you? I must say, you really went above and beyond for authenticity.
Toward the end, your composure cracks. Luminita tilts her head in confusion, as if not understanding why you are upset, before her practiced smile slides back into place.

speaker: Luminita
content: Right, I should've known. Once the Bureau and you got involved, I was bound to get caught.

speaker: Luminita
content: Okay, sure, our haunted property adventure might've had some... coordination difficulties. But come on—you've got to admit the overall atmosphere was pretty impressive. Told you we didn't need real ghosts with me in the lead!

speaker: Luminita
content: Besides, I didn't even charge you, Chief, so cut me some slack, alright? Who knew that developer would chicken out that hard?
Luminita, are you seriously going to keep avoiding the issue with this act?
At this point, no one's going to buy the "just a prank" excuse anymore.

Your words echo through the silent room. She watches you quietly, the smile on her lips gradually flattening into a straight line. The silence between you stretches like an over-tightened string, ready to snap at any moment.
The next second, a soft scoff breaks the standoff.

speaker: Luminita
content: ...You're right. Keeping up this charade wouldn't look good on me, and it's pointless anyway.

speaker: Luminita
content: Look, that jerk down there and those backing him stole the relocation funds meant for the residents in the old district. Now that they can't cover up their embezzlement, they're turning the screws on the property owners here instead.

speaker: Luminita
content: Those contracts are nothing but legal traps—no provision for relocation housing, no demolition compensation. The residents tried to hold them off by refusing to sign, but I never imagined they'd stoop this low.
So you worked with the property owners to spread haunting rumors, all to delay the demolition project?

speaker: Luminita
content: If we could scare you officials today, that would be ideal. But even if that failed, just spreading rumors about "Corruptor sightings causing fainting spells in the old district" would've stalled demolition anyway.

speaker: Luminita
content: How's that for an answer? Does that satisfy your curiosity, Chief?
You ignore the mockery and hostility in her words and continue your questioning.
Why continue with this plan even after coming to the Bureau? You had other options.

speaker: Luminita
content: Of course I knew it was risky and wouldn't solve the root problem. But it would at least save the houses and buy them time.

speaker: Luminita
content: As long as these houses are still standing, people have something to fight for, a chance to find a real solution...
You know that's not what I'm asking.
Luminita is stunned for a few seconds. After making out your expression, she finally grasps your words left unsaid. Then she lets out a soft laugh, as if she's heard something amusing.

speaker: Luminita
content: You're asking why I didn't just come clean during my interrogation and seek help from you and the Bureau, aren't you?

speaker: Luminita
content: But why should I trust you?

speaker: Luminita
content: You've never opposed the higher-ups' decision to demolish the old district, and you've admitted that the developers are difficult to deal with. Officially, you're a Bureau employee—practically in the same boat as them.

speaker: Luminita
content: Even official documents with signatures and seals can be elaborate traps. And I'm just a dangerous Sinner under your supervision, Chief. I have no reason whatsoever to believe you'd actually help me.

Her voice stays detached, as if she's merely stating objective facts. The recorder on the floor continues to whisper about "home" over and over, unexpectedly bringing to mind the bedridden elder and the child staying at her bedside.
If you really thought we were on opposite sides, weren't you worried I'd hold you accountable once everything came out?

speaker: Luminita
content: The haunting rumors were entirely my idea. I couldn't just watch the old district get trampled, so I stuck my nose where it didn't belong. I'm just not good enough to scare you off.

speaker: Luminita
content: If you're not convinced and send investigators anyway, they'll confirm the property owners "knew nothing about it," and these children were just manipulated by me.

speaker: Luminita
content: Of course, after today, there might be fresh rumors about monsters appearing in the old district and someone fainting. How many would believe it? What impact would they have? Well, that would have nothing to do with "me."
Just then, your comms device suddenly springs to life with an alert.
The atmosphere in the room instantly freezes. Luminita clearly isn't as confident as she's been pretending to be—you notice her hand tightening once again on her end of the weapon.
In the silent standoff, you press the answer button on the device, never taking your eyes off Luminita's face.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, you've significantly exceeded your scheduled return time. I've noticed that both you and Sinner Luminita are still located in the old district. Is there a problem?
We encountered Corruptors that broke in unexpectedly. The developer fainted from shock, and several children are trapped here. No other casualties. Please help send backup.
Also, please notify the relevant departments that all demolition activities in this area must be suspended. I'll explain the details when I return.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Understood. Medical team and backup are on their way.
You end the call, and silence reclaims the room.
Luminita's face is hidden in the shadow of her beret, only her exceptionally bright eyes visible, staring at you in disbelief.

speaker: Young Boy
content: Luminita!

speaker: Luminita
content: It's been a while, kiddo! Have you been good at home? Getting used to living here yet?

speaker: Property Owner
content: Oh, the kid's perfectly fine. We're all just glad you're okay, Lumy. That Bureau didn't give you too much trouble, did they?

speaker: Young Boy
content: I'm sorry... It's all because I wasn't clever enough that Luminita got into trouble...

speaker: Luminita
content: Hey, what are you talking about? I'm absolutely fine.

speaker: Luminita
content: What about all of you, though? Many people from the old district still haven't found new homes, right? And you just went ahead and signed the demolition contracts... Was it because you were worried about me? Or did someone use those hauntings to pressure you?

speaker: Property Owner
content: So young, yet so full of worries. But don't fret—there's a new developer in charge now, and we've had every clause checked. The terms are fair, and the compensation should clear any day.

speaker: Luminita
content: Still, you shouldn't have rushed to sign. You need to stay cautious—who knows if they'll keep their word?

speaker: Property Owner
content: Hahaha! If we stayed cautious forever, we'd never get anything done!
The elderly resident casts a deliberate glance toward the door, and Luminita knows that the person who has specifically arranged for her exit today is waiting for her outside.

speaker: Property Owner
content: Before, I didn't want to sign the contract. The compensation was part of it, but... leaving the place I've called home for decades wasn't easy. That house holds so many memories, and I had hoped to pass it down to the next generation.

speaker: Luminita
content: My grandma used to say the same thing.

speaker: Property Owner
content: Yeah, people my age do cling to such things. But when I really thought about it—stubbornly holding onto it just for sentiment, always looking over my shoulder... that's not what a home should be, is it?

speaker: Property Owner
content: A house that doesn't give you peace of mind isn't really a home at all.

speaker: Property Owner
content: Now that the contract is signed, I actually feel more at ease. We know you and the Chief must have worked hard behind the scenes. We trust you both, and we want to believe we've made the right choice.
The elderly resident gently ruffles the child's hair, a warm smile spreading across her face. Luminita watches, her thoughts adrift in some long-ago memory, before she finally finds her voice again.

speaker: Luminita
content: If you have any trouble finding a new place, you absolutely have to come to me!

speaker: Property Owner
content: Of course! We've all kept your business card. When we need a new place, you'll definitely be our first call.
The sound of the door opening and closing echoes from behind. Luminita stands at the doorway, thoughtfully staring at her toes, seemingly lost in contemplation.
Is something still bothering you?

speaker: Luminita
content: Oh... no, they all seem to be doing well. By the way, Chief, there's something I don't think I've ever told you in person.

speaker: Luminita
content: Thank you.
Huh? About what?
Luminita fidgets with the brim of her hat, her gaze skittering away—a rare crack in her usual composure.

speaker: Luminita
content: I heard from people at the Bureau that if you hadn't reported those jerks, and if you hadn't kept pushing for new project management and relocation contract revision, this whole situation wouldn't have been resolved so quickly.

speaker: Luminita
content: And the fact that I can still come here without any trouble is all thanks to you keeping those haunting rumors under wraps.

speaker: Luminita
content: So... thank you. I was wrong to assume you wouldn't help me. I really was too shortsighted, and I'm sorry about that.
Ensuring government projects run smoothly is just part of my job. As for the hauntings... I still have that huge stack of reflection letters you wrote during your detention sitting on my desk.
Given how thorough that punishment was, I'd say we're square.

speaker: Luminita
content: We're square, just like that? Well then, I'm going to start bragging to everyone that I've got the MBCC Chief watching my back!
Your response puts Luminita at ease. Her tone becomes light as she glances out the window, then turns back to you with a smile.

speaker: Luminita
content: Since we've still got time and you're being so accommodating, Chief, I'm going to push my luck and ask for one more favor!

speaker: Luminita
content: Why don't you come over to my place? I don't think I've ever told you where I live, have I?
Birds circle in the clear blue sky as sunlight bathes the green landscape around you. Luminita leads you to a scenic garden in Eastside, strolling aimlessly as if on an ordinary walk.
Suddenly she quickens her pace, gets a few steps ahead of you, then turns around with her arms spread wide.

speaker: Luminita
content: Here we are! Welcome to my home!
You mean... right here?

speaker: Luminita
content: That's right! Remember what I told you before? When I was a kid, my family barely scraped by. Spent most nights on park benches.

speaker: Luminita
content: This exact bench right here! Go ahead, say hello to it... Oh come on, don't look at me like that, I'm just kidding!

speaker: Luminita
content: My home really is here. It used to be here.
Luminita sits down on the bench and swings her legs, patting the empty space beside her. After you sit down, she continues.

speaker: Luminita
content: See that rock hill on the left? That was the exercise spot back in the day. Every morning, the old-timers would work the parallel bars like they were in the circus. They'd got some real skills!

speaker: Luminita
content: This used to be just an old neighborhood, nothing as pretty as it is now. My grandmother raised me here; lived in these streets long as I can remember.

speaker: Luminita
content: Then came the demolition notice. Everyone thought it was a good thing at first. Then it turned out the management played us—sweet-talked people into signing the contracts, then kicked us all out.

speaker: Luminita
content: And we lost our homes just like that... Even when my grandmother got sick later on, she still blamed herself for being careless and falling for their lies.

She recounts the story with practiced detachment, but her eyes carry an unmistakable weight as they scan the surroundings, as if looking straight through the meticulously maintained garden plants into a distant past.
You decided to help those residents in the old district because you didn't want them to go through what you experienced, right?

speaker: Luminita
content: Hmm... I guess you could say that. I just poked my nose where it didn't belong, that's all.

speaker: Luminita
content: After all, being homeless in Eastside is a miserable experience. One day you're getting evicted; the next you're freezing under a bridge, never waking up again. Fewer living that nightmare, the better.

speaker: Luminita
content: But they're way luckier than I was! They've got someone like you who can actually step in and do something about it. You've really made a difference for them.
She raises her voice to a higher pitch and tilts her head, playfully winking at you. However, you remain unfazed by her calculated attempts at flattery.
Luminita seems unaware that whenever she tries to hide something, she puts on the same mask-like smile to deflect questions.
Beyond the old district situation, why do you go to such lengths to create "haunted houses" and sell them at practically giveaway prices to people who couldn't otherwise afford homes?

speaker: Luminita
content: Haven't you asked me this before? It's just business. The "hauntings" are pure marketing, nothing personal.
I did ask before, but this isn't the same. No interrogation room, no official business—just me wanting to know your real answer.

Faking "haunted houses" to turn a profit or stall demolition isn't your only play, or even your best one. With your skills and resources, you could've easily stirred up property rights disputes that'd give developers just as many headaches.
And yet you still chose the haunting approach. Luminita, I'm curious why you're so particularly attached to the idea of "haunted houses."

speaker: Luminita
content: What would knowing all this mean to you anyway?
From an investigative standpoint, it has no particular importance.
But personally speaking... maybe I'm pushing my luck? After all, you did invite me to your "home." That probably means you trust me—at least a little more than before.

Birds still circle overhead in the canopy of sky. After a brief silence, she lets out a sigh—long and slow, part surrender, part relief—like she's finally carved out a small hollow in her burdened heart.

speaker: Luminita
content: Actually, I've never really thought about why. I've just... kept doing it.

speaker: Luminita
content: But if I have to come up with an answer... it's probably just selfishness on my part.

speaker: Luminita
content: I want to put my grandmother's soul at ease, and prove to my past self that I can protect my own "home" now, while helping everyone else have a "home" to return to.

speaker: Newscast
content: ...The demolition project has officially launched, with all local residents evacuated and properly resettled. According to municipal planning, to increase urban greenery, this area will soon become the Eastside Scenic Garden, expected to be another landmark attraction for DisCity...
Ding-dong. Ding-dong.
In the early morning, she clutched the old woman's already cold hand. The harsh doorbell of the rental apartment shrieked, but to her, it was muffled, worlds away.
The elderly woman lay still in bed, her coughing silenced, her whispered worries about home and granddaughter finally quieted—as though she had slipped into a dream too deep to break.

speaker: Landlord B
content: Are you deaf? Can't you hear the doorbell? I let it slide last time, but this time you're moving out, whether you like it or—

speaker: Landlord B
content: ...Talk about bad timing. Couldn't she have croaked somewhere else?

A shrill ringing drowned out the landlord's curses, filling her skull like static. Still just a child, she was shoved aside as strangers filed in and out of the room, bombarding her with questions about her personal information.
She had no idea how to respond, frozen in place as she endured the stares—some filled with pity, others hollow with complete indifference.

By the time she came to her senses, officials had already taken her grandmother's body away. The landlord had thrown her out, along with everything the two of them had ever owned, dumping it all outside the door.

speaker: Landlord B
content: If I'd never rented to you lot, I wouldn't be drowning in this cursed bad luck!

speaker: Landlord B
content: Listen up, you little brat. Keep your mouth shut about the death here. If this place gets a "haunted" reputation and I can't rent it out, I swear I'll make you pay for it.

speaker: Luminita
content: So I wandered for what felt like ages, dragging my luggage with me. The strap marks on my palms took a whole month to fade.

speaker: Luminita
content: The strange thing was, the farther I walked, the lighter my bag felt. I thought I was just toughening up—until I finally found a place to sleep on the street and saw the hole in the bag...
She tries to lighten the mood with a forced smile several times, but each attempt falls flat. Eventually, her gaze drops to her palms, to the long-vanished marks only she remembers.

speaker: Luminita
content: As a kid, I was never scared, no matter how late I stayed out playing. Even if I missed the last bus and had to walk those dark, broken-light streets—because I knew Grandma would be waiting, with a light always left on.

speaker: Luminita
content: But then, there was nothing left behind me. Just as Grandma had feared—the house was gone, my home was gone, the light went out, and even Grandma was gone. I was left all alone.

speaker: Luminita
content: When Grandma's illness got really bad, we couldn't even scrape together money for medicine. She was in so much pain she could barely speak, but all she worried about was still what would happen to me without a home after she was gone.

speaker: Luminita
content: So I made up my mind that I'd get my own house someday, even if only to let Grandma rest in peace. I lied about my age to get work, saved every penny I could, and met plenty of others like me along the way.

speaker: Luminita
content: But the housing prices in Eastside are impossibly high.
She unconsciously furrows her brow, her hands tightening into fists on her knees.

speaker: Luminita
content: Most of those places aren't worth half the asking price! Faulty fire alarms and bad drainage are just the start. The worst ones even have crumbling foundations and cracked walls.

speaker: Luminita
content: And despite all that, they can still jack up prices and rents to unreasonable levels—enough to scare off anyone who even looks at the listings.

speaker: Luminita
content: Only those so-called "haunted houses" are different.

speaker: Luminita
content: The funny thing? You don't even need a real tragedy. Just a little creative storytelling, some strategic hype, and suddenly those baseless rumors send prices into a nosedive.
Luminita leans forward, her eyes widening as she looks at you, seemingly seeking your validation.

speaker: Luminita
content: People break their backs their whole lives, pour every penny into honest work, and still can't afford a home or dig out of mortgage hell. And for what? Places that aren't even half as good as the price tag claims.

speaker: Luminita
content: So if a few tricks and some fabricated hauntings can knock prices down and give everyone a place to call home, why wouldn't I play that game?
But these haunted houses you create are ultimately built on lies. And with lies, there's always the risk of being exposed.

speaker: Luminita
content: That's just theory. And honestly? Still beats watching people rot on the streets and drift through life.
For every person who can accept that risk, there's someone else who'd lose sleep over it. Besides, not everyone equates a physical property with a "home."
Luminita, you're actually the same way, aren't you?
You keep saying that only a house makes a home, but after you invited me to your "home," you brought me here, to this garden.
The house where you once lived with your grandmother is no longer here, but something else remains that you still consider "home"—something that belongs to you.
She lowers her gaze, her upturned coat collar concealing her expression. Only after a moment do you hear her speak, her words measured and slow.

speaker: Luminita
content: Earlier, the property owner from the old district said something similar to me.
What?

speaker: Luminita
content: She told me that a house that doesn't give you peace of mind isn't really a home at all. And back at the Bureau, some Sinners turned me down when I tried to sell them houses, saying that they were fine just having the Bureau.

speaker: Luminita
content: To be honest, I can't quite wrap my head around it. To me, only a house that's yours carries enough weight to be called a home—walls you own, a key you hold. If you can't trust that, what else in the world can you rely on?

speaker: Luminita
content: But like you said, I've handled so many properties over the years, so why do I end up coming back here?
A gentle breeze blows from behind, slipping through the space between you two on the bench, the whisper of wind nearly drowning out her soft murmuring.

speaker: Luminita
content: I've been shoving houses at people, acting like my idea of "home" is universal. Now I wonder... am I really any better than those who inflate property values while pressuring others into homeownership?

speaker: Luminita
content: Chief, tell me... have I been wrong about this all along?
This is the closest you've ever come to Luminita's raw heart since you first met her.

Her past experience with forced eviction and the death of a loved one has created an obsession with home ownership that far exceeds normal concerns. Yet this fixation seems to have never filled the hollow place in her heart.

Or maybe that hole isn't empty at all, but rather filled with too many painful memories. And whenever she touches it, she has no defenses left but the raw, child-shaped wound of losing her grandmother—leaving her with no choice but to cling to her obsession.
You can feel Luminita's confusion and uncertainty. For years, she's clung to her grandmother's last words—only a house makes a home—but she's now looking to you for a new truth to follow.
And all you can offer in response is...
I don't know the answer either.

speaker: Luminita
content: What do you mean?
Whether you see a house as a home or not, either way is perfectly valid. It's simply a personal choice—what matters is that your choice brings you peace of mind.

Objectively speaking, nothing in this world is truly permanent. You could put down a deposit, only for construction to be abandoned. You could hold the deed and still lose the house to disaster or an accident the very next day.
Nothing material is ever certain. Maybe the true peace of mind only comes from trusting in your own choices.

speaker: Luminita
content: Sounds like you're just trying to make yourself feel better.
But if it works, why not?

Perhaps someday, you'll return to a place you once stayed, only to find everything you remember is all gone. But the fact that this place was once "home"... it stays with you—in memories, in your bones.
