If you choose to believe in those memories, they may become a sanctuary you can return to anytime—something far more lasting than property deeds, only growing more precious with time.
More than whether you owned a house or not, I believe what your grandmother truly cared about was whether you could live in peace.
Then again, that's just how I see it. No need to take it as gospel.
Having said that, you stand up and dust off your clothes, smiling down at Luminita who remains on the bench, looking somewhat dazed.

You're free to believe what you want, and I won't deny Eastside's real estate has many serious problems that need addressing. However, that doesn't mean I can justify your methods of fabricating hauntings.
Still, I look forward to the day when the Bureau becomes a place where you can say "I'm home" when you walk through the door.
That would make me very happy.
Your revealing statement makes Luminita narrow her eyes instinctively. She stands up and moves closer, her face now inches from yours.

speaker: Luminita
content: So... can I still come back even after doing something bad? Would you still take me in if I walked up and said, "Hey Chief, I just tied up three Corruptors today to haunt a house"?
...Then it won't be as simple as just confinement and written reflection.

speaker: Luminita
content: That whole speech you just gave me is part of your plan to stop me from pestering you about buying a house, isn't it?
I didn't realize there was that interpretation. Can't believe you saw right through me.
The girl can no longer contain herself and bursts into hearty laughter.

After her laughter subsides, she looks at you with newfound ease, like a river freed at last from the final obstruction after years of blockage. The current still stutters, but the truth is undeniable: given time, it will run smooth and clear.

speaker: Luminita
content: Thank you. Changing my ways won't happen overnight, but I'll try.

speaker: Luminita
content: Well, then I'll also look forward to the day you greet me with "Welcome back" at the Bureau.
The soaring bird finally folds its wings and perches on the evergreen tree beside the bench.

Soon after, the personal investigation into Luminita concludes, confirming that her harboring of Corruptors was solely to create paranormal phenomena in "haunted houses" with no intent to harm people. The Bureau consequently reassesses her threat level.
Considering the nature of Luminita's work and her personal wishes, you apply for her bail.
The day her bail processes, you arrive at the detention area only to find her gone. But the room isn't empty—belongings she deliberately chose not to take are still scattered throughout.
On the desk, pinned beneath a book, rests a scrap of paper torn to business-card size. A single line of text stares up, followed by a phone number, all in wildly scrawled handwriting.
"Personal business card with my private contact info."
"I'll be back to stay for a few days once I wrap up this job. Don't throw my stuff away!"

Beyond the borders of DisCity, howling gales tear across the landscape, carrying stinging clouds of sand and gravel. The air itself is thick with Mania, an unsettling aura that heralds the approaching Tide of Ashes.
Despite these brutal conditions, your group pilots a sand ship through the storm, struggling toward coordinates that flicker intermittently on your terminal.

speaker: Siglinde
content: The Tide of Ashes is projected to reach us in 36 hours. We've been en route for five, and the target signal is still elusive.

speaker: Siglinde
content: At our current rate of advance, completing the rescue within the safety window is statistically improbable.

speaker: Siglinde
content: Chief, given your physical state, are you certain you wish to continue the mission?

speaker: Chief
content: I'm fine... cough cough.
A sharp pain lances through your chest, but you bite it back, managing a terse nod for Siglinde.

speaker: Chief
content: The rescue mission is our top priority. We're seeing this through.

speaker: Siglinde
content: ...I see.

speaker: Siglinde
content: Then I must strongly recommend we increase our pace. To hesitate now is to cede every tactical advantage.

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: We're pushing as hard as we can without breaking our necks. We don't need a reminder.

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: Look around. Visibility's shot to hell. One misstep in this soup, and we're done.

speaker: Siglinde
content: My apologies. I was speaking from the operational standards of DisCorps.

speaker: Siglinde
content: It was inconsiderate of me. I should better account for my new team's practical constraints.

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: ...What's that supposed to mean?

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: If our "constraints" are such a problem, maybe you should go back to your Nirvana Port! No one's stopping you!
Your voice cuts through the argument, sharp and final.
A heavy silence instantly blankets the sand ship's cabin, thick and abrasive as swallowed grit.

In the sudden void of speech, the rattle of sand against the hull becomes deafening. Siglinde's face is an unreadable mask as she lowers her gaze, while the FAC soldiers instinctively avert their eyes. The atmosphere stretches taut, a bowstring drawn to its limit.
This mission was born from a desperate plea: a distress signal from a border village, soon to be consumed by the advancing Tide of Ashes. You led an FAC squad here without hesitation.

The brutal sandstorms scrambled the signal, rendering the coordinates a ghost on your terminal. That's why Siglinde is here—a senior liaison officer from DisCorps, now with the Bureau. Her expertise was meant to be the key to navigating the storm.
On paper, it was a sound strategy. In reality, you underestimated the deep-seated tension between the FAC and DisCorps.
Throughout the journey, the FAC soldiers have barely concealed their suspicion of the DisCorps liaison, and Siglinde's impeccably professional words have carried subtle, precise barbs in return.
—This can't continue. The team will shatter long before you complete the mission.

speaker: Chief
content: I think we're all aware of our current situation.

speaker: Chief
content: Siglinde is right about the Tide. Speed is critical.

speaker: Chief
content: But the FAC's concern is also valid. The worse the conditions get, the more we need caution. A single misstep could doom this entire operation.
Your gaze sweeps the cabin, calm yet resolute, silencing the last of the tension with its unyielding finality.

speaker: Chief
content: Yes, the conditions are harsh, but we've faced worse and prevailed. I have no doubt we can do it again. But there's one condition: we act as one.

speaker: Chief
content: On this mission, every single skill set here is indispensable. Our success depends on synergy.
You take a deep breath.

speaker: Chief
content: So I need you all to table the distrust. The mission comes first.

speaker: Chief
content: Whatever your past affiliations, right now, we are comrades. And comrades trust each other enough to watch their backs.
Your words still carry undeniable weight. The arguing parties fall silent, the tension broken. Seizing the moment, the FAC squad captain steps forward.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: ...Understood, Chief. My apologies.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: I'll ensure my team maintains professionalism. We will coordinate with Liaison Officer Siglinde to complete the mission.

speaker: Siglinde
content: ...You are the commanding officer of this operation, Chief ${PlayerName}. I will follow your orders.

speaker: Chief
content: Good. Now let's keep moving.
[Scene Change]
After hours of searching, you finally reach the source of the distress signal. But the sight that greets you steals the very breath from your lungs.

Beneath the ochre haze of the sandstorm awaits the skeletons of a village. Homes are shattered into splinters and rubble. Scattered possessions lie half-buried, telling a silent story of panic and flight. Among the ruins, there is only the wind; not a single soul remains.

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: The sandstorm's getting worse, and comms are completely down. Chief, searching the WhiteSands blind isn't just impossible; it's a death sentence...

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: Did we... get here too late?

speaker: Siglinde
content: No.
Suddenly, a shard of static shatters the grim silence.
You turn to see Siglinde's head bowed over her portable cassette device, her fingers turning the knobs with focused intensity. A moment later, she meets your gaze and gives a sharp, definitive nod.

speaker: Siglinde
content: I'm picking up a new signal. Faint, but traceable.

speaker: Siglinde
content: It's constantly moving, though. Survivors must be carrying a portable transmitter as they flee.

speaker: Siglinde
content: We can follow it, but for precise tracking, we'll need to leave the sand ship and proceed on foot. I've already charted a potential route.

speaker: Siglinde
content: In a successful rescue? I'm not a professional search-and-rescue dog, Chief. I can't give you odds.

speaker: Siglinde
content: But as long as that transmitter is active, I can intercept its signal.
She puts it lightly, but her tone leaves no room for debate.
Yet, you feel the fragile calm shatter. A new, more volatile tension grips the air.

speaker: FAC Soldier A
content: Leave the sand ship? That's suicide...

speaker: FAC Soldier B
content: With interference this severe from the sandstorm, our top-shelf gear is fried. How is her... cassette player... even getting a signal?
The soldiers whisper among themselves. Some check their own devices, as if to refute her. Others stare with distrust, hard and unmoving, at the equipment in her hands.

speaker: FAC Soldier C
content: Can she even guarantee those coordinates? One wrong reading, and we're not just failing a mission; we're getting a burial in the dunes...

speaker: FAC Soldier D
content: What if this is intentional? We've heard the stories about DisCorps. Radicals. War-crazed. Who knows what her real orders are?

speaker: FAC Soldier D
content: I... I don't trust her.
Skeptical murmurs ripple through the ranks, each one tightening the invisible screw of tension. The unease is contagious, spreading faster than any order you could give.
Siglinde offers no justification. She merely lifts her head, her gaze calmly sweeping over the whispering faces. Her expression is a placid lake, her tone as steady and unyielding as stone.

speaker: Siglinde
content: If you lack confidence in my judgment, you are welcome to wait here. The sandstorm will soon resolve our dilemma.

speaker: Siglinde
content: No signal means no survivors to rescue anymore. A tragically simple conclusion, isn't it?
She pauses, the corners of her mouth lifting into a smile so impeccably polite it feels more ruthless than the sandstorm screaming outside.

speaker: Siglinde
content: The storm is dangerous, of course. Prudence is a virtue. But if you're too frightened to even leave the vehicle... perhaps you should reconsider your line of work. "Died Hiding" makes for a poor epitaph.
The words are barely out of her mouth when chaos erupts.

speaker: FAC Soldier A
content: Who the hell do you think you are?!

speaker: FAC Soldier B
content: We're not cowards! We're just discussing viable routes. No one's asking for your judgment!

speaker: FAC Soldier C
content: Who made you the commander? You don't get to boss around!

Soldiers surge to their feet, their shouts tangling into a raw chorus of anger. The air crackles as one takes a threatening step forward, then another, escalating in a heartbeat from protest to the brink of violence.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Silence!
A sharp bark from the FAC captain cuts through the uproar before you can even draw breath.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Is this the time for petty infighting? Remember your duty!

speaker: FAC Captain
content: While our people are waiting for rescue, you'd rather bicker and second-guess here, forget the Chief's words and disgrace the uniform?
His face darkens, a silent promise of reprimand as his gaze sweeps over the men. The soldiers instantly fall into a chastened silence, their heads bowing under the weight of his stare.
Only once the order is restored does he turn to you, his salute crisp and definitive.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Chief, permission to lead a team with Liaison Officer Siglinde to locate the signal source.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: I do. And I accept them.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: I can't verify her intel. But you were right, Chief. The mission comes first.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: If there's even a chance, we have to take it.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Protecting our city-state and its people... that's the duty we swore to uphold. With our lives, if necessary.
Then, without a moment's pause, he fixes his attention on Siglinde.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Can you guarantee that the cassette device won't fail? Even under such heavy electromagnetic interference?
A faint, mocking smile touches Siglinde's lips as she arches a single eyebrow.

speaker: Siglinde
content: I assure you, Captain, my "cassette device" is far more reliable than your sanctioned hardware. If you prefer to navigate blind, by all means, proceed without it.
Her retort is a scalpel, precise and sharp. The barb lands perfectly, forcing the FAC captain to draw a slow, measured breath as he visibly masters his temper.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: One more question. Your planned route isn't the most direct path. Are these detours necessary, or a miscalculation?
Siglinde offers a soft, derisive laugh, the kind reserved for the most absurd of jokes.

speaker: Siglinde
content: Ah. So it's my judgment you question.

speaker: Siglinde
content: This "detour" avoids two Mania concentrations and an unstable sinkhole. Threats that no scanner would be able to register.
She never wavers, her gaze holding a steady, unshakable certainty. Then, abruptly, the edge in her voice melts away.

speaker: Siglinde
content: Believe me, I have no vested interest in your demise. Your mission's success is the only reason I'm here.

Her words linger, a charged silence following them. The team shares a series of uneasy glances. Some wear their skepticism plainly but hold their tongues; others find sudden, furtive purpose in their equipment, their movements now hesitant and cautious.
For a moment, the scene is a tableau of held breaths and suspended action, frozen by tension. And then you step into the center, shattering the stalemate.

speaker: Chief
content: I'm going with you.
The FAC captain stares, stunned. The idea that you would join the mission personally had clearly never occurred to him. His shock lasts only a second before it is eclipsed by a flash of deep concern.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Chief, with all due respect, your condition—

speaker: Chief
content: My condition doesn't absolve me of my duty as the MBCC Chief. Mania is my responsibility, same as you.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: ...Understood.
With a solemn expression, the captain turns back to face his team.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: All right, listen up!

speaker: FAC Captain
content: This bickering ends now. You will set aside your personal grievances. And you will not hold any baseless suspicion.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: As the Chief said, whatever our past affiliations, right now, we are comrades. We move as one, we fight as one. Do I make myself clear?
The FAC soldiers snap their acknowledgment in resolute unison, their voices loud and firm.
Through it all, Siglinde has been a silent observer, her expression unreadable, the same composed and inscrutable smile gracing her lips. You turn, meeting her gaze.

speaker: Chief
content: I have complete faith in your expertise. DisCorps wouldn't have sent you if you weren't the best.

speaker: Chief
content: Lead us to the villagers. Get us through this before the Tide hits.

speaker: Chief
content: Whatever our pasts, we share one objective now. What do you say, Siglinde?
At your words, Siglinde offers a graceful, immediate nod.

speaker: Siglinde
content: I will spare no effort in this mission.

speaker: Chief
content: Good. Let's move out.
After an arduous night-long search, the rescue team finally locates the survivors.
They are huddled behind a massive, wind-carved rock, clinging to one another as a desperate buffer against the violent sandstorm.
When you appear, the villagers break into tearful cheers, rushing forward as if you are saviors descended from the heavens.

speaker: Villager A
content: The FAC! You came for us!

speaker: Villager B
content: Thank goodness! I knew we could make it!

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Alright, everyone, form a line! Stay calm and orderly! We'll get you all to safety—
While you help maintain order, Siglinde stands silently behind you. She neither speaks nor assists—a statue of stillness amid the commotion, watching everything unfold like a perfect shadow.
The moment the last villager is safely aboard, she turns to slip away unnoticed.
But a weathered hand, rough with calluses and coated in sand, gently catches her sleeve. It is an elderly villager whose voice, though still trembling from the ordeal, carries unmistakable sincerity.

speaker: Villager C
content: Officer... thank you... We owe you our lives... We'd have been buried under the dunes if your team hadn't found us...
He rambles on, the words a floodgate of relief, until the moment he looks up and truly sees Siglinde's face.
His gratitude dies in his throat. His expression shatters.
As if burned, he yanks his hand back, staggering away to instinctively duck behind you for protection, his voice turning shrill with terror.

speaker: Villager C
content: Wait... you... It's her! The "Black Ghost" from the rumors...!
His words land like a stone in a still pool, and the fragile calm shatters. The crowd, barely settled from their ordeal, erupts into an anxious commotion.

speaker: Villager A
content: The Black Ghost...? The monster even the desert bandits are terrified of...?

speaker: Villager B
content: Why's the FAC working with her...

Shock and dread ripple through them. Some villagers stumble backward, while others silently draw children behind them. The space around Siglinde widens, an invisible barrier erected in a heartbeat as people discreetly retreat.
You turn to Siglinde.

Amid the chaos, she is an island of absolute calm, her gaze as unreadable as still water. The wind tugs at her cape and stirs dust at her feet, etching a hazy, desolate outline around her solitary figure.

speaker: Siglinde
content: Chief, my duties as liaison are complete.

speaker: Siglinde
content: Combat isn't my specialty. The FAC can handle the escort from here. Besides, they're far better equipped to reassure these people.
Her decision is made. The DisCorps liaison officer gives you a single, respectful nod. Then she turns, her movement a clear and deliberate severance from the people she just helped save.
Something stirs within you. You step forward, decisively taking command of the situation.

speaker: Chief
content: Please, everyone, remain calm. Officer Siglinde is not your enemy. Without her guidance in that sandstorm, we would never have found you in time.

speaker: Chief
content: You have my word. The MBCC will ensure your protection, and the FAC will see you safely evacuated. No one will be left behind.

Your voice, low but firm, cuts through the panic and anchors the crowd. The chaotic emotions settle, the frantic energy receding as all eyes turn back to you, and the wavering atmosphere steadies into order.

There is no time to dwell. You plunge back into the rescue operation. The team works with practiced efficiency, and the headcount is completed swiftly. The good news is that most villagers are now safely accounted for.
Then, in the next instant, a nearby detection device flashes with a blinding crimson alert, its piercing alarm shredding the momentary calm.

speaker: Device Alert
content: Warning. Mania levels abnormal. Multiple subjects detected with contamination exceeding safety thresholds. Several at high risk of Corruptor transformation.
The FAC captain strides over, his brow a deep canyon of concern. He scans the data before looking up. His voice drops to a hushed whisper.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Multiple survivors have been exposed to varying degrees of Mania contamination. Some of them have M-values approaching the threshold.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: ...The Tide's radiation is worse than we predicted.
His gaze sweeps over the crowd—over the frail, exhausted survivors. Some tremble as they clutch their children; others, still blissfully unaware, huddle together for scant comfort.
A heavy silence falls over him before he finally speaks, his tone grave.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: In theory, they could be treated. But our medical supplies and protective equipment are extremely limited, and the journey back risks further exposure for everyone...

speaker: FAC Captain
content: ...If we try to evacuate them all, we may put the uninfected villagers into greater danger.
He hesitates, his eyes a battlefield of conflict and clashing duty. Finally, he forces the words out, each one a weight he seems to physically bear.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Therefore, I propose... we evacuate only the uninfected, those with mild symptoms... and the children.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: As for the rest—
Before the remaining words can land, a cold, steel-edged voice cuts through the air from the side.

speaker: Siglinde
content: You're proposing we abandon some of them?
The entire gathering freezes. Every head turns toward Siglinde. She hasn't moved, but an unmistakable, sharp intensity now glints in her eyes.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: ...It's not about want; it's about reality. This is the only way to guarantee anyone gets out safely.
He speaks with a measured calm, but it's this very control that makes his words feel heavier, as if weighted with stone. Beneath the tone, you detect a deep, weary resignation.

speaker: Siglinde
content: Hah. "Safely."
A short, scornful laugh escapes her—the first time you have ever witnessed such open derision on Siglinde's otherwise impenetrable face.

speaker: Siglinde
content: Your mission is to rescue the surviving villagers, if I recall correctly.

speaker: Siglinde
content: But now, for the sake of "safety," you're playing god with their lives. And you call that a completed mission?
She lets the silence hang for a beat, her tone dropping several degrees, becoming cold enough to burn.

speaker: Siglinde
content: This half-hearted "victory"... I have no frame of reference for it. And I refuse to accept it.

speaker: Siglinde
content: I was told the FAC held civilian lives above all. It seems that reputation is just... words. Hollow, convenient words.

speaker: Siglinde
content: Shirking duty and abandoning salvageable lives because the math is easier... In DisCorps, we have a term for that.
Her gaze sweeps across the ranks, sharp as a honed blade, as if dissecting each person she sees.

speaker: Siglinde
content: Cowardice.

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: You have no right! You don't get to judge our captain's decision!!

speaker: Siglinde
content: You're correct. I have no official standing here. But...
Siglinde doesn't even acknowledge the FAC soldier's outburst. Instead, she continues, a cold smile playing on her lips that never touches her eyes.

speaker: Siglinde
content: If DisCorps were handling the mission, we would never have been cornered into such an incompetent choice. We do not accept partial solutions. We achieve absolute victory.
She lets her gaze fall slightly, her voice lowering to a quieter register that somehow carries an even more potent, icy gravity.

speaker: Siglinde
content: Unexpected variables are a given. A real soldier adapts, acts decisively, and ensures the others remain unharmed. At any cost.

speaker: Siglinde
content: Even if all we could recover were bones, we would bring every last one home. We do not leave our people to die in the dust, waiting for a salvation that never comes.
Her final words don't fade; they seem to freeze in the air, plunging the scene into a vacuum of silence. The only sound is the stifled breathing of those around you.

The FAC captain's eyes flicker. His jaw tightens almost imperceptibly, and his knuckles rap a single, sharp, unconscious tap against the equipment pouch at his waist before he stills the motion. He doesn't respond immediately, visibly wrestling with the storm inside.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: ...Easy for you to say.
When he finally speaks, his voice is quiet, yet it carries a razor's edge of barely contained anger.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Have you considered what happens if one of them turns into a Corruptor mid-transit? Who takes responsibility? Who protects the children then?

He lifts his head to face Siglinde. In that moment, the veneer of composure shatters, and his eyes turn sharp for the first time, revealing not simple anger, but the raw, grinding struggle of a man pushed to his absolute limit.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: I don't care what you think. It's FAC conducting this rescue operation now.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: And I don't care how DisCorps run your parade-ground operations. That's not my concern.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: My mission is to save as many people as I can. Not to chase a perfect, heroic fantasy that gets everyone killed!
His voice cracks like a whip, making the soldiers beside him tense visibly. The very air freezes solid, swallowing even the distant howl of the wind.
As if startled by his own loss of control, the FAC captain draws a sharp, deep breath, his shoulders rising and falling heavily as he wrestles his voice back to a measured, official tone.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Sometimes, refusing to make a choice is what costs the most lives.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Liaison Officer Siglinde, my duty is to safeguard lives. Not to use them as bargaining chips in a high-stakes gamble to prove a point.

His fingers curl into a tight fist, as if physically cramming his raging emotions down into the cage of his palm. When his eyes meet Siglinde's again, they have regained their composure, but now gleam with a colder, harder resolve.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Human lives are not chips to be gambled with.
A heavy silence descends, lasting several heartbeats. No one in the group dares to speak, the air itself grown thick and suffocating under the weight of the razor-sharp confrontation.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: If Command has a problem with my call... I'll answer for it. The consequences are mine alone to bear.
Seeing the conflict about to flare up again, you quickly step forward and position yourself between them.

speaker: Chief
content: You won't bear this burden alone, Captain. You have my support.

speaker: Siglinde
content: ...Is that your final judgment, Commander?

speaker: Chief
content: It's not a perfect solution. But in our current reality, it's the most responsible one we have. Our duty is to save the most lives possible.

speaker: Chief
content: Some sacrifices... are unavoidable.

The atmosphere freezes. In the sudden, profound quiet, the only movement is the distant swirl of sand and wind scouring the landscape, like a host of unseen eyes bearing witness to this agonizing choice.
Just then, a voice, thin and trembling yet unmistakably resolute, rises from the heart of the crowd.
...You're right.
A hunched elderly woman steps out from the line, clutching the hand of a timid little girl. The faint, tell-tale lesions on their skin are clear evidence: they, too, have been contaminated.

speaker: Elderly Woman
content: I've heard it all... your debate, your concerns. I understand.

speaker: Elderly Woman
content: If someone must stay... let it be me. I have lived my life...

She looks down at her granddaughter, her clouded eyes swimming with unbearable grief. Yet, with a final, tender squeeze, she places the girl's small hand into the captain's, her voice a fragile vessel carrying both a desperate plea and an unshakeable resolve.

speaker: Elderly Woman
content: But my granddaughter... she has so much left to see. So many sunrises, so many stories... so many flowers yet to bloom in her life.

speaker: Elderly Woman
content: I believe in you. I believe you'll help her survive. Please... I am begging you. Save her...!
The FAC captain stares at the tiny hand in his for a long, silent moment. Then, he slowly kneels, meeting the girl at her level, and takes her hand in a solemn, unbreakable grip.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: ...You have my word. I will protect her with my life.
Hearing this, the elderly woman gives a gentle nod, tears glistening in the corners of her eyes. She turns to Siglinde, her voice quivering, yet soft and tender.

speaker: Elderly Woman
content: And you, Miss Liaison Officer, thank you.

speaker: Elderly Woman
content: We know the tales of DisCorps. I believe you would truly do everything in your power to bring us all home.

speaker: Elderly Woman
content: But I do not wish to become a monster in my granddaughter's eyes. I will not have her see me... put down like a beast.
She offers a gentle smile, the wrinkles on her face softening in the harsh wind, as if she is trying to etch this final, kind expression into the memory of everyone present.

speaker: Elderly Woman
content: Let an old woman stay in her home, here at WhiteSands. Let me send you off with a smile, as I once did for my own son.

speaker: Elderly Woman
content: That way... when you remember me, it will be with this smile. Not a nightmare.
In the crowd, someone shifts. Then another. You cannot tell who moved first, but one by one, the infected villagers step forward, quietly forming a line before you.

speaker: Infected Villager A
content: I'll stay too. Cough... No sense in me being a burden.

speaker: Infected Villager B
content: And me... Let those who have a real chance... take it.

speaker: Infected Villager C
content: I... I'll stay behind too!

Their faces are etched with exhaustion, yet their resolve is unshaken. There are no grand speeches, no cries of protest—only a silence that speaks louder than any lament, a choice that hangs in the air, profound and heartbreaking.

Siglinde stands apart, her expression a mask of neutrality, her arguments spent. But a faint tremor in her lowered fingertips betrays her. For a moment, the unyielding soldier is gone, replaced by a mere witness, burdened by the weight of what she has seen.
Finally, she gives a single, slow nod, her voice barely a whisper over the wind:

speaker: Siglinde
content: ...I will remember you all.
The wind gusts, whipping the sand into a hazy veil as the order to return is given. You lead the survivors onward, while the infected remain at the edge of WhiteSands—
Their faces, like wind-carved monuments, watch your retreat until you are swallowed by the distance.
Until they are nothing but a memory against the relentless dunes.
[Scene Change]
Deep within WhiteSands, the wind howls, clawing at you as you fight your way back to the sand ship through the stinging air.
The sky sickens to a murky gloom as a dull roar echoes. On the horizon, a gray-black shadow crawls, then races, a tidal wave of darkness consuming the world with frightening speed.

speaker: Terminal Alert
content: Warning! Abnormal atmospheric disturbance detected. Unusual sandstorm rapidly approaching! Projected impact zone expanding!
Red warnings splatter across your terminal screen. The simulation map glitches violently, your safe route steadily erased by a creeping, crimson mass.

A concussive blast of wind screams through the area. Villagers cry out, stumbling and falling. You throw yourself against a rock, your fingers digging into the stone as the gale tries to pry you loose.

speaker: Chief
content: ...Is the Tide of Ashes early?
Siglinde's brow furrows, her eyes darting across the screen as she processes the data.

speaker: Siglinde
content: Yes. The wind patterns and pressure systems are converging abnormally. We've been pushed into an uncharted zone of shifting sands. Our only option is a rapid crossing.

speaker: Siglinde
content: If that storm front engulfs us... survival will be impossible. We must return to the sand ship, now!

The words have barely left her lips when the desert convulses. Dunes slump inward, the ground churning as if a leviathan were awakening beneath them, throwing people from their feet. A single, sharp scream cuts through the chaos from the rear—

speaker: Villager
content: Gods, no! Someone... someone's fallen in! The quicksand!!
You rush over. Through the shifting sand, a small figure is being dragged down. The sand itself has become a predatory thing, a maw of grit and gravity clenched around her legs.
It's the little girl, the one the old woman entrusted to the FAC captain! She lets out faint, terrified cries, only for them to be shredded by the wind.

speaker: Little Girl
content: Cough... cough! H-help me! FAC mister, please—!
Nearly half her body has sunk into the quicksand. Her eyes are wide pools of pure terror, and with every one of her frantic, thrashing movements, the hungry earth pulls her deeper.

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: Don't struggle! We'll get you— Captain?!
A figure shoots past everyone faster than thought, launching himself into the pit.

His hands lock around the girl's wrists in an iron grip, even as his own body is instantly claimed by the sand, sinking rapidly. Jaw set, he strains with every ounce of his strength against the suffocating pull.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Easy now. I've got you. Here, step onto my shoulders. Slowly now, climb up...

speaker: FAC Captain
content: I promised I'd keep you safe, and I will... Just do exactly as I say. Trust me, okay?
The girl, sobbing, nods and fumbles for his collar, hauling herself up his braced arms. The quicksand is at his waist now, a crushing, suffocating weight, yet he holds as steady as an anchor.
As he secures her, the team moves in, forming a chain from the solid ground. Hands grab the girl's arms, and with a unified heave, you wrench her free.

speaker: Siglinde
content: Mmph!
With a final, concerted pull, the girl spills onto solid ground. Siglinde sweeps her into a firm embrace, wresting her from the jaws of calamity.
But her rescuer remains, shrouded in the quicksand's grip, death's shadow tightening around him.

speaker: Chief
content: Hang in there! We'll pull you out right away!

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Don't. It's over.
The FAC captain's voice is unnervingly calm. Buried to his shoulders, he is utterly immobilized, able only to turn his head slightly to stop you.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: I can't get free.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: The Tide's almost here. There's no more time. You have to go. Now.
Nearby, the Tide of Ashes advances, a roaring, suffocating wall. Its winds shriek like a chorus of the damned, a physical pain against the eardrums. You know, with cold certainty, that he is right.

speaker: FAC Soldier A
content: No... no... We're not leaving you here...!

The younger FAC soldier makes a desperate lunge forward, only to be thrown down by a brutal gust. He looks up, his eyes raw and bloodshot, his voice hoarse like a man hanging on the precipice of total collapse.

speaker: FAC Soldier A
content: We can pull you out! Let's try again! Just hold on a little longer, please, I'm begging you!
His fingers claw at the ground, scraping forward a desperate inch as if will alone could drag his captain back from the abyss.
The other soldiers bow their heads, a silent chorus of grief. Jaws clenched and knuckles white, they stand as statues, their stoic silence a fragile dam holding back a tide of anguish.
But the captain does not waver.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Everyone, listen up! This is an order! Evacuate the survivors immediately!
His gaze cuts through the swirling sand, past the others, and locks directly onto you. His voice carries a note of grim apology.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Chief, forgive my failure. I couldn't see this through. I'm entrusting the rest to you.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Please... lead them to safety. Get them out of the Tide. Let them live.

speaker: FAC Soldier A
content: Captain! No!

speaker: FAC Soldier B
content: CAPTAIN!!!
The FAC captain drowns out his team's desperate cries, his voice firm and unyielding as he barks his final order.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Do not forget—
In an instant, the quicksand swallows him whole. The sand churns, then settles, leaving no trace behind, as if he had never been there at all.
Yet his final words cut through the storm with startling clarity, ringing out like a battle horn that shakes the very soul of everyone present—even Siglinde.
And she hears, with perfect, chilling clarity, the last words the FAC captain leaves to this world:

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Do not forget your oath. No matter what lies ahead—no matter the enemy, or the comrades you lose—never abandon your duty.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Defend our city-state and protect our people with your lives. Fulfill this sacred duty until your last breath!
[Scene Change]
Time runs thin. There is no space for grief, no breath for a lament. You wipe your stinging eyes and flee, your flight as desperate as the sandstorm at your back.
Yet the Tide of Ashes clings to your heels, a persistent nightmare that breathes with your every step, swallowing the world behind you.

speaker: Villager A
content: I-it's almost here...!

speaker: Chief
content: Just keep moving! We'll be safe once we reach the sand ship!

speaker: Villager B
content: No... we're not gonna make it! It's too far... We'll be swallowed alive before we're even halfway...
An unspeakable dread bleeds through the crowd. Whimpers rise, delicate and human, only to be shredded to nothing by the storm's roar.
The FAC soldiers need only a look. A lifetime of shared battles has woven their minds together.
As one, they turn, forming a living bulwark around the survivors—a final line of defense woven from flesh and conviction.

speaker: FAC Soldier A
content: Protecting our city-state and its people...

speaker: FAC Soldier B
content: That's the duty we swore to uphold. With our lives, if necessary!
Against the sky-consuming fury, they are steadfast, sustained by nothing but spirit and the unshakable ground of their duty.
Siglinde watches the firm set of their shoulders, her grip on her "cane" tightening until her knuckles ache.
[Enter Flashback]

speaker: Iron Mask
content: Siglinde. Your mission is to infiltrate DisCity and get close to the Chief of the MBCC.

speaker: Iron Mask
content: Keep your true purpose concealed. And do not reveal the full extent of your capabilities if unnecessary.
[Scene Change]

speaker: Instructor
content: Sig, your parents died on the battlefield. They served their duty with unwavering resolve to the very end. They were the finest of us.

speaker: Instructor
content: When you grow up, you will follow in their footsteps. You will become a soldier of honor!
[End of Flashback]

speaker: Siglinde
content: To sacrifice for duty... to show courage in the face of one's goals... If these are the virtues of a soldier of honor...

speaker: Siglinde
content: ...Then isn't that precisely what the FAC is doing here?
Unlike DisCorps, they do not pursue absolute victory or martial prowess. What they value more are the concepts of "life" and "protection."
Their ideals may sound pretentiously noble, but upholding them demands extraordinary resolve—a solitary, almost martyr-like courage. That is anything but cowardice.
To DisCorps, death is a shameful mark of failure, a brand of incompetence. But to the FAC, it is a beacon, guiding their comrades to the shores of victory.

speaker: Siglinde
content: I think... this, too, must be a form of that honor.

speaker: Siglinde
content: Then I must uphold it as well.
You push yourself to muster your strength, despite the risk of worsening contamination, determined to stand with the FAC. But suddenly—

speaker: Siglinde
content: Signal source deployed!

A brilliant arc of electromagnetic light flashes before your eyes. The expected Mania disaster never comes. Instead, an enormous barrier field materializes, intercepting the Tide of Ashes like a celestial net.

speaker: Chief
content: ...Siglinde?
You watch as the DisCorps liaison officer's elegant walking stick extends and reconfigures, transforming in moments into a massive mobile transmitter.
The barrier holding back the Tide of Ashes radiates from this very device.

speaker: Siglinde
content: Move, now!
Siglinde stands before you, shouldering the massive Rancor—a stark contrast to her slender frame. She barks the command without turning, her voice cold and unyielding.
You snap back to your senses and continue organizing the evacuation.
Pushing aside their shock, the survivors board the sand ships under the FAC's direction. Shielded by Siglinde's barrier, they finally escape the Tide of Ashes' consuming grasp.
Though the rescue operation succeeded, with over eighty percent of the villagers saved, it was not without sacrifice.
Yet, not everyone in DisCity is satisfied. An anonymous letter of complaint lands on your desk, filled with suspicion and a single, clear purpose:
To demand that you interrogate Siglinde, the liaison officer from DisCorps.
Despite the confined space and the circumstances, Siglinde's posture is perfectly erect, her characteristic composure firmly in place.

speaker: Siglinde
content: Good afternoon, Chief.

speaker: Siglinde
content: I assume this is about the complaint letter, isn't it?

speaker: Chief
content: Let's get straight to it, then.
You open the anonymous complaint letter; two pages slip free, and you pick them up. Altogether, the document is a hefty seven pages long.

speaker: Siglinde
content: Hmm. Someone went to a great deal of trouble to fabricate so many baseless accusations.

speaker: Siglinde
content: I'm almost flattered by the effort.

speaker: Chief
content: ...This isn't a joke, Siglinde. You know what happens to MBCC if anything goes wrong with you here.
Siglinde sits straight in the interrogation chair, listening attentively as you enumerate the accusations made against her in the anonymous letter.

speaker: Chief
content: "The longstanding rivalry between DisCorps and the FAC is a matter of public record. Dispatching Siglinde as a liaison at this critical juncture is, at best, a highly suspicious maneuver."

speaker: Chief
content: "Given DisCorps's well-known ambitions, Liaison Officer Siglinde can only be seen as a plant, strategically embedded to infiltrate and compromise both the FAC and the MBCC. She is undoubtedly operating with ulterior motives."

speaker: Siglinde
content: A compelling argument. Logical, well-structured. The author has clearly been watching us very closely.

speaker: Chief
content: "...During the rescue operation, Officer Siglinde willfully concealed the volatile and unstable nature of her powers. Her subsequent actions directly sabotaged FAC soldiers, leading to the death of a captain. This constitutes a clear and present danger to the security of DisCity."

speaker: Siglinde
content: That part is true. The account is accurate. Everyone saw it.
Her composure is unshakable, each response a calculated, precise counterpoint. To your surprise, she's even relaxed enough to crack some ill-timed jokes.
test
test
test
test
test
test
You produce another letter from the folder, waving it before her eyes.

speaker: Chief
content: Additionally, the FAC soldiers who were with us that day have submitted their own statements.

speaker: Siglinde
content: I can't imagine that brings good news.

speaker: Chief
content: You saw it coming already?

speaker: Siglinde
content: We were never on friendly terms. If not for your repeated mediation during the rescue, Chief, we would have come to blows.

speaker: Siglinde
content: As you've seen, the FAC soldiers never trusted me. After I revealed my abilities, they must have thought, "She had the power to save everyone, yet she let the captain die." I would think the same in their place. It's only logical.

speaker: Siglinde
content: So I assume this is another testimony against me. I'm not surprised.
You don't speak. Instead, you unfold the letter and slide it across the table toward her, a silent command to read.

speaker: Chief
content: It's not.
After just two lines, Siglinde's expression wavers, marking the first true crack in her flawless composure.

speaker: Chief
content: The FAC commended your actions during the rescue. They stated you were the first to locate the signal source outside the village. They noted how you cared for the survivors, never leaving anyone behind. And most critically, they confirmed that you were the one who turned the tide, saving all of us.

speaker: Chief
content: "Liaison Officer Siglinde is an exceptional soldier, demonstrating both outstanding capability and remarkable courage. She is not only an exemplary liaison officer, but a comrade worthy of our complete trust."

speaker: Chief
content: Those are their exact words.
You leave the final sentence of the letter unread, allowing Siglinde to absorb its conclusion in silence.

Her eyes find the words: "All FAC members who participated in the Tide of Ashes rescue operation unanimously declare the allegations to be completely false. Every charge against Liaison Officer Siglinde is deemed invalid."

speaker: Chief
content: I'm guessing you didn't see that coming.

speaker: Siglinde
content: They... defended me?

speaker: Chief
content: They defended the truth they witnessed with their own eyes.
A heavy silence descends upon the room, so profound you can hear the faint intake of every breath. It stretches on, until at last, Siglinde is the one to break it.

speaker: Siglinde
content: I... don't know what to say.

speaker: Siglinde
content: This... contradicts everything I was taught.

speaker: Chief
content: I thought as much. I've heard about DisCorps's methods of... indoctrination.

speaker: Siglinde
content: As you know, I was raised to be a soldier, to hold duty above all and embrace sacrifice. DisCorps's iron discipline taught me that any compromise is merely weakness.

speaker: Siglinde
content: I've always disliked having to make choices. I believed that options breed hesitation—paralyzing people with consequences, making them fear both success and failure.

speaker: Chief
content: I've heard that DisCorps has always seen the FAC as weak. Subservient. In your eyes, they just bow to Paradeisos. They lack a "soldier's honor," don't they? Your people have always looked down on them.

speaker: Chief
content: But now you've seen them for yourself. Fought beside them. Do you still believe that?
Of course she doesn't. This young woman, a picture of serene and unflappable control, would not have her composure shattered so completely without a profound crisis of belief.

She has seen the DisCity soldiers sacrifice everything for the city-state and its people. She has faced their unwavering, unto-death commitment to duty. Confronted with such raw conviction, how could the beliefs she once held so certain not crumble?

speaker: Siglinde
content: I'm beginning to see... that my past judgments were narrow.

speaker: Siglinde
content: Those ruthless principles, victory at any cost... they were the hallmarks of a soldier's glory. But must glory be defined solely by that?
Her voice is little more than a murmur, the question posed as much to the air between you as it is to her own conscience.

speaker: Siglinde
content: If not... then what did my parents... what did they sacrifice themselves for?

speaker: Siglinde
content: If all of this is real—these people, these events, these ideas—then which of them represents the belief I should hold...?
You see the doubt in her eyes and decide against a direct answer. Instead, you offer a suggestion.

speaker: Chief
content: The memorial service for the FAC captain is about to begin. Will you come with me?

speaker: Siglinde
content: In what capacity? I'm practically a suspect out on bail.
You shake your head.

speaker: Chief
content: No, you're not. Don't you see? The answer is right in front of you.

speaker: Chief
content: It's in that letter.

The young woman lowers her gaze to the paper, reading the testimony from beginning to end a final time. She does not look up until she has reached the last word, and then she draws a long, steadying breath.

speaker: Siglinde
content: As a teammate... I should be there.

speaker: Siglinde
content: It's the least I can do. To pay my final respects.
[Scene Change]
Silence is the keynote of this memorial.
No colors, no commotion—only a solitary stone and a photograph frozen in time.
Yet for Siglinde, that night rushes back.

Yellow sand grits in her teeth and fills her nose, suffocating. Then, the FAC soldier—her supposed rival—seizes her arm, hauling her from the quicksand's grasp. He lifts her to safety, and in doing so, gives her life anew.
For a moment, Siglinde almost believes the person he saved wasn't the girl who had just lost her grandmother, but her very self.

speaker: Chief
content: Hey, Siglinde. The ceremony is about to begin.
A slight shudder runs through her slender frame as the present moment reclaims her.
The ceremony begins.
There is no funeral dirge. Only brilliant sunlight pours over the serene memorial stone, accompanied by the whisper of the wind.

All FAC members march in formation.
They activate their communicators, stand at attention, and take turns calling out the captain's identification number.
The memorial offers no response. On the other end, the captain's gray profile icon will never light again.
Yet they call out, persistent and unwavering, as if unaware, sending the number skyward until it is etched into every heart.
When your turn comes, you call the number, then glance at Siglinde.

Not a single soldier breaks discipline to look at her.
The young liaison from DisCorps hesitates, then raises her own transceiver and follows the others' example.

speaker: Siglinde
content: ...Calling 097. Please respond if you receive.
In that moment, something pierces her to the core. This soldier, forged by ruthless military doctrine, nearly breaks as tears threaten to fall.
The devastating realization crashes down upon her:
Even the most elite liaison officer cannot raise a response from the dead.

All FAC members silently accept her participation in the memorial ceremony.
No rejection, no wariness, as if she were just another comrade come to mourn. Nothing could feel more natural.
After the final call is made, the Commander-in-Chief takes his place at the front and makes the final, solemn declaration.

speaker: Commander-in-Chief
content: He upheld a soldier's duty to his last breath. He completed his mission. He brought honor to the uniform, and to all of us who wear it.

speaker: Commander-in-Chief
content: I hereby declare this identification number officially retired. Rest now, soldier. And on your journey, remember this: we fought side by side. You will always be our brother.
As the soldier's real name is spoken, Siglinde's eyes widen. She stands utterly still, holding that pose until the communication channel severs.
The gray profile icon flickers, forever vanishing from the screen.
[Scene Change]
After the ceremony, you find Siglinde by the fountain on the edge of the memorial square.

speaker: Chief
content: I saw you were on the verge of tears back there.

speaker: Siglinde
content: Yes. For a moment, I realized... I'm actually capable of crying.

speaker: Chief
content: Now you're starting to seem a little more human.

speaker: Siglinde
content: Don't I seem human when I tell jokes?
You rub your arms with a theatrical shiver, and she meets it with a faint, knowing smile.

speaker: Siglinde
content: Thank you. I think... I'm beginning to understand.

speaker: Siglinde
content: As a liaison officer, I must learn to see the full picture. To gather all the intelligence before I can synthesize it and draw a clear conclusion.

speaker: Siglinde
content: So, I will no longer blindly accept ideologies that were forced upon me.

speaker: Chief
content: Are you allowed to say that? It sounds dangerously close to rebellion.
Siglinde shakes her head.

speaker: Siglinde
content: It's not about rejecting my past. It's a reminder to myself that preconceptions are a form of bias. And bias can never lead to the truth.

speaker: Siglinde
content: After all, the FAC members set aside their prejudices and accepted me as a comrade, didn't they?

speaker: Chief
content: Are you grateful to them?

speaker: Siglinde
content: Of course. Everyone appreciates being trusted. I'm sure you understand that feeling, Chief.
The two of you sit at the fountain's edge as evening falls. The sunset's afterglow washes over DisCity, painting it not with the dread of night, but with the promise of the dawn to come.

speaker: Siglinde
content: My comrades were right. They say people who spend all their time in comms rooms either lack social skills or have a few screws loose.

speaker: Chief
content: ...They actually say that about you? To your face?

speaker: Siglinde
content: Hahaha, but they're not entirely wrong, are they?

speaker: Siglinde
content: I need to be here. On the ground. To truly understand what it means to be a soldier. To find my own path, and the cause I choose to defend.

speaker: Siglinde
content: Like my parents... I may have lost my way, but I still believe they found a purpose worth a soldier's ultimate sacrifice.

speaker: Siglinde
content: You'll be there to support me, won't you?
The evening breeze stirs her hair, and in the sunset's glow, she seems softer somehow. Yet her gaze holds an unshakable resolve.
You are certain she will become an exceptional soldier, a peer to her comrades, and a worthy heir to her parents' legacy.

You know that when the choking grit of sand no longer fills her lungs, when the murky tides of confusion clear from her eyes—when she can finally meet the world with all her senses open—she will become something truly remarkable.

speaker: Chief
content: You have my word.

speaker: Chief
content: The real fight is just beginning. Are you ready to stand with your comrades?
A smile finally brightens the young liaison officer's face—a little awkward, as if unfamiliar to her, but undeniably real.

speaker: Siglinde
content: Always.
[Bureau Recreation Area][Portraits of OwO, Yanyan, and Shrooma]
Inside the Bureau's game room, several young Sinners are practicing with their special powers, their laughter and giggles echoing throughout the small space.

speaker: OwO
content: Yanyan, you're cheating! Help! Your flame is about to burn OwO's lion butt!

No one notices a prudent gray figure in the shadows. Upon hearing the "distress signal," the figure takes a small, nervous step forward. She clutches a tiny gray-clad candle figurine in her hand, seemingly for emotional support.

This is her third time coming here since joining the Bureau. Though she hasn't seen that person again, this place has warm lighting, dry air, and peers her own age, who she rarely saw before... Perhaps this could be a safe place?
Whoosh! A playful flame darts right past her face, startling her and causing her to step out of the shadows.
N-no... not safe. The flame... it might burn you... P-please be careful...
She gently extends her hand, sending liquid wax spiraling toward the lively little flame.

speaker: Rumina
content: Rumina knows all about candle flames... and how to handle them... Let Rumina find a way to put it out.

speaker: Yanyan
content: Oh, it's Rumina! Come play with us! Wow... liquid wax! Is that your ability?

Yanyan is the first to spot their new friend emerging from the shadows. She jumps up and waves her arms, greeting Rumina warmly. OwO and Shrooma turn at the sound. Their eyes light up, and they both come forward grinning with delight.
As they chat, no one notices the tiny flame catalyzed by the young Eastian Sinner's ability is finally coming into contact with Rumina's Mania-infused wax.
The two distinct powers instantly create an abnormal catalytic reaction. The moment they touch, time seems to freeze uncannily for a second. Everyone's eyes slowly widen...
BOOM!!
In an instant, the game room erupts in flames and fills with black smoke. Smoke alarms and panicked screams echo chaotically.
Fortunately, the safety protocols specifically designed for young Sinners activate immediately, quickly bringing the situation under control, though the splattered wax isn't so easily contained.

OwO, covered in wax from head to toe, clutches the equally wax-coated lion's head, looking utterly miserable. The hardened wax has glued one of the lion's eyelids open, leaving the head in a lifeless, unpleasant expression.

speaker: Rumina
content: I-it's okay... Rumina can help clean it for you. We can scrape it away...

speaker: Rumina
content: Don't worry about damaging the lion's head... We can just use melted wax to patch it up...

OwO's mouth is opening and closing, but Rumina can't hear her response. The world seems coated in a layer of wax, with sounds and images blurring together. Everyone's reactions are nothing like their earlier cheerfulness. Rumina's breathing quickens as she takes a step backward.

speaker: Yanyan
content: Wow... I can't believe Rumina's wax reacted so vigorously with my flames!

speaker: Even without power, the tides will eventually carry us to shore. It's just a matter of time.
content: Yanyan must look into this! I must study this properly!
Yanyan curiously approaches with a wax-coated magnifying glass, observing from all angles before moving it right up to Rumina's face. The two stare at each other through the magnifying glass.

speaker: Rumina
content: Mmph...!
Rumina trembles involuntarily. She takes another step backward hastily, only to accidentally step on someone's foot.

speaker: Shrooma
content: Owww, my foot! Nightingale, are you there? Come help us, please!
The surveillance camera flashes with a red light as a female voice, familiar to all the young Sinners, comes through the central system.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Copy, on my way.

Rumina is startled by the mysterious voice coming out of nowhere. She searches anxiously around the room but sees no one else. Meanwhile, people outside receive the alert, and a cacophony of voices and footsteps now floods toward them.

speaker: Rumina
content: Even this place is... not... not safe anymore...
The air is thick with the acrid smell of overheated wax. Murmuring, Rumina instinctively backs away little by little before frantically retreating into the darkness.
[Black Screen]
A few days later...
[Chief's Office]

Nightingale appears in your office carrying a stack of documents requiring your immediate attention, along with someone who also needs your immediate attention: the young Sinner who was recently taken in by the Bureau, Rumina.

She stands behind Nightingale now, half-hidden, her body rigid. She seems uncomfortable in this part of the Bureau she's never visited before. But the moment her gaze meets yours, you notice her listless eyes slowly beginning to light up.
Nightingale gives a soft sigh, and says a little wryly.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, this is the fourth "accident" Rumina has caused this month. Luckily, the scope and severity haven't been significant...

speaker: Nightingale
content: Anyway, here's a report of the impact and damages from the previous incidents... Please have a look.
Before handing you the document, she hastily wipes away a bit of wax from her cheek and the folder, clear evidence that she's just done handling this fourth incident.
You take the report and see the endless list of minor mishaps the young Sinners have suffered because of Rumina. You don't know whether to laugh or sigh.

speaker: Chief
content: Has the investigation uncovered any specific causes?
Nightingale pauses, her eyes filled with concern as she carefully chooses her next words.

speaker: Nightingale
content: The Mania corruption has significantly affected Rumina's mental state and cognitive functions. According to the behavioral and psychological assessments, she is highly detached from the "real world." Furthermore, she was never properly socialized during her formative years.

speaker: Nightingale
content: That's why we can only classify these incidents as "accidents." As for the other concerns... I believe your personal intervention might be necessary, Chief.
Out of the corner of your eye, you notice Rumina taking a few small steps toward you hopefully. It's clear she has no understanding of what these so-called "accidents" actually mean.
Like a child unaware of the trouble she's caused, she seems more concerned with whether your attention is on her, seeming to trust and like you for some reason.

After the "Witchwoven Folio" incident, Rumina was "handed over" to the MBCC by Irrheia. Although you're not sure of Irrheia's true intentions, it's probably for the better as far as Rumina is concerned.

speaker: Chief
content: I understand. Please have the interrogation room ready for me. It's probably time for the routine questioning. I'll escort her there myself.

speaker: Nightingale
content: ...Wait, Chief. She is quite good at hiding whenever an incident happens. After she returned to her room, she always managed to evade surveillance for a few minutes, sometimes even well over ten minutes.

speaker: Nightingale
content: It's still unclear if this is related to her "melting" ability. I recommend having someone else accompany you, for her own safety.
When she finishes, you feel a small, cold hand slip into yours.
Looking down, you see Rumina has somehow already come close, her face turned up. To your surprise, she has reached for your hand herself, and her pale cheeks are slowly reddening.

speaker: Rumina
content: It's been... it's been so long since Rumina last saw you. Rumina has missed you very much.

speaker: Rumina
content: Did you just say... you're going to take Rumina with you?
(Scene change)
[Interrogation Room]
The staff member secures the last clasp on the interrogation chair and connects all the equipment to monitor Rumina's vital signs before leaving. The interrogation room falls silent.

Rumina belatedly squirms and adjusts herself in the chair. You're organizing your documents when her movements catch your attention. When you look up, she's already settled perfectly, greeting you with a smile, docile like a small animal.
That candle hand named "Seon" rests obediently on the armrest. The two of them seem perfectly calm.
You smile gently.

speaker: Chief
content: It's indeed been a long time since I last saw you, Rumina. How have you been doing at the Bureau?

speaker: Chief
content: We can talk about anything. It's just the two of us here. No one will disturb us.
Like striking a match, your words seem to ignite something in the air. She immediately perks up under your gaze.

speaker: Rumina
content: Rumina... likes this. Being with you.

speaker: Rumina
content: It feels... safe. This little room. Being with you. I feel safe.
Her eyelashes flutter gently, like the fragile wings of a fledgling.

speaker: Rumina
content: But... there are no nice picture books here... Could you fetch some for me from my room?
She often creates her own picture books. You remember this little habit of hers. She looks at you with hopeful eyes, but this isn't why you're meeting privately.
You meet her gaze steadily, maintaining a deliberately gentle pace in your speech.

speaker: Chief
content: Rumina, there are some things I want to know about you. I'd like to get your answers and record them while we're here.

speaker: Chief
content: If you'd like, we can go to your room together afterward and look at your picture books. Would that be alright?

speaker: Rumina
content: Okay... You want to know more about Rumina. Rumina is very happy about that.
...A child's mind is so easily distracted.

The preliminary report on Rumina indicates that, having carried Mania in her body since childhood and experienced extreme trauma during her awakening as a Sinner, both her behavior and cognitive functions remain at the immature level they were before her awakening.
As the Mania corruption intensifies, her mental capacity continues to deteriorate, frequently resulting in cognitive dissonance and mental chaos.
The incident that occurred closest to the time of her awakening as a Sinner was the legend of the "Midnight Hot Spring Inn" in an old district of Syndicate. You decide to start there.

speaker: Chief
content: Rumina, take a look at this. Do you remember this place?

The video is recorded from live streams of horror content creators. Accompanied by a familiar nursery rhyme in the background, the center of the frame shows a large, abandoned wax factory in Syndicate. Beneath the soft, unsettling melody, you can hear the loud wailing and moaning of wind passing through the factory's eroded, hole-riddled walls.
You notice a slight movement on the armrest as "Seon" nervously grips it.

"The creepy legend of Syndicate's old district is actually real?! Today, we'll venture into the haunted factory! Remember to smash that follow button! If we hit 100K likes, you'll get a ghost hunting live!!" "Listen to the creepy nursery rhymes in the abandoned factory at midnight... Cleanse your souls at this serial killer's hideout with sticky steam! At only 300 DisCoins, you can now join our membership and follow our fearless squad to uncover more unsolved mysteries..."
An abandoned factory. Eerie nursery rhymes. A horror urban legend circulating on the internet... You watch Rumina's reaction closely.
Her gaze lingers on the screen as she swings her dangling feet that don't quite reach the floor. Suddenly, she smiles brightly.

speaker: Rumina
content: Yes, Rumina knows this place... This is our home. Rumina and Seon's home.

speaker: Rumina
content: My brother, Seon.
"Seon" immediately releases the armrest, then does a strange little "bow," like it's trying to be courteous.

According to the file, Rumina's parents died early. Her father had already been deceased when her mother gave birth to her after contracting Mania. She was raised by her brother, who was eight years her senior.
Her brother's name was indeed Seon, the lowest-paid live-in apprentice at the wax factory. Before Rumina awakened as a Sinner, he and his sister lived in the factory's basement.
This candle hand called "Seon" must have been molded after her brother's actual hand. It seems the siblings shared quite a close bond.
Could you describe your "home" for me?

speaker: Rumina
content: Hmm... There was a big hot spring bath... with warm steam rising from it...

speaker: Rumina
content: Rumina did all the housework, keeping our home clean and bright... Rumina cleaned everything all by herself.

speaker: Rumina
content: Inside there was another tiny room with lots and lots of picture books my brother drew. That was Rumina's safe house.
She smiles with her hands clasped under her chin, excited by these happy memories. She also lets out a couple of soft coughs.
"Safe house"...? You can't help but recall the hot spring inn in Cirrenfold that she never left. Perhaps the two are similar to her.

speaker: Chief
content: Why do you call it a "safe house"? Was it... not safe outside?
You ask cautiously. She smiles, narrowing her eyes, then blinking at you emphatically.

speaker: Rumina
content: Hmm, in the picture books Seon made for Rumina, there were "bad guys" outside. If they were all driven away, Rumina's health would get better, and then Rumina could help Seon do many more things.

speaker: Rumina
content: There was something wrong with Rumina's body... I couldn't hold things properly... and fell down a lot... and sometimes I fell asleep on the floor...

speaker: Rumina
content: The picture books said that as long as Rumina stayed in the safe house and never went outside, Rumina would be safe.
Her smile gradually becomes forced. Her slender fingers smooth the white towel in her hands, her knuckles turning so pale they seem to merge with the fabric.

speaker: Rumina
content: Every day, Seon would leave early to chase away all the "bad guys" outside and protect Rumina's safe house... Seon worked so hard, so Rumina would clean the home spotlessly every day and prepare a hot bath so he could rest properly.

speaker: Rumina
content: Seon worked so hard to protect the safe house. That's why he got all tired...
You ask aloud.

speaker: Rumina
content: They were... those ugly people who kept saying mean things and asking Seon for money.

speaker: Rumina
content: That's all the picture books said... Rumina can't really remember anything else about them.
She shakes her head innocently. It seems this is the full extent of what she knows about these "bad guys."
The video continues playing, but you pay it no mind. The pieces of memories Rumina has offered are pulling you into deep thoughts.
So the notorious legend of the "Midnight Hot Spring Inn" is in fact just an attention-grabbing internet sensation. In Rumina's eyes, it's actually a "safe house" carefully protected by Seon?
If that's the case, then why did the wax factory later... Could it be connected to those "bad guys" she mentioned?

A draft slips through the door with a soft rattle. You rise to close it. When you turn back, you meet Rumina's gaze, her eyes following your every movement while drowning in a desperate kind of attachment.

speaker: Rumina
content: Ding-a-ling... Ding-a-ling... That's the sound of the door opening. It only happened once a day. It meant Seon was home.

speaker: Rumina
content: No... I think... Seon... didn't come home...

speaker: Rumina
content: Where... did he go after that...?
Her past memories begin to blur and jumble at this moment. She mumbles to herself in confusion, her gaze drifting to the video still playing on the screen.

"It's on fire! That 'hot spring inn' is burning down! Cough, cough... Someone call the fire department! Most of these are abandoned buildings here... Hurry up! Hey, stop filming and help!" "Wait, there's someone inside... I see someone! Is that a little girl?! There's a figure by the window!" "...She's gone. Did you all see that? She... she just disappeared?!"
Rumina's expression becomes frozen, her pitch-black pupils reflecting the image of the wax factory being consumed by raging flames in the video.
(Flashback)
(The old wax factory collapses with a thunderous crash amid the flames)
(Flashback)
(The same booming sound as the accident in the recreation room earlier)
(End of Flashback)

speaker: Rumina
content: N-no... no... not safe anymore. N-no, no, no...
Forgetting she's still strapped to the interrogation chair, she cries out as she tries to leap forward and grab the collapsing building on the screen, but she remains unmovable in the chair.

speaker: Rumina
content: Rumina's safe house... Rumina and Seon's home... No... no! The safest place, it's being destroyed...?!
As the collapsing factory makes a thunderous crash in the video, Rumina's gaze fixed intently on the screen suddenly trembles, all light in her eyes going out instantly.
No good. You quickly shut off the evidence video and check on the girl's condition. You've never seen her so agitated before.
The M-value in the room steadily rises as the monitoring equipment's needles swing wildly. Rumina writhes in agony against her restraints in the chair, scratches gradually appearing over her body.

speaker: Chief
content: Rumina, I'm right here. Don't be afraid. Just look at me...

speaker: Rumina
content: Not safe anymore... Have to go outside... No, it's... dangerous outside...

speaker: Rumina
content: Going to be tied up... Going to die...
She hangs her head, her body trembling like she's sobbing. Liquid gradually begins to stream down her cheeks.
You catch the faint message in her broken sentences. Recalling your previous conversation, you do your best to calm her down.

speaker: Chief
content: It's okay... Shh, it's okay. Seon is fighting the "bad guys." He'll chase all the "bad guys" away, just like before. You're still safe.
The M-value continues surging as Rumina's mind descends into chaos. She shakes her head violently, as if trying to cast off painful memories.

speaker: Rumina
content: No, no! There were so many... so many bad guys... Seon couldn't beat them. He was... he was pushed into the hot spring bath... He was screaming... He was crying...

speaker: Rumina
content: ...There's no safe place anymore. It's gone, forever...!

The heat of melting wax distorts the air in the interrogation room as you struggle to stay conscious. Your vision alternates between clarity and blurriness, as if obscured by a layer of wax. In Rumina's hollow eye sockets, her gaze seems to hold both terror... and profound grief.
Her condition makes it unsuitable to forcibly stabilize her with the shackles. After quick deliberation, you decide to pause the interrogation.

speaker: Chief
content: If you don't feel safe here, I can take you back to your room now. You have your favorite picture books there, and stories about Seon...

speaker: Chief
content: Rumina, I'll help you out of the interrogation chair. Let's go somewhere safe, okay?

speaker: Chief
content: Would you like me to take you away from here?
For a brief second, the thick, oppressive air seems to cool down.

Then Rumina instinctively reaches forward with all her might, desperately yearning to be close to you, or perhaps just to anyone at all, like a child who will only stop crying when held in a warm embrace.

speaker: Whispers
content: "Is there anywhere else safe?"
The closer she gets to you, the more the hot air feels like twisted candlelight licking at your nerves.

speaker: Whispers
content: "Seon is dead. The safe house is gone. Where can I ever be safe again..."

speaker: Whispers
content: "I-I'm so scared. I can rely on no one else... I'm completely lost..."

Rumina's voice rings in your ears, but it seems fragmented and scattered. Some parts are filled with pain, others with joy, and still others with sorrow... These voices laugh, cry, and scream as they wander through your ears and mind, like a child who cannot find their way home.
You take a deep breath, then approach while holding your breath, reaching toward the locks on the interrogation chair.

speaker: Rumina
content: ...Mmph...
She suddenly seizes your fingers. The moment you touch, your eyes meet, and an overwhelming wave of pain crashes over you, muffling your nose and mouth.
She gasps for air between violent sobs, completely breaking down.

speaker: Rumina
content: No more... It's no more...

speaker: Rumina
content: There's no safe place anywhere... not anymore...
(Flashback)

speaker: Seon
content: Rumina, I'm sorry...
(End of Flashback)

speaker: Chief
content: That's...!
Bang! A sudden gust of wind bursts open the interrogation room door. Alarms blare wildly as you finally notice something strange happening to your palm.
You only hear a sorrowful sigh as warm breath brushes against your cheek. And then, Rumina completely melts away before your eyes.
[Bureau Corridor on Alert]

Shrill alarms echo through the Bureau as the pursuit team quickly assembles to investigate the situation. They soon trace Rumina's possible whereabouts by detecting the Mania residue left by the Sinner, though they seem hesitant about their findings.

speaker: Staff Member
content: Chief, this may sound bizarre, but after Sinner Rumina melted in the interrogation room, she's currently...

speaker: Staff Member
content: Flowing in three different unknown directions within the Bureau.
Flowing... in three directions? You recall the voices you heard while freeing her from the chair. Were those all different... "parts" of Rumina?
[Shackles Effect, Red Flash Only]

The shackles in your palm flicker as you sense the connection between you... Though faint, these "parts" exist like tiny flames pulsing with their own heartbeats, some stronger, others barely perceptible.

speaker: Staff Member
content: Judging from the Mania residue, each "part" of Rumina has an extremely limited survival time and is displaying minimal activity, so it's difficult to detect their exact locations and forms. At this point, we can only confirm they're still somewhere inside the Bureau, making no attempt to leave.

speaker: Staff Member
content: Chief, there's no time to lose. Rumina's melting ability is highly unstable. If we miss the three-hour window when her special power is at its peak, she may never be able to take human form again. And besides...
The staff member hands you the monitoring terminal, which displays surging Mania levels in all other Sinners within the Bureau.

speaker: Staff Member
content: During this process, her "parts" will be leaking Mania constantly, which will also affect the other Sinners.

speaker: Chief
content: I see. I'll be quick.
Suddenly, something tugs at your pant leg.
You look down. To your surprise, you see "Seon," the candle hand.
It rubs itself nervously, gesturing vigorously on the ground, pointing in various directions.
Coincidentally, the directions match what you're sensing through your shackles. It seems that it is also very worried about Rumina and wants to help you find her.

speaker: Staff Member
content: Chief, should we come with you?

speaker: Chief
content: No need. Rumina... just needs patience and time. She isn't dangerous.

speaker: Chief
content: We'll find her and help her return to her normal form. Let's go.
"Seon" eagerly scurries ahead to lead the way.

"Seon" stops here, unable to approach the iron door heated by flames with its wax body. After a moment of hesitation, it lifts the flame atop its "head" and places its hope in you.
You enter alone. The shackles in your palm vibrate, alerting you that you've found the first "part" of Rumina.
[Red Wax Figure's portrait appears]

speaker: Red Wax Figurine
content: Why... can't Rumina get in?! Rumina wants to bathe in the hot spring too!
[Red Flash]

She looks up and tilts her head slightly. In the depths of her pitch-black eyes, a nameless flame burns.

speaker: Rumina
content: In Rumina's mind, Seon's face has been set aflame and is no longer visible... No matter how hard Rumina tries to remember, it's impossible now...

speaker: Rumina
content: ...Now, you are the family Rumina has chosen.
Her voice is detached and calm.

speaker: Rumina
content: You and Rumina will never leave this safe house again. We will live here happily ever after, just like in the picture books...
The doorbell chimes softly. A gentle breeze rustles through a picture book, lifting its cover. On the title page, two figures are holding hands, small hand in big hand.

speaker: Rumina
content: Rumina may accidentally knock over dishes, and you'll help me pick them up and rub my palms. Rumina may also make flames and wax explode sometimes, and you'll help put it out without scolding me...

speaker: Rumina
content: And then we'll grow very, very old together, and finally die peacefully in our sleep.
She raises her face once more, but this time tears glisten in her eyes, her expression tinged with melancholy.

speaker: Rumina
content: Rumina has finally found it...

speaker: Rumina
content: This is truly the safest place in the world. There is no place safer than here.

speaker: Rumina
content: Isn't this good enough?
Sunlight draws a dividing line across her face. You look into her sorrowful eyes wordlessly.
You pick up the picture book from the floor, turning the pages.
