The pages contain outdated stories long forgotten by children in Eastside, carefully copied onto rough paper that had been smoothed out as flat as possible. The handwriting isn't beautiful, but the effort is evident, with occasional finger-shaped smudges.
The pages turned into books, which then piled up into a heap of dozens of picture books.

All of them were made by Seon back then. In what little free time he had between jobs, late into every night, he worked by the dim candlelight, copying from pages torn out of Eastside students' picture books, painstakingly handcrafting these readers for his beloved sister.
After a long while, Rumina stiffens for a moment as she feels a hand gently stroking her wavy hair.

speaker: Chief
content: Rumina, would you like me to read you a picture book story?
She seems incredulous, staring at you confusedly. When she sees you're not taking back the offer, she gives a hesitant nod.
You open the picture book, turn to the first page, and point at the two stick figures as you begin.

speaker: Chief
content: Once upon a time... two toothpicks were wandering all alone in the forest...

speaker: Rumina
content: Um, no, they're...
You wave your hand emphatically, interrupting Rumina's attempt to correct you.

speaker: Chief
content: Once upon a time, two toothpicks were wandering all alone in the forest... They were hungry and thirsty, and the little toothpick kept falling down, making the big toothpick very worried.

speaker: Chief
content: But unlike in the picture books, they never met a kind-hearted fairy, never found a golden ax or silver ax, never came across a beautiful gem-studded cottage to sleep in.

speaker: Chief
content: Finally, one day, to save the little toothpick, the big toothpick made a deal with the devil. Before disappearing, it entrusted the little toothpick to...

speaker: Chief
content: A giant hedgehog as big as a castle.

speaker: Rumina
content: H... hedgehog?
She stares at you with a dazed expression, repeating the word.
You nod determinedly.

speaker: Chief
content: That's right, a hedgehog! It had many, many spines on its back. With all these spines, it was heavy and moved quite slowly, but steadily.

speaker: Chief
content: The hedgehog carried the little toothpick on its back too, and it was only then that the little toothpick discovered...

speaker: Rumina
content: What did it discover?
You deliberately drag out your words to build suspense, and she eagerly waits for you to continue.
You look into her eyes gently and speak softly.

speaker: Chief
content: The little toothpick discovered that the countless spines on the hedgehog's back were, in fact, toothpicks, just like itself.

speaker: Chief
content: Some were big, some were small. Some tall, some short. Some were wild and expressive, while others were quiet and melancholic...

speaker: Chief
content: But they were all the little toothpick's friends. They occasionally bumped into each other and sometimes stuck up messily in all directions, but they always held each other's hands to help the hedgehog travel farther and more easily.

speaker: Chief
content: This is the story of the MBCC. The "house" you see as mine is that hedgehog.
Slowly, you close the picture book.
Rumina is still lost in your "reimagined" picture book story, murmuring to herself.

speaker: Rumina
content: They're all toothpicks...

speaker: Rumina
content: Are they all... the little toothpick's friends?

speaker: Rumina
content: They sometimes bump into each other... and they stick up messily... but they always hold hands...?
You can finally give her the most definitive answer.

options: Yes, we are all your family.

content: A hint of color flushes her pale face, and somehow, a faint candlelight appears in her vision.
(Flashback)

That candlelight crosses over the steaming, terrifying wax pool and travels to a night many years ago. Drowsily, Rumina faintly heard Seon returning home, sitting wearily at the table in the dim candlelight, gazing at her with silent sadness.

speaker: Seon
content: Dad, Mom...
His voice came in fits and starts, choking up like a child who had been pretending to be an adult.

speaker: Seon
content: Rumina has grown up so much. She's so mature and well-behaved. She doesn't tell me much, but I know... she longs for the outside world. But... perhaps I'm being selfish. I want her to be healthy and stay by my side a little longer...

speaker: Seon
content: ...I've already lost you. I can't lose her too. She's my last remaining family in this world...
A candlestick in hand, he stumbled to Rumina's bedside, yet guilt stopped him from reaching out to touch her.
The candlelight bathed the girl's profile in a warm glow. Instinctively, she reached out to grasp her brother's hand, the rough yet warm palm making her smile contentedly in her dreams.
Large teardrops fell onto their clasped hands as the gaunt teenager curled up beside her bed.

speaker: Seon
content: It was probably a silly decision to make up stories about defeating "bad guys" and write her fairy tales about the safe house... but that was all I could do for her, as her brother...

speaker: Seon
content: When Rumina grows up... when I'm no longer by her side... what will happen to her...

speaker: Seon
content: If you can hear me, please... let her live the rest of her life in peace and safety, free from harm and suffering. Let her find someone who can protect her. Give her a safe haven. Anything at all. I just want to know she'll be taken care of.
He lifted his head, his dirt-covered face streaked with tears, making him look even more pitiful.

The face behind the candlelight became clear at last. She finally saw him. The face that bore such a strong resemblance to her own reflection in the mirror. That person was Seon, her brother, who loved her more than anything in the world.
In this moment, his face began to fade away with the flickering candlelight. She reached out with a trembling hand, desperate to touch the last trace of warmth.
(End of Flashback)
It turns out that "Seon" has somehow entered the picture book space with you as well. It's quietly waiting for her touch, approaching her with serene relief.
The flame above its head shatters the moment her fingertips make contact. Behind the candlelight is your apologetic face.
That expression is so similar to Seon's from that night, yet so different.

speaker: Chief
content: I'm sorry. I should have helped you understand this world that feels so foreign to you, instead of letting you search for safety on your own, in fear.

speaker: Chief
content: Rumina... you have a long life ahead of you. Love is something so immense yet so trivial. I can never, and will never, replace your brother, but I hope you'll always remember his love. It's like a flame that will forever burn in your heart as you move forward.

speaker: Chief
content: I'll always stand behind you, watching over you together with him, while you step forward.
Rumina stands motionless, staring deeply into your eyes, or looking at someone else through you.
The wind rises, making the dilapidated cabin creak and groan. The adhesive strips on the window peel away once more, shaking in the breeze before reluctantly abandoning their hold on the frame.

speaker: Chief
content: The world outside... it certainly won't be as cozy or happy as it is here. There might be pain and suffering, but we'll all be by your side.

speaker: Chief
content: If you ever become scared or get hurt, or if you feel lazy or weary, no longer wanting to venture out anymore...

speaker: Chief
content: Just look over your shoulder, and you'll see I'm always there. I won't judge you or blame you. I may not be your "safe house"...

speaker: Chief
content: But I can be your safe haven, a place where you can rest in security and just be a child again.

speaker: Chief
content: And when you're ready again, the hedgehog will carry you, along with all your friends, and we'll keep journeying forward.
Bit by bit, the cabin falls apart in the wind. Sunlight and wood debris transform into torn book pages, floating toward you as everything begins to disintegrate.
She finally makes a sound.

speaker: Rumina
content: When Rumina steps outside, you'll always be there behind Rumina...

speaker: Rumina
content: ...Are you really?
Before you can reassure her once more, she calmly looks up and nods, taking the initiative herself.

speaker: Rumina
content: Yes, I know... you'll always be there.
You smile, and the corners of Rumina's lips curl into a small smile as well.
The space shakes, pages fly, and the cabin that once was has completely faded away. Your vision is enveloped in soft white light.
In the final moment, you hear the tiny gray girl in front of you whisper something.

speaker: Rumina
content: Rumina...

speaker: Rumina
content: ...will do her best.
[White light gradually envelops everything, white screen, transition for 3 seconds]
[Black Screen]

speaker: Noisy Voices
content:
Rumina!
Baby Candle!
Rumina!
[Sinners' Quarters]
A flash of white light, and after the next breath, you've successfully returned to the Bureau. A new note has appeared in your hand.
You hear a commotion. Several young Sinners seem to be peeking around outside Rumina's room.

speaker: OwO
content: There you are, Baby Candle! OwO's lion's head is all nice and clean again! Wanna touch it? Hey, what game are you and Chief playing? You're being so secretive! Why didn't you invite OwO to join?

speaker: Yanyan
content: Yeah, yeah, count us in too! Yanyan still hasn't figured out how that "BOOM!" thing happened before. Rumina, do you know why? How about doing another experiment with Yanyan?

speaker: Shrooma
content: Don't get discouraged. We can always try again. It probably won't go like last time. Hmph, since Chief is still playing with us, I guess you're not just another boring adult after all.
Rumina blinks a few times, instinctively looking in your direction again.

speaker: Chief
content: I haven't played with you guys for quite a while, indeed. I've really missed you.

speaker: Chief
content: Rumina, would you like to join us?
You watch her calmly, waiting patiently for her decision, her first brave step toward engaging with the world.
Rumina's face flushes bright red, but finally she nods decisively.

speaker: Rumina
content: ...Yes! I want to join you!
She reaches out to open the door, but before she even completes her first step, six small hands grab her and whisk her away hastily.
The little Sinners vanish in a flash, leaving behind only a faint echo near the end of the hallway.

speaker: Shrooma & OwO & Yanyan
content: Chief... come on, keep up!
You smile contentedly to yourself, then open your palm.
[Flashback: Cabin Space]
[First Note]
I went to great lengths to build this safe house for Rumina. I already gave her what she wanted... Why are you so determined to tear it down?
(End of Flashback)
[Second Note]
Well, your burden just got heavier now, dear Chief.
[Scribbling Noise]

I know it's you, Irrheia.
Stop hiding behind the curtains. Isn't this exactly the "anomaly" you were expecting?
[Scribbling Noise]
Heh heh... Believe it or not, I do care about her. Perhaps not infinitely, but certainly not insignificantly.
Now, I can truly rest easy, entrusting Rumina to your care.
[Bureau Corridor]
A shrill alarm blares throughout the Bureau. The corridor, once neat and orderly, lies now in shambles.
Papers scatter through the air; cups topple over. In the next instant, a dark tide erupts from every vent, pipe crack, and the edges of electronic access panels.

Centipedes mingle with pillbugs; spiders weave their threads among snakes. They blanket the floors and walls with alarming speed, encasing the modern facilities beneath a writhing, glistening layer of living matter.

speaker: Wynn
content: Chief! Big problem! We're picking up major biosigns. There's gotta be... dozens? No, hundreds of bugs and snakes are flooding the whole building!

Wynn clutches a terminal to her chest and nearly collides with you as you step out of your office. She anxiously raises the device, its screen swarms with a dense cluster of red dots scattered throughout every corner of the Bureau. One area shows an especially concentrated mass.

speaker: Wynn
content: Looks like it's all coming from... the Outdoor Activity Area!

You rush to the Outdoor Activity Area. As expected, the insect swarm has already overrun it, a writhing shadow given form. Within that darkness, an unusual Mania fluctuation makes itself known to you.

The crescent moon hangs high, insect shadows run deep; some rejoice while others despair! This granny just came for a peek, not to tear the place down. Must everyone get their britches in such a twist?

The humming pauses, then a charming, playful voice rises from deep within the swarm. As if commanded, the venomous insects and serpents part to either side, revealing the mastermind hidden among them—
Well, well. Such a grand place you've got here, <color=#fb9259>little one</color>.
The girl speaks in a light, casual tone, as if she were your acquaintance. But those grayish-white eyes hold you like a hunter watching prey, rippling with unmistakable satisfaction.
[Chief's Office]

A Few Days Later
Chief's Office

speaker: Nightingale
content: The vermin inside the Bureau have been largely eradicated. One logistics staff member sustained a minor head injury after being startled by a flying cockroach and striking a desk corner. No other casualties or property damage have been logged.

speaker: Nightingale
content: The Sinner responsible for the disturbance has been identified as <color=#fb9259>Ayiguo</color>. She expressed a voluntary desire to remain in Bureau custody and is currently detained pending standard medical clearance.

speaker: Nightingale
content: However, she has declined to communicate with any staff besides you, Chief. In the past 72 hours, we have received 17 informal complaints regarding her conduct. I strongly advise scheduling her interrogation at the earliest opportunity.

speaker: Chief
content: Seventeen complaints already? What's she been doing that even you're in a hurry to get her interrogated?

speaker: Nightingale
content: Her infractions include, but are not limited to: adulterating the cafeteria soup stock with an unknown insect-and-herb mixture she described as an "Eastian delicacy." She also presented live beetles to EMP, whose subsequent reaction caused a short in an electrical panel and a 34-minute localized power disruption. Additionally, she employed some method to temporarily neutralize the sense of taste in several staff members who glanced in her direction.
As Nightingale lists out the incidents caused by this mysterious Eastian visitor at the Bureau one by one, a headache is already building behind your eyes.

speaker: Chief
content: She's from Eastia, and she seems to know me. But I don't remember meeting anyone like her at Northsnow Manor...
[Flashback]

speaker: Girl
content: Just call me <color=#fb9259>Granny</color>...
[Flashback]
No, wait. There is someone. Your hazy memory holds an encounter with a mysterious girl, though you cannot say whether it belongs to a dream or to reality.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Her demonstrated capabilities and potential threat level significantly exceed our expectations. Additionally, her <color=#fb9259>physiology</color> presents several anomalies. The medical report contains multiple unidentifiable biomarkers, and toxic residue has been detected on both her epidermis and clothing.

speaker: Nightingale
content: I must urge you to maintain extreme vigilance during your interactions, Chief.

Your gaze lands on a screenshot from Ayiguo's apprehension a few days ago. Her seemingly innocent smile as she looks back from the center of the insect swarm merges with the playful expression in her profile photo.

speaker: Chief
content: Yeah. I'll be careful. Whatever she can do, and whatever she's really here for... I'll get to the bottom of it.
Ayiguo sits cross-legged, her wrist rotating idly as she watches a small spider trace futile circles around it.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: My, my... you're a tough one to pin down for a chat, little one. Is this the Disian way to treat a weary guest who's traveled from afar?

speaker: Chief
content: Guests usually knock before they swarm the door. We're not used to this kind of entrance.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Oh, don't be such a stick in the mud! A proper visit requires a proper gift. Everyone knows that.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Those little darlings were my welcoming party for you. And judging by all that delightful hollering, I'd say my gift was quite the hit.

speaker: Chief
content: Can't say I'm up to speed on Eastian party etiquette. So, vermin control is your thing? And you still haven't told me how you tracked this location.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Those fellows are just a bit of roadside riffraff I picked up along the way. A little flash to let you know I was coming.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: This is proper control.
With a curl of her fingertip, a small spider—silver-white with cyan-tinged legs—emerges from beneath your collar. No sooner does it touch the ground than it scurries toward her.
The spider on her wrist cedes its spot without hesitation. They swap places in one fluid motion, and the newcomer nestles affectionately against Ayiguo's finger.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: There you are, my sweet little Seven. Did you have a nice ride? She hitched a lift all the way here, and I just followed the string between us.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: I must say, hiding away inside this giant tin can... how very dramatic. Took a fair bit of oomph just to find a crack in the door.
This creature was hiding on you as far back as Northsnow Manor? And you noticed nothing at all?

speaker: Chief
content: What were you doing at Northsnow Manor? I never saw your face among the guests.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Well, of course you didn't! No invitation, no grand entrance. I had to make do, so I slipped in through the back. Word of that legendary codex traveled fast, you know. Who wouldn't want to sneak a peek? I simply wanted to see it for myself.

speaker: Chief
content: You trailed me all the way to DisCity, then stuck your neck out breaking into the Bureau. It's enough detours. What's the real reason?

speaker: Ayiguo
content: You've got them, don't you? Those... red, spiky things. Shackles, yes? That's what you call them?

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Do you think a frail little thing like me would drag herself all the way to this strange land if she had any other road to walk?
Chin resting in her hand, her eyes soften suddenly as her voice assumes a deliberately fragile tone.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: When I was just a sprout, nasty folk snatched me up. Made me steep my bones in poison—day in, day out. I wriggled free eventually, but the damage was done. It's like a nest of hungry worms in here, always chewing, never quiet.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: At the manor, I felt it. Your shackles... they made the gnawing stop. So I thought... maybe you could lend a hand and heal me up proper.

speaker: Chief
content: You're telling me I used the shackles on you back at Northsnow Manor? I'm drawing a blank on that.
Seeing that you cut straight to the heart of the matter, Ayiguo chooses to deflect instead.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Ahem. Well, you were in quite a fog then, dear. Can't blame you for forgetting.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: But that's water under the bridge! Now, even if you haven't a drop of pity for a poor, aching girl, you've still got a job to do, don't you, Chief?

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Precisely! Here I am: a strange Sinner, suspicious origins, broke into your big metal house uninvited. Your job is to keep Sinners in check with those lovely shackles, isn't it? I'm presenting myself! Go on, then, do your worst!
At the mention of shackles, Ayiguo eagerly presses her palms together and offers them to you, as though she can barely contain her anticipation of restraint.

speaker: Chief
content: You seem plenty stable to me. There's no need to restrain you with shackles.
Stable is an understatement. She still has enough energy to play games and keep things hidden from you.
Seeing that you remain unmoved, Ayiguo releases a resigned sigh.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Must I spell it out for you? All this fuss is just a brave face. But fine, if you're going to be dense about it, the least you could do is stop jabbing at a girl's wounds.
You arch an eyebrow and wait to see where she takes this performance next.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Years and years, I've kept to myself, hidden away. All so no one else would get hurt. Day after day, night after night, just me and this gnawing ache, hoping for one clean breath. One ordinary day.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: As if the poison wasn't a curse enough, Mania had to sink its teeth in too. Now look at me. Not quite human, not quite ghost! Hideous marks all over. Can't even cover them properly.

Ayiguo's body does indeed carry many strangely colored markings. You have assumed until now that they are traditional Eastian patterns, yet it appears far more probable that they are manifestations of poison, or perhaps mutations wrought by Mania.

speaker: Chief
content: You say you want to hide them. Your wardrobe tells a different story.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Oh, my! Stereotypes, even all the way out here in DisCity? I expected better.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Is it so wrong for a girl to want pretty things? To stroll down a sunny street, take in the noise and the bustle, feel alive without something chewing at her insides?

speaker: Ayiguo
content: You understand, don't you? This wanting to just... be normal?
She gazes at you expectantly, eyes bright and sparkling. She truly looks the part of an innocent, naive little girl.

speaker: Chief
content: I understand wanting that. But you're still lying to me.

Ayiguo's sob story rings plausible at first, yet it remains only a surface-level facade. The spider tracking you since Northsnow Manor, the elaborate breach of the Bureau, her offhand manner toward experiences that ought to be traumatic—all of it confirms that Ayiguo is anything but the innocent girl she portrays.
You reach out, spread open the files Nightingale has prepared, and slide them toward her.
test
test
test
test
test
test

speaker: Chief
content: Eastia's outside our jurisdiction. Info's thin, but not that thin. Over a hundred suspicious deaths with your fingerprints on them, with the oldest one dating back sixty years. Among them, twenty-seven confirmed mass poisonings.

speaker: Chief
content: When Eastia was tearing itself apart, people lived in fear of a poison master. Someone who looked like a girl, moved like a ghost, and killed on a whim. Commanded every venomous thing that crawled or slithered.

speaker: Chief
content: She always had golden spiders in her shadow, so they called her... <color=#fb9259>Granny Goldspider</color>.

speaker: Chief
content: You call this wanting to be normal?
Ayiguo leans back in her chair, crosses her legs, and clicks her tongue in impatience. A cold smile curves her lips.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Well, well. You have been thorough. Fancy that, I had no idea I'd kept myself so entertained all these years.

The shift is instantaneous, which only makes her earlier act seem more effortless. She clearly does not care what you make of her. If the deception holds, fine. If not, she keeps plenty of other tricks up her sleeve.

Anyone who stirs chaos through Eastia's martial world cannot possibly be good. She is either a murderer who tramples human life like dirt, or some ancient monster stripped of all feeling. Either way, extreme caution is necessary.

speaker: Chief
content: Sixty-plus years, and you still look like a girl. Is it the Mania? The poison? Or is something else keeping that body of yours from aging a day?

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Maybe I'm just built stubborn. All those toxins I've swallowed over the years pickled me from the inside out, perhaps?

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Well now, isn't that handy? A poisonous old monster like me, wandering loose in your tidy little city. How terribly dangerous! Quick, slap those shackles on and lock me up. It's for everyone's good.

speaker: Chief
content: You're pushing awfully hard for something most Sinners would rather die than accept. The shackles mean surveillance. Obedience. A leash around your neck. You understand exactly what you're signing away, so what are you planning to do with them?

speaker: Chief
content: You're capricious. Life and death with you is a coin toss on a bad mood. What assurance do I have that the moment I put those shackles on, you won't turn DisCity into a sequel to every massacre in that file?

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Enough prattling! This granny came to you with open hands, and you can't even muster a "thank you"? Must I show you exactly what I'm capable of before you learn some manners?!

She has not even finished speaking when a dense rustling erupts from the corners of the interrogation room. Swarms of tiny insects emerge, drawn by Ayiguo, and the air fills with their shrill, piercing buzz.
Purple-black mist radiates from Ayiguo in waves, steadily filling the room as it closes in on you. She is releasing poison on purpose! You quickly clamp a hand over your nose and mouth.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Still won't fight back? Fine! Let's see how long that stubborn body of yours holds out!

With Ayiguo's movements, the M-value in the interrogation room spikes sharply. Alarms blare, and red warning lights wash over everything. Something writhes and churns beneath her skin, inside her vessels, as if her veins carry not blood, but a tide of insects.

Window frames and door frames groan; even the steel-reinforced concrete strains under the pressure. If you hesitate any longer, the interrogation room will buckle under the force of the Mania, and poison will seep through every fissure into the world beyond. She is forcing your hand.
The shackles' crimson light tears through the poisonous fog, coiling straight for Ayiguo. Her body convulses hard as insects rain from the walls and ceiling in a pattering downpour.

She spits a mouthful of blood—purple-black gore alive with writhing things. Still, she laughs in triumph, utterly indifferent to the wretched sight she presents with blood pouring from her lips and nose.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Yes... there! It works! It really works!
You immediately withdraw the shackles.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Why did you stop?! Keep going! Now!

speaker: Chief
content: That's enough. You caught me off guard once. I won't be maneuvered twice.

speaker: Chief
content: I'll have Nightingale arrange maximum security, isolation, and full surveillance. Your movement will be restricted, and any access to me or the shackles will be cut off completely. Unless you're ready to tell me why you're really here. You want the shackles? Trade me the truth.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Questions, questions, questions! Good grief! You Disians are so complicated! Won't use them, won't stop using them, always have to poke and prod and interrogate everything!

speaker: Ayiguo
content: I told you to use the shackles. So use them. Don't think for a second I won't poison you mute, hollow out that busy little mind of yours, and make you my puppet. Then you'll use them whenever I say!
[Flashback]

speaker: Girl
content: Just call me <color=#fb9259>Granny</color>. Look at you, head full of cotton, can't remember your own name, probably. What's the point of explaining?

speaker: Girl
content: Don't bother with thanks. Granny just brushed some snow off. If you'd gone and kicked the bucket here, all my running around this godforsaken manor all day would've been for nothing!
[Flashback]
Your confrontation with Ayiguo stirs something deep inside. Hazy memories of Northsnow Manor sharpen and come clear.

speaker: Chief
content: It's coming back now. You can't actually control people with your poison, can you? Otherwise, you would have done it back at the manor instead of playing tag with your insects all the way here.
You finish laying out your theory, and she falls abruptly silent. You have struck true.

The interrogation room lights flicker, mirroring Ayiguo's volatile mood. One moment she grits her teeth in apparent fury; the next, she shifts into languid indifference. The poison thins and dissipates, the insect swarm recedes, and she resumes her former appearance. She seems to be out of tricks. Unable to overpower you, she has little choice but to negotiate.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: You ungrateful little brat. Since you remember this granny saved your hide, shouldn't you be showing a bit of gratitude instead of all this suspicion?

speaker: Ayiguo
content: I wasn't sure about those shackles of yours before. Poked at them a few times but couldn't get them to bite. Coming here was a gamble, I'll admit. But now? Now I know they work beautifully. And what I told you before wasn't all lies.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Using them on me costs you nothing. You even get a dangerous granny on a leash. I fail to see the hesitation. For one so young, you're more tangled than a spider's web.
After that exchange, you are certain beyond any doubt that she truly came for the shackles, and her obsession with them runs deep.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Oh... is that it? You're afraid that if you use them on me, I'll flip the leash around and lead you? How does a coward like you manage a whole bureau of Sinners? Did you whimper and beg your way into that chair?

She props her feet up on the armrest and lets words tumble out unchecked, though her eyes stay vacant and far away as though she is savoring some private memory. Perhaps the shackles really do relieve her suffering, as she says, if only for that fleeting moment.

speaker: Chief
content: The shackles go both ways. I'm not taking that risk on a dare. You'll stay at the Bureau for now. Supervised, basic quarters. Until we have some actual trust to build on.

speaker: Chief
content: During that time, if you try to move your swarms, release toxins, or threaten anyone, the arrangement ends. I'll contact the Eastian authorities and have you deported.
Ayiguo stares at you in silence, her eyes calm and cold as a spider's. She appears to weigh the odds of a successful cooperation.

Something skitters through the shadows, its scraping sounds deeply unsettling. Ayiguo's gaze sharpens into something vicious, though held in check. At last, it softens into stillness, and the world around her quiets in turn.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Well, well. A stubborn little stone, aren't you? It's been ages since anyone made this granny work this hard.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Fine, then. I'll be gracious and allow you the privilege of serving me.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: But let's be clear. You'd best keep the food coming and the entertainment lively. Keep this granny nice and comfortable. Otherwise... Well, I can't promise one of my little darlings won't get bored and wander off to nibble on someone.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: This granny has all the time in the world. I CAN WAIT YOU OUT.
Her threat delivered, Ayiguo hops down from the chair and turns to go. Without warning, she staggers, crumples to the floor, and curls into herself, her face twisting with pain.
Instinct moves you to reach out and help her—

speaker: Ayiguo
content: This old body's soaked in poison, you foolish brat! Do you have a death wish?!

Ayiguo swats your hand aside. Her voice emerges hoarse. Even speech seems to cost her tremendous effort. She recovers on the floor for several minutes, then forces herself upright and staggers out of the interrogation room, leaving you alone to process what has just happened.
Ayiguo unsettles you more deeply than other Sinners. It is not merely her uncanny command over vermin and serpents; it is the warp of her logic at the root.

What others fear and loathe, she names her little darlings with genuine affection. An invasive breach, in her mind, is merely dropping by. She claims she wants the shackles to mend her body, to live as an ordinary girl, and yet that ordinary wish sounds anything but ordinary on her tongue.
You look down at the two documents resting on the desk: one a fragmented file spanning decades, the other a medical report riddled with unknowns...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Nightingale, send Ayiguo's medical report to Banyan Medical College. I need their assistance.
Since the interrogation, you have been waiting to see what Ayiguo does next.
Strangely, the past few days have passed in utter quiet. There is no sign of action. You do not spot so much as a single insect. Rather than putting you at ease, the silence only deepens your unease.
As if to confirm your premonition, a knock comes at your office door.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief. Sinner Ayiguo left her supervised zone three minutes ago.

speaker: Chief
content: How did she get out? Reason?

speaker: Nightingale
content: Method of departure unconfirmed. Security doors are intact. No alarms were triggered. Internal surveillance shows 3.7 seconds of anomalous interference. After that window, she was gone.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Her motive remains unclear, but the bio-monitoring system flagged an unusually high-frequency bioelectricity resonance signal.

You set up this system specifically to monitor the insects surrounding Ayiguo. After days of observation, you confirm that these spiders and crawling vermin lack any intelligence of their own. They merely follow Ayiguo's will.
Yet it is less a command and more a shared consciousness with Ayiguo. She controls them without a single physical gesture.
You have never seen anything like this. It bears no resemblance to a Mania-induced mutation. Rather, it appears to be... some mysterious power from Eastia.
Under Nightingale's control, the system decodes the signal and converts it to audio.

speaker: Faye
content: ...Intel's solid, I'm telling you. Underground auction, Eastside. Star item... you've ever heard of "Genesis Powder"? Old Eastian secret recipe. The rumors are wild. Some say it can bring dead wood back to bloom... Starting bid's through the roof.

speaker: Faye
content: But word from the inside says it's bad news. No known source, no ingredient list. It's flagged as high-risk contraband... Me? Hard pass. Way too creepy for my taste.
The noise-reduced dialogue comes through with perfect clarity. It is Faye's voice, and what you hear is shocking. You take the terminal, your heart sinking.

speaker: Chief
content: Her insects caught this conversation. She's after the powder.

speaker: Nightingale
content: That's the assessment, yes. She also left this behind.
Nightingale hands you a note. The handwriting is crooked and uneven, as if a spider has just crawled across the page. It bears only a single cryptic sentence:
Going to buy some cosmetics. Be back soon!

speaker: Nightingale
content: Should I organize a pursuit team?

speaker: Chief
content: No. Her temperament is unstable, and her methods are unpredictable. A rushed grab in public could escalate into a city-wide incident.

speaker: Chief
content: She left those breadcrumbs for a reason. She wants me to follow. Prep a vehicle. We're heading to Eastside.
You stand up and grab your coat from the chair.

speaker: Chief
content: One more thing, contact Banyan Medical College. Tell them I need her physical examination results the moment the analysis is complete.

speaker: Chief
content: Notify the Public Security Bureau. I want a discreet perimeter around the auction venue, but no visible presence.

speaker: Chief
content: Until we know what she's actually after, she doesn't get within arm's reach of that Genesis Powder. An unevaluated high-risk item in her possession is not an option.
(Scene change)

Afternoon
Eastside Underground Auction

Through a secret door disguised as an embossed wall, you ascend a spiral staircase carpeted in deep purple velvet. You obtained the auction's address and invitation by threatening Faye, and now you put on the mask the venue provides.
At the top of the staircase lies a circular hall with soaring ceilings. Guests are seated in small clusters, giving the scene the appearance of an ordinary business reception.

Your arrival draws little attention. Once you settle onto a corner sofa, you quickly spot a figure in the VIP section diagonally opposite—Ayiguo. She is not wearing a mask, and her Eastian attire stands out brazenly among the crowd.

speaker: Guest 1
content: What's the story with that Outland girl? Three bids in, and suddenly nobody wants to raise a paddle.

speaker: Guest 2
content: No clue, but she must be connected. Look, she hasn't touched a single other lot all afternoon. Only has eyes for the Genesis Powder.

speaker: Guest 1
content: So the powder's legit, then? Some kind of Eastian miracle cure? Damn. Should've thrown in when I had the chance...

speaker: Guest 2
content: Shh... Keep your voice down. You didn't see? The guy bidding against her went white as a sheet and bolted. Staff didn't say a word. When's the last time a finale item closed in three rounds? She's got juice. The kind that makes auction houses nervous.
According to what those two just said, Ayiguo has already secured the Genesis Powder.

You rise and approach her, betraying no emotion. Dozens of nearly invisible black specks are crawling out from the collars and cuffs of other guests, quietly making their way back into her sleeves. To your surprise, Ayiguo seems to sense your presence. She stands gracefully to greet you and raises her glass in salute.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: My, my. Granny doesn't recall raising such a clingy little pest. Tsk, tsk. And here I thought you'd learned to behave.

speaker: Chief
content: Impressive resources you've got. If you can afford to bid like that, why bother using insects to scare off the competition?

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Save when you should, spend when you must. I didn't rob anyone blind, and that's me being polite, little one. If something caught your eye, just say so. Make this granny smile, and perhaps I'll buy it for you.

speaker: Chief
content: You left supervision. That violates the terms we set. Walk away now, and we can still settle this quietly.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Threatening this granny? How unseemly. Didn't I leave you a perfectly lovely note?

Though the auction has ended, many people linger to chat and mingle. Unwilling to cause a scene, you decide to play along with Ayiguo's banter and wait for an opportunity to persuade her to return to the Bureau.

speaker: Chief
content: Your abilities are too volatile. I can't let you wander Eastside unchecked. Come back to the Bureau before this gets worse.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Tch. There's an old Eastian saying, child. "Sending a god away is hard. Inviting one? Even harder." Do you know why?

speaker: Chief
content: Isn't it "inviting a god is easy but sending one away is hard"? Anyway, what's your point?

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Because... gods don't take orders. I came all this way. I'm not leaving with nothing but a scolding.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: You didn't come alone, did you? All those little shadows outside... are they here to escort this granny home? Or drag her?
Ayiguo sees right through your plan, yet she gives nothing away. Instead, she patiently engages you in this verbal dance. She is waiting for something.

speaker: Waiter
content: Your item, ma'am.
She is waiting for the Genesis Powder.

The attendant appears at precisely this moment. Your gaze and hers fall upon the velvet tray at once. A transparent crystal bottle holds a strange greenish-purple liquid, black specks roiling inside like bubbles.
Ayiguo reaches for it. You move first, pressing your hand down on the edge of the tray.

speaker: Chief
content: This item needs inspection first.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: What?! On what grounds? This granny paid good money for that!

speaker: Chief
content: It's not a request. Unknown hazardous materials require inspection and registration by the technical department.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Dangerous, my spider leg! There isn't a poison in this world more dangerous than this granny herself! Now hand it over!

speaker: Chief
content: You're standing on DisCity soil. You're on the MBCC roster. That means MBCC rules. Now tell me, what exactly do you intend to do with this?
Beads of sweat now dot Ayiguo's forehead, her brows drawn tightly together. Her tone turns agitated, simmering with frustration.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: What do I want? I want to live! I came to you for the shackles, and you refused. I try to find my own remedy, and you block that too. You're leaving me no road to walk!

With a violent swat, she knocks your hand away and lunges for the crystal bottle. But you have already moved. You push the attendant aside and seize the entire tray. Ayiguo's hand closes on empty air.

speaker: Chief
content: We can find a solution, but not with something unvetted. Not like this.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Hah! Easy words from someone who isn't rotting from the inside out. If there were another way, do you think this granny would've spent decades swallowing poison just to survive?
She lunges forward without warning, her poisonous breath coming close enough to graze your face.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: I see you now. Clear as glass. You're just another coward wearing honest skin. All those pretty words about trust and cooperation... Spare me. You're afraid my poison will stain your precious Eastside. Afraid this mad old dog will bite your reputation to shreds!

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Listen well. I'm taking that Genesis Powder. You won't save me? Fine. I'll save myself! This granny has been beautiful her whole long life, and I refuse to rot away in your little city!

Following Ayiguo's threats, commotion erupts in the corners of the auction hall. Just as at the Bureau earlier, swarms of snakes, insects, rats, and ants pour in. Guests scream and scatter in all directions.

speaker: Chief
content: Can't get your way, so you throw a tantrum? That's cheap.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Why should I play fair in your city? Nobody here knows this granny anyway!
A thin snake coiled on the chandelier suddenly drops like a black bolt of lightning, striking precisely toward the crystal bottle in your hand.
You react without hesitation, raising your hand to release your shackles. The snake is blasted backward, its tail falling limp as the crystal bottle slips from your grasp and flies into the air.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Mine!!
Almost simultaneously, you both leap into the air. Your goal is to intercept the crystal bottle, while Ayiguo lunges desperately to seize it. Your fingertips cross in mid-air.

speaker: Chief
content: Enough.
You hold the height advantage and reach the bottle first.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Let go! You're stealing from me and acting righteous about it?! Give it here!

The force of your struggle pops the stopper off with a sharp crack. Viscous, dark green liquid tinged with purple spills through the air. By sheer coincidence, most of it pours directly into a wine glass Ayiguo has somehow grabbed with her other hand.
Hiss—
The poison mixes with the strong liquor and releases a bubbling, corrosive sound. You and Ayiguo both freeze, staring at the strange liquid roiling in the glass.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Fine then... this way's faster.
Before you can stop her, she tilts her head back and drains the glass in one swift gulp, swallowing the entire mixture of poison and liquor. A triumphant laugh slips from her lips.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Haha! You little brat, think you can outsmart this granny? You're still far from—

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Urgh—! Ahhh—!!
Her laughter cuts off without warning, transforming into agonized shrieks.
She doubles over violently, hands clawing desperately at her throat, as though something is tearing her apart from within.

Her once fair, smooth face is instantly covered in deep wrinkles, like ravines carved into stone. Greenish-blue veins bulge violently along the side of her neck and spread like a spider web across half her face. Insect-shaped shadows writhe beneath the skin, then break through to the surface, crawling across her face in a truly horrifying sight.
You quickly remove your coat, meaning to cover Ayiguo, but she dodges out of reach.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: My face... What's happening to my face?!
In the reflection of the glass display case, Ayiguo sees her face. One half remains youthful; the other is a horrifying visage, aging rapidly before her eyes.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: AAAAHHHHH!!!

Her shriek detonates chaos. Black ripples of Mania explode outward with her at the epicenter, and the hall's M-value skyrockets in an instant. The auction house transforms into a toxic den as guests scream and flee in blind panic.

You push through the lethal poison and Mania contamination, trying to close the distance, but the swarm reacts faster. Spiders pour from Ayiguo's body in all directions, spewing venom-laced silk that weaves itself into a massive web glowing with an eerie green light. Within moments, it envelops the entire hall and wraps Ayiguo in countless layers.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Eugene, move in with Public Security. Full evacuation. Lock down every block surrounding this location!
At the center of the web, an ominous cocoon is already taking shape with alarming speed.

speaker: Eugene
content: Copy that! Backup's en route. Poison specialists are being scrambled. Chief, keep yourself breathing until they arrive!
Your terminal vibrates. The report from Banyan Medical College comes through. You scroll through the screen without hesitation—

...The subject's physiological age is estimated to be 100 years or older. Over one hundred distinct toxic compounds coexist within her body. It is presumed that she has long consumed exotic poisons, relying on the mutual balance among these toxins to sustain her vital functions... ...An unknown venomous agent has been detected within the subject. This toxin is not parasitic but rather an inherent component of her biological makeup... The subject displays extraordinary resilience. Her survival to the present day is nothing short of miraculous. Current medical science offers no means of intervening in her condition. WARNING: Any external intervention risks disrupting the existing equilibrium, leading to complete systemic collapse...
You scroll to the end, where the special notation section glares in red:
DO NOT make direct contact. She IS the poison itself.
(Scene change)

speaker: Ayiguo
content: This old body's soaked in poison, you foolish brat! Do you have a death wish?!
(Scene change)

speaker: Ayiguo
content: What do I want? I want to live! I came to you for the shackles, and you refused. I try to find my own remedy, and you block that too. You're leaving me no road to walk!
(Scene change)

You approach the massive cocoon. Muffled, inhuman whimpers emanate from somewhere deep within. The venomous silk continues to thicken as the runaway Mania and toxins are forcibly contained inside. The immense energy building within stretches the silk cocoon until it becomes nearly translucent.
Even before losing consciousness, she was instinctively containing the damage.

speaker: Chief
content: Ayiguo? Can you hear me?
The insects around you begin to converge toward the cocoon. A small spider drops from your body, pushes aside the dense venomous silk, and crawls toward Ayiguo.
Is that Seven? Or Eight? Who knows when she planted yet another spider on you?

Could it be that she knew you would come all along, yet she still waited here, risking capture. Her condition must be far graver than you imagine, grave enough that she has to take that poison without delay.
<color=#fb9259>Whether in Eastia or DisCity, everything she has ever done is to survive.</color>
You sink into thought. Through the comms, Eugene's anxious voice pulls you back to the present.

speaker: Eugene
content: Chief! Toxin concentration at the venue is 700% over the limit! You need to evacuate, now!

speaker: Eugene
content: Chief! You must—

speaker: Chief
content: Notify the perimeter. Expand the evacuation zone. Ten kilometers, minimum. Toxin specialists and security team in maximum-grade hazmat. Contain the spread of poison and Mania. Clean what you can.
You pause for a brief second, then speak into the terminal with a renewed sense of resolve.

speaker: Chief
content: I'm going in.

speaker: Eugene
content: What?! Chief, the concentration inside that cocoon—

speaker: Chief
content: She's my Sinner.
You press your hand against the wall of the cocoon. It feels alive beneath your touch, a faint pulse throbbing steadily under your palm.

Your mind drifts back to the tense standoff in the interrogation room. She was already at the end of her strength back then; all that pain and desperation were genuine. Even though you know she cannot hear you from inside, you lean in closer to the cocoon.

speaker: Chief
content: You couldn't wait any longer. Why didn't you say something back then? What happened to you... that made trusting anyone this impossible?
You have missed the best chance to help her. You will not let a second one slip away.

speaker: Chief
content: If you won't tell me yourself, then I'll see it with my own eyes.

Static crackles across the comms before the Mania cuts the line entirely. The poison threads sense your touch and part in silence, revealing a narrow opening. Just as you have done countless times before, you step into the massive cocoon and enter the Mania without hesitation.

Eerie purple mist drags you forward, and in an instant, the world shifts. You find yourself back at the Bureau, but it's now empty and cold. Then the walls begin to writhe. Flesh-like growths sprout across their surface and split open with violent force. Countless eyes pour forth from the wounds, watching.

A corrosive pain sears from your nose through your chest, the only anchor keeping you remotely rational. The illusion twists and crumbles around you as roiling darkness and toxic miasma close in. Lost and alone, you cling to consciousness through endless poison and pain, relying on even stronger toxins to suppress the agony. A cycle with no escape, repeating forever.
Is this what Ayiguo endures in every single moment of her century-long existence? Your senses abandon you entirely. Through sheer willpower alone, you stretch out your hand and reach forward.

speaker: Chief
content: Ayiguo.
Your voice turns hoarse in the toxic miasma. Poison marks bloom on your arms, just like hers. You hold no fear for Mania, but you are far from immune to every toxin.
No response. Yet the poison threads around you tremble, faint. You endure the agony of toxins seeping into your body. You push through the Mania's turbulence. You keep reaching—
Until your hand touches something.
In a single instant, all darkness and all pain dissolve into nothing. You stand at the center of a lake.
You stand on the lake's surface, alone and shadowless.
This is less a lake than a single slab of cool blue-green jade that time has forgotten. Nothing ripples here. Nothing reflects. An absolute stillness hangs in the air, inspiring dread.
At the far end stand two hollow doors, and from them emanates a soft, dreamlike glow.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So this is her consciousness? A "lake" steeped in poison and time.
You walk toward the doors. White motes of light rise from your footsteps, coalescing before you into human-shaped phantoms—

speaker: Mama
content: Papa went fishing today. When he comes home, we'll make fish soup. The broth will be so white and good. Drink it all up, and you'll grow fair and strong, my little one.

speaker: Mama
content: Mama's sweet child... grow up healthy. Grow up beautiful. The prettiest girl in the whole village, you'll be.
The woman's features are blurred, but her gestures remain clear. She tucks a wildflower into the little girl's hair and gently smooths the strands the wind tousles.

speaker: Mama
content: Slow down, sweetheart! Don't fall now. Don't scar that pretty face.

speaker: Mama
content: Mama's precious girl... my Ayiguo... you have to live on. Beautiful and bright.
The little girl seems oblivious to her mother's words. Still laughing, she runs toward you, passes straight through your body, and dissolves back into falling motes of light.
You continue forward. The phantoms around you grow denser. The warm white light darkens without warning, turning heavy and oppressive. The scenes before you shift abruptly—

speaker: Companion
content: So many bugs! Snakes everywhere! Don't bite me! Get away, get away! Papa! Mama! Where are you?! It hurts!

speaker: Companion
content: Do you think we'll make it? I'm so scared... I don't want to die here. I want to go home...

speaker: Companion
content: Ayiguo... that's your name, right? That's good. You still remember your name...

speaker: Companion
content: Ayiguo... I don't want to die yet...

The pool of blood churns. Insects and snakes tear at flesh. The joyful little girl from the previous illusion plunges into the crimson depths. Blood and filth coat her face. Her skin rots and heals, only to rot again in an endless cycle. Her anguished screams and struggles give way slowly to numb stillness. Around her, companions come and go in waves.

Gradually, the venomous creatures lose their power over her. Her gaze grows dull, lifeless. Blood vessels burst and fade in her eyes, over and over, until at last they settle into a permanent crimson ring around each pupil.

The little girl stares at a wildflower blooming by the pool's edge, as if wondering how such beauty can exist in a place of blood. You reach out to her. Your hand passes through her phantom form as expected, dissolving into nothing.

At last, you pass through Ayiguo's fragmented memories, a century's worth, and arrive before the two doors. The scattered motes of white light coalesce into dozens of palm-sized paper figures. They encircle you.

speaker: Paper Figures
content: Boo-hoo, boo-hoo, the tears fall down. The weeping child can't be found. Seek and search, look all around. Two doors wait. Which way is sound?
You step closer and peer inside. Two auras churn within the doors, utterly opposed—a brilliant golden light that radiates from the left, and a pitch darkness that fills the right.
You rest your hand on the doorframe. The wood grain feels warm and solid beneath your palm. Inside, afternoon sunlight flows like honey, saturating the wooden cabin entirely.
Soup bubbles on the kitchen stove. A young couple busies themselves with cooking. White-haired Ayiguo sits in a woven bamboo chair, children nestled at her side, begging for stories.

speaker: Elder Ayiguo
content: Those adventure tales you love so much... they're all so far from us. This granny's lived a simple life. A happy one. To be ordinary... to grow old in peace... that's fate's greatest gift.
Golden sunlight traces her silhouette gently. Each wrinkle seems to hold a quiet contentment. The house is serene, beautiful, filled only with the soft echo of her peaceful voice...

You rest your hand on the doorframe. Inside lies a viscous darkness. Within a poison pool, venomous insects and serpents churn through bloody water. Ayiguo stands at its center in her youthful form, and with a casual crook of her fingers, countless creatures surge at her command.

speaker: Monster Ayiguo
content: Beauty. Power. Who wouldn't reach for them? Heehee... Now I'm a monster. This is right. This is how it should be.
The girl's whisper sends the poison pool into a sudden boil. Black shadows begin to creep outward, surging toward the doorway with the stench of decay...
[End of Branch]

You rest your hand on the doorframe. Inside lies a viscous darkness. Within a poison pool, venomous insects and serpents churn through bloody water. Ayiguo stands at its center in her youthful form, and with a casual crook of her fingers, countless creatures surge at her command.

speaker: Monster Ayiguo
content: Beauty. Power. Who wouldn't reach for them? Heehee... Now I'm a monster. This is right. This is how it should be.
The girl's whisper sends the poison pool into a sudden boil. Black shadows begin to creep outward, surging toward the doorway with the stench of decay...
You rest your hand on the doorframe. The wood grain feels warm and solid beneath your palm. Inside, afternoon sunlight flows like honey, saturating the wooden cabin entirely.
Soup bubbles on the kitchen stove. A young couple busies themselves with cooking. White-haired Ayiguo sits in a woven bamboo chair, children nestled at her side, begging for stories.

speaker: Elder Ayiguo
content: Those adventure tales you love so much... they're all so far from us. This granny's lived a simple life. A happy one. To be ordinary... to grow old in peace... that's fate's greatest gift.
Golden sunlight traces her silhouette gently. Each wrinkle seems to hold a quiet contentment. The house is serene, beautiful, filled only with the soft echo of her peaceful voice...
[End of Branch]

You pull your gaze away and step back, examining both doors. One is an illusory dream, the other reality... Or are both of them traps? Before you can think it through, the paper figures leap out and urge you onward.

speaker: Paper Figures
content: Boo-hoo, boo-hoo, the heart beats fast. The weeping child awaits at last. Left door, right door, choose your path!

speaker: Chief
content: What happens if I choose wrong?

speaker: Paper Figures
content: Choose right, go home tonight. Choose wrong, you're gone, swallowed whole!

The nursery rhyme grows shriller and shriller as the paper figures slap at you with insistence. You want more time to think, but the entire space begins to tremble violently. Beneath your feet, the jade-like surface of the lake splinters, delicate cracks spreading like ice about to fracture.

speaker: Paper Figures
content: Choose now! Choose now! The heart will break! The doors will close!
Your body screams with searing pain and suffocation. There is no time left to hesitate. You struggle toward the door on the left.

speaker: Monster Ayiguo
content: Little one, where are you going? This side is better, isn't it? Ayiguo will be here. She must be.
Your body screams with searing pain and suffocation. There is no time left to hesitate. You struggle toward the black door on the right.

speaker: Elder Ayiguo
content: To live an ordinary life as a normal person... isn't that the better dream? Ayiguo will be here. She must be.
A voice from the other door whispers in your ear. It tempts you. You hesitate, stop again. Your insides twist together, forcing you to double over in agony.
Even more irritating are the clamoring paper figures. They are fluttering, ramming into you from every side.

speaker: Paper Figures
content: Choose now! Choose now! The sky will fall! The earth will cave!

Your legs buckle beneath you. You sink to one knee on the lake surface, arms trembling as they barely hold you up. Then you see strange-colored patterns rising from your fingertips, a perfect mirror of those on Ayiguo's body. You freeze. Ayiguo did mention her wish before...

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Is it so wrong for a girl to want pretty things? To stroll down a sunny street, take in the noise and the bustle, feel alive without something chewing at her insides?

speaker: Ayiguo
content: You understand, don't you? This wanting to just... be normal?
You endure the pain of toxins corrupting your body and struggle toward the golden door, the one on the left.

speaker: Chief
content: But after gaining that much power... can anyone really settle for ordinary? After enduring pain like hers... can simple happiness ever be enough?
Just as you are about to step through the golden door, your feet stop once more. But... time is up.
CRASH!!!

The entire space shudders as though struck by a massive hammer. The jade-like lake surface shatters, sending debris flying in every direction. The paper figures are torn to shreds, their piercing shrieks echoing through the chaos. The door frames shake violently, and the glows within them begin to flicker as if they could slam shut at any moment.
The consciousness space is collapsing! There is no time left to overthink. You dive through the door just as it begins to fall apart—
(Scene change)
No sunlight reaches this place. There is only the viscous poison and the endless churning of insect carcasses.

Ayiguo lies in the pool, her body divided—half in bloom of youth, half in ruin. A network of spiderweb veins, purple-black in hue, maps her once-fair skin as the poison spreads through her with a will of its own. She takes no notice. She merely seizes a passing poisonous insect and consumes it without ceremony.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Buzzing bugs, behaving bugs... all fly into Granny's mouth!

Ayiguo licks the venom from her fingertips, and her laughter rises, sharp and growing. With a single swallow, the decayed half of her face begins to mend, the rot receding inch by inch as life creeps back into the flesh.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: That silly boy's been wandering in here an awfully long time... What, did he come all this way just to sightsee?
female_content: That silly girl's been wandering in here an awfully long time... What, did she come all this way just to sightsee?

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Ah, well. That illusion was so lovely, so warm and gentle. He'll choose it, surely. After all... this granny told him herself. "I just want an ordinary life."
female_content: Ah, well. That illusion was so lovely, so warm and gentle. She'll choose it, surely. After all... this granny told her herself. "I just want an ordinary life."

speaker: Ayiguo
content: "I won't believe a word you say"—wasn't that the line? And yet, when it mattered most... you still believed this wretched old liar's sincerity. Hahaha...

She raises her left hand and lets the venom cascade over her head. Wherever it flows, the poisonous scars fade into smoothness. Then she raises her right hand, and the wrinkles on her face vanish without a trace.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: People always say an ordinary life is what truly matters. That's only because they've never tasted what it's like to be a god.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: They fear me because I hold the power of life and death in my fingertips. They call me a monster draped in poisonous scars... But I'll stay young. Beautiful. Forever.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Being a villain is wonderful. Why can't anyone understand that? Ah... but I suppose the strong are destined for solitude. Expecting mere mortals to grasp such things... perhaps this granny asks too much.

The space beyond the poison pool collapses, and the water trembles in answer. At the entrance, the light flickers, threatening to seal the place shut at any moment. Ayiguo's smile falters for an instant as the thought of that person in gray crosses her mind. A fleeting shadow of regret passes over her face.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Sigh... It seems that little one isn't coming after all. This granny... really is going to rot away in here alone.

speaker: Chief
content: So this is how you stay young?
A voice cuts through the dark.
Ayiguo, who has been resting with eyes closed, opens them now. A glimmer of joy slips across her gaze, unfelt by her own awareness.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Oh? And here I was certain you'd choose poorly. Yet here you stand. Didn't you see the other door, little one?

speaker: Ayiguo
content: A perfectly safe path, right there for the taking. And instead you come barging into this old granny's poison den? Tired of breathing, are we?

You ignore the horrifying sights that surround you and the collapsing illusion beyond the door. You approach the poison pool. Along its edge, white and yellow wildflowers sway, the same ones you saw in the illusion.

speaker: Chief
content: This pool is nothing but death. But flowers still grow here. You never forgot what your mother told you, did you? "You have to live on. Beautiful and bright."

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Ancient history. Who bothers remembering such things?

speaker: Chief
content: You remember. That's why you're torn in two. You want an ordinary life, but you know there's no road back to it.

speaker: Chief
content: I almost walked through that beautiful illusion. But then I realized it. I needed to know what you would choose. Not what I thought you wanted.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Oh? Reading minds now, are we? Go on, then. Let's hear this grand theory of yours.

speaker: Chief
content: Maybe you wanted ordinary once. A simple, quiet life. But after everything you've survived... you know that door's been closed for a long time.

speaker: Chief
content: You don't want someone to save you... You want to keep living, beautifully and freely. Without anyone's leash around your neck. That's why you'd never choose what's behind that other door.

speaker: Chief
content: Everything you've endured... it won't let you accept an ugly version of yourself. And it won't let you just lie down and die.

speaker: Chief
content: If you had another choice, you wouldn't want the shackles either. But this was the best answer you could find. You don't trust me, just as I don't trust you.
Ayiguo picks impatiently at her ear with her pinky, yet something flickers in the depths of her eyes.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: So what?

speaker: Chief
content: So we can work together. But first, you need to wake up.

speaker: Chief
content: You're still inside the illusion. Your real body is out there, bleeding poison and Mania. The longer you stay here, the worse it gets. The more damage you take.

speaker: Chief
content: You wrapped yourself in that cocoon at the last second. I don't know how much longer it holds. When it breaks, and I suppose it will, the Mania and poison flood Eastside. The people there—
Before you can finish, the bloody water of the poison pool transforms into tentacles and sweeps you up into the air.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Work together? How precious. When this granny came to you with open hands, you turned me away. But now that you need something, here you are with pretty words and pleading eyes?

speaker: Ayiguo
content: You think a few smooth sentences will make this old granny dance to your tune? Hah! You underestimate me, little one.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: What happens out there is none of my concern. I'm no upstanding citizen. I'm Granny Goldspider—capricious, immortal, a monster grown old.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: So what if they all perish? Those creatures who called me filthy. Cursed me as a freak. Prayed I'd rot away in some dark corner where they wouldn't have to look at me... Ignorant, small-minded fools, screeching their worthless noise. Not one of them is worth a single tear.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: What gave them the right... Who are they to judge me? Despise me? Drive me away? Call for my head like I was some rabid thing to be put down?
The people from her past and the fleeing figures of reality merge into one. Ayiguo's expression darkens, turning unreadable.

The bloody water of the poison pool suddenly boils. Ayiguo rises with it into the air, facing you down. Frenzied shadows whirl around her, carrying with them a swarm of venomous insects that buzz through the stagnant air.
A single venomous insect lands on the corner of your eye. Its sharp mouthparts emit a piercing shriek, a sound that echoes Ayiguo's seething bloodlust.

speaker: Mania
content: Kill him. Devour him. Take his power... and you will become the strongest being this world has ever known.
female_content: Kill her. Devour her. Take her power... and you will become the strongest being this world has ever known.

speaker: Mania
content: Power without chains... Eternal youth and beauty... Wealth beyond measure... All yours.

speaker: Mania
content: This flesh you wear is nothing but morality's cage. Only through destruction can you be reborn.

speaker: Mania
content: You will never suffer again. Never be alone. Never be bound by their rules, their world, their scorn. You will be... free. Forever.
Shadows born of Mania seep from the poison pool and coil around Ayiguo. They whisper to her, tempting her toward surrender. You meet her gaze, finding her eyes now stained with darkness.

speaker: Chief
content: The flower is still blooming, Ayiguo.

speaker: Chief
content: It grows in a pool of blood because some part of you still wants to live. Not as a mindless monster, but as you.

speaker: Chief
content: Ayiguo, don't let Mania fool you. I've seen what happens to Sinners who give in. They become monsters, Corruptors.

speaker: Chief
content: Have you forgotten? You refuse to submit to any power, not even Mania! That's how you've survived everything thrown at you.

speaker: Mania
content: Ayiguo... You have no other road. Will you crawl back to your cage?!

speaker: Chief
content: There's a third road. I'll give you the shackles!

speaker: Mania
content: Have you forgotten?! Imprisoned. Controlled. Rejected. Cast out like a thing to be feared and buried!

speaker: Chief
content: Then let's make a bet. You can master your poison and my shackles. Together, we find a way for you to live, not as a monster, not as a mortal. As something else entirely.
The shadows refuse to relent. They keep whispering in Ayiguo's ear.
Ayiguo lowers her head and says nothing. The silence stretches for long seconds. Then, abruptly, she leans forward, grabs hold of your collar, and drags you near.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Little one, do you understand what you're offering?

speaker: Chief
content: Can't be worse than what's already happening.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: If you lose this bet, my poison eats through you. Nothing left but a stain. And you still want to roll the dice?

speaker: Chief
content: I didn't walk in here expecting to walk out clean.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Hahaha! You are an interesting little thing! Just like this granny... a gambler to the marrow!

Ayiguo lets out a hearty laugh, loosens her grip on your collar, and steps away. The darkness drains from her eyes, her agitation ebbing by degrees. In you, she catches a glimpse of herself, someone willing to stare death in the face for the slimmest chance at life.
Beside her, Mania's shadow continues its ceaseless prattling. Ayiguo turns her head and spits a mouthful of poison its way. The shadow corrodes on contact and dissolves into nothing.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Enough yapping out of you, you overgrown pest!

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Well then. If you've got the stomach for it, let's give this a try.
Ayiguo stretches out her wrist toward you. The restraints that bind you fall away.
A blinding burst of red light erupts as the shackles activate. Before Ayiguo, a third door materializes into being.
(Scene change)
You gasp sharply and sit upright on the auction hall floor. A fit of violent coughing seizes you, and you spit up dark fluid laced with blood.
The spider silk that had swallowed the hall has vanished. The bystanders are evacuated. On the empty floor, Ayiguo lies curled in a fetal position, still shrouded in tattered remnants of silk.

You do not stop to assess your own wounds. You rush to her side and tear the poison-soaked silk away with your bare hands, uncovering her face. Her eyes are pressed shut. Your fingertips blacken swiftly on contact, then the next moment, the decay halts, suppressed by some invisible will.
Ayiguo's consciousness stirs. She is protecting you.
(Scene change)

Ayiguo stands in the fields of Eastia. Overhead, the sky opens wide and endless, clouds drifting lazily toward the horizon. A soft breeze moves through the grass and stirs the air around her. She cannot recall the last time such peace has settled upon her.

speaker: Mama
content: My precious girl, you have to live on. Beautiful and bright.

speaker: Companion
content: Do you think we'll make it?

speaker: Passerby
content: Monster! You're an undying monster!
Countless phantoms flicker at the edges of sight, appearing and dissolving like mist beneath the sun—present one moment, vanished the next.
Ayiguo watches with a strange fascination. She lowers her gaze to her own hands, clean and unmarked, and finds them unfamiliar.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: How lovely... to feel nothing at all.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: That little one was right. An ordinary life...? I lost the road back to that a long, long time ago.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: I clawed and killed and swallowed poison to survive like this. Not so I could wither away and die some pitiful death in a dark corner. Isn't that right?
The third door looms before her, sheathed in crimson spikes that coil like brambles and gleam like blades. But fear does not touch her.

She takes a step. From the ground, countless withered hands surge upward, clawing at her ankles, desperate to drag her back. She does not slow. Her stride, unwavering, tears through every grasping finger.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: My, my. What a heavy load this old granny's been hauling all these years. Give it a rest, won't you? Old friends. Old foes. Doesn't matter anymore.
The torn hands shift and flatten into paper figures. They link hands and form a ring around her, their voices rising in a nursery rhyme achingly familiar.
Little one who weeps, don't wander far. Round the world but never still. Steady stand the mountains tall, Clear and bright the waters fall...

Ayiguo inhales deeply. The air is laced with the faint, distant scent of her mother's steamed rice cakes. She steps across the threshold, and a warm red light, nearly searing, pours out and swallows her whole.
(Scene change)
A Few Days Later

speaker: Chief
content: This is for you. Congratulations on being back among the living.
You place a small gift box on Ayiguo's bedside table, where it joins an assortment of snacks and flowers from other Sinners and staff members.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: A hair clip? Such a plain little thing. A single flower, no sparkle, no shine. Have you been living under a rock, <color=#fb9259>sweet pea</color>?
Sweet pea? Since when does this granny give you new nicknames?

speaker: Chief
content: It's like the one you used to wear, isn't it? I used that as a guide. If it's not to your taste, I can swap it for something else.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Hey, hey! A gift given is a gift kept, no taking it back! Since you've shown proper respect to your elders, this granny supposes she'll hold onto it.
Afraid you might change your mind, Ayiguo quickly tucks the hair clip into her inner pocket, then lies back down with a contented smile.

speaker: Chief
content: How are you feeling? You've been horizontal for days.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: This granny's right as rain. But you... you've got more nerve than sense. Weren't you the least bit worried about getting poisoned to death inside my cocoon?

speaker: Chief
content: You've been keeping poison on a leash for over a century. Mania's probably just another strong toxin as far as your body's concerned. And even if things went sideways, I'm the Bureau Chief. I would've managed.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: My, aren't we full of ourselves. Handed over the shackles without blinking. Not a single worry that this granny might turn the tables and use her poison to pull your strings?

options: What kind of Chief would I be if I get scared that easy?
Not at all. If I go down, you won't last long either.

speaker: Chief
content: But that's a good point. I could use this chance to test how the shackles affect you.

speaker: Chief
content: Anyway, we've both got something on the other now. If it came to blows, we'd both be scraping ourselves off the floor.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Bah! Bah! Such foul luck, always rattling on about death! This granny intends to live a thousand years in perfect health and beauty.

speaker: Chief
content: Then I'd better watch my step. I'll be counting on you to look out for me from now on. Stub my toe too hard, and those shackles might give you a little jolt in sympathy.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: What's that supposed to mean?! Making this granny your personal bodyguard? The nerve! Taking advantage of a poor old woman! Bullying your elders!

speaker: Ayiguo
content: ...Still. I imagine more than a few eyes are on you. An elixir of immortality, walking around on two legs. Tempting target.

speaker: Ayiguo
content: Perhaps I should find a place nearby. Just to keep a proper eye on things. You, specifically.
Warning lights flash intermittently along the corridor leading to the interrogation room.
Ninety-Nine trails behind you. The sound of heavy breathing mixes with the noise of shackles dragging across the floor, sending chills down your spine.
Even though the person behind you is deprived of vision and mobility, you can still sense that she is extremely dangerous.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: It's you?

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: I recognize your scent.
Ninety-Nine sits before you quietly, as if everything that has happened was a dream.
Yet you can still sense her primal instincts. Her senses are sharp even in the dark, prompting you to sit upright.
After all, you tried to stab me a few days ago... The FAC considers you a high-level threat.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: The Legion wanted me to capture you alive.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: I took their money, so I should do the job.
Do you do this sort of thing often?

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: What sort of thing?
Hunting down your target.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: Yes, because they offer money, and we need money.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: Murder is the easiest job we can find.
Ninety-Nine answers calmly and casually as if discussing a mundane, everyday topic.
But deep down, fear permeates through your body. The shackles jingles as a reminder.
This woman is different from all the other captured Sinners.
Even though you turned yourself in to the MBCC, we still have to interrogate you to evaluate the risk you pose.
I hope you will cooperate.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: I will answer all of your questions.
test
test
test
test
test
test

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: I already answered that question.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: They wanted me to catch you alive.
Are you sure you were trying to catch me alive?

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: Yes. I always try my best to complete the mission, otherwise they will dock my pay.
They asked you to capture me <color=#fb9259>alive</color>.
I believe you were trying to take my life back there.
Ninety-Nine raises her head. Even though her eyes are covered, her gaze still pierces through you.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: I was just carrying out my mission.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: They provided the coordinates and plans, and I'd kill or capture the target according to their requirements. That's it.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: But you're quite impressive. After all, you are still here, safe and sound.
Ninety-Nine dutifully answers all of your questions. She doesn't seem like a brutal monster who may chop people into pieces at all.
But that makes her even more frightening. You can never be sure if she really has no intention of murdering you... or just waiting for the right moment.
You try to focus. You put aside your fears and muster the courage to continue interrogating Ninety-Nine.
Do you remember the monsters from the crypt?

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: Yes.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: They were strong and unafraid of my blades. They continued to attack even though their legs were chopped off.
That's right. They are terrifying creatures.
But I'm curious... They are quite similar to you.
