You gaze at Ninety-Nine quietly and utter those words carefully. You hope to elicit a different reaction from her.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: What are you trying to say?
Ninety-Nine suddenly speaks up. Her monotonous voice startles you.
I was just curious.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: We are similar because they came from my body.
What do you mean? Are they your clones?

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: No. I don't know what they are.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: But when my consciousness is blurred, many monsters looking like me would appear.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: It was the same in the crypt.
Could it be Mania Crystals? The fear in your heart grew.
The files do show that the Laboratory of Parma is conducting heinous and illegal experiments and using Mania crystals to make Mania weapons.
You're so badly infected... You might be in manic when you lost consciousness.
Based on what you said, it shouldn't be the first time this happened... Was this already the case when you were in the Laboratory of Parma?
You carefully uttered that name. Before you could finish, you felt the heat rise in the interrogation room. Ninety-Nine glared at you with her blood-red eyes.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: Yes. There, day after day, I was injected and would then fall unconscious.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: My temperature would heat up like boiling water.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: Then, I'd destroy everything I saw...
Ninety-Nine calmly recounts her ordeal in the laboratory, but her gaze remains fixated on you like a predator about to pounce on its prey.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: I don't know why, but at that place...

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: A lot of Ninety-Nines came into being because of me. They were all monsters.
Did they... really use your Mania Crystals to make weapons?
Ninety-Nine's words make you gradually realize what went on at the Laboratory of Parma. You look at her, whose eyes are quivering with resentment.
But at this point, you can't give up this chance to learn more about the Parma lab. You calm yourself down and pick up another file from the FAC...
test
test
test

options: Let's talk a bit more about it.

content: Other than drawing blood, what else did they do to you?

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: They took me apart here and here. Then they reassembled me.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: They required me to fight... but I almost killed every opponent by accident.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: The arena's walls had blackened dents. Sometimes I could even see broken bones and sticky mud-like substances.
There is a hint of fanaticism in Ninety-Nine's voice. It seems like she is looking for a fight with you, too.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: Are you scared? Because... I'm also a monster.
The dread inside the interrogation room envelops you bit by bit. There's no doubt that you're talking to a "monster."

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: I'm Ninety-Nine.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: But I'm also a monster.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: Yes.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: The Laboratory of Parma holds nothing but monsters.
Your instincts sense danger. Though Ninety-Nine hasn't made a sound, you feel the suffocating dread building up around you.
You... know her.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: Yes, I do. Actually, there's so much more than "knowing" between us.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: She's not a monster. She's the sunshine that lit up my world.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: She took my hand and led me out from underground. She gave me... freedom.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: I will... I will always protect her. For eternity.
This surprises you. When you interrogated Hella, she refused to talk about Ninety-Nine. You thought Hella hated Ninety-Nine; she's a girl who really holds grudges anyway.
But Ninety-Nine's words changed your perception.
Ninety-Nine's breathing quickened, and the entire interrogation room felt like a steamer. A chill went down your spine. Ninety-Nine was exuding her desire to kill.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: ...Are you done with your questions?
What?
It is the first time Ninety-Nine has asked you something in this interrogation room. Although she was bound, her words strikes fear in your heart.
Ninety-Nine sits upright, blocking out the warning lights.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: Now it's my turn to question you.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: Not long ago, there was a riot at the MBCC. Everyone has been talking about it.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: They said all the Sinners had fled to Syndicate... yet I couldn't find her.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: I searched many places for many days, but she was nowhere to be seen…

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: Do you know… where Hella is?
Hella is still at the MBCC.
She intended to escape under cover of the chaotic riot, yet failed.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: She failed?
She couldn't break out of her cell. And she still tried hard to get away after we got her out of it...
But she's a Sinner... As the Chief, I could not just let her slip away.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: So... you constrained her?
Perhaps...
When I regained consciousness, the shackles were already on her body.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: I see.
Ninety-Nine nodded as if she accepted your claims. However...

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: Hella is the freest little mouse in Syndicate.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: The gangster hideouts, the MBCC cells... and even the Laboratory of Parma couldn't constrain her.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: How could she submit to your constraint?
Ninety-Nine's tone is still calm, but you know from the room's rising heat that she has been incensed.
Steam rises from her skin, breaking the chains with rapidly increasing temperature.
Giant dark shadows spread out from behind her, and her mutated dark black hands effortlessly remove the muzzle and the blindfold.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: I heard that...

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: …once you shackle a Sinner, the shackles will only break if one of you dies.
You suddenly realize Ninety-Nine wasn't so naive as to turn herself in. She's smarter than you thought, or rather, more wildly intuitive. She's here to kill you and rescue Hella.
In the dark interrogation room, her eyes, red as the Carmen Lúcia Ruby, are fixated on your neck, where there are arteries, the most fragile part of your body.
As danger edges closer and closer, you find yourself unable to move an inch.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: You're lying, Chief.
In an instant, Ninety-Nine pounces towards you, scalding the air around her. She's like a predator at the top of the food chain hunting down helpless prey.
In terror, you instinctively unleash the shackles' power and command Ninety-Nine not to hurt you.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: The shackles?! So these are what you use to imprison us...

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: ...and what keep her from coming back to me!
Ninety-Nine buckles under the power of the shackles but shows no sign of surrender. The pain makes her even more enraged and violent.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: You... despicable scum!

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: I want you to feel... what it's like to be experimented upon!
Despite the shackles, she tries to attack you again and again. Her speed is slowed down enough for you to dodge, but the room begins to crumble from it.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: I must kill you... I must kill you to free Hella!

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: We shall both regain our freedom!
The shackles linking you two start to tremor as if about to snap. Ninety-Nine's power is spraying mist everywhere, burning your arms.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: You can't stop me! I must kill you!
Stop it, Ninety-Nine! You'll die if you keep this up!

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: I don't care if I die! I only want her! I'll do anything to free us from bondage!
Cough...!
The tremor from the shackles grow stronger and stronger. The force of backlash makes you taste blood in your throat.
Then... are you willing... for her... to be left all alone... in this world?
Ninety-Nine doesn't stop attacking. She grits her teeth and spits out a few words.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: As long as... she can live free... I... have no regrets.
Noticing noise in the interrogation room, Nightingale quickly summons help. But you must keep control of Ninety-Nine's shackles, or everyone will die from her attacks.
Ninety-Nine, you have to stop using your power! Your Syndrome Mania is going out of control! Ugh...! Do you not care... if you become a real monster?!

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: I am a monster! Free Hella!
Ninety-Nine's mutation is clearly worsening. Mania is eroding her. Keeping a tight grip on the shackles, you try to cope with the immense pressure.
However, Ninety-Nine seems to be accustomed to the pain. She struggles towards you step by step and grabs you by the neck.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: I'll say it again! Free Hella!
Nightingale and the guards shoot at her, but boiling blood quickly pushes the bullets out of her body. Her grip on your neck doesn't loosen one bit. You feel yourself losing consciousness.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Call for...

speaker: Interrogation Intercom
content: No, Ninety-Nine! Don't kill him!
female_content: No, Ninety-Nine! Don't kill her!

content: A voice from the loudspeaker froze Ninety-Nine in her tracks. You felt the grip on your neck loosening.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: Where... where are you?
Ninety-Nine stumbles towards the familiar voice in confusion. Nightingale seizes the moment to electroshock Ninety-Nine and injects her neck with a powerful sedative.
As Ninety-Nine slumps to the ground, she knocks down a metal chair with a loud clang that transmits to the other end of the loudspeaker. Immediately, exasperated cries erupt from the other side.

speaker: Interrogation Intercom
content: Ninety-Nine? Ninety-Nine, what happened? What did you bastards do to her?! Let me go! Ninety-Nine...!
Nightingale cuts the speaker, but you have recognized the voice. It was Hella.
Having lost consciousness, Ninety-Nine's temperature gradually returns to normal. After notifying your superiors, Ninety-Nine is sent to a higher-level security cell.
Nightingale! What are the results?!

speaker: Nightingale
content: Due to Sinner Ninety-Nine's outburst, the FAC has intervened in her case.

speaker: Nightingale
content: She had been subjected to a long period of medical experimentation. Moreover, she had been exposed to mutations in Black Water Crypt on the last mission.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Ninety-Nine's limbs have mutated to become like those of a Corruptor, and these mutations have spread throughout her body.

speaker: Nightingale
content: When she was captured, she had already surpassed stage one of the infection, and was heading towards stage two.

speaker: Nightingale
content: You must have noticed that the shackles were no longer sufficient to halt her mutations.

speaker: Nightingale
content: She will soon become a full-fledged Corruptor. By then, she will corrode and contaminate your spirit even more.

speaker: Nightingale
content: The FAC will not allow any harm to come to you.
What are they planning to do...

speaker: Nightingale
content: ...Execute the mutant Sinner Ninety-Nine.
I'm sorry. At the time, a lot of people got involved in the riot.
We are still unable to find Hella.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: No. You imprisoned her.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: Hella is the freest little mouse in Syndicate. She won't let anyone constrain her.
You answer has provoked Ninety-Nine. Her mood deteriorates into a rage.
Heat rapidly rises all around her and she breaks free from the shackles.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: The reason why she didn't come back... is you!
Giant dark shadows spread out from behind her, and her mutated dark black hands effortlessly remove the muzzle and the blindfold.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: Your shackles have imprisoned her.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: I've no choice but to kill you.
The impound deadline is fast approaching. You try to halt Ninety-Nine's mutation with the shackles every day, but to little effect.

speaker: FAC researcher
content: Chief, Ninety-Nine's mutations have exceeded the critical threshold, and her limbs are 60% corrupted.

speaker: FAC researcher

It's an evil weapon made using crystallized Mania. The gangs covet the Sinister Singularities' power, even if it infects them with Mania, turns innocent people into monsters, and floods the Syndicate with rivers of blood.
The FAC has yet to uncover the Mania weapon's creator, but it has locked on to the source of the earliest batch of those evil crystals—the Rust.
High-grade Mania crystals are obtained from Sinner experimentation, while high yields of low-grade crystals are refined from the many Corruptor remains piled up on the Rust.

content: Hahahaha, okay! I like you more and more!
You ignore her chilling laughter and turn on the virtual projection. A number of photos appear before Wendy.
Red-black liquid containing contaminants mixed with unnameable detritus trickles over the ground, staining the land black.

speaker: Wendy
content: The Rust! The place where I belong...
You seem to know the ins and outs of the Rust. Are there many monsters?

speaker: Wendy
content: Monsters? You mean the Corruptors, or me?

speaker: Wendy
content: Hee hee, whatever it is, there's always a lot... Alive, dead, inhuman... all kinds.

speaker: Wendy
content: Monster remains, blue rain, black mud, impossibly dangerous garbage, and people with no place to go... Whatever you don't want ends up in the Rust. The Rust welcomes all.
From the data you've consulted, the Rust was specially demarcated as an abandoned zone.

Beginning in Nightfall 84, pollutants and biological tissues that couldn't be disposed of were dumped into the Rust, gradually turning it into a cradle of monstrosities. It's also a haunt for dangerous outlaws.

speaker: Wendy
content: Hee hee, why are you always staring at me like that?

Our investigation revealed that most of the raw materials used to make the Mania weapon came from the Rust. So, we believe there are people nearby who are stealing Corruptors and extracting biological material from them as "merchandise".
They can carve their "merchandise" into small pieces and move them away, and they're strong enough to fight the Corruptors.
Is that what you do, Wendy?

speaker: Wendy
content: Carve... Did you say "carve"?! Yes, yes, yes! I like doing this, and I like chasing them, too... and listening to that piercing sound they make... Hahaha!
You're a suspect, and that's a felony.

speaker: Wendy
content: Ahahaha! The carving, that was definitely me!! I was at the Rust! I cut up the pretty cake into pieces, they were like beehives, soft... sticky... disgusting!!!

speaker: Wendy
content: Do you wanna know what it feels like, too?
Wendy looks at you, making no effort to conceal her desire to eat you whole.
You admit to gathering Corruptor remains and collecting contaminated tissues from them. Correct? To what end?

speaker: Wendy
content: Hee hee, that was the mission!

speaker: Wendy
content: Bodies dumped in the Rust, wandering Corruptors, cute little monsters... None can leave the Rust...

speaker: Wendy
content: I’d find them, cut them up, cut them to pieces... There’s no higher honor than this mission!

options: Who tasked you with this mission?

speaker: Wendy
content: Who...?
Wendy gives you a cold and eerie look, then lowers her voice to a whine like an overhead extractor fan...

speaker: Wendy
content: Who gave me the mission never mattered... I just wanted this mission.

speaker: Wendy
content: Their bodies are slightly decayed and ooze dark chocolate paste... And the toys buried in the paste jump and jump... while the little cherries dotting the cake giggle and snicker.

speaker: Wendy
content: We spent every single day together and played with them! Sharing their flavor... listening to their cries and dreaming beautiful dreams... Hee hee hee...

speaker: Wendy
content: You know what? Those things decay in a way you can't even imagine. They're half meat-stink, half... crawling black mud.

speaker: Wendy
content: I have to separate them carefully and clean them well, then save the black stuff. They’re like a pool of barf...

speaker: Wendy
content: Bleuugh!
Wendy makes an awful vomiting sound with her throat, letting saliva drip down onto the tips of her shoes.

speaker: Wendy
content: Rotting bit by bit, chopping piece by piece!

speaker: Wendy
content: Death and death, grave after grave!

speaker: Wendy
content: Go to ****ing hell and make a deal with the Devil!
She shakes violently, giving you a fright as the chains restraining her collide together with a series of ear-piercing sounds.

speaker: Wendy
content: Ahahahaha!

speaker: Wendy
content: You little coward, hiding behind your power like trash!
You've already grown accustomed to these sudden crazed outbursts of hers and are getting tired of her jumbled answers.
You even start to think that it's not impossible that she could be going to all this effort just to obfuscate her crimes.

According to the FAC's investigative report, the trafficking of Corruptor remains near the Rust is a highly developed trade with the flawless technique when it comes to selling, stealing, transporting, and concealment.
This just isn't something that a mere "lunatic" could pull off.
We have reason to suspect that you have a partner or collaborator. Is it a Syndicate gang?

speaker: Wendy
content: Syndicate? Where’s that?
Sigh... I can hardly keep my eyes open...
Are the mobsters who are after the Mania weapon your partners?

speaker: Wendy
content: Don’t compare us to them.

speaker: Wendy
content: My companions are way more refined and powerful than they are.

speaker: Wendy
content: Hee hee hee... That's right, my companions, friends, and family who I'd give my life for... not like those chuckleheads, and not like you, either!

speaker: Wendy
content: I have a LOT of companions!

speaker: Wendy
content: We’re very strong, and glorious, too... We carry out missions together and bring light to this world! Hee hee hee...

speaker: Wendy
content: We’re always together, and no monster is a match for us.

speaker: Wendy
content: They turn to corpses in the Rust, and all the corpses are ours...
Her voice gradually trails off as her smile grows deeper. Your intuition tells you that she believes every maniacal word she's saying.
Her companions... What could they be like?

speaker: Wendy
content: Who? Uh... my friends? My family?

speaker: Wendy
content: They’re at home... but I brought their stuff.

speaker: Wendy
content: Why don’t you look for them yourself?
A rusty chain slips out from the clothing on Wendy's chest, looking out of place among the other items on her person.
You walk over to her side and gently lift up the chain—it's a metal chain with several dog tags hanging from it. You can feel the heat it carried from Wendy's body in your palm.
The dozen or so metal dog tags strung on the chain sway gently, reflecting a cold ray of light—This isn't an emblem of any Syndicate gang.

Their style is sharp and the information is encrypted, it would appear they're part of a highly systematized organization. And the material is some sort of high-grade alloy, meaning that this organization has considerable support in terms of equipment and supplies.
But their surfaces are covered in contaminants and bloodstains. They've clearly seen countless deaths and battles.

speaker: Wendy
content: Ah! My companions, my comrades, my family...
This time, the affection in her voice makes your hair stand on end.
A large, elite organization like this not only has control of the Rust and the Corruptor remains, but they have a Sinner like Wendy, too...
And you didn't realize they even existed until now?!

options: What kind of organization are you?

speaker: Wendy
content: Are you scared? Are you scared, Chief? Hahahahaha!!

speaker: Wendy
content: Don’t be afraid of us, what’s there to be afraid of? How could you forget about us?

speaker: Wendy
content: As the FAC’s dog, you should know everything about us!
The FAC's dog...?

speaker: Wendy
content: The blood flowed into the machine, branding us into this thing...

speaker: Wendy
content: Like a dog chain... tethering us all.

speaker: Wendy
content: You don’t remember? ...The genetic brand.

speaker: Wendy
content: Everyone had to undergo genetic branding, it made their corpses easier to identify after the war.
Genetic branding?!
They used lasers to engrave individual blood ions on special metal dog tags—that's the FAC's original technology!
You mean...?!
You forcefully wipe the stains from the surface of the dog tag and to reveal a few letters from under the years of filth overlaying it—
W...Mortician?
In the blink of an eye, Wendy grows unusually quiet. Now, the only noise you can hear in the interrogation room is the humming of various monitoring instruments.

speaker: Wendy
content: It’s been a long time... since anyone called us that.

speaker: Wendy
content: Ah, poor undertakers!

speaker: Wendy
content: Slumbering under a cold mound of dirt...
The ID on this dog tag is from the FAC troops... Were you with the FAC?
But... how did you end up at the Rust? Why would you get involved with the Mania weapon? ...And why didn't any of this come up in the investigative report?

speaker: Wendy
content: Hehe... Hehe... Hahahahaha...
No longer answering your questions, all that remains in the interrogation room is Wendy's unsettling crazed laughter.

options: Contact Nightingale to investigate the truth

content:
S-084, FAC Addendum Investigative Report
Access Permissions: High

　W0403, Framework Against Catastrophe subsidiary level 6 department, Catastrophe Contamination Cleanup Squad, secrecy: High
　Designation: Mortician, the undertakers.
Functions: Battlefield cleanup, recovering Corruptor remains, taking care of residual contamination
Current Status: All deceased, unit abolished

Retrieved File:
Ex-Catastrophe Contamination Cleanup Squad W0403 Corruptor Remains Trade Incident Report
...Collective dereliction of duty by the Catastrophe Contamination Cleanup Squad W0403 confirmed, illegal disposal of contaminated residual substances resulting in their circulation within the Syndicate...
...Start time unknown...Downstream transfer unknown...Chief conspirator unknown
...July 1st, N.F. 110, the FAC established an investigation team, however, due to the deaths of all members suspected of violating the rules, the investigation was aborted and the unit was abolished.
Access restrictions to related events have been increased to the highest level and the information has been blocked. Access unavailable to ordinary members...

Retrieved File:
Ex-Catastrophe Contamination Cleanup Squad W0403 Mass Casualty Incident Report
...June 30th, N.F. 110, Catastrophe Contamination Cleanup Squad W0403V experienced a violent attack on their stronghold at the Rust, which was completely destroyed...

...Captain XX...Confirmed dead...
...Team member XX...Remains were found in an area nearby...Confirmed dead...
...XX...Unable to recover remains...confirmed dead the following year...
...XX...Unable to recover remains...confirmed dead the following year...
...Wendy...Unable to recover remains...confirmed dead the following year...

speaker: Wendy
content: Ah, poor undertakers!

speaker: Wendy
content: Abandoned in the abyss...
As night falls, the banks of the Rust are instantly plunged into darkness.
The piles of trash mixed together with the polluted river give off an eye-watering stench.
From dark corners, a few unnamable creatures oozing a black, foul-smelling pus-like liquid watch the nearby human motionlessly.
A few low growls come from behind you, and before you can react, the Corruptor is shot and falls to the ground.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Target eliminated. You should be more careful, Chief... you have a mission to complete.
Thanks, I will.
A few hours earlier...

speaker: Nightingale
content: Emergency mission order from the FAC.
Nightingale transfers a vigilantly sealed document over to you.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Your orders are to go straight to the Rust and use Wendy as a decoy to investigate the source of the Corruptor weapon materials.

speaker: Nightingale
content: As well as to get to the bottom of the former secret cleanup unit.

speaker: Nightingale
content: The connection to this previously presumed dead former cleanup unit has been confirmed. the higher-ups are taking this matter very seriously.

speaker: Nightingale
content: This is our only chance to get in close contact with the organization dealing in Corruptor remains!
I know what to do.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Support will be stationed 5 kilometers from your position and will await your orders. Snipers, however, will be on standby.

speaker: Nightingale
content: They can be activated whenever the need arises.
As you contemplate how to carry out the mission, the roar of a chainsaw grates against your ears as the Corruptor that was just shot is pinned to the garbage pile and instantly severed in two.
...Wendy.

speaker: Wendy
content: Oh... Did I scare you? Hahaha... that’s the Rust for ya, Chiefy!

speaker: Wendy
content: There are monsters everywhere! They’re monsters and I’m a monster! And you are, too! Hahaha!

speaker: Wendy
content: If you’re scared... then you’d better head back to your shelter while you still can!
It wasn't anything serious, of course, but thanks for your help.

speaker: Wendy
content: Hehe.
The creatures hiding in the corner seem to fear Wendy. Not daring to rush forward again, they whimper reluctantly from where they are.

speaker: Wendy
content: Hee hee... that’s the Rust for you...

speaker: Wendy
content: To survive, you have to try as hard as you can to become a monster yourself...

speaker: Wendy
content: The cans in the garbage heaps, the maggots born on the rotting meat—all fuel for survival!

speaker: Wendy
content: Hehehe... If that doesn't work, those monsters' bodies could pull you through for a day or two.

speaker: Wendy
content: Let’s go, Chief. You won’t get a full view of the Rust sitting behind a high wall with those flying little bugs.
Wendy once again chucks the chainsaw behind her. It falls into a corner of a nearby reconnaissance aircraft with a crash that makes the monsters yelp and babble.

speaker: Wendy
content: Hee hee hee hee hee... How I’ve waited to hear those screams!
Wendy seems rather excited now, perhaps because she's returned to a familiar place.
You were always saying that you wanted to come back and see the Rust.
Given how cooperative you've been in our talks, I submitted a request to the higher-ups to let you come with me.

speaker: Wendy
content: Go with you? This many people?
...It's just you and me.

speaker: Wendy
content: Heh...
Wendy scoffs, yanks at your hand suddenly as her pace quickens, then slips into some ruins.
Wendy?!
Your chest tightens—Most of the ruins around here are the remains of the Black Ring explosions, which also threw the magnetic fields into chaos.

You hear some electric hums from the communication device concealed behind your ear before it stops working completely. You have no way to call for support and your positioning system has been disrupted.
Fortunately, Wendy comes to a stop before long and looks steadily forward. Seeing that you've caught up, she pulls you to her side and points ahead.
What's that?!
Under the moonlight, you can make out several figures in black cloaks. They're digging for something.
How... could there still be people wandering the Rust at a time like this?!
Moments later, a distinctive smell mixed with the damp stench of the Rust wafts over and sends chills down your spine.
These people... They're digging up buried bodies!!
Were you pointing at these people? Are they your companions?

speaker: Wendy
content: No.

speaker: Wendy
content: They’re devils...

speaker: Wendy
content: They held back in the darkness for so long... then waited until I was gone... to dig up the bodies...

speaker: Wendy
content: But what they don’t know... is that I would disappear, then reappear again... Hahahaha...

speaker: Wendy
content: I think this is... the mission the Rust gave to me.
Mission? You mean you're going to carve those dead corruptors or...?

speaker: Wendy
content: They aren't good people at all, so it's okay to kill them, right? It's okay to kill them!
It took such a long to pick up their trail, and now you're worried that Wendy's actions would frighten them off. You gently grab her hand and keep her by your side.
Not so fast, Wendy.

speaker: Corpse Dealer B
content: *Cough cough* Ugh, it smells like **** around here...

speaker: Corpse Dealer A
content: Keep your ****ing voice down.

speaker: Corpse Dealer A
content: Just because the Reaper’s been gone for a while doesn’t mean we can suddenly let our guard down!

speaker: Corpse Dealer A
content: We’ve finished digging here. I hear they found a few more pits of this stuff to the south.

speaker: Corpse Dealer A
content: Let’s go and dig ‘em all up! Then that’ll be a wrap on this month’s quota!
Buried somewhere else... Even if these smugglers aren't from this transport chain, what they're doing now is grounds enough for an arrest.
Wendy, you...

speaker: Wendy
content: South? How dare you... defile my home...!

speaker: Wendy
content: No! I won’t let you get away with it!
You realize that Wendy has already wrenched herself free from your hand and is staring daggers at the group.
Her tightly clenched teeth grind together, making an unnerving sound. Wendy grips the chainsaw, looking like she'll charge forward at any moment.
Easy there, Wendy. If you're trying to tip them off to help them escape, I must say, this is...
Before you can finish your sentence, Wendy has bolted.
Contrary to your expectations, Wendy is not helping those people escape—she's raising her chainsaw.

speaker: Corpse Dealer B
content: Hey! Someone’s rushing this way!

speaker: Corpse Dealer A
content: Who’re you?! Here to steal the bodies?!

speaker: Corpse Dealer A
content: That’s not it!! That sound and... that weapon...

speaker: Corpse Dealer A
content: It’s "the Reaper of the Rust"!!!!
You rush to catch up with Wendy, who fortunately hasn't crossed the line just yet.
She hasn't let them go, but she hasn't killed them all yet either. Instead, she's giving two of them a serious thrashing and stamping on their wrists to stop them from doing anything.

speaker: Wendy
content: Hee hee hee... The Rust’s little mice...
Now forcefully restrained by Wendy, the two hurl curses at her one minute then bitterly beg for mercy the next.
As you prepare to check their identities, you discover something strange.
Wait a minute... What's that on your necks?!
The FAC has always believed that the ones behind the Rust body trade were leftover dissidents from the Catastrophe Cleanup Squad.
But the body brokers you see before you aren't anything like you imagined.
The symbols on their necks mean that they're from Black Water, and their faces don't match any of the rebels in the database.
It's always the last person you want to see that you end up running into, huh?

speaker: Wendy
content: Chief, how about you just let me kill them? They're all garbage and scumbags, they deserve to die...

speaker: Corpse Dealer A
content: Ch-Chief?! Wait a minute, you’re the chief of the Bureau?!
That's me. Have you decided to surrender?

speaker: Corpse Dealer A
content: Ah! You really are with the FAC! Th-That’s great!

speaker: Corpse Dealer A
content: L-Let’s talk this over!

options: What do you want to talk about?

speaker: Corpse Dealer A
content: Hehe, there’s nothing to be nervous about! Let’s work out a deal!

speaker: Corpse Dealer A
content: Let’s work together—You never saw me, and you’ll tell your superiors that you didn’t discover anything unusual.

speaker: Corpse Dealer A
content: And when we finish up our... business... we’ll give you a cut! Whaddya say?
The two gravediggers kneel on the ground and smile obsequiously.

speaker: Corpse Dealer A
content: And don’t you worry, this wouldn’t be the first time there’s been a deal like this! Not by a long shot!

speaker: Corpse Dealer A
content: Our old boss had one with your, uh, whatchamacallit cleaning squad. Heck, we all just called them the Undertakers! They had a good few deals! Now that was a captain that really got it!
The Undertakers? The Undertakers were the secret contamination cleanup squad?
Hearing that familiar word, you can't help but look over at Wendy. She's turned stiff as a board listening to the body broker's story.

speaker: Corpse Dealer A
content: Yeah, that’s it! The something contamination cleanup squad, they were one of the FAC’s! They got it!

speaker: Corpse Dealer A
content: Your top brass would make ‘em do all this dangerous stuff without even sending them good gear.

speaker: Corpse Dealer A
content: Heh, they’d make the contaminated ones clean up the Corruptors bare-handed, basically making Corruptor production bases!

speaker: Corpse Dealer A
content: Ha! What’s so impossible about it? Those were their underlings, after all!

speaker: Corpse Dealer A
content: Isn’t that what they think at the top? What are the lives of a few underlings? They’ll all have to die in the end anyway!

speaker: Corpse Dealer A
content: Don’t believe me if you don’t want to, but have a good think about this deal!

speaker: Corpse Dealer A
content: Just like that Undertaker captain!!

speaker: Corpse Dealer A
content: I’ll be blunt—they sent you all the way here for an investigation because they were hoping you’d get yourself killed! Isn’t that right, Chief?
The body brokers chatter on, looking like flies struggling in the mud.
You also notice that Wendy hasn't made a sound in a while... Especially since she heard them talking about the Undertakers.
Wendy, go ahead and tie these guys up... What are you doing?!

speaker: Wendy
content: Hahaha... Undertakers? I’m an Undertaker!

speaker: Wendy
content: Fancy that, it was you guys all along...

speaker: Corpse Dealer A
content: You're an Undertaker?! I heard they were all executed, I didn't think there were any left alive!

speaker: Corpse Dealer A
content: Ahahaha, since you’re one of them, then you must get how badly those guys at the top treated you!

speaker: Corpse Dealer A
content: Just do what your captain did...
Wendy charges forward, steps on the body broker's head with one foot, and plunges her rapidly whirling chainsaw into the ground next to his head, kicking up dirt and debris.

speaker: Wendy
content: You seem to remember our captain... very well.

speaker: Wendy
content: Yes... We were the Undertakers!

speaker: Wendy
content: In this filthy world, someone had to step up to the plate and face the contamination head-on.

speaker: Wendy
content: We carried a heavy responsibility... to clear a bright path for everyone else!

speaker: Wendy
content: But those traitors! They sold us all out!

speaker: Corpse Dealer A
content: Th-That’s perfectly normal!

speaker: Corpse Dealer A
content: Think of the job you had, and you had no protection or even bonuses for doing it!

speaker: Corpse Dealer A
content: Your top brass treated you like tattered rags! They used you and threw you away!

speaker: Corpse Dealer A
content: What your captain did is completely understandable!

speaker: Wendy
content: Completely understandable?

speaker: Corpse Dealer A
content: Yes! Think about it, you didn’t even have any decent protective equipment!

speaker: Corpse Dealer A
content: I remember there was also a young kid in your squad back then. Your captain brought it up.

speaker: Corpse Dealer A
content: Tsk, tsk, so young, but right at the front and wrapped up in a few pieces of scrap metal.

speaker: Wendy
content: Yes... yes... the child!!!

speaker: Wendy
content: He got completely infected during the mission... and turned crazy just like me!

speaker: Wendy
content: I wanted to save him... but the captain kept telling me he was dead!

speaker: Wendy
content: In the end, I was left with just his clothes and toys...
Wendy lifted the body broker by the collar, forcing him to look into her eyes.

speaker: Wendy
content: I buried one, two, three... people.

speaker: Wendy
content: So many people left me, and now they're stuck rotting in filthy piles of garbage!

speaker: Wendy
content: I won’t accept his end or theirs!! I can’t!

speaker: Wendy
content: Damn him, he... He betrayed everything we believed in!! I'll kill them, kill them all, those... traitors!!

speaker: Wendy
content: You... You dirtbags, you’re just more trash in this stream of filth, you can’t even be called human!
Raising her chainsaw, Wendy hits the switch to unleash her powers. She looks like she wants to tear the people before her into pieces.

speaker: Wendy
content: Your hands... Your feet... You won't be wanting those, will you!

speaker: Wendy
content: Hahaha... Look... Look at this filthy cake, it took a tumble into the mud! It’s trash now! Lemme just cut it all up!

speaker: Wendy
content: Captains, Corruptors, people that sell corpses—they're all just nasty garbage!

speaker: Wendy
content: I’m an Undertaker... a cleanser!

speaker: Wendy
content: I can’t let the contamination... overflow to the world!
Chief
Stop!

speaker: Wendy
content: Get out of here!

speaker: Wendy
content: You wanna make a deal? With them?!

speaker: Wendy
content: So, you’re gonna betray me, too?!
You can hear the rage and hurt in Wendy's voice, and its power has grown extraordinarily.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, the Sinister Singularity’s mood is extremely unstable! A sniper must be activated immediately...
You don't want to resort to snipers or use your abilities.
Wendy, I believe you, I believe that everything you just said is the truth!
The chainsaw presses against your shoulder, rending its skin and flesh. The pain is so excruciating you're unable to finish speaking.
Hnnggg...!
Wendy, listen to me! You can't make yourself guilty of killing these two people!
I... I want to become your companion, I want... No, I can be someone you can depend on now and after all this! Please... believe me!
Wendy's roar stops and she stares at you with vacant, bloodshot eyes, not moving a muscle.

speaker: Wendy
content: Why...

speaker: Wendy
content: Why do you want to be my companion...? You’ll only turn crazy like me! Or into a corpse!

speaker: Wendy
content: Yo would really... do that...?
The chainsaw whines horribly as it swings down and carves in.
A warm, sticky liquid sprays onto each of your faces.

speaker: Wendy
content: Cleanup, cleanup complete.

speaker: Wendy
content: Filth.
The chain of clues was broken due to Wendy's impulsive killing.
The FAC confirmed that Wendy and the Undertakers were collaborating with Black Water, and that they were done away with to cover up the Undertakers' defection and smuggling of Mania weapons.
Wendy will face serious punishment in the future, and the Undertakers... a settlement order was passed down—Not even their bodies would be allowed to go free.
"Please... believe me!"
Wendy looks at this person who, though injured, is continuing to embrace her. She slowly puts down her weapon.
Seeing Wendy's expression turn calm, you take her to a secluded area to rest a while.
Meanwhile, you begin to attempt to reestablish your comms.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, are you all right?
Yes, everything's fine.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Our monitoring data is showing that you’re bleeding from your shoulder and the Sinister Singularity’s emotional state reached a tipping point. You call that "everything’s fine"?
Listen to me, Nightingale. It wasn't Wendy's fault, and I'm fine.
You briefly and precisely summarize everything that just happened. Nightingale is silent for a while, then grants you permission to question Wendy alone outside.

speaker: Nightingale
content: I understand the situation. The support squad will set off right away to collect the two individuals you captured.

speaker: Nightingale
content: She has an in-depth understanding of the Rust and she’s agile in combat... You should know that, while S-084 has been cleared of suspicion with regards to this incident, her mental state remains unstable. She’s dangerous, Chief.

speaker: Nightingale
content: ...I understand. I’ll switch off the monitoring equipment, but if anything happens, contact me immediately.
When you return to Wendy's side, she's sitting on the ground in silence. Her hands and face are sticky with blood and her face looks expressionless—rather like an undertaker indeed.
Wendy doesn't respond, but quietly nods.
Wendy, you and your companions are stopping the spread of Corruptors, aren't you?
You can see that, rather than trading in cadavers, Wendy is the one trying to resolve the matter, and that the Undertakers weren't a dissident group, but rather a secret contamination cleanup squad.

speaker: Wendy
content: Hah... You’re only just realizing this now?

speaker: Wendy
content: That’s right, I’m an Undertaker.

speaker: Wendy
content: This is everything I believe in.
You're the Undertaker who stayed true to your beliefs.
But I'd just like to know more about you... and your truth.

speaker: Wendy
content: My truth... Everything you see now is the truth!
I only see you right now, Wendy.
Would you be willing to tell me some more stories from back then?

speaker: Wendy
content: Why... are you so interested in me?
I think it's one of the steps required to become a trustworthy companion.
Perhaps moved once again by this word, Wendy fell silent for a while, lingering in the conciliation, before speaking in a faint voice.

speaker: Wendy
content: I was an orphan, and that person adopted me. I was bound to become an Undertaker...

speaker: Wendy
content: There, everyone was the same—We were all people with no future.

speaker: Wendy
content: Our clothes were ragged... and we were injured but didn’t have any medicine. Once our wounds were exposed to the contamination, they gnawed away at us little by little...

speaker: Wendy
content: We lived each day under threat by monsters, and... the contamination, the crazy thoughts...

speaker: Wendy
content: Yes, that’s it... Our job was to clean up the filth, so much filth, day in and day out. Over time, our vision got blurry and there were people talking nonstop in our heads...

speaker: Wendy
content: I even wondered... if I wasn’t also just a monster with a sword hanging over my head... Haha... We’d go crazy sooner or later...

speaker: Wendy
content: But... everyone said it’s fine...

speaker: Wendy
content: They said that, since the contamination had taken everything from us, we couldn’t allow it to take away more people’s happiness.

speaker: Wendy
content: Since there was nothing left to take from us, we were the best people for this great task.

speaker: Wendy
content: They said... since we’d found such a great task, we—these dead folk walking—had found a reason to live...

speaker: Wendy
content: See, aren’t they just the noblest, greatest people in the world?
Wendy smiles slightly. It's a gentle smile, but also a profoundly sad one.

speaker: Wendy
content: The captain... once said this to me...

speaker: Wendy
content: He said that our sacrifice was worth something, that people would thank us... that we would be remembered as heroes of the DisCity...

speaker: Wendy
content: Haha... Idiot... What good are other people’s thanks...? Isn’t having each other enough?

speaker: Wendy
content: What do people in high places know about danger? What do they know about contamination?!

speaker: Wendy
content: Those thieves, too... Dirty, vile... We were doing it to fight the contamination, we didn’t want their filthy money! Or those hypocritical thank-yous!

speaker: Wendy
content: But the captain betrayed us all, all for those insignificant nobodies...
Wendy chokes up slightly again, but stubbornly continues speaking.

speaker: Wendy
content: It was too cruel for him...

speaker: Wendy
content: That little boy... His eyes were red and streaming with tears before he was taken away... but he couldn't stop... laughing like a crazy person.

speaker: Wendy
content: I asked him, that man, the captain...

speaker: Wendy
content: He said there was nothing we could do, not anything. "The people above" wouldn't allow it.

speaker: Wendy
content: I wanted to know why "the people above" couldn’t protect him, couldn’t protect us!

speaker: Wendy
content: That’s why I followed him that day, to get a clear answer.
Wendy looks towards the person collapsed on the ground, her words bristling with indignation.

speaker: Wendy
content: I learned from their conversation that, to the top, we're not even worth mentioning... We were always meant to die out here.

speaker: Wendy
content: We’re just scum with no way out! They can get as many maggots like us as they like!

speaker: Wendy
content: Once one batch is all used up, they can just move on to the next one! There’s no need to give them good equipment!

speaker: Wendy
content: We’re the ones with the responsibility, we’re the ones who face the danger... but those dirtbags?!

speaker: Wendy
content: Those dirtbags, they’re just more trash in this polluting stream of filth, there’s nothing human about them!

speaker: Wendy
content: I'll chop off their fat-filled heads! While I still have breath... I'll split their necks open!
The tears that have been gathering in Wendy's eyes roll down her face and plummet to the ground.
Through gritted teeth, she denounces the forces responsible for her tragic past. It's heartbreaking to listen to.
You hold her hand and gently place it over your heart, hoping she can feel it beat.
Thank you for trusting me enough to tell me this. I believe you, Wendy.
I'm sorry for making you think about such awful things... I'm going to help prove your and your companions' innocence.
So, can you let me meet your companions?

speaker: Wendy
content: My companions... What are you gonna do to them?!

speaker: Wendy
content: Lock them up, put them in chains, and throw them into danger again?!
No, Wendy, definitely not...
None of you were traitors to the organization, on the contrary, you paid a huge price on its behalf.
I won't let you all stay buried here like this.
I have a duty to fight for the innocence you deserve.
Consider it a thank-you... to you and your comrades for fighting for the light in this world.

speaker: Wendy
content: But... can I trust you all?
After hearing this, Wendy is silent for a long time. Finally, she bursts into loud laughter, as if having just heard a joke.
She takes you by the hand and leads you to that piece of earth in the morning sun.

speaker: Wendy
content: Hahahaha...!

speaker: Wendy
content: I was wrong, Mister Chief.
female_content: I was wrong, Ms. Chief.

speaker: Wendy
content: I’ll take you... to see my comrades, Chief.
Wendy takes your hand and leads you straight ahead. You realize that you're headed "south" like those two body brokers mentioned.
You pass through the stench of rotting corpses and finally arrive at a quiet clearing.

speaker: Wendy
content: We’re here...

speaker: Wendy
content: Nova? John? Are you guys awake?

speaker: Wendy
content: Ah... Sorry, Chief. They’re still sleeping, so they’re not ready to see you yet. Come in, we can wait for them to get up together.

speaker: Wendy
content: Welcome to the house of the Undertakers.
She speaks in an exceptionally gentle voice, but no one comes out to greet you from the place she calls home.
In the bright red sunlight, you can clearly see that several holes have been dug in this place before hastily being filled back up...
Strange things have been placed in front of the pits, as if they were nestled up together in a peaceful slumber.

speaker: Wendy
content: Come in, come in, just... keep your voice down a little...
Wendy's voice lowers as she raises a finger over her pursed lips.

speaker: Wendy
content: They’re tired, we should let them sleep.

speaker: Wendy
content: I’ll introduce you to all of them—quietly, of course.

speaker: Wendy
content: This is Nova, he’s a big goofball. It’s almost impossible to move him once he’s gone to sleep, even though we clearly eat the same things every day.

speaker: Wendy
content: And this one, the one I set with stones!
Wendy points to a different pit, atop of which is strewn several small stones commonly found by the Rust.

speaker: Wendy
content: This is John, he’s an orphan who can’t even count, but he can clearly remember how many Corruptors he buried.

speaker: Wendy
content: For everyone he buried, he would find a stone to remember it by and carry it with him... I put all those stones next to his pillow!

speaker: Wendy
content: But he asked me to add one more stone this time. He said that when he turns into a Corruptor completely, he’ll bury himself...

speaker: Wendy
content: But I didn’t add it. Since he’s so tired, he won’t notice if it’s there or not while he’s sleeping.

speaker: Wendy
content: Then there’s her... My poor Lily...

speaker: Wendy
content: She’s Fino’s good friend, but she could only watch as Fino mutated little by little... there was nothing we could do. In the end, we buried Fino together...

speaker: Wendy
content: It wasn’t easy getting her to fall asleep, so make sure you don’t wake her up. Otherwise, she’ll start crying again.
Wendy gently pats the pit, as if lulling a child to sleep.

speaker: Wendy
content: As for me... This is my bed here!
She points to a newly-dug shallow pit at the end of the row of graves, then lies down in it, curling up and smiling at you.

speaker: Wendy
content: I sleep here every day together with everyone else. Too bad they’re always sleeping in, I’m the only one who ever gets up.
Wendy... you can't sleep with them...
They're... already dead.

speaker: Wendy
content: They’re... They’re dead?!
I'm sorry, Wendy.
Those people already have their eyes on this place, these bodies can't stay here anymore.
The best thing we can do for them is taking them away from here...

speaker: Wendy
content: Why would you say that they’re dead...? Why do you want to take them away...?

speaker: Wendy
content: Those traitors said the same thing... Do you want their bodies, too?!

speaker: Wendy
content: They’re not dead! They’ll never leave me!!
Wendy breaks down again and her eyes look so red that blood could drip out of them.
She cries, laughs, and snarls at you.

speaker: Wendy
content: Hahahaha! I knew it, you FAC dog!

speaker: Wendy
content: You’re just like them! Trampling on us!

speaker: Wendy
content: I know all about your depraved ideas!

speaker: Wendy
content: But one day... you’ll be just like the Undertakers were back then!

speaker: Wendy
content: Betrayed by your loved ones... Betrayed by everyone!!!

speaker: Wendy
content: You’ll see everyone die right before your eyes...

options: Apologize to Wendy and reassure her

content: I'm sorry, Wendy. I don't want to separate you and your companions whatsoever.
Ignoring the chainsaw pointed at you, you slowly walk forward and hold her hand.

speaker: Wendy
content: You’re no companion of mine, don’t touch me...
But I can't leave you here all alone.

speaker: Wendy
content: What are you talking about? Everyone’s right here with me. The Undertakers will be together forever.

speaker: Wendy
content: I want to wait for them to wake up...
You already know this, don't you...

speaker: Wendy
content: Shut up!
She shouts this angrily, but her gradually reddening eyes avoid your gaze, as if she is trying hard to resist something.
You look at the pit where she "sleeps peacefully every night".

options: That's the grave you dug for yourself, isn't it?

content: You remembered the day that each of them left and gave them a comfortable final resting place. You gave them all a warm burial.
But Wendy, now that you've seen everyone off, who will lay you to rest?

speaker: Wendy
content: Ooohhh... Waaahhhhh!!!
Her suppressed choking sobs finally burst into cries of grief. Her chainsaw drops into the mud, and the last Undertaker falls to her knees, trembling.
You lean down and gently cup her face, wiping away her endless stream of tears.

speaker: Wendy
content: I’m the last one, there won’t be any new Undertakers in this world again. This will all end here with me, I swear it!

speaker: Wendy
content: If they were still here, I could go on shouldering the burden of the undertakers... but those scumbags want their remains...!!

speaker: Wendy
content: I just want them!
You take her into your arms. The scent of the soil from the grave has dispelled the smell of blood from her body, like opening a room that has been shut for a long time.

speaker: Wendy
content: Let them stay with me, don’t take them away from me... please.
Someday, if you also... want to sleep, I'll take you to be with them... I can promise you that much.
But you're still alive right now... You're still a human being, Wendy. While you're alive, why don't you stay with me?

speaker: Wendy
content: ...Why?
Because I'm just like you, I can't bear the pain of losing people close to me.
If I die, how will you feel?

speaker: Wendy
content: No, I don’t want you to die. I won’t allow it.

speaker: Wendy
content: I won’t bury you. If you die... I’ll really have nothing left... So, you’re not allowed to die!
Okay... I'll do my best. Thanks for letting me be your companion.
Since you're carrying the burden of the Undertakers, then until the day you return to their side...

options: Let me carry it with you.

speaker: Wendy
content: Okay... I promise, too.

speaker: Wendy
content: Before they come to take me home, you’ll... be my home.
Her voice grows smaller and smaller as she slowly closes her eyes. After a long and exhausting night, she drifts off to sleep in your arms.
Did you save her?
You don't know.
But at the very least, tonight she won't have to sleep on a pillow of death in that small, cold pit.
Through the glass flap on the door, you see the young girl in the interrogation room.
She sits there quietly without the slightest hint of warmth in her eyes.

You feel the thick protective suit on you, and glance at the myriad of surveillance devices in the interrogation room. After confirming that it's safe, you push the door open and switch on the lights.
Hi, Pacassi.
Pacassi lifts her head slightly, on which is her pale, apathetic face.
MBCC and the Ring Research Institute have reached an agreement to transfer you here. You will live here as a Sinner detained by MBCC from now on.
Of course, given that you will be living in the Bureau from now on, I'll have to confirm some important security matters with you.

speaker: Pacassi
content: I understand.
Pacassi's voice is cold and distant.

speaker: Pacassi
content: Please start the interrogation.

You glance at the nuclear detection module on the wall. The old device, provided by the Ring Research Institute, is almost static. The numbers on the screen fluctuate between 0.3 and 0.5—which means you're safe, for now.
You pick up the files in your hand and unwrap the bag labeled with a nuclear radiation warning sign, thinking about your conversation with Nightingale earlier today.
Nightingale frowns next to the desk. When she sees you coming in, she puts down the file in her hand and stands up with a stern face.
Since the Ring Research Institute transferred Pacassi over, MBCC has been preparing for Pacassi's detainment, while Nightingale sorts out some relevant information.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Below are the original descriptions.

speaker: Nightingale
content: "Although the subject has shown no intent to attack, radiation levels continue to accumulate when she stays in one place for a long time."

speaker: Nightingale
content: "When the subject experiences emotional fluctuations, the radiation level increases abnormally and can reach up to 1986.4 Roentgen."

speaker: Nightingale
content: "Tissue cut from the subject continues to emit intense radiation, and decontamination is extremely costly."
She's not a Sinner from the DisCity, is she? How does she have such a dangerous ability?
Nightingale shakes her head.

speaker: Nightingale
content: It's not specified in the file. It is only known that eight years ago, an unusual energy reaction was detected somewhere 2,000 kilometers north of the DisCity, where the Ring Research Institute monitored.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Documents show that an abandoned nuclear power plant was located there.
A nuclear power plant?

speaker: Nightingale
content: It's an energy facility in the olden days. It used technology destroyed and eliminated by the city-states—which had devastating power too.

speaker: Nightingale
content: ...When the rescue team arrived, the human settlement, Mayek, was already leveled to the ground. Pacassi was the only survivor.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Some researchers suspected that Pacassi was responsible for the nuclear accident, but there was no evidence.
And they never asked Pacassi about it?

speaker: Nightingale
content: There's no relevant information. The Research Institute didn't have a professional interrogation department after all, and they would't do anything beyond their duties.

speaker: Nightingale
content: In fact, they only studied Pacassi's abilities for the first couple of years. For the few years after that, Pacassi had been locked in a radiation isolation room.

speaker: Nightingale
content: The Research Institute didn't care about this Sinner who had lost her research value, nor was it obligated to find out the truth behind the incident in Mayek.

speaker: Nightingale
content: They just dismissed Pacassi as a nuisance and sent her to the Bureau.
Now, this "nuisance," the suspect behind Mayek's destruction, is sitting before you.
You waste no time, flipping through the file Nightingale has summarized for you, and formally begin the interrogation.

Tell me about your ability.
Pacassi looks at you in the eyes and replies,

speaker: Pacassi
content: A radiation field with a maximum radius of about 100 meters and a maximum level of about 2,000 Roentgen.

speaker: Pacassi
content: It can be activated by will, or reactively released by external triggers.
Looks like you know your ability very well.

speaker: Pacassi
content: I just memorized what they said in their research.
Her voice sounds calm while her body remains unmoved.
How are you feeling?

speaker: Pacassi
content: Great.

speaker: Pacassi
content: I don't need to eat or rest. My strength and endurance have improved a lot. And the radiation doesn't affect me.

speaker: Pacassi
content: I feel great.
Pacassi shakes her head while her eyes subconsciously glance at her mechanical arm.
Does your arm hurt?
The dark metal sheen of the paint looks out of place on the young girl.

speaker: Pacassi
content: ...Okay.

speaker: Pacassi
content: The nerves connected to the prosthesis can hurt.
Did the Ring Research Institute install the prosthesis for you?
You are a little curious. After all, it isn't very common to see such exquisite bionic device, even in the DisCity.
If Pacassi had lost her arm in a small remote town before gaining the Sinner's ability, it would have been a massive inconvenience in her life.

speaker: Pacassi
content: They added the bionic fibers, but the metal structure inside was installed in the town.

speaker: Pacassi
content: It's been too long. The nerves were already connected to it, so it couldn't be replaced anymore.
Did it happen before the explos... before you became a Sinner?

speaker: Pacassi
content: Yes.

speaker: Pacassi
content: It was an accident in a pipe repair.

speaker: Pacassi
content: I got used to the prosthesis very quickly. The pain was tolerable, and it didn't affect work.
You had to work after you lost your arm? What did you do?

speaker: Pacassi
content: Same as before.

speaker: Pacassi
content: Check and repair the pipes of the nuclear power plant three times a week, weed the fields, and help the mayor process and deliver documents.

speaker: Pacassi
content: That's all.
That's too much work for a child.

speaker: Pacassi
content: Chief.
Pacassi stares into your eyes, her voice clearly sounding more emotional.

speaker: Pacassi
content: The DisCity is different from us and most places in the world.

speaker: Pacassi
content: The DisCity has abundant energy and Hypercubes to avoid natural disasters.

speaker: Pacassi
content: But Mayek didn't... We couldn't afford to feed idlers.
...I'm sorry.

speaker: Pacassi
content: I didn't mean to blame you.
I know, but I must apologize.
Pacassi speaks no more. The atmosphere becomes peaceful again.
Only then do you realize that not once did the device on the wall send out an alarm during the whole process of questioning just now.
This isn't quite consistent with what the Ring Research Institute claimed.

You lay out more documents before Pacassi, and a few of the images look particularly appalling.
Large, ruined steel and concrete buildings, piles of shattered concrete blocks and debris, and a crumbling ghost town covered with vines...
This is Mayek, Pacassi's hometown. Or rather, the ruins of her hometown.
Pacassi, there's an important issue I must figure out in this interrogation.
The truth behind Mayek's destruction.
Pacassi lowers her head.

speaker: Pacassi
content: It was an accident.

options: Was it planned? Or was it a mere accident?

speaker: Pacassi
content: Both.
Can you elaborate more?

speaker: Pacassi
content: ...The nuclear power plant in Mayek had been close to its limits for as long as I could remember.

speaker: Pacassi
content: We were struggling to keep it running, but there's no way we could stop it from deteriorating and becoming more dangerous.
Was there no other solution?

speaker: Pacassi
content: Mayek was in this continent's northernmost part. Half of the year was winter.

speaker: Pacassi
content: There was no way we could survive without the energy generated from the nuclear power plant.

speaker: Pacassi
content: Many did, including my parents.

speaker: Pacassi
content: They went to the south, to the city of dreams where they didn't have to worry about the cold and hunger... They abandoned us.

speaker: Pacassi
content: But there were always people who wanted to stay.
Pacassi raises her head.

speaker: Pacassi
content: We knew about the nuclear war that destroyed half the world after Nightfall and the risk of accidents with nuclear power plants.

speaker: Pacassi
content: But we had no choice if we wanted to survive in our hometown.
But still, your town...

speaker: Pacassi
content: Fewer and fewer people stayed. Eventually, we didn't even have enough staff to operate the power plant.

speaker: Pacassi
content: There was more and more work on everyone's shoulders. A lot of them couldn't take it anymore.

speaker: Pacassi
content: Before the accident, there were only two people left in the town.
You and the mayor, Longyear?

speaker: Pacassi
content: Yes.
You said Mayek's destruction wasn't entirely a pure accident.
If it wasn't you, was it Longyear the mayor?
Pacassi looks slightly stunned.

speaker: Pacassi
content: No... He just...

speaker: Pacassi
content: It was my fault.
The fact that Pacassi tries to hide it makes you more certain of your speculation.

In the early years of Nightfall, a nuclear war lasting for years wiped out most of human civilization. The survivors signed the Nuclear Restriction Pact, which banned all nuclear technology, including nuclear power plants.
You should know the implications of this pact, Pacassi.
Pacassi purses her lips without giving a response.
All I want is the truth, a reason for you to stay in the Bureau without being feared...
Whatever you've gone through in Mayek is all in the past. Mayek doesn't exist anymore. There's nothing more for you to protect.

speaker: Pacassi
content: That's not true!
Pacassi suddenly raises her voice.

speaker: Pacassi
content: I'm still alive. Mayek hasn't disappeared!

speaker: Pacassi
content: It's Longyear's life. It's our home... They were the ones who took me in when I was abandoned...

speaker: Pacassi
content: Yet I couldn't save him...
Pacassi looks up, her eyes full of tears.

speaker: Pacassi
content: I deserted him. I deserted Mayek...
Pacassi lowers her head after finishing the words in trembles. With her going through such emotional turmoil, you subconsciously glance at the surveillance device on the wall.
To your surprise, the numbers on the device are as calm as a late autumn lake.
Looking at the young girl weeping in front of you, you can't help but reaching out.
Pacassi...
Don't worry. The Bureau is your new shelter. We won't abandon you, and we won't use you for experiments...
You can consider it your... home, if you will.
You try to comfort her, yet your words seem so empty.

speaker: Pacassi
content: I don't have a home anymore. Not since that winter when Mayek and Longyear was gone.
Pacassi's voice is cold and resisting.
Looking at the grieving young girl before you, you realize any words of comfort are simply pointless right now.
Perhaps you should leave her alone for now.
You walk in the sports field in the Bureau. The Sinners are free to move about in the designated area during this time of day, and today is no exception.
The afternoon sun is bright and warm. You look over to the bench by the fence and find Pacassi there as expected.
Pacassi budges up without closing the book in her hand.
What are you reading?

speaker: Pacassi
content: The History of the DisCity, 6th edition.
You have heard of it, a well-known historiographical work that has been reprinted many times.
What made you want to read this?

speaker: Pacassi
content: I want to know about the history of the DisCity.

speaker: Pacassi
content: But more than that, I want to know how you guys view the world...
So what do you think of the Bureau now?

speaker: Pacassi
content: It's great here. I don't have to be in all sorts of experiments and can even have time to myself.

speaker: Pacassi
content: I'm really happy with my life now.
She never goes out of control, always finishes the work given to her, and never makes any mistakes, even in battles, which isn't her strong suit... Pacassi has always been reassuringly stable.
But she also hardly interacts with others. She's always alone, like an outsider.
This isn't what you want to see.
Pacassi, I have some questions for you.

speaker: Pacassi
content: Aren't we going to the interrogation room?
No, you've already proven yourself.
Instead of as a Chief and a Sinner, I hope we can talk as friends.
Pacassi looks at you, her head slightly tilted, and closes her book.

speaker: Pacassi
content: What would you like to ask?
Pacassi takes the directory from you readily.
It's just some personal questions I have. I want to know more about Mayek.
I want to know about you guys' past.
Pacassi caresses the leather cover gently.

speaker: Pacassi
content: Mayek was once a prosperous city, with an ice-free port which was rare in the north, and an independent nuclear power plant.

speaker: Pacassi
content: Mayek had a population of half a million at its peak.

speaker: Pacassi
content: But that was all before Nightfall.
Pacassi flips through the directory. Each page was filled with names that were then crossed out.

speaker: Pacassi
content: Actually, for the first few decades, there wasn't a significant decline in the population of Mayek, thanks to the nuclear power plant.

speaker: Pacassi
content: But since thirty years ago, the town's population had dropped below ten thousand.
Five hundred thousand to ten thousand... What happened?

speaker: Pacassi
content: Thirty years ago, the nuclear power plant stopped running for the first time.

speaker: Pacassi
content: I had read Longyear's notes. It was just a problem with the cooling tower's pipes, but they couldn't figure it out at that time no matter how much they tried.

speaker: Pacassi
content: To prevent the reactor core from overheating, possibly causing an irreversible accident, they shut it down.

speaker: Pacassi
content: When the power plant was up and running again, the town had lost three thousand people.
Did they leave the town? Or...

speaker: Pacassi
content: It was December. No one could leave alive.

speaker: Pacassi
content: People thought they were merely stuck in the winter, which they could survive through with the nuclear power plant.

speaker: Pacassi
content: But it wasn't until that day did they realize that the winter was longer than they expected.
The warm sunlight pours on the pages, making the names in bright red particularly glaring.

speaker: Pacassi
content: Since then, the nuclear power plant had more and more frequent accidents, which could last from half a day to as long as a month.

speaker: Pacassi
content: Longyear was elected as the new mayor, because he fixed the cooling tower in the first accident. But what he couldn't fix was the distress in the residents' hearts.

speaker: Pacassi
content: People had enough of living in fear, enough of mashed potatoes with ice shreds. They heard about the DisCity in the south, far more prosperous than the town they were in.
Pacassi heaves a soft breath.

speaker: Pacassi
content: This kind of emotion reached its peak when I was four.
What happened?

speaker: Pacassi
content: Same as every time. Power outage.

speaker: Pacassi
content: A major power outage, lasting from summer to early winter.
Pacassi flips a few pages in the directory and points to a name.

speaker: Pacassi
content: Leroy was a great chef. Everyone loved his borscht. Even I still remember the taste of it.

speaker: Pacassi
content: He left Mayek that year. And there has been no restaurant in town ever since.
Pacassi continues to flip to the back of the directory.

speaker: Pacassi
content: Nastia was an elementary school teacher. Her daughter went missing the year before.

speaker: Pacassi
content: She searched for her daughter all winter.
Did she find her?

speaker: Pacassi
content: Yes.

speaker: Pacassi
content: At the end of summer, she found her under melted snow.

speaker: Pacassi
content: The three-month power outage forced everyone to plan for the worst.

speaker: Pacassi
content: That was when my parents left me.
Why didn't they take you with them?
Pacassi shakes her head.

speaker: Pacassi
content: I don't remember.

speaker: Pacassi
content: All I remember is that Longyear took me to his house later.

speaker: Pacassi
content: He gave me a place to live and made me fruit soup. Longyear told me he would fix the power plant, and everything would be fine.

speaker: Pacassi
content: But that year, when he was fixing the power plant, he lost his legs and his only son...

options: That must have been really tough for him
I'm the boss of the company, and I have to work my fingers to the bone to put food on the table. It's so demeaning...

speaker: Pacassi
content: Yes.

speaker: Pacassi
content: Perhaps...

speaker: Pacassi
content: But, at least he didn't abandon me, like he never abandoned Mayek.
What happened then?

speaker: Pacassi
content: After that, I took over his son's work, and became his assistant.

speaker: Pacassi
content: On top of the assigned work, I also helped him with chores and maintenance reports for the power plant.
What happened to the nuclear power plant after that?
Pacassi lowers her head.

speaker: Pacassi
content: Accidents happened more and more frequently, and there were fewer and fewer people in the town.

speaker: Pacassi
content: In the last two years, the power plant never started again. The remaining residents survived by demolishing abandoned houses for fuel.

speaker: Pacassi
content: And Longyear's mental health became more and more... unstable.

speaker: Pacassi
content: Everyone realized that perhaps all is lost for Mayek.
But you stayed till the end.

speaker: Pacassi
content: We later saw a glimpse of hope.
Pacassi lifts her head and looks at you.

speaker: Pacassi
content: One day, an oddly-dressed traveling merchant came to town.

speaker: Pacassi
content: He said he was from the DisCity and offered us a type of stone for sale—a stone that he claimed to provide protection from natural disasters.
Hypercubes?

speaker: Pacassi
content: Yes.

speaker: Pacassi
content: I bought the Hypercubes and the complementary device with spare precious metals in the nuclear power plant, and kept it secret from Longyear.

speaker: Pacassi
content: After we started up the device, we were able to repair the power plant in only two days. For the next two months, the plant ran stably.

speaker: Pacassi
content: Until Longyear found out about it...
What did he do?

speaker: Pacassi
content: He smashed the device, called us all traitors, and told us to get out.

speaker: Pacassi
content: At that time, there were only a dozen people or so left in the town.
Why did he do that?

speaker: Pacassi
content: Maybe he was just too tired... Or maybe he realized what he had been insisting for the whole time was totally pointless...

speaker: Pacassi
content: No one understood him. Everyone said he was out of his mind. He destroyed our last hope, and everyone left that summer.
So, in the last days, it was just you and Longyear?
Pacassi shakes her head.

speaker: Pacassi
content: In the last days, Longyear wouldn't talk to me. For the whole summer, he just wandered around the town without uttering a word.

speaker: Pacassi
content: Eventually, we were the only two left in the town. He showed up at my door and said to me,

speaker: Pacassi
content: "Why are you still here? Have you no shame? Get the hell out! Out of my town!"

speaker: Pacassi
content: I left Mayek... I abandoned him.

speaker: Pacassi
content: At that time, I just headed south with my mind totally blank.

speaker: Pacassi
content: It was only in the next evening when it started snowing that I realized I couldn't leave Longyear there alone.

speaker: Pacassi
content: When I raced back to the town, I found the power plant running, with thick steam rising from the cooling tower.

speaker: Pacassi
content: It was as warm as summer around the power plant, so warm, even the snow melted.

speaker: Pacassi
content: I searched everywhere. In the end I found Longyear asleep in the duty room in his wheelchair...
That was when the power plant...

speaker: Pacassi
content: I don't remember the details of what happened afterwards.

speaker: Pacassi
content: I just remember something rushing into my body and I didn't feel cold anymore.

speaker: Pacassi
content: When I woke up again, I was already in the DisCity.

speaker: Pacassi
content: Longyear, the nuclear plant, Mayek... they were all gone. I'm the only one that survived.
Longyear belonged there. He couldn't leave his past behind, but at the end of his life, he didn't want you to be buried with the past.
He protected you, Pacassi, even when he kicked you out of the town. He wanted you to find your future.

speaker: Pacassi
content: ...I don't need a future.

speaker: Pacassi
content: Everyone was leaving for the future, leaving the past behind.

speaker: Pacassi
content: No one remembered Mayek and Longyear.

speaker: Pacassi
content: Who else will remember them if I don't?

speaker: Pacassi
content: I don't want this to happen.
Ring—Ring—
A rapid bell rings, indicating that the free time for the Sinners is over.
Pacassi hands the directory back to you, picks up the book on the side, and stands up.

speaker: Pacassi
content: Thank you. Thank you so much for all you've done.

speaker: Pacassi
content: You are so kind. You listened to my dull stories, gave me books I wanted to read, and treated all Sinners equally... But I'm not like them... I don't belong here.

speaker: Pacassi
content: I should go now.
Pacassi heads toward the nearby building hurriedly. The afternoon sun shines on her face.
Yet you can't feel the slightest warmth.
Pacassi looks at herself in the floor-to-ceiling mirror in the mall and speaks to you somewhat embarrassedly.

speaker: Pacassi
content: This jacket...

speaker: Pacassi
content: Constrains my movement. And the fabric is too thin...

options: It's time to buy some new clothes.

speaker: Pacassi
content: Thank you...

speaker: Pacassi
content: But...
You should buy some more summer outfits too. It's not good to always wear such thick layers.

speaker: Pacassi
content: I don't mind heat that much...
How about trying something else?
In this Eastside's busiest commercial street, Pacassi, who got dragged out by you, seems slightly uncomfortable being faced with a dazzling array of items.

speaker: Pacassi
content: I'm... really not used to this.
You need to relax.

speaker: Pacassi
content: Life at the Bureau is very relaxed already.
Pacassi speaks as she watches the bustling passersby and vehicles, and flinches back slightly timidly.
If you don't like it here, why don't we go somewhere else?

speaker: Pacassi
content: ...I don't have any place I want to go.

options: There's a place you will be interested in.

content: You can see Pacassi feeling slightly helpless.
You hold Pacassi's hands as you walk along the garden street. It's a nice day, and the sun sprinkles through the leaves onto the ground.
You walk down the long road, and a huge billboard comes into view.

speaker: Pacassi
content: Is this... Nastia?
On the billboard is an old lady, surrounded by children, with a heartfelt smile on her face.
Do you remember what she looked like? You were very young when she left Mayek, right?

speaker: Pacassi
content: Yeah, I do remember.
It says here that she's a celebrity tutor at this language school now. Seems like she's doing well.
How about we go see her together?

speaker: Pacassi
content: It's okay.

speaker: Pacassi
content: She may not recognize me. Even if she does, seeing me will only bring back unpleasant memories for her.
You say nothing. Going around the corner, you two come to a restaurant.
This is it.

speaker: Pacassi
content: As I told you, I don't need to eat.
They make really good borscht here. Wanna try?

speaker: Pacassi
content: Alright.
Pacassi replies very quietly. You take her hand and walk in.
The restaurant is doing well with many customers inside. Fortunately, you have already made a reservation. The waiter leads you to your seats.
After taking a seat, Pacassi skims through the menu and stops at one of the pages.

speaker: Pacassi
content: Borsc... Beet soup and bread, please.

speaker: Waiter
content: Is that all, Miss?
Looking at the waiter's slightly awkward smile, you sigh and take the menu.
Any recommendations?

speaker: Waiter
content: I strongly recommend our strawberry parfait for the two of you.

speaker: Pacassi
content: Parfait is... ice cream, right?

speaker: Waiter
content: That's right.

speaker: Pacassi
content: I'm alright, thanks.
You order a few more dishes, and the waiter hurries back to the kitchen.
It's noon time, and the restaurant is packed with customers. Thankfully, the restaurant is very speedy in serving food. It doesn't take long before the dishes are brought to the table.
Pacassi breaks the bread into small pieces and soaks them in the soup before putting it in her mouth—a way of eating rarely seen in the DisCity.
How is it? Do you like it?

speaker: Pacassi
content: Okay.
Does it taste familiar to you?

speaker: Pacassi
content: ...uh-huh.
Pacassi nods.
This restaurant is owned by Leroy.
Pacassi puts down the silverware as her eyes widen.
As she looks around at the restaurant packed with customers, Pacassi smiles in relief.

speaker: Pacassi
content: Looks like he's doing great.
Indeed. They're all doing great.
Do you still remember all these people?
You take a group photo out from your inside pocket.

speaker: Pacassi
