content: This is... Boris? Victoria, Nastia... Leroy? Why are they all together?
The Mayekens have begun their new lives in the DisCity.
They even formed a support group. I met with them the other day—they are very happy to take you in.

speaker: Pacassi
content: I'm... a Sinner.

speaker: Pacassi
content: They can't help me, and neither can I help them.
You should give it a chance. Maybe they can help you put your past behind...

speaker: Pacassi
content: ...I don't deserve it.
Silence falls. Pacassi quickly finishes the soup in front of her.

speaker: Pacassi
content: Let's go.
No need to rush. We have the whole afternoon.

speaker: Pacassi
content: Where else... are we going?
You hear resignation in Pacassi's voice, but also veiled excitement.

options: I promise you're going to like this.

content: You two come to a gray building, which seems to be still under renovation. You wave at the Bureau staff by the entrance.
How's the project going?

speaker: Staff
content: Everything's great! It'll be open for visits next week by the latest.
What about the real estate contract?

speaker: Staff
content: That's not a problem. We found the original contract. In the initial allocation, the FAC didn't specify we had to use it as a depot.

speaker: Staff
content: It doesn't matter if this is turned into a nightclub. It'll still be the Bureau's property.
Workers are carefully unloading some old equipment off the truck on the side.

speaker: Pacassi
content: Is this...

speaker: Pacassi
content: The hot spring pipes in pre-Nightfall Mayek?

speaker: Pacassi
content: You guys... went to Mayek?
You smile without directly answering Pacassi's question.
There's more inside. Let's go in and have a look.
Inside the building, the limited space is divided into several areas, with several "exhibits" in each area.

speaker: Pacassi
content: A reactor core, levers, and even the broadcasting station.

speaker: Pacassi
content: They're all here...
Pacassi names the "garbage" one by one, as if they are family treasures.
I've moved all your memories in Mayek here.
Pacassi's voice trembles. She takes a few steps back and hides in the shadows.

speaker: Pacassi
content: ...Please stop wasting time on me.
How can it be a waste of time?
Pacassi tugs at the corner of her jacket and says nothing.
You never eat unless you feel weak.

speaker: Pacassi
content: I don't need to...
You don't take any rest during battles, and neither do you ever think about your own safety.
You've helped me a lot. You've helped us all a lot. You're always so thoughtful to those around you.

speaker: Pacassi
content: I'm just doing what I should do.
You have things you like and things you want to talk about too... You don't have any sin. Even if you had, you would've redeemed yourself long ago.
You don't have to always be so humble. Try to accept kindness from your friends once in a while.
As the noise from the power switch reverberates, warm lights illuminate the entire hall.
Now let me present to you...
You take a piece of paper out of your pocket and read the words on it out loud.
Welcome to the land's northernmost part, a place where people battled against natural disasters with ancient nuclear technology and determination for a whole century without using Hypercubes.
Though the town no longer exists, its stories and people will continue to live.
This is the Mayek Museum. Please join me in witnessing the heroic town...
You turn around again and extend your hand toward Pacassi.
Do you like the opening speech? I'm going to have it engraved on the museum entrance.
Pacassi slowly steps forward out of the shadows.

speaker: Pacassi
content: Thank you.
Tears glisten in her eyes, yet her lips can't stop curling into a smile.

speaker: Pacassi
content: I love it...
Explain yourself. Why did you do that?

speaker: Dolly
content: Hmm... Does it matter?
You give no response, but simply activate the big screen and press the play button on the security footage.
You turn on the lights while you're at it. In the footage, Dolly constantly swings her baseball bat at the Corruptors in front of her.

speaker: Dolly
content: What's wrong with that? I'm just carrying out a mission.

speaker: Dolly
content: Now if you wrongly accuse me, you'll have to compensate me with an Eastside baseball poster!
You ignore Dolly and keep pressing the fast-forward button.
An explosion occurs, and the smoke completely blocks the camera.
The smoke gradually dissipates, and an angry Dolly charges at you with a roar, as if she regards you as her enemy.
You press the pause button.

options: Do you not want to explain?
I guess you're not wrongly accused at all.

speaker: Dolly
content: Ugh. To be honest, I'm a little bit disappointed in you.

speaker: Dolly
content: You talk exactly like those FAC guys.
Forget about that. How did you answer them?
I don't think this is a stupid question, by the way.

speaker: Dolly
content: I just said I went out of control. They even took the opportunity to give me a full examination.

speaker: Dolly
content: See? I'm back here now because they <color=#fb9259>did not find any problems</color>.

speaker: Dolly
content: And now you made me sit here... Are you questioning the FAC's decision? Hmm?
Dolly, with her hands folded, has an attitude of "I'll see what you're gonna do with me" written all over her face.
The FAC's decision is obviously non-disputable, but Dolly's behavior in the mission was so peculiar that you even pulled out Dolly's FAC training records for comparison.
Your power is so strong that you can even break free from the "shackles" when I get off guard.
Combined with the FAC survey report, I believe... Your ability is stronger than that.
test
test
test
test
test
test
"Findings on the ability of Dolly the Sinner"
Based on the records and the thirty MBCC adaptation training, it is discovered that Dolly the Sinner has the "Berserk" ability.

However, she becomes unconscious in the Berserk state. The Sinner in such a state performs destructive actions on all surrounding objects, with only the Chief of the Bureau's ability able to get her out of the state.
Upon analysis, it is confirmed that the Berserk state of Dolly the Sinner is most directly related to the feeling of her safety being threatened.
In this "battle" state, Dolly instinctively protects herself with her ability.

In the MBCC venue, we tried to quantify her abilities with combat devices. The initial tests were very successful, but all the testing robots were destroyed. It is expected that a new round of tests can be carried out next week.

speaker: Dolly
content: Pfft! That's it? More pointless tests for me?

speaker: Dolly
content: Listen. My ability only went out of control because I got too emotional, not because of some threat to my safety.

speaker: Dolly
content: The mission site was so close to the Eastside baseball stadium. I lost my consciousness just hearing the sound of the crowd chanting.
In that case, why did the FAC not write the report according to the descriptions of the subject Sinner?

speaker: Dolly
content: Simple. I'm a Syndican. They didn't think I was telling the truth.

options: You seem to have a bias against FAC.

content: The FAC never makes judgments this subjective.

speaker: Dolly
content: Hah... Have they not? They beat me back then, but luckily I was strong enough to take them all down.
Why were you involved with the FAC? You were in Syndicate.

speaker: Dolly
content: Well... I...

speaker: Dolly
content: I... accidentally hurt an Eastsider.
Then it should've been taken care of by the sheriffs in Syndicate. What has it got to do with the FAC?

speaker: Dolly
content: The sheriffs in Syndicate couldn't defeat me.
But the ones in Eastside could?

speaker: Dolly
content: E-Eastside? No... No, they were directly under the FAC.
Her lies are full of contradictions, but what baffles you is why she has to make up such lies.
You take out a piece of news back then.
test
test
test
test
test
test
test
On September 13 at 9:30 am, the biennial DIS Professional Baseball League was held at the Eastside Stadium. The opening game was between the Fountons and the Highlanders.
The Fountons' scores were behind, and their seed, Dolly, was underperforming. 33 minutes in the game, there was a violent beating incident.

Dolly, from the Fountons, got involved in a conflict with Haliaka from the Highlanders 
and punched her, sending the game into chaos.
Fortunately, the FAC members stationed in the venue arrived in time, bringing the situation under control and restoring order in the stadium.
However, due to the disruption, temporary venue maintenance was needed, delaying the following games by one day.
The game between the two teams will be rescheduled to next week. The player Dolly was sent off and will receive a lifetime ban.

According to the news, when you were playing baseball in Eastside, you punched a player on the opposing team and the FAC who were there to maintain order. But nothing is mentioned about anyone beating you up.
With each sentence you read, Dolly buries her face lower and lower.
So why did you say the FAC beat you?

speaker: Dolly
content: It's because... because!
Dolly's face becomes completely red.

speaker: Dolly
content: Urgh, kill me!... Because if I didn't say that, I wouldn't even be able to go back to Syndicate! I have no choice but to say it's a reaction triggered by being beaten up!

speaker: Dolly
content: I came all the way from Syndicate to Eastside for this game. And even risked violating that damned West District Regulations!

speaker: Dolly
content: The FAC found out who I was in the middle of the game, so they tried to pause the game and take me away. I definitely wouldn't let them!

options: You actually managed to beat them up?

speaker: Dolly
content: Of course, I beat them up the first time I activated my ability. Pretty impressive, right?

speaker: Dolly
content: I was thinking like, "Even if they're arresting me, they'll have to wait until this game's done." And the thought gave me strength.

speaker: Dolly
content: My "emotion" enabled me to knock them all out of the way just with that baseball bat.
Your emotions add so much power to your abilities?

speaker: Dolly
content: Chief, just put yourself in my shoes.

speaker: Dolly
content: It's your first time on the stage of your dreams. All the spectators are cheering for you. When you're about to get ahead of the other team, someone comes over and tells you to leave the field. Aren't you gonna be mad?
And then you fled back to Syndicate, saying that the FAC members beat you up and disqualified you from baseball games?

speaker: Dolly
content: Humph... That was my first time using my ability, so I couldn't quite control myself.

speaker: Dolly
content: If I can still play in the games... I'll definitely be able to control myself and I won't let those FAC guys find out!
If it weren't for me, you might have been treated as a Corruptor and got shot down by the FAC today.

speaker: Dolly
content: ...Humph.
In the face of your scolding, Dolly goes silent.
Is emotion really the cause for Dolly going out of control? Did the FAC really make a mistake in their investigation?
Your shackles never had any issues, yet she broke free from your control today.
What in the world went wrong... Could it be the battle process?

speaker: Dolly
content: Gosh. Do you have any more questions or not?!

speaker: Dolly
content: If not, let me go. I haven't practiced my bat swinging today!
Dolly seems impatient. Her iconic bat sits in a corner of the room. It certainly made its mark in her conflict with the FAC. But... Dolly doesn't fight with it very often.
You want to ask Dolly about this one more possibility.

options: Do you often fight with a baseball bat?

speaker: Dolly
content: What made you ask?

speaker: Dolly
content: Not really. Some Corruptors simply don't deserve it. Fists are the most direct weapon in Syndicate.
And you didn't use your baseball bat in those thirty tests either?

speaker: Dolly
content: Of course not. I didn't want to break the testing device and cause trouble for you guys.

speaker: Dolly
content: But those things seem to be even less sturdy than I thought.

options: And you practice your swing every day, right?

speaker: Dolly
content: I've been preparing for the Eastside Baseball League all along.
How do you feel when you swing the bat?

speaker: Dolly
content: How do I feel? Does the anxiety of wanting a game count?
Seems like the ban has a really big impact on you.

speaker: Dolly
content: The ban is on Dolly as a Sinner. What does it have to do with Dolly the baseball player? You'll help me, right, Chief?
Be serious. I'm asking you a serious question here.

speaker: Dolly
content: I am being serious here! I honestly really want to go back and play baseball games again!

speaker: Dolly
content: Can you just do me a favor and fight for a chance for me, Chief?! If you're concerned or anything, just stand by there and watch me with those shackles of yours!

speaker: Dolly
content: I promise, I'll definitely be able to control myself!

speaker: Dolly
content: Gosh... How petty of you.
According to my analysis, you won't have much of a chance to play baseball on the field anymore.

speaker: Dolly
content: Well, you never came across... as someone who likes to joke around like this... Hahaha.

speaker: Dolly
content: Come on now, Chief, be honest... Do you not want to help me?
You're not a baseball player. You're a Sinner.

speaker: Dolly
content: Ha... Hahaha... I've heard this too many times.

speaker: Dolly
content: I told you, I'll be able to control myself if you are there with me!

speaker: Dolly
content: Right? Don't you think? Well, shouldn't it be super easy for you? You must've got distracted today, that's all. It's okay... I totally get it.
I was doing my best with your shackles today.

speaker: Dolly
content: Well, you were just not feeling your best then! Come on... It happens to everyone! Look at me, I don't get to hit a home run every time either.
I honestly do not think you will ever be able to play in baseball games again.
I am sorry. There's nothing I can do to help you.
I am being serious. You... will probably never be able to play in baseball games again.

speaker: Dolly
content: Now I'm really getting mad if you keep saying things like this.
It's not that I don't want to help you. I'm simply not able to help. Look at this.
test
test
test
test
test
test
You head toward the corner and show her the broken bat.
The metal bat was squeezed by external forces and eventually snapped in two.
The surface where it snapped is stained with Corruptors' blood, and the bat is covered with pits from the blows.
The reason why you went manic must have something to do with this.

speaker: Dolly
content: ...Is this some kind of lame joke? And I'm supposed to play along with you or something?

speaker: Dolly
content: Don't be silly. It's not like I haven't played baseball after my ability got awakened.

options: I don't deny your point from earlier.

content: No one knows you better than yourself.
But you don't seem to have fought much with this bat. You usually reserved it for those you subconsciously believe to be the "strongest enemies."
Am I right?

speaker: Dolly
content: Yep—
As far as I can see, your ability isn't just related to emotions.
It has more to do with this.
You swing the bat in your hand.

speaker: Dolly
content: Gosh... now can you stop being ridiculous. It isn't even funny anymore.

speaker: Dolly
content: I always start my batting practice after practicing my swing, and I've never got into the same state as I did today.
How about this? Let's make a bet.
If you win, I'll get you in the Eastside baseball stadium and let you play a baseball game all you like.

speaker: Dolly
content: What the hell...

speaker: Dolly
content: Wait... Qualification for the Eastside Baseball League?!

speaker: Dolly
content: Are you serious?!
Of course, but only if you do as I say.

speaker: Dolly
content: But no strange requests.
You will come with me on the next mission at the Rust.
Oh wait.
Remember to bring your baseball bat.

speaker: Dolly
content: ...That's it?
That's it. It's just the weakest Corruptors. You might not even need to use your ability.
"Emotion" is only one of the triggers for Dolly's ability. All the uncontrollable situations involved that one bat.
In the Eastside baseball stadium, she knocked down countless FAC members with the bat. During the mission, this same bat allowed her to break free from your shackles.
Without the bat, she's no more than a more explosive and less obedient Sinner.
You believe that the secret lies behind this bat.

speaker: Dolly
content: Hahahahaha! Why don't you just give me the ticket? This mission is so easy that even those FAC rookies can do it.
You sigh as you watch Dolly getting smugger.
Of course, you will have to wait in the cell for the few days before this mission.

speaker: Dolly
content: The cell?! Isn't... Isn't it only for Sinners who've made serious mistakes...?
So attacking the MBCC Chief is a small mistake?
Nightingale will take you there.

speaker: Dolly
content: Can I bring my bat?
No. No weapons are allowed in the cell.

speaker: Dolly
content: But I just want to practice...

speaker: Dolly
content: Tsk... I'm gonna teach you a lesson... You wait till I come out...

speaker: Dolly
content: You're just an MBCC Chief... Just a Chief!
You leave the interrogation room with Dolly gritting her teeth in her seat.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Dolly the Sinner, are you awake?

speaker: Nightingale
content: There is a mission for you. Please get ready.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, the cell has already been unlocked.

speaker: Nightingale
content: I've got to go deal with other Bureau business.
Before Nightingale disappears in sight, the person curled up in the cell starts moving.

speaker: Dolly
content: ...Huh?

speaker: Dolly
content: Urgh!!
Being just woken up by Nightingale, Dolly immediately gains her energy at the sight of you.

speaker: Dolly
content: Chief! You're finally here!

speaker: Dolly
content: Heh heh... Time for the mission, right?! I was almost bored to death for the past few days!

speaker: Dolly
content: What are we waiting for then?! Let's go!

speaker: Dolly
content: The sooner we finish, the sooner I can prepare for the Eastside Baseball League!

speaker: Dolly
content: Right, Chief?!

speaker: Dolly
content: You liar! I thought we agreed?!
It isn't really a mission.
Think of it as the 31st... test.

speaker: Dolly
content: Tsk. Whatever. I'm sure I'll be able to control myself.
That couldn't be better. Oh, and this is for you.
You toss the baseball bat to Dolly, who leaps up eagerly like an excited puppy, snatching it midair before nuzzling it against her face affectionately.

speaker: Dolly
content: I miss you so much! I couldn't even have a good night's sleep without you.
Looks like you're in high spirits though.
Dolly glares at you.

speaker: Dolly
content: By the way, can we get there by motorcycle?

speaker: Dolly
content: I haven't enjoyed that feeling of speeding along for a while!
You shake your head and pat your pocket.

options: Maybe we don't need a motorcycle to get speeding

content: The Rust's rundown scene recedes swiftly on the sides. After driving through a high-risk zone, you switch on the autopilot mode.

speaker: Dolly
content: Well... I feel kind of nostalgic looking at this place.

speaker: Dolly
content: I had no fear for anyone back then, and I ended up almost killing myself in a pile of Corruptors.

options: What were you doing at the Rust?

content: Trying to make ends meet?

speaker: Dolly
content: Now you're underestimating me. Why would I ever do such a thing?

speaker: Navigator
content: Upcoming left turn. Rough road conditions ahead. Please fasten your seat belt.

speaker: Dolly
content: Looks like the Bureau's sat nav isn't that familiar with the Rust after all.

speaker: Dolly
content: We're gonna run into Corruptors going this way.

speaker: Corruptor
content: Roarrrr—!
Before Dolly finishes her sentence, a Corruptor charges out from behind a garbage pile. You hurriedly switch the car to manual control and accelerate at full speed.
The Corruptor's speedy with a good hearing. When it notices the sound, it rushes towards you.

speaker: Dolly
content: It's a mutant and a tough one. Should I get out to deal with it?

speaker: Dolly
content: Oh... Okay, then. Good luck.
You press down the gas hard, but the Corruptor doesn't get any slower and continues to follow behind.

speaker: Dolly
content: You look like you're struggling. Since you won't let me fight, I'll drive for you!
She reaches out from the back seat and grabs the sat nav.

speaker: Dolly
content: Don't worry—I know this area like the back of my hands.
She draws a few lines on the sat nav and frowns, then presses the confirm button.

speaker: Navigator
content: The route has been changed. Direction revision in progress.
The car leaps high above the piles of trash in the Rust, crashes through the mountain of trash, and lands on the other side of the gulch.

speaker: Dolly
content: Ohhhh. Exciting! All we need to do is to trick that big idiot!
The Corruptor is left well behind while you continue onward toward your destination.
Was this how you got to Eastside?

speaker: Dolly
content: Of course.

speaker: Dolly
content: This is the fastest and most convenient way for Syndicans to get into Eastside.
Why would you do that? Weren't you worried about the West District Regulations?

speaker: Dolly
content: West District Regulations... Psst. A whole bunch of nonsense.

speaker: Dolly
content: Even if I did get caught in Eastside and deported, there's really nothing for me to lose.

speaker: Dolly
content: The approval takes such a long time and the road fees are so incredibly expensive. Most of all, I simply couldn't wait any longer.
For what? The baseball game?

speaker: Dolly
content: Of course. I want to get to the top stage and play against the strongest players. There was no match for me in Syndicate anymore.
Her answer is so definite and without any hesitation.
But Eastside and Syndicate are like worst enemies. Aren't you worried you're going to be condemned by Syndicans?

speaker: Dolly
content: Pfft... Hahaha.

speaker: Dolly
content: To be honest, I had never thought about it at all.

options: ...Well, that is definitely an answer you'd give.

speaker: Dolly
content: If there has to be a reason... I wanted to show the Eastsiders that Syndicans can be great baseball players too.
An electronic voice interrupts her words.

speaker: Navigator
content: We're at the destination. Please exit.

speaker: Dolly
content: Well, the Bureau certainly has high quality vehicles. My motorcycle would definitely have been torn to pieces if I drove it like that.

speaker: Dolly
content: You haven't forgotten our agreement, have you?
You nod.

speaker: Corruptor
content: Ha—
The Corruptors seem to have sensed humans and begin to gather around you.
In the face of the Corruptors coming at the vehicle, you give Dolly the order.

speaker: Dolly
content: Take this!
Before you even finish speaking, Dolly dashes like a sharp arrow piercing straight into the center of the Corruptors.
She swings the metal bat in her hand as hard as she can, knocking down the Corruptors one after another.
But even someone as strong as Dolly simply cannot fight against the Corruptors without using her ability.

speaker: Dolly
content: Tsk... I thought I could easily win the bet.

speaker: Dolly
content: I hope you didn't set me up for something. Stay away from me, I'm going to clear them all up.

options: Just don't get out of control.

speaker: Dolly
content: Okay... Okay...

speaker: Dolly
content: I won't...

speaker: Dolly
content: I won't... Ahhhhhhhhhhhh!
The amount of Corruptors isn't decreasing at all. After ordering her not to attack you, you begin to step back.
Dolly begins to release her energy as she did in the Bureau's tests.
The only difference is that she has a baseball bat in her hand this time.

speaker: Dolly
content: Aaahhh—
Like a fighting machine that never gets tired, she weaves through the Rust with her all-destructive power.
She gets faster and faster, to a speed so fast that your eyes can barely catch up.
This is the first time you watch Dolly in battle so closely.
It's also the first time you feel Dolly's power tearing your consciousness so fiercely.

speaker: Dolly
content: Die...!
With each swing of her bat, the shackles binding her gets torn apart even more.

speaker: Dolly
content: ...I... won't go out of control...
For Dolly, this is no longer a fight against the Corruptors, but against herself.
You notice Dolly's twisted face as she desperately tries to control her emotions.

speaker: Dolly
content: Why...?

speaker: Dolly
content: Isn't it working... Ahhh!
Unfortunately, even though she remains more conscious than ever, her body is swinging the bat uncontrollably.

speaker: Dolly
content: Stop... Come on... Stop!
The situation is getting out of hand very quickly. You have to do something.
You try hard to control the shackles to disable Dolly's ability.
But Dolly is so fast that you have to release the shackles in a hurry.
You decide to trust Dolly.
But as the figure speeds toward you, you have no choice but to change your plan and release the shackles.
Her body pauses for a moment. This isn't really a disruption.
She shakes her head and continues swinging her bat at you. To avoid her attack, you have to keep on using the shackles.
You keep trying. It's somewhat effective, but not enough to get her out of the state.

speaker: Dolly
content: Aaah... Aaah... Dodge!!
Dolly still has no control of her body, though she can now say complete words.
You shut your eyes to compose yourself and try one last time.

speaker: Dolly
content: Ah... Ah!!
Her yell is getting closer and closer, like a hurricane swooping down, about to annihilate you from the earth.
All the sounds halt.
You feel the cold metal of the baseball bat on your forehead.
You open your eyes, only to see Dolly freeze like an ice sculpture before you, panting with her mouth wide open, unable to make a sound.
As with the last mission, you get Dolly out of the state just in time. It was so close.
Your ability has more to do with this than your emotions.
You reach out and take the baseball bat stopping at your forehead back to Dolly's hands.
Baseball is Dolly's life.
You don't know how to comfort her, but you believe it's better to tell her the truth than to keep her in the dark.
Once again, you tell her the grave truth—

speaker: Dolly
content: Sob...
Upon learning the news, Dolly does not become berserk. She simply sits helplessly on the ground, like a puppet with broken strings.

speaker: Dolly
content: Then... what... what should I do?

speaker: Dolly
content: Baseball... playing baseball is the only thing I can do. If I can't play... I might as well just die.

speaker: Dolly
content: I... remember it now.
She hugs her knees and weeps uncontrollably.

speaker: Dolly
content: During the battle just now, I remembered why I... was like that.

speaker: Dolly
content: I was attacked by a Corruptor... on the way to Eastside. I desperately swung my bat to fight them when I was about to die, which was when I got this ability.

speaker: Dolly
content: Swinging the bat activates my ability.

speaker: Dolly
content: I'm just a... bat swinging machine!

speaker: Dolly
content: Haha... What a fool I was. How could I forget something so important... I even wrote a letter for myself to read three years from then... Hahaha.
Dolly sat on her knees, her eyes unfocused.

speaker: Dolly
content: I'm such an idiot who can do nothing other than swinging the bat nonstop.

speaker: Dolly
content: ...Like a robot, getting faster... and faster with each swing.

speaker: Dolly
content: Chief... You won. I can never go back to the stadium again. I'll only destroy the place with my bat.

speaker: Dolly
content: The more I swing the bat, the further I am from the stadium.

speaker: Dolly
content: Just let me... rot away like this.
She's probably exhausted from activating her ability, or maybe she just needs some time to herself.
After getting into the vehicle, Dolly curls up in the back seat and falls sound asleep before long.

speaker: Navigator
content: You have a call from "Nightingale." Please answer.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, are you still around Eastside?

speaker: Nightingale
content: Great.
Seems like Nightingale lets out a sigh of relief.

speaker: Nightingale
content: There's a Corruptor attack at the Eastside Stadium in the middle of a game, and the FAC squad can't get all the spectators out. They need our help.
Hold on, we'll be right there.

speaker: Navigator
content: Destination changed to "Eastside Stadium."
After hanging up, you shoot a glance at Dolly in the back seat, and at the baseball bat she's clutching tightly in her hands even while asleep.
Perhaps, there's still a chance.
You drive all the way to Eastside while Dolly sleep-talks on the way.
Most of them are about baseball, like "See how you catch my home run" and "Let's watch a baseball game together next time."

speaker: Dolly
content: Where... are we? I thought we were heading back to the Bureau.
How was your nap?
You pull the brakes and park the car.

speaker: Dolly
content: This is... near the Eastside Baseball Stadium? What did you bring me here for? Playing Baseball?

speaker: Dolly
content: ...You know all too well that I can't play baseball anymore.
Not baseball, of course. We're working overtime.
You open the vehicle door for Dolly. The stadium is surrounded by firefighters and busy FAC members.

speaker: Dolly
content: What... is going on here?
A Corruptor attack.

speaker: Dolly
content: Sorry, Chief. I... I can't do it here...
Dolly stares at the stage she once dreamed to be in, raising and lowering the baseball bat in her hand. Maybe she doesn't think she deserve to swing her bat here anymore.
Of course, it's totally fine if you say no. This place means a lot to you, after all.
Bang—
The Eastside stadium starts to shake violently and the outer brick wall begins to crumble as you speak.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, the Corruptors are rushing out from underground. Please act now.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Or the Eastside Stadium might collapse completely.

speaker: Dolly
content: Collapse...?
Dolly has refused the mission. Please send me another Sinner.

speaker: Dolly
content: I am joining the mission!

speaker: Dolly
content: Even if I have to use my ability here... It's better than the place being destroyed by Corruptors!

speaker: Dolly
content: I'm going to totally crush the Corruptors this time! They were the ones who caused me to be like this...

speaker: Nightingale
content: Great. Then, mission continues.

speaker: Nightingale
content: The objective of this mission: to evacuate the spectators as much as possible.
You show your ID card to the FACs around you and enter the Eastside Stadium with Dolly.
Corruptors crawl out from the ground continually. Luckily, they don't move fast.

speaker: Dolly
content: I'm already... doing it!
Dolly carries the baseball bat behind her back and punches the attacking Corruptors only with her fists.

speaker: Dolly
content: You're safe now... Go.

speaker: Spectator
content: But I paid for my ticket...

speaker: Dolly
content: Forget about the ticket! Just get the hell out of here!

speaker: Dolly
content: Or I'll kill you too.

speaker: Spectator
content: I-I... I'm going now! Gosh!
Looking at the spectators fleeing in a panic, you quietly sigh. Thankfully, Dolly is doing her best to rescue people.
Hopefully, her emotions won't get out of hand during the rescue, or it'll be big trouble.

options: Can I trust your "emotions" this time?

speaker: Dolly
content: Humph... Of course you can.
You travel all the way from the east to the west of the stadium, rescuing many who didn't manage to escape along the way.
Some thank Dolly, while others are scared away by her.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Scanning the site...

speaker: Nightingale
content: There is one sign of life remaining, 43 meters to your east, under the spectators' seats.

speaker: Nightingale
content: After rescuing this person, focus on the underground cave under the stadium center where Corruptors generated. The current earthquake level is 4.1, which suggests more Corruptors under the ground, so hurry up!
Before Nightingale can finish, Dolly lifts all the seats in front of her with her bat.
As expected, a middle-aged man is shivering underneath.

speaker: Dolly
content: Go.

speaker: Middle-Aged Spectator
content: Wh-Who... Who are you?

speaker: Dolly
content: We're here to save you. Don't be ungrateful.

speaker: Middle-Aged Spectator
content: To save me... Well, you're really lucky. If you mention my name to the Eastside Baseball Club, you'll get special privileges!

speaker: Dolly
content: Just shut up and go. I still have those Corruptors to fight.

speaker: Middle-Aged Spectator
content: Hold on... You look like... Are you...
The middle-aged man's expression changes rapidly.

speaker: Middle-Aged Spectator
content: You're the one who messed up the game two years ago! That baseball monster girl!

speaker: Middle-Aged Spectator
content: Did you know?! Did you know how much I bet on that game?!

speaker: Middle-Aged Spectator
content: Tsk. Gosh, what a bummer.

speaker: Middle-Aged Spectator
content: Damn you disgusting Syndican! Ah—Aaah!!
Dolly swings a punch straight at the man. He is knocked off the glass fence to the ground.

speaker: Middle-Aged Spectator
content: How... How dare you hit me?! I'm a member of the Eastside Baseball Club!

speaker: Dolly
content: Can I pretend I've never seen this guy?
Yes, you can. But scumbags have the right to live too.
No, you can't. But you have my permission to give him one more kick.

speaker: Middle-Aged Spectator
content: You... You're her boss, right? Help me! Help!
You look to Dolly and wait for her to decide.
Dolly lifts the man by the collar.

speaker: Middle-Aged Spectator
content: Ah... I'm telling you... I'm telling you, think twice!
With Dolly's powerful toss, the man is thrown to an emergency exit.

speaker: Dolly
content: Now you remember! You're saved by a Syndican!

speaker: Dolly
content: And it's a Syndican who's about to enter the stadium too! Got it?!
Without turning back, Dolly walks toward the center of the stadium.
The ground starts to shake even more violently, as if something is about to burst out from the ground.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief! We have an emergency!

speaker: Nightingale
content: A giant monster is coming out in the Eastside Stadium. Mission aborted. Retreat now!
You hear an extremely anxious Nightingale from the comms.
Dolly, however, walks straight toward the center of the stadium as if she hears nothing.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Dolly the Sinner! Stop going forward! Stop now!
Dolly tosses her headset to the ground and gets into a batting pose.
The ground trembles as a bizarre monster emerges from underground, rushing straight to the opponent in front of it.

speaker: Monster
content: Roarrrr—

speaker: Monster
content: What a blessing... What a blessing!

speaker: Dolly
content: Ah... How ironic.

speaker: Dolly
content: I'm on the stage of my dreams now.

speaker: Dolly
content: But doing this kind of drudge work.
The battlefield is your stadium, and the stadium right now is your battlefield.
It's just that this time, instead of spectators, you are facing a monster.

speaker: Dolly
content: Ha... You don't have to comfort me like that. I get it.
I know you won't get to play baseball anymore, but I'm here with you, to let you fulfill your dreams on the battlefield.
These monsters are your strongest and best opponents.
While I am your best coach.

speaker: Dolly
content: Gosh. You never know when to shut up, do you?

speaker: Dolly
content: I wish I had a quieter coach.

speaker: Dolly
content: Haha... Pity I don't have a choice.
Dolly's hand reaches behind her back for her baseball bat.

speaker: Dolly
content: Let's start the game, coach.
Dolly swings her bat and her ability is activated in an instant.
She leaps up high, swings her arms in full force, and smashes the bat into the monster with all her strength.
Like a moth chasing the light, the closer it gets to the light it desires, the closer it is to destruction.
But what if the moth is destruction itself?
That's probably something nobody has never experienced.
The monster lets out an ear-piercing shrill and collapses to the ground as if it has lost its shape.

speaker: Dolly
content: Mission accomplished! You did a good job this time. It's probably one of the few missions I enjoyed.
You enjoyed fighting the monster?

speaker: Dolly
content: Humph, definitely not as much as teaching that fat Eastsider a lesson.
The light that belongs to her has finally come.

speaker: Dolly
content: So why am I still being locked up here?
Because you disobeyed orders, of course.

speaker: Dolly
content: ...What? Come on!
And I am with you.

speaker: Dolly
content: But you're outside!?

options: That's my privileges as a coach.

content: Anyway, why don't you tell me about that letter you wrote to yourself in three years?

speaker: Dolly
content: Urgh... Whatever. Just stop bugging me.
Dear Dolly in three years,
By the time you are reading this letter again, I'm sure you'll be on the Eastside baseball podium, ready to accept the "Best Hitter" award.
Haha... Just kidding, of course. I've considered the possibility of not being able to win at all after getting to Eastside.
By then, I'll definitely work ten times harder than I do now, because this is my dream.
I won't be distressed even if I don't get famous in the end.
After all, I'll have proved myself. And I'll have done my best in this stadium.
Alright, I guess that's it for now.
I gotta leave early for Eastside. It's so big there, you don't wanna get lost.

2 weeks after the Black Ring incident in the Square
Office of the MBCC Chief
How are her injuries now?

speaker: Nightingale
content: Moderate concussion, open trauma, multiple fractures... The medical department tried their best, but her conditions are still worrying.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Horo can only perform simple activities at the moment. She needs at least another month to rest and heal if you want to put her into battle.
The MBCC hasn't sunk to the point of forcing injured Sinners to fight. However, I do have some things to confirm with her.

speaker: Nightingale
content: You mean...
Yes. About the Legion.
The Public Security Bureau's counter attacks these days are really unusual. They go beyond the scope of retaliation.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Indeed. They seem to be looking for something.
The Legion sent Horo here in the name of protecting wounded personnel, but it's probably not that simple.

speaker: Nightingale
content: ...I see.
Nightingale turns on her mic.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Inform the medical department to bring Horo to the interrogation room...

speaker: Nightingale
content: Yes, immediately...
Horo's body is wrapped in clean gauze. The interrogation room smells of topical antibiotics.
How are your injuries?

speaker: Horo
content: Nothing serious.

speaker: Horo
content: Your people helped me... Thank you.
Even though Horo is in poor physical and mental condition, she is still holding up to talk to you.
Horo's injuries are severe, and she needs to rest. You should get straight to the point so as not to prolong her pain.
Take it easy, Horo.
The Legion sent you here. The MBCC will keep you safe until threat is cleared.

speaker: Horo
content: I know.
Good. I have some questions. Please answer them truthfully, as they have to do with your safety and the well-being of the Legion.

speaker: Horo
content: Okay.
Horo's attitude is a bit unusual. She hasn't been so obedient in your past encounters with her.
Maybe she just doesn't have the strength to resist, or perhaps Zoya's missing and Earl's death have brought her too heavy a blow.
Whatever the reason, this interrogation shouldn't last too long.

options: When did you join the Legion?

speaker: Horo
content: Eight years ago, on April 21, Earl and I joined the Nirvana Convoy.

You cross-check the information in your hands: eight years ago, the Legion didn't exist yet. The organization that later came to terrify all the gangs was still a logistics company under the Nirvana Group back then.
What did you do there?

speaker: Horo
content: Earl worked in the docking zone at first, and I...

speaker: Horo
content: I did nothing.
You quickly jot this information down in your notebook.
Do you know of Zoya's whereabouts?

speaker: Horo
content: Boss Zoya?
Horo sounds slightly surprised, but she quickly lowers her head again.

speaker: Horo
content: ...I don't know.

speaker: Horo
content: Ever since we parted two weeks ago, I've been recuperating at a Legion stronghold.

speaker: Horo
content: I haven't seen her since then.
Your pen tip scratches across the paper. The atmosphere is extremely heavy.

speaker: Horo
content: ${PlayerName}... Chief.

speaker: Horo
content: Can you tell me...

speaker: Horo
content: How's the Legion doing now?
You hear her question, and answer her briefly as you continue to write down notes.
In the incident at the square, Zoya was in the Corpseborne process, but was forcefully stopped by Earl.
Earl became a Corpseborne in Zoya's place and died, while Zoya was seriously injured and missing.
Having lost their main combat Sinners, the Legion is now in a difficult situation.
In the face of the Public Security Bureau's counterattacks, they can only stay in fixed strongholds to defend themselves for the time being...
You lift your head to see Horo's eyes lose focus as her face turns ashen.
Horo?
Are you okay?

speaker: Horo
content: I... I'm fine...

speaker: Horo
content: I just...
Horo's breathing almost stops, making it hard for her to even utter a sound.
It takes a long time for her breath to fully recover.
Wait, are you hearing about this for the first time?

speaker: Horo
content: Okay.

speaker: Horo
content: They just said... Syndicate is totally in a mess, and that Boss Zoya and Earl are still fighting...

speaker: Horo
content: I knew it. I knew it all along... Earl is my... brother, after all.

speaker: Horo
content: I just... need some time to take it in.
Horo tries to put on a calm expression, but the emotion in her voice reveals her feelings.
Don't worry. At least no one can threaten you here.
The Legion will be fine. They're a strong bunch. You know this better than anyone else, don't you?
Your meager attempt to comfort her comes off quite bland, but Horo still forces a smile.

speaker: Horo
content: Thank you, ${PlayerName}.

speaker: Horo
content: But I'm not a child... You don't have to comfort me like that.
Horo clenches her fists, and faint red marks appear on the white gauze.

speaker: Horo
content: The Legion is in grave danger now, right?
Gazing into Horo's eyes, you let out a sigh.
Indeed. The Legion is in a really challenging situation now.
The chief culprit of the events in Keylan Square is dead, but the forces behind him have not given up.

speaker: Horo
content: Can't you stop them?
After the Black Ring broke out in the square, the FAC lost a lot of manpower, and now the rescue and cleanup efforts have overwhelmed them.
Not to mention that the Corpseborne who directly caused the Black Ring outbreak was... Earl.
The 9th Agency won't act unless they attain clear evidence, while the MBCC lacks the power to confront the Public Security Bureau and the City Council head-on.
I did promise Zoya that I would help the Legion. But as of now, what I can do is pretty limited.
However, things still have a chance to turn around.
test
test
test
test
test
test
The remnants of the Public Security Bureau have scattered across Syndicate to attack the Legion's strongholds.
It is worth noting that their goal does not appear to be taking revenge. After breaking into several Legion strongholds, they conducted thorough searches instead of continuing their attack.
They are looking for something, or rather, someone.
Your gaze falls back on Horo.
I believe they're looking for you, Horo. The Public Security Bureau is taking the risk to attack the Legion, just to find you.
Do you happen to know some information that terrifies the Public Security Bureau?
Horo lowers her head. It doesn't take long for her to think, and she gives you the answer after a quick moment.

speaker: Horo
content: A few months ago, I was caught by the Public Security Bureau.

speaker: Horo
content: I overheard them trading Mania weapons with a few people who claimed to be representing "Parma."
Do you know the identities of the persons involved or the transaction details?
Horo shakes her head.

speaker: Horo
content: Sorry.
No need to apologize.
Even in the absence of detailed evidence, this information reveals the Public Security Bureau's motives.
If confirmed to be true, it's enough to bring the 9th Agency into the case, which means that the matter can be completely resolved.
Do you have any evidence to back up your claim?
It doesn't even have to be evidence. It can be anything that narrows the scope of the investigation to identify potential participants of the Parma deal.
Please try to remember, Horo. This is very important.
This time, she spends quite a while trying to remember. The silence in the room is somewhat depressing.

speaker: Horo
content: ...Earl.

speaker: Horo
content: Earl has always been gathering intelligence on the Legion's enemies.

speaker: Horo
content: He keeps detailed records of those people. If I see the records, maybe I... I can definitely recognize them.
Nightingale.
You switch on the comms without hesitation.
Contact the Legion and ask them to send over the records Earl collected.
Actually no, it's too dangerous for the Legion to send information at this time... Make arrangements for me to go there myself.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Copy that.
After hanging up the comms, you quickly tidy up the files on your desk and prepare to leave.
The crisis the Legion faces is worsening with each passing moment.

speaker: Horo
content: You won't find it like that.
Horo's words halt you in your tracks.
Why not?

speaker: Horo
content: Earl... seldom trusts others.

speaker: Horo
content: He is very cautious, and he would hide all his important information in somewhere more secretive.
Somewhere the Legionnaires don't know?

speaker: Horo
content: Yes... I...
Horo hesitates for a while, but finally gazes up at you.

speaker: Horo
content: Let me go along with you.
But your injuries...

speaker: Horo
content: I'm fine.

speaker: Horo
content: Don't underestimate us Sinners. I'm okay with everyday movements now.
Gazing into Horo's determined eyes, you find yourself somewhat convinced.
The situation in Syndicate is complicated. There are nooks and crannies you might miss if you just do things by the book.
It would definitely be more efficient to form an elite team and sneak in with Horo as your guide.
You insist on going back because you want to see how the Legion is doing, no?
Horo lowers her head in silence without refuting your claim.
She has changed a lot since coming to the MBCC. She has become a totally different person from the brash girl she used to be.
The Legion's upheaval has dealt her a heavy blow, but perhaps it has also led to her growing up overnight.
Alright.
Follow the doctor's orders to the teeth and recover as much as possible.
There's no room for wounded stragglers on this mission.

speaker: Horo
content: Okay.
Horo nods heavily, obeying your harsh commands without complaint.
You guys wait here.
At the previous stronghold, Hella got into a quarrel with some Legionnaires. Leaving her here to stand guard is clearly the best option.

speaker: Hella
content: As if I want to go!
Hella pouts, but stays as she is told.
You and Horo walk in through the entrance. The interior of the Legion's stronghold comes into view.
As always, everything is made of steel and cement, in line with the Legion's style.
It's just that the building is a bit old.

speaker: Lenny
content: Horo? How come you're here too?

speaker: Horo
content: Lenny, what's the situation?

speaker: Lenny
content: Situation? Oh, you mean those buffoons from the Public Security Bureau.

speaker: Lenny
content: Beaten and fled. No stronghold has been attacked in the past few days. Guess they're probably scared witless.

speaker: Lenny
content: They should know better than to get in our Legion's way. Who do they think they are?
He speaks with an air of triumphant indifference, but his scar-ridden body suggests that he has bitten off more than he can chew.

speaker: Jer
content: ...Come here!
Another Legionnaire named Jer pulls you to the side.

speaker: Jer
content: Why did you bring Horo here? Aren't you supposed to be protecting her?
As you can see, I am protecting her.

speaker: Jer
content: You think you're protecting her by bringing her back to this Syndicate war zone? Have you forgotten your promise to Boss Zoya?!
Horo and I made this decision together.
We are looking for information left by Earl.
Jer's face sinks at the mention of Earl's name.
As long as we find the right records, the 9th Agency will have a reason to get involved and sweep up the remnants of the Public Security Bureau.
Horo's safety and the threats faced by the Legion will all be resolved in one go.

speaker: Jer
content: Cut the bullcrap! Aside from you, I don't trust any of those Eastside bastards!
The shouts catch Horo's attention. Jer quickly lowers his voice again.

speaker: Jer
content: Fine. At least I trust Horo. Those two kids... I watched them grow up.

speaker: Jer
content: Earl's room is 301, but he didn't leave much there. You can look for it yourself.
You enter Room 301 together. After many minutes of searching, you still find nothing of use.
...It's not here either.
Horo frowns, pondering other possible places.
We already visited all the Legion strongholds mentioned earlier. Where else could the records be hidden?

speaker: Horo
content: ...The only place left is the trailer park.

speaker: Lenny
content: The trailer park? Hasn't that been abandoned long ago?

speaker: Horo
content: After the Convoy left, Earl and I continued to live there for two years.

speaker: Horo
content: After some... misunderstandings, I never went back. But Earl still goes there from time to time.
Is it a well-hidden place?

speaker: Horo
content: Sort of. I mean, hardly anyone goes there now, since all the valuables have been looted long ago.
Great place for a secret hideout, no?
Horo nods.
No time to waste. Let's go.

speaker: Horo
content: Okay.

speaker: Jer
content: Hold on.

speaker: Horo
content: Jer?

speaker: Jer
content: You've been wandering in Syndicate for a while now. Some spies might have noticed you.

speaker: Jer
content: Lenny, Danny, Kevin, come. Let's go together.

speaker: Horo
content: What about the defense of the stronghold?

speaker: Jer
content: There hasn't been an attack for days. And it's only 20 minutes to the old trailer park from here. We shouldn't be that unlucky.

speaker: Jer
content: Plus their target is ultimately you. So I'm worried...
Jer looks to Horo with concern in his eyes.
Horo looks back at you, as if seeking your opinion.
...Let's go together then.
You sigh somewhat helplessly.

speaker: Hella
content: This is some ****ing shabby place.

speaker: Hella
content: And that stench... How can anyone live here?

speaker: Hella
content: Hey lil' bitty, now I get why you didn't come back for so long. That Earl...

speaker: Hecate
content: Hella...
Hecate hisses at Hella, who realizes she has said something she shouldn't have. She purses her lips and doesn't speak again.

speaker: Horo
content: Up ahead.
Horo doesn't seem to care. Under her guidance, the group comes to a rusty trailer.
Horo walks up to the trailer door, kicks the lower left corner, shakes the door handle roughly a few times, then pushes it hard.
The door opens with a nauseating creak.

speaker: Hella
content: That's some way to open a door...
Unlike its rusty, run-down exterior, the inside of the trailer is meticulously maintained, complete with a full kitchen set that is old but well-polished.
The succulents on the windowsill are lush and green, having obviously been watered by their owner not long ago.

speaker: Horo
content: The room is on the left.
Horo utters a reminder.
Inside the room, there is a bunk bed, as well as stacks of papers piled up around a desk.

speaker: Hella
content: ...I'm heading out. I won't be much help here anyways.
Hella pulls Hecate out of the trailer.
You, Horo, and several other team members begin to read the information in front of you.
An hour passes, and more than half of Earl's records have been filtered out. Yet you still haven't found the information you're looking for.
Horo seems a bit absent-minded all this time.
Horo.

speaker: Horo
content: Yes?
Horo's mind has wandered again.
You understand how she feels. Her brother just died, and this place is full of his memories. It would be extremely difficult to keep calm.
Let's take a break.

speaker: Horo
content: ...Okay.
Horo, realizing that she'll only slow down the progress in her current state, silently leaves the room.
You follow her.
Don't be too sad...
You think for a long time, yet you fail to find anything useful to say.

speaker: Horo
content: I told you, I'm not a child.
I understand how you feel.

speaker: Horo
content: You've also lost someone dear to you before?
You are taken aback by Horo's sudden response.
Horo's lips gently curl into a bitter smile.

speaker: Horo
content: You're just like my brother. Too clumsy to even comfort people.

speaker: Horo
content: You're lucky to have not experienced anything like this...

speaker: Horo
content: But I've experienced it, over and over again. I can remember everything so clearly...

speaker: Horo
content: After Mom and Dad left, I lived here with my brother.

speaker: Horo
content: He was our breadwinner. He would always teach the boys who bullied me a good lesson. No one in the mean streets could beat him.

speaker: Horo
content: He was really amazing.
Horo caresses the dining table, where two sets of cutlery are neatly arranged.

speaker: Horo
content: Later, he joined the Convoy. He was doing two men's work and dead tired when he came home every day.

speaker: Horo
content: I felt really bad, but I didn't know what I could do, so I just watched.

speaker: Horo
content: One day, some men from the Convoy carried him back home. He had lost a leg.

speaker: Horo
content: I was so scared that he would leave me just like Mom and Dad did.

speaker: Horo
content: The pain kept him awake all night, and I cried the whole night next to him. Yet there was still nothing I could do to help. I didn't know how to handle his wound, I couldn't comfort him, and I couldn't relieve his pain.

speaker: Horo
content: That day was when I realized I must grow up quickly to help him.

speaker: Horo
content: So I joined the Convoy too. And later, the Convoy became the Legion.

speaker: Horo
content: But the harder I tried to prove myself, the more he tried to stop me.

speaker: Horo
content: He always thought that I was just a little kid who should hide behind him, and that he should shoulder everything himself.

speaker: Horo
content: I was so mad. The madder I got, the more I argued with him. In the end, I stopped talking to him altogether.
Horo wipes her eyes with her arm.

speaker: Horo
content: ${PlayerName}, I'm so stupid.

speaker: Horo
content: He was the dearest family to me, yet I couldn't even speak properly to him.
Tears stream out from her reddened eyes. Her emotions that has been pent up for many days are finally gushing out.
After a while, her sobs slowly subside.

speaker: Horo
content: Earl is dead.

speaker: Horo
content: I can't be the little kid who hides behind him anymore.
Horo wipes away her tears and flashes a heart-wrenching smile.

speaker: Horo
content: I'm sorry, ${PlayerName}. I must be boring you with my rant.
Of course not.

speaker: Horo
content: ...I just remembered that my brother has a bad habit of hiding things.
Horo goes back into the study and pulls open the desk drawers. She pries open the bottom plates one by one, revealing a few notebooks.

speaker: Horo
content: I knew it. He used to love hiding things in these places.
Horo rummages for a while and flips open one of the notebooks. Her eyes are still a bit red, but her expression is calm and determined.

speaker: Horo
content: D'Artagnan, Bliss, Massi... I remember these names.

speaker: Horo
content: These are the people the Public Security Bureau dealt with.
You take the notebook. It contains records of the aforementioned people's dealings with the Public Security Bureau, and the destruction of Mania weapons.
As long as the locations in this file are found, it would be enough to convict those in the Public Security Bureau—but that's the 9th Agency's job.
Your work here is done.

speaker: Mission Operative
content: If Earl had given this to the Chief earlier... Things wouldn't have gotten to this.
One of the mission operatives expresses regret.

speaker: Horo
content: Regret is meaningless.

speaker: Horo
content: Plus, there was no way my brother could trust you back then.

speaker: Mission Operative
content: Then at least he should have told someone else.

speaker: Horo
content: The Legion has enough enemies as it is. It would've only added to everyone's burden.
You don't know from when, but Horo has started to think like Earl and Zoya.
After confirming the information, you send messages to the MBCC and the 9th Agency.

options: Get the team together and retreat ASAP

content: Everyone heeds your order and quickly leaves the trailer after sorting out the materials that need to be taken away.
Only Horo looks back longingly.

speaker: Horo
content: I'll be back... But for now, it's time to say goodbye...
Boom!
An explosion nearby interrupts the sentimental farewell.
After a few gunshots, Hella rushes back with Lenny.

speaker: Hella
content: Why are you still dilly-dallying here? The Public Security Bureau forces are here!
Hella pants heavily as Hecate explains the situation.

speaker: Hecate
content: There's more than a hundred of them, and they have Mania weapons.

speaker: Hecate
content: We're surrounded.
Bang!
Hella knocks an enemy to the ground with a steel water pipe.

speaker: Hella
content: Why are y'all looking so sulky? Shouldn't you be happy that I got rid of another one?
Nine minutes into the battle, one-third of the team has already been wounded.
If it weren't for the complex terrain of the trailer park, the enemy's absolute advantage in numbers would have wiped out your entire team in those few minutes.
Even so, tasked with protecting Horo and two other seriously wounded teammates, the situation is becoming worse for you.
Under the circumstances, it's almost impossible to evacuate everyone safely.

options: Stay behind to hold back the enemy

content: Hecate.

speaker: Hecate
content: Yes.
You and Team B escort Horo and the wounded westward. Avoid the spies as much as possible and take them back to the Legion's stronghold.

speaker: Hella
content: What about me?
We'll stay and feint to the east.
We'll make as big of a distraction as possible to cover their retreat.

speaker: Hella
content: Hahaha, I knew it! No one can handle a suicide mission better than the two of us!

speaker: Horo
content: No!
Horo's voice isn't all that loud, but very firm.

speaker: Hella
content: Why, you wanna stay? In this pathetic state? No thanks. I don't want no burden dragging me down when I fight!

speaker: Hella
content: Listen to the Chief now, you lil' bitty.
Hella approaches Horo with a smug look on her face. Though she calls her "lil' bitty," the two are actually around the same height.

speaker: Horo
content: No true Legionnaire ever flees without a fight.
Horo does not snap back at Hella. Instead, her calm words win the approval of the Legionnaires around her.

speaker: Horo
content: Plus, I can't watch others die for me anymore.
Feeling awkward, Hella takes a step back and mutters to herself.

speaker: Hella
content: What a poser...

speaker: Hella
content: I can protect this buddy by myself. Besides, you didn't even bring any weapons. What are you going to fight with?

speaker: Horo
content: My Sinner powers don't need weapons.
The battle mark on Horo's body starts to glow through the bandages.

speaker: Horo
content: And don't forget, this is a trailer park, and I am a daughter of the Convoy.

speaker: Horo
content: There are enough parts here for me to use.
After saying all this, both Horo and Hella look towards you.
Time is running out and a decision must be made as soon as possible.
I understand...
Then let's break through the siege together.

speaker: Hella
content: Pfft.
Hella snorts in dissatisfaction, but stops objecting. She hoists her water pipe over one shoulder.
This plan is too idealistic. Your chances of breaking through the siege are slim.
Yet by now, you notice that everyone is already clenching their weapons tightly.
The cloud of gloom and uncertainty has disappeared from their faces.
A bullet whizzes by and pierces Hella's forearm.

speaker: Hella
content: Hecate!
The Nightmare tears apart the incoming enemy, creating a space for Hella to stand.
Hella leaps forward, swinging the steel pipe in her hand.

speaker: Hella
content: Had enough fun? My turn!
Bang!
The enemies before her collapse in one swoop. The battle pauses temporarily.

speaker: Public Security Bureau Commander
content: Imbeciles! ******* losing even with ******* Mania weapons in your hands!

speaker: Public Security Bureau henchman
content: S-sir, what are we gonna do now?

speaker: Public Security Bureau Commander
content: We can't wait anymore. Their reinforcements are probably arriving.

speaker: Public Security Bureau Commander
content: Set fire and smoke them out!

speaker: Public Security Bureau henchman
content: But... but Sir...

speaker: Public Security Bureau Commander
content: Shut the **** up and do it!

speaker: Public Security Bureau Commander
content: Set the fire and we get discharged at most. But if we let them escape, we're all totally f****** damned! Do you understand?!

speaker: Public Security Bureau henchman
content: Un...understood.
Molotov cocktails strike the trailer one after another. Feeding on the piles of garbage, the fire grows bigger and bigger.
The head of the group grabs a nearby henchman's Mania weapon and aims at the only escape route.

speaker: Public Security Bureau Commander
content: The wind is in the right direction. The gods are on my side! I'm not going to lose to you **** dumba**es!
Scattered footsteps get closer and closer. The commander's face flushes with excitement, his teeth grinding in relish.

speaker: Public Security Bureau Commander
content: Prepare to die, you f***ers!

speaker: Horo
content: You're the one who's going to die.
The voice from above leaves him momentarily stunned.
A petite girl wielding a particularly large weapon stands atop the trailer.
The next instant, she leaps down and hacks the hideous Mania weapon to pieces with her ax. The man carrying the weapon is flung a few meters into the distance.
After rolling over a dozen times on the ground, the man twitches before losing consciousness.

speaker: Horo
content: Attack!
As Horo roars, all the Sinners, mission operatives, and Legionnaires surge at once to repel the now leaderless Public Security Bureau forces.
In the chaos, you grab a kneeling Horo and carry her out of the encirclement.
You sprint for a long time and finally completely rid yourselves of the enemies after you.
The raging fire exacerbated the chaos. The Public Security Bureau forces are no longer a threat.

speaker: Horo
content: What a pity... I had wanted to go back again someday.
You gasp for breath as you keep running with Horo on your back. Though she is light, you are still exhausted.
Maybe it's time to exercise more.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, the coast is clear. Please stay where you are. A convoy will pick you up soon.
It begins to rain. Gazing at the Legion stronghold nearby, you realize the time to part ways has come.
No... it's impossible! I refuse to believe that the captain would accept such an operation!

speaker: Jer
content: Lenny is seriously injured. We have to bring him back quickly and make preparations for the next round of attacks from the Public Security Bureau.

speaker: Hella
content: What's there to be scared of? They won't be around much longer.
Hearing Hella's and the Legionnaire's voices, Horo stirs on your shoulders.

speaker: Horo
content: ${PlayerName}, let me down.
Don't move around. It's gonna tear your wound even more.

speaker: Horo
content: I'm fine.

speaker: Hella
content: Fine my butt!
Horo doesn't bother to bicker with Hella, but she insists that you put her down. You finally relent.
After all, she has to say goodbye to her fellow Legionnaires. It'll be a long time until they can meet again.

speaker: Horo
content: Jer... Lenny... Danny... Kevin...

speaker: Horo
content: Black-Haired Woman

speaker: Jer
content: Thanks to you... and this Chief, we all survived.

speaker: Horo
content: When this is all over, you won't have to fight anymore.

speaker: Horo
content: After all, Syndicate's gangs are gone, so there's nothing left to conquer.

speaker: Jer
content: Yeah. All we have to do is holding on to what we have.

speaker: Jer
content: We used to be the Convoy back in the day anyways. If there aren't any gangs to fight, we can work in logistics again. We won't starve.

speaker: Horo
content: Good... I no longer want to see...
As Horo lets out a sigh of relief, her feet go limp, making her almost fall to the ground.
You grab her just in time.
Jer looks at both of you with mixed feelings in his eyes.

speaker: Jer
content: Sigh... At first, we were just carrying out Zoya's orders to protect Horo.

speaker: Jer
content: She's always a little girl in our eyes.

speaker: Jer
content: It's only natural for adults to protect kids.

speaker: Horo
content: I told you, I'm not a kid anymore.

speaker: Jer
content: You're right. You're not.
Jer's voice sounds totally sincere.

speaker: Jer
content: Zoya was right. You are the one who shall take up her torch.

speaker: Jer
content: You are fit to be the Legion's leader.

speaker: Horo
content: I'm... not really a leader.

speaker: Horo
content: Boss Zoya will come back someday. She has been and will be the only leader of the Legion.

speaker: Horo
content: However, before she returns, Chief ${PlayerName} and I won't sit idly by if the Legion runs into any trouble.

speaker: Horo
content: Right?
Horo looks toward you.
Um-hmm.

speaker: Hella
content: Quit pretending to be tough, you lil' bitty. It's really comical to throw around such big talk when you're coughing up blood, ya know?
The rumble of the convoy steadily approaches. It's time to bid farewell.
The rain gradually extinguishes the fire behind you.
On the way back, your comms device rings. A familiar name flashes on the screen.

speaker: Langley
content: Hey there, newbie. Great job this time.
Langley seems to already know everything that happened.
What do you need me to do?

speaker: Langley
content: Keep going ahead and stop at the third intersection.

speaker: Langley
content: My people will be waiting there. Give them what you found.
With that, Langley hangs up.
At the third intersection, a man in a gray hat is waiting under an umbrella.
After taking the files, he flashes a polite smile and tips his hat to you.
You guys were nearby this whole time?

speaker: 9th Agency Personnel
content: Yes.

speaker: 9th Agency Personnel
content: I know what you're trying to say, honorable Chief.

speaker: 9th Agency Personnel
content: But it's probably not the best idea for us two mere intelligence agents to battle the vicious Public Security Bureau forces.
The people from the 9th Agency are as repulsively cunning as always.

speaker: 9th Agency Personnel
content: But don't worry, the Public Security Bureau will soon cease to exist.

speaker: 9th Agency Personnel
content: As long as your Legion friends survive today, no one will threaten them anymore.
The engine rumbles, and the man waves to you.
To your other side, Horo is already fast asleep. Though she is seriously injured, a smile lingers on her face.

speaker: Horo
content: Earl...
You gently stroke Horo's forehead, wiping the tears from her eyes.
Hope she has a sweet dream.

speaker: Mess
content: You're here!
The moment you enter the interrogation room, Mess comes up to you, excitement writ large on her face.

speaker: Mess
content: I'm bored to death here. When can I leave?

speaker: Mess
content: I've got a bunch of commissions on my hands. Can I go now? I'll come back after I finish them.
Be serious, Mess.
I know what you did; I know the game you're playing.
Now, I ask questions, you answer them. Let's get this over with.

speaker: Mess
content: Hehe, interesting... Are you this serious when you are interrogating other people?

speaker: Mess
content: All right, all right, I'll be the bigger person. Ask away!

speaker: Eastside Public Security Officer
content: ...The attackers are using a bomb that releases an unknown gas when detonated. If ordinary people inhale the gas, their M-values will soar, and they will become overly excited, short-tempered, and even deranged.

speaker: Eastside Public Security Officer
content: Some victims will assault other people indiscriminately. So far, more than 100 victims have been identified...

speaker: Eastside Public Security Officer
content: We haven't been able to attain a sample of the poisonous gas. When the bombs explode, the gaseous residues will dissipate completely, even if they've been kept in an airtight container, and reasons for this are unknown.

speaker: Eastside Public Security Officer
content: The attackers are very cautious. They seem to know their way around the network of monitoring systems in Eastside. We are unable to tracking them down.
So you haven't found any useful clues at all?

speaker: Eastside Public Security Officer
content: ...Not entirely. We found this.
test
test
test
test
test
test

speaker: Mess
content: Are you saying...

speaker: Mess
content: Those worthless sheriffs think I did that, because of this empty canister with the logo of my workshop on it?
You're a suspect.

speaker: Mess
content: But I've been here with you this whole time.

speaker: Mess
content: If I was out there placing gas bombs, doesn't that mean you were in on it too?

options: You might be part of a team.

content: The weapon maker doesn't need to be present. You could totally be part of a team.

speaker: Mess
content: Oh, well done, Sherlock.
Mess' face takes on an expression of mock admiration.

speaker: Mess
content: Then what? Do you have evidence?

Unfortunately, you don't. Clues provided by the public security agency in Eastside are scarce, and the investigation conducted by the MBCC itself has failed to find anything that suggests Mess is in cahoots with someone.

speaker: Mess
content: No? Okay then... I've had enough of this. You have to let me go now.
Apparently, Mess had no intention of cooperating in the first place.
But you don't have the time to play charades with her now.
Listen, Mess... We haven't found out who the attackers are, and the lives of millions of Eastsiders are on the line.
I know you don't care about any of this. I know you don't care who might get hurt or die.
But I have to do my job. You'd better cooperate, or...
I'll have to be tougher with you, if push comes to shove.

speaker: Mess
content: Uh-huh?
Mess smiles, not intimidated by your seriousness.
It's an irritating smile.

speaker: Mess
content: Sigh... what choice do I have? I'm just a Sinner under detention. You have the shackles. You think I dare to disobey you?

speaker: Mess
content: But allow me to ask you a few questions before I answer any of yours.

speaker: Mess
content: Great, I knew you'd be generous. Here are my questions.
What would you do if I said no?

speaker: Mess
content: I'd fight you as best I can, for as long as I can.

speaker: Mess
content: I know that I'd eventually succumb to the invincible shackles, but still, I'd go all out to make your life miserable, even for a short time.

speaker: Mess
content: How's that for a plan of action?
That's not a pleasant scenario.
You don't want to waste your time engaging in a tug-of-war with her. You decide to answer her questions ASAP.
Ask your questions then.
A self-satisfied smirk curves up the corners of her mouth.

speaker: Mess
content: Great, here's the first one...

speaker: Mess
content: Is there someone in Eastside that you care about a lot?
The question catches you unawares.

speaker: Mess
content: No one, I suppose? I hear the new Chief of the MBCC is a poor soul who suffers from amnesia and has been made to step into the predecessor's shoes.

speaker: Mess
content: You've been busy putting out fires all over the place ever since you took office. Surely you haven't got around to making friends in Eastside?

speaker: Mess
content: Okay, you answered the first question, sort of. Here is my second question...

speaker: Mess
content: Are you supposed to be the one responsible for handling this gas bomb thing?

speaker: Mess
content: The answer is no, right? Your responsibility is limited to the capture of Sinners, and the handling of Black Rings. It shouldn't fall to you to take care of such a minor business.

speaker: Mess
content: Sorry, I forgot the first few questions already. Can I just answer the last one? About my works...

speaker: Mess
content: Have you ever asked yourself what's the point of all this?
Mess puts her hand on her mouth, as if to hide a smile.

speaker: Mess
content: You poor thing, being bossed around by this organization, running errands for that supervisor, day in, day out. You give it your all, you risk your life, but you don't even get a thank-you.

speaker: Mess
content: Think about it... Have they ever shown you one tiny bit of respect?

speaker: Mess
content: In their eyes, you're just a convenient tool, designed to do their dirty, taxing, and shady jobs.

speaker: Mess
content: If you really think about it, you're no different from those little darlings I made. Wait, no. The darlings I made are treasured and maintained well by their owners. Hahaha!

speaker: Mess
content: Or...
Mess leans in closer.

speaker: Mess
content: Maybe... you can show them that you're not a tool.

speaker: Mess
content: Cut open the puppeteers' hands, let them see blood... Don't you find this prospect exciting?
Mess whispers in your ear, like a demon at work.

speaker: Mess
content: Those arrogant high-ups must pay. ${PlayerName}, you're powerful, and you have Sinners that are truly loyal to you. That's reason enough...

speaker: Mess
content: Go make it happen. Stop being a puppet. And damn those idle good-for-nothings. You should be the master of the DisCity.
You're right, I should be the master of the DisCity...
When that day comes, I'll eliminate Mania and bring true peace to the city.
Mess is dumbfounded for a few moments, staring at the amusing look on your face, and then bursts into laughter.
No, I don't need that.
I only hope that Mania can be eliminated, and true peace can come to the city.
Mess is dumbfounded for a few moments, staring at your face, and then bursts into laughter.

speaker: Mess
content: Hahaha... Interesting, interesting indeed!

speaker: Mess
content: You dismissed my suggestion like it's the craziest idea in the world, even though all I did was give voice to what you desire... This is a first for me. Hahaha!

speaker: Mess
content: Hahaha! You're surrounded by su-ch a powerful force of dark malice, and you're not controlled by it. Are you really a human being? Hahaha...

options: Are you done with your questions?

speaker: Mess
content: Oh, sorry, sorry... I'm done.

speaker: Mess
content: You don't have to say anything more. I've got the answers I need.

speaker: Mess
content: Quid pro quo. Now it's my turn to answer questions.
Mess sits up straighter, wipes away the tears brought forth by the bout of laughing and gives you that sly grin of hers, a grin that kind of gets on your nerves.
Before you can say anything, she picks up the small empty canister.

speaker: Mess
content: I know what you want to ask. Let me be straight with you... I made this.

speaker: Mess
content: But I'm no partner of the attackers. Or at least I don't think the customer who commissioned me to make this thing told me what it'd be used for.

speaker: Mess
content: As for information about this customer, I don't remember any... Sorry.
It was made no more than half a year ago. You don't remember anything about the customer?

speaker: Mess
content: Do you remember who you had a meal with half a year ago?

speaker: Mess
content: Come on, I got half a dozen commissions every week. I can't remember every little detail, can I?
Are you saying that you know nothing about this deal?

speaker: Mess
content: Be patient... I'm gonna help you out.

speaker: Mess
content: I'm still waiting for you to awe me in some way, after all...
Then what other information can you give me?

speaker: Mess
content: 15th Floor, 109 Garden Avenue, Eastside. The address of my private workshop.

speaker: Mess
content: I keep my ledger there. Every commission I have taken on in the past two years is recorded in it. With this ledger...
Mess has barely finished speaking when you stand up and turn on your communications device.
Right, get a car ready, I'm going to Eastside.

speaker: Mess
content: Wait, wait, I'm coming with you.
You turn around.
You're still a suspect.

speaker: Mess
content: I hid the ledger! And the information in it is encrypted. Only I can decipher it.

speaker: Mess
content: Don't look at me like that. I always take customer privacy seriously.
Looking at your cold eyes, Mess decides to play the role of a pestering child.

speaker: Mess
content: Could you please, please take me along? There's no harm in that. I haven't been home for a long time. I really miss it. Please, please...

speaker: Mess
content: You don't want to waste time decoding the information, right? You have the shackles, so you don't have to worry about losing control over me.
Right at this moment, your communications device beeps. You've heard back from your team.
You searched it? No ledger?

speaker: Mess
content: Well, well, well. Breaking into the room of a maiden... Is this how your MBCC does things?!
You take a look at the noisy maiden before you and decide to give in to her request.
...Yes, I'm taking Mess with me. She'll help us find and decode the ledger.

speaker: Mess
content: Hooray! I'm gonna buy up all the new arrivals in the shop downstairs!

speaker: Mess
content: Er... I use the MBCC's car to bring them back, right?

speaker: Mess
content: See? I told you it wouldn't take up too much of your time. You said a few words, and it's taken care of, simple as that.
Holding a massive teddy bear under her arm, Mess fishes out a key with the other hand and unlocks the door.
Only just now, when the two of you walked past the toy store downstairs, Mess said to the person inside, "As usual, pack up all the new arrivals and send them upstairs."
Then she scooped up the teddy bear near the counter and made her way straight for the elevator.

speaker: Mess
content: Voilà! Welcome to my humble abode!
When the door opens, you are greeted with wallpaper and interior decor that exude cuteness.
