The delicate tea-things, the stuffed animals on the sofa, the anvil and hammer with cartoon stickers by the fireplace...
It is more like the living room of a teenage girl than a workshop.

speaker: Mess
content: Take a seat. I'll go look for the ledger.
I can ask my people to look for it.

speaker: Mess
content: There's too much stuff around here. They wouldn't be able to find it. You sit tight, and don't make it harder for me by messing around with my things.

speaker: Mess
content: Oh, I almost forgot... You already did.

speaker: Mess
content: By the way, there's a tin of loose tea leaves on the table; help yourself.
Mess starts searching high and low for the ledger. And you, with nothing better to do, starts appraising the decor.
You own all these stuffed animals?

speaker: Mess
content: Yes. Too many, I know... But I bought them with my own money.

speaker: Mess
content: I'm rich. I've got so many commissions that I won't be able to finish them all until next year.

speaker: Mess
content: Why do you ask?
Nothing. It's just that this doesn't look like your style.

speaker: Mess
content: Huh?!
Mess, who has been searching for the ledger with her back to you, turns her head to look at you.

speaker: Mess
content: What do you mean? Because I'm a blacksmith, a Sinner, I don't deserve to have these cute little things?
That's not what I meant.
Do you like them?
You point at the big pile of stuffed animals on the sofa.

speaker: Mess
content: I do, I very much do.

speaker: Mess
content: Don't you think it makes you feel better to look at cute stuff?
What about forging? Do you like it?

speaker: Mess
content: Yes, I do. One thing doesn't contradict the other.
No, not at all. I'm just feeling that...

speaker: Mess
content: Ah, I know what you're trying to say.

speaker: Mess
content: Weapons are for doing harm, while stuffed animals are harmless. So you can't love them both. Is this what you're thinking?

speaker: Mess
content: I'm not the one doing the harm. I just make the weapons. And I enjoy this forging process.

speaker: Mess
content: Hmm, weird... It's not here either. Where did I put it...?
You look at the little anvil near the fireplace; it has been adorably decorated, much like a kid's piano with a baking finish.
So you use this thing to forge weapons?

speaker: Mess
content: Don't be ridiculous! That's a work of art, a work of art. Use your head!

speaker: Mess
content: Forging weapons makes a lot of soot and stuff. No way I'm doing it in this lovely room. I've got common sense.
Where is your workshop then?

speaker: Mess
content: Downstairs.

speaker: Mess
content: My bedroom and my living room are here. This is where I keep my non-forging-related things.

speaker: Mess
content: No, not here either...
You wonder if you should give some advice to Mess, who has been running around like a headless chicken.

speaker: Mess
content: Uh, no, I don't think it is.

speaker: Mess
content: Oh my god, oh my god, did I actually lose it? All right then... I'll go downstairs and check.
You and Mess go downstairs and into her workshop.
The workshop is a world apart from the rooms upstairs. It is dim, dirty, and messy with a blackened ceiling, the way a traditional smithy should be.
You're making weapons in an office building. No complaints?

speaker: Mess
content: Complaints, no complaints... there's no difference. I give the management office a fat check every year; they've got my back.

speaker: Mess
content: ...Let me see where you're hiding, my little precious.
Mess drags a few heavy-looking treasure chests out into the open space.
She opens the lids. The chests are crammed with weapons of all kinds, but mainly frightening cold weapons of different sizes.
For some reason, you feel instinctively uncomfortable when you see them.
These are...?

speaker: Mess
content: Backups.

speaker: Mess
content: I make an extra copy of every weapon I'm commissioned to make. For future reference, just in case.
No, these backups can't be ordinary weapons.
The chill you've experienced when the lids were opened just now was in no way an illusion.

speaker: Mess
content: Ha! Here you are!
The ledger?

speaker: Mess
content: No, just my first works after my arrival in Eastside.
Mess withdraws a long sword from inside one of the chests. It has a hilt and scabbard that seem to be made of pure silver and are embedded with red gemstones. It looks magnificent.
But the sight of this magnificent sword turns your stomach.

speaker: Mess
content: Oh, you sense the nature of this thing.

speaker: Mess
content: Commissioned by an old man. He looked respectable, but acted like a Scrooge when it came time to pay.

speaker: Mess
content: He planned to use this weapon to take care of his rich wife, I guess...
You knew his plan, but you didn't call the police?

speaker: Mess
content: He didn't tell me what he was going to do. It's just my guess. Call the police... what good would that have done without evidence?
Did he do it then?

speaker: Mess
content: How should I know? I haven't seen him since... Look at these two babies!
Mess picks up two terrifying one-handed morning stars.

speaker: Mess
content: Made them for two scions. They wanted two identical weapons for some sort of armored combat. They acted like best buddies when they were upstairs in my living room.

speaker: Mess
content: Then they came to me in private, one after the other, and each asked me to make his weapon heavier so he could destroy his opponent in combat.

speaker: Mess
content: The Eastsiders are hypocrites. In Syndicate, if two persons fight, they fight fair and square.

speaker: Mess
content: This one wanted to take his father out, this one wanted to get back at her ex-boyfriend, this one... I don't remember what this one wanted to do, probably not something very serious.
How...

speaker: Mess
content: Don't ask me how I know. Like I told you, I make guesses.

speaker: Mess
content: Or let me put it this way... I know by looking at them.
You can read minds?

speaker: Mess
content: I'm not that good.

speaker: Mess
content: I can only see malice.

speaker: Mess
content: If you welcome malice into your heart, it will turn you into a puppet doing its bidding sooner or later. And the writing is on the wall for its victims.
Now you understand why you had that uncomfortable feeling when the chests were opened. It stemmed from the malice of the owners of the weapons, as Mess pointed out.
Upon hearing Mess' little speech, you have a feeling that the collective malice contained in the chests seems to have taken on a new life. It almost makes you retch.

speaker: Mess
content: How are you feeling? Does it feel as if your dark side is about to break through?

speaker: Mess
content: Are you gonna do something about it? Do what people in such circumstances usually do, do something malicious...

speaker: Mess
content: ...Hey, give me some reaction. I don't just bring anybody here to look at the weapons. You're my special guest...
You didn't bring me here to look for the ledger?

speaker: Mess
content: You are so naive! This workshop is run by me and me alone. I don't need a ledger.

speaker: Mess
content: I keep a copy of every piece of work. I'm sure that's good enough.
You know what your customers are going to do with the weapons, why do you still provide your services to them?!

speaker: Mess
content: You want to know why...? There are several reasons, actually.

speaker: Mess
content: First and foremost, I don't care. What they want to do with the weapons is none of my concern.

speaker: Mess
content: Second, most Eastsiders are chickens. They have evil thoughts, but they wouldn't dare to put them into action.
Any other reasons?

speaker: Mess
content: Other reasons? You wouldn't understand if I told you... but, er, I guess there's no harm in telling you.

speaker: Mess
content: I'm fighting against a terrible, terrible thing.
What is it?

speaker: Mess
content: You're a muggle. No wonder you don't know its existence.

speaker: Mess
content: This thing... it makes people do things against their will. It's the agent of all violence, the culprit for human depravity.

speaker: Mess
content: Malice among mankind is its manifestation in this world. It lays waste to whatever it comes into contact with, but it is visible to no one.

speaker: Mess
content: I couldn't do anything about it before. But then I became a Sinner, so I figured maybe I have a chance at it.

speaker: Mess
content: My plan is to collect malevolent energies, beat this thing at its own game, and even eliminate it...

speaker: Mess
content: Each piece of work here represents each of my attempts to beat it. So far, I have had no luck. I haven't built a weapon that can hurt it.

speaker: Mess
content: But that's okay. I'm making a powerful secret weapon. When it's done, I can definitely destroy this thing!
Mess is talking gibberish as if she were a lunatic. You can't get any useful information from it.
She said she doesn't have a ledger here, but she has kept a copy of every weapon she's ever made.
You said, you keep a copy of every weapon you make, right?
Find me that gas bomb, stat.

speaker: Mess
content: Okay, okay, I knew you wouldn't have the patience to hear me out. I'll find you the gas bomb.
Reluctantly, Mess starts rummaging in the chests again. A short while later, she comes up with a transparent canister with liquid in it.

speaker: Mess
content: Here you go! This is the one.
Tell me about this customer.

speaker: Mess
content: Oh, normally I don't make gas bombs for customers. I find it distasteful.

speaker: Mess
content: But this guy, he's interesting. He's one of the biggest asses among my customers, though not as big an ass as you... but big enough.

speaker: Mess
content: He...
Mess' voice trails off, and she looks at you, wearing an unpleasant smile.

speaker: Mess
content: I changed my mind. I don't want to tell you about him.
You have to. This is an order.

speaker: Mess
content: What would you do if I refused?
Mess' provocative question drives you to the end of your patience.
With the lives of millions of Eastsiders on the line, you can't afford to let this drag on any longer.
Tell me everything about this man.

speaker: Mess
content: Ahhh!

speaker: Mess
content: Cough cough... Hahaha...

speaker: Mess
content: Hahaha! Looks like you're not invincible after all... Hahaha!

speaker: Mess
content: Things have just... Hahaha... got interesting. Hahaha... You can be controlled...
Mess struggles against the power of the shackles, but fails quickly. Puffing and panting, she gives up all the information.

speaker: Mess
content: Jack... Jack Naper, son of the deputy chief of... of the Eastside Public Security Bureau, a-an infamous spoiled son.
Good, continue.
Mess' breathing is steadying.

speaker: Mess
content: He came to me half a year ago. Said he wanted a weapon that could create a lot of fun.
You take a look at the canister in your hand and go on questioning Mess.
What's this liquid? Why does it make people go crazy? Is there an antidote?

speaker: Mess
content: No antidote. I made it with his malice.

speaker: Mess
content: You remove the safety and then pull the string, and that's it. In a few minutes, the liquid will become harmless, like water.

speaker: Mess
content: Jack was happy with the product. And I haven't seen him since.
Enough.
Having attained the information you need, you turn on your communications device.
The culprit is Jack Naper, son of the deputy chief of the Eastside Public Security Bureau. Track him down immediately.
...Yes, get our people ready. We'll be right there.

speaker: Mess
content: Ah, he's attacking again tonight, isn't he?
You guessed right. Or maybe, it's not a guess at all.
You turn to face Mess, and give her an order in a cold voice.
You're coming with me to stop him.

speaker: Mess
content: Heh... do I get to say no?
That unpleasant smile of hers curves up the corners of her mouth once again.

speaker: Mission Operative
content: Chief, everything went according to plan here, and we've captured Jack Naper's four accomplices.
Great. And I've located the man himself.

speaker: Mission Operative
content: Do you need backup?
I'm good. I can handle it.

speaker: Mission Operative
content: Copy that.
You hang up. The wind is strong on the rooftop. You run your fingers through your hair and move on ahead.
Jack Naper is right there.

speaker: Jack Naper
content: The nightscape of Eastside is splendid, isn't it?
Yes, enjoy it while you can.
You'll be locked up in a dark cell soon, and you might not have another chance of enjoying this view.

speaker: Jack Naper
content: Oh, is that so?

speaker: Jack Naper
content: I say you'd better stay where you are.
Jack turns around. He is holding a rod-shaped gadget with a button on it.

speaker: Jack Naper
content: Latest remote detonator, impervious to electromagnetic interference. Cool, huh?

speaker: Jack Naper
content: Good. Now we're talking.

speaker: Jack Naper
content: Well, if it isn't Miss Mess! Thank you for your help. I've been having a blast lately.

speaker: Mess
content: You're welcome.

speaker: Jack Naper
content: I hear that the new Chief of the MBCC is a force to be reckoned with. Only a few months on the job, and the Chief has pulled off quite a few high-profile missions.

speaker: Jack Naper
content: But shouldn't you be dealing with Sinners and Mania? Where do you find the time to hang out with a law-abiding citizen like me?
Law-abiding citizen? You?

speaker: Jack Naper
content: My old man is well-respected in Eastside...

speaker: Jack Naper
content: I'm his only child. Of course I'm a law-abiding citizen.
Do you know what you're doing?

speaker: Jack Naper
content: Having fun.
Having fun?!

speaker: Jack Naper
content: You don't understand the pain of being the son of a successful man.

speaker: Jack Naper
content: My life was a bore.

speaker: Jack Naper
content: Money, luxuries, all the usual forms of entertainment had lost their appeal to me. And there wasn't much else to do.

speaker: Jack Naper
content: Sometimes I even envied those Syndican hooligans. To make things worse, Yagyu was gone; and gone was my only source of merriment, manhunt.

speaker: Mess
content: That's discrimination! I'm from Syndicate.

speaker: Jack Naper
content: Whatever. It doesn't matter where you come from. This city has long been a hopeless mess.

speaker: Jack Naper
content: Life was so boring and tiring. I was trying to make the best out of a bad situation.

speaker: Jack Naper
content: And I found my new toys.
Jack looks down at the pedestrians on the street, each the size of an ant.

speaker: Jack Naper
content: They're so weak, so naive. They think that as long as they stay in Eastside, their futures are secure. They live their lives from one day to the next in a state of numbing bliss. It makes me sick.

speaker: Jack Naper
content: That's why it's so funny to see their sad faces and hear their wailing when they are forced into a corner.

speaker: Jack Naper
content: Surely you agree with me, Miss Mess, right? Or you wouldn't have made that for me.

speaker: Mess
content: I certainly don't agree with you.

speaker: Mess
content: You're doing this for fun. Ugh! That's distasteful.
Good, since you don't approve of what he is doing, then...

options: Order Mess to stop the culprit

content: Stop him, now!
You made the weapon, and you know his plan. You must have a contingency plan; I know your style.
Nullify his weapon, or restrain him directly.
Do whatever needs to be done; just stop him before he presses the button.
Mess tilts her head and looks at you with great interest. And then she turns you down outright, punctuating each and every word of her refusal.

speaker: Mess
content: I DON'T WANT TO.

speaker: Mess
content: What makes you think that I'll be able to stop him? I'm just a blacksmith.
You're also a Sinner.

speaker: Mess
content: Do Sinners have a duty to stop others from causing harm?
No, that's my duty.
But you're my Sinner.

speaker: Mess
content: Heh...

speaker: Jack Naper
content: Hey!
As you and Mess argue, Jack feels neglected, which seems to have angered him.

speaker: Jack Naper
content: Where are your manners? You're supposed to look at the person you're talking to.

speaker: Mess
content: You talk too much.
Mess doesn't turn her head, still looking at you straight in the eyes.

speaker: Jack Naper
content: W-what did you say?

speaker: Mess
content: Shut up! Stay there and be quiet. Do not interrupt us!

speaker: Jack Naper
content: Aren't... aren't you afraid of me pressing the button? You made this. You know how powerful it is!

speaker: Mess
content: Yes, I made it, and it's just a piece of iron now.

speaker: Mess
content: Try it. See if I'm telling the truth.
Jack's face turns an ugly color. He looks at the gadget in his hand, then back at you. He can't seem to summon up the courage to press the button.

speaker: Mess
content: Hahaha! Fooled you, you little coward! I can't nullify that thing.

speaker: Mess
content: What a loser! You're useless without your father.

speaker: Mess
content: You think you can always count on your dad to bail you out, huh? Now the Chief of the MBCC has got involved; things have got nasty for you. This time, even your dad won't be able to get you out of trouble.

speaker: Mess
content: And you're too cowardly to press the button. You're using that thing as a deterrent, but the moment you press the button, you'll be arrested. Am I right?

speaker: Mess
content: ... So pathetic. Without your dear daddy protecting you, you don't even dare to step out of line.
Enough!
Jack's face is contorting out of shape. You can't let Mess provoke him further.

speaker: Mess
content: Ah, you want to join this taunting game, Chief? Or do you think I'm going too far, and you want to give him a hand?
Stop wasting time. Go stop him.

speaker: Mess
content: No can do.
An annoying smile takes up her whole face.

speaker: Mess
content: His malice is about to burst through. I'm going to make a good harvest.

speaker: Mess
content: Or... you can use your shackles to force me to stop him. Isn't this what you are good at, manipulating your Sinners?
I don't use my shackles if I can help it. But right now I don't seem to have a choice.

speaker: Mess
content: Really?
A light of joy dances in her eyes.

speaker: Mess
content: Bring it on!
Red light wrapped around her torso, she moves forward silently, one hand stretched out to Jack.

speaker: Jack Naper
content: No, no... Stop! What are you doing?!

speaker: Jack Naper
content: Ahhh!
Mess' hand reaches for Jack. A stream of dark energy pours out of his chest and gathers around Mess' fingertips.
Then Jack falls onto the floor, unconscious.
You turn on the communications device.
The culprit has been apprehended. Get a team over here and take him back, ASAP.

speaker: Mess
content: Why...
Your conversation with the response team member is disrupted by a cry uttered by Mess, who has her back to you.

speaker: Mess
content: Why, why, why, why...

speaker: Mess
content: Anger, disappointment, frustration...

speaker: Mess
content: You had such an abundance of emotions that could have been turned into malice. Why...

speaker: Mess
content: You were facing an incurable scumbag and a Sinner, and you couldn't even give me a tiny bit of malice. Why?!
Listen, Mess.
I don't know why you're so obsessed with the concept of malice. I don't know what you've gone through.
But you're my Sinner now. I'll give you time to overcome it, to shed your dark past.
But at the moment, I have a more urgent business to deal with. I must save the Eastsiders, whether or not they are manipulated by the thing you mentioned.
This is my duty.

speaker: Mess
content: Heh... I planned this for so long, I put so much energy into the plan, and all I got in return is this...

speaker: Mess
content: Doesn't it make me look like a clown?

speaker: Mess
content: Why couldn't you just be a bad person like the rest of us?
What are you talking about?
Mess' voice is a whisper, barely audible above the whistling of the wind.

speaker: Mess
content: I said...

speaker: Mess
content: I WANT YOU TO DISAPPEAR!!
A blade appears in Mess' hand out of nowhere. A dark aura runs the length of the blade, giving off a sinister vibe.
Mess raises the blade and hacks at the sky with all her strength.

speaker: Mess
content: Ahhhhhhh!!
She hacks at it again, and again, and again... The thick clouds in the sky are split open, as if by invisible air currents.
She keeps on swishing the sword until she wears herself out and falls onto the floor.
She lies there for what seems like a long time.
You hear weak sniffles.
What... On earth are you fighting against?

speaker: Mess
content: The thing...
The thing?
Mess mentioned it before, but you don't know what it really is.

speaker: Mess
content: Do you remember my dream? The dream in which we met for the first time.

speaker: Mess
content: You must have forgotten it. But not me.

speaker: Mess
content: I remember every dream I've ever had. I will never forget them.
You remember it now.

speaker: Mess
content: That's the only good dream in my memory; I'm not lying.

speaker: Mess
content: Although what happened in the dream was not real, we did beat it there.

speaker: Mess
content: But no one can beat it in the real world.

speaker: Mess
content: It took control of my dad, my mom, and everyone else I ever met...

speaker: Mess
content: I still don't understand why it doesn't take control of you. Your shackles... It's such a dark entity.

speaker: Mess
content: I might have had a chance of beating it if I had been able to take advantage of you...

speaker: Mess
content: I sometimes wonder whether it would be better if I just died.

speaker: Mess
content: That way, at least I could put an end to the tortures.
Where is it?

speaker: Mess
content: It's right there. Can't you see it?
Mess raises her limp arm and points at the sky.
It's a clear sky dotted with a moon and many stars. They give out a soft light, but nothing more.
I can't see it, Mess.

speaker: Mess
content: You can't see it? Of course you can't. Who else can see it but me?
...Maybe you can learn to trust other people. Believe in their strength to contain the malice within them, instead of leading them to destruction.
I don't know if the thing you're talking about is real or not. Either way, you now are a Sinner under the MBCC.
You can rely on me, on us. You don't have to fight on your own in this whirlpool of madness.

speaker: Mess
content: Rely on you? Don't make me laugh. You can't even see the enemy I'm fighting. Rely on you?

speaker: Mess
content: ...Maybe they're right. Maybe I'm the one who has a problem. Hahaha...

speaker: Mess
content: Maybe I'm just a lunatic... Forever fighting an enemy invisible to everyone else...

speaker: Mess
content: Hahahaha...!
You don't know how to comfort the girl before you.
She is normally cunning, vicious, and hard to figure out.
Now she looks so vulnerable. It's hard to decide which is the real her.
As you ponder, Nightingale's voice pipes up in your earphone.
Yes, it's been taken care of. The culprit has been restrained.
No, no accident, she, er, she is stable at the moment, not a danger.
You take a glance at the sightless girl on the floor.
What will become of her, I don't know. But we must help her, no matter what.

In the interrogation room, Corso sits slumped in a chair, her chin resting in her hand. She looks sideways at you when you come in. Despite her relaxed posture, the intensity of her gaze is unmistakable.
Corso is warlike. She was arrested by the sheriffs during a low-level fighting contest and then transferred to the MBCC.

The reasons given by the FAC for her arrest are "picking quarrels and provoking trouble," "disrupting public order," "compromising the fairness of the contest," and "revealing her identity as a Sinner."
You met Corso on several occasions when she was still a member of Rustfire. You don't know her well, but her unconventional behavior has made a strong impression on you.
This Sinner is fickle and unpredictable like a ticking time bomb. It's wise to be on your guard around her, even though you have put the shackles on her.

speaker: Corso
content: Ah, it's you... What am I here for? Just come right out and tell me.
It's about a disciplinary issue.
test
test
test
test
test
test
I've received a report on your performance regarding the recent field operation.

speaker: Corso
content: Oh, what does it say?

speaker: Corso
content: Does it mention how flawless my combat skills are, or how beautifully I accomplished my tasks?
Corso bursts into laughter. A realization, though an incorrect one, has come to her.

speaker: Corso
content: You brought me here, to compliment me?

speaker: Corso
content: Hahaha... You guys are discerning, I'll give you that.
Corso's unabashed self-praise renders you speechless for a moment.
Don't flatter yourself.
According to the report, you disobeyed orders and went AWOL without explanation, and this happened on multiple occasions.
This is a serious disciplinary violation for a Sinner. Explain yourself!

speaker: Corso
content: Geez, this is what I'm here for?
Corso yawns, bored again.

speaker: Corso
content: My reason for going AWOL... Well, let's just say I felt like it, all right?
Take this seriously, and answer my question!
In the heat of the moment, you smack your hand, along with the report, down on the table. You then point out the glaring section where her misconduct is listed.
You absconded to do what? Answer me!

speaker: Corso
content: Okay, okay... Good Lord, you're a real pain in the neck.
Corso picks up the report and gives it a once-over before releasing it and blowing it away.

speaker: Corso
content: Those few days I went missing, I fought in some fighting contests. I can't believe you're pestering me with this tiny-ass thing.
Fighting contests?

speaker: Corso
content: Yeah.

speaker: Corso
content: The tasks you assigned me were too easy; they were just warm-up exercises. And those obedient Sinners of yours, none of them wanted to fight me. It was killing me, the boredom.

speaker: Corso
content: So I took matters into my own hands and went looking for some action.
As Corso explains her disappearances, the accusatory tone is hard to miss, as if the MBCC had mistreated her in some way.
Your reason sounds far-fetched to me.
You call up a map of Syndicate and circle a few spots on the map.
I've put the shackles on you, so I know where you've been to.

speaker: Corso
content: I'm aware of that. I went to these places, because that's where most fighting contests are held these days.
Corso remains nonchalant. You frown.
These are some of the most dangerous places in Syndicate. If I'm not mistaken, it's in one of these places that you were arrested.

speaker: Corso
content: So what?
I want you to be honest with me.
Besides taking part in fighting contests, did you do something else after you snuck away?
Corso straightens up slightly and raises her eyebrows at you.

speaker: Corso
content: Something else? Please, enlighten me, what else could I have done? Because I don't have a clue.
test
test
test
test
test
test
test
Following the Rustfire infighting, most of its grassroots members left the organization. They're now scattered around Syndicate.
They're under the influence of Mania, so they are mentally unstable, and highly liable to mental derangement when incited. They have already caused many outbreaks of public disorder.

speaker: Corso
content: Why are you telling me this? I can't see how it has anything to do with me.
You scrutinize Corso's smiling face, but it gives nothing away.
We have reason to believe that you might have gotten in touch with some of the former Rustfire members.

speaker: Corso
content: What? You're so hilarious.
Corso guffaws, as if you've just told the funniest joke in the world.

speaker: Corso
content: Hahaha... You're not seriously thinking that I'm the one who incited them to cause trouble?

speaker: Corso
content: My "brilliant" Chief, you have been misled by your preconceptions.
Under your scathing gaze, Corso finally stops laughing and resumes talking.

speaker: Corso
content: I did work with those brainless guys occasionally when I was still a member. But I'm nothing like them.
Then how do you explain why they always showed up in the same places as you?

speaker: Corso
content: Well, these old "friends" of mine, they are drawn to things that are exciting and violent.

speaker: Corso
content: And fighting contests are exciting and violent.

speaker: Corso
content: To tell you the truth, some of them did come up to me at one time or another, but I just gave them the cold shoulder. I'd rather have a couple more fights than listen to their nonsense.
Why do I get the feeling that you don't like them very much?

speaker: Corso
content: I loathe them. Like I said, I'm nothing like them.
Then why did you join Rustfire in the first place?
Corso laughs, more loudly this time.

speaker: Corso
content: Rustfire meant nothing to me.
She shrugs, almost dramatically, her face wearing a scornful look.

speaker: Corso
content: I joined them, simply because it gave me a chance to challenge the great fighters in the organization.

speaker: Corso
content: Rustfire was just a source of entertainment for me. I couldn't care less about their game plan.

speaker: Corso
content: They talked about rejuvenating Syndicate, about protecting the downtrodden. That only made me laugh.

speaker: Corso
content: The truth is that they were just a bunch of scum. Their ego was magnified by the little power they possessed, and their judgment was clouded as a result.
Corso shakes her head, putting on a hurt expression, while her tone is dripping with contempt.

speaker: Corso
content: Intimidation, violence, robbery, looting... They were capable of anything. They were not much different from those who they vowed to take down.

speaker: Corso
content: I was sick of them, those brainless predators. So I returned to my old pastime; fighting contests are good fun.
When the subject returns to fighting contests, Corso becomes animated. She leans forward and starts speaking in an excited tone.

speaker: Corso
content: You won't believe how thrilling it is to beat one fighter after another!

speaker: Corso
content: I'm reaching the top. But there is this one fighter I haven't beaten yet. When I defeat him, I'll become the best fighter there is.

speaker: Corso
content: To tell you the truth, I snuck away to look for him, the man who stands between me and the Holy Grail.
You were looking for a man?

speaker: Corso
content: Yes. A man I have yet to defeat.
Corso pauses for a moment, then speaks again through gritted teeth.

speaker: Corso
content: I must defeat him to attain the ultimate glory in the underground arena.

speaker: Corso
content: But he looks down on me and sees our matches as a chore. Sometimes, he just disappears right before our match starts, nowhere to be seen.

speaker: Corso
content: He makes a fascinating opponent, more fascinating even than the great fighters in Rustfire. I'm taking part in every fighting contest I can find in Syndicate, because I want to find him and defeat him once and for all.
You can see the fierce determination in her eyes, and it is also clearly conveyed to you through the shackles. You know for sure that she is not lying.
That's no excuse for disciplinary violations.
You're now one of the Sinners managed by the MBCC. You're working under me; I'm responsible for you, both in terms of your behavior and your work.
I'll take your situation into consideration. In the future, I'll assign more challenging tasks to you, to satisfy your need for, um, exercise.

speaker: Corso
content: Ah, that's fantastic. I like challenging tasks. The more, the better.
Corso is elated, but her elation is curtailed by your attaching a condition, delivered in a measured tone, to the arrangement.
But at the same time, you need to agree to closer supervision.

speaker: Corso
content: Closer supervision?
Yes. Someone will stay by your side around the clock whenever you're out for a task, to make sure you won't fly the coop again.

speaker: Corso
content: ${PlayerName}... Chief, what about this?

speaker: Corso
content: You can give me as many tasks as I can manage, and I promise I'll carry them out to the best of my ability. There's really no need to have someone watch over me...
She is trying to negotiate with you, but her voice sounds somewhat threatening.

speaker: Corso
content: Look, I've completed so many tasks for you without asking for anything in return. How about you give me some of those... what do they call it, uh, yes, Sinner benefits?

speaker: Corso
content: Please don't take away my freedom. I need to be able to go around and enjoy my pastime.
Your pastime? You mean fighting contests?

speaker: Corso
content: What else could it be? Didn't I make myself clear enough?
Corso haggles on with dogged persistence. You can't help but snort with laughter.
You were very clear. Still, I can't let you run around like a wild animal. We have rules here in the MBCC. We can't break them just for someone's convenience.

speaker: Corso
content: All right then. If that's the case, how about we host a fighting contest here in the MBCC?
What?

speaker: Corso
content: Well, some of your Sinners seem like strong fighters. I challenged them to a fight before, but none was on board. Could you get them to accept my challenge?
Corso's voice is getting more excited, and her eyes are growing brighter, like those of a predator ready to pounce on its prey.

speaker: Corso
content: Or maybe you can be my opponent. What do you say? I've been wondering about that curious ability of yours, the one you use to restrain me.
She leans even closer. And you lean back to keep a comfortable distance between you.
I can answer your questions now...
My answers are... no and no.

speaker: Corso
content: Why?
Corso, I respect your inclinations and needs, and I'm trying my best to accommodate them.
You can't be a lone wolf, that's the bottom line. If you keep pushing it, you won't get any preferential treatment from me.
And you won't be allowed to go on field operations anymore.
In the face of your tough stand, the playful smile Corso has been wearing like a mask starts to dissolve. She stares at you with a frown on her face, and you stare back.

speaker: Corso
content: All right, all right, I'll take the deal.
Corso reclines back on the chair, nonchalant again.

speaker: Corso
content: Whatever you say, boss. Just don't forget your promise. More challenging tasks for me.
Corso has finally agreed to your terms. You breathe a sigh of relief, hoping that this energetic Sinner won't stir more things up anytime soon.
Your terminal vibrates. You answer it, and EMP's voice comes through, hot and bothered.

speaker: EMP
content: It's me, Chief. Corso, that rotten thing, sh-sh-she's pulled one over on me, again!
EMP grumbles on. Only after a while do you straighten out what she's complaining about: Corso has gone AWOL again.

Earlier today, you assigned EMP to keep a close eye on Corso. During the mission, Corso went to the bathroom. But it's a ruse. She put her shoes on the bathroom floor to trick EMP and escaped through the vent. She hasn't been seen since.
You pacify EMP, who fell victim to Corso's deception and waited outside the bathroom stall for a long time. The phone call ends, and you hand the terminal to Nightingale.

speaker: Nightingale
content: What do we do now, Chief?
I have an idea where she might be. I'll bring her back before she causes bigger troubles.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Do we need to get the guards and the FAC involved?
Ask them to stand by and wait for my message. The place I'm going is chaotic; if there are too many of us there, it might put them on alert. I'll make contact if I need help.

speaker: Nightingale
content: All right. Be careful out there.

Guided by the shackles, you come to a topsy-turvy region of Syndicate where the signal linked to Corso is strongest. You turn into a well-concealed alley, and suddenly, it feels as though you have entered the lion's den.
The alley is teeming with hooligans, whose faces are glowing with excitement and whose hands are holding colorful pieces of paper.

speaker: Hooligan A
content: Yo, you've got the ticket too.

speaker: Hooligan B
content: I sure do. A fighting contest in the old arena... Wouldn't miss it for the world.
The word arena rings a bell. Corso mentioned it during the interrogation. You creep closer, listening in on them.

speaker: Hooligan A
content: It was shut down after the Legion destroyed all the other gangs. Glad it's opening again. The fights were so damn exciting there.

speaker: Hooligan B
content: Agreed. Those low-level fights are like catfights, boring as ****.

speaker: Hooligan B
content: I heard the host who bought the land has invited all the old fighters back.

speaker: Hooligan A
content: Yeah, I'm here for Angus, the best fighter in the arena.

speaker: Hooligan B
content: Hehe, I sure as hell want to watch Corso fight. She's not on the list, unfortunately.

speaker: Hooligan A
content: Mad Dog? I didn't know you were into that kind of stuff.

speaker: Hooligan B
content: Do you ever get a little tired of watching two big dudes throwing punches at each other?

speaker: Hooligan A
content: Better than watching Mad Dog, no doubt about it. A dirty player, she is. And in Syndicate, physical strength rules the day.

speaker: Hooligan B
content: Seriously? You have no taste. Let me tell you: nothing is more exciting than an unexpected winning counterattack.

speaker: Hooligan A
content: Unexpected counterattack? Sneak attack, more like. Without those little tricks, that tiny little thing wouldn't stand a chance of winning even one game.

speaker: Hooligan A
content: Hold on a second, isn't there some unfinished business between them? Angus is back in the game. Where is Mad Dog?

speaker: Hooligan A
content: Too afraid to show her face, I'd say. Hahaha...
You had no idea Corso was so well-known. You're contemplating a way to approach the hooligans as you listen to their argument.
Hi, bros... I overheard you talking about the contest. You must be familiar with this area.
First time in the hood. Kind of lost. Would you mind telling me where the entrance is?
You try to recall how Hella and EMP talk, and mimic them while talking to the hooligans.

speaker: Hooligan A
content: Lost?
They look at you with suspicion.

speaker: Hooligan B
content: You don't know the way? Never seen you before... Who are you?

speaker: Hooligan A
content: Hang on a second, this event is not open to the public. It's by invitation only. Who invited you?
My friend. We, um, got separated.
You look around, as if hoping to see your made-up friend. They press on.

speaker: Hooligan B
content: Show us your ticket.
I don't have it with me. My friend is holding it for me.

speaker: Hooligan A
content: Are you a tiger or a pig?
Excuse me?

speaker: Hooligan A
content: This is a cop all right.

speaker: Hooligans A & B
content: Hey, guys, we've got a pig here.
I am not...
Yo, what's going on here?
When the tension is about to boil over, a familiar voice cuts through the air. You feel a hand on your shoulder, and its owner quickly stands in front of you.

speaker: Corso
content: Cop? Where? I can't see any cop around here. My friend here, he's a bit on the timid side. Please don't scare him, okay?
female_content: Cop? Where? I can't see any cop around here. My friend here, she's a bit on the timid side. Please don't scare her, okay?

speaker: Hooligan A
content: M-mad Dog...

speaker: Hooligan B
content: Mad... Corso, this person is with you?

speaker: Corso
content: Uh-huh. Do you have a problem with that?

speaker: Corso
content: You took care of my friend while I was not around.

speaker: Corso
content: As a thank-you from him, I think I should take care of you now.
female_content: As a thank-you from her, I think I should take care of you now.

content: Corso brandishes her nail-studded wooden plank, and grins at the hooligans, exposing her pointed canine teeth.

speaker: Hooligan B
content: It's just a misunderstanding, that's all. I was too stupid to see that your friend is one of us.

speaker: Corso
content: Okay, let's chalk that one up to a misunderstanding. But I also heard someone saying I'm afraid of Angus. That can't be a misunderstanding, can it?

speaker: Hooligan B
content: It's him. He said it.

speaker: Hooligan A
content: You ******* idiot! I... I didn't mean what I said earlier...

speaker: Corso
content: Angus and I do have some unfinished business.

speaker: Corso
content: I'm here to take care of it. Now get lost!
Relieved to have escaped punishment, the hooligans run as fast as their legs can carry them.
The sorry sight elicits a snort from Corso. She then drapes her arm around your shoulders and steers you in the direction where the crowd is gathered.

speaker: Corso
content: I didn't expect to see you here, ${PlayerName}. You've come to watch the matches too?
Don't play dumb with me. You know why I'm here.
Not wanting to see a repeat of the cop incident, you decide not to shrug her arm off. You wear a smile and ask a question through gritted teeth.
Angus... that's the man you're looking for, right?

speaker: Corso
content: Exactly. Aren't you bright!

speaker: Corso
content: Let's go meet the man.

Her arm still draped around your shoulders, Corso guides you through the crowd. Presently, the two of you arrive at a guarded entrance. Upon realizing it's Corso, the guard steps aside and lets you come through.
On the other side of the entrance is a narrow flight of steps that leads underground. As you descend, your surroundings grow gloomier, and a sense of uneasiness sets in.
Finally, Corso stops in front of what looks like a wall at first glance. But it's not a wall, but a masterfully-camouflaged door.

speaker: Corso
content: My friend, I present to you... the most exhilarating, electrifying form of traditional underground entertainment in all of Syndicate!
She gives you a mischievous grin. The moment the door opens, she gives you a gentle push, and you stumble inside.
All your senses come under assault. The blinding light, the deafening shrieks, the crowd's restlessness... they come at you all at once.

speaker: Corso
content: Welcome to the old underground arena, a fighter's paradise.

speaker: Corso
content: Nice place, huh?
I'd very much like to find out the M-values of these people.
You're knocked off balance by the hullabaloo. You wish to get away from the fanatics.

But that's not happening. Corso grabs your arm and, pulling you behind her, squeezes through the crowd. The two of you come to the front of the grandstand, where the light is the brightest and the noise the loudest.

speaker: Corso
content: There's nothing to worry about. A fighting contest is supposed to be noisy and chaotic. Since you're already here, why don't you get into the spirit of things?
Standing at the rail beside Corso, you have a good view of the goings-on below.
You now understand why the crowd is being hysterical. The fight in the arena is reaching a crescendo.

<size=31>A man who is built like a tank knocks his opponent to the floor as if he's a sack of potatoes. The poor soul on the floor is struggling to stand up, but before he can do so, the giant puts a merciless foot on the back of his head; he gives up the struggle and lies still.</size>
The referee crouches down beside the motionless man. Having ascertained that he won't be able to get up, the referee stands up, grabs the giant's arm, and raises it high.
The spectators shriek with excitement, each of them a witness to the winner's moment of glory. The hysteria is so contagious that your heart starts pounding, and your blood pulsing.

speaker: Corso
content: See that guy? That's Angus.
The winner, proud like a king bathed in glory, runs his eyes slowly over the crowd. But his face falls when Corso enters his line of sight.
Angus makes a thumbs-down gesture at Corso, and then runs his thumb over his throat while sticking out his tongue. Corso answers the provocative gesture by baring her teeth.

speaker: Angus
content: Didn't expect to see you here, Mad Dog. Come down here. Let's fight it out.

speaker: Angus
content: I wouldn't have noticed you if you weren't standing that high up. You know how tiny you are, right? Hahaha...

speaker: Corso
content: It's been a while since I last saw you fight. Your fighting style hasn't changed a bit, still boring as hell.

speaker: Angus
content: Ah, not every fighter is like you, you cunning little thing.

speaker: Angus
content: Your dirty little tricks are nothing compared to absolute physical strength.
A sneer clings to her lips as Corso listens to Angus's provocative diatribe.

speaker: Corso
content: My little tricks have helped me beat all the powerful fighters except you.

speaker: Angus
content: That's because you're a ******* dirty fighter! Let me tell you something: Your little tricks might have worked on them, but they'll never work on me.

speaker: Angus
content: As long as I'm here, you'll never become the No.1 fighter.

speaker: Angus
content: That title only belongs to someone with absolute physical strength.

speaker: Corso
content: Bravo! And let me tell you something: I'm gonna defeat you today.
A crazed brightness has crept into Corso's eyes.

speaker: Corso
content: I'm gonna dethrone you and claim the throne for myself.

speaker: Corso
content: Then simple-minded brutes like you will kneel before me begging for mercy.

speaker: Angus
content: Come down here, and show me what you got.
The gauntlet has been thrown down, and it has been picked up.
The shackles vibrate strongly. You realize that Angus's scornful remarks are dried wood to the fire that's burning inside Corso.
There is no mistaking Corso's burning desire for victory, victory over her archenemy. Nothing will quench her raging fire until he's groveling at her feet.
With the fight pending, Corso turns around and leaves the grandstand without a backward glance. You follow her to a deserted corner.

speaker: Corso
content: You're not thinking about tying me up and carrying me back to the MBCC, are you?
No. You can have this fight.

speaker: Corso
content: Really? Why are you being so understanding all of a sudden? Carrot and stick, is this how the MBCC rolls? Is this some sort of charity?
This is not charity, and I'm not pitying you. It's just that I know some people were born to be great fighters. They all need a once-in-a-lifetime win to prove their worth to themselves.
And if someone takes that chance away from them, they will never trust this someone again.

speaker: Corso
content: Hahaha... Who knows, you might make a better "dog trainer" than me.
I have two conditions, though.

speaker: Corso
content: Fire away.
You must return to the MBCC with me after the fight, whatever the result. That's the first condition.

speaker: Corso
content: Will do.
The second one... I need to put a restraint on you through the shackles.
The restraint is You can't battle with anyone other than Angus. And it won't be lifted until you've turned to the MBCC with me.
You must agree to this condition if you want to fight Angus. You can't blame me for taking the precaution, considering you lied to me before.
Corso's face slightly contorts. Then slowly, she opens her arms, as if resigning herself to further control by you.

speaker: Corso
content: It doesn't feel any different.
You can try...
Before you can finish the sentence, a rush of air comes at your face. Corso's blue-veined fist is inches away from your nose.

speaker: Corso
content: Well, looks like this shackles thing is working.
I didn't ask you to try it on me.

speaker: Corso
content: Don't get angry. When I get bitten by a dog while I'm training it, I never blame it; I blame myself for failing to keep it on a stronger leash.

speaker: Corso
content: ${PlayerName}, you should be happy that your leash is working well, and you should pray that it will always work well, or...
Her voice trails off. She then gives an evil smile.
You let me worry about that. You should go get ready for the fight. And I hope you will win.

speaker: Corso
content: Ah, I will win, I definitely will.
Clutching the ticket Corso gave you, you find your seat in the front row. In the fighting area below, Corso and Angus are facing each other, waiting for the fight to begin.

speaker: Angus
content: Remember all those times when I kicked your ass in this very arena? It makes my heart sing just thinking about it. Hahaha...
Angus looks down at Corso, contempt writ large on his face.

speaker: Angus
content: I'm gonna show you what a true Syndican fighter is like.

speaker: Corso
content: Yeah, yeah, whatever.
Corso picks her ears with her finger, looking bored. When she's done with that, she starts flexing her wrists.

speaker: Corso
content: Jabber, jabber, jabber... Talk all you want while you still can.

speaker: Angus
content: What did you say?
The referee announces the commencement of the match. Angus comes at Corso with his poleaxe raised.

Corso makes a pretense of deflecting the coming blow and jumps out of the way at the last second. The momentum carries Angus forward, and with a loud clank, his poleaxe smashes into the floor, which cracks.
Frustrated and furious, Angus picks up the poleaxe, ready to mount another attack. But before he can straighten all the way up, Corso sneaks up on him and hits his head with a wooden plank.

speaker: Angus
content: Ow!!!

speaker: Corso
content: Hey, what's wrong with your back, you bent old man?

speaker: Angus
content: Ahhhhhh...
Driven over the edge, Angus grabs behind him, catches hold of Corso, and sends her flying. He is the current No.1 fighter, not someone to trifle with.
At first, neither fighter seems to have the upper hand. But as the match progresses, Angus shows signs of fatigue. Corso's dexterity and sneak attacks are proving too much for him to handle.

speaker: Angus
content: You sly little monkey, stop running and fight me, if you dare!

speaker: Corso
content: Tired already, huh? How about I let you catch your breath for a minute?
With that, Corso comes to a halt, and stands on the spot with her arms folded in front of her.

speaker: Angus
content: You, you, you... you little ****!!

Howling, Angus throws himself at Corso. When he is about to reach her, Corso leaps into the air, and jumps over Angus using his shoulders as a springboard. She hits his head again with the glue-covered plank.

speaker: Angus
content: My hair! My hair!

speaker: Angus
content: What the **** did you put on the goddamn plank?!
The plank is glued to Angus's hair. Corso pulls at it, twisting Angus's face out of shape. He is in so much pain that he drops his weapon.

speaker: Corso
content: Oops, sorry. That's glue. I didn't clean it up properly.
Corso smiles widely, not loosening her grip on the plank.
Corso throws Angus to the floor and presses a knee hard against one of his weak spots. Angus, hair glued to a wooden plank and lying pinned to the floor, has never felt so humiliated.

speaker: Corso
content: Are you gonna admit defeat or what, tough guy?
Angus's eyes are wide and red; his chest is rising and falling rapidly. Unexpectedly, he grabs something hidden behind the small of his back and throws them at Corso.

speaker: Angus
content: Not in a million years!
The flying knives catch the light, gleaming maliciously. Corso had sensed that something was amiss, and had jumped out of the way, but one of the knives still grazed her cheek.

speaker: Corso
content: Knives?
Corso touches the cut and bursts out laughing.

speaker: Corso
content: Hahaha... Angus, I didn't know you played dirty too.

speaker: Corso
content: You were all high and mighty a moment ago. You should take a look at yourself now. Can't believe you had the gall to call me a dirty fighter.

speaker: Angus
content: I can't lose, you piece of crap!
Angus brushes his ragged hair back with his hand, and realizing what has happened to his hair, he starts raving and stamping.

speaker: Angus
content: I'm the No.1 fighter. Whatever way I choose to fight, I'll still be a ******* better fighter than you!

speaker: Angus
content: Who do you think you are, you skinny little thing? I can crush you like a bug. How dare you question my strength, you piece of ****?

speaker: Corso
content: You're babbling. Hahaha...
Corso laughs harder. She sticks out her tongue, an open act of provocation.

speaker: Corso
content: You were done for, the moment you threw those knives at me.

speaker: Corso
content: Because by doing that, you admitted that you can't defeat me with physical strength alone.

speaker: Angus
content: Shut up! I've crushed you many times over. You, on the other hand, have never won a match against me.

speaker: Angus
content: You little **** used to be a punchbag in this arena, a sitting duck, fair game for everybody! Just because you can win a game or two now, doesn't mean your little tricks can win you our respect. Wake up!

speaker: Angus
content: I'm gonna beat you at your own game. I'm gonna make mincemeat of you.
In the face of this new round of taunting from Angus, Corso gives as good as she takes.

speaker: Corso
content: You're so full of crap. That tiny brain of yours, you could have ten more, and you still wouldn't be able to come up with one useful trick to "crush" me, as you put it.

speaker: Corso
content: As someone with more experience in this area, I don't mind teaching you a thing or two, so that you'll know how much inferior you are to a... weapons master!
A clanking exchange of throwing weapons ensures.
Just as Corso predicted, Angus, who is less resourceful when it comes to playing tricks, soon has a hard time keeping up with Corso.
By comparison, Corso deflects each oncoming weapon with ease. She already has the match in the bag, you're confident.

speaker: Audience
content: Corso! Corso! Corso!
The crowd cheers Corso and chants her name. Listening to the hysterical shouting, you finally understand why so many fighters are obsessed with their pursuit of victory.
If it's a thrilling experience to simply watch from afar as a spectator, it must be an intoxicating one to be actually in the heat of it as a winner.

speaker: Corso
content: A hoarder, aren't you? Come on, show me everything you've got!

speaker: Angus
content: I'll show you all right!
Angus looks daggers at Corso. Huffing and puffing, he smashes his poleaxe down on the floor three times.
The back door swings open. A group of fighters armed to the teeth streams out. They surround Corso.

speaker: Corso
content: Angus, you called in backup? This is against the rules.

speaker: Angus
content: Against the rules? I don't think so. They're just... my weapons.

speaker: Angus
content: I'm not breaking any rules here. You can ask the referee, if you like.
Angus looks confident, convinced that he is in the right. The referee nods assent and lets the fight continue.
The crowd watches this dramatic turn of events unfold and starts talking among themselves. A short moment later, the crowd erupts.

speaker: Angus
content: See? They all agree with me.

speaker: Angus
content: Everybody, are you ready to extend "hospitality" to our old friend Mad Dog?
Angus raises his hand and brings it down, and the fighters, each wearing a menacing grin, close in on Corso. You then hear the two spectators next to you talk in astonishment.

speaker: Spectator A
content: I can't believe that Angus has brought all the old fighters here to help him!

speaker: Spectator B
content: He sure has. This is gonna be good!
Corso knows she is in a bind, but she keeps her cool, even smiling at her enemies.

speaker: Corso
content: Old friends, I see. What brings you here? Want to get your asses kicked again?
One of the fighters produces a thick iron chain, clanking in his hands. He is attempting to wrap it around Corso's neck.

speaker: Fighter A
content: You're a nobody. You're not a real fighter, just some errand girl from a weapons factory.
Another of the fighters comes closer. He is attempting to tackle Corso to the floor from the side.

speaker: Fighter B
content: I'm gonna send you flying!
Corso quickly ducks out of the way, and the two fighters smash into each other.

speaker: Corso
content: Oh my, you guys are as dumb as ever.
The fighters keep up their onslaught on Corso, employing a wide variety of weapons.

speaker: Fighter C
content: Stop throwing those spiked balls willy-nilly, you dumbass. We're running low!

speaker: Fighter D
content: She's coming your way. Use the Molotov cocktails, quick!

speaker: Corso
content: Hahaha, idiots... Even sloths are more agile than you.
Corso moves around swiftly, dodging attacks with ease, and remains mostly unharmed. So far, she hasn't mounted a single counterattack.

speaker: Angus
content: Morons, can't you see she's making a fool of you? There are many of you, and there is only one of her. Hasn't it occurred to you to corner her?
You're getting anxious, for you know that Corso is not counter-attacking, not because she is toying with her enemies, but because of the restraint you've put on her through the shackles.

speaker: Fighter B
content: Ahhhhhh...
One of the fighters produces a Mania weapon from God knows where and opens fire on Corso.
The others follow suit. They form a tighter and tighter circle around Corso. This is not a fighting contest anymore, but a hunt.
The situation is spinning out of control. It's more than you can handle alone, so you contact the FAC for backup. Now you and Corso have to tough it out until help arrives.

speaker: Angus
content: Nowhere to run, I see.
Corso is concerned, her back against the wall. Angus is standing behind his lackeys, mocking her.

speaker: Angus
content: You and I go back a long way, Corso. I don't want to make this ugly.

speaker: Angus
content: I'll cut you a deal. You go down on your knees and beg for mercy, and I'll ask them to spare you. What do you think? I'm doing this out of the kindness of my heart. Hahaha...
Corso laughs out loud. There's a fierce look in her eyes now. She stops laughing and spits on the floor.

speaker: Corso
content: Over my dead body! I'll never admit defeat, ever!

speaker: Angus
content: Then you leave me no choice. Take her down!

speaker: Audience
content: Angus! Angus! Angus!
The crowd, who was chanting Corso's name only a minute ago, is now chanting Angus's name.
You feel an overwhelming urge to help Corso. You don't want to see the victory that's rightly hers snatched from her.
You jump over the rail of the grandstand and land between Corso and her enemies.

speaker: Angus
content: Who the **** are you? Get the hell out of here. Don't meddle in what doesn't concern you.
I beg to differ. It does concern me.
You stand up, dust yourself down, and walk over to stand beside Corso. Matter-of-factly, you start explaining.
Like your men here, I'm also a weapon, Corso's weapon.

speaker: Angus
content: You, a weapon?
Angus looks you up and down.

speaker: Angus
content: You're all skin and bones. You wouldn't make a half-decent side dish. Get your ass out of here! Or you'll get a good beating too.
Corso tilts her head to the side and looks at you in puzzlement.

speaker: Corso
content: ${PlayerName}, you're gonna give orders again, aren't you?
You want to win, right, Corso?

speaker: Corso
content: Isn't that obvious?
Good.
You nod and put your hand on her shoulder.
Here is my order: Do Not Lose!
Beams of red light burst out from your palm. In your mind's eye, you see a vicious, teeth-baring dog being unleashed.

speaker: Angus
content: W-what kind of weapon is that? A new type of flash bang? Stop your stupid gimmick!

speaker: Corso
content: Hahahaha!
Corso starts laughing heartily. She steps forward to stand in front of you, and points the business end of her nail-studded plank at Angus's head.

speaker: Corso
content: Great. I like it. I like this new order very much!

speaker: Corso
content: I'm gonna win this. Just wait and see!
Slowly, Corso moves forward. The fighters, intimidated by her overpowering aura, step backward.

speaker: Angus
content: What are you afraid of? It's just her and a burden. Don't be a bunch of chickens!
The fighters come charging at Corso, howling. She is unfazed and even bends forward to pick up a few pieces of scrape from the floor.

speaker: Corso
content: Tsk tsk, what a waste! Good raw materials, but the craftsmanship leaves much to be desired.

speaker: Corso
content: Um, I guess I'll have to make the best of it. Use the trash to take out this bunch of trash... that's an idea.
Corso scoops up a couple of round stones with her plank and sends them flying. They penetrate the kneecaps of the fighter at the front.

speaker: Fighter A
content: Ahhhhhhhhhh!!!

Then she picks up the iron chain from the floor and flings it. It wraps itself around the ankles of one of the fighters and those of another, and the momentum sends them flying through the air for a long distance.

speaker: Fighter B&C
content: Ahhhhhh!!
A few other fighters come near Corso, but before they can lay a finger on her, they are flung to the floor, where they convulse and pass out.
The rest of the fighters are too afraid to charge now. They start shooting at her with their Mania weapons, and Corso has to block the volley of shots.
Right at this moment, Angus comes howling out of nowhere, his poleaxe raised, and makes to hack at Corso.
Clank, clank, clank... The sound of steel on steel ends with a dull thud of something heavy hitting the floor.
Angus takes an astonished look at his poleaxe without its head and falls onto the floor.

speaker: Angus
content: W-what are you?
Corso gets a small cramp in the hand from holding the nail-studded plank too tightly. She pays no heed to it, only sneers at Angus. The floor is strewed with the carcasses of weapons.
Weapon in hand, she advances on Angus, who scrambles backward. His face now contorts with fear, devoid of arrogance and haughtiness.
For all he knows, Corso could be a wily demon disguised as a skinny girl who is ready to show her true colors and tear him into ribbons.

speaker: Angus
content: Stop! Don't get any closer!!
He wraps his arms around his head, anticipating a deadly onslaught. But to his surprise, he only receives a couple of kicks here and there.

speaker: Corso
content: Argh, I didn't know you were such a wuss.

speaker: Corso
content: Hey, are you listening?

speaker: Angus
content: Huh?

speaker: Corso
content: Are you gonna admit defeat or not?
Angus nods his head so rapidly.

speaker: Angus
content: Yes, yes... You won. I lost!

speaker: Corso
content: Say it. Say I'm the ultimate winner in this arena!

speaker: Angus
content: Y-you are the ultimate winner in this arena!
The crowd erupts, applauding and cheering the new Queen of the Arena. The winner does not address the crowd; instead, she waves at you and runs toward you with a proud look on her face.

speaker: Corso
content: Hey, ${PlayerName}, did you hear that? I won!
I did. Congratulations, Queen of the Arena.
The FAC has arrived at the scene to sort out the mess. You leave with the Sinner, heading back to the MBCC.
Corso obediently follows you into the vehicle. Once inside, she keeps a steady gaze on you. The gaze is not malicious, but it makes you uncomfortable nonetheless.

speaker: Corso
content: ${PlayerName}, what made you lift the restraint on me? What changed your mind?

speaker: Corso
content: Wouldn't it be easier for you to bring me back to the MBCC if I had been beaten half to death?
You breathe a sigh of relief now that she's started talking, instead of staring at you.
I'm not some sadistic warden. I don't find locking people up particularly enjoyable.
Besides, I bet on you to win the fight.

speaker: Corso
content: Ah, you won the bet. I won!
But I don't think beating people like Angus is much of a challenge for you.

speaker: Corso
content: Then what is?
Helping the MBCC solve the Mania crisis. It's much more exciting than beating up those fighters. Wouldn't you agree?
Now that you've conquered the arena, I dare you to fight the Mania crisis alongside the MBCC.
Corso's eyes brighten up as she listens to you. She's happy with what you've just suggested.

speaker: Corso
content: Hahaha... I don't scare easily, as you must have known. Fighting the Mania crisis sounds like a good idea.

speaker: Corso
content: If I've got to stay somewhere, I might as well stay by your side.

speaker: Corso
content: I can help you with my power and bring you victory, just like what I did today.

speaker: Corso
content: But you must not forget what you promised me. Assign me the most dangerous, exciting tasks.

speaker: Corso
content: If you go back on your word, you'll be bitten by the most vicious dog.
I won't disappoint you. You have my word.

speaker: Corso
content: Okay. I hope you're as good as your word.

speaker: Reporter
content: Hey there, dear viewers! Coming to you live from the heart of the Public Security Bureau, we've got the latest scoop on the jaw-dropping case that's rocked Eastside—How the High-Profile Heist Hits Business Tycoon's Antique Vault.

speaker: Reporter
content: Sheriff, good to see you. Do we have any solid leads on this case? Any suspects in the crosshairs...?

speaker: Sheriff
content: Um...
Ding—
The video feed featuring the Sheriff's awkward pause is abruptly cut off by a pop-up alert on the screen.

Emergency Alert:
Red Alert! Code Red! I've got something mega, ultra, life-or-death important that I need to talk to you about ASAP!
—Christina

speaker: Christina
content: You made it, finally! I've been on pins and needles waiting for you!
As soon as you walk into the interrogation room, Christina practically leaps out of her seat and bolts over to you.
She yanks your arm and hauls you in front of a desk at the center of the room. The once-spotless desk is now a landscape of paper mountains, a mess of documents and files.
Is this...?

speaker: Christina
content: Got the case files from the Public Security Bureau, and you bet I've combed through every last one. Sorted them by how crucial, pressing, and sketchy they are.

speaker: Christina
content: Yep, knew they'd be lost without me. A few months out, and the place is swamped with unsolved mysteries.

speaker: Christina
content: But hey, as Eastside's numero uno detective and the go-to lifesaver for my coworkers, it's on me to untangle these knotty puzzles they can't crack!
So you've been cooped up in your room all this while, just to focus on this?
You inquire, putting on a shocked face.

speaker: Christina
content: Are you kidding me? You're seriously underestimating my game. Knocked this out in a week, easy! Before that, I was digging into...
She halts mid-sentence, catching your eye as if she's just spilled the beans. She bites her lip, clearly irritated, and says stiffly:

speaker: Christina
content: Just some ancient history, no big deal.

You're well aware of what those "ancient histories" she's avoiding talking about really are. Even since landing at MBCC, Christina hasn't been able to shake off her hang-ups about Shalom. She's been on a mission to dig up the dirt on that elusive Hush.
The case files strewn across the desk are actually a diversion, a strategy you've implemented by quietly liaising with the Public Security Bureau.
You making any headway on that old skeleton in your closet?
You inquire with great caution. Christina displays a faint sneer, softly murmuring.

speaker: Christina
content: Yeah, right. If only digging up dirt on someone was a walk in the park...
Christina, I'm here for you if you ever need someone to talk to or a helping hand.

speaker: Christina
content: I get it, isn't that why I'm here in the first place?
She casts a meaningful glance at the disordered heap of case files strewn across her desk. She is clearly trying to change the topic.
Perhaps this is not the moment for such discussions.
Noting the palpable tension and caution in her gaze, you silently exhale a breath of resignation. Any attempt to coerce her into speaking would undoubtedly yield counterproductive results.
So you decide to follow her topic.
test
test
test
test
test
test
Okay, so what's the big deal you were hyping up in your SOS?
Noticing that you've decided not to probe any further, she appears to let out a subtle sigh of relief. She then gestures toward a particular stack amid the small hills of case files to your left.

speaker: Christina
content: You need to look at this.

You saw it coming. The Public Security Bureau has been up to their necks dealing with the antique theft investigation, leaving them little time for case selection. So they've likely lumped all the recent low-priority reports and dumped them here.
Still, as you start to delve into the contents of the case files, your facial expression shifts to one of nuanced bewilderment.

A domestic squabble at the Fernley Manor? Eerie noises haunting Inkborough in the dead of night? A celebrity contralto on Sceptentine Street missing her personal photo collection? Some tipsy suburbanite swearing he spotted a luminous, unidentified creature of the canine variety?

speaker: Christina
content: ...Uh? Oh, whoops, my bad—wrong pile. These are the ones that are kinda sketchy but not exactly red-alert material. The real do-or-die stuff is that one over there, heh.
With a touch of awkwardness, she scratches her head and subtly shifts her fingers to indicate another document adjacent to her.
For a moment, you find yourself at a loss for words, internally questioning the significance of these seemingly trivial details. Nonetheless, you proceed to lift the pertinent case file.
As you unveil the cover, your eyes meet an oversized inscription: "The Great Cat Heist"—
A cat café in Eastside was victim to a burglary during the early morning hours three days prior, and three cats were abducted by the criminals?

speaker: Christina
content: You got it. This case is a real head-scratcher. Start by checking out the CCTV footage we pulled from the cat café.

In the dead of night, precisely at 2:15 a.m., a tall, slender young man materializes before the glass door of the cat café. Ensuring he is unobserved, he deftly retrieves a toolkit from his pocket and commences the delicate art of lock-picking. After ten minutes, the lock finally acquiesces.

Upon crossing the threshold, his eyes dart to the overhead security camera before he unerringly navigates to a secluded corner: the sanctuary for the café's feline residents. With a flick of his wrist, the latch is undone, and he steps into the realm of the cats.

Once inside, the man finds himself instantly besieged by a small clowder of cats. With discerning eyes, he singles out one feline and sets it beyond the enclosure's boundary. Navigating a minefield of strewn toys and food dishes, he advances to a dim corner where two other cats are lost in slumber.

He scoops them into his arms with minimal disturbance. As he prepares to make his exit, another cat trails behind him only to be returned to its confines by the man. Sealing the enclosure, he cradles the trio of chosen cats and departs the café as the clock strikes 2:30 a.m.

speaker: Christina
content: Playback's over. Spot anything fishy?
This guy's a weird one... Don't your typical burglars usually go incognito? You know, a mask or a hat, something to hide their mug.
Christina gives a nod of approval.

speaker: Christina
content: That's right. Usually, crooks go to great lengths to disguise their looks when they're pulling a job, just to throw us off the scent. But this fella? No mask, no hat, nothing.

speaker: Christina
content: Heck, he even eyeballed the camera, like he's daring us: "Hey, I'm Henry! Come get me if you dare!"
Henry, you say? So you've got a bead on this guy already?

speaker: Christina
content: Yep, had some friends over at the Public Security Bureau do a facial scan. He's got a rap sheet, so he popped up right away.
As she speaks, she opens a folder next to her and hands it to you.

speaker: Christina
content: Take a look, Henry's dossier. Freshly sent over just 30 minutes ago.
Henry's a high school dropout, jobless wanderer, no next of kin, scraping by on government handouts and random gig work at a corner store. Even has a history of getting into scraps.
...His profile checks all the boxes of a typical crook.

speaker: Christina
content: And trust me, nabbing those cats wasn't some last-minute whim; it was clearly preplanned.
Preplanned?

speaker: Christina
content: Did you catch that? When he made eye contact with the camera, he didn't even have to look around for it. Knew exactly where it was. And when he got into the kitty playground, the guy popped that latch like he’d done it a hundred times.

speaker: Christina
content: He knows that café like the back of his hand; definitely did his homework before making his move.

speaker: Christina
content: Another thing, the cats in there didn't seem to mind him one bit. That's not typical cat behavior for an intruder in their turf at that hour. So they've got to know him at least.

speaker: Christina
content: Looks like he's put in some solid groundwork to get on their good side.
You ponder for a moment.
Speaking of cats...
Snatching cats? That's pretty out there, especially when there's pricier stuff in the café... So, you think he's in it for the cats, not the cash?

speaker: Christina
content: Heh, look at you, detective-in-the-making! You're right on the money with my own thoughts!
At this point, Christina snaps her fingers in delight.

speaker: Christina
content: We can't say it's a surefire thing, but odds are, you're right.

speaker: Christina
content: He didn't just grab any cats; he had his eye on those three specifically. One other cat tried to tag along, but he didn't just sweep it up—put it right back where it came from.
What's he after, then?

speaker: Christina
content: Ah, that's the million-dollar question! And it's up to yours truly, the Chief Detective, to dig it up and lay it bare!

speaker: Christina
content: Ahem, so we're still in the dark about what drives this guy, but one thing's for sure—the cats are no ordinary felines. Crack that mystery, and we're a hop, skip, and a jump away from busting this case wide open.

speaker: Christina
content: But let's not forget, we're dealing with a loose cannon with a violent past. No telling what he might do to those helpless kitties. So, chop-chop, sign off on my field trip request, will ya?

Shelving her earlier enthusiasm and self-satisfaction from her investigative zeal, she locks eyes with you, her expression now solemn. With deliberate care, she sifts through the chaotic mound of papers strewn across her desk to unearth a form that had been prepped in advance.

speaker: Christina
content: So, my deep dive's got you clued in on how critical this is, yeah? I've got a full-blown game plan ready to roll. The clock's ticking, and every tick puts those hostages in deeper trouble. Time's of the essence for this rescue mission!
She pauses for a moment.

speaker: Christina
content: Uh... did I say "hostages"? Feline hostages?

speaker: Christina
content: Whatever, semantics. The point is, we've gotta get those cats outta harm's way, and slap some cuffs on that no-good catnapper!
With a surge of righteous fury, she clenches her fists tightly, her arm casting a forceful swing into the void, as though to deliver justice to a nefarious villain absent from the scene.

speaker: Christina
content: Hmph, any jerk who dares to harm innocent, adorable critters is totally, totally, totally unforgivable!
Christina's spirited and energetic demeanor brings you some comfort.
It seems that your "tactic of delay" worked. At least for now, she is fully engrossed in the "Great Kitty Caper," momentarily shelving the concerns that have been gnawing at her.
So you promptly take the form and sign your name.

speaker: You
content: Of course, no problem. How could I, a humble chief, stand in the way of a great detective cracking a case...

speaker: Christina
content: Yay!!!
Before you can get a word in edgewise, she bursts into cheers. You have no choice but to clear your throat and cut in:
But I have a condition—I have to go with you.
Her excitedly waving arm is still suspended in mid-air.

speaker: Christina
content: Hmm? You're also going?
You nod.

Christina bears faint dark circles beneath her eyes, her visage still carrying traces of fatigue. It might be the residue of her tireless delve into bygone matters, or the recent nocturnal hours spent organizing case files.
Regardless of the cause, considering her present state, it's unthinkable to allow her to venture out alone.

speaker: Christina
content: I didn't think you were into this kind of stuff...
She caresses her chin in thought for a good while before she finally manages to release a hesitant sigh.

speaker: Christina
content: ...Alright. Since you managed to answer fairly well just now, I'll begrudgingly let you tag along on this case as a temporary little assistant!

speaker: Christina
content: But just to be clear, solving cases isn't child's play, you have to follow my lead, got it? No going off on your own, otherwise, I can't ensure your safety...

speaker: Christina
content: Oh, and don’t forget, you’re just a temporary sidekick! You're on probation till you prove your worth. And just a heads up, I run a tight ship!
Observing her bend her fingers, earnestly establishing the ground rules with you, a smile surfaces on your face.
Alright, I'll follow the grand detective's orders to a T.

As you step through the doorway, the gentle chime of the wind bell welcomes you, its tone crisp and melodious. Perhaps it's the lull before the typical rush hour, but you find yourselves as the sole patrons within the cafe's quaint ambiance.

Unburdened by the day's commerce, the cats are nestled comfortably in their designated spots, with some curled up in slumber while others sprawl lazily in the activity area, basking in the sun's warmth, enjoying a serene afternoon unique to their kind.

speaker: Christina
content: Since the cat's our lead, it only makes sense our investigation kicks off at the scene of the event—the cat cafe! Little buddy, make sure you soak it all in and see how a real sleuth gets down to business!
Okay.

speaker: Bartender
content: Welcome, what can I get for you two?
Seeing you both standing there, looking around unsurely, a young store staff approaches, her face adorned with a warm smile.

speaker: Christina
content: You go ahead and order, I'll go check on the cats.
Christina pats your shoulder, making her way directly to the bustling cats area.

speaker: Christina
content: Kitty cats, look who’s come to play!
The cats proceed with their grooming and napping, seemingly unimpressed by the sudden human presence among them, deeming her unworthy of even a fleeting glance.
Faced with such apathy, Christina’s resolve only firms. She sets her sights on an orange tabby, squatting down before it, hand poised for a gentle stroke.

speaker: Orange Cat
content: Ha!

speaker: Christina
content: Whoa!
In a fluid motion, the cat snarls and swings its claws. Evading the attack, Christina loses her footing and falls back onto the ground, narrowly dodging the menacing claws.
...Are you okay?
You, having just wrapped up your meal, hurry over to assist her back to her feet. Christina brushes off the dirt, sticking out her tongue with a touch of lingering fright from the near miss.

speaker: Christina
content: I'm fine... But that little furball sure has a temper, haha...
