Unnoticed by the diligent staff crafting drinks behind the counter, the minor stir goes on. You both select a table nestled by the window and as you settle down, Christina finally draws her gaze away from the handful of cats.

speaker: Christina
content: By the way, what did you get for drinks?
Two cups of Civet Coffee. The barista said it's a house favorite.

speaker: Christina
content: Um...
She hesitates, struggling with herself for a moment, then leans in and lowers her voice.

speaker: Christina
content: You don't suppose the Civet Coffee here is... authentically local, right...?

What? Oh, no. The civet that produces the beans for Civet Coffee and cats are two totally different animals. Plus, these beans are a bit on the rare side, so they're pretty pricey. I guess serving Civet Coffee in a cat cafe is likely the owner's way of pulling a playful one on the patrons...
You mention this and remember the fairly decent price for the two cups of coffee, pausing for a beat.
...Maybe?

speaker: Bartender
content: Here's your coffee, please enjoy.
Just as a silence descends between you both, the staff brings over the coffee, and Christina promptly halts her.

speaker: Christina
content: Hey, could we borrow you for a few minutes? We're here to look into the Cat Cap... ahem, the theft case. I'm the Acting Inspector from the Eastside Public Security Bureau, and this is my assistant.

speaker: Bartender
content: Ah, Miss Inspector! You've finally arrived, please, you must help us find our kitties!
Christina gives a nod, delving into the roomy pocket of her detective attire to retrieve a photo of Henry, showcasing it to the staff.

speaker: Christina
content: This is the cat burglar captured on camera. Based on my initial analysis, he probably scoped out your place beforehand. Do you recognize him?

speaker: Bartender
content: His name's Henry, a regular around here. Honestly, without the surveillance catching him, I would've never thought he'd pull off something like this.

speaker: Christina
content: ...Huh? A regular? What does that mean?

speaker: Bartender
content: It's like this, one evening, a co-worker didn't latch the door tight after hours, and all the cats dashed out. It was Henry who pitched in, finding and bringing them back one by one.

speaker: Bartender
content: He seemed to have a soft spot for cats. After that incident, he'd come around often to play with the kitties here, and the little furballs really took to him.

speaker: Christina
content: Was he genuinely fond of cats? Or was it a front for something else?

speaker: Bartender
content: I don't believe so. He had a way with cats, and the sincere smile that lit up his face around them, it didn't seem like something one could fake. Besides, cats can pick up on that sort of thing.
"An authentic cat lover" Christina scribbles these words in her notebook with a furrowed brow, then lifts her gaze once more.

speaker: Christina
content: Do you think there's a particular reason he took the cats? Was it out of sheer love, wanting to have them all to himself?

speaker: Bartender
content: I'm not sure about that. "Orange Juice" is Henry's favorite cat, they usually have a great time together, but he didn't take it. It's been a bit down lately because of this...

The staff gestured towards the feisty orange cat that had almost given Christina a piece of its mind earlier—it was the same one seen in the surveillance footage, being escorted back to its enclosure by Henry.
Christina chuckled nervously a couple of times.

speaker: Christina
content: I've had a firsthand encounter with that...

speaker: Bartender
content: What?

speaker: Christina
content: Nothing... ahem, onto the next question.

speaker: Christina
content: Could you give us some details about the three cats that were taken? Was there anything unique about them?

speaker: Bartender
content: Hold on, let me grab their photos... This Siamese one is named "Big Bro," he's the top cat around here, quite haughty, doesn't mingle with humans much, except for Henry.

speaker: Christina
content: You can totally see that from the expression in his photo...

speaker: Bartender
content: This white furball goes by "Red Ink," a real bundle of energy and mischief, super friendly and not a bit shy, but a knack for finding trouble.

speaker: Christina
content: Uh... I've got a tiny question. Why call a white cat "Red Ink"?

speaker: Bartender
content: Oh, because on its debut day in our cafe, it managed to topple a bottle of red ink, and sported a red coat for several days afterward.

speaker: Christina
content: Oh, that explains it..

speaker: Bartender
content: This calico fur buddy is named "140," since it tipped the scales as the heaviest kitten in the litter, boasting a birth weight of 140 grams. It's on the shy side though, often curling up in a corner for a nap when it's idle.

speaker: Christina
content: The kitties here sure have some unique names...

speaker: Christina
content: Just out of curiosity, are these kitties left here by their owners?

speaker: Bartender
content: No, we got them straight from a cat shelter.

speaker: Christina
content: Well, that pretty much rules out catnapping for ransom or spiteful retaliation.

She nods, probing further into the likes and daily routines of the cats. She scribbles down these bits of information along with their names, and asked the staff for photos of the three cats, which she then tucks between the pages of her notebook.

speaker: Christina
content: Alright, that wraps up my questions for now. Thanks for your cooperation. We'll get in touch as soon as there are any updates on the case.
Closing her notebook, she pulls you along to leave the cat café, amid the staff's words of thanks.

speaker: Christina
content: Things are really heating up...

speaker: Christina
content: Alright, junior, time for a pop quiz! What have you gleaned from our inquiry so far?
Um... the takeaway?
Hesitant, you struggle to grasp her line of reasoning. Given the superficial questioning you've just undergone, drawing any definitive "conclusions" seems a stretch at best.
Noticing your hesitation, she releases a resigned sigh, gently patting your shoulder as she offers some sincere consolation.

speaker: Christina
content: No worries, it's par for the course to miss the mark on your first case. Don't sweat it—just keep grinding.

speaker: Christina
content: What I'm getting at is, Henry deserves a second look; he's not matching up with our initial impressions. Let's dash to the next locale, see what fresh leads we can dig up.
With five minutes of concentrated work, Christina successfully breaches Henry's door using her specialized lock-picking kit.

What greets you is a basement room that seems to offer nothing more than affordable rent. It's a dingy, claustrophobic space—musty and poorly lit, with just a sliver of a window at street level barely contributing to either lighting or ventilation.
Resting near the window is a table that looks like it's been rescued from a scrap heap, its surface marred by countless scratches and devoid of any paint.

The newspaper on top screams a headline: "How the High-Profile Heist Hits Business Tycoon's Antique Vault." Adjacent to it, a stack of aid station supply coupons are neatly held together by a paperclip.

speaker: Christina
content: Hey, Sidekick, wanna take another crack at it?
Feeling the weight of Christina's expectant eyes on you, you tentatively venture to speak.
Hmm... The newspapers are all dated in a sequence, which suggests Henry's a daily news junkie, right? But the most recent issue is three days old... So, he's been MIA for that long?
Hearing your deductions, she enthusiastically flashes you a thumbs-up.

speaker: Christina
content: Nice work, really! You're catching on, don't you think? Sleuthing's not rocket science, is it?
Then, a sizable box hidden beneath the table catches your eye. You wrestle it out into the open, and upon unsealing it, you're astonished to discover it's chock-full of bagged cat food.
Stockpiling all this cat food? Think he's got a cat?

speaker: Christina
content: Doubt it... I don't see a shred of evidence like a kitty bed or a litter tray.

Christina takes a moment to survey the confining quarters, then grabs the pile of aid vouchers. She meticulously cross-references the cost of the stockpiled cat food against the financial aid he's received.

speaker: Christina
content: This food doesn't come cheap. Looks like he's sinking nearly all his aid bucks into it... But why?
The modest bed against the wall mirrors the rest of the room's decor—worn but fairly tidy.

speaker: Christina
content: Wait a sec, are those books stashed under the clothes?

Christina, ever observant, fishes out three tattered books from beneath a mound of clothes at the bedside. Their spines are frayed, their pages yellowed and warped, signs of being pored over again and again.

speaker: Christina
content: "The Comeback of Detective Nutty," "The Gilded Bug," "Three-Cent Copper"... Who knew this dude was a whodunit junkie? He's got taste! And check out all these scribbles and notes in the margins...

Christina's eyes sparkle as she leafs through the worn pages, reveling in a newfound camaraderie over the shared love for whodunits. She nods in satisfaction, giving you a hearty shoulder slap as she goes.

speaker: Christina
content: So, Sidekick, ever get around to "The Comeback of Detective Nutty"? Heh, this chapter, "The Jigging Miniature," is where Henry scribbled the most. It's a gem! You gotta know, the lead character, he...
Lost in a book again, aren't we? Sherlock, we've pretty much scoped out the place, yeah? Time to hit the next spot?

speaker: Christina
content: Yeah, we've got bigger fish to fry... but that Detective Nutty though...
You let out an exasperated sigh, finally coaxing the ever-chatty Christina out of the basement, though she keeps stealing glances back.
Time seems to slip through your fingers during the marathon of visits. As you check off the last two spots on your investigative itinerary, you realize dusk is settling in.

speaker: Christina
content: Ugh... I'm wiped out...

Christina removes her deerstalker hat, dabbing away sweat, and plops herself unceremoniously against the side of a building. Seeing that you're equally worn out, you sit beside her, giving your overtaxed legs a much-needed breather.
Being a detective is far from a walk in the park.

speaker: Christina
content: You said it. What's really getting to me is that we've been hoofing it all day and haven't run into a single soul—or even a stray cat.
But hey, it's not a total wash...
The Welfare Office

speaker: Tramp
content: Ah, Henry? I can't say why he's in the same boat as us, needing handouts to get by, but the dude's solid, no doubt.

speaker: Tramp
content: You know, there was this one time a volunteer girl messed up and gave him an extra share. Guy didn't hesitate—gave it back the very next day. Even the folks running the place were like, "Never seen anyone like that here."

speaker: Tramp
content: The guy's a gem, really. Pops in now and then for a chat, helps patch up our clothes, even lugs stuff around for us. Oh, and get this—he's the go-to guy for the local strays.

speaker: Tramp
content: He's got like, eight or nine cats under his wing. Feeds 'em like clockwork, and last winter? Built 'em a cozy little den.

speaker: Christina
content: Strays, huh? So that's what all that cat food's for.

speaker: Christina
content: You run into him recently?

speaker: Tramp
content: Nah... He was a no-show at the handout the other day. You think something's up?
The Thrift Shop

speaker: Boss Grandma
content: Henry, ah yes. I first met Henry last winter. He was wandering around my store like he was lost or something. Finally plucked up the courage to say he needed some old bedding for stray cats.

speaker: Boss Grandma
content: Kid had empty pockets, so he asked if he could work off the cost. How could you turn down a good-hearted guy like that? Lucky for him, we were restocking that day, so he rolled up his sleeves and busted his hump all day.

speaker: Boss Grandma
content: Since then, he'd pop by to do some odds and ends for me. I couldn't offer him much, but he never half-assed it.

speaker: Boss Grandma
content: Oh, and there was this one time, some punk kid was swiping stuff right under my nose—my eyes aren't what they used to be. Henry saw it, though, and chased the brat down. Even got into a bit of a scrap. Can you believe the kid had the nerve to play the victim and drag us to the cops? Still eats at me, you know.

speaker: Christina
content: So that's the backstory of his "fighting rap," huh...

speaker: Christina
content: So to sum it up—Henry's not just some "bad news bear," he's more like your all-around stand-up guy, always pitching in where he can.

speaker: Christina
content: He loves detective novels, crazy about cats, and spends his tight welfare checks on cat food for strays. Even made them little nests for the winter. So why the heck would he nab cats?

speaker: You
content: But we're all on the same page that he's not gonna hurt those cats, right?

speaker: Christina
content: You took the words right out of my mouth. It's like finding a needle of good in a haystack of bad.

speaker: Christina
content: Ah, chasing justice is never a walk in the park, is it?

speaker: Christina
content: Most folks would be throwing in the towel by now, but not me. I'm the top sleuth in Eastside, and it's gonna take more than this to trip me up!

speaker: Christina
content: I've got a lead on a spot that's just begging for a closer look. Something's gotta turn up...
You mean those kitty hideouts Henry whipped up at the corner?

speaker: Christina
content: Bingo! If he's that invested in those strays, there's no way he'd skip mealtime. We could totally stake out the spot and snag him!

speaker: Christina
content: Wow, you're picking this up quick! From clueless newbie this morning to a budding pro now. Keep on this track, and you'll be my go-to sidekick in no time!

Christina beams at you and gives you a playful wink, as though she's been miraculously rejuvenated right where she stands. She rises to her feet in one fluid motion and, without a moment's hesitation, lifts you up from the ground as well.

speaker: Christina
content: Come on, chop-chop! No time to lose! Off to the secret lair of the stray cat we go... oh, hold up!
She tugs you forward for a few strides, then abruptly comes to a standstill. You find yourself scrambling to halt your own momentum, narrowly averting a collision with her.

speaker: Christina
content: Whoa, almost slipped my mind! We gotta bring some treats for those furballs! Trust me, these cats are no fools; no goodies, no gossip!
You meander through the backstreets, burdened with two cumbersome sacks. After navigating a maze of wrong turns, you at last stumble upon the elusive "Stray Cat Haven" concealed in a secluded nook.

To dub it a "Stray Cat Haven" is wholly fitting. Within this diminutive realm claimed by the strays, you encounter not merely an assortment of cats, cozy nests, and feeding stations, but even a towering cat tree ingeniously crafted from reclaimed odds and ends.
The wall at your back is a canvas of street art, but a bold numeral "2" dominates the scene, impossible to overlook.

At first, these feline residents merely offer you a cursory glance before resuming their activities. But the moment you extract kibble from your bags and fill their feeding dishes, their demeanor undergoes a dramatic reversal.

An imposing legion of cats rapidly converges from every corner, encircling the food bowls and diving into their meal without a shred of decorum. A handful even vocalize a few meows and proceed to tenderly lap at your hands.

speaker: Christina
content: Ah, just as I thought—two-faced little furballs. What's the saying? In a world as harsh as this, a full belly can make even a cat play nice...
As Christina caresses their velvety coats, feigning a ponderous sigh, her focus is abruptly diverted by a specific cat beside her.

speaker: Christina
content: Huh? Where'd you run off to? You look like you've been through the wringer!

Your eyes trace the path of her gaze, finally settling on a "white cat" that is thoroughly enjoying its feast. It's only then that you grasp her words in their literal sense—this little rascal has inexplicably become a canvas of paint, each whisker uniquely tinted.

speaker: Christina
content: Hold on... no way, is that you?!

She narrows her eyes at the paint-streaked cat, then lets out a sudden cry of astonishment. Fumbling through her pocket, she retrieves her notebook and a photograph of the missing cat, her expression brimming with both elation and wonder.

speaker: Christina
content: Red Ink! You're Red Ink, right?

speaker: Red Ink
content: Meow?
Upon hearing Christina utter its name, Red Ink lifts its head in puzzlement and tilts it slightly in her direction.
In that case, the other two must be around here somewhere!

speaker: Christina
content: Yeah, let's hustle and look around...

speaker: Christina
content: Siamese... Siamese... Gotcha!

Christina hoists a cat away from the feeding station by gripping the scruff of its neck. The cat's disgruntled expression, set against its dark visage, is a spitting image of the "Big Bro" from the photograph.

speaker: Big Bro
content: Meow. (Hey, you're messing with my chow time here.)

speaker: Christina
content: Big Bro, that's you, right?

speaker: Big Bro
content: Meow. (Well, duh.)
As she locks eyes with "Big Bro," a subtle twitch tugs at the corner of Christina's mouth.

speaker: Christina
content: ...? Wait, did it just give me the side-eye?
Well... it seems like it did...

speaker: Christina
content: Is this what a regular cat is supposed to act like?

speaker: Big Bro
content: Meow. (You guys idiots or what?)

speaker: Christina
content: Why do I get the vibe it's throwing shade at me...
After an exhaustive search, you finally glimpse the barely visible, rotund posterior of a cat tucked away in a secluded corner. Christina advances and delicately prods it with her fingertip.

speaker: Christina
content: Hey there, furball. Mind turning around? We've got a few questions for ya.
Meow... (Hey, why poking my behind like that...)
The feline posterior vanishes with a swift "whoosh," only for a calico cat to cautiously emerge moments later, its paws securely shielding its visage.
Looks like we've got our shy guy, 140, no doubt about it.

speaker: Christina
content: So we've got our cat, but why would Henry go through the hassle of swiping it from a cat café just to stash it in some alley-cat hideout? Doesn't add up...
Christina murmurs under her breath as she paces to and fro, fraught with tension.

speaker: Christina
content: Ugh, it's like I'm so close to the truth, but I just can't put my finger on it! What am I overlooking here...

speaker: Christina
content: Hey, did you catch that? The food bowls were spotless, like mirror-clean. Looked like they'd been licked over and over.

It's true—the cats do appear to be famished. Could it be that he hasn't been around to feed them lately? And didn't the homeless guy at the welfare office mention he skipped picking up his handout a couple of days ago?

speaker: Christina
content: Okay, let's think. No going home, no picking up aid, no talking to anyone—that's weird enough. But skipping out on feeding his beloved cats?

speaker: Christina
content: What if he's not dodging us on purpose? What if he can't show up because he's in some sort of jam? These cats could be breadcrumbs he's left for us!
So why these three furballs? What's he trying to spill through them?

speaker: Christina
content: If he's dropping hints for folks who don't know these kitties, then whatever "standout traits" he wants us to catch have gotta be in-your-face. Like breed, looks, or maybe...
Those names! They struck us as odd when we first heard them at the cat café, right? "Big Bro," "Red Ink," "140"—what's the deal?

speaker: Christina
content: ...The books in his room! "The Jigging Miniature," "The Gilded Beetle," "Three-Cent Copper." They're all about secret codes. He's gotta be dropping us a coded message! Maybe we're supposed to mix and match letters from those names?
But how do we piece them together? There's a gazillion combos... He's gotta have left us some breadcrumbs, right?

speaker: Christina
content: Let's see, the most standout thing around here is...
Christina tugs you toward a graffiti-covered wall, where a glaring numeral "2" catches your eye.
Look at this, a big ol' "2" right in our faces. What does it mean, take the second letter? ...Bro, 4, Ink? 4, Bro, Ink? Ink, Bro, 4...
...Inkborough!

speaker: Christina
content: 4 Inkborough Street!!!
You both blurt out at the same time.

speaker: Christina
content: He left us an address!

Exhausted from your travels, you and Christina make your way to the Public Security Bureau. She quickly entrusts three cats to a young officer before guiding you through the clamorous main hall. Without a moment's pause, she thrusts open the door to the sheriff's office.

speaker: Sheriff
content: What do you mean they've vanished into thin air!? This town's so small you could walk across it in five minutes! You've had the whole squad on this for days and still no sign of these lowlifes? What, did they sprout wings and fly away!? Get back out there and find them!
The sheriff ends the call, his expression clouded with irritation. Evidently, the "High-Profile Antique Heist" remains at a standstill.
Forgoing any unnecessary small talk, Christina cuts to the chase, laying the dossier for the "Cat Café Kitty Kidnapping" squarely on his desk.

speaker: Christina
content: The purloined kitties are safe and sound back at the bureau, but we've hit a snag—our guy Henry's been MIA for at least three days now. No clue why, but he left a breadcrumb: 4 Inkborough Street.

speaker: Christina
content: We think he's in hot water over there. Send a team, ASAP!

speaker: Sheriff
content: 4 Inkborough Street?

The mention of the address finally captures the sheriff's attention. Yet, as he lifts Henry's file and scans the photograph within, he emits a contemptuous snort, his visage a canvas of undisguised revulsion.

speaker: Sheriff
content: Can't shake that warehouse, can he? He's the one who cried wolf about robbers hiding out there just four days ago. We rolled in, guns blazing, and what did we get? A whole lot of nothing!

speaker: Christina
content: Now we've got Henry's angle! It's all coming together! 4 Inkborough Street's gotta be tied to the antique heist. Looks like after striking out with the cops, Henry played the bait, swiping cats to drop breadcrumbs and get us sniffing around...

With the final piece of the puzzle in hand, Christina can't help but slam her fist onto the table in exhilaration. She meticulously unravels her entire chain of deductions, informed by the day's discoveries.
Yet, the sheriff remains stoically unimpressed, his impatience manifesting in multiple glances at his wristwatch.

speaker: Sheriff
content: Look, Christina, hats off for the legwork you've done on cracking this case. I'll get someone to shuttle those cats back to the café, and we can put this one to bed for now.
Christina's eyes go wide, a picture of sheer incredulity.

speaker: Christina
content: Put this one to bed!? What about the search? What's gonna happen to Henry?

speaker: Sheriff
content: I never said we're calling off the search. A deadbeat drifter causing false alarms and breaking and entering? Oh, we'll nab him alright, just not on today's to-do list.

speaker: Christina
content: What... You're missing the point. Henry's in danger right now, we've got to move—

speaker: Sheriff
content: No, you're missing my point. We've got bigger fish to fry. The top priority for the whole precinct is cracking the antique heist and getting the loot back. We can't afford any distractions. No one's got time for your little sleuthing escapades.

speaker: Christina
content: But these two cases aren't at odds! If we save Henry, it could be a game-changer for your case too... Admit it, you just don't buy what I'm selling!

speaker: Sheriff
content: How can I? Based on your wild theories? You claim he's gone AWOL—anyone come forward to report him missing? You say he's in a tight spot—got any proof? Blood, a weapon, CCTV footage of him being snatched—anything?

speaker: Sheriff
content: Christina, you've been playing the Acting Inspector for some time now. Do we really need a refresher on the ABCs? Our "belief" needs to be built on solid proof.

speaker: Sheriff
content: Ever wonder how this whole mess looks through my eyes?

speaker: Sheriff
content: A low-level hoodlum with a rap sheet for violence, caught red-handed on camera breaking and entering. Plus, we've got a whole squad that can vouch he cried wolf.

speaker: Sheriff
content: So, he's skedaddling to dodge the law, tossing out red herrings to throw us off his scent, all to buy himself a little more freedom—this is what I've pieced together from cold, hard facts.

speaker: Christina
content: But you've got zilch to prove I'm off base! Plus, I cracked this case with my ace detective sidekick, ${PlayerName}. No way we're wrong!

When Christina belts out these words in defiance, her entire face flushes a deep crimson. Her tone is as decisive as a guillotine's blade, but the sheriff can only respond by wearily pinching the bridge of his nose.

speaker: Sheriff
content: Christina, you really wanna keep butting heads with me? Alright, let's cut to the chase.

speaker: Sheriff
content: Pouring resources into some nobody, especially when we're down to the wire on bigger fish to fry, is a total waste of time.

speaker: Sheriff
content: Look, until we solve this antique heist, the best we can do is put the word out to all the shelters in Eastside. If Henry pops up, they'll hold him. Trust me, guys like him can't last long without a handout. He'll come crawling back.
Christina places both hands on the sheriff's desk, her head bowed. Her face is obscured by the shadows thrown by her hair and hat, leaving her expression a mystery to you.

speaker: Christina
content: Guys like him? Come on, you don't even know the first thing about him. He swiped that cat to give us a lead, for crying out loud! He's putting his neck on the line for what's right!

speaker: Christina
content: And you're telling me it's a waste of time to go after him? Isn't the whole point of the force to chase justice and keep folks safe? Worst-case scenario, we end up on a fool's errand. But that's a hell of a lot better than having his blood on our hands 'cause we dragged our feet!

speaker: Christina
content: Do you know what I consider a complete waste of time?

Christina raises her head once more. In her eyes, tinged with a subtle shade of red, you glimpse a complex tapestry of emotions—pain and restraint, as if haunted by memories, yet also a resolute and unwavering determination.

speaker: Christina
content: My parents' sacrifice back then was a complete waste, a tragedy! And I swear on my life, I won't let history repeat itself, not on my watch!

speaker: Sheriff
content: You...

Clearly caught off guard by her mention of her parents, the sheriff's face is a mask of surprise. Sensing the tension reaching a boiling point, you quickly intervene, aiming to defuse the standoff between the two.
How about this? I'll go with Christina and we'll do some digging. If we find anything concrete, we'll loop you in with solid proof.
This way, we're not draining police resources, and we're also doing our best to keep Henry safe.
The sheriff's face remains stern, but he knows he has to give you some leeway. With a reluctant sneer, he finally speaks, his voice laced with a cutting edge.

speaker: Sheriff
content: Fine, knock yourselves out. Seems like you, the big-shot MBCC Chief, have time to kill, messing around with this hard-headed young lady.
Christina's face flushes with heightened anger. You quietly take her hand in yours, locking eyes with the sheriff as you prepare to speak.
No, I wouldn't call this messing around. I have faith in her instincts.

speaker: Christina
content: ...My apologies. You're here to back me up, and all I've done is drag you into this hot mess.
Moments after being practically booted from the sheriff's office, Christina murmurs an apology, her voice tinged with regret. You offer a reassuring smile, attempting to lighten the palpable tension.
No worries. "No good deed goes unpunished," right? That's your line, isn't it? As your trusty sidekick, I knew what I was signing up for.

speaker: Christina
content: To be honest, other than Mr. Dole, it feels like no one at the Public Security Bureau ever took me seriously. They probably think I'm just riding someone's coattails or that I'm a loose cannon.
Frustrated, Christina gave a stone on the road a forceful kick.

speaker: Christina
content: They keep calling me a hothead who's all talk and no action, saying I'm just a naive kid. But isn't chasing justice and keeping this city safe why we signed up to be detectives in the first place?
Her head dropped, weighed down by the gravity of her own words.

speaker: Christina
content: Look, I get it. When they're knee-deep in high-profile cases, the heat's on from the media and everyone else. Tempers flare, words fly. I get it.

speaker: Christina
content: But come on, since when did justice become exclusive to finding lost treasures for the rich and famous? Helping the average Joe matters just as much. Mr. Dole would back me up on that.

speaker: Christina
content: Henry's a lone wolf, no ties, no one to miss him if he vanishes off the face of the Earth. So, if we don't step up, who will?

speaker: Christina
content: Maybe, just maybe, it's not the high-rollers and celebs who need us most. Maybe it's the "nobodies" like Henry who really need someone in their corner.

As you absorb her words, a revelation strikes you. This young-appearing Acting Inspector is far more mature and nuanced than you had initially estimated. She's not just filling a role; she embodies it, more so than anyone else you can think of.
Hmm, going after Henry isn't a mistake, and standing up for what's right is a no-brainer. We can't win them all, but sticking to our principles? That's non-negotiable.
Hey, being a "passionate crusader for justice" isn't a bad rap, you know? In a world that's fifty shades of messed up, we need people like you to be the compass. Get what I'm saying?
With a warm smile, you gently pat her shoulder, your touch conveying a world of encouragement and understanding.
I've got your back. Whether it's playing the hero or shouting from the rooftops for justice, you've got this.
Sensing a sudden stillness beside you, you glance back. Christina stands there, rooted to the spot, her eyes locked onto you as if caught in a moment of revelation.
Something on your mind?
With a soft laugh, she quickens her pace to fall back in step with you.

speaker: Christina
content: Nah, it's just that Mr. Dole once told me something along those lines.
You've brought up this "Mr. Dole" a lot. He must've made quite an impression on you, huh?

speaker: Christina
content: Absolutely! Mr. Dole is a legend in the precinct! Sure, he's got a permanent scowl and zero patience, but he's never belittled me like the others. He's been my rock and cheerleader all along.
So, do we need to ask Mr. Dole for help?

speaker: Christina
content: Nah, we're good! I'm not a kid anymore; I can handle things myself. And hey, I've got you as my kickass sidekick now, don't I?
Christina beams as she takes your hand, her spirit and zeal miraculously back in full swing.

speaker: Christina
content: Chin up! A top-notch detective never throws in the towel! So what if we're flying solo without backup? You and me, we've got what it takes to crack this case wide open and bring them home!
Yo, what's the game plan with this dude?

Hearing the distant chatter, you and Christina move in unison, your footsteps barely making a sound. You both duck behind a metal shelving unit, its surfaces layered with years of grime, that stands beside the corridor. Through the narrow openings between stacked crates, you steal a surreptitious glance.
In the heart of the warehouse, three imposing figures, unmistakably mercenaries, loom over the trussed-up Henry. His mouth is gagged with a grimy cloth, and he's soiled from head to toe.
The mercenary at the forefront gives Henry an irritable kick, drawing from him a moan of helpless agony.

speaker: Henry
content: Mmph mmph mmph...
Just get rid of him; he knows too much.

Only when an icy voice pierces the air do you become aware of a fifth presence in the room. Emerging from behind the imposing metal shelving that had concealed him, another individual leisurely strides into your line of sight—
The individual who emerges from the shadows is the last person anyone would expect—the affluent business owner who played the role of a hapless victim on the news, lamenting his stolen treasures.

The term "inside job" pops into your head like a lightning bolt. It all makes sense now; the authorities have been chasing their tails for days because he's been controlling the narrative from the start.

Shaking off your initial shock, you pivot toward Christina, planning to remind her to capture evidence for the Public Security Bureau. But she's already on it—she's pulled a tiny camera from her pocket and flashes you an approving thumbs-up.

speaker: Head Mercenary
content: Ha, you've got it easy, just running your mouth. Let's not forget, we agreed to just help you shift your stuff out of the warehouse, stash it for a bit, make the scene look legit, and then haul it back after the cops clear out from your place.

speaker: Head Mercenary
content: Now we're stuck cleaning up your mess after dodging that surprise search from the cops... We've been saving your hide more times than I can count.

speaker: Rich Businessman
content: Hey, let's not point fingers, alright? If you guys hadn't been caught red-handed moving stuff that night, we wouldn't be dealing with this headache now.

The rich businessman, a veteran in the cutthroat world of commerce, isn't one to back down. While the head mercenary maintains his smug smile, his two underlings advance a step, their faces stern, ratcheting up the tension in the room.

speaker: Head Mercenary
content: So, what you're saying is, we dropped the ball?

speaker: Henry
content: Mmph mmph mmph!

speaker: Head Mercenary
content: Oh? Got something on your mind?
He extends his hand and forcefully removes the gag from Henry's mouth. Coughing to clear his throat, Henry raises his head, his eyes methodically scanning the faces of those assembled.

speaker: Henry
content: Cough, cough... The cops will pick up on the breadcrumbs I've left and come running. You lot won't stand a chance.

speaker: Head Mercenary
content: Ha! Still playing the knight in shining armor, even when you're knocking on death's door? It's almost cringeworthy. Snap out of it, kid. You've been our guest in this lovely place for three days now. Where's your cavalry?

speaker: Head Mercenary
content: Ever heard of "The Boy Who Cried Wolf"? You think they'll come running a second time after a wild goose chase? Or maybe you think you're some VIP they can't afford to lose?

speaker: Henry
content: You're clueless. You mean to tell me that in that massive security bureau, there's not one person with half a brain?

speaker: Head Mercenary
content: Fine, keep playing the waiting game. We'll see if they show up in time to scrape you off the floor.

Irritated by the lack of the expected begging and instead receiving a sharp comeback, the head mercenary darkens his expression. He forcefully jams the gag back into Henry's mouth before pivoting back to the rich businessman.

speaker: Head Mercenary
content: Look, no need to burn bridges here. Let's meet halfway. We'll help you handle the surprise inspection from the cops as a make-good for our slip-up during the move. But if we're talking life-and-death stuff, that's a whole different ballgame and it's gonna cost you.

speaker: Rich Businessman
content: Alright, what's your price?

speaker: Head Mercenary
content: Double or nothing.

speaker: Rich Businessman
content: ...Don't you think that's pushing it?

speaker: Head Mercenary
content: What's the deal? Getting cold feet? You're gonna make a killing from insurance fraud, and you can't even toss us a bone? That's not how you climb the ladder, my friend.

speaker: Rich Businessman
content: Look, if I hadn't lost my shirt in those investments and wasn't desperate for cash, do you think I'd be rolling the dice on insurance fraud? And let's be clear, that payout is just plugging holes, nothing more.

speaker: Head Mercenary
content: Last chance to change your mind.

The head mercenary lets out a sly laugh as he pulls a gun from his waistband, leveling it at the businessman's temple. The businessman, who was just moments ago full of bravado, goes weak in the knees, his face drenched in a cold sweat.

speaker: Rich Businessman
content: Alright, alright, you've got yourself a deal. Double it is.

speaker: Head Mercenary
content: Deal sealed. Now, let's get down to your fate. To be frank, we didn't have the time or the patience to chase you down. But hey, you practically begged for this by showing up.

He crouches down, lightly tapping Henry's cheek with the cold steel of the gun barrel. The imminent threat of death hangs heavy in the air, piercing through Henry's once-steadfast composure. He starts to thrash about, his muffled cries echoing the desperation of a creature backed into a corner.

speaker: Henry
content: Mmm! Mmm! Mmm!!!

Just as his finger tightens around the trigger, an unexpected thud reverberates through the room. The detective's casebook, hefty as a brick, sails through the air, unerringly disarming the mercenary.

speaker: Christina
content: Christina, Acting Inspector of Eastside's Public Security Bureau. You're all under arrest—fraud and kidnapping, the whole nine yards!

Christina, clutching her cane, strides purposefully toward the assembled group. As they get a good look at her, their faces become a tableau of mixed emotions—the businessman exhales a sigh of relief, Henry's face is a mask of residual terror, while the mercenaries erupt into raucous laughter.

speaker: Head Mercenary
content: Sent a rookie chick to handle this, huh? The Public Security Bureau must be scraping the bottom of the barrel.

speaker: Christina
content: Ha, who's looking down on whom? You're just bit players in this drama, so watch closely to see who's really going down!

Capitalizing on the moment when the mercenaries are preoccupied with Christina, you covertly snatch up her detective dossier and use it to knock out the businessman attempting to flee amidst the chaos. Swiftly untying Henry, the two of you haul the businessman behind a large metal crate that can serve as makeshift cover.

speaker: Henry
content: Are you guys really the cops?
Yeah, we got the leads you left. Good job. Backup from the precinct is en route. Here, take this communicator and keep them updated, we are counting on you.

speaker: Henry
content: Will do.
Just as Henry grabs the walkie-talkie you pass him, Christina's voice cuts in right on cue.

speaker: Christina
content: Hey, Sidekick! Where ya at? Time to kick some butt and have some fun
I'm here.

speaker: Christina
content: Let's roll! The dynamic duo, unstoppable and undefeated!
She twirls her staff and lunges into the fray, as you, standing behind her, slowly lift your hand.
Empowered by your shackles, Christina's combat prowess escalates. Incoming bullets are either deflected by your shackles or parried by her staff, scattering metallically across the floor.
The three mercenaries soon find themselves backed into a corner, their faces etched with defeat. With nowhere else to go, they aim their firearms, ready for a desperate last stand.

speaker: Head Mercenary
content: Damn it! These two are Sinners!

speaker: Junior Mercenary
content: What's the plan, boss? I'm almost outta bullets here...

speaker: Head Mercenary
content: Ugh, fine. Bring out the big gun.
The three lock eyes for a split second, each unholstering a spherical device from their belts and launching it in your direction.

speaker: Christina
content: Watch out—
Christina reflexively brandishes her staff, inadvertently setting off the trio of compact gas grenades. With a resounding pop, a suffocating cloud of white smoke engulfs the room in an instant.
You both find yourselves coughing and tearing up, hurriedly pulling up your sleeves to shield your mouth and nose.

As the white haze finally starts to dissipate, the corner you were focusing on is eerily vacant. The only trace left is the receding sound of chaotic footsteps echoing from behind you. You whirl around in haste, but only manage to spot the tail end of a garment vanishing behind a row of shelves.
They're heading for the depot entrance! They're trying to escape!

speaker: Christina
content: Damn it... We can't let them get away!

speaker: Rise
content: For now, working here is the best choice. There's only a few days left before my probation ends. I should be able to pass easily.

speaker: Rise
content: Now... it's time to leave work.

speaker: Intern
content: I-I'm really sorry! There's still a bit left, and I might not be able to finish it today. Can I submit this report to you tomorrow? I will definitely finish it tomorrow!

speaker: New Boss
content: Have you considered how much your late submission will delay other colleagues? If you knew you weren't going to finish, why didn't you give me a heads-up?

content: I'm sorry, I miscalculated the time... I only received this task this morning, and only later did I realize that it's too much to finish in one day...

content: I care about the results, not the process. You've been interning here for some time now, yet I haven't seen any progress from you.

speaker: Intern
content: It's my first time dealing with this type of work, and no one trained me how to do it. I had to figure it out myself, which took a lot of time...

content: Enough with the excuses! No one is guiding the other newbies either, yet they manage to complete their work beautifully. Why is it that you can't do the same?

speaker: Intern
content: I can do it... Can I just have some more time, please? I promise I'll do it well...!

speaker: New Boss
content: The worst thing you can have is an attitude problem! Sigh... I really thought better of you.

speaker: New Boss

speaker: Intern
content: I'm sorry, I've caused you trouble. I'm wrong, I'm really sorry...

Besides, you're in no position to be uppity.

The past and the present are the same. It's just that before, she was the victim, and now she's an observer.
She thought she found respect and equality here, but it was all just a hidden bribe, luring her to become a beneficiary, luring her to become part of the facade...

speaker: Rise
content: It's the same everywhere. How disgusting...

speaker: New Boss
content: Alright, enough with your apologizing... Well, I'll give you another chance to make up for it.

speaker: New Boss

speaker: Rise
content: Goals? High standards? I've looked over the intern's assignment already, and it's not urgent enough to require completion today. In fact, she should have ample time for revisions.

speaker: New Boss

Rise?

content: With this resume, even if you don't look for a job, opportunities would come knocking at your door. It would be hard to find anyone with better qualifications than you, not just in the job market, but all of Eastside.

speaker: Rise

speaker: Rise

speaker: Rise
content: Yes, but...
She pauses, bearing the confused look of a traveler suddenly lost in a fog.
Then, she slowly continues, as if questioning you, or perhaps herself.

speaker: Rise
content: But it's the same everywhere; Nirvana is just a snapshot of the overall toxicity of DisCity.

speaker: Rise
content: What do you think I should do? Just find another company and continue to endure?

speaker: Rise
content: You see... even if the lightsaber can't eradicate the problem, it can at least eliminate some of the scum and have some short-term effects.

speaker: Chief
content: Is equality and respect maintained by violence really what you want? Rise, I don't think you'd condone such a self-righteous illusion.

speaker: Rise
content: Then tell me, what else can I do?

speaker: Rise
content: When one place fails me, I look for another, then another... It may seem like I'm on the search, but in reality, I'm just constantly fleeing!

speaker: Chief
content: Then stop looking.

speaker: Rise
content: Hmm...
You interrupt Rise, and she looks at you with a puzzled gaze.

speaker: Chief
content: I'm offering you another possibility.

speaker: Chief
content: If you can't find an existing work environment that's good enough, why not help create one?

speaker: Chief
content: If you think about it, the lightsaber is not just a weapon, but also a torch to find companions. A fair and comfortable workplace is a common wish for many.

speaker: Chief
content: So, Rise, would you consider working with others to create the workplace you want?

speaker: Rise
content: ...Chief, please be more direct.

speaker: Chief
content: Alright... I'll be more direct, then. If you want a place where you can work with peace of mind, the MBCC is a promising choice.

speaker: Chief
content: There are still some problems now, but many of us here share your beliefs. I'm confident that you'll shine here.

speaker: Chief
content: But ultimately, this is an interview. I feel like I'm tooting my own horn.
You sigh helplessly. Rise clearly didn't expect you to still consider this an interview. After a brief pause, she chuckles softly.

speaker: Rise
content: Isn't this interview just an excuse for you to interrogate me?

speaker: Chief
content: It's my duty as the Chief to interrogate, but this interview is my personal invitation to you.

speaker: Chief
content: This is a mutual selection, and my choice remains unchanged. Rise, now it's your turn to choose.
Rise glances at the electronic wristwatch on her wrist.

speaker: Rise
content: ...It's about time to conclude this interview, then. To wrap things up, shouldn't we discuss the most important part about salary and benefits?

speaker: Chief
content: The position is quite special, so the salary isn't high... uh, or rather, almost nonexistent.

speaker: Chief
content: But it's not without advantages! We cover all living expenses, and it's very stable. You never have to worry about being laid off.

speaker: Rise
content: ...Chief, you're really not suited to be an interviewer.

speaker: Rise
content: However, I can accept what you offer.

speaker: Chief
content: You've made up your mind? Sure you don't want to compare it to some other offers?

speaker: Rise
content: If the price of a high salary is endless exploitation and abuse, then I'd rather not have it. Respect, equality, comfort... many things are much more important to me than money.

speaker: Rise
content: Given our previous experience working together, I think I have a good understanding of your abilities and character. After thinking about it... working for you is the most ideal choice for me right now.
You extend your hand again. This time, Rise grasps it tightly without hesitation.

speaker: Rise
content: Chief, I'm willing to trust you, for now. I hope you won't forget the promise you made to me today.

speaker: Chief
content: I will strive to extend this trust indefinitely.

speaker: Chief
content: I shall help you realize your vision and free you from those needless burdens. Someday, respect and equality will reign as the norm around here, and we'll bear witness to its final form together.

speaker: Rise
content: ...That really sounds like something a hero like Anniken would do.

speaker: Rise
content: I'm looking forward to it.
The red shackles pierce and connect your palms together. This is your "work contract" with Rise.
"The lightsaber will take me to my companions. I shall not walk alone down this path."
She is not the lonely one.

speaker: Local
content: Outsiders who've been here...? Nah, except you.
...Other than me, I mean. Spot any merchants around? I was hoping to do some business here...

speaker: Local
content: Last time we had merchants in Tuco was 'bout two weeks ago, I think. Things have gotten rough lately, and with the desert bandits runnin' wild, no traders in their right mind would come here! Take my advice, you'd best give up on that idea...

speaker: Merchant
content: Oh, gimme a break! Stop babbling with your rotten memory... Don't listen to this old fool, newcomer! Just two days ago, there was a passing merchant who made a stop in our town—someone with a huge backpack.

speaker: Merchant
content: He just showed up out of nowhere late at night. Lucky for him he found our little backwater, otherwise the WhiteSands storms would've eaten him alive that night.

It's just past noon, and the shaded area beneath the market canopies is packed with townspeople, the crowd as bustling as the blazing sun above. You wipe the sweat from your face and raise your voice over the cacophony of merchant calls and haggling.
I see! Do you know where he is now? I'd love to pick his brain about what sells well in WhiteSands...

speaker: Merchant
content: Now? Think he's gone already... Hmm, I'm not sure. Why don't you check upon the motel he stayed at?

speaker: Coachman
content: Oh, that guy? He's gone! Only stayed one night at Mira's, then took off at dawn toward eastern WhiteSands with all his bags. I saw it myself when I got up to feed my horses.

speaker: Coachman
content: And hey, I'll have two lizard skewers! Extra spice and make sure it's the leg meat!

speaker: Merchant
content: Coming right up! Hey newcomer, wanna give it a try? You'll love my secret spice blend, oh you'll love it. You won't find lizard meat this tasty anywhere else!
You nod to the vendor's enthusiastic spiel and step aside. While waiting, you begin to piece together the leads you've gathered...

Several days ago, due to frequent sandstorms, multiple trading outposts and shelters were suffering critical Hybercube depletion. A refill was in urgent need to maintain operations, but the actual delivered Hypercubes fell far short of the requested volume.
It's virtually impossible for these barely functioning outposts and shelters to wait for the next shipment after a litany of approval process.

If the missing Hypercubes cannot be retrieved immediately, DisCity will have no choice but to abandon these hard-won facilities in WhiteSands, leaving them to be swallowed by the sandstorms once again.

The MBCC and the FAC have launched an urgent investigation, evidence pointing to a repeat smuggler operating in WhiteSands. Being responsible for multiple Hypercube smuggling cases, the suspect, still at large, shows exceptional counter-surveillance skills and has made unpredictable moves.
The FAC had been tracking the smuggler until two days ago, when all traces suddenly vanished at this obscure desert town you'd never heard of—Tuco.

Suspecting the smuggler might still be hiding in town, you hold the FAC crew nearby to avoid raising any alarms. Meanwhile, you assumed the role of a traveling merchant to investigate the town personally.
This obscure town has proven far more welcoming than you expected. You never would have imagined a desert settlement could be such a busy hub of activity.
A wave of searing heat snaps you back to reality. Lost in thought, you didn't notice the harsh sun shifting overhead.
You step back, trying to return to the shade that has since moved, when you accidentally bump into something.
Mmph!
You hear a startled cry, followed by the sound of objects scattering and rolling across the ground.
I'm sorry. I didn't notice you were behind me. Are you alright?

You've bumped into an Outland girl who came to shop at the market. Her tanned skin makes her bright blue eyes stand out even more vividly. She's carrying a basket nearly half her height, its contents now spilled all over the ground.
No, no, it's fine! I was walking too fast and didn't see you either.
You stoop down and apologetically help gather the fallen items back into her basket. Something prickles your palm. You look down and see a round prickly pear.
These are for making juice. Thank goodness they didn't get crushed. Nothing's more refreshing than prickly pear juice in the desert... Oh and, thank you so much for your help.
No worries. It's because of me you dropped them anyway.
The girl takes the last prickly pear from your hand and stands up holding her now-refilled basket.
She studies your face for a moment, as if committing it to memory, then her eyes crinkle as she smiles radiantly.
You are not local, are you, coming from outside... or perhaps from DisCity? If you're not in a hurry, how about drop by my place later? It's over there, not very far.
Take a seat and have a glass of cactus pick-me-up. All on me, as thanks for your help today. I bet you'll like it.
Before you can respond, a playful whistle interrupts your conversation. You turn around to find the vendor with an amused grin.

speaker: Merchant
content: Stop chatting up the young lady! C'mere, your lizard skewers are hot as hell!
Thanks. How much?
The vendor gestures a number. After you pay and turn back to where the girl was, she's already gone, leaving only some shallow dents in the ground where the prickly pears fell.
You start exploring other parts of the town, posing as an inexperienced businessman looking for seasoned merchants and business opportunities.
female_content: You start exploring other parts of the town, posing as an inexperienced businesswoman looking for seasoned merchants and business opportunities.

content: Most townsfolks don't recall the person you describe, with only a few giving accounts same with those of the coachman and the vendor. You've found nothing suspicious in this peaceful-looking little town.
By the time you circle back to the marketplace, it's almost evening. The crowded square is bustling with vendors packing up their stalls for the day.
The desert's evening breeze weaves through the crowd, carrying wisps of food aroma, bringing a gentle close to another ordinary day in the townsfolks' lives.

speaker: Child
content: Daddy!

speaker: Merchant
content: Whoa there, big guy! Getting heavier, aren't you? Tell me all about your day!
The man lets go of his grill cart handles and opens his arms wide, catching the boy as he runs over. He hoists his son onto his shoulders, drawing excited squeals from the kid.
When you walk by, he notices you and calls out to you in his booming voice.

speaker: Merchant
content: Hey, you still asking around? Look, you can't rush it when it comes to searching for someone. Why not try again tomorrow?

speaker: Merchant
content: ...And it's getting late. Why not spend the night in town? Looks like we're in for some strong winds tonight. It wouldn't be safe to travel.

speaker: Merchant
content: Right over there—there's the only motel in town. Want me to show you the way?
That's too kind of you. But I think I can find it on my own. Thanks for that.

speaker: Merchant
content: Alright then! Take care! We should head home too. Come on, son, say goodbye!
Still perched on his father's shoulders, the boy waves to you shyly at his father's prompting.
After seeing off the father and son, you take out your device and send what you've gathered so far to the crew stationed outside town.
<color=#fb9259>${PlayerName}</color>: The suspect has gone east of Tuco with the Hypercubes. Send a team to scout and keep me posted.
After sending the message, you pull your coat closer and head toward the town's only motel.
Good evening! To stay or to go... Oh hey, it's you again!
The person behind the counter turns around and your eyes meet. The sunset's glow mingles with the motel's warm lights, illuminating the girl's surprised but thrilled expression upon seeing you.
You recognize that she's the girl from the marketplace earlier today. Recalling what you've heard from the townsfolk, you cautiously venture a guess.
You're... Mira, the owner of this motel?

speaker: Mira
content: Yes, that's me! Looks like the others have already told you about me. Oh dear, I hope they didn't ruin my image!
The girl nods, her delicate features lighting up with a warm, amiable smile. When you met her earlier, you never would have guessed that the tiny young girl would turn out to be the owner of a motel.

speaker: Mira
content: Is there anything I can help you with? Or did you just come by for that cactus pick-me-up I promised you? Sure thing, I always keep my word.
I'd like to stay for the night. Do you have any rooms available?

speaker: Mira
content: Of course, all clean and ready. I can show you your room whenever you'd like.

speaker: Mira
content: Though I guess... you probably haven't had dinner yet, have you? I happened to have cooked a bit more food than I can eat today. If you don't mind, we could dine together.
Thank you. I'd love to, if you don't mind.

speaker: Mira
content: Not at all! This is just part of my job as the host. I simply never allow tired guests to go bye-bye on an empty stomach in my place.
Mira gives you a playful wink as she guides you to a dining table.
When you offer to help, she smiles, gently but firmly pushing down on your shoulders from behind, making you sit in the chair before you can protest.

speaker: Mira
content: No worries. I'll do it. As my guest, your only job is to relax and enjoy.
With practiced efficiency, Mira lays out the tablecloth and sets the cutlery. She weaves gracefully between the tables and chairs, bringing out one steaming stew after another.
The dishes may lack the elaborate presentation of Eastside's fancy restaurants, but they have a charming warmth unique to home-style cooking, making your mouth water instantly.

The motel's interior gives you the same impression. It's a snug space with rough wooden walls and floor, a small bar, and a few dining tables. It's basic, perhaps rudimentary even, yet everything is kept spotlessly clean and tidy.
The carefully arranged strip lights, desert plants, tapestries, wall ornaments, and small decorations present everywhere add a warm, cozy feeling to the space.

speaker: Mira
content: Hehe, what are you waiting for? Dig in! The food tastes better before it gets cold.
As she speaks, she brings you a glass of refreshing cactus pick-me-up and serves several pieces of delectable lamb into your bowl.

speaker: Mira
content: The desert lamb chop is my specialty. What do you think?
The motel owner's hospitality seeps into your body and mind tense from the mission. So this is what it means to truly feel at home away from home.
Surrounded by such a cozy atmosphere and with warm food in your stomach, you find yourself unwittingly beginning to relax.
You cook so well, especially the lamb. I've never tasted anything like that before. It's really good.

speaker: Mira
content: You think so? I'm so glad! Please, help yourself to more. My motel may not be much, but there's always plenty of food to go around.
Smiling, she serves you another helping.

speaker: Mira
content: I was worried they might taste too foreign to you. The cuisine in DisCity is quite different from what we have here, after all.
You are not local, are you, coming from outside... or perhaps from DisCity? If you're not in a hurry, how about drop by my place later? It's over there, not very far.
You recall how she instantly identified you as someone from DisCity back at the marketplace.
You seem to know a lot about DisCity. Have you been there?

speaker: Mira
content: I wouldn't say I know much. In fact, I've never even left Tuco. It's just that I've had quite a few guests from DisCity over the years, so I've picked up bits and pieces here and there.
Her words catch you by surprise.
...You've been running this place for years? But you seem quite young.

speaker: Mira
content: I grew up here. It originally belonged to my parents. They're not in good health these days, so I've taken over.
...I see.
Her tone is natural and sincere for her to be telling lies. You can't help but feel sympathy for the young motel owner.
You've been here for a while but haven't seen a single staff member. It must be incredibly difficult for such a young lady to run a motel alone in the harsh desert.
After a brief silence, Mira smoothly changes the subject to continue the chat.

speaker: Mira
content: Alright, enough about me. Now let's talk about you. When we met earlier, you seemed to be looking for someone. Did you find them?
No, he seems already left from Tuco. But before that, he probably had spent a night here at your motel.

speaker: Mira
content: Maybe, since we're the only motel in town, all outsiders looking for accommodation end up here. When did he  arrive here you said?
Two days ago, I believe.

speaker: Mira
content: Two days ago... Ah, I remember that!

speaker: Mira
content: Honestly, I was almost startled! He just came out of nowhere, pounding on the door in the middle of the night. The sand he shook off from his clothes and boots piles up a small dune even.

speaker: Mira
content: He only stayed for two or three hours, then insisted on checking out before dawn. I wonder if he got any rest at all.
I see... Did he mention anything when he checked in? Like his name, why he's here, where he was headed?

speaker: Mira
content: Well... I'm not sure about any of that. I let him in and offered him some late-night snacks, but he snapped at me, telling me to keep my mouth shut. Then he went to his room, no word until he left.
Mira shakes her head and looks down, placing a hand over her heart as if still shaken by the memory.

speaker: Mira
content: What a strange one.
Her account matches what the other townsfolks have said. You shake your head in frustration.
Damn it... Looks like there's no way to retrieve my stuff in time. That crafty thief is going to slip away again.

speaker: Mira
content: ...Oh, so the person you're looking for is actually a thief? Did he steal from you?
You give a wry smile.
Yeah, and it's not the first time either.

speaker: Mira
content: So that's why... I found it odd how he kept clutching his bag like his life depended on it. And he kept looking around like he was always on alert.

speaker: Mira
content: If only I had known about this earlier. I would have done everything I could to stop him from running away.
Mira gently swirls her glass, staring at the remaining drink with a sigh, reminiscing.

speaker: Mira
content: Sigh, WhiteSands is crawling with outlaws these days. Rampaging here, they'd even kill a person over some loose change, let alone something as valuable as <color=#fb9259>Hypercubes</color>...
You frown.
I never said it was Hypercubes.
The words hang in the air. An unnatural silence looms over the room, broken only by the soft crackling of the scented candles.
Your expression hardens as you stare at Mira with a frown. Under your gaze, her smile falters for just a moment.

speaker: Mira
content: Oh... It's not Hypercubes that you've lost?

speaker: Mira
content: I was just taking a wild guess. You've been searching so desperately for long. It has to be something incredibly important... After all, nothing seems more valuable than Hypercubes for you DisCity folks...

speaker: Mira
content: Sorry, I was just trying to sound smart.
Mira's suspicious behavior alerts you to reassess the entire situation.

Your eyes scan the motel's decor once more. Nothing seems out of place at first glance, but now you wonder if these elaborate furnishings and ornaments, like their owner, might be concealing something beneath.
Your instincts tell you that Tuco's only motel may not be as ordinary and harmless as it appears. You'll investigate this place thoroughly when you catch a chance.
When your gaze returns to Mira, several theories are already emerging in your mind.
Could she be the smuggler's accomplice?
Or even, could this motel be a secret smuggling waypoint? Maybe she's so good at concealing it that no one in Tuco has noticed?
If so, was what she said about herself all a lie? Does she keep no staff here so as not to risk exposing the real business of this place?
...Oh, don't worry about it. It's nothing.
Despite your racing thoughts, you give her a reassuring smile and resume eating, carefully maintaining an air of peace.

speaker: Mira
content: Right, so, do you know this guy? How did he manage to steal from you so many times...
Likely conscious of her own flimsy explanation, Mira hastily changes the subject. You give her a vague answer, and she listens attentively without pressing further.
After that, you chat a bit more and none of you bring up the previous topic again.
After dinner, Mira offers to clean up and shows you your room.

speaker: Mira
content: Rest well, my dear guest. Have a good night.

Night finally falls. Through the door crack, you see Mira put out the counter candles and head to her room with a yawn. In fifteen minutes, the last light in the motel goes out. Here comes your chance.
You creep downstairs in the dark, returning to the lobby. By the moonlight, you begin to examine the decorations that caught your suspicion earlier one by one.
You dig through each decorative plant in the corners, but find nothing but mere soil. There aren't any surveillance or wiretapping devices hidden within.
You carefully examine every component of the ornaments, but they turn out to be just ordinary decorations. No hidden switches or secret mechanisms are found.
You lift the tapestries, but find only seamless, solid wooden walls. No signs of hidden rooms or secret passages.
You pull open the drawers under the bar and find only ordinary purchase orders, receipts, and account books. Nothing suspicious. However, the wine cabinet behind the bar catches your attention.
The wooden cabinet holds several rows of various bottles, nothing particularly valuable or high-end. But what stands out is that almost every bottle is labeled a nametag.
Are these wines kept here by those townspeople?
This is a motel for travelers, yet it stores wines for townsfolk like a tavern. That means those people gather here often.

speaker: Merchant
content: Now? Think he's gone already... Hmm, I'm not sure. Why don't you check upon the motel he stayed at?

speaker: Merchant
content: ...And it's getting late. Why not spend the night in town? Looks like we're in for some strong winds tonight. It wouldn't be safe to travel.

speaker: Merchant
content: Right over there—there's the only motel in town. Want me to show you the way?
Come to think of it, the townsfolks kept bringing up this motel in your conversations. It was almost as if they were intentionally trying to guide you here.
...Were they all in cahoots?! Is this entire town a Hypercube smuggling waypoint? And they deliberately led me here to...
The thought sends a chill down your spine. You feel a creeping sense of dread crawling in your back.

You hold your breath and listen intently. No suspicious noise. Mira is still in her room, and you're still alone in the lobby. Only then do you let out a soft sigh, taking several deep breaths to calm yourself down.
Fretting over unproven assumptions is a big mistake... There must be more clues around here. Look harder...
After searching around, you find something suspicious at the stairway landing: a crude marking on the outside of the wooden banister, looking inconsistent with its decorative carvings.
There are some dried brown stains along the edges of each scratch mark, as if someone desperately clawed them into the wood with their fingernails.
Could this be... one of those direction markers used in WhiteSands?
Your brow furrows deeper as you study the dried blood on the mark.
Who left this? Was the maker of this mark dragged away? And where does it lead?
You follow the marks in the corner down into the cellar. The brown stains grow darker while the marks themselves become fainter, finally stopping at a narrow hidden door.
Your tense, heavy breathing echoes in your ears. The cellar is so quiet and far removed that not even a sliver of moonlight reaches here.
You're perfectly aware this is likely a trap set for you, yet it's your only lead so far.

After a moment's consideration, you send a message requesting support from the FAC crew on standby. Retrieving the stolen Hypercubes is of utmost importance. Right now, you're the only one who can investigate without setting off any alarms.
The hidden door creaks open, revealing the pitch-black space behind. With only faint light from your device screen, you cautiously step inside.
The moment you enter, you hear a thunderous crash behind you. A massive stone door slams down automatically from above, crushing the worn hidden door and cutting off any chance of retreat.
You hear the piercing whip of something cutting through the air in the dark. You dodge instinctively, but the hidden weapon still manages to slash your palm.
The knife pins your device to the wall, its shattered screen flickering a few times before dying, just enough for you to read the new message.
<color=#fb9259>Advance Team</color>: Chief, no signs of movement detected east of Tuco. The intel might have been inaccurate, but we'll continue searching further out.
Just as I thought.

Hidden weapons rain down from every direction past your head and the sides of your body from an invisible source in the dark. You try your best to keep your weight down and press yourself against the wall, searching for a way out while waiting for support.
Watch out!
In the dark, someone yanks you aside with incredible strength.
From where you were just standing, you hear the loud clang of a weapon being knocked off by a sharp object.
The figure shields you in the front. Your shackles react to the momentary pulse of Mania belonging to a Sinner.
...Mira? You're a Sinner? What is all this about?

speaker: Mira
content: No time for questions now. I'll explain later.

speaker: Mira
content: But right now, just stay close to me!
With practiced ease, Mira feels the wall until a mechanism clicks into place. She then pulls you through another hidden door with perfect timing.
The next second, you hear a hail of knives hitting the other side of the door.
You take several turns and stumble down a few flights of stairs. You couldn't have imagined the small motel having an underground space this huge.
As Mira drags you through the dark, winding passages, your thoughts race chaotically. You force yourself to stay calm and assess the situation.
Where are you taking me?

speaker: Mira
content: Ha... ha... Just know I'm trying to save you! If you had stayed there...

speaker: Mira
content: We'll be safe once we're through this door! Hurry, I don't want anything to happen to you.
She makes a stop before a door, letting out a long breath. Her reassuring words now only provoke further suspicion and wariness from you.
You pull your hand free, your tone steely.
Thanks for saving me back there. But unless I'm mistaken... You and your motel are in cahoots with that smuggler, aren't you?
And it's not just you... The whole town of Tuco is in on it. This whole place is a Hypercube smuggling waypoint!

speaker: Mira
content: No! That's not true!
Mira furrows her brow, her voice urgent but hushed as she protests.

speaker: Mira
content: We would never stoop to colluding with smugglers! He... that man is just our prey... just like you.
Your expression turns grimmer. So everything here is indeed a trap.
Keep going. Since I'm your prey, are you trying to hog me for yourself?
Deep beneath the motel, the cellar is wrapped in complete silence, filled with only the musty scent of aged wood.
The girl lets out a sigh, averting her gaze before slowly beginning to speak.

speaker: Mira
content: You're partly right. Yes, the entire town of Tuco is in on it. The busy crowds you saw during the day were just an illusion we created in disguise. But we're no smugglers, we're just...

speaker: Mira
content: ...putting on an act, working together to lure those smugglers and racketeers to get our survival necessities. Right, we're a bunch of criminals robbing criminals, says you.

speaker: Mira
content: And of course, sometimes, the loots include Hypercubes.
You recall the marks you saw on the banister in the hallway. You can't help but ask Mira the question.

speaker: Mira
content: The smuggler? We've gotten rid of him, of course.
As she goes through the whole thing casually, new doubts surface in your mind.
If things are what you said, those people trying to catch me outside must be your accomplices. Then why save me? Wouldn't it be easier to just let them in?
Answer my first question. Are you trying to keep me for yourself? Or you set special traps for certain prey?
When you saved me, you used your special power. You... wanted me to know you're a Sinner, didn't you?
Your tone leaves no room for denial. Mira hesitates for a moment, then pulls a crumpled slip of paper from her pocket.

speaker: Mira
content: I thought you were another smuggler in the first place, going after the previous one's Hypercubes. I was going to follow the plan with everyone else and get rid of you.

speaker: Mira
content: But while you were downstairs, I searched your room and found this. That's when I changed my mind.
You take the paper from Mira. It's a reimbursement invoice from some time ago, with an MBCC printed in the header and your signature at the bottom.
You must have stuffed it in your pocket a while ago and forgotten about it, and it just fell out in your room.

speaker: Mira
content: So you're that MBCC's Chief, I guess? I've heard of that place... Some facility in DisCity whose mission is to detain and manage Sinners.

speaker: Mira
content: I'd like to... make a deal with you. I know you have the power to make it happen.
Mira takes a deep breath and looks up to meet your gaze, her eyes no longer avoiding yours.

speaker: Mira
content: I'll help you escape from here, and no one's gonna find out. In exchange, I need you to promise me one thing.
Mira's voice is firm and sincere as she makes her promise decisively, stepping forward to take your hand again. But you still can't trust her, instinctively taking half a step back.

speaker: Mira
content: Yeah, I know that.
She gives a disappointed smile and withdraws her hand.

speaker: Mira
content: But I really need your help. I swear I won't do anything to harm you.

speaker: Mira
content: Would you at least come with me? I'll show you I mean my promise. Whether you decide to help me or not... that's completely up to you then.
She reaches for your hand again, and this time you don't pull away.
Mira leads you forward through some passages, so mazy that you would never find your way out without her. After a while, a dimly lit basement finally appears before you.
She skillfully operates the mechanism to close the gate, then steps aside to press a switch on the wall.
After a noisy electrical buzz, pale light floods the basement.
As your eyes adjust to the brightness and the room comes into focus, you can't hold back a gasp.
What...?!
You're in a small, barely furnished basement. In the center of the room, a middle-aged man and a woman of similar age lie side by side, their lifeless faces as pale as the harsh light above.
Only the feeble beeps of worn-out medical equipment by their beds indicate they're still alive.

speaker: Mira
content: I know that I'm nothing more than a cunning con woman in your eyes... but please, just this once, you have to believe me.

speaker: Mira
content: They need better treatment and medical equipment. You're my last hope. I can't lose them...

speaker: Little Mira
content: Daddy, I found a mistake in the ledger! It should be 8, not 7 here. My calculation is correct!

speaker: Daddy
content: Let me see... Well, you're indeed right! So clever my lil lady, haha! Looks like I can hand over the motel to you and enjoy an early retirement!

speaker: Little Mira
content: Dummy Daddy and Miracle Mira, haha!

speaker: Daddy
content: Oh my! Well then, would my genius lady like to guess what I got for her birthday?

speaker: Little Mira
content: ...Wow! A new dress! How pretty is this bow!

speaker: Mother
content: It is pretty, isn't it? And it's breathable, right? Or she will get heat rash if walking in the desert wearing this. Did you buy it with some secret savings, hon?

speaker: Daddy
content: What... no, honey! The guest last night was a clothing merchant from DisCity. I simply gave her a half off for the rate. Didn't spend a single penny!

speaker: Daddy
content: Come on, dear, don't worry about money. Our motel's doing just fine. Mira's happiness is what matters most!
I've lived in this motel with my parents in Tuco since I was born.

It's really just a tiny motel. But for little me, it was just perfect. Its small door and windows kept all the bad things outside, while under our narrow roof, travelers from everywhere became my temporary family.
During the day, time always flew by at the motel in a flurry of activity. Mom would cook and clean the rooms, while Dad would greet guests and tend to their needs.

speaker: Daddy
content: Buenas, traveler! My, that's quite some heavy luggage you've got there... Please, let me take those. Go rest in your room! No worries about a thing. As our guest, your only job is to relax and enjoy.

speaker: Mother
content: ...Oh! Have you had lunch yet? I'm just cooking for my husband and daughter. Why don't you join us... No trouble at all, really! The pleasure is ours!
That's how they were, tending to every desert traveler going in and out of town with scrupulous care and heartfelt sincerity.
Dad always told me it's the host's job to make every guest feel at home. That's how I've run things since then, always keeping his words close to my heart.
At night, when three quarters of our world is covered by the starlit sky, we'd gather with our guests on the remaining quarter of desert sand, dancing and singing around the bonfire...

Our small town had its share of peculiar neighbors, but they were all good people. Some they'd also "play house" like we kids do, and when it was done, a party would be thrown in the town square. Though I didn't quite understand what they're doing, I always had fun then.
I loved our motel. I loved Mom and Dad, and my life with the townspeople then.
Then one day, the desert's starry sky began to lose its clarity.

The winds grew stronger, and sandstorms became more frequent. Armed raiders would storm into town, looting everything in sight. At the slightest hint of trouble, my parents would lock the motel's door, terrified.

speaker: Daddy
content: Ugh... The desert bandits smashed our windows again. There wasn't much left in the storage anyway. Let them take what they want. But if this continues, soon we won't be able to survive in this town.

speaker: Mother
content: We can't stay here any longer! Even if we could endure this, I won't let Mira suffer like this. We've saved enough money. We'll find a way out of Tuco, whatever it takes.

speaker: Daddy
content: All right, I'll start asking around.

speaker: Mother
content: Mira? When did you come in... Oh, come here and try on these clothes I just mended.

speaker: Mother
content: Hmm, the hem's too short. Haven't you grown taller again? My Mira just grows so fast! I'll fix this, sweetheart... Soon, we'll be able to get you beautiful new clothes.

speaker: Little Mira
