content: It's okay, Mommy. I don't like clothes from the sellers anyway. I love the ones you made for me.

speaker: Little Mira
content: I'll eat less. That way I won't grow up so fast and Mommy won't have to keep fixing my clothes.
Why did Mom suddenly hug me and say sorry?
This question was too hard for my younger self. Back then, I just thought I said something wrong and made Mom cry, so I felt so bad and cried with her.

speaker: DisCity Merchant
content: You got all the money with you? There's plenty of hands to grease along the way. Don't count on me if you're short on cash!

speaker: Daddy
content: Yes, yes. Please, gentlemen, lead the way.

speaker: Little Mira
content: Daddy, where are we going? Are we leaving our motel?

speaker: Daddy
content: No, Mira, we're not leaving it. We're just... going somewhere else. There won't be any sandstorms there, and we won't have to worry about the bad people. We can open another motel...

speaker: Daddy
content: My sweet girl, we're going to DisCity!

speaker: Little Mira
content: Really? But these people look so mean, and they keep us locked up in here...

speaker: Mother
content: We... we just have to wait here while they get our papers done. We'll be on our way again soon.

speaker: DisCity Merchant
content: Tsk, that broke loser. This isn't even worth our time. Should've known Tuco folks were all penniless. Hey, can't you find some rich marks to scam next time?

speaker: Desert Bandit B
content: My crap! Rich people aren't that stupid to fall for your DisCity fairy tale!

speaker: Little Mira
content: We already paid them, why won't they let us go... Daddy, Mommy, I'm so hungry... I'm scared. I want to go home...
Dad fought hard to keep his voice from trembling as he forced a weak smile for me.

speaker: Daddy
content: ...Everything will be alright, Mira. Don't be scared. We can go out soon. Everything's good...

speaker: Mother
content: Mira, Mira, wake up...

speaker: Little Mira
content: Mmm... Mommy? Can we leave now?

speaker: Mother
content: Yes, we can leave now, sweetheart. Here's some water. Tie it to yourself. Don't drink it all at once, remember?

speaker: Daddy
content: Listen carefully, Mira. Once you get out of here, follow the moon and keep walking. Don't ever stop.

speaker: Little Mira
content: Just me alone? No, I don't want to! Why aren't you coming with me?

speaker: Mother
content: Because... you walk slower than us, Mira, so you need to start first. We walk much faster, and we'll catch up to you very soon.

speaker: Desert Bandit
content: Hey, you there! What's going on?!
The savage-looking desert bandit noticed our movement and approached us with a knife. Dad shoved me hard, pushing me through the gap he'd pried in the iron door.

speaker: Daddy
content: Run, Mira, run! Don't look back, just keep running!

Dad clung to the iron bars, veins bulging and eyes wild with desperation as he frantically waved me away. He roared in a hoarse voice, a sound I had never heard from his usually gentle, soft-spoken throat.

speaker: Daddy
content: The names Li Xianling told you would be the Realm of Yang and the Void of Yin, I imagine.
That night, the desert sky was exceptionally clear, the moon big and bright.
I ran on and on, never looking back, as if I could convince myself that Mom and Dad would indeed catch up if I didn't turn to check.
Until the pursuer's curses finally faded, until the moon set in the west and the sun rose again, until my water flask ran dry...
After fleeing for a day and a night, I finally collapsed from exhaustion on the sand, unable to get up again.
The sandstorm was spreading and the whipping wind hurt my face. Sand slipped into my eyes as I thought they would bleed. But what almost killed me was a dire thought...

It overwhelmed my exhaustion, like wildfire coursing through my body, burning through every vein until the pain became almost unbearable. I wanted nothing more than to lie down and let myself end there.
But I refused to give up like this. I was still waiting for Mom and Dad.
Huh? How come a child's lying there... Mira? Is that you, Mira?! Why are you out here alone? Where are your parents?!
Amidst adversity, this is the courage required. I'll clear a path for you!
As my consciousness slipped away, I heard the Tuco folks' cries, but still no sign of the ones who promised to catch up to me.

speaker: Mira
content: I was lucky. The awakening of my Sinner power pulled me back from death's door.

speaker: Mira
content: But by the time I woke up and begged the townsfolks to help save my parents, those desert bandits posing as DisCity merchants had vanished without a trace.

speaker: Mira
content: Mom and Dad... their bodies were covered in wounds, cast aside by those bastards like trash. The town's doctor said they had missed the best timing for treatment, and might... never wake up again.
As Mira tells you her story in a low voice, she picks up a photo frame from beside the hospital bed.
It's a family portrait, the colors faded with age. She gently caresses the faces in the photograph.
Though sunlight never reaches this basement, the patients' bedding still feels dry and warm. You look at Mira and feel your earlier distrust for her fading.
Your instincts tell you you can trust her through these details, this photo, and the poor middle-aged couple in it.
The deal you want to make with me, is it about your parents?

speaker: Mira
content: Yes. As you can see, their condition is critical. They're barely clinging to life, depending entirely on the IV and the life support machines.

speaker: Mira
content: But the medications and equipment maintenance cost a fortune, far more than my motel can sustain. And with Tuco constantly running with sudden desert bandit raids and disasters... I... I cannot...
So you joined the other Tuco folks in their scheme, scamming money out of travelers and even killing them when necessary.

speaker: Mira
content: I never wanted to do this, but... but I had no other choice!

speaker: Mira
content: My parents are still here in this town, their lives in the townsfolks' hands. I had no choice but to oblige them to lie and steal...

speaker: Mira
content: Sometimes I dream of Mom and Dad waking up. But that would mean they'd know everything I've done, and that terrifies me. I don't know how I can ever face them...

speaker: Mira
content: But I'm truly grateful to have met you... You've given me hope of escaping this nightmare...
She steps closer, taking your hands in hers like clutching onto a lifeline, her eyes pleading as she looks into yours.

speaker: Mira
content: I can help you escape! You can have all the Hypercubes we took from that smuggler. I know where they hid it! And if that's not enough... I'll surrender myself to the MBCC!

speaker: Mira
content: But in return, I beg you, please. Once you're safe, come back here and take my parents to DisCity for treatment! This is truly... their last chance...
Mira's chest heaves with emotion, tears welling in her reddened eyes. In the brief silence that follows, you can hear her quick, anxious breathing.
Her confession sounds so heartfelt and moving that for a moment, you almost can't bring yourself to question its authenticity.
You've never been able to turn away from someone's desperate plea. Resigned, you let out a quiet sigh.
You have my word, Mira. I'll help you and take your parents to DisCity.

speaker: Mira
content: Really?! Oh thank goodness, Chief! I'm deeply grateful...
But rushing out recklessly isn't our best option. I've already sent an SOS to the FAC crew stationed nearby. It would be safer to wait here in the basement until they arrive.

speaker: Mira
content: ...I see, you've thought this through, but... but there's still something concerning.
After a moment's hesitation, Mira bites her lip anxiously before speaking again.
What is it?

speaker: Mira
content: According to the original plan, I should've already gotten rid of you by now and rejoined the others... I'm worried they'll soon realize something's wrong and come look for us.
As soon as the words are out of her mouth, you hear strange noises from somewhere above you.

speaker: Local
content: Where is she? Where's Mira?! Where did she go?! Don't tell me that girl ran off with the lamb!!!

speaker: Local
content: That can't be! We have eyes everywhere. Not even a rat can slip out of town without us knowing. Search more thoroughly! If they're not in the motel, they're somewhere in town!

speaker: Local
content: All right, you lot guard the entrance. The rest of you, follow me into the motel!

speaker: Mira
content: Chief! They're already here! If we don't go now, we'll never get another chance!
Mira's grip on your hand tightens, her palm slightly damp with nervous sweat.
With your device damaged, you can't send your exact location to your team. You're not even sure if this basement door will hold until reinforcements arrive.
The chaotic footsteps and shouts draw closer. With no time left to think, you make your decision and grip Mira's hand.
...There's no other way. Mira, get us out of here!
Right outside the town of Tuco, a circular manhole cover is lifted, sending a cloud of sand into the air.
Mira emerges nimbly, tosses the bag of Hypercubes aside, then turns back to pull you out of the secret passage connecting the motel to the surface.

speaker: Mira
content: Here, give me your hand. Now, to get away from Tuco, all we need to do is run into the desert. Have you got anyone waiting for you out there?

speaker: Local
content: Found them! There they are! And they've got the Hypercubes!!

speaker: Local
content: Stop them!! Don't let them get away!!!
You've just got out of the secret passage when shouts break out nearby. In the moonlight, you see multiple trails on the sand spreading rapidly toward you.
This way, run!
There's no time to waste. You grab Mira, who stands frozen in shock, and sprint in the direction where you remember your team is stationed.
In the endless expanse of nighttime WhiteSands, strong winds hurl waves of sand into your face. You can barely see where you're going, and soon Mira is pulling you along as you both stumble forward.

speaker: Local
content: They're right ahead of us! Don't let them escape! We must get those Hypercubes back!
The same townsfolks who greeted you with warm smiles during the day are now pursuing you relentlessly like a pack of vicious, greedy hyenas.
Hasty gunfire erupts behind you as bullets barely scrape past you, sending up sprays of sand at your feet.
Bang! Bang!

speaker: Mira
content: Chief, look out! ...Argh!
A violent impact shoves you aside as Mira cries out in pain. You catch her as she collapses, and find your hands stained with blood.
Hang in there! We can't give up here!
You pull Mira up and hoist her onto your shoulders, forcing your way forward with every ounce of strength you have left.
Your steps grow heavier as the shouts behind you draw closer.

speaker: Mira
content: Hey... You...

speaker: Mira
content: You should just leave me here... I can't... drag you into this...
Don't talk. You're not dragging me into this, and I'm not breaking my promise.
You grit your teeth, hoist her onto your body, and keep running desperately.

speaker: Support Squad
content: ...Chief's location confirmed! I repeat, Chief's location confirmed! Hostile targets detected. Initiate defensive formation and ensure Chief's safety!

speaker: Local
content: ****, cops! Scatter, idiots! Get the hell back, now!

By sheer luck, your chosen escape route leads you straight into the approaching support squad. The townsfolks after you immediately turn tail, disappearing into the swirling sandstorm without a trace.

speaker: Support Squad
content: FAC WhiteSands operation squad reporting in. We apologize for our late arrival, Chief. Your orders, please.
With a soft clap, a trembling hand clutches yours tightly, a warm, sticky liquid trickling down your hand.

speaker: Mira
content: ...Chief... don't forget...

speaker: Mira
content: You've promised... You must, you must come back... for them...
With these final words, Mira falls unconscious in your arms.
Swirling sand shrouds the starry sky. In the dark, you can barely examine her wounds, but there's no ignoring the heavy scent of blood that fills your nostrils.
There's only one option to perform treatment and keep her alive. After quickly weighing the situation, you make your decision.
The Hypercubes have been retrieved. Mission accomplished. Our current priorities are to transport the Hypercubes to the disaster area and tend to the wounded.
Our targets know WhiteSands better than we do, and we can't hold out long in this sandstorm. Retreat for now and return to Tuco for the arrest later!

If what Mira told you is true, then Tuco's organized crime activities must have been ongoing and this is no single incident. Furthermore, they possess a substantial cache of weapons, making them considerably armed.
You must be extremely cautious with the pursuit of such a dangerous gang.

After making all the necessary arrangements, you immediately lead a large force across the vast barren desert, fully prepared for what's ahead. But when you finally reach this remote corner deep in the desert...

speaker: Armed Squad Member A
content: No way! This is not what we saw last night!
You find nothing but another stretch of barren desert.
The people, the town, the houses... Everything has vanished into thin air, like water evaporating under the sun.
...Search the area. See if they left any clues when they evacuated.

speaker: Armed Squad Member B
content: Chief, we found something!
All that remains of the vanished town of Tuco is an entrance leading to that basement.
...Mmph! Mmmph—!
And there, bound and abandoned at the entrance, is the wounded smuggler Mira said she had gotten rid of.
When you enter the interrogation room, Mira has just finished telling a WhiteSands joke, and the smiles have yet to fade from the two staff members beside her.

speaker: Mira
content: Oh my... I got so caught up that I lost track of time. Is it already time for our appointment?
Mira turns to you with the perfect amount of surprise and apology on her face. As she moves, you notice the edge of a bandage around her shoulder peeking out from beneath her collar.
I apologize for asking you to do this before your wounds have healed.
However, I need your help to clear some doubts about the recent smuggling case.

speaker: Mira
content: Don't worry about it. I wasn't that badly injured. Consider me almost fully recovered after the past few days of rest.
As Mira speaks, she smooths out the creases in her collar so that it covers the bandage. Then, she gives you a reassuring smile.

speaker: Mira
content: So, what would you like to know from me?
At your gesture, the staff leave the interrogation room. Mira leans back casually in her chair, smiling gently as she quietly waits for your questions.
You decide to start with what matters to her most.
As I promised you before, while you were recuperating here, we returned to Tuco and brought your parents to DisCity. They've been admitted to the hospital for specialized treatment.
After initial diagnosis, the doctors believe there's a possibility of recovery.

speaker: Mira
content: Really...? That's wonderful!

speaker: Mira
content: When the others at the Bureau told me this, I couldn't quite believe it, but hearing it from you puts my mind completely at ease... Chief, you indeed deserve my trust. I'm glad I placed my bet on you.
You do not respond to her seemingly flattering remarks, and simply continue with a smile.
Sounds like you've really settled in. Getting along well with everyone?

speaker: Mira
content: Oh, yeah... It's really just because everyone here is so kind and helpful. It's not like me doing anything special.
You're well aware of her ability to make people lower their guard. In just a few days, she has won over many at the Bureau with her gentle demeanor and social finesse.
Now, the smile she shows you is one with an endearing mix of modesty and shyness.
But having encountered the unexpected situations during your return to the town and analyzed the entire incident, you no longer look at this seemingly fragile and innocent motel keeper the same way.
That's why you remain unmoved by her display and go on as you've planned.
Besides your parents, we also brought back that smuggling suspect. Despite a head injury, he was lucid enough to confess to smuggling Hypercubes alone, with all the details matching up the records.

speaker: Mira
content: Oh, that's wonderful news. Congrats!
Aren't you surprised?

speaker: Mira
content: ...Why would I be?
Because he is still alive.

speaker: Mira
content: Of course he's alive. I never said he was dead. Chief, are you perhaps misunderstanding something?
Mira gives you a good-natured smile, her tone sincere yet tinged with craftiness.
Then what did you mean by getting rid of him?

speaker: Mira
content: When we're done milking these cash cows dry, we usually sell them off to do manual labor. You know, digging up cacti under the sun on a 140-degree day and stuff.

speaker: Mira
content: Those are no good folks anyway. They had it coming. Selling them off brings extra profit for us.

speaker: Mira
content: As for why this one hadn't been shipped off yet... I suppose it's because you arrived too soon, Chief. They hadn't gotten around to it.
What about Tuco? Tell me, how did you manage to make an entire town vanish overnight?

speaker: Mira
content: Oh... Haven't I told you about that already?
At your question, Mira widens her eyes and covers her mouth with her hand somewhat dramatically.

speaker: Mira
content: All the houses in Tuco were built with detachable wooden panels, with sand ships hidden underneath. They were built that way so we can pack up and vanish whenever we need to.

speaker: Mira
content: It was my friend's idea. When you're dealing with either sandstorms or desert bandits every single day, it's really quite a practical solution.

speaker: Mira
content: Oh... I must have forgotten to tell you about that. How careless of me!
Mira gives you an innocent wink, but there isn't a trace of remorse in her voice. Her dismissive attitude annoys you slightly.
I suspect there's quite a bit more you've forgotten to tell me. Would you like me to refresh your memory?
You were far more than a coerced accomplice in Tuco, Mira. At least in this incident, you were the real mastermind behind it all.
This time, Mira doesn't look surprised anymore. She merely narrows her eyes, watching you with keen interest.

speaker: Mira
content: What makes you think that?

You kept insisting that the townsfolks forced you to participate in their scam by threatening your parents' lives. But when we left, you abandoned them in the basement. Weren't you worried about what might happen to them when your betrayal came to light?

speaker: Mira
content: The IV could still last for two to three more days, and I'm the only one who knows how to operate the basement's mechanism. No one else could get in.

If that was the case, why did we leave in the first place? If the townsfolks couldn't get in, and I had already agreed to your terms, wouldn't waiting for rescue in the basement have been a safer and wiser choice?
You made the situation sound so urgent that I barely had time to think. I overlooked that, I have to admit.

speaker: Mira
content: Chief, don't forget that I took a bullet for you. If I really were the mastermind, why would the townsfolks shoot at us?
I'm afraid that's also part of your plan.
You speak coldly as you produce Mira's special power assessment report.

Your power greatly enhances your strength and reaction speed, allowing you to predict a bullet's trajectory. So when you decided to take that shot for me, you'd already made sure it wouldn't cause a critical injury.
You really went to extraordinary lengths to earn my trust with that performance.
In the brief silence, you lock eyes with Mira, waiting for her response.
Just as you expected, a moment later, Mira begins clapping slowly and lets out a soft laugh, like a cunning little fox.

speaker: Mira
content: All right, all right. Since you're already making such a bold accusation, I guess there's no point in keeping up the act anymore.
She says, giving you an approving nod.

speaker: Mira
content: Yes, the townsfolks have never threatened me with my parents. And I've never felt any disgust or weariness toward scamming for a living. As for this plan to steal the Hypercubes, I indeed played the biggest part in it.

options: Ask why she let you off

content: But that would mean you and the people of Tuco were in this together. There would have been no reason for you to escape.
So why did you change your mind and let me go? What other plans did you guys have?

speaker: Mira
content: Our only plan...

speaker: Mira
content: ...is to escape. To let the whole town of Tuco escape.
She lowers her eyes, her smile unchanged yet somehow taking on a cold edge.

speaker: Mira
content: Be grateful your position saved you from a grim fate, Chief.

speaker: Mira
content: If we'd seriously crossed someone of your status, the bigwigs of DisCity like you wouldn't have let Tuco off easily. You guys would have wiped Tuco out like brushing away a grain of sand.

speaker: Mira
content: So I changed my plan and decided to let you go, so you'd owe me a favor.

speaker: Mira
content: ...And of course, that alone wouldn't have been enough.
Mira's lips curl into a knowing smile.

speaker: Mira
content: I needed to mix lies into truth to earn your sympathy and trust, making you willingly play into my new plan.

speaker: Mira
content: Like telling you the truth about my past and my parents. Like risking my life to take that bullet for you.

speaker: Mira
content: This way, you would choose to retreat, buying time for everyone in Tuco to escape. And the heavy sandstorm that night was perfect for concealing the sand ships' tracks.
We had only known each other for less than a day then. How were you so certain I wouldn't go back to clear out the town first?

speaker: Mira
content: You wouldn't. Because you have a conscience. It's the easiest quality to spot in a person, and I saw it in you right away.
Mira is smiling cunningly again. You recall that back in Tuco, this charming lady was always one step ahead of your thoughts.

speaker: Mira
content: I tried hard, Chief, to make you believe I was gravely wounded while saving you, and that there were people in danger desperately needing those Hypercubes. That guilty conscience behind these beliefs drives your next move, stronger than any other emotion.

speaker: Mira
content: I'm truly sorry, but I did use you for my own ends.
Her smile carries an unbothered ease unusual for her young age. You can't really tell if it contains more remorse for tricking you or smugness from succeeding in doing so.
Your plan certainly worked this time. With your help, everyone in Tuco evaded our capture.
But what about next time?
Mira fixes you with an enigmatic smile.

speaker: Mira
content: Is that a threat, Chief? Just because you have me, the mastermind, under control doesn't mean Tuco will be left helpless and surrender easily. Tuco has a good leader. It's no easy prey for you.

speaker: Mira
content: Unless the leader comes to you personally, you won't find even a single trace of Tuco.
Leader? Is that the friend you mentioned earlier, the one who hid sand ships under the houses?
She answers with only a smile, clearly not intending to reveal anything more.
You remain unfazed, turning instead to the investigation report received today. It details several cases allegedly involving Tuco and the evacuation route confirmed by thorough on-site analysis.
No matter how capable this leader of yours might be, I doubt she could stand against the FAC and the MBCC alone.
Based on the evidence we've gathered, there are substantial grounds to suspect Tuco's involvement in several unsolved Hypercube smuggling cases.
Stealing strategic resources, disrupting official trade... neither of these are minor offenses.
With the FAC's force and intelligence network, it's only a matter of time before we pinpoint their location again.
Her expression freezes for a moment as she stares at the report in your hand. But she quickly regains her composure and speaks firmly, though her speech has noticeably quickened.

speaker: Mira
content: You're not going to do it, Chief. You're just bluffing.

speaker: Mira
content: The Hypercubes have been retrieved and the case is closed. You must have more important matters to attend to than pursuing a bunch of harmless small-time scammers like us.
Sorry but that's merely your own speculation.
As the Chief of Minos, I'm responsible for DisCity's safety too. Mira, perhaps you don't know me as well as you think you do.
The interrogation room falls into complete silence.
The gentle smile slowly fades from Mira's face. For the first time, you see clear hostility in her icy gaze.

speaker: Mira
content: ...By DisCity's laws, Tuco has indeed committed many crimes, and this wasn't the first time we'd scammed smugglers either.

speaker: Mira
content: But why should we play by your rules?

speaker: Mira
content: WhiteSands isn't DisCity. We don't get to live comfortably by monopolizing Hypercubes. To survive in the desert, we must become the most ruthless and powerful predator. That's the law of survival in WhiteSands.

speaker: Mira
content: Were those "victims" truly innocent? What happened to my parents wasn't an isolated incident. These desert bandits and smugglers have ruined countless lives.

speaker: Mira
content: Tuco is merely acting in self-defense. Those who commit atrocities and drive others into the dead-end of life, are the ones who should be arrested and held accountable.
She gives you a faint mocking smile.

speaker: Mira
content: Or, does the honorable and righteous DisCity only dare to prey on easy targets like us?
Ignoring her blatant provocation, you simply point to the section about the treatment of the Hypercubes in the document.
Take a look at this.

The Hypercubes that Tuco stole for its survival were also vital to other bases and shelters in WhiteSands. It looks like your self-defense might also be built on indirectly harming other innocent people.

speaker: Mira
content: But we didn't know about this before, and the smugglers are the root cause of all this. Tuco isn't the real culprit!

That doesn't change the fact that you were involved in it, and DisCity authorities cannot turn a blind eye to this. The turmoil in WhiteSands has persisted far too long with severe consequences. We will take immediate action to...

speaker: Mira
content: Enough! Save your fancy talk! I don't want to hear it!
Your condescending attitude enrages her. Mira bursts out in anger.

speaker: Mira
content: Have any of you pampered DisCity elites ever truly cared about the lives in WhiteSands?!

speaker: Mira
content: The "turmoil in Whitesands"? "Immediate action"? But the truth is you only care when your own interests are at stake!

speaker: Mira
content: And you've never done anything more than chasing the smugglers away and setting up barriers. There's never been any real arrest or control.

speaker: Mira
content: And after driving these criminals into WhiteSands, you even began targeting the ordinary people of WhiteSands who were already struggling to survive!

speaker: Mira
content: You've protected your interests, but what about us?
She glares at you with an intense gaze that carries both sorrow and disappointment.

speaker: Mira
content: ${PlayerName}, the renowned new Chief of Minos, your great achievements have reached even us in WhiteSands, and we've all been in awe.

speaker: Mira
content: A while ago, we happened to meet a young Syndican girl from Minos. She'd been through hard times too, but whenever she spoke of you, she was filled with trust and pride, as if you were the most remarkable person in the world to her.

speaker: Mira
content: That's why I thought you might be different from those condescending officials, that maybe you would understand. That's why I decided to leave with you and even entrust my parents' life to you...

speaker: Mira
content: But now I see, I was just being naive.
Mira slumps back in her chair, and silence falls over the interrogation room, just like when you had that conversation in the dark.
Mira, I'm glad you've shared your true feelings. But before you lose faith in me completely, please let me finish.
You take a deep breath and clear your throat.
I'm well aware of these problems too, which is why I've  already assigned more forces to capture these roaming desert bandits and smugglers, just a few days ago.
Do you think this will work, Mira?
The unexpected words clearly catch Mira off guard. Confusion flashes across her face before she quickly composes herself, narrowing her eyes with a mix of resignation and reproach.

speaker: Mira
content: ...Chief, I didn't take you as the type to tease. So were you just trying to get back to me by scaring me? Bravo, even I couldn't tell whether you're being serious or not.
Well, now you get a taste of your own medicine.
You set aside the Tuco investigation report and drop the playful tone, restating your stance seriously.
As a DisCity official, I must say certain correct words, as required by my job. But as you pointed out earlier, this kind of rigid correctness doesn't always apply to every situation.
It's easy to judge with an absolute right or wrong, but doing so to those struggling to survive hardships without having gone through them yourself, is nothing but arrogant and cruel.
While my duties require me to judge your actions, I agree with you that there should be a proper order of priority in how we handle this.

Compared to those struggling to survive, it's the desert bandits and smugglers who sowed this in the first place, and that should be our primary targets. This should be the true purpose of my duty to judge.
You look at Mira sitting across from you. She's lowered her head, hiding her reaction. For a moment, you can only hear her breathing in the interrogation room.

Then, she raises her head and smiles at you. It's the first time you've seen a smile carrying this kind of emotion on her face. It's pure and refreshing like a spring in the desert. You know this is a genuine smile from Mira.

speaker: Mira
content: ...Chief, I'm truly glad to hear that from you.

speaker: Mira
content: If you like, I'm willing to do whatever I can to help you catch those bastards in WhiteSands. After all, I'm one of the Bureau's Sinners now. You can find me whenever you want.
Mira's casual remark brings a long-lingering question to your mind.
Being detained by the Bureau means a certain degree of restraint. Mira, when you first planned all this, did you already consider sacrificing your freedom for the people of Tuco?

speaker: Mira
content: Sacrifice? I wouldn't really call it a sacrifice.

speaker: Mira
content: Look at how things have turned out. You caught the smuggler, retrieved the Hypercubes, and brought back this Sinner who was the "mastermind" that tried to trick you. Your mission is a huge success.

speaker: Mira
content: As for me, my parents now have access to better treatment and proper care, while everyone in Tuco managed to evade capture.

speaker: Mira
content: If I must say what I had in mind when planning this... I guess this is exactly the best win-win situation I hoped for.
Mira gives you a playful wink, seeming optimistic about her arrest and even a bit smug about how things have turned out.
You sigh inwardly. Worried that she hasn't fully grasped her situation, you decide to remind her gently.
I'm not sure if you're aware, but detained Sinners aren't free to leave the Bureau. This means you won't be able to go home, at least for now. Are you really okay with that?

speaker: Mira
content: Hmm... for those of us who grew up in the desert, home isn't necessarily a fixed place. Home is where our family is. Since my parents are in DisCity now, this can be my home too.

speaker: Mira
content: Besides, I'm not that child who could only run away crying for help anymore. Nope. Now I can thrive anywhere.

speaker: Mira
content: As for Tuco, it's not like I can never go back. I've already asked around in the Bureau. You have a parole system, right? There are quite a few Sinners who already got out.
...I see you've made yourself at home in the Bureau, getting along with everyone and keeping yourself well-informed. That's good. However, parole has special requirements that you don't meet yet.

speaker: Mira
content: Oh? Well, I'll meet them very soon.
She smiles, her tone light but inexplicably sure.
What are you plotting this time?
Your eyes narrow with suspicion, but Mira only returns your gaze innocently as she earnestly defends herself.

speaker: Mira
content: Nothing! Chief, I'll surely follow the rules and be on my best behavior in your territory. After all, I'm counting on your approval to let me visit my hometown occasionally.

speaker: Mira
content: It's just... who knows what the future holds. Things happen, right?
Her smile remains gentle and harmless, yet her thoughts beneath remain mysteriously unreadable.
Since she clearly understands her situation and has her future plotted well, there's no need to press further as long as she doesn't break any rules.
Having got the answers to all your questions, you check the time, then carefully take out something you've been carrying with you.
You carefully hand the family photo you retrieved from the basement back to Mira.
I thought this might be important to you? I brought it back with me.
Seeing her eyes light up with joy, you smile and tell her about the second surprise.

Also, I've arranged for your temporary release tomorrow, and I'll accompany you to the hospital. You haven't seen your parents since coming to DisCity, right? It'll put your mind at ease to see them in person.
Thank you. You think that's what she says in that trembling, almost choked voice.

speaker: Mira
content: I'm home! Did you miss me while I was away?
In the sunlit hospital room, Mira replaces the photo frame by her parents' bedside.
She sits down on the chair beside them, tenderly fixing her parents' hair and clothes as they lie in bed. Then, she begins with a gentle smile.

speaker: Mira
content: ...I've missed you two, so much.

speaker: Mira
content: Look, we've finally made it to DisCity, together! What a tough journey it was. But at least your wish has come true.

speaker: Mira
content: There are many trees and bustling streets everywhere. At night, the city lights shine brighter than the stars... If only you could open your eyes to see them.

speaker: Mira
content: The doctors here say they might be able to cure you. So, wake up, okay? I'm right here waiting for you, not going anywhere.
A lump rises in her throat and tears well in her eyes. Mira takes several deep breaths to force down the surge of emotions, just as she always does.

speaker: Mira
content: But don't make me wait too long... please...
She catches a glimpse of the figure waiting patiently outside the hospital room, and a smile finds its way back to her eyes before she notices.

speaker: Mira
content: Oh, and you know, I was right about that Chief. Told you, I know a good person when I see one.

speaker: Mira
content: I've always trusted my judgment, but I was still worried... What if he went back on his word and refused to bring you back? Thankfully, that didn't happen. Maybe this means I can trust him a little more?
female_content: I've always trusted my judgment, but I was still worried... What if she went back on her word and refused to bring you back? Thankfully, that didn't happen. Maybe this means I can trust her a little more?

speaker: Mira
content: I'm doing well at the MBCC under his cover. Everyone back home is doing fine too.
female_content: I'm doing well at the MBCC under her cover. Everyone back home is doing fine too.

speaker: Mira
content: He says I can visit the desert whenever I miss it. I should take him with me next time! You should've seen him when he first came to Tuco. We gave him quite a scare! But we haven't shown him real desert hospitality yet!
female_content: She says I can visit the desert whenever I miss it. I should take her with me next time! You should've seen her when she first came to Tuco. We gave her quite a scare! But we haven't shown her real desert hospitality yet!

speaker: Mira
content: I wonder if he'll sing and dance at the bonfire fest...
female_content: I wonder if she'll sing and dance with us at the bonfire fest...

content: A sudden breeze sweeps through the treetops outside the hospital window.
The leaves rustle softly, like words filled with longing from a distance, too soft to be heard, responding to the girl: They are listening.
Plant your feet there and hold onto me.
The fastener around your waist snaps tight, and you instinctively grip the person in front of you.

You struggle to find purchase on the slick surface of the sheer cliff. Unlike your companion, who clings to the wall with hawk-like agility and stability, you arduously try to push off with your feet a few times, but fail.
...Engage your core. You need to work out more.
Hang in there. We can survive this wave.
Screams wash over the area in waves, drawing closer from the distance. The darkness fills with growls and terror.

speaker: Terrified Man
content: Up ahead! The shelter is right up ahead! The key! Who's got the key?!

speaker: Weeping Woman
content: N-no idea! I think Rou... you know, that girl, had it. Where did she go?!

speaker: Terrified Man
content: **** it, first we need to survive this! Just don't let them catch us! Ahhh!!!
The person in the lead runs desperately toward the corner where you're hiding, swinging the flashlight frantically with each movement.

Behind the two people scrambling below is a tide of countless monsters with glowing red eyes. Drooling and baring their razor-sharp fangs, they tear apart anyone who falls behind. Each monster's body is contorted into an inhuman, grotesque form.

speaker: Corpse Tide
content: Grrrr... Grrrrowl!!!
In the erratic flashes of light from the chaos, you finally see your situation clearly:

Below you is a terrifying drop, with sharp rocks and mechanical traps littering the bottom. In front of you, Lysandra hangs suspended by a single rope, occasionally shifting the thin stick in her mouth. Her breathing remains steady as her calm gaze sweeps over the fleeing crowd below, locating the shelter not far away.
As for you, you're simply fastened to her body in a neat and secure fashion...
...just like a tool pouch casually strapped to her side.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Focus. Everyone else is already dead. It's just the two of us now. Control your breathing. Don't let them detect us.

speaker: Lysandra
content: We're running out of time. The shelter is just ahead...

speaker: Lysandra
content: Why are you trembling? Are you acrophobic? Just hold on to me tighter.

options: The fastener is so tight my circulation is getting cut off...

speaker: Lysandra
content: Whatever. Let's move.
You hear a countdown begin somewhere. Ten, nine, eight...

Before you can finish speaking, Lysandra's body is already in motion. She precisely locates each tiny handhold on the seemingly smooth rock face, moving up and down with fluid agility, momentarily suspended in the air before landing precisely... Through your dizzy vision and the heart-stopping weightlessness, you see the shelter drawing ever closer.
Five, four, three...

speaker: Terrified Man
content: We're almost there! The gate! Can't open the gate without the key! What do we do?!

The shelter is within arm's reach, its entrance firmly secured by solid rock on all sides. There is only a small gap at the top, filled with massive stalactites hanging from the dome like interlocking fangs...
One!

speaker: Lysandra
content: Now, duck down.

The buckle at your waist is suddenly yanked upward, and an enormous centrifugal force hurls you through the air! Through the rushing wind, you hear Lysandra's wrench whistling alongside you through the darkness, heading straight for the stalactites.

Time seems to have frozen. You open your eyes mid-air in a daze, witnessing Lysandra's wrench precisely shattering each stalactite hanging from the dome, clearing your path. The falling fragments trace the very edges of your eyelids as they narrowly miss you, one after another, like a movie scene in slow motion. You sigh, resigning yourself to fate as you close your eyes.
Bang!
Wham!!!
[Transition 2s]
[Screen brightens, view from inside the cage]
Clank... Clank...
The lights inside the shelter flicker on. Through the cage-like gate, you can see in the distance the stone entrance to the final tomb has slowly begun to open.

The Corpse Tide suddenly comes to a halt. One by one, the monsters begin lifting off their masks, revealing staff members underneath who are exhaling heavily and wiping away the sweat covering their faces.

The two players who were running for their lives moments ago collapse to the ground, nearly fainting as they wave their hands frantically. The Corpse Tide crew immediately help them up, supporting them as they walk side by side past the shelter. When they step over the mess of shattered stalactites covering the ground, they shoot nervous glances at you and Lysandra before timidly shuffling away, eager to escape the area.
Among the departing Corpse Tide, you spot a familiar silhouette bouncing playfully along with them...
Lysandra leans casually against the gate with her arms crossed, her eyes scanning the area outside.

speaker: Lysandra
content: The kid who came with us, where'd she go? What's her name again, Roulecca?
[Roulecca's portrait]
It's Roulecca who's leaving with the Corpse Tide crew. She turns around to make a silly face at you both, jumping up and waving. You can see her face is covered in sweat from all the excitement.
Yet strangely, not a single one of the Corpse Tide actors has noticed her, as if she were actually one of them.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That kid... her luck never fails her. Made it all the way here without being spotted...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Ahem, she's fine. Looks like she's found something more thrilling to do and wandered off on her own.

speaker: Lysandra
content: DisCity folks... no, Eastsiders sure are an interesting bunch.
Standing beside you, Lysandra follows your gaze in the direction where the Corpse Tide crew have gone and comments offhandedly.

speaker: Lysandra
content: This escape room thing is some kind of game, right? No money at stake. No lives at risk. Just for fun.

speaker: Lysandra
content: They live such sheltered lives that they feel the need to recreate the treacherous WhiteSands tombs for fun. But if you actually dropped them into a real WhiteSands crypt, they'd sure be wetting their pants.
She articulates her words like she doesn't care whether you're listening or how you might react.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Tsk... A few cozy days in and I've already let that kid provoke me.
You pat Lysandra on the shoulder.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Can't be helped. Roulecca's the luckiest person all of us have ever known. Nobody ever wins a bet against her.
...Well, just as you suspected, this whole situation is the result of Roulecca's elaborate scheme to get herself out of the Bureau.
[Flashback to the Bureau]

speaker: Roulecca
content: Ah!

speaker: Roulecca
content: I'm sooo bored...
Bang! Bang! Bang! Bang!
Eyes closed, Roulecca hangs upside down from the gym equipment in the Bureau's Training Room, casually firing her gun in random directions with her good arm.
The smoke clears to reveal perfect bullseye shots on the entire row of targets before her.
Roulecca opens her eyes and immediately heaves a bored sigh. As expected, every single one of the casually fired shots has found its way to the throats of the human-shaped targets.
The machines whir and the battered targets are gradually lowered while new ones rise into position. Roulecca's face is all scrunched up.

speaker: Roulecca
content: Ahhh! Sooo bored!!!

speaker: Echoes
content: Booored... ed... ed...
In the empty Training Room, only Roulecca's own echoes respond to her. She glances down and fidgets with the bandage on her hand.

A few days ago on a mission, Roulecca carelessly sprained her wrist. But fortunately, if she hadn't injured herself at that exact moment, the Corruptor's attack would likely have caused her far more serious harm.
To ensure her proper recovery, the Bureau has separated her training sessions from the others'. It's been three months now, and Roulecca hasn't seen another soul during her training hours.

speaker: Roulecca
content: Hmm? Is someone there?!
Nearby, a woman with grayish blue hair braided into a plait is doing her regular training methodically. Her arm is wrapped in bandages which tighten and loosen with each controlled movement.

speaker: Roulecca
content: That lady... that lady... Oh! I remember her!

Roulecca's first impression of her goes back to a flyer advertising a newly launched, massive escape room in Eastside with a WhiteSands Underground Tomb theme. This woman here, apparently a recent detainee in the Bureau, sneered at that flyer that got Roulecca all hyped up.

speaker: Lysandra
content: It's fake, no matter how immersive they claim it is.
A mischievous glint flashes in Roulecca's eyes as she creeps near the training woman.

speaker: Roulecca
content: Well, well, if it isn't Miss Lysandra!

speaker: Roulecca
content: Why are you training here all by yourself? Aren't you a tomb raider? Has Chief not let you out on parole to stretch your legs and do some leisure grave-robbing?
Completely ignored by Lysandra, Roulecca pouts sulkily.

speaker: Roulecca
content: Isn't it so boring to be training here? Don't you want to go do something fun with Roulecca instead?
Lysandra's training is interrupted yet again as a crumpled flyer is thrust before her eyes. Finally, she turns her attention to Roulecca.

speaker: Roulecca
content: Since you can't get out on parole yet, why not come with Roulecca to this place instead?

speaker: Roulecca
content: I overheard Chief's conversation with Adjutant Nightingale the day you arrived. They said you're an exceptionally skilled tomb raider. It's been months now, aren't you itching to get back to it?
Roulecca clutches the escape room flyer, inching closer to Lysandra with an expression that clearly says she'll keep pestering Lysandra until she agrees to go with her.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Do you have any idea what a real tomb in WhiteSands looks like? The mechanisms and traps inside can't be overcome with mere luck alone, kiddo.
Roulecca points at the flyer and edges even closer.

speaker: Roulecca
content: Really? But it says right here that besides the fixed route, there are also special lucky exits...

speaker: Roulecca
content: I've also heard people say that the tombs in WhiteSands are so deadly that those who make it out alive... must have at least a little bit of luck on their side.
Lysandra looks at Roulecca, then follows her gaze downward to find a coin wedged on the edge of her own pocket. Her brow twitches slightly as she pushes it inside.

speaker: Roulecca
content: Care to make a bet with me, Miss Tomb Raider?

speaker: Roulecca
content: Let's see which is more powerful—my luck or your skill?

speaker: Lysandra
content: ...You have no idea what you're getting yourself into.
[Scene Transition: Chief's Office]
A flyer of a recently launched escape room in Eastside is thrust into your hand.

CRAZY DEAL! The most immersive, authentic, and challenging experience now awaits you at XXX Escape Room in Eastside! Sarcophagus Rendezvous—Try our tomb raiding-themed room with a team of three or more! Group discounts available! Only 998 DisCoins if your group succeeds! Find your way out and take home the grand prize! Prizes also available for successful escapes through lucky exits!
[Roulecca's portrait and Lysandra's portrait side by side]
Since Lysandra was detained by the Bureau, this is the first time you've seen her outside of her room and the Training Room.
But... why is she with Roulecca, of all people? You notice Roulecca standing behind Lysandra with a triumphant smirk on her face, and guesses begin to form in your head.
Lysandra stands at your office doorway with her arms crossed, maintaining a calculated distance from you, her face completely expressionless.

speaker: Lysandra
content: I need to get out, to this escape room. This kid is coming with me. We need two permits.
Surprise seizes you for a moment.
Lysandra has always strictly followed the Bureau's rules for Sinners and never asked for anything in particular. This is the first time.

But then you've also barely had any chance to truly get to know this reticent Sinner. You only ever glimpse her in the Outdoor Activity Area silently gazing up at the simulated night sky on your way back to your quarters after working late.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Is something wrong?

speaker: Lysandra
content: We need to get out. We need two permits.
Lysandra seems to struggle with reading complex facial expressions on others. Noticing your silence, she simply restates her purpose, even slowing down a little deliberately.
You don't know what to feel about this.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Ah, nothing... I'm just a little surprised. This is the first time you've approached me on your own, and you're requesting to go out with Roulecca.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Both things are quite unusual, so I was taken aback for a moment.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: May I ask why?
She lets out a small oh, shifts the thin stick in her mouth and answers rather languidly.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Never been in DisCity. Never tried your escape rooms.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Haven't gone tomb raiding in ages so I'm getting an itch. Want to form a team. With three people we can get in.

speaker: Lysandra
content: That's it.

speaker: Lysandra
content: You won't lose out. Think of it as a tomb raiding job. Once we get the treas... the grand prize, you'll get a 10% cut. But you need to pitch in first.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Only 998, crazy deal.
Lysandra extends her hand to you with a deadpan expression while Roulecca frantically winks and makes faces at you.

speaker: Roulecca
content: It's a super bargain, Chief! A once-in-a-lifetime chance to go on an adventure with a real tomb raider—and not just any tomb raider, but one I've only read about in books!

speaker: Roulecca
content: Don't you want to come along too?
You grasp Lysandra's extended hand and finally manage to get back on your feet, albeit still covered in dirt.

Hoping to use this opportunity to better understand this Sinner who's been nothing but a model detainee since her arrival, you handed the permits to Lysandra and Roulecca, but only after repeatedly reminding Roulecca to be careful with her injured hand and making it clear that you must accompany them.

Up until the Corpse Tide chase, the stages were so simple that Roulecca could clear them just by randomly tapping a brick on the wall or rearranging some items. The easy challenges left Roulecca disappointed and she was throwing a tantrum about wanting to leave halfway through. Meanwhile, Lysandra kept walking behind you two indifferently.

It wasn't until you entered this thrilling stage that gradually transformed into a multi-level arena with immersive theatrical elements that Lysandra finally became more animated. Looking back, you accomplished the challenge with ease under her guidance while witnessing a side of her you'd never seen before.
Clack!
The shelter's gate swings open with the sound. The Corpse Tide is completely gone. It seems the next stage is ready.
Lysandra tightens the bandages on her hand. Before setting off again, she looks directly into your eyes with unexpected seriousness.

speaker: Lysandra
content: The MBCC's been a cozy stay. There's always food, drinks, and a warm bed waiting for me. No need to wonder where I'll wake up tomorrow, or if I'll wake up at all.

speaker: Lysandra
content: I guess I can understand now why you'd want to throw yourselves into this kind of unnecessary trouble.
Her tone remains perfectly calm, but in the dim chamber, you see her remove her goggles, revealing a pair of bright, serene eyes.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Let's do this then, Chief. I'll make sure you get your money's worth.
Without another word, she strides through the gate and heads toward the final chamber.

Watching her back, you notice how expertly she navigates the place with her professional gear and excellent instincts, advancing with steady confidence. Almost unconsciously, you find yourself following behind her with complete trust.

speaker: Lysandra
content: ...Wait.

speaker: Lysandra
content: From now on, step only where I've walked. Don't place your feet anywhere else, and don't touch anything.
Her voice flickers like the lights of the chamber.

speaker: Lysandra
content: There's indeed something big in this final chamber...

speaker: Lysandra
content: Interesting.
As you move forward, you feel wind blowing from the far end of the chamber, carrying waves of dry, scorching air. You recognize this scent. It's the unmistakable sandy smell of WhiteSands.
You furrow your brow.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...What's going on? This sandy smell...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Why does it smell like this here? How's that possible?
While carefully following Lysandra's exact path, you take out your comms device to search up this escape room, but all you can see on the screen is searching for signal.
You stand still, holding your device up at various angles and even giving it a few hopeful taps.
A moment later, it finally catches a signal after being disconnected for so long. Immediately, it vibrates rapidly with the influx of messages.
Five minutes ago.

Roulecca: Chief, here's something super exciting Roulecca has just discovered!

Roulecca: And by that I mean joining the Corpse Tide! It's sooo much fun! I just have to twist my body like they do and chase after the other players, and I can make anyone abandoned by their friends play roulette with me!

Roulecca: Oh, right! While mingling with the Corpse Tide, Roulecca overheard some super important intel! They say nobody has reached the final level since the launch! And that last stage is the real immersive, authentic, and challenging part! The owner spent tons of money creating it based on their experiences trading in WhiteSands. I'm sure Lysandra knows all about that! Roulecca: K, gotta go! Will meet you guys when I'm done having fun! Love ya, Chief!!! <3
[Turn off device]
You look up.

At the far end, Lysandra is crouching down examining something. Looking ready to proceed, she stands to face you. In the faint light from the cave entrance, all you can make out is the glint of a coin being flipped up and down, and the blurred outline of her enigmatic half-smile.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Ready for a truly nasty WhiteSands tomb, Chief?

The rubbing of the sand sounds like ancient whispers as more and more grains pelt against your body. Following Lysandra, you pass through a long, dim corridor engraved with ancient script before quickly reaching the heart of the sandstorm.

You stand speechless, frozen in awe at the sight before you—a chamber rivaling any authentic WhiteSands underground temple. Sand walls flow like liquid gold throughout the sacred space while amber firelight illuminates the dome above, pulsing like a heart.

The soft hissing of sand echoes beneath the dome, interrupted by the squeaks of strained chains like the labored breaths of some colossal beast. Your gaze drifts upward, following the firelight to what hangs directly above the temple. An enormous, rust-covered balance scale.
One side hangs empty, while the other holds an earthenware urn filled with crimson sand slowly trickling through the hole at its bottom.
...Someone built this in Eastside? Would the authorities even approve a construction project of this magnitude? Is this... is this really just an escape room puzzle meant to be solved?
You instinctively step backward, only to find nothing but empty space beneath your foot...
Lysandra grabs your arm just in time, yanking you back to the safe ground behind her while waving her tactical flashlight toward the area beside you.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Watch out. That's a deep fall.

Following the beam of light, you steady your nerves and look down. Sand storms upward from an altar at the bottom of the pit, coarse grains violently striking your cheeks, as if actively defending against your intrusion.
Lysandra reaches out, rolling the sand between her fingers as a rare gleam appears in her eyes.

speaker: Lysandra
content: It really is from WhiteSands. Interesting.
...You're not sure if it's your imagination, but she seems almost exhilarated, like an animal returning to familiar territory.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Look down. That altar beneath the balance scale was used as an execution platform by border tribes in WhiteSands centuries ago. One wrong step and there goes your head.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Back when I was raiding tombs, a few guys competing with me lost their lives to traps like this.

speaker: Lysandra
content: People have named this type of mechanism...

speaker: Lysandra
content: The Crimson Inferno.
Lysandra leans down, her warm breath brushing against your ear, her deliberately lowered voice like a demon's whisper.
You freeze for a moment, but Lysandra has already straightened up, surveying the entire temple with amusement and something like a faint smile on her face.

speaker: Lysandra
content: The owner definitely has seen a thing or two in WhiteSands and put in considerable effort here.
As she speaks, she deftly taps the rock face with a wrench, causing large chunks to immediately crumble away.

speaker: Lysandra
content: They even transported truckloads of sand and rocks from WhiteSands to build this place, perfectly replicating that loose structure that tomb explorers fear most.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Cave-ins, quicksand... We're in for quite a time, Chief.
Lysandra walks straight ahead with her arms crossed, lazily bumping her shoulder into you. Still dazed, you nearly stumble.

speaker: Lysandra
content: That altar trap is obviously a fake. It won't decapitate you, don't worry.

speaker: Lysandra
content: If you want to back out now, there's still time. I couldn't care less. There's nothing valuable here anyway.
Before you can process all this information, the passage behind you slams shut with a thunderous rumble.
The sound of the stone door sealing reverberates through your chest as a creeping sense of unease rises within you.
She glances at the door behind you and shrugs.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Looks like there's no way back now.
By the time you snap back to reality, she's already identified several footholds and gestures for you to follow.

As you follow her, you watch Lysandra, tied to ropes, gliding up and down like a spider as she explores the entire temple. Your mind drifts back to the stack of investigation reports delivered to your desk when Lysandra had just been detained.
[Flashback: Chief's Office]

*Entry I: There was a band of treasure hunters roaming the borders of WhiteSands who made a living by selling artifacts found in the ruins. Despite their own hardships, they took in homeless children in WhiteSands and taught them the necessary skills to survive in this harsh environment. *Entry II: Lysandra was one of these children. Her parents' identities cannot be traced, and the only connection that can be established to her past is this group of treasure hunters.

*Entry III: X years ago, when DisCity tightened restrictions on foreign trade, the senior hunters of the group took desperate risks to make ends meet. But fortune was not on their side and all perished in a cave-in inside a tomb. All the children disappeared as well.

*Entry IV: Beyond these details, all other information remains missing.

Of everyone in the group, only Lysandra survived. She inherited their legacy, becoming a tomb raider who'd since never come off the perilous tightrope of the trade, sustaining herself by selling ancient artifacts, until she was detained by the MBCC.
[End of flashback]
Whenever Lysandra pauses at a secure foothold, she efficiently identifies the surrounding structures and potential dangers, as if conducting a precise archaeological survey.

Remembering what she said about the Crimson Inferno, a chill runs down your spine. The real tombs of WhiteSands must be infinitely more treacherous than these chambers, where one misstep means certain death.

Your eyes follow Lysandra's practiced movements. Absolute composure and razor-sharp instincts. This is how she confronts countless terrifying traps in real tombs, driven by her quest to unearth the most unique treasures. With graceful agility, she navigates the ancient tombs of WhiteSands... Her voice suddenly breaks your contemplation.

speaker: Lysandra
content: ...I've surveyed the entire area. Besides the ventilation ducts in the dome installed by the owner, there's only one way out.

speaker: Lysandra
content: The stone walls throughout the entire temple have no gaps or cavities, so...
You remember the altar.

speaker: Lysandra
content: That altar is the exit.

With a swing of the rope, Lysandra positions herself on the far side opposite you, studying the massive balance scale that towers dozens of meters high in the center. Her voice echoes through the space, sounding near and distant at once.

speaker: Lysandra
content: We need to activate this balance scale to reach the altar.

speaker: Lysandra
content: It's a mechanism for testing precision. We'll need to calculate the rate at which the sand slips away and the timing of weight shifts on the scale.

speaker: Lysandra
content: You're lighter. You go first.
You step over the wobbly wooden planks that seem ready to collapse at any moment, reaching the edge near the balance scale.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Should I step onto it?

speaker: Lysandra
content: Yes. The moment you step on it, it will start tilting. I'll go onto the opposite side as soon as that happens and adjust my position from there.

speaker: Lysandra
content: The scale is narrow and you have no muscle strength whatsoever, so try not to fall off.
She always manages to make objective judgment sound like mockery.

You take a deep breath and jump onto the balance scale. The whole mechanism violently shakes upon impact. The sand leaking from the urn rustles as the balance's hinges creak. The grains gleam blood-red in the firelight.
The balance scale rapidly tilts toward you. You instantly lower your center of gravity and grab onto the bronze structure for stability.
Lysandra lets out a stifled snort before swinging over to join you.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Not bad. You're doing way better than in the last stage.
The next second, her gaze sharpens as she lands precisely on a spot opposite you. The balance scale tilts like a seesaw, jerking you upward, and you desperately tighten your grip.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Take three steps forward, then wait for me.
The balance scale hasn't fully stabilized, but Lysandra is already giving her instructions. You grit your teeth and struggle to maintain your balance as you move forward.
Below you lies a drop of dozens of meters. You force yourself to ignore the distracting pounding of your heart and exhale deeply.
You take three steps forward.

But the balance scale's swaying throws off your balance. In your peripheral vision, you notice a hand extended at your side. It stops at just the right distance, somehow reassuring you a great deal. Only once you've safely reached your destination does Lysandra withdraw her hand.

Meanwhile, her feet never stop moving as she keeps finding the next exact landing spot based on the rate at which the sand is leaking and your weight difference. Lysandra seems completely immune to any external distractions that might cause errors in her judgment or movements.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Good, now take two steps forward.
Now that you've become slightly used to it, you slowly straighten up and take two steps forward.
As you walk, Lysandra continuously adjusts her position in perfect response to your movements and the subtle shifts of the balance scale, maintaining an impeccable equilibrium throughout the process.
Though the balance scale's swaying gradually diminishes, the sand in the urn is nearly depleted. Lysandra still hasn't told you the next step, and you can't help but grow increasingly anxious.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Lysandra, the sand is almost all gone...
The flash of a coin being tossed and caught interrupts you. After the soft whir of metal cutting through the air, you hear Lysandra's voice, never as steady and certain before.
She grips the fallen coin, lowers her gaze, and delivers her final instruction with absolute conviction.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Okay. Now, take the final step forward.

options: Quickly take the final step forward

content: After taking the final step, both of you halt simultaneously.

The moment the perfect balance is achieved, you hear a crisp click from the hidden mechanism. The sound echoes throughout the temple, followed immediately by the grinding of gears and bearings. You know you've succeeded.
The entire balance scale begins descending slowly and steadily toward the altar at the bottom of the pit.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Phew...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: We actually did it... Smooth as a dream.
You quietly wipe the sweat from your palms and turn to look at Lysandra, who appears as casual as if she's just doing some sightseeing here.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I thought you might say something, considering we just succeeded.
Standing straight as a ramrod, Lysandra appears completely unfazed and does not even turn to look at you.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Say what?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You know... like congrats or good job. Or that we were really lucky, that sort of thing.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Lucky?
For the first time, Lysandra sounds obviously annoyed.

speaker: Lysandra
content: You think we solved that mechanism because we were lucky?
She emphasizes the last word.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Of course not. But well, I just think it's cooler to attribute it to luck after pulling off something difficult.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Like that coin in your hand. When it came to that crucial final step, that habitual flip of yours helped you confirm something, right?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Every time you have a major decision to make, you flip that coin. But you never check the result. Instead, the moment you clutch it in your hand, you act decisively.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This ritual must mean something to you, doesn't it?
[Flashback: Chief's Office]

A thin folder with just a few scattered pages tells the entire story of Lysandra's twenty-six years. The parts not yet buried by the sands, at least. From what you can see, there is nothing suspicious in her background, and her daily conduct has been satisfactory. You decide to schedule just one routine interrogation.
Just before putting the file away, you notice a photograph on the last page.

Also preserved from the sands is a photo of WhiteSands' landscape casually captured by a passing delegation. It shows a weathered bag half-buried in sand containing several dirty coins—identical to the one Lysandra now carries.
[End of flashback]
Recalling the photograph you saw in your office and that bag of old coins, your voice grows ever softer.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I think, perhaps, for you... it's some sort of lucky charm?

speaker: Lysandra
content: No, it has no meaning.
Her voice grows increasingly cold, her words forced through clenched teeth.

speaker: Lysandra
content: A coin is just a coin. It has no special meaning.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Stop this nonsense about luck. The last thing I believe in...

speaker: Lysandra
content: ...Is luck.
The change in Lysandra's tone feels unfamiliar to you. You seem to have touched on a topic she'd rather avoid.
Somewhere hidden in the bearing of a descending gear, a tiny screw that hadn't been used since the launch turns a few times after the mechanism has been activated, then suddenly comes loose.
With a soft click, the balance scale suddenly freezes in mid-air.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Wait, don't...

In the next instant, the balance scale plummets, sending sparks flying from the intersecting central tracks. The exit that has been open suddenly slams shut when a snapped pipe falls onto the other side of the balance scale, upsetting the equilibrium.
Before you can brace yourself, an overwhelming weightlessness sends you tumbling downward.
Lysandra immediately sprints toward you across the plummeting plate.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Hey! Give me your hand! Grab onto me!
As the damaged balance scale shakes the entire space, the rock faces around you begin to crack apart in rapid succession, dissolving into churning quicksand.
You reach out desperately, your fingertips nearly touching Lysandra's when suddenly the plate slams against the rock face. The impact instantly tears you away from each other—
All you can hear is a thunderous crash before tons of roaring sand surge upward and engulf you both.
[Black screen, 3 second transition]
[Flashback: Lysandra's Perspective]
Clink, clink, clink. The sound of a coin purse shaking in a hand.
One hand after another reaches into the purse to take one coin after another.

speaker: Tanned Boy
content: Everyone listen to me! Three, two, one...
Big and small hands all come together in a circle as everyone looks down at what is in the other's palms.

speaker: Scrawny Boy
content: It's Lysandra. She drew the number eight coin... How nice. We're all too unlucky...
The scrawny boy says stutteringly.
[Flashback: Lysandra's Perspective]
Clank, clank, clank. The sound of precious antiquities tumbling out of a tattered sack.
One hand after another reaches into the pile of treasures.

speaker: Veteran Tomb Raider
content: ...Lysandra, I swear, your luck is something else! How do you always manage to dig up the most valuable treasures?

speaker: Veteran Tomb Raider
content: If the other kids had even half your luck, we'd all be more than satisfied!
The old men are all gawking in surprise.
A blood-stained hand tosses the number eight coin back into the bag of old coins.
[Black Screen]
A figure jolts awake, emerging from the sand.
Not far away, someone is sinking into quicksand. Lysandra's breath catches as she scrambles to her feet and races toward the person.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Quicksand! Get out of there!

speaker: Lysandra
content: Don't just lie there!
She sprints to where a trench coat is barely visible, slides to her knees at the quicksand's edge, and grips the coat with all her strength.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Can you hear me? Don't struggle! I'll pull you out!
Thanks to her experience, the coat is sinking much more slowly now. She takes a deep breath, every muscle in her body tensing as she fights against the quicksand's pull. Sweat trickles down her face.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Hold on.

speaker: Lysandra
content: I won't let go. Don't you give up either, you hear me?
No response comes from beneath the quicksand.
Just as she's about to run out of strength, she quickly frees one hand and tightly wraps the coat's fabric around a wrench, using its weight to help overcome the inertia.

When one arm gives out, she switches to the other. Veins bulge on her forehead as fragmented images flash across her vision, yet Lysandra persists, drawing on rescue techniques from WhiteSands to maintain her grip and steadily pull back the coat.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Trust yourself, and trust me...

speaker: Lysandra
content: I can save you... I can... We're going to make it out together.
Ting-a-ling...
A faint sound comes from a nearby pile of sand.
Still catching her breath, Lysandra freezes in disbelief before slowly turning her head toward the sound.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Ly... Lysandra...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What... are you doing? Cough, cough...
The owner of the gray coat stumbles up from a nearby pile of sand, now wearing only a dust-covered Bureau uniform shirt.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Y-you're okay?!
The person gives Lysandra a weak smile, then extends a hand, clutching something.
He opens his palm.
female_content: She opens her palm.

content: It's Lysandra's coin.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Look, I have your coin now.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Guess that makes me as lucky as you are...
Seeing the tension in Lysandra, you try to lighten the mood with a casual tone. But before you can finish, she lunges forward, snatches the coin from your hand, and grabs you by the collar.
Her lips press tightly together as her reddened eyes reflect your face, while her own face is reflected in your eyes similarly.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Stop this nonsense about luck!

speaker: Lysandra
content: You think this coin could shield you from deadly cave-ins, protect you from Mania, or kill savage beasts for you?

speaker: Lysandra
content: You think it saved you?

speaker: Lysandra
content: With the luck it brought you?
Still gritting her teeth, she releases your collar, and the shackles in your hand begin to resonate with the Mania rushing through her.

speaker: Lysandra
content: You didn't survive the countless cave-ins, the Mania outbreaks, and the nasty fights with the tomb guardians because you were lucky.

speaker: Lysandra
content: But because of your careful calculation and sound judgment, because you know how to control your well-trained body and detect even the slightest changes in hostile environments. That's how you've saved your own life over and over again.

speaker: Lysandra
content: In places like this, no one has your back. No one cares whether you live or die.

speaker: Lysandra
content: And those who didn't survive didn't die because luck wasn't on their side. They simply couldn't do it!
You're this close to releasing your shackles when you suddenly realize that every time she says you, she's talking about herself.
To your surprise, the shackles in your hand gradually calm down within a few seconds. Lysandra has suppressed her own surging Mania, regaining her composed, self-controlled demeanor.
Yet her voice has never sounded so cold, frigid as a bottomless, stagnant pool.

speaker: Lysandra
content: You've read my file.

speaker: Lysandra
content: You think those geezers died of accidents, fate, or bad luck?
She slowly raises her gaze to meet yours, her eyes burning with a calm madness.

speaker: Lysandra
content: They couldn't do what I could, so they died...

speaker: Lysandra
content: That was the only cause.
You fall silent. The way she speaks, it's as if those who died weren't her friends but merely strangers.
Something must have happened, something buried in those sand-swept records. Is the story pieced together from those seemingly coherent fragments really the truth? You furrow your brow.
Standing before you amid the ruins, Lysandra looks as cold as an emotionless machine in the wild, scorching sands.
A vast distance seems to separate you, as if you're staring down from the entrance of a desert tomb at Lysandra, who once gazed up from the abyss.
The space between you fills with an oppressive silence. Lysandra tightens the bandage on her forearm and speaks first.

speaker: Lysandra
content: The balance mechanism is damaged. We need to find the equilibrium once more to reopen the altar exit.

Lysandra gives you a quick glance before leaping onto the massive balance scale. She pulls out her climbing rope, secures it overhead, and scans the area for anything heavy enough to reactivate the mechanism.
After searching for a moment, her eyes lock on the ventilation duct above.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Let's do it together.

speaker: Lysandra
content: No need. Stand back. I don't want it falling on you.

With that, Lysandra steadily begins her ascent, carefully testing each handhold on the partially collapsed wall to find sections solid enough to bear her weight as she climbs toward the ventilation duct.
Chief! Lysandra! Here I come!
Clank! The ventilation cover on the dome is suddenly kicked loose.

The heavy metal cover crashes onto the balance scale with a thunderous thud. The plate slowly sinks down before finally settling into some sort of equilibrium, triggering the altar exit mechanism. Just like that, a path opens up.
And of course, the only person who can open up the exit with zero skills and pure luck is...

speaker: Roulecca
content: Hiya! I knew you guys would be here! Oof!
Looking up, you see Roulecca perched at the edge of the ventilation duct, legs dangling playfully as she grins down at you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Roulecca, how did you get up there?

speaker: Roulecca
content: That so-called lucky route was super boring! The ventilation duct maze was way more fun! Then I heard you two making all this noise in here and thought maybe you found something cool to do without counting me in, so I came to check it out!

speaker: Roulecca
content: But looks like you've already solved the puzzle? Must be because Roulecca's brought you luck!

speaker: Roulecca
content: Hmm! Next time I should just tag along with you guys. I bet Chief's knack for getting into trouble will make a place like this ten times more exciting!
Having solved the final chamber, you exit through the doorway. Roulecca bounces off excitedly to claim her coveted prize, while Lysandra silently brushes past the two of you.
While Roulecca cheers jubilantly, you watch as Lysandra rewraps the bandage that has come loose from her earlier exertions in a restrained and precise manner.
It's as if she's collecting all the emotions she just displayed, carefully folding them away, and now... she's determined to lock them up again.
She leaves the chamber without looking back. You watch her solitary figure disappear as your own expression turns complicated.
This is the first time you've met Lysandra after that nerve-wracking but ultimately harmless escape room adventure.
Though it's been only two days, and Nightingale has already swiftly delivered the additional materials you requested, somehow you still feel that time has been passing exceptionally slowly.
Lysandra, meanwhile, has lost the composed demeanor she displayed when first detained by the Bureau, looking restless and distracted.
The clearest sign being that since entering the interrogation room, she's been constantly shifting the thin stick in her mouth, and the coin she usually fidgets with is notably missing from her hand.
You organize the documents in your hands, preparing to begin the interrogation.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Since N.F. 114, there have been a series of artifact thefts along the border between WhiteSands and DisCity. Our investigation has determined that all the trafficking routes can be traced back to a single source.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This individual has committed multiple offenses in unregulated zones throughout WhiteSands, including unauthorized entry into archaeological sites, artifact smuggling, and illegal reselling.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That person is you, isn't it, Lysandra?

speaker: Lysandra
