content: Correct. Thought I could feed the living with what the dead no longer needed.
She glances away as she answers casually.

speaker: Lysandra
content: I have the skills to extract those things the dead have no use for, turning them into food and shelter for the living. They gain new value rather than just rotting beside corpses as worthless junk.

speaker: Lysandra
content: The dead never complain, so I don't see why not.
You produce one of the photos from your new file. It's an ancient tomb the MBCC has tracked down which contains Lysandra's traces. The interior has been completely ransacked.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: During your excavations, you only ever took the most valuable treasures.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You were turning sites filled with invaluable historical records and precious artifacts into ruins, making it impossible for scholars to study the evolution of civilizations.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Furthermore, evidence of your method can be clearly seen at the edges of the tomb. You've caused extensive destruction.

speaker: Lysandra
content: First, timing and opportunity are key in tomb raiding. Any excess weight that restricts movement can mean death for a tomb raider. That's why I only select the most valuable treasures to bring with me.

speaker: Lysandra
content: I've seen plenty of greedy tomb raiders who tried to take everything. It only cost every single one of them their lives.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Second, I destroy my traces for my own safety. Once I discover a tomb location, others will swarm in like flies, all wanting their share of the spoils.
Lysandra sits up straight.

speaker: Lysandra
content: I must say, your people have got keen eyes to have identified me despite that level of destruction.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It's thanks to our Mania detector. We picked up traces of your Mania in that area.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Mania detector...

speaker: Lysandra
content: Heh, I see, some fancy gadget those of us in WhiteSands would never know about.
You don't miss the momentary flicker in Lysandra's eyes.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That covers the basic information. Now, let's discuss other matters.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: First of all, thank you. I know if that game had been real, I would've already died in that quicksand without you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm surrounded by so many extraordinary people, including those like Roulecca who are naturally blessed with exceptional luck. Getting help from them feels like good fortune simply falling into my lap.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But I know there are hidden struggles and painful pasts behind all this, things they'd rather not mention. The luck I experience is only the surface of the story.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So... I'd like to understand you better, to learn about the struggles that shaped you. If you're willing to share.
You close the dossier and quietly observe Lysandra, who has been cooperative throughout. She returns your gaze, the corner of her mouth curling slightly in a composed smile.

speaker: Lysandra
content: I'm not much of a talker, but ask and I'll answer.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: OK.
Your eyes meet hers as you begin carefully.
You take out the coin engraved with the number eight and place it in front of Lysandra.
Her eyes dart away as you slowly push the coin toward her. When her breathing noticeably shallows, you stop considerately.
She pauses, then speaks calmly after a few seconds, as if the brief agitation has just been your imagination.

speaker: Lysandra
content: The coin belonged to the geezers. A keepsake of some sort they left behind.

speaker: Lysandra
content: After they died, I took one. That's all.
She answers your question, but only in the most technical sense.

speaker: Lysandra
content: A gang of tomb raiders from WhiteSands who scraped by looting ancient ruins. Same job I do now.

speaker: Lysandra
content: When they traveled around, they'd take in orphans they came across. I was one of them.

speaker: Lysandra
content: I survived on the jobs they gave me, and it was always feast or famine.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Eventually they went into a tomb and never came out. After that, I was on my own.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What about the other children who were with you?

speaker: Lysandra
content: I don't know.
She gives a quick answer and shuts her mouth. Until now, she's only been telling you what you already know.
Her response now is markedly different from how she handled your questions about the artifact thefts earlier. She knows what you want to know. She just doesn't want to say it.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Let's cut to the chase, Lysandra.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The file I initially received about you contained only a few pages. Based on these pieces, the average person would piece together your story like this:

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: A poor orphan was taken in by a group of WhiteSands tomb raiders and grew up happily alongside other children. But to survive, the aging raiders had to take up a risky job and ended up all perishing in a cave-in. Only you, the lucky one, survived.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: They were the only family you had, the mentors who taught you how to survive, and an eternal memory...
You point at the coin worn to a shine.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But that's not how the story really goes, is it?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No, I mean, maybe it did start that way...
You produce another document. You can feel Lysandra's body tense.

speaker: Lysandra
content: How much do you know?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're clever and careful enough. Just as you erase your tracks in tombs, you've also removed quite a bit of evidence of your story.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But when the MBCC wants to know something, nothing escapes us.

speaker: Lysandra
content: What are you trying to s...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: They didn't die in a cave-in, did they?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: At the entrance of the ancient tomb where they disappeared, we found evidence of your sabotage, Lysandra.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It carried your Mania, the highest M-Value we've ever recorded from you in all our investigations and tests.
You pause for a few seconds.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: They didn't die in a cave-in...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You killed them, Lysandra.
After a silent moment similar to the one you shared in the escape room, you hear a soft laugh.

speaker: Lysandra
content: ...Of course they didn't die in a cave-in.

speaker: Lysandra
content: It was just...

speaker: Lysandra
content: Bad luck.
Her eyes trace the coin in front of her before she looks up at you with a mocking smile.
(Flashback)

speaker: Scrawny Boy
content: ...Lysandra, hey, they're getting impatient about the drawing. Everyone's waiting for you!

speaker: Scrawny Boy
content: Wake up! Old Fernando found a water source. Whoever volunteers to go down into the tomb gets a jar of water... Cough, cough, I'm so thirsty... but...

speaker: Scrawny Boy
content: But I don't want to end up unlucky like Noah and Jacob, who went in and never came back.
The scrawny boy stands with a limp, his hands clasped against his chest as he wipes snot and tears from his face with his arm.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Miguel, your leg...

speaker: Miguel
content: I didn't clean up their dishes yesterday fast enough... so they beat me.

speaker: Miguel
content: If Noah and Jacob couldn't make it back even with their healthy bodies, I'm totally doomed...

The sandy wind picks up, burying Miguel's sobs. Hot grains sting their faces, blurring their vision as Lysandra weakly rises to her feet. From the distant edge of the rock, where rare patches of shade offer respite, comes the cursing of the old bastards.

speaker: Rough Shouting Voice
content: Get over here, you useless things! Come now or I'll send both of you down to scout that tomb today!

speaker: Lysandra
content: Don't be afraid. Let's go.
[Beside the rock]

speaker: Tanned Boy
content: Everyone listen to me! Three, two, one...
Miguel's hands tremble as he turns over the coin. Number eight. He's doomed.
A hand swiftly grabs the number eight coin from him, swapping it with another. Miguel nearly cries out in shock.

speaker: Tanned Boy
content: Who has the number eight coin... Number eight... Phew, it's Lysandra.
Lysandra stands expressionless, opening her palm to reveal the coin engraved with the number eight.

speaker: Miguel
content: It's Lysandra. She drew the number eight coin... How nice. We're all too unlucky...
As Miguel stammers through his words, Old Fernando cracks the whip in his hand. The sound of it ripping the air makes every child present tremble with fear.

speaker: Old Fernando
content: Hurry up! Who drew the number eight coin? Step forward now.

speaker: Old Fernando
content: Ah, it's you, Lysandra.

He swirls the battered flask in his hand. Lysandra's lips are cracked from dryness, her clothes are in tatters, and her face is covered in sand. Hearing the sound of water sloshing inside the flask, she involuntarily swallows, her throat burning like fire.
Old Fernando bares his teeth, satisfied with her reaction. He tosses a dagger and an old rope at her, then points behind himself.

speaker: Old Fernando
content: Let's see if today's your lucky day.
[Flashback to the interrogation room]
Lysandra reaches out and picks up the coin, examining it as if seeing it for the first time.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Let me think, where to begin... Let's start with those old bastards who took in the orphans so benevolently.

speaker: Lysandra
content: They scoured WhiteSands for homeless orphans, taking in anyone who was still breathing. Then they turned us into their expendable scouts.

speaker: Lysandra
content: They made them draw coins to decide which child would enter the tombs as their scout each day. If one died, they'd simply move on to the next one.

speaker: Lysandra
content: They called it... testing their luck.
You feel a knot form in your stomach.

speaker: Lysandra
content: In WhiteSands, power belongs to whoever controls the supplies. With food and water at their disposal, they could make the rules about who lived and who died.

speaker: Lysandra
content: The children who died were simply dismissed as having bad luck. After a night's sleep, the children would wake to face another day worrying whether they'd be lucky enough to survive.

speaker: Lysandra
content: And something as intangible as luck only bred deeper fear.
She fiddles with the coin between her fingertips. Under the harsh ceiling light of the interrogation room, it appears lusterless.

speaker: Lysandra
content: We lived each day in terror, fearing that fifty percent chance. Every day of survival felt like it had been pried from the tight grasp of luck itself.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Miguel's leg had been badly beaten the night before. If he had been selected to enter the tomb, it would have been death for him.

speaker: Lysandra
content: So that day I went into the tomb in Miguel's place. And that's when the cave-in happened.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Folks in WhiteSands all know that hardly anyone has ever survived a cave-in...

speaker: Lysandra
content: But I did, and I brought back the most valuable treasure from that tomb.
You recall her tension in the escape room when she thought you had been swallowed by quicksand, the trembling she tried to hide beneath her calm exterior.
You've personally experienced the dangers of tomb raiding in the escape room. An actual WhiteSands tomb would only present a far more extreme survival challenge beyond imagination.

options: That's why back in the escape room...

content: Remembering how she nearly lost her composure in the escape room, Lysandra awkwardly shifts the thin stick in her mouth, her eyes darting away as she speaks in a subdued voice.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Your big city sure has the craziest technology. Even fake things are made to seem so real.

speaker: Lysandra
content: After all, experiences like this will never feel just like a game for me.
She leans back in the interrogation room chair and flips her coin into the air.

speaker: Lysandra
content: The game of the coin was a game of life and death. So, why would you call it a lucky charm?

speaker: Lysandra
content: This coin that almost got me killed in the tombs countless times?
She snatches the falling coin in one swift motion, the corners of her mouth curling into a widening smile that contains not a trace of joy.

speaker: Lysandra
content: I survived with my knowledge of WhiteSands, with what I remembered from what those geezers said about the tombs every day, with the skills to escape quicksand and locate solid sandstone structures during scouting. It was all me.

speaker: Lysandra
content: But those geezers...

speaker: Lysandra
content: They said it was only because I was lucky.
The smile fades from her face. You watch her, feeling a complex mix of emotions yourself.

speaker: Lysandra
content: How ridiculous.

speaker: Lysandra
content: The moment I climbed out, I knew that my life was in my hands alone.

speaker: Lysandra
content: By relying on myself alone, I could become someone who changed the rules—who made the rules. I could truly gain the power to fight back.
She casually tosses the coin onto the desk and looks directly into your eyes, her piercing gaze seeming to cut right through you.

speaker: Lysandra
content: As I became more skilled, I obtained more resources from them, which meant the children received more from me.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Because of me, they survived safely and no longer lived in constant fear. I gradually took control of the situation.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Eventually, I got better and better, quietly memorizing everything they ever showed me. Scouting tombs, identifying treasures, gathering intel, finding contacts, negotiating deals.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Funnily enough...
Her lips twist into a bitter smile.

speaker: Lysandra
content: I actually began to enjoy the process.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And then, you became infected with Mania...
She smiles sardonically again.

speaker: Lysandra
content: After the trade restrictions got stricter, on a completely ordinary day, they discovered another tomb, one that was ancient and lethal.

speaker: Lysandra
content: As usual, I volunteered to go. No one objected.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So, that tomb expedition was what got them killed?
She answers without hesitation.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Yes. That was also when I got infected with Mania. When I emerged carrying the most valuable treasures they'd ever seen, those geezers couldn't believe their eyes.
(Flashback)
Clank, clank, clank. The sound of precious antiquities tumbling out of a tattered sack.
One hand after another reaches into the pile of treasures.

speaker: Old Fernando
content: ...Lysandra, I swear, your luck is something else! How do you always manage to dig up the most valuable treasures?

speaker: Old Fernando
content: If the other kids had even half your luck, we'd all be more than satisfied!
A blood-stained hand tosses the number eight coin back into the bag of old coins.
Seeing Lysandra covered in wounds, her body marked with strange patterns, electric sparks constantly crackling from her hands, the old men's eyes grew wider and wider with shock.

speaker: Then I'll make you spit out everything you've devoured.
content: Wait, wait a second... You went into that tomb and came out a Sinner?! The beasts down there can't kill you anymore, can they?!

speaker: Old Fernando
content: Wow, it's just unbelievable... Talk about hitting the jackpot!
As if struck by an idea, Old Fernando's expression morphs from terror to greed. He begins kicking the children on the ground, shoving them toward the entrance of the ancient tomb.

speaker: Old Fernando
content: You lot, and you over there, get up now, you worthless wretches!

speaker: Old Fernando
content: Move it! All of you, get down in that tomb now!
Lysandra stands panting, the Mania still swirling visibly around her body. A wrench in her scarred hand, she positions herself between them and the terrified, trembling kids.

speaker: Lysandra
content: What... what are you doing?!

speaker: Lysandra
content: I've already been down there! There's Mania in there! Why would you send them down there too?!
Old Fernando, the leader, greedily licks his lips, revealing a gleaming gold tooth.

speaker: Old Fernando
content: Once they're all infected with Mania like you, we'll have more profit-making tools at our disposal!

speaker: Old Fernando
content: Look at how much stronger and more powerful you got! Imagine how many treasures you can dig out now!
He smacks his lips as his face contorts into a menacing grimace.

speaker: Old Fernando
content: You've always volunteered to go down into tombs just to protect them. You're valuable with your treasure-hunting skills. I'll give you that. That's why we've turned a blind eye to your little hero act until now.

speaker: Old Fernando
content: But today, you don't get a say anymore! Supplies are already scarce, so it'll only solve our problem if some of them end up dying. And if they're lucky like you and survive Mania, they'll be even more useful to us...
He advances menacingly, forcing Lysandra and the children to back up until they're nearly at the edge of the tomb pit.

speaker: Old Fernando
content: All of you, get down there now! Argh!!
The wrench strikes his skull with resolute, devastating force.
[End of flashback]

In this cruel game of luck, Lysandra finally took matters into her own hands, ending this insane system. She refused to tolerate the dark side of humanity any longer, completely reclaiming control over her own destiny.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Just like that, I disposed of them, pushed them into the tomb, and erased any trace of my involvement by staging it as a cave-in.

speaker: Lysandra
content: I only took this coin with me... as a reminder to never trust fate in those moments when I'll face the unknown and must make a decision.

speaker: Lysandra
content: To just trust myself.
She says emphatically, concluding her story.
The interrogation is nearly over as you sort through the documents in your hand, alongside everything she's just told you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You've told me everything about your past and what happened to those old raiders. While I can't condone your methods, I wasn't in your position, so I can't easily judge what was right or wrong.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But if I had been under those same circumstances, I think I would have shared your idea.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Breaking free from the game of life or death dictated by luck, and instead making your own rules. That is what it means to trust in yourself and take your fate into your own hands.
Your words momentarily catch her off guard. Then, the corner of her mouth turns up slightly, as if a heavy burden has just been lifted from her shoulders.

speaker: Lysandra
content: ...Thank you.
Yet throughout her entire account, she seems to have deliberately avoided one seemingly insignificant detail.
As she's about to leave the interrogation room, you call out, stopping her in her tracks.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I still have one last question.

options: What happened to those children in the end?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Throughout your entire story, you've left out one seemingly insignificant detail...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What happened to those kids in the end?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: After you got rid of those old raiders, whenever the children's whereabouts came up, you either claimed you didn't know or deliberately changed the subject.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm curious. If you went as far as abolishing the rules of luck to protect them, surely you'd care about what happened to them afterward.
A heavy silence falls. The briefly lightened atmosphere now feels even more suffocating.
You wait quietly. You know Lysandra will give you an answer.

Perhaps it's the determined way she guided you through that escape room, the brief panic in her eyes when you fell from the balance scale, or how she refused to let you go when you were sinking into the quicksand.
It's the trust she's built with you during that escape room challenge. You just know that even though she might try to avoid the topic or ignore her own feelings, she will ultimately answer you.
She finally speaks, her face hidden in shadow, her voice painfully hoarse.

speaker: Lysandra
content: I don't know.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Why?
Another strained, uncomfortable silence.

speaker: Lysandra
content: ...After I took out those bastards, I let the children go.

speaker: Lysandra
content: I gave them all the money I had and everything else I'd gathered. Told them to get as far away as possible and never come back.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Then?
You study her intently, but she keeps her lips tightly pressed together, refusing to meet your eyes.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Lysandra, what do you fear?
Something suddenly clicks for her. She lurches forward, staring directly into your eyes.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Why do you keep asking about where they went... Did you find them? Are they still alive?

speaker: Lysandra
content: They're not dead, are they?
Before you can even answer, Lysandra takes a deep breath, her hand trembling as she tightens her grip on the coin, and interrupts you.

speaker: Lysandra
content: No, don't answer me.

speaker: Lysandra
content: ...They could barely buy any food or water in WhiteSands with the scraps I gave them. Miguel and Yulen had always been sickly... they couldn't have survived long.

speaker: Lysandra
content: They couldn't have survived at all...
Lysandra falls silent.

She finally recalls that moment she thought had already been lost in her memory. The farewell beneath the blood-red moon. All those pairs of mournful eyes. That instant which still cuts through her heart every time she flips her coin.

She took back control over the children's lives from those old raiders, only to repeat their cruelty after her impulsive action left her unable to establish a new shelter for them. That game of luck she once sneered at played a cruel joke on Lysandra in the end.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Hah... In that final moment, I told them to... try their luck. To see how long they could survive on their own.

speaker: Lysandra
content: I was just like those old bastards. I did the same thing... I left those barely clothed children alone to fend for themselves.
Lysandra stares helplessly at the coin, her eyes trembling with anguish.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Listen, Lysandra.
You approach her, leaning down to meet her troubled gaze directly.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I know you did your best back then.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You already did what you could to protect them... You destroyed that cruel system under those harsh circumstances.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I know, in WhiteSands, you couldn't all survive with the meager resources you had.
You gently guide her gaze away from the coin, directing her attention to you instead.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're good at calculating the odds of success and failure, right? In that situation, you must have done the same. You weighed the two options: everyone dying together, or you surviving while giving others a chance to find their own path to survival.

It is precisely because she always relies on these meticulous calculations that she has spent countless sleepless nights rethinking which choice would have given them the better chance of survival. Yet the endless calculations have never truly convinced her, because she continues to blame herself for one thing—that she chose to leave it all to luck in that crucial moment.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You did your best, Lysandra.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You did everything you could.
You repeat these words over and over, your voice growing softer each time, trying to soothe Lysandra as she collapses under the weight of guilt and self-blame.

You believe in her, just as you did in that escape room. You know she'll once again work through her pain, confusion, and anxiety, allowing her usual analytical mind to return, once again finding back the Lysandra who refuses to leave it up to fate.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You need to accept that... there are things you can't do.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: We can't control everything, every twist and turn of our stories. Even if we remain perfectly calm and cautious and calculate every possibility, it's still impossible to take responsibility for others' fates when making a decision.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Don't let your pride get to you, Lysandra.

Lysandra slowly draws her unfocused gaze back from the shadows and fixes her eyes on your face, like a machine receiving commands for the first time after a complete shutdown from suppressing its emotions for too long.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You know better than anyone that one should always rely on oneself and control one's own fate...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So what makes you think the children shouldn't do the same? Isn't that exactly what you wanted to teach them?
You smile at her.

speaker: Lysandra
content: What...
Her eyelashes flutter as she seems to be analyzing the meaning behind your smile.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I investigated. They all survived, every single one of them.

speaker: Lysandra
content: They... all survived?
The light slowly returns to her lifeless eyes as you watch her quietly, offering your silent support.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: They all survived, every single one of them.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Took the MBCC some effort to look into that. But fortunately, the results were good. Miguel became an apprentice in a merchant caravan. Yulen works as a guard at a DisCity border station, and then there's Logan...
You lay out evidence of their updates one by one as Lysandra examines each photo with disbelief, carefully identifying their appearances.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You saved them, Lysandra. Just as you saved me in that escape room.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What truly protected me and allowed me to wake up in the end wasn't luck.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But that you remembered to secure my rope in the last moment so that I could dodge the overturning balance scale, and your voice calling out to me...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That got me back on my feet.
She slowly sits down.

Your words wind their way into the depths of her heart, gently loosening the knot of guilt and self-blame she's carried for so long. At last, the light returns to Lysandra's eyes as she looks at the photos before her and smiles faintly.

She imprisoned herself in that night when, left with no other choices, she had to betray her own belief and rely on luck. And ever since then, she's forbidden herself from forgetting, forcing herself to remember by flipping the coin over and over again.
Lysandra shifts slightly, the corner of her mouth lifting in a relieved smile.

speaker: Lysandra
content: ...Even though I couldn't catch you when you fell?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It was only an escape room.
You shrug, like she does all the time. When she genuinely smiles, a tiny dimple appears at the corner of her mouth. It vanishes so quickly that you wonder if you imagined it.

speaker: Lysandra
content: I'll accept that there are things I can't do, but that won't stop me from giving my best shot...

speaker: Lysandra
content: Is that enough?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Yes, that's enough.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Don't be so hard on yourself.
You pick up the coin and place it back in her palm. Her skin is warm, the metal connecting your shared warmth.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You don't need the coin to remind yourself what you must accomplish. You've already accomplished all your decisions with your efforts.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You are stronger than fate, destiny, or luck could ever be.
[Exiting Interrogation Room - Scene Transition]
A few days later...
After processing the final approval for shutting down that new escape room in Eastside, you close your eyes, feeling somewhat exhausted.

You recall the multiple reports you've submitted to your superiors requesting leniency for Sinner Lysandra's crimes, along with the numerous attempts of vouching for her personally. With the outcome still uncertain, you can't help but worry.
Someone knocks on your window frame, interrupting your thoughts. You turn to look.
The person yanks your window open, then leans against the frame with crossed arms, fiddling with a thin stick with her lips.
Before you can identify who it is, Roulecca bumps that figure aside and pops up energetically.

speaker: Roulecca
content: Hey, hey! Caught by Roulecca again! Lysandra, you've been hanging around Chief's office an awful lot lately...

speaker: Roulecca
content: Are you planning to sneak out again? Hey, you're not allowed to go out and have fun without Roulecca!
[Lysandra's portrait]

speaker: Lysandra
content: Of course not.

speaker: Lysandra
content: I came to invite Chief to another escape room. I heard a new one just opened.

speaker: Roulecca
content: Huh? Another escape room? Count me out then. I thought about it. With Roulecca's talent, solving those dead people's puzzles is only gonna get more boring.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Perfect. You can just stay at the MBCC and nurse your injury, kid.

speaker: Roulecca
content: Heyyy! Chief, I've changed my mind! Roulecca wants to go with you after all, and crush those puzzles with my luck before Lysandra gets to show off!

speaker: Lysandra
content: I don't mind. As long as he's okay with it.
female_content: I don't mind. As long as she's okay with it.

content: As Roulecca keeps protesting, you notice Lysandra staring at you quietly.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Yes?

speaker: Lysandra
content: Why not settle this with a little game?
She looks at you like she's discovering an uncharted ruin that's mysterious, dangerous, and irresistibly tempting to Lysandra the tomb raider.
Ting-a-ling...
A familiar coin is flipped high into the air before your eyes and falls back down.
But this time, instead of clutching it in her palm as usual, she presses the coin on the back of her other hand, covering it.
The two of you exchange a smile.

speaker: Lysandra
content: Take a guess, Chief. Heads or tails?
You stand on the deck of the sand ship, the dry winds of WhiteSands howling past your ears. In the distance, sand waves surge and roll, revealing faint black shadows within them.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: This is the sand ship we've been talking about.
You take the binoculars he hands you, twist the focusing knob, and watch as the blurry silhouette gradually sharpens into focus.
It's larger than ordinary sand ships, with a sharper bow. A prominent emblem is painted on its hull.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: You should be able to see that emblem on the hull. That's the insignia of DisCorps.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Judging by its model, this ship was likely used by DisCity's military forces during the Outland War and earned distinguished achievements on the battlefield.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: This model of sand ship should have been completely decommissioned twenty years ago. And yet, here it is, roaming WhiteSands.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: The FAC has sent teams to approach it multiple times, but during these encounters, we discovered they likely possessed Mania weapons. That's why we requested the MBCC's assistance.
Not far from you, an FAC soldier stands at the bow, directing the loading of artillery shells.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Could this ship be smuggling Mania weapons?
As you're pondering this, something in your sight begins to move slowly.
You adjust the focus again, trying to locate whatever caught your attention in the view.
Meanwhile, an unsettling feeling of being watched slowly rises within you.
The pitch-black barrel of a cannon points directly at you, as if staring back into your eyes.
[Screen violently shakes with cannon blast sound]

speaker: FAC Captain
content: EVERYBODY HIT THE DECK!!!
The binoculars are jolted from your hands and crash to the deck. The massive shock wave leaves you dizzy and disoriented.
You struggle to steady yourself, barely managing to focus your vision, only to see the FAC soldier who was standing at the bow now dangling from the ship's edge, about to fall at any moment.
You grit your teeth, stagger to your feet, and lunge toward the soldier.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I've got you! Watch out!
The ship shakes violently again, instantly numbing your entire arm. Your grip on the ship's edge is about to give way.
In the final moment, you use all your remaining strength to fling the soldier back onto the deck, only for the momentum to throw you overboard.
The shouts behind you gradually fade away as a gale of sandy wind blasts against your face, filling your mouth and nostrils with grains.
You plunge into WhiteSands.
[Scene Change]
Zulu Zulu! You're awake!
A voice reaches your ears, muffled as if filtering through a drum skin. You struggle to open your eyes, immediately wincing as bright light stabs at your vision.
Can you stand up?
A hand is extended in front of you.
Still dazed from just regaining consciousness, you instinctively reach out and take the hand. It is slender yet strong, yanking you to your feet in one swift motion.
But your legs are still weak and you stagger, nearly falling over. A pair of shoulders quickly braces against you, holding you firmly upright.
Take it easy. No rush.
Only now do you clearly see that the person supporting you is a girl who looks barely into her teens.
This is the Ark. I'm the captain of this ship. Call me Ark.
You raise an eyebrow. This girl who looks barely of age calls herself the captain. Besides, she's carrying what appears to be... an arm cannon?
What catches your attention even more is the girl's name and voice. You can't shake the feeling that they're somehow familiar, but...
Your thoughts are interrupted as Ark's hands begin fumbling about your body. You flinch in surprise and jerk backward.

speaker: Ark
content: Hold still! I'm checking if you have any other injuries.
She bounces energetically around you, patting your face one moment, tugging at your arms the next, and finally gives your shoulder a confirming tap.

speaker: Ark
content: Looks like you're still in one piece. Zulu Zulu!
She gives your arm a gentle pat.

speaker: Ark
content: In any case, you should get some proper rest first. We've prepared a cabin for you. Come with me.
As she speaks, she turns to look at a tall man standing behind her. He's staring at you intently.

speaker: Ark
content: Samuel, keep an eye on things while I'm busy. This passage is particularly treacherous.

speaker: Samuel
content: ...Understood.
You suddenly notice the small crowd standing behind Ark, eyeing you with caution.
The group consists of people of all ages and genders, but apart from the tall man, everyone else appears somewhat frail.
They wear the distinctive body paint and beads of WhiteSands natives. More than an ordinary sand ship, this looks more like... a cruising refugee camp?

speaker: Old Man
content: Ark...
An elderly man from the front of the crowd takes a few steps toward you both. There's something strange about his gait. Your eyes are drawn to his right leg... which is in fact a wooden staff.
He frowns, casting quick glances at you while muttering something in a WhiteSands dialect you can barely understand. Not compliments, that's for sure.
A young boy and a woman step forward as well, talking rapidly and gradually more loudly until they're nearly arguing. Ark smiles through it all, seemingly trying to reassure them about something.

speaker: Old Man
content: Hey!
The elderly man suddenly points a finger at you and speaks in broken Disian.

speaker: Old Man
content: I warn you...

speaker: Ark
content: That's enough! You're scaring our guest, Amir.
Ark interrupts him, gives your hand a gentle squeeze, and looks at you with a warm smile.

speaker: Ark
content: It's okay. Come with me now!
[Scene Change]
You follow Ark down into the ship's corridor, deliberately slowing your pace to fall behind her. You seize the moment to slip a hand into your pocket and send your coordinates to the FAC.

speaker: Ark
content: I'll have Samuel bring you something to eat in a bit. Yeah, that big guy from earlier... Hey, what's wrong?
She asks and quickly returns to your side.

speaker: Ark
content: Are you alright? Can you still walk?
She raises her hand to touch your forehead, and you nimbly remove your hand from your pocket to stop her. Your movement is smooth, and Ark seems to pay no special attention to it.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm fine... I'm just a slow walker.

speaker: Ark
content: Well... you sure look like one! And yet you still dared to wander around WhiteSands. By the way, I haven't asked yet. How did you end up knocked out in the sands?

You study the WhiteSands-esque face paint on her cheeks and remind yourself how little you know about this ship named the Ark. Erring on the side of caution, you quickly fabricate a harmless identity for yourself.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm a merchant. Was unlucky enough to run into some desert bandits on the way, and well...

speaker: Ark
content: Desert bandits?! How dare they operate in these parts when the Ark is right here?!

speaker: Ark
content: We just chased a bandit ship away a couple days ago! Zulu Zulu!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Oh? Is the Ark a patrol ship?

speaker: Ark
content: She's actually a rescue ship. Whenever we enter a new area, we broadcast survival hacks with our coordinates so that anyone in need who hears it can come find us for help.

speaker: Ark
content: Of course, that means bandits will always find a way to us. When they dare show up, we make sure they regret it!
The words survival hacks suddenly awaken a long-forgotten memory in you. Without thinking, you blurt out.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Lizards are highly nutritious. Remove the innards, cut off the head and tail, then roast them for a satisfyingly crispy texture. Alternatively, they can also be made into a stew...

speaker: Ark
content: ... Just close your eyes, and it'll taste no different than chicken soup.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That was you!
Your face contorts as you shake your head.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Lizard meat tastes nothing like chicken, for the record.
Ark places her hands on her hips indignantly.

speaker: Ark
content: But it is indeed a nutritious ingredient, isn't it? That part is true, at least!
You look at each other and burst into laughter almost simultaneously.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I once caught some messages from you guys. Back then... they helped me a great deal. Thank you.

speaker: Ark
content: Don't mention it! Just doing our best to help.

Your thoughts drift back to that dark, humid lighthouse, and you can almost hear the crackling static of the radio again, soothing you. Ark helped you once back then, and now she's doing it a second time.
Looking at her radiant smile, a thought suddenly crosses your mind: Perhaps she could help you a third time, by helping you find that mysterious warship?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So, I basically got robbed clean by those desert bandits. I wonder if I'll ever get my things back... You said your ship regularly patrols this area. Have you perhaps seen the bandit ship I'm talking about?

speaker: Ark
content: You want your stuff back? Leave it to us! But words alone are not enough leads. There are more ships in WhiteSands than clouds in the sky. I have no idea which one you're talking about...

speaker: Ark
content: Oh, right! We have plenty of photos of other sand ships we've encountered in the control room. Why don't you come with me and take a look?
[Scene Change]
You arrive at the control room. Ark jogs over to the panel and immediately starts digging through a cluttered pile of documents and photographs.
Instead of hurrying after her, you take this opportunity to survey the sand ship's control room.
To your surprise, the Ark's control room is fully equipped, with perfectly arranged instruments and terminals, comparable even to some of the FAC's most active sand ships.
Your attention is drawn to a wall covered with photos. At the same time, Ark excitedly holds up a photo she's found.

speaker: Ark
content: Could this be the one you're talking about? We've run into it before, but it got away! This ship has cannons too...
The wall is decorated with photos of various sand ships. Among them is one with an austere silhouette, a razor-sharp bow, and a faded DisCorps emblem on its hull.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That's the one.
Ark looks up at your words. She's still holding a picture in her hand as she glances with confusion at the photo wall in front of you.

speaker: Ark
content: ...That one?

speaker: Ark
content: Are you saying this is the ship that attacked you?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Yes. You've run into it too?
Ark continues to stare at that photo with a bewildered expression, as if still processing what you've said. In a serious tone, you begin warning her.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: There is something very hostile about this ship. Were you attacked when you encountered them? They might be equipped with Mania weapons...
Ark blinks several times before finally snapping out of it.

speaker: Ark
content: Um, no...

speaker: Ark
content: Because that's...

speaker: Ark
content: A photo of the Ark.
Slowly, she gathers the photos in her hand and places them on the desk beside her.

speaker: Ark
content: Are you from DisCity? What's your relationship with those FAC guys?
You don't answer, immediately glancing toward the door. But Ark has already moved to block your way out.

speaker: Ark
content: You won't talk. I see.
She touches a hand to her shoulder and stretches her body.

speaker: Ark
content: As I just said, the Ark is a rescue ship, but we also run into our fair share of ill-intentioned strangers. We get them out of danger, only for them to turn on us and try to seize our ship...
You hear a strange mechanical noise.

speaker: Ark
content: But they're not that hard to deal with. All you need to do is just...
She raises her arm slowly, aiming the pitch-black barrel of her arm cannon somewhere beneath your feet.

speaker: Ark
content: Send them all to hell!!!
Before you realize what's happening, you feel hot air searing your ear. The next second, a charred pit has already appeared in the floor next to where you stand.
The hem of your trench coat is slightly singed. Fragments of fabric twirl in the air before slowly falling to the ground.
Ark smiles maliciously, aiming her arm cannon at you directly this time as she advances with unhurried steps.
Your back presses against the cold wall.
There's nowhere else to go.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm not trying to take your ship, I...
The floor trembles with Ark's every step as she closes in on you. The light between you dwindles.

speaker: Ark
content: Too bad the Ark's cannon didn't blow you up sooner, you DisCity thief. But don't worry...

speaker: Ark
content: My cannon can do the job just as well!
The next shot lands just shy of your head, sending another blast of searing air past your ear. Sparks are sprayed onto one side of your face, burning so hot that you can't keep your eyes open.

Before the rush of relief can hit you, Ark suddenly charges forward, driving her elbow directly into your cheekbone. Your vision instantly goes dark, your knees buckle, and you collapse to the ground.
With what little consciousness remains, you crawl away, trying to put as much distance as possible between you and her, desperately fighting for your survival.
Ark turns around, peering down at you. Along with her gaze, you feel the weight of Mania energy surging from her body.
She's... a Sinner.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Cough... cough...
You stagger to your feet, grabbing the nearby desk covered in documents to steady yourself as you regain your balance.
Ark narrows her eyes, studying the desk you're using for support. Decisively, she raises her fist and charges straight at you.

Your body reacts before your mind can. You instinctively dodge sideways, but your chest slams into her shoulder. As sharp pain shoots through your head, you manage to flip up your hand and grab her wrist.
If you could just get the shackles on her, you might be able to restrain her temporarily.
A pair of hands seizes your collar from behind and slams you against the wall. You hear the sickening crack of your own bones before collapsing limply to the floor, overcome by excruciating pain.
Chaotic footsteps surround you. Before you can even lift your head, something presses down on your back with overwhelming force, rendering you completely immobile.
Doesn't feel like a foot... More like a wooden staff.

speaker: Amir
content: Abu, give me a hand here!

speaker: Abu
content: Ughhh... What do we do now?

speaker: Amir
content: Now we tie the intruder up.
Someone opens a nearby fire safety box and pulls out a length of rope, winding it around you in tight circles.
The open door now faces you, swinging back and forth while its metal hinges creak. The emblem painted on its surface has faded.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That's... the insignia of DisCorps!

speaker: Amir
content: Don't let him turn around!
female_content: Don't let her turn around!

content: [Screen violently shakes with impact sound effect]

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So... I ended up in the right place after all.
This is your final thought before you black out again.
[Black Screen Transition]
You wake up to a throbbing pain at the back of your head. You try to focus, but there's only darkness before your eyes. The air is tinged with the smell of rotting wood.
You blink.
[Blank Screen]
You blink again, harder this time.
[Blank Screen]
You can't tell if you've been blinded during the earlier confrontation or if you're simply sitting in pitch darkness. The only thing you know for certain is that you've been tied up.
The sailors must know a thing or two about knots. The twine binding you is fastened perfectly, just tight enough to prevent escape, but not overly so as to cut off circulation to your arms.
You twist your body and inch forward until your forehead touches cold, hard metal. Turning your head, you press your cheek against it, trying to feel its shape and position.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: A cage...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Looks like I'm not the first person who's been here.
There's no immediate way to escape. You decide to use this moment to comb through what you already know.

You're now on the old warship you are to investigate. It's occupied by WhiteSands dwellers who are intensely hostile to outsiders, and there's also a Sinner among them. Though they claim to be rescuers, given your current predicament, perhaps you shouldn't believe their words.
But... lying here now, you remember days spent in similar darkness when you clutched a radio, waiting to hear Ark's voice. You want to believe her.
If you had another chance to talk with Ark, could things take a turn for the better?
There's also a last resort. Waiting for the FAC to rescue you. But considering Ark and her crew's attitude... things would no doubt get ugly.
[Door opening sound + Scene Change]
The sudden brightness stings your eyes, but you have no free hands to shield them.
Well, at least now you can confirm there's nothing wrong with your eyesight.
A tall figure appears in the doorway, approaching you step by step. It's Samuel.
He opens the cage, tosses a bowl in front of you, then quickly locks it again. As if you could possibly crawl out in those few seconds. As the bowl hits the ground, you catch the scent of food.
You shift your shoulders slightly.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: How am I supposed to eat this?

speaker: Samuel
content: You don't need hands to eat. Just bow your head. Or you can choose to starve yourself to death. Makes no difference to me.
He speaks in fluent Disian, the words pronounced flawlessly.
A DisCity native on this ship? Your mind races with possibilities: Could he be a captive like you? Or perhaps he's somehow connected to the ship's origins?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Are you from DisCity?
Samuel raises an eyebrow.

speaker: Samuel
content: So what if I am? Don't try to get friendly with me.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Just a bit surprising is all. She kept calling me a DisCity thief earlier. I thought she had something against us.

speaker: Samuel
content: We didn't lock you up because you're from DisCity. You're a dog who belongs to the FAC, FCA, whatever it's called. Am I right?
You remain silent. Samuel lets out a contemptuous snort.

speaker: Samuel
content: I figured as much. I already told Ark that your appearance near our ship at this exact time was just too convenient.

speaker: Samuel
content: Don't try to drive a wedge between us. It won't work. Besides, she's half Disian herself. I mean, she's... an immigrant. Her parents...
Suddenly realizing he's said too much, Samuel cuts himself off, and awkwardly licks his lips.
His boots shift on the floor with a few creaks, suggesting his exit.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Are you really from DisCity? And you don't know about the FAC?
He stops in his tracks, then stomps several paces toward you, clearly fuming.

speaker: Samuel
content: Am I really from DisCity?! When I left that place, this FAC thing didn't even exist yet!

speaker: Samuel
content: A few years back, I met another punk like you, who said he'd escaped from some place called Syndicate. I asked where that shithole was, and he laughed at me and called me a fake.

speaker: Samuel
content: I was already hustling in West District before that kid's dad even thought of making that stupid mistake!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So you're from West District? I'm quite familiar with that area myself...
Samuel shuts you up with a dismissive wave of his hand.

speaker: Samuel
content: Don't wanna hear it. That punk already told me West District is now controlled by gangs and thugs. It's no longer a place for decent folks.
His head dips slightly and his voice grows lower.

speaker: Samuel
content: Just let me remember West District as it once was.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Well, then I've got some good news for you. Syndicate is now known as West District again.

So you share what you know about West District, recounting everything from the Black Ring eruption to the abolition of the West District Order Management Regulations, and the changes in the streets. Samuel gradually becomes entranced, leaning against the wall. In the dim light, you notice his eyes slowly softening.
When you finish, he finally smiles faintly and shakes his head.

speaker: Samuel
content: Alright, I've heard enough. If you keep going, I'll start remembering things from my childhood.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: There's nothing wrong with reminiscing. Why don't you go back and see it for yourself sometime?
You shift your shoulders toward him again.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It's not like you're all tied up like me.
Samuel lets out a wry laugh and shakes his head.

speaker: Samuel
content: I was a deserter, to put it simply. I was only a teenager when I left DisCity, and that was... decades ago.

speaker: Samuel
content: Who knows how many people I once knew are still alive? Even if they are, who would even remember me?

speaker: Samuel
content: Now, the Ark is my home. My commanding officer sent me to die, but the Ark saved me.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I understand. But no matter how you look at it, life in WhiteSands is less stable than life in DisCity.
Samuel doesn't respond. You gesture with your chin toward the suspicious fluid in the bowl before you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Is this stuff only served to captives like me, or does everyone on the ship eat it?
Samuel remains silent. You let out a sigh.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This is your captain's specialty, right? Lizard stew...

speaker: Samuel
content: ... Just close your eyes, and it'll taste no different than chicken soup.
Samuel smiles and shakes his head.

speaker: Samuel
content: Things haven't been good lately. We just weathered a sandstorm, and now we're constantly being harassed by DisCity warships, with no chance to dock anywhere...

speaker: Samuel
content: This is the only food we've left. Ark told me to bring you some. She doesn't want anyone starving to death on our ship. After all, we're a rescue ship.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I was nearly blasted to pieces on this rescue ship of yours just a while ago.

speaker: Samuel
content: If Ark had really wanted to kill you, you'd have been roasted and tossed overboard to feed the sand beasts already.

speaker: Samuel
content: She tends to lose her temper when it comes to threats to our ship. She has indeed hurt hijackers before, but afterward she would be too guilty to sleep.

speaker: Samuel
content: But if you ask me, I wouldn't hesitate to feed those people to sand beasts.

speaker: Samuel
content: We've run into too many of those ******* bastards. If it weren't for Ark, we'd all have died several times over by now. Hmph. It wouldn't be the first time.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What has happened on this ship?
Samuel's lips twitch, like he wants to speak but then thinks better of it. Finally, he just gives you a sidelong glance and sneers.

speaker: Samuel
content: There have been far too many like you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Since you were once a DisCity soldier, you should understand better than anyone. This is a DisCorps warship, and I'm only here to conduct an official investigation. I have no intention of seizing your ship.

speaker: Samuel
content: So you're some big shot, huh?

speaker: Samuel
content: But we couldn't care less about you and what kind of warship the Ark used to be. I've spent most of my life on this ship and I've watched over Ark since she was born. This ship means more than our lives, and no one can take her away.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What you really want, is it this ship itself, or a home?
After a moment of silence, a heavy sigh comes from above.

speaker: Samuel
content: Without this ship, where would our home even be?
Then, the floor creaks, and soon you're plunged back into boundless darkness.
As he opens the door, you call out to stop him.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What do you think of DisCity?
[Black Screen]
After Samuel is gone, you're once again enveloped in darkness, eventually drifting into sleep. You have no idea how much time has passed when a piercing alarm jolts you awake.
[Alarm sound effect + visual effect]

speaker: Impatient Crew Member
content: Hurry up! It's those damn warships again!

speaker: Agitated Crew Member
content: ****! Again? Ain't they got nothing better to do?!
Chaotic footsteps rush past your door, then fade away. You hold your breath, waiting patiently until the alarm finally stops and silence returns around you.
Just as the familiar darkness surrounds you again, you hear something metallic scraping faintly outside the door.
[Blank Screen + Door Opening & Footstep Sound Effects]
The lock on your cage clicks open and falls down. Samuel is standing before you.

speaker: Samuel
content: Hurry! Your people say they're going to open fire!
He nervously glances over his shoulder while shoving a tool into your hands for you to cut the rope.
[Scene Change]
Chaos erupts across the deck. Crew members crowd around the gunwale, arguing heatedly. Out in the sands, several DisCity warships have completely surrounded them.
Ark rushes over. The moment the crew members spot her, they immediately wave her over.

But she doesn't even need to get close to know it's those stubborn DisCity warships again. Ever since they arrived in this region and caught DisCity's attention, people have been trying to board their ship every other day with different excuses, demanding they return the Ark.
This time, however, those Disians aren't just circling around them like flies—they've started buzzing like them too.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Hand over the hostage immediately! Or else...
All their main cannons are trained on the Ark, poised to fire.

speaker: Amir
content: They came out of nowhere! Our cannons aren't even warmed up yet. We're outgunned now...
On the opposing deck, a uniformed officer lowers his hand.

speaker: FAC Captain
content: Ready!
The cannon muzzles rotate, rumbling thunderously.
But Ark just smiles. She tilts her head slightly, gently reassuring the crew member beside her.

speaker: Ark
content: Don't worry. Leave it all to me.
She raises her hand calmly.
With an ear-splitting boom, the opposing warship's main cannons launch instantly, spitting flames into the sky.
Mania energy radiates from her, spreading rapidly across the deck. The Ark vibrates in response, as if coming alive, all cannon muzzles firing in perfect unison.
[Blank Screen + Screen Shakes]
Artillery shells land beside the FAC sand ship, kicking up massive sand waves that nearly capsize the vessel. The soldiers aboard desperately cling to the railings to keep their balance.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Stop it!
Your voice suddenly rings out. Ark's back stiffens with a jolt.

speaker: Ark
content: So you want to die!
Ark whips around, her arm cannon already raised and aimed directly at you.
But when she finally sees what's happening, her voice nearly cracks.

speaker: Ark
content: Samuel?!
The tip of your wire cutter is pressed against Samuel's throat, flashing blindingly in the sunlight.

speaker: Ark
content: You, you...

speaker: Ark
content: You Disian scum... Let him go! Or I'll kill you right now!

Ark charges at you like a lioness, roaring with rage. You can hardly believe such a furious sound is coming from such a small, thin frame. The deck beneath your feet rumbles ominously, as if the Ark herself shares her captain's fury toward you.
You quickly drag Samuel backward, retreating several steps.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Freeze! One more step and he's dead.
Ark immediately comes to a halt, glaring at you furiously, her weapon still raised and aimed at you.

speaker: Ark
content: You dare threaten me on my ship?!

speaker: Ark
content: You think this stunt will get you off my ship safely? Dream on!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Do exactly as I say, and we'll all walk away from this safely.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Listen carefully. I need you to come with me to DisCity. You and your crew won't be harmed. Otherwise...
You turn the metal pliers in your hand slowly, making sure she sees how the sharp tip could pierce through Samuel's throat.
Ark's eyes widen in fear, the color draining from her face. You feel a twinge of guilt, but you know this is no time for mercy.

speaker: Ark
content: Why the hell should I trust you?!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You can choose to trust me and come along, or we can find out which is faster: your cannon, or...
You tighten your grip, cutting a small incision on Samuel's neck. Bright red drops of blood trickle down his throat. He shudders violently but remains silent, eyes squeezed shut.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Well? Want to gamble with his life?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Make your choice, Ark. How much longer he can hold on is entirely up to you.
Her eyes dart back and forth between your face and Samuel's before finally fixing on you with an intense stare.
Her hands slowly clench into fists, knuckles turning white from the pressure.
After a brief silence, she finally speaks with a trembling voice.

speaker: Ark
content: ...Okay.

speaker: Ark
content: You win. I'll go with you.
[Scene Change]
The night before
What do you think of DisCity?

speaker: Samuel
content: Are you inviting us to rot in a DisCity prison cell?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No, I want to help you. If I can confirm you pose no threat to others, I'll convince the DisCity authorities to grant you protection. The Ark might even be allowed to stay. I just need Ark to come with me. But I promise, I won't harm her.

speaker: Samuel
content: Wow. Just what kind of big-time position do you hold in DisCity? Does the entire city obey your orders?
You let out a sigh.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That's not far from the truth. And that's why if I were to go missing, the FAC wouldn't let you off so easily.

speaker: Samuel
content: ...Are you threatening me?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm merely stating a fact.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: To defend the ship, Ark would probably launch some suicidal attack on them. Though you may not be familiar with the FAC, you must realize that if you were to clash with DisCity's armed forces, you wouldn't stand a chance.
His eyes flashed at the mention of Ark's name. He approached slowly, raised his hand, then slammed his fist against your cage.
You remain unfazed, lifting your head to stare directly into his eyes.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I contacted the FAC as soon as I boarded the ship. The rescue team will arrive within twenty-four hours.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: When that time comes, the choice will be in your hands.
You enter the interrogation room carrying a thick folder filled with every scrap of information you could find about the Ark.
Ark fixes her gaze on you, her eyes like a wounded beast.

speaker: Ark
content: I swear, if you dare harm a single one of them...

speaker: Ark
content: I'll reduce this whole place to rubble, even if I have to go down with you!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I give you my word: your crew will remain perfectly safe, as long as they don't initiate any conflicts.
Ark lets out a cold snort.

speaker: Ark
content: Why should I believe you?

speaker: Ark
content: You held my crew member to threaten me, and now you're telling me you'll protect them? Do you take me for a complete idiot?!

Sighing, you take out your device, and call the FAC unit in WhiteSands. The interrogation room suddenly fills with a commotion. You turn the screen toward her, on which the crew of the Ark are standing by the gunwale, hurling insults at the FAC soldiers.
Ark freezes in surprise, then tries to snatch the device from your hand, but you swiftly slip it back into your pocket.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: See? They're doing fine.
Ark's shoulders relax slightly, but a trace of indignation still lingers on her face as she eyes you suspiciously.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You'll be reunited with them soon enough. I just need to get some information from you first.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The Ark is actually a DisCity warship from the Outland War era. Although this model has long been decommissioned, it still remains DisCity public property.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Not only have you taken possession of the Ark, but according to reports from other sand ships, you frequently use it to attack...
Ark's fist slams down hard on the armrest of her chair, cutting you off.

speaker: Ark
content: Attack other sand ships?! Those despicable vultures are the ones trying to steal the Ark for themselves, just like you!

speaker: Ark
content: And taking possession of public property? That's nonsense! The Ark is my home, where I was born and raised...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So this ship had been drifting in WhiteSands before you were born. Who was the ship's original captain, then?
The moment you ask this question, Ark immediately bites her lip and lowers her head, avoiding your gaze.
You both face each other in tense silence for a moment. Finally, you sigh and open your folder.
test
test
test
test
test
test

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Alisa and Rudolf were once senior researchers at DisCorps's research institute. They led the design and construction of the DXVI-type cruiser. They were considered DisCity's most brilliant engineers—until they defected.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Records from the institute show they were last seen at the DisCorps shipyard. That same year, the prototype of the DXVI cruiser also disappeared.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And this missing warship, our investigation confirms, is the Ark.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Do these two names sound familiar to you?

As your words hang in the air, the atmosphere in the interrogation room turns suffocating. Ark doesn't look at you. The silence stretches so long that you begin to wonder if she even understood your question.
Suddenly, she begins shaking her head, over and over, then speaks in almost stubborn denial.

speaker: Ark
content: No, no... The Ark is our home...

speaker: Ark
content: The Ark is no warship...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I understand. You all feel deeply connected to the Ark.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But life in WhiteSands is relentless. Sandstorms, desert bandits, and what you probably hate most, annoying Disians like us...

speaker: Ark
content: I don't hate Disians.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Right. Samuel mentioned that to me. You can be considered a Disian yourself, right?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Haven't you ever thought about returning to DisCity?

speaker: Ark
content: You and Samuel are in cahoots, aren't you? You bribed him with the promise of returning to DisCity.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: How did you figure that out?

speaker: Ark
content: Samuel is our best fighter. I've faced you in combat before. There's no way you could have subdued him.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Yet despite knowing this, you still agreed to come with me for his sake.

speaker: Ark
content: What else could I have done? Let you slit his throat?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I wouldn't have done that. I never intended to harm any of your crew members.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But now that you know he colluded with me, aren't you angry with him?
Both her tone and her gaze finally begin to soften.

speaker: Ark
content: He's been on this ship for so long. I know he just wanted a peaceful life when he first joined us. If he wants to return to his roots, to go back to DisCity... then so be it.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What about you?

speaker: Ark
content: My parents died in WhiteSands long ago. DisCity means nothing to me.
Her voice sounds distant, yet carries a hint of wistfulness.

speaker: Ark
content: Those two people you mentioned... they were my parents.
[Scene Change]

speaker: Rudolf
content: Hey! Ark, careful, don't touch that!
In the bridge, the man swiftly scooped Ark up as she reached for the control panel.

speaker: Ark
content: But you and Mom both said I'm the captain of the Ark!

speaker: Rudolf
content: When you grow up! Once you're older, you can truly become the captain and lead rescue missions in our place.
Ahead, the figures on the shore grew clearer.

speaker: Ark
content: Dad, can I go ashore with you later? Those people sounded so helpless on the radio just now. I want to come help them too.

speaker: Rudolf
content: Sure thing, our little captain. But the sun is about to set, so you'll need to bundle up. Where's that hat Granny Savana knitted for you?

speaker: Ark
content: This hat's too big. Granny said she'll have to readjust it.
Bursting into laughter, the man shook out the wrinkled hat Ark just pulled from her pocket, and plopped it on her head crookedly.
The hat slides down, covering one of her eyes. Ark giggles.
[Scene Change + Screen Shakes]

Granny Savana had once told her that at her future coming-of-age ceremony, she would personally paint beautiful patterns on Ark's face. After that, Ark would be recognized as a true and proud child of WhiteSands.

She clutched the elderly woman's ice-cold hand, its fingertips having just traced beneath her eye, the fresh crimson perfectly covering her wound. It felt almost like the coming-of-age ceremony she had longed for, if only she could ignore the metallic scent of blood.
The very people they had come to rescue were now patrolling the sand ship that didn't belong to them with arms in their hands.
A pair of feet stopped in front of her. She looked up in confusion. A strange man was staring down at her, axe in hand.

speaker: Ark
content: You've got it all wrong... We came to rescue you, to save you...
The man didn't even bother with the axe. He simply kicked her aside. As she fell to the ground, she found herself staring into her father's lifeless eyes.
In the next instant, her mother rushed over and wrapped her in a tight embrace.

speaker: Ark
content: Didn't we come to rescue them? What did we do wrong? Why...

speaker: Alisa
content: We did nothing wrong. We came to save people, and that's never a wrong thing to do, it's just...

speaker: Alisa
content: Ahhh!!!

speaker: Ark
content: Mom?... Mom... Mom!
Her heart ached unbearably, as if burning along with the flames before her. The deck rumbled beneath her feet, groaning mournfully.

speaker: Burly Bandit
content: Is she the one crying?

speaker: Gaunt Bandit
content: Yeah. Let's finish her off and be done with it.

speaker: Ark
content: ...I want you all dead.

speaker: Ark
content: You ungrateful bastards...

speaker: Ark
content: I want all of you dead!!!
[Screen Shakes + Black Screen Transition]
A hand rested on her shoulder. She trembled slightly.

speaker: Ark
content: Samuel, tell me, am I a true and proud child of WhiteSands now?
Samuel turned his head, looking at the bodies scattered across the deck. After a long silence, he finally spoke in a low voice.

speaker: Samuel
content: ...Look what the ship has become. Perhaps it's time we find a place to settle down for good.

speaker: Ark
content: No... no. We can't stop yet... The Ark can't stop yet.

speaker: Ark
content: My parents' wish... they can no longer fulfill it themselves...
Blood had dried on her face. She slowly rose to her feet.

speaker: Ark
content: Then I'll do it for them!
[Scene Change]

speaker: Ark
content: The Ark... the Ark isn't a warship. Mom and Dad weren't traitors either... All they wanted... was just to save people...
Ark's chest heaves. She clenches her teeth tightly, her eyes glistening.

speaker: Ark
content: Call me a brute or thug. Say whatever you want. The fact is, when it comes to protecting the Ark and everyone on board, you're right, there's nothing I won't do!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I remember. I remember how fiercely you fought to protect them.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That crew member's name was Aisha, wasn't it?
Ark's body stiffens at the mention of the name, her pupils quivering slightly.

speaker: Ark
content: You heard how those bastards killed Aisha... Do you still think what I did was wrong?
Her lips tremble uncontrollably, her voice somewhat indignant.
You shake your head.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: At the time, I wasn't thinking about what was right or wrong. I only thought: This radio station helped me survive the storm, so I wanted them to live on too.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What I wished for even more was that they could protect what they cherished and find the peace they truly longed for.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Not fighting a lonely, perpetual battle, always covered in wounds.
Your eyes fall on the scars hidden beneath the face paint on Ark's cheeks, then slowly move upward to meet her gaze.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So I'd like to propose a different solution, one that can bring peace without using violence. I will offer permanent sanctuary in DisCity to every crew member of the Ark.

speaker: Ark
content: And what are you asking... in return?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: In return, I ask that the Ark continue its original mission. I want you to keep on leading it to help others in need.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And I will provide you with a shipyard.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Because I was once rescued by the Ark myself. In my heart, it's never been a warship.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I know that from its creation, it was never designed for warfare.

You pull a sheet of paper from your file and hand it to her. It's the original blueprint for the DXVI model. In this initial design, where cannons now sit, there are only row after row of rescue ladders.
Ark looks down, her fingers tracing over the familiar handwriting on the paper. The same hands once taught her to read, write, and protect others. She lets out a soft laugh.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So, will you give me a chance? ...Captain.
Her shoulders shift slightly, as if she's about to reach out her hand.
[Blank Screen + Alarm]
Hurried footsteps approach from a distance. The interrogation room door swings open, and you immediately stand up.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, the Ark has just broken through the FAC fleet's blockade and is about to charge into DisCity.
[Scene Change]

speaker: FAC Captain
content: This is your final warning! Stop immediately! Or suffer the consequences!
On WhiteSands, the Ark advances toward DisCity with a line of FAC vessels trailing it.
At the stern of the Ark, an elderly man is vehemently hurling insults at the FAC ships.

speaker: Amir
content: Give Ark back, or get the hell out of our way!

speaker: Abu
content: The cannons... won't heat up. What do we do...
Hearing this, the old man bends down and tosses his wooden prosthetic at Abu.

speaker: Amir
content: You useless fool! When have you ever done anything right?!

speaker: Abu
content: Don't... don't be angry, sir. Here, your leg...
As your boat draws closer, the arguing voices become increasingly clear.
On the deck of the Ark, crew members anxiously watch your approach. When you are close enough for them to make out your faces, their eyes suddenly widen in shock.

speaker: Amir
content: ...Ark?! Finally... Finally!
Without a moment's hesitation, they leap onto your boat one after another, rushing toward you. Their sudden boarding causes your small vessel to rock unstably.
Someone lunges forward with an outstretched hand, nearly grabbing Ark, but FAC soldiers quickly step between them.

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: Step back!
In the midst of the chaos, a familiar tall figure pushes to the front of the crowd, raising both hands in an attempt to calm everyone's anger.

speaker: Samuel
content: For our safety, let's not resist them...

speaker: Amir
content: Oh shut it!
The old man punches Samuel square in the face. Samuel staggers several steps backward, clutching his bleeding lip.
He shakes the blood off his knuckles, then pulls a handgun from his waist.

speaker: Amir
content: I'll show them what this old man can do!
The next second, Amir chambers a round. The soldiers immediately lunge to seize the gun. In the ensuing chaos, the barrel swings toward the crowd.

speaker: Samuel
content: ****, watch where you're pointing that gun! No!!!
[Blank Screen + Gunshot Sound Effect]

speaker: FAC Soldier
content: Chief!
For a second, your entire left arm feels numb, then intense pain hits you. Looking down at the wound, you see bright red blood rapidly soaking through your sleeve.
The crew member you shielded instinctively pushes you away, then stares in horror at the blood. He reaches out hesitantly, unsure whether he should touch you.
You struggle to your feet, swaying unsteadily. Scorching blood streams down your arm, turning thick and cold by the time it reaches your fingertips.
But at least that's quieted them down.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I know you've been fighting thieves and bandits throughout your journey. I know you've lost loved ones along the way... I've heard your stories myself.
Your vision blurs, but you take a deep breath, force yourself to stand straighter, and continue speaking in a more confident and sincere tone.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I didn't come here to take anything away from you or destroy your home.

Some crew members furrow their brows while others slowly lower their heads. You scan the faces on deck, finally resting your gaze on Ark, who stands at a distance with a conflicted expression. Your tone softens slightly.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I've come here to make you a promise: DisCity will grant you permanent protection.
As you speak, your eyes drift to your blood-soaked left arm.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Even though I was nearly torn to pieces back when I first set foot on the Ark...
Someone on deck shifts slightly, and the tense atmosphere begins to loosen a bit.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But the Ark did offer me the help I needed. That's why I won't take the ship away. On the contrary, I want it to continue sailing the WhiteSands.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...If only for my own sake, as someone who once received your help.
Suddenly, your vision goes black and you collapse forward uncontrollably. The young crew member you saved earlier steps forward and catches you with both hands.

speaker: Young Crew Member
content: Stop talking for now...
The remaining crew members exchange uncertain glances, suddenly unsure how to respond to this situation.
Silence blankets the deck, broken only by the soft patter of dry wind against the hull.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I hope... you'll consider my proposal.
Just as your words fade, a thunderous boom erupts nearby.
[Blank Screen + Sound Effect]

speaker: Abu
content: R-r-ready to fire!!!

speaker: Amir
content: ****! Hold on! Don't fire!
He drops his gun, rushes to the bow, and frantically waves both arms at the Ark.

speaker: Amir
content: For ****'s sake! Stop firing! Stop it!
The cannon barrel seems to be breathing slowly, and you can almost feel its temperature rising.
[Blank Screen + Footsteps]
You sense Ark's presence behind you.

speaker: Ark
content: Don't be afraid.
She moves past you, her slender frame now standing in front of you. She doesn't look at you, her gaze fixed steadily on the Ark.
She raises her arm toward the Ark, extending her hand with slightly trembling fingertips, as if bearing some immense, invisible pressure.
Hot air rushes this way, blowing back her sleeves and turning her exposed skin red.
But she doesn't stop, simply pushing her hand forward another inch, defying the scorching heat of the cannon barrel.

speaker: Ark
content: She just...

speaker: Ark
content: ...needs a little more time to remember.
The cannon muzzle pointing directly at you finally begins to slow down. The machinery emits noises of friction as the rotating parts pause momentarily.
She turns her palm downward, patting rhythmically as if soothing a small beast. The sand ship before you obediently submits to Ark's touch, gradually slowing to a halt and gently lowering itself.
Silence reigns again. Only the sound of the wind remains.
Ark gazes at it with soft eyes.

speaker: Ark
content: This is how she's supposed to be. When I first saw her on shore, she was just like this.

Many years ago, when she was still small enough to ride on her father's shoulders, she stepped onto land for the first time. Turning back, she saw the ship where she was born and raised for the first time.
