She had no idea that in the distant DisCity, they called her the Scythe, because her razor-sharp bow had harvested countless enemy lives.
Each of these individual lives became merely a part of an enormous figure, ultimately simplified as a glorious achievement in history.
But all she saw was the Ark outlined in gold by the setting sun. Her family and friends leaned against the railings, waving to them from the deck.

speaker: Voice in the Memory
content: I'm going to sail this ship and rescue lots and lots of people, bringing everyone safely aboard our ship.

speaker: Voice in the Memory
content: I'll make sure everyone in WhiteSands knows they can come to us whenever they're in trouble!
Her eyes shine bright, and her tone is firm.

speaker: Ark
content: The Ark has never ever been a warship.
Metal clanks and hits the deck. The crew wordlessly lower their weapons, watching as their captain walks slowly toward you.
She lifts her head and stands tall, extending her hands to you. These same hands have both helped you up and fought against you in the past.
But now, they want to hold yours.

speaker: Ark
content: As captain of the Ark, I accept your proposal on behalf of my crew.
Your hands clasp together. The sun shines over your shoulders, casting shadows before you.
[Scene Change]
Ark's slender fingers work the bandage deftly, carefully wrapping it around your wound. When she applies pressure, a sharp pain makes you wince and draw in a quick breath.

speaker: Ark
content: Did I press too hard? Just bear with it for a moment.

speaker: Ark
content: It's the only way to help it heal faster.
She coos, like she's comforting a child. You watch her concentrated profile as bright sunlight streams through the porthole, illuminating her youthful face. You can't help but smile.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Yes, Captain.
Abu rushes in frantically with a copper bowl in his hands, spilling some of the broth onto the floor.

speaker: Abu
content: Grub's up! Watch out, it's pipin' hot!
When you finally make out what's in the bowl, you press your hand to your forehead and sigh miserably.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I was just freed from the cage...
Glimpsing your face, Ark laughs brightly.

speaker: Ark
content: Just close your eyes, and it'll taste no different than chicken soup! Zulu Zulu!

speaker: Iron
content: How have you been, Chief ${PlayerName}?
She deliberately enunciates your name in a not so friendly way.

speaker: Iron
content: Thanks to you, my patients and colleagues are dead, my hospital has been blown up, and now...

speaker: Iron
content: You've confined me to this interrogation room. What do you want?
The harsh lighting doesn't deter Iron at all. She glares at you from across the table with piercing gaze.
With such hostility, it will probably be hard to convince her to work with the FAC.

options: Put on relaxed airs & cozy up to her

content: We're no strangers to each other. You can relax a bit.
Back at SALVA, we were even comrades-in-arms...

speaker: Iron
content: Ha, comrades-in-arms?
She cuts you off with a cold chuckle.
I'm deeply sorry for what happened at SALVA. I know you won't be able to talk to me calmly anytime soon.
But as you saw, I harbor no ill intentions toward Sinners. You don't need to be so guarded against me. We have the same goal.

speaker: Iron
content: Ha, the same...
She cuts you off with a cold chuckle.

speaker: Iron
content: SALVA sacrificed lives to save Syndicate. How can it be the same?

speaker: Iron
content: Now, Chief of Minos Bureau of Crisis Control, there are two things you need to be clear about.

speaker: Iron
content: First, I am innocent. Everything I've done is to heal Syndicate.

speaker: Iron
content: Put away your interrogation tactics. I don't care for them. No matter what evidence you have, I will not kowtow to authority.

speaker: Iron
content: Second...
She gazes at you with a tiny trace of gloom in her eyes.

speaker: Iron
content: Second, I'm not your comrade-in-arms, let alone your friend.

speaker: Iron
content: We both know how much damage your presence has dealt to the hospital.

speaker: Iron
content: You want me to put on a smile and chat with you like nothing ever happened? And in this tapped interrogation room full of surveillance equipment, of all places? Ha...

speaker: Iron
content: Dream on.
She clearly has no more patience to humor you after saying this. Her mechanical left hand clenches and unclenches impatiently.

speaker: Iron
content: If you get what I mean, then stop wasting time. Now tell me, what do those cowards want from me?

speaker: Iron
content: Pfff... the FAC, that organization who's supposed to exist for the sole purpose of controlling Mania.

speaker: Iron
content: And yet, they sent a clueless Chief and two little girls to Syndicate when the Mania crisis is at its peak.

speaker: Iron
content: Though all you could do was to hide behind the Sinners, at least your shackles and decisions played a crucial role. But as for them...

speaker: Iron
content: All the disorder and evil in Syndicate nowadays, they're inextricably linked to the FAC's incompetence and dereliction of duty. Can you blame me for calling them cowards?

options: Fair enough. I've heard worse curses in Syndicate...
How do you know I'm sent by the FAC?

content: You don't know how Nightingale will react if you talk about FAC's noble deeds under close surveillance, but for the sake of the negotiations, you have no choice but to continue the topic.
But how did you know it has to do with the FAC?

speaker: Iron
content: An educated guess.

speaker: Iron
content: Back at SALVA, you saw my surgical experiments. Your reaction at the time was interesting.

speaker: Iron
content: My observations of you tell me that the authorities have not yet grasped how to surgically suppress Mania.

speaker: Iron
content: Surely they won't ignore the mountain of patient data SALVA retrieved from Syndicate, as well as over a hundred clinical records I made.
But you just said FAC was incompetent in the face of Mania. How can you be sure that they want to know about your surgeries?

speaker: Iron
content: ...Because of you.
Iron's tone softens noticeably.

speaker: Iron
content: I can tell that you want to save lives, regardless of gender or age, or whether they're civilians, Maniacs or Sinners.

speaker: Iron
content: It's true that I'm not sure what the FAC wants, but as for you... I know for sure that you won't give up on treating Mania. You'll definitely push for military-civilian cooperation.

As she had guessed, you listed in detail what you saw and heard at SALVA in the Syndicate mission report, and refuted rumors about horrific experiments taking place there. You hope that SALVA's good deeds in Syndicate can be taken seriously by the FAC.
But Iron got one thing wrong.
test
test
test
test
test
test

I did report the contributions made by you and SALVA towards fighting Mania to my superiors, but this cooperation isn't pushed by me. The FAC issued an order before I could draft a cooperation proposal.
My report piqued their interest, and they hope to collaborate with you on Mania research and find a cure.
Her brows twitch as she carefully examines the order document on the table, but she remains silent.
The wait for her reply is torturous. After what seemed like an eternity, she finally lifts her head.

speaker: Iron
content: I refuse.
Why?
Iron's decision seems incomprehensible. The FAC can provide her with personnel, technical and limitless financial support, yet she still chooses to reject the offer after careful consideration.
Sensing your confusion, she smiles and pushes the document back to you.

speaker: Iron
content: Compared to a few empty promises on paper, I'm more inclined to trust what I saw in Syndicate with my own eyes.

options: You still don't trust the FAC

speaker: Iron
content: What has the FAC ever been responsible for that merits any trust? The gang wars? The proliferation of Mania weapons? Or... the patients on my operating table that they've neglected and abandoned?
Her sudden sharp questions leave you speechless.

speaker: Iron
content: Ha, forget it. I thank them for their kind offer, but I refuse to cooperate until I see some sincerity from the FAC.

speaker: Iron
content: Even without funding, technology, or even a clinic, I will continue the Mania research on my own.

speaker: Iron
content: Even if I'm the only one left...
Iron speaks in an extra grave tone as she frowns at her left arm. It seems that she is trying to convince herself more so than you.
Perhaps you already know why she's frowning...
But can you really continue only on your own?

speaker: Iron
content: What do you mean? Are you doubting my medical skills now?
No, I'm doubting how well a doctor can treat an illness when she is seriously ill herself.
test
test
test
test
test
test
test
According to the tests taken at the time of your detainment, your base M-value is higher than most other Sinners.
As a professional researcher of Mania, you know better than I do what this means.
Iron does not respond. She just stares at the file data in cold silence, so you continue the topic yourself.

This means that when you awakened as a Sinner, your M-value was already so high that you were on the brink of derangement. Each time your M-value increases, you get one step closer to becoming a Corruptor.
If the mutation really occurs, you won't even be able to save yourself with your sanity lost, let alone save Syndicate.

speaker: Iron
content: There are no what-ifs. Your shackles are the best bet for suppressing Mania.
The shackles won't last forever. If something happens to me...

speaker: Iron
content: I told you, there are no what-ifs!
Your words enrage Iron for some reason. Her mechanical left arm slaps against the armrest of the interrogation chair, making shrill noises.

speaker: Iron
content: For your information, I already told Anne before I met you that I'd operate on myself before I mutate.

options: You'll perform nerve modification surgery on yourself?

content: Then you'll become like Ted. You'll lose all desires and become a walking corpse...

speaker: Iron
content: What I become has nothing to do with you!

speaker: Iron
content: But your shackles are critical to the M-value of every Sinner in the Bureau. It's the unsolved enigma to restraining Mania, and the hope of DisCity!

speaker: Iron
content: I won't let these what-ifs come true.
Those are supposed to be words showing concern, but she manages to make them sound harsh and menacing.

options: I promise you, I won't die easily
I'm sorry, I shouldn't have joked about such things

content: You take back your assumptions, and Iron's rage cools a bit.
Yet as you observe Iron fuming, you can't help but remember that iron-blooded devil standing before the ruins of SALVA.
Irritability is a Mania symptom, and it is still affecting her life.
My shackles can indeed prevent you from mutating, but what about the nightmares, insomnia, the mental and emotional anguish? What about the searing sores on your body...
You look at Iron's left shoulder, where her robotic arm connects to her torso. According to the physical examination, there had been severe ulcerations there.
What Sinners with high M-value are suffering from is a hundred times worse than what has been recorded on paper.

speaker: Iron
content: Pain, insomnia, and irritability can all be controlled with medication.
Long-term use of such medication will definitely lead to dependence and resistance, which can only be restrained by taking more medication. There is no end to such treatment.
She caresses her left arm, pretending to not care.

speaker: Iron
content: I'm a medical professional. I know what dosage to use. No need for you to worry about it.

options: You are as ruthless to yourself as you are to the patients

speaker: Iron
content: ...I'm not trying to be ruthless.

speaker: Iron
content: It's a choice that must be made to heal Syndicate.
She has left herself no room to back out.
By this point, it doesn't seem like anything new will come from the interrogation. You two just sit face-to-face in silence across the FAC files and medical reports. She's waiting for you to talk.

options: That's it for the interrogation today.
So you are still not willing to cooperate with the FAC?

speaker: Iron
content: You still haven't completed the mission your superiors assigned you.
You said that you refuse to cooperate until you see some sincerity from the FAC.
I'll make sure you see some.
She smiles, finally relaxing a bit.

speaker: Iron
content: I can do it on my own.
I will let you see the FAC's sincerity.
She smiles, finally relaxing a bit, noncommittal at your answer.

speaker: Iron
content: All the nurses at SALVA call me stubborn behind my back. No one can sway my decisions. But this time...
She flashes her eyebrows half-jokingly.

speaker: Iron
content: I seem to have met my match.
Thud!
The Corruptors hysterically slam their bodies against the battered wooden door. You are nestled inside the room behind the door with a team of guards and some frightened civilians.
Ten minutes ago, you heard calls for help on your way back from a field mission. To protect the civilians in need, you were caught up in a small-scale contamination outbreak.

The Corruptor siege grows more and more frenzied. You have nowhere left to retreat. Your last line of defense wavers as the wooden door is battered to pieces, while aid from the Sinners is still far away.
Everyone, take cover and distract the Corruptors! Protect the Chief and the civilians to safety first!

options: Is it help from the MBCC?

content: It's not the MBCC.
Gunshots ring out from outside the door, and an unfamiliar female voice begins to speak through the comms.

speaker: Claire
content: Chief ${PlayerName}, I'm Captain Claire of the 6th Squadron. As the closest FAC squadron to you, we are here to keep you safe!

speaker: Claire
content: Leave the fighting to us. Adjutant Nightingale has already dispatched medical support from the MBCC, so please don't worry.
The message from the comms is intertwined with the roars of the monsters beyond the door. It seems that the situation is still dismal.

options: Is there anything we can do?

speaker: Claire
content: ...You've already used up a lot of gunpowder and stamina to protect the civilians. What you need to do now is trust us.
A sense of reassuring smile can be heard from the comms. The civilians behind the door let out sighs of relief.

speaker: Claire
content: Nash, keep your distance, beware of Mania contamination!

speaker: Claire
content: Direct all your firepower at seven o'clock—
The battle situation outside is a haze. You can only guess what's going on through Captain Claire's commands.

speaker: Claire
content: Katya, watch out—ahh!

speaker: Katya
content: Captain!
Screeching noises erupt from the comms as the equipment on the other side is impacted in battle.

speaker: Claire
content: It's okay, just a few scratches... Everyone, deploy your defense barriers at eight o'clock! Don't let the monsters get close!
The battle rages on, and no one behind the door dares to relax. Everyone leans firmly against the wooden door, observing the battle situation through the comms with bated breaths.
The gunshots finally subside, and the Corruptors let out their final howls.

speaker: Claire
content: Phew... Chief, the crisis is over. You are safe now.
The guards carefully push open the door and peek out. Corruptor remains are strewn everywhere amidst the smoldering gunsmoke.
A female soldier in a bloodstained uniform stands nearby. She leads her team to salute you from a distance.

speaker: Claire
content: Chief, all eight members of the FAC's 6th Squadron are here. There are no casualties.

speaker: Claire
content: No problem. It is the 6th Squadron's mission to fight. It is our duty.
She glances at the wounded civilians and guards.

speaker: Claire
content: The MBCC's medical reinforcements should be arriving soon. Chief, all the follow-up work is now in your hands.
Don't worry. Guards, listen up.
Check to see if anyone is injured, and if they are, have them wait here for the medical team. As for everyone else, escort the civilians back home...

speaker: 6th Squadron
content: Captain!!
You sense something ominous when you hear the shout. Turning around, you see that Claire has collapsed to the ground.
The seemingly innocuous scratch on her jaw begins to emit eerie wisps of black smoke.

speaker: Panicking squadron member
content: Look, it's... a Mania Crystal! The Captain has been infected?!

speaker: Katya
content: The Captain was trying to protect me... Chief, what do we do?!
The joy of triumph suddenly vanishes. The squadron members all look at you in anticipation. They have no commanding officer now and need your orders.
Don't panic. Guards, carry on with your tasks. 6th Squadron...
You don't show any panic, but you are all too familiar with Mania Crystals. Anybody who comes into contact with them will mutate into a Corruptor very soon.
Don't worry. She got injured while trying to help the MBCC, so the MBCC will definitely save her.
Breathing as calmly as possible, you reach out to Claire. The medical team has not arrived yet. Perhaps you have to give it a go... and try to contain her Mania with your shackles.
Do you want to die with her here?
A familiar voice rings out from behind.
A robotic arm pushes through the crowd, and a reassuring white-robed figure comes to your side.
Iron?

speaker: Iron
content: Calm enough. Good job.
She raises her brows and nods. Eschewing any further pleasantries, she jumps into working mode and begins checking the patient's wound right away.
A Mania Crystal scratched her right lower jaw during the battle.

speaker: Iron
content: Time?
Around fifteen minutes ago.
While cleaning up the infection, Iron frowns as she measures with fingers the distance between Claire's wound and her brain.

speaker: Iron
content: The nerves are most active during high-intensity combat. Fifteen minutes... I'm afraid...
She kneels beside the patient and picks up the name tag on Claire's uniform.

speaker: Iron
content: FAC...?
You are the only one who notices Iron's wariness towards the three letters.

speaker: Iron
content: ...Captain Claire of the FAC's 6th Squadron, can you hear me? Open your eyes!
Claire frowns in pain.

speaker: Iron
content: Claire, can you hear me?
As Iron speaks, she puts her hand on top of Claire's head and begins to probe the contamination levels in her body with her neuroelectric powers.

speaker: Claire
content: I'm... sorry...
After the third call, Claire forces open her eyelids with her lips trembling. Her right eye has already turned dark purple from being too close to the wound.
All the squadron members gasp at the Mania spreading so fast.

speaker: Iron
content: Try to make fists with both hands. Can you do it?
Claire's left hand clenches successfully, but her right hand stays still.

speaker: Iron
content: There is still consciousness, but the neural connections have been severely corrupted, and the contamination has spread to the brain. Simply cleaning the wound won't help. Surgery is needed immediately.

speaker: Katya
content: Surgery? Now? Here?

speaker: Iron
content: All unnecessary personnel, get lost! ${PlayerName}, stay to help.
The squadron members wince at you, obviously not comfortable with handing over their captain to a stranger.
Iron doesn't bother to assuage them. She has already started fishing out tools from her medical kit.
She's an excellent doctor. Trust her and step back.
The squadron members step back grudgingly. At the same time, after some simple sterilization, Iron quickly locates the area of incision on the right side of the skull.

speaker: Iron
content: Chief, give me the hook... the third tool from the left.
As Iron talks, she injects anesthesia into Claire, while scalpels and pincers pop out from her mechanical arm.
You recognize the shape of the robotic arm at this moment. Ted's benumbed face flashes in your mind. Tool in hand, your arm pauses in mid-air.

options: You're performing a nerve modification surgery?

speaker: Iron
content: You ask them to trust me, but you don't seem to trust me yourself?
Is this really the only option?

speaker: Iron
content: What other choice do we have? Use your shackles on her and then perish together after losing control?

speaker: Iron
content: ...You have twenty seconds to decide. The anesthesia will come into effect soon. This is a race against the spread of Mania!

options: You have no right to decide her future

content: Seeing Iron's conviction, you also stop hesitating. You kneel down to whisper into Claire's ear.
Listen, Claire. This operation can save your life, but you will lose all your emotions, desires, and memories. You will never be a soldier again.
Are you still willing to have the surgery under these conditions?

speaker: Iron
content: You have no right to let her die here! Mania won't wait for a consent form to be signed.

speaker: Iron
content: If we suppress her Mania first, the doctors in Eastside may be able to help her recover later. But if she dies here now, it would really be over.
You can't argue with that. But as a soldier, is Claire really willing to lose her emotions, desires, and memories to live...? The twenty-second time limit ticks by bit by bit.

speaker: Claire
content: Live...
On the verge of death, Claire struggles to look towards her squadron members.

speaker: Claire
content: Save me... no matter what... they're... waiting for me...
Iron's silver mechanical arm is already in place when Claire spoke, as if expecting this answer from the beginning. Her other hand is outstretched to take the tool.

speaker: Iron
content: I know more about one's desire to survive than you... The third one from the left on the ground, please. Open up here. Hurry.
The surgery officially begins.
Having retreated to a distance, the 6th Squadron members cannot hear your conversation, nor witness Iron's breathtaking surgical skills. They can only wait anxiously.

speaker: Katya
content: Nash, did you see that electric current...

speaker: Katya
content: She's a Sinner... But in this situation, guess there's nothing else we can do.

speaker: Katya
content: Everyone from the squadron who touched that kind of crystal in the past, they all...

speaker: Nash
content: But Sinners are the source of the Mania crisis themselves!
Struggling, reluctant, and helpless... Every member of the squadron falls into silence.

speaker: Nash
content: Do you remember what the Captain always likes to say?

speaker: Katya
content: It is the 6th Squadron's duty to fight.

speaker: Nash
content: If that Sinner does anything that desecrates a soldier's dignity, I won't spare her!
Though comatose, Claire's vital signs are stable, and with the help of Iron's neuroelectric power, she feels no pain. The air reeks of burnt flesh and blood.
The operation is progressing smoothly. The murmurs in the distance do not affect Iron in the slightest.
One may find it hard to believe that the M-value of this calm doctor already approached the critical threshold many years ago.

speaker: Iron
content: Yes, I can hear them... you can release the hook now.
Is it because you're a Sinner?

speaker: Iron
content: Mhmm... Needle and thread, please.
Should I explain on your behalf?

speaker: Iron
content: Explain what? It's true that I'm a Sinner, and the aftereffects of the surgery are indeed very severe.

speaker: Iron
content: But it's also true that I'm the only one who can save her life.
Iron's tone is unusually calm. You notice that her actions have slowed down.
Are you encountering some difficulties in the surgery?

speaker: Iron
content: I'm just stitching. I don't want to leave any ugly scars on her, so I'm taking a bit more time.
Iron cuts free the last thread of stitching and puts down the surgical tool in her hands.

speaker: Iron
content: Did you get a good look at today's surgery?
Iron's speed was breathtaking. You only recall that she cut out some dark purple jelly-like tissue from a blurry mass of flesh, her tools traversing between blood vessel-like filaments.

speaker: Iron
content: ...It's fine. I've already completed my purpose by letting you watch once.

speaker: Iron
content: The surgery is over. You can call them to come over.

speaker: Nash
content: What did you say?!
The squadron member grabs her angrily by the collar, but Iron doesn't dodge. She just stares numbly at the all-too-familiar commotion, and repeats herself once more.

speaker: Iron
content: The Mania lesions have been removed. All her emotions, desires, and memories have been lost.

speaker: Iron
content: To suppress Mania, any violent impulses must be rooted out.

speaker: Nash
content: Do you realize that she won't be able to go to the battlefield like this?! This is worse to her than killing her!

speaker: Iron
content: This was her choice. It's a necessary sacrifice to survive.

speaker: Katya
content: No... it's impossible! I refuse to believe that the captain would accept such an operation!

speaker: Katya
content: The captain always told our teammates who got contaminated to have no regrets. The FAC lives for Mania and dies for Mania. Death by contamination is an honor!

speaker: Katya
content: She has always been a captain who shoulders everyone's willpower as she fights. If she knows she has to eke out a miserable, contaminated living, she'd never forgive herself...

speaker: Iron
content: Shut up! The life of a cripple is no different from that of a hero.

speaker: Nash
content: Who are you calling a cripple?

speaker: Nash
content: This is all your fault! You prolonged the captain's pain with your stupid surgery and desecrated the dignity of a soldier!!

speaker: Iron
content: Is this how you FAC people treat their lifesavers?
Iron pushes aside the vexatious squadron members, fishes out a scalpel from her bag and flings it next to the comatose Claire.

speaker: Iron
content: If you believe that dying on the battlefield is the proper dignity for a soldier, then go ahead.

speaker: Nash
content: We... we certainly want her to live more than anyone else! But we also know Claire. She wouldn't have wanted...
Nash gawks at the scalpel on the ground, panting angrily, but someone else rush towards the blade without hesitation.

speaker: Nash
content: Katya! What are you doing?!
The squadron member named Katya ignores her teammate's shout and lunges at Iron with the blade.
Stop!
Battle-weary Katya has long exhausted her fighting strength. You halt her easily, and she falls to her knees.
If it weren't for Iron, Claire would've mutated into a Corruptor by now, and we would've had to kill her. How can you be so ungrateful?

speaker: Katya
content: I... I can't do anything... I have to at least punish this vile woman who turned the captain into a walking corpse...

speaker: Katya
content: The 6th Squadron had eight members, now there are...
She has lost her wits and glares at Iron with burning hatred.
Claire knew what the surgery would cause. But she accepted it so she could return to you guys...

speaker: Katya
content: No! It can't be! I don't believe it! It must be the Sinner! This Sinner must have made the decision herself!
The rest of the squadron surrounds the unconscious captain, acquiescing to Katya's tantrum.
This is not how a life-saving doctor should be treated, but Iron's calm expression tells you that she faces such hostility on a daily basis.

speaker: Iron
content: As I said, there is no need to explain. Don't waste your time.
She grabs you by the collar and turns to leave, ignoring the torrent of abuse from behind.
female_content: She grabs you by the wrist and turns to leave, ignoring the torrent of abuse from behind.

speaker: Nash
content: Typical Sinner... Like I thought, you're all monsters... Coldhearted, ruthless monsters!

speaker: Iron
content: Ha. Monsters you say...
Maybe you are hallucinating from battle fatigue, but you seem to see Iron smile upon hearing the word "monsters." It is a smile that is both helpless and reminiscent.

speaker: Student A
content: Hey, have you heard? That Iron from the neurosurgery department refused the offers of every major hospital! She said she's going to Syndicate to treat Mania!

speaker: Student B
content: Mania? Hasn't that already been determined to be a terminal illness with no cure?

speaker: Student A
content: Yeah, and it's a disease that only those Syndicate hood rats get. It's their karmic retribution!

speaker: Student B
content: Syndicate... ugh, even thinking about that place makes me want to puke.

speaker: Student A
content: Tsk tsk, we lowly mortals simply can't fathom the mind of a genius from a medical heritage. Guess we are not worthy of working with her in Eastside.

speaker: Student B
content: Hey, do you think genius Iron will turn into some wretched monster too after going to Syndicate?

speaker: Student A
content: Hahahaha, what did she call it? To sacrifice for one's ideals? Oh yes, noble ideals...

I could hear all their sneers and taunts. The onslaught of scorn never stopped from the moment I decided to treat Mania. Those self-righteous med students at Banyan mocked me mercilessly, even as I took to the stage to speak on their behalf.
Of course, I was self-righteous, too.

speaker: Iron
content: Greetings, dear teachers and fellow students. I'm Iron, valedictorian of this year's graduating class.

speaker: Iron
content: It is the graduation ceremony of Banyan Medical College today. As the lucky beneficiaries of Eastside's elite medical education, we'll soon be applying the clinical knowledge we've learned to treating diseases and saving lives.

speaker: Iron
content: Someday, most of us will become the pillars of DisCity's health system, but...

speaker: Iron
content: I have no faith in such a future.

speaker: Iron
content: How can a bunch of doctors who abandoned Syndicate, ignored the plight of thousands, and turned a deaf ear to the Mania spreading across DisCity, expect trust from their patients?

speaker: Student A
content: What kind of crazy nonsense is she spewing this time?

speaker: Student B
content: Whoa, is her M-value already spiking up before she even steps her foot in Syndicate?
I shared years of my research and analysis of Mania and the danger of its spread, but no one in the audience cared.
I did elicit an uproar. Not because they realized the severity and danger of Mania, but because they thought what I said, and myself, was a joke.

speaker: Iron
content: According to my research, even though Mania is greatly affected by M-value, in essence it is still a communicable disease.

speaker: Iron
content: My father always said that a doctor's duty is to fight diseases. Are we going to give up Mania research just because it's known as a terminal illness?

speaker: Principal
content: Ms. Iron, this is not the speech we agreed upon.

speaker: Iron
content: Even a hoodlum has the right to live. And this is not just a problem for Syndicate. Sooner or later it will become a problem for Eastside, and even all of DisCity.

speaker: Principal
content: Ms. Iron!

speaker: Iron
content: The destiny of mankind is a shared one. If we allow Mania to spread or even mutate into other forms, everyone here will turn into a Corruptor someday!

speaker: Principal
content: Enough!
I was ushered off the stage before I could finish my speech. Now that I think about it, it was probably just a meaningless, impulsive outburst, venting my youthful indignation.

speaker: Hoodlum
content: Show me who dares to open a clinic on the boss's turf?

speaker: Iron
content: Those here for medical treatment, line up and take a number. The elderly, the disabled and the pregnant, go to the front of the line. Troublemakers, buzz off.

speaker: Hoodlum
content: Wow, newcomer to Syndicate and you already have the gall to act so tough. See if you can keep that attitude up in front of my fists.
I didn't have my power back then. It was harder than I imagined to gain a foothold in that unfamiliar city of disorder.
But gang warfare was just one of many problems. It was the endless cycle of violence that really brought the treatment of Mania to an impasse.

speaker: Woman
content: Dr. Iron, please, please save my child! He's been running a high fever ever since he got caught in that crossfire...

speaker: Gang member
content: Outta my way, you old broad! I came here first! Save me first! Their Mania weapons are just too... ahhh!

speaker: Hoodlum
content: Why are more and more markings showing up on my body?! ****! Aren't you a professional doctor from Eastside?! Find a way to save me! I... I don't want to turn into a monster!
I used to hate my colleagues' "little white lies." I thought those were just fig leaves for their incompetence. Yet now, I was drained of all my energy just to ease their pain.
"Save lives"? Something so natural for doctors was a luxury here in Syndicate.
I became impatient. Mania research was at a bottleneck. As long as the thirst for harm and violence still existed, there would be no end to such chaos.

speaker: Zoya
content: Syndicate doesn't have any proper medical institutions, nor any professional staff. You want to treat Maniacs here? You can't do it alone.

speaker: Zoya
content: How about you join the Legion?
She gave a lucrative offer that was even more enticing than the FAC's offer today.
But I knew very well that the woman in front of me was a source of Syndicate's incessant warfare. I refused to fight fire with fire.

speaker: Iron
content: Since there's no professional staff, I'll pick and train some myself. Since there are no medical institutions, I'll set up the only neutral organization here.
In the end, she didn't force me. But after she left, the harassment of the clinic by other gangs eased markedly.
But as old problems were resolved, new problems arose.

speaker: Youth
content: Doctor... your left hand... has the same Mania markings as I do...

speaker: Youth
content: So you have been infected as well...?

speaker: Iron
content: Given the Chief's generosity toward the Bureau's employees, it's only natural that you would be reluctant to give up your current position, Miss. How about this...
When I came back to my senses, I had already pressed my scalpel against the kid's artery.
It was not the first time that I lost control of my emotions. My rage cost me quite a few pieces of equipment. I could not put my patients at risk. I had to temporarily close down the clinic.
It seemed that my journey to treat Mania and save Syndicate was coming to an end too.

speaker: Iron
content: Today is the eleventh day of my Mania infection. My symptoms... include a severe headache, twitching of the limbs, poor coordination, and a strong burning sensation in the left arm.

speaker: Iron
content: I lost consciousness for two hours and tried to break open the clinic door to go out and harm others.

speaker: Iron
content: My stock of painkillers has been exhausted, and when I tried to call the major hospitals in Eastside and medical departments of DisCity... my signal was blocked...

speaker: Iron
content: I predict that the Mania contamination in my left arm will spread to my heart in... two days...
I no longer had the strength to write, so I had to log my daily symptoms with audio recordings. There was an unprecedented downpour that night, so the recording wasn't clear.
Though I didn't contribute much to curing Mania, it might be helpful for others to leave behind a detailed case record...
I thought I'd get through that long night alone, just like the past ten days...
Is anyone here? There's a child who needs medical help!
Please, I beg you, open the door!

speaker: Iron
content: The clinic is closed and not operating.
Please, just give us a bottle of medicine! Any medicine is fine!

speaker: Iron
content: You can't just use some random medicine... Tell me the symptoms and I'll make a diagnosis.
She... she is a Corruptor... she just mutated half an hour ago.
But trust me, she's in a coma and doesn't threaten anyone. Her pulse... is very weak.

speaker: Iron
content: Sssss—
Are you alright? Sounds like you're in pain.

speaker: Iron
content: It's nothing. I haven't been in contact with anyone for too long. I almost...
I almost opened the door and let out all my rage of incompetence on them.
If it's really too difficult for you, can you point us towards a nearby hospital? A pharmacy would be good, too...
Please... her only wish is to live...
Hospital? Pharmacy? Those don't exist in Syndicate. It's raining so heavily. They had nowhere else to go.
I was the only one stupid enough to do those things in Syndicate. Mania, it was all on me...

speaker: Iron
content: Give me five minutes, please. I'll open the door for you.
Amputation is a piece of cake, but this was the first time I'm amputating myself.
The hand is the soul of the surgeon.

speaker: Iron
content: I'm ready. Bring her in.

speaker: Anne
content: You... must stop the bleeding quickly!
I must have startled her when I opened the door looking like that.

speaker: Iron
content: It's alright. I can tough it out. The medicine in the clinic is running out. Give them to her first.
Unfortunately, the child named Paige didn't make it past dawn. But I overcame Mania and became a Sinner.
My M-value temporarily stopped growing because of my will to resist... Then perhaps Mania could be controlled by curbing the urge for violence.
I could only perfect such an unprecedented type of surgery through trial and error.

speaker: Gangster
content: Wanna hear something hot off the press?

speaker: Hoodlum
content: Another gang scandal?

speaker: Gangster
content: No! Do you remember that Eastside doctor named Iron?

speaker: Hoodlum
content: That dud who kept talking about curing Mania? she's just a scammer from Eastside if you ask me. She hasn't been showing up for a long time, what happened?

speaker: Gangster
content: Her clinic reopened under the new name SALVA! The strange thing is, she took in many Maniacs, but when they left they were all brain-dead!

speaker: Gangster
content: They were all just stuttering about, looking dumb. They don't laugh or cry or know anything, so much that they don't even look human anymore. I'd say it's a life worse than death!

speaker: Hoodlum
content: My ***! And they call it SALVA? More like SAVAGE! What about Mania, then? Can it really be cured?

speaker: Gangster
content: Ha, what kind of place do you think this is? So what if you are cured. You'll get infected again anyway!

speaker: Gangster
content: But that's not all! I heard that Iron replaced her left arm with a robotic one. And everyone is saying that she is literally no longer human!

speaker: Hoodlum
content: Then what is she now?

speaker: Gangster
content: A monster! A cold monster more ruthless than any Corruptor!
On the way back, Iron keeps staring at her left arm, deep in thought.
Are you upset by their insults?

speaker: Iron
content: If I cared about that, SALVA would have long ceased to exist.
At least you can explain to them that nerve modification surgery is the only option.

speaker: Iron
content: Explain? My requirements for the FAC are the same as the ones I have for myself. I value results over verbal promises.

speaker: Iron
content: I can suppress one's Mania and extend one's life. That should be a good enough explanation in and of itself. If it's not enough to persuade some people, I don't want to waste my breath on them.

speaker: Iron
content: And they got one thing right. I am a cold monster. Only a cold surgical machine can save a place like Syndicate.

speaker: Iron
content: Warmth will only render one unable to make decisions at critical times.

options: I can't be so cold and ruthless like you talked about
I don't think you have no warmth

content: It's precisely because there's warmth in people, that they have emotions and compassion.
You said that you could tell I wanted to save lives. You were putting trust in my warmth, weren't you?

speaker: Iron
content: Think what you will.
Then why do you save people, Dr. Iron? Surely not because you're "cold"?
It is precisely because you're warm towards every person that you want to save every life.
Even if a certain life is meaningless in the eyes of others, you are unwilling to let it perish.

speaker: Iron
content: Don't assume that you know me well.
But you didn't refute me either.

speaker: Iron
content: Heh...
Iron gazes down at her right hand, releasing and then re-clenching it.

speaker: Iron
content: Even I can't save everyone.

options: That's why you need support from the FAC

content: That's why you let me watch the surgery up close, right?
Personnel, technical and financial support... These can all definitely help you. Going about it alone is not good for your M-value.

speaker: Iron
content: You've seen the surgery already. Do you still not understand? You had a hard time keeping up with just your eyes. Imagine if you had to keep up with your hands! At present, the most critical part of this treatment is the surgeon's skills.

speaker: Iron
content: Aside from me, there are no other surgeons who can perform such a complicated procedure in DisCity. Besides, my future goal is the possibility of full recovery after a patient's Manic tumors are removed. That will require even higher skills.
So what you're saying is, the FAC should first train doctors who are willing to treat Mania?

speaker: Iron
content: How many do you think will voluntarily step up to the challenge?

speaker: Iron
content: Mania has been spreading for a long time, but Syndicate has ever only had one proper clinic.
Even in the FAC, which you regard as incompetent, there are people like the 6th Squadron, like Claire.
Mania is not just a crisis for Syndicate, but one that threatens all of DisCity, and even the fate of humanity.
I'm sure there will be people who are willing to step up, just like you did back then.

speaker: Iron
content: Hahahaha...
What's so funny?

speaker: Iron
content: You're very much like me from before... but you're luckier than I was back then.

speaker: Iron
content: You have many friends, and that's why you're willing to believe in the good in humanity.
Now you have a friend, too.
She pushes up her glasses. The reflection of the lenses conceals the trace of earnest sincerity behind her scoff.

speaker: Iron
content: Alright, you lackey Chief. No need to butter me up. I haven't promised to work with you or the FAC.

speaker: Iron
content: You only saved a roomful of people. Don't get too cocky.

speaker: Iron
content: I want to save all of Syndicate.
In the interrogation room, Sumire seems quiet and composed, as if totally unaware of her situation.
The FAC will arrive at the MBCC shortly to perform a special interrogation on Sumire. You still have about 30 minutes, enough time to dig for some info in advance.
Sumire smiles and nods at you when she notices you walking in.

speaker: Sumire
content: Good day, Chief.
Good day. I've heard a lot about you, Ms Sumire.
I heard your works are very popular among the Eastside dignitaries and have always been in high demand.

speaker: Sumire
content: I'm flattered, but it's really nothing worth mentioning. My skills still have a lot of room for improvement.
There's a garden at the Bureau campsite. Feel free to use it during your break.

speaker: Sumire
content: I sincerely appreciate that.

speaker: Sumire
content: Although I don't think you're here today to talk to me about the Bureau's <color=#e45515>Garden</color>, right?
Sumire always wears a friendly smile as she speaks, making her very hard to read.
But you know the FAC's intel is not mistaken. It's highly likely that Sumire works for the assassin organization "the Garden," or at least she knows something about it.
Time is running out. The FAC will be here anytime. No time to beat around the bush anymore.
Can you tell me about the other "Garden"?

speaker: Sumire
content: I'll try my best.
test
test
test
test
test
test
This investigation report says the Garden is a secret assassin organization that has existed for a long time. None of its formal members have been exposed or arrested...
Sumire reads through the report carefully several times, even though there is hardly any information on the merely three pages.

speaker: Sumire
content: There is no problem with your intelligence.

speaker: Sumire
content: But this isn't much information...
There is indeed very little valid information on the report, which is very unusual considering the FAC's intelligence power.

speaker: Sumire
content: Well, don't be too harsh on those who collect information... The job is way too dangerous for them indeed.
You mean the Garden will kill FAC intelligence officers?

speaker: Sumire
content: A secret assassin organization must clear any threats as soon as it can.
Sumire looks as usual with her smile not fading the slightest.
So the Garden dares to take on FAC personnel?
That is the largest official institution in the DisCity, with over ten thousand armed personnel... Countless cases have proven that no Sinner, however powerful and ferocious, can fight it.

speaker: Sumire
content: You are right. The FAC is very powerful indeed, and it is very... brutal with Sinners.

speaker: Sumire
content: This is exactly why a Sinner assassin organization like the Garden won't avoid them.

options: Is the Garden not afraid that the FAC might retaliate?

speaker: Sumire
content: They can't.

speaker: Sumire
content: The document is proof that the FAC knows very little about the Garden. They can't get to the Garden with such superficial information.
Is the Garden able to evade the FAC's investigation?

speaker: Sumire
content: The Garden is a core organization. Most people don't even know it's the Garden they're working for.
What about those within the organization? Have you guys not failed at all?

speaker: Sumire
content: As far as I know...

speaker: Sumire
content: Yes.

options: How long has the Garden been around?

speaker: Sumire
content: Longer than any other assassin organization in the DisCity.
Sumire's answer sends chills down your spine. This means that this extremely dangerous assassin organization has existed for years without anyone realizing it.

options: Do <color=#e45515>you guys</color> have special ways to assassinate?

content: Sumire blinks and makes no comment on how you're addressing her differently.

speaker: Sumire
content: The Garden is a Sinner organization...
The dangerous and unpredictable abilities of Sinners can indeed hide a lot of important information. But this answer is still too general.
You have another file, which can help narrow down the Garden assassin's identity.
test
test
test
test
test
test
test

It's a name list of FAC members who died in accidents in recent years. Sumire picks it up, and this time, she flips through it very quickly. It takes her less than two minutes to read the pile of lists.
She closes the file after flipping through it and looks at you again.

options: Talk about what happened on May 30

content: Wiese Momoa. Died of heart failure around 4:00 a.m. on May 30.
Liszt Lampard. Died in a car accident at 8:51 a.m. on May 30.
Dylan. Died of drowning around 9:00 p.m. on May 30.
These causes of death don't seem suspicious, but having three FAC officers dying on the same day is extremely unusual in itself.
This is also what the FAC's intelligence officer highlighted in the report as "cases most likely to be assassinations by the Garden."

speaker: Sumire
content: These people were indeed targeted by the Garden.
Sumire answers before you ask her, as if she knows what question you have in mind.
How?

speaker: Sumire
content: It isn't difficult. It simply requires experience and patience.
Surely it requires much more to assassinate that many FAC officers and keep unnoticed.

speaker: Sumire
content: We also have the most convenient and secretive tool... Sinners' abilities.
...So it was you who killed these people?

speaker: Sumire
content: No. According to the Garden's rules, I don't deal with commissions of this level.
What level of people do you deal with then?
Sumire simply smiles and fixates her gentle gaze on you without giving an answer. Her expression sends chills down your spine for some reason and stops you from pressing further.
After a moment of silence, you ask your next question.
Your sudden question makes Sumire show a rare look of slight confusion. She seems to be baffled by why you have asked such a question.

speaker: Sumire
content: The Garden is the best assassin organization. They won't be overly picky when it comes to commission targets.

speaker: Sumire
content: Besides, the target is the FAC, which basically all Sinners hate. The Garden has the ability and intention to complete these commissions.
I'm not asking why you guys are assassinating FAC staff.
You are a "core member of the Garden," right? Your organization doesn't have a record of simply revealing information about yourselves like this.
Do you wish to be a state witness? Did you fall out with the Garden? Or did you deliberately get caught to set up some kind of trap? Why are you here?

speaker: Sumire
content: No, I love and respect everyone in the Garden.

speaker: Sumire
content: See it as a... warning if you wish to believe so.
A warning? That I should let you go? Or that the Garden is going to kill me?
Your questions take Sumire by surprise for a moment, but then a smile quickly returns to her face.

speaker: Sumire
content: All I hope is that... you and the FAC will stop investigating the Garden.

speaker: Sumire
content: You won't achieve anything other than provoking the Garden.
Is the Garden going to confront the FAC openly?

speaker: Sumire
content: "Going to" isn't quite the right word. The Garden has always seen the FAC as an enemy.
But you've revealed so much crucial information already—your assassin identity and the garden's ways of doing things.
Considering your past identity as an ikebana artist in Eastside, we will be able to identify more assassins from the Garden with a large-scale screening.
With your identities exposed, Are assassins like you still able to threaten the FAC?

speaker: Sumire
content: Maybe not, if it's just us.

speaker: Sumire
content: But the Garden has a real trump card.
What kind of trump card?
There's a hint of hesitation on her face. But after a moment, Sumire gives a name.

speaker: Sumire
content: ...The Mentor.

speaker: Sumire
content: ...She's a true ikebana artist, the master of the Garden.

speaker: Sumire
content: It is she who gives new life to each flower.
The Garden dares to fight against the whole FAC with just one person?

speaker: Sumire
content: Yes.
Sumire doesn't hesitate the slightest when answering this question.
That's impossible.

speaker: Sumire
content: ...You haven't met the Mentor, so you won't understand how strong her power is.
Tension lingers in the room for a moment. You heave a deep sigh.
You just said you loved and respected your fellows in the Garden, right?

speaker: Sumire
content: Yes.
So what do you think of the FAC?

speaker: Sumire
content: I don't like killing people if I'm not commissioned to.

speaker: Sumire
content: I prefer to spend my time practicing ikebana... Unfortunately, I had made my choice a long time ago.
Although Sumire hasn't said so explicitly, her attitude is evident—She doesn't particularly hate the FAC.
In that case, I hope you will give me all the information about the Garden honestly.

speaker: Sumire
content: Why?
This time it's Sumire asking.
The FAC already knows about the Garden and is planning to deal with you guys. As you know, the FAC can be very... radical toward Sinners.
Sumire nods in agreement with your statement.
If you give me more information about the Garden and the Mentor, I'll be able to take in the other Sinners before the FAC does.
And with the power of the Bureau and the shackles, I'll be able to stop a bigger conflict from breaking out.

speaker: Sumire
content: You're always so... kind.
Kindness isn't really a desirable quality in this world.
I just want to prevent unnecessary sacrifices, whether that's in the FAC or the Garden.
The smile on Sumire's face becomes somewhat bitter. After a long silence, she lets out a soft sigh.

speaker: Sumire
content: Please forgive me for not being able to say yes.

speaker: Sumire
content: I've told you too much information indeed, some of which was even related to the core of the Garden. But it was all because...
Sumire pauses.

speaker: Sumire
content: I can't betray the Garden.
The situation is already out of your control.
The FAC special commissioner is arriving soon. If they force you with truth serum and torturing, I won't even have the authority to intervene.

speaker: Sumire
content: I'm telling you all these information as an ikebana artist.

speaker: Sumire
content: When facing the FAC... the creations of the Garden do not speak. Don't worry.
That's not what I'm worried about, of course...

speaker: Sumire
content: Besides, he might not be able to make it here.
Not able to make it here? What do you mean?

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, the Commissioner's car will arrive soon. A request is sent to let him in.
Sumire's interrogation remains unresolved. You stand up somewhat irritably and pick up the files on the desk to meet the FAC commissioner.
An envelope slips out of the files and drift onto the floor.

speaker: Sumire
content: These are...?
You ponder for a few seconds but fail to recall where the letter comes from.
It isn't in the directory, so it probably belongs to a staff member.

speaker: Sumire
content: Can I... have a look?
test
test
test
test
test
test
You pick it up and find elegant handwriting on the back of the envelope that writes: "To Sumire." A full moon is stamped on the purple wax.
So this is yours?
Sumire doesn't answer and opens the letter.
You glance at the letter and see only one sentence—"The return is nigh. Gather the flowers while you can."
...Sumire?
You want to ask some questions when you notice her usual calm and gentle smile has disappeared from her face.
Are you okay?
Sumire remains silent and motionless, holding the letter in her hand.

options: Is there something wrong with this letter?
"The return is nigh. Gather the flowers while you can." What does it mean?

content: Sumire is still silent, with her face even paler than the letter sheet.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief. We have an emergency.
Nightingale's voice suddenly rings out over the comms.

speaker: Nightingale
content: That FAC Commissioner... is dead.
What happened?

speaker: Nightingale
content: Only after pulling up did the driver realize that the commissioner had already died in the back seat.
Your mind goes blank. This is completely beyond expectations. You take a few dozen seconds to make sense of the situation.
Even though Sumire is acting very suspiciously, there are more important things to get on with.
You shoot Sumire a glance, whose face remains pale.
You just said the commissioner might not even make it here...
No, wait. You had been here with me the whole time. There was no way you could kill...
I will figure it all out—everything about the Garden, who the Mentor is, and... what you're trying to achieve.
Sumire still doesn't respond, but her gaze becomes determined the moment you turn away.
A blood moon fills your sight like the eye of the sky, gazing coldly down the earth.
You are standing in a sea of flowers, and the overflowing purple petals flood at you like a tidal wave.
Fear creeps up closer and closer. You can't help but run frantically.
But there is no escape. You are doomed to be devoured by the eye of the sky and the purple tide.
You open your mouth to call for help, but no words come out, nothing but your heavy panting noise.
In the flower fields around, eerie vines start to grow and entangle around your body. Chilling, mystical glimmers sprinkle on the purple petals in the moonlight.
You open your eyes, only to see a blur of darkness. Your headache and dizziness make it impossible to move.
After a while, you gradually regain your vision, then you notice a purple flower grown on the back of your hand.
Meanwhile, Sumire is standing in front of you in silence.
The Garden, the assassination, the FAC, the Mentor, the words Sumire said... A huge flood of information run through your brain, finally boiling down to one conclusion.
Sumire is here to kill you.

options: Remove the flower on your hand

content: You try shouting to alert the guards, but you are too weak to make any sound that can be heard outside this room.
You try to remove that eerie little purple flower on the back of your hand, but a thousand pounds seem to be pressing down your arms. You simply can't move.
You realize you have probably been shot with some neurotoxin. It's only a matter of time before you die.
The intense headache stops you from focusing, and you can't even use the shackles.
That is your last hope dashed.

options: Are you here to kill me?

content: You hope Sumire will deny it straight away, but she doesn't answer.
After a long while, Sumire finally speaks. On her face is her usual smile, yet with an unfamiliar hint of resigned bitterness.

speaker: Sumire
content: Remember... that letter?

speaker: Sumire
content: It's an order from the Mentor.
They managed to sneak the letter into the FAC's files... The Garden is not to be underestimated indeed.
Your speech is slow and slightly slurred, but Sumire seems to be listening patiently.
If it was an assassination order, aren't you here a little too late?
What was the point of the letter if you received the order already? To risk exposing you?

speaker: Sumire
content: The mission to assassinate you was posted a long time ago.

speaker: Sumire
content: The letter was an ultimatum to me.
So you deliberately exposed yourself and got captured by the Bureau.
Was it all part of the Garden's plan?

speaker: Sumire
content: You must... be very disappointed.
No, just a little regretful.
I should've been more cautious.
A clear glint of sorrow flashes through Sumire's eyes.

speaker: Sumire
content: It shouldn't have ended like this...

speaker: Sumire
content: I was hoping things didn't have to end this way.
Sumire's voice overflows with sorrow. It's almost as if she is an ordinary woman who has come to your office to talk about her misfortunes in life.
But she is no ordinary woman. She has come all the way to the Bureau, evading all the security, just to kill you.
Why don't you just do it?
With a bitter smile, Sumire shakes her head.

speaker: Sumire
content: No, you don't understand what I meant... I...
Sumire seems to be caught in a tangle of hesitation and distress. After a long while, she finally speaks again, in a whisper.

speaker: Sumire
content: ...When I used to create my ikebana works, I'd always give them a story.

speaker: Sumire
content: Let me tell you a story this time.
A wave of intense headache hits you once more. Everything becomes a blur. All you can make out is Sumire's voice.

speaker: Sumire
content: Once upon a time in Syndicate, there was a girl named Nana...

speaker: Sumire
content: One day, Nana's parents went missing, then the hooligans in the neighborhood started pestering her.

speaker: Sumire
content: Nana couldn't fight back and almost died. That was when a lady showed up.

speaker: Sumire
content: The lady gave Nana a knife and two options—either kill the hooligans, leave Syndicate, and join her organization to be her mentee; or just die like that.

speaker: Sumire
content: Nana just wanted to survive.
Sumire pauses, which gives you time to figure out the meaning of the story. There is no doubt that "Nana" in this story is Sumire herself.

speaker: Sumire
content: The training in the organization... was incredibly harsh. Some died, while those who survived were able to gain power to survive in a city like this.
Sinners...

speaker: Sumire
content: Yes... Nana worked very hard and managed to survive the trials and even gained power—a power strong enough to defend herself even in a city like this.

speaker: Sumire
content: Nana worked very hard and was very lucky, she survived the trials. The Mentor... the lady was very pleased with Nana's growth.

speaker: Sumire
content: She gave Nana a new name and taught her the art of ikebana, which gave her the ability to get a foothold in Eastside... she gave Nana everything Nana has today.
She's just controlling Nana.

speaker: Sumire
content: Nana knew that, but she didn't care. She just wanted to repay her Mentor.

speaker: Sumire
content: Nana had completed every mission the Mentor gave her, without the slightest hesitation, and without failure. Step by step, she became almost the best assassin in the organization.

speaker: Sumire
content: Until she met the last assassination target... Nana failed that mission.
Why did she fail?

speaker: Sumire
content: ...The longer one has been as a Sinner, the easier it is to perceive the intangible.

speaker: Sumire
content: It haunts everyone, along with the gift of the ability. It's like the Garden... It gives you the hope of new life along with the "gift" of pain.

speaker: Sumire
content: But when Nana first approached the target, she found that those hallucinations haunting her for so long had disappeared, which caused her to miss the opportunity.
Then what happened next?

speaker: Sumire
content: Nana observed the person for a long time. He wasn't stubborn like the FAC guys, neither was he blind as the Eastsiders who chased after her.
female_content: Nana observed the person for a long time. She wasn't stubborn like the FAC guys, neither was she blind as the Eastsiders who chased after her.

speaker: Sumire
content: He would think about whether he was doing the right thing... The Sinners with him were never puppets who only carried out orders... They were all happy.
female_content: She would think about whether she was doing the right thing... The Sinners with her were never puppets who only carried out orders... They were all happy.

speaker: Sumire
content: Nana had never met anyone like that before. At first it was just curiosity, but then she became envious... Before Nana realized it, she could no longer bring herself to assassinate him.
female_content: Nana had never met anyone like that before. At first it was just curiosity, but then she became envious... Before Nana realized it, she could no longer bring herself to assassin her.

content: He was probably just doing what he should.
female_content: She was probably just doing what she should.

speaker: Sumire
content: To do what you should do... It's never easy.

speaker: Sumire
content: In ikebana, the standard for the highest craftsmanship is... "like flowers in the wild." No matter how much flowers in vases resemble being in the wild, they are still rootless.

speaker: Sumire
content: But this time, Nana felt that she had found the land she could truly fall back on.
Sumire takes a deep breath. The dizziness starts to fade, and her voice becomes clearer and clearer.

speaker: Sumire
content: When Nana returned, the Mentor didn't punish her for her failure but simply sent another assassin to cover her mistake.

speaker: Sumire
content: But not only did Nana not appreciate her Mentor's mercy, but she also repeatedly sabotaged the assassinations and even injured her friend.

speaker: Sumire
content: Later, Nana even exposed herself and went to that person.
Are you saying that Nana is protecting the assassination target?

speaker: Sumire
content: ...She just couldn't watch that person die.

speaker: Sumire
content: Nana fended several attacks, but she became more and more worried...
Why?
Sumire gave you a sorrowful smile.

speaker: Sumire
content: Because of...
...The Mentor?

speaker: Sumire
content: ...Yes, the Mentor.

speaker: Sumire
content: Everyone in the organization learned to kill and the skills to make a living from the Mentor. No one can defeat her.

speaker: Sumire
content: The Mentor has endless patience with her "creations." But she has zero tolerance for betrayal.

speaker: Sumire
content: And Nana... betrayed her.
Despair surfaces in her eyes.

speaker: Sumire
content: Nana hoped for the chance that the Mentor might not care about such a trivial matter, or that she still has sentiments for her mentees.

speaker: Sumire
content: But that letter shattered all her hope. The Mentor would not let them go. If Nana didn't act, the Mentor would deal with it herself.
...I see.
Sumire shakes her head.
The chilling light slants through the window on her, but as if only shining into a darkest corner—only those eyes are glinting with faint shimmers.

speaker: Sumire
content: You won't understand.
Sumire looks out of the window at the sky.

speaker: Sumire
content: I must leave now.
Leave?!
According to Sumire, she betrayed the Mentor. That letter has given her the last chance to prove her loyalty.
You're not killing me?

speaker: Sumire
content: I will go to my Mentor and ask her to revoke the assassination order...

speaker: Sumire
content: I will not let you die.
Will your Mentor let you off if you go back?
Sumire gives a smile again, gentle and friendly just as always, only with tears in her eyes.

speaker: Sumire
content: Meeting you was the luckiest thing that happened in my life.

speaker: Sumire
content: I never deserved to be named after the flower, Sumire. I'm just a venomous insect that lurks in a dark corner and causes harm.

speaker: Sumire
content: But You barged into the darkness and brought me a beam of... light. Now it's time to return to the darkness, for this beam of light.
Sumire turns around.

speaker: Sumire
content: Farewell.
You force yourself back up on your feet, trying to use the shackles to stop her from leaving.
But an intense headache knocks you off balance, and you fall heavily onto the ground.
Sumire has already walked to the door, but turns back at the noise. She's standing in the dark and you can't see her expression on her face, but you notice her shoulders slightly shivering.
Finally, Sumire turns around and disappears into the dark.
You don't know how long it's been before you wake up again and everything around you gradually becomes clear.
Traces of fighting are all over the room—blood, a broken bookcase, an empty syringe, and a small metal can.
You struggle back up and switch on the security camera in the office.

speaker: Female Voice
content: Are you really going to betray the Mentor, Sumire?

speaker: Female Voice
content: For this man?!
female_content: For this woman?!

speaker: Sumire
content: Okay.

speaker: Female Voice
content: He must die.
female_content: She must die.

content: The woman raises the blade.

speaker: Sumire
content: ...I'm saving him.
female_content: ...I'm saving her.

content: In a split second, Sumire turns sideways and dodges a fatal stab. The blade in her hand sweeps across a lock of hair, and a flower of blood blooms at her opponent's right eye.
A grunt sounds. The attacker kneels on the floor, covering her eye. Sumire slowly steps forward to take her bag.

speaker: Sumire
content: It's antidote... I knew there's still a chance to turn things around.

speaker: Sumire
content: Go and tell the Mentor I'll go back to see her.
Sumire watches the woman leave, then turns toward you, and injects the antidote into your hand.
Then you wake up in the footage.
You lift your hand and find no purple flower but a tiny hole from injection.
Sumire never meant to kill you. You were wrong about her.
You hobble out of the Bureau following Sumire's trail.
You can still use your ability to sense her location using your connection with the Sinners. Your head still hurt, but it hardly stops you from moving now.
You can't let her just leave like this. You have to find her.
The courtyard entrance isn't guarded, but the entire building is shrouded in some kind of indistinguishable halo.
It's probably the moon. You think to yourself as you climb over the wall into the courtyard. In the moonlight, you fall into a flowering shrub.
It's hard to imagine so many flowers can fit in such a small courtyard.
But more importantly, Sumire is kneeling near the flowers with a large amount of blood on her abdomen, which has soaked her clothes.
In the corridor stand two aloof, similarly dressed women. Behind them is some flickering candlelight, which outlines a seated figure on the paper screen.
The pressure is so incredibly intense, you feel as if it's almost breaking through the door. The next instant, you can clearly feel that the figure behind that door has already noticed you.
You can vaguely hear the conversation over a dozen meters away.

speaker: Sumire
content: I... willingly accept the punishment.

speaker: Sumire
content: I just wish that you can...

speaker: Woman in Kimono
content: The Mentor has given you a chance, but you're still so stubborn.
A piercing sound of rupture sweeps past. Sounds like some weapon has struck Sumire.
Sumire trembles slightly. You hear the sound of blood dripping onto the stone.

speaker: Sumire
content: He... has everyone in his mind, even the Sinners, even us in the Garden... He would take the risk to save anyone he could.
female_content: She... has everyone in her mind, even the Sinners, even us in the Garden... She would take the risk to save anyone she could.

speaker: Sumire
content: He's not like those people.
female_content: She's not like those people.

content: The woman in the corridor sneers.

speaker: Woman in Kimono
content: The Mentor and everyone in the Garden are your only companions.

speaker: Woman in Kimono
content: Yet you attacked them because of an outsider...

speaker: Sumire
content: I'm really sorry.

speaker: Woman in Kimono
content: You're really sorry? Can you make up for your mistakes by saying sorry?!
Got it.
The woman behind the screen, or rather, the Mentor, finally speaks.

speaker: Mentor
content: You should know, Sumire.

speaker: Mentor
content: Every one of you is my mentee, my cherished masterpiece.

speaker: Mentor
content: I won't punish you too harshly no matter what mistakes you make.

speaker: Mentor
content: Except for betrayal...

speaker: Sumire
content: My mentor, it's my fault... I have upset you.
Sumire grits her teeth. Her wound is still bleeding.

speaker: Mentor
content: Good girl...

speaker: Mentor
content: I will give you one more chance.
The Mentor's voice sounds extraordinarily gentle. Sumire jerks her head up as if she has found a glimpse of hope.
The shadow on the paper screen points to you. All eyes are on you, leaving you nowhere to hide.

speaker: Mentor
content: Kill him.
female_content: Kill her.

content: Sumire spots you. Her shock, anxiety and fear all coalesce into deep despair.
But eventually, it turns into a few gentle words.

speaker: Sumire
content: You... came after all.

options: I couldn't leave you like this.

content: Sumire turns around to face the Mentor again.

speaker: Sumire
content: I'll bear the responsibility for this.

speaker: Woman in Kimono
content: You'll bear the responsibility? Humph. Sumire, you're as stupid as this person.

speaker: Woman in Kimono
content: Even though you stopped me from capturing him alive, he still came to have himself killed.
female_content: Even though you stopped me from capturing her alive, she still came to have herself killed.

content: Sumire doesn't respond but simply stares at the figure behind the paper screen.

speaker: Sumire
content: Please let go of... cough cough...
Sumire's body is shaky and almost falling. The Mentor behind the paper screen sighs.

speaker: Mentor
content: I've seen so many betrayals, but never one like yours.

speaker: Mentor
content: Perhaps you're just bewitched.
Her words are still so gentle, yet a second later, you are overwhelmed by an intense suffocating sense of danger.
The next thing you know, Sumire is standing before you.
You hear or see nothing, yet a split second later, Sumire tumbles down to the ground. A large amount of blood gushes out of the split wound in her abdomen.
Sumire looks back at you, then slowly collapses onto the ground.
You rush forward to hold her up.
Sumire!
Her face is pale. She bites her lip and says nothing.
Hang in there. I'll get you out of here.
Sumire shakes her head.

speaker: Sumire
content: Please just leave me... alone. This is the Garden's internal affair and has nothing to do with you.

speaker: Sumire
content: I just want you to get out of here.
Sumire breaks away from your hand and stands up to face the Mentor again.

speaker: Sumire
content: It's all my fault...

speaker: Sumire
content: I've never pleaded for anything with you... but please, let him go...
female_content: I've never pleaded for anything with you... but please, let her go...

content: The person behind the paper screen remains silent for a long time.
You can't just carry Sumire and run away—At this moment, exposing your back to that terrifying Mentor simply means death.
You still have one last trump card. But at such a distance with two people in the corridor, using the shackles will probably only allow you to die with a little more dignity.
As you are figuring out a way to break through, the Mentor finally speaks up.

speaker: Mentor
content: ...Whatever. I didn't care whether this person is dead or not.

speaker: Mentor
content: But Sumire, you stay here.

speaker: Sumire
content: Thank you...
Without the slightest hesitation, Sumire smiles in relief and extends her hand to the Mentor.
Sumire's hand appear exceptionally pale in the moonlight, perhaps due to the excessive blood loss.
Sumire has blocked assassination after assassination for you without you knowing it, and now she is sacrificing herself for you.
You won't let her sacrifice herself again this time.
Sumire must come back with me. She's my Sinner.

You extend your hand to use the shackles, trying your best to reach the woman behind the screen in the distance. But in a split second, you feel excruciating pain in your left arm. It goes numb, hanging on your body, unable to move.
Fortunately, you are now used to the pain from the toxin earlier today.
The Mentor's shadow has not moved the slightest the entire time, as if it's imprinted on the paper screen. You can't even sense how she attacked you and Sumire.

speaker: Mentor
content: I'll give you one last chance.

speaker: Mentor
content: Leave.

An intimidating aura strikes you, darkening the surroundings. The murderous aura fills the small courtyard. It's simply impossible to imagine how powerful this woman, who calls herself the Mentor, really is.
It's as if every single cell in your body is screaming, urging you to run. But under this horrifying pressure, your mind becomes clearer than ever.
The dreadful murderous sense in the air is almost coagulating and dripping.
But you haven't taken a single step back.
You hold Sumire's hand firmly.

speaker: Mentor
content: Is this your decision, Sumire?

speaker: Mentor
content: You will be betrayed eventually.

speaker: Sumire
content: I... don't care.
Before you realize it, the two people across the hallway are already gone. The candle flames in the tatami room are also out.
Now it's just you and Sumire in the courtyard, with all the flower petals drifting in the air.
For some reason, the Mentor seems to have decided to let both of you go.
Sumire is sitting on her knees. Your hands are still firmly held together.
You force yourself up onto your feet, try to carry Sumire and leave, but your body is too weak to do anything.
You tumble down and sit under the giant tree with white flowers in the center of the courtyard.
You've made far too many thoughtless decisions today. Perhaps the neurotoxin has affected your rationale.
You are extremely exhausted, and your surroundings begin to blur.
Sorry, I'm a little worn out.
Give me... a bit.
Sumire wipes off the blood at the corner of her mouth, smiles without saying anything, and lets you rest on her lap under the tree.
Petals sway and dance in the air, and Sumire opens an umbrella. Moonlight fills the courtyard, making everything look incredibly surreal.
It feels just like a dream...

speaker: Sumire
content: Maybe it is a dream.

speaker: Sumire
content: Just take a nap here. It'll all be over when you wake up. Don't worry. I'll protect you.

options: It's me who will protect you

speaker: Sumire
content: Alright. You will protect me.
You don't seem to believe it at all.

speaker: Sumire
content: I never doubted you.
Okay... but why?
Forget it...
You look at Sumire's smiling face and figure not to bother with questions for now.
You remember what the Mentor said... that "prophecy" of betrayal.
I will never betray you.

speaker: Sumire
content: I know.
Sumire smiles. After a pause, she looks up at the sky.

speaker: Sumire
content: The moon is beautiful tonight.
The main lights in the interrogation room are off. Still, you sense that the person you're about to interrogate is at home.

speaker: McQueen
content: Well, I'll be damned! Our beloved MBCC Chief is a young Adonis! You have a bright future ahead of you.
female_content: Well, I'll be damned! Our beloved MBCC Chief is a young Aphrodite! You have a bright future ahead of you.

content: McQueen delivers the compliment with a hint of sarcasm, which is hard to miss in the smile she gives you.
McQueen is a habitual liar. She can't be trusted. Lisa warned you the moment she learned about McQueen's arrival in the MBCC.
Nice to meet you, Miss McQueen.
Or should I call you Miss Art Dealer, Miss Forgery Trader, or Miss Former Painter?

speaker: McQueen
content: Ah, looks like Lisa told you a lot about me. What else did she tell you?

speaker: McQueen
content: Did she mention how incredibly stunning I am, or how unbelievably charismatic?
test
test
test
test
test
test
She said you are greasy, cunning, have no respect for other people's personal space, and are overly affectionate toward whoever you meet for the first time.

speaker: McQueen
content: Yeah, that sounds like Miss Lisa.
It's also mentioned in the testimony that you may have a murky past, and that you detest the sickening Eastside ways.
McQueen neither confirms nor denies the claim. She just shrugs nonchalantly.

speaker: McQueen
content: She knows a lot, and talks a lot too.

speaker: McQueen
content: The intelligence was true; you are a crafty character, Chief. Even that reclusive, mean critic is willing to serve you.

speaker: McQueen
content: One thing the Eastside black market has in abundance is secret information. Word on the street is that you're a competent chief.

speaker: McQueen
content: So, are you interested in working with the McQueen Art Agency? I could use your talents. Together, we will make it big.
Bigger than making a replica of every single work of art on exhibition except Sosia, and distributing them around the market, all done in one night?

speaker: McQueen
content: Lisa told you that?
No, she just suspected you may have had an ulterior motive for attending the exhibition. She doesn't make unsubstantiated claims. It's the MBCC that found out about what you did.
test
test
test
test
test
test
test
You know the black market inside out, you're an expert in intelligence gathering, and you're an old hand at selling forgeries.
You create a forgery using your power, let it change hands a few times, so no one knows who the original owner is, then you appear among the rich as an art dealer to introduce the artwork to them.

speaker: McQueen
content: Hahaha...

speaker: McQueen
content: Clever, huh? I've done this act over and over for so many years, and no one has been any the wiser.

speaker: McQueen
