However, there's still no hint of panic on Eureka's face. She turns her backpack upside down, shaking out a bunch of plastic little frogs.
Ribbit ribbit ribbit ribbit ribbit... The noisy little green fellows hop over the stone slab to the other end and spit out long plastic tongues, stuffing the tank's cannon.
Bang... Kaboom!
The entire tank breaks apart like a misfired gun. Shining metal fragments are blasted into the air, illuminating the sky with spectacular, colorful sparks.
You watch Eureka skillfully "command the battle" from nearby. It's like watching a strange yet breathtaking performance. You can't help but admit that you really underestimated this quirky inventor.

speaker: Jessie
content: Damn it... what about this? Eureka, you remember this, don't you? You were really scared of it back then.
Eureka purses her lips. On Jessie's thin, scarred arm is the familiar arm-style gun that had haunted her for so many years.

speaker: Jessie
content: Over the years, I've modified and upgraded it repeatedly, significantly increasing the bullet capacity and firing speed. This time, even your ridiculous surfboard won't be able to escape my bullets!
What's the matter? Are you worried that you can't handle this gun?
Eureka shakes her head slowly.

speaker: Eureka
content: No, Chief, I think I can win. I... I'm just worried that I will lose control of my power again like last time...
You won't, Eureka. I'm here this time.
You give her a comforting and encouraging look. Endless power circulates between the links of the shackles.
I can help suppress your power. Just do what you need to do. Your inventions won't be exploited by others again. They won't become weapons that hurt people again.

A barrage of bullets sweeps towards you like a violent storm. Eureka raises a handheld fan. Backed by her power, the thin fan blades whip up a massive tornado, diverting countless bullets off their course.

The arm-mounted gun emits black smoke after firing its last bullet, loosening from Jessie's arm and falling to the ground. There's nothing left behind Jessie, but she stubbornly bites her lip so hard that it almost bleeds.

speaker: Jessie
content: That's impossible, I can't lose...! I've been preparing these things for many years... How could you possibly beat me!

speaker: Jessie
content: It's not over... It's not over yet!

Jessie suddenly changes direction, and throws something with a sparking fuse at you. Eureka's pupils constrict. In that moment, memories flood back like a tidal wave. She sees again the cowering civilians in the underground lab, their faces twisted in their final moments.

speaker: Eureka
content: Chief!!!

speaker: Narration
content: A bomb. Another bomb. You think back to the day this all started, in the interrogation room... there was also a bomb. You close your eyes, listening to Eureka's shouts and the sound of her footsteps, but this time, you feel strangely reassured.

speaker: Mini Robot
content: Clack! Clack clack!

A dazzling white light forms a protective shield around you. The sound of the explosion is blocked out, and you feel only a slight impact before quickly regaining your footing. At the same time, you hear sirens in the distance.

speaker: Jessie
content: How could this be... I put in so much effort... Why is it still the same result...

speaker: Jessie
content: There's still a way... There must be a way... I can still do something... Just you wait...
Jessie slumps to the ground in defeat, muttering to herself as she desperately searches through the wreckage for fragments of her inventions.
Enough, Jessie, it's all over.
The sheriffs will be here soon, and you'll pay for what you've done.

Things have come to a close. The sheriffs who arrive take Jessie away. Some stay behind to clean up the Mania-tainted machine parts, which have been mostly destroyed in the recent fight. Only a few remain in the ruins, tightly guarded.
No longer in her sharp and agile combat mode, Eureka reverts back to her usual absent-minded self, muttering to herself as she stares blankly ahead.

speaker: Eureka
content: Oh my, I've blown up this place for the second time... The cat hole is gone. The automatic stirring feeding bowl is also broken... What a pity. I was planning to take it back for the pets at the Bureau...
It's indeed a pity... but a bit of damage shouldn't be an obstacle for you, right?
You carefully pick out the fragments of the porcelain bowl buried in the sand, put them all into a plastic bag, and hand it to Eureka.

speaker: Eureka
content: ...Ch... Chief? What do you mean...?
Hmm... maybe you could try fixing it and then upgrade it when we get back?

speaker: Schorl
content: Ah, I got it! I'll add automatic cooking, heating, and cooling functions to it! That way, the pets can eat food that suits their taste at any time!
Great idea! Genius inventor Eureka's new invention will surely be a hit at the MBCC!
In response to your praise, Eureka scratches her head and smiles somewhat bashfully.

speaker: Eureka
content: Th... thank you, Chief... but I'm just a terrible inventor who has caused a lot of trouble for everyone...

Really? But the person who found Jessie, cracked all her dangerous weapons, defeated her, and successfully confiscated those dangerous Mania-tainted parts, is you. Don't always be so modest. You are the most amazing inventor I have ever met.

speaker: Mini Robot
content: Clack! A complete victory! Cheering for you! Clack clack clack! Great inventor! Eureka!
The familiar clacking sound comes from Eureka's toolkit, continuing your words on its own.
It can talk!?

speaker: Eureka
content: Huh? I don't know... Let me see...
Eureka looks around in bewilderment, holding the small robot at eye level with both hands.

The setting sun's afterglow envelops the bombed-out factory. She gently gazes at the little robot she created, softly stroking its smooth head, treating it with love and awe as if it were a living creature.
Here, is rebirth. The creator here is...
Eureka, the "terrible inventor."

Several days after Coquelic's arrest
Ruins of the Garden's hideout

speaker: Garden Member
content: ...After you left, the Mentor became listless. She often sat by the window, as if waiting for someone's return.

speaker: Garden Member
content: No one dared to disturb her. We were all hoping you'd bring back good news to lift her spirits.

speaker: Garden Member
content: And then the MBCC came. They came heavily armed—with guns, shields, and whatnot, catching us completely off guard.

speaker: Garden Member
content: We wanted to cover the Mentor so that she could escape to safety, but she thought we were cramping her style and told us to scram...

speaker: Thistle
content: So you chickened out and ran away?

speaker: Garden Member
content: What else could we have done? The Mentor couldn't withstand their firepower, even after deploying that power of hers. We didn't want to see her efforts go to waste, so...

speaker: Garden Member
content: The Mentor must have thought we would be of no help even if we stayed... Thistle, where are you going? Thistle...

speaker: Thistle
content: Where do you think I'm going?

speaker: Thistle
content: To the goddamned MBCC, is where I'm going. I'm going to bring the Mentor back!

speaker: Thistle
content: Whatever it takes... I can't stand the thought of the Mentor, badly wounded, being kept in that hellhole designed to lock up Sinners.
Night has fallen. Tonight, the MBCC is a restless beast, and even the patrols are less orderly than usual. A guard spots a shadowy figure and walks over to investigate.
A dull thud... A pale hand picks up the fallen walkie-talkie. A side door opens, and the figure slips into the Bureau building.

Hours after Coquelic's attack on the Chief
MBCC Chief's break room
She is in a coma, and still her vital signs are deteriorating? Is the situation that grim?

speaker: Nightingale
content: Yes. You can refer to the medical log I've sent you for the details. Simply put, almost all her vital signs are problematic, and her prognosis is poor.

speaker: Nightingale
content: This is partly due to the depletion of her life force, which was, in turn, caused by the overuse of her Mania power. It was a miracle she could move around the way she did, considering the condition her body was in.
And she still tried to kill me using her Mania power... Looks like she was determined to take me down with her.
You open the medical log sent by Nightingale. The projected image is crowded with large patches of red. You furrow your brow at the sight.
These red patches seem to you a manifestation of that comatose patient's determination to send you to hell, even at the cost of her own life.
The Garden's strongest Sinner, top assassin, Mentor... Coquelic. I understand why she wanted to kill me. But at the cost of her own life?
She almost died in her attempt to kill me. No assassin organization would make a losing deal of that magnitude. Unless... the reward for taking my life was too great to resist.
That reward was her motivation, the thing that might show us who she really is beneath her fanatical exterior. What could it be?
Your instinct tells you that to unravel this mystery, you have to delve into Coquelic's past.

Someone at the Bureau was deeply involved in the investigation into the assassination of Paradeisos officials that was choreographed by Coquelic. This person may be able to provide you with some insight.
Is Christina at the Bureau now? I need... Cough... I need to talk to her.

speaker: Hecate
content: Chief, didn't you say you would rest right after hearing the report?

speaker: Hecate
content: Or does time work differently in your world?

Hecate, who has taken it upon herself to look after you and make sure you have enough rest, looks at you, her somewhat solemn eyes making you feel a tinge of guilt. And it is clear that Nightingale isn't going to take your side this time.

speaker: Nightingale
content: According to the record, Sinner Christina has applied to leave the premises in accordance with the Sinner Bail Regulations. She's currently involved in an investigation initiated by the Eastside Public Security Bureau, having reported that she might be unreachable for a while.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Looks like you can't use your I'll-rest-right-after excuse this time, Chief. You may have forgotten this, but Hecate and I sure haven't: You've just survived an assassination attempt and are severely injured. Please, be a good patient and rest now.
All right, all right, I'll rest now. I'll talk to her when she returns. Resting is my first priority now. See? I'm turning off the projector.
With the projector off, the room is now in semi-darkness. To put the other two's minds at ease, you make to lie down, rearranging the thin blanket wrapped around your chest and waist.
You're feeling dizzy, nauseated, cold... Thanks to Coquelic, you have little choice but to take a break from your official duties and stay on bed rest.
And then the silence of the room is broken by a distant explosion. You become fully alert.

speaker: Nightingale
content: <size=30>...What's wrong? Wasn't the location covered by the patrol routes of the guards? And no eyewitness reports?</size>
Nightingale, what happened? Was that an explosion?

speaker: Nightingale
content: Yes, it happened just a minute ago, near the northeast side door. I'm organizing a search for the suspects.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Judging by the available information, it's tentatively determined to be an attack on the Bureau, and it's likely that the attacker has infiltrated...
Boom! Boom! Boom!
Nightingale has hardly finished talking when more explosions take place in rapid succession, each sounding closer than the last.

speaker: Hecate
content: Chief, are you all right?
I'm okay... Cough, cough, cough...
The vibrations from the consecutive explosions compound the dizziness, making you, already short of breath, gasp for air.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Supervision Center...?! No... pattern...?! So many... Could it be...? More than one... person?
To make matters worse, one of the explosions has interfered with the communication devices, and your conversation with Nightingale is cut short.
Is this also part of the attacker's plan? Cough... That's quite impressive, I must admit...

speaker: Hecate
content: Can't believe someone has managed to break into the Bureau, and in such a haphazard fashion. Didn't this person worry that they would get hurt because of the explosions?
I don't think it was haphazard. It seemed like a clever move to me...
Consider the explosions. They were not large in scale. It's unlikely they were aimed at demolishing buildings or causing destruction. Cough... The explosions are probably a means to an end...
Still, it was a violent means of distraction. Who knows how much more violent it can be when it comes time for the attacker to achieve the end?
In any case, before we figure out the true purpose of the attack, we must... cough... proceed with caution...

speaker: Hecate
content: I understand. Chief, you shouldn't be talking.
Then comes a frantic knock on the door.
Are you still in there, Chief? Better hurry and take shelter. It'll be too late once smoke appears.
The door, which hasn't been securely closed, opens, and Hecate's sharp eyes take in that familiar medical attire.

speaker: Hecate
content: Did Adjutant Nightingale send you? The Chief isn't feeling well. Do you have any medicine with you?

speaker: Nurse
content: The elevator's out of service, and I wasn't able to bring the cart up here. I only have a few common medications on me.

speaker: Nurse
content: What's wrong with the Chief? Let me see if there's anything... Ahhh!
The nurse has been in the room for just a few minutes when another explosion occurs, closer still. The floor shakes, and she loses her balance and lurches forward.

speaker: Hecate
content: Are you all right?

speaker: Nurse
content: (Groans) I'm fine, I'm fine. Let me see if there's any medication that can alleviate your discomfort.

speaker: Nurse
content: And we need to get out of here now, Chief. You might have to suffer for a while longer. This most recent explosion was very close. It's more likely than not that the attacker is coming for you.
Cough... Thank you.
But we shouldn't leave this place. And it is precisely because the attacker is coming for me.

speaker: Nurse
content: Huh?
The first explosion was to attract attention, the second to destroy communication... Cough... This attacker is not only skilled but also purposeful.
So this most recent explosion, even though it couldn't destroy any building, it must have served a purpose...
Like... to lure you out of safety into their turf.

speaker: Nurse
content: Ah, I think I get it now! The enemy expects us to evacuate after the explosion, and if we do, we'll fall right into their trap!

speaker: Nurse
content: So it's better to stay here and wait for rescue. That way, when Adjutant Nightingale sends people to help us, they'll know where to find us.
Cough, cough... Exactly.
You and Hecate may have some work to do, though. We need to hold out here until Nightingale arrives with reinforcements, and there might be more explosions or other forms of attack in the meantime.

speaker: Nurse
content: Leave it to us! But... there isn't much I can do here, other than to help alleviate the Chief's discomfort.

speaker: Nurse
content: If the attacker really...

speaker: Hecate
content: If the attacker really comes, I'll handle them.

speaker: Hecate
content: I'll guard the door. Anyone who wants to harm the Chief has to get past me and Nightmare first.
Your analysis has eased the minds of the young nurse and Hecate, and they have found what they can do to help. You lean back and breathe a sigh of relief.

speaker: Nurse
content: Hey, Hecate, come take a look at this...

speaker: Hecate
content: Hmm... Ahhh!
Hecate!!!
It's happened all too quickly. The nurse, who was full of concern just a minute ago, has struck Hecate on the back of the neck with the side of her hand, knocking Hecate out. You sit up abruptly.
Then she draws a Fire Blade from her waist, her eyes murderous.
Cough... So you're the attacker. Your plan was effective, and your reactions were quick. You've won, I concede.
If you want to kill me, be my guest. But before you do so, at least let me know who I've lost to.
You can't make out the attacker's face, but her murderous intention is unmistakable. The situation is dire, and you must find a way to save yourself.

speaker: Assassin
content: Fishing for information, huh? Even when you're so close to death.
You don't have to be so guarded. Let's talk. You're young. Cough... You probably don't think much about the consequences before acting, right?
Well, you should. I'm the Chief of the MBCC, a position of no small importance. If you strike me down, whoever has put you up to this might be able to get out of this unscathed, but you...
You don't spell out the consequences the assassin might face, in case they're construed as a threat. But you believe she understands what is implied.
I give you my word that if you make a deal with me, I'll let all of this go. That way, you can achieve your goal more easily, without all this...

She has done a good job of disguising herself, but her youthfulness and the aura of malice are unmistakable. These are the few clues you must take advantage of, if you wish to stir her emotionally and stop her from killing you.
Moreover, the more scornful she is of you, the more certain you are that she's hiding something.

speaker: Assassin
content: You can stop this pathetic attempt to stall for time. I won't fall for it.

speaker: Assassin
content: I can get what I want without making a deal with you. I only have to kill you to get it!
The attacker steps over the various pieces of furniture you've overturned in an attempt to buy time, going for your vulnerable spots; she is merciless, determined, and extremely calm.

speaker: Assassin
content: So... Die now!

speaker: Hecate
content: ...Nightmare!
At this critical juncture, Hecate wakes up. In a hoarse voice, she shouts, "Nightmare!" Nightmare swoops in and hurls a heavy table at the assassin.
The assassin dodges the table, but only narrowly. A sharp corner of the table grazes her face, damaging her disguise.

speaker: Assassin
content: Tsk tsk, what a nuisance.
A stranger's face?
How could there be two strangers in such a short time span who would go to any lengths to kill you?

speaker: Hecate
content: Chief, watch out!
You duck just in time to avoid the projectile. Thanks to Hecate and Nightmare, you've managed to put some distance between you and the assassin, but she is still too close for comfort.
You'll be cornered, if you don't do something soon. The fire and the assassin... You must find a way to break the deadlock.
While the assassin is busy fighting Nightmare, you grab anything that lies near you and throw them at her, hoping to distract her. Bottles, cups, documents... even your communication device.

It is an act of desperation. Surprisingly, it works wonders. Right after you throw the last object at your disposal, a red light appears in the room. It's a shade of red different from that of the Fire Blade.

The light is coming from the projector, which you've turned on by accident. Coquelic's medical log is being displayed. The numbers and letters in the log are either white or red, as is Coquelic's face in the photo. The assassin's face is illuminated.
She stares at the pale face in the photo, frozen.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Seize the opportunity, rescue the Chief!
You hear a familiar voice. It's Nightingale. She's arrived with reinforcements. The staff members and Sinners swarm in and quickly restrain the assassin.
You are hurried to the side, to a safe zone set up by the Sinners. One of them even has had a thin blanket ready for you.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, are you all right? Do you need to rest? No? All right, please don't push yourself too hard.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Here is the current state of affairs: The attacker has been apprehended, the fire is being extinguished, and on account of the satisfactory execution of the disaster response plan, the explosions did not result in any casualties.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Given this person's high Threat Rating and aggressive behavior, I suggest we put her in solitary confinement for now. We can consider how to proceed from there after a thorough investigation.
Hmm...

speaker: Assassin
content: Don't you dare!

speaker: Assassin
content: I'm gonna kill you! Just wait and see. I'm gonna kill you!
You look at the assassin, who is pinned down but still looking daggers at you. She's gripping the terminal so hard that its casing is creaking. She is still dangerous.

But you won't forget that unexpected moment when she was at a complete loss, when her true self surfaced, though only for a split second. It was the sight of Coquelic's medical log that drew this reaction from her.
This may be the window of opportunity you've been waiting for.
No, don't put her in solitary. Get the interrogation room ready. I want to interrogate her now.
No doubt she'll be useful in helping me solve the puzzle that's been nagging at me lately.

The lights come on, so harsh that your eyes, though long used to bright light, narrow slightly. The Sinner in front of you, however, stares unblinkingly at you, as if her hostility toward you is strong enough to override her physiological instincts.
You don't like me, do you? Or should I say... hate me?
But I don't recall ever provoking or hurting you.

speaker: Thistle
content: You must've persecuted quite a few Sinners, by the sound of it.
Oh? Looks like someone told you that I'm a supervillain who persecutes Sinners.
Was this the same person who sent you to assassinate me?

speaker: Thistle
content: No one told me anything, and I don't need to be told to know how dangerous those darn shackles of yours are to us Sinners. Even a half-wit knows that.
She sneers and gives a shake of her hand, seemingly remembering the red thorns that appeared when the shackles pierced her body.

speaker: Thistle
content: You restrain Sinners with your shackles, lock them up in this place. I've seen it with my own eyes. I want to kill you, and that's my own decision!
She's stubborn. It seems you won't be able to get the information you need out of her by persuasion. You have to try a different approach.
test
test
test
test
test
test
I understand why you feel this way, but I can't just let this matter drop without giving it a try. Sorry.
Since you're not forthcoming... well, let me show you the information I've found about you. For instance, your residential records.
You used to report incidents to the authorities quite often, and as a result, there is no lack of biological information about you on record, so it wasn't difficult to find a match.
Thistle stares at you with cold eyes, as if waiting for you to make your move. You sigh and continue.
It's not my intention to reopen old wounds... You come from an FAC family, right?
And you tried very hard to seek revenge on behalf of your parents.
The girl in front of you remains silent, but you observe a slight tremble in her eyelids. So you open the file and start reading aloud.
Hills, female, father a member of the FAC, mother a homemaker. After her father died in battle in N.F. 103, she was raised by her mother alone, and they later moved to the outskirts of Eastside.
In N.F. 111, Hills reported her mother's disappearance to the Eastside Public Security Bureau, but no file was opened. Her mother never reappeared, which effectively made her an orphan.
Perhaps because she has her guard up, upon hearing these details of her past, there is only a brief moment of surprise before she quickly regains her composure.

These few lines of text encapsulate the hardships that Hills has endured, hardships that should be too overwhelming for a young girl to overcome. And yet it appears that she has turned the page and has been toughened by her circumstances.
Would someone go out of their way to kill you just because they picture you as a bad person and think you may harm them?
Perhaps this is the root of your hatred toward us, the powers that be? Because the Eastside Public Security Bureau did not fulfill its duties?

But this matter has nothing whatsoever to do with the MBCC Sinners, nor with the Bureau or me. Or did you encounter something else that inspired your hatred of us, like the incident that turned you into a Sinner?

speaker: Thistle
content: Something else?

speaker: Thistle
content: I hate you because you're bullies who oppress the common people and bootlickers who do the bidding of the rich degenerates. That's reason enough!
It seems you're not going to tell me the truth. Well, it's understandable that you don't trust us. After all, you had no one to count on but yourself in your search for your mother.
The record shows that immediately after being refused help, you started looking for your mother on your own.

You were proactive. You did everything you could, and you did it by yourself. Asking passersby, putting up posters, letting the media know the injustice done to you and your mother... Very impressive, I must say.
But by the end of N.F. 111, you suddenly disappeared from the public eye, no longer active. No one knew where you went.
Why? Did someone approach you? Did this person offer to help you seek revenge and try to get you to join some organization?

speaker: Thistle
content: What if that was the case? What if it wasn't?

speaker: Thistle
content: Is this what you've been trying so hard to pry out of me by playing the good guy?
She sees through your strategy, making it clear to you that she's not buying it.
The carrot approach is not working. A change of tactic is called for.
All right then, let's lay our cards on the table. Actually, it doesn't matter if you answer my questions or not, because I have already found a clue.
Not long ago, there was one other reckless assassin who came to the Bureau for me.
Your fighting styles were very similar. I guess you two are from the same organization. Her name is...
...Coquelic. Do you know her? Well, if you helped me wrap this up quickly, maybe I could take you to see her, before it's too late...
You draw out your words, trying to sound disdainful. It's far from an award-winning performance, but it successfully provokes the Sinner.
Despite all her efforts to conceal the raging fire of anger beneath her calm exterior, the shackles convey it to you, as well as her attempt to use her abilities to summon her Fire Blade.

speaker: Thistle
content: You're so obvious. Don't think I can't see through your little game. You're a lousy actor.

speaker: Thistle
content: Continue with your performance, but you're never gonna get any information out of me.
Is that so? I may be an awful actor, but you're worse.
In case you don't already know, the shackles are an infallible lie detector.
She's speechless. This is the reaction you've been waiting for. Your strategy is working.

Truth be told, you wouldn't have resorted to such an extreme method, if it weren't for the fact that the clock is ticking for that person on the sickbed and you don't have the time to slowly coax the information out of Thistle.
From the look of things, you two really do belong to the same organization. It was she who brought you to the Garden in N.F. 111, wasn't it?
I hear they excel at exploiting character flaws, like anger and the desire for vengeance, by molding them into a force they can command.
This is probably what happened to you. You were deceived and manipulated, eventually becoming a knife in Coquelic's hands.
Did she promise you that, as long as you joined the Garden, you would have a chance to take revenge?
The president of the Future Foundation died at your hands. And that was the chance Coquelic promised you, the Garden's killer, wasn't it? You must be very grateful to her, right?
Thistle's expression looks nothing like that of someone whose darkest secret has just been exposed; she simply sneers.

speaker: Thistle
content: Yes, I am a member of the Garden, and I am grateful to the Mentor. So what?

speaker: Thistle
content: Yes, she created a chance for me to take revenge. She is always willing to take a chance on people like me, people in the gutter! Without her, we wouldn't have been able to survive, much less avenge ourselves.

speaker: Thistle
content: She is our Mentor, the best and strongest member of the Garden! Of course I'm grateful to her. You're not so delusional as to expect me to be grateful to you bastards, are you?
Thistle remains defiant and confrontational, making sharp retorts at every turn.
But you can tell from her clenched fists and her sudden talkativeness that she is reaching the limit of her patience.

speaker: Thistle
content: Where were you when we were being persecuted? Where were you when we were being forced into a corner? Now that we've sorted things out ourselves, you're coming at us in the name of "justice"?

speaker: Thistle
content: You take us for pushovers? You think we won't fight back?

speaker: Thistle
content: Well, let me tell you this: we're not something to be scoffed at!

speaker: Thistle
content: That's why I'm targeting you. That's why I must get rid of you. And I will get rid of you. How about that, are you satisfied with this answer?
She's still hiding something. But this is the closest you've gotten to her true feelings. You know that one more step in the right direction, and you'll have a clear view of her inner self.
Get rid of me? That might be difficult for you. After all, even your "best and strongest" Mentor couldn't do it.

And that's the part I can't quite wrap my head around. I expected her, as your Mentor, to be much more cool-headed and cautious than you. So why would she attempt to assassinate me knowing full well that there was little chance of success?

At the very least, she should've brought some Garden members along, like you; that was just the smart thing to do from a professional standpoint. Given her physical condition at the time and the lack of help, her attempt on my life was doomed from the start.
Ah, I get it now. Is it because you're too weak, and she deemed you unworthy, so she didn't bring you along? She wanted nothing to do with you, did she?
After all, you couldn't even handle the Bureau's...
Clang!
Before you can finish your sentence, Thistle lunges at you; you've received no warning from the shackles.

Clearly, propelled by extreme fury, Thistle has experienced a burst of energy and has broken all the restrictions placed on her. She has crawled over the interrogation room's cold metal table, and is about to punch you straight in the face.

speaker: Thistle
content: Die! Die! Die!

As she has lunged at you, her body has hit the table, making a dull sound, but she doesn't cry out in pain, nor does she shrink back in the slightest, so intense is her fury and so determined is she to unleash that fury on your face.

She is opting for brute force over tactics or her special power. In this very moment, she is once again that helpless little girl from many years ago whose passion was the only thing that propelled her.
Looking into Thistle's eyes up close, you become more acutely aware of the intensity of her desire to kill you and of the foot of the desire.
Was Coquelic's reckless attempt on your life the product of the same logic?

speaker: Hecate
content: Nightmare, protect the Chief!
In the nick of time, the door crashes open, and Nightmare swoops in, and lifting you by the back of your collar, swiftly transports you out of harm's way.
Nightingale and many others rush into the interrogation room, forming a protective semi-circle around you that separates you from the dangerous attacker.

speaker: Wynn
content: Chief! Are you all right? Are you hurt? Do I have to remind you that you're still recovering?

speaker: Nightingale
content: All right, get the A-Class Sinner under control first. Make sure she is completely incapacitated this time!

speaker: Nightingale
content: The rest of you, get out of the way. Don't crowd around the Chief. Give the medical staff some space, so they can do their work.
Because of Nightingale's clear instructions, order is quickly restored in the interrogation room.
But Hecate pays no heed. She rushes to your side. Her voice trembles with fear when she speaks.

speaker: Hecate
content: Chief, you... Didn't you say you knew you hadn't fully recovered and wouldn't provoke her?

speaker: Hecate
content: If... If Adjutant Nightingale hadn't been keeping a close watch on you, and if we hadn't arrived in time to protect you, what would have become of you?
All right, all right... I'm totally fine. You can see it for yourself. Don't be mad now. I promise I won't do it again...
You console the MBCC members gathered around you, listening to their complaints, making promises. Their voices somehow make the interrogation room feel like a home, even just for a while.
Still...

While receiving caring words and concerned looks, you've never taken your eyes off the young Sinner sitting on the floor for a moment. She keeps her head down. You can't see her expression, but you know she hasn't given up.

speaker: Thistle
content: <size=30>...Don't think this will dissuade me from my goal... It won't...</size>

speaker: Thistle
content: <size=30>I may not be able to go after you now, or save the Mentor, but it won't stay this way forever...</size>
Thistle's voice is low but firm. She is feeling frustrated at yet another failure, but is trying hard to turn the frustration into a motivator.
You sigh and walk toward her.
You silly child, you can't hurt me. As you've seen, I'm surrounded by people who would do anything to protect me, much like you would do anything to protect your Mentor.
So I wouldn't say what you did was wrong. I believe that, the way you saw it, that was the best course of action open to you.

speaker: Thistle
content: ...What are you trying to say?
What I'm saying is, your escapade has given me a new perspective. Thanks to you, I now understand why that woman was so desperate to take my life.

speaker: Thistle
content: What do you mean?
Her eyes widen. She looks deflated. The anger and resentment are gone. In their place is panic, an emotion you haven't seen her display until now.
She's scared that her recklessness might have become a blade that will be used to hurt her Mentor, and that unwittingly, she has once again helped someone pry into her Mentor's plans.
Now... Cough, cough...
Let someone you trust more explain it all to you. After her explanation, you might look at the situation from a whole new perspective.
You cough into your hand and then nod at Nightingale.
Nightingale leaves the room. A moment later, she returns, followed by a girl dressed in detective attire.

speaker: Christina
content: Look at the state of you! Why do you always look a mess every time I see you?

speaker: Thistle
content: It's you...?!

speaker: Christina
content: What, are you not pleased to see me? I heard an old acquaintance of mine was causing havoc again because of her impulsive tendencies, so I dropped everything and rushed back.

speaker: Christina
content: You seem to have quite a few misunderstandings about the MBCC. I'll set you straight. But let's have those wounds looked at first. Come, follow me...
...Oh, there's also Sumire... Including Thistle, over 70% of the members have been found, if I'm not mistaken...
As for Coquelic, there seem to be some promising developments in the new treatment plan...

speaker: Terminal
content: One new meeting request pending approval. Applicant: Sinner Thistle. Desired time of meeting: As soon as possible.
Seeing the name that just flashed through your mind, you smile and press "Approve."

speaker: Hecate
content: Chief, are you sure you want to meet her here?

speaker: Hecate
content: There are so many important documents here. If she... the loss would be significant. Besides, there is your health to consider.
Christina has talked with her, and the record has been set straight.
I don't think there will be any problems. Let's play it by ear then.
Presently, the office door opens and Thistle walks in.
That was quick! You haven't been waiting to see me, have you? Please take a seat.

speaker: Thistle
content: I... I think I'll stand. I... I just have a question to ask you.
I see. Well, as long as you're comfortable.
There is a silence. You wait for Thistle to speak. She looks so out of her element; under Hecate's watchful eye, she doesn't seem to know where to put her hands.

speaker: Thistle
content: I, um... I, um, wanted to ask you...
Thistle opens her mouth, guilt writ large on her face, but after much hemming and hawing, she closes it again.
She's taking forever to get out whatever she's come to say. Hecate's body, unable to maintain the state of high vigilance, relaxes slightly.
You laugh, feeling at ease now. Thistle is no longer that dangerous girl harboring feelings of intense hostility toward you. It's only pride that's keeping her from opening up.
Ah, I think I have a pretty good idea of what you want to say. Hecate, could we give us a minute?
Don't worry. Everything is gonna be fine.
Hecate understands what you're trying to say. Somewhat reluctantly, she leaves in silence. In the doorway, she, almost childishly, casts a stern look at Thistle, as if to say, "I haven't forgotten."
That look seems to make Thistle even more uneasy. It is some time before she starts speaking, in a halting voice.

speaker: Thistle
content: ...W-Why didn't you tell me?
Tell you what?

speaker: Thistle
content: That you were feeble because you were bearing some of the Mentor's Mania with your shackles...

speaker: Thistle
content: You should've told me. I feel like an ungrateful idiot.
If I had told you, would you have believed me?
She falls silent, a somewhat guilty look on her face. Clearly, both of you know the answer to that question.
She doesn't stay silent for long. With a determined expression on her face, she brings up your previous questions.

speaker: Thistle
content: The things you tried to get out of me before, do you, um, still want to know them?

speaker: Thistle
content: Since it isn't you who've harmed the Mentor, I guess it's okay to share them with you. Assuming, of course, that you still think they are useful to you.
Of course. I really want to know.
Thistle starts telling you what happened to her after the turmoil in N.F. 113, up until Coquelic's attempt on your life at the Bureau; that's the missing piece of your puzzle.

It was by no means a comfortable existence. The Garden had collapsed overnight, and Thistle had to flee with her severely wounded Mentor. It was a time of scarcity for them. Thistle kept a low profile in the West District, going into hiding when necessary but never stopping searching for the other Garden members.

As she recounts these tribulations of her life, there is no hint of complaint in her voice. She is in control of her emotions, and it is only when she mentions her Mentor's sudden departure—as well as her Mentor's failing health, and the missing Garden members, does she sound sorrowful.
This is the story of the Garden, told from a completely new perspective.
I see. So on the day the MBCC went to bring Coquelic in for questioning, you weren't on the scene?
And you don't know the whereabouts of the Sinners she commanded to leave her that day, or how they are doing now?

speaker: Thistle
content: Yes. S-Sorry, I wish I could be more useful...
Nonsense. You've been a great help. Don't worry, we'll find your companions, every one of them.
Of course, we'll need your continued support. The Bureau knows very little about them, so we could use all the clues we can get regarding their whereabouts.
The same goes for Coquelic's treatment. We'll do our best to save her, but at the same time, we hope you and the other Garden members can offer whatever help you're able to provide.
Let's work together, Thistle.

speaker: Thistle
content: Certainly. If the others are here too... I have no doubt the Mentor will get better. And things won't be like they used to be...

speaker: Thistle
content: Please let me know if there's anything I can do. Even though the Mentor always finds me annoying... I think there must be something I can do.

speaker: Thistle
content: Anything I can do to help the Mentor, I mean anything, I'll do it.

She says these words with an intensity that makes you believe that if you were to say a certain panacea could be found in a certain place, she would dash out of the room to bring it back to save her beloved Mentor.

Actually, you find this intense side of her quite charming. She is genuine, proactive, and has unshakable core beliefs. If you look past her indifferent facade, she is very much like Christina. Yes, she can be impulsive, but at the same time, it can be invigorating to be around someone like her.

options: There is something you can do now.

speaker: Thistle
content: What is that?
Go see your Mentor.
You withdraw a document from the pile of papers near at hand, turn it, and hand it to her. It details the changes in Coquelic's vital signs following visits from Garden Sinners.
Since visits were allowed, many Garden Sinners have applied to visit Coquelic, and her vital signs have shown some improvement.
Although the medical staff were initially skeptical of my theory, she indeed responds to your voices.
Currently, a new treatment plan based on this phenomenon is in its final stages of validation. Maybe your visit could further bolster their confidence.
You thought Thistle would agree there and then, but she doesn't. Then you realize that she has never applied to visit Coquelic, which is unusual.

speaker: Thistle
content: Me visiting my Mentor? Would it really help? I... I think that might not be a good idea.

speaker: Thistle
content: I... I'm so weak, I always mess up the Mentor's plans. She even finds my presence annoying...

speaker: Thistle
content: If my visit ended up having the opposite effect... It's better to just let the other members visit her...
She finds you annoying because you're weak? Why would you think that?

speaker: Thistle
content: The Mentor told me so herself... on the morning of that day when you attacked.

speaker: Thistle
content: That day, I figured that since the Mentor hadn't had a petal bath in a while, I should prepare one for her. But when I tried to... she told me to leave, to get out of her sight. I still remember her words.

speaker: Coquelic
content: Ah, stop buzzing around in front of me. It's irritating! So much fuss! Could you please give me a moment's peace?

speaker: Coquelic
content: If you really have nothing better to do, then get out of my sight and send someone capable in. Garofano or Sumire, either would do.

Thistle's impression of Coquelic fails to capture the essence of the latter's demeanor, but judging by the fact that she could recite Coquelic's exact words, it's clear that she has taken her Mentor's disdain to heart.
Hmm, I don't know what a "capable" person is like in your Mentor's eyes, but I don't think you're weak.
You broke through the Bureau's security, made it all the way to my sickbed, and nearly finished me off.
And you say you're weak? Nightingale, who spent three days tabulating the damage you caused, would be among the first to disagree with you.
Your attempt at humor fails to dispel Thistle's gloom completely. She is still puzzled, but not as convinced of her Mentor's dislike of her as before.

speaker: Thistle
content: But if I'm not weak, then why would the Mentor...
I think it's because she wanted to get you out of harm's way.
A Sinner from the Garden told me that she seemed to be waiting for someone that day.
She must have known in advance about the MBCC's operation... So she made up some excuse and sent you away.

speaker: Thistle
content: The Mentor was prepared to fight you guys to the death, right?

speaker: Thistle
content: The only reason she sent me away at a time like that... could only be that she thought I was too weak to be of any help, right? She let the other members stay, after all.
For the first time, Thistle has laid bare her inner conflict for you to see. Looking at this perplexed girl, you make a valiant attempt not to smile.
Try looking at it from a different angle. As you know, that day in the Garden, your Mentor made herself the target of MBCC fire and ordered the other members to escape.
If you hadn't been sent away, would you have obeyed your Mentor's order and run away like the others?

speaker: Thistle
content: Of course not!
She answers your question without the slightest hesitation, as if it were a reflex action. You can't help but laugh a little.
There you have it. If I were your Mentor, I'd have done the same thing.
It's not that she didn't trust you, and certainly not that she thought you were too weak and would hold her back.
It's because she knew, to protect you, she had to take a different approach with you than with the other members. There was no other way around it.
Her eyes light up at your words. You can't help but reach out and ruffle her hair, the way you do with Hella and Hecate.
Honestly, I didn't understand Coquelic at first. To me, she was just like a madwoman.
But now, having had the chance to meet you, I finally understand her. I've been there myself. I understand what one must do to protect, not just some of, but all of the people one cares about.
Everyone is unique. You take each person's personality into account when you try to devise a course of action to ensure their safety. What works with one person might not work with the next.
That's why you might choose to take someone under your wing to keep them safe, or you might decide to send them away to prevent harm from coming their way.

speaker: Thistle
content: Sob... Mentor...

speaker: Coquelic
content: All right, stop crying now. Did you really think anybody could hurt me? Look at me, not a scratch—good as new. It was not a big deal. I told you I'd be back. Have I ever lied to you?

speaker: Hecate
content: Chief, you... Didn't you say you knew you hadn't fully recovered and wouldn't provoke her?
All right, all right... I'm totally fine. You can see it for yourself. Don't be mad now. I promise I won't do it again...
Something you said must have touched Thistle. She's now looking at you spellbound.

speaker: Thistle
content: Mentor...
Hmm...

speaker: Thistle
content: I mean, is that really what the Mentor thought?
Hmm...
As you ponder, the terminal makes a beep that signals the arrival of an urgent message.
Under Thistle's anxious gaze, you call up the message and read it.

speaker: Thistle
content: Is... is it about the Mentor?
Yes.

Thistle correctly intuits the message is about Coquelic; it is as if they are connected spiritually in some way. This reminds you of how Coquelic, even in her deep slumber, is responding to the voices of the Garden members.
The message is from the medical team, saying that for the first time, Coquelic's vital signs have significantly improved, and there are no signs of relapse.
Go see her. Call her name, say whatever you want to say to her, ask whatever you want to ask her...
Maybe she'll wake up and answer you right away.
No sooner have you finished speaking than Thistle turns on her heel and runs away. Watching her retreating figure, you smile and shake your head, and then you push yourself up from the table.
Everyone is doing what they can to wake you up from your long sleep. I can't be lazy either. Of course, neither can you.
The Mentor of the Garden. I'm looking forward to the day you wake up. Hope it won't be far away. A lot of people are waiting for you to wake up.
The late-night office is silent with only the gentle hum of the air conditioner, a sharp contrast to the piercing male voice on the other end of the call.
I've been calling for half an hour. Glad you're finally free to pick up the phone.
You glance at the two-digit number following the caller ID, mustering the energy to switch to your most polite voice.

speaker: Chief
content: Excuse me, may I know if you're Shrooma's...?

speaker: Chief
content: I've already explained the situation to Shrooma's aunt, second aunt-in-law, and third cousin when they called before.

speaker: Chief
content: We're at a crucial stage of the summer camp and we strongly advise against taking her away unless it's absolutely necessary, as this would cause her to fall behind her classmates...
Cut it out if you're just going to repeat the same thing!
The man's voice interrupts you vehemently, as if your rehearsed sentences have kindled his pent-up anger.
Like we've emphasized repeatedly, the banquet in two days is of utmost importance to our family. We need Shrooma to be there despite any situation!
She's our golden girl who's never made a mistake. She will serve her family when need be. When we called before, didn't you praise her a lot too?
In that case, why would you stop her from leaving the camp for just one night?!
As her guardians, we have every right to suspect that something's gone wrong under your supervision! Your every move is a deliberate cover-up!
Despite any situation, "golden girl," "serve her family"... His anger sounds genuine, which only makes you more helpless.
It's hard to imagine these words being used on a schoolgirl and worse still, turned by her guardians into an unavoidable curse against you, the "instructor."

speaker: Chief
content: Our summer camp is compliant with all the regulations, please do not worry. That being said... I hear what you're saying.

speaker: Chief
content: If the guardians insist, we will review Shrooma's leave request and provide you with a definite answer the soonest we can.
It was wise to back down. After getting a satisfactory answer, the man immediately ends the call. His purpose can't be made clearer.
Before you can catch your breath, the ever-efficient Adjutant Nightingale brings you the important file you're waiting for. A folder containing the necessary documents to bail Shrooma out.

speaker: Nightingale
content: According to the documents, Sinner Shrooma's psychological evaluation, supervision records, and special power assessment have all passed review, but she firmly refuses to sign the bail form.
The blank form speaks for the girl's decision. You can't help but pinch your nose bridge.

speaker: Chief
content: Her guardians are equally adamant about her attending the so-called banquet and won't stop pressuring us. We must find a way to untangle this deadlock...

speaker: Nightingale
content: Considering her situation, her bail request will no doubt be accepted. Chief, why don't you open up to her guardians about the truth of the "summer camp" and tell them what she thinks?

speaker: Chief
content: We still don't know why she refuse bail. Maybe she simply doesn't want to go home. Doing so would mean shifting the pressure onto Shrooma.

speaker: Chief
content: Let's arrange for an interrogation tomorrow. I think we need to have an in-depth talk with our little Sinner.

speaker: Shrooma
content: Greetings, Chief.
The girl in the interrogation chair sits upright, her hands placed neatly on her knees, good upbringing reflected even in her perfect smile.

speaker: Chief
content: Morning, Shrooma.

speaker: Chief
content: How are you finding life in the Bureau? Everything good?

speaker: Shrooma
content: I'm a bit attached to my usual bed, so my sleep has been affected slightly. Other than that, everything's fine.

speaker: Shrooma
content: Everyone here doesn't fuss over me because of my age and I get along with them well. Adjutant Nightingale also takes good care of me.

speaker: Shrooma
content: Overall, I think I'm adapting pretty well. At least I feel much better than at school! After all, on campus, big shots like you will never personally check on me like this.
She answers honestly in a relaxed tone. As far as interrogations go, it's a good start.
But you sense that she's still wary of you. She can clearly tell you're not here just for small talk. Unfortunately, her hunch is right.

speaker: Chief
content: That's great to hear. I'm glad you're adjusting well to your new life and not feeling stressed from the change.

speaker: Chief
content: I've noticed you seem to be posting fewer rants on forums recently.

speaker: Chief
content: Is that why you refuse to be bailed out and go back to school and your family?
You gently tap the blank signature section of the bail form on the desk with your knuckle, inquiring about Shrooma's thoughts with a dull thud.

speaker: Chief
content: Is it because hiding here allows you to escape the overwhelming stress in your life, just like hiding behind a fake username on a forum?
The girl's pupils contract slightly, clearly taken aback by your bluntness. She bites her lip almost defensively.

speaker: Chief
content: Don't be afraid. I'm not here to lecture you today. I just want to know what concerns you about the bail.

speaker: Chief
content: We understand that the current pre-bail assessment may not be enough. If you feel that your family and social circles can't provide you enough support to return as a Sinner...

speaker: Chief
content: The Bureau will not force you to go back.
A long silence. When Shrooma speaks again, her honesty becomes more genuine, yet also more aggressive, much like the voices on the other end of those phone calls.

speaker: Shrooma
content: ...That sounds fair. But Chief, that's not why you brought me here today, is it?

speaker: Shrooma
content: You just want me to sign the bail form and get out of here, right?

speaker: Shrooma
content: My family have been pushing you, haven't they? Are they circling you like hungry pigeons begging for food, bothering you?

speaker: Chief
content: Shrooma, you're more mature than I imagined.
"Mature" was your first impression of her, but right now, what she displays surpasses that apt maturity and turns into wisdom that demands serious attention.

speaker: Shrooma
content: You can be honest with me. I'm not the little fool you think I am.

speaker: Shrooma
content: My family is so eager for me to show up... Is it some important social event within their circle? Some boring upper-class ball? Or is it that banquet?

speaker: Shrooma
content: Your face tells that I've guessed right. It's the banquet.

speaker: Chief
content: ...Are all these things you just mentioned already scheduled?

speaker: Shrooma
content: Of course, my schedule is always full.
She sneers with disdain.

speaker: Shrooma
content: You must know how the high society of Eastside views immigrants. They despise these upstarts, and are also wary of the foreigners.

speaker: Shrooma
content: My family is no exception. As mere immigrant merchants, we don't qualify for invitations to those elite banquets.

speaker: Shrooma
content: Only through "academic socializing" can my family scrape into these disgusting exchanges to pick up some leftovers.

speaker: Shrooma
content: The so-called pure, non-political socializing among family successors in their youthful school days.

speaker: Shrooma
content: In reality, it's just a hypocritical show they put their children through.

speaker: Shrooma
content: Show off your superb violin skills and upper-class etiquette... And show off your family's obedience and humility toward the rules!
The well-trained smile that Shrooma always wears has long disappeared.
Her habitual obedience is no doubt also just a "show"... Probably a social capital her family uses to exchange for benefit.

speaker: Chief
content: Is that why you refuse to sign the form and go home? Because you're tired of adults asking you to "put on a show"?

speaker: Shrooma
content: Of course!
Your words are free of contempt, but Shrooma still raises her voice as if triggered.

speaker: Shrooma
content: Those who barely made it into an elite school don't deserve to enjoy youth! Not only must I get good grades, but I also need to flatter my classmates!

speaker: Shrooma
content: Which means enduring every jerk's pranks and kissing those idiots' arse! Only then can I become the class president and get those invitations for my family!

speaker: Shrooma
content: Who would want that kind of life? I can't even breathe! Everywhere I go, I must keep that same smile and repeat "it's okay" again and again!
She growls out the words as her chest heaves slightly, her emotions finally peeking over the high walls built by so-called etiquette and discipline.
This reminds you of those anonymous posts she posted on forums, venting her hatred toward the arrogant classmates and snobbish teachers. You begin to understand her.
She must keep putting on a perfect show for her family's benefit and to spare them harm. The internet might be the only outlet for her emotions.
She's our golden girl who's never made a mistake. She will serve her family when need be.
But... rather than turning a blind eye to them, her family seem genuinely unaware of her suppressed disgust and emotions. They truly think she's "perfect." Why?

speaker: Chief
content: Do you never let down your disguise even in front of your family...? Are they dangerous to you too?

speaker: Shrooma
content: Huh? What? Are you saying that's what I should do, or that I shouldn't be too sensitive?!

speaker: Chief
content: No, I didn't mean that. It's just that your family is not as loving and caring as our initial assessment suggested, which is an oversight on our part.

speaker: Chief
content: Such an environment may not be accepting enough to accommodate a Sinner who could bring more risks than benefits.

speaker: Shrooma
content: You think so too, don't you? How could a family accept a Sinner if they can't even accept her "imperfections"?

speaker: Chief
content: Yes, I understand. In that case, agreeing to be bailed out and revealing your identity as a Sinner indeed bring more harm than good.

speaker: Shrooma
content: Exactly! Since you get it now, does that mean I can...!
Her eyes light up. Perhaps your empathy, sincerity, and courage to admit your mistakes have moved her.
But that's also why you can't brush her off with lies.

speaker: Chief
content: Hold on, let me finish. This is just a guess, and since your legal guardians are still alive, the Bureau has no legitimate reason to take over your guardianship.

speaker: Chief
content: Whether you get bailed out or not, the rules demand us to disclose your identity as a Sinner to your guardians sooner or later.

speaker: Shrooma
content: ...What if I never sign the bail?
Back to square one. Seeing Shrooma's childish attempt at passive resistance, you tentatively present the alternative you've prepared.

speaker: Chief
content: I understand your reluctance, but complete confidentiality is indeed unrealistic. There may be room for compromise...

speaker: Chief
content: For instance, can your parents or anyone in your family who can sign as your guardian help conceal the truth from the rest of your family?
The dimmed eyes, her silence, and those clenched fingers already answer your question.

speaker: Chief
content: Alright. In that case, we can come up with something else...
Before you finish speaking, your device rings. You glance at the screen and raise your hand, but your hovering fingers never pick it up.

speaker: Chief
content: Another unknown call? No, wait...
Shrooma seems to realize something. She stares intently at your hand, her gaze almost searing.
She leans forward, pupils shrunk... Beneath this aggressive look, you can sense a wavering fear. You know she's waiting for your "verdict."
The piercing ringtone never stops, tearing apart the thin trust recently established between you and Shrooma. The atmosphere has turned confrontational again.

speaker: Chief
content: ...Guess there's no other way.
In the tense air, your finger finally falls. You immediately hear the busy signal.

speaker: Shrooma
content: You hung up their call? What does this mean? Are you... going to side with me and help me skip the banquet?

speaker: Chief
content: Not really. I think we should attend it.
Before Shrooma shows any frustration or disappointment, you lay out the plan you've hastily put together.

speaker: Chief
content: But instead of bailing you out, we'll just apply for a leave. During this period, I will help conceal your identity as a Sinner.

speaker: Chief
content: I'll accompany you to the banquet as your instructor, and there I'll evaluate your family and social situation up close.

speaker: Chief
content: If your family can't positively influence your control over your emotions and power... As the Chief of the Bureau, I have the right to make the best managerial decision for my people.

speaker: Chief
content: Since you're not a little fool, you must understand what I mean, right?
Given Shrooma's precociousness, you're sure she understands your implication. But to your surprise, she doesn't seem as pleased and cooperative as you expected.
In her expression... you even see more painful hesitation than hopeful joy.

speaker: Shrooma
content: ...I see.
You take a mental note of this sophistication beyond her age, adding it to the list of mysteries about Shrooma you need to solve.

speaker: Shrooma
content: Oh, Mrs. Ritz, long time no see. I've tried the cookie recipe you taught me last time. It's really amazing...

speaker: Shrooma
content: Elle, my dear! Long time no see! I will catch up with you about the summer camp later...
As advised by Shrooma, the two of you arrive at the banquet well ahead of time. To your surprise, the place is already bustling before the event even starts.
Despite seeming repulsed by the banquet in the car, Shrooma is in her element once she enters the crowd, making small talk effortlessly with a perfect smile.
Shrooma, you're already here?
Shrooma stops at the voice, smiling as she turns to the three approaching figures. But standing right next to her, you notice her smile turn slightly stiff and her fingers clutch at her dress softly.

speaker: Shrooma's Grandfather
content: Oh, you must be the summer camp instructor who's been looking after Shrooma! I'm her grandfather. Thanks for taking care of our little one these days.

speaker: Chief
content: Not at all, Shrooma is very well-behaved and polite, and she is popular at the summer camp.

speaker: Shrooma's Grandfather
content: Haha, indeed, we always teach Shrooma to be kind and modest at home. I'm sure she wouldn't cause any trouble at the summer camp.

speaker: Shrooma's Grandfather
content: By the way, she's quite good at the violin. If you ever need a performance at the summer camp or other occasions, she'd be more than willing to make her group proud. Right, Shrooma?

speaker: Shrooma
content: That's true, Grandpa.
The old man smiles kindly and seems to speak well of Shrooma. But behind Shrooma's calm responses lies the repressed irritation from the shackles, like a bubbling swamp.
Perhaps it's due to his barely hidden disciplinary tone? You shift your gaze to the noble lady behind the old man, trying to change the subject for Shrooma.

speaker: Chief
content: And ma'am, you must be Shrooma's mother, right? Are you here to cheer for her performance?

speaker: Shrooma's Mother
content: Oh... Um. Hello. Yes, I...

speaker: Boy
content: Nice to meet you. I'm Shrooma's cousin, and I go by Joshua.
A little boy in an exquisite suit suddenly chimes in.

speaker: Joshua
content: I've always appreciated the summer camp hosted by your school. I was wondering if the food at the camp is really that good? Shrooma seems to have put on some weight since I last saw her.

speaker: Shrooma
content: Thanks for asking, Joshua, but I don't see any change in my weight.

speaker: Joshua
content: Shrooma, I'm still talking! Don't chime in. Grandpa already gave you the chance to do the solo performance, you can at least let me chat with the instructor!

speaker: Joshua
content: Besides, it's only because I care about you. You might worry about your weight but I don't. If you need any help about the solo, I'm here!

speaker: Shrooma's Grandfather
content: Joshua! Didn't I tell you not to joke about these things in public!

speaker: Shrooma's Grandfather
content: Today is the perfect opportunity for Shrooma to show you a good example! Learn from her and be wise!
The boy's remarks toward Shrooma are obviously pointed. The old man pretends to scold him before sending the two away with a look, then turns to you with an apologetic smile.

speaker: Shrooma's Grandfather
content: My apologies. These kids in our family are close, so sometimes they forget their manners. You know, boys at this age think everything is a joke.

speaker: Chief
content: Did he mean that as a joke?

speaker: Shrooma's Grandfather
content: Ah, I understand your point. Rather than joking, he was probably just concerned for his cousin!
The old man doesn't flinch at your question. You just know that even if you showed him the uncomfortable feelings from the shackles, he would simply pretend he didn't understand.
After all, even Shrooma's mother didn't say anything despite looking anxious.

speaker: Shrooma's Grandfather
content: Ah, Sir Hurst, I didn't expect to see you here! Yes, yes, it's Shrooma, the pride of our family...

speaker: Shrooma's Grandfather
content: Oh, you sure have a keen eye. This is Shrooma's instructor at the summer camp. Yes, that's right, the school has always valued us...

speaker: Hurst
content: Instructor at the summer camp? Hmm...
You feel uneasy. Sir Hurst has been looking you up and down for a while now.

speaker: Hurst
content: Excuse me, I may have mistaken you for someone else, but you do look familiar to me. You don't happen to be related to that Chief of the MBCC, do you?
Before you can come up with a sound excuse to deny that, the old man standing next to you already turns pale at the mention of the MBCC.

speaker: Shrooma's Grandfather
content: MBCC? Please joke about something else! We certainly have nothing to do with that! You know, we're all law-abiding citizens in our family. There have never been any degenerates among us!

speaker: Shrooma's Grandfather
content: Besides, the instructor is just assigned to lead the school's summer camp! Shrooma only signed up for it because she doesn't want to waste her summer break. I hear their coursework is very tense!

speaker: Hurst
content: Oh, of course, you're right. I've misspoken...
The old man's drastically different reaction to this "joke" is astonishing. His values and prejudice against Sinners are also repulsive.

speaker: Chief
content: Please excuse me, I'd like to go and check on Shrooma. I've got a few reminders for her before she goes onstage.
Having escaped the flattery, perfume, and finery with an excuse, you can finally breathe normally again.
The urgent task is to find Shrooma. Her mood is very unstable at the moment, which worries you a little.

speaker: Guest A
content: Did you see that family? Still the same, always turning the other cheek, except for when it comes to their reputation, that's when they get all worked up.

speaker: Guest B
content: That's how immigrants are. Their business relies entirely on their good reputation and connections. Say if there really was a Sinner in the family, who would dare be near them?

speaker: Guest A
content: True, but I just feel sorry for their poor children. They have to learn these trite rules from such a young age. Serve the family, never make a misstep, and all that...
The things you overhear as you weave through the crowd complete and confirm your suspicions about Shrooma's family.

speaker: Chief
content: For such a family... a child who brings no benefit and might potentially tarnish their reputation will never be accepted, or worse, she might be abandoned immediately.

speaker: Chief
content: This explains why Shrooma refuses to be bailed out and doesn't trust her family. As intelligent as she is, she must have foreseen this outcome.
However... you still feel something is off. After meeting her family, you now understand her secrecy, the mask she puts on, and her firm refusal, yet her actions remain contradictory.
The doubts in your heart have not vanished and are even intensifying with the quickening pulse from the shackles!

speaker: Chief
content: It still doesn't make sense... Judging from Shrooma's attitude, she should want to break free from her family's restraints.

speaker: Chief
content: But if that's the case, she should seize the opportunity to get bailed out, let her family reject her as a Sinner, and then escape. She shouldn't be trying to hide the truth. Unless...
Your steps slow down as the complex thoughts in your mind begin to unravel, revealing a conclusion you'd never considered before.

speaker: Chief
content: Unless... what she fears isn't the consequences, but the very fact that her Sinner identity is exposed to her family?

speaker: Chief
content: But why?

No matter the reason, this is clearly something you can't deduce with the information you currently have. You stop thinking and come to your senses, only to find yourself standing in front of an unfamiliar passage.

speaker: Joshua
content: Look at you, you can't even handle the summer camp, yet you dare to take the spotlight at the banquet? You're going to embarrass the family again!

speaker: Shrooma
content: You're right, Joshua. I think it should be your turn too. But since the decision is already made, you shouldn't worry about it anymore.

speaker: Chief
content: ...It's Shrooma and her cousin?

speaker: Joshua
content: What do I have to worry about?! You better make a fool of yourself onstage. That way, Grandpa will see who can truly shoulder the family's future!

speaker: Shrooma
content: I'm glad you're this ambitious. I'll be sure to convey that to Grandpa.
In contrast to her cousin's sharp, indignant tone, Shrooma's voice is calm and graceful, seemingly unwilling to argue with Joshua.
But despite her wish, her placatory attitude further enrages the boy, provoking him to scream almost hysterically.

speaker: Joshua
content: Quit acting like a goody-goody! You may be able to fool the outsiders, but do you think I don't know?!

speaker: Joshua
content: You really think you can hide it your whole life? Don't think any of your achievements will make everyone forget that thing about you and your monster mother!!

speaker: Joshua
content: Grandpa won't believe you, and neither will I. We're all watching you! You who did that to your sister even in the womb...

speaker: Shrooma
content: Joshua!!!
The word almost sounds spat out from a bottomless swamp, each syllable soaked with suppressed anger. Startled, the boy takes a few steps back.
You're instinctively aware that the interrupted sentence likely contains the secret Shrooma desperately wants to hide. But the tension doesn't allow you to listen in further.

Emotion is the explicit indicator of a Sinner's destructive power. And across the shackles, the negative emotions Shrooma has been accumulating since entering the venue are skyrocketing and about to explode.

speaker: Chief
content: Shrooma! How did you end up here?!
Right before Shrooma loses control, you shout her name and stride into the passage, verbally cautioning her while separating the two of them with your body.

speaker: Chief
content: Are you guys arguing about something? Joshua, would you calm down too? Anyway we are at the banquet.
Clearly not expecting you to hear his not-so-perfect words, the boy flees the scene in panic.

Only then do you turn around to look at Shrooma, who keeps her head down. Her fists are clenched, and her expression is hidden in the shadows, so you can only check her condition through the shackles.
Irritation, anger, fear... Her emotions still bubble like a boiling swamp, and you can only muster all your energy to suppress her nearly overflowing power.
Yet a few small mushrooms still sprout on the velvet-covered walls, their colors bright and vibrant, boldly displaying their poisonous nature.

speaker: Chief
content: Are you okay? Thankfully it's not too late. If someone found out...
The girl suddenly raises her head, interrupting you with a taunting smile. She seems to know you've overheard her secret and has given up pretending.

speaker: Shrooma
content: If someone found out? About what?

speaker: Shrooma
content: That I'm a loser who hates my so-called family? That I'm a Sinner, a monster?

speaker: Shrooma
content: A maggot in the gutter, a poisonous mushroom, a disgusting thing that must be hidden? Something that deserves to be ignored, chopped up, and thrown in the trash?

speaker: Chief
content: You know I would never think that.

speaker: Shrooma
content: Huh? Are you going to pretend you don't dislike me? Haven't you seen those posts? You should know full well what kind of person I am.

speaker: Shrooma
content: I know what they've written about me in those psychological assessments. You don't need to pretend that you understand me!

speaker: Shrooma
content: That's right, I'm a pathetic person. I typed every single one of those toxic words in those posts!

speaker: Shrooma
content: Those are all my true thoughts. Because yes, I hate everything!

speaker: Chief
content: Shrooma, listen to me. I will never despise or shun you because of the rants you posted on the dark web.
You try to calm her, but the explosive emotions have completely taken over the girl. The restless Mania is swirling around her, as if she exists in a vacuum filled only with malice.

speaker: Shrooma
content: It's true. I have a lot of malicious thoughts I need to get out of me! So what? Why can't I say them openly?

speaker: Shrooma
content: Why do you all despise malicious thoughts? As if you don't also get them? But everyone does, right?!
You shake your head, knowing it won't change anything even if you shout into her ear now.
So you give up on verbal communication and use the shackles to suppress her power, dragging her out of the banquet hall toward the empty courtyard.

speaker: Shrooma
content: W-what are you doing!!!
Shrooma lowers her voice in resistance. You drag her all the way to a big tree.

speaker: Chief
content: This will do.

speaker: Shrooma
content: Wh-what?

speaker: Chief
content: See this hollow in the tree? Shout into it. Say everything you've always wanted to say. Get it all out of your system.

speaker: Chief
content: Don't worry, I'll keep watch for you. No one will come.
Shrooma seems hesitant, but once she sees that you're serious, she pokes her head into the tree hollow gingerly and yells into it.

speaker: Shrooma
content: Joshua, you damn idiot! You brainless, stupid weirdo!!!
After that, she quickly pulls her head out and glances back at you. You command all your facial muscles to give her an encouraging smile.
This time, she seems to understand your intention. Her face looks enlivened and she turns back into the tree hollow, screaming again.

speaker: Shrooma
content: Go to hell, you *********!
After a while, Shrooma stops, panting heavily. Her face is flushed, but her eyes seem especially bright.

speaker: Chief
content: How does that feel? Better? Still want to let Mania take over you now?
Shrooma looks at you as if seeing you for the first time, scrutinizing you up and down.

speaker: Shrooma
content: Am... Am I... cursing too much?

speaker: Chief
content: The word choice is a little over the top, but emotionally, I understand it completely.
Seeming surprised at your response, Shrooma asks dazedly.

speaker: Shrooma
content: You're saying it's normal that I hold such malicious thoughts toward others?

speaker: Shrooma
content: It's okay to not hold back, and to vent it out like this? Am I not a piece of toxic trash?

speaker: Chief
content: First, let's get this right. What you were just venting, and those things you posted online, they are not malicious thoughts, just negative emotions.

speaker: Chief
content: Everyone gets these emotions, but if you don't handle them properly and promptly, they can fester into something more toxic. That's when it becomes real malice.

speaker: Chief
content: For instance, you almost got corrupted by Mania just now because you didn't handle them properly, which could have caused much greater harm than making posts online.

speaker: Chief
content: Of course, you may still harm others if you don't control the way you vent your emotions. That's where the Bureau comes in.

speaker: Shrooma
content: Do you also get such emotions and thoughts, Chief?

speaker: Shrooma
content: Do you also scream into tree holes like this?

speaker: Chief
content: ...Ahem, I'd appreciate some privacy.

speaker: Chief
content: In short, I don't think having negative emotions makes you a piece of toxic trash, or anything like that.
Shrooma looks stunned, as if hearing this kind of words for the first time. Her effort to digest your saying looks cute but so heart-wrenching.
But just as you can't resist walking over to pat her head, she steps back.

speaker: Shrooma
content: ...Hmph, don't act like you know me so well. Wait until you find out about everything before playing the savior.

speaker: Shrooma
content: By then, you may despise me and regret having said all this today.
She turns around and runs toward the banquet hall. You consider running after her, but give up after some thought.
You turn your head and see the hem of a delicate and luxurious dress peeking out from the shadows.
From behind the slightly open door comes the sound of dragging footsteps. Shrooma pushes the door open and shuffles in with her rubber clogs, standing nonchalantly in front of you.

speaker: Shrooma
content: Why did you send for me suddenly? I thought you've blacklisted me or something!

speaker: Shrooma
content: Or is ignoring me not enough? You must get rid of me, huh? Am I on your to-be-executed list?
She talks with bubble gum in her mouth, occasionally blowing a pink bubble, but not skillful enough to make it last.
You've already heard from Nightingale about her recent behavior, but witnessing it with your own eyes still amuses you.

speaker: Chief
content: As far as I know, the Bureau doesn't have such a list.

speaker: Chief
content: But I'm glad to see you so active, Shrooma. It seems your life has become much more eventful in just a few days?

speaker: Shrooma
content: How can I resist? Everyone here is so having the gift of the gab. I just love it!

speaker: Shrooma
content: Besides, I've even got the wonderful Chief to care about me, haven't I? I'm simply overwhelmed with surprise!
She has an indifferent, cheeky grin on her face, as if waiting for you to look disgusted and scold her. But you simply smile gently.

speaker: Chief
content: Well, I'm the one who should be surprised. Why are you suddenly so candid in front of me? Have you given up on acting like a good kid?

speaker: Chief
content: What happened to "I did nothing wrong. You will see that very soon"?

speaker: Shrooma
content: Hey, you're not being fair. Haven't we done the tree hole-shouting thing together already? Why are you still playing dumb with me?
She points at the folder on the desk with her chin, her tone increasing precocious.

speaker: Shrooma
content: You've spent days investigating before coming to me. You must have all the evidence to keep me trapped for ten... No, for a lifetime.

speaker: Shrooma
content: So why would I keep pretending? I've got nothing to lose anyway!

speaker: Chief
content: I don't think you've done anything deserving of lifelong detention in the Bureau.

speaker: Shrooma
content: Huh? Is it fun to bait me? Or you wanna force me to confess it myself?
