content: For a while, I felt betrayed by you. How could you get better? We're supposed to be beaten down by society, living every day miserably, doing things we don't want to do. But I quickly realized that I had never been able to accept the fact that I was sick.

speaker: Angry Fan
content: Thank you for helping me recognize my wrong behavior. I'm going to therapy regularly now. I hope that one day... I'll be able to formally apologize to you in your comment section.
For a moment, Poffy's choked sobs are the only sound in the office. Tears dampen the screen, the video paused where the fans are giving Poffy a thumbs up.
You hand her some tissues thoughtfully. Once she's managed to collect herself, you take out a handmade seal plushie and give it to Poffy.

speaker: Chief
content: This was handmade by that fan of yours. She asked me to give it to you.

speaker: Chief
content: They all wanted me to tell you this: No matter how many times you change your account, they'll always follow you and watch your videos. And if you ever want to chat, they'll always be there for you.

speaker: Chief
content: They liked you in the past, and they like you now. As long as you're being yourself, they'll always be your fans. Because that's the real Poffy no one else gets to define.
As Poffy runs her fingers over the stitches of the little seal plushie, the tears she has just managed to stop begin falling again.

speaker: Poffy
content: I, I never thought... that someday I could be a source of strength for someone else...

speaker: Poffy
content: Actually, I was worried at first that I might have made a mistake. Would the new me end up disappointing the people who liked the old me? I felt lost about that for so long...
Poffy quickly goes through the entire pack of tissues. She grabs her sleeve and rubs her eyes before lifting her head to look at you.

speaker: Poffy
content: Thank you, Chief! Thank you for helping me find them, recording these videos, and bringing me their gifts. Hearing their encouragement and seeing their faces have helped me accept myself more and more!

speaker: Poffy
content: Chief, you... did so much for me without me knowing... Thank you for noticing my worries, helping me through my struggles, and even encouraging me to start my new account. You helped me get to where I am today... Ah, I'm gonna cry again, sob...
Poffy's tearful, emotional smile overwhelms you a little as well. You clear your throat, signaling for her to listen to what you're about to say.

speaker: Chief
content: Those were all gifts from your fans. I haven't given you my gift yet.

speaker: Chief
content: It's not an expensive or nostalgic gift. It's not handmade either. Um... unless a handwritten card counts as well.

speaker: Chief
content: I hope Miss Poffy, who's just reached a hundred fans, won't despise my gift.
Poffy takes the card from your hand, flips it over, and sees a line of text.
The next second, she clutches the card and rushes over to hug you, crying loudly.

speaker: Nightingale
content: What's going on?! Chief, did something happen?!
Nightingale rushes through the door looking extremely worried, only to witness the scene unfolding before her. The situation immediately spirals out of control.

speaker: Poffy
content: Chief! You're the best! Boohoo, wahhhh, why don't you just detain me? I don't ever want to leave anymore! I can stream from the Bureau! Wahhhhh!

speaker: Nightingale
content: What? Streaming from the Bureau? Chief, that's against our rules!

speaker: Chief
content: No, Nightingale, let me explain. That's not what Poffy means...

speaker: Poffy
content: Chief! Wahhhh! I love you so much, Chief!!!
Amid the chaos, the card slips from Poffy's hand and falls onto the desk.

This is a spell to control yourself. When you feel anxious, recite it three times:
Take a deep breath and relax
I can control my body
I can control my desires
I can calm my fears
I am in full control of myself and I can do this
[Scene Change]
Before leaving the Bureau, Poffy waves at you and mysteriously gestures for you to lean your ear closer.

speaker: Poffy
content: In fact... I set up my own arrest by the Bureau.

speaker: Chief
content: What?

speaker: Poffy
content: I had someone write you an anonymous letter and provide the leads. So the whole lurking glutton incident... Well, I made it up.

speaker: Poffy
content: I never actually lost control from hunger and attacked innocent passersby. I might have slipped up once or twice in the past, but I definitely wouldn't have let it happen a third time.
Poffy gives a cheerful laugh and waves goodbye to you. You say nothing, watching the direction she left in, and find yourself smiling too.
You open your work journal to the new evaluation you wrote some time after Poffy resolved her contract issues with MCN.
No plans, but plenty of ideas. No acting skills, but full of courage.
Since she wants to believe that she can create her own new beginning and shape her own path...
Then it's all good.

When you push open the interrogation room door, your steps falter for just a moment. The room is the same familiar space: one desk, two chairs, smooth walls, steady lighting. Yet something feels subtly off about these ordinary furnishings.

The items on the desk have been rearranged. The recording pens have been lined up, their tips all pointing in the same direction. File boxes that were once scattered have been stacked into perfect rectangles, their edges perfectly aligned. Even the paperclip holder that's always sat haphazardly on the desk corner has been placed parallel to the edge.
It's as if someone had arrived before you and reset the entire room to match its blueprint.

Your gaze travels across the desk, and you see a woman with dark red hair. She wears a pair of thin-rimmed glasses, the lenses catching a faint glint under the lights. Her Public Security Bureau uniform is perfectly pressed without a single crease, cuffs buttoned carefully.
She's reading through some documents with her head lowered, pen tip gliding rapidly across the pages, pausing occasionally to mark something down.

When she hears the door open, she doesn't look up immediately. Only after you approach the desk does she close the final page of the documents in her hand, file them neatly into her briefcase, and zip it shut with a crisp, efficient motion.
You glance at her, then speak tentatively.

speaker: Norma
content: Hello, Chief.

She glances up at you, then back down at her watch. The second hand ticks past a mark with a soft click. In the quiet room, the sound is especially clear, somehow creating a sense of urgency, reminding you that no time should be wasted.

speaker: You
content: Sorry for the wait. I hope I didn't interrupt your work.

speaker: Norma
content: Not at all. Thank you for being punctual. We still have two minutes and fourteen seconds until the scheduled time, but I typically allow a two-to-three-minute buffer for unforeseen circumstances. We can begin now.
She pauses briefly, her tone still flat and formulaic, devoid of any unnecessary emotion.

speaker: Norma
content: Chief, please close the door behind you. Time is limited, and I'd prefer not to be interrupted.

This is supposed to be your interrogation room, yet somehow it feels like a conference space Norma has reserved for herself. She sits behind the desk, every item already adjusted according to her preferences, while you're just a visitor who's been granted entry.

Looking at her stern face, you recall Nightingale's reminder from earlier today: A visitor from the Public Security Bureau had requested a meeting and specifically asked to use the interrogation room, which happened to be vacant today.
The reason is simple, and very Norma. This room is absolutely quiet, with no risk of irrelevant interruptions.

You've encountered this analyst from the Public Security Bureau's Forensics Division several times during the previous <color=#fb9259>MBCC Mania Leakage Incident</color>, and you've since looked into her file.

Calm, rational, meticulous. Born into a scholarly family and graduated from a top research institute in Eastside. One of the core analysts in the Public Security Bureau's Forensics Division. Outstanding academic record and exceptional professional competence. Almost ruthlessly rigorous in everything she does.
Her manner matches what you remember, but when that rationality manifests in every minute detail, the excessive orderliness becomes oddly unsettling.

You fall silent for a moment, then close the door as requested. Just as you're about to ask the usual questions—if she would want something to drink, if the room temperature is okay, if she consents to the conversation being recorded—she speaks first.

speaker: Norma
content: Early this morning, "Moses" predicted an imminent threat. According to the model's calculations, if this incident occurred, the Public Security Bureau would likely suffer a casualty rate of roughly 20% among its staff. This figure is significantly higher than the average casualty rate of roughly 5% for typical major incidents.

speaker: Norma
content: Therefore, I've determined that your intervention will be necessary.
Her voice is toneless, as if just reading out some regular calculation results. Without any preamble or embellishment, she sounds so direct it comes across as stilted and abrupt.
For a moment, no one speaks. You blink, realizing you haven't been following what she was saying at all.

speaker: Norma
content: Moses was a prehistoric prophet. It's the name I gave to my large-scale intelligent predictive model.

speaker: You
content: ...What kind of threat did it predict? Does it involve Mania or Sinners?

speaker: Norma
content: No specific connection has been confirmed at this time.
She pauses for a moment.

speaker: Norma
content: But that possibility hasn't been ruled out.

You frown. If the threat hasn't been confirmed to be related to Sinners, then officially, the Public Security Bureau should investigate it first before deciding whether to involve the MBCC. Norma clearly isn't following that procedure.

speaker: You
content: Miss Norma, the MBCC could get involved. But before that, I need to confirm something. Instead of submitting a report to the Public Security Bureau requesting an investigation, you came straight to me. Is there a reason for that?
Norma is quiet, and for the first time, an awkward hesitation crosses her face.
Several hours earlier, inside the Public Security Bureau building.

The office door is ajar. Outside in the corridor, several people holding coffee cups and folders peek occasionally inside quietly and nosily. Inside, the atmosphere isn't heated yet, but there is clearly tension in the air.

speaker: Boss
content: Norma, this project has been terminated. Your "upgraded model" wasn't approved, and there's no need for further review.

speaker: Norma
content: I understand the project is currently frozen. However, the model's algorithmic framework has been updated, and its predictive accuracy has improved by 17.6%. The "threat" it detected this time is not a mere fluctuation within the margin of error.
She places a document on the desk, the pages spreading across the surface.

speaker: Norma
content: The complete calculation process and data sources are all here. The error rate is only 0.087‰. If the prediction holds true, the scale of the damage will at least be between 8% and 12%. The cost of investigation is far lower than the potential loss.
The man doesn't even glance at the document. He lets out a faint sigh, his weary tone clearly implying he is not interested in discussing further.

speaker: Boss
content: Norma, don't you know why this project was shut down in the first place? You, of all people, should understand the consequences of what happened last time.
The onlookers in the corridor quiet down slightly. Someone lets out a low "tsk." But even as her superior's impatience grows, Norma's tone remains calm.

speaker: Norma
content: That incident was caused by missing source data and artificial parameter bias, not flawed mathematical logic. Moses 1.0 couldn't identify human bias, but the system has now been upgraded to version 2.012 with a self-correction mechanism. If we don't start the investigation now...
The man's fingers rap sharply against the desk, cutting her off. This time, his tone turns noticeably cold.

speaker: Boss
content: You're asking the Public Security Bureau to deploy human resources to verify the results calculated by a project that was shut down due to lack of credibility?

Muffled laughter drifts in from the corridor. "Here she goes again." "She still hasn't given up on that thing." "Talk about stubborn..." The murmurs aren't clearly audible, but they aren't discreet either. Seeming not to hear them, Norma simply pushes the data on the desk toward the man once again.

speaker: Norma
content: The logical framework is all in the report. Every variable, sample source, and deduction process can be verified. All it requires is a one-off investigation.
The man's jaw tightens, as if forcing down some rising emotion. He looks down at the report, pauses briefly, then snaps it shut and throws it back heavily to the other side of the desk.

speaker: Boss
content: I've already told you. Your request will never be approved.
Norma is wordless for a moment, then fixes him with an unwavering stare.

speaker: Norma
content: ...You're letting emotion drive your decision. Humans may reach faulty conclusions due to emotional or memory bias, but Moses does not. It relies on repeated calculations and cross-verification based on evidence chain anchors.

The man furrows his brow sharply, growing even more irritated. The whispers outside have quieted down at some point. Everyone can tell that the patience of the head of the Public Security Bureau's Technology Department is running out. Everyone except Norma, who seems entirely oblivious.

speaker: Norma
content: This is a warning. If you ignore it, your emotional decision may lead to a catastrophic outcome...

speaker: Boss
content: Enough!
The man cuts her off again. This time, he doesn't bother keeping his voice down. He points straight at the door, his tone ice-cold.

speaker: Boss
content: Get out, now.
The crowd outside disperses quickly. Some shrug. Others wear expressions that say they saw this coming.
Norma says nothing more. She simply puts the document back into her briefcase with practiced efficiency, then turns to leave.

speaker: Norma
content: I'm not here on behalf of the Public Security Bureau. I came of my own accord. You know me. You know I don't lie.

Norma has put you in a difficult position. Judging by her expression, the Public Security Bureau clearly doesn't support her view or method. While the MBCC operates independently, it still cooperates frequently with the Public Security Bureau. Getting involved could easily strain that relationship.
More importantly, you know little about Norma's model. Is its prediction worth dragging the MBCC into troubled waters?

speaker: You
content: I'm sorry, Miss Norma. The incident hasn't happened yet. Without concrete evidence that it will occur, I cannot be convinced to invest resources into this either.

speaker: Norma
content: Moses doesn't make mistakes, as long as the input parameters are true and accurate.

speaker: You
content: ...But I know very little about this great "prophet" of yours.

Norma glances at you and rapidly performs a set of calculations concerning efficiency in her brain. Her conclusion: Without providing detailed information about the model, she can never convince you to commit resources.

speaker: Norma
content: What do you want to know?

speaker: You
content: How does it work, for instance?

speaker: Norma
content: The world is composed of measurable parameters. Chaos is simply a complex system that has yet to be deconstructed. Given a complete logical framework, the future is not unpredictable.

speaker: You
content: ...Can you put that in simpler terms?

speaker: Norma
content: What are you holding right now?

speaker: You
content: The air conditioner remote.

speaker: Norma
content: If you let go, what will happen?
...What is she getting at?

speaker: Norma
content: Correct. You've just made a prediction.

speaker: Norma
content: You know the remote will fall thanks to experience and observation. But that only provides a rough judgment. You cannot work out precisely the time it will hit the floor, and the exact position it will land on.

speaker: Norma
content: But if you quantify the process—the height, initial position, gravitational acceleration, and external forces—you can then calculate those two things, even down to the millimeter and millisecond. That is the law of mechanics.

speaker: Norma
content: Similar patterns exist in human society. Crime rates, for instance, can be estimated and predicted with historical data, population density, infrastructure, and social variables. Moses simply extends this calculation to an extreme scale.
Norma speaks with confidence across from you, but your mind suddenly drifts to something you saw while reviewing her file. An old document about the Public Security Bureau's early predictive model.

options: If it's really this accurate... has it ever been wrong?

content: Something flickers in Norma's eyes.

speaker: You
content: I've heard rumors about an incident that happened at the Public Security Bureau years ago. It was apparently related to a predictive model.

speaker: Norma
content: You don't need to be so tactful about it.
Her tone remains unchanged, yet the pause is noticeable.

speaker: Norma
content: During my first year at the Public Security Bureau, I participated in a crime rate intervention pilot program targeting a high-risk area. I collected variables related to local crimes and built a predictive model. That was Moses 1.0.

speaker: Norma
content: After six months of trial, the prediction accuracy reached 98.72%. The Public Security Bureau reallocated patrol resources accordingly, reducing the area's crime rate by 14%.

speaker: Norma
content: But at the end of that year, the Bureau leadership adjusted certain patrol points and rosters without informing me. The criminals in the high-risk area migrated in response, committing violent crimes in an area marked as low-risk by the model, resulting in fifteen casualties.

You recall the Public Security Bureau's official statement on the incident: "While the model was theoretically competent, it failed to adequately factor in the complexity of human nature and social dynamics, creating risks in its application."

options: Why would the Public Security Bureau make such a decision?

speaker: Norma
content: Because an important official was scheduled to inspect the area that week. To accommodate his visit and create the appearance of a "safe neighborhood," the Public Security Bureau administratively intervened in the patrol arrangement, even though it went against the data.
...So that's what happened. The truth never made it into the official statement. The logic behind was diluted with carefully chosen words, the cause and effect rearranged.

speaker: Norma
content: The model never failed. I did. I overlooked a variable that had never been properly factored into my calculations—human flaws.
It's the first time you've seen her expression change so visibly. Anger, resentment, and perhaps something even more complex flicker briefly in her eyes before vanishing.

speaker: Norma
content: Humans are such a fragile species. Fear, servility, and other noises that could interfere with sound judgment. They are the greatest source of chaos in this world.

speaker: Norma
content: When faced with pressure and self-interest, people will always choose to sacrifice the purity of logic and ignore irrefutable evidence. This calculated hypocrisy disgusts me far more than pure, natural chaos ever could. Humans are traitors to rationality itself.
Of course, you cannot agree with such an extreme, radical point of view.

speaker: You
content: It's true that emotion can lead people to make irrational choices. But that doesn't mean it's nothing but a burden.

speaker: You
content: Because emotion is also often what drives people to make choices that defy rational calculation in extreme situations—to protect others, to shoulder risks, or even to summon extraordinary strength.
Hearing your counterargument, Norma simply scoffs.

speaker: Norma
content: Emotions and feelings are nothing more than the outward expressions of hormonal reactions. The pathetic part is that humans cannot control them, and they make themselves slaves to them instead. The human heart is a highly unstable, highly confounding, and low-yield variable. It is the root cause of systemic disorder.

You frown. Some people may naturally be less sensitive to emotion, but she seems so angry, as if she once suffered considerable trauma because of emotion. She's trying to defend rationality, yet the words coming out of her mouth right now are clearly anything but rational.
This feels more like a trauma response, a means of self-defense... What exactly happened to her?

You don't press the argument any further. Whatever she's been through, clearly, you cannot sway her with just a few sentences, and that's not why you're here today anyway. You steer the conversation back on track.

speaker: You
content: ...So after that incident, you took the fall for the Public Security Bureau and were reassigned to the Forensics Division? I'm...
Before you can even say the word "sorry," Norma cuts you off expressionlessly. Sure enough, now that you've changed the subject, she's quickly returned to her usual composed self.

speaker: Norma
content: No need to pity me. It's actually for the best. The Forensics Division has shorter chains of evidence, fewer variables, and minimal social interference. It's more efficient, and so I'm more at ease.

speaker: You
content: ...Fair point. Dead people don't introduce many variables, I suppose. At least they won't suddenly move just because some bigwig from Eastside walks in.
You try to lighten the mood with a joke. Norma tilts her head slightly. She clearly doesn't get it.

speaker: Norma
content: Indeed, theoretically speaking, corpses do not move on their own. Even if post-mortem bloating or muscular contractions occur, the force generated is insufficient to cause displacement.
Her unironic explanation leaves you speechless. How can a person have absolutely zero sense of humor?

As Norma continues her explanation, the terminology becomes increasingly incomprehensible. Worse still, the way she's looking at you is starting to resemble how she might examine a specimen on her table. A chill runs down your spine, and you quickly go back to your original topic.

speaker: You
content: ...So what about your model? What happened to it?

speaker: Norma
content: Moses 1.0's model was taken down by the Public Security Bureau. All related code and data have been archived. But I was able to reconstruct the core algorithm from memory and continue refining Moses 2.0. I only have access to public data now, so the prediction accuracy has been affected, but it can still identify certain risks.

speaker: Norma
content: For example, this morning, the system detected an abnormal risk indicator, and its highly unlikely associated entity. A live puzzle-solving game.

speaker: You
content: ...A puzzle-solving game?
Norma switches on her laptop and turns the screen toward you. You see an ad for the game. The title stands out in bold letters: "Reshaping the Future—The Only Experience Tailored Just for You."

speaker: Norma
content: The model's projections indicate that if this game is allowed to continue operating, it will trigger a series of interconnected crises within a matter of months. I've reviewed all available public information. Approximately twenty-three thousand players have participated in it so far.
She taps a few keys.

speaker: Norma
content: But there isn't any developer information available publicly. The brand, the team, and their previous works have all been deliberately hidden. It's as if the developer knew from the very beginning that people would be looking for them, and they don't want to be found.

speaker: Norma
content: Furthermore, it puts a lot of emphasis on the "personalized experience" element. The story, stages, and feedback every player encounters are different. Theoretically, a product like this should generate substantial discussion about those varied experiences.
She pauses, fingertip tapping the screen.

speaker: Norma
content: But the reviews show the exact opposite. No one is discussing the game mechanics, narrative, or any specifics. Every single review parrots the same phrase: "An unparalleled experience." The players all seem to unanimously agree with this comment.

speaker: You
content: That doesn't sound "personalized" at all. More like... everyone's being guided toward the same conclusion.
Norma nods slightly.

speaker: Norma
content: I attempted to contact several players directly. Yet, regardless of how I phrased my questions, their responses were identical to the reviews. That level of consistency is inherently illogical.
You try to follow her reasoning.

speaker: You
content: So either the data were fabricated... or the players themselves were influenced?

speaker: Norma
content: I don't have enough information yet to reach that conclusion. But what I can confirm is that this so-called "personalized experience" cannot genuinely rely on randomness. The paths, feedback, and nodes must all be built upon existing data.

speaker: Norma
content: With sufficient data, a model can be built, and predictions can be made. All I need to do is enter it myself, collect enough samples, and I can reconstruct its underlying structure.
She stares at you. There isn't a hint of hesitation in her tone.

speaker: Norma
content: My model has never been wrong. Whether or not the MBCC decides to get involved, I'm investigating this myself. If you believe in my model, then come with me.
You don't respond immediately. Your eyes linger on those nearly identical reviews, and an uneasiness suddenly arises within you.

speaker: You
content: ...Over twenty thousand people. No matter how precisely designed something is, there's bound to be errors. There will always be people who dislike it, people who stray from the intended path, people who give a different answer. But it looks like there hasn't even been a single "anomaly."

speaker: You
content: Or... were all the "anomalies" already factored in?
Norma doesn't respond, simply watching you wordlessly.

speaker: You
content: You're right. Most so-called "personalization" is just pre-designed paths. That's why I want to see how it manages to drive so many different people's choices toward the same conclusion.
You look at her.

speaker: You
content: As for your model... I'm not entirely convinced by it yet.
Norma frowns, about to object, but you smile at her and speak first.

speaker: You
content: But I trust you. Come on, let's find out if this game is indeed free of anomalies, or if it's simply turned them into "inevitability."
The clock on the wall chimes for the ninth time. The sound of turning cogwheels floods in from all sides. The chandelier sways, casting unsteady shadows on the floor.

speaker: Norma
content: I've said this three times already: middle, right, left. Trigger the mechanisms in that order, and the passage will open within thirty seconds.

speaker: Young Woman
content: Saying it three times doesn't make it true. I just feel like we should start with the one on the right.

speaker: Norma
content: Did you even read the question? That's the most obvious distraction...
You stand between the two arguing women and let out a sigh. You've been stuck here for five minutes now. At this rate, the most probable outcome is all of you being eliminated.

speaker: You
content: How about... rock-paper-scissors? Picking one at random at least gives us a shot.
You raise a hand, trying to salvage the situation. Both of them turn around at the same time and glare at you.

speaker: Norma/Young Woman
content: No!

The place is more crowded than you expected. The line nearly fills the entire entrance plaza, and a lot of these people are clearly regulars, chattering in small groups. You can feel the enthusiasm in the air.

You follow Norma to the end of the line and casually ask if she knows how this type of game works. You don't really expect her to have an answer. After all, a workaholic like Norma doesn't seem the type to spend her free time playing live puzzle-solving games.

But to your surprise, she does have an answer. In fact, she explains all the details from the basic structure to the core mechanics, then to the common patterns, all in one breath. She is speaking so fast and dumping so much information on you that before long, you're starting to lose track.

speaker: You
content: Wait, hold on... What is this "classic three-part structure" you just mentioned?

speaker: Norma
content: The standard escape room structure. The basic information is given upon entry. The first part tests your observation skills. The second part tests your teamwork and efficiency. The third part typically delivers a narrative twist. In some games, clues can even be hidden in the background soundtracks.
You stare at her in shock, feeling as though you've just revealed a hidden character trait in her. Perhaps made uncomfortable by your gaze, she adds a little stiffly:

speaker: Norma
content: It's a highly formulaic design. With enough exposure and analysis, the deduction process becomes quite straightforward.

speaker: You
content: ...So you play these games regularly?
Norma clears her throat.

speaker: Norma
content: ...Occasionally.

You suppose the poker-faced analyst of the Forensics Division does need some way to decompress. You just assumed it would be something like reading research papers or building statistical models, not solving escape room puzzles.

The line moves forward slowly. You're about to ask a few more questions when the large screen overhead suddenly lights up. A heavily distorted figure appears onscreen. The face is obscured and the voice is digitally altered, making it impossible to even tell this person's gender. The caption at the bottom says: Founder "X."

speaker: X
content: Welcome to "Reshaping the Future," a revolutionary immersive puzzle-solving experience. Now, I will introduce the core mechanics of the game...
As "X" speaks, images flash past the screen, showing intricate environment models, animated data streams, and players racing through corridors.

You pay close attention to the video, searching for anything unusual, while Norma beside you is already discreetly recording it with her comms device. Some kind of analysis software seems to be running in the background as well.
However, a few seconds later, she frowns.

speaker: Norma
content: Tch... The video structure's been re-encoded. The audio too. Even the Forensics Division's internal recovery program can't crack it. I can't even extract the basic identifying features.
The promotional video continues. It cuts to the electronic wristbands you were given at the entrance, with data like heart rate, pupil dilation, and galvanic skin response floating around.

speaker: X
content: To ensure the optimal experience, this game uses a powerful, cutting-edge technology. The system tracks each player's physiological indicators and psychological state throughout the entire process, generating personalized storylines and challenges while dynamically adjusting the content in real time.

speaker: X
content: Every playthrough is a unique experience.

speaker: You
content: That sounds... pretty impressive?
You glance down at the wristband, somewhat taken aback. Norma shifts her gaze from the screen to you, her tone still laced with obvious skepticism.

speaker: Norma
content: This is most likely just false advertising. If what they're claiming is true, this level of technology would rival, or even surpass, the Public Security Bureau's...
You're telling me NOW you can't make it!? Something suddenly came up? Where the hell were you earlier!
Norma's analysis is suddenly cut short by a shrill, urgent voice from somewhere behind you. The sound rings out sharply in the plaza, like a stone thrown into still water.

speaker: Young Woman
content: I already bought the tickets, I'm already here, and now you're saying you're not coming? So what the hell am I supposed to do? Stand at the entrance and watch everyone else play?

You instinctively glance back. A young woman stands not far behind you, phone pressed to her ear, brow deeply furrowed. Her voice pitches up and down with her bursting anger and anxiety, attracting looks from people nearby.

speaker: Young Woman
content: ...Tch, you know what, forget it. I'm not wasting more time talking to you. I'll figure something out myself.

She ends the call briskly, then takes a deep breath, as if trying to push down her emotions. But the irritation still clearly lingers around her eyes. She looks up, gaze sweeping the area absently, and finally locks eyes with Norma.
In that instant, both of them freeze. They don't greet each other or say anything. There's not even time for the slightest shift in their expressions. Just a brief, awkward exchange of glances.
Your inquisitive gaze shifts between the two of them. You speak up tentatively.

speaker: You
content: ...You know each other?

speaker: Young Woman
content: Of course not!
The woman answers first, speaking quickly, then immediately looks away. You turn to Norma. With a complicated expression, she nods... then shakes her head.
At her answer, the woman's body goes stiff. The air between them turns strained and uncomfortable. Before you can press further, an announcement chimes through the venue:

speaker: Announcement
content: Next group, please. Team of three.

You, Norma, and the woman are assigned to the same group. Once the game begins, it moves at an almost unrealistically fast pace. The wristband grows warm around your wrist. Announcements come from the overhead speakers from time to time. The system is clearly monitoring you.

The first puzzle appears, and Norma solves it with just a single glance. The second and third follow just as quickly. Before you and your other teammate can even understand the clues, she's already pressed the correct button. You give up trying to follow her logic and turn your attention to the surroundings instead.
The rooms change constantly, but you can't discern any pattern. One moment it's a cluttered bedroom with oversaturated colors and messy items everywhere...
The next, you're on a university campus with academic buildings and a library on either side. A bulletin board is covered with club recruitment posters and lecture announcements.
Then a laboratory...
An auditorium...
A library...

The background music keeps changing erratically. Sometimes fast, sometimes slow. Sometimes soft, sometimes grating. The PA periodically cuts in with calm commentary such as "excellent logical judgment," "poor cooperation," "too dependent on individual leadership," and "slow team response."
Meanwhile, you notice the subtle changes in the woman's expression. At the library stage, she stops before a desk, head bowed, her face hidden from view. The light overhead flickers faintly.
You walk over. On the desk sit several books: Neurocognition, Emotion Regulation, Behavioral Intervention. Beside them lies a neatly organized document titled Emotional State Enhancement Plan.
You ask if she has any thoughts about these clues. She simply shakes her head, murmurs "Nothing," and turns to leave. But that nagging, strange feeling in your heart never fades.
The three of you barely talk to each other as you progress through the stages—until now. There are three locks and three mechanisms, requiring all three of you to work together.

speaker: Norma
content: The sequence is middle, right, left, with three-second intervals. You take the middle.
Norma's tone is clipped, almost commanding. The woman's eyebrows arch immediately. At nearly the same instant, a comment comes from the PA.

speaker: Announcement
content: Cooperation-related stress rising.

speaker: Young Woman
content: And I'm supposed to just do what you say?

speaker: Norma
content: It's the best solution.
The background music tenses up suddenly, its tempo quickening.

speaker: Young Woman
content: And you get to decide what the best solution is? Stop acting so superior all the time. I've had enough of you. Why must we listen to you?

speaker: Norma
content: Then should we listen to you? Your error rate in the previous rooms was 62%.

speaker: Announcement
content: Conflict level rising.

speaker: Young Woman
content: ...Excuse me?!
And that's how things have ended up the way they are now.
Now, inside the escape room.

speaker: Norma
content: Could you please stop being so emotional?

speaker: Young Woman
content: Who's the one being emotional? You don't trust anyone but yourself!

speaker: Norma
content: My judgment is evidence-based. I already explained the reasoning process. Do you want to keep on arguing or clear this game?
The lights flicker again, more noticeably this time.

speaker: Announcement
content: Individual desire for control intensifying.

speaker: Young Woman
content: "I"! "Me"! "My"! You make everything about yourself! Did you even pay attention when I shared my experience? You think I haven't tried that already? It doesn't work!

speaker: Young Woman
content: You think I'm arguing for the sake of arguing, huh? Sure, I'm not as smart and capable as you. So why don't you do it yourself then? Just ignore the idiot who you think is below you!

They both refuse to back down, their voices rising. At some point, the lights dim. The background music grows urgent, laced with a countdown-like rhythm that pounds against your nerves with each beat.
The wristband feels warmer than before too. You start to feel a dull pressure in your head.

Something must have happened between these two. They just had to run into each other here... Failing the game would be one thing, but if this derails the investigation, the entire trip will be wasted. Norma is clearly agitated as well, likely thinking the same thing.

speaker: Norma
content: Enough, Eileen! Just cut it out.

Norma finally loses her patience and calls out the other woman's name. You're taken aback. Not by what she said, but by... something unusual in her tone. The woman named Eileen slowly turns her head, a mocking smile on her lips.

speaker: Eileen
content: How kind of you, Norma. So you do remember me after all.
Eileen.
This is not a name I try to remember consciously. It'll be more accurate to say that the name itself constitutes part of my failure. I've tried every method to forget it. Every time, I failed.

The rational part of me tells me that memories are nothing more than mere arrangements of proteins. Proteins degrade. Dopamine fades. The half-life of hormones never exceeds six months. The rational part of me tells me that with my active intervention—engaging in complex calculations whenever unpleasant memories surface, using working memory to activate the prefrontal cortex—I can suppress these unwanted feelings, make all that unnecessary noise disappear.

speaker: Norma
content: I must have made a mistake in one of the steps. Try again. Take a deep breath. Locate the sensitive memory zone. Reduce the dopamine and norepinephrine responses.

speaker: Eileen
content: Hi, you must be Norma, right? I'm Eileen! Oh, this is great. I have a new friend! Where do you like to sleep? I've already set up a hammock on the balcony—use it whenever you like! Oh, and I'm planning to add a swing too, so we can both... Ah!

She was running too fast and lost a slipper. I caught her, then looked past her at our new dorm room. Messy, colorful, and utterly chaotic. Bubble skirts, cartoon curtains, fairy lights, and comic books scattered across the floor. And dye that hadn't been cleaned up.

This place was nothing like the environment I grew up in. There, everything had to be orderly, controllable, and categorizable. Emotions were no different from unnecessary decorations. They were confounding variables that needed to be eliminated.

speaker: Norma
content: Your slipper... It's on the sofa.

speaker: Eileen
content: Oh, sorry! I must have flung it over there earlier. Hope you don't mind.
She smiled and casually wiped her dye-stained hands on her clothes.

speaker: Eileen
content: Sorry, I was just dyeing my hair. Would you like to try too?

And so, on my very first day in the new dorm, I got green hair. All because I had no idea how to stop my new roommate Eileen from pestering me... She was like some kind of alien creature I simply could not comprehend.
At nine o'clock in the evening, normally I should be wrapping up my assignments and getting ready for bed. Yet here I was, at a night market with this strange creature.
The lights, noise, people, and smells all mixed together. The information was so dense and unstructured. An utterly inefficient environment. I couldn't understand why people enjoyed this.

speaker: Eileen
content: No way. You've never had fried chicken before?

speaker: Norma
content: High fat intake...
Before I could finish, she stuffed a piece of fried chicken in my mouth. The batter was crispy and the meat inside was warm. The fat and spices spread all over my tongue.

It was a sensation... that I couldn't deconstruct. Not just the taste, but the temperature, the smell, her laughter, and the clamor of the crowd around us... Everything blended together into something that couldn't be broken down.

speaker: Eileen
content: Isn't it so tasty?

speaker: Norma
content: What's... "tasty"?

speaker: Eileen
content: Seriously, Norma? Doesn't your mom ever cook you tasty food?

speaker: Norma
content: Mother...

speaker: Mother
content: Your current weight is 39 kilograms. You may consume 60 grams of cereal, one boiled egg, 250 milliliters of milk, and 100 grams of spinach. On top of that, you'll need some vitamins. After the meal, take 50 grams of blueberries from the fridge and eat them.

speaker: Norma
content: Mom, I don't want to eat boiled eggs. They're not tasty.
Mother had looked at me. Not with anger, but disappointment. That look meant she had identified an error that needed correction.

speaker: Mother
content: What's "tasty"? The combined result of chemoreceptor activation, physical texture perception, and the central nervous system's reward mechanism. An illusion generated during the body's biochemical processes. The more unhealthy a food is, the better it is at deceiving your brain with chemical substances.
Was "tasty"... just a form of deception? I looked at the fried chicken in my hand. I knew it was illogical, yet I still wanted another bite.
At the school's welcoming dance, Eileen made me wear an embarrassingly colorful dress and dragged me into the center of the crowd. Lights flickered all around us amid the clamorous noise.

speaker: Norma
content: I... I don't know how to... dance.

speaker: Eileen
content: I don't know how either. Everyone here's just faking it too. Just start dancing and...

speaker: Norma
content: Sorry, I stepped on you. Ah!

speaker: Eileen
content: Hehe, it's fine. Ha! Got my revenge.

We kept stepping on each other's feet, yet somehow we couldn't stop laughing. Eventually, people on the dance floor began staring at us strangely. A tall man came over and asked Eileen for a dance, but she turned him down instantly.

speaker: Eileen
content: My little Norma, what were you thinking just now? You looked a bit worried. That type of guy's like a perpetual motion machine on the dance floor—always searching for the next partner, always getting rejected.

speaker: Norma
content: Um... I'd say he's currently experiencing a failure of self-awareness inhibition due to elevated dopamine levels.

Eileen froze for a moment, then suddenly burst out laughing. She hugged me and said I was "adorable." I had no idea what was funny about what I'd said, nor did I know... whether I was supposed to hug her back.
I thought we'd spend our college years together like this. Chaotic, yet... not entirely unacceptable.

But as it turned out, Mom was right. All the so-called "joy" and "beauty" you feel are nothing more than uncontrollable hormonal responses, the very source of chaos in this world. Happiness is fleeting. If you don't keep your emotions in check, they will only drag you into an abyss of loss and disorder.
During our senior year, Eileen's family was struck by sudden tragedy.

Her father's business failed, and he went bankrupt. Unable to cope, he abandoned his family. Her mother worked day and night trying to pay off the debts, and soon fell ill. Now the entire burden had fallen on Eileen's shoulders.
But Eileen couldn't handle it on her own. She hadn't attended classes for a week straight. She just cried every night and barely ate. Her efficiency was plummeting. I had to help her.

speaker: Norma
content: I experienced similar emotional breakdowns during my childhood too. But fortunately, chaos is not insurmountable. Once deconstructed and quantified, a model can be built, and it can certainly be rectified.

speaker: Norma
content: I've consulted a large amount of literature and formulated a precise action plan for you. An Emotional State Enhancement Plan. It includes a sleep schedule, permitted crying breaks, caloric intake, social interaction frequency, cognitive training exercises, and other elements.

speaker: Norma
content: Eileen, let me take care of you. We'll work through this together. Your family needs you.
Eileen stared at me expressionlessly and nodded. I was elated, thinking everything would soon return to normal.
...But looking back now, perhaps I implemented the plan too hastily. Like an IV drip with a too-strong flow, it caused venous spasms and rebound bleeding instead.

At first, she did comply. She woke up on time, ate her meals, and logged her mood swings. But over time, her execution began to deviate from the plan. Her frequency declined, and errors grew more serious.
One day, she reached out and grabbed my hand. Her voice was barely a whisper.

speaker: Eileen
content: Norma... will you stay with me for a bit?
I paused for a second.

speaker: Norma
content: We're outside your designated emotional release window now. You should finish your meal first, then proceed with emotion regulation.

speaker: Eileen
content: ...But I'm really sad. I can't keep going like this. Can't you at least give me a hug?
Her voice was so fragile, like it might shatter. In that moment, I did consider whether to satisfy her request. But I reached my conclusion quickly.

speaker: Norma
content: Short-term physical contact may provide temporary relief, but it won't improve your overall condition. Furthermore, it would interfere with your ability to independently regulate your emotions, which is counterproductive to long-term recovery.
She was silent for a long time, just staring at me. At the time, I didn't understand what that look meant.

speaker: Eileen
content: Norma, tell me... I'm just a broken machine that can't be fixed, aren't I?
She cried. But it wasn't the designated time for crying.

speaker: Norma
content: Your grief response intensity has exceeded the threshold for too long. This will slow down your recovery. You should do a breathing exercise to regulate it immediately.
Eileen looked at me, tears streaming down her face, and suddenly she started to laugh.

speaker: Eileen
content: Just go, Norma. Leave me alone.

speaker: Norma
content: No. Your emotional state is currently unstable. It needs to be recalibrated...
A low roar shakes the ground, and the thick fog begins to surge. The wind becomes a violent storm, lifting her short hair from behind.
Eileen struggled to her feet and started hurling everything within reach at me, trying to keep me away.

speaker: Eileen
content: Get out! Get lost! Get out of this room! I don't ever want to see you again!

I froze in place. The hoarse screaming and sobbing, the broken sentences, the sounds of different objects striking the wall and shattering, and the mess scattered across the floor... all of it flooded my senses like uncategorizable noises.
In that instant, my perception underwent an inexplicable change.
Numbers suddenly appeared all over Eileen. The evaporation rate of her tears, the irregular frequency of her heartbeat, the short-term curves of hormones in her body...
And all those flickering, fluctuating numbers were ultimately quantified into violently pulsating crimson values labeled "panic" and "despair."

...I didn't understand. I was trying to help her. Why couldn't she follow even the simplest instructions? Why was she so angry? Why did she reject me and tell me to leave? I also didn't understand the heavy, oppressive feeling spreading through my chest.

So, it was finally proven by facts. The human heart is a source of chaos inexplicable by logic, one that is extremely dangerous. That failed experiment in emotional interaction taught me that emotion is a highly unstable, highly destructive variable. Human emotions create massive, unpredictable disturbances in their behavior. If they cannot be effectively incorporated into a model and properly controlled, they will have a detrimental effect on efficiency and cause complete deviation from intended outcomes. I included this conclusion in my graduate thesis, A Predictive Model of Social Behavior. It became the foundation of Moses.
As for Eileen...

Later, I built that swing on our dorm balcony. It was something she'd mentioned when we first met, but I'd kept putting it off for one reason or another. By the time I finally finished it, Eileen never came back.

speaker: Eileen
content: Why are you so quiet? You're clearly annoyed. You've got so much pent-up anger you want to let out, haven't you? Then argue with me! Fight me, even! To hell with your order and logic! Stop using them as excuses to suppress yourself!
A flicker of emotion starts to rise, only to be forcibly shoved back down. Norma's tone remains controlled, but she's beginning to crack.

speaker: Norma
content: ...Can you, just for once, stay calm and rational? There may be abnormal risks hidden in this game. I'm trying to confirm that, and you're only interfering with my judgment.
Eileen scoffs.

speaker: Eileen
content: Abnormal risks? A result from your model's calculations again? Just like that project at the Public Security Bureau back then? ...Heh. It was all over the news. Of course, I heard about it.

speaker: You
content: Enough, both of you! This isn't the time to dredge up the past...

speaker: Eileen
content: This is between me and her. Stay out of it!
Stage

speaker: Eileen
content: You know why your model failed? Because what matters most in this world is people. And you? It's like you're not even human. All you care about is your data, results, and accuracy.

speaker: Eileen
content: And those people who died in that incident? To you, they're nothing more than negligible "sample errors," aren't they? Of course, you don't feel guilty about them. I bet you've never even visited their graves!
Norma's gaze drops for a brief moment.

speaker: You
content: You've gone too far. Norma isn't...

speaker: Norma
content: She's right.

This time, it's Norma who cuts you off. She doesn't even spare you a glance, clearly unappreciative of your defense. Her tone is cold, edged with a sharp arrogance that brooks no argument. She is neither defensive nor hesitant, as if she's simply stating an immutable, indisputable fact.

speaker: Norma
content: The human body is no different from any other matter. Molecules degrade. Visiting graves serves no practical purpose.

speaker: Eileen
content: I thought after all these years, after everything that happened, you might've changed just a little. How naive of me. Just listen to yourself. You're a cold-blooded monster. You're beyond human comprehension...

speaker: Announcement
content: Cooperation level plunging to critical threshold. Risk of conflict approaching peak.

Before Eileen can finish, the PA suddenly blares again. The reminder sounds repetitively while the lights flash alarmingly. The arguing voices, the PA warnings, and the ever-quickening background music layer over one another, building up the irritation that's been sitting inside you.

speaker: You
content: I've had enough. I should just make them shut up. End this argument the quick way...
...No. The horrifying thought that never should've crossed your mind jolts you back to clarity. It's not them—it's this place. You wrench your gaze away and quickly scan your surroundings.

The flickering of the lights, the timing of the PA interruptions, the quickening rhythm of the music, and the sequence of the rooms. None of it is random. They're all working together to direct your attention, intensify the stimulation, and amplify the emotional responses.

You recall the path you've taken. The bedroom, the campus, the laboratory, and the library... These weren't just random stages, but their shared past, reconstructed. The announcements and environmental changes aren't merely for the atmosphere either. Together, they form a psychological trap to guide, amplify, and even manipulate your emotions.
Without another moment's hesitation, you yank off your wristband and step between them.

speaker: You
content: Stop! This place is messing with us. It's using the environment to manipulate our emotions, steering us toward the outcome it wants.
Both of them freeze. Norma's pupils contract slightly, as though your words have forcibly interrupted some calculation running in her mind.

Just moments ago, her thinking had already been guided onto a predetermined track. Her emotions were deconstructed, analyzed, and back-validated, yet all of it pointed toward a false conclusion. Her overly rational mind has made her easier to manipulate.

Norma closes her eyes. When she opens them again, her gaze has regained the previous focus and clarity. She quickly scans the changing nodes in the surroundings, her speech returning to its usual measured pace.

speaker: Norma
content: ...This isn't a simple manipulation mechanism. It's a behavioral guidance system based on structured modeling. It designates "conflict" as the desired outcome, then reverse-engineers its conditions: memory activation, emotional accumulation, and threshold breach. From there, it constructs a pathway to lead to the manifestation of the desired behavior.
She pauses for a moment, her voice dropping lower.

speaker: Norma
content: The logic is consistent with my crime prediction model, only the causality has been inverted. My model uses existing data to extrapolate future outcomes. But this game... presets the desired result, then reverse-engineers the conditions and process needed to achieve it.
Your heart sinks.

options: But if someone wanted to construct an inverted version of Moses...

speaker: Norma
content: They would first need access to Moses's original model and source code. And these resources, aside from myself, are only accessible to very few individuals at the Public Security Bureau.
Clack. Clack, clack, clack.

The moment the words leave her mouth, a series of mechanical locks snap shut loudly. The lights go out. Red warning lights flood the space. The floor cracks open, and spiky metal tracks burst upward with a piercing screech, tearing in from all sides.

A razor-sharp blade slashes down, barely missing you. You instinctively pull back, activating your shackles to hook onto the wall to roll yourself back. Norma dodges sideways, almost syncing with your motion.

speaker: Norma
content: Three o'clock.

Without thinking, your body is already reacting precisely and seamlessly, but the attacks are accelerating too. Thrusting, slashing, blocking off the paths, the layers of assault keep multiplying, as if forcing you to make a misstep.
Eileen is backed into a corner, frozen in place. You grit your teeth and rush forward, blocking a piercing blow aimed at her.

speaker: You
content: You alright?
You shout in Eileen's direction, but she's too paralyzed with fear to respond, only trembling uncontrollably.

Noticing the situation on your side, Norma pauses. Her eyes rapidly sweep across the structural nodes, trajectory blind spots, and energy distribution patterns, searching for a gap that hasn't yet closed. Then she locks on.

speaker: Norma
content: There!

Following the direction of her finger, you spot a side door that isn't fully closed. Norma launches herself forward, pushing through the relentless barrage of attacks. She grabs Eileen and shoves her through the door.
Through the narrow gap, Norma glances at Eileen. In that moment, her expression is remarkably calm, almost serene.

speaker: Norma
content: This time, I finally managed to save you. Now go.
Clack. The passage is sealed off completely, red light flooding everything. Outside, Eileen snaps out of her daze and frantically pounds against the door.

speaker: Eileen
content: Hey! You think this makes you some kind of hero?! Open the door! I'm not leaving! Open it!!

Her voice is drowned out by the blaring alarms, fading bit by bit.
Inside, you can no longer hear anything.

The mechanical rumbling gradually dies down. You lean against the wall, steadying your breath. Norma stands nearby, breathing hard, yet her posture remains perfectly straight. The overhead lights flicker on, and a clinical, high-definition holographic projection slowly appears in the air.

It's Founder "X," the figure that repeatedly appeared in the promotional video. But now, every filter and disguise has been stripped away. The voice and face are no longer obscured. That gentle smile remains, yet it feels unnervingly hollow, like a carefully sculpted mask.
A flicker of icy fury flashes across Norma's eyes.

speaker: Norma
content: I was right. It really is you.
The hologram doesn't deny it. Instead, the man surveys the damaged mechanisms around them, as though inspecting the results of a satisfactory experiment.

speaker: Boss
content: Did you enjoy yourself, Norma? Quite the thrilling game, wasn't it? And familiar, too, I imagine?

speaker: Norma
content: You plagiarized my model.
The hologram lets out a soft laugh.

speaker: Boss
content: Oh, don't say that. This isn't plagiarism. It's refinement. An old prophet like "Moses" no longer fits in the world we live in. What we need is someone brave enough to reshape the future, to rebuild the very logic of our civilization. I've named it "Saint Paul."
He raises one hand, and streams of data unfurl slowly behind him, like a wall woven with countless behavioral patterns.

speaker: Boss
content: What human society truly needs isn't prediction, but control. All the Public Security Bureau can do is mitigate damage after it has been done or issue warnings beforehand. But you can't just calculate or predict chaos away.

speaker: Boss
content: Rather than passively waiting for tragedies to happen and then trying to repair the damage, wouldn't it be better to eliminate them at the source?
His voice remains gentle, yet it carries a chilling certainty.

speaker: Boss
content: What I want is a society with real order. No chaos, no accidents, and none of those errors caused by the "complications" of human nature.

speaker: Boss
content: Emotions can be guided. Choices can be designed. Behavior can be calculated. When all of this falls under control, order ceases to be a matter of probability. It becomes inevitable. As for democracy, discussion, negotiation between parties... These things sound noble enough, but they're merely noises that slow down the decision-making process.

This seems more like an extremely twisted sense of order than simple lust for power. He genuinely believes that once human emotions, choices, and behavior are brought entirely under control, society will become safer and more stable.
Public security, public opinion, resource allocation, elections... In his eyes, these are all mere parameters that can be rearranged.

speaker: Boss
content: That's why I reversed your model. It's no longer used to predict the future, but to shape it.

speaker: Norma
content: ...This is your testing ground. Are you using those players as test subjects?

speaker: Boss
content: Test subjects? No.
He shakes his head gently.

speaker: Boss
content: Data.

speaker: Boss
content: "Saint Paul" still has its flaws. What I need is authentic human data. I need to understand, under deliberate guidance, how emotions are triggered, how choices are narrowed down, and how conflicts can be led back to the best solution. And the Public Security Bureau cannot provide me with these data.
He turns to look at Norma, undisguised admiration in his gaze.

speaker: Boss
content: You know, Norma, from the very beginning, I saw your model's true potential. That's why I pushed through opposition and brought you into the Public Security Bureau exceptionally. You are the very cornerstone of all of this.
Norma's gaze darkens. All those overlooked details, all those errors she's written off as "coincidence"... At this moment, they piece together a far more cruel and ugly truth.

speaker: Norma
content: ...Those last-minute adjustments to the patrol rosters, were they really just for accommodating that "inspection"?
The air falls silent for a moment. Then the hologram suddenly begins to clap, laughing cheerfully.

speaker: Boss
content: Of course, that was only a pretext, a necessary trigger condition. If I hadn't fabricated an incident "extreme" enough, your model would never have been shut down. And I could never have obtained its source code.

He talks about it so casually. All those bloody deaths, reduced to a single line of negligible footnote. Norma clenches her fists, but quickly regains her composure. Only this time, the coldness in her eyes grows even colder.

speaker: Boss
content: Though the current situation is turning out far more interesting than I anticipated.
He leans forward slightly, his tone taking on an edge of inscrutable interest.

speaker: Boss
content: At first, when you volunteered to investigate "Reshaping the Future," it did surprise me a little. I thought you'd already discovered something. I nearly called off this experiment altogether.
He pauses, as if savoring the memory.

speaker: Boss
content: But I quickly realized something. If you could trace your way here, it meant your model must have achieved a new breakthrough. And that was exactly what I needed. You were so insistent, so I thought I would let you into my system. With a few pushes, I might just gain access to your optimized algorithm.

speaker: Herb-Gathering Girl
content: Everything was going so smoothly... until that "anomaly" appeared. Your friend, Eileen.
He says the name in a cold, scrutinizing tone.

speaker: Boss
content: Emotional interference, decision deviation, path detachment... She amplified all these negligible noises. And somehow you broke free from the model's constraints because of it. But that only proved one thing: Your value is even greater than I initially calculated.
He extends his hand, his tone composed.

speaker: Boss
content: Therefore, instead of continuing to oppose one another, why don't we work together?

speaker: Norma
content: ...You want me to help you improve "Saint Paul"?

speaker: Boss
content: Exactly. We are indeed quite similar in character, aren't we? We both believe in mathematics and logic, and we despise hypocrisy and chaos. Securing the safety of the majority at a minimal cost—this is the most basic optimization problem.

speaker: Boss
content: Once we perfect "Saint Paul," you'll witness firsthand the construction of a society without accidents or casualties.
A faint smile crosses his face as he adds one final point:

speaker: Boss
content: As for that friend of yours... in a world like that, she would never have to suffer emotional breakdowns or pain again.
A brief silence. Norma lowers her head, her shadow on the floor shifting slightly.
Then...

speaker: Norma
content: No.
It's one simple word, but it's clear and unwavering, without a trace of hesitation. She lifts her head.

speaker: Norma
content: Do you know why I believe in logic? Because logic is part of the world's fundamental truth. It doesn't bend to anyone's will. It doesn't serve anyone's desires. It simply is.

speaker: Norma
content: But everything you just said was based on a single assumption: You think you can define what's "right."
She takes a step forward.

speaker: Norma
content: You start with your desired outcome, then reverse-engineer the process to make it all seem reasonable. But what lies behind it is not reason, but the falsification of logic.

speaker: Norma
content: You disguise control as "safety." You call the stripping of rights "stability." You camouflage the elimination of choice as a "best solution." Then you tell everyone this is right. But you've been constructing a lie from the very beginning.
She pauses for a moment, her voice turning ice cold.

speaker: Norma
content: That incident years ago wasn't a "necessary price." It was the result of your deliberate fabrication. And you didn't build your model to understand the world, but to control it.
Her sharp gaze cuts like a scalpel, methodically peeling away the pretense in his words, laying bare the corruption and self-interest rotting at the core of his so-called logic.

speaker: Norma
content: If conclusions can be bent just to pay a price or serve anyone's interests, then all research will lose its meaning. You've never understood what it means to pursue truth. You just need an excuse that makes you sound reasonable.

speaker: Norma
content: And your so-called "order" is nothing but blasphemy against truth, against science, against logic itself!
Her words resound with firm conviction.

speaker: Norma
content: So don't you dare compare yourself to me. My principles have nothing in common with yours.
The moment she says those words, the hologram's expression freezes completely, then fractures. His calm facade is torn apart, exposing the barely contained rage and bitter indignation beneath.

options: That's enough. End of the debate.

content: You step out from the shadows and wave the comms device in your hand before him.

speaker: You
content: Every word you just said, including the truth about that incident, has already been transmitted to the MBCC in real time.

speaker: Boss
content: What... MBCC... You're...

speaker: You
content: A pleasure to meet you... though I doubt the feeling is mutual. I'm ${PlayerName}, Chief of the MBCC. Everything you just confessed will serve as evidence, and I'll be testifying alongside Norma to ensure you're brought to justice.
The hologram seems taken aback, then laughs abruptly. The single sharp burst of laughter keeps growing louder and more uncontrollable.

speaker: Boss
content: In that case, I have no choice but to eliminate you both!
He raises his hand suddenly. A piercing rumbling erupts as a fresh wave of mechanisms crashes down like a downpour, faster, denser, and more precise than before.

speaker: Boss
content: "Saint Paul" has just digested your behavioral patterns and refined its analysis. This time, there's no chance you're making it out alive!
Just as he says, every move you and Norma make is predicted, disrupting your combat rhythm. The space closes in around you, every inch of your escape route gradually being sealed off.

speaker: Norma
content: Watch out!

You turn your head. A spinning metal saw blade is bearing down on you. Time seems to stretch in this instant. You can make out every charred mark left on its surface, see its edges glowing dull red from the friction of its relentless spin.
Too late.

Snap!
The lights go out. Everything grinds to an abrupt halt. The blade stops centimeters from your eye, quivering for a heartbeat before going completely still.
Overhead, the previously steady hologram flickers violently. That "perfect" face begins to distort and warp, as if the signal has been cut off.

Zzzzt.
All of a sudden, the hologram shatters, dissolving into broken flecks of light before vanishing completely. In the brief darkness and silence that follows, you can barely tell where reality ends and illusion begins.

Bang!
Right then, the locked side door is hacked open from the outside! Shattered metal panels crash to the ground as smoke and dust billow through. A figure stands by the door, firefighter ax in hand.

It's Eileen.
Hair utterly disheveled, she's panting, but her eyes are bright with energy.

speaker: Norma
content: ...Why did you come back?

speaker: Eileen
content: I know what you're about to say. "That's an irrational decision." But if it hadn't been for my "irrationality," you two would have been dead at that scumbag's hands right now!

speaker: Norma
content: I told you to leave. This place is too dangerous for you...

speaker: Eileen
content: Oh, just shut up!!
She yells, her sharp and urgent voice ringing through the confined space. A small laugh escapes you. The suffocating tension is torn up instantly by that single shout. You turn to look at Norma.

speaker: You
content: "The human heart is an uncontrollable, irrational thing." Isn't that what you always say?

Rendered speechless, Norma simply stares blankly at Eileen like a computer that's just crashed. Eileen, meanwhile, casually raises her hand and dumps the firefighter ax on the ground with a resounding thud.
She looks up toward the concealed door in the distance that was once tightly closed but is now sliding open due to the system failure. Her lips curl into an obvious mocking grin.
Behind it lies a hidden control room. With the power cut, the door unlocks automatically, the heavy panels sliding open inch by inch. The real person standing behind it has nowhere left to hide.

speaker: Eileen
content: How can someone be so smart and yet still have never thought of maybe keeping a backup server and power supply?

speaker: Boss
content: D-d-did you just destroy the server room?

The man stands before the control panel, his face turning deathly pale. Gone is the composure and "perfection" of his projected image. All the control he carefully maintained is completely crushed in this instant. Eileen gives the ax a casual kick, her tone relaxed and scornful.

speaker: Eileen
content: Took me forever to smash open that fire cabinet and get this ax. Good thing your wiring wasn't that complicated, and I didn't sleep through all my physics classes at school. Found it quickly enough.

speaker: Eileen
content: Way easier to just cut the power and smash the computers than waste time cracking all your finicky traps, don't you think?
The man takes a step back hastily. His eyes dart between the three of you, calculating, weighing, assessing. Then, without a moment's hesitation, he turns and bolts.
You lunge to the side, cutting off his shortest escape route. Norma also moves quickly and with precision, stopping his retreat toward the other side.

The man tries to change direction, only to collide head-on with Eileen charging straight at him. She seizes his collar and wrenches him forward. You catch his wrist and twist it back, while Norma sweeps in with a kick, knocking him off balance cleanly.

Thud!
The man is slammed heavily to the ground, no longer able to resist.

When you leave the Public Security Bureau, you and Norma happen to be heading the same way. For the first time ever, she doesn't check her watch or turn down your suggestion to walk together for the sake of saving time. Instead, she's got something to tell you.

But once you actually start walking, she stays silent. You pass by one streetlight after another. Her fingers curl slightly, then relax. She seems to be running through every possible way to start the conversation in her mind, searching for the "best solution," yet unable to arrive at one.
You notice, but say nothing. You simply match her pace, unhurried, waiting for her to begin.
Finally...

speaker: Norma
content: ...Thank you!

speaker: You
content: Huh?!
You're caught off guard by her sudden sentence. Norma reflexively pushes up her glasses, the tips of her ears flushing red as her gaze darts away, but she doesn't recoil.

speaker: Norma
content: I-I mean... Thank you for believing in me. For investigating this game with me, even when I didn't have enough evidence. And... for standing by my side through all of that.
Her voice trembles with nervousness, but she doesn't stop.

speaker: Norma
content: And, and thank you for helping me clear Moses's name. That... meant a lot to me. I couldn't have done any of this without you.
You can't help but smile.

speaker: You
content: Who says you don't know how to express your feelings? You're killing it!

speaker: Norma
content: Ugh! I-I... I'm not...
She fumbles, words catching in her throat, nothing like that sharp-tongued analyst during that debate.

speaker: You
content: Alright. I'll stop teasing you.
You clear your throat and put on a more serious tone.

speaker: You
content: I chose to trust you because you were persistent. Your abilities and your judgment were the reason why we were able to solve this case.

speaker: You
content: I might not have trusted a cold, purely numerical "model" so easily. But when you told me your story, I saw the "human" side of you.

speaker: You
content: I think both Eileen and that criminal were wrong about you. You are someone with feelings. You have a tireless passion for your work, and you care about everyone's safety. You may not be good at expressing emotions, but you do care. That's what helped me understand you. That's what made me trust you.

Norma doesn't respond right away. She ponders silently, as if breaking down your words, reorganizing them, then slowly integrating them into her understanding. After a long moment, she finally begins quietly.

speaker: Norma
content: ...Perhaps you're right. Human emotions aren't completely pointless. In certain extreme situations, they can indeed produce... outcomes that exceed what any model could predict.

speaker: You
content: That's right. Emotions are hard to quantify and accurately incorporate into models... but they're always there. Whether you try to analyze them or not, they'll always...
You pause for a moment.

speaker: You
content: Remind you that you actually care about certain people and certain things.
Norma seems dazed for a moment. She doesn't deny it. Instead, she lets out a soft breath, and a faint, somewhat bitter smile touches her lips.

speaker: Norma
content: Perhaps you're right.
After a brief silence, you change the subject.

speaker: You
content: Speaking of which... what are you planning to do about Eileen? You both clearly care about each other. It'd be a shame to just leave things like this, don't you think? Why not sit down and talk it through properly?
Norma's steps falter slightly. Her gaze drifts ahead, settling on nothing in particular.

speaker: Norma
content: ...There's no need. I did hurt her back then. She was right. I shouldn't have imposed my logic on her. Maybe she would've been better off without me. Then she wouldn't have been so seriously traumatized. I have no right to ask for her forgiveness.

speaker: Norma
content: Just being able to see her again... was already a bonus. And besides...
Her voice softens slightly.

speaker: Norma
content: Eileen seems... better now than she was before. She was able to move on and recover. I'm glad for her.
You don't press further, only offering a soft hum of acknowledgment. As the sky turns dark, streetlights cast long shadows on the ground.
Another weekend arrives. You invite Eileen out and bring her all the way to Norma's apartment building.

speaker: Eileen
content: What exactly is this "fun activity" you're talking about?

speaker: You
content: Following Norma.

speaker: Eileen
content: Huh?! Hey, just because we had a falling out doesn't mean I'm going to help you stalk her!

speaker: You
content: Shh. Follow me.
The building door clicks open. Norma steps out, her stride as brisk as ever.
You raise your hand, signaling Eileen to follow. She stamps her feet in protest but ultimately relents and catches up.
You tail her through the streets and watch as she enters a bank. Through the glass window, the counter's light falls on Norma, illuminating her calm and focused expression.

speaker: Bank Teller
content: Hi, Miss Norma, good to see you again. Same as usual? Fifteen transfers to the designated accounts? Would you like me to give you an update on their financial situations?

speaker: Norma
content: I've already reviewed the monthly reports. Johnny's family still lacks a sustainable income source. I'll set up an online game design course tailored to his situation next month. When he comes to withdraw his cash, please try to suggest to him that he could maybe become a game designer.

speaker: Norma
content: Also, please pay Holly's counseling fees while you're at it.
Eileen seems surprised.

speaker: Eileen
content: Johnny and Holly... Could they be...
You nod, confirming her guess.

speaker: You
content: That's right. Those are the victims from that incident years ago, or their family members.
Eileen doesn't say another word, simply watching Norma. Something shifts in her gaze.

speaker: Bank Teller
content: Don't worry, I'll take care of it. Miss Norma, you've been anonymously helping these families for years now. You truly have a heart of gold.

speaker: Norma
content: Don't call me Norma. How many times do I have to tell you? I go by Cindy here.

speaker: Bank Teller
content: Of course, Miss Norma.
The two are clearly well acquainted. Norma shoots the teller a sharp glare, but the teller only smiles, unfazed.

speaker: Eileen
content: ...You brought me here so I'd see the kindness Norma never displays in front of anyone, didn't you?
Eileen lowers her gaze and sighs softly.

speaker: Eileen
content: At first, when the pain was at its worst... I did resent her. I hated that she couldn't just be normal for once and understand how powerless I felt back then.

speaker: Eileen
content: But of course I knew she only wanted to help. It's just... in that state, I couldn't meet her expectations anymore. I was terrified of disappointing her, and I hated myself for not being able to just... heal faster.

speaker: Eileen
content: All of it piled up, bit by bit, until it crushed me. I projected the disgust I felt for myself on Norma... But maybe, deep down, I just wanted to push her away. So my pain wouldn't affect her anymore.

speaker: You
content: Maybe what hurt her was never being affected by your pain, but that you pushed her away. You might be one of the few friends she had... perhaps her only friend. So, will you consider giving her another chance?

speaker: Eileen
content: Didn't I already give her a chance? But she actually locked me behind a fire door! Damn it, she still thought she was helping me...
Eileen's eyebrows shoot up, the edge returning to her voice. But she catches herself in the middle and stops. Her shoulders sag slightly as she shakes her head in resignation.

speaker: Eileen
content: ...Whatever. That's just how she is. Dumb and stubborn, always deciding things for others. Guess I'll just have to be more forgiving.
She lowers her head with a smile, her voice softening.

speaker: Eileen
content: I'll reach out to her again. She's an important friend to me. Always has been, and still is. All those memories we shared... I don't want to just let them go.
You look over at Norma.
