speaker: Wolverine
content: He's the dog trainer who taught me how to track. He forced me to memorize the map of the Rust.
He flips through the files and points at the next picture.

speaker: Wolverine
content: This guy didn't let me eat at the table! He'd just throw a plate on the floor. And if I didn't catch a Corruptor, I wouldn't get any meat.

speaker: Wolverine
content: This guy would take me out on a leash to hunt Corruptors. He's such a coward that he was afraid I would bite him, so he always squeezed the rope on my collar as tight as it would be.
It seems like every name is a raw scar for Wolverine. Even though he's putting up a calm front, he's clenching his fists tighter and tighter.
But there's no time to be heartbroken over his past. None of the answers have been what you're looking for.
This is the gang leader. He should be the last on the list.

speaker: Wolverine
content: Hm, him... One time near the Rust, we were cornered by Corruptors. It was him who told me to hold the Corruptors back until he could get some weapons here with gang members.

speaker: Wolverine
content: Then, he ordered everyone to drop the unimportant baggage and escaped.
He averts his eyes so that you can't see the emotions in his eyes. But even Pippy realizes how hurt Wolverine feels, and softly whimpers to comfort him.
Unimportant baggage... Did this include Wolverine? You don't have the heart to ask him.

speaker: Wolverine
content: Then I lived by myself along the Rust until these guys came back and asked me to hunt in exchange for meat.

options: Follow up on who's behind the scenes

content: Did the leader ever take orders from some mysterious character?

speaker: Wolverine
content: I don't know. I don't think so.

options: Follow up on the source of Mania weapon info

content: Who told them how to make Mania weapons?

speaker: Wolverine
content: How should I know?

options: Follow up on how Mania weapons are sold

content: They've produced so many weapons. How do they sell them all?

speaker: Wolverine
content: Enough already, this is annoying!

speaker: Wolverine
content: It's been a long time since I had anything to do with those bastards!
Wolverine seems ready to leave, and even Pippy starts to show impatience.
Are there really no more leads? Just when you've decided to give up and put away the list, you discover there is one more page stuck at the back.
He looks like a scavenger—why is he on the gang roster?
Wait up. Before you leave, would you take a look at this one last person? He doesn't look like a gangster. He's called Hank...

speaker: Wolverine
content: Hank?!
As soon as he hears the name, Wolverine grabs the paper from you before you can ask more questions.
Do you know the person in this picture?
Hank... What does he have to do with gangsters and mania weapons?

speaker: Wolverine
content: What did you say? Hank?!
Hold on, you know the person in the picture?
Wolverine snatches the paper from your hand.

speaker: Wolverine
content: Far more than "knowing". I'll remember him until the day I die!
Wolverine growls the words through clenched teeth. If this man were standing here, Wolverine might rip him apart and devour him.
What's the relationship between you two?

speaker: Wolverine
content: Nothing! He is my enemy! If that old man ever lets me catch sight of him near the Rust, he's dead!

speaker: Wolverine
content: He hooks people with smooth words, then turns around and sells them off once he finds he can profit off them.

speaker: Wolverine
content: I was doing just fine alone in the Rust until he conned me out of it, tricked me into the gang, and then hauled ass with the money!
Hank was the one who got Wolverine stuck in the gang? If he provides toughs for the gang, no wonder he's on the list.
Wolverine mutters angrily, but you can sense a hint of grievance. Seems like he wasn't made into what he is just by the gang. Maybe this attached file will give him some comfort.
test
test
test
test
test
test
test
You should be happy. Your enemy is already dead.

speaker: Wolverine
content: Huh?
Your enemy, Hank, is confirmed dead.
Wolverine's breath catches. He looks at you in a daze, saying nothing. Silence falls in the interrogation room.
Pippy nudges his frozen master, but Wolverine still doesn't react for quite a while.

speaker: Wolverine
content: He's... dead?
That's right.
He repeats the question, his throat sounding drier than ever.

speaker: Wolverine
content: That old bastard... is dead?
The report claims so.

speaker: Wolverine
content: He can't be dead!
Without waiting for you to finish, Wolverine lets out a low growl.

speaker: Wolverine
content: Shouldn't he just take the gang's money and go spend it on booze and meat?

speaker: Wolverine
content: The old bastard is like a sewer rat, how could he die...
Wolverine opens and closes his mouth a few times, as if he can't quite swallow this new information. Whatever he wants to say, he can't get it out.
Didn't you say he was your enemy? You don't seem happy.

speaker: Wolverine
content: I am... happy. Of course I'm happy.

speaker: Wolverine
content:
But... I never got to beat him up, and he just died...
That old bastard got off too easy...
Even as he says that, the drooping corners of his mouth and strange reaction seem more like sorrow, not the joy of hearing that his enemy got what he deserved.

speaker: Wolverine
content: No.
But you look...

speaker: Wolverine
content: You're wrong.
You both sit in silence, until Wolverine speaks again, hoarsely.

speaker: Wolverine
content: How did Han... the old bastard die?
The cause of death?
You scan the file, but the only information about Hank is, "The scavenger Hank is confirmed dead." No cause of death, no autopsy report.
It's not recorded, which is strange. I can't believe someone would tamper with it. Maybe it had something to do with the weapon trade...
You close the folder and stand up. Wolverine is still sitting where he was, thinking over what you just said.
That's enough for today. I need time to go to the Rust and search for Hank's residence.

speaker: Wolverine
content: Wait!
He grabs your hand.

speaker: Wolverine
content: When are you going? I can be your guide.
You want to know how he died, right?

speaker: Wolverine
content: Who cares about that old man! It's... it's because the Rust is too dangerous, and you're an idiot. You'll get lost.
It doesn't seem like he's ready to be honest about the real reason he cares about Hank.
Okay, I can take you along.
I have a dedicated navigation device, I don't need a guide.

speaker: Wolverine
content: What, you mean one of those electric talking pieces of garbage? That won't help you...
You really want to go?

speaker: Wolverine
content: It's not that... I...
Alright, you can go.

speaker: Wolverine
content: Really?
On one condition: you have to promise not to do what you did to those guards today. Please don't hurt people without waiting for an explanation.

speaker: Wolverine
content: Okay...
Wolverine nods hard, and looks less like someone who has any connection to this case than a poor feral kid doing what he has to do to get by.
But what did Hank and Wolverine really have to do with each other? And what was the missing information hiding? You hope that what Hank left behind may hold some clues about the mania weapons.

It is the Rust, and it is a dump.
Filthy water flows openly, and awful smells fill your nose.
There are always pairs of eyes peering out from the dark places. With ill-intent, they track every stranger who sets foot in this region.
In order to investigate Hank's cause of death, you and Wolverine have come to his home, hoping that you will be able to find some clue among his belongings.

speaker: Wolverine
content: We're here, it's that tent up ahead.
He calls it a tent, but it's more like a bunch of rags supported on some wooden sticks, shaking perilously in the rotten wind.

speaker: Wolverine
content: Only the two of us? Aren't they coming along?
Wolverine glances at the guards stationed not far off.

options: Right, the two of us are enough.
They have other things to do.

content: It doesn't look that dangerous here. We don't need to call in the cavalry.
And it's not like you enjoy dealing with them anyway.
And right, don't forget you've promised...

speaker: Wolverine
content: I know, not to hurt anyone... so annoying.

As you step deeper, you feel the smell is enough to make your hair stand on end. There's rotten and stinky food, the ground is covered with filthy blackened clumps, and everyday items are piled in a corner. It's like a miniature dump.

speaker: Wolverine
content: These are the old bastard's clothes. Sometimes he would hide little things in his waistband.
Wolverine kicks some nearby rags, and Pippy raises his head to sniff them. He freezes, lets out a clear "O!" and hurries back to hide behind Wolverine.

Wolverine doesn't seem bothered. He searches through the trash intently. You see something bright flash out of the corner of your eye, and you follow the light to its source. It is a distorted steel basin.
It looks like a steel basin...

speaker: Wolverine
content: The old man washed food and bathed in it.
All in the same basin?

speaker: Wolverine
content: Of course. When he found me at the Rust, he used it to...

speaker: Wolverine
content: Well, forget it... It's not important...

speaker: Wolverine
content: Enough talk. Don't you have your work to do?
Wolverine turns his head away, avoiding your searching gaze. He continues digging through the trash.

options: Is there something you're looking for?

speaker: Wolverine
content: I... I just hate that you're going so slow!
Really?

Hank's belongings are messy and scattered. After a long time of searching, you haven't found anything. Just when you're ready to leave this reeking place to get some fresh air, a shadow appears in front of you.
Yo yo yo, isn't it that Wolverine who got sold to the gang? It's me! Don't you remember me? I'm Labiche! I used to live nearby!
When he hears the voice, Wolverine's steps slow down. He glares at him and walks right up.

speaker: Wolverine
content: Get out of here, I don't know you.

speaker: Labiche
content:
Don't be like that! I held you when you were found.
Oh, we have an honored guest here. Friend, may I know...
Labiche turns his flattering gaze toward you. You know how sensitive the MBCC is, so you vaguely tell him that—

speaker: Labiche
content: Ho ho, the cub has really latched onto a big shot, huh?

speaker: Labiche
content: Ho ho, how could we have someone as fancy as you passing by here? You must be some big shot the cub has latched onto.

speaker: Labiche
content: Look at that weapon, those clothes, and that fat, white little pet... Tsk tsk, you've been living the good life! No wonder you never came back to see us.

speaker: Labiche
content: Friend, let me tell you. Forget how clean he is now—when he was little, he was a little animal scrambling through the Rust basin. Naked, consorting every day with Corruptor monsters—he couldn't even speak!

speaker: Labiche
content: All he could say was ook ook, aa aa aha ha ha ha—

speaker: Pippy
content: Hiss!
None of what Labiche is saying is particularly kind. Even Pippy feels uncomfortable, baring his teeth at him.

speaker: Wolverine
content: Stop jabbering and stay out of our way!

speaker: Labiche
content: Out of your way? Maybe I could be your help! Friend, you came here for Hank, right?
On hearing Hank's name, Wolverine raises his question eagerly.

speaker: Wolverine
content: You know where Hank is? He's still alive, isn't he!

speaker: Labiche
content: Alive? He's been dead a while. I was there when he was found. He was stone cold, that man, buried in a hurry by two security officers.
You have confirmed multiple times that Hank is actually dead, but still do not know the reason.

speaker: Labiche
content: You want to know how old Hank died? You've come to the right person, friend!
You have confirmed multiple times that Hank is actually dead, but still do not know the reason. Perhaps there is a clue in what Labiche saw...

speaker: Labiche
content: You've come to the right person, friend! I got a good look at every wound on Hank's body.
Seemingly disinterested, Wolverine pricks up his ears to listen closely to Labiche.

speaker: Labiche
content: I've been a scavenger along the Rust for years. I've seen it a million times before. I'm sure he was killed by Corruptors.
Corruptors?

speaker: Labiche
content: Right! The weird thing is he had a ton of injuries. There were flesh and guts everywhere...

speaker: Labiche
content: Living in the Rust basin for that long, the old guy had to have a lot of skill, so there must have been a crazy number of Corruptors to rip him up like that!

speaker: Labiche
content: Back then when he sold this little animal, he didn't share a coin of what he earned with us. Ha, guess he deserves it!
Was there anything suspicious about his death?

speaker: Labiche
content: Isn't that many Corruptors killing one old guy suspicious enough? I didn't see one piece of skin left whole on Old Hank, it's like they're revenging or something! I'd say he was punished for what he had done before!
While you're still thinking through this, Wolverine's veins have begun to bulge.
Pippy also seems to feel his master's anger and looks worriedly at Wolverine. Only Labiche continues his monologue as if he hasn't noticed anything.

speaker: Labiche
content:
Finding this little beast made him so proud, he taught him how to speak and the so-called meaning of life.
That **** was always talking about "the Meaning of Life," but he was trampled by Corruptors in the end, he deserves it, hahaha...

speaker: Labiche
content: Ah—!
Before you can react, Wolverine has already punched the scavenger's face.

speaker: Labiche
content: What's wrong with you, you little beast!
Wolverine is shaking with rage.

speaker: Wolverine
content: Stop laughing! Is this funny to you?

speaker: Labiche
content: When was I laughing at you? Oh... you still don't like being called a little beast.

speaker: Wolverine
content: Hank is dead! Do you think this is funny?!

speaker: Labiche
content: Huh? Of course it's...

speaker: Labiche
content: Aah!
Wolverine hits Labiche again, and throws him to the ground.
Stop! Before we left, you promised me you wouldn't hurt anyone!
Wolverine is too furious to listen to you. He chokes Labiche and slams his head against the ground, then punches him again.

speaker: Wolverine
content: I'll show you funny!
Another punch, and you hear a sharp cracking sound from Labiche's nose.

speaker: Labiche
content: Help... Friend... help...

speaker: Wolverine
content: Show you funny!
Labiche's front teeth have been knocked out, and he's out of breath to call for help. The thick smell of blood mixes with the rotten stench of the dump.
Wolverine, stop! You'll kill him!

speaker: Wolverine
content: I want to kill him!
Wolverine has no intention of staying his hand, cruelly raining down blow after blow on Labiche's head and body. Labiche's bones make a series of cracking noises and sag deeply.
Wolverine, stop!
Deep red shackles cover Wolverine and bind him, devouring the scarlet in his eyes.
The shackles force him to stop punching, but he still struggles against them.

speaker: Wolverine
content: Let me go! I want to kill him!
He lets out angry growls and tries to break free from the shackles. All he is thinking of is pouncing again on the already-dying Labiche.

speaker: Wolverine
content: Get out of here! This has nothing to do with you!
Wolverine pushes away from you and continues to torment the dying scavenger.
By the time Hecate sees the red light of the shackles and brings guards, Labiche is practically a corpse.

speaker: Hecate
content: Sinner S-076 attempted to kill a civilian in the Rust—vile behavior. Chief, according to the rules, he needs to be locked up...

speaker: Wolverine
content: So do it. Wouldn't that be just right?
He has no intention of defending himself and is not giving you a chance to explain things to him.

speaker: Wolverine
content:
I see it now, you aren't any different from those gang bastards.
You just want a dog on a leash who won't bite. You're just using me!

options: Why did you want to kill him?

speaker: Wolverine
content: How could I!

speaker: Wolverine
content: Hank fed me, clothed me, taught me to speak! He was the first person to treat me like a human being!

speaker: Wolverine
content: Even when he was starving, he would put aside a mouthful of soup for me!

speaker: Wolverine
content: Hank is different from this bastard, the gang dog trainers, and the people in the Bureau!

speaker: Wolverine
content: And he would never put me in such shackles!

speaker: Wolverine
content: I won't let anyone laugh at him or insult him!

speaker: Wolverine
content: Because he deserved it! I won't allow trash like that to insult Hank!
Isn't Hank your enemy, who sold you to the gang?

speaker: Wolverine
content: But he was also the only one who ever treated me like a human being!

speaker: Wolverine
content: Hank fed me, clothed me, and taught me how to speak! Even when he was starving himself, he'd set aside a mouthful of soup for me!

speaker: Wolverine
content: Hank is different from this bastard, the gang dog trainers, and the people in the Bureau!

speaker: Wolverine
content: And he would never put me in such shackles!

This is the first time you've heard Wolverine speak so much at once.
Now you not only know Hank's significance to him but also realize his complaints about you.
I never intend to control you. I was trying to stop you from making another wrong choice.

speaker: Wolverine
content: I wasn't wrong!
Murder is wrong!

speaker: Wolverine
content: He deserved to die!
He was extremely rude, but you can't let yourself be controlled by your emotions. You have to respect ethics and the law!

speaker: Wolverine
content: What do ethics and the law have to do with me!
Of course they have to do with you. You said you don't like being called a dog or a monster, right?
I believe that hunting Corruptors was a matter of survival for you, but if I had just let you kill him today, you'll be considered all the more as just a mad dog who bites anyone you see.
If you can't control your own emotions, body, and killing instinct, then you will only ever be a wild beast, and will never be considered a human being.
Wolverine stares at the floor and clenches his fist angrily, but stops struggling. His fingernails are digging into his palms.
Now, calm down. Violence doesn't solve anything.

speaker: Wolverine
content: It's none of your damn business! Let me go!
Okay, I can release the shackles. But you know, if you had really killed that scavenger today, you would be considered a wild beast.

speaker: Wolverine
content: I don't want to listen to your crap...
The difference between a human being and a monster is that humans are limited by the law and ethics.
Don't you want people to stop calling you beast and treating you like a dog?
But if you can't control your own emotions, body, and killing instinct, then you will only ever be a wild beast, and will never be considered a human being.

Wolverine opens his mouth a few times, but ends up saying nothing. Lowering his head, he stares at the ground and angrily clenches his fists, but stops struggling at last. His fingernails are digging into his palms.
You hear a voice from far away, as Hecate calls the guards here.

speaker: Hecate
content: Chief, there was a red flash just now. You were using your ability...
Hecate stops her words. The blood all over the ground, the comatose Labiche and the Wolverine restrained by the shackles... The situation is obvious.

speaker: Hecate
content: Sinner S-076 has hurt a civilian and must be dealt with severely.
Wolverine is still staring stunned at the ground, processing what you just said.
I will teach and discipline Wolverine personally. Nothing to worry about.

speaker: Hecate
content: Understood... Any progress in the investigation of the Corruptor trade?
Hm... Have you ever heard of a whole lot of Corruptors in the Rust banding together to attack one person?

speaker: Hecate
content: Corruptor attacks don't follow any pattern. They normally just happen.

speaker: Hecate
content: A few Corruptors attacking are enough to kill an ordinary person with no special ability.

speaker: Hecate
content: A whole lot of Corruptors attacking the same target... You think someone was controlling them?
The scavenger is about to be in serious trouble. We should get him to medical treatment first.

speaker: Hecate
content: OK. And S-076...
I will teach and discipline Wolverine personally. Now I have something more important for you.
Going by that scavenger's story, Hank's death was strange indeed.
If Hank was an old man with no special ability, a few Corruptors would have been enough to kill him. Why did so many attack him?

speaker: Hecate
content: You suspect someone is controlling Corruptors?
I'm not sure yet. We do need to look into everything in this place carefully again.
Hecate immediately takes the staff to clean up the scene.
Without saying a word, Wolverine watches them carry Labiche away and pack up Hank's belongings. He looks a bit nostalgic.

After all, this was where he had lived.
His first "home."

speaker: Report
content: "The items brought back have been individually checked. In addition to household items, a black cloth was found, on which excess Mania residue was detected. This has been submitted to the FAC for further research."

speaker: Report
content: "The team also found a wolf tooth necklace, well-preserved. Fingerprints thereon matched Sinner S-076's. It is suspected to be the Sinner's property and has been left to the Chief to handle..."
This investigation finds almost nothing. While brooding over Mania weapons, you hear a rustling noise from the pile of documents.
Chk chk chk! Chk chk chk!
A black and white furball peeks out of the pile of documents on your desk.
Chk chk chk!!!
The furball angrily raises its head. It's Wolverine's pet, Pippy.
Aren't you Pippy who's always on Wolverine's shoulder? What are you doing here?

speaker: Pippy
content: Chk!
Seeing that you recognize him, Pippy climbs on top of your files and points to the picture of Wolverine, tugging your sleeve.
Wolverine? What's wrong with him?
Pippy keeps trying to pull you outward with all his might.
Pippy nods and gestures. You fail to understand.
It seems you should follow Pippy to see what's happening. And... you have something to give Wolverine anyway.
You follow Pippy into the yard, where Wolverine is sitting alone on top of a wall, facing the Rust.
Pippy nimbly climbs up the wall and sits back onto his master's shoulder, reporting that he has finished his task.

options: What are you doing up there?

content: He points to his nose without answering your question.

speaker: Wolverine
content: Everything alright here?
Labiche is fine. He seemed pretty happy once we paid out compensation.

speaker: Wolverine
content: Tsk, who cares about that bastard... I'm asking about your nose! I hit you in the interrogation room.

speaker: Wolverine
content: Tsk, idiot... I'm asking about your nose! I hit you in the interrogation room.
I had almost forgotten about it until you said something. That was just a little tap. I recovered ages ago.

speaker: Wolverine
content: Oh... Well, I'm sorry.
Wolverine pouts absentmindedly and won't look directly at you.

speaker: Wolverine
content: Also... I'm sorry I lost control, and didn't respect our agreement.
Wolverine is apologizing but still looks arrogant. He doesn't lower his head and keeps looking toward the Rust.
Now that you know it was wrong, don't do it again.

speaker: Wolverine
content:
That's all?
...You're as strange as he was.

speaker: Wolverine
content: No matter what happened, with those two little words—I'm sorry—he would forgive everything.
You don't look like knowing why what you did was wrong.

speaker: Wolverine
content: I. Am. Sorry.

speaker: Wolverine
content: Aren't those the magic words? You're just as picky as him.
"Him"? You mean Hank? Is that why you only listened to me in the interrogation room, because I'm like him?

speaker: Wolverine
content: Who said I listen to you? You just have those same stinky habits the way he did... What's there to be proud of?

speaker: Hank
content: Hey, kid! Why aren't you wearing any clothes? Where are your mommy and daddy?

speaker: Hank
content: Are you going around on all fours? No way, you look like a wild baby... Ow! You bit me!

speaker: Little Wolverine
content: Grr—

speaker: Hank
content: If it's meat you want, I'll cook some! Relax!
Hank escapes with some struggles. He turns away and pulls a piece of meat protected by layers of newspapers from his pile of trash. Then he puts it onto a hot stone until the fat begins to sizzle.

speaker: Hank
content: Ah ah ah, this meat is a good thing. You don't see many people like me anymore, who will repay evil with kindness. Now, what do you say about biting me just now?

speaker: Little Wolverine
content: ...Awoo?

speaker: Hank
content: I forgot you're a feral child. You can't speak. Okay, repeat after me: I'm sorry, gramp, you're a good man, I shouldn't have bitten you.

speaker: Hank
content: That's a little long, huh? Ok, try this one: I'm. Sorry.

speaker: Little Wolverine
content: Aye. Sawi...

speaker: Hank
content: I. Am. Sorry.

speaker: Little Wolverine
content: Aye. Sawi?

speaker: Hank
content: ...Alright, I'll forgive you for now. We still have a long time to learn!

speaker: Little Wolverine
content: Aye! Sawi!

speaker: Hank
content: Okay, okay, eat your meat!

speaker: Wolverine
content: Heh...
You hear the young man on the wall make a soft, happy noise, but you have never heard Wolverine laugh, except for sneers.

speaker: Wolverine
content: Me?
You and Pippy both nod.

speaker: Wolverine
content: Oh, maybe... I was thinking back to when I was little.
That was Pippy laughing. It definitely wasn't you!

speaker: Wolverine
content: You've got to get your ears checked...
So it was you?

speaker: Wolverine
content: What, can't I laugh? I was just... thinking back to when I was little.

speaker: Wolverine
content: I was trained by the gang for too long, and then I lived alone for a while—there's a lot I've forgotten.

speaker: Wolverine
content: But since I met you, I've recalled some of it.

speaker: Tramp
content: Hahaha, look, everyone! The old bastard's brought a young bastard, and they're playing house!
The tramp throws a stone at Wolverine from far away.

speaker: Tramp
content: Hey, little freak, beg me and I'll give you and the old man some meat!
Little Wolverine bares his teeth. It looks like he's about to jump on the tramp and rip out his throat.

speaker: Hank
content: Wolverine, stop!

speaker: Little Wolverine
content: Die!

speaker: Hank
content: It's not a big deal, we'll find meat on our own. Ignore him!

speaker: Tramp
content: You can talk! You've fed the pup your winter stores. What food do you have left? You gonna eat trash? Hahaha.

speaker: Little Wolverine
content: Kill!

speaker: Hank
content: Every day with the shouting "beat" and "kill." Is the animal name making you a real animal?

speaker: Hank
content: Do you remember what gramp said to you? What makes you different from the animals is—

speaker: Hank
content: It's in one ear and out the other—Don't be impulsive! Impulses are the devil!

speaker: Tramp
content: Yo, do you even know how to spell "impulsive"? What a load!

speaker: Hank
content: The hell business is it of yours? When Wolverine grows up, he'll learn and teach it to me!

speaker: Wolverine
content: Hey, Ch— you!
Up on the wall, Wolverine whirls around to face you.

speaker: Wolverine
content: Do you know how to spell "impulsive"?
Of course. Do you want to learn to read and write?

speaker: Wolverine
content: I don't want to learn anything else, just that one word, "impulsive."
While you're still trying to figure out what Wolverine means, a black shadow springs from behind you—

speaker: Demolia
content: Hey, Chief!!
The girl's voice is loud, and you're completely startled.
Demolia? When did you get here?

speaker: Demolia
content: Just now, but shouldn't Wolferine have noticed me, sitting up that high?

speaker: Wolverine
content: It's Wol-VER-ine!
Wolverine crosses his arms and turns around, unhappy at being interrupted.

speaker: Demolia
content: What are you doing sitting on a wall? Oh, I know, you like pondering the meaning of life, like me. Life is like scavenging in trash...
Demolia! Why are you here?

speaker: Demolia
content: I almost forgot! I was looking for you to come drinking, Chief! A lot of people are waiting for you! Let's go!
Demolia pulls you to leave the yard. Wolverine acts like he didn't hear, keeping his back turned and not showing any intention to stop you.
Wolverine, do you want to come with us?

speaker: Demolia
content: Hey, that's a great idea! He's never joined us in anything before!

speaker: Wolverine
content: No, I don't know them.
Don't you want to learn how to write? If you come, I'll teach you how to write "impulsive."

speaker: Wolverine
content: Tsk. I'll ask someone else.
There's a lot of good food at a party!
Pippy starts to salivate, but Wolverine still doesn't move.
Time to play the trump card.
So you are afraid?
After all, it's easy to lose control when you're drunk. Then, learning to write "impulsive" and even copying it out a hundred times wouldn't change anything.

speaker: Wolverine
content: Nothing that makes you lose control can be a good thing! I'm definitely not going!
He's clearly eager, but won't stop being stubborn.
Time to play the trump card.

Wolverine jumps down from the wall before you can finish.

content: I'll go.

speaker: Demolia
content: Hooray!
Wolverine takes the box from your hands and opens it before he's even come to a stop. A wolf tooth necklace lies within. The crude tooth is a little yellow and strung on a leather cord.
When Hecate was checking through the scene, she found a clue to the Mania weapon trade and this necklace.

options: It seemed like you were looking for this.

speaker: Wolverine
content: ...Yes.
The person who found it said it was hidden in a box and taken care of very well. It was important, right?

speaker: Wolverine
content: The old bastard gave it to me. When I realized he was selling me to the gang, I threw it away.

speaker: Wolverine
content: I don't know where he got it back...

speaker: Little Wolverine
content: Hank, what are you doing?

speaker: Hank
content: Hehe, I'm making you a present. Look, do you like it?

content: Don't want a present. I want meat.

speaker: Hank
content: A year ago today was the day I found you. It might as well be your birthday. You should have a heartfelt gift better than meat.

speaker: Little Wolverine
content: You mean you couldn't get any meat.

speaker: Hank
content: You little jerk. I'll sell you before I let us starve to death!

content: No.

speaker: Hank
content: What do you mean no? If you go with someone else, you'll be able to eat as much as you want. I wish I had someone to sell me!

speaker: Little Wolverine
content: No!

speaker: Hank
content: Hahaha, I'm kidding. What are you angry about? I don't know how you got so petty... Anyway, do you want the necklace or not?

speaker: Little Wolverine
content: Yes!
Wolverine looks at the necklace in his hands, distracted.
What was Hank—the man who most wanted to see Wolverine become a human being—thinking when he found this necklace, after learning that the gang had turned Wolverine into their war dog?
Did Hank regret at that moment?
You may never know.

speaker: Demolia
content: What are you waiting for? Hurry, hurry! They'll drink it all before we get there!
Let's go, Wolverine!
Wolverine collects the necklace and follows behind you towards people and places unknown.

speaker: Wolverine
content: Okay, I'm coming.
You push open the door and walk into the reception room.
Upon hearing you enter, the man in front of you stands up, a big smile on his face. He extends his hand to you.
Thank you for taking the time to meet with me, Chief.
The man is wearing a crumpled trench coat, and his tie has come loose. He looks every bit the typical middle-aged man you'd see around Eastside.
He is courteous, but looks uneasy. Nevertheless, you shake his outstretched hand.
My name is Frank Miller; I'm a clerk from the City Council.

speaker: Frank
content: Ah, when I sent the email requesting a visit, I thought: The Chief of the MBCC was the most popular figure these days. My email would probably go unanswered, and I should count myself lucky if I received a rejection email.

speaker: Frank
content: I really lucked out. I can't believe that the Chief of the MBCC, who saved millions of lives in the West District, would agree to meet someone as insignificant as me. You do live up to the name "Heroic Chief."
The man's over-the-top tone and demeanor are making you feel a bit uncomfortable.

speaker: Chief
content: Thank you, Mr. Frank. That's what I should do.
You check the time on your terminal and decide to put a stop to his cringeworthy praises.

speaker: Chief
content: Tell me why you've come.

speaker: Frank
content: Sorry, sorry... What you and your Sinners have accomplished in the West District is really, really inspiring! Seeing you in person, I-I just got carried away...
The man adjusts his tie.

speaker: Frank
content: Long story short: thanks to you, the number of supporters of our policy has been increasing, and our work is going more smoothly now.

speaker: Chief
content: ...Whose policy? Whose work?
The man hears the doubt in your voice.

speaker: Frank
content: Ours...

speaker: Frank
content: The progressives in the City Council.

speaker: Frank
content: I'm here today to invite you to a hearing scheduled to take place one week from now...

You must have heard about the hearing. It's a public meeting scheduled by the City Council, in response to the recent events that have transpired in the West District. As soon as the news about the hearing was out, it attracted attention from all walks of life in Eastside.

speaker: Chief
content: So, you guys want me to... pick sides at this hearing regarding the Executive Committee's dereliction of duty, to declare support for the progressives...

speaker: Frank
content: No, no, we're not asking you to pick sides. Currently, the majority of the City Council members are, for lack of a better word, conservatives... We know we're no match for them; we wouldn't ask you to make an enemy out of them.

speaker: Frank
content: All you need to do is speak your mind and tell the truth when the time comes.
The man rubs his palms together, looking somewhat uneasy.

speaker: Frank
content: At this juncture, the liberation and welfare of the people of the West District is a sure thing.

speaker: Frank
content: We're not asking you to take our side. We're just hoping you'll stay on the side of the people of the West District. You're on their side, aren't you?

speaker: Frank
content: I heard that there's another MBCC member who played an active role in the recent events and fared brilliantly. The name is Matilda. If Miss Matilda could choose the side of the people of the West District as well, it would undoubtedly be a huge help!
After his passionate speech, the man gives you a meaningful smile.

speaker: Frank
content: Of course, you won't be fighting alone.

speaker: Frank
content: We've won over some of the media outlets that are eligible to attend the hearing, and they'll report the truth. We'll also help hold back pressure from the conservatives.

speaker: Frank
content: On top of that, we've had some funds ready, for investigation purposes. You can make use of them whenever you need.
The man produces a black card from his pocket and slides it over the tabletop.
Without saying a word, you slide the card back.
Surprise registers in the man's eyes. Finally, you speak.

speaker: Chief
content: I will attend the hearing.

speaker: Frank
content: I've heard so much about how noble the Chief of the MBCC is. Today, I've seen it with my own eyes.

speaker: Chief
content: As for Matilda...
You look the man in the eye.

speaker: Chief
content: I'm her superior, yes, but I still need to ask for her opinion.

speaker: Chief
content: She's a former member of the Executive Committee, after all. Whether she wants to choose sides at this point is her decision entirely.

speaker: Frank
content: Of course, of course.
The man can no longer keep joy from his face. He makes himself look slightly more presentable before extending his hand to you once again.

speaker: Frank
content: I have faith in Miss Matilda. She'll make the choice she believes to be right.

speaker: Matilda
content: So, you've given them your word?

speaker: Chief
content: I only promised to tell the truth.
Despite the fact that you haven't had much contact with Matilda since she arrived at the Bureau, her meticulous and efficient working style has left a strong impression on you.
Although she can come across as rigid and formal—a result of her strict adherence to rules, she's a very reliable adjutant professionally.

speaker: Chief
content: But I'm not going to speak for the benefit of the progressives, even though their offer is indeed tempting.
A large amount of money, political quid pro quo... You explain the progressives' offer to Matilda.
Throughout your explanation, the neatly dressed former Executive Committee adjutant listens without uttering a word.
When you're finished, she ponders for a moment before making her comments.

speaker: Matilda
content: If I may speak frankly, Chief, this invitation might not be what you think it is.

speaker: Matilda
content: It is... a trap.

speaker: Matilda
content: Yes, a trap.

speaker: Matilda
content: That the progressives in the City Council will make a move after the Executive Committee's debacle is to be expected. But, to put it bluntly, they don't have what it takes to pull off anything major.

speaker: Matilda
content: Political quid pro quo... well, that's possible, given that they hold 8% of the seats on the City Council.

speaker: Matilda
content: But the funds...

speaker: Matilda
content: I don't know the exact amount. But the card you just mentioned... if I'm not mistaken, it was issued by a private bank that has business dealings with many big figures in Eastside's political and business circles.

speaker: Matilda
content: They only provide one-on-one services, known for their ability to guarantee complete confidentiality for their clients. Whether your assets are gray or black, they can make them clean.

speaker: Matilda
content: Unfortunately for the councilors from the progressive wing, their private assets might not be large enough to qualify them for cards from this bank.

speaker: Chief
content: Are you saying...

speaker: Matilda
content: Yes. I'm certain that this Frank is not a member of the progressive wing.

speaker: Matilda
content: These so-called progressives appeared on the scene several decades ago. But ten years ago, they were completely defeated, and they've never been on center stage since.

speaker: Matilda
content: Today, they exist on the periphery of the City Council, serving as a "necessary opposing voice." They owe their existence to the mercy of those in power.

speaker: Matilda
content: The Executive Committee's debacle represents an opportunity for them, one that they must seize. Unfortunately for them, this kind of game...
Matilda looks at you with a smile on her face.

speaker: Matilda
content: It's simply out of their league.

speaker: Chief
content: Your understanding of the workings of the City Council far exceeds my expectations.
Matilda knows too much for an adjutant of a frontline Executive Officer.

speaker: Chief
content: If it weren't for you, I would still be kept in the dark.

speaker: Matilda
content: It's what I should do as your subordinate.

speaker: Matilda
content: You don't deal with them often. It's hard to know the truth without sufficient information.

speaker: Matilda
content: Add that to what this Frank did... The Speaker's faction has always been good at using these little tricks... This is why I'm so sure of my conclusion.

speaker: Chief
content: The Speaker's faction?
The conclusion, so casually made by Matilda, confuses you even more.

speaker: Chief
content: You're saying the Speaker, leader of the conservative wing of the City Council, wants me to truthfully present the situation in the West District, to make statements that are harmful to them?
Matilda picks up on your confusion and goes on to explain:

speaker: Matilda
content: Yes. Although it seems contradictory, the logic is not hard to grasp.

speaker: Matilda
content: Like I said earlier, this is a trap, but you're not the target, Chief.

speaker: Matilda
content: I am.
Matilda pauses for a moment. Looking you in the eye, she continues:

speaker: Matilda
content: Bernadette Cavendish... You must've heard of this name, I presume?
You have. You're not in the habit of seeking out news about the political scene, but you've heard this name mentioned here and there, through this channel or that.
The de facto leader of the Cavendish family, a star member of the City Council, a role model for the women in Eastside... and a popular candidate for the Speaker's seat in next year's election.
And then the full name of Matilda springs to your mind. You first came across the name while skimming through her file when she was transferred to the MBCC.

speaker: Chief
content: Matilda Cavendish...

speaker: Matilda
content: Yes, that's my full name. Councilor Bernadette, the current City Secretary...

speaker: Matilda
content: She is my aunt.
Things start to make sense now.
When the West District Reconstruction Committee was dissolved following its failure, many of its members faced dire consequences.
As a former member, Matilda was swiftly transferred to the MBCC, the safest place a Sinner can be.
And now, the consequences have come looking for her.

speaker: Chief
content: So, the Speaker's faction intends to use you against your aunt, right?

speaker: Matilda
content: Yes.

speaker: Matilda
content: The real threat to the Speaker has never been the progressives, but his overly active "subordinate" who has announced her candidacy.

speaker: Matilda
content: Few things pose a threat to Ms. Bernadette. Unfortunately, due to a combination of many uncontrollable factors, I seem to have become the only weak point that the Speaker can take advantage of.
Matilda looks up at you, her eyes filled with apology.

speaker: Matilda
content: Chief, I'm sorry for getting you involved...

speaker: Chief
content: If you're worried about the possible adverse effect on Councilor Bernadette, I can make a joint statement with you at the hearing, cutting ties with all factions...
Before you can finish, Matilda shakes her head.

speaker: Matilda
content: It won't work.

speaker: Matilda
content: I'm a member of the Cavendish family. Once I stand behind the podium to say my piece, everything I have done, everything I have said... it will be used by the other conservatives to attack Ms. Bernadette.

speaker: Matilda
content: A relative of a conservative councilor openly expressing sympathy for the West District... This is likely to become the biggest stain on Ms. Bernadette's political career...

speaker: Matilda
content: I could claim that I did what I did in the West District because I was forced to. This would possibly minimize the damage to our family's interests, but...

speaker: Matilda
content: After all I have been through, I can't, in good conscience, bring myself to lie.
Matilda lowers her head. Her lips are moving, as if she has something more to say, but nothing comes out.
The fact that Matilda is in so much agony can only mean one thing...
She has decided to attend the hearing.

speaker: Chief
content: You're right. We've been through it all together...

speaker: Chief
content: I don't know much about politics, but I can play tricks too.

speaker: Chief
content: I can get you a medical report saying that you were critically injured during an operation in the West District and almost died.

speaker: Chief
content: Or I can tell them that you've been sent to a satellite town for an important task.

speaker: Chief
content: My point is, as long as you're not available, they can't use you to attack Councilor Bernadette...
Your attempt at humor works, at least for a moment. Matilda's furrowed brow relaxes slightly.

speaker: Matilda
content: Haha...

speaker: Matilda
content: Even if I disappeared from DisCity, it wouldn't really help the situation.

speaker: Matilda
content: The Speaker's faction has set their plan in motion. They're going to pull out all the stops to turn the spotlight on me, whether I attend the hearing or not.

speaker: Matilda
content: I won't let that stop me from speaking up for the West District. If not me, who else will?
You understand Matilda's choice.

You understand why she is choosing to speak up for the West District, even though she can't really change anything or weaken the conservatives' position in the City Council, and anything she says and does can be used against her family.
Since the very beginning, she has never considered not attending the hearing. She is anxious to convey everything she saw and learned in the West District to Eastside.
Her mind is made up. Matilda looks back at you with a determined look in her eyes.

speaker: Matilda
content: I won't run away. I must attend the hearing.

speaker: Matilda
content: Even if the Speaker's faction has considered everything, there's one thing they got wrong.

speaker: Matilda
content: I, the "pawn," am the only variable.

speaker: Chief
content: You have thought of a countermeasure?

speaker: Matilda
content: I wouldn't call it a countermeasure, but... I want to give it a try.

speaker: Matilda
content: Ms. Bernadette must've known about the Speaker's faction's move, but so far, the Cavendish family hasn't made any public announcement to sever ties with me.

speaker: Matilda
content: Which means that Ms. Bernadette believes that I'll make the right choice, even though it may not be a choice the family would want me to make. But I will never let my aunt and the rest of my family down.

speaker: Matilda
content: I'll do everything I can before the hearing to find a way to turn the situation around.
Matilda takes a deep breath. Her expression becomes even more determined.

speaker: Chief
content: All right... I understand.

speaker: Chief
content: By the way, is there anything I can help you with?
Matilda thinks for a moment, and then gives you a somewhat shy smile; she rarely smiles.

speaker: Matilda
content: If it's not too much to ask...

speaker: Matilda
content: Could I use your office for a while?
36 hours before the hearing, 4:29 A.M.
You've just wrapped up the day's work, ready to get some rest, but a source of bright light draws you to the second floor of the workspace.
The light comes from your office. You let Matilda use the office, where she has easy access to a large amount of documents and confidential information.
There haven't been many pressing matters that require your attention lately. To give Matilda space, you moved out of your office. Nevertheless, you're surprised to find Matilda up this late.
The door is ajar. You ease it open wider. Behind the mountain of files and disposable coffee cups on the table, you see the person hard at work.
The soft rustling of pen against paper is constant in the quiet, and she doesn't seem to notice your presence.

speaker: Matilda
content: Chief?

speaker: Matilda
content: You're still up?

speaker: Chief
content: Just got off work.

speaker: Chief
content: Are you still prepping for tomorrow's hearing?

speaker: Matilda
content: ...Yes.
Matilda sounds tired. Still, she's making an effort to keep lethargy out of her voice while answering you.

You glance at the corner of the table and notice the sheets of paper covered with color-coded notes. From something as small as a punctuation mark to something as large as a whole paragraph, nothing has escaped her meticulous pen. Collectively, they reflect the writer's thorough thought process.
However, it's obvious that this stack of paper is unwanted.
The writer holds herself to extremely high standards, and while that is true, it's the mental burden that plays a major role in her being so hard on herself.

speaker: Chief
content: Only a few pages of paper...

speaker: Matilda
content: Sorry, what did you say?
Your voice is low, and Matilda has a lapse of concentration and fails to catch what you've just said.

speaker: Chief
content: What I was trying to say is, we've been through a lot in the West District, but it can be summed up on just a few pieces of copy paper.

speaker: Chief
content: It's in fact a story worthy of the adjective "epic."
You remove a piece of paper from the unwanted stack and give it a quick scan.

speaker: Chief
content: A lot of numbers in here, a lot of zeros. Like how much drinking water the West District needs every day, or how many emergency supplies, or how much of this or that is needed to maintain the stability of the entire West District.

speaker: Chief
content: You must've put a lot of thought into deciding on what units to use; you're trying to explain the problems faced by the West District without embarrassing the people involved too much.

speaker: Chief
content: Unfortunately, numbers are cold. They arise from the collision of different interests; they are conditions added as an afterthought when the big shots are trying to reach an agreement.

speaker: Chief
content: Even the experiences we had together in the West District, the emotions these experiences evoked... They can tell a more touching tale than numbers ever will.
Matilda listens to your long speech. When you're finished, she puts down the pen she's holding.

speaker: Matilda
content: How I wish I could tell stories to them.
Matilda rises to her feet, reaches out reflexively for a paper cup, but catches herself.

speaker: Matilda
content: At this hour... I don't think it's a good idea to offer you coffee.

speaker: Chief
content: It's okay. Take a break. Let's have a chat.

speaker: Chief
content: Speaking of stories, I know nothing about your story before you joined the Executive Committee. Care to share it?
Matilda looks you in the eye, and sighs as if with resignation.

speaker: Matilda
content: Are you always this blunt when you "chat" with others?

speaker: Chief
content: Haha...
Matilda looks away from your smiling face and toward the window.

speaker: Matilda
content: My story is not a complicated one... My childhood was not that different from that of most Eastside children. If there's any difference, it's probably that my father's last name is Cavendish.

speaker: Matilda
content: I grew up under the protection of my parents. Until the incident in N.F. 104 changed everything...

speaker: Matilda
content: Yes.

speaker: Matilda
content: The political scene of Eastside was thrown into turmoil that year. That came about when Abel, a candidate for the Speaker's seat supported by the Cavendish family, was assassinated and died during a campaign speech.

speaker: Matilda
content: The Cavendish family poured all its resources into this attempt at ascending to the peak of power in the City Council, but almost ended up the way the Executive Committee did, narrowly avoiding the fate of being divided up by the family's political enemies.

speaker: Matilda
content: My parents lost their lives in the turmoil...

speaker: Chief
content: ...It must have been a very difficult time.

speaker: Matilda
content: For the family, yes.

speaker: Matilda
content: But relatively speaking, I was lucky...

speaker: Matilda
content: After my parents passed away, my aunt, Ms. Bernadette, adopted me.

speaker: Chief
content: Your guardian is the star councilor in the City Council, the leader of a political family... She couldn't have had much time for her small "family," right?
Matilda gives a soft laugh, her eyes sparkling.

speaker: Matilda
content: You're right. She didn't have much time to care for me. But that doesn't mean she failed as a guardian.

speaker: Matilda
content: She sent me to the best elite school in all of Eastside, hired the best teachers to give me private lessons on etiquette and teach me all the other skills useful in social situations...

speaker: Matilda
content: We didn't spend much time together, but whenever she was with me, she'd always let me know that she knew about my latest achievements, and she'd give me suggestions for what I should do next.

speaker: Matilda
content: I made many mistakes, but she never made me feel bad about them.

speaker: Matilda
content: She allowed my mistakes, my immaturity, my shortsightedness.

speaker: Matilda
content: At the same time, she made a point of telling me, "The most important thing is to find your true self when your mistakes lead you astray and locate the path that suits you best."

speaker: Chief
content: Find your true self, huh? Sounds like your aunt was a major influence in your life.

speaker: Chief
content: Sadly, your aunt's true self seems to have led her to a completely different path from yours.
Matilda's bright eyes dull somewhat at your remark.
She closes her eyes, as if reminiscing, or contemplating the true meaning of the term "true self."
After a long while, she opens her eyes and, slowly, she speaks:

speaker: Matilda
content: I didn't understand what true self really meant at first.

speaker: Matilda
content: I was just an ordinary person, with no outstanding talents. I couldn't hold a candle to those real geniuses at the elite school.

speaker: Matilda
content: From the textbooks, the teachers at the school, the propaganda from Eastside... I learned the rules of society.

speaker: Matilda
content: I thought that if I followed these rules and worked really hard, I could at least narrow the gap between Ms. Bernadette and me.

speaker: Matilda
content: It's like target practice... Do you know anything about target practice, Chief?

speaker: Matilda
content: The concept of target practice is simple. All you need to do is hit the bull's-eye, or get as close to it as you can.

speaker: Matilda
content: For the longest time, I stayed in the shooting range that was Eastside and shot targets other people put up for me...

speaker: Matilda
content: Ms. Bernadette, taught me all the techniques and rules, and even the "gun" in my hand was given by her.

speaker: Matilda
content: I used to think that I didn't need to think too much, that all I needed to do was shoot the targets, but now...

speaker: Matilda
content: I don't know when, but my target has changed, and the person who has been standing behind me and supporting me is now blocking my view of the bull's-eye I want so much to hit.

speaker: Chief
content: And you can't bring yourself to pull the trigger this time around?

speaker: Matilda
content: I wouldn't dare.

speaker: Matilda
content: Forgive me, I'm just too immature.

speaker: Chief
content: I don't think this is a matter of maturity.

speaker: Chief
content: You're just worried, about how that relative who means so much to you will treat you after your bullet hits the bull's-eye.

speaker: Chief
content: You're worried that there will no be turning back once you pull the trigger, right?
Matilda is silent for a long while, then nods with resignation.

speaker: Chief
content: But isn't your true self telling you to aim for this particular bull's-eye?

speaker: Chief
content: "The most important thing is to find your true self when your mistakes lead you astray and locate the path that suits you best."
Doubt is leaving Matilda's eyes.

speaker: Matilda
content: You're right, Chief. I...

speaker: Matilda
content: I get it now. Instead of being timid, I should just pull the trigger first.

speaker: Chief
content: Not my words. That's what Ms. Bernadette taught you, isn't it?

speaker: Matilda
content: You're right.

speaker: Chief
content: You have a great aunt.

speaker: Chief
content: Sensible, wise, patient with her descendants, and willing to guide.

speaker: Chief
content: Among the many Sinners in the MBCC, very few can claim to have a relative half as good as yours.

speaker: Chief
content: Maybe she's just been deceived by the one-sided voices in Eastside?

speaker: Chief
content: Tomorrow, at the hearing, when you go up there to speak the truth about the West District and awe everyone present, I believe she'll understand why you do what you do.

speaker: Chief
content: The people of the West District have changed you. I can't see why they can't change more people. Have faith in Ms. Bernadette.

speaker: Chief
content: If you win over a powerful ally like your aunt, the future of the West District will be even more secure.
Matilda looks out of the window.

speaker: Matilda
content: Perhaps...
Sensing Matilda's reluctance to talk more about her aunt, you drop the subject.

speaker: Chief
content: In any case, don't stress yourself out. Just go do what you want to do and what you should do. I'll support you in the background.
Matilda turns her gaze toward you. The smile she gives you this time is filled with warmth and determination.

speaker: Matilda
content: Mm... I know.
She thinks for a moment, then speaks again:

speaker: Matilda
content: Thank you for taking the time to chat with me about these things.

speaker: Matilda
content: I won't let you guys down.

speaker: Chief
content: You're welcome...
You yawn, feeling sleepy.

speaker: Chief
content: Go to bed as soon as you finish revising the draft. You don't want to speak at the hearing with dark circles under your eyes.
Matilda smiles and nods.

speaker: Matilda
content: Mm, you should get some rest too.

speaker: Black Screen
content: █/█, 7:00 P.M., some venue in Eastside

speaker: Frank
content: You came.

speaker: Frank
content: And Miss Matilda is here too. It's been days; the heroes of the West District look as dazzling as ever.
You see a familiar face the moment you enter the venue.
The man is neatly dressed and full of vitality today, a world away from how he looked a week ago.

speaker: Chief
content: You clean up nice.

speaker: Frank
content: Well, it's a formal occasion after all. I thought I should dress up a bit.
Just then, a middle-aged man enters the venue. When Frank sees the man, he smiles and excuses himself.

speaker: Frank
content: Sorry, I've got some business to attend to. Excuse me.
Frank walks up to the man in long strides and whispers in his ear. As he does so, you notice them looking your way a few times, both wearing a self-pleased expression.
After their brief exchange, the middle-aged man walks over to the front row.

speaker: Chief
content: Do you know that man?

speaker: Matilda
content: Reagan, the current Deputy Speaker, valued by the Speaker for his fund-raising ability.

speaker: Chief
content: Heh, looks like they've decided to drop the act.

speaker: Matilda
content: Well, they have achieved their goal.
More people flood into the venue. You notice a man giving a nod of acknowledgment to Matilda.

speaker: Chief
content: Who is that?

speaker: Matilda
content: Kadis Cavendish, my distant cousin, currently Ms. Bernadette's right-hand man.

speaker: Chief
content: Some cousin. Didn't even come over and say hi...

speaker: Chief
content: So, is he the representative of the Cavendish family at this hearing?

speaker: Matilda
content: Yes.

speaker: Chief
content: Ms. Bernadette is not coming?
As more and more people flood into the venue, some murmurs reach your ears.

speaker: Noise
content: Hey, did you see that? Bernadette is a no-show. Is she admitting defeat to the Speaker?

speaker: Noise
content: What else could it be? Obviously, they're making that poor girl a scapegoat.

speaker: Noise
content: That's a shame. Looks like the old man's re-election is a done deal. I was hoping she would be elected and reshuffle the City Council.

speaker: Noise
content: Look on the bright side. At least this way, the Cavendish family is bound to take a hit. If Councilor Bernadette wants to save her own skin, she'll have to do more than let a girl take the blame.

speaker: Noise
content: You're right. Gotta make her cough up what she's swallowed over the past two years.

speaker: Noise
content: Heh, it's only been a few years since the Abel incident, and Bernadette still has her sights on the Speaker's position... I don't think the Cavendish family will be able to come back from this ever again.
Gradually, you notice, all eyes in the room are being trained on Matilda.
Feigned sympathy, ill-concealed hatred, and more often than not, pure schadenfreude... Some of them even begin to look at Matilda as if evaluating a commodity.
You have no doubt that the former Executive Committee adjutant sitting next to you can also sense those unpleasant stares.
You place your hand on Matilda's shoulder.
The girl turns to you, and the smile she gives you is pure and genuine.
You realize that she's been ready all along.

As an elderly judge walks up to take his place behind the podium, the gazes on Matilda are slowly drawn away. A silence quickly falls over the venue, punctuated only by the clicking of camera flashes and the occasional cough.

You learned about the identity of the judge beforehand from the intelligence department. He is the Speaker's elder brother, who was swiftly promoted to his current position after his predecessor died in an "accident."

speaker: Chief
content: Heh, in the end, neither the Speaker nor Ms. Bernadette showed up. But it seems that the Speaker's side is well-prepared.
The judge cuts short your mockery of him. He clears his throat and turns on the microphone.

speaker: Judge
content: Ahem, the purpose of this hearing is to clarify the events that have occurred in the West District over the past year and discuss the City Council's future plans and actions regarding the region.

speaker: Judge
content: Given that the Executive Committee has failed to achieve the expected goals in its reconstruction work in the West District, it is necessary and obligatory for all government agencies in Eastside to reflect on the overall policy concerning the West District.
The judge's eyes sweep around the venue, and only after confirming that the attention of all the attendees is on him, does he continue:

speaker: Judge
content: I declare, the hearing has now begun.
The judge has hardly put down the microphone when a young politician at the front stands up to speak.
The show begins.

speaker: Young official
content: Greetings, Judge. I'm Mensa, an official of the city's Treasury Department.

speaker: Young official
content: As we all know, the Treasury Department has been under tremendous pressure over the past year to support the City Council's series of measures in the West District.

speaker: Young official
content: Normally, I'd cite data and reports, but I've decided to forego that step, since this hearing is about problem-solving.

speaker: Young official
content: On behalf of my colleagues and the four million taxpayers in Eastside, I would like to ask the City Council the following questions:
The young councilor looks around the room and continues:

speaker: Young official
content: First question: The City Council claims that the Executive Committee was established to replace the ineffective Public Security Bureau. Specifically, it was established following the Keylan Square incident to bring the West District, commonly known as Syndicate, back on track.

speaker: Young official
content: But... In just one short year, billions have gone into the restoration of order in the West District, without anything to show for it. If anything, the entire region seems to have grown more chaotic.

speaker: Young official
content: May I ask what explanation the City Council, the most vigorous facilitator of the establishment of the Executive Committee, would give to the people of DisCity?
This standard line of questioning directed at the Speaker-led City Council, assertive and forceful, can certainly "represent" the voice of the majority of people who care about the future of DisCity.
However, you know that it's just a carefully orchestrated show.
Sure enough, the spokesman for the Speaker, Reagan, makes no move at all. The city official sitting next to him adjusts his glasses and stands up.

speaker: City Official
content: First of all, I would like to make one thing clear to you. The West District is a lawless zone that has long been controlled by illegal violent groups.

speaker: City Official
content: This has always been how the City Council characterizes the West District. It was in the past, it is now, and it seems that it will be for a long time to come.

speaker: City Official
content: The West District was in chaos before the City Council green-lighted the establishment of the Executive Committee. And the causes of the chaos were the incompetence of the local security precinct in the region and the ineffectiveness of the West District Order Management Regulations!

speaker: City Official
content: To deal with the criminals and rioters, we had to use unconventional means...

speaker: Young official
content: Sorry to interrupt.

speaker: Young official
content: Are you saying that the Executive Committee did nothing wrong, and that they should've stepped up their effort by bringing in more chariots and machine guns to... clean up the West District?
The young councilor frowns, seemingly reluctant to utter the words "clean up."

speaker: City Official
content: Your description of the Executive Committee's method is not accurate, but the basic idea is right.

speaker: City Official
content: In the early stages of their execution of the plan, the Executive Committee achieved great results. They eradicated gangs and other illegal organizations, and successfully restored some order to the West District.

speaker: City Official
content: And then serious dereliction of duty occurred within the Executive Committee.

speaker: City Official
content: Some Executive Committee officials lapped up the rhetoric of the so-called "progressives" and attempted to obstruct law enforcement. They advocated establishing "channels of communication" and solving problems in a "peaceful manner" by working with a group of rioters, gangsters, and ruffians.

speaker: City Official
content: That was undoubtedly a betrayal.

speaker: City Official
content: It was these despicable traitors who jeopardized the interests of Eastside; they betrayed the Executive Committee's internal information to a West District organization called Rustfire, which eventually led to the failure of the Executive Committee's operations in the West District.
The remark causes uproar in the crowd.
Some of them may be hearing it for the first time, and their surprise is real, but the vast majority are just acting surprised.

speaker: Young official
content: Sir, that's a very serious allegation you just made there. Is it the official opinion of the City Council?

speaker: City Official
content: Yes, it is.

speaker: City Official
content: What I just said is not unfounded, nor is it an attempt to shift the blame. It is what actually happened in the West District.

speaker: City Official
content: As for the details... Miss Matilda Cavendish, you don't mind providing them for our benefit, right?
Once again, all eyes are on the girl next to you.
Aside from you, everyone in the room seems to bear Matilda ill will, if the looks they give her are anything to go by.
Before you can say anything, Matilda gives you a determined look.

speaker: Judge
content: The prosecution... no, um... Witness Matilda Cavendish, please take the stand.
The sleepy judge on the platform mumbles incoherently. This old man would probably have fallen asleep, you think to yourself, if he hadn't been called upon to continue with his duties.
Matilda stands up and walks over to take the stand.

speaker: Young official
content: Miss Cavendish, please introduce yourself before testifying and swear that you will tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth, and that everything you're going to say is free of any form of coercion.
The young official places emphasis on the word "Cavendish."
Your gaze involuntarily drifts toward the spokesman for the Cavendish family. He is quietly flipping through a file, seemingly unconcerned about Matilda.

speaker: Matilda
content: I, Matilda Cavendish, hereby swear that everything I am going to say at this hearing is free from any form of coercion. It is factual information as I observed it while serving as an adjutant to a frontline Executive Officer of the Executive Committee.
Matilda speaks into the microphone, her voice calm and resolute.

speaker: Young official
content: Then, Miss Cavendish, please enlighten us about what exactly happened in the West District.
Matilda takes a deep breath. Then she speaks in a calm, even voice:

speaker: Matilda
content: The failure of the Executive Committee, from what I saw, had nothing to do with the so-called "internal dereliction of duty," as the city official makes it out to be. And it's utterly absurd to talk about "traitors."

speaker: Matilda
content: The failure of the West District Reconstruction Committee was inevitable. The only explanation is that its action plan was outdated and completely wrong!

speaker: Matilda
content: Chariots and machine guns did not deter the people of the West District; instead, they united them. Rustfire, the most prominent organization in the region, gained unprecedented influence because of this!
The crowd falls silent after Matilda's brief remarks for a moment and then erupts.

speaker: Noise
content: The Cavendish girl is losing it. Is she trying to take her family down with her?!

speaker: Noise
content: How I wish Bernadette was here. I'd die to see her face when she hears this.

speaker: City Official
content: Nonsense! The Executive Committee did eradicate a large number of violent organizations in the West District in the beginning. You cannot deny this!
Among the din of the crowd, the voice of the city official sounds particularly harsh.

speaker: Matilda
content: About the eradication of violent West District organizations... Don't you think the accounts of those who were there carry more weight than the readings of a couple of reports by someone in Eastside?

speaker: Matilda
content: The Minos Bureau of Crisis Control, under the FAC, was deeply involved in the events related to the violent organizations in the West District, and the Chief of the Bureau...

speaker: Matilda
content: ...is here with us.
For some reason, the crowd quiets down.
Matilda looks at you with a determined gaze.

speaker: Judge
content: You're... the Chief of the Minos Bureau of Crisis Control?

speaker: Chief
content: Yes.

speaker: Chief
content: I have something to add regarding Miss Matilda's statement and the doubts I sense from the audience.
The crowd falls silent, their eyes on you.
The judge squints his eyes and, after a moment, gives you permission to speak with a wave of his hand.
You take the microphone, look around, and begin to speak:

speaker: Chief
content: First of all, I would like to clarify one thing to you.

speaker: Chief
content: The Executive Committee had nothing to do with the eradication of violent organizations in the West District.

speaker: Chief
content: The West District was indeed a lawless zone, but only up until last August. And it's not the Executive Committee who put an end to the chaos, but an organization called the Legion.

speaker: Chief
content: After the appearance of the Square Black Ring, almost all major gangs in the West District were wiped out. A new equilibrium was established, and the people of the West District—chief among them the Drifter Camp—were starting to rebuild their homes.

speaker: Chief
content: However, as someone who has always been on the front line, I can responsibly tell you that the arrival of the Executive Committee did help the establishment of this new order tremendously.

speaker: Chief
content: A period of turbulence and friction followed the establishment of the Executive Committee, but it didn't last. The people of the West District reached a consensus: rather than waiting for the Executive Committee to come rolling in, they decided to set aside their differences and joined hands to drive away their common enemy.
You look around the room again and appreciate the miscellaneous reactions registering on their faces.

speaker: Chief
content: Of course, the City Council can choose to up the stakes by pouring more money into the bottomless pit.

speaker: Chief
content: And we'll see how destructive the power of the eight million people of the West District can be when they are forced to unite for a common cause.
Your speech seems to have caused the temperature inside the legislative hall to suddenly drop a few degrees. You can't help but feel pleased by the faces frozen in varying degrees of surprise.
Matilda gives you a small nod, her way of saying thank you to you.
Before the city official can respond, the microphone is snatched from his hand by a grim-faced Reagan.

speaker: Reagan
content: What you just said is alarmist. The City Council has obtained detailed information about Rustfire and has hand-picked a new team of extraordinary talent to address the situation.

speaker: Reagan
content: Once we eliminate this leading violent organization in the next operation, the situation in the West District will be completely reversed! The City Council...

speaker: Matilda
content: Sorry...

speaker: Matilda
content: Are you actually considering an all-out war with the West District?

speaker: Reagan
content: The West District is part of DisCity. This is an indisputable fact!

speaker: Reagan
content: If conflict can't be avoided, then it should be resolved as quickly as possible by force. The City Council will not tolerate any form of separatism in DisCity...

speaker: Matilda
content: Wasn't it the City Council that signed the West District Order Management Regulations and left the eight million people of the West District to fend for themselves?
Reagan is lost for words. He gives Matilda a hostile look.
Giving Reagan no more attention, she scans the room and continues with her speech:

speaker: Matilda
content: Please open your eyes and take a good look at the situation.

speaker: Matilda
content: While the City Council has been obsessed with factional struggles, the West District has undergone a complete transformation.

speaker: Matilda
content: The revival of the West District's mining industry has won them some bargaining chips. Capitalists, progressives, and even the Outlands have smelled the business opportunity and come to the negotiating table, hoping to get a share of the huge profits on the horizon.

speaker: Matilda
content: Even so, the City Council is still bent on suppressing the West District by force and taking the whole cake.

speaker: Matilda
content: Let's set aside for a moment the fact that the City Council's actions in recent years have caused some executive departments, such as the FAC, to drift away...

speaker: Matilda
content: I just want to ask this question: Is the City Council really the highest authority in DisCity?

speaker: Matilda
content: Will Paradeisos sit by and let a war break out between Eastside and the West District?
Complete silence...
Almost everyone in the room is stunned into a stupor by Matilda's speech. It's so quiet that you can hear their heavy breathing.
They've shut down like computers—a thousand of them—when their processing power is not enough to handle the information they've received.
The sound of hands clapping...
Sporadic applause rises from the back rows, where the reporters are.
A reporter stands up and speaks in a loud voice:

speaker: Reporter
content: Miss Cavendish, what do you think is the best course of action given the current circumstances?
Matilda answers the reporter's question without so much as a pause:

speaker: Matilda
content: Cooperation.
Her voice is calm and even, but it carries an undeniable note of determination.

speaker: Matilda
content: Stop hostility, show goodwill. It's as simple as that.

speaker: Matilda
content: Once upon a time, in the darkest days, DisCity, hailed as the last hope for human civilization, was built with the West District as the starting point.

speaker: Matilda
content: This wouldn't have been possible without the contribution of the West District miners.

speaker: Matilda
content: Yet for many years now, the West District has been cut off from the rest of DisCity because of the Mania problem. Is this fair?

speaker: Matilda
content: Is it fair to label the people of the West District as a destabilizing factor? They are sons and daughters of DisCity, just like the rest of us.

speaker: Matilda
content: They have gone through the darkest, most bleak night. Now, they can see the light and have the chance to start anew... As compatriots from across the river, shouldn't we lend them a helping hand?

speaker: Matilda
content: Eastside should make overtures as soon as possible and repair its relationship with the West District, even if it's just for the sake of its own interests.

speaker: Matilda
content: Or we'll be forced to watch the Hypercube from the new mines flowing into the Outlands. How is that going to benefit Eastside in any way?
The progressives in the corner, who have been silent up to this point, seem to have found hope. They whisper to each other frequently, and when they look at Matilda, there is eagerness in their eyes.
The Speaker's faction, on the other hand, falls silent.
After a while, Deputy Speaker Reagan takes the microphone and says in a slow but tyrannical tone of voice:

speaker: Reagan
content: I see, so this is the Cavendish family's stand on the matter?
The discussion veers away from such lofty topics as "Eastside's destiny" and "Eastside's future."
Now it's once again a game of politics, pure and simple.
Just then, Kadis Cavendish, Matilda's distant cousin and the spokesman for the Cavendish family, speaks up in an even voice...

speaker: Kadis
content: Miss Matilda's statement fully represents the position of the Cavendish family...
Silence again...
Reagan's face is wearing a gloomy expression. Kadis continues:

speaker: Kadis
content: Two days ago, an aid convoy from the Cavendish family crossed the Rust, and began negotiations with the West District forces led by Rustfire...

speaker: Kadis
content: Earlier today, we reached a preliminary consensus and agreed to cooperate with each other...

speaker: Kadis
content: One area of cooperation concerns the reopening of the West District mines, which you are most concerned about. The Cavendish family has successfully invested in it, on the condition that we donate materials and heavy equipment needed for the mining process.

speaker: Kadis
content: Of course, although the Cavendish family calls for setting aside differences and establishing cooperation, the above actions were not taken in the name of the City Council and will not affect the City Council's future plans for the West District.

speaker: Kadis
content: So, this is the Cavendish family's position on the matter, and Ms. Bernadette's too.
Dahlia Guide
Then the reporters in the back join in. Very soon, almost everyone in the room, except for Reagan and his followers, is applauding.
At least a third of the attendees, you notice, are trying to contact their families or factions with their terminals, without taking too long a break from their applauding.
