content: I see, but unfortunately, this person isn't a Sinner. There is no Sinner in Eastside.

speaker: Player
content: Not a Sinner... Well, in that case, I'll have to ask Nightingale about this. We'll do a background check first, of course.

speaker: Jane
content: Hahaha...
Jane laughs so hard that tears come out of her eyes.

speaker: Jane
content: You are actually considering it?

speaker: Player
content: The bureau's logistics department could use one or two more staffers. I don't see why not, if it's someone you trust.

speaker: Jane
content: If the chance presents itself, I'll tell this person you're hiring and have them message you.

speaker: Player
content: So what's your colleague's name?

speaker: Jane
content: That's a secret.
With that, Jane gives a wave and sets off in the direction of the Public Security Bureau.
Two grappling hooks are securely attached to the ledge of the roof of the Bank of Eastside building. The leader of the group tugs at the rope to make sure it's in working order.

speaker: Leopard
content: Boss, do we still wait for her?

speaker: Warg
content: It's better if she doesn't come. More money for us.

speaker: Coleman
content: She will come.
With that, he grabs the pulley attached to the rope and quickly descends to the predetermined location. The rest of the group, all heavily armed, follow suit.

With a kick, the glass shatters. Almost at the same moment, the lights go out, accompanied by the impatient rat-a-tat of submachine guns and the screams of the crowd. The <color=#fb9259>Ghosts</color> have stormed into the bank.

speaker: Coleman
content: Listen up, everyone! Hands over your head and squat in the corner. No one is coming to save you. So if you want to live, keep your mouth shut.
The security guard tries to fight back, only to be shot by Coleman in the chest and fall onto the floor.

speaker: Coleman
content: Don't worry. I'm sure the bullet didn't penetrate your bulletproof vest. Cracked a rib or two, maybe. I've given you a chance to take a few days' leave. Ah, I'm so very kind.
The teller at the counter frantically presses the panic button, but it doesn't respond.

speaker: Leopard
content: The bank's main power switch has been turned off. Once the boss finishes the job, we'll split the money. Same as always.

speaker: Warg
content: What's the percentage for each of us this time?

speaker: Leopard
content: Ten percent.

speaker: Warg
content: Ten percent? I don't understand why the boss wants that bratty girl in on this and take a cut.
If two of them were gone, would the rest get more?

speaker: Leopard
content: Of course. Isn't that obvious?

speaker: Warg
content: Wait...
A familiar mask appears behind the two. Before they know what happens, bang, bang...
The lights in the bank blink on, and the alarm goes off.

speaker: Coleman
content: Looks like you've learned a lot.

speaker: Coleman
content: You're finally owning up to your desires, it seems. Fewer people, more money, right?

speaker: Jane
content: Yeah. Never hesitate to shoot. That's what you taught me, remember?

speaker: Coleman
content: Hahaha... Of course I remember. Now this is the way the future leader of the <color=#fb9259>Ghosts</color> is supposed to be!

speaker: Coleman
content: Let's go. We're heading back! There will be bigger banks for us to rob, and larger sums of money to steal in the future.

speaker: Jane
content: I'm not going, Coleman.

speaker: Coleman
content: Sigh... I thought you had sorted yourself out. You've proved me wrong again...
As soon as he finishes speaking, they open fire on each other.
They move deftly in the dim light, dodging behind this iron structure or that to protect themselves from the flying bullets.

Coleman vaults over an obstacle and unleashes several shots in Jane's direction. Jane quickly glides out of the way. The bullets hit the thick vault door, ricochet off it, and one of them grazes Jane's shoulder and draws blood.

Jane is losing. She keeps getting hit, moving backward step by step. Bullets have pierced her left arm and right leg. The excruciating pain makes even the simple act of holding her gun steady difficult for her.
She keeps pulling the trigger, even after she has exhausted the bullets in the magazine and all the spare ones. Her body is trembling uncontrollably.

speaker: Coleman
content: Tsk tsk! What a letdown.
Striding nonchalantly as if he's bored with what's going on, he comes to stand in front of Jane. He knocks the gun out of her hand and points his at her forehead.

speaker: Jane
content: Sigh...
Jane closes her eyes, her body trembling slightly.
Have I failed again? Failed to escape from this demon's clutches.
The expected pain doesn't come. Jane hears a shout coming from afar. The voice sounds familiar...
When you and Hecate storm into the bank, you're greeted by a scene of utter confusion.
The marble pillars are riddled with bullet holes, and the bank documents are scattered everywhere, courtesy of a hand grenade's impact.
You see the frightened civilians trapped in the bank and ask the Sinner who has come with you to protect them.
You walk into the bowels of the building. The strong door to the vault stands half open. A man and a woman are facing off inside. They are wearing masks. You recognize one of them.
Jane is in a dire situation. You quickly call Hecate by radio for help.
Help arrives immediately. A purple laser beam melts the wall and makes its way into the vault.

speaker: Coleman
content: Ah, you were quick.
Nightmare's laser beam hits the masked man but fails to incapacitate him. He quickly retreats, disappearing behind the vault door.

speaker: Jane
content: Stop! Don't go! I'm gonna kill you here and now!

Jane's wounds are nowhere near fatal, but they hinder her mobility greatly. Her hands are trembling so hard that she can't aim properly, yet she grits her teeth, raises her gun, and points it at the fleeing man.
You sense the vibration of the shackles inside of you. It's caused by another powerful source of Mania other than Hecate's.
It's Jane, you realize.
You've always suspected that she is a Sinner, but you couldn't be certain, because you never saw her use her Sinner ability, not even in her battle against the Corruptor.
Who exactly is that person who escaped?

The bank robbers have prepared a perfect escape route beforehand. The remaining members of the group start firing at the sheriffs just outside the main entrance of the bank. You pull Jane along and hide behind the counter.

speaker: Jane
content: You saved me again.

speaker: Player
content: I will...

speaker: Jane
content: Take it from here, again?
She interrupts you, removing her mask.

speaker: Jane
content: No. I'm not letting you. I have to do it myself this time.

speaker: Jane
content: Because of him, I became a Sinner. Because of him, I became a notorious robber.

speaker: Jane
content: He planted the seeds of my sins, and they grew in the soil that was the <color=#fb9259>Ghosts</color>...

speaker: Jane
content: I couldn't do anything back then. But now, now I want to end it with my own hands.
You look at the injured girl in front of you, shaking your head.
With an effort, she leans forward and rests her chin on your shoulder. You can't see her face. Her soft voice whispers in your ear.

speaker: Jane
content: Give me the shackles.

speaker: Jane
content: Please... give me the shackles...
You've never received such a request from a Sinner before. It's a plea.

speaker: Jane
content: I want... to take a gamble...

speaker: Jane
content: All my life, I've let others make tough decisions for me...

speaker: Jane
content: There's no need for you to make any promises or feel responsible for whatever might happen...

speaker: Jane
content: Lend me the power to fight back... That's all I ask of you.

speaker: Sheriff
content: Will you come and participate in other operations in the future?

speaker: Sheriff
content: If you don't, I'll come find you.

speaker: Jane
content: Or you could make me an MBCC Sinner. That way, I can use the power of your shackles.

speaker: Jane
content: Maybe it's because this person thought they could do better and wanted to live a virtuous life.
So obstinate.
That's only to be expected. She is a Sinner, after all.
You hold her hand. The red chain appears and hovers over her body for a second before disappearing again.

speaker: Player
content: This is a Heal Potestas. Not as powerful as the abilities of Catalyst Sinners, but it'll have to do.

speaker: Player
content: Here, take my gun. It still has bullets in it.
You remove your gun and hand it to Jane.

speaker: Jane
content: ...Thank you.
She takes the gun, cocks it, and steps out of the hiding place.
The masked man reappears, his skin now adorned with visible cracks. Hecate wants to attack him again but you stop her.

speaker: Jane
content: Let's have another round, just you and me. No one will interfere.

speaker: Coleman
content: You'd better kill me this time, or...
Their showdown resumes...
Bullets whistle in the air. She dodges out of the way, gets closer to her target, and unleashes a volley of shots. One of the bullets hits and passes through his left arm.
This is the first time he's sustained any significant amount of damage, but he bursts into laughter, his body trembling.

speaker: Coleman
content: Hahaha... great, great! You're finally showing your true colors!

speaker: Coleman
content: Embrace your true self, Jane. Deep down you know you're not a Public Security Bureau sheriff.

speaker: Coleman
content: You're in my camp, always have been. You're not a sheriff, you're a bank robber!

speaker: Coleman
content: We're the most notorious bank robbers in Eastside.
Coleman raises his gun to shoot. Jane dodges while responding to the man's remarks.

speaker: Jane
content: I know I was a bank robber.

speaker: Jane
content: I've lived in fear for too long. I feared the consequences of failure, feared everything I cherished would be destroyed by you.

speaker: Jane
content: It's different now. Now I have the power to fight back. I'm going to end my nightmare today.

speaker: Coleman
content: Hahaha! You're all bark and no bite.

speaker: Coleman
content: I know you well. You don't have the courage to do what you say you're going to do. Staying on the dark side with us and doing evil, that's what you were born to do. And you know how wonderful it makes you feel.

speaker: Coleman
content: I still remember the look on your face when you opened a bank vault for the first time and got your hands on your first stolen sum of money.

speaker: Coleman
content: It wasn't a look of shame or self-reproach, but a look of excitement, indescribable excitement.

speaker: Jane
content: Shut up!
Jane fires continuously at Coleman, but Coleman is still laughing like a madman.

speaker: Coleman
content: Ah, what you've been suppressing isn't your desire to kill, but your power—Criminal Palpitations.

speaker: Coleman
content: You're not fit to be a sheriff at all. I didn't stop you from joining the Public Security Bureau, because I wanted to see how big a fool you would make of yourself...
You sense, via the shackles, that Jane's emotions are in turmoil.
Very few Sinners reveal their identities willingly, especially those in Eastside.
Jane revealed hers, only because she wanted you to put the shackles on her to become more powerful.

options: She must have been a victim of oppression for too long...

content: Believe in yourself. That's what you need to do.
I believe in myself.
I don't care about what other people say, or do.
You're now blessed with the power of the shackles. Go and win the battle.
The shackles blink red and bright. The duel between the two heavily wounded fighters is nearing its end.
There is no bullet left in the magazine of either of their guns. They're locked in a stalemate. Who will emerge victorious?

speaker: Coleman
content: The winner... is me! You have no means of harming me now.

speaker: Coleman
content: You in gray clothes, you said you wouldn't interfere. I'm leaving now. You won't stop me, I reckon?

speaker: Jane
content: I must... do this...
Coleman turns to leave, planning to join his accomplices. Jane musters all her strength and lunges at Coleman.

speaker: Coleman
content: You...

speaker: Coleman
content: Why are you so eager to die? I'll grant your wish then.
Coleman pulls out a dagger and forcefully stabs Jane.

speaker: Coleman
content: What a pity. We're so alike. We're both monsters... I didn't want to kill you.

speaker: Jane
content: But... I... want to kill you!
With blood dripping from her mask, Jane presses the muzzle of her handgun against Coleman's unprotected forehead.

speaker: Coleman
content: You ran out of bullets long ago. Stop fooling yourself.

speaker: Jane
content: I've got one left. The one I should've put in your head three years ago...

speaker: Jane
content: Goodbye, my... nightmare.
Coleman opens his mouth to say something, but the bullet shuts him up. Bang! He falls onto the floor.
The shell casing jumps out of the chamber and lands on the floor.
There's a small line of text written on it.
Dear daughter, forge ahead without fear and overcome any force of evil that stands in your way.
Jane is sitting silently in the interrogation room, as if waiting for a judgment to be delivered on her.
You follow your question with a gesture that says, "Just play along and go through the motions."
Jane averts her gaze, seemingly unwilling to just go through the motions. You indicate the camera and let her know that you're being recorded.

speaker: Player
content: Practically speaking, he would be more useful alive than dead.

speaker: Player
content: We could've pried useful information on the criminal organization out of him...

speaker: Jane
content: He's more useful to me dead.
Jane interrupts you and takes over the conversation. Shaking your head, you decide to indulge her.

speaker: Jane
content: The year the life of my family was turned upside down, my father was still a sheriff.

speaker: Jane
content: He was a kind and upstanding man. He wouldn't tolerate any injustice. This got him into a lot of trouble.

speaker: Jane
content: I admired him greatly. I thought he was the perfect example of a good sheriff. I wanted to become a virtuous sheriff just like him.

speaker: Jane
content: Tragedy struck when he was investigating a case involving Nirvana. Nirvana didn't like the idea of someone looking into their business.

speaker: Jane
content: Mysteriously and suddenly, he was heavily in debt to some loan shark. They broke his arms and legs and locked him up.
Jane gives a bitter laugh and continues.

speaker: Jane
content: Since my father couldn't pay off the debts, they came after my mother and me. We sold everything valuable in our house, but it wasn't enough. I tried many ways to make money, but it was just a drop in the bucket.

speaker: Jane
content: Those debt collectors threatened us on a daily basis. One day, they tried to kidnap my mom and sell her for money.

speaker: Jane
content: I remember that day clearly. It was the first time I'd ever shot someone. Fifteen bullets in the magazine, one for each debt collector. They lay flat on the floor, every one of them.

speaker: Player
content: That was when you became a Sinner?

speaker: Jane
content: Yes. I had to protect my mom. I awakened my power as I was shooting the debt collectors.

speaker: Jane
content: But... it was not a good thing, having this new power. Because of it, I was in constant danger of losing my self-control, and I became hypersensitive to blood, bullets, and crime.

speaker: Jane
content: Every day, I tried my best to control my emotions and mental state, even while I was in the <color=#fb9259>Ghosts</color>.

options: When did you and Coleman first meet?

speaker: Jane
content: Right after I took down those debt collectors.

speaker: Jane
content: He said he liked my new power, and that we were birds of a feather. He took care of those debt collectors, and covered the whole thing up so no one knew their whereabouts.

speaker: Jane
content: He said he would keep my parents safe if I joined the <color=#fb9259>Ghosts</color> and worked for him, which involved robbing banks all around Eastside.

speaker: Jane
content: In fact, he did. Sadly, that also afforded him the leverage to control me.

speaker: Jane
content: The new power was constantly corrupting me. Every time I stormed into a bank, I heard a voice in my head, my own voice.

speaker: Jane
content: It told me to kill everyone in the bank and leave with the money.

speaker: Jane
content: When I put the money in front of Coleman, the voice would say, "You should've kept some. No one would've known."

options: Did you listen to that voice?

speaker: Jane
content: No. Never.

speaker: Jane
content: I wanted out after a few bank jobs. I wanted to stay by my parents' side. Money would be tight, I knew, but I could find normal work and support them with the salary.

speaker: Jane
content: But it was easy to get in, impossible to get out. Coleman would never allow it. Once you joined the <color=#fb9259>Ghosts</color>, he practically owned you.

speaker: Jane
content: He would never let me go. Each of my solo bank jobs brought him millions, tens of millions, of DisCoins. He was hell-bent on turning me into <color=#fb9259>Coleman</color> 2.0.

speaker: Option
options: He was grooming you to become his successor?

speaker: Jane
content: Yes, otherwise... he would've killed me long ago.

speaker: Jane
content: I had so many weaknesses. It would've been so easy for him to kill me. He kept me alive, because I was still useful to him.

speaker: Jane
content: So I worked for him for another year, as a bank robber.

speaker: Jane
content: Before entering a bank, I would repeatedly tell myself, "Don't kill. Don't hurt anyone. Just take the money and leave." To keep my mind from being completely overtaken by my corrupting power, I strove to finish a bank job within two minutes.
Jane sighs and shakes her head.

speaker: Jane
content: Those days were a living hell. On one hand, I was forced to rob banks. On the other, I was scared that my parents might get hurt again.

speaker: Jane
content: Day in day out... I was on the brink of losing my sanity.

speaker: Jane
content: Roughly a year ago, when I was desperate for a break, I told him I needed some time away from him and the organization, and that I wouldn't reveal anything about the Ghosts to anyone.

speaker: Jane
content: He did. In his eyes, I was just one of his puppets.

speaker: Jane
content: He didn't stop me even when I joined the Public Security Bureau. Because he knew he had a myriad of ways to bring me back to the fold.

speaker: Option
options: How did you manage to get into the Public Security Bureau?

speaker: Jane
content: Well... I passed the exam. It wasn't hard.
Jane blinks, as if it's the most ordinary thing.

speaker: Player
content: They must have done a background check on you. They didn't find out you were a bank robber?

speaker: Jane
content: I'd never been caught, nor had anyone ever discovered my identity. So in official records, I was still "daughter of a former sheriff."

speaker: Jane
content: After I joined the Public Security Bureau, for a year, I lived a much simpler life. I carried out my duties as a new sheriff, I did what I was familiar with. And I... did good deeds.

speaker: Jane
content: I wanted to do as many good deeds as possible, catch as many bad guys as possible. I wanted to repay the 37 million DisCoins I'd stolen.
She takes out the note she received from Coleman in the hospital and tears it to shreds.

speaker: Jane
content: I thought I could leave my past behind, but I was wrong. No matter how many good deeds I did, I would always be a robber. The crimes I committed followed me anywhere I went.

speaker: Jane
content: As long as I was alive, I would always be a bank robber.

speaker: Jane
content: As long as Coleman was alive, as long as this madman was still breathing, my nightmare would never end.

speaker: Jane
content: I decided to seek mutual destruction. If I was dead, my debt of 37 million DisCoins would go away, in a way; if he was dead, no one would ever know my past.

speaker: Jane
content: So with your help, I did what I hadn't had the courage to do on the fateful day by shooting him in the head...

speaker: Jane
content: Using the bullet I had kept with me since that day to pierce a head harder than Hypercube.

speaker: Jane
content: Unfortunately, killing the madman didn't bring back what I'd lost. I can never get my old life back.

speaker: Option
options: You might still have a chance.

content: You lift the restraint the shackles are exerting on Jane and place a document in front of her.

In stopping the robbery of the Bank of Eastside, Trainee Sheriff Jane carried out her duties outstandingly and fearlessly. She annihilated the <color=#fb9259>Ghosts</color>, an organization of bank robbers long active in Eastside, and prevented significant economic losses the region might have suffered if not for her valiant actions.
Such actions would merit the granting of the Eastside Sheriff Medal of Excellence under normal circumstances. However, given Sheriff Jane's special identity and alleged association with the <color=#fb9259>Ghosts</color>, and after considering her contributions and mistakes, the Eastside Public Security Bureau has decided not to reward or punish her.
She shall continue her service to the Eastside Public Security as a sheriff, if she so chooses.

speaker: Player
content: This is Eastside's decision.

speaker: Player
content: You have a decision to make yourself. You can go back to Eastside, or you can go home and be with your parents.

speaker: Player
content: You're free to make your own choices now. This is great news for you.
You extend your hand to Jane, who is free to go now. She takes your hand. You try to pull her up.
But she shows no intention of getting up, holding your hand firmly.

speaker: Jane
content: You mean...

speaker: Jane
content: I, a former member of the <color=#fb9259>Ghosts</color>, am being released without charge?

speaker: Jane
content: Just because I killed Coleman?

speaker: Jane
content: I would have nothing against such an arrangement, if I had died in the bank.

speaker: Jane
content: Yes, I did.

speaker: Jane
content: And I will spend the rest of my new life repenting my sins.

speaker: Jane
content: I'll repay the 37 million DisCoins I stole, and rectify the damage caused by my collusion with the <color=#fb9259>Ghosts</color> and my inaction as a member of the Public Security Bureau.

speaker: Jane
content: If I walked out of this interrogation room today without having to suffer the consequences of my past actions, Eastside would likely be plagued with more criminal organizations like the <color=#fb9259>Ghosts</color>, more madmen like Coleman.
Upon seeing how determined Jane is, you decide not to dissuade her.

speaker: Player
content: Eastside has decided not to punish you, but the MBCC still can. I have a proposal here that I'd like you to relay to your sheriff friend.
You clear your throat and present your proposal.

speaker: Player
content: She will become a Sinner under the authority of the MBCC from now on. Does she agree?

speaker: Jane
content: She agrees.

speaker: Player
content: She will follow orders willingly and participate in fights against Corruptors. Does she agree?

speaker: Jane
content: She agrees.

speaker: Player
content: All her income will automatically go to the Bank of Eastside until she's paid the full amount of money due. Does she agree?

speaker: Jane
content: She agrees.

speaker: Player
content: By becoming an MBCC Sinner, she will be forever seen as an outcast in the public eye and will have to endure slanders. Does she accept this?

speaker: Jane
content: She does.

speaker: Player
content: By becoming an MBCC Sinner, she will forever be restrained by the shackles. Does she accept this?

speaker: Jane
content: She does.
However, if she proves herself capable of keeping her power under control and giving up robbing banks, then I will...
You trail off deliberately.

speaker: Jane
content: Then you will what?
Then I will give her considerable freedom. She'll be able to visit her parents whom she hasn't seen for a long time and take some time off to care for them.

speaker: Jane
content: Deal.

speaker: Jane
content: I'm sure she will be very happy to hear this.

speaker: Logistics Worker A
content: The new girl with the helmet, she's a true workaholic.

speaker: Logistics Worker B
content: How so?

speaker: Logistics Worker A
content: She moved that mountain of stuff in the Supply Office into position in two hours.

speaker: Logistics Worker B
content: Really? Those things must have weighed at least a few tons. Is she even human?

speaker: Logistics Worker A
content: Maybe she's not.

speaker: Logistics Worker B
content: What?

speaker: Logistics Worker A
content: I mean, she may be a Sinner, I think.

speaker: Logistics Worker B
content: A Sinner working in the logistics department? Now Sinners are competing with us for low-paying jobs?

speaker: Logistics Worker A
content: Not just logistics. I hear she can do a lot of other things, like paperwork and firearm maintenance.

speaker: Logistics Worker A
content: What's more ridiculous is she also participates in field missions!

speaker: Logistics Worker B
content: Really? She sounds like a real busy bee. I wonder why the bureau hired me.

speaker: Logistics Worker A
content: Well, some people around here are lazy. That fella with the eyepatch in the depot is one example. He's always slacking. Some are even worse, sleeping in broad daylight, and on their feet. Now with this new girl, things kind of balance out.

speaker: Logistics Worker B
content: You have a point...
You stand at the corner where two passageways meet, listening in on the conversation between the two logistics workers.
Ever since Jane, a Sinner who doubles as a logistics worker, joined the bureau, everyone has become much more active.
Despite looking cold and distant on the outside, she is actually very approachable.
You stretch. You're heading to your office to start work when your communication device beeps. It's a message from Jane.

speaker: Reporter
content: Mr. Worthington, there are rumors suggesting that the pharmaceutical factory explosion was directly caused by aging equipment. Can you confirm if this is true?

speaker: Worthington
content: Yes, according to regulations, pharmaceutical facilities must undergo safety inspections every six months. However, they deliberately skipped this procedure to cut costs and brazenly falsified their inspection reports... The official investigation report will be released tonight, where you can find all the specific details.

speaker: Worthington
content: The equipment malfunction destroyed the research facility, resulting in hundreds of casualties. The production lines have completely halted. While the survivors are physically safe, they now face the burden of unemployment... Every aspect of this tragedy weighs heavily on our hearts.

speaker: Worthington
content: But what's done cannot be undone. All we can do now is minimize the negative impact of this accident: rebuild the factory, provide support to the bereaved families, compensate for both financial and emotional damages, and offer assistance to those who have lost their jobs...

The man answering reporters' questions at the podium is Worthington. He's the current Councilor of Shedde, a small town near Eastside. His exceptional handling of the recent pharmaceutical factory explosion and subsequent relief measures have thrust him into the spotlight, earning him widespread acclaim and public approval in Eastside.
Now, with his political career flourishing, it seems only a matter of time before he officially enters Eastside's political arena.

speaker: Journalism Student
content: So what you're saying is, even though this accident wasn't your responsibility and you had no connection to the factory, you've been pushed forward to clean up their mess?
Suddenly, a woman's voice cuts through the applause and admiring murmurs, her deep tone ringing out with startling clarity and bite.
The incessant camera flashes briefly cease as all eyes turn to the source of the voice in the crowd—a young woman with an intern's badge pinned to her chest.
Her baseball cap is pulled low, her entire face obscured by the shadow of its brim.

speaker: Worthington
content: ...I won't shirk my responsibilities. I failed to uncover the factory management's deliberate concealment of safety hazards, which was indeed a dereliction of duty. Moreover, as the Town Councilor, it's only right that I should be the first to step forward when such a tragic accident befalls our town.

speaker: Journalism Student
content: Tsk, Councilor, your words might be too convoluted for everyone to understand. How about I interpret that for you—

speaker: Journalism Student
content: This accident may be a hassle, but it's also a golden opportunity. Just a little "strategic handling," and you'll secure yourself a neat package deal—public approval, a good reputation, and a stepping stone for your political career. You couldn't ask for a more convenient and foolproof investment.

speaker: Journalism Student
content: If I'm not mistaken, your rush to shoulder all responsibility is nothing but a calculated move to pad your political resume and secure your entry into Eastside's political arena, isn't it?

speaker: Worthington
content: Young lady, I think there's been a misunderstanding...
The young woman completely ignores Worthington's words and continues her relentless questioning.

speaker: Journalism Student
content: Moreover, have you actually kept any of your promises? From what I know, numerous compensation payments are still pending, repeatedly delayed. Are you genuinely trying to help those people, or is this all just a publicity show for the media?

speaker: Journalism Student
content: Or perhaps... there's something more sinister behind this accident that you're not telling us?

speaker: Worthington
content: ...This is outrageous! If you're going to make such claims, bring forth concrete evidence! A professional journalist should not be throwing around baseless accusations!

speaker: Journalism Student
content: Hah... Baseless accusations... How dare you bring that up? When it comes to baseless accusations, who could possibly surpass your expertise?

Amid the murmuring crowd, the young woman raises her head slightly, locking eyes with Worthington. As he discerns the face beneath the cap brim, his impeccably maintained friendly smile wavers ever so subtly.

speaker: Worthington
content: It's you...

As the security guards close in, the young woman pulls her cap lower and swiftly ducks, vanishing into the crowd in one fluid motion. She weaves through obstacles with incredible agility, making a break for the auditorium's back exit—only to freeze mid-stride just before reaching freedom.

speaker: Journalism Student
content: Wh-what are you doing here?!
She takes two steps back as a man in a gray trenchcoat emerges into view.
female_content: She takes two steps back as a woman in a gray trenchcoat emerges into view.

content: Finally found you.
Intern reporter? Just how many hats do you wear? Come with me—Sinner Pine.
Pine lounges in the interrogation chair, loudly crunching on a lollipop. Her gaze occasionally flicks towards you before darting away to casually take in the interrogation room's layout.
...Pine, did you catch anything I just said?

speaker: Pine
content: Huh?
She clearly hasn't been listening at all... You let out a quiet sigh, compose your expression, and adopt a sterner tone.
I understand you're eager to conduct your investigation, but as a Sinner, you need to submit a comprehensive exit application with all the required documentation in compliance with regulations.
I won't approve applications without legitimate reasons. No matter how many times you submit applications like this one, the result will remain the same. Do you understand?
Far from showing any sign of compliance, Pine's flippant demeanor only escalates as she lets out a mocking scoff in your direction.

speaker: Pine
content: Are you saying that my reasons for the request aren't legitimate enough? If simply going out to work isn't deemed acceptable, then what exactly meets your criteria for legitimacy?
Do you remember what you wrote in the application? "To gather materials, don't ask questions"? You really think that counts as a legitimate reason?

speaker: Pine
content: What else do you expect me to write? I'm a professional journalism content creator. I never disclose any details about my reports to anyone before they're officially released.
She tilts her chin up slightly, her words brimming with pride and self-importance.

speaker: Pine
content: If I can't even handle basic confidentiality like this, how can I claim to uphold my channel's reputation? How could I possibly expose the schemes and dirty secrets of those crafty politicians?
Over time, you've gotten a good grasp of her channel, the Hedgehog's Eye—instead of delving into investigation and truth-seeking, it appears to focus more on smearing and concocting false narratives.

You've even taken the time to read through several articles on her channel, which are mostly conspiracy theories cobbled together from completely unrelated news stories, gossip, scandals, and hearsay.

While completely lacking in factual evidence, her creative angles and clever writing style are undeniably engaging. It's no wonder her content spread so widely and gained such viral popularity during the election season.
But naturally, to avoid straining your relationship with Pine further, you keep these opinions to yourself—after all, you can see just how much seriousness and pride she takes in it.

speaker: Pine
content: ...Let's not drag this out and find a middle ground, okay? It's just about a standard application, isn't it? I'll draft it now, and you can approve it right away. Time's of the essence here.

speaker: Pine
content: Sigh, you were so decisive during the election season. I'd hoped for something different, but turns out you're just like those suited bureaucrats—all red tape and endless procedures, with none of the efficiency...
You brush aside her vocal complaints about bureau regulations and make a suggestion:

Since you think I'm being inefficient, why don't we try a different approach? The Hedgehog's Eye is a social media account that publishes content online, right? Couldn't you get your work done without leaving the Bureau?

The Bureau has excellent network connectivity—you can easily contact your external sources and have them send materials to you while staying here to write and publish your reports in peace. If you need, I can even arrange a private room for you to work on your content without distraction.
Pine furrows her brow and clicks her tongue in irritation.

speaker: Pine
content: You don't understand. This one's different—it's not something I can piece together just from leads passed along by informants.
Realizing she has divulged more than intended, Pine presses her lips into a thin line, refusing to elaborate further.

speaker: Pine
content: This is none of your business.

speaker: Pine
content: If you really want to know, you'll just have to wait and catch it on the Hedgehog's Eye. What's the fun in knowing about a bombshell before it drops? The true excitement lies in witnessing it explode in real time.
Since Pine clearly won't volunteer the information, you arch an eyebrow and glance at the document beside you before sliding it across to her.
Why don't you take a look? This might be useful for your investigation.
Just as anticipated, Pine's pupils constrict as her eyes fall on the name on the cover, betraying a hint of shock beneath her typically impassive facade.

speaker: Pine
content: You...
Pine's voice pauses as her eyes narrow, a flash of recognition crossing her face. The realization dawns on her—just how much authority you wield as the leader here.

speaker: Pine
content: Hah, of course you know. You've been tracking my movements, and you knew I'd be at that public speech. Nothing gets past you, does it?

speaker: Pine
content: This is exactly why I avoid doing my research and evidence gathering online—because people like you are always watching!
Pine lets out a sneer and shoves the file aside, then leans forward across the table, fixing you with a piercing stare.

speaker: Pine
content: But seriously, if you have enough time to spy on every webpage that Sinners browse, don't you think you're taking this Chief position a bit too leisurely?

This isn't spying. After the dark web incident, Eastside has mandated stricter network monitoring across all districts and departments—especially for MBCC, where information flow is crucial. I need to keep track of Sinners' online activities to prevent any uncontrollable incidents.

speaker: Pine
content: Pfft, what's the difference? It's just the same thing wrapped in prettier words—typical bureaucratic wordplay from people like you.
...Sarcasm won't get you anywhere. If you really want to go outside, you'd better tell me everything about this situation right now. Only then can I help you.
You let out a sigh and take back the document, flipping it open to a particular page in front of her.
In the photo, despite being bathed in the spotlight, this so-called voice of the people appears oddly distant and unreachable.
—I'm not just here to rubber stamp your leave request. Perhaps I could also let you make use of... this authority you so despise, but that I happen to have?
Under your firm gaze, the mockery slowly fades from Pine's face. After a moment of tense silence, she finally relents.

speaker: Pine
content: Last week, the Hedgehog's Eye received a private message from an anonymous sender who claimed they wanted to expose Hale.
She points at the photo printed on the inner page of the document.

speaker: Pine
content: Hale, just another unremarkable rookie serving as Shedde Town's administrative officer. I'd run into him a few times before—he was like a young sapling back then, full of naivety and boundless enthusiasm.

speaker: Pine
content: I've seen too many of his kind. Like clockwork, they show up in front of department buildings, convinced they'll change the world with their abilities, desperate to prove their existence means something grand.

speaker: Pine
content: But when reality and temptation come knocking? With a snap, they just break under their own weight.
Pine claps her hands once, the sharp sound cracking through the air like a branch snapping right before your eyes.
So this... Hale, he fell for reality and temptation?
Going by the records alone, there's nothing remarkable about him. Seems like a well-behaved rookie who keeps his head down.

speaker: Pine
content: Appearances can be deceiving, Chief. According to our anonymous source, this rookie may look like some harmless, bright-eyed idealist, but he's been up to plenty of dirty business behind closed doors!
You furrow your brow.
Even so, what kind of damage could an administrative officer like him do? With such limited influence, there's only so much trouble he could cause, right?

speaker: Pine
content: You're right about that. The accusations in that tip-off are just the usual minor infractions—illegal trades, backroom deals, abuse of power, and so on. Nothing but your run-of-the-mill corruption.

speaker: Pine
content: I get a dozen tips like this every week. Such unremarkable cases aren't worth publishing on the Hedgehog's Eye.
Then what made you interested in him...?
Pine meets your inquiring gaze, barely containing the excitement flickering across her face.

speaker: Pine
content: Because right here—the final accusation states that he orchestrated the pharmaceutical factory explosion in Shedde.
The factory explosion in Shedde? Is that the same incident brought up during that public speech three days ago, where you made a scene? So that's why you showed up there—to investigate?

speaker: Pine
content: Actually, no. I didn't have this tip-off at that time; I was just there to join in the fun. What? Is it really that strange for me to show up at high-profile events and get under the bigwigs' skin?
Pine adjusts her glasses and pulls out a pen from her pocket, placing it between the two of you.

It looks just like any ordinary ballpoint pen, and you might have been fooled too if not for your experience—the tiny red light blinking on the cap would be nearly impossible for most people to notice.

speaker: Pine
content: Funny coincidence though—I received this tip-off just a couple days after you brought me back. Ugh, if only they'd sent it a few days earlier, I could have gathered some useful intel during that public speech. What a waste...

speaker: Pine
content: So now you're my only shot at getting some insider info. You're someone of importance after all—do you know this rookie? Got any dirt on him?
I regret to say I've never crossed paths with him, but—

While doing research, I did come across some opinions about him. When he first took office, he openly opposed numerous political proposals, and even went as far as publicly condemning several high-ranking Eastside officials.
Pine offers a nod.

speaker: Pine
content: That's exactly what makes him an idealistic hothead. His career's been going nowhere, with no one willing to back him—what else would you expect when you burn bridges with the bigwigs right out of the gate?

speaker: Pine
content: And among all of them, his direct superior Worthington had the biggest impact on his career. It wasn't just public backlash—Hale repeatedly reported Worthington's abuse of power to higher authorities behind the scenes, but each time it was dismissed due to "insufficient evidence."

speaker: Pine
content: Despite throwing everything he had at Worthington, Hale couldn't even scratch his reputation. Worse still, Worthington knew about every single move he made.
Pine pauses, her tone resolute and knowing.

speaker: Pine
content: Worthington's a cunning one. He knew that with hotheads like this, corruption works better than suppression—better to have a puppet you can control than an enemy you can't, right?

speaker: Pine
content: He must have shown Hale exactly what power and status could buy him, making sure he got a taste of those perks himself.

speaker: Pine
content: Manipulating public resources, turning a blind eye to smuggling, greenlighting illegal deals... A little maneuvering is all it takes for endless profits to flow effortlessly into their pockets.

speaker: Pine
content: But after seeing all of Worthington's tricks, Hale's appetite only grew bigger. He wasn't content playing the role of obedient subordinate anymore, so he decided to create an opportunity to oust Worthington once and for all.

speaker: Pine
content: You see, this pharmaceutical factory has been the backbone of the town's economy. Even though the accident wasn't Worthington's fault, such a major incident in his jurisdiction could have easily cost him his entire career.
You process Pine's information carefully before speaking slowly.
So, if Worthington got dismissed over this, the position of Town Councilor would be vacant, and Hale could step in?
Pine snaps her fingers approvingly.

speaker: Pine
content: That's right. You've got quite a sharp mind there.

So Hale's original plan was to bring Worthington down. But he never expected Worthington to handle the whole situation so well—not only did he turn the crisis around, he even managed to win public favor and support?
Pine lets out a sigh, appearing somewhat troubled by how the events have unfolded.

speaker: Pine
content: Sigh, usually I love watching these dogs tear each other apart. I was actually excited about Hale taking down Worthington, but blowing up the factory? That's crossing a line.

speaker: Pine
content: And to make matters worse, Worthington managed to turn the crisis around completely. Not only did he keep his job, he's about to get promoted. Who could stomach watching their elaborate scheme end up benefiting their enemy instead?

speaker: Pine
content: So, my top priority now is to keep a close eye on Hale. He must've lost it right now—there's no telling what other crazy things he might try.

speaker: Pine
content: As for Worthington, his glory days won't last long either. Once I'm done with Hale, he's next. I won't let that scumbag get away with anything.
Pine grits her teeth, seething with anger.

speaker: Pine
content: That old bastard is anything but innocent. With all the filthy things he's done... he deserves to die a thousand times.
You notice how Pine's disgust and contempt spike dramatically whenever she mentions Worthington, and you can't help but wonder why.
If we're looking at this objectively, Worthington is also a victim in this "accident," but you seem even more fixated on him than on Hale. Why is that?

speaker: Pine
content: He's the one who dragged Hale into this mess in the first place. You call that being a "victim"?

speaker: Pine
content: ...Never mind, there's no point discussing this now. I need to focus on dealing with the immediate problem.
Pine crosses her arms defensively, displaying reluctance to discuss the matter as she abruptly changes the subject.

speaker: Pine
content: I've told you everything you need to know. Can I go out and investigate now?

speaker: Pine
content: Of course, I'm just being polite. Because whether you agree or not, I'm getting out of here anyway.

speaker: Pine
content: Trust me, I have plenty of ways to make your job difficult. So, for your own peace of mind, I suggest you read the situation and meet me halfway. Let's not make this messier than it needs to be.
You've faced countless challenges as the MBCC Chief and oversee numerous Sinners, yet here you are, being bluntly threatened.
Pine's words leave you with mixed feelings. You want to say more, but her stubborn determination to get her way is giving you a headache.
I'll approve it.

speaker: Pine
content: What?
I'll go with you. You can introduce me as your assistant or whatever role you see fit—I just need to be there. After all, having an extra pair of hands at your disposal never hurts, right?
—Or to put it in Pine's own words, this is just "an excuse wrapped in prettier words." You're insisting on going along to keep an eye on Pine and prevent her from stirring up more trouble.

You've taken Pine into custody, and her charges go far beyond disrupting a public speech. More significantly, she's accused of spreading misinformation during the election period, interfering with the electoral process, and inciting civil unrest.

You've been attempting to apprehend her for some time, but her cunning and cautious nature helped her evade capture each time. It wasn't until this public speech, when someone anonymously tipped you off about Pine's whereabouts, that you were finally able to arrive in time and take her into custody.

As for the identity of this anonymous source, you have a pretty good idea. Pine was on the verge of uncovering something she shouldn't have, and there are plenty of people who want her silenced. This tip was handed to you as a gift, but it can just as easily be interpreted as a warning.

Your detention and supervision of her serve as a form of protection. At least she's safe in your custody—if she'd continued her reckless behavior out there, she might have mysteriously gone missing one day.
Of course, she doesn't need to know any of this.

speaker: Pine
content: You... Seriously, you?

Pine sizes you up, her eyes scanning you critically with unhidden reluctance. After a long moment, she finally waves her hand at you impatiently, as if resigned to making the best of an unwanted situation.

speaker: Pine
content: Fine, fine. You've made a concession, so I'll play along. But don't you dare slow me down, got it?
You shrug, pull out her leave request form from the document folder, check the approval box, and sign your name.
At 7:30 in the morning, you and Pine arrive at the Shedde Town Municipal Office building, a full hour and a half before its official opening time.
At Pine's insistence, you've traded your signature gray coat—"too conspicuous," as she put it—for all-black attire and a dark baseball cap matching hers.

speaker: Pine
content: Tch, why is he here so early? I was planning to plant a bug on him during his morning commute...
Pine glares irritably at the only lit office upstairs. Through the spotless windows, you can see Hale already seated at his desk near the window, starting his day's work.

speaker: Pine
content: Forget about it. Let's set up the surveillance network first.
Pine pulls out a handful of devices from her pocket and jerks her head toward you.

speaker: Pine
content: You, plant these in his conference room, break room, and private office.
You look down and see an array of miniature surveillance equipment—cameras, listening devices, and similar gadgets—spread out in front of you.
How... how do I do this?

speaker: Pine
content: Tsk, what exactly are you good for anyway?

Pine shoots you a look of contempt, draws a launcher from her waist, and loads all the devices into it at once. Skillfully, she ascends a wall, clambers up a tree, and fires—each motion precise and practiced.
Within mere moments, those miniature devices are expertly placed in strategic, covert locations along the exterior walls and windowsills of the office building.
That was incredible... With skills like these, why not become a paparazzo? I bet no one in all of Eastside could dig up dirt better than you.

Despite having heard stories about her capabilities, witnessing these expert moves firsthand leaves you utterly stunned. Your jaw-dropped expression seems to amuse Pine, who responds with a knowing arch of her eyebrow.

speaker: Pine
content: Who says I haven't been one?
Before you can process her words, Pine grabs your wrist and pulls you toward the central garden.

speaker: Pine
content: Come on, let's find a safe spot to monitor the surveillance.
The morning soon slips away, yet the results your surveillance has yielded turn out quite disappointing.

Helping injured field officers with their errands, visiting elderly residents in the community, volunteering at the animal shelter, organizing fundraisers for colleagues in need and receiving commendation banners in return...
Everything about Hale turns out to be these scattered acts of kindness, completely contradicting your initial profile of a desperate madman.

Pine clearly realizes this too. With a bare lollipop stick between her teeth and an increasingly furrowed brow, she keeps her eyes glued to the rapidly scrolling footage on her laptop screen, desperately searching for any crucial evidence to support her theory.
After much hesitation, you finally voice your thoughts in the most diplomatic way possible.
Pine, isn't it possible that Hale is simply an earnest person trying to do good? At least that's what our current evidence suggests, and his colleagues seem to think highly of him, too.
You mentioned he's publicly opposed many proposals from higher-ups, affecting their interests. Could it be that someone's seeking revenge by making an anonymous report to the Hedgehog's Eye?

You know the influence the Hedgehog's Eye carries, and your perspectives are... well, quite unique. Maybe someone's counting on you not investigating personally, using you as a tool to harm an honest young man. That's not impossible, right?

speaker: Pine
content: For the Chief of MBCC to be this naive... I'm starting to worry about the Sinners under your command.
Pine lets out a contemptuous sneer and extends her arm, pointing directly at the office building across the street.

speaker: Pine
content: See that building? All shiny windows and polished surfaces, but beneath them all lies nothing but a pit of mud. Once you step inside, you leave behind stains on your path that can never be scrubbed clean.

speaker: Pine
content: And those who appear the most righteous? They're the truly terrifying ones! They scrub harder than anyone else to clean the mud from their shoes, desperate to keep others from catching the stench of their corruption when they get too close.

speaker: Pine
content: I've seen plenty of pretenders in my time. Their masks always have cracks—just a little pressure and their true faces emerge. But Hale? He's different. I've never seen someone maintain such an airtight mask before.

speaker: Pine
content: Fascinating, isn't it?
Pine slams her laptop shut and clenches her fist, her piercing gaze fixed on the gleaming windows of the building across the street.

speaker: Pine
content: Even if the whistleblower is lying, I still need to see Hale's true face for myself and find out how he maintains such a perfect image!
Since the first interrogation, you've noticed that Pine's fixation on these people is different from those who simply chase clicks and fame.
Why is she so obsessed? What fuels her hatred? What did those in power do to her? What is she truly seeking?
Before you can voice your questions, Pine gathers her belongings and rises from the bench.

speaker: Pine
content: If long-range surveillance doesn't work, then we'll switch to close-quarters tactics.

Equipped with Pine's tool kit and forged IDs, you both change into maintenance uniforms and slip into the building through the service entrance, making your way to the equipment room on the first floor without any resistance.

The reception room, separated from the equipment room by just a wall, is bustling with activity. To your surprise, besides the regular office staff, you spot numerous familiar faces from Eastside who've come for the pharmaceutical factory incident and Worthington, the supposed hero.
But what surprises you even more is Pine herself. Given her usual stubborn independence and perpetually impassive expression, you had long since mentally filed her away as "socially challenged."
You find it hard to believe that this is the same person—now she's gliding through crowds of strangers with a warm smile, effortlessly joining every conversation as if catching up with old friends.
Appearances can be deceiving, indeed...
Lost in thought, you suddenly feel Pine yanking your arm. At the same moment, something collides with your shoulder—
Oh! I'm so sorry. Are you hurt?
A young, familiar face appears before you, wearing an apologetic expression.
I'm fine...
You start to respond instinctively, but Pine moves faster, covering your shoulder and putting distance between you and the man—none other than Hale, your investigation target.

speaker: Pine
content: Sorry, sir. I wasn't able to keep him steady.
female_content: Sorry, sir. I wasn't able to keep her steady.

speaker: Pine
content: ...Oh, please don't worry. My friend just got a bit dizzy from low blood sugar. It happens from time to time—nothing a short rest won't fix.
Pine first gives Hale a polite smile, then takes your arm with warm concern as she speaks.

speaker: Pine
content: Let's get you some rest and something to eat, shall we?
While Pine's words are gentle, her grip is firm as she guides you towards the elevator. Hale gives you both an apologetic nod, still appearing guilty about the minor accident.

speaker: Pine
content: Nice work. Looks like you're good for something, after all.

Only when the elevator doors close does Pine release her grip on you, letting out a deep breath of relief. She pulls out a pair of miniature earpieces from her pocket, putting one on herself before fitting the other to your ear.
You made me bump into him on purpose so you could plant a bug on him?

speaker: Pine
content: That's exactly why I said you're good for something after all.

speaker: Pine
content: No one in the lobby knows anything useful about Hale, but I managed to get his office password. Let's go search his office thoroughly—might find something interesting. Once we're done, we'll take the staff elevator to B1 and slip out...
As Pine speaks, she pulls out a white keycard from her pocket and waves it in front of you with a mischievous grin.

speaker: Pine
content: Oh right, forgot to mention—I "borrowed" this from one of the cleaning staff just now.

The moment you step out of the elevator, your shackles detect Pine activating her special power. She becomes like a shadow melding with its surroundings, effortlessly concealing your presence along with hers.
She pulls you along through the bustling hallways, yet everyone passing by remains oblivious to your unfamiliar faces. Without a single interruption, you make your way straight into Hale's office.

After quietly closing the office door, Pine swiftly surveys the room. Her eyes dart from the decorative paintings on the wall to the hidden panels in the bookshelf and the desk drawers, mentally mapping every possible location where evidence might be concealed.
In one fluid motion, she pulls a black cloth from her toolkit and swings it over the security camera. Then, pointing at you, she lowers her voice.

speaker: Pine
content: Check the desk drawers for files, especially anything marked confidential. I'll handle everything else.

She crouches down by the safe in the corner, producing a thin wire and a stethoscope-like device before skillfully working on the lock. While you sort through the files in the drawers, you can't help but ask a question.
First climbing trees and pickpocketing, now cracking safes... Does everyone in your line of work need to learn such bizarre skills?
With a soft click, the safe door swings open. Pine pulls out a stack of documents, letting out a dismissive snort.

speaker: Pine
content: Hah, only paparazzi would know those tricks. No self-respecting journalist climbs trees.
You can't tell if she's being sarcastic or actually telling the truth.
Wait... were you actually a paparazzo?

speaker: Pine
content: Yeah, but who in their right mind would pick up that crappy job if they didn't have bills to pay... I actually wanted to be a political journalist at first, but things took quite a different turn.

Though Pine speaks casually, her words spark your curiosity. This is the first time she's voluntarily shared anything about her past, and these few sentences offer you a glimpse into who she used to be. You carefully pursue this line of conversation.
So, your interest in politics started pretty early?

speaker: Pine
content: It wasn't really about interest at first. I just wanted to understand certain things.

speaker: Pine
content: Ever since I was a kid, I liked wandering around by myself, exploring every corner of the city. No real purpose to it—just passing time.

speaker: Pine
content: But watching all these people hurrying about their different lives, I couldn't help but wonder—why did they live the way they did? So I started piecing together these fragments, trying to understand how the world really worked.

speaker: Pine
content: Eventually, being a mere observer wasn't enough to satisfy my curiosity. I began creating false identities for myself, infiltrating different social circles to experience their lives firsthand.

speaker: Pine
content: But the deeper I dug, the more nauseating the truth became—the wealthy were duplicitous and scheming, the middle class numb and indifferent, the poor ignorant and malicious...

speaker: Pine
content: These completely different scums, despite their many conflicts, somehow found a way to coexist in society, each carving out their own territory while also keeping each other in line. I wanted to find out who was pulling the strings behind this system, so I set my sights on those at the top.

speaker: Pine
content: They were DisCity's "guiding lights," always radiating brilliance on screen, spouting endless hope—making everyone believe they'd make the world a better place.
As Pine speaks, her words grow slower, and her expression darkens. Her gaze falls to the documents in her hands, fingers unconsciously tightening until the papers crumple beneath her grip.
...Pine, are you alright?
You approach carefully, not wanting to startle her. Keeping your voice low, you wait for her response.
After a long moment, Pine finally snaps out of it. She tosses aside the now-useless documents and manages a self-deprecating smile.

speaker: Pine
content: Back then, I thought that even though most of them were hypocrites peddling false hope to line their own pockets, surely someone would make the world better... Those far-off hopes always seem so enticing, don't they?

Before you can ask anything else, Pine suddenly raises her index finger, shooting you a sharp glance while mouthing "quiet." In one fluid motion, she crouches silently behind the desk and turns up the reception frequency on her headphones.

speaker: Hale
content: The person you mentioned... Yeah, I know what to do... Don't worry... later...

You also catch fragments of the conversation through the headphones. Before you can ask Pine about it, she has already pulled out a portable signal amplifier, expertly adjusting the frequency to capture Hale's call more clearly.
Her brow furrows slightly, her concentration as intent as a surgeon's during a precise operation, completely shutting out all external distractions.

Unfortunately, the building's signal blocking proves too effective—before you can make out the details of the conversation, the call ends with a click, followed by footsteps echoing through the headphones. The crowd noise gradually fades as Hale exits the building.

After confirming through the window that Hale has gotten into a taxi, Pine packs away her equipment and swiftly returns everything in the room to its original place. Her movements flow with the grace of a trained operative—fluid, swift, and precise.

speaker: Pine
content: He left alone. Come on, let's tail him.

The tracker leads you to a dilapidated alley. The ground is muddy, strewn with moss. With its remote location, decrepit infrastructure, and complete lack of surveillance cameras, this seems like the perfect spot for shady dealings.
You follow Pine, carefully picking your way through the treacherous ground deeper into the alley. Soon enough, you hear Hale's familiar voice ahead.

speaker: Hale
content: ...Please, I insist you take this money.
Is he finally showing his true colors? You exchange a glance with Pine before carefully peering around the corner toward the source of the voice.
Contrary to your expectations, the person standing opposite Hale isn't some high-ranking official, wealthy businessman, or fugitive criminal—but a white-haired elderly man with a hunched back.

speaker: Old Man
content: I've already told you, I can't accept this money. How many more times do I have to say it?

speaker: Hale
content: Your son gave his life for Shedde, and the compensation you received doesn't align with what was publicly promised—that in itself was unjust. I hope you can find some peace and at least use this money to move out of this alley.

speaker: Hale
content: Your granddaughter will be starting school soon. Living here without even an air conditioner—it's too much for both you and the child to bear.

Finally, the elderly man silently accepts the money and gestures for Hale to join him for tea inside. Hale gladly accepts, and their figures disappear one after another behind the dark curtain of the doorway.
Pine... should we continue investigating Hale?

speaker: Pine
content: Is that even a question? Of course we continue. One good deed isn't enough to clear him of suspicion.

speaker: Pine
content: Besides, this is clearly all an act—I've seen it too many times... He's probably got cameras hidden somewhere already, ready to capture footage of the "selfless model officer in action" for his own promotion.

Pine's gaze remains fixed on where Hale has disappeared, her stance unyielding, determined to pursue this to the bitter end. In her worldview, it seems impossible for anyone within the circles of power to be genuinely good.
Pine, I'm not trying to convince you that Hale is a good person or anything like that. I just think we could try looking at this from a different angle—

Let's set aside whether Hale is truly a hypocrite or not—his actions are at least bringing some relief to the victims' families. If this anonymous tip-off succeeds, we won't even see these orchestrated acts of kindness anymore.
So wouldn't you say that, compared to Hale, this anonymous informant might be the bigger problem?
Pine narrows her eyes and turns to face you with keen interest.

speaker: Pine
content: Go on.

Let's break down the potential motives of the informant. One: Hale is genuinely corrupt, and the informant is either his victim or someone who couldn't stand by watching his misdeeds. Two: Hale is actually innocent, but he's hurt someone's interests, and the informant is among those affected—in which case, all this evidence is fabricated to frame him.

speaker: Pine
content: To frame him...
Pine mutters to herself, lost in thought.
Based on our firsthand investigation findings, I personally lean toward the second possibility. What do you think?

speaker: Pine
content: Interesting.
Pine gives a slight smile, her eyes showing approval.

speaker: Pine
content: You do have a point there. I didn't expect bringing you along would actually prove useful.
Having reached an understanding with her, you let out a sigh of relief.
In that case, let's head back to MBCC to plan our next move. I'll have our intelligence team trace the source of that message you received...
Before you can finish your sentence, Pine cuts you off.

speaker: Pine
content: No need. We've already got a prime suspect right here who's worth looking into.
You mean... Worthington?
Pine gives a decisive nod.

speaker: Pine
content: We discussed this before—if Worthington were to fall from grace, Hale would benefit the most since he'd be the prime candidate to take over as Shedde's Town Councilor.

speaker: Pine
content: But let's look at it from another angle: now that Worthington's getting promoted, his position will be vacant too. Someone like him would surely want to maintain his grip on Shedde. So among all his subordinates, who would be the last person he'd want as his successor?
...Hale.

speaker: Pine
content: The tip-off clouded my judgment. That's why I made the mistake of viewing Worthington as a passive player in all this... Hah, since when has he ever been passive about anything?
Pine lets out a cold scoff, her voice carrying its usual caustic mockery, but now tinged with barely contained hatred.

speaker: Pine
content: That blood-stained bastard always manages to mask himself with integrity and altruism. After all these years, he's still pulling the same dirty tricks—framing others and climbing the ladder by stepping on everyone in his way...
She jerks her head up, her eyes blazing with a cutting fury, her voice sharp enough to send chills down one's spine.

speaker: Pine
content: Those people he crushed might have thought they were finished. But too bad for him—I'm still here. And I'll make him pay for everything he owes, down to the last debt!

You hesitate, your eyes darting between Pine's stone-cold expression and her clenched fists. Her demeanor seems even sharper than usual, and this obvious emotional surge makes you wonder if there's more to the story.
...Pine, your attitude towards Worthington seems to be more than just your typical disdain for his kind.
You carefully phrase your question while studying her expression, trying to glean more information from her reaction.
Did you know each other before? Is there some history between you two?

speaker: Pine
content: Hah, it goes far beyond just some history.
With a cold laugh, she yanks off the necklace from her neck—beneath the black band lies a faint but unmistakable scar stretching across her throat.

speaker: Pine
content: It's a blood feud.

speaker: Paparazzo A
content: Hey, did you hear? Pine topped the readership rankings again this month! It's so frustrating—she's barely out of college, just some rookie girl, and she's getting these incredible numbers?

speaker: Paparazzo B
content: Don't be so jealous. Like the editor-in-chief says, some people are just cut out for this job. Look, she just secured another hefty hush payment for the company. Our bonuses this month are all thanks to her.

Meanwhile, in a corner of the room, the girl who has been the subject of office gossip slouches wearily in an uncomfortable chair. On her monitor played the day's political news, creating a stark contrast with her work notes sprawled across her desk—a chaotic mess of papers.

Who was having a secret relationship, who was committing fraud, who was splurging at luxury boutiques for their new flame... The pages were filled with notes about vapid celebrities and their even more vapid daily lives.

speaker: Pine
content: It's all just petty, mind-numbing, disgusting nonsense, draining my brain, wasting my time... Why am I even here, churning out trash like some machine...
With a sigh, she buries her face in her hands, utterly dejected.

Across the papers, beyond the celebrity gossip, several connecting lines led to other notes detailing how Eastside's bigwigs lined their pockets with embezzled funds, traded favors for sexual bribes, and lived lives of endless debauchery... Their supposedly noble cause of "leading DisCity towards a better future" was nowhere to be seen from their actions.
Suddenly, the news broadcast was cut off.

speaker: Newscast
content:
Breaking news:

We have received confirmation that the renowned actress Liz was discovered deceased in her residence at 5:45 this afternoon. Police have secured the scene. Preliminary investigation indicates the cause of death as sudden cardiac arrest, with time of death estimated at early this morning.
Please stay tuned for further updates...

speaker: Pine
content: What...? She's dead?

Pine jolted upright, her hands flipping back through her notes until they landed on a particular page where Liz's name stood out. The very same woman now being reported dead had paid Pine's company a substantial sum just days ago to bury a story.

From Liz's name on the page, a striking red line extended outward, linking directly to Vick, the Town Councilor of Shedde who had been making frequent appearances in Eastside lately, rumored to be on the fast track for promotion.

While investigating Liz's private life, Pine stumbled upon her secret relationship with Vick. Just another politician-celebrity liaison—nothing surprising—so Pine had simply saved the footage of their argument from last night to her memory card without giving it much thought.

speaker: Pine
content: A healthy person with a normal lifestyle, no recent acting jobs to stress over—how does someone like that just drop dead from "sudden cardiac arrest"? This was no accident. The person at her house last night had to be...
The newscast had already moved on to international coverage. Even the death of a public figure, it seemed, wasn't worth more than a moment of people's attention.
But Pine's blood was racing as the red line in her notebook seemed to come alive, weaving through her mind and connecting all the scattered pieces of evidence—
She straightened up and started writing with an intense fervor.

speaker: Editor-in-Chief
content: ...What is this garbage? "Rising Political Star's Murky Ties to Deceased Actress"? You might as well openly accuse him of murder! There's no way we can publish this. You have three days to write something new.

speaker: Pine
content: Why?! This is all first-hand evidence from my own investigation, and everything in this article comes from my own leads. How can you just throw it out like this?!

speaker: Editor-in-Chief
content: Evidence? This is nothing but speculation! You're a journalism graduate from a respected college. Don't you realize that reporters must uphold professional integrity and ethical standards? And here you are, throwing around baseless accusations!
As Pine listened to this sanctimonious lecture about journalistic integrity, she could only marvel at the sheer absurdity of it all.

speaker: Pine
content: Now you lecture me about evidence and ethical standards? Where was all this talk about journalistic integrity and objectivity when you had us stalking celebrities and fabricating trashy tabloid stories for clicks?!

speaker: Editor-in-Chief
content: You...! Do you have any idea who you're trying to smear?! Do you know how much influence Vick has right now?! You'll bring us all down with you over a trivial piece of truth!

speaker: Pine
content: Hah, now we get to the truth! You're too scared to challenge someone powerful, so you'd rather bury the story and turn a blind eye. And you expect me to do the same? Keep dreaming!

speaker: Editor-in-Chief
content: I'm not forcing you—this is just how the world works! If you want a normal life, you need to learn when to look the other way. Especially in this industry, what you know isn't always what you see, and what you see isn't always the truth.
Seeing Pine unfazed with her arms crossed, the editor softened his tone. His expression shifted to one of concern, though a veiled threat lurked beneath his words.

speaker: Editor-in-Chief
content: ...Tell you what—I'll pay you a nice sum to write something more... appropriate. Remember, you're just a fresh graduate with an average degree and no connections in this industry. I might be your only shot at staying employed.

speaker: Pine
content: Is this coming from you, or from Vick?

speaker: Pine
content: You took his hush money, and now that I won't play along, you're generously offering me a cut to keep quiet? I'll say it again—keep dreaming.

speaker: Pine
content: I quit.

With those final words hanging in the air, Pine stormed out, slamming the door behind her. She strode down the hallway past her stunned colleagues, pushing through the office's main entrance—all while completely ignoring the editor-in-chief's furious shouts.
A world of possibilities unfolded anew before Pine as she stepped outside, the fresh breeze carrying with it the promise of freedom and the chance to pursue her ideals.
After leaving the news company, Pine divided her time between investigating the actress' death and tracking Vick's every move, determined to uncover evidence of his corrupt dealings.
However, having learned from his past mistakes, Vick had become far more cautious, bringing Pine's investigation to a standstill.
Then, on a stormy night, Pine's email notification chimed—an anonymous message appeared in her inbox with an attachment coming along.

speaker: Pine
content: "The thing you're investigating"... What kind of strange email title is that?
Despite her suspicions, Pine decided to download the file.

10%, 40%, 90%... The moment the download was completed, the file self-extracted, filling the screen with photos of Vick at various underground establishments. Dozens of video files lined the bottom of the window, along with contact information.

Pine arrived at the meeting spot right on time. The cafe is empty save for a single customer—a man sitting by the window, calmly reading his newspaper. After a moment's hesitation, Pine approached him cautiously.

speaker: Pine
content: Are you... the one who contacted me?
Yes, that's right. Miss Pine, pleased to meet you. Please, have a seat. You actually came to meet me... I see I wasn't wrong about you.
The man rose with a smile to shake Pine's hand, then guided her to the seat across from him with practiced courtesy. His every gesture exuded an air of warmth and reliability.

Now then, time is short, so let's cut to the chase—Miss Pine, I know what you've been working on. I greatly admire your efforts, and I wanted to help. That's why I sent you all the evidence in my possession...

speaker: Pine
content: Hold on... Who are you? And how do you know about all this?
Pine cut him off with a frown, and the man responded to her wariness with a slightly apologetic smile.

speaker: Worthington
content: Ah, my apologies. I got ahead of myself—I'm Worthington, an administrative officer in Shedde Town, and I happen to be Vick's subordinate... as well as his student.

speaker: Pine
content: Student?

speaker: Worthington
content: Yes, I've worked under him since graduating college. He taught me that we must act with integrity and live with honor, never yielding to temptation. Only then, he said, could we give our people hope for tomorrow and build a better future.

speaker: Worthington
content: I idolized him and lived by his every word, until one day... I stumbled upon his secret and finally realized he was nothing but a hypocrite who preached virtue while practicing vice.
A wry smile crossed Worthington's face, his voice tinged with bitter resignation.

speaker: Worthington
content: I tried to convince Vick to stop his wrongdoing, but he just mocked me for being naive. From that day on, I lost his trust and found myself pushed aside in every way possible.

speaker: Worthington
content: All these years, he's played his political games and climbed to great heights, while I remain just a minor commissioner with nothing but the scraps of evidence I've managed to gather...

speaker: Pine
content: So you came to me, hoping I'd help expose him? But why now, of all times? I don't even have a platform to publish anymore—I just quit my job, and I'm sure you know that.
Worthington took a deep breath, his gaze fixed on Pine with sincere determination.

speaker: Worthington
content: I admit, it was my own cowardice that kept me from exposing this evidence. But it wasn't until that lady's death that I finally realized—if Vick continues unchecked, more and more innocent people will be dragged into this.

speaker: Worthington
content: Yes, I came to you hoping you would help me with this. I know you've left the news company, and I know why. In fact, that's exactly what motivated me to take the risk of seeking your help.

speaker: Worthington
content: Because you're someone with a true sense of justice. You can't be bribed, you won't yield to threats or temptation, and above all, you won't compromise your own principles.

speaker: Worthington
content: Can you forgive my past cowardice and join me in overcoming this challenge? I believe together we can turn empty promises into real action. Starting now, at the very least!
In that moment, Pine felt her blood surge with renewed passion.

Her heart resonated with his words, and she found herself unable to resist believing in the person before her. Perhaps in this broken and chaotic world, there were still those who stood righteous, persistently bringing hope to everyone.
After their conversation, Pine returned to her apartment and spent three days meticulously compiling Worthington's evidence into a scathing report, each line a damning indictment of Vick's misdeeds.
The moment the article went live, Vick found himself at the center of a firestorm. Despite his vehement denials, the overwhelming public outcry caught the attention of the Public Security Bureau.
When Pine learned that Vick had been taken in for questioning and would soon face sentencing, her heart pounded in her chest, racing with the gravity of the moment.

speaker: Pine
content: Finally... I've finally done it...

The young woman murmured to herself as she collapsed onto her bed. She hadn't properly rested for days, constantly monitoring the article's analytics and public response. Now, at last, she could close her eyes and drift into peaceful dreams.
