speaker: Thalia
content: I don't know what this is.
Ignoring her reaction, you flip deliberately through the pages until you land on the one where the vase lies.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This looks familiar, doesn't it?
Below the image, stark black text on a white background reads: Contraband Item No. ZX37.
Thalia's composure finally fractures. Her breath quickens, turning shallow, and the nervous clearing of her throat betrays her, only making her panic more obvious.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Recently, the Public Security Bureau intercepted a major shipment of Mania-contaminated contraband that poses a serious threat to DisCity's safety.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And one of those illegal items? It just so happens to be displayed right here in your streaming room. That makes you the primary suspect in this smuggling case, which is why you're being questioned now. Does that clear things up for you?

speaker: Thalia
content: You have no evidence to prove I'm directly connected to the smuggling. Holding me like this is against the law.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Miss Ellington, just having a Mania-contaminated item in your possession is enough to warrant an arrest. Right now, you're only under temporary supervision, which is already a lenient approach.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Is that clear enough for you?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Now, are you ready to have a proper conversation with me?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: However, just to be clear: moving forward, anything you say could be used as evidence in legal proceedings, so I strongly recommend being completely truthful.

The interrogation room's atmosphere turns glacial. Thalia's lips press into a thin line, her brow furrowing as her chest heaves. She clearly bristles at your firm stance, yet holds her tongue, defiance simmering beneath the surface.
Ten minutes crawl by before she finally moves, smoothing her hair with deliberate calm. Then, a soft, humorless laugh escapes her.

speaker: Thalia
content: It's getting pretty awkward, isn't it? Oh, come on, no need to look so serious. I'd much rather... talk things over peacefully.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Miss Ellington, you're not in a position to negotiate terms with me.
Thalia looks at you with a bright smile.

speaker: Thalia
content: Of course, I'm completely aware of that. But before you decide, why not hear what I have to share? You're still free to walk away with this little gift from me afterward. Consider it... my way of taking a step back.
Faced with her proposal, you fall silent, offering no further objections. After all, as she pointed out, you have nothing to lose by hearing her out before she states her terms.

speaker: Thalia
content: I like talking with someone as reasonable as you.
Thalia smooths the wrinkles from her coat—creased from sitting too long—and begins to speak, her words deliberate and measured.

speaker: Thalia
content: A few years ago, my family went bankrupt. I couldn't even afford one single apartment room on the outskirts of Eastside. With no other options, I found myself in Syndicate, just trying to survive.

speaker: Thalia
content: Back then, I took any work I could get, if it meant having a place to sleep at night. But most of the time, it was just odd jobs—never steady, never enough. Some days, I wasn't even sure where my next meal would come from.

speaker: Thalia
content: Then, an opportunity came my way: a delivery job with a long-term contract and... unusually high pay.

speaker: Thalia
content: I knew something wasn't right, but at the time, I couldn't afford to hesitate. That money would've meant a real room, with a real bed. Before that? I was sleeping on fast food chairs every night.
Here, Thalia hesitates, her gaze lingering on you with deliberate weight. The unspoken meaning hangs between you, instantly clear.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I understand the realities of working in Syndicate. Sometimes operating in gray areas is just part of the business. You have my word that our investigation is focused only on this case and nothing beyond that.

speaker: Thalia
content: My job was driving a truck twice a week, from somewhere near the Rust to a location in Syndicate. The cargo compartment was always tightly locked.

speaker: Thalia
content: If you know Syndicate, you probably already understand how things work there. Some questions... well, it's better not to ask them. Unless you want trouble.

speaker: Thalia
content: Then, one day, a gang hijacked my truck. And that's when I finally found out what I'd been delivering all that time—

speaker: Thalia
content: Corruptor remains. That's what was inside.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And that was also when you awakened.

speaker: Thalia
content: Yes... I barely made it out of that gunfire alive. That was the moment I knew: I had to get back to Eastside.

speaker: Thalia
content: I don't like to think about my time in Syndicate. Even now, those memories still find their way into my nightmares.

speaker: Thalia
content: But the truth is, I wouldn't be here today if it weren't for the people who looked out for me back then. That's why I still keep in touch with some of them, helping where I can.

speaker: Thalia
content: Nothing illegal, of course. It's just that Syndicans who want to do legitimate business in Eastside often face prejudice, and sometimes they struggle to get things done. So, if I can help out, I do.

speaker: Thalia
content: Last week, an old friend reached out, which rarely happens, asking if he could store some goods at my place.

speaker: Thalia
content: I must admit... anything tied to Syndicate "goods" brings back bad memories. But he seemed truly desperate. He said someone had told him to bring them to Eastside for safekeeping, but he had nowhere to stay.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Didn't it seem off to you? Like maybe he was just looking for someone to pass the problem to?

speaker: Thalia
content: Of course I had my suspicions. But in Syndicate, the payment from a job like that could mean life or death for someone. I know that kind of struggle all too well. Like I just said, if I can help out, I do.

speaker: Thalia
content: A few days later, he came back to tell me the buyer had suddenly... changed their mind.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Changed their mind?

speaker: Thalia
content: Right, the deal was off, just like that. He never got his payment either, so he told me to sell the stuff for whatever I could get, said it was his way of thanking me. That's when I finally opened the package. I'll admit I was curious: what kind of goods could possibly be discarded so carelessly?

speaker: Thalia
content: But when I opened it up... I never imagined I'd find this.
She tilts her chin slightly, her gaze directed toward the vase pictured in the catalog you're holding.

speaker: Thalia
content: This vase—its proper name is the Crystal Silver Lion Vase—was handcrafted by Outland artisans. It was actually exhibited at the Great Expo... not the recent one, but from ages ago. So you see, I'd only ever heard stories about it until now.

speaker: Thalia
content: I have no idea whose hands it's passed through over all these years. All I know is that it was meant to be the star of next week's annual Eastside auction, searching for its new custodian.

speaker: Thalia
content: When I first held it, I could certainly feel the Mania clinging to the vase. But it was simply too exquisite to part with.

speaker: Thalia
content: I thought to myself, "Well, any antique this old is bound to carry some... history with it, isn't it?" So I decided to keep it close. As for what happened afterward... I believe you might know more about that than I do.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Do you know who the sender is?

speaker: Thalia
content: I only know the person who handled the transportation, but even he didn't know who the sender was. Their exchanges were completely anonymous, supposedly to avoid surveillance, or as they say, "to stay clear of the 'cops.'"
You can't help but show a knowing smile upon hearing that familiar term.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What exactly is this so-called "Eastside auction"? And how do you know this piece is connected to it?

speaker: Thalia
content: It's an annual auction, but not the kind open to the public. It's exclusive to Eastside's elite; only celebrities and wealthy individuals the association deems "worthy" receive invitations. Because of that, it doesn't even have a formal name. Among insiders, it's just called "that auction," and everyone understands exactly what it means.

speaker: Thalia
content: The event takes place in a villa that looks completely ordinary from the outside. Most people wouldn't even find the location, and even if they did, without an invitation, no one gets in, not even the MBCC Chief.

speaker: Thalia
content: And honestly, the attendees are all so cautious. When you're dealing with people who have that much wealth, well... let's just say everyone has something to hide. If they caught wind of an investigation, they'd probably postpone everything and relocate in a heartbeat.

You keep waiting for her to pause, expecting her to halt mid-explanation and begin negotiating terms. But as Thalia lays everything out with deliberate patience, it dawns on you: her bargaining chip is never the information itself.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I assume you have a way to get into that auction?
Her gaze remains steady, unreadable. There's no glint of triumph in her eyes, no smug satisfaction of someone who knows they hold all the cards.

speaker: Thalia
content: As one of the invited guests, I happened to see this vase in the auction catalog they sent me ahead of time.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So, this is your bargaining chip.

speaker: Thalia
content: I'm simply offering you a possible option: since this piece is tied to the auction, wouldn't it be best to look into it directly if given the chance?

speaker: Thalia
content: And as it happens... I can indeed get you that opportunity.
Thalia raises her hand, resting it gently beside her face as that mild yet confident smile returns to her lips.

speaker: Thalia
content: If you want to settle this quickly and find the real mastermind, I can bring you in as my assistant. I'll provide cover for your investigation inside, and with my connections, I promise it'll be worth your while.

speaker: Thalia
content: So... what do you think? Will you take me up on my offer?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What's with the sudden cooperation?

speaker: Thalia
content: I do have my personal reasons for attending that auction, you see.

speaker: Thalia
content: And as I mentioned before, I truly believe I'm innocent. The sooner evidence is found, the sooner my name can be cleared. Wouldn't that be better for both of us?
Thalia's voice remains gentle and composed, her tone measured and unhurried, yet beneath its calm surface lingers a subtle, almost hypnotic persuasiveness.
In her livestream, the products could be anything she chooses to recommend. But here, in the interrogation room, the thing she's promoting is her own reputation, and the promise of special treatment.
Yet the more lucrative a deal seems, the steeper the price that must be paid.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: As a major suspect, you currently don't have authorization to leave the Bureau.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So a more reasonable plan would be for me to go in your place.

speaker: Thalia
content: I consider myself quite the celebrity in Eastside. You attending in my place would be pretty unrealistic, don't you think?

speaker: Thalia
content: Besides... I did explain that the auction is important to me for my own reasons.
Seeing your continued hesitation, Thalia lets out a deliberately theatrical sigh.

speaker: Thalia
content: Surely the esteemed Chief can handle one little, unarmed Sinner?

speaker: Thalia
content: If you still have doubts, I'm willing to accept any conditions the MBCC requires: monitoring, or even...

speaker: Thalia
content: Restraints.
Thalia lifts a finger to her chest, tapping it gently as she speaks.

speaker: Thalia
content: Chief, my sincerity couldn't be more genuine.
Given the circumstances, you nod and rise to your feet.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: In one week, I'll accompany you to the auction as your assistant. Until then, you're not allowed to leave the Bureau. During the auction, I'll be monitoring your every move to determine whether you'll be eligible for bail afterward.

speaker: Thalia
content: A wise choice, Chief.

Thalia reaches out, her hand lingering in the space between you. You hesitate, and let the moment pass, leaving her gesture unanswered. She doesn't seem bothered, however, and instead offers you a graceful smile.

speaker: Thalia
content: To a successful partnership.

One Week Later
Auction

speaker: Receptionist
content: Miss Ellington, thank you for joining us this evening. Our records show you've registered with one companion. Would that be this person beside you?

speaker: Thalia
content: Yes, this is my assistant.

speaker: Receptionist
content: Perfect. We'll ensure everything is ready for you both. There's still some time before the auction begins, but in the meantime, you're welcome to explore the exhibition hall, where a selection of tonight's pieces is on display.

speaker: Receptionist
content: When the event is about to start, a member of our team will personally escort you to your seats.
Thalia offers a polite, professional smile before turning on her heel and striding toward the exhibition hall, her pace brisk and purposeful.

With a flick of her fingers, she signals for you to keep up, navigating through the space with practiced ease. She heads straight for the exhibits at the back, her attention already fixed on their details.
You trail behind, your gaze skimming over the displays. None of them match what you're searching for, so your focus drifts instead to the venue itself.
Despite the crowd, the cavernous space swallows sound whole, leaving only the sharp, solitary click of heels against polished floors.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I've attended quite a few elite gatherings in Eastside myself, but I've never been to this place before.

speaker: Thalia
content: The booking process here is incredibly complicated—applications, reviews, and a waiting list of at least six months. Honestly, most people wouldn't bother with all that trouble.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: A six-month wait... Does Eastside really have that many events going on year-round?

speaker: Thalia
content: Oh, it's just to make the place seem more exclusive. You know, "A place even money can't book"—sounds impressive, right? In my line of work, we call this "hunger marketing."

speaker: Thalia
content: But in reality? If the owner considers you valuable enough, you can just give him a call, and he'll personally come pick you up the very next day.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Sounds like you're speaking from experience?

speaker: Thalia
content: Well, this place isn't far from my home. Every year, my father would...
At the mention of her father, Thalia flinches, a sharp, involuntary reaction like biting down on a needle. The words die in her throat. You can't help but look.
She catches your gaze. For a heartbeat, her lips tremble, betraying some unspoken tension, before she sculpts them into that familiar, practiced smile.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Were you and your father not on good terms?

You come to a halt before an Outland oil painting. In the depicted scene, a man clad in a sumptuous robe sits at a table, his plate holding nothing but a single stale crust of black bread. His eyes dart over his shoulder, shadowed with unease, as though he fears unseen watchers.
Beneath the frame, the title reads: "A Nobleman's Meal."
Thalia's fingers brush the edge of the information plaque, her laugh low and humorless.

speaker: Thalia
content: He... There's really not much worth saying about him.

speaker: Thalia
content: My father was the typical spoiled rich kid, never accomplished a thing. As far back as I can remember, his only job was... indulging himself.

speaker: Thalia
content: To him, money just appeared out of thin air. He lent huge sums to so-called relatives and friends, and when he finally asked for it back? They just laughed in his face.
Thalia lets out another cold snort.

speaker: Thalia
content: I remember begging one of my friends for help... but she told me her parents had warned her to stay away from our entire family.

speaker: Thalia
content: That was how I found out he'd already gone to them for money. She said I was just like him back then.

speaker: Thalia
content: I was just like him... just like him...
Her voice drips with bitterness and pain.

speaker: Thalia
content: But... I'm nothing like that man. Just look—

speaker: Thalia
content: Look who's standing here now.
As Thalia speaks, she lifts her chin, her smile bold and unrestrained.

speaker: Thalia
content: I've worked so hard for so long... all for this moment.
You suddenly remember her words back in the interrogation room.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...That's why you have to attend the auction?

speaker: Thalia
content: What? You think that's not a "noble enough" reason?
Catching your expression, Thalia's smile slowly fades.

speaker: Thalia
content: Save the pity. If we're talking holier-than-thou, I used to be way worse than you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No, I just find it hard to believe.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: To just attend this auction, you accepted the Bureau's surveillance, letting me put the shackles on you. You'd rather give up all your personal freedom just to stand here again.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But does a single auction really define someone's status and worth?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And let's be honest, I'm not exactly "elite" either, yet here I am, right beside you. That kind of judgment seems way too arbitrary.

speaker: Thalia
content: ...Are you done talking?

speaker: Thalia
content: You have no idea...
Thalia lowers her voice, forcing out each word through gritted teeth.

speaker: Thalia
content: I was homeless at eighteen, sleeping on the streets, taking humiliation from anyone who felt like kicking me when I was down... So yeah, excuse me if I don't feel bad crawling my way back here. You don't get it. You've never had everything ripped away.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I have no idea, that's true. But Thalia, by standing here, do you really think you've earned back the respect you want?

speaker: Thalia
content: You're my assistant now. Remember to call me Miss Ellington.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Does being addressed that way make you feel any better?
Thalia doesn't respond, only glaring at you. Perhaps it's that so-called noble dignity of hers, restraining her from losing her temper in public. After all, such an outburst would be beneath her.
Oh, Miss Ellington!
An unfamiliar voice breaks the silence between you. You turn toward the sound to see a young man striding toward you, his burgundy satin suit whispering of money.
He extends his hand toward Thalia, his diamond cufflinks glinting like ice under the light.

speaker: Guest A
content: She wanted happiness, and I wanted her to have it without having to feel guilty about leaving me behind. So I erased our shared memories of us arguing, of us hating and hurting each other.

speaker: Thalia
content: Pardon me, you are...?

speaker: Guest A
content: Haha, you probably don't know me. Just call me Charlie. I'm with Madison Electronics Group.
He pulls a business card from his wallet and hands it to Thalia.

speaker: Guest A
content: I've always been a huge fan. Bumping into you here feels like such a lucky break. I couldn't resist coming over to say hello.

speaker: Thalia
content: Oh, I see! Thank you so much for your support.

speaker: Guest A
content: Honestly, it's because your content is exceptional. I rarely have time for streams, but yours? I make an exception. Your recommendations are so refined. It's a breath of fresh air compared to those streamers from the smaller districts.
Thalia's eyebrow twitches imperceptibly, yet her practiced smile never wavers, her silence speaking volumes.

speaker: Guest A
content: Look, let's not even go there... Anyway, I'd be honored to have the chance to connect.
Thalia reads between the lines and retrieves a business card from her purse, offering it in return.

speaker: Thalia
content: Oh, please, no need to be so formal. If anything, the honor is all mine.
Seizing the moment, the nearby guests—who had been watching intently—swarm in, eager to join the conversation and "connect" with her.

speaker: Guest B
content: ...Well then, it's settled, Miss Ellington. I hope fame won't make you forget the little people, haha...

speaker: Thalia
content: Of course not. Look, I've kept your card safe and sound, haven't I?

speaker: Guest C
content: Miss Ellington, would you mind sharing where you got that outfit of yours too?
Thalia basks in her triumph, radiant and self-assured, while you linger silently at her side, the very picture of a devoted assistant.

Yet from the shadows of a nearby corner, you catch a group of strangers staring this way, their hushed whispers threading through the clamor of the crowd. Their muted, somber attire stands in stark contrast to the glittering opulence around Thalia.
Test, test... Ladies and gentlemen...

speaker: Host
content: Greetings, everyone. I'll be your host for today's auction. We're about to begin, so please follow the instructions from our staff and take your seats promptly.

The moment the announcement echoes through the hall, the crowd around you disperses in every direction. You fall into step behind the staff, trailing them into a smaller, dimly lit chamber tucked away from the main hall.

The auction begins without fanfare, its opening acts a parade of mediocrity. Beside you, Thalia's fingers drum an impatient rhythm against her armrest—contempt in every tap—while your own idle tapping mirrors only boredom.
As the auction reaches its midpoint, you finally spot what you came here for.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Just as I thought, many of these pieces are on the contraband catalog, like that pair of porcelain plates.
Hearing your words, Thalia pulls a pen from her handbag and quietly clicks down the clip. Then, she raises a finger to her lips, gesturing for you to stay quiet.
Only when the porcelain collection finds its new owner does she finally break her silence, waving the pen.

speaker: Thalia
content: It might come in handy for your investigation later.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You carry a recording pen with you?

speaker: Thalia
content: When I meet with clients privately, I like to record our conversations.
With Thalia providing cover, you send notifications to the Bureau and FAC, requesting them to dispatch personnel to the venue immediately to investigate both the buyers and sellers here.
Seeing your message go through, Thalia visibly eases. She crosses her legs, sinks into her seat with effortless grace, and flips through the auction catalog, a faint smile playing on her lips.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It's not over yet.

speaker: Thalia
content: But I'm already in the clear.

speaker: Thalia
content: Oh, and if your people show up before the auction ends, don't drag me into it, okay? I don't want to miss the final item.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: There's something good at the end?
Thalia lets out a soft snort.

speaker: Thalia
content: The final item is always the real highlight, and it never appears in the catalog. I guess you could call it a little surprise.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Did you pick up your sales skills from places like this?
Thalia glances up at you with a smile but remains silent.
The auction races toward its conclusion. At last, she sets aside the catalog and straightens in her seat, her attention fixed on the stage.

speaker: Host
content: And now, it's time for the final highlight of today's event.
A staff member wheels in a small cart, its contents hidden beneath a sleek black silk drape.
Even before the reveal, the audience erupts into applause—proof enough, as Thalia said, that being chosen as the grand finale speaks volumes about this item's value.
With a flourish, the host signals the staff member.

speaker: Host
content: Please.

The black cloth slips away, unveiling an emerald hummingbird brooch perched atop a velvet stand. Bathed in the spotlight, the creature's jeweled eyes glint with an almost lifelike intensity, its wings catching the light in a dazzling dance of refracted color—as if, at any moment, it might take flight.
The brilliance of it floods your senses, its radiance undeniable. No wonder this piece is the auction's crown jewel.

speaker: Host
content: This is the last auction item for today: the Emerald Hummingbird Brooch.
You turn to Thalia, a question on your lips, only to freeze. She sits rigid, her usual poise shattered, every trace of warmth drained from her face.
Her gaze is locked onto the brooch, unblinking, her fingers clenched around the armrests with such force that her knuckles stand out like bone against skin.
And immediately, your question is answered.

speaker: Host
content: This exquisite brooch was personally commissioned by the founding patriarch of the Ellington family, crafted by the world's finest master jeweler, for their eyes alone.

speaker: Host
content: It became their crest, a symbol of diligence, prosperity, and legacy... which is why, for generations, it has never left family hands.

speaker: Host
content: ...Though, given the Ellington name... one might call that symbolism... ironic.
At this point, the host lets out a few dry chuckles, and the audience responds with scattered, half-hearted laughter.

speaker: Host
content: Nevertheless, artistry knows no scandal. This remains a masterpiece, untouched by time. A chance like this is truly unrepeatable. Now, let the bidding begin!
The moment he finishes speaking, the crowd erupts into a frenzy. People around you lean forward, scrambling to place their bids.
Then the air shivers. A faint ripple of energy. Your instincts scream at you, and you lunge for Thalia's wrist. But you're too late. Her bidding paddle is already raised.

speaker: Host
content: We have five million from Number 28!
The number she calls out is so absurd that the entire venue falls dead silent.

speaker: Host
content: Five million, going once...
Thalia shakes off your grip, her sleeve slipping from your fingers.

speaker: Thalia
content: My father sold this brooch long ago to settle his debts... but I never found out who bought it...
Her voice trembles, but more unsettling are the waves of Mania rolling off her, growing stronger, wilder.

speaker: Host
content: Five million, going twice...

speaker: Thalia
content: All this time, I've been searching... I've reclaimed everything else, but this... this was the one thing I couldn't find. And the most important one...

speaker: Host
content: Five million, going three times...

speaker: Thalia
content: I won't leave it behind. It belongs with me. No one else has the right to keep it. Go ahead, laugh if you want...
Almost simultaneously...

speaker: Host
content: And... sold!

speaker: Thalia
content: Laugh all you want!
The moment the gavel falls, the Mania fluctuations cease abruptly. Thalia releases a long, shaky breath and sags against the back of her chair, as if the tension has drained from her all at once.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Are you alright?

speaker: Thalia
content: I'm fine. Sorry, that was unbecoming of me.

speaker: Thalia
content: Thank you. Earlier I...
She seems about to say something more, but two figures approach you both.

speaker: Staff Member
content: Miss Thalia? This gentleman represents the seller of the item you've just won. They'd like a word with you, if you're available.
You and Thalia stand up together, and she nods politely to him.

speaker: Thalia
content: Good day.
To your surprise, the man doesn't respond. He just stares, his silence heavy between you. Thalia clears her throat and finally speaks up, her voice tinged with awkwardness.

speaker: Thalia
content: May I ask when the formal transaction process will begin?

speaker: Assistant
content: Our sincerest apologies, but Madam has had a change of heart and will no longer be offering the brooch for sale.

speaker: Thalia
content: What? Are you kidding me?

speaker: Assistant
content: We sincerely apologize for this situation. In accordance with the auction house's policies, we'll honor the breach of contract terms and provide the agreed compensation.
Despite his words, the man doesn't even bother to nod.

speaker: Thalia
content: I'm truly sorry as well, but I just can't accept this solution. Compensation isn't what I'm after; I want that brooch, and nothing else.
Their hostility is unmistakable. You grab Thalia's wrist, pressing down firmly to steady her. She inhales sharply, fingers curling into fists before exhaling through clenched teeth.

speaker: Thalia
content: ...The price isn't a concern, but I won't accept leaving with nothing. Please let the madam know that I'd like to speak with her directly.
Then you catch it: the faintest twitch at the corner of the man's mouth. A ghost of a smile, there and gone.

speaker: Assistant
content: Then let me check with Madam first, if you don't mind.
He turns away, hand pressed to his earpiece as he murmurs something too low to hear. Within seconds, he's facing you again.
—You think that was a bit too fast.

speaker: Assistant
content: Madam has agreed to see you. Right this way, please.
You immediately step forward to follow, but the man's arm blocks your path.

speaker: Assistant
content: Miss Ellington alone will suffice.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...We haven't actually introduced ourselves, have we?
Thalia catches on to the issue as well, and you quickly exchange a glance.

speaker: Thalia
content: I need my assistant with me.

speaker: Assistant
content: In that case, there's nothing to discuss.
Thalia turns to you, her gaze searching for your input. At that same moment, your phone vibrates in your pocket. The operatives have likely arrived.
Unease tightens in your chest, but you know nothing will deter her. Not when the brooch is within reach. With a reluctant nod, you watch as she follows the assistant away.
[Empty Shot]

The VIP room is bathed in low light, its shadows deepened by the faint glow of a few lamps at the door. The guests, clad in dark formalwear, melt seamlessly into the dimness, the occasional flicker of their cigarettes cutting through the gloom like distant fireflies.
Thalia stands beneath the light, hesitating over whether to speak first, when a voice from the past reaches her, one she hasn't heard in years.
Well, well... look who it is. Thalia. Darling, has it really been that long?

speaker: Thalia
content: ...Kara?
Something stirs in the shadows, then the woman called Kara steps forward, her face betraying no surprise as she meets Thalia's gaze.

speaker: Kara
content: What's with the cold shoulder? Don't tell me you've forgotten me already.

speaker: Thalia
content: ...It's been a long time.

speaker: Kara
content: How long has it been since we stood together like this? It really brings back memories.

speaker: Kara
content: Look at you...
As the woman speaks, she inches closer, her hand reaching toward Thalia.
In a flash, Thalia seizes her wrist and locks eyes with her, gaze icy.

speaker: Thalia
content: Don't you think it's a little late to be saying that now?

speaker: Kara
content: Oh, darling, you're not still holding a grudge, are you?

speaker: Thalia
content: How could I ever forget? Kara, we were close friends for over ten years. And in all that time, I only asked you for help once...
[Empty Shot]

speaker: Thalia
content: Kara...? You came for me? I knew it... I knew you would help me!

speaker: Kara
content: Ugh, Thalia, let go of me. And what is that smell?

speaker: Thalia
content: What? I don't... I don't smell anything...

speaker: Kara
content: The smell of Syndicans...

speaker: Thalia
content: Kara, please, just let me come with you! I only need a place to stay for a little while, I swear. Just until I can find a job... I'll work hard and pay you back, every penny! Please...

speaker: Kara
content: Gosh, keep your voice down! You're making a scene, just like your father did when he came begging at our door. It's so embarrassing. My father said we absolutely cannot let your family drag us down like this.

speaker: Thalia
content: Kara...? What are you saying? I thought you... wanted to help me?

speaker: Kara
content: Help you how? I just wanted to see how far you'd fall. Tell me, Thalia, what will you become down in Syndicate?

speaker: Kara
content: And spare me the "hard work" speech. You've become just like those Syndicans—all talk, no results... Honestly, being seen with you is mortifying.

speaker: Thalia
content: Kara, don't say that. I won't... Wait! ...Kara! Kara!
[Empty Shot]
Thalia's lips curl into a bitter smile, her voice sharp as a blade.

speaker: Thalia
content: Looks like you've become exactly what you were always meant to be.

Kara doesn't answer. Her brow furrows, confusion flickering in her eyes. The words sound sardonic, but their meaning slips through her grasp. Whatever Thalia is referring to, it's long buried in the past, forgotten.

speaker: Thalia
content: ...Forget it.

speaker: Thalia
content: I didn't come here just to chat about the past. My brooch... you've been holding onto it all this time?
Kara lets out a soft hum.

speaker: Kara
content: You know, after you left, I started missing you a little. Then I remembered this little brooch tucked away in our cabinet. The one your father pawned off to us.

speaker: Thalia
content: Now that the bid is mine, you can return it to me.

speaker: Kara
content: Oh, but I've changed my mind. I suddenly find this brooch quite charming from every angle. I can't possibly part with it now.

speaker: Thalia
content: Kara! You know exactly how much that means to me...

speaker: Kara
content: Darling, of course I know that. But why would I care?

The VIP room plunges into dead silence. All eyes lock onto the spectacle unfolding before them. They wait—poised on the edge of delight—for the punchline to land, ready to erupt into laughter. And the star of this cruel joke is none other than Thalia Ellington herself.

speaker: Thalia
content: ...How much do you want? Just name your price.

speaker: Kara
content: I know you can afford it now. But money? Everyone has that.
She reaches out and lightly pats Thalia's cheek.

speaker: Kara
content: Has all that fan adoration gone straight to your head? You think just because you can claw back some money, you can buy back your dignity too?

speaker: Kara
content: Honestly, Thalia, how long do you expect to keep this up? Smiling like some desperate salesgirl, peddling your tacky little trinkets to strangers who'll forget you tomorrow?

speaker: Kara
content: Do you think you're still worthy of wearing that brooch? If your grandfather saw what you've turned into, do you think he'd let you disgrace the Ellington name like this?
Kara's tone shifts suddenly, softening into gentle persuasion.

speaker: Kara
content: Thalia... I was too young to help you before. That's why you fell so far.

speaker: Kara
content: But now, I'm offering you a real chance, to reclaim your place, your family's honor...

speaker: Kara
content: To earn back the right to wear this brooch. And when you do? I'll put it in your hands myself.

speaker: Kara
content: So, what do you say?
Her friend's gaze burns with intensity, every word dripping with raw, heartfelt anguish, yet beneath each sentence lurks something colder, sharper. That familiar flicker of manipulation.
Thalia's thoughts blur. The words cling to her, heavy and disorienting. How much of it was real?
Her fingers dig into her own arm, nails pressing hard into her skin.

speaker: Thalia
content: ...What do you want from me?
Kara raises one finger.

speaker: Kara
content: I only need you to do one thing. Something you're best at.
Kara raises her hand with a smile, summoning her assistant to her side.

speaker: Kara
content: I happen to have a rather... delicate collection on my hands. The usual sales channels are... unavailable, so selling them requires a certain finesse.

speaker: Kara
content: But you—our star influencer—could make this vanish with a single livestream. For someone of your caliber, this should be effortless, no?

speaker: Thalia
content: ...Show me your goods first.
The assistant brings a thick catalog to Thalia, flipping through its pages with methodical precision.

A low, creeping unease has been tugging at her since earlier. But now, as she stares at the inventory laid bare before her, that feeling sharpens into something undeniable, solidifying like lead in her chest.
Every item matches. This is the exact same catalog as the Mania-contaminated contraband seized by the FAC, down to the very piece that had once been delivered to her studio.

speaker: Thalia
content: This is... Heh, so from the very beginning, this is all just a trap...
Kara dramatically places her hand over her chest, putting on a wounded expression.

speaker: Kara
content: Darling, now you're just breaking my heart. I've been racking my brain trying to think of how to help you.
Having said that, she immediately slips back into that perfect smile, raising her hand to signal the assistant to put the catalog away.

speaker: Thalia
content: Where did you get these?

speaker: Kara
content: I've been in this business for years. I have my own connections.

speaker: Thalia
content: Do you even realize how dangerous this is? Is it the money? These things could hurt you, everyone around you—

speaker: Kara
content: Oh my, are you worried about me?

speaker: Thalia
content: ...Don't flatter yourself.
The woman shakes her head with a smile.

speaker: Kara
content: The truth is, I only do this for the thrill of it.
As she speaks, the woman takes on a wistful, melancholic expression.

speaker: Kara
content: You've lived the gilded life, Thalia. Endless studies, tedious social circuits, more money than you could ever spend. Everything is handed to you the moment you snap your fingers...

speaker: Kara
content: Except for one thing. That is... anything to do with Mania.

speaker: Kara
content: My only regret is that I'm not a Sinner.

speaker: Kara
content: Alright, back to business. I'll be straight with you: this batch is dirty, and if you're not careful, you'll drown in it. Then again... if you can move it all? Well, that'd prove you're as capable as you claim, wouldn't it?

speaker: Kara
content: Do this, and I'll honor every promise I've made.
The assistant has already prepared the transfer contract, with the donor's name already neatly signed. Only the recipient's line remains blank.
With polished courtesy, he presses the pen into Thalia's hand, his grip firm enough to leave no room for refusal.

speaker: Kara
content: Sign. I don't think you have any reason to refuse.
Her palm grows damp, the pen slipping in her grasp. As she raises it, her wrist jerks involuntarily.
The pen clatters to the floor, spinning away before coming to a stop.

speaker: Kara
content: Pick it up.
Thalia stares at it, her jaw clenched so tightly her chin trembles. After a weighted pause, she steadies herself, then reaches into her purse with shivering hands and withdraws her own pen.
Just as the tip touches paper, the woman seizes her wrist.

speaker: Kara
content: Oh, by the way, don't try anything clever.

speaker: Gang Leader
content: Let's be clear. That brooch of yours? It's contaminated now, too. The moment you report me and they start digging, it'll be confiscated right along with the rest. So if you ever want to see it again... don't try to play games with me. Understood?

speaker: Kara
content: If I can corner you this easily, imagine what else I could do. Ruin isn't even the half of it.

speaker: Kara
content: But why go there? Just help me move these pieces quietly, and we'll call it even.

speaker: Kara
content: Thalia, I mean it. I do want to help you. And I'd love for us to be close again, just like before.
Thalia looks up, her gaze locking onto her former friend with quiet intensity. Then, without warning, she breaks into a wide, dazzling grin.

speaker: Thalia
content: I know. After all, we were best friends.

speaker: Thalia
content: Of course I'll sign it.
With deliberate flourish, she lifts her hand and writes down the name she wears like a crown—Thalia Ellington—before folding her arms against her chest.

speaker: Thalia
content: To a successful partnership.

speaker: Thalia
content: My dear viewers, it's been too long! Did you miss me these past few days?

speaker: Thalia
content: Oh, don't worry, I could never forget about you all! Actually, while I was away, I've been... let's say, curating something very special. And today, I finally get to share it with you!

speaker: Thalia
content: That's right! These stunning pieces behind me? They're not just pretty decorations. Every single one is a genuine antique!

speaker: Thalia
content: I spent so much time researching these pieces to give you all the best experience possible.

It's like stepping into an exclusive exhibition, with Thalia as its most erudite curator. She doesn't just display the craftsmanship; she unveils the historical eras, the stories behind each piece's creation, weaving it all into her expert commentary for the audience.
And Thalia knows this city's pulse. Most of what she showcases are Outland crafts.

speaker: Thalia
content: Take this piece, for instance, a handwoven Fraser carpet, centuries old and still in such pristine condition. The pattern you see here depicts Fraser's most renowned port from over a century ago.
Beyond the stream, social media erupts. Few care about the artifacts themselves; they're too busy dissecting the Outlands, their politics, their very existence.
Piece by piece, the collection unfolds on the table, and the viewer count swells, until Thalia shatters the platform's record.
Then, as the number makes one final leap, she sets down the artifact in her hands, smooths her jacket, and turns to the camera. Her posture remains perfectly straight, as always.

speaker: Thalia
content: However...

speaker: Thalia
content: These collectibles are actually smuggled goods. And not just any smuggled goods, they're contaminated with Mania.
Thalia smiles serenely at the screen and gives slow, deliberate nods. Yet her unshakable composure only pours gasoline on the fire, igniting a fresh storm of furious comments.

speaker: Thalia
content: That's right, that's right. "Disregard for the law," "utterly deranged"—you're all spot on.

speaker: Thalia
content: But here's the real kicker: this batch of goods didn't just magically appear out of thin air.

speaker: Thalia
content: Over the past few days, someone went through a lot of trouble to track me down. They wanted me to help move these goods, all for her profit, of course.

speaker: Thalia
content: And that person is none other than Eastside's most celebrated philanthropist, Kara Henninger.

speaker: Thalia
content: Oh yes, Miss Henninger and I go way back. That's why she came to me for help. But here's the thing: she also threatened me. If I didn't play along? Well... let's just say the consequences wouldn't be pretty.
Thalia picks up the voice recorder—left untouched on the table the entire stream—gives it a quick shake, and presses play.

speaker: Kara
content: If I can corner you this easily, imagine what else I could do. Ruin isn't even the half of it.

speaker: Kara
content: But why go there? Just help me move these pieces quietly, and we'll call it even.

speaker: Thalia
content: If anyone missed it, just let me know in the comments. I don't mind playing it again for you all.

The instant the recording plays, the livestream erupts into chaos. Viewers flood the chat, their frenzied keystrokes sending a tidal wave of comments—so many that the feed seizes, overwhelmed, freezing mid-scroll.

speaker: Thalia
content: By bringing all of this into the light, I've made my stance clear.
Thalia pauses, her next words hanging unspoken. Then, as she breaks the silence, something unreadable flashes in her gaze.

speaker: Thalia
content: I've been streaming for years now, going from a complete nobody to where I am today. And I know exactly what drew most of you to me. The whole "inspirational fallen heiress" story.
Thalia gives a knowing smile, her eyes narrowing slightly.

speaker: Thalia
content: Yes, I'll admit it, it was a marketing angle. But it worked so well that I've used it from day one until now. For so long that... sometimes, I'm not even sure if it's still just an act or if it's become a part of me.

speaker: Thalia
content: But recently, I received a letter from a fan. She lives in Syndicate, just like I once did, and for that exact reason, she watches my stream every day.

speaker: Thalia
content: She has watched me climb back from Syndicate step by step, from an unknown nobody to where I am today.

speaker: Thalia
content: She told me she believes that one day, she can build a better life too, through hard work, honestly and steadily. And she asked me... to never change.
Her gaze pierces through the screen, finding only those who truly listen.

speaker: Thalia
content: I want to protect that dream. So I won't change. Because that's my dream, too.

speaker: Thalia
content: Even if there are consequences, I refuse to betray the people who believe in me. So, Kara Henninger, if you're coming for me, then come.
A thunderous crash interrupts her—the splintering of a door being forced open. Yet Thalia's eyes remain locked on the camera, unflinching.

speaker: Thalia
content: Whatever comes next, I trust that you, my dear viewers, will see the truth for what it is.

speaker: Thalia
content: I am Thalia Ellington. Thank you... for being here with me tonight.
[Empty Shot]
[Empty Shot]
[Empty Shot]
At the same moment, in an opulent Eastside living room somewhere in Eastside, Thalia's face shatters across the wall-mounted display.
The woman before it is deathly pale, her breath ragged, still frozen in the position from hurling the remote at the TV screen.

speaker: Kara
content: Oh, fine... Thalia, this was your choice.

speaker: Kara
content: And once again, you've picked... the wrong path.

speaker: Kara
content: How amusing. How very amusing...
Then, without warning, she erupts into laughter, jagged and unhinged, before gasping as if the sound has hollowed her out.

speaker: Kara
content: Where are they?

speaker: Assistant
content: They've already broken in, searching for where she's hiding—
Before the man can finish, she seizes him by the collar.

speaker: Kara
content: Listen to me, I don't give a damn about the fallout. I want her to pay for this—
Open the door!

content: FAC Public Security Bureau. We have a search and arrest warrant for you. You and your family are now in custody. You are required to cooperate fully with our investigation.
The people in the room are clearly caught off guard. The assistant jerks into motion, fumbling for a weapon, but FAC operatives are already upon them, restraint swift and merciless.

speaker: Officer A
content: All targets are in custody. What's your status?

speaker: Officer B
content: Copy that. We're inside the building and moving toward the target location.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Please keep Miss Thalia safe at all costs.

speaker: Kara
content: Aren't... aren't you Thalia's assistant?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I was then, but not anymore.

speaker: Kara
content: You planned this together...
You offer her a faint smile, a perfect mirror of Thalia's.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Miss Ellington and I just reached a pleasant agreement to collaborate.

Three Days Ago
After the Auction Ended
When Thalia's message finally comes, it's late, well past midnight, with a fine drizzle falling in the air.
The meeting spot she chooses is some distance from the auction house. She offers no explanation, but you suspect she wants to avoid the auction crowds.

By the time you arrive, the villa takes you by surprise. It's the kind of place that belongs to old money, luxurious and grand. Your shoes click against the stone path as you approach, and there she is, waiting at the top of the steps.
Thalia perches on the edge of the staircase, her usual poise softened. The Thalia you know would fret over the way her coat crumples beneath her. But not tonight.
At the sound of your footsteps, she glances up with a smile, pushing damp strands of hair from her face.

speaker: Thalia
content: How's your investigation going?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: FAC operatives searched the venue, but as you predicted, everyone there was extremely cautious. The investigation hasn't made much progress.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: However, as the FAC points out, even if we find the smuggled goods, securing a conviction won't be easy. If the suspects are just ordinary citizens, they can simply claim they had no idea the items were contaminated with Mania.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...What about you? Did you get what you were after?

speaker: Thalia
content: I met the seller of the brooch. Heh, turns out she's an old friend of mine.

speaker: Thalia
content: She used to be my best friend... We were inseparable.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If she were really your best friend... she'd know that brooch was yours.
Thalia lets out a chuckle, not saying anything.

speaker: Thalia
content: She's the mastermind you've been looking for. She has an extensive collection of Mania artifacts, and she wanted me to help move them through my livestreams.
After a moment of silence, Thalia speaks again.

speaker: Thalia
content: I said yes.

speaker: Thalia
content: ...So I could make another deal with you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...What deal?
A soft snicker escapes Thalia's lips.

speaker: Thalia
content: ...You're awfully calm. Shouldn't you be asking what I stand to gain from telling you this?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I thought the deal you proposed before was fair, so I'm open to hearing what you're thinking now.

speaker: Thalia
content: FAC's suspicions aren't wrong. I've seen the contract, and the transferor's name isn't hers. So no, you can't tie those smuggled goods directly to her.

speaker: Thalia
content: I did record her threatening me... but she was careful. Never outright said the items were Mania-contaminated. So that alone isn't enough evidence.

speaker: Thalia
content: But... if I betray her now—when she thinks she's already won—she'll take it as the ultimate humiliation. And she will stop at nothing to destroy me.

speaker: Thalia
content: So tell me, if she does attack me... a threat recording plus assault charges, would that be enough to convict her?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You want to expose her during a livestream.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But if our goal is to catch them in the act, we can't promise immediate protection, and there's always the risk of retaliation. You'd be putting yourself in serious danger.

speaker: Thalia
content: I know. But I'm willing to take that risk.

speaker: Thalia
content: So, what do you say?

speaker: Thalia
content: ...You still don't trust me?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: By telling me this, you've already made your decision, haven't you?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I was just thinking... The thing that matters most to you is right within reach. But instead of holding onto it, you're letting it go and putting yourself at risk, too.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're all about win-win situations, so why are you doing this?
Thalia offers a faint smile and pats the empty space beside her.
As you settle in, something rustles inside your coat. The letter. You've nearly forgotten that a colleague at the Bureau asked you to deliver it to Thalia earlier.

speaker: Thalia
content: This is my family's ancestral home. And you see that swimming pool behind us? That's where my father drowned.

speaker: Thalia
content: The night before, I watched him drink himself into a stupor. I had this awful feeling, like he was about to do something irreversible. But I didn't dare think about what.
Thalia shakes her head gently to herself.

speaker: Thalia
content: I never really knew my mother. And after that day, I didn't have a father, either.

speaker: Thalia
content: Three days later, the bank was set to seize everything. This house, the pool, all of it. But because he killed himself, I had to take his place, working with the bank officials to inventory all our remaining assets.

speaker: Thalia
content: That person stopped at each and every item, asking me to confirm its value. And I had to watch as they wrote down numbers in their little book, packing away my life piece by piece.

speaker: Thalia
content: Funny, though, all I could see was the dining table where we ate together. The mirror where we'd make stupid faces. The swing he built just for me.

speaker: Thalia
content: And the longer I stood there, the angrier I became. I hated him...

speaker: Thalia
content: Why didn't he take me with him?
On the lawn before you, a swing stands silent in the rain.

You try to imagine: Long ago, a girl in a white dress sat there, her face fresh with youth. With a push of her feet, she soared skyward, hair and dress streaming behind her as the world stretched open before her.
Long ago.

speaker: Thalia
content: After that, none of it mattered. They would sit at the bank's auction, waiting for their next owners. And with them, that life I once had would be gone.

speaker: Thalia
content: But I promised myself, quietly, that I'd get it all back. The house, my family, the memories...

speaker: Thalia
content: ...And my pathetic dignity.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You did get it back.
You raise your hand, gesturing toward the swing before you both.
Thalia's lips part—just for a breath—before twisting into a smile edged with quiet bitterness.

speaker: Thalia
content: When I bought this house back... the old swing was already gone. I built this one myself. Tried to match the memory as best I could.

speaker: Thalia
content: I've come so far just to be back here... and yet, in the end, things are just things, aren't they?

speaker: Thalia
content: ...Maybe I've been clinging too hard. I'm... a bit tired.

speaker: Thalia
content: This is...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: My colleague at the Bureau gave me this earlier. It's a fan letter for you.
Thalia smooths the letter open across her knee, its pages illuminated by the dim glow of the porch lamp.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The letter came from Syndicate. Looks like you've inspired quite a few people.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Come to think of it, it's no surprise. From Eastside to Syndicate, then back to Eastside again... this whole time, you only had yourself. And you made it. That's something to be really proud of, don't you think?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: At the very least, I admire you. The person you've always been, through everything.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What you were looking for? You found it a long time ago. Actually, you never lost it in the first place.
You watch her quietly. Raindrops bead on her lashes; when she blinks, they spill, dampening the letter.

The water's touch seems to startle her back to the present. With deliberate care, she folds the letter, tucking it into its envelope. Then she presses it to her chest, as if she could seal the words inside, beneath the steady drum of her heartbeat.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I hope you never lose that, no matter where life takes you. And honestly, I can't wait to see where you'll go from here.
She chuckles softly and nods.

speaker: Thalia
content: I know. I need to let go of the past.

speaker: Thalia
content: After all... I still have such a long road ahead, don't I?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Well then, I'd love to be one of your loyal viewers, always cheering you on.
You offer your hand to Thalia. She meets it with hers, and your fingers weave together beneath the rain.

speaker: Thalia
content: To a successful partnership.
With Thalia's assistance, FAC and MBCC have gathered sufficient evidence, bringing the Mania smuggling case to a successful conclusion.
Thalia has also been cleared of all suspicions, and thanks to her outstanding contribution during the investigation, she is granted bail.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: These are your certification documents. Remember to bring all of them when you come back to the Bureau for your regular check-ins.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And one more thing...

speaker: Thalia
content: I'm listening.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Kara's case is now in the trial phase. When it goes to court, you might need to testify as a witness.
Hearing your words, Thalia pauses, her fingers brushing thoughtfully over her left wrist. Beneath the sleek black leather of her glove, the faint outline of bandages lingers.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You were just recently hurt by her. If you have concerns about seeing her again, I can file a request with the Public Security Bureau to have you classified as a protected witness. Then, you wouldn't need to appear in court.

speaker: Thalia
content: It's fine. I'm not afraid of her...

speaker: Thalia
content: Though, if I'm being honest... maybe I'm a bit shaken in hindsight.

speaker: Luminita
content: You know... sometimes I wonder. If my father hadn't gone bankrupt, if none of it had happened... that could've been me. We were so close back then, it was like... she was me, and I was her.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: No. I think the Miss Ellington I know wouldn't have gone down that path.

speaker: Thalia
content: Oh, come on. Don't you start being all formal with me.
She lifts her chin.

speaker: Thalia
content: Just call me when the time comes. I'll be there.
You give her a nod.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Oh, and about your brooch, even though it was also contaminated, we might be able to remove the contamination and return it to you.

speaker: Thalia
content: If it's too much trouble, then don't worry about it.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'll think of something.

speaker: Thalia
content: Oh, give me that look... Here, let me tell you something else. Actually, by auction standards, that brooch would be considered defective.

speaker: Thalia
content: When I was little, I once sneaked it out to play with and accidentally dropped it. A few of the diamonds chipped right off.

speaker: Thalia
content: I was so scared, frozen stiff, but when my father found out, he told me...

speaker: Thalia
content: "A hummingbird was never meant to be burdened by the weight of gems. It's meant to brave the wind and rain, shedding what holds it back so it can soar freely into the blue sky."

speaker: Thalia
content: He said that was the true meaning of our family crest.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I really like that story.

speaker: Thalia
content: Come to think of it, when I was little, I might've acted like a perfect little angel in public, but I was actually quite the handful at home.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Not that surprising, actually.

speaker: Thalia
content: But he never scolded me.
Thalia's voice drops to a whisper, the words slow and deliberate.

speaker: Thalia
content: Actually... I think I miss him. Just a little.
Her gaze falters, flickering downward, but only for a heartbeat. Then she lifts her chin, brightening as her eyes meet yours again, a smile playing at her lips.

speaker: Thalia
content: Everything else I have to say... I already told you that night.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I see.
Thalia!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Your actual assistant is here to pick you up.

speaker: Thalia
content: Looks like it's time to say goodbye to my stand-in assistant.
Thalia waves at you before turning to walk toward the woman waiting in the distance. But after a few steps, she suddenly whirls around.

speaker: Thalia
content: But if you ever feel like switching things up, you're always welcome to intern with me.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Working for you? I'm not sure I could handle that.

speaker: Thalia
content: Don't worry, I'm actually a pretty chill boss.
You share one last smile, a fleeting wave, and bid each other goodbye—officially this time.
You watch as she walks away, her stride light yet deliberate, the sharp click of her heels against the pavement fading into the city's distant clamor.
Above, the sky stretches endless and blue. DisCity's rains have passed at last, and the forecast promises nothing but sunshine ahead.
She still has such a long road ahead of her.

content: ******* hell. I signed up for the pay, not a coffin. I'm not dying in this ****hole...
The door slams open. On the shelf, labeled bottles tremble and clatter; a few pitch forward and shatter on the floorboards, their last few drops bleeding into the wood.
Forty-nine days into this posting.
She dives for the cabinet against the wall, wrenching the door open. Her hands scramble through the hollow contents: a skeletal sewing kit, gutted cans, a flattened cigarette pack...
Then, her fingers close on a bottle of anesthetic. It, too, is empty.

speaker: Agitated Soldier
content: ...Are you ******* kidding me? Nothing! There's nothing left!
The door opens again. A gaunt man rushes forward and grabs her arm.

speaker: Gaunt Soldier
content: Freyna! Freyna, take a breath!

speaker: Freyna
content: Get off me!

speaker: Freyna
content: Ranor, you and that woman wanna lick Fraser's boots? Fine. But I'll be damned if I rot here with you!

speaker: Ranor
content: And go where? You saw the scouts. It's a death sentence out there!

speaker: Freyna
content: I'd rather take my chances than starve waiting on a miracle!

Ranor draws breath to argue, and freezes at the sound of footsteps in the doorway. He knows without turning. He stands, hands pressed flat to his sides, posture rigid. Beside him, Freyna only rummages faster.
A woman pauses on the threshold, her gaze a winter chill over the shattered mess. Then she moves, crossing the room in swift strides to clamp a hand around Freyna's wrist.
The grip is vice-tight, draining the color from Freyna's skin. Slowly, Freyna raises her eyes, giving a look of simmering contempt.

speaker: Freyna
content: —But I guess our dear Captain doesn't get that.

speaker: Captain
content: We follow orders. That is the job.

speaker: Freyna
content: Save that ******* lecture for the graves!

Freyna wrenches her wrist free. From the cabinet, she snatches the ragged remains of a combat jacket and hurls it between them. The fabric is stiff, the bloodstains dried to a cracked black. The name once stitched across the chest is now illegible.

speaker: Captain
content: He... died with honor.

speaker: Freyna
content: ******* bullshit! Anyone with eyes can see it! We've been left to die! If reinforcements were coming, they'd be here a month ago! If you'd just given the order to fall back—

speaker: Captain
content: Enough! There are no cowards under my command. Look at your insignia. Remember why we stand here! We fight... for Fraser's future.

speaker: Captain
content: This is the battle that matters. Let me be clear: in my unit, there are soldiers. Not deserters. Anyone who tries to leave...

speaker: Captain
content: ...will be dealt with as the law allows.
Freyna holds the woman's gaze, unblinking. Her jaw is a locked vise, her silence louder than any shout. Ranor cannot bear it; he turns his face away.

speaker: Captain
content: The Senate's strategy is beyond our sight. Their promise will be honored. No matter what, we will hold—

speaker: Helga
content: <color=#fb9259>Alsa Highlands</color>. That's where we're headed.

"Ten o'clock, roughly five kilometers out." She makes it sound so simple. But you lack her preternatural vision. Squinting through the binoculars, you sweep the horizon—once, twice, again—finding only an endless, rippling expanse of gray-yellow rock.
Finally, you lower the lenses, defeated.

Behind you on the farland watchtower platform, Helga is already on to more tangible work. She's tilted back in her seat, foot braced against her toolbox, carefully tinkering a music box brought to her by one of the settlement's children.

speaker: Helga
content: Place like that has always been a magnet for a fight. In my day, the old Fraser hands used to say that heading to Alsa meant you'd already dug half your own grave.

speaker: Helga
content: A damn mass grave like that, plus all the Mania weapons they used... Yeah, Alsa's been Corruptor territory for years now.
A soft click echoes in the quiet. Helga gives the toy a gentle, content shake, then glances up. Your gazes finally meet.
She catches your bewildered expression and lets out a low chuckle. Pushing herself to her feet, she rests a hand on your shoulder and points a decisive finger toward the far horizon.

speaker: Helga
content: Follow my finger... Ease left a little... more... There. See it now, kid?

Following the farlands' declaration of independence, Fraser extended surface-level recognition while simultaneously imposing an undeclared blockade through various covert measures.

This ensured that, despite Farland Researcher Hypatia's capacity to locate Hypercube deposits, critical supplies remained inaccessible, threatening the farlands with catastrophic famine.

Hope emerged when farland scouts identified an unpatrolled route circumventing Fraser's primary checkpoints, almost as if Fraser had deliberately left it open.

Its neglect was no accident. The path traversed the <color=#fb9259>Alsa Highlands</color>, a region notoriously saturated with Corruptors.

Clearing a Corruptor zone of this scale was beyond the farlands' capabilities, but for a seasoned Bureau Chief like you, it was routine. Armed with proper equipment and experience, the task required minimal support.

That is why, one week ago, Helga showed up at your door alone.

Having spent years building a formidable farland underground network in Fraser, she now stood as the first Speaker of the Farland Assembly, here to formally request your aid.

You agreed to assist in a personal capacity, as official diplomatic channels between DisCity and the farlands did not yet exist. With Helga personally vouching for your safety, you've brought enough purification devices to cleanse the highlands. All that remains is to trigger them at the right moment.

speaker: Deep Female Voice
content: Speaker, we've arrived.
You and Helga turn to see three silhouettes framed in the watchtower doorway.
Helga swiftly seals the music box inside her toolbox before stepping forward, deliberately placing herself in front of you. With an open-armed gesture, she begins the introductions.

speaker: Helga
content: This is Tavera. Finest spear in all the settlements. She'll be watching our backs on this run.
The tall woman at the center plants her spear on the ground. Then, inclining her head and shoulders, she offers you a slight bow.

speaker: Helga
content: This one's Milonn. His people live around these parts. No one knows the path to Alsa like he does.
A short, scrawny man gives you a nervous nod, his whole frame seeming to shiver with the motion.

speaker: Helga
content: And this is Vester. Sent by the Assembly. Specifically to...

speaker: Helga
content: ...keep an eye on me for this mission.
The remaining man, lean and wiry, fixes his gaze on you, his face twisting into a forced smile.

speaker: Vester
content: Then you must be—

speaker: Helga
content: This is ${PlayerName}. Our Mania expert.
The success of this mission will determine the very survival of the farlands. That is why each major settlement has sent a representative to support the operation.
But old wounds bleed fresh. The war may be over on paper, yet the chasm between the farlands and DisCity runs as deep as ever.
Consider Tavera: Helga describes her as courageous and unshakably loyal—a loyalty that manifests as a pure, venomous hatred for anything Disian.
You cannot reveal you are from DisCity. So while your role on the team remains that of a Mania expert, you are not the Chief of MBCC. Instead, you are—

speaker: Helga
content: Also my grandson.
female_content: Also my granddaughter.

content: Helga beams at you with a grandmotherly warmth so genuine, you could almost believe you were family.
...Granny.

speaker: Vester
content: This is the first I've heard of you having a grandson, Speaker.
female_content: This is the first I've heard of you having a granddaughter, Speaker.

content: Helga releases a booming laugh and sweeps you into a tight, engulfing hug.

speaker: Helga
content: Every kid in our camp is one of mine.

speaker: Vester
content: Your camp had a Mania expert all this time? Funny how you've never mentioned such a valuable asset before.
Vester presses you, but you hold your ground. You came ready for this, and your rehearsed reply comes with practiced ease.
I got captured by a DisCity unit once, one that handled Mania. A blessing in disguise, I guess. Picked up a thing or two just by listening.
At your words, Milonn flinches. He has been trembling since he entered, and now the last of the color drains from his face, leaving him deathly pale.

speaker: Milonn
content: And you call yourself an expert?! <size=30>Y-you're joking, right...?</size>

speaker: Tavera
content: "A thing or two" isn't good enough. Speaker, can this ki— can this expert really handle it?
Every eye locks onto you at once.

The mission itself is simple by your assessment. But you're playing the part of a naive farlander with only surface-level knowledge, so you pause, consider your options, and then adopt your most guileless expression.
Guess we'll find out soon enough, won't we?
Milonn's face goes even paler.

speaker: Helga
content: Relax. I trust him.
female_content: Relax. I trust her.

content: Helga's arm wraps around your shoulders, giving a firm squeeze. Along with the solid weight comes a peculiar scent from her jacket—the sharp tang of machine oil mingled with the earthy warmth of leftover stew.

speaker: Hyenas
content: Woo—! Woo-ooop! Wooop!
You and Helga peer down from the tower. Below, the hyena pack guarding the post has clustered, their eerie cries rising in a chorus.
Flanked by the animals, a massive, hunched figure is shuffling toward the outpost gate.
Helga snatches her toolbox and is already rushing down the stairs, the weight on your shoulders vanishing with her. You bolt after her, and after a moment of hesitation, the other three follow.
[Downstairs]

A deafening bang echoes as the door downstairs bursts open. You can finally see the figure clearly: a dazed young man staggering under the weight of a body, slick with blood, slumped across his shoulders. The blood falls in a grim, steady rhythm onto the floorboards.

speaker: Panicked Young Man
content: Granny... Granny! It's Vigne... He's not gonna make it...!

speaker: Helga
content: When the hell did you two sneak out?!

speaker: Panicked Young Man
content: We didn't go far! ...We saw the food running low, and the next shipment's days off, so we thought we'd try to hunt something, and then... and then...
He can't utter another word. His body sags, then collapses. Kneeling there, he covers his mouth, a muffled, wrenching noise escaping him—the sound of grief and sickness warring in his throat.

speaker: Helga
content: ${PlayerName}, Tavera, push the tables together. Milonn, grab that canvas off the wall.

speaker: Helga
content: ...Milonn? Milonn?!
On the floor, Milonn is a portrait of panic, mumbling and scuttling backward like a crab.
Seeing this, Vester clicks his tongue in irritation. He strides to the wall, yanks down the nailed canvas, and lets it snap open. Together, you and Tavera heave the wounded man onto the rough cloth.
The injuries are brutal: gouges so deep they glint with bone, the signature work of Corruptors. Miraculously, the skin shows no sickly bloom of Mania.
You remember your duty, fetching the Bureau-issued medicine from your kit and carefully administering the dose to his lips. It's a stopgap, not a cure, but it will prevent further Mania infection.
All the while, you sense the weight of Vester's sidelong gaze.

speaker: Vester
content: That medicine... looks like quality stuff.
He wants to say more, but the harsh rip of tearing gauze silences him. Helga shoulders Vester aside without a glance, clamping the bandages against the ravaged flesh with immediate pressure.
Blood blooms through the cloth, dyeing her hands red, yet her motions remain steady and precise. Gradually, the wounded man's agonized sounds fade into ragged breaths.
Finished, she finally looks down. Her eyes settle on the other youth, who remains curled on the floor, still weeping.

speaker: Helga
content: There, there... It's not your fault.

Her hand instinctively lifts to offer a pat of comfort, but she halts, seeing the dark blood caked in the lines of her palm. A beat passes. She simply wipes her hands clean on her trousers and releases a quiet, weary sigh.
The thud of a spear butt against the floor breaks the silence. Tavera stands rigid, staring at the bloodstains on the ground, her jaw clenched with fury.

speaker: Tavera
content: Damn them...! Those cursed monsters... and those Fraser bastards!

speaker: Helga
content: Looks like Corruptors are already prowling near the outpost. We can't waste any more time. We need to clear out Alsa now.

speaker: Milonn
content: N-no... I only agreed to guide! This is suicide! I'm not going... <size=45>I won't do it!</size>

speaker: Tavera
content: You spineless worm! You disgrace every farlander alive...!

speaker: Helga
content: ...If he doesn't want to go, let him stay.

speaker: Milonn
content: R-really...? Then I'm staying!

speaker: Helga
content: Vester, what about you? ...What's with the shifty eyes? Spit it out.

speaker: Vester
content: I haven't decided yet.
He shrugs, feigning innocence.

speaker: Vester
content: Going or staying, both look like bad moves right now. I'd rather not gamble my neck.
Helga's lips twist into a scornful smirk, and she lets out a cold scoff.

speaker: Helga
content: You just don't want to be the one left holding the bag, do you?
Finally, Helga turns to you.

Your gaze sweeps over the farlanders before you—faces etched with anger, anxiety, and at least one with a hostility you don't understand. You then look at Milonn, huddled and shivering against the wall.
It's clear: you can't place your faith in them.
I don't think we're ready yet. Maybe we should wait a little longer.
Vester lets out a whistle at your words.
Helga holds your gaze, silent, waiting for more until the silence stretches taut.
Only then does she lower her eyes to the dried blood on the floor. She shakes her head, slowly, deliberately.

speaker: Helga
content: ...We can't wait. This is our last chance. Several camps have only a few weeks' worth of rations left.

speaker: Helga
content: If we keep dragging our feet, the Corruptors won't need to lift a finger. We'll starve ourselves to death.
After a heavy moment of quiet, she comes to you, reaches up, and gives your shoulder a firm squeeze.

speaker: Helga
content: ...But still, thank you.
With that, she picks up the toolbox at her feet. Her fingers linger on the handle, hesitating.
A beam of sunlight falls across her shoulder. Finally, she straightens, her voice crisp once more.

speaker: Helga
content: Tavera, let's go.
Tavera follows close behind. As she passes, you feel the weight of her scrutiny lingering on you.
—Or perhaps it's just your imagination. You're an outsider here. What reason do you have to feel guilty? And who is she to judge you?

You force yourself to ignore Vester's meaningful stare burning into your back, and the stifled groans of the wounded man. Ahead, the two figures grow smaller and smaller until they're no longer of your concern.
Just like the fate of the farlands.
You study the faces before you: a mosaic of fear, doubt, anger, and defiance, all knotted together. It is like staring at a reflection of the farlands themselves.
There's no turning back now. Time to move.
Vester glances at you, then at Helga. A grin pulls at the corner of his mouth.

speaker: Vester
content: Well, if our expert says so, I suppose I'd better tag along and see this through myself.

speaker: Tavera
content: Now you're talking. Hmph... Four's a good number. More room in the back, at least.
With your gear secured, you take a step toward the door. Before your foot can land, a pair of arms dart out from the shadows and seize your leg in a desperate, clinging hold.

speaker: Milonn
content: Wait! Wait... Don't leave me here. What if...
He lowers his voice and glances back at the young man lying on the table.

speaker: Milonn
content: <size=30>What if that kid turns into one of them? What then?</size>
His sincerity is undeniable; the man clearly values his own skin above all else. You suppress a sigh. It's best Helga didn't hear that.
Bending down, you work his desperate hands loose from your calf.

speaker: Milonn
content: No...! Please! Take me with—
Then, grasping his thin, bony fingers, you haul him to his feet.
Let's go.
[On the Road]

speaker: Vester
content: You sure this is the way?

The jeep jolts along the road toward <color=#fb9259>Alsa Highlands</color>. The midday sun hangs directly overhead outside the window. Its light feels thin and distant, unable to penetrate the growing gloom that swallows the landscape.

speaker: Milonn
content: Yeah... It matches the map. <size=30>Don't blame me if it's wrong...</size>
Milonn concludes his mumbled excuses and curls inward like a frightened animal.
He'd walked right into the verbal trap, but his total surrender leaves Vester with nothing to confront. Vester can only snort in frustration, the fight draining out of him.
The jeep's interior is hot and close, but the silence that follows is worse.
Ordinarily, you welcome silence—those rare moments when you can set the mask aside and just breathe.

But now, with scrutinizing eyes from the back seat and tension humming between your companions, there is no peace. You find yourself mentally rehearsing your cover story on a loop, each iteration wearing the edges a little thinner.

To distract yourself, you study the jeep's interior. Cracks web the upholstery, and dents of varying depth pock the metal frame. This vehicle has clearly weathered its share of struggles. It isn't hard to guess who it belongs to.
Your focus eventually lands on a small bobblehead hyena fixed to the dashboard. With every jolt of the jeep, it nods along in a clumsy, adorable rhythm.
It's clearly handmade from scrap. On closer look, the plastic shell is fissured with cracks, meticulously held together by layers of tape.
Helga notices your gaze and glances over. Her eyes crinkle into a warm, knowing smile.

speaker: Helga
content: Little Vick made that for me. Remember her? Short thing, stuck to me like glue at the last gather-up.

speaker: Vester
content: I remember that kid. What's she up to now?

speaker: Helga
content: Oh, that one's never still. Tinkering with Aurum Secretum under Hypatia's watch these days.

speaker: Vester
content: Hmph. That Fraser girl again... She—
