Vester catches Helga's gaze in the rearview mirror and immediately thinks better of it. He cuts off mid-thought, his gaze sliding away—then landing squarely on you.

speaker: Vester
content: So, ${PlayerName}, you come from Fraser with Helga? Or one of the other camps?
You tell them you were born and raised in Fraser's refugee district. Your parents died young, leaving you to survive alone on the streets until a twist of fate led you to Helga.
You invent a farland settlement on the spot, describing its destruction in some long-ago catastrophe. Years of solitary wandering, you claim, ended only when Helga took you in.
You rush through the freshly fabricated tale, but your vague answers do not satisfy Vester. He purses his lips, silently turning your words over as if testing their weight.
What Vester doesn't know—cannot know—is that you have no memories at all. Even if someone asked you to recount the simplest detail of DisCity's past, your mind would offer only a blank wall.
If memory is what makes a person, then maybe you haven't lied to them. Perhaps you really don't qualify as a Disian after all.

speaker: Helga
content: Why dig up old graves? That's for us wrinkled cabbages. You young folks got the long road ahead to worry about!
Helga's tone is warm, smiling. She catches your eye in the rearview mirror and gives a quick wink. On the dashboard, the little scrap-built hyena wobbles in cheerful accord...
Thud!
The jeep lurches, throwing you forward before your tailbone crashes back into the seat. Pain lances up your spine. Helga groans under her breath and hauls back on the handbrake.

speaker: Helga
content: Sounds like the tire's gone. I'll check it. Keep quiet; last thing we need is the Corruptors' company. We're close to Alsa.
Helga hops out of the jeep. In the rearview mirror, you see Vester's eyes darting. He looks ready to start another argument.

Without hesitating, you roll down the window and lean out. Helga spots you and gives a knowing smile, gesturing you over. You shove the door open and stumble out like a drowning person clawing for air.
The long drive has left your legs shaky, but Helga's steadying grip catches you before you falter.
You fetch the toolbox and set it at her feet. She crouches down, her hands moving with practiced efficiency, but her frown deepens with every second.
Then you hear the sound of the rear window rolling down. You glance up to meet Milonn's anxious face peering out.
...What is it?
He remains silent, his bulging eyes rolling in their sockets as they study you. After a suspended moment, he leans closer. You can almost feel the tremor of his lips hovering just above your head.

speaker: Milonn
content: ...This is bad. A bad sign. The mission... It's not gonna work out.

speaker: Milonn
content: <size=30>Vester said the Speaker... c-can't be trusted...</size>
You stifle a weary sigh, your mind scrambling for a reply. Before you can form a word, a snide voice cuts through the air from the other side of the vehicle.

speaker: Vester
content: <size=30>Now, there's really no need for that...</size>
Vester deliberately raises his voice, ensuring every word carries clearly to you and Helga outside the jeep.

speaker: Vester
content: We've got an expert with us, don't we? Brought all sorts of tricks. I'm sure we'll manage.
A tug at your sleeve. Helga wordlessly hands you something: the nail she just pulled from the tire.
It's long. The surface is clean, dry, with no mud. You run your thumb along the shaft, and your fingers catch on rough wood shavings clinging to the threads near the head.
This nail was planted before you even left.

speaker: Vester
content: Of course, if we all end up dead... well, that'd be on the Speaker's poor judgment, wouldn't it?
Helga straightens up, fixing Vester with an unblinking stare.
[Alsa Highlands] (Add gunfire sound)

speaker: Captain
content: ...Enough!
She picks off several machine gunners with swift precision before ducking back into the trench. Even under the overcast sky, her aim is nothing short of remarkable.
On the <color=#fb9259>Alsa Highlands</color> front, the deafening thunder of battle finally falls silent, leaving only a lingering haze of gunsmoke.

Ranor tucks his canteen back under his coat, his expression crestfallen. The captain ejects her spent magazine, and only as she shifts to pull a fresh one from her pocket does she notice the look on his face.

speaker: Captain
content: ...Sorry. I'm fine. Save it.

speaker: Freyna
content: Swat us down, then pretend to be polite? Some people have really perfected that act.

The captain's hands clench around the magazine, her knuckles blanching white. Her jaw is set so tight it aches, a desperate dam holding back the torrent. But in the end, she can't bring herself to let it slide.

speaker: Captain
content: ...Who are you talking about?

speaker: Freyna
content: I'm talking about the fat-ass senators joking over roast beef right now.

speaker: Freyna
content: Oh, and the bootlickers who think a fancy uniform makes them one of them.
In the trench's sudden quiet, the harsh rasp of the captain's breathing fills the space. Ranor's hand moves, lifting the canteen once more—

speaker: Captain
content: Fraser gave us a home.

speaker: Freyna
content: A home? Don't forget who put us on the street like dogs in the first place. Same people.

speaker: Freyna
content: We're out here bleeding for them, and for what? A few hot meals? Ptui! We joined to live. Not to die forgotten in this shithole!

speaker: Freyna
content: ...Those were your words. Remember?

speaker: Captain
content: I didn't know any better back then. I only saw what was in front of me. My next meal. That ignorance... that's what kept us in the gutter. It was no life. We couldn't stay there.
She keeps her head down, working the grip of her gun in careful, repetitive motions. A low murmur escapes her, less a conversation and more a whisper to herself.

speaker: Captain
content: This is the way. We earned our place. And because we stand here, others get to live better...

speaker: Freyna
content: So, you mean... we deserved all that suffering?

speaker: Freyna
content: You ******* hypocrite! Too ashamed of where you came from? Do you even hear yourself?!

speaker: Freyna
content: Open your eyes! Look at us! Everyone's dead! Is this the better life?!

speaker: Captain
content: That is exactly why their deaths can't be wasted. They mean something—

speaker: Freyna
content: They mean the senators can stuff their faces a little more!!!

speaker: Freyna
content: <size=45>What have they ever given you?! What have they ever lost for you to kiss their boots like this?!</size>

speaker: Freyna
content: Ha... Right. You climbed the ladder. You got your seat at their table. Congrats.

speaker: Captain
content: Shut up. Shut up! I order you to be silent!

speaker: Ranor
content: Both of you, stop it! Two o'clock, enemy gunner, dug in!

speaker: Ranor
content: ...Freyna? Why are you standing—? FREYNA, GET DOWN!!!
[On the Road]

Helga stalks around the car and wrenches the rear door open with enough force to nearly tear it from its hinges. Vester, who had been slumped against the window, lurches forward and almost pitches out onto the ground.

speaker: Helga
content: Vester. Get out here and say it to my face. If you've got a better plan, let's hear it.
Everything about her body suggests confrontation, but her voice betrays no heat. The question comes out calm, almost curious, as though she truly wants to know.

speaker: Vester
content: Hmph, the problem is you're rushing. The Corruptors up in Alsa won't be cleaned up easy, not even if you go yourself!

speaker: Vester
content: If it comes to it... we could always move on Fraser. Those *************, pushing us to the brink...

speaker: Helga
content: You talk a good game, and you're not wrong. I wish it were that simple.

speaker: Helga
content: But while you all bicker in meetings, people are starving. What have any of you done but point fingers?

speaker: Vester
content: We sent people! But where do we find the hands? The supplies? We're stretched thin!

speaker: Helga
content: Right. Everyone's got their troubles. Heard talk last meeting about cutting a few camps loose. Abandon one, then what? Who's next?

speaker: Vester
content: That was them, not me! I never suggested—

speaker: Helga
content: We can't even manage relief, and you're talking war with Fraser?

speaker: Helga
content: This trade route is our last chance. If it stays closed, every camp in the farlands falls. No exceptions.
Vester says nothing. For a long moment, he seems unable to. Then, haltingly, the words come, his voice unsteady.

speaker: Vester
content: Helga, I've got no problem with you...
His gaze drifts around for a moment before finally settling on you.

speaker: Vester
content: What I don't know is whether your new kid here is worth a damn. Last thing we need is dead weight getting us all killed.
In the distraction of this minor conflict, a thick, cloying presence slithers in, enveloping you all without a sound.
The others dismiss it as mere fog, still locked in their standoff. But you recognize the stench: decay and madness intertwined.
It's <color=#fb9259>Mania</color>!
Watch out! We're surrounded by Corruptors!
The moment your warning leaves your lips, Helga is already moving. She kicks off the ground and vaults onto the roof of the vehicle in one fluid motion.

speaker: Helga
content: Battle positions! Now!
The group, at each other's throats moments before, snaps into combat mode. Tavera unleashes a low growl and charges to the front. Vester draws his blade, cursing.
Even Milonn grips his cane, though no one expects him to fight.
Bang! Bang! Bang!
Helga's shots drop the leading Corruptors mid-lunge. Tavera seizes the opening and pushes forward.

speaker: Helga
content: Tavera, two on your left! I've got your flank!
They fight in perfect sync—one striking from range, the other in close—their combined assault shredding through Corruptors with lethal efficiency.
In a brief lull, Helga's eyes snap to yours, her words quick and clipped.

speaker: Helga
content: Watch Vester. Don't let him near your stuff.
Your nod is sharp with comprehension. Vester is nowhere to be seen, and the distinctive whistle of his blade is silent.
Suspicion drives you to the back of the vehicle. There he is, framed by the open trunk, shoulders tense as he searches for something. You lunge, fingers clamping onto his forearm.
What are you doing?

speaker: Vester
content: Trying to keep us alive, of course! Isn't this what your precious gear is for?
What's in there isn't for this.
You shove him away with all your strength. Vester stumbles, recovers, and snatches the scimitar leaning against the vehicle.

speaker: Milonn
content: H-help... <size=45>Help!</size> <size=50>HELP ME!</size>
From the other side of the vehicle, Milonn screams in terror. You glance over to see Tavera fighting two Corruptors, completely pinned down.
The cry draws Helga's eye. She spins, slamming a fresh magazine home with muscle memory, but the motion is a heartbeat too slow. A Corruptor is already stooping over Milonn's limp body.
Your eyes dart between Vester and your gear. He stands poised, blade in hand, gaze fixed on you.
He hasn't moved, teeth gritted in impatient fury, but his stance has already shifted, ready to bolt past you toward his companion.
The game is over. You break into a dead sprint toward Milonn. A farland curse hisses behind you—Vester is right there.
The two Corruptors looming over Milonn sense your charge. They freeze, then pivot with a slow, horrifying synchronicity. A guttural moan tears from their throats as they fix on you.
Get back!
You step forward, shielding both Milonn and Vester behind you.
Release the shackles
[Alsa Highlands]
The captain collapses against the sandbag wall. A bullet has torn through her shoulder blade. The chilling thought follows: she may never raise a rifle again.

speaker: Freyna
content: ...Why the hell did you take that bullet for me?!

speaker: Freyna
content: You were going to let me rot here anyway. Sooner or later, what's the difference?! ...I was deserting! Let them shoot me for it! Consider it them doing you the favor of a field execution!

speaker: Ranor
content: Freyna, shut it! Now isn't the time for this...
The captain can only watch as Ranor strips off her coat. Her shirt is soaked through, plastered to her skin with blood. He tears the right sleeve clean away and retrieves the alcohol.
A waste of supplies. She tries to push him off, but her hand merely claws at the air before falling—and finding another hand.
Freyna leans close, muttering words the captain can no longer discern. Nothing kind ever comes from Freyna's lips, but the strength to argue is gone. So is the will.
Why did she do it? Her body moved before her mind could catch up.
A final tide of searing pain and blood loss crashes over her, drowning the world in white noise. She closes her eyes and drifts back to a night in Fraser City.
[Flashback]

She was sitting alone on the low rooftop of a tenement house. Across Fraser City, lights blazed in celebration of a distant victory. Below, a clamorous river of revelers flowed through the streets, their joy a distant murmur.
She was so adrift she didn't notice Freyna sidle up beside her, nor the warm bread pressed into her hand.

It was the touch that broke the spell. Freyna rolled up her sleeve and gently touched her arm. The sharp sting made her gasp, snapping her back. She looked down, startled to find the bread in her hand already missing a bite.

speaker: Captain
content: You... Where'd you steal this from...?
Freyna went still for a heartbeat, then a wide grin lit up her face.

speaker: Freyna
content: Relax! The bakery lady on East Street gave it to me. Said since it's such a big day, it was a blessing for the troops.

speaker: Freyna
content: Her son's enlisted too. She doesn't know when he'll be back... But with how the war's going, it can't be long, right...?

speaker: Freyna
content: Alright, let me see that wound... ******* hell. That old bastard really laid into you...
That morning, she and Freyna had tried to scavenge food from an inspector's house, only to be spotted by a guard. In a nearby alley, they were cornered.
Given the auspicious day, they'd shown "mercy": twenty lashes, then release. For a refugee district thief, it was a lenient sentence.
Now, the stripes on her arm were still raised and tender. Freyna's fingers hovered, not quite touching the angry skin. In a flash, her own wrist twisted up, capturing Freyna's hand in a firm grip.

speaker: Captain
content: Let's join the army.

speaker: Freyna
content: The army?! Are you cracked? Don't joke like that. Today was my fault... Well, the alley was too damn long! I'll run faster next time. I won't slow you down again.

speaker: Captain
content: In the army, we'd have food, clothes... and a real name. It's better than this. Besides, we're already good at—
Freyna snickered.

speaker: Freyna
content: Good at what? Picking pockets? They've got guns out there! We'd come back missing pieces...

speaker: Captain
content: I heard if we sign up together, they'll put us in the same unit. I'll protect you. We'll make it through.

speaker: Captain
content: ...Don't believe me? Even that inspector today said I had the makings of a soldier. Said it's a waste, me doing this.
She was so excited that she sprang up, yet her hold on Freyna's hand never faltered. She nearly yanked Freyna up with her.
Even on the battlefield, she would never let go of this hand, would she?

speaker: Captain
content: They're recruiting at the range next week. They'll give us rifles! Hit the 8-ring with one shot, and we're in.

speaker: Captain
content: Once I'm in, I'll do something big. And when I do...
With her free hand, she formed a pistol, squinted one eye, and aimed it at the golden palace shimmering in the distance.

speaker: Freyna
content: ...Alright, alright, I believe you! Now sit back down...
She raised her finger slightly, and in the distance, fireworks lit up all of Fraser City.
[Alsa Highlands]
She surfaces to a familiar face—Ranor, his expression tight with worry. She has made it back. But Freyna is gone.
[On the Road]

The Corruptors are violently hurled back the instant they touch the red barrier. From ruined chest cavities, they unleash shrieks of pure agony and fury, thrashing wildly against the energy that holds them at bay.
—Bang! Bang!
Two precise shots cut the screams short. The figures jerk and go limp.
Helga dismounts from the car roof with a heavy thud, interposing herself between you and the Corruptor remains. She meets everyone's gaze, the faint wisp of smoke curling from her barrel.

speaker: Helga
content: Everyone still in one piece?
Her gaze sweeps over Vester and Milonn, both shielded behind you, then locks onto you in a long, assessing stare.

speaker: Vester
content: Traitor!!!
Vester makes his move in a sudden burst of motion, but Helga reacts instantly, blocking his path with the hard edge of her rifle's stock and hauling him backward.

speaker: Helga
content: What the hell are you doing?!

speaker: Vester
content: What... what was that just now?! You pulled something out of thin air!

speaker: Vester
content: You all saw it, didn't you?! That wasn't any farland trick!
Milonn is a silent, curled shape on the earth, his hands shielding his eyes. Vester, driven by a rising desperation, gives him a sharp kick.

speaker: Tavera
content: ...I saw it too. That red thing. Covered in spikes.
As she speaks, her grip tightens around the spear, its tip now unwavering and leveled directly at you.

speaker: Tavera
content: Who are you?

options: Try to keep up the act

content: You step forward slowly, calmly meeting all the hostile gazes fixed on you.
I don't know what you're talking about. This mad man just accused me out of—
Before you can finish, Vester shoves past everyone and bolts to the back of the vehicle. He yanks your gear from the trunk.
A heavy metal crate thuds to the ground. The Bureau's emblem and a line of fine DisCity lettering are stamped plainly on the lid.
There's no turning back now. The secret is laid bare.
I'm actually the Chief of DisCity's Bureau of Crisis Control, specifically in charge of handling Mania incidents.
I came here to—
You don't get to finish. Tavera's knuckles whiten on her spear as she drives it toward you.

speaker: Tavera
content: Disian... Die!
However, a hand—wiry and strong—snaps out and catches the shaft mid-thrust, halting it cold.
The moment Tavera sees whose hand it is, all the strength drains from her grip.

speaker: Tavera
content: Speaker... You knew?

speaker: Vester
content: Knew? She was the one who planned it!

speaker: Vester
content: Our scouts saw her. The esteemed Speaker slipped into DisCity alone days ago. Now this brat shows up. It's a setup! She's selling out the farlands!

speaker: Helga
content: This "Disian brat" just saved your lives.

speaker: Vester
content: Only because he'd have died with us! Hmph, I risked everything to expose this—
female_content: Only because she'd have died with us! Hmph, I risked everything to expose this—

speaker: Helga
content: You call planting a nail in our tire "risking everything"? Leaving us all as Corruptor bait?
Vester freezes at Helga's words.
Helga's hand emerges from her pocket, clutching a twisted metal nail dusted with black tire shards. She raises it slowly, turning it so all can see.

speaker: Helga
content: This came from our tire. It's a nail from the outpost wall. And you were the only one who could've gotten to it.
Her stare pins Vester, intense enough to feel like a physical brand.

speaker: Helga
content: You think you're clever? To expose your "enemy," you'd get everyone on this truck killed? That's acceptable to you?

speaker: Helga
content: If this mission fails and another camp starves... whose head will that be on?
Vester is speechless. His breath comes in heavy, ragged gasps that fill the silence. In that charged stillness, you decide to—
This is a conflict among the farlanders themselves. You don't feel it's your place to intervene, so you stand beside Helga in silence, an observer.
This seems like the moment to make your stance clear. You step forward, your voice measured and steady.
I did not come here as an enemy of the farlands. In fact, I'm not here on behalf of DisCity.
I came simply because Helga asked, hoping to help the farlands—

speaker: Vester
content: What's it to you?! Don't you two stand there playing good cop, bad cop with me!
Vester shoves you aside and storms up to Helga.

speaker: Vester
content: Helga, you always think I'm against you. Well, I am! Because you keep trusting outsiders! First that Fraser girl, now this Disian!

speaker: Vester
content: Yeah, I sabotaged the tire. I wanted to stop us from reaching Alsa! I won't let some Disian hold our fate! How is that any different from bowing to Fraser?!

speaker: Vester
content: If I hadn't, how else was I supposed to get through to you?! You're so busy protecting this brat, you wouldn't have heard a word!
He's trembling with fury. His finger jabs at you, then hammers hard against his own chest.

speaker: Vester
content: Helga, I don't care if you look down on me. But how I've stood by our people all these years—you've seen it. Everything I've done... has been for the farlands!

speaker: Vester
content: You want to know if it was worth it? Fine. I can't speak for anyone else, but my life? Take it, if that's what you want!
Helga holds him in her gaze. When her lips part, it's not words that emerge first, but a long, exhausted sigh.

speaker: Helga
content: Vester... do you think that makes you a hero?

speaker: Helga
content: Do you think being in charge gives you the right to decide who lives and who dies?

speaker: Vester
content: This is all for the farlands!

speaker: Tavera
content: ENOUGH!!!
Tavera's roar leaves the group in stunned silence. Her chest heaves, eyes bloodshot and fixed on Helga. Though the tip of her spear dips slightly, her grip on it is still iron-tight.

speaker: Tavera
content: Speaker, I don't care about the rest. Just answer me one thing. Do you really trust him?
female_content: Speaker, I don't care about the rest. Just answer me one thing. Do you really trust her?

content: Helga turns and gives you a long, meaningful look.
[Alsa Highlands]
The captain rips her arm from Ranor's grip. A hot rush signals the wound giving way, leaving a ruin of blood and torn cloth. She doesn't stop. She staggers on, steps faltering but unceasing.

speaker: Freyna
content: Those gun nests she took out are still empty. That's our gap. I can blow us a path.

speaker: Ranor
content: Don't you see? Their attacks are falling apart too! They can't last much longer. Maybe... maybe if we just hold on...

speaker: Freyna
content: She can't hear you... So drop the act. She was the only one who ever bought it.

From a distance, she watches Freyna go. The way she moves is exactly the same: the same quick, light gait that once carried her to a roof's edge in one fluid jump. Freyna would always land first, then turn, arm outstretched, to pull her up after.

speaker: Freyna
content: Ranor, you know what she told me once?

speaker: Ranor
content: What? To punish you? Whatever it was, she was just angry... When has she ever not thrown herself in front of us?
Freyna's skills, already impressive, have been honed to a razor's edge by years of service. Even now, with over a dozen kilos of explosives on her back, she moves with a predator's lightness.
The captain watches, breath held, as if at any moment Freyna will turn.

speaker: Freyna
content: Yeah. Call her "Captain" once, and she'll walk through fire for you. That's why she's so damn grateful for every scrap Fraser tosses her way. I hate that about her... but I also...

speaker: Freyna
content: I've followed her all these years 'cause she promised to keep me alive. Even if she's forgotten... I haven't.

speaker: Captain
content: I remember... I remember all of it...

speaker: Captain
content: All I ever wanted... was for everyone to make it out alive...
Is it her wounds? The exhaustion? No matter how hard she drives her body forward, Freyna pulls farther ahead. How can this open path feel endless, longer than that shadowed alley ever did?

speaker: Freyna
content: When she wakes up, tell her. I'm not doing this for Fraser... I'm not noble like her.
Freyna is too skilled, too fast.
She has already gained the high ground. In the next heartbeat, a bloom of red erupts on her chest. Her form twists, a marionette with its strings cut.

speaker: Freyna
content: I'm just a thief... a deserter. And now... I'm going to use that noble duty of hers one last time...

speaker: Freyna
content: Live for me. After all... it doesn't matter who survives. It's all the same.

speaker: Captain
content: Stop... Stop! That's an order...!

speaker: Captain
content: FREYNA!!!
Freyna turns. In the final instant before she falls, her lips part—
Then, the deafening roar. Her body, her unspoken words, everything dissolves in the blast. Ash drifts down like the fading embers of spent fireworks.
[On the Road]

speaker: Helga
content: I do.
Tavera stumbles back and jams her spear into the mud. She sags against the shaft—the only thing holding her upright.

speaker: Helga
content: Not only do I trust this person, I wish every soul in the farlands could do the same, too.

speaker: Helga
content: Because this "Disian brat" just saved your lives. And the "Fraser girl" you were talking about is out there digging for Hypercubes for us right now.

speaker: Helga
content: I don't give a damn about factions or borders! The only ones I trust are those who stand on the front line!

speaker: Helga
content: And you... you think as long as you say it's "for the farlands," it doesn't matter if everyone on this truck dies? If more people starve?

speaker: Helga
content: Fine. You want to be honorable—I won't argue. But don't you dare call what you're doing "for the farlands" ever again!
No one answers. Her words hang in the air, thick and unclaimed, before sinking into an absolute silence.

speaker: Tavera
content: I see. If that's what you believe...
Her jaw tightens, every muscle straining as if to physically wring the next words from her throat.

speaker: Tavera
content: Forgive me. But I cannot follow you, Speaker.

speaker: Tavera
content: The Disians slaughtered my people. How can you ask me to just... forget all those lives?
She retreats slowly, arms folded tight across her chest, her gaze fixed firmly elsewhere. Vester releases a quiet breath of relief and nods to Tavera, an unspoken approval.

speaker: Tavera
content: Don't look at me like that. You're a traitor too.

speaker: Helga
content: Yeah... So many lives lost. How could anyone forget?
Helga lowers her gaze and nods wearily.

speaker: Helga
content: Fine. If that's your choice, I won't force you.

speaker: Helga
content: Whether you want to survive, or stay true to your roots... you're not wrong. None of you are.

speaker: Helga
content: I won't order anyone to walk a path they don't believe in.

speaker: Helga
content: But me? I'm not stopping. This road has to be opened, no matter what.
A heavy silence descends, broken only by the wind's low, mournful whistle.
Into that quiet, you move to stand beside Helga. Without speaking, you bend down, lift the equipment from the ground, and settle its weight onto your shoulder.
Let's go.
Something shifts in Helga's eyes. The faintest smile touches her lips, and she gives you a single, solid nod.
You and Helga unload the gear and explosives from the jeep. No one offers to help. No one says goodbye.
But the road ahead is treacherous for everyone. After a moment, you retrieve two spare Bureau-issue weapons from your pack and approach the three staying behind.
Take these. They're shock devices designed to deal with Corruptors. More effective than regular bullets.
Vester scoffs and turns his head away. Tavera hesitates, then squeezes her eyes shut.
Only Milonn accepts, his hands trembling as he cradles the devices. He stares at their cold metallic gleam, handling them as though they held the weight of his survival.
You walk over to Helga. She is gazing out at the wasteland, her expression distant.
For... the farlands?
She gives a slow nod, then shakes her head, as if arguing with herself. Her boots scrape heavily against the ground.

speaker: Helga
content: Doesn't matter who it's for. I want to carve out a path that keeps people alive.

speaker: Helga
content: ${PlayerName}, tell me... Do you think this path can work?
It will. We haven't given up yet, have we?
...I don't know. But I know if we don't start walking now, it never will.

Helga listens in silence. She offers no words, only raises her hand and rests it firmly on your shoulder. You feel the weight of it—steadying, grounding—and beneath that certainty, the faintest tremor.

speaker: Helga
content: Let's go.
You cast one last look behind you. The jeep stands motionless where you left it, the three silent passengers blurred into silhouettes by the thick air.
Mm.
<color=#fb9259>Alsa Highlands</color> waits just beyond.
[Alsa Highlands - Convergence]

speaker: Captain
content: Almost there...
Ranor clutches his rifle to his chest, leaning against the bunker wall, his breaths shallow and frayed.
<color=#fb9259>Alsa Highlands</color> lies in unnatural silence. Yet, the captain hears whispers—the wind, or the dead?
The 24th Company began with twenty-eight. Now, only two remain.
Before them stretches the path Freyna blasted open, a scar leading forward and upward. It seems impossible that someone so slight could have carved such a wide road.
At the thought, her body sways.

speaker: Captain
content: Ranor, let's go.
Ranor gives her a weak smile.

speaker: Ranor
content: Okay... let's go. We're... we're going home...
He braces on his hands, tries to rise, sways, then crumples to his knees before her. His rifle clatters. Blood pours from his chest.

The captain retrieves the pocket watch from the wound. His father's gift. His "lucky" charm, though luck had abandoned his father years ago to a sickbed. Just moments before, Ranor had said the watch stopped a bullet for him.
It did. Just not enough. The cheap metal casing was no match for the round.
Ranor is now still. She closes her fingers around the watch. Its tiny heart has ceased to beat.
The battlefield falls into a silence so profound, one could almost call it—
<color=#fb9259>Peaceful.</color>
The thought is an intrusion. A sob claws at her throat. She cannot draw a full breath.
Soaked in blood and filth, she squeezes her eyes shut, then opens them. She straightens her broken posture, lifts her chin, and takes a step. Then another.
Above, dark silhouettes sway into view.
Reinforcements? They've... finally come.
Fraser's promise... it was real. They only had to hold on a little longer.
For the first time, she lowers her weapon and raises her hands. Forgotten sunlight washes over her face. Her shoulder pulses, a flare of pain with every step.
Yet it is this very pain that reminds her she is still alive. It nearly brings her to tears.

speaker: Captain
content: This is... Fraser Army, 24th Company. Sole survivor reporting. Captain—

speaker: Helga
content: <color=#fb9259>Helga.</color>
[Shift Perspective]
The Alsa Highlands unfold before you. Unthinking, you've drifted to the cliff's edge. The wind sweeps past, carrying dust into the void.
The view is brutally clear: below the highlands, there is only a churning sea of shadows and bleached bones—a mass grave where friend and foe are long since indistinguishable.
Helga crouches slowly beside you. She scoops up a handful of dry earth, then opens her fingers, letting the sand and grit trickle back down. It falls like a quiet, gritty defiance.

speaker: Helga
content: I really thought they were coming to save us. What a damn joke... I led everyone around me to their deaths with my own hands, and here I am, still breathing.

speaker: Helga
content: The shadows I saw... they were soldiers already lost to Mania. No sense left in them. If there had been, Freyna wouldn't have made it over the ridge at all.

speaker: Helga
content: In the end... even our enemies had written us off.

speaker: Helga
content: This is... our story.
One week ago.
Helga, the current Speaker of the Farland Assembly, sat across from you. She watched you with a warm smile and a steady gaze.
Strictly speaking, it was not a formal interrogation. After all, a Sinner had rarely voluntarily taken that seat to ask for help.
Helga had come alone, and for one purpose only: she hoped you could help the Farland Alliance carve out a trade route through Fraser's blockade.
...I'm truly sorry.
Until DisCity and the farlands establish formal diplomatic relations, I have no authority to send anyone in an official capacity. It would be seen as interference.
You paused briefly, watching for Helga's reaction. You had expected disappointment, perhaps even anger, but she simply raised an eyebrow.

speaker: Helga
content: I'm sitting right here, in the flesh. Isn't this formal enough?

Her question was posed as if it were the most natural thing in the world, with a disarmingly candid expression. You wondered for a moment if you were overthinking it; perhaps the farlanders simply dismissed formal protocol.
I appreciate that, but by the book...
test
test
test
test
test
test
This is the Bureau's visitor registry. If this were a formal diplomatic visit, I'd see your name on it.

speaker: Helga
content: Well, put it like that, and hardly a soul knows I'm in DisCity right now.
...Are you admitting that your Assembly doesn't know you're here?
Helga waves a hand, brushing the question aside.

speaker: Helga
content: Quit with the formal talk. You'll tie your tongue in knots, and it's wearing my ears out.

speaker: Helga
content: The Assembly... Bunch of windbags. Ever since we got free, all they do is yap themselves blue around a table.

speaker: Helga
content: I've heard enough noise. Time someone did something that actually needs doing.
Her decision to steer the conversation toward the Assembly and openly criticize its members had practically confirmed that her visit lacked official sanction.
However, a more pressing concern lingered: how had she managed to pinpoint this location and identify you personally?

Given that the farlands were still establishing themselves, it seemed highly unlikely they possessed the resources to place a spy. Nonetheless, the troubling possibility of a security breach within the Bureau gnawed at you.
You kept your questions to yourself for the moment. Helga went on.

speaker: Helga
content: Our lot won't take outside help. Call it "true self-reliance." Even with a ceasefire with DisCity, they aren't ready to shake hands with any Disian.

speaker: Helga
content: Heard the Fraser nobles are having a right laugh. Say we brought it on ourselves. That we're getting what we deserve.

speaker: Helga
content: But you gotta understand: Farlanders spent too many years living on someone else's say-so. Used when we were handy, tossed out like trash when we weren't. People are scared. And now Fraser has the gall to call us ungrateful.

speaker: Helga
content: Don't blame them, honestly. Everyone's been hurt too deep to trust easy. And hate? Yeah, I got plenty of that in me, too.
She fell silent for a moment, as if caught by a memory, but quickly shook her head.

speaker: Helga
content: But if we all just white-knuckle that hate, it's gonna dig a grave and push us all in.
Deep-seated beliefs don't change overnight. Same story here in DisCity.
Even people born with every advantage... Actually, especially them. That's often where the worst prejudices take root.
Just days ago, there were hate crimes against farland immigrants in Eastside.
A heavy sigh escaped Helga as she nodded in acknowledgment.

speaker: Helga
content: There'll always be folks carrying a grudge. But there are always folks with sense, too. Look, I'm here, right? Talking to you. That's gotta count for something.
Her casual tone was what finally drew the nagging question to the surface. You realized this was your moment to ask what you had wondered from the start.

options: How did you find out about the MBCC?

content: But how did you, Speaker, even think to come to a place that... isn't exactly on the map?
The MBCC doesn't advertise. And for all you knew, I could've been just another Disian who holds hatred and prejudice toward the farlands.

speaker: Helga
content: I've got my sources, of course.
Noticing your furrowed brow, Helga burst into sudden, hearty laughter. The boisterous sound felt almost out of place in the stark interrogation room.

speaker: Helga
content: You've been sitting on that one a while, eh? Can't blame you. Chatting like this, I damn near forgot what sort of room I'm in.
After a perfunctory glance around the room, her gaze settled back on you. Her expression was now serious.

speaker: Helga
content: Don't fret. I'm not talking about spies, and no one's been leaking your secrets.

speaker: Helga
content: We've got a young researcher among us. Name's Hypatia. Sharp as a new pin. Says she knows you.

The story Rust had told you about that name came back to mind: she was once the young lady of the Campbell family, who took a path that diverged completely from her brother's. She had repeatedly defended the farlanders, eventually giving up her family name to stand with them.

speaker: Helga
content: She told me there's a place in DisCity called the Bureau of Crisis Control. That its Chief is a good sort. Gutsy, responsible.
I've heard of her. But I don't believe we've ever met directly.

speaker: Helga
content: But you'd know the name "Archivist 19260817," yeah?
As soon as the name reached you, a feeling stirred deep in your chest. You could almost hear the echo of keystrokes in the dead of night—you, alone before a glowing screen, typing with conviction.

speaker: Helga
content: She told me what the Chief once said to her: We farlanders will forge our own path. Find our own answers.

speaker: Helga
content: Without the Chief's trust back then, she never would've found the guts to expose Fraser's long game, even if it almost got her killed.
Is she... doing alright in the farlands now?

speaker: Helga
content: Some see a savior. Plenty still don't trust her. I mean, that bearing of hers screams Fraser nobility. The old hardliners in the Assembly are the worst. Convinced she's a spy, looking for any slip-up.
...She doesn't deserve that.

speaker: Helga
content: That's just the Farland Assembly for you these days.

speaker: Helga
content: Everyone's dug in, clinging to their grudges. Won't budge an inch. Talk a big game about the future, but don't spare a glance for the folks bleeding on the front lines.

speaker: Helga
content: I've seen that type before: sitting around big tables, deciding who lives and dies with a few words. I won't let our Assembly turn into that.
A faint undercurrent had stirred beneath her words. It might have been anger, sorrow, or disappointment. Yet the feeling was distant, its edges worn smooth, like river stones shaped by endless water.
You studied her. She appeared at ease, but a readiness was held in the line of her back, the tension in her core. Pale, old scars etched faint paths across her neck.
You're the current Speaker of the farlands, but you don't strike me as someone who sits behind a desk. If I had to guess... you were a soldier?
Helga nodded, a smile on her face.

speaker: Helga
content: Grew up in Fraser's refugee district. Served in their army for a good few years after. Though your spies in Fraser won't find a trace of me—Sorry. Old soldier's habit. I say what I think.

speaker: Helga
content: Fraser Army, 24th Company. I was their captain. After I deserted, command scrubbed us from the records. Simple as that, like we never happened.
You don't seem the type to desert under fire.

speaker: Helga
content: It was a suicide mission. Or rather, a mission to get my unit killed. Command called it a "grievous but necessary sacrifice."

speaker: Helga
content: To the brass, lives are numbers. War's a game. They've never set foot on the line. Never seen the kids in the med tents, blown to pieces.

speaker: Helga
content: Heh. They're too soft for that. The sight would ruin their appetites for a week.
A cold laugh escaped her before her expression hardened, her gaze fixing intently on you.

speaker: Helga
content: But I have.

speaker: Helga
content: That's why I only trust the kids on the front lines. Doesn't matter where they're from.

speaker: Helga
content: I trust Hypatia. I've seen how she fights for our people. So I wanted to meet you myself, the one who said those words to her.

speaker: Helga
content: I'm not here for the Assembly. And I've got nothing to trade you. Just think of it as a personal ask, from one regular farlander to someone who might be a friend worth trusting.
With that, she shook her head, a knowing smile on her face.

speaker: Helga
content: I know it sounds damn foolish. To your DisCity politicians, this must seem downright childish.

speaker: Helga
content: But then, I was never much of a proper leader. Here I am, my age, and I can't even keep my own Assembly in line.

speaker: Helga
content: Childish, foolish—call it what you want. I just want to do right by the people around me.
When she finished, she simply held your gaze. In her eyes, you could see the echoes of many familiar faces.
In that moment, you knew you could not refuse her.
Funny. "Childish." "Foolish." I hear those words aimed at me a lot, too.
You gently set aside the documents in your hands.
I can't act as the Chief officially. But then, I can also just be a person. If there's anything I can do to help, I will.
So, let me introduce myself again. Please, call me ${PlayerName}.

speaker: Helga
content: Just Helga is fine.

You stood and opened the interrogation room door, motioning for her to go ahead. Helga got to her feet, smoothing her lapels and adjusting her coat. Her posture was rigid—shoulders squared, back rod-straight—the unmistakable carriage of someone with military training.
—Or, as she herself had put it, not a soldier. A deserter.
That military experience you mentioned. I'm curious. Is it a long story?

speaker: Helga
content: Yeah. It's a long one alright...
That's fine. We've got time on the way.
[Alsa Highlands]

Following the planned route along the windswept cliffs of Alsa Highlands, you and Helga place the explosive charges with methodical precision. At the seventh emplacement, as you set the device, a sharp sting bites into your fingertip.
...Hngh!
Your hand recoils from the soil. Jutting from the dirt is a jagged sliver of metal. You carefully work it free and wipe the grime from its surface with your sleeve.

speaker: Helga
content: A Fraser Third Class Merit. One of the cooks in my unit had one just like it.

speaker: Helga
content: Used to be a machine gunner, till a bullet took his leg. Command wanted him discharged. He refused. Said he'd only ever done odd jobs before the army, had no family to speak of; a cripple going back meant no one would take him. So they stuck him in the mess instead.

speaker: Helga
content: This medal was the most valuable thing he ever owned. Look at it now. Rusted to hell.
You lift the forlorn medal, turning its face to the weak sun. The design etched upon it has been worn away by time and touch, rendered a mystery.

speaker: Helga
content: Fraser never sent reinforcements. From the start, they meant for us to die here, to hand the position over. It was a deal they'd struck. Everyone knew. Everyone but me.

speaker: Helga
content: Or maybe... I did know. I just refused to believe it.

speaker: Helga
content: Refused to believe the skills I was so damn proud of meant nothing to Fraser's brass. Refused to believe the glory and the life I thought I'd earned... were never meant for me at all.
The sun burns low and immense, a smearing glare that blurs the world.
Against that vast, untouchable light, the only tangible thing left is the weight of the rusted medal in your hand.
This is also where you made contact with Mania.
With a silent nod, Helga takes the medal from your hand. Her eyes fall to the ground, fixing on the blackened earth where blood soaked deep into the soil long ago.

speaker: Helga
content: I thought fate would be fair. So many died because of me. What right did I have to live? But not only did I live... I came out seeing clearer than ever.

speaker: Helga
content: Every bone, every drop of blood my friends left behind... I can see it all, crystal clear. I became exactly what Fraser needed. The old me would've been over the damn moon...
Her fingers close into a hard fist. There's a soft, brittle crunch as the rust-weakened metal folds in her grip.
So, is this the ending you want to tell?
She stands motionless, head bowed, as the oppressive darkness moans around her.
Then, her gun snaps up toward you.
Bang!
The gunshot cuts the air, silencing the whimper. A Corruptor tumbles backward into the pit.
And in the wake of the shot, the trench beneath you erupts. The shadows boil, and a forest of twisted, clawing arms reaches up from the depths.

speaker: Helga
content: ...They're awake. We need to move. How many left?
Four.
You force a quicker pace, but reality itself seems to decay faster. From the depths below, a wave of dark, Mania-charged mist erupts, plunging the highlands into a frigid twilight instantly.
A cold deeper than ice penetrates your skin. The Mania readings are off the scale. Helga's warning echoes in your mind: delay any longer, and the outpost will be next.

Corruptors lunge from the murk, forcing you to a crawl. Helga's covering fire is a desperate staccato, but you see the toll the mist is taking: her reloads are fumbled, her aim growing heavy and slow.

speaker: Helga
content: ...Behind you!!!
You spin around to find a Corruptor towering at your back.
Just as its limb whistles down, the air solidifies into a wall of familiar blue light, shielding you from the danger.
It's the defensive field from the anti-Mania device you left with Milonn.

The field's disruptive pulse staggers the surrounding Corruptors, buying a precious second. That's all the time a lithe, fast-moving figure needs to plant herself before you, her spear sweeping out in a defiant crescent.

speaker: Tavera
content: Back off!!!
The farland warrior strikes with ferocity, a single kick sending the Corruptor tumbling back into the pit. She plants her spear and takes a protective stance before you.
Her gaze flickers back, her body instinctively edging away. Her lips part, then close. After a pause, she finally speaks:

speaker: Tavera
content: ...According to the Speaker's original plan, I'm to guard you.
From close by, Vester's scoff carries over the chaos. He fights beside Helga, his scimitar flashing in a clean, lethal arc that splits a Corruptor. With the creature falling, he adds:

speaker: Vester
content: Milonn lost his nerve. Didn't think we'd make it out alone, so he came scrambling after you... Hmph, fear's rotted his brains.

speaker: Milonn
content: ...That's why I had to follow! They gave me the gear to survive... They're my only chance to make it out alive!

speaker: Vester
content: And Tavera? Insists on following the Speaker. "Loyalty." She uses that word very... selectively.

speaker: Tavera
content: Everything I know about fighting, the Speaker taught me... If she tells me to fight beside a Disian... then fine. This once.

speaker: Vester
content: Heh. So it seems I'm the only one left out in the cold.
With that said, his scimitar whips out to fell another foe.

speaker: Vester
content: Go on, laugh, Helga. When we get back, I'll be sure to give the Assembly a full report. Every last detail.

speaker: Helga
content: Do it. Tell them how we cleared the Alsa Highlands and put a wrench in Fraser's plans.
She pauses, her gaze shifting to the young person nearby.

speaker: Helga
content: And be sure to tell them ${PlayerName} helped us. You remember that name. You hear me?
After a final, scathing look at Helga, Vester vanishes back into the storm of combat. His style is unmistakable: swift, precise, and brutal cuts that speak of a seasoned warrior.
Your path is cleared by their desperate fight, allowing you to reach the last demolition point at last. But the area is already submerged in a dense, corrosive fog of Mania.
The Mania contamination is too dense. They can't pass through.
A single look passes between you. Helga reads your intent instantly. Before you can move, her hand is on your arm, fingers closing tight enough to stop you.

speaker: Helga
content: You've done more than enough for the farlands already.
No... this isn't just for the farlands. Isn't it the same for you?
The truth is, I don't remember my own past. I've never done any of this out of loyalty to a city, or to some higher-up. It was never about that.
But even so... there are people I care about. People I trust. They come from everywhere, and they'll go everywhere, walking their own paths.
You said it yourself, Helga. The road ahead is long. So...
I just have to keep moving forward.
You take a final breath and leap into the churning Mania below.
A frigid, viscous presence swallows you. Countless spectral hands claw at your limbs, dragging you toward the abyss. The world dissolves into a chorus of maddened whispers—
Why me... Why does it have to be me... I don't want to die... I want to go home!
Kill! Kill them! Kill every last one!
I'm still young... Am I...? We shouldn't have known only this... They taught us nothing but killing!
It was the only way... the only path to the future they promised...
That place... Will there be a place for me there, Mom?
You're adults. Please, tell us the answer.
Who were <color=#fb9259>they</color>? Whose children? Whose friends? Whose lovers?
Who could <color=#fb9259>they</color> have been?
Bang!
A bullet grazes the air beside your head, yet you're untouched.
Behind you, Helga lands almost in sync, rifle already rising to her shoulder—a motion polished across countless battlefields.
Each round she fires is a calculated denial, keeping the lunging Corruptors at bay.
All you have to do is run. Forward. Only forward.
So, is this how the story ends?

speaker: Helga
content: No. This is not the end.

Another shot, and then the rifle falls silent, its magazine spent. Without pause, Helga's hand finds a fresh one, the reload a seamless ritual. The weapon barks back to life, carving a safe passage forward for the young one.

speaker: Helga
content: When I finally dragged myself back to Fraser, to the streets I knew... folks were still living worse than dogs. And way off in the distance, that golden palace was still shining, bright as ever.

speaker: Helga
content: We were gone so long, but not a damn thing changed. Like we never even lived.

speaker: Helga
content: I can't stop wondering what you'd all be like if you'd made it. Made it to thirty, or forty. I try to picture it... but I can't. And that eats at me.

speaker: Helga
content: I swore I'd kill every last one of 'em in the Senate. Kill them all, even if it killed me too...

speaker: Helga
content: But I can't die. You all told me to keep living, so I did. Lived a long time now. In a world like this, how many get to my age? I owe you all for that.

speaker: Helga
content: So I listened. I'll live. I have to live.
The young man doesn't glance behind. He becomes a blur of motion, legs driving him forward with a speed that seems to outpace the bullets.
female_content: The young woman doesn't glance behind. She becomes a blur of motion, legs driving her forward with a speed that seems to outpace the bullets.

content: Keep up with him, Helga tells herself. This time, keep up.
female_content: Keep up with her, Helga tells herself. This time, keep up.

speaker: Helga
content: So I kept on living. Met all sorts along the way. So many remind me of you. The good parts, sure, but the stubborn streaks even more... Thinking of that, I just can't stay mad at them.
He stumbles forward, and for a moment, his silhouette merges with the memory of theirs.
female_content: She stumbles forward, and for a moment, her silhouette merges with the memory of theirs.

speaker: Helga
content: It finally clicked... so many kids in this world are just like you. And they'll be everywhere, always.
One could ask him a thousand times why he presses on, and hear a thousand different answers. But behind them all lies the same truth:
female_content: One could ask her a thousand times why she presses on, and hear a thousand different answers. But behind them all lies the same truth:

content: Because there is still something in this world worth hoping for.

speaker: Helga
content: Yeah... I've lived a long life. It'll end one day.

speaker: Helga
content: Fraser, DisCity, these farland camps, all those little towns I never heard of... they'll all be gone someday too.

speaker: Helga
content: ...But even then, someone'll still be walking this road.
Reload. Aim. Fire. Again.

speaker: Helga
content: Before I'm too old to go on, I'll make sure these kids keep walking, straight on forever! I'll make damn sure this road never ends!
One more shot. The Corruptor ahead convulses and falls silent, its form parting the viscous gloom like a curtain.
—You're there. The last charge is set. You turn, and the soft beep in your ear begins its fatal cadence.
You can't stop yet. Your body screams—fire in the chest, grating joints, salt in the eyes—but you run.
Behind you, the world erupts.
The blast swallows sound. Yet the rugged highland terrain beneath your feet firms into an unnatural smoothness, as if a road laid down by the fallen.
It carries you, steadfast, through the rain of cinders.
<size=44><color=#fb9259>Alsa Highlands has been purified.</color></size>
But you must not stop. You run, with everything you have, until—

Until it feels as though you have run through four decades in one gasping moment. The mist dissolves, and sunlight reveals the elder woman before you: her hair returning to its youthful hue, her scars fading from sight.
Until you are looking into eyes that are young again, alight with a hope not yet worn down by years.
The young woman with frayed sleeves offers a hand and pulls you up.
Her lips part, and she speaks.
"I wish you a long road ahead."
On the outskirts of Eastside, wild grass runs rampant. A few drab, weathered buildings hunch silently under the midday glare.
Quick, measured footsteps approach and then stop dead outside an abandoned factory. Without a word, the pursuit team leader signals, and the squad dissolves along the wall, melting into position.

You press against a pillar by the door. In your earpiece, nothing but a thin static hiss. From an old residential block nearby, a TV news report leaks through the silence, its voice fraying in and out.

speaker: News
content: ...Eastside's academic community has been rocked by yet another scandal. Renowned scholar Professor Morris has been taken into custody by the Public Security Bureau, formally charged with years of academic fraud. According to sources, a whistleblower has provided multiple news outlets with a complete body of evidence, including photographs, audio recordings, and comparative data analysis...
Behind you, the squad holds its breath, dark muzzles trained on the rusty iron door. Even through its thick bulk, you can feel clearly the restless Mania energy churning on the other side.
The team captain flashes you a signal, fingers curling into a fist. All exits sealed.
You answer with a flat palm held low, then slice it quietly forward.

speaker: You
content: Copy. On my signal.

speaker: News
content: ...Morris has since provided authorities with the names of multiple individuals involved in the case. Among those mentioned repeatedly is a mysterious supplier operating under the alias "Pixel." Sources familiar with the matter indicate that this individual has long been active on the dark web, with an extensive range of services...
You raise your hand.

speaker: You
content: Three, two...

speaker: News
content: ...The true identity of "Pixel," however, remains a mystery. Some believe the suspect is an individual deeply familiar with Eastside's academic community and highly skilled with the internet. Others suggest the alias may not belong to a single person, but could instead be an outsourcing front for an entire organization...

speaker: You
content: One! Breach!
Bam!
The iron door crashes down. In the same instant, the squad pours into the factory under the cover of smoke, weapons raised, all trained on the figure at the center of the room.

speaker: Eugene
content: Freeze! Drop everything. Hands where I can see...

speaker: Eugene
content: Wha—?!
The acrid smoke thins and the room sharpens. And the captain's warning dies mid-sentence, like a duck strangled silent.

At the center of the room, hunched over a battered computer, is someone who looks exactly like Pixel's online avatar from the case file. She hears the commotion and, after a stiff delay, creaks her head around.
A girl's body, topped with a computer head. Unsettling doesn't quite cover it. Where a face should be, a screen glows and stutters, endlessly flickering.

She spots the squad, and her pixel features cycle through expressions in quick succession: [startled], [confused], then [shocked]. You stare at her, and she... and the pixel dots on the screen stare back.
No time to process. You unleash the shackles on this high M-Value threat without hesitation. Just as relief begins to settle in your chest at the clean capture, she moves.

speaker: Pixel
content: Don't kill me! Don't kill me!

The computer head girl hits the floor with a thud, then scrambles over on all fours and latches onto your leg. Her screen strobes through a frantic carousel of weeping pixel faces, while her very human body writhes and clings. The whole scene feels less like an arrest and more like stumbling onto the set of a horror film.

speaker: Pixel
content: I'll talk! I'll tell you everything! Three deposits this afternoon, that's all I took! I told those fossils I was totally trustworthy, but the whole time I was recording every single word!

speaker: Pixel
content: The files are all on this computer. Except it's dead, because I dropped potato chip crumbs in the fan and the whole thing, hard drive included, just decided to explode! But my backup folder! My backup folder is called "Little Girl and the Digital Werewolf." Romantic, right? A little sci-fi, a little tragic? You have to admit it's got flair.

speaker: Pixel
content: I've read manga with this exact plot... Ah! I am cooperating! I'm the most cooperative! Please don't kill me, I'm begging you. When you really think about it, I'm just a monitor. A screen with legs!
The nonsense keeps spilling out. Incoherent, erratic, scared witless and utterly unhinged... Is she really a high M-Value Sinner?
You watch the so-called mysterious broker thrash across the floor, wailing from her throat and her screen in stereo. Words fail you. Only one thought remains:
...No way this lunatic is Pixel. The Pixel who could upend everything in Eastside academia... You've got to be kidding me...
The guards march Pixel to the interrogation room and shove her into the chair. Her mouth hasn't stopped running the entire way.

speaker: Pixel
content: So your elevator, is it encrypted? Because I tried to ping a signal when the doors opened, and it didn't just block me. It bounced me right back! Internal comms, right? What happens during a blackout? Do you get a private elevator, Chief? A sea-view suite up on the twenty-eighth floor, very corporate president chic?

speaker: Pixel
content: What's the official policy on housing Sinners? Am I staying long? Asking for my screen, mostly. The lighting in here is very hostile to my color calibration. I'm a warm-tone girl, honestly, and this place is all cold fluorescents. If I start flickering or getting dead pixels, does the Bureau cover repairs?

speaker: Pixel
content: Oh! And this chair! The texture is amazing. Seriously, my studio is desperate for a chair like this. My last one had a screw that just quietly gave up on life, and one day I went for a dramatic roll backward and, bam, total wipeout!

speaker: Pixel
content: See this? This dent right here on my head? That was the floor's fault... Took me forever to find a matching paint!
You sit across the table and watch her performance in silence. The case file from the Public Security Bureau lies open before you.

Professor Morris's scandal didn't unravel from within. Someone leaked it straight to the press. Once the public firestorm hit, all the usual academic damage control became impossible. The Public Security Bureau had to step in under full public glare and make the arrest fast.

During interrogation, Morris flipped. Hoping to reduce his sentence, he coughed up a long list of names. Pixel's was on it. A preliminary check flagged her as a suspected Sinner, so the case was transferred to you.

Tucked inside the case file is a photo, a screenshot from the dark web chat interface. The account's avatar is a glitching monitor with a cheeky pixel art tongue-out emoji. The person wearing the monitor for a head throws a peace sign with one hand and flips the bird with the other.
Miss Pixel, please mind yourself. I'm the one asking questions here. You're not running a Q&A about MBCC.
You slap the file down on the table and cut through her rambling with a cold, level voice.
Only then does she seem to remember where she is. The pixel expression on her screen stutters once and flips to an innocent smile.

speaker: Pixel
content: Oh, don't be so grumpy. I'm being super cooperative right now.

speaker: Pixel
content: Pixel! That's the full thing, no surname. But you can mix it up if you want. Pix-el. Pi-xel. Pixe-l. They all work. Each one's got a different vibe, right? All easy to remember.
Stay on topic. What are you wearing on your head?
Her screen responds instantly. The pixel expression flips to a heart, with pink bubbles floating up in a steady stream.

speaker: Pixel
content: It's a statement piece. Modern art. It's called symbolism, maybe you've heard of it? This is my tribute to the father of the Internet. Bless that man. Without him, how would I ever express the full spectrum of my dazzling personality with such precision?
...Tell me about your ability.

speaker: Pixel
content: Does it have to be about my ability? Because if I had to pick a position here at the Bureau, I'd want admin. Totally serious. Admin staff hear everything. They know all the secrets. Like, for example, do you ever dance in your office when your favorite team wins?

Pixel does not acknowledge that this is an interrogation. Her answers veer between irrelevant and inventively insane, delivered with total conviction. Every threat, every lure, every pressure point you push lands soft, swallowed whole like a fist into cotton. Each time you think you have her pinned, she squirms away in some new direction.
You take a breath, steady yourself, and switch tactics.
Alright. Let's talk about something else, then. Your name came up a lot in the files the Public Security Bureau sent over.
You leaf through the documents in your hand. The inventory is meticulous.

...Ghostwriting papers. Fabricating experimental data. Getting prohibited materials into university labs. Student essays, tenure reviews, quick graduation projects, long-term contraband supply... You've got your hands in everything, don't you?
That's quite the business you're running, Miss Pixel. Very full-service.
Pixel responds with a bashful little wave of her hand.

speaker: Pixel
content: Full-service? Well... I wouldn't say I do everything. But honestly? I do most things.

speaker: Pixel
content: Ghostwriting, data fabrication, sneaking restricted materials into university labs right under their noses... That's not even my core business anymore.

speaker: Pixel
content: Anybody can train a monkey to type. Two hands, a keyboard, and zero morals? Dime a dozen. The real money is in being the one who knows things and connects people.
That's why you chose to do everything online?

speaker: Pixel
content: Obviously! I mean, I did think about going offline at first. House calls, face-to-face, very boutique. But thank the father of the Internet, I went digital instead. That's where I built my modest but extremely profitable little domain!

speaker: Pixel
content: Offline is so dangerous anyway. One wrong turn and someone corners you in an alley, and then what? But behind a screen? Behind a screen I'm untouchable. Total control!
Her voice suddenly drops. The pixelated face on her screen tilts to a new angle, with light and shadow splitting across the display.

speaker: Pixel
content: No one finds me. No one catches me. That's the whole point.

You remember the file. The Public Security Bureau's preliminary investigation had already linked the name Pixel to a trail of academic cases, big and small. The client list she had cultivated over the years carried enough weight to crack the entire power structure of academia wide open.
A loose cannon like that, volatile and unpredictable. There must have been no shortage of people who wanted her gone.
I see. So you somehow stuck a computer on your head as a disguise to keep anyone from figuring out who you really are?
Pixel smacks the side of her head with a loud pop. The screen snaps back to that carefree grin.

speaker: Pixel
content: Wrong! One hundred percent wrong! It's not a disguise, it's a brand! Instantly recognizable, completely iconic! And for the last time, I. Was. Born. With. This. Computer. Head.
...You can't seriously expect me to believe that.
Pixel ignores your remark entirely. She reaches up and taps a finger playfully against the monitor at her neck. A rose colored pixel bird appears on the screen and immediately breaks into song.

speaker: Pixel
content: ♪ I'm a little bird, flying free, a soul that no one'll ever find... My virtual face became my real one, and now I float along, among the streams of data... ♪ Haha! That's a good one! A Pixel like this does whatever she wants, and no one gets to say otherwise!
Her bright voice crackles with a grainy, electronic edge. Right now, she has decided she is a machine, and the interrogation room is her stage.

You watch this strange, erratic creature drift in and out of her own world and still cannot square her with the underground legend who allegedly holds half of Eastside's academia in her palm. The file in your hands begins to feel less like fact and more like a bet someone else made.
The things Professor Morris accused you of. Did you actually do all of that?

You push the confession toward her. Plain as day, right there in ink. Morris states that Pixel provided prohibited materials and falsified data across several experiments. A final handoff was scheduled for today—the remaining materials and one critical dataset.

speaker: Pixel
content: Oh, absolutely. Every single thing you've found about me so far? All me. What he told you I did? I did it. What he didn't tell you I did? I did that too.
You narrow your eyes. A keyword in her words snags your attention.
"What he didn't tell you." What's that supposed to mean?

speaker: Pixel
content: Ahhh, well, I mean...
She spreads her hands. The pixel mouth on her screen pops open into a perfectly innocent circle.

speaker: Pixel
content: See, the professor came to me the summer before last. Referral from a regular, very hush-hush. His project was something about biochemical emissions from tiny insects. He wanted to publish in the "S" academic journal. The one where landing a paper basically makes you a god of the field overnight. You've heard of it, right, Chief?

speaker: Pixel
content: He told me if I could get him published, he'd throw in a bonus this much on top of my regular fee! And of course I said yes! Who says no to money? I'm not an idiot. But here's the thing that's been tickling my circuits ever since... Where does a university professor get that kind of funding?

Pixel mumbles to herself, ticking numbers off on her fingers, then suddenly looks up. Her monitor suddenly floods with transaction logs, billing statements, and chat records, scrolling past in an eager, relentless parade.
Miss Pixel, forgive me for cutting in. But you do realize all this evidence you're so proudly showing off works just as well to prove your own guilt, right?
Every time the gods close all the doors on me, I always find a tiny crack. You made this possible for me.
You're laying all this out for me. You want to spend the rest of your life in a cell?

speaker: Pixel
content: ...Huh?
She freezes. The pixel face on her screen lags like a bad signal, mouth hanging half open, staring at you as if her brain is still loading.
Satisfied, you ease back into your chair and change tack.

Here's the thing, though. You hand over your full client list and cooperate with the investigation, and I can put in a word for you. MBCC has always been willing to go easy on Sinners who've lost their way.

The girl's digital expression lurches from stunned to panicked, then from panicked to eager. But caught between those two frames, something else flashes, a look that is gone so fast you almost doubt you saw it at all.

The next second, she scrambles to pull up every file she has, thrusting both hands forward in offering, while her pixel face squeezes out a fawning grin so theatrical it practically dares you to believe it.

speaker: Pixel
content: Take it, take it, take it! It's all yours! Please, please, Chief, don't throw me in prison! I'm way too young for prison! I haven't even saved up enough to buy out every potato chip company in Eastside yet!

Yet something about her breathless tone and the pink bubbles swarming her screen feels off. It's too eager. Not the eagerness of fear, but of someone who has been waiting for you to say those exact words.
But you don't have time to linger on it. The name list is already on your terminal, each entry tagged with a neat service note.

Harold, Dean of Life Sciences: tenure paper ghostwriting, publication report fabrication. Lennard, Senior Professor of Theoretical Biology: prohibited lab equipment purchase, experimental data falsification. Philip, Associate Dean of the Institute of Advanced Life Studies: paper authorship for sale, student appeal management ...
It reads like a roll call of every notable name in Eastside academia, all gathered in one place.
You read on, torn between disgust and astonishment at the grime beneath those polished titles, until a single line of notes pins your gaze in place.
Your head snaps up.

options: This record right here. Is it accurate?

speaker: Pixel
content: Wittmann. The big, big name in biochemistry. Mania-contaminated biological material purchase... Ohhh, that's what grabbed you, huh?

speaker: Pixel
content: It was fairly recent, actually. He placed the order with me, but the supplier was someone else, though. I'm just the friendly neighborhood middleman.
A cold weight settles in you. This is no longer about falsified data or bought authorships. Mania-contaminated materials mean the red line has been crossed. A bomb with a lit fuse.
Do you know what he was experimenting on?
You frown, the weight of it pressing into your voice. Pixel answers with the same airy lilt she might use to comment on a sunny afternoon.

speaker: Pixel
content: How should I know? It's Mania, sweetheart, the clue's in the name!

Every alarm in your head blares at once. If Pixel is telling the truth, this man is not falsifying research anymore. He is engineering a disaster. An academic giant with access to Mania-contaminated materials, working out of an unsecured university lab. Every second that passes is a countdown.
He needs to be arrested. Now.
There is no time to waste. You file for an emergency deployment order and head to Eastside University, Pixel in tow.

For most students, this is just another ordinary day. The sun is warm, the tree-lined paths dappled with light and shadow. They cross the campus with books and laptops cradled in their arms, their faces full of the bright, untroubled future they still believe in.
Just before the lab door, Pixel stops and turns. The pixel face on her screen resolves into a knowing smile.

speaker: Pixel
content: You know what, Chief? In a place like this, you open a door thinking you're walking toward knowledge. Truth is, more often than not, you're walking straight into hell.
The unspoken thing in her words hangs in your mind, but before you can voice it, Pixel shoves the door open and steps inside.

Professor Wittmann stands at the lab bench, a titan of biochemistry known across academia, calmly organizing documents. He looks up at the intrusion. His eyes pass over you and pause on Pixel. For the briefest moment, something breaks through his composure. Then it seals over, and he is unreadable again.
You hold up your badge and identify yourself.

MBCC has received evidence of your purchase of Mania-contaminated materials. We have reason to believe you are conducting unauthorized Mania experiments. We ask that you cooperate fully with our investigation.

speaker: Wittmann
content: There must be some misunderstanding. My research has nothing whatsoever to do with Mania. You're welcome to search the lab. You won't find a thing.

He adjusts his glasses, his voice perfectly level. A faint, condescending smirk tugs at the corner of his mouth, as if your words are too absurd to dignify. Then his gaze shifts back to Pixel, and he lets out a sneer.

speaker: Wittmann
content: I know who you are. The little digital ghost. Every grubby scandal that's dragged Eastside's academic community through the mud, you've had your fingers in it somewhere. Utterly contemptible.

speaker: Wittmann
content: And now the authorities are working hand in hand with a criminal. What an extraordinary partnership. Is this how you clear your name, then? Slap together a few false accusations and drag the entire academic world down with you? What exactly are you hoping to get out of this?

Whether the Mania experiments are real is something we'll determine through our investigation. But that aside, Professor Morris gave up your name when he was taken into custody. You're implicated in the academic misconduct. That much isn't in dispute. So save the righteous indignation until after you've been cleared.

speaker: Wittmann
content: I'm aware of that. And I have already cooperated fully with the investigation. The data falsification in my research, that's something I cannot deny. But I am deeply troubled by all of this, because the matter itself...

He steps aside just enough to show what was behind him.
In the corner, a gaunt girl stands hunched in a rumpled lab coat. Her fingers knot together, knuckles blanched bone white. Her face is the color of raw plaster.
Wittmann shakes his head, his voice thickening with a show of disappointment.

speaker: Wittmann
content: How could you... falsify the work of an entire lab, just to get the results you wanted? I've told you from day one: if you want to stand in this field, first you have to stand as a person of integrity.

speaker: Wittmann
content: Of all people... I never imagined it would be you. My most dutiful, well-behaved student. And to think I only learned what you'd done when the investigators came knocking and laid every last ugly mistake out in the open.
The girl trembles uncontrollably, her lip caught hard between her teeth. No words come.
There are no words that would help. The lab drops into a heavy silence, every gaze fixed on her like a stain on a coat bleached a hundred times.

speaker: Pixel
content: Enough.

speaker: Pixel
content: Oh come on, this trick again? After all these years, you still haven't gotten sick of it?
Her voice is not particularly loud, but every syllable cuts through the room, cold and sardonic. She sounds like a completely different person from the manic girl of minutes ago.
The whole lab freezes, every head swiveling toward the strange figure with the computer head.

Pixel stands in the doorway. The pixel face on her screen holds no discernible expression, yet you can read it all the same. Contempt, loathing, and underneath... a faint trace of weariness. The way one watches a spent clown who should have exited the stage long ago.
Pixel seems delighted to have the spotlight. A cheerful chime rings out as a tiny golden lightbulb pops onto her screen.

She claps her hands, strides lightly to the center of the lab, and with one swift motion sweeps every document off the table. Then she hops onto the edge and swings her legs like a child on a park bench.

speaker: Pixel
content: Alright, everyone! You've been working so hard. How about a little break? Come play the mini-game Pixel just finished coding! No wipes, no paywalls, completely free to test. Try not to cry. It's just a developer pouring her heart and soul out for you!

A breezy, slightly off-kilter electronic jingle fills the air as Pixel extends her hands. Above her palms, white pixel cubes flicker into existence and stack themselves in neat layers, like a 3D printer weaving something out of nothing.
A vintage projector solidifies in her grip. She clicks the switch, and a curtain of light unfurls in midair.
Through the shimmering colors, crooked letters bounce into view, wobbling like pellets from a game of Snake.
Life in Academia
[Chapter One: An Ordinary Family]

This is a perfectly ordinary Eastside family. The father drives freight for a living. The mother works the counter at a convenience store. The living room walls are covered in old, ordinary stickers. Beneath the glass of the coffee table, an ordinary family photo sits pressed flat.

The only thing that does not fit is the daughter, who is anything but ordinary.
Brilliance from humble roots, they call it. Her grades are exceptional. Her mind simply works differently.

The extraordinary daughter accepts the tutoring schedule her ordinary mother has scraped together every penny to afford. She holds the secondhand textbooks, marked by her ordinary father's fingerprints.

speaker: Father
content: Just focus on your studies, alright? Make something of yourself. Your mom and I work ourselves to the bone so you don't end up like us.

speaker: Mother
content: We can't give you much. You know that. But we'll give you everything we've got. All you have to do is study hard. That's all we ask.

options: Studying is so exhausting. I give up.
You're right. I want a better life than this.

speaker: Pixel
content: Pathetic! Seriously, what else are you going to do at your age if not study? Your parents are running themselves into the ground for you, and you're just going to quit? Pick again!

speaker: Pixel
content: There we go! Now that's more like it. Your parents are giving you everything they've got. The absolute least you can do is work hard!
The day the acceptance letter arrives from Eastside's best university, her mother cries on the yellowed sofa while her father drinks himself blind, nearly tumbling beside the coffee table.
In this ordinary family, everyone is lit up with genuine joy. The girl stands in her cramped room, facing a wall of certificates curled at the edges, her heart pounding with heat.

She is proud. She is full of fire.
She believes in the world. She believes the rules are fair, that opportunity treats every competitor the same.

So what if she comes from nothing?
Even the most ordinary kid in Eastside, if she works hard enough, will get exactly what she deserves.
