She stands at the entrance of the imposing university, gazing up at the old stone halls and the crowds of brilliant young people drawn from across the globe. Not a flicker of doubt crosses her mind.
Her future is bright. She can almost touch it.
[Chapter Two: A Twist of Fate]

speaker: Doctor
content: ...Thankfully, your father's life is no longer in danger. But I need you to prepare yourself. The damage from the accident is permanent. He won't ever fully recover.

speaker: Nurse
content: Poor thing... Her mother collapsed right while I was changing her father's IV. First the accident, and now this. And she's only just started university. I don't know how she's going to manage all this on her own...
Two thin medical files are all it takes to hold one ordinary family now nearly broken in half. The girl leans against the white wall outside the inpatient ward, tears spilling silently down her face.
But this is a hospital. The one place in the world where tears mean nothing. No one stops. No one looks.
Brrriiing—

speaker: Girl
content: Hello...?

speaker: Fixer
content: Hey, you know that student loan thing you were asking about? I found something. It's a joint program between the school and an outside group, fast-tracked for top students like you. The paperwork's straightforward, and the money comes through quick. Just take it for now. We'll figure out the rest later, alright?

speaker: Pixel
content: Oh, sure, don't sign it. Great plan. Forget tuition, you don't even know where dinner's coming from tonight.

The girl never shakes her unease about the loan. In the end, she cannot bring herself to sign.

Not long after, she submits her withdrawal and returns to the cramped house on the city's edge.

She finds a job nearby. By some bitter coincidence, it is the same convenience store where her mother once worked.

She takes hold of the scanner her mother gripped through endless day and night shifts, and when the door chime rings, she looks out past the storefront.

The future she dreamed of as a child is gone. She cannot see it anymore.

speaker: Pixel
content: "I can always make more money." Oh, sure, that's the line, isn't it? And it's true! You CAN make more money, but it also goes out. And out. And out.
The loan lands in her account and douses the immediate fire. It also lights the fuse on a nightmare.
With every passing minute, the interest multiplies, feeding on itself like a parasite.

speaker: Girl
content: Yes, yes, I understand. I'll have this month's payment ready, I promise...

speaker: Girl
content: I'm sorry. Please, just two more days. My part-time job pays weekly. Just a little more time, please...
The same desperate pleas echo through her small terminal, almost every single day.
She can't bring herself to tell her parents, terrified of adding even more weight to a family already crushed by hardship. So she weeps alone in the dark, swallowing every bitter drop in silence.
[Background Flash]
[Background Flash]
[Background Flash]

From coffee shops to fast food counters, convenience stores to street corners where she hands out flyers, and tutoring sessions after school each day, she works relentlessly. Some days she bounces between four different places, sleeping less than four hours. All for when the month ends, she can receive one fewer call, speak one fewer word of pleading.
Her slipping grades tell the story plainly, yet she dares not stop. If she does, those figures will become a monster and consume her entirely.

speaker: Wittmann
content: I looked over your last coursework. It's sloppy. You barely put anything into it.

speaker: Wittmann
content: And you've been distracted in class lately. Completely somewhere else. What's going on? Are you in some kind of trouble?
Maybe it's because he's the first one in recent memory to ask her, "What's going on?" The girl suddenly cannot hold back her tears and bursts into violent sobs.

Everything comes spilling out. The pressure she has been carrying, heavy as a boulder on her chest, finally lifts as the words rush forth. She grips the professor's sleeve the way a drowning person seizes a floating straw.

speaker: Wittmann
content: ...Poor child. Something this serious, why didn't you come to me sooner?

speaker: Girl
content: I... I've let you down... I'm so sorry...

speaker: Wittmann
content: Come work in my lab. It won't be easy work, but the pay will be enough. Enough to let you drop a few of those other jobs, get some rest, and put your mind back where it belongs. You still want to study. I can see that.
The professor hands her a clean tissue so she can dry her tears.

speaker: Wittmann
content: You have a real gift for this. Given half a chance, you'll get through this and go far. I believe that.

speaker: Wittmann
content: So, what do you say?

options: Decline the offer and stick to the part-time arrangement
Gratefully accept the offer and resolve to make the professor proud

speaker: Pixel
content: An idealist. Hehehe. This isn't some feel-good web novel. You don't claw your way out of the gutter all by yourself. That's not how the real world works.

The girl knows by now that she must not be a burden to others.

A single lab position, after all, will never match the money she can scrape together from juggling multiple jobs out in the city.

She declines the professor's kindness and hurls herself back into work with reckless intensity. Her grades fall off a cliff.

At last, she cannot clear her student loans. What arrives instead is a withdrawal notice and a thin slip of paper with a diagnosis.

The night is cold, as it always is. She stands on the rooftop, watching a city full of lit windows, and sees no light that belongs to her...

speaker: Pixel
content: ...Yes, there we go. How could you not repay him? Without that man, your <color=#fb9259>future</color> wouldn't even exist.
[Chapter Three: The Boiling Frog]

Life in the lab begins unremarkably enough. She organizes data, cleans glassware, and assists the senior students in recording their experiments... Everyone is kind to her, genuinely happy to include her. For the first time, she feels like part of a real team, working together toward something.

The professor never holds back his generosity. Aware of her struggles, he places his meal card in her pocket and simply leaves it there. Occasionally, he takes the entire lab out for a proper meal, urging them to pursue their studies with dedication and build a future they can be proud of.
What she earns is now enough to meet her monthly payments. With the professor's support, she no longer bounces between jobs on an empty stomach, never knowing where her next meal will come from.
Slowly, the harrying phone calls grow fewer and farther between. At last, the girl can catch her breath. She sleeps deeply, opens her textbooks, and lets herself sink into the world of knowledge.
Until one day.

speaker: Wittmann
content: This dataset here needs a little adjustment.

speaker: Girl
content: Adjustment?

speaker: Wittmann
content: It's minor. Won't change the overall conclusions at all. But if we submit the numbers as they are, the whole team has to redo the experiment. That's a lot of time down the drain for everyone.

speaker: Girl
content: ...Okay. I'll take care of it.
Then the next time comes.

speaker: Wittmann
content: This chart needs some polishing. The review board expects cleaner-looking results than this.

speaker: Girl
content: ...I understand.
She is bent over her work, nervously making revisions, when the senior at the next station leans in. After a glance at the screen, she drops a casual comment:

speaker: Older Student
content: Oh, that? Totally standard. Mine went through five rounds of revisions last month. Data, charts, conclusions, all of it. Still got published. Nobody reads that carefully, trust me.
She says it with the offhand ease of someone talking about today's lunch menu.
After that, it's another senior student. One day, while she is organizing her experiment notes, he appears at her side and speaks in a hushed tone.

speaker: Senior
content: Hey. You're strapped for cash, right?

speaker: Girl
content: ...I'm managing.

speaker: Senior
content: Come on. You don't have to pretend. We all know the deal. Look, I've got something. Ghostwriting an undergrad thesis. Not a long one, and the research topic's pretty close to what you're already working on. The pay's enough to cover your expenses for three months. You want in?

speaker: Girl
content: But... isn't that...

speaker: Senior
content: Oh, please. It's nothing. The kid's family has money, but he's got rocks for brains. He's never graduating without help. You help him, he pays you. Everybody's happy. And honestly? We're not the only ones running this kind of thing. Everyone does it.

The words "academic misconduct" rise to her lips, but he's already strolling off with a smile. He tosses back a casual "let me know when you've thought it over," his back radiating total confidence that she'll agree.
Then comes the fourth time, the fifth, the sixth... Each time a "small problem," each one wrapped in a perfectly sensible reason.

Ghostwriting assignments and papers, falsifying lab records, helping spoiled rich kids coast their way to a degree. The seniors treated it all as a "side hustle," eagerly sending clients her way, calling it "resource sharing" and "mutual support."
As time passes by, the girl comes to realize that behind every polished result in this gleaming laboratory, there are secrets that must never be spoken.
But when she looks around, every student wears the same unmoved expression. As if all of this is not only perfectly reasonable to them, but simply how things are done.

options: Follow your conscience and leave the lab
Blend in and become a true part of the lab

speaker: Pixel
content: A conscience! How adorable. I love people with consciences! But here's the thing: conscience doesn't pay the bills. It doesn't put food on the table. So tell me, is it really worth it?

The girl knows it is wrong.

Today, it's falsifying data. Tomorrow, taking credit for someone else's paper. And the day after that?

She can't go on like this. Her student loan has already worn her spirit thin. If she steps onto this dark path as well, where will it lead?

She submits her resignation to the professor and signs a nondisclosure agreement, swearing never to reveal what happens inside that lab.

But the moment she steps outside, she sees the truth. The world has already changed.
She is right back in that hell where the numbers multiply endlessly and swallow her life whole.

speaker: Pixel
content: Not a bad choice at all. Of course, that all depends on one tiny little thing: whether they actually see you as one of them.
Yes, the professor and the seniors have all been so kind to me. I must repay that kindness. And I need the money to survive. In the end, that reasoning wins out, and the girl makes up her mind.

speaker: K.K.
content: It's just a few small adjustments. It's nothing. I was overthinking it. I don't know any better yet, that's why I got so worried. The professor has his reasons. Everyone has their reasons. This is just... how academia works.
She packs her conscience into a box, seals it tight with tape, and stows it away in a hidden corner of her heart. She tells herself she can open it later, after graduation, once the loan is paid off.
The water is just the right temperature. The frog inside has no desire to jump out. Not yet.
[Chapter Four: His "Gratitude"]

speaker: Wittmann
content: This paper is brilliant. I'm very glad I brought you onto this project.

speaker: Girl
content: Thank you... There's still a small gap in the data, though. Just give me two more weeks. Two weeks, and I can finish it. Please, give me some more time!

The girl steps out of the office, dark circles heavy beneath her eyes from sleepless nights. But she is happy. She knows that once she fills in the missing data, this paper will be her stepping stone to academia, an achievement she can truly be proud of.
Then, a week later, she sees her paper in a leading journal.
The data is immaculate. Her name appears in a forgotten corner of the page, denied even the status of corresponding author.
She rushes to the professor's office without a second thought.

speaker: Girl
content: Professor! You...
Contrary to all her expectations, he does nothing more than lift his eyes to her face.

speaker: Wittmann
content: It's just a simple exchange of interests. Is there a problem?

speaker: Girl
content: ...An exchange of interests?

speaker: Wittmann
content: That authorship has already gotten you money, strong grades, and the chance to keep studying here. You're young. Don't get greedy.

speaker: Girl
content: But that's fraud! I told you, I just needed two more weeks for the data. I could have finished it. I could have made it right. How could you just...

speaker: Wittmann
content: You want to call it fraud now? Tell me something. Were you really blind to all those "little problems" before?

speaker: Wittmann
content: You've been looking the other way this whole time, haven't you?

speaker: Wittmann
content: The only reason you're standing in my office right now is that this time, the "little problem" finally cost you something. Isn't that the truth?
She tries to speak, but her voice fails her.
She can't remember walking out of that office. All she recalls is the hallway, impossibly long, and the way she had to drag every ounce of herself just to get through it.
The professor's final words stay with her, ringing louder than any of those harrowing phone calls:

speaker: Wittmann
content: You really don't know how this works? Everyone does it. No one has their hands clean. Do you honestly think every paper in the top journals holds up if you look too close? Do you think those esteemed, distinguished scholars you look up to have never done worse?

speaker: Wittmann
content: Welcome to the real world, kid.

speaker: Wittmann
content: If you're still set on reporting me, go right ahead. But understand something: you had a hand in that falsified data. We've been in the same boat for a long time now.

speaker: Wittmann
content: I go down, your graduation goes with me. I stay safe, you stay safe.

speaker: Wittmann
content:
A win-win. That's the smart choice, isn't it?
And you've always been a smart girl. I know talent when I see it.

options: Refuse to accept this and report him
Agree with him and let it go

speaker: Pixel
content: Told you so. Blow the whistle and you go down right alongside him. And look! Here comes your payback, right on schedule!

The girl compiles all the evidence she has and hands it over to the authorities.

On the day she is taken away, she sits in the police car with her hands concealed beneath her jacket, the sound of the handcuffs rattling her senses.

Then one day, inside the detention center, she hears the news update on the television about the academic fraud investigation:

"Investigation concludes Professor B is innocent of all charges. A student maliciously fabricated claims of academic misconduct as an act of revenge..."

In that moment, the world spins and sends her straight into hell.

speaker: Pixel
content: The boiling frog should be dead by now.

She goes back to the lab and resumes the work that fills her with disgust.
Day by day, she becomes as numb and mechanical as the instruments around her.

A slow hatred takes root. She hates the data sheets and beakers in her hands. She hates the professor, the seniors, the spoiled rich kids who buy their way through school with purchased papers and fabricated assignments. She hates the corruption of academia. And she hates her own powerlessness even more.
The studies she once loved, and the work she had hoped would speak for her, now nauseate her at a single glance.

What is it she truly needs? A graduation certificate? But if every achievement behind it is fabricated, what does that certificate even mean? A costly testament to her sins, a mark she will carry forever, reminding her that her life is forever tainted?
Sleep abandons her. She lies awake night after night, watching forged data and manipulated charts float past her mind's eye.
Occasionally, she jolts upright, then sinks back down in defeat.
What difference would it make now?
[Chapter Five: The End of Everything]
Then one day, police cars roll onto campus. The lab doors are sealed with tape, and the professor is led away.

She stands among the onlookers, watching, a dark joy stirring inside her.
Just as she had believed when she was young, justice would find its way.
Yet the trial never comes to pass. Instead, she is called into an office and made to sit before a panel of investigators.

speaker: Investigator
content: You were the professor's assistant, yes? You processed the data. Your name is on that paper. We've spoken with your fellow students, and they've confirmed your involvement.

speaker: Investigator
content: Is there anything you'd like to add?

Anything she'd like to add? Of course she has something to say. She has plenty to say. But when she seeks out witnesses to stand beside her, each one lowers their gaze and retreats into the shadows like a rat vanishing into its hole, refusing to utter a single word.

speaker: Classmate
content: Sorry, I was just helping out here and there. Whatever was going on between you and the professor, I wouldn't know anything about that.

speaker: Roommate A
content: Sorry. I got into grad school. I have to move out basically right now. The program's starting early. Let's catch up another time.

speaker: Roommate B (Phone)
content: "Beep... Beep... The number you have dialed is currently unavailable. Please..."

She ends the call, and the phone slides from her fingers. Beyond the window, graduating students stroll under the shade of the trees, their laughter bright, their eyes fixed on the future. She remains in the gloom of her dormitory, the door closed on her from the outside, abandoned to her own helplessness.
In the end, everyone else gets what they wanted.
It turns out she is the one they can throw away at any time.
An official reprimand. Withdrawal procedures. Her name placed on the academic blacklist and on the permanent exclusion rosters of every university that matters.
The whole machinery grinds through in under three days, swift as though the outcome had been decided long before. She is shoved along every step of the way, powerless to resist.
One last time, she sits down at her computer and logs into the campus system.

She only finds her student ID revoked, her inbox and the academic database no longer accessible.
All those sleepless nights spent compiling data. Every sentence she carefully typed. The works she poured her heart into that were eventually published under another's name...
University Website Notice [You don't have permission to access this resource.]
She stares at those words, then opens her personal folder to find rows of files turned gray.
The cursor pulses on the screen like a sneer, ridiculing her for ever daring to reach so high.
She begins copying the file names into a memo, one after another, as if this small act might leave some trace of her behind. But midway, her fingers fall still.
What's the point?
These things were never hers, not from the very start.

A pressure builds in her chest, hot and burning, threatening to tear her apart from the inside. Her hands shake above the keys. Then she does what the girl she once was would never have had the courage to do.

options: Smash it all and get out of here!
Smash it all and get out of here!
Smash it all and get out of here!

content: She grabs the keyboard and slams it into the screen.

The thunderous impact cracks through both, sending shards scattering in every direction. Then she grabs the monitor and throws it to the ground, picks up the chair, and swings. Once. Twice. Three times.
Her mind is empty through it all, save for one circling thought: she is already expelled, already has nothing, already free from ever having to be the good student again.
Out in the corridor, someone glances through the half-open door and stares with a mixture of shock and disdain. The old her would have been crushed by that look. Now, she only thinks it is absurd.

speaker: Girl
content: The hell are you looking at? What, never seen a crazy person before?

After she has destroyed everything within reach, she stands panting amid the ruins and realizes her hand is bleeding. Perhaps the glass got her, or a flying shard of plastic. She looks down at it for a moment, then raises that bloodied hand and flips off what remains of the computer.

speaker: Girl
content: Don't have permission? **** you!

Her reflection stares back from the broken monitor, split into jagged fragments. She looks at those scattered pieces of herself for a long moment, then breaks into laughter.
A sense of relief washes over her, pure and unlike anything she has ever known.

On the day she carries her luggage out through the school gates, the weather is impossibly fine. Sunlight drapes itself over the magnificent entrance, the ancient buildings, the students strolling past with futures shining in their eyes.
Inside the library, heads are bent over books. The labs glow with relentless light. Everything remains so orderly, so lovely, so full of promise.

And she, standing beyond the iron gates, takes it all in and begins to laugh. A small sound at first, then swelling until it racks her body. She bends at the waist, tears spilling down her cheeks, unable to separate the laughter from the weeping.

speaker: Girl
content: Fairness. Justice.

speaker: Girl
content: Hard work changes your fate.

speaker: Girl
content: A ladder to climb. A sanctuary of knowledge.
What pretty words they are. Each one glitters. Each one fills people with longing.
But what is the truth?

The truth is that rules, power, and interest are interlocked, fitted together like a perfectly engineered machine. Those seated high above are the operators. Ordinary people are nothing but parts. A part wears out, it gets replaced. It outlives its use, it gets discarded.

They spin those beautiful lies and illusions so people believe that effort will be rewarded, that everyone has equal opportunities. All so people will stay a dutiful little part, squeezed dry, used up, and cast aside.
When the laughter fades at last, she straightens her back and glances over her shoulder at the campus one final time. At that instant, something detonates deep within her.
She majored in biochemistry. She knows perfectly well what Sinners and their awakened powers are.

And then it hits her. That power might be the only crack in this seamless system, the one opening an ordinary person can pry apart. It is the thing those above cannot fully command, the final chance bestowed by fate upon a scapegoat.

speaker: Girl
content: If being the good little rule-follower gets you nothing...
She tightens her fist, and blood begins to seep between her fingers. Her face no longer carries fear, nor hesitation, nor the torment of wondering whether what she does is right.

speaker: Girl
content: Then fine. A lunatic it is.

speaker: Girl
content: Everything you took from me, I'm taking back. This whole machine that ate me alive, along with countless others like me... I'm going to tear it apart until there's nothing left!
Crack.

The projection cuts out without warning.
When you turn, you see that the projector in Pixel's hand is already crumbling.

speaker: Pixel
content: Whoops! So sorry, but the rest is premium content. Gotta pay to unlock.

speaker: Pixel
content: There's way juicier stuff ahead! Want to see how a total nobody pulls off the ultimate comeback? How she grows to power and declares war on the entire rotten academia all by herself? Want a front-row seat while she schemes and plots and drags those high-and-mighty types off their pedestals, one by one by one?

speaker: Pixel
content: Then head over to the platform and smash that subscribe button! Officially launching next quarter, crowdfunding link in the description, and don't forget to like, comment, and share!

speaker: Wittmann
content: You... you...
Wittmann's lips tremble. He jabs a finger at Pixel and stammers:

speaker: Wittmann
content: You lunatic! You're insane! How are you still alive?! You... you're...

He tries to speak, reaching deep into his memory for that name. Yet the depths are crowded with too many students he has cast aside and forgotten, their faces worn away beyond recognition. Pixel cocks her head, and her pixel mouth twists into a mocking curve.

speaker: Pixel
content: What's wrong? Can't quite place the name? Yeah, that tracks. When you've gone through so many students, stepping stones, sacrificial lambs, tools you toss the second they've outlived their usefulness... how could one insignificant little me possibly stand out from the pile?

speaker: Pixel
content: But that's okay! You know how it is at a grand royal ball. Nobody ever dares call the queen by name! Give it enough time, and people might forget what she was called, but they will never, ever forget what she did. Isn't that right?

Her screen lights up with an emoji crying with laughter. The girl skips about, all smiles, chattering without pause. So when she pulls out her gun and pulls the trigger, not a single person sees it coming.
"Bang!"

speaker: Students
content: AHHHH! She has a gun!
The lab fills with shrieks in an instant. You quickly stand between the students and Pixel while reaching out one hand to Pixel, desperate to halt her madness in its tracks.
You don't have to do this, Pixel! I'll make sure he answers for what he did, all of it. I swear. But if you pull that trigger right now, the case dies with him!

speaker: Pixel
content: Oh, Chief. You're really underestimating me.

speaker: Pixel
content: Let's say I give you every benefit of the doubt. Let's say you really are different from the rest of them. One good person in this world, in this circle? That's not nearly enough. Not even close.

speaker: Pixel
content: He goes in, he pulls some strings, calls in a few favors, and walks right back out. You know it. I know it.

speaker: Pixel
content: You think I haven't once tried believing in justice? After all these years?
Pixel grows more and more frantic as she talks, her entire frame shaking. Her display flickers wildly in response, breaking apart into waves of distortion, glitch lines, and fractured pixels.

speaker: Pixel
content: Enough! I said enough! I am done! Done with all of it! Ahh!

Possessed by frenzy, she pulls the trigger again and again, bullets tearing through the lab without aim. Reagent bottles explode under the onslaught, spewing corrosive fumes and burning liquid into the air.
The fire alarms shriek instantly, and the chaos spills out of the laboratory, consuming the entire research building.
Pixel, stop!
You chase after her, cutting hard around the corner of the corridor until she finally falls within the shackles' reach.
As you lift your hand, the shackles stretch silently toward the staggering figure with the computer head. Yet just before they can touch her, she lets out a startled cry and tumbles to the floor.

You throw yourself forward and grab her by the collar. Her head snaps up, and suddenly her computer head and that flashy patchwork coat disintegrate into a cloud of white pixels, scattering into nothing.
The figure now clutched in your hands is not Pixel at all, but the girl Wittmann used as a scapegoat in the lab. She huddles on the floor, pale as ash, her lips quivering.
You go still. Is this Pixel's power, or just an illusion? You glance back over your shoulder. The corridor behind you stands empty. No pursuers. Nothing but the fire alarm wailing on.
It's you... What's going on?!

The girl no longer struggles to escape. She raises her gaze, and in her eyes is not only fear but something indefinable, the expression of a person who has cut off every path of retreat and has nothing left to lose.

speaker: Girl
content: Pixel got in touch with me before you arrested her.

speaker: Girl
content: She said once you had a lead on those Mania materials, I'd be the one they threw under the bus the second you showed up. She said... why just sit there waiting to take the fall, when I could help her put on a little show and take that bastard down instead.
...Then how did you pull all that off? The computer head, the outfit, all of it?

speaker: Girl
content: I don't know exactly. One second we were surrounded by all these white pixel blocks, just appearing out of nowhere, and the next... we'd switched. She told me to run this way. Said you'd follow me for sure.

Your grip loosens, and a short silence settles between you. What the girl describes reminds you of the projector you witnessed earlier. Pixel's ability, you realize, must be the power to print objects into existence from nothing.
During the chaos, she exchanged her conspicuous appearance with this girl. One body to lure you off, another to slip away. A remarkably clever tactic.

Your mind races. The anonymous informant who first flagged Professor Morris. Pixel, who surrendered herself so easily into your custody. The casual way she dropped clues about Wittmann's Mania research during interrogation.

Each moment was calibrated perfectly, each one steering you precisely where she wanted. The entire thing had been orchestrated from the start. She was fishing, and you were nothing more than the line she threw into the water.

speaker: Girl
content: I'm sorry for tricking you. If you need to arrest someone, just... arrest me.
The girl keeps her head down, her voice muffled. But you have no time to waste here, so you press her urgently:
Where did she go?
The girl gives a small shake of her head.

speaker: Girl
content: I don't know.

After getting the girl somewhere safe, you tear out of the campus. The wail of the fire alarms fades into the distance, overtaken by the chaos of Eastside: voices overlapping, horns blaring, the heavy thud of bass leaking from storefront speakers.
You stop in the middle of the pedestrian street and strain your shackles to their farthest reach, searching... The thread holds. She headed west. You break into a sprint.

One street bleeds into another as you push through the crowd, shouldering past strangers amid a chorus of curses and gasps. None of it matters. The connection from your shackles flickers, faint then strong, like a strand of spider silk trembling in a gale.

You burst into Eastside's most crowded intersection. It is Friday evening, and the city has snapped to life. People surge from subway tunnels, stream out of shopping malls, and trickle from every back alley until they merge into a single endless river of bodies.

Headlights, neon, and the glow of countless phone screens dissolve into one chaotic blur. So does the noise: laughter, chatter, footsteps, and the hoarse singing of a street performer under a distant bridge. You stand at the center of it all, nearly swept off your feet by the tide.
You stare at the faces flowing past you, every one painted with a different emotion, shifting and multiplying like the pixel expressions on Pixel's screen.
Then realization strikes. The connection from your shackles has not vanished. There are just too many of them—

From all sides, from everywhere at once, countless searing threads burst up through the ground and twist around your ankles, your wrists, your throat. Each one screams for attention, each one tugs toward a different destination. You fight to isolate a single thread, but the harder you struggle, the more tangled they become.
Dropping into a crouch, you sweep your hand across the chilly ceramic rim of a planter bed. Your fingers snag on a tiny, rigid object. You pluck it from the ground and hold it up to your eyes.

It is a scrap of plastic no bigger than a fingernail, warped and crude, its edges rough with the ridges of printed layers. Stamped upon it is a pixel smiley face with mismatched eyes and a grin stretching border to border. A whisper of Mania still lingers on its surface.
This is her power, her mark, her... taunt.
You straighten up and look around.

There, on a sticker plastered to a lamppost. On the handle of a public trash bin. Inside the basket of a bicycle left by the curb. Wedged into the cardboard sleeve of a milk tea cup held by a couple strolling past...

This Friday evening, along Eastside's most crowded street, Pixel's "presents" lie scattered around every unsuspecting soul. Strewn carelessly across every visible and hidden surface, each one burns with her unmistakable trace, each one hurls the same loud taunt:
"Catch me if you can!"

Your fist tightens around the plastic fragment, its sharp edge pressing into your palm. The crowd surges past like a relentless tide. You stand at the city's most clamorous crossroads, a solitary rock battered by the current.
Lost, you search the faces streaming by. Strangers. Ordinary faces. Faces with no ties to yours, forgotten the instant they pass.
Some smile. Some furrow their brows. Some hide behind headphones, expressionless. One by one, you study them, hunting desperately for something, anything, you recognize.
Then the truth settles over you. You were never going to find her.
Because at this moment, Pixel needs no elaborate trick. She simply has to remove the computer head from her shoulders and vanish into the crowd with a face no one has ever laid eyes on.

She could be any of them. The girl scrolling idly through her phone. The woman hurrying past with bags in both hands. The student kneeling to retie a shoelace. She might even be the stranger who just slipped by you, shoulder grazing your arm.
And you would never recognize her.

speaker: You
content: I lost. I can't find you anymore.
The words leave your lips in a whisper, only to be devoured instantly by the roar of the city, leaving nothing behind.
In the days that follow, the Bureau presses on with its investigation into Pixel.
You had already glimpsed her past through that game demo, but records can be erased. A person who once walked this earth, however, cannot help but leave marks behind.
A faded attendance sheet pulled from the dust-choked archives. Shards of recollection coaxed from a retired professor's mind. A name crammed into the margins of an old paper's author list...

Slowly, painstakingly, as if piecing together a puzzle torn to scraps and scattered to the wind, you assemble the portrait of a girl named <color=#fb9259>Lucy</color>. And at last, you find her parents' address.
Old Residential District, Eastside Outskirts

They say this neighborhood was marked for demolition years ago. But the ones who live here are too poor to make a life anywhere else, even with a payout, so the plans gather dust and the people gather years, left behind as Eastside pushes on without them.

Grey plaster peels in cracked sheets. Cobblestones jut at odd angles. Roof tiles are split and seeping. Children in ill-fitting hand-me-downs race through the alleys, laughing, blowing tiny bubbles from jars of homemade soap water, and a row of parked bicycles clatters to the ground behind them.
You stand before a rust-flecked iron door, your hand hovering over the buzzer before you finally press it. Nothing. The bell is dead. You rap your knuckles against the metal instead.

The woman who opens the door carries the weight of decades she has not yet lived. Liver spots bloom across her skin, and her fingers are thick-knuckled, worn into that shape by cold water and detergent. Behind her, a man limps into view, a scar tracing a long, pale path from his wrist up into the dark of his sleeve.
Hello. I'm...

speaker: Woman
content: Oh! You must be ${PlayerName}, the friend Lucy told us about! Come in, come in, don't just stand there!

speaker: Man
content: Sit, sit. I'll go get some fruit. Make yourself comfortable.

The man limps as he leads you in, his right leg dragging behind him as though it no longer answers to him. Then he and the woman squeeze into the cramped kitchen, his body leaning hard to one side with every step.

You let your gaze wander. The wallpaper is yellowed and peeling, and the walls carry the faint, stale scent of rain-soaked plaster that never fully dried. Curling, faded award certificates still cling to the living room wall. On the screen of the old television, a crooked handmade sticker reads, "A bright future ahead."
A chip mars one corner of the coffee table glass, and from it, a web of cracks spreads outward, stopping just short of a row of family portraits. In them, a girl grows up frame by frame.

A scrunched-up newborn cradled in loving arms. A child with pigtails, proudly holding a certificate between her parents. A young woman in a graduation gown, her arms draped over their shoulders, her eyes squeezed shut with joy.
The woman fills your cup with tea, then slides the plate of fruit a little closer.

speaker: Woman
content: Here, have some tea. Help yourself to the fruit.

speaker: Woman
content: The road out here's not easy. It rained a couple days ago and almost washed part of it out. I told my husband, don't go messing around out there, but he wouldn't listen. Went and found some bricks, laid them down himself. Said he didn't want his girl stepping in puddles when she came home.
She says it like a reproach, yet a smile lingers in her eyes. The man drinks his tea in silence, offering no words, but the corner of his lips betrays the faintest movement.

speaker: You
content: Does she... come home often? For the holidays?

speaker: Woman
content: Oh, she's been so busy ever since she graduated. There's always something.

speaker: Woman
content: We weren't well enough to make it to her graduation, either of us. So she mailed her diploma home so we could see it. And she gave us a bank card too, saying she wanted to send her salary back every month.

speaker: Woman
content: We don't really know what she does at that research company, exactly. She's just... always working. I ask her if she's eaten and she never answers at mealtimes. Sometimes it's almost midnight, and her dad and I are missing her, so we try calling. But she's either still at work or already passed out. Getting her on a video call... it's been impossible.
The man beside her gives a nod. At the mention of his daughter, a tangled look crosses his face. Pride, certainly, but also longing and a tender worry.
He is a quiet father, the kind who speaks through silence. His fingers fidget with his teacup, his eyes wandering from the certificates on the wall to the family photo of the three of them.

Too busy with work. The project is at a crucial stage. The holiday is too short to justify the trip home... One hollow excuse after another, and yet somehow they were enough to sustain the image her parents clung to: a good daughter to be proud of.

What could you possibly tell them now?
That their girl is a wanted Sinner who just opened fire on someone?
That the child they have been so proud of their entire life was already crushed beyond recognition by a pitiless world, broken the moment they fell sick all those years ago?
In all this time, did even a whisper of what she endured ever reach their ears?
But the words refuse to leave your lips.

The dark spots blooming on the woman's skin. The long scar tracing the man's forearm. The tea still warm in its cup. The awards still hanging on the wall, faded and curling at the edges, too precious to ever take down. This family clings to the illusion of that good daughter. It has been the sole light guiding them through the long darkness.
They cannot survive another storm.

You open your mouth, but the words will not form. Instead, you lift the teacup and drink in silence. The liquid is bitter at first, yet as it slips down, the faintest hint of sweetness blooms at the back of your throat, so subtle you almost miss it.
When the time comes to go, the woman pulls open a drawer and retrieves an envelope, placing it gently in your hands.

speaker: Woman
content: A few days ago, she told me a friend of hers would be coming by. Asked me to give this to you.

speaker: Woman
content: If you see her... tell her to eat properly, will you? Real meals, not just whatever's quick. And to put on a coat when it's cold.

speaker: Woman
content: And tell her... come home when she has time. Come home when she's tired. That her mom and dad will always be here for her.
You promise her you will.
Only later, seated in the car as the city scrolls past the window, do you finally tear open the envelope.

speaker: Pixel
content: Hey, my dear Chief! Thanks for checking on my folks!

speaker: Pixel
content: I'm sorry I lied to you. I put on quite the show, and it was all to use you. I just wanted to feel like I'd gotten something back, some small revenge, some tiny repair, for a life that's already ruined. I wanted "Lucy" to finally get a piece of the justice she was owed.

speaker: Pixel
content: I've seen you working these past days, digging into "Lucy's" past, clearing charges that never should have stuck. I've seen all of it. Thank you. (That's right. I've been watching from the shadows this whole time! Here's your reward: one Pixel doodle sticker!)

speaker: Pixel
content: I know someone like you will catch me eventually. So here's my deal: don't come after me just yet, alright? I still have so much left to do. I need to keep hiding in the dark, shining a light on the things no one else dares to say out loud.

speaker: Pixel
content: Once I've dragged every last one of them out, once the system that let all this happen has been torn down, once the students underneath it all can stop being afraid, can chase what they want and get what they deserve... I'll come back on my own. I'll face whatever judgment you have for me.

speaker: Pixel
content: In the meantime, let me be your eyes. I'll go where you can't see and talk to people you can't reach yet. I'll walk through every dark corner for you until the sun falls where it was always supposed to, on every inch of ground the shadows have swallowed, and on every page that was always meant to be clean.

speaker: Pixel
content: (Oh, and I have a little gift for you! This list is real, I promise. Every name is tied to Mania research. So get moving and round them up, my dear Chief!)
A tiny chip is fastened to the bottom of the letter.

Now you see why Pixel spoke so pointedly about the importance of academic connections. Operating as a supplier and fixer in the underground, she has gained access to all of this with ease. And now, with solemn faith, she entrusts it to you.

You flip the letter over. On the back, one last line waits.
The paper around it is faintly wrinkled, as if a drop of water had once landed there and long since dried.

speaker: Pixel
content: Did she make you tea? Have some extra cups for me. My mom makes the best tea in the world.
Beyond the window, twilight settles over Eastside. One by one, the streetlamps awaken, weaving a slender chain of light that reaches toward a vanishing point far beyond sight.
You press your lips together gently. The faint sweetness of the tea still lingers in your mouth, as if a silent greeting had traveled across an impossible distance just to reach you.
Perhaps next time, she can be the one to go home and drink that tea herself.

"La... la la... la..."
The girl hums softly in the darkness. The intermittent notes echo across the silent interrogation room.

speaker: Victoria
content: It's the Chief! Cough cough...

options: Are you alright? Are you feeling unwell?
Please bear with me, the interrogation will end soon.

content: Victoria has been kept in a sterile ward for medical reasons. Maybe she's not used to the air in the interrogation room.

speaker: Victoria
content: I'm alright Chief. Don't worry...
Victoria's voice is still feeble, but it sounds like her breathing has stabilized.

speaker: Victoria
content: It's because I'm too excited to be locked in the interrogation room. I couldn't catch my breath for a while.

speaker: Victoria
content: Bear with you? Why do you phrase it like that?
The interrogation room is not as hygienic as the sterile ward you were in. I take it that you're a bit uncomfortable here?

speaker: Victoria
content: Sorry for making you worry, Chief, but Victoria isn't that weak... cough cough...

speaker: Victoria
content: It's because I... I'm too excited to be locked in the interrogation room. I couldn't control my breath for a while.
People are usually nervous and frightened to be interrogated one-on-one like this.

speaker: Victoria
content: What is there to be nervous about?
She smiles and looks around.

speaker: Victoria
content: A confined space, a room full of monitoring equipment... this all must mean that you love me, Chief.
Love?
Of all the Sinners you've encountered, few used such warm, sentimental terms.

speaker: Victoria
content: That's right. "Love" is an apt word to describe someone who uses everything at their disposal to guard another like a caged bird...
She utters these absurd words with a calm, matter-of-fact tone.
These so-called expressions of "love" correspond to Victoria's abnormal behaviors.
test

speaker: Complaint from Medical Dept
content: "Victoria added several bottles of liquid dietary supplement to my plate when I was away from the dining table. She refused to apologize when I found out, and even tried to spoon-feed me the food..."

speaker: Report from Security Dept
content: "Sinner No. 103 locked other Sinners in the detention room multiple times, using the blood crystals produced by her ability to block the keyholes."

speaker: Nightingale's advice
content: "She exhibits violent tendencies and attacks staff members with discarded syringes for no apparent reason. We recommend for her to be immediately expelled from the sterile ward and placed in confinement as punishment."
Victoria listens carefully to every accusation. To your incredulity, she looks pleased and relieved.

speaker: Victoria
content: Finally, the actions I dedicate to "love" are being recognized!
Dedicate? Love? I don't understand.

speaker: Victoria
content: That's fine. One day you'll understand. See, Sis Nightingale said I need to be locked up. Isn't that a response to my love?

speaker: Victoria
content: Dedication begets rewards. Soon, I'll be surrounded by love again...
Immersed in her own thoughts, she simply babbles to herself in circles. For someone in this state of mind, it is pointless to pursue the matter any further...
Nightingale is not responding to your "love." On the contrary, she wants me to control your behavior.
Your so-called "love" already constitutes malicious harm and unlawful detainment towards others. Your actions have caused them suffering.

speaker: Victoria
content: I don't understand what you mean, Chief... is everyone trying to reject Victoria's love?
It is as if she never expected to hear this answer. Her breathing quickens rapidly.

speaker: Victoria
content: How can it be... I... I had good intentions... why would they reject it?
Perhaps it's not a response to "love," but rather a rejection?

speaker: Victoria
content: Rejection?
Yes. Your so-called "love" inflicted harm upon others. We hope you can stop this behavior.
She frowns and ponders for a moment, still unable to understand what you mean.

speaker: Victoria
content: I don't understand... how could it be harmful... this is clearly Victoria's love...

options: You shouldn't ignore other people's feelings

content: Actions that cause others to suffer cannot be called "love" at all.
Perhaps you can express your "love" in a more acceptable way?

speaker: Victoria
content: You're lying! Cough cough...

speaker: Victoria
content:
That's what Daddy taught me!
Daddy must be right... he must be...
You've triggered an emotional outburst from her. Even though she struggles to breathe, she refuses to give you the slightest chance to refute her.

speaker: Victoria
content: Daddy... That's how he loved Victoria.

speaker: Victoria
content:
He locked me in the ward and forced me to take medicine... all kinds of medicine...
And taking injections... countless syringe holes...

speaker: Victoria
content: He... he did everything to protect me! This is love! You don't understand, none of you do! You're all wrong... only Daddy and I have the right love... cough cough!

options: So you were influenced by your father?
Calm down! Take a deep breath first

content: Your father confined you to your home and harmed you in the name of "love," so you mistook similar behavior as expressions of "love"?

speaker: Victoria
content: How can it be a mistake?! I'm the only one who understands him!

speaker: Victoria
content: Not only that, but I have come to realize even purer, more intense love on my own!

speaker: Victoria
content: ...Sigh... Never mind, you don't understand.
Victoria sighs and calms down again. She looks at you with pity in her eyes.

speaker: Victoria
content: It seems that only Daddy can appreciate my love... that feeling of being pierced in the chest—
She seems to be immersed in some warm memory. Her face flushes in an eerie and unsettling way.
The disappearance of Victoria's father, the tortured Corruptor body in the villa, the huge hole in the corpse's chest... You seem to have found answers to the remaining two pieces of evidence.

speaker: Victoria
content: That's a photo of Daddy.
Victoria affectionately refers to the tormented and disfigured creature in the evidence as her father.

options: Why did your father turn into a Corruptor?

speaker: Victoria
content: Sob... I haven't seen Daddy for a long time. Sis Anne said he went somewhere far, far away. Will I be able to see Daddy back someday?
Mesmerized by the "masterpiece" in the evidence, she ignores your question completely.
Why did your father turn into a Corruptor?
Did you kill this Corruptor?

speaker: Victoria
content: Chief, can you give me this photo? It'd be nice if this photo kept me company while I wait for Daddy to return...
You are simply talking to a wall. Victoria scrutinizes the evidence, immersed in her thoughts.

speaker: Victoria
content: But he didn't look like this before. It's all because we drank that strange medicine together to help me heal...

speaker: Victoria
content: Fortunately, there are still traces of Victoria's love in the photo. You see...here, and here... I did all this.
Like a child, she shows off the fruits of her actions to you, proudly pointing to the pills overflowing from the Corruptor's mouth and the syringes all over its body.

speaker: Victoria
content: Oh right, there's also this! Do you know what this is, Chief?
She points to the festering wound on the Corruptor's chest that spans more than ten centimeters in diameter.
Even though it's just a photo, you can practically smell the Corruptor's rotting corpse.

options: So this is your "most intense love"
These are fatal wounds that killed him

speaker: Victoria
content: See? I knew it! You can understand that this is my love, right Chief?

speaker: Victoria
content: I knew from the moment you took me to the Bureau and locked me in the interrogation room that you'd understand me! Cough cough... because Chief, you're just like Daddy, you love Victoria the same way he did!
You were the one who described it as giving your father the most intense love, I was merely following your line of logic...
Your explanation falls on deaf ears. The girl babbles excitedly to herself.

speaker: Victoria
content: Chief gave me a photo of Daddy and understood our love... what shall I do to repay you... what shall I do...

speaker: Victoria
content: Not only that, but it's also my purest love...
She shows no grief over the subject of her father's death.

speaker: Victoria
content: Look at how calm his expression is... he must be enjoying my love so much...
He's calm because he's dead...
You are already exhausted from explaining common sense over and over again, but the girl in front of you still lives in her own world.

speaker: Victoria
content: Yes, I know that Daddy will only be away from me for a little while. But I have this photo that the Chief gave me, so Victoria isn't lonely.

speaker: Victoria
content: Chief, you gave me a photo of Daddy... what shall I do to repay you... what shall I do...
No need, it's just a piece of evidence...

speaker: Victoria
content: Ah, I got it!
She interrupts you and stares straight ahead, but her pupils aren't focused on you. It's as if she is talking to the air behind you.

speaker: Victoria
content: How about I repay you with my most intense love, Chief...
Victoria bites her right hand without the slightest change on her face.
What are you doing?
A sharp blood crystal sprouts out of the wound and pierces towards you without warning!
You successfully dodge the first blood crystal, yet there's a second, then a third!
In this dark, tiny space, there is no place to hide. You feel a stinging pain as a blood crystal pierces through your left shoulder!
Sssss—
The girl with bloodied hands seems unable to hear your painful inhalation, and happily admires the new wound on your body.
You try to say something, but you're already going into limbo from blood loss. Fortunately, Adjutant Nightingale arrives promptly with help.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Quick! Stop the bleeding for the Chief!

speaker: Nightingale
content: Everyone else, take Victoria away and put her under strict lockdown! Do not give her any chance to attack the Chief!

You don't have the strength to open your eyes anymore, so you don't see Victoria's face when they escort her away. You only vaguely remember her innocent and excited tone of voice, like that of a five-or-six-year-old child.

speaker: Victoria
content: Cough cough, can you feel it now? This is the most intense love!

speaker: Victoria
content: Chief, do you... Do you love Victoria as well? Just like Daddy!
A split second before the crystal plunges into your heart, the shackles spring into action, halting the crystal an inch before you. It dissolves into liquid and splashes onto your uniform.

Victoria doesn't seem to care at all about your life hanging by a thread. She looks at the blood on your clothes in confusion, then looks at her hand. Blood gushes out of her wound, staining her entire right hand with blood.

speaker: Victoria
content: The bleeding... hasn't stopped?
She takes another bite at the original wound and extends her bloodstained right hand towards you.

speaker: Victoria
content: My blood won't turn into crystals anymore?

speaker: Victoria
content: Why did this have to happen now... I-I wanted to show the Chief my love... oh why...
She pulls and squeezes her wound, spurting more blood on her white coat, white skirt, and pale thighs. The contrast of colors is glaring.

speaker: Victoria
content: Love, my love for Chief... why is it not there any more? Cough cough cough!

options: Because the shackles have limited your abilities

content: You don't have the ability to hurt others with your blood now. I won't allow you to make more mistakes.

speaker: Victoria
content: Shackles? You used shackles on me to limit my abilities?
Yes. I prefer not to control Sinners too harshly, but given the emergency just now...

speaker: Victoria
content: Hahahaha...
She suddenly bursts out laughing, letting out a sigh of relief as she gently hugs herself with her blood-stained hands.

speaker: Victoria
content: I thought that after Daddy left, I was all alone... It turns out that this love never left.

speaker: Victoria
content:
Because I just received it—this is confinement only for me, right?
In that moment, your gaze, your thoughts, they exist for Victoria alone...
No. It's to stop you from harming others.

speaker: Victoria
content: Daddy, did you see it? Chief is keeping me company just like you did...
Her voice grows weaker and weaker. You notice that the wound on her right hand is still gushing a lot of blood.
It was just one bite. Why is it so serious?

speaker: Victoria
content: Daddy said that Victoria was a child chosen by the gods and would bleed non-stop if she got wounded.
Victoria's lips begin to turn white.
Nightingale, arrange for medical staff to treat her wounds now.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Okay. Help is on the way.

speaker: Victoria
content: You want to heal me, just like Daddy, right?... How wonderful.
Seconds after you hang up the comms system, footsteps echo outside the door.

speaker: Victoria
content: Ah... Someone... is coming to interfere with our love...

speaker: Victoria
content: No, they want to separate us again... cough cough!

The medical staff enter the interrogation room in an orderly manner. They ignore Victoria's feeble resistance and give her some basic bandaging. But when they try to take her away for further examinations, Victoria refuses to get up.

options: Persuade her to cooperate with the treatment

content: Today's interrogation is already over. You have lost a lot of blood. Go with them for some examinations. I will also restore your abilities.

speaker: Victoria
content:
So these shackles only for Victoria, they're coming to an end... Will I be interrogated again after that?
Will you, continue to imprison me?
...The source of your criminal and abnormal behavior is basically clear now. There is no need to continue the interrogation.

speaker: Victoria
content: It must be because they disturbed us. That's why you took back the shackles, right?
Victoria glances warily at the medical staff. Evidently, she is still in her own world.

speaker: Victoria
content: If it were just the two of us, our love could go on...
You misunderstood. The shackles have nothing to do with "love."

speaker: Victoria
content: I'll be waiting for you, waiting for a chance to be alone with you, waiting for you to shackle me again... just like I'll be waiting for Daddy to come back.
But Victoria, your father...
He's not coming back.
Chief... Chief?
A familiar voice wakes you up. You find yourself surrounded by darkness, your hands and feet bound by rope.

speaker: Victoria
content: Chief, you recognized my voice right away...
Victoria lowers her voice carefully and chuckles softly in your ear.

speaker: Victoria
content: Hehe, don't worry, I've sent everyone away. No one will find us here.

speaker: Victoria
content: This is a place only Victoria knows of...
She lowers her voice and chuckles softly in your ear.

speaker: Victoria
content: Don't worry, I've sent everyone away. No one will find us here.
The whispering voice in your ear drips with eerie pleasure, jolting you awake completely.

"Hiss—"
The girl lights an old mining lamp. Under the dim light, you finally see your surroundings clearly—
It is an underground depot full of cardboard boxes imprinted with MBCC logos. There is also a small cart that Faye uses to deliver goods.

speaker: Victoria
content: Shh—Nightingale thought I escaped from the Bureau and took you with me. Don't let her hear us.
What did you do?

speaker: Victoria
content: Don't be nervous, Chief. I just want to continue our unfinished business without being disturbed.

content: Did you forget? Love, shackles, imprisonment... In the interrogation room, our love was interrupted, and I lost the shackles you gave me.

speaker: Victoria
content: I waited until my body recovered, and when Sis Nightingale let her guard down, I finally found a chance to be alone with you.

speaker: Victoria
content: Come on, confine me like you did last time.
She edges closer to you step by step. You're tied to a chair with no way to escape.

content: Chief? I shouldn't have had to bother you with such a minor issue... I was negligent.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Although it's just an A-Class Sinner, the target is incredibly cunning. That kid seems aware that we wouldn't dare to escalate things in Eastside, giving us a lot of trouble.
Nightingale hands you the documents. The images captured by the surveillance camera seem familiar to you.
How did you find the child?

speaker: Nightingale
content: The sheriffs received a message from a civilian who had taken in a child who claimed to be a domestic abuse victim but then went missing in a few days. The civilian was worried something had happened to the child and contacted the sheriffs.

speaker: Nightingale
content: The sheriffs didn't take it seriously at first, but similar messages kept cropping up and more well-dressed young men and women were getting tricked. They finally had to take action.

speaker: Nightingale
content: They indeed found a child on the street that matched the description, but the child ran off at the sight of the sheriffs. During the chase, they discovered that...
The child is a Sinner who can generate very fine threads with special power.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Do you know the target?
I almost forgot about this kid... Do you remember the incident at the toy factory?

speaker: Nightingale
content: Sure... I've read your report. Was the target also involved in that...

speaker: Nightingale
content: Oh, I remembered... Oliver!
You nod and pass the documents to Nightingale.
You just mentioned that Oliver has been seeking help from well-dressed young men and women.
So we just need to match that requirement.

speaker: Oliver
content: Carrying her doll, She cries with her face covered...

speaker: Oliver
content: She has no children of her own, only a doll...
In the dim basement, where even light can hardly penetrate, a soft tune echoes like a ghost's whispers.
Crawling on the ground, the voice is very light but serious. The singer must be thinking carefully about something.
Clack!
The sound of something snapping.
The singing stops. Someone is walking, but no one is talking.

speaker: Oliver
content: Oh dear! Cousin, you're too careless!

speaker: Oliver
content: Why didn't you take good care of her, Auntie? Look, she's hurt herself again. It won't look good if it leaves a scar.

speaker: Oliver
content: Oliver hates ugly things. If you make a mistake and break my "toys", you're not a good kid anymore.

speaker: Oliver
content: Since I was little, Auntie has always told me that bad kids who don't behave will be punished.

speaker: Oliver
content: Now... You've misbehaved too. How should Oliver punish you?

speaker: Clerk
content: The investigation results from the Eastside Public Security Bureau have arrived.

speaker: Clerk
content: Chief and Adjutant Nightingale were right. Oliver does live in this house, but only returns every now and then and rarely stays for long.

speaker: Clerk
content: According to our investigation, Oliver lost both parents at a young age, and was adopted by aunt after that. This house is registered under Oliver's aunt and uncle.

speaker: Clerk
content: And they have a biological daughter, who is Oliver's cousin.

speaker: Clerk
content: But the three of them have gone missing for many years. They've stopped going to school or work.

speaker: Nightingale
content: What do their neighbors say?

speaker: Clerk
content: This is the strangest part! The neighbors speak highly of Oliver and say they are a very harmonious family.

speaker: Clerk
content: They still see the family gathering around happily every night!

speaker: Nightingale
content: If they're indeed a loving family, Oliver wouldn't need to frequently go out and ask for strangers' help, right?

speaker: Nightingale
content: There must be something more behind Oliver's relationship with the aunt's family... Chief, are you sure your plan will work?
Nightingale eyes your brand new outfit with a complicated expression.
Oliver only saw a gray rag doll in the toy factory. The kid won't recognize me like this.
I searched everywhere in the Bureau to put together this outfit. I'm sure it won't be a wasted trip for everyone.
You confirm the plan with all parties once more, and head toward the dilapidated house covered in cobwebs in front of you.
Knock, knock. The unhurried knocks on the door interrupt Oliver's pleasant reminiscence in the basement.

speaker: Oliver
content: How strange... Who would be visiting at this time...

speaker: Oliver
content: Alright, I'll be right back! Remember to behave yourselves while I'm away. Don't ruin our little secret in the basement.
Knock, knock. The person knocks again. Oliver comes to the door, a bit annoyed.

speaker: Oliver
content: Who is it? Is there something you need?
Oh, thank god, yes. Can you please help me?
I came here alone for a walk and got mugged... I gave them my phone and seized the chance to run away, but then I got lost around here.

speaker: Oliver
content: My family's not here. I'm alone...
Oliver fakes a helpless and innocent voice, seeming reluctant to open the door.
Cough, cough... I have some health issues that give me trouble breathing after running. Please, a cup of water and a place to sit will help me recover very soon.
Impatient, Oliver stands on tiptoes to look through the peephole in the door skeptically, but Oliver's expression brightens instantly at the sight of the visitor's outfit...

speaker: Oliver
content: Wow, how glamorous... Oh, I mean, please come in, sir!
female_content: Wow, how glamorous... Oh, I mean, please come in, miss!

content: You take a good look around the house.
Overall, the furnishings of the house are not much different from most ordinary families in Eastside, adequate but unremarkable.
A sturdy wooden table. Old-fashioned home appliances. Some items on the cabinets seem to have been removed, leaving only the dusty marks in their original positions.
Clearly, no one has taken care of this place for a long time. This matches the Bureau's findings.
Something does feel off here... If the aunt's family is indeed gone, why does Oliver return here so often? And what's the deal with the harmonious family the neighbors see?
But if they still live here... You carefully observe the surroundings. It's very quiet. Besides you and Oliver, you don't feel the presence of a third person.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Are you sure you don't need more support?

I'll be fine on my own. Oliver has been able to evade capture so many times, the kid must be highly vigilant. It'd look less suspicious if I go alone. I can gain Oliver's trust more easily and try to pry for more information.
If we directly take Oliver back to the MBCC for interrogation, I don't think the kid will tell the truth.
As for the peculiarity of this family, I'll have to go into the house and see for myself.
A Mania-like scent seems to permeate the space. You instinctively search for its source and glimpse a hastily closed door left ajar.

speaker: Oliver
content: What are you looking at, sir? You wanted to sit down and rest, no?
female_content: What are you looking at, miss? You wanted to sit down and rest, no?

content: Oh right... Cough, cough... I must be too tired. I'm feeling a bit dizzy...

options: Where are the adults of your family?

content: Staying alone in this house must be so lonely...

speaker: Oliver
content: The adults... My parents passed away a long time ago. I've been living with my aunt and her family ever since.

speaker: Oliver
content: But you know, I'm not their biological child after all... I understand it...

speaker: Oliver
content: It's okay, don't worry about me! Take your time and rest well, sir!
female_content: It's okay, don't worry about me! Take your time and rest well, miss!

content: How unfamiliar this kind face seems to you. Oliver takes over the conversation skillfully and brushes the dust off the couch thoughtfully, inviting you to sit down.

speaker: Oliver
content: You must be exhausted after what you've been through, right?

speaker: Oliver
content: May I offer you a shoulder massage?
Before you even answer, Oliver moves closer. The bandage around Oliver's neck has come undone, revealing the bruises underneath.
Although it's clear Oliver shows them to you on purpose, you still play along and express your concern.
Oh no! Did you get hurt?

speaker: Oliver
content: Ah... No, it's nothing! You didn't see anything!

speaker: Oliver
content: I'm fine. It'll get better soon. It doesn't hurt at all...
Oliver tightens the sleeve even more. The dark bruises are particularly noticeable against the pale skin.
Don't tell me... your aunt and her family did this?

speaker: Oliver
content: It's Oliver's fault. Oliver couldn't win the affection of Auntie's family... I'm not good enough for them.

speaker: Oliver
content: They're the only family Oliver has left. The more they see me as a burden, the more I want to prove myself.

speaker: Oliver
content: I work and tell lies for them. I've tried so hard... But all I've ever gotten is punishment.
Oliver's hands shake with the sobs, but the massaging motion never stops.
Why don't you run away if they're treating you so poorly?

speaker: Oliver
content: ...Me? Where can I go on my own?

speaker: Oliver
content: Oliver is trapped here forever if I can't find someone kind and rich like you to take me in, sir.
female_content: Oliver is trapped here forever if I can't find someone kind and rich like you to take me in, miss.

speaker: Oliver
content: Indeed... Auntie doesn't let me eat. My cousin forces me to wear her old dresses. My uncle vents his anger by beating me. But what can I do...
Oliver looks at you with envy, but then tactfully averts the gaze and continues to massage you conscientiously.
The kid knows when to push and when to take a step back. This must be a skill Oliver has honed over time. Fortunately, you are well aware of the purpose of your visit.
The dilapidated house is still quiet. The inexplicable surge of Mania is still active. You sigh as you look at the injuries on Oliver.
Oliver, do you think you're a good child?

speaker: Oliver
content: Huh?
Those forced tears haven't dried yet. Oliver looks up at you a little confusedly.
How they treat you has nothing to do with who you really are.
Sincerity and kindness... These are the true criteria of a good child.
If you think you're a good child, I'd be happy to help you escape from here and buy you the best toy in Eastside.

speaker: Oliver
content: A toy! Really? Does Oliver deserve something so nice?
Oliver skillfully avoids the topic of good child and focuses on the benefits you can provide.
You don't press Oliver for an answer yet and pretend to cough weakly.
I don't remember the last time I met a child I got along with so well! We've been chatting non-stop, I'm a bit thirsty.
Can you pour me a glass of water?
The change of topic is admittedly quite abrupt, but it's enough to coax a child. Thinking of the toy you mentioned, Oliver frowns but still nods and dashes off.
You quietly wait for a while. Once you hear the running water, you stealthily approach the source of the Mania activity.
Darkness.
Utter darkness.

You grope your way down the stairs and enter the basement behind the door. You hear some faint noise in the darkness, repeating over and over again in a fixed rhythm, reminding you of the long, disorderly legs of an arthropod.
The basement is dark, slippery, and humid. In the damp air, you can smell a rotten stench.
In the thick shadows, you vaguely see several overlapping human figures.
Are those... mannequins?
As you fumble your way closer, you see three lifelike mannequins. Dressed in old and discolored clothes, they lie haphazardly on a three-legged wooden table, miraculously maintaining their balance.
As you lock eyes with the three mannequins, the strange feeling in your heart grows stronger.
No, these are no ordinary mannequins...

You lean in a bit closer and notice that the mannequins' fingers are firmly pressing against the table. Their fingertips are straining to support the weight of their entire bodies, the bones almost protruding...
Oops...
You've found out.
You hear Oliver's voice behind you. Tap, tap, tap.
Holding a toy unicorn, the Sinner steps toward you. The glass in Oliver's hand is empty.

speaker: Oliver
content: I was wondering why you chose to rest at my place, sir... It's quite bizarre, isn't it?
female_content: I was wondering why you chose to rest at my place, miss... It's quite bizarre, isn't it?

speaker: Oliver
content: Well, well... Even more bizarre, I was already making myself sound so pitiful, yet you still had no intention of helping me.

speaker: Oliver
content: You even tried to teach me a lesson!

speaker: Oliver
content: Ah, I remember now. A seemingly gullible person who turns out to be so adamant and preachy... I think I've met someone like that before...
Oliver throws the empty glass onto the floor with a cold expression.

speaker: Oliver
content: You're that rag doll from the toy factory, aren't you?
The shattered glass breaks the unsettling balance. The three puppets can no longer control their bodies and fall to the ground all at once.
Before hitting the ground, they suddenly leap up in inhuman postures, firmly grabbing the table, their limbs flailing.

They're chatting and hugging each other intimately, their dancing limbs twisting in the opposite direction of their joints. They make the silhouette of a harmonious family as described by the neighbors.
What controls their movements are the dense fine threads in the room formed by the Sinner's special power.
These threads fill the entire space and also surround you.
Now that you've recognized me, let's have a heart-to-heart? I remember you once said that the toy factory was just a distasteful parody of a family? Then what is this...

speaker: Oliver
content: Shut up!
The threads wrapped around the three people are retracted all at once, converging into a force that shoots right in your face!
You're as impatient as always. Too bad, I'm no longer that rag doll you could push around.
Red spikes spread out and cut off Oliver's powerful attack, piercing into Oliver's body.
As the red light flickers, the Mania is temporarily suppressed and all those threads are rendered futile.

speaker: Oliver
content: Mmph! You...
Knocked down by the power of the shackles, Oliver cries out in shock. At the same time, the aunt's family seem to have regained their souls, screaming as they feel the irresistible pain...

speaker: Aunt
content: Oliver, you dirty little rat! Give it to me! Where did you hide it!

speaker: Uncle
content: Oh... I can repay you soon! Don't chase after me! Just sell that little punk to them!

speaker: Cousin
content: How dare you do this to us... Useless burden! We'll beat you to death and throw you out!
Biting back the pain, Oliver hugs the toy unicorn tightly and covers its ears.
The chaotic and excited murmurs sound especially harsh in the basement. You send a call to Nightingale...
Sinner Oliver has been shackled and successfully detained.
I've found Oliver's family too...

speaker: Oliver
content: Haha, you call them... my family?
Slumped on the floor, Oliver lets out a snicker, curling up around the toy and muttering...

speaker: Oliver
content: There's nothing I despise more...

speaker: Oliver
content: Than family...
Oliver... When I'm gone, you must listen to your aunt.
From now on, your aunt, uncle, and cousin will be your family...
You're a very sweet child, Oliver. You'll definitely get along with them, won't you...
It's all Mommy's fault... I've left you nothing...
During the trip back to the Bureau, Oliver resisted hard with all kinds of tricks and sweet talks. After being left in the confinement cell alone for a few days, Oliver finally begins to calm down.
Bleary-eyed, Oliver seems to have just woken up, but doesn't appear surprised to see you.

speaker: Oliver
content: Hey, if it isn't Chief who's best at tricking Oliver?

speaker: Oliver
content: Oliver behaved so well while you were away! I didn't run away or cry! I'm a good child, aren't I?

speaker: Oliver
content: As a reward for my good behavior, can I go home now?
Oliver trots over enthusiastically, holding the toy and leaning toward you, looking just like a child longing for company.
But you've already seen the real Oliver in the factory and that house of mannequins.

options: Quit playing dumb. You can't fool me.

content: You're too smart not to understand your current situation.
Your stern attitude seems to have genuinely taken Oliver aback. The kid returns to the seat forlornly.

speaker: Oliver
content: Tsk... You were more fun as a doll and a sketchy rich person.

speaker: Oliver
content: Now, you're no different from those stinky, annoying adults.
Oliver looks away and mutters into the toy. You can see the kid's knees shaking. After all, a place like this is too intimidating and stressful to a Sinner of Oliver's age.
Oliver... This is the MBCC, a Sinner supervision facility. We only carry out the interrogation to learn more about you. It won't take long.
Your tone softens slightly.
I said I'd be happy to help you escape from that house of mannequins and buy you the best toy in Eastside. That wasn't a lie.
I also want to hear the truth from you.
Let's talk about those people you tricked in Eastside.
Oliver glimpses the list you've collected and looks up innocently.

speaker: Oliver
content: Tricked... What do you mean? I have no idea...
Oliver!

speaker: Oliver
content: Oh, I simply fell in front of them accidentally, showed them my injuries accidentally, and told them I hadn't eaten in days accidentally...

speaker: Oliver
content: They all voluntarily helped Oliver. Are you saying that's Oliver's fault too?
Ignoring your warnings, Oliver smirks cunningly, head tilting as if certain you can't catch any solid evidence.
You won't stop lying even now? Your aunt's family is completely under your control, where did those scars on your body come from?
The Bureau's doctor has already examined them. They are all self-inflicted!
You throw out those badges of the Homeless that Oliver used while escaping.
What about these fake badges then? Are they an accident too?

speaker: Oliver
content: What are these? Oliver has no idea.

speaker: Oliver
content: Did you guys pick these up somewhere? Some poor child must have dropped them. You must return them quickly.
Feigning innocence, Oliver pushes the evidence back to you, along with your last bit of patience and sympathy.
...I'm giving you one last chance, Oliver.
I believe not all Sinners are as irredeemable as people say. Many of the Sinners I've encountered simply had no other choices.
You just said you wanted to go home. Why not start by explaining what's going on at home?
If you were treated unfairly or hiding a secret, I'll try my best to help. But first, you have to tell the truth.
You pull out a stack of photos showing the horrific scenes from the basement of that house.
We just saw them not long ago. Don't tell me you don't know what you're looking at.
Why did you do this?

speaker: Oliver
content: Why... Oh, Oliver wants to know why too...

speaker: Oliver
content: Why must Oliver eat their leftovers, use their worn-out things, and wear their hand-me-downs...

speaker: Oliver
content: I tried so hard to please them. No matter what they did, I always smiled. Why did they still scold me, order me around, call my smile fake and disgusting? If they thought I was a burden, they could have just thrown me away!
These grievances are genuine. You can tell these emotions are not a lie.
It's them who mistreated you. You've already told me that, and I believe you.
So you did all this out of revenge?

speaker: Oliver
content: Revenge? Oliver is a good child. I would never take revenge on them.

speaker: Oliver
content: Oliver promised to get along with them. I must keep my word!

speaker: Oliver
content: ...Did you know how easy it is to control the puppets? It's just like playing house. With our shadows cast on the window, we look just like a happy family!

speaker: Oliver
content: Cousin pours water for me, Auntie cooks for me, and Uncle takes me to school...

speaker: Oliver
