content: Everyone believes it. They think Oliver is a good child! Oliver did it! I'm so smart, aren't I?
Oliver laughs gleefully, hugging the toy and rocking the interrogation chair.
You scrutinize Oliver's face closely, but not even a trace of regret can be found.
You sigh and tidy up the scattered evidence on the table, then stand up and make your way out.

speaker: Oliver
content: Wait, where are you going? Are you going to leave Oliver alone here?

speaker: Oliver
content: What did Oliver do wrong? Why won't you let me go home!
You know full well what you did wrong... There's no need to continue the interrogation.

speaker: Oliver
content: Huh?
I forgot to tell you that after the toy factory incident, the MBCC investigated everyone involved.
We've found that the transformation is not random. Most people turn into the object they're most familiar with.
If I'm not mistaken, Eve turned you into a toy unicorn, didn't she?

speaker: Oliver
content: ...What, what are you bringing this up for?
Nothing... I specifically allowed you to bring the toy into the interrogation room.
I wonder how this toy would feel, having heard what you just said.

speaker: Mother
content: It's all Mommy's fault... I've left you nothing...

speaker: Oliver
content: That's not true! This unicorn Mommy gave me is my favorite.

speaker: Mother
content: Silly child. What would a toy do for you...

speaker: Mother
content: Take this, keep it safe...
A priceless opal necklace was sewn into the heart of the toy.

speaker: Oliver
content: I don't want it! I don't want this! I just want Mommy to be with me, by my side!

speaker: Mother
content: Shh, don't cry... Mommy can't do that anymore. It'll be with you on my behalf.

speaker: Mother
content: From now on, you have to be a good child on your own. Listen to your aunt and uncle, get along with them, and grow up healthily...

speaker: Mother
content: I know my Oliver is the sweetest child...

speaker: Oliver
content: That's not true... Oliver hasn't been good...

speaker: Oliver
content: I haven't been good at all... I'm sorry... Mommy...

speaker: Oliver
content: But I have no other choice... Don't go... Wait for me...

speaker: Oliver
content: Wait, don't go...!
Oliver suddenly grabs you as you're about to get up and leave, tears welling up in those big eyes.

speaker: Oliver
content: They made me do it! Auntie and her family gambled all their money away! They wanted to take Mommy's necklace from me, to pay off their debts!

speaker: Oliver
content: I was obedient until then! I listened to everything they said! I'd thought it all out. I'll be able to leave and support myself once I grow up!

speaker: Oliver
content: They went too far! Oliver wanted to be a good child! But I had no choice!

speaker: Oliver
content: Please don't...

speaker: Oliver
content: Please don't hate Oliver...

speaker: Oliver
content: Nightingale! Have you seen Chief today?

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief is very busy now. What do you need?

speaker: Oliver
content: Oh, I thought so... I've tried to look for Chief many times but I always get the same answer.

speaker: Oliver
content: It's okay. I understand Chief's work is very important...

speaker: Oliver
content: Can you pass a message to Chief please, Nightingale? Just one sentence!

speaker: Nightingale
content: What is it?

speaker: Oliver
content: Oliver has been eating well these past few days! I've also attended the foundation classes arranged by the Bureau!

speaker: Oliver
content: I've learned a lot of new things! Everyone says Oliver is a fast learner and that I'm bright!

speaker: Oliver
content: Oliver doesn't lie anymore... I've also lent a hand to many people...

speaker: Oliver
content: I guess... Oliver has become a good child...
Oliver's head drops lower and lower.

speaker: Oliver
content: That's more than one sentence... Forget it. I don't want to leave a message anymore.

speaker: Nightingale
content: That's not a problem. Also, I happen to need to see you too.

speaker: Oliver
content: Is it about... the bad things Oliver did before? You're going to punish me, aren't you?

speaker: Nightingale
content: No, Chief has something to give you.

speaker: Oliver
content: ...This is!
If you think you're a good child, I'd be happy to help you escape from here and buy you the best toy in Eastside.
The child runs into the giant colorful toy and starts crying loudly, like a newborn in the most loving embrace in the world.
Knock knock knock...
Come in.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, we've finished sorting the info on Sinner Lamia. After going through all the posts and rumors online, this is what we've got.
Nightingale hands you a folder. When you open it, there are only two pieces of paper inside.
One is her basic bio. The other is half a page of personal info unrelated to her role as "Ocean Messenger."
...That's all?

speaker: Nightingale
content: Yeah. Sorry, Chief. Repeated investigations by the intelligence department yielded the same results.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Lamia's "Ocean Messenger" identity has covered up a lot about her own identity.

speaker: Nightingale
content: While the President of the Thaumas Society primed Lamia, he deleted a lot of information about her, and even altered her appearance for their livestreams. The technical department is trying to restore some of the data, but it will take time.
Okay, got it.
Then please arrange an interrogation in two days. It seems that we must learn about her past, including her involvement with the Thaumas Society, in her own words.
You see Lamia flinching visibly the moment the light turns on. She sneaks a glance at you and her voice trembles, just like when you first met her.

speaker: Lamia
content: ...Chief? What am I doing here?

speaker: Lamia
content: It's so dark and scary here... Did something happen? Is that why you brought me here...
Her eyes are downcast and full of worry, but not for herself—instead, she seems to be worried about the potential trouble you're facing.
Don't be scared, Lamia. You've behaved quite well since coming to the MBCC. You haven't violated any rules, and everyone has spoken highly about you.
I'm just here for a routine inquiry. I want to know some details about the Thaumas Society.

speaker: Lamia
content: ...Really? I'm glad I didn't cause trouble for you guys.
She sighs in relief and unknits her brows, revealing a faint smile.

speaker: Lamia
content: So, what do you want to know, Chief? I'll make sure to help you as much as I can.
I've been curious about the Thaumas Society since arriving to Ogygia Villa. What kind of organization is it?
You've been tracking this organization online and suspect that Sinners are involved, but it's too strictly guarded. Even if you pay to become a member, the chance of meeting a core member is slim.

speaker: Lamia
content: Ah... are you interested in becoming a Seafarer? We are a maritime culture research organization. We facilitate the exchange of ideas between ocean enthusiasts.

speaker: Lamia
content: All life originated from the ocean, so we believe it is the cradle of all souls. The deep sea is spiritual and wise, and holds the immense power to purify and enlighten.

speaker: Lamia
content: In addition, we believe there is another world at the bottom of the sea, where life that remained in the ocean gained intelligence and established their own civilization.
I've read that already on your homepage. I want to ask about the things not available to the general public.

speaker: Lamia
content: What do you mean?
For example... your offline gatherings?

speaker: Lamia
content: Ah, you mean our in-person meetings?

speaker: Lamia
content: Yes, the President regularly invites our most dedicated fans, as well as those with unique insights into maritime culture, to meet with me at Ogygia Villa. It's an opportunity to exchange ideas and explore the mysteries of the world together.
Just to exchange ideas?

speaker: Lamia
content: Yes... why do you ask?
She fidgets in her chair, and her eyes dart about. It's evident that she's hiding something, and... lying.
Speaking of the "President," what kind of person is he? How is your relationship with him?

speaker: Lamia
content: The President... is a very good person. I've always felt grateful towards him. He is patient and kind, and takes care of everyone, including myself. Anyone who has attended our meetings has more or less experienced that. So...
She clasps her hands over her chest and flashes a faint smile.

speaker: Lamia
content: We all admire the President. I pray every day that he gets the ocean's blessings that he yearns for.
So, you don't know... that he died in Ogygia Villa?
Your question seems to shock Lamia.

speaker: Lamia
content: Wh-what?! The President... he...!!
We found a corpse in Ogygia Villa. The MBCC's autopsy confirmed it to be the President of the Thaumas Society.

speaker: Lamia
content: How could this be... He... He said that we'd go back to the Society together after dinner...

speaker: Lamia
content: I... I was still worrying about missing that meeting... How could the President have... ended up in the sea...
Lamia lowers her head even more, resting her chin on her clasped hands. Tears brim in her eyes and tremble on her eyelashes.
So... you knew nothing about this?

speaker: Lamia
content: W-what's that supposed to mean? Of course I don't know anything about this! Surely you don't think I have something to do with this!

speaker: Lamia
content: I was with you and Miss Cabernet when it happened, remember?
test
test
test
test
test
test
You're a lousy liar, Miss Lamia.
You put the autopsy report on the table and push it towards Lamia.
I don't think you understood what I meant by "the MBCC's autopsy."
What happened in Ogygia Villa was a Mania incident, so all the evidence went through the MBCC's lab. We have evidence to prove that he died from a poisonous, hallucination-inducing Sinner's power.
The autopsy report completely blows her cover. She's now fully aware that there's solid evidence against her.

speaker: Lamia
content: Ah... Chief, I... it's not what you think! I-I really didn't want to, but I had no choice... Please trust me!
Stuttering in defense, she looks pleadingly at you with tearful eyes, as if you're her last hope for survival.
No choice? Why?
As if wanting to say something but hesitant and afraid to, Lamia lowers her head and clasps tightly onto the armrests.

options: Ask her to tell the truth

content: You lean in close to her, softening your tone.
The people who planned that banquet will all be investigated and punished. If you hide anything from us, we might consider you to be an accomplice.
So... if you keep hiding the truth, I can't help you.

speaker: Lamia
content: ...All right, I'll tell you.
Biting her lip, she finally makes up her mind and starts to talk:

speaker: Lamia
content: Like I said before, I've always truly respected, appreciated and depended on the President.

speaker: Lamia
content: After all, when a freak like me came to this wholly unfamiliar world, had nowhere to go and almost starved to death on the streets, he was the one who took me in.

speaker: Lamia
content: The President gave me a place to stay, and made me realize that I, too, had the worth to keep on living.
"Wholly unfamiliar world"...?
Her odd wording makes you frown, but you continue to listen without interrupting.

speaker: Lamia
content: He helped me come to terms with my skin color. He also taught me how to comfort those driven to desperation by this cruel world at in-person meetings, so that they may rekindle their hope and passion for life...

speaker: Lamia
content: In fact, I often feel that the Seafarers and I are each other's saviors. I heal their wounds, while they make me feel accepted and loved.
...So this is the truth of your in-person meetings? You use your power to comfort them?

speaker: Lamia
content: ...No. This is what I thought was the truth.
Lamia shakes her head, smiling bitterly.

speaker: Lamia
content: I wish I hadn't passed by the President's room that night. I wish I hadn't eavesdropped out of curiosity. Perhaps then I could've continued to live in my dream, and all those bad things wouldn't have happened.
Lamia curls up in her chair, seeming to recall a very painful scene.

speaker: Lamia
content: But in reality, he didn't do any of those things for the sake of those poor, tormented Seafarers. It was all for greed and money. I was just a tool... a puppet he used to trick others...

speaker: Lamia
content: It wasn't till that night that I found out everyone had to pay him a hefty "membership fee" to join my in-person meetings.

speaker: Lamia
content: Those poor, desperate Seafarers sought me for comfort because of how much they suffered.

speaker: Lamia
content: Yet the President exploited their pain and suffering for money. That's not something I can accept.

speaker: Lamia
content: I didn't want to go to that banquet and participate in his scams anymore... We had an argument in the Ogygia Villa's control room... He said there were plenty of others who'll do what I won't...

speaker: Lamia
content: He said there weren't that many honorable souls in this world, and that I could be replaced at any moment. He even decided to abandon me on the spot and kill me.

speaker: Lamia
content: I was so scared that I lost control... I swear, I really didn't mean to, I just wanted to live...

speaker: Lamia
content: I truly wanted to relieve the Seafarers' suffering. I truly wanted to help them, but ended up helping the President harm them instead.

speaker: Lamia
content: Maybe I'm just destined to be a monster who brings disaster to those around me... It was all an illusion. I didn't attain salvation, nor could I save others.
Lamia's voice is so full of pain and guilt that you can't help but feel moved.
Based on previous investigations, you know that such organizations are usually scams. They took in a desperate soul like Lamia and exploited her power to scam others.
All you can do is try to uproot such organizations and save one Lamia after another.

speaker: Lamia
content: Sorry, Chief. I choked up a bit. How embarrassing.
As you ponder how to comfort her, she wipes the corners of her eyes and flashes you a grateful smile.

speaker: Lamia
content: I've always been the one listening to others' troubles... It's my first time confessing my own troubles to someone else... It feels so good. Thank you for listening to me.

Sorry for bringing up these awful memories, but it's a routine procedure. Thank you for cooperating. I now have a general understanding of the Thaumas Society. I have one last question before wrapping up our interrogation today.
Perhaps surprised by how quickly the interrogation is ending, her expression becomes a bit off, but she quickly fixes it.

speaker: Lamia
content: Of course... Ask away.
You mentioned just now that "the President took you in"... That was indeed the case. We found an old nurse and learned some things from her. Perhaps... it's related to your past.
You put a voice recording pen on the table. Lamia stares at it with a grim look on her face.
If what she says is true, and you want to pursue the matter... we can offer you help.

speaker: Lamia
content: Is the past... of particular importance to the Bureau? I joined the Society at an early age. I don't remember what happened before then.

Lamia is being overtly resistant, making you puzzled as well as troubled. But you need to get to know her better—you hope that after leaving Thaumas, she can learn to survive without using her power or trickery.
Sorry. The Bureau's top psychiatrist will be right at the door. I will immediately stop the recording if you feel unwell... But I still hope that you can confirm its content.
test
test
test
test
test
test
test
Lamia nods lightly, and you start to play the recording. Amidst the rustling static, an elderly voice begins to speak.

speaker: Old Nurse
content: My my, how could I forget such a special child? I've been a midwife for decades and delivered thousands of babies, but I've never seen anything quite like her.

speaker: Old Nurse
content: That child was as gray as ash when she was born. Quite the bad omen! The doctors and nurses were all shocked. Even the mother screamed and fainted when she saw the child.

speaker: Old Nurse
content: Moreover, I heard that the mother died of illness not long after. Nobody dared to adopt that monstrous-looking child. They kicked her around like a ball for quite some time, until some distant relatives were pressured to take her in.

speaker: Old Nurse
content: I don't know what happened after that. The child was illegitimate to begin with, so her relatives took her from the hospital without filling in the proper papers. They didn't leave any information with us.

speaker: Lamia
content: I... I don't remember... I really don't remember...
Lamia mutters to herself as pain and panic creeps onto her face.

speaker: Lamia
content: ...Don't hurt me... Let me go... Let me go...
She begins to tremble uncontrollably, curling up into a fetal position. Her eyes lose focus and her breathing speeds up as she mutters incomprehensibly.

speaker: Lamia
content: Ah!!!
Lamia lets out a piteous scream. You quickly stop the recording and cast your shackles to stabilize Lamia.
Lamia, don't be scared. You're safe and sound in the MBCC. No one will hurt you here...
After a long silence, Lamia finally calms down.
Let's call it a day. Go back and get some rest.
You did well... I pushed you too hard. I didn't mean any harm. I just wanted to help you.
As you get up to lead her out, she suddenly grabs the corner of your shirt.

speaker: Lamia
content: Eastside Psychiatric Hospital
...What?
As if making a difficult decision, she takes a deep breath and looks up at you again.

speaker: Lamia
content: Eastside Psychiatric Hospital. That's where you can find out about... my "past."

speaker: Lamia
content: You're right. Only by knowing this will you be able to help me...

speaker: Lamia
content: Help me, Chief.

speaker: Pedestrian A
content: Hey! Look over there! That girl has gray skin!

speaker: Pedestrian B
content: Gray skin... I feel like I've seen her somewhere before... Ah, it's Lamia! The Ocean Messenger of the Thaumas Society! I think I follow her online!

speaker: Pedestrian C
content: What? Is it actually her?! So she really is gray! I thought it was just a filter.

speaker: Pedestrian A
content: How can anyone have gray skin? It's just makeup, right? Let's get a closer look...

speaker: Pedestrian B
content: We mustn't miss such a rare opportunity! My camera is all ready to go! Quick, let's go closer and see where she's going...
You and Lamia are on your way to Eastside Psychiatric Hospital. Her eccentric appearance has attracted the attention of many passersby.
More and more onlookers gather around you, pointing excitedly and snapping photos.
You're unable to disperse the pestering crowd despite warning them repeatedly. As you prepare to shoo them away again, Lamia stops you.

speaker: Lamia
content: Let's just go, Chief. It's no use. You won't be able to get rid of them.
Lamia quickens her pace, dragging you through the insufferable crowd with her head bowed. You don't quite understand her approach.
...Is she just going to let them do whatever they want?
Even you feel disturbed by all the eyes gawking at Lamia as if she were some zoo animal. How can Lamia tolerate it herself?

speaker: Lamia
content: What else can I do?
She shakes her head and says in exasperation:

speaker: Lamia
content: I'm... used to this kind of thing.

speaker: Lamia
content: Plus, I think they're just doing it out of curiosity or because they like me. At least they don't hate me, fear me, or want to hurt me. That's already more than I can ask for.
As if she remembered something, Lamia's voice is tinged with pain and sorrow. Yet her pitiful expression gives you the same troubled feeling you got back in the interrogation room.
When questioned about her childhood earlier, her reaction was a tad dramatic and unnatural. The subsequent transition was also oddly fast for someone who deceives for a living.
You sigh to yourself as you look at Lamia, who is putting on a courageous smile.
Hope I'm overthinking.

Only upon reaching the psychiatric hospital do you manage to shake off the crowd, who gets dispersed by security guards at the door. Lamia leads you up the stairs, down a long corridor, and finally stops at a room near the end.
Her head still bowed, she rests her trembling palms on the door frame, but doesn't muster the courage to open the door.

speaker: Lamia
content: I'm so scared...

speaker: Lamia
content: I... never thought that I'd come back here and see him again...
Don't worry. I'll be by your side.
You comfort her softly and push open the door.
Hello...?
You see a trembling young man curled up in a corner of the hospital bed, his cowering appearance at odds with his brawny body.
Though facing the door, he ignores your greeting, and his eyes are glazed and unfocused. You fail to elicit any response from him, so you turn to ask Lamia.
Is this the person you wanted me to meet?
Lamia nods.
Who is he...?

speaker: Lamia
content: ...My cousin.
Cousin...? But you said you had nowhere to go and no place to stay...
Lamia doesn't answer. She takes out a mirror from her pocket and carefully holds it up in front of the man she calls cousin.
The moment the man's gaze meets the mirror, his dazed face contorts in pain and panic.

speaker: Cousin
content: Ahhh!!! Don't come over!!!
He shrieks hysterically and waves his arms wildly as if trying to fight off some invisible enemy, knocking the mirror from Lamia's hands.

speaker: Cousin
content: I was wrong! I won't talk back again!

speaker: Cousin
content: I'm so tired, I just want to rest for a while...

speaker: Cousin
content: ...Cough cough cough! I'm a dumb fish! I'm a monster from the sea... Please let go of me, I can't breathe...
The nurses outside notice the man's sudden outburst. They rush into the room, elbowing you and Lamia aside.

speaker: Lamia
content: That was what happened between me and him. To be more precise... That was what happened to me.
The nurses hold the man down and inject him with a sedative, restoring his sluggish demeanor.
You realize what she wants to tell you by bringing you here.

speaker: Lamia
content: He held my head in the water tank... He was so strong that I couldn't fight back. I was choking to death. I just wanted to live, but then it turned out like this all of a sudden...

speaker: Lamia
content: I was so scared when it happened. I ran away from home and never went back, and never saw him again... I, I didn't know the consequences would be so severe.

speaker: Lamia
content: I feel sad and guilty seeing him like this. It was my fault. I could've handled things differently...
You're almost convinced by her again. But this proves that her odd shift in expression was to deliberately arouse your suspicion and make you come here with her.
...Lamia.
You interrupt her.
What are you trying to prove by showing me this? To prove... that your actions were justified?

speaker: Lamia
content: Chief...
Surprised that you're suspicious of her intentions, Lamia freezes on the spot. Even the piteous look on her face freezes.
Monster! Shoo! Stay away from my son!
A shrill female voice breaks the silence. A purse comes flying through the door, striking Lamia's shoulder and knocking her back a few steps.
A middle-aged woman storms in, her eyes burning with resentment and rage. She looks ready to pounce on Lamia at any moment.

speaker: Lamia
content: W-what are you doing here?

speaker: Relative
content: Ha, to seek justice for my baby boy, of course! I have to thank all your fans for sharing clips of you online. Why else would you take this route, if not to come to this hospital to see my son?

speaker: Relative
content: If it weren't for them, I wouldn't have been able to find you, you little bastard!

speaker: Relative
content: God must be blind to grant you so much success... But now that you're living the high life, isn't it time to atone for your sins?

speaker: Lamia
content: Sins? Me?

speaker: Relative
content: Quit acting, you can't fool me. You think I don't know that you're the reason he ended up like this?
The woman sneers contemptuously and points to her bedridden son.

speaker: Relative
content: The doctors can't cure him. They say it's as if he's trapped in some inescapable nightmare, which drove him insane... You put a curse on him!

speaker: Relative
content: You should pay for this with your life! But I'm a softie. We're family, after all. As long as you compensate us enough, we'll be done with each other!

speaker: Relative
content: Otherwise, I'll expose you online for what you did to my son and make you a pariah! I know that for a "public figure" like you, reputation is more important than anything. Think it over!
The woman glares at Lamia with taunting smugness. The fury and hatred on her face has given way to shrewdness and greed.
As opposed to "seeking justice for her son," the real purpose of her visit seems to be seeking compensation from Lamia.

speaker: Lamia
content: Uh huh.
Lamia sneers coldly. When she lifts up her head again, it's as if she's a totally different person. Dripping with icy scorn, she locks eyes with the woman without a hint of fear.

speaker: Lamia
content: What did I do? I just gave him a taste of what I went through.
The woman glances at you in a fluster, then puts her hands on her hips and raises her voice.

speaker: Relative
content: Don't slander us! Haven't we been kind enough to you? Who else would have taken in a freak like you?

speaker: Relative
content: We fed you and sheltered you. Shouldn't you be grateful, obedient and do whatever you can to thank us?

speaker: Relative
content: If it weren't for us, you'd be rotting away in some garbage heap. How would you get the glamorous life you have now? What an ungrateful brat!

speaker: Lamia
content: You took me in, so I deserve to be locked up and treated as a slave? To be a punching bag who never fights back? To be abused by your son every day?

speaker: Relative
content: S-stay back, or else I'll scream for help!
Lamia's reaction makes the woman back away a few steps. Fear dawns in her eyes as she realizes the girl in front of her is no longer the same as before.
At the same time, your shackles begin to stir—Mania is oozing from Lamia and whirling in the air.
Lamia! Calm down!
Lamia turns a deaf ear to your warning. She closes in on the cornered woman like a predator eyeing her prey, slowly raising her arm.

speaker: Lamia
content: Come on, hit me. Weren't you so good at that before?

speaker: Lamia
content: ...What's wrong? Too scared to do it now? Cowards like you who fear the strong and bully the weak really disgust me.

speaker: Lamia
content: Both you and your son can go to hell!
Ready to tell the truth this time?

speaker: Lamia
content: You've already seen my true colors. No need for me to keep acting, right?
The gray-skinned girl smiles at you from behind the glass of the detainment cell. She looks relaxed and at ease, totally different from her previous self.
Her mental state is much better than you expected—totally unlike someone who had been confined for two days.

speaker: Lamia
content: Ah... I must say, I can finally be myself now. It's so nice to ditch my mask.
She stretches and moves closer, locking eyes with you confidently.

speaker: Lamia
content: But I'm curious, when did you start doubting me?

Right after the interrogation. You shouldn't be that clumsy at lying—it's what you do for a living, isn't it? The fact that you deliberately exposed yourself... means that you want the poor Chief to match your pace.

speaker: Lamia
content: Even if I didn't do that, you'd still be able to match my pace.
She sighs dramatically, yet there's no hint of regret in her tone.

speaker: Lamia
content: But you know, my piteous persona worked really well with that old fart. In all my years in the Society, he never suspected a thing. Do you think it's because he's too stupid, or because you're too smart?
You don't intend on answering that question. Instead, you calmly bring the topic back on track.
Enough with the banter. Let's cut to the chase.

speaker: Lamia
content: All right, what do you want to know about? Let me guess... my cousin?
I don't doubt the authenticity of your childhood experiences. Your aunt sufficiently proved that you weren't lying.
She looks surprised for a second, then breaks into a smile again.

speaker: Lamia
content: Hahaha, I see. Chatting with a smart one really saves time.
But now that you mention it, I do have one more question.

speaker: Lamia
content: Oh?

Your childhood experience was something traumatic that you probably don't want to remember. Judging from your initial reaction, you didn't want to tell me. Why did you then change your mind and take me to your cousin?

speaker: Lamia
content: Hmm... to make things clear, those experiences were more humiliating than traumatic. Originally, I didn't want anyone to know, but you found that nurse, didn't you?

speaker: Lamia
content: I have a good grasp of what the MBCC is capable of. Even if I didn't tell you myself, you'd find out sooner or later.

speaker: Lamia
content: Since this is the case, it's better for me to take a preemptive strike—to show you my vulnerable and tragic past to win your trust and sympathy.

speaker: Lamia
content: I just didn't expect that you already had your suspicions about me. Plus, that woman butted in halfway through to mess up things even more... Sigh, I had planned it so well. The MBCC was going to be the next Thaumas Society, and you were going to be the next President.

speaker: Lamia
content: Too... bad... so... sad.

She fixes her gaze on you as she spits out each word. Her fearsome gaze and icy tone sends a chill down your spine. You know that you can't appear weak right now, so you gaze back at her calmly with a poker face.
Got it. Let's move on to the next question.

options: Let's talk about the President's death again.

content: How did the President really die? I don't think it was simply an accident.

speaker: Lamia
content: You're right. How could it be an accident? I've planned it for a long time.
As if disappointed by your reaction, Lamia looks down at her nails, murmuring casually as if describing her breakfast.

speaker: Lamia
content: As for when I started to plan it... I'd have to say, from the day I joined the Society.

speaker: Lamia
content: After escaping from that house, I saw the dazzling outside world for the first time. I thought I was finally free, but after wandering the streets for a few days, I realized that wasn't the case.

speaker: Lamia
content: People here didn't yell at me or beat me, but they also viewed me as a freak. They'll take pictures of me, but when I approach them, they avoid me like the plague.

speaker: Lamia
content: I finally understood that the outside world is just a bigger version of my aunt's house. I still need to hide and disguise myself, and use my Sinner power to survive. That's why I approached the Thaumas Society on my own accord.

speaker: Lamia
content: As for the President... I've never believed in his stories. I knew from the very beginning that he'd use me as a tool to make money.

speaker: Lamia
content: But compared to my cousin's family, he treated me quite well. At least he fed and clothed me well, and satisfied most of my needs.

speaker: Lamia
content: But from my previous experience, I knew that if I wanted to live well, I must take control and not live at others' mercy.
Lamia looks up at you.

speaker: Lamia
content: Remember when I told you that... "He said there are plenty of others who can replace me, and decided to abandon me on the spot and kill me"? In a sense I wasn't lying—that's what would've happened if I didn't strike first.

speaker: Lamia
content: You know that an online club like that may not last a long time. The President might even find a more useful puppet before the club goes under.

speaker: Lamia
content: So to preempt against that, I must seize control of the Thaumas Society and make it my own safety net and hunting ground.

speaker: Lamia
content: But I owe that old fart, after all. Believe it or not, it was not my intention to kill him. I just wanted him to lose his mind and give up control of the Society.

speaker: Lamia
content: Too bad he was too old to survive. Who is there to blame but himself?
You open your mouth, but no words come out. Lamia looks at your troubled expression and smiles indifferently.

speaker: Lamia
content: You check the battery level—2%. Theoretically, it's enough for a full-power signal, but the ancient equipment is a liability. If the power surges and fails, every effort you and Ceto have made will be for nothing.
You're not a monster or a freak. We're all the same.
You reply earnestly, but she laughs as if she heard a big joke.

speaker: Lamia
content: Really? You're probably the only one who feels this way.

speaker: Lamia
content: If we're all the same, then why do they look at me like that? Why can't I get their acceptance or approval no matter what I do?

speaker: Lamia
content: They view me as a filthy and ominous monster, as a puppet to be manipulated, as a lofty idol who can grant their wishes... but they never view me as a human being like them.

speaker: Lamia
content: You know, in my whole life, I've never encountered kindness from human beings.

speaker: Lamia
content: Since I can't join 'em, I'll have to be strong enough to beat 'em. Thus, the only way I can survive is to be a hunter in disguise.

speaker: Lamia
content: What kind of expression is that? Don't get me wrong, I've already passed the stage of wanting to be a human being. I don't need your pity.

speaker: Lamia
content: I've known the true face of mankind for a long time now. If you're kind enough to share your bread with someone, he'll just backstab you and snatch the rest.

speaker: Lamia
content: Human nature is inherently ignorant, wicked and vile. This dark world has plunged mankind into despair, but in their cowardice, they can only mitigate the pain by bullying the weak or deceiving themselves.

speaker: Lamia
content: I'm perfectly fine with not becoming such a hopeless and debased type of creature.
But not all humans are like that, nor is the world totally dark. There's also light in this world.

speaker: Lamia
content: I never said there wasn't light in this world.

speaker: Lamia
content: I've seen and heard too much in my life. I know of such duality all too well.

speaker: Lamia
content: But it's precisely because of how intertwined they are, the fragile light always gets swallowed up by darkness. People inevitably succumb to their own weaknesses.

speaker: Lamia
content: Or to put it more bluntly, the "beautiful light" is nothing but an illusion, a fragile bubble on a tidal wave. The cruel darkness is the underlying reality.

speaker: Lamia
content: Courage, perseverance, kindness, love... Mankind's virtues stem from naivete about the world, and are no match against the cruel realities of life.
That's not true. Light doesn't always get devoured by darkness, and not everyone gives in to their weakness...

speaker: Lamia
content: Shut up!
Your rebuttal probably touched a nerve. Lamia writhes violently, rattling the chains around her hands and roaring like an angry beast.

speaker: Lamia
content: As someone who has so much privilege, who are you to judge my point of view?

speaker: Lamia
content: <size=31>Do you know what it's like to live on the streets, be pointed and sneered at, and have no choice but to steal and pick through trash? Do you know what it's like to be controlled and watched all the time, and forced to wear a mask of subservience and fawning?</size>

speaker: Lamia
content: I've been through it all. I went to hell and back, but you haven't! Who are you to dismiss what I've learned through tears and blood with a few lofty words?
She glares at you with tearful eyes, her chest heaving up and down. It takes her a long time to calm down again.

speaker: Lamia
content: ...I know you may not be able to accept the cruel reality of the world all at once. But don't worry, I will prove it to you with facts.

speaker: Lamia
content: I can take you to witness the light and darkness of the human soul. Let me clear your illusions, and show you how blindly overconfident and self-righteous you are.
She lifts up her chin and looks at you smugly.

speaker: Lamia
content: How about it? Do you dare take up my offer?
On a sunny afternoon, you follow Lamia into an Eastside residential neighborhood. It's one of Eastside's rare old neighborhoods, somewhat cluttered and dilapidated, but full of life.

Walking through the narrow alleyways, you pass by children who just got off school, middle-aged folks talking on their phones, and senior citizens with bags of groceries, before finally reaching an apartment building at the edge of the neighborhood.
While waiting for the elevator, you overhear the conversation of two residents chatting in front of their homes.

speaker: Resident A
content: Did you hear? The folks from 601 went to complain to the management yesterday!

speaker: Resident B
content: Oh, about what?

speaker: Resident A
content: About 602, of course! What else could it be about?

speaker: Resident B
content: Oh... as they should. We can hear those strange sounds even from the 8th floor, and the elevator reeks every time it passes by the 6th floor. Tsk tsk, I can only imagine what they must go through living on the same floor.

speaker: Resident A
content: I know, right? But it's no use complaining. The family in 602 is as creepy as hell. The useless management here is too chicken to do anything about them. All they do is keep saying the "relevant departments have been notified."

speaker: Resident B
content: Sigh. Now that you mention it, weren't they quite normal before? How did they end up like this?

speaker: Resident A
content: I think it's because they joined that... what is it called? The Thau-something Society? The popular one online that talks about the ocean. I was curious, so I searched them up.

speaker: Resident B
content: And?

speaker: Resident A
content: They're really something else! You won't believe this, but their Ocean Messenger has gray skin all over!

speaker: Resident B
content: ...! L-like her?
The stout man pats the lanky man on the shoulder and points at you guys. The latter can't help but shriek when he sees Lamia.

speaker: Resident A
content: Y-yeah... She's here to visit 602?!
At this point, Lamia glances back at them. The pair flees in terror, tugging on each other's arms.

speaker: Resident B
content: Shhh! Stop talking! She might make you insane, too... run run run!
As they flee, Lamia looks away and snickers disdainfully.

speaker: Lamia
content: Uh huh.
Did you bring me here to meet your "Seafarers"?

speaker: Lamia
content: That's right.

Ding——the elevator door opens. Lamia leads you to the unit directly across the hall. A thin layer of dust had accumulated on the shoe rack by the door, while the apartment number "602" hangs lopsided with no one to fix it.

speaker: Lamia
content: Go and see for yourself, my righteous Chief.
Smiling, she twists the doorknob and gestures dramatically at you to enter.

speaker: Lamia
content: Welcome to the place where dreams come true.
As soon as she opens the door, you're hit by the stench of rotting garbage fermenting for months in an airless environment.
The lights are turned off inside. The windows are closed and the curtains are tightly drawn. There are only a few faint rays of light leaking out from the seams where the fabric meets the floor.

You blink, struggling to take in the surroundings under the faint light—the dusty ground is littered with packaging bags and unidentifiable clutter, making it impossible for you to move around freely.
This place looks more like an abandoned ruin than a lived-in home.
You can't see your way clearly in the dark. You swat at the buzzing flies as you carefully tread over all the obstacles, but still end up kicking a coffee table.
The table's legs screech against the floor as the bottles and jars on top tumble to the ground. The clatter echoes loudly across the silent room, startling even yourself.
...Are you sure they're really still here?

speaker: Lamia
content: Have some patience. Look, don't you see someone coming?
Only then do you notice the rustling sounds from the next room. You look over and see a blurry figure approaching slowly.
When the figure gets up close, you see that it's a disheveled woman.
She's holding a tray of something you can't make out. Her face is grimy, and her hair and clothes are a mess. She practically looks like a zombie.
You stare at the strange woman nervously, ready to defend yourself. However, she passes by you as if you don't exist.
...She can't see me?

speaker: Lamia
content: That's right. She only has her husband and daughter in her eyes. Follow her and keep observing.
You follow the woman across the living room to a bedroom. You peek inside curiously, but all you can see in the darkness is the outline of a small bed, where a middle-aged man is sitting.
She knocks on the door frame and enters with a smile.

speaker: Woman
content: Have some tea I just made, dear.

speaker: Man
content: Oh, why did you do it yourself again? What do we have a cook and servants for? Just leave this kind of thing to them. Don't tire yourself out.
The man gets up from the bed, takes the tray from the woman and puts it on the desk beside him. Only then do you see what's on the tray...

The cup is filled with murky liquid that gives off a foul sour odor, and there seems to be something wriggling among the ancient food scraps in the plate. You quickly turn away, your stomach churning.

speaker: Woman
content: Don't worry, I'm fine. It's my little hobby.
The woman seems to be quite receptive to the man's concern, and smiles in contentment.

speaker: Girl
content: Mommy! Do we have any of those lemon tarts I like?
The crisp voice of a child rings out from behind the man. Only then do you notice another person under the pile of blankets. You sneak over as they chat to take a look.
But what you see makes you gasp in horror...
An emaciated little girl with gaunt cheeks lies motionless on her back. She doesn't even have the strength to get up, but is still giggling non-stop as if she can't feel the pain.
In stark contrast to the bubbly vigor in her voice, you see a gravely ill child who has withered away before getting the chance to bloom.

speaker: Woman
content: Of course we do. Mommy made them just for you. It's to reward my baby for being top of the class again.

speaker: Girl
content: Wow, all right! I'll make sure to be top of the class forever!

speaker: Man
content: Hahaha, it seems that I'm in for a treat thanks to my daughter.

speaker: Woman
content: The lemon tarts are for our daughter, but this chocolate muffin is to celebrate your promotion, dear! If it weren't for your hard work, we wouldn't be able to live in such a luxurious house...
You watch as the family lives out their happy fantasy in the suffocating, bug-infested darkness. The absurd and disturbing contrast makes you break out in cold sweat.
Your incredulous frown seems to amuse Lamia. She opens up her arms as if presenting a masterpiece.

speaker: Lamia
content: Their daughter's illness has no cure, but I helped them out. Look how happy they are now.
This isn't helping them.

speaker: Lamia
content: Why isn't it? I never impose upon anyone. They were the ones who asked me to fulfill their wish at all costs. I just helped them to see what they wanted to see, and they are quite happy in their illusion.
But none of it's real.

speaker: Lamia
content: It's their own choice. Reality is too painful for them. They don't have the means or courage to solve their problems, so they seek comfort in fantasy. Aren't all human beings like this?
No, I don't think everyone's like that.

speaker: Lamia
content: Ha, if you don't believe me, go ask them yourself.
Hmm...
Lamia grabs your hand, and the scene in front of you begins to distort.
When you come back to your senses again, you find yourself standing in a warm and lovely children's room.
The dilapidated ruins around you have disappeared without a trace, replaced by pink wallpaper, cartoon bedding, plush dolls, and spotless floors and table tops.

speaker: Woman
content: Ah, if it isn't the Messenger! What brought you here all of a sudden?
You hear the woman's surprised gasp. She quickly goes forward and takes Lamia's hand.

speaker: Woman
content: You should've told me you were coming. I didn't make any preparations...
Lamia pats the woman's hand with a smile.

speaker: Lamia
content: No need for such formalities, my dear Seafarer.

speaker: Man
content: O Messenger! We couldn't be happier to see you! Alas, if it weren't for you, those quack doctors would've killed my daughter... You are our family's great savior! W-we really don't know how to thank you!
The man leads his daughter over, beaming happily like his wife.

The little girl looks at you and Lamia in curiosity, her big round eyes sparkling and her cherub cheeks a healthy pink. She looks completely different from the gaunt, bedridden skeleton you saw just now.

speaker: Lamia
content: Don't thank me. It's your sincerity that moved the soul of the deep sea. I simply helped to the best of my ability. I'm very glad to see how happy you are now.

speaker: Man
content: We're very happy indeed! We've never been happier in our lives!
The man hugs his wife and daughter tightly as he speaks.

speaker: Woman
content: Yeah, our daughter is everything to us. We're willing to pay whatever cost to restore her health. Why, I'd gladly pay with my own life, let alone a small membership fee!

speaker: Man
content: Besides, whatever money we spend, we can earn back. I used to be a workaholic and neglected my family. When I finally realized it, it was too late... But fortunately, you gave me a second chance, O Messenger!

speaker: Man
content: Now my boss appreciates me more than ever. My workload has reduced, while my salary has more than doubled! Everything keeps getting better and better! I'm also trying to be a better husband and a better father.

speaker: Woman
content: Our daughter is also doing great. Though she can be naughty at times, she's very smart and hardworking. After recovering and going back to school, she made a lot of new friends, and her teachers all praise her. She's our little angel and I'm so proud of her...

speaker: Girl
content: Mommy! Can I go outside to play for a bit?
Either bashful from being praised or tired of hearing the adults banter, the girl tugs at her mother's sleeve and asks to leave.

speaker: Woman
content: Of course. Just don't go too far.

speaker: Girl
content: I'm off then... Bye Mommy and Daddy! Bye mister! Bye miss!
female_content: I'm off then... Bye Mommy and Daddy! Bye ladies!

content: Before leaving, the well-mannered little girl bids you goodbye. You smile and pat her head. The warm and realistic touch bewilders you.
The woman's eyes brim with tears as she watches her daughter skip into the distance.

speaker: Woman
content: When I got the diagnosis from the hospital, I felt like I had been struck by a bolt of lightning. Terminal illness... We've all seen such things on TV, but who can imagine it happening to their own child?

speaker: Woman
content: She's only eleven. Her life is only beginning! Thank goodness she had the great fortune of meeting you, otherwise... What would she do? What would I do? I can't even begin to imagine...
Choking up again, she and her husband kneel down together and kowtow to Lamia.

speaker: Woman
content: O merciful Ocean Messenger, you're our great savior!

Lamia proudly looks down at the kowtowing pair, as if relishing in some type of success. However, the gentle smile on her face soon vanishes. When she speaks again, there is no trace of warmth in her voice.

speaker: Lamia
content: Sigh, but too bad, your happy days are coming to an end.

speaker: Man
content: W-what do you mean by that?
The couple gets up and looks at Lamia in confusion. Lamia shoots you a taunting look, making sure to enunciate every word:

speaker: Lamia
content: Someone asked me to come here to tell you the truth.

speaker: Woman
content: ...The truth? What truth? I-I don't understand...
The woman follows Lamia's gaze and stares at you, visibly unnerved. Lamia wriggles her eyebrows at you, prompting you to take over the conversation.
You look at the scene around you, then turn your gaze back to the couple huddling together. Their fearful eyes make your heart heavy.
To shatter this piteous family's last hope and illusion, and throw them back into the heart-wrenching despair of reality, is indeed tougher and crueler than you had imagined.
You take a deep breath and finally muster up the courage to speak.
What you see around you is just an illusion. Your child's health is actually getting worse day by day. There is no cure. This is the truth.
After a long silence, the man lets out a dry laugh.

speaker: Man
content: Y-you must be joking... You saw for yourselves, she just went out to play... Sh-she's in good health now! She even won second place in her school race! How can she be...

speaker: Man
content: O Messenger... h-he's lying, isn't he?!
female_content: O Messenger... sh-she's lying, isn't she?!

content: He looks over at Lamia pleadingly, his tone becoming increasingly desperate. Lamia's answer, however, shatters his last bit of hope.

speaker: Lamia
content: I'm sorry.
With a wave of her hand, you all return to the filthy apartment, where the emaciated, bedridden little girl is still struggling to breathe.

As the illusion disappears, the woman slumps to the ground, sobbing into her hands. The man also stumbles back in despair, leaning on a desk to stop himself from falling over. He lets out a low, hopeless chuckle.

speaker: Man
content: I knew it... How could it be so easy... How could we be so lucky... How could fate have spared us so easily?

speaker: Man
content: It's too late... It's too late after all...
Heavy sorrow and despair fills every inch of the room, making it hard for you to breathe.

speaker: Lamia
content: If I let you choose, will you choose to return to reality and live in pain, or for me to wipe your memory and let you keep on living in that happy illusion?

speaker: Woman
content: The illusion! Please wipe my memory and bring back the illusion! Please...
Lamia barely finishes her sentence before the woman yells out her reply without hesitation.
But hiding in that illusion won't really solve the problem.

speaker: Woman
content: Then tell us, how do we solve our problem?! Who can solve it for us? Can you? Can you cure her?
You don't know what to reply. You know there's nothing you can do for them. But if someone really yearned for that illusion so much, they wouldn't be dragged back to reality with just one sentence.

speaker: Woman
content: I know it's just a means of escape... But what's wrong with escaping forever? Reality is just too cruel. How can I keep on living without a shred of hope?

speaker: Woman
content: If I return to reality, I might be able to be with her in her last moments, but here, I have all the time in the world! In the illusion, I can be with her for decades, maybe even forever!

speaker: Woman
content: Here, I can watch her grow up, follow her dreams, and do whatever she wants. I can watch her find love, start a family, and have children of her own... I want to see her live a full life!
But... none of it's real...

speaker: Man
content: Who can say what's real and what's not?

speaker: Man
content: To us, the joy of this illusion is real enough. This is also my choice. We're too tired.
You fall silent. You know that no matter what you say, they won't change their decision.

speaker: Lamia
content: I must say, as one of mankind's rare positive sides, "love" is indeed an incredible thing. It can make a person overcome their innate selfishness and give unconditionally to someone else.

speaker: Lamia
content: But you see, human beings will eventually be weakened, hurt and blinded by it, and consequently lose their minds. Like I said, everything will eventually descend into darkness.

speaker: Lamia
content: Let's go. It's already clear who won.
Lamia starts to activate her power to leave the illusion, but you grab her hand.
There's still someone you haven't asked—the one who is the object of all this love. Her parents' choice is not necessarily her choice.

speaker: Lamia
content: Ridiculous. Even her parents made this choice. You expect the suffering child herself to choose differently?
We won't know till you ask.

speaker: Lamia
content: You... really are the most stubborn person I've ever met. Fine, then. To beat you fair and square, I'll make sure that you have no illusions left whatsoever.
Your surroundings change again. You come to a garden, where the little girl is staring into the distance from a swaying swing. The scene is strangely melancholy.
Lamia walks up to the little girl confidently and asks her the same question.
The girl hesitates for a long time, then gives a surprising answer.

speaker: Girl
content: I... I want to go back to reality.

speaker: Lamia
content: What!?
Lamia can't believe her ears. She grabs the girl by the shoulders somewhat hysterically.

speaker: Lamia
content: Here, you can live a healthy and happy life, and do whatever you want. If you go back to reality, you'll be in constant pain and suffering. You won't be able to run around freely, or even get a good night's sleep...

speaker: Lamia
content: Have you forgotten what that's like?!

speaker: Lamia
content: This cruel and unjust world tormented you so much for no reason. It robbed you of the life you should've had. Why would you want to go back?!
The girl flinches, but still looks courageously into Lamia's eyes.

speaker: Girl
content: Because of Mommy and Daddy.

speaker: Lamia
content: They can be with you in the illusion forever.

speaker: Girl
content: But they're trying to find a way to cure me. They want me to be cured for real.

speaker: Lamia
content: Don't you understand? You can't be cured! Your life is over!
Lamia...
You want to stop her. It's unbearably cruel to tell a child this ugly truth, but the girl just nods and accepts it calmly.

speaker: Girl
content: Life will be over for me soon, but not for Mommy and Daddy. I want to tell them I love them. I want them to start a new life...

speaker: Girl
content: That way, they can live well even outside the illusion. And I would feel... relieved.
The illusion cracks and collapses before your eyes, shattering into dust before vanishing without a trace.

speaker: Lamia
content: How... how could this be... how is this possible...
Lamia stands alone amidst the debris. It's the first time you see true vulnerability and confusion in her eyes.
You walk over and put a gentle hand over her shoulder.

I can't deny that there's more darkness than light in this world. I know that in their powerlessness, most will choose to flee, compromise, or succumb to the darkness when faced with the cruel reality of life.

Yet at the same time, there will always be those who refuse to give up the light, no matter how mired they are. They choose to face and overcome their pain. That's why these glimmers of light in the dark are so precious.

speaker: Lamia
content: They choose to...
She chuckles bitterly.

speaker: Lamia
content: But what about me? All this time, when did I ever get the chance to choose?

options: You have a chance right now.

content: You can choose to bid farewell to the past, let go of your prejudices, and see yourself and the world in a new light.
I've never condemned your way of life. I truly think that you're amazing to have survived such a depressing and hopeless world.
I know most people can't even begin to imagine how much you've suffered, but don't let that make you embrace the darkness and turn your back on the light.

You've never been a freak. Being special is not a bad thing. It means that you're unique. You deserve love, acceptance and admiration. At least when you're with me, in the MBCC, you can let go of all your masks and be your true self.
Lamia falls silent. You know it'll be a long, arduous journey to fully change her views, but at least you're taking the first step together.
The little girl wakes up. She grabs the corner of Lamia's shirt and smiles weakly but earnestly.

speaker: Girl
content: Thank you for granting my wish and bringing us back to reality, miss.

speaker: Girl
content: I didn't get to tell you in the illusion just now, but I think you're really cool and pretty. If I got the chance to grow up, I'd want to be just like you.
You open the heavy curtains. The afterglow of the setting sun instantly disperses the darkness, filling every corner of the room.
There is a lot of dust and grime on the windows, but the warm golden light shines through them, gently illuminating Lamia.
Lamia stands next to the girl's bed, clasping her hands in genuine reverence.
It's as if the sunlight had finally reached the depths of the ocean.
Two sets of documents are neatly placed on the office desk. On the left is a Sinner dispatch report received a few days ago, while on the right is the latest pathology diagnosis report.
test
test
test
test
test
test

During the street operation, the subject disguised as an artist and attracted too much unnecessary attention with her discordant playing.

Throughout the performance, the subject unconsciously released Mania, causing the M-value of the nearby crowd to rise. Despite being stopped and driven away by several onlookers, the subject remained steadfast in performing.

In the end, due to the subject's overly high-profile performance, the undercover mission failed.
Based on observations, Sinner Echo still poses a certain threat to the public. Careful arrangement of her missions is advised.

You simply couldn't understand why, having lost the influence of Lady Pearl's power, Echo's playing level can drop so much that it reaches the level of "public hazard"... until you receive another report.
test
test
test
test
test
test
test
The patient was diagnosed with congenital amusia.

The clinical manifestations of amusia include the inability to discern the accuracy of pitch and the quality of melody.

Patients usually have a strong desire to perform and express themselves, and are not good at discerning others' emotions in communication.

speaker: Chief
content: But this isn't the most difficult part...
You flip to the last page of the report, where Echo's psychological assessment results are...
The patient shows no understanding of this condition and does not believe that she has a physiological disorder.

Due to her past living environment, the patient has subconsciously formed the identity of a "musical genius" and uses it as mental support.

When proposing treatment, please word it carefully to avoid rashly breaking the patient's self-understanding. Otherwise, she could have an emotional breakdown, resulting in an irreversible situation.
You're getting a headache from thinking about how to explain to Echo her situation.
A notification sound snaps you out of your contemplation.

speaker: Communications
content: Sinner Echo is waiting in the interrogation room.

speaker: Chief
content: ...Well, let's see how it goes.
You take a few deep breaths, pick up the two reports, and get up to head for the interrogation room.

speaker: Echo
content: Long time no see, Chief!

speaker: Chief
content: Long time no see, Echo. I called you here today because... there are some things I want to discuss with you.

speaker: Echo
content: Really? What a coincidence! I also have some good news!
Echo is very happy today. You can see that the smile on the girl's face is brighter than usual, perhaps something good has happened.
However, you're the "bad guy" today. You have to burst those beautiful bubbles of happiness, music and dream that wrap her inner world.
After all, if Echo's unaware of her condition, it'll only cause more serious issues for her and others.

speaker: Chief
content: I'm sorry, Echo... I have bad news.

speaker: Echo
content: Bad news? How bad can it be?
Echo shakes her head nonchalantly.

speaker: Echo
content: Based on my years of experience of being homeless... I mean, a performer, there can't be anything worse than the past! What is it?
You hesitate for a moment, but instead of the diagnosis report, you hand her the dispatch feedback report.

speaker: Chief
content: Have a look, it's the performance evaluation of your undercover mission.

speaker: Echo
content: Performance evaluation? Is it for my street performance?!
Echo cheerfully takes the report, and immediately lowers her head to read it.
As the sound of flipping paper gets faster and faster, the smile on her face becomes more and more stiff; in the end, she slaps the report on the table and asks angrily.

speaker: Echo
content: What do these people mean?!

speaker: Chief
content: Calm down, calm down...
You quickly add:

speaker: Chief
content: The MBCC mission report requires detailed and objective information, they are just writing out their observations and thoughts.

speaker: Echo
content: No... they aren't telling the truth!

speaker: Echo
content: Those people gathered around clearly because I played so well! I'm a super talented saxophonist, how could my music possibly be, what, discordant?

speaker: Echo
content: My performance can't be bad! I'm sure of it. You can't wrong me just based on this one report!

speaker: Chief
content: This isn't the only one. There have been many other previous reports on similar situations, I have to take it seriously.

speaker: Chief
content: And I have to be responsible for every Sinner in the Bureau. I'm concerned about your situation and hope to help you find a solution.

speaker: Chief
content: I suspected that you might have some underlying health issues... so I arranged a physical examination for you.

speaker: Chief
content: The examination results show that your perception of pitch is indeed somewhat abnormal.

speaker: Echo
content: Physical examination? Could it be that one...
Echo pauses for a moment, her plump cheeks puff up even more after she realizes.

speaker: Echo
content: I can't believe it, Chief, how could you trick me?!

speaker: Echo
content: You said that was the annual physical examination for Sinners, and you lured me with a lavish meal after the examination! You...

speaker: Chief
content: Cough, you seemed to enjoy the meal, so I didn't exactly lie to you, did I...

speaker: Echo
content: Hmph, there's nothing wrong with me!

speaker: Echo
content: There's no way my music sounds bad! I don't believe you!
Echo decisively refutes you. Through the link of shackles, you feel her confidence in her "excellent" playing skills.
...Obviously, Echo doesn't take your words to heart at all. She is still indulging in her imagination, unwilling to open her eyes.
When proposing treatment, please word it carefully to avoid rashly breaking the patient's self-understanding. Otherwise, she could have an emotional breakdown, resulting in an irreversible situation.
Indirect approach won't get Echo to accept the diagnosis or cooperate with treatment. Yet, because of the suggestions on the medical report, you're not sure how to break the news to her.
"Based on observations, Sinner Echo still poses a certain threat to the public."
But if you let things slide, the Mania that Echo unconsciously brings about will only intensify. Before it gets worse, you have to come up with something to alleviate the current situation.
Seeing you fall silent, Echo seems to think you've finally admitted defeat, and she smugly continues.

speaker: Echo
content: Chief, let me tell you, there are still many people out there who love my music.

speaker: Echo
content: Just the other day, I ran into my old friend, Sally!

speaker: Echo
content: Oh right, you don't know who Sally is. She's an old friend from the orphanage when I was a kid, and she's now in charge there!

speaker: Echo
content: She really liked my performance. She cheered for me, and also invited me to the orphanage's charity concert!

speaker: Echo
content: I reunited with an old friend thanks to my music, and of course, thanks to my little Kute as well!
Echo excitedly hugs her saxophone close and affectionately rubs her cheek against it.

speaker: Echo
content: This is the good news I was gonna tell you! I'm going to play at the concert.
Her expression is so proud and excited, but you still have to dampen her mood.

speaker: Chief
content: But...

speaker: Echo
content: Hey! You tricked me before, and now you're babbling on about how I'm not a good saxophone player!

speaker: Echo
content: I'm really upset now, boohoo... Anyway, I demand compensation!
Before you can finish your sentence, you're interrupted by Echo again.

Regardless of the occasion or urgency of the matter, and without even understanding the meaning behind your words, the young girl is focused on how she feels, and expressing those emotions without any consideration.

speaker: Chief
content: (Okay, this is also one of the symptoms of amusia; she can't help it. Don't get angry at the patient, stay calm, take a deep breath...)

speaker: Echo
content: Chief, you see... There's a reason I really have to go...
Echo suddenly changes her tone, her expression and tone becoming pitiful. Apart from her musical shortcomings, she really is a talented performer.

speaker: He's said too much. Rust's eyes flick skyward, where a violet star drifts past the zenith—the signal from his contact.
content: I once messed up an important performance at the orphanage...

speaker: Echo
content: After that, no one wanted to listen to my singing, and they stopped talking to me. Until I left, no one was willing to watch my performances.

speaker: Echo
content: That was the darkest, most miserable time of my life... I've always wanted to make up for that terrible performance...

speaker: Echo
content: And the opportunity finally came! Sally recognized me from my performance on the street. She acknowledged me as a musician!

speaker: Echo
content: Maybe this is a breakthrough. I can finally redeem myself, and conquer the audience there with a perfect performance!

speaker: Echo
content: Please, Chief, this concert is really important to me! Please let me go!
Echo's passionate plea moves you.
However, considering Echo's special condition, you doubt there would be a normal concert that would invite a musician of her level to participate. Something's fishy.

speaker: Chief
content: Echo, considering the physical condition we just discussed, are you sure your old friend is serious about it? At least sleep on it before you accept.

speaker: Echo
content: Man... I was pouring my heart out here, why are you still hesitating?
Seeing that you're not giving in, Echo doesn't get discouraged. She quickly puts on a bright and cheerful smile.

speaker: Echo
content: Alright, I have an idea... If words can't convince you, then I'll just move you with music!
The self-proclaimed musical genius decisively picks up the saxophone, gets into position, brings her lips to the mouthpiece, and then takes a deep breath...
It's too late.
You can't describe the sound you're hearing.
It's deafening, earth-shaking, and overwhelming... At this moment, the entire world seems to have nothing but this terrifying sound.
The discordant, eerie sound of the saxophone resonates in the enclosed space, forcefully entering your ears, hitting you right in the gut.
You feel like your soul almost got shaken out of your body by this demonic sound. The interrogation room never felt so small before, and the door so far away from your seat.

speaker: Chief
content: Echo... enough...

speaker: Echo
content: What is it, Chief? Are you going to give me permission?

speaker: Echo
content: If you still won't agree... I'll keep playing, even if you go to sleep, I'll be playing by your bed!

speaker: Echo
content: I will play until you're moved by my music!
Echo seems ready to continue, you gasp and quickly shout to stop her.

speaker: Chief
content: ...Alright, that's enough!

speaker: Chief
content: I'm moved, I get it now! You can go, okay?!
The music stops abruptly. Echo opens her eyes wide, looking at you eagerly.

speaker: Echo
content: You promise? No lies? No backing out?

speaker: Chief
content: ...I promise. But on one condition, I have to go to the concert with you, to avoid any accidents.

speaker: Echo
content: Of course, no problem, I will get an invitation for you! It's a deal!
Echo jumps off her seat excitedly, and gives you a big hug. Amid her joyful cheers, you can only smile wryly.
Two days ago.

speaker: Chief
content: ...So that's what we're dealing with. Echo doesn't believe she's tone-deaf and is refusing treatment.

speaker: Chief
content: Therefore, I want to use concert practice as an excuse, and hope you can try to correct some of her issues.

speaker: Joan
content: What does she think about it?

speaker: Chief
content: Echo takes her performance very seriously. She agreed as soon as she heard it's for the concert.

speaker: Joan
content: Alright, nothing difficult if it's just practice sessions.

speaker: Dudu
content: I won't ask for much, the tuition fee is 100,000 DisCoins, paid in one lump sum. What do you say, Chief?

speaker: Peggy
content: Ha! No problem, count on me!
It's been two days since you entrusted Echo to those three musicians.
Today, you finally manage to get away from your busy duties and plan to check on them.

speaker: Chief
content: A rapper, a rock star, a folk musician...

speaker: Chief
content: With those three training her, it should be fine, right...
Wooooo!
However, the reality, despite Echo's denial, is much more brutal than imagined.
A strange, loud noise almost ruptures your eardrums. You rush over immediately and push the door open.

speaker: Peggy
content: Finally, you're here!
Peggy pulls you aside with lightning speed, followed closely by Joan and Dudu.
And you notice that Echo is playing the saxophone with her eyes closed, completely engrossed. The terrifying sound just now came from that brass instrument.

speaker: Peggy
content: I'm telling you, this is much more serious than what you told us!

speaker: Peggy
content: Are you sure you want her to play at that concert? For real?

speaker: Dudu
content: I demand injury compensation!

speaker: Dudu
content: Every day I head back, I almost forget how to play my suona. As soon as I pick it up, I feel a buzzing in my head.

speaker: Joan
content: Echo's pitch is terrible, she's always out of tune.

speaker: Joan
content: I played the guitar better than her when I was three!
It's clear that everyone has been tormented by Echo's "demonic sound." They complain to you one after another, and you can only smile apologetically.

speaker: Chief
content: Thanks for your hard work, really! I wouldn't know what to do without you all...

speaker: Chief
content: So, how's the rehearsal going...?

speaker: Joan
content: ...There's still some progress, I guess.

speaker: Joan
content: Echo's memory is not bad. Apart from the music scores, she can remember every fingering and skill that has been demonstrated to her.

speaker: Dudu
content: But correcting movements doesn't ensure the pitch is accurate...
Dudu adds in a melancholic tone.

speaker: Dudu
content: A wind instrument player also needs to pay attention to lip control and breathing rhythm, which is hard for people with a poor sense of pitch to learn by listening.

speaker: Dudu
content: So we can only ask Echo to play over and over again, and we listen and correct her errors so that she memorizes the correct playing method. Although she has improved, but meanwhile...

speaker: Peggy
content: Our ears and mental health have suffered immensely!

speaker: Chief
content: I know it's not easy for you guys... Don't worry! I'll do my best to fulfill the requests you mentioned before!

speaker: Chief
content: Whether it's Peggy's equipment, Joan's new album, or... Dudu's injury compensation, I'll fight for it!
After your reassurance and a series of promises, the trio finally look much less resentful.

speaker: Dudu
content: ...Let's make it clear, Chief.

speaker: Dudu
content: This training method can only allow Echo to barely play these few pieces correctly. It's not helping her amusia at all.

speaker: Chief
content: For now, it's good enough. Let's just get through that concert first, it's fine as long as she doesn't continue to spread Mania to the general public with her noise.

speaker: Chief
content: We'll talk about the treatment later.

speaker: Dudu
content: Well then! Now...

speaker: Peggy
content: You must stay here with us!!!

speaker: Chief
content: Alright, alright...
Being held "hostage," you have no choice but to stay and experience this "captivating and bewitching melody."
Even so, you still feel a sense of relief in this situation—After all, Echo's performance has indeed improved. She sounds much better than before.

speaker: Chief
content: ...Thank goodness, there's still hope.
When Echo sees you, she excitedly raises her saxophone. You respond with an encouraging smile, and she plays even more passionately.
For the next few hours, you keep on smiling until your facial muscles are about to go stiff. Although you don't give anything away, you fully understand the pain of Dudu and the others.
The three who have been tortured all day can't endure like you anymore, their faces looking even worse than before—they're barely holding on.
You immediately stand up and clap your hands.

speaker: Chief
content: That's it for today! Joan, Dudu, Peggy, thank you, head back and get some rest!
The three let out a sigh of relief. They rush out the door one after another, not willing to stay a moment longer.

speaker: Chief
content: You did well too, Echo. Now, maybe we can start designing the stage for the performance?

speaker: Chief
content: Stage design is also a part of the performance, right?

speaker: Echo
content: Of course, you always think of everything, Chief.
After wiping her saxophone, Echo carefully puts it away, then enthusiastically takes out a variety of strange props and decorations.
The props are a mix of everything, old, chipped, ruggedly shaped, you name it. But they're all very clean, clearly well cared for by their owner.

speaker: Echo
content: I got these ribbons from a bakery owner. She had some extra left from packing her cakes. I scraped off the cream on them, tasted pretty good!

speaker: Echo
content: These balloons were from a school's art festival. I deflated them and smuggled them out before the cleaners arrived!

speaker: Echo
content: And these were picks left behind by street bands, I strung them together. Usually, when a show ends, many picks are left on the ground...

speaker: Echo
content: Oh, right, how could I forget my favorite teddy bear and drumming monkey! They were thank-you gifts I received for helping a toy store owner move his storage all day!

speaker: Echo
content: Look at this monkey, I heard it used to move... What a pity, if it wasn't broken, it could have joined my performance.
Echo vividly recounts the stories behind each prop. It seems, to her, they aren't just trash picked up from the streets, but rare and precious gifts in her life.
Then, she picks up a few pages of torn sheet music, carefully cradling them in front of her chest, her face beaming with joy.

speaker: Echo
content: I really wish I could have a perfect, awe-inspiring performance just like those legendary bands...

speaker: Echo
content: The audience would applaud me, cheer for me, and praise the saxophone as the most charming instrument in the world!

speaker: Echo
content: Most importantly, if they acknowledge me, they will feel the power of the saxophone music—the music that gives me strength and hope in the coldest winter nights!
Her expression becomes very serious, as if she's declaring some grand ambition.

speaker: Chief
content: Why "the coldest winter nights" specifically?

speaker: Echo
content: Because... Eastside's winters are very cold, especially at night. It feels like a bunch of needles hitting your bones when the wind blows your way.

speaker: Echo
content: The underpass is a great spot to hide from the cold. Last year, I had my eye on one for the winter since autumn, but another group of people took over my "home" and forced me out onto the streets...

speaker: Echo
content: It was a holiday that day, every house was warmly lit... but not a single door, not a single light belonged to me.

speaker: Echo
content: I was cold and hungry, and when I felt like I couldn't hold on any longer, I heard an incredibly beautiful melody in my daze...
The moment she mentions that "beautiful melody," a smile of bliss emerges on Echo's face.

speaker: Echo
content: I followed the sound to the brightest spot on the street, which seemed to be a theater with many people singing and dancing inside.

speaker: Echo
content: But I didn't care about that, I pressed my face against the window, wanting to listen carefully to that dreamy and gentle melody...

speaker: Echo
content: Finally, I heard it clearly, a warm, enchanting sound...!

speaker: Echo
content: As I listened, the cold and hunger were gone, and my body was once again filled with inexhaustible strength!
She clenches her fists, her eyes shining, and yells excitedly:

speaker: Echo
content: It was like a miracle!

speaker: Chief
content: That's... quite an amazing experience...

speaker: Echo
content: Yes! So I believed that was a form of art, a very noble and sacred one!

speaker: Echo
content: After the melody ended, people came out from the theatre. I grabbed them and asked what that music was, and a kind person told me, it was saxophone!

speaker: Chief
content: Wait, the saxophone piece during the theatre's closing...
You recall your experience at the Fortuna Theater and instantly understand what Echo had heard.

speaker: Echo
content: Is something wrong?

speaker: Chief
content: ...No, nothing. So, after that, you fell in love with saxophone?

speaker: Echo
content: Yeah! I was super lucky. I found a saxophone in a discarded box by the theatre's door, and that became my Kute! It's old, but in good condition, and can play great tunes.

speaker: Echo
content: I even found a few saxophone textbooks and sheet music next to it! Hehe, I, Echo, the once-in-a-century musical genius just read those books once, and completely mastered it!

speaker: Echo
content: And I decided, I want to become a legendary saxophonist, and perform for everyone around the world, connecting with them and touching their heart with my music!

speaker: Echo
content: This is my lifelong mission!
Echo dramatically spreads her arms wide and lifts her head, lost in her overwhelming emotions.
You have to admit, disregarding her actual playing level, this is indeed an inspiring and touching fairytale-like story.
A warmth fills your chest, you can't help but be moved by her passion. You probably understand why being a "genius saxophonist" is such an important thing to her...
Saxophone and music have become the reason for Echo to keep going. Therefore, she refuses to admit that she has a condition that might stop her from achieving this "perfect goal."
If she admits it, that means she has to give up her dream, and her ideal life.

speaker: Chief
content: ...I didn't know you have such a big ambition.
You pat Echo's head, and give her a thumbs-up.

speaker: Chief
