content: In that case, you need to keep practicing. I heard from Dudu and the others that there is a lot you need to improve on in your performance.

speaker: Echo
content: I know! I'll give my best!

speaker: Chief
content: I believe that as long as you keep working hard, you'll be able to play the best music at the concert.

speaker: Echo
content: That's what I've been saying. You just didn't believe me!

speaker: Echo
content: In that case, on the day of the concert, you have to enjoy my perfect performance from the audience!

speaker: Chief
content: Alright, I'll be there.

speaker: Chief
content: I'll be watching you from the audience, supporting you. I'll be your most loyal spectator no matter what.
Echo's eyes sparkle with joy as she gives you an enthusiastic thumbs up.

speaker: Echo
content: You made a promise. Don't go missing on that day!

speaker: Sally
content: Welcome back, Echo!
When Echo arrives, Sally warmly greets her at the door with a hug, just like how they used to when they were in the orphanage. After that failed performance, Echo never got a hug again.

speaker: Echo
content: Thank you for welcoming me, Sally! I've practiced a few of my best pieces, I won't mess up the performance again!

speaker: Sally
content: Great... I'm looking forward to it.
Sally nods with a smile and leads her inside before going off to attend to other things. Inside the auditorium, the charity concert is about to start and the audience is gradually taking their seats.
So, Echo finds an empty seat and sits down, thinking about Chief who was held up by an urgent task, and the conversation they had just before she left.

speaker: Chief
content: Echo, I promise, as soon as the mission is over, I'll rush to the concert.

speaker: Chief
content: Trust me, a promise is a promise. I'll definitely be there, as your most loyal spectator.
Hi, are you one of the performers today?
A sudden question from the side catches Echo off guard, and she notices that the spectators around her are eyeing her and the instrument in her hands.

speaker: Echo
content: Yes, that's right!

speaker: Spectator A
content: Your saxophone is quite unique. Seems like you cherish it a lot.

speaker: Echo
content: Yes, it's called Kute. It's my best friend and my best partner!

speaker: Spectator A
content: Haha, it even has a name?

speaker: Echo
content: Yes! It's been with me for a very long time. Even though it looks old, it can still make the most wonderful sounds!
The number of people chatting with Echo increases, and the girl can hardly contain her excitement. She feels that she made the right choice by coming here today!

speaker: Spectator B
content: The performance won't start for a while, could you give us a little preview?

speaker: Echo
content: Hmm... I'll save the pieces I prepared for later. For now, I'll improvise a little something for everyone!
Echo raises her saxophone with a serious look, closes her eyes, and starts playing with all her heart.
In her head, beautiful notes are constantly flowing out of the brass tube, spreading joy in the air, and all the listeners are intoxicated by it...
As the melody ends, a satisfied smile forms on Echo's lips as she slowly opens her eyes.
However, the faces around her aren't smiling like her, but rather showing a variety of strange expressions.

Some people are twitching at the corners of their eyes, some look pale, and some even cover their ears tightly. When they notice her gaze, they hurriedly lower their hands and awkwardly tug at the corners of their mouths.

speaker: Spectator A
content: Uh, not bad, that's some... unique music...

speaker: Spectator B
content: I need to go to the restroom, excuse me...
No applause nor praise, unlike what she expected. The audience who were just curious about her scatter like birds. Before Echo can react and think about it, Sally comes over and holds Echo's wrist.

speaker: Sally
content: The performance is about to start, let's go backstage.
Her old friend, Sally, has a polite smile on her face. Echo can only nod, hold her saxophone tightly, and follow her.

speaker: Echo
content: Why hasn't Chief arrived yet...
While Echo is rehearsing the pieces she's going to play in her head, she keeps checking her terminal, but the person she is waiting for never sends a message.

speaker: Sally
content: Echo, you're up next, are you ready?

speaker: Echo
content: Sally, I think I might need to wait a bit longer...

speaker: Sally
content: Why? I thought you were looking forward to getting on stage.

speaker: Echo
content: Because, I'm waiting for someone important...

speaker: Echo
content: Can I swap places with other performers? Just move my performance to a later slot.

speaker: Echo
content: My spectator hasn't arrived yet, we agreed that I have to wait for him before I can start my performance...
female_content: My spectator hasn't arrived yet, we agreed that I have to wait for her before I can start my performance...

content: After hearing Echo's somewhat incoherent request, Sally shakes her head, looking slightly troubled.

speaker: Sally
content: You're the last one, Echo.

speaker: Sally
content: If you don't go on stage... I can only tell them the concert is over.

speaker: Echo
content: Ah... in that case...

speaker: Sally
content: It's your call. But if that person is really looking forward to your performance, and you give up now, wouldn't it be even more disappointing to him?
female_content: It's your call. But if that person is really looking forward to your performance, and you give up now, wouldn't it be even more disappointing to her?

speaker: Echo
content: Hmm, You're right... Let's go then!
The curtain rises, the lights fall, and the young saxophonist is personally led to the center of the stage by the concert organizer.

speaker: Spectator A
content: Um... Isn't she the terrible saxophone player from earlier...
As soon as they see her, the audience who have heard Echo's playing before start to discuss among themselves.

speaker: Spectator B
content: She's really a performer? I thought she was just messing around.

speaker: Spectator C
content: Yeah, how come you guys really let her on stage? My kid cried after listening to her earlier!
They clamor, telling others how awful Echo's performance was, and loudly question Sally as to why she would invite such a poor musician for the final performance of the day.

speaker: Sally
content: Please, everyone, may I have your attention?
Sally calmly brings the microphone to her lips, soothing the audience with a smile.

speaker: Sally
content: Everyone is used to hearing beautiful and elegant music, but have you ever tried those fresh and intriguing tunes?

speaker: Sally
content: There's a rumor going around Eastside. A notorious homeless, known for their oddity, plays all sorts of discordant tunes on the streets. They say that noise is even more horrifying than the shrieks of a Corruptor...

speaker: Spectator C
content: I think I've heard this rumor before...

speaker: Spectator D
content: Is that true? Can someone really play such a ridiculous sound?

speaker: Spectator C
content: If that sounds anything like what she played... that might be true.

speaker: Spectator D
content: Interesting, I'd like to hear it!

speaker: Sally
content: So, to satisfy everyone's curiosity, I've invited a special guest today.

speaker: Sally
content: Yes, you've guessed it! The one on stage right now is the tone-deaf musician whose skills are worse than a third-rate artist's, yet more flamboyant and confident than a superstar. Let's give it up for the "fourth-rate artist," Echo!

speaker: Sally
content: Now, please enjoy her saxophone solo performance!
The applause is thunderous, and the audience stops protesting. But Echo just stands there, looking lost...

speaker: Sally
content: What's the matter, Echo? Why aren't you starting? Everyone is waiting for you.
Seeing that Echo hasn't started playing, Sally steps forward and holds her in her arms, as gentle as when she first welcomed her.
Echo trembles in her arms, trying hard to maintain her usual cheerful tone, her voice shaking as she speaks.

speaker: Echo
content: Sally, stop joking around, this isn't funny at all...

speaker: Echo
content: Do you know? I've been preparing for today's concert for a long time!

speaker: Echo
content: Three other excellent musicians have been helping me rehearse... My performance tonight will be the most exciting one!

speaker: Echo
content: Also, do you remember when we used to live together in the orphanage? ...Back then you all praised my singing, clapped for me, and said that I would definitely become a superstar when I grew up...

speaker: Echo
content: Now I'm here to prove it to you, you were right, I...!

speaker: Echo
content: ...What you said... tone-deaf, noise... You were just joking, right?

speaker: Sally
content: ...You're still so naive, Echo.
Sally sighs helplessly.

speaker: Sally
content: It's time to wake up from your dream. You've grown up, but you haven't become a superstar, have you?

speaker: Sally
content: After all these years, you still seriously believe those lies we told you? I'm telling you the truth out of the goodness of my heart and you don't believe it. You're... such a fool.
Echo freezes, looking incredulously at the girl in front of her, trying to find any hint of a joke on her face.
But she fails. The face of her old friend, hidden in the shadows, is full of mockery. Sally leans into Echo's ear and whispers, each word she utters is heart-wrenching.

speaker: Sally
content: You want to know the truth? Alright then... You were a joke when you were so engrossed in your playing even though you were completely out of tune. In the dull and boring orphanage, you were the only fun we had.

speaker: Sally
content: In order to keep this "fun," we agreed to lie to you, just so you wouldn't discover the truth.

speaker: Sally
content: But we didn't expect that you would have no self-awareness at all, and even made a fool of yourself at the most important annual party, turning everyone else into a joke!
Many years ago, an annual party at the Eastside Orphanage.
Ribbons, burst balloons, and instruments scatter all over the floor, the audience whispering in hushed voices.

speaker: Adopter A
content: Oh my goodness, she's so off-key... Does she have some kind of condition? Why didn't the institution take her to a check-up?

speaker: Adopter B
content: No way, are the children in this orphanage all like this...?

speaker: Adopter C
content: I can't take a child with a hidden illness home. Excuse me, I'm leaving.

speaker: Sponsor
content: This is how you planned your annual party, by having a tone-deaf kid on stage? This is a disaster!

speaker: Dean
content: We are truly sorry, we didn't know she would suddenly run up on stage, it was an oversight...

speaker: Dean
content: Echo! You little brat! Do you have any idea what you've done tonight?!

speaker: Little Sally
content: ...I heard from the volunteer teachers that the people who were ready to adopt have decided not to come. Many of the ongoing adoptions have also been terminated.

speaker: Orphan A
content: It's all Echo's fault! She insisted on going up to sing! She ruined everything!

speaker: Orphan B
content: Does she really think she sings well with that voice? It was so out-of-tune, how embarrassing!

speaker: Orphan C
content: Sob... I don't want to stay in the orphanage... Sob sob... I won't talk to her ever again...

speaker: Orphan A
content: Let's shut that annoying mouth from now on. Shut her up! That's what happens to bad guys! She deserves it!

speaker: Sally
content: You remember now? What a harsh world, right? I was also one of the children whose adoption was canceled back then.

speaker: Sally
content: Since then, no one has come to adopt me, and the orphanage has been quiet since, it's no different from an overgrown garden.

speaker: Sally
content: Ordinary music concerts can't attract the attention of the public these days, so I need a new gimmick to make everyone notice us, and that's you, Echo.
Sally says with a smirk, cruelly bursting the fragile bubble that has been wrapping Echo's beautiful dream.

speaker: Sally
content: If you don't believe me, look at the audience. Whether they've heard you before or not, they're all expecting what horrible sounds you can make.
Echo stiffly looks around at the audience, where every pair of eyes is filled with curiosity and mockery.
This malicious attention, completely different from what she imagined, makes Echo shiver, as if she's back in that icy winter night. But this time, there's no miraculous melody to save her.

speaker: Sally
content: You see now? Very good.

speaker: Sally
content: I'm glad you haven't improved at all. This is the opportunity for you to make amends. This is what you owe us.
When you hastily arrive at the concert venue, this is what you see.
Echo, with her head down, is in a young woman's embrace, clutching her saxophone as if it were her last lifeline.
Her face is flushed red, even the freckles on her nose are crinkled together, her eyes are brimming with tears, but she stubbornly refuses to let them fall.

Through the shackles, you sense that Echo is on the verge of a breakdown... She's shaken, questioning herself after persisting for years; she's in pain, because her fantasy has been shattered, and the harsh reality is right in her face.

speaker: Chief
content: I'm here, Echo!
You immediately jump onto the stage and grab Echo's hand. As you pull her away from Sally, you can feel she's trembling.

speaker: Echo
content: Chief, you're finally here...

speaker: Echo
content: Tell me, is my playing really that bad?

speaker: Echo
content: Am I really sick, like you said? Was all my effort just a joke in everyone's eyes?
Before you can answer, the audience starts to stir. All they see is a performer wasting their time and you who appear out of nowhere. The voices of dissatisfaction in the crowd grow louder.

speaker: Audience
content: What's going on, why hasn't the performance started yet!

speaker: Sally
content: Sir, you...
female_content: Miss, you...

speaker: Chief
content: Please, give us a moment.
You raise your hand to stop her from approaching. Ignoring the surroundings, you cup Echo's face with your hands, making her focus on you. You tell her in your softest, most determined voice.

speaker: Chief
content: That's not true, Echo.

speaker: Chief
content: You're not a joke, and your efforts aren't meaningless. After practicing and training all this time, you've proven your capabilities.

speaker: Chief
content: Echo, you've improved. Your playing has gotten much better, your music is not just terrible noises now. Even Dudu and the others are proud of your training results. So believe in yourself.

speaker: Echo
content: But I'm tone deaf, I...

speaker: Chief
content: Tone-deafness is a symptom of amusia, but it's not your fault. Don't blame yourself for something you can't control.

speaker: Chief
content: Echo, think about why you have to come here.

speaker: Chief
content: You said you want to return to this stage and make up for that performance with a perfect one.

speaker: Echo
content: But I...

speaker: Chief
content: Remember everything Dudu and the others taught you.

speaker: Chief
content: Those fingerings, techniques, breathing rhythms, and the saxophone playing method that I don't quite understand. Your memory is outstanding, as long as you can recall those muscle memories, you can do it.
Echo takes a deep breath, fuddling with the saxophone in her hand, her nervous expression slightly eased.

speaker: Echo
content: ...You'll be watching me in the audience, right?

speaker: Chief
content: Of course, I promised you. When you play, I'll be watching and supporting you in the audience.

speaker: Chief
content: Even if everyone here thinks you're a joke, to me, you're always a promising saxophonist.

speaker: Echo
content: ...Yes!
Echo smiles, nodding at you firmly. Her eyes are brimming with tears, but her heart no longer wavers. At this moment, she feels like she's been saved by another miracle.
The girl stands in the center of the stage, the spotlight shining on her, like a streetlight on a winter night.
She closes her eyes.
What is she thinking about? That near-death cold night, or her somewhat unique life now?
Or perhaps it's the orphanage life after she was forced to stop singing, or the carefree happiness from her nomadic days?
None of that matters now. You know that, to Echo, the most important thing is here and now, she plays her own, living tune with the saxophone.

speaker: Saxophone
content: Woooo!

The music ends. It's not a horrifically discordant tune as imagined, but a smooth, occasionally off-key rendition of a few classic pieces. The rowdy audience suddenly loses interest, applauding half-heartedly.

speaker: Spectator D
content: That's it? Just an average beginner, not terribly off-putting.

speaker: Spectator C
content: Well, it's much better than when she was playing before the concert...
Echo opens her eyes, not to look at the audience's reaction, but to search for you. The moment she finds you, she hugs her saxophone, jumps off the stage, and rushes towards you.

speaker: Echo
content: Chief, Chief! How was it?

speaker: Chief
content: Very good. To me, that was a perfect performance!

speaker: Echo
content: Really? I was actually very nervous just now...

speaker: Dudu
content: It was really good. You've improved a lot, totally worth our long practice sessions. Well done!

speaker: Echo
content: Dudu, Joan, Peggy... How come you're all here!
Echo looks at the three who suddenly appeared in disbelief, too stunned to speak.

speaker: Peggy
content: We couldn't stop worrying about you, so we came with Chief. We listened to the whole thing!

speaker: Joan
content: I'm quite satisfied with the performance, but this is the result of your own persistence and hard work.
As Joan speaks, she takes out a pick and places it in Echo's palm.

speaker: Joan
content: You like collecting these things, right? Here, a new one for you. Let's keep playing together in the future. Your style might be unconventional, but if you find the right path, you can create unique music.

speaker: Joan
content: But it will be a difficult path. Now that you understand your own situation, give it some thought.

speaker: Echo
content: I-I... Of course, it would be an honor to play with you!
Unable to find any words to express her emotions, the tears Echo's been holding back finally fall.
After the concert, you return to the Bureau with your Sinners.
Although it was quite eventful, fortunately, things turned out alright. On your way back, Echo has agreed to the treatment for amusia.

speaker: Echo
content: Chief, do you know? Before you showed up, I was about to give up.
You listen quietly, not interrupting her heartfelt confession.

speaker: Echo
content: The moment I found out the truth, I realized that I'm not some genius musician. I can't play perfect music with the saxophone. It was all my wishful thinking.

speaker: Echo
content: And those imaginations... were once my motivation to keep on living.
Echo takes a deep breath, trying hard to hold back her tears.

speaker: Echo
content: I should have given up when my fantasy was shattered, but I heard your voice.

speaker: Echo
content: With such a warm voice, you told me that there's always a turning point, that I can still continue my performance on stage. You gave me courage and strength.

speaker: Echo
content: So I think... perhaps I can turn fantasy into a dream with hard work... If I could play a normal tune by practicing, I might be able to achieve my goal.

speaker: Echo
content: I'm still a little scared... but I've decided to try to accept my flaw. I want to tell people with my music that, just like me, everyone can be saved in times of despair and helplessness.

speaker: Echo
content: The saxophone saved me last time, this time it was you. Thank you, Chief.

speaker: Choice
options: It wasn't just your saxophone, or me.

speaker: Chief
content: You saved yourself too. Everything you've been through, the path you've taken... these have all become the strength to keep you going.

speaker: Chief
content: Those who can bravely face reality and choose to start over can certainly play more powerful music.

speaker: Chief
content: I'm still waiting for your exclusive concert, the most-promising saxophonist.
Echo laughs heartily, this time, the corners of her eyes are adorned with tears of gratitude.

speaker: Echo
content: Someday, my most loyal spectator!
Under the streetlights on a winter night, a homeless girl picks up a worn saxophone at the entrance of the theatre, carefully cradling it in her arms.
This night will be free of sorrow, and this winter will not be long and harsh.
In your stuffy office where the air hangs heavy and still, you silently leaf through a medical report about Wuhuanzi's patients.
As you read on, your brow furrows in confusion. You're reading the words, but you're not understanding anything.

speaker: Chief
content: Drinking water mixed with paper talisman ashes, sticking talismans on people's bodies, making patients dig up weeds, acupuncture... These treatment methods sure seem familiar to you.

speaker: Chief
content: After what happened at the fete, nothing surprises me anymore.
Nightingale gives a slight smile as you turn the pages, coming across the patients' latest physical examination results.

speaker: Nightingale
content: The Bureau arranged medical examinations for these patients, and well... They're all in good shape. Healthier than before, even.

speaker: Chief
content: Eastian medicine... is truly beyond our understanding.
You stroke your chin thoughtfully, setting aside your doubts for now as you pick up another report—this one tracking her movements.

speaker: Nightingale
content: After entering DisCity, Wuhuanzi ran street clinics in crowded areas. Despite her low fees, she attracted few patients. She would also often get driven away by security officers for practicing without a license.

speaker: Chief
content: It's understandable that DisCity residents would be wary of such a young traveling doctor claiming to be from Eastia.
Even if her skills are genuine, those treatment methods would scare quite a few people away. You add inwardly while unconsciously checking for nonexistent acupuncture marks on your body.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Eventually she reached the Drifter Camp and stayed there for a while before continuing her medical practice elsewhere, until she got involved in the Wisteria Mania incident. After that, she remained there offering free medical services. For good karma, she said.

speaker: Chief
content: ...For <color=#fb9259>good karma</color>.
She kept mentioning this word during the fete too. What exactly does good karma mean? You were too busy recovering your Qi to ask back then, but perhaps now is a good time to find out.

speaker: Chief
content: Has she shown any changes since joining the Bureau?
Nightingale shakes her head and looks up from her device.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Since joining the Bureau, she's been proactively offering treatment to both Sinners and staff members. She's not offended when they refuse either. She simply returns after some time and offers her service again like it's some kind of routine check-up.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, Wuhuanzi's Interrogation is scheduled for two days from now. Do we need more time for observation? Also, should we stop her from providing unauthorized medical treatment within the Bureau?

Instead of answering Nightingale right away, you tap your fingers thoughtfully on the desk. While Wuhuanzi's behavior seems consistent with her pattern since her arrival in DisCity, something about it feels off.
According to these two reports, Wuhuanzi never stays in one place for too long, and she appears to show no interest in following up on her patients' conditions.
Just like at the Bureau, patients everywhere are often skeptical and refuse her treatment. But rather than showing any frustration, she simply moves on to the next potential patient.

Day after day, she lives this life of constant rejection and suspicion, showing neither desire nor initiative. You begin to wonder if her medical practice is just another part of her well-programmed routine.
Rather than curing her patients thoroughly, Wuhuanzi seems more concerned with treating as many people as possible. Almost as if she's trying to... meet some kind of performance quota.

speaker: Chief
content: No need. We'll proceed with the interrogation as scheduled. As for how to handle her unauthorized medical practice, the interrogation should give us our answers.
In the interrogation room, the petite Eastian girl sits stiffly in her chair.
She takes a brief glance around the claustrophobic room, showing neither panic nor anxiety. Instead, she sits in silence, waiting for your arrival.
You turn on the light. Due to a faulty connection, it flickers several times before finally staying on.
Wuhuanzi instinctively raises her hand to shield her eyes. Realizing the light isn't as harsh as she expected, she slowly lowers it.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Phew, that's a relief... I thought this would be the fifth light I would have broken since coming to the Bureau.

speaker: Chief
content: Relax. The Bureau's equipment is sturdier than that.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: My friend, your complexion has worsened during the days I didn't see you. Ashen face, furrowed brow, lifeless eyes, pale lips...

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Did you bring me to this private cell today so I could give you a special consultation?
Her eyes are largely hidden behind thick bangs, making her expression unreadable, but in her quiet muttering, you detect some sort of... enthusiasm?

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: One must never turn a blind eye to their ailments, however mild they might be. As fortune would have it, I wrote a new healing talisman just yesterday...

Wuhuanzi leans forward and pulls a bright yellow talisman from her wide sleeve. You wave your hands frantically in refusal, terrified that she might burn it into ashes and force you to drink them any second now.

speaker: Chief
content: I'm in reasonably good health, thank you.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: ...Very well, you can come to me for treatment whenever you need it.
Wuhuanzi looks unbothered. Seemingly used to this kind of response, she tucks the talisman back into her sleeve and meticulously straightens the cuff.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Eastian medicine focuses on observing one's vital energy, predicting its course, and treating ailments before they manifest. It's simply a different approach from DisCity's prevailing medical theories.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: As the saying goes, prevention is better than cure. Best not to wait until the illness becomes untreatable...
As Wuhuanzi rattles off an incomprehensible stream of medical terms, you feel like she's practically writing your epitaph already.

You've interrogated many Sinners before, and plenty tried to dodge questions with sweet talk and tall tales. But this is the first time someone has tried to distract you with an entire medical lecture.
She still sounds like that concerned young healer you know, but unlike during the fete incident, there's no real risk of Qi depletion for you anymore.
If not for your extensive interrogation experience, her elaborate medical discourse might have successfully diverted you from the matter at hand.

speaker: Chief
content: Thanks for the Eastian medicine crash course. Let's set that aside for now.

speaker: Chief
content: Pay careful attention to my following questions. Your answers to them will determine the level of supervision you'll be placed under.
With the medical discussion over, Wuhuanzi reverts to her usual gloomy self. She adjusts her clothes and shrinks back into her chair.

speaker: Chief
content: Why were you at the fete when the Wisteria Mania broke out?

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Because of my bad luck.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Sigh... I wish I knew. I tried so hard to avoid that storyteller. When she went left, I went right. But somehow, no matter which direction I took, all paths led to the same place. I still ended up getting dragged into her story.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: And this time it was even worse. Dreams piled on top of illusions, and I ended up in that bizarre fete. Not only did I nearly die, but now I'm locked up in this... Bureau, or whatever it is.
As Wuhuanzi hangs her head in dejection, you find yourself feeling sympathy for her. Here's another soul cursed with the same awful luck as you.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Don't look at me with such pity. I've grown accustomed to walking hand in hand with misfortune. It's simply something I have to live with.
Her melancholy lasts but a moment before she regains her serene composure. You avert your gaze.

speaker: Chief
content: What brought you to DisCity?

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: To save lives, of course.

speaker: Chief
content: What I mean is, you're from the Healer Vale in Eastia. Why travel all the way to DisCity to practice medicine? Weren't there enough patients back in Eastia?

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: I'm merely an herbalist. Traveling to heal the sick is my calling and how I gain experience. With Mania running rampant in DisCity, there are naturally more patients here, and thus, more opportunities to earn good karma.

speaker: Chief
content: You say you practice medicine for <color=#fb9259>good karma</color>. What exactly does it mean?

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: It's part of the spiritual cultivation practice. Accumulating good karma lessens karmic burden, wards off misfortune, and enhances one's spiritual power and enlightenment.
What's karmic burden? Spiritual power and enlightenment? Now there are even more terms that are unheard-of.
Seeing your bewildered expression, Wuhuanzi realizes it's useless to pull you further into this cycle of incomprehension.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: ...Let's just say healing people earns me good karma.
According to Wuhuanzi, healing people earns her good karma. Does she mean that good karma is her only motivation for helping others, or is it a byproduct of her charitable acts?

speaker: Chief
content: I've known other Sinners who were doctors. They acted out of professional calling, never mentioning any personal gain from helping others.

speaker: Chief
content: Even considering regional differences and varying medical philosophies, could practitioners of the same profession really have such contrasting motivations?

speaker: Chief
content: Are your persistent attempts to treat me also about earning good karma?

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Yes. And... since you're someone important around here, your life is worth even more good karma.
Wuhuanzi adds seriously as if she's trying to sound more convincing. You're not sure if you should be glad to hear about your high karmic value.

speaker: Chief
content: Did I ever reveal that I was someone important during the fete?
Wuhuanzi mumbles something incoherent without giving a proper explanation. Seeing her evasiveness, you press on with your questions.

speaker: Chief
content: But you've also helped ordinary citizens and people from the Drifter Camp. They're hardly what you'd call important people.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: ...In Eastia, we also believe having something is better than having nothing.
She fumbles with her words before finally forcing out a reasonable-sounding answer.
You let out a sigh, having expected her to say something more compassionate, like wanting to help patients recover or that she's unable to ignore others' suffering.

speaker: Chief
content: So according to what you're saying, you earn different amounts of good karma depending on who you save. Do you lose karma if you fail to treat them? How many ordinary citizens would equal one VIP? Is there a formula for this?
Your rapid-fire questions visibly unsettle Wuhuanzi, though she manages to maintain her composure.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: ...The mechanism behind is not meant to be understood by mere mortals like us.

speaker: Chief
content: So does practicing without a license reduce your good karma?

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: I merely lack DisCity's official permission. That doesn't affect my ability to heal patients.
Wuhuanzi deliberately sidesteps any questions about how karma is calculated, brushing them aside with vague answers.

speaker: Chief
content: I can understand people's desire to accumulate wealth, but what's your purpose in accumulating good karma? Your belief seems to lack any support from concrete theory or data.
After a long silence, Wuhuanzi finally speaks, her voice barely above a whisper.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: To... break free from my curse of misfortune.
Out of all the things Wuhuanzi has said, two concepts appear more frequently than others: good karma and misfortune. They seem to form an impregnable barrier around her, like a looming shadow.

speaker: Chief
content: How much good karma do you need to break the curse? Um... Is there some kind of progress bar to track it?
Wuhuanzi shakes her head.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: The ancient texts say: Three good deeds a day for three years shall bring heaven's blessing. Since my misfortune persists, I must not have accumulated enough good karma yet.
This baffles you a little. Would anyone really keep at something when absolutely no results can be seen?

speaker: Chief
content: Help me understand something. As a physician, when you prescribe medicine, don't you adjust the treatment plan based on how the patient responds?

speaker: Chief
content: So, going back to our subject... If your actions aren't bringing any changes to your life, could it be that good karma simply isn't the right medicine for breaking your curse?
Wuhuanzi lifts her head slightly as if to speak, but after a moment, she drops her gaze again, fidgeting nervously with her fingers.

speaker: Chief
content: What I mean is, you've accumulated so much good karma already, and yet you still seem constantly troubled by bad luck...
Before you can finish speaking, you feel a surge of depressive energy coursing through the shackles. At the same time, you realize you might have just said exactly the wrong thing.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: ...You're right. I've tried so hard to accumulate good karma, so why am I still cursed with such terrible luck?

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: A disaster destroyed my homeland and took my family away. I lost everything that mattered to me, only to end up cursed with this endless misfortune.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: I don't know how much good karma is considered enough. I can only keep trying to earn more... Surely one day I'll have enough to break this curse, right?
Instead of deflecting with her usual mystical theories, Wuhuanzi opens up about her past in Eastia. Her last words sound less like a question and more like a quiet confession to herself.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: What good would knowing the truth do? Nothing can be changed... It would only bring more pain...
Her head sinks lower and lower as waves of despair seem to materialize around her, dark energy gathering and wrapping her in an ever-deeper darkness.
The shackles help bring Wuhuanzi back to her senses. You give her shoulder a gentle pat, pause the interrogation, and offer her a glass of water.
Good karma. You pick up your pen and write down this unfamiliar Eastian term.
Could something so intangible truly exist? Could accumulating good karma really break the curse of misfortune that plagues Wuhuanzi?
What makes her believe so firmly in this? Has she witnessed the miraculous power of good karma firsthand? Or is she simply chasing after some vague Eastian myth?
As the interrogation progresses, instead of finding answers, you're left with even more mysteries, ones that seem impossible to solve.
You set down your pen, having come to a decision.

speaker: Chief
content: That concludes this interrogation.

speaker: Chief
content: The Bureau has been monitoring and examining the conditions of your patients, and turns out they're all in good health. Though you may be practicing without a license, you are, without doubt, a qualified physician.
At your words, Wuhuanzi's tensed body begins to unfurl. She glances at you, and finding no trace of mockery in your expression, finally lets out a deep breath of relief.

speaker: Chief
content: Many people at the Bureau need medical attention. While we do have our own infirmary, I suppose we could give Eastian medicine a try.

speaker: Chief
content: Of course, our infirmary will monitor the progress. If you need anything, you can always reach out to Nightingale.
Wuhuanzi is taken aback. Not only have you stopped questioning her, but you've even permitted her unauthorized practice. Her usually expressionless face shows a mixture of disbelief and astonishment.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: ...Thank you. So, um, I can go now?
You nod and watch quietly as Wuhuanzi makes her way out of the interrogation room.
You try to organize your thoughts, setting aside for now your questions about good karma and misfortune.

speaker: Chief
content: If we consider good karma as a kind of currency, Wuhuanzi's practice isn't much different from regular medical care. Sometimes she even offers free treatment, not receiving any actual payment at all.

speaker: Chief
content: ...How is this any different from charity work?
Earlier, you had the impression she only cared about the number of patients she treated, not the actual results of her treatment.
But just now when she heard about her patients' excellent health, her visible relief was unmistakable. She didn't look like a doctor who would simply neglect her patients' conditions.

speaker: Chief
content: Does she not want people to see her work as acts of kindness? Or maybe she's even trying to hide how much she truly cares about saving lives?

speaker: Chief
content: Then... could she be using good karma as an excuse to hide her true feelings? Do people like her really exist? But why?
Try as you might, you can't make sense of it. Wuhuanzi is a web of contradictions, and her true motives remain frustratingly unclear.

speaker: Chief
content: During today's interrogation, she kept dancing around my questions. Maybe she was also aware that her explanations didn't hold water, but just couldn't bring herself to admit it?
This guess seems a bit far-fetched even to you, but without more information, you can't come to any other conclusions.
She helped you in the illusion, and now you want to return the favor. Even if you can't break her so-called curse of misfortune, at least you might help her understand her true feelings.

A dull headache throbs in your temples as Wuhuanzi's cryptic Eastian incantations echo in your mind. You grab your pen again, drawing circles around the term good karma before adding a large question mark beside it.

speaker: Chief
content: It looks like it all comes back to good karma in the end.

speaker: Chief
content: Sigh... One step at a time.
In your office, Nightingale is briefing you on the aftermath of the Wisteria Mania incident.

Due to widespread exposure to the dream, both the Drifter Camp and Eastside are showing elevated M-values and increased Mania fluctuations. Several Mania incidents have already occurred in Eastside's outskirts, resulting in casualties.

The situation at the Drifter Camp is deteriorating as well. The peripheral buildings, still under repair from previous damage, have been attacked again. The FAC has already dispatched forces and equipment, and the MBCC needs to send support as well.
You rub your tired eyes as you stare at the lengthy task list before you.

speaker: Chief
content: There's still so much to be done... I should make time to visit the Drifter Camp, see what else we can do for them...
Knock, knock, knock...
The urgent knocking interrupts Nightingale's report, and before you can say come in, Wuhuanzi barges through the door.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Ch... Chief! Would you spare a moment? It's something urgent.
Wuhuanzi is clutching a copy of the newspaper the Bureau subscribes to, her face flushed from what appears to be a rushed journey here.
She rarely comes here, except when it's to offer medical consultations or insist on treating your ailments.

speaker: Chief
content: Nightingale, proceed with the standard procedures for now. Email me about any tasks that need my attention.
Taking the hint, Nightingale picks up her device and leaves, leaving you two alone.

speaker: Chief
content: We're alone now. Tell me what's on your mind.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: I need... a permit to leave, now.
Early the next morning, you drive from the Bureau to the Drifter Camp by the shortest route. Having visited countless times before, you know these streets like the back of your hand.
This time, however, you let Wuhuanzi take the lead. After all, you're only here as her official escort for this emergency leave.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: I'm sorry... If we hadn't been in such a hurry, you wouldn't have blown out that tire right after we left.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: I drew a divination stick last night. The reading warned of obstacles ahead, so this must be my misfortune at work again. I'll pay you back with the money I make from my consultations.

speaker: Chief
content: Stop blaming your misfortune for everything.

speaker: Chief
content: I was just showing off my amazing driving skills. Thought I'd give the spare tire a chance to shine.

speaker: Chief
content: This counts as an official expense. I can probably get reimbursed.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Really? Would Adjutant Nightingale approve of that?

speaker: Chief
content: She will... probably.

speaker: Chief
content: The funeral begins in less than thirty minutes. Your task now is to locate where it's being held, and fast.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: I need... a permit to leave, now.

speaker: Chief
content: What's your reason?
Wuhuanzi rarely requests to go out except for purchasing herbs. This must be something important.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: A few months ago, I treated an old lady at the Drifter Camp.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: I know I cured her... So why is her name in the obituaries? Something must have gone wrong...
Wuhuanzi's fingernails are digging into the newspaper. You gently pry her fingers away and take the paper for a closer look.
The newspaper is crammed with reports of events from every corner of DisCity. Where her fingers left their marks is a tiny, perfectly square column tucked away in the corner of the page.

This section carries the names of the deceased without embellishment or flowery words. Some days the list runs long, others short. The obituary notes the funeral will be held tomorrow morning at the Drifter Camp.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Did I miss something? Could there have been an underlying condition I failed to spot? Or was there something wrong with the medicine I prescribed...
Wuhuanzi paces anxiously before you, frantically going through every detail of her treatment, desperate to find some explanation for the elderly woman's death.

speaker: Chief
content: I remember her name from the medical reports. You did cure her condition. There might be some misunderstanding in there. Her death may not have anything to do with your treatment. Try to stay calm.

speaker: Chief
content: The Bureau receives multiple Mania incident reports every day. The Drifter Camp hasn't been peaceful lately...
As you watch Wuhuanzi's anxious demeanor, you recall something she said before.
Is Wuhuanzi so concerned about the elderly woman's death because she's worried about her good karma? Would the good karma she earns from healing someone vanish upon their death?

speaker: Chief
content: What are you hoping to find at the Drifter Camp?
Wuhuanzi lifts her head to meet your gaze. Her tone is earnest and slightly imploring.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: I need to verify the true cause of Granny Wu's death.

Contrary to your assumption, Wuhuanzi doesn't mention anything about good karma. Perhaps she isn't as obsessed with it as she claims to be. Right now, she's simply a doctor who's concerned about her patient's life.
You sense that a chance to understand Wuhuanzi's true thoughts is about to present itself.

speaker: Chief
content: Let's go.

speaker: Chief
content: A Sinner needs a supervisor for emergency outings, right?

speaker: Chief
content: And... a driver.

speaker: Chief
content: The permit is approved.

speaker: Chief
content: The MBCC isn't some heartless organization, you know.

speaker: Chief
content: Think of it as... paying our last respects to that old lady.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: ...This is it. We're here.
By the time you arrive, the funeral is about to begin.

This appears to be where the old lady lived. Her modest home has been transformed into a simple memorial hall, too small to accommodate more than a few people inside. Neighbors who can't get in crowd around the doorway.
Wuhuanzi tries to squeeze through the crowd several times without success. She can only stand on tiptoes, eagerly peering inside over people's shoulders.

speaker: Gossiping Neighbor A
content: How did Ms. Wu pass away so suddenly? Didn't she recover from her leg condition? I heard she was even looking for part-time work.

speaker: Gossiping Neighbor B
content: Who knows? Maybe she wasn't really cured at all. I remember that doctor. She was muttering strange things constantly and looking so gloomy. Probably just another quack.

speaker: Gossiping Neighbor C
content: Don't spread rumors! I heard Ms. Wu encountered a Corruptor while working outside the Drifter Camp. That's what happened!

speaker: Gossiping Neighbor A
content: Sigh... What's the point of going through the treatment? She still ended up dead all the same.

speaker: Gossiping Neighbor B
content: I warned her not to wander around outside. Just look how dangerous it is out there these days. If she had just stayed home, none of this would have happened.

speaker: Gossiping Neighbor D
content: How can you talk like that? What's wrong with getting treatment? Try to show some respect!
The neighbors continue their back-and-forth, each chiming in with their own opinion.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: ...Is it all pointless? Do you also think that... in times like these, saving lives is just a futile effort?
Amid the bustling crowd and murmured condolences, Wuhuanzi stops in her tracks. She echoes fragments of their conversation softly as her hand withdraws timidly.
For a doctor... for Wuhuanzi, each life is one she's literally wrestled away from death's grasp. How could anyone dismiss such an achievement so casually?
You've witnessed Wuhuanzi's medical expertise firsthand. Calling her a quack based on groundless rumors is not only unfair to her, but also a disrespect to the lives she's saved.
You approach Wuhuanzi, words of comfort on the tip of your tongue, but as funeral music begins to play, she hurries away as if fleeing.
Natural light barely reaches the heart of the Drifter Camp, and lights stay on constantly as the only source of illumination. After Wuhuanzi leaves the funeral, you quietly follow her.
After walking for a while, Wuhuanzi gradually slows down until she's walking side by side with you.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: I've heard such talk many times before. It doesn't bother me anymore.
Wuhuanzi speaks with an air of detachment, as if she's used to numbing herself with these words.
The young wandering healer returns to the Drifter Camp to check on her former patient, only to be met with misunderstandings and wounded by cruel rumors.

speaker: Chief
content: Does it really not bother you, or have you just grown used to it?
Wuhuanzi comes to a stop beside you, your question giving her the courage to speak.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: If it were you... If you knew that saving someone now might expose them to greater dangers later, and you'd be misunderstood by others for it, would you still offer your help?
Seeing the dejection in Wuhuanzi's expression, you carefully choose your words, keeping your tone gentle.

speaker: Chief
content: Eastia and DisCity are worlds apart in everything. Language, mythology, theoretical frameworks, and even fundamental ways of thinking.

speaker: Chief
content: You're a doctor, and I'm the Chief of the MBCC. We operate in completely different environments, with entirely different approaches to saving lives.

speaker: Chief
content: I'm not confident I can give you a good answer simply by applying my imagination. And I know my answer won't be useful to you right away. But I can share with you my personal experience at the Drifter Camp. Would you like to hear my perspective?
Wuhuanzi nods, and you both head toward the bustling street. You've barely taken a few steps when someone recognizes you.

speaker: Local A
content: ...Oh? If it isn't ${PlayerName}!

speaker: Local A
content: It's been ages since you last visited! Check out my new home. Just finished rebuilding it yesterday. What do you think?

speaker: Chief
content: It looks very nice!

speaker: Local B
content: ${PlayerName}, you wouldn't believe it. A Corruptor broke in yesterday, but our guys from Rustfire managed to take care of it.

speaker: Chief
content: Mania incidents have been on the rise lately. Stay safe, and get those outer defenses rebuilt as soon as you can.
As you discuss Mania and reconstruction, Wuhuanzi timidly interjects with a question.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Why rebuild it?

speaker: Local B
content: Hmm? What's that, young lady?

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: I said... With so many Corruptors out there, why not move somewhere safer instead of rebuilding this place?

speaker: Local B
content: Huh? But this is our home. When something breaks in your home, you fix it up. Can't just abandon it now, can we...
Before you can form a response to Wuhuanzi's question, more locals recognize you and crowd around.

speaker: Local C
content: ${PlayerName}, I think I've developed a sleepwalking problem! In my dream, I was circling around this huge wisteria tree, and when I woke up, I found myself on top of the awning above the market!
Some shake your hand enthusiastically, others sob and sniffle as they pour out their troubles. There are even people asking you to sign some old photos of you, hoping to sell them for a good price...

speaker: Option
options: Find a way to slip away

speaker: Chief
content: Everyone, please calm down. I'm here today to assess the impact of the Mania incidents.

speaker: Chief
content: Please, don't crowd around.
After addressing everyone's concerns and questions, the crowd finally disperses.
Just as you think you finally have time to answer Wuhuanzi's question, another local approaches you hesitantly.

speaker: Local D
content: So you're the renowned...

speaker: Chief
content: Yes, yes, that's me. Happy to be of service.

speaker: Local D
content: ${PlayerName}, you see, my old man's a little superstitious. He keeps forcing me to buy all sorts of protective charms to hang around the house. Ancient coins, peach wood swords, even crosses and garlic...

speaker: Local D
content: Sigh, I don't know how to reason with him. He keeps saying we must be cursed with bad luck, that's why we keep suffering through these disasters.

speaker: Local D
content: Then he starts going on about how I'm not trying hard enough. Says I need to defy destiny, or else don't bother coming home.
You give a simplified explanation for the Wisteria incident, sharing only the information cleared for public knowledge.

speaker: Chief
content: This has nothing to do with luck or personal effort. Mania, Corruptors, and even Black Rings are real threats that exist whether we like it or not, crises that we all need to face together.

speaker: Chief
content: As for those lucky charms... if they really worked, we wouldn't need the Public Security Bureau or FAC. We could all just pray our problems away.
The man leaves after giving his thanks, but not before insisting you take his newly bought lucky bracelet.
After watching you field question after question from everyone, Wuhuanzi fixes you with a serious look and poses one of her own.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: My friend, do you think... that a person's fortune has nothing to do with how hard they try?
You can't help but shake your head in amusement. Why is everyone coming to you with questions today? Do you really look like some kind of walking fortune cookie dispenser?

speaker: Chief
content: I believe... luck is nothing more than probability. I consider myself a hardworking person, but that doesn't seem to improve my luck one bit.
I even died once. You only add inwardly.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: What about lucky charms? Have you ever tried using them?

speaker: Chief
content: You mean this?
You show her the lucky bracelet the local just gave you. With a gentle tug, the string breaks, and before you can catch it, the beads are scattering all over.
With a patter, the beads bounce erratically before rolling to a stop next to Wuhuanzi's and your feet.

speaker: Chief
content: If it can't even hold itself together, how's it supposed to protect me? See? Now I even have to try to put it back in one piece.
Wuhuanzi kneels down helpfully beside you, helping to pick up the scattered beads one by one.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Then... if neither effort nor lucky charms work, what can I do to avoid disaster, to escape all this... misfortune?

speaker: Chief
content: Shouldn't Eastian philosophy have explanations for this? I don't know much about it, but I remember you practice divination and consult almanacs.

speaker: Chief
content: And what about your talismans, your peach wood sword, all these... tools you carry? Shouldn't you know better than me about these things?

speaker: Option
options: Don't tell me you're not sure about them either?

content: Wuhuanzi rises to her feet, staring down at the collected beads in her hands, her long bangs hiding her eyes. Standing before you now, she somehow resembles a student seeking guidance from a teacher.
After a long while, she answers in a stifled voice.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: I'm indeed not sure...

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: In the books I've studied, it is written that virtue brings fortune to those who practice it, and that morality is the foundation of all things.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: I kept telling myself that healing others was just to accumulate good karma, that everything would get better once I'd earned enough. But it seems... I never really convinced myself of that.
Now it's your turn to be confused.

speaker: Chief
content: Are you saying you've been lying to yourself? Why?
Wuhuanzi's brows knit together. Her lips part a few times and press shut again.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Back in the interrogation room, when I said I was accumulating good karma to break my misfortune... I wasn't lying to you. I just... withheld certain things...

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: My misfortune wasn't something I was born with. It came from the disaster that destroyed my hometown.

speaker: Gentle Female Voice
content: Youyou, have you memorized the new passage from yesterday?

speaker: Youyou?
content: Yes, yes! I know it! Fortune and misfortune come not unbidden, but through our own doing. The fruit of good and evil follows us, just like... like one's shadow!

speaker: Gentle Female Voice
content: Excellent! Now, do you understand what those words mean?

speaker: Youyou?
content: A senior disciple explained it to me! It means our actions determine our fortune, so good deeds bring good fortune, and bad deeds bring misfortune!

speaker: Kind Male Voice
content: Your mother and I have chosen a nickname for you—Wuhuanzi. When you grow up, if you also wish to...

speaker: Gentle Female Voice
content: Oh my, it's too early for such talk. All we wish is for Youyou to grow up healthy and carefree.

speaker: Gentle Female Voice
content: Whether she wants to inherit this nickname or become a healer, it's all up to her.

speaker: Kind Male Voice
content: Youyou, here's another saying I want you to know: A single act of kindness can ward off a hundred calamities.

speaker: Kind Male Voice
content: Whenever you feel chased by bad luck, just remember to be kind. The good karma you accumulate will help ward off all your troubles.

speaker: Youyou?
content: Like how you heal people and save lives?

speaker: Gentle Female Voice
content: Ah yes, that's right. The more good we do, the better this world becomes.

speaker: Panicked Male Voice
content: The disaster is here! Run!

speaker: Kind Male Voice
content: Someone's injured here! Quick! Stop the bleeding!

speaker: Gentle Female Voice
content: Tie a tourniquet around the severed limb. Needle the vital points, then...

speaker: Kind Male Voice
content: Watch out! Rockfall! Ugh...

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: No... Father! Mother! Someone help us!

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: M... Monsters?! People are turning into monsters?!

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: N-no, stay back!

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: How could this happen... The Vale is gone...

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: ...Didn't you say healing others would save the world? Father, Mother, you lied to me...

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Didn't you tell me doing good deeds could ward off all troubles? Then why... why did you leave me...

speaker: Senior Disciple A
content: There's nothing wrong with healing others. But, this was a calamity that no one could have escaped.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Father, Mother... None of us did anything wrong. We healed people and saved lives. Why were we still struck by such a tragedy?

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Please, I can't make sense of it... Was our faith not strong enough?

speaker: Senior Disciple A
content: Youyou, stay strong! It must... it must be that our spiritual cultivation was still lacking!

speaker: Senior Disciple B
content: Y-yes, that's right! We hadn't earned enough good karma to ward off such a destructive disaster!

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: So... so that's why?

speaker: Senior Disciple B
content: That must be it! There can be no other reason...

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: That disaster destroyed the Healer Vale and took my parents from me.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: I survived narrowly and even awakened my special power. But with it came this misfortune that has haunted me ever since.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: My fellow disciples were like family to me. They comforted me and encouraged me to overcome my grief.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: I had no time to dwell on my sorrow. With Eastia ravaged by disasters and sickness, I set out on my journey to heal and save as many as I could.
Wuhuanzi speaks softly, her gaze traveling across the winding streets of the Drifter Camp and lingering on the half-rebuilt structures at its edges.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Throughout my journey, I've saved many lives... and lost just as many.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: I once thought I could wrestle lives from death's grasp, but in the end, I realized how powerless I truly was... When the world itself is crumbling, what can one person do to stop it?

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: All my medical knowledge means nothing in the face of the calamity.
She lets out a long, heavy sigh, each word of this painful truth seeming to drag itself unwillingly from her lips.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: I watched helplessly as those I had healed were slaughtered by monsters, crushed by falling rocks, burned alive in flames. The dying transformed into monsters themselves, while the survivors lost their homes and families...

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: I've convinced myself that I'm only healing others to earn good karma, as instructed by the ancient texts, and attribute my misfortune to not having done enough.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: But every time I try to save someone, I'm terrified.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Is the act of saving lives ultimately meaningless? Am I truly saving them, or merely changing the way they'll meet their end?
Wuhuanzi's voice catches in her throat as she looks up at you, tears welling in her eyes.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Have I been wrong all along? In a world like this... it's pointless to try to save someone's life, isn't it?
Like someone drowning, she's desperately grasping for anything that might keep her afloat.

speaker: Chief
content: You choose to save others because that's who you are, someone with a kind heart.
Children dash past with playful shouts. Street vendors call out their wares. Warm light spills from the windows of homes, carrying the sound of laughter.
It all feels so ordinary, so beautiful, as if things like Mania, Corruptors, and Black Rings all only belong in some distant world.

speaker: Chief
content: Look around you. These simple moments of daily life continue because of the lives you've saved. Isn't that the point?

speaker: Chief
content: You've come such a long way on your own, witnessed so much death and despair, yet you've never stopped trying to save lives. That takes remarkable strength.
Following your gaze, Wuhuanzi looks out at the Drifter Camp. She's seen these daily scenes countless times before, but always through the eyes of a doctor searching for patients.
All she saw was people's illnesses and all she cared about was rushing to cure them, never realizing that saving lives meant more than the simple matter of life and death.

speaker: Chief
content: The difficult task of saving lives took its toll on you, so you found yourself an excuse... or rather, an anchor to hold onto.

speaker: Chief
content: It does help steady your heart and numb the pain. But like any anesthetic, its effects grow weaker over time...

speaker: Chief
content: I'm glad you shared this with me. It means you're starting to trust me, aren't you?
Wuhuanzi nods, sniffling slightly as she collects herself.

speaker: Chief
content: You asked me earlier, if I knew that saving someone now might expose them to greater dangers later, and I might be misunderstood by others for it, would I still offer my help.

speaker: Chief
content: Of course I would.

speaker: Chief
content: Those people who just came to share their stories and express their gratitude, they're the ones I've saved. I could never stand by and watch them die.

speaker: Chief
content: There's only so much I can do, and those I've saved still face many challenges ahead. Some of them are doing well now, while others are worse off than before.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Do they ever regret being saved by you?
You smile.

speaker: Chief
content: Hmm... I don't know, but I do know that the dead have no chance for regret.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Before saving someone, do you ever consider what might happen to them afterward?

speaker: Chief
content: I mean, is there really time for that?

speaker: Chief
content: Choosing not to save someone leads to only one outcome—death. But choosing to save them creates endless possibilities, both for them and for yourself.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Even if death will still claim them in the end?

speaker: Option
options: Even if death will still claim them in the end.

speaker: Chief
content: The existence of something cannot be undone.

speaker: Chief
content: People may die, but the memories we share with them live on. Buildings may crumble, but as long as their builders survive, they can be rebuilt.

speaker: Chief
content: Take this area and West District. Some places have been reduced to ruins, while others have risen again with towering new buildings. Even ruins themselves become historic landmarks that people remember and visit.

speaker: Chief
content: I've saved others, and others have saved me in turn. That's the sole reason I'm still standing here with you today.
As Wuhuanzi listens intently, understanding seems to be dawning on her.
You reach the memorial at the foot of the Drifter Camp. Though reconstruction here isn't complete yet, some camp residents are voluntarily clearing away the scattered rubble.
You and Wuhuanzi keep your distance, not wanting to disturb their work.

speaker: Chief
content: Death is never meaningless. Things happen, and people remember.

speaker: Chief
content: This memorial stands for all those who gave their lives for the Drifter Camp and the mine.

speaker: Chief
content: No matter how many times this place is destroyed, people will rebuild it again and again. It's because of people like this that humanity's history continues to be written.

speaker: Chief
content: And to be honest, I don't really care about being remembered. I don't do what I do to leave behind a legacy, or achieve what people would call a happy ending.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Then why... What do you save lives for?
Realizing the conversation has gotten rather heavy, you shrug and stretch your stiff muscles.

speaker: Chief
content: Simply because I want to.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: That's it?

speaker: Chief
content: That's it.
Wuhuanzi stares at you blankly, waiting for you to elaborate.

speaker: Chief
content: Well... I just couldn't stand by and do nothing, so I helped them out.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: I... I don't understand. Saving lives is a complex task. Can the motivation really be that simple? A person's life or death affects so many people, so many things...
Seeing Wuhuanzi caught in another loop, you let out a resigned sigh, pondering how to help her break free from this mental maze.
Just then, a group of young people appears near you, the faint scent of incense still clinging to their clothes.

speaker: Youngster A
content: Let's hurry and clear this area. Ms. Wu was really concerned about rebuilding the memorial before she passed away.

speaker: Youngster B
content: Ms. Wu cared about so many things. Kids' education at the Drifter Camp, support for the elderly left on their own... We must carry on all these missions she left behind.

speaker: Youngster A
content: Of course we will! Ms. Wu sure kept herself busy after recovering from her leg injury, taking on so many responsibilities...
The young people chat casually as they work, white origami flowers pinned to their chests as they roll up their sleeves to clear away the rubble at their feet.
You gently nudge Wuhuanzi with your arm, gesturing for her to observe them.

speaker: Youngster B
content: But at least Ms. Wu was happy. She kept talking about that gifted young healer who cured her leg, saying she wanted to properly thank her if they ever met again...

speaker: Youngster B
content: Sigh, it's too late for that now... I wonder if that young healer came to Ms. Wu's funeral today...
Upon hearing them mention Ms. Wu and young healer, Wuhuanzi turns to you with disbelief in her eyes.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Are they... Granny Wu's students?
You nod. Judging from their clothes and conversation, there's no doubt about it.

speaker: Chief
content: You see? Even though Ms. Wu has passed away, treating her sure isn't meaningless, is it?

speaker: Chief
content: As you guys like to say in Eastia, every encounter happens for a reason. There must be a reason why we met them here today.
Wuhuanzi blinks.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: My friend, you're growing more and more knowledgeable about Eastian culture.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Actually... Before coming here, I was wondering if treating her legs somehow led to her accident.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: If I hadn't cured her self-righteously, she could still be reading by the window or making crochet dolls. She might not have ventured into danger and died such a meaningless death.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: I couldn't accept Ms. Wu's eventual death despite my treatment. It's my one-sided regret. Am I forcing my will upon the natural order by thinking like this?

speaker: Chief
content: Perhaps your belief that she died a meaningless death is just as one-sided?
Your words seem to catch at a loose thread of Wuhuanzi's thoughts, gently beginning to unravel it. Under your gentle gaze, she reaches out and grasps it herself.
Wuhuanzi clenches her fists briefly, as if cheering for herself, then walks toward one of the youngsters.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Is Granny Wu's funeral... over?
When you return to the funeral, the mourners have already dispersed, leaving only Granny Wu's family to tend to the final arrangements.
The Drifter Camp is home to people from all walks of life, and their funerals are simple affairs, lacking the elaborate ceremonies common in Eastia.
Before you can get closer, a woman who has been watching anxiously by the door hurries over and takes Wuhuanzi's hands in hers.

speaker: Emotional Woman
content: Young healer, you came back! Thank goodness.

speaker: Emotional Woman
content: My brother and I were completely overwhelmed with the funeral arrangements. We only heard from the neighbors afterward that you'd come by, but got scared off by the crowd.

speaker: Emotional Woman
content: My brother went out looking for you while I waited here. And here you are!
The woman seems overwhelmed by sentiment. Unused to handling this kind of emotional display in others, Wuhuanzi turns to you with a helpless look.
Curious to see how she'll handle this, you pretend not to notice her discomfort and simply give her an encouraging look.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: ...Please accept my deepest condolences.
Wracking her brain, Wuhuanzi falls back on the most common Eastian condolence phrase she can think of.

speaker: Ms. Wu's Daughter
content: My mother spoke of you a lot. She would tell us how much you helped her when you were here, and what a dear, kind person you were.

speaker: Ms. Wu's Daughter
content: She was always worried about you, if you had a place to stay, if you were eating properly, or if law enforcement was bothering you.
Hearing about the old woman's constant concern for her, Wuhuanzi's throat tightens and she seems unable to hide her grievances any longer.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Your mother... she was truly a kind soul. She was the one who took me in when I couldn't afford to stay in an inn.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: When everyone else doubted me and refused my treatment, she gave me a chance, saying she hadn't been able to walk for years anyway.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Is there... anything I could do to help? Something I could do... for your mother?
Wuhuanzi asks gingerly.

speaker: Ms. Wu's Daughter
content: You've already done so much for us. My brother and I will take care of the funeral arrangements. Please don't worry.

speaker: Ms. Wu's Daughter
content: In fact, I wonder if we could do anything for you?
The woman looks at Wuhuanzi with such tender concern that it catches her off guard. The same kind of look you gave her not too long ago.

speaker: Ms. Wu's Daughter
content: Oh, I hope I'm not being presumptuous. It's just that you look so sad and aggrieved...
Touched by her kindness, Wuhuanzi gently waves her hand as she replies.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: May I know... after she regained her ability to walk, was your mother happy?

speaker: Ms. Wu's Daughter
content: Of course, she was over the moon. And it wasn't just her, my brother and I were overjoyed to see her that way as well.

speaker: Ms. Wu's Daughter
content: Because of her leg, she hadn't left the Drifter Camp for many years. While we were away working, she spent most of her time alone at home.

speaker: Ms. Wu's Daughter
content: Her spirits lifted considerably. She used to be a teacher, so she even found a part-time nanny job in Eastside. She wouldn't stop telling us how full of energy she felt. She was even saving money to buy gifts for her grandchildren.
Hearing about Granny Wu's new life, a faint smile touches Wuhuanzi's lips. All the dreams her patient once shared about life after recovery had come true.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Then... how did she pass away?
Hearing the question, sadness washes over the woman's face.

speaker: Ms. Wu's Daughter
content: A few days ago, a rogue Corruptor appeared in the outskirts of Eastside. My mother was on an outing with her employers and their child at the time.

speaker: Ms. Wu's Daughter
content: She died protecting the child from the Corruptor, but her sacrifice bought enough time before the sheriffs arrived.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: No way...
Wuhuanzi's voice trembles.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: If... if she had stayed in the Drifter Camp, maybe she wouldn't have...

speaker: Ms. Wu's Daughter
content: No, please don't think like that. She never regretted leaving home, and she would never regret saving that child.

speaker: Ms. Wu's Daughter
content: Though her death broke our hearts, we feel proud of her. She dedicated her whole life to nurturing children, and she died protecting one she loved.

speaker: Ms. Wu's Daughter
content: My mother always preferred tranquility, so we kept her funeral simple and quiet. We wanted her to depart this world in peace and serenity.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Was she... at peace when she passed? Did she... suffer at all?
After much hesitation, Wuhuanzi finally gathers the courage to ask what has been weighing heaviest on her mind.

speaker: Ms. Wu's Daughter
content: It happened quickly, which was a mercy...

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: I see... That's a relief...
Wuhuanzi rubs her eyes and manages a bitter smile, her voice catching as she speaks.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: May I go in?

speaker: Ms. Wu's Daughter
content: Of course you can. My mother would have been very happy to see you.
The room, which was bustling earlier in the morning, now lies in silence. Though modestly furnished, everything is kept in perfect order, a testament to how much she cherished life.
On the table in the center of the room sits a photograph of an elderly woman, her gentle smile reaching her eyes.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Granny Wu, I'm here...
Wuhuanzi takes a white flower from the long table by the door and gently places it before the elderly woman's photograph.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: I'm at a place called the Bureau now. I have a room there, food on my table, and someone who patiently answers all my questions. I can continue healing people and doing good deeds...
Wuhuanzi's throat tightens as her voice begins to quiver despite her best efforts.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: I'm doing well, so wherever you are now... please don't worry about me.

A breeze drifts through the window, stirring the flower petals. Wuhuanzi's vision blurs with tears, but she stubbornly fights back a sob, quickly wiping away the tears with her sleeve before they can fall.
After bidding farewell to Granny Wu's daughter, you both leave the alley behind.
Wuhuanzi fiddles with a crochet doll given to her by Granny Wu's daughter. After regaining her zest for life, Granny Wu had made many such dolls to help support her family.

speaker: Chief
content: So, young healer, did you find the answers you were looking for?
Wuhuanzi stops in her tracks and nods, taking a small step closer to you.

speaker: Chief
content: You see, things aren't always as simple as they seem.

speaker: Chief
content: When danger strikes, the urge to save others comes naturally. It's the same for Granny Wu. She did that because she had a kind heart, and so do you.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Then...

speaker: Chief
content: So stop talking about the crumbling world and how everything's beyond saving. Leave all these troubles to those big shots.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Is that really okay? Isn't it foolish to keep trying when it seems pointless?

speaker: Chief
content: Yeah, it is pretty foolish. But thanks to that very foolishness, we've both managed to save quite a few people, haven't we?

speaker: Chief
content: Saving DisCity might seem impossible, but we can always help the person right in front of us, whether through a kind deed or a gentle word of guidance. Who knows? Once we've helped everyone we can reach, we might just find we've saved the world in the process.

speaker: Chief
content: After all, the world is made up of the people you see. Whatever you witness, whatever you feel, that becomes your world.
After a long silence, you finally hear Wuhuanzi whisper something to her crochet toy.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: I understand now. Whether something is truly foolish or meaningful... we'll never know unless we give it a try.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: From now on, I'll help everyone I want to help, whether it earns me good karma or not.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: My friend, thank you for bringing me to the Drifter Camp, and for walking this long path with me...

speaker: Chief
content: I'm glad you've found the answer. Mental turmoil is terrible for one's well-being. You keep trying to heal me, but you should take care of yourself as well.
Wuhuanzi raises her head, a warm smile playing across her face as she asks you.

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Then... can I start by helping you?

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: Not for any particular reason. I simply want to. Even... even if you don't want my help, I'm going to help you anyway. And of course, free of charge!
Seeing the new hope in Wuhuanzi's eyes, you find it impossible to refuse.

speaker: Chief
content: Of course you can. Why don't we start with you helping me resolve the Mania-related issues at the Drifter Camp?

speaker: Chief
content: Ah, for instance... How about sealing that breach the Corruptor made on the east side? Maybe with your talismans...
Several days later, MBCC Chief's Office
Looking at the steaming herbal decoction on your desk, then at Wuhuanzi's stern little face, you finally realize just how rash your earlier decision was.

speaker: Chief
content: Do I really have to drink this?

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: You must.

speaker: Chief
content: Can I please skip this one?

speaker: Wuhuanzi
content: No.
Wuhuanzi's gaze remains resolute, completely unmoved by your desperate pleas.

speaker: Chief
content: Sigh...
You squeeze your eyes shut and try to convince yourself: Just pretend it's a budget version of the Bureau's signature coffee!

speaker: Refugee Boy
content: Thani, can we... can we rest for a bit? Dima can't walk anymore.
The children's voices pierced the silent night of WhiteSands. They'd left trails of tiny footprints in the sand. Beneath their refugee cloaks, their faces were all young yet weary.
The girl leading them stopped immediately, turned around, and gazed up at the pale moon hanging in the night sky.

speaker: Thani
content: Then let's camp here for the night. Hmm, it's a bit exposed out here... but we should be fine! Shura, can you help me?
A frail figure darted out from the group. The girl looked barely older than ten. She pulled out various tools and supplies from her backpack and handed them to Thani.

The children sat in a circle with Thani standing in the center, skillfully building a fire and cooking. Shura produced a waterskin from her backpack and handed it to the companion beside her. The children each took just a small sip before passing it to the next person. The firelight illuminated their faces.

speaker: Refugee Boy
content: Hey, Dima, why aren't you drinking?

speaker: Refugee Girl
content: Thani... we've been running in WhiteSands for so long. Will we... ever get back to the refugee camp?

As soon as the girl spoke, the chattering children instantly fell silent, looking down and fidgeting with their fingers. For a moment, the only thing they could hear was Thani's spoon stirring and clinking against the pot.

speaker: Refugee Girl
content: Does that mean... I'll never see Mom and Dad again?

speaker: Refugee Boy
content: Dima, please don't...

speaker: Refugee Girl
