content: If I'd known it would be like this, I should have just stayed with Mom and Dad...

speaker: Refugee Boy
content: Stay with them? They were long gone! Dead! Don't you get it? Is that what you want too, to die with them?!

speaker: Refugee Boy
content: ...Oh no, d-don't cry!

speaker: Thani
content: Who says everyone's gone?
Thani stopped what she was doing. The crying ceased instantly. The girl looked up, meeting Thani's smile.

speaker: Thani
content: Don't believe what those DisCity people say!

speaker: Thani
content: Granny Afra once told me that we children of WhiteSands are blessed by the Desert Goddess. Even when we die, our souls become sand and we live on forever, always staying with our families.

speaker: Thani
content: Everyone's been away from home for so long that they've forgotten this truth. No matter how cruelly the DisCity people treat us, they can never truly separate us. We've fooled them all!
Thani's vehemence grew with every word, and she thrust her arm upward, slicing it through the air with a fierce gesture.

speaker: Refugee Boy
content: Thani... that sounds like... something Granny made up to comfort you...

speaker: Thani
content: Hehe, I used to think the same thing. But you know what? I can still hear Granny's favorite song in the wind sometimes.

speaker: Refugee Girl
content: Thani, can you really hear it?

speaker: Thani
content: Of course! Don't you trust my ears?

speaker: Refugee Girl
content: Then... can you try to see if you can catch any messages Mom and Dad left for me?

speaker: Thani
content: Sure thing! Let's see...
Thani closed her eyes, cupping one hand to her ear while gently resting the other on the girl's shoulder, as if to soothe her anxiety.

The night was still, yet she heard the children's hopeful breaths, barely suppressed. In the distance, a lone beast growled at the moon. Blown by the wind, the sand rippled like waves, spreading across the darkness.
Suddenly, her brow furrowed slightly. Her eyes remained closed, but her body froze for an instant as if catching some signal, her breath momentarily caught.
She could hear it now. Footsteps were approaching across the undulating sand, faint yet distinct.
Thani opened her eyes, the smile still on her face.

speaker: Thani
content: I heard them! Your mom and dad are warning us about approaching danger. We need to pack up quickly now, but don't worry. They'll help hold back those bad guys for a while!

speaker: Shura
content: Thani? Could it be... those people from the institute again?!

speaker: Thani
content: Shh... pack up your things quickly now. Shura, lead everyone back the way we came. Remember, don't make any noise.
Thani raised an index finger to her lips in a shushing gesture. Her eyes, however, already turned toward the distance, as if she'd spotted something.

speaker: Shura
content: Thani, aren't you coming with us? In that case... I'm staying too!

speaker: Thani
content: I can't let them go alone. Remember those trail markers we've been using? I'll follow them to catch up with you all.

speaker: Shura
content: B-but if you don't come with us, everyone will be terrified! What if... what if!
Shura looked away. Thani watched her, a rare shadow shrouding her eyes for just a moment. But her smile quickly returned, just as it always did.

speaker: Thani
content: Trust me, I won't be like those adults... I promise I'll catch up with you in three days. Three days, tops!
Shura looked up at that familiar smile, the one that always made even the worst disasters feel tolerable, and finally nodded decisively.

speaker: Shura
content: Leave it to me then! I promise I won't lose a single one of them before you come back!
Thani bent down and stoked the fire higher, the smoke providing cover as the children hastily packed up and helped one another disappear into the distance.
Now, with her companions gone and the desert beasts asleep, Thani turned around. What she faced was nothing but waves of black sand, surging toward her in relentless torrents.
The waves were getting closer, growing larger.
Sandy wind whipped her face, slicing her cheeks. Thani flinched from the stinging pain, but quickly steadied herself, planting her feet firmly into the sand.

speaker: Thani
content: Now, I'll need the blessings from all of you back at the refugee camp...

She murmured to herself, lifting her hand to touch the metal bracelet on her wrist. In the next moment, her fingers clenched tightly around her wooden staff as she swept it across the ground, kicking up clouds of sand.

speaker: Thani
content: Hey! You! I'm right here! Come and get me!
[Empty Shot]

speaker: Nightingale
content: This is the Outlander girl our patrol rescued from WhiteSands.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Did you capture her attackers?

speaker: Nightingale
content: No. Though they were outnumbered, the attackers knew WhiteSands better than we did and were clearly well-trained. Once they realized they were losing, they retreated without a second thought. We've conducted a few searches since then, but so far there's been no sign of them.

speaker: Nightingale
content: However, we have managed to gather some information about the victim's identity.
Nightingale turns her head, and you follow her gaze toward the interrogation room. The girl sits in a chair, occasionally glancing at you both through the glass.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Her name is Thani. An A-Class Sinner with severe Mania corruption. On top of that, she has been exposed to Aurum Secretum radiation.

The medical report in your hand reads: Severe Mania resulting from Aurum Secretum infection. The subject exhibits hypersensitivity for all five senses. Under high-stress situations, she may also experience symptoms such as fainting and shock.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Aurum Secretum... What's her connection to Fraser?

speaker: Nightingale
content: Given that our patrol found her near the Aurum Secretum Research Institute, we suspect she may have direct ties to the facility, or possibly even to BR-005, but...
Nightingale shakes her head.

speaker: Nightingale
content: We currently have no concrete evidence linking them. She was recently attacked and is still in shock, which explains her guarded attitude toward us.

speaker: Nightingale
content: But I believe you can gain her trust.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I see. Open the door for me, please.
The interrogation room's seat is hard and cold. Though Thani has tucked the hem of her jacket beneath her to avoid direct contact of her skin with the metal, she can't stop fidgeting uncomfortably.
She unconsciously touches her wrist, which is now completely bare.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: We're keeping your bracelet for now. It helps manage your Aurum Secretum symptoms, doesn't it? It's taken quite a bit of wear and tear though. We'll return it to you once it's repaired.
Thani remains silent. You give her a gentle smile.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This is the Minos Bureau of Crisis Control, an organization that shelters and rehabilitates Sinners. I'm the Chief here. The people who rescued you from your attackers and brought you here are also our staff.

speaker: Thani
content: Th-thank you all...

speaker: Thani
content: What about those bad guys? Did you catch them all?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm afraid we didn't catch any of them. We only managed to save you.

speaker: Thani
content: Oh, really...

speaker: Thani
content: Then did you see anyone else? Besides the attackers?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: There were others?

speaker: Thani
content: No! I, I was just... wondering! I just think I got really lucky... Hehe, I'm the sole survivor, aren't I...
She says this, but her hands can't stop fussing with the hem of her clothes.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Just wondering?
Thani glances at you, then quickly averts her eyes.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I understand you're frightened. You were attacked and woke up in a strange place. But please trust me. We mean you no harm. We only want to help you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If you know who attacked you, or have any other relevant information, please tell me. Including anything about these others you mentioned.

She opens her mouth, about to say something, when the overhead light suddenly flickers. She flinches, shielding her eyes with her hand. When she regains her composure, she glances around the room with newfound suspicion, presses her lips together, and decides to remain silent.
She can't bring herself to trust you in this setting. You decide to change tactics and try to find another way past her defenses.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: When our team rescued you, you had no food supplies or tools, not even a water bottle. Without these essentials, no one could survive more than three days in the desert.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Unless you weren't the one carrying these necessities.

speaker: Thani
content: I did have supplies with me! I was carrying several kilos of dried food. But... but...

speaker: Thani
content: The desert bandits took everything! That's right! Those thieves are ruthless. They stole all my food and water, even took my can opener...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You said you had several kilos of dried food. Was that all just for you?

speaker: Thani
content: Huh? Y-yes. How else would it be enough for... I mean, enough for me...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You were lugging several kilos of food, plus water and tools, on your own, trekking through WhiteSands for months? You must be some kind of miracle.

speaker: Thani
content: Don't judge me by my size! I'm actually super strong! Back at the refugee camp, I even helped build houses...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Which refugee camp?
You cut her off abruptly, giving her no time to think. Thani freezes, her face visibly turning red.

speaker: Thani
content: Geez, whichever you think it is! Just some random refugee camp! Why do you have to dig into everything...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So why did you leave the refugee camp? Sure, it might not be the most comfortable home, but it must be better than wandering alone?

speaker: Thani
content: I just wanted to! There's no why... The folks there... the folks at the camp bullied me! No, wait... it was because of the desert bandits! Hmm... no, there was a sandstorm! I left because...
You interrupt her again.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Or, was the refugee camp destroyed?

speaker: Thani
content: ...What?
She falls silent, staring at you in shock. You move closer, looking directly into her eyes.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The place where we found you isn't far from the bombed Aurum Secretum Research Institute.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: From what I know, there used to be a refugee camp near the institute. Now, like the facility itself, it's been completely burned to the ground.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You claim you're from the refugee camp and that you're being hunted by unknown pursuers. At the same time, you're also infected with Aurum Secretum.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'll stop going around in circles. Tell me, what is your connection to the Aurum Secretum Research Institute?
Thani snaps back to reality, her eyes darting frantically around the room. Finally, with a defiant tilt of her chin, she says:

speaker: Thani
content: ...Okay, okay! You're right, I'm from there. But I'm no refugee, I'm...
Thani unconsciously yanks at her tattered sleeve.

speaker: Thani
content: I'm a researcher from the Fraser Institute! So you'd better let me go right now, or else... or else...
Seeing your unfazed expression, her voice gradually dwindles.

speaker: Thani
content: Or else... something bad will happen...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Even if you really were from the Fraser Institute, we still couldn't just let you go. Your life would be in constant danger out there. And not just because someone's hunting you down.
You sigh and pick up a document from the desk.
test
test
test
test
test
test

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Our doctors have examined you. You're suffering from severe Mania infection. Without immediate suppression treatment, you'll soon lose your mind completely and turn into a Corruptor.

speaker: Thani
content: How is that possible...? My mind is perfectly clear right now, except for a few minor side effects...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: The corruption in your body has progressed thoroughly. Those Aurum Secretum marks on your skin are proof. You may feel relatively normal now, but once your Mania flares up, you'll deteriorate much faster than others.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Thani, you don't have much time left.
Thani's body begins to tremble. You soften your voice to comfort the shivering girl before you.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But don't be afraid. I have a way to help you.

speaker: Thani
content: R-Really?!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Yes, this is part of my job. But first, I need to know what really happened to you and why you were wandering in WhiteSands.
Thani's eyes dart nervously as her lips tremble. You notice her defenses weakening and adjust your tone accordingly.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I know you don't trust me. When you asked if I'd seen anyone else, you were checking whether your companions were safe, weren't you?

speaker: Thani
content: I... I was just afraid you might have killed them...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: On the contrary, we want to protect all of you.

speaker: Thani
content: Why should I believe you? The people at Fraser said the same thing before, and then...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Because we're investigating the incident related to the Aurum Secretum Research Institute. And by that I mean we're seeking the truth, not silencing witnesses. If you and your companions are connected to the facility, then ensuring your safety is our absolute priority.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Furthermore, as I mentioned, I'm Chief of this Bureau that shelters Sinners, which means your safety matters to me.
Your voice softly fades away, followed by a long silence. Thani hangs her head as tears fall silently onto her knees.
Finally, she tilts up her face, wiping away the dampness with her hand, a glimmer of tears still lingering in her eyes.

speaker: Thani
content: I did grow up in the refugee camp outside the Aurum Secretum Research Institute. Until that massive explosion happened. I remember that day, when the entire sky went dark.
Without a doubt, that massive explosion Thani refers to is BR-005.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What happened before and after the explosion?

speaker: Thani
content: We found out the Aurum Secretum Research Institute was experimenting on refugees, turning them into monsters. So we helped blow the place up.

speaker: Thani
content: But after it was all over, suddenly, the adults said they needed to attend a sacrificial ritual... They followed Saffar, and then... the explosion happened, and they all turned into monsters just like the Apostles.

speaker: Thani
content: ...They died.
Thani's voice gradually fades until it's barely audible.

speaker: Thani
content: Before they left, they told me to take care of the other kids and stay alive. I originally planned for us to keep living at the refugee camp. But after that, the institute came for us and burned everything down. I overheard them saying that they had to eliminate all evidence.

speaker: Thani
content: So I took everyone and left. I thought maybe we could find somewhere to stay in WhiteSands.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So you are the evidence. Living, breathing witnesses who know what happened.

speaker: Thani
content: I don't know anything about what happened inside... I just... wanted us all to survive together.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Where are your companions now?

speaker: Thani
content: Still in WhiteSands. I promised them I'd go back. They left markers that we used to leave when playing games. Only we know about them.
Thani bites her lip, her shoulders trembling slightly.

speaker: Thani
content: They're still waiting for me to come back. I promised them...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'll help you bring them back. Tell us about these markers so we know where to find them.
You stand up, retrieve a piece of paper and a pen from the desk, and hand them to her.
She hesitates for a moment before taking the pen with a tremulous hand. But just as she's about to write, her hand suddenly stops. She looks up at you.

speaker: Thani
content: ...You said I'm very sick. If I actually die from this illness, will you still look for them?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Yes. Your health condition is a separate matter from their rescue mission.
You give her a smile.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Besides, we won't let it come to that.

speaker: Thani
content: All right...
She lowers her head and slowly begins drawing symbols on the paper. But her hand shakes, making her drawing slow and messy. When she finishes, she looks up again.

speaker: Thani
content: So... when you find them, will I be able to stay with them?
You pause for a moment, not answering her directly.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This is a facility reserved for Sinners. So, if none of your companions show signs of Mania like you do, we'll place them in an orphanage where they'll be taken care of and receive education.
Thani's shoulders slowly slump with each word you speak.

speaker: Thani
content: So... I'll be separated from everyone? Even if... even if I recover?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It won't be a goodbye. You'll get to visit them, I promise.

speaker: Thani
content: No. Then I don't want to be treated anymore. You all claim you're helping me, but you're just tearing us apart!
She tries to stand up abruptly, but something seems to scratch against her skin. She instantly curls up with a sharp hiss of pain, pressing hard against the spot where her bracelet once was.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You want to protect them, don't you? You've done everything possible to help them escape from the refugee camp and evade the pursuers... If you want to keep them safe, you should start by getting yourself treated, so they won't have to worry about you.
You approach slowly, squatting down to meet her at eye level.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I can help you. I'll place my shackles on you, which can control your Mania and alleviate your Aurum Secretum symptoms.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Please trust me.
She grits her teeth wordlessly, her eyes filled with conflicted emotions. After a long moment, she finally speaks in a small voice.

speaker: Thani
content: ...What exactly are these shackles?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Put simply, it's a link between a Sinner and myself.

speaker: Thani
content: A link... So, once I have these shackles on me, you'll be able to find me whenever you want?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Technically speaking, yes, that is part of its function. In your current situation, it would also allow me to check on your safety at any time.
Thani purses her lips.

speaker: Thani
content: Can I... have some time to think about it...?
Under the harsh lights of the interrogation room, Thani's face is deathly pale, sweat pouring down her skin, yet her eyes remain defiant. After a long moment, you finally nod.

That night, you dispatch operatives to WhiteSands. You suspect Thani wants to see her companions one last time before accepting the shackles, but her infection is already too bad. Meanwhile, Fraser's assassins are closing in on the children. Time is running out for everyone.
<i>But the next day, Thani is gone.
Inside the dark cave, you advance slowly, feeling along the clammy, rough rock faces.

<i>Thani has fled the Bureau in haste, forgetting to remove the ankle monitor the hospital puts on all its patients. The data shows that she's snuck onto a sand ship and then jumped off mid-journey before wandering aimlessly through WhiteSands.
You've finally tracked her to this maze-like canyon cave system. Knowing she still doesn't trust you, you order your squad to wait outside while you venture in alone.
Your fingers brush against several scratches on the rock face. They're rough and hastily made, clearly left there by someone.

Despite being in WhiteSands, not even a whisper of the desert's dry air reaches inside this cave. This place is so cold and humid, it's definitely uninhabitable. Yet somehow, there are plenty of signs of human activity.
Right at your feet lies a rope trap, cunningly positioned in a deceptive spot that nearly makes you lose your balance.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Judging by the condition of the rope... this trap was set quite recently.
But since entering this cave, you haven't heard a single footstep other than your own.
While you are pondering this, you suddenly hear faint giggles coming from somewhere ahead.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Is that... a child?
You carefully step over the rope trap and enter a slightly more spacious area ahead, only to find even more traps lying in wait.
At the end of these intricate rope networks are sharpened wooden stakes, rigged to pierce any intruder who triggers the trap.
You pull out your detector and carefully navigate around these crude traps, moving toward the source of the earlier sounds.
Meanwhile, in the darkness nearby, two girls are pressed tightly into a rift in the rock face.

speaker: Shura
content: Come on, take the bait...

speaker: Thani
content: Shhh... Be patient. Though this is indeed trickier than I expected... If all else fails, I'll go out myself as bait.

speaker: Shura
content: No way! You only just made it back to us, Thani. You can't let those bad people catch you again... I'll do it!

speaker: Thani
content: Huh? Don't go out there! Wait!

speaker: Shura
content: Ah!
[Blank Screen] Background shakes + sound effect
A scrawny girl crashes to the ground in front of you, and you instinctively step forward. Immediately, you hear something swishing through the air.
The sound of a trap being triggered.

A wooden stick flies toward you, hitting your shoulder strap, but it's not nearly as deadly as it appears. You feel only a slight impact against your chest. The stick falls to the ground, rolling several times.

speaker: Thani
content: Shura! Are you okay?!

speaker: Shura
content: Thani! Run! Don't worry about me! My spirit will stay with you all forever!

speaker: Shura
content: You gray-haired fiend! If you must catch someone, take me instead!
Shura's impassioned voice echoes throughout the cave. Small pebbles occasionally sprinkle down from the ceiling, as if even the rocks are moved by her dramatic pledge of self-sacrifice.
Meanwhile, you and Thani exchange bewildered looks speechlessly.

speaker: Thani
content: What? It's you?! I thought it was them...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...I came here to find you.

speaker: Shura
content: Ugh... Thani... m-my foot really hurts...
Hearing Shura's cry, Thani rushes over immediately and helps the girl to her feet.

speaker: Thani
content: Let me see... I think you've sprained it. It'll probably swell up in a day. This is going to be a problem...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Here, use this for now.
You produce a small tube of ointment from your pocket and offer it to Thani. She hesitates for a moment, but eventually takes it.

speaker: Thani
content: Th-thank you...
Thani meticulously applies the ointment to the girl's ankle, but there's also a large patch of skin scraped off her knee that has started to bleed.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I can carry her on my back.
Thani's fingers fidget with the ointment nervously as she weighs her options.

speaker: Thani
content: ...All right then, please take her.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Come...
You kneel down in front of the girl. Thani helps her climb onto your back. The weight you feel is disturbingly light.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Your name is Shura, right?
The girl on your back gives a reluctant grunt of acknowledgment.

speaker: Shura
content: Don't think you can cozy up to me and Thani so easily, gray-haired fiend...

With Thani leading the way, the dark cave feels considerably less threatening. She moves with nimble steps, avoiding loose rocks and slippery moss underfoot, as well as the various traps her group has set.

In the darkness, the monotonous yet distinct sound of dripping water only emphasizes the cave's deathly silence. You can clearly hear your own slightly labored breathing, and the faint echo of Thani's footsteps ahead, bouncing between the rock faces.
After what feels like an eternity, finally, the space before you suddenly opens up.
[Scene Change]

You stand at the edge of a steep cliff, facing a desert stretching endlessly to the horizon. Night has already fallen, yet the moonlight is almost blindingly bright. The wind from the cave entrance carries the dryness of sand, quickly evaporating the moisture from your clothes.
You set Shura down and hear her uneven footsteps dwindle in a certain direction. Your eyes follow her to discover a group of children in tattered clothes huddled against the rock face.

speaker: Thani
content: I'm back!
Thani announces jubilantly. Spotting you beside her, the children study you with wary yet curious gazes.
Seeing their reaction, you open the backpack you've been carrying.

Having been wandering in WhiteSands for so long, hunger is no longer a strange sensation to Thani and her companions. Anticipating this, you specifically packed essential supplies and food before setting out.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I brought some things you might find useful.
The children stare transfixed at the food and medicine you pull out, their previous wariness forgotten as they swarm around you in an instant.
Compressed biscuits, antibiotics, bandages... All common items found in the Bureau.

speaker: Thani
content: Wait! I don't think you can eat that!

Thani nimbly stops a small child who has somehow snuck up beside you and was just about to gnaw on a medicine box. You sort the edible items from the inedible ones, then grab a few cans and open them for the children.
A boy is nudged forward by the others, eyeing you warily while clutching the opened cans against his chest.
He dumps the contents of the cans into a worn copper pot balanced on a few stones. Beneath it flickers a feeble flame.

speaker: Thani
content: That's Kash, our master chef. And that's Dima beside him. They are brother and sister.

speaker: Thani
content: Hehe, don't let his silence fool you! He's usually quite the chatterbox, with a temper to match!
The boy stirring the pot clearly hears Thani's comment. His lips tighten into a pout, his face glowing red in the firelight as he stirs visibly harder.
You sit with the children around the fire as the warm aroma of food fills the air, drawing small, eager murmurs from their hungry lips.
A familiar figure limps toward your group.

speaker: Shura
content: The soup's ready! Here you go!

speaker: Shura
content: This one's for Thani, and this one's for Master Fiend.
Shura even sounds a little proud, as if she's just completed an important mission.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Master Fiend...?

speaker: Thani
content: You should take that as a compliment!
You accept the bowl, finding the ingredients you shared earlier floating in the broth alongside a few berries.
The children cradle identical bowls, trying to savor each spoonful yet unable to resist gulping down the soup. In their crude firepit, flames continue to dance.
You take a sip. The broth is much blander than what you're used to at the Bureau. Salt is clearly a precious commodity for these children.

From across the circle, Dima watches your reaction with curious anticipation. When she catches your eye, she timidly offers you a tiny piece of bread crumb, softened from being carried close to her body.
In the firelight, Thani sits beside you, her eyes crinkling with contentment. After a while, she begins humming an Outland melody you've never heard before.
By day I bury the seeds of light, by night I gaze at the starry sky.
Winds sweep through the forgotten door, bringing songs from my faraway home...
As the song fades and the bowls empty, the children, with their bellies now full, huddle together and drift off to sleep, their breathing growing slow and steady.
You and Thani sit near the cave entrance, backs pressed against the cold rocks as you keep watch over the sleeping children.

speaker: Thani
content: They haven't slept this peacefully in ages. The last time was... maybe right after we left the refugee camp?
Thani speaks in a whisper, careful not to wake the children.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What about you? You look... barely older than them, yet you need to watch over everyone.

speaker: Thani
content: Hehe... Compared to them, I'm practically a grown-up. I promised the adults back at the refugee camp that I'd look after these kids, keep them safe.
Thani's fingers absently trace the sharpened stick resting across her knees, her makeshift weapon for self-defense.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Thani, come back with me.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Your Mania contamination is too severe. If this continues, you'll turn into a Corruptor.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: My shackles can cure you, and they'll also give you the power to truly protect these children.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You can't live like this in WhiteSands forever. Coming to DisCity would be best for all of you.

speaker: Thani
content: I know... But there's only one thing I care about.

speaker: Thani
content: We're going to be separated, right?

speaker: Still, Graves nestles closer to the source of warmth, her shoulders touching the other person's as a gentle warmth passes between the two.
content: ...Yes.
Thani lowers her head, avoiding your gaze.

speaker: Thani
content: The people at the institute once told me the same thing.
[Flashback]

speaker: Fraser Researcher
content: We've got your medical report.
Thani held her breath nervously. The room was suddenly devoid of noise.
After a few seconds, the researcher's face brightened with a friendly smile.

speaker: Fraser Researcher
content: Congratulations! Your medical results are excellent. Welcome to the Aurum Secretum Research Institute. From now on, you're an honored member of our facility.

speaker: Thani
content: R-really?! I can stay at the institute and perhaps one day become like Synex?

speaker: Fraser Researcher
content: Absolutely. We see tremendous potential in you. Who knows? You might even surpass Synex herself.

speaker: Fraser Researcher
content: Go ahead, place your handprint here. Someone will come for you shortly. Starting today, you're no longer just another orphan from the refugee camp.

speaker: Thani
content: Oh, but what does that mean? I am from the refugee camp.

speaker: Fraser Researcher
content: It means you don't have to go back to that miserable life of never knowing when you can have your next meal. Here, we'll provide you with nutritious food and medical care, and we'll nurture you into someone exceptional.

speaker: Thani
content: What if... I want to go back?

speaker: Fraser Researcher
content: Oh dear, that would be a problem. According to our protocols, once you're part of the institute, you can't go back.

speaker: Thani
content: ...But that's no trouble at all! I know the way! I can go back by myself...

speaker: Fraser Researcher
content: No, you cannot go back, and you can never contact anyone from the refugee camp again. Those are the rules, and even I have no say in the matter. Just settle in here. Don't you want to become like Synex? She once went through the exact same thing.

speaker: Fraser Researcher
content: Don't look so glum. Think about it, do you really want to go back to the refugee camp? Do you really miss the constant hunger, the endless fear that the next minor ailment might finally kill you?

speaker: Fraser Researcher
content: And those people at the camp? Nothing but lazy parasites. If they found out how special you are, they'd use every trick to exploit you until there's nothing left.

Thani's fist tightened with each word from the researcher, until her fingers brushed against several syringes hidden beneath the sheets, supplies she'd secretly stashed away and was hoping to sneak back to the refugee camp.
She pulled one out.

speaker: Thani
content: ...Take this!

speaker: Fraser Researcher
content: What did you just throw... Hey! Wait!

speaker: Fraser Researcher
content: Help needed at Lab No. 4: Test Subject #1672 has attacked staff and escaped. Do not let her out of the facility! In case of resistance, lethal force is authorized!
[Scene Change]

speaker: Female Refugee
content: Thani! Why are you here? Aren't you supposed to be at the institute?

speaker: Thani
content: Auntie Isha! Please, keep your voice down... I barely managed to escape.

speaker: Male Refugee
content: What?! You silly girl, you made it to the institute! Why on earth would you run away? If you're selected, you could become like Synex!

speaker: Thani
content: But the people there...!
Thani's voice cut off abruptly. She couldn't bring herself to repeat those words. Facing the concerned looks of those she considered family, she picked and chose her words carefully.

speaker: Thani
content: They said a lot of mean things about the refugee camp... And they told me that according to the rules, I could never come back or see any of you again...

speaker: Thani
content: Even if they could really cure me, what's the point of a better life if I have to live it all alone...

speaker: Thani
content: Besides, my condition hasn't been an entirely bad thing! I wouldn't have escaped without it. If it really comes to that... I can try to sneak back in there again!
After hearing Thani's answer, the two exchanged a glance, but neither could find the words to respond.

speaker: Thani
content: Anyway, enough about that. Look what I smuggled out! You could use some of this medicine, right, Auntie Isha? And this bag here is full of Aurum Secretum fragments I collected on my way out. The institute is really loaded with useful stuff!
[Back to Reality]

speaker: Thani
content: That night, everyone in the camp brought out their best ingredients and made a huge pot of soup for me. I hadn't done anything special, yet they treated me like I was one of those important people from the institute.

speaker: Thani
content: The researchers were wrong. Everyone at the camp was so kind... If I'd stayed at the facility, how would I ever taste such wonderful soup again? And besides, I would've been turned into... a monster...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But the Bureau...

speaker: Thani
content: I know what you're going to say. The Bureau is different.
Thani shakes her head firmly.

speaker: Thani
content: Even if what you're saying is true, I still won't leave them. Even if it means I can't get my treatment, even if we have to wander in WhiteSands forever...

speaker: Thani
content: Because... I made them a promise. I'll always stay by their side, no matter what.
Thani lowers her eyes, purses her lips, and speaks slowly.

speaker: Thani
content: I have these dreams all the time. Dreams where everyone's still here. Dreams of us gathering wild berries together, playing pranks on neighbors, telling jokes to the elderly. You see, they didn't have a good memory, so they'd laugh at the same jokes no matter how many times we told them.

speaker: Thani
content: Often, these beautiful dreams terrify me more than nightmares ever could.

speaker: Thani
content: All this time, we only managed to survive in WhiteSands by staying together as a family. But now...

speaker: Thani
content: That's why I promised them I wouldn't let anything tear us apart again.
You remain silent for a moment, then slowly nod.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: As Chief of the Bureau, I still hope you'll come to DisCity. It would be safest for all of you. But I'll give you time to think about it. Until then, I'll stay with you. WhiteSands are too dangerous.
You give her a smile.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And I want to thank you. For trusting me tonight.
Thani scratches the back of her head, looking somewhat embarrassed.

speaker: Thani
content: Actually... I noticed you had a bunch of good stuff on you, so I figured I'd just grab whatever you had first and worry about the rest later...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I see...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Hmm, and who just told me not long ago that they were robbed clean by desert bandits? The pot's calling the kettle black, huh?

speaker: Thani
content: But I didn't actually do it! It was just a fleeting thought...
She grumbles under her breath, but the next moment, she suddenly freezes. Her body tenses and her back goes rigid, as if she's detected something in the darkness.
Your chest tightens as you leap to your feet, instinctively positioning yourself between the girl and whatever danger lurks nearby.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What's the matter?

speaker: Thani
content: Those people... I think they've found us again!
You follow her gaze out toward the desert. The once-peaceful WhiteSands now reveals threatening silhouettes against the night sky.
In the shadows of jagged rock formations, two dark figures are silently scaling the steep cliff face.

Your breathing grows heavier as you watch them. Their movements are cautious yet expertly efficient, creating not even the faintest sound. Time is running out. They could appear before you at any moment.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Get the children to safety!

Thani nods anxiously, grabbing her wooden stick and tapping it against the ground several times. The children jolt awake, their drowsy eyes filled with confusion and the dawning recognition of danger.

speaker: Thani
content: Follow me! Everyone into the cave!
Thani herds the children forward, dragging and pushing them into the pitch-black cave.
Meanwhile, you dash to the opposite side of the cave entrance, away from where the children fled. You quickly turn on your comms device and transmit your current coordinates.
After completing these steps, you bend down to grab an empty can and hurl it forcefully against a jutting rock below the cave entrance.
[Empty Shot]
The climbing figures below freeze momentarily, then immediately change course, accelerating directly toward your position.

The lead assassin reaches the ledge's edge in seconds. In one fluid motion, he hoists himself up onto the ledge. Moonlight glints off the blade in his hand. He crouches low, muscles tensed, and lunges toward you.
[Empty Shot]
With a sharp crack, warm blood splatters all over your face.
The assassin before you clutches his wrist, staggering backward a few steps.
And standing beside you is Thani.
She grips the sharpened wooden stick tightly in her hand, her eyes full of feigned calmness while her body trembles slightly.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Thani! Go hide with the others!

speaker: Thani
content: You won't last long on your own... Every second we can buy counts!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But you're not strong enough...
Your warning is cut short. The other assassin has silently landed on the ledge, his dagger slicing through the air toward your ribs. You twist away, the blade grazing your shoulder.
Your shoulder strap blocks the blow once again, but this time, the leather splits and blood seeps from your shoulder.

As you dodge the strike, the first assassin regains his footing. Abandoning his fallen knife, he pulls an even smaller dagger from his boot and lunges toward Thani, who has her back turned to him while anxiously watching your fight.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Thani! Behind you!
In that critical moment, Thani does something unexpected. Instead of dodging, she swings her wooden stick with all her might at the assassin's legs while using the momentum to fling herself backward.
[Blank Screen] Screen shakes + impact sound effect
Her back slams hard against the rock face.
You rush to her side, hoping to at least shield one side of her body from further attacks.

speaker: Thani
content: I... I'm okay...
Despite her words, her body is clearly at its breaking point.

Slowly closing in on you, the assassins drag their blades across the rocks, the metal making ear-splitting screeches. Each scrape feels like a knife thrust to Thani. Her legs shake violently, ready to give out at any moment.
Suddenly, one of them throws something at the rock face beside you, creating an explosive bang.

speaker: Thani
content: ...Ahhh!
Thani's knees slam to the ground as her stick rolls off. She clamps her hands over her ears and curls into a ball.
Unable to cause any direct injuries, they're now trying to break Thani's mind by torturing her senses.
At this rate, you won't last until rescue arrives. You must use your shackles on Thani now, if only to temporarily relieve her amplified pain.
You reach out to Thani, but a sword suddenly flies at you both. With a flick of your wrist, you attempt to catch it.
But it slices your palm, cutting into your flesh. The blade, now slick with your blood, doesn't slow down at all, but glides straight toward Thani.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Watch out!
Right then, a tiny shadow emerges.
[Screen Shake Effect]

speaker: Thani
content: Shura!

speaker: Thani
content: Uncle Saen, Aunt Isha, where... where are you going?

speaker: Thani
content: We've driven those bad guys from the Fraser Institute away! Let's have a celebration feast tonight. I'll invite Hella and the others...

speaker: Female Refugee
content: Thani, you've already done more than enough.

speaker: Thani
content: What... what do you mean?
The woman standing before her didn't answer, simply placing a warm hand on top of her head.
In the distance, the sun was slowly being swallowed.

speaker: Female Refugee
content: We adults have only survived this long because of your care, even though you're still just a child yourself...
Those hands gently pressed down, and just as they were about to withdraw, Thani grabbed them tightly.

speaker: Thani
content: Please don't say that...

speaker: Male Refugee
content: We can't go on like this anymore. We need to take responsibility and protect our children... Thani, take the kids and go.

speaker: Female Refugee
content: Remember, we aren't abandoning you. Someday, you'll understand...
[Exit Flashback]

speaker: Thani
content: But I never did understand...

speaker: Thani
content: I don't understand why the adults did what they did.
Thani cradles the smaller girl in her arms as blood gradually soaks through their clothes, rivulets of it trickling down their bodies. Sobs slowly well up from her throat.

speaker: Thani
content: Why... Why would they choose to separate from their families, to be transformed forever into... that... just to gain some so-called power...

speaker: Thani
content: Every day, I dream about all of us being together again. Even in the harshest desert, even with countless enemies hunting us, I wouldn't be afraid... We could have rebuilt a home together and lived our lives properly.
She takes a deep breath and looks up at you.

speaker: Thani
content: Chief... it never could have been possible, could it? In a world like this... how could we ever live the kind of life I imagine?

speaker: Thani
content: It's like... it's like the fruit trees outside the refugee camp. We picked them too often until they couldn't bear fruit anymore... Just like how I was abandoned by my parents to begin with, left alone without any family.

speaker: Thani
content: I know it. I've always known it. I'm not a child anymore. I can't keep running away like this forever.
Thani raises her hand and clutches your sleeve tightly, leaving dark, damp marks on the fabric.
She yanks you forward suddenly, pulling you into her intense gaze.

speaker: Thani
content: I can't stand by and watch my family die again. I want to protect everyone with my own hands...
Tears stream continuously from her eyes, but not for a moment does she close them.

speaker: Thani
content: Chief, I want the shackles!

speaker: Thani
content: I want to protect everyone, even if it means I cannot be with them...

speaker: Thani
content: Even so, I still want to protect them!
Release the shackles
In an instant, countless unfamiliar memories flood into your mind.
A pair of hands brushes away the sand and gently cradles you, a swaddled infant.
This baby has red eyes... how strange. Look, she's even smiling.
How extraordinary. She's bound to have a bright future. Let's give her a name. What about... Thani?
Someone fills the bowl in your hands with soup, a few wild berries floating on its surface. Warmth radiates from the bottom of the bowl into your palms.
Eat up, though it's not much of a meal...
Thani, if it weren't for the medicine you brought, Shura and I would've...
Heh, she even said she wanted to follow your example to improve our living conditions. As her mom, I should have been the one giving her a better life...
The girl standing before you opens her palm, revealing a tiny, shriveled fruit.
Thani! You don't know me, but my mom says you're our hero! Hehe, in my heart, you're even cooler than Synex!
I just found this outside. It's sweet and delicious! It's for you! If I can find more tomorrow, I'll bring you another one!
Oh right, my name...
It's Shura!
The next moment, a strange sensation pulls you back to reality. A gust of wind seems to brush against your skin, yet you haven't moved.
You look up to see Thani darting past, sliding between you and the assassin. She circles around the attacker in one fluid motion before extending her foot to land a precise kick.
The other assassin has already lunged forward, sword drawn, but Thani moves faster than the blade itself. She strikes the assassin's wrist with a powerful blow.
The dagger tumbles to the ground as the assassin angrily swipes back to grab her, but Thani has already nimbly sprung backward, evading his reach.
Having done all that, Thani rushes back to your side, the air stirring around her from her speed.

speaker: Thani
content: They move fast, but... I can see them clearly.

speaker: Thani
content: ...The one on the left will come at us in three seconds!
Just as Thani finishes speaking, the assassin on the left leaps up, but she simply sidesteps the blow with grace. The blade slices through empty air and crashes against the rock.
You seize an opening and drive your foot into his knee. He grunts in pain and staggers backward. Pressing forward, you follow with a crushing elbow strike to his throat.
Meanwhile, Thani seizes the moment to scoop up a handful of gravel from the ground and fling it at the other assassin's eyes.

The two assassins stumble back a few steps. At that moment, the roar of engines erupts from behind distant sand dunes. You look up to see a helicopter rapidly closing in, its cabin door wide open and gun barrels aimed at the ground below.

speaker: Task Force Operative
content: Get down!
You grab Thani and pull her to the ground. A split second later, gunfire erupts as precise bullet shots strike the ground around the assassins' feet, forcing them into complete submission.

Amid the thundering gunfire, you feel Thani wrench herself free from your grasp. You instinctively reach for her, but your fingers only brush the fluttering hem of her clothes as she scrambles desperately toward the other girl.

speaker: Shura
content: Thani...? Is that... you?
As the two assassins are pinned to the ground, the gunfire gradually ceases.
You hear leather boots approaching from behind. A sound that normally would bring you complete relief.

speaker: Task Force Operative
content: Chief, we've neutralized all enemies in the area!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Someone has been wounded here.

Before you all, the two girls huddle together, their faces softly illuminated by moonlight. You don't really need to look for Thani's hands. They're pressed against Shura's abdomen, desperately trying to stop the blood gushing out between her fingers.
Despite the thundering helicopter rotors, you can hear the girls' voices clearly.

speaker: Shura
content: Thani... am I... am I finally as strong... as you?...

speaker: Thani
content: Of course... you're our brave little Shura.

speaker: Shura
content: Will you... will you miss me?
Thani reaches out to wipe the girl's face clean, but tears keep falling, mixing with the sand and dust and sticking stubbornly to her skin.

speaker: Thani
content: Do you remember the story I told you?

speaker: Shura
content: Thani... that story you told me... it's true, isn't it?

speaker: Thani
content: Yes, yes.

speaker: Thani
content: We will never be apart. Never ever.

speaker: Thani
content: You'll stay with me, and I'll always stay with you. Forever and ever.

speaker: Shura
content: Just like... how we've been... together on our journey...

speaker: Thani
content: Yes, just like how we've been together on our journey.
Reassured by the answer, the girl closes her eyes with a smile on her face.
She's about to have a very long dream.
In her dream, moonlight pours down over the warmly lit homes, while the white sand beneath her feet sparkles like the milky way.
[Scene Change]
The mission is over. You will bring Thani and the children back to DisCity. Afterward, these kids from the refugee camp will be placed in an orphanage in the city to begin their new lives.
Thani will follow you back to the Bureau to receive medical treatment.
This time, she doesn't refuse.
Before your official departure, you and Thani come to the desert to say goodbye to your friend.
Along the way, Thani cradles a small box in her arms with great care, walking in silence.
Suddenly, she snaps out of her daze, looks at you, and breaks into a smile.

speaker: Thani
content: Chief, do you remember that song I sang before?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Of course I remember.

speaker: Thani
content: Actually, an elderly lady from the refugee camp taught me that song. She also told me a story.

speaker: Thani
content: Legend says that everyone born in WhiteSands is blessed by the Desert Goddess. When our bodies perish, our souls will transform into a single grain of sand in WhiteSands, living on in this world forever.

speaker: Thani
content: Which means that, here in the desert, if you close your eyes and listen with your heart, you can hear the voices of your departed loved ones in the wind.

speaker: Thani
content: I've shared this story before, but no one really seemed to believe it. Chief, do you believe it?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Yes, I believe all of you have been blessed.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm sorry... but it's a beautiful story.

speaker: Thani
content: Hehe, actually, I didn't believe it before! Like I said, I wasn't a little kid anymore!

speaker: Thani
content: Granny got a bit forgetful in her later years. She would often mix up elements of the story. Sometimes it was the Desert Goddess's blessing, other times it was the Wind God's. Eventually, I had to remind her of her original version.

speaker: Thani
content: If that story was really true, why couldn't she remember it properly?

speaker: Thani
content: Besides, after I got sick, I spent so much time listening to the wind. But even with my super-hearing, I never once caught Granny's song.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Thani...

speaker: Thani
content: But now I believe it. Because last night, I saw your memories.

speaker: Thani
content: Why do you look so surprised? You obviously saw mine too!

speaker: Thani
content: I saw you fighting side by side with so many people, and they were all so amazing!

speaker: Thani
content: Even though they looked a bit odd, just like the folks at the refugee camp, I could feel they were all good people!

speaker: Thani
content: They're your family, aren't they?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Yes. Every single one of them. My important family.
You raise your hand to your chest. The shackles vibrate slightly, as if responding to your words.

speaker: Thani
content: So that's why we won! It was because they were helping us, wasn't it?

speaker: Thani
content: Before yesterday, I wouldn't have even dared to imagine fighting those killers! But last night, it wasn't just the two of us in that battle. There were so many others cheering us on.

speaker: Thani
content: So I think maybe Granny's story was true after all.

speaker: Thani
content: Our family will always watch over us. Even when they can't physically be by our side, even when... we can never see them again, their strength remains with us.
Thani bows her head, smiling down at the box in her hands.

speaker: Thani
content: As long as the wind keeps blowing, we'll always be together. After all, don't we all share the same sky above us?
She opens the box, and the wood makes a soft sound, like a child's mischievous giggle.

speaker: Thani
content: So I believe she'll always be with me.

speaker: Thani
content: Shura.
Her voice catches, tears threatening to fall at any moment and dampen the ashes in the container.
But you see no tears. When she lifts her face to the wind again, there's only a radiant smile.

speaker: Thani
content: Bless me, Shura.
She raises her hands, holding the box up to the wind.
You watch as the white sand before you gets scattered by the wind, then gathers together again before drifting away into the distance.
The wind continues to blow. On this stretch of the mortal world, you seem to hear the whispered murmurs of countless old friends, carried by the breeze coming from behind, gently embracing you.
Beside you, Thani begins humming that song again. Her voice catches before she finishes the first bit of the melody, but she quickly resumes softly, never faltering again.
...In my dreams I light my lanterns, gazing up at the stars from the ruins.
My friend who saw me off, are you singing the same song too?
[Scene Change]
It's another ordinary day at the Bureau. You've just finished a meeting and are heading back to your office.
[Blank Screen] Effect
You sense someone's presence.
Thani is clinging to the wall with her four limbs, an overstuffed backpack strapped to her back.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Thani, what are you up to again?

speaker: Thani
content: Shh... I'm going to visit Kash and the others at the orphanage.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You don't need to sneak around like this to leave the Bureau. Just file a request.

speaker: Thani
content: No way! This is part of my training. If I can avoid triggering the alarms this time, it means I've gotten stronger!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Okay. Just be careful...
Before you can finish your sentence, you hear a loud crash. Almost simultaneously, pain shoots through your body as a massive weight slams into you.

speaker: Thani
content: Waaah! Why is the floor so slippery today?!
The contents of her bag scatter across the floor. A can rolls right to your feet.
Thani lies flat on her back, having managed to save only a bag of fruit. She can't help but laugh at herself as she clutches the heavy bag to her chest.
From the other end of the corridor, a mechanical female voice speaks.

speaker: Labyrinth
content: Labyrinth is here to report that today's floor waxing has been completed. Master may inspect the results whenever you want.

speaker: Chief
content: Good morning, Evie.

speaker: Evie
content: Good morning. It's a pleasure to meet you. I look forward to working... Oh, sorry, force of habit. I didn't mean to imply that I'm glad to take up your precious morning work hours...

speaker: Choice
options: Laugh it off and reassure her

speaker: Chief
content: There's no need to be so tense, Evie. I won't bite. You can relax a little.

Evie nods along obediently, but her body remains stiff as a board, her face completely pale. Well, that's to be expected. To her, an MBCC Interrogation is about as far removed from everyday life as Phanuel's speech at that concert.

speaker: Chief
content: How about this—let's start by going over some basic information. It'll help you ease into things. Could you tell me a bit about yourself? I'd like to cross-reference it with what we have on file.

speaker: Evie
content: Of course. My name is Evie. I'm 25... wait, no, 26 years old. Female. I work in the marketing department of a cosmetics company in Eastside. I was born in Eastside, both my parents are still alive, and my bank balance is...

She's remarkably cooperative, and doesn't hide a single thing about herself. The moment you stop her, she simply closes her mouth. Among all the people you've interrogated, she ranks among the most compliant—and most oblivious—of ordinary civilians.

speaker: Chief
content: Thank you for your cooperation. I can see that you are a perfectly upstanding, model citizen of Eastside. Now then, Evie. Do you know why someone with a clean record like yours would end up sitting here?

speaker: Evie
content: ...Is it because of an abnormal fluctuation in my M-value?
She sounds like a student who's suddenly been picked to answer a question in class. You correct her.

speaker: Chief
content: To be precise, it's because those fluctuations have been affecting your body. Although minor, our monitoring equipment did pick up signs of your power going berserk multiple times. That is what made MBCC's intervention mandatory.

speaker: Evie
content: Really...?! I'm... I'm so sorry! I didn't mean to cause anyone any trouble.

She nearly springs out of the interrogation chair, but the momentum doesn't carry her through the apology. She stops mid-sentence, presses a hand to her chest, and takes a long moment to steady herself before finishing.

speaker: Evie
content: The thing is, I really didn't feel any issues with my health, or, well, my power going berserk... I mean, I eat just fine, sleep just fine, and my performance at work is... perfectly normal too. I'm doing perfectly well...

speaker: Chief
content: You don't need to hide how you're really feeling out of fear of being a burden. Your dark circles and those dizzy spells speak louder than anything. Besides, even if it isn't your condition that's causing this, we'll need to find the real reason behind your M-value fluctuations either way. I hope you can understand.

speaker: Evie
content: Sorry about that... I guess people like us are just too used to being subhealthy. Though I guess if anything has changed about my daily routine... it'd be that I've started actively using my <color=#fb9259>power</color>...?

She seems genuinely puzzled. It's only after mulling it over for a moment that she manages to piece together a clue. You gesture for her to continue, and she immediately lays out why she started using her power on her own.

speaker: Evie
content: It started when my personal account received a private message from a stranger, claiming to be <color=#fb9259>Mimi-meow</color>'s manager...
Terminal or 14 Chat Frame - Web Chat

speaker: Manager
content:
<color=#7683a2>Economics Dept. - Contact for Mimi-meow Related Matters</color>: ...It was your remarkable performance during the Phanuel incident that first caught our attention. We were absolutely delighted to discover that someone with such profound insight into the idol industry... is actually a fan of our Mimi-meow!

<color=#7683a2>Economics Dept. - Contact for Mimi-meow Related Matters</color>: As you are no doubt aware, the Phanuel incident dealt a severe blow to the idol industry, and the prejudice against us has only grown worse as a result. Our Mimi-meow, despite being a growing underground idol, has not been spared from the fallout.

<color=#7683a2>Economics Dept. - Contact for Mimi-meow Related Matters</color>: In order to counter the impact of the negative press, our company is working hard to organize promotional events for her. Our hope is that more people will come to see her dedication, and know that there are still idols out there who give their all to bring love and courage to their fans.

<color=#7683a2>Economics Dept. - Contact for Mimi-meow Related Matters</color>: If someone as prominent as yourself were willing to attend these events and show your support for Mimi-meow... it would surely help her win more hearts and become an even better idol! This is something only you can do!

<color=#7683a2>Economics Dept. - Contact for Mimi-meow Related Matters</color>: And these events will become memories that belong to you and Mimi-meow only. Surely... you wouldn't refuse, yes?

<color=#fb9259>Evie (23F, Section C, Left 07)</color>: Of course not! Oh, I mean, I'll definitely be there! Please, you have to let me be a part of this! I'll do anything if it means helping Mimi-meow!
[End of Chat Log]

speaker: Chief
content: I see... But as far as I can tell, he was simply looking to capitalize on the fame you gained from the Phanuel incident, no? So how did that lead to you using your power?
You skim through the invitation written with loaded language. For someone like Evie, who adores Mimi-meow, these carefully crafted words are nothing short of irresistible.

speaker: Evie
content: The promotional events escalated step by step. At first, it was just solo interviews, and I'm pretty sure only underground idol fans would be able to recognize me in them. But then, a clip of me with Mimi-meow went viral out of nowhere.

speaker: Evie
content: Not only did I start trending, Mimi-meow's name also became one of the most searched terms! It was the first time she'd ever trended on social media. I was so...
Her eyes light up, her pale cheeks gaining a flush of color.

But the warmth doesn't brighten her sickly face so much as drain it. It's as if the excitement is burning through whatever energy is left in her. She suddenly starts swaying mid-sentence, and it takes a few seconds for her to recover.

speaker: Evie
content: ...so proud. When the manager saw how well it worked, he kept at it and came up with a new plan!

speaker: Evie
content: I have to say, he's such a visionary! He didn't fear my power at all! If anything, he said it was perfect for promoting Mimi-meow! He said that if I used my power at Mimi-meow's live show, it would tell everyone—
Recall

speaker: Melodramatic Broadcast
content: Everyone, may I have your attention, please! What's <color=#fb9259>shining upon</color> Mimi-meow on stage right now isn't the venue's lights—it's the <color=#fb9259>power</color> of the one and only operator of the Mimi-meow Shrine fan account, Mimi-meow's devoted fan, Miss Evie!

speaker: Melodramatic Broadcast
content: It may not be the steadiest, and it may not be the brightest. But what matters is that this light shines with sincerity, and it burns with her passion. Behold! With <color=#fb9259>love</color> as <color=#fb9259>kindling</color>, even a fan can light up a stage like this, and <color=#fb9259>illuminate</color> our beloved <color=#fb9259>idol</color>!

speaker: Melodramatic Broadcast
content: And of course, our idol wouldn't be able to sing on this stage without the support of everyone here! Now, raise the light in your hands! Let us shine with Mimi-meow!

The crowd erupts. A wave of orange glow sticks floods the venue, and the screams nearly tear through the roof. At the edge of the side curtain, still in her business suit, the girl watches her idol, bathed in light and cheers. Her eyes slowly well up.

speaker: Fans
content: Mimi-meow! Mimi-meow! Mimi-meow, the sun within the night! This time, we'll light up the stage for you, Mimi-meow!
(End of Flashback)

speaker: Evie
content: Sob... S-sorry, I lost my composure just now. It's just that whenever I think about how my power was able to light up Mimi-meow's stage, and even serve as a beacon for those who dedicate themselves to her... I can't hold back my tears...

speaker: Evie
content: Mimi-meow and I are both so lucky to have such a dedicated team behind the scenes...! Cough, cough, as long as we keep at it, cough, cough, I know Mimi-meow will reach even greater heights and shine for even more people...!
Classic corporate nonsense. Nevertheless, Evie is eating it right up. She's been moved to tears by these memories, and even the coughing couldn't stop her from finishing her passionate speech.

speaker: Chief
content: Alright, that's enough, Evie. I think I have a pretty good idea of what happened now. Including, of course, why your M-value fluctuations have been affecting your health.
You press a hand to your forehead and cut her off, giving her a chance to catch her breath before she passes out.

speaker: Chief
content: It sounds like Mimi-meow's management knew full well that you have a full-time job, and yet they still had you skip sleep at night to use your powers for their shows. Hardly surprising that your power's been going out of control, given your body's been pushed past its limit already.

speaker: Evie
content: That... can't be the only reason though. I think at least. I tend to get dizzy and cough a lot when I pull all-nighters at the office anyway. And the ringing in my ears is probably caused by the speakers at the venue being too loud...

She's still trying to swallow her discomfort and put all the blame on herself. You now realize that getting through to her will mean shifting the focus beyond herself. So, you put on a grave expression, and start to speak in a more serious tone.

speaker: Chief
content: And I suppose violating performance regulations is perfectly normal too? Sinners are required to submit a notice before using their powers at public events or commercial shows. Any professional organizer should have reminded you to file such an application. Did they?

speaker: Evie
content: Huh?! There's a regulation like that...?! I'm so sorry, I had no idea... I'll make sure to check the relevant rules beforehand from now on. I won't let it happen again!
The strategy works. As expected, the term "violating regulations" would send a law-abiding soul such as her into genuine panic, so much so that her dark circles look even darker now.

speaker: Evie
content: I didn't realize it'd involve so much... I thought it was something I could just grit my teeth and get through, even if my body started feeling a bit off...

speaker: Evie
content: I just wanted Mimi-meow to be happy... Same for her manager, her staff, everyone who loves her just like I do. As long as everyone's happy, that's all that matters. A few side effects... are nothing...

speaker: Chief
content: You're already thinking about next time? Do you actually plan to drag yourself there in this state if they call again?

This again. The whole "I'm fine, I can hold on, what matters is that everyone else is happy" philosophy. You're a little dumbfounded at this point, and you've even started to question whether she's just pretending not to lack common sense. Still, you can't help but be a little concerned.

speaker: Chief
content: Evie, I'm not sure how well you understand what it means to be a Sinner, or what Mania really is. But you need to know that because of how useful your abilities can be, there will always be people looking to exploit you.

speaker: Chief
content: Even in Eastside, Mania is still a sensitive subject. If you want to keep living a normal life, that's something you'll need to be aware of. Are you... sure you haven't been taken advantage of? Has the management ever probed you in this regard?
Evie shakes her head, then hesitates and nods.

speaker: Evie
content: They did want to use the story of my power awakening as promotional material, but I turned them down. I just didn't want Mimi-meow to feel bad about it if she found out. Does... that count?

speaker: Choice
options: The story of your power awakening?

speaker: Chief
content: If I recall correctly... You awakened your power and became a Sinner after being attacked with an unregistered, crude Mania weapon, yes? And the attacker stated that their intended target was actually the underground idol, <color=#fb9259>Mimi-meow</color>.

speaker: Chief
content: You were just waiting by the backstage exit when you stepped in to protect her. A commendable act, yes, but also an undeserved misfortune. You've given up so much for her... yet you insist on keeping it a secret just so she won't feel guilty?
Evie responds to your question with a simple nod, as if her quiet suffering and thankless sacrifice were too ordinary to warrant further discussion.

speaker: Evie
content: Is there... something wrong with that? Mimi-meow is such a kind person. If she ever found out, she'd definitely feel terrible! The last thing I want is to make her doubt whether she should keep being an idol because of this!

speaker: Evie
content: Her performance saved me once... so I know just how much her existence means. I just want her to keep doing what she does on that stage... She doesn't need to concern herself, cough cough, with these little things.

Evie drops her gaze, lost in memory, a warm and bashful smile tugging at the corners of her mouth. She lingers in the sweetness of it, utterly unconcerned with the danger she's in or what she stands to lose, never once stopping to ask herself whether any of this is right.

Getting infected with Mania and becoming a Sinner to save her idol, running her body into the ground doing promotional work for her idol... These are "little things," according to her. Is nothing a big deal to this girl, as long as it means wearing herself down for someone else's sake?
Just what has she been through to become like this? And what would it even take to pull her out of this dangerous tendency of sacrificing herself?

You are no savior, and you cannot fix everything. But as the Chief of MBCC, you have a responsibility to make sure the person in front of you never again falls into the abyss of Mania, simply because she's <color=#fb9259>giving too much of herself</color>.

speaker: Chief
content: And what does your family think about this "little thing"? Even if they don't expect some kind of repayment, surely they'd at least want Mimi-meow to know what happened and be grateful?

speaker: Evie
content: My family? You mean... my parents? Well... actually, they don't even know I'm a Sinner...

speaker: Chief
content: You never told them? Why not? Did you decide to shoulder everything alone so you wouldn't worry them?

speaker: Evie
content: Well... that's part of it. But... It's also because I can still go to work and live my life normally, even though I've become a Sinner. I haven't caused too much trouble for anyone, so...

speaker: Chief
content: I'm not worried about you causing trouble for others, Evie. I'm worried about you. You're always thinking about others, afraid of burdening them. But what about you?

speaker: Chief
content: It's true that unless a Sinner is a minor, the Bureau doesn't notify their family. But that policy exists to protect privacy, not to force you to fight alone. Have you ever considered that your way of thinking is what's causing your body to fall apart?

The words seem to touch on something Evie never even considered. She freezes, her expression going blank, and it takes a long moment before she finally processes things and manages to mutter out an uncertain response.

speaker: Evie
content: Is it...? But... <color=#fb9259>that's</color> just how it always is at home...

speaker: Chief
content: <color=#fb9259>That</color>?

speaker: Evie
content: It's nothing special, really. My family is... pretty ordinary. My father had a pretty high salary, but he was always busy. He'd come home late, or sometimes not at all. And on the rare occasions he did come home, he never liked hearing about household troubles or anything unpleasant.

speaker: Evie
content: My mother cared deeply for my father, and her mood was easily affected by him. I couldn't be a substitute for my father, so I just... did what I could. At the very least, I didn't want to make things harder for her.

speaker: Chief
content: Harder?

speaker: Evie
content: Yes. Every day, my mother would sit in the living room, waiting for my father. Sometimes she'd sit there all night. She'd say it was fine, that he was doing it all for the family. But I could tell she was really sad when he didn't come home. She wanted someone to be there for her.

speaker: Evie
content: So I'd talk with her, get water for her, and remind her to go to bed soon. I kept whatever was going on at school to myself so I wouldn't worry her. Sometimes, she'd pat me on the head and say she was glad to have such a sensible child. That made me really happy.
She smiles as she talks. Yet, all you can see is a young Evie learning to be her mother's emotional anchor, giving more and more of herself just to earn a small measure of her mother's attention.

speaker: Evie
content: As long as I pay a little more attention to how everyone's feeling and try a little harder, I can make the people around me happy. And when they're happy, I'm happy too. What's... wrong with that?

speaker: Chief
content: Is that something your mother taught you?

speaker: Evie
content: Well... she'd just say that a little discomfort was no big deal. That as long as she <color=#fb9259>gave</color> enough, my father would notice her efforts, and he'd repay her with an equal amount of <color=#fb9259>love</color>.

The logic behind her self-destruction finally becomes clear. She pushes past the damage to her body and keeps on <color=#fb9259>giving</color> because she believes it's the only way to earn what she calls <color=#fb9259>love</color>.

speaker: Chief
content: Which is why you don't know how to say no, why you give without keeping score, and why you keep pushing. But the logic doesn't hold, does it? If those who give are truly always compensated in full, you wouldn't need some idol to be your anchor, would you? Nor would you be looking for something more.
Your question cuts straight to the heart of it, yet she doesn't flinch or falter. Evie simply looks back at you, genuinely puzzled.

speaker: Evie
content: That's just... normal, isn't it? You have to give to receive. That's just... how life is. I might be tired, but all I need is to find something that'll keep me going for a little longer and help me push through.

speaker: Evie
content: My dad, my mom, my boss, my coworkers... they all work hard. They're all doing their best. I'm not special or anything.

speaker: Evie
content: If someone has something come up, or someone's not feeling well, I'll pick up the slack and handle a bit more work at night... That's all perfectly normal. Sometimes, people even thank me when they notice I'm working overtime!

speaker: Evie
content: If anyone has it hard... it's Mimi-meow. She's the one who showed me that even when you're struggling, you can still shine and illuminate the people around you!
The moment Mimi-meow's name comes up, her gaze drifts somewhere distant, and her voice becomes much more lively.

speaker: Evie
content: Without her, I don't know if I'd have made it this far! I still remember the first time I went to her live show. I was so exhausted I could barely lift my head, but she still drew me in!

speaker: Evie
content: It was winter, and she was out on the street doing promotions in a little skirt. She must have been freezing, but she still noticed how tired I was. She asked if I was doing okay, and if she could sing me a song to cheer me up.

speaker: Evie
content: Yes! And that's how I found my sun! The stage was tiny, the crowd was small, even the glow sticks were freebies. But she sang with everything she had regardless, and every time we awkwardly waved our arms, she'd break into the most radiant smile!

speaker: Evie
content: That's when I thought—this must be what my mom was talking about! She keeps shining and radiating warmth, even when she's struggling herself. She's someone who earned her happiness by <color=#fb9259>giving</color>... cough cough cough!

The coughing hits her without warning, perhaps because she was getting too excited. She doubles over, struggling to catch her breath, yet still fights to compose herself so that she can get across all the emotions welling up inside her.

speaker: Evie
content: And that's how I came to be her fan. She's the star that lights up my life! I want her to stand on a bigger, brighter stage, so that everyone can see her shine!

speaker: Evie
content: If you'd seen her live, you'd understand! Mimi-meow is genuinely worth it. She's not the kind of idol who's only in it for the fame. She takes her work seriously, she's gentle, she remembers anything the fans have said to her, and she even reminds everyone not to stay up all night voting for her!
She looks at you with something close to reverence, her eyes bright and glimmering. The timid Sinner who shuffled into the interrogation room moments ago is nowhere to be seen now.

You can tell Evie genuinely sees Mimi-meow for who she is, rather than a commodity to be consumed. More importantly, if Mimi-meow truly is everything Evie says she is, then it might just be the key to bringing her back down to earth.

speaker: Chief
content: Doesn't sound like Mimi-meow would approve of what you're doing then.

speaker: Chief
content: If she's someone who'd remind her fans not to stay up all night voting for her, I'd say she'd be anything but happy knowing you're working all day before heading to events at night, and constantly using your power. Wouldn't you agree?
A flicker of doubt crosses Evie's face, but she quickly finds a refutation, stumbling over her words as she speaks up.

speaker: Evie
content: But I'm doing this so more people can see her! Mimi-meow always says she wants to bring <color=#fb9259>love</color> and courage to as many people as possible. If my efforts can make that happen a little sooner, she'll definitely... cough cough, she'll definitely understand!
And there it is again, the self-sacrifice theory that Evie keeps using to justify her recklessness. It seems there's little hope of digging any deeper before you break this loop.
So you let it go for now. You'll likely need to pay a visit to this little idol, who might just be able to help you progress.
Whether she truly is as flawless as Evie makes her out to be, or simply another Phanuel hiding behind a perfect mask.

speaker: Chief
content: Alright. Let's just say Mimi-meow would understand. Still, the Bureau has an obligation to prevent Mania outbreaks, and I can't stand by while you keep using your power in your current condition.

speaker: Chief
content: I'll need you to resubmit the application for every time you've used your powers without authorization. On top of that, you'll need to sign a written declaration that this won't happen again. Any objections?

speaker: Evie
content: No, but... I mean, could I...

With your conclusions drawn and your approach set, the interrogation is coming to an end. However, Evie doesn't comply as readily as you'd expected. Instead, she squirms and makes a rather presumptuous request.

speaker: Evie
content: Could you give me just one last chance...? There's a <color=#fb9259>special live show</color> the day after tomorrow. It means a lot to Mimi-meow and us fans, and I already promised I'd be there to <color=#fb9259>work as the lights</color>...

speaker: Evie
content: I know it's against the rules, but... what if I filed an application right now? If that's still not okay... could I ask you to come supervise in person? I know you're busy, but this really means a lot to me. I promise it won't take up too much of your time...
She peeks at you through her hair, like a puppy that's gauging its owner's mood.

speaker: Chief
content: I thought I made it clear that your power is taking a toll on your body?

speaker: Evie
