content: The thing is, it's a big day for Mimi-meow, and I've put together a special celebration event... If I, the organizer, suddenly don't show up, everyone will be left in a bind, and it might affect Mimi-meow too...

speaker: Choice
options: Let me check my schedule first. I've been pretty busy lately.
If it means that much to you, sure.

content: Option 1

You look down to open your schedule, acting like you're hesitant. You haven't looked once during that time, yet you can practically feel Evie's gaze burning into your terminal, equal parts hope and prayer.

speaker: Chief
content: You're lucky. Things aren't too hectic right now. Underground idol shows are usually in the evenings, right? I should be able to afford to keep one night open.

speaker: Chief
content: I'll come with you, but not as a supervisor. The shackles can help offset the burden of using your special power. Think of me as a field medic sent by the medical department.

speaker: Evie
content: I-is that really okay?! Are you sure it's not too much trouble? Wait, do I, cough cough cough, need to do some kind of test? It's okay, just treat me like a lab rat! Thank you, I really mean it, thank you so much!

Evie's distress melts away at your words. She's coughing up a storm and practically beside herself with joy, so much so that she doesn't know what to do with her hands or feet. You can't help but shake your head with a smile.
Of course, you have no plans to use her as a "lab rat" for anything. You're heading there to meet a certain someone. But if it puts her at ease, maybe it's a good thing.

speaker: Evie
content: I'll put together everything for you in advance! The time, location, schedule, and the manager's contact info. I'll also send over a starter playlist for getting into Mimi-meow... Oh, sorry, that last part... probably has nothing to do with the approval process, does it?

speaker: Chief
content: Feel free to attach it for now.

speaker: Evie
content: O-okay!

She finally lets out a smile that's genuinely relaxed, her fan merchandise swaying softly with the movement. But all that color and brightness can't hide the pallor on her face or the dark circles under her eyes.

Then let's see if the "center of her world" can help you treat both the symptoms and the cause. Let's see if she can stabilize this dim star that's always on the verge of <color=#fb9259>burning out</color>.

The backstage area before the show is more chaotic than you expected. Racks of performance outfits hang in rows, decorative ribbons and balloons are strewn about, and in the middle of the hallway, a large number sticker sits all alone, for whatever reason.

speaker: Evie
content: Chief, this is your temporary backstage pass. Just hang it around your neck. Though you're from the Bureau, there are a lot of people today. It'd be a hassle if one of the staff stopped you...

speaker: Choice
options: Aren't you one of the staff?

speaker: Evie
content: Not exactly. I just help out pretty often, so I happen to know the ropes.

But the folder in her hands, covered in color-coded sticky notes, tells a different story. Lighting, supplies, flower arrangements, the surprise cake, entry routes—every item is meticulously marked in various colors.
You watch as Evie briskly handles one crisis after another. It's hard to imagine that this is the same girl who was afraid a single cough might take up too much of your time.

speaker: Fan A
content: Evie! The banners just arrived! I'd like to start cutting them right away, but the delivery guy said there are too many boxes, so he can only drop them at the back door. What do we do?

speaker: Evie
content: The back door? But that's where the equipment goes through later. We can't afford to have it blocked... Let me think, cough cough...
Though she looks ghastly right now, she still does her best to act like a proper organizer and see every last thing through. Seems like she really doesn't want to waste the chance you gave her.

speaker: Evie
content: ...Have them leave everything by the warehouse entrance for now. Just make sure they don't block the fire exit. Oh, and, get a couple of people over there to move the stuff.

speaker: Fan B
content: Evie, um... I just checked the final payment for the cake, and it looks like it's a bit over budget. Should I send a payment request to the group chat? Get the people online to chip in?

speaker: Evie
content: It's fine, I'll cover it for now. Everyone's already worked so hard. Let's not let something like this get in the way of today's surprise.

speaker: Fan B
content: We can't just let you cover it all yourself! Today is Mimi-meow's 365th live AND her first anniversary! We absolutely cannot drop the ball! I don't care if I have to live on dirt for a while, I... What the?! How are you so fast, Evie?!

The moment she finishes speaking, Evie lowers her head and makes the transfer on her terminal. The motion is practiced, almost like she's handling payment for office supplies at work, except nobody is ever going to reimburse her for this one. Still, she doesn't spare it a second thought.

speaker: Fan C
content: Right?! No fair, Evie! You always rush to pay and handle all the logistics, and by the time you're done, there's nothing left for us to do! We never even get a chance to show our love for Mimi-meow... Come on, throw us a bone here!

And yet, her <color=#fb9259>sacrifices</color> don't stand out here at all. If anything, it's something to fight over. Perhaps that, more than anything else, is what makes this lively, devoted little group so special.
It becomes even more obvious when you look at the numerous people rushing back and forth—not a single one of them is wearing a staff uniform.

speaker: Chief
content: Wait... are all these people fans who volunteered to <color=#fb9259>help</color>?

speaker: Evie
content: Well, not all of them... Haha. But there are a lot more volunteers than usual today, so the regular staff have basically been swallowed up by the crowd. It's the anniversary live, after all. Everyone wants to see their efforts help Mimi-meow shine <color=#fb9259>brighter</color>!

speaker: Evie
content: Honestly, I never expected the manager to hand over so much control for this surprise event and just let us fans take the reins... Hehe, it feels great to be trusted. Makes me want to work even harder!
Trust, or exploitation? Ever since you saw the manager's persuasion tactics and learned that he had manipulated Evie into using her power illegally, you've been wary of him and whoever's backing him.

This troubling culture in Mimi-meow's fandom, one where giving beyond their means is seen as a badge of honor, may well be a result of the company deliberately fostering and steering such a mindset for profit.

Of course, you won't point any of that out in front of the believers. For now, the task is to observe and blend in... You need to see whether the star of this show could be the key to changing everything.

speaker: Evie
content: Sorry, I need to take this... Yes, you got the right place. Is this the cake delivery? The front entrance is for the audience, could you come around to the back... Huh? You ran into the equipment truck? But I don't think anyone's free to go meet up with you right now...
It sounds like Evie has run into a staffing problem. Her eyes sweep back and forth across the bustling crowd in front of her, trying to work out the logistics in her head.

speaker: Evie
content: But...

speaker: Chief
content: Just stay here. You're on medical leave. I can't have you running to the back door and back again. What if you collapse on the way?

speaker: Evie
content: ...Then I'll leave it to you! Thank you so, so much!
She pulls a sheet from her folder, flips it over, and scrawls out a route in seconds, the instructions already tumbling out of her mouth.

speaker: Evie
content: Once you get the cake, just bring it here! This is the highlight of our event, so I really can't thank you enough for helping. I'll come meet up with you as soon as I can!
Alley

One look at the cake and you immediately understand what Evie meant by "highlight." Calling it a cake would be an understatement. It's more like a miniature stage model, dressed up in buttercream and icing.

The cake has three tiers in an orange gradient, topped with a fondant figurine of Mimi-meow. Beside it is a glittering plaque that reads: "Happy 1st Anniversary to our idol! For the one and only Mimi-meow!"

speaker: Delivery Person
content: Careful with that. There's dry ice and light strips inside. Apparently, they're supposed to light up when the cake goes on stage.
As the delivery person hands the cart over to you, there's a hint of sympathy in their expression. Looks like they've taken you as a porter.

speaker: Chief
content: First I've heard of a cake that has power.

speaker: Delivery Person
content: Fan support culture is pretty crazy these days. This isn't even that over the top, in fact.
...This isn't over the top? You can't quite hide your disbelief as you silently wheel that saccharine, expensive, and impossibly heavy monument of <color=#fb9259>love</color> into the backstage.

As you do, a question quietly surfaces. If even you, the one merely pushing the cart, feel the weight of it... will the person receiving this surprise really not feel burdened by it? Or are you simply too unfamiliar with fandom culture to understand?
Livehouse Backstage

speaker: Evie
content: No dents, light strip connector's intact, dry ice is perfect... Thank you so much, Chief!

speaker: Evie
content: The show's about to start! Could you stay and wait with me a little longer? We're planning to wheel it onto the stage during the fifth song!
After rushing over to check on the cake, Evie stays by your side at the edge of the stage with no intention of moving. You can't help but ask—

speaker: Chief
content: Aren't you going to watch from the front?

The opening announcement from out front signals the start of the show, and the backstage briefly falls quiet. Music pours through the walls and curtains, the beat strong enough to set the decorative lights on the cart trembling.

The cheers from the crowd roll in like a tide of burning emotion. Even from where you stand, far from the best seats, you can feel their passion. Evie stands at the edge of the curtain, her hands clutching the flow chart tightly. Yet, there's a smile on her face.

speaker: Evie
content: Not today! We managed to keep this surprise secret thanks to the manager's help. Even Mimi-meow doesn't know about it! I have to stay on standby here!

The fact that Mimi-meow has no idea casts a shadow over the question that had formed in your mind earlier, but you don't press further. You simply wait alongside Evie, who can't help swaying gently and singing along to the music, even from back here.
Before long, the moment to reveal the surprise comes.
Stage
The last note fades, and Mimi-meow is already posed for the next song. But the intro doesn't come. She waits half a beat before glancing at the sound booth, puzzled and still catching her breath.
Before the audience can register the pause and start murmuring, the manager strides out from the other side of the stage, microphone in hand.

speaker: Manager
content: Today is a very special day. Three hundred and sixty-five shows. That means, thanks to all your love and passion, we've been able to light up Mimi-meow's stage in this city three hundred and sixty-five times.

speaker: Manager
content: For such a grand occasion, it'd be a real shame to just go through the setlist like usual and call it a night, don't you think?
The crowd finally catches on, and the cheers build steadily, heating the atmosphere up little by little.

speaker: Fans
content: Yeah!!!

speaker: Manager
content: So, today, a group of people who <color=#fb9259>love</color> Mimi-meow more than anything have prepared a gift for her in secret. Mimi-meow, please look to the left side of the stage!
The crowd erupts, while Mimi-meow, caught off guard by the announcement, freezes. She grips the microphone so hard her fingers nearly go white, though she eases her hold not long after and smiles.

That smile is practiced, yet cold. Like a light that switches on the moment it's told to. Does she always smile like that? You glance over at Evie, only to find her so tense with anticipation that she doesn't seem to have noticed anything off at all.

speaker: Evie
content: I-it's my turn. Alright... I can do this!

Evie takes a deep breath. A flush of color surges up and washes away the pallor of her face. Her body sways as she pushes the cake cart forward, and you instinctively reach out to steady her. Only then do you realize she's already drawing on her power, despite her state.

speaker: Chief
content: Evie.

speaker: Evie
content: I'll... keep it under control, Chief. Please, lend me your strength... even a little is fine!

An orange light rises from her fingertips, tracing along the light strip at the base of the cake cart before spilling across the floor like stars in the night sky, spreading all the way to the center of the stage.
The light is bright but unstable. It trembles and flickers like Mania straining against its shackles. Even so, it makes Mimi-meow shine far more brilliantly than any stage light ever could.

speaker: Fan D
content: It's Evie!!! Look, she's been coughing all night, but her light is still so bright!!! Her <color=#fb9259>love</color> has <color=#fb9259>lit up</color> the whole venue!!!

speaker: Fan E
content: Incredible! She's doing this even when she's sick! You're a legend, a role model, and the gold standard for fans, Miss Mimi-meow! Let's show everyone our <color=#fb9259>love</color> for Mimi-meow!!!

speaker: Manager
content: Look! The light that's shining upon this gift right now isn't powered by electricity—it's powered by <color=#fb9259>love</color>. Mimi-meow, this is everyone's message to you: you have never shone alone on that stage!

The manager's melodramatic speech carries to every corner of the venue through the speakers. Glow sticks rise one after another in the crowd, swaying like a tide. Screams, applause, and Mimi-meow's name pile on top of each other until the stage itself seems to be floating above the clouds.

Evie pushes the cake cart forward along the trail of light, and you can see that her eyes have already gone red. She looks genuinely moved by the miracle she helped create, her footsteps light and unsteady, as if she might drift off the ground.

The harsh orange light cuts across at an angle, partially blocked by the towering decorations and fondant signs. What the audience sees is an idol surrounded by <color=#fb9259>love</color>, but what you see is her face, caught squarely in a sliver of shadow.
Is she really smiling?

speaker: Evie
content: M-Mimi-meow! Today is your 365th show, and your first anniversary as an idol... so we, cough, cough, we put together these little surprises to show you how grateful we are...
Evie finally manages to push the cake up to Mimi-meow. She picks up the microphone, coughing twice before forcing it back down. She doesn't want even a hint of noise to mar this perfect moment.

speaker: Evie
content: You've given me, and all of us, so much <color=#fb9259>love</color> and courage. You're the one who lit up our colorless lives and helped us find just a little more strength to carry on. So today... we want to be the ones to give you light.

speaker: Evie
content: Without you, I don't know if I'd still be here... cough, wait, no, I shouldn't be saying things like that on a day like this! Mimi-meow, all you need to know is that I'll keep supporting you, no matter what!

Her words begin to trail off into a jumble, her voice becoming choked. She laughs it off with an embarrassed smile and pulls herself together, then presents a knife with an orange ribbon tied to its handle.

speaker: Evie
content: Go on then, Mimi-meow! Make the first cut, and take all our <color=#fb9259>love</color> with it!

speaker: Mimi-meow
content: ...Aren't you going to cut it with me? You put so much thought into this, spent so much money, pushed yourself to use your power for the lights even when you're sick, gave it everything just to stand here... and you won't cut it with me?

speaker: Evie
content: Huh? Me? Of course not. You're the star of today, and you'll always be the star in my heart. Today, the spotlight belongs to you and you alone!

Mimi-meow watches her with heavy eyes, as if a thousand words are lodged in her throat. Beside her, the manager gives her a gentle smile and a nod. Below the stage, countless cameras are on them, all waiting for that perfect, emotional moment to close the night.
And it takes a long while before she finally raises her hand—but not to take the knife. Instead, she reaches for her own microphone.

speaker: Mimi-meow
content: Thank you, everyone. But... I'm sorry. I'm not feeling the best today...
She manages a smile, one that's anything but genuine.

speaker: Mimi-meow
content: We may need to pause the show for a moment... I'm sorry.

She steps back, avoiding the cake cart and the knife still hanging in the air, then turns and walks briskly off the other side of the stage. Meanwhile, Evie only stands there, arm still stretched out, knife in hand, with no idea what to do.

A wave of worried cries erupts from the audience. The manager's smile drops from his face as he turns and hurries after her. Evie remains frozen for a moment, her gaze sweeping past you in search of help. Ultimately, though, she wills herself to follow.

speaker: Chief
content: Evie, retract your power first!

You can feel the life force she had barely sustained through sheer emotion draining away, and fast. You curse under your breath as you push through the stage to chase after her, all while working to suppress her rapidly surging Mania.
Livehouse Backstage

By the time you reach her, Evie has already stopped outside the dressing room door. Yet, she doesn't go in. The ribbons she had carefully arranged just hours ago hang in the corridor, trampled into crumpled heaps by the people rushing back and forth.

Every word of the argument spilling out from the dressing room is sharp and piercing, puncturing the dream that had wrapped itself around the entire venue—a dream of idols, light, and <color=#fb9259>love</color>.

speaker: Manager
content: What was that just now? Why'd you walk out on all those fans, just like that?! You think that makes you cool or something?! Have you forgotten what your image is supposed to be? Is that how a bright, bubbly little sun is supposed to act?!

speaker: Manager
content: Those ATMs are easy to milk, but they're not stupid! Do you really think they'll spend even a cent on you if you keep putting on an attitude and disregarding their devotion?! What, do you think you're some superstar?! Without those people out there, you're **** doomed!

speaker: Mimi-meow
content: Sure, I'm not a superstar, but we're business partners! What gives you the right to do all that and hide everything from me?! I never asked for any of this, and I definitely never asked for this shameless promotional scheme!

speaker: Mimi-meow
content: Crowdfunding regardless of their financial situation, demanding volunteer work regardless of their health... Is it fun to exploit my fans like that? Aren't you the least bit afraid of word getting out?! You're basically handing antis what they need on a silver platter!

Mimi-meow's tone is blunt, carrying a firmness completely unlike her approachable persona as an idol. Her every word is laced with biting sarcasm, leaving the manager speechless for a moment. So, he begins to shift tactics, his tone softening as he speaks.

speaker: Manager
content: ...You're right, there are risks, but the returns are just as clear! We don't have an unlimited budget, so I had no other choice. We want to make your little dream come true too... what was it again... right, to bring love and hope to more people!

speaker: Manager
content: The flower walls, the ribbons, the whole venue... Someone else took care of all of it. Isn't that great? And the thing is, they loved every second of it! Just look at Evie! She's coughing her lungs out and was still smiling as she handed you that knife. This is exactly what the people want to see!

speaker: Manager
content: Look, I've got a heart too. Truth be told, the reason I agreed this time was because I was genuinely touched when they proposed doing something special, Mimi-meow. Why on earth would you turn away this <color=#fb9259>love</color> that's being handed right to you?

Throughout this exchange, soaked in cold calculation, Evie has kept her head down and endured. And yet, the manager's sugar-coated words are enough to make her look up again. She's waiting for a word of approval from Mimi-meow, her eyes gleaming with hope.

speaker: Mimi-meow
content: <color=#fb9259>Love</color>? You call blindly sacrificing all that someone has, without thinking about whether they can actually handle it, "love"? That's nothing but <color=#fb9259>self-gratification</color>!
But the voice from inside the dressing room only shatters the last bit of illusion she has left. Mimi-meow's cold words land like arrows, pinning her to the spot.

speaker: Mimi-meow
content: If this is what <color=#fb9259>love</color> looks like, then I don't want it, nor can I afford it. Don't do anything like this again. You're only putting me in a difficult position.
Days of preparation, a surprise arranged under enormous strain—all of it, in this very moment, has been reduced to a joke in front of a product manufactured by money.
...Has your worst fear come true? Is this just another idol who sees her fans as nothing but a meal ticket? Your heart sinks as you turn to look at Evie.

Her reaction, however, is smaller than you expected. She simply lowers her head again, slowly, eyes falling to the cake knife still in her hand. It's as if she's only now realizing that what the delicate little thing has faced was never a rejection. It was never taken at all.

The emotions on the other end of the shackles drain away all at once, leaving behind nothing but a hollow, plummeting coldness. The excitement and anticipation that had kept her shining on that stage moments ago are being ground to dust by a simple statement: "Don't do anything like this again. You're only putting me in a difficult position."

You reach out, hoping to pull her out of the spiral of negativity for even a moment, only to realize she's still forcing a smile. She looks up at you, lips parting, as if she's trying to tell you she's fine.
But before she can voice a single syllable, her frail body sways once, twice, like a marionette whose strings have been cut, and she crumples to the ground, her face drained of all color.

speaker: Chief
content: Evie!
You barely manage to catch her. The fabric of her suit, soaked in cold sweat, clings to your palms, clammy and uncomfortable. It makes the summer heat outside feel like a lie.

There's no time to blame anyone. You curse yourself for having underestimated just how much discomfort Evie was willing to hide and endure for the sake of supporting Mimi-meow. You yank out your terminal and make an emergency call to the Bureau's medical team.

speaker: Manager
content: What is going on?! Why is she here? And you—

The commotion outside has cut the argument short, and Mimi-meow comes rushing along with the manager. The manager recognizes Evie, who's collapsed in your arms, and for a moment, his anger falters, only to give way to annoyance.

speaker: Manager
content: Don't tell me Mimi-meow actually called it? We've barely made any returns, and now she's messing everything up... Tch, the crowd's still out there. Do not let them know!

speaker: Choice
options: Oh, you don't need to worry about that.

content: Mimi-meow stands behind him, her makeup still immaculate. It's a mask for her to conceal every flicker of emotion, yet right now, it fails to hide the faint redness rimming her eyes. For a moment, it seemed like she wanted to take a step forward. But she stops herself in the end.

speaker: Chief
content: The Bureau's ambulance is on its way. I'd suggest ending the show and clearing out non-essential personnel to avoid any unnecessary complications, but... I'll leave that for you to decide.

speaker: Chief
content: I hope you find yourselves a new ATM. One that wouldn't collapse as easily.

Your jab lands on the manager, but Mimi-meow doesn't react to it at all. It's the mention of the ambulance that cracks her mask open. She looks at Evie. Then, the flicker of hesitation in her eyes quickly turns into something resolute.

Something stirs in you. Is this the kind of expression, the kind of reaction, you'd expect from a self-serving idol who drains everything from those around her? What was she hesitating over, and what did she steel herself for?
Could what lies behind that hesitation... be a turning point?

speaker: Staff A
content: Miss Evie, are you heading to the front desk of the recovery ward? In that case, could you bring this little package over for me? I've got something urgent to deal with...

speaker: Staff B
content: Oh, Miss Evie, when you go get water, could you bring some for the little girl in the next room too? She never drinks enough water! I've told her a million times but it never gets through!

speaker: Evie
content: Okay... Sure... Of course...

speaker: Choice
options: Wait and see how things unfold
See how many unrelated things she comes back with

content: You trail behind Evie, watching as she picks up documents, a lunch tray, and packages along the way. The glass of water she originally went out to fetch, on the other hand, never once makes it into her hands.

No matter how many people stop her, she responds to each one with the same compliance, taking on everything as though she can't feel strain. Even as her arms grow sore, she trudges on, step by shuffling step.
She's like a dried-out tumbleweed. She always seems to be on her way somewhere, yet has no real sense of where that somewhere is. She's simply rolling whichever way each person nudges her.

speaker: Nurse
content: Evie! Not again! Can you stop being such a pushover? That's exactly why you're taking so long to recover. Someone calls, and you just go along with whatever they say! Do you even care about your own body?

speaker: Evie
content: Sorry...

speaker: Nurse
content: I've heard that a million times too. Has anything I've said gotten through to you at all?! Chief, you talk some sense into her too! At this rate, she's never going to be discharged!

It makes sense that nothing's getting through. Evie may not have closed off her heart, but it's hollow all the same. She's lost the only pillar she always leaned on, and that's likely the main reason she's recovering so slowly.
In reality, though, you already know where to find the cure.
Inside the vehicle

speaker: Evie
content: ...Is this the little surprise... that you said will help with my recovery?

The car turns the corner and pulls up in front of a worn-down livehouse. Evie, who had let herself be dragged into the car like a sleepwalker without a word of protest, widens her eyes ever so slightly the moment she sees it.

speaker: Chief
content: That's right. A friend of yours and I spent a good while putting this together. I hope it'll help with your recovery... and more than anything, I hope you like it.

speaker: Evie
content: A friend? But I don't really have any friends...
Black Screen

speaker: Evie
content: Wait?! Wh-what is this...?!
Inside the livehouse

You push open the back door. The hinges let out a soft creak. Lights come on one by one, but what they reveal is no dusty relic of the past. The moment the freshly decorated backstage comes into view, whatever words Evie had on her lips die in her throat.

The old walls are covered in panels of deep black and blue, with strings of small orange lights and cat-ear stickers tucked into the corners. It's clear that whoever designed this meant for Evie to be the center of this stage, and Mimi-meow is simply the decoration around her.

It has all the makings of a carefully planned exhibition. Draped display boards stand paired with boxes in front of them, each one a puzzle waiting to be opened alongside its answer. Evie is stunned, unsure what to say as her gaze sweeps across it all. Then, she looks back at you, as if to seek your help.

speaker: Choice
options: Gesture for her to explore on her own

speaker: Evie
content: Can I really... touch any of this? That box is so big and tall... there's got to be a cake or a sculpture inside... What if I break something...
She hesitantly lifts the lid, only to find that it really is a cake inside. It looks identical to the one she never got to give away. The only difference is the writing on top: For our dear Evie.

speaker: Evie
content: This is... for me? But... why would...

speaker: Chief
content: Who knows? Maybe someone saw the feelings you never got to express, and wanted to give something back.

speaker: Evie
content: But I've ordered one before... I know how expensive this is! Who would ever want to get this for me...?

speaker: Chief
content: That just means they think you're worth it. Now then, why don't you cut into it and have a taste? After all, you never got to eat the last one, no?

Sure enough, there's a cake knife inside the box. Last time, amidst those blazing lights and the expectant eyes of a crowd, Evie had pushed it toward her idol. This time, however, Evie is the one who needs to decide whether to pick it up.

speaker: Evie
content: I didn't know... that cutting a cake like this is so difficult... Of course, I'm well aware of how expensive and special it was, but I never once thought about how hard it'd be to cut into, how hard it'd be to hold...

She struggles with every cut, her hands still too weak to apply much force. Then, as she finally works through the thick layer of frosting, she accidentally pulls the draping cloth off the display board beside her.

speaker: Evie
content: Are these... photos of me?

On the board are several photos, all captured from behind the scenes. One depicts Evie leaning over to adjust the lights, another depicts her solemnly flipping through the runsheet. There's also one that shows Evie looking back with a smile as she wheels out the cake, as if cradling the entire sea of orange lights in her arms.
And beside them is decorative lettering that appears to be a personal reflection—

<color=#675E8F>"I didn't understand it back then. Is this really necessary? And how is this worth it? But even when effort is pointed in the wrong direction, the sincerity behind it still warrants gratitude. So no matter how things turned out, I will always remember it, and honor it."</color>

speaker: Evie
content: So... you kept a record of all this too. Thank you, Chief. I really... don't know what to say.

speaker: Chief
content: This is only the first one, Evie. It's a little too early for thanks. Now then, keep going.

She sets down the cake and moves toward the other display boards. This time, her steps are much quicker, much more certain than before. You walk alongside her as the photos on the boards take you back to the past, from that 365th show, all the way to even earlier days:

One Evie hand-drew signs to patch up the organizer's mistakes and was mistaken for staff. One Evie knitted wool stockings by hand for cheering on Christmas Eve. One Evie is holding a flashlight to light the way during a blackout, from before her powers awakened...

Every little thing she herself had forgotten—brushed off as "no big deal," "nothing worth mentioning"—had been carefully cleaned, arranged, and dated by someone else. Under the warm orange glow, they now lead her deeper into her own memories.

speaker: Evie
content: <color=#675E8F>"Nobody knew you could draw until that day. Just how many surprises are you hiding?" "The colors might be off, but this has to be the best stocking anyone could ever receive as a gift." "Your lighting work was actually better back then."</color>...

Through the back door, down the corridor, past the wings, across the stage, and into the audience seats. Evie walks through the live house from the back to the front, not wanting to miss a single display board, losing her breath more than once along the way.

Finally, she stops before the last box and display board, set up right at the main entrance of the venue. She turns to look at you with tears in her eyes, the doubt and confusion that once tainted her voice now gone.

speaker: Evie
content: ...You weren't the one who actually prepared these, were you, Chief?

speaker: Evie
content: There's so much here that you... or even the others in Mimi-meow's fandom... couldn't possibly know about... I didn't even know anyone still remembered any of this...
You only smile. Evie doesn't press for your confirmation either, and simply turns around to open the box behind her.

Sure enough, inside is a blurry photo taken from the stage. In it, Evie is plainly dressed and in an absolute mess of tears. Meanwhile, Mimi-meow is beside her with an expression that is equal parts awkward and inexperienced. This is from that very first live show. Their first meeting.

speaker: Evie
content: <color=#675E8F>"You always tell everyone you'll never forget how radiant I was at that show. But if anything, I'm the one who'll never forget—it was the look on your face that convinced me so."</color>

Evie reads the words on the display board, choking and sobbing all the while. As for who prepared all this, the answer is clear as day to her now—it's Mimi-meow. It's her who set all this up, who cropped every photo to put Evie at the center.

Light, it turns out, was never a one-sided thing. She had always believed she was simply lucky enough to be illuminated by that sun, never knowing that her every response was what fueled that brilliance.

speaker: Evie
content: Mimi-meow... it was you, wasn't it? You actually remembered all these little things...

speaker: Evie
content: There must have been a reason you said those things back then! I won't misunderstand you again, so... please come out!
Evie wipes her tears with the back of her hand, her gaze sweeping the room without direction. Her voice grows urgent, still a little nasal from crying, and barely able to contain her anticipation.
It echoes through the empty live house for a moment, yet no one answers. You watch as Evie stands there, a little lost, and step forward to give her one last hint.

speaker: Chief
content: Hold on, take a look outside the door. Maybe Mimi-meow hasn't shown up yet... because you haven't finished the route?
Outdoor Clearing

speaker: Evie
content: There's... one last box? But... the debut live is as far back as I can remember... Don't tell me... D-did I forget something Mimi-meow considers important...?! I-I'm a failure as a fan!

She pushes open the door to find a path decorated with paper blossoms, gold and silver ribbons, and hand-drawn stickers. At the far end, atop a makeshift stage, sits the last box. Evie approaches it, confused and nervous. Yet, inside is nothing but an old flyer.
The flyer is yellowed and poorly printed. On it is a Mimi-meow with a very forced smile, her poses exaggerated. She looks brand new and unpolished, like something fresh out of the packaging.

speaker: Evie
content: This... I had one of these too. I kept it tucked in my files, but when I got a new bag... I lost it. I felt awful about it for a while. But... what does this mean?

She thinks for a long while, but the answer still eludes her. Figures. You lightly shake your head, press the button hidden behind your back, and the lights around blaze to life at once. This was the signal you arranged with your special guest.

In the next instant, the gold and silver ribbons catch the light and shatter into countless glittering sparks, as the idol whose name has been called so many times makes her grand entrance from the far end of the path.

The moment she sees Mimi-meow, Evie drops her gaze, almost unable to look directly at her. She becomes rooted to the spot, too overcome to take a single step forward. She only manages to wave her hands frantically, stumbling over her words as she tries to express just how moved she is.

speaker: Evie
content: I'm sorry, I never should have doubted you. I always knew you were the best idol in the world... Thank you for all of this. I'll never question whether you truly care about your fans again. No matter what happens from here, I'll support you for the rest of my——

The crisp click of heels cuts her off and makes her look up. Her idol had been standing at the far end of that light just a moment ago, looking exactly as she did the first time Evie ever saw her, when she lit up Evie's world.

But now, she walks toward her, draped in light and crowned in stars. It's as if she's stepping out from that old flyer, those display boards, those treasured memories... She closes the distance between them one step at a time, until they've finally come face-to-face. She opens her mouth with a smile.

speaker: Mimi-meow
content: I'm the one who should be thanking you, Evie. Thank you for being willing to give me another chance, even after hearing those hurtful words. Thank you for making it all the way here.
Mimi-meow reaches out and takes Evie's restless hands. She pauses, then shakes her head.

speaker: Mimi-meow
content: But... I'm sorry. I can't accept those compliments. Because today, I'm not standing here as an idol.

speaker: Evie
content: ...Not as an idol? What does that mean? It's just like last time, when you said you "don't need our love"... I know you probably meant no harm, and maybe you were just looking out for me, but... it just confuses me even more.

speaker: Evie
content: Did I do something wrong... as a fan? Or have you given up on the idol industry, and you don't want to be an <color=#fb9259>idol</color> anymore? Is it that you don't want to be my <color=#fb9259>light</color> anymore?!

speaker: Mimi-meow
content: No, of course not, Evie. Please, calm down. I've always felt genuinely proud that my work can bring happiness to people. Because even if that happiness is fleeting, even if it's not entirely real, I know you care. Someone cares.

Mimi-meow takes Evie's hand, gentle and reassuring, then turns to lead her toward the path stretching behind them. The display boards and old objects they passed along the way rest quietly, like a still and luminous river.

speaker: Mimi-meow
content: Seeing the darker side of the idol industry won't make me deny the hope it's given you. The reason I stepped onto that stage in the first place was to offer a little warmth and light for people like you.

speaker: Evie
content: Then why... why did you turn me down like that? You saved me, so I wanted to repay the favor, to help more people see you... That's how I show love. That's how any fan shows love.
Evie's voice is trembling, barely above a whisper. The pain of being wholly dismissed rises in her again, and still she has no answer.

speaker: Evie
content: Is there something I could've done better? Something you didn't like? But you remembered everything I did, you kept all of it... Isn't this whole path proof of that? So why do you make it sound like none of it was enough?

speaker: Mimi-meow
content: It's not that there's something I don't like, Evie. I just can't accept you hurting yourself for my sake.

speaker: Mimi-meow
content: Yes, it's natural to want to do something for someone you care about. And I've always treasured everything you've done for me. But if the price of that <color=#fb9259>love</color> means you need to cough until you can barely stand, to smile and say you're fine when you're completely exhausted...

speaker: Mimi-meow
content: Then I don't want <color=#fb9259>it</color>, nor can I afford it.
Evie looks down at her hand, held in Mimi-meow's. That same hand that has done so much for others now sits there, uncertain what to do with itself, simply because someone is holding it with care.

speaker: Evie
content: But... I really don't know what else I can do. If I'm not out there doing something for you, what right do I have to be <color=#fb9259>illuminated</color> by you?
This time, she doesn't say sorry. The genuine confusion she has always kept tucked behind those "I'm fine" and "I can do it" finally finds its voice here.

speaker: Mimi-meow
content: The fledgling underground idol back then was no different from any other girl in Eastside with her head in the clouds. If we're talking about "rights," what right did she have to be chosen by you, to be saved by you?

speaker: Evie
content: What... do you mean...?
Seeing that Evie hasn't understood at all, Mimi-meow can't help but chuckle. She takes a step back and lifts the cloth covering the last display board with her free hand.
On it is a photograph of the Eastside nightscape, entirely unremarkable.
Eastside Nightscape, Flashback

speaker: Mimi-meow
content: Hello there! I'm an underground idol making my debut tonight. My name is Mimi-meow. The show is free, would you like to come and give it a listen?

Showtime draws closer and closer, yet the unknown underground idol is still out on the street with a promotional flag strapped to her back, handing out flyers. If the audience count doesn't meet the minimum her agency set, it's back to the gutter for her.

speaker: Mimi-meow
content: Hello! Long day at work? How about a song to lift your spirits? I'll give it everything I've got out there, so come on down to my free debut show!
Sorry, but I'm in a rush to get home...
No luck again. The weary office workers shuffling past are always equal parts hollow and hurried, so the fact that this girl even bothered to respond is, if anything, a courtesy.

Mimi-meow has already given up. She carefully presses the back of her hand to the corner of her eye, not wanting to smudge her makeup, then puts on a smile again and turns to face the next disappointment. Yet, the office worker before her catches the glimmer at the edge of her eye, and suddenly comes to a stop.

speaker: Evie
content: Wait, hold on. Is that you on this flyer? You're so cute! Can I have one...? You said the show is free, right? Do I just need to bring the flyer to get in?

speaker: Mimi-meow
content: ...! Yes! The flyer is your ticket! A-and you'll get a custom orange glow stick too! You'll really feel like part of the show, so please, do come watch!

speaker: Evie
content: Oh, but the venue looks a little hard to find, and I'm not sure where it is exactly... The show's starting pretty soon, right? I can wait here while you finish handing out flyers. Could you walk me there?

speaker: Mimi-meow
content: Of course! I'll lead the way!

Their exchange draws the attention of a few passersby. Some of them had been eyeing the address on the promotional flag with skepticism. After hearing the back-and-forth, they hesitantly step up, forming a short little tail of a line.

speaker: Passerby A
content: It's not too far off anyway. Might as well check it out if someone's leading the way.

speaker: Passerby B
content: Huh? Why's there a line over there? Maybe I'll go take a look.

speaker: Mimi-meow
content: Hello! Hello! Yes, it's my debut show tonight! I'm Mimi-meow, an <color=#fb9259>underground idol</color> who's here to bring everyone <color=#fb9259>love</color>, hope, and the scent of oranges! Care to come take a listen?
Outdoor Clearing

speaker: Mimi-meow
content: If it weren't for you, I never could have filled the quota my agency set. I wouldn't be standing here today. And yet, whenever you tell the story of how we met, you always leave that part out.

speaker: Mimi-meow
content: It was never me who started it all. It was you. Before I ever <color=#fb9259>"saved"</color> you, before I ever <color=#fb9259>"illuminated"</color> you, you had already saved me. You're the one who changed my fate, Miss Softhearted.

speaker: Mimi-meow
content: So you see, Evie, you don't need to push yourself to your limits or endure the pain to do something worthwhile. You already managed to <color=#fb9259>illuminate</color> me that night, just like the neon lights of Eastside.
Evie's face goes blank. She murmurs.

speaker: Evie
content: I completely forgot that even happened... It really was just a coincidence... M-Mimi-meow, did you cry back then? I don't remember anymore...

speaker: Mimi-meow
content: That's okay. Because it only proves that simply following your heart and doing what you truly want to do is enough to obtain <color=#fb9259>love</color>. You've proven it yourself, no?
Mimi-meow steps aside and guides Evie to the center of the stage. She watches Evie, bathed in light, with satisfaction. The tears she had held back behind her glittery stage makeup finally fall.

speaker: Mimi-meow
content: And that's exactly why I don't want the agency to deceive you, exploit you, use you for your commercial value, or make you hurt yourself in the process.

speaker: Mimi-meow
content: That's why I told Chief I wanted to give you an exhibition with you as the star, a stage where you stand at the center.

speaker: Mimi-meow
content: I wanted you to know that a fan doesn't need to use herself as <color=#fb9259>kindling</color> to <color=#fb9259>illuminate</color> an idol. From the very beginning, it should have been two lights reflecting off each other. The light you gave me was never supposed to come at the cost of extinguishing your own.

Evie's eyes begin to tear up. Not because she feels wounded from being scolded, nor is it because of some delirious joy from being praised by her idol. Those tears come from something that has long taken root deep inside her, a seedling that has finally found sunlight and rain, now breaking through the clouds in her chest.

speaker: Evie
content: C-can I... really still be <color=#fb9259>loved</color>, even without doing all those things? Can I really obtain <color=#fb9259>love</color> for myself... without putting in so much more effort than everyone else?
Mimi-meow lifts their still-joined hands, gestures down the path she walked in from, then up toward the lights above. She asks, beaming—

speaker: Mimi-meow
content: Evie, am I brilliant?
Evie says nothing, and simply nods.

speaker: Mimi-meow
content: You were the one who gave this path and light to me. So, if you think it's brilliant...
She pauses, her voice dropping, somewhere between a plea and a prayer.

speaker: Mimi-meow
content: Then please, love the you who gave me that light. Love the you that I love.

Evie is too moved to speak, but her hand reaches out without a moment's hesitation to wipe the tears from the corner of Mimi-meow's eyes. She keeps wiping until the redness fades and the tears stop falling. Only then does she turn to brush her own face dry.

speaker: Evie
content: Thank you, Mimi-meow, thank you for doing so much for me... I'll try! I-I don't know if I can manage it right away, but I'll try...
Watching the scene before you, you finally can't help but break into a warm round of applause.

speaker: Evie
content: Ch-Chief...! Th-thank you too... Mimi-meow couldn't have arranged all of this on her own, right...? Otherwise, she would have done it long ago...

speaker: Evie
content: I've caused you so much trouble already, and you still came with me to the concert, helped me keep my Mania in check, and on top of all that, you went out of your way to do all this for me... I-I really don't know how I could ever repay you...

speaker: Choice
options: I thought we're past the whole repaying thing now?

speaker: Chief
content: Well, Mimi-meow and I didn't plan all of this to tell you that caring for others and giving of yourself is wrong, anyway. We just want you to value yourself more, and to recognize your own worth.

speaker: Chief
content: And I hope you'll stop draining yourself. Don't push your special power past its limits for the kind of love that comes wrapped in pretty words and a price tag anymore. Don't destabilize your M-value for such things.

speaker: Chief
content: As for the agency inducing a Sinner to participate in commercial promotions and using powers in violation of regulations, you can leave them to the Bureau. That is not a responsibility you need to shoulder on anyone else's behalf.

speaker: Evie
content: I'll keep that in mind...
Evie, convinced she's been nothing but a burden, flushes red and nods. She stumbles over her words, caught somewhere between an apology and a thank-you. You stop her before she can get either out.

speaker: Chief
content: Don't give us too much credit. There's a saying among Eastia's Sinners—let he who tied the bell on the tiger take it off. If you hadn't already laid the groundwork, Mimi-meow and I would have had nothing to build on. You were always the one who saved yourself.

speaker: Mimi-meow
content: ${PlayerName} is right, Evie. I don't want you putting yourself below me all the time, always thinking about how to repay me. All you really need to do is come to my shows as a fan, and just enjoy them.

speaker: Evie
content: ...Okay!
Mimi-meow lets out a sigh of relief at the rare certainty in that answer. Finally, a familiar smile breaks through. That expression is bright and warm, one that belongs to an idol.

speaker: Mimi-meow
content: That's wonderful! Now that Evie's trip down memory lane has come to a perfect close, it's time for the encore! Just sit back and enjoy this last song. I'm dedicating it to you!
Evie goes red from her face all the way down to her neck, both surprised and delighted. You smile, pull out a speaker, and start the music. Apparently, it's a cover Mimi-meow sang at her debut show.

As the melody begins, Evie tries to step off the stage, but Mimi-meow catches her hand and refuses to let go. So, she stays. At first she's stiff as a rock, but by the time the chorus rolls around, that awkwardness has all but dissipated, and she's clapping along and singing under her breath.

Just then, the lights above the stage flicker twice. The makeshift wiring pulled from the near-derelict building has finally been pushed past its limit. A couple of the old fixtures crackle, and then go dark.

speaker: Evie
content: Oh, the lights...!
Half of Mimi-meow's figure is swallowed by the darkness. Almost by instinct, Evie's Mania stirs, and a familiar flicker of orange light rises to her fingertips.
You don't rush to activate your shackles. You simply watch as she closes her own hand first, letting that small light flicker softly in her palm, then fade.

speaker: Evie
content: No, wait... I made a promise to Mimi-meow and Chief. I need to think of another way...

She turns and unclips a string of decorative lights from the edge of the flower path. Since they were powered by batteries, they still work fine, though the plastic casing is rough to the touch and the light they give off is faint. Even with several strung together, they couldn't hope to light a whole stage.

But that's alright. She wraps the lights around her and Mimi-meow's joined hands, then lifts them up to Mimi-meow's face. The warm glow catches the little idol's smile, still as bright and lovely as ever.
It's the first time she's learned to answer Mimi-meow with her own light, however small. And there, in the dim glow, you feel that Mimi-meow is smiling too.
Chief's Office.
A few days later, on an ordinary weekday lunch break, your terminal lights up with a string of notifications. You open it to find a few messages from Evie.

<color=#7683a2>Evie</color>: Sorry to bother you, Chief. The results from my last check-up at the Bureau came back, and I've been cleared to return to normal life.

<color=#7683a2>Evie</color>: You might already know this, but I wanted to personally let you know anyway, since you've done so much for me.

<color=#fb9259>${PlayerName}</color>: That's great to hear. But... no staying up late, no excessive caffeine, no standing for too long... That's quite a few restrictions. Will you really be able to stick to all these?

<color=#7683a2>Evie</color>: Mimi-meow said she'll be keeping an eye on me, and the punishment for going back on my word is terrifying, so... Definitely! [Scared face emoji]

<color=#fb9259>${PlayerName}</color>: Please elaborate.

<color=#7683a2>Evie</color>: [image]

<color=#7683a2>Evie</color>: We spotted this pair of little figurines at a boutique in Eastside the other day, and the color scheme looked just like me and Mimi-meow!

<color=#7683a2>Evie</color>: She bought the orange-yellow one for me, and I bought the blue-black one for her. She said if I can't keep it together, she'll take my Mimi-meow away.

<color=#7683a2>Evie</color>: I can't afford to lose custody, so...

<color=#fb9259>${PlayerName}</color>: Sounds like it's very effective. This plan has my full support.

speaker: Chief
content: Neither of them insisted on paying for both. A good sign, if I may say so myself.
You close the chat with a smile, and as you do, your eyes catch Evie's profile status. It reads: "I'm free!!!!"

speaker: Ariel
content: W-what is this place?
The girl's voice trembles a little as she tries to contain her unease.
This is the interrogation room, where you will be interrogated for your crimes.

speaker: Ariel
content: Ah...
