content: Hahahahah, do you still not want to admit what you've done?
The three who were talking to you suddenly turn into Wendy wielding a chainsaw, letting out shrill laughter.

speaker: Wendy
content: Do you believe that the Sinners should thank you? That everyone who died in my memories should thank you? Hahahahah!
When did you get here...?

speaker: Pacassi
content: There's nothing you can do... Tragedy has already struck.
The people in front of you are making instantaneous changes. This is not normal at all! You start to feel a dizzying headache.

speaker: Ignis
content: You're just curious about what we're hiding. Don't make it so glorious.

speaker: Demon
content: You want to pry into our suffering.
That's not true.

speaker: Ninety-Nine
content: Are you proud to see us being tortured by your shackles?
I never had such intention.
You try to calm yourself down, but your brain is a mess.

speaker: Anne
content: Actually, I had no choice but to cooperate with the interrogation...

speaker: Wolverine
content: Obnoxious bastard, stop being a hypocrite.

speaker: Chelsea
content: A friend? I cannot afford a friend like you.
The Sinners' constant criticism is a nightmare.
Wait, a nightmare...?
You seem to have figured out what's going on.
(Clank)
You hear the familiar clanking sound of metal again.

speaker: Chameleon
content: Hmm, you woke up a little later than expected.
Chameleon is still sitting in the interrogation room, playing with the pocket watch in her hand.

options: When did you start hypnotizing me?
Why did you show me that?

speaker: Chameleon
content: Heheh, ever since Nightingale interrupted the interrogation. It was all mirage.
Was it to avoid the interrogation?
If you don't want to answer case-related questions, you can remain silent. But it is unethical to hypnotize others without their consent.

speaker: Chameleon
content: Aha, relax. I just wanted to see how confident you are towards interrogations and mental connections.
There's no point in doing this. It is my duty and obligation to interrogate Sinners about their past and sort out their crimes.

speaker: Chameleon
content: Hahahahah, if you were that determined, how come I was able to hypnotize you?
You...
You are unable to retort. The pain of being rejected, questioned, and alienated by the Sinners under hypnosis still haunts you.

speaker: Chameleon
content: Actually, apart from prying into others' pain, we share one more crime, that is, exploiting others' trust.

speaker: Chameleon
content: You build trust with Sinners to extract information. Similarly, hypnosis requires gaining the patient's trust.
I've never believed a single word you said.

speaker: Chameleon
content: That's not important... Isn't absolute suspicion just another kind of trust?
She does not seem to plan on explaining her words, only looking at you condescendingly.
This arrogance once again makes you realize the "danger" that Nightingale warned.
It looks like coercive measures are necessary.
A dark red glow covers and wraps around Chameleon. She shows no signs of resistance and does not even take a glance down at the changes.
After controlling your ability, I have many ways to make you talk. Are you not afraid?

speaker: Chameleon
content: And are you not afraid of me, Chief? Someone who has been hypnotized once will surely have a second and a third time...
I'm not going to let you get away with it again.

speaker: Chameleon
content: Hold that back for now, Chief. Hypnosis can be a useful psychotherapeutic tool, especially when you want to forget or remember something...

speaker: Chief
content: I don't need it.

speaker: Chameleon
content:
Heheh, who knows?
If there's something you feel you've forgotten, feel free to come to me for advice.

options: Call Nightingale and end the interrogation

content: Nightingale, put Chameleon into solitary confinement, confiscate her pocket watch, and have guards watching her on regular shifts.
Until she confesses the motive for her crimes, do not let anyone get near her!

speaker: Chameleon
content: Looks like you don't want to pay attention to me anymore... Are you mad because you're so ashamed?

speaker: Chameleon
content: Relax, we're the same. We've both been in pain and brought pain to others.
She leans in close to your ear.

speaker: Chameleon
content: But in these chaotic times, pain... may not be a bad thing.
Your unease does not subside until Chameleon is taken away by the guards.
Is her lack of honesty in the interrogation room just a means to avoid confessing the truth?
"Pain may not be a bad thing." Perhaps this is the only true thing she said today.

Clock cabinet, sculpture, flames, hostages...
You feel the blood seeping, a girl sobbing, the life-threatening danger lingering in the flames and slowly approaching you...
Whose dream is this again?

The details of the dream seem so vague. You cannot help but think of what Chameleon said in the interrogation room,
"If there's something you feel you've forgotten, feel free to come to me for advice..."
When you wake up, your intuition tells you to go seek clarification from Chameleon.

speaker: Chameleon
content: I knew you would come.
Chameleon leisurely puts on her <color=#e45515>glasses</color>. She seems to be unaffected even after being in confinement for so long.

options: What have you done to me?
How did you know I would be coming here?

speaker: Chameleon
content: It wasn't me, but you yourself.
She puts away her smile and reveals a look of deep grief that you've never seen before.

speaker: Chameleon
content: Your shackles have created some kind of connection between us.

speaker: Chameleon
content: I sensed that you entered my dream.

speaker: Chameleon
content: Because I saw you entering my dream.
She puts away her smile and reveals a look of deep grief that you've never seen before.

speaker: Chameleon
content: It must have been your shackles that established some kind of connection between us.
She does not look like she was lying. Did you really see Chameleon's past? Does it have anything to do with her crime?
However, your residual memories of that dream are so vague that you only remember fragments. The clock cabinet, the sculpture, and the flames—they are not enough to recreate what she went through.
You already predicted that I would forget some things since the last interrogation. Was it really not intentionally planned by you?

speaker: Chameleon
content: I admit that I like to make jokes at you sometimes.

speaker: Chameleon
content: But are you not curious about how I awakened to be a Sinner? Would you not like to know the connection?
I remember seeing a clock cabinet in the dream. Did that belong to you?

speaker: Chameleon
content: That was one of my father's vintage clocks. The clock pendulum would make a dull ringing sound...
She softly pushes her <color=#e45515>glasses</color>, sounding a bit nostalgic.

speaker: Chameleon
content: My parents were both psychologists, but they didn't want me to pursue their profession.

speaker: Chameleon
content: When I was young, I hid in the clock cabinet and peeked through the cracks to see how they would consult their patients.

speaker: Chameleon
content: And do you remember the sculpture on the desk in the dream?
It's an exquisite stone statue of about thirty centimeters in height.

speaker: Chameleon
content: Hypnos, the god of dreams, could make people fall into slumber and sweet dreams.

speaker: Chameleon
content: Dignified, holy, immaculate... My parents had extremely high demands on their profession, and all treatments were conducted under the supervision of the god of dreams.
Chameleon's description of the clock cabinet and the sculpture is somehow different from what you saw in your dream...
As if to give an answer to your unease, she shows a bitter smile.

speaker: Chameleon
content: Unfortunately, some patients did not trust that their psychiatrists would keep their unpleasant secrets.

speaker: Chameleon
content: Everything I just talked about was destroyed in fire.

speaker: Chameleon
content: The white marble sculpture was stained with blood after being smashed to the back of their heads. The clock cabinet cut me off from my parents, the murderer, and the sea of fire. We fell into two different worlds.
When the blurred memories are pieced together with Chameleon's guidance, a new picture flashes through your mind.
A thin man tied to a chair is in what seems to be an abandoned depot.
Is there nothing else apart from this experience in your dreams?

speaker: Chameleon
content: I will awaken when the flames begin to dance... Do you still not believe me, Chief?
She does not seem to know about that man.
I saw something different in your dream.

speaker: Chameleon
content: Is that so? I would wake up after the big fire, so I can't remember anything after that...
There seems to be a "hostage" tied up in a remote location...

speaker: Chameleon
content: A remote location... What exactly is that referring to?
There seems to be some unusual excitement in her tone.
I don't remember... Could this be important to you?

speaker: Chameleon
content: Of course it is. It wasn't easy to help you recall your memories...
It's nothing. I was just a little lost in thought.

speaker: Chameleon
content: Really?

speaker: Chameleon
content: I thought you finally remembered something about the "hostage."

speaker: Chameleon
content: That's weird... I was so "sincere" in helping you restore your memories. Has it not taken effect yet?
What do you mean?
She just faintly smiles and pushes her <color=#e45515>glasses</color>. The reflection of her lens is extremely blinding for some reason and you feel dizzy.

speaker: Chameleon
content: You were also curious, right? Who was that man? Where was he tied up? Why is he appearing in your memories?

speaker: Chameleon
content: Trust me. Just do as I say... and I'll help you remember it...
Your eyelids become uncontrollably heavy, and Chameleon's face starts to get blurry.

speaker: Chameleon
content: Don't worry. Do as you're told. Get some sleep and you'll remember everything.
A flash of white light passes and you find yourself in an unfamiliar environment.

speaker: Chameleon
content: Welcome to your subconscious world, Chief.
My subconscious? Weren't we talking about your dreams?

speaker: Chameleon
content: Take it easy. It's too early to reveal the answer.

You look around but do not see Chameleon.
The hypnotist's bewildering voice only exists inside your mind and you no longer hear any traces of the sadness and nostalgia from earlier.
You've been acting all this time just for this moment when you can hypnotize me.

speaker: Chameleon
content: Shh, I'm busy with something right now and am not in the mood to bicker with you.
As soon as Chameleon says that, a woman with a cane steps out of the darkness.
You shouldn't have abused your authority to come here even if you're the chief of the MBCC.
Who is she?

speaker: Chameleon
content: The person who will give me the answer.
You seem to also know the woman in front of you, but cannot clearly see her face hidden under the brim of her hat.

options: Observe and try to save yourself

content: You have too many questions. "Who are you? Where is this? How do I escape from Chameleon's control and return to reality?"
However, before you are able to speak, the hypnotist's command rings in your head.
This archive feels familiar—the files are arranged like those in the MBCC.
However, before you are able to determine if that is the case, the hypnotist's command rings in your head.

speaker: Chameleon
content: Chief, tell this nosy woman that you are here to interrogate Chameleon regarding the whereabouts of the "hostage."
You repeat Chameleon's words reluctantly. After all, this is her home turf.

speaker: Chameleon
content: Good. Come, let's hear what she has to say to that.
Your resistance proved futile as this is Chameleon's home turf.

speaker: Chameleon
content: Good, don't waste your energy. Why don't we listen to what she has to say to that?
The hostage is being held in an abandoned depot on the border of Eastside, which can be found by walking south along the Rust.
The mysterious person says that while handing the document in hand to you.

speaker: Chameleon
content: This woman cannot be trusted. It's best you confirm the document's contents.
The hypnotist puts tremendous pressure on you, forcing you to look down and open the document in your hand.

Chameleon, female, born on February 14, N.F. 86, is a psychology professor at Banyan Medical College and is currently serving as a special psychology consultant for the 9th Agency.
Special ability: Tampering with the subconscious mind of others.
Profile:
Her father Dane Theseus and mother Lilian Theseus were both graduates of Banyan Medical College who specialized in subconscious therapy. They have had a private psychological clinic since N.F. 84.
In N.F. 96, <color=#e45515>the Theseuses</color> were murdered and the clues were destroyed by fire. Their daughter Chameleon was found in a coma inside the clock cabinet.
 <color=#e45515>The murderer and arson suspect Oris</color>, a key councilor in Paradeisos, was released at the end due to a lack of evidence.

In N.F. 106, the murderer's wife and parents cut ties with him for unspecified reasons. After losing the <color=#e45515>Jacknal family's </color>asylum, he lost his residency in Paradeisos and was deported.
In N.F. 107, the 9th Agency found Oris mind-controlled in Chameleon's private clinic <color=#e45515>and secretly held him hostage at the agency's old depot</color>. In the same year, Chameleon accepted an invitation from the 9th Agency to provide guidance in criminal psychology.
In N.F. 111, a group of civilians from the Jacknal family suffered from auditory hallucinations, which are a sequela of hypnosis. They were suspected to have been <color=#e45515>tampered with subconsciously</color>.
In N.F. 112, Chameleon was formally arrested by the 9th Agency on suspicion of tampering with others' subconscious and was transferred to the MBCC.

speaker: Chameleon
content: The old depot of the agency, very good... You've done a good job, Chief...
Chameleon contently repeats the address and her voice gets softer each time.
No one responds, and the voice looking down on the subconscious word is now completely silent.
Chameleon?
End the hypnosis now.
Chameleon!
What do you think she's going to do after she got this information?
?! Are... Are you talking to me?
There are only the two of us here.
Didn't you exist in the subconscious memory? How could you possibly...
Answer me. What do you think her objective is?
Her authoritative voice compels you to answer.

options: Going to the depot for the hostage

content: But I'm stuck in this dream. How am I supposed to stop her?
Instead of answering your question directly, she gives a statement, trying to make you less confused.
The dreaming one is not her, but you.
What you see in hypnosis is the extraction and processing of actual memories.
I still don't get it...
Being in the subconscious world, you must be able to find those things that were forgotten.
Forgotten things? What did you forget?

speaker: Guard
content: You scared me, Chief. What are you doing here so late instead of sleeping?
I have a classified mission. I need to go to the higher-classified archive to request clearance.

speaker: Guard
content: I see. Your eyes were half-closed, so I thought you were sleepwalking... Do you need me to notify Adjutant Nightingale?
No need. Keep this a secret from everyone.
Is this your memory? How come you seem to have no recollection of it at all?

speaker: Chameleon
content: You will find an opportunity to go to the 9th Agency's archive alone and investigate the hostage's whereabouts...
Okay... I will go to the higher-classified archive and investigate the hostage's whereabouts...

speaker: Chameleon
content: You will forget some details and use the remaining memory fragments for the dream in our spiritual connection...
I will forget some details and use the remaining memory fragments for the dream in our spiritual connection...

speaker: Chameleon
content: Very good. Next, you will see Nightingale enter the interrogation room and will be subjected to Sinners' disdain and blame...
If I guessed correctly, she will lie to you that it was all a dream. But in fact, it was real.
Yes...

What terrifies you even more is that every topic she mentioned, be it spiritual connections, dreams, reluctance to be interrogated, or childhood nightmares, was deliberately crafted to steer you. Her every little gesture was calculated.
I'm sure you know what to do next.
The woman raises her cane and taps the document in your hand.
Remember to leave the document behind before you leave. Be careful as it is the key to the dangerous door.
Wait!
You still have unanswered questions.

options: Why didn't she kill her enemy back then?
Who are you? How are you able to talk to me?

content: Instead of letting Oris fall into the hands of the 9th as leverage and going to great lengths to get the info, why didn't she kill her enemy at the very first?
Even Chameleon had no access to these documents and had to use me to get the information. How did you know about all this?
Not only do you know Chameleon, but you also seem to know me well. It's like you predicted I would go into my own memories, so that you leave these words as a reminder. Who exactly are you?
She does not respond to you.
(Thud)
With the sound of the cane hitting the ground, you feel dizzy again.
You are back in the confinement room. Sure enough, Chameleon is not there anymore.

options: Call Nightingale to apprehend the Sinner!

content: Nightingale! Send guards immediately to apprehend Chameleon. She's escaped.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chameleon? Weren't you in the confinement room?
I underestimated her first hypnosis.
Chameleon's ability is not simply hypnosis, but rather the distortion and manipulation of the subconscious world. She tampered with my subconscious actions and even my memories.

speaker: Nightingale
content: But haven't you already put shackles on her and confiscated her pocket watch?
Since she could manipulate you without your knowledge, it shouldn't have been difficult for her to unlock the shackles and fool all the MBCC guards.
Not to mention, the pocket watch isn't her only hypnosis prop. You remember the pair of gold-rimmed glasses that made you feel uneasy.
Damn, I don't have enough time to explain now! Go south along the Rust. Chameleon went to the 9th Agency's old depot!
The 9th must have their reasons for keeping her away from the hostage. Hurry, we must stop her.
Chameleon might well have killed the hostage and even...
Even committed evil acts that you cannot speculate or control for now.

speaker: Langley
content: Be careful as it is the key to the dangerous door.

speaker: Guard A
content: Unconscious guards found. The east exit has been blocked. Over.

speaker: Guard B
content: Hostage survival confirmed. The west exit has been blocked. Over.

speaker: Guard C
content: Snipers are in position and have locked onto the suspect. Ready to breach at any time.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Copy that.
You have reached the hostage's location and have surrounded the site. Everyone is holding breath, waiting for your next command.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, what should we do next?
Anything that would threaten the lives of the hostage and the suspect would be a bad idea. Besides, if the raid team gets hypnotized, we'll be in big trouble.
I'll go in and distract her to create a window of opportunity for you.

speaker: Nightingale
content: No, that's too dangerous.
My shackles can at least limit some of her abilities. And... I'm sure you'll keep the chief of the MBCC from danger.

speaker: Nightingale
content: ...I see.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Understood! All teams at my command...

speaker: Nightingale
content: Three...

speaker: Nightingale
content: Two...

speaker: Chameleon
content: Chief!
From the communications device comes a familiar voice that catches even Nightingale off guard.

speaker: Chameleon
content: Relax, one of your subordinates "voluntarily" gave me the communications device. Oh, and I did not hurt him.

speaker: Chameleon
content: Let's have a chat, Chief. Face to face.
Then she hangs up as if she does not care about your answer or already knows what you will do.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Don't go, Chief. This is obviously a trap.
I know that... but since she has the confidence to provoke us, I'm sure she's done her preparations.
Rather than be at a disadvantage during the breach, let's do as she says and see what she really wants.

speaker: Nightingale
content: ...I understand. I will have the troops stand by.
Nightingale shoves her sidearm into your hand.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Just in case.

You do not make any more chatter. 
After seeing Nightingale relay the orders, you hide your sidearm in your overcoat and enter the depot alone.
The situation becomes clearer as you slowly approach your target, step by step.
The hostage, Oris, is tied to a chair in a semi-conscious state. He looks dazed and is drooling at the mouth.
Chameleon is standing no more than a foot away from the hostage, admiring her masterpiece.

speaker: Chameleon
content: I've been waiting for a while, Chief!

speaker: Chameleon
content: Let me see what you recall. Is it that wonderful night that I orchestrated?

speaker: Chameleon
content: Shh, it's not time for questions yet.
Her index finger is placed at her mouth to make the gesture of silence. You can clearly see the damned pocket watch still hanging around her hand.

speaker: Chameleon
content: Come, let me introduce to you. This is Oris, 35 years old, former secretary of a councilor and a self-made man who married into the Jacknal family.

speaker: Chameleon
content: Take a guess, Chief, as to what secret this man has that he had to kill his psychologists.
It was not recorded in the 9th's documents.

speaker: Chameleon
content: That's because his story does not deserve to be recorded. He couldn't resist his repeated desire to cheat and feared losing the protection of his fiancée's family.

speaker: Chameleon
content: How ridiculous that this made him anxious and lose sleep.

speaker: Chameleon
content: My parents' treatment was perfect. I witnessed it in the clock cabinet. All he had to do was go back to sleep to forget all this unpleasantness.

speaker: Chameleon
content: However, he decided to lift the sculpture and smash it onto...

Chameleon takes a deep breath and looks up at the roof of the old depot. 
The sun never shines here.
You've already taken everything he values most: his wife, his status, and his power. Is that not enough?

speaker: Chameleon
content: Taken away? I've only allowed the people around him to see his true colors. How is that enough?

speaker: Chameleon
content: I will turn him into a ghost in the sea of fire, forever repenting in hell for his sins.
Chameleon lifts his chin with her fingers and scrutinizes every inch of the hostage's pale face.

speaker: Chameleon
content: Didn't you ask me just now, Chief, why I didn't run away?

speaker: Chameleon
content: That's because...

speaker: Chameleon
content: It would be a shame if there were no audience for such a wonderful show.

speaker: Chameleon
content: Shh, it's not time for questions yet.
Her index finger is placed at her mouth to make the gesture of silence. You can clearly see the damned pocket watch still hanging around her hand.

speaker: Chameleon
content: Come, let me introduce to you. This is Oris, 35 years old, former secretary of a councilor and a self-made man of the Paradeisos.

speaker: Chameleon
content: Take a guess, Chief, as to what secret this man has that he had to kill his psychologists.
It was not recorded in the 9th's documents.

speaker: Chameleon
content: That's because his story does not deserve to be recorded. He couldn't resist his repeated desire to cheat and feared losing the protection of his fiancée's family.

speaker: Chameleon
content: How ridiculous that this made him anxious and lose sleep.

speaker: Chameleon
content: My parents' treatment was perfect. I witnessed it in the clock cabinet. All he had to do was go back to sleep to forget all this unpleasantness.

speaker: Chameleon
content: However, he decided to lift the sculpture and smash it onto...

Chameleon takes a deep breath and looks up at the roof of the old depot. 
The sun never shines here.
You've already taken everything he values most: his wife, his status, and his power. Is that not enough?

speaker: Chameleon
content: Taken away? I've only allowed the people around him to see his true colors. How is that enough?

speaker: Chameleon
content: I will turn him into a ghost in the sea of fire, forever repenting in hell for his sins.
Chameleon lifts his chin with her fingers and scrutinizes every inch of the hostage's pale face.

speaker: Chameleon
content: Didn't you ask me just now, Chief, why I didn't kill him?

speaker: Chameleon
content: That's because...

speaker: Chameleon
content: We will need the cooperation of actors to achieve a wonderful performance.
Performance?

speaker: Chameleon
content:
Last time, the audience was nosy and took my actor.
This time, you wouldn't want to miss it. This performance will show the wicked falling into the abyss.
By "wicked," is she referring to Oris or herself?
You do not make it on time to ask this question as you hear clanking from the pocket watch flap.

speaker: Oris
content: Fire!! I'm burning!!
Oris begins to struggle violently while screaming incoherently.

speaker: Oris
content: H-HELP ME! HELP! HELP ME!

speaker: Oris
content: I admit I was wrong! T-there's no exit!

speaker: Oris
content: It's you guys again... Don't come any closer! Don't come any closer!
His wrists rub against the rope, bleeding. But Oris seems unable to perceive the pain and continues jerking his body with all his might, fighting with an invisible enemy.

options: What have you done to him?!

speaker: Chameleon
content: I tailored a nightmare for him.

speaker: Chameleon
content: This dream has no end but only a sea of flames and countless sharp blades forged by my hatred.
This is mental abuse!

speaker: Chameleon
content: Hahahahah, why do you seem so surprised?

speaker: Chameleon
content: Hahahahahah, he's already entered the mind maze I tailored for him. A nightmare of an endless sea of flames. Revenge without an end.

speaker: Chameleon
content: Stop? Pfft, did you actually think I would stop?

speaker: Chameleon
content: Looks like that woman is playing the game of checks and balances... Didn't she tell you?

speaker: Chameleon
content: The reason why the 9th would not let me approach the hostage.
Chameleon dips her fingertips into the blood flowing from the hostage's wrists and holds it to her mouth with a look of intoxicating pleasure.

speaker: Chameleon
content: Then let me tell you personally...

speaker: Chameleon
content: I am one of the best hypnotists in the DisCity, a professor of psychology at Banyan Medical College, a psychological consultant at 9th, and at the same time...

speaker: Chameleon
content: I'm also a psychopath that thrives on schadenfreude, hahahahahah.
Chameleon's presumptuous laughter sends a chill down your spine.
You might be too late: the hostage—or the "key"—has unlocked the dangerous door to Chameleon's madness.
Even though you failed to stop her from hypnotizing the hostage, you can at least end the abuse!
The dark glow flows in your palm, but the situation has not changed in the slightest. Oris is still screaming and struggling.

speaker: Chameleon
content: Heheh, Chief. Looks like those shackles you're proud of have failed you.

speaker: Chameleon
content: Do you know why?
Chameleon leans in close towards you, her voice trying to lead you.
After two hypnosis sessions, you know you should ignore what she has to say.

options: Try to unleash the shackles again!

content: You ignore Chameleon, but you still fail to unleash the shackles.

speaker: Oris
content: Fire!! Everything is in flames!! Let me out!

speaker: Chameleon
content: This is the perfect toy for me. All of my pain is caused by him, and all of his pain is forged by me...

speaker: Chameleon
content: My toy is calling for your help! But why can't you even use the shackles that you're so good at?
She disguises her schadenfreude as concern.

options: Ignore her. Continue unleashing the shackles!

content: Sure enough, it still fails.

speaker: Chameleon
content: Have you ever wondered about the anomaly?

speaker: Chameleon
content: Is it possible that this is not the world you are familiar with?
Your reason tells you that you failed because your subconscious mind remembers that "Chameleon can manipulate you to unfasten the shackles." You must not let her words lead you.
But at the same time, the skepticism caused by the two hypnosis sessions makes you wonder whether everything here is fake.

speaker: Chameleon
content: That's right, could it all be fake?
She seems to be able to read your mind.

speaker: Chameleon
content: From the moment I closed my pocket watch, from the moment you stepped foot into the depot, and from the moment you brought your men to surround this place, you—all of you—have been stuck in the dream that I prepared!

options: Could this really be a dream?

speaker: Chameleon
content: How can you be so sure? Maybe this false life is an illusory dream in itself.

speaker: Chameleon
content: Yes, this false life is just an illusory dream, hahaha.
At the sound of her laughter, the ground begins to tilt, the walls distort and Chameleon's voice starts to get muddled.
The hypnosis this time is much more powerful than ever. Although you repeatedly tell yourself that everything is an illusion, you still feel a splitting headache.
Your last shred of sanity allows you to feel for the pistol hidden in your coat.
Looks like you've got to give it a shot.
Bang!!
You only hit Chameleon in the thigh as you are wobbling. Everything stabilizes for a moment after the gunshot.

options: Use this opportunity to unleash the shackles again!

content: Interrupting the hypnosis by attacking the hypnotist boosts your confidence. The shackles are released and the hostage is no longer struggling.
You hypnotized me twice and I retaliated once. I think is quite fair.

speaker: Chameleon
content: Interesting...
female_content: So beautiful...

content: What?
Only now do you notice that Chameleon is not concerned at all about her wounds or the hostage. Her face glows with a look of strange ecstasy as she keeps her eyes glued to you.

speaker: Chameleon
content: I thought it was not true that the shackles could connect to the spiritual world, but just now, I saw it—

speaker: Chameleon
content: A world more fascinating than the abyss of pain. That was your deep spiritual world.
Stop playing tricks. I don't want to hurt you anymore.

speaker: Chameleon
content: No, you do! The moment you were about to pull the trigger, all you had in your mind was how to shoot and kill me.
Chameleon's voice is surprisingly calm, but you can tell that compared to the usual well-disguised psychologist, this one has a lot more deep emotions mixed into it.
You can't deny that you had the intention to kill her when you pointed the gun at her and that you were disappointed when your shot only hit her thigh.
During this silence, Nightingale arrives with her men.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief! Are you hurt?!

options: I'm good. Deal with the hostage first.

content: Send Oris back to the 9th and never ever tell me where they will be hiding him.

speaker: Chameleon
content: Hide him? Hahahah... You've already experienced the pleasure of malice and you're still trying to pretend?

speaker: Chameleon
content: What you're thinking right now is clear: "If only Chameleon had killed the hostage!"
I'm not.

speaker: Chameleon
content: You can't wait for me and that loser Oris to disappear from this world.
That's enough!

speaker: Chameleon
content: Hahahah, admit it. You and I are the same. We're both selfish.

speaker: Chameleon
content: The seeds of evil have been planted in your subconscious world, slowly taking root...

speaker: Chameleon
content: Slowly sprouting...
Bang!!
A bullet goes through your thigh and the sharp pain brings you back to your senses immediately. There are no longer any floating walls or floors, just a hostage needing to be freed.

options: Use this opportunity to unleash the shackles again!

content: The sensation of pain stimulates your perception and crisis awareness. The shackles are successfully released and the hostage is no longer struggling.
Nightingale, who hears the gunshot, rushes in with her men and escorts slumped Oris out of the door.
The guards surround Chameleon, but she is unfazed. All of her attention is directed toward you.

speaker: Chameleon
content: You actually woke up... using this method? Hah...
She looks at your bleeding gun wound incredulously. Just as she tries to touch it, she is stopped by the guards raising their guns.
Don't resist. You no longer have any advantages.
She looks around. After realizing her situation, she drops her gaze back at you.

speaker: Chameleon
content: Interesting... Hahaha, how interesting...

speaker: Chameleon
content: Still sounding tough even with a gunshot wound, huh... You've sure grown a lot, Chief.

speaker: Chameleon
content: You're no longer the same greenhorn who could be meekly hypnotized.
Chameleon's voice is surprisingly calm. You seem to see the gentle and kind doctor of the past in this psychopath. Unfortunately, that gentle doctor was a mere facade.
I'm already able to resist hypnosis on my own. You've lost your last bargaining chip. Just surrender.

speaker: Chameleon
content: Sure, I'll go back with you.
She agrees without thinking and even lets the guards cuff her.
I will send the hostage back to the 9th and hide him in a place that even I don't know about...

speaker: Chameleon
content: It doesn't matter anymore.
She smiles and interrupts your explanation.

speaker: Chameleon
content: I already found a better toy!
What are you trying to pull this time?

speaker: Chameleon
content: Take it easy. I've already lost this round, haven't I? I'm not going to pull any tricks.

speaker: Chameleon
content: There are still many days ahead of us...

Chameleon was brought back to the Bureau and put under the strict surveillance for an S-class danger.
There, she was playing the role of a psychologist like she was before. She has not mentioned anything related to "hostage" or "psychopath."
It doesn't seem like there will be any more incidents, but you still feel vaguely uneasy.

Your game with her seems to have just begun.
The door of the interrogation room slams shut loudly behind you, but the woman before you gazes at the ground with her head lowered and doesn't seem to notice.

speaker: Anne
content: Ah... has it begun already? Sorry, I was a bit distracted.

speaker: Anne
content: You're going to interrogate me, right? I'll answer any questions about my crime.
Anne tries to force a smile, but the blinding light of the interrogation room still exposes her exhaustion in an instant.

speaker: Anne
content: Maybe it's because I've had a bit of insomnia recently... don't worry, it won't affect the interrogation.

speaker: Anne
content: Where would you like me to begin? How about from my awakening as a Sinner?
For some reason, she seems eager to tell you all the "truth" about herself.
Anne, your behavior is surprising. Why are you so eager to confess?
Under the pressure of interrogation, ordinary people would subconsciously try to conceal themselves in self-defense. That would be the most typical response.

speaker: Anne
content: I'm a Sinner who gained my power from Syndrome Mania... I can no longer be counted as "ordinary people."
Her reason is so unconvincing that she avoids your gaze.
You don't trust me?

speaker: Anne
content: Chief, you don't trust me either, no? We are no longer in SALVA.

speaker: Anne
content: Here, you are not my patient, and I am no longer the head nurse you can trust...
We can become trusted partners in a common battle.

speaker: Anne
content: Really? Sounds pretty great...
She is still on guard against you. Maybe she hasn't fully recovered since the changes in SALVA.
Even if you know I won't believe everything you say, please say what you must.

speaker: Anne
content: Okay...

speaker: Anne
content: My awakening happened before I joined SALVA.

speaker: Anne
content: I'm not sure if you've heard of the strange disease that went around Syndicate a few years ago.

speaker: Anne
content: No one knew the specific symptoms of that disease, but they say the FAC secretly established a closed prevention and control site holding about a hundred members. A team of volunteers from Eastside Hospital also went to help the technologically backward Syndicate.

speaker: Anne
content: But in the end, out of the 90 people at the prevention and control site, only one Eastside volunteer escaped. The rest all went missing.
You're the one who escaped?

speaker: Anne
content: Yes, and the rumors didn't stop there. Some said that the escaped nurse killed all the other volunteer doctors and patients. Others said that the nurse got the mysterious disease too...

speaker: Anne
content: What do you think the truth is, Chief?

options: The "mysterious disease" is actually Syndrome Mania.

speaker: Anne
content: Yeah, it was a small outbreak of Mania. I was the only one who got away because I was a Sinner. As for the 89 others...

speaker: Anne
content: One by one, they became Corruptors, killing each other in front of my eyes... All I could do was ask SALVA to accept them.
Are they the remains of the Corruptors you secretly stored underground?

speaker: Anne
content: Yeah, everything started because of me.

speaker: Anne
content: I insisted on keeping the patients from the past. I caused the rumors about human experiments in SALVA. I selfishly decided to take away the girl's body.

speaker: Anne
content: These were all my decisions alone. It had nothing to do with Iron or anyone from SALVA.

speaker: Anne
content: The FAC can punish me however they want, but please spare SALVA. With Syndicate's current situation, it cannot lose another neutral clinic.
She looks at you earnestly and firmly, without a word of denying responsibility.
Is that what you were so anxious to tell me? You want to take all the blame yourself?

speaker: Anne
content: I deserve to take the blame. When I kept those 89 people, I knew...
You knew they were "remains" already.

speaker: Anne
content: Because... like I said, I'm a Sinner. Ordinary people's common sense does not apply to me.

speaker: Anne
content: It shouldn't be a surprise that Syndrome Mania turned me into a crazy nurse who loves hoarding remains...
She looks away again.
Whether or not you are to blame for the series of crimes in SALVA is still uncertain.
But there must be more to why you kept all those Corruptor remains, right?
You have other concerns? Can you tell me?

speaker: Anne
content: No... you won't believe it, you'll just think I'm babbling nonsense...
How would you know if you don't tell me?
She is still reluctant to speak. It seems like Anne didn't realize you already held key information.

speaker: Anne
content: Where did you find this?
Underground in SALVA, in your office.
She places her hand on the notebook with a nostalgic gaze. One can tell she is intimately familiar with it.

speaker: Anne
content: I thought it got lost in the chaos...
You flip open the notebook and show its contents to Anne.
Since it's yours, you should know exactly what's written in it, right?
You checked and recorded the conditions of the Corruptors in the immersion tank every day. These numbers haven't changed over the years.
She looks away. She doesn't dare to read the contents of the notebook, nor respond to your questions

options: Read the medical records to her.

content: "Immersion Tank #001, patient, Paige, female. Record #732, pulse 0, respiration 0, blood pressure 0, M value..."

speaker: Anne
content: Stop reading, please...
"Record #733, Record #734..."

speaker: Anne
content: I know already, the results are all the same, don't read anymore...

speaker: Anne
content: Enough!
She snatches the notebook and shuts it hastily.
If I were to guess, you've been observing these remains because you think there's still a chance that they can be revived?
Are you... hoping that they come back from the dead?
You seem to have struck a nerve. She looks back at you in a daze.

speaker: Anne
content: Back from the dead... hehe...

speaker: Anne
content: Very funny, isn't it?

speaker: Anne
content: To hope for something so absurd. I know you won't understand...
Does Iron know? As a professional physician, she must know very well what these numbers mean.

speaker: Anne
content: She knew that these were just remains with no signs of life. But she can understand me because she has also heard those voices...
What voices?

speaker: Anne
content: Voices pleading for help...
Anne's fingertips land softly on the notebook's pages, highlighting each name that once belonged to someone alive and well.

speaker: Anne
content: Paige. This was the youngest patient in the closed prevention and control site back then. She was about the same age as that Sinner under Ted.

speaker: Anne
content: She was suffering from Mania at the time and had almost completely lost her mind. With her last trace of consciousness, she grabbed my hand and begged... "Save me."

speaker: Anne
content: Help me, help me, help me! ...Gradually, there were more and more such voices.
Without warning, she grabs the notebook into her arms.

speaker: Anne
content: Finally, I heard each of their voices clearly!

speaker: Anne
content: In my dream! In my spiritual world! 89 living faces—they are still alive!

options: Could it be a hallucination caused by Syndrome Mania?
It's an auditory hallucination from too much stress.

speaker: Anne
content: No! I can feel it, it's a spiritual connection!

speaker: Anne
content: Their spirits are alive! Their will to live is alive!
None of it's real...

speaker: Anne
content: I knew it. You must think I'm crazy, because you've never been surrounded by voices like that.
Anne looks lovingly at the notebook in her arms, as if carefully swaddling a baby.

speaker: Anne
content: Do you know what it's like for someone as dear as a family member to gradually lose warmth in your arms?

speaker: Anne
content: If you've experienced it even once, it wouldn't matter if the spiritual connection was true or not.

speaker: Anne
content: To come back from the dead—that's our only hope!

options: This kind of thing is impossible...

speaker: Anne
content: But modern medicine can't explain the existence of Syndrome Mania. How can you be sure there won't be unexplainable miracles?

speaker: Anne
content: What if? What if they can come back to life?
Then they will become monsters like Corruptors!

speaker: Anne
content: That's fine... Monsters... At least they'll be alive...
You witness Anne shed tears of despair for the first time.

speaker: Anne
content: "Everything will be fine in seven days," "Everything will be fine in three days," "Just hold on and get through tonight..."

speaker: Anne
content: I gave them too many promises, none of which could be fulfilled.

speaker: Anne
content: "To live" was their last hope... I can't... let them down again...
With the FAC's merciless instructions in hand, you don't know how to break the news to her.

Anne, today's interrogation actually has another purpose...
The FAC wants to dispose of these Corruptor remains, so as to eliminate the risk of contamination.

speaker: Anne
content: Dispose of?
She raises her head and looks at you in disbelief, her voice cracking a little.
Yes... they are to be disposed of as soon as possible.
She leans against the chair, speechless.
I didn't tell you at first, because even back at SALVA, I could tell that these Corruptor remains meant a lot to you.
I was going to investigate your connection to them through this interrogation, but I didn't realize... I'm sorry.

speaker: Anne
content: Do you... also support the disposal?
She trembles as she breathes, struggling to resist the urge to sob.
The SALVA isolation zone has been damaged. The contamination has been exposed, and it must be controlled.
Anne... they may be "alive" to you, but to others, they are a potential threat.

speaker: Anne
content: When my patients and colleagues were suffering from Syndrome Mania, it was the FAC who took up arms and sealed off the control site, severing our path to survival.

speaker: Anne
content: Now, for the same reason, you want me to abandon these patients again?
How is this abandoning?

speaker: Anne
content: Right, I forgot... You are no longer my patient, but a subordinate of the FAC, the Chief of the MBCC. You are the same as the FAC.
She holds the notebook full of cold data in her arms as cautiously as if she were carrying a baby.

speaker: Anne
content: Don't worry Paige, I won't hand you over.

speaker: Anne
content: Horo
Ignoring your obstruction, she rises and leaves the interrogation room, with her footsteps somewhat aloof.

speaker: Anne
content: All your spirits are still alive, I can hear you... it must be so... it must...
Her muttering fades into the distance.
You are left in the interrogation room alone. Nightingale's voice cuts through the silence via the comms system.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, is she really okay like this?
...What kind of person do you think Anne is?

speaker: Nightingale
content: According to the report from the SALVA operation and her behavior at the Bureau, she is a stable and reliable nurse. The medical staff all depend heavily on her.
Yes, Anne's professionalism shows that she is not an impulsive person. Hence, her seemingly childish persistence may actually be the result of countless internal struggles.
My persuasion alone is useless to stop her persistence.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Think she can figure it out on her own, Chief?

options: I don't want to force her.

content: Anne won't even give up the life of a deceased patient. She won't allow the contamination to spread.
I hope to become trusted friends with the Sinners. Forcing them will only backfire.
For the time being, cordon off SALVA's underground isolation zone. The public must be prohibited from the vicinity until Anne makes a decision.

speaker: Nightingale
content: The FAC...
I will communicate with my superiors and move forward with the cleanup as soon as possible. She is my Sinner now. I will take responsibility for any problems.
Anne must make a choice between keeping the Corruptor remains of the 89 family-like people who call out for help every day in her dreams, and eliminating the potential threat.
This step will be meaningful only if she takes it herself. She just needs the right opportunity.
What could be this critical opportunity? A name came out...
Paige?

speaker: Anne
content: Up ahead is the junction between Syndicate and the Rust. Why do you bring me here?
Gravel and rubble along the road forces you to leave the car and continue on foot. Anne follows you with a medical kit slung over her back, not knowing your intentions.
