I've heard that you're good with kids, so I take you out for this field mission. It's also a break for me.

speaker: Anne
content: I'm sorry, I've been restless lately. I've caused trouble for everyone at the medical department.

speaker: Anne
content: But what are you going to do when you find a Maniac? Eliminate them, or...
I just want to ask him a question for my friend.
Anne realizes what you mean. During your conversations, you tacitly avoid the cause of Anne's anxiety—the Corruptor remains in the SALVA's basement.
These are all you found? But this is a boy.

speaker: Nightingale
content: The sheriffs at Syndicate don't have the habit of recording their duties. All the info you want for "the Maniac of the same age as Paige" are here.
Forget it. Give it a try. I hope she will make a reasonable choice this time.

speaker: Nightingale
content: What exactly are you trying to do? Don't you need to bring along a guard?
No, I'll go with Anne alone.
The adjutant is still looking at you with distrust.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Every time you show up with a Sinner after an interrogation, you do something out of line.
You follow the map Nightingale gave you all the way west, but don't encounter the little boy described by the sheriff.

speaker: Anne
content: We can't go any further. The Rust is up ahead, and there are roaming Corruptors everywhere. It would be hard for the two of us to come back alive.

speaker: Anne
content: It's getting dark soon. I'm afraid it's not very safe here either.
Maybe he left temporarily for something?
With his physical condition as a Maniac, he shouldn't be able to go too far.

speaker: Anne
content: Perhaps we came too late, and he's already...
Before Anne can finish, there is a sudden rustling sound from behind the crooked tree.

speaker: Anne
content: And who's that?
I should be the one asking you.
A hooded boy emerges, his back against the setting sun. The hood obscures his face.

speaker: Anne
content: Are you the Maniac the sheriff told us about? Great, you're still alive!
Ha. Open your eyes and take a good look.
The boy takes off his hood.
Even though you have seen quite a few monsters, his mutated state still makes you both gasp.
Sixty percent of his body is covered with dark pus. His skin can no longer resist corruption and has begun to rot.
Without his hood, his mutations are terrifying.

speaker: Boy
content: Hey, what's wrong with that woman in white? Why is she staring at me like that? It's annoying.

options: Maybe you remind her of an old friend.
Didn't you tell her to take a good look?

speaker: Boy
content: Is that why you come to find me?

speaker: Boy
content: Pfff... are you here to see me?

speaker: Anne
content: I'm here to help you!
Anne lowers her head and rummages through the medical kit.

speaker: Anne
content: The wounds on your body must be very painful. I have painkillers and anesthetics here!

speaker: Anne
content: Don't worry, they're all tailored for Syndrome Mania, they can definitely...

speaker: Boy
content: Got anything sweet to eat?

speaker: Anne
content: Let me see...
She actually finds a lollipop in her bag.

options: Why do you carry lollipops around with you?

speaker: Anne
content: It's a habit I picked up from the prevention and control site. When kids don't want to take their shots, I coax them with lollipops.

speaker: Anne
content: It's a bit melted though. Is that alright?

speaker: Boy
content: That's fine, toss it over. Let me have a taste.
The boy catches the lollipop, unwraps it clumsily, and gives it a lick.

speaker: Boy
content: Hmm... So this is the taste.

speaker: Anne
content: Hmm...

speaker: Boy
content: Why are you still here? It's getting dark.

speaker: Anne
content: Is there anything else I can help you with?

speaker: Boy
content: Anything else? Yes actually. I want to go to see Eastside. I heard it's a dazzling place with lots to eat and drink, and nobody goes Maniac...

speaker: Boy
content: But I definitely can't enter with this look.

speaker: Boy
content: It's probably better for me to take adventures in the Rust.

speaker: Boy
content: From there, I might be able to catch a glimpse of Eastside from afar.

speaker: Anne
content: Do you have...any other wishes?
Anne doesn't go on, but you know what she wants to ask.

speaker: Boy
content: Duh! You think I want to die? But I'm already like this...

speaker: Anne
content: Wait! What if one day Maniacs can be cured?

speaker: Boy
content: What will happen after I'm cured? I'll still be a monster, right? Will they let me in Eastside?
The boy's tone is unusually calm.

speaker: Boy
content: As you say, it's only "what if." I can tell from your gloomy look that you're bluffing.

speaker: Anne
content: ...I'm sorry.

speaker: Boy
content: Um, what are you apologizing for?

speaker: Anne
content: As a healthcare worker, I cannot fulfill your wish to live.

speaker: Boy
content: Stop flattering yourself! At most, you can make my heart beat again. That doesn't count as fulfilling a wish.
The boy bites the lollipop in annoyance.

speaker: Boy
content: It's boring to live just for the sake of staying alive...

speaker: Boy
content: There are just many things that I haven't done yet. But what does that have to do with you?
The boy's words seem to remind Anne of something. She gazes quietly at the child who outshines her in maturity, and stays silent for a long time.

speaker: Boy
content: Don't do anything weird to me! If it's just a beating heart, I don't want it.

speaker: Anne
content: Don't worry, it won't. It won't beat again...

speaker: Boy
content: What?

speaker: Paige
content: Anne, why do you become a nurse?

speaker: Anne
content: Because Syndicate has poor medical conditions. I had to go to Eastside to learn nursing and bring back the knowledge to help everyone.

speaker: Patient
content: Ah! So Anne is from Syndicate. That must be tough.

speaker: Patient
content: I'm not that ambitious. I just want to make a name for myself in a gang. But I don't dare to touch those strange weapons anymore.

speaker: Anne
content: Really? Then who was the one swearing to become rich?

speaker: Patient
content: Eh? Wasn't it the internist?

speaker: Doctor
content: Me? I just want to return to Eastside after finishing my volunteer work. My wife is still waiting for me.

speaker: Anne
content: What about Paige? What do you want to do when you grow up?

speaker: Paige
content: Anything! As long as I can be with Anne!

speaker: Anne
content: Hahaha, what kind of wish is that?

speaker: Paige
content: What are you laughing at! I'm serious! Cough cough cough...

speaker: Anne
content: Alright, Miss Tag-Along, it's time to take your medicine. Open your mouth...

speaker: Anne
content: If I've promised to save you, but failed to do so, and your dream could not be realized, would you really not blame me?

speaker: Boy
content: You're so annoying! Didn't you ask that already? I told you, it has nothing to do with you.

speaker: Anne
content: Okay...
The boy looks at absent-minded Anne impatiently.

speaker: Boy
content: Hey, is she okay? Why is she crying and laughing?
It seems like she's already got the answer.
She looks at you with both gratitude and guilt.

speaker: Anne
content: Chief, thank you for taking me out today. But what I'm going to do next may cause you some trouble, so please forgive me...
She walks over to the boy, opens her bag, and fishes out each item one by one to explain.

speaker: Anne
content: Can you see this clearly?

speaker: Boy
content: What... what are you going to do?

speaker: Anne
content: This is a serum I crafted with my power, which can delay your mutation. One injection every morning and evening should be enough to support you another month.

speaker: Anne
content: This is the painkiller that Iron made.

speaker: Anne
content: I know the spread of Mania is very painful. This will make you feel a bit better...

speaker: Anne
content: Lastly...
Anne zips up the bag, stands up and picks up her weapon.

speaker: Anne
content: This will help you leave immediately... without pain.

speaker: Anne
content: You can choose between extending your final days to complete what you've always wanted to do, or the syringe in my hand...
Anne...
She aims the weapon at the boy. Her face is unusually devoid of smiles, with a look of calm ruthlessness.
But both you and the boy can see that Anne's hands are shaking.

speaker: Boy
content: A month? ...That's fine too.
The boy picks up the medicine from the ground.

options: Are you going to let him go?
Don't you have a third option?

content: Anne purses her lips and lowers her head to avoid your gaze.
Are you really going to let this kid go? In the eyes of the FAC, it is a serious dereliction of duty to let go of a Maniac.
Put him in the special potion. He's our new hope.
Anne doesn't speak. She purses her lips and lowers her head to avoid your gaze.
It seems like she's already made a new choice. Are you really going to let this kid go? Even at the cost of malfeasance...
You can't guarantee that he won't ever hurt anyone.

speaker: Anne
content: Chief, didn't you bring me out here to let me make a choice? Why...
Not on this matter.
You prepare to step forward to attack, but suddenly you feel a stab in the back of your neck.
You!...
You black out and fall into Anne's arms.

speaker: Anne
content: Chief, I won't run away, but... sorry, this kid still wants to see the world.
Confused, you overhear Anne's last words to the boy.

speaker: Anne
content: Never get yourself caught by the Bureau. Go to the Rust and run far away from here.

speaker: Anne
content: I wish you luck for your last month. I hope we... won't see each other again...
Let's go back to the MBCC. Anne, nothing happened today.

speaker: Anne
content: You will be blamed...
I know.

speaker: Anne
content: I won't let you take the blame.
Anne takes out a syringe from her pocket.

speaker: Anne
content: This is anesthesia. I won't hurt you or run away.
You'll take the insensible me back to the MBCC and take all the blame yourself.

speaker: Anne
content: ...That's the best solution I can think of.
She wants to take all the blame herself again.
You never thought that I'd agree to let him go?

speaker: Anne
content: It is your duty to eliminate Maniacs...
But that kid still wants to see the world. That's what "to live" means for him.
Anne looks at you in surprise. The anesthetic syringe in her hand falls to the ground and breaks in two.
You hope that you can do more than just "persistence" to eliminate Mania. So do I.

options: Tell the boy to stay away from others.

content: In your final month, you can go to the Rust, but stay away from other humans. Don't congregate with the Corruptors either. If you hurt someone and get discovered by the FAC, I really can't help you.

speaker: Boy
content: Got it! Thanks!
The boy waves the leftover lollipop in his hand. You and Anne watch him turn around and disappear into the distance.

speaker: Boy
content: My name is Gary! If you get the chance, go visiting Eastside for me!

speaker: Hecate
content: Chief, everything is ready. Anne has agreed to commence the contamination cleanup at any time.
Considering the safety of the areas around Syndicate, the MBCC has removed all the immersion tanks from SALVA.
At the moment, hundreds of Corruptor remains slumber in the blue potion in front of you.

speaker: Hecate
content: Anne said she didn't want to do it herself, but she told me how to open the immersion tank. She also left you a notebook.
After the interrogation, you returned the notebook to its original owner. Now, it is in your hands again.
Why did she give this to me?

speaker: Hecate
content: My job is just giving it to you.
You open the familiar notebook and discover some changes.
A new "wish" has been added to the records of each immersion tank.
"Return to Eastside to be with my wife"... "Make a name for myself in a gang"... "Become a singer"... "Teach my son to read"...
Anne recalled the wishes of each patient. She didn't forget to add Gary's wish of "Visiting Eastside for fun" and Paige's wish to "be with Anne."
You browse through these newly added annotations and find a letter in the middle of the notebook.
You open the letter. The handwriting is neat and graceful, and the paper seems to be tinged with the tranquil fragrance of the notebook's owner.

speaker: Anne
content: Dear Chief, hope this letter finds you well.

speaker: Anne
content: I haven't gone out for so many days. I must have worried you.

By the time you read this letter, the FAC's contamination cleanup may have already begun.
In the face of death, I show more fear than a child. Although you don't say it directly, in your heart you may have secretly blamed me...
I'm sorry that my naive persistence has brought you a lot of trouble.

The notion of "back from the dead" is just a selfish lie to appease my own guilt. I've not only deceived my patients, but also deceived myself.
While I thought I can store them in the immersion tanks, I failed to realize that their reasons for living were never simply to stay "alive."
They are still alive in my memory, and shall stay there for the rest of my life.
I will do what I can to fulfill their wishes.

As the only survivor of the prevention and control site and a SALVA Hospital nurse, there is another thing I need to complete.
Continue Syndrome Mania research.
Sinners usually experience enormous mental stress during the incubation period after their infection. Their abilities are awakened at the same time as their will to fight, and their mutation also stagnates at this time... I think this is by no means a mere coincidence. It may hold the key to curing Mania.

I volunteer as a Sinner test subject to facilitate the FAC's research.
This is not only for my past patients, but also for those in Syndicate who have not yet been affected. As long as we can cure Syndrome Mania, I am willing to try.
Even if there is only a tiny sliver of hope.
Head Nurse of SALVA Hospital, MBCC Sinner, Anne, N.F. 112.
Each pen stroke extends gently across the thin pages, yet in your hands they feel like a thousand kilos.
When you look back at the annotations in the notebook, you can almost see from the circles what Anne looked like when she was writing them.
She locked herself in the room and tried to recall all the moments she shared with the deceased patients, and the experiences they told her.
Anne got to know each patient like her own family and friends. While analyzing the will to live, she also forced herself to return to the empty hospital beds.
You look up from the letter. Hecate still stands before you, awaiting your next order.

speaker: Hecate
content: Alright... Chief, are you going to watch?

speaker: Hecate
content: The scene may cause you discomfort.
Then do you know where Anne is? She's probably not feeling well either. I'll go take a look.

speaker: Hecate
content: After she gave me these things, she went out alone.

speaker: Hecate
content: No, she said she couldn't bear to watch, and then left alone.
Then please handle everything according to procedure. I'm going to see her.

speaker: Hecate
content: Okay.
You find Anne in a secluded corner of the Bureau.
Anne sits quietly under a canopy of stars, gazing up at the night sky without looking back.

speaker: Anne
content: Chief, the weather is nice tonight.

options: How did you know it was me?

speaker: Anne
content: People's footsteps are different.

speaker: Anne
content: Iron's footsteps are always in a hurry. She has a clear purpose and will not stop for anything.

speaker: Anne
content: Victoria's footsteps are light and airy. She doesn't know where she's going, but she's curious about the things around her and always walks slowly.
What about mine?

speaker: Anne
content: Chief, your footsteps are gentle and won't disturb others. But they are also very firm... Every step is thought out, and knows its direction.

options: You like to observe these things?

speaker: Anne
content: It's part of my job to observe carefully and identify the needs of doctors and patients before they realize themselves.

speaker: Anne
content: From what I know about you, I guess you're here to comfort me, right?
You're right.

speaker: Anne
content: Don't worry, I'm fine.
She gently points to her heart.

speaker: Anne
content: These days, I already bid them farewell here.
She smiles in relief.

speaker: Anne
content: Thank you, Chief.

speaker: Anne
content: From saving the girl in SALVA, to letting go of Gary, to now keeping me company, you have done so much for me. Yet I have nothing to repay you with.
That's not true!

options: You can repay me with work.
You can repay me with yourself.

content: The nurses from the MBCC medical department come to my office every day to ask "Why hasn't Anne come back to work?"... "Why did Anne lock herself up?"... "Chief, if you mistreat Anne, the entire medical department will not spare you"...

speaker: Anne
content: Pfff...
Why are you laughing?

speaker: Anne
content: Chief, you're adorable when you imitate how others talk.
Really...

speaker: Anne
content: Oh my, Chief, you're blushing!

speaker: Anne
content: Eh? Chief, you want me to give myself to you?
You think I'm that corrupt?!
I'm saying that the MBCC needs you! The medical staff are all waiting for you to go back and help!

speaker: Anne
content: Oh, is that so?

speaker: Anne
content: Chief, what are you blushing for?
...I'm not!

speaker: Anne
content: Hahahaha... alright.
Anne flashes a rare relaxed smile. Usually, her smiles are of a professional nature.
Since you've known her, there have been two huge weights on her chest. One was the expectations of patients, and the other was the guilt of a healthcare worker.
Boom—
A loud noise echoes from the depot, and a strange fragrance wafts in from the distance.

speaker: Anne
content: It's the smell of potion that stores remains... seems like Hecate is finished.
Neither of you speak. You simply sit side by side amidst the fragrance, quietly gazing at the night sky.
Suddenly, a white light flashes across the sky.
Anne, it's a meteor.

speaker: Anne
content: No, that's...
Anne's voice chokes with joy.

speaker: Anne
content: That's Paige.
So, this is how it feels to be in a position like this.
Kisugi Hitomi
Not half bad though.
To defeat your enemy you must know your enemy.
Am I right, Chief?
You turn on the light. For a split second, Sinner Fox's pupils contract.
They look like those of a cunning fox.
Yes.
Pleasure to meet you, Eastside's golden lawyer.
Is that so?
Or maybe, what you really mean is that you've known me quite well?
Mr. Fox shrugs and points at the file in your hand.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Looks like you've done your research on me too.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: I guess we can skip the pleasantries then.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Let's go straight into the problem we're here to discuss.
The Sinner cuts right to the chase even before the interrogation begins. It seems to you that he is confident about how the interrogation will turn out.
Works for me. It'll save us time.
test
test
test
test
test
test
I've received your application for a leave permit...
The reason is... you need to defend a client?

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: That's right.
Mr. Fox says so briskly, adjusting his glasses.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: I took on a case two days before you arrested me as a Sinner.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: My clients count on me to help them seek justice. I can't stand them up.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: One of the MBCC rules stipulates, "If deemed necessary, detention of Sinners who are members of the elite may be suspended to allow the said Sinners to carry out their duties in their respective fields."

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: I count as a member of the elite, I believe?
There is indeed such a rule, and you do count as a member of the elite.
You open the file, which contains documents on the cases taken on by Mr. Fox as a lawyer.
I've gone through the cases you took on. You won every single one of them. That's very impressive.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Thank you.
Just out of curiosity, do you take on every case that comes your way? It's difficult, if not impossible, to win every single case, right?
Mr. Fox hesitates for a split second before answering.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Every lawyer is different. We have different personalities and tastes. We may refuse to take on a case or two occasionally. Nothing unusual about that.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Why? Does it have anything to do with me getting a leave permit?
You don't answer; you only shrug.
But... Mr. Fox, the performance of that rule is subject to certain conditions.
And this is why I'm here today.
I need to do an appraisal before deciding whether we should suspend your detention and allow you to return to Eastside.
Mr. Fox ponders for a long moment before giving a knowing smile.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Fair enough. In your eyes... in the eyes of ordinary folks, we Sinners are way too powerful and dangerous.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: It's like a set of unbalanced scales. The closer one gets to heaven, the more afraid they are of those standing on the opposite end, in the doorway to hell.
That's not the only consideration, Mr. Fox.
test
test
test
test
test
test
test
I've perused your cases.
I want to know more about some of these cases, so that I can decide whether or not you qualify to go out.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: I won all the cases. Isn't that enough?
I'm afraid not, Mr. Fox.
Let's talk about the copycat case that shocked Eastside not so long ago.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Oh, about that...

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: If I remember correctly, the defendant in this case tried to copy the M.O. of another case, a centuries-old case.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: The detestable criminal in this old case suffered from severe mental illness and harmed similar-looking victims one after another.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: In fact, I once wondered what strategy I would've used to win this case if I had represented one side... or the other.

<size=32>"The suspect in this case, in an attempt to copy the killer in the original case, planned to... harm several females from the same company. They had the same hair, eye, and skin color. But the suspect was caught before the plan was carried out."</size>

"But in the Court of Appeal, the plaintiffs recanted their testimonies and denied the witnesses' statements. They proclaimed that the suspect had been just helping them with their jobs, and that it was purely accidental that they got injured."

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Yeah, those were three unexpected accidents in a row, just like their name suggests, they're the kind of surprises you can stumble upon, but can't really chase after.
Mr. Fox, you represented the defendant in this case, didn't you?

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Yes. A big-eyed girl. My fees are not cheap, so to pay me, she sold everything she owned in the Back Alley...

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Including herself, I might add.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: But I'll never forget the overjoyed look in her eyes when she was acquitted.
Previous to this, the witnesses' testimonies, the evidence gathered from the scene, public opinion... all had pointed to your client committing attempted murder.
You turn to one of the pages which records some of the testimonies for the case.
"The three girls were the defendant's colleagues. The defendant was their senior. They were up for promotion because of their stellar performances."
"Before the incident, they all invited this senior of theirs to a weekend party. And it's at this party that they almost lost their lives."

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: That's not enough to prove that my client was the culprit. Don't you think so?
Mr. Fox adjusts his glasses again, the corner of his mouth lifted by a sardonic smile.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: All the testimonies were recanted in the Court of Appeal.
I've reviewed the court records for the case. The testimonies and evidence the plaintiffs gave after the recantation were almost ludicrous and even self-contradictory.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: So what? Ludicrous or not, testimony can be a lethal weapon, as long as it helps prove my client innocent.
They recanted their testimonies... Was it because of something you did?

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: If you're asking if I visited the witnesses and others who'd give evidence to get the lethal weapon I needed, then yes...

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: I took on the client, which means I would do everything in my power to help her get whatever she wanted.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: The moment the deal was made, I unconditionally believed that my client was innocent.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: If her definition of justice was proof of her innocence, then that's what I'd get her.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Whatever it took...

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: And that's my credo, Chief.
Correct me if I'm wrong, you paid the witnesses to change their stories, or made them do so with your power.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: All for the purpose of getting my client the justice she expected.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Like I said, I'd do everything in my power to prove the client's innocence.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Alas, that gave you a reason to detain me. I understand that you think it's more unforgivable for me to do what I do to get a fellow Sinner like the Countess off the hook than to help a regular Joe escape punishment.
That's not justice, Mr. Fox.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: What is then?

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Spending the rest of her life enduring looks of contempt? Or withering away behind high walls until she becomes as significant as a speck of dust?

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Chief, even those living in hell deserve a lifeline, however thin that lifeline might be.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: For them, justice is victory in court.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: And when the usual courses of action can't bring them what they want, money and my power will...
You snap the file shut and throw it on the table.

I guess there's no need for us to discuss the details of the other cases. The FAC has discovered through their investigation that suspiciously high amounts of money changed hands between you and your clients.
It's also been found that you cut backdoor deals with key witnesses from the opposing side, and that you used your power on many occasions.
Your application is refused, Mr. Fox.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Chief... a defendant, no matter how suspicious-looking, has a right to justice.
Your version of justice comes at the expense of the other party's legitimate interests.
I know about the case you're working on. Your client is the mistress of a manor. She accused one of her maids of poisoning her husband, the patriarch of the manor.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Yes, she pressed charges the day after the husband was found dead and hired me to represent her.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: I hear that the maid is still being locked up in the manor, waiting to be transferred to a prison in Eastside after trial.
With all due respect, I don't think that the maid has anything to gain from the death of the patriarch of the manor.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Chief, you've led many successful missions in Syndicate, don't tell me you don't know that there is more to human nature than meets the eye.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: The truth about human nature is like evidence. You need to guide it, to bring it to light.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Surely you don't want to see justice entombed, never to see the light of day again?
What you've just said makes sense, in a way. But what you do still goes against the current rules. Some restrictions are called for.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: So you're going to refuse my application?
Yes.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Which means I won't be able to appear in court to defend my client...
They will find the lady another lawyer, a more... fair-minded one.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: How she will fare in court is none of my concern now.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Not defending a client in court myself is as good as losing the case.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: I'm a champion of justice. And in my book, justice means an unbroken run of wins.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: I appear in court for each and every one of my clients. I defend them, and I win, as simple as that.
Mr. Fox's expression becomes increasingly somber, and his eyes are fixed on you.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Since you're not signing my permit, I've got no other choice...
An invisible force seems to come off the man before you, pining you down in your seat.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: "Do not fight me, Chief."

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: "Be a dear and do as you're told."
Y-you are using your power against me?

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Uh, ugh...
There is a suggestion of unsteadiness in his searchlight-like eyes.
You notice a dense layer of tiny beads of sweat on the tip of his nose.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Holder of the shackles... you do live up to the name!

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: It's taxing... to force your hand with my power.
You can tell from his expression that there is a build-up of strain inside of him. Then he raises his hands and grasps his neck.
He tightens his grip, as if to force words out of his throat.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: "Take out... my... application form..."

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: "Sign it!"
Mr. Fox's voice is hoarse. Never has he tried to control someone as powerful as the new Chief of the MBCC, someone more powerful than he is.
But he must appear in court for his client, to do his job as a champion of justice.
Under Mr. Fox's steady gaze, you take out the form and sign it.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: "Lift... the restraint... Let me out..."
Mr. Fox is huffing and puffing, his voice as thin as a thread on the point of breaking.
His entire head is throbbing with pain. Bright red liquid streams down his face and gives off a strange metallic smell.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Thank you, Chief.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: And if you don't mind...

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: "Please lift the restraint on me."
You pause for a moment, stand up, and press the button to lift the restraint.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Thank you once again.
Mr. Fox's voice is so hoarse that his words are almost unintelligible. He scrambles to his feet, takes a look at you, and makes to walk out of the interrogation room.
Mr. Fox, you should know that it's extremely difficult, if not impossible, for you to control a holder of the shackles.

speaker: Fox
content: "If that's the case, let's meet at the end of heaven."

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, you were not actually controlled by Fox, were you?

speaker: Nightingale
content: Why did you sign the permit?
There's no use in keeping him here.
I'm gonna take a trip to Eastside. Miss Nightingale, please get everything ready.
And... find out everything you can on the manor case, and send a copy to my terminal.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Eastside? You want to follow Mr. Fox again?
No, I want to beat him at his own game.
An MBCC vehicle pulls up in front of a grandiose manor.
The manor looks like something straight out of a novel or TV drama. An elegant fountain, well-manicured hedges, a cast-iron gate abutting a gilded plate that bears the family name: Golstoy.
But there is a gloomy atmosphere surrounding the manor, impervious to the jauntiness of the dancing water in the fountain.

speaker: Waiter
content: Hello, special representative from the city hall, Mr. ${PlayerName}?
female_content: Hello, Special representative from the city hall, Miss ${PlayerName}?

speaker: Waiter
content: Mrs. Golstoy has been waiting for you. This way please.
The servant leads you to the main building on the property. Along the way, uniformed servants, male or female, whisper when they spot you, all wearing a suspicious look.
Standing by the front door leading into the hall is a lady in exquisite attire.

speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
content: Sorry about their rudeness.

speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
content: Who would have thought that they would find a criminal in their ranks?

options: The truth has yet to be unearthed.

content: That's why I've come.
I'd appreciate your cooperation.
Mrs. Golstoy presses her lips together, and saying nothing further, leads you into the house.

speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
content: She is held in her room for lawful detention. The crime scene is being protected by the police.

speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
content: Feel free to look around, and you can talk to her if you like.

speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
content: But it's an ironclad fact that she's guilty. I don't think the presence of a special representative will make any difference.
Mrs. Golstoy puts her handkerchief over her nose, and as if realizing it's inappropriate, lowers her hand. Then she points at somewhere down the hallway.

speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
content: It's over there. I'll leave you to it then.
Thank you for leading the way.
Sensing your confusion, she smiles and pushes the document back to you.

speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
content: She's the murderer.
Mrs. Golstoy stops in her tracks, turns around, and stares down at you.

speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
content: I'm not going to lose this case.

options: It all depends on how the trial will pan out.

content: The judge's gavel will bring us the truth.
Mrs. Golstoy falls silent, gives you a cold look, and continues her ascent upstairs.
You approach the bar, near which two police officers keep guard. You show them the document Nightingale got you that identifies you as a special representative, and they stand aside to let you pass.
Mr. Golstoy dropped dead while reading the newspaper at the bar after a meal. Inside the roped-off area is a chalk outline.
Excuse me, could you tell me where the suspect is kept?

speaker: Police Officer A
content: Second room to the left of the bar. It's in fact a bedroom for servants.
Thank you.

speaker: Police Officer A
content: Here's the deal. You can talk to her, but only through the small window in the door. No physical contact. I hope you can understand.

speaker: Police Officer A
content: And the scene... you can look around, but please try not to touch anything.
You look in the direction of the room and see the window in the door. It's a small window that opens outward. You catch a glimpse of the inside of the room.
She lives in a room like that? It's just a glorified prison cell.

speaker: Police Officer B
content: Some rich people can be very mistrustful. And they're not wrong, considering what's transpired here.

speaker: Police Officer B
content: She looks delicate. I didn't know she had it in her. But even a worm turns. Maybe the man was asking for it...
Dissing a dead man in the middle of the day... Officer, you're not worried it might bring you bad luck?

speaker: Police Officer B
content: Heh... go ahead and look around, sir.
female_content: Heh... go ahead and look around, miss.

content: You pull on the gloves and shoe covers the officer handed you, and start inspecting the dining hall.

The police combed the scene after Mrs. Golstoy reported the death of her husband. You've looked through the physical evidence the police gathered, but noticed nothing particularly suspicious—you have a feeling that it was made to look that way.
The victim started his meal at around eight o'clock. By then, the hard-working maids had cleaned the dining hall inside out.
As your eyes sweep around the hall, you catch sight of a nearby table on which are displayed seasoning jars of different sizes.
What's this? <color=#fb9259>Two identical jars</color> of seasoning?
You pick them up and open one of them. Inside the jar are fine white crystals, probably table sugar.
Inside the other jar are also white crystals, finer than those in the first jar, but the substance doesn't smell like a seasoning.
You produce an evidence bag and shake some of the substance into the bag.

speaker: Police Officer A
content: Special representative...
You said try not to touch anything.
I tried, but without success.
You've inspected the dining table. The chalk outline, water stains, a flower arrangement, wine bottles, and cartons of cigarettes... these are things left on the table.
To the right and near the top of the chalk outline is an open box of cigars lying next to a gray <color=#fb9259>cigar cutter</color>, which is attached to an expensive-looking leather string.

There's a small pile of broken glass lying not far away from the edge of the carpet. At the time, Mr. Golstoy, weak and losing consciousness, must have thrown the glass against the wall and shattered it.
Although the glass was shattered and it had been empty when Mr. Golstoy threw it, the police managed to detect in a few drops of liquid what might have been the drug that killed Mr. Golstoy.
This piece of evidence might have led the police to believe that the maid was the culprit...
Drug poisoning?
You notice the whiskey bottle beside the dining table. Less than one third is left in the bottle. Mr. Golstoy must have been in the habit of using a drink or two every now and again.
As you reach out, you bump against the table, which wobbles with a grating noise. The picture frame falls face-down on the table.
Hmm?
A shabby table in a rich household... That's strange.

speaker: Police Officer B
content: Sir, look where you're putting your feet! Be careful not to break anything. Please don't make trouble for us.
female_content: Miss, look where you're putting your feet! Be careful not to break anything. Please don't make trouble for us.

content: The carpet in the dining hall is a light color， seemingly to create a nice atmosphere for the diners.
But there are patches that look sticky and stiffened, courtesy of some repulsive liquid.
You gauge the distances, trying to figure out how the liquid landed on the carpet. And then you come upon a patch with some strange stains on it when you get near the midsection of the dining table.
It's so far away... The liquid couldn't have landed here.
You cut the stiffened patch off the carpet with a pair of scissors and bring it to your nose.
You smell a hint of artificial essence mixed with something that is hard to put into words. You sigh when you realize what it might be.
Still going at it like a young stallion?

You take a final look at the stained piece of material before putting it in an evidence bag, which you'll give to Nightingale. She'll order a test run on it and report the results back to you as soon as they're available.
Having inspected the scene, you pick up the fallen picture frame and replace it.

The victim started his meal at around eight o'clock. By then, the hard-working maids had cleaned the dining hall inside out.
As your eyes sweep around the hall, you catch sight of a nearby table on which are displayed seasoning jars of different sizes.
What's this? <color=#fb9259>Two identical jars</color> of seasoning?
You pick them up and open one of them. Inside the jar are fine white crystals, probably table sugar.
Inside the other jar are also white crystals, finer than those in the first jar, but the substance doesn't smell like a seasoning.
You produce an evidence bag and shake some of the substance into the bag.

speaker: Police Officer A
content: Special representative...
You said try not to touch anything.
I tried, but without success.
You've inspected the dining table. The chalk outline, water stains, a flower arrangement, wine bottles, and cartons of cigarettes... these are things left on the table.
To the right and near the top of the chalk outline is an open box of cigars lying next to a gray <color=#fb9259>cigar cutter</color>, which is attached to an expensive-looking leather string.

There's a small pile of broken glass lying not far away from the edge of the carpet. At the time, Mr. Golstoy, weak and losing consciousness, must have thrown the glass against the wall and shattered it.
Although the glass was shattered and it had been empty when Mr. Golstoy threw it, the police managed to detect in a few drops of liquid what might have been the drug that killed Mr. Golstoy.
This piece of evidence might have led the police to believe that the maid was the culprit...
Drug poisoning?
You notice the whiskey bottle beside the dining table. Less than one third is left in the bottle. Mr. Golstoy must have been in the habit of using a drink or two every now and again.
As you reach out, you bump against the table, which wobbles with a grating noise. The picture frame falls face-down on the table.
Hmm?
A shabby table in a rich household... That's strange.

speaker: Police Officer B
content: Sir, look where you're putting your feet! Be careful not to break anything. Please don't make trouble for us.
female_content: Miss, look where you're putting your feet! Be careful not to break anything. Please don't make trouble for us.

content: The carpet in the dining hall is a light color， seemingly to create a nice atmosphere for the diners.
But there are patches that look sticky and stiffened, courtesy of some repulsive liquid.
You gauge the distances, trying to figure out how the liquid landed on the carpet. And then you come upon a patch with some strange stains on it when you get near the midsection of the dining table.
It's so far away... The liquid couldn't have landed here.
You cut the stiffened patch off the carpet with a pair of scissors and bring it to your nose.
You smell a hint of artificial essence mixed with something that is hard to put into words. You sigh when you realize what it might be.
Still going at it like a young stallion?

You take a final look at the stained piece of material before putting it in an evidence bag, which you'll give to Nightingale. She'll order a test run on it and report the results back to you as soon as they're available.
Having inspected the scene, you pick up the fallen picture frame and replace it.

In the picture, Mr. and Mrs. Golstoy are holding hands, like an affectionate couple do. And beside Mr. Golstoy stands the third member of the family.
I remember him. He's Golstoy Junior, right?

speaker: Police Officer A
content: Yes. But his birth mother isn't the current Mrs. Golstoy.

speaker: Police Officer B
content: I heard it's a difficult birth, and there's fetal hypoxia. Golstoy Junior was born with mental disabilities, and his birth mother died in childbirth. He is an adult now, but there's something not quite right here.
The officer indicates what's wrong with Golstoy Junior by tapping his finger on the side of his own head.
I see...

speaker: Police Officer B
content: Women came and went as Mr. Golstoy strove for a healthy heir. God knows how many Mrs. Golstoys have come before the current one!
The other officer gives the arm of his partner a tug. He probably thinks that his partner is being flippant and talking too much.
Thank you for telling me this.
You nod at the police officers and come to the door of the room where the maid is kept. Looking through the window, you see her sitting in a chair.
She keeps fiddling with the edge of her apron, looking so high-strung that it's almost painful to watch.
Hello...
You knock on the door. Like a startled rabbit, she whips around in her seat, lips trembling. When she sees you standing outside the door, she jumps to her feet.

speaker: Maid
content: S-sorry, sir.
female_content: S-sorry, miss.

speaker: Maid
content: I... I'm here. What can I do for you?
No need to worry. I just want to ask you a few questions.

speaker: Maid
content: Are you... are you here to prove my innocence?
The law and evidence will prove it, if you really are innocent, that is.

speaker: Maid
content: You're the first person who has ever shown any interest in hearing my side of the story...
I hope you can answer my questions honestly, miss.

speaker: Maid
content: Rita, you can call me Rita, sir.
female_content: Rita, you can call me Rita, miss.

content: Rita, did you spike Mr. Golstoy's whisky?

speaker: Rita
content: I... I did. But I did it because...
Rita clasps her hands together in front of her chest, as if in prayer, eager to explain herself.

speaker: Rita
content: Mr. Golstoy was not feeling well. He complained of widespread body aches. It was an old illness. I was the one handling his medicines. But this particular medicine was too bitter, so Mr. Golstoy was not very willing to take it.

speaker: Rita
content: Mrs. Golstoy, she told me to dissolve the medicine in alcohol and let Mr. Golstoy drink it. That's why I did it.
In any case, it's wrong to let a patient take medicine with alcohol.

speaker: Rita
content: I... I didn't know you're not supposed to mix medicine with alcohol. I just followed Mrs. Golstoy's order.

speaker: Rita
content: This new Mrs. Golstoy is quite overbearing. We're all kind of scared of her. We do whatever she tells us.
New Mrs. Golstoy?

speaker: Rita
content: Yes, she moved in only five months ago.

speaker: Rita
content: Sir, I dared not make any attempt on Mr. Golstoy's life, not in a million years. I'm just a nobody at the bottom of the pile, as insignificant as a creepy-crawly...
female_content: Miss, I dared not make any attempt on Mr. Golstoy's life, not in a million years. I'm just a nobody at the bottom of the pile, as insignificant as a creepy-crawly...

content: Rest assured, neither money nor someone's... special power can tip Lady Justice's scales in their favor.

speaker: Rita
content: A-are you telling me that I can trust you, sir?
female_content: A-are you telling me that I can trust you, miss?

content: Rita's mouth tightens into a thin line, and the outer edges of her eyes turn downward. She reaches out and puts her hand on the small window.
Miss Rita, all I can say is I'm at the service of law and morality.
The look in her eyes turns solemn. Before you can say anything more, someone darts in to stand between you and the door.
Bad person? You... bad person?

speaker: Police Officer A
content: Sorry. He burst in, and we didn't dare stop him.
The unexpected visitor has dull, empty eyes that somehow chill you. His clothes are disheveled but evidently made of fine material.
You recognize him: Mr. Golstoy's son, Golstoy Junior. No wonder the police officers didn't dare to stop him.
I don't think I'm a bad person, Master Golstoy.
Sorry about your father... My condolences.
If you have anything you want to share with me, please do so...

speaker: Golstoy Junior
content: Bad... Bad person hits me, shouts at me, lets... lets the rat bite my fingers... Bad person…
Who is this bad person? Who hits you and shouts at you?
You don't want your questions to stress the young man out, so you soften your tone.
The young man seems to be pondering your questions, remembering. He is murmuring, eyes downcast and unfocused, hands on the head.

speaker: Golstoy Junior
content: It hurts, it hurts... the rat bites my fingers... it hurts...

speaker: Golstoy Junior
content: Rita... Rita doesn't let the rat bite my fingers...

speaker: Golstoy Junior
content: She gives me milk. She is a good person.

speaker: Golstoy Junior
content: She heats milk, hot milk for me, for... for Daddy.

speaker: Rita
content: Master!
She growls at the young man, her voice uncharacteristically stern. You and Golstoy Junior turn to her.

speaker: Rita
content: Sorry, sir. I'm also the one who takes care of Master Golstoy in his daily life.
female_content: Sorry, miss. I'm also the one who takes care of Master Golstoy in his daily life.

speaker: Rita
content: I'm locked up, and there are so many strangers around. He must be scared. Please forgive both of us...
It's okay. Innocent people tend to tell the truth. I'd like to talk some more with him.

speaker: Rita
content: But, um, he's scared. He can't speak clearly now. Please let him go back and rest.
Rita's comforting words seem to have calmed Golstoy Junior down. He looks at you, and then at Rita, before following the officer out of the dining hall.
Having gathered the information you need, you leave the property. As you drive out, you see another black sedan. Then one of the opaque rear windows is rolled down.
The man in the back seat smiles at you.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Chief, are you going to represent Miss Rita?
I could ask for a certificate allowing me to represent the defender.
But I don't think that's the right thing to do.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: You should use whatever tool at your disposal to get what you want.
Mr. Fox shrugs, as if he has just told you something mundane.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Of course, I don't mind you watching me killing it in court as a spectator.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Chief, thank you for your understanding. See you around.
See you. My understanding doesn't come free.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: I can't wait.
The next day...

Eastside's supreme court. To protect the privacy of the Golstoy family, one of the noble families in Eastside, the trial is not being held in open court. You, as a special representative, are now sitting in the far corner of the spectator area.
Mrs. Golstoy and Mr. Fox are sitting at the plaintiff's table, which seems better illuminated than the defendant's table.

Rita, the poor maid, is at the defendant's table, uneasy and troubled, the way she was the last time you saw her, sitting in that chair in that cramped room, a room in which she has lived and to which she has been confined.

No one wanted to represent her. In a humanitarian gesture, the court appointed a lawyer to represent her. Now, the lawyer is turning the pages of a document, looking as if he's got nothing better to do.
He has sighed five times in three minutes.

speaker: Judge
content: Eastside's supreme court. We now will begin the case of the Golstoy manor.
The judge pounds the gavel. The air in the room is heavy with tension, and everyone is perceptibly on edge, except for Fox.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Allow me to recapitulate on this case.
Fox stands up, adjusts his glasses, and casts a glance in your direction.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Mr. Golstoy died two days ago in the dining hall of his manor. According to the autopsy report, Mr. Golstoy suffered no traumas or fatal injuries, but his blood pH was off the charts, a clear sign of acidosis.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: He also suffered a cardiac arrest, so after considering all the factors, the forensic experts determined the cause of death as acidic drug-induced acute toxicity.
Mr. Fox shows the room the autopsy report, on which a conspicuous red stamp proclaims the authenticity of the report.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: We have good reason to suspect you, Miss Rita. It had always been you who handled Mr. Golstoy's medicine. If anyone had the opportunity to tamper with his medicine, it was you.
Fox gives a slight nod and puts on a vulpine smile, delivering his conclusion with finality.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: In conclusion, you, Miss Rita, murdered Mr. Golstoy.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Miss Rita, you said you're as insignificant as a creepy-crawly...

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: But are you a harmless earthworm, or a poisonous centipede that bites?
Miss Rita turns ashen. She opens her mouth to say something, but nothing comes out.

speaker: Defendant's Lawyer
content: She can't benefit from the death of her employer.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: There isn't always a logical reason for such behavior. Humans are cruel creatures... It's a good thing that we have lawyers. We exist to get to the bottom of a case and bring the culprit to justice.
Fox turns to the judge and asks to call the first witness.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: To prove that Miss Rita had the chance to poison her employer and did take advantage of the chance, I'd like to call one of Miss Rita's colleagues to the stand.
A girl in a uniform similar to Rita's approaches the witness stand, casting nervous looks at Fox.

speaker: Maid A
content: H-hi, everyone...

speaker: Maid A
content: I had nothing to do with it, really... There's nothing special about the foods Mr. Golstoy had that day, just the usual, and what Mr. Golstoy would eat was decided beforehand.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Miss, you needn't worry. Just tell us what you know.

speaker: Maid A
content: But... But I... I...
The maid on the stand stammers, eyes blinking. Finally, she hangs her head and resumes giving testimony. She sounds as if she's talking to herself.

speaker: Maid A
content: I... I'm not entirely sure, but I think I saw Rita pour some powder into Mr. Golstoy's drink. We did the dishes together after breakfast that day.

speaker: Maid A
content: And the night before, I also saw her add something to the milk she was heating in the dining hall. It was also some kind of powder, I think...

speaker: Maid A
content: Later that night, it was in Mr. Golstoy's bedroom that I saw a milk glass, and I took it outside.

speaker: Rita
content: It's sugar. I added sugar to the milk!

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Admit it, Miss Rita! You didn't succeed with the milk, so the next day, you spiked the drink.
Rita's clenched fists are shaking. She can't think of anything else to defend herself.
This may not be the case.
You rise to your feet. Fox narrows his eyes at you, staring at you as if you were a prey.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: This is...?

speaker: Defendant's Lawyer
content: Oh, he's a special representative sent by the authorities, but I don't know why they sent him…
female_content: Oh, she's a special representative sent by the authorities, but I don't know why they sent her...

content: I'm a special representative from the City Council. Some aspects of this case may fall within the City Council's jurisdiction, so I was sent down here to take care of them.
In light of what's happened, I wish to argue the case with this... lawyer.

speaker: Judge
content: ...Go ahead then, special representative from the City Council.

speaker: Judge
content: But next time, please follow the normal procedure if you wish to speak. Now, please come to the witness stand, sir.
female_content: But next time, please follow the normal procedure if you wish to speak. Now, please come to the witness stand, miss.

content: You make to take the witness stand, but Fox comes up to you.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: It didn't surprise me to see you here, but I didn't expect that you'd take the stand.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Am I supposed to take it as a challenge?
Fox chuckles. You seem to glimpse a hint of craziness in his reddish eyes.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Haha, very well, very well... I used my power against you in our last encounter, and it took a great toll on my mind. I don't think I'll be able to use my power again any time soon.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: But that's for the better. Since I can't use my power, there's no reason for you to use the shackles.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: This way, we can fight it out on a level playing field. I accept your challenge. May the best person win!

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: It's been so long since I felt so...
Fox doesn't finish his sentence. He looks at you for a long while before stepping aside to let you go up to the witness stand.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Tell us your theory then, sir.
female_content: Tell us your theory then, miss.

content: You can sense that everyone in the room is looking at you. There are appraising looks, grateful looks, distrustful looks, and looks of anticipation. You must control the whole situation here and now.
As a special representative, I had the opportunity to look around the dining hall of the Golstoy manor and to ask a few persons. And I found something interesting.
test
test
test
test
test
test
You show the room the powder sample you collected in the kitchen and the lab report provided by Nightingale.
I had the powder in the jar tested. It was indeed the medicine for treating Mr. Golstoy's pains and other symptoms. It comes in white fine grains, very much like table sugar.

Putting two similar-looking substances in two similar jars on the same table, one is a drug, the other is table sugar... The cook and others in the manor wouldn't have allowed it, right? Even if it'd make it convenient to administer the medicine.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: But Miss Rita was in charge of the dining hall and she could decide where to put the jar. Isn't this proof that she had the chance to get her employer overdosed at any time?
I don't think it's Miss Rita who decided to put it there.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Who do you think was behind it then, sir?
female_content: Who do you think was behind it then, miss?

content: There was only one person in the manor who could do it. If this person wanted this jar of potentially dangerous substance placed there, no one else would say no.
Am I right, Mrs. Golstoy?

speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
content: Hmm?

speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
content: Are you saying I put it there?
Your mention of her name surprises Mrs. Golstoy.

speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
content: Are you joking?
If you ordered that something be put somewhere, no one would dare to disobey you.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: It doesn't make sense. You said it yourself. Someone could have consumed it by accident. Why would Mrs. Golstoy put herself in danger?
It's an order from the employer; the servants had to obey. There wasn't much they could do other than be careful not to use the wrong jar.
As for why Mrs. Golstoy did that, I guess it's because the medicine would be easier to access that way, and it would be easier for her to pin it on someone else.

speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
content: Are you accusing me of killing my husband?

speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
content: Nonsense!

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Sir, have you given the submitted case file a close reading?
female_content: Miss, have you given the submitted case file a close reading?

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Mrs. Golstoy was not in the dining hall at the time of her husband's death. She had finished eating and left, and she had even given her husband a kiss before she left.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Please enlighten us on how Mrs. Golstoy could possibly manage to poison her husband.
Mr. Fox, is the autopsy report... reliable?

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: ...Are you questioning the credibility of the best forensic experts in Eastside?
For the sake of justice and the truth, we must exhaust all possible avenues. Questioning the credibility of authorities should be one of them.
Fox chuckles, adjusting his glasses.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: I'm glad you remember something I said. But the reliability of the report has no bearing on this case, because there's no doubt that Mr. Golstoy was poisoned.
I beg to differ. The reliability of the report is of the essence here. Because I think Mr. Golstoy died of acidic drug-induced chronic toxicity, not acute toxicity.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: What difference does it make?

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Chronic toxicity can result from long-term consumption of higher-than-recommended doses of a certain drug. Miss Rita also had the opportunity to do this to Mr. Golstoy.
That's true. Miss Rita did have the opportunity.
But I've learned from Miss Rita that it was only recently that Mr. Golstoy decided to take the medicine for widespread body aches.
If it had been acute toxicity, Mr. Golstoy would have died sooner. If it had been chronic toxicity caused by this particular medicine, it would've taken longer for it to kill him.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: What's your point? According to your theory, Mrs. Golstoy should be in the clear. She couldn't have possibly gotten Mr. Golstoy to consume a medicine over a long period of time.
test
test
test
test
test
test
test
I found something on the dining-hall carpet. I had, um, one of my guys run a test on it to determine the components. For easier understanding, I'll use their commonly used names.
The mixture contains a personal lubricant and a bodily fluid. I'm sure you know what bodily fluid I'm referring to here.
Mrs. Golstoy flushes red at your words. She's been holding her head high, but now, out of embarrassment, she looks away quickly.
And it also contains some sort of acidic drug powder and medicated oil made from the acidic drug powder.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Sir, you may have accidentally revealed someone's big secret.
female_content: Miss, you may have accidentally revealed someone's big secret.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: This might lead to another trial.

Cough, cough... My point is, isn't it possible that Mrs. Golstoy might have found a way to get Mr. Golstoy to absorb a high dose of the medicine on a daily basis while she was being intimate with him?
The table in the dining hall squealed loudly if you so much as touched it. I bet it must have been used quite a lot.
A couple of weeks, a month... that's enough time for chronic toxicity to kill a person.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Sir, that's a very unusual angle, very unusual indeed.
female_content: Miss, that's a very unusual angle, very unusual indeed.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: But that still doesn't answer Mrs. Golstoy's question. Why would she want to kill her husband?

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Of course, you can take a page from my book and chalk it up to the dark side of human nature that predisposes human beings to evil deeds.
She might've acted out of self-interest, but that doesn't mean she's evil by nature.
Mr. Golstoy's first wife bore him only one heir, and this heir is mentally challenged. Any subsequent Mrs. Golstoy would have to bear him a healthy heir to secure her future in the Golstoy manor.
But physically, it might have become impossible for Mr. Golstoy to get his latest wife pregnant.
Mrs. Golstoy lived in constant fear of being deserted by her husband. On the other hand, a mentally handicapped kid was much easier to control.
Mrs. Golstoy lowers her head. You can't see her expression, but you notice how the brim of her hat trembles with her body.
You breathe a sigh, your eyes still on Mrs. Golstoy, half expecting to hear the sound of the judge's gavel.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Neat deduction, sir.
female_content: Neat deduction, miss.

content: Clapping his hands, Mr. Fox leaves the plaintiff's table and goes over to stand before you.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Unfortunately, your deduction is flawed, from the very beginning.
You can't believe what you've just heard. Standing on the step behind the witness stand, you look down at Fox and catch glimpses of a shiny bead on his tongue as he talks.
At the plaintiff's table, Mrs. Golstoy looks up and smiles at you, her delicate face without a trace of panic.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Your entire argument, including the part about the motive, is based on my client being Mrs. Golstoy.
What do you mean?

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Legally speaking, my client, the Mrs. Golstoy you talked about, has no connection whatsoever with Mr. Golstoy.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: She asked me not to reveal this secret, unless it's absolutely necessary.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Because she was worried that if the secret was out, she would lose the right to take care of Golstoy Junior. What a kind-hearted lady she is.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Sir, Mrs. Golstoy has nothing to gain from Mr. Golstoy's death at all. According to the law, Mrs. Golstoy won't get anything out of all this, not even a dime.
female_content: Miss, Mrs. Golstoy has nothing to gain from Mr. Golstoy's death at all. According to the law, Mrs. Golstoy won't get anything out of all this, not even a dime.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: The same can't be said for Miss Rita...
Fox changes his target and starts attacking Miss Rita, but he is still looking at you.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: As far as I know, you and Golstoy Junior are very close, right?

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: I believe that we should always consider the worst-case scenario when it comes to human nature...

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: On the one hand, we have a mother who doesn't have the law on her side. On the other hand, we have a young lady on whom a gullible heir to a large fortune relies.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: For this young lady, the only stumbling block was the patriarch of the family. Who do you think would control the manor if she removed the stumbling block and married the heir?
Miss Rita finally rises to her feet, tears welling up in her eyes, and starts shouting.

speaker: Rita
content: If... if you all think I did it, so be it.

speaker: Rita
content: But please don't leave Master Golstoy with Mrs. Golstoy.

speaker: Rita
content: He'll be... be tortured to death if he falls into their hands.

speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
content: Shut up. You're twisting the facts. Torture? Do you have proof?!

speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
content: In any case, nobody is gonna believe the words of those who can't prove their own innocence.

Chief, Sinner Poffy's Emotion Test results came back normal. Her stats are at a stable, above-average level. Her social skills, cognitive function, and values all meet our standards for an ordinary person.
Miss Rita, are you bringing another charge against Mrs. Golstoy?
Taken aback by the idea, Rita is lost for words.

speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
content: What's the point of listening to what a murderer has to say? Let's...

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Let her finish.
Mr. Fox interrupts his client. His voice is deep but sounds somewhat irritated.
Mr. Fox knows what Rita has to say might hurt his client's case, but he still wants to hear it. For a second, your shackles stir. You sense a slight change in the psyche of the Sinner.
As if realizing he's spoken out of turn, Fox clears his throat and makes a gesture at Mrs. Golstoy that's meant to comfort her.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: There's nothing you can say that will change the indisputable fact, but we're kind, so go ahead and say your piece.
Miss Rita is clutching the hem of her dress, working up the courage.
Miss Rita's shaky voice ricochets off the walls of the spacious courtroom, echoing ever so slightly.

speaker: Rita
content: <size=32>Mr. Golstoy didn't like Master Golstoy, never treated him as a son. He hit Master Golstoy, shouted at him. He forbade him from eating at the same table, and even ordered him around like a servant. It had been like this ever since I came to the manor.</size>

speaker: Rita
content: Later on, I started bringing heated milk to Master Golstoy every night. I kept this from the others. If they... they saw Master Golstoy drinking milk in the dining hall, they'd take the milk away.

speaker: Rita
content: Mrs. Golstoy can't be trusted to take good care of Master Golstoy.

speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
content: That's funny. Why would I steal food from a dim-witted kid?

speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
content: Besides, it's Mr. Golstoy who did that to him. What are you blaming me for?
Sometimes, silence is complicity, Mrs. Golstoy.
Golstoy Junior might have difficulty expressing himself, but I think it's necessary to give him a chance to speak his mind.

speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
content: You brought that kid here?!
In a moment of panic, Mrs. Golstoy, forgetting her manners, stands up, leaves the plaintiff's table, and points a finger at you.

speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
content: He's, um, not right in the head. His words can't be taken seriously.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: If that's the case, then we have nothing to worry about.
Fox returns to the plaintiff's table and places a hand on Mrs. Golstoy's shoulder. Mrs. Golstoy sits back down.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Let's give the floor to Golstoy Junior then. Everyone... everyone has a right to justice.
You know that Golstoy Junior, concerned about his friend Rita, has followed her to the court in secret.
He takes tentative steps, but every time he gets to the front, he becomes scared and runs back to hide behind Rita.
Don't be afraid.
Tell us what you know.

speaker: Golstoy Junior
content: I... I don't know... anything.

speaker: Golstoy Junior
content: Bad person hits me. The rat, rat, gray rat, it bites me...

speaker: Golstoy Junior
content: I'm not a bad boy. Don't let the gray rat bite me. It hurts... I'm not a bad boy, not a bad boy...

speaker: Golstoy Junior
content: Mommy, Mommy... It hurts, Mommy.

speaker: Dignified Lady
content: You never listen to me. You failed to do what you were told. You're a bad kid.

speaker: Dignified Lady
content: You're a bad kid. You deserve to be punished.

speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
content: I-I never laid a finger on you.

speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
content: Your father beat you, only because you didn't listen to him. I told you not to be naughty.

speaker: Golstoy Junior
content: You... you let the rat bite me.

speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
content: There's no rat in the manor!
With his elbows on the table, Fox listens attentively, wearing a frown on his face.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Master Golstoy, do you have evidence to back up what you've just said?

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: <size=32>If you do... then we shall go to hell together.</size>
Fox makes the remark in a light tone, as if it's directed at himself.

speaker: Rita
content: He must have. I often found bruises on him. We kept medicated oil at hand, and applied it on him every so often.
You walk over to the teenager and gently roll up his sleeve.
His arm is marked by faded bruises, a sign that he's been harmed before.

speaker: Golstoy Junior
content: The rat... bites my fingers... It hurts...

speaker: Haggard Woman
content: Thank you... Thank you...

speaker: Haggard Woman
content: Why thank you? Ah, because you showed us that he's a bad kid.

speaker: Haggard Man
content: You were right. The law is fair and just... He never listens to us, and he will never become a good kid.

speaker: Haggard Man
content: You won the case, which means our kid really is a bad seed. He has to be punished, has to atone for his sins... We all have sinned! That's why we've brought you here.

speaker: Haggard Woman
content: His wounds are proof of his sins, a punishment he deserves.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: No... You got it all wrong...

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: I was just... just trying to uphold justice. You got it all wrong...

speaker: Haggard Woman
content: He should go to hell.

speaker: Haggard Man
content: Yes, we should go to hell too.

speaker: Haggard Woman
content: Thank you, sir, thank you for letting us see the truth. Hell awaits us...

speaker: Boy Covered in Scars
content: Goodbye...

The wind whistles past a dilapidated building. In the moonlight, he hears the sound of several heavy objects hitting the hard ground in quick succession. It makes him feel suffocated. And then, he sees the scene of hell and makes for it.

Before he can get close, a gigantic hand grabs him and lifts him higher and higher to the sky until he reaches a place infused with bright light. The light burns him, crushes him, and lets him see the horrifying souls down below.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: <size=32>Argh...</size>

speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
content: Mr. Fox, quit spacing out!

speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
content: And get this over with.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Quiet!
Fox's voice is restrained but renders Mrs. Golstoy speechless. She is wide-eyed with astonishment.
Only you can sense it: Fox has activated his power.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Mrs. Golstoy, you kept it from me.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: You didn't tell me there's child abuse involved in this case!
Fox is still recovering from his last confrontation with you. Activating his power again gives him a splitting headache.

speaker: Mrs. Golstoy
content: I... I didn't abuse the kid...
With great effort, Mr. Fox raises his head and looks in your direction.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Let's put an end to all this.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Hell awaits me.
The atmosphere of the room has taken a sharp turn.
Mrs. Golstoy is no longer her demure self, now there's panic on her face. Restrained by Fox's power, she can do nothing but wait for a verdict to be delivered on her sins.
Golstoy Junior said, "The rat bites his fingers."
Of course there's no rat in the manor. But intellectually, he's just a small kid. We shouldn't take his words literally.
I noticed Mr. Golstoy's cigar cutter on the table in the dining hall. It's gray, and it was attached to a leather string.
You gently pick up Golstoy Junior's fisted hand, and open it. His fingers are dotted with long, thin scars.

Rita heated milk for him at night. No doubt that he stayed in the dining hall to drink it. The cigar cutter was a convenient tool. If someone found out he was hurt, it could be explained away by saying that he must have cut himself by accident.

<size=32>And fingertip wounds are hard to notice. As for why the perpetrator hurt him, my guess is that she wanted to, other than vent her anger, get Golstoy Junior's fingerprint on a document that stated his intention to transfer his inheritance rights.</size>
Mrs. Golstoy jumps to her feet, teeth grinding noisily. She keeps running her hand over her face, trying desperately to say something, to no avail.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: You and I are already deep in the mire. I couldn't care less about what your version of the truth really is.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: You wanted justice, you paid the right price, and I'd get you what you wanted. That's our deal.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: But you kept this child abuse business from me... You crossed a line that you should never have crossed.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: You shouldn't have done what you did to that kid.
Fox closes his eyes, and opens them again to look at you.
Your honor, it won't be difficult to track down the document. It's time to end this trial.
The trial ends. Mrs. Golstoy's scheme has been exposed. She's still shouting that Rita is guilty, but no one in the courtroom believes her.
Rita takes Golstoy Junior back to the Golstoy manor, to the messy dining hall. All the other servants are dismissed. Rita stands in the center of the dining hall, motionless like a statue.

speaker: Rita
content: Master, we're free, we're finally free...

speaker: Golstoy Junior
content: Rita...?

speaker: Rita
content: Hahaha... Hahaha...
Rita, who was all timid and shy in the courtroom, bursts out laughing, a high-pitched, blood-curdling laugh.

speaker: Rita
content: Stupid woman! Hahaha... Even luck was on my side!

speaker: Rita
content: It never occurred to her that your milk contained some of the powdered drug, or that the drink contained some of the medicated oil used for your fingertips.

speaker: Rita
content: That thing... it can kill you if you consume it.

Golstoy Junior stands there dumbfounded. He stares at his friend as her fair skin melts away, giving off the stench of something rotten. The molten skin then starts flowing like slow-moving black slime.
Her innocent, lovely face contorts out of shape, into a terrifying mask.

speaker: Rita
content: Those people, those rich people, they should all die... They have no right, no right at all, to enslave me, to make me their property, to make me feel invisible!

speaker: Golstoy Junior
content: Rita, you're so scary...

speaker: Rita
content: You too!
Rita twists her head around to look at her friend. There's something inhuman about her movements. And then she raises her hand.

speaker: Rita
content: An imbecile like you... You're lucky to have lived so long. You wouldn't have survived long in our household.

speaker: Rita
content: You're no use to me anymore. You never listen to me. Now die!

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: "Stop, Rita."
There's a red flash. Rita freezes, her hand inches from Golstoy Junior.
But her body continues mutating. A husky groan comes forth from deep in her throat, as if she's releasing all her pent-up emotional energy.
The man who's just walked out of the shadow, unsteady on his feet, gives Rita a second order.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: "Leave the manor. End yourself!"
Fox controls Rita, who's now turned into a monster, with his power-infused voice. She moves her hand away from Golstoy Junior slowly and places it on her own chest.
As she strides ahead, she knocks over Golstoy Junior on her path.

speaker: Golstoy Junior
content: Rita, where are you going? Rita, you don't want to play with me anymore?

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: That's not the Rita you know.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Say goodbye to her.
Not trusting his legs to support him, he leans back against the rickety table, which protests irritatingly.
Are you okay?

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Ha, I didn't expect that even with the support of the shackles, it'd still be so taxing on me... I guess I should refrain from using my power on you in the future.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: You knew she was infected with Mania, didn't you?
Yes, I realized that when I first talked to her.
You were not the reason I got involved in the trial; she was. Her M-value was higher than normal.
You pick Golstoy Junior up from the floor, sit him down in one of the chairs, and call the city hall, so that he can be taken care of.
All right then. Mr. Fox, you've assisted the MBCC in handling the murderer and Corruptor in the case of the Eastside Golstoy manor. You'll not be punished for leaving the MBCC without permission.
Mr. Fox chuckles at your words.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Are you abusing your power?
No. If this sort of thing happens again, I won't let you leave the MBCC premises ever again.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Hahaha... Whatever you said. You're the winner.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: I wouldn't have agreed to take on this case if I had learned more details about it.
Really? That's interesting. I guess this case was not quite to your taste then, Mr. Fox. Right?
Is it because there's child abuse involved in this case?
Fox narrows his eyes, and looks you up and down, as if seeing you for the first time.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: You seem to know more about my past than I expected.
I told you I knew a lot about you when we first met. I'm the Chief of the MBCC; it's my job to dig into the past of every detained Sinner.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: Hahaha... You're right, it is because there's child abuse involved in the case. Because of me, a kid, the plaintiff in an abuse case, jumped to his death.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: The sad thing wasn't that I couldn't follow him and meet the same hellish fate, because I had been restrained, but that I gained my ability because of it, an ability that allowed me to stand on the side of justice, albeit a distorted version of it.
You became a Sinner.
Then why did you keep...

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: I needed more sins, more unforgivable sins, so that my final punishment would be more... horrific.
Mr. Fox stands up, his reddish eyes gleaming in the dimness, like those of a predator locking onto its prey.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: I used to think that everything in this world could be manipulated and exploited, and that's why I had won so many victories.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: But I had no peace of mind, until I met you.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: I've been waiting for the person who'll mete out my sentence.

speaker: Mr. Fox
content: If I really am a bad seed, then I hope you'll be the one who sends me down to hell.
In just one night, a stack of complaint letters as thick as half a coin piles up on the desk.

There are all sorts of Sinners in the Bureau. Those who like to play the guitar, those who like to dance, those who like to raise flowers or animals... And usually, you respect their innocuous little hobbies.

But this newcomer Dudu really puts you in a bind. She loves to play the same song on her suona over and over again. At first, everyone was entertained by something new, but after a while, no one can stand it anymore.

You've talked to her several times about this, but she's sly and can't be persuaded. She'll simply agree to your demands and then keep doing what she always does. Recently, there are even signs of her behavior worsening...
