Her blaring suona kept you up all night last night. Judging from these complaints, you weren't the only one.
A burst of footsteps snaps you out of your thoughts. Nightingale has come to tell you that both the venue and Dudu are ready for you.
You shake your head and stand up, taking along the stack of complaints.
Let's go.

speaker: Dudu
content: Hey boss, you're finally here? Sleep well last night?
Dudu starts blabbering eagerly as soon as you sit down across from her.
This little girl is always full of life and sociable, yet there always seems to be some wicked intentions lurking beneath her toothy grin.
She leans forward, observing you carefully.

speaker: Dudu
content: Oh no, the dark circles under your eyes tell me you didn't. In that case... I'll play you a song on my suona to cheer you up? Since you're the boss, I'll give you a 20% discount for listening...

As she speaks, she takes out the incriminating "weapon" as if revealing a treasure, the precious suona that she forbids anyone to touch. Once, when someone touched it out of curiosity, Dudu almost pounced on him in a fit of rage.
No, thanks.

speaker: Dudu
content: Huh? Did I charge you too much? Don't worry, the price is negotiable. A 50% discount, then...
That's enough. Check these out.
You cut her off, and push the stack of complaint letters towards her.
She looks around, then suddenly lowers her voice mysteriously.

speaker: Dudu
content: Cough cough. I'll give you a 50% discount, but don't tell the others. It'll be a secret between us.
She looks at you eagerly, but doesn't get a reply.

speaker: Dudu
content: Uhh... Why aren't you saying anything?
Are you done? Then let's get to the topic.

speaker: Dudu
content: The topic? You're not here to listen to my music?
You don't reply, but just push the complaint letters towards her.
Look at these.
test
test
test
test
test
test
Dudu's gaze follows your hands and lands on the pile of letters. Her eyes widen incredulously.

speaker: Dudu
content: These are...?
You pick out a few at random, clear your throat and start reading them out loud.
"Chief, I haven't been able to shut my eyes for three whole days because of that damn suona. The dark circles under my eyes are so thick that the alarm goes off when the sensors scan my face."
"Chief, I feel like I'm in the countryside again, only the roosters back home don't crow as much as she does."
"I'm going insane. If I hear that song one more time, I'll put poison on her mouthpiece at night. I'll really do it! It's me or the suona... One of us has to go!"
After reading out these complaints, you can't help but worry about everyone's mental health. Dudu's smile fades.
I remember warning you multiple times not to play that song all day and night. If this continues, I'll have no choice but to confiscate your suona.
Sure enough, the words "confiscate your suona" instantly makes her panic and yell at you.

speaker: Dudu
content: Who gives you the right to confiscate my suona?!

speaker: Dudu
content: How is me playing the suona any different from the combat training y'all do? You know what'll happen if I don't practice and get rusty? My livelihood depends on it!

speaker: Dudu
content: Plus, my teacher taught me this piece back in the day. It's the one I play best!

speaker: Dudu
content: I was like this back in the Drifter Camp. I'd go play whenever there was a wedding or funeral, and if there were none, I'd just play by the roadside.

speaker: Dudu
content: Everyone in the Drifter Camp loves hearing me play. The generous ones even give me money. I really don't get why you folks at the Bureau hate it so much.
Her lips tremble, as if she had just suffered a grave injustice.

speaker: Dudu
content: Since y'all find me so annoying, just let me go home! This place cramps my style anyways...
You mean to the Drifter Camp?

speaker: Dudu
content: Of course. Where else?
If I remember correctly, aren't you an Outlander? You couldn't have been in the Drifter Camp for more than a few years.

speaker: Dudu
content: So? The Drifter Camp is the place that truly accepts me. It's my home.
Dudu snorts, unimpressed.

speaker: Dudu
content: So what if I haven't been there that long? I know the Drifter Camp as well as any local!

speaker: Dudu
content: Let me put it this way. Even if you drop me into the Drifter Camp blindfolded, I can tell which street I'm on by the smell alone.
Are you being serious?
Though her tone is calm and convincing, you can't help but wonder if she's mixed the real with the imaginary.

speaker: Dudu
content: Of course I'm being serious!

speaker: Dudu
content: Who's the biggest spender, who you should never cross, which part of the river is best for catching fish, which forest grove is best for a date, who sells the yummiest stinky tofu, whose cat catches the most mice, who's the best matchmaker in the camp... I know the answers to all these questions!
She pauses, her eyes shifting about. Heaven knows what tricks are popping into her head.

speaker: Dudu
content: Hmm... If you don't believe me, I'll give you a consultation for free.
For free? Knowing you, shouldn't you be extorting some sort of fee?
You raise your brows in surprise.

speaker: Dudu
content: Pfft, I make my money from honest work, okay? How can you call it "extortion"... Anyways, back to the subject. I'm doing you a big favor this time. Ask me anything you want. If I can't answer it, I'll swap the syllables of my name back to front!
...But wouldn't that still be Dudu?
Your mouth twitches. You calm yourself down, trying your best not to let her ruin your composure.
This little girl had tricked you many times before, so you're always extra vigilant when dealing with her. Even now, you're keenly aware that she's goading you to ask her about the Drifter Camp.
In that case... It's better to just go along and see what tricks she has up her sleeve.
Then... Did anything major happen in the Drifter Camp recently?

speaker: Dudu
content: Anything major...
Dudu rubs her chin, thinks for a moment, then flashes a confident smile.

speaker: Dudu
content: Of course there has!

speaker: Dudu
content: A goose escaped from the market and chased the blacksmith's youngest son for three miles straight. This trauma has left him with a deep fear of birds, and now he pees his pants at the honk of a goose.

speaker: Dudu
content: The egg seller's daughter plucked a bunch of chicken feathers to make a shuttlecock, but she spooked her family's hens so much that they stopped laying eggs. Her mother beat her up for this.

speaker: Dudu
content: Our building manager's son is getting married next month. He's ecstatic and preparing a huge wedding. I must go and play him a song or two.

speaker: Dudu
content: Ah, there's more! The old lady who lives next door to me hasn't been in the best health. She felt that she didn't have much time left, so she asked me to help arrange her funeral...
Even though it was just a casual question, you can't help but cut off her incessant blabbering. These petty trivialities couldn't be farther from "anything major."
I asked if "anything major" happened. Maybe you can pick some important things to talk about.

speaker: Dudu
content: These things aren't important? They may seem meaningless to you, but for us in the Drifter Camp, these things make up our daily lives.

speaker: Dudu
content: We're not like you. We don't have any lofty ideals. Survival is our only pursuit. So yeah, those things are pretty major to us.
Her stubborn, willful gaze puts you out of words.
...Sorry, you're right. I didn't think of it that way. I shouldn't have said that.
A look of astonishment flashes across her face. She obviously didn't expect you to apologize. After regaining her focus, she rubs her nose and coughs awkwardly.

speaker: Dudu
content: Cough... Okay, okay. I forgive you.
That little episode makes you curious about the source of her news, so you take the lead in breaking the ice.
Where did you get all that news from?

speaker: Dudu
content: Ah, well that requires some technique.
Perhaps you're just imagining it, but you feel that Dudu has become more relaxed and sincere towards you.

speaker: Dudu
content: The best places in the Drifter Camp to get news are: the riverside where ladies wash clothes in the evening, the night market stalls where people grab food after work, the game tables of senior citizens, and the roadside where the Homeless beg.

speaker: Dudu
content: Each of these places has it pros and cons.

speaker: Dudu
content: The laundry ladies aren't very vigilant. They start chatting nonstop whenever they bump into someone, but it's usually just neighborhood gossip that won't interest you.

speaker: Dudu
content: You can get a wider variety of news from where the workers gather. These aren't limited to just neighborhood gossip. After all, they have diverse sources. But these middle-aged men love to brag, so a lot of it is hearsay.

speaker: Dudu
content: As for the elderly, they've lived a long time and have seen a lot, but often their minds are a bit muddled, so it's easy for them to forget the details of past events.

speaker: Dudu
content: The Homeless are everywhere in the Drifter Camp. Nothing escapes their eyes and ears. Getting news from them is often the most efficient choice, and their news is the most accurate. But these guys are very greedy, and will probably try to rip you off.
You listen quietly and intently to Dudu. It seems that she really knows the Drifter Camp like the back of her hand, and has a lot of experience gathering information.

speaker: Dudu
content: So how about it, boss? Now do you believe how well I know the camp?
I believe you.

speaker: Dudu
content: In that case, I have another brilliant idea. Want to hear it?
Sure enough, she can't wait to let the cat out of the bag. This is exactly what you've been waiting for.

speaker: Dudu
content: Why don't you send me to the Drifter Camp for a while to gather news for you?

speaker: Dudu
content: I know that the MBCC is now in contact with the Drifter Camp. You probably need a lot of intelligence. As someone who is intimately familiar with the place and won't raise suspicion from the locals, I'm your best choice.
You listen to her premeditated proposal and smirk.
So after leading me down the garden path, this is what you really wanted to say?
Though a bit annoyed that you didn't take the bait, she continues to push for her cause.

speaker: Dudu
content: Well, that way, not only will I get to keep my suona and livelihood, you also don't have to worry about looking after me, and no one's life will be disturbed. Isn't it a win-win?
…Sorry, the MBCC has no precedent for releasing detained Sinners. We also have dedicated agents for gathering intelligence.

speaker: Dudu
content: What... So it's still a no after all that. I wasted my breath for nothing.
She mumbles quietly to herself, her fawning grin vanishing from her face. But your heart softens upon seeing her so upset.
Though I can't let you go back, I can ask the intelligence agents to regularly share information with you about the camp.

speaker: Dudu
content: For real? Are you being serious? You're not pulling my leg?
Dudu looks at you in surprise, lifting her head as if she has heard something unbelievable.
Of course I'm being serious. I'm not that cold-hearted.
Having gotten an affirmative answer, Dudu beams with joy, her eyes squinting from her fawning smile.

speaker: Dudu
content: Having some information to hear is better than nothing! No wonder you're the Chief of the MBCC! You're so wise and caring towards the masses!

speaker: Dudu
content: What are they?
From today onwards, you must abide by the Bureau's work and rest schedule. You may only play the suona at specified times and places, and you must not disturb other people's rest.
If you violate any of these conditions, the information sharing will cease immediately.
She salutes you goofily with a playful smile.

speaker: Dudu
content: Roger that! Don't worry boss, I promise I'll be good!
You tell Nightingale to take Dudu back. Watching her skip happily behind Nightingale, you finally let out a sigh of relief.
A wave of exhaustion sweeps over you. After reaching a deal with this little troublemaker, you can finally live a few days in peace.
However, you have only enjoyed a few days of hard-earned peace and quiet in the office, and it was once again shattered by a high-decibel shout.
Ch-chief! Something major has happened!
The office door swings open with a "bang." Dudu puts one hand on the door frame, gasping for breath as she tries to speak. Judging from the sweat streaming down her face, she ran all the way here.
Calm down. Tell me slowly what you want to say.
Dudu gathers her breath to talk, but what she says next comes as a complete surprise...

speaker: Dudu
content: Someone from the Drifter Camp has gotten ahold of intelligence about <color=#fb9259>Parma</color>!
Parma?! But I didn't see anything about it in the intelligence agent's report.

speaker: Dudu
content: Pfft, how long has he been there? How can he know as much as I do? To be honest, I only realized it when I was chatting with him today.

speaker: Dudu
content: It's my fault for not realizing it before... Anyway, we need to hurry and go as soon as possible! You'll understand when you get there!
You look at Dudu suspiciously. You can't tell if that rare look of seriousness on her face means she's trying to trick you again, or if she's really figured out something important.
But considering that anything related to Parma is no trivial matter, you'd rather be safe than sorry. You immediately assemble a team to go investigate the Drifter Camp.
Following Dudu's instructions, you lead a team of five to an old residential building in the southeast corner of the Drifter Camp.

You squint at the ivy-covered walls, which are mottled from years of wind and rain. You then glance at the senior citizens outside the building, who are chatting and fanning themselves under the shade. Your expression becomes a bit perplexed.

options: Are you sure this is the place?

content: Dudu nods furiously.

speaker: Dudu
content: A hundred and ten percent! I live right next door!
...Okay.
You nod and begin to give instructions to the guards around you.
You hide in the flower bed over there, and you guard the door. The rest of you, come up with me.

speaker: Dudu
content: Uhh... Well...
Dudu stammers hesitantly. You assume that she's scared, so you pat her on the shoulder.
It's okay, don't be afraid. Just stay behind me when the time comes.

speaker: Dudu
content: Ahhh... Actually... Hey!
Before Dudu can finish her sentence, you start leading the force inside. She has no choice but to stomp her feet and follow you.
You give a look to the guards around you. They aim their guns, kick open the door, and rush inside all in one go.
The moment you break open the door, you get bathed in large swathes of sunlight. Yet the scene before your eyes is totally different from what you had imagined...
Instead of a secret hideout filled with contraband, weapons and black-clad gangsters, it's just a plain old-fashioned home.

The decor is old and plain, but also neat and tidy, as if someone frequently cleans it. The extremely simple layout makes the tiny space feel unusually vast and empty. One can get a sweeping view of the entire home from the door, with absolutely no room to hide.
Your eyes all land on the only living being in the room. Standing alone before the window is...
An old lady?
You and the guards gawk at each other for a while. You then finally turn to Dudu.

speaker: Dudu
content: Hehe... Actually, I wanted to tell you just now that there's no need to make such a big commotion...
Dudu scratches her head, grinning widely.

speaker: Dudu
content: But you were all serious-faced and dispatching everyone here and there, so I couldn't butt in at all.
You take a deep breath.
So the person who you claim has the important information... is her?

speaker: Dudu
content: Yes!

You carefully observe the old lady, who's gazing out the window with blank eyes. She's old and frail, with a lame foot, and doesn't seem to be in her right mind. Even though a bunch of gun-toting strangers just broke into her house, she shows no reaction whatsoever.
You can't connect this common old lady in front of you with Parma at all.
You can't joke about such important things.

speaker: Dudu
content: I'm not joking at all.
She walks over to help the old lady sit down on the bed. You also go over, and watch as Dudu starts to peel an orange from the coffee table.

speaker: Dudu
content: Granny, why did you go to the window again? How many times have I told you not to stand that long? Your legs can't handle it.

speaker: Old Lady
content: ...Who is it? You... I don't know you...
The old lady stares blankly at Dudu for a while. Then, a wary look appears on her face. She slurs her words and has trouble speaking, but Dudu understands her effortlessly.
Dudu lets out a helpless sigh. She stuffs half the orange into her mouth, then puts the other half into the old lady's hand.

speaker: Dudu
content: Don't you remember me? I'm Dudu. I live next door.

speaker: Old Lady
content: You... Pa... ma... Give me back... Pa... ma...
Frowning, you listen to her mumble the word "Pa... ma" over and over again, but you just can't make out what the syllable in the middle is.
Dudu takes a glance at you, then starts to gently question the old lady.

speaker: Dudu
content: You keep saying "Parma, Parma." Who is Parma?

speaker: Old Lady
content: Pa... ma... important...

speaker: Old Lady
content: The old elm tree... climb the tree...

speaker: Dudu
content: ...What?

speaker: Old Lady
content: In the chicken coop...

speaker: Old Lady
content: I still... wait...
Totally befuddled, you cast a puzzled look at Dudu. The old lady suddenly becomes agitated for no reason. Stomping her cane with all her might, she starts to shoo you away.

speaker: Old Lady
content: Get out! You're not welcome here! Leave! Leave!

speaker: Dudu
content: How come you... You're so full of energy. It doesn't seem like anything bad happened... Sigh, okay okay, we're leaving! Quit stomping your cane!
After shooing all of you to the door, she hobbles back to the window, leaving you to face her frail, stooped but stubborn back.

speaker: Dudu
content: I really don't know what there is to look all day...
What did she mean by "elm tree" and "chicken coop?"

speaker: Dudu
content: Who knows? She has some mental problems and can't speak clearly. It seems to be caused by a tumor in her head. She was already like this before I moved here. The last time she was clear-headed was two or three months ago, when she asked me to arrange her funeral after she dies.
Dudu scratches her head, then looks at you as if seeking praise.

speaker: Dudu
content: You heard her, didn't you? I wasn't lying. She really knows about Parma.
But was she really saying "Parma"? I could only make out "pa" at the beginning and "ma" at the end, but the syllable in the middle sounded more like...
You rub your chin and ponder, but get interrupted by Dudu's nervous laughter.

speaker: Dudu
content: Ahaha, boss, your imagination is too wild. Of course she's saying "Parma." What else could she be saying?

speaker: Dudu
content: Let's go see what clues we can find from the elm tree and chicken coop she was talking about...
She pulls your arm and walks out as she speaks, trying to change the subject. Seeing her pompous and guilty reaction, you get a pretty good sense of   what's going on.
After all the trouble just now, you're pretty sure that the delirious old lady has nothing to do with Parma, but you still let Dudu drag you along and continue the investigation.
First, it's a good chance to observe how people live in the Drifter Camp, and second, you want to see what tricks Dudu has up her sleeve.
You send the other team members back to the Bureau, and delve deeper into the Drifter Camp with Dudu on your own.

Dudu first climbs onto an old elm tree in front of the vegetable market and pretends to search around. As you expect, she finds nothing, then scampers away with the excuse of "searching the chicken coop."
While she's gone, you try to strike up conversations with the residents here. Seeing that you came with Dudu, they don't seem to be on guard against you.
Hi, excuse me, do you know Parma?
The blacksmith stops cleaning his furnace and looks at you, puzzled.

speaker: Blacksmith
content: Parma? You mean as in Parmesan cheese?
You're speechless for a moment.
You know... The one that the granny who lives in the southeast corner is always mumbling about...?
The blacksmith seems to have an epiphany and lets out a hearty laugh.

speaker: Blacksmith
content: Oh, so it's "Parma," is it? I could never tell what she was mumbling about. Haha, my ears are no match against you young folks'.

options: Do you know that lady well?

speaker: Blacksmith
content: Oh, I know her all right. She was a well-known shrew in our Drifter Camp back in the day. Even the most vicious gangsters avoided her when they saw her. In a fight, she can curse with the strength of ten people, and yell at you so hard that you get a heart attack. It was terrifying!
This information catches you by surprise. Although you could tell from the old lady's face that she's not a kind and gentle character, you didn't expect her to have such a notorious reputation.
The blacksmith lets out a long sigh, then changes the subject.

speaker: Blacksmith
content: But ever since she got that tumor in her head a few years ago, she's completely lost it. Now she's dazed all day, and can't even take care of herself.

speaker: Blacksmith
content: So now, Dudu does all her cleaning and plumbing. She does all this hard work for free, but still has to endure that crazy woman's tantrums. It's really tough for Dudu.

options: Dudu would do things like that?!

content: You can't help but blurt out your doubt. The blacksmith looks at you long and hard.

speaker: Blacksmith
content: You must've met Dudu not long ago, so you still don't know her well, eh?

speaker: Blacksmith
content: The little tyke's got a lot of bad habits, that's for sure. She's cunning, greedy, annoying, a freeloader, full of bad ideas, and loves to fool others... But she's definitely not a bad or selfish person.

speaker: Blacksmith
content: Didn't that crazy woman's condition worsen over the past two days? Dudu must have been worried after hearing the news, so she hurried back.

speaker: Blacksmith
content: Although Dudu's an Outlander, we all know that she thinks of the Drifter Camp as her home and us as her family. She does all those chores voluntarily, and while she complains, she never stops her actions of care and love. Isn't that what family does?
Really...
The Dudu described by the blacksmith is so different from the Dudu you know. Then... which one is the real her?
As you lower your head to ponder, an energetic voice rings out.

speaker: Dudu
content: Boss! I'm back!

Dudu stands before you with messy hair and chicken feathers all over her body, as if afraid that others won't know where she went. You suppress your laugh as you help pick off the feathers and tidy her hair.
You already know the answer, but you still ask her as a formality.

speaker: Dudu
content: Sigh, what a bummer. I didn't find Parma. Just eggs.
Yet there's no sign of disappointment on her face. She weighs the eggs in her hands a few times, then slips them into her pocket.

speaker: Dudu
content: But it wasn't a wasted trip. I can get an extra meal when we go back.
The little boy who has been curiously listening to you chat stares at the scattered chicken feathers in fear, then shifts his shocked gaze to Dudu.
You suddenly remember that Dudu told you about a poor kid in the camp who got chased by a goose and became terrified of birds. This is probably him.

speaker: Blacksmith's Son
content: You got pecked, too, Dudu?
The little boy asks timidly, but Dudu flashes him a bright smile.

speaker: Dudu
content: How's that possible? This is from my epic battle with it.

speaker: Blacksmith's Son
content: Then did you win?

speaker: Dudu
content: Do you even need to ask? Of course I won!

speaker: Blacksmith's Son
content: You're so cool, Dudu! How did you win?

speaker: Dudu
content: Ta-da! My invincible suona! Whether it's a chicken, duck or goose, one song will scare 'em away!
Dudu proudly takes out her suona, and the little boy looks at her with adoring eyes.

speaker: Blacksmith's Son
content: Wow!

speaker: Dudu
content: Want to hear it?

speaker: Blacksmith's Son
content: Yeah!

speaker: Dudu
content: Then I'll play you a song...

speaker: Blacksmith
content: Stop! We don't want to be extorted again!
Just as Dudu raises her suona to play, the blacksmith stops her in annoyance. Dudu doesn't get angry. She simply puts away her suona and makes a face at the little boy.

speaker: Dudu
content: I'll stop, otherwise your dad will beat me. But I can teach you how to play the suona, so that you don't have to be scared of geese anymore.

speaker: Blacksmith
content: Shush! Stop fooling my kid! I'll really beat you if you don't leave!
The blacksmith starts shooing her away with the rag in his hand. Dudu sticks out her tongue at him, then drags you away.
She pulls you nimbly through the narrow alleys of the Drifter Camp. You gaze at the light and shadows cast upon her hair by the golden afternoon sun, feeling suddenly dazed.
In this moment, she's like a fairy who has strayed into the mortal world, forever lively, free, happy and unrestrained.
Next, you guys come to a vegetable stall.

speaker: Vegetable Seller
content: Parma? Never heard of it.

speaker: Dudu
content: Then can you tell my boss about the old lady who lives alone in the southeast corner?
She takes one look at Dudu and waves her hand impatiently.

speaker: Vegetable Seller
content: I don't care who's with you. Go go go. Don't get in the way of my business.
A grinning Dudu fishes out your wallet from your pocket and generously pulls out a couple of large bills for the seller.

speaker: Dudu
content: Keep the change, ma'am. A few random veggies will do.
Hey...
You reach out in alarm to stop Dudu, but the vegetable seller swiftly grabs the money and stuffs it into her pocket. She flashes you a fawning smile, reversing her attitude completely.

speaker: Vegetable Seller
content: Your boss wants to know about that old hag, right?

speaker: Dudu
content: Yes!
You look at Dudu in exasperation, but she winks at you without any remorse, as if to say, "This is how we do things in the Drifter Camp."

speaker: Vegetable Seller
content: That piece of work, tsk tsk... Back when she was still clear-headed, she'd haggle with me for half an hour for a green onion or two. I was really scared of her.

speaker: Vegetable Seller
content: This must be her karma for being so cruel and callous when she was young. Now she can only die alone.
As she says these unkind words, she shoves a big bag of vegetables into your arms.

speaker: Vegetable Seller
content: That's all I know, boss. Thank you, come again.
However, when you turn to leave, you hear her telling her daughter to cook some extra food for the evening to give to the old lady.
Doesn't the vegetable seller despise the old lady?
You ask Dudu in confusion, but Dudu responds matter-of-factly.

speaker: Dudu
content: Yeah. Everyone in the Drifter Camp despises her. So?
Then why did she ask her daughter to give her food?
Dudu sighs.

speaker: Dudu
content: We can't just watch the old lady starve to death. She's childless and has no one to take care of her to begin with. Now that she's lost her mind, she can't do anything.

speaker: Dudu
content: That's why people like us have to step up and take the responsibility. The vegetable seller would bring her food regularly, while the blacksmith would go to her house every now and then to see if anything needs fixing. As for me, I just help with some cleaning and chores.
...That's why her home is so clean.

speaker: Dudu
content: To tell you the truth, no one likes this kind of thankless work. It's dirty, tiring and unpaid, and sometimes she yells at me for no reason. There are times when my temper flares up and I swear to quit, but then I feel sorry for her again when I see her staring blankly out the window and mumbling to herself.

speaker: Dudu
content: If even we don't take care of her, she'll really end up dead. After all, we're the only ones she can rely on.
Deep in thought, you pace through the narrow alleys of the Drifter Camp with a big bag of vegetables in your arms. The sun overhead has already set.
Although you didn't get any information about Parma today, it was by no means a fruitless trip.
The Drifter Camp you witnessed is completely different from what you had imagined. Even the jabbering girl beside you seems more vivid and adorable now.

The sincerity between the camp residents makes you feel unprecedentedly relaxed. Here, no one has to put on a facade or watch their backs. People can be their truest selves, and express their truest thoughts with the frankest words.
Everyone here is struggling for survival, but they still love life. They are doing their best to live every day.

They despise the old lady, yet voluntarily take care of her. One should not judge someone's nature by what they say, but by what they do. Their plebeian vulgarities cannot conceal their warm and kind hearts.
It's getting late. Let's head back to the Bureau.
Dudu looks at the vegetables in your arms, her eyes shifting about. You wonder what tricks she's come up with this time.

speaker: Dudu
content: Wait a minute! I know!

speaker: Dudu
content: Let's go to one last place! Maybe we'll be able to find something!

The person you're visiting this time is the oldest man in the Drifter Camp. He has lived alone in a remote corner of the camp for many years. People say he's withdrawn and eccentric, and knows many things that others don't.

speaker: Dudu
content: Gramps, it's me, Dudu! Are you surprised?
The old man who answered the door snorts.

speaker: Old Man
content: What's there to be surprised about? Who else besides you would run around all over the place for no reason?

speaker: Dudu
content: Sigh, I haven't seen you for so long. Don't you miss me at all? Look, I brought so much food for you.

As soon as you enter the house, Dudu grabs the vegetables from your hands and puts them on the dining table. After going through the plastic bag, the old man's face finally lightens up, and he nods towards you.

speaker: Old Man
content: I knew a little devil like you would have ulterior motives. Tell me, what do you want from me this time?

speaker: Dudu
content: Hehe... Well, the thing is, my boss has a question for you.
As she says this, Dudu elbows you a few times, hinting for you to speak.
Do you know what is this "Parma" that the old lady from the southeast corner is always mumbling about?
You tiredly repeat this question that you've been asking over and over again all day, but this time, you get a different answer.
The old man looks at you, then at Dudu, then flashes a knowing expression.

speaker: Old Man
content: If you mean the lady with the brain tumor, then what she's saying is <color=#fb9259>"Palama"</color>, not "Parma."

speaker: Dudu
content: What? Palama?!

Dudu cries out in surprise. This is the first time today that you see a look of genuine surprise on her face. You calmly press Dudu's arm to tell her not to get too excited. She quiets down and glances at you guiltily.
Ever since you left the old lady's house, you no longer hold any expectations about investigating Parma. Instead, this "Palama" that appeared out of the blue has piqued your interest.
What could Palama be? A type of homophony? A mysterious person? An important item? Or... a code name the common folk use for a certain event? Whatever it is, it's worth investigating.
Can you tell me more about this "Palama"?

speaker: Old Man
content: So many years have passed in the blink of an eye. I'm probably the only person here who still remembers Palama.
...Remembers? The strange wording makes you frown.

speaker: Old Man
content: There is an abandoned building about three or four hundred meters to the northwest of the Drifter Camp. Palama is inside.

speaker: Dudu
content: The abandoned building that was struck by lightning?
You know it?

speaker: Dudu
content: Of course. It's one of the Drifter Camp's most infamous tragedies... One stormy night many years ago, roaring thunder shook the land, and there was so much lightning that the entire night sky was lit up. The Drifter Camp had never experienced anything like it.

speaker: Dudu
content: Suddenly, a lightning bolt struck the antenna on top of that building, instantly lighting up the whole structure in flames. The fire was so big that it burned for a whole day and night before it got finally put out. They say that many people didn't escape in time and burned to death inside.
The old man continues on from Dudu.

speaker: Old Man
content: Precisely. It became a notorious haunted building ever since. With dozens of wronged souls trapped inside, it'd be strange for it not to be haunted! Many young daredevils have gone to explore it in the middle of the night, but every single one of them ended up fleeing while peeing their pants.

speaker: Old Man
content: They say there's a female ghost dressed in white who wanders through the rooms, weeping and muttering incomprehensible words. Sometimes it's low-pitched sobs, other times it's hysterical screams and wails. It's really eerie.

speaker: Old Man
content: And Palama is inside that building.
After finishing his sentence, the old man shakes his head and goes into another room, leaving you and Dudu in the empty living room.

speaker: Dudu
content: Um... boss... about "Parma," I can explain...
Dudu breaks the silence first. She chuckles awkwardly as she cautiously tugs on your sleeve.
Enough. You think I didn't know that you made up the so-called "Parma intelligence"?

speaker: Dudu
content: Y-you already knew? Then why did you come here with me?

You must have your reasons for wanting to return to the camp so urgently. Now I know it's because you wanted to see the old lady after learning about her worsening condition from the intelligence agent, right? If this is the reason, you could've told me from the start. I would've let you come back.
Dudu's eyes glimmer. She lowers her head in guilt.

speaker: Dudu
content: You guessed it, boss. I made up the story about "Parma" and tricked you into bringing me back here because I was worried about the old lady. But after seeing that she's fine, I wanted to see everyone in the camp who I haven't seen for a long time. I made you run around with me all day, and also spent a lot of your money ...

speaker: Dudu
content: I shouldn't have done this... I'm sorry.
Then can you tell me the truth now? What is Palama, and what's the connection with that abandoned building?
To your surprise, Dudu shakes her head.

speaker: Dudu
content: I've asked many people in the Drifter Camp what "Pa-something-ma" was, but everyone thought it was just the old lady's delusions. In fact, today's the first time that I found out that she's actually saying "Palama."

speaker: Dudu
content: As for what that word means and how it's connected to that building, I really don't have a clue... I'm telling the truth this time! You've got to believe me, boss!
Should we still go to that abandoned building, then?

speaker: Dudu
content: Of course we should. The old lady entrusted me with arranging her funeral. I have to find out what is this "Palama" that she still yearns for despite losing her mind.
Dudu laughs.

speaker: Dudu
content: I can always ask Oak Casket to help realize her unfulfilled wishes after death, but if possible, I still want to clarify this matter when she's still alive.
You bid farewell to the old man and prepare to head northwest to the abandoned building. Before leaving, Dudu scoops out an arm-long green onion from the grocery bag and holds it in front of you.
You look at her incredulously.

speaker: Dudu
content: What if we run into danger? I have my suona with me, so I'm not afraid, but you don't have any handy weapons. Make do with this. Something is better than nothing.
As she says this, she swings the green onion a couple of times like a club. The water sprinkled on it by the vegetable seller splashes all over your face.
You wipe your face and look at the serious-faced Dudu in exasperation.
Even if those ghost stories, which are probably made up to scare people, are real, a green onion is totally useless as a weapon...

speaker: Dudu
content: This ghastly place looks scary enough on the outside, but it turns out to be even scarier on the inside! And it's so dark! I can't even see the way in front of me!

speaker: Dudu
content: By the way, dozens of people have died here... (Shivers) No wonder I feel a chill down my spine.

speaker: Dudu
content: Oh Amitabha, blessed Buddha, please have mercy on us. Ladies and gents, we're just passing by. We don't want to disturb you. Just pretend that we don't exist, and keep sleeping and wandering and chatting as you would... As long as you don't bump into us.

speaker: Dudu
content: In short, let's just mind our own business. Please don't pick on us. After we leave, we'll make sure to burn some extra joss money and play a few extra songs for y'all. I'm a professional at this, satisfaction guaranteed...
Dudu's mouth hasn't stopped blabbering for a moment since entering the building. You know it's because she's nervous.
She's a bit short on breath, and you suddenly remember from her file that she's claustrophobic. You decide to speak up and distract her by chatting.

options: The things you just said are quite interesting.

content: Where did you learn it from?

speaker: Dudu
content: ...Hmm? Oh, that. I learned it from my teacher. All my skills, including my sharp tongue, come from his teachings.

speaker: Dudu
content: There's no one in this world who's more interesting and remarkable than him. Without him, I really don't know what I'd be like now.
Dudu calms down a lot at the mention of her teacher. You can even detect a hint of a smile and nostalgia in her voice.

speaker: Dudu
content: Boss, you know that I'm from the Outland. The place where I was born had long been cut off from various supplies. In order to survive, my teacher took me to DisCity.

speaker: Dudu
content: Along the way, we cobbled together a theatrical troupe with other drifters, and made a living by forcing passers-by to watch us perform.

speaker: Dudu
content: Those wandering days were really hard. We had nowhere to go at night, and often had to sleep in graveyards. But I was little, and staying in those places made me think of all the ghost stories I had heard about. I was so scared that I'd shake all over and not sleep a wink.

speaker: Dudu
content: But my teacher told me that death is not the end. It's simply a process that everyone must go through. So ghosts, graveyards, and corpses are nothing to be scared of. To help me overcome my fear, he taught me the tune I always play.

speaker: Dudu
content: He said it's the Song of the Phoenix. The phoenix is a symbol of reincarnation, representing both life and death. Hence, it can be played for the living as well as the dead.
Dudu's vivid description makes you visualize the scene of her as a child, hugging her knees and trembling in fear. You can't help but want to tease her again.
So you were scared of ghosts when you were a child, but not anymore?
Dudu laughs.

speaker: Dudu
content: Not anymore.

speaker: Dudu
content: You know, boss? In all the years we've traveled, we've met all sorts of people.

speaker: Dudu
content: People who don't dare take responsibility for the sins they've committed, and beg the gods for forgiveness instead; people who pretend to be messiahs, and deceive others in the name of the gods; people who only have their own interests in mind, and don't treat others as human beings...

speaker: Dudu
content: People are the only ones who harm other people. They are way scarier than any ghosts.
Her tone is light and brisk as she says this, but as the listener, you can't help but feel heavy.
What about your teacher? How is he?
You hear Dudu halt her footsteps in the darkness. She stays silent for a while before speaking again.

speaker: Dudu
content: He died.
What...

speaker: Dudu
content: DisCity was not the city of hope that my teacher had envisioned. We came here after so much tribulation, only to run into Syndicate's most turbulent times. Once, during a gang war, someone used a mania weapon.

speaker: Dudu
content: Everyone got infected except me. I was spared only because my teacher hid me in the cellar. But in that dark cellar, I could still hear... all the terrible noises outside.
That horrible experience might be the source of her claustrophobia.
I'm sorry. I shouldn't have brought up those bad memories...

speaker: Dudu
content: ...It's fine. They're all in the past.

speaker: Dudu
content: I buried them and played them that tune. They must have all gone to a better place, and our shared memories will forever remain in my heart.

speaker: Dudu
content: So I'm... not sad. I just miss them a bit every once in a while.
The dark clouds outside the window dissipate, revealing the moon. The pale moonlight shines into the dark corridor, and also upon your faces and shoulders.

speaker: Dudu
content: ...But I've never told anyone about these things. You're not allowed to laugh at me or tell anyone else!
Dudu sniffles and looks at you with some embarrassment. You suddenly realize that the little girl in front of you might be much tougher than you thought.
You smile at her reassuringly.
Don't worry. It'll be our little secret.

speaker: Dudu
content: Then it's a deal! As the great MBCC Chief, you're not allowed to break your promise! Now that the moon is out and we can see the way clearly, let's move forward quickly...
Dudu's liveliness has returned to her, but after only two steps, she gasps as if she's found something, and squats down to stare at the floor.

speaker: Dudu
content: Boss! Come see this, quick!

You go over quickly and look in the direction of her finger. You see a few faint clusters of scattered footprints amidst the gravel on the ground. Judging from the amount of dust covering them, they should be from two or three months ago.
Dudu compares her own foot with the footprints on the ground.

speaker: Dudu
content: It's around the same size as my foot, so it should be a woman?
The left foot makes slightly deeper prints than the right foot. This is someone with a leg injury or disability. Let's follow the footprints.
You follow the footprints to a room deep in the abandoned building.
Plastered on the charred walls are a few cartoon and sports posters. Though faded and old, there are no burn marks on them. They must have been placed there after the lightning incident.

This tells you that someone cleaned and redecorated the room after the building was abandoned. The same conclusion can be drawn from the dusty but debris-free floor and neatly arranged items on the table.

speaker: Dudu
content: Boss! Come look at this!

Dudu takes down a framed picture from the shelf, which depicts two people. The side with the little boy is peppered with scratch marks, as if it had been repeatedly rubbed by someone's fingers. The old woman beside the boy looks familiar to you.

speaker: Dudu
content: That's right, it's the granny that lives next door to me!
Who's the boy? I thought she didn't have any family?

speaker: Dudu
content: I don't know either...
Let's look separately for some more clues.
In an inconspicuous corner next to the poster is a half-burned crayon drawing. The paper is charred, so you can only make out some messy lines.
Dudu comes over.

speaker: Dudu
content: What is this a drawing of? What are those circles and triangles? It's so burnt that I can't tell...
You squint hard at the picture for a while.
Isn't that a square under the triangle? It looks like... a roof?

speaker: Dudu
content: Are you sure? That's way too abstract... Huh? There seem to be words underneath?
As Dudu says this, she takes the drawing off the wall, dusts it off and wipes it with the hem of her shirt. She walks to the window and reads the words under the moonlight.

speaker: Dudu
content: <color=#fb9259>Granny and me</color>...?

speaker: Dudu
content: So these two circles are the heads of stick people, and the triangle is indeed a roof.
Lying quietly in the drawer is a stack of charred paper fragments, which someone had clearly rescued from the debris piece by piece and carefully preserved.
Luvia
Greeting card, New Year, eight years old, birthday, nine years old, wish you happiness, ten years old... For <color=#fb9259>Palama</color>!
After quickly sorting out all the clues from this room in your head, everything seems to click in the blink of an eye. Dudu also flashes a shocked expression upon hearing the name "Palama."

speaker: Dudu
content: So... this is the house where the old lady used to live? The Palama she speaks of... is actually her grandson?!
You nod slightly.
Yet these greeting card fragments mention nothing beyond the age of ten. Something must have happened to her grandson when he was ten years old.
Those who came to explore must've seen the old lady when she was tidying the room or mourning her grandson and thought she was a ghost. This is the truth behind the haunted building.
In the end, the sharp-eyed Dudu discovers a dilapidated notebook between the table and the bed.
It's rude to look through others' personal belongings without their consent, but you can't think that much under the circumstances.
You nervously flip open the cracked cover. Written with colored pencils on the inner front page are the words "Palama's Diary."
The last piece of the puzzle has finally fallen into place. The truth of everything is within hand's reach. Your heart is racing, as if about to pop out of your throat.
The handwriting inside the diary is as childish as that of the title page, yet each pencil stroke is neat and tidy...

"Today, I went climbing a tree again. The old elm tree by the vegetable market is my favorite, but I only stayed on it for a little while before Grandma called me down. I know she worries about me, but her sudden shout is the biggest danger of all! I almost slipped and fell off..."

"Today, I fell by accident when getting eggs from the chicken coop. The pants that Grandma washed for me yesterday got dirty again. Sigh. It's hard for her to squat with her bad knees, so I thought I could help. But I ended up making her angry again."

Today is Grandma's birthday. Aside from exchanging cards as usual, I also tried making my favorite bean cake for her. Though it turned out ugly, and I put too much sugar, Grandma ate it all and said it was yummy.

"Grandma got a lot more white hair recently. I really hope she doesn't have to work so hard. Sigh, why am I only ten years old? Time passes by too slowly. I want to grow up faster so that Grandma can depend on me."
Then, there are several blank pages in a row. You continue to flip onwards.
Text reappears, but in completely different handwriting.
Palama, everyone says that you died in that accident, but I don't believe it. As long as I keep waiting, you'll come back one day, right?

"I had another big fight with the vegetable seller today. I bought so many vegetables from her, yet she refuses to give me a discount on the green onions. But I know you'd pull me away if you were there. You hate it when I fight with people. My brashness embarrasses you."

"Actually, I hate it too, but I have to force myself to be like that. If I don't try hard to be stronger, who'd protect us? Who'd protect you? I always think of your parents' accident. If I had been braver and tougher back then, would everything be different?"
"Palama, Grandma's sick. They say I have a tumor in my head that's affecting my memory. No wonder I've been having trouble finding my keys lately."
From that page onwards, the paper is frequently wrinkled from wet stains that have dried, and there are many smudged ink spots. You can almost smell the salty scent of tears.
"They say that as the tumor grows, not only will I forget my loved ones one by one, but I might also lose the ability to wash, cook, walk, and talk..."
"The other things don't matter to me. I don't care if I become a bedridden cripple, but I don't want to forget you. If I forget you, then I really have nothing."
"Grandma is really scared. What if I don't recognize you when you come back?"
"I've never done anything evil in my life, so why is fate so cruel to me? No... I won't let the last bit of hope and happiness in my life be taken away!"
After that, the handwriting becomes messier and messier, making most of the content unreadable.
You flip page after page all the way to the end. On the very last page is a final sentence, written so forcefully that it pierced through the paper...
"Palama, Grandma wants to see you one last time."
The last entry in the diary dates to three months ago. Has she already forgotten how to come to this place by now?
You gently close the diary, but your heart is still racing. In just a few minutes, you've read through her entire tragic life story from this old diary.

speaker: Dudu
content: Chief... Let's visit the old lady and give her back the photo and diary she left behind.
Dudu's voice is a bit hoarse. She takes the framed photo from the table and gently wipes the dust off the glass.
Your heart feels just as somber as you caress the cracks on the diary cover.
Okay.

speaker: Dudu
content: Granny? Are you there?
Dudu knocks on the door, but there's no response from inside. She twists the doorknob, and the door opens with a click.
You push open the unlocked door and walk inside, only to find that under the moonlight, the old lady had stopped breathing in her dreams.

She lies on her bed in silence, her hands folded across her stomach, her face as peaceful as a sleeping child's. The clear moonlight cascading in from the window bathes her in an almost sacred silver sheen.

speaker: Dudu
content: Granny, this is the first time that I've seen such a kind and gentle smile on your glum face...

speaker: Dudu
content: You must've reached another world by now, reunited with your family and that precious grandson you've been waiting decades for, right?
Yeah. She's been losing things her entire life. She lost her family, her grandson, her health, and even her memory, but she never lost hope.
You solemnly put the photo and diary back into the old lady's arms. The lost treasures have finally been returned to their rightful owner.

speaker: Dudu
content: Now... It's time for me to deliver on my promise.

Dudu stands by the window and starts to play her song. Under the moonlight, the suona's blaring wails sound mournfully beautiful, as if each note drifting into the night breeze carries a memory of the old lady and her grandson.

The hard but happy life they shared seems to unfold before your eyes. You see the undying resilience that kept the old lady going in the lonely days after the incident. You hear her call out to her grandson again and again as she reminisces his smiling face, if only to remember his name...
And when all the dust has settled, you see the most beautiful reunion that belongs to her dreams.

speaker: Dudu
content: Chief...
When the song is finished, Dudu puts down the suona and looks up at you, her eyes filled with sorrow.

speaker: Dudu
content: My teacher told me before that death is not the ultimate end of a life, but being forgotten is.

speaker: Dudu
content: Now that Granny is gone, will Palama completely disappear from this world?
You take a deep breath and look at Dudu with warm, reassuring eyes.
At least we shall remember him for her.
When the Interrogation Room is lit up, the girl hugging the lantern still has her head tilted in a sweet slumber.
One night not long ago, Letta sleepwalked to the Bureau's gate. She didn't show the slightest sign of resistance when you shackled her and brought her back to the MBCC.
She's been cooperative and compliant during her detention. Aside from her involuntary sleepwalking at night, she's one of the last Sinners you'll have to worry about.

You thumb the envelope with black patterns branded with the Devonshire family name. The graceful couple who gave it to you solemnly requested you to "please make sure this was passed onto their daughter Letta."
Hey, Letta.

speaker: Letta
content: Zzz... Hmm... Oh, hello there, Mr. Chief...
female_content: Zzz... Hmm... Oh, hello there, Miss Chief...

content: She rubs her eyes and looks at your blearily before closing them again.

speaker: Letta
content: It's not yet... time for school...
...Letta! Come on, I know you're not really sleeping.
test
test
test
test
test
test
You sigh and slide the envelope to the girl.
Get up and read this letter.

speaker: Letta
content: ...Letter?
She opens her eyes slightly and glances at the letter.
Yes, your parents asked me to pass it to you.
Letta curls her lip with an unwilling look. Still, she opens the envelope and reads the letter out loud.

speaker: Letta
content: "Dear Letta, how are you? Since you left home, we've been extremely worried."

speaker: Letta
content: "In fact, we'd long realized you might be going through some drastic change. But as parents, whether our child is an ordinary person or a Sinner, we only wish to protect you the best we can."

speaker: Letta
content: "And that was why we became even stricter with you."

speaker: Letta
content: "Although you failed to understand our intention and escaped from your family's protection, we still hope you can receive proper care. Fortunately, the MBCC can provide that."

speaker: Letta
content: "So Letta, my dear, stay there and forget your childish escape plans. The outside world is complex and cruel to Sinners... We fear you may get hurt."

speaker: Letta
content: "You've always been a clever child, but you oversimplify the idea of 'choice-making.' Anyway, we believe that you're simply going through a phase."

speaker: Letta
content: "Do you still remember the Growth Plan we've made for you? That's the life plan we've mapped out for you after meticulous consideration, the best choice you can have."

speaker: Letta
content: "Once you think it through, hopefully you'll choose the path the most beneficial to yourself and continue to follow it, for that's the plan tailored for you. It'll make you a better person."

speaker: Letta
content: "Lots of love, Father and Mother."
When she reaches the last sentence, she can't help grumbling softly.

speaker: Letta
content: Ugh... Can't believe they still haven't gotten over that Growth Plan!

speaker: Letta
content: Nothing more than a boring itinerary...
Letta puffs up her cheeks childishly.

speaker: Letta
content: Like it says in the letter, Father and Mother are obsessed with perfectly organized plans... So they also expect me to be the same.

speaker: Letta
content: The Growth Plan is a roadmap tailored for me. They think that so long as I follow each step scrupulously, I'll grow up to be the perfect heiress to the Devonshire family.
Your parents seem to have high expectations for you.

speaker: Letta
content: Yeah... But they give me a lot of pressure too!

speaker: Letta
content: Can you imagine? They picked me up as soon as school was over just so I could attend even more private tutorials. I never went anywhere besides home and school.

speaker: Letta
content: I could deal with the heavy schoolwork, but what's worse was that... Father and Mother rarely let me step out of home!

speaker: Letta
content: They always said it was dangerous out there and there were too many distractions. They wanted me to focus on my study... But the outside world just seemed so much fun...
At the mention of that, she starts to sound aggrieved.

speaker: Letta
content: When I was trapped at home, the most I could do was stare out of the window. At school, my classmates were always chatting about fun places they went and interesting things they saw.

speaker: Letta
content: When I listened to them, I felt so envious. Because I'd never experienced those things... naturally... they didn't want to hang out with me...
Feeling a tinge of sympathy for the caged bird craving for freedom, you can't help but agree with her.
I see... That's indeed a depressing life.

speaker: Letta
content: You think so too, don't you? But then, hehe...
Letta suddenly smiles cunningly.

speaker: Letta
content: Although Father and Mother always asked me to be a good girl... I was dying to see the outside world for myself.

speaker: Letta
content: So, one night... while no one was watching, I nicked the lantern at home and snuck out!
The lantern in Letta's arms radiates a soft light. You recall that her special ability is cast through this medium.
And the urban legend she's inspired, the Lantern Ghost of Sloane Street, has only become popular recently.
Your guess is that something happened on that day and turned Letta into a Sinner.
Can you tell me more about that night?

speaker: Letta
content: Hmm... It was very foggy that night in Eastside and there happened to be a Mania attack on the street.

speaker: Letta
content: Father, Mother, and the servants were all busy guarding the house and maintaining its Mania defense, so no one thought of me. And there, I stumbled upon a small opening on the defense...
...So you just snuck out through that opening?
Letta gives an exaggerated little nod.

speaker: Letta
content: I did!
You're baffled. This little bird has a wild heart. It'll snatch the first chance to flap its wings and break the cage, oblivious of how much danger lurks in the forest.
Stepping out on a Mania-ridden foggy night... Were you aware of how dangerous this was?

speaker: Letta
content: Um, yes...
Letta bows her head in embarrassment.

speaker: Letta
content: But... that was my only chance! I wanted to go out so badly!

speaker: Letta
content: You see, I wasn't entirely unprepared either... The lantern I took was embedded with Hypercubes. It would protect me!
Alright... And what did you see after getting out?

speaker: Letta
content: The second I got out, I wanted to find those interesting toy shops my classmates had mentioned. But most shops had shut their doors due to the Mania attack.

speaker: Letta
content: I fought so hard for this chance, so I didn't want to just head back like that. As I was still debating, I spotted the silhouettes of some Corruptors in the fog!
You ran into Corruptors?

speaker: Letta
content: Yes... I was terrified, I thought they had me... But those Corruptors didn't come close. In fact, they avoided me. It was then I realized that the lantern repelled them!

speaker: Letta
content: So, ugh, that gave a boost to my courage... I decided to wander a little more, hoping to see more interesting things...
How could you... Anyway, go on.

speaker: Letta
content: I used the lantern to see and made my way through the fog, into the center of the neighborhood. But little by little, I felt my body becoming heavier and I began to have trouble breathing...

speaker: Letta
content: It was too much and I wanted to go back. But the moment I turned, I saw a ton of Corruptors hiding in the fog, all around me!

speaker: Letta
content: The lantern had gotten dimmer too. The light was dwindling, like it might go out any second. I finally realized... I might not make it back out...
Letta recoils and hugs her lantern tightly. Once she collects herself, she begins again.

speaker: Letta
content: I could only retreat step by step with my lantern in my arms, until I was cornered into an alley by the Corruptors. At the moment they were about to reach me, I closed my eyes, and then...
Letta drags out the sentence. You draw in a long breath reflexively.
And then?

speaker: Letta
content: And then I heard the Corruptors' screams! Once those horrible noises stopped, I finally dared open my eyes and found that... they were all gone!

speaker: Letta
content: I was alone in the fog, and miraculously my lantern lit up again, even brighter than before.

speaker: Letta
content: It shot a long beam that extended out of the fog. I couldn't see where it ended. Somehow it was guiding me...

speaker: Letta
content: So I followed the beam and kept walking and walking. And before I realized it, I was home!
...You were lucky.

speaker: Letta
content: Father and Mother said so too...

speaker: Letta
content: I told them I wasn't injured and that the FAC escorted me back, but they still seemed concerned. From then on, they'd become even stricter with me.

speaker: Letta
content: But none of that could stop me anymore because...
Letta bats her eyes complacently.

speaker: Letta
content: I discovered that as long as I carried the lantern, I could walk through any wall freely!

speaker: Letta
content: So every night, I would sleepwalk onto the streets! Hehe, it was always so much fun in the fog.

speaker: Letta
content: I ran into people who'd lost their ways all the time. Unable to see clearly, they kept walking in circles anxiously... Usually, I'd start by playing a little game with them.

speaker: Letta
content: I'd sneak close to them and tap on their shoulders. The braver ones would go entirely stiff and the fainthearted would outright scream. Everyone reacted differently. Oh, I had so much fun!

speaker: Letta
content: Then, I'd hold their hands and lead them out of the fog...

speaker: Letta
content: Once I sent everyone out of the fog, I'd sleepwalk back home. Father and Mother couldn't do anything about it!
With that, Letta flashes a cute, demure smile, but her eyes are filled with a prankster's satisfaction. The truth is plain as day now.

Faced with Corruptors during her escape on a foggy night, Letta unleashed her potential with her immense survival instinct. With the Hypercubes' guidance, she eventually awakened as a Sinner and saved herself from danger.

Grounded against her will, she frequently used this convenient power to sneak out and wandered in the fog, pranking and guiding lost passersby ignorant of the truth. That's the origin of the lantern ghost.
From your parents' letter, they seem to have been aware of your Sinner identity for some time.
And the strict supervision was their way to protect you... Despite the good intention, it's indeed a bit extreme.

speaker: Letta
content: Yes, I know it was for my own good... But I couldn't stand that life without freedom any longer.

speaker: Letta
content: Mr. Chief, did you know... I came to the Bureau on purpose so you could arrest me.
female_content: Miss Chief, did you know... I came to the Bureau on purpose so you could arrest me.

speaker: Letta
content: You heard it right! I wanted to go somewhere where no one would intervene in what I did, where I could dictate my life.

speaker: Letta
content: I want to make my own Growth Plan.
I see, you already have an idea. What kind of plan do you want to make?

speaker: Letta
content: First of all... I want to go on an adventure!
Letta looks exceptionally excited all of a sudden. She produces a thick notebook and passes it to you. You see the handwritten title on the cover: DisCity Adventure Journal.

speaker: Letta
content: Hehe, take a look.

speaker: Letta
content: It details all the most unique and thrilling attractions in DisCity I've gathered from the internet, magazines, and urban legends!
You flip open the notebook, whose sensational content makes your pupils tremble.
What's this... The Four Strange Tale Locations of Eastside?
You scan that paragraph of exaggerated description packed with overly dramatized anecdotes.
Ever-blooming flower field, steel maze of the roaring monster, midnight phantom ball, and... eerie castle of doom and mystery?

speaker: Letta
content: Aha! You've spotted them right away! These are my top four destinations!
She clasps her hands together against her chest and stares up at you with irresistible twinkling eyes.

speaker: Letta
content: Please let me out, Mr. Chief!
female_content: Please let me out, Miss Chief!

speaker: Letta
content: Everyone sees me as an urban legend now, but I'm just a knockoff! I want to experience the real strange tales firsthand!
As reluctant as you are to spoil the girl's mood, you remind her tactfully.
Ugh, I must admit these do sound very strange...
But you said it yourself, the urban legend character inspired by you is fake. Likewise, these tales may not be as you imagine...

speaker: Letta
content: Hmm, you're not wrong. But... but this is a plan I've already finalized! I want to go so badly!

speaker: Letta
content: Surely you can indulge me with this little wish, can't you, Mr. Chief?
female_content: Surely you can indulge me with this little wish, can't you, Miss Chief?

content: Hearing no response from you, Letta doesn't seem discouraged at all. She simply closes one eye and makes a puzzled expression.

speaker: Letta
content: If you don't agree, I won't push further...

speaker: Letta
content: But as you know, I have this sleepwalking condition that I can't control.

speaker: Letta
content: They say your dreams reflect your desires... If one night I accidentally wander off, I hope you'll understand it's not my intention at all!
The girl has the most innocent look on her face. Your head starts hurting.
Indeed, with her special power, sneaking out unnoticed is a piece of cake to Letta.
Even though you can locate her with the shackles, it'll be a headache if this becomes a habit.
Okay, Letta. I'll let you go out.
But on one condition. I must go with you.

speaker: Letta
content: ...Go with me?
Yes. You said you wanted to dictate your life, so I won't intervene in any of your actions. Just think of me as... a travel companion.

speaker: Letta
content: Hehe, hurray!
Letta gives you that adorable, satisfied smile again.

speaker: Letta
content: Before you even knew my identity, you were one of the few people who weren't scared of me. Going on an adventure with you must be fun!

speaker: Letta
content: Deal!
Letta leaves in high spirits to plan the itinerary. Subconsciously, you sense trouble. Those so-called strange tale locations don't sound too promising...

speaker: Letta
content: According to the guide... this is our first destination today, the ever-blooming flower field!
But isn't this just a small park...?
You and Letta stand in front of a nameless park in an Eastside suburb, staring at each other.

speaker: Letta
content: Perhaps the flower field lies in this park...?
Possibly... But given the season, it's unlikely we'll see any flower field. Maybe that's why it's a strange tale.

speaker: Letta
content: Hmm... Let's go in and have a look!
Are you here to visit? Welcome!
A man in staff uniform emerges and approaches them hospitably.
Hello, we were wondering if, um... is this the ever-blooming flower field?

speaker: Staff Member
content: You're exactly right! Here, you'll enter a fairyland where flowers bloom in all seasons! To experience the miraculous scenery, you need only...
He raises a small board which reads: Entry Ticket: 100 DisCoins/Person.
Letta stares at you with an anticipating look and tugs at your shirt. You sigh.

speaker: Staff Member
content: That'll be 200 DisCoins, thank you!
The staff member takes the money and leads you into the park with a wide grin.
The park is not exactly big. After taking a small path, you see a field of vivid colors distantly.

speaker: Letta
content: Wow! That's the flower field...
Excited, she wants to get closer, but is immediately stopped by the straight-faced staff member.

speaker: Staff Member
content: Please don't go any closer, Miss. This flower field can only be viewed at a distance. Once the flowers are tainted with human scent, they'll wilt instantly... and this magnificent scenery will be no more!

speaker: Letta
content: Oh, I remember now, the strange tale does mention that. Too bad then...
Letta halts her steps awkwardly. Something feels off to you.

speaker: Letta
content: Ah, the wind...
A gust of wind rolls up the hem of her dress. She presses on her hat to prevent it from getting blown away by the rising wind.
Suddenly, Letta opens her eyes widely and stares ahead in surprise. You follow her gaze and find that half of the flower field has collapsed in the wind.

speaker: Staff Member
content: Ah! My flower field!
The staff member shouts and runs over in panic.
You follow him and finally see the truth of the flower field. They're merely fake flowers propped up in the soil.

speaker: Letta
content: I see, the ever-blooming flowers... are fake...

speaker: Staff Member
content: Sh-shush!
He refutes defensively as he tries to set the collapsed fake flowers right. But as soon as he fixes a bunch, the other ones get blown down again, so his effort is all wasted.
Don't waste your time. Those at the back have all gone down too.
You point at the fake flowers facing down on the distant slope. Finally, the staff member gives up and slumps down on the ground wearily.
He sighs as he plucks off his hat, and begins to vent at you.

speaker: Staff Member
content: I'm so sorry. As you can see, the ever-blooming flower field doesn't exist... The flowers are not real.

speaker: Staff Member
content: This park has poor operations and mediocre landscapes. It's going out of business.

speaker: Staff Member
content: But I wanted to make a final attempt. I pulled some strings and got these fake flowers that were going to the landfill and created the fake scenery...

speaker: Staff Member
content: Then I made up a lot of exaggerated rumors and spread them as much as possible, hoping to attract more visitors and sell some tickets.

speaker: Staff Member
content: Once I earn enough money, I can buy some seedlings and grow a real flower field...

speaker: Staff Member
content: But for now, the fake flowers remain fake... I'm really sorry. Please forgive me!
His honest confession somehow leaves you speechless.
Letta is still staring blankly at the flower field, as if still processing the disappointment from her ruined fantasy.
Letta, what do you think?

speaker: Letta
content: ...Oh, me? Well, it is what is it! I'm fine!
She snaps out of the daze and gestures to the staff member indifferently.

speaker: Letta
content: The park is still beautiful... I hope the next time we visit, we'll see a real flower field!
You say goodbye to the park's staff member. Letta leads you to the next destination enthusiastically, the steel maze of the roaring monster.
This is a rooftop piled with construction materials and pipes. The metal lies silently in the dark and divides the space into several dim diverging paths, indeed making the place seem like a maze.

speaker: Letta
content: Legend has it that when the night falls, the monster in the heart of the maze roars furiously to intimidate all intruding enemies...
But I hear no roars...
Just as you say that, the ground beneath your feet suddenly vibrates and the pipes around you begin rumbling.

speaker: Letta
content: ...Listen! The monster's roaring!
Letta feels the pipes carefully to detect the source of the roar and immediately starts going in that direction excitedly.

speaker: Letta
content: Come, Mr. Chief, let's go find the monster!
female_content: Come, Miss Chief, let's go find the monster!

content: You nod and let Letta lead the way.

Having been fooled by the previous strange tale, you don't have high expectations for the remaining destinations. But the environment here is kind of spooky... Perhaps it'll prove slightly more legit than the fake flowers at the park?

speaker: Letta
content: The path ends here... Oh, a door?
Fumbling along the pipes, you reach the end of the maze and find a door on the wall that seems to lead downstairs.
You hear the constant roars through the metal door, from the interior of the building. Letta turns the handle but fails to open it.

speaker: Letta
content: Of course, we mustn't leave the adventure unfinished! Follow me closely!
The lantern flickers. Letta holds your hand and leads you through that locked door.
Behind it is a dark, long corridor with only an eerie glimmer glowing at the distant end. She raises the lantern to repel the darkness. The deeper you go, the louder the roars grow.
Through your linked hands, the shackles pass all of Letta's excitement and anxiety to you.

speaker: Letta
content: I'm so excited... Chief, what do you think we'll see this time?
Before you can answer, a cacophony of clanks interrupts you.

speaker: Letta
content: Is that the monster...?

speaker: Letta
content: It's alright, I'm not scared... If anything happens, I'll get you out of here... Ah!
In the pitch black, you're suddenly met with several pairs of eyes.
Letta screams instinctively. You're equally shocked by the sudden sight. You immediately drag her back and stand before her.
At the peak of your anxiety, the eyes begin talking.
Who are you? How did you get in?
The clanks resume as the eyes gradually hover toward you. Letta's lantern dims with fear, so the light is just enough for you to make out their appearance. To your relief, those are human eyes.
Several workers dressed in heavy gear stand there, dark masks covering their entire faces. Their eyes are the only bare parts on their bodies; they stare at you in confusion.
And they're still carrying different tools as if they've just left their duties hurriedly.
Behind them, a large machine is still running dutifully, the pipes connecting to it rumbling rhythmically. That's it. That's the roar.

speaker: Worker
content: Are you... spies sent by that factory across the street?

speaker: Worker
content: We only work discreetly at night, and still you've managed to sneak into the factory...
Though only their eyes are visible, you can sense the deepening suspicion and hostility in them.

speaker: Worker
content: No way, we won't let you leak what you've seen!
Having said that, they close in on you in an attempt to subdue you.
...Hold on! I'm an Eastside sheriff. I received a complaint from this lady here about nighttime noises from this site that disturbed the neighborhood. I'm here for an inspection.
You straighten your back immediately and imitate the tone of a sheriff on duty, trying to turn the situation around.
Why are you operating large machinery outside working hours? This is against the regulations.
Show me your special permit if you have one. Otherwise, I'll report this to my superior and temporarily close down this site.
Intimidated by your confidence and righteousness, the workers' attitude softens.

speaker: Worker
content: Permit... Of course we have one, but we don't have it with us now. Please give us a chance, we'll make sure we have all the papers ready next time!
...Alright, I'll let you off this time. I'll come back again tomorrow, but you must cease your work for today.

speaker: Worker
content: Sure, no problem...
The workers turn off the machine, pack up their tools, and file out of the exit on the other side. You grab Letta's hand and turn back to the way you came at once.
We must leave before they notice something's wrong!

speaker: Letta
content: G... Got it!
After coming down from the rooftop, Letta calms herself and says gratefully while holding onto you.

speaker: Letta
content: Mr. Chief, how could you remain so calm in that situation...
female_content: Miss Chief, how could you remain so calm in that situation...

content: Ahem... Years of training taught me that.
You touch your nose and ask.
Letta, seeing that the last two locations were hugely different from the descriptions in the tales, the other ones may be the same... Should we continue?
Letta gazes into the pitch black maze and remembers the narrow escape just now. She nods and smiles at you.

speaker: Letta
content: ...Yes! We're only halfway through our exploration, don't give up so soon!

speaker: Letta
content: Now that we've survived that kind of scary strange tale, whatever may come will be nothing more than a sprinkle of water, to put it in the mother tongue of that little kid!
She opens the DisCity Adventure Journal she's brought with her to look for the next destination.

speaker: Letta
content: Amazing, the midnight phantom ball happens to be nearby! Let's go there now!
As soon as you turn into that dark alley she's marked out, you hear eerie music coming out of it. Before the hidden archway at its end, several bizarre figures are lurking.

speaker: Letta
content: Hmm... Could those be the phantoms?
... I suppose so?

speaker: Phantom
content: Yo, are you two newbies? Never seen you before!
A phantom notices you and hovers over, the long hem of his outfit trailing behind.

speaker: Phantom
content: Your look is a tad too plain to match our theme...
He judges your outfit disapprovingly before turning his gaze onto Letta and nodding appreciatively.

speaker: Phantom
content: Little Miss here has put in much more effort in her costume! Though you don't appear exactly like a phantom, you look cute and those accessories are on point!

speaker: Phantom
content: The masquerade ball begins soon. Let's have a dance together once you're in there!

speaker: Letta
content: ...Masquerade ball? Isn't this the phantom ball?

speaker: Phantom
content: Yes, this is a phantom-themed masquerade ball!
The phantom is briefly caught off guard by Letta's question, and then goes on to answer her.

speaker: Phantom
content: Don't tell me you took that gimmicky ad seriously?

speaker: Phantom
content: This dance hall is known for its supernatural-themed midnight events. They make ads in strange tale formats as a gimmick.

speaker: Phantom
content: It seems that the descriptions are so realistic that many believe they're true stories... Well, guess their marketing strategy worked!
At that moment, understanding dawns on you both: this strange tale too is fake.
Under the phantom's cordial invitation, you still step inside the dance hall.
Having been fooled by several fake attractions by now, you begin to worry that Letta may feel disappointed or frustrated.
To your surprise, the second she steps inside, she becomes entranced by the dancing phantoms on the dance floor. You see none of the expected negative emotions on her face.
Letta, what do you think of the adventures we've just had?

speaker: Letta
content: Hehe... They're very fun!
Letta answers unthinkingly, her eyes bright.

speaker: Letta
content: Moreover, all the destinations were chosen by me. I decide where we go and what we do! It feels so good!
Even if the result might be different from what you imagined?

speaker: Letta
content: Sigh, I won't say I wasn't disappointed...

speaker: Letta
content: But these are my own choices, so even if I'm faced with setbacks, I'll accept that without regrets.

speaker: Letta
content: After all, what's an adventure if it's without surprises or accidents?
Her optimism finally calms your nerves.
That's good to hear. These strange tale locations have all been a bit too surprising, so I was worried that might ruin your day.
Hearing that from you reassures me.
Letta blushes in embarrassment.

speaker: Letta
content: After all the things I've asked of you, I'm even making you worried. Sorry...
You're my Sinner, of course I care about your feelings.
There's only one destination left. We mustn't leave the adventure unfinished, right?

speaker: Letta
content: Exactly! Off we go!
This is a towering abandoned structure that stands ominously in the wilderness. It resembles a dilapidated castle piled up with debris and fragments.

speaker: Letta
content: Mr. Chief, this place is so bleak...
female_content: Miss Chief, this place is so bleak...
