content: Can we not do this, babe? Just tell me what you want. I'll reserve two hours just for you every day... No, three... four... How about eight hours? I'll report to you like it's my job. Can't you just give me a bit of space? Let me breathe some free air online?

speaker: Shawn
content: You don't really expect me to stick with you around the clock, do you? I love you, but I have my own life too. Besides, would you really be so cruel as to break a hundred cute girls' hearts all at once?

speaker: Chief
content: Didn't you say I was too possessive? As one of DisCity's stressed citizens, it's normal to have a quirk or two.

speaker: Chief
content: Confiscating your communication terminal is my quirk.
Shawn looks at you in shock. She probably never expected you to use her own words against her.
Realizing she's completely outmaneuvered, Shawn finally raises her hands in surrender.

speaker: Shawn
content: I surrender, darling. You've bested me...

speaker: Shawn
content: But about quitting the internet... Maybe we should think twice?
Shawn peeks at your face before going on to explain.

speaker: Shawn
content: We really shouldn't rush it... You know how much of an issue mental health is in DisCity. You don't think an outgoing, mentally healthy person would be fooled by a catfish like me, do you?

speaker: Shawn
content: A few of those kids... Well, they were already on the brink of a mental breakdown before we met.

speaker: Shawn
content: Not to toot my own horn, but I'm part of the reason why they haven't attempted to harm themselves... They may even consider me a pillar of support or a reason to keep living on.

speaker: Shawn
content: What will they do if I suddenly disappear?
Your "drastic approach" seems to have worked. Shawn drops her previously flippant tone, and even her expression becomes more solemn.
She sighs softly, a look of resignation on her face. Under your gaze, she taps on the social media app and pulls up a friend list named "Darlings".

speaker: Shawn
content: This is Atia, the daughter of Wellmart's owner. She's a young, passionate, and generous lover.

speaker: Shawn
content: She thinks I'm a poor art student from Eastside School of Art. She's still sponsoring me and paying my rent... Apparently, it's the only thing that gives her a sense of purpose. She feels the most energetic when she sends me money.
Though she seems generally listless, Shawn seems quite confident when talking about her "prey".

speaker: Shawn
content: Northshore Breeze, this one's from Syn... Um, now it's called the West District. Used to be in a gang, but I think she's already quit.

speaker: Shawn
content: And this one, "Ragdoll Kitty". She's just a shy, adorable girl with an angelic voice...
Shawn's finger flies over the screen, then she stops at another name.

speaker: Shawn
content: And then there's Ceci...

speaker: Shawn
content: This kid, well. Her dad's a gambler and her mom's been bedridden for years. She worked really hard and got into Banyan Medical College and has been juggling school and work.

speaker: Shawn
content: The past two years have been very hard for her. I've been through everything with her...

speaker: Shawn
content: We've talked about our dreams, poetry and life beyond the here and now. I used to tell her bedtime stories with my most charming voice too. Those memories still warm my heart...

speaker: Chief
content: Just get to the point.

speaker: Shawn
content: Hmm, the point...
Her finger lingers over the name "Slumber under Cherry".

speaker: Shawn
content: This girl... The person she loved died a few years ago. Her mental condition hasn't been good and she's been suicidal several times.

speaker: Shawn
content: I've almost used up all the sweet nothings I could think of just to persuade her against suicide...

speaker: Shawn
content: She wanted me to stay with her forever. "Forever" is a lie in itself, but I still promised her.

As Shawn talks, you keep observing her. In her indifferent demeanor, you finally catch a glimpse of sincerity. Watching her finger linger over those names, you might have found a breakthrough in this conversation.
She may not be lying. These people do need her and depend on her, and for their sake, Shawn can't easily cut herself off from them. But she also hasn't told the whole truth.

speaker: Chief
content: They may need you, but what can you get from them?

speaker: Chief
content: Yes, you. Why do you do these things?

speaker: Chief
content: I've had my revenge on you for your harassment with that throw. Making you quit the internet is not really my quirk. Forcing you to cut ties with people is just a means of interrogation.

speaker: Chief
content: I've never heard you talk about your true feelings like this before. Let's have a heart-to-heart, shall we?
She's dazed for a moment, then quickly bows her head to avoid your probing gaze.

speaker: Shawn
content: That's why I rarely do real dates. I can't stand a crystal-clear gaze like yours.

speaker: Shawn
content: Why do I go around flirting with people online... If I say I have no idea, would you believe me?

speaker: Chief
content: But we can find the answer together.
You point at the communication terminal in her hand on which there's an endless list of names.

speaker: Chief
content: Maybe you'll know the reason why you're addicted to talking with them under a mask when you take it off.

speaker: Shawn
content: In the end, you still want me to quit the internet...

speaker: Chief
content: So, will you do it or not?
You pretend to leave the choice to Shawn, watching her reaction.
Uncharacteristically, she doesn't try to sweet-talk herself out of this, looking down at each of the IDs she's conversed with seriously.

speaker: Shawn
content: Promise me to just tell the truth to those who are more stable, so they can move on. But for the rest...

speaker: Chief
content: I understand. We'll take a gentler approach with the special cases. We'll monitor them and ease them into the truth.

speaker: Shawn
content: So this day has finally come. In the end, love built on lies can't last. I knew it...

speaker: Shawn
content: I knew it. You're just jealous!

speaker: Shawn
content: You want me to watch my exes leave me, huh? I gotta say, you're kinda sadistic...

speaker: Shawn
content: Well, you'll have me all to yourself then. I'm in your thrall, babe.
As if the sincere confession never happened, the heartbreaker returns to her usual nonchalant self, throwing you a coquettish wink.

speaker: Wynn
content: Whenever you're ready, Chief.
In the brightly lit room, four computers are set up in a row, each seated with an operator.
The computers are equipped with software provided by Summer, capable of controlling the camera of the interlocutor's terminal to provide better tech support for this operation.
At your command, they all begin their tasks at hand.
Shawn also grabs a chair to sit next to the operators reaching out directly to the interlocutors.

speaker: Chief
content: Start with the ones who are more stable emotionally.

speaker: Shawn
content: The cruel moment has finally arrived...

Shawn's attitude toward this operation has been vague. Despite seeming resistant and evasive, she complies with the plan. Perhaps, as she's claimed, she indeed wants to understand her own dependence on these online relationships.
And you just happen to have given her the option to snap out of this numbness.

speaker: Shawn
content: Let's begin with Atia. Objectively, she's successful in all aspects of life. We're least likely to run into a problem with her.
Summer's software works perfectly. The camera is hacked and a beautiful, fashionable Eastside woman appears on the adjacent screen.
The hacked camera enables you to see her responses so that you can cope with any potential emergencies. Of course, she can't see what's happening here.
This is of course in no way ethical, but considering the victims' mental state and safety, it's not entirely unacceptable.

speaker: Atia
content: Oh, my dear Sergey boo! You finally remembered to call me. Aren't you supposed to be working on some drafts these days though?
The woman says a stranger's name naturally.
Atia fiddles with her recently styled hair, glancing at the screen absentmindedly.
You've done some research beforehand. The Eastside tycoon's daughter is already 40 years old. Her impeccable appearance is proof of her wealth.
Judging by the surroundings, she seems to be in a luxurious hair salon.

speaker: Shawn
content: Actually, there's something I want to tell you.

speaker: Atia
content: Are you short on cash again?

speaker: Shawn
content: ...No, it's not about money.

speaker: Atia
content: Oh, baby, you artists all have a big ego, don't you? You always sound awkward when it comes to money.

speaker: Atia
content: I want you to concentrate on your art and worry about nothing else. Someone as talented as you shouldn't be troubled by this kind of thing.

speaker: Atia
content: I have nothing else to give you other than money, anyway. I'll make the transfer now, alright? I don't ask for much, just think of me and chat with me whenever you're not busy making art. That will please me enough.

speaker: Shawn
content: ...I really don't want your money.

speaker: Shawn
content: I have something else to tell you this time.

speaker: Atia
content: Something else? What could it be?
Shawn pauses for a moment, her tone low and melancholic.

speaker: Shawn
content: We've known each other for quite a while, right?

speaker: Atia
content: Yeah, almost two years now.

speaker: Shawn
content: What was your first impression of me when we first met?

speaker: Atia
content: Oh, but why...

speaker: Shawn
content: Didn't you find me boring, always talking artsy nonsense?

speaker: Atia
content: But you said your perspective on the world changed after a sudden family tragedy half a year ago... You also said you'd had a crush on me for so long and only then had the courage to tell me...

speaker: Atia
content: Your reluctance came from your artist pride, but you woke up from it. That prideful shell would only pull you away from your true love...

speaker: Shawn
content: The truth is, you've been conned.

speaker: Shawn
content: I'm not the Sergey you know. After his dad went bankrupt, he didn't stay at Eastside School of Art but ran away to Outland with him.

speaker: Shawn
content: I stole his social media account. You've been chatting with me for the past six months.

speaker: Atia
content: Then who... who are you?

speaker: Shawn
content: Just some catfish on the internet.

speaker: Atia
content: Why are you telling me all this? You could have just...

speaker: Shawn
content: Because I've been caught.
On the other side of the camera, Atia bows her head so you can't make out her expression.

speaker: Shawn
content: I'm sorry, Atia. I may have told you many lies. Even my identity is a lie. But know that...

speaker: Shawn
content: I love you. This alone has never been a lie.
Atia lifts her head, her hand covering her mouth, her eyes slightly moist.

speaker: Atia

content: So, what did you say? Care to satisfy my curiosity?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I told her this place is pretty cool—that you might even run into a paper plane contest winner here.

speaker: Orange-Haired Girl
content: Really? Looks like I made an impression! Well, if you want to learn the secret of my paper plane folding... buy me a Free Bird first. Maybe I'll think about it after I finish the drink.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: How about this: if I get you two drinks, maybe you could also consider briefing me your name?
She breaks into a hearty laugh at your unsubtle attempt at small talk, turning to face you and resting her chin on her hand as she sizes you up.
After a moment, she gestures for you to hold out your palm.

Her fingertip dances across your palm, sketching letters as your eyes track its movements, struggling to discern the meaning behind her gestures. However, the ticklish sensation impedes your focus, making it challenging to concentrate.
Noticing your fluster, she gives an amused smile and slows down, tracing each letter again while quietly pronouncing them.
You awkwardly follow her rhythm, slowly sounding out each syllable of her name—

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Ze-phy-r.

speaker: Zephyr
content: That's right! Zephyr. That's my name.
As you say her name, Zephyr looks at you with evident delight.

speaker: Zephyr
content: This is your first time here, right?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Yes. You can tell just by looking?

speaker: Zephyr
content: Of course. You're a new face around here, and...
With cheerful enthusiasm, she leans right in and flicks your unfinished drink with her fingernail, making the glass ring with a clear chime.

speaker: Zephyr
content: You can tell a lot about someone from their drink! This bland choice is every newcomer's go-to, but I don't think it fits your vibe at all.
Your terminal vibrates. As you put it away after responding to the message, you notice Zephyr watching you with an unwavering stare.
Her pensive gaze causes you to falter momentarily. In a gesture of surrender, you spread your hands wide, releasing a weary sigh.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Work never really lets up, you know, even on my days off.

speaker: Zephyr
content: Yeah totally get it! Honestly, you look exactly like the type who'd bring a laptop to a bar for a meeting. Ugh, I'm getting exhausted just thinking about your life!
With practiced nonchalance, she averts her gaze, diverting her attention to the overcast sky beyond, all the while absentmindedly flicking the switch on her pager up and down.
At this close distance, you notice her pager is a model commonly used in transportation communications. Eyeing up the emblem on her jacket sleeve, you carefully choose your next words.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What about you? Being a pilot must be pretty swamped too, right?

speaker: Zephyr
content: Hmm... There was all that hassle with memorizing manuals and taking tests, but that's ancient history now.

speaker: Zephyr
content: But once you're soaring up in the sky, all the rest just fades away! Your worries stay down below, and when you're enveloped in that blue-ness, your think about nothing but pure joy.
She doesn't deny your guess about her profession. The moment your conversation turns to flying, her eyes light up with unmistakable enthusiasm.
The rain outside shows no sign of letting up. You decide to follow her train of thought.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Yeah I remember flying one or two times before, for work. It was indeed quite a view when you see that endless expanse of sky stretching beyond the horizon.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Though I imagine the joy of being a passenger is quite different from what a pilot feels, right?

speaker: Zephyr
content: For passengers... I suppose getting to your destination matters more than the flying itself, right? You're all about reaching your endpoint as fast as you can.

speaker: Zephyr
content: But for pilots—no, for me... I just want to stay up in the sky all the time... just a little longer... and longer...
Her cheeks, tinted by the alcohol, lend her words a raw, heartfelt flow. She lightly taps her knuckles against the window, your reflections mirrored in the darkened glass.

speaker: Zephyr
content: Sure, it's dark and rainy tonight, can't see a thing out there. But if you just pull back on the yoke and keep ascending, above those dense clouds - and further up - that's where you hit the bright sunshine.

speaker: Zephyr
content: The sky up there is clear as crystal, you know, just like this glass right here. When I'm up in the air, sometimes I almost feel like I could see my own reflection.
Following her gaze upward, you see the night sky shrouded in a deep, gray curtain of rain.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Must be pretty challenging to fly in weather like this, right?

speaker: Zephyr
content: Yep, that's the theory. You've got lousy visibility, slippery runways, cyclones, thunderstorms, and all that jazz...

speaker: Zephyr
content: But come on, who do you think I am? Like a bit of mortal danger would ever stop me from taking to the skies!
The intense rain and the late hour pose a dual challenge: not only do they render flying conditions hazardous, but they will also impede FAC's prompt response time.

You've already sent your location and Zephyr's description to Nightingale, asking her to search the archives and provide support. With FAC's arrival still some time away, you need to keep Zephyr engaged and under control.
You decide to keep things light with a playful tone.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Could you tell me more, like... what it feels like? I wish I could experience it myself, but it's not like anyone can just hop on a plane whenever they want, isn't it?

speaker: Zephyr
content: Says who? Look, if you really want to try it, how about we have a try right now?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Hmm...
A sudden hush falls over the conversation, leaving only the bar's background music to fill the silence.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Right now? You have a PLANE?

speaker: Zephyr
content: Not yet, but I can get one real quick.
Zephyr takes your lack of outright refusal as a yes. Her eyes sparkle with excitement. Rising to her feet, she reaches out her hand towards you, her expression brimming with anticipation.
It's as if a single nod from you would be all she needs to sweep away every obstacle and whisk you off to wherever her heart desires.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But with all this rain...

speaker: Zephyr
content: So what? We'll make a run for it! Come on, let's roll—!
Before you can finish, she grabs your sleeve and yanks you to your feet, making you stumble forward.

The bar door creaks as she shoves it open and lets it slam shut behind you. The icy rain lashes against your face, compelling your eyes to close, yet in the darkness, you can still sense the warmth of her hand firmly gripping yours.
Through the suffocating curtain of midnight rain, Zephyr pulls you along in a wild dash.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Can we actually fly in this rain?

speaker: Zephyr
content: Hey, I'm a licensed pilot! Trust me!

speaker: Zephyr
content: It's exactly this kind of sky that hides something extraordinary.

The rain immediately soaks through your clothes, the damp fabric clinging heavily to your skin. You trail closely behind Zephyr as she weaves through the empty streets of Eastside in the dead of night.

You consider pulling your hand away, but dismiss the idea—it's not yet time to startle this possible Sinner. Instead, you quietly activate your terminal's tracking, following her along until you uncover the destination she's heading towards.

speaker: Zephyr
content: You'll be my first passenger since I started flying! We can catch the sunrise together from up there—I'm getting all hyped just thinking about it!

She dashes ahead, spinning gleefully around lamp posts one moment, deliberately splashing through puddles the next. Her laughter rings out freely in the downpour, each moment lived with such wild abandon as if it were her last.

You squeeze sideways through narrow gaps between buildings, wade through knee-deep muddy water under bridges, and climb drainage pipes onto unfamiliar rooftops. Then, amidst blaring alarms slicing through the air, you make a daring leap from one rooftop to a balcony several meters away.

With no destination in sight, you begin to suspect that Zephyr's talk of flying might just be an excuse for this endless chase born from a whim. As you follow her, it feels like chasing after a kite set loose from its tether.
However, whenever you begin to lag behind, this kind kite halts—shaking raindrops from her hair with a hearty laugh—ready to catch you as you land.
After setting off countless alarms throughout the night, you finally come to a stop in front of a lit manor.
With mud smeared across her cheeks, Zephyr stares intently at the manor's back door, lost in thought.

speaker: Zephyr
content: Huh, an electronic lock—perfect! I know just how to crack this one.

Instead of tampering with the electronic lock directly, she takes a step back and raises the pager in her hand. The moment she presses the button, your shackles detect the same pulse of Mania that once emanated from your terminal back at the bar.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Zephyr.

speaker: Zephyr
content: Yes! ...Hold your horses, will ya—we'll be up in the air in a jiffy. Just bear with me a bit longer.
No sooner do the words escape her lips than the tampered electronic lock begins to emit a shrill alarm.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Zephyr, this is breaking and entering.

speaker: Zephyr
content: Come on, don't be a party pooper! I've done my homework—Mr. Woods hardly swings by this place a couple of times a year. Leaving stuff here untouched is just a waste.
She strides in with practiced familiarity, then rounds a corner and spins around with dramatic flair, proudly revealing the treasure behind her.
There sits a beautifully painted light aircraft.

speaker: Zephyr
content: This aircraft rocks the best specs available right now, top performance in its latest production run too.

speaker: Zephyr
content: Uh, such a shame, leaving it here gathering dust. I might as well take it for a spin and iron out any wrinkles while I'm at it.

You thought running through the rain to fly a plane was outlandish enough, but now, here she stands, nonchalantly explaining her impromptu aircraft theft as if it's the most natural thing in the world. You're torn between feeling absurd and simply acknowledging that this behavior is quintessentially her.
In the blink of an eye, Zephyr uses her power once again to break through the cockpit lock.

Now that you've confirmed both her identity as a Sinner and her intentions, there is no reason to let this farce continue. Your terminal vibrates in your coat pocket right on cue—the perfect moment to act has presented itself.
Just before Zephyr's hand reaches the control yoke, you grab her wrist. The crimson shackles pulse violently in your palm, piercing through her body.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Sinner Zephyr.
Your voice carries gravity as you gaze at her quivering pupils.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: As Chief of MBCC, I'm issuing you an official warning. Cease your actions immediately.

speaker: Zephyr
content: ...What?
Abruptly, glaring spotlights illuminate from all angles, converging on the aircraft's cockpit.
Zephyr raises a hand to shield her eyes from the blinding light. Through the spotlights, Nightingale strides ahead of the arriving FAC reinforcements and quickly joins you at your side.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Sorry, Chief. The weather and signal interference delayed our arrival.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Former pilot Zephyr, discharged for signal interference with flight routes. Given your status as a Sinner and your multiple offenses, including unlicensed operation and property theft, MBCC will enact mandatory detention upon you. Your cooperation is demanded.
On the tarmac, FAC officers take Zephyr into custody. She offers no resistance, only fixing her gaze directly on you, the light in her eyes fading like the night rain.

speaker: Zephyr
content: If I'd been just a little faster...
She shows no surprise at your unexpected intervention, nor does she oppose the arrest. Her expression only hints at regret for letting the opportunity slip through her fingers.

The rain that has lasted all night finally ceases. On your way back to MBCC, you ponder Zephyr's last words, while the image of her face—etched with both regret and yearning as she was led away—remains vivid in your mind.

█ █, N.F. ██

One month after Zephyr's detention

speaker: Nightingale
content: Chief, I've completed archiving Sinner Zephyr's personal files and behavioral records. Please review them at your convenience.

You retrieve the files from Nightingale—noticeably thicker than when Zephyr was initially apprehended. The updated disciplinary reports are numerous, encompassing unauthorized absences, vandalism of public facilities, and various other infractions.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Zephyr has demonstrated strong resistance to Bureau regulations, persistently exhibiting defiant behavior. The higher-ups are particularly concerned about her recent attempted aircraft theft in Eastside and have requested a detailed investigation report from us regarding the incident.

speaker: Nightingale
content: Based on our assessment, the findings of this interrogation report are expected to influence the level of oversight required for Zephyr going forward. As for her... I'm afraid this interrogation won't be easy, Chief.
The records alone portray a clear image: someone as free-spirited and resistant to rules as her won't yield without a struggle.

Inside the interrogation room, Zephyr lounges casually on the chair's armrest, toying with a paper plane she crafted while waiting for your arrival. Yet the marks on her restraints tell a different story—clear signs of violent resistance.
Seeing your entrance, she retains her nonchalant demeanor. Though she straightens up slightly to face you, her posture still exudes informality.

speaker: Zephyr
content: Chief, how much longer are you going to keep me here...

speaker: Zephyr
content: We just got a bit carried away that night and crossed some lines. Now that we're sober, can't we just pretend none of it happened?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Using special powers for signal interference, breaking into private property, attempting an aircraft theft, and operating without a license or registration... The Bureau can't simply "pretend none of it happened."

speaker: Zephyr
content: But none of it really put anyone else in harm's way, did it? Flying in the rain was a gamble I chose to make, and even if I had crashed, I'm confident in my abilities to steer clear of causing harm to others.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If this was indeed a spur-of-the-moment decision, we could consider categorizing it as an attempted theft.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: However, your actions were decisive and purposeful, with extensive knowledge of the aircraft's location and specs. All signs indicate premeditation on your part.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If you still don't grasp the situation, let me break it down: Woods is a top private aircraft supplier in Eastside, and his aviation operations carry considerable weight within DisCity. Just this fact alone is enough for authorities to tag you as a threat to DisCity's air safety.

speaker: Zephyr
content: In this verdict, except for the fact that my actions were "decisive and purposeful," isn't everything else just speculation?

speaker: Zephyr
content: You were there that day. You know it yourself—it really was just something that happened on a whim.

speaker: Zephyr
content: Now you're accusing me of "premeditation" after the fact? That's pretty sneaky.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Given what you did, proving the existence of premeditation is far more logical than proving its absence, isn't it?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And your past record does little to alleviate your suspicion—"Escape from orphanage at age 8," "Instances of disrupting public order in Eastside," "Allegedly organizing events that incited civil unrest"...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Your history will serve as perfect ammunition for others to scrutinize your every move. I doubt they'll be able—or even willing—to accept that you attempted this theft simply because it's a "spur-of-the-moment."

speaker: Zephyr
content: People always document my history based on their own thoughts of me. They didn't even bother to ask me before writing it. How can you be so sure that everything on it is accurate?
She presses her lips dismissively, showing utter indifference to the record of infractions laid out before her.

speaker: Zephyr
content: Why can't the story be like this? An eight-year-old girl broke free from her cage, encountered a series of adventures and hurdles, and voila! —Grew up into a brilliant, resilient adult.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: That said, in your version, the story should continue like this: She suddenly decided to fly a plane on a rainy day and embarked on multiple daring adventures to reach her destination, only to fail in the final moments before dawn?

speaker: Zephyr
content: Mm-hmm, not bad! That's exactly the kind of story I like.
Her nonchalant, flippant tone show no sign of seriousness and your talk won't yield any useful results. Without confirming her motive for the theft, she will only face stricter surveillance measures.
You need to find an emotional trigger that will make her take the current situation seriously.
test
test
test
test
test
test

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So, this free-spirited protagonist suddenly decided one day to turn over a new leaf, choosing to undergo the training and tests she despised most, all to become a pilot...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: And then, coincidentally during her very first test flight, she caused the biggest route jamming ever in history. Miss Protagonist, isn't this all a bit too convenient even for a novel?

speaker: Zephyr
content: ...So this is how you talk into people?
Her smile freezes for a moment as her hands slowly clench into fists beneath her jacket sleeves.

speaker: Zephyr
content: Look, even if someone's done some wild things in the past—and sure, maybe not all of it was great—you can't just weave every little dot into some grand conspiracy.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm simply stating the most logical and obvious speculation based on your records and current words.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If I were to put that story you just told as your motive in the investigation report, people who read it would jump to far worse assumptions about you than I have.

speaker: Zephyr
content: ...Such dirty minds you cops have! Why do you always have to assume the worst just because of some dumb record from the past, huh?

speaker: Zephyr
content: Did that damn file even tell you that I was one of the victims, too?!

Her sudden raised voice shatters the stillness of the interrogation room, leaving a resonant echo in its wake. Under your relentless questioning, Zephyr's chest heaves as a mix of anger and hurt finally bursts through her facade.

speaker: Zephyr
content: On my very first flight ever, I was suddenly hit by that—that Mania or whatever it's called. Before I could even grasp what was going on, the control panel went haywire, and there I was, stuck in the cockpit, alone and helpless.

speaker: Zephyr
content: Sure, I love a good thrill, but I don't have a death wish, for crying out loud!
It was her very first flight. While the sky soared ever higher in the sunset's afterglow, she was plummeting towards earth.

In the cockpit, instrument needles spun wildly out of control. All contact with her fellow test pilots was lost. Warning lights flashed erratically in crimson, like a silent countdown to the demise of her own life.

speaker: Zephyr
content: Mayday, mayday... hah... (cough) Crashing on my first flight... bet there aren't many pilots who can claim that record.

The air pressure changed violently as her vision blurred in free fall... yet her senses were still pierced by the intense light from above. As she forced her eyes open to face the sun, she found herself with her back to DisCity, embracing the entire sky under the sun's blazing gaze.
To a pilot's ears, a crash always means absolute silence. Beep. In that perfect silence, the sound of reconnected signals pierced through.
She opened her eyes again amidst the pungent smell of disinfectant. The hospital room ceiling came into focus, along with her left leg suspended in traction.

speaker: Staff Member
content: The test results are back. The doctor says that your leg injury will have some serious long-term effects, which means you are no longer suitable as a pilot. The incident has settled, and given your injuries, they've decided to arrange your discharge from service.

speaker: Staff Member
content: I'm sorry. No one wanted this to happen. But, Zephyr... someone has to be responsible for this.
She stared at her leg, now held together with steel plates. It had only been her first flight.

speaker: Zephyr
content: I said, and I swear, if I hadn't struggled to restore contact with the control tower, everyone else up there would've been done for!

speaker: Zephyr
content: I wish someone had captured my heroic sacrifice for everyone's safety on camera. Even the Association never questioned me back then, so how did I end up being seen as some sort of dirty criminal?

The accident report indeed makes no mention of casualties from that incident. You thought it was just incomplete documentation, but now it seems more like a deliberate omission to shift responsibility.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Didn't you ever mention that you restored the signal connection? If that was verified, why would they still discharge you?

speaker: Zephyr
content: They told me they admired my bravery, saying I was let go all because my leg injury made me fail the physical... but the truth is, after my power kicked in, I didn't even feel the injury anymore...
The official record explicitly states that Zephyr was discharged for disrupting air traffic protocols, but her testimony indicates the Association must have known the truth.
If Zephyr's account holds true, she is far from being the mastermind behind the signal disruption, but merely a victim of a Mania outbreak who even paid for it with one of her legs.

speaker: Zephyr
content: So why do you people always jump to conclusions so carelessly? The minute you hear a story, you just slot people into your neat little categories without a second thought.

speaker: Zephyr
content: You're all the same—you, whoever wrote that file, that old coot at the orphanage, every single one of you! You're either painting me as a mastermind plotting some grand scheme or blaming my "troubled family history" for my "twisted personality."

speaker: Zephyr
content: My friends always say I'm an open book, wearing my heart on my sleeve, but everyone else just look past me, desperate to dig up some hidden trauma or ulterior motive.

speaker: Zephyr
content: But I'm right here in front of you, aren't I? If you really want to get to know me, see me for who I am—just ask me!
Her loss of composure is a rare sight. Rather than dwelling on your earlier misunderstanding, she seems more concerned with your choice to be made at this very moment.

As you hold her gaze, you come to understand that her principles are even more straightforward than you'd imagined. Leading with this angle in the investigation report might help dispel others' doubts about the theft incident.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'm sorry. It was careless of me to judge you based only on your files. I apologize for that.
Hearing your words, Zephyr freezes for a moment. Her gaze falls away from you briefly, only to return with a newfound sparkle.

speaker: Zephyr
content: ...Well, didn't expect that. I was mad at you for like three minutes, but you said sorry! So, cool, now the good vibes have swept away my anger. I'm starting to dig that.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: While I still can't guarantee the inquiry will all go smooth, I'll try to hear your full explanation before drawing any conclusions. Would that work for you?
You remain composed under her scrutiny as she narrows her eyes, trying to read you for a few seconds before giving a decisive nod.
Having come to an understanding with Zephyr, you revisit her case file. She clearly showed lingering fear while recounting the crash, but why does she remain so enthusiastic about flying again?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: For something like this to happen, most people would probably steer clear of flying for a while, or even be traumatized just seeing a plane afterward. But you seem completely unfazed by what you've been through.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: In fact, you still get quite excited when talking about flying again, like you did at the bar.

speaker: Zephyr
content: Cause if I don't fly again, my entire aviation career will end with nothing but an accident, a revoked license, and a broken leg.

speaker: Zephyr
content: I hate adventure stories that end mid-chapter.

speaker: Zephyr
content: The sky is sooooo vast! It couldn't care less whether I'm scared or nervous when I reach for its embrace, and it definitely won't be asking for any permits when I try to get up close.
At the mention of flying, Zephyr's eyes light up instantly—just like that rainy night when you talked across your drinks.

speaker: Zephyr
content: You know what, I've been to the tallest building in Eastside, and let me tell you, when you gaze out from up there—all of DisCity lies tiny beneath your feet, like you could almost see past the Rust straight to Syndicate in just one glance.

speaker: Zephyr
content: But when I'm up in the sky, even DisCity looks like a speck. The entire world just stretches out below, flat beneath my feet. It feels like I could go anywhere, reach any corner as long as I keep flying forward.
It was one dawn, before her first flight.

Zephyr and her friend snuck past security patrols to climb to the highest point in Eastside. As the horizon stretched out in the dawn light, she stood at the edge of the roof, her toes dangling over the precipice, watching the slumbering city beneath her in the refreshing breeze.
On an impulse, she spread her arms wide, drew in a deep breath, and shouted at the top of her lungs.

speaker: Zephyr
content: —I, Zephyr, will fly a plane—! I WILL FLY—UP HIGH—

speaker: Friends
content: Hey, didn't you say your parents passed away in a travel flight? Seems like you've totally got it over.

speaker: Zephyr
content: Why does everyone have to live in fear of the past? I'd rather honor their memory by finishing the journey they never could.

speaker: Zephyr
content: I, Zephyr! Will never let fear keep me trapped!
That was one dawn before she had ever known flight. To her, reaching for that uncharted sky was an adventure—a symbol of absolute freedom.

speaker: Zephyr
content: It was the same feeling when I decided to become a pilot, and the that night I tried to fly... I guess I just... love adventures where I can go anywhere, anytime, without anything holding me back.

speaker: Zephyr
content: Chief, can you see how I feel?
Unexamined judgments often lead to misunderstandings. But now, though you can't fully digest her words, you're starting to grasp why Zephyr pursues flying so relentlessly.

Her free-spirited upbringing shaped both her carefree nature and her unconventional expectations of society. That's why, after losing that freedom, she persistently rebels while searching for something to fill that void.
You realize this is also why she's been so completely honest with you about her past, including what drove her to attempt the theft.
—Because for what others see as life-changing decisions which require tremendous courage, Zephyr simply deems it as mere little adventures to be embarked upon without a second thought.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I'll classify the theft incident as a crime of impulse in the report, and I'll back up your statement with evidence of your personality and background.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If this report does dispel their doubts about you, I hope you will fulfill your obligations as a Sinner, from then on...

speaker: Zephyr
content: So once their verdict comes in, I can leave this place, right?
She eagerly cuts off your sentence. Met with her hopeful gaze, you maintain your composure and firmly shake your head.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Zephyr, you still have to remain under MBCC's supervision.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...That's it? You should know, Mountain Lord, that I'm not convinced by your answer. The fatal wounds on the Scholar's chest were obviously claw marks left by a fierce beast.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Moreover, the main purpose of MBCC is to detain Sinners, and actions like your blatant appropriation of private property are exactly what warrants detention.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: All I can do for you right now is prevent others with ulterior motives from pinning additional charges on you.

speaker: Zephyr
content: I thought if I just explained everything, then...

speaker: Zephyr
content: Then tell me, what exactly do I have to do to get out of here?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: I can't give you a definite answer right now. The parole process for Sinners involves multiple procedures. Not every Sinner is eligible for parole, and it will depend on the outcomes of your future evaluations.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But I can promise you this: I'll grant you as much freedom as my authority allows.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If you're interested, I can increase your participation in field missions or dispatch work. And of course, as long as circumstances allow, I'll do my best to secure short-term travel permits for you...
As you list out the flexible provisions in the Bureau's detention regulations, Zephyr's eyes glaze over with apparent disinterest.

Twirling a loose strand of hair around her finger, she maintains a heavy silence, her distant gaze fixed on you. The regret and yearning reflected in her eyes echo that rainy night when she was taken into custody.

After wrapping up the interrogation results, you escort Zephyr out of the interrogation room. Your footsteps echo in tandem down the hall, their steady rhythm only serving to amplify the unusual silence between you.
If Zephyr's boundless vitality that rainy night was unsettling, her current silence weighs on you just as heavily.
Suddenly, one set of footsteps drops out of the duet.

You turn around to find Zephyr standing before the glass door to the Activity Area. Today's simulated weather is sunny, and she stares at the artificial blue sky, her expression etched with profound melancholy.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What I promised you just now wasn't just talk. I'll work hard to secure your freedom here, but of course, it needs you to be cooperative too.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: If you're into adventures, there are some fun-loving Sinners here at the Bureau. You could be friends...

She turns to gaze at you, and though her eyes hold no judgment, your words somehow die in your throat. A strange distance hangs between you—physically shoulder to shoulder, yet emotionally as far apart as the sky above.
After a moment, she changes the subject on her own accord.

speaker: Zephyr
content: Do you know what my parents said during our family trip, on the day they passed away?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Maybe... "have fun," "always be happy" or something?

speaker: Zephyr
content: I asked them where we were going.

speaker: Zephyr
content: Then Mom said, "I don't know. We've got a full ten days ahead. Let's just top up the tank and see how far it takes us. We're bound to find something before we need to refuel."

speaker: Zephyr
content: Now I finally understand. Mom was right.

As the Outdoor Activity Area follows its programmed schedule to shift the sky view, the light gradually dims. The glass door before you slowly darkens into a mirror, reflecting your and Zephyr's silhouettes.
The silver door frame cuts between your reflections, as if dividing you and her into two separate, irreconcilable worlds.

speaker: Zephyr
content: You have to do all the fun things you want before the adventure ends. But it seems my own adventure will be just like my parents'—stuck halfway through, forever.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...Zephyr?

speaker: Zephyr
content: Actually, I recognized who you were that night at the bar.

speaker: Zephyr
content: You were really terrible at disguising, you know.

Memories of that night surge from the depths of your mind—her playful taps on the glass, her pensive stares, and that frantic run through the rain when she dragged you along as if staking everything on that moment...
You freeze for a moment. Seemingly amused by your expression, her lips curl into a slight smile that never reaches her eyes.

speaker: Zephyr
content: I always knew I might be taken away after becoming a Sinner, but I never thought that day would come so soon.

speaker: Zephyr
content: So, instead of saying, "I might as well go steal a plane today," what I truly thought that night was, "If I let this chance slip by, I may never fly again."
Just as abruptly as she brought up the topic, Zephyr drops it on her own accord again.

At her request, you spend some time with her in the Outdoor Activity Area, watching the sky together before escorting her back to the detention area. As you say goodbye, she waves at you with her usual smile.
You thought that Zephyr, like other new arrivals, would acclimate to life here gradually. However, within a month, reports surface of her growingly audacious escape attempts.
Only now do you truly realize that the understanding and connection you believed you had established with Zephyr during the interrogation might have been nothing more than your own wishful thinking.
On a rainy day, Zephyr disappeared.

I want to fly one more time.
Til we meet again.

Zephyr

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Any sign of her?

speaker: Staff A
content: All Sinner-authorized areas have been checked. We didn't find the target.

speaker: Staff B
content: Chief! The tech team is working at full throttle to resolve the signal interference. So far, there's no sign of Sinner Zephyr in the restored surveillance zones.
Due to malicious signal interference, the Bureau has automatically activated its defense protocols. Security lasers scan the corridors as defense weapons stand ready to engage any suspicious targets.
You rush through the security measures with your clearance, trying to sense the Sinner's location through your shackles while issuing commands.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Target is still nearby. Expand search radius and keep looking for her. Avoid armed conflict unless absolutely necessary. Report any findings immediately!

speaker: Staff Members A & B
content: Copy that... Chi—
Still unstable, the recently restored communications signal suddenly cuts out.

Just as you lower your hand, the terminal—which should have lost all signal—suddenly buzzes with a message. As you feel the device vibrate in your hand, your heart skips a beat as if sensing a harbinger of things to come.

Zephyr: Hey, I promised to take you flying with me, but looks like that plan's a no-go. MBCC won't let us do this, so I'm going on my own.

Zephyr: Besides, this old bird might be a bit dangerous to fly. I'll take you up when it's safer next time.

Zephyr: Don't worry about me, but feel free to miss me a bit.
The notice of no signal pops up. You fail to send out the message.

Just like what she did before, Zephyr has hijacked the communication, denying you any chance to reach her. As you stare at the red exclamation mark on the terminal screen, your anxiety continues to mount.

You can't simply let a Sinner escape. Apart from the consequences she will inevitably face, the prevailing weather conditions and her physical condition make it impossible to ensure her safety during the flight. You can't stand by and watch Zephyr put herself in danger.
You carefully recall her messages, considering where she might have gone. Finally, all the details point to one location.
Near MBCC, at the decommissioned aircraft salvage yard, the orange-haired figure you've been desperately searching for stands beside the only old aircraft that hasn't been dismantled yet.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Zephyr!
Zephyr has just opened the cockpit and settled into the pilot's seat. Upon spotting you, she offers you a casual wave.
Under her operation, the engine emits a piercing screech as the fuselage violently shudders, threatening to fall apart at any moment.

Yet she remains oblivious to all these dangers. With her hand on the control yoke, Zephyr could take off at any second. You keep your voice gentle to lower her guard while looking for an opportunity to approach the cockpit.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Hurry and come down, Zephyr. Echo and Mess are looking for you tonight—being all secretive like they're planning something behind my back.

speaker: Zephyr
content: You arranged all that, didn't you, Chief?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What?

speaker: Zephyr
content: You told everyone to have me involved while having fun. And when things got a little wild at the Bureau, you kind of just turned a blind eye, didn't you?

speaker: Zephyr
content: The Bureau really is more interesting than I thought. I even scored some missions outside every now and then. Turns out, this place isn't half as uptight as I imagined.

speaker: Zephyr
content: There was also one time that I saw... they erased a record of me coming back late from a mission.

speaker: Zephyr
content: Thank you for trying to make things easier for me, even as a supervisor.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: It's really not that difficult. If there's something you want to do, just tell me. We can make it without breaking the rules.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: We can figure it out, together.

speaker: Zephyr
content: It's precisely because there's so much freedom here, and because you, Chief, try so hard to make life comfortable for us Sinners... that I've realized I'm more greedy than I thought.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Change and adaptation take time. Many Sinners felt the same way when they first came to the Bureau.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Zephyr, you don't need to rush to any conclusions about yourself. We can take things one step at a time...

speaker: Zephyr
content: But that's not enough. What I want is more than that.

speaker: Zephyr
content: You know what? I'm really craving a pineapple bun today.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: What?
Such a random statement catches you off guard. Your brain works intensively processing it, only to produce a questioning sound.

speaker: Zephyr
content: I got up at seven in the morning and waited forever until afternoon tea time, only to find out the cafeteria suddenly stopped making pineapple buns today.

speaker: Zephyr
content: So I borrowed the kitchen from Kelvin, thinking I could whip up some myself if I tried hard enough. But I had a dispatch mission in the afternoon, which left me only an hour to work with.

speaker: Zephyr
content: Then I thought I could just buy some instead... but by the time I finished my mission, the bakery had sold out of pineapple buns.

speaker: Zephyr
content: Coming out of the bakery, I thought to myself: the old me would've turned Eastside upside down just to get my hands on a pineapple bun today.

speaker: Zephyr
content: But back then, my first thought was actually: other bakeries are too far away, and there's not enough time left, so maybe I'll just let it go.

speaker: Zephyr
content: My ambitions have shrunk smaller than a pineapple bun.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: We can discuss all your wishes. MBCC has handled tougher situations before. As long as the requests are reasonable, I'm sure we can figure out a way to make it happen...

speaker: Zephyr
content: That's exactly what I hate!
Zephyr cuts you off mid-sentence, her voice charged with emotion.

speaker: Zephyr
content: Ever since becoming a Sinner, I need to file paperwork just to get to talk, just to see someone who can help me. Then everything I want to do gets numbered and sorted by priority and urgency.

speaker: Zephyr
content: Even with you, Chief, even the most empathetic person towards Sinners in the entire Bureau, our peak of mutual understanding was probably just that talk in the interrogation room. After that, everything I've wanted to do has to come after a "request form."

speaker: Zephyr
content: Once my past and crimes were understood and documented, it felt like my story was archived and shelved away. Any greater adventures that might come after... they probably will no longer have anything to do with me.

speaker: Zephyr
content: Sinner Zephyr may have found a bit of freedom in MBCC, but what about I, Zephyr, myself and my own life after this? Will I ever get to see wider skies again?

speaker: Zephyr
content: Is there any chance for more interesting stories to unfold in my life?

She tilts her head back slightly, as if releasing all the questions that have built up during her time at the Bureau. Yet she doesn't seem to be throwing them at you for answers—it's more like she's thinking aloud to herself.

speaker: Zephyr
content: The freedom I want isn't just having permission to do things once or twice in a never-changing life—

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Then can you tell me what it is that you want? Do you have an answer now?

speaker: Zephyr
content: I don't...

speaker: Zephyr
content: ...But I know I'll never be able to find out by looking up from down here.
Her expression remains unchanged as she speaks, but you keenly sense a subtle shift within her.
The situation is spiraling out of control. You rush toward the cockpit, your voice rising involuntarily.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Zephyr, don't risk your life for this!

speaker: Zephyr
content: If I could just fly above the clouds one more time, I know I'd finally understand what I truly want.

speaker: Zephyr
content: It won't affect anyone else this time! Besides, this plane is headed for the scrapyard anyway, right? I've done my research.

speaker: Zephyr
content: I just checked, and the good news is this model's only showing age-related wear, nothing severely damaged.

speaker: Zephyr
content: The bad news is there's barely any fuel left, the autopilot's locked up, the engine's making weird noises, the frame's a bit shaky, the instruments are off, and even the control yoke gets stuck when I try to pull it back...

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Do you have any idea what could happen if you try to fly it in this condition?!

speaker: Zephyr
content: This means I can only guarantee it'll make it up into the sky. What happens next, though? Your guess is as good as mine.

speaker: Zephyr
content: If luck's on my side, I'll touch down safely after sunrise.

speaker: Zephyr
content: And if I'm not so lucky, well, I suppose I'll be free up there in the sky.
She speaks of death as casually as if discussing tomorrow's weather, the words flowing from her lips like any other trivial matter.
In that split second of your distraction, Zephyr gives you a playful wink and decisively slams her palm down on the engine start button.
Your body moves before your mind can catch up. You leap into the cockpit and grab Zephyr's wrist just before she can pull the control yoke.
But the engine has already sprung to life, the power gauge on the dashboard steadily rising as the aged propellers start to thunder, signaling the imminent departure.

speaker: Zephyr
content: Wha—Why do you come up here?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Stop, Zephyr! This plane is in no condition to fly. It's too dangerous!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: You're getting off with me.

speaker: Zephyr
content: I'm not!
The propellers spin faster and faster. You have no time left.

Crimson thorns pierce through Zephyr's body. With the neural interference of her powers blocked, you know the pain in her injured leg will be magnified intensely—but to stop her from doing something even more reckless, you are left with no choice.
Restrained by your shackles, her movements become visibly labored. Fine beads of sweat form on her forehead as she fights to suppress what must be excruciating pain.

speaker: Zephyr
content: No matter what, I MUST fly!

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...The shackles have sealed your power. Without your signal interference ability, you can't maintain the autopilot system. You'd have to fly manually.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: This isn't the time to act all tough, Zephyr. Taking off in the rain with an injured leg and uncontrollable pain—you will die.

speaker: Zephyr
content: So what?
In the pilot's seat, her steel-plated leg lies rigid and unmoving. Her face has turned deathly pale from the pain, yet it only makes her determined gaze ahead burn all the brighter.

speaker: Zephyr
content: So what if it's bad weather? So what if I lost my power? What difference does it make?!

speaker: Zephyr
content: Sinner or not, I'm Zephyr—the greatest pilot there is!
As the plane accelerates towards takeoff speed, the nose cone starts to rise. However, halfway through the ascent, the power abruptly cuts out, causing the aircraft to plummet downwards.
The landing gear crashes against the ground, dragging with an ear-splitting screech of metal.
Amidst violent turbulence, Zephyr grits her teeth, but the pain drains the strength from her arms, rendering her completely unable to move the rusted control yoke.

speaker: Zephyr
content: Jump! Now! There's still time!
Zephyr's sweat-soaked orange hair clings to her forehead as she valiantly battles through the excruciating pain, still finding the breath to urge you to evacuate the aircraft.
Even though the plane remains grounded, she gazes ahead with unwavering determination, as if already beholding the view of her dreams, her eyes devoid of any hint of hesitation.
You steel your resolve and take Zephyr's hand. After exchanging a resolute look, you grip the control yoke with both hands, helping her pull.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Messing with death? Oh, trust me—I've got way more practice with that than you do.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: ...All this fuss just to look cool, seriously?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Now I'm not going to let you get away without showing me these skies you dream of.
Zephyr freezes for a moment, then her demeanor changes, becoming once again that vibrant soul you first met at the bar.

speaker: Zephyr
content: You asked for it... Now get ready to see what I'm really capable of!
As the plane suddenly accelerates in a straight line, the overpowering gravity pull slams you back, prompting you to clutch Zephyr's hand tighter. Yet you give her a firm nod.

speaker: Zephyr
content: Now... Welcome to Zephyr's territory!

speaker: Zephyr
content: Dear honored first passenger, our aircraft is about to take off and will be passing through the nimbostratus cloud in just a few minutes. If you're feeling a bit nervous, just close your eyes—zoom, and we'll zip right through it!
The deafening roar of the engines grows more violent. Inside the cockpit, Zephyr's gaze remains locked dead ahead, her hands navigating the controls without a moment's hesitation.

After one last shudder, the aircraft's nose abruptly points up at an unthinkable angle. The city's silhouette shrinks rapidly below while the aging plane strains against the fierce winds, its structure groaning as if on the verge of crumbling apart.
Your eardrums throb with painful pressure. You squeeze your eyes shut, feeling the extraordinary turbulence rattle your body as you instinctively hold your breath.

speaker: Zephyr
content: We did it! We made it, Chief! Look!
After what seems like an eternity, the aircraft finally steadies itself. As your companion's exclamation pierces through the air, you slowly open your eyes...

speaker: Zephyr
content: DisCity is really huge—we're way high up and still can't see where it ends. I was hoping to catch a glimpse of the Outlands from here at least.
The aircraft hovers at DisCity's peak. Beneath you, the entire city rests suspended between sleep and wakefulness in the pre-dawn blue, both precious and fragile.
This view of DisCity is new to you—your previous flights were all combat missions during tumultuous times.
This city now seems unusually peaceful... stretching endlessly onward, brimming with infinite possibilities.

speaker: Zephyr
content: ${PlayerName}, how's it? How do you like it? I was so hyped the first time I flew up here and caught this view!
Beyond her excitement, there's a barely perceptible trace of nervousness in Zephyr's voice as she gauges your reaction...
You try to understand Zephyr.
Within the layer of clouds, a sea of ever-changing white envelops both of you. The emerging dawn and fading moonlight blend together, their boundaries dissolving into one.
As the clouds disperse, a faint ribbon of light unfurls between the city and the sky. You and Zephyr track its course through the air, and at this moment, the world becomes vivid and tangible.
When you open your eyes and look down, DisCity is right beneath your feet, slowly stirring to life as the slanting morning light bathes it in warmth.

options: The view up here is so different from what I'm used to.

speaker: Zephyr
content: Right?!

speaker: Zephyr
content: Gorgeous, isn't it?!

speaker: Zephyr
content: Actually, ${PlayerName}, I was a bit worried earlier... If you found the view here lame, you might think all those days I spent breaking out weren't worth it...

speaker: Zephyr
content: You're my first ever passenger, and in a way, this is my first official flight as a pilot. I really wanted us to experience this happiness together.
At this moment, your own encounter intertwines with a memory of Zephyr's past. Now you truly understand who Zephyr is and what she wants.
Understand her devotion to the boundless sky, and her yearning for freedom that runs bone-deep.

speaker: Zephyr
content: That day, when my parents and I left home, it was pouring rain. But as we drove on and on, it felt like we were leaving the bad weather behind us.

speaker: Zephyr
content: We drove far enough that all those little arguments from before we left just melted away. By the end, my moms were just marveling at how fascinating the new places were.

speaker: Zephyr
content: Freedom and new adventures always have a way of washing away troubles. But when you're stuck, pain just festers in that cramped space.

speaker: Zephyr
content: After seeing just how vast the sky can be, who'd still want to stay cooped up in some corner of DisCity?! Even if I have to be in the gutter, I'm always gonna look up at the sky.

speaker: Josh
content: When you're in the sky's embrace, it catches you no matter what you become. It holds endless possibilities of my life!

speaker: Zephyr
content: And now that you're here with me, ${PlayerName}, it feels like we're both embracing this future full of endless possibilities.
Just as Zephyr touches down on the cross-shaped landing marker of the high-rise rooftop, the sun bursts through the clouds.
The city basks in the gentle sunlight, as if the rain and clouds from mere hours ago had never existed.
Zephyr leans on the railing, gazing at the distant horizon.

speaker: Nightingale
content: ...Finally went through. Chief, are you all right? Is Sinner Zephyr with you?

speaker: Nightingale
content: The signal is back to normal now, and the interference on the Bureau channels has cleared up.
The rare moment of tranquility between you is broken by the restored communications.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Yes, we're both safe. There's been a misunderstanding . I'll submit a detailed report when I return.
You offer Nightingale a brief reassurance regarding the situation before ending the call. As you do so, you catch Zephyr gazing at you with a peculiar expression.

speaker: Zephyr
content: Cough...

speaker: Zephyr
content: I won't put up a fight this time, if you need to arrest me as part of your job... Honestly, I thought I'd be surrounded by security forces the moment we touched down.

speaker: Zephyr
content: If my first crash showed me a taste of freedom, then now I really get it—flying itself is my freedom!

speaker: Zephyr
content: I'm totally digging this answer about freedom, so I don't regret breaking the rules to make a run for it at all. Of course, I'll take it in stride if you have to slap the cuffs on me, Chief. That's your freedom, too.
Though Zephyr tries to make light of possibly being arrested again, her expression of grim resignation betrays her true feelings.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: So, are you going to break out again?

speaker: Zephyr
content: ...Well, I can't really promise that. But Chief, I have to say—after today, I see you've got a pretty wild streak in you. It's making me believe that life at MBCC might not be as awful as I thought, and I think I'm finally moving on.

speaker: Zephyr
content: Surely you can be like the sky and embrace my occasional whims?

speaker: Zephyr
content: But you never know what might happen, so at least let me keep the possibility of escape as a comforting thought, will you?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Just as I thought... still can't drop my guard.
With a sigh, you gesture for Zephyr to hold out her hand. Mirroring what she did at the bar, you gently trace a few words on her palm with your fingertip.
Zephyr looks bewildered by your sudden gesture, furrowing her brow as she tries to decipher your meaning. Then you pull out a neatly folded note from your pocket and place it in her palm.

speaker: Zephyr
content: Yes?
You gesture at her hand again, prompting Zephyr to open it in puzzlement.

speaker: Zephyr
content: Sinner Parole Permit?!
You close your eyes and dodge away for a moment before quickly heading for the stairs. Zephyr immediately catches up, chattering non-stop by your ear.

speaker: Zephyr
content: Hey—does this mean I don't have to stay at the Bureau every day anymore?

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Technically, correct.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: While MBCC can't give you complete freedom or fulfill all your wishes, I'll do my best to advocate for Sinners within the bounds of regulation.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: But we need to set some ground rules. First, I know you don't like rules, but you must follow everything stated in the parole permit.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Second, you need to maintain long-term cooperation and communication with MBCC, responding according to mission urgency.

speaker: ${PlayerName}
content: Third, ensure your own safety when you're out, and contact MBCC immediately if there's an emergency.
As your words trail off, your eyes meet in a shared moment of silence.
Suddenly, Zephyr throws her arms around your neck. The force nearly makes you stumble as her joyous laughter fills your ears.

speaker: Zephyr
content: You got it! I'll hit you up ASAP if anything pops off! By the way, is it cool if I reach out even when everything's chill?
You steady her and let out a relieved sigh. Meeting her bright, hopeful eyes, you offer her a warm smile and a reassuring nod.
A few days later...
At three in the morning, the sound of knocking from your office window startles you. You open it and look around, only to find no one in sight.
When you return to your desk, you find a paper plane resting there. Unfolding it reveals Zephyr's unmistakable handwriting.
${PlayerName}, Prepping a fly later. Care to join?
The night is silent, like a drop of wine sealed in glass.
Cassian stands before the door and knocks. Two soft "thud, thud" sounds fall, followed by faint stirring from within. A moment later, the door opens.
Falke slouches against the table, a silk robe hanging loose on his shoulders. He has the look of an old beast, smug and sated after feasting on a prey. He glances at Cassian, his tone dismissive.

speaker: Falke
content: Room service? I didn't order anything.

speaker: Cassian
content: My apologies for the intrusion. This is a complimentary offering from Euphoria for our most distinguished guests.

With Falke's nod of approval, Cassian steps inside, his head bowed, and sets a silver tray down on the table. It holds a drink of his own concoction. He uncorks the bottle and pours a glass. The amber liquid swirls, its rich aroma almost overpowering the faint scent of rot in the air.

speaker: Cassian
content: It's your usual blend. I've taken the liberty of making some minor adjustments. I added... something better suited for memories.

speaker: Falke
content: Oh?
He lifts the glass, takes a sip, and raises an eyebrow.

speaker: Falke
content: Not bad at all. When did you come aboard? I don't think I've seen you before.

speaker: Cassian
content: I'm a recent hire.
Cassian's voice stays calm and steady in the dim, hazy lights of the VIP suite. He slowly raises his head, revealing the horrendous scars on his burned face.

speaker: Cassian
content: But I think you have seen me before. You've simply forgotten.
Falke freezes, his expression cracking.

speaker: Falke
content: You are...

Before he can finish, Cassian runs a finger along the rim of the glass. A wisp of vapor rises, and the bouquet twists into invisible blades, piercing deep into Falke's mind. The man's face contorts. The glass slips from his fingers and shatters on the floor.

speaker: Falke
content: What is this... you... you're—!
He finally recognizes the face, the eyes of the boy who once pleaded at his feet. A pained groan escapes Falke's lips as his consciousness splinters under the psychic assault.
Cassian watches coldly, the liquor dancing on his fingertips. All he can see are the shadows of his own past, stretching across an endless night.
On his first day aboard the ship, he'd played the piano and mixed drinks with every ounce of skill he had, all to secure a position on Euphoria.

speaker: Recruiter
content: That scar's an eyesore. Skills are mediocre at best. The only things you've got going for you are these hands... pale, slender fingers, well-proportioned.
He ran his fingers over Cassian's knuckles, examining them like merchandise at an auction. Suddenly, his tone shifted, and he clicked his tongue in mock pity.

speaker: Recruiter
content: Such a shame... They're not soft enough.
Without warning, the man's hand clenched. He snapped Cassian's little finger with a sickening crack.

Cassian let out an agonizing scream. He struggled, but the guards behind him held him fast. Thumb, index finger, middle finger, ring finger. Then the other hand. The excruciating pain seemed to have no end.
Finally, they dumped his limp body in the garbage-strewn rear cabin, like a broken doll.

speaker: Recruiter
content: Don't give me that look. I'm just putting you where you belong. Sleep tight, Mr. Cassian. May you be worth something in your next life.
And earlier, when his family was crushed by false accusations, Cassian had knelt before Falke's expensive leather shoes in his father's old formal suit.

speaker: Falke
content: Begging me? What good will that do? Fate decided that you and your family would serve me. It also decided how you would make your exit.

speaker: Falke
content: If you must hate something, hate yourselves. You weren't born as hawks. No matter how high you climb, you're still doomed to fall to your death.

speaker: Falke
content: Try not to be born in the gutter next time. Now, say your prayers. Serve me one last time.

Then came the screams, the wails, the roaring fire. Through the smoke and ash, his mother's scalding hands touched his burning, bleeding face. "Live," she whispered, before shoving him away, vanishing forever into the void of memory.
Cassian clenches his fist. The amber liquor rises into the air, writhing and contorting before plunging into Falke's eyes, his ears, his nostrils, his mouth.
Falke howls, toppling over his chair. He convulses madly on the floor, his throat producing only torn grunts as he plummets, struggles, drowns in illusions.
Cassian stands motionless, his eyes calm, as though he's looking at someone long dead. He steps forward, crouches, and leans close to Falke's ear.

speaker: Cassian
content: Do you remember? You told me to pray and serve you one last time. So here I am. This judgment... this is the last service you'll have from me.

Several days later
Eastside Hospital
Cassian gets up. He pulls the IV needle from his arm and disconnects the monitors. He takes his clothes from the locker, changes, and quietly slips out of the room.

His last memories of Euphoria are vague. The last thing he remembers is steering the boat carrying the three of them away from the quicksand before exhaustion claimed him. How he got out of WhiteSands, how he ended up back in Eastside... he has no idea.
But none of that matters anymore.
Cassian walks the streets of Eastside like a ghost drifting among the living. Pedestrians hurry past, all of them strangers, indifferent to the story of someone whose shoulder they just brushed.
Only the massive electronic billboard overhead is still tirelessly cycling through the news...

speaker: Newscast
content: <color=#fb9259>[WhiteSands Cruise Ship Explodes, Dozens Missing]</color>

speaker: Newscast
content: <color=#fb9259>[Eastside Official Falke Survives Explosion, in Critical Care with Severe Mental Trauma]</color>
Cassian stares at that familiar face.
The hypocrite who once stood in the light and preached about "justice" now lies inert in a hospital bed, riddled with tubes. People speak of him with a mixture of shock and pity.

speaker: Cassian
content: I won.
He mutters to himself, his words drowned in the city's din.
He remembers himself from years ago, staggering down these same streets, bruised and broken and barely clinging to life, his tattered coat doing little to shelter his skinny frame.

He'd stood beneath this very screen, watching that same man give a smiling interview about "stabilizing the situation" and rooting out "the corrupt parasites." In that moment, hatred had burned like a fire in his blood.
Cassian had imagined his vengeance countless times, fantasizing about dragging that man from his pedestal, watching him weep and beg for mercy.
But now that the fire has burned out, he feels nothing but emptiness.
It's like a piece of his heart is missing, leaving him too numb even for pain. He doesn't know where to go, or what to do next.
His feet carry him, unbidden, to the roof of a skyscraper. He leans against the railing, his gaze empty as he looks down at the city with its rivers of traffic and tides of neon lights.

speaker: Cassian
content: Is it over...? What... should I do now?
He murmurs to no one in particular. He doesn't know if it's a statement or a question. For him, right now, the difference between staying and leaving has become blurred.
Then, he hears a calm voice from behind him.

speaker: You
content: If you're unsure what to do... why not start by helping me with a case?
Cassian turns to see you standing by the door, your gaze deep.

speaker: You
content: Here's the warrant.

speaker: You
content: Mr. Cassian, time is of the essence. Please come with us.

He doesn't resist when you take him back to the Bureau. Not a single question, not a word of protest. He complies in silence, goes through the security checks, surrenders his belongings, gets assigned to his room, following each step like a machine.
That night, during his registration at the Bureau, Cassian gives a shocking testimony: the Euphoria incident likely involved forces from the Underground, and he encountered their puppets on the ship.

He doubts that the ship's owner, Mr. E, is really dead, but he doesn't think the man could have possessed the power to destroy the entire vessel. The true mastermind behind the massive Mania sorcery must be someone else. But his knowledge ends there. The only person who saw the true culprit was Milly, he adds, but she has yet to regain consciousness.
Cassian isn't in good shape. He can't tell you much, and the questioning is cut short. But you know that there are still many unanswered questions—about Euphoria, and about the man himself.

However, the case is tangled in bureaucracy and politics. Many files are still being requested, and the formal interrogation is repeatedly postponed. For now, all you can do is place him in the detention area for observation.
You'd thought his aimlessness on the rooftop that night was temporary, but your observations over the past few days have deepened your unease.
He is too quiet. It's not the quiet of inaction, but of a life disassembled into a series of trivial, silent, orderly motions, like a performance for an empty room.

His tiny room in the detention area is always spotless. His clothes are folded with almost rigid precision, and his cleaning supplies are meticulously arranged. Even his bath towel is folded into a perfect square and placed in the same corner.

You note that Cassian, despite his wealthy upbringing, is surprisingly good at cleaning and keeping himself tidy. Even in the sparse room, he would always fold his meager set of clothes and wipe every last trace of water from the sink.
He seems to require no human contact, only the comfort of a pristine space and precise movements, as if these alone could fill the emptiness within him.
Every evening, he pours a glass of liquor he never drinks. He just holds it by the rim and sits by the window, staring into space from dusk until late into the night.
The day you go to see him, you find him polishing a brooch. A family crest, carved from dark gemstones and set in silver, burnished until it gleams in his hands.
It's the only thing he treats with genuine care each day.

speaker: Cassian
content: It's the only thing I have left of my family. It's beautiful, isn't it?
He speaks softly, his fingers caressing the gem with unusual tenderness. Then he looks up at you, his voice calm like he's stating a simple fact.

speaker: Cassian
content: You've been watching me. It's all right. I've known for a while.
You're taken aback, but he merely offers a faint smile before lowering his eyes again.

speaker: Cassian
content: There's no need to be so guarded. I won't do anything you don't want me to. I won't cause you any trouble.

His tone is polite, gentle, even considerate. But beneath it, you hear a submission so absolute it feels like the stillness of death. It's not the result of rational self-restraint, but the instinctive response of someone who has completely given up on himself.

speaker: You
content: ...We need to talk.
You say it after a moment's silence. He nods, rises to his feet, and silently follows you into the interrogation room.

The interrogation room is sterile, the lights cold. Cassian sits across from you, eyes downcast, quiet as a statue robbed of its soul. You don't cut to the chase. Instead, you flip through a case file and speak in a casual tone, as if to make small talk.

speaker: You
content: Quite eventful lately, isn't it? After that night on Euphoria, Falke had a complete mental breakdown. They managed to save his life, but his prognosis isn't looking good.

speaker: You
content: This is no small matter. His doctor thinks it's trauma from the explosion, but I can't shake the feeling there's more to it than that.
You pause, looking up at him.

speaker: You
content: You were on Euphoria that night, Cassian. What do you know?
The enemies still alive... where are they hiding?

speaker: Cassian
content: I did it.

speaker: You
content: ...You're admitting it, just like that?
Your hands pause over the file, your eyes betraying your astonishment. You're taken aback by his frankness, but he simply nods, his tone calm and forthright.

speaker: Cassian
content: Yes, I used my ability to cause Falke's mental breakdown.

speaker: Cassian
content: You can lock me up right now. Prosecute me according to your regulations.

speaker: Cassian
content: The case is closed, Chief. You don't need to waste any more time on this. I won't cover up what I've done.
