His voice is devoid of emotion, as if he has already passed judgment on himself and is ready to accept any verdict. As if he's actively seeking punishment. But you shake your head, your gaze settling on his gaunt face.
He's just a man who's lost everything, struggling to survive in the wreckage. His methods may have been extreme, nearly costing him his own life, but this isn't the time to be assigning blame.

speaker: You
content: I'm not here to press charges. I'm more interested in your help investigating Falke's other crimes than in judging you for what you've done.
For the first time, a flicker of surprise crosses his face.

speaker: You
content: The reason Falke survived, despite his mental breakdown, is that one of his powerful old friends took him along during the escape. But that same friend threw him to the wolves the moment they were back in the city.

speaker: You
content: He's accusing Falke of being involved in several cold cases. The media is sitting on the story for now, but the news is already spreading like wildfire through Eastside's upper crust.

speaker: You
content: Falke's finished. His so-called allies are scrambling to distance themselves, pointing fingers, cutting ties, kicking him while he's down. It's quite the show.

speaker: You
content: Given the stakes, we've joined the investigation. But there are still gaps to fill, crucial information that only insiders can provide. Someone like you.
You pause, studying his tired but composed face.

speaker: You
content: None of this surprises you, does it?
Cassian lets out a short, bitter laugh, his eyes full of scorn.

speaker: Cassian
content: Not at all. That's how they are. They lick the boots of whoever's in power and walk over anyone who falls from grace. One day you're the guest of honor, the next you're a worthless pawn.

speaker: Cassian
content: It's exactly what happened to my family. He lifted us to the heavens overnight, then kicked us straight into hell. Now it's his turn. What goes around, comes around.
The contempt in his voice is sharp as a razor's edge. But beneath it, you hear something else: a wound that will never heal, the harsh echo of a cruel era still weighing on his shoulders.
His cynicism isn't baseless. It was forged in blood and fire.

You watch his pale face in the brief silence. His eyes are hard and cold, but you notice the almost imperceptible slump of his shoulders, as though he's running out of the strength to hold himself upright.
You suddenly realize that he seems more lost than ever, a traveler derailed, pushed forward only by inertia. You soften your voice.

speaker: You
content: I've heard about what happened back then. In fact, that's why I'm here. Your family was innocent, weren't they?

speaker: Cassian
content: Of course. Falke used them as scapegoats. My father took his own life. My mother died in the fire. The rest were either framed for crimes they didn't commit or died in "accidents."
Cassian nods, his eyes showing no flicker of emotion, only a frozen darkness.

speaker: Cassian
content: I was the only one who made it out alive. The only one they managed to save.
The air grows still. You sense that what hangs between you isn't anger or grief, but something deeper, a fathomless, suffocating weight.
He is leaning slightly forward. It seems his body is present, but his soul has drifted away.

speaker: You
content: ...So that's why you kept going? To get revenge for them?

speaker: Cassian
content: Yes.
He nods without a second of hesitation.

speaker: Cassian
content: I wanted to kill him. But I couldn't control my ability as well as I'd like to. He survived.

speaker: Cassian
content: But it's better this way. Letting him live, broken and trapped in his own head... he deserves a fate worse than death.

For the first time, you hear a raw, potent emotion in his voice. A sharp, searing hatred that burns away everything else. You understand, then, that this hatred was the only thing keeping him alive. Revenge was his raison d'être.
The Interrogation room falls into a prolonged silence, until you finally speak in a low voice:

speaker: You
content: Now that you've had your revenge... are you happy?
Cassian laughs.

speaker: Cassian
content: Of course I am. The one thing I kept myself alive for is done. What more could I possibly want?
His tone is so light it's almost cruel, and it makes your chest tighten.

Cassian has accomplished the life goal he set for himself. The vengeful obsession that kept him alive has burned itself out. Now, he's an empty shell that has fulfilled its purpose, with nowhere else to go.
He is no longer living. He merely stays.

speaker: You
content: So what did this revenge get you, in the end?

speaker: Cassian
content: Closure. For my family, who were toyed with and murdered by those in power.
You keep your emotions in check and ask calmly:

speaker: You
content: But what about you?
Cassian falters. A brief, fleeting confusion crosses his face. He falls silent, struggling to find an answer to a question he's never bothered to ask himself.
After a long while, he slowly shakes his head.

speaker: Cassian
content: I... don't matter. What matters is that I did what I had to do. It's all over.
You look into his eyes, which seem incapable of reflecting a future, and find yourself at a loss for words. You finally realize that what he truly lost wasn't his family or his dignity, but himself.
You speak softly:

speaker: You
content: So you're planning to end it all, is that it?

speaker: Cassian
content: Perhaps.
He says it with a slight curve of his lips, almost like a smile.

speaker: You
content: But they fought so hard to keep you alive. I don't think they did it just for "closure."
In that moment, you see the tips of Cassian's fingers tremble.
But he says nothing, and lowers his head again.

speaker: Option
options: Stop pressing and change the subject

content: You're the first to break the silence. You gather the documents on the table and nod at him.

speaker: You
content: In any case, thank you for your cooperation. I have the basics now. That's all for today.

speaker: You
content: But I'll need you to come with me for the next couple of days.
Cassian looks up, his eyes sharp.

speaker: Cassian
content: If you're planning to take me on a field trip and "rekindle my passion for life," please don't trouble yourself.
His voice is cold, laced with undisguised resistance and detachment.

speaker: Cassian
content: I don't need it. And it would be pointless.

speaker: You
content: You misunderstand. I'm going to file a petition to clear your family's name. That old case is clearly tied to Falke, so it falls within the scope of our current investigation. I thought having you there, as a directly affected party, would make our case more compelling.
You pause and look up at him with sincere eyes. You want him to see that you're not doing this out of pity, but out of equality and respect.

speaker: You
content: It's long overdue, but at least we can restore their honor. I thought that might be something you'd want to do. Or something you should do. Isn't it?
Cassian clearly never expected to hear anything like this. His eyes widen in surprise.
After a moment, you hear him say:

speaker: Cassian
content: Thank you.
The next day, you compile everything Cassian mentioned during the interrogation into a detailed report. After reading it through, word by word, he finally nods and agrees to go with you.
You soon arrive at the department in charge and go through the procedures: submitting the materials, meeting with the officers, confirming your petition, and giving testimony.
The process is cold, but efficient enough. Once everything is done, you let out a long sigh of relief and stretch your stiff shoulders.

speaker: You
content: Phew... finally done. Now we just wait for their investigation and follow-up. How are you holding up?
You smile at Cassian, and he turns to meet your gaze, his lips curved up.

speaker: Cassian
content: I'm alright, thanks to you.
But in that same moment, his gaze freezes.
You notice his expression change. Following his line of sight, you spot a well-dressed young man strolling down the hallway.
The moment his eyes meet Cassian's, the young man stops. A flash of surprise crosses his face, quickly replaced by a gentle, yet inscrutable, smile.

speaker: Young Noble
content: ...Ah. I never thought I'd see you here.
He walks toward you, his voice calm yet tinged with patronizing regret, like he's commenting on an old trinket gathering dust for too long.

speaker: Young Noble
content: You've changed. Even your eyes aren't the same. You used to look at us so cautiously, as if terrified that one wrong move would get you thrown out.
You feel Cassian tense beside you imperceptibly. He says nothing, eyes downcast, reining in some roiling emotion.

speaker: Young Noble
content: It's a good thing.
For a split second, you notice the whiteness of Cassian's knuckles and sense a kind of bewilderment—not anger, but a much deeper-seated weariness.
He has achieved his long-sought revenge, and he is no longer the child desperate for acceptance. But in doing so, he's lost his purpose, uncertain what he's even living for now.
The young noble finally glances your way, his eyes sweeping over you as if you're an insignificant prop on a stage.

speaker: Young Noble
content: A new friend?

speaker: Cassian
content: This is ${PlayerName}, Chief of the MBCC.
The young noble is taken aback, and his expression becomes guarded and complex. His smile softens, however, now laced with a veiled probing and mockery, like a blade in the water.

speaker: Young Noble
content: I see. You always were... good at choosing the right people to keep close. In that sense, you haven't changed much at all.
He turns to you, his tone taking on a gentlemanly warmth.

speaker: Young Noble
content: It's a pleasure to make your acquaintance, esteemed Chief from the Bureau. I hear you've been terribly busy lately. We appreciate your hard work.
His tone is proper, his attitude civil, but his eyes scan you with unconcealed appraisal, trying to judge whether you are worthy of his courtesy.
Though you find this pompous youth rather distasteful, you're compelled to give a slight nod out of politeness. He doesn't seem to care, just smiles before steering the conversation back to Cassian.

speaker: Young Noble
content: He was always like this, you know. Always knew how to make people "like" him. Especially when he needed something from you.
He says it nonchalantly, with the air of someone reminiscing about a harmless past, yet every word is meant to pick at old wounds.

speaker: Young Noble
content: In our circles, he was always... quite the likable figure. Docile, proper, understanding, never stepping out of line. He always smiled at the right moment and said the right words, just like...
He pauses, his smile deepening. His voice is light as a feather, but carries the hidden prick of a thorn.

speaker: Young Noble
content: Like he was carefully tamed.

speaker: Young Noble
content: Back then...
Cassian was still a boy when his life veered off course.

His father, a low-level clerk, happened to meet Falke, an influential official from Eastside, during a government function. Unexpectedly catching Falke's eye, he was quickly promoted, his career soaring and his family rising with him.
From then on, Cassian's family was no longer obscure. They were catapulted into Eastside's political scene, the "lucky newcomers" in the spotlight of high society.

The family was swept into that world, and Cassian was quickly transferred to an academy for nobles, where he took classes, dined, and attended festivals and balls with peers who were born with silver spoons in their mouths.
But Cassian and his family knew that simply entering that world was not enough. Truly securing their footing would be the real struggle they had to endure.

speaker: Father
content: Cassian. I know this will be exhausting and hard to accept. But I need you to understand that we are different from the other families.

speaker: Father
content: We're ordinary people who stumbled into fortune. But at the end of the day, we're not one of them, and perhaps we never can be...

speaker: Father
content: The things we fight tooth and nail for are things they get without lifting a finger. So you must always be mindful of your words and actions. Be humble and polite to everyone. That's the only way you won't give them a reason to find fault.

speaker: Father
content: You must always appreciate what we have now. Know that this is all due to luck, and just preserving it will be difficult enough.
Cassian, of course, understood. The precocious boy had seen the arrogance and recklessness of his peers, yet never once thought to imitate them.
He knew that he was not one of them. Only by treading carefully could he carve out a small space for himself in the margins of their world.
Beyond earning excellent grades every year, he had put in so much more effort: dining etiquette, art appreciation, ballroom dancing, golf, wine tasting, musical instruments...
He mastered every skill associated with the upper class. To be worthy of his new status, he applied himself diligently to everything, never daring to slack off.

speaker: Mother
content: Darling, you're too hard on yourself. Let yourself relax, please?

speaker: Cassian
content: Don't worry, Mom. I know what I'm doing.

speaker: Cassian
content: I'm not being hard on myself. I'm learning to become the person I need to be. Maybe when I fit in, I can make true friends.
That was how Cassian reassured his mother.
But he knew it was a mere fantasy. Those people never had any intention of accepting him. He would always be standing on the wrong side of the door.
Even so, he had to keep going.

speaker: Classmate A
content: Cassian's quite pretty, isn't he? I heard Miss Carr from the other class wants him to be her boyfriend. She's been sending him afternoon tea treats.

speaker: Classmate B
content: Really? That Miss Carr who goes through boyfriends like tissues? You know how she likes to pick her playthings from among the commoners. She'll get bored and toss him aside. Doesn't that mean... hee hee.

speaker: Teacher A
content: Cassian is a sensible boy who knows his place. He does whatever I ask without a mistake, which is wonderful. Having such an obedient student who's at your beck and call makes our lives so much easier.

speaker: Teacher B
content: His grades are exceptional, but you know... grades alone are worthless here.

speaker: Councilor A
content: Their son? Of course we know him. He has the most beautiful hands. It's a pleasure to watch them, whether he's playing the piano or mixing a drink.

speaker: Councilor B
content: To be fair, the boy is certainly talented. He works hard, and he's better than most. But you know Falke. He didn't promote that family out of some laughable "appreciation." It's best to keep your distance.

speaker: Councilor A
content: Tsk, tsk. What a shame.
The teasing remarks came disguised as compliments, but Cassian keenly sensed that in their eyes, he was nothing more than a novel, entertaining object.
The mockery in their tone, the relish in their eyes, the perverse amusement... they never felt the need to hide them.

speaker: Classmate A
content: Cassian used to be a commoner. He lived on that street on the west end of Eastside. What kind of street is that? I don't know... Ugh, of course I've never been to a place like that. I never would.

speaker: Classmate B
content: Cassian, I hear you play the piano well. My father's pianist fell ill. Why don't you take his place and perform for our dinner party? Don't keep everyone waiting.

speaker: Elite A
content: The way you hold your glass is quite convincing! A pity it's just an imitation. True elegance comes from one's breeding, and you... ah, sadly, you weren't born with it.

speaker: Elite B
content: My dear, we don't really need your opinion. You're pretty enough that just standing here is your ticket in. So promise me you won't think too hard, alright? A beautiful vase doesn't need to think. Neither do you.
Faced with such blatant mockery, such malicious scrutiny, Cassian maintained his composure and never dropped his pleasant smile. Yet only he knew that his heart was already scarred by fractures.
Swallow all the contempt and humiliation. Endure all the prejudice and cold stares. This is life. Grind up the pain, force it down your throat, and smile.

speaker: Cassian
content: Even if they never thought of me as one of them.

speaker: Cassian
content: Even if they never planned on leaving a corner for me to stand in.

speaker: Cassian
content: Even if we will never, ever exist in the same world.

...But what does it matter? His father was still trying to master the art of socializing he was so bad at. His mother was hosting every dinner with anxious care. His aunts and uncles were exhausted with pleasantries at tea parties, forcing themselves to keep up a facade of grace.
Cassian couldn't turn a blind eye to the efforts of his family, and he must do the same: he must endure, ignore the malice, and keep climbing.
He couldn't allow himself to stop. He couldn't allow himself to fall.
So he learned to be numb, forgot how to feel pain, and abandoned himself. He became a weightless shadow, existing only for his family and their "honor."
As the shadows of the past fade away, the face of the man before him overlaps with memories that feel like they belong to another lifetime. For a moment, it all seems absurdly comical.
After everything he's been through, Cassian is no longer the same person he once was.
He looks coolly at this "old friend." Even from the sofa, looking up, Cassian keeps his back straight. He unclenches his fist, and a sardonic smile slowly spreads across his lips.

speaker: Cassian
content: After all these years, you haven't changed at all. But I don't need to be your dog anymore.
His voice is calm, but his words are sharp as blades. The man freezes, as if he didn't understand.

speaker: Cassian
content: So stop clinging to the past. You're not a child anymore, still obsessing over who climbed up from where. It just sounds... pathetic.

The words aren't loud or heated, but they land squarely on the man's pride like a dull blow. This is the first time Cassian has ever, in the light of day, returned the spite he was given. He will no longer tolerate their malice. He will no longer stay silent.
It's true, he has nothing now. But it also means he no longer has to live at their mercy.
The young noble's face darkens. He opens his mouth as if to argue, but fumbles for words. His eyes dart around for a moment before landing back on you, and he forces a strained smile.

speaker: Young Noble
content: Heh. You talk tough now that you've found a new master.

speaker: Young Noble
content: But you're still the same, always climbing up on someone else's back. Don't say I didn't warn you. You should remember very well... how you got in, and how you came crashing down.

speaker: You
content: Rest assured, we both have excellent memories. But some things won't be happening again.
You raise an eyebrow at the young noble and cut in coldly, your tone official and direct.

speaker: You
content: He is now a consulting investigator for the MBCC and a key figure in our ongoing case concerning Eastside elites.

speaker: You
content: Given the current climate, I'm sure a man as smart and respectable as yourself understands that some people are no longer yours to order around.

He glares at you, his face pale. You can see he desperately wants to fire back, but is likely deterred by your title as Chief of the MBCC. Swallowing his anger, the young noble forces out a "Fine, fine," and beats a hasty, undignified retreat.
You spread your hands and give Cassian an innocent shrug.

speaker: You
content: Was it something I said? Why'd he get so worked up?
Cassian looks down and chuckles softly, shaking his head. There's a resigned look in his eyes.

speaker: Cassian
content: I'm sorry. I put you in a difficult position.

speaker: You
content: Not at all. I was just telling the truth.
You pause, your voice firm and sincere.

speaker: You
content: Cassian, I've never once thought you needed to depend on anyone. Even if you once forgot who you were, you should know by now—you are not, and never have been, anyone's accessory.
He looks up at you, and for a second, you see a flicker disturb the calm of his eyes, like ripples on still water.

speaker: You
content: You've always been yourself.

speaker: You
content: Since we're already here, why don't we stop by and see someone?
When you suggest visiting his "uncle" at Eastside Prison, Cassian's expression changes. For a moment, he says nothing.

speaker: Cassian
content: I'm not going.
His voice is low and final, a gut reaction. He abruptly stops walking, his shoulders tense.
You stop too and look at him, confused.

speaker: You
content: From what I've heard, he isn't one of your relatives, but you were close. He worked with your family for years. Were you not on good terms?

speaker: Cassian
content: No. We were. That's why I...
Cassian smiles bitterly and avoids your gaze.

speaker: Cassian
content: He was my father's best friend. He watched me grow up, and I... I haven't seen him in years.

speaker: Cassian
content: During that conspiracy, my family knew they were doomed. But they fought with their last breath to save my life.

speaker: Cassian
content: Uncle helped me so much... but he ended up in prison because of us. I dragged him down with me. And now I've ended up like this. How am I supposed to face him?
His fingers instinctively drift to the scar on his cheek before falling back to his side.
You look at him and let out a soft sigh.

speaker: You
content: But he deserves to hear the good news. And you're the only one who has the right to deliver it. Isn't that right?
Cassian falls silent. He wants to object, but can't find the strength. Something tightens in his throat, making it hard to breathe.
In the end, he goes with you.

The prison visiting room is stark and silent. Cassian sits on one side of the transparent partition, his head bowed, though his back is ramrod straight. His face looks even more haggard in the bleak gray light.
His fingertips dig into his knees, as if clinging to his last line of retreat.
He stiffens when the door is pushed open.

The heavy iron door creaks open. The footsteps that enter are slow, but as steady as they've always been. The man is dressed in a prison uniform. His face is weathered and his black hair streaked with gray, but he still carries himself with a hint of his old dignity.
Cassian recognizes him instantly. At the same moment, the man he's always known as his uncle sees him.
Time seems to stop. Cassian's heart hammers against his ribs, his breath catching in his chest.
He hangs his head awkwardly, unable to meet the man's eyes, trying to hide the scar on his face with his hair. He tucks his hands behind his back, anxiously twisting the hem of his shirt.
He's afraid.
Afraid of being blamed. Afraid of seeing disappointment. Afraid of being asked: we gave everything to save you, why did you turn out this way?
But the man seems lost for words.
He slowly approaches the partition. From a pocket close to his chest, he carefully removes a yellowed photograph.
It's an old photo of him with Cassian's family. The image is worn from being touched over and over, its corners curled, the creases nearly torn.
He gazes at the picture for a long while before finally looking up at Cassian, his eyes gentle in a way that seems impossible for someone imprisoned for years.
A smile slowly spreads across his face. He raises a hand to his own shoulder.

speaker: Uncle
content: You've grown up.

speaker: Uncle
content: The last time I saw you, you were only... about this tall.
At those words, Cassian jerks his head up, his eyes wide with bewilderment. His throat feels tight, his chest heaving.
No blame.
No criticism of his failure, no questions about why he had taken so long, not even the slightest trace of resentment.
Just that simple, almost clumsy phrase: "You've grown up." As if all these years, he hadn't been waiting for vindication or release. He was only waiting to know that this child was still alive.
Cassian stares at him, stunned.

He sees how much has changed in this man, his father's closest friend, who used to clap him on the shoulder and say with a laugh, "Your dad was even more of a troublemaker than you back then." Gone is his former vigor. His shoulders are thin, his eyes wrinkled at the corners, his lips pale and chapped. Even his voice is raspy.
And still, he smiles.
As if nothing has changed, as if time hasn't taken anything away. As if he's still standing at the door, waiting for Cassian to come home from school.
Suddenly, Cassian can't breathe.

speaker: Cassian
content: Sorry...
His voice is choked and broken, almost like his throat is run through with rusty nails.

speaker: Cassian
content: I... couldn't protect anything.
He covers his face, the metal of the finger brace pressed against his scar. The wound feels raw again, the pain churning through his flesh.
Watching his shoulders tremble, you finally understand.

He has never been unfeeling. He simply buries all his pain in silence, tucks it away inside the brooch he keeps in his pocket but never wears, hides it in the finger brace he cannot remove and the past he dares not touch.
And in this moment, he finally allows himself to cry.
The older man raises his shackled hands and gently presses them to the visitor's window. His rough, dry fingers are covered in tiny cracks, but they're still warm.

speaker: Uncle
content: You're alive.
He says softly.

speaker: Uncle
content: You're here before me. That alone... is enough.
The visitation time is over, and Cassian watches his uncle disappear behind the door. He follows you in a daze, bumping into people without seeming to notice.

speaker: You
content: The paperwork is in. Once Falke's crimes are made public, your uncle's exoneration will be processed immediately.

speaker: You
content: You'll be able to bring him home soon. You two can finally start a proper life together.

It's a beautiful day. The sun is shining, and the chattering of birds seems to rouse every slumbering soul. The streets are bustling with crowds and traffic; even the car horns sound unusually cheerful and alive.
For the first time, it dawns on Cassian:
Perhaps the past isn't beyond repair.
Maybe... he could rebuild connections. Earn the right to live. Be accepted by the world again.
Out of habit, Cassian reaches into his pocket to touch the family brooch he always carries with him. It's what he does whenever he needs strength.
This time, his fingers stop short.

speaker: You
content: Cassian? What's wrong?
Noticing his pause, you stop and turn to him. Under the bright sun, his face has gone deathly pale.

speaker: Cassian
content: My brooch. It's gone.
He frantically pats down every pocket, but the cherished brooch is nowhere to be found. And with it, his wallet is gone, too.

speaker: Cassian
content: My brooch is gone... What do I do...

The sun is still bright, the streets bustling with life, but he looks like he's just fallen into a bottomless abyss. You see his fingers tremble, his face ashen. His breathing grows ragged, as if he's about to collapse.

speaker: You
content: Stay calm, Cassian. Take a deep breath.
You gently place your hand on his shoulder and speak in a soft, reassuring voice.

speaker: You
content: Try to think. Did you leave it somewhere? Or... did you notice anyone, anything unusual?

Your calm voice is a tether that pulls him back from the edge of panic. Cassian closes his eyes, forcing himself to rewind the chaotic last few minutes in his mind. Before long, he snaps them open again, his voice sharp with urgency.

speaker: Cassian
content: Yes... The kid who bumped into me.
You follow his gaze. There, amid the busy crowd, a small figure is peeking around a street corner. He bolts the second his eyes meet yours.

speaker: Cassian
content: That's him!
He takes off after the kid, and you follow close behind.
Cassian chases the kid through the streets and alleys like a possessed man, sunlight shattering behind him against the grimy walls.
He practically throws himself at the boy, tackling him to the ground and clutching his collar.

speaker: Cassian
content: Give it back!
He growls through gritted teeth. The boy, clearly terrified, flails his bony arms and struggles desperately, eyes filled with defiance and fear.

speaker: Child
content: Let me GO! What's your problem?! I didn't do nothin'!
Despite being caught red-handed, he's still spitting denials, kicking and thrashing like a trapped animal. But he's too small and thin to break an adult's hold.
Cassian frowns as he fishes his wallet and brooch out of the kid's pocket. Seeing his prize reclaimed, the boy gives up fighting and hollers at the top of his lungs:

speaker: Child
content: Fine! Take your shiny junk! But the wallet was my score. It's MINE!
The sheer brazenness is almost funny.

speaker: You
content: Are you kidding me...
Grrrumble...
A hollow, distinct rumble cuts you off. It's coming from the boy's stomach, and his face flushes red.

For the first time, you get a good look at the young thief. He's frighteningly skinny, his face and arms caked with dirt. His clothes are so ragged they look like they were pulled from a dumpster. It's clear he hasn't had a real meal in a very long time.

speaker: Child
content: Hey! Let me go! You hear me?!
He starts yelling again, his voice hoarse and shrill. But Cassian meets the boy's eyes and freezes, nailed to the spot.
The look of rage, resentment, and stubborn pride, all wrapped around a core of stinging humiliation and helplessness.

He's struck by a sickening sense of familiarity. He knows that look. The look of being backed into a corner and trampled by fate. He's seen it staring back at him from the mirror more times than he can count.

After losing his parents, family, and home, he'd kneeled in cramped alleys just like this one, hands bloody, forcing down scraps of leftover bread and telling himself, "As long as I stay alive, there's still a chance."
He'd curled up at the feet of drunks, trading his silence for a sip of water and a place to sleep for the night.
He'd knocked on doors that led who knows where and handed over a forged resume, bowing and thanking them again and again, only to be met with sneers. "You think trash like you can get in?"

He remembers his first gig off the books, when he was tossed into a squalid dorm for temp workers. As he huddled against a cold, damp bunk, covered in bruises, someone next to him muttered, "Just accept it. People like us are lucky to get scraps."
To this day, he can still feel the way he'd gritted his teeth, swallowing his dignity inch by painful inch.

He'd been through it all, the hardship, the indignity. He'd done things he wasn't proud of just to survive. He'd been caught, mocked, and humiliated, and prayed they would just let him go, all while feeling bitter resentment toward the easy lives others led.
He wasn't the only one in this world who held a grudge, nor the only one desperately struggling to stay alive in the mire of society's lowest depths.
The boy's glare summoned it all back—the desperation, the pain, the tangled mess of emotions from his past.

speaker: Child
content: Hey!
The boy's voice trembles, but he's still staring defiantly at Cassian.

speaker: Child
content: You gonna call the cops? Go on! Been caught twice already. What's one more time...

Cassian snaps out of his memories and looks at the objects clutched in his hand: the wallet and the brooch. He carefully returns the brooch to his pocket. Then he shoves the wallet back into the boy's hands.

speaker: Cassian
content: I'm not forgiving you. It's just... I've walked this path before.
He lets go of the boy and stands up. The kid stares for a second, looking from the wallet in his hand to Cassian, his expression uncertain.

speaker: Child
content: ...You really giving this to me?
Cassian doesn't answer, only says calmly:

speaker: Cassian
content: Go get something to eat.
The boy opens and closes his mouth. In the end, he says in a small voice:

speaker: Child
content: Thanks... for the gift. I'll give it to uncle and auntie. They'll get everyone somethin' nice to eat.
He keeps his head down, awkwardly picking at the grimy hem of his shirt. Then he points toward a cluster of dilapidated buildings in the distance.

speaker: Child
content: See, that's where I live. So... I can get going now?
Seeing that neither of you makes any move to stop him, he visibly relaxes, then spins around and scurries away.
A breeze passes through the alley. The sky is still bright, and a narrow strip of sunlight filters into the alley, falling into Cassian's eyes.
He stands there for a moment, staring in the direction the boy had gone, lost in thought.

speaker: Cassian
content: Nothing. It's just... I used to live in that direction.
He turns to you hesitantly, a hint of uncertainty and questioning in his eyes. He seems to be asking if he has reason, if he is allowed, to return to a place he left behind so long ago.

speaker: Cassian
content: Can I... go take a look?

speaker: You
content: Of course.
You smile at him. The answer is easy. Side by side, you walk with him toward the familiar, yet foreign, neighborhood of his past.
You follow the boy through the broken patchwork of the city's labyrinthine gray alleys, before finally stopping before the rusted iron gate of an abandoned construction site.
The boy's about to slip inside when he whirls around and sees you. He looks panicked.

speaker: Child
content: Why... why'd you follow me? I... I told you I'd share the food...
Before you can explain, he grabs your hands in a huff and pulls you inside.

speaker: Child
content: I'm not lying! Hmph, come see for yourself!
As you push open the gate, you're met with a wave of damp air, thick with the smell of smoke and dust. But as you step inside the shabby old building, you're greeted by the clamor of life.

Someone is tending a fire in a corner with an old kettle perched on a metal bucket, merrily bubbling away. An old woman is mending clothes for children, muttering, "Gotta stitch 'em tight now, the wind gets sharp at night."

A few drifters are huddled in a corner of the hallway, playing chess with beer caps, their laughter and friendly curses bouncing off the walls. A discarded kaleidoscope mirror hangs on the exposed concrete, next to a handwritten list of "Rules": "Food served in order" and "Elderly & kids first."
This is a haven for the homeless in the area, a pocket of warmth tucked away in the city's forgotten corner.
You're spotted the moment you step inside. A middle-aged man with a salt-and-pepper stubble approaches, grinning as he ruffles the boy's hair.

speaker: Vagrant A
content: Hey there, little fella. Who'd you bring back today? My, you're dressed nice. Don't look like our kind.

speaker: Child
content: They helped me earlier. I invited them over.

speaker: Vagrant B
content: Guests are always welcome! Make yourselves at home.
Another man brings you two bowls of hot soup. It tastes of tomato and crushed beans, thin, but warm.

speaker: Vagrant B
content: We might be poor, and this place might be a mess, but at least we have hot soup!

speaker: Vagrant C
content: Hey kid! I made some extra coin today and bought the good stuff! Want a taste?

speaker: Child
content: Nope! I'm still a kid, I'm not old enough to drink that!
The abandoned building echoes with the laughter of people beaten down by life. It's not hard to imagine them holding each other up through the hardest days, their hearts full of hope for the future.
Cassian's expression softens as he watches them. You can't help but smile.

speaker: You
content: You look much better now.

speaker: Cassian
content: Yes. This place... it reminds me of the old days.

speaker: You
content: I heard you grew up in the commoners' district?

speaker: Cassian
content: I did. We lived in a cramped apartment building. It was an unremarkable place, a little run-down, even.
His gaze drifts, seeing into the distant past.

speaker: Cassian
content: My mother was an office clerk, and my father worked a low-level government job. He was on the bottom rung of the ladder and never had a chance to climb up.

speaker: Cassian
content: We had many good neighbors. Everyone was always looking out for each other. They'd remind you to bring in the laundry when it rained, help babysit the kids, and save a hot meal for anyone coming home late.

speaker: Cassian
content: And my parents... they were never unhappy with that life. They both worked long hours, but every Friday night, we'd always have curry together.

speaker: Cassian
content: My mother wasn't much of a cook. It was the only dish she knew how to make well. And my father would always come home with some fruit he got on sale, saying it was "to celebrate the weekend."
His lips curve gently in a smile, like he's pulling a precious, long-untouched memory from the ashes, carefully brushing off the dust.

speaker: Cassian
content: We didn't have money or power. It was a simple life. But... back then, I truly believed the world was a beautiful place.

speaker: You
content: ...Your parents sound like wonderful people.
Cassian nods, his gaze drifting to the lightwell, which frames a patch of shattered blue sky.

speaker: Cassian
content: My mother always used to say, "Cassian, no matter who you grow up to be, never forget that you are loved."
The warmth of those bygone days touches a tender place deep within his heart. His features soften, and a faint smile touches his eyes.
Ding... Dong... CLANG!

A few jarring piano notes ring out from the other end of the building. You and Cassian exchange a glance and follow the sound, pushing through a few rickety fire doors until you reach a dim, old warehouse.

The floor is cluttered with junk, and the corners are thick with cobwebs. Yet a group of children are gathered around an upright piano covered in charred scorch marks, banging on the keys and making a racket.

speaker: You
content: A piano? In a place like this?
You're surprised. One of the adults nearby explains:

speaker: Vagrant A
content: Why not? The thing still works! A few of us found it at the dump.

speaker: Vagrant A
content: Probably tossed after a fire in some rich family's house. It's burned, sure, but the keys still make a noise, so we hauled it back. The kids love it.
Beside you, Cassian looks as if he's been struck. He walks toward the piano, almost in a trance.

You watch as he stares at it, his hand trembling as he reaches out to trace the burnt wood, his fingers finally settling on the keys. A string of notes flows from his fingertips, sending ripples through the dusty air.
It's his piano. The one he practiced on every day since he was eight.
The chip on the leg... he'd done that himself while messing around. His mother put the flower sticker on the lid to encourage him to keep playing.
And most striking of all are the burns—the marks left by the fire, seared deep into the wood grain like old scars.

speaker: Child
content: Oooh, you know how to play! Play something for us! Play a song!
The children gather around him, their faces bright with excitement. But Cassian just stands there, frozen, his fingers trembling.

speaker: Cassian
content: I-I'm not very good. My hands... they are...

speaker: Child
content: It doesn't matter! Your hands are pretty! Please, just play one song for us!
These same words, once spoken by those in power, now come from the lips of innocent children. Miraculously, Cassian finds himself calming down.
In the end, he sits down. He lets his fingers drift over the keys, and slowly, haltingly, he presses the first note.
It's that song. The one his mother loved. Gentle, slow, like the first thaw of spring.

As his fingers touch the keys, all the emotions he's been holding back begin to pour out through the broken melody. The piano is badly out of tune, and several keys are dead. His scarred hands are clumsy, slow, unable to keep a steady rhythm.
But in this moment, none of it matters.
What matters is that he is playing.

It is the boy he used to be who is playing, the tender part of him that never died. It is the deepest part of his soul, the part that longs to be understood and accepted again, reawakened here in this derelict building, in the sincere gaze of a group of strangers.
Someone quietly turns away to wipe at their eyes. Another hums along softly to the melody. For the first time, the children fall quiet, listening with rapt attention.
Cassian keeps playing. He can feel a heavy warmth slowly enveloping his stiff body.
The broken fingers, the struggles in the trash dump, all the years of hardship... they are all dissolving in the broken melody, fading like dust motes in the morning sun.
All that remains is the memory of a beautiful past, where his eternally patient, gentle mother smiles and softly strokes his hair.

speaker: Mother
content: Cassian, my child. You've really grown up.
The evening breeze blows through the old district's streets, and puddles shimmer in the cracks between the cobblestones.
You and Cassian walk side-by-side. In the streetlights, your faint shadows part and merge in the wind. The sky is a tranquil steel blue. The stars have yet to appear, and the city is still awake.
He suddenly breaks the silence, his voice as low as ever, but more genuine than ever before.

speaker: Cassian
content: Thank you. And I mean that.
He looks down at his hands—hands that once coaxed the piano, hands that once held onto hate. The knuckles are somewhat stiff, the palms covered in fine, thin calluses.

speaker: Cassian
content: It's... finally over.
There's a weariness in his tone, but also relief.

speaker: Cassian
content: If I'd met you sooner, maybe things could have been different. But it's too late for that now.
You stop and stand before him, your gaze steady and sure.

speaker: You
content: No, it's not too late at all.

speaker: Cassian
content: Why? My hands are ruined. I can't play anymore. I can only use my ability to... My life is a complete failure.
He looks at you, bemused, a flicker of doubt in his eyes. He looks as if he can't believe what you said, or as if he's refusing an answer he's never allowed himself to hope for.

speaker: You
content: You call yourself a failure. But I see someone who's been through hell and is still standing.

speaker: You
content: You've endured so much hardship and suffering. You've been betrayed, misunderstood, exploited by so many people, yet still, you made it through. That in itself is incredible, Cassian.
The wind sweeps through the alley, rustling the hem of his shirt. He slowly lifts his head.

speaker: You
content: All this time, you've been trying your best to turn yourself into the person others wanted you to be. Driven by pressure and duty, you were forced to do things that you had to do.

speaker: You
content: But starting today, you no longer need to be chained by expectations, or duty, or hatred. You can just live as Cassian. You can be your true self.

speaker: You
content: So maybe this isn't the end. It's a new beginning.

speaker: You
content: You're free, Cassian.

speaker: Cassian
content: Free...
He says the word softly, as if he's hearing it for the first time, or for the first time in a very long while. He looks lost for a moment, then shakes his head.

speaker: Cassian
content: I don't even know what I really want.

speaker: You
content: That's okay. Figuring out who you are and what you want... it's a long journey for anyone.

speaker: You
content: And you took the first step today, didn't you?

speaker: Cassian
content: I did? When?

speaker: You
content: When you stood up to that arrogant noble. When you let that kid go. When you chose to play the piano for those people.

speaker: You
content: That's a pretty good start, isn't it?
He looks at you, his gaze slowly softening, as if something hard inside him is starting to give way.

To say no to what he doesn't want. To give himself a break. To make peace with himself.
It all touched him in some way, led to a change. And now, all he needs is to give himself time and patience to accept it all and learn how to live a new life.

speaker: You
content: If you want, we can help you get that piano back. When your uncle is back and you're ready to start your new life, you can have it with you. It means a lot, doesn't it?
To your surprise, however, Cassian thinks for a moment, then shakes his head.

speaker: Cassian
content: No... it's okay.

speaker: Cassian
content: My hands can no longer play. The piano would become meaningless if left with me. Since those children love it, it's best to let it stay there.
Let my past stay there, too. Let me say goodbye.
You can almost hear him say these words.
One by one, more streetlights flicker on as dusk falls. And there, surrounded by the lights of countless homes, Cassian looks out over the world, a genuine smile finally appearing on his face.

speaker: Cassian
content: Besides, I won't need a piano to kill time at the MBCC.

speaker: Cassian
content: No one there will treat me like a plaything. There are many interesting things to do.
His casual words drift away on the wind. You turn to look at him.
He doesn't look back at you. His face is slightly turned to the side, and as the wind catches the ends of his hair, you see the light in his eyes.
It isn't avoidance, or weariness, or sorrow. It's a gentle, long-forgotten glimmer of anticipation.
You don't say anything, just smile quietly.
Your shadows stretch out, long and thin in the lamplight. They meet and join on the pavement, like two worlds meeting at last.
Forensica stares blankly into space. Her eyes are calm, and she appears to be lost in thought. You notice her fingers gripping the pocket of her clothes.
She's remained uncooperative ever since her arrest, refusing to answer any questions.
By now, you can make out the shape of the object from it being pressed against the pocket—it's a pinky bone.
Let me introduce myself. I'm the Chief of the MBCC, and I'm in charge of your interrogation for this case.
Forensica doesn't move, but her gaze sharpens as it falls on you. You know that look. It's wariness, one you'd find in a cornered animal. She looks you up and down, sizing you up.
Despite never having met before, she seems to be extremely hostile towards you. She keeps her mouth shut, repulsion written all over her face.
Body theft may not be a serious crime, but it still involves endangering public safety and desecrating human remains.
I heard you used to be a forensic pathologist. You should understand the charges better than I do.
When you mention her work as a forensic pathologist, Forensica can't help but slip her hand into her pocket.
You notice the movement, and the finger bone is now partially visible at the edge of her pocket.
Do you have anything to say about what you've done?
...Or rather, is there anything I can help you with?
Forensica lets out a cold laugh and finally speaks, her tone extremely sharp.

speaker: Forensica
content: Help me? You hypocrites would be doing me a great favor already if you'd just go far, far away.
So you do need help.

speaker: Forensica
content: It's one thing to listen to people's dying wishes, it's another to pry into private memories. Going deeper requires strong persistence. Since I don't have any, I can't fulfill your request.
It seems her wariness isn't directed at you specifically, but rather a certain group of people.
The records show that Forensica used to work at a forensic examination center before being dismissed for certain reasons.
These days, while she might appear to be an empty shell, she never actually gave up on forensic examination and related work.
In order to make a living, she became Clementine's consultant, providing expertise in forensics for her novels.
She's exactly as described in Clementine's novels—eccentric, peculiar, and guarded.
Perhaps it's because the novel's portrayal was so vivid. Even though she should be a complete stranger, you feel as if you've known her for ages.
This sense of familiarity intrigues you, and makes you more patient. You want to understand what Forensica is truly thinking.
If you don't want to talk about the case, we can discuss something else.
How's Dorothy doing?

speaker: Forensica
content: ...I don't know what you're talking about.
You take out the bestselling book, "Murder on the Praeva Express," and set it in front of her.
I'm sure you know this book—you're basically the same person in and outside of it.
We may have never met in person, but we made quite a good combo in Clementine's novel, didn't we?
In the story, we worked together to find the killer. As a token of our friendship, you gave me a finger bone.
That finger bone came from your collection. Dorothy, if I recall correctly.

speaker: Seconds drag by before the presence retreats into the distance. You lift your gaze and find Chengxiao's masked face above you, the corner of his mouth tilted faintly upward.
content: You know Clementine?
More than that, we've had many in-depth conversations.
Clementine mentioned how all the forensic expertise in her novels came from you. She even went as far as to say that you're her most trusted consultant.
Forensica reaches out and closes the novel you had opened. The dust jacket is covered in highly positive reviews and recommendations.

speaker: Forensica
content: That woman... I suppose she's a decent novelist. At least she respects the facts.
Whether it's because of Clementine, or because you acknowledged the novel, Forensica's hostility, while not entirely gone, has noticeably diminished.
Clementine holds you in very high regard, you know. She said you're a rare genius whose knowledge and intuition far surpass the ordinary.

speaker: Forensica
content: A genius? I highly doubt a real genius would end up being locked up in a place like this, waiting to be judged.

speaker: Forensica
content: What exactly are you getting at anyway? Are you trying to approach me as the same character that's in the novel? Or are you just trying to brag about how much you read?
I was trying to bridge the gap between us. Doesn't seem to be working, though.
That said, we did work together to find the killer in the novel. Perhaps we can do the same now.
You pull up the files on the various charges against Forensica. Nearly every single one points to her investigating something.
I just want to know why you did this. Are you investigating the truth behind a particular case?

speaker: Forensica
content: Truth? As if such a thing exists.

speaker: Forensica
content: Everyone just wants to close a case, bury the body, and move on as quickly as possible. That's the only "truth."

speaker: Forensica
content: Everyone has their own agenda in this world. Whoever holds the power gets to decide what "truth" is.
You seem to have struck a nerve. Forensica grows increasingly agitated, her choice of words becoming much harsher.
You should know that we found the truth behind the arson case about the orphanage.

speaker: Forensica
content: So what? If you'd found the truth sooner, Clementine wouldn't have had to write that novel in the first place.

speaker: Forensica
content: Clementine wouldn't be who she is today, and her friends would still be alive.

speaker: Forensica
content: Bloated institutions full of red tape, breeding nothing but parasites and incompetent trash... What right does a system like that have to pass judgment on anything?
Society requires us to follow due process, but that doesn't mean we can't pursue the truth.
Gathering evidence takes time. As a forensic pathologist, you should understand that better than anyone.

speaker: Forensica
content: It's BECAUSE I'm a forensic pathologist that I know just how idiotic that "due process" is!

speaker: Forensica
content: The evidence is right there in front of us, yet people abuse their authority to manipulate procedures and turn justice into nothing but empty words!
Forensica glares at you, her hand curled tightly in her pocket, the fabric of her clothes trembling slightly from the force of her grip.
And I'm guessing that's why you refuse to work with any forensic institutions now?
Your file shows you had an outstanding academic record at DisCity University's School of Forensic Science, but your employment history after graduation...
Seven jobs in five years, and every single one ended in conflict with your superiors or colleagues.

speaker: Forensica
content: Don't even get me started on those idiots! They could barely get basic autopsy procedures right, and yet they can't stand having anyone correct them!

speaker: Forensica
content: Clumsy, careless, treating the dead like they don't matter... I was only pointing out their mistakes! What's so wrong with that?
There's nothing wrong with pointing out mistakes, but workplaces do need certain rules to be in place if they are to function properly, and...

speaker: Forensica
content: What, so we should favor those rules over truth and evidence?
Forensica's eyes darken, making no attempt to hide her displeasure.
That's not what I meant.

speaker: Forensica
content: Then are you questioning my abilities? I'll have you know, I'm the best forensic pathologist in DisCity—no, in the entire world.

speaker: Forensica
content: Tch. Can we just get this over with already? I don't have time to waste on idiots.
Truth and evidence are fragile. Sometimes, rules aren't obstacles—they're tools. When used properly, they can help the truth surface faster.

speaker: Forensica
content: Hooray, more pretty speeches. Just what I needed.

speaker: Forensica
content: Let me guess, now you're going to say "procedures exist for a reason," right? Or how "adapting to society is important?"

speaker: Forensica
content: All you and those so-called guardians of order do is put on airs, looking down from your pedestals, acting all benevolent when you're not.

speaker: Forensica
content: If you've ever seen a real corpse, looked into those cloudy, lifeless eyes of someone who died with unfinished business... you'd understand. Hypocrisy is far more revolting than even malevolence.
You can see a complex array of emotions across Forensica's face—fury at unjust authority, and grief for those who died with wrongs unavenged.

She despises rigid rules and convoluted legal procedures, yet she hasn't abandoned her work as a forensic pathologist. She still operates by her own code, helping anyone who needs someone to speak for the dead.
It shows that deep down, she holds something sacred. A conviction strong enough to keep her going no matter what stands in her way.
